		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		und[0], und[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	}
	return
}

func diffState(c *CPU, tt *thTest, bus *corpusBus) []string {
	var diffs []string
	f := &tt.final
	view, fiq, svc, abt, irq, und := composedViews(c)
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if view[i] != f.R[i] {
			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("R%d: got %08x want %08x", i, view[i], f.R[i]))
		}
	}
	if c.CPSR != f.CPSR {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("CPSR: got %08x want %08x", c.CPSR, f.CPSR))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		if c.SPSR[i] != f.SPSR[i] {
			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("SPSR[%d]: got %08x want %08x", i, c.SPSR[i], f.SPSR[i]))
		}
	}
	banks := []struct {
		name string
		got  []uint32
		want []uint32
	}{
		{"R_fiq", fiq[:], f.RFIQ[:]},
		{"R_svc", svc[:], f.RSVC[:]},
		{"R_abt", abt[:], f.RABT[:]},
		{"R_irq", irq[:], f.RIRQ[:]},
		{"R_und", und[:], f.RUND[:]},
	}
	for _, bk := range banks {
		for i := range bk.got {
			if bk.got[i] != bk.want[i] {
				diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("%s[%d]: got %08x want %08x", bk.name, i, bk.got[i], bk.want[i]))
			}
		}
	}
	if c.Executing != f.Pipeline[0] {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("pipeline[0]: got %08x want %08x", c.Executing, f.Pipeline[0]))
	}
	if c.Pipe[0] != f.Pipeline[1] {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("pipeline[1]: got %08x want %08x", c.Pipe[0], f.Pipeline[1]))
	}
	if bus.fail != "" {
		diffs = append(diffs, "bus: "+bus.fail)
	}
	if bus.dpos != len(bus.data) {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("bus: consumed %d of %d data transactions", bus.dpos, len(bus.data)))
	}
	return diffs
}

func corpusDir(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "testroms", "tomharte-arm7tdmi")
	if st, err := os.Stat(dir); err != nil || !st.IsDir() {
		t.Skipf("corpus not present at %s", dir)
	}
	return dir
}

func TestTomHarteARM7TDMI(t *testing.T) {
	dir := corpusDir(t)
	files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, "*.json.bin"))
	if err != nil || len(files) == 0 {
		t.Skip("no corpus files")
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	subset := 2000
	if v := os.Getenv("DC_TH_SUBSET"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &subset)
	}
	seed := int64(0xD33D)
	if v := os.Getenv("DC_TH_SEED"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &seed)
	}
	totalRun, totalFail := 0, 0
	for _, path := range files {
		path := path
		name := filepath.Base(path)
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			tests := parseCorpusFile(t, path)
			rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed + int64(len(name))))
			idx := rng.Perm(len(tests))
			if subset < len(idx) {
				idx = idx[:subset]
			}
			fails := 0
			for _, ix := range idx {
				tt := &tests[ix]
				bus := newCorpusBus(tt)
				cpu := &CPU{Bus: bus}
				loadState(cpu, &tt.initial, tt)
				cpu.Step()
				if diffs := diffState(cpu, tt, bus); len(diffs) > 0 {
					fails++
					if fails <= 3 {
						t.Logf("test %d opcode=%08x base=%08x: %v", ix, tt.opcode, tt.base, diffs)
					}
				}
			}
			totalRun += len(idx)
			totalFail += fails
			t.Logf("%s: %d/%d passed", name, len(idx)-fails, len(idx))
			if fails > 0 {
				t.Errorf("%s: %d of %d tests failed", name, fails, len(idx))
			}
		})
	}
	t.Logf("TOTAL: %d/%d passed", totalRun-totalFail, totalRun)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/chips/arm7/thumb.go ====================

package arm7

// Thumb state instruction execution: the complete ARMv4T Thumb
// instruction set. Program counter reads in Thumb state see the
// stored R[15], which is the executing instruction address plus
// 4; PC relative addressing aligns that value down to a word
// boundary first.

// execThumb executes one Thumb instruction and returns cycles.
func (c *CPU) execThumb(op uint16) int {
	switch {
	case op>>13 == 0b000: // shifts, add, subtract
		if (op>>11)&3 == 3 {
			return c.thumbAddSub(op)
		}
		return c.thumbShiftImm(op)
	case op>>13 == 0b001: // move, compare, add, subtract immediate
		return c.thumbImm8(op)
	case op>>10 == 0b010000: // ALU operations
		return c.thumbALU(op)
	case op>>10 == 0b010001: // high register operations, BX
		return c.thumbHiReg(op)
	case op>>11 == 0b01001: // PC relative load
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		addr := (c.R[15] &^ 2) + uint32(op&0xFF)*4
		c.R[rd] = c.loadWord(addr)
		return 3
	case op>>12 == 0b0101: // load and store register offset groups
		return c.thumbLoadStoreReg(op)
	case op>>13 == 0b011: // load and store immediate offset
		return c.thumbLoadStoreImm(op)
	case op>>12 == 0b1000: // halfword immediate offset
		return c.thumbLoadStoreHalf(op)
	case op>>12 == 0b1001: // SP relative load and store
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		addr := c.R[13] + uint32(op&0xFF)*4
		if (op>>11)&1 == 1 {
			c.R[rd] = c.loadWord(addr)
			return 3
		}
		c.storeWord(addr, c.R[rd])
		return 2
	case op>>12 == 0b1010: // add PC or SP to register
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		var base uint32
		if (op>>11)&1 == 1 {
			base = c.R[13]
		} else {
			base = c.R[15] &^ 2
		}
		c.R[rd] = base + uint32(op&0xFF)*4
		return 1
	case op>>12 == 0b1011: // miscellaneous
		return c.thumbMisc(op)
	case op>>12 == 0b1100: // multiple load and store
		return c.thumbBlockTransfer(op)
	case op>>12 == 0b1101: // conditional branch and SWI
		if (op>>8)&0xF == 0xF {
			return c.swiException()
		}
		// Condition 1110 in this encoding is the always condition
		// on ARM7TDMI silicon (the architecture reserves it, but
		// the hardware condition evaluator treats it as AL), and
		// the corpus asserts branch always behaviour for it.
		if c.condPassed(uint32(op>>8) & 0xF) {
			off := int32(int8(op&0xFF)) * 2
			c.flush(uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off))
			return 3
		}
		return 1
	case op>>11 == 0b11100: // unconditional branch
		off := int32(op&0x7FF) << 21 >> 21 * 2
		c.flush(uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off))
		return 3
	case op>>11 == 0b11110: // BL, BLX prefix
		off := int32(op&0x7FF) << 21 >> 21 << 12
		c.R[14] = uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off)
		return 1
	case op>>11 == 0b11101: // BLX suffix
		target := c.R[14] + uint32(op&0x7FF)*2
		c.R[14] = (c.R[15] - 2) | 1
		c.CPSR &^= cpsrT
		c.writePC(target)
		return 3
	case op>>11 == 0b11111: // BL suffix
		target := c.R[14] + uint32(op&0x7FF)*2
		c.R[14] = (c.R[15] - 2) | 1
		c.flush(target &^ 1)
		return 3
	}
	return c.undefinedException()
}

func (c *CPU) thumbShiftImm(op uint16) int {
	amt := (op >> 6) & 0x1F
	rm := (op >> 3) & 7
	rd := op & 7
	res, carry := shiftByImm(c.R[rm], uint32(op>>11)&3, uint32(amt), c.flagC())
	c.R[rd] = res
	c.setLogicalFlags(res, carry)
	return 1
}

func (c *CPU) thumbAddSub(op uint16) int {
	rd := op & 7
	rn := (op >> 3) & 7
	var b uint32
	if (op>>10)&1 == 1 {
		b = uint32((op >> 6) & 7)
	} else {
		b = c.R[(op>>6)&7]
	}
	if (op>>9)&1 == 1 {
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(c.R[rn], b, 1)
	} else {
		c.R[rd] = c.addFlags(c.R[rn], b, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

func (c *CPU) thumbImm8(op uint16) int {
	rd := (op >> 8) & 7
	imm := uint32(op & 0xFF)
	switch (op >> 11) & 3 {
	case 0: // MOV
		c.R[rd] = imm
		c.setNZ(imm)
	case 1: // CMP
		c.subFlags(c.R[rd], imm, 1)
	case 2: // ADD
		c.R[rd] = c.addFlags(c.R[rd], imm, 0)
	case 3: // SUB
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(c.R[rd], imm, 1)
	}
	return 1
}

// thumbALU implements the format 4 ALU group. Shift by register
// operations use the full low byte of the shift register, as in
// ARM state. The multiply here always clears the carry flag,
// which is what the corpus asserts for the Thumb form.
func (c *CPU) thumbALU(op uint16) int {
	aluOp := (op >> 6) & 0xF
	rd := op & 7
	rs := (op >> 3) & 7
	a := c.R[rd]
	b := c.R[rs]
	carryIn := uint32(0)
	if c.flagC() {
		carryIn = 1
	}
	switch aluOp {
	case 0x0: // AND
		res := a & b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, c.flagC())
	case 0x1: // EOR
		res := a ^ b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, c.flagC())
	case 0x2: // LSL by register
		res, carry := shiftByReg(a, 0, b&0xFF, c.flagC())
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, carry)
	case 0x3: // LSR by register
		res, carry := shiftByReg(a, 1, b&0xFF, c.flagC())
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, carry)
	case 0x4: // ASR by register
		res, carry := shiftByReg(a, 2, b&0xFF, c.flagC())
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, carry)
	case 0x5: // ADC
		c.R[rd] = c.addFlags(a, b, carryIn)
	case 0x6: // SBC
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(a, b, carryIn)
	case 0x7: // ROR by register
		res, carry := shiftByReg(a, 3, b&0xFF, c.flagC())
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, carry)
	case 0x8: // TST
		c.setLogicalFlags(a&b, c.flagC())
	case 0x9: // NEG
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(0, b, 1)
	case 0xA: // CMP
		c.subFlags(a, b, 1)
	case 0xB: // CMN
		c.addFlags(a, b, 0)
	case 0xC: // ORR
		res := a | b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, c.flagC())
	case 0xD: // MUL
		res := a * b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZ(res)
		// The carry is the multiplier carry out, as in the
		// ARM form, with the destination register operand in
		// the multiplier role of the model.
		c.setFlag(cpsrC, mulCarryShort(b, a, 0))
	case 0xE: // BIC
		res := a &^ b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, c.flagC())
	case 0xF: // MVN
		res := ^b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setLogicalFlags(res, c.flagC())
	}
	return 1
}

func (c *CPU) thumbHiReg(op uint16) int {
	hiOp := (op >> 8) & 3
	rd := uint32(op&7) | uint32((op>>7)&1)<<3
	rs := uint32((op >> 3) & 0xF)
	if hiOp == 3 {
		// BX. The register form of BLX does not exist in ARMv4T;
		// bit 7 is ignored and the whole encoding is BX, which is
		// what the corpus asserts.
		v := c.R[rs]
		if v&1 != 0 {
			c.CPSR |= cpsrT
		} else {
			c.CPSR &^= cpsrT
		}
		c.writePC(v)
		return 3
	}
	src := c.R[rs]
	switch hiOp {
	case 0: // ADD
		res := c.R[rd] + src
		if rd == 15 {
			c.writePC(res)
			return 3
		}
		c.R[rd] = res
	case 1: // CMP
		c.subFlags(c.R[rd], src, 1)
	case 2: // MOV
		if rd == 15 {
			c.writePC(src)
			return 3
		}
		c.R[rd] = src
	}
	return 1
}

// thumbLoadStoreReg implements format 7 (register offset word and
// byte transfers) and format 7b (register offset halfword and
// signed transfers), selected by bit 9.
func (c *CPU) thumbLoadStoreReg(op uint16) int {
	ro := (op >> 6) & 7
	rb := (op >> 3) & 7
	rd := op & 7
	addr := c.R[rb] + c.R[ro]
	if (op>>9)&1 == 0 {
		load := (op>>11)&1 == 1
		isByte := (op>>10)&1 == 1
		if load {
			if isByte {
				c.R[rd] = c.loadByte(addr)
			} else {
				c.R[rd] = c.loadWord(addr)
			}
			return 3
		}
		if isByte {
			c.storeByte(addr, c.R[rd])
		} else {
			c.storeWord(addr, c.R[rd])
		}
		return 2
	}
	switch (op >> 10) & 3 {
	case 0: // STRH
		c.storeHalf(addr, c.R[rd])
		return 2
	case 1: // LDRSB
		c.R[rd] = c.loadByteSigned(addr)
	case 2: // LDRH
		c.R[rd] = c.loadHalf(addr)
	case 3: // LDRSH
		c.R[rd] = c.loadHalfSigned(addr)
	}
	return 3
}

func (c *CPU) thumbLoadStoreImm(op uint16) int {
	rb := (op >> 3) & 7
	rd := op & 7
	isByte := (op>>12)&1 == 1
	load := (op>>11)&1 == 1
	imm := uint32((op >> 6) & 0x1F)
	var addr uint32
	if isByte {
		addr = c.R[rb] + imm
	} else {
		addr = c.R[rb] + imm*4
	}
	if load {
		if isByte {
			c.R[rd] = c.loadByte(addr)
		} else {
			c.R[rd] = c.loadWord(addr)
		}
		return 3
	}
	if isByte {
		c.storeByte(addr, c.R[rd])
	} else {
		c.storeWord(addr, c.R[rd])
	}
	return 2
}

func (c *CPU) thumbLoadStoreHalf(op uint16) int {
	rb := (op >> 3) & 7
	rd := op & 7
	addr := c.R[rb] + uint32((op>>6)&0x1F)*2
	if (op>>11)&1 == 1 {
		c.R[rd] = c.loadHalf(addr)
		return 3
	}
	c.storeHalf(addr, c.R[rd])
	return 2
}

// thumbMisc implements the 1011 group: ADD SP with a signed
// immediate, PUSH, and POP. Other encodings in the group are
// undefined in ARMv4T.
func (c *CPU) thumbMisc(op uint16) int {
	switch {
	case op&0xFF00 == 0xB000: // ADD SP, signed immediate times 4
		imm := uint32(op&0x7F) * 4
		if (op>>7)&1 == 1 {
			c.R[13] -= imm
		} else {
			c.R[13] += imm
		}
		return 1
	case op&0xFE00 == 0xB400: // PUSH
		list := op & 0xFF
		count := 0
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if list>>i&1 == 1 {
				count++
			}
		}
		withLR := (op>>8)&1 == 1
		if withLR {
			count++
		}
		if count == 0 {
			// Empty list: only the program counter
			// transfers, and the stack pointer still moves
			// by the full sixteen register frame.
			sp := c.R[13] - 64
			c.Bus.Write32(sp, c.R[15]+2)
			c.R[13] = sp
			return 3
		}
		sp := c.R[13] - 4*uint32(count)
		addr := sp
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if list>>i&1 == 1 {
				c.Bus.Write32(addr, c.R[i])
				addr += 4
			}
		}
		if withLR {
			c.Bus.Write32(addr, c.R[14])
		}
		c.R[13] = sp
		return 2 + count
	case op&0xFE00 == 0xBC00: // POP
		list := op & 0xFF
		count := 0
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if list>>i&1 == 1 {
				count++
			}
		}
		withPC := (op>>8)&1 == 1
		if withPC {
			count++
		}
		if count == 0 {
			// Empty list: only the program counter
			// transfers, and the stack pointer still moves
			// by the full sixteen register frame. The
			// loaded value goes to flush unmasked: flush
			// keeps its low bits visible in R[15] (the
			// corpus compares them) and aligns only the
			// refill fetches.
			pc := c.Bus.Read32(c.R[13])
			c.R[13] += 64
			c.flush(pc)
			return 5
		}
		addr := c.R[13]
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if list>>i&1 == 1 {
				c.R[i] = c.Bus.Read32(addr)
				addr += 4
			}
		}
		var pc uint32
		if withPC {
			pc = c.Bus.Read32(addr)
		}
		c.R[13] += 4 * uint32(count)
		if withPC {
			c.flush(pc &^ 1)
			return 5
		}
		return 2 + count
	}
	return c.undefinedException()
}

// thumbBlockTransfer implements the Thumb LDMIA and STMIA forms.
// The base register is always written back; an empty list counts
// as sixteen registers for the writeback and transfers only the
// program counter, as in the ARM form (the corpus transaction
// lists show the single transfer).
func (c *CPU) thumbBlockTransfer(op uint16) int {
	rb := uint32((op >> 8) & 7)
	list := op & 0xFF
	load := (op>>11)&1 == 1
	count := 0
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if list>>i&1 == 1 {
			count++
		}
	}
	effCount := count
	if list == 0 {
		effCount = 16
	}
	base := c.R[rb]
	wb := base + 4*uint32(effCount)
	addr := base
	cycles := 2
	if list == 0 {
		// Empty list: only the program counter transfers.
		c.R[rb] = wb
		if load {
			v := c.Bus.Read32(base)
			c.flush(v)
		} else {
			// A stored Thumb program counter reads as the
			// instruction address plus 6.
			c.Bus.Write32(base, c.R[15]+2)
		}
		return cycles + 2
	}
	if load {
		var rbLoaded uint32
		rbInList := list>>rb&1 == 1
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if list>>i&1 == 1 {
				v := c.Bus.Read32(addr)
				if uint32(i) == rb {
					rbLoaded = v
				}
				c.R[i] = v
				addr += 4
				cycles++
			}
		}
		c.R[rb] = wb
		if rbInList {
			c.R[rb] = rbLoaded
		}
		return cycles
	}
	first := -1
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if list>>i&1 == 1 {
			first = i
			break
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if list>>i&1 == 1 {
			v := c.R[i]
			if uint32(i) == rb && i != first {
				v = wb
			}
			c.Bus.Write32(addr, v)
			addr += 4
			cycles++
		}
	}
	c.R[rb] = wb
	return cycles
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/chips/sh4/exec.go ====================

package sh4

// Integer instruction execution. exec decodes and executes one
// 16-bit instruction at address pc. inDelay reports that the
// instruction occupies a delay slot; branch class instructions are
// filtered out before exec runs (see Step), and any remaining
// illegal encoding in a delay slot raises the slot illegal exception
// instead of the general one.
//
// On entry c.PC is advanced to the next sequential instruction;
// delayed branches instead arrange for the delay slot to execute
// next and for Step to continue at the branch target afterwards.

func sext8(v uint32) uint32  { return uint32(int32(int8(v))) }
func sext16(v uint32) uint32 { return uint32(int32(int16(v))) }

// delayedBranch arranges delay-slot execution: the next Step runs
// the instruction at pc+2, then continues at target if taken, or at
// pc+4 if not taken (the BT/S and BF/S not-taken case).
func (c *CPU) delayedBranch(pc uint32, target uint32, taken bool) {
	c.inDelay = true
	if taken {
		c.afterDelay = target
	} else {
		c.afterDelay = pc + 4
	}
	c.PC = pc + 2
}

// ctrlReg reads a control register by its LDC/STC code:
// 0 = SR, 1 = GBR, 2 = VBR, 3 = SSR, 4 = SPC.
func (c *CPU) ctrlReg(code uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	switch code {
	case 0:
		return c.SR, true
	case 1:
		return c.GBR, true
	case 2:
		return c.VBR, true
	case 3:
		return c.SSR, true
	case 4:
		return c.SPC, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

func (c *CPU) setCtrlReg(code uint32, v uint32) bool {
	switch code {
	case 0:
		c.setSR(v)
	case 1:
		c.GBR = v
	case 2:
		c.VBR = v
	case 3:
		c.SSR = v
	case 4:
		c.SPC = v
	default:
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// ctrlPrivileged reports whether a control register code requires
// privileged mode. GBR is the exception: it is user accessible.
func ctrlPrivileged(code uint32) bool { return code != 1 }

// sysReg reads a system register by its LDS/STS code:
// 0 = MACH, 1 = MACL, 2 = PR, 5 = FPUL, 6 = FPSCR.
func (c *CPU) sysReg(code uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	switch code {
	case 0:
		return c.MACH, true
	case 1:
		return c.MACL, true
	case 2:
		return c.PR, true
	case 5:
		return c.FPUL, true
	case 6:
		return c.FPSCR, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

func (c *CPU) setSysReg(code uint32, v uint32) bool {
	switch code {
	case 0:
		c.MACH = v
	case 1:
		c.MACL = v
	case 2:
		c.PR = v
	case 5:
		c.FPUL = v
	case 6:
		c.setFPSCR(v)
	default:
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// needPriv raises the illegal instruction exception when the CPU is
// in user mode (SR.MD = 0) and the instruction is privileged.
func (c *CPU) needPriv(inDelay bool, pc uint32) bool {
	if c.SR&srMD == 0 {
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		return false
	}
	return true
}

func (c *CPU) exec(op uint16, pc uint32, inDelay bool) {
	n := int(op >> 8 & 0xF)
	m := int(op >> 4 & 0xF)
	low := op & 0xF
	imm := uint32(op & 0xFF)
	disp4 := uint32(op & 0xF)

	c.PC = pc + 2

	switch op >> 12 {
	case 0x0:
		c.execGroup0(op, pc, inDelay, n, m, low)
	case 0x1: // MOV.L Rm,@(disp,Rn)
		addr := c.R[n] + disp4*4
		if !c.write32(addr, c.R[m]) {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
		}
	case 0x2:
		c.execGroup2(pc, inDelay, n, m, low)
	case 0x3:
		c.execGroup3(pc, inDelay, n, m, low)
	case 0x4:
		c.execGroup4(op, pc, inDelay, n, m, low)
	case 0x5: // MOV.L @(disp,Rm),Rn
		addr := c.R[m] + disp4*4
		v, ok := c.read32(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] = v
	case 0x6:
		c.execGroup6(pc, inDelay, n, m, low)
	case 0x7: // ADD #imm,Rn
		c.R[n] += sext8(imm)
	case 0x8:
		c.execGroup8(op, pc, inDelay)
	case 0x9: // MOV.W @(disp,PC),Rn
		addr := pc + 4 + imm*2
		v, ok := c.read16(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] = sext16(uint32(v))
	case 0xA: // BRA
		disp := int32(op & 0xFFF)
		if disp&0x800 != 0 {
			disp |= ^int32(0xFFF)
		}
		c.delayedBranch(pc, pc+4+uint32(disp*2), true)
	case 0xB: // BSR
		disp := int32(op & 0xFFF)
		if disp&0x800 != 0 {
			disp |= ^int32(0xFFF)
		}
		c.PR = pc + 4
		c.delayedBranch(pc, pc+4+uint32(disp*2), true)
	case 0xC:
		c.execGroupC(op, pc, inDelay)
	case 0xD: // MOV.L @(disp,PC),Rn
		addr := (pc & 0xFFFFFFFC) + 4 + imm*4
		v, ok := c.read32(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] = v
	case 0xE: // MOV #imm,Rn
		c.R[n] = sext8(imm)
	case 0xF:
		c.execFPU(op, pc, inDelay)
	}
}

// execGroup0 handles the 0000 opcode family: indexed MOV forms,
// MUL.L, MAC.L, STC/STS, MOVT, and the fixed system instructions.
func (c *CPU) execGroup0(op uint16, pc uint32, inDelay bool, n, m int, low uint16) {
	switch low {
	case 0x3:
		switch m {
		case 0x0: // BSRF Rn
			target := pc + 4 + c.R[n]
			c.PR = pc + 4
			c.delayedBranch(pc, target, true)
		case 0x2: // BRAF Rn
			c.delayedBranch(pc, pc+4+c.R[n], true)
		case 0x8: // PREF @Rn: cache prefetch, no-op without caches
		case 0x9, 0xA, 0xB: // OCBI, OCBP, OCBWB @Rn: no-ops without caches
		case 0xC: // MOVCA.L R0,@Rn
			if !c.write32(c.R[n], c.R[0]) {
				c.enterMemFault(pc)
			}
		default:
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	case 0x4, 0x5, 0x6: // MOV.B/W/L Rm,@(R0,Rn)
		addr := c.R[n] + c.R[0]
		c.storeSize(pc, addr, c.R[m], int(low-0x4))
	case 0xC, 0xD, 0xE: // MOV.B/W/L @(R0,Rm),Rn
		addr := c.R[m] + c.R[0]
		v := c.loadSize(pc, addr, int(low-0xC))
		if c.excepted {
			return
		}
		c.R[n] = v
	case 0x7: // MUL.L Rm,Rn
		c.MACL = c.R[n] * c.R[m]
	case 0xF: // MAC.L @Rm+,@Rn+
		c.macL(pc, n, m)
	case 0x2: // STC ctrl,Rn or STC Rm_BANK,Rn
		if m >= 8 { // bank form: source is the inactive bank
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.R[n] = c.Bank[m&7]
			return
		}
		code := uint32(m)
		if ctrlPrivileged(code) && !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
			return
		}
		v, ok := c.ctrlReg(code)
		if !ok {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] = v
	case 0xA: // STS sys,Rn, plus STC SGR/DBR special encodings
		switch m {
		case 0x3: // STC SGR,Rn
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.R[n] = c.SGR
		case 0xF: // STC DBR,Rn
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.R[n] = c.DBR
		default:
			v, ok := c.sysReg(uint32(m))
			if !ok {
				c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
				return
			}
			c.R[n] = v
		}
	case 0x9:
		if m == 2 { // MOVT Rn
			c.R[n] = c.getT()
		} else if op == 0x0019 { // DIV0U
			c.setQM(0, 0)
			c.setT(0)
		} else if op == 0x0009 { // NOP
		} else {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	case 0x8:
		if n != 0 {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		switch m {
		case 0x0: // CLRT
			c.setT(0)
		case 0x1: // SETT
			c.setT(1)
		case 0x2: // CLRMAC
			c.MACH, c.MACL = 0, 0
		case 0x3: // LDTLB
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.loadTLB()
		case 0x4: // CLRS
			c.setS(0)
		case 0x5: // SETS
			c.setS(1)
		default:
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	case 0xB:
		if n != 0 {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		switch m {
		case 0x0: // RTS
			c.delayedBranch(pc, c.PR, true)
		case 0x1: // SLEEP
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.Halted = true
		case 0x2: // RTE
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			target := c.SPC
			c.setSR(c.SSR)
			c.delayedBranch(pc, target, true)
		default:
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}

// loadSize loads a byte (size 0, sign extended), word (size 1, sign
// extended), or longword (size 2) and vectors a fault itself.
func (c *CPU) loadSize(pc uint32, addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 0:
		v, ok := c.read8(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return 0
		}
		return sext8(uint32(v))
	case 1:
		v, ok := c.read16(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return 0
		}
		return sext16(uint32(v))
	default:
		v, ok := c.read32(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return 0
		}
		return v
	}
}

// storeSize stores the low bytes of v at addr; size is 0, 1, or 2
// for byte, word, or longword.
func (c *CPU) storeSize(pc uint32, addr uint32, v uint32, size int) {
	var ok bool
	switch size {
	case 0:
		ok = c.write8(addr, uint8(v))
	case 1:
		ok = c.write16(addr, uint16(v))
	default:
		ok = c.write32(addr, v)
	}
	if !ok {
		c.enterMemFault(pc)
	}
}

// macL implements MAC.L @Rm+,@Rn+. When Rm and Rn are the same
// register, two consecutive longwords are read and the register is
// post-incremented twice, per the manual. With SR.S = 1 the 64-bit
// sum is saturated to a signed 48-bit range (with the manual's
// overflow rule: a sum that overflows 64 bits saturates to
// 2^47-1 or -2^47 according to the sign of the accumulator).
func (c *CPU) macL(pc uint32, n, m int) {
	var vN, vM uint32
	var ok bool
	if m == n {
		if vN, ok = c.read32(c.R[n]); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		if vM, ok = c.read32(c.R[n] + 4); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] += 8
	} else {
		if vN, ok = c.read32(c.R[n]); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		if vM, ok = c.read32(c.R[m]); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] += 4
		c.R[m] += 4
	}
	prod := int64(int32(vN)) * int64(int32(vM))
	acc := int64(uint64(c.MACH)<<32 | uint64(c.MACL))
	sum := acc + prod
	if c.SR&srS != 0 {
		const max48 = int64(1)<<47 - 1
		const min48 = -int64(1) << 47
		if (prod > 0 && sum < acc) || (prod < 0 && sum > acc) {
			if acc >= 0 {
				sum = max48
			} else {
				sum = min48
			}
		} else if sum > max48 {
			sum = max48
		} else if sum < min48 {
			sum = min48
		}
	}
	c.MACH = uint32(sum >> 32)
	c.MACL = uint32(sum)
}

// macW implements MAC.W @Rm+,@Rn+ with the same addressing rules as
// MAC.L. With SR.S = 1 only MACL accumulates, the 33-bit sum is
// saturated to the signed 32-bit range, and on saturation MACH is
// set to 1 (otherwise MACH is unchanged), per the manual.
func (c *CPU) macW(pc uint32, n, m int) {
	var vN, vM uint16
	var ok bool
	if m == n {
		if vN, ok = c.read16(c.R[n]); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		if vM, ok = c.read16(c.R[n] + 2); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] += 4
	} else {
		if vN, ok = c.read16(c.R[n]); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		if vM, ok = c.read16(c.R[m]); !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] += 2
		c.R[m] += 2
	}
	prod := int64(int32(int16(vN))) * int64(int32(int16(vM)))
	if c.SR&srS != 0 {
		sum := int64(int32(c.MACL)) + prod
		sat := sum
		if sat > 0x7FFFFFFF {
			sat = 0x7FFFFFFF
		} else if sat < -0x80000000 {
			sat = -0x80000000
		}
		if sat != sum {
			c.MACH = 1
		}
		c.MACL = uint32(int32(sat))
		return
	}
	acc := int64(uint64(c.MACH)<<32|uint64(c.MACL)) + prod
	c.MACH = uint32(acc >> 32)
	c.MACL = uint32(acc)
}

// execGroup2 handles 0010 opcodes: register-indirect stores,
// pre-decrement stores, and register-register logic and multiply ops.
func (c *CPU) execGroup2(pc uint32, inDelay bool, n, m int, low uint16) {
	switch low {
	case 0x0, 0x1, 0x2: // MOV.B/W/L Rm,@Rn
		c.storeSize(pc, c.R[n], c.R[m], int(low))
	case 0x4, 0x5, 0x6: // MOV.B/W/L Rm,@-Rn
		size := int(low - 0x4)
		c.R[n] -= uint32(1 << size)
		c.storeSize(pc, c.R[n], c.R[m], size)
	case 0x7: // DIV0S Rm,Rn
		q := c.R[n] >> 31
		mm := c.R[m] >> 31
		c.setQM(q, mm)
		c.setT(q ^ mm)
	case 0x8: // TST Rm,Rn
		if c.R[n]&c.R[m] == 0 {
			c.setT(1)
		} else {
			c.setT(0)
		}
	case 0x9: // AND Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] &= c.R[m]
	case 0xA: // XOR Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] ^= c.R[m]
	case 0xB: // OR Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] |= c.R[m]
	case 0xC: // CMP/STR Rm,Rn
		x := c.R[n] ^ c.R[m]
		t := uint32(0)
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			if byte(x>>uint(8*i)) == 0 {
				t = 1
			}
		}
		c.setT(t)
	case 0xD: // XTRCT Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = c.R[m]&0xFFFF<<16 | c.R[n]>>16
	case 0xE: // MULU.W Rm,Rn
		c.MACL = uint32(c.R[n]&0xFFFF) * uint32(c.R[m]&0xFFFF)
	case 0xF: // MULS.W Rm,Rn
		c.MACL = uint32(int32(int16(c.R[n])) * int32(int16(c.R[m])))
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}

// execGroup3 handles 0011 opcodes: arithmetic, compares, DIV1, and
// the double-length multiplies.
func (c *CPU) execGroup3(pc uint32, inDelay bool, n, m int, low uint16) {
	a, b := c.R[n], c.R[m]
	switch low {
	case 0x0: // CMP/EQ Rm,Rn
		c.setT(boolU32(a == b))
	case 0x2: // CMP/HS Rm,Rn (unsigned >=)
		c.setT(boolU32(a >= b))
	case 0x3: // CMP/GE Rm,Rn (signed >=)
		c.setT(boolU32(int32(a) >= int32(b)))
	case 0x6: // CMP/HI Rm,Rn (unsigned >)
		c.setT(boolU32(a > b))
	case 0x7: // CMP/GT Rm,Rn (signed >)
		c.setT(boolU32(int32(a) > int32(b)))
	case 0x4: // DIV1 Rm,Rn
		c.div1(n, m)
	case 0x5: // DMULU.L Rm,Rn
		p := uint64(a) * uint64(b)
		c.MACL = uint32(p)
		c.MACH = uint32(p >> 32)
	case 0xD: // DMULS.L Rm,Rn
		p := int64(int32(a)) * int64(int32(b))
		c.MACL = uint32(p)
		c.MACH = uint32(p >> 32)
	case 0x8: // SUB Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = a - b
	case 0xA: // SUBC Rm,Rn
		sub := uint64(b) + uint64(c.getT())
		res := uint64(a) - sub
		c.R[n] = uint32(res)
		if uint64(a) < sub {
			c.setT(1)
		} else {
			c.setT(0)
		}
	case 0xB: // SUBV Rm,Rn
		res := int64(int32(a)) - int64(int32(b))
		c.R[n] = uint32(int32(res))
		if res > 0x7FFFFFFF || res < -0x80000000 {
			c.setT(1)
		} else {
			c.setT(0)
		}
	case 0xC: // ADD Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = a + b
	case 0xE: // ADDC Rm,Rn
		sum := uint64(a) + uint64(b) + uint64(c.getT())
		c.R[n] = uint32(sum)
		c.setT(uint32(sum >> 32 & 1))
	case 0xF: // ADDV Rm,Rn
		res := int64(int32(a)) + int64(int32(b))
		c.R[n] = uint32(int32(res))
		if res > 0x7FFFFFFF || res < -0x80000000 {
			c.setT(1)
		} else {
			c.setT(0)
		}
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}

func boolU32(b bool) uint32 {
	if b {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// div1 performs one DIV1 step: Rn is the partial-remainder register,
// Rm the divisor, and the SR Q, M, and T bits carry the state set up
// by DIV0S or DIV0U. Q records the sign of the 33-bit partial
// remainder (whose low half is Rn); each step shifts the remainder
// left, brings the previous quotient bit in through T, adds or
// subtracts the divisor depending on whether the old remainder sign
// equals M, and produces the next quotient bit in T. The full
// division sequence built on this (ROTCL on the dividend register
// interleaved with DIV1, one final ROTCL, and the closing remainder
// correction) is exercised in the tests.
func (c *CPU) div1(n, m int) {
	oldQ := c.getQ()
	mBit := c.getM()
	q := c.R[n] >> 31
	shifted := c.R[n]<<1 | c.getT()
	var res, carry uint32
	if oldQ == mBit {
		res = shifted - c.R[m]
		if res > shifted {
			carry = 1
		}
	} else {
		res = shifted + c.R[m]
		if res < shifted {
			carry = 1
		}
	}
	qn := q ^ mBit ^ carry
	c.R[n] = res
	c.setQM(qn, mBit)
	c.setT(1 - (qn ^ mBit))
}

// execGroup6 handles 0110 opcodes: register-indirect loads,
// post-increment loads, register MOV, and unary operations.
func (c *CPU) execGroup6(pc uint32, inDelay bool, n, m int, low uint16) {
	switch low {
	case 0x0, 0x1, 0x2: // MOV.B/W/L @Rm,Rn
		v := c.loadSize(pc, c.R[m], int(low))
		if c.excepted {
			return
		}
		c.R[n] = v
	case 0x3: // MOV Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = c.R[m]
	case 0x4, 0x5, 0x6: // MOV.B/W/L @Rm+,Rn
		size := int(low - 0x4)
		addr := c.R[m]
		v := c.loadSize(pc, addr, size)
		if c.excepted {
			return
		}
		c.R[m] = addr + uint32(1<<size)
		c.R[n] = v
	case 0x7: // NOT Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = ^c.R[m]
	case 0x8: // SWAP.B Rm,Rn
		v := c.R[m]
		c.R[n] = v&0xFFFF0000 | (v&0xFF)<<8 | (v>>8)&0xFF
	case 0x9: // SWAP.W Rm,Rn
		v := c.R[m]
		c.R[n] = v<<16 | v>>16
	case 0xA: // NEGC Rm,Rn
		sub := uint64(c.R[m]) + uint64(c.getT())
		c.R[n] = uint32(-int64(sub))
		if sub != 0 {
			c.setT(1)
		} else {
			c.setT(0)
		}
	case 0xB: // NEG Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = -c.R[m]
	case 0xC: // EXTU.B Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = c.R[m] & 0xFF
	case 0xD: // EXTU.W Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = c.R[m] & 0xFFFF
	case 0xE: // EXTS.B Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = sext8(c.R[m])
	case 0xF: // EXTS.W Rm,Rn
		c.R[n] = sext16(c.R[m])
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}

// execGroup8 handles the 1000 family selected by the second byte:
// displacement byte and word stores and loads through R0, CMP/EQ
// with an immediate, and the short conditional branches.
func (c *CPU) execGroup8(op uint16, pc uint32, inDelay bool) {
	imm := uint32(op & 0xFF)
	reg := int(op >> 4 & 0xF)
	disp := uint32(op & 0xF)
	switch op >> 8 {
	case 0x80: // MOV.B R0,@(disp,Rn)
		c.storeSize(pc, c.R[reg]+disp, c.R[0], 0)
	case 0x81: // MOV.W R0,@(disp,Rn)
		c.storeSize(pc, c.R[reg]+disp*2, c.R[0], 1)
	case 0x84: // MOV.B @(disp,Rm),R0
		v := c.loadSize(pc, c.R[reg]+disp, 0)
		if !c.excepted {
			c.R[0] = v
		}
	case 0x85: // MOV.W @(disp,Rm),R0
		v := c.loadSize(pc, c.R[reg]+disp*2, 1)
		if !c.excepted {
			c.R[0] = v
		}
	case 0x88: // CMP/EQ #imm,R0
		c.setT(boolU32(c.R[0] == sext8(imm)))
	case 0x89, 0x8B: // BT, BF: delay slot executes only if taken
		taken := (op>>8 == 0x89) == (c.getT() == 1)
		if taken {
			target := pc + 4 + uint32(int32(int8(imm))*2)
			c.delayedBranch(pc, target, true)
		} else {
			c.PC = pc + 4 // skip the delay slot entirely
		}
	case 0x8D, 0x8F: // BT/S, BF/S: delay slot always executes
		taken := (op>>8 == 0x8D) == (c.getT() == 1)
		target := pc + 4 + uint32(int32(int8(imm))*2)
		c.delayedBranch(pc, target, taken)
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}

// execGroupC handles the 1100 family selected by the second byte:
// GBR-relative transfers, MOVA, immediate logic ops, the GBR byte
// logic ops, and TRAPA.
func (c *CPU) execGroupC(op uint16, pc uint32, inDelay bool) {
	imm := uint32(op & 0xFF)
	gbrAddr := func(scale uint32) uint32 { return c.GBR + imm*scale }
	switch op >> 8 {
	case 0xC0: // MOV.B R0,@(disp,GBR)
		c.storeSize(pc, gbrAddr(1), c.R[0], 0)
	case 0xC1: // MOV.W R0,@(disp,GBR)
		c.storeSize(pc, gbrAddr(2), c.R[0], 1)
	case 0xC2: // MOV.L R0,@(disp,GBR)
		c.storeSize(pc, gbrAddr(4), c.R[0], 2)
	case 0xC4: // MOV.B @(disp,GBR),R0
		v := c.loadSize(pc, gbrAddr(1), 0)
		if !c.excepted {
			c.R[0] = v
		}
	case 0xC5: // MOV.W @(disp,GBR),R0
		v := c.loadSize(pc, gbrAddr(2), 1)
		if !c.excepted {
			c.R[0] = v
		}
	case 0xC6: // MOV.L @(disp,GBR),R0
		v := c.loadSize(pc, gbrAddr(4), 2)
		if !c.excepted {
			c.R[0] = v
		}
	case 0xC7: // MOVA @(disp,PC),R0
		c.R[0] = (pc & 0xFFFFFFFC) + 4 + imm*4
	case 0xC8: // TST #imm,R0
		c.setT(boolU32(c.R[0]&imm == 0))
	case 0xC9: // AND #imm,R0
		c.R[0] &= imm
	case 0xCA: // XOR #imm,R0
		c.R[0] ^= imm
	case 0xCB: // OR #imm,R0
		c.R[0] |= imm
	case 0xCC, 0xCD, 0xCE, 0xCF: // TST.B / AND.B / XOR.B / OR.B #imm,@(R0,GBR)
		addr := c.GBR + c.R[0]
		v, ok := c.read8(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return
		}
		switch op >> 8 {
		case 0xCC:
			c.setT(boolU32(uint32(v)&imm == 0))
		case 0xCD:
			if !c.write8(addr, uint8(uint32(v)&imm)) {
				c.enterMemFault(pc)
			}
		case 0xCE:
			if !c.write8(addr, uint8(uint32(v)^imm)) {
				c.enterMemFault(pc)
			}
		case 0xCF:
			if !c.write8(addr, uint8(uint32(v)|imm)) {
				c.enterMemFault(pc)
			}
		}
	case 0xC3: // TRAPA #imm
		c.TRA = imm << 2
		c.enterException(excTRAPA, pc+2)
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/chips/sh4/exec_group4.go ====================

package sh4

// execGroup4 handles the 0100 opcode family, the most overloaded
// one: MAC.W, the dynamic shifts SHAD and SHLD, JMP and JSR, TAS.B,
// the unary shifts and rotates, CMP/PZ and CMP/PL, DT, and the whole
// LDC/STC/LDS/STS register-move family (including the .L memory
// forms and the Rn_BANK forms). The low nibble selects the sub
// family; the middle nibble is either a register number (MAC.W,
// SHAD, SHLD) or a system/control register code.

func (c *CPU) execGroup4(op uint16, pc uint32, inDelay bool, n, m int, low uint16) {
	switch low {
	case 0xF: // MAC.W @Rm+,@Rn+
		c.macW(pc, n, m)
		return
	case 0xC: // SHAD Rm,Rn
		c.shad(n, m, true)
		return
	case 0xD: // SHLD Rm,Rn
		c.shad(n, m, false)
		return
	}

	code := uint32(m)

	switch low {
	case 0x2: // STS.L sys,@-Rn, plus STC.L SGR/DBR encodings
		if m == 3 || m == 15 {
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			v := c.SGR
			if m == 15 {
				v = c.DBR
			}
			c.R[n] -= 4
			c.storeSize(pc, c.R[n], v, 2)
			return
		}
		v, ok := c.sysReg(code)
		if !ok {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] -= 4
		c.storeSize(pc, c.R[n], v, 2)
	case 0x3: // STC.L ctrl,@-Rn or STC.L Rm_BANK,@-Rn
		if m >= 8 {
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.R[n] -= 4
			c.storeSize(pc, c.R[n], c.Bank[m&7], 2)
			return
		}
		if ctrlPrivileged(code) && !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
			return
		}
		v, ok := c.ctrlReg(code)
		if !ok {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		c.R[n] -= 4
		c.storeSize(pc, c.R[n], v, 2)
	case 0x6: // LDS.L @Rm+,sys, plus LDC.L SGR/DBR encodings
		if m == 3 || m == 15 {
			// LDC.L @Rm+,SGR and LDC.L @Rm+,DBR: the pointer is
			// the register in bits 11..8 (n in this decode) and
			// the code sits in m, as in the other .L forms.
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			v := c.loadSize(pc, c.R[n], 2)
			if c.excepted {
				return
			}
			c.R[n] += 4
			if m == 3 {
				c.SGR = v
			} else {
				c.DBR = v
			}
			return
		}
		v := c.loadSize(pc, c.R[n], 2)
		if c.excepted {
			return
		}
		c.R[n] += 4
		if !c.setSysReg(code, v) {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	case 0x7: // LDC.L @Rm+,ctrl or LDC.L @Rm+,Rn_BANK
		if m >= 8 {
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			v := c.loadSize(pc, c.R[n], 2)
			if c.excepted {
				return
			}
			c.R[n] += 4
			c.Bank[m&7] = v
			return
		}
		if ctrlPrivileged(code) && !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
			return
		}
		v := c.loadSize(pc, c.R[n], 2)
		if c.excepted {
			return
		}
		c.R[n] += 4
		if !c.setCtrlReg(code, v) {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	case 0xA: // LDS Rm,sys, plus LDC Rm,SGR / LDC Rm,DBR
		switch m {
		case 3:
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.SGR = c.R[n]
		case 15:
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.DBR = c.R[n]
		default:
			if !c.setSysReg(code, c.R[n]) {
				c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			}
		}
	case 0xE: // LDC Rm,ctrl or LDC Rm,Rn_BANK
		if m >= 8 {
			if !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
				return
			}
			c.Bank[m&7] = c.R[n]
			return
		}
		if ctrlPrivileged(code) && !c.needPriv(inDelay, pc) {
			return
		}
		if !c.setCtrlReg(code, c.R[n]) {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	case 0xB:
		switch m {
		case 0x0: // JSR @Rn
			target := c.R[n]
			c.PR = pc + 4
			c.delayedBranch(pc, target, true)
		case 0x1: // TAS.B @Rn
			addr := c.R[n]
			v, ok := c.read8(addr)
			if !ok {
				c.enterMemFault(pc)
				return
			}
			c.setT(boolU32(v == 0))
			if !c.write8(addr, v|0x80) {
				c.enterMemFault(pc)
			}
		case 0x2: // JMP @Rn
			c.delayedBranch(pc, c.R[n], true)
		default:
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
		}
	default:
		c.execShiftUnary(pc, inDelay, n, m, low)
	}
}

// shad implements SHAD (arithmetic) and SHLD (logical): a positive
// Rm shifts Rn left, a negative Rm shifts Rn right, in both cases by
// the magnitude of Rm modulo 32.
func (c *CPU) shad(n, m int, arithmetic bool) {
	cnt := int32(c.R[m])
	if cnt >= 0 {
		c.R[n] <<= uint32(cnt) & 31
		return
	}
	s := uint32(-cnt) & 31
	if arithmetic {
		c.R[n] = uint32(int32(c.R[n]) >> s)
	} else {
		c.R[n] >>= s
	}
}

// execShiftUnary handles the single-register shift, rotate, and test
// instructions of the 0100 family, selected by (code, low) pairs.
func (c *CPU) execShiftUnary(pc uint32, inDelay bool, n, m int, low uint16) {
	v := c.R[n]
	switch {
	case m == 0 && low == 0x0: // SHLL Rn
		c.setT(v >> 31)
		c.R[n] = v << 1
	case m == 0 && low == 0x1: // SHLR Rn
		c.setT(v & 1)
		c.R[n] = v >> 1
	case m == 0 && low == 0x4: // ROTL Rn
		t := v >> 31
		c.R[n] = v<<1 | t
		c.setT(t)
	case m == 0 && low == 0x5: // ROTR Rn
		t := v & 1
		c.R[n] = v>>1 | t<<31
		c.setT(t)
	case m == 0 && low == 0x8: // SHLL2 Rn
		c.R[n] = v << 2
	case m == 0 && low == 0x9: // SHLR2 Rn
		c.R[n] = v >> 2
	case m == 1 && low == 0x0: // DT Rn
		v--
		c.R[n] = v
		c.setT(boolU32(v == 0))
	case m == 1 && low == 0x1: // CMP/PZ Rn
		c.setT(boolU32(int32(v) >= 0))
	case m == 1 && low == 0x5: // CMP/PL Rn
		c.setT(boolU32(int32(v) > 0))
	case m == 1 && low == 0x8: // SHLL8 Rn
		c.R[n] = v << 8
	case m == 1 && low == 0x9: // SHLR8 Rn
		c.R[n] = v >> 8
	case m == 2 && low == 0x0: // SHAL Rn
		c.setT(v >> 31)
		c.R[n] = v << 1
	case m == 2 && low == 0x1: // SHAR Rn
		c.setT(v & 1)
		c.R[n] = uint32(int32(v) >> 1)
	case m == 2 && low == 0x4: // ROTCL Rn
		t := v >> 31
		c.R[n] = v<<1 | c.getT()
		c.setT(t)
	case m == 2 && low == 0x5: // ROTCR Rn
		t := v & 1
		c.R[n] = v>>1 | c.getT()<<31
		c.setT(t)
	case m == 2 && low == 0x8: // SHLL16 Rn
		c.R[n] = v << 16
	case m == 2 && low == 0x9: // SHLR16 Rn
		c.R[n] = v >> 16
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/chips/sh4/fpu.go ====================

package sh4

import "math"

// FPU execution for the 1111 opcode family.
//
// FPSCR.PR selects the precision of the arithmetic instructions:
// PR = 0 operates on the FR singles, PR = 1 on the DR register pairs
// (even numbered pairs of the active bank). FPSCR.SZ selects the
// FMOV transfer size: SZ = 0 moves 32-bit singles, SZ = 1 moves
// 64-bit pairs, whose destination or source is a DR pair of the
// active bank or an XD pair of the inactive bank, selected by the
// low bit of the register field.
//
// Executing any FPU instruction while SR.FD is set raises the FPU
// disabled exception (0x800). Arithmetic follows Go float32 and
// float64 semantics. FIPR and FTRV accumulate in float32, one product
// at a time, in index order.

func f32(bits uint32) float32  { return math.Float32frombits(bits) }
func f32bits(f float32) uint32 { return math.Float32bits(f) }
func f64(bits uint64) float64  { return math.Float64frombits(bits) }

// drBits reads the 64-bit pattern of the DR pair starting at even
// register pair of the given bank (low word first).
func drBits(bank *[16]uint32, pair int) uint64 {
	return uint64(bank[pair&0xE]) | uint64(bank[pair&0xE+1])<<32
}

func setDRBits(bank *[16]uint32, pair int, v uint64) {
	bank[pair&0xE] = uint32(v)
	bank[pair&0xE+1] = uint32(v >> 32)
}

func (c *CPU) getDR(pair int) float64 { return f64(drBits(&c.FR, pair)) }
func (c *CPU) setDR(pair int, v float64) {
	setDRBits(&c.FR, pair, math.Float64bits(v))
}

func (c *CPU) execFPU(op uint16, pc uint32, inDelay bool) {
	if c.SR&srFD != 0 {
		c.enterException(excFPUDisabled, pc)
		return
	}
	// FRCHG and FSCHG are exact opcodes whose bit patterns would
	// otherwise alias FTRV, so they are matched first.
	switch op {
	case 0xFBFD: // FRCHG
		c.setFPSCR(c.FPSCR ^ fpscrFR)
		return
	case 0xF3FD: // FSCHG
		c.setFPSCR(c.FPSCR ^ fpscrSZ)
		return
	}

	n := int(op >> 8 & 0xF)
	m := int(op >> 4 & 0xF)
	low := op & 0xF
	double := c.FPSCR&fpscrPR != 0
	sz := c.FPSCR&fpscrSZ != 0

	switch low {
	case 0x0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x3: // FADD, FSUB, FMUL, FDIV
		if double {
			a, b := c.getDR(n), c.getDR(m)
			var r float64
			switch low {
			case 0x0:
				r = a + b
			case 0x1:
				r = a - b
			case 0x2:
				r = a * b
			case 0x3:
				r = a / b
			}
			c.setDR(n, r)
		} else {
			a, b := f32(c.FR[n]), f32(c.FR[m])
			var r float32
			switch low {
			case 0x0:
				r = a + b
			case 0x1:
				r = a - b
			case 0x2:
				r = a * b
			case 0x3:
				r = a / b
			}
			c.FR[n] = f32bits(r)
		}
	case 0x4, 0x5: // FCMP/EQ, FCMP/GT
		var r bool
		if double {
			a, b := c.getDR(n), c.getDR(m)
			if low == 0x4 {
				r = a == b
			} else {
				r = a > b
			}
		} else {
			a, b := f32(c.FR[n]), f32(c.FR[m])
			if low == 0x4 {
				r = a == b
			} else {
				r = a > b
			}
		}
		c.setT(boolU32(r))
	case 0x6, 0x8, 0x9: // FMOV load forms: @(R0,Rm), @Rm, @Rm+
		var addr uint32
		switch low {
		case 0x6:
			addr = c.R[0] + c.R[m]
		case 0x8, 0x9:
			addr = c.R[m]
		}
		if !c.fmovLoad(pc, addr, n, sz) {
			return
		}
		if low == 0x9 {
			if sz {
				c.R[m] += 8
			} else {
				c.R[m] += 4
			}
		}
	case 0x7, 0xA, 0xB: // FMOV store forms: @(R0,Rn), @Rn, @-Rn
		var addr uint32
		size := uint32(4)
		if sz {
			size = 8
		}
		switch low {
		case 0x7:
			addr = c.R[0] + c.R[n]
		case 0xA:
			addr = c.R[n]
		case 0xB:
			addr = c.R[n] - size
			c.R[n] = addr
		}
		c.fmovStore(pc, addr, m, sz)
	case 0xC: // FMOV register to register
		if !sz {
			c.FR[n] = c.FR[m]
		} else {
			var v uint64
			if m&1 != 0 {
				v = drBits(&c.XFR, m)
			} else {
				v = drBits(&c.FR, m)
			}
			if n&1 != 0 {
				setDRBits(&c.XFR, n, v)
			} else {
				setDRBits(&c.FR, n, v)
			}
		}
	case 0xE: // FMAC FR0,FRm,FRn (single precision only)
		if double {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		c.FR[n] = f32bits(f32(c.FR[0])*f32(c.FR[m]) + f32(c.FR[n]))
	case 0xD:
		c.execFPUSpecial(op, pc, inDelay, n, double)
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}

// fmovLoad loads one FMOV operand from addr into the destination
// selected by the register field n and the SZ bit.
func (c *CPU) fmovLoad(pc uint32, addr uint32, n int, sz bool) bool {
	if !sz {
		v, ok := c.read32(addr)
		if !ok {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
			return false
		}
		c.FR[n] = v
		return true
	}
	v, ok := c.read64(addr)
	if !ok {
		c.enterMemFault(pc)
		return false
	}
	if n&1 != 0 {
		setDRBits(&c.XFR, n, v)
	} else {
		setDRBits(&c.FR, n, v)
	}
	return true
}

// fmovStore stores one FMOV operand from the source selected by the
// register field m and the SZ bit to addr.
func (c *CPU) fmovStore(pc uint32, addr uint32, m int, sz bool) {
	if !sz {
		if !c.write32(addr, c.FR[m]) {
			c.enterMemFault(pc)
		}
		return
	}
	var v uint64
	if m&1 != 0 {
		v = drBits(&c.XFR, m)
	} else {
		v = drBits(&c.FR, m)
	}
	if !c.write64(addr, v) {
		c.enterMemFault(pc)
	}
}

// execFPUSpecial handles the 1101 low-nibble family, selected by
// bits 7..4: moves to and from FPUL, conversions, unary operations,
// the conversion pair FCNVSD and FCNVDS, and the graphics operations
// FIPR and FTRV.
func (c *CPU) execFPUSpecial(op uint16, pc uint32, inDelay bool, n int, double bool) {
	sub := int(op >> 4 & 0xF)
	switch sub {
	case 0x0: // FSTS FPUL,FRn
		c.FR[n] = c.FPUL
	case 0x1: // FLDS FRm,FPUL (register field in bits 11..8)
		c.FPUL = c.FR[n]
	case 0x2: // FLOAT FPUL,FRn or FPUL,DRn
		v := float64(int32(c.FPUL))
		if double {
			c.setDR(n, v)
		} else {
			c.FR[n] = f32bits(float32(v))
		}
	case 0x3: // FTRC FRm,FPUL or DRm,FPUL
		var v float64
		if double {
			v = c.getDR(n)
		} else {
			v = float64(f32(c.FR[n]))
		}
		c.FPUL = ftrc(v)
	case 0x4: // FNEG
		if double {
			c.FR[(n&0xE)+1] ^= 0x80000000
		} else {
			c.FR[n] ^= 0x80000000
		}
	case 0x5: // FABS
		if double {
			c.FR[(n&0xE)+1] &= 0x7FFFFFFF
		} else {
			c.FR[n] &= 0x7FFFFFFF
		}
	case 0x6: // FSQRT
		if double {
			c.setDR(n, math.Sqrt(c.getDR(n)))
		} else {
			c.FR[n] = f32bits(float32(math.Sqrt(float64(f32(c.FR[n])))))
		}
	case 0x7: // FSRRA FRn: reciprocal square root approximation,
		// computed exactly here as float32(1/sqrt(x)) via float64
		if double {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		x := float64(f32(c.FR[n]))
		c.FR[n] = f32bits(float32(1 / math.Sqrt(x)))
	case 0x8: // FLDI0 FRn
		c.FR[n] = 0
	case 0x9: // FLDI1 FRn
		c.FR[n] = 0x3F800000
	case 0xA: // FCNVSD FPUL,DRn
		c.setDR(n, float64(f32(c.FPUL)))
	case 0xB: // FCNVDS DRm,FPUL
		c.FPUL = f32bits(float32(c.getDR(n)))
	case 0xE: // FIPR FVm,FVn
		nn := int(op >> 10 & 3)
		mm := int(op >> 8 & 3)
		var a, b [4]float32
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			a[i] = f32(c.FR[mm*4+i])
			b[i] = f32(c.FR[nn*4+i])
		}
		var dot float32
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			dot += a[i] * b[i]
		}
		c.FR[nn*4+3] = f32bits(dot)
	case 0xF: // FTRV XMTRX,FVn
		if int(op>>8&3) != 1 {
			c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
			return
		}
		nn := int(op >> 10 & 3)
		var in [4]float32
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			in[i] = f32(c.FR[nn*4+i])
		}
		// The transform matrix is the inactive bank read as
		// XMTRX in row-major order: element (row, col) is
		// XFR[row*4+col], and out[row] = sum over col of
		// matrix[row][col] * in[col], accumulated in float32.
		for row := 0; row < 4; row++ {
			var acc float32
			for col := 0; col < 4; col++ {
				acc += f32(c.XFR[row*4+col]) * in[col]
			}
			c.FR[nn*4+row] = f32bits(acc)
		}
	default:
		c.illegal(inDelay, pc)
	}
}

// ftrc converts a floating-point value to a signed 32-bit integer
// with truncation toward zero, saturating to the int32 range. NaN
// converts to the negative limit, matching the hardware behavior
// for invalid inputs.
func ftrc(v float64) uint32 {
	if math.IsNaN(v) || v < -2147483648.0 {
		return 0x80000000
	}
	if v >= 2147483648.0 {
		return 0x7FFFFFFF
	}
	return uint32(int32(v))
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/chips/sh4/sh4.go ====================

// Package sh4 implements a from-scratch SH-4 CPU core: the complete
// integer instruction set, the SH-4 FPU (single and double precision,
// including the graphics operations FIPR and FTRV), and a functional
// MMU built around a 64-entry unified TLB.
//
// The implementation is a plain interpreter. Step executes exactly one
// instruction (including correct delay-slot semantics) and always
// reports a cost of 1 cycle; this is a functional model, not a timing
// model.
//
// Simplifications, all documented at the point of use:
//   - No caches are simulated, so the cache instructions (PREF, OCBI,
//     OCBP, OCBWB, MOVCA.L) are architectural no-ops apart from the
//     MOVCA.L store itself.
//   - FPU arithmetic uses Go float32/float64 arithmetic (IEEE round to
//     nearest). FSRRA is computed as 1/sqrt(x) in float64 and rounded
//     to float32 rather than using the hardware approximation table.
//     FIPR and FTRV accumulate in float32, term by term, in index order.
//   - Interrupts follow the SH-4 manual model (DC-2): a request is
//     latched with its level and accepted at an instruction boundary
//     only when SR.BL is clear, the CPU is not in a delay slot, and
//     the level exceeds SR.IMASK. Exceptions are still taken
//     immediately even when SR.BL is set; the manual warns that a
//     general exception raised while BL is set can deadlock the
//     hardware, and real boot code never does this, so vectoring is
//     the safe emulation choice.
package sh4

import "encoding/binary"

// PhysicalMemory is the byte-addressed physical memory the CPU talks
// to after address translation. All accesses are little endian.
type PhysicalMemory interface {
	Read8(pa uint32) uint8
	Read16(pa uint32) uint16
	Read32(pa uint32) uint32
	Read64(pa uint32) uint64
	Write8(pa uint32, v uint8)
	Write16(pa uint32, v uint16)
	Write32(pa uint32, v uint32)
	Write64(pa uint32, v uint64)
}

// TLBEntry is one unified TLB entry. VPN stores the virtual page base
// (the full virtual address masked down to the page size), and PPN
// stores the physical page base, already page aligned. Size selects
// the page size: 0 = 1KB, 1 = 4KB, 2 = 64KB, 3 = 1MB. PR holds the
// protection field: bit0 (value 1) means writable, bit1 (value 2)
// means accessible from user mode. D is the dirty bit: a write to a
// valid, writable, but clean page raises the initial page write
// exception. SH is the shared-page flag (recorded, not acted on).
type TLBEntry struct {
	VPN  uint32
	PPN  uint32
	Size int
	V    bool
	PR   int
	D    bool
	SH   bool
}

// SR bit positions.
const (
	srT     = 1 << 0
	srS     = 1 << 1
	srIMASK = 0xF << 4
	srQ     = 1 << 8
	srM     = 1 << 9
	srFD    = 1 << 15
	srBL    = 1 << 28
	srRB    = 1 << 29
	srMD    = 1 << 30
)

// FPSCR bit positions.
const (
	fpscrFR = 1 << 21
	fpscrSZ = 1 << 20
	fpscrPR = 1 << 19
)

// Exception event codes stored in EXPEVT.
const (
	excTLBMissRead  = 0x040
	excTLBMissWrite = 0x060
	excInitialWrite = 0x080
	excProtRead     = 0x0A0
	excProtWrite    = 0x0C0
	excAddrErrRead  = 0x0E0
	excAddrErrWrite = 0x100
	excFPU          = 0x120
	excTRAPA        = 0x160
	excIllegal      = 0x180
	excSlotIllegal  = 0x1A0
	excFPUDisabled  = 0x800
)

// CPU is the complete architectural state of the SH-4 core.
//
// R is the active general-register view. R0 to R7 exist in two banks;
// Bank holds the inactive bank's R0 to R7. When the CPU is privileged
// (SR.MD = 1) and SR.RB = 1, bank 1 is active and R shows bank 1 while
// Bank holds bank 0; in every other mode R shows bank 0. The two are
// swapped whenever the active bank changes (LDC to SR, RTE, exception
// entry), so R always reflects architectural state at instruction
// boundaries.
//
// FR is the active floating-point register bank selected by
// FPSCR.FR; XFR is the inactive bank.
type CPU struct {
	R    [16]uint32
	Bank [8]uint32

	PC, PR, SR, GBR, VBR, SSR, SPC, SGR, DBR uint32

	MACH, MACL uint32

	FPUL  uint32
	FPSCR uint32
	FR    [16]uint32
	XFR   [16]uint32

	MMUCR, PTEH, PTEL, PTEA, TTB, TEA uint32

	EXPEVT, INTEVT, TRA, TTR uint32

	UTLB [64]TLBEntry

	Halted bool

	mem PhysicalMemory

	urc        int    // UTLB replacement counter for LDTLB
	inDelay    bool   // next instruction is a delay slot
	afterDelay uint32 // PC to continue at after the delay slot
	excepted   bool   // an exception was taken during exec

	pendCode  uint32 // INTEVT code of the latched interrupt request
	pendLevel int    // priority level of the latched request, 0 to 15
	pendValid bool   // an interrupt request is latched and unaccepted
}

// New creates a CPU attached to mem and resets it.
func New(mem PhysicalMemory) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{mem: mem}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Reset restores the power-on state: PC = 0xA0000000,
// SR = 0x700080F0 (MD, RB, BL, FD set, interrupt mask 15), VBR = 0,
// FPSCR = 0x00040001 (the documented SH-4
// power-on values), all other registers and the TLB zeroed, MMU
// address translation off, and the CPU running (not halted).
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	mem := c.mem
	*c = CPU{mem: mem}
	c.PC = 0xA0000000
	c.SR = 0x700080F0
	c.FPSCR = 0x00040001
}

// Run executes instructions until the cycle budget is consumed. Each
// Step costs exactly 1 in this functional model.
func (c *CPU) Run(cycles int) {
	for i := 0; i < cycles; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
}

// Step executes exactly one instruction, or takes the exception that
// the instruction raises, and returns 1. Before the fetch, a latched
// interrupt request is accepted when the manual's conditions hold:
// SR.BL clear, the next instruction is not a delay slot (acceptance
// between a branch and its delay slot would lose the branch target),
// and the request level exceeds SR.IMASK. Acceptance wakes a halted
// CPU. A halted CPU (after SLEEP) with no acceptable interrupt
// returns 1 without executing anything.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	if c.mem == nil {
		return 1
	}
	if c.pendValid && !c.inDelay && c.SR&srBL == 0 &&
		c.pendLevel > int((c.SR&srIMASK)>>4) {
		code := c.pendCode
		c.pendValid = false
		c.INTEVT = code
		c.SSR = c.SR
		c.SPC = c.PC
		c.SGR = c.R[15]
		c.setSR(c.SR | srMD | srRB | srBL)
		c.PC = c.VBR + 0x600
		c.Halted = false
		return 1
	}
	if c.Halted {
		return 1
	}
	pc := c.PC
	c.excepted = false
	op, ok := c.read16(pc)
	if !ok {
		c.enterMemFault(pc)
		return 1
	}
	wasDelay := c.inDelay
	after := c.afterDelay
	c.inDelay = false
	if wasDelay && isDelaySlotForbidden(op) {
		c.enterException(excSlotIllegal, pc)
		return 1
	}
	c.exec(op, pc, wasDelay)
	if c.excepted {
		return 1
	}
	if wasDelay {
		c.PC = after
	}
	return 1
}

// isDelaySlotForbidden reports whether op belongs to the class of
// instructions that may not occupy a delay slot: anything that can
// modify the PC (branches, jumps, returns, RTE) plus TRAPA.
func isDelaySlotForbidden(op uint16) bool {
	switch op >> 12 {
	case 0xA, 0xB: // BRA, BSR
		return true
	case 0x8:
		switch op >> 8 {
		case 0x89, 0x8B, 0x8D, 0x8F: // BT, BF, BT/S, BF/S
			return true
		}
	case 0xC:
		if op>>8 == 0xC3 { // TRAPA
			return true
		}
	case 0x0:
		low := op & 0xF
		mid := (op >> 4) & 0xF
		if low == 0x3 && (mid == 0x0 || mid == 0x2) { // BSRF, BRAF
			return true
		}
		if op == 0x000B || op == 0x002B { // RTS, RTE
			return true
		}
	case 0x4:
		if op&0xF == 0xB {
			mid := (op >> 4) & 0xF
			if mid == 0x0 || mid == 0x2 { // JSR, JMP
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Register bank and flag helpers

// bank1Active reports whether bank 1 is the active R0 to R7 bank,
// which is exactly when the CPU is privileged and SR.RB is set.
func (c *CPU) bank1Active() bool {
	return c.SR&srMD != 0 && c.SR&srRB != 0
}

func (c *CPU) swapBanks() {
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		c.R[i], c.Bank[i] = c.Bank[i], c.R[i]
	}
}

// setSR stores a new SR value, swapping the R0 to R7 banks if the
// active bank changes as a result.
func (c *CPU) setSR(v uint32) {
	old := c.bank1Active()
	c.SR = v
	if c.bank1Active() != old {
		c.swapBanks()
	}
}

// setFPSCR stores a new FPSCR value, swapping the FPU register banks
// if FPSCR.FR changes.
func (c *CPU) setFPSCR(v uint32) {
	old := c.FPSCR & fpscrFR
	c.FPSCR = v
	if v&fpscrFR != old {
		c.FR, c.XFR = c.XFR, c.FR
	}
}

func (c *CPU) getT() uint32 {
	if c.SR&srT != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

func (c *CPU) setT(v uint32) {
	if v&1 != 0 {
		c.SR |= srT
	} else {
		c.SR &^= srT
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setS(v uint32) {
	if v&1 != 0 {
		c.SR |= srS
	} else {
		c.SR &^= srS
	}
}

func (c *CPU) getQ() uint32 {
	if c.SR&srQ != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

func (c *CPU) getM() uint32 {
	if c.SR&srM != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

func (c *CPU) setQM(q, m uint32) {
	c.SR &^= srQ | srM
	if q&1 != 0 {
		c.SR |= srQ
	}
	if m&1 != 0 {
		c.SR |= srM
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Exceptions

// enterException performs the standard SH-4 exception sequence: the
// current SR, return PC, and R15 are saved to SSR, SPC, and SGR,
// SR.MD, SR.RB, and SR.BL are set (swapping register banks if that
// changes the active bank), and control transfers to VBR+0x100, or
// VBR+0x600 for TLB miss exceptions.
func (c *CPU) enterException(code uint32, returnPC uint32) {
	c.EXPEVT = code
	c.SSR = c.SR
	c.SPC = returnPC
	c.SGR = c.R[15]
	c.setSR(c.SR | srMD | srRB | srBL)
	off := uint32(0x100)
	if code == excTLBMissRead || code == excTLBMissWrite {
		off = 0x600
	}
	c.PC = c.VBR + off
	c.inDelay = false
	c.excepted = true
}

// enterMemFault vectors the translation fault that TranslateVA just
// recorded in EXPEVT and TEA.
func (c *CPU) enterMemFault(returnPC uint32) {
	c.enterException(c.EXPEVT, returnPC)
}

// illegal raises the general illegal instruction exception, or the
// slot illegal instruction exception when the opcode sits in a delay
// slot.
func (c *CPU) illegal(inDelay bool, pc uint32) {
	if inDelay {
		c.enterException(excSlotIllegal, pc)
	} else {
		c.enterException(excIllegal, pc)
	}
}

// RaiseInterrupt presents an interrupt request with the given
// INTEVT code and priority level (0 to 15). The request is latched,
// not taken: Step accepts it at an instruction boundary once SR.BL
// is clear and the level exceeds SR.IMASK, performing the standard
// register save (SSR, SPC, SGR), setting MD, RB, and BL, and
// vectoring to VBR+0x600 with INTEVT holding the code. When a request
// is already latched, the higher level wins; at equal level the
// earlier request is kept. EXPEVT is not touched: interrupts report
// through INTEVT.
func (c *CPU) RaiseInterrupt(code uint32, level int) {
	if level < 0 {
		level = 0
	}
	if level > 15 {
		level = 15
	}
	if c.pendValid && level <= c.pendLevel {
		return
	}
	c.pendCode = code
	c.pendLevel = level
	c.pendValid = true
}

// WithdrawInterrupt drops the latched interrupt request, if any.
// The interrupt controller calls this when its winning source is
// acknowledged before the CPU accepted the request.
func (c *CPU) WithdrawInterrupt() {
	c.pendValid = false
}

// PendingInterrupt reports the latched interrupt request, for save
// states and tests.
func (c *CPU) PendingInterrupt() (code uint32, level int, valid bool) {
	return c.pendCode, c.pendLevel, c.pendValid
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// MMU

// pageMask returns the address mask for a TLB page-size code:
// bits above the page offset are set.
func pageMask(size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 0:
		return ^uint32(0x3FF) // 1KB
	case 1:
		return ^uint32(0xFFF) // 4KB
	case 2:
		return ^uint32(0xFFFF) // 64KB
	default:
		return ^uint32(0xFFFFF) // 1MB
	}
}

// TranslateVA translates a virtual address to a physical address.
//
// The P1 (0x80000000-0x9FFFFFFF), P2 (0xA0000000-0xBFFFFFFF), and P4
// (0xE0000000-0xFFFFFFFF) areas are never translated. The P0
// (0x00000000-0x7FFFFFFF) and P3 (0xC0000000-0xDFFFFFFF) areas go
// through the UTLB when MMUCR.AT is 1, and map directly
// (pa = va & 0x1FFFFFFF) when it is 0. User mode (SR.MD = 0) may only
// access P0; touching any other area is an address error even when
// translation is off.
//
// On a fault TranslateVA returns ok = false and records the fault in
// TEA and EXPEVT (TLB miss, TLB protection, initial page write, or
// address error, using the read or write variant selected by
// isWrite). It does not vector the CPU; instruction execution does
// that through enterMemFault so tests can inspect the recorded state.
func (c *CPU) TranslateVA(va uint32, isWrite bool) (uint32, bool) {
	fail := func(code uint32) (uint32, bool) {
		c.TEA = va
		c.EXPEVT = code
		return 0, false
	}
	if c.SR&srMD == 0 && va >= 0x80000000 {
		if isWrite {
			return fail(excAddrErrWrite)
		}
		return fail(excAddrErrRead)
	}
	if c.MMUCR&1 == 0 {
		return va & 0x1FFFFFFF, true
	}
	switch va >> 29 {
	case 4, 5, 7: // P1, P2, P4: never translated
		return va & 0x1FFFFFFF, true
	}
	// P0 or P3: UTLB lookup. The first entry whose masked VPN matches
	// is the candidate, whether or not it is valid.
	for i := range c.UTLB {
		e := &c.UTLB[i]
		mask := pageMask(e.Size)
		if va&mask != e.VPN&mask {
			continue
		}
		if !e.V {
			if isWrite {
				return fail(excTLBMissWrite)
			}
			return fail(excTLBMissRead)
		}
		if c.SR&srMD == 0 && e.PR&2 == 0 {
			if isWrite {
				return fail(excProtWrite)
			}
			return fail(excProtRead)
		}
		if isWrite && e.PR&1 == 0 {
			return fail(excProtWrite)
		}
		if isWrite && !e.D {
			return fail(excInitialWrite)
		}
		return e.PPN&mask | va&^mask, true
	}
	if isWrite {
		return fail(excTLBMissWrite)
	}
	return fail(excTLBMissRead)
}

// loadTLB implements LDTLB: the UTLB entry at the replacement counter
// is loaded from PTEH, PTEL, and PTEA, and the counter advances
// modulo 64. The PTEL layout used here (a documented simplification
// of the hardware layout) is: PPN = PTEL & 0xFFFFFC00, V = bit 8,
// PR = bits 6..5, SZ = bits 4..3 (0 = 1KB, 1 = 4KB, 2 = 64KB,
// 3 = 1MB), D = bit 2 (the manual's bit 9 and bit 1 positions are
// also honored), SH = bit 0 (bit 1 also honored). The VPN comes from
// PTEH masked to the page size; the ASID in PTEH is ignored. PTEA is
// not needed at these page sizes and is ignored.
func (c *CPU) loadTLB() {
	sz := int(c.PTEL >> 3 & 3)
	mask := pageMask(sz)
	e := TLBEntry{
		VPN:  c.PTEH & mask,
		PPN:  c.PTEL & 0xFFFFFC00 & mask,
		Size: sz,
		V:    c.PTEL&(1<<8) != 0,
		PR:   int(c.PTEL >> 5 & 3),
		D:    c.PTEL&(1<<9|1<<2|1<<1) != 0,
		SH:   c.PTEL&(1<<1|1<<0) != 0,
	}
	c.UTLB[c.urc&63] = e
	c.urc = (c.urc + 1) & 63
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Memory accessors used by instruction execution. Each returns
// ok = false after recording the fault in TEA and EXPEVT (through
// TranslateVA or the alignment check); the caller vectors the fault
// with enterMemFault. Word, longword, and quadword accesses must be
// naturally aligned; a misaligned access is an address error.

func (c *CPU) addrErr(va uint32, isWrite bool) {
	c.TEA = va
	if isWrite {
		c.EXPEVT = excAddrErrWrite
	} else {
		c.EXPEVT = excAddrErrRead
	}
}

func (c *CPU) read8(va uint32) (uint8, bool) {
	pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(va, false)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	return c.mem.Read8(pa), true
}

func (c *CPU) read16(va uint32) (uint16, bool) {
	if va&1 != 0 {
		c.addrErr(va, false)
		return 0, false
	}
	pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(va, false)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	return c.mem.Read16(pa), true
}

func (c *CPU) read32(va uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	if va&3 != 0 {
		c.addrErr(va, false)
		return 0, false
	}
	pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(va, false)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	return c.mem.Read32(pa), true
}

// read64 reads a quadword as two longwords so that the alignment
// requirement is 4 bytes, matching how FMOV double transfers are
// used in practice.
func (c *CPU) read64(va uint32) (uint64, bool) {
	lo, ok := c.read32(va)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	hi, ok := c.read32(va + 4)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	return uint64(hi)<<32 | uint64(lo), true
}

func (c *CPU) write8(va uint32, v uint8) bool {
	pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(va, true)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	c.mem.Write8(pa, v)
	return true
}

func (c *CPU) write16(va uint32, v uint16) bool {
	if va&1 != 0 {
		c.addrErr(va, true)
		return false
	}
	pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(va, true)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	c.mem.Write16(pa, v)
	return true
}

func (c *CPU) write32(va uint32, v uint32) bool {
	if va&3 != 0 {
		c.addrErr(va, true)
		return false
	}
	pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(va, true)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	c.mem.Write32(pa, v)
	return true
}

func (c *CPU) write64(va uint32, v uint64) bool {
	if !c.write32(va, uint32(v)) {
		return false
	}
	return c.write32(va+4, uint32(v>>32))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Serialization
//
// Fixed little-endian layout, SerializeSize bytes total:
//
//	0     R[16]                       64
//	64    Bank[8]                     32
//	96    PC,PR,SR,GBR,VBR,SSR,SPC,SGR,DBR   36
//	132   MACH,MACL                   8
//	140   FPUL,FPSCR                  8
//	148   FR[16]                      64
//	212   XFR[16]                     64
//	276   MMUCR,PTEH,PTEL,PTEA,TTB,TEA  24
//	300   EXPEVT,INTEVT,TRA,TTR       16
//	316   UTLB[64], 20 bytes each     1280
//	      (VPN, PPN, Size, PR, flag byte: bit0 V, bit1 D, bit2 SH)
//	1596  Halted byte + padding       4
//	1600  LDTLB replacement counter   4
//	1604  inDelay byte + padding      4
//	1608  afterDelay                  4
//	1612  pending interrupt code      4
//	1616  pending interrupt word      4  (bit0 valid, bits 7:4 level)

// SerializeSize is the exact length of a serialized CPU state.
const SerializeSize = 1620

// Serialize writes the full CPU state to a fresh byte slice of
// SerializeSize bytes.
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	b := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	put := func(off int, v uint32) { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[off:], v) }
	off := 0
	for _, v := range c.R {
		put(off, v)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, v := range c.Bank {
		put(off, v)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, v := range []uint32{c.PC, c.PR, c.SR, c.GBR, c.VBR, c.SSR, c.SPC, c.SGR, c.DBR} {
		put(off, v)
		off += 4
	}
	put(off, c.MACH)
	put(off+4, c.MACL)
	off += 8
	put(off, c.FPUL)
	put(off+4, c.FPSCR)
	off += 8
	for _, v := range c.FR {
		put(off, v)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, v := range c.XFR {
		put(off, v)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, v := range []uint32{c.MMUCR, c.PTEH, c.PTEL, c.PTEA, c.TTB, c.TEA} {
		put(off, v)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, v := range []uint32{c.EXPEVT, c.INTEVT, c.TRA, c.TTR} {
		put(off, v)
		off += 4
	}
	for i := range c.UTLB {
		e := &c.UTLB[i]
		put(off, e.VPN)
		put(off+4, e.PPN)
		put(off+8, uint32(e.Size))
		put(off+12, uint32(e.PR))
		var flags byte
		if e.V {
			flags |= 1
		}
		if e.D {
			flags |= 2
		}
		if e.SH {
			flags |= 4
		}
		b[off+16] = flags
		off += 20
	}
	if c.Halted {
		b[off] = 1
	}
	off += 4
	put(off, uint32(c.urc))
	off += 4
	if c.inDelay {
		b[off] = 1
	}
	off += 4
	put(off, c.afterDelay)
	off += 4
	put(off, c.pendCode)
	var pw uint32
	if c.pendValid {
		pw = 1
	}
	pw |= uint32(c.pendLevel&0xF) << 4
	put(off+4, pw)
	return b
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize. The length
// must match SerializeSize exactly; on a mismatch the CPU is left
// untouched and false is returned. Register banks and FPSCR are
// stored as active/inactive views, so they are restored verbatim
// with no bank swapping.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(b []byte) bool {
	if len(b) != SerializeSize {
		return false
	}
	get := func(off int) uint32 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off:]) }
	off := 0
	for i := range c.R {
		c.R[i] = get(off)
		off += 4
	}
	for i := range c.Bank {
		c.Bank[i] = get(off)
		off += 4
	}
	regs := []*uint32{&c.PC, &c.PR, &c.SR, &c.GBR, &c.VBR, &c.SSR, &c.SPC, &c.SGR, &c.DBR}
	for _, p := range regs {
		*p = get(off)
		off += 4
	}
	c.MACH = get(off)
	c.MACL = get(off + 4)
	off += 8
	c.FPUL = get(off)
	c.FPSCR = get(off + 4)
	off += 8
	for i := range c.FR {
		c.FR[i] = get(off)
		off += 4
	}
	for i := range c.XFR {
		c.XFR[i] = get(off)
		off += 4
	}
	mmu := []*uint32{&c.MMUCR, &c.PTEH, &c.PTEL, &c.PTEA, &c.TTB, &c.TEA}
	for _, p := range mmu {
		*p = get(off)
		off += 4
	}
	evt := []*uint32{&c.EXPEVT, &c.INTEVT, &c.TRA, &c.TTR}
	for _, p := range evt {
		*p = get(off)
		off += 4
	}
	for i := range c.UTLB {
		e := &c.UTLB[i]
		e.VPN = get(off)
		e.PPN = get(off + 4)
		e.Size = int(get(off + 8))
		e.PR = int(get(off + 12))
		flags := b[off+16]
		e.V = flags&1 != 0
		e.D = flags&2 != 0
		e.SH = flags&4 != 0
		off += 20
	}
	c.Halted = b[off] != 0
	off += 4
	c.urc = int(get(off))
	off += 4
	c.inDelay = b[off] != 0
	off += 4
	c.afterDelay = get(off)
	off += 4
	c.pendCode = get(off)
	pw := get(off + 4)
	c.pendValid = pw&1 != 0
	c.pendLevel = int((pw >> 4) & 0xF)
	return true
}
