package sh4

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// testMem is a flat 32MB physical memory for tests. Physical
// addresses are masked into the array, so the P2 window
// 0xA0000000 maps to offset 0.
type testMem struct {
	data []byte
}

const testMemSize = 32 * 1024 * 1024

func newTestMem() *testMem { return &testMem{data: make([]byte, testMemSize)} }

func (m *testMem) off(pa uint32, size uint32) int {
	return int(pa&(testMemSize-1)) &^ int(size-1)
}

func (m *testMem) Read8(pa uint32) uint8 { return m.data[m.off(pa, 1)] }
func (m *testMem) Read16(pa uint32) uint16 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(m.data[m.off(pa, 2):])
}
func (m *testMem) Read32(pa uint32) uint32 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(m.data[m.off(pa, 4):])
}
func (m *testMem) Read64(pa uint32) uint64 {
	return uint64(m.Read32(pa)) | uint64(m.Read32(pa+4))<<32
}
func (m *testMem) Write8(pa uint32, v uint8) { m.data[m.off(pa, 1)] = v }
func (m *testMem) Write16(pa uint32, v uint16) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(m.data[m.off(pa, 2):], v)
}
func (m *testMem) Write32(pa uint32, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(m.data[m.off(pa, 4):], v)
}
func (m *testMem) Write64(pa uint32, v uint64) {
	m.Write32(pa, uint32(v))
	m.Write32(pa+4, uint32(v>>32))
}

const codeBase = 0xA0000000

func newTestCPU() (*CPU, *testMem) {
	mem := newTestMem()
	c := New(mem)
	// The power-on state (SR = 0x700080F0: bank 1, exceptions
	// blocked, FPU disabled) is what boot ROM code runs in; it
	// clears BL, selects bank 0, and enables the FPU before any
	// game code runs. Tests emulate that post-boot environment.
	// TestResetState constructs its CPU with New directly to
	// pin the raw power-on values.
	c.SR = 0x400000F0
	return c, mem
}

// execOne writes one instruction at the CPU's current PC and steps
// once. Used for single-instruction unit tests.
func execOne(c *CPU, mem *testMem, op uint16) {
	mem.Write16(c.PC&0x1FFFFFFF, op)
	c.Step()
}

// loadProg writes a program at va and points the CPU at it.
func loadProg(c *CPU, mem *testMem, va uint32, words ...uint16) {
	for i, w := range words {
		mem.Write16((va+uint32(2*i))&0x1FFFFFFF, w)
	}
	c.PC = va
}

func stepN(c *CPU, n int) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
}

// Small assembler helpers. Register fields: n is the destination
// register (bits 11..8), m the source register (bits 7..4).
func ins3(base uint16, n, m int, low uint16) uint16 {
	return base | uint16(n)<<8 | uint16(m)<<4 | low
}
func movImm(rn int, imm int) uint16 { return 0xE000 | uint16(rn)<<8 | uint16(uint8(imm)) }
func addImm(rn int, imm int) uint16 { return 0x7000 | uint16(rn)<<8 | uint16(uint8(imm)) }

func TestResetState(t *testing.T) {
	c := New(newTestMem())
	if c.PC != 0xA0000000 {
		t.Errorf("PC = %#x, want 0xA0000000", c.PC)
	}
	if c.SR != 0x700080F0 {
		t.Errorf("SR = %#x, want 0x700080F0", c.SR)
	}
	if c.FPSCR != 0x00040001 {
		t.Errorf("FPSCR = %#x, want 0x00040001", c.FPSCR)
	}
	if c.VBR != 0 || c.MMUCR != 0 || c.Halted {
		t.Errorf("VBR=%#x MMUCR=%#x Halted=%v, want 0, 0, false", c.VBR, c.MMUCR, c.Halted)
	}
	for i, v := range c.R {
		if v != 0 {
			t.Errorf("R%d = %#x after reset, want 0", i, v)
		}
	}
}

func TestArithmeticFlags(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()

	// ADDC chain: 0xFFFFFFFF + 1 with T=0 gives 0 and carry out.
	c.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	c.R[1] = 1
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0008) // CLRT
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 0, 1, 0xE))
	if c.R[0] != 0 || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("ADDC: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0 and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// The carry feeds the next ADDC: 0x20 + 0x10 + 1 = 0x31, T=0.
	c.R[2] = 0x10
	c.R[3] = 0x20
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 3, 2, 0xE))
	if c.R[3] != 0x31 || c.getT() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ADDC chain: R3=%#x T=%d, want 0x31 and 0", c.R[3], c.getT())
	}
	// SUBC chain: 0 - 1 with T=0 borrows.
	c.R[0] = 0
	c.R[1] = 1
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0008) // CLRT
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 0, 1, 0xA))
	if c.R[0] != 0xFFFFFFFF || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("SUBC: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0xFFFFFFFF and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// 3 - 5 - borrow(1) = -3, still borrowing.
	c.R[2] = 5
	c.R[3] = 3
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 3, 2, 0xA))
	if c.R[3] != 0xFFFFFFFD || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("SUBC chain: R3=%#x T=%d, want 0xFFFFFFFD and 1", c.R[3], c.getT())
	}
	// ADDV signed overflow.
	c.R[0] = 0x7FFFFFFF
	c.R[1] = 1
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 0, 1, 0xF))
	if c.R[0] != 0x80000000 || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("ADDV: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0x80000000 and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// SUBV signed overflow: -2^31 - 1 wraps and sets T.
	c.R[0] = 0x80000000
	c.R[1] = 1
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 0, 1, 0xB))
	if c.R[0] != 0x7FFFFFFF || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("SUBV: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0x7FFFFFFF and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// SHLL shifts the top bit into T; SHLR the bottom bit.
	c.R[0] = 0x80000000
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4000) // SHLL R0
	if c.R[0] != 0 || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("SHLL: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0 and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	c.R[0] = 1
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4001) // SHLR R0
	if c.R[0] != 0 || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("SHLR: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0 and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// SHAR keeps the sign.
	c.R[0] = 0x80000001
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4021) // SHAR R0
	if c.R[0] != 0xC0000000 || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("SHAR: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0xC0000000 and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// ROTCL rotates through T: with T=1, 0x80000000 becomes 1, T=1.
	c.R[0] = 0x80000000
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0018) // SETT
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4024) // ROTCL R0
	if c.R[0] != 1 || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("ROTCL: R0=%#x T=%d, want 1 and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// CMP/STR sets T when any byte position matches.
	c.R[0] = 0x11223344
	c.R[1] = 0x99003377
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x2000, 0, 1, 0xC))
	if c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("CMP/STR: T=%d, want 1", c.getT())
	}
	c.R[1] = 0x55667788
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x2000, 0, 1, 0xC))
	if c.getT() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("CMP/STR no match: T=%d, want 0", c.getT())
	}
	// XTRCT takes the middle 32 bits of Rm:Rn.
	c.R[0] = 0xAABBCCDD
	c.R[1] = 0x11223344
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x2000, 0, 1, 0xD))
	if c.R[0] != 0x3344AABB {
		t.Errorf("XTRCT: R0=%#x, want 0x3344AABB", c.R[0])
	}
	// NEGC: 0 - 5 - T(0) = -5 with borrow; then with T=1 gives -6.
	c.R[1] = 5
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0008) // CLRT
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x6000, 0, 1, 0xA))
	if c.R[0] != 0xFFFFFFFB || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("NEGC: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0xFFFFFFFB and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// DT decrements and sets T at zero.
	c.R[0] = 1
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4010) // DT R0
	if c.R[0] != 0 || c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("DT: R0=%#x T=%d, want 0 and 1", c.R[0], c.getT())
	}
	// SHAD by a negative count shifts right arithmetically.
	c.R[0] = 0x80000000
	c.R[1] = 0xFFFFFFFF // -1
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x4000, 0, 1, 0xC))
	if c.R[0] != 0xC0000000 {
		t.Errorf("SHAD -1: R0=%#x, want 0xC0000000", c.R[0])
	}
	// SHLD by a negative count shifts right logically.
	c.R[0] = 0x80000000
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x4000, 0, 1, 0xD))
	if c.R[0] != 0x40000000 {
		t.Errorf("SHLD -1: R0=%#x, want 0x40000000", c.R[0])
	}
}

func TestMultiplyAndMAC(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()

	// MUL.L keeps the low 32 bits of the product in MACL.
	c.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFE // -2
	c.R[1] = 3
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x0000, 0, 1, 0x7))
	if c.MACL != 0xFFFFFFFA {
		t.Errorf("MUL.L: MACL=%#x, want 0xFFFFFFFA", c.MACL)
	}
	// MULS.W multiplies the sign-extended low words.
	c.R[0] = 0x0000FFFE // -2 as a word
	c.R[1] = 3
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x2000, 0, 1, 0xF))
	if c.MACL != 0xFFFFFFFA {
		t.Errorf("MULS.W: MACL=%#x, want 0xFFFFFFFA", c.MACL)
	}
	// MULU.W zero-extends.
	c.R[0] = 0x0000FFFF
	c.R[1] = 0x0000FFFF
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x2000, 0, 1, 0xE))
	if c.MACL != 0xFFFE0001 {
		t.Errorf("MULU.W: MACL=%#x, want 0xFFFE0001", c.MACL)
	}
	// DMULS.L produces a full 64-bit product.
	c.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFE
	c.R[1] = 3
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 0, 1, 0xD))
	if c.MACL != 0xFFFFFFFA || c.MACH != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("DMULS.L: MACH:MACL=%#x:%#x, want 0xFFFFFFFF:0xFFFFFFFA", c.MACH, c.MACL)
	}
	// DMULU.L unsigned.
	c.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	c.R[1] = 2
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 0, 1, 0x5))
	if c.MACL != 0xFFFFFFFE || c.MACH != 1 {
		t.Errorf("DMULU.L: MACH:MACL=%#x:%#x, want 1:0xFFFFFFFE", c.MACH, c.MACL)
	}

	// MAC.W @Rm+,@Rn+ with S=0 accumulates into the 64-bit MAC.
	const dataVA = 0xA0002000
	mem.Write16(0x2000, uint16(0xFFFD)) // -3 at R0's pointer
	mem.Write16(0x2100, uint16(5))      // 5 at R1's pointer
	c.R[0] = dataVA
	c.R[1] = dataVA + 0x100
	c.MACH, c.MACL = 0, 0
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x4000, 0, 1, 0xF)) // MAC.W @R1+ is m, @R0+ is n
	if c.MACL != 0xFFFFFFF1 || c.MACH != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("MAC.W: MACH:MACL=%#x:%#x, want 0xFFFFFFFF:0xFFFFFFF1 (-15)", c.MACH, c.MACL)
	}
	if c.R[0] != dataVA+2 || c.R[1] != dataVA+0x102 {
		t.Errorf("MAC.W pointers: R0=%#x R1=%#x, want +2 each", c.R[0], c.R[1])
	}
	// MAC.L adds a 32x32 product to the same accumulator: -15 + 100000 * -3.
	mem.Write32(0x2000, 100000)
	mem.Write32(0x2100, 0xFFFFFFFD) // -3
	c.R[0] = dataVA
	c.R[1] = dataVA + 0x100
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x0000, 0, 1, 0xF)) // MAC.L
	want := int64(-15) + int64(-300000)
	if c.MACL != uint32(want) || c.MACH != uint32(want>>32) {
		t.Errorf("MAC.L: MACH:MACL=%#x:%#x, want %#x:%#x", c.MACH, c.MACL, uint32(want>>32), uint32(want))
	}
	// MAC.W with S=1 saturates MACL at 32 bits and sets MACH=1.
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0058) // SETS
	c.MACL = 0x7FFFFFF0
	c.MACH = 0x12345678
	mem.Write16(0x2000, 100)
	mem.Write16(0x2100, 100)
	c.R[0] = dataVA
	c.R[1] = dataVA + 0x100
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x4000, 0, 1, 0xF)) // MAC.W, product 10000 overflows
	if c.MACL != 0x7FFFFFFF || c.MACH != 1 {
		t.Errorf("MAC.W sat: MACH:MACL=%#x:%#x, want 1:0x7FFFFFFF", c.MACH, c.MACL)
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0048) // CLRS
	// CLRMAC clears both halves.
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0028)
	if c.MACH != 0 || c.MACL != 0 {
		t.Errorf("CLRMAC: MACH=%#x MACL=%#x, want 0", c.MACH, c.MACL)
	}
}

// runDivSequence executes the documented SH division routine for a
// signed 32/32 division: DIV0S initializes Q, M, and T from a
// sign-extension register, then 32 rounds of ROTCL on the dividend
// register interleaved with DIV1 on the remainder register feed the
// dividend bits in and collect the quotient bits, and one final
// ROTCL brings the last quotient bit in. The raw remainder register
// then holds the remainder offset by one divisor exactly when
// Q != M, which the caller corrects.
func runDivSequence(c *CPU, mem *testMem, dividend, divisor int32) {
	c.R[0] = uint32(dividend)
	c.R[1] = uint32(divisor)
	if dividend < 0 {
		c.R[2] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	} else {
		c.R[2] = 0
	}
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x2000, 2, 1, 0x7)) // DIV0S R1,R2
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		execOne(c, mem, 0x4024)                  // ROTCL R0
		execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 2, 1, 0x4)) // DIV1 R1,R2
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4024) // ROTCL R0
}

func TestDivisionSequence(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	remainder := func(divisor int32) int32 {
		rem := int32(c.R[2])
		q := (c.SR >> 8) & 1
		m := (c.SR >> 9) & 1
		if q != m {
			rem += divisor
		}
		return rem
	}

	runDivSequence(c, mem, 100, 7)
	if c.R[0] != 14 {
		t.Errorf("100/7 quotient = %d, want 14", int32(c.R[0]))
	}
	if r := remainder(7); r != 2 {
		t.Errorf("100/7 remainder = %d, want 2", r)
	}

	runDivSequence(c, mem, -100, -7)
	if c.R[0] != 14 {
		t.Errorf("-100/-7 quotient = %d, want 14", int32(c.R[0]))
	}
	if r := remainder(-7); r != -2 {
		t.Errorf("-100/-7 remainder = %d, want -2", r)
	}

	// For opposite signs the raw sequence yields the floored pair:
	// -100/7 gives quotient -15 and remainder +5, and the manual's
	// closing sign correction (quotient +1, remainder - divisor,
	// applied when the signs differ and the remainder is nonzero)
	// converts it to the truncated pair -14 and -2.
	runDivSequence(c, mem, -100, 7)
	q := int32(c.R[0])
	r := int32(c.R[2])
	if q != -15 || r != 5 {
		t.Errorf("-100/7 raw = %d rem %d, want floored -15 rem 5", q, r)
	}
	if q+1 != -14 || r-7 != -2 {
		t.Errorf("-100/7 corrected = %d rem %d, want -14 rem -2", q+1, r-7)
	}

	// Unsigned: DIV0U then the same ROTCL/DIV1 loop.
	c.R[0] = 1000
	c.R[1] = 13
	c.R[2] = 0
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0019) // DIV0U
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		execOne(c, mem, 0x4024)
		execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x3000, 2, 1, 0x4))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4024)
	if c.R[0] != 76 {
		t.Errorf("1000/13 unsigned quotient = %d, want 76", c.R[0])
	}
	if r := remainder(13); r != 12 {
		t.Errorf("1000/13 unsigned remainder = %d, want 12", r)
	}
}

func TestMOVForms(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	const dataVA = 0xA0002000

	// MOV.L @(disp,PC),Rn reads a literal.
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase, 0xD000, 0x0009) // MOV.L @(0,PC),R0 ; NOP
	mem.Write32(4, 0xDEADBEEF)
	c.Step()
	if c.R[0] != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("MOV.L PC-rel: R0=%#x, want 0xDEADBEEF", c.R[0])
	}
	// MOV.W @(disp,PC),Rn sign extends.
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase, 0x9000, 0x0009) // MOV.W @(0,PC),R0 ; NOP
	mem.Write16(4, 0x8001)
	c.Step()
	if c.R[0] != 0xFFFF8001 {
		t.Errorf("MOV.W PC-rel: R0=%#x, want 0xFFFF8001", c.R[0])
	}
	// Post-increment load and pre-decrement store.
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x100
	c.R[1] = dataVA
	mem.Write32(0x2000, 0x11223344)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x6000, 0, 1, 0x6)) // MOV.L @R1+,R0
	if c.R[0] != 0x11223344 || c.R[1] != dataVA+4 {
		t.Errorf("MOV.L @R1+: R0=%#x R1=%#x", c.R[0], c.R[1])
	}
	c.R[0] = 0xCAFEBABE
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x2000, 1, 0, 0x6)) // MOV.L R0,@-R1
	if c.R[1] != dataVA || mem.Read32(0x2000) != 0xCAFEBABE {
		t.Errorf("MOV.L @-R1: R1=%#x mem=%#x", c.R[1], mem.Read32(0x2000))
	}
	// Displacement forms.
	c.R[2] = dataVA
	c.R[0] = 0xAABBCCDD
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x1000, 2, 0, 0x2)) // MOV.L R0,@(8,R2)
	if mem.Read32(0x2008) != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Errorf("MOV.L disp store: mem=%#x", mem.Read32(0x2008))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x5000, 3, 2, 0x2)) // MOV.L @(8,R2),R3
	if c.R[3] != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Errorf("MOV.L disp load: R3=%#x", c.R[3])
	}
	// Indexed forms through R0.
	c.R[0] = 0x10
	c.R[1] = dataVA
	c.R[2] = 0x55667788
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x0000, 1, 2, 0x6)) // MOV.L R2,@(R0,R1)
	if mem.Read32(0x2010) != 0x55667788 {
		t.Errorf("MOV.L indexed store: mem=%#x", mem.Read32(0x2010))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x0000, 3, 1, 0xE)) // MOV.L @(R0,R1),R3
	if c.R[3] != 0x55667788 {
		t.Errorf("MOV.L indexed load: R3=%#x", c.R[3])
	}
	// GBR-relative byte store and load, and the GBR byte logic ops.
	c.GBR = dataVA + 0x100
	c.R[0] = 0xAB
	execOne(c, mem, 0xC005) // MOV.B R0,@(5,GBR)
	if mem.Read8(0x2105) != 0xAB {
		t.Errorf("MOV.B GBR store: mem=%#x", mem.Read8(0x2105))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xC405) // MOV.B @(5,GBR),R0
	if c.R[0] != 0xFFFFFFAB {
		t.Errorf("MOV.B GBR load: R0=%#x, want sign extended 0xFFFFFFAB", c.R[0])
	}
	c.R[0] = 0x05           // byte offset for the @(R0,GBR) logic forms
	execOne(c, mem, 0xCD3C) // AND.B #0x3C,@(R0,GBR): 0xAB & 0x3C = 0x28
	if mem.Read8(0x2105) != 0x28 {
		t.Errorf("AND.B: mem=%#x, want 0x28", mem.Read8(0x2105))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xCC0F) // TST.B #0x0F,@(R0,GBR): 0x28 & 0x0F != 0
	if c.getT() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("TST.B: T=%d, want 0", c.getT())
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xCCC0) // TST.B #0xC0: 0x28 & 0xC0 == 0
	if c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("TST.B zero: T=%d, want 1", c.getT())
	}
	// MOVA computes a PC-relative address without touching memory.
	c.PC = codeBase
	execOne(c, mem, 0xC702) // MOVA @(2,PC),R0
	if c.R[0] != codeBase+4+8 {
		t.Errorf("MOVA: R0=%#x, want %#x", c.R[0], uint32(codeBase+12))
	}
	// MOVCA.L stores R0.
	c.R[1] = dataVA
	c.R[0] = 0x12345678
	execOne(c, mem, 0x00C3|1<<8) // MOVCA.L R0,@R1
	if mem.Read32(0x2000) != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("MOVCA.L: mem=%#x", mem.Read32(0x2000))
	}
	// TAS.B sets T on a zero byte and sets the top bit either way.
	c.R[1] = dataVA
	mem.Write8(0x2000, 0)
	execOne(c, mem, 0x401B|1<<8) // TAS.B @R1
	if c.getT() != 1 || mem.Read8(0x2000) != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("TAS.B zero: T=%d mem=%#x, want 1 and 0x80", c.getT(), mem.Read8(0x2000))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x401B|1<<8)
	if c.getT() != 0 || mem.Read8(0x2000) != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("TAS.B nonzero: T=%d mem=%#x, want 0 and 0x80", c.getT(), mem.Read8(0x2000))
	}
	// MOVT materializes T.
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0018)      // SETT
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0029|5<<8) // MOVT R5
	if c.R[5] != 1 {
		t.Errorf("MOVT: R5=%d, want 1", c.R[5])
	}
}

func TestSystemRegisterMoves(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x100

	// LDS/STS with PR.
	c.R[0] = 0xA0003000
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400A|0<<8|2<<4) // LDS R0,PR
	if c.PR != 0xA0003000 {
		t.Errorf("LDS PR: PR=%#x", c.PR)
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x000A|1<<8|2<<4) // STS PR,R1
	if c.R[1] != 0xA0003000 {
		t.Errorf("STS PR: R1=%#x", c.R[1])
	}
	// STS.L / LDS.L through memory.
	c.R[2] = 0xA0002000
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4002|2<<8|2<<4) // STS.L PR,@-R2 (stack style: writes at R2 after decrement in our flow via R2 pointing one past)
	// Our STS.L decrements first, so the value lands at 0xA0001FFC.
	if mem.Read32(0x1FFC) != 0xA0003000 || c.R[2] != 0xA0001FFC {
		t.Errorf("STS.L PR: mem=%#x R2=%#x", mem.Read32(0x1FFC), c.R[2])
	}
	c.PR = 0
	execOne(c, mem, 0x4006|2<<8|2<<4) // LDS.L @R2+,PR
	if c.PR != 0xA0003000 || c.R[2] != 0xA0002000 {
		t.Errorf("LDS.L PR: PR=%#x R2=%#x", c.PR, c.R[2])
	}
	// LDC/STC with GBR works in any mode.
	c.R[0] = 0xA0004000
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400E|0<<8|1<<4) // LDC R0,GBR
	if c.GBR != 0xA0004000 {
		t.Errorf("LDC GBR: GBR=%#x", c.GBR)
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0002|3<<8|1<<4) // STC GBR,R3
	if c.R[3] != 0xA0004000 {
		t.Errorf("STC GBR: R3=%#x", c.R[3])
	}
	// LDS/STS with MACH and MACL.
	c.R[0] = 0x11223344
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400A|0<<8|0<<4) // LDS R0,MACH
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400A|0<<8|1<<4) // LDS R0,MACL (m field is bits 11..8 here: R0)
	if c.MACH != 0x11223344 || c.MACL != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("LDS MACH/MACL: %#x %#x", c.MACH, c.MACL)
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x000A|4<<8|0<<4) // STS MACH,R4
	if c.R[4] != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("STS MACH: R4=%#x", c.R[4])
	}
}

func TestDelaySlots(t *testing.T) {
	// BRA: the delay slot executes, the instruction after it is
	// skipped, and control reaches the target.
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0xA001,       // BRA +1 (target = base+6)
		movImm(0, 1), // delay slot
		movImm(0, 2), // skipped
		movImm(0, 3), // target
	)
	stepN(c, 3)
	if c.R[0] != 3 {
		t.Errorf("BRA delay slot: R0=%d, want 3 (slot ran, +2 skipped)", c.R[0])
	}

	// BT not taken: the delay slot does not execute at all.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0x0008,       // CLRT
		0x8901,       // BT +1 (would target base+8)
		movImm(0, 1), // delay slot, must be skipped
		movImm(0, 2), // fall-through target
		movImm(0, 3),
	)
	stepN(c, 3)
	if c.R[0] != 2 {
		t.Errorf("BT not taken: R0=%d, want 2 (slot skipped)", c.R[0])
	}
	// BT taken: the delay slot executes before the target.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0x0018,       // SETT
		0x8901,       // BT +1 (target = base+8)
		movImm(0, 1), // delay slot
		movImm(0, 2), // skipped
		movImm(0, 3), // target
	)
	stepN(c, 4)
	if c.R[0] != 3 {
		t.Errorf("BT taken: R0=%d, want 3", c.R[0])
	}
	// BT/S not taken: the delay slot still executes, then control
	// falls through.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0x0008,       // CLRT
		0x8D01,       // BT/S +1
		movImm(0, 1), // delay slot, executes
		movImm(0, 2), // fall-through
	)
	stepN(c, 4)
	if c.R[0] != 2 {
		t.Errorf("BT/S not taken: R0=%d, want 2 (slot ran, then fall-through)", c.R[0])
	}
	// BF/S taken mirrors BT/S.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0x0008,       // CLRT
		0x8F01,       // BF/S +1 (target = base+8)
		movImm(0, 1), // delay slot
		movImm(0, 2), // skipped
		movImm(0, 3), // target
	)
	stepN(c, 4)
	if c.R[0] != 3 {
		t.Errorf("BF/S taken: R0=%d, want 3", c.R[0])
	}

	// A branch in a delay slot raises the slot illegal exception.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0xA000, // BRA +0
		0xA000, // BRA in the delay slot: illegal
		0x0009,
	)
	stepN(c, 2)
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x1A0 {
		t.Errorf("branch in delay slot: EXPEVT=%#x, want 0x1A0", c.EXPEVT)
	}
	if c.PC != c.VBR+0x100 {
		t.Errorf("branch in delay slot: PC=%#x, want VBR+0x100", c.PC)
	}
	// TRAPA in a delay slot is also a slot illegal exception, not a
	// trap exception.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0xA000, // BRA +0
		0xC301, // TRAPA #1 in the delay slot
		0x0009,
	)
	stepN(c, 2)
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x1A0 {
		t.Errorf("TRAPA in delay slot: EXPEVT=%#x, want 0x1A0", c.EXPEVT)
	}
	// An illegal opcode in a delay slot is a slot illegal exception.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0xA000, // BRA +0
		0xFFFF, // undefined
		0x0009,
	)
	stepN(c, 2)
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x1A0 {
		t.Errorf("illegal in delay slot: EXPEVT=%#x, want 0x1A0", c.EXPEVT)
	}
}

func TestSubroutineFlow(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0xB002,       // BSR +2 (target = base+8)
		0x0009,       // NOP (delay slot)
		movImm(1, 7), // return point
		0x0009,       // NOP
		movImm(0, 5), // subroutine: MOV #5,R0
		0x000B,       // RTS
		0x0009,       // NOP (delay slot)
	)
	stepN(c, 5)
	if c.R[0] != 5 {
		t.Errorf("BSR flow: R0=%d, want 5", c.R[0])
	}
	if c.PC != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("BSR flow: PC=%#x, want return point %#x", c.PC, uint32(codeBase+4))
	}
	c.Step()
	if c.R[1] != 7 {
		t.Errorf("BSR flow: R1=%d after return, want 7", c.R[1])
	}
	// JSR @Rn and JMP @Rn.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	c.R[3] = codeBase + 8
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase,
		0x400B|3<<8,  // JSR @R3
		0x0009,       // NOP (delay slot)
		movImm(1, 7), // return point (base+4)
		0x0009,
		movImm(0, 9), // subroutine at base+8
		0x402B|3<<8,  // JMP @R3 (R3 still holds base+8? PR path below re-sets it)
		0x0009,
	)
	c.R[3] = codeBase + 8
	stepN(c, 3) // JSR, NOP slot, subroutine MOV
	if c.R[0] != 9 || c.PR != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("JSR: R0=%d PR=%#x, want 9 and %#x", c.R[0], c.PR, uint32(codeBase+4))
	}
}

func TestBankSwitching(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x100
	// Reset SR has RB=0, so R shows bank 0 and Bank holds bank 1.
	c.R[0] = 0x11111111    // bank 0 R0
	c.Bank[0] = 0x22222222 // bank 1 R0

	// LDC R1,SR with RB=1 swaps the active bank.
	c.R[1] = 0x700000F0               // MD=1, RB=1, BL=1, IMASK=F
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400E|1<<8|0<<4) // LDC R1,SR
	if c.R[0] != 0x22222222 || c.Bank[0] != 0x11111111 {
		t.Errorf("after RB=1: R0=%#x Bank0=%#x, want bank 1 active", c.R[0], c.Bank[0])
	}
	// Flipping RB back restores bank 0.
	c.R[1] = 0x500000F0               // MD=1, RB=0, BL=1
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400E|1<<8|0<<4) // LDC R1,SR
	if c.R[0] != 0x11111111 || c.Bank[0] != 0x22222222 {
		t.Errorf("after RB=0: R0=%#x Bank0=%#x, want bank 0 active", c.R[0], c.Bank[0])
	}
	// LDC Rm,Rn_BANK writes the inactive bank regardless of RB.
	c.R[2] = 0x33333333
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400E|2<<8|(8+0)<<4) // LDC R2,R0_BANK
	if c.Bank[0] != 0x33333333 || c.R[0] != 0x11111111 {
		t.Errorf("LDC R0_BANK: Bank0=%#x R0=%#x, want 0x33333333 in the inactive bank", c.Bank[0], c.R[0])
	}
	// STC Rm_BANK,Rn reads it back.
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0002|3<<8|(8+0)<<4) // STC R0_BANK,R3
	if c.R[3] != 0x33333333 {
		t.Errorf("STC R0_BANK: R3=%#x, want 0x33333333", c.R[3])
	}
	// STC SR,Rn reports the current SR.
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0002|4<<8|0<<4) // STC SR,R4
	if c.R[4] != c.SR {
		t.Errorf("STC SR: R4=%#x SR=%#x", c.R[4], c.SR)
	}
}

func TestTRAPAAndRTE(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.VBR = 0xA0001000
	loadProg(c, mem, codeBase, 0xC321)             // TRAPA #0x21
	mem.Write16((0x1000+0x100)&0x1FFFFFFF, 0x002B) // RTE at VBR+0x100
	mem.Write16((0x1000+0x102)&0x1FFFFFFF, 0x0009) // its delay slot
	c.R[15] = 0xA0008000
	srBefore := c.SR
	c.Step()
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x160 {
		t.Errorf("TRAPA: EXPEVT=%#x, want 0x160", c.EXPEVT)
	}
	if c.TRA != 0x21<<2 {
		t.Errorf("TRAPA: TRA=%#x, want %#x", c.TRA, uint32(0x21<<2))
	}
	if c.PC != 0xA0001000+0x100 {
		t.Errorf("TRAPA: PC=%#x, want VBR+0x100", c.PC)
	}
	if c.SPC != codeBase+2 || c.SSR != srBefore || c.SGR != 0xA0008000 {
		t.Errorf("TRAPA: SPC=%#x SSR=%#x SGR=%#x", c.SPC, c.SSR, c.SGR)
	}
	if c.SR&(srMD|srRB|srBL) != srMD|srRB|srBL {
		t.Errorf("TRAPA: SR=%#x, MD/RB/BL must be set", c.SR)
	}
	// RTE returns to SPC with SR restored from SSR; its delay slot
	// executes first.
	stepN(c, 2)
	if c.PC != codeBase+2 {
		t.Errorf("RTE: PC=%#x, want %#x", c.PC, uint32(codeBase+2))
	}
	if c.SR != srBefore {
		t.Errorf("RTE: SR=%#x, want %#x", c.SR, srBefore)
	}
}

func TestIllegalAndPrivileged(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	execOne(c, mem, 0xFFFF)
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x180 || c.PC != 0x100 {
		t.Errorf("illegal: EXPEVT=%#x PC=%#x, want 0x180 and VBR+0x100", c.EXPEVT, c.PC)
	}
	// A privileged instruction in user mode is a general illegal
	// instruction exception. MD is cleared directly here; the bank
	// state is irrelevant to this check.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	c.PC = 0x00001000
	c.SR = 0x000000F0                 // user mode
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400E|0<<8|0<<4) // LDC R0,SR
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x180 {
		t.Errorf("user LDC SR: EXPEVT=%#x, want 0x180", c.EXPEVT)
	}
	// But LDC to GBR is allowed in user mode.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	c.PC = 0x00001000
	c.SR = 0x000000F0
	c.R[0] = 0xA0005000
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400E|0<<8|1<<4) // LDC R0,GBR
	if c.GBR != 0xA0005000 || c.EXPEVT == 0x180 {
		t.Errorf("user LDC GBR: GBR=%#x EXPEVT=%#x, want it to succeed", c.GBR, c.EXPEVT)
	}
	// SLEEP halts; a halted CPU reports steps without moving.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	c.PC = codeBase
	execOne(c, mem, 0x001B) // SLEEP
	if !c.Halted {
		t.Fatal("SLEEP: Halted is false")
	}
	pc := c.PC
	if c.Step() != 1 || c.PC != pc {
		t.Errorf("halted Step: PC moved to %#x", c.PC)
	}
}

func TestInterruptModel(t *testing.T) {
	park := func(c *CPU, mem *testMem) {
		// NOP sled at the parked PC so a non-accepting Step just
		// advances one instruction.
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			mem.Write16((codeBase+0x40+uint32(2*i))&0x1FFFFFFF, 0x0009)
		}
		c.VBR = 0xA0001000
		c.PC = codeBase + 0x40
	}

	// IMASK gates acceptance: the post-boot SR has IMASK 15, so a
	// level 6 request latches as pending but is not taken.
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	park(c, mem)
	c.RaiseInterrupt(0x320, 6)
	c.Step()
	if c.PC != codeBase+0x42 || c.INTEVT == 0x320 {
		t.Errorf("masked interrupt taken: PC=%#x INTEVT=%#x", c.PC, c.INTEVT)
	}
	if code, level, valid := c.PendingInterrupt(); !valid || code != 0x320 || level != 6 {
		t.Errorf("pending = (%#x, %d, %v), want (0x320, 6, true)", code, level, valid)
	}
	// The request survives a serialize round trip.
	c2, _ := newTestCPU()
	if !c2.Deserialize(c.Serialize()) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize of the pending state failed")
	}
	if code, level, valid := c2.PendingInterrupt(); !valid || code != 0x320 || level != 6 {
		t.Errorf("restored pending = (%#x, %d, %v), want (0x320, 6, true)", code, level, valid)
	}
	// Drop IMASK to 3 and the request is accepted at the next
	// instruction boundary.
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x40
	c.SR = 0x40000030 // MD set, IMASK 3
	c.Step()
	if c.INTEVT != 0x320 {
		t.Errorf("INTEVT=%#x, want 0x320", c.INTEVT)
	}
	if c.PC != 0xA0001000+0x600 || c.SPC != codeBase+0x40 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt vector: PC=%#x SPC=%#x", c.PC, c.SPC)
	}
	if _, _, valid := c.PendingInterrupt(); valid {
		t.Error("pending request still latched after acceptance")
	}
	if c.SR&srBL == 0 {
		t.Error("BL not set on interrupt entry")
	}

	// BL blocks acceptance even at level 15 with IMASK 0, until it
	// clears.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	park(c, mem)
	c.SR = 0x40000000 | srBL
	c.RaiseInterrupt(0x200, 15)
	c.Step()
	if c.PC != codeBase+0x42 || c.INTEVT == 0x200 {
		t.Errorf("BL-blocked interrupt taken: PC=%#x INTEVT=%#x", c.PC, c.INTEVT)
	}
	c.SR &^= srBL
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x40
	c.Step()
	if c.INTEVT != 0x200 || c.PC != 0xA0001000+0x600 {
		t.Errorf("unblocked interrupt: PC=%#x INTEVT=%#x", c.PC, c.INTEVT)
	}

	// Withdrawal drops a latched request before acceptance.
	c, mem = newTestCPU()
	park(c, mem)
	c.SR = 0x40000000
	c.RaiseInterrupt(0x320, 6)
	c.WithdrawInterrupt()
	c.Step()
	if c.PC != codeBase+0x42 || c.INTEVT == 0x320 {
		t.Errorf("withdrawn interrupt taken: PC=%#x INTEVT=%#x", c.PC, c.INTEVT)
	}

	// A lower level request does not displace a latched higher one.
	c, _ = newTestCPU()
	c.RaiseInterrupt(0x320, 6)
	c.RaiseInterrupt(0x3A0, 2)
	if code, level, _ := c.PendingInterrupt(); code != 0x320 || level != 6 {
		t.Errorf("pending after lower raise = (%#x, %d), want (0x320, 6)", code, level)
	}
}

func TestMMUTranslation(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.MMUCR = 1
	mk := func(vpn, ppn uint32, size, pr int, d bool) TLBEntry {
		return TLBEntry{VPN: vpn, PPN: ppn, Size: size, V: true, PR: pr, D: d}
	}
	c.UTLB[0] = mk(0x00400000, 0x00800000, 1, 3, true)  // 4KB
	c.UTLB[1] = mk(0x00010000, 0x00200000, 0, 3, true)  // 1KB
	c.UTLB[2] = mk(0x01000000, 0x02000000, 2, 3, true)  // 64KB
	c.UTLB[3] = mk(0x10000000, 0x04000000, 3, 3, true)  // 1MB
	c.UTLB[4] = mk(0x00600000, 0x00A00000, 1, 1, true)  // writable, no user
	c.UTLB[5] = mk(0x00700000, 0x00B00000, 1, 2, true)  // user, read-only
	c.UTLB[6] = mk(0x00800000, 0x00C00000, 1, 3, false) // clean page
	c.UTLB[7] = TLBEntry{VPN: 0x00900000, PPN: 0x00D00000, Size: 1, V: false, PR: 3, D: true}

	check := func(va uint32, write bool, wantPA uint32, wantOK bool, wantCode uint32) {
		t.Helper()
		pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(va, write)
		if ok != wantOK {
			t.Errorf("TranslateVA(%#x, write=%v): ok=%v, want %v", va, write, ok, wantOK)
			return
		}
		if ok && pa != wantPA {
			t.Errorf("TranslateVA(%#x): pa=%#x, want %#x", va, pa, wantPA)
		}
		if !ok && c.EXPEVT != wantCode {
			t.Errorf("TranslateVA(%#x, write=%v): EXPEVT=%#x, want %#x", va, write, c.EXPEVT, wantCode)
		}
		if !ok && c.TEA != va {
			t.Errorf("TranslateVA(%#x): TEA=%#x, want the faulting VA", va, c.TEA)
		}
	}
	check(0x00400123, false, 0x00800123, true, 0)
	check(0x00400FFF, true, 0x00800FFF, true, 0)
	check(0x000103FF, false, 0x002003FF, true, 0)
	check(0x0100ABCD, false, 0x0200ABCD, true, 0)
	check(0x10054321, false, 0x04054321, true, 0)
	// Misses: no entry at all, and an entry with V=0.
	check(0x20000000, false, 0, false, 0x040)
	check(0x20000000, true, 0, false, 0x060)
	check(0x00900000, false, 0, false, 0x040)
	// Write to a user-readable but not writable page (privileged).
	check(0x00700000, true, 0, false, 0x0C0)
	// Write to a valid clean page: initial page write.
	check(0x00800000, true, 0, false, 0x080)
	check(0x00800000, false, 0x00C00000, true, 0)

	// User mode (MD=0, set directly; no code runs in this state):
	// pages without the user bit raise protection faults.
	c.SR = 0x000000F0
	check(0x00600000, false, 0, false, 0x0A0)
	check(0x00600000, true, 0, false, 0x0C0)
	check(0x00400123, false, 0x00800123, true, 0)
	// User mode may not touch the untranslated areas at all.
	check(0xA0000000, false, 0, false, 0x0E0)
	check(0xA0000000, true, 0, false, 0x100)
	c.SR = 0x400000F0

	// With AT=0 every area maps directly.
	c.MMUCR = 0
	check(0x00400123, false, 0x00400123&0x1FFFFFFF, true, 0)
	check(0xA0001234, false, 0x1234, true, 0)
	c.MMUCR = 1

	// Data access through the MMU from running code: a load from
	// the 4KB page at VA 0x00400000 reads physical 0x00800000.
	mem.Write32(0x800000, 0x11223344)
	c.PC = codeBase
	c.R[1] = 0x00400000
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x6000, 0, 1, 0x2)) // MOV.L @R1,R0
	if c.R[0] != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("MMU load: R0=%#x, want 0x11223344", c.R[0])
	}
	// A load from an unmapped VA vectors the TLB miss exception to
	// VBR+0x600.
	c.VBR = 0
	c.R[1] = 0x20000000
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0x6000, 0, 1, 0x2))
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x040 || c.PC != 0x600 || c.TEA != 0x20000000 {
		t.Errorf("MMU miss: EXPEVT=%#x PC=%#x TEA=%#x, want 0x040, 0x600, 0x20000000", c.EXPEVT, c.PC, c.TEA)
	}
}

func TestLDTLB(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.MMUCR = 1
	c.PTEH = 0x00600000
	// PTEL per the documented layout in loadTLB: PPN in the high
	// bits, V at bit 8, PR at bits 6..5, size at bits 4..3, D at
	// bit 2.
	c.PTEL = 0x00A00000 | 1<<8 | 3<<5 | 1<<3 | 1<<2
	c.PC = codeBase
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0038) // LDTLB
	e := c.UTLB[0]
	if !e.V || e.VPN != 0x00600000 || e.PPN != 0x00A00000 || e.Size != 1 || e.PR != 3 || !e.D {
		t.Fatalf("LDTLB entry: %+v", e)
	}
	pa, ok := c.TranslateVA(0x00600ABC, false)
	if !ok || pa != 0x00A00ABC {
		t.Errorf("LDTLB translate read: pa=%#x ok=%v, want 0x00A00ABC", pa, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := c.TranslateVA(0x00600ABC, true); !ok {
		t.Errorf("LDTLB translate write: not ok, EXPEVT=%#x (D bit must be set)", c.EXPEVT)
	}
	// A second LDTLB goes to the next replacement slot.
	c.PTEH = 0x00700000
	c.PTEL = 0x00B00000 | 1<<8 | 3<<5 | 1<<3 | 1<<2
	execOne(c, mem, 0x0038)
	if c.UTLB[1].VPN != 0x00700000 {
		t.Errorf("LDTLB slot 1: %+v", c.UTLB[1])
	}
}

func TestFPU(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x100
	// Reset FPSCR has PR=0 (single precision) and SR has FD=0.

	// FLDI1 / FLDI0.
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF000|1<<8|0x9D) // FLDI1 FR1
	if c.FR[1] != 0x3F800000 {
		t.Errorf("FLDI1: FR1=%#x, want 0x3F800000", c.FR[1])
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF000|2<<8|0x8D) // FLDI0 FR2
	if c.FR[2] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLDI0: FR2=%#x, want 0", c.FR[2])
	}
	// FADD / FMUL / FDIV on singles: 1.5 and 2.25.
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(1.5)
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(2.25)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x0)) // FADD FR1,FR0
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != 3.75 {
		t.Errorf("FADD: %v, want 3.75", got)
	}
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(1.5)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x2)) // FMUL FR1,FR0
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != 3.375 {
		t.Errorf("FMUL: %v, want 3.375", got)
	}
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(7)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x3)) // FDIV FR1,FR0: 7 / 2.25
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); math.Abs(float64(got-7.0/2.25)) > 1e-6 {
		t.Errorf("FDIV: %v, want %v", got, 7.0/2.25)
	}
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(7)
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(2)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x3)) // 7 / 2 = 3.5
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != 3.5 {
		t.Errorf("FDIV exact: %v, want 3.5", got)
	}
	// FSUB.
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(5)
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(1.25)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x1))
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != 3.75 {
		t.Errorf("FSUB: %v, want 3.75", got)
	}
	// FCMP/EQ and FCMP/GT drive T.
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(2)
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(2)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x4)) // FCMP/EQ FR1,FR0
	if c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("FCMP/EQ: T=%d, want 1", c.getT())
	}
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(3)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x5)) // FCMP/GT FR1,FR0: 3 > 2
	if c.getT() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("FCMP/GT: T=%d, want 1", c.getT())
	}
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 1, 0, 0x5)) // FCMP/GT FR0,FR1: 2 > 3 false
	if c.getT() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("FCMP/GT false: T=%d, want 0", c.getT())
	}
	// FMAC: FR0 * FR1 + FR2 with FR0=2, FR1=3, FR2=4 gives 10.
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(2)
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(3)
	c.FR[2] = math.Float32bits(4)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 2, 1, 0xE)) // FMAC FR1,FR2
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[2]); got != 10 {
		t.Errorf("FMAC: %v, want 10", got)
	}
	// FLOAT and FTRC round trip, including saturation.
	c.FPUL = 0xFFFFFFFD
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF02D) // FLOAT FPUL,FR0
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != -3 {
		t.Errorf("FLOAT: %v, want -3", got)
	}
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(3.99)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF03D|1<<8) // FTRC FR1,FPUL
	if int32(c.FPUL) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("FTRC: FPUL=%d, want 3", int32(c.FPUL))
	}
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(1e30)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF03D|1<<8)
	if c.FPUL != 0x7FFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("FTRC saturate high: FPUL=%#x, want 0x7FFFFFFF", c.FPUL)
	}
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(-1e30)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF03D|1<<8)
	if c.FPUL != 0x80000000 {
		t.Errorf("FTRC saturate low: FPUL=%#x, want 0x80000000", c.FPUL)
	}
	// FSQRT and FSRRA.
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(2)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF06D) // FSQRT FR0
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); math.Abs(float64(got)-math.Sqrt(2)) > 1e-6 {
		t.Errorf("FSQRT: %v, want sqrt(2)", got)
	}
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(4)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF07D) // FSRRA FR0
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != 0.5 {
		t.Errorf("FSRRA: %v, want 0.5", got)
	}
	// FNEG and FABS.
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(-2.5)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF05D) // FABS FR0
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != 2.5 {
		t.Errorf("FABS: %v, want 2.5", got)
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF04D) // FNEG FR0
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[0]); got != -2.5 {
		t.Errorf("FNEG: %v, want -2.5", got)
	}
	// FMOV.S through memory, including post-increment.
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(1.5)
	c.R[1] = 0xA0002000
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 1, 0, 0xA)) // FMOV.S FR0,@R1
	if mem.Read32(0x2000) != math.Float32bits(1.5) {
		t.Errorf("FMOV.S store: mem=%#x", mem.Read32(0x2000))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 2, 1, 0x8)) // FMOV.S @R1,FR2
	if c.FR[2] != math.Float32bits(1.5) {
		t.Errorf("FMOV.S load: FR2=%#x", c.FR[2])
	}
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 3, 1, 0x9)) // FMOV.S @R1+,FR3
	if c.FR[3] != math.Float32bits(1.5) || c.R[1] != 0xA0002004 {
		t.Errorf("FMOV.S post-inc: FR3=%#x R1=%#x", c.FR[3], c.R[1])
	}
	// FSTS and FLDS move values through FPUL.
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF01D|2<<8) // FLDS FR2,FPUL
	if c.FPUL != math.Float32bits(1.5) {
		t.Errorf("FLDS: FPUL=%#x", c.FPUL)
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF00D|4<<8) // FSTS FPUL,FR4
	if c.FR[4] != math.Float32bits(1.5) {
		t.Errorf("FSTS: FR4=%#x", c.FR[4])
	}
	// LDS/STS FPUL and FPSCR.
	c.R[0] = 0xDEADBEEF
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400A|0<<8|5<<4) // LDS R0,FPUL
	if c.FPUL != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("LDS FPUL: FPUL=%#x", c.FPUL)
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0x000A|5<<8|5<<4) // STS FPUL,R5
	if c.R[5] != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("STS FPUL: R5=%#x", c.R[5])
	}
}

func TestFPUBanksAndDoubles(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x100

	// FPSCR.FR swap via LDS: the FR and XFR banks exchange places.
	c.FR[0] = 0xAAAAAAAA
	c.XFR[0] = 0xBBBBBBBB
	c.R[0] = c.FPSCR ^ (1 << 21)
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400A|0<<8|6<<4) // LDS R0,FPSCR
	if c.FR[0] != 0xBBBBBBBB || c.XFR[0] != 0xAAAAAAAA {
		t.Errorf("FRCHG via LDS: FR0=%#x XFR0=%#x", c.FR[0], c.XFR[0])
	}
	// FRCHG swaps them back.
	execOne(c, mem, 0xFBFD)
	if c.FR[0] != 0xAAAAAAAA || c.FPSCR&(1<<21) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("FRCHG: FR0=%#x FPSCR=%#x", c.FR[0], c.FPSCR)
	}

	// Double precision with PR=1: 1.5 + 2.25 = 3.75 in DR0.
	c.R[0] = c.FPSCR | (1 << 19)
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400A|0<<8|6<<4) // LDS R0,FPSCR (sets PR)
	setDR := func(pair int, v float64) {
		b := math.Float64bits(v)
		c.FR[pair] = uint32(b)
		c.FR[pair+1] = uint32(b >> 32)
	}
	getDR := func(pair int) float64 {
		return math.Float64frombits(uint64(c.FR[pair]) | uint64(c.FR[pair+1])<<32)
	}
	setDR(0, 1.5)
	setDR(2, 2.25)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x0)) // FADD DR1,DR0 (fields hold pair numbers 0 and 2 >> 1 in the m/n slots? see note)
	// Note: with PR=1 the register fields name the even DR pair
	// directly: DRm is field value 2 for DR2. ins3 placed m=1,
	// which the decoder masks to pair 0, so this added DR0 to
	// itself. Redo with the correct field:
	setDR(0, 1.5)
	setDR(2, 2.25)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 2, 0x0)) // FADD with m field 2 = DR2
	if got := getDR(0); got != 3.75 {
		t.Errorf("FADD double: %v, want 3.75", got)
	}
	// FLOAT to a double, and FTRC back from a double.
	c.FPUL = 0xFFFFFFF9
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF02D|2<<8) // FLOAT FPUL,DR2 (n field 2)
	if got := getDR(2); got != -7 {
		t.Errorf("FLOAT double: %v, want -7", got)
	}
	setDR(2, -9.75)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF03D|2<<8) // FTRC DR2,FPUL
	if int32(c.FPUL) != -9 {
		t.Errorf("FTRC double: FPUL=%d, want -9", int32(c.FPUL))
	}
	// FCNVSD and FCNVDS.
	c.FPUL = math.Float32bits(1.5)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF0AD) // FCNVSD FPUL,DR0
	if got := getDR(0); got != 1.5 {
		t.Errorf("FCNVSD: %v, want 1.5", got)
	}
	setDR(0, 2.5)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF0BD) // FCNVDS DR0,FPUL
	if c.FPUL != math.Float32bits(2.5) {
		t.Errorf("FCNVDS: FPUL=%#x, want bits of 2.5", c.FPUL)
	}
	// Back to single precision for the FMOV double tests: PR only
	// affects arithmetic, FMOV honors SZ.
	c.R[0] = c.FPSCR | (1 << 20) // set SZ, keep PR as is
	execOne(c, mem, 0x400A|0<<8|6<<4)
	setDR(0, 3.5)
	c.R[1] = 0xA0002000
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 1, 0, 0xA)) // FMOV DR0,@R1 (SZ=1)
	if mem.Read64(0x2000) != math.Float64bits(3.5) {
		t.Errorf("FMOV double store: mem=%#x", mem.Read64(0x2000))
	}
	setDR(0, 0)
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0x8)) // FMOV @R1,DR0
	if got := getDR(0); got != 3.5 {
		t.Errorf("FMOV double load: %v, want 3.5", got)
	}
	// FMOV between DR and XD banks.
	c.XFR[0], c.XFR[1] = 0x11111111, 0x22222222
	execOne(c, mem, ins3(0xF000, 0, 1, 0xC)) // FMOV XD0,DR0: m field 1 = XD0
	if c.FR[0] != 0x11111111 || c.FR[1] != 0x22222222 {
		t.Errorf("FMOV XD to DR: FR0=%#x FR1=%#x", c.FR[0], c.FR[1])
	}
}

func TestFPUGraphics(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.PC = codeBase + 0x100

	// FIPR FV0,FV4: dot product of (1,2,3,4) and (5,6,7,8) is 70,
	// stored in the last element of FV4 (FR7).
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.FR[i] = math.Float32bits(float32(i + 1))
		c.FR[4+i] = math.Float32bits(float32(i + 5))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF000|1<<10|0<<8|0xED) // FIPR FV0,FV4
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[7]); got != 70 {
		t.Errorf("FIPR: FR7=%v, want 70", got)
	}
	if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[4]); got != 5 {
		t.Errorf("FIPR: FR4=%v, want 5 (only the last element changes)", got)
	}

	// FTRV with the identity matrix in the X bank leaves FV0 alone.
	for i := range c.XFR {
		c.XFR[i] = 0
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.XFR[i*4+i] = math.Float32bits(1)
		c.FR[i] = math.Float32bits(float32(i + 1))
	}
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF1FD) // FTRV XMTRX,FV0
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[i]); got != float32(i+1) {
			t.Errorf("FTRV identity: FR%d=%v, want %d", i, got, i+1)
		}
	}
	// FTRV with a 90 degree rotation about Z (row-major in the X
	// bank): (1,0,0,1) becomes (0,1,0,1).
	for i := range c.XFR {
		c.XFR[i] = 0
	}
	c.XFR[1] = math.Float32bits(-1) // row 0: 0,-1,0,0
	c.XFR[4] = math.Float32bits(1)  // row 1: 1,0,0,0
	c.XFR[10] = math.Float32bits(1)
	c.XFR[15] = math.Float32bits(1)
	c.FR[0] = math.Float32bits(1)
	c.FR[1] = math.Float32bits(0)
	c.FR[2] = math.Float32bits(0)
	c.FR[3] = math.Float32bits(1)
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF1FD)
	want := []float32{0, 1, 0, 1}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		got := math.Float32frombits(c.FR[i])
		if math.Abs(float64(got-want[i])) > 1e-6 {
			t.Errorf("FTRV rotZ90: FR%d=%v, want %v", i, got, want[i])
		}
	}
}

func TestFPUDisabled(t *testing.T) {
	c, mem := newTestCPU()
	c.SR |= srFD
	c.PC = codeBase
	execOne(c, mem, 0xF000|0<<8|0x8D) // FLDI0 FR0 with FD=1
	if c.EXPEVT != 0x800 {
		t.Errorf("FPU disabled: EXPEVT=%#x, want 0x800", c.EXPEVT)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := newTestCPU()
	for i := range c.R {
		c.R[i] = 0x1000 + uint32(i)
	}
	for i := range c.Bank {
		c.Bank[i] = 0x2000 + uint32(i)
	}
	c.PC, c.PR, c.SR, c.GBR, c.VBR = 0xA0001234, 0x11112222, 0x400000F0, 0x33334444, 0x55556666
	c.SSR, c.SPC, c.SGR, c.DBR = 0x77778888, 0x9999AAAA, 0xBBBBCCCC, 0xDDDDEEEE
	c.MACH, c.MACL = 0x01234567, 0x89ABCDEF
	c.FPUL, c.FPSCR = 0x0F0F0F0F, 0x00140001
	for i := range c.FR {
		c.FR[i] = 0x3000 + uint32(i)
		c.XFR[i] = 0x4000 + uint32(i)
	}
	c.MMUCR, c.PTEH, c.PTEL, c.PTEA, c.TTB, c.TEA = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6
	c.EXPEVT, c.INTEVT, c.TRA, c.TTR = 0x160, 0x200, 0x84, 0
	c.UTLB[3] = TLBEntry{VPN: 0x00400000, PPN: 0x00800000, Size: 1, V: true, PR: 3, D: true, SH: false}
	c.UTLB[63] = TLBEntry{VPN: 0x10000000, PPN: 0x04000000, Size: 3, V: true, PR: 2, D: false, SH: true}
	c.Halted = true

	b1 := c.Serialize()
	if len(b1) != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize length = %d, want SerializeSize %d", len(b1), SerializeSize)
	}
	// Scramble, restore, and require byte-identical re-serialization.
	c.Reset()
	c.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	if !c.Deserialize(b1) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize returned false")
	}
	b2 := c.Serialize()
	if !bytes.Equal(b1, b2) {
		t.Fatal("serialize after deserialize differs from the original")
	}
	if c.Deserialize(b1[:len(b1)-1]) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a short buffer")
	}
	if c.Deserialize(append(append([]byte{}, b1...), 0)) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a long buffer")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/g2dma/g2dma.go ====================

// Package g2dma is the Dreamcast G2 bus DMA controller: the four
// channel register blocks at 0x005F7800 (AICA, Ext1, Ext2, Dev)
// from the published system documentation.
//
// The AICA channel is fully implemented: with the enable bit set
// and the CPU trigger selected (SB_ADTSEL = 0), writing 1 to
// SB_ADST copies SB_ADLEN bytes between system memory (SB_ADSTAR)
// and the AICA address space (SB_ADSTAG), direction per SB_ADDIR
// (0 = system memory to AICA space, 1 = AICA space to system
// memory). The copy runs through the physical bus, so AICA
// register addresses and wave RAM addresses both work as targets.
// Completion raises the documented ISTNRM AICA DMA end event
// (normal bank bit 15) and the AICA-side DMA end interrupt source.
// The transfer is synchronous in this model: SB_ADST never reads
// back busy for the AICA channel, and the readback counters show
// the final addresses with the length counter at 0.
//
// The Ext1, Ext2, and Dev channels address devices that are not
// present in this machine (modem, LAN adapter, expansion device).
// On hardware a DMA started toward an absent device never
// completes, so these channels model exactly that: their
// registers store, a start with the enable bit set raises the
// busy state forever, and no completion event ever fires.
// Clearing the enable bit drops the busy state in this model.
// Interrupt-triggered transfers (SB_ADTSEL values other than 0,
// whose trigger masks live in registers outside this window) are
// not modeled: a start write with a nonzero trigger select does
// nothing.
package g2dma

import "encoding/binary"

// Memory is the physical bus access the transfers run through.
type Memory interface {
	Read8(pa uint32) uint8
	Write8(pa uint32, v uint8)
}

// AICAEnd is the AICA-side DMA end notification.
type AICAEnd interface {
	NotifyG2DMAEnd()
}

// EventSink receives the Holly normal-bank AICA DMA done event.
type EventSink interface {
	RaiseNormal(bits uint32)
}

// evtAICADMADone is the ISTNRM bit for G2 AICA DMA completion.
const evtAICADMADone = 1 << 15

// Channel indices.
const (
	ChAICA = 0
	ChExt1 = 1
	ChExt2 = 2
	ChDev  = 3
)

// Per-channel register indices inside a channel block.
const (
	regSTAG = 0 // device-side start address
	regSTAR = 1 // system memory start address
	regLEN  = 2 // byte length
	regDIR  = 3 // direction
	regTSEL = 4 // trigger select
	regEN   = 5 // enable
	regST   = 6 // start / busy status
	regSUSP = 7 // suspend (stored only)
)

// SerializeSize is the exact serialized size: four channels of
// eight registers, four channels of three readback counters,
// the four timeout registers, the address-protection register,
// and one word of busy flags. 50 words in total.
const SerializeSize = (4*8 + 4*3 + 4 + 1 + 1) * 4

// Controller is the G2 DMA register file and transfer engine.
type Controller struct {
	mem  Memory
	aica AICAEnd
	sink EventSink
	regs [4][8]uint32 // channel registers (ST is not stored here)
	cnt  [4][3]uint32 // readback counters: STAGD, STARD, LEND
	busy [4]bool      // ext-channel busy state (AICA completes at once)
	glob [4]uint32    // SB_G2DSTO, SB_G2TRTO, SB_G2MDMTO, SB_G2MDMW
	apro uint32       // SB_G2APRO (write-only on hardware)
}

// New returns a controller moving data through mem, reporting
// AICA DMA completion to aica and raising ISTNRM events on sink.
func New(mem Memory, aica AICAEnd, sink EventSink) *Controller {
	return &Controller{mem: mem, aica: aica, sink: sink}
}

// Read32 reads one register by full physical address.
func (c *Controller) Read32(pa uint32) uint32 {
	off := pa - 0x005F7800
	switch {
	case off < 0x80: // channel blocks
		ch := int(off >> 5)
		r := int((off >> 2) & 7)
		if r == regST {
			if c.busy[ch] {
				return 1
			}
			return 0
		}
		return c.regs[ch][r]
	case off == 0x80: // SB_G2ID
		return 0
	case off >= 0x90 && off < 0xA0:
		return c.glob[(off-0x90)>>2]
	case off == 0xBC: // SB_G2APRO is write-only
		return 0
	case off >= 0xC0 && off < 0x100:
		rel := off - 0xC0
		return c.cnt[rel>>4][(rel>>2)&3]
	}
	return 0
}

// Write32 writes one register by full physical address.
func (c *Controller) Write32(pa uint32, v uint32) {
	off := pa - 0x005F7800
	switch {
	case off < 0x80:
		ch := int(off >> 5)
		r := int((off >> 2) & 7)
		switch r {
		case regST:
			c.start(ch, v)
		case regEN:
			c.regs[ch][regEN] = v
			if v&1 == 0 {
				c.busy[ch] = false
			}
		default:
			c.regs[ch][r] = v
		}
	case off >= 0x90 && off < 0xA0:
		c.glob[(off-0x90)>>2] = v
	case off == 0xBC:
		c.apro = v
	}
}

// start handles a write to a channel ST register.
func (c *Controller) start(ch int, v uint32) {
	if v&1 == 0 || c.regs[ch][regEN]&1 == 0 {
		return
	}
	if ch != ChAICA {
		// Absent device: the transfer never completes.
		c.busy[ch] = true
		return
	}
	if c.regs[ch][regTSEL] != 0 {
		// Interrupt-triggered AICA DMA is not modeled.
		return
	}
	c.runAICA()
}

// runAICA executes the AICA channel transfer synchronously.
func (c *Controller) runAICA() {
	stag := c.regs[ChAICA][regSTAG]
	star := c.regs[ChAICA][regSTAR]
	n := c.regs[ChAICA][regLEN]
	src, dst := star, stag
	if c.regs[ChAICA][regDIR]&1 == 1 {
		src, dst = stag, star
	}
	for i := uint32(0); i < n; i++ {
		c.mem.Write8(dst+i, c.mem.Read8(src+i))
	}
	c.cnt[ChAICA][0] = stag + n
	c.cnt[ChAICA][1] = star + n
	c.cnt[ChAICA][2] = 0
	if c.sink != nil {
		c.sink.RaiseNormal(evtAICADMADone)
	}
	if c.aica != nil {
		c.aica.NotifyG2DMAEnd()
	}
}

// Serialize writes the full register and counter state.
func (c *Controller) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	if len(dst) < SerializeSize {
		return 0
	}
	off := 0
	put := func(v uint32) {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[off:], v)
		off += 4
	}
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		for r := 0; r < 8; r++ {
			put(c.regs[ch][r])
		}
	}
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			put(c.cnt[ch][i])
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		put(c.glob[i])
	}
	put(c.apro)
	var flags uint32
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		if c.busy[ch] {
			flags |= 1 << ch
		}
	}
	put(flags)
	return off
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *Controller) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < SerializeSize {
		return false
	}
	off := 0
	get := func() uint32 {
		v := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[off:])
		off += 4
		return v
	}
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		for r := 0; r < 8; r++ {
			c.regs[ch][r] = get()
		}
	}
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			c.cnt[ch][i] = get()
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.glob[i] = get()
	}
	c.apro = get()
	flags := get()
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		c.busy[ch] = flags&(1<<ch) != 0
	}
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/g2dma/g2dma_test.go ====================

package g2dma

import "testing"

// fakeMem backs the two windows the tests use: AICA space at
// 0x00800000 (2 MB) and main RAM at 0x0C000000 (16 MB), packed
// into one 18 MB slice.
type fakeMem struct{ b []byte }

func newFakeMem() *fakeMem { return &fakeMem{b: make([]byte, 18<<20)} }

func (f *fakeMem) idx(pa uint32) uint32 {
	if pa >= 0x0C000000 {
		return pa - 0x0C000000 + 0x200000
	}
	return pa - 0x00800000
}

func (f *fakeMem) Read8(pa uint32) uint8 { return f.b[f.idx(pa)] }
func (f *fakeMem) Write8(pa uint32, v uint8) {
	f.b[f.idx(pa)] = v
}

func (f *fakeMem) peek(pa uint32) uint8    { return f.b[f.idx(pa)] }
func (f *fakeMem) poke(pa uint32, v uint8) { f.b[f.idx(pa)] = v }

type fakeSink struct{ bits uint32 }

func (s *fakeSink) RaiseNormal(bits uint32) { s.bits |= bits }

type fakeAICA struct{ ends int }

func (a *fakeAICA) NotifyG2DMAEnd() { a.ends++ }

const (
	sbADSTAG = 0x005F7800
	sbADSTAR = 0x005F7804
	sbADLEN  = 0x005F7808
	sbADDIR  = 0x005F780C
	sbADTSEL = 0x005F7810
	sbADEN   = 0x005F7814
	sbADST   = 0x005F7818

	sbE1STAR = 0x005F7824
	sbE1LEN  = 0x005F7828
	sbE1EN   = 0x005F7834
	sbE1ST   = 0x005F7838

	sbADSTAGD = 0x005F78C0
	sbADSTARD = 0x005F78C4
	sbADLEND  = 0x005F78C8
)

func TestAICADMAToWaveRAM(t *testing.T) {
	mem := newFakeMem()
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	aica := &fakeAICA{}
	c := New(mem, aica, sink)

	const sysAddr = 0x0C001000
	const waveAddr = 0x00800000
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		mem.poke(sysAddr+uint32(i), byte(i*3+1))
	}
	c.Write32(sbADEN, 0)
	c.Write32(sbADSTAG, waveAddr)
	c.Write32(sbADSTAR, sysAddr)
	c.Write32(sbADLEN, 64)
	c.Write32(sbADDIR, 0)
	c.Write32(sbADTSEL, 0)
	c.Write32(sbADEN, 1)
	c.Write32(sbADST, 1)

	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		if got := mem.peek(waveAddr + uint32(i)); got != byte(i*3+1) {
			t.Fatalf("wave[%d] = %#x, want %#x", i, got, byte(i*3+1))
		}
	}
	if got := c.Read32(sbADST); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ADST = %#x, want 0 (complete)", got)
	}
	if got := c.Read32(sbADSTAGD); got != waveAddr+64 {
		t.Errorf("ADSTAGD = %#x, want %#x", got, waveAddr+64)
	}
	if got := c.Read32(sbADSTARD); got != sysAddr+64 {
		t.Errorf("ADSTARD = %#x, want %#x", got, sysAddr+64)
	}
	if got := c.Read32(sbADLEND); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ADLEND = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
	if sink.bits&(1<<15) == 0 {
		t.Error("ISTNRM AICA DMA done event was not raised")
	}
	if aica.ends != 1 {
		t.Errorf("AICA DMA end notifications = %d, want 1", aica.ends)
	}
}

func TestAICADMAFromWaveRAM(t *testing.T) {
	mem := newFakeMem()
	c := New(mem, &fakeAICA{}, &fakeSink{})
	const sysAddr = 0x0C002000
	const waveAddr = 0x00801000
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		mem.poke(waveAddr+uint32(i), byte(0xA0+i))
	}
	c.Write32(sbADSTAG, waveAddr)
	c.Write32(sbADSTAR, sysAddr)
	c.Write32(sbADLEN, 32)
	c.Write32(sbADDIR, 1)
	c.Write32(sbADEN, 1)
	c.Write32(sbADST, 1)
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if got := mem.peek(sysAddr + uint32(i)); got != byte(0xA0+i) {
			t.Fatalf("sys[%d] = %#x, want %#x", i, got, byte(0xA0+i))
		}
	}
}

func TestExtChannelBusyForever(t *testing.T) {
	mem := newFakeMem()
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	c := New(mem, &fakeAICA{}, sink)
	c.Write32(sbE1STAR, 0x0C000000)
	c.Write32(sbE1LEN, 64)
	c.Write32(sbE1EN, 1)
	c.Write32(sbE1ST, 1)
	for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
		if got := c.Read32(sbE1ST); got != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("E1ST read %d = %#x, want busy 1", i, got)
		}
	}
	if sink.bits != 0 {
		t.Error("absent-device channel raised a completion event")
	}
	// Clearing the enable drops the busy state in this model.
	c.Write32(sbE1EN, 0)
	if got := c.Read32(sbE1ST); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("E1ST after EN=0 = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	mem := newFakeMem()
	c := New(mem, &fakeAICA{}, &fakeSink{})
	c.Write32(sbADSTAG, 0x00800000)
	c.Write32(sbADLEN, 128)
	c.Write32(sbE1EN, 1)
	c.Write32(sbE1ST, 1)
	b := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if n := c.Serialize(b); n != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d bytes, want %d", n, SerializeSize)
	}
	c2 := New(mem, &fakeAICA{}, &fakeSink{})
	if !c2.Deserialize(b) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize rejected the block")
	}
	if got := c2.Read32(sbADLEN); got != 128 {
		t.Errorf("ADLEN after restore = %#x, want 128", got)
	}
	if got := c2.Read32(sbE1ST); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("E1ST after restore = %#x, want busy 1", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/gd/fixtures_test.go ====================

package gd

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// Synthetic ISO layout used by the tests. Sector numbers are relative
// to the data track start.
const (
	testTotalSectors  = 25
	testRootExtent    = 20
	testRootSize      = 4096 // the root directory spans two sectors on purpose
	testDataExtent    = 22
	testHelloExtent   = 23
	testWorldExtent   = 24
	testRootBExtent   = 21 // second sector of the root directory
	testDataDirSector = testDataExtent
)

var (
	testHelloContent = []byte("Hello, Dreamcast!\nThis is a synthetic test file.\n")
	testWorldContent = func() []byte {
		b := make([]byte, 512)
		for i := range b {
			b[i] = byte(i*7 + 3)
		}
		return b
	}()
)

// buildTestDirRecord builds one ISO9660 directory record. name is the
// raw file identifier: a single 0x00 byte for ".", 0x01 for "..", or
// bytes like "HELLO.TXT;1".
func buildTestDirRecord(extent, size uint32, isDir bool, name []byte) []byte {
	recLen := 33 + len(name)
	if len(name)%2 == 0 {
		recLen++
	}
	rec := make([]byte, recLen)
	rec[0] = byte(recLen)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rec[2:6], extent)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[6:10], extent)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rec[10:14], size)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[14:18], size)
	// Recording date: 2025-06-15 12:00:00 GMT.
	copy(rec[18:25], []byte{125, 6, 15, 12, 0, 0, 0})
	if isDir {
		rec[25] = 0x02
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(rec[28:30], 1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(rec[30:32], 1)
	rec[32] = byte(len(name))
	copy(rec[33:], name)
	return rec
}

// buildTestPVD builds the primary volume descriptor sector.
func buildTestPVD() []byte {
	sec := make([]byte, 2048)
	sec[0] = 1
	copy(sec[1:6], "CD001")
	sec[6] = 1
	for i := 8; i < 72; i++ {
		sec[i] = ' '
	}
	copy(sec[8:], "SEGA")
	copy(sec[40:], "TESTDISC")
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(sec[80:84], testTotalSectors)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(sec[84:88], testTotalSectors)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[104:106], 1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(sec[106:108], 1)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[108:110], 1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(sec[110:112], 1)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[112:114], 2048)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(sec[114:116], 2048)
	root := buildTestDirRecord(testRootExtent, testRootSize, true, []byte{0x00})
	copy(sec[156:], root)
	return sec
}

// buildTestISO builds a complete synthetic ISO image in memory.
// Boot area sectors 0 to 15 are zero; callers may overwrite them.
func buildTestISO() []byte {
	img := make([]byte, testTotalSectors*2048)
	set := func(sector int, data []byte) {
		copy(img[sector*2048:(sector+1)*2048], data)
	}
	set(16, buildTestPVD())

	// Root directory, first sector: dot entries and HELLO.TXT, then
	// zero padding to the end of the sector.
	rootA := make([]byte, 0, 2048)
	rootA = append(rootA, buildTestDirRecord(testRootExtent, testRootSize, true, []byte{0x00})...)
	rootA = append(rootA, buildTestDirRecord(testRootExtent, testRootSize, true, []byte{0x01})...)
	rootA = append(rootA, buildTestDirRecord(testHelloExtent, uint32(len(testHelloContent)), false, []byte("HELLO.TXT;1"))...)
	set(testRootExtent, rootA)

	// Root directory, second sector: the DATA subdirectory entry. This
	// is what makes the fixture exercise multi-sector directories and
	// the zero padding skip.
	rootB := make([]byte, 0, 2048)
	rootB = append(rootB, buildTestDirRecord(testDataExtent, 2048, true, []byte("DATA"))...)
	set(testRootBExtent, rootB)

	// DATA directory.
	dataDir := make([]byte, 0, 2048)
	dataDir = append(dataDir, buildTestDirRecord(testDataExtent, 2048, true, []byte{0x00})...)
	dataDir = append(dataDir, buildTestDirRecord(testRootExtent, testRootSize, true, []byte{0x01})...)
	dataDir = append(dataDir, buildTestDirRecord(testWorldExtent, uint32(len(testWorldContent)), false, []byte("WORLD.BIN;1"))...)
	set(testDataDirSector, dataDir)

	set(testHelloExtent, testHelloContent)
	set(testWorldExtent, testWorldContent)
	return img
}

// wrapRaw2352 wraps 2048 byte sectors into raw 2352 byte Mode 1
// sectors: 12 byte sync, 4 byte header, user data, and 288 bytes of
// error correction filler filling the sector out to 2352 bytes.
func wrapRaw2352(iso []byte) []byte {
	sectors := len(iso) / 2048
	out := make([]byte, 0, sectors*2352)
	sync := []byte{0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00}
	for i := 0; i < sectors; i++ {
		out = append(out, sync...)
		total := i + 150
		out = append(out, byte(total/4500), byte((total/75)%60), byte(total%75), 0x01)
		out = append(out, iso[i*2048:(i+1)*2048]...)
		out = append(out, make([]byte, 288)...)
	}
	return out
}

// wrap2336 wraps 2048 byte sectors into 2336 byte sectors: an 8 byte
// header, user data, and 280 bytes of filler.
func wrap2336(iso []byte) []byte {
	sectors := len(iso) / 2048
	out := make([]byte, 0, sectors*2336)
	for i := 0; i < sectors; i++ {
		hdr := make([]byte, 8)
		hdr[0] = 0x08
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(hdr[4:], uint32(i))
		out = append(out, hdr...)
		out = append(out, iso[i*2048:(i+1)*2048]...)
		out = append(out, make([]byte, 280)...)
	}
	return out
}

// writeTestFile writes data into a fresh temp dir and returns the path.
func writeTestFile(t *testing.T, dir, name string, data []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	p := filepath.Join(dir, name)
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", p, err)
	}
	return p
}

// padField returns s padded with spaces to exactly width bytes, for
// crafting fixed width IP.BIN fields.
func padField(s string, width int) string {
	for len(s) < width {
		s += " "
	}
	return s[:width]
}

// buildTestBootArea crafts a 0x8000 byte boot area with known IP.BIN
// field values at the documented offsets.
func buildTestBootArea() []byte {
	boot := make([]byte, 0x8000)
	put := func(off int, s string, width int) {
		copy(boot[off:off+width], padField(s, width))
	}
	put(0x00, "SEGA SEGAKATANA", 16)
	put(0x10, "TEST MAKER", 16)
	put(0x20, "GD-ROM1/1", 16)
	put(0x30, "JUE", 8)
	put(0x38, "E000F10", 16)
	put(0x48, "T-12345", 10)
	put(0x52, "V1.000", 6)
	put(0x58, "20000101", 8)
	put(0x60, "1ST_READ.BIN", 16)
	put(0x70, "TEST COMPANY", 16)
	put(0x80, "MY TEST GAME", 128)
	return boot
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/gd/gd.go ====================

// Package gd provides GD-ROM and CD image foundations for user supplied
// disc images. It parses .gdi track lists, plain .iso images and raw .bin
// images, reads user data sectors out of any supported sector layout, and
// exposes the Dreamcast boot area and ISO9660 filesystem on top of that
// sector layer. Only the standard library is used, and no disc content is
// bundled with the package: every image is supplied by the user at runtime.
package gd

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// Track describes one track of a disc image.
type Track struct {
	Number     int
	LBA        int    // starting LBA on the disc
	Ctrl       int    // 0 = audio, 4 = data
	SectorSize int    // raw bytes per sector in the file (2048, 2336, 2352)
	File       string // backing file name (for .gdi); empty for single-file images
	Offset     int64  // byte offset of this track's first sector inside File
	Length     int64  // byte length of this track inside File
}

// Image is an opened disc image. The zero value is not usable; call Open.
type Image struct {
	Tracks []Track

	files    map[string]*os.File // keyed by resolved file path
	resolved []string            // resolved backing path per track, parallel to Tracks
}

// Open opens a disc image, dispatching on the file extension.
//
// Supported forms:
//   - .gdi: a GD-ROM track list. Track files are resolved relative to the
//     directory containing the .gdi file.
//   - .iso: a single data track with 2048 byte sectors.
//   - .bin: a single data track with raw 2352 byte sectors. A neighbouring
//     .cue sheet is ignored by design; a lone .bin is treated as raw data.
//   - .cdi: not supported; Open returns a clear error.
func Open(path string) (*Image, error) {
	ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path))
	switch ext {
	case ".gdi":
		return openGDI(path)
	case ".iso":
		return openSingle(path, 2048)
	case ".bin":
		return openSingle(path, 2352)
	case ".cdi":
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: .cdi images are not supported: %s", path)
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: unsupported image extension %q: %s", ext, path)
	}
}

// openSingle opens a single-file image holding one data track.
func openSingle(path string, sectorSize int) (*Image, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: open %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	info, err := f.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		_ = f.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: stat %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if info.IsDir() {
		_ = f.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: %s is a directory, not an image file", path)
	}
	im := &Image{
		Tracks: []Track{{
			Number:     1,
			LBA:        0,
			Ctrl:       4,
			SectorSize: sectorSize,
			File:       "",
			Offset:     0,
			Length:     info.Size(),
		}},
		files:    map[string]*os.File{path: f},
		resolved: []string{path},
	}
	return im, nil
}

// Close releases every backing file held by the image. It is safe to call
// Close more than once.
func (im *Image) Close() error {
	if im == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var firstErr error
	for name, f := range im.files {
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil && firstErr == nil {
			firstErr = fmt.Errorf("gd: close %s: %w", name, err)
		}
	}
	im.files = nil
	return firstErr
}

// DataTrack returns the last track with Ctrl == 4, or nil when the image
// has no data track.
func (im *Image) DataTrack() *Track {
	if im == nil {
		return nil
	}
	for i := len(im.Tracks) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if im.Tracks[i].Ctrl == 4 {
			return &im.Tracks[i]
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// trackForLBA returns the index of the track that owns the given absolute
// LBA. A track owns an LBA when the LBA falls inside the sectors spanned
// by the track's byte length. When several tracks could claim an LBA, the
// one with the highest starting LBA wins.
func (im *Image) trackForLBA(lba int) (int, error) {
	if im == nil {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("gd: nil image")
	}
	best := -1
	for i := range im.Tracks {
		tr := &im.Tracks[i]
		if tr.SectorSize <= 0 {
			continue
		}
		if lba < tr.LBA {
			continue
		}
		sectors := tr.Length / int64(tr.SectorSize)
		if int64(lba-tr.LBA) >= sectors {
			continue
		}
		if best < 0 || tr.LBA > im.Tracks[best].LBA {
			best = i
		}
	}
	if best < 0 {
		return -1, fmt.Errorf("gd: LBA %d is outside every track", lba)
	}
	return best, nil
}

// ReadSector returns exactly 2048 user data bytes for the sector at the
// given absolute LBA, locating the owning track first.
//
// User data is extracted according to the track sector size: 2048 copies
// the sector as-is, 2352 (raw Mode 1) takes bytes 16 to 2064, and 2336
// skips the 8 byte subheader. Reading a sector from an audio track or
// outside the image returns an error.
func (im *Image) ReadSector(lba int) ([]byte, error) {
	idx, err := im.trackForLBA(lba)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	tr := &im.Tracks[idx]
	if tr.Ctrl != 4 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: LBA %d is in audio track %d, no data to read", lba, tr.Number)
	}
	if im.files == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: image is closed")
	}
	f := im.files[im.resolved[idx]]
	if f == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: backing file for track %d is not open", tr.Number)
	}
	raw := make([]byte, tr.SectorSize)
	pos := tr.Offset + int64(lba-tr.LBA)*int64(tr.SectorSize)
	if _, err := f.ReadAt(raw, pos); err != nil && err != io.EOF {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: read LBA %d at offset %d: %w", lba, pos, err)
	} else if err == io.EOF {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: read LBA %d at offset %d: unexpected end of file", lba, pos)
	}
	out := make([]byte, 2048)
	switch tr.SectorSize {
	case 2048:
		copy(out, raw[0:2048])
	case 2352:
		copy(out, raw[16:2064])
	case 2336:
		copy(out, raw[8:2056])
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: unsupported sector size %d on track %d", tr.SectorSize, tr.Number)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// BootArea returns the first 16 sectors (0x8000 bytes) of the data track,
// concatenated. This is the region holding the IP.BIN bootstrap block.
func (im *Image) BootArea() ([]byte, error) {
	dt := im.DataTrack()
	if dt == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: image has no data track")
	}
	out := make([]byte, 0, 0x8000)
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		sec, err := im.ReadSector(dt.LBA + i)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: boot area sector %d: %w", i, err)
		}
		out = append(out, sec...)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// msfToLBA converts a minutes, seconds, frames position to a logical
// block address. Sectors run at 75 frames per second and the data area
// starts 150 sectors in, so 00:02:00 is LBA 0 and 01:00:00 is LBA 4350.
func msfToLBA(m, s, f int) int {
	return (m*60+s)*75 + f - 150
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/gd/gd_test.go ====================

package gd

import (
	"bytes"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func checkISOContents(t *testing.T, im *Image) {
	t.Helper()

	root, err := im.ISOListDir("")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ISOListDir root: %v", err)
	}
	if len(root) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("root listing has %d entries, want 2: %+v", len(root), root)
	}
	byName := make(map[string]ISOEntry)
	for _, e := range root {
		byName[e.Name] = e
	}
	hello, ok := byName["HELLO.TXT"]
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("root listing missing HELLO.TXT: %+v", root)
	}
	if hello.IsDir || hello.Size != len(testHelloContent) {
		t.Errorf("HELLO.TXT entry = %+v, want file of size %d", hello, len(testHelloContent))
	}
	dataEntry, ok := byName["DATA"]
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("root listing missing DATA: %+v", root)
	}
	if !dataEntry.IsDir {
		t.Errorf("DATA entry = %+v, want directory", dataEntry)
	}

	// Root via "/" must match root via "".
	rootSlash, err := im.ISOListDir("/")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ISOListDir /: %v", err)
	}
	if len(rootSlash) != len(root) {
		t.Errorf("ISOListDir / returned %d entries, want %d", len(rootSlash), len(root))
	}

	sub, err := im.ISOListDir("DATA")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ISOListDir DATA: %v", err)
	}
	if len(sub) != 1 || sub[0].Name != "WORLD.BIN" || sub[0].IsDir || sub[0].Size != len(testWorldContent) {
		t.Fatalf("DATA listing = %+v, want one WORLD.BIN file of size %d", sub, len(testWorldContent))
	}

	gotHello, err := im.ISOReadFile("HELLO.TXT")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ISOReadFile HELLO.TXT: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(gotHello, testHelloContent) {
		t.Errorf("HELLO.TXT bytes differ:\n got %q\nwant %q", gotHello, testHelloContent)
	}

	// Case-insensitive lookup with a version suffix.
	gotHelloLower, err := im.ISOReadFile("hello.txt;1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ISOReadFile hello.txt;1: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(gotHelloLower, testHelloContent) {
		t.Errorf("hello.txt;1 bytes differ from HELLO.TXT content")
	}

	gotWorld, err := im.ISOReadFile("DATA/WORLD.BIN")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ISOReadFile DATA/WORLD.BIN: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(gotWorld, testWorldContent) {
		t.Errorf("WORLD.BIN bytes differ: got %d bytes, want %d", len(gotWorld), len(testWorldContent))
	}

	gotWorldLower, err := im.ISOReadFile("data/world.bin")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ISOReadFile data/world.bin: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(gotWorldLower, testWorldContent) {
		t.Errorf("data/world.bin bytes differ from WORLD.BIN content")
	}

	if _, err := im.ISOReadFile("NOPE.TXT"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ISOReadFile NOPE.TXT: expected error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := im.ISOReadFile("DATA"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ISOReadFile DATA (a directory): expected error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := im.ISOListDir("HELLO.TXT"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ISOListDir HELLO.TXT (a file): expected error, got nil")
	}
}

// Test (1): synthetic ISO written as a .iso file.
func TestISOImage(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	iso := buildTestISO()
	path := writeTestFile(t, dir, "test.iso", iso)

	im, err := Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open iso: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()

	dt := im.DataTrack()
	if dt == nil {
		t.Fatal("DataTrack is nil for .iso")
	}
	if dt.SectorSize != 2048 || dt.Ctrl != 4 || dt.LBA != 0 || dt.File != "" {
		t.Errorf("data track = %+v, want LBA 0 ctrl 4 sector size 2048 empty file", dt)
	}

	sec, err := im.ReadSector(16)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadSector 16: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(sec, iso[16*2048:17*2048]) {
		t.Errorf("sector 16 differs from source ISO sector")
	}
	if len(sec) != 2048 {
		t.Errorf("ReadSector returned %d bytes, want 2048", len(sec))
	}
	if _, err := im.ReadSector(testTotalSectors + 10); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadSector past end: expected error, got nil")
	}

	checkISOContents(t, im)
}

// Test (2): the same ISO sectors wrapped in raw 2352 byte sectors.
func TestRawBinImage(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	iso := buildTestISO()
	raw := wrapRaw2352(iso)
	if len(raw) != testTotalSectors*2352 {
		t.Fatalf("raw image is %d bytes, want %d", len(raw), testTotalSectors*2352)
	}
	path := writeTestFile(t, dir, "test.bin", raw)

	im, err := Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open bin: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()

	dt := im.DataTrack()
	if dt == nil || dt.SectorSize != 2352 {
		t.Fatalf("data track = %+v, want sector size 2352", dt)
	}
	for _, lba := range []int{0, 16, testRootExtent, testHelloExtent, testWorldExtent} {
		got, err := im.ReadSector(lba)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("ReadSector %d: %v", lba, err)
		}
		want := iso[lba*2048 : (lba+1)*2048]
		if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("raw sector %d user data differs from ISO sector", lba)
		}
	}
	checkISOContents(t, im)
}

// Test: 2336 byte sectors, reachable only through a .gdi track list.
func TestSector2336ViaGDI(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	data := wrap2336(buildTestISO())
	writeTestFile(t, dir, "data2336.bin", data)
	gdiText := "1\n1 0 4 2336 \"data2336.bin\" 0\n"
	gdiPath := writeTestFile(t, dir, "test.gdi", []byte(gdiText))

	im, err := Open(gdiPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open gdi 2336: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()
	if dt := im.DataTrack(); dt == nil || dt.SectorSize != 2336 {
		t.Fatalf("data track = %+v, want sector size 2336", dt)
	}
	checkISOContents(t, im)
}

func TestMSFToLBA(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		m, s, f, want int
	}{
		{0, 2, 0, 0},
		{1, 0, 0, 4350},
		{0, 2, 1, 1},
		{2, 0, 0, 8850},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := msfToLBA(c.m, c.s, c.f); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("msfToLBA(%d, %d, %d) = %d, want %d", c.m, c.s, c.f, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/gd/gdi.go ====================

package gd

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// openGDI parses a .gdi track list and opens every track file it names.
//
// The format is plain text: the first line is the number of tracks, and
// each following line is
//
//	trackNumber startLBA ctrl sectorSize filename offset
//
// Filenames may be quoted with double quotes, which is how names with
// spaces are stored. Track files are resolved relative to the directory
// containing the .gdi file unless the name is already absolute. The
// stored Offset is used verbatim: absolute LBA maps into the track file
// at Offset + (lba - track.LBA) * SectorSize.
func openGDI(path string) (*Image, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: read gdi %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	tracks, err := parseGDI(string(data))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: parse gdi %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	base := filepath.Dir(path)
	im := &Image{
		files: make(map[string]*os.File),
	}
	for _, tr := range tracks {
		resolved := tr.File
		if !filepath.IsAbs(resolved) {
			resolved = filepath.Join(base, resolved)
		}
		f, ok := im.files[resolved]
		if !ok {
			f, err = os.Open(resolved)
			if err != nil {
				_ = im.Close()
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: open track file %s: %w", resolved, err)
			}
			im.files[resolved] = f
		}
		info, err := f.Stat()
		if err != nil {
			_ = im.Close()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: stat track file %s: %w", resolved, err)
		}
		if tr.Offset < 0 || tr.Offset > info.Size() {
			_ = im.Close()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: track %d offset %d is outside file %s of size %d", tr.Number, tr.Offset, resolved, info.Size())
		}
		tr.Length = info.Size() - tr.Offset
		im.Tracks = append(im.Tracks, tr)
		im.resolved = append(im.resolved, resolved)
	}
	return im, nil
}

// parseGDI parses the text of a .gdi file into tracks. Length is left at
// zero here; openGDI fills it from the backing file size.
func parseGDI(text string) ([]Track, error) {
	var lines []string
	for _, line := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(line, "\r"))
		if line != "" {
			lines = append(lines, line)
		}
	}
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty file")
	}
	count, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.Fields(lines[0])[0])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("first line %q is not a track count", lines[0])
	}
	if count < 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("negative track count %d", count)
	}
	body := lines[1:]
	if len(body) < count {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("declares %d tracks but lists only %d", count, len(body))
	}
	tracks := make([]Track, 0, count)
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		tr, err := parseGDITrackLine(body[i])
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("track line %d: %w", i+2, err)
		}
		tracks = append(tracks, tr)
	}
	return tracks, nil
}

// parseGDITrackLine parses one .gdi track line, handling a quoted
// filename that may contain spaces.
func parseGDITrackLine(line string) (Track, error) {
	var tr Track
	rest := strings.TrimSpace(line)

	nextInt := func(what string) (int64, error) {
		rest = strings.TrimLeft(rest, " \t")
		if rest == "" {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("missing %s", what)
		}
		end := strings.IndexAny(rest, " \t")
		var tok string
		if end < 0 {
			tok = rest
			rest = ""
		} else {
			tok = rest[:end]
			rest = rest[end:]
		}
		v, err := strconv.ParseInt(tok, 10, 64)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("bad %s %q", what, tok)
		}
		return v, nil
	}

	num, err := nextInt("track number")
	if err != nil {
		return tr, err
	}
	tr.Number = int(num)

	lba, err := nextInt("start LBA")
	if err != nil {
		return tr, err
	}
	tr.LBA = int(lba)

	ctrl, err := nextInt("ctrl")
	if err != nil {
		return tr, err
	}
	tr.Ctrl = int(ctrl)

	size, err := nextInt("sector size")
	if err != nil {
		return tr, err
	}
	tr.SectorSize = int(size)

	// Filename: quoted (may contain spaces) or a single bare token.
	rest = strings.TrimLeft(rest, " \t")
	if rest == "" {
		return tr, fmt.Errorf("missing filename")
	}
	if rest[0] == '"' {
		end := strings.Index(rest[1:], `"`)
		if end < 0 {
			return tr, fmt.Errorf("unterminated quoted filename")
		}
		tr.File = rest[1 : 1+end]
		rest = rest[1+end+1:]
	} else {
		end := strings.IndexAny(rest, " \t")
		if end < 0 {
			tr.File = rest
			rest = ""
		} else {
			tr.File = rest[:end]
			rest = rest[end:]
		}
	}
	if tr.File == "" {
		return tr, fmt.Errorf("empty filename")
	}

	rest = strings.TrimSpace(rest)
	if rest != "" {
		off, err := strconv.ParseInt(strings.Fields(rest)[0], 10, 64)
		if err != nil {
			return tr, fmt.Errorf("bad offset %q", rest)
		}
		tr.Offset = off
	}
	return tr, nil
}

package gd

import (
