// Test (3): a .gdi with an audio track and a data track whose file has
// a quoted name containing spaces and a non-zero offset.
func TestGDIImage(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	iso := buildTestISO()
	raw := wrapRaw2352(iso)

	// Audio dummy: ten raw silent sectors.
	audio := make([]byte, 10*2352)
	writeTestFile(t, dir, "track01.raw", audio)

	// Data file: a 123 byte prefix the track offset must skip, then
	// the raw sectors. The file name contains spaces and is quoted
	// in the .gdi, exercising the quoted name parser.
	const dataOffset = 123
	dataFile := make([]byte, 0, dataOffset+len(raw))
	dataFile = append(dataFile, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xAB}, dataOffset)...)
	dataFile = append(dataFile, raw...)
	writeTestFile(t, dir, "track 03 data.bin", dataFile)

	gdiText := "2\n" +
		"1 0 0 2352 \"track01.raw\" 0\n" +
		"3 450 4 2352 \"track 03 data.bin\" 123\n"
	gdiPath := writeTestFile(t, dir, "game.gdi", []byte(gdiText))

	im, err := Open(gdiPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open gdi: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()

	if len(im.Tracks) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("image has %d tracks, want 2", len(im.Tracks))
	}
	if im.Tracks[0].Number != 1 || im.Tracks[0].Ctrl != 0 || im.Tracks[0].LBA != 0 {
		t.Errorf("track 1 = %+v, want number 1 audio at LBA 0", im.Tracks[0])
	}
	dt := im.DataTrack()
	if dt == nil {
		t.Fatal("DataTrack is nil for .gdi")
	}
	if dt.Number != 3 || dt.LBA != 450 || dt.Ctrl != 4 || dt.SectorSize != 2352 {
		t.Errorf("data track = %+v, want number 3 LBA 450 ctrl 4 sector size 2352", dt)
	}
	if dt.File != "track 03 data.bin" {
		t.Errorf("data track file = %q, want %q", dt.File, "track 03 data.bin")
	}
	if dt.Offset != dataOffset {
		t.Errorf("data track offset = %d, want %d", dt.Offset, dataOffset)
	}
	if dt.Length != int64(len(raw)) {
		t.Errorf("data track length = %d, want %d", dt.Length, len(raw))
	}

	// Absolute LBA mapping: the PVD lives at data LBA 450 + 16.
	sec, err := im.ReadSector(450 + 16)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadSector 466: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(sec, iso[16*2048:17*2048]) {
		t.Errorf("sector at absolute LBA 466 differs from ISO sector 16")
	}

	// Audio sectors must be refused.
	if _, err := im.ReadSector(0); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadSector on audio track: expected error, got nil")
	}
	// The gap between the audio track end and the data track start,
	// and space past the end of the disc, must both be refused.
	if _, err := im.ReadSector(100); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadSector in track gap: expected error, got nil")
	}
	if _, err := im.ReadSector(450 + testTotalSectors + 5); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadSector past data track end: expected error, got nil")
	}

	checkISOContents(t, im)
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/gd/ipbin.go ====================

package gd

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// IPBin is the parsed bootstrap block found in the first 16 sectors of a
// Dreamcast data track. Every field is a fixed width, space padded ASCII
// string in the raw block; ParseIPBin trims trailing spaces and NULs.
type IPBin struct {
	HardwareID   string // offset 0x00, 16 bytes, e.g. "SEGA SEGAKATANA "
	MakerID      string // 0x10, 16
	DeviceInfo   string // 0x20, 16
	AreaSymbols  string // 0x30, 8
	Peripherals  string // 0x38, 16
	ProductNo    string // 0x48, 10
	Version      string // 0x52, 6
	ReleaseDate  string // 0x58, 8 (YYYYMMDD)
	BootFilename string // 0x60, 16
	CompanyName  string // 0x70, 16
	Title        string // 0x80, 128
}

// ipField extracts one fixed width field, trimming trailing spaces and
// NUL padding.
func ipField(b []byte, off, length int) string {
	return strings.TrimRight(string(b[off:off+length]), " \x00")
}

// ParseIPBin parses a boot area (or at least its first 0x100 bytes) into
// an IPBin. The block must be at least 0x100 bytes long and its hardware
// ID must begin with "SEGA", otherwise an error is returned.
//
// Note on the company name offset: some references place other data in
// the 0x70 slot, but this package follows the layout in the public API
// contract, where 0x70 holds the 16 byte company name and the title
// follows at 0x80.
func ParseIPBin(b []byte) (*IPBin, error) {
	if len(b) < 0x100 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: IP.BIN block too short: %d bytes, need at least 0x100", len(b))
	}
	if string(b[0x00:0x04]) != "SEGA" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: IP.BIN hardware ID %q does not begin with SEGA", ipField(b, 0x00, 16))
	}
	return &IPBin{
		HardwareID:   ipField(b, 0x00, 16),
		MakerID:      ipField(b, 0x10, 16),
		DeviceInfo:   ipField(b, 0x20, 16),
		AreaSymbols:  ipField(b, 0x30, 8),
		Peripherals:  ipField(b, 0x38, 16),
		ProductNo:    ipField(b, 0x48, 10),
		Version:      ipField(b, 0x52, 6),
		ReleaseDate:  ipField(b, 0x58, 8),
		BootFilename: ipField(b, 0x60, 16),
		CompanyName:  ipField(b, 0x70, 16),
		Title:        ipField(b, 0x80, 128),
	}, nil
}

// IPBin reads the image boot area and parses it with ParseIPBin.
func (im *Image) IPBin() (*IPBin, error) {
	boot, err := im.BootArea()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return ParseIPBin(boot)
}

func TestParseIPBinDirect(t *testing.T) {

		t.Fatalf("ParseIPBin: %v", err)

		t.Errorf("ParseIPBin fields wrong: %+v", *ip)
	}

	ip2, err := ParseIPBin(boot[:0x100])
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseIPBin on exactly 0x100 bytes: %v", err)

==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/gd/iso9660.go ====================

package gd

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// ISOEntry is one entry of an ISO9660 directory listing. Name has any
// version suffix (";1") stripped.
type ISOEntry struct {
	Name  string
	Size  int
	IsDir bool
}

// dirRecord is one parsed ISO9660 directory record.
type dirRecord struct {
	extent uint32
	size   uint32
	flags  byte
	name   string // display name: "." and ".." for the 0x00 and 0x01 ids, otherwise version stripped
	isDir  bool
}

// isoDataTrack returns the data track or an error explaining its absence.
func (im *Image) isoDataTrack() (*Track, error) {
	dt := im.DataTrack()
	if dt == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: image has no data track for ISO9660 access")
	}
	return dt, nil
}

// isoRoot parses the Primary Volume Descriptor at relative sector 16 of
// the data track and returns its root directory record. Sector numbers
// in this file are always relative to the data track start; absolute
// LBA is dataTrack.LBA + relative sector.
func (im *Image) isoRoot() (dirRecord, error) {
	dt, err := im.isoDataTrack()
	if err != nil {
		return dirRecord{}, err
	}
	sec, err := im.ReadSector(dt.LBA + 16)
	if err != nil {
		return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("gd: read volume descriptor: %w", err)
	}
	if sec[0] != 1 {
		return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("gd: sector 16 is not a primary volume descriptor (type %d)", sec[0])
	}
	if string(sec[1:6]) != "CD001" {
		return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("gd: sector 16 has no CD001 identifier")
	}
	// The root directory record sits at offset 156 of the descriptor
	// and is 34 bytes long in practice.
	rec, _, err := parseDirRecord(sec, 156)
	if err != nil {
		return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("gd: parse root directory record: %w", err)
	}
	return rec, nil
}

// parseDirRecord parses the directory record starting at off in data and
// returns the record and its total on-disc length. Both-endian (733)
// fields are read from their little-endian half, per the API contract.
func parseDirRecord(data []byte, off int) (dirRecord, int, error) {
	var rec dirRecord
	if off < 0 || off >= len(data) {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("offset %d outside buffer of %d bytes", off, len(data))
	}
	recLen := int(data[off])
	if recLen == 0 {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("zero length record")
	}
	if recLen < 34 {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("record length %d is below the 34 byte minimum", recLen)
	}
	if off+recLen > len(data) {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("record at %d with length %d overruns buffer of %d bytes", off, recLen, len(data))
	}
	rec.extent = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[off+2 : off+6])
	rec.size = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[off+10 : off+14])
	rec.flags = data[off+25]
	rec.isDir = rec.flags&0x02 != 0
	nameLen := int(data[off+32])
	if 33+nameLen > recLen {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("name length %d overruns record length %d", nameLen, recLen)
	}
	nameBytes := data[off+33 : off+33+nameLen]
	switch {
	case nameLen == 1 && nameBytes[0] == 0x00:
		rec.name = "."
	case nameLen == 1 && nameBytes[0] == 0x01:
		rec.name = ".."
	default:
		rec.name = stripISOVersion(string(nameBytes))
	}
	return rec, recLen, nil
}

// stripISOVersion removes a trailing ";N" version suffix, and a trailing
// dot left behind by names stored as "NAME.;1".
func stripISOVersion(name string) string {
	if idx := strings.Index(name, ";"); idx >= 0 {
		name = name[:idx]
	}
	name = strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".")
	return name
}

// readExtent reads size bytes starting at relative sector extent of the
// data track, spanning as many whole sectors as needed.
func (im *Image) readExtent(extent, size uint32) ([]byte, error) {
	dt, err := im.isoDataTrack()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if size == 0 {
		return []byte{}, nil
	}
	sectors := (int64(size) + 2047) / 2048
	out := make([]byte, 0, sectors*2048)
	for i := int64(0); i < sectors; i++ {
		sec, err := im.ReadSector(dt.LBA + int(extent) + int(i))
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out = append(out, sec...)
	}
	return out[:size], nil
}

// readDirRecords reads and parses every record of the directory stored
// at the given extent. Directories may span several sectors; records
// never cross a sector boundary, so a zero length byte means the rest
// of the current sector is padding.
func (im *Image) readDirRecords(extent, size uint32) ([]dirRecord, error) {
	buf, err := im.readExtent(extent, size)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var records []dirRecord
	for off := 0; off < len(buf); {
		if buf[off] == 0 {
			off = (off/2048 + 1) * 2048
			continue
		}
		rec, recLen, err := parseDirRecord(buf, off)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: directory at extent %d, offset %d: %w", extent, off, err)
		}
		records = append(records, rec)
		off += recLen
	}
	return records, nil
}

// splitISOPath splits a slash separated path into cleaned components.
// Empty components are dropped, so "", "/" and "DATA/" all behave as
// expected.
func splitISOPath(p string) []string {
	p = strings.TrimSpace(p)
	var parts []string
	for _, part := range strings.Split(p, "/") {
		part = strings.TrimSpace(part)
		if part != "" {
			parts = append(parts, part)
		}
	}
	return parts
}

// findEntry locates a child of the directory described by dir, matching
// case-insensitively. Dot entries are skipped.
func (im *Image) findEntry(dir dirRecord, name string) (dirRecord, error) {
	records, err := im.readDirRecords(dir.extent, dir.size)
	if err != nil {
		return dirRecord{}, err
	}
	for _, rec := range records {
		if rec.name == "." || rec.name == ".." {
			continue
		}
		if strings.EqualFold(rec.name, name) {
			return rec, nil
		}
	}
	return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("gd: %q not found", name)
}

// resolveDir walks from the root through each component, which must
// name a directory, and returns the final directory record.
func (im *Image) resolveDir(parts []string) (dirRecord, error) {
	cur, err := im.isoRoot()
	if err != nil {
		return dirRecord{}, err
	}
	for _, part := range parts {
		next, err := im.findEntry(cur, part)
		if err != nil {
			return dirRecord{}, err
		}
		if !next.isDir {
			return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("gd: %q is not a directory", part)
		}
		cur = next
	}
	return cur, nil
}

// ISOListDir lists the directory at path. An empty path or "/" lists the
// root directory. Names are returned with version suffixes stripped and
// the "." and ".." entries omitted.
func (im *Image) ISOListDir(path string) ([]ISOEntry, error) {
	dir, err := im.resolveDir(splitISOPath(path))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	records, err := im.readDirRecords(dir.extent, dir.size)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	entries := make([]ISOEntry, 0, len(records))
	for _, rec := range records {
		if rec.name == "." || rec.name == ".." {
			continue
		}
		entries = append(entries, ISOEntry{
			Name:  rec.name,
			Size:  int(rec.size),
			IsDir: rec.isDir,
		})
	}
	return entries, nil
}

// ISOReadFile reads the file at name, for example "1ST_READ.BIN" or
// "DATA/FOO.TXT". Matching is case-insensitive and a ";1" version suffix
// on any component is ignored.
func (im *Image) ISOReadFile(name string) ([]byte, error) {
	parts := splitISOPath(name)
	if len(parts) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: empty file name")
	}
	for i, part := range parts {
		parts[i] = stripISOVersion(part)
	}
	dir, err := im.resolveDir(parts[:len(parts)-1])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	rec, err := im.findEntry(dir, parts[len(parts)-1])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if rec.isDir {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("gd: %q is a directory", name)
	}
	return im.readExtent(rec.extent, rec.size)
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/holly/holly.go ====================

// Package holly is the Dreamcast system interrupt controller: the
// SB_ISTNRM, SB_ISTEXT, and SB_ISTERR status registers and the
// SB_IML2LVL, SB_IML4LVL, and SB_IML6LVL per-source level mask
// registers at 0xA05F6900, per the published Holly documentation.
//
// Three source banks collect events: normal (ISTNRM), external
// (ISTEXT), and error (ISTERR). The register order in the window
// is ISTNRM at +0x00, ISTEXT at +0x04, ISTERR at +0x08, and each
// mask row holds its three bank words in normal, external, error
// order. (DC-2 had the external and error banks swapped in this
// decode; DC-3 corrects it to the published addresses, which the
// AICA and Maple interrupt paths depend on.) Each bank has one
// mask word per delivery level (2, 4, 6); a set source bit whose
// mask bit is set at any level makes that bank a candidate at the
// highest such level. The winning level across the banks is
// presented to the SH-4 as an IRL-style interrupt: level 6
// arrives as IRL9 with INTEVT 0x320, level 4 as IRL11 with
// INTEVT 0x360, and level 2 as IRL13 with INTEVT 0x3A0, the
// documented external interrupt event codes.
//
// Acknowledgment rules: ISTNRM and ISTERR are write-1-to-clear (a
// handler acknowledges the sources it serviced by writing their
// bits back). ISTEXT bits are owned by the external devices and
// are cleared through ClearExternal, never by a register write.
// ISTNRM reads additionally carry two summary bits: bit 31 set
// while any ISTERR bit is set, bit 30 set while any ISTEXT bit
// is set.
package holly

import "encoding/binary"

// Source banks.
const (
	BankNormal   = 0 // SB_ISTNRM sources
	BankError    = 1 // SB_ISTERR sources
	BankExternal = 2 // SB_ISTEXT sources
)

// ASIC event bit indices in the normal bank, from the published
// ASIC event table (the current KallistiOS numbering, which
// matches the hardware SB_ISTNRM bit assignments).
const (
	EvtRenderDoneVideo = 0  // PVR render finished, video stage
	EvtRenderDoneISP   = 1  // PVR render finished, ISP stage
	EvtRenderDoneTSP   = 2  // PVR render finished, TSP stage (render done)
	EvtVBlankIn        = 3  // SPG vblank-in line reached
	EvtVBlankOut       = 4  // SPG vblank-out line reached
	EvtHBlank          = 5  // SPG hblank position reached
	EvtYUVDone         = 6  // TA YUV conversion finished
	EvtOpaqueDone      = 7  // TA opaque list transfer finished
	EvtOpaqueModDone   = 8  // TA opaque modifier list transfer finished
	EvtTransDone       = 9  // TA translucent list transfer finished
	EvtTransModDone    = 10 // TA translucent modifier list transfer finished
	// EvtPVRDMADone is bit 11 per the published event table.
	// DC-2 and DC-3 carried the channel-2 DMA end value 19
	// here by mistake; nothing in the module ever raised or
	// tested the constant (a module-wide grep at DC-4 time
	// found this declaration as its only use), so DC-4 fixes
	// it to the documented value. Bit 19 is channel-2 DMA end,
	// an event this core does not model.
	EvtPVRDMADone   = 11 // PVR DMA finished (no PVR DMA modeled yet)
	EvtMapleDMADone = 12 // Maple DMA transfer finished
	EvtAICADMADone  = 15 // G2 AICA DMA transfer finished
	EvtPunchDone    = 21 // TA punchthrough list transfer finished
)

// ASIC event bit indices in the error bank (the published table
// numbers error events from 0x200; the bank bit is the event code
// minus 0x200).
const (
	ErrISPOutOfMemory   = 0 // ISP ran out of parameter memory
	ErrStripHalt        = 1 // ISP strip halt
	ErrParamOutOfMemory = 2 // parameter memory exhausted
	ErrOPBOutOfMemory   = 3 // object pointer buffer exhausted
	ErrTAInputError     = 4 // TA input error
	ErrTAInputOverflow  = 5 // TA FIFO overflow
)

// Register offsets inside the controller window at physical
// 0x005F6900.
const (
	regISTNRM = 0x00
	regISTEXT = 0x04
	regISTERR = 0x08
	regIML2   = 0x10 // mask row for level 2, one word per bank
	regIML4   = 0x20 // mask row for level 4
	regIML6   = 0x30 // mask row for level 6
)

// bankForColumn maps a mask word's position inside its row
// (0, 1, 2 for the words at +0x0, +0x4, +0x8) to a bank index.
// The published order is normal, external, error.
func bankForColumn(col uint32) int {
	switch col {
	case 1:
		return BankExternal
	case 2:
		return BankError
	default:
		return BankNormal
	}
}

// levels are the delivery levels indexed by mask row (row 0 is
// IML2LVL, row 1 is IML4LVL, row 2 is IML6LVL), and intevt maps a
// delivery level to the INTEVT code presented to the CPU.
var (
	levels = [3]int{2, 4, 6}
	intevt = map[int]uint32{2: 0x3A0, 4: 0x360, 6: 0x320}
)

// Sink is the CPU-side interrupt endpoint the controller drives.
// RaiseInterrupt latches a request at the given level;
// WithdrawInterrupt drops an unaccepted request whose sources have
// all been acknowledged.
type Sink interface {
	RaiseInterrupt(code uint32, level int)
	WithdrawInterrupt()
}

// SerializeSize is the exact length of a serialized controller:
// three status words and nine mask words.
const SerializeSize = 48

// Controller is the Holly interrupt controller state.
type Controller struct {
	status [3]uint32    // pending source bits per bank
	mask   [3][3]uint32 // mask[row][bank], rows are levels 2, 4, 6
	sink   Sink
}

// New returns a controller presenting interrupts to sink. All
// sources and masks start clear, so nothing is presented until
// software programs the IMLxLVL masks.
func New(sink Sink) *Controller {
	return &Controller{sink: sink}
}

// Raise sets source bits in a bank, as a device event does, and
// re-evaluates what is presented to the CPU.
func (c *Controller) Raise(bank int, bits uint32) {
	if bank < 0 || bank > 2 || bits == 0 {
		return
	}
	c.status[bank] |= bits
	c.update()
}

// ClearExternal clears ISTEXT source bits. External sources are
// acknowledged by their device, not by a write to the status
// register.
func (c *Controller) ClearExternal(bits uint32) {
	c.status[BankExternal] &^= bits
	c.update()
}

// Status returns the raw pending bits of a bank, for tests and
// debugging.
func (c *Controller) Status(bank int) uint32 {
	if bank < 0 || bank > 2 {
		return 0
	}
	return c.status[bank]
}

// Level returns the delivery level currently presented to the
// CPU (0 when no masked source is pending).
func (c *Controller) Level() int {
	win := 0
	for bank := 0; bank < 3; bank++ {
		for row := 0; row < 3; row++ {
			if c.status[bank]&c.mask[row][bank] != 0 && levels[row] > win {
				win = levels[row]
			}
		}
	}
	return win
}

// update re-presents the winning level to the CPU. The previous
// request is withdrawn first: the controller output is a level
// signal, so when the winning source set changes (a higher source
// acknowledged, leaving a lower one), the CPU must see the new
// winner, not the stale latch.
func (c *Controller) update() {
	if c.sink == nil {
		return
	}
	c.sink.WithdrawInterrupt()
	if lvl := c.Level(); lvl > 0 {
		c.sink.RaiseInterrupt(intevt[lvl], lvl)
	}
}

// Read32 reads one controller register by full physical address.
func (c *Controller) Read32(pa uint32) uint32 {
	switch pa & 0x3F {
	case regISTNRM:
		v := c.status[BankNormal]
		if c.status[BankError] != 0 {
			v |= 1 << 31 // error summary
		}
		if c.status[BankExternal] != 0 {
			v |= 1 << 30 // external summary
		}
		return v
	case regISTEXT:
		return c.status[BankExternal]
	case regISTERR:
		return c.status[BankError]
	}
	off := pa & 0x3F
	if row, ok := maskRow(off); ok {
		return c.mask[row][bankForColumn((off&0xF)>>2)]
	}
	return 0
}

// Write32 writes one controller register by full physical address.
// ISTNRM and ISTERR are write-1-to-clear; ISTEXT writes are
// ignored; mask rows store plainly.
func (c *Controller) Write32(pa uint32, v uint32) {
	switch pa & 0x3F {
	case regISTNRM:
		// The summary bits are read-only; mask them out of the
		// clear value so a read-modify-write cannot clear by
		// accident through them (they carry no source bits).
		c.status[BankNormal] &^= v & 0x3FFFFFFF
		c.update()
	case regISTEXT:
		// Owned by the external devices; writes do nothing.
	case regISTERR:
		c.status[BankError] &^= v
		c.update()
	default:
		if row, ok := maskRow(pa & 0x3F); ok {
			c.mask[row][bankForColumn((pa&0xF)>>2)] = v
			c.update()
		}
	}
}

// maskRow maps a register offset to a mask row index.
func maskRow(off uint32) (int, bool) {
	switch {
	case off >= regIML2 && off < regIML2+12:
		return 0, true
	case off >= regIML4 && off < regIML4+12:
		return 1, true
	case off >= regIML6 && off < regIML6+12:
		return 2, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// Serialize writes the controller state: three status words then
// the nine mask words in row-major order.
func (c *Controller) Serialize() []byte {
	b := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[i*4:], c.status[i])
	}
	off := 12
	for row := 0; row < 3; row++ {
		for bank := 0; bank < 3; bank++ {
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[off:], c.mask[row][bank])
			off += 4
		}
	}
	return b
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize and
// re-presents the winning level.
func (c *Controller) Deserialize(b []byte) bool {
	if len(b) != SerializeSize {
		return false
	}
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		c.status[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[i*4:])
	}
	off := 12
	for row := 0; row < 3; row++ {
		for bank := 0; bank < 3; bank++ {
			c.mask[row][bank] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off:])
			off += 4
		}
	}
	c.update()
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/holly/holly_test.go ====================

package holly

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"
)

// Physically addressed register window base used by the tests.
const (
	sbISTNRM  = 0x005F6900
	sbISTEXT  = 0x005F6904
	sbISTERR  = 0x005F6908
	sbIML2NRM = 0x005F6910
	sbIML4NRM = 0x005F6920
	sbIML6NRM = 0x005F6930
	sbIML6ERR = 0x005F6938
	sbIML4EXT = 0x005F6924
)

// fakeSink records the request stream the controller presents.
type fakeSink struct {
	raises    [][2]uint32 // (code, level) per RaiseInterrupt call
	withdraws int
	latched   bool
	code      uint32
	level     int
}

func (s *fakeSink) RaiseInterrupt(code uint32, level int) {
	s.raises = append(s.raises, [2]uint32{code, uint32(level)})
	if !s.latched || level > s.level {
		s.latched = true
		s.code = code
		s.level = level
	}
}

func (s *fakeSink) WithdrawInterrupt() {
	s.withdraws++
	s.latched = false
	s.code = 0
	s.level = 0
}

func TestMaskGatesPresentation(t *testing.T) {
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	c := New(sink)
	c.Raise(BankNormal, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	if sink.latched {
		t.Fatal("unmasked source presented an interrupt")
	}
	// Assign the vblank-in source to level 6: it is presented as
	// IRL9, INTEVT 0x320.
	c.Write32(sbIML6NRM, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	if !sink.latched || sink.code != 0x320 || sink.level != 6 {
		t.Errorf("presented = (%#x, %d, %v), want (0x320, 6, true)", sink.code, sink.level, sink.latched)
	}
	if got := c.Level(); got != 6 {
		t.Errorf("Level = %d, want 6", got)
	}
}

func TestHighestLevelWinsAndRepresents(t *testing.T) {
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	c := New(sink)
	c.Write32(sbIML6NRM, 1<<EvtRenderDoneTSP)
	c.Write32(sbIML4NRM, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	c.Raise(BankNormal, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	if sink.level != 4 || sink.code != 0x360 {
		t.Fatalf("presented = (%#x, %d), want (0x360, 4)", sink.code, sink.level)
	}
	c.Raise(BankNormal, 1<<EvtRenderDoneTSP)
	if sink.level != 6 || sink.code != 0x320 {
		t.Fatalf("presented = (%#x, %d), want (0x320, 6)", sink.code, sink.level)
	}
	// Acknowledge the level 6 source: the level 4 source is
	// re-presented, not lost.
	c.Write32(sbISTNRM, 1<<EvtRenderDoneTSP)
	if !sink.latched || sink.level != 4 || sink.code != 0x360 {
		t.Errorf("after ack presented = (%#x, %d, %v), want (0x360, 4, true)", sink.code, sink.level, sink.latched)
	}
	// Acknowledge the last source: presentation withdraws.
	c.Write32(sbISTNRM, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	if sink.latched {
		t.Error("interrupt still presented after all sources acked")
	}
	if got := c.Read32(sbISTNRM); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ISTNRM = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestWriteOneToClearIsSelective(t *testing.T) {
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	c := New(sink)
	c.Raise(BankNormal, (1<<EvtVBlankIn)|(1<<EvtHBlank))
	c.Write32(sbISTNRM, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	if got := c.Status(BankNormal); got != 1<<EvtHBlank {
		t.Errorf("status = %#x, want only hblank", got)
	}
	// ISTERR clears the same way.
	c.Raise(BankError, 1<<ErrTAInputOverflow)
	c.Write32(sbISTERR, 1<<ErrTAInputOverflow)
	if got := c.Status(BankError); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("error status = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestExternalBankAndSummaryBits(t *testing.T) {
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	c := New(sink)
	c.Raise(BankExternal, 0x40)
	v := c.Read32(sbISTNRM)
	if v&(1<<30) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("ISTNRM = %#x, want external summary bit 30 set", v)
	}
	if got := c.Read32(sbISTEXT); got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("ISTEXT = %#x, want 0x40", got)
	}
	// A register write must not clear external sources.
	c.Write32(sbISTEXT, 0x40)
	if got := c.Status(BankExternal); got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("external status after write = %#x, want 0x40", got)
	}
	// The device clears its own source.
	c.ClearExternal(0x40)
	if got := c.Read32(sbISTNRM); got&(1<<30) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ISTNRM = %#x, summary bit still set", got)
	}
	// Error sources raise the bit 31 summary.
	c.Raise(BankError, 1<<ErrISPOutOfMemory)
	if got := c.Read32(sbISTNRM); got&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("ISTNRM = %#x, want error summary bit 31 set", got)
	}
	// Masked external and error sources present at their levels.
	c.Write32(sbIML4EXT, 0x80)
	c.Raise(BankExternal, 0x80)
	if sink.level != 4 || sink.code != 0x360 {
		t.Errorf("external presented = (%#x, %d), want (0x360, 4)", sink.code, sink.level)
	}
}

func TestMaskRowsArePerBank(t *testing.T) {
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	c := New(sink)
	// A mask word written for the error bank must not enable the
	// same bit in the normal bank.
	c.Write32(sbIML6ERR, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	c.Raise(BankNormal, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	if sink.latched {
		t.Error("normal source presented through the error bank mask")
	}
	c.Raise(BankError, 1<<EvtVBlankIn)
	if !sink.latched || sink.level != 6 {
		t.Errorf("error source presented level = %d, want 6", sink.level)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	c := New(sink)
	c.Write32(sbIML6NRM, 1<<EvtRenderDoneTSP)
	c.Write32(sbIML2NRM, 1<<EvtHBlank)
	c.Raise(BankNormal, (1<<EvtRenderDoneTSP)|(1<<EvtHBlank))
	b := c.Serialize()
	if len(b) != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize len = %d, want %d", len(b), SerializeSize)
	}
	sink2 := &fakeSink{}
	c2 := New(sink2)
	if !c2.Deserialize(b) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize failed")
	}
	if got := c2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, b) {
		t.Error("round trip state differs")
	}
	// The restored controller re-presents its winner (level 6).
	if !sink2.latched || sink2.level != 6 || sink2.code != 0x320 {
		t.Errorf("restored presentation = (%#x, %d, %v)", sink2.code, sink2.level, sink2.latched)
	}
	if c2.Deserialize(b[:SerializeSize-1]) {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted a truncated state")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/libretro/main.go ====================

// Command libretro is the libretro shell for the
// from-scratch Go Dreamcast core (DC-4). It follows the
// family pattern set by the SNES, Genesis, and PS1 shells:
// a c-shared package main exporting the retro_* C ABI,
// with the machine behind it in the system package.
//
// Choices specific to this core:
//
//   - Content loads by path (need_fullpath): a .gdi
//     needs its track files resolved relative to the
//     .gdi's own directory, which only a real path can
//     do. The gd layer opens .gdi, .iso, and .bin images
//     (there is no .cue parser in this core, so cue is
//     not advertised), and the machine boots the disc
//     through the HLE BIOS (system BootDisc). A disc
//     with a missing or malformed IP.BIN is rejected.
//   - Geometry is fixed at 640x480, the PVR Present
//     output, XRGB8888, aspect 4:3 (the app convention).
//   - Timing: the machine frame is a flat budget of
//     3,333,333 SH-4 cycles at the documented 200 MHz
//     nominal clock, so the declared fps is the quotient
//     200,000,000 / 3,333,333 = 60.000006..., declared
//     as computed below rather than rounded to the
//     NTSC 59.94 figure the brief first suggested: the
//     core's own constants give 60.0, not 59.94.
//   - Audio is the AICA's native 44,100 Hz stereo.
//   - The pad maps the libretro standard layout onto
//     the Dreamcast pad: A, B, X, Y, Start, and the
//     dpad from the joypad buttons; the analog triggers
//     from the libretro analog button axes (L2 and R2),
//     falling back to a full press from the digital L
//     and R buttons; the main stick from the left analog
//     axes, scaled to the pad's 0..255 axes with 128
//     centered. The iTaK Go bridge serves only digital
//     joypad state, so through the app the stick reads
//     centered and the triggers read through L and R.
//   - RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM is the 16 MB main RAM;
//     RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM is the live 128 KB VMU
//     image of port 0's storage device.
//   - At unload, the BIOS HLE diagnostics (every
//     unimplemented BIOS call shape the game hit) are
//     printed through the frontend log interface when
//     any were seen, the PS1 core's pattern.
package main

/*
#cgo CFLAGS: -std=c11

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef bool (*godc_environ_cb_t)(unsigned cmd, void *data);
typedef void (*godc_video_refresh_cb_t)(const void *data, unsigned width, unsigned height, size_t pitch);
typedef void (*godc_audio_sample_cb_t)(int16_t left, int16_t right);
typedef size_t (*godc_audio_sample_batch_cb_t)(const int16_t *data, size_t frames);
typedef void (*godc_input_poll_cb_t)(void);
typedef int16_t (*godc_input_state_cb_t)(unsigned port, unsigned device, unsigned index, unsigned id);
typedef void (*godc_log_printf_t)(int level, const char *fmt, ...);

static godc_environ_cb_t godc_environ_cb;
static godc_video_refresh_cb_t godc_video_cb;
static godc_audio_sample_cb_t godc_audio_cb;
static godc_audio_sample_batch_cb_t godc_audio_batch_cb;
static godc_input_poll_cb_t godc_input_poll_cb;
static godc_input_state_cb_t godc_input_state_cb;
static godc_log_printf_t godc_log_fn;

static void godc_set_environ_cb(godc_environ_cb_t cb) { godc_environ_cb = cb; }
static void godc_set_video_cb(godc_video_refresh_cb_t cb) { godc_video_cb = cb; }
static void godc_set_audio_cb(godc_audio_sample_cb_t cb) { godc_audio_cb = cb; }
static void godc_set_audio_batch_cb(godc_audio_sample_batch_cb_t cb) { godc_audio_batch_cb = cb; }
static void godc_set_input_poll_cb(godc_input_poll_cb_t cb) { godc_input_poll_cb = cb; }
static void godc_set_input_state_cb(godc_input_state_cb_t cb) { godc_input_state_cb = cb; }

static bool godc_call_environ(unsigned cmd, void *data) {
	if (!godc_environ_cb) return false;
	return godc_environ_cb(cmd, data);
}
static void godc_call_video(const void *data, unsigned w, unsigned h, size_t pitch) {
	if (godc_video_cb) godc_video_cb(data, w, h, pitch);
}
static void godc_call_audio(int16_t l, int16_t r) {
	if (godc_audio_cb) godc_audio_cb(l, r);
}
static size_t godc_call_audio_batch(const int16_t *data, size_t frames) {
	if (!godc_audio_batch_cb) return 0;
	return godc_audio_batch_cb(data, frames);
}
static void godc_call_input_poll(void) {
	if (godc_input_poll_cb) godc_input_poll_cb();
}
static int16_t godc_call_input_state(unsigned port, unsigned device, unsigned index, unsigned id) {
	if (!godc_input_state_cb) return 0;
	return godc_input_state_cb(port, device, index, id);
}

struct godc_log_callback { godc_log_printf_t log; };
static void godc_grab_log(void *data) {
	struct godc_log_callback *lc = (struct godc_log_callback *)data;
	if (godc_call_environ(27, data)) { // GET_LOG_INTERFACE
		godc_log_fn = lc->log;
	}
}
static void godc_log_msg(int level, const char *msg) {
	if (godc_log_fn) godc_log_fn(level, "%s", msg);
}

struct godc_game_info {
	const char *path;
	const void *data;
	size_t size;
	const char *meta;
};

import "C"

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/system"
)

// libretro constants used by this shell.
const (
	envSetPixelFormat = 10

	pixelFormatXRGB8888 = 1

	deviceJoypad = 1
	deviceAnalog = 5

	// Analog axis indexes: left stick 0, right stick 1,
	// analog buttons (the trigger axes) 2.
	analogLeft   = 0
	analogButton = 2
	analogX      = 0
	analogY      = 1

	// Joypad ids for the analog trigger axes.
	joypadL2 = 12
	joypadR2 = 13

	logInfo = 1
	logWarn = 2

	memSaveRAM   = 0 // RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM
	memSystemRAM = 1 // RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM

	// fps is the machine's frame rate from its own
	// documented constants: 200 MHz nominal SH-4 clock
	// over the 3,333,333 cycle flat frame budget.
	fps = 200_000_000.0 / system.FrameCycles

	sampleRate = 44100 // the AICA's native output rate
)

var (
	sys        *system.Machine
	diagLogged bool
)

// joypadMap pairs libretro joypad ids with the DC pad
// bits they drive. Select (2), L3 (14), and R3 (15) have
// no Dreamcast counterpart and are not mapped.
var joypadMap = []struct {
	id  uint
	bit uint16
}{
	{0, system.BtnB},     // B
	{1, system.BtnY},     // Y
	{3, system.BtnStart}, // Start
	{4, system.BtnUp},    // Up
	{5, system.BtnDown},  // Down
	{6, system.BtnLeft},  // Left
	{7, system.BtnRight}, // Right
	{8, system.BtnA},     // A
	{9, system.BtnX},     // X
	{10, system.BtnLT},   // L (digital trigger fallback)
	{11, system.BtnRT},   // R (digital trigger fallback)
}

// dcLog prints one line through the frontend log
// interface when one was offered.
func dcLog(level int, msg string) {
	cmsg := C.CString(msg)
	C.godc_log_msg(C.int(level), cmsg)
	C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cmsg))
}

// logDiagnostics emits the BIOS HLE's unimplemented
// call tally, once per loaded game, when anything
// unimplemented was seen. The iTaK bridge prints core
// log lines to stderr; RetroArch shows them in its log.
func logDiagnostics() {
	if sys == nil || diagLogged {
		return
	}
	diagLogged = true
	d := sys.BIOSDiagnostics()
	if len(d.Calls) == 0 && d.Overflow == 0 {
		return
	}
	dcLog(logWarn, "[GoDC] "+d.String())
}

// loadPath loads a disc image from a filesystem path
// and boots it through the HLE BIOS. It is the
// Go-level core of retro_load_game, kept plainly typed
// so the shell test can drive it in-process.
func loadPath(path string) bool {
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".gdi", ".iso", ".bin":
	default:
		dcLog(logWarn, "[GoDC] unsupported content: "+path)
		return false
	}
	m := system.New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(path); err != nil {
		dcLog(logWarn, "[GoDC] cannot open disc image: "+err.Error())
		return false
	}
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
		dcLog(logWarn, "[GoDC] disc does not boot: "+err.Error())
		return false
	}
	pf := C.int(pixelFormatXRGB8888)
	C.godc_call_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&pf))
	sys = m
	diagLogged = false
	dcLog(logInfo, "[GoDC] loaded "+path)
	return true
}

// stickAxis reads one libretro analog stick axis as an
// unsigned pad axis byte, 128 centered.
func stickAxis(index, id uint) uint8 {
	v := int(C.godc_call_input_state(0, deviceAnalog, C.uint(index), C.uint(id)))
	return uint8((v >> 8) + 128)
}

// triggerAxis reads one libretro analog trigger axis
// as a 0..255 pull; a zero analog read with the digital
// button down is a full press.
func triggerAxis(id uint, digital bool) uint8 {
	v := int(C.godc_call_input_state(0, deviceAnalog, analogButton, C.uint(id)))
	if v < 0 {
		v = 0
	}
	t := uint8(v >> 7)
	if t == 0 && digital {
		t = 255
	}
	return t
}

// readPad polls the frontend and returns the DC pad
// state for player 0.
func readPad() system.PadState {
	var mask uint16
	down := map[uint]bool{}
	for _, b := range joypadMap {
		if C.godc_call_input_state(0, deviceJoypad, 0, C.uint(b.id)) != 0 {
			mask |= b.bit
			down[b.id] = true
		}
	}
	// The digital trigger buttons also count as held
	// for the trigger fallback even though they are in
	// the map already; the analog read decides.
	return system.PadState{
		Mask:     mask,
		TriggerL: triggerAxis(joypadL2, down[10]),
		TriggerR: triggerAxis(joypadR2, down[11]),
		JoyX:     stickAxis(analogLeft, analogX),
		JoyY:     stickAxis(analogLeft, analogY),
	}
}

// runFrame advances the loaded machine one frame,
// presenting video and audio. It is the Go-level core
// of retro_run.
func runFrame() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	C.godc_call_input_poll()
	sys.SetButtons(readPad())
	sys.RunFrame()
	if fb := sys.Framebuffer(); len(fb) >= system.Width*system.Height {
		C.godc_call_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]), C.uint(system.Width),
			C.uint(system.Height), C.size_t(system.Width*4))
	}
	pairs := sys.AudioBuffer()
	if len(pairs) == 0 {
		return
	}
	flat := make([]int16, 2*len(pairs))
	for i, p := range pairs {
		flat[2*i], flat[2*i+1] = p[0], p[1]
	}
	done := int(C.godc_call_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&flat[0])), C.size_t(len(pairs))))
	for i := done; i < len(pairs); i++ {
		C.godc_call_audio(C.int16_t(pairs[i][0]), C.int16_t(pairs[i][1]))
	}
}

//export retro_api_version
func retro_api_version() C.uint { return 1 }

	// The iTaK bridge calls retro_deinit without a
	// preceding retro_unload_game; emit the

	sys = nil
}

//export retro_serialize_size

	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.StateSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) bool {
	if sys == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	if int(size) < len(state) {
		return false
	}
	C.memcpy(data, unsafe.Pointer(&state[0]), C.size_t(len(state)))
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) bool {
	if sys == nil {
		return false
	}
	return sys.Deserialize(C.GoBytes(data, C.int(size)))
}

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.uint) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		// Port 0's 128 KB VMU image.
		return unsafe.Pointer(&sys.VMUImage()[0])
	case memSystemRAM:
		return unsafe.Pointer(&sys.SystemRAM()[0])
	}
	return nil
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.uint) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.VMUImage()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SystemRAM()))
	}
	return 0
}

func retro_cheat_reset() {}

==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/libretro/main_test.go ====================

package main

// In-process shell gates. The payload is a minimal
// synthetic .iso whose IP.BIN carries a tiny hand
// assembled program (the IP itself is the program: it runs
// straight from the IP image at 0x8C008300), driven
// through the same Go-level load and run functions the
// retro_* exports wrap. The literal C ABI is gated end to
// end by the shared enginetest harness (go_backend), which
// loads the built .so through the production bridge; the
// full boot through the BIOS GD interface is gated in the
// system package (TestDC4Enginetest). This test exists so
// go test alone catches shell regressions: load by path,
// boot, magic word, save state round trip, memory
// regions, clean rejection of bad content.

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/system"
)

// shellISO builds a minimal ISO: the boot area carries a
// valid IP.BIN header plus a tiny program at the entry
// offset that stores a magic word at 0x8C200000 and spins.
//
//	0x300: D103  MOV.L @(3,PC),R1   ; literal at 0x310
//	0x302: D204  MOV.L @(4,PC),R2   ; literal at 0x314
//	0x304: 2122  MOV.L R2,@R1
//	0x306: AFFE  BRA -2              ; spin
//	0x308: 0009  NOP                 ; delay slot
//	0x30A: 0009  NOP
//	0x30C: 0000  pad
//	0x30E: 0000  pad
//	0x310: .long 0x8C200000
//	0x314: .long 0x600DCAFE
func shellISO(t *testing.T) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	img := make([]byte, 20*2048)
	put := func(off int, s string) {
		for len(s) < 16 {
			s += " "
		}
		copy(img[off:off+16], s)
	}
	put(0x00, "SEGA SEGAKATANA")
	put(0x60, "1ST_READ.BIN")
	prog := []uint16{
		0xD103, 0xD204, 0x2122, 0xAFFE, 0x0009,
		0x0009, 0x0000, 0x0000,
		0x0000, 0x8C20, // 0x8C200000
		0xCAFE, 0x600D, // 0x600DCAFE
	}
	for i, w := range prog {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(img[0x300+2*i:], w)
	}
	return img
}

func TestShellLoadBootAndState(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	p := filepath.Join(dir, "game.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, shellISO(t), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !loadPath(p) {
		t.Fatal("loadPath(.iso) returned false")
	}
	defer func() { sys = nil }()
	if sys == nil {
		t.Fatal("machine not set after load")
	}
	if !sys.Booted() {
		t.Error("machine not booted after shell load")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	if got := sys.Bus.Read32(0x0C200000); got != 0x600DCAFE {
		t.Errorf("guest magic = %#08x, want 0x600DCAFE", got)
	}
	if fb := sys.Framebuffer(); len(fb) != system.Width*system.Height {
		t.Errorf("framebuffer length = %d, want %d", len(fb), system.Width*system.Height)
	}

	// Memory regions: 16 MB system RAM, 128 KB VMU image.
	if got := retro_get_memory_size(memSystemRAM); int(got) != 16*1024*1024 {
		t.Errorf("SYSTEM_RAM size = %d, want %d", got, 16*1024*1024)
	}
	if got := retro_get_memory_size(memSaveRAM); int(got) != 128*1024 {
		t.Errorf("SAVE_RAM size = %d, want %d", got, 128*1024)
	}
	if retro_get_memory_data(memSystemRAM) == nil || retro_get_memory_data(memSaveRAM) == nil {
		t.Error("memory data pointer is nil for a documented region")
	}

	// Save state round trip through the machine the shell
	// wraps.
	saved := sys.Serialize()
	if len(saved) != sys.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state length actual %d, want StateSize %d", len(saved), sys.StateSize())
	}
	m2 := system.New()
	if !m2.Deserialize(saved) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize of the shell machine's state failed")
	}
	if again := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(saved, again) {
		t.Error("state bytes differ after a serialize/deserialize round trip")
	}

	// Reset reboots the same disc and the guest runs again.
	sys.Bus.Write32(0x0C200000, 0)
	retro_reset()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	if got := sys.Bus.Read32(0x0C200000); got != 0x600DCAFE {
		t.Errorf("guest magic after reset = %#08x, want 0x600DCAFE", got)
	}
}

func TestShellRejects(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	// An unsupported extension.
	cue := filepath.Join(dir, "game.cue")
	if err := os.WriteFile(cue, []byte("FILE \"game.bin\" BINARY\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if loadPath(cue) {
		t.Error("loadPath(.cue) returned true, want false (no cue parser in this core)")
	}
	// A zeroed ISO: no SEGA header in the IP.BIN.
	zero := filepath.Join(dir, "zero.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(zero, make([]byte, 20*2048), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if loadPath(zero) {
		t.Error("loadPath(zero.iso) returned true, want false")
	}
	// A missing file.
	if loadPath(filepath.Join(dir, "missing.gdi")) {
		t.Error("loadPath(missing.gdi) returned true, want false")
	}
	if sys != nil {
		t.Error("machine set after rejected loads")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/maple/maple.go ====================

// Package maple implements the Dreamcast Maple bus host: the DMA
// table walker and register block at physical 0x005F6C00, one
// controller per port, and one VMU storage device per port on the
// first sub device address, per the official Sega Dev.Box System
// Architecture document (worked examples in section 2.6.8 and the
// Maple register section 8.4.1.2) and the public KallistiOS maple
// headers.
//
// Each of the four ports always answers as a controller at its
// main device address and as a VMU at its first sub device
// address. The VMU holds 256 blocks of 512 bytes (128 KB total).
//
// Simplifications chosen for this implementation, stated plainly:
//
//   - Transfers complete synchronously inside the register write
//     or vblank call that starts them, so SB_MDST never reads
//     back busy.
//   - SB_MSYS powers on as 0x3A980000 (timeout count 0x3A98 in
//     bits 31:16, every other field zero) and stores later writes
//     verbatim. The rate and delay fields are stored only and
//     have no timing effect.
//   - SB_MDAPRO stores writes verbatim without checking the
//     documented security code 0x6155 in bits 31:16. It and
//     SB_MSHTCL are write only and read back zero.
//   - Header pattern values other than zero are treated as
//     pattern zero, the only implemented pattern.
//   - Counter choice: SB_MTXDAD holds the address of the entry
//     being processed while the walk runs and the address just
//     past the last entry when the walk ends. SB_MRXDAD and
//     SB_MRXDBD both hold the receive address of the last entry
//     processed.
//   - All Status replies carry the 28 word device info followed
//     by two condition words: the controller condition words for
//     a controller, two zero words for a VMU.
//   - Get Media Info reports its geometry in payload word 1 as
//     total blocks in the high half and block size in the low
//     half: (256 << 16) | 512. Payload word 2 is zero.
//   - VMU function data in the device info is word 1 =
//     0x00010100 (one in the high half, 256 blocks in the low
//     half), word 2 = 512 (bytes per block), word 3 = 0. The Get
//     Media Info reply is the authoritative geometry source.
//   - Reset and Kill write no reply at all and leave the receive
//     buffer untouched. They also leave the pad state alone.
package maple

import "encoding/binary"

// Memory is the main RAM access the DMA walker uses. Addresses
// are physical.
type Memory interface {
	Read32(pa uint32) uint32
	Write32(pa uint32, v uint32)
}

// EventSink is the Holly normal bank endpoint. Maple DMA done is
// bit 12 (1 << 12), raised once when a table walk completes. The
// bit stays set in Holly until the CPU clears it there.
type EventSink interface {
	RaiseNormal(bits uint32)
	ClearNormal(bits uint32)
}

// PadState is one controller report in the system button mask:
// A 1<<0, B 1<<1, X 1<<2, Y 1<<3, Start 1<<4, Up 1<<5, Down
// 1<<6, Left 1<<7, Right 1<<8, LT 1<<9, RT 1<<10. The analog
// triggers run 0 to 255 and stick value 128 is center.
type PadState struct {
	Buttons  uint16
	TriggerL uint8
	TriggerR uint8
	JoyX     uint8
	JoyY     uint8
}

// Register window base and offsets from it.
const (
	baseAddr = 0x005F6C00

	regMDSTAR = 0x04 // DMA table start address
	regMDTSEL = 0x10 // trigger select: 0 software, 1 vblank
	regMDEN   = 0x14 // DMA enable
	regMDST   = 0x18 // DMA start and busy
	regMSYS   = 0x80 // DMA system settings
	regMST    = 0x84 // line monitor status, read only
	regMSHTCL = 0x88 // hard trigger clear, write only
	regMDAPRO = 0x8C // DMA protect, write only
	regMMSEL  = 0xE8 // mode select
	regMTXDAD = 0xF4 // last transmit table address, read only
	regMRXDAD = 0xF8 // last receive address, read only
	regMRXDBD = 0xFC // last receive buffer address, read only
)

// Main RAM bounds for table and receive addresses.
const (
	ramBase    = 0x0C000000
	ramTop     = 0x0FFFFFFF
	tableTop   = 0x0FFFFFE0
	maxEntries = 4096
)

// Function codes carried in the first payload word of condition,
// media, and block frames.
const (
	funcController = 0x01000000
	funcStorage    = 0x02000000
)

// Command bytes (requests) and response bytes.
const (
	cmdDeviceRequest = 1
	cmdAllStatus     = 2
	cmdReset         = 3
	cmdKill          = 4
	cmdDeviceInfo    = 5
	cmdAllInfo       = 6
	cmdDeviceReply   = 7
	cmdDataTransfer  = 8
	cmdGetCondition  = 9
	cmdGetMediaInfo  = 10
	cmdBlockRead     = 11
	cmdBlockWrite    = 12
	cmdSetCondition  = 14

	respFileError   = 0xFB
	respDeviceError = 0xFC
	respUnknownCmd  = 0xFE
	respNoDevice    = 0xFFFFFFFF
)

// VMU geometry: 256 blocks of 512 bytes is 128 KB per port.
const (
	vmuBlocks    = 256
	vmuBlockSize = 512
	vmuSize      = vmuBlocks * vmuBlockSize
)

// Serialized layout sizes. The register block is ten words, each
// pad packs into eight bytes, then the four VMU images follow.
const (
	serRegsSize = 40
	serPadSize  = 8
	serPadsOff  = serRegsSize
	serVMUOff   = serPadsOff + 4*serPadSize
)

// SerializeSize is the exact byte size of a serialized Maple:
// the register block, four pad states, and four 128 KB VMU
// images. 40 + 32 + 524288 = 524360.
const SerializeSize = serVMUOff + 4*vmuSize

// Maple is the Maple bus host state.
type Maple struct {
	mem  Memory
	sink EventSink

	mdstar uint32
	mdtsel uint32 // bit 0 only
	mden   uint32 // bit 0 only
	msys   uint32
	mmsel  uint32 // bit 0 only
	mshtcl uint32 // stored, write only
	mdapro uint32 // stored, write only
	txdad  uint32
	rxdad  uint32
	rxdbd  uint32

	pads [4]PadState
	vmu  [4][]byte
}

// New returns a Maple host reading and writing main RAM through
// mem and reporting DMA completion to sink. Power on register
// values: SB_MSYS is 0x3A980000 and SB_MMSEL is 1, all other
// registers are zero. Every pad starts centered with no buttons
// pressed and every VMU starts zeroed.
func New(mem Memory, sink EventSink) *Maple {
	m := &Maple{
		mem:   mem,
		sink:  sink,
		msys:  0x3A980000,
		mmsel: 1,
	}
	for i := range m.pads {
		m.pads[i] = PadState{JoyX: 128, JoyY: 128}
	}
	for i := range m.vmu {
		m.vmu[i] = make([]byte, vmuSize)
	}
	return m
}

// Read32 reads one register by full physical address inside the
// window 0x005F6C00 to 0x005F6CFF. Unlisted offsets read zero.
func (m *Maple) Read32(pa uint32) uint32 {
	switch pa & 0xFF {
	case regMDSTAR:
		return m.mdstar
	case regMDTSEL:
		return m.mdtsel
	case regMDEN:
		return m.mden
	case regMDST:
		// Transfers complete synchronously, so busy never reads
		// back set.
		return 0
	case regMSYS:
		return m.msys
	case regMST:
		return 0xFF // line monitor idle
	case regMMSEL:
		return m.mmsel
	case regMTXDAD:
		return m.txdad
	case regMRXDAD:
		return m.rxdad
	case regMRXDBD:
		return m.rxdbd
	}
	// SB_MSHTCL and SB_MDAPRO are write only and read zero, as
	// does every unlisted offset.
	return 0
}

// Write32 writes one register by full physical address. Writing
// 1 to SB_MDST starts a transfer in software trigger mode when
// SB_MDEN is set; in vblank trigger mode SB_MDST writes are
// ignored and OnVblankOut starts the transfer instead.
func (m *Maple) Write32(pa uint32, v uint32) {
	switch pa & 0xFF {
	case regMDSTAR:
		m.mdstar = v
	case regMDTSEL:
		m.mdtsel = v & 1
	case regMDEN:
		m.mden = v & 1
		// Writing 0 aborts. Busy is never latched in this
		// synchronous model, so there is nothing else to clear.
	case regMDST:
		if v&1 != 0 && m.mdtsel == 0 && m.mden == 1 {
			m.doTransfer()
		}
	case regMSYS:
		m.msys = v
	case regMSHTCL:
		m.mshtcl = v
	case regMDAPRO:
		m.mdapro = v
	case regMMSEL:
		m.mmsel = v & 1
	}
	// SB_MST and the three counters are read only; writes to
	// them and to unlisted offsets do nothing.
}

// SetPad records the controller state for a port (0 to 3).
// Out of range ports are ignored.
func (m *Maple) SetPad(port int, p PadState) {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return
	}
	m.pads[port] = p
}

// OnVblankOut is called by the system when a vblank out event
// fires. In vblank trigger mode (SB_MDTSEL bit 0 set) with DMA
// enabled it starts a table walk; in software mode it does
// nothing.
func (m *Maple) OnVblankOut() {
	if m.mdtsel == 1 && m.mden == 1 {
		m.doTransfer()
	}
}

// VMUImage returns the live 128 KB storage image of a port, for
// tests and state code. Out of range ports return nil.
func (m *Maple) VMUImage(port int) []byte {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return nil
	}
	return m.vmu[port]
}

// doTransfer walks the DMA table at SB_MDSTAR. Each entry is a
// header word, a receive address word, then the frame words the
// header counts. The walk stops after the entry whose header has
// bit 31 set. On completion it raises the Holly normal bank
// Maple DMA done event, bit 12.
func (m *Maple) doTransfer() {
	if m.mem == nil {
		return
	}
	addr := m.mdstar
	if addr < ramBase || addr > tableTop {
		// No valid table start, so no walk and no completion
		// event.
		return
	}
	for n := 0; n < maxEntries; n++ {
		header := m.mem.Read32(addr)
		recv := m.mem.Read32(addr + 4)
		frameWords := int(header&0xFF) + 1
		last := header&(1<<31) != 0

		m.txdad = addr
		m.rxdad = recv
		m.rxdbd = recv

		frame := make([]uint32, frameWords)
		for i := range frame {
			frame[i] = m.mem.Read32(addr + 8 + uint32(i)*4)
		}
		m.processFrame(recv, frame)

		addr += uint32(2+frameWords) * 4
		m.txdad = addr
		if last {
			break
		}
		if addr < ramBase || addr > tableTop {
			break
		}
	}
	if m.sink != nil {
		m.sink.RaiseNormal(1 << 12)
	}
}

// validRecv reports whether a receive address sits in main RAM.
// Frames with an address outside main RAM write nothing but are
// still consumed.
func validRecv(recv uint32) bool {
	return recv >= ramBase && recv <= ramTop
}

// processFrame routes and answers one Maple frame. frame[0] is
// the frame header word: command in bits 31:24, recipient in
// bits 23:16, sender in bits 15:8, payload word count in bits
// 7:0. The payload words follow it.
func (m *Maple) processFrame(recv uint32, frame []uint32) {
	if len(frame) == 0 {
		return
	}
	head := frame[0]
	cmd := byte(head >> 24)
	recipient := byte(head >> 16)

	payload := frame[1:]
	if n := int(head & 0xFF); n < len(payload) {
		payload = payload[:n]
	}
	var fn uint32
	if len(payload) > 0 {
		fn = payload[0]
	}

	port := int(recipient>>6) & 3
	hostAddr := byte(port << 6)
	mainAddr := hostAddr | 0x20
	vmuAddr := hostAddr | 0x21

	isVMU := false
	switch recipient {
	case mainAddr:
		// The controller answers.
	case vmuAddr:
		isVMU = true
	default:
		// No device at this address: the documented reply is a
		// single 0xFFFFFFFF word in the receive buffer.
		if validRecv(recv) {
			m.mem.Write32(recv, respNoDevice)
		}
		return
	}
	devAddr := recipient

	switch cmd {
	case cmdDeviceRequest:
		m.writeResponse(recv, cmdDeviceInfo, hostAddr, devAddr, deviceInfoPayload(isVMU))
	case cmdAllStatus:
		info := deviceInfoPayload(isVMU)
		if isVMU {
			info = append(info, 0, 0)
		} else {
			w1, w2 := conditionWords(m.pads[port])
			info = append(info, w1, w2)
		}
		m.writeResponse(recv, cmdAllInfo, hostAddr, devAddr, info)
	case cmdReset, cmdKill:
		// No reply is written and the receive buffer is left
		// untouched.
		return
	case cmdGetCondition:
		if !isVMU && fn == funcController {
			w1, w2 := conditionWords(m.pads[port])
			m.writeResponse(recv, cmdDeviceReply, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn, w1, w2})
		} else {
			m.writeResponse(recv, respDeviceError, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn})
		}
	case cmdGetMediaInfo:
		if isVMU && fn == funcStorage {
			// Word 1: total blocks in the high half, block
			// size in the low half. Word 2 is zero.
			geo := uint32(vmuBlocks<<16) | uint32(vmuBlockSize)
			m.writeResponse(recv, cmdDataTransfer, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn, geo, 0})
		} else {
			m.writeResponse(recv, respDeviceError, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn})
		}
	case cmdBlockRead:
		m.blockRead(recv, hostAddr, devAddr, port, isVMU, payload, fn)
	case cmdBlockWrite:
		m.blockWrite(recv, hostAddr, devAddr, port, isVMU, payload, fn)
	case cmdSetCondition:
		if !isVMU && fn == funcController {
			// Accept on a controller is a no op that replies
			// with the function word only.
			m.writeResponse(recv, cmdDeviceReply, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn})
		} else {
			m.writeResponse(recv, respDeviceError, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn})
		}
	default:
		// Unknown command: response byte 0xFE, no payload.
		m.writeResponse(recv, respUnknownCmd, hostAddr, devAddr, nil)
	}
}

// writeResponse writes one response frame at recv: the header
// word (response byte, host address as recipient, device address
// as sender, payload word count) then the payload words. Nothing
// is written when recv is outside main RAM.
func (m *Maple) writeResponse(recv uint32, resp byte, hostAddr, devAddr byte, payload []uint32) {
	if !validRecv(recv) {
		return
	}
	head := uint32(resp)<<24 | uint32(hostAddr)<<16 | uint32(devAddr)<<8 | uint32(len(payload))
	m.mem.Write32(recv, head)
	for i, w := range payload {
		m.mem.Write32(recv+4+uint32(i)*4, w)
	}
}

// writeFileError writes the 0xFB file error response: payload
// word 0 is the function code, word 1 is the error code word,
// which is zero here.
func (m *Maple) writeFileError(recv uint32, hostAddr, devAddr byte, fn uint32) {
	m.writeResponse(recv, respFileError, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn, 0})
}

// blockAddr splits a block address word: bits 15:0 block number,
// bits 23:16 partition, bits 31:24 phase.
func blockAddr(w uint32) (block, partition, phase uint32) {
	return w & 0xFFFF, (w >> 16) & 0xFF, (w >> 24) & 0xFF
}

// blockRead answers command 11 for the VMU of a port.
func (m *Maple) blockRead(recv uint32, hostAddr, devAddr byte, port int, isVMU bool, payload []uint32, fn uint32) {
	if !isVMU || fn != funcStorage {
		m.writeResponse(recv, respDeviceError, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn})
		return
	}
	if len(payload) < 2 {
		m.writeFileError(recv, hostAddr, devAddr, fn)
		return
	}
	addrWord := payload[1]
	block, partition, phase := blockAddr(addrWord)
	if phase != 0 || partition != 0 || block >= vmuBlocks {
		m.writeFileError(recv, hostAddr, devAddr, fn)
		return
	}
	out := make([]uint32, 0, 130)
	out = append(out, fn, addrWord)
	img := m.vmu[port]
	off := int(block) * vmuBlockSize
	for i := 0; i < vmuBlockSize/4; i++ {
		out = append(out, binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(img[off+i*4:]))
	}
	m.writeResponse(recv, cmdDataTransfer, hostAddr, devAddr, out)
}

// blockWrite answers command 12 for the VMU of a port. A write
// whose data words are missing is reported as a file error.
func (m *Maple) blockWrite(recv uint32, hostAddr, devAddr byte, port int, isVMU bool, payload []uint32, fn uint32) {
	if !isVMU || fn != funcStorage {
		m.writeResponse(recv, respDeviceError, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn})
		return
	}
	if len(payload) < 2 {
		m.writeFileError(recv, hostAddr, devAddr, fn)
		return
	}
	addrWord := payload[1]
	block, partition, phase := blockAddr(addrWord)
	if phase != 0 || partition != 0 || block >= vmuBlocks {
		m.writeFileError(recv, hostAddr, devAddr, fn)
		return
	}
	if len(payload) < 2+vmuBlockSize/4 {
		m.writeFileError(recv, hostAddr, devAddr, fn)
		return
	}
	img := m.vmu[port]
	off := int(block) * vmuBlockSize
	for i := 0; i < vmuBlockSize/4; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(img[off+i*4:], payload[2+i])
	}
	m.writeResponse(recv, cmdDeviceReply, hostAddr, devAddr, []uint32{fn, addrWord})
}

// deviceInfoPayload builds the 28 word (112 byte) device info
// payload shared by Device Request and All Status replies. The
// first four words are the function code and function data. The
// remaining 96 bytes are: area code 0xFF, connector direction
// 0x00, a 30 byte space padded product name, 60 zero bytes of
// product license (left blank on purpose), standby power 43 and
// max power 50 as little endian u16 values, in that order.
func deviceInfoPayload(isVMU bool) []uint32 {
	b := make([]byte, 112)
	var name string
	if isVMU {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[0:], funcStorage)
		// Function data: word 1 holds one in the high half
		// and 256 blocks in the low half, word 2 is the
		// block size in bytes, word 3 is zero.
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[4:], 0x00010100)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[8:], vmuBlockSize)
		name = "Dreamcast VMU"
	} else {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[0:], funcController)
		// The documented controller capability word: buttons
		// and axes bitmask. Words 2 and 3 are zero.
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[4:], 0xFE060F00)
		name = "Dreamcast Controller"
	}
	b[16] = 0xFF // area code: all regions
	b[17] = 0x00 // connector direction
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		b[18+i] = ' '
	}
	copy(b[18:48], name)
	// Bytes 48 to 107 (product license) stay zero.
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[108:], 43) // standby power
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[110:], 50) // max power
	words := make([]uint32, 28)
	for i := range words {
		words[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[i*4:])
	}
	return words
}

// conditionWords converts a PadState into the two controller
// condition words. Word 1 packs the active low button bits in
// the high half, then the right trigger, then the left trigger.
// Word 2 packs the main stick in the low half and the second
// stick, always centered, in the high half.
//
// System mask bits map to wire bits as: A to 1<<2, B to 1<<1,
// X to 1<<10, Y to 1<<9, Start to 1<<3, Up to 1<<4, Down to
// 1<<5, Left to 1<<6, Right to 1<<7. The digital LT and RT
// system bits drive the matching analog trigger to 255 when the
// analog value is lower.
func conditionWords(p PadState) (uint32, uint32) {
	var pressed uint16
	if p.Buttons&(1<<0) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 2 // A
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<1) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 1 // B
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<2) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 10 // X
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<3) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 9 // Y
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<4) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 3 // Start
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<5) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 4 // Up
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<6) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 5 // Down
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<7) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 6 // Left
	}
	if p.Buttons&(1<<8) != 0 {
		pressed |= 1 << 7 // Right
	}
	ltrig := uint32(p.TriggerL)
	if p.Buttons&(1<<9) != 0 && ltrig < 255 {
		ltrig = 255
	}
	rtrig := uint32(p.TriggerR)
	if p.Buttons&(1<<10) != 0 && rtrig < 255 {
		rtrig = 255
	}
	activeLow := uint32(^pressed)
	w1 := activeLow<<16 | rtrig<<8 | ltrig
	w2 := uint32(p.JoyX) | uint32(p.JoyY)<<8 | 128<<16 | 128<<24
	return w1, w2
}

// Serialize writes the Maple state into dst and returns the
// number of bytes written, SerializeSize. It returns 0 and
// writes nothing when dst is too small. Layout:
//
//	words 0 to 9   MDSTAR, MDTSEL, MDEN, MSYS, MMSEL, MSHTCL,
//	                MDAPRO, MTXDAD, MRXDAD, MRXDBD
//	bytes 40 to 71  four pad states, eight bytes each: buttons
//	                as a little endian u16, then TriggerL,
//	                TriggerR, JoyX, JoyY, then two zero bytes
//	bytes 72 on     the four 128 KB VMU images, ports 0 to 3
func (m *Maple) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	if len(dst) < SerializeSize {
		return 0
	}
	regs := []uint32{m.mdstar, m.mdtsel, m.mden, m.msys, m.mmsel,
		m.mshtcl, m.mdapro, m.txdad, m.rxdad, m.rxdbd}
	for i, v := range regs {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[i*4:], v)
	}
	for i, p := range m.pads {
		off := serPadsOff + i*serPadSize
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(dst[off:], p.Buttons)
		dst[off+2] = p.TriggerL
		dst[off+3] = p.TriggerR
		dst[off+4] = p.JoyX
		dst[off+5] = p.JoyY
		dst[off+6] = 0
		dst[off+7] = 0
	}
	for i := range m.vmu {
		copy(dst[serVMUOff+i*vmuSize:], m.vmu[i])
	}
	return SerializeSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It returns
// false and leaves the live state alone when src is shorter
// than SerializeSize.
func (m *Maple) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < SerializeSize {
		return false
	}
	m.mdstar = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[0:])
	m.mdtsel = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[4:])
	m.mden = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[8:])
	m.msys = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[12:])
	m.mmsel = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[16:])
	m.mshtcl = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[20:])
	m.mdapro = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[24:])
	m.txdad = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[28:])
	m.rxdad = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[32:])
	m.rxdbd = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[36:])
	for i := range m.pads {
		off := serPadsOff + i*serPadSize
		m.pads[i] = PadState{
			Buttons:  binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(src[off:]),
			TriggerL: src[off+2],
			TriggerR: src[off+3],
			JoyX:     src[off+4],
			JoyY:     src[off+5],
		}
	}
	for i := range m.vmu {
		copy(m.vmu[i], src[serVMUOff+i*vmuSize:serVMUOff+(i+1)*vmuSize])
	}
	return true
}

package maple

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

const (
	testBase  = 0x005F6C00
	ramWindow = 0x0C000000
	ramSize   = 1 << 20

	tableAddr = 0x0C010000
	recvA     = 0x0C020000
	recvB     = 0x0C021000
)

// fakeMem is a byte slice standing in for the main RAM window.
type fakeMem struct {
	b []byte
}

func newFakeMem() *fakeMem { return &fakeMem{b: make([]byte, ramSize)} }

func (f *fakeMem) Read32(pa uint32) uint32 {
	off := pa - ramWindow
	if off+4 > uint32(len(f.b)) {
		return 0
	}
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(f.b[off:])
}

func (f *fakeMem) Write32(pa uint32, v uint32) {
	off := pa - ramWindow
	if off+4 > uint32(len(f.b)) {
		return
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(f.b[off:], v)
}

// fakeSink records the Holly normal bank bits raised to it.
type fakeSink struct {
	raised  uint32
	cleared uint32
}

func (s *fakeSink) RaiseNormal(bits uint32) { s.raised |= bits }
func (s *fakeSink) ClearNormal(bits uint32) { s.cleared |= bits }

// frame builds a frame word slice: header word then payload.
func frame(cmd, recipient, sender byte, payload ...uint32) []uint32 {
	out := make([]uint32, 0, len(payload)+1)
	head := uint32(cmd)<<24 | uint32(recipient)<<16 | uint32(sender)<<8 | uint32(len(payload))
	return append(append(out, head), payload...)
}

// writeEntry writes one DMA table entry at addr and returns the
// address of the next entry.
func writeEntry(f *fakeMem, addr, recv uint32, last bool, fr []uint32) uint32 {
	hdr := uint32(len(fr) - 1)
	if last {
		hdr |= 1 << 31
	}
	f.Write32(addr, hdr)
	f.Write32(addr+4, recv)
	for i, w := range fr {
		f.Write32(addr+8+uint32(i)*4, w)
	}
	return addr + uint32(2+len(fr))*4
}

// start programs MDSTAR, enables DMA, and fires the software
// trigger.
func start(m *Maple, table uint32) {
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDSTAR, table)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDEN, 1)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDST, 1)
}

// runOne runs a single entry table holding fr with receive
// buffer recv against a fresh Maple on f.
func runOne(f *fakeMem, m *Maple, recv uint32, fr []uint32) {
	writeEntry(f, tableAddr, recv, true, fr)
	start(m, tableAddr)
}

func bytesToWords(b []byte) []uint32 {
	out := make([]uint32, len(b)/4)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[i*4:])
	}
	return out
}

func wordsToBytes(ws []uint32) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, len(ws)*4)
	for i, w := range ws {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[i*4:], w)
	}
	return out
}

// Test 1: Device Request on port 0 returns the controller device
// info and raises the DMA done event.
func TestDeviceRequestPort0(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeMem()
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	m := New(f, sink)

	runOne(f, m, recvA, frame(1, 0x20, 0x00))

	head := f.Read32(recvA)
	wantHead := uint32(5)<<24 | uint32(0x00)<<16 | uint32(0x20)<<8 | 28
	if head != wantHead {
		t.Fatalf("response header = %#08x, want %#08x", head, wantHead)
	}
	if got := f.Read32(recvA + 4); got != 0x01000000 {
		t.Fatalf("function word = %#08x, want 0x01000000", got)
	}
	if got := f.Read32(recvA + 8); got != 0xFE060F00 {
		t.Fatalf("capability word = %#08x, want 0xFE060F00", got)
	}
	if sink.raised&(1<<12) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("sink raised = %#x, want bit 12 set", sink.raised)
	}
	if got := m.Read32(testBase + regMDST); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("MDST after transfer = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
}

// Test 2: Get Condition packs buttons and analogs exactly.
// A and Start pressed, TriggerL 200, TriggerR 0, JoyX 0,
// JoyY 255.
func TestGetCondition(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeMem()
	m := New(f, &fakeSink{})
	m.SetPad(0, PadState{
		Buttons:  (1 << 0) | (1 << 4), // A + Start in the system mask
		TriggerL: 200,
		TriggerR: 0,
		JoyX:     0,
		JoyY:     255,
	})

	runOne(f, m, recvA, frame(9, 0x20, 0x00, 0x01000000))

	head := f.Read32(recvA)
	wantHead := uint32(7)<<24 | uint32(0x20)<<8 | 3
	if head != wantHead {
		t.Fatalf("response header = %#08x, want %#08x", head, wantHead)
	}
	if got := f.Read32(recvA + 4); got != 0x01000000 {
		t.Fatalf("payload word 0 = %#08x, want function 0x01000000", got)
	}
	// Wire bits: A is 1<<2 and Start is 1<<3, so pressed is
	// 0x000C and active low is 0xFFF3. Word 1 is active low in
	// the high half, rtrig 0, ltrig 200.
	wantW1 := uint32(0xFFF3)<<16 | uint32(0)<<8 | 200
	if got := f.Read32(recvA + 8); got != wantW1 {
		t.Fatalf("condition word 1 = %#08x, want %#08x", got, wantW1)
	}
	// Word 2: joyx 0, joyy 255, second stick centered at 128.
	wantW2 := uint32(0) | uint32(255)<<8 | uint32(128)<<16 | uint32(128)<<24
	if got := f.Read32(recvA + 12); got != wantW2 {
		t.Fatalf("condition word 2 = %#08x, want %#08x", got, wantW2)
	}
}

// Test 3: VMU block write then block read through the DMA path
// round trips 512 bytes at block 7.
func TestVMUBlockRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeMem()
	m := New(f, &fakeSink{})

	data := make([]byte, 512)
	for i := range data {
		data[i] = byte(i*3 + 5)
	}
	writePayload := []uint32{0x02000000, 7}
	writePayload = append(writePayload, bytesToWords(data)...)
	runOne(f, m, recvA, frame(12, 0x21, 0x00, writePayload...))

	head := f.Read32(recvA)
	wantHead := uint32(7)<<24 | uint32(0x21)<<8 | 2
	if head != wantHead {
		t.Fatalf("write reply header = %#08x, want %#08x", head, wantHead)
	}
	if got := f.Read32(recvA + 8); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("write reply address echo = %#x, want 7", got)
	}
	img := m.VMUImage(0)
	if img == nil || len(img) != 128*1024 {
		t.Fatalf("VMUImage length = %d, want %d", len(img), 128*1024)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(img[7*512:8*512], data) {
		t.Fatal("VMU image block 7 does not match the written data")
	}

	runOne(f, m, recvB, frame(11, 0x21, 0x00, 0x02000000, 7))
	head = f.Read32(recvB)
	wantHead = uint32(8)<<24 | uint32(0x21)<<8 | 130
	if head != wantHead {
		t.Fatalf("read reply header = %#08x, want %#08x", head, wantHead)
	}
	if got := f.Read32(recvB + 4); got != 0x02000000 {
		t.Fatalf("read reply function = %#08x, want 0x02000000", got)
	}
	if got := f.Read32(recvB + 8); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("read reply address echo = %#x, want 7", got)
	}
	gotWords := make([]uint32, 128)
	for i := range gotWords {
		gotWords[i] = f.Read32(recvB + 12 + uint32(i)*4)
	}
	if got := wordsToBytes(gotWords); !bytes.Equal(got, data) {
		t.Fatal("block read data does not match the written data")
	}
}

// Test 6: a two entry table serves both entries, with the last

// Test 7: serialize and deserialize preserve VMU contents,
// registers, and pad state.
func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeMem()
	m := New(f, &fakeSink{})

	img := m.VMUImage(2)
	for i := 0; i < 512; i++ {
		img[3*512+i] = byte(i ^ 0x5A)
	}
	m.SetPad(3, PadState{Buttons: 0x155, TriggerL: 9, TriggerR: 250, JoyX: 1, JoyY: 254})
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDSTAR, 0x0C030000)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDTSEL, 1)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMSYS, 0x12345678)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDAPRO, 0x61550001)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMMSEL, 0)

	dst := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if n := m.Serialize(dst); n != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize returned %d, want %d", n, SerializeSize)
	}
	if n := m.Serialize(make([]byte, 8)); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize into a short buffer returned %d, want 0", n)
	}

	f2 := newFakeMem()
	m2 := New(f2, &fakeSink{})
	if !m2.Deserialize(dst) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize rejected a valid state")
	}
	if m2.Deserialize(make([]byte, 8)) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a short state")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(m2.VMUImage(2), m.VMUImage(2)) {
		t.Fatal("VMU image did not survive the round trip")
	}
	if got := m2.Read32(testBase + regMDSTAR); got != 0x0C030000 {
		t.Fatalf("MDSTAR = %#x, want 0x0C030000", got)
	}
	if got := m2.Read32(testBase + regMDTSEL); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("MDTSEL = %#x, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := m2.Read32(testBase + regMSYS); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("MSYS = %#x, want 0x12345678", got)
	}
	if got := m2.Read32(testBase + regMMSEL); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("MMSEL = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
	dst2 := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	m2.Serialize(dst2)
	if !bytes.Equal(dst, dst2) {
		t.Fatal("second serialize differs: pad or VMU state did not round trip")
	}
}

// Extra: vblank trigger mode ignores the software start bit and
// runs on OnVblankOut.
func TestVblankTriggerMode(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeMem()

	writeEntry(f, tableAddr, recvA, true, frame(1, 0x20, 0x00))
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDSTAR, tableAddr)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDTSEL, 1)
	m.Write32(testBase+regMDEN, 1)

	m.Write32(testBase+regMDST, 1) // ignored in vblank mode
	if got := f.Read32(recvA); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("receive buffer = %#x after ignored MDST write, want 0", got)
	}
	m.OnVblankOut()
	head := f.Read32(recvA)
	wantHead := uint32(5)<<24 | uint32(0x20)<<8 | 28
	if head != wantHead {
		t.Fatalf("header after vblank = %#08x, want %#08x", head, wantHead)
	}
	if sink.raised&(1<<12) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("sink did not get the DMA done bit after vblank transfer")
	}
}
