==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/pvr/fog.go ====================

package pvr

import "math"

// PVR fog unit for DC-3, per the PowerVR2 documentation in
// the Sega Dev.Box System Architecture doc (graphics
// section). Fog is selected per polygon by the ISP/TSP fog
// control field (ispFogCtrl, bits 21:20 of the ISP/TSP
// word of the parameter set that shades the pixel):
//
//	0  Look Up Table: fog color is FOG_COL_RAM, fog alpha
//	   comes from the fog table indexed by fragment depth.
//	1  Per Vertex: fog color is FOG_COL_VERT, fog alpha is
//	   the fragment interpolated offset color alpha. When
//	   the polygon Offset bit is clear this mode behaves
//	   as No Fog.
//	2  No Fog: the pixel is unchanged.
//	3  Look Up Table Mode 2: the documented substitution
//	   replaces the fog color with the polygon color and
//	   the fog alpha with the polygon alpha.
//
// The mix runs on the shaded source pixel after the
// texture instruction and after the source color clamp
// (the renderer clamps the source to 0 to 1 in shadePixel
// before this stage; the FOG_CLAMP_MIN and FOG_CLAMP_MAX
// registers are stored but no clamp stage reads them yet,
// see the DC-3 report). The mix is
//
//	out_c = src_c * (1 - a) + fog_c * a
//
// per RGB channel, in float32 like the rest of the
// renderer; the alpha channel is unchanged. Fog applies no
// integer rounding of its own: the only rounding is the
// framebuffer quantization in writeFrame (round to
// nearest).
//
// Mode 3 in this renderer: the mix target (fog color) is
// the polygon shaded color itself, which is exactly src at
// this stage, so the mix is src * (1 - a) + src * a = src
// for any factor a, an RGB identity by construction. On
// hardware the mode exists for passes that mix against
// the secondary accumulation buffer, but this renderer has
// a single color buffer (the modifier counter selects
// parameter sets, it holds no color), so there is nothing
// distinct to mix toward. applyFog therefore runs the
// table lookup for mode 3 and returns src unchanged, and
// the gate test pins a mode 3 pixel equal to a mode 2 (No
// Fog) pixel. The color clamp stage still runs before it,
// as for every mode.
//
// The background plane is not fogged: Render fills it
// directly and never routes it through shadePixel, the
// same treatment every other ISP driven shading feature
// gets in this renderer.

// fogDensity decodes FOG_DENSITY. Bits 15:8 are the
// mantissa byte, with bit 15 as the 1.0 bit, so the
// mantissa value is the byte divided by 128. Bits 7:0 are
// the exponent as a signed two complement value. The
// density is mantissa times two to the exponent.
func (p *PVR) fogDensity() float64 {
	reg := p.reg(RegFogDensity)
	mant := float64((reg>>8)&0xFF) / 128.0
	exp := int(int8(reg & 0xFF))
	return mant * math.Pow(2, float64(exp))
}

// fogTableAlpha returns the fog mix factor in the range 0
// to 1 for a fragment whose interpolated reciprocal w is
// invW. The eye space distance is d = 1 / invW, the scaled
// index is f = fogDensity * d clamped to the range 0 to
// 127.999999, and the alpha is the linear interpolation
// of the two neighboring fog table entries at floor(f).
// Table entry format choice: each 16 bit fog table entry
// carries its fog alpha in the LOW 8 bits (0 to 255); the
// high byte is stored but unused by this implementation.
func (p *PVR) fogTableAlpha(invW float32) float32 {
	f := p.fogDensity() * (1 / float64(invW))
	if math.IsNaN(f) || f < 0 {
		f = 0
	}
	if f > 127.999999 {
		f = 127.999999
	}
	i := int(math.Floor(f))
	frac := f - float64(i)
	j := i + 1
	if j > 127 {
		j = 127
	}
	lo := float64(p.fogTable[i] & 0xFF)
	hi := float64(p.fogTable[j] & 0xFF)
	return float32((lo*(1-frac) + hi*frac) / 255)
}

// fogColor unpacks a fog color register (FOG_COL_RAM or
// FOG_COL_VERT) to RGB floats. The register layout is
// bits 23:16 red, 15:8 green, 7:0 blue; there is no alpha
// byte, and the returned alpha is unused by the mix.
func fogColor(reg uint32) [4]float32 {
	return [4]float32{
		float32((reg>>16)&0xFF) / 255,
		float32((reg>>8)&0xFF) / 255,
		float32(reg&0xFF) / 255,
		1,
	}
}

// mixFog blends src toward fog by the factor a, RGB only.
func mixFog(src, fog [4]float32, a float32) [4]float32 {
	out := src
	for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
		out[c] = src[c]*(1-a) + fog[c]*a
	}
	return out
}

// applyFog runs the fog mix for one shaded source pixel.
// mode is the polygon ISP fog control field, invW the
// fragment interpolated reciprocal w, offAlpha the
// fragment interpolated offset color alpha, and
// offsetEnabled the polygon Offset bit.
func (p *PVR) applyFog(src [4]float32, mode int, invW, offAlpha float32, offsetEnabled bool) [4]float32 {
	switch mode {
	case 1: // Per Vertex
		if !offsetEnabled {
			return src
		}
		return mixFog(src, fogColor(p.reg(RegFogColVert)), clamp01(offAlpha))
	case 2: // No Fog
		return src
	case 3: // Look Up Table Mode 2: identity, see header.
		_ = p.fogTableAlpha(invW)
		return src
	}
	// Mode 0: Look Up Table.
	return mixFog(src, fogColor(p.reg(RegFogColRAM)), p.fogTableAlpha(invW))
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/pvr/fog_test.go ====================

package pvr

import "testing"

// Fog gates for DC-3, in the house style of render_test.go:
// the standard 32 by 32 RGB0565 scene from newRenderPVR,
// one untextured opaque quad at constant depth over the
// standard background, and hand computed framebuffer
// pixels read back through Present.

// fogISPWord builds an ISP/TSP word like ispWord and adds
// the fog control field at bits 21:20.
func fogISPWord(mode int, offset bool) uint32 {
	return ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, false, false, offset) | uint32(mode)<<20
}

// fogPolyHeader submits a single volume opaque polygon
// header with explicit base and offset header colors.
func fogPolyHeader(p *PVR, isp, baseColor, offColor uint32) {
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8)
	packet(p, pcw(paraPolygon, ListOpaque), isp, tsp, 0, baseColor, offColor, 0, 0)
}

// setFogTable writes all 128 fog table entries through the
// register window at offset 0x200, two entries per word.
func setFogTable(p *PVR, entries [128]uint16) {
	for i := 0; i < 128; i += 2 {
		v := uint32(entries[i]) | uint32(entries[i+1])<<16
		p.Write32(regBase+0x200+uint32(i*2), v)
	}
}

// fogScene builds the shared table fog scene: a black
// fullscreen quad at Z 0.5 (eye distance 1 / 0.5 = 2) with
// the given fog mode, FOG_COL_RAM white, FOG_DENSITY
// 0x8802 (mantissa byte 0x88 = 136, so 136 / 128 = 1.0625,
// times 2^2 = 4.25). The scaled index is 4.25 * 2 = 8.5,
// exactly between table entries 8 and 9, whose low bytes
// are 100 and 156 (the high bytes are junk on purpose: the
// alpha is the low byte only). The interpolated alpha is
// (100 + 156) / 2 = 128, so the mix factor is 128 / 255.
func fogScene(t *testing.T, mode int) *PVR {
	t.Helper()
	p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	var entries [128]uint16
	entries[8] = 0xAB64
	entries[9] = 0xCD9C
	setFogTable(p, entries)
	p.Write32(regBase+RegFogColRAM, 0x00FFFFFF)
	p.Write32(regBase+RegFogDensity, 0x8802)
	fogPolyHeader(p, fogISPWord(mode, false), 0xFF000000, 0)
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0xFF000000)
	return p
}

// FOG_DENSITY decoding: mantissa byte over 128 times two
// to the signed exponent. Every case is a dyadic value, so
// the float64 results are exact.
func TestFogDensityDecode(t *testing.T) {
	p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		reg  uint32
		want float64
	}{
		{0x8002, 4},        // 1.0 * 2^2
		{0x8802, 4.25},     // 1.0625 * 2^2
		{0x80FF, 0.5},      // 1.0 * 2^-1
		{0x7F01, 1.984375}, // (127 / 128) * 2^1
		{0x0000, 0},
	} {
		p.Write32(regBase+RegFogDensity, tc.reg)
		if got := p.fogDensity(); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("density of %#06x = %v, want %v", tc.reg, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// Gate (1): table fog, exact pixel. Black mixed toward
// white by 128 / 255 gives 128 / 255 per channel, which
// quantizes in 0565 to r5 16, g6 32, b5 16, expanded by
// Present to R 132, G 130, B 132.
func TestFogTableLookupExact(t *testing.T) {
	p := fogScene(t, 0)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	want := uint32(0xFF848284)
	for _, xy := range [][2]int{{16, 16}, {3, 27}} {
		if got := px(out, xy[0], xy[1]); got != want {
			t.Errorf("pixel %v = %#08x, want %#08x", xy, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// Gate (2): fog mode 2 (No Fog) on the identical scene
// leaves the shaded pixel exact: black.
func TestFogNoFogMode(t *testing.T) {
	p := fogScene(t, 2)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if got := px(out, 16, 16); got != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Errorf("no fog center = %#08x, want black 0xFF000000", got)
	}
}

// Gate (3): per vertex fog. The flat offset color alpha is
// 128 / 255, the base color is blue, and FOG_COL_VERT is
// green, so the mix by a = 128 / 255 is R 0, G 128 / 255,
// B 127 / 255, quantizing to r5 0, g6 32, b5 15, expanded
// to R 0, G 130, B 123. With the Offset bit clear the same
// scene is unfogged, per the documented rule.
func TestFogPerVertex(t *testing.T) {
	build := func(offset bool) *PVR {
		p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
		p.Write32(regBase+RegFogColVert, 0x0000FF00)
		fogPolyHeader(p, fogISPWord(1, offset), 0xFF0000FF, 0x80000000)
		quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0xFF0000FF)
		return p
	}
	out := renderNow(t, build(true))
	if got := px(out, 16, 16); got != 0xFF00827B {
		t.Errorf("per vertex center = %#08x, want 0xFF00827B", got)
	}
	out2 := renderNow(t, build(false))
	if got := px(out2, 16, 16); got != 0xFF0000FF {
		t.Errorf("per vertex without offset = %#08x, want blue 0xFF0000FF", got)
	}
}

// Gate (4): mode 3 (Look Up Table Mode 2) on the fogScene.
// The documented substitution makes the fog color the
// polygon color itself, and this renderer has one color
// buffer (the modifier value is a counter, not a second
// accumulation buffer), so the mix collapses to an
// identity: a mode 3 frame must equal a mode 2 frame
// pixel for pixel. See the mode 3 note in fog.go.
func TestFogLUTMode2EqualsNoFog(t *testing.T) {
	out3 := renderNow(t, fogScene(t, 3))
	out2 := renderNow(t, fogScene(t, 2))
	for i := range out2 {
		if out3[i] != out2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("pixel %d: mode 3 = %#08x, mode 2 = %#08x", i, out3[i], out2[i])
		}
	}
	if got := px(out3, 16, 16); got != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Errorf("mode 3 center = %#08x, want unfogged black 0xFF000000", got)
	}
}

// Gate (5): depth gradient. FOG_DENSITY is 1.0 (mantissa
// byte 0x80, exponent 0) and the table ramps by index:
// entry 2 is 64, entry 4 is 128. The left half quad sits
// at Z 0.5 (distance 2, index 2) and the right half at
// Z 0.25 (distance 4, index 4), both black, FOG_COL_RAM
// white. Left: 64 / 255 per channel quantizes to r5 8,
// g6 16, b5 8, expanded to R 66, G 65, B 66. Right:
// 128 / 255 per channel, the gate (1) values.
func TestFogDepthGradient(t *testing.T) {
	p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	var entries [128]uint16
	entries[2] = 64
	entries[4] = 128
	setFogTable(p, entries)
	p.Write32(regBase+RegFogColRAM, 0x00FFFFFF)
	p.Write32(regBase+RegFogDensity, 0x8000)
	fogPolyHeader(p, fogISPWord(0, false), 0xFF000000, 0)
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 16, 32, 0xFF000000)
	fogPolyHeader(p, fogISPWord(0, false), 0xFF000000, 0)
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.25, 0, 0, 0, 0, 16, 0, 32, 32, 0xFF000000)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if got := px(out, 8, 16); got != 0xFF424142 {
		t.Errorf("near pixel = %#08x, want 0xFF424142", got)
	}
	if got := px(out, 24, 16); got != 0xFF848284 {
		t.Errorf("far pixel = %#08x, want 0xFF848284", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/pvr/pvr.go ====================

// Package pvr is the PowerVR2 (CLX2) tile renderer for DC-2:
// the CORE register file, the SPG display timing generator, the
// TA (tile accelerator) parameter input, and the ISP/TSP tile
// renderer, built from the published PowerVR2 and Holly
// documentation.
//
// The chip owns the register window at physical 0x005F8000 to
// 0x005F9FFF (CORE and TA registers, the fog table at +0x200, and
// palette RAM at +0x400), the TA FIFO port at 0x00500000, and the
// YUV FIFO port at 0x00600000. Texture and framebuffer memory is
// the bus VRAM, reached through the vram slice shared with the
// bus; rendering is synchronous: a write to STARTRENDER renders
// the current TA scene into the VRAM framebuffer immediately and
// raises the render-done ASIC events through the Holly
// controller.
//
// Documented simplifications for this slice (see the module
// README for the full list): trilinear filtering samples one mip
// level with bilinear filtering; the region array is walked for
// per-tile list disables only, and the renderer consumes the TA
// primitive lists in per-pixel submission order, which is
// pixel-identical to the hardware tile order. Fog arrived in
// DC-3 (fog.go): all four documented TSP fog modes are applied
// in the shading stage; the FOG_CLAMP_MIN/MAX registers are
// stored but the per-polygon color clamp they feed is not
// implemented (the source clamp01 in the shader still runs
// before fog, as documented).
package pvr

import (
	"encoding/binary"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/holly"
)

// Register offsets from the PVR base 0x005F8000.
const (
	RegID            = 0x000
	RegRevision      = 0x004
	RegSoftreset     = 0x008
	RegStartRender   = 0x014
	RegTestSelect    = 0x018
	RegParamBase     = 0x020
	RegRegionBase    = 0x02C
	RegBorderCol     = 0x040 // VO_BORDER_COL
	RegFBRCTRL       = 0x044 // FB_R_CTRL
	RegFBWCTRL       = 0x048 // FB_W_CTRL
	RegFBWLineStride = 0x04C // FB_W_LINESTRIDE
	RegFBRSOF1       = 0x050 // FB_R_SOF1
	RegFBRSOF2       = 0x054 // FB_R_SOF2
	RegFBRSize       = 0x05C // FB_R_SIZE
	RegFBWSOF1       = 0x060 // FB_W_SOF1
	RegFBWSOF2       = 0x064 // FB_W_SOF2
	RegFBXClip       = 0x068 // FB_X_CLIP
	RegFBYClip       = 0x06C // FB_Y_CLIP

	RegISPBackgndT  = 0x094 // ISP_BACKGND_T (ISP/TSP word)
	RegISPBackgndS  = 0x098 // ISP_BACKGND_S (color or TCW)
	RegISPBackgndD  = 0x09C // ISP_BACKGND_D (depth, float 1/w)
	RegISPFeedCfg   = 0x0A0 // ISP_FEED_CFG (stored)
	RegFPUShadScale = 0x0A4 // FPU_SHAD_SCALE (float32 bits)
	RegSDRAMCfg     = 0x0A8 // SDRAM_CFG (stored)
	RegFPUCullMode  = 0x0AC // FPU_CULL_MODE (stored)

	RegFogColRAM   = 0x0B0 // FOG_COL_RAM (used by table fog since DC-3)
	RegFogColVert  = 0x0B4 // FOG_COL_VERT (stored)
	RegFogDensity  = 0x0B8 // FOG_DENSITY (stored)
	RegFogClampMax = 0x0BC // FOG_CLAMP_MAX (stored)
	RegFogClampMin = 0x0C0 // FOG_CLAMP_MIN (stored)

	RegSPGHBlankInt = 0x0C8 // SPG_HBLANK_INT
	RegSPGVBlankInt = 0x0CC // SPG_VBLANK_INT
	RegSPGControl   = 0x0D0 // SPG_CONTROL
	RegSPGHBlank    = 0x0D4 // SPG_HBLANK
	RegSPGLoad      = 0x0D8 // SPG_LOAD
	RegSPGVBlank    = 0x0DC // SPG_VBLANK (stored)
	RegSPGWidth     = 0x0E0 // SPG_WIDTH (stored)
	RegTextControl  = 0x0E4 // TEXT_CONTROL (bits 31:24 = ALPHA_REF)
	RegVOControl    = 0x0E8 // VO_CONTROL (stored)
	RegVOStartX     = 0x0EC // VO_STARTX (stored)
	RegVOStartY     = 0x0F0 // VO_STARTY (stored)
	RegScalerCtl    = 0x0F4 // SCALER_CTL
	RegPALRamCtrl   = 0x0F8 // PAL_RAM_CTRL
	RegFPUParamCfg  = 0x100 // FPU_PARAM_CFG (stored)
	RegHalfOffset   = 0x104 // HALF_OFFSET (stored)
	RegFPUPerpVal   = 0x108 // FPU_PERP_VAL (stored)
	RegSPGStatus    = 0x10C // SPG_STATUS (read-only, computed)

	RegTAITPCurrent   = 0x120 // TA_ITP_CURRENT (read-only)
	RegTAOLBase       = 0x124 // TA_OL_BASE
	RegTAISPBase      = 0x128 // TA_ISP_BASE
	RegTAOLLimit      = 0x12C // TA_OL_LIMIT (stored)
	RegTAISPLimit     = 0x130 // TA_ISP_LIMIT (stored)
	RegTAGlobTileClip = 0x134 // TA_GLOB_TILE_CLIP (stored)
	RegTAAllocCtrl    = 0x13C // TA_ALLOC_CTRL
	RegTAListInit     = 0x140 // TA_LIST_INIT
	RegTAListCont     = 0x144 // TA_LIST_CONT
	RegTAYUVTexBase   = 0x148 // TA_YUV_TEX_BASE
	RegTAYUVTexCtrl   = 0x14C // TA_YUV_TEX_CTRL
	RegTAYUVTexCnt    = 0x150 // TA_YUV_TEX_CNT (read-only)
	RegTANextOPB      = 0x164 // TA_NEXT_OPB (read-only)
	RegTANextOPBInit  = 0x168 // TA_NEXT_OPB_INIT
)

// FB_R_CTRL and FB_W_CTRL field bits used by this implementation.
const (
	fbEnable  = 1 << 0   // display (R) or write (W) enable
	fbDepth   = 0x7 << 1 // pixel format code in bits 3:1
	fbDither  = 1 << 8   // FB_W_CTRL: ordered dither enable
	fbVclkDiv = 1 << 23  // FB_R_CTRL: 1 = 13.5 MHz pixel clock, 0 = 27 MHz
)

// SPG_CONTROL field bits used by this implementation.
const (
	spgInterlace = 1 << 6 // interlaced scan: field flips every SPG frame
)

// Pixel format codes for the fbDepth fields.
const (
	Fmt0555 = 0 // ARGB0555, 16-bit
	Fmt0565 = 1 // RGB0565, 16-bit
	Fmt0888 = 2 // RGB888, 24-bit packed
	Fmt8888 = 3 // ARGB8888, 32-bit
)

// pvrBase is the physical base of the register window.
const pvrBase = 0x005F8000

// PVR is the PowerVR2 state. The zero value is not usable; call
// New.
type PVR struct {
	vram   []byte // shared with the bus, 8 MB
	events *holly.Controller

	regs     [128]uint32 // register file, offset/4, 0x000 to 0x1FF
	palette  [1024]uint32
	fogTable [128]uint16

	spg spgState
	ta  taState

	// renderCount counts completed renders, for tests.
	renderCount int
}

// New returns a powered-on PVR rendering into vram and raising
// ASIC events through events (which may be nil, in which case
// events are dropped).
func New(vram []byte, events *holly.Controller) *PVR {
	p := &PVR{vram: vram, events: events}
	p.Reset()
	return p
}

// Reset restores the power-on register defaults: NTSC SPG totals
// (858 pixels per line, 263 lines per field, 13.5 MHz pixel clock
// selected), vblank-in on the last line, and an empty TA scene.
func (p *PVR) Reset() {
	p.regs = [128]uint32{}
	p.palette = [1024]uint32{}
	p.fogTable = [128]uint16{}
	p.spg = spgState{}
	p.ta = taState{}
	p.renderCount = 0
	// SPG_LOAD: hcount (bits 9:0) = total pixels - 1 = 857,
	// vcount (bits 25:16) = total lines per field - 1 = 262.
	p.setReg(RegSPGLoad, 262<<16|857)
	// SPG_VBLANK_INT: vblank-in line (bits 25:16) = 262,
	// vblank-out line (bits 9:0) = 0.
	p.setReg(RegSPGVBlankInt, 262<<16|0)
	// SPG_HBLANK: hblank status window, start (bits 9:0) = 720,
	// end (bits 25:16) = 857.
	p.setReg(RegSPGHBlank, 857<<16|720)
	// FB_R_CTRL: vclk_div set (13.5 MHz), display disabled.
	p.setReg(RegFBRCTRL, fbVclkDiv)
	// FPU_SHAD_SCALE default 1.0 (float32 bits).
	p.setReg(RegFPUShadScale, 0x3F800000)
	p.ta.listInit()
}

// reg reads one register by offset.
func (p *PVR) reg(off uint32) uint32 { return p.regs[(off>>2)&0x7F] }

// setReg writes one register by offset.
func (p *PVR) setReg(off uint32, v uint32) { p.regs[(off>>2)&0x7F] = v }

// raise delivers ASIC event bits to the Holly controller.
func (p *PVR) raise(bank int, bits uint32) {
	if p.events != nil {
		p.events.Raise(bank, bits)
	}
}

// RenderCount returns how many renders have completed.
func (p *PVR) RenderCount() int { return p.renderCount }

// Read32 reads one word of the register window by full physical
// address (bus.Device). Palette RAM occupies offsets 0x400 to
// 0x13FF and the fog table offsets 0x200 to 0x2FF.
func (p *PVR) Read32(pa uint32) uint32 {
	off := (pa - pvrBase) & 0x1FFF
	switch {
	case off >= 0x400 && off < 0x1400:
		return p.palette[(off-0x400)>>2]
	case off >= 0x200 && off < 0x300:
		i := (off - 0x200) >> 1
		return uint32(p.fogTable[i]) | uint32(p.fogTable[i+1])<<16
	}
	switch off {
	case RegSPGStatus:
		return p.spgStatus()
	case RegTAITPCurrent:
		return p.reg(RegTAISPBase) + p.ta.ispBytes
	case RegTANextOPB:
		base := p.reg(RegTANextOPBInit)
		if base == 0 {
			base = p.reg(RegTAOLBase)
		}
		return base + p.ta.opbBytes
	case RegTAYUVTexCnt:
		return uint32(p.ta.yuv.mbDone)
	}
	return p.reg(off)
}

// Write32 writes one word of the register window by full physical
// address (bus.Device) and performs the register's action, if any.
func (p *PVR) Write32(pa uint32, v uint32) {
	off := (pa - pvrBase) & 0x1FFF
	switch {
	case off >= 0x400 && off < 0x1400:
		p.palette[(off-0x400)>>2] = v
		return
	case off >= 0x200 && off < 0x300:
		i := (off - 0x200) >> 1
		p.fogTable[i] = uint16(v)
		p.fogTable[i+1] = uint16(v >> 16)
		return
	}
	switch off {
	case RegSPGStatus, RegTAITPCurrent, RegTANextOPB, RegTAYUVTexCnt:
		return // read-only
	case RegSoftreset:
		if v&1 != 0 { // TA reset
			p.ta.listInit()
		}
		if v&2 != 0 { // core reset: register defaults, TA included
			p.Reset()
		}
		return
	case RegStartRender:
		p.Render()
		return
	case RegTAListInit:
		if v&(1<<31) != 0 {
			p.Render() // render the finished scene first
		}
		p.ta.listInit()
		return
	case RegTAListCont:
		return // appends to the open scene; nothing resets
	}
	p.setReg(off, v)
}

// Port is a bus.Device view of one of the PVR streaming ports.
// Reads return 0; each 32-bit write feeds one word to the port.
type Port struct {
	p   *PVR
	yuv bool
}

// Read32 on a streaming port returns 0.
func (pt Port) Read32(uint32) uint32 { return 0 }

// Write32 feeds one word to the port.
func (pt Port) Write32(_ uint32, v uint32) {
	if pt.yuv {
		pt.p.YUVWrite(v)
	} else {
		pt.p.TAWrite(v)
	}
}

// TAPort returns the TA FIFO port device (attach at 0x00500000).
func (p *PVR) TAPort() Port { return Port{p: p} }

// YUVPort returns the YUV FIFO port device (attach at 0x00600000).
func (p *PVR) YUVPort() Port { return Port{p: p, yuv: true} }

// TAWrite feeds one word of a TA parameter stream.
func (p *PVR) TAWrite(v uint32) { p.ta.writeWord(p, v) }

// YUVWrite feeds one word (four bytes, little-endian) of YUV
// converter input.
func (p *PVR) YUVWrite(v uint32) { p.ta.yuvWrite(p, v) }

// vram32 reads a 32-bit word from VRAM at a byte offset.
func (p *PVR) vram32(off uint32) uint32 {
	off &= 0x7FFFFF
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(p.vram[off:])
}

// vramWrite32 writes a 32-bit word to VRAM at a byte offset.
func (p *PVR) vramWrite32(off uint32, v uint32) {
	off &= 0x7FFFFF
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(p.vram[off:], v)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Serialization
//
// Layout (variable length because the TA scene is serialized):
//
//	regs          512 bytes (128 words)
//	palette       4096 bytes
//	fog table     256 bytes
//	SPG state     28 bytes
//	TA state      fixed part, then the primitive lists
//
// The total length is p.SerializeSize() for the current state.

// SerializeSize returns the byte length of Serialize for the
// current state.
func (p *PVR) SerializeSize() int {
	n := 512 + 4096 + 256 + 28
	n += p.ta.serializeSize()
	return n
}

// Serialize writes the full PVR state.
func (p *PVR) Serialize() []byte {
	b := make([]byte, 0, p.SerializeSize())
	tmp := make([]byte, 4)
	put := func(v uint32) {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp, v)
		b = append(b, tmp...)
	}
	for _, v := range p.regs {
		put(v)
	}
	for _, v := range p.palette {
		put(v)
	}
	for _, v := range p.fogTable {
		b = append(b, uint8(v), uint8(v>>8))
	}
	// SPG state: frac, hcount, vcount, field, frames (8), flags.
	put(p.spg.frac)
	put(p.spg.hcount)
	put(p.spg.vcount)
	put(p.spg.field)
	put(uint32(p.spg.frames))
	put(uint32(p.spg.frames >> 32))
	var fl uint32
	if p.spg.inVBlank {
		fl = 1
	}
	put(fl)
	b = p.ta.serialize(b)
	return b
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. On a size
// mismatch the PVR is left untouched and false is returned.
func (p *PVR) Deserialize(b []byte) bool {
	if len(b) != p.expectedSize(b) {
		return false
	}
	r := &reader{b: b}
	for i := range p.regs {
		p.regs[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range p.palette {
		p.palette[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range p.fogTable {
		p.fogTable[i] = r.u16()
	}
	p.spg.frac = r.u32()
	p.spg.hcount = r.u32()
	p.spg.vcount = r.u32()
	p.spg.field = r.u32()
	lo := r.u32()
	hi := r.u32()
	p.spg.frames = uint64(lo) | uint64(hi)<<32
	p.spg.inVBlank = r.u32()&1 != 0
	if !p.ta.deserialize(r) {
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// SerializedSize returns the total length of the serialized PVR
// state that b begins with, as implied by the counts inside it,
// or -1 when b is too short or malformed to hold one.
func SerializedSize(b []byte) int {
	p := &PVR{}
	return p.expectedSize(b)
}

// expectedSize computes the total serialized length implied by
// the primitive counts stored inside b, or -1 when b is too short
// to hold them.
func (p *PVR) expectedSize(b []byte) int {
	// Fixed prefix up to the TA section.
	const prefix = 512 + 4096 + 256 + 28
	if len(b) < prefix+taFixedSize {
		return -1
	}
	return prefix + taSerializedSize(b[prefix:])
}

// reader is a little-endian cursor over a serialized state.
type reader struct {
	b   []byte
	off int
}

func (r *reader) u32() uint32 {
	v := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(r.b[r.off:])
	r.off += 4
	return v
}

func (r *reader) u16() uint16 {
	v := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(r.b[r.off:])
	r.off += 2
	return v
}

func (r *reader) u8() uint8 {
	v := r.b[r.off]
	r.off++
	return v
}

func (r *reader) bytes(n int) []byte {
	v := r.b[r.off : r.off+n]
	r.off += n
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/pvr/pvr_test.go ====================

package pvr

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/holly"
)

// fakeSink records what the Holly controller presents.
type fakeSink struct {
	raises    [][2]uint32
	withdraws int
}

func (s *fakeSink) RaiseInterrupt(code uint32, level int) {
	s.raises = append(s.raises, [2]uint32{code, uint32(level)})
}

func (s *fakeSink) WithdrawInterrupt() { s.withdraws++ }

func newTestPVR() (*PVR, *holly.Controller, *fakeSink) {
	sink := &fakeSink{}
	hc := holly.New(sink)
	return New(make([]byte, 8<<20), hc), hc, sink
}

func reg(p *PVR, off uint32, v uint32) { p.Write32(pvrBase+off, v) }
func rd(p *PVR, off uint32) uint32     { return p.Read32(pvrBase + off) }

// packet feeds one 32-byte TA parameter (8 words, zero padded).
func packet(p *PVR, words ...uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		var w uint32
		if i < len(words) {
			w = words[i]
		}
		p.TAWrite(w)
	}
}

func f32b(f float32) uint32 { return math.Float32bits(f) }

// programSmallSPG sets a 20 pixel by 10 line SPG with vblank-in
// on line 8 and vblank-out on line 0.
func programSmallSPG(p *PVR) {
	reg(p, RegSPGLoad, 9<<16|19)
	reg(p, RegSPGVBlankInt, 8<<16|0)
}

// cyclesForPixels converts pixels to CPU cycles under the
// default 13.5 MHz pixel clock (27/400 per cycle), rounding up.
func cyclesForPixels(px int) int { return (px*400 + 26) / 27 }

func TestDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	p, _, _ := newTestPVR()
	if got := rd(p, RegSPGLoad); got != 262<<16|857 {
		t.Errorf("SPG_LOAD default = %#x, want NTSC 858x263", got)
	}
	if p.PixelsPerLine() != 858 || p.LinesPerField() != 263 {
		t.Errorf("totals = %dx%d, want 858x263", p.PixelsPerLine(), p.LinesPerField())
	}
	// 858 pixels at 13.5 MHz: 200e6 * 858 / 13.5e6 = 12711.1
	if got := p.CyclesPerLine(); got != 12712 {
		t.Errorf("CyclesPerLine = %d, want 12712", got)
	}
}

func TestSPGVBlankWindowAndCounter(t *testing.T) {
	p, hc, sink := newTestPVR()
	programSmallSPG(p)
	// Deliver vblank-in at level 6.
	reg(p, 0, 0) // no-op sanity
	hc.Write32(0x005F6930, 1<<holly.EvtVBlankIn)

	// Advance to line 8 (160 pixels): vblank-in fires exactly
	// once and the status bit reads back.
	p.Advance(cyclesForPixels(160))
	if !p.InVBlank() {
		t.Fatal("not in vblank at line 8")
	}
	if p.SPGLine() != 8 {
		t.Errorf("line = %d, want 8", p.SPGLine())
	}
	if got := hc.Status(holly.BankNormal); got != 1<<holly.EvtVBlankIn {
		t.Errorf("holly status = %#x, want vblank-in only", got)
	}
	if len(sink.raises) != 1 || sink.raises[0] != [2]uint32{0x320, 6} {
		t.Errorf("raises = %v, want one (0x320, 6)", sink.raises)
	}
	if got := rd(p, RegSPGStatus); got&(1<<11) == 0 || got&0x3FF != 8 {
		t.Errorf("SPG_STATUS = %#x, want line 8 with vblank bit", got)
	}
	// Acknowledge, then run four more fields: exactly four more
	// vblank-in deliveries, one per field, and vblank-out fired
	// on every wrap (its bit stays set until acked too).
	hc.Write32(0x005F6900, 1<<holly.EvtVBlankIn)
	for f := 0; f < 4; f++ {
		p.Advance(cyclesForPixels(200))
		if got := hc.Status(holly.BankNormal); got&(1<<holly.EvtVBlankOut) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("field %d: vblank-out bit not set", f)
		}
		hc.Write32(0x005F6900, 1<<holly.EvtVBlankIn)
	}
	if got := p.SPGFrames(); got != 4 {
		t.Errorf("frames = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if len(sink.raises) != 5 {
		t.Errorf("raises = %d, want 5 (one per field)", len(sink.raises))
	}
	// Without the ack the source stays pending (the handler that
	// never clears ISTNRM would be re-entered on hardware).
	p.Advance(cyclesForPixels(200))
	if got := hc.Status(holly.BankNormal); got&(1<<holly.EvtVBlankIn) == 0 {
		t.Error("vblank-in bit cleared without an ack")
	}
}

func TestSPGFieldFlipInterlace(t *testing.T) {
	p, _, _ := newTestPVR()
	programSmallSPG(p)
	reg(p, RegSPGControl, spgInterlace)
	if p.SPGField() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("field starts at 1")
	}
	p.Advance(cyclesForPixels(200))
	if p.SPGField() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("field after one field = %d, want 1", p.SPGField())
	}
	if got := rd(p, RegSPGStatus); got&(1<<12) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("SPG_STATUS = %#x, want field bit set", got)
	}
	p.Advance(cyclesForPixels(200))
	if p.SPGField() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("field after two fields = %d, want 0", p.SPGField())
	}
	// Progressive mode never flips.
	p2, _, _ := newTestPVR()
	programSmallSPG(p2)
	p2.Advance(cyclesForPixels(400))
	if p2.SPGField() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("progressive field = %d, want 0", p2.SPGField())
	}
}

func TestSPGHBlankEventsAndStatus(t *testing.T) {
	p, hc, _ := newTestPVR()
	programSmallSPG(p)
	reg(p, RegSPGHBlankInt, 5)                 // fire at pixel 5 of each line
	reg(p, RegSPGHBlank, 19<<16|10)            // status window pixels 10..19
	hc.Write32(0x005F6910, 1<<holly.EvtHBlank) // level 2 masks

	count := 0
	for line := 0; line < 3; line++ {
		p.Advance(cyclesForPixels(20))
		if hc.Status(holly.BankNormal)&(1<<holly.EvtHBlank) != 0 {
			count++
			hc.Write32(0x005F6900, 1<<holly.EvtHBlank)
		}
	}
	if count != 3 {
		t.Errorf("hblank events for 3 lines = %d, want 3", count)
	}
	// Status: mid-line the hblank window bit reads set at a pixel
	// inside 10..19, clear before it.
	p2, _, _ := newTestPVR()
	programSmallSPG(p2)
	reg(p2, RegSPGHBlank, 19<<16|10)
	p2.Advance(cyclesForPixels(12))
	if got := rd(p2, RegSPGStatus); got&(1<<10) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("SPG_STATUS = %#x, want hblank window bit at pixel 12", got)
	}
	// The disable bit stops the event.
	p3, hc3, _ := newTestPVR()
	programSmallSPG(p3)
	reg(p3, RegSPGHBlankInt, 5|(1<<31))
	p3.Advance(cyclesForPixels(60))
	if hc3.Status(holly.BankNormal)&(1<<holly.EvtHBlank) != 0 {
		t.Error("hblank event fired while disabled")
	}
}

func TestRegisterWindowStorage(t *testing.T) {
	p, _, _ := newTestPVR()
	reg(p, RegTextControl, 0x80000000|0x1234)
	if got := rd(p, RegTextControl); got != 0x80001234 {
		t.Errorf("TEXT_CONTROL = %#x", got)
	}
	reg(p, RegPALRamCtrl, 2)
	if got := rd(p, RegPALRamCtrl); got != 2 {
		t.Errorf("PAL_RAM_CTRL = %#x, want 2", got)
	}
	// Palette RAM lives at +0x400.
	p.Write32(pvrBase+0x400+4*17, 0xAABBCCDD)
	if got := p.Read32(pvrBase + 0x400 + 4*17); got != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Errorf("palette[17] = %#x", got)
	}
	if p.palette[17] != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Errorf("palette backing = %#x", p.palette[17])
	}
	// Fog table at +0x200 holds 16-bit entries.
	p.Write32(pvrBase+0x200, 0x11223344)
	if p.fogTable[0] != 0x3344 || p.fogTable[1] != 0x1122 {
		t.Errorf("fog table = %#x %#x", p.fogTable[0], p.fogTable[1])
	}
	if got := p.Read32(pvrBase + 0x200); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("fog readback = %#x", got)
	}
	// SPG_STATUS ignores writes.
	before := rd(p, RegSPGStatus)
	p.Write32(pvrBase+RegSPGStatus, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	if got := rd(p, RegSPGStatus); got != before {
		t.Errorf("SPG_STATUS changed by a write: %#x -> %#x", before, got)
	}
}

func TestTAParserBuildsPrimAndISPBlock(t *testing.T) {
	p, hc, _ := newTestPVR()
	reg(p, RegTAISPBase, 0x1000)
	reg(p, RegTAListInit, 0)
	hdr := []uint32{
		(4 << 29) | (ListOpaque << 24), // polygon header, opaque
		uint32(DepthAlways),            // ISP/TSP: depth always
		0, 0,                           // TSP, TCW
		0xFF112233, 0, // base color, offset
		0, 0,
	}
	packet(p, hdr...)
	vtx := func(x, y float32, eos bool) []uint32 {
		pcw := uint32(7 << 29)
		if eos {
			pcw |= pcwEOS
		}
		return []uint32{pcw, f32b(x), f32b(y), f32b(0.5), 0, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}[:8]
	}
	packet(p, vtx(0, 0, false)...)
	packet(p, vtx(32, 0, false)...)
	packet(p, vtx(0, 32, false)...)
	packet(p, vtx(32, 32, true)...)
	if len(p.ta.prims[ListOpaque]) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("opaque prims = %d, want 1", len(p.ta.prims[ListOpaque]))
	}
	pr := p.ta.prims[ListOpaque][0]
	if len(pr.Verts) != 4 || pr.BaseColor != 0xFF112233 {
		t.Errorf("prim = %+v", pr)
	}
	if pr.Verts[2].X != 0 || pr.Verts[2].Y != 32 || !pr.Verts[3].EOS {
		t.Errorf("verts = %+v", pr.Verts)
	}
	// The ISP parameter block landed in VRAM at TA_ISP_BASE.
	if got := p.vram32(0x1000); got != hdr[0] {
		t.Errorf("ISP block PCW = %#x, want %#x", got, hdr[0])
	}
	if got := rd(p, RegTAITPCurrent); got != 0x1000+36 {
		t.Errorf("TA_ITP_CURRENT = %#x, want %#x", got, 0x1000+36)
	}
	// End of list fires the opaque-done event.
	packet(p, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	if got := hc.Status(holly.BankNormal); got&(1<<holly.EvtOpaqueDone) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("holly status = %#x, want opaque-done set", got)
	}
}

func TestTAParserErrorsAndClip(t *testing.T) {
	p, hc, _ := newTestPVR()
	reg(p, RegTAListInit, 0)
	// A vertex with no header raises the TA input error.
	packet(p, 7<<29, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	if got := hc.Status(holly.BankError); got&(1<<holly.ErrTAInputError) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("error status = %#x, want TA input error", got)
	}
	// User tile clip packet: word 1 packs x0, y0, x1, y1.
	packet(p, 1<<29, 1|2<<8|30<<16|40<<24, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	if p.ta.clip != [4]uint8{1, 2, 30, 40} {
		t.Errorf("clip = %v", p.ta.clip)
	}
	// Control packet with the endian flip set: a byte-swapped
	// header parses as written.
	packet(p, 2<<29, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	swap := func(v uint32) uint32 { return bitsReverseBytes(v) }
	hdr := []uint32{(4 << 29) | (ListTrans << 24), uint32(DepthAlways), 0, 0, 0xFF0000FF, 0, 0, 0}
	sw := make([]uint32, 8)
	for i, w := range hdr {
		sw[i] = swap(w)
	}
	packet(p, sw...)
	if !p.ta.hdrValid || p.ta.hdr.List != ListTrans {
		t.Errorf("swapped header not parsed: valid=%v list=%d", p.ta.hdrValid, p.ta.hdr.List)
	}
}

func bitsReverseBytes(v uint32) uint32 {
	return v<<24 | (v&0xFF00)<<8 | (v>>8)&0xFF00 | v>>24
}

func TestYUVConverter(t *testing.T) {
	p, hc, _ := newTestPVR()
	reg(p, RegTAYUVTexBase, 0x2000)
	reg(p, RegTAYUVTexCtrl, 1<<16|1) // 1x1 macroblocks: 16x16 texels
	// One macroblock: U = V = 128 (neutral chroma), Y = 128,
	// fed as 96 words of 0x80808080.
	for i := 0; i < 96; i++ {
		p.YUVWrite(128 | 128<<8 | 128<<16 | 128<<24)
	}
	if got := hc.Status(holly.BankNormal); got&(1<<holly.EvtYUVDone) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("holly status = %#x, want YUV done", got)
	}
	r, g, b := yuvToRGB(128, 128, 128)
	want := uint16(uint32(r>>3)<<11 | uint32(g>>2)<<5 | uint32(b>>3))
	for _, xy := range [][2]int{{0, 0}, {15, 15}, {3, 9}} {
		idx := twiddleIndex(xy[0], xy[1], 16, 16)
		got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(p.vram[0x2000+idx*2:])
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("texel %v = %#04x, want %#04x", xy, got, want)
		}
	}
	if got := rd(p, RegTAYUVTexCnt); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("YUV count after completion = %d, want 0 (reset)", got)
	}
}

func TestPVRSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	p, _, _ := newTestPVR()
	programSmallSPG(p)
	p.Advance(cyclesForPixels(37)) // beam mid-line
	reg(p, RegTAISPBase, 0x1000)
	reg(p, RegTAListInit, 0)
	packet(p, (4<<29)|(ListOpaque<<24), uint32(DepthAlways), 0, 0, 0xFF00FF00, 0, 0, 0)
	packet(p, 7<<29, f32b(0), f32b(0), f32b(0.5), 0, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0)
	packet(p, 7<<29|pcwEOS, f32b(10), f32b(0), f32b(0.5), 0, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0)
	// A second prim left open mid-strip.
	packet(p, (4<<29)|(ListTrans<<24), uint32(DepthGreater), 0, 0, 0xFFFF0000, 0, 0, 0)
	packet(p, 7<<29, f32b(1), f32b(2), f32b(0.25), 0, 0, 0xFF123456, 0)
	p.palette[5] = 0xDEADBEEF

	b := p.Serialize()
	if len(b) != p.SerializeSize() {
		t.Fatalf("len = %d, SerializeSize = %d", len(b), p.SerializeSize())
	}
	if got := SerializedSize(b); got != len(b) {
		t.Fatalf("SerializedSize = %d, want %d", got, len(b))
	}
	p2, _, _ := newTestPVR()
	if !p2.Deserialize(b) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize failed")
	}
	if got := p2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, b) {
		t.Error("round trip state differs")
	}
	if len(p2.ta.prims[ListTrans]) != 1 || len(p2.ta.prims[ListTrans][0].Verts) != 1 {
		t.Error("open prim not restored")
	}
	if p2.ta.open != 0 {
		t.Errorf("open index = %d, want 0", p2.ta.open)
	}
	if p2.Deserialize(b[:len(b)-1]) {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted a truncated state")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/pvr/render.go ====================

package pvr

import (
	"math"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/holly"
)

// ISP/TSP renderer for DC-2. Render consumes the primitive
// lists the TA built, rasterizes them into internal float
// buffers, and writes the result back into the VRAM
// framebuffer in the format FB_W_CTRL selects. The internal
// buffers hold RGBA color as floats in the range 0 to 1, a
// float depth per pixel (the depth value is the reciprocal
// of w, exactly as submitted in the vertex Z), and a signed
// modifier counter per pixel used by modifier volumes, shadow
// texture instructions, and two-volume parameter selection.
//
// Documented simplifications for this slice:
//   - The background plane is color only, even when the
//     texture bit in ISP_BACKGND_T is set.
//   - Trilinear filter modes sample one mip level (the LOD
//     level) with bilinear filtering.
//   - VQ textures are not mipmapped.
//   - Modifier volumes never write depth.
//   - Primitives are consumed in per-pixel submission order
//     within the hardware list order, which is pixel
//     identical to the hardware tile order for this model.

// texFmt8888 is the TCW pixel format code for ARGB8888,
// which has no named constant in ta.go.
const texFmt8888 = 7

// tspTexInstr extracts the TSP texture instruction field,
// bits 25:24: 0 replace, 1 modulate, 2 decal, 3 shadow.
func tspTexInstr(w uint32) int { return int((w >> 24) & 3) }

// frame is the internal render target for one Render call.
type frame struct {
	w, h  int
	color []float32 // RGBA per pixel
	depth []float32
	mod   []int32
}

// Render rasterizes the current TA scene and writes the
// finished frame into the VRAM framebuffer at FB_W_SOF1.
// When the FB_W_CTRL enable bit is clear the pipeline still
// runs into the internal buffers but the VRAM write is
// skipped, so Present (which reads VRAM) shows nothing new.
func (p *PVR) Render() {
	w, h := p.renderWidth(), p.renderHeight()
	fb := &frame{w: w, h: h,
		color: make([]float32, w*h*4),
		depth: make([]float32, w*h),
		mod:   make([]int32, w*h)}

	// Background: depth from ISP_BACKGND_D, color from
	// ISP_BACKGND_S (alpha bits 31:24, then R, G, B bytes).
	bgDepth := math.Float32frombits(p.reg(RegISPBackgndD))
	bg := p.reg(RegISPBackgndS)
	bgCol := [4]float32{
		float32((bg>>16)&0xFF) / 255,
		float32((bg>>8)&0xFF) / 255,
		float32(bg&0xFF) / 255,
		float32((bg>>24)&0xFF) / 255,
	}
	for i := range fb.depth {
		fb.depth[i] = bgDepth
		copy(fb.color[i*4:], bgCol[:])
	}

	alphaRef := float32((p.reg(RegTextControl)>>24)&0xFF) / 255
	regionBase := p.reg(RegRegionBase)
	tilesX := (w + 31) / 32

	// Hardware list order: opaque, opaque modifier,
	// punchthrough, translucent modifier, translucent.
	order := [5]int{ListOpaque, ListOpaqueMod, ListPunch, ListTransMod, ListTrans}
	for _, list := range order {
		for i := range p.ta.prims[list] {
			p.drawPrim(fb, &p.ta.prims[list][i], alphaRef, regionBase, tilesX)
		}
	}

	p.writeFrame(fb)
	p.renderCount++
	p.raise(holly.BankNormal, 1<<holly.EvtRenderDoneISP)
	p.raise(holly.BankNormal, 1<<holly.EvtRenderDoneTSP)
}

// paramSet is one ISP/TSP + TSP + TCW parameter triple of a
// primitive: set 0 is the primary triple, set 1 the second
// triple of a two-volume primitive.
type paramSet struct {
	isp, tsp, tcw uint32
}

func primSet(pr *Prim, idx int) paramSet {
	if idx == 1 {
		return paramSet{pr.ISPTSP2, pr.TSP2, pr.TCW2}
	}
	return paramSet{pr.ISPTSP, pr.TSP, pr.TCW}
}

// vertInterp holds the per-vertex values one triangle
// interpolates for one parameter set. The u, v and color
// channels are premultiplied by Z (which is 1/w) so the
// rasterizer can divide by the interpolated Z per pixel,
// the perspective-correct form the hardware uses.
type vertInterp struct {
	u, v   float32 // raw texture coordinates, for LOD
	uq, vq float32
	base   [4]float32 // RGBA, premultiplied by Z
	off    [4]float32 // RGBA, premultiplied by Z
}

// buildInterp prepares the interpolated values of one vertex
// for one parameter set. Gouraud primitives take colors from
// the vertex; flat primitives take the header colors.
// Two-volume primitives always take colors from the vertex,
// because their headers carry no colors, and sprites do the
// same, because the TA bakes the sprite vertex parameter's
// base and offset colors into every corner vertex.
func buildInterp(pr *Prim, v *Vertex, setIdx int, z float32) vertInterp {
	set := primSet(pr, setIdx)
	var u, vv float32
	var baseWord, offWord uint32
	if setIdx == 1 {
		u, vv = v.U2, v.V2
		baseWord, offWord = v.Base2, v.Offset2
	} else {
		u, vv = v.U, v.V
		baseWord, offWord = v.Base, v.Offset
	}
	if set.isp&ispGouraud == 0 && !pr.TwoVolume() && !pr.Sprite {
		baseWord, offWord = pr.BaseColor, pr.OffsetColor
	}
	vi := vertInterp{u: u, v: vv, uq: u * z, vq: vv * z}
	bc := unpackARGB(baseWord)
	oc := unpackARGB(offWord)
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		vi.base[c] = bc[c] * z
		vi.off[c] = oc[c] * z
	}
	return vi
}

// unpackARGB converts a packed ARGB8888 word to RGBA floats
// in the range 0 to 1.
func unpackARGB(word uint32) [4]float32 {
	return [4]float32{
		float32((word>>16)&0xFF) / 255,
		float32((word>>8)&0xFF) / 255,
		float32(word&0xFF) / 255,
		float32((word>>24)&0xFF) / 255,
	}
}

func clamp01(f float32) float32 {
	if f < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if f > 1 {
		return 1
	}
	return f
}

// depthPass applies one ISP depth compare mode: the new
// value q against the stored depth.
func depthPass(mode int, q, stored float32) bool {
	switch mode {
	case DepthNever:
		return false
	case DepthLess:
		return q < stored
	case DepthEqual:
		return q == stored
	case DepthLEqual:
		return q <= stored
	case DepthGreater:
		return q > stored
	case DepthNotEq:
		return q != stored
	case DepthGEqual:
		return q >= stored
	case DepthAlways:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// edgeFn is the signed double area of the triangle a, b, p.
func edgeFn(ax, ay, bx, by, px, py float32) float32 {
	return (bx-ax)*(py-ay) - (by-ay)*(px-ax)
}

// drawPrim rasterizes every triangle of one primitive strip.
func (p *PVR) drawPrim(fb *frame, pr *Prim, alphaRef float32, regionBase uint32, tilesX int) {
	if len(pr.Verts) < 3 {
		return
	}
	isVolume := pr.List == ListOpaqueMod
	twoVol := pr.TwoVolume()
	for k := 0; k+2 < len(pr.Verts); k++ {
		vs := [3]*Vertex{&pr.Verts[k], &pr.Verts[k+1], &pr.Verts[k+2]}
		// Surface facing: signed area in submitted order,
		// flipped on odd strip indices.
		a2 := edgeFn(vs[0].X, vs[0].Y, vs[1].X, vs[1].Y, vs[2].X, vs[2].Y)
		if a2 == 0 {
			continue // degenerate: covers no pixels
		}
		facing := a2
		if k%2 == 1 {
			facing = -a2
		}
		switch ispCullMode(pr.ISPTSP) {
		case 1:
			if facing == 0 {
				continue
			}
		case 2:
			if facing < 0 {
				continue
			}
		case 3:
			if facing > 0 {
				continue
			}
		}

		var interp [2][3]vertInterp
		var lod [2]int
		for s := 0; s < 2; s++ {
			if s == 1 && !twoVol {
				break
			}
			for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
				interp[s][i] = buildInterp(pr, vs[i], s, vs[i].Z)
			}
			set := primSet(pr, s)
			if set.isp&ispTextured != 0 {
				lod[s] = p.texLOD(set.tsp, set.tcw, vs, interp[s])
			}
		}

		minX := minf3(vs[0].X, vs[1].X, vs[2].X)
		maxX := maxf3(vs[0].X, vs[1].X, vs[2].X)
		minY := minf3(vs[0].Y, vs[1].Y, vs[2].Y)
		maxY := maxf3(vs[0].Y, vs[1].Y, vs[2].Y)
		x0 := clampInt(int(math.Floor(float64(minX))), 0, fb.w-1)
		x1 := clampInt(int(math.Floor(float64(maxX))), 0, fb.w-1)
		y0 := clampInt(int(math.Floor(float64(minY))), 0, fb.h-1)
		y1 := clampInt(int(math.Floor(float64(maxY))), 0, fb.h-1)

		for y := y0; y <= y1; y++ {
			for x := x0; x <= x1; x++ {
				cx, cy := float32(x)+0.5, float32(y)+0.5
				l0 := edgeFn(vs[1].X, vs[1].Y, vs[2].X, vs[2].Y, cx, cy) / a2
				l1 := edgeFn(vs[2].X, vs[2].Y, vs[0].X, vs[0].Y, cx, cy) / a2
				l2 := edgeFn(vs[0].X, vs[0].Y, vs[1].X, vs[1].Y, cx, cy) / a2
				if l0 < 0 || l1 < 0 || l2 < 0 {
					continue
				}
				idx := y*fb.w + x
				if regionDisabled(p, regionBase, tilesX, pr.List, x, y) {
					continue
				}
				q := l0*vs[0].Z + l1*vs[1].Z + l2*vs[2].Z

				if isVolume {
					// Modifier volume: no color output
					// and no depth write, ever. Pixels
					// passing the volume's own depth test
					// adjust the counter by facing.
					if !depthPass(ispDepthMode(pr.ISPTSP), q, fb.depth[idx]) {
						continue
					}
					if facing > 0 {
						fb.mod[idx]++
					} else if facing < 0 {
						fb.mod[idx] += -1
					}
					continue
				}
				p.shadePixel(fb, pr, idx, interp, lod, l0, l1, l2, q, alphaRef)
			}
		}
	}
}

func minf3(a, b, c float32) float32 {
	m := a
	if b < m {
		m = b
	}
	if c < m {
		m = c
	}
	return m
}

func maxf3(a, b, c float32) float32 {
	m := a
	if b > m {
		m = b
	}
	if c > m {
		m = c
	}
	return m
}

// regionDisabled reports whether the region array disables
// this list inside the tile holding pixel (x, y). The array
// entry for a tile is 6 words at RegionBase + tile*24, and
// word 0 bits 4:0 hold one disable bit per list.
func regionDisabled(p *PVR, regionBase uint32, tilesX, list, x, y int) bool {
	if regionBase == 0 {
		return false
	}
	tile := (y/32)*tilesX + x/32
	word := p.vramWord(regionBase + uint32(tile*24))
	return (word>>uint(list))&1 != 0
}

// shadePixel runs depth, texturing, punchthrough, and
// blending for one covered pixel of a shaded primitive.
func (p *PVR) shadePixel(fb *frame, pr *Prim, idx int, interp [2][3]vertInterp, lod [2]int,
	l0, l1, l2, q float32, alphaRef float32) {
	if q == 0 {
		return // no projective divide is possible
	}
	odd := fb.mod[idx]&1 != 0
	setIdx := 0
	if pr.TwoVolume() {
		if odd {
			setIdx = 1
		}
	} else if pr.List == ListTransMod && odd {
		// Single-volume translucent modifier primitives
		// shade only where the counter is even.
		return
	}
	set := primSet(pr, setIdx)
	if !depthPass(ispDepthMode(set.isp), q, fb.depth[idx]) {
		return
	}
	iv := interp[setIdx]
	u := (l0*iv[0].uq + l1*iv[1].uq + l2*iv[2].uq) / q
	v := (l0*iv[0].vq + l1*iv[1].vq + l2*iv[2].vq) / q
	var base, off [4]float32
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		base[c] = (l0*iv[0].base[c] + l1*iv[1].base[c] + l2*iv[2].base[c]) / q
		off[c] = (l0*iv[0].off[c] + l1*iv[1].off[c] + l2*iv[2].off[c]) / q
	}

	src := base
	texA := base[3]
	if set.isp&ispTextured != 0 {
		tex := p.sampleTexture(set.tsp, set.tcw, u, v, lod[setIdx])
		texA = tex[3]
		if pr.List == ListPunch && texA < alphaRef {
			return // discarded: no depth or color write
		}
		switch tspTexInstr(set.tsp) {
		case 0: // replace
			src = tex
			if tspIgnoreTexA(set.tsp) {
				src[3] = base[3]
			}
		case 1: // modulate
			for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
				src[c] = tex[c] * base[c]
			}
			if tspIgnoreTexA(set.tsp) {
				src[3] = base[3]
			} else {
				src[3] = tex[3] * base[3]
			}
		case 2: // decal
			for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
				src[c] = tex[c]*tex[3] + base[c]*(1-tex[3])
			}
			src[3] = base[3]
		case 3: // shadow: modulate, then scale by the
			// shadow scale where the counter is odd
			for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
				src[c] = tex[c] * base[c]
			}
			if tspIgnoreTexA(set.tsp) {
				src[3] = base[3]
			} else {
				src[3] = tex[3] * base[3]
			}
			if odd {
				scale := math.Float32frombits(p.reg(RegFPUShadScale))
				for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
					src[c] *= scale
				}
			}
		}
	} else if pr.List == ListPunch && texA < alphaRef {
		return
	}
	if set.isp&ispOffset != 0 {
		for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
			src[c] += off[c]
		}
	}
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		src[c] = clamp01(src[c])
	}
	// Fog: after the texture instruction and the source
	// color clamp, before blending, selected by this
	// polygon ISP fog control field. See fog.go.
	src = p.applyFog(src, ispFogCtrl(set.isp), q, off[3], set.isp&ispOffset != 0)

	if set.isp&ispZWriteDis == 0 {
		fb.depth[idx] = q
	}
	dst := [4]float32{fb.color[idx*4], fb.color[idx*4+1], fb.color[idx*4+2], fb.color[idx*4+3]}
	if pr.List == ListTrans || pr.List == ListTransMod || tspUseAlpha(set.tsp) {
		sf := tspSrcBlend(set.tsp)
		df := tspDstBlend(set.tsp)
		for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
			dst[c] = src[c]*blendFactor(sf, c, src, dst) + dst[c]*blendFactor(df, c, src, dst)
		}
	} else {
		dst = src
	}
	copy(fb.color[idx*4:], dst[:])
}

// blendFactor evaluates one TSP blend function for channel
// c (0 R, 1 G, 2 B, 3 A) of the src and dst colors.
func blendFactor(code, c int, src, dst [4]float32) float32 {
	switch code {
	case BlendZero:
		return 0
	case BlendOne:
		return 1
	case BlendDstColor:
		return dst[c]
	case BlendOneMinusDst:
		return 1 - dst[c]
	case BlendSrcAlpha:
		return src[3]
	case BlendOneMinusSrcA:
		return 1 - src[3]
	case BlendDstAlpha:
		return dst[3]
	case BlendOneMinusDstA:
		return 1 - dst[3]
	}
	return 0
}

// Texture sampling

// texInfo describes one mip level of one texture for the
// duration of a sample.
type texInfo struct {
	tsp, tcw uint32
	fmt      int
	w, h     int    // level dimensions in texels
	base     uint32 // VRAM byte offset of the level data
	vq       bool
}

// bppBits returns the storage size of one texel.
func bppBits(fmt int) int {
	switch fmt {
	case TexPal4:
		return 4
	case TexPal8:
		return 8
	case texFmt8888:
		return 32
	}
	return 16
}

// mipMaxLevel returns the index of the smallest mip level.
func mipMaxLevel(w, h int) int {
	l := 0
	for (w>>l) > 1 || (h>>l) > 1 {
		l++
	}
	return l
}

// texLOD picks the mip level for one triangle. The footprint
// is the texel-space step per pixel, from screen-space
// derivatives of the texture coordinates formed by finite
// differences over the triangle vertices, and the level is
// round(log2(footprint)) adjusted by the TSP mip bias field
// (bias minus 4, matching the signed hardware bias form).
func (p *PVR) texLOD(tsp, tcw uint32, vs [3]*Vertex, iv [3]vertInterp) int {
	if !tcwMipMapped(tcw) {
		return 0
	}
	tw, th := tspUSize(tsp), tspVSize(tsp)
	maxLevel := mipMaxLevel(tw, th)
	det := (vs[1].X-vs[0].X)*(vs[2].Y-vs[0].Y) - (vs[2].X-vs[0].X)*(vs[1].Y-vs[0].Y)
	if det == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	deriv := func(f0, f1, f2 float32) (float32, float32) {
		dx := ((f1-f0)*(vs[2].Y-vs[0].Y) - (f2-f0)*(vs[1].Y-vs[0].Y)) / det
		dy := ((f2-f0)*(vs[1].X-vs[0].X) - (f1-f0)*(vs[2].X-vs[0].X)) / det
		return dx, dy
	}
	dudx, dudy := deriv(iv[0].u, iv[1].u, iv[2].u)
	dvdx, dvdy := deriv(iv[0].v, iv[1].v, iv[2].v)
	foot := math.Max(math.Abs(float64(dudx))*float64(tw), math.Abs(float64(dvdx))*float64(th))
	foot = math.Max(foot, math.Abs(float64(dudy))*float64(tw))
	foot = math.Max(foot, math.Abs(float64(dvdy))*float64(th))
	if foot < 1 {
		foot = 1
	}
	lod := int(math.Round(math.Log2(foot))) + tspMipBias(tsp) - 4
	if lod < 0 {
		lod = 0
	}
	if lod > maxLevel {
		lod = maxLevel
	}
	return lod
}

// texLevel builds the texInfo for one LOD level. Mipmapped
// textures store the smallest levels first in VRAM and the
// largest (level 0) last, so a level's offset accumulates
// the texel counts of every smaller level.
func (p *PVR) texLevel(tsp, tcw uint32, lod int) texInfo {
	tw, th := tspUSize(tsp), tspVSize(tsp)
	ti := texInfo{tsp: tsp, tcw: tcw, fmt: tcwPixelFmt(tcw), vq: tcwVQ(tcw)}
	base := tcwAddr(tcw)
	if ti.vq {
		// VQ textures are not mipmapped in this
		// implementation: the codebook and index data sit
		// at the texture base at full size.
		ti.w, ti.h, ti.base = tw, th, base
		return ti
	}
	if !tcwMipMapped(tcw) {
		ti.w, ti.h, ti.base = tw, th, base
		return ti
	}
	maxLevel := mipMaxLevel(tw, th)
	if lod > maxLevel {
		lod = maxLevel
	}
	smaller := 0
	for l := lod + 1; l <= maxLevel; l++ {
		smaller += maxInt(1, tw>>l) * maxInt(1, th>>l)
	}
	ti.w = maxInt(1, tw>>lod)
	ti.h = maxInt(1, th>>lod)
	ti.base = base + uint32(smaller*bppBits(ti.fmt)/8)
	return ti
}

func maxInt(a, b int) int {
	if a > b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

// sampleTexture samples one texture at (u, v) under the TSP
// filter mode, returning RGBA floats in the range 0 to 1.
func (p *PVR) sampleTexture(tsp, tcw uint32, u, v float32, lod int) [4]float32 {
	ti := p.texLevel(tsp, tcw, lod)
	filter := tspFilter(tsp)
	if filter == 0 {
		// Point sampling: nearest texel.
		x := wrapCoord(int(math.Floor(float64(u)*float64(ti.w))), ti.w, tspUClamp(tsp), tspUFlip(tsp))
		y := wrapCoord(int(math.Floor(float64(v)*float64(ti.h))), ti.h, tspVClamp(tsp), tspVFlip(tsp))
		return p.fetchTexel(&ti, x, y)
	}
	// Bilinear. Trilinear modes 2 and 3 also land here,
	// sampling the single LOD level (documented above).
	s := float64(u)*float64(ti.w) - 0.5
	t := float64(v)*float64(ti.h) - 0.5
	x0 := int(math.Floor(s))
	y0 := int(math.Floor(t))
	fx := float32(s - float64(x0))
	fy := float32(t - float64(y0))
	c00 := p.fetchTexel(&ti, wrapCoord(x0, ti.w, tspUClamp(tsp), tspUFlip(tsp)), wrapCoord(y0, ti.h, tspVClamp(tsp), tspVFlip(tsp)))
	c10 := p.fetchTexel(&ti, wrapCoord(x0+1, ti.w, tspUClamp(tsp), tspUFlip(tsp)), wrapCoord(y0, ti.h, tspVClamp(tsp), tspVFlip(tsp)))
	c01 := p.fetchTexel(&ti, wrapCoord(x0, ti.w, tspUClamp(tsp), tspUFlip(tsp)), wrapCoord(y0+1, ti.h, tspVClamp(tsp), tspVFlip(tsp)))
	c11 := p.fetchTexel(&ti, wrapCoord(x0+1, ti.w, tspUClamp(tsp), tspUFlip(tsp)), wrapCoord(y0+1, ti.h, tspVClamp(tsp), tspVFlip(tsp)))
	var out [4]float32
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		top := c00[c]*(1-fx) + c10[c]*fx
		bot := c01[c]*(1-fx) + c11[c]*fx
		out[c] = top*(1-fy) + bot*fy
	}
	return out
}

// wrapCoord applies one texture axis mode to a texel
// coordinate: clamp to the edge, mirror with period 2*size,
// or repeat with period size.
func wrapCoord(c, size int, clampMode, flipMode bool) int {
	if size <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if clampMode {
		return clampInt(c, 0, size-1)
	}
	if flipMode {
		m := c % (2 * size)
		if m < 0 {
			m += 2 * size
		}
		if m >= size {
			m = 2*size - 1 - m
		}
		return m
	}
	m := c % size
	if m < 0 {
		m += size
	}
	return m
}

// fetchTexel reads one texel of the level at integer
// coordinates already passed through the axis modes.
func (p *PVR) fetchTexel(ti *texInfo, x, y int) [4]float32 {
	if ti.vq {
		return p.fetchVQTexel(ti, x, y)
	}
	var idx int
	if tspLinear(ti.tsp) {
		stride := ti.w
		if tspStride(ti.tsp) {
			bytes := int((p.reg(RegTextControl)>>1)&0x3F) * 32
			if texels := bytes * 8 / bppBits(ti.fmt); texels > 0 {
				stride = texels
			}
		}
		idx = y*stride + x
	} else {
		idx = twiddleIndex(x, y, ti.w, ti.h)
	}
	switch ti.fmt {
	case TexPal4:
		b := p.vramByte(ti.base + uint32(idx/2))
		nib := int(b & 0xF)
		if idx%2 == 1 {
			nib = int(b >> 4)
		}
		return p.paletteColor(tcwPalSelect(ti.tcw)*16 + nib)
	case TexPal8:
		b := p.vramByte(ti.base + uint32(idx))
		palIdx := ((tcwPalSelect(ti.tcw) & 0x30) << 4) + int(b)
		return p.paletteColor(palIdx)
	case TexYUV:
		// One 32-bit word holds two texels: low byte Y0,
		// then U, then Y1, then V. Even x uses Y0, odd x Y1.
		word := p.vramWord(ti.base + uint32((idx/2)*4))
		yy := int(word & 0xFF)
		if x%2 == 1 {
			yy = int((word >> 16) & 0xFF)
		}
		r, g, b := yuvToRGB(yy, int((word>>8)&0xFF), int((word>>24)&0xFF))
		return [4]float32{float32(r) / 255, float32(g) / 255, float32(b) / 255, 1}
	}
	return p.decodeTexelAt(ti.base+uint32(idx*bppBits(ti.fmt)/8), ti.fmt)
}

// fetchVQTexel reads one texel of a VQ compressed texture.
// The codebook holds 256 entries of 4 texels at the texture
// base; index data follows, one byte per 2x2 block, with the
// block coordinates twiddled over the half-size grid. The
// texel order inside a block is (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1).
func (p *PVR) fetchVQTexel(ti *texInfo, x, y int) [4]float32 {
	texelBytes := bppBits(ti.fmt) / 8
	entryBytes := 4 * texelBytes
	codebookBytes := 256 * entryBytes
	bw := maxInt(1, ti.w/2)
	bh := maxInt(1, ti.h/2)
	bidx := twiddleIndex(x/2, y/2, bw, bh)
	code := int(p.vramByte(ti.base + uint32(codebookBytes+bidx)))
	pos := (y&1)*2 + (x & 1)
	off := ti.base + uint32(code*entryBytes+pos*texelBytes)
	return p.decodeTexelAt(off, ti.fmt)
}

// decodeTexelAt decodes one raw texel at a VRAM byte offset
// in a non-palette pixel format.
func (p *PVR) decodeTexelAt(off uint32, fmt int) [4]float32 {
	switch fmt {
	case Tex565:
		return decode565(uint16(p.vramWord16(off)))
	case Tex4444:
		return decode4444(uint16(p.vramWord16(off)))
	case texFmt8888:
		return decode8888(p.vramWord(off))
	case TexPal4, TexPal8:
		// Palette formats store indices, not colors; the
		// fetch paths resolve them before this point. A
		// zero color is returned for direct calls.
		return [4]float32{}
	}
	// Tex1555, and TexBump treated as Tex1555 in this slice.
	return decode1555(uint16(p.vramWord16(off)))
}

// paletteColor resolves one palette RAM entry to RGBA under
// the PAL_RAM_CTRL format: 0 = 1555, 1 = 565, 2 = 4444,
// 3 = 8888 (entry word as ARGB).
func (p *PVR) paletteColor(idx int) [4]float32 {
	if idx < 0 || idx >= len(p.palette) {
		return [4]float32{}
	}
	entry := p.palette[idx]
	switch p.reg(RegPALRamCtrl) & 3 {
	case 1:
		return decode565(uint16(entry))
	case 2:
		return decode4444(uint16(entry))
	case 3:
		return decode8888(entry)
	}
	return decode1555(uint16(entry))
}

func decode1555(v uint16) [4]float32 {
	a := float32(0)
	if v&0x8000 != 0 {
		a = 1
	}
	return [4]float32{
		float32((v>>10)&0x1F) / 31,
		float32((v>>5)&0x1F) / 31,
		float32(v&0x1F) / 31,
		a,
	}
}

func decode565(v uint16) [4]float32 {
	return [4]float32{
		float32((v>>11)&0x1F) / 31,
		float32((v>>5)&0x3F) / 63,
		float32(v&0x1F) / 31,
		1,
	}
}

func decode4444(v uint16) [4]float32 {
	return [4]float32{
		float32((v>>8)&0xF) / 15,
		float32((v>>4)&0xF) / 15,
		float32(v&0xF) / 15,
		float32((v>>12)&0xF) / 15,
	}
}

func decode8888(word uint32) [4]float32 {
	return unpackARGB(word)
}

// vramByte reads one byte of VRAM with the offset masked to
// the 8 MB space.
func (p *PVR) vramByte(off uint32) byte {
	return p.vram[off&0x7FFFFF]
}

// vramWord16 reads one 16-bit value from VRAM, byte by byte
// so offsets near the end of the space cannot overrun.
func (p *PVR) vramWord16(off uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(p.vramByte(off)) | uint32(p.vramByte(off+1))<<8
}

// vramWord reads one 32-bit value from VRAM, byte by byte.
func (p *PVR) vramWord(off uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(p.vramByte(off)) | uint32(p.vramByte(off+1))<<8 |
		uint32(p.vramByte(off+2))<<16 | uint32(p.vramByte(off+3))<<24
}

// vramPutByte writes one byte of VRAM with the offset masked
// to the 8 MB space.
func (p *PVR) vramPutByte(off uint32, b byte) {
	p.vram[off&0x7FFFFF] = b
}

// Framebuffer write-back

// bayer4 is the 4x4 ordered dither matrix.
var bayer4 = [4][4]int{
	{0, 8, 2, 10},
	{12, 4, 14, 6},
	{3, 11, 1, 9},
	{15, 7, 13, 5},
}

// quantize rounds a 0 to 1 channel to an integer with the
// given maximum, round to nearest.
func quantize(f float32, max int) int {
	n := int(clamp01(f)*float32(max) + 0.5)
	if n > max {
		n = max
	}
	return n
}

// writeFrame stores the internal frame into VRAM at
// FB_W_SOF1 in the FB_W_CTRL format, clipped by the
// FB_X_CLIP and FB_Y_CLIP scissor. A clip max of 0 disables
// the scissor on that axis.
func (p *PVR) writeFrame(fb *frame) {
	ctrl := p.reg(RegFBWCTRL)
	if ctrl&fbEnable == 0 {
		return
	}
	format := int((ctrl & fbDepth) >> 1)
	bpp := 2
	switch format {
	case Fmt0888:
		bpp = 3
	case Fmt8888:
		bpp = 4
	}
	stride := fb.w * bpp
	if ls := p.reg(RegFBWLineStride); ls != 0 {
		stride = int((ls&0x3FF)+1) * 8
	}
	xClip := p.reg(RegFBXClip)
	yClip := p.reg(RegFBYClip)
	xMin, xMax := int(xClip&0x7FF), int((xClip>>16)&0x7FF)
	yMin, yMax := int(yClip&0xFFF), int((yClip>>16)&0xFFF)
	if xMax == 0 {
		xMax = fb.w - 1
	}
	if yMax == 0 {
		yMax = fb.h - 1
	}
	base := p.reg(RegFBWSOF1)
	dither := ctrl&fbDither != 0
	for y := 0; y < fb.h; y++ {
		if y < yMin || y > yMax {
			continue
		}
		for x := 0; x < fb.w; x++ {
			if x < xMin || x > xMax {
				continue
			}
			idx := (y*fb.w + x) * 4
			r, g, b, a := fb.color[idx], fb.color[idx+1], fb.color[idx+2], fb.color[idx+3]
			off := base + uint32(y*stride+x*bpp)
			switch format {
			case Fmt0565:
				dr, dg, db := ditherOffsets(dither, x, y)
				val := uint16(quantize(r+dr, 31))<<11 |
					uint16(quantize(g+dg, 63))<<5 |
					uint16(quantize(b+db, 31))
				p.vramPutByte(off, byte(val))
				p.vramPutByte(off+1, byte(val>>8))
			case Fmt0555:
				dr, dg, db := ditherOffsets(dither, x, y)
				var val uint16
				if a >= 0.5 {
					val = 1 << 15
				}
				val |= uint16(quantize(r+dr, 31))<<10 |
					uint16(quantize(g+dg, 31))<<5 |
					uint16(quantize(b+db, 31))
				p.vramPutByte(off, byte(val))
				p.vramPutByte(off+1, byte(val>>8))
			case Fmt0888:
				p.vramPutByte(off, byte(quantize(b, 255)))
				p.vramPutByte(off+1, byte(quantize(g, 255)))
				p.vramPutByte(off+2, byte(quantize(r, 255)))
			case Fmt8888:
				word := uint32(quantize(a, 255))<<24 |
					uint32(quantize(r, 255))<<16 |
					uint32(quantize(g, 255))<<8 |
					uint32(quantize(b, 255))
				for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
					p.vramPutByte(off+uint32(i), byte(word>>(8*i)))
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

// ditherOffsets returns the ordered dither offsets for the
// 5-bit and 6-bit channels at one pixel: the returned values
// are (red and blue offset, green offset, blue offset), all
// zero when dither is off. The offset is (m/16 - 0.5) scaled
// by one quantization step of the channel.
func ditherOffsets(on bool, x, y int) (float32, float32, float32) {
	if !on {
		return 0, 0, 0
	}
	m := float32(bayer4[y&3][x&3])
	o5 := (m/16 - 0.5) * (1.0 / 31)
	o6 := (m/16 - 0.5) * (1.0 / 63)
	return o5, o6, o5
}

// Display output

// Present fills out (w by h XRGB8888 pixels) with the
// displayed frame read back from VRAM under FB_R_CTRL and
// FB_R_SIZE. When the display is disabled, or outside the
// source rectangle, pixels take the border color.
func (p *PVR) Present(out []uint32, w, h int) {
	border := 0xFF000000 | (p.reg(RegBorderCol) & 0xFFFFFF)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = border
	}
	ctrl := p.reg(RegFBRCTRL)
	if ctrl&fbEnable == 0 {
		return
	}
	size := p.reg(RegFBRSize)
	widthWords := int(size&0x3FF) + 1
	height := int((size>>10)&0x3FF) + 1
	moduloWords := int((size >> 20) & 0x3FF)
	strideWords := widthWords + moduloWords
	format := int((ctrl & fbDepth) >> 1)
	srcW := widthWords * 2
	switch format {
	case Fmt8888:
		srcW = widthWords
	case Fmt0888:
		srcW = widthWords * 4 / 3
	}
	scale := p.reg(RegScalerCtl)&1 != 0
	presW := srcW
	if scale {
		// The scaler halves the presented width by
		// sampling every other source pixel.
		presW = srcW / 2
	}
	interlace := p.reg(RegSPGControl)&spgInterlace != 0
	sof1 := p.reg(RegFBRSOF1)
	sof2 := p.reg(RegFBRSOF2)
	for y := 0; y < h && y < height; y++ {
		base := sof1
		line := y
		if interlace {
			line = y / 2
			if y%2 == 1 {
				base = sof2
			}
		}
		for x := 0; x < w && x < presW; x++ {
			sx := x
			if scale {
				sx = x * 2
			}
			out[y*w+x] = p.readDisplayPixel(base, uint32(line*strideWords*4), sx, format)
		}
	}
}

// readDisplayPixel converts one framebuffer pixel at a byte
// line offset plus a pixel index to XRGB8888, with the top
// byte always FF.
func (p *PVR) readDisplayPixel(base, lineOff uint32, x, format int) uint32 {
	switch format {
	case Fmt0565:
		v := uint16(p.vramWord16(base + lineOff + uint32(x*2)))
		return 0xFF000000 | uint32(expand5(int((v>>11)&0x1F)))<<16 |
			uint32(expand6(int((v>>5)&0x3F)))<<8 | uint32(expand5(int(v&0x1F)))
	case Fmt0888:
		off := base + lineOff + uint32(x*3)
		b := uint32(p.vramByte(off))
		g := uint32(p.vramByte(off + 1))
		r := uint32(p.vramByte(off + 2))
		return 0xFF000000 | r<<16 | g<<8 | b
	case Fmt8888:
		word := p.vramWord(base + lineOff + uint32(x*4))
		return 0xFF000000 | (word & 0xFFFFFF)
	}
	// Fmt0555.
	v := uint16(p.vramWord16(base + lineOff + uint32(x*2)))
	return 0xFF000000 | uint32(expand5(int((v>>10)&0x1F)))<<16 |
		uint32(expand5(int((v>>5)&0x1F)))<<8 | uint32(expand5(int(v&0x1F)))
}

// expand5 replicates a 5-bit channel into 8 bits.
func expand5(v int) int { return (v << 3) | (v >> 2) }

// expand6 replicates a 6-bit channel into 8 bits.
func expand6(v int) int { return (v << 2) | (v >> 4) }

package pvr

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// Test scaffolding for the renderer gates. The frame is
// 32 by 32 pixels at VRAM offset 0x100000 in RGB0565, the
// texture area starts at 0x2000, and TA parameter blocks
// land at TA_ISP_BASE 0 (all clear of each other).

const (
	testFB   = 0x100000
	testTex  = 0x2000
	testW    = 32
	testH    = 32
	regBase  = 0x005F8000
	bg565Val = 0x4410 // the 0565 encoding of the test background
)

// bgWord is the ISP_BACKGND_S value used by most gates: its
// channels are exact 0565 values (r5 8, g6 32, b5 16), so it
// round trips through the framebuffer unchanged.
const bgWord = 0xFF428284

// bgPresent is bgWord as Present reports it.
const bgPresent = 0xFF428284

func newRenderPVR(t *testing.T) (*PVR, []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	vram := make([]byte, 8<<20)
	p := New(vram, nil)
	wr := func(off, v uint32) { p.Write32(regBase+off, v) }
	wr(RegFBXClip, 31<<16)
	wr(RegFBYClip, 31<<16)
	wr(RegFBWCTRL, 1|(Fmt0565<<1)) // write enable, RGB0565
	wr(RegFBWSOF1, testFB)
	wr(RegFBRCTRL, 1|(Fmt0565<<1)) // display enable, RGB0565
	wr(RegFBRSOF1, testFB)
	wr(RegFBRSize, 15|(31<<10)) // 16 words wide, 32 lines
	wr(RegISPBackgndS, bgWord)
	wr(RegISPBackgndD, math.Float32bits(0))
	return p, vram
}

// TA parameters are fed with the packet helper from
// pvr_test.go (one 32-byte parameter, zero padded).

func pcw(para, list uint32) uint32 { return para<<29 | list<<24 }

func f32(f float32) uint32 { return math.Float32bits(f) }

// ispWord builds an ISP/TSP instruction word.
func ispWord(depth, cull int, textured, gouraud, offset bool) uint32 {
	w := uint32(depth) | uint32(cull)<<4
	if textured {
		w |= ispTextured
	}
	if gouraud {
		w |= ispGouraud
	}
	if offset {
		w |= ispOffset
	}
	return w
}

// tspWord builds a TSP word. sizeCode maps a texture size to
// its field code: size is 8 shifted left by the code.
func tspWord(filter int, srcBlend, dstBlend int, useAlpha bool, uSize, vSize int) uint32 {
	w := uint32(filter)
	w |= uint32(dstBlend) << 16
	w |= uint32(srcBlend) << 19
	if useAlpha {
		w |= 1 << 23
	}
	w |= uint32(sizeCode(uSize)) << 26
	w |= uint32(sizeCode(vSize)) << 29
	return w
}

func sizeCode(size int) int {
	c := 0
	for s := 8; s < size; s *= 2 {
		c++
	}
	return c
}

// tcwWord builds a TCW word for a texture at a VRAM byte
// offset in the given pixel format.
func tcwWord(addr uint32, format int, vq bool, palSelect int) uint32 {
	w := (addr / 8) & 0x1FFFFF
	w |= uint32(palSelect&0x3F) << 21
	w |= uint32(format) << 27
	if vq {
		w |= 1 << 30
	}
	return w
}

// vertex submits one 32-byte vertex parameter.
func vertex(p *PVR, list uint32, eos bool, x, y, z, u, v float32, base, off uint32) {
	w := pcw(paraVertex, list)
	if eos {
		w |= pcwEOS
	}
	packet(p, w, f32(x), f32(y), f32(z), f32(u), f32(v), base, off)
}

// quad submits a four vertex strip covering the rectangle
// (x0,y0) to (x1,y1), with UV corners (u0,v0) to (u1,v1).
func quad(p *PVR, list uint32, z, u0, v0, u1, v1, x0, y0, x1, y1 float32, base uint32) {
	vertex(p, list, false, x0, y0, z, u0, v0, base, 0)
	vertex(p, list, false, x1, y0, z, u1, v0, base, 0)
	vertex(p, list, false, x0, y1, z, u0, v1, base, 0)
	vertex(p, list, true, x1, y1, z, u1, v1, base, 0)
}

// polyHeader submits a single-volume polygon header.
func polyHeader(p *PVR, list uint32, isp, tsp, tcw, baseColor uint32) {
	packet(p, pcw(paraPolygon, list), isp, tsp, tcw, baseColor, 0, 0, 0)
}

// renderNow triggers a render the way software does, by
// writing STARTRENDER, and returns the presented frame.
func renderNow(t *testing.T, p *PVR) []uint32 {
	t.Helper()
	p.Write32(regBase+RegStartRender, 1)
	out := make([]uint32, testW*testH)
	p.Present(out, testW, testH)
	return out
}

func px(out []uint32, x, y int) uint32 { return out[y*testW+x] }

// expand565 converts a raw 0565 framebuffer word to the
// XRGB8888 value Present reports for it.
func expand565(v uint16) uint32 {
	r := int((v >> 11) & 0x1F)
	g := int((v >> 5) & 0x3F)
	b := int(v & 0x1F)
	return 0xFF000000 | uint32((r<<3)|(r>>2))<<16 |
		uint32((g<<2)|(g>>4))<<8 | uint32((b<<3)|(b>>2))
}

func putTexel565(vram []byte, base uint32, x, y, w, h int, val uint16) {
	off := base + uint32(twiddleIndex(x, y, w, h))*2
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(vram[off:], val)
}

// Gate (a): the background plane fills the frame.
func TestRenderBackground(t *testing.T) {
	p, vram := newRenderPVR(t)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if p.RenderCount() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("render count = %d, want 1", p.RenderCount())
	}
	for _, xy := range [][2]int{{0, 0}, {31, 0}, {0, 31}, {31, 31}, {16, 16}} {
		if got := px(out, xy[0], xy[1]); got != bgPresent {
			t.Errorf("pixel %v = %#08x, want %#08x", xy, got, bgPresent)
		}
	}
	// The raw framebuffer holds the hand-computed 0565
	// word: r5 8 in bits 15:11, g6 32 in bits 10:5,
	// b5 16 in bits 4:0 gives 0x4410.
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(vram[testFB:]); got != bg565Val {
		t.Errorf("raw framebuffer word = %#06x, want %#06x", got, bg565Val)
	}
	// The last pixel of the frame, at stride 64 bytes.
	off := testFB + 31*64 + 31*2
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(vram[off:]); got != bg565Val {
		t.Errorf("last pixel word = %#06x, want %#06x", got, bg565Val)
	}
}

// Gate (b): one opaque textured quad, point sampled, plus a
// bilinear midpoint computed by hand.
func TestRenderTexturedQuadPoint(t *testing.T) {
	p, vram := newRenderPVR(t)
	// 8x8 RGB565 texture. Texel (x,y) encodes r5 = x*4,
	// g6 = y*8, b5 = 31 - x*4, all distinct per texel.
	texel := func(x, y int) uint16 {
		return uint16(x*4)<<11 | uint16(y*8)<<5 | uint16(31-x*4)
	}
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			putTexel565(vram, testTex, x, y, 8, 8, texel(x, y))
		}
	}
	isp := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, true, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8) // point filter
	tcw := tcwWord(testTex, Tex565, false, 0)
	polyHeader(p, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, tcw, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.5, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	// Pixel centers map to texels by (px/4, py/4).
	for _, tc := range []struct{ px, py, tx, ty int }{
		{2, 2, 0, 0}, {6, 2, 1, 0}, {14, 10, 3, 2},
		{30, 30, 7, 7}, {18, 26, 4, 6},
	} {
		want := expand565(texel(tc.tx, tc.ty))
		if got := px(out, tc.px, tc.py); got != want {
			t.Errorf("pixel (%d,%d) = %#08x, want texel (%d,%d) %#08x",
				tc.px, tc.py, got, tc.tx, tc.ty, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestRenderTexturedQuadBilinearMidpoint(t *testing.T) {
	p, vram := newRenderPVR(t)
	// Texels (2,2) pure red and (3,2) pure green, all else
	// black.
	putTexel565(vram, testTex, 2, 2, 8, 8, 0xF800)
	putTexel565(vram, testTex, 3, 2, 8, 8, 0x07E0)
	isp := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, true, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(1, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8) // bilinear
	tcw := tcwWord(testTex, Tex565, false, 0)
	polyHeader(p, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, tcw, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	// UV offset 1/32 and range 2 in both axes. At pixel
	// (5,4) the center (5.5, 4.5) maps to u = 6/16 and
	// v = 10/32, so s = u*8 - 0.5 = 2.5 (exactly between
	// texels 2 and 3 in U) and t = v*8 - 0.5 = 2.0 (exactly
	// on texel row 2, so the V fraction is 0). The sample
	// is the exact average of red and green.
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.5, 0.03125, 0.03125, 2.03125, 2.03125, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	// Average (0.5, 0.5, 0) quantizes in 0565 to
	// r5 = round(0.5*31) = 16, g6 = round(0.5*63) = 32,
	// which Present expands to R 132, G 130, B 0.
	want := uint32(0xFF848200)
	if got := px(out, 5, 4); got != want {
		t.Errorf("bilinear midpoint = %#08x, want %#08x", got, want)
	}
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(vram[testFB+4*64+5*2:]); got != 0x8400 {
		t.Errorf("raw midpoint word = %#06x, want 0x8400", got)
	}
}

// Gate (c): depth compare. The far quad has Z 0.25, the near
// quad Z 0.75 (Z is 1/w, larger is nearer).
func TestRenderDepthGreater(t *testing.T) {
	const (
		red   = 0xFFFF0000
		green = 0xFF00FF00
	)
	isp := ispWord(DepthGreater, 0, false, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8)

	// Far first, near second: the near quad wins.
	p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	polyHeader(p, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, 0, red)
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.25, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 32, red)
	polyHeader(p, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, 0, green)
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.75, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 32, green)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if got := px(out, 16, 16); got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Errorf("far then near: center = %#08x, want green", got)
	}

	// Near first (it writes depth), far second with
	// DepthGreater: 0.25 > 0.75 is false, so the far quad
	// does not overwrite.
	p2, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	polyHeader(p2, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, 0, green)
	quad(p2, ListOpaque, 0.75, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 32, green)
	polyHeader(p2, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, 0, red)
	quad(p2, ListOpaque, 0.25, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 32, red)
	out2 := renderNow(t, p2)
	if got := px(out2, 16, 16); got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Errorf("near then far: center = %#08x, want green", got)
	}
}

// Gate (d): translucent blending, half alpha white over the
// background, SrcAlpha / OneMinusSrcA.
func TestRenderTranslucentBlend(t *testing.T) {
	p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	isp := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, false, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendSrcAlpha, BlendOneMinusSrcA, false, 8, 8)
	polyHeader(p, ListTrans, isp, tsp, 0, 0x80FFFFFF)
	quad(p, ListTrans, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0x80FFFFFF)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	// src alpha a = 128/255. Background channels are
	// (66, 130, 132)/255. out = a*1 + (1-a)*bg per channel:
	// R: 0.50196 + 0.49804*0.25882 = 0.63088, quantized
	// r5 = 20, expanded to 165.
	// G: 0.50196 + 0.49804*0.50980 = 0.75587, g6 = 48,
	// expanded to 195.
	// B: 0.50196 + 0.49804*0.51765 = 0.75979, b5 = 24,
	// expanded to 198.
	want := uint32(0xFFA5C3C6)
	if got := px(out, 16, 16); got != want {
		t.Errorf("blended center = %#08x, want %#08x", got, want)
	}
}

// Gate (e): punchthrough alpha test against ALPHA_REF 0x80.
func TestRenderPunchthrough(t *testing.T) {
	p, vram := newRenderPVR(t)
	p.Write32(regBase+RegTextControl, 0x80<<24) // ALPHA_REF = 128/255
	// 8x8 ARGB4444 texture: left half alpha nibble 4
	// (68/255, below the reference), red; right half
	// alpha nibble 12 (204/255, above), green.
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			val := uint16(0x4F00)
			if x >= 4 {
				val = 0xC0F0
			}
			off := testTex + uint32(twiddleIndex(x, y, 8, 8))*2
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(vram[off:], val)
		}
	}
	isp := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, true, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8)
	tcw := tcwWord(testTex, Tex4444, false, 0)
	polyHeader(p, ListPunch, isp, tsp, tcw, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	quad(p, ListPunch, 0.5, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if got := px(out, 6, 16); got != bgPresent {
		t.Errorf("low alpha half = %#08x, want background %#08x", got, bgPresent)
	}
	if got := px(out, 26, 16); got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Errorf("high alpha half = %#08x, want green", got)
	}
}

// Gate (f): a modifier volume over the left half, then a
// two-volume translucent modifier quad. The second
// parameter set applies where the counter is odd.
func TestRenderModifierVolumeTwoVolume(t *testing.T) {
	p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	p.Write32(regBase+RegISPBackgndS, 0xFF000000) // black bg

	// Volume primitive in the opaque modifier list over
	// the left half. Its strip triangles are front
	// facing (signed area positive after strip parity),
	// so the counter goes up by 1 inside.
	ispVol := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, false, false, false)
	packet(p, pcw(paraPolygon, ListOpaqueMod)|pcwShadow, ispVol, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	quad(p, ListOpaqueMod, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 16, 32, 0)

	// Two-volume fullscreen quad in the translucent
	// modifier list. Set 0 (even counter, outside) is
	// blue; set 1 (odd counter, inside) is red. Both sets
	// blend One / Zero so the source color lands as is.
	isp1 := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, false, true, false)
	tsp1 := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8)
	packet(p, pcw(paraPolygon, ListTransMod)|pcwVolume,
		isp1, tsp1, 0, isp1, tsp1, 0, 0)
	twoVolQuad(p, ListTransMod)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if got := px(out, 8, 16); got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Errorf("inside pixel = %#08x, want red (second set)", got)
	}
	if got := px(out, 24, 16); got != 0xFF0000FF {
		t.Errorf("outside pixel = %#08x, want blue (first set)", got)
	}
}

// twoVolQuad submits a fullscreen two-volume quad strip:
// first set color blue, second set color red, per vertex.
func twoVolQuad(p *PVR, list uint32) {
	const blue = 0xFF0000FF
	const red = 0xFFFF0000
	corners := [][4]float32{
		{0, 0, 0, 0}, {32, 0, 1, 0}, {0, 32, 0, 1}, {32, 32, 1, 1},
	}
	for i, c := range corners {
		w := pcw(paraVertex, list)
		if i == len(corners)-1 {
			w |= pcwEOS
		}
		// First 32 bytes: PCW, X, Y, Z, U, V, base, offset.
		packet(p, w, f32(c[0]), f32(c[1]), f32(0.5), f32(c[2]), f32(c[3]), blue, 0)
		// Second 32 bytes: U2, V2, base2, offset2, unused.
		packet(p, f32(c[2]), f32(c[3]), red, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	}
}

// Gate (g): VQ texture. The declared size is 8x8 (the TSP
// size fields cannot express 4), and the quad samples only
// the 0 to 0.5 UV range, which is the top-left 4x4 texels.
// Every block index is 0, so every 2x2 block shows codebook
// entry 0, whose four texels are red, green, blue, white
// in block order (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1).
func TestRenderVQTexture(t *testing.T) {
	p, vram := newRenderPVR(t)
	entry := [4]uint16{0xF800, 0x07E0, 0x001F, 0xFFFF}
	for i, v := range entry {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(vram[testTex+i*2:], v)
	}
	// Index data follows the 2048-byte codebook; the
	// 8x8 texture has a 4x4 block grid, 16 bytes, all 0.
	isp := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, true, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8)
	tcw := tcwWord(testTex, Tex565, true, 0)
	polyHeader(p, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, tcw, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.5, 0, 0, 0.5, 0.5, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	// Texel (tx,ty) center sits at pixel (tx*8+4, ty*8+4).
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		px, py int
		want   uint32
	}{
		{4, 4, 0xFFFF0000},   // texel (0,0) red
		{12, 4, 0xFF00FF00},  // texel (1,0) green
		{4, 12, 0xFF0000FF},  // texel (0,1) blue
		{12, 12, 0xFFFFFFFF}, // texel (1,1) white
		{20, 4, 0xFFFF0000},  // block (1,0), texel (0,0) again
		{28, 12, 0xFFFFFFFF}, // block (1,0), texel (1,1)
	} {
		if got := px(out, tc.px, tc.py); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("pixel (%d,%d) = %#08x, want %#08x", tc.px, tc.py, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

// Gate (h): 8-bit palette texture with 0565 palette RAM.
func TestRenderPaletteTexture(t *testing.T) {
	p, vram := newRenderPVR(t)
	p.Write32(regBase+RegPALRamCtrl, 1) // palette format 0565
	// Palette select 16 puts the Pal8 bank at index 256:
	// ((16 & 0x30) << 4) = 256. Texture bytes 1 and 2 then
	// resolve to entries 257 (red) and 258 (green).
	p.Write32(regBase+0x400+4*257, 0xF800)
	p.Write32(regBase+0x400+4*258, 0x07E0)
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			b := byte(1)
			if x >= 4 {
				b = 2
			}
			vram[testTex+uint32(twiddleIndex(x, y, 8, 8))] = b
		}
	}
	isp := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, true, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8)
	tcw := tcwWord(testTex, TexPal8, false, 16)
	polyHeader(p, ListOpaque, isp, tsp, tcw, 0xFFFFFFFF)
