	quad(p, ListOpaque, 0.5, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 32, 32, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if got := px(out, 6, 16); got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Errorf("palette left = %#08x, want red", got)
	}
	if got := px(out, 26, 16); got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Errorf("palette right = %#08x, want green", got)
	}
}

// f16 encodes a float32 with magnitude in the normal half
// range as IEEE half bits, for sprite UV words. Only the
// values 0 and 1 are used by the sprite gate.
func f16(f float32) uint32 {
	if f == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	bits := math.Float32bits(f)
	sign := (bits >> 31) & 1
	exp := int((bits>>23)&0xFF) - 127 + 15
	frac := (bits >> 13) & 0x3FF
	return sign<<15 | uint32(exp)<<10 | frac
}

// Sprite gate: a header of parameter type 5 plus the
// 64-byte sprite vertex parameter renders a solid quad.
func TestRenderSprite(t *testing.T) {
	p, _ := newRenderPVR(t)
	isp := ispWord(DepthAlways, 0, false, false, false)
	tsp := tspWord(0, BlendOne, BlendZero, false, 8, 8)
	packet(p, pcw(paraSprite, ListOpaque), isp, tsp, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	// Corners A (4,4), B (28,4), C (4,28); the fourth
	// corner D = B + C - A = (28,28) is computed by the TA.
	// First half: unused word, A xyz, B xyz, C x.
	packet(p, 0, f32(4), f32(4), f32(0.5), f32(28), f32(4), f32(0.5), f32(4))
	// Second half: C y, C z, three UV words, base color
	// (solid magenta), offset color, unused word.
	uv := f16(0) | f16(0)<<16
	packet(p, f32(28), f32(0.5), uv, uv, uv, 0xFFFF00FF, 0, 0)
	out := renderNow(t, p)
	if got := px(out, 16, 16); got != 0xFFFF00FF {
		t.Errorf("sprite center = %#08x, want magenta", got)
	}
	if got := px(out, 26, 26); got != 0xFFFF00FF {
		t.Errorf("sprite near D corner = %#08x, want magenta", got)
	}
	if got := px(out, 1, 1); got != bgPresent {
		t.Errorf("outside sprite = %#08x, want background %#08x", got, bgPresent)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/pvr/spg.go ====================

package pvr

import "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/holly"

// SPG (sync pulse generator) timing. The beam position is derived
// from the CPU cycle stream with an exact fraction: the pixel
// clock is 27 MHz against the 200 MHz CPU clock, or 13.5 MHz when
// FB_R_CTRL has vclk_div set, so pixels advance at 27/200 or
// 27/400 per CPU cycle with the remainder carried in spg.frac (the
// same accumulate-and-carry pattern the SNES core uses for its APU
// clock ratio).
//
// Register fields implemented:
//   - SPG_LOAD: bits 9:0 = pixels per line minus 1, bits 25:16 =
//     lines per field minus 1.
//   - SPG_VBLANK_INT: bits 25:16 = vblank-in line, bits 9:0 =
//     vblank-out line. Reaching the in line sets the vblank state
//     and raises EvtVBlankIn; reaching the out line clears it and
//     raises EvtVBlankOut.
//   - SPG_HBLANK_INT: bits 9:0 = pixel position of the hblank
//     event each line; bit 31 disables the event.
//   - SPG_HBLANK: bits 9:0 = hblank status window start, bits
//     25:16 = end, reported in SPG_STATUS.
//   - SPG_CONTROL bit 6: interlace. Each completed field flips
//     the field bit; without interlace the field stays 0.
//   - SPG_STATUS (read): bits 9:0 = current line, bit 10 = hblank
//     window active, bit 11 = vblank active, bit 12 = field.
//
// In interlace mode one SPG frame is one field (262 or 263 lines
// for NTSC), so the frames counter counts fields. SPG_VBLANK and
// SPG_WIDTH are stored but do not gate anything in this model.

type spgState struct {
	frac     uint32 // pixel clock remainder, in cycle*27 units
	hcount   uint32 // pixels into the current line
	vcount   uint32 // lines into the current field
	field    uint32 // current field, 0 or 1
	frames   uint64 // completed fields (frames when progressive)
	inVBlank bool
}

// htotal returns the programmed pixels per line.
func (p *PVR) htotal() uint32 { return (p.reg(RegSPGLoad) & 0x3FF) + 1 }

// vtotal returns the programmed lines per field.
func (p *PVR) vtotal() uint32 { return ((p.reg(RegSPGLoad) >> 16) & 0x3FF) + 1 }

// pixelDenominator returns the pixel clock ratio denominator:
// pixels per CPU cycle = 27/denominator.
func (p *PVR) pixelDenominator() uint64 {
	if p.reg(RegFBRCTRL)&fbVclkDiv != 0 {
		return 400 // 13.5 MHz
	}
	return 200 // 27 MHz
}

// CyclesPerLine returns the CPU cycles in one scanline under the
// current SPG_LOAD and pixel clock, rounded up. The machine uses
// it to interleave CPU execution with SPG event delivery.
func (p *PVR) CyclesPerLine() int {
	d := p.pixelDenominator()
	return int((uint64(p.htotal())*d + 26) / 27)
}

// Advance moves the beam by the given number of CPU cycles,
// raising hblank and vblank events at the programmed positions.
func (p *PVR) Advance(cycles int) {
	if cycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	d := p.pixelDenominator()
	acc := uint64(p.spg.frac) + uint64(cycles)*27
	px := acc / d
	p.spg.frac = uint32(acc % d)
	for ; px > 0; px-- {
		p.advancePixel()
	}
}

// advancePixel steps the beam one pixel, wrapping lines and
// fields and firing the per-line events.
func (p *PVR) advancePixel() {
	s := &p.spg
	s.hcount++
	hb := p.reg(RegSPGHBlankInt)
	if hb&(1<<31) == 0 && s.hcount == hb&0x3FF {
		p.raise(holly.BankNormal, 1<<holly.EvtHBlank)
	}
	if s.hcount < p.htotal() {
		return
	}
	s.hcount = 0
	s.vcount++
	if s.vcount >= p.vtotal() {
		s.vcount = 0
		s.frames++
		if p.reg(RegSPGControl)&spgInterlace != 0 {
			s.field ^= 1
		}
	}
	vbi := p.reg(RegSPGVBlankInt)
	vbin := (vbi >> 16) & 0x3FF
	vbout := vbi & 0x3FF
	if s.vcount == vbin {
		s.inVBlank = true
		p.raise(holly.BankNormal, 1<<holly.EvtVBlankIn)
	}
	if s.vcount == vbout && vbout != vbin {
		s.inVBlank = false
		p.raise(holly.BankNormal, 1<<holly.EvtVBlankOut)
	}
}

// spgStatus computes the SPG_STATUS read value.
func (p *PVR) spgStatus() uint32 {
	var v uint32
	v |= p.spg.vcount & 0x3FF
	hb := p.reg(RegSPGHBlank)
	if p.spg.hcount >= hb&0x3FF && p.spg.hcount <= (hb>>16)&0x3FF {
		v |= 1 << 10
	}
	if p.spg.inVBlank {
		v |= 1 << 11
	}
	if p.spg.field != 0 {
		v |= 1 << 12
	}
	return v
}

// SPGLine returns the current line within the field.
func (p *PVR) SPGLine() int { return int(p.spg.vcount) }

// SPGField returns the current field (0 or 1; flips per field in
// interlace mode).
func (p *PVR) SPGField() int { return int(p.spg.field) }

// SPGFrames returns the number of completed fields (frames in
// progressive mode).
func (p *PVR) SPGFrames() uint64 { return p.spg.frames }

// InVBlank reports whether the beam is inside the programmed
// vblank window.
func (p *PVR) InVBlank() bool { return p.spg.inVBlank }

// PixelsPerLine returns the programmed line total.
func (p *PVR) PixelsPerLine() int { return int(p.htotal()) }

// LinesPerField returns the programmed field total.
func (p *PVR) LinesPerField() int { return int(p.vtotal()) }


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/pvr/ta.go ====================

package pvr

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"math/bits"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/holly"
)

// TA (tile accelerator) parameter input. Parameters arrive as
// 32-byte packets at the TA FIFO (64 bytes for two-volume
// vertices and sprite vertices). The first word of a packet is
// the parameter control word (PCW):
//
//	bits 31:29  parameter type: 0 end of list, 1 user tile clip,
//	            2 control, 4 polygon or modifier volume header,
//	            5 sprite header, 7 vertex
//	bit  28     end of strip (vertex parameters)
//	bits 26:24  list type: 0 opaque, 1 opaque modifier, 2
//	            translucent, 3 translucent modifier, 4 punchthrough
//	bit  23     shadow (modifier volume semantics)
//	bit  22     two-volume: the header and its vertices carry a
//	            second ISP/TSP + TSP + TCW parameter set
//	bits 17:16  user clip mode: 0 off, 2 inside, 3 outside
//
// Polygon header packet layout (single volume): PCW, ISP/TSP
// instruction word, TSP word, TCW word, base color (packed
// ARGB8888), offset color, then two unused words. Two-volume
// headers replace the colors: PCW, set 0 (ISP/TSP, TSP, TCW),
// set 1 (ISP/TSP, TSP, TCW), one unused word; colors then live
// in the 64-byte vertices.
//
// Vertex packet layout (32 bytes, the standard textured type):
// PCW, X, Y, Z (floats; Z carries 1/w as on hardware), U, V
// (floats, or 16-bit floats in the low half of each word when
// the ISP/TSP word has UV16 set), base color, offset color.
// Two-volume vertices are 64 bytes: the same first 8 words, then
// U2, V2, base color 2, offset color 2, and four unused words.
//
// Only the packed color format is implemented; the floating
// point and intensity color formats are deferred (listed in the
// README) and such streams are read as packed.
//
// The TA also builds the hardware bookkeeping in VRAM: each
// completed primitive's parameter block (9 words) is stored at
// TA_ISP_BASE (TA_ITP_CURRENT tracks the write position), and an
// object pointer entry per covered tile is appended in the OPB
// area at TA_OL_BASE under the TA_ALLOC_CTRL per-list budgets.
// The renderer consumes the in-core primitive lists, which hold
// exactly the primitives those VRAM structures reference, in the
// same order.
const (
	pcwParaShift = 29
	pcwEOS       = 1 << 28
	pcwListShift = 24
	pcwShadow    = 1 << 23
	pcwVolume    = 1 << 22
	pcwClipShift = 16
)

const (
	paraEnd      = 0
	paraUserClip = 1
	paraControl  = 2
	paraPolygon  = 4
	paraSprite   = 5
	paraVertex   = 7
)

// Display list indices.
const (
	ListOpaque    = 0
	ListOpaqueMod = 1
	ListTrans     = 2
	ListTransMod  = 3
	ListPunch     = 4
)

// ISP/TSP instruction word fields.
const (
	ispZWriteDis = 1 << 3
	ispTextured  = 1 << 6
	ispOffset    = 1 << 7
	ispGouraud   = 1 << 8
	ispUV16      = 1 << 9
)

func ispDepthMode(w uint32) int   { return int(w & 7) }
func ispCullMode(w uint32) int    { return int((w >> 4) & 3) }
func ispFogCtrl(w uint32) int     { return int((w >> 20) & 3) }
func ispColorClamp(w uint32) bool { return w&(1<<22) != 0 }

// TSP word fields.
func tspFilter(w uint32) int      { return int(w & 7) }
func tspMipBias(w uint32) int     { return int((w >> 3) & 7) }
func tspUClamp(w uint32) bool     { return w&(1<<9) != 0 }
func tspVClamp(w uint32) bool     { return w&(1<<10) != 0 }
func tspUFlip(w uint32) bool      { return w&(1<<11) != 0 }
func tspVFlip(w uint32) bool      { return w&(1<<12) != 0 }
func tspStride(w uint32) bool     { return w&(1<<13) != 0 }
func tspLinear(w uint32) bool     { return w&(1<<14) != 0 }
func tspDstBlend(w uint32) int    { return int((w >> 16) & 7) }
func tspSrcBlend(w uint32) int    { return int((w >> 19) & 7) }
func tspIgnoreTexA(w uint32) bool { return w&(1<<22) != 0 }
func tspUseAlpha(w uint32) bool   { return w&(1<<23) != 0 }
func tspUSize(w uint32) int       { return 8 << ((w >> 26) & 7) }
func tspVSize(w uint32) int       { return 8 << ((w >> 29) & 7) }

// TCW word fields. Texture pixel formats:
const (
	Tex1555 = 0
	Tex565  = 1
	Tex4444 = 2
	TexYUV  = 3
	TexBump = 4
	TexPal4 = 5
	TexPal8 = 6
)

func tcwAddr(w uint32) uint32    { return (w & 0x1FFFFF) * 8 }
func tcwPalSelect(w uint32) int  { return int((w >> 21) & 0x3F) }
func tcwPixelFmt(w uint32) int   { return int((w >> 27) & 7) }
func tcwVQ(w uint32) bool        { return w&(1<<30) != 0 }
func tcwMipMapped(w uint32) bool { return w&(1<<31) != 0 }

// Depth compare modes for the ISP/TSP depth field.
const (
	DepthNever   = 0
	DepthLess    = 1
	DepthEqual   = 2
	DepthLEqual  = 3
	DepthGreater = 4
	DepthNotEq   = 5
	DepthGEqual  = 6
	DepthAlways  = 7
)

// Blend functions for the TSP src/dst fields.
const (
	BlendZero         = 0
	BlendOne          = 1
	BlendDstColor     = 2
	BlendOneMinusDst  = 3
	BlendSrcAlpha     = 4
	BlendOneMinusSrcA = 5
	BlendDstAlpha     = 6
	BlendOneMinusDstA = 7
)

// Vertex is one TA vertex. Z carries the reciprocal of the
// projective W, exactly as submitted; colors are packed
// ARGB8888. The 2-suffixed fields are the second parameter set
// of a two-volume primitive.
type Vertex struct {
	X, Y, Z        float32
	U, V           float32
	Base, Offset   uint32
	U2, V2         float32
	Base2, Offset2 uint32
	EOS            bool
}

// Prim is one display-list primitive: a strip of vertices under
// one parameter header, in submission order.
type Prim struct {
	List    int
	Sprite  bool
	PCW     uint32
	ISPTSP  uint32
	TSP     uint32
	TCW     uint32
	ISPTSP2 uint32
	TSP2    uint32
	TCW2    uint32
	// BaseColor and OffsetColor are the header colors, used for
	// flat shading. Two-volume headers leave them zero.
	BaseColor   uint32
	OffsetColor uint32
	Verts       []Vertex
}

// TwoVolume reports whether the primitive carries a second
// parameter set.
func (pr *Prim) TwoVolume() bool { return pr.PCW&pcwVolume != 0 }

// ClipMode returns the PCW user clip mode (0 off, 2 inside,
// 3 outside).
func (pr *Prim) ClipMode() int { return int((pr.PCW >> pcwClipShift) & 3) }

// listDoneEvent maps a list index to its TA transfer-done ASIC
// event bit.
func listDoneEvent(list int) uint32 {
	switch list {
	case ListOpaque:
		return holly.EvtOpaqueDone
	case ListOpaqueMod:
		return holly.EvtOpaqueModDone
	case ListTrans:
		return holly.EvtTransDone
	case ListTransMod:
		return holly.EvtTransModDone
	case ListPunch:
		return holly.EvtPunchDone
	}
	return holly.EvtOpaqueDone
}

// Long parameter kinds for the 64-byte parameter accumulator.
const (
	longNone = iota
	longSprite
	longVertex
)

type yuvState struct {
	mbDone   int
	partial  [384]byte // one macroblock: U, V, then four Y blocks
	partialN int
}

type taState struct {
	fifo       [8]uint32
	fifoN      int
	flipEndian bool

	hdr      Prim
	hdrValid bool
	open     int // index of the open prim in prims[hdr.List], -1 = none
	prims    [5][]Prim

	ispBytes     uint32
	opbBytes     uint32
	clip         [4]uint8 // user tile clip: x0, y0, x1, y1 in tiles
	opbCounts    []uint16
	opbErrRaised bool

	longArmed   int
	longKind    int
	longPending bool
	longBuf     [16]uint32

	yuv yuvState
}

// listInit resets the TA to accept a fresh scene.
func (t *taState) listInit() {
	t.fifoN = 0
	t.flipEndian = false
	t.hdr = Prim{}
	t.hdrValid = false
	t.open = -1
	for i := range t.prims {
		t.prims[i] = t.prims[i][:0]
	}
	t.ispBytes = 0
	t.opbBytes = 0
	t.clip = [4]uint8{0, 0, 255, 255}
	t.opbCounts = nil
	t.opbErrRaised = false
	t.longArmed = longNone
	t.longKind = longNone
	t.longPending = false
}

// writeWord consumes one word of the TA FIFO stream.
func (t *taState) writeWord(p *PVR, v uint32) {
	if t.flipEndian {
		v = bits.ReverseBytes32(v)
	}
	t.fifo[t.fifoN] = v
	t.fifoN++
	if t.fifoN < 8 {
		return
	}
	t.fifoN = 0
	pkt := t.fifo
	if t.longPending {
		copy(t.longBuf[8:], pkt[:])
		t.longPending = false
		switch t.longKind {
		case longSprite:
			t.finishSprite(p)
		case longVertex:
			t.addVertex64(p, t.longBuf)
		}
		return
	}
	if t.longArmed != longNone {
		copy(t.longBuf[:], pkt[:])
		t.longKind = t.longArmed
		t.longArmed = longNone
		t.longPending = true
		return
	}
	t.packet(p, pkt)
}

// packet dispatches one assembled 32-byte parameter.
func (t *taState) packet(p *PVR, pkt [8]uint32) {
	pcw := pkt[0]
	switch int(pcw >> pcwParaShift) {
	case paraEnd:
		t.closePrim(p)
		p.raise(holly.BankNormal, 1<<listDoneEvent(int((pcw>>pcwListShift)&7)))
	case paraUserClip:
		t.clip = [4]uint8{uint8(pkt[1]), uint8(pkt[1] >> 8), uint8(pkt[1] >> 16), uint8(pkt[1] >> 24)}
	case paraControl:
		if pkt[1]&1 != 0 {
			t.flipEndian = true
		}
		if pkt[1]&2 != 0 {
			t.flipEndian = false
		}
	case paraPolygon:
		t.closePrim(p)
		pr := Prim{List: int((pcw >> pcwListShift) & 7), PCW: pcw,
			ISPTSP: pkt[1], TSP: pkt[2], TCW: pkt[3]}
		if pcw&pcwVolume != 0 {
			pr.ISPTSP2 = pkt[4]
			pr.TSP2 = pkt[5]
			pr.TCW2 = pkt[6]
		} else {
			pr.BaseColor = pkt[4]
			pr.OffsetColor = pkt[5]
		}
		t.hdr = pr
		t.hdrValid = true
	case paraSprite:
		t.closePrim(p)
		pr := Prim{List: int((pcw >> pcwListShift) & 7), PCW: pcw,
			ISPTSP: pkt[1], TSP: pkt[2], TCW: pkt[3],
			BaseColor: pkt[4], OffsetColor: pkt[5], Sprite: true}
		t.hdr = pr
		t.hdrValid = true
		t.longArmed = longSprite
	case paraVertex:
		if !t.hdrValid {
			p.raise(holly.BankError, 1<<holly.ErrTAInputError)
			return
		}
		if t.hdr.TwoVolume() {
			copy(t.longBuf[:], pkt[:])
			t.longKind = longVertex
			t.longPending = true
			return
		}
		t.addVertex(p, decodeVertex32(pkt, t.hdr.ISPTSP&ispUV16 != 0))
	}
}

// decodeVertex32 reads one 32-byte vertex packet.
func decodeVertex32(pkt [8]uint32, uv16 bool) Vertex {
	v := Vertex{
		X:      math.Float32frombits(pkt[1]),
		Y:      math.Float32frombits(pkt[2]),
		Z:      math.Float32frombits(pkt[3]),
		Base:   pkt[6],
		Offset: pkt[7],
		EOS:    pkt[0]&pcwEOS != 0,
	}
	if uv16 {
		v.U = float16(pkt[4])
		v.V = float16(pkt[5])
	} else {
		v.U = math.Float32frombits(pkt[4])
		v.V = math.Float32frombits(pkt[5])
	}
	return v
}

// addVertex64 decodes one 64-byte two-volume vertex.
func (t *taState) addVertex64(p *PVR, w [16]uint32) {
	uv16 := t.hdr.ISPTSP&ispUV16 != 0
	v := Vertex{
		X:       math.Float32frombits(w[1]),
		Y:       math.Float32frombits(w[2]),
		Z:       math.Float32frombits(w[3]),
		Base:    w[6],
		Offset:  w[7],
		Base2:   w[10],
		Offset2: w[11],
		EOS:     w[0]&pcwEOS != 0,
	}
	if uv16 {
		v.U = float16(w[4])
		v.V = float16(w[5])
		v.U2 = float16(w[8])
		v.V2 = float16(w[9])
	} else {
		v.U = math.Float32frombits(w[4])
		v.V = math.Float32frombits(w[5])
		v.U2 = math.Float32frombits(w[8])
		v.V2 = math.Float32frombits(w[9])
	}
	t.addVertex(p, v)
}

// finishSprite builds the four corner vertices of a sprite from
// its 64-byte vertex parameter: corners A, B, C are explicit,
// the fourth is D = B + C - A. UV words pack two 16-bit floats
// each (U in the low half, V in the high half).
func (t *taState) finishSprite(p *PVR) {
	w := t.longBuf
	f := func(i int) float32 { return math.Float32frombits(w[i]) }
	ax, ay, az := f(1), f(2), f(3)
	bx, by, bz := f(4), f(5), f(6)
	cx, cy, cz := f(7), f(8), f(9)
	uv := func(i int) (float32, float32) {
		return float16(w[i]), float16(w[i] >> 16)
	}
	u0, v0 := uv(10)
	u1, v1 := uv(11)
	u2, v2 := uv(12)
	base, off := w[13], w[14]
	verts := []Vertex{
		{X: ax, Y: ay, Z: az, U: u0, V: v0, Base: base, Offset: off},
		{X: bx, Y: by, Z: bz, U: u1, V: v1, Base: base, Offset: off},
		{X: bx + cx - ax, Y: by + cy - ay, Z: bz + cz - az,
			U: u1 + u2 - u0, V: v1 + v2 - v0, Base: base, Offset: off},
		{X: cx, Y: cy, Z: cz, U: u2, V: v2, Base: base, Offset: off, EOS: true},
	}
	for _, v := range verts {
		t.addVertex(p, v)
	}
}

// addVertex appends a vertex to the open primitive, opening one
// from the current header when needed.
func (t *taState) addVertex(p *PVR, v Vertex) {
	if t.open < 0 {
		pr := t.hdr
		pr.Verts = nil
		t.prims[pr.List] = append(t.prims[pr.List], pr)
		t.open = len(t.prims[pr.List]) - 1
	}
	pr := &t.prims[t.hdr.List][t.open]
	pr.Verts = append(pr.Verts, v)
	if v.EOS {
		t.closePrim(p)
	}
}

// closePrim finalizes the open primitive: its parameter block is
// stored in VRAM at TA_ISP_BASE and an OPB entry is appended for
// every tile it covers.
func (t *taState) closePrim(p *PVR) {
	if t.open < 0 {
		return
	}
	pr := &t.prims[t.hdr.List][t.open]
	t.open = -1
	if len(pr.Verts) == 0 {
		return
	}
	base := p.reg(RegTAISPBase)
	words := [9]uint32{pr.PCW, pr.ISPTSP, pr.TSP, pr.TCW,
		pr.ISPTSP2, pr.TSP2, pr.TCW2, pr.BaseColor, pr.OffsetColor}
	for i, w := range words {
		p.vramWrite32(base+t.ispBytes+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
	ispAddr := base + t.ispBytes
	t.ispBytes += 36
	if lim := p.reg(RegTAISPLimit); lim != 0 && base+t.ispBytes > lim && !t.opbErrRaised {
		t.opbErrRaised = true
		p.raise(holly.BankError, 1<<holly.ErrParamOutOfMemory)
	}
	t.writeOPB(p, pr, ispAddr)
}

// allocSizes decodes TA_ALLOC_CTRL into per-list OPB budgets in
// bytes: size code 0 = no allocation, else 4<<code bytes.
func allocSizes(ctrl uint32) [5]uint32 {
	var out [5]uint32
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		code := (ctrl >> (4 * l)) & 3
		if code != 0 {
			out[l] = 4 << code
		}
	}
	return out
}

// writeOPB appends the primitive's object pointer to the OPB
// chain of each tile its screen bounding box covers.
func (t *taState) writeOPB(p *PVR, pr *Prim, ispAddr uint32) {
	sizes := allocSizes(p.reg(RegTAAllocCtrl))
	if sizes[pr.List] == 0 {
		return
	}
	var total uint32
	off := uint32(0)
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		if l == pr.List {
			off = total
		}
		total += sizes[l]
	}
	w, h := p.renderWidth(), p.renderHeight()
	tilesX := (w + 31) / 32
	minX, minY := float32(w), float32(h)
	maxX, maxY := float32(0), float32(0)
	for _, v := range pr.Verts {
		if v.X < minX {
			minX = v.X
		}
		if v.X > maxX {
			maxX = v.X
		}
		if v.Y < minY {
			minY = v.Y
		}
		if v.Y > maxY {
			maxY = v.Y
		}
	}
	x0 := clampInt(int(minX)/32, 0, tilesX-1)
	x1 := clampInt(int(maxX)/32, 0, tilesX-1)
	y0 := clampInt(int(minY)/32, 0, (h+31)/32-1)
	y1 := clampInt(int(maxY)/32, 0, (h+31)/32-1)
	olBase := p.reg(RegTAOLBase)
	for ty := y0; ty <= y1; ty++ {
		for tx := x0; tx <= x1; tx++ {
			tile := ty*tilesX + tx
			idx := tile*5 + pr.List
			for len(t.opbCounts) <= idx {
				t.opbCounts = append(t.opbCounts, 0)
			}
			n := uint32(t.opbCounts[idx])
			if (n+1)*4 > sizes[pr.List] {
				if !t.opbErrRaised {
					t.opbErrRaised = true
					p.raise(holly.BankError, 1<<holly.ErrOPBOutOfMemory)
				}
				continue
			}
			addr := olBase + uint32(tile)*total + off + n*4
			p.vramWrite32(addr, ispAddr)
			t.opbCounts[idx]++
			t.opbBytes += 4
		}
	}
}

func clampInt(v, lo, hi int) int {
	if v < lo {
		return lo
	}
	if v > hi {
		return hi
	}
	return v
}

// renderWidth and renderHeight give the render target size from
// the FB clip registers (640x480 when unprogrammed).
func (p *PVR) renderWidth() int {
	maxX := int((p.reg(RegFBXClip) >> 16) & 0x7FF)
	if maxX == 0 {
		return 640
	}
	return maxX + 1
}

func (p *PVR) renderHeight() int {
	maxY := int((p.reg(RegFBYClip) >> 16) & 0xFFF)
	if maxY == 0 {
		return 480
	}
	return maxY + 1
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// YUV converter
//
// YUV data written to the YUV FIFO is grouped into macroblocks
// of 384 bytes: an 8x8 U block, an 8x8 V block, then four 8x8 Y
// blocks (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) for a
// 16x16 pixel macroblock. TA_YUV_TEX_CTRL gives the texture size
// in macroblocks (bits 10:0 wide, bits 26:16 high). Each finished
// macroblock is converted to a twiddled RGB565 texture at
// TA_YUV_TEX_BASE (a VRAM byte address) using the BT.601
// conversion; when the last macroblock lands, EvtYUVDone fires.

func (t *taState) yuvWrite(p *PVR, v uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		t.yuv.partial[t.yuv.partialN] = uint8(v >> (8 * i))
		t.yuv.partialN++
		if t.yuv.partialN == len(t.yuv.partial) {
			t.yuv.partialN = 0
			t.convertMacroblock(p)
			t.yuv.mbDone++
			if total := yuvTotalMB(p); total > 0 && t.yuv.mbDone >= total {
				t.yuv.mbDone = 0
				p.raise(holly.BankNormal, 1<<holly.EvtYUVDone)
			}
		}
	}
}

// yuvTotalMB returns the macroblock count of the YUV texture
// being converted.
func yuvTotalMB(p *PVR) int {
	ctrl := p.reg(RegTAYUVTexCtrl)
	return int(ctrl&0x7FF) * int((ctrl>>16)&0x7FF)
}

// convertMacroblock converts the assembled macroblock into
// twiddled RGB565 texels in VRAM.
func (t *taState) convertMacroblock(p *PVR) {
	ctrl := p.reg(RegTAYUVTexCtrl)
	mbw := int(ctrl & 0x7FF)
	if mbw == 0 {
		return
	}
	mbx := t.yuv.mbDone % mbw
	mby := t.yuv.mbDone / mbw
	w := mbw * 16
	h := int((ctrl>>16)&0x7FF) * 16
	base := p.reg(RegTAYUVTexBase) & 0x7FFFFF
	d := t.yuv.partial
	ublock := d[0:64]
	vblock := d[64:128]
	yblock := func(bx, by int) []byte { return d[128+(by*2+bx)*64 : 128+(by*2+bx)*64+64] }
	for y := 0; y < 16; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < 16; x++ {
			yb := yblock(x>>3, y>>3)
			yy := int(yb[(y&7)*8+(x&7)])
			uu := int(ublock[(y>>1)*8+(x>>1)])
			vv := int(vblock[(y>>1)*8+(x>>1)])
			r, g, b := yuvToRGB(yy, uu, vv)
			texel := uint32(r>>3)<<11 | uint32(g>>2)<<5 | uint32(b>>3)
			off := base + uint32(twiddleIndex(mbx*16+x, mby*16+y, w, h))*2
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(p.vram[off&0x7FFFFF:], uint16(texel))
		}
	}
}

// yuvToRGB converts one pixel with the BT.601 coefficients the
// hardware documents (full-range studio swing form).
func yuvToRGB(y, u, v int) (int, int, int) {
	c := float64(y-16) * 1.164
	r := c + 1.596*float64(v-128)
	g := c - 0.813*float64(v-128) - 0.391*float64(u-128)
	b := c + 2.018*float64(u-128)
	return clamp255(r), clamp255(g), clamp255(b)
}

func clamp255(f float64) int {
	if f < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if f > 255 {
		return 255
	}
	return int(f + 0.5)
}

// twiddleIndex returns the texel index of (x, y) inside a
// twiddled texture of w by h texels (both powers of two). The
// bits of y occupy the even positions and the bits of x the odd
// positions, the smaller dimension's bits first; the remaining
// bits of the larger dimension follow in order.
func twiddleIndex(x, y, w, h int) int {
	idx := 0
	bit := 0
	xb := bits.Len(uint(w - 1))
	yb := bits.Len(uint(h - 1))
	for i := 0; i < xb || i < yb; i++ {
		if i < yb {
			idx |= ((y >> i) & 1) << bit
			bit++
		}
		if i < xb {
			idx |= ((x >> i) & 1) << bit
			bit++
		}
	}
	return idx
}

// float16 decodes an IEEE half-precision value held in the low
// 16 bits of w. Denormals flush to signed zero (documented).
func float16(w uint32) float32 {
	h := uint16(w)
	sign := uint32(h>>15) << 31
	exp := (h >> 10) & 0x1F
	frac := uint32(h & 0x3FF)
	switch {
	case exp == 0:
		return math.Float32frombits(sign)
	case exp == 0x1F:
		return math.Float32frombits(sign | 0x7F800000 | frac<<13)
	}
	return math.Float32frombits(sign | uint32(exp+112)<<23 | frac<<13)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// TA serialization
//
// Fixed part (taFixedSize bytes), then the variable part: five
// prim counts, the prims, the OPB count length, and the OPB
// counts.

const taFixedSize = 556

// primHeaderSize is the serialized size of one prim header.
const primHeaderSize = 44

// primVertSize is the serialized size of one vertex.
const primVertSize = 48

func (t *taState) serializeSize() int {
	n := taFixedSize + 20
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		for i := range t.prims[l] {
			n += primHeaderSize + primVertSize*len(t.prims[l][i].Verts)
		}
	}
	n += 4 + 2*len(t.opbCounts)
	return n
}

// taSerializedSize computes the TA section length implied by the
// counts inside a serialized TA section, or -1 if it is
// malformed.
func taSerializedSize(b []byte) int {
	if len(b) < taFixedSize+20 {
		return -1
	}
	off := taFixedSize
	var counts [5]int
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		counts[l] = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off:]))
		off += 4
	}
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		for i := 0; i < counts[l]; i++ {
			if off+primHeaderSize > len(b) {
				return -1
			}
			nv := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off+40:]))
			off += primHeaderSize + primVertSize*nv
			if off > len(b) {
				return -1
			}
		}
	}
	if off+4 > len(b) {
		return -1
	}
	nopc := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off:]))
	return off + 4 + 2*nopc
}

func (t *taState) serialize(b []byte) []byte {
	tmp := make([]byte, 4)
	put := func(v uint32) {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp, v)
		b = append(b, tmp...)
	}
	for _, w := range t.fifo {
		put(w)
	}
	put(uint32(t.fifoN))
	var flags uint32
	if t.hdrValid {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if t.flipEndian {
		flags |= 2
	}
	if t.opbErrRaised {
		flags |= 4
	}
	if t.longPending {
		flags |= 8
	}
	flags |= uint32(t.longKind&3) << 8
	flags |= uint32(t.longArmed&3) << 16
	put(flags)
	b = serializePrim(b, &t.hdr)
	put(t.ispBytes)
	put(t.opbBytes)
	put(uint32(t.clip[0]) | uint32(t.clip[1])<<8 | uint32(t.clip[2])<<16 | uint32(t.clip[3])<<24)
	for _, w := range t.longBuf {
		put(w)
	}
	put(uint32(t.yuv.mbDone))
	put(uint32(t.yuv.partialN))
	b = append(b, t.yuv.partial[:]...)
	open := t.open
	put(uint32(int32(open)))
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		put(uint32(len(t.prims[l])))
	}
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		for i := range t.prims[l] {
			b = serializePrim(b, &t.prims[l][i])
		}
	}
	put(uint32(len(t.opbCounts)))
	for _, c := range t.opbCounts {
		b = append(b, uint8(c), uint8(c>>8))
	}
	return b
}

// serializePrim appends one prim (header and vertices).
func serializePrim(b []byte, pr *Prim) []byte {
	tmp := make([]byte, 4)
	put := func(v uint32) {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp, v)
		b = append(b, tmp...)
	}
	b = append(b, uint8(pr.List))
	var fl uint8
	if pr.TwoVolume() {
		fl |= 1
	}
	if pr.Sprite {
		fl |= 2
	}
	b = append(b, fl, 0, 0)
	put(pr.PCW)
	put(pr.ISPTSP)
	put(pr.TSP)
	put(pr.TCW)
	put(pr.ISPTSP2)
	put(pr.TSP2)
	put(pr.TCW2)
	put(pr.BaseColor)
	put(pr.OffsetColor)
	put(uint32(len(pr.Verts)))
	for _, v := range pr.Verts {
		put(math.Float32bits(v.X))
		put(math.Float32bits(v.Y))
		put(math.Float32bits(v.Z))
		put(math.Float32bits(v.U))
		put(math.Float32bits(v.V))
		put(v.Base)
		put(v.Offset)
		put(math.Float32bits(v.U2))
		put(math.Float32bits(v.V2))
		put(v.Base2)
		put(v.Offset2)
		var vf uint32
		if v.EOS {
			vf = 1
		}
		put(vf)
	}
	return b
}

func (t *taState) deserialize(r *reader) bool {
	for i := range t.fifo {
		t.fifo[i] = r.u32()
	}
	t.fifoN = int(r.u32())
	flags := r.u32()
	t.hdrValid = flags&1 != 0
	t.flipEndian = flags&2 != 0
	t.opbErrRaised = flags&4 != 0
	t.longPending = flags&8 != 0
	t.longKind = int((flags >> 8) & 3)
	t.longArmed = int((flags >> 16) & 3)
	if !deserializePrim(r, &t.hdr) {
		return false
	}
	t.ispBytes = r.u32()
	t.opbBytes = r.u32()
	clip := r.u32()
	t.clip = [4]uint8{uint8(clip), uint8(clip >> 8), uint8(clip >> 16), uint8(clip >> 24)}
	for i := range t.longBuf {
		t.longBuf[i] = r.u32()
	}
	t.yuv.mbDone = int(r.u32())
	t.yuv.partialN = int(r.u32())
	copy(t.yuv.partial[:], r.bytes(384))
	t.open = int(int32(r.u32()))
	var counts [5]int
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		counts[l] = int(r.u32())
	}
	for l := 0; l < 5; l++ {
		t.prims[l] = t.prims[l][:0]
		for i := 0; i < counts[l]; i++ {
			var pr Prim
			if !deserializePrim(r, &pr) {
				return false
			}
			t.prims[l] = append(t.prims[l], pr)
		}
	}
	nopc := int(r.u32())
	t.opbCounts = make([]uint16, nopc)
	for i := range t.opbCounts {
		t.opbCounts[i] = r.u16()
	}
	return true
}

// deserializePrim reads one prim written by serializePrim.
func deserializePrim(r *reader, pr *Prim) bool {
	pr.List = int(r.u8())
	fl := r.u8()
	pr.Sprite = fl&2 != 0
	r.u8()
	r.u8()
	pr.PCW = r.u32()
	pr.ISPTSP = r.u32()
	pr.TSP = r.u32()
	pr.TCW = r.u32()
	pr.ISPTSP2 = r.u32()
	pr.TSP2 = r.u32()
	pr.TCW2 = r.u32()
	pr.BaseColor = r.u32()
	pr.OffsetColor = r.u32()
	nv := int(r.u32())
	pr.Verts = make([]Vertex, nv)
	for i := range pr.Verts {
		v := &pr.Verts[i]
		v.X = math.Float32frombits(r.u32())
		v.Y = math.Float32frombits(r.u32())
		v.Z = math.Float32frombits(r.u32())
		v.U = math.Float32frombits(r.u32())
		v.V = math.Float32frombits(r.u32())
		v.Base = r.u32()
		v.Offset = r.u32()
		v.U2 = math.Float32frombits(r.u32())
		v.V2 = math.Float32frombits(r.u32())
		v.Base2 = r.u32()
		v.Offset2 = r.u32()
		v.EOS = r.u32()&1 != 0
	}
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/system/bios.go ====================

package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// BIOS HLE for DC-4. There is no Sega BIOS in this core and
// there never will be; the boot ROM window keeps its DC-1 NOP
// sled plus one page of handler stubs written by us (bus
// physical 0x800, eight stubs of eight bytes: RTS, NOP, NOP,
// NOP). BootDisc points the documented syscall vector slots in
// low RAM at those stubs, and the machine intercepts execution
// whenever the program counter reaches a stub, services the
// call in Go, and returns through PR. The stub's own RTS is a
// safety net for execution arriving by any other path.
//
// The vector layout and calling conventions follow the public
// Dreamcast development documentation of the BIOS syscall
// interface (the same interface Flycast's reios and KallistiOS
// implement):
//
//	0x8C0000B0  system / sysinfo calls, function in R7
//	0x8C0000B4  ROM font calls, function in R1
//	0x8C0000B8  flashrom calls, function in R7
//	0x8C0000BC  GD-ROM calls (R6 = 0) and misc calls (R6 = -1),
//	            function in R7
//	0x8C0000C0  GD-ROM calls, alternate entry (same handler)
//	0x8C0000E0  system boot calls, function in R4
//	0x8C0010F0  GD-ROM direct entry (same handler as 0xBC)
//
// Handlers preserve every register except R0 (the return value)
// and memory they are documented to write; a call is charged one
// step in the machine's flat cycle model. Anything outside the
// implemented subset is recorded (see UnimplementedBIOSCalls)
// and returns 0xFFFFFFFF, the documented error shape; it never
// crashes the machine.
//
// The GD-ROM subset is the documented asynchronous request
// model, executed synchronously at EXEC_SERVER time:
//
//	functions (R7, R6 = 0):
//	  0 REQ_CMD      R4 = command, R5 = pointer to 4 parameter
//	                 words; returns a request id, or 0 while a
//	                 request is still busy
//	  1 GET_CMD_STAT R4 = request id, R5 = pointer to a status
//	                 array; returns the status (0 busy, 1
//	                 complete, 2 error) and writes the status
//	                 word followed by the first three result
//	                 words into the array
//	  2 EXEC_SERVER  executes the queued request now
//	  3 INIT_SYSTEM  (re)initializes the GD system, drops any
//	                 pending request; returns 0
//	  4 GET_DRV_STAT R4 = pointer to 4 words; writes the drive
//	                 status and the disc format
//	  7 RESET        drops any pending request; returns 0
//
//	commands (the R4 of REQ_CMD):
//	 16 PIOREAD      params FAD, sector count, buffer, 0
//	 17 DMAREAD      same layout as PIOREAD in this HLE
//	 19 GETTOC2      params session, buffer, 0, 0
//	 20 PLAY         completes at once (no CD audio model)
//	 21 PLAY2        completes at once
//	 22 PAUSE        completes at once
//	 23 RELEASE      completes at once
//	 24 INIT         initializes the drive; completes
//	 29 GET_VERSION  params buffer, 0, 0, 0; writes this HLE's
//	                 own version banner, NUL padded to 32 bytes
//	 30 GETSCD       params buffer, format, 0, 0; writes a zeroed
//	                 96 byte subcode block (data disc, stopped)
//
// Sector addresses are FADs: the absolute LBA plus 150, exactly
// as the hardware GD interface numbers them. A read result
// word 0 is the number of bytes transferred.
//
// The misc interface (R6 = -1) implements function 0 (INIT,
// returns 0); every other misc function is logged. SYSINFO
// implements function 0 (init, returns 0) and function 2 (reads
// the 24 byte console id block, zeroed here because no flash
// sysinfo partition is modeled). The system boot vector
// implements function 0 (exit to the BIOS menu: the CPU halts;
// there is no menu, so the machine idles on its last frame).
// The font and flashrom vectors are logged stubs: the public
// boot documentation does not put them on the IP boot path.

// BIOS stub ids in the handler stub page (bus physical 0x800,
// eight bytes per stub). The vector slots in RAM hold the P2
// (uncached) aliases, the way the real BIOS is reached.
const (
	stubGD       = 0 // GD-ROM and misc dispatcher
	stubSysinfo  = 1
	stubFont     = 2
	stubFlash    = 3
	stubSystem   = 4
	stubGDEntry  = 5 // GD-ROM direct entry slot (0x8C0010F0)
	stubCatchAll = 6
	stubCount    = 8

	biosStubPhysBase = 0x800
)

// biosStubAddr returns the P2 virtual address of a stub.
func biosStubAddr(id int) uint32 {
	return 0xA0000000 | uint32(biosStubPhysBase+id*8)
}

// GD-ROM function numbers (R7 with R6 = 0).
const (
	gdFuncReqCmd     = 0
	gdFuncGetCmdStat = 1
	gdFuncExecServer = 2
	gdFuncInitSystem = 3
	gdFuncGetDrvStat = 4
	gdFuncReset      = 7
)

// GD-ROM command numbers (the R4 of REQ_CMD).
const (
	gdCmdPIORead    = 16
	gdCmdDMARead    = 17
	gdCmdGetTOC     = 18
	gdCmdGetTOC2    = 19
	gdCmdPlay       = 20
	gdCmdPlay2      = 21
	gdCmdPause      = 22
	gdCmdRelease    = 23
	gdCmdInit       = 24
	gdCmdGetVersion = 29
	gdCmdGetSCD     = 30
)

// GD request status values, returned by GET_CMD_STAT.
const (
	gdStatBusy     = 0
	gdStatComplete = 1
	gdStatError    = 2
)

// gdMaxReadSectors bounds one read request; a real request
// never approaches it, and the bound keeps a garbage parameter
// block from spinning the HLE.
const gdMaxReadSectors = 8192

// gdRequest is the one outstanding asynchronous GD request.
type gdRequest struct {
	active bool
	id     uint32
	cmd    int32
	params [4]uint32
	status int32
	result [4]uint32
}

// biosState is the HLE BIOS runtime state. It is part of the
// save state (version 4) so a restore mid-boot keeps the GD
// request queue and the diagnostics.
type biosState struct {
	booted     bool
	gdInit     bool
	exitToMenu bool
	nextID     uint32
	req        gdRequest
	unimpl     []BIOSCall
	unimplOver int
}

// BIOSCall records one unimplemented BIOS call shape: the
// vector it arrived on, the function number, and how many
// times it was hit.
type BIOSCall struct {
	Vector   string
	Function int32
	Count    int
}

// maxBIOSUnimpl caps the recorded unimplemented call shapes.
const maxBIOSUnimpl = 8

// Vector ids for the serialized form of a BIOSCall.
const (
	biosVecGD = iota
	biosVecGDCmd
	biosVecSysinfo
	biosVecFont
	biosVecFlash
	biosVecSystem
	biosVecMisc
	biosVecStub
)

var biosVecNames = []string{
	"GD 0x8C0000BC", "GD command", "SYSINFO 0x8C0000B0",
	"FONT 0x8C0000B4", "FLASHROM 0x8C0000B8", "SYSTEM 0x8C0000E0",
	"GD misc (R6=-1)", "BIOS stub",
}

func biosVecID(name string) int {
	for i, n := range biosVecNames {
		if n == name {
			return i
		}
	}
	return biosVecStub
}

// UnimplementedBIOSCalls returns a copy of the recorded
// unimplemented BIOS call shapes, in the order first seen.
func (m *Machine) UnimplementedBIOSCalls() []BIOSCall {
	out := make([]BIOSCall, len(m.bios.unimpl))
	copy(out, m.bios.unimpl)
	return out
}

// BIOSDiagnostics is the unload-time summary of the BIOS HLE:
// whether the machine booted, and every unimplemented call
// shape it met. The libretro shell logs it at unload, the same
// pattern as the PS1 core.
type BIOSDiagnostics struct {
	Booted   bool
	Calls    []BIOSCall
	Overflow int
}

// BIOSDiagnostics returns the machine's BIOS HLE diagnostics.
func (m *Machine) BIOSDiagnostics() BIOSDiagnostics {
	return BIOSDiagnostics{
		Booted:   m.bios.booted,
		Calls:    m.UnimplementedBIOSCalls(),
		Overflow: m.bios.unimplOver,
	}
}

// String renders the diagnostics summary.
func (d BIOSDiagnostics) String() string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "GoDC BIOS HLE: booted=%v", d.Booted)
	if len(d.Calls) == 0 {
		sb.WriteString(", no unimplemented BIOS calls")
		return sb.String()
	}
	sb.WriteString(", unimplemented BIOS calls:")
	for _, c := range d.Calls {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, " [%s fn %d x%d]", c.Vector, c.Function, c.Count)
	}
	if d.Overflow > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&sb, " (+%d more shapes)", d.Overflow)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// Booted reports whether BootDisc has run on this machine.
func (m *Machine) Booted() bool { return m.bios.booted }

// recordUnimpl notes an unimplemented BIOS call shape.
func (m *Machine) recordUnimpl(vecID int, fn int32) {
	name := biosVecNames[vecID]
	for i := range m.bios.unimpl {
		if m.bios.unimpl[i].Vector == name && m.bios.unimpl[i].Function == fn {
			m.bios.unimpl[i].Count++
			return
		}
	}
	if len(m.bios.unimpl) >= maxBIOSUnimpl {
		m.bios.unimplOver++
		return
	}
	m.bios.unimpl = append(m.bios.unimpl, BIOSCall{Vector: name, Function: fn, Count: 1})
}

// stepBIOS services a BIOS syscall if the CPU is sitting on a
// handler stub, returning true when it did. The return is the
// documented shape of a BIOS call: PC becomes PR.
func (m *Machine) stepBIOS() bool {
	pc := m.CPU.PC
	switch pc >> 29 {
	case 0, 4, 5: // P0 (MMU off), P1, P2
	default:
		return false
	}
	phys := pc & 0x1FFFFFFF
	if phys < biosStubPhysBase || phys >= biosStubPhysBase+stubCount*8 {
		return false
	}
	off := phys - biosStubPhysBase
	if off&7 != 0 {
		return false
	}
	m.execBIOSStub(int(off >> 3))
	m.CPU.PC = m.CPU.PR
	return true
}

// execBIOSStub runs one stub's handler with the CPU registers
// as its arguments.
func (m *Machine) execBIOSStub(id int) {
	switch id {
	case stubGD, stubGDEntry:
		m.gdDispatch()
	case stubSysinfo:
		m.sysinfoDispatch()
	case stubFont:
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecFont, int32(m.CPU.R[1]))
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	case stubFlash:
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecFlash, int32(m.CPU.R[7]))
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	case stubSystem:
		m.systemDispatch()
	default:
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecStub, int32(id))
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	}
}

// gdDispatch routes the GD-ROM / misc vector by R6 and R7.
func (m *Machine) gdDispatch() {
	fn := int32(m.CPU.R[7])
	switch sel := int32(m.CPU.R[6]); {
	case sel == -1:
		// The misc interface. Function 0 is INIT.
		if fn == 0 {
			m.CPU.R[0] = 0
			return
		}
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecMisc, fn)
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	case sel == 0:
		switch fn {
		case gdFuncReqCmd:
			m.gdReqCmd()
		case gdFuncGetCmdStat:
			m.gdGetCmdStat()
		case gdFuncExecServer:
			m.gdExecServer()
		case gdFuncInitSystem:
			m.bios.gdInit = true
			m.bios.req = gdRequest{}
			m.CPU.R[0] = 0
		case gdFuncGetDrvStat:
			m.gdGetDrvStat()
		case gdFuncReset:
			m.bios.req = gdRequest{}
			m.CPU.R[0] = 0
		default:
			// Known but unimplemented functions (G1 DMA end,
			// read abort, change data type, set PIO callback)
			// and every unknown function land here.
			m.recordUnimpl(biosVecGD, fn)
			m.CPU.R[0] = gdStatError
		}
	default:
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecGD, fn)
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	}
}

// guestPA translates a guest virtual address to the
// physical address the bus routes on. The machine runs with
// the MMU off, so the P0, P1, and P2 areas all mask down to
// the physical address.
func guestPA(va uint32) uint32 { return va & 0x1FFFFFFF }

// gdReqCmd queues a command from the parameter block at R5.
func (m *Machine) gdReqCmd() {
	if m.bios.req.active && m.bios.req.status == gdStatBusy {
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0
		return
	}
	ptr := guestPA(m.CPU.R[5])
	var params [4]uint32
	for i := range params {
		params[i] = m.Bus.Read32(ptr + uint32(4*i))
	}
	m.bios.nextID++
	m.bios.req = gdRequest{
		active: true,
		id:     m.bios.nextID,
		cmd:    int32(m.CPU.R[4]),
		params: params,
		status: gdStatBusy,
	}
	m.CPU.R[0] = m.bios.req.id
}

// gdExecServer executes the queued request synchronously.
func (m *Machine) gdExecServer() {
	m.CPU.R[0] = 0
	req := &m.bios.req
	if !req.active || req.status != gdStatBusy {
		return
	}
	req.status, req.result = m.execGDCommand(req.cmd, req.params)
}

// gdGetCmdStat reports the queued request's status.
func (m *Machine) gdGetCmdStat() {
	id := m.CPU.R[4]
	ptr := guestPA(m.CPU.R[5])
	req := &m.bios.req
	if !req.active || req.id != id {
		if ptr != 0 {
			m.Bus.Write32(ptr, gdStatError)
		}
		m.CPU.R[0] = gdStatError
		return
	}
	if ptr != 0 {
		m.Bus.Write32(ptr, uint32(req.status))
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			m.Bus.Write32(ptr+uint32(4*(i+1)), req.result[i])
		}
	}
	m.CPU.R[0] = uint32(req.status)
}

// gdGetDrvStat writes the drive status block at R4: the drive
// status (2 standby when a disc is present, 7 empty when not,
// in the published drive status numbering), the disc format
// (0 GD-ROM), and two zero words.
func (m *Machine) gdGetDrvStat() {
	ptr := guestPA(m.CPU.R[4])
	stat, format := uint32(7), uint32(0)
	if m.Disc != nil {
		stat = 2
	}
	m.Bus.Write32(ptr, stat)
	m.Bus.Write32(ptr+4, format)
	m.Bus.Write32(ptr+8, 0)
	m.Bus.Write32(ptr+12, 0)
	m.CPU.R[0] = 0
}

// execGDCommand runs one GD command now.
func (m *Machine) execGDCommand(cmd int32, params [4]uint32) (int32, [4]uint32) {
	var zero [4]uint32
	switch cmd {
	case gdCmdInit:
		m.bios.gdInit = true
		return gdStatComplete, zero
	case gdCmdPIORead, gdCmdDMARead:
		n, ok := m.gdReadSectors(params[0], params[1], params[2])
		if !ok {
			return gdStatError, zero
		}
		return gdStatComplete, [4]uint32{n, 0, 0, 0}
	case gdCmdGetTOC2:
		if !m.gdWriteTOC(params[0], params[1]) {
			return gdStatError, zero
		}
		return gdStatComplete, zero
	case gdCmdGetVersion:
		// This HLE's own version banner; not a Sega string.
		banner := "ITAK GD HLE 1.000"
		buf := make([]byte, 32)
		copy(buf, banner)
		m.writeGuest(params[0], buf)
		return gdStatComplete, zero
	case gdCmdGetSCD:
		// A zeroed 96 byte subcode block: a data disc at rest.
		m.writeGuest(params[0], make([]byte, 96))
		return gdStatComplete, zero
	case gdCmdPlay, gdCmdPlay2, gdCmdPause, gdCmdRelease:
		// CD audio is not modeled; the commands complete.
		return gdStatComplete, zero
	default:
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecGDCmd, cmd)
		return gdStatError, zero
	}
}

// gdReadSectors reads count 2048 byte sectors starting at the
// given FAD into guest RAM at buf. It returns the byte count.
func (m *Machine) gdReadSectors(fad, count, buf uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	if m.Disc == nil || count > gdMaxReadSectors {
		return 0, false
	}
	lba := int(fad) - 150
	var total uint32
	for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++ {
		sec, err := m.Disc.ReadSector(lba + int(i))
		if err != nil {
			return total, false
		}
		m.writeGuest(buf+total, sec)
		total += uint32(len(sec))
	}
	return total, true
}

// gdSessions derives the session start FADs of the loaded
// disc: a session starts at the first track and at every data
// track that follows an audio track, the standard two session
// GD layout (and the single session MIL-CD layout).
func (m *Machine) gdSessions() []uint32 {
	var starts []uint32
	prevAudio := false
	for i, tr := range m.Disc.Tracks {
		isData := tr.Ctrl&4 != 0
		if i == 0 || (isData && prevAudio) {
			starts = append(starts, uint32(tr.LBA)+150)
		}
		prevAudio = !isData
	}
	return starts
}

// gdWriteTOC writes the TOC table for GETTOC2 at buf:
//
//	word 0        number of sessions
//	word 1        number of tracks
//	words 2..     per session: start FAD, end FAD
//	then          per track: FAD, control byte value
//
// The session parameter selects nothing in this HLE beyond a
// range check; the full table is always written.
func (m *Machine) gdWriteTOC(session, buf uint32) bool {
	if m.Disc == nil {
		return false
	}
	starts := m.gdSessions()
	if int(session) > len(starts) {
		return false
	}
	tracks := m.Disc.Tracks
	// Disc end FAD: the last track's end LBA plus 150.
	endFAD := uint32(0)
	if n := len(tracks); n > 0 {
		last := tracks[n-1]
		endFAD = uint32(last.LBA+int(last.Length)/last.SectorSize) + 150
	}
	words := []uint32{uint32(len(starts)), uint32(len(tracks))}
	for i, s := range starts {
		end := endFAD
		if i+1 < len(starts) {
			end = starts[i+1] - 1
		}
		words = append(words, s, end)
	}
	for _, tr := range tracks {
		words = append(words, uint32(tr.LBA)+150, uint32(tr.Ctrl))
	}
	data := make([]byte, 4*len(words))
	for i, w := range words {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(data[4*i:], w)
	}
	m.writeGuest(buf, data)
	return true
}

// writeGuest copies bytes into guest RAM through the bus.
func (m *Machine) writeGuest(va uint32, data []byte) {
	pa := guestPA(va)
	for i := 0; i+3 < len(data); i += 4 {
		m.Bus.Write32(pa+uint32(i), binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[i:]))
	}
	for i := len(data) &^ 3; i < len(data); i++ {
		m.Bus.Write8(pa+uint32(i), data[i])
	}
}

// sysinfoDispatch routes the system / sysinfo vector by R7.
func (m *Machine) sysinfoDispatch() {
	switch fn := int32(m.CPU.R[7]); fn {
	case 0: // SYSINFO_INIT
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0
	case 2: // SYSINFO_ID: the 24 byte console id block. No flash
		// sysinfo partition is modeled, so the block stays zeroed,
		// matching the copy BootDisc leaves at 0x8C000068.
		m.writeGuest(m.CPU.R[4], make([]byte, 24))
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0
	default:
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecSysinfo, fn)
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	}
}

// systemDispatch routes the system boot vector by R4.
// Function 0 is the documented exit to the BIOS menu: real
// software never returns from it. This HLE has no menu, so the
// CPU halts and the machine idles on its last frame.
func (m *Machine) systemDispatch() {
	switch fn := int32(m.CPU.R[4]); fn {
	case 0:
		m.bios.exitToMenu = true
		m.CPU.Halted = true
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0
	default:
		m.recordUnimpl(biosVecSystem, fn)
		m.CPU.R[0] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	}
}

// biosStateSize is the serialized size of the BIOS block:
// booted / gdInit / exitToMenu flags and padding (4), nextID
// (4), the GD request (active byte and padding 4, status 4,
// id 4, cmd 4, params 16, result 16 = 48), the unimplemented
// call shapes (count 4, overflow 4, then maxBIOSUnimpl records
// of vector id 4, function 4, count 4, padding 4 = 128).
const biosStateSize = 4 + 4 + 48 + 8 + maxBIOSUnimpl*16

// serializeBIOS writes the BIOS block.
func (m *Machine) serializeBIOS() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, biosStateSize)
	if m.bios.booted {
		out[0] = 1
	}
	if m.bios.gdInit {
		out[1] = 1
	}
	if m.bios.exitToMenu {
		out[2] = 1
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[4:], m.bios.nextID)
	req := &m.bios.req
	if req.active {
		out[8] = 1
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[12:], uint32(req.status))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[16:], req.id)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[20:], uint32(req.cmd))
	for i, v := range req.params {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[24+4*i:], v)
	}
	for i, v := range req.result {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[40+4*i:], v)
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[56:], uint32(len(m.bios.unimpl)))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[60:], uint32(m.bios.unimplOver))
	for i, c := range m.bios.unimpl {
		off := 64 + 16*i
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], uint32(biosVecID(c.Vector)))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off+4:], uint32(c.Function))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off+8:], uint32(c.Count))
	}
	return out
}

// deserializeBIOS reads the BIOS block back.
func (m *Machine) deserializeBIOS(b []byte) {
	m.bios = biosState{
		booted:     b[0] != 0,
		gdInit:     b[1] != 0,
		exitToMenu: b[2] != 0,
		nextID:     binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[4:]),
		req: gdRequest{
			active: b[8] != 0,
			status: int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[12:])),
			id:     binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[16:]),
			cmd:    int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[20:])),
		},
		unimplOver: int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[60:])),
	}
	for i := range m.bios.req.params {
		m.bios.req.params[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[24+4*i:])
		m.bios.req.result[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[40+4*i:])
	}
	n := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[56:]))
	if n > maxBIOSUnimpl {
		n = maxBIOSUnimpl
	}
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		off := 64 + 16*i
		vecID := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off:]))
		if vecID < 0 || vecID >= len(biosVecNames) {
			vecID = biosVecStub
		}
		m.bios.unimpl = append(m.bios.unimpl, BIOSCall{
			Vector:   biosVecNames[vecID],
			Function: int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off+4:])),
			Count:    int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off+8:])),
		})
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/system/boot.go ====================

package system

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-dreamcast/gd"
)

// BIOS HLE boot (DC-4), following the documented Dreamcast boot
// sequence. The real BIOS reads the disc's IP.BIN (the first 16
// sectors of the data area, 32 KB) into RAM at 0x8C008000, sets
// up the BIOS state in low RAM, and jumps to the IP's entry at
// 0x8C008300; the IP then loads the boot file named in its own
// header (offset 0x60, conventionally 1ST_READ.BIN) through the
// GD-ROM syscall interface and jumps to it at 0x8C010000.
//
// BootDisc performs exactly the machine side of that contract.
// No Sega BIOS bytes exist or run anywhere in the process: the
// syscall vectors point at this core's own handler stubs (see
// bios.go), and the work the BIOS would have done between power
// on and the IP entry is done here in Go.
//
// Documented handover state established here:
//
//   - IP.BIN is copied to 0x8C008000 (physical 0x0C008000).
//   - The BIOS variables page 0x8C000000 to 0x8C001000 is
//     cleared, then the syscall vector table is written at its
//     documented slots: sysinfo 0x8C0000B0, font 0x8C0000B4,
//     flashrom 0x8C0000B8, GD-ROM 0x8C0000BC and 0x8C0000C0,
//     system boot 0x8C0000E0, and the GD-ROM direct entry
//     pointer at 0x8C0010F0.
//   - The SYSINFO id block lives at 0x8C000068 (24 bytes). It
//     stays zeroed: the real BIOS copies it from the flash
//     sysinfo partition, which this core does not model.
//   - The CPU enters at PC 0x8C008300 with SP 0x8C00F000 (the
//     boot stack region the public boot documentation places
//     just below the 0x8C00F000 vector and scratch block) and
//     PR 0. SR keeps the CPU's power-on value; a real IP sets
//     its own SR, VBR, and stack as its first act, and the
//     fixture IP does exactly that.
//
// The boot file itself is descrambled on retail discs; this
// HLE serves the file bytes as stored, so unscrambled
// (homebrew layout) images are the supported form.

const (
	// IPLoadAddr is the documented IP.BIN load address.
	IPLoadAddr = 0x8C008000
	// IPEntryAddr is the documented IP entry point.
	IPEntryAddr = 0x8C008300
	// BootFileAddr is the documented load address of the boot
	// file the IP loads (1ST_READ.BIN on retail discs).
	BootFileAddr = 0x8C010000
	// bootStackTop is the stack pointer at IP entry.
	bootStackTop = 0x8C00F000
	// biosVarsSize is the cleared BIOS variables area size.
	biosVarsSize = 0x1000
)

// BootDisc boots the loaded disc through the HLE BIOS: it reads
// and validates the disc's IP.BIN with the gd parser, installs
// it and the BIOS handover state in RAM, and enters the IP.
// It fails cleanly, before touching the CPU, when the disc has
// no IP.BIN or the IP.BIN is malformed.
func (m *Machine) BootDisc() error {
	if m.Disc == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: BootDisc with no disc loaded")
	}
	ipRaw, err := m.Disc.BootArea()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: read IP.BIN: %w", err)
	}
	if _, err := gd.ParseIPBin(ipRaw); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: parse IP.BIN: %w", err)
	}

	m.CPU.Reset()
	m.bios = biosState{}

	// The BIOS variables page starts cleared, as does the rest
	// of the IP's footprint (IP.BIN overwrites 0x8000 on).
	for i := 0; i < biosVarsSize; i++ {
		m.Bus.RAM[i] = 0
	}
	copy(m.Bus.RAM[0x8000:], ipRaw)

	// The documented syscall vector table. The slots are
	// named by their virtual addresses (0x8C0000B0 and
	// family); the bus routes physical addresses, so these
	// are the physical forms (RAM offsets 0xB0 and 0x10F0).
	wr := func(pa, v uint32) { m.Bus.Write32(pa, v) }
	wr(0x0C0000B0, biosStubAddr(stubSysinfo))
	wr(0x0C0000B4, biosStubAddr(stubFont))
	wr(0x0C0000B8, biosStubAddr(stubFlash))
	wr(0x0C0000BC, biosStubAddr(stubGD))
	wr(0x0C0000C0, biosStubAddr(stubGD))
	wr(0x0C0000E0, biosStubAddr(stubSystem))
	// The GD-ROM direct entry pointer in the stub block.
	wr(0x0C0010F0, biosStubAddr(stubGDEntry))

	// Post-BIOS CPU state: enter the IP.
	m.CPU.PC = IPEntryAddr
	m.CPU.R[15] = bootStackTop
	m.CPU.PR = 0
	m.bios.booted = true
	return nil
}

// Reset powers the machine back to its post-boot state: a
// fresh machine with the same disc (if any) booted again
// through BootDisc. The host pad state is preserved across the
// reset, the way a held controller survives a console reset.
func (m *Machine) Reset() {
	disc := m.Disc
	discPath := m.discPath
	pad := m.pad
	*m = *New()
	m.pad = pad
	m.SetButtons(pad)
	if disc != nil {
		m.Disc = disc
		m.discPath = discPath
		// BootDisc can only fail on a disc that already
		// booted once; ignore the result.
		_ = m.BootDisc()
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/system/dc2_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Interrupt delivery gate: a hand assembled SH-4 program plus its
// interrupt handler, run on the whole machine.
//
// The program (VA 0x8C000000, data page at 0x8C000800) sets up
// SR and VBR, programs the Holly masks (vblank-in at level 6,
// render-done at level 4) and a small SPG (20x10, vblank-in on
// line 8), then raises SR.IMASK to 7, submits an end-of-list TA
// packet, and triggers a render. The render-done interrupt
// (level 4) must stay pending while IMASK is 7: the handler
// copies a flag the program sets just before dropping IMASK to
// 0, so flagcopy == 1 proves the handler could not have run
// during the masked window. Each vblank handler entry increments
// a counter and appends 'V' to a log; the render entry appends
// 'R'. After RunFrame the counter must equal the PVR field count
// exactly (one serviced vblank per field, no re-entry, which is
// what the handler's ISTNRM write-1-to-clear ack guarantees) and
// the log must start with R, then only V.

var irqProgramWords = []uint16{
	// 0x00: load the data page base, jump over the literal.
	0xDA01,         // MOV.L @(1,PC),R10   ; literal at 0x08
	0xA003,         // BRA 0x0C
	0x0009,         // NOP (delay slot)
	0x0009,         // pad
	0x0800, 0x8C00, // 0x08: .long 0x8C000800
	// 0x0C: main setup. R10 = data page.
	0x50A0,                         // MOV.L @(0,R10),R0   ; SR value, IMASK 0
	0x400E,                         // LDC R0,SR
	0x50A1,                         // MOV.L @(1,R10),R0   ; VBR value
	0x402E,                         // LDC R0,VBR
	0x5FA2,                         // MOV.L @(2,R10),R15  ; stack top
	0x51A3,                         // MOV.L @(3,R10),R1   ; IML6LVL addr
	0x52A4,                         // MOV.L @(4,R10),R2   ; vblank-in bit
	0x2122,                         // MOV.L R2,@R1
	0x51A5,                         // MOV.L @(5,R10),R1   ; IML4LVL addr
	0x52A6,                         // MOV.L @(6,R10),R2   ; render-done bit
	0x2122,                         // MOV.L R2,@R1
	0x51A7,                         // MOV.L @(7,R10),R1   ; SPG_LOAD addr
	0x52A8,                         // MOV.L @(8,R10),R2   ; SPG_LOAD value
	0x2122,                         // MOV.L R2,@R1
	0x51A9,                         // MOV.L @(9,R10),R1   ; SPG_VBLANK_INT addr
	0x52AA,                         // MOV.L @(10,R10),R2
	0x2122,                         // MOV.L R2,@R1
	0x50AF,                         // MOV.L @(15,R10),R0  ; SR value, IMASK 7
	0x400E,                         // LDC R0,SR
	0x51AB,                         // MOV.L @(11,R10),R1  ; TA FIFO addr
	0xE200,                         // MOV #0,R2
	0x2122, 0x2122, 0x2122, 0x2122, // MOV.L R2,@R1 x8: end of list
	0x2122, 0x2122, 0x2122, 0x2122,
	0x51AC, // MOV.L @(12,R10),R1  ; STARTRENDER addr
	0x2122, // MOV.L R2,@R1        ; render: level 4 pends under IMASK 7
	0x51AE, // MOV.L @(14,R10),R1  ; scratch base
	0xE201, // MOV #1,R2
	0x1123, // MOV.L R2,@(3,R1)    ; flag = 1
	0x50A0, // MOV.L @(0,R10),R0   ; SR value, IMASK 0
	0x400E, // LDC R0,SR           ; mask drops: render IRQ accepted next
	0xAFFE, // loop: BRA loop
	0x0009, // NOP (delay slot)
}

// irqHandlerWords sits at image offset 0x1600 (VBR 0x8C001000 +
// 0x600). Bank 1 registers are the handler's own; R10 still
// points at the data page and R3 at the scratch page. Note the
// core's BT/BF model (as documented in the DC-1 machine test):
// the delay slot of a conditional branch runs only when the
// branch is taken, so every BT delay slot here holds a NOP and
// no load-bearing instruction sits in one.
var irqHandlerWords = []uint16{
	0x50AD, // MOV.L @(13,R10),R0  ; ISTNRM addr
	0x53AE, // MOV.L @(14,R10),R3  ; scratch base
	0x6102, // MOV.L @R0,R1        ; ISTNRM value
	0xE204, // MOV #4,R2           ; render-done bit
	0x2128, // TST R2,R1
	0x8909, // BT +9 -> 0x1620 (skip render service)
	0x0009, // NOP (delay slot)
	0x5434, // MOV.L @(4,R3),R4    ; render IRQ count
	0x7401, // ADD #1,R4
	0x1344, // MOV.L R4,@(4,R3)
	0x5433, // MOV.L @(3,R3),R4    ; flag
	0x1345, // MOV.L R4,@(5,R3)    ; flagcopy = flag
	0xE652, // MOV #0x52,R6        ; 'R'
	0xB00F, // BSR log (0x163C)
	0x0009, // NOP (delay slot)
	0x2022, // MOV.L R2,@R0        ; ack render-done
	// 0x1620:
	0xE208, // MOV #8,R2           ; vblank-in bit
	0x2128, // TST R2,R1
	0x8907, // BT +7 -> 0x1636 (done)
	0x0009, // NOP (delay slot)
	0x5430, // MOV.L @(0,R3),R4    ; vblank counter
	0x7401, // ADD #1,R4
	0x1340, // MOV.L R4,@(0,R3)
	0xE656, // MOV #0x56,R6        ; 'V'
	0xB004, // BSR log (0x163C)
	0x0009, // NOP (delay slot)
	0x2022, // MOV.L R2,@R0        ; ack vblank-in
	// 0x1636:
	0x002B, // RTE
	0x0009, // NOP (delay slot)
	0x0009, // pad (unreachable)
	// 0x163C: log: append the byte in R6 at scratch+32+loglen
	// (offset 32 keeps the log clear of the counter words).
	0x5431, // MOV.L @(1,R3),R4    ; log length
	0x6533, // MOV R3,R5
	0x7520, // ADD #32,R5
	0x354C, // ADD R4,R5
	0x2560, // MOV.B R6,@R5
	0x7401, // ADD #1,R4
	0x1341, // MOV.L R4,@(1,R3)
	0x000B, // RTS
	0x0009, // NOP (delay slot)
}

// irqDataPage is written by the test at physical 0x0C000800.
var irqDataPage = []uint32{
	0x40000000,     // 0: SR, IMASK 0
	0x8C001000,     // 1: VBR
	0x8C010000,     // 2: stack top
	0xA05F6930,     // 3: SB_IML6LVL (NRM row)
	0x00000008,     // 4: vblank-in bit
	0xA05F6920,     // 5: SB_IML4LVL (NRM row)
	0x00000004,     // 6: render-done (TSP) bit
	0xA05F80D8,     // 7: SPG_LOAD
	(9 << 16) | 19, // 8: 20 pixels, 10 lines
	0xA05F80CC,     // 9: SPG_VBLANK_INT
	(8 << 16) | 0,  // 10: in on line 8, out on line 0
	0xA0500000,     // 11: TA FIFO
	0xA05F8014,     // 12: STARTRENDER
	0xA05F6900,     // 13: SB_ISTNRM
	0x8C002000,     // 14: scratch base
	0x40000070,     // 15: SR, IMASK 7
}

const (
	scratchPhys = 0x0C002000
)

func loadIRQMachine(t *testing.T) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	img := make([]byte, 0x1700)
	put := func(off int, words []uint16) {
		for i, w := range words {
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(img[off+2*i:], w)
		}
	}
	put(0, irqProgramWords)
	put(0x1600, irqHandlerWords)
	m := New()
	m.LoadProgram(0x0C000000, img)
	// The data page sits inside the image span (offset 0x800), so
	// it is written after the image.
	for i, v := range irqDataPage {
		m.Bus.Write32(0x0C000800+uint32(4*i), v)
	}
	return m
}

func TestInterruptProgramOrderAndCounting(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadIRQMachine(t)
	m.RunFrame()

	counter := m.Bus.Read32(scratchPhys + 0)
	frames := m.PVR.SPGFrames()
	if frames < 100 {
		t.Fatalf("SPG frames after one RunFrame = %d, want > 100", frames)
	}
	// The counter must track the frame count closely. It cannot
	// be exact for the first frame: until the program reprograms
	// the SPG, RunFrame chunks by the default scanline (12,712
	// cycles), and the beam crosses several of the tiny 10-line
	// fields inside the first chunk's single PVR advance, so a
	// few vblank-in events coalesce in the ISTNRM bit before the
	// CPU can service them (the same coalescing the hardware
	// status bit exhibits). What must hold exactly: one log entry
	// per serviced interrupt, and the deficit must not grow on
	// the second frame (a missed ack would make the handler
	// re-enter endlessly and the counter would run away instead).
	deficit := int64(frames) - int64(counter)
	if deficit < 0 || deficit > 8 {
		t.Errorf("vblank counter = %d, SPG frames = %d, deficit %d outside [0, 8]", counter, frames, deficit)
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(scratchPhys + 16); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("render IRQ count = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(scratchPhys + 20); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("flagcopy = %d, want 1 (handler ran only after IMASK dropped)", got)
	}
	logLen := int(m.Bus.Read32(scratchPhys + 4))
	if logLen != int(counter)+1 {
		t.Fatalf("log length = %d, want counter+1 = %d", logLen, counter+1)
	}
	if b := m.Bus.Read8(scratchPhys + 32); b != 'R' {
		t.Errorf("log[0] = %q, want 'R' (render-done serviced first)", b)
	}
	for i := 1; i < logLen; i++ {
		if b := m.Bus.Read8(scratchPhys + 32 + uint32(i)); b != 'V' {
			t.Fatalf("log[%d] = %q, want 'V'", i, b)
		}
	}

	// A second frame keeps the count exact (the ack in the
	// handler is what stops re-entry; a missed ack would make
	// the counter run away from the frame count).
	m.RunFrame()
	counter = m.Bus.Read32(scratchPhys + 0)
	deficit2 := int64(m.PVR.SPGFrames()) - int64(counter)
	if deficit2 < 0 || deficit2 > deficit {
		t.Errorf("after frame 2: deficit grew from %d to %d (counter %d, frames %d)",
			deficit, deficit2, counter, m.PVR.SPGFrames())
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(scratchPhys + 16); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("render IRQ count after frame 2 = %d, want still 1", got)
	}
	if logLen2 := int(m.Bus.Read32(scratchPhys + 4)); logLen2 != int(counter)+1 {
		t.Errorf("log length after frame 2 = %d, want counter+1 = %d", logLen2, counter+1)
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Textured quad end to end: the texture is uploaded through the
// 64-bit VRAM window (bank interleave), submitted as a TA stream
// over the bus, rendered, and read back from the VRAM
// framebuffer. The quad spans (0.5, 0.5) to (64.5, 64.5) of a
// 64x64 target, so pixel (4,4) samples texel (0,0) exactly,
// pixel (12,4) texel (1,0), and pixel (8,4) the exact bilinear
// midpoint of texels (0,0) and (1,0).

func twiddle(x, y, w, h int) int {
	idx, bit := 0, 0
	for i := 0; (1<<i) < w || (1<<i) < h; i++ {
		if (1 << i) < h {
			idx |= ((y >> i) & 1) << bit
			bit++
		}
		if (1 << i) < w {
			idx |= ((x >> i) & 1) << bit
			bit++
		}
	}
	return idx
}

// writeVRAM64 stores img at VRAM backing offset base by writing
// through the 64-bit window, applying the inverse of the bus
// bank interleave: the window presents backing bank 0's words at
// doubled offsets (window word 2k is backing word k, window word
// 2k+1 is bank 1 word k), so a bank 0 word at backing offset o
// is written at window offset 2*o. Fixtures here live in bank 0.
func writeVRAM64(m *Machine, base uint32, img []byte) {
	for i := 0; i+4 <= len(img); i += 4 {
		w := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(img[i:])
		m.Bus.Write32(0x05000000+2*(base+uint32(i)), w)
	}
}

func pvrReg(m *Machine, off uint32, v uint32) { m.Bus.Write32(0x005F8000+off, v) }

func taPacket(m *Machine, words ...uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		var w uint32
		if i < len(words) {
			w = words[i]
		}
		m.Bus.Write32(0x00500000, w)
	}
}

// setupTexturedScene programs the PVR for a 64x64 565 target,
// uploads the 8x8 texture, and submits the quad, but does not
// start the render.
func setupTexturedScene(t *testing.T, m *Machine) {
	t.Helper()
	pvrReg(m, 0x48, 0x3)        // FB_W_CTRL: enable, 565
	pvrReg(m, 0x60, 0)          // FB_W_SOF1 = VRAM 0
	pvrReg(m, 0x44, 0x800003)   // FB_R_CTRL: enable, 565, vclk_div
	pvrReg(m, 0x50, 0)          // FB_R_SOF1 = VRAM 0
	pvrReg(m, 0x5C, 63<<10|31)  // FB_R_SIZE: 64 lines, 32 words per line
	pvrReg(m, 0x68, 63<<16)     // FB_X_CLIP max 63
	pvrReg(m, 0x6C, 63<<16)     // FB_Y_CLIP max 63
	pvrReg(m, 0x98, 0xFF000000) // background: opaque black
	pvrReg(m, 0x9C, 0)          // background depth 0
	pvrReg(m, 0x128, 0x10000)   // TA_ISP_BASE

	// 8x8 texture of 565 texels, twiddled layout.
	texel := func(x, y int) uint16 {
		switch {
		case x == 0 && y == 0:
			return 0xF800 // red
		case x == 1 && y == 0:
			return 0x07E0 // green
		case x == 0 && y == 1:
			return 0x001F // blue
		}
		return 0xFFFF // white
	}
	img := make([]byte, 8*8*2)
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(img[twiddle(x, y, 8, 8)*2:], texel(x, y))
		}
	}
	writeVRAM64(m, 0x1000, img)
	// The upload must read back identically through the linear
	// 32-bit window.
	for i := 0; i < len(img); i += 4 {
		want := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(img[i:])
		if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x04001000 + uint32(i)); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("texture word %d = %#x, want %#x", i/4, got, want)
		}
	}

	pvrReg(m, 0x140, 0) // TA_LIST_INIT
	f32 := math.Float32bits
	hdr := []uint32{
		4 << 29,              // polygon header, opaque list
		1<<6 | 7,             // ISP/TSP: textured, depth always
		1 | 1<<24,            // TSP: bilinear, modulate
		1<<27 | (0x1000 / 8), // TCW: 565 texture at 0x1000
		0xFFFFFFFF, 0, 0, 0,  // base color white
	}
	taPacket(m, hdr...)
	vtx := func(x, y, u, v float32, eos bool) []uint32 {
		pcw := uint32(7 << 29)
		if eos {
			pcw |= 1 << 28
		}
		return []uint32{pcw, f32(x), f32(y), f32(1), f32(u), f32(v), 0xFFFFFFFF, 0}
	}
	taPacket(m, vtx(0.5, 0.5, 0, 0, false)...)
	taPacket(m, vtx(64.5, 0.5, 1, 0, false)...)
	taPacket(m, vtx(0.5, 64.5, 0, 1, false)...)
	taPacket(m, vtx(64.5, 64.5, 1, 1, true)...)
	taPacket(m, 0) // end of list
}

func TestTexturedQuadThroughBus(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.LoadProgram(0x0C000000, []byte{0xFE, 0xAF, 0x09, 0x00}) // spin: BRA -2, NOP
	setupTexturedScene(t, m)
	pvrReg(m, 0x14, 0) // STARTRENDER
	if got := m.PVR.RenderCount(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("RenderCount = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	fb16 := func(x, y int) uint16 {
		return m.Bus.Read16(0x04000000 + uint32((y*64+x)*2))
	}
	checks := []struct {
		x, y int
		want uint16
		what string
	}{
		{4, 4, 0xF800, "texel (0,0) red"},
		{12, 4, 0x07E0, "texel (1,0) green"},
		{8, 4, 0x8400, "bilinear midpoint red/green"},
		{4, 12, 0x001F, "texel (0,1) blue"},
		{60, 60, 0xFFFF, "texel (7,7) white"},
	}
	for _, c := range checks {
		if got := fb16(c.x, c.y); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("fb(%d,%d) = %#04x, want %#04x (%s)", c.x, c.y, got, c.want, c.what)
		}
	}
	// The presented frame carries the quad in its top-left.
	m.RunFrame()
	px := m.Framebuffer()[4*Width+4]
	if px>>16&0xFF < 0xF0 || px>>8&0xFF > 0x10 || px&0xFF > 0x10 {
		t.Errorf("presented pixel (4,4) = %#08x, want red", px)
	}
}

func TestSaveRestoreMidSceneRendersIdentical(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.LoadProgram(0x0C000000, []byte{0xFE, 0xAF, 0x09, 0x00})
	setupTexturedScene(t, m)
	// Snapshot after TA submission, before the render.
	state := m.Serialize()

	pvrReg(m, 0x14, 0) // STARTRENDER on the original
	m.RunFrame()
	wantFB := append([]uint32(nil), m.Framebuffer()...)
	wantState := m.Serialize()

	m2 := New()
	if !m2.Deserialize(state) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize of the mid-scene state failed")
	}
	pvrReg(m2, 0x14, 0)
	m2.RunFrame()
	if got := m2.Framebuffer(); !bytes.Equal(u32s(got), u32s(wantFB)) {
		t.Error("restored machine framebuffer differs")
	}
	if got := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Errorf("restored final state differs (%d vs %d bytes)", len(got), len(wantState))
	}
}

func u32s(v []uint32) []byte {
	b := make([]byte, 4*len(v))
	for i, x := range v {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[4*i:], x)
	}
	return b
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-dreamcast/system/dc3_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// DC-3 whole machine gate: one SH-4 program, one ARM sound
// driver, one Maple poll, one fog scene, running together.
//
// The SH-4 program (house style: hand assembled words plus a
// data page at 0x0C000800) copies the ARM driver image from
// main RAM to AICA RAM, releases the ARM7 by clearing ARMRST,
// builds a two entry Maple DMA table (Get Condition on port 0,
// Device Request on port 1), programs the Holly masks for the
// Maple DMA done event (normal bank bit 12, level 2) and the
// AICA external event (bit 1, level 2), starts the Maple DMA,
// and spins. The interrupt handler at VBR+0x600 counts Maple
// completions in scratch word 0 (acking ISTNRM bit 12) and
// AICA timer interrupts in scratch word 1 (clearing the AICA
// pending bit through MCIRE).
//
// The ARM driver (hand assembled ARM words, a synthetic
// fixture, not firmware) programs slot 0 for a 64 sample
// 16-bit PCM loop at unity pitch, keys it on, and arms timer
// A (TIMA 250, prescaler 1) at level 2. The ARM takes timer
// A as an FIQ (SCIEB bit 6) and end-of-interrupts it in its
// handler, which counts entries in wave RAM at 0x2000. The
// SH-4 side watches timer B instead (MCIEB bits 6 and 7):
// timer B is not in SCIEB, so the ARM never acknowledges it
// and its pending bit survives until the SH-4 handler clears
// it through MCIRE, which is what the SH-4 count measures.
//
// The fog scene is the pvr package gate scene rebuilt through
// the bus: a black 32 by 32 quad at Z 0.5, FOG_DENSITY 0x8802
// (4.25), fog table entries 8 and 9 with low bytes 100 and
// 156, FOG_COL_RAM white. The center pixel must present as
// 0xFF848284, the same value the pvr gate pins.
//
// The gate then saves state mid run, runs one more frame on
// the original and on a restored machine, and requires byte
// identical continuation: state bytes, drained audio, and the
// presented framebuffer.

// armDriverWords is the ARM7 sound driver, loaded at wave RAM
// 0 (the ARM reset entry). Register bases: slot registers at
// 0x00800000, common registers at 0x00802800.
var armDriverWords = []uint32{
	0xEA000006, // 0x00: B start (0x20)
	0x00000000, // 0x04: undefined vector (unused)
	0x00000000, // 0x08: SWI vector (unused)
	0x00000000, // 0x0C: prefetch abort vector (unused)
	0x00000000, // 0x10: data abort vector (unused)
	0x00000000, // 0x14: reserved
	0xEAFFFFFE, // 0x18: IRQ vector: spin (IRQ stays masked)
	0xEA00002C, // 0x1C: FIQ vector: B fiq (0xD4)
	// start:
	0xE59FD0CC, // 0x20: LDR SP, [PC, #0xCC]   ; literal 0xF4 = 0x0007F000
	0xE59F00CC, // 0x24: LDR R0, [PC, #0xCC]   ; literal 0xF8 = 0x00800000
	0xE3A01C42, // 0x28: MOV R1, #0x4200       ; KYONB + LPCTL, PCM16
	0xE5801000, // 0x2C: STR R1, [R0]          ; slot 0 reg 0
	0xE3A01A01, // 0x30: MOV R1, #0x1000
	0xE5801004, // 0x34: STR R1, [R0, #4]      ; SA low = 0x1000
	0xE3A01000, // 0x38: MOV R1, #0
	0xE5801008, // 0x3C: STR R1, [R0, #8]      ; LSA = 0
	0xE3A0103F, // 0x40: MOV R1, #63
	0xE580100C, // 0x44: STR R1, [R0, #0xC]    ; LEA = 63
	0xE59F10AC, // 0x48: LDR R1, [PC, #0xAC]   ; literal 0xFC = 0x3C1F
	0xE5801014, // 0x4C: STR R1, [R0, #0x14]   ; KRS off, DL 0, RR 31
	0xE3A0101F, // 0x50: MOV R1, #0x1F
	0xE5801010, // 0x54: STR R1, [R0, #0x10]   ; AR 31, D1R 0, D2R 0
	0xE3A01000, // 0x58: MOV R1, #0
	0xE5801018, // 0x5C: STR R1, [R0, #0x18]   ; OCT 0, FNS 0
	0xE580101C, // 0x60: STR R1, [R0, #0x1C]   ; LFO off
	0xE5801020, // 0x64: STR R1, [R0, #0x20]   ; ISEL 0, IMXL 0
	0xE3A01C0F, // 0x68: MOV R1, #0xF00
	0xE5801024, // 0x6C: STR R1, [R0, #0x24]   ; DISDL 15, DIPAN 0
	0xE3A01004, // 0x70: MOV R1, #4
	0xE5801028, // 0x74: STR R1, [R0, #0x28]   ; TL 0, Q 4 (pass)
	0xE59F1080, // 0x78: LDR R1, [PC, #0x80]   ; literal 0x100 = 0x1FF8
	0xE580102C, // 0x7C: STR R1, [R0, #0x2C]   ; FLV0
	0xE5801030, // 0x80: STR R1, [R0, #0x30]   ; FLV1
	0xE5801034, // 0x84: STR R1, [R0, #0x34]   ; FLV2
	0xE5801038, // 0x88: STR R1, [R0, #0x38]   ; FLV3
	0xE580103C, // 0x8C: STR R1, [R0, #0x3C]   ; FLV4
	0xE59F206C, // 0x90: LDR R2, [PC, #0x6C]   ; literal 0x104 = 0x00802800
	0xE3A0100F, // 0x94: MOV R1, #0xF
	0xE5821000, // 0x98: STR R1, [R2]          ; MVOL 15
	0xE3A010FA, // 0x9C: MOV R1, #0xFA         ; TACTL 0, TIMA 250
	0xE5821090, // 0xA0: STR R1, [R2, #0x90]   ; timer A control
	0xE3A01040, // 0xA4: MOV R1, #0x40         ; source 6 (timer A)
	0xE582109C, // 0xA8: STR R1, [R2, #0x9C]   ; SCIEB (ARM side)
	0xE3A010C0, // 0xAC: MOV R1, #0xC0         ; sources 6 and 7
	0xE58210B4, // 0xB0: STR R1, [R2, #0xB4]   ; MCIEB (SH-4 side)
	0xE3A01040, // 0xB4: MOV R1, #0x40
	0xE58210AC, // 0xB8: STR R1, [R2, #0xAC]   ; SCILV1: level 2
	0xE10F1000, // 0xBC: MRS R1, CPSR
	0xE3C11040, // 0xC0: BIC R1, R1, #0x40     ; unmask FIQ
	0xE121F001, // 0xC4: MSR CPSR_c, R1
	0xE59F1038, // 0xC8: LDR R1, [PC, #0x38]   ; literal 0x108 = 0xC200
	0xE5801000, // 0xCC: STR R1, [R0]          ; KYONEX: key on
	0xEAFFFFFE, // 0xD0: B .                   ; idle loop
	// fiq:
	0xE59F8030, // 0xD4: LDR R8, [PC, #0x30]   ; literal 0x10C = 0x2000
	0xE5989000, // 0xD8: LDR R9, [R8]
	0xE2899001, // 0xDC: ADD R9, R9, #1
	0xE5889000, // 0xE0: STR R9, [R8]          ; timer IRQ counter++
	0xE59F8024, // 0xE4: LDR R8, [PC, #0x24]   ; literal 0x110 = 0x00802D04
	0xE3A09001, // 0xE8: MOV R9, #1
	0xE5889000, // 0xEC: STR R9, [R8]          ; end of interrupt
	0xE25EF004, // 0xF0: SUBS PC, LR, #4       ; return from FIQ
	// literal pool:
	0x0007F000, // 0xF4: stack top (wave RAM)
	0x00800000, // 0xF8: slot register base
	0x00003C1F, // 0xFC: reg 0x14 value
	0x00001FF8, // 0x100: FLV value
	0x00802800, // 0x104: common register base
	0x0000C200, // 0x108: KYONEX + KYONB + LPCTL
	0x00002000, // 0x10C: counter address (wave RAM)
	0x00802D04, // 0x110: M register (end of interrupt)
}

// dc3ProgramWords is the SH-4 side of the gate. R10 points at
// data page A (0x8C000800, entries 0 to 15) and R9 at data
// page B (0x8C000840, entries 16 to 27) for the whole run:
// the MOV.L @(disp,Rn) displacement field is four bits, so a
// single base register reaches only 16 words. The handler
// relies on both bases surviving.
var dc3ProgramWords = []uint16{
	0xDA01,         // 0x00: MOV.L @(1,PC),R10  ; literal at 0x08
	0xA003,         // 0x02: BRA 0x0C
	0x0009,         // 0x04: NOP (delay slot)
	0x0009,         // 0x06: pad
	0x0800, 0x8C00, // 0x08: .long 0x8C000800
	0x50A0,         // 0x0C: MOV.L @(0,R10),R0   ; SR value
	0x400E,         // 0x0E: LDC R0,SR
	0x50A1,         // 0x10: MOV.L @(1,R10),R0   ; VBR value
	0x402E,         // 0x12: LDC R0,VBR
	0x5FA2,         // 0x14: MOV.L @(2,R10),R15  ; stack top
	0xD916,         // 0x16: MOV.L @(22,PC),R9   ; literal at 0x70: page B
	0x5193,         // 0x18: MOV.L @(3,R9),R1    ; IML2NRM addr
	0x5294,         // 0x1A: MOV.L @(4,R9),R2    ; Maple done bit
	0x2122,         // 0x1C: MOV.L R2,@R1
	0x5195,         // 0x1E: MOV.L @(5,R9),R1    ; IML2EXT addr
	0x5296,         // 0x20: MOV.L @(6,R9),R2    ; AICA bit
	0x2122,         // 0x22: MOV.L R2,@R1
	0x51A3,         // 0x24: MOV.L @(3,R10),R1   ; copy source
	0x52A4,         // 0x26: MOV.L @(4,R10),R2   ; copy destination
	0x53A5,         // 0x28: MOV.L @(5,R10),R3   ; copy count
	0x6014,         // 0x2A: loop: MOV.B @R1+,R0
	0x2200,         // 0x2C: MOV.B R0,@R2 (address field is bits 11:8)
	0x7201,         // 0x2E: ADD #1,R2
	0x4310,         // 0x30: DT R3
	0x8BFA,         // 0x32: BF loop
	0x0009,         // 0x34: NOP (delay slot)
	0x51A6,         // 0x36: MOV.L @(6,R10),R1   ; ARMRST addr
	0xE000,         // 0x38: MOV #0,R0
	0x2102,         // 0x3A: MOV.L R0,@R1        ; release the ARM7
	0x57A7,         // 0x3C: MOV.L @(7,R10),R7   ; Maple table address
	0x50A8,         // 0x3E: MOV.L @(8,R10),R0
	0x1700,         // 0x40: MOV.L R0,@(0,R7)    ; entry 0 header
	0x50A9,         // 0x42: MOV.L @(9,R10),R0
	0x1701,         // 0x44: MOV.L R0,@(1,R7)    ; entry 0 receive buffer
	0x50AA,         // 0x46: MOV.L @(10,R10),R0
	0x1702,         // 0x48: MOV.L R0,@(2,R7)    ; Get Condition frame
	0x50AB,         // 0x4A: MOV.L @(11,R10),R0
	0x1703,         // 0x4C: MOV.L R0,@(3,R7)    ; function word
	0x50AC,         // 0x4E: MOV.L @(12,R10),R0
	0x1704,         // 0x50: MOV.L R0,@(4,R7)    ; entry 1 header (last)
	0x50AD,         // 0x52: MOV.L @(13,R10),R0
	0x1705,         // 0x54: MOV.L R0,@(5,R7)    ; entry 1 receive buffer
	0x50AE,         // 0x56: MOV.L @(14,R10),R0
	0x1706,         // 0x58: MOV.L R0,@(6,R7)    ; Device Request frame
	0x51AF,         // 0x5A: MOV.L @(15,R10),R1  ; SB_MDSTAR addr
	0x5290,         // 0x5C: MOV.L @(0,R9),R2    ; table physical address
	0x2122,         // 0x5E: MOV.L R2,@R1
	0x5191,         // 0x60: MOV.L @(1,R9),R1    ; SB_MDEN addr
	0xE201,         // 0x62: MOV #1,R2
	0x2122,         // 0x64: MOV.L R2,@R1        ; MDEN = 1
	0x5192,         // 0x66: MOV.L @(2,R9),R1    ; SB_MDST addr
	0x2122,         // 0x68: MOV.L R2,@R1        ; MDST = 1: transfer runs
	0xAFFE,         // 0x6A: spin: BRA spin
	0x0009,         // 0x6C: NOP (delay slot)
	0x0009,         // 0x6E: pad
	0x0840, 0x8C00, // 0x70: .long 0x8C000840
}

// dc3HandlerWords sits at image offset 0x1600 (VBR 0x8C001000
// plus 0x600). It counts the two interrupt sources the gate
// arms and acknowledges each at its own controller. Data page
// B entries are reached through R9.
var dc3HandlerWords = []uint16{
