==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/README.md ====================

# go-gameboy: a Nintendo Game Boy core written in Go

Clean-room Game Boy (DMG) and Game Boy Color emulator core for iTaK
Gaming, written in Go and exposed through the libretro API so the iTaK
engine can load it exactly like any other core.

Why this exists: the Gambatte core bundled today is fine license-wise,
but David's standing rule for iTaK Gaming is that every system gets its
own from-scratch Go core, 100 percent our own code (MIT, same as the
rest of iTaK Gaming), written from published hardware documentation:
the Sharp SM83 instruction set documentation as collected in the
Game Boy Pan Docs and the published opcode references, the documented
PPU, timer, DMA, and APU behavior, plus the documented cartridge
header and memory bank controller (MBC) behavior.

Conformance is proven the standard way: Blargg's cpu_instrs test ROMs
(all eleven individual tests plus the combined ROM), Blargg's
dmg_sound suite (all twelve singles), the dmg-acid2 PPU rendering
test (pixel-exact against the reference image), and the mooneye-gb
acceptance suite, run headless against the system package in this
module. The test ROMs are public conformance suites, kept locally
under `testroms/` and never committed to the repository.

## Status

- GB-1 (done): module skeleton, the SM83 CPU (`chips/sm83`),
  cartridge header and MBC0/MBC1/MBC3/MBC5 mapping (`cart`), and the
  Blargg cpu_instrs gate.
- GB-2 (done): the real machine. `system/` is a dot-clocked system in
  the go-genesis shape: `RunFrame` produces the 160x144 framebuffer
  plus interleaved int16 audio at 44100 Hz, `SetButtons` feeds the
  joypad, and `Serialize`/`Deserialize` cover the whole machine.
  - `ppu/`: dot-stepped PPU (456 dots per line, 154 lines, a frame
    is exactly 70224 dots), modes 2/3/0/1 with the mode 3 fetch
    penalties, LY/LYC compare with the stored coincidence flag (the
    comparison clock stops while the LCD is off), STAT interrupt
    sources and blocking, background, window (own line counter),
    and sprites with DMG priority, the 10-per-line limit, and
    mode-based VRAM/OAM access blocking. LCD turn-on has the
    warmup delay before the first OAM scan.
  - Timers: the falling-edge TIMA model with the DIV-write and
    TAC-write glitches, the 4-dot overflow reload delay, and the
    reload-cycle TIMA/TMA write quirks.
  - OAM DMA: 160 bytes, one per M-cycle after a 2 M-cycle
    startup, with the CPU restricted to HRAM while the transfer
    runs, and the queued-restart behavior. (GB-3 made the pacing
    M-cycle based so double speed halves the dot count; see the
    GB-3 notes for the bug that proved it matters.)
  - Joypad matrix with the press-edge interrupt, serial transfers
    on the internal clock (the test capture hook remains), and
    interrupt dispatch with the mid-push cancellation behavior.
  - `sound/`: the full APU, four channels (square with sweep,
    square, wave with its RAM and the DMG access quirks, noise
    LFSR), the 512 Hz frame sequencer, length/sweep/envelope
    clocks with the trigger quirks, NR52 power behavior, NR51
    panning and NR50 volume mixing.
  - Save states are whole-machine and verified with a real
    homebrew game: serialize mid-play, continue, restore, and
    the continuation matches frame for frame and sample for
    sample. (GB-3 changed the framebuffer to XRGB8888 and grew
    the layout; current sizes are in the GB-3 notes.)
  - The CPU gained M-cycle access slots: each bus access is
    preceded by the dots the hardware spends reaching it, which
    is what makes the timer, DMA, PPU, and ie_push timings land
    on the right dot.
- GB-3 (done): Game Boy Color support, the libretro shell, and the
  app wiring that swaps Gambatte for this core (staged, ships with
  the next build).
  - CGB mode is chosen by the cartridge header (flag 0x80 or 0xC0);
    plain DMG cartridges keep the GB-2 machine. The CGB adds:
    BG and OBJ palette RAM (64 bytes each) behind BCPS/OCPS with
    auto-increment and the mode 3 access block, VRAM bank 1 behind
    VBK carrying tile data and the attribute map (palette, bank,
    flips, priority), WRAM banks 2-7 behind SVBK in the D000
    window, double-speed mode (KEY1 arm plus STOP switch), HDMA
    (general-purpose and HBlank modes), the infrared register as a
    documented stub, and the CGB boot register set (A=0x11).
  - Timing model: the frame stays 70224 device dots. An M-cycle
    is 4 device dots at normal speed and 2 in double speed; the
    timer divider advances at CPU rate, the APU frame sequencer
    is clocked from a divider twin that always advances at the
    device rate so music tempo does not change with CPU speed,
    and the serial bit period halves in double speed (the CGB
    fast clock is 16 dots). OAM DMA is M-cycle paced in both
    speeds (one byte per M-cycle after a 2 M-cycle startup); a
    real GBC homebrew caught why this matters: with the DMA
    clocked in raw dots it outlasted the game's HRAM wait loop in
    double speed and the CPU executed open-bus bytes into a reset
    loop.
  - DMG compatibility mode (a DMG cartridge on CGB hardware) is
    modeled as a register lock surface only: KEY1, HDMA, the
    palette data ports, OPRI, SVBK, and FF74 read 0xFF while the
    index registers and FF72/FF73/FF75 keep working, and the boot
    registers are the compatibility set. Compatibility coloring
    of DMG games is out of scope; DMG cartridges in the app run
    on the DMG model, so compatibility mode is exercised by the
    CGB conformance ROMs (which are DMG images written for CGB
    hardware) rather than by shipped games.
  - The framebuffer is XRGB8888 end to end (the four DMG shades
    go through the DMG palette registers into the same format),
    the shell negotiates pixel format 1, 160x144 at 59.7275 fps
    with a 10/9 aspect, audio batch at 44100 Hz, and the memory
    interface exposes cartridge RAM and work RAM banks 0-1.
  - Save states grew to layout version 2 (the CGB blocks join the
    trailer; version 1 states are rejected cleanly). A CGB state
    is 273657 bytes for µCity (a 128 KB RAM cartridge) and a DMG
    state is 150777 bytes for Tobu Tobu Girl.
  - Proofs on the built core through the iTaK bridge: Tobu Tobu
    Girl (DMG) passes the engine test end to end (ALL TESTS
    PASSED). µCity (GBC) loads, renders, plays non-silent audio,
    and round-trips the per-player save manager; its one
    enginetest flag is the restore check, whose premise (screen
    unchanged two frames after the save point) the game's
    blinking menu violates on its own timeline. The stronger
    proof passes exactly: state bytes re-saved after a restore
    are identical (0 of 273657 differ), and restored continuation
    frames and audio match the original continuation hash for
    hash over 300 frames. No commercial ROMs were available
    locally for these proofs; both games are homebrew (see
    `homebrew/SOURCES.md`).

## Conformance notes

Mooneye acceptance: 43 of 75 ROMs report a pass (the rest target
other boot ROMs or models, the GameShark environment, CGB/SGB
behavior, or intra-instruction access order inside instruction
families). The GB-2 gating sets all pass: the timer suite entire,
the OAM DMA suite, the PPU timing and STAT set, and
interrupts/ie_push. One PPU test is excluded from the gate with
its reason recorded in the test: intr_2_mode0_timing_sprites
measures the pixel FIFO's internal fetch phase between sprites at
different X positions, which a line-wise renderer does not
simulate.

CGB conformance (GB-3): cgb-acid2 renders pixel-exact against its
reference image, and the gated mooneye CGB misc ROMs pass
(boot_regs-cgb, bits/unused_hwio-C). Excluded with reasons
recorded in the test: the boot_div-cgb tests and boot_hwio-C
(boot ROM execution state this machine does not model; it models
the documented register hand-off), and ppu/vblank_stat_intr-C
(interrupt latency measured against a mid-frame DIV reset with
one 256-dot period of tolerance, balanced on the boot ROM's
frame phase). The Blargg DMG suites (cpu_instrs 11/11 plus
combined, dmg_sound 12/12) and dmg-acid2 stay green.

## Layout

- `chips/sm83/` the Sharp SM83 CPU (the Game Boy processor), pure Go,
  with exact flag behavior, interrupt dispatch, the EI delay, the HALT
  bug, M-cycle access slots, and full save-state serialization
- `cart/` ROM image parsing: header facts, header checksum, and the
  MBC0, MBC1, MBC3 (with RTC state), and MBC5 memory bank controllers
- `ppu/` the dot-stepped picture processing unit
- `sound/` the audio processing unit and its resampler
- `system/` the assembled machine: bus, timers, DMA, joypad, serial,
  the frame runner, and whole-machine save states, plus the
  conformance harness
- `libretro/` the libretro C ABI shell (c-shared build): 24
  retro_* exports mirroring the go-genesis shell's structure,
  XRGB8888 video, 44100 Hz audio batch, serialize via the system
  state, and the standard joypad bit mapping (A/X to the console
  A, B/Y to the console B)


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/cart/cart.go ====================

// Package cart loads and describes a Game Boy cartridge image.
//
// Written clean-room from the published cartridge header layout. The
// header occupies the bytes at 0x100-0x14F of every Game Boy ROM: an
// entry point and logo, then the title, mapper type, ROM and RAM
// size codes, and checksums.
//
// The package also implements the memory bank controllers the games
// use to page ROM and RAM through the 16-bit address space: MBC0
// (plain ROM), MBC1, MBC3 (with real-time clock state), and MBC5.
// Cartridge RAM contents live in Cart.RAM, which the system owns for
// battery persistence; mapper bank registers and RTC state are kept
// here and serialized with the mapper.
package cart

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// MapperKind selects the bank switching implementation.
type MapperKind int

const (
	MBC0 MapperKind = iota // ROM only, no mapper
	MBC1
	MBC2 // parsed but not implemented in GB-1 (tiny internal RAM)
	MBC3
	MBC5
	MBCUnsupported
)

func (k MapperKind) String() string {
	switch k {
	case MBC0:
		return "MBC0 (ROM only)"
	case MBC1:
		return "MBC1"
	case MBC2:
		return "MBC2"
	case MBC3:
		return "MBC3"
	case MBC5:
		return "MBC5"
	default:
		return "unsupported"
	}
}

// RTC holds the MBC3 real-time clock state: the live counters and
// the latched copies a game reads after a latch pulse. The system
// advances the live counters; the mapper only stores and latches.
type RTC struct {
	Seconds, Minutes, Hours uint8
	DayLow                  uint8 // low 8 bits of the day counter
	DayHigh                 uint8 // bit 0: day bit 8; bit 6: halt; bit 7: day carry
	Latched                 [5]uint8
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed size of the serialized mapper state
// (bank registers, control state, and the RTC block).
const SerializeSize = 32

const serializeVersion = 1

// Cart is a loaded cartridge image plus the facts parsed from its
// header, the mapper state, and the cartridge RAM.
type Cart struct {
	Data []byte // raw ROM image as stored on the cartridge

	Title      string // title (header 0x134), trailing NULs trimmed
	CGBFlag    uint8  // 0x143: 0x80 CGB-enhanced, 0xC0 CGB-only
	SGBFlag    uint8  // 0x146
	TypeCode   uint8  // 0x147: cartridge type byte
	TypeName   string
	Kind       MapperKind
	ROMSize    int   // ROM size in bytes declared by the header
	ROMBanks   int   // number of 16 KB ROM banks
	RAMSize    int   // cartridge RAM size in bytes declared by the header
	HeaderSum  uint8 // header checksum stored at 0x14D
	HeaderOK   bool  // stored checksum matches the computed one
	LogoOK     bool  // boot logo bytes at 0x104 match the known bitmap
	Version    uint8 // 0x14C
	HasBattery bool
	HasTimer   bool // MBC3 with RTC

	RAM []byte // cartridge RAM contents, owned by the system for saves
	RTC RTC    // MBC3 clock state (only meaningful when HasTimer)

	// Mapper registers.
	ramEnabled  bool
	romBankLow  uint8 // MBC1 low 5 bits / MBC3 7 bits / MBC5 low 8 bits
	romBankHigh uint8 // MBC5 bit 8, or MBC1 upper bits register
	ramBank     uint8
	bankingMode uint8 // MBC1: 0 ROM banking, 1 RAM banking
	rtcSelect   int   // MBC3 RAM window: -1 RAM, else RTC register 0..4
	latchPrev   uint8 // MBC3 latch edge detector
}

// headerChecksum computes the Game Boy header checksum: starting
// from zero, subtract each byte from 0x134 to 0x14C and one more.
func headerChecksum(data []byte) uint8 {
	var x uint8
	for i := 0x134; i <= 0x14C; i++ {
		x = x - data[i] - 1
	}
	return x
}

// romSizeBytes maps the header ROM size code to a byte count.
func romSizeBytes(code uint8) (int, error) {
	switch {
	case code <= 8:
		return 32768 << code, nil
	case code == 0x52:
		return 72 * 16384, nil // 1.125 MB, 72 banks
	case code == 0x53:
		return 80 * 16384, nil // 1.25 MB, 80 banks
	case code == 0x54:
		return 96 * 16384, nil // 1.5 MB, 96 banks
	}
	return 0, fmt.Errorf("cart: unknown ROM size code 0x%02X", code)
}

// ramSizeBytes maps the header RAM size code to a byte count.
func ramSizeBytes(code uint8) (int, error) {
	switch code {
	case 0:
		return 0, nil
	case 1:
		return 2048, nil
	case 2:
		return 8192, nil
	case 3:
		return 32768, nil
	case 4:
		return 131072, nil
	case 5:
		return 65536, nil
	}
	return 0, fmt.Errorf("cart: unknown RAM size code 0x%02X", code)
}

// classify maps the cartridge type byte to a mapper kind and the
// battery and timer facts.
func classify(code uint8) (kind MapperKind, name string, battery, timer bool, err error) {
	switch code {
	case 0x00:
		return MBC0, "ROM ONLY", false, false, nil
	case 0x01:
		return MBC1, "MBC1", false, false, nil
	case 0x02:
		return MBC1, "MBC1+RAM", false, false, nil
	case 0x03:
		return MBC1, "MBC1+RAM+BATTERY", true, false, nil
	case 0x05:
		return MBC2, "MBC2", false, false, nil
	case 0x06:
		return MBC2, "MBC2+BATTERY", true, false, nil
	case 0x08:
		return MBC0, "ROM+RAM", false, false, nil
	case 0x09:
		return MBC0, "ROM+RAM+BATTERY", true, false, nil
	case 0x0F:
		return MBC3, "MBC3+TIMER+BATTERY", true, true, nil
	case 0x10:
		return MBC3, "MBC3+TIMER+RAM+BATTERY", true, true, nil
	case 0x11:
		return MBC3, "MBC3", false, false, nil
	case 0x12:
		return MBC3, "MBC3+RAM", false, false, nil
	case 0x13:
		return MBC3, "MBC3+RAM+BATTERY", true, false, nil
	case 0x19:
		return MBC5, "MBC5", false, false, nil
	case 0x1A:
		return MBC5, "MBC5+RAM", false, false, nil
	case 0x1B:
		return MBC5, "MBC5+RAM+BATTERY", true, false, nil
	case 0x1C:
		return MBC5, "MBC5+RUMBLE", false, false, nil
	case 0x1D:
		return MBC5, "MBC5+RUMBLE+RAM", false, false, nil
	case 0x1E:
		return MBC5, "MBC5+RUMBLE+RAM+BATTERY", true, false, nil
	}
	return MBCUnsupported, fmt.Sprintf("type 0x%02X", code), false, false,
		fmt.Errorf("cart: unsupported cartridge type 0x%02X", code)
}

// bootLogo is the 48-byte bitmap the boot ROM compares against
// 0x104-0x133, reproduced from the published header specification.
var bootLogo = [48]byte{
	0xCE, 0xED, 0x66, 0x66, 0xCC, 0x0D, 0x00, 0x0B, 0x03, 0x73, 0x00, 0x83,
	0x00, 0x0C, 0x00, 0x0D, 0x00, 0x08, 0x11, 0x1F, 0x88, 0x89, 0x00, 0x0E,
	0xDC, 0xCC, 0x6E, 0xE6, 0xDD, 0xDD, 0xD9, 0x99, 0xBB, 0xBB, 0x67, 0x63,
	0x6E, 0x0E, 0xEC, 0xCC, 0xDD, 0xDC, 0x99, 0x9F, 0xBB, 0xB9, 0x33, 0x3E,
}

// Load parses a ROM image. data is the whole file contents. Errors
// are header problems only: a truncated image, a bad size code, or
// an unsupported mapper type. A wrong header checksum or logo is
// reported through HeaderOK and LogoOK, not as an error, so test
// and homebrew images still load.
func Load(data []byte) (*Cart, error) {
	if len(data) < 0x150 {
		return nil, errors.New("cart: image too small to hold a Game Boy header")
	}
	c := &Cart{Data: data, rtcSelect: -1}
	title := data[0x134:0x144]
	if i := strings.IndexByte(string(title), 0); i >= 0 {
		title = title[:i]
	}
	c.Title = strings.TrimRight(string(title), " ")
	c.CGBFlag = data[0x143]
	c.SGBFlag = data[0x146]
	c.TypeCode = data[0x147]
	c.Version = data[0x14C]

	kind, name, battery, timer, err := classify(c.TypeCode)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c.Kind, c.TypeName = kind, name
	c.HasBattery, c.HasTimer = battery, timer
	// The MBC1 and MBC3 ROM bank registers can never hold zero (a
	// zero write selects bank one), so the register powers on as 1.
	// MBC5 has no such fixup and legitimately starts on bank 0.
	if kind == MBC1 || kind == MBC3 {
		c.romBankLow = 1
	}

	romSize, err := romSizeBytes(data[0x148])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c.ROMSize = romSize
	c.ROMBanks = len(data) / 16384
	if c.ROMBanks < 2 {
		c.ROMBanks = 2 // smallest real cartridge: 32 KB fixed
	}
	ramSize, err := ramSizeBytes(data[0x149])
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c.RAMSize = ramSize
	// MBC2 carries 512 half-bytes of internal RAM regardless of the
	// size code; it is parsed here but not mapped in GB-1.
	if kind == MBC2 {
		c.RAMSize = 512
	}
	c.RAM = make([]byte, c.RAMSize)

	c.HeaderSum = data[0x14D]
	c.HeaderOK = c.HeaderSum == headerChecksum(data)
	c.LogoOK = true
	for i, b := range bootLogo {
		if data[0x104+i] != b {
			c.LogoOK = false
			break
		}
	}
	return c, nil
}

// romByte reads the ROM image at a bank-relative address, wrapping
// out-of-range banks the way masked address lines would.
func (c *Cart) romByte(bank int, offset uint16) uint8 {
	bank %= c.ROMBanks
	addr := bank*16384 + int(offset)
	if addr < 0 || addr >= len(c.Data) {
		return 0xFF
	}
	return c.Data[addr]
}

// ReadROM serves the 0x0000-0x7FFF ROM window for the active mapper.
func (c *Cart) ReadROM(addr uint16) uint8 {
	switch c.Kind {
	case MBC1:
		if addr < 0x4000 {
			bank := 0
			if c.bankingMode == 1 {
				bank = int(c.romBankHigh) << 5
			}
			return c.romByte(bank, addr)
		}
		bank := int(c.romBankLow) | int(c.romBankHigh)<<5
		return c.romByte(bank, addr-0x4000)
	case MBC3:
		if addr < 0x4000 {
			return c.romByte(0, addr)
		}
		return c.romByte(int(c.romBankLow), addr-0x4000)
	case MBC5:
		if addr < 0x4000 {
			return c.romByte(0, addr)
		}
		bank := int(c.romBankLow) | int(c.romBankHigh)<<8
		return c.romByte(bank, addr-0x4000)
	default: // MBC0 and anything unimplemented read as flat ROM
		return c.romByte(0, addr)
	}
}

// ReadRAM serves the 0xA000-0xBFFF cartridge RAM window. A disabled
// or absent RAM reads as 0xFF, as open bus does on the hardware.
func (c *Cart) ReadRAM(addr uint16) uint8 {
	if !c.ramEnabled || len(c.RAM) == 0 {
		if c.Kind == MBC3 && c.rtcSelect >= 0 && c.ramEnabled {
			return c.RTC.Latched[c.rtcSelect]
		}
		return 0xFF
	}
	offset := int(addr - 0xA000)
	switch c.Kind {
	case MBC1:
		bank := 0
		if c.bankingMode == 1 {
			bank = int(c.ramBank)
		}
		return c.ramByte(bank*8192 + offset)
	case MBC3:
		if c.rtcSelect >= 0 {
			return c.RTC.Latched[c.rtcSelect]
		}
		return c.ramByte(int(c.ramBank)*8192 + offset)
	case MBC5:
		return c.ramByte(int(c.ramBank&0x0F)*8192 + offset)
	default:
		return c.ramByte(offset)
	}
}

func (c *Cart) ramByte(addr int) uint8 {
	if addr < 0 || addr >= len(c.RAM) {
		return 0xFF
	}
	return c.RAM[addr]
}

// Write handles writes to the cartridge address space: mapper
// control registers below 0x8000 and the RAM window above 0xA000.
func (c *Cart) Write(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if addr >= 0xA000 && addr <= 0xBFFF {
		c.writeRAM(addr, val)
		return
	}
	switch c.Kind {
	case MBC1:
		switch {
		case addr < 0x2000:
			c.ramEnabled = val&0x0F == 0x0A
		case addr < 0x4000:
			c.romBankLow = val & 0x1F
			if c.romBankLow == 0 {
				c.romBankLow = 1 // bank zero is not selectable here
			}
		case addr < 0x6000:
			c.romBankHigh = val & 0x03
			c.ramBank = val & 0x03
		default:
			c.bankingMode = val & 1
		}
	case MBC3:
		switch {
		case addr < 0x2000:
			c.ramEnabled = val&0x0F == 0x0A
		case addr < 0x4000:
			c.romBankLow = val & 0x7F
			if c.romBankLow == 0 {
				c.romBankLow = 1
			}
		case addr < 0x6000:
			c.writeMBC3Select(val)
		default:
			if c.latchPrev == 0 && val == 1 {
				c.latchRTC()
			}
			c.latchPrev = val
		}
	case MBC5:
		switch {
		case addr < 0x2000:
			c.ramEnabled = val&0x0F == 0x0A
		case addr < 0x3000:
			c.romBankLow = val
		case addr < 0x4000:
			c.romBankHigh = val & 1
		case addr < 0x6000:
			c.ramBank = val & 0x0F
		}
	}
}

// writeMBC3Select handles the MBC3 RAM bank and RTC register select
// range: values 0x00-0x03 pick a RAM bank, 0x08-0x0C pick an RTC
// register for the RAM window.
func (c *Cart) writeMBC3Select(val uint8) {
	switch {
	case val <= 0x03:
		c.ramBank = val
		c.rtcSelect = -1
	case val >= 0x08 && val <= 0x0C:
		c.rtcSelect = int(val - 0x08)
	}
}

// latchRTC copies the live RTC counters into the latched set.
func (c *Cart) latchRTC() {
	c.RTC.Latched = [5]uint8{
		c.RTC.Seconds, c.RTC.Minutes, c.RTC.Hours, c.RTC.DayLow, c.RTC.DayHigh,
	}
}

func (c *Cart) writeRAM(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if !c.ramEnabled {
		return
	}
	offset := int(addr - 0xA000)
	switch c.Kind {
	case MBC3:
		if c.rtcSelect >= 0 {
			c.writeRTCReg(c.rtcSelect, val)
			return
		}
		c.storeRAM(int(c.ramBank)*8192+offset, val)
	case MBC1:
		bank := 0
		if c.bankingMode == 1 {
			bank = int(c.ramBank)
		}
		c.storeRAM(bank*8192+offset, val)
	case MBC5:
		c.storeRAM(int(c.ramBank&0x0F)*8192+offset, val)
	default:
		c.storeRAM(offset, val)
	}
}

func (c *Cart) storeRAM(addr int, val uint8) {
	if addr >= 0 && addr < len(c.RAM) {
		c.RAM[addr] = val
	}
}

// writeRTCReg writes one live RTC register by its latched index:
// 0 seconds, 1 minutes, 2 hours, 3 day low, 4 day high.
func (c *Cart) writeRTCReg(i int, val uint8) {
	switch i {
	case 0:
		c.RTC.Seconds = val
	case 1:
		c.RTC.Minutes = val
	case 2:
		c.RTC.Hours = val
	case 3:
		c.RTC.DayLow = val
	case 4:
		c.RTC.DayHigh = val
	}
}

// Serialize writes the mapper register and RTC state into buf, which
// must be at least SerializeSize bytes long. RAM contents are not
// included; the system saves those with the battery file.
func (c *Cart) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("cart: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	for i := 0; i < SerializeSize; i++ {
		buf[i] = 0
	}
	buf[0] = serializeVersion
	if c.ramEnabled {
		buf[1] = 1
	}
	buf[2] = c.romBankLow
	buf[3] = c.romBankHigh
	buf[4] = c.ramBank
	buf[5] = c.bankingMode
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[6:], int16ToU16(c.rtcSelect))
	buf[8] = c.latchPrev
	r := &c.RTC
	buf[9] = r.Seconds
	buf[10] = r.Minutes
	buf[11] = r.Hours
	buf[12] = r.DayLow
	buf[13] = r.DayHigh
	copy(buf[14:19], r.Latched[:])
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *Cart) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("cart: deserialize buffer too small")
	}
	if buf[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("cart: unsupported serialize version")
	}
	c.ramEnabled = buf[1] != 0
	c.romBankLow = buf[2]
	c.romBankHigh = buf[3]
	c.ramBank = buf[4]
	c.bankingMode = buf[5]
	c.rtcSelect = int(int16(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[6:])))
	c.latchPrev = buf[8]
	r := &c.RTC
	r.Seconds, r.Minutes, r.Hours = buf[9], buf[10], buf[11]
	r.DayLow, r.DayHigh = buf[12], buf[13]
	copy(r.Latched[:], buf[14:19])
	return nil
}

func int16ToU16(v int) uint16 { return uint16(int16(v)) }


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/cart/cart_test.go ====================

package cart

import "testing"

// makeROM builds a synthetic ROM image of the given size with a
// valid header for the given type and size codes. bankFill, when
// non-nil, fills each 16 KB bank with its bank index plus bankFill.
func makeROM(t *testing.T, size int, typeCode, romCode, ramCode uint8, fillBanks bool) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	data := make([]byte, size)
	if fillBanks {
		for b := 0; b < size/16384; b++ {
			for i := 0; i < 16384; i++ {
				data[b*16384+i] = uint8(b)
			}
		}
	}
	copy(data[0x104:0x134], bootLogo[:])
	title := "TESTCART"
	copy(data[0x134:], title)
	data[0x147] = typeCode
	data[0x148] = romCode
	data[0x149] = ramCode
	data[0x14D] = headerChecksum(data)
	return data
}

func TestLoadHeaderFacts(t *testing.T) {
	data := makeROM(t, 32768, 0x1B, 0, 3, false)
	c, err := Load(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if c.Title != "TESTCART" {
		t.Fatalf("Title = %q, want TESTCART", c.Title)
	}
	if c.Kind != MBC5 || !c.HasBattery {
		t.Fatalf("Kind = %v battery=%v, want MBC5 with battery", c.Kind, c.HasBattery)
	}
	if c.ROMBanks != 2 || c.RAMSize != 32768 {
		t.Fatalf("ROMBanks=%d RAMSize=%d, want 2 and 32768", c.ROMBanks, c.RAMSize)
	}
	if !c.HeaderOK || !c.LogoOK {
		t.Fatalf("HeaderOK=%v LogoOK=%v, want both true", c.HeaderOK, c.LogoOK)
	}
}

func TestLoadRejectsGarbage(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := Load(make([]byte, 100)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("tiny image accepted")
	}
	bad := makeROM(t, 32768, 0x00, 0, 0, false)
	bad[0x147] = 0x77
	if _, err := Load(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("unsupported mapper accepted")
	}
}

func TestMBC1BankSwitching(t *testing.T) {
	data := makeROM(t, 8*16384, 0x03, 2, 2, true)
	c, err := Load(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x4000); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("power-on switchable bank reads bank %d, want 1", got)
	}
	c.Write(0x2000, 2)
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x4000); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("after bank write switchable bank = %d, want 2", got)
	}
	// Bank zero written to the selector acts as bank one.
	c.Write(0x2000, 0)
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x4000); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("bank zero write selected bank %d, want 1", got)
	}
	// Upper bits join in for big ROMs: mode 0, upper=1, low=2 gives
	// bank 0x22 masked over 8 banks = bank 2... use a 64-bank image
	// instead for a clean check.
	data = makeROM(t, 64*16384, 0x03, 5, 3, true)
	c, _ = Load(data)
	c.Write(0x2000, 2)
	c.Write(0x4000, 1)
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x4000); got != 0x22 {
		t.Fatalf("upper bits: switchable bank = %d, want 34 (0x22)", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x0000); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mode 0 fixed bank = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	c.Write(0x6000, 1) // RAM banking mode: fixed region takes upper bits
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x0000); got != 0x20 {
		t.Fatalf("mode 1 fixed bank = %d, want 32 (0x20)", got)
	}
}

func TestMBC1RAMGatingAndBanking(t *testing.T) {
	data := makeROM(t, 32768, 0x03, 0, 3, false) // 32 KB RAM, 4 banks
	c, _ := Load(data)
	c.Write(0xA000, 0x55)
	if got := c.ReadRAM(0xA000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("RAM read while disabled = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	c.Write(0x0000, 0x0A)
	c.Write(0xA000, 0x55)
	if got := c.ReadRAM(0xA000); got != 0x55 {
		t.Fatalf("RAM read = 0x%02X, want 0x55", got)
	}
	// RAM banking needs mode 1 before the bank register counts.
	c.Write(0x6000, 1)
	c.Write(0x4000, 2)
	c.Write(0xA000, 0x77)
	c.Write(0x4000, 0)
	if got := c.ReadRAM(0xA000); got != 0x55 {
		t.Fatalf("bank 0 RAM = 0x%02X, want 0x55", got)
	}
	c.Write(0x4000, 2)
	if got := c.ReadRAM(0xA000); got != 0x77 {
		t.Fatalf("bank 2 RAM = 0x%02X, want 0x77", got)
	}
}

func TestMBC3RTCSelectAndLatch(t *testing.T) {
	data := makeROM(t, 32768, 0x10, 0, 3, false) // MBC3+TIMER+RAM+BATTERY
	c, err := Load(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !c.HasTimer {
		t.Fatal("HasTimer false for type 0x10")
	}
	c.Write(0x0000, 0x0A) // enable RAM and RTC access
	c.RTC.Seconds = 0x42
	c.RTC.DayHigh = 0xC0
	c.Write(0x4000, 0x08) // select RTC seconds
	// Before a latch pulse the latched copy is stale.
	if got := c.ReadRAM(0xA000); got != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("latched seconds before latch = 0x%02X, want 0x00", got)
	}
	c.Write(0x6000, 0x00)
	c.Write(0x6000, 0x01) // latch pulse
	if got := c.ReadRAM(0xA000); got != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("latched seconds = 0x%02X, want 0x42", got)
	}
	// Writing through the window updates the live register.
	c.Write(0xA000, 0x17)
	if c.RTC.Seconds != 0x17 {
		t.Fatalf("RTC.Seconds = 0x%02X, want 0x17", c.RTC.Seconds)
	}
}

func TestMBC5NineBitBankAndBankZero(t *testing.T) {
	data := makeROM(t, 256*16384, 0x1B, 8, 3, true)
	c, err := Load(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// MBC5 allows bank zero in the switchable window (no fixup).
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x4000); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("power-on switchable bank = %d, want 0 on MBC5", got)
	}
	c.Write(0x2000, 0x23)
	c.Write(0x3000, 0x01) // bank bit 8: bank 0x123, masked to 256 banks
	if got := c.ReadROM(0x4000); got != 0x23 {
		t.Fatalf("switchable bank content = %d, want 0x23 (bank 0x123 mod 256)", got)
	}
}

func TestCartSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	data := makeROM(t, 32768, 0x10, 0, 3, false)
	c, _ := Load(data)
	c.Write(0x0000, 0x0A)
	c.Write(0x2000, 5)
	c.RTC.Minutes = 0x33
	buf := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := c.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c2, _ := Load(data)
	if err := c2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if c2.romBankLow != 5 || !c2.ramEnabled || c2.RTC.Minutes != 0x33 {
		t.Fatalf("round trip mismatch: bank=%d enabled=%v minutes=0x%02X",
			c2.romBankLow, c2.ramEnabled, c2.RTC.Minutes)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/chips/sm83/cb.go ====================

package sm83

// executeCB runs one CB-prefixed instruction. The opcode splits into
// x (bits 7-6: operation class), y (bits 5-3: operation or bit
// index), and z (bits 2-0: operand register, 6 means (HL)).
//
// Cycles: register operands cost 2 M-cycles, (HL) operands cost 4,
// except BIT with (HL) which costs 3 because it only reads.
func (c *CPU) executeCB(bus Bus, op uint8) int {
	x := op >> 6
	y := int(op>>3) & 7
	z := int(op) & 7

	switch x {
	case 0: // rotates and shifts
		v := c.getR(bus, z)
		res, cy := c.cbShift(y, v)
		c.setR(bus, z, res)
		c.setFlags(res == 0, false, false, cy)
		if z == 6 {
			return 4
		}
		return 2
	case 1: // BIT: Z reports the bit is zero, N clears, H sets,
		// C is preserved (handled by not touching it below).
		v := c.getR(bus, z)
		cy := c.f&flagC != 0
		c.setFlags(v>>uint(y)&1 == 0, false, true, cy)
		if z == 6 {
			return 3
		}
		return 2
	case 2: // RES: no flags change
		c.setR(bus, z, c.getR(bus, z)&^(1<<uint(y)))
		if z == 6 {
			return 4
		}
		return 2
	default: // SET: no flags change
		c.setR(bus, z, c.getR(bus, z)|(1<<uint(y)))
		if z == 6 {
			return 4
		}
		return 2
	}
}

// cbShift performs the eight CB rotate and shift operations selected
// by y: 0 RLC, 1 RRC, 2 RL, 3 RR, 4 SLA, 5 SRA, 6 SWAP, 7 SRL.
// It returns the result and the bit that lands in the carry flag;
// SWAP reports no carry.
func (c *CPU) cbShift(y int, v uint8) (uint8, bool) {
	oldC := uint8(0)
	if c.f&flagC != 0 {
		oldC = 1
	}
	switch y {
	case 0: // RLC
		return v<<1 | v>>7, v>>7 != 0
	case 1: // RRC
		return v>>1 | v<<7, v&1 != 0
	case 2: // RL: through carry
		return v<<1 | oldC, v>>7 != 0
	case 3: // RR: through carry
		return v>>1 | oldC<<7, v&1 != 0
	case 4: // SLA
		return v << 1, v>>7 != 0
	case 5: // SRA: sign bit preserved
		return v>>1 | v&0x80, v&1 != 0
	case 6: // SWAP nibbles
		return v<<4 | v>>4, false
	default: // SRL
		return v >> 1, v&1 != 0
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/chips/sm83/exec.go ====================

package sm83

// execute fetches and runs one instruction and returns its length in
// M-cycles. Branch instructions return the taken or not-taken cost as
// documented. The eleven unused opcodes (D3, DB, DD, E3, E4, EB, EC,
// ED, F4, FC, FD) jam the real hardware; here they execute as a
// one-cycle NOP so a stray jump cannot wedge the test rig. No
// conformance ROM executes them deliberately.
func (c *CPU) execute(bus Bus) int {
	op := c.fetchOp(bus)

	// LD r, r' block, with HALT at 0x76.
	if op >= 0x40 && op <= 0x7F {
		if op == 0x76 {
			return c.execHalt(bus)
		}
		dst := int(op>>3) & 7
		src := int(op) & 7
		c.setR(bus, dst, c.getR(bus, src))
		if dst == 6 || src == 6 {
			return 2
		}
		return 1
	}
	// ALU A, r block.
	if op >= 0x80 && op <= 0xBF {
		idx := int(op>>3) & 7
		src := int(op) & 7
		c.alu(idx, c.getR(bus, src))
		if src == 6 {
			return 2
		}
		return 1
	}

	switch {
	case op&0xC7 == 0x04: // INC r
		i := int(op>>3) & 7
		c.setR(bus, i, c.inc8(c.getR(bus, i)))
		if i == 6 {
			return 3
		}
		return 1
	case op&0xC7 == 0x05: // DEC r
		i := int(op>>3) & 7
		c.setR(bus, i, c.dec8(c.getR(bus, i)))
		if i == 6 {
			return 3
		}
		return 1
	case op&0xC7 == 0x06: // LD r, d8
		i := int(op>>3) & 7
		c.setR(bus, i, c.fetch8(bus))
		if i == 6 {
			return 3
		}
		return 2
	case op&0xCF == 0x01: // LD rp, d16
		c.setRP(int(op>>4)&3, c.fetch16(bus))
		return 3
	case op&0xCF == 0x03: // INC rp
		i := int(op>>4) & 3
		c.setRP(i, c.getRP(i)+1)
		return 2
	case op&0xCF == 0x0B: // DEC rp
		i := int(op>>4) & 3
		c.setRP(i, c.getRP(i)-1)
		return 2
	case op&0xCF == 0x09: // ADD HL, rp
		c.addHL(c.getRP(int(op>>4) & 3))
		return 2
	case op&0xE7 == 0x20: // JR cc, r8
		e := int8(c.fetch8(bus))
		if c.cond(int(op>>3) & 3) {
			c.pc = uint16(int32(int16(c.pc)) + int32(e))
			return 3
		}
		return 2
	case op&0xE7 == 0xC0: // RET cc (bit 5 is part of the pattern:
		// without it the LDH and ADD SP opcodes alias here)
		if c.cond(int(op>>3) & 3) {
			c.pc = c.pop16(bus)
			return 5
		}
		return 2
	case op&0xE7 == 0xC2: // JP cc, a16
		addr := c.fetch16(bus)
		if c.cond(int(op>>3) & 3) {
			c.pc = addr
			return 4
		}
		return 3
	case op&0xE7 == 0xC4: // CALL cc, a16
		addr := c.fetch16(bus)
		if c.cond(int(op>>3) & 3) {
			c.push16(bus, c.pc)
			c.pc = addr
			return 6
		}
		return 3
	case op&0xCF == 0xC1: // POP rp2
		c.setRP2(int(op>>4)&3, c.pop16(bus))
		return 3
	case op&0xCF == 0xC5: // PUSH rp2
		c.push16(bus, c.getRP2(int(op>>4)&3))
		return 4
	case op&0xC7 == 0xC6: // ALU A, d8
		c.alu(int(op>>3)&7, c.fetch8(bus))
		return 2
	case op&0xC7 == 0xC7: // RST vec
		c.push16(bus, c.pc)
		c.pc = uint16(op & 0x38)
		return 4
	}

	switch op {
	case 0x00: // NOP
		return 1
	case 0x02: // LD (BC), A
		c.wr(bus, c.bc(), c.a)
		return 2
	case 0x0A: // LD A, (BC)
		c.a = c.rd(bus, c.bc())
		return 2
	case 0x12: // LD (DE), A
		c.wr(bus, c.de(), c.a)
		return 2
	case 0x1A: // LD A, (DE)
		c.a = c.rd(bus, c.de())
		return 2
	case 0x08: // LD (a16), SP
		addr := c.fetch16(bus)
		c.wr(bus, addr, uint8(c.sp))
		c.wr(bus, addr+1, uint8(c.sp>>8))
		return 5
	case 0x07: // RLCA: zero flag always clears on the SM83 rotates
		cy := c.a >> 7
		c.a = c.a<<1 | cy
		c.setFlags(false, false, false, cy != 0)
		return 1
	case 0x0F: // RRCA
		cy := c.a & 1
		c.a = c.a>>1 | cy<<7
		c.setFlags(false, false, false, cy != 0)
		return 1
	case 0x17: // RLA
		var in uint8
		if c.f&flagC != 0 {
			in = 1
		}
		cy := c.a >> 7
		c.a = c.a<<1 | in
		c.setFlags(false, false, false, cy != 0)
		return 1
	case 0x1F: // RRA
		var in uint8
		if c.f&flagC != 0 {
			in = 0x80
		}
		cy := c.a & 1
		c.a = c.a>>1 | in
		c.setFlags(false, false, false, cy != 0)
		return 1
	case 0x10: // STOP: two-byte instruction. The hardware checks the
		// joypad wake condition before stopping: if any input line
		// already reads low (a button is pressed), STOP is skipped
		// and execution continues. Otherwise the CPU enters the
		// stopped state and Step idles until the machine wakes it.
		// This matters in practice: cartridge code that probes for
		// a CGB speed switch on plain DMG hardware reaches STOP
		// with the joypad lines in the pressed state.
		c.fetch8(bus) // padding byte
		if c.OnStopSwitch != nil && c.OnStopSwitch() {
			// CGB speed switch: KEY1 was armed, the machine
			// toggled speed, no stop happens.
			return 1
		}
		if c.rd(bus, 0xFF00)&0x0F == 0x0F {
			c.stopped = true
		}
		return 1
	case 0x18: // JR r8
		e := int8(c.fetch8(bus))
		c.pc = uint16(int32(int16(c.pc)) + int32(e))
		return 3
	case 0x22: // LD (HL+), A
		c.wr(bus, c.hl(), c.a)
		c.setHL(c.hl() + 1)
		return 2
	case 0x2A: // LD A, (HL+)
		c.a = c.rd(bus, c.hl())
		c.setHL(c.hl() + 1)
		return 2
	case 0x32: // LD (HL-), A
		c.wr(bus, c.hl(), c.a)
		c.setHL(c.hl() - 1)
		return 2
	case 0x3A: // LD A, (HL-)
		c.a = c.rd(bus, c.hl())
		c.setHL(c.hl() - 1)
		return 2
	case 0x27: // DAA
		c.daa()
		return 1
	case 0x2F: // CPL
		c.a = ^c.a
		c.f = (c.f & (flagZ | flagC)) | flagN | flagH
		return 1
	case 0x37: // SCF
		c.f = (c.f & flagZ) | flagC
		return 1
	case 0x3F: // CCF
		var cy uint8
		if c.f&flagC == 0 {
			cy = flagC
		}
		c.f = (c.f & flagZ) | cy
		return 1
	case 0xC3: // JP a16
		c.pc = c.fetch16(bus)
		return 4
	case 0xC9: // RET
		c.pc = c.pop16(bus)
		return 4
	case 0xCB: // CB prefix
		return c.executeCB(bus, c.fetch8(bus))
	case 0xCD: // CALL a16
		addr := c.fetch16(bus)
		c.push16(bus, c.pc)
		c.pc = addr
		return 6
	case 0xD9: // RETI: interrupts enable immediately, unlike EI
		c.pc = c.pop16(bus)
		c.ime = true
		c.eiDelay = 0
		return 4
	case 0xE0: // LDH (a8), A
		c.wr(bus, 0xFF00+uint16(c.fetch8(bus)), c.a)
		return 3
	case 0xE2: // LD (C), A
		c.wr(bus, 0xFF00+uint16(c.c), c.a)
		return 2
	case 0xE8: // ADD SP, r8
		c.sp = c.addSPe8(c.fetch8(bus))
		return 4
	case 0xE9: // JP (HL)
		c.pc = c.hl()
		return 1
	case 0xEA: // LD (a16), A
		c.wr(bus, c.fetch16(bus), c.a)
		return 4
	case 0xF0: // LDH A, (a8)
		c.a = c.rd(bus, 0xFF00+uint16(c.fetch8(bus)))
		return 3
	case 0xF2: // LD A, (C)
		c.a = c.rd(bus, 0xFF00+uint16(c.c))
		return 2
	case 0xF3: // DI
		c.ime = false
		c.eiDelay = 0
		return 1
	case 0xF8: // LD HL, SP+r8
		c.setHL(c.addSPe8(c.fetch8(bus)))
		return 3
	case 0xF9: // LD SP, HL
		c.sp = c.hl()
		return 2
	case 0xFA: // LD A, (a16)
		c.a = c.rd(bus, c.fetch16(bus))
		return 4
	case 0xFB: // EI: IME takes effect after the next instruction.
		// The enable is scheduled once: a second EI executed while
		// an enable is already pending does not postpone it (the
		// mooneye ei_sequence test pins this down: in a run of EIs,
		// the interrupt lands after the second one).
		if c.eiDelay == 0 {
			c.eiDelay = 2
		}
		return 1
	}
	// Unused opcodes: D3, DB, DD, E3, E4, EB, EC, ED, F4, FC, FD.
	return 1
}

// execHalt runs the HALT instruction. With an interrupt pending and
// IME clear the CPU does not halt; instead the HALT bug arms, and the
// next opcode fetch leaves PC in place so the following byte is read
// twice. With nothing pending the CPU halts until a request arrives.
func (c *CPU) execHalt(bus Bus) int {
	if c.pendingInterrupts(bus) != 0 && !c.ime {
		c.haltBug = true
		return 1
	}
	c.halted = true
	return 1
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/chips/sm83/sm83.go ====================

// Package sm83 is an original implementation of the Sharp SM83 CPU,
// the processor inside the Game Boy, written from the published
// instruction set documentation (the opcode and flag tables collected
// in the Game Boy Pan Docs and the published SM83 opcode references).
//
// The implementation is a straightforward fetch, decode, execute core:
// one Step runs exactly one instruction, one interrupt dispatch, or
// one idle M-cycle while halted or stopped, and returns the number of
// M-cycles consumed (1 M-cycle is 4 T-cycles at the Game Boy's base
// clock). Documented hardware quirks are modeled deliberately: the
// flags register's low nibble is hardwired to zero, EI enables
// interrupts only after the following instruction completes, RETI
// enables them immediately, the HALT bug makes the instruction after
// HALT fetch its opcode byte twice when an interrupt is pending with
// IME clear, and the accumulator rotates (RLCA, RRCA, RLA, RRA)
// always clear the zero flag even when the result is zero.
package sm83

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Bus is the machine interface the CPU drives. Opcode fetches and data
// accesses both go through Read; the CPU does not distinguish them.
type Bus interface {
	Read(addr uint16) uint8
	Write(addr uint16, val uint8)
}

// Flag bit positions inside the F register. The low nibble of F is
// not stored anywhere in the hardware and always reads as zero.
const (
	flagZ = 0x80 // zero
	flagN = 0x40 // subtract (last ALU op was a subtraction)
	flagH = 0x20 // half carry
	flagC = 0x10 // carry
)

// Interrupt enable and interrupt flag register addresses.
const (
	addrIE = 0xFFFF
	addrIF = 0xFF0F
)

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size in bytes.
const SerializeSize = 26

const serializeVersion = 1

// Registers is a snapshot of the programmer-visible CPU state.
type Registers struct {
	A, F, B, C, D, E, H, L uint8
	SP, PC                 uint16
}

// CPU is a single SM83 instance.
type CPU struct {
	a, f, b, c, d, e, h, l uint8
	sp, pc                 uint16

	ime     bool // master interrupt enable
	eiDelay int  // instructions remaining before a pending EI takes effect
	halted  bool
	haltBug bool // next opcode fetch does not advance PC
	stopped bool

	cycles uint64 // total M-cycles executed since reset

	// OnCycle, when set by the machine, is called as each M-cycle
	// boundary inside a step passes, just before the bus access
	// that starts the new cycle. It lets the machine advance its
	// devices so every access lands on its hardware cycle instead
	// of the step's first cycle.
	OnCycle func()

	// OnStopSwitch, when set by a CGB machine, is consulted when
	// STOP executes: if it returns true, the STOP was a speed
	// switch request with KEY1 armed, the machine has toggled its
	// clock speed, and the CPU does not enter the stopped state.
	// When it returns false (or is unset), STOP behaves as on the
	// DMG: the joypad wake-condition check decides.
	OnStopSwitch func() bool

	slots int // M-cycle slots consumed so far in the current step
}

// New returns a CPU in its power-on state: registers zero, PC zero,
// interrupts disabled. The machine applies the post-boot register
// values itself when it models a boot ROM hand-off.
func New() *CPU {
	return &CPU{}
}

// Reset returns the CPU to its power-on state. The OnCycle hook
// is machine wiring, not CPU state, and survives.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	hook := c.OnCycle
	sw := c.OnStopSwitch
	*c = CPU{OnCycle: hook, OnStopSwitch: sw}
}

// Regs returns a snapshot of the programmer-visible registers.
func (c *CPU) Regs() Registers {
	return Registers{
		A: c.a, F: c.f, B: c.b, C: c.c, D: c.d, E: c.e, H: c.h, L: c.l,
		SP: c.sp, PC: c.pc,
	}
}

// SetRegs installs a register snapshot. F is masked to its high
// nibble, matching the hardware.
func (c *CPU) SetRegs(r Registers) {
	c.a, c.f = r.A, r.F&0xF0
	c.b, c.c = r.B, r.C
	c.d, c.e = r.D, r.E
	c.h, c.l = r.H, r.L
	c.sp, c.pc = r.SP, r.PC
}

// Cycles returns the total M-cycles executed since reset.
func (c *CPU) Cycles() uint64 { return c.cycles }

// IME reports the master interrupt enable state.
func (c *CPU) IME() bool { return c.ime }

// Wake leaves the STOP state. The machine calls it when a joypad
// button is pressed, the hardware's wake source for STOP.
func (c *CPU) Wake() { c.stopped = false }

// Halted reports whether the CPU is in the HALT state.
func (c *CPU) Halted() bool { return c.halted }

// Stopped reports whether the CPU is in the STOP state.
func (c *CPU) Stopped() bool { return c.stopped }

func (c *CPU) bc() uint16 { return uint16(c.b)<<8 | uint16(c.c) }
func (c *CPU) de() uint16 { return uint16(c.d)<<8 | uint16(c.e) }
func (c *CPU) hl() uint16 { return uint16(c.h)<<8 | uint16(c.l) }

func (c *CPU) setBC(v uint16) { c.b, c.c = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v) }
func (c *CPU) setDE(v uint16) { c.d, c.e = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v) }
func (c *CPU) setHL(v uint16) { c.h, c.l = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v) }

// getRP reads a 16-bit register pair by its opcode index:
// 0 BC, 1 DE, 2 HL, 3 SP.
func (c *CPU) getRP(i int) uint16 {
	switch i {
	case 0:
		return c.bc()
	case 1:
		return c.de()
	case 2:
		return c.hl()
	default:
		return c.sp
	}
}

// setRP writes a 16-bit register pair by its opcode index.
func (c *CPU) setRP(i int, v uint16) {
	switch i {
	case 0:
		c.setBC(v)
	case 1:
		c.setDE(v)
	case 2:
		c.setHL(v)
	default:
		c.sp = v
	}
}

// getRP2 reads a register pair for PUSH and POP by opcode index:
// 0 BC, 1 DE, 2 HL, 3 AF.
func (c *CPU) getRP2(i int) uint16 {
	if i == 3 {
		return uint16(c.a)<<8 | uint16(c.f)
	}
	return c.getRP(i)
}

// setRP2 writes a register pair for PUSH and POP. AF masks F to the
// high nibble, as the hardware does on POP AF.
func (c *CPU) setRP2(i int, v uint16) {
	if i == 3 {
		c.a, c.f = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v)&0xF0
		return
	}
	c.setRP(i, v)
}

// getR reads an 8-bit operand by opcode index:
// 0 B, 1 C, 2 D, 3 E, 4 H, 5 L, 6 (HL), 7 A.
func (c *CPU) getR(bus Bus, i int) uint8 {
	switch i {
	case 0:
		return c.b
	case 1:
		return c.c
	case 2:
		return c.d
	case 3:
		return c.e
	case 4:
		return c.h
	case 5:
		return c.l
	case 6:
		return c.rd(bus, c.hl())
	default:
		return c.a
	}
}

// setR writes an 8-bit operand by opcode index.
func (c *CPU) setR(bus Bus, i int, v uint8) {
	switch i {
	case 0:
		c.b = v
	case 1:
		c.c = v
	case 2:
		c.d = v
	case 3:
		c.e = v
	case 4:
		c.h = v
	case 5:
		c.l = v
	case 6:
		c.wr(bus, c.hl(), v)
	default:
		c.a = v
	}
}

// cond reports whether condition cc holds: 0 NZ, 1 Z, 2 NC, 3 C.
func (c *CPU) cond(cc int) bool {
	switch cc {
	case 0:
		return c.f&flagZ == 0
	case 1:
		return c.f&flagZ != 0
	case 2:
		return c.f&flagC == 0
	default:
		return c.f&flagC != 0
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setFlags(z, n, h, cy bool) {
	var f uint8
	if z {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	if n {
		f |= flagN
	}
	if h {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if cy {
		f |= flagC
	}
	c.f = f
}

// slot marks the start of the next M-cycle slot within the
// current step. Every bus access occupies one slot, in order; an
// access in slot k observes the machine after k M-cycles have
// elapsed, so the hook fires before every slot after the first.
// Purely internal cycles that precede an access still collapse
// into the step's trailing cycles (accounted by the machine from
// the returned total), which matches every access timing the
// conformance suites gate on.
func (c *CPU) slot() {
	if c.slots > 0 && c.OnCycle != nil {
		c.OnCycle()
	}
	c.slots++
}

// rd reads through the slot timing model.
func (c *CPU) rd(bus Bus, addr uint16) uint8 {
	c.slot()
	return bus.Read(addr)
}

// wr writes through the slot timing model.
func (c *CPU) wr(bus Bus, addr uint16, v uint8) {
	c.slot()
	bus.Write(addr, v)
}

// SlotsUsed returns how many M-cycle slots the last Step consumed
// with bus accesses or explicit idle slots. The machine ticks the
// remaining cycles of the step itself.
func (c *CPU) SlotsUsed() int { return c.slots }

// push16 writes a 16-bit value to the stack, high byte first.
func (c *CPU) push16(bus Bus, v uint16) {
	c.sp--
	c.wr(bus, c.sp, uint8(v>>8))
	c.sp--
	c.wr(bus, c.sp, uint8(v))
}

// pop16 reads a 16-bit value from the stack, low byte first.
func (c *CPU) pop16(bus Bus) uint16 {
	lo := c.rd(bus, c.sp)
	c.sp++
	hi := c.rd(bus, c.sp)
	c.sp++
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// fetchOp reads the next opcode byte. Under the HALT bug the byte is
// read but PC does not advance, so the same byte is seen again by the
// following fetch.
func (c *CPU) fetchOp(bus Bus) uint8 {
	v := c.rd(bus, c.pc)
	if c.haltBug {
		c.haltBug = false
	} else {
		c.pc++
	}
	return v
}

// fetch8 reads an operand byte and advances PC.
func (c *CPU) fetch8(bus Bus) uint8 {
	v := c.rd(bus, c.pc)
	c.pc++
	return v
}

// fetch16 reads a 16-bit little-endian operand and advances PC.
func (c *CPU) fetch16(bus Bus) uint16 {
	lo := c.fetch8(bus)
	hi := c.fetch8(bus)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// add performs A = A + v + carryIn and sets all four flags.
func (c *CPU) add(v uint8, carryIn bool) {
	cin := uint8(0)
	if carryIn {
		cin = 1
	}
	sum := uint16(c.a) + uint16(v) + uint16(cin)
	half := (c.a&0x0F)+(v&0x0F)+cin > 0x0F
	c.a = uint8(sum)
	c.setFlags(c.a == 0, false, half, sum > 0xFF)
}

// sub performs A = A - v - carryIn and sets all four flags. For CP
// the caller discards the result.
func (c *CPU) sub(v uint8, carryIn bool) uint8 {
	cin := uint8(0)
	if carryIn {
		cin = 1
	}
	res := int(c.a) - int(v) - int(cin)
	half := int(c.a&0x0F)-int(v&0x0F)-int(cin) < 0
	out := uint8(res)
	c.setFlags(out == 0, true, half, res < 0)
	return out
}

// alu runs arithmetic/logic operation i (0 ADD, 1 ADC, 2 SUB, 3 SBC,
// 4 AND, 5 XOR, 6 OR, 7 CP) on A with operand v.
func (c *CPU) alu(i int, v uint8) {
	carry := c.f&flagC != 0
	switch i {
	case 0:
		c.add(v, false)
	case 1:
		c.add(v, carry)
	case 2:
		c.a = c.sub(v, false)
	case 3:
		c.a = c.sub(v, carry)
	case 4:
		c.a &= v
		c.setFlags(c.a == 0, false, true, false)
	case 5:
		c.a ^= v
		c.setFlags(c.a == 0, false, false, false)
	case 6:
		c.a |= v
		c.setFlags(c.a == 0, false, false, false)
	case 7:
		c.sub(v, false) // CP: result discarded, flags kept
	}
}

// inc8 increments an 8-bit value with INC flag rules: carry is
// preserved, N clears, H reports carry out of bit 3.
func (c *CPU) inc8(v uint8) uint8 {
	res := v + 1
	cy := c.f&flagC != 0
	c.setFlags(res == 0, false, v&0x0F == 0x0F, cy)
	return res
}

// dec8 decrements an 8-bit value with DEC flag rules: carry is
// preserved, N sets, H reports borrow into bit 4.
func (c *CPU) dec8(v uint8) uint8 {
	res := v - 1
	cy := c.f&flagC != 0
	c.setFlags(res == 0, true, v&0x0F == 0x00, cy)
	return res
}

// addHL performs HL = HL + v with ADD HL flag rules: Z is preserved,
// N clears, H reports carry out of bit 11, C out of bit 15.
func (c *CPU) addHL(v uint16) {
	hl := c.hl()
	sum := uint32(hl) + uint32(v)
	half := (hl&0x0FFF)+(v&0x0FFF) > 0x0FFF
	z := c.f&flagZ != 0
	c.setHL(uint16(sum))
	c.setFlags(z, false, half, sum > 0xFFFF)
}

// addSPe8 computes SP + signed byte offset with the ADD SP and
// LD HL,SP+e8 flag rules: Z and N always clear, H and C are computed
// from the low byte addition of the unsigned offset byte.
func (c *CPU) addSPe8(e uint8) uint16 {
	sp := c.sp
	half := (sp&0x0F)+(uint16(e)&0x0F) > 0x0F
	cy := (sp&0xFF)+(uint16(e)&0xFF) > 0xFF
	c.setFlags(false, false, half, cy)
	return uint16(int32(int16(sp)) + int32(int8(e)))
}

// daa adjusts A after a BCD addition or subtraction, following the
// published algorithm: corrections of 0x06 and 0x60 are applied based
// on the H and C flags and the operand ranges; N is preserved, H
// clears, Z follows the result, C may be set by the 0x60 correction.
func (c *CPU) daa() {
	a := int(c.a)
	adj := 0
	carry := c.f&flagC != 0
	sub := c.f&flagN != 0
	if c.f&flagH != 0 || (!sub && a&0x0F > 9) {
		adj |= 0x06
	}
	if carry || (!sub && a > 0x99) {
		adj |= 0x60
		carry = true
	}
	if sub {
		a -= adj
	} else {
		a += adj
	}
	c.a = uint8(a)
	c.setFlags(c.a == 0, sub, false, carry)
}

// pendingInterrupts returns the enabled and requested interrupt bits.
func (c *CPU) pendingInterrupts(bus Bus) uint8 {
	return bus.Read(addrIE) & bus.Read(addrIF) & 0x1F
}

// dispatch services an interrupt over 5 M-cycles: two internal
// cycles, a push of PC's high byte, a push of the low byte, and
// the jump to the vector. The high-byte push can itself write the
// IE register when SP is 0x0000, and the hardware evaluates which
// interrupt to take only after that push: if the write removed
// every enabled request, the dispatch is cancelled and PC becomes
// 0x0000 instead of a vector (IME still clears, IF is untouched);
// if another request is still enabled, that one is taken instead.
// A low-byte push into IE comes too late to matter. All of this
// is exercised by the mooneye ie_push test.
func (c *CPU) dispatch(bus Bus) int {
	c.slot() // internal cycle 1
	c.slot() // internal cycle 2
	c.sp--
	c.wr(bus, c.sp, uint8(c.pc>>8))
	// Sampled in the same cycle as the push, after it landed.
	now := bus.Read(addrIE) & bus.Read(addrIF) & 0x1F
	c.sp--
	c.wr(bus, c.sp, uint8(c.pc))
	c.ime = false
	c.eiDelay = 0
	c.halted = false
	if now == 0 {
		c.pc = 0x0000
		c.cycles += 5
		return 5
	}
	bit := 0
	for now>>uint(bit)&1 == 0 {
		bit++
	}
	bus.Write(addrIF, bus.Read(addrIF)&^(1<<uint(bit)))
	c.pc = 0x40 + uint16(bit)*8
	c.cycles += 5
	return 5
}

// Step executes one instruction, one interrupt dispatch, or one idle
// M-cycle while halted or stopped, and returns the M-cycles consumed.
func (c *CPU) Step(bus Bus) int {
	c.slots = 0
	if c.stopped {
		c.cycles++
		return 1
	}
	if c.halted {
		pending := c.pendingInterrupts(bus)
		if pending == 0 {
			c.cycles++
			return 1
		}
		c.halted = false
		if c.ime {
			return c.dispatch(bus)
		}
		// IME clear: the CPU simply resumes executing. The HALT bug
		// does not apply here; it is decided when HALT executes.
	} else if c.ime {
		if pending := c.pendingInterrupts(bus); pending != 0 {
			return c.dispatch(bus)
		}
	}
	n := c.execute(bus)
	// A pending EI takes effect once the instruction after EI has
	// completed. eiDelay is armed to 2 by EI itself so its own step
	// does not consume the delay.
	if c.eiDelay > 0 {
		c.eiDelay--
		if c.eiDelay == 0 {
			c.ime = true
		}
	}
	c.cycles += uint64(n)
	return n
}

// Serialize writes the full CPU state into buf, which must be at
// least SerializeSize bytes long.
func (c *CPU) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("sm83: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	for i := 0; i < SerializeSize; i++ {
		buf[i] = 0
	}
	buf[0] = serializeVersion
	buf[1] = c.a
	buf[2] = c.f
	buf[3] = c.b
	buf[4] = c.c
	buf[5] = c.d
	buf[6] = c.e
	buf[7] = c.h
	buf[8] = c.l
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[9:], c.sp)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[11:], c.pc)
	if c.ime {
		buf[13] = 1
	}
	buf[14] = uint8(c.eiDelay)
	if c.halted {
		buf[15] = 1
	}
	if c.haltBug {
		buf[16] = 1
	}
	if c.stopped {
		buf[17] = 1
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[18:], c.cycles)
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("sm83: deserialize buffer too small")
	}
	if buf[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("sm83: unsupported serialize version")
	}
	c.a, c.f = buf[1], buf[2]&0xF0
	c.b, c.c = buf[3], buf[4]
	c.d, c.e = buf[5], buf[6]
	c.h, c.l = buf[7], buf[8]
	c.sp = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[9:])
	c.pc = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[11:])
	c.ime = buf[13] != 0
	c.eiDelay = int(buf[14])
	c.halted = buf[15] != 0
	c.haltBug = buf[16] != 0
	c.stopped = buf[17] != 0
	c.cycles = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[18:])
	return nil
}

package sm83

import "testing"

// flatBus is a plain 64 KB test bus.
type flatBus struct{ mem [65536]uint8 }

func (b *flatBus) Read(addr uint16) uint8       { return b.mem[addr] }
func (b *flatBus) Write(addr uint16, val uint8) { b.mem[addr] = val }
func (b *flatBus) load(at uint16, bytes ...uint8) {
	copy(b.mem[at:], bytes)
}

// run executes n steps of a program placed at 0x0100 and returns the
// CPU and bus for inspection.
func run(t *testing.T, prog []uint8, setup func(c *CPU, b *flatBus), steps int) (*CPU, *flatBus) {
	t.Helper()
	b := &flatBus{}
	b.load(0x0100, prog...)
	c := New()
	c.SetRegs(Registers{SP: 0xFFFE, PC: 0x0100})
	if setup != nil {
		setup(c, b)
	}
	for i := 0; i < steps; i++ {
		c.Step(b)
	}
	return c, b
}

func TestDAAAfterAddition(t *testing.T) {
	// 0x15 + 0x27 = 0x3C raw; DAA must give 0x42, no carry.
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0x3E, 0x15, 0xC6, 0x27, 0x27}, nil, 3)
	if c.Regs().A != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("A = 0x%02X, want 0x42", c.Regs().A)
	}
	if c.Regs().F&flagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("carry set, want clear (F=0x%02X)", c.Regs().F)
	}
}

func TestDAAAfterAdditionWithCarry(t *testing.T) {
	// 0x99 + 0x99 = 0x98 with carry after DAA (99 + 99 = 198).
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0x3E, 0x99, 0xC6, 0x99, 0x27}, nil, 3)
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.A != 0x98 || r.F&flagC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("A=0x%02X F=0x%02X, want A=0x98 with carry", r.A, r.F)
	}
}

func TestDAAAfterSubtraction(t *testing.T) {
	// 0x42 - 0x27 = 0x1B raw (N and H set); DAA must give 0x15.
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0x3E, 0x42, 0xD6, 0x27, 0x27}, nil, 3)
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.A != 0x15 {
		t.Fatalf("A = 0x%02X, want 0x15", r.A)
	}
	if r.F&flagN == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("N cleared by DAA, want preserved (F=0x%02X)", r.F)
	}
}

func TestCBRotateFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// RLC B with B=0x80: result 0x01, carry set, zero clear.
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0xCB, 0x00}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		c.SetRegs(Registers{B: 0x80, SP: 0xFFFE, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.B != 0x01 || r.F&flagC == 0 || r.F&flagZ != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("RLC: B=0x%02X F=0x%02X, want B=0x01 C=1 Z=0", r.B, r.F)
	}
	// RLC B with B=0x00: result 0x00, zero SET (unlike the A rotates),
	// carry clear.
	c, _ = run(t, []uint8{0xCB, 0x00}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		c.SetRegs(Registers{B: 0x00, SP: 0xFFFE, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	r = c.Regs()
	if r.B != 0x00 || r.F&flagZ == 0 || r.F&flagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("RLC zero: B=0x%02X F=0x%02X, want B=0x00 Z=1 C=0", r.B, r.F)
	}
	// RL B through a clear carry with B=0x80: result 0x00, zero set,
	// carry set.
	c, _ = run(t, []uint8{0xCB, 0x10}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		c.SetRegs(Registers{B: 0x80, F: 0, SP: 0xFFFE, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	r = c.Regs()
	if r.B != 0x00 || r.F&flagZ == 0 || r.F&flagC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("RL: B=0x%02X F=0x%02X, want B=0x00 Z=1 C=1", r.B, r.F)
	}
}

func TestAccumulatorRotateZeroQuirk(t *testing.T) {
	// RLCA with A=0x00 gives 0x00 but the SM83 still clears Z.
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0x07}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		c.SetRegs(Registers{A: 0x00, SP: 0xFFFE, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	if c.Regs().F&flagZ != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("RLCA set Z on a zero result; the SM83 never does (F=0x%02X)", c.Regs().F)
	}
}

func TestAddSPFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// SP=0xFFF8, +8: result 0x0000, H and C from the low byte, Z=0.
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0xE8, 0x08}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		c.SetRegs(Registers{SP: 0xFFF8, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.SP != 0x0000 {
		t.Fatalf("SP = 0x%04X, want 0x0000", r.SP)
	}
	if r.F != flagH|flagC {
		t.Fatalf("F = 0x%02X, want exactly H|C (Z and N clear)", r.F)
	}
	// SP=0x1000, +1: no half carry, no carry.
	c, _ = run(t, []uint8{0xE8, 0x01}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		c.SetRegs(Registers{SP: 0x1000, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	if c.Regs().F != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("F = 0x%02X, want 0", c.Regs().F)
	}
	// SP=0x0008, -8: result 0x0000; low byte 0x08+0xF8 carries both.
	c, _ = run(t, []uint8{0xE8, 0xF8}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		c.SetRegs(Registers{SP: 0x0008, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	r = c.Regs()
	if r.SP != 0x0000 || r.F != flagH|flagC {
		t.Fatalf("SP=0x%04X F=0x%02X, want SP=0 F=H|C", r.SP, r.F)
	}
}

func TestLDHAddressing(t *testing.T) {
	// LDH (0x80), A then LDH A, (0x80) via a different register.
	c, b := run(t, []uint8{0x3E, 0x5A, 0xE0, 0x80, 0x3E, 0x00, 0xF0, 0x80}, nil, 4)
	if b.mem[0xFF80] != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("memory at 0xFF80 = 0x%02X, want 0x5A", b.mem[0xFF80])
	}
	if c.Regs().A != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("A = 0x%02X, want 0x5A", c.Regs().A)
	}
}

func TestPopAFMasksFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// Stack holds 0xFFFF; POP AF must give A=0xFF and F=0xF0.
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0xF1}, func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		b.mem[0xFFFC] = 0xFF
		b.mem[0xFFFD] = 0xFF
		c.SetRegs(Registers{SP: 0xFFFC, PC: 0x0100})
	}, 1)
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.A != 0xFF || r.F != 0xF0 {
		t.Fatalf("A=0x%02X F=0x%02X, want A=0xFF F=0xF0", r.A, r.F)
	}
}

func TestEIDelay(t *testing.T) {
	// EI; NOP; NOP with a pending enabled interrupt. The interrupt
	// must not dispatch until the instruction after EI completes.
	prog := []uint8{0xFB, 0x00, 0x00}
	setup := func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		b.mem[0xFFFF] = 0x01 // IE: VBlank enabled
		b.mem[0xFF0F] = 0x01 // IF: VBlank requested
	}
	c, b := run(t, prog, setup, 1) // EI
	if c.Regs().PC != 0x0101 || c.IME() {
		t.Fatalf("after EI: PC=0x%04X IME=%v, want PC=0x0101 IME=false", c.Regs().PC, c.IME())
	}
	c.Step(b) // NOP executes; no dispatch yet
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.PC != 0x0102 || r.SP != 0xFFFE {
		t.Fatalf("after NOP post-EI: PC=0x%04X SP=0x%04X, want PC=0x0102 SP untouched", r.PC, r.SP)
	}
	c.Step(b) // now the dispatch happens
	r = c.Regs()
	if r.PC != 0x0040 {
		t.Fatalf("after dispatch step: PC=0x%04X, want 0x0040", r.PC)
	}
	if b.mem[0xFFFC] != 0x02 || b.mem[0xFFFD] != 0x01 {
		t.Fatalf("pushed return = 0x%02X%02X, want 0x0102", b.mem[0xFFFD], b.mem[0xFFFC])
	}
	if b.mem[0xFF0F]&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("IF bit not cleared by dispatch")
	}
}

func TestHaltBugDoublesNextByte(t *testing.T) {
	// IME=0 with a pending enabled interrupt: HALT does not halt,
	// and the byte after HALT (INC A) executes twice.
	prog := []uint8{0x76, 0x3C, 0x3C}
	setup := func(c *CPU, b *flatBus) {
		b.mem[0xFFFF] = 0x01
		b.mem[0xFF0F] = 0x01
		c.SetRegs(Registers{A: 0, SP: 0xFFFE, PC: 0x0100})
	}
	c, _ := run(t, prog, setup, 1) // HALT
	if c.Halted() {
		t.Fatalf("CPU halted despite a pending interrupt with IME clear")
	}
	c2, _ := run(t, prog, setup, 3) // HALT, INC A (bugged fetch), INC A
	if c2.Regs().A != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("A = %d after HALT;INC A under the bug, want 2 (byte fetched twice)", c2.Regs().A)
	}
	if c2.Regs().PC != 0x0102 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = 0x%04X, want 0x0102 after the doubled byte plus one real fetch", c2.Regs().PC)
	}
}

func TestHaltWakesOnInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	// Nothing pending: HALT halts; an idle step costs 1 cycle; when
	// the request arrives with IME clear the CPU resumes in place.
	b := &flatBus{}
	b.load(0x0100, 0x76, 0x3C) // HALT; INC A
	c := New()
	c.SetRegs(Registers{SP: 0xFFFE, PC: 0x0100})
	c.Step(b)
	if !c.Halted() {
		t.Fatalf("CPU did not halt with nothing pending")
	}
	if n := c.Step(b); n != 1 || !c.Halted() {
		t.Fatalf("idle halted step = %d cycles, halted=%v, want 1 and true", n, c.Halted())
	}
	b.mem[0xFFFF] = 0x01
	b.mem[0xFF0F] = 0x01
	c.Step(b) // wakes and runs INC A
	if c.Regs().A != 1 || c.Halted() {
		t.Fatalf("after wake: A=%d halted=%v, want A=1 halted=false", c.Regs().A, c.Halted())
	}
}

func TestInstructionCycles(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name   string
		prog   []uint8
		cycles int
	}{
		{"NOP", []uint8{0x00}, 1},
		{"LD BC,d16", []uint8{0x01, 0x34, 0x12}, 3},
		{"LD (a16),SP", []uint8{0x08, 0x00, 0xC0}, 5},
		{"CALL a16", []uint8{0xCD, 0x00, 0x02}, 6},
		{"RET", []uint8{0xC9}, 4},
		{"PUSH BC", []uint8{0xC5}, 4},
		{"POP BC", []uint8{0xC1}, 3},
		{"LD (HL),d8", []uint8{0x36, 0x99}, 3},
		{"BIT 7,(HL)", []uint8{0xCB, 0x7E}, 3},
		{"RLC (HL)", []uint8{0xCB, 0x06}, 4},
		{"JP (HL)", []uint8{0xE9}, 1},
		{"ADD SP,r8", []uint8{0xE8, 0x01}, 4},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		b := &flatBus{}
		b.load(0x0100, tc.prog...)
		b.load(0x0200, 0xC9) // CALL target: RET
		b.mem[0xFFFC] = 0x00 // RET/POP stack fodder
		b.mem[0xFFFD] = 0x01
		c := New()
		c.SetRegs(Registers{SP: 0xFFFC, PC: 0x0100})
		if n := c.Step(b); n != tc.cycles {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d M-cycles, want %d", tc.name, n, tc.cycles)
		}
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := run(t, []uint8{0x3E, 0x77, 0x06, 0x42}, nil, 2)
	buf := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := c.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c2 := New()
	if err := c2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if c.Regs() != c2.Regs() || c.Cycles() != c2.Cycles() {
		t.Fatalf("round trip mismatch: %+v vs %+v", c.Regs(), c2.Regs())
	}
	if err := c2.Deserialize([]byte{0xFF}); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("short buffer accepted")
	}
	bad := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	bad[0] = 99
	if err := c2.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("bad version accepted")
	}
}

func TestEIChainSchedulesOnce(t *testing.T) {
	// The mooneye ei_sequence scenario: the program raises IF and IE
	// itself, then executes a run of EIs. The enable scheduled by
	// the first EI fires after the second EI completes; later EIs
	// do not postpone it. The dispatch must push 0x010A (the third
	// EI's address) and jump to the serial vector.
	b := &flatBus{}
	b.load(0x100,
		0x3E, 0x08, // LD A, 8 (serial)
		0xEA, 0x0F, 0xFF, // LD (IF), A
		0xEA, 0xFF, 0xFF, // LD (IE), A
		0xFB, 0xFB, 0xFB, 0xFB, // EI x4 at 0x108..0x10B
		0x00,
	)
	c := &CPU{pc: 0x100, sp: 0xFFFE}
	for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
		c.Step(b)
	}
	if c.pc != 0x58 {
		t.Fatalf("after 6 steps PC = 0x%04X, want serial vector 0x0058", c.pc)
	}
	ret := uint16(b.mem[c.sp]) | uint16(b.mem[c.sp+1])<<8
	if ret != 0x010A {
		t.Errorf("pushed return = 0x%04X, want 0x010A", ret)
	}
}

func TestEIBeforeHaltDispatches(t *testing.T) {
	// The mooneye halt_ime0_ei scenario at the CPU level: IE is
	// enabled, IF is clear, and EI immediately precedes HALT. When
	// the interrupt source raises IF while the CPU sits in HALT,
	// the CPU must dispatch (the EI has taken effect, so this is
	// IME=1 halt behavior), not just wake and continue.
	b := &flatBus{}
	b.load(0x100,
		0x3E, 0x01, // LD A, 1 (vblank)
		0xEA, 0xFF, 0xFF, // LD (IE), A
		0xFB, // EI
		0x76, // HALT
		0x00, // NOP (resume target if wrongly woken)
	)
	c := &CPU{pc: 0x100, sp: 0xFFFE}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.Step(b)
	}
	if !c.halted {
		t.Fatal("CPU should be halted after HALT with no pending interrupt")
	}
	b.mem[0xFF0F] = 0x01 // interrupt source raises IF
	c.Step(b)
	if c.pc != 0x40 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = 0x%04X, want vblank vector 0x0040 (dispatch, not resume)", c.pc)
	}
	ret := uint16(b.mem[c.sp]) | uint16(b.mem[c.sp+1])<<8
	if ret != 0x0107 {
		t.Errorf("pushed return = 0x%04X, want 0x0107", ret)
	}
}

// Command libretro builds the Go Game Boy core as a libretro shared
// library (go build -buildmode=c-shared). It is a thin C ABI shell
// over the system package: the frontend (the iTaK engine) registers
// its callbacks, hands us a ROM, and calls retro_run once per frame.
// The same binary serves .gb and .gbc images; the system package
// picks DMG or CGB mode from the cartridge header.
package main

/*
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>

typedef bool (*retro_environment_t)(unsigned cmd, void *data);
typedef void (*retro_video_refresh_t)(const void *data, unsigned width, unsigned height, size_t pitch);
typedef void (*retro_audio_sample_t)(int16_t left, int16_t right);
typedef size_t (*retro_audio_sample_batch_t)(const int16_t *data, size_t frames);

typedef int16_t (*retro_input_state_t)(unsigned port, unsigned device, unsigned index, unsigned id);

static retro_audio_sample_t audio_cb;

static void gb_set_environ(retro_environment_t cb) { environ_cb = cb; }

static void gb_set_audio(retro_audio_sample_t cb) { audio_cb = cb; }
static void gb_set_audio_batch(retro_audio_sample_batch_t cb) { audio_batch_cb = cb; }

static void gb_set_input_state(retro_input_state_t cb) { input_state_cb = cb; }

static bool gb_environ(unsigned cmd, void *data) { return environ_cb ? environ_cb(cmd, data) : false; }
static void gb_video(const void *data, unsigned w, unsigned h, size_t pitch) { if (video_cb) video_cb(data, w, h, pitch); }
static size_t gb_audio_batch(const int16_t *data, size_t frames) { return audio_batch_cb ? audio_batch_cb(data, frames) : 0; }
static void gb_audio_sample(int16_t l, int16_t r) { if (audio_cb) audio_cb(l, r); }
static void gb_input_poll(void) { if (input_poll_cb) input_poll_cb(); }
static int16_t gb_input_state(unsigned port, unsigned dev, unsigned idx, unsigned id) { return input_state_cb ? input_state_cb(port, dev, idx, id) : 0; }

static const char *gb_get_name() { return "iTaK GoGameBoy"; }
static const char *gb_get_version() { return "0.1"; }
static const char *gb_get_exts() { return "gb|gbc"; }

struct gb_system_info { const char *library_name; const char *library_version; const char *valid_extensions; bool need_fullpath; bool block_extract; };
struct gb_game_geometry { unsigned base_width; unsigned base_height; unsigned max_width; unsigned max_height; float aspect_ratio; };
struct gb_system_timing { double fps; double sample_rate; };
struct gb_av_info { struct gb_game_geometry geometry; struct gb_system_timing timing; };
struct gb_game_info { const char *path; const void *data; size_t size; const char *meta; };
*/

// libretro constants used here (from the public libretro API).
const (
	envSetPixelFormat  = 10
	pixelFormatXRGB888 = 1
	deviceJoypad       = 1
	joypadB            = 0
	joypadY            = 1
	joypadSelect       = 2
	joypadStart        = 3
	joypadUp           = 4
	joypadDown         = 5
	joypadLeft         = 6
	joypadRight        = 7
	joypadA            = 8
	joypadX            = 9
	regionNTSC         = 0
	gbFPS              = 59.7275 // 4194304 dots / 70224 dots per frame
	gbAspect           = 1.1111  // 160/144 = 10/9 pixel aspect 1:1

//export retro_api_version

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_gb_game_info) C.bool {
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	} else if info.path != nil {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(C.GoString(info.path))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		data = b
	} else {
		return false
	}
	s, err := system.New(data)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	sys = s
	// Ask the frontend for XRGB8888 frames (what the PPU produces).
	fmt888 := C.uint32_t(pixelFormatXRGB888)
	C.gb_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&fmt888))
	return true
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() { sys = nil }

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys != nil {
		sys.Reset()
	}
}

func pressed(port int, id uint) bool {
	return C.gb_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceJoypad, 0, C.unsigned(id)) != 0
}

// pollPad translates libretro joypad state into the system button
// mask. The Game Boy has four buttons: libretro A and X are the
// console A, B and Y are the console B (the usual handheld map).
func pollPad(port int) uint16 {
	var m uint16
	if pressed(port, joypadRight) {
		m |= system.ButtonRight
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadLeft) {
		m |= system.ButtonLeft
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadUp) {
		m |= system.ButtonUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadDown) {
		m |= system.ButtonDown
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadA) || pressed(port, joypadX) {
		m |= system.ButtonA
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadB) || pressed(port, joypadY) {
		m |= system.ButtonB
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadSelect) {
		m |= system.ButtonSelect
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadStart) {
		m |= system.ButtonStart
	}
	return m
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() {
	if sys == nil || !sys.Loaded() {
		return
	}
	C.gb_input_poll()
	sys.SetButtons(0, pollPad(0))
	sys.SetButtons(1, pollPad(1))
	sys.RunFrame()

	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) > 0 {
		C.gb_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]),
			C.unsigned(sys.Width()), C.unsigned(sys.Height()),
			C.size_t(ppu.Width*4))
	}
	ab := sys.AudioBuffer()
	if len(ab) >= 2 {
		frames := len(ab) / 2
		done := int(C.gb_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&ab[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
		for i := done; i < frames; i++ {
			C.gb_audio_sample(C.int16_t(ab[2*i]), C.int16_t(ab[2*i+1]))
		}
	}
}

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.SerializeSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.SerializeSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	return sys.Serialize(buf) == nil
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.SerializeSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	return sys.Deserialize(buf) == nil
}

// The memory interface exposes cartridge RAM as SAVE_RAM and the
// first two work RAM banks as SYSTEM_RAM, the standard libretro
// memory map ids.

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.unsigned) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var ram []uint8
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		ram = sys.SaveRAM()
	case memSystemRAM:
		ram = sys.SystemRAM()
	}
	if len(ram) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Pointer(&ram[0])
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.unsigned) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SaveRAM()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SystemRAM()))
	}
	return 0
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/ppu/ppu.go ====================

// Package ppu is an original implementation of the Game Boy
// pixel processing unit, covering both the DMG and the Game Boy
// Color (CGB) models, written from the published hardware
// documentation (the Pan Docs graphics chapters and the published
// pixel FIFO research).
//
// The framebuffer is XRGB8888 (one uint32 per pixel, 0xFFRRGGBB):
// the format the libretro bridge negotiates. DMG shades map to
// the gray levels FF, AA, 55, 00 the acid2 references prescribe;
// CGB 15-bit colors are upconverted per channel with the standard
// (v<<3)|(v>>2) expansion the cgb-acid2 reference prescribes.
//
// The PPU is dot-stepped: one frame is 154 lines of 456 dots
// (70,224 dots). Each visible line runs mode 2 (OAM scan, 80 dots),
// mode 3 (pixel transfer, variable length), and mode 0 (HBlank) in
// order; lines 144-153 are mode 1 (VBlank). Mode 3 lasts
// 172 + (SCX mod 8) plus the sprite and window fetch penalties
// described at latchLine.
//
// Lines are rendered whole at the mode 3 to mode 0 transition from
// the scroll, palette, and sprite state latched when the line's
// transfer began, with tile data read live (VRAM writes are blocked
// during mode 3, so the bytes a transfer would have fetched cannot
// change under it). Register writes that land during HBlank
// therefore apply to the next line, as they do on hardware.
package ppu

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Geometry of the DMG picture.
const (
	Width         = 160
	Height        = 144
	DotsPerLine   = 456
	LinesPerFrame = 154
	DotsPerFrame  = DotsPerLine * LinesPerFrame // 70,224

	modeHBlank = 0
	modeVBlank = 1
	modeOAM    = 2
	modeDraw   = 3
)

// lcdWarmup is the number of dots the first line after an LCD
// turn-on spends reading mode 0 before the first OAM scan begins.
const lcdWarmup = 88

// IRQ callback bits: the system passes a function the PPU calls to
// request an interrupt. Bit 0 is VBlank, bit 1 is LCD STAT.
const (
	IRQVBlank = 0
	IRQSTAT   = 1
)

// shadeXRGB maps the four DMG shades (0 lightest to 3 darkest) to
// XRGB8888 pixels. The gray levels are the ones the dmg-acid2
// reference prescribes for comparison: FF, AA, 55, 00.
var shadeXRGB = [4]uint32{0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFAAAAAA, 0xFF555555, 0xFF000000}

// expand5 upconverts one 5-bit color channel to 8 bits.
func expand5(v uint16) uint32 {
	return uint32(v<<3 | v>>2)
}

// colorXRGB upconverts a CGB 15-bit color (RRRRRGG GGGBBBBB in a
// little-endian palette word) to an XRGB8888 framebuffer pixel.
func colorXRGB(c uint16) uint32 {
	return 0xFF000000 |
		expand5(c&0x1F)<<16 |
		expand5((c>>5)&0x1F)<<8 |
		expand5((c>>10)&0x1F)
}

// sprite is one OAM entry latched for a scanline during mode 2.
type sprite struct {
	y, x  uint8
	tile  uint8
	flags uint8
	index int // OAM order, breaks X ties
}

// PPU is one pixel processing unit. A PPU built with NewCGB
// models the Game Boy Color: two VRAM banks, tile attribute maps,
// color palettes, and CGB priority rules; New models the DMG,
// where the CGB registers are absent and bank 1 is unreachable.
type PPU struct {
	cgb    bool
	compat bool         // DMG compatibility mode: palette data ports lock
	vram   [0x4000]byte // two 8 KB banks; the DMG uses bank 0 only
	oam    [0xA0]byte
	fb     []uint32 // Width*Height XRGB8888

	// CGB state: the VBK-selected VRAM bank, palette RAM and the
	// BCPS/OCPS index registers (bit 7 of an index is the
	// auto-increment flag), and the FF6C object priority mode
	// (0 = OAM order, 1 = X order, the DMG rule).
	vbk    uint8
	bgPal  [64]byte
	objPal [64]byte
	bcps   uint8
	ocps   uint8
	opri   uint8
	bgAttr [Width]uint8 // per-pixel BG attribute latched by renderLineCGB
	spPalN [Width]uint8 // per-pixel sprite palette number (CGB render)
	spPrio [Width]bool  // per-pixel sprite priority flag (CGB render)

	// OnHBlank, when set by the machine, is called on the dot the
	// PPU enters mode 0 on a visible line. The system uses it to
	// clock HBlank HDMA transfers.
	OnHBlank func()

	// Registers.
	lcdc   uint8
	statEn uint8 // STAT bits 3-6: interrupt enables
	scy    uint8
	scx    uint8
	lyc    uint8
	bgp    uint8
	obp0   uint8
	obp1   uint8
	wy     uint8
	wx     uint8

	lcdOn bool
	line  int // current scanline 0-153 (register LY while on)
	dot   int // dot within the line 0-455
	mode  int

	statLine bool // current level of the STAT interrupt line

	// Per-line latched state, captured when a line's mode 2 ends.
	sprites    [10]sprite
	spPal      [Width]bool // per-pixel sprite palette choice while rendering
	numSprites int
	latScx     uint8
	latWx      int // window trigger X for this line, or -1
	wyArmed    bool
	winLine    int // window internal line counter
	winUsed    bool
	mode3Len   int

	lycEq bool // stored LYC coincidence flag. The comparison only
	// advances while the LCD is on (the comparison clock stops when
	// it is off), so the flag freezes across an LCD-off period and
	// LYC writes then have no effect. Recomputed on line changes,
	// LYC writes, and LCD turn-on, all while on.

	// LCD turn-on warmup: the first line after the LCD turns on
	// spends its first lcdWarmup dots reading mode 0 before the
	// first OAM scan begins, and its HBlank is shortened by the
	// same amount so the frame stays 456 dots per line. The
	// warmup length is bracketed by the mooneye lcdon_timing
	// measurements (mode still reads 0 at 68 dots, mode 3 reached
	// by 240 dots); the exact value is not pinned by the gated
	// tests.
	warm    int // warmup dots remaining on the current line
	shorten int // dots this line is shortened by (the warmup)
}

// New returns a PPU in the DMG post-boot state: the boot ROM hands
// over with the LCD on (LCDC 0x91), BGP 0xFC, object palettes 0xFF,
// parked at the top of a frame in mode 2.
func New() *PPU {
	p := &PPU{fb: make([]uint32, Width*Height)}
	p.Reset()
	return p
}

// NewCGB returns a PPU in the CGB post-boot state: the DMG
// hand-off plus cleared palette RAM (all colors read white until
// the game writes its palettes, the documented boot behavior) and
// VRAM bank 0 selected.
func NewCGB() *PPU {
	p := &PPU{fb: make([]uint32, Width*Height), cgb: true}
	p.Reset()
	return p
}

// CGB reports whether this PPU models the Game Boy Color.
func (p *PPU) CGB() bool { return p.cgb }

// SetCompat marks DMG compatibility mode (a DMG cartridge running
// on CGB hardware): the palette data ports and the sprite
// priority register lock to reads of 0xFF, as the hardware locks
// them, while the index registers keep working.
func (p *PPU) SetCompat() { p.compat = true }

// LCDOn reports whether the LCD is currently enabled.
func (p *PPU) LCDOn() bool { return p.lcdOn }

// Reset restores the post-boot state and clears the memories.
func (p *PPU) Reset() {
	for i := range p.vram {
		p.vram[i] = 0
	}
	for i := range p.oam {
		p.oam[i] = 0
	}
	for i := range p.fb {
		p.fb[i] = shadeXRGB[0]
	}
	p.vbk = 0
	p.bcps, p.ocps = 0, 0
	p.opri = 0
	for i := range p.bgPal {
		p.bgPal[i] = 0xFF
	}
	for i := range p.objPal {
		p.objPal[i] = 0xFF
	}
	p.lcdc = 0x91
	p.statEn = 0
	p.scy, p.scx = 0, 0
	p.lyc = 0
	p.bgp = 0xFC
	p.obp0, p.obp1 = 0xFF, 0xFF
	p.wy, p.wx = 0, 0
	p.lcdOn = true
	p.line, p.dot, p.mode = 0, 0, modeOAM
	p.lycEq = true
	p.statLine = false
	p.wyArmed = false
	p.winLine = 0
	p.winUsed = false
}

// Framebuffer returns the current frame as Width*Height
// XRGB8888 pixels, row major.
func (p *PPU) Framebuffer() []uint32 { return p.fb }

// LY returns the current scanline, or 0 while the LCD is off (the
// beam position is not observable then).
func (p *PPU) LY() int {
	if !p.lcdOn {
		return 0
	}
	return p.line
}

// Mode returns the current STAT mode (0 while the LCD is off).
func (p *PPU) Mode() int {
	if !p.lcdOn {
		return 0
	}
	return p.mode
}

// coincidence reports the stored LYC coincidence flag. The
// comparison clock only runs while the LCD is on, so the flag
// freezes (retained, not recomputed) while the LCD is off, and
// LYC writes then do not move it.
func (p *PPU) coincidence() bool { return p.lycEq }

// evalSTAT recomputes the STAT interrupt line from the enables and
// conditions and requests the STAT interrupt on a rising edge. The
