// line is the OR of the enabled sources; while it stays high no
// new request is made, which is the hardware's STAT blocking
// behavior (a source that is already active when enabled, or that
// never drops, cannot retrigger).
func (p *PPU) evalSTAT(irq func(bit int)) {
	line := false
	if p.lcdOn {
		if p.statEn&0x40 != 0 && p.coincidence() {
			line = true
		}
		if p.statEn&0x20 != 0 && p.mode == modeOAM {
			line = true
		}
		if p.statEn&0x10 != 0 && p.mode == modeVBlank {
			line = true
		}
		if p.statEn&0x08 != 0 && p.mode == modeHBlank {
			line = true
		}
	}
	if line && !p.statLine && irq != nil {
		irq(IRQSTAT)
	}
	p.statLine = line
}

// Read handles a read from the PPU register and memory area
// (0x8000-0x9FFF VRAM, 0xFE00-0xFE9F OAM, 0xFF40-0xFF4B registers).
// Mode-based access blocking follows the hardware: VRAM is
// unreachable during mode 3, OAM during modes 2 and 3; blocked
// reads return 0xFF.
func (p *PPU) Read(addr uint16) uint8 {
	switch {
	case addr >= 0x8000 && addr < 0xA000:
		if p.lcdOn && p.mode == modeDraw {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return p.vram[int(p.vbk)*0x2000+int(addr-0x8000)]
	case addr >= 0xFE00 && addr < 0xFEA0:
		if p.lcdOn && (p.mode == modeOAM || p.mode == modeDraw) {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return p.oam[addr-0xFE00]
	}
	switch addr {
	case 0xFF40:
		return p.lcdc
	case 0xFF41: // STAT: bit 7 set, enables, LYC flag, mode
		v := uint8(0x80) | p.statEn
		if p.coincidence() {
			v |= 0x04
		}
		return v | uint8(p.Mode())
	case 0xFF42:
		return p.scy
	case 0xFF43:
		return p.scx
	case 0xFF44:
		return uint8(p.LY())
	case 0xFF45:
		return p.lyc
	case 0xFF47:
		return p.bgp
	case 0xFF48:
		return p.obp0
	case 0xFF49:
		return p.obp1
	case 0xFF4A:
		return p.wy
	case 0xFF4B:
		return p.wx
	case 0xFF4F: // VBK: CGB only; unused bits read back set
		if !p.cgb {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return 0xFE | p.vbk
	case 0xFF68: // BCPS
		if !p.cgb {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return 0x40 | p.bcps
	case 0xFF69: // BGPD: palette RAM is unreachable during mode 3
		if !p.cgb || p.compat || (p.lcdOn && p.mode == modeDraw) {
			return 0xFF
		}
		v := p.bgPal[p.bcps&0x3F]
		if p.bcps&0x80 != 0 {
			p.bcps = 0x80 | (p.bcps+1)&0x3F
		}
		return v
	case 0xFF6A: // OCPS
		if !p.cgb {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return 0x40 | p.ocps
	case 0xFF6B: // OBPD
		if !p.cgb || p.compat || (p.lcdOn && p.mode == modeDraw) {
			return 0xFF
		}
		v := p.objPal[p.ocps&0x3F]
		if p.ocps&0x80 != 0 {
			p.ocps = 0x80 | (p.ocps+1)&0x3F
		}
		return v
	case 0xFF6C: // OPRI: CGB object priority mode select
		if !p.cgb || p.compat {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return 0xFE | p.opri
	}
	return 0xFF
}

// Write handles a write to the PPU area. Blocked writes (VRAM in
// mode 3, OAM in modes 2 and 3) are ignored, as on hardware. LY is
// read-only. STAT stores only its interrupt enable bits.
func (p *PPU) Write(addr uint16, val uint8, irq func(bit int)) {
	switch {
	case addr >= 0x8000 && addr < 0xA000:
		if !(p.lcdOn && p.mode == modeDraw) {
			p.vram[int(p.vbk)*0x2000+int(addr-0x8000)] = val
		}
		return
	case addr >= 0xFE00 && addr < 0xFEA0:
		if !(p.lcdOn && (p.mode == modeOAM || p.mode == modeDraw)) {
			p.oam[addr-0xFE00] = val
		}
		return
	}
	switch addr {
	case 0xFF40:
		p.writeLCDC(val, irq)
	case 0xFF41:
		p.statEn = val & 0x78
		p.evalSTAT(irq)
	case 0xFF42:
		p.scy = val
	case 0xFF43:
		p.scx = val
	case 0xFF44:
		// LY is read-only.
	case 0xFF45:
		p.lyc = val
		if p.lcdOn {
			p.lycEq = p.line == int(val)
			p.evalSTAT(irq)
		}
	case 0xFF47:
		p.bgp = val
	case 0xFF48:
		p.obp0 = val
	case 0xFF49:
		p.obp1 = val
	case 0xFF4A:
		p.wy = val
	case 0xFF4B:
		p.wx = val
	case 0xFF4F: // VBK
		if p.cgb {
			p.vbk = val & 1
		}
	case 0xFF68: // BCPS
		if p.cgb {
			p.bcps = val & 0xBF
		}
	case 0xFF69: // BGPD: ignored during mode 3, as on hardware
		if p.cgb && !p.compat && !(p.lcdOn && p.mode == modeDraw) {
			p.bgPal[p.bcps&0x3F] = val
			if p.bcps&0x80 != 0 {
				p.bcps = 0x80 | (p.bcps+1)&0x3F
			}
		}
	case 0xFF6A: // OCPS
		if p.cgb {
			p.ocps = val & 0xBF
		}
	case 0xFF6B: // OBPD: ignored during mode 3
		if p.cgb && !p.compat && !(p.lcdOn && p.mode == modeDraw) {
			p.objPal[p.ocps&0x3F] = val
			if p.ocps&0x80 != 0 {
				p.ocps = 0x80 | (p.ocps+1)&0x3F
			}
		}
	case 0xFF6C: // OPRI
		if p.cgb && !p.compat {
			p.opri = val & 1
		}
	}
}

// writeLCDC handles the LCD control register, including the LCD
// power transitions. Turning the LCD off parks the beam: LY reads
// as 0, the mode as 0, and no interrupts are generated. Turning it
// back on restarts the frame at line 0 in mode 2.
func (p *PPU) writeLCDC(val uint8, irq func(bit int)) {
	was := p.lcdOn
	p.lcdc = val
	p.lcdOn = val&0x80 != 0
	if was && !p.lcdOn {
		p.line, p.dot, p.mode = 0, 0, modeHBlank
		p.warm, p.shorten = 0, 0
	}
	if !was && p.lcdOn {
		// The beam restarts at line 0; the first OAM scan
		// begins after the turn-on warmup (see the warm
		// field). The comparison clock restarts too, which
		// can raise the STAT line right here (LY 0 vs LYC 0).
		p.line, p.dot, p.mode = 0, 0, modeHBlank
		p.warm, p.shorten = lcdWarmup, lcdWarmup
		p.lycEq = int(p.lyc) == 0
		p.wyArmed = false
		p.winLine = 0
		p.evalSTAT(irq)
	}
}

// ReadVRAMRaw and the OAM raw accessors bypass mode blocking. The
// DMA unit uses them: its transfers run on the bus independent of
// the pixel transfer, and its OAM writes are the entire point.
// ReadVRAMRaw reads the VBK-selected bank; WriteVRAMRaw writes a
// VRAM offset (0x0000-0x1FFF) in the VBK-selected bank, which is
// what HDMA targets.
func (p *PPU) ReadVRAMRaw(addr uint16) uint8 {
	return p.vram[int(p.vbk)*0x2000+int(addr-0x8000)]
}
func (p *PPU) WriteVRAMRaw(off int, val uint8) {
	if off >= 0 && off < 0x2000 {
		p.vram[int(p.vbk)*0x2000+off] = val
	}
}
func (p *PPU) WriteOAMRaw(off int, val uint8) {
	if off >= 0 && off < len(p.oam) {
		p.oam[off] = val
	}
}
func (p *PPU) ReadOAMRaw(off int) uint8 {
	if off >= 0 && off < len(p.oam) {
		return p.oam[off]
	}
	return 0xFF
}

// latchLine runs at the start of a visible line's mode 3: the OAM
// scan result (up to ten sprites covering this line, in OAM order)
// and the scroll and window state the transfer will use.
func (p *PPU) latchLine() {
	// OAM scan: two dots per entry over mode 2; the first ten
	// sprites whose Y range covers the line are latched.
	height := 8
	if p.lcdc&0x04 != 0 {
		height = 16
	}
	p.numSprites = 0
	for i := 0; i < 40 && p.numSprites < 10; i++ {
		y := p.oam[i*4]
		if int(p.line)+16 >= int(y) && int(p.line)+16 < int(y)+height {
			p.sprites[p.numSprites] = sprite{
				y: y, x: p.oam[i*4+1], tile: p.oam[i*4+2],
				flags: p.oam[i*4+3], index: i,
			}
			p.numSprites++
		}
	}
	p.latScx = p.scx
	// Window arming: the window becomes drawable on the line
	// where LY reaches WY, and stays armed for the rest of the
	// frame. The trigger X is WX - 7; WX below 7 triggers at the
	// left edge, WX above 166 never triggers.
	if int(p.wy) == p.line {
		p.wyArmed = true
	}
	p.latWx = -1
	// On the DMG the window needs LCDC bits 5 and 0; on the CGB
	// bit 0 is priority-only and the window displays without it.
	if p.lcdc&0x20 != 0 && (p.cgb || p.lcdc&0x01 != 0) && p.wyArmed {
		t := int(p.wx) - 7
		if t < 0 {
			t = 0
		}
		if t < Width {
			p.latWx = t
		}
	}
	// Mode 3 length: the base transfer plus the scroll discard,
	// the window fetch, and the sprite fetch penalties. A sprite
	// fetch stalls the pixel FIFO for 6 dots; the first sprite
	// fetched also pays the phase alignment of its X position
	// (8 - (X mod 8) in total for that fetch), and sprites at
	// X >= 168 sit fully off the right edge and are never
	// fetched. The full phase interaction between sprites at
	// different X positions is FIFO-internal; this is the
	// documented level the mooneye mode timing tests check apart
	// from intr_2_mode0_timing_sprites, which stays out of the
	// gate for exactly that reason.
	p.mode3Len = 172 + int(p.latScx&7)
	fetched := 0
	minX := 0
	for i := 0; i < p.numSprites; i++ {
		if int(p.sprites[i].x) < 168 {
			if fetched == 0 || int(p.sprites[i].x) < minX {
				minX = int(p.sprites[i].x)
			}
			fetched++
		}
	}
	if fetched > 0 {
		p.mode3Len += 8 - (minX & 7) + 6*(fetched-1)
	}
	if p.latWx >= 0 {
		p.mode3Len += 6
	}
	p.winUsed = false
}

// renderLine draws the current line into the framebuffer from the
// latched state and live tile data. The CGB renderer handles
// color; the DMG renderer below handles monochrome.
func (p *PPU) renderLine() {
	if p.cgb {
		p.renderLineCGB()
		return
	}
	y := p.line
	out := p.fb[y*Width : (y+1)*Width]
	bgOn := p.lcdc&0x01 != 0
	winOn := p.lcdc&0x20 != 0 && p.latWx >= 0
	var bgIdx [Width]uint8

	bgMap := uint16(0x1800)
	if p.lcdc&0x08 != 0 {
		bgMap = 0x1C00
	}
	winMap := uint16(0x1800)
	if p.lcdc&0x40 != 0 {
		winMap = 0x1C00
	}
	signedTiles := p.lcdc&0x10 == 0

	tilePixel := func(mapBase uint16, tx, ty, px, py int) uint8 {
		idx := p.vram[mapBase+uint16(ty)*32+uint16(tx)]
		var data uint16
		if signedTiles {
			data = 0x1000 + uint16(int(int8(idx))*16)
		} else {
			data = uint16(idx) * 16
		}
		lo := p.vram[data+uint16(py)*2]
		hi := p.vram[data+uint16(py)*2+1]
		bit := uint(7 - px)
		return (hi>>bit&1)<<1 | lo>>bit&1
	}

	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		var idx uint8
		if bgOn {
			if winOn && x >= p.latWx {
				// Window pixel: the window's own line counter
				// supplies the tile row.
				wx := x - p.latWx
				idx = tilePixel(winMap, wx/8, p.winLine/8, wx%8, p.winLine%8)
				p.winUsed = true
			} else {
				bx := x + int(p.latScx)
				by := y + int(p.scy)
				idx = tilePixel(bgMap, (bx/8)%32, (by/8)%32, bx%8, by%8)
			}
		}
		bgIdx[x] = idx
		out[x] = uint32(idx)
	}

	// Sprites: priority order is smallest X first, OAM order
	// breaking ties; the first sprite to claim a pixel wins it,
	// subject to the BG-over-sprite flag (which only yields to a
	// background color index of 0).
	if p.lcdc&0x02 != 0 {
		height := 8
		if p.lcdc&0x04 != 0 {
			height = 16
		}
		order := make([]int, p.numSprites)
		for i := range order {
			order[i] = i
		}
		// Stable insertion sort by X (lists hold at most ten).
		for i := 1; i < len(order); i++ {
			for j := i; j > 0 && p.sprites[order[j]].x < p.sprites[order[j-1]].x; j-- {
				order[j], order[j-1] = order[j-1], order[j]
			}
		}
		var claimed [Width]bool
		for _, oi := range order {
			sp := p.sprites[oi]
			row := y + 16 - int(sp.y)
			if sp.flags&0x40 != 0 { // Y-flip
				row = height - 1 - row
			}
			tile := sp.tile
			if height == 16 {
				tile &^= 1
				if row >= 8 {
					tile++
					row -= 8
				}
			}
			data := uint16(tile) * 16
			lo := p.vram[data+uint16(row)*2]
			hi := p.vram[data+uint16(row)*2+1]
			for px := 0; px < 8; px++ {
				sx := int(sp.x) - 8 + px
				if sx < 0 || sx >= Width || claimed[sx] {
					continue
				}
				bit := uint(px)
				if sp.flags&0x20 == 0 { // X-flip mirrors the pixel order
					bit = uint(7 - px)
				}
				ci := (hi>>bit&1)<<1 | lo>>bit&1
				if ci == 0 {
					continue
				}
				claimed[sx] = true
				if sp.flags&0x80 != 0 && bgIdx[sx] != 0 {
					continue // BG wins over this sprite pixel
				}
				out[sx] = uint32(ci) | 0x80 // tag as sprite for the palette pass
				p.spPal[sx] = sp.flags&0x10 != 0
			}
		}
	}

	// Palette pass: background pixels through BGP, sprite pixels
	// (tagged with bit 7 of the stored value) through the object
	// palette their flags selected.
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		v := out[x]
		if v&0x80 != 0 {
			pal := p.obp0
			if p.spPal[x] {
				pal = p.obp1
			}
			out[x] = shadeXRGB[(pal>>(2*(v&3)))&3]
		} else {
			out[x] = shadeXRGB[(p.bgp>>(2*v))&3]
		}
	}
}

// renderLineCGB draws one line with CGB color: tile attributes
// from VRAM bank 1 (palette, tile bank, flips, priority), sprites
// with per-sprite palettes and banks, and the CGB priority
// resolution between the background and sprite layers:
//
//   - LCDC bit 0 is the BG/window master priority. Clear, the
//     background and window still display, but sprites always
//     win over them: the priority bits are ignored. (Blanking
//     the background is the DMG compatibility mode behavior,
//     which this core does not model.)
//   - A background color index of 0 always loses to a sprite.
//   - Otherwise, if either the BG attribute priority bit or the
//     sprite's priority bit is set, the background wins; if not,
//     the sprite wins.
//
// Sprite overlap uses OAM order (the first sprite in OAM keeps
// the pixel), unless FF6C (OPRI) selects the DMG rule (smallest
// X, OAM order breaking ties).
func (p *PPU) renderLineCGB() {
	y := p.line
	out := p.fb[y*Width : (y+1)*Width]
	master := p.lcdc&0x01 != 0
	winOn := p.lcdc&0x20 != 0 && p.latWx >= 0

	bgMap := uint16(0x1800)
	if p.lcdc&0x08 != 0 {
		bgMap = 0x1C00
	}
	winMap := uint16(0x1800)
	if p.lcdc&0x40 != 0 {
		winMap = 0x1C00
	}
	signedTiles := p.lcdc&0x10 == 0

	// tilePixelCGB resolves one background or window pixel: the
	// tile index from bank 0, its attribute from bank 1, and the
	// tile data from the attribute's bank, flips applied.
	tilePixel := func(mapBase uint16, tx, ty, px, py int) (idx uint8, attr uint8) {
		off := mapBase + uint16(ty)*32 + uint16(tx)
		tile := p.vram[off]
		attr = p.vram[0x2000+off]
		if attr&0x20 != 0 { // X flip
			px = 7 - px
		}
		if attr&0x40 != 0 { // Y flip
			py = 7 - py
		}
		var data uint16
		if signedTiles {
			data = 0x1000 + uint16(int(int8(tile))*16)
		} else {
			data = uint16(tile) * 16
		}
		base := int(attr>>3&1) * 0x2000
		lo := p.vram[base+int(data)+py*2]
		hi := p.vram[base+int(data)+py*2+1]
		bit := uint(7 - px)
		return (hi>>bit&1)<<1 | lo>>bit&1, attr
	}

	var bgIdx [Width]uint8
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		var attr uint8
		if winOn && x >= p.latWx {
			wx := x - p.latWx
			bgIdx[x], attr = tilePixel(winMap, wx/8, p.winLine/8, wx%8, p.winLine%8)
			p.winUsed = true
		} else {
			bx := x + int(p.latScx)
			by := y + int(p.scy)
			bgIdx[x], attr = tilePixel(bgMap, (bx/8)%32, (by/8)%32, bx%8, by%8)
		}
		p.bgAttr[x] = attr
		out[x] = uint32(bgIdx[x]) // resolved in the composite pass
	}

	// Sprites: the first sprite (in the active priority order)
	// to claim a pixel with a non-transparent index keeps it.
	var spIdx [Width]uint8
	var claimed [Width]bool
	if p.lcdc&0x02 != 0 {
		height := 8
		if p.lcdc&0x04 != 0 {
			height = 16
		}
		order := make([]int, p.numSprites)
		for i := range order {
			order[i] = i
		}
		if p.opri&1 != 0 {
			// DMG ordering: smallest X first, OAM order breaking
			// ties (stable sort).
			for i := 1; i < len(order); i++ {
				for j := i; j > 0 && p.sprites[order[j]].x < p.sprites[order[j-1]].x; j-- {
					order[j], order[j-1] = order[j-1], order[j]
				}
			}
		}
		for _, oi := range order {
			sp := p.sprites[oi]
			row := y + 16 - int(sp.y)
			if sp.flags&0x40 != 0 {
				row = height - 1 - row
			}
			tile := sp.tile
			if height == 16 {
				tile &^= 1
				if row >= 8 {
					tile++
					row -= 8
				}
			}
			base := int(sp.flags>>3&1) * 0x2000
			data := base + int(tile)*16
			lo := p.vram[data+row*2]
			hi := p.vram[data+row*2+1]
			for px := 0; px < 8; px++ {
				sx := int(sp.x) - 8 + px
				if sx < 0 || sx >= Width || claimed[sx] {
					continue
				}
				bit := uint(px)
				if sp.flags&0x20 == 0 {
					bit = uint(7 - px)
				}
				ci := (hi>>bit&1)<<1 | lo>>bit&1
				if ci == 0 {
					continue
				}
				claimed[sx] = true
				spIdx[sx] = ci
				p.spPalN[sx] = sp.flags & 0x07
				p.spPrio[sx] = sp.flags&0x80 != 0
			}
		}
	}

	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		bgPalIdx := p.bgAttr[x] & 0x07
		bg := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(p.bgPal[bgPalIdx*8+bgIdx[x]*2:])
		if claimed[x] {
			spriteWins := false
			switch {
			case bgIdx[x] == 0:
				spriteWins = true
			case !master:
				spriteWins = true
			case p.bgAttr[x]&0x80 != 0 || p.spPrio[x]:
				spriteWins = false
			default:
				spriteWins = true
			}
			if spriteWins {
				out[x] = colorXRGB(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(
					p.objPal[p.spPalN[x]*8+spIdx[x]*2:]))
				continue
			}
		}
		out[x] = colorXRGB(bg)
	}
}

// Tick advances the PPU by the given number of dots, calling irq
// for interrupt requests. While the LCD is off the beam is parked
// and Tick does nothing; the caller keeps frame pacing.
func (p *PPU) Tick(dots int, irq func(bit int)) {
	if !p.lcdOn {
		return
	}
	// Advance in jumps to the next event dot (warmup expiry, a
	// mode boundary, or the end of the line) instead of stepping
	// dot by dot: nothing observable changes between event dots,
	// and callers only sample PPU state at tick boundaries. The
	// transitions below are the per-dot ones, fired in the same
	// order at the same dots.
	for dots > 0 {
		if p.warm > 0 {
			// Warmup dots still advance the line dot count,
			// so the first line totals 456 dots like any other.
			step := dots
			if p.warm < step {
				step = p.warm
			}
			if rem := DotsPerLine - p.dot; rem < step {
				step = rem
			}
			if step < 1 {
				step = 1
			}
			p.dot += step
			p.warm -= step
			dots -= step
			if p.warm == 0 {
				p.mode = modeOAM
				p.evalSTAT(irq)
			}
			if p.dot == DotsPerLine {
				p.endLine(irq)
			}
			continue
		}
		var boundary int
		switch p.mode {
		case modeOAM:
			boundary = 80 + p.shorten
		case modeDraw:
			boundary = 80 + p.shorten + p.mode3Len
		default: // modeHBlank, modeVBlank
			boundary = DotsPerLine
		}
		step := dots
		if rem := boundary - p.dot; rem < step {
			step = rem
		}
		if step < 1 {
			step = 1
		}
		p.dot += step
		dots -= step
		switch p.mode {
		case modeOAM:
			if p.dot == 80+p.shorten {
				p.latchLine()
				p.mode = modeDraw
				p.evalSTAT(irq)
			}
		case modeDraw:
			if p.dot == 80+p.shorten+p.mode3Len {
				p.renderLine()
				p.mode = modeHBlank
				if p.OnHBlank != nil {
					p.OnHBlank()
				}
				p.evalSTAT(irq)
			}
		case modeHBlank, modeVBlank:
			if p.dot == DotsPerLine {
				p.endLine(irq)
			}
		}
	}
}

// endLine advances to the next scanline at the line boundary:
// LY changes (with its LYC evaluation), VBlank entry raises the
// VBlank interrupt, the window line counter advances when the
// window drew, and the frame wraps after line 153.
func (p *PPU) endLine(irq func(bit int)) {
	p.dot = 0
	p.shorten = 0
	if p.winUsed {
		p.winLine++
	}
	p.line++
	if p.line >= LinesPerFrame {
		p.line = 0
		p.wyArmed = false
		p.winLine = 0
	}
	p.lycEq = p.line == int(p.lyc)
	if p.line == 144 {
		p.mode = modeVBlank
		if irq != nil {
			irq(IRQVBlank)
		}
		p.evalSTAT(irq)
		return
	}
	if p.line < Height {
		p.mode = modeOAM
	} else {
		p.mode = modeVBlank
	}
	p.evalSTAT(irq)
}

// --- save states ---------------------------------------------------------

// SerializeSize is the fixed size of the PPU state: both VRAM
// banks, OAM, the framebuffer, palette RAM, registers, and beam
// state.
const SerializeSize = 0x4000 + 0xA0 + Width*Height*4 + 128 + 128

const serializeVersion = 2

// Serialize writes the full PPU state into buf.
func (p *PPU) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("ppu: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	for i := 0; i < SerializeSize; i++ {
		buf[i] = 0
	}
	off := 0
	copy(buf[off:], p.vram[:])
	off += len(p.vram)
	copy(buf[off:], p.oam[:])
	off += len(p.oam)
	for i, px := range p.fb {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off+i*4:], px)
	}
	off += len(p.fb) * 4
	copy(buf[off:], p.bgPal[:])
	off += len(p.bgPal)
	copy(buf[off:], p.objPal[:])
	off += len(p.objPal)
	b := buf[off:]
	b[0] = serializeVersion
	b[1] = p.lcdc
	b[2] = p.statEn
	b[3] = p.scy
	b[4] = p.scx
	b[5] = p.lyc
	b[6] = p.bgp
	b[7] = p.obp0
	b[8] = p.obp1
	b[9] = p.wy
	b[10] = p.wx
	if p.lcdOn {
		b[11] = 1
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[12:], uint16(p.line))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[14:], uint16(p.dot))
	b[16] = uint8(p.mode)
	if p.statLine {
		b[17] = 1
	}
	if p.wyArmed {
		b[18] = 1
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[19:], uint16(p.winLine))
	if p.winUsed {
		b[21] = 1
	}
	b[22] = p.latScx
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[23:], uint16(int16(p.latWx)))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[25:], uint16(p.mode3Len))
	b[27] = uint8(p.numSprites)
	for i := 0; i < p.numSprites; i++ {
		sp := p.sprites[i]
		b[28+i*5] = sp.y
		b[29+i*5] = sp.x
		b[30+i*5] = sp.tile
		b[31+i*5] = sp.flags
		b[32+i*5] = uint8(sp.index)
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[80:], uint16(p.warm))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[82:], uint16(p.shorten))
	if p.lycEq {
		b[84] = 1
	}
	if p.cgb {
		b[85] = 1
	}
	b[86] = p.vbk
	b[87] = p.bcps
	b[88] = p.ocps
	b[89] = p.opri
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (p *PPU) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("ppu: deserialize buffer too small")
	}
	off := 0
	copy(p.vram[:], buf[off:])
	off += len(p.vram)
	copy(p.oam[:], buf[off:])
	off += len(p.oam)
	for i := range p.fb {
		p.fb[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off+i*4:])
	}
	off += len(p.fb) * 4
	copy(p.bgPal[:], buf[off:])
	off += len(p.bgPal)
	copy(p.objPal[:], buf[off:])
	off += len(p.objPal)
	b := buf[off:]
	if b[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("ppu: unsupported serialize version")
	}
	p.lcdc = b[1]
	p.statEn = b[2]
	p.scy = b[3]
	p.scx = b[4]
	p.lyc = b[5]
	p.bgp = b[6]
	p.obp0 = b[7]
	p.obp1 = b[8]
	p.wy = b[9]
	p.wx = b[10]
	p.lcdOn = b[11] != 0
	p.line = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[12:]))
	p.dot = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[14:]))
	p.mode = int(b[16])
	p.statLine = b[17] != 0
	p.wyArmed = b[18] != 0
	p.winLine = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[19:]))
	p.winUsed = b[21] != 0
	p.latScx = b[22]
	p.latWx = int(int16(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[23:])))
	p.mode3Len = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[25:]))
	p.numSprites = int(b[27])
	for i := 0; i < p.numSprites && i < 10; i++ {
		p.sprites[i] = sprite{
			y: b[28+i*5], x: b[29+i*5], tile: b[30+i*5],
			flags: b[31+i*5], index: int(b[32+i*5]),
		}
	}
	p.warm = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[80:]))
	p.shorten = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[82:]))
	p.lycEq = b[84] != 0
	// The model's identity comes from how the PPU was built, not
	// from the state; the stored flag is only a sanity marker.
	p.vbk = b[86]
	p.bcps = b[87]
	p.ocps = b[88]
	p.opri = b[89]
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/ppu/ppu_test.go ====================

package ppu

import "testing"

func irqCounter() (func(bit int), *int, *int) {
	vbl, stat := 0, 0
	return func(bit int) {
		if bit == IRQVBlank {
			vbl++
		} else {
			stat++
		}
	}, &vbl, &stat
}

func TestFrameLengthAndModes(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	irq, vbl, _ := irqCounter()
	p.Reset()
	if p.Mode() != 2 || p.LY() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("after reset: mode=%d line=%d, want mode 2 line 0", p.Mode(), p.LY())
	}
	tick := func(n int) {
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			p.Tick(1, irq)
		}
	}
	tick(79)
	if p.Mode() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("dot 79: mode=%d, want 2 (OAM scan)", p.Mode())
	}
	tick(1) // dot 80
	if p.Mode() != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("dot 80: mode=%d, want 3 (transfer)", p.Mode())
	}
	tick(172) // dot 252
	if p.Mode() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("dot 252: mode=%d, want 0 (HBlank)", p.Mode())
	}
	tick(456 - 252) // end of line 0
	if p.LY() != 1 || p.Mode() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("line wrap: line=%d mode=%d, want line 1 mode 2", p.LY(), p.Mode())
	}
	// Run to the end of the visible frame: VBlank IRQ exactly
	// once, at line 144.
	tick(456*143 + 456 - 456) // through line 143 into 144
	if *vbl != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("vblank IRQs = %d, want 1", *vbl)
	}
	if p.LY() != 144 || p.Mode() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("vblank: line=%d mode=%d, want 144/1", p.LY(), p.Mode())
	}
	// Finish the frame: total dots from reset must be 70224.
	tick(456 * 10)
	if p.LY() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("after full frame: line=%d, want 0", p.LY())
	}
}

func TestVRAMOAMAccessBlocking(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	irq, _, _ := irqCounter()
	p.Reset()
	// Move to HBlank, where both memories are CPU-accessible.
	for p.Mode() != 0 {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	p.Write(0x8000, 0xAB, irq)
	p.Write(0xFE00, 0xCD, irq)
	if got := p.Read(0x8000); got != 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("VRAM read in mode 0 = 0x%02X, want 0xAB", got)
	}
	// Line 1 mode 2 (OAM scan): OAM blocked, VRAM open.
	for p.Mode() != 2 {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	if got := p.Read(0xFE00); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("OAM read in mode 2 = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	if got := p.Read(0x8000); got != 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("VRAM read in mode 2 = 0x%02X, want 0xAB", got)
	}
	p.Write(0xFE00, 0x11, irq) // ignored
	// Mode 3 (transfer): both blocked.
	for p.Mode() != 3 {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	if got := p.Read(0x8000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("VRAM read in mode 3 = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	p.Write(0x8000, 0x55, irq) // ignored
	// HBlank again: both open, and the ignored writes never landed.
	for p.Mode() != 0 {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	if got := p.Read(0x8000); got != 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("VRAM after mode 3 = 0x%02X, want 0xAB (write was blocked)", got)
	}
	if got := p.Read(0xFE00); got != 0xCD {
		t.Fatalf("OAM after mode 2 = 0x%02X, want 0xCD (write was blocked)", got)
	}
}

func TestLCDOffFreezesDisplay(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	irq, vbl, stat := irqCounter()
	p.Reset()
	for i := 0; i < 1000; i++ {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	p.Write(0xFF40, 0x11, irq) // LCD off, BG on
	if got := p.Read(0xFF44); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("LY with LCD off = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if p.Mode() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mode with LCD off = %d, want 0", p.Mode())
	}
	v, s := *vbl, *stat
	for i := 0; i < DotsPerFrame; i++ {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	if *vbl != v || *stat != s {
		t.Fatalf("interrupts fired with LCD off: vbl %d->%d stat %d->%d", v, *vbl, s, *stat)
	}
	p.Write(0xFF40, 0x91, irq) // back on at line 0
	if p.LY() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("line after LCD on = %d, want 0", p.LY())
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	irq, _, _ := irqCounter()
	p.Reset()
	p.Write(0x8010, 0x3C, irq)
	p.Write(0xFF47, 0xE4, irq)
	for i := 0; i < 30000; i++ {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	buf := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := p.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	q := New()
	if err := q.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if q.LY() != p.LY() || q.Mode() != p.Mode() {
		t.Fatalf("restored line/mode = %d/%d, want %d/%d", q.LY(), q.Mode(), p.LY(), p.Mode())
	}
	buf2 := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := q.Serialize(buf2); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := range buf {
		if buf[i] != buf2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("state mismatch at byte %d: 0x%02X vs 0x%02X", i, buf[i], buf2[i])
		}
	}
	// Both PPUs must finish the frame identically.
	for i := 0; i < DotsPerFrame; i++ {
		p.Tick(1, irq)
		q.Tick(1, irq)
	}
	fa, fb := p.Framebuffer(), q.Framebuffer()
	for i := range fa {
		if fa[i] != fb[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer mismatch at pixel %d after restore", i)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/sound/sound.go ====================

// Package sound is an original implementation of the Game Boy (DMG)
// audio processing unit, written from the published hardware
// documentation (the Pan Docs audio chapters).
//
// Four channels: two square waves (channel 1 with a frequency
// sweep), a wave channel reading a 32-entry 4-bit sample table, and
// a noise channel driven by a 15-bit LFSR. A 512 Hz frame sequencer
// clocks the length counters, the sweep, and the envelopes. The
// mixer routes each channel to the left (SO2) and right (SO1)
// outputs under NR51, scales by the NR50 side volumes, and the
// result is box-filtered down to the host sample rate.
//
// The frame sequencer is not timed by this package: on hardware it
// is clocked by a falling edge of the system divider's bit 12, so
// the system calls StepFrameSequencer at those edges and the APU's
// length, sweep, and envelope timing inherits the divider's exact
// phase (including the quirk that a DIV write dropping bit 12
// clocks the sequencer).
package sound

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"math"
)

// SampleRate is the host output rate the APU renders to.
const SampleRate = 44100

// clockHz is the Game Boy master clock; channel timers and the
// sample resampler count in these T-cycles (dots).
const clockHz = 4194304

// Register addresses.
const (
	regNR10 = 0xFF10
	regNR52 = 0xFF26
	regWave = 0xFF30
)

// dutyPatterns are the four square waveforms, one bit per step,
// MSB first in step order.
var dutyPatterns = [4]uint8{0x01, 0x03, 0x0F, 0x3F}

// noiseDivisors maps NR43's divisor code to the LFSR timer base
// period in dots (before the shift clock is applied).
var noiseDivisors = [8]int{8, 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 112}

type square struct {
	enabled bool
	dacOn   bool
	freq    uint16 // 11-bit frequency value
	timer   int    // dots until the next duty step
	dutyPos int
	duty    int // 0-3

	length   int
	lengthOn bool

	vol      int // live envelope volume
	envInit  int // NRx2 initial volume, loaded at trigger
	envTimer int
	envPace  int
	envUp    bool

	// Sweep (channel 1 only).
	shadow     uint16
	sweepTimer int
	sweepPace  int
	sweepSlope int
	sweepNeg   bool
	sweepOn    bool
}

type wave struct {
	enabled  bool
	dacOn    bool
	freq     uint16
	timer    int
	pos      int // 0-31 nibble position
	length   int
	lengthOn bool
	volCode  int // NR32 volume code 0-3
}

type noise struct {
	enabled  bool
	dacOn    bool
	lfsr     uint16
	timer    int
	length   int
	lengthOn bool

	vol      int // live envelope volume
	envInit  int // NR42 initial volume, loaded at trigger
	envTimer int
	envPace  int
	envUp    bool
}

// APU is one DMG audio processing unit.
type APU struct {
	ch1 square
	ch2 square
	ch3 wave
	ch4 noise

	// Register shadows for read-back of the readable registers.
	nr10, nr11, nr12, nr21, nr22 uint8
	nr30, nr32                   uint8
	nr42, nr43                   uint8
	nr50, nr51                   uint8
	len1, len2, len4             uint8 // NRx1 length fields as written
	len3                         uint8
	ctrl1, ctrl2, ctrl3, ctrl4   uint8 // NRx4 as written (bit 6 read back)

	waveRAM [16]byte

	power  bool
	fsStep int // next frame sequencer step to run, 0-7

	// Sample generation: every dot adds the mixed output to the
	// accumulators; the phase accumulator emits one output sample
	// per SampleRate-th of a second of dots, box-filtered over the
	// dots it spans.
	phase float64
	sumL  float64
	sumR  float64
	sumN  int
	out   []int16 // pending samples (interleaved stereo)

	// Cached mixed output. The mix only changes when a channel
	// steps (duty, wave position, or LFSR clock), when an
	// envelope, sweep, or length clock lands, or when a register
	// is written; between those events the mix is reused from the cache
	// values instead of re-evaluating all four channels per dot.
	mixL     float64
	mixR     float64
	mixStale bool
}

// New returns an APU in its power-on state: powered, all channels
// off, frame sequencer at step 0.
func New() *APU {
	s := &APU{power: true, mixStale: true}
	s.ch4.lfsr = 0x7FFF
	return s
}

// Trigger helper: the length counter quirk. When a channel's
// length enable rises in an NRx4 write and the next frame
// sequencer step is a length-clock step, the counter is clocked
// immediately; if that empties it, the channel turns off.
func (s *APU) lenEnableEdge(length *int, lengthOn *bool, enabled *bool, newOn bool) {
	if newOn && !*lengthOn && s.nextStepClocksLength() {
		if *length > 0 {
			*length--
			if *length == 0 {
				*enabled = false
			}
		}
	}
	*lengthOn = newOn
}

func (s *APU) nextStepClocksLength() bool {
	// Length counters clock on sequencer steps 0, 2, 4, 6.
	return s.fsStep%2 == 0
}

// Write handles a write to the APU register area 0xFF10-0xFF3F.
// While powered off, writes to NR10-NR51 are ignored (wave RAM
// stays writable); NR52 is the power switch itself.
func (s *APU) Write(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	s.mixStale = true
	if addr >= regWave && addr < regWave+16 {
		// DMG wave RAM quirk: while the wave channel is playing,
		// writes are ignored (reads return 0xFF; see Read).
		if !s.ch3.enabled {
			s.waveRAM[addr-regWave] = val
		}
		return
	}
	if addr == regNR52 {
		s.writePower(val)
		return
	}
	if !s.power {
		return
	}
	switch addr {
	// Channel 1.
	case 0xFF10:
		s.nr10 = val
		s.ch1.sweepPace = int(val>>4) & 7
		s.ch1.sweepNeg = val&0x08 != 0
		s.ch1.sweepSlope = int(val) & 7
	case 0xFF11:
		s.nr11 = val
		s.ch1.duty = int(val >> 6)
		s.len1 = val & 0x3F
		s.ch1.length = 64 - int(s.len1)
	case 0xFF12:
		s.nr12 = val
		s.ch1.dacOn = val&0xF8 != 0
		if !s.ch1.dacOn {
			s.ch1.enabled = false
		}
		s.ch1.envInit = int(val >> 4)
		s.ch1.envUp = val&0x08 != 0
		s.ch1.envPace = int(val) & 7
	case 0xFF13:
		s.ch1.freq = s.ch1.freq&0x700 | uint16(val)
	case 0xFF14:
		s.ctrl1 = val
		s.ch1.freq = s.ch1.freq&0xFF | uint16(val&7)<<8
		s.lenEnableEdge(&s.ch1.length, &s.ch1.lengthOn, &s.ch1.enabled, val&0x40 != 0)
		if val&0x80 != 0 {
			s.triggerSquare(&s.ch1, true)
		}
	// Channel 2.
	case 0xFF16:
		s.nr21 = val
		s.ch2.duty = int(val >> 6)
		s.len2 = val & 0x3F
		s.ch2.length = 64 - int(s.len2)
	case 0xFF17:
		s.nr22 = val
		s.ch2.dacOn = val&0xF8 != 0
		if !s.ch2.dacOn {
			s.ch2.enabled = false
		}
		s.ch2.envInit = int(val >> 4)
		s.ch2.envUp = val&0x08 != 0
		s.ch2.envPace = int(val) & 7
	case 0xFF18:
		s.ch2.freq = s.ch2.freq&0x700 | uint16(val)
	case 0xFF19:
		s.ctrl2 = val
		s.ch2.freq = s.ch2.freq&0xFF | uint16(val&7)<<8
		s.lenEnableEdge(&s.ch2.length, &s.ch2.lengthOn, &s.ch2.enabled, val&0x40 != 0)
		if val&0x80 != 0 {
			s.triggerSquare(&s.ch2, false)
		}
	// Channel 3.
	case 0xFF1A:
		s.nr30 = val
		s.ch3.dacOn = val&0x80 != 0
		if !s.ch3.dacOn {
			s.ch3.enabled = false
		}
	case 0xFF1B:
		s.len3 = val
		s.ch3.length = 256 - int(val)
	case 0xFF1C:
		s.nr32 = val
		s.ch3.volCode = int(val>>5) & 3
	case 0xFF1D:
		s.ch3.freq = s.ch3.freq&0x700 | uint16(val)
	case 0xFF1E:
		s.ctrl3 = val
		s.ch3.freq = s.ch3.freq&0xFF | uint16(val&7)<<8
		s.lenEnableEdge(&s.ch3.length, &s.ch3.lengthOn, &s.ch3.enabled, val&0x40 != 0)
		if val&0x80 != 0 {
			s.triggerWave()
		}
	// Channel 4.
	case 0xFF20:
		s.len4 = val & 0x3F
		s.ch4.length = 64 - int(s.len4)
	case 0xFF21:
		s.nr42 = val
		s.ch4.dacOn = val&0xF8 != 0
		if !s.ch4.dacOn {
			s.ch4.enabled = false
		}
		s.ch4.envInit = int(val >> 4)
		s.ch4.envUp = val&0x08 != 0
		s.ch4.envPace = int(val) & 7
	case 0xFF22:
		s.nr43 = val
	case 0xFF23:
		s.ctrl4 = val
		s.lenEnableEdge(&s.ch4.length, &s.ch4.lengthOn, &s.ch4.enabled, val&0x40 != 0)
		if val&0x80 != 0 {
			s.triggerNoise()
		}
	// Master.
	case 0xFF24:
		s.nr50 = val
	case 0xFF25:
		s.nr51 = val
	}
}

// writePower handles NR52's bit 7. Powering off clears every sound
// register and disables all channels, and resets the frame
// sequencer to step 0; the length counters keep their values,
// which the documentation calls out explicitly (a channel powered
// back on with a surviving counter still times out on it once
// re-enabled). Wave RAM is not touched.
func (s *APU) writePower(val uint8) {
	on := val&0x80 != 0
	if on == s.power {
		return
	}
	s.power = on
	if !on {
		l1, l2, l3, l4 := s.ch1.length, s.ch2.length, s.ch3.length, s.ch4.length
		wr := s.waveRAM
		*s = APU{power: false, out: s.out[:0]}
		s.ch1.length, s.ch2.length, s.ch3.length, s.ch4.length = l1, l2, l3, l4
		s.waveRAM = wr
		s.ch4.lfsr = 0x7FFF
	}
}

// triggerSquare starts a square channel: length reloads if empty,
// the envelope restarts, and (channel 1) the sweep restarts with
// its immediate overflow check.
func (s *APU) triggerSquare(ch *square, swept bool) {
	if !ch.dacOn {
		ch.enabled = false
		return
	}
	ch.enabled = true
	if ch.length == 0 {
		ch.length = 64
		if ch.lengthOn && s.nextStepClocksLength() {
			ch.length--
		}
	}
	ch.timer = (2048 - int(ch.freq)) * 4
	// The envelope restarts from the register's initial volume.
	ch.vol = ch.envInit
	ch.envTimer = ch.envPace
	if swept {
		ch.shadow = ch.freq
		ch.sweepTimer = ch.sweepPace
		if ch.sweepTimer == 0 {
			ch.sweepTimer = 8
		}
		ch.sweepOn = ch.sweepPace != 0 || ch.sweepSlope != 0
		if ch.sweepSlope != 0 {
			if ch.calcSweep() > 2047 {
				ch.enabled = false
			}
		}
	}
}

// calcSweep computes the frequency the sweep would move to.
func (ch *square) calcSweep() uint16 {
	delta := ch.shadow >> uint(ch.sweepSlope)
	if ch.sweepNeg {
		return ch.shadow - delta
	}
	return ch.shadow + delta
}

func (s *APU) triggerWave() {
	if !s.ch3.dacOn {
		s.ch3.enabled = false
		return
	}
	s.ch3.enabled = true
	if s.ch3.length == 0 {
		s.ch3.length = 256
		if s.ch3.lengthOn && s.nextStepClocksLength() {
			s.ch3.length--
		}
	}
	s.ch3.timer = (2048 - int(s.ch3.freq)) * 2
	s.ch3.pos = 0
}

func (s *APU) triggerNoise() {
	if !s.ch4.dacOn {
		s.ch4.enabled = false
		return
	}
	s.ch4.enabled = true
	if s.ch4.length == 0 {
		s.ch4.length = 64
		if s.ch4.lengthOn && s.nextStepClocksLength() {
			s.ch4.length--
		}
	}
	s.ch4.lfsr = 0x7FFF
	s.ch4.timer = noisePeriod(s.nr43)
	s.ch4.vol = s.ch4.envInit
	s.ch4.envTimer = s.ch4.envPace
}

// noisePeriod converts NR43 to the LFSR timer period in dots.
func noisePeriod(nr43 uint8) int {
	code := int(nr43) & 7
	shift := int(nr43>>4) & 0xF
	return noiseDivisors[code] << uint(shift)
}

// Read handles a read from the APU register area, applying the
// documented read-back masks (write-only fields read as 1s).
func (s *APU) Read(addr uint16) uint8 {
	if addr >= regWave && addr < regWave+16 {
		// DMG wave RAM quirk: while the wave channel is playing,
		// reads return 0xFF.
		if s.ch3.enabled {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return s.waveRAM[addr-regWave]
	}
	switch addr {
	case 0xFF10:
		return s.nr10 | 0x80
	case 0xFF11:
		return s.nr11&0xC0 | 0x3F
	case 0xFF12:
		return s.nr12
	case 0xFF13:
		return 0xFF
	case 0xFF14:
		return s.ctrl1&0x40 | 0xBF
	case 0xFF16:
		return s.nr21&0xC0 | 0x3F
	case 0xFF17:
		return s.nr22
	case 0xFF18:
		return 0xFF
	case 0xFF19:
		return s.ctrl2&0x40 | 0xBF
	case 0xFF1A:
		return s.nr30&0x80 | 0x7F
	case 0xFF1B:
		return 0xFF
	case 0xFF1C:
		return s.nr32&0x60 | 0x9F
	case 0xFF1D:
		return 0xFF
	case 0xFF1E:
		return s.ctrl3&0x40 | 0xBF
	case 0xFF20:
		return 0xFF
	case 0xFF21:
		return s.nr42
	case 0xFF22:
		return s.nr43
	case 0xFF23:
		return s.ctrl4&0x40 | 0xBF
	case 0xFF24:
		return s.nr50
	case 0xFF25:
		return s.nr51
	case regNR52:
		v := uint8(0x70)
		if s.power {
			v |= 0x80
		}
		if s.ch1.enabled {
			v |= 1
		}
		if s.ch2.enabled {
			v |= 2
		}
		if s.ch3.enabled {
			v |= 4
		}
		if s.ch4.enabled {
			v |= 8
		}
		return v
	}
	return 0xFF
}

// StepFrameSequencer runs one 512 Hz frame sequencer step: length
// counters on steps 0/2/4/6, sweep on 2/6, envelopes on step 7. The
// system calls it on each falling edge of divider bit 12.
func (s *APU) StepFrameSequencer() {
	s.mixStale = true
	if !s.power {
		return
	}
	step := s.fsStep
	s.fsStep = (s.fsStep + 1) & 7
	switch step {
	case 0, 2, 4, 6:
		s.clockLengths()
	}
	switch step {
	case 2, 6:
		s.clockSweep()
	case 7:
		s.clockEnvelopes()
	}
}

func (s *APU) clockLengths() {
	clock := func(length *int, lengthOn bool, enabled *bool) {
		if lengthOn && *length > 0 {
			*length--
			if *length == 0 {
				*enabled = false
			}
		}
	}
	clock(&s.ch1.length, s.ch1.lengthOn, &s.ch1.enabled)
	clock(&s.ch2.length, s.ch2.lengthOn, &s.ch2.enabled)
	clock(&s.ch3.length, s.ch3.lengthOn, &s.ch3.enabled)
	clock(&s.ch4.length, s.ch4.lengthOn, &s.ch4.enabled)
}

func (s *APU) clockSweep() {
	ch := &s.ch1
	if !ch.sweepOn || ch.sweepPace == 0 {
		return
	}
	if ch.sweepTimer > 0 {
		ch.sweepTimer--
	}
	if ch.sweepTimer != 0 {
		return
	}
	ch.sweepTimer = ch.sweepPace
	if !ch.enabled {
		return
	}
	next := ch.calcSweep()
	if next > 2047 {
		ch.enabled = false
		return
	}
	ch.freq = next
	ch.shadow = next
	if ch.calcSweep() > 2047 {
		ch.enabled = false
	}
}

func (s *APU) clockEnvelopes() {
	env := func(chVol *int, timer *int, pace int, up bool, dacOn bool) {
		if pace == 0 || !dacOn {
			return
		}
		if *timer > 0 {
			*timer--
		}
		if *timer == 0 {
			*timer = pace
			if up && *chVol < 15 {
				*chVol++
			}
			if !up && *chVol > 0 {
				*chVol--
			}
		}
	}
	env(&s.ch1.vol, &s.ch1.envTimer, s.ch1.envPace, s.ch1.envUp, s.ch1.dacOn)
	env(&s.ch2.vol, &s.ch2.envTimer, s.ch2.envPace, s.ch2.envUp, s.ch2.dacOn)
	env(&s.ch4.vol, &s.ch4.envTimer, s.ch4.envPace, s.ch4.envUp, s.ch4.dacOn)
}

// Tick advances the channel timers by the given number of dots and
// generates output samples into the pending buffer.
// phaseInc is the sample phase accumulator step per dot: one
// output sample period spans clockHz/SampleRate dots.
const phaseInc = float64(SampleRate) / float64(clockHz)

// Tick advances the APU by the given number of dots. The span
// is split at the nearest channel step: before that dot every
// channel output is constant, on the step dot the stepped
// channel state applies. Each part is accumulated in bulk
// instead of dot by dot.
func (s *APU) Tick(dots int) {
	for dots > 0 {
		seg := dots
		expiring := false
		if s.ch1.enabled && s.ch1.timer <= seg {
			seg = s.ch1.timer
			expiring = true
		}
		if s.ch2.enabled && s.ch2.timer <= seg {
			seg = s.ch2.timer
			expiring = true
		}
		if s.ch3.enabled && s.ch3.timer <= seg {
			seg = s.ch3.timer
			expiring = true
		}
		if s.ch4.enabled && s.ch4.timer <= seg {
			seg = s.ch4.timer
			expiring = true
		}
		if seg < 1 {
			seg = 1
		}
		if expiring {
			s.mixSpan(seg - 1)
			s.advanceChannels(seg)
			s.mixSpan(1)
		} else {
			s.advanceChannels(seg)
			s.mixSpan(seg)
		}
		dots -= seg
	}
}

// advanceChannels runs the four channel timers forward by d
// dots in closed form: a channel whose timer expires steps its
// duty position, wave position, or LFSR exactly as the per-dot
// countdown would.
func (s *APU) advanceChannels(d int) {
	if s.ch1.enabled {
		if d < s.ch1.timer {
			s.ch1.timer -= d
		} else {
			period := (2048 - int(s.ch1.freq)) * 4
			exp := 1 + (d-s.ch1.timer)/period
			s.ch1.timer += exp*period - d
			s.ch1.dutyPos = (s.ch1.dutyPos + exp) & 7
			s.mixStale = true
		}
	}
	if s.ch2.enabled {
		if d < s.ch2.timer {
			s.ch2.timer -= d
		} else {
			period := (2048 - int(s.ch2.freq)) * 4
			exp := 1 + (d-s.ch2.timer)/period
			s.ch2.timer += exp*period - d
			s.ch2.dutyPos = (s.ch2.dutyPos + exp) & 7
			s.mixStale = true
		}
	}
	if s.ch3.enabled {
		if d < s.ch3.timer {
			s.ch3.timer -= d
		} else {
			period := (2048 - int(s.ch3.freq)) * 2
			exp := 1 + (d-s.ch3.timer)/period
			s.ch3.timer += exp*period - d
			s.ch3.pos = (s.ch3.pos + exp) & 31
			s.mixStale = true
		}
	}
	if s.ch4.enabled {
		if d < s.ch4.timer {
			s.ch4.timer -= d
		} else {
			period := noisePeriod(s.nr43)
			exp := 1 + (d-s.ch4.timer)/period
			s.ch4.timer += exp*period - d
			// Clock the LFSR: the new bit is the XOR of bits 0
			// and 1, entering at bit 14 (and bit 6 in the
			// 7-bit width mode).
			for i := 0; i < exp; i++ {
				nb := (s.ch4.lfsr ^ (s.ch4.lfsr >> 1)) & 1
				s.ch4.lfsr = s.ch4.lfsr>>1 | nb<<14
				if s.nr43&0x08 != 0 {
					s.ch4.lfsr = s.ch4.lfsr&^(1<<6) | nb<<6
				}
			}
			s.mixStale = true
		}
	}
}

// channelOut returns the current per-channel DAC output in
// [0, 1], before panning and side volume.
func (s *APU) channelOut(ch int) float64 {
	switch ch {
	case 0:
		if !s.ch1.enabled || !s.ch1.dacOn {
			return 0
		}
		if dutyPatterns[s.ch1.duty]>>uint(7-s.ch1.dutyPos)&1 != 0 {
			return float64(s.ch1.vol) / 15
		}
		return 0
	case 1:
		if !s.ch2.enabled || !s.ch2.dacOn {
			return 0
		}
		if dutyPatterns[s.ch2.duty]>>uint(7-s.ch2.dutyPos)&1 != 0 {
			return float64(s.ch2.vol) / 15
		}
		return 0
	case 2:
		if !s.ch3.enabled || !s.ch3.dacOn {
			return 0
		}
		nib := s.waveRAM[s.ch3.pos/2]
		if s.ch3.pos%2 == 0 {
			nib >>= 4
		} else {
			nib &= 0x0F
		}
		switch s.ch3.volCode {
		case 1:
			return float64(nib) / 15
		case 2:
			return float64(nib) / 30
		case 3:
			return float64(nib) / 60
		}
		return 0
	case 3:
		if !s.ch4.enabled || !s.ch4.dacOn {
			return 0
		}
		if s.ch4.lfsr&1 == 0 {
			return float64(s.ch4.vol) / 15
		}
		return 0
	}
	return 0
}

// DebugChannelSample returns channel ch's output as a centered
// waveform in [-1, 1], for measurement tests: it is the raw DAC
// output with its midpoint subtracted, so zero crossings of the
// return value are the channel's cycles.
func (s *APU) DebugChannelSample(ch int) float64 {
	// Peak amplitude per channel is 1 in channelOut units; center
	// the [0, peak] waveform on 0.
	switch ch {
	case 0:
		return s.channelOut(0)*2 - float64(s.ch1.vol)/15
	case 1:
		return s.channelOut(1)*2 - float64(s.ch2.vol)/15
	case 2:
		return s.channelOut(2)*2 - 0.5
	case 3:
		return s.channelOut(3)*2 - float64(s.ch4.vol)/15
	}
	return 0
}

// DebugLength returns channel ch's length counter (test support).
func (s *APU) DebugLength(ch int) int {
	switch ch {
	case 0:
		return s.ch1.length
	case 1:
		return s.ch2.length
	case 2:
		return s.ch3.length
	case 3:
		return s.ch4.length
	}
	return 0
}

// DebugEnabled reports whether channel ch is currently on.
func (s *APU) DebugEnabled(ch int) bool {
	switch ch {
	case 0:
		return s.ch1.enabled
	case 1:
		return s.ch2.enabled
	case 2:
		return s.ch3.enabled
	case 3:
		return s.ch4.enabled
	}
	return false
}

// computeMix evaluates the current mixed stereo output from the
// four channels, panning, and side volumes.
func (s *APU) computeMix() (l, r float64) {
	if s.power {
		volL := float64(((s.nr50>>4)&7)+1) / 8
		volR := float64((s.nr50&7)+1) / 8
		for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
			o := s.channelOut(ch)
			if o == 0 {
				continue
			}
			if s.nr51>>(uint(ch)+4)&1 != 0 { // SO2: left
				l += o
			}
			if s.nr51>>uint(ch)&1 != 0 { // SO1: right
				r += o
			}
		}
		l *= volL / 4
		r *= volR / 4
	}
	return l, r
}

// mixSpan accumulates n dots of the cached mixed output and
// emits a finished sample whenever the phase accumulator
// crosses a whole output sample period. The box filter sums
// may span several calls; a sample is the mean of the dots
// accumulated since the previous emission.
func (s *APU) mixSpan(n int) {
	if s.mixStale {
		s.mixL, s.mixR = s.computeMix()
		s.mixStale = false
	}
	// Fast path: the span ends before the next sample
	// boundary, so the sums just grow by the span length.
	if s.phase+phaseInc*float64(n) < 1 {
		s.sumL += s.mixL * float64(n)
		s.sumR += s.mixR * float64(n)
		s.sumN += n
		s.phase += phaseInc * float64(n)
		return
	}
	for n > 0 {
		k := int(math.Ceil((1 - s.phase) / phaseInc))
		if k < 1 {
			k = 1
		}
		if k > n {
			k = n
		}
		s.sumL += s.mixL * float64(k)
		s.sumR += s.mixR * float64(k)
		s.sumN += k
		s.phase += phaseInc * float64(k)
		n -= k
		if s.phase >= 1 {
			s.phase -= 1
			m := float64(s.sumN)
			s.out = append(s.out,
				clamp16(s.sumL/m*32767), clamp16(s.sumR/m*32767))
			s.sumL, s.sumR, s.sumN = 0, 0, 0
		}
	}
}

func clamp16(v float64) int16 {
	if v > 32767 {
		return 32767
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return -32768
	}
	return int16(v)
}

// Produce drains up to n pending interleaved stereo samples. With
// n <= 0 it drains everything pending.
func (s *APU) Produce(n int) []int16 {
	if n <= 0 || n > len(s.out) {
		n = len(s.out)
	}
	out := make([]int16, n)
	copy(out, s.out[:n])
	s.out = append(s.out[:0], s.out[n:]...)
	return out
}

// Pending returns how many samples are waiting in the buffer.
func (s *APU) Pending() int { return len(s.out) / 2 }

// --- save states ---------------------------------------------------------

// SerializeSize is the fixed size of the APU state.
const SerializeSize = 512

const serializeVersion = 1

// Serialize writes the full APU state into buf: registers, wave
// RAM, every channel's dynamic state, the frame sequencer step,
// and the sample generator accumulators (they drive the render
// ledger, so a restore must resume them exactly).
func (s *APU) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("sound: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	for i := 0; i < SerializeSize; i++ {
		buf[i] = 0
	}
	buf[0] = serializeVersion
	buf[1] = s.nr10
	buf[2] = s.nr11
	buf[3] = s.nr12
	buf[4] = s.nr21
	buf[5] = s.nr22
	buf[6] = s.nr30
	buf[7] = s.nr32
	buf[8] = s.nr42
	buf[9] = s.nr43
	buf[10] = s.nr50
	buf[11] = s.nr51
	buf[12] = s.len1
	buf[13] = s.len2
	buf[14] = s.len3
	buf[15] = s.len4
	buf[16] = s.ctrl1
	buf[17] = s.ctrl2
	buf[18] = s.ctrl3
	buf[19] = s.ctrl4
	if s.power {
		buf[20] = 1
	}
	buf[21] = uint8(s.fsStep)
	copy(buf[22:38], s.waveRAM[:])

	off := 38
	putSquare := func(ch *square) {
		b := buf[off:]
		if ch.enabled {
			b[0] = 1
		}
		if ch.dacOn {
			b[1] = 1
		}
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[2:], ch.freq)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[4:], uint32(int32(ch.timer)))
		b[8] = uint8(ch.dutyPos)
		b[9] = uint8(ch.duty)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[10:], uint16(ch.length))
		if ch.lengthOn {
			b[12] = 1
		}
		b[13] = uint8(ch.vol)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[14:], uint16(ch.envTimer))
		b[16] = uint8(ch.envPace)
		if ch.envUp {
			b[17] = 1
		}
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[18:], ch.shadow)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[20:], uint16(ch.sweepTimer))
		b[22] = uint8(ch.sweepPace)
		b[23] = uint8(ch.sweepSlope)
		if ch.sweepNeg {
			b[24] = 1
		}
		if ch.sweepOn {
			b[25] = 1
		}
		off += 26
	}
	putSquare(&s.ch1)
	putSquare(&s.ch2)
	{
		b := buf[off:]
		if s.ch3.enabled {
			b[0] = 1
		}
		if s.ch3.dacOn {
			b[1] = 1
		}
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[2:], s.ch3.freq)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[4:], uint32(int32(s.ch3.timer)))
		b[8] = uint8(s.ch3.pos)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[9:], uint16(s.ch3.length))
		if s.ch3.lengthOn {
			b[11] = 1
		}
		b[12] = uint8(s.ch3.volCode)
		off += 13
	}
	{
		b := buf[off:]
		if s.ch4.enabled {
			b[0] = 1
		}
		if s.ch4.dacOn {
			b[1] = 1
		}
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[2:], s.ch4.lfsr)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[4:], uint32(int32(s.ch4.timer)))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[8:], uint16(s.ch4.length))
		if s.ch4.lengthOn {
			b[10] = 1
		}
		b[11] = uint8(s.ch4.vol)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[12:], uint16(s.ch4.envTimer))
		b[14] = uint8(s.ch4.envPace)
		if s.ch4.envUp {
			b[15] = 1
		}
		off += 16
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[off:], math.Float64bits(s.phase))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[off+8:], math.Float64bits(s.sumL))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[off+16:], math.Float64bits(s.sumR))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off+24:], uint32(s.sumN))
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (s *APU) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("sound: deserialize buffer too small")
	}
	if buf[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("sound: unsupported serialize version")
	}
	out := s.out[:0]
	*s = APU{out: out}
	s.nr10, s.nr11, s.nr12 = buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]
	s.nr21, s.nr22 = buf[4], buf[5]
	s.nr30, s.nr32 = buf[6], buf[7]
	s.nr42, s.nr43 = buf[8], buf[9]
	s.nr50, s.nr51 = buf[10], buf[11]
	s.len1, s.len2, s.len3, s.len4 = buf[12], buf[13], buf[14], buf[15]
	s.ctrl1, s.ctrl2, s.ctrl3, s.ctrl4 = buf[16], buf[17], buf[18], buf[19]
	s.power = buf[20] != 0
	s.fsStep = int(buf[21])
	copy(s.waveRAM[:], buf[22:38])
	// Re-derive the register-driven channel fields.
	s.ch1.sweepPace = int(s.nr10>>4) & 7
	s.ch1.sweepNeg = s.nr10&0x08 != 0
	s.ch1.sweepSlope = int(s.nr10) & 7
	s.ch1.duty = int(s.nr11 >> 6)
	s.ch2.duty = int(s.nr21 >> 6)
	s.ch1.dacOn = s.nr12&0xF8 != 0
	s.ch2.dacOn = s.nr22&0xF8 != 0
	s.ch4.dacOn = s.nr42&0xF8 != 0
	s.ch3.dacOn = s.nr30&0x80 != 0
	s.ch3.volCode = int(s.nr32>>5) & 3
	s.ch1.envUp = s.nr12&0x08 != 0
	s.ch1.envPace = int(s.nr12) & 7
	s.ch1.envInit = int(s.nr12 >> 4)
	s.ch2.envUp = s.nr22&0x08 != 0
	s.ch2.envPace = int(s.nr22) & 7
	s.ch2.envInit = int(s.nr22 >> 4)
	s.ch4.envUp = s.nr42&0x08 != 0
	s.ch4.envPace = int(s.nr42) & 7
	s.ch4.envInit = int(s.nr42 >> 4)

	off := 38
	getSquare := func(ch *square) {
		b := buf[off:]
		ch.enabled = b[0] != 0
		ch.dacOn = b[1] != 0
		ch.freq = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[2:])
		ch.timer = int(int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[4:])))
		ch.dutyPos = int(b[8])
		ch.duty = int(b[9])
		ch.length = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[10:]))
		ch.lengthOn = b[12] != 0
		ch.vol = int(b[13])
		ch.envTimer = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[14:]))
		ch.envPace = int(b[16])
		ch.envUp = b[17] != 0
		ch.shadow = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[18:])
		ch.sweepTimer = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[20:]))
		ch.sweepPace = int(b[22])
		ch.sweepSlope = int(b[23])
		ch.sweepNeg = b[24] != 0
		ch.sweepOn = b[25] != 0
		off += 26
	}
	getSquare(&s.ch1)
	getSquare(&s.ch2)
	{
		b := buf[off:]
		s.ch3.enabled = b[0] != 0
		s.ch3.dacOn = b[1] != 0
		s.ch3.freq = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[2:])
		s.ch3.timer = int(int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[4:])))
		s.ch3.pos = int(b[8])
		s.ch3.length = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[9:]))
		s.ch3.lengthOn = b[11] != 0
		s.ch3.volCode = int(b[12])
		off += 13
	}
	{
		b := buf[off:]
		s.ch4.enabled = b[0] != 0
		s.ch4.dacOn = b[1] != 0
		s.ch4.lfsr = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[2:])
		s.ch4.timer = int(int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[4:])))
		s.ch4.length = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[8:]))
		s.ch4.lengthOn = b[10] != 0
		s.ch4.vol = int(b[11])
		s.ch4.envTimer = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[12:]))
		s.ch4.envPace = int(b[14])
		s.ch4.envUp = b[15] != 0
		off += 16
	}
	s.phase = math.Float64frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[off:]))
	s.sumL = math.Float64frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[off+8:]))
	s.sumR = math.Float64frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[off+16:]))
	s.sumN = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off+24:]))
	s.mixStale = true
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/sound/sound_test.go ====================

package sound

import (
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// Register addresses in the APU's own map.
const (
	nr10 = 0xFF10
	nr11 = 0xFF11
	nr12 = 0xFF12
	nr13 = 0xFF13
	nr14 = 0xFF14
	nr21 = 0xFF16
	nr22 = 0xFF17
	nr23 = 0xFF18
	nr24 = 0xFF19
	nr30 = 0xFF1A
	nr31 = 0xFF1B
	nr32 = 0xFF1C
	nr33 = 0xFF1D
	nr34 = 0xFF1E
	nr41 = 0xFF20
	nr42 = 0xFF21
	nr43 = 0xFF22
	nr44 = 0xFF23
	nr50 = 0xFF24
	nr51 = 0xFF25
	nr52 = 0xFF26
)

// powered returns an APU with the master power on and full volume.
func powered() *APU {
	s := New()
	s.Write(nr52, 0x80)
	s.Write(nr50, 0x77)
	s.Write(nr51, 0xFF)
	return s
}

// freqReg converts a frequency in Hz to the 11-bit period
// register: tone = clock / (32 * (2048 - reg)).
func freqReg(hz float64) int {
	return 2048 - int(math.Round(4194304/(32*hz)))
}

// measureFreq estimates a channel's dominant frequency by counting
// rising zero crossings of its debug waveform over dots samples.
func measureFreq(s *APU, ch int, dots int) float64 {
	crossings := 0
	prev := s.DebugChannelSample(ch)
	for i := 0; i < dots; i++ {
		s.Tick(1)
		v := s.DebugChannelSample(ch)
		if prev <= 0 && v > 0 {
			crossings++
		}
		prev = v
	}
	return float64(crossings) * 4194304 / float64(dots)
}

// triggerSquare2 programs square channel 2 (index 1) and triggers it.
func triggerSquare2(s *APU, reg int, duty uint8) {
	s.Write(nr21, duty<<6)
	s.Write(nr22, 0xF0) // volume 15, envelope off
	s.Write(nr23, uint8(reg))
	s.Write(nr24, 0x80|uint8(reg>>8))
}

func TestSquareA4(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	reg := freqReg(440)
	triggerSquare2(s, reg, 2) // 50% duty
	if !s.DebugEnabled(1) {
		t.Fatal("square 2 not enabled after trigger")
	}
	got := measureFreq(s, 1, 4194304/4) // a quarter second
	cents := 1200 * math.Log2(got/440)
	if math.Abs(cents) > 25 {
		t.Fatalf("square A4 measured %.2f Hz (%.1f cents off)", got, cents)
	}
	t.Logf("square A4: reg=%d measured %.2f Hz (%.1f cents)", reg, got, cents)
}

func TestSweepMovesFrequency(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	reg := freqReg(128)
	// Square 1: sweep pace 1, up, slope 2: each sweep clock
	// replaces the register with reg + reg>>2. Sweep clocks
	// land on sequencer steps 2 and 6, so 8 sequencer steps
	// apply two calculations: 1024 -> 1280 -> 1600. (Each clock
	// also runs a second overflow-check calculation that does
	// not store; here it peaks at 2000, so the channel lives.)
	s.Write(nr10, 0x12)
	s.Write(nr11, 2<<6)
	s.Write(nr12, 0xF0)
	s.Write(nr13, uint8(reg))
	s.Write(nr14, 0x80|uint8(reg>>8))
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		s.StepFrameSequencer()
	}
	if !s.DebugEnabled(0) {
		t.Fatal("channel died during a non-overflowing sweep")
	}
	got := measureFreq(s, 0, 4194304/4)
	want := 4194304 / (32 * float64(2048-1600))
	if math.Abs(got-want)/want > 0.05 {
		t.Fatalf("swept square measured %.1f Hz, want about %.1f Hz", got, want)
	}
	t.Logf("sweep: 128 Hz swept to %.1f Hz (model %.1f)", got, want)
}

func TestSweepOverflowDisables(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	reg := 2000 // sweeping up by reg>>1 overflows 2047 at once
	s.Write(nr10, 0x11)
	s.Write(nr11, 2<<6)
	s.Write(nr12, 0xF0)
	s.Write(nr13, uint8(reg))
	s.Write(nr14, 0x80|uint8(reg>>8))
	if s.DebugEnabled(0) {
		t.Fatal("channel with an overflowing sweep should be disabled at trigger")
	}
}

func TestEnvelopeDecaysOnSchedule(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	s.Write(nr21, 2<<6)
	s.Write(nr22, 0xF1) // volume 15, decreasing, pace 1
	reg := freqReg(440)
	s.Write(nr23, uint8(reg))
	s.Write(nr24, 0x80|uint8(reg>>8))
	peak := func() float64 {
		m := 0.0
		for i := 0; i < 20000; i++ {
			s.Tick(1)
			if v := s.DebugChannelSample(1); math.Abs(v) > m {
				m = math.Abs(v)
			}
		}
		return m
	}
	p0 := peak() // volume 15: full scale
	// Envelope clocks land on sequencer step 7, one per 8 steps
	// at pace 1 the volume drops every envelope clock.
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		s.StepFrameSequencer()
	}
	p1 := peak() // volume 14
	for i := 0; i < 7*8; i++ {
		s.StepFrameSequencer()
	}
	p8 := peak() // volume 7 after 8 envelope clocks total
	if !(p0 > p1 && p1 > p8) {
		t.Fatalf("envelope did not decay stepwise: %.3f -> %.3f -> %.3f", p0, p1, p8)
	}
	if want := p0 * 7 / 15; math.Abs(p8-want) > 0.05*p0 {
		t.Fatalf("after 8 envelope clocks amplitude %.3f, want about %.3f (vol 7/15)", p8, want)
	}
}

func TestLengthCounterStopsChannel(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	// Length load 60 gives a counter of 4; length enabled.
	s.Write(nr21, 2<<6|60)
	s.Write(nr22, 0xF0)
	reg := freqReg(440)
	s.Write(nr23, uint8(reg))
	s.Write(nr24, 0xC0|uint8(reg>>8)) // trigger + length enable
	n0 := s.DebugLength(1)
	if n0 < 3 || n0 > 4 {
		t.Fatalf("length counter after trigger = %d, want 4 (or 3 if the enable edge clocked it)", n0)
	}
	drops := 0
	prev := n0
	disabledAt := -1
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		s.StepFrameSequencer()
		l := s.DebugLength(1)
		if l < prev {
			drops++
			prev = l
		}
		if !s.DebugEnabled(1) && disabledAt < 0 {
			disabledAt = drops
		}
	}
	if disabledAt != n0 {
		t.Fatalf("channel disabled after %d length clocks, want %d", disabledAt, n0)
	}
}

func TestWaveChannelPlaysTable(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	// Wave RAM: first half loud (0xF), second half silent.
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		s.Write(0xFF30+uint16(i), 0xFF)
	}
	for i := 8; i < 16; i++ {
		s.Write(0xFF30+uint16(i), 0x00)
	}
	s.Write(nr30, 0x80) // DAC on
	s.Write(nr31, 0)    // length 256
	s.Write(nr32, 0x20) // volume 100%
	reg := freqReg(220)
	s.Write(nr33, uint8(reg))
	s.Write(nr34, 0x80|uint8(reg>>8))
	if !s.DebugEnabled(2) {
		t.Fatal("wave channel not enabled after trigger")
	}
	// The wave position advances one sample per (2048-reg)*2
	// dots; over one full table cycle the output must show both
	// the loud half and the silent half.
	loud, silent := false, false
	period := (2048 - reg) * 2
	for i := 0; i < period*32; i++ {
		s.Tick(1)
		v := s.DebugChannelSample(2)
		if v > 0.2 {
			loud = true
		}
		if v < -0.2 {
			silent = true
		}
	}
	if !loud || !silent {
		t.Fatalf("wave output did not follow the table: loud=%v silent=%v", loud, silent)
	}
	// DMG quirk: wave RAM reads return 0xFF while the channel plays.
	if got := s.Read(0xFF30); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("wave RAM read while playing = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
}

func TestNoiseChannelRuns(t *testing.T) {
	run := func(wide bool) []float64 {
		s := powered()
		s.Write(nr41, 0)
		s.Write(nr42, 0xF0)
		v := uint8(0x03) // divisor 3, shift 0: period 64 dots-ish
		if wide {
			v |= 0x08
		}
		s.Write(nr43, v)
		s.Write(nr44, 0x80)
		if !s.DebugEnabled(3) {
			t.Fatal("noise channel not enabled after trigger")
		}
		out := make([]float64, 0, 4096)
		for i := 0; i < 4096; i++ {
			s.Tick(16)
			out = append(out, s.DebugChannelSample(3))
		}
		return out
	}
	a, b := run(false), run(true)
	pos, neg := false, false
	for _, v := range a {
		if v > 0 {
			pos = true
		}
		if v < 0 {
			neg = true
		}
	}
	if !pos || !neg {
		t.Fatal("noise output never toggles")
	}
	diff := false
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			diff = true
		}
	}
	if !diff {
		t.Fatal("7-bit LFSR mode produces the same stream as 15-bit")
	}
}

func TestPowerOffClearsRegistersKeepsLengths(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	s.Write(nr21, 2<<6|20) // length counter becomes 44
	s.Write(nr22, 0xF0)
	reg := freqReg(440)
	s.Write(nr23, uint8(reg))
	s.Write(nr24, 0x80|uint8(reg>>8))
	s.Write(nr52, 0x00) // power off
	if got := s.Read(nr52) & 0x0F; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("NR52 channel bits after power off = 0x%X, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := s.DebugLength(1); got != 44 {
		t.Fatalf("length counter after power off = %d, want 44 (lengths survive power cycles)", got)
	}
	// Register writes are ignored while off: an NR21 write now
	// must not move the length counter.
	s.Write(nr52, 0x00)
	s.Write(nr21, 63)
	if got := s.DebugLength(1); got != 44 {
		t.Fatalf("length counter after off-state NR21 write = %d, want 44 (write ignored)", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	s := powered()
	triggerSquare2(s, freqReg(330), 2)
	s.Write(nr10, 0x23)
	for i := 0; i < 5000; i++ {
		s.Tick(7)
	}
	buf := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := s.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	other := New()
	if err := other.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	buf2 := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := other.Serialize(buf2); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := range buf {
		if buf[i] != buf2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("state mismatch at byte %d: 0x%02X vs 0x%02X", i, buf[i], buf2[i])
		}
	}
	// Both APUs must now render identical samples when ticked
	// the same way. Drain first: the original still holds its
	// pre-serialize backlog, the restored one starts empty.
	_ = s.Produce(-1)
	_ = other.Produce(-1)
	for i := 0; i < 3000; i++ {
		s.Tick(7)
		other.Tick(7)
	}
	a := s.Produce(-1)
	b := other.Produce(-1)
	if len(a) != len(b) || len(a) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("produce lengths differ: %d vs %d", len(a), len(b))
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			t.Fatalf("rendered sample %d differs after restore: %d vs %d", i, a[i], b[i])
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gameboy/system/cgb_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// homebrew ROM paths (see homebrew/SOURCES.md): a DMG game and a
// GBC game.
func homebrewPath(name string) string {
	return filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "homebrew", name)
}

func TestCGBModeDetection(t *testing.T) {
	dmg, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("tobutobugirl.gb")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if dmg.CGB() {
		t.Error("DMG homebrew engaged CGB mode")
	}
	gbc, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !gbc.CGB() {
		t.Error("GBC homebrew did not engage CGB mode")
	}
	if gbc.compat {
		t.Error("CGB-flagged cart booted in compatibility mode")
	}
	forced, err := NewCGB(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("tobutobugirl.gb")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !forced.CGB() || !forced.compat {
		t.Error("forced CGB machine for a DMG cart is not in compatibility mode")
	}
}

func TestCGBBootRegisters(t *testing.T) {
	gbc, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r := gbc.CPU.Regs()
	if r.A != 0x11 || r.F != 0x80 || r.B != 0x00 || r.C != 0x00 ||
		r.D != 0xFF || r.E != 0x56 || r.H != 0x00 || r.L != 0x0D ||
		r.SP != 0xFFFE || r.PC != 0x0100 {
		t.Errorf("CGB boot registers = %+v", r)
	}
	compat, err := NewCGB(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("tobutobugirl.gb")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r = compat.CPU.Regs()
	if r.A != 0x11 || r.D != 0x00 || r.E != 0x08 || r.H != 0x00 || r.L != 0x7C {
		t.Errorf("compat boot registers = %+v", r)
	}
}

func TestPaletteAccess(t *testing.T) {
	s, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF40, 0x00) // LCD off: palette ports never blocked
	s.Write(0xFF68, 0x80) // BG palette index 0, auto-increment
	s.Write(0xFF69, 0x34)
	s.Write(0xFF69, 0x12)
	if got := s.Read(0xFF68); got != 0x40|0x82 {
		t.Errorf("BCPS after two auto-incremented writes = 0x%02X, want 0xC2", got)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF68, 0x80)
	if lo := s.Read(0xFF69); lo != 0x34 {
		t.Errorf("BGPD[0] = 0x%02X, want 0x34", lo)
	}
	if hi := s.Read(0xFF69); hi != 0x12 {
		t.Errorf("BGPD[1] (after read auto-increment) = 0x%02X, want 0x12", hi)
	}
}

func TestVRAMBanking(t *testing.T) {
	s, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF40, 0x00) // LCD off so VRAM is always reachable
	s.Write(0xFF4F, 0)
	s.Write(0x8000, 0x11)
	s.Write(0xFF4F, 1)
	if got := s.Read(0x8000); got != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("bank 1 VRAM starts 0x%02X, want 0x00", got)
	}
	s.Write(0x8000, 0x22)
	s.Write(0xFF4F, 0)
	if got := s.Read(0x8000); got != 0x11 {
		t.Errorf("bank 0 VRAM = 0x%02X, want 0x11", got)
	}
	if got := s.Read(0xFF4F); got != 0xFE {
		t.Errorf("VBK readback = 0x%02X, want 0xFE", got)
	}
}

func TestWRAMBanking(t *testing.T) {
	s, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF70, 2)
	s.Write(0xD000, 0x33)
	s.Write(0xFF70, 3)
	if got := s.Read(0xD000); got != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("bank 3 WRAM starts 0x%02X, want 0x00", got)
	}
	s.Write(0xD000, 0x44)
	s.Write(0xFF70, 2)
	if got := s.Read(0xD000); got != 0x33 {
		t.Errorf("bank 2 WRAM = 0x%02X, want 0x33", got)
	}
	// SVBK 0 selects bank 1; the C000 fixed window never banks.
	s.Write(0xFF70, 0)
	s.Write(0xD000, 0x55)
	s.Write(0xFF70, 1)
	if got := s.Read(0xD000); got != 0x55 {
		t.Errorf("bank 1 via SVBK 0 = 0x%02X, want 0x55", got)
	}
	if got := s.Read(0xFF70); got != 0xF9 {
		t.Errorf("SVBK readback = 0x%02X, want 0xF9", got)
	}
	s.Write(0xC000, 0x66)
	if got := s.Read(0xE000); got != 0x66 {
		t.Errorf("echo of C000 = 0x%02X, want 0x66", got)
	}
}

// spinROM builds a minimal ROM image whose entry code arms KEY1,
// executes STOP, then spins: enough to drive the speed switch
// through the real bus.
func spinROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x8000)
	code := []byte{
		0x3E, 0x01, // LD A,1
		0xE0, 0x4D, // LDH (FF4D),A : arm the speed switch
		0x10, 0x00, // STOP
		0x18, 0xFE, // JR -2 (spin)
	}
	copy(rom[0x100:], code)
	return rom
}

func TestSpeedSwitch(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := New(spinROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// The spin ROM is DMG-flagged on DMG hardware: KEY1 is absent
	// and STOP is a plain stop.
	if got := m.Read(0xFF4D); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("DMG KEY1 read = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	c, err := NewCGB(spinROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Forced CGB + DMG cart = compatibility mode: KEY1 locks too.
	if got := c.Read(0xFF4D); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("compat KEY1 read = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	// Full CGB mode: use a CGB-flagged header on the spin ROM.
	rom := spinROM()
	rom[0x143] = 0x80
	g, err := New(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := g.Read(0xFF4D); got != 0x7E {
		t.Errorf("KEY1 idle read = 0x%02X, want 0x7E", got)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 10 && g.Speed() == 1; i++ {
		g.Step()
	}
	if g.Speed() != 2 {
		t.Fatal("STOP with KEY1 armed did not switch to double speed")
	}
	if got := g.Read(0xFF4D); got != 0xFE {
		t.Errorf("KEY1 in double speed = 0x%02X, want 0xFE", got)
	}
	// Device dots per M-cycle: a plain spin loop on a fresh
	// machine (never switches) against the switched machine.
	plain := spinROM()
	plain[0x100] = 0x18 // JR -2 from the entry point, no KEY1 code
	plain[0x101] = 0xFE
	plain[0x143] = 0x80
	n, err := New(plain)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	before := n.Cycles()
	n.RunMCycles(102)
	normalDots := n.Cycles() - before
	before = g.Cycles()
	g.RunMCycles(102)
	doubleDots := g.Cycles() - before
	if normalDots != 2*doubleDots {
		t.Errorf("dots per 102 M-cycles: normal %d, double %d (want exactly half)", normalDots, doubleDots)
	}
}

func TestHDMAGeneralPurpose(t *testing.T) {
	s, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF40, 0x00) // LCD off
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		s.Write(0xC000+uint16(i), uint8(0xA0+i))
	}
	s.Write(0xFF51, 0xC0) // source 0xC000
	s.Write(0xFF52, 0x00)
	s.Write(0xFF53, 0x00) // destination offset 0
	s.Write(0xFF54, 0x00)
	s.Write(0xFF55, 0x01) // general-purpose, 2 blocks
	if got := s.Read(0xFF55); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("HDMA5 after GP completion = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF4F, 0)
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if got := s.Read(0x8000 + uint16(i)); got != uint8(0xA0+i) {
			t.Fatalf("VRAM[%d] = 0x%02X, want 0x%02X", i, got, 0xA0+i)
		}
	}
}

func TestHDMAHBlankAndCancel(t *testing.T) {
	s, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		s.Write(0xC000+uint16(i), uint8(0x50+i))
	}
	setRegs := func() {
		s.Write(0xFF51, 0xC0)
		s.Write(0xFF52, 0x00)
		s.Write(0xFF53, 0x00)
		s.Write(0xFF54, 0x00)
	}
	setRegs()
	s.Write(0xFF55, 0x83) // HBlank mode, 4 blocks
	if got := s.Read(0xFF55); got != 0x03 {
		t.Errorf("HDMA5 while HBlank transfer runs = 0x%02X, want 0x03", got)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF55, 0x00) // cancel
	if got := s.Read(0xFF55); got != 0x83 {
		t.Errorf("HDMA5 after cancel = 0x%02X, want 0x83", got)
	}
	setRegs()
	s.Write(0xFF55, 0x81) // HBlank mode, 2 blocks
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := s.Read(0xFF55); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("HDMA5 after HBlank completion = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	s.Write(0xFF40, 0x00) // LCD off to inspect VRAM
	s.Write(0xFF4F, 0)
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if got := s.Read(0x8000 + uint16(i)); got != uint8(0x50+i) {
			t.Fatalf("VRAM[%d] = 0x%02X, want 0x%02X", i, got, 0x50+i)
		}
	}
}

func TestCompatLocks(t *testing.T) {
	s, err := NewCGB(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("tobutobugirl.gb")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, chk := range []struct {
		addr uint16
		want uint8
	}{
		{0xFF4D, 0xFF}, // KEY1
		{0xFF51, 0xFF}, // HDMA
		{0xFF55, 0xFF},
		{0xFF70, 0xFF}, // SVBK
		{0xFF74, 0xFF},
		{0xFF69, 0xFF}, // BGPD
		{0xFF6C, 0xFF}, // OPRI
	} {
		if got := s.Read(chk.addr); got != chk.want {
			t.Errorf("compat read 0x%04X = 0x%02X, want 0x%02X", chk.addr, got, chk.want)
		}
	}
	// The index registers still respond in compatibility mode.
	s.Write(0xFF68, 0x85)
	if got := s.Read(0xFF68); got != 0x40|0x85 {
		t.Errorf("compat BCPS = 0x%02X, want 0xC5", got)
	}
	// FF72 storage is not part of the lock set.
	s.Write(0xFF72, 0x5A)
	if got := s.Read(0xFF72); got != 0x5A {
		t.Errorf("compat FF72 = 0x%02X, want 0x5A", got)
	}
}

func TestCGBSaveStateDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	s, err := New(loadROM(t, homebrewPath("ucity.gbc")))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Logf("CGB whole-machine save state: %d bytes", s.SerializeSize())
	for i := 0; i < 120; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
	}
	_ = s.AudioBuffer() // drain the title-screen audio
	state := make([]byte, s.SerializeSize())
	if err := s.Serialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var wantAudio []int16
	for i := 0; i < 45; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
		wantAudio = append(wantAudio, s.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	wantFrame := hashFrame(s)
	if err := s.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var gotAudio []int16
	for i := 0; i < 45; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
		gotAudio = append(gotAudio, s.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	if got := hashFrame(s); got != wantFrame {
		t.Errorf("frame after restore = 0x%X, want 0x%X", got, wantFrame)
	}
	if len(gotAudio) != len(wantAudio) || len(gotAudio) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("audio after restore: %d samples, want %d", len(gotAudio), len(wantAudio))
	}
	for i := range wantAudio {
		if gotAudio[i] != wantAudio[i] {
			t.Fatalf("audio sample %d after restore differs", i)
		}
	}
}
