				quo.Sub(quo, big.NewInt(1))
			} else {
				quo.Add(quo, big.NewInt(1))
			}
			fr = true
		}
	}
	return quo, inexact, fr
}

// execMTFSB implements mtfsb0 and mtfsb1. The RN bits (30
// and 31 in PowerPC numbering) are never altered, per the
// manual. No other restriction on mtfsb1 could be verified
// in the Gekko manual, so all other bits are written
// literally; the write is a software move and does not
// recompute the summary bits.
func (c *CPU) execMTFSB(w uint32, set bool) {
	crbD := f1(w)
	if crbD == 30 || crbD == 31 {
		return
	}
	mask := uint32(1) << uint(31-crbD)
	if set {
		c.FPSCR |= mask
	} else {
		c.FPSCR &^= mask
	}
	if w&1 != 0 {
		c.recordCR1()
	}
}

// execMTFSF implements mtfsf: the FM field (instruction
// bits 6..13 in PowerPC numbering, with bit 6 the L bit)
// selects which FPSCR nibbles are copied from the low word
// of frB. FM's most significant bit (instruction bit 7)
// corresponds to FPSCR field 0. With L set, the whole
// register is copied regardless of FM.
func (c *CPU) execMTFSF(w uint32) {
	b := f3(w)
	src := uint32(c.FPR[b])
	l := (w >> 25) & 1
	fm := (w >> 17) & 0xFF
	if l != 0 {
		c.FPSCR = src
	} else {
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if fm&(0x80>>uint(i)) != 0 {
				shift := uint(28 - 4*i)
				c.FPSCR = c.FPSCR&^(0xF<<shift) | src&(0xF<<shift)
			}
		}
	}
	if w&1 != 0 {
		c.recordCR1()
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/chips/gekko/fp_test.go ====================

package gekko

import (
	"math"
	"math/rand"
	"testing"
)

// GCN-2 scalar FPU gates. Instruction encoders mirror the
// helpers in gekko_test.go (ins builds an X/A form word).

func fpCPU() (*CPU, *ramBus) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.MSR |= MSRFP
	c.MSR &^= MSRIP
	return c, bus
}

// fa builds an A-form word for opcodes 59 and 63:
// frD, frA, frB field, frC field, 5-bit XO, Rc.
func fa(op, d, a, b, cc, xo5, rc int) uint32 {
	return uint32(op)<<26 | uint32(d)<<21 | uint32(a)<<16 |
		uint32(b)<<11 | uint32(cc)<<6 | uint32(xo5)<<1 | uint32(rc)
}

// fx63 builds an opcode 63 X-form word: frD (or cr field in
// the top bits), frA, frB, 10-bit XO, Rc.
func fx63(d, a, b, xo10, rc int) uint32 {
	return 63<<26 | uint32(d)<<21 | uint32(a)<<16 |
		uint32(b)<<11 | uint32(xo10)<<1 | uint32(rc)
}

func runAt(c *CPU, bus *ramBus, addr uint32, words ...uint32) {
	prog(c, bus, addr, words...)
	steps(c, len(words))
}

func dbl(f float64) uint64 { return math.Float64bits(f) }

func TestFPRoundingModesFRSP(t *testing.T) {
	// x sits above the midpoint between the singles 1.0
	// and 1+2^-23, inexactly.
	x := 1 + math.Ldexp(1, -24) + math.Ldexp(1, -26)
	// want holds the single bits each mode must choose.
	cases := []struct {
		rn   uint32
		want uint32
	}{
		{0, 0x3F800001}, // nearest: up
		{1, 0x3F800000}, // toward zero: down
		{2, 0x3F800001}, // toward +Inf: up
		{3, 0x3F800000}, // toward -Inf: down
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		c, bus := fpCPU()
		c.FPSCR = tc.rn
		c.FPR[1] = dbl(x)
		runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2, 0, 1, 12, 0)) // frsp f2, f1
		if got := c.FPR[2]; got != dbl(float64(math.Float32frombits(tc.want))) {
			t.Fatalf("rn=%d: frsp=%#x, want single %#x widened", tc.rn, got, tc.want)
		}
		if c.FPSCR&fpscrFI == 0 || c.FPSCR&fpscrXX == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("rn=%d: frsp of an inexact value must set FI and XX, FPSCR=%#x", tc.rn, c.FPSCR)
		}
	}
	// The exact midpoint ties to even under RN: 1.0 wins.
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(1 + math.Ldexp(1, -24))
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2, 0, 1, 12, 0))
	if c.FPR[2] != dbl(1.0) {
		t.Fatalf("tie: frsp=%v, want 1.0", math.Float64frombits(c.FPR[2]))
	}
	// Negative mirror: -x under RP goes toward +Inf (down
	// in magnitude), under RM away.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPSCR = 2 // RP
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(-x)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2, 0, 1, 12, 0))
	if got := c.FPR[2]; got != dbl(-1.0) {
		t.Fatalf("RP negative: frsp=%#x, want -1.0", got)
	}
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPSCR = 3 // RM
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(-x)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2, 0, 1, 12, 0))
	if got := c.FPR[2]; got != dbl(float64(math.Float32frombits(0xBF800001))) {
		t.Fatalf("RM negative: frsp=%#x, want single 0xBF800001 widened", got)
	}
}

func TestFCTIWPatterns(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		in   uint64
		z    bool // use fctiwz instead of fctiw
		want uint64
	}{
		{"+Inf", dbl(math.Inf(1)), false, 0x000000007fffffff},
		{"-Inf", dbl(math.Inf(-1)), false, 0xffffffff80000000},
		{"NaN", qnanDoubleBits, false, 0xffffffff80000000},
		{"over range", dbl(3e9), false, 0x000000007fffffff},
		{"under range", dbl(-3e9), false, 0xffffffff80000000},
		{"fctiwz 42.9", dbl(42.9), true, 42},
		{"fctiwz -42.9", dbl(-42.9), true, 0xffffffffffffffd6},
		{"fctiw RN 2.5 ties even", dbl(2.5), false, 2},
		{"fctiw RN 3.5 ties even", dbl(3.5), false, 4},
		{"fctiw RN -2.5 ties even", dbl(-2.5), false, 0xfffffffffffffffe},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		c, bus := fpCPU()
		c.FPR[1] = tc.in
		xo := 14
		if tc.z {
			xo = 15
		}
		runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2, 0, 1, xo, 0))
		if c.FPR[2] != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("%s: fctiw result=%#x, want %#x", tc.name, c.FPR[2], tc.want)
		}
	}
	// Out-of-range conversion raises VXCVI.
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(math.Inf(1))
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2, 0, 1, 14, 0))
	if c.FPSCR&fpscrVXCVI == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fctiw +Inf: VXCVI not set, FPSCR=%#x", c.FPSCR)
	}
}

func TestFMADDSingleRounding(t *testing.T) {
	// Pinned case found by exact rational search: with
	// these operands the separately rounded product loses
	// one ulp that the fused operation keeps.
	a := uint64(0xbfb4aedac30e6d50)
	b := uint64(0xbfdae86fa12d0764)
	add := uint64(0x3ef688994d13d958)
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1], c.FPR[2], c.FPR[3] = a, add, b
	// fmul f4, f1, f3 then fadd f5, f4, f2 (the C operand
	// of fmul is the field at bits 21..25, here register 3).
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		fa(63, 4, 1, 0, 3, 25, 0), // fmul f4, f1, f3
		fa(63, 5, 4, 2, 0, 21, 0), // fadd f5, f4, f2
		fa(63, 6, 1, 2, 3, 29, 0), // fmadd f6, f1, f2, f3
	)
	if c.FPR[5] != 0x3fa1671eaa5f2fce {
		t.Fatalf("separate mul+add: got %#x, want 0x3fa1671eaa5f2fce", c.FPR[5])
	}
	if c.FPR[6] != 0x3fa1671eaa5f2fcf {
		t.Fatalf("fmadd: got %#x, want 0x3fa1671eaa5f2fcf (one ulp above separate)", c.FPR[6])
	}
}

func TestFCMPUNaN(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = qnanDoubleBits
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(1.0)
	// fcmpu cr2, f1, f2 (cr field is in the top of the
	// frD field: crfD<<2).
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2<<2, 1, 2, 0, 0))
	if nib := (c.CR >> 20) & 0xF; nib != 1 { // cr2 occupies value bits 23..20
		t.Fatalf("fcmpu NaN: CR field=%04b, want 0001 (unordered)", nib)
	}
	if fpcc := (c.FPSCR >> 12) & 0xF; fpcc != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("fcmpu NaN: FPCC=%04b, want 0001", fpcc)
	}
	if c.FPSCR&(fpscrVXSNAN|fpscrVXVC) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fcmpu quiet NaN: no invalid bit expected, FPSCR=%#x", c.FPSCR)
	}
	// fcmpo with a quiet NaN raises VXVC.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = qnanDoubleBits
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(1.0)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(2<<2, 1, 2, 32, 0))
	if c.FPSCR&fpscrVXVC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fcmpo quiet NaN: VXVC not set, FPSCR=%#x", c.FPSCR)
	}
	// A signaling NaN raises VXSNAN for both forms.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = 0x7FF0000000000001
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(1.0)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(0, 1, 2, 0, 0))
	if c.FPSCR&fpscrVXSNAN == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fcmpu signaling NaN: VXSNAN not set, FPSCR=%#x", c.FPSCR)
	}
	// Ordinary less-than: CR nibble 1000 and FPCC matches.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(1.0)
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(2.0)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fx63(0, 1, 2, 0, 0))
	if nib := (c.CR >> 28) & 0xF; nib != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("fcmpu 1<2: CR0=%04b, want 1000", nib)
	}
	if fpcc := (c.FPSCR >> 12) & 0xF; fpcc != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("fcmpu 1<2: FPCC=%04b, want 1000", fpcc)
	}
}

func TestMTFSB1MFFS(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.FPSCR = 2 // RN = toward +Inf; mtfsb must never touch RN
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		fx63(6, 0, 0, 38, 0),  // mtfsb1 6 (the XX bit)
		fx63(3, 0, 0, 583, 0), // mffs f3
	)
	if c.FPR[3]&uint64(fpscrXX) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mffs after mtfsb1: XX bit missing, FPSCR copy=%#x", c.FPR[3])
	}
	if c.FPSCR&fpscrRNMask != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("RN changed by mtfsb1, FPSCR=%#x", c.FPSCR)
	}
	// mtfsb1 on bit 31 and mtfsb0 on bit 30 must leave RN
	// exactly as it was.
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100,
		fx63(31, 0, 0, 38, 0), // mtfsb1 31: ignored
		fx63(30, 0, 0, 70, 0), // mtfsb0 30: ignored
	)
	if c.FPSCR&fpscrRNMask != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("mtfsb touched RN: FPSCR=%#x", c.FPSCR)
	}
	// mtfsfi writes an immediate into one FPSCR field.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, 63<<26|uint32(7<<2)<<21|3<<12|134<<1) // mtfsfi cr7, 3
	if c.FPSCR&fpscrRNMask != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("mtfsfi RN: FPSCR=%#x, want RN=3", c.FPSCR)
	}
	// mtfsf with FM selecting only field 7 copies the low
	// nibble from frB and leaves the rest alone.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPSCR = 0xA0000000
	c.FPR[5] = 0x00000001
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, 63<<26|uint32(0x01)<<17|5<<11|711<<1) // mtfsf fm=0x01, f5
	if c.FPSCR != 0xA0000001 {
		t.Fatalf("mtfsf field 7: FPSCR=%#x, want 0xa0000001", c.FPSCR)
	}
}

func TestFPArithmeticBasics(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(1.5)
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(2.25)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		fa(63, 3, 1, 2, 0, 21, 0), // fadd f3, f1, f2
		fa(63, 4, 2, 1, 0, 20, 0), // fsub f4, f2, f1
		fa(63, 5, 1, 0, 2, 25, 0), // fmul f5, f1, f2
		fa(63, 6, 2, 1, 0, 18, 0), // fdiv f6, f2, f1
	)
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(3.75) || c.FPR[4] != dbl(0.75) ||
		c.FPR[5] != dbl(3.375) || c.FPR[6] != dbl(1.5) {
		t.Fatalf("basic ops: %v %v %v %v", c.FPR[3], c.FPR[4], c.FPR[5], c.FPR[6])
	}
	// fsqrt is correctly rounded.
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(2.0)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100, fa(63, 3, 0, 1, 0, 22, 0)) // fsqrt f3, f1
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(math.Sqrt(2)) {
		t.Fatalf("fsqrt 2: got %#x, want %#x", c.FPR[3], dbl(math.Sqrt(2)))
	}
	// Overflow sets OX and yields Inf under RN.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(math.MaxFloat64)
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(math.MaxFloat64)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fa(63, 3, 1, 2, 0, 21, 0))
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(math.Inf(1)) || c.FPSCR&fpscrOX == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("overflow: res=%#x FPSCR=%#x", c.FPR[3], c.FPSCR)
	}
	// 1/0 yields +Inf and ZX, with no invalid bit.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(1)
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(0)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fa(63, 3, 1, 2, 0, 18, 0))
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(math.Inf(1)) || c.FPSCR&fpscrZX == 0 || c.FPSCR&fpscrVX != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("1/0: res=%#x FPSCR=%#x", c.FPR[3], c.FPSCR)
	}
	// 0/0 is invalid VXZDZ with a quiet NaN result.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(0)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fa(63, 3, 1, 2, 0, 18, 0))
	if c.FPR[3] != qnanDoubleBits || c.FPSCR&fpscrVXZDZ == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("0/0: res=%#x FPSCR=%#x", c.FPR[3], c.FPSCR)
	}
	// Rc on arithmetic writes CR1 from FPSCR bits 0..3:
	// an overflowing fadd. leaves FX and OX set, so CR1 is
	// 1001 (FEX stays clear, enables are off).
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(math.MaxFloat64)
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(math.MaxFloat64)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fa(63, 3, 1, 2, 0, 21, 1))
	if nib := (c.CR >> 24) & 0xF; nib != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("fadd. CR1=%04b, want 1001", nib)
	}
	// Singles: fadds computes on singles and stores the
	// result widened to a double.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(float64(float32(0.1)))
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(float64(float32(0.2)))
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, fa(59, 3, 1, 2, 0, 21, 0))
	want := float32(0.1) + float32(0.2)
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(float64(want)) {
		t.Fatalf("fadds: got %#x, want single %#x widened", c.FPR[3], math.Float32bits(want))
	}
}

func TestFPMovesAndSel(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(-2.5)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		fx63(2, 0, 1, 264, 0), // fabs f2, f1
		fx63(3, 0, 1, 40, 0),  // fneg f3, f1
		fx63(4, 0, 1, 136, 0), // fnabs f4, f1
		fx63(5, 0, 1, 72, 0),  // fmr f5, f1
	)
	if c.FPR[2] != dbl(2.5) || c.FPR[3] != dbl(2.5) ||
		c.FPR[4] != dbl(-2.5) || c.FPR[5] != dbl(-2.5) {
		t.Fatalf("moves: %v %v %v %v", c.FPR[2], c.FPR[3], c.FPR[4], c.FPR[5])
	}
	// fsel: frA >= 0 picks frC, negative and NaN pick frB.
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(0.0)
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(111)
	c.FPR[3] = dbl(222)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100, fa(63, 4, 1, 2, 3, 23, 0)) // fsel f4, f1, f2, f3
	if c.FPR[4] != dbl(222) {
		t.Fatalf("fsel +0: got %v, want frC 222", math.Float64frombits(c.FPR[4]))
	}
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(-0.5)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1200, fa(63, 4, 1, 2, 3, 23, 0))
	if c.FPR[4] != dbl(111) {
		t.Fatalf("fsel negative: got %v, want frB 111", math.Float64frombits(c.FPR[4]))
	}
	c.FPR[1] = qnanDoubleBits
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1300, fa(63, 4, 1, 2, 3, 23, 0))
	if c.FPR[4] != dbl(111) {
		t.Fatalf("fsel NaN: got %v, want frB 111", math.Float64frombits(c.FPR[4]))
	}
	// fres and frsqrte are exact here: 1/4 and 1/sqrt(4).
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(float64(float32(4)))
	c.FPR[2] = dbl(4)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		fa(59, 3, 0, 1, 0, 24, 0), // fres f3, f1 (single)
		fa(63, 4, 0, 2, 0, 26, 0), // frsqrte f4, f2
	)
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(0.25) || c.FPR[4] != dbl(0.5) {
		t.Fatalf("estimates: fres=%v frsqrte=%v", math.Float64frombits(c.FPR[3]), math.Float64frombits(c.FPR[4]))
	}
}

func TestFPLoadStoreRoundTrips(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	// stfd then lfd.
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(3.141592653589793)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		insD(54, 1, 4, 0), // stfd f1, 0(r4)
		insD(50, 2, 4, 0), // lfd f2, 0(r4)
	)
	if c.FPR[2] != c.FPR[1] {
		t.Fatalf("lfd/stfd: got %#x, want %#x", c.FPR[2], c.FPR[1])
	}
	// lfs widens a single; stfs rounds a double back.
	bus.Write32(0x2100, 0x3FC00000) // 1.5f
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100,
		insD(48, 3, 4, 0x100), // lfs f3, 0x100(r4)
	)
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(1.5) {
		t.Fatalf("lfs: got %#x, want 1.5 widened", c.FPR[3])
	}
	c.FPR[5] = dbl(2.5)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1200,
		insD(52, 5, 4, 0x110), // stfs f5, 0x110(r4)
	)
	if got := bus.Read32(0x2110); got != 0x40200000 {
		t.Fatalf("stfs: memory=%#x, want 0x40200000 (2.5f)", got)
	}
	// Update forms write EA back to rA.
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2200
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(-7.25)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1300,
		insD(55, 1, 4, 8), // stfdu f1, 8(r4)
	)
	if c.GPR[4] != 0x2208 {
		t.Fatalf("stfdu: r4=%#x, want 0x2208", c.GPR[4])
	}
	c.GPR[4] = 0x21F8
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1400,
		insD(51, 6, 4, 0x10), // lfdu f6, 0x10(r4) -> 0x2208
	)
	if c.GPR[4] != 0x2208 || c.FPR[6] != dbl(-7.25) {
		t.Fatalf("lfdu: r4=%#x f6=%#x", c.GPR[4], c.FPR[6])
	}
	// Indexed forms: stfdx/lfdx, stfsx/lfsx, stfiwx.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2300
	c.GPR[5] = 0x10
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(9.5)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		ins(31, 1, 4, 5, 727, false), // stfdx f1, r4, r5
		ins(31, 3, 4, 5, 599, false), // lfdx f3, r4, r5
		ins(31, 1, 4, 5, 663, false), // stfsx f1, r4, r5
		ins(31, 2, 4, 5, 535, false), // lfsx f2, r4, r5
	)
	if c.FPR[3] != dbl(9.5) {
		t.Fatalf("lfdx after stfdx: got %#x, want 9.5", c.FPR[3])
	}
	if c.FPR[2] != dbl(9.5) {
		t.Fatalf("lfsx after stfsx: got %#x, want 9.5 widened", c.FPR[2])
	}
	negThree := int64(-3)
	c.FPR[7] = uint64(negThree)                         // low word is the integer image
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100, ins(31, 7, 4, 5, 983, false)) // stfiwx f7, r4, r5
	if got := bus.Read32(0x2310); got != 0xFFFFFFFD {
		t.Fatalf("stfiwx: memory=%#x, want 0xfffffffd", got)
	}
	// Little-endian double round trip through stfd/lfd. In
	// this core LE mode also fetches instructions
	// byte-swapped (see TestLittleEndianAccess), so the
	// two program words are stored swapped.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.MSR |= MSRLE
	c.FPR[1] = dbl(1.25)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2400
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		insD(54, 1, 4, 0),
		insD(50, 2, 4, 0),
	)
	bus.Write32(0x1000, swap32(insD(54, 1, 4, 0)))
	bus.Write32(0x1004, swap32(insD(50, 2, 4, 0)))
	c.PC = 0x1000
	steps(c, 2)
	if c.FPR[2] != c.FPR[1] {
		t.Fatalf("LE lfd/stfd: got %#x, want %#x", c.FPR[2], c.FPR[1])
	}
}

func TestFPUnavailableWhenFPOff(t *testing.T) {
	// An FP load with MSR[FP]=0.
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, insD(50, 1, 4, 0)) // lfd f1, 0(r4)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecFPUnavail {
		t.Fatalf("lfd with FP off: PC=%#x, want FP unavailable vector", c.PC)
	}
	// A paired single op with MSR[FP]=0.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, fa(4, 3, 1, 2, 0, 21, 0)) // ps_add
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecFPUnavail {
		t.Fatalf("ps_add with FP off: PC=%#x, want FP unavailable vector", c.PC)
	}
}

func TestFPSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	if SerializeSize != 4688+36 {
		t.Fatalf("SerializeSize=%d, want 4724 (GCN-1 4688 + FPSCR 4 + GQR 32)", SerializeSize)
	}
	c, _ := fpCPU()
	c.FPSCR = 0x1E2C4800
	c.SetSPR(SPRGQR0+0, 0xDEADBEEF)
	c.SetSPR(SPRGQR0+7, 0x01234567)
	if got := c.GetSPR(SPRGQR0Alt + 0); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("GQR alias 912: got %#x, want 0xdeadbeef", got)
	}
	c.setPair(9, 0x3FC00000, 0xC0200000) // (1.5, -2.5)
	state := c.Serialize()
	c2, _ := fpCPU()
	if err := c2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if c2.FPSCR != c.FPSCR || c2.GQR != c.GQR || c2.FPR[9] != c.FPR[9] {
		t.Fatalf("round trip: FPSCR %#x/%#x GQR %v/%v FPR9 %#x/%#x",
			c2.FPSCR, c.FPSCR, c2.GQR, c.GQR, c2.FPR[9], c.FPR[9])
	}
	// Reset clears FPSCR and the GQRs.
	c2.Reset()
	if c2.FPSCR != 0 || c2.GQR != [8]uint32{} {
		t.Fatalf("reset: FPSCR=%#x GQR=%v", c2.FPSCR, c2.GQR)
	}
}

func TestFPRandomDifferential(t *testing.T) {
	// Differential check of the exact rational engine
	// against the host IEEE operations, which are
	// correctly rounded under round-to-nearest: fadd,
	// fmul, fdiv, fmadd (against math.FMA), and the single
	// forms fadds and fmuls. Bit patterns are filtered to
	// finite values.
	rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(0xC0FFEE))
	finite := func() uint64 {
		for {
			b := rng.Uint64()
			if classDouble(b) != classQNaN && classDouble(b) != classSNaN &&
				!classDouble(b).isInf() {
				return b
			}
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 120; i++ {
		a, b, cc := finite(), finite(), finite()
		fa64, fb64, fc64 := math.Float64frombits(a), math.Float64frombits(b), math.Float64frombits(cc)
		c, bus := fpCPU()
		c.FPR[1], c.FPR[2], c.FPR[3] = a, b, cc
		runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
			fa(63, 4, 1, 2, 0, 21, 0), // fadd f4, f1, f2
			fa(63, 5, 1, 0, 2, 25, 0), // fmul f5, f1, f2
			fa(63, 6, 1, 2, 0, 18, 0), // fdiv f6, f1, f2
			fa(63, 7, 1, 2, 3, 29, 0), // fmadd f7, f1, f2, f3
		)
		if want := fa64 + fb64; c.FPR[4] != dbl(want) {
			t.Fatalf("iter %d fadd: got %#x want %#x (a=%#x b=%#x)", i, c.FPR[4], dbl(want), a, b)
		}
		if want := fa64 * fb64; c.FPR[5] != dbl(want) {
			t.Fatalf("iter %d fmul: got %#x want %#x (a=%#x b=%#x)", i, c.FPR[5], dbl(want), a, b)
		}
		if fb64 != 0 {
			if want := fa64 / fb64; c.FPR[6] != dbl(want) {
				t.Fatalf("iter %d fdiv: got %#x want %#x (a=%#x b=%#x)", i, c.FPR[6], dbl(want), a, b)
			}
		}
		if want := math.FMA(fa64, fc64, fb64); c.FPR[7] != dbl(want) {
			t.Fatalf("iter %d fmadd: got %#x want %#x (a=%#x b=%#x c=%#x)", i, c.FPR[7], dbl(want), a, b, cc)
		}
		// Singles: operands are the float32 conversions
		// of the doubles, skipping patterns whose
		// conversion lands on Inf or NaN (the host NaN
		// sign there is not the architected canonical
		// result this core produces).
		sa := float32(fa64)
		sb := float32(fb64)
		if math.IsInf(float64(sa), 0) || math.IsInf(float64(sb), 0) {
			continue
		}
		c.FPR[1] = dbl(float64(sa))
		c.FPR[2] = dbl(float64(sb))
		runAt(c, bus, 0x2000,
			fa(59, 4, 1, 2, 0, 21, 0), // fadds f4, f1, f2
			fa(59, 5, 1, 0, 2, 25, 0), // fmuls f5, f1, f2
		)
		if want := sa + sb; c.FPR[4] != dbl(float64(want)) {
			t.Fatalf("iter %d fadds: got %#x want %#x", i, c.FPR[4], dbl(float64(want)))
		}
		if want := sa * sb; c.FPR[5] != dbl(float64(want)) {
			t.Fatalf("iter %d fmuls: got %#x want %#x", i, c.FPR[5], dbl(float64(want)))
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/chips/gekko/gekko.go ====================

// Package gekko implements the integer CPU of the Nintendo
// GameCube and Wii: a PowerPC 750 derivative (IBM/Motorola
// Gekko on GameCube, Broadway on Wii), written from the
// PowerPC Microprocessor Family Programming Environments
// manual and the PowerPC 750 user manual.
//
// Slice GCN-1 scope: the complete integer instruction set
// (arithmetic, logical, rotate and shift, load and store in
// every form including multiple, string, and byte-reversed,
// reservation instructions, branches, condition register
// operations, system registers and exceptions), BAT address
// translation, the time base and decrementer, and full
// serialization.
//
// Slice GCN-2 adds the floating point unit and the paired
// single unit in fp.go and ps.go: scalar double and single
// arithmetic with exact rounding and FPSCR reporting, the
// FPSCR move instructions, paired single arithmetic, and
// the quantized paired loads and stores driven by the GQRs.
//
// FPR representation (mixed view, used throughout): an FPR
// is one uint64. A scalar double operand or result is the
// full uint64 read as an IEEE double. A scalar single result
// is stored widened to the double value of that single. A
// paired single value packs its PS0 lane in the high 32 bits
// and its PS1 lane in the low 32 bits, each lane an IEEE
// single. Which view an instruction uses is fixed by the
// instruction, exactly as on hardware, and code that reads
// an FPR through the wrong view gets the corresponding
// reinterpretation.
package gekko

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// MSR bit masks (32-bit register values).
const (
	MSRPOW uint32 = 1 << 18 // power management enable
	MSRILE uint32 = 1 << 16 // interrupt little-endian mode
	MSREE  uint32 = 1 << 15 // external interrupt enable
	MSRPR  uint32 = 1 << 14 // privilege level (1 = user)
	MSRFP  uint32 = 1 << 13 // floating point available
	MSRME  uint32 = 1 << 12 // machine check enable
	MSRFE0 uint32 = 1 << 11 // FP exception mode 0
	MSRSE  uint32 = 1 << 10 // single-step trace
	MSRBE  uint32 = 1 << 9  // branch trace
	MSRFE1 uint32 = 1 << 8  // FP exception mode 1
	MSRIP  uint32 = 1 << 7  // interrupt prefix (1 = 0xFFF00000)
	MSRIR  uint32 = 1 << 6  // instruction address translation
	MSRDR  uint32 = 1 << 5  // data address translation
	MSRPM  uint32 = 1 << 4  // performance monitor marked mode
	MSRRI  uint32 = 1 << 2  // recoverable interrupt
	MSRLE  uint32 = 1 << 0  // little-endian mode
)

// Exception vector offsets from the interrupt base.
const (
	VecReset        uint32 = 0x100
	VecMachineCheck uint32 = 0x200
	VecDSI          uint32 = 0x300
	VecISI          uint32 = 0x400
	VecExternal     uint32 = 0x500
	VecAlignment    uint32 = 0x600
	VecProgram      uint32 = 0x700
	VecFPUnavail    uint32 = 0x800
	VecDecrementer  uint32 = 0x900
	VecSyscall      uint32 = 0xC00
	VecTrace        uint32 = 0xD00
)

// SRR1 cause bits for the program exception.
const (
	SRR1ProgIllegal    uint32 = 1 << 19
	SRR1ProgPrivileged uint32 = 1 << 18
	SRR1ProgTrap       uint32 = 1 << 17
)

// DSISR cause bits (also used as SRR1 cause bits for ISI).
const (
	DSISRNoTranslation uint32 = 1 << 30
	DSISRProtection    uint32 = 1 << 27
	DSISRStore         uint32 = 1 << 25
)

// Special purpose register numbers.
const (
	SPRXER   = 1
	SPRLR    = 8
	SPRCTR   = 9
	SPRDSISR = 18
	SPRDAR   = 19
	SPRDEC   = 22
	SPRSDR1  = 25
	SPRSRR0  = 26
	SPRSRR1  = 27
	SPRSPRG0 = 272
	SPRTBLRD = 268 // mftb/mfspr read of time base lower
	SPRTBURD = 269 // mftb/mfspr read of time base upper
	SPRTBLWR = 284 // mtspr write of time base lower
	SPRTBUWR = 285 // mtspr write of time base upper
	SPRPVR   = 287

	SPRIBAT0U = 528
	SPRDBAT0U = 536

	// GQR0 to GQR7. The task wiring for this slice is SPR
	// 896..903. The Gekko manual also names 912..919 for the
	// same registers, so both ranges are wired to the same
	// storage in GetSPR and SetSPR.
	SPRGQR0    = 896
	SPRGQR0Alt = 912
)

// PVR value for the GameCube Gekko (read-only).
const PVRGekko uint32 = 0x00083200

// Bus is the physical memory interface the CPU drives after
// address translation. Read16 and Read32 return big-endian
// values assembled from memory; the CPU applies little-endian
// swapping itself when MSR[LE] is set. Implementations must
// tolerate unaligned addresses (Gekko performs most unaligned
// accesses in hardware by splitting them; this core performs
// them as single bus transactions and does not take a
// second-page fault for a cross-page unaligned access).
type Bus interface {
	Read8(addr uint32) uint8
	Read16(addr uint32) uint16
	Read32(addr uint32) uint32
	Write8(addr uint32, v uint8)
	Write16(addr uint32, v uint16)
	Write32(addr uint32, v uint32)
}

// CPU is the Gekko core.
type CPU struct {
	GPR [32]uint32
	FPR [32]uint64 // see the mixed view note in the package comment
	CR  uint32
	XER uint32 // SO=1<<31, OV=1<<30, CA=1<<29, string byte count in low 7 bits
	LR  uint32
	CTR uint32
	PC  uint32
	MSR uint32

	// FPSCR is the floating point status and control
	// register. Bit constants use PowerPC bit numbering in
	// fp.go; the stored uint32 keeps the conventional layout
	// in which PowerPC bit 0 is the value bit 1<<31.
	FPSCR uint32

	// GQR holds the eight graphics quantization registers
	// used by the paired single quantized loads and stores.
	// Field layout is defined in ps.go.
	GQR [8]uint32

	SRR0  uint32
	SRR1  uint32
	DSISR uint32
	DAR   uint32
	SDR1  uint32
	SR    [16]uint32
	SPRG  [4]uint32

	// TB is the time base counter. It ticks once per four
	// CPU cycles (the Gekko bus clock ratio).
	TB uint64

	// Halted stops Step from doing anything (the system
	// starts the CPU halted after staging a DOL).
	Halted bool

	bus Bus

	dec        uint32
	decPending bool
	tbRem      uint32 // accumulated sub-tick cycles, 0..3
	irq        bool

	reservAddr  uint32
	reservValid bool

	ibat [4][2]uint32 // [i][0] = upper (BATU), [i][1] = lower (BATL)
	dbat [4][2]uint32

	extras [1024]uint32 // all non-dedicated SPR storage

	curIA uint32 // address of the instruction being executed
}

// New returns a CPU in its reset state driving bus.
func New(bus Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{bus: bus}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Reset restores the documented power-on state: exceptions
// prefixed to 0xFFF00000, translation off, interrupts off,
// PC at the reset vector. The wholesale struct replacement
// also clears FPSCR and all GQRs to zero.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	*c = CPU{
		bus: c.bus,
		MSR: MSRIP,
		PC:  0xFFF00000 + VecReset,
	}
}

// SetIRQ drives the external interrupt input line.
func (c *CPU) SetIRQ(on bool) { c.irq = on }

// IRQ reports the external interrupt input line.
func (c *CPU) IRQ() bool { return c.irq }

// Decrementer returns the current DEC value.
func (c *CPU) Decrementer() uint32 { return c.dec }

// faultInfo aborts the current instruction via panic and is
// recovered in Step, where it becomes exception entry.
type faultInfo struct {
	vec   uint32
	srr0  uint32
	cause uint32 // SRR1 cause bits
	dsisr uint32 // DSISR value, for DSI and alignment
	dar   uint32 // DAR value, for DSI and alignment
	setDA bool   // write DSISR and DAR on entry
}

func fault(info faultInfo) { panic(&info) }

// Step executes one instruction and returns the cycles it
// consumed. The cycle model is flat: one instruction is one
// cycle (the 750 is superscalar on hardware; this core does
// not model dispatch width). TB and DEC advance at one tick
// per four cycles.
func (c *CPU) Step() (n int) {
	if c.Halted {
		return 0
	}
	n = 1
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			if f, ok := r.(*faultInfo); ok {
				if f.setDA {
					c.DSISR = f.dsisr
					c.DAR = f.dar
				}
				c.enterException(f.vec, f.srr0, f.cause)
			} else {
				panic(r)
			}
		}
		c.tick(1)
	}()

	// Pending interrupts are sampled between instructions.
	if c.decPending && c.MSR&MSREE != 0 {
		c.decPending = false
		c.enterException(VecDecrementer, c.PC, 0)
		return 1
	}
	if c.irq && c.MSR&MSREE != 0 {
		c.enterException(VecExternal, c.PC, 0)
		return 1
	}

	ia := c.PC
	c.curIA = ia
	w := c.fetch(ia)
	c.PC = ia + 4
	c.exec(w, ia)
	return 1
}

// tick advances the time base and decrementer by cycles CPU
// cycles. TB and DEC tick once per four CPU cycles. When
// DEC decrements past zero the decrementer exception is
// requested; it is taken at the next Step boundary if
// MSR[EE] is set.
func (c *CPU) tick(cycles uint32) {
	c.tbRem += cycles
	for c.tbRem >= 4 {
		c.tbRem -= 4
		c.TB++
		if c.dec == 0 {
			c.decPending = true
		}
		c.dec--
	}
}

// enterException performs exception entry: SRR0 and SRR1
// are loaded, the reservation is cleared, MSR is replaced
// by its exception value (ME and IP preserved, LE takes
// ILE), and PC moves to the vector. In this core SRR1 saves
// the low half of MSR plus the cause bits; rfi restores
// exactly the architected field mask from it.
func (c *CPU) enterException(vec, srr0, cause uint32) {
	c.SRR0 = srr0
	c.SRR1 = (c.MSR & 0xFFFF) | cause
	old := c.MSR
	nm := old & (MSRME | MSRIP)
	if old&MSRILE != 0 {
		nm |= MSRLE
	}
	c.MSR = nm
	c.reservValid = false
	base := uint32(0)
	if old&MSRIP != 0 {
		base = 0xFFF00000
	}
	c.PC = base + vec
}

// Translate converts an effective address to a physical
// address. fetch selects instruction translation (MSR[IR]
// and the IBATs); otherwise data translation applies
// (MSR[DR] and the DBATs). store marks a write access for
// protection checks. ok is false when translation faults;
// the caller raises DSI or ISI. The translation scope is
// documented in TranslatePhys.
func (c *CPU) Translate(ea uint32, fetch, store bool) (pa uint32, ok bool) {
	pa, _, _, ok = c.translate(ea, fetch, store)
	return pa, ok
}

// translate implements the GCN-1 translation scope:
//
//   - Translation off (IR or DR clear): identity.
//   - Translation on: BAT array lookup with the documented
//     block sizes (128 KB to 256 MB in powers of two) and PP
//     protection qualified by the segment register keys. A
//     matching valid BAT wins.
//   - No page table walk in this slice: a BAT miss raises
//     the same translation exception the hardware raises
//     when its walk finds no PTE (DSISR/ISI translation
//     bit). GC software at boot and the SDK runtime
//     program BATs for the whole address space they use,
//     so this covers the boot path exactly.
func (c *CPU) translate(ea uint32, fetch, store bool) (pa uint32, prot, miss bool, ok bool) {
	if fetch {
		if c.MSR&MSRIR == 0 {
			return ea, false, false, true
		}
		return c.batLookup(c.ibat, ea, store)
	}
	if c.MSR&MSRDR == 0 {
		return ea, false, false, true
	}
	return c.batLookup(c.dbat, ea, store)
}

func (c *CPU) batLookup(bats [4][2]uint32, ea uint32, store bool) (uint32, bool, bool, bool) {
	user := c.MSR&MSRPR != 0
	sr := c.SR[ea>>28]
	ks := sr&(1<<30) != 0
	kp := sr&(1<<29) != 0
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		batu := bats[i][0]
		batl := bats[i][1]
		vs := batu&(1<<1) != 0
		vp := batu&1 != 0
		if user {
			if !vp {
				continue
			}
		} else if !vs {
			continue
		}
		bl := (batu >> 2) & 0x7FF
		size := (bl + 1) << 17 // 128 KB units
		mask := ^(size - 1)
		if ea&mask != batu&0xFFFF8000&mask {
			continue
		}
		pp := batl & 3
		// Key gate: a set key bit for the current privilege
		// level denies all access through this BAT.
		if (!user && ks) || (user && kp) {
			return 0, true, false, false
		}
		if pp == 0 || (store && pp != 2) {
			return 0, true, false, false
		}
		pa := (batl & 0xFFFF8000) | (ea & (size - 1))
		return pa, false, false, true
	}
	return 0, false, true, false
}

// fetch reads the instruction word at ea, raising ISI on a
// translation fault.
func (c *CPU) fetch(ea uint32) uint32 {
	pa, prot, _, ok := c.translate(ea, true, false)
	if !ok {
		cause := uint32(DSISRNoTranslation)
		if prot {
			cause = DSISRProtection
		}
		panic(&faultInfo{vec: VecISI, srr0: ea, cause: cause})
	}
	w := c.bus.Read32(pa)
	if c.MSR&MSRLE != 0 {
		w = swap32(w)
	}
	return w
}

// load reads size bytes (1, 2, or 4) at effective address
// ea as an unsigned big-endian value, raising DSI on a
// translation fault.
func (c *CPU) load(ea uint32, size int) uint32 {
	pa, prot, _, ok := c.translate(ea, false, false)
	if !ok {
		panic(&faultInfo{
			vec: VecDSI, srr0: c.curIA, setDA: true,
			dsisr: dsisrCause(prot, false), dar: ea,
		})
	}
	var v uint32
	switch size {
	case 1:
		v = uint32(c.bus.Read8(pa))
	case 2:
		v = uint32(c.bus.Read16(pa))
	default:
		v = c.bus.Read32(pa)
	}
	if c.MSR&MSRLE != 0 {
		switch size {
		case 2:
			v = uint32(swap16(uint16(v)))
		case 4:
			v = swap32(v)
		}
	}
	return v
}

// store writes the low size bytes of v at effective address
// ea, raising DSI on a translation fault.
func (c *CPU) store(ea uint32, size int, v uint32) {
	pa, prot, _, ok := c.translate(ea, false, true)
	if !ok {
		panic(&faultInfo{
			vec: VecDSI, srr0: c.curIA, setDA: true,
			dsisr: dsisrCause(prot, true), dar: ea,
		})
	}
	if c.MSR&MSRLE != 0 {
		switch size {
		case 2:
			v = uint32(swap16(uint16(v)))
		case 4:
			v = swap32(v)
		}
	}
	switch size {
	case 1:
		c.bus.Write8(pa, uint8(v))
	case 2:
		c.bus.Write16(pa, uint16(v))
	default:
		c.bus.Write32(pa, v)
	}
}

func dsisrCause(prot, store bool) uint32 {
	d := uint32(DSISRNoTranslation)
	if prot {
		d = DSISRProtection
	}
	if store {
		d |= DSISRStore
	}
	return d
}

// alignFault raises the alignment exception for ea.
func (c *CPU) alignFault(ea uint32) {
	panic(&faultInfo{
		vec: VecAlignment, srr0: c.curIA, setDA: true,
		dsisr: 0, dar: ea,
	})
}

func swap16(v uint16) uint16 { return v<<8 | v>>8 }

func swap32(v uint32) uint32 {
	return v<<24 | (v&0xFF00)<<8 | (v>>8)&0xFF00 | v>>24
}

// sprPrivileged reports whether an SPR is supervisor-only.
// The architected rule: SPR bit 4 of the ten-bit number
// (value 0x10) marks the privileged half of the space.
func sprPrivileged(spr int) bool { return spr&0x10 != 0 }

// GetSPR reads a special purpose register, applying the
// dedicated storage for the registers this core models.
func (c *CPU) GetSPR(spr int) uint32 {
	switch spr {
	case SPRXER:
		return c.XER
	case SPRLR:
		return c.LR
	case SPRCTR:
		return c.CTR
	case SPRDSISR:
		return c.DSISR
	case SPRDAR:
		return c.DAR
	case SPRDEC:
		return c.dec
	case SPRSDR1:
		return c.SDR1
	case SPRSRR0:
		return c.SRR0
	case SPRSRR1:
		return c.SRR1
	case SPRSPRG0 + 0, SPRSPRG0 + 1, SPRSPRG0 + 2, SPRSPRG0 + 3:
		return c.SPRG[spr-SPRSPRG0]
	case SPRTBLRD:
		return uint32(c.TB)
	case SPRTBURD:
		return uint32(c.TB >> 32)
	case SPRPVR:
		return PVRGekko
	}
	if spr >= SPRGQR0 && spr < SPRGQR0+8 {
		return c.GQR[spr-SPRGQR0]
	}
	if spr >= SPRGQR0Alt && spr < SPRGQR0Alt+8 {
		return c.GQR[spr-SPRGQR0Alt]
	}
	if spr >= SPRIBAT0U && spr < SPRIBAT0U+8 {
		n := spr - SPRIBAT0U
		return c.ibat[n/2][n%2]
	}
	if spr >= SPRDBAT0U && spr < SPRDBAT0U+8 {
		n := spr - SPRDBAT0U
		return c.dbat[n/2][n%2]
	}
	return c.extras[spr&0x3FF]
}

// SetSPR writes a special purpose register. Writes to the
// read-only PVR and to the time base read numbers are
// ignored, as on hardware.
func (c *CPU) SetSPR(spr int, v uint32) {
	switch spr {
	case SPRXER:
		c.XER = v
	case SPRLR:
		c.LR = v
	case SPRCTR:
		c.CTR = v
	case SPRDSISR:
		c.DSISR = v
	case SPRDAR:
		c.DAR = v
	case SPRDEC:
		c.dec = v
		c.decPending = false
	case SPRSDR1:
		c.SDR1 = v
	case SPRSRR0:
		c.SRR0 = v
	case SPRSRR1:
		c.SRR1 = v
	case SPRSPRG0 + 0, SPRSPRG0 + 1, SPRSPRG0 + 2, SPRSPRG0 + 3:
		c.SPRG[spr-SPRSPRG0] = v
	case SPRTBLRD, SPRTBURD, SPRPVR:
		// Read-only through the SPR interface.
	case SPRTBLWR:
		c.TB = (c.TB & 0xFFFFFFFF00000000) | uint64(v)
	case SPRTBUWR:
		c.TB = (c.TB & 0x00000000FFFFFFFF) | uint64(v)<<32
	default:
		if spr >= SPRGQR0 && spr < SPRGQR0+8 {
			c.GQR[spr-SPRGQR0] = v
			return
		}
		if spr >= SPRGQR0Alt && spr < SPRGQR0Alt+8 {
			c.GQR[spr-SPRGQR0Alt] = v
			return
		}
		if spr >= SPRIBAT0U && spr < SPRIBAT0U+8 {
			n := spr - SPRIBAT0U
			c.ibat[n/2][n%2] = v
			return
		}
		if spr >= SPRDBAT0U && spr < SPRDBAT0U+8 {
			n := spr - SPRDBAT0U
			c.dbat[n/2][n%2] = v
			return
		}
		c.extras[spr&0x3FF] = v
	}
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size of the CPU:
// GPRs 128, FPRs 256, twelve registers 48, TB 8, segment
// registers 64, SPRGs 16, IBATs 32, DBATs 32, the generic
// SPR file 4096, reservation address 4, flags 4, and the
// GCN-2 tail: FPSCR 4 plus the eight GQRs 32. The GCN-2
// tail is appended after the flags word so every GCN-1
// field keeps its offset; only the total size grew, by 36.
const SerializeSize = 128 + 256 + 48 + 8 + 64 + 16 + 32 + 32 + 4096 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 32

// Serialize writes the complete CPU state.
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	off := 0
	put32 := func(v uint32) {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], v)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, r := range c.GPR {
		put32(r)
	}
	for _, f := range c.FPR {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[off:], f)
		off += 8
	}
	put32(c.CR)
	put32(c.XER)
	put32(c.LR)
	put32(c.CTR)
	put32(c.PC)
	put32(c.MSR)
	put32(c.SRR0)
	put32(c.SRR1)
	put32(c.DSISR)
	put32(c.DAR)
	put32(c.SDR1)
	put32(c.dec)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[off:], c.TB)
	off += 8
	for _, s := range c.SR {
		put32(s)
	}
	for _, s := range c.SPRG {
		put32(s)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		put32(c.ibat[i][0])
		put32(c.ibat[i][1])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		put32(c.dbat[i][0])
		put32(c.dbat[i][1])
	}
	for _, e := range c.extras {
		put32(e)
	}
	put32(c.reservAddr)
	var flags uint32
	if c.Halted {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if c.irq {
		flags |= 2
	}
	if c.decPending {
		flags |= 4
	}
	if c.reservValid {
		flags |= 8
	}
	flags |= c.tbRem << 8
	put32(flags)
	// GCN-2 appended tail: FPSCR, then GQR0 through GQR7.
	put32(c.FPSCR)
	for _, g := range c.GQR {
		put32(g)
	}
	if off != SerializeSize {
		panic("gekko: serialize size mismatch")
	}
	return out
}

// ErrStateSize reports a CPU state block of the wrong size.
var ErrStateSize = errors.New("gekko: bad CPU state size")

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != SerializeSize {
		return ErrStateSize
	}
	off := 0
	get32 := func() uint32 {
		v := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
		return v
	}
	for i := range c.GPR {
		c.GPR[i] = get32()
	}
	for i := range c.FPR {
		c.FPR[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(in[off:])
		off += 8
	}
	c.CR = get32()
	c.XER = get32()
	c.LR = get32()
	c.CTR = get32()
	c.PC = get32()
	c.MSR = get32()
	c.SRR0 = get32()
	c.SRR1 = get32()
	c.DSISR = get32()
	c.DAR = get32()
	c.SDR1 = get32()
	c.dec = get32()
	c.TB = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(in[off:])
	off += 8
	for i := range c.SR {
		c.SR[i] = get32()
	}
	for i := range c.SPRG {
		c.SPRG[i] = get32()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.ibat[i][0] = get32()
		c.ibat[i][1] = get32()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.dbat[i][0] = get32()
		c.dbat[i][1] = get32()
	}
	for i := range c.extras {
		c.extras[i] = get32()
	}
	c.reservAddr = get32()
	flags := get32()
	c.Halted = flags&1 != 0
	c.irq = flags&2 != 0
	c.decPending = flags&4 != 0
	c.reservValid = flags&8 != 0
	c.tbRem = (flags >> 8) & 3
	// GCN-2 appended tail: FPSCR, then GQR0 through GQR7.
	c.FPSCR = get32()
	for i := range c.GQR {
		c.GQR[i] = get32()
	}
	return nil
}
