package gekko

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"
)

// ramBus is a flat big-endian test memory.
type ramBus struct{ b []byte }

func newRAM() *ramBus {
	return &ramBus{b: make([]byte, 16<<20)}
}

func (r *ramBus) mask(a uint32) uint32 { return a & uint32(len(r.b)-1) }
func (r *ramBus) Read8(a uint32) uint8 { return r.b[r.mask(a)] }
func (r *ramBus) Read16(a uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(r.Read8(a))<<8 | uint16(r.Read8(a+1))
}
func (r *ramBus) Read32(a uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(r.Read8(a))<<24 | uint32(r.Read8(a+1))<<16 |
		uint32(r.Read8(a+2))<<8 | uint32(r.Read8(a+3))
}
func (r *ramBus) Write8(a uint32, v uint8) { r.b[r.mask(a)] = v }
func (r *ramBus) Write16(a uint32, v uint16) {
	r.Write8(a, uint8(v>>8))
	r.Write8(a+1, uint8(v))
}
func (r *ramBus) Write32(a uint32, v uint32) {
	r.Write8(a, uint8(v>>24))
	r.Write8(a+1, uint8(v>>16))
	r.Write8(a+2, uint8(v>>8))
	r.Write8(a+3, uint8(v))
}

// ins builds an X/XO-form instruction word.
func ins(op, f1v, f2v, f3v, xov uint32, rc bool) uint32 {
	w := op<<26 | f1v<<21 | f2v<<16 | f3v<<11 | xov<<1
	if rc {
		w |= 1
	}
	return w
}

// insD builds a D-form instruction word.
func insD(op, f1v, f2v, imm uint32) uint32 {
	return op<<26 | f1v<<21 | f2v<<16 | imm&0xFFFF
}

const nop = 0x60000000 // ori r0, r0, 0

// prog loads words at addr and points the CPU at them.
func prog(c *CPU, bus *ramBus, addr uint32, words ...uint32) {
	for i, w := range words {
		bus.Write32(addr+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
	c.PC = addr
}

func steps(c *CPU, n int) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
}

func TestRLWinmMasks(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		v          uint32
		sh, mb, me uint32
		want       uint32
	}{
		{0x12345678, 0, 0, 31, 0x12345678},
		{0x12345678, 0, 8, 23, 0x00345600},
		{0x89ABCDEF, 0, 28, 3, 0x8000000F},  // wrapping mask
		{0x80000001, 1, 0, 31, 0x00000003},  // rotate across the top
		{0xDEADBEEF, 0, 16, 15, 0xDEADBEEF}, // wrap band covering all bits
		{0xFFFFFFFF, 0, 4, 27, 0x0FFFFFF0},
		{0x00000001, 31, 0, 0, 0x80000000}, // single bit rotated to the top
		{0xA5A5A5A5, 8, 8, 15, 0x00A50000}, // MB/ME are PowerPC-numbered: bits 8..15 are value bits 23..16
	}
	for i, tc := range cases {
		bus := newRAM()
		c := New(bus)
		c.GPR[4] = tc.v
		// rlwinm r3, r4, sh, mb, me
		w := 21<<26 | 4<<21 | 3<<16 | tc.sh<<11 | tc.mb<<6 | tc.me<<1
		prog(c, bus, 0x1000, w)
		steps(c, 1)
		if c.GPR[3] != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("case %d: rlwinm = %#08x, want %#08x", i, c.GPR[3], tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestRLWimiAndRLWnm(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.GPR[3] = 0xFF00FF00
	c.GPR[4] = 0x0000ABCD
	// rlwimi r3, r4, 8, 16, 23: insert rotated low half of r4
	// (0x00ABCD00) into r3 bits 16..23 -> 0xFFCDFF00? bits
	// 16..23 of the result are mask positions 8..15 in value
	// terms: mask = bits with MB=16, ME=23 -> 0x0000FF00.
	// rotl(0xABCD, 8) = 0x00ABCD00; & 0x0000FF00 = 0x0000CD00.
	// r3 = 0xFF00FF00 with those bits replaced = 0xFF00CD00.
	w := uint32(20<<26 | 4<<21 | 3<<16 | 8<<11 | 16<<6 | 23<<1)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, w)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[3] != 0xFF00CD00 {
		t.Fatalf("rlwimi = %#08x, want 0xFF00CD00", c.GPR[3])
	}

	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x00000003
	c.GPR[5] = 30
	// rlwnm r3, r4, r5, 0, 1: rotl(3, 30) = 0xC0000000,
	// mask MB=0 ME=1 -> 0xC0000000.
	w = 23<<26 | 4<<21 | 3<<16 | 5<<11 | 0<<6 | 1<<1
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, w)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[3] != 0xC0000000 {
		t.Fatalf("rlwnm = %#08x, want 0xC0000000", c.GPR[3])
	}
}

func TestCarryOverflow(t *testing.T) {
	type tc struct {
		name  string
		words []uint32
		pre   func(c *CPU)
		reg   int
		want  uint32
		ca    int // -1 = do not check
		ov    int
	}
	addc := func(rd, ra, rb uint32, oe, rc bool) uint32 {
		w := ins(31, rd, ra, rb, 10, rc)
		if oe {
			w |= 0x400
		}
		return w
	}
	subfc := func(rd, ra, rb uint32, oe bool) uint32 {
		w := ins(31, rd, ra, rb, 8, false)
		if oe {
			w |= 0x400
		}
		return w
	}
	cases := []tc{
		{"addc carry", []uint32{addc(3, 4, 5, false, false)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4], c.GPR[5] = 0xFFFFFFFF, 1 }, 3, 0, 1, -1},
		{"addc no carry", []uint32{addc(3, 4, 5, false, false)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4], c.GPR[5] = 7, 8 }, 3, 15, 0, -1},
		{"addco overflow", []uint32{addc(3, 4, 5, true, false)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4], c.GPR[5] = 0x7FFFFFFF, 1 }, 3, 0x80000000, 0, 1},
		{"addco neg no overflow", []uint32{addc(3, 4, 5, true, false)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4], c.GPR[5] = 0x80000000, 1 }, 3, 0x80000001, 0, 0},
		{"subfc borrow", []uint32{subfc(3, 4, 5, false)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4], c.GPR[5] = 5, 3 }, 3, 0xFFFFFFFE, 0, -1},
		{"subfc no borrow", []uint32{subfc(3, 4, 5, false)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4], c.GPR[5] = 3, 5 }, 3, 2, 1, -1},
		{"subfo overflow", []uint32{subfc(3, 4, 5, true)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4], c.GPR[5] = 0x80000000, 0x7FFFFFFF }, 3, 0xFFFFFFFF, -1, 1},
		{"subfic borrow", []uint32{insD(8, 3, 4, 10)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4] = 20 }, 3, 0xFFFFFFF6, 0, -1},
		{"subfic no borrow", []uint32{insD(8, 3, 4, 10)},
			func(c *CPU) { c.GPR[4] = 3 }, 3, 7, 1, -1},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		bus := newRAM()
		c := New(bus)
		tc.pre(c)
		prog(c, bus, 0x1000, tc.words...)
		steps(c, len(tc.words))
		if c.GPR[tc.reg] != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: r%d = %#08x, want %#08x", tc.name, tc.reg, c.GPR[tc.reg], tc.want)
		}
		if tc.ca >= 0 {
			got := 0
			if c.XER&(1<<29) != 0 {
				got = 1
			}
			if got != tc.ca {
				t.Errorf("%s: CA = %d, want %d", tc.name, got, tc.ca)
			}
		}
		if tc.ov >= 0 {
			got := 0
			if c.XER&(1<<30) != 0 {
				got = 1
			}
			if got != tc.ov {
				t.Errorf("%s: OV = %d, want %d", tc.name, got, tc.ov)
			}
			if tc.ov == 1 && c.XER&(1<<31) == 0 {
				t.Errorf("%s: SO not latched with OV", tc.name)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestAddChainAndMulDiv(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	// addc wraps to zero setting CA, addze then adds the
	// carry into the high word.
	c.GPR[4] = 0xFFFFFFFF
	c.GPR[5] = 1
	c.GPR[6] = 41
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		ins(31, 3, 4, 5, 10, false),   // addc r3, r4, r5
		ins(31, 7, 6, 0, 202, false),  // addze r7, r6
		ins(31, 8, 4, 5, 75, false),   // mulhw r8, r4, r5
		ins(31, 9, 4, 5, 11, false),   // mulhwu r9, r4, r5
		ins(31, 10, 4, 5, 491, false), // divw r10, r4, r5
	)
	steps(c, 5)
	if c.GPR[3] != 0 || c.GPR[7] != 42 {
		t.Fatalf("addc/addze: r3 = %#x r7 = %#x", c.GPR[3], c.GPR[7])
	}
	// mulhw of -1 * 1 = -1 -> high = 0xFFFFFFFF; mulhwu of
	// 0xFFFFFFFF * 1 -> high = 0.
	if c.GPR[8] != 0xFFFFFFFF || c.GPR[9] != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mulhw/mulhwu: r8 = %#x r9 = %#x", c.GPR[8], c.GPR[9])
	}
	if c.GPR[10] != 0xFFFFFFFF { // -1 / 1
		t.Fatalf("divw: r10 = %#x", c.GPR[10])
	}
}

func TestStringInstructions(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	copy(bus.b[0x2000:], "ABCDEFGHIJ")
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	// lswi r5, r4, 10
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 5, 4, 10, 597, false))
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[5] != 0x41424344 || c.GPR[6] != 0x45464748 || c.GPR[7] != 0x494A0000 {
		t.Fatalf("lswi: r5=%#08x r6=%#08x r7=%#08x", c.GPR[5], c.GPR[6], c.GPR[7])
	}

	// Register window wrap: lswi r31 with 6 bytes fills r31
	// and wraps into r0.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	copy(bus.b[0x2000:], "ABCDEF")
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 31, 4, 6, 597, false))
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[31] != 0x41424344 || c.GPR[0] != 0x45460000 {
		t.Fatalf("lswi wrap: r31=%#08x r0=%#08x", c.GPR[31], c.GPR[0])
	}

	// stswi stores the bytes back out, MSB first.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	c.GPR[5] = 0x41424344
	c.GPR[6] = 0x45460000
	c.GPR[4] = 0x3000
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 5, 4, 6, 725, false))
	steps(c, 1)
	if got := string(bus.b[0x3000:0x3006]); got != "ABCDEF" {
		t.Fatalf("stswi: memory = %q", got)
	}

	// lswx takes its byte count from XER.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	copy(bus.b[0x2000:], "HELLO")
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	c.XER = 5
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 8, 0, 4, 533, false)) // lswx r8, r0, r4
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[8] != 0x48454C4C || c.GPR[9] != 0x4F000000 {
		t.Fatalf("lswx: r8=%#08x r9=%#08x", c.GPR[8], c.GPR[9])
	}
}

func TestReservation(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	bus.Write32(0x2000, 0xDEADBEEF)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	c.GPR[5] = 0x12345678
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		ins(31, 3, 0, 4, 20, false),  // lwarx r3, r0, r4
		ins(31, 5, 0, 4, 150, false), // stwcx. r5, r0, r4
		ins(31, 5, 0, 4, 150, false), // stwcx. again: must fail
	)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[3] != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("lwarx loaded %#08x", c.GPR[3])
	}
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.crField(0)&2 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("first stwcx. should set CR0 EQ")
	}
	if bus.Read32(0x2000) != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("stwcx. did not store")
	}
	c.GPR[5] = 0x99999999
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.crField(0)&2 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("second stwcx. should clear CR0 EQ")
	}
	if bus.Read32(0x2000) != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("failed stwcx. stored anyway")
	}

	// A reservation on one address does not authorize a
	// store to another.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	c.GPR[6] = 0x2004
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		ins(31, 3, 0, 4, 20, false),
		ins(31, 5, 0, 6, 150, false),
	)
	steps(c, 2)
	if c.crField(0)&2 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("stwcx. to a different address should fail")
	}
}

func TestBATTranslation(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	// Identity while DR is off.
	if pa, ok := c.Translate(0x80001234, false, false); !ok || pa != 0x80001234 {
		t.Fatalf("identity: pa=%#x ok=%v", pa, ok)
	}
	// DBAT0: 1 MB block, EA 0x80000000 -> PA 0x00000000,
	// supervisor read/write.
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U, 0x80000000|(7<<2)|(1<<1))
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U+1, 2) // BRPN 0, PP = 2
	c.MSR |= MSRDR
	if pa, ok := c.Translate(0x80012345, false, false); !ok || pa != 0x00012345 {
		t.Fatalf("bat 1MB: pa=%#x ok=%v", pa, ok)
	}
	if pa, ok := c.Translate(0x800FFFFF, false, true); !ok || pa != 0x000FFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("bat top: pa=%#x ok=%v", pa, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := c.Translate(0x80100000, false, false); ok {
		t.Fatalf("bat miss above block should fault")
	}
	// Shrink to 128 KB (BL = 0).
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U, 0x80000000|(0<<2)|(1<<1))
	if pa, ok := c.Translate(0x8001FFFF, false, false); !ok || pa != 0x1FFFF {
		t.Fatalf("bat 128K: pa=%#x ok=%v", pa, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := c.Translate(0x80020000, false, false); ok {
		t.Fatalf("bat 128K miss should fault")
	}
	// User mode: Vp is clear in BATU, so the BAT does not
	// apply and the access misses.
	c.MSR |= MSRPR
	if _, ok := c.Translate(0x80000000, false, false); ok {
		t.Fatalf("user access through supervisor-only BAT should fault")
	}
	// Set Vp and PP = 1 (read only): loads pass, stores
	// fault.
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U, 0x80000000|(0<<2)|(1<<1)|1)
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U+1, 1)
	if _, ok := c.Translate(0x80000000, false, false); !ok {
		t.Fatalf("user read through PP=1 BAT should pass")
	}
	if _, ok := c.Translate(0x80000000, false, true); ok {
		t.Fatalf("user store through PP=1 BAT should fault")
	}
	// PP = 0 denies the supervisor too.
	c.MSR &^= MSRPR
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U+1, 0)
	if _, ok := c.Translate(0x80000000, false, false); ok {
		t.Fatalf("PP=0 BAT should deny supervisor reads")
	}
}

func TestDSIOnProtectedLoad(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U, 0x80000000|(7<<2)|(1<<1))
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U+1, 0) // PP = 0: no access
	c.MSR |= MSRDR
	c.GPR[4] = 0x80001000
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, insD(32, 3, 4, 0)) // lwz r3, 0(r4)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecDSI {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %#x, want DSI vector", c.PC)
	}
	if c.DSISR&DSISRProtection == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("DSISR = %#x, want protection bit", c.DSISR)
	}
	if c.DSISR&DSISRStore != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("DSISR store bit set on a load")
	}
	if c.DAR != 0x80001000 {
		t.Fatalf("DAR = %#x", c.DAR)
	}
	if c.SRR0 != 0x1000 {
		t.Fatalf("SRR0 = %#x, want faulting instruction", c.SRR0)
	}
}

func TestDecrementerTiming(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	pat := []byte{0x60, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00}
	for i := range bus.b {
		bus.b[i] = pat[i%4]
	}
	c.MSR |= MSREE
	c.SetSPR(SPRDEC, 100)
	// DEC ticks at steps 4, 8, ...; it reaches zero at step
	// 400, wraps at step 404, and the exception is taken at
	// the start of step 405.
	got := 0
	for s := 1; s <= 1000; s++ {
		c.Step()
		if c.PC == 0xFFF00000+VecDecrementer {
			got = s
			break
		}
	}
	if got != 405 {
		t.Fatalf("decrementer taken at step %d, want 405", got)
	}
	if c.TB != 101 {
		t.Fatalf("TB = %d, want 101", c.TB)
	}
	if c.SRR0 != 0xFFF00100+4*404 {
		t.Fatalf("SRR0 = %#x, want the interrupted PC", c.SRR0)
	}
	// mftb reads the time base back. The TBR number (268)
	// sits scrambled in the SPR field, bits 11-20.
	bus2 := newRAM()
	c2 := New(bus2)
	tbr := uint32((268&0x1F)<<5 | 268>>5)
	prog(c2, bus2, 0x1000, 31<<26|3<<21|tbr<<11|371<<1) // mftb r3
	c2.TB = 0x1122334455667788
	steps(c2, 1)
	if c2.GPR[3] != 0x55667788 {
		t.Fatalf("mftb low = %#08x", c2.GPR[3])
	}
}

func TestBranchConditions(t *testing.T) {
	type tc struct {
		bo, bi uint32
		cr     uint32
		ctr    uint32
		taken  bool
		ctrOut uint32
	}
	eqField := uint32(2) << 28 // CR0 EQ bit (bit 2) set
	cases := []tc{
		{12, 2, eqField, 0, true, 0}, // beq, equal
		{12, 2, 0, 0, false, 0},      // beq, not equal
		{4, 2, eqField, 0, false, 0}, // bne, equal
		{4, 2, 0, 0, true, 0},        // bne, not equal
		{16, 0, 0, 3, true, 2},       // bdnz, ctr 3 -> 2
		{16, 0, 0, 1, false, 0},      // bdnz, ctr 1 -> 0
		{18, 0, 0, 1, true, 0},       // bdz, ctr 1 -> 0
		{18, 0, 0, 2, false, 1},      // bdz, ctr 2 -> 1
		{20, 0, 0, 0, true, 0},       // unconditional form
		{12, 0, 8 << 28, 0, true, 0}, // blt form: LT is CR bit 0
		{12, 0, 0, 0, false, 0},      // blt form, clear
	}
	for i, tc := range cases {
		bus := newRAM()
		c := New(bus)
		c.CR = tc.cr
		c.CTR = tc.ctr
		// bc bo, bi, +0x40
		w := 16<<26 | tc.bo<<21 | tc.bi<<16 | 0x40
		prog(c, bus, 0x1000, w)
		steps(c, 1)
		want := uint32(0x1004)
		if tc.taken {
			want = 0x1040
		}
		if c.PC != want {
			t.Errorf("case %d (bo=%d bi=%d): PC = %#x, want %#x", i, tc.bo, tc.bi, c.PC, want)
		}
		if c.CTR != tc.ctrOut {
			t.Errorf("case %d: CTR = %d, want %d", i, c.CTR, tc.ctrOut)
		}
	}
}

func TestExceptionEntry(t *testing.T) {
	// sc: SRR0 is the next instruction, vector 0xC00.
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, 17<<26)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecSyscall || c.SRR0 != 0x1004 {
		t.Fatalf("sc: PC=%#x SRR0=%#x", c.PC, c.SRR0)
	}
	if c.MSR&MSREE != 0 || c.MSR&MSRIP == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("sc: MSR = %#x, EE should be clear, IP kept", c.MSR)
	}

	// tw with TO = 31 always traps.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 31, 3, 4, 4, false))
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecProgram || c.SRR1&SRR1ProgTrap == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("tw: PC=%#x SRR1=%#x", c.PC, c.SRR1)
	}

	// Illegal instruction word 0.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, 0)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecProgram || c.SRR1&SRR1ProgIllegal == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("illegal: PC=%#x SRR1=%#x", c.PC, c.SRR1)
	}

	// Floating point with MSR[FP] clear raises FP
	// unavailable (GCN-2 executes it when MSR[FP] is set;
	// that path is covered in fp_test.go).
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, 63<<26|3<<21|4<<16|5<<11|21<<1) // fadd-class word
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecFPUnavail {
		t.Fatalf("fp: PC=%#x, want FP unavailable vector", c.PC)
	}

	// Privileged instruction in user mode.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	c.MSR |= MSRPR
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 3, 0, 0, 146, false)) // mtmsr r3
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecProgram || c.SRR1&SRR1ProgPrivileged == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("priv: PC=%#x SRR1=%#x", c.PC, c.SRR1)
	}
}

func TestAlignmentFaults(t *testing.T) {
	// lmw at a non-word-aligned address.
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2002
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, insD(46, 5, 4, 0)) // lmw r5, 0(r4)
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecAlignment || c.DAR != 0x2002 {
		t.Fatalf("lmw align: PC=%#x DAR=%#x", c.PC, c.DAR)
	}

	// stwcx. at a non-word-aligned address.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2001
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 5, 0, 4, 150, false))
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.PC != 0xFFF00000+VecAlignment || c.DAR != 0x2001 {
		t.Fatalf("stwcx align: PC=%#x DAR=%#x", c.PC, c.DAR)
	}

	// Unaligned scalar lwz is performed, not faulted.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	bus.Write32(0x2000, 0xAABBCCDD)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2001
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, insD(32, 3, 4, 0))
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[3] != 0xBBCCDD00 {
		t.Fatalf("unaligned lwz = %#08x, want 0xBBCCDD00", c.GPR[3])
	}
}

func TestLoadStoreForms(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	c.GPR[3] = 0x11223344
	c.GPR[5] = 0x80000000
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		insD(36, 3, 4, 0),            // stw r3, 0(r4)
		insD(34, 6, 4, 1),            // lbz r6, 1(r4)
		insD(42, 7, 4, 0),            // lha r7, 0(r4)
		ins(31, 8, 0, 4, 534, false), // lwbrx r8, r0, r4
		ins(31, 3, 0, 4, 662, false), // stwbrx r3, r0, r4
		insD(32, 9, 4, 0),            // lwz r9, 0(r4)
		insD(37, 5, 4, 8),            // stwu r5, 8(r4)
	)
	steps(c, 7)
	if c.GPR[6] != 0x22 {
		t.Fatalf("lbz = %#x", c.GPR[6])
	}
	if c.GPR[7] != 0x1122 {
		t.Fatalf("lha = %#x", c.GPR[7])
	}
	if c.GPR[8] != 0x44332211 {
		t.Fatalf("lwbrx = %#08x", c.GPR[8])
	}
	// stwbrx wrote the byte-reversed word; lwz read it back.
	if c.GPR[9] != 0x44332211 {
		t.Fatalf("lwz after stwbrx = %#08x", c.GPR[9])
	}
	if bus.Read32(0x2008) != 0x80000000 || c.GPR[4] != 0x2008 {
		t.Fatalf("stwu: mem=%#08x r4=%#x", bus.Read32(0x2008), c.GPR[4])
	}

	// lmw/stw round trip.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.GPR[28+i] = 0xA0 + uint32(i)
	}
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		insD(47, 28, 4, 0), // stmw r28, 0(r4)
		insD(46, 28, 4, 0), // lmw r28, 0(r4) after clobber
	)
	c.Step()
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.GPR[28+i] = 0
	}
	c.Step()
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if c.GPR[28+i] != 0xA0+uint32(i) {
			t.Fatalf("lmw r%d = %#x", 28+i, c.GPR[28+i])
		}
	}
}

func TestLittleEndianAccess(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.MSR |= MSRLE
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2000
	c.GPR[3] = 0x11223344
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, insD(36, 3, 4, 0)) // stw
	// In LE mode the instruction word itself is fetched
	// byte-swapped; emulate that by storing it swapped.
	bus.Write32(0x1000, swap32(insD(36, 3, 4, 0)))
	c.PC = 0x1000
	steps(c, 1)
	if got := bus.b[0x2000]; got != 0x44 {
		t.Fatalf("LE stw first byte = %#x, want 0x44", got)
	}
	if bus.Read32(0x2000) != 0x44332211 {
		t.Fatalf("LE stw word (BE read) = %#08x", bus.Read32(0x2000))
	}
}

func TestSPRAndZeroRule(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.GPR[0] = 0x77777777
	lrField := uint32((8&0x1F)<<5 | 8>>5) // SPR 8 (LR), scrambled
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		insD(14, 3, 0, 5),               // addi r3, r0, 5 (r0 reads as 0)
		31<<26|4<<21|lrField<<11|339<<1, // mfspr r4, LR
	)
	c.LR = 0xCAFEBABE
	steps(c, 2)
	if c.GPR[3] != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("addi r0 rule: r3 = %#x", c.GPR[3])
	}
	if c.GPR[4] != 0xCAFEBABE {
		t.Fatalf("mfspr LR: r4 = %#08x", c.GPR[4])
	}
	if got := c.GetSPR(SPRPVR); got != PVRGekko {
		t.Fatalf("PVR = %#08x", got)
	}
	// SPR storage round trip through instructions.
	bus = newRAM()
	c = New(bus)
	c.GPR[3] = 0x0BADF00D
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000,
		ins(31, 3, 0, 0, 467, false), // mtspr (field encodes SPR below)
		ins(31, 4, 0, 0, 339, false), // mfspr r4
	)
	// Patch both words with the SPRG1 field encoding.
	spr := uint32(SPRSPRG0 + 1)
	f := (spr&0x1F)<<5 | spr>>5
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w := bus.Read32(0x1000 + uint32(4*i))
		w = w&^(0x3FF<<11) | f<<11
		bus.Write32(0x1000+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
	steps(c, 2)
	if c.GPR[4] != 0x0BADF00D {
		t.Fatalf("SPRG round trip: r4 = %#08x", c.GPR[4])
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	c.GPR[3] = 0x11111111
	c.GPR[31] = 0x22222222
	c.FPR[7] = 0x3FF0000000000000
	c.CR = 0x12345678
	c.XER = 0xA0000005
	c.LR = 0x80004000
	c.CTR = 99
	c.MSR |= MSRDR | MSREE
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U, 0x8000001E)
	c.SetSPR(SPRDBAT0U+1, 2)
	c.SetSPR(SPRDEC, 12345)
	c.TB = 0x1122334455667788
	c.SR[3] = 0x0BADBEEF
	state := c.Serialize()
	if len(state) != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(state), SerializeSize)
	}
	c2 := New(newRAM())
	if err := c2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(c2.Serialize(), state) {
		t.Fatalf("serialize after deserialize differs")
	}
	if c2.GPR[3] != 0x11111111 || c2.TB != 0x1122334455667788 ||
		c2.Decrementer() != 12345 || c2.SR[3] != 0x0BADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("restored state mismatch")
	}
	if err := c2.Deserialize(state[:100]); err != ErrStateSize {
		t.Fatalf("short state: err = %v", err)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/chips/gekko/logical_test.go ====================

package gekko

import "testing"

// TestLogicalXFormFieldLayout pins the architected field
// layout of the register logical instructions (GCN-4):
// the source sits in the f1 field (rS), the destination
// in the f2 field (rA), the second source in f3 (rB),
// the same layout andi. and ori use in D form and the
// shifts use in X form. The GCN-4 enginetest fixture
// caught an earlier build writing the result into the
// f1 register; these vectors use distinct source and
// destination registers so the fields cannot be swapped
// without failing.
func TestLogicalXFormFieldLayout(t *testing.T) {
	const (
		xoAnd  = 28
		xoAndc = 60
		xoOr   = 444
		xoOrc  = 412
		xoXor  = 316
		xoNand = 476
		xoNor  = 124
		xoEqv  = 284
	)
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		xo   uint32
		a    uint32 // rS value, f1 field
		b    uint32 // rB value, f3 field
		want uint32
	}{
		{"and", xoAnd, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0x00F00F00},
		{"andc", xoAndc, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0xF000F000},
		{"or", xoOr, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0xFFF0FFF0},
		{"orc", xoOrc, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0xF0FFFF0F},
		{"xor", xoXor, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0xFF00F0F0},
		{"nand", xoNand, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0xFF0FF0FF},
		{"nor", xoNor, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0x000F000F},
		{"eqv", xoEqv, 0xF0F0FF00, 0x0FF00FF0, 0x00FF0F0F},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		bus := newRAM()
		c := New(bus)
		// or r7, r5, r6 shape: f1 = rS = 5, f2 = rA = 7,
		// f3 = rB = 6. Sources in r5 and r6, the result
		// must land in r7 and leave r5 untouched.
		prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 5, 7, 6, tc.xo, false))
		c.GPR[5] = tc.a
		c.GPR[6] = tc.b
		c.GPR[7] = 0xDEADBEEF
		steps(c, 1)
		if c.GPR[7] != tc.want {
			t.Fatalf("%s: r7 = %#x, want %#x", tc.name, c.GPR[7], tc.want)
		}
		if c.GPR[5] != tc.a {
			t.Fatalf("%s: source r5 clobbered: %#x", tc.name, c.GPR[5])
		}
		if c.GPR[6] != tc.b {
			t.Fatalf("%s: source r6 clobbered: %#x", tc.name, c.GPR[6])
		}
	}

	// mr r29, r3 (or r29, r3, r3) moves without touching
	// the source: the exact shape the GCN-4 fixture opens
	// with to save the boot argument.
	bus := newRAM()
	c := New(bus)
	prog(c, bus, 0x1000, ins(31, 3, 29, 3, xoOr, false))
	c.GPR[3] = 0x80005100
	steps(c, 1)
	if c.GPR[29] != 0x80005100 || c.GPR[3] != 0x80005100 {
		t.Fatalf("mr r29, r3: r29 = %#x, r3 = %#x", c.GPR[29], c.GPR[3])
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/chips/gekko/ps.go ====================

package gekko

import (
	"math"
)

// Paired single support: arithmetic on the two packed
// single lanes of an FPR, the quantized loads and stores
// driven by the GQRs, and dcbz_l.
//
// GQR layout (PowerPC bit numbers, stored in a uint32 with
// bit 0 at value 1<<31):
//
//	bits 2..7   LD_SCALE (value bits 29..24, signed 6-bit)
//	bits 13..15 LD_TYPE  (value bits 18..16)
//	bits 18..23 ST_SCALE (value bits 13..8, signed 6-bit)
//	bits 29..31 ST_TYPE  (value bits 2..0)
//
// Type codes, from the Gekko manual's quantized data type
// table: 0 float (no conversion), 1..3 reserved, 4 unsigned
// 8-bit, 5 unsigned 16-bit, 6 signed 8-bit, 7 signed 16-bit.
// Reserved codes are treated as float pass-through in this
// core (boundedly undefined on hardware).
const (
	gqrTypeFloat = 0
	gqrTypeU8    = 4
	gqrTypeU16   = 5
	gqrTypeS8    = 6
	gqrTypeS16   = 7
)

func gqrLoadScale(g uint32) int  { return sign6(int(g>>24) & 0x3F) }
func gqrLoadType(g uint32) int   { return int(g>>16) & 7 }
func gqrStoreScale(g uint32) int { return sign6(int(g>>8) & 0x3F) }
func gqrStoreType(g uint32) int  { return int(g) & 7 }
func sign6(v int) int {
	if v&0x20 != 0 {
		return v - 64
	}
	return v
}

// gqrTypeSize is the memory size in bytes of one quantized
// element of the given type.
func gqrTypeSize(t int) int {
	switch t {
	case gqrTypeU8, gqrTypeS8:
		return 1
	case gqrTypeU16, gqrTypeS16:
		return 2
	default: // float and reserved
		return 4
	}
}

// psLaneBits returns one packed lane of a register: lane 0
// is PS0, the high word; lane 1 is PS1, the low word.
func (c *CPU) psLaneBits(reg, lane int) uint32 {
	if lane == 0 {
		return uint32(c.FPR[reg] >> 32)
	}
	return uint32(c.FPR[reg])
}

func (c *CPU) setPair(reg int, ps0, ps1 uint32) {
	c.FPR[reg] = uint64(ps0)<<32 | uint64(ps1)
}

// psLane returns one lane as an operand descriptor with the
// NI input flush applied in single terms.
func (c *CPU) psLane(reg, lane int) fpDesc {
	return descSingle(c.flushNISingleValue(c.psLaneBits(reg, lane)))
}

// dequantize converts one integer element read from memory
// to a single, following the manual formula F = I * 2^(-S)
// where S is the signed LD_SCALE: the scale is subtracted
// from the exponent. The product is exact in a single (the
// integer has at most 16 bits), as the scale test in
// ps_test.go pins for scale 5: I=32 gives exactly 1.0.
func dequantize(raw uint32, typ, scale int) uint32 {
	var iv int64
	switch typ {
	case gqrTypeU8:
		iv = int64(raw & 0xFF)
	case gqrTypeS8:
		iv = int64(int8(raw))
	case gqrTypeU16:
		iv = int64(raw & 0xFFFF)
	case gqrTypeS16:
		iv = int64(int16(raw))
	default:
		return raw // float and reserved pass through
	}
	f := float64(iv) * math.Ldexp(1, -scale)
	return math.Float32bits(float32(f))
}

// quantize converts one single lane to the integer bit
// pattern stored to memory, following the manual formula
// I = ROUND(F * 2^S) with S the signed ST_SCALE, where ROUND
// rounds toward zero and then clamps to the type range.
// NaN and +Inf convert to the positive clamp value and -Inf
// to the negative clamp value (zero for unsigned types), as
// the manual's overflow adjustment specifies.
func quantize(bits uint32, typ, scale int) uint32 {
	switch typ {
	case gqrTypeU8, gqrTypeU16, gqrTypeS8, gqrTypeS16:
	default:
		return bits // float and reserved pass through
	}
	var lo, hi int64
	switch typ {
	case gqrTypeU8:
		lo, hi = 0, 255
	case gqrTypeU16:
		lo, hi = 0, 65535
	case gqrTypeS8:
		lo, hi = -128, 127
	case gqrTypeS16:
		lo, hi = -32768, 32767
	}
	f := math.Float32frombits(bits)
	if math.IsNaN(float64(f)) || math.IsInf(float64(f), 1) {
		return uint32(hi)
	}
	if math.IsInf(float64(f), -1) {
		return uint32(lo) & 0xFFFF
	}
	scaled := math.Trunc(float64(f) * math.Ldexp(1, scale))
	if scaled >= float64(hi) {
		return uint32(hi)
	}
	if scaled <= float64(lo) {
		return uint32(lo) & 0xFFFF
	}
	return uint32(int64(scaled)) & 0xFFFF
}

// psqLoadOne loads and dequantizes one element at ea.
func (c *CPU) psqLoadOne(ea uint32, g uint32) uint32 {
	typ := gqrLoadType(g)
	sz := gqrTypeSize(typ)
	if sz > 1 && ea%uint32(sz) != 0 {
		c.alignFault(ea)
	}
	raw := c.load(ea, sz)
	return dequantize(raw, typ, gqrLoadScale(g))
}

// psqStoreOne quantizes and stores one lane at ea.
func (c *CPU) psqStoreOne(ea uint32, bits uint32, g uint32) {
	typ := gqrStoreType(g)
	sz := gqrTypeSize(typ)
	if sz > 1 && ea%uint32(sz) != 0 {
		c.alignFault(ea)
	}
	v := quantize(bits, typ, gqrStoreScale(g))
	c.store(ea, sz, v)
}

// execPSQ executes a quantized load or store given its
// effective address and fields. update writes EA back to rA
// after the transfer, except when rA is 0, which names the
// literal base 0 and has no update target.
func (c *CPU) execPSQ(op, reg, ra int, ea uint32, wBit, gi int, update bool) {
	g := c.GQR[gi&7]
	sz := uint32(gqrTypeSize(gqrLoadType(g)))
	if op == 60 || op == 61 {
		sz = uint32(gqrTypeSize(gqrStoreType(g)))
	}
	switch op {
	case 56, 57: // psq_l, psq_lu
		ps0 := c.psqLoadOne(ea, g)
		ps1 := math.Float32bits(1.0)
		if wBit == 0 {
			ps1 = c.psqLoadOne(ea+sz, g)
		}
		c.setPair(reg, ps0, ps1)
	case 60, 61: // psq_st, psq_stu
		c.psqStoreOne(ea, c.psLaneBits(reg, 0), g)
		if wBit == 0 {
			c.psqStoreOne(ea+sz, c.psLaneBits(reg, 1), g)
		}
	}
	if update && ra != 0 {
		c.GPR[ra] = ea
	}
}

// execPSQD handles the D-form quantized instructions:
// primary 56 psq_l, 57 psq_lu, 60 psq_st, 61 psq_stu. The
// displacement is a signed 12-bit field; the bits above it
// carry W (bit 16) and the 3-bit GQR index I (bits 17..19).
func (c *CPU) execPSQD(w uint32) {
	c.fpAvail()
	op := int(w >> 26)
	reg := f1(w)
	ra := f2(w)
	wBit := int(w>>15) & 1
	gi := int(w>>12) & 7
	disp := int(w & 0xFFF)
	if disp&0x800 != 0 {
		disp -= 0x1000
	}
	ea := c.base(ra) + uint32(int32(disp))
	c.execPSQ(op, reg, ra, ea, wBit, gi, op == 57 || op == 61)
}

// execPS is the primary opcode 4 dispatch: paired single
// arithmetic and moves, the indexed quantized forms, the
// paired compares, and dcbz_l.
func (c *CPU) execPS(w uint32) {
	// dcbz_l is a cache instruction, not a floating point
	// one, so it is dispatched before the FP gate.
	if xo(w) == 1014 {
		ea := (c.base(f2(w)) + c.GPR[f3(w)]) &^ 31
		for i := uint32(0); i < 32; i += 4 {
			c.store(ea+i, 4, 0)
		}
		return
	}
	// The indexed quantized forms spend the low 6 bits of
	// the X field on their sub-opcode (6, 7, 38, 39) and
	// the four bits above it on W and I.
	if w&1 == 0 {
		switch (w >> 1) & 0x3F {
		case 6, 7, 38, 39: // psq_lx, psq_stx, psq_lux, psq_stux
			c.fpAvail()
			sub := (w >> 1) & 0x3F
			reg := f1(w)
			ra := f2(w)
			ea := c.base(ra) + c.GPR[f3(w)]
			wBit := int(w>>10) & 1
			gi := int(w>>7) & 7
			op := 56
			if sub == 7 || sub == 39 {
				op = 60
			}
			c.execPSQ(op, reg, ra, ea, wBit, gi, sub == 38 || sub == 39)
			return
		}
	}

	c.fpAvail()
	d := f1(w)
	a := f2(w)
	b := f3(w)
	cc := cField(w)
	rc := w&1 != 0
	f := fmtSingle

	// X forms on the full 10-bit extended opcode.
	switch xo(w) {
	case 0, 32, 64, 96: // ps_cmpu0, ps_cmpo0, ps_cmpu1, ps_cmpo1
		crfD := int(w>>23) & 7
		lane := 0
		if xo(w) >= 64 {
			lane = 1
		}
		ordered := xo(w) == 32 || xo(w) == 96
		c.fpComparePair(c.psLane(a, lane), c.psLane(b, lane), ordered, crfD)
		return
	case 40, 72, 136, 264: // ps_neg, ps_mr, ps_nabs, ps_abs
		p0, p1 := c.psLaneBits(b, 0), c.psLaneBits(b, 1)
		switch xo(w) {
		case 40:
			p0 ^= 1 << 31
			p1 ^= 1 << 31
		case 136:
			p0 |= 1 << 31
			p1 |= 1 << 31
		case 264:
			p0 &^= 1 << 31
			p1 &^= 1 << 31
		}
		c.setPair(d, p0, p1)
		if rc {
			c.recordCR1()
		}
		return
	case 528, 560, 592, 624: // ps_merge00, 01, 10, 11
		a0, a1 := c.psLaneBits(a, 0), c.psLaneBits(a, 1)
		b0, b1 := c.psLaneBits(b, 0), c.psLaneBits(b, 1)
		var p0, p1 uint32
		switch xo(w) {
		case 528:
			p0, p1 = a0, b0
		case 560:
			p0, p1 = a0, b1
		case 592:
			p0, p1 = a1, b0
		case 624:
			p0, p1 = a1, b1
		}
		c.setPair(d, p0, p1)
		if rc {
			c.recordCR1()
		}
		return
	}

	// A forms on the 5-bit extended opcode. All source lanes
	// are read before the destination is written, so a
	// destination that aliases a source behaves correctly.
	a0, a1 := c.psLane(a, 0), c.psLane(a, 1)
	b0, b1 := c.psLane(b, 0), c.psLane(b, 1)
	c0, c1 := c.psLane(cc, 0), c.psLane(cc, 1)
	rawA0, rawA1 := c.psLaneBits(a, 0), c.psLaneBits(a, 1)
	rawB0, rawB1 := c.psLaneBits(b, 0), c.psLaneBits(b, 1)
	rawC0, rawC1 := c.psLaneBits(cc, 0), c.psLaneBits(cc, 1)
	_ = rawA0
	_ = rawA1

	pair := func(r0 uint64, st0 fpStatus, r1 uint64, st1 fpStatus) {
		c.setPair(d, uint32(r0), uint32(r1))
		st0.merge(st1)
		c.applyFPStatus(st0, rc)
	}
	binPair := func(op func(x, y fpDesc) (uint64, fpStatus)) {
		r0, s0 := op(a0, b0)
		r1, s1 := op(a1, b1)
		pair(r0, s0, r1, s1)
	}

	switch aFormXO(w) {
	case 21: // ps_add
		binPair(func(x, y fpDesc) (uint64, fpStatus) { return c.addDesc(x, y, f) })
	case 20: // ps_sub
		binPair(func(x, y fpDesc) (uint64, fpStatus) { return c.addDesc(x, y.negated(), f) })
	case 18: // ps_div
		binPair(func(x, y fpDesc) (uint64, fpStatus) { return c.divOp(x, y, f) })
	case 25: // ps_mul
		r0, s0 := c.mulOp(a0, c0, f)
		r1, s1 := c.mulOp(a1, c1, f)
		pair(r0, s0, r1, s1)
	case 28, 29, 30, 31: // ps_msub, ps_madd, ps_nmsub, ps_nmadd
		xo := aFormXO(w)
		negProd := xo == 30 || xo == 31
		negAdd := xo == 28 || xo == 31
		r0, s0 := c.fmaOp(a0, c0, b0, negProd, negAdd, f)
		r1, s1 := c.fmaOp(a1, c1, b1, negProd, negAdd, f)
		pair(r0, s0, r1, s1)
	case 12, 13: // ps_muls0, ps_muls1
		cs := c0
		if aFormXO(w) == 13 {
			cs = c1
		}
		r0, s0 := c.mulOp(a0, cs, f)
		r1, s1 := c.mulOp(a1, cs, f)
		pair(r0, s0, r1, s1)
	case 14, 15: // ps_madds0, ps_madds1
		cs := c0
		if aFormXO(w) == 15 {
			cs = c1
		}
		r0, s0 := c.fmaOp(a0, cs, b0, false, false, f)
		r1, s1 := c.fmaOp(a1, cs, b1, false, false, f)
		pair(r0, s0, r1, s1)
	case 10, 11: // ps_sum0, ps_sum1
		// Manual operation: the sum is frA(ps0) + frB(ps1)
		// in both forms. ps_sum0 places it in ps0 and copies
		// frC(ps1) into ps1; ps_sum1 copies frC(ps0) into
		// ps0 and places the sum in ps1. FPRF follows the
		// lane that received the sum.
		r, s := c.addDesc(a0, b1, f)
		if aFormXO(w) == 10 {
			c.setPair(d, uint32(r), rawC1)
		} else {
			c.setPair(d, rawC0, uint32(r))
		}
		c.applyFPStatus(s, rc)
	case 23: // ps_sel: frA lane >= 0 selects frC lane, else frB lane
		sel := func(ad fpDesc, rb, rcBits uint32) uint32 {
			if !ad.kind.isNaN() && (!ad.neg || ad.kind.isZero()) {
				return rcBits
			}
			return rb
		}
		c.setPair(d, sel(a0, rawB0, rawC0), sel(a1, rawB1, rawC1))
		if rc {
			c.recordCR1()
		}
	case 24: // ps_res: exact reciprocal per lane
		r0, s0 := c.recipOp(b0, f)
		r1, s1 := c.recipOp(b1, f)
		pair(r0, s0, r1, s1)
	case 26: // ps_rsqrte: exact 1/sqrt per lane (see fp.go)
		r0, s0 := c.recipSqrtOp(b0, f)
		r1, s1 := c.recipSqrtOp(b1, f)
		pair(r0, s0, r1, s1)
	default:
		c.illegalAt()
	}
}

// fpComparePair is the paired compare core: same FPCC and
// CR rules as the scalar compares in fp_exec.go.
func (c *CPU) fpComparePair(da, db fpDesc, ordered bool, crfD int) {
	var st fpStatus
	unordered := da.kind.isNaN() || db.kind.isNaN()
	if da.kind == classSNaN || db.kind == classSNaN {
		st.invalid |= fpscrVXSNAN
	} else if unordered && ordered {
		st.invalid |= fpscrVXVC
	}
	var nib uint32
	switch {
	case unordered:
		nib = 1
		st.fprf = fprfQNaN
	default:
		fa, fb := descValue(da), descValue(db)
		switch {
		case fa < fb:
			nib = 8
			st.fprf = fprfNegNorm
		case fa > fb:
			nib = 4
			st.fprf = fprfPosNorm
		default:
			nib = 2
			st.fprf = fprfPosZero
		}
	}
	c.applyFPStatus(st, false)
	c.setCRField(crfD, nib)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/chips/gekko/ps_test.go ====================

package gekko

import (
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// GCN-2 paired single gates.

// psA builds an opcode 4 A-form word.
func psA(d, a, b, cc, xo5, rc int) uint32 { return fa(4, d, a, b, cc, xo5, rc) }

// psX builds an opcode 4 X-form word.
func psX(d, a, b, xo10, rc int) uint32 {
	return 4<<26 | uint32(d)<<21 | uint32(a)<<16 |
		uint32(b)<<11 | uint32(xo10)<<1 | uint32(rc)
}

func pairOf(x, y float32) (uint32, uint32) {
	return math.Float32bits(x), math.Float32bits(y)
}

func setPairF(c *CPU, reg int, x, y float32) {
	p0, p1 := pairOf(x, y)
	c.setPair(reg, p0, p1)
}

func getPairF(c *CPU, reg int) (float32, float32) {
	return math.Float32frombits(uint32(c.FPR[reg] >> 32)),
		math.Float32frombits(uint32(c.FPR[reg]))
}

func TestPSLaneArithmetic(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	setPairF(c, 1, 2, 3)
	setPairF(c, 2, 10, 20)
	setPairF(c, 3, 5, 7)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		psA(4, 1, 2, 3, 12, 0), // ps_muls0 f4, f1, f3 -> (2*5, 3*5)
		psA(5, 1, 2, 3, 13, 0), // ps_muls1 f5, f1, f3 -> (2*7, 3*7)
		psA(6, 1, 2, 0, 21, 0), // ps_add f6, f1, f2   -> (12, 23)
		psA(7, 2, 1, 0, 20, 0), // ps_sub f7, f2, f1   -> (8, 17)
		psA(8, 1, 2, 3, 25, 0), // ps_mul f8, f1, f3   -> (10, 21)
	)
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 4); x != 10 || y != 15 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_muls0: got (%v,%v), want (10,15)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 5); x != 14 || y != 21 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_muls1: got (%v,%v), want (14,21)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 6); x != 12 || y != 23 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_add: got (%v,%v), want (12,23)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 7); x != 8 || y != 17 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_sub: got (%v,%v), want (8,17)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 8); x != 10 || y != 21 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_mul: got (%v,%v), want (10,21)", x, y)
	}
	// ps_madd and ps_div.
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100,
		psA(9, 1, 2, 3, 29, 0),  // ps_madd f9, f1, f2, f3 -> (2*5+10, 3*7+20)
		psA(10, 2, 1, 0, 18, 0), // ps_div f10, f2, f1    -> (5, 20/3)
	)
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 9); x != 20 || y != 41 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_madd: got (%v,%v), want (20,41)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 10); x != 5 || y != float32(20)/float32(3) {
		t.Fatalf("ps_div: got (%v,%v)", x, y)
	}
	// ps_madds0 multiplies both lanes by frC ps0.
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1200, psA(11, 1, 2, 3, 14, 0)) // (2*5+10, 3*5+20)
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 11); x != 20 || y != 35 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_madds0: got (%v,%v), want (20,35)", x, y)
	}
}

func TestPSSumCrossLane(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	setPairF(c, 1, 1, 100) // frA
	setPairF(c, 2, 10, 2)  // frB: its ps1 (2) feeds the sum
	setPairF(c, 3, 20, 30) // frC: copied lane source
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		psA(4, 1, 2, 3, 10, 0), // ps_sum0: (A0+B1, C1) = (3, 30)
		psA(5, 1, 2, 3, 11, 0), // ps_sum1: (C0, A0+B1) = (20, 3)
	)
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 4); x != 3 || y != 30 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_sum0: got (%v,%v), want (3,30)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 5); x != 20 || y != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_sum1: got (%v,%v), want (20,3)", x, y)
	}
}

func TestPSMergeAndMoves(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	setPairF(c, 1, 1, 2)
	setPairF(c, 2, 3, 4)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		psX(3, 1, 2, 528, 0), // ps_merge00 -> (1,3)
		psX(4, 1, 2, 560, 0), // ps_merge01 -> (1,4)
		psX(5, 1, 2, 592, 0), // ps_merge10 -> (2,3)
		psX(6, 1, 2, 624, 0), // ps_merge11 -> (2,4)
	)
	wants := [][2]float32{{1, 3}, {1, 4}, {2, 3}, {2, 4}}
	for i, wnt := range wants {
		if x, y := getPairF(c, 3+i); x != wnt[0] || y != wnt[1] {
			t.Fatalf("merge %d: got (%v,%v), want %v", i, x, y, wnt)
		}
	}
	setPairF(c, 1, -1.5, 2.5)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100,
		psX(3, 0, 1, 40, 0),  // ps_neg -> (1.5, -2.5)
		psX(4, 0, 1, 264, 0), // ps_abs -> (1.5, 2.5)
		psX(5, 0, 1, 136, 0), // ps_nabs -> (-1.5, -2.5)
		psX(6, 0, 1, 72, 0),  // ps_mr  -> (-1.5, 2.5)
	)
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 3); x != 1.5 || y != -2.5 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_neg: (%v,%v)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 4); x != 1.5 || y != 2.5 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_abs: (%v,%v)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 5); x != -1.5 || y != -2.5 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_nabs: (%v,%v)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 6); x != -1.5 || y != 2.5 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_mr: (%v,%v)", x, y)
	}
}

func TestPSSelResCmp(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	setPairF(c, 1, 1, -1)                         // frA: the per-lane condition
	setPairF(c, 2, 10, 20)                        // frB: taken when frA lane < 0
	setPairF(c, 3, 30, 40)                        // frC: taken when frA lane >= 0
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, psA(4, 1, 2, 3, 23, 0)) // ps_sel f4, f1, f2, f3
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 4); x != 30 || y != 20 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_sel: got (%v,%v), want (30,20)", x, y)
	}
	// ps_res and ps_rsqrte are the documented approximate
	// pair; here the inputs make the exact values
	// representable, so the results are exact too.
	setPairF(c, 5, 4, 0.25)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100,
		psA(6, 0, 5, 0, 24, 0), // ps_res f6, f5 -> (0.25, 4)
		psA(7, 0, 5, 0, 26, 0), // ps_rsqrte f7, f5 -> (0.5, 2)
	)
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 6); x != 0.25 || y != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_res: got (%v,%v), want (0.25,4)", x, y)
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 7); x != 0.5 || y != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_rsqrte: got (%v,%v), want (0.5,2)", x, y)
	}
	// ps_cmpu0 compares the ps0 lanes only: 9 vs 1 in ps1
	// must not matter.
	setPairF(c, 1, 1, 9)
	setPairF(c, 2, 2, 1)
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1200, psX(0, 1, 2, 0, 0)) // ps_cmpu0 cr0, f1, f2
	if nib := (c.CR >> 28) & 0xF; nib != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_cmpu0: CR0=%04b, want 1000 (less)", nib)
	}
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1300, psX(0, 1, 2, 64, 0)) // ps_cmpu1: 9 vs 1, greater
	if nib := (c.CR >> 28) & 0xF; nib != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("ps_cmpu1: CR0=%04b, want 0100 (greater)", nib)
	}
}

// makeGQR packs a GQR value from its fields.
func makeGQR(ldScale, ldType, stScale, stType int) uint32 {
	return uint32(ldScale&0x3F)<<24 | uint32(ldType)<<16 |
		uint32(stScale&0x3F)<<8 | uint32(stType)
}

// psqD builds a primary 56/57/60/61 word.
func psqD(op, fr, ra, wBit, gi, disp int) uint32 {
	return uint32(op)<<26 | uint32(fr)<<21 | uint32(ra)<<16 |
		uint32(wBit)<<15 | uint32(gi)<<12 | uint32(disp&0xFFF)
}

func TestPSQScaleProof(t *testing.T) {
	// Dequantize proof from the manual pseudocode: the
	// scale is subtracted from the exponent, so the loaded
	// float is I * 2^(-S). With S = 5 and I = 32 (s16) the
	// value is exactly 32 * 2^-5 = 1.0. The opposite sign
	// convention would give 1024.0 and fail here.
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.SetSPR(SPRGQR0+2, makeGQR(5, gqrTypeS16, 5, gqrTypeS16))
	bus.Write32(0x3000, 0x0020FF9C) // s16 elements 32 and -100
	c.GPR[4] = 0x3000
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, psqD(56, 3, 4, 0, 2, 0)) // psq_l f3, 0(r4), gqr2
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 3); x != 1.0 || y != -100.0/32 {
		t.Fatalf("psq_l scale5: got (%v,%v), want (1, %v)", x, y, -100.0/32)
	}
}

func TestPSQRoundTrips(t *testing.T) {
	types := []struct {
		typ  int
		size int
		raw  []uint32 // raw element patterns, 2 elements per case
	}{
		{gqrTypeU8, 1, []uint32{200, 3}},
		{gqrTypeU16, 2, []uint32{60000, 1234}},
		{gqrTypeS8, 1, []uint32{0x80, 0x7F}},      // -128, 127
		{gqrTypeS16, 2, []uint32{0x8000, 0x7FFF}}, // -32768, 32767
		{gqrTypeS16, 2, []uint32{0xCFC7, 0x03E7}}, // -12345, 999
	}
	for _, scale := range []int{0, 5} {
		for _, tc := range types {
			c, bus := fpCPU()
			c.SetSPR(SPRGQR0+1, makeGQR(scale, tc.typ, scale, tc.typ))
			// Write the raw elements big-endian.
			base := uint32(0x3000)
			for i, r := range tc.raw {
				switch tc.size {
				case 1:
					bus.Write8(base+uint32(i), uint8(r))
				case 2:
					bus.Write16(base+uint32(i*2), uint16(r))
				}
			}
			c.GPR[4] = base
			runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
				psqD(56, 3, 4, 0, 1, 0),    // psq_l f3
				psqD(60, 3, 4, 0, 1, 0x40), // psq_st f3 at +0x40
			)
			for i, r := range tc.raw {
				var got uint32
				switch tc.size {
				case 1:
					got = uint32(bus.Read8(base + 0x40 + uint32(i)))
				case 2:
					got = uint32(bus.Read16(base + 0x40 + uint32(i*2)))
				}
				if got != r {
					t.Fatalf("typ=%d scale=%d elem=%d: round trip got %#x, want %#x",
						tc.typ, scale, i, got, r)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	// Float type ignores the scales entirely.
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.SetSPR(SPRGQR0+0, makeGQR(5, gqrTypeFloat, 5, gqrTypeFloat))
	bus.Write32(0x3000, math.Float32bits(1.25))
	bus.Write32(0x3004, math.Float32bits(-0.5))
	c.GPR[4] = 0x3000
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
		psqD(56, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0),
		psqD(60, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0x20),
	)
	if got := bus.Read32(0x3020); got != math.Float32bits(1.25) {
		t.Fatalf("float psq_st ps0: %#x", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read32(0x3024); got != math.Float32bits(-0.5) {
		t.Fatalf("float psq_st ps1: %#x", got)
	}
	// Store clamping: a too-large u8 value clamps to 255.
	c, bus = fpCPU()
	c.SetSPR(SPRGQR0+0, makeGQR(0, gqrTypeU8, 0, gqrTypeU8))
	setPairF(c, 3, 300, -5)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x3100
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, psqD(60, 3, 4, 0, 0, 0))
	if bus.Read8(0x3100) != 255 || bus.Read8(0x3101) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("u8 clamp: got %d,%d want 255,0", bus.Read8(0x3100), bus.Read8(0x3101))
	}
}

func TestPSQForms(t *testing.T) {
	// W=1 load: only PS0 transfers, PS1 becomes 1.0.
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	c.SetSPR(SPRGQR0+0, makeGQR(0, gqrTypeFloat, 0, gqrTypeFloat))
	bus.Write32(0x3000, math.Float32bits(7.5))
	bus.Write32(0x3004, math.Float32bits(9.5))
	c.GPR[4] = 0x3000
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, psqD(56, 3, 4, 1, 0, 0))
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 3); x != 7.5 || y != 1.0 {
		t.Fatalf("psq_l W=1: got (%v,%v), want (7.5,1)", x, y)
	}
	// W=1 store writes only PS0; the second slot keeps its
	// sentinel.
	bus.Write32(0x3104, 0xDEADBEEF)
	setPairF(c, 3, 2.25, 8.75)
	c.GPR[4] = 0x3100
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1100, psqD(60, 3, 4, 1, 0, 0))
	if got := bus.Read32(0x3100); got != math.Float32bits(2.25) {
		t.Fatalf("psq_st W=1 ps0: %#x", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read32(0x3104); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("psq_st W=1 wrote ps1 slot: %#x", got)
	}
	// Update load writes EA back to rA.
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2FF0
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1200, psqD(57, 5, 4, 0, 0, 0x10)) // psq_lu f5, 0x10(r4)
	if c.GPR[4] != 0x3000 {
		t.Fatalf("psq_lu: r4=%#x, want 0x3000", c.GPR[4])
	}
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 5); x != 7.5 || y != 9.5 {
		t.Fatalf("psq_lu data: (%v,%v)", x, y)
	}
	// Indexed load: psq_lx with W/I in the X-form bits.
	c.GPR[4] = 0x2F00
	c.GPR[5] = 0x100
	word := uint32(4)<<26 | 6<<21 | 4<<16 | 5<<11 | 0<<10 | 0<<7 | 6<<1
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1300, word) // psq_lx f6, r4, r5, gqr0, W=0
	if x, y := getPairF(c, 6); x != 7.5 || y != 9.5 {
		t.Fatalf("psq_lx: (%v,%v)", x, y)
	}
}

func TestDCBZL(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	for i := 0; i < 96; i++ {
		bus.Write8(0x4000+uint32(i), 0xAA)
	}
	c.GPR[4] = 0x4000
	c.GPR[5] = 37                                // unaligned offset; the block is aligned down
	runAt(c, bus, 0x1000, psX(0, 4, 5, 1014, 0)) // dcbz_l r4, r5
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if bus.Read8(0x4020+uint32(i)) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("dcbz_l: byte %d of the aligned block not zeroed", i)
		}
	}
	if bus.Read8(0x401F) != 0xAA || bus.Read8(0x4040) != 0xAA {
		t.Fatalf("dcbz_l: bytes outside the block were touched")
	}
}

func TestPSMatrixVec4(t *testing.T) {
	// 4x4 matrix times vec4 with ps ops only: per row, two
	// ps_mul pairs, one ps_add, and one ps_sum0 horizontal
	// reduction. All values are small integers, so the
	// float32 pipeline and the float64 reference agree
	// exactly.
	m := [4][4]float32{{1, 2, 3, 4}, {0, 1, 0, 2}, {5, 0, 1, 1}, {2, 2, 2, 2}}
	v := [4]float32{5, 6, 7, 8}
	c, bus := fpCPU()
	setPairF(c, 20, v[0], v[1]) // vec low pair
	setPairF(c, 21, v[2], v[3]) // vec high pair
	for row := 0; row < 4; row++ {
		setPairF(c, 22, m[row][0], m[row][1])
		setPairF(c, 23, m[row][2], m[row][3])
		runAt(c, bus, 0x1000,
			psA(24, 22, 0, 20, 25, 0), // ps_mul t0, row01, vec01
			psA(25, 23, 0, 21, 25, 0), // ps_mul t1, row23, vec23
			psA(26, 24, 25, 0, 21, 0), // ps_add s, t0, t1
			psA(27, 26, 26, 0, 10, 0), // ps_sum0 out, s, s, anyC
		)
		got, _ := getPairF(c, 27)
		want := float64(0)
		for k := 0; k < 4; k++ {
			want += float64(m[row][k]) * float64(v[k])
		}
		if float64(got) != want {
			t.Fatalf("row %d: got %v, want %v", row, got, want)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/di/di.go ====================

// Package di models the GameCube disc interface: the
// status, cover, command buffer, configuration, DMA
// address and length, and control registers, plus the
// small synchronous command set games issue through the
// command buffers.
//
// The MMIO window base is 0x0C006000. All access here is
// through 16 bit lanes at offsets inside that window: a
// 32 bit register occupies two lanes, the high half at
// the even offset and the low half at the next offset.
// Side effects trigger on the low lane write.
//
// Commands run instantly and synchronously when TSTART
// is written: a simplification of the real drive, which
// seeks and reads over time, documented here because
// results (data in memory, TCINT, DILENGTH at zero) are
// already final when the DICR write returns.
package di

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Source is the inserted disc as the drive sees it.
type Source interface {
	// Read copies disc bytes at byte offset off into
	// dst and returns how many bytes were copied: a
	// short count, or zero, past the end of the disc.
	Read(off uint32, dst []byte) int
	// Header returns the disc identity fields used by
	// the Identify command.
	Header() (sysID byte, game, company string, discNo, version byte)
}

// Mem is physical MEM1 as the DI sees it, for DMA.
type Mem interface {
	Read8(addr uint32) uint8
	Write8(addr uint32, v uint8)
}

// DISR bits.
const (
	disrBRK       = 1 << 0
	disrDEINT     = 1 << 1 // drive error interrupt, write 1 to clear
	disrDEINTMSK  = 1 << 2
	disrTCINT     = 1 << 3 // transfer complete interrupt, write 1 to clear
	disrTCINTMSK  = 1 << 4
	disrBRKINT    = 1 << 5 // break interrupt, write 1 to clear
	disrBRKINTMSK = 1 << 6
	disrW1C       = disrDEINT | disrTCINT | disrBRKINT
)

// DICVR bits.
const (
	dicvrCVR       = 1 << 0 // cover open, set by SetCover only
	dicvrCVRINT    = 1 << 1 // cover interrupt, write 1 to clear
	dicvrCVRINTMSK = 1 << 2
)

// DICR bits.
const (
	dicrTSTART = 1 << 0 // write 1 to execute, always reads 0
	dicrDMA    = 1 << 1
	dicrRW     = 1 << 2 // set means a write command
)

// Register offsets inside the MMIO window.
const (
	regDISR    = 0x00
	regDICVR   = 0x04
	regCMDBUF0 = 0x08
	regCMDBUF1 = 0x0C
	regCMDBUF2 = 0x10
	regDICFG   = 0x14
	regDIMAR   = 0x18
	regDILEN   = 0x1C
	regDICR    = 0x20

	readbackSize     = 32
	serializeVersion = 1
)

// DI is the disc interface device.
type DI struct {
	src Source
	mem Mem

	disr  uint32
	dicvr uint32 // the CVR bit mirrors coverOpen
	cmd   [3]uint32
	dicfg uint32
	dimar uint32
	dilen uint32 // DMA bytes remaining, zero when done
	dicr  uint32 // TSTART is never stored, so it reads 0

	coverOpen bool
	stopped   bool   // set by the stop motor command
	audioCfg  uint32 // last audio family command word
	readback  [readbackSize]byte
	readLen   uint32 // valid bytes in readback
}

// New returns a disc interface in its reset state,
// backed by the disc src (nil means no disc inserted)
// and MEM1 mem for DMA transfers.
func New(src Source, mem Mem) *DI {
	d := &DI{src: src, mem: mem}
	d.Reset()
	return d
}

// Reset restores the power on state: every register
// zero except DICFG, which resets to 1, the cover
// closed, the motor running and no audio configuration.
func (d *DI) Reset() {
	src, mem := d.src, d.mem
	*d = DI{src: src, mem: mem, dicfg: 1}
}

// SetCover records the cover state. CVR follows it, and
// any change raises CVRINT; repeating the same state
// changes nothing.
func (d *DI) SetCover(open bool) {
	if open == d.coverOpen {
		return
	}
	d.coverOpen = open
	if open {
		d.dicvr |= dicvrCVR
	} else {
		d.dicvr &^= dicvrCVR
	}
	d.dicvr |= dicvrCVRINT
}

// IRQAsserted reports whether any interrupt source is
// both pending and unmasked.
func (d *DI) IRQAsserted() bool {
	return (d.disr&disrDEINT != 0 && d.disr&disrDEINTMSK != 0) ||
		(d.disr&disrTCINT != 0 && d.disr&disrTCINTMSK != 0) ||
		(d.disr&disrBRKINT != 0 && d.disr&disrBRKINTMSK != 0) ||
		(d.dicvr&dicvrCVRINT != 0 && d.dicvr&dicvrCVRINTMSK != 0)
}

// Stopped reports whether the stop motor command has
// stopped the drive motor.
func (d *DI) Stopped() bool { return d.stopped }

// AudioConfig returns the last audio family command
// word (top byte 0xE0, 0xE1 or 0xE2), or zero.
func (d *DI) AudioConfig() uint32 { return d.audioCfg }

// reg returns the register at a 32 bit base offset.
func (d *DI) reg(off uint32) uint32 {
	switch off {
	case regDISR:
		return d.disr
	case regDICVR:
		return d.dicvr
	case regCMDBUF0, regCMDBUF1, regCMDBUF2:
		return d.cmd[(off-regCMDBUF0)/4]
	case regDICFG:
		return d.dicfg
	case regDIMAR:
		return d.dimar
	case regDILEN:
		return d.dilen
	case regDICR:
		return d.dicr
	}
	return 0
}

// Read16 reads one 16 bit MMIO lane at off: the lane
// at the even offset of a register pair is its high
// half, the next lane its low half.
func (d *DI) Read16(off uint32) uint16 {
	v := d.reg(off &^ 2)
	if off&2 == 0 {
		return uint16(v >> 16)
	}
	return uint16(v)
}

// Write16 writes one 16 bit MMIO lane at off.
func (d *DI) Write16(off uint32, v uint16) {
	switch off {
	case regDISR:
		d.disr = d.disr&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
	case regDISR + 2:
		// Interrupt bits are write 1 to clear; the rest
		// of the low half is stored as written.
		low := (uint32(v) &^ disrW1C) | (d.disr & disrW1C &^ uint32(v))
		d.disr = d.disr&0xFFFF0000 | low
	case regDICVR:
		d.dicvr = d.dicvr&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
	case regDICVR + 2:
		// CVR is hardware state and ignores writes;
		// CVRINT is write 1 to clear.
		low := (uint32(v) &^ (dicvrCVR | dicvrCVRINT)) |
			(d.dicvr & dicvrCVR) |
			(d.dicvr & dicvrCVRINT &^ uint32(v))
		d.dicvr = d.dicvr&0xFFFF0000 | low
	case regCMDBUF0, regCMDBUF0 + 2, regCMDBUF1, regCMDBUF1 + 2, regCMDBUF2, regCMDBUF2 + 2:
		setLane(&d.cmd[(off&^2-regCMDBUF0)/4], off&2 != 0, v)
	case regDICFG, regDICFG + 2:
		setLane(&d.dicfg, off&2 != 0, v)
	case regDIMAR, regDIMAR + 2:
		setLane(&d.dimar, off&2 != 0, v)
	case regDILEN, regDILEN + 2:
		setLane(&d.dilen, off&2 != 0, v)
	case regDICR:
		d.dicr = d.dicr&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
	case regDICR + 2:
		d.dicr = d.dicr&0xFFFF0000 | uint32(v)&^dicrTSTART
		if v&dicrTSTART != 0 {
			d.execute()
		}
	}
}

// setLane merges one 16 bit lane into a 32 bit register:
// low is true for the lane at the odd half offset.
func setLane(reg *uint32, low bool, v uint16) {
	if low {
		*reg = *reg&0xFFFF0000 | uint32(v)
	} else {
		*reg = *reg&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
	}
}

// execute runs the command in the command buffers. See
// the package comment for the synchronous model.
func (d *DI) execute() {
	cmd0 := d.cmd[0]
	switch {
	case cmd0>>24 == 0xA8 && cmd0&0xFF == 0:
		d.cmdRead()
	case cmd0>>24 == 0xAD:
		d.cmdIdentify()
	case cmd0>>24 == 0xE3:
		// Stop motor: DEINT is the documented response
		// path for drive commands.
		d.stopped = true
		d.disr |= disrDEINT
	case cmd0>>24 == 0xE0 || cmd0>>24 == 0xE1 || cmd0>>24 == 0xE2:
		d.audioCfg = cmd0
		d.disr |= disrDEINT
	default:
		d.disr |= disrDEINT
	}
}

// dmaWrite copies data into MEM1 at DIMAR with its low
// 5 bits ignored, as DMA transfers require.
func (d *DI) dmaWrite(data []byte) {
	if d.mem == nil {
		return
	}
	base := d.dimar &^ 0x1F
	for i, b := range data {
		d.mem.Write8(base+uint32(i), b)
	}
}

// cmdRead runs the read command: CMDBUF1 shifted left
// by 2 is the disc offset and CMDBUF2 is the length.
func (d *DI) cmdRead() {
	if d.dicr&dicrRW != 0 {
		// A write command to a read only drive is an
		// error.
		d.disr |= disrDEINT
		return
	}
	if d.src == nil {
		d.disr |= disrDEINT
		return
	}
	off := d.cmd[1] << 2
	length := d.cmd[2]
	if d.dicr&dicrDMA == 0 {
		// Non DMA reads land in a small internal
		// readback buffer and leave the command buffers
		// unchanged, a documented simplification: games
		// use DMA reads.
		n := length
		if n > readbackSize {
			n = readbackSize
		}
		d.readback = [readbackSize]byte{}
		d.readLen = n
		got := d.src.Read(off, d.readback[:n])
		_ = got
		d.disr |= disrTCINT
		return
	}
	d.dilen = length
	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	done := uint32(0)
	for done < length {
		chunk := length - done
		if chunk > uint32(len(buf)) {
			chunk = uint32(len(buf))
		}
		n := d.src.Read(off+done, buf[:chunk])
		if n < 0 {
			n = 0
		}
		if n > int(chunk) {
			n = int(chunk)
		}
		// A short read past the end of the disc pads
		// with zeros so the transfer still completes.
		for i := n; i < int(chunk); i++ {
			buf[i] = 0
		}
		if d.mem != nil {
			base := (d.dimar &^ 0x1F) + done
			for i := uint32(0); i < chunk; i++ {
				d.mem.Write8(base+i, buf[i])
			}
		}
		done += chunk
		d.dilen -= chunk
	}
	d.disr |= disrTCINT
}

// cmdIdentify runs the identify command, which builds
// the 32 byte drive info block from the disc header:
// bytes 0 to 3 zero, the game code at bytes 4 to 5, the
// company code at bytes 6 to 7, the disc number at byte
// 8, the version at byte 9, the system ID at byte 10
// and zeros elsewhere.
func (d *DI) cmdIdentify() {
	if d.src == nil {
		d.disr |= disrDEINT
		return
	}
	sysID, game, company, discNo, version := d.src.Header()
	var block [readbackSize]byte
	copy(block[4:6], game)
	copy(block[6:8], company)
	block[8] = discNo
	block[9] = version
	block[10] = sysID
	// The transfer length: the preset DILENGTH when one
	// was loaded, else CMDBUF2 when nonzero, else the
	// full 32 byte block, and never past the block.
	n := uint32(readbackSize)
	switch {
	case d.dilen != 0 && d.dilen < n:
		n = d.dilen
	case d.dilen == 0 && d.cmd[2] != 0 && d.cmd[2] < n:
		n = d.cmd[2]
	}
	if d.dicr&dicrDMA != 0 {
		d.dmaWrite(block[:n])
		switch {
		case d.dilen != 0:
			d.dilen -= n
		case d.cmd[2] != 0:
			d.dilen = d.cmd[2] - n
		}
	} else {
		d.readback = block
		d.readLen = n
	}
	d.disr |= disrTCINT
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed save state size: a version
// byte, the ten 32 bit registers, the drive flags and
// the readback buffer.
const SerializeSize = 1 +
	10*4 + // DISR, DICVR, CMDBUF0 to 2, DICFG, DIMAR, DILENGTH, DICR, audio config
	1 + 1 + // cover open, stopped
	4 + // readback length
	readbackSize

// ErrBadState reports a state block of the wrong size
// or version.
var ErrBadState = errors.New("di: bad save state")

// Serialize writes the complete DI state.
func (d *DI) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	off := 1
	put32 := func(v uint32) {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], v)
		off += 4
	}
	put32(d.disr)
	put32(d.dicvr)
	put32(d.cmd[0])
	put32(d.cmd[1])
	put32(d.cmd[2])
	put32(d.dicfg)
	put32(d.dimar)
	put32(d.dilen)
	put32(d.dicr)
	put32(d.audioCfg)
	if d.coverOpen {
		out[off] = 1
	}
	off++
	if d.stopped {
		out[off] = 1
	}
	off++
	put32(d.readLen)
	off += copy(out[off:], d.readback[:])
	if off != SerializeSize {
		panic("di: serialize size mismatch")
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (d *DI) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != SerializeSize || in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return ErrBadState
	}
	off := 1
	get32 := func() uint32 {
		v := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
		return v
	}
	d.disr = get32()
	d.dicvr = get32()
	d.cmd[0] = get32()
	d.cmd[1] = get32()
	d.cmd[2] = get32()
	d.dicfg = get32()
	d.dimar = get32()
	d.dilen = get32()
	d.dicr = get32()
	d.audioCfg = get32()
	d.coverOpen = in[off] != 0
	off++
	d.stopped = in[off] != 0
	off++
	d.readLen = get32()
	if d.readLen > readbackSize {
		return ErrBadState
	}
	copy(d.readback[:], in[off:])
	return nil
}
