==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/si/si.go ====================

// Package si models the GameCube serial interface (SI),
// the controller bus at MMIO window base 0x0C006400,
// written from published SI documentation. Four controller
// channels are polled into input buffers, and a command
// transfer engine exchanges byte streams with the pad on
// one channel through the output buffer and the 128-byte
// I/O buffer window.
//
// Polling is simplified: hardware polls at vblank, here a
// write to the POLL register with enable bits polls at
// once, and the system calls PollFrame once per frame to
// re-poll while any channel stays enabled.
package si

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Pad is one controller state, as reported by the provider.
// Buttons uses the system pad bit order (PadA is 0x0100 and
// so on); it is passed through unchanged in reports.
type Pad struct {
	Buttons            uint16
	TriggerL, TriggerR uint8
	StickX, StickY     uint8
	CStickX, CStickY   uint8
}

// Register offsets. Channel registers stride 0x0C.
const (
	regOutBuf = 0x00
	regInHi   = 0x04
	regInLo   = 0x08

	offPoll   = 0x30
	offComCSR = 0x34
	offStatus = 0x38
	offIOBuf  = 0x40
	ioBufSize = 128
)

// COMCSR bits.
const (
	comTSTART     = 1 << 0
	comCOMERR     = 1 << 28 // status, write 1 to clear
	comRDSTINTMSK = 1 << 30
	comRDSTINT    = 1 << 31 // status, write 1 to clear

	// Config bits stored from a COMCSR write: channel,
	// output length, input length and the interrupt mask.
	// Bit 28 overlaps the top input length bit in this
	// layout and also carries COMERR on reads.
	comCfgMask = 0x7F3F0006
)

// SI is the serial interface state.
type SI struct {
	provide func() [4]Pad

	// Connected marks which channels have a controller.
	// Channel 0 defaults to connected.
	Connected [4]bool

	outBuf [4]uint32
	inHi   [4]uint32
	inLo   [4]uint32

	poll     uint32
	comCfg   uint32 // stored COMCSR config bits
	comStage uint32 // staging for the in-progress COMCSR write
	comErr   bool
	rdstInt  bool
	rdst     [4]bool

	ioBuf [ioBufSize]byte
	motor [4]int
}

// New returns an SI in its reset state sampling pads from
// the provider, which is called at poll and transfer time.
func New(pads func() [4]Pad) *SI {
	s := &SI{provide: pads}
	s.Connected = [4]bool{true, false, false, false}
	s.Reset()
	return s
}

// Reset clears every register, the I/O buffer and the
// rumble motors. The Connected set is system wiring and
// survives a reset.
func (s *SI) Reset() {
	s.outBuf = [4]uint32{}
	s.inHi = [4]uint32{}
	s.inLo = [4]uint32{}
	s.poll = 0
	s.comCfg, s.comStage = 0, 0
	s.comErr, s.rdstInt = false, false
	s.rdst = [4]bool{}
	s.ioBuf = [ioBufSize]byte{}
	s.motor = [4]int{}
}

func (s *SI) pads() [4]Pad {
	if s.provide == nil {
		return [4]Pad{}
	}
	return s.provide()
}

// reg32 reads the 32-bit register containing off.
func (s *SI) reg32(off uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	switch {
	case off < 0x30:
		ch := off / 0x0C
		switch off % 0x0C &^ 3 {
		case regOutBuf:
			return s.outBuf[ch], true
		case regInHi:
			return s.inHi[ch], true
		case regInLo:
			return s.inLo[ch], true
		}
	case off&^3 == offPoll:
		return s.poll, true
	case off&^3 == offComCSR:
		v := s.comCfg
		if s.comErr {
			v |= comCOMERR
		}
		if s.rdstInt {
			v |= comRDSTINT
		}
		return v, true
	case off&^3 == offStatus:
		var v uint32
		for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
			if s.rdst[c] {
				v |= 1 << uint(28+c)
			}
		}
		return v, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// Read16 reads one 16-bit lane of a register, or two I/O
// buffer bytes big-endian inside the buffer window.
// Reading a channel INBUF_LO clears that channel RDST bit
// in STATUS.
func (s *SI) Read16(off uint32) uint16 {
	if off >= offIOBuf && off < offIOBuf+ioBufSize {
		i := off - offIOBuf
		var v uint16
		v = uint16(s.ioBuf[i]) << 8
		if i+1 < ioBufSize {
			v |= uint16(s.ioBuf[i+1])
		}
		return v
	}
	v, ok := s.reg32(off)
	if !ok {
		return 0
	}
	if off < 0x30 && off%0x0C&^3 == regInLo {
		s.rdst[off/0x0C] = false
	}
	if off&2 == 0 {
		return uint16(v >> 16)
	}
	return uint16(v)
}

// Write16 writes one 16-bit lane of a register, or two I/O
// buffer bytes inside the buffer window. Side effects
// (POLL polling, COMCSR transfers) fire on the low lane
// write, once the full register value is assembled. INBUF
// and STATUS are read only.
func (s *SI) Write16(off uint32, v uint16) {
	if off >= offIOBuf && off < offIOBuf+ioBufSize {
		i := off - offIOBuf
		s.ioBuf[i] = byte(v >> 8)
		if i+1 < ioBufSize {
			s.ioBuf[i+1] = byte(v)
		}
		return
	}
	high := off&2 == 0
	switch {
	case off < 0x30:
		ch := off / 0x0C
		if off%0x0C&^3 != regOutBuf {
			return // INBUF writes are ignored
		}
		if high {
			s.outBuf[ch] = s.outBuf[ch]&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
		} else {
			s.outBuf[ch] = s.outBuf[ch]&0xFFFF0000 | uint32(v)
		}
	case off&^3 == offPoll:
		if high {
			s.poll = s.poll&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
		} else {
			s.poll = s.poll&0xFFFF0000 | uint32(v)
			if s.poll&0xF != 0 {
				s.pollEnabled()
			}
		}
	case off&^3 == offComCSR:
		if high {
			s.comStage = s.comStage&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
		} else {
			s.comStage = s.comStage&0xFFFF0000 | uint32(v)
			s.applyComCSR(s.comStage)
		}
	}
}

// applyComCSR folds a completed COMCSR write in: the two
// status bits are write 1 to clear, config bits are
// stored, and TSTART runs a transfer at once.
func (s *SI) applyComCSR(written uint32) {
	if written&comRDSTINT != 0 {
		s.rdstInt = false
	}
	if written&comCOMERR != 0 {
		s.comErr = false
	}
	s.comCfg = written & comCfgMask
	s.comStage = s.comCfg
	if written&comTSTART != 0 {
		s.runTransfer()
	}
}

// packPad packs one pad report into an INBUF word pair.
// A disconnected channel answers with the error packet:
// the buttons word 0x8000 and zeros everywhere else.
func packPad(p Pad, connected bool) (hi, lo uint32) {
	if !connected {
		return 0x8000 << 16, 0
	}
	buttons := p.Buttons &^ 0x8000
	hi = uint32(buttons)<<16 | uint32(p.StickX)<<8 | uint32(p.StickY)
	lo = uint32(p.CStickX)<<24 | uint32(p.CStickY)<<16 |
		uint32(p.TriggerL)<<8 | uint32(p.TriggerR)
	return hi, lo
}

func (s *SI) pollChannel(c int, pads [4]Pad) {
	s.inHi[c], s.inLo[c] = packPad(pads[c], s.Connected[c])
	s.rdst[c] = true
}

func (s *SI) pollEnabled() {
	pads := s.pads()
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		if s.poll&(1<<uint(c)) != 0 {
			s.pollChannel(c, pads)
		}
	}
}

// PollFrame re-polls every enabled channel. The system
// calls it once per frame.
func (s *SI) PollFrame() {
	if s.poll&0xF != 0 {
		s.pollEnabled()
	}
}

// Motor returns the last rumble motor byte sent to a
// channel by the get status command (0 for none, or for
// an out of range channel).
func (s *SI) Motor(ch int) int {
	if ch < 0 || ch > 3 {
		return 0
	}
	return s.motor[ch]
}

// IRQAsserted reports the SI interrupt output.
func (s *SI) IRQAsserted() bool {
	return s.rdstInt && s.comCfg&comRDSTINTMSK != 0
}

// runTransfer executes the COMCSR transfer on the selected
// channel. The output stream is the channel OUTBUF word
// followed by I/O buffer bytes, OUTLNGTH bytes in total
// (zero means the OUTBUF word alone, 4). The response is
// truncated or zero padded to INLNGTH bytes and written
// into the I/O buffer at offset 0. Status-class responses
// (origin and get status, plus the disconnected error
// packet) are also packed into the channel INBUF pair.
func (s *SI) runTransfer() {
	ch := int(s.comCfg>>1) & 3
	outLen := int(s.comCfg>>16) & 0x3F
	if outLen == 0 {
		outLen = 4
	}
	inLen := int(s.comCfg>>24) & 0x3F

	out := make([]byte, 0, outLen)
	var word [4]byte
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(word[:], s.outBuf[ch])
	for i := 0; i < outLen; i++ {
		if i < 4 {
			out = append(out, word[i])
		} else if i-4 < ioBufSize {
			out = append(out, s.ioBuf[i-4])
		} else {
			out = append(out, 0)
		}
	}
	cmd := out[0]

	connected := s.Connected[ch]
	pad := s.pads()[ch]

	var resp []byte
	statusClass := false
	if !connected {
		resp = []byte{0x80, 0x00, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
		statusClass = true
	} else {
		switch cmd {
		case 0x00, 0xFF: // info or reset: type ID 0x0900 plus status
			resp = []byte{0x09, 0x00, 0x00}
		case 0x41: // origin
			resp = statusPacket(pad)
			resp = append(resp, 0, 0)
			statusClass = true
		case 0x42: // get status; second output byte is rumble
			if len(out) >= 2 {
				s.motor[ch] = int(out[1])
			}
			resp = statusPacket(pad)
			statusClass = true
		default:
			resp = nil // unknown commands answer with zeros
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < inLen && i < ioBufSize; i++ {
		var b byte
		if i < len(resp) {
			b = resp[i]
		}
		s.ioBuf[i] = b
	}
	if statusClass && inLen > 0 {
		var pkt [8]byte
		copy(pkt[:], resp)
		s.inHi[ch] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(pkt[0:4])
		s.inLo[ch] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(pkt[4:8])
	}
	s.comErr = !connected
	s.rdstInt = true
	s.rdst[ch] = true
}

// statusPacket builds the eight-byte status response:
// buttons big-endian, then the six analog channels.
func statusPacket(p Pad) []byte {
	buttons := p.Buttons &^ 0x8000
	return []byte{
		byte(buttons >> 8), byte(buttons),
		p.StickX, p.StickY, p.CStickX, p.CStickY,
		p.TriggerL, p.TriggerR,
	}
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed save state size: a version
// byte, the channel register triples, POLL and the COMCSR
// config, the status flags, the I/O buffer, the motors and
// the Connected set.
const SerializeSize = 1 + 4*3*4 + 4 + 4 + 1 + 1 + ioBufSize + 4 + 4

// ErrBadState reports a state block of the wrong size or
// version.
var ErrBadState = errors.New("si: bad save state")

const serializeVersion = 1

// Serialize writes the SI state covered by SerializeSize.
func (s *SI) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	off := 1
	put32 := func(v uint32) {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], v)
		off += 4
	}
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		put32(s.outBuf[c])
		put32(s.inHi[c])
		put32(s.inLo[c])
	}
	put32(s.poll)
	put32(s.comCfg)
	var flags byte
	if s.comErr {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if s.rdstInt {
		flags |= 2
	}
	out[off] = flags
	off++
	var rdst byte
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		if s.rdst[c] {
			rdst |= 1 << uint(c)
		}
	}
	out[off] = rdst
	off++
	off += copy(out[off:], s.ioBuf[:])
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		out[off] = byte(s.motor[c])
		off++
	}
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		if s.Connected[c] {
			out[off] = 1
		}
		off++
	}
	if off != SerializeSize {
		panic("si: serialize size mismatch")
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. The
// pad provider is wiring and is not part of the state.
func (s *SI) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != SerializeSize || in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return ErrBadState
	}
	off := 1
	get32 := func() uint32 {
		v := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
		return v
	}
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		s.outBuf[c] = get32()
		s.inHi[c] = get32()
		s.inLo[c] = get32()
	}
	s.poll = get32()
	s.comCfg = get32()
	s.comStage = s.comCfg
	flags := in[off]
	off++
	s.comErr = flags&1 != 0
	s.rdstInt = flags&2 != 0
	rdst := in[off]
	off++
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		s.rdst[c] = rdst&(1<<uint(c)) != 0
	}
	off += copy(s.ioBuf[:], in[off:])
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		s.motor[c] = int(in[off])
		off++
	}
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		s.Connected[c] = in[off] != 0
		off++
	}
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/si/si_test.go ====================

package si_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/si"
)

func w32(s *si.SI, off uint32, v uint32) {
	s.Write16(off, uint16(v>>16))
	s.Write16(off+2, uint16(v))
}

func r32(s *si.SI, off uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(s.Read16(off))<<16 | uint32(s.Read16(off+2))
}

func chanOff(ch int, within uint32) uint32 { return uint32(ch)*0x0C + within }

const (
	offPoll   = 0x30
	offComCSR = 0x34
	offStatus = 0x38
	offIOBuf  = 0x40
)

func setIO(s *si.SI, data []byte) {
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(data)+1 && i < 128; i += 2 {
		var v uint16
		v = uint16(data[i]) << 8
		if i+1 < len(data) {
			v |= uint16(data[i+1])
		}
		s.Write16(offIOBuf+uint32(i), v)
	}
}

func getIO(s *si.SI, n int) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 0, n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i += 2 {
		v := s.Read16(offIOBuf + uint32(i))
		out = append(out, byte(v>>8))
		if i+1 < n {
			out = append(out, byte(v))
		}
	}
	return out
}

func fillIO(s *si.SI, b byte) {
	setIO(s, bytes.Repeat([]byte{b}, 128))
}

func stdPad() si.Pad {
	return si.Pad{
		Buttons:  0x1100,
		StickX:   128,
		StickY:   130,
		CStickX:  100,
		CStickY:  110,
		TriggerL: 20,
		TriggerR: 30,
	}
}

// Expected packings for stdPad: INBUF_HI carries the
// buttons word, stick X, stick Y; INBUF_LO carries the
// C-stick pair and the two triggers.
const (
	stdHi = 0x11008082
	stdLo = 0x646E141E
)

var stdPacket = []byte{0x11, 0x00, 128, 130, 100, 110, 20, 30}

func newSI(pads *[4]si.Pad) *si.SI {
	return si.New(func() [4]si.Pad { return *pads })
}

func TestPollPackingAndRDST(t *testing.T) {
	var pads [4]si.Pad
	pads[0] = stdPad()
	s := newSI(&pads)

	// POLL: Y in bits 24-31, X in bits 16-22, EN bit 0.
	pollVal := uint32(200)<<24 | uint32(3)<<16 | 1
	w32(s, offPoll, pollVal)
	if got := r32(s, offPoll); got != pollVal {
		t.Fatalf("POLL readback = %#x, want %#x (X and Y stored)", got, pollVal)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(0, 0x04)); got != stdHi {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_HI = %#x, want %#x", got, stdHi)
	}
	if got := r32(s, offStatus); got != 1<<28 {
		t.Fatalf("STATUS = %#x, want only RDST for channel 0 (bit 28)", got)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(0, 0x08)); got != stdLo {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_LO = %#x, want %#x", got, stdLo)
	}
	if got := r32(s, offStatus); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("STATUS after reading INBUF_LO = %#x, want RDST cleared", got)
	}

	// PollFrame re-polls the enabled channel with fresh data.
	pads[0].Buttons = 0x0200
	s.PollFrame()
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(0, 0x04)); got != 0x02008082 {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_HI after PollFrame = %#x, want 0x02008082", got)
	}
	if got := r32(s, offStatus); got != 1<<28 {
		t.Fatalf("STATUS after PollFrame = %#x, want RDST set again", got)
	}
}

func TestPollDisconnectedChannel(t *testing.T) {
	var pads [4]si.Pad
	pads[1] = stdPad()
	s := newSI(&pads)
	if s.Connected[1] {
		t.Fatal("channel 1 should start disconnected")
	}
	w32(s, offPoll, 1<<1) // EN channel 1 only
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(1, 0x04)); got != 0x80000000 {
		t.Fatalf("disconnected INBUF_HI = %#x, want the 0x8000 error packet", got)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(1, 0x08)); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("disconnected INBUF_LO = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func comcsr(channel, outLen, inLen int) uint32 {
	// TSTART | CHANNEL | OUTLNGTH | INLNGTH | RDSTINTMSK.
	return 1 | uint32(channel)<<1 | uint32(outLen)<<16 | uint32(inLen)<<24 | 1<<30
}

func TestGetStatusTransfer(t *testing.T) {
	var pads [4]si.Pad
	pads[0] = stdPad()
	s := newSI(&pads)
	fillIO(s, 0xAA)

	// OUTBUF bytes: command 0x42, rumble motor byte 0x01.
	w32(s, chanOff(0, 0x00), 0x42010000)
	w32(s, offComCSR, comcsr(0, 2, 8))

	if got := getIO(s, 8); !bytes.Equal(got, stdPacket) {
		t.Fatalf("IOBUF after 0x42 = %v, want the status packet %v", got, stdPacket)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(0, 0x04)); got != stdHi {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_HI after 0x42 = %#x, want %#x", got, stdHi)
	}
	if got := r32(s, offStatus); got != 1<<28 {
		t.Fatalf("STATUS after transfer = %#x, want RDST channel 0", got)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(0, 0x08)); got != stdLo {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_LO after 0x42 = %#x, want %#x", got, stdLo)
	}
	cc := r32(s, offComCSR)
	if cc&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("RDSTINT not set after the transfer completed")
	}
	if cc&(1<<28) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("COMERR set for a connected channel (INLNGTH 8 leaves bit 28 clear)")
	}
	if !s.IRQAsserted() {
		t.Fatal("IRQ not asserted with RDSTINT set and RDSTINTMSK enabled")
	}
	if got := s.Motor(0); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("Motor(0) = %d, want 1 (the second output byte)", got)
	}
	// RDSTINT is write 1 to clear.
	w32(s, offComCSR, 1<<31|1<<30)
	if s.IRQAsserted() {
		t.Fatal("IRQ still asserted after RDSTINT was cleared")
	}
	if r32(s, offComCSR)&(1<<31) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("RDSTINT still set after the clear write")
	}
}

func TestInfoAndOriginCommands(t *testing.T) {
	var pads [4]si.Pad
	pads[0] = stdPad()
	s := newSI(&pads)

	for _, cmd := range []uint32{0x00000000, 0xFF000000} {
		fillIO(s, 0xAA)
		w32(s, chanOff(0, 0x00), cmd)
		w32(s, offComCSR, comcsr(0, 1, 3))
		if got := getIO(s, 3); !bytes.Equal(got, []byte{0x09, 0x00, 0x00}) {
			t.Fatalf("info command %#x response = %v, want [09 00 00]", cmd>>24, got)
		}
	}

	fillIO(s, 0xAA)
	w32(s, chanOff(0, 0x00), 0x41000000)
	w32(s, offComCSR, comcsr(0, 1, 10))
	want := append(append([]byte{}, stdPacket...), 0, 0)
	if got := getIO(s, 10); !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("origin response = %v, want %v (status packet plus two zero bytes)", got, want)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(0, 0x04)); got != stdHi {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_HI after origin = %#x, want %#x", got, stdHi)
	}
}

func TestDisconnectedTransferSetsCOMERR(t *testing.T) {
	var pads [4]si.Pad
	pads[1] = stdPad()
	s := newSI(&pads)
	fillIO(s, 0xAA)

	w32(s, chanOff(1, 0x00), 0x42000000)
	w32(s, offComCSR, comcsr(1, 2, 8))

	cc := r32(s, offComCSR)
	if cc&(1<<28) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("COMERR not set for a transfer on a disconnected channel")
	}
	if cc&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("RDSTINT not set after the disconnected transfer")
	}
	if got := r32(s, offStatus); got != 1<<29 {
		t.Fatalf("STATUS = %#x, want only RDST for channel 1 (bit 29)", got)
	}
	if got := getIO(s, 8); !bytes.Equal(got, []byte{0x80, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}) {
		t.Fatalf("IOBUF error response = %v, want [0x80 0 0 0 0 0 0 0]", got)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(1, 0x04)); got != 0x80000000 {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_HI error packet = %#x, want 0x80000000", got)
	}
	if got := r32(s, chanOff(1, 0x08)); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("INBUF_LO error packet = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestUnknownCommandAnswersZeros(t *testing.T) {
	var pads [4]si.Pad
	pads[0] = stdPad()
	s := newSI(&pads)
	fillIO(s, 0xAA)
	w32(s, chanOff(0, 0x00), 0x99000000)
	w32(s, offComCSR, comcsr(0, 1, 4))
	if got := getIO(s, 4); !bytes.Equal(got, []byte{0, 0, 0, 0}) {
		t.Fatalf("unknown command response = %v, want zeros", got)
	}
	if r32(s, offComCSR)&(1<<28) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("COMERR set for an unknown command on a connected channel")
	}
}

func TestSISerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	var pads [4]si.Pad
	pads[0] = stdPad()
	s := newSI(&pads)
	s.Connected[2] = true

	w32(s, offPoll, 1) // poll channel 0 into INBUF
	w32(s, chanOff(0, 0x00), 0x42010000)
	w32(s, offComCSR, comcsr(0, 2, 8)) // motor 1, RDSTINT set
	// Distinctive IOBUF tail bytes that no transfer wrote.
	s.Write16(offIOBuf+100, 0xBEEF)

	pollBefore := r32(s, offPoll)
	comBefore := r32(s, offComCSR)
	statusBefore := r32(s, offStatus)
	ioBefore := getIO(s, 128)

	blob := s.Serialize()
	if len(blob) != si.SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize length = %d, want %d", len(blob), si.SerializeSize)
	}

	var pads2 [4]si.Pad
	s2 := newSI(&pads2)
	if err := s2.Deserialize(blob); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if s2.Connected != s.Connected {
		t.Fatalf("restored Connected = %v, want %v", s2.Connected, s.Connected)
	}
	if got := r32(s2, chanOff(0, 0x04)); got != stdHi {
		t.Fatalf("restored INBUF_HI = %#x, want %#x", got, stdHi)
	}
	// STATUS is checked before INBUF_LO on purpose:
	// reading INBUF_LO clears the channel RDST bit.
	if got := r32(s2, offStatus); got != statusBefore {
		t.Fatalf("restored STATUS = %#x, want %#x", got, statusBefore)
	}
	if got := r32(s2, chanOff(0, 0x08)); got != stdLo {
		t.Fatalf("restored INBUF_LO = %#x, want %#x", got, stdLo)
	}
	if got := r32(s2, offPoll); got != pollBefore {
		t.Fatalf("restored POLL = %#x, want %#x", got, pollBefore)
	}
	if got := r32(s2, offComCSR); got != comBefore {
		t.Fatalf("restored COMCSR = %#x, want %#x", got, comBefore)
	}
	if got := getIO(s2, 128); !bytes.Equal(got, ioBefore) {
		t.Fatal("restored IOBUF differs")
	}
	if got := s2.Motor(0); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("restored Motor(0) = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := s2.Motor(9); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Motor(9) = %d, want 0 for an out of range channel", got)
	}
	if err := s2.Deserialize([]byte{9}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize of a short state should fail")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/system/system.go ====================

// Package system assembles the GameCube machine: the
// Gekko CPU (chips/gekko), 24 MB of MEM1 main memory, the
// hardware register pages, and a disc image staged through
// the disc package.
//
// Slice GCN-1 scope: the CPU runs integer code from a
// staged DOL; the IPL ROM window reads as zeros because
// this project ships no Nintendo IPL bytes.
//
// Slice GCN-2 wires the GX renderer (package gpu) into
// the machine: the CP register window and the GX FIFO
// write port on the 0x0C hardware page route to the GPU,
// Framebuffer presents the GPU's embedded frame buffer,
// and save states grow to version 2 with the full GPU
// state included.
//
// Slice GCN-3 wires the remaining Flipper devices into
// the machine: the DSP (chips/dsp), the audio interface
// (ai), the disc interface (di), the external interface
// (exi), the serial interface (si) and the video
// interface (vi), plus the processor interface (PI)
// interrupt aggregate handled here, and an HLE boot path
// (BootDisc) that reconstructs the documented IPL boot
// state without executing or embedding any IPL code.
// Save states grow to version 3 with every device block
// included.
package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/ai"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/chips/dsp"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/chips/gekko"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/di"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/disc"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/exi"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/gpu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/si"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/vi"
)

// Framebuffer dimensions the GX slice will render at.
const (
	Width  = 640
	Height = 480
)

// MEM1Size is the GameCube main memory size: 24 MB.
const MEM1Size = 24 << 20

const (
	lockedCacheSize = 256 << 10 // the 0xE0000000 locked cache window
	hwPageSize      = 64 << 10  // one 0x0C / 0x0D register page
)

// CyclesPerFrame is the frame budget at the Gekko clock
// of 486 MHz and 60 frames per second.
const CyclesPerFrame = 486_000_000 / 60

const serializeVersion = 3

// StateSize is the whole-machine save state size.
const StateSize = 1 + 4 + gekko.SerializeSize + gpu.SerializeSize + MEM1Size +
	lockedCacheSize + 2*hwPageSize +
	dsp.SerializeSize + ai.SerializeSize + di.SerializeSize +
	exi.SerializeSize + si.SerializeSize + vi.SerializeSize +
	stateTailSize

const stateTailSize = 16 + 8 + 4 + 4 + 1 // pad, started, entry, plus GCN-3: total cycles, DSP remainder, PI INTMSK, booted

// GamePad button bits, in the standard controller report
// order used by the SI polling format.
const (
	PadLeft  uint16 = 0x0001
	PadRight uint16 = 0x0002
	PadDown  uint16 = 0x0004
	PadUp    uint16 = 0x0008
	PadZ     uint16 = 0x0010
	PadR     uint16 = 0x0020
	PadL     uint16 = 0x0040
	PadA     uint16 = 0x0100
	PadB     uint16 = 0x0200
	PadX     uint16 = 0x0400
	PadY     uint16 = 0x0800
	PadStart uint16 = 0x1000
)

// PadState is one controller's state: two button bytes
// (in Buttons) and the analog channels.
type PadState struct {
	Buttons  uint16
	TriggerL uint8
	TriggerR uint8
	StickX   uint8
	StickY   uint8
	CStickX  uint8
	CStickY  uint8
}

// PI interrupt cause bits in PI_INTSR and PI_INTMSK.
const (
	piCauseDSP   uint32 = 0x00000001
	piCauseAI    uint32 = 0x00000002
	piCauseEXI   uint32 = 0x00000004
	piCauseSI    uint32 = 0x00000008
	piCauseDI    uint32 = 0x00000010
	piCauseVI    uint32 = 0x00000020
	piCauseGX    uint32 = 0x00000040 // reserved: the GPU exposes no PE interrupt output in this slice, so this bit is never raised
	piCauseError uint32 = 0x00000080 // never raised in this slice
)

// MMIO window identifiers on the 0x0C hardware page.
const (
	winCP = iota
	winVI
	winPI
	winDSP
	winDI
	winSI
	winEXI
	winAI
	winCount
)

// mmioLatch is the per-window byte latch used to assemble
// a 16-bit device register from its two bus bytes. The
// latch only ever lives inside one bus write transaction;
// save states are taken between instructions, never here,
// so latch state is not serialized.
type mmioLatch struct {
	val uint8
	ok  bool
}

// Machine is the assembled GameCube.
type Machine struct {
	cpu *gekko.CPU
	gpu *gpu.GPU

	dsp *dsp.DSP
	ai  *ai.AI
	di  *di.DI
	exi *exi.EXI
	si  *si.SI
	vi  *vi.VI

	mem1   []byte
	locked []byte
	hw0C   []byte
	hw0D   []byte

	fb      []uint32
	pad     PadState
	started bool
	booted  bool
	entry   uint32

	loaded *disc.Image

	totalCycles uint64
	dspRem      uint32 // DSP cycle remainder accumulator, 0..5
	piINTMSK    uint32
	piRaw       [16]uint32 // stored PI words other than INTSR and INTMSK

	latches [winCount]mmioLatch
}

// gpuMem adapts MEM1 to the gpu.Memory interface. The GPU
// reads physical, zero-based MEM1 addresses; anything
// outside MEM1 reads as zero.
type gpuMem struct{ m *Machine }

func (a gpuMem) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	if addr < MEM1Size {
		return a.m.mem1[addr]
	}
	return 0
}

func (a gpuMem) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(a.Read8(addr))<<8 | uint16(a.Read8(addr+1))
}

func (a gpuMem) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(a.Read8(addr))<<24 | uint32(a.Read8(addr+1))<<16 |
		uint32(a.Read8(addr+2))<<8 | uint32(a.Read8(addr+3))
}

// physMem adapts MEM1 to the byte interface the DSP, AI,
// DI and EXI devices use for DMA. Addresses are physical,
// zero-based MEM1 addresses; anything outside MEM1 reads
// as zero and ignores writes.
type physMem struct{ m *Machine }

func (a physMem) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	if addr < MEM1Size {
		return a.m.mem1[addr]
	}
	return 0
}

func (a physMem) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	if addr < MEM1Size {
		a.m.mem1[addr] = v
	}
}

// diSource adapts the loaded disc image to the DI Source
// interface. It resolves the image at call time, so a disc
// loaded after the DI device was constructed is the disc
// the drive reads.
type diSource struct{ m *Machine }

func (a diSource) Read(off uint32, dst []byte) int {
	if a.m.loaded == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return a.m.loaded.ReadAt(off, dst)
}

func (a diSource) Header() (sysID byte, game, company string, discNo, version byte) {
	img := a.m.loaded
	if img == nil {
		return 0, "", "", 0, 0
	}
	return img.SystemID, img.GameCode, img.CompanyCode, img.DiscNumber, img.Version
}

// New returns a powered-off machine with no disc loaded.
func New() *Machine {
	m := &Machine{
		mem1:   make([]byte, MEM1Size),
		locked: make([]byte, lockedCacheSize),
		hw0C:   make([]byte, hwPageSize),
		hw0D:   make([]byte, hwPageSize),
		fb:     make([]uint32, Width*Height),
	}
	m.gpu = gpu.New(gpuMem{m})
	m.cpu = gekko.New(m)
	m.cpu.Halted = true
	mem := physMem{m}
	m.dsp = dsp.New(mem)
	m.ai = ai.New(mem)
	m.ai.OnAIDInt = m.dsp.SetAIDInt
	m.di = di.New(diSource{m}, mem)
	m.exi = exi.New(mem)
	m.si = si.New(m.siPads)
	m.si.Connected = [4]bool{true, false, false, false}
	m.vi = vi.New()
	return m
}

// siPads is the SI pad provider: channel 0 reports the
// machine pad state, channels 1 to 3 report zero pads.
func (m *Machine) siPads() [4]si.Pad {
	var out [4]si.Pad
	out[0] = si.Pad{
		Buttons:  m.pad.Buttons,
		TriggerL: m.pad.TriggerL,
		TriggerR: m.pad.TriggerR,
		StickX:   m.pad.StickX,
		StickY:   m.pad.StickY,
		CStickX:  m.pad.CStickX,
		CStickY:  m.pad.CStickY,
	}
	return out
}

// CPU exposes the processor for test harnesses and tools.
func (m *Machine) CPU() *gekko.CPU { return m.cpu }

// GPU exposes the GX renderer for test harnesses and
// tools.
func (m *Machine) GPU() *gpu.GPU { return m.gpu }

// DSP exposes the DSP for test harnesses and tools (for
// example to upload IRAM microcode before a boot).
func (m *Machine) DSP() *dsp.DSP { return m.dsp }

// AudioBuffer drains the AI output buffer: interleaved
// stereo samples at AudioRate.
func (m *Machine) AudioBuffer() []int16 { return m.ai.Drain() }

// SystemRAM returns the live MEM1 backing store, for the
// libretro memory interface (RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM).
// Writes through it are writes to machine memory.
func (m *Machine) SystemRAM() []byte { return m.mem1 }

// AudioRate returns the AI sample rate in Hz.
func (m *Machine) AudioRate() int { return m.ai.Rate() }

// CardImage returns the live backing image of an EXI
// memory card slot (0 is slot A, 1 is slot B). Card images
// are persistent media and are not part of save states.
func (m *Machine) CardImage(slot int) []byte { return m.exi.CardImage(slot) }

// resetDevices resets every GCN-3 device and the cycle
// accounting, deterministically, as part of LoadDisc.
func (m *Machine) resetDevices() {
	m.dsp.Reset()
	m.ai.Reset()
	m.ai.OnAIDInt = m.dsp.SetAIDInt
	m.di.Reset()
	m.exi.Reset()
	m.si.Reset()
	m.si.Connected = [4]bool{true, false, false, false}
	m.vi.Reset()
	m.totalCycles = 0
	m.dspRem = 0
	m.piINTMSK = 0
	m.piRaw = [16]uint32{}
	m.latches = [winCount]mmioLatch{}
	m.booted = false
}

// LoadDisc stages a parsed disc image: the DOL sections
// are copied to their load addresses, the BSS is zeroed,
// and the CPU is reset to the DOL entry point, halted.
// Call Start to run it, or BootDisc for the HLE boot path.
func (m *Machine) LoadDisc(img *disc.Image) error {
	dol, err := img.DOL()
	if err != nil {
		m.loaded = nil
		return err
	}
	m.loaded = img
	for i := range m.mem1 {
		m.mem1[i] = 0
	}
	for i := range m.locked {
		m.locked[i] = 0
	}
	m.resetDevices()
	for _, s := range dol.Sections {
		for i, b := range s.Data {
			m.Write8(s.Address+uint32(i), b)
		}
	}
	for i := uint32(0); i < dol.BSSSize; i++ {
		m.Write8(dol.BSSAddress+i, 0)
	}
	m.cpu.Reset()
	m.cpu.PC = dol.Entry
	m.cpu.Halted = true
	// A staged disc boots against a clean GX: register
	// files, TMEM, and the EFB all return to reset state.
	m.gpu.Reset()
	m.started = false
	m.booted = false
	m.entry = dol.Entry
	return nil
}

// Start unhalts the CPU at the staged entry point.
func (m *Machine) Start() {
	m.started = true
	m.cpu.Halted = false
}

// Started reports whether the CPU has been started.
func (m *Machine) Started() bool { return m.started }

// Entry returns the staged DOL entry point.
func (m *Machine) Entry() uint32 { return m.entry }

// intSR computes the PI_INTSR aggregate from the device
// interrupt outputs.
func (m *Machine) intSR() uint32 {
	var sr uint32
	if m.dsp != nil && m.dsp.IRQAsserted() {
		sr |= piCauseDSP
	}
	if m.ai != nil && m.ai.IRQAsserted() {
		sr |= piCauseAI
	}
	if m.exi != nil && m.exi.IRQAsserted() {
		sr |= piCauseEXI
	}
	if m.si != nil && m.si.IRQAsserted() {
		sr |= piCauseSI
	}
	if m.di != nil && m.di.IRQAsserted() {
		sr |= piCauseDI
	}
	if m.vi != nil && m.vi.Pending() {
		sr |= piCauseVI
	}
	// piCauseGX is reserved and never raised in this slice:
	// the GPU exposes no PE interrupt output. piCauseError
	// is never raised either.
	return sr
}

// refreshIRQ drives the CPU external interrupt line from
// the PI interrupt aggregate and mask.
func (m *Machine) refreshIRQ() {
	if m.cpu == nil {
		return
	}
	m.cpu.SetIRQ(m.intSR()&m.piINTMSK != 0)
}

// piRead16 reads one 16-bit lane of a PI register. PI
// registers are 32-bit: the lane at the even offset is
// the high half, the next lane the low half.
func (m *Machine) piRead16(off uint32) uint16 {
	wordOff := off &^ 2
	var v uint32
	switch wordOff {
	case 0x00: // PI_INTSR: computed, read-only
		v = m.intSR()
	case 0x04: // PI_INTMSK
		v = m.piINTMSK
	default:
		if wordOff/4 < uint32(len(m.piRaw)) {
			v = m.piRaw[wordOff/4]
		}
	}
	if off&2 == 0 {
		return uint16(v >> 16)
	}
	return uint16(v)
}

// piWrite16 writes one 16-bit lane of a PI register.
// Writes to PI_INTSR are ignored.
func (m *Machine) piWrite16(off uint32, v uint16) {
	wordOff := off &^ 2
	low := off&2 != 0
	merge := func(dst *uint32) {
		if low {
			*dst = *dst&0xFFFF0000 | uint32(v)
		} else {
			*dst = *dst&0x0000FFFF | uint32(v)<<16
		}
	}
	switch wordOff {
	case 0x00: // PI_INTSR is read-only
	case 0x04:
		merge(&m.piINTMSK)
	default:
		if wordOff/4 < uint32(len(m.piRaw)) {
			merge(&m.piRaw[wordOff/4])
		}
	}
}

// RunCycles steps the CPU for up to n cycles (fewer if it
// is halted). The DSP, AI, EXI and VI devices advance with
// the CPU: the DSP at its 81 MHz rate (one DSP cycle per
// six CPU cycles, with the remainder carried), the others
// per CPU cycle. If the CPU is halted the devices do not
// advance.
func (m *Machine) RunCycles(n int) {
	for n > 0 {
		s := m.cpu.Step()
		if s == 0 {
			return
		}
		n -= s
		m.totalCycles += uint64(s)
		acc := int(m.dspRem) + s
		m.dsp.Step(acc / 6)
		m.dspRem = uint32(acc % 6)
		m.ai.Advance(s)
		m.exi.Advance(s)
		m.vi.Advance(s)
	}
	m.refreshIRQ()
}

// RunFrame consumes one frame of CPU cycles and polls the
// SI controllers once at the end of the frame.
func (m *Machine) RunFrame() {
	m.RunCycles(CyclesPerFrame)
	m.si.PollFrame()
}

// Framebuffer returns the current frame: the GPU's EFB
// presented as a 640x480 XRGB8888 buffer (nearest-fit
// copy of the BP copy source rectangle, no deflicker).
func (m *Machine) Framebuffer() []uint32 {
	m.gpu.Present(m.fb)
	return m.fb
}

// SetButtons records the controller state.
func (m *Machine) SetButtons(p PadState) { m.pad = p }

// Buttons returns the recorded controller state.
func (m *Machine) Buttons() PadState { return m.pad }

// decode maps a physical address to its backing store.
// The standard GameCube windows are decoded: MEM1 at its
// physical base and at the cached (0x80000000) and
// uncached (0xC0000000) aliases, the 0x0C and 0x0D
// hardware pages, and the locked cache window. The IPL
// window at 0xFFF00000 and anything unmapped read as the
// stub value zero and ignore writes.
func (m *Machine) decode(addr uint32) ([]byte, uint32, bool) {
	switch {
	case addr < MEM1Size:
		return m.mem1, addr, true
	case addr >= 0x80000000 && addr < 0x80000000+MEM1Size:
		return m.mem1, addr - 0x80000000, true
	case addr >= 0xC0000000 && addr < 0xC0000000+MEM1Size:
		return m.mem1, addr - 0xC0000000, true
	case addr >= 0x0C000000 && addr < 0x0C000000+hwPageSize:
		return m.hw0C, addr - 0x0C000000, true
	case addr >= 0x0D000000 && addr < 0x0D000000+hwPageSize:
		return m.hw0D, addr - 0x0D000000, true
	case addr >= 0xE0000000 && addr < 0xE0000000+lockedCacheSize:
		return m.locked, addr - 0xE0000000, true
	}
	return nil, 0, false
}

// gxWindow maps an address in the Flipper register page
// to its page offset. The page is decoded at its physical
// base (0x0C000000) and at the cached (0x8C000000) and
// uncached (0xCC000000) aliases, which is where GameCube
// software actually addresses the device registers and
// the GX FIFO write port.
func (m *Machine) gxWindow(addr uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	for _, base := range []uint32{0x0C000000, 0x8C000000, 0xCC000000} {
		if addr >= base && addr < base+hwPageSize {
			return addr - base, true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

// Offsets inside the Flipper page: the CP MMIO register
// window occupies 0x0000-0x007F (16-bit registers) and the
// GX FIFO write port occupies 0x8000-0x80FF. The GCN-3
// device windows are VI 0x2000, PI 0x3000, DSP 0x5000,
// DI 0x6000, SI 0x6400, EXI 0x6800 and AI 0x6C00. Every
// other offset stays plain stored state in the hw0C page.
const (
	gxFIFOBase = 0x8000
	gxFIFOEnd  = 0x8100
)

// mmioWindowFor maps a Flipper page offset to its device
// window, the window base, and whether the offset is in a
// device window at all.
func mmioWindowFor(off uint32) (win int, base uint32, ok bool) {
	switch {
	case off >= 0x2000 && off < 0x2060:
		return winVI, 0x2000, true
	case off >= 0x3000 && off < 0x3040:
		return winPI, 0x3000, true
	case off >= 0x5000 && off < 0x5030:
		return winDSP, 0x5000, true
	case off >= 0x6000 && off < 0x6024:
		return winDI, 0x6000, true
	case off >= 0x6400 && off < 0x64C0:
		return winSI, 0x6400, true
	case off >= 0x6800 && off < 0x683C:
		return winEXI, 0x6800, true
	case off >= 0x6C00 && off < 0x6C40:
		return winAI, 0x6C00, true
	}
	return 0, 0, false
}

// devRead16 reads one 16-bit device register lane in the
// given window at a window-relative lane offset.
func (m *Machine) devRead16(win int, rel uint32) uint16 {
	switch win {
	case winVI:
		return m.vi.Read16(rel)
	case winPI:
		return m.piRead16(rel)
	case winDSP:
		return m.dsp.Read16(rel)
	case winDI:
		return m.di.Read16(rel)
	case winSI:
		return m.si.Read16(rel)
	case winEXI:
		return m.exi.Read16(rel)
	case winAI:
		return m.ai.Read16(rel)
	}
	return 0
}

// devWrite16 writes one 16-bit device register lane in
// the given window at a window-relative lane offset.
func (m *Machine) devWrite16(win int, rel uint32, v uint16) {
	switch win {
	case winVI:
		m.vi.Write16(rel, v)
	case winPI:
		m.piWrite16(rel, v)
	case winDSP:
		m.dsp.Write16(rel, v)
	case winDI:
		m.di.Write16(rel, v)
	case winSI:
		m.si.Write16(rel, v)
	case winEXI:
		m.exi.Write16(rel, v)
	case winAI:
		m.ai.Write16(rel, v)
	}
}

// Read8 implements gekko.Bus.
func (m *Machine) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	if off, ok := m.gxWindow(addr); ok {
		switch {
		case off < 0x80:
			// CP MMIO window: 16-bit registers, big-endian
			// byte order across the pair.
			v := m.gpu.ReadMMIO(off &^ 1)
			if off&1 == 0 {
				return uint8(v >> 8)
			}
			return uint8(v)
		case off >= gxFIFOBase && off < gxFIFOEnd:
			return 0 // the FIFO port is write-only
		default:
			if win, base, isDev := mmioWindowFor(off); isDev {
				rel := off - base
				v := m.devRead16(win, rel&^1)
				m.refreshIRQ()
				if off&1 == 0 {
					return uint8(v >> 8)
				}
				return uint8(v)
			}
			return m.hw0C[off]
		}
	}
	if s, off, ok := m.decode(addr); ok {
		return s[off]
	}
	return 0
}

// Read16 implements gekko.Bus (big-endian assembly).
func (m *Machine) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(m.Read8(addr))<<8 | uint16(m.Read8(addr+1))
}

// Read32 implements gekko.Bus (big-endian assembly).
func (m *Machine) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(m.Read8(addr))<<24 | uint32(m.Read8(addr+1))<<16 |
		uint32(m.Read8(addr+2))<<8 | uint32(m.Read8(addr+3))
}

// Write8 implements gekko.Bus.
func (m *Machine) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	if off, ok := m.gxWindow(addr); ok {
		switch {
		case off < 0x80:
			// CP MMIO window: assemble the 16-bit register
			// from its two bytes, using the CP latch.
			lt := &m.latches[winCP]
			if off&1 == 0 {
				lt.val = v
				lt.ok = true
			} else if lt.ok {
				m.gpu.WriteMMIO(off-1, uint16(lt.val)<<8|uint16(v))
				lt.ok = false
			}
		case off >= gxFIFOBase && off < gxFIFOEnd:
			// Every byte stored anywhere in the FIFO port
			// window pushes one byte into the GX FIFO, in
			// bus order.
			m.gpu.WriteFIFO([]byte{v})
		default:
			if win, base, isDev := mmioWindowFor(off); isDev {
				// Device window: assemble the 16-bit
				// register from its two bytes, using this
				// window's own latch so alternating windows
				// cannot corrupt a pair, and call the
				// device on the odd byte.
				rel := off - base
				lt := &m.latches[win]
				if off&1 == 0 {
					lt.val = v
					lt.ok = true
				} else if lt.ok {
					m.devWrite16(win, rel-1, uint16(lt.val)<<8|uint16(v))
					lt.ok = false
				}
				m.refreshIRQ()
				return
			}
			m.hw0C[off] = v
		}
		return
	}
	if s, off, ok := m.decode(addr); ok {
		s[off] = v
	}
}

// Write16 implements gekko.Bus.
func (m *Machine) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	m.Write8(addr, uint8(v>>8))
	m.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v))
}

// Write32 implements gekko.Bus.
func (m *Machine) Write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	m.Write8(addr, uint8(v>>24))
	m.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v>>16))
	m.Write8(addr+2, uint8(v>>8))
	m.Write8(addr+3, uint8(v))
}

// ErrNoDisc reports a BootDisc call with no GameCube disc
// loaded.
var ErrNoDisc = errors.New("system: no disc loaded")

// physOf converts a DOL load address to its MEM1 physical
// address through the standard windows.
func physOf(ea uint32) uint32 {
	switch {
	case ea >= 0x80000000 && ea < 0x80000000+MEM1Size:
		return ea - 0x80000000
	case ea >= 0xC0000000 && ea < 0xC0000000+MEM1Size:
		return ea - 0xC0000000
	default:
		return ea
	}
}

func align32(v uint32) uint32 { return (v + 31) &^ 31 }

// BootDisc performs the HLE boot for the disc loaded by
// LoadDisc. LoadDisc must be called first: it stages the
// DOL and resets the machine, and BootDisc then installs
// the boot state the IPL would have left behind (the FST
// in MEM1, the boot info block, exception vectors holding
// a branch to self, BATs and segment registers covering
// MEM1, translation and the FPU on) and starts the CPU at
// the DOL entry point. No IPL or apploader code is
// executed or embedded; the layout follows published
// boot info facts only.
func (m *Machine) BootDisc() error {
	if m.loaded == nil {
		return ErrNoDisc
	}
	img := m.loaded
	dol, err := img.DOL()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// The FST goes immediately after the highest DOL
	// section end or BSS end, aligned up to 32 bytes.
	var top uint32
	for _, s := range dol.Sections {
		if end := physOf(s.Address) + s.Size; end > top {
			top = end
		}
	}
	if end := physOf(dol.BSSAddress) + dol.BSSSize; end > top {
		top = end
	}
	fstPhys := align32(top)
	fstEff := 0x80000000 | fstPhys
	fst := make([]byte, img.FSTSize)
	img.ReadAt(img.FSTOffset, fst)
	for i, b := range fst {
		if fstPhys+uint32(i) < MEM1Size {
			m.mem1[fstPhys+uint32(i)] = b
		}
	}
	arenaLo := 0x80000000 | align32(fstPhys+img.FSTSize)
	const arenaHi uint32 = 0x81800000
	const stackPtr uint32 = 0x817FFFE0

	// Boot info block at physical MEM1 offsets.
	m.Write32(0x00, 1)          // console type: retail GameCube
	m.Write32(0x20, 0x0D15EA5E) // BS2 executed magic
	m.Write32(0x28, MEM1Size)   // simulated memory size
	m.Write32(0x2C, fstPhys)    // FST start, physical
	m.Write32(0x30, arenaLo)    // OS arena low, effective cached
	m.Write32(0x34, arenaHi)    // OS arena high
	m.Write32(0x38, img.FSTSize)

	// Exception vectors: a branch to self in every slot
	// from 0x100 through 0x1F00.
	for off := uint32(0x100); off <= 0x1F00; off += 0x100 {
		m.Write32(off, 0x48000000)
	}
	// The return trampoline LR points at.
	m.Write32(0x2000, 0x48000000)

	cpu := m.cpu
	for i := range cpu.SR {
		cpu.SR[i] = 0x80000000
	}
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRIBAT0U+0, 0x800003FF) // IBAT0U
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRIBAT0U+1, 0x00000002) // IBAT0L
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRIBAT0U+2, 0x000003FF) // IBAT1U
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRIBAT0U+3, 0x00000002) // IBAT1L
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRDBAT0U+0, 0x800003FF) // DBAT0U
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRDBAT0U+1, 0x00000002) // DBAT0L
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRDBAT0U+2, 0x000003FF) // DBAT1U
	cpu.SetSPR(gekko.SPRDBAT0U+3, 0x00000002) // DBAT1L
	cpu.MSR = gekko.MSRFP | gekko.MSRIR | gekko.MSRDR
	cpu.GPR[1] = stackPtr
	cpu.GPR[3] = fstEff
	cpu.GPR[4] = img.FSTSize
	cpu.LR = 0x80002000
	cpu.PC = dol.Entry
	cpu.Halted = false
	m.started = true
	m.booted = true
	m.entry = dol.Entry
	return nil
}

// Booted reports whether BootDisc has run.
func (m *Machine) Booted() bool { return m.booted }

// Serialize writes the whole-machine state: version byte,
// the CPU state, the GPU state, MEM1, the locked cache
// window, both hardware pages, the GCN-3 device blocks
// (DSP, AI, DI, EXI, SI, VI), and the machine tail (pad,
// started, entry, and the GCN-3 extension: total cycles,
// DSP remainder, PI INTMSK, booted flag).
func (m *Machine) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	cpuState := m.cpu.Serialize()
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[1:], uint32(len(cpuState)))
	off := 5
	off += copy(out[off:], cpuState)
	off += copy(out[off:], m.gpu.Serialize())
	off += copy(out[off:], m.mem1)
	off += copy(out[off:], m.locked)
	off += copy(out[off:], m.hw0C)
	off += copy(out[off:], m.hw0D)
	off += copy(out[off:], m.dsp.Serialize())
	off += copy(out[off:], m.ai.Serialize())
	off += copy(out[off:], m.di.Serialize())
	off += copy(out[off:], m.exi.Serialize())
	off += copy(out[off:], m.si.Serialize())
	off += copy(out[off:], m.vi.Serialize())
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[off:], m.pad.Buttons)
	out[off+2] = m.pad.TriggerL
	out[off+3] = m.pad.TriggerR
	out[off+4] = m.pad.StickX
	out[off+5] = m.pad.StickY
	out[off+6] = m.pad.CStickX
	out[off+7] = m.pad.CStickY
	if m.started {
		out[off+8] = 1
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off+12:], m.entry)
	tail := off + 16
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[tail:], m.totalCycles)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[tail+8:], m.dspRem)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[tail+12:], m.piINTMSK)
	if m.booted {
		out[tail+16] = 1
	}
	if tail+17 != StateSize {
		panic("system: serialize size mismatch")
	}
	return out
}

// ErrBadState reports a state block that does not match
// this machine's layout or version.
var ErrBadState = errors.New("system: bad save state")

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (m *Machine) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != StateSize || in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return ErrBadState
	}
	cpuLen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[1:]))
	if cpuLen != gekko.SerializeSize {
		return ErrBadState
	}
	off := 5
	if err := m.cpu.Deserialize(in[off : off+cpuLen]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += cpuLen
	if err := m.gpu.Deserialize(in[off : off+gpu.SerializeSize]); err != nil {
		return ErrBadState
	}
	off += gpu.SerializeSize
	off += copy(m.mem1, in[off:])
	off += copy(m.locked, in[off:])
	off += copy(m.hw0C, in[off:])
	off += copy(m.hw0D, in[off:])
	blocks := []struct {
		size int
		load func([]byte) error
	}{
		{dsp.SerializeSize, m.dsp.Deserialize},
		{ai.SerializeSize, m.ai.Deserialize},
		{di.SerializeSize, m.di.Deserialize},
		{exi.SerializeSize, m.exi.Deserialize},
		{si.SerializeSize, m.si.Deserialize},
		{vi.SerializeSize, m.vi.Deserialize},
	}
	for _, b := range blocks {
		if err := b.load(in[off : off+b.size]); err != nil {
			return ErrBadState
		}
		off += b.size
	}
	// The AI Deserialize may report an AIINT change through
	// OnAIDInt; make sure the wiring still points at the DSP.
	m.ai.OnAIDInt = m.dsp.SetAIDInt
	m.pad.Buttons = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(in[off:])
	m.pad.TriggerL = in[off+2]
	m.pad.TriggerR = in[off+3]
	m.pad.StickX = in[off+4]
	m.pad.StickY = in[off+5]
	m.pad.CStickX = in[off+6]
	m.pad.CStickY = in[off+7]
	m.started = in[off+8] != 0
	m.entry = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off+12:])
	tail := off + 16
	m.totalCycles = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(in[tail:])
	m.dspRem = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[tail+8:])
	m.piINTMSK = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[tail+12:])
	m.booted = in[tail+16] != 0
	m.cpu.Halted = !m.started
	return nil
}
