package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"math"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/chips/gekko"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/disc"
)

// MMIO window bases used by the GCN-3 tests, at the
// uncached alias software normally uses.
const (
	mmioVI  = 0xCC002000
	mmioPI  = 0xCC003000
	mmioDSP = 0xCC005000
	mmioDI  = 0xCC006000
	mmioSI  = 0xCC006400
	mmioEXI = 0xCC006800
	mmioAI  = 0xCC006C00
)

// PI cause bits, mirrored from system.go for assertions.
const (
	piBitDSP uint32 = 0x00000001
	piBitAI  uint32 = 0x00000002
	piBitEXI uint32 = 0x00000004
	piBitSI  uint32 = 0x00000008
	piBitDI  uint32 = 0x00000010
	piBitVI  uint32 = 0x00000020
)

func TestDIReadThroughMMIO(t *testing.T) {
	img, err := disc.Parse(syntheticImage())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(img); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Unmask the transfer complete interrupt, aim the DMA
	// at MEM1 0x4000, and read 64 disc bytes from disc
	// offset 0x40 (CMDBUF1 holds the offset shifted by 2).
	m.Write32(mmioDI+0x00, 0x10)       // DISR: TCINTMSK
	m.Write32(mmioDI+0x08, 0xA8000000) // DICMDBUF0: read
	m.Write32(mmioDI+0x0C, 0x10)       // DICMDBUF1: offset 0x40
	m.Write32(mmioDI+0x10, 64)         // DICMDBUF2: length
	m.Write32(mmioDI+0x18, 0x4000)     // DIMAR
	m.Write32(mmioDI+0x20, 0x3)        // DICR: TSTART | DMA

	want := make([]byte, 64)
	if n := img.ReadAt(0x40, want); n != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("disc ReadAt = %d, want 64", n)
	}
	for i, b := range want {
		if got := m.Read8(uint32(0x4000 + i)); got != b {
			t.Fatalf("MEM1 byte %d = %#x, want %#x from the disc", i, got, b)
		}
	}
	if got := m.Read32(mmioDI + 0x1C); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("DILENGTH = %d, want 0 when done", got)
	}
	// The PI aggregate shows the DI cause, and with the DI
	// bit in PI_INTMSK the CPU IRQ line asserts.
	if got := m.Read32(mmioPI + 0x00); got&piBitDI == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("PI_INTSR = %#x, want the DI bit set", got)
	}
	m.Write32(mmioPI+0x04, piBitDI)
	if got := m.Read32(mmioPI + 0x04); got != piBitDI {
		t.Fatalf("PI_INTMSK = %#x, want %#x", got, piBitDI)
	}
	if !m.CPU().IRQ() {
		t.Fatal("CPU IRQ line not asserted with DI pending and unmasked in PI")
	}
}

func TestSIPollThroughMMIO(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.SetButtons(PadState{
		Buttons: PadA | PadStart, TriggerL: 3, TriggerR: 4,
		StickX: 200, StickY: 30, CStickX: 1, CStickY: 2,
	})
	// POLL with channel 0 enabled polls at once in this
	// model.
	m.Write32(mmioSI+0x30, 1)
	hi := m.Read32(mmioSI + 0x04)
	wantHi := uint32(PadA|PadStart)<<16 | 200<<8 | 30
	if hi != wantHi {
		t.Fatalf("SI INBUF_HI = %#08x, want %#08x", hi, wantHi)
	}
	lo := m.Read32(mmioSI + 0x08)
	wantLo := uint32(1)<<24 | uint32(2)<<16 | uint32(3)<<8 | 4
	if lo != wantLo {
		t.Fatalf("SI INBUF_LO = %#08x, want %#08x", lo, wantLo)
	}
}

func TestVIInterruptsOverThreeFrames(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadMachine(t)
	m.Start()
	// Display interrupt 0 at halfline 4, enabled, and the
	// VI cause unmasked in the PI.
	m.Write32(mmioVI+0x14, (1<<28)|4) // VIDI0: DIE | target 4
	m.Write32(mmioPI+0x04, piBitVI)

	fires := 0
	for frame := 0; frame < 3; frame++ {
		m.RunFrame()
		if got := m.Read32(mmioPI + 0x00); got&piBitVI != 0 {
			fires++
		} else {
			t.Fatalf("frame %d: PI_INTSR = %#x, want the VI bit set", frame, got)
		}
		// Clear DIS between frames, as hardware requires:
		// write the VIDI0 high lane with DIS clear and DIE
		// kept (DIE is lane bit 12).
		m.Write16(mmioVI+0x14, 1<<12)
		if got := m.Read32(mmioPI + 0x00); got&piBitVI != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("frame %d: VI bit still set after the DIS clear", frame)
		}
	}
	if fires != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("VI assertions over 3 frames = %d, want exactly 3", fires)
	}
}

// spinImage builds a synthetic disc whose DOL is a
// single branch-to-self at 0x80001000: a CPU that steps
// forever without touching anything, for tests that only
// need the devices clocked.
func spinImage() []byte {
	data := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	data[0] = 'G'
	copy(data[0x20:], "GCN-3 Spin Synthetic")
	put32(data, 0x1C, disc.GCMagic)
	put32(data, 0x420, 0x5000) // DOL offset
	dol := uint32(0x5000)
	put32(data, dol+0x00, 0x100)      // text0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x48, 0x80001000) // text0 address
	put32(data, dol+0x90, 4)
	put32(data, dol+0xE0, 0x80001000) // entry
	put32(data, 0x5100, 18<<26)       // b .
	return data
}

func spinMachine(t *testing.T) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	img, err := disc.Parse(spinImage())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(img); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.Start()
	return m
}

// aiFillSine fills MEM1 at the physical base address
// with a stereo sine buffer.
func aiFillSine(m *Machine, base uint32, frames int, freq float64) {
	for i := 0; i < frames; i++ {
		phase := 2 * math.Pi * freq * float64(i) / 48000
		s := uint16(int16(10000 * math.Sin(phase)))
		off := base + uint32(i*4)
		m.Write16(off, s)
		m.Write16(off+2, s)
	}
}

// aiProgram programs the AI through MMIO to stream
// frames stereo frames from the physical base address.
func aiProgram(m *Machine, base uint32, frames int, volL, volR uint32) {
	m.Write32(mmioAI+0x04, volL<<16|volR) // AIVR
	m.Write32(mmioAI+0x20, base)          // DMA address
	// DMA length: the length low lane first, then the
	// high lane with the enable bit, because the DMA
	// starts on the high lane write.
	m.Write16(mmioAI+0x26, uint16(frames*4))
	m.Write16(mmioAI+0x24, 0x8000|uint16(frames*4>>16))
	m.Write32(mmioAI+0x00, 1|2) // AICR: PSTAT | AIINTMSK
}

func TestAIDMAAtSystemLevel(t *testing.T) {
	m := spinMachine(t)

	const frames = 960 // 20 ms at 48000 Hz
	const base = 0x8000
	aiFillSine(m, base, frames, 440)
	aiProgram(m, base, frames, 127, 127)
	if got := m.AudioRate(); got != 48000 {
		t.Fatalf("AudioRate = %d, want 48000", got)
	}
	m.Write32(mmioPI+0x04, piBitAI)
	m.RunCycles(frames * 10125) // exactly 960 sample frames

	out := m.AudioBuffer()
	if len(out) != 2*frames {
		t.Fatalf("AudioBuffer = %d samples, want %d", len(out), 2*frames)
	}
	crossings := 0
	for i := 1; i < frames; i++ {
		if out[(i-1)*2] < 0 && out[i*2] >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
	}
	// 440 Hz over 20 ms is 8.8 periods: 8 or 9 positive
	// zero crossings, a frequency within tolerance.
	if crossings < 8 || crossings > 9 {
		t.Fatalf("positive zero crossings = %d, want 8 or 9 (440 Hz)", crossings)
	}
	freq := float64(crossings) * 48000 / frames
	if freq < 400 || freq > 480 {
		t.Fatalf("measured frequency = %.0f Hz, want 440 within tolerance", freq)
	}
	// The DMA completion raised the AI interrupt, visible
	// in the PI aggregate and on the CPU IRQ line.
	if got := m.Read32(mmioPI + 0x00); got&piBitAI == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("PI_INTSR = %#x, want the AI bit set", got)
	}
	if !m.CPU().IRQ() {
		t.Fatal("CPU IRQ line not asserted with AI pending and unmasked in PI")
	}

	// Volume scaling: a short constant stream at left
	// volume 64, right volume 127.
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		off := base + uint32(i*4)
		m.Write16(off, 1000)
		m.Write16(off+2, uint16(0xF830)) // -2000
	}
	// Clear AIINT (write 1 to clear), keep playing.
	m.Write32(mmioAI+0x00, 1|2|4)
	aiProgram(m, base, 8, 64, 127)
	m.RunCycles(8 * 10125)
	out = m.AudioBuffer()
	if len(out) < 2 {
		t.Fatalf("volume run produced %d samples", len(out))
	}
	if out[0] != 503 { // 1000 * 64 / 127
		t.Fatalf("left sample at volume 64 = %d, want 503", out[0])
	}
	if out[1] != -2000 { // full volume passes through
		t.Fatalf("right sample at volume 127 = %d, want -2000", out[1])
	}
}

// dspMailProgram is a small IRAM program in the
// published GCDSP encodings: it loads the CPU mail low
// word from DMBL (0xFFFD, which clears the pending
// flag), doubles it in ACC0 through the AX0 path, loads
// the magic 0x2A2A into ACC0.M, stores ACC0.M to DMBH
// and ACC0.L to DMBL (which commits the return mail),
// raises DSPINT through DIRQ, and halts.
func dspMailProgram() []uint16 {
	return []uint16{
		0x00D8, 0xFFFD, // LR $ax0.l, @0xFFFD
		0x6800,         // MOVAX $ac0, $ax0
		0x4800,         // ADDAX $ac0, $ax0 (ac0 = 2 * mail low)
		0x009D, 0x2A2A, // LRI $ac0.m, #0x2A2A
		0x0092, 0x00FF, // LRI $cr, #0xFF (SRS page)
		0x2DFC,         // SRS @0xFFFC, $ac0.m (DMBH = magic)
		0x2CFD,         // SRS @0xFFFD, $ac0.l (DMBL = doubled)
		0x16F9, 0x0001, // SI @0xFFF9, #1 (DIRQ)
		0x0021, // HALT
	}
}

// dspSetup uploads the mail program through the DSP
// accessor, releases DSPRST with DSPINTMSK set through
// the CONTROL lane at the DSP window, and sends the
// mail 0x00001234 from the CPU side.
func dspSetup(t *testing.T, m *Machine) {
	t.Helper()
	m.DSP().UploadIRAM(0, dspMailProgram())
	// CONTROL: DSPRST clear (release), DSPINTMSK set.
	m.Write16(mmioDSP+0x0C, 0x0008)
	m.Write16(mmioDSP+0x00, 0x0000) // mail high
	m.Write16(mmioDSP+0x02, 0x1234) // mail low, sets pending
}

func TestDSPMailboxAtSystemLevel(t *testing.T) {
	m := spinMachine(t)
	dspSetup(t, m)
	m.RunCycles(600)

	hi := m.Read16(mmioDSP + 0x04)
	if hi != 0x8000|0x2A2A {
		t.Fatalf("DSP mail high = %#04x, want 0x8000|0x2A2A (ready, magic)", hi)
	}
	lo := m.Read16(mmioDSP + 0x06)
	if lo != 0x2468 {
		t.Fatalf("DSP mail low = %#04x, want 0x2468 (doubled 0x1234)", lo)
	}
	// The DIRQ raised the DSP cause in the PI aggregate,
	// and unmasking it there asserts the CPU IRQ line.
	if got := m.Read32(mmioPI + 0x00); got&piBitDSP == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("PI_INTSR = %#x, want the DSP bit set", got)
	}
	m.Write32(mmioPI+0x04, piBitDSP)
	if !m.CPU().IRQ() {
		t.Fatal("CPU IRQ line not asserted with DSP pending and unmasked in PI")
	}
}

// bootImage builds a synthetic disc whose DOL stores a
// magic word at 0x80003000 and spins, with a BSS block
// ending at physical 0x5100 and an FST of fstSize pattern
// bytes at disc offset 0x6000.
func bootImage(fstSize uint32) []byte {
	data := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	data[0] = 'G'
	copy(data[0x20:], "GCN-3 Boot Synthetic")
	put32(data, 0x1C, disc.GCMagic)
	put32(data, 0x420, 0x5000)  // DOL offset
	put32(data, 0x424, 0x6000)  // FST offset
	put32(data, 0x428, fstSize) // FST size
	for i := uint32(0); i < fstSize; i++ {
		data[0x6000+i] = byte(i*3 + 1)
	}

	prog := []uint32{
		d(15, 3, 0, 0x8000), // addis r3, r0, 0x8000
		d(14, 3, 3, 0x3000), // addi r3, r3, 0x3000
		d(15, 4, 0, 0x1234), // addis r4, r0, 0x1234
		d(24, 4, 4, 0x5678), // ori r4, r4, 0x5678
		d(36, 4, 3, 0),      // stw r4, 0(r3)
		18 << 26,            // spin: b .
	}
	// The text sits at physical 0x2100, above the boot
	// exception vectors (0x100 to 0x1F00) and the return
	// trampoline at 0x2000, as real DOLs keep low memory
	// clear.
	dol := uint32(0x5000)
	put32(data, dol+0x00, 0x100)      // text0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x48, 0x80002100) // text0 address
	put32(data, dol+0x90, uint32(4*len(prog)))
	put32(data, dol+0xD8, 0x80005000) // BSS address
	put32(data, dol+0xDC, 0x100)      // BSS size: ends at physical 0x5100
	put32(data, dol+0xE0, 0x80002100) // entry
	for i, w := range prog {
		put32(data, 0x5100+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
	return data
}

func TestBootDiscGate(t *testing.T) {
	if err := New().BootDisc(); err != ErrNoDisc {
		t.Fatalf("BootDisc with no disc = %v, want ErrNoDisc", err)
	}

	const fstSize = 0x30
	img, err := disc.Parse(bootImage(fstSize))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(img); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cpu := m.CPU()

	// FST placement: immediately after the BSS end
	// (physical 0x5100, already 32-byte aligned).
	const fstPhys = 0x5100
	const fstEff = 0x80000000 | fstPhys
	if cpu.GPR[3] != fstEff {
		t.Fatalf("r3 = %#x, want the FST effective address %#x", cpu.GPR[3], fstEff)
	}
	if cpu.GPR[4] != fstSize {
		t.Fatalf("r4 = %#x, want the FST size %#x", cpu.GPR[4], fstSize)
	}
	for i := uint32(0); i < fstSize; i++ {
		if got, want := m.Read8(fstEff+i), byte(i*3+1); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("FST byte %d at the effective address = %#x, want %#x", i, got, want)
		}
	}

	// Boot info block.
	checks := []struct {
		off  uint32
		want uint32
		name string
	}{
		{0x00, 1, "console type"},
		{0x20, 0x0D15EA5E, "BS2 executed magic"},
		{0x28, MEM1Size, "simulated memory size"},
		{0x2C, fstPhys, "FST start physical"},
		// Arena low is the FST end aligned up to 32 bytes:
		// 0x5100 + 0x30 = 0x5130, aligned up is 0x5140.
		{0x30, 0x80000000 | 0x5140, "arena low"},
		{0x34, 0x81800000, "arena high"},
		{0x38, fstSize, "FST max size"},
	}
	for _, c := range checks {
		if got := m.Read32(c.off); got != c.want {
			t.Fatalf("boot info %s at %#x = %#x, want %#x", c.name, c.off, got, c.want)
		}
	}

	// CPU boot state.
	if cpu.GPR[1] != 0x817FFFE0 {
		t.Fatalf("r1 (stack) = %#x, want 0x817fffe0", cpu.GPR[1])
	}
	if cpu.LR != 0x80002000 {
		t.Fatalf("LR = %#x, want 0x80002000", cpu.LR)
	}
	if got := m.Read32(0x2000); got != 0x48000000 {
		t.Fatalf("trampoline at physical 0x2000 = %#x, want branch to self", got)
	}
	for _, vec := range []uint32{0x100, 0x500, 0x900, 0x1F00} {
		if got := m.Read32(vec); got != 0x48000000 {
			t.Fatalf("vector at %#x = %#x, want branch to self", vec, got)
		}
	}
	if cpu.MSR != gekko.MSRFP|gekko.MSRIR|gekko.MSRDR {
		t.Fatalf("MSR = %#x, want %#x (FP, IR, DR)", cpu.MSR, gekko.MSRFP|gekko.MSRIR|gekko.MSRDR)
	}
	if cpu.SR[0] != 0x80000000 || cpu.SR[15] != 0x80000000 {
		t.Fatalf("segment registers = %#x .. %#x, want 0x80000000", cpu.SR[0], cpu.SR[15])
	}
	bats := []struct {
		spr  int
		want uint32
	}{
		{528, 0x800003FF}, {529, 0x00000002},
		{530, 0x000003FF}, {531, 0x00000002},
		{536, 0x800003FF}, {537, 0x00000002},
		{538, 0x000003FF}, {539, 0x00000002},
	}
	for _, b := range bats {
		if got := cpu.GetSPR(b.spr); got != b.want {
			t.Fatalf("SPR %d = %#x, want %#x", b.spr, got, b.want)
		}
	}
	if cpu.PC != 0x80002100 || cpu.Halted {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %#x halted = %v, want entry 0x80002100 running", cpu.PC, cpu.Halted)
	}
	if !m.Started() || !m.Booted() {
		t.Fatal("machine should report started and booted after BootDisc")
	}

	// Control reaches the DOL entry: its first store lands
	// in MEM1 through the boot BATs.
	m.RunCycles(50)
	if got := m.Read32(0x80003000); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("DOL store at 0x80003000 = %#x, want 0x12345678", got)
	}
}

// TestGCN3ExtendedDeterminism boots the GCN-2 GX scene
// disc through BootDisc (its DOL text relocated above
// the boot vectors), runs it with a DSP mailbox program
// and an AI DMA stream live, saves mid-run, restores
// into a fresh booted machine, and requires the
// continuation to be byte-identical in state, pixels
// and audio.
func TestGCN3ExtendedDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	raw := gxImage()
	// Relocate the DOL text and entry from physical
	// 0x1000 to 0x2100, above the boot exception vectors.
	put32(raw, 0x5000+0x48, 0x80002100)
	put32(raw, 0x5000+0xE0, 0x80002100)
	img, err := disc.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	setup := func() *Machine {
		m := New()
		if err := m.LoadDisc(img); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		dspSetup(t, m)
		aiFillSine(m, 0x6000, 480, 440)
		aiProgram(m, 0x6000, 480, 127, 127)
		return m
	}

	ref := setup()
	ref.RunCycles(200000)
	mid := ref.Serialize()
	if len(mid) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(mid), StateSize)
	}
	ref.RunCycles(200000)
	stateRef := ref.Serialize()
	fbRef := append([]uint32(nil), ref.Framebuffer()...)
	audioRef := ref.AudioBuffer()

	// Sanity: all three subsystems actually ran.
	if px := fbRef[240*Width+320]; px != 0xFFC81E3C {
		t.Fatalf("GX quad center pixel = %#08x, want ffc81e3c", px)
	}
	if len(audioRef) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("reference run produced no audio")
	}
	if lo := ref.Read16(mmioDSP + 0x06); lo != 0x2468 {
		t.Fatalf("reference DSP mail low = %#04x, want 0x2468", lo)
	}

	m2 := setup()
	if err := m2.Deserialize(mid); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m2.RunCycles(200000)
	if !bytes.Equal(m2.Serialize(), stateRef) {
		t.Fatal("continuation after restore diverged from the uninterrupted run")
	}
	fb2 := m2.Framebuffer()
	for i := range fbRef {
		if fb2[i] != fbRef[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d differs after restore: %#08x vs %#08x", i, fb2[i], fbRef[i])
		}
	}
	audio2 := m2.AudioBuffer()
	if len(audio2) != len(audioRef) {
		t.Fatalf("audio after restore = %d samples, want %d", len(audio2), len(audioRef))
	}
	for i := range audioRef {
		if audio2[i] != audioRef[i] {
			t.Fatalf("audio sample %d differs after restore: %d vs %d", i, audio2[i], audioRef[i])
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/system/system_gcn4_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/disc"
)

// GCN-4 homebrew enginetest: a fully synthetic GameCube
// disc whose DOL, entered through the real BootDisc HLE
// boot with no seeding, drives every subsystem the core
// built across GCN-1 to GCN-3 and reports progress in
// milestone flag words in MEM1. The DOL walks the FST to
// find TESTDATA.BIN, DI-DMAs it into MEM1 and checksums
// it, streams a 440 Hz sine through the AI, polls the SI
// pad, round-trips a 512 byte pattern through memory
// card A over EXI, pushes a GX FIFO stream that clears
// the EFB to a programmed color and draws a flat-shaded
// quad, then spins on the VI current-halfline register.
//
// Effective addresses the DOL uses: work areas ride the
// boot BAT0 MEM1 window (0x80000000). The hardware page
// at 0x0C000000 sits outside both boot BATs (DBAT1 spans
// only the first 32 MB), so the DOL programs DBAT2 for
// it through mtspr before touching any device, the same
// thing the SDK runtime does on real software.

const (
	engFlags   = 0x80006000 // five milestone words
	engLog     = 0x80006100 // stage numbers in completion order
	engSIBuf   = 0x80007000 // SI INBUF pair copied here
	engSinePhy = 0x00008000 // AI DMA source (physical)
	engDIDest  = 0x00009000 // DI DMA destination (physical)
	engCardPat = 0x0000A000 // card pattern source (physical)
	engCardRB  = 0x0000B000 // card readback destination (physical)
	engTestOff = 0x20000    // TESTDATA.BIN offset on the disc
	engTestLen = 2048
	engSineN   = 960 // stereo frames of 440 Hz sine
)

// testDataByte is the TESTDATA.BIN content pattern.
func testDataByte(i int) byte { return byte(i*7 + 3) }

func testDataSum() uint32 {
	var s uint32
	for i := 0; i < engTestLen; i++ {
		s += uint32(testDataByte(i))
	}
	return s
}

// ppcAsm is a tiny two-pass assembler for the fixture
// program: instructions are emitted with named labels,
// and branches are patched once every label is known.
type ppcFix struct {
	at     int
	label  string
	bo, bi uint32
	abs    bool
}

type ppcAsm struct {
	code   []uint32
	labels map[string]int
	fix    []ppcFix
	serial int
}

func newAsm() *ppcAsm { return &ppcAsm{labels: map[string]int{}} }

func (a *ppcAsm) e(w uint32) { a.code = append(a.code, w) }

func (a *ppcAsm) lab(name string) { a.labels[name] = len(a.code) }

func (a *ppcAsm) uniq(prefix string) string {
	a.serial++
	return prefix + string(rune('a'+a.serial%26)) + string(rune('0'+(a.serial/26)%10))
}

func (a *ppcAsm) b(label string) {
	a.fix = append(a.fix, ppcFix{at: len(a.code), label: label, abs: true})
	a.e(0)
}

func (a *ppcAsm) bc(bo, bi uint32, label string) {
	a.fix = append(a.fix, ppcFix{at: len(a.code), label: label, bo: bo, bi: bi})
	a.e(0)
}

func (a *ppcAsm) beq(label string) { a.bc(12, 2, label) }
func (a *ppcAsm) bne(label string) { a.bc(4, 2, label) }

// li32 loads a 32 bit constant with lis plus ori.
func (a *ppcAsm) li32(rt int, v uint32) {
	a.e(d(15, uint32(rt), 0, v>>16))
	a.e(d(24, uint32(rt), uint32(rt), v&0xFFFF))
}

func (a *ppcAsm) words() []uint32 {
	for _, f := range a.fix {
		target, ok := a.labels[f.label]
		if !ok {
			panic("ppcAsm: unknown label " + f.label)
		}
		off := target - f.at
		if f.abs {
			a.code[f.at] = 18<<26 | (uint32(off)&0xFFFFFF)<<2
		} else {
			a.code[f.at] = 16<<26 | f.bo<<21 | f.bi<<16 | (uint32(off)&0x3FFF)<<2
		}
	}
	return a.code
}

// rlwinm encodes a rotate-left-word-immediate then AND
// with mask: the shape srwi and field extracts use.
func rlwinm(rs, ra, sh, mb, me uint32) uint32 {
	return 21<<26 | rs<<21 | ra<<16 | sh<<11 | mb<<6 | me<<1
}

// gxStreamGCN4 is the FIFO stream the DOL pushes: the
// audited CP and BP setup from the GCN-2 gate, a
// fullscreen quad in the clear color (20, 40, 200), then
// the flat center quad in (200, 30, 60). The pixel
// probes the gate asserts were measured against this
// core before the stream was baked into the fixture.
func gxStreamGCN4() []byte {
	var b bytes.Buffer
	cp := func(reg byte, v uint32) {
		b.WriteByte(0x08)
		b.WriteByte(reg)
		var w [4]byte
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w[:], v)
		b.Write(w[:])
	}
	bp := func(reg byte, v uint32) {
		b.WriteByte(0x61)
		var w [4]byte
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w[:], uint32(reg)<<24|(v&0xFFFFFF))
		b.Write(w[:])
	}
	cp(0x50, (1<<9)|(1<<13)) // VCD low: position direct, color 0 direct
	cp(0x60, 0)              // VCD high
	cp(0x70, 1|(4<<1)|(1<<13)|(5<<14))
	cp(0x80, 0)
	cp(0x90, 0)
	bp(0x43, 2) // PE control: RGBA8 pixel format
	bp(0x40, 0) // Z mode off
	bp(0x00, 0) // gen mode: no culling
	quad := func(half float32, r, g, bl byte) {
		b.WriteByte(0x80)
		var n [2]byte
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(n[:], 4)
		b.Write(n[:])
		verts := [][3]float32{
			{-half, half, 0}, {half, half, 0}, {half, -half, 0}, {-half, -half, 0},
		}
		for _, v := range verts {
			for _, f := range v {
				var w [4]byte
				binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w[:], math.Float32bits(f))
				b.Write(w[:])
			}
			b.Write([]byte{r, g, bl, 255})
		}
	}
	quad(1.0, 20, 40, 200)
	quad(0.5, 200, 30, 60)
	return b.Bytes()
}

// mtspr builds a move-to-SPR word; the SPR number is
// encoded in bits 11 to 20 with its two 5 bit halves
// swapped, per the architecture.
func mtspr(spr, rs int) uint32 {
	enc := uint32((spr&0x1F)<<5 | (spr >> 5))
	return 31<<26 | uint32(rs)<<21 | enc<<11 | 467<<1
}

// engineProgram assembles the DOL. streamAddr and
// nameAddr are the effective addresses of the FIFO stream
// and the TESTDATA.BIN name literal inside data0.
func engineProgram(streamLen int, streamAddr, nameAddr uint32) []uint32 {
	a := newAsm()
	milestone := func(k int, flagOff uint32) {
		a.e(d(14, 27, 0, uint32(k))) // addi r27, r0, k
		a.e(d(36, 27, 31, flagOff))  // stw r27, flagOff(r31)
		a.e(d(36, 27, 30, 0))        // stw r27, 0(r30)
		a.e(d(14, 30, 30, 4))        // addi r30, r30, 4
	}
	badFlag := func(k int, flagOff uint32) {
		a.li32(27, 0xBAD00000|uint32(k))
		a.e(d(36, 27, 31, flagOff)) // stw r27, flagOff(r31)
	}

	// Setup: r29 = FST base (the boot argument in r3),
	// r31 = flags, r30 = log pointer; both areas zeroed.
	a.e(x(3, 29, 3, 444)) // or r29, r3, r3
	a.li32(31, engFlags)
	a.li32(30, engLog)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		a.e(d(36, 0, 31, uint32(4*i))) // stw r0, flags
		a.e(d(36, 0, 30, uint32(4*i))) // stw r0, log (r30 advances later)
	}
	// The log stores above used r30 as base before it
	// starts advancing; reset it to the log base.
	a.li32(30, engLog)

	// The boot BATs map MEM1 only (DBAT0 at 0x80000000,
	// DBAT1 over the first 32 MB at 0). The hardware page
	// at 0x0C000000 is outside both, so the DOL maps it
	// itself with DBAT2: a 32 MB block, effective and
	// physical both 0x0C000000, supervisor read/write.
	a.li32(27, 0x0C0003FF)
	a.e(mtspr(540, 27)) // DBAT2U
	a.li32(27, 0x0C000002)
	a.e(mtspr(541, 27)) // DBAT2L

	// Stage 1: walk the FST from r29 for the one file,
	// verify its name, then DI DMA read and checksum it.
	a.e(d(32, 5, 29, 8))         // lwz r5, 8(r29): entry count
	a.e(rlwinm(5, 10, 2, 0, 29)) // slwi r10, r5, 2
	a.e(rlwinm(5, 9, 3, 0, 28))  // slwi r9, r5, 3
	a.e(x(10, 10, 9, 266))       // add r10, r10, r9 (count * 12)
	a.e(x(11, 29, 10, 266))      // add r11, r29, r10: string table base
	a.e(d(14, 6, 0, 1))          // addi r6, r0, 1 (entry index)
	a.e(d(14, 7, 29, 12))        // addi r7, r29, 12 (entry cursor)
	a.lab("fstloop")
	a.e(x(0, 6, 5, 0)) // cmpw r6, r5
	a.beq("fstfail")
	a.e(d(34, 8, 7, 0)) // lbz r8, 0(r7): entry type
	a.e(d(11, 0, 8, 0)) // cmpwi r8, 0
	a.bne("fstnext")
	a.e(d(32, 8, 7, 0))         // lwz r8, 0(r7): type and name offset
	a.e(rlwinm(8, 9, 0, 8, 31)) // extract name offset
	a.e(x(10, 11, 9, 266))      // add r10, r11, r9: name pointer
	a.li32(23, nameAddr)        // expected name literal
	a.e(d(14, 12, 0, 12))       // addi r12, r0, 12
	a.e(x(10, 13, 10, 444))     // or r13, r10, r10
	a.e(x(23, 14, 23, 444))     // or r14, r23, r23
	a.lab("namecmp")
	a.e(d(34, 15, 13, 0)) // lbz r15, 0(r13)
	a.e(d(34, 16, 14, 0)) // lbz r16, 0(r14)
	a.e(x(0, 15, 16, 0))  // cmpw r15, r16
	a.bne("fstnext")
	a.e(d(14, 13, 13, 1))
	a.e(d(14, 14, 14, 1))
	a.e(d(14, 12, 12, 0xFFFF)) // addi r12, r12, -1
	a.e(d(11, 0, 12, 0))       // cmpwi r12, 0
	a.bne("namecmp")
	a.e(d(32, 25, 7, 4)) // lwz r25, 4(r7): file disc offset
	a.e(d(32, 24, 7, 8)) // lwz r24, 8(r7): file size
	a.b("distart")
	a.lab("fstnext")
	a.e(d(14, 7, 7, 12))
	a.e(d(14, 6, 6, 1))
	a.b("fstloop")
	a.lab("fstfail")
	badFlag(1, 0)
	a.b("stage2")
	a.lab("distart")
	a.li32(28, 0x0C006000)         // DI window
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 0x10))        // TCINTMSK
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 0))          // stw DISR
	a.li32(27, 0xA8000000)         // read command
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 8))          // stw CMDBUF0
	a.e(rlwinm(25, 27, 30, 2, 31)) // srwi r27, r25, 2
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 12))         // stw CMDBUF1
	a.e(d(36, 24, 28, 16))         // stw CMDBUF2 = size
	a.li32(27, engDIDest)
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 24)) // stw DIMAR (physical)
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 3))   // TSTART | DMA
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 32)) // stw DICR
	a.lab("dipoll")
	a.e(d(32, 27, 28, 0))   // lwz r27, DISR
	a.e(d(28, 27, 27, 0x8)) // andi. r27, r27, TCINT
	a.beq("dipoll")
	a.li32(13, 0x80000000|engDIDest)
	a.e(d(14, 14, 0, 0))    // sum = 0
	a.e(x(24, 15, 24, 444)) // or r15, r24, r24 (count)
	a.lab("dick")
	a.e(d(34, 16, 13, 0)) // lbz r16, 0(r13)
	a.e(x(14, 14, 16, 266))
	a.e(d(14, 13, 13, 1))
	a.e(d(14, 15, 15, 0xFFFF))
	a.e(d(11, 0, 15, 0))
	a.bne("dick")
	a.li32(26, testDataSum())
	a.e(x(0, 14, 26, 0)) // cmpw sum, expected
	a.beq("s1ok")
	badFlag(2, 0)
	a.b("stage2")
	a.lab("s1ok")
	milestone(1, 0)

	// Stage 2: AI DMA of the sine table the DOL carries
	// in data1 at physical 0x8000; poll AIINT.
	a.lab("stage2")
	a.li32(28, 0x0C006C00) // AI window
	a.li32(27, 0x007F007F) // AIVR: full volume both sides
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 4))
	a.li32(27, engSinePhy)
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 32)) // DMA address lanes at +0x20
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, engSineN*4))
	a.e(d(44, 27, 28, 38)) // sth lenL at +0x26 first
	a.li32(27, 0x00008000) // lenH with the enable bit
	a.e(d(44, 27, 28, 36)) // sth lenH at +0x24 starts the DMA
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 3))   // PSTAT | AIINTMSK
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 0))  // stw AICR
	a.lab("aipoll")
	a.e(d(32, 27, 28, 0))
	a.e(d(28, 27, 27, 0x4)) // AIINT
	a.beq("aipoll")
	milestone(2, 4)

	// Stage 3: SI poll of channel 0 into the buffer.
	a.li32(28, 0x0C006400) // SI window
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 1))
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 48)) // stw POLL = channel 0 enable
	a.li32(13, engSIBuf)
	a.e(d(32, 27, 28, 4))
	a.e(d(36, 27, 13, 0))
	a.e(d(32, 27, 28, 8))
	a.e(d(36, 27, 13, 4))
	milestone(3, 8)

	// Stage 4: memory card A over EXI channel 0.
	a.li32(28, 0x0C006800)
	exiSel := func() { a.li32(27, 0x100); a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 0)) }
	exiDesel := func() { a.e(d(36, 0, 28, 0)) }
	exiClear := func() { a.li32(27, 0x108); a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 0)) }
	exiPoll := func() {
		l := a.uniq("exipoll")
		a.lab(l)
		a.e(d(32, 27, 28, 0))
		a.e(d(28, 27, 27, 0x8)) // TCINT
		a.beq(l)
	}
	exiCmd := func(cmd uint32, cr uint32) {
		exiClear()
		if cmd == 0 {
			a.e(d(36, 0, 28, 16))
		} else {
			a.li32(27, cmd<<24)
			a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 16))
		}
		a.e(d(14, 27, 0, cr))
		a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 12))
		exiPoll()
	}
	// (a) Read ID: wakes the card; expect 0x1000 in the
	// top half of DATA (16 Mbit size byte, then zero).
	// The first transfer writes the one-byte ID command;
	// the second clocks the two ID bytes into DATA (its
	// DATA store is inert, only the CR write matters).
	exiSel()
	exiCmd(0x00, 0x9)  // write 1 byte: the ID command
	exiCmd(0x00, 0x11) // read 2 bytes into DATA
	a.e(d(32, 27, 28, 16))
	a.e(rlwinm(27, 27, 16, 16, 31)) // srwi r27, r27, 16
	a.e(d(11, 0, 27, 0x1000))
	a.beq("idok")
	badFlag(4, 12)
	a.b("stage5")
	a.lab("idok")
	exiDesel()
	// (b) Write one 512 byte page at card address 0 from
	// the pattern at physical 0xA000.
	exiSel()
	exiCmd(0xF2, 0x9)  // write page command, 1 byte
	exiCmd(0x00, 0x29) // address word, 4 bytes (DATA = 0)
	exiClear()
	a.li32(27, engCardPat)
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 4)) // MAR
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 512))
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 8)) // LENGTH
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 0xB))
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 12)) // CR: TSTART | DMA | write
	exiPoll()
	exiDesel()
	// (c) Read the page back to physical 0xB000.
	exiSel()
	exiCmd(0x52, 0x9)  // read command, 1 byte
	exiCmd(0x00, 0x29) // address word, 4 bytes
	exiClear()
	a.li32(27, engCardRB)
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 4))
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 512))
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 8))
	a.e(d(14, 27, 0, 0x3))
	a.e(d(36, 27, 28, 12)) // CR: TSTART | DMA | read
	exiPoll()
	exiDesel()
	// (d) Byte-compare pattern and readback.
	a.li32(13, 0x80000000|engCardPat)
	a.li32(14, 0x80000000|engCardRB)
	a.e(d(14, 15, 0, 512))
	a.lab("cardcmp")
	a.e(d(34, 16, 13, 0))
	a.e(d(34, 17, 14, 0))
	a.e(x(0, 16, 17, 0))
	a.bne("cardbad")
	a.e(d(14, 13, 13, 1))
	a.e(d(14, 14, 14, 1))
	a.e(d(14, 15, 15, 0xFFFF))
	a.e(d(11, 0, 15, 0))
	a.bne("cardcmp")
	milestone(4, 12)
	a.b("stage5")
	a.lab("cardbad")
	badFlag(5, 12)

	// Stage 5: push the GX FIFO stream byte by byte.
	a.lab("stage5")
	a.li32(13, streamAddr)
	a.e(d(14, 14, 0, uint32(streamLen)))
	a.li32(28, 0x0C008000) // GX FIFO port
	a.lab("gxloop")
	a.e(d(34, 27, 13, 0))
	a.e(d(38, 27, 28, 0))
	a.e(d(14, 13, 13, 1))
	a.e(d(14, 14, 14, 0xFFFF))
	a.e(d(11, 0, 14, 0))
	a.bne("gxloop")
	milestone(5, 16)

	// Spin on the VI current halfline: wait for it to
	// change, forever.
	a.li32(28, 0x0C002000)
	a.lab("spin")
	a.e(d(40, 27, 28, 16)) // lhz r27, VICURR
	a.lab("spinwait")
	a.e(d(40, 13, 28, 16))
	a.e(x(0, 13, 27, 0))
	a.beq("spinwait")
	a.b("spin")

	return a.words()
}

// buildEngineDisc builds the synthetic enginetest disc:
// header, bi2 and apploader stubs, the DOL (engineProgram
// plus the FIFO stream and name literal in data0), an FST
// with the single file TESTDATA.BIN, and the file bytes.
func buildEngineDisc() []byte {
	stream := gxStreamGCN4()
	nameLit := []byte("TESTDATA.BIN\x00")
	dataLen := len(stream)
	if dataLen%4 != 0 {
		dataLen += 4 - dataLen%4
	}
	nameOff := dataLen
	dataLen += len(nameLit)
	prog := engineProgram(len(stream), 0x80004000, 0x80004000+uint32(nameOff))

	data := make([]byte, 0x21000)
	data[0] = 'G'
	copy(data[1:], "GT")
	copy(data[3:], "01")
	copy(data[0x20:], "iTaK GoGCN Engine Test")
	put32(data, 0x1C, disc.GCMagic)
	put32(data, 0x420, 0x5000) // DOL offset
	// FST: root plus one file, string table "\0TESTDATA.BIN\0".
	fstSize := uint32(24 + 14)
	put32(data, 0x424, 0x6000)
	put32(data, 0x428, fstSize)
	put32(data, 0x444, 24<<20) // bi2 simulated memory size
	copy(data[0x2440:], "2026/10/13")
	fst := uint32(0x6000)
	data[fst] = 1 // root directory
	put32(data, fst+8, 2)
	data[fst+12+1] = 0
	data[fst+12+2] = 0
	data[fst+12+3] = 1 // file name offset 1 in the string table
	put32(data, fst+12+4, engTestOff)
	put32(data, fst+12+8, engTestLen)
	copy(data[fst+24:], "\x00TESTDATA.BIN\x00")
	for i := 0; i < engTestLen; i++ {
		data[engTestOff+i] = testDataByte(i)
	}

	dol := uint32(0x5000)
	put32(data, dol+0x00, 0x100)      // text0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x48, 0x80002100) // text0 address
	put32(data, dol+0x90, uint32(4*len(prog)))
	put32(data, dol+0x1C, 0x2000) // data0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x64, 0x80004000)
	put32(data, dol+0xAC, uint32(dataLen))
	// data1 is the AI sine table, so the disc is
	// self-contained: real homebrew carries its data in
	// the DOL instead of relying on the host to stage
	// memory. It lands at physical engSinePhy, which is
	// where the DOL points the AI DMA.
	put32(data, dol+0x20, 0x3000) // data1 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x68, 0x80000000|engSinePhy)
	put32(data, dol+0xB0, uint32(engSineN*4))
	put32(data, dol+0xD8, 0x8000C000) // BSS address
	put32(data, dol+0xDC, 0x100)      // BSS size
	put32(data, dol+0xE0, 0x80002100) // entry
	for i, w := range prog {
		put32(data, 0x5100+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
	copy(data[0x7000:], stream)
	copy(data[0x7000+uint32(nameOff):], nameLit)
	for i := 0; i < engSineN; i++ {
		phase := 2 * math.Pi * 440 * float64(i) / 48000
		s := uint16(int16(10000 * math.Sin(phase)))
		off := 0x8000 + uint32(i*4)
		data[off] = byte(s >> 8)
		data[off+1] = byte(s)
		data[off+2] = byte(s >> 8)
		data[off+3] = byte(s)
	}
	return data
}

// cardPattern is the EXI round-trip pattern the harness
// stages in MEM1.
func cardPattern(i int) byte { return byte(i ^ 0x5A) }

// engineSetup loads and boots the enginetest disc and
// stages the card pattern and the pad state. (The AI
// sine table ships inside the DOL as data1, so the
// disc runs identically through the libretro shell,
// where no test harness stages memory for it.)
func engineSetup(t *testing.T) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	img, err := disc.Parse(buildEngineDisc())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(img); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !m.Booted() {
		t.Fatal("machine did not report booted")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 512; i++ {
		m.Write8(engCardPat+uint32(i), cardPattern(i))
	}
	m.SetButtons(PadState{
		Buttons: PadA | PadStart, TriggerL: 3, TriggerR: 4,
		StickX: 200, StickY: 30, CStickX: 1, CStickY: 2,
	})
	return m
}

func TestGCN4HomebrewEnginetest(t *testing.T) {
	m := engineSetup(t)
	for i := 0; i < 25; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}

	// Milestones, in order: the flag words carry the
	// stage numbers and the log records completion order.
	for k := 1; k <= 5; k++ {
		off := uint32(4 * (k - 1))
		if got := m.Read32(engFlags + off); got != uint32(k) {
			t.Fatalf("milestone flag %d = %#x, want %d", k, got, k)
		}
		if got := m.Read32(engLog + off); got != uint32(k) {
			t.Fatalf("milestone log %d = %#x, want %d", k, got, k)
		}
	}

	// Framebuffer: the flat quad color at the center, the
	// programmed clear color elsewhere.
	fb := m.Framebuffer()
	if px := fb[240*Width+320]; px != 0xFFC81E3C {
		t.Fatalf("center pixel = %#08x, want ffc81e3c (flat quad)", px)
	}
	for _, pt := range [][2]int{{0, 0}, {639, 479}, {10, 10}, {630, 20}} {
		if px := fb[pt[1]*Width+pt[0]]; px != 0xFF1428C8 {
			t.Fatalf("pixel (%d,%d) = %#08x, want ff1428c8 (clear color)", pt[0], pt[1], px)
		}
	}

	// Audio: the 440 Hz sine the AI DMA streamed.
	out := m.AudioBuffer()
	if len(out) < 2*engSineN {
		t.Fatalf("audio = %d samples, want at least %d", len(out), 2*engSineN)
	}
	crossings, peak := 0, 0
	for i := 0; i < engSineN; i++ {
		s := int(out[2*i])
		if s < 0 {
			s = -s
		}
		if s > peak {
			peak = s
		}
		if i > 0 && out[2*(i-1)] < 0 && out[2*i] >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
	}
	if crossings < 8 || crossings > 9 {
		t.Fatalf("sine positive zero crossings = %d, want 8 or 9 (440 Hz)", crossings)
	}
	if peak < 5000 {
		t.Fatalf("sine peak = %d, want a non-silent stream", peak)
	}

	// DI: the exact TESTDATA.BIN bytes landed in MEM1.
	for i := 0; i < engTestLen; i++ {
		if got := m.Read8(0x80000000 + engDIDest + uint32(i)); got != testDataByte(i) {
			t.Fatalf("DI byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, got, testDataByte(i))
		}
	}

	// EXI card: the pattern is in the card media itself
	// and in the readback buffer.
	card := m.CardImage(0)
	if len(card) < 512 {
		t.Fatalf("card image = %d bytes", len(card))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 512; i++ {
		if card[i] != cardPattern(i) {
			t.Fatalf("card byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, card[i], cardPattern(i))
		}
		if got := m.Read8(0x80000000 + engCardRB + uint32(i)); got != cardPattern(i) {
			t.Fatalf("card readback byte %d = %#x", i, got)
		}
	}

	// SI: the polled pad matches the staged buttons.
	wantHi := uint32(PadA|PadStart)<<16 | 200<<8 | 30
	if got := m.Read32(engSIBuf); got != wantHi {
		t.Fatalf("SI buffer high = %#08x, want %#08x", got, wantHi)
	}
	wantLo := uint32(1)<<24 | uint32(2)<<16 | uint32(3)<<8 | 4
	if got := m.Read32(engSIBuf + 4); got != wantLo {
		t.Fatalf("SI buffer low = %#08x, want %#08x", got, wantLo)
	}
}

func TestGCN4Determinism(t *testing.T) {
	ref := engineSetup(t)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		ref.RunFrame()
	}
	ref.AudioBuffer() // drain at the save point, both runs alike
	mid := ref.Serialize()
	if len(mid) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(mid), StateSize)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		ref.RunFrame()
	}
	stateRef := ref.Serialize()
	fbRef := append([]uint32(nil), ref.Framebuffer()...)
	audioRef := ref.AudioBuffer()

	m2 := engineSetup(t)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		m2.RunFrame()
	}
	m2.AudioBuffer()
	if err := m2.Deserialize(mid); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		m2.RunFrame()
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(m2.Serialize(), stateRef) {
		t.Fatal("continuation after restore diverged from the uninterrupted run")
	}
	fb2 := m2.Framebuffer()
	for i := range fbRef {
		if fb2[i] != fbRef[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d differs after restore", i)
		}
	}
	audio2 := m2.AudioBuffer()
	if len(audio2) != len(audioRef) {
		t.Fatalf("audio after restore = %d samples, want %d", len(audio2), len(audioRef))
	}
	for i := range audioRef {
		if audio2[i] != audioRef[i] {
			t.Fatalf("audio sample %d differs after restore: %d vs %d", i, audio2[i], audioRef[i])
		}
	}
}

// TestGCN4WriteDiscFixture writes the synthetic disc to
// the path in GCN4_DISC_OUT when set, so the shared
// enginetest harness can run the same disc through the
// built libretro shell. It skips when the variable is
// unset.
func TestGCN4WriteDiscFixture(t *testing.T) {
	path := os.Getenv("GCN4_DISC_OUT")
	if path == "" {
		t.Skip("GCN4_DISC_OUT not set")
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, buildEngineDisc(), 0644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/system/system_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gamecube/disc"
)

func d(op, f1v, f2v, imm uint32) uint32 {
	return op<<26 | f1v<<21 | f2v<<16 | imm&0xFFFF
}

func x(f1v, f2v, f3v, xov uint32) uint32 {
	return 31<<26 | f1v<<21 | f2v<<16 | f3v<<11 | xov<<1
}

func put32(b []byte, off uint32, v uint32) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[off:], v)
}

// testProgram is a hand-assembled PowerPC program: it
// sums the 16 data bytes at 0x80002000 into the word at
// 0x80003000, loads the decrementer with 40, enables
// external interrupts (which also drops the interrupt
// prefix, so the decrementer vector is physical 0x900),
// and spins. A one-word handler (b .) sits at 0x900.
func testProgram() []uint32 {
	mtsprDEC := uint32(31<<26 | 8<<21 | 704<<11 | 467<<1) // mtspr 22, r8
	return []uint32{
		d(14, 3, 0, 0),                  // addi r3, r0, 0        ; sum = 0
		d(15, 4, 0, 0x8000),             // addis r4, r0, 0x8000  ; r4 = 0x80000000
		d(14, 4, 4, 0x2000),             // addi r4, r4, 0x2000   ; data pointer
		d(14, 5, 0, 16),                 // addi r5, r0, 16       ; count
		d(34, 6, 4, 0),                  // loop: lbz r6, 0(r4)
		x(3, 3, 6, 266),                 // add r3, r3, r6
		d(14, 4, 4, 1),                  // addi r4, r4, 1
		d(14, 5, 5, 0xFFFF),             // addi r5, r5, -1
		d(11, 0, 5, 0),                  // cmpwi r5, 0
		16<<26 | 4<<21 | 2<<16 | 0xFFEC, // bne loop (-20)
		d(15, 7, 0, 0x8000),             // addis r7, r0, 0x8000
		d(14, 7, 7, 0x3000),             // addi r7, r7, 0x3000
		d(36, 3, 7, 0),                  // stw r3, 0(r7)
		d(14, 8, 0, 40),                 // addi r8, r0, 40
		mtsprDEC,                        // mtspr DEC, r8
		d(24, 0, 9, 0x8000),             // ori r9, r0, 0x8000 (MSR EE)
		x(9, 0, 0, 146),                 // mtmsr r9
		18 << 26,                        // spin: b .
	}
}

// syntheticImage builds a GC disc image whose DOL contains
// testProgram plus the decrementer handler and data.
func syntheticImage() []byte {
	data := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	data[0] = 'G'
	copy(data[0x20:], "System Synthetic")
	put32(data, 0x1C, disc.GCMagic)
	put32(data, 0x420, 0x5000) // DOL offset

	dol := uint32(0x5000)
	prog := testProgram()
	put32(data, dol+0x00, 0x100)      // text0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x48, 0x80001000) // text0 address
	put32(data, dol+0x90, uint32(4*len(prog)))
	put32(data, dol+0x04, 0x200)      // text1 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x4C, 0x80000900) // text1 address (the DEC vector page)
	put32(data, dol+0x94, 4)
	put32(data, dol+0x1C, 0x300)      // data0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x64, 0x80002000) // data0 address
	put32(data, dol+0xAC, 16)
	put32(data, dol+0xE0, 0x80001000) // entry

	for i, w := range prog {
		put32(data, 0x5100+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
	put32(data, 0x5200, 18<<26) // handler: b .
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		data[0x5300+i] = byte(i + 1)
	}
	return data
}

func loadMachine(t *testing.T) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	img, err := disc.Parse(syntheticImage())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(img); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return m
}

func TestMemoryMap(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.Write32(0x80000000, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if got := m.Read32(0x00000000); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("physical alias read = %#x", got)
	}
	if got := m.Read32(0xC0000000); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("uncached alias read = %#x", got)
	}
	m.Write16(0x0C001234, 0xABCD)
	if got := m.Read16(0x0C001234); got != 0xABCD {
		t.Fatalf("hw page = %#x", got)
	}
	m.Write8(0x0D00FFFF, 0x5A)
	if got := m.Read8(0x0D00FFFF); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("hw page 0D = %#x", got)
	}
	m.Write32(0xE0000100, 0x12345678)
	if got := m.Read32(0xE0000100); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("locked cache = %#x", got)
	}
	if got := m.Read32(0xFFF00100); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("IPL stub read = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
	m.Write32(0xFFF00100, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	if got := m.Read32(0xFFF00100); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("IPL stub accepted a write")
	}
	if got := m.Read32(0x10000000); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unmapped read = %#x", got)
	}
}

func TestLoadAndRunWithSaveState(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadMachine(t)
	if m.CPU().PC != 0x80001000 {
		t.Fatalf("entry PC = %#x", m.CPU().PC)
	}
	if m.Started() {
		t.Fatal("machine should start halted")
	}
	// Halted: cycles pass, nothing executes, no result.
	m.RunCycles(200)
	if got := m.Read32(0x80003000); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("halted machine produced %#x", got)
	}
	if got := m.Read8(0x80002000); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("data section not staged: %#x", got)
	}
	if got := m.Read8(0x8000200F); got != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("data section end: %#x", got)
	}

	m.SetButtons(PadState{Buttons: PadA | PadStart, TriggerL: 12, StickX: 200, CStickY: 33})
	m.Start()
	// 103 instructions take the program through the stw
	// of the checksum (4 setup + 96 loop + 3).
	m.RunCycles(103)
	if got := m.Read32(0x80003000); got != 136 {
		t.Fatalf("checksum = %d, want 136", got)
	}
	state1 := m.Serialize()
	if len(state1) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(state1), StateSize)
	}

	// Continue: the decrementer (40 ticks of 4 cycles,
	// loaded at instruction 105, EE enabled at 107) fires
	// and the CPU lands in the handler at 0x900 spinning.
	m.RunCycles(400)
	if pc := m.CPU().PC; pc != 0x900 {
		t.Fatalf("PC after DEC exception = %#x, want 0x900", pc)
	}
	if srr0 := m.CPU().SRR0; srr0 != 0x80001044 {
		t.Fatalf("SRR0 = %#x, want the spin loop 0x80001044", srr0)
	}
	stateA := m.Serialize()

	// A fresh machine restored from the mid-run state must
	// continue bit-identically.
	m2 := loadMachine(t)
	if err := m2.Deserialize(state1); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !m2.Started() {
		t.Fatal("restored machine lost its started flag")
	}
	if m2.Buttons() != m.Buttons() {
		t.Fatalf("restored buttons = %+v", m2.Buttons())
	}
	m2.RunCycles(400)
	if pc := m2.CPU().PC; pc != 0x900 {
		t.Fatalf("restored PC = %#x, want 0x900", pc)
	}
	if got := m2.Read32(0x80003000); got != 136 {
		t.Fatalf("restored checksum = %d", got)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(m2.Serialize(), stateA) {
		t.Fatal("continuation after restore diverged from the uninterrupted run")
	}
}

func TestFramebufferAndBadStates(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	fb := m.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) != Width*Height {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer = %d pixels", len(fb))
	}
	// GCN-2: the framebuffer is the GPU's EFB presented
	// after reset, which is opaque black, not the zeroed
	// stub buffer of GCN-1.
	for i, px := range fb {
		if px != 0xFF000000 {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d = %#x, want opaque black", i, px)
		}
	}
	if CyclesPerFrame != 8_100_000 {
		t.Fatalf("CyclesPerFrame = %d", CyclesPerFrame)
	}
	if err := m.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err != ErrBadState {
		t.Fatalf("short state err = %v", err)
	}
	bad := m.Serialize()
	bad[0] = 99
	if err := m.Deserialize(bad); err != ErrBadState {
		t.Fatalf("wrong version err = %v", err)
	}
}

// gxStream builds the GX FIFO byte stream the GCN-2
// determinism program copies out of MEM1: CP setup for
// direct f32 position plus direct RGBA8 color vertices
// (VAT 0 programmed through the documented CP addresses:
// group A 0x70, group B 0x80, group C 0x90), BP setup for
// the RGBA8 EFB format with depth off, and one quad.
func gxStream() []byte {
	var b bytes.Buffer
	cp := func(reg byte, v uint32) {
		b.WriteByte(0x08)
		b.WriteByte(reg)
		var w [4]byte
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w[:], v)
		b.Write(w[:])
	}
	bp := func(reg byte, v uint32) {
		b.WriteByte(0x61)
		var w [4]byte
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w[:], uint32(reg)<<24|(v&0xFFFFFF))
		b.Write(w[:])
	}
	cp(0x50, (1<<9)|(1<<13)) // VCD low: position direct, color 0 direct
	cp(0x60, 0)              // VCD high
	// VAT 0 group A: position 3 components f32, color 0
	// present in RGBA8 format.
	cp(0x70, 1|(4<<1)|(1<<13)|(5<<14))
	cp(0x80, 0) // VAT 0 group B
	cp(0x90, 0) // VAT 0 group C
	bp(0x43, 2) // PE control: RGBA8 pixel format
	bp(0x40, 0) // Z mode off
	bp(0x00, 0) // gen mode: no culling
	b.WriteByte(0x80)
	var n [2]byte
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(n[:], 4)
	b.Write(n[:])
	verts := [][3]float32{
		{-0.5, 0.5, 0}, {0.5, 0.5, 0}, {0.5, -0.5, 0}, {-0.5, -0.5, 0},
	}
	for _, v := range verts {
		for _, f := range v {
			var w [4]byte
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w[:], math.Float32bits(f))
			b.Write(w[:])
		}
		b.Write([]byte{200, 30, 60, 255})
	}
	return b.Bytes()
}

// gxProgram is the hand-assembled GCN-2 gate program: it
// enables the FPU, runs a paired-single add through the
// quantized load and store (GQR0 float, scale 0), then
// copies the GX FIFO stream staged at 0x80005000 byte by
// byte to the FIFO write port at 0xCC008000, and spins.
func gxProgram(streamLen int) []uint32 {
	psqL := uint32(56<<26 | 0<<21 | 3<<16)       // psq_l f0, 0(r3), W=0, GQR0
	psAdd := uint32(4<<26 | 1<<21 | 21<<1)       // ps_add f1, f0, f0
	psqSt := uint32(60<<26 | 1<<21 | 3<<16 | 16) // psq_st f1, 16(r3), W=0, GQR0
	return []uint32{
		d(24, 0, 9, 0x2000),             // ori r9, r0, 0x2000 (MSR FP)
		x(9, 0, 0, 146),                 // mtmsr r9
		d(15, 3, 0, 0x8000),             // addis r3, r0, 0x8000
		d(24, 3, 3, 0x4000),             // ori r3, r3, 0x4000
		psqL,                            // f0 = (1.5, 2.25)
		psAdd,                           // f1 = (3.0, 4.5)
		psqSt,                           // result cell at 0x80004010
		d(15, 3, 0, 0x8000),             // addis r3, r0, 0x8000
		d(24, 3, 3, 0x5000),             // ori r3, r3, 0x5000 (stream)
		d(14, 4, 0, uint32(streamLen)),  // addi r4, r0, len
		d(15, 5, 0, 0xCC00),             // addis r5, r0, 0xCC00
		d(24, 5, 5, 0x8000),             // ori r5, r5, 0x8000 (FIFO port)
		d(34, 6, 3, 0),                  // loop: lbz r6, 0(r3)
		d(38, 6, 5, 0),                  // stb r6, 0(r5)
		d(14, 3, 3, 1),                  // addi r3, r3, 1
		d(14, 4, 4, 0xFFFF),             // addi r4, r4, -1
		d(11, 0, 4, 0),                  // cmpwi r4, 0
		16<<26 | 4<<21 | 2<<16 | 0xFFEC, // bne loop
		18 << 26,                        // spin: b .
	}
}

// gxImage builds a synthetic disc whose DOL carries the
// gate program, the paired-single operands, and the FIFO
// stream.
func gxImage() []byte {
	stream := gxStream()
	prog := gxProgram(len(stream))
	data := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	data[0] = 'G'
	copy(data[0x20:], "GCN-2 Synthetic")
	put32(data, 0x1C, disc.GCMagic)
	put32(data, 0x420, 0x5000) // DOL offset

	dol := uint32(0x5000)
	put32(data, dol+0x00, 0x100)      // text0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x48, 0x80001000) // text0 address
	put32(data, dol+0x90, uint32(4*len(prog)))
	put32(data, dol+0x1C, 0x400)      // data0 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x64, 0x80004000) // data0 address (ps operands)
	put32(data, dol+0xAC, 24)
	put32(data, dol+0x20, 0x500) // data1 offset
	put32(data, dol+0x68, 0x80005000)
	put32(data, dol+0xB0, uint32(len(stream)))
	put32(data, dol+0xE0, 0x80001000) // entry

	// DOL section offsets are relative to the DOL header,
	// which sits at file offset 0x5000 in this image.
	for i, w := range prog {
		put32(data, 0x5100+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
	put32(data, 0x5400, math.Float32bits(1.5))
	put32(data, 0x5404, math.Float32bits(2.25))
	copy(data[0x5500:], stream)
	return data
}

func TestGXAndPairedSingleDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	img, err := disc.Parse(gxImage())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	load := func() *Machine {
		m := New()
		if err := m.LoadDisc(img); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		m.Start()
		return m
	}

	// Uninterrupted reference run.
	ref := load()
	ref.RunCycles(300)
	midState := ref.Serialize()
	ref.RunCycles(400)
	if got := ref.Read32(0x80004010); got != math.Float32bits(3.0) {
		t.Fatalf("ps_add ps0 result = %#x, want 3.0f bits", got)
	}
	if got := ref.Read32(0x80004014); got != math.Float32bits(4.5) {
		t.Fatalf("ps_add ps1 result = %#x, want 4.5f bits", got)
	}
	fbRef := append([]uint32(nil), ref.Framebuffer()...)
	if px := fbRef[240*Width+320]; px != 0xFFC81E3C {
		t.Fatalf("quad center pixel = %#08x, want ffc81e3c", px)
	}
	if px := fbRef[0]; px != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Fatalf("outside pixel = %#08x, want opaque black", px)
	}
	stateRef := ref.Serialize()

	// The mid-run state was taken while the FIFO copy was
	// partway through the draw command, so the GPU's
	// partial-command buffer is inside the state. A fresh
	// machine restored from it must continue identically.
	m2 := load()
	if err := m2.Deserialize(midState); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m2.RunCycles(400)
	if !bytes.Equal(m2.Serialize(), stateRef) {
		t.Fatal("continuation after restore diverged from the uninterrupted run")
	}
	fb2 := m2.Framebuffer()
	for i := range fbRef {
		if fb2[i] != fbRef[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d differs after restore: %#08x vs %#08x", i, fb2[i], fbRef[i])
		}
	}
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/vi/vi.go ====================

// Package vi models the GameCube video interface (VI)
// register window, based at 0x0C002000 on the hardware
// page, from published VI register documentation. The
// register file is accessed in 16-bit lanes; 32-bit
// registers occupy two consecutive lanes, the lane at the
// lower offset holding the high half (the machine is
// big-endian).
//
// Timing model (deliberately simple and self-consistent,
// stated exactly): one machine frame is CyclesPerFrame
// CPU cycles (486 MHz / 60). The number of fields per
// frame is 1 when the VIDCR NIN bit is set (non-interlaced)
// and 2 otherwise. Lines per field are ACV + PRB + PSB,
// where ACV comes from VITV and PRB and PSB always come
// from the even-field vertical timing register VIVTE in
// this simplified model (the odd-field register VIVTO is
// stored but never used for timing). Lines per frame are
// linesPerField times fieldsPerFrame, and the total
// halflines per frame are 2 times linesPerFrame. The
// halfline counter is
//
//	CurrentHalfline = (cyclesIntoFrame * totalHalflines) / CyclesPerFrame
//
// where cyclesIntoFrame is the accumulated cycle count
// modulo CyclesPerFrame. The counter is monotonic within
// a frame and wraps at the frame boundary.
//
// Presentation is not part of this package: the frame
// buffer base registers (VITFBL, VITFBR, VIBFBL, VIBFBR)
// are stored state only, and actual presentation stays
// with the GX embedded frame buffer in package gpu.
package vi

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// CyclesPerFrame is the frame budget at the Gekko clock
// of 486 MHz and 60 frames per second.
const CyclesPerFrame = 8_100_000

// Register offsets within the VI window (base 0x0C002000).
const (
	regVITV      = 0x00 // vertical timing: ACV bits 0-9, EQ bits 10-14
	regVIDCR     = 0x02 // display control: ENB 0, RST 1, NIN 2, FMT bits 8-9
	regVIHTR0    = 0x04 // horizontal timing 0 (32-bit, stored)
	regVIHTR1    = 0x08 // horizontal timing 1 (32-bit, stored)
	regVIVTO     = 0x0C // odd field vertical timing: PSB bits 0-9, PRB bits 10-15
	regVIVTE     = 0x0E // even field vertical timing, same layout
	regVICURR    = 0x10 // current halfline (read-only, computed)
	regVIDI0     = 0x14 // display interrupt 0 (32-bit)
	regVIDI1     = 0x18 // display interrupt 1 (32-bit)
	regVIDI2     = 0x1C // display interrupt 2 (32-bit)
	regVIDI3     = 0x20 // display interrupt 3 (32-bit)
	regVIDIL0    = 0x24 // display interrupt location 0 (32-bit, stored)
	regVIDIL1    = 0x28 // display interrupt location 1 (32-bit, stored)
	regVIPICCONF = 0x2C // picture configuration (32-bit, stored)
	regVIHSR     = 0x30 // horizontal scaling (stored)
	regFilter0   = 0x34 // first of 12 filter coefficient words, through 0x4A
	regVITFBL    = 0x4C // top field frame buffer left (32-bit, stored)
	regVITFBR    = 0x50 // top field frame buffer right (32-bit, stored)
	regVIBFBL    = 0x54 // bottom field frame buffer left (32-bit, stored)
	regVIBFBR    = 0x58 // bottom field frame buffer right (32-bit, stored)
	regEnd       = 0x5C // one past the last register byte
)

// Display interrupt register bit fields (32-bit view).
const (
	dilTargetMask = 0x7FF          // bits 0-10: target line, in halflines
	dilDIS        = 1 << 16        // status: set by hardware when the interrupt fires
	dilDIE        = 1 << 28        // enable
	dilDISLaneBit = 1 << 0         // DIS within the high 16-bit lane
	dilDIELaneBit = 1 << (28 - 16) // DIE within the high 16-bit lane
)

// VI is the video interface state.
type VI struct {
	regs [regEnd / 2]uint16 // 16-bit lanes, offset/2 indexed

	totalCycles int64 // cycles accumulated by Advance, never reset except by Reset
}

// New returns a VI in its reset state.
func New() *VI {
	v := &VI{}
	v.Reset()
	return v
}

// Reset restores the documented 480i NTSC-like defaults:
// VITV with EQ 6 and ACV 240, VIDCR with ENB set and
// interlaced output (NIN clear), and both field vertical
// timing registers with PRB 15 and PSB 3. Every other
// register and the cycle accumulator are zeroed.
func (v *VI) Reset() {
	*v = VI{}
	v.regs[regVITV/2] = (6 << 10) | 240
	v.regs[regVIDCR/2] = 1 // ENB
	v.regs[regVIVTO/2] = (15 << 10) | 3
	v.regs[regVIVTE/2] = (15 << 10) | 3
}

// Read16 reads one 16-bit register lane at off. The
// VICURR lane returns the computed current halfline and
// offsets outside the register window read as zero.
func (v *VI) Read16(off uint32) uint16 {
	off &^= 1
	if off >= regEnd {
		return 0
	}
	if off == regVICURR {
		return uint16(v.CurrentHalfline())
	}
	return v.regs[off/2]
}

// Write16 writes one 16-bit register lane at off. Writes
// to VICURR are ignored, as are offsets outside the
// register window. For the display interrupt registers,
// the high lane carries the DIS status bit: writing that
// lane with the DIS bit clear clears a pending status,
// and writing it set leaves the status unchanged (only
// hardware sets DIS).
func (v *VI) Write16(off uint32, val uint16) {
	off &^= 1
	if off >= regEnd || off == regVICURR {
		return
	}
	if isVIDIHighLane(off) {
		old := v.regs[off/2]
		dis := old & dilDISLaneBit
		if val&dilDISLaneBit == 0 {
			dis = 0
		}
		v.regs[off/2] = (val &^ dilDISLaneBit) | dis
		return
	}
	v.regs[off/2] = val
}

// isVIDIHighLane reports whether off is the high lane of
// one of the four display interrupt registers.
func isVIDIHighLane(off uint32) bool {
	switch off {
	case regVIDI0, regVIDI1, regVIDI2, regVIDI3:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// reg32 reads a 32-bit register from its two lanes.
func (v *VI) reg32(off uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(v.regs[off/2])<<16 | uint32(v.regs[off/2+1])
}

// fieldsPerFrame returns 1 for non-interlaced output
// (VIDCR NIN set) and 2 otherwise.
func (v *VI) fieldsPerFrame() int {
	if v.regs[regVIDCR/2]&(1<<2) != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 2
}

// linesPerField returns ACV + PRB + PSB, with PRB and PSB
// taken from the even-field register VIVTE (see the
// package timing model).
func (v *VI) linesPerField() int {
	acv := int(v.regs[regVITV/2] & 0x3FF)
	vte := v.regs[regVIVTE/2]
	psb := int(vte & 0x3FF)
	prb := int((vte >> 10) & 0x3F)
	return acv + prb + psb
}

// totalHalflines returns the halflines in one frame:
// 2 * linesPerField * fieldsPerFrame.
func (v *VI) totalHalflines() int {
	return 2 * v.linesPerField() * v.fieldsPerFrame()
}

// CurrentHalfline returns the current halfline position
// within the frame, in 0..totalHalflines-1.
func (v *VI) CurrentHalfline() int {
	total := v.totalHalflines()
	if total <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	into := v.totalCycles % CyclesPerFrame
	return int(into * int64(total) / CyclesPerFrame)
}

// Advance accumulates cpuCycles and fires any enabled
// display interrupt whose target halfline the counter
// crossed during the advance, including across the frame
// wrap. An advance of a full frame or more crosses every
// target. Firing sets the register DIS bit.
func (v *VI) Advance(cpuCycles int) {
	if cpuCycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	prev := v.CurrentHalfline()
	v.totalCycles += int64(cpuCycles)
	cur := v.CurrentHalfline()
	fullFrame := cpuCycles >= CyclesPerFrame
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		off := uint32(regVIDI0 + 4*i)
		r := v.reg32(off)
		if r&dilDIE == 0 || r&dilDIS != 0 {
			continue
		}
		target := int(r & dilTargetMask)
		crossed := false
		switch {
		case fullFrame:
			crossed = true
		case cur >= prev:
			crossed = prev < target && target <= cur
		default: // wrapped at the frame boundary
			crossed = target > prev || target <= cur
		}
		if crossed {
			v.regs[off/2] |= dilDISLaneBit
		}
	}
}

// Pending reports whether any display interrupt register
// has both its status (DIS) and enable (DIE) bits set.
func (v *VI) Pending() bool {
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		r := v.reg32(uint32(regVIDI0 + 4*i))
		if r&dilDIS != 0 && r&dilDIE != 0 {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size: a version
// byte, the register lanes, and the cycle accumulator.
const SerializeSize = 1 + regEnd + 8

const serializeVersion = 1

// ErrBadState reports a state block of the wrong size or
// version.
var ErrBadState = errors.New("vi: bad save state")

// Serialize writes the complete VI state.
func (v *VI) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	off := 1
	for _, lane := range v.regs {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[off:], lane)
		off += 2
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[off:], uint64(v.totalCycles))
	off += 8
	if off != SerializeSize {
		panic("vi: serialize size mismatch")
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (v *VI) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != SerializeSize || in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return ErrBadState
	}
	off := 1
	for i := range v.regs {
		v.regs[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(in[off:])
		off += 2
	}
	v.totalCycles = int64(binary.BigEndian.Uint64(in[off:]))
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gamecube/vi/vi_test.go ====================

package vi

import "testing"

// read32 assembles a 32-bit register from its two lanes,
// high lane at the lower offset.
func read32(v *VI, off uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(v.Read16(off))<<16 | uint32(v.Read16(off+2))
}

// write32 stores a 32-bit register as two lanes. For the
// display interrupt registers the caller keeps the DIS
// bit (bit 16) explicit in val, following the lane rules
// in Write16.
func write32(v *VI, off uint32, val uint32) {
	v.Write16(off, uint16(val>>16))
	v.Write16(off+2, uint16(val))
}

// programDI0 sets display interrupt 0 to target with the
// enable bit set and the status bit clear.
func programDI0(v *VI, target uint32) {
	write32(v, regVIDI0, dilDIE|(target&dilTargetMask))
}

// clearDI0 clears the DIS status of interrupt 0 by
// writing its high lane with bit 16 clear, enable kept.
func clearDI0(v *VI) {
	v.Write16(regVIDI0, dilDIELaneBit)
}

func TestResetDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	if got := v.Read16(regVITV); got != (6<<10)|240 {
		t.Errorf("VITV = %#04x, want %#04x", got, (6<<10)|240)
	}
	if got := v.Read16(regVIDCR); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("VIDCR = %#04x, want 0001 (ENB, interlaced)", got)
	}
	for _, off := range []uint32{regVIVTO, regVIVTE} {
		if got := v.Read16(off); got != (15<<10)|3 {
			t.Errorf("reg %#02x = %#04x, want %#04x", off, got, (15<<10)|3)
		}
	}
	for _, off := range []uint32{regVIHTR0, regVIHTR1, regVIDI0, regVIDIL0, regVIPICCONF, regVITFBL} {
		if got := read32(v, off); got != 0 {
			t.Errorf("reg %#02x = %#08x, want 0 after reset", off, got)
		}
	}
	if got := v.Read16(regVIHSR); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("VIHSR = %#04x, want 0 after reset", got)
	}
	if v.Pending() {
		t.Error("Pending after reset, want false")
	}
	if got := v.CurrentHalfline(); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("CurrentHalfline after reset = %d, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestStoredRegisters(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	// 32-bit stored registers round trip lane by lane.
	write32(v, regVIHTR0, 0xABCD1234)
	write32(v, regVIHTR1, 0x0BADF00D)
	write32(v, regVIDIL0, 0x11112222)
	write32(v, regVIDIL1, 0x33334444)
	write32(v, regVIPICCONF, 0x55556666)
	write32(v, regVITFBL, 0x80000000)
	write32(v, regVITFBR, 0x80001000)
	write32(v, regVIBFBL, 0x80002000)
	write32(v, regVIBFBR, 0x80003000)
	for off, want := range map[uint32]uint32{
		regVIHTR0: 0xABCD1234, regVIHTR1: 0x0BADF00D,
		regVIDIL0: 0x11112222, regVIDIL1: 0x33334444,
		regVIPICCONF: 0x55556666, regVITFBL: 0x80000000,
		regVITFBR: 0x80001000, regVIBFBL: 0x80002000,
		regVIBFBR: 0x80003000,
	} {
		if got := read32(v, off); got != want {
			t.Errorf("reg %#02x = %#08x, want %#08x", off, got, want)
		}
	}
	// 16-bit stored registers: HSR and all 12 filter
	// coefficient words at 0x34 through 0x4A.
	v.Write16(regVIHSR, 0xBEEF)
	if got := v.Read16(regVIHSR); got != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("VIHSR = %#04x, want beef", got)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 12; i++ {
		off := uint32(regFilter0 + 2*i)
		v.Write16(off, uint16(0x1000+i))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 12; i++ {
		off := uint32(regFilter0 + 2*i)
		if got := v.Read16(off); got != uint16(0x1000+i) {
			t.Errorf("filter word %d at %#02x = %#04x, want %#04x", i, off, got, 0x1000+i)
		}
	}
	// VIDCR fields are stored, including FMT.
	v.Write16(regVIDCR, 1|(1<<2)|(2<<8))
	if got := v.Read16(regVIDCR); got != 1|(1<<2)|(2<<8) {
		t.Errorf("VIDCR = %#04x, want %#04x", got, 1|(1<<2)|(2<<8))
	}
	// Out of window offsets read zero and ignore writes.
	v.Write16(0x80, 0xFFFF)
	if got := v.Read16(0x80); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("out of window read = %#04x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestDisplayInterruptFiresAndClears(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	programDI0(v, 4)
	if v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("Pending before any advance, want false")
	}
	// Half a frame is well past halfline 4.
	v.Advance(CyclesPerFrame / 2)
	if !v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("Pending after crossing target, want true")
	}
	if got := read32(v, regVIDI0); got&dilDIS == 0 {
		t.Errorf("VIDI0 = %#08x, want DIS (bit 16) set", got)
	}
	// Writing the register with bit 16 set leaves DIS set.
	v.Write16(regVIDI0, dilDIELaneBit|dilDISLaneBit)
	if !v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("write with bit 16 set cleared DIS, want it left set")
	}
	// Writing with bit 16 clear clears DIS; DIE survives.
	clearDI0(v)
	if v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("Pending after clear write, want false")
	}
	if got := read32(v, regVIDI0); got&dilDIE == 0 || got&dilDIS != 0 {
		t.Errorf("VIDI0 = %#08x, want DIE set and DIS clear", got)
	}
	// Advance to just before the target point of the next
	// frame: finish this frame, then step to halfline 2.
	v.Advance(CyclesPerFrame / 2) // exactly the frame boundary
	v.Advance(20000)              // halfline 2 of the new frame
	if v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("Pending just before target next frame, want false")
	}
	// Cross the target again: the interrupt fires again.
	v.Advance(20000) // halfline 5
	if !v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("Pending after crossing target next frame, want true")
	}
}

func TestDisplayInterruptDisabledNeverFires(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	write32(v, regVIDI1, 4) // target set, DIE clear
	v.Advance(CyclesPerFrame)
	if v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("Pending with DIE clear, want false")
	}
	if got := read32(v, regVIDI1); got&dilDIS != 0 {
		t.Errorf("VIDI1 = %#08x, want DIS clear when DIE is clear", got)
	}
}

func TestDisplayInterruptOncePerFrame(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	programDI0(v, 4)
	fires := 0
	for frame := 0; frame < 3; frame++ {
		v.Advance(CyclesPerFrame)
		if v.Pending() {
			fires++
			clearDI0(v)
		}
	}
	if fires != 3 {
		t.Errorf("firings over 3 frames = %d, want 3", fires)
	}
}

func TestCurrentHalflineMonotonicAndWraps(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	prev := v.CurrentHalfline()
	if prev != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("initial halfline = %d, want 0", prev)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		v.Advance(1_000_000)
		cur := v.CurrentHalfline()
		if cur < prev {
			t.Fatalf("halfline went backwards inside a frame: %d then %d", prev, cur)
		}
		prev = cur
	}
	if prev == 0 {
		t.Fatal("halfline never advanced inside the frame")
	}
	// One more step crosses the frame boundary (8,000,000
	// plus 200,000 cycles total) and the counter wraps.
	v.Advance(200_000)
	if got := v.CurrentHalfline(); got >= prev {
		t.Errorf("halfline after wrap = %d, want less than %d", got, prev)
	}
	// VICURR reads the same value and ignores writes.
	if got := v.Read16(regVICURR); int(got) != v.CurrentHalfline() {
		t.Errorf("VICURR = %d, want %d", got, v.CurrentHalfline())
	}
	before := v.CurrentHalfline()
	v.Write16(regVICURR, 999)
	if got := v.CurrentHalfline(); got != before {
		t.Errorf("halfline after VICURR write = %d, want %d", got, before)
	}
}

func TestNonInterlacedTiming(t *testing.T) {
	interlaced := New()
	interlaced.Advance(CyclesPerFrame / 2)
	// Defaults: 258 lines per field, 2 fields, so 1032
	// halflines per frame and half a frame is halfline 516.
	if got := interlaced.CurrentHalfline(); got != 516 {
		t.Errorf("interlaced half frame halfline = %d, want 516", got)
	}
	progressive := New()
	progressive.Write16(regVIDCR, 1|(1<<2)) // ENB + NIN
	progressive.Advance(CyclesPerFrame / 2)
	// NIN: 1 field per frame, 516 halflines per frame, so
	// half a frame is halfline 258.
	if got := progressive.CurrentHalfline(); got != 258 {
		t.Errorf("non-interlaced half frame halfline = %d, want 258", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	write32(v, regVIHTR0, 0xABCD1234)
	v.Write16(regFilter0, 0x777)
	programDI0(v, 4)
	v.Advance(1_234_567)
	state := v.Serialize()
	if len(state) != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize size = %d, want %d", len(state), SerializeSize)
	}
	v2 := New()
	if err := v2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for off := uint32(0); off < regEnd; off += 2 {
		if got, want := v2.Read16(off), v.Read16(off); got != want {
			t.Errorf("reg %#02x after restore = %#04x, want %#04x", off, got, want)
		}
	}
	if got, want := v2.CurrentHalfline(), v.CurrentHalfline(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("halfline after restore = %d, want %d (cycle count not preserved)", got, want)
	}
	if v2.Pending() != v.Pending() {
		t.Errorf("Pending after restore = %v, want %v", v2.Pending(), v.Pending())
	}
	// Both copies keep advancing in lockstep.
	v.Advance(100_000)
	v2.Advance(100_000)
	if got, want := v2.CurrentHalfline(), v.CurrentHalfline(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("halfline after post-restore advance = %d, want %d", got, want)
	}
	if err := v2.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err != ErrBadState {
		t.Fatalf("short state error = %v, want ErrBadState", err)
	}
	bad := append([]byte(nil), state...)
	bad[0] = 99
	if err := v2.Deserialize(bad); err != ErrBadState {
		t.Fatalf("bad version error = %v, want ErrBadState", err)
	}
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/README.md ====================

# go-gba

A from-scratch Game Boy Advance core in Go for iTaK Gaming,
built the same way as the go-genesis, go-gameboy, go-nes and
go-snes cores in this repository: every chip is our own code,
written from published hardware documentation (GBATEK and the
ARM7TDMI technical reference manual), proven against public
conformance corpora kept as local evidence only, and wrapped
in a libretro-compatible shell for the app when it is ready.
No third-party Go dependencies.

## Status

**The GBA core is complete (GBA-1 through GBA-4). On top
of the CPU, bus, PPU, peripherals, BIOS and sound of the
first three slices, GBA-4 adds the cartridge save
devices (battery SRAM, the 64 KB and 128 KB flash parts
with their full command protocol, and the serial
EEPROMs), the libretro shell, and the real-game gate:
Anguna, a complete open-source homebrew GBA game, boots,
plays through its title, menus and first animated scene
for 3,600 gated frames, and a state saved mid-flow
restores with a byte-identical 120 frame continuation.
The core passed the shared engine harness end to end
except the audio line, which the harness marks silent
because this game itself makes no sound in the tested
stretch (traced exhaustively; see the honesty notes).
The app swap off mGBA is prepared (build 53 bindings)
and ships once the parent verifies, per the project
rule.**

- `cart`: the GBA cartridge header, parsed exactly as GBATEK
  lays it out. Minimum size check, the fixed byte at 0xB2
  (must be 0x96), title at 0xA0 (12 bytes, trailing zeros and
  spaces trimmed), game code at 0xAC, maker code at 0xB0,
  version at 0xBC, the header checksum at 0xBD verified as
  `-(0x19 + sum of bytes 0xA0..0xBC)` and reported as a flag
  (a bad checksum does not refuse the image), the entry word
  at 0x00, ROMSize as the smallest power of two that holds the
  image capped at 32 MB, and the save type found by scanning
  the image for the ASCII signatures games embed (SRAM_V,
  FLASH_V, FLASH512_V, FLASH1M_V, EEPROM_V, each reported
  with its version digits; the longer FLASH512_V and
  FLASH1M_V signatures are checked before the FLASH_V stem
  they share). The 156 byte logo bitmap at 0x04 is never
  embedded or checked: it is Nintendo data, not ours.
- `bus`: the full GBATEK memory map. BIOS (16 KB window,
  backed by a writable 16 KB store that the bios package
  installs its own code into), EWRAM (256 KB, mirrored over
  its 16 MB slot), IWRAM (32 KB, mirrored), IO (a plain 1 KB
  register store plus optional IORead and IOWrite hooks: when
  a hook claims an access it serves it, and whatever it does
  not claim falls back to the plain store, which is how
  WAITCNT and the other behaviorless registers still work),
  palette RAM (1 KB, mirrored), VRAM (96 KB in the 128 KB
  window: offsets 0x18000 and up fold back onto
  0x10000..0x17FFF, the documented mirror), OAM (1 KB,
  mirrored), the three GamePak ROM windows at 0x08, 0x0A and
  0x0C with mirroring of undersized images, and GamePak SRAM
  (64 KB store behind a byte wide window: wide reads
  replicate the addressed byte across all lanes, wide writes
  store only the low byte; the system narrows the window
  index to 32 KB for battery SRAM cartridges, so the upper
  half mirrors the lower). GBA-4 added SaveRead and
  SaveWrite bus hooks, consulted before the SRAM fast path
  and the backing stores, which let the save devices claim
  their windows (see `save`).
  Unmapped reads return the open bus value and unmapped
  writes are ignored. The bus returns raw aligned units with
  no rotation: Read(addr, 4) is the aligned word at addr&^3,
  Read(addr, 2) is the aligned halfword at addr&^1 zero
  extended, and Read(addr, 1) is the byte at addr; writes
  force the address to the access alignment (SRAM writes
  excepted, low byte only). The GBATEK misaligned load
  rotation lives in the CPU, which is also what the
  conformance corpus expects, since its recorded bus
  transactions carry the raw units. Backing stores are
  exported for serialization and tools.
- `save`: the cartridge save devices with a bus protocol,
  driven by the `cart` save-type detection and installed
  behind the bus save hooks. Flash (64 KB, and 128 KB in
  two switchable banks) implements the documented command
  protocol end to end: the unlock pair (0xAA to 0x5555,
  0x55 to 0x2AAA), ID mode (0x90) returning the chosen
  documented part IDs (Macronix 0xC2/0x1C for the 64 KB
  parts, Sanyo LE26FV10N1TS 0x62/0x13 for the 128 KB
  part), exit (0xF0), byte program (0xA0) with AND-only
  cell semantics (a program can only clear bits), erase
  setup (0x80) with 4 KB sector erase (0x30) and chip
  erase (0x10), and bank switch (0xB0) on the 128 KB part;
  programming and erasing complete at the triggering
  write, so the documented data-polling reads see the
  final byte at once (stated simplification). EEPROM
  (512 byte and 8 KB) implements the serial protocol on
  the 0x0D window, one bit per bus access: read requests
  (start, 1, address, stop, then 4 dummy bits and 64 data
  bits, most significant first) and write requests
  (start, 0, address, 64 data bits, stop; the block
  commits at the stop bit and the ready poll reads 1
  immediately, the programming interval collapsed and
  stated). The cartridge signature does not name the
  EEPROM size, so the device learns it from the first
  transfer's address width (6 or 14 bits); the window
  follows the documented ROM-size rule (the whole 0x0D
  window for ROMs up to 16 MB, only offsets
  0xFFFF00..0xFFFFFF above that). Battery SRAM stays in
  the bus store, narrowed to its 32 KB by the system.
  Gates: package-level protocol tests (IDs, AND program,
  sector and chip erase, bank 1, EEPROM write-then-read
  at nonzero addresses for both sizes, the window rule)
  plus system-level gates behind synthetic SRAM_V,
  FLASH_V, FLASH512_V, FLASH1M_V and EEPROM_V headers.
- `gpu`: the PPU at scanline granularity. All register
  behavior for DISPCNT, DISPSTAT, VCOUNT, the four BG
  control and scroll registers, the affine reference points
  and parameters, windows, blending (BLDCNT, BLDALPHA,
  BLDY) and MOSAIC, including the documented read and write
  quirks (scroll registers read as zero, VCOUNT writes are
  ignored, affine reference writes take effect at once).
  Rendering covers text backgrounds in modes 0, 1 and 2
  (4bpp and 8bpp, all screen sizes with wrapping, palette
  banks), affine backgrounds in modes 1 and 2 (8bpp, the
  internal reference point accumulates the per-line dx and
  dy terms across the frame exactly as documented), the
  bitmap modes 3, 4 and 5 with page selection from DISPCNT
  bit 4, and all 128 OBJ entries (every shape and size,
  1D and 2D character mapping, affine sprites with the 32
  parameter sets and the double-size flag, semi-transparent
  flag into the blender, OBJ window, mosaic). Composition
  follows the documented priority rules (lower priority
  number wins, sprites win ties against backgrounds of the
  same priority, earlier OAM entries win sprite ties), then
  windows (WIN0, WIN1, WINOBJ with WININ and WINOUT masks),
  then color effects (alpha blending with the documented
  clamp when the coefficients sum past 16, brightness up
  and down, all against the backdrop as the bottom layer).
  Output is the 240x160 XRGB8888 framebuffer. Hand-derived
  probes pin exact pixels for text tiles in both depths,
  palette banks, priority, affine identity and half-scale
  sampling, mode 3 and mode 4 pixels, the blend clamp,
  brightness extremes, window clipping, mosaic block size,
  and semi-transparent sprite blending.
- `apu`: the complete sound unit. The four PSG channels
  follow GBATEK's GBA sound section and share their
  design with the Game Boy APU in this repository's
  go-gameboy core (the same documented design, and its
  Blargg-proven behaviors are ported: envelope timing in
  1/64 s steps, the sweep unit with its double
  calculation overflow check, the length counters with
  the length-enable edge quirk and the trigger reload
  quirk). Channel 1 is a square wave with sweep, channel
  2 a plain square (duty cycles 12.5, 25, 50 and 75
  percent; frequency 131072/(2048-n) Hz), channel 3 plays
  32 4-bit digits from one of two 16-byte wave RAM banks
  (the bank bit selects the playing bank, CPU accesses at
  0x04000090 hit the other bank; the dimension bit plays
  both banks as 64 digits; volume codes 100, 50 and 25
  percent plus the force-75 percent bit), and channel 4
  is noise from the documented polynomial counter (a
  Galois-form LFSR, 15-bit and 7-bit widths, seeded
  0x4000 or 0x40 at (re)start, clocked at 524288/r/2^(s+1)
  Hz). The two Direct Sound channels hold signed 8-bit
  samples from 32-byte FIFOs, popped once per overflow of
  the timer each channel selects in SOUNDCNT_H and held
  between overflows; when a pop leaves a FIFO at or below
  16 bytes the unit requests a refill, and the system
  answers with one 4-word FIFO DMA burst (DMA1 feeds
  FIFO A, DMA2 feeds FIFO B), the documented half-empty
  rule. Mixing follows the documented output model: each
  PSG channel spans one quarter of the output range and
  each FIFO the full range in a 10-bit domain, the sums
  are scaled by the SOUNDCNT_L side volumes and enables
  and the SOUNDCNT_H PSG ratio (25, 50 or 100 percent),
  the SOUNDBIAS value is added, the result is clipped to
  the 10-bit range, and the stream is emitted as int16
  stereo at the rate the SOUNDBIAS resolution bits
  select (32768, 65536, 131072 or 262144 Hz), box
  filtered from the per-cycle mix by an exact cycle
  accumulator. The frame sequencer (512 Hz: length,
  sweep and envelope clocks) derives from the 16.78 MHz
  machine clock exactly. SOUNDCNT_X bit 7 is the master
  enable: clearing it zeroes the PSG registers
  0x60-0x81, stops all channels and silences the output,
  while SOUNDCNT_H, SOUNDBIAS, wave RAM and the FIFO
  contents survive, exactly as documented. Gates are
  measured, not vibes: channel 1 playing A4 (frequency
  register 0x6D6, the documented value for 440 Hz) counts
  exactly 440 positive zero crossings in one second of
  output; a rising sweep steps 256 to 384, 576, 864, 1296
  and 1944 at the documented sweep clock cycles and shuts
  down on the overflow the double calculation predicts;
  an envelope from 15 at step 1 reaches volume 0 at
  exactly 15/64 s with the output amplitude falling from
  16384 peak-to-peak to a constant; a length-32 counter
  stops its channel at cycle 2064384 on the nose; the
  wave channel reproduces a loaded ramp digit for digit
  at one output sample per digit; the LFSR sequences
  match an independent implementation of the documented
  rule for both widths; and a save state taken
  mid-playback restores with the next 4096 output samples
  bit-identical.
- `periph`: the interrupt controller, timers, DMA and
  keypad, in one package because they share the register
  dispatch pattern. The interrupt controller holds IE, IF
  and IME at their documented offsets, implements the
  write-one-to-acknowledge IF semantics and the pending
  rule (an IRQ is deliverable when a source is enabled,
  latched and IME is set). The four timers have the
  documented prescalers (1, 64, 256, 1024), reload on
  overflow, cascade counting, and overflow IRQs; the
  internal divider survives save states so a restored
  timer stays in phase; GBA-3 added an overflow callback
