//   - While the CPU sits halted, no dispatcher has run
//     yet. A Halt wakes when any of the IF flag bits 0 to
//     13 is pending (IME and IE gating is the documented
//     simplification: Halt wakes on any pending flag) and
//     the IRQ itself is then taken on the next step, so
//     the user handler still runs before the waiting
//     code. An IntrWait can complete here only if its
//     check word bits are already present.
//   - An accepted interrupt wakes the halted CPU (see
//     arm7tdmi.Step) and the BIOS dispatcher records the
//     acknowledged flags in the check word, calls the
//     user handler, and returns to the wait's resume
//     address. If the awaited condition now holds, Poll
//     consumes it (for IntrWait, clearing its bits from
//     the check word) and the wait is over; the CPU is
//     already positioned at the resume address. If it
//     does not hold (the wake was an unrelated interrupt),
//     IntrWait halts again at the resume address, exactly
//     the BIOS IntrWait loop; a plain Halt needs no such
//     re-check because any accepted interrupt ends it.
//   - While the CPU is inside the IRQ dispatcher (IRQ
//     mode) Poll leaves everything alone: the dispatcher
//     is still deciding the wait's outcome.
func (h *Handler) Poll(c *arm7tdmi.CPU) {
	if !h.waiting {
		return
	}
	if c.CPSR&0x1F == arm7tdmi.ModeIRQ {
		return
	}
	switch h.kind {
	case waitHalt:
		if c.Halted {
			if h.mem.Read(0x04000202, 2)&0x3FFF != 0 {
				h.wake(c)
			}
			return
		}
		// The CPU woke to service an interrupt and its
		// handler has returned: the halt is over.
		h.finish()
	case waitIntr:
		word := h.mem.Read(CheckWordAddr, 4)
		if word&h.mask != 0 {
			h.mem.Write(CheckWordAddr, 4, word&^h.mask)
			if c.Halted {
				h.wake(c)
			} else {
				h.finish()
			}
			return
		}
		if !c.Halted && executingAddr(c) == h.ret {
			// An unrelated interrupt woke the CPU and its
			// dispatcher run did not set the awaited
			// bits: halt again at the resume address.
			c.Halted = true
		}
	}
}

// HandlerStateSize is the serialized size of the Handler
// wait state in bytes: a flags word (bit 0 waiting, bits 8
// to 15 the wait kind), the IntrWait mask, the return
// address, and one reserved word kept zero.
const HandlerStateSize = 16

// Serialize writes the wait state to dst, which must be at
// least HandlerStateSize bytes, and returns the byte count.
func (h *Handler) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	if len(dst) < HandlerStateSize {
		return 0
	}
	var flags uint32
	if h.waiting {
		flags |= 1
	}
	flags |= uint32(h.kind) << 8
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[0:], flags)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[4:], h.mask)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[8:], h.ret)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[12:], 0)
	return HandlerStateSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It
// reports false, leaving the Handler untouched, when src
// is too short.
func (h *Handler) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < HandlerStateSize {
		return false
	}
	flags := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[0:])
	h.waiting = flags&1 != 0
	h.kind = int((flags >> 8) & 0xFF)
	h.mask = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[4:])
	h.ret = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[8:])
	return true
}

// Small memory helpers used by the SWI routines.

func (h *Handler) rd8(addr uint32) uint32  { return h.mem.Read(addr, 1) }
func (h *Handler) rd16(addr uint32) uint32 { return h.mem.Read(addr, 2) }
func (h *Handler) rd32(addr uint32) uint32 { return h.mem.Read(addr, 4) }

func (h *Handler) wr8(addr uint32, v uint32)  { h.mem.Write(addr, 1, v) }
func (h *Handler) wr16(addr uint32, v uint32) { h.mem.Write(addr, 2, v) }
func (h *Handler) wr32(addr uint32, v uint32) { h.mem.Write(addr, 4, v) }


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/bios/bios_test.go ====================

package bios

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi"
)

// rig bundles a bus with the BIOS installed, a handler and
// a CPU whose pipeline is parked as if a SWI at swiAt is
// about to be answered by a direct Hook call.
type rig struct {
	b *bus.Bus
	h *Handler
	c *arm7tdmi.CPU
}

const swiAt = 0x08000100

func newRig(t *testing.T) *rig {
	t.Helper()
	b := bus.New()
	Install(b.BIOS[:])
	// A zero filled ROM gives Jump targets harmless words
	// (zero decodes to a condition failed AND) to refill
	// the pipeline with, and a home for hand built data.
	b.SetROM(make([]byte, 0x8000))
	h := New(b)
	c := arm7tdmi.New(b)
	c.SWIHook = h.Hook
	return &rig{b: b, h: h, c: c}
}

// callSWI invokes the hook directly with the CPU set up as
// if executing a SWI at swiAt in ARM state: R15 is the SWI
// address plus 8. It reports the hook result.
func (r *rig) callSWI(num uint32) (int, bool) {
	r.c.CPSR &^= arm7tdmi.BitT // ARM state
	r.c.R[15] = swiAt + 8
	return r.h.Hook(r.c, num)
}

// branchTarget decodes an ARM branch word at addr.
func branchTarget(addr, word uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	if word>>24 != 0xEA {
		return 0, false
	}
	off := int32(word<<8) >> 8
	return uint32(int32(addr+8) + off<<2), true
}

func TestInstallVectors(t *testing.T) {
	store := make([]byte, bus.BIOSSize)
	Install(store)
	cases := []struct {
		off  uint32
		want uint32
	}{
		{0x00, bootAddr},
		{0x18, dispatcherAddr},
		{0x08, returnStubAddr},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		word := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(store[tc.off:])
		got, ok := branchTarget(tc.off, word)
		if !ok || got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("vector %#x: word %#08x decodes to %#x (ok %v), want target %#x", tc.off, word, got, ok, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if w := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(store[returnStubAddr:]); w != returnStub {
		t.Errorf("return stub word %#08x, want %#08x", w, returnStub)
	}
}

func TestBootStubExecution(t *testing.T) {
	b := bus.New()
	Install(b.BIOS[:])
	// A sentinel in the check word proves the stub clears it.
	b.IWRAM[0x7FF8] = 0xFF
	b.IWRAM[0x7FF9] = 0xFF
	b.IWRAM[0x7FFA] = 0xFF
	b.IWRAM[0x7FFB] = 0xFF
	// Cartridge entry: an infinite branch to itself.
	rom := make([]byte, 0x200)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom, 0xEAFFFFFE)
	b.SetROM(rom)

	c := arm7tdmi.New(b)
	c.Reset()
	for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
	if got := c.R[15] - 8; got != 0x08000000 {
		t.Errorf("executing at %#x, want cartridge entry 0x08000000", got)
	}
	if c.Executing != 0xEAFFFFFE {
		t.Errorf("executing word %#08x, want the cartridge infinite branch", c.Executing)
	}
	if mode := c.Mode(); mode != arm7tdmi.ModeSYS {
		t.Errorf("mode %#x, want SYS (%#x)", mode, arm7tdmi.ModeSYS)
	}
	if c.R[13] != UserStackTop {
		t.Errorf("SYS stack pointer %#x, want %#x", c.R[13], UserStackTop)
	}
	if c.RIRQ[0] != IRQStackTop {
		t.Errorf("IRQ stack pointer %#x, want %#x", c.RIRQ[0], IRQStackTop)
	}
	if c.RSVC[0] != SVCStackTop {
		t.Errorf("SVC stack pointer %#x, want %#x", c.RSVC[0], SVCStackTop)
	}
	if v := b.Read(CheckWordAddr, 4); v != 0 {
		t.Errorf("check word %#x, want 0", v)
	}
	if c.CPSR&arm7tdmi.BitI != 0 {
		t.Error("IRQ should be enabled after boot (I bit clear)")
	}
	if c.CPSR&arm7tdmi.BitF == 0 {
		t.Error("FIQ should be masked after boot (F bit set)")
	}
}

// TestDispatcherExecution runs the installed dispatcher on
// the real CPU: IRQ mode, one pending vblank flag, and a
// user handler that is a bare BX LR stub in EWRAM.
func TestDispatcherExecution(t *testing.T) {
	b := bus.New()
	Install(b.BIOS[:])
	b.SetROM(make([]byte, 0x8000))

	// Handler stub in EWRAM: BX LR.
	b.Write(0x02000100, 4, 0xE12FFF1E)
	// Return target in the ROM window: branch to itself.
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b.ROM[0x200:], 0xEAFFFFFE)

	b.Write(0x04000200, 2, 1) // IE: vblank
	b.Write(0x04000202, 2, 1) // IF: vblank pending
	b.Write(HandlerPtrAddr, 4, 0x02000100)

	c := arm7tdmi.New(b)
	// Enter IRQ mode by hand for the test: the bank swap
	// helpers are private, so set the fields the dispatcher
	// actually touches (current SP and LR, the IRQ SPSR it
	// returns through) directly.
	c.CPSR = (c.CPSR &^ 0x1F) | arm7tdmi.ModeIRQ
	c.R[13] = IRQStackTop
	c.R[14] = 0x08000200 + 4 // SUBS PC, LR, #4 lands at 0x08000200
	c.SPSR[arm7tdmi.SPSRIRQ] = arm7tdmi.ModeSYS
	c.R[0] = 0xAABBCCDD // sentinel the dispatcher must preserve
	c.Jump(dispatcherAddr)
	for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
	if v := b.Read(CheckWordAddr, 4); v != 1 {
		t.Errorf("check word %#x, want 1 (vblank ORed in by the dispatcher)", v)
	}
	if got := c.R[15] - 8; got != 0x08000200 {
		t.Errorf("executing at %#x, want the return target 0x08000200", got)
	}
	if c.RIRQ[0] != IRQStackTop {
		t.Errorf("IRQ stack pointer after return %#x, want balanced %#x", c.RIRQ[0], IRQStackTop)
	}
	if c.R[0] != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Errorf("R0 %#x, want preserved sentinel 0xAABBCCDD", c.R[0])
	}
}

func TestDiv(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	cases := []struct {
		num, den    int32
		q, rem, abs int32
	}{
		{100, 7, 14, 2, 14},
		{-100, 7, -14, -2, 14},
		{100, -7, -14, 2, 14},
		{-100, -7, 14, -2, 14},
		{7, 0, 1, 7, 1}, // documented divide by zero behaviour
		{-7, 0, -1, -7, 1},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		r.c.R[0] = uint32(tc.num)
		r.c.R[1] = uint32(tc.den)
		if _, ok := r.callSWI(0x06); !ok {
			t.Fatalf("Div(%d, %d) not handled", tc.num, tc.den)
		}
		if int32(r.c.R[0]) != tc.q || int32(r.c.R[1]) != tc.rem || int32(r.c.R[3]) != tc.abs {
			t.Errorf("Div(%d, %d) = q %d r %d abs %d, want q %d r %d abs %d",
				tc.num, tc.den, int32(r.c.R[0]), int32(r.c.R[1]), int32(r.c.R[3]), tc.q, tc.rem, tc.abs)
		}
		// DivArm takes the inputs swapped and must agree.
		r.c.R[0] = uint32(tc.den)
		r.c.R[1] = uint32(tc.num)
		if _, ok := r.callSWI(0x07); !ok {
			t.Fatalf("DivArm(%d, %d) not handled", tc.den, tc.num)
		}
		if int32(r.c.R[0]) != tc.q || int32(r.c.R[1]) != tc.rem || int32(r.c.R[3]) != tc.abs {
			t.Errorf("DivArm swapped (%d, %d) = q %d r %d abs %d, want q %d r %d abs %d",
				tc.num, tc.den, int32(r.c.R[0]), int32(r.c.R[1]), int32(r.c.R[3]), tc.q, tc.rem, tc.abs)
		}
	}
}

func TestSqrt(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	cases := []struct{ in, want uint32 }{
		{0, 0}, {1, 1}, {2, 1}, {144, 12}, {0xFFFFFFFF, 65535}, {0xFFFE0001, 65535},

		if _, ok := r.callSWI(0x08); !ok {
			t.Fatalf("Sqrt(%#x) not handled", tc.in)
		}
		if r.c.R[0] != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("Sqrt(%#x) = %d, want %d", tc.in, r.c.R[0], tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestArcTan(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	// tan 0 -> angle 0; tan 1.0 (0x4000 in 1.14) -> one
	// eighth of a turn, 0x2000.
	r.c.R[0] = 0
	r.callSWI(0x09)
	if r.c.R[0] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ArcTan(0) = %#x, want 0", r.c.R[0])
	}
	r.c.R[0] = 0x4000
	r.callSWI(0x09)
	if r.c.R[0] != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("ArcTan(0x4000) = %#x, want 0x2000", r.c.R[0])
	}
	// ArcTan2: (x=1.0, y=0) -> 0; (x=0, y=1.0) -> a quarter
	// turn, 0x4000.
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1] = 0x4000, 0
	r.callSWI(0x0A)
	if r.c.R[0] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ArcTan2(1, 0) = %#x, want 0", r.c.R[0])
	}
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1] = 0, 0x4000
	r.callSWI(0x0A)
	if r.c.R[0] != 0x4000 {
		t.Errorf("ArcTan2(0, 1) = %#x, want 0x4000", r.c.R[0])
	}
}

func TestUnknownSWI(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	if _, ok := r.callSWI(0x77); ok {
		t.Error("unknown SWI 0x77 should be unhandled so the CPU takes the exception")
	}
	// The encoded ARM form (number in bits 16 to 23) must
	// decode to the same function.
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1] = 100, 7
	r.c.R[15] = swiAt + 8
	if _, ok := r.h.Hook(r.c, 0x06<<16); !ok {
		t.Fatal("encoded SWI 0x060000 not handled")
	}
	if r.c.R[0] != 14 {
		t.Errorf("encoded Div quotient %d, want 14", r.c.R[0])
	}
}

func TestSoftResetFlagZero(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	// Flag byte at 0x03007FFA is zero: restart goes through
	// the BIOS reset entry, so the pipeline refills at 0.
	r.callSWI(0x00)
	if r.c.R[15] != 8 {
		t.Errorf("R15 after SoftReset %#x, want 8 (refill at the reset vector plus 8)", r.c.R[15])
	}
	if r.c.Executing != binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(r.b.BIOS[0:]) {
		t.Error("executing word after SoftReset is not the reset vector branch")
	}
}

func TestSoftResetFlagSet(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	r.b.Write(0x03007FFA, 1, 1)              // restart flag
	r.b.Write(HandlerPtrAddr, 4, 0x08000401) // stored target, thumb bit set
	r.callSWI(0x00)
	// Target used with the low bit cleared: refill at
	// 0x08000400 in ARM state gives R15 = target + 8.
	if r.c.R[15] != 0x08000400+8 {
		t.Errorf("R15 after flagged SoftReset %#x, want %#x", r.c.R[15], 0x08000408)
	}
}

func TestRegisterRamReset(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	fill := func(addr uint32, size int) {
		for i := 0; i < size; i += 4 {
			r.b.Write(addr+uint32(i), 4, 0xAAAAAAAA)
		}
	}
	fill(0x02000000, 0x100) // EWRAM
	fill(0x03000000, 0x100) // IWRAM low
	fill(0x05000000, 0x100) // palette
	fill(0x06000000, 0x100) // VRAM
	fill(0x07000000, 0x100) // OAM
	// Sentinels in the preserved IWRAM system area.
	r.b.Write(0x03007F00, 4, 0x12345678)
	r.b.Write(0x03007FF8, 4, 0x9ABCDEF0)

	r.c.R[0] = 0x1F // bits 0 to 4: the five memory areas
	r.callSWI(0x01)
	for _, addr := range []uint32{0x02000000, 0x03000000, 0x05000000, 0x06000000, 0x07000000} {
		if v := r.b.Read(addr, 4); v != 0 {
			t.Errorf("region at %#x still %#08x, want cleared", addr, v)
		}
	}
	if v := r.b.Read(0x03007F00, 4); v != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("system area at 0x03007F00 = %#08x, want preserved sentinel", v)
	}
	if v := r.b.Read(0x03007FF8, 4); v != 0x9ABCDEF0 {
		t.Errorf("check word = %#08x, want preserved sentinel", v)
	}
}

func TestCpuSet(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000100)
	for i, v := range []uint16{0x1111, 0x2222, 0x3333} {
		r.b.Write(src+uint32(2*i), 2, uint32(v))
	}
	// 16 bit copy of 3 units.
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1], r.c.R[2] = src, dst, 3
	r.callSWI(0x0B)
	for i, want := range []uint32{0x1111, 0x2222, 0x3333} {
		if v := r.b.Read(dst+uint32(2*i), 2); v != want {
			t.Errorf("copied half %d = %#x, want %#x", i, v, want)
		}
	}
	// 32 bit fill of 4 units from one source word.
	r.b.Write(0x02000200, 4, 0xDEADBEEF)
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1] = 0x02000200, 0x02000300
	r.c.R[2] = 4 | (1 << 24) | (1 << 26)
	r.callSWI(0x0B)
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if v := r.b.Read(0x02000300+uint32(4*i), 4); v != 0xDEADBEEF {
			t.Errorf("filled word %d = %#08x, want 0xDEADBEEF", i, v)
		}
	}
}

func TestCpuFastSetRounding(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000400)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		r.b.Write(src+uint32(4*i), 4, 0x1000+uint32(i))
	}
	// Count 3 must round up to 8 units of 32 bits.
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1], r.c.R[2] = src, dst, 3
	r.callSWI(0x0C)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if v := r.b.Read(dst+uint32(4*i), 4); v != 0x1000+uint32(i) {
			t.Errorf("fast copied word %d = %#x, want %#x (count rounds to 8)", i, v, 0x1000+i)
		}
	}
}

// buildAffineSrc packs one BgAffineSet source entry using
// the documented 20 byte layout (see affine.go).
func buildAffineSrc(r *rig, at uint32, originX, originY int32, centerX, centerY, ratioX, ratioY int16, angle uint16) {
	r.b.Write(at+0, 4, uint32(originX))
	r.b.Write(at+4, 4, uint32(originY))
	r.b.Write(at+8, 2, uint32(centerX))
	r.b.Write(at+10, 2, uint32(centerY))
	r.b.Write(at+12, 2, uint32(ratioX))
	r.b.Write(at+14, 2, uint32(ratioY))
	r.b.Write(at+16, 2, uint32(angle))
}

func TestBgAffineSetIdentity(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000100)
	// Identity: angle 0, ratios 1.0 (0x100). By the
	// formulas: pa = pd = 0x100, pb = pc = 0, and
	// dx = originX - centerX, dy = originY - centerY
	// (the >>8 cancels the 0x100 scale exactly).
	buildAffineSrc(r, src, 0x1000, 0x2000, 10, 20, 0x100, 0x100, 0)
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1], r.c.R[2] = src, dst, 1
	r.callSWI(0x0E)
	checks := []struct {
		off  uint32
		size int
		want int32
	}{
		{0, 2, 0x100}, {2, 2, 0}, {4, 2, 0}, {6, 2, 0x100},
		{8, 4, 0x1000 - 10}, {12, 4, 0x2000 - 20},
	}
	for _, ch := range checks {
		got := r.b.Read(dst+ch.off, ch.size)
		if int32(got) != ch.want {
			if ch.size == 2 {
				if int32(int16(got)) == ch.want {
					continue
				}
			}
			t.Errorf("dest +%d = %#x, want %#x", ch.off, got, ch.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestBgAffineSetQuarterTurn(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000100)
	// Angle 0x4000 is a quarter turn: cos 0, sin 1. With
	// ratios 0x100: pa = 0, pb = -0x100, pc = 0x100,
	// pd = 0. Then
	// dx = originX - ((0*10 + -0x100*20) >> 8)
	//    = 0x1000 - (-20) = 0x1014
	// dy = originY - ((0x100*10 + 0*20) >> 8)
	//    = 0x2000 - 10 = 0x1FF6
	buildAffineSrc(r, src, 0x1000, 0x2000, 10, 20, 0x100, 0x100, 0x4000)
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1], r.c.R[2] = src, dst, 1
	r.callSWI(0x0E)
	if v := int16(r.b.Read(dst+0, 2)); v != 0 {
		t.Errorf("pa = %d, want 0", v)
	}
	if v := int16(r.b.Read(dst+2, 2)); v != -0x100 {
		t.Errorf("pb = %d, want -256", v)
	}
	if v := int16(r.b.Read(dst+4, 2)); v != 0x100 {
		t.Errorf("pc = %d, want 256", v)
	}
	if v := int16(r.b.Read(dst+6, 2)); v != 0 {
		t.Errorf("pd = %d, want 0", v)
	}
	if v := int32(r.b.Read(dst+8, 4)); v != 0x1014 {
		t.Errorf("dx = %#x, want 0x1014", v)
	}
	if v := int32(r.b.Read(dst+12, 4)); v != 0x1FF6 {
		t.Errorf("dy = %#x, want 0x1FF6", v)
	}
}

func TestBitUnpack(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst, params := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000100), uint32(0x02000200)
	// Source byte 0b11100100 holds four 2 bit units LSB
	// first: 0, 1, 2, 3. Widened to 8 bits with an offset
	// of 0x10 on nonzero units: 0, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13.
	r.b.Write(src, 1, 0xE4)
	r.b.Write(params+0, 2, 1)    // source length: 1 byte
	r.b.Write(params+2, 1, 2)    // source width 2
	r.b.Write(params+3, 1, 8)    // dest width 8
	r.b.Write(params+4, 4, 0x10) // offset, add-to-all flag clear
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1], r.c.R[2] = src, dst, params
	r.callSWI(0x10)
	for i, want := range []uint32{0, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13} {
		if v := r.b.Read(dst+uint32(i), 1); v != want {
			t.Errorf("unpacked byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, v, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestLZ77(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000100)
	// Payload "ABCABCABC" (9 bytes): three literals then
	// one back reference of length 6 at displacement 3.
	// Flag byte bits (MSB first): 0,0,0,1 then unused 0s
	// gives 0x10. Reference bytes: length 6 -> high
	// nibble 6-3 = 3; displacement 3 -> disp-1 = 2, so
	// b0 = 0x30, b1 = 0x02.
	r.b.Write(src, 4, 9<<8|0x10) // header
	stream := []byte{0x10, 'A', 'B', 'C', 0x30, 0x02}
	for i, v := range stream {
		r.b.Write(src+4+uint32(i), 1, uint32(v))
	}
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1] = src, dst
	r.callSWI(0x11)
	for i, want := range []byte("ABCABCABC") {
		if v := r.b.Read(dst+uint32(i), 1); v != uint32(want) {
			t.Errorf("byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, v, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestRLUnComp(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000100)
	// Payload "AAAAAXYZ" (8 bytes): a run of five 'A'
	// (flag 0x80 | (5-3) = 0x82, then the byte), then a
	// literal run of three (flag 3-1 = 0x02, then bytes).
	r.b.Write(src, 4, 8<<8|0x30)
	stream := []byte{0x82, 'A', 0x02, 'X', 'Y', 'Z'}
	for i, v := range stream {
		r.b.Write(src+4+uint32(i), 1, uint32(v))
	}
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1] = src, dst
	r.callSWI(0x14)
	for i, want := range []byte("AAAAAXYZ") {
		if v := r.b.Read(dst+uint32(i), 1); v != uint32(want) {
			t.Errorf("byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, v, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestDiff16(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)

	// Output [0x1000, 0x1005, 0x0FF0]: first halfword
	// literal, deltas +0x0005 and -0x15 (0xFFEB). Size is
	// 6 bytes (3 halfwords), header type byte 0x81.
	r.b.Write(src, 4, 6<<8|0x81)

	r.callSWI(0x18)
	for i, want := range []uint32{0x1000, 0x1005, 0x0FF0} {

			t.Errorf("halfword %d = %#x, want %#x", i, v, want)
		}

func TestHuffUnComp(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	src, dst := uint32(0x02000000), uint32(0x02000100)
	// Hand built tree and stream for the output "ABA"
	// with 8 bit symbols.
	//
	// Tree block (4 bytes, so the size byte N satisfies
	// (N+1)*2 = 4, N = 1):
	//   byte 0: 0x01, the size byte
	//   byte 1: 0xC0, the root node: offset 0, bit 6 set
	//           (left child is data), bit 7 set (right
	//           child is data). The child pair sits at
	//           (1 AND NOT 1) + 0*2 + 2 = 2, so the left
	//           child is byte 2 and the right is byte 3.
	//   byte 2: 'A' (the left symbol)
	//   byte 3: 'B' (the right symbol)
	// Stream bits walk 0 for A and 1 for B, MSB first in
	// a 32 bit word: A B A is bits 0, 1, 0 from the top,
	// the word 0x40000000.
	r.b.Write(src, 4, 3<<8|0x28) // header: type 0x20 | 8, size 3
	tree := []byte{0x01, 0xC0, 'A', 'B'}
	for i, v := range tree {
		r.b.Write(src+4+uint32(i), 1, uint32(v))
	}
	r.b.Write(src+8, 4, 0x40000000) // stream word
	r.c.R[0], r.c.R[1] = src, dst
	r.callSWI(0x13)
	for i, want := range []byte("ABA") {
		if v := r.b.Read(dst+uint32(i), 1); v != uint32(want) {
			t.Errorf("byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, v, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestHaltAndPoll(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	r.callSWI(0x02)
	if !r.c.Halted || !r.h.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("Halt should halt the CPU and mark the handler waiting")
	}
	// No IF flags: Poll must not wake.
	r.h.Poll(r.c)
	if !r.c.Halted {
		t.Fatal("Poll with no pending IF woke the CPU early")
	}
	r.b.Write(0x04000202, 2, 1) // IF: vblank
	r.h.Poll(r.c)
	if r.c.Halted || r.h.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("Poll with a pending IF should wake the CPU")
	}
	if want := uint32(swiAt + 4 + 8); r.c.R[15] != want {
		t.Errorf("R15 after wake %#x, want %#x (return address plus pipeline 8)", r.c.R[15], want)
	}
}

func TestIntrWaitImmediateReturn(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	// Check word already holds bit 2, plus an unrelated
	// bit 3 that must survive.
	r.b.Write(CheckWordAddr, 4, (1<<2)|(1<<3))
	r.c.R[0] = 0      // discard flag clear
	r.c.R[1] = 1 << 2 // mask
	r.callSWI(0x04)
	if r.c.Halted || r.h.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("IntrWait with a pending masked bit should return immediately")
	}
	if v := r.b.Read(CheckWordAddr, 4); v != 1<<3 {
		t.Errorf("check word %#x, want %#x (waited bit consumed, other bit kept)", v, 1<<3)
	}
}

func TestIntrWaitBlocking(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	r.b.Write(CheckWordAddr, 4, 0)
	r.c.R[0] = 1 // discard
	r.c.R[1] = 1 << 1
	r.callSWI(0x04)
	if !r.c.Halted || !r.h.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("IntrWait with a clear check word should block")
	}
	r.b.Write(CheckWordAddr, 4, 1<<1) // dispatcher sets the flag
	r.h.Poll(r.c)
	if r.c.Halted || r.h.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("Poll should wake the IntrWait once its bit lands")
	}
	if v := r.b.Read(CheckWordAddr, 4); v != 0 {
		t.Errorf("check word %#x, want 0 (bit consumed on wake)", v)
	}
	if want := uint32(swiAt + 4 + 8); r.c.R[15] != want {
		t.Errorf("R15 after wake %#x, want %#x", r.c.R[15], want)
	}
	// The wake refilled the pipeline at the return
	// address: the CPU is executing there now (checked via
	// R15 above), and one step advances it to the next
	// instruction, proving the return address executed.
	r.c.Step()
	if got := r.c.R[15] - 8; got != swiAt+4+4 {
		t.Errorf("after one step, executing at %#x, want %#x (one past the return address)", got, swiAt+8)
	}
}

func TestVBlankIntrWaitDiscardsStaleBit(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	// A stale vblank bit is already in the check word.
	// VBlankIntrWait discards it and waits for the next one.
	r.b.Write(CheckWordAddr, 4, 1)
	r.callSWI(0x05)
	if !r.c.Halted || !r.h.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("VBlankIntrWait should block even with a stale vblank bit present")
	}
	if v := r.b.Read(CheckWordAddr, 4); v != 0 {
		t.Errorf("check word %#x, want 0 (stale bit discarded)", v)
	}
	r.b.Write(CheckWordAddr, 4, 1) // the next vblank lands
	r.h.Poll(r.c)
	if r.c.Halted {
		t.Fatal("Poll should wake VBlankIntrWait on the next vblank bit")
	}
}

func TestHandlerSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig(t)
	r.c.R[0] = 1
	r.c.R[1] = 0x55
	r.callSWI(0x04) // blocks: waiting state is live
	buf := make([]byte, HandlerStateSize)
	if n := r.h.Serialize(buf); n != HandlerStateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d bytes, want %d", n, HandlerStateSize)
	}
	h2 := New(r.b)
	if !h2.Deserialize(buf) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize rejected a valid state")
	}
	if !h2.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("restored handler should still be waiting")
	}
	// The restored handler wakes on its mask like the original.
	r.b.Write(CheckWordAddr, 4, 0x55)
	h2.Poll(r.c)
	if r.c.Halted {
		t.Fatal("restored handler failed to wake the CPU")
	}
	if h2.Deserialize(make([]byte, 4)) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize should reject a short buffer")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/bios/swi.go ====================

package bios

import (
	"math"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi"
)

// softReset (SWI 0x00) restarts execution. The documented
// flag byte at 0x03007FFA selects the restart target: when
// it is zero, control goes back through the BIOS reset
// entry, which reruns the boot stub stack setup and enters
// the cartridge; when it is nonzero, control goes directly
// to the word stored at the handler pointer address with
// its low bit cleared.
//
// Choice made here, per the calling convention: in the
// zero flag case we Jump to the reset vector 0x00 so the
// boot stub re-establishes every stack exactly as at power
// on. In the flag case we Jump straight to the stored
// target, since the caller has already set up its own
// context there.
func (h *Handler) softReset(c *arm7tdmi.CPU) int {
	if h.rd8(0x03007FFA) != 0 {
		target := h.rd32(HandlerPtrAddr) &^ 1
		c.Jump(target)
		return 3
	}
	c.Jump(0x00)
	return 3
}

// clearRange zeroes the half open range [start, end) in
// word sized writes. Every range RegisterRamReset clears
// is word aligned with a word multiple length.
func (h *Handler) clearRange(start, end uint32) {
	for addr := start; addr < end; addr += 4 {
		h.wr32(addr, 0)
	}
}

// registerRamReset (SWI 0x01) clears the memory areas and
// IO ranges selected by the flag bits in R0. The top 0x200
// bytes of IWRAM hold the BIOS system area (stacks, the
// check word, the handler pointer) and are preserved.
func (h *Handler) registerRamReset(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32) int {
	flags := c.R[0]
	work := 0
	if flags&(1<<0) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x02000000, 0x02040000) // EWRAM
		work += 0x10000
	}
	if flags&(1<<1) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x03000000, 0x03007E00) // IWRAM below the system area
		work += 0x1F80
	}
	if flags&(1<<2) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x05000000, 0x05000400) // palette RAM
		work += 0x100
	}
	if flags&(1<<3) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x06000000, 0x06018000) // VRAM
		work += 0x6000
	}
	if flags&(1<<4) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x07000000, 0x07000400) // OAM
		work += 0x100
	}
	if flags&(1<<5) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x04000100, 0x04000160) // SIO IO range
		work += 0x18
	}
	if flags&(1<<6) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x04000060, 0x040000B0) // sound IO range
		work += 0x14
	}
	if flags&(1<<7) != 0 {
		h.clearRange(0x04000000, 0x04000400) // all IO registers
		work += 0x100
	}
	c.Jump(ret)
	return 3 + work
}

// intrWait (SWI 0x04, and SWI 0x05 in its fixed form)
// waits for one of the masked IRQ bits to appear in the
// BIOS check word. The dispatcher ORs acknowledged IRQ
// flags into the check word as interrupts fire.
//
// If discard is false and a masked bit is already present,
// those bits are consumed and the call returns at once.
// If discard is true, any masked bits already present are
// cleared first and the call always blocks. While blocked
// the CPU is halted; Poll performs the wake side.
func (h *Handler) intrWait(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, discard bool, mask, ret uint32) int {
	word := h.rd32(CheckWordAddr)
	if !discard && word&mask != 0 {
		h.wr32(CheckWordAddr, word&^mask)
		c.Jump(ret)
		return 3
	}
	if discard {
		h.wr32(CheckWordAddr, word&^mask)
	}
	h.enterWait(c, waitIntr, mask, ret)
	return 3
}

// div performs the shared Div and DivArm math: the
// quotient truncates toward zero, the remainder takes the
// sign of the numerator, and R3 receives the absolute
// value of the quotient. Division by zero follows the
// documented BIOS behaviour: the quotient is 1 when the
// numerator is nonnegative and -1 otherwise, the remainder
// is the numerator, and R3 is 1.
func (h *Handler) div(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, num, den int32, ret uint32) int {
	var q, r int64
	n64, d64 := int64(num), int64(den)
	if den == 0 {
		if num >= 0 {
			q = 1
		} else {
			q = -1
		}
		r = n64
	} else {
		// int64 arithmetic gives the overflow case (the
		// most negative value divided by -1) a well defined
		// quotient of 2^31, whose low 32 bits are the value
		// the hardware style result carries.
		q = n64 / d64
		r = n64 - q*d64
	}
	absq := q
	if absq < 0 {
		absq = -absq
	}
	c.R[0] = uint32(int32(q))
	c.R[1] = uint32(int32(r))
	c.R[3] = uint32(absq)
	c.Jump(ret)
	return 10
}

// isqrt returns floor(sqrt(v)) for an unsigned 32 bit v.
// The float64 estimate is corrected with 64 bit products
// so values near the top of the range (where the float
// root can round up to 65536) land exactly.
func isqrt(v uint32) uint32 {
	r := uint64(math.Sqrt(float64(v)))
	for (r+1)*(r+1) <= uint64(v) {
		r++
	}
	for r*r > uint64(v) {
		r--
	}
	return uint32(r)
}

// angleScale converts radians to the BIOS angle unit: an
// unsigned 16 bit value where 0x10000 is a full turn. The
// result is rounded to the nearest unit and wrapped into
// [0, 0x10000).
func angleScale(radians float64) uint32 {
	scaled := int64(math.Round(radians * (0x10000 / (2 * math.Pi))))
	m := scaled % 0x10000
	if m < 0 {
		m += 0x10000
	}
	return uint32(m)
}

// arcTan (SWI 0x09) takes a tangent in signed 1.14 fixed
// point and returns its angle. The input is a full s32 but
// arctan saturates smoothly, so no clamping is needed
// beyond the natural range of math.Atan.
func arcTan(tan32 int32) uint32 {
	return angleScale(math.Atan(float64(tan32) / 16384.0))
}

// arcTan2 (SWI 0x0A) takes x in R0 and y in R1, both
// signed 1.14 fixed point, and returns the angle of the
// vector (x, y). The fixed point scale cancels in the
// ratio but is applied anyway so the zero vector behaves
// exactly like math.Atan2(0, 0).
func arcTan2(x32, y32 int32) uint32 {
	x := float64(x32) / 16384.0
	y := float64(y32) / 16384.0
	return angleScale(math.Atan2(y, x))
}

// cpuSetWork performs a CpuSet style transfer: count
// units of unitSize bytes (2 or 4) from src to dst. In
// copy mode each unit is read once from the advancing
// source; in fill mode the first unit is read once and
// written to every destination unit.
func (h *Handler) cpuSetWork(src, dst, count uint32, unitSize int, fill bool) {
	if unitSize == 4 {
		if fill {
			v := h.rd32(src)
			for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++ {
				h.wr32(dst+4*i, v)
			}
			return
		}
		for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++ {
			h.wr32(dst+4*i, h.rd32(src+4*i))
		}
		return
	}
	if fill {
		v := h.rd16(src)
		for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++ {
			h.wr16(dst+2*i, v)
		}
		return
	}
	for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++ {
		h.wr16(dst+2*i, h.rd16(src+2*i))
	}
}

// cpuSet (SWI 0x0B): R2 control bits 0 to 20 are the unit
// count, bit 24 selects fill over copy, bit 26 selects
// 32 bit units over 16 bit units.
func (h *Handler) cpuSet(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32) int {
	control := c.R[2]
	count := control & 0x1FFFFF
	unitSize := 2
	if control&(1<<26) != 0 {
		unitSize = 4
	}
	h.cpuSetWork(c.R[0], c.R[1], count, unitSize, control&(1<<24) != 0)
	c.Jump(ret)
	return 3 + int(count)
}

// cpuFastSet (SWI 0x0C) has the same control layout but
// always moves 32 bit units, and the unit count is rounded
// up to a multiple of 8.
func (h *Handler) cpuFastSet(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32) int {
	control := c.R[2]
	count := (control&0x1FFFFF + 7) &^ 7
	h.cpuSetWork(c.R[0], c.R[1], count, 4, control&(1<<24) != 0)
	c.Jump(ret)
	return 3 + int(count)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/bios/unpack.go ====================

package bios

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi"
)

// The decompression SWIs share a header layout: a word at
// the source whose low byte is a type tag and whose upper
// 24 bits are the decompressed size in bytes.

// bitUnpack (SWI 0x10) widens (or narrows) a packed bit
// stream. The parameter block at R2 reads:
//
//	u16 source length in bytes
//	u8  source bit width (1, 2, 4 or 8)
//	u8  destination bit width (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32)
//	u32 offset word: bits 0 to 30 are an offset, bit 31
//	    is the add-offset-to-all-data flag
//
// Source units are consumed LSB first from the source bit
// stream. Each unit that is nonzero gains the offset; zero
// units stay zero unless bit 31 is set, in which case every
// unit gains it. Destination units are written at their
// width: word and halfword writes for 32 and 16, and for
// narrower widths the units pack into bytes LSB first.
func (h *Handler) bitUnpack(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32) int {
	src, dst, params := c.R[0], c.R[1], c.R[2]
	srcLen := int(h.rd16(params + 0))
	srcWidth := int(h.rd8(params + 2))
	dstWidth := int(h.rd8(params + 3))
	offsetWord := h.rd32(params + 4)
	offset := offsetWord & 0x7FFFFFFF
	addAll := offsetWord&(1<<31) != 0
	c.Jump(ret)
	if srcWidth == 0 || dstWidth == 0 {
		return 3
	}
	totalUnits := srcLen * 8 / srcWidth

	// Source bit reader: bitPos counts bits consumed from
	// the source, LSB first within each byte.
	bitPos := 0
	readUnit := func() uint32 {
		var v uint32
		for b := 0; b < srcWidth; b++ {
			byteVal := h.rd8(src + uint32(bitPos/8))
			bit := (byteVal >> uint(bitPos%8)) & 1
			v |= bit << uint(b)
			bitPos++
		}
		return v
	}

	// Destination accumulator for sub byte widths.
	dstAddr := dst
	var acc uint32
	accBits := 0
	flush := func() {
		if accBits > 0 {
			h.wr8(dstAddr, acc)
			dstAddr++
			acc, accBits = 0, 0
		}
	}
	dstMask := uint32(0xFFFFFFFF)
	if dstWidth < 32 {
		dstMask = (uint32(1) << uint(dstWidth)) - 1
	}
	for i := 0; i < totalUnits; i++ {
		v := readUnit()
		if v != 0 || addAll {
			v += offset
		}
		v &= dstMask
		switch {
		case dstWidth == 32:
			h.wr32(dstAddr, v)
			dstAddr += 4
		case dstWidth == 16:
			h.wr16(dstAddr, v)
			dstAddr += 2
		case dstWidth == 8:
			h.wr8(dstAddr, v)
			dstAddr++
		default:
			acc |= v << uint(accBits)
			accBits += dstWidth
			if accBits >= 8 {
				flush()
			}
		}
	}
	flush()
	return 3 + totalUnits
}

// lz77 (SWI 0x11 for WRAM destinations, 0x12 for VRAM)
// decompresses the GBA LZSS format: a header word (type
// 0x10, size in the upper 24 bits), then flag bytes whose
// bits are consumed from the most significant bit down.
// A 0 bit introduces a literal byte; a 1 bit introduces a
// two byte back reference: the length is the high nibble
// plus 3, and the displacement is the remaining 12 bits
// plus 1, counted back from the current destination. The
// copy runs byte by byte, so overlapping references repeat
// as expected. Both variants write byte by byte here: on
// hardware the VRAM variant stages through a buffer
// because VRAM ignores byte writes, and byte writes are
// the safe equivalent for this HLE.
func (h *Handler) lz77(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32) int {
	src, dst := c.R[0], c.R[1]
	header := h.rd32(src)
	size := int(header >> 8)
	srcPos := src + 4
	dstPos := dst
	produced := 0
	for produced < size {
		flags := h.rd8(srcPos)
		srcPos++
		for bit := 7; bit >= 0 && produced < size; bit-- {
			if flags&(1<<uint(bit)) == 0 {
				h.wr8(dstPos, h.rd8(srcPos))
				srcPos++
				dstPos++
				produced++
				continue
			}
			b0 := h.rd8(srcPos)
			b1 := h.rd8(srcPos + 1)
			srcPos += 2
			length := int(b0>>4) + 3
			disp := int(((b0&0x0F)<<8)|b1) + 1
			for k := 0; k < length && produced < size; k++ {
				v := h.rd8(dstPos - uint32(disp))
				h.wr8(dstPos, v)
				dstPos++
				produced++
			}
		}
	}
	c.Jump(ret)
	return 3 + size
}

// huffUnComp (SWI 0x13) decompresses Huffman coded data.
// The header low byte is 0x20 plus the data bit width
// (1, 2, 4 or 8) and the upper 24 bits are the
// decompressed size in bytes.
//
// After the header comes the tree block. Its first byte N
// says the block occupies (N+1)*2 bytes including that
// byte. The root node is the next byte. A node byte holds,
// in bits 0 to 5, an offset in 2 byte units to its pair of
// children, counted from the node's own position rounded
// down to even, plus one pair (the documented GBATEK
// formula adds 2 bytes, then 0 for the left child and 1
// for the right); bit 6 marks the left child as data and
// bit 7 marks the right child as data. A data child byte
// is the symbol value itself, not a node.
//
// The coded stream follows the tree as 32 bit words, bits
// consumed from the most significant bit down: 0 walks to
// the left child, 1 to the right child, until a data child
// yields one symbol. Symbols narrower than a byte pack
// into output bytes LSB first, wider ones are whole bytes.
func (h *Handler) huffUnComp(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32) int {
	src, dst := c.R[0], c.R[1]
	header := h.rd32(src)
	bitsPerSymbol := int(header & 0x0F)
	size := int(header >> 8)
	c.Jump(ret)
	if bitsPerSymbol == 0 || size == 0 {
		return 3
	}
	treeBase := src + 4
	treeBytes := int(h.rd8(treeBase)+1) * 2
	dataBase := treeBase + uint32(treeBytes)

	// Tree bytes are read relative to the block start; the
	// root node sits at relative offset 1, right after the
	// size byte.
	treeByte := func(rel int) uint32 {
		return h.rd8(treeBase + uint32(rel))
	}

	totalSymbols := size * 8 / bitsPerSymbol

	// Bit reader over the 32 bit stream words, MSB first.
	wordIndex := 0
	bitIndex := 32 // forces a load on first use
	var streamWord uint32
	readBit := func() uint32 {
		if bitIndex >= 32 {
			streamWord = h.rd32(dataBase + uint32(4*wordIndex))
			wordIndex++
			bitIndex = 0
		}
		bit := (streamWord >> uint(31-bitIndex)) & 1
		bitIndex++
		return bit
	}

	dstPos := dst
	var acc uint32
	accBits := 0
	emit := func(sym uint32) {
		if bitsPerSymbol == 8 {
			h.wr8(dstPos, sym)
			dstPos++
			return
		}
		acc |= (sym & ((uint32(1) << uint(bitsPerSymbol)) - 1)) << uint(accBits)
		accBits += bitsPerSymbol
		if accBits >= 8 {
			h.wr8(dstPos, acc)
			dstPos++
			acc, accBits = 0, 0
		}
	}

	for s := 0; s < totalSymbols; s++ {
		node := 1 // relative offset of the root node
		for {
			nodeByte := treeByte(node)
			offset := int(nodeByte & 0x3F)
			bit := readBit()
			// Child pair address, relative offsets: the
			// node's pair base, plus the offset in 2 byte
			// units, plus one pair, plus 0 or 1 for the
			// side.
			pairBase := node &^ 1
			child := pairBase + offset*2 + 2 + int(bit)
			isData := false
			if bit == 0 {
				isData = nodeByte&(1<<6) != 0
			} else {
				isData = nodeByte&(1<<7) != 0
			}
			if isData {
				emit(treeByte(child))
				break
			}
			node = child
		}
	}
	if accBits > 0 {
		h.wr8(dstPos, acc)
	}
	return 3 + totalSymbols
}

// rlUnComp (SWI 0x14 for WRAM, 0x15 for VRAM) decodes the
// run length format: after the header (type 0x30), each
// block starts with a flag byte. With bit 7 set, the low
// 7 bits plus 3 give a run length for copies of the next
// single byte; with bit 7 clear, the low 7 bits plus 1
// literal bytes follow. Both variants write byte by byte
// (see the LZ77 note for why that is the safe HLE form).
func (h *Handler) rlUnComp(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32) int {
	src, dst := c.R[0], c.R[1]
	header := h.rd32(src)
	size := int(header >> 8)
	srcPos := src + 4
	dstPos := dst
	produced := 0
	for produced < size {
		flag := h.rd8(srcPos)
		srcPos++
		if flag&0x80 != 0 {
			count := int(flag&0x7F) + 3
			v := h.rd8(srcPos)
			srcPos++
			for k := 0; k < count && produced < size; k++ {
				h.wr8(dstPos, v)
				dstPos++
				produced++
			}
			continue
		}
		count := int(flag&0x7F) + 1
		for k := 0; k < count && produced < size; k++ {
			h.wr8(dstPos, h.rd8(srcPos))
			srcPos++
			dstPos++
			produced++
		}
	}
	c.Jump(ret)
	return 3 + size
}

// diffUnFilter (SWI 0x16 and 0x17, 8 bit; SWI 0x18, 16
// bit) reverses difference filtering. The header type
// byte is 0x80 for the 8 bit form and 0x81 for the 16 bit
// form, with the size in bytes in the upper 24 bits as
// usual. The data starts with one literal unit; every
// following unit is a delta added to the previous output
// unit, wrapping at the unit width.
func (h *Handler) diffUnFilter(c *arm7tdmi.CPU, ret uint32, wide bool) int {
	src, dst := c.R[0], c.R[1]
	header := h.rd32(src)
	size := int(header >> 8)
	srcPos := src + 4
	dstPos := dst
	if wide {
		count := size / 2
		if count > 0 {
			prev := h.rd16(srcPos)
			srcPos += 2
			h.wr16(dstPos, prev)
			dstPos += 2
			for i := 1; i < count; i++ {
				prev = (prev + h.rd16(srcPos)) & 0xFFFF
				srcPos += 2
				h.wr16(dstPos, prev)
				dstPos += 2
			}
		}
		c.Jump(ret)
		return 3 + size
	}
	if size > 0 {
		prev := h.rd8(srcPos)
		srcPos++
		h.wr8(dstPos, prev)
		dstPos++
		for i := 1; i < size; i++ {
			prev = (prev + h.rd8(srcPos)) & 0xFF
			srcPos++
			h.wr8(dstPos, prev)
			dstPos++
		}
	}
	c.Jump(ret)
	return 3 + size
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/bus/bus.go ====================

// Package bus implements the Game Boy Advance memory map
// for GBA-1, written from the published GBATEK memory map.
//
// The map, by the top byte of the address:
//
//	0x00000000  BIOS, 16 KB window (read only; the backing
//	            store stays zero filled in this core, see
//	            the README honesty notes)
//	0x02000000  EWRAM, 256 KB, mirrored over its 16 MB slot
//	0x03000000  IWRAM, 32 KB, mirrored over its 16 MB slot
//	0x04000000  IO registers, 1 KB plain store in this slice
//	            (WAITCNT at 0x204 included; no register has
//	            behavior yet, and wait states are not timed)
//	0x05000000  Palette RAM, 1 KB, mirrored over its slot
//	0x06000000  VRAM, 96 KB, in a 128 KB window: the top
//	            32 KB of the window (offsets 0x18000 and up)
//	            mirrors the 32 KB below it (0x10000..0x17FFF),
//	            and the window repeats over the slot
//	0x07000000  OAM, 1 KB, mirrored over its slot
//	0x08000000  GamePak ROM, wait state 0 window (32 MB)
//	0x0A000000  GamePak ROM, wait state 1 window (32 MB)
//	0x0C000000  GamePak ROM, wait state 2 window (32 MB)
//	0x0E000000  GamePak SRAM, 64 KB, byte wide (0x0F000000
//	            mirrors the same SRAM, as on hardware)
//
// Everything else is unmapped. Unmapped reads return the
// open bus value and unmapped writes are ignored.
//
// Open bus model: the bus remembers the last value a read
// or a fetch drove onto it, and an unmapped read returns
// that value unchanged. That is an approximation of the
// real hardware, where an open read returns whatever the
// bus capacitance last held (in practice the prefetched
// instruction word for code running in other regions);
// last-value tracking is the documented GBA-1 model.
//
// Width rules at the bus level: Read returns the raw
// aligned unit, with no rotation: Read(addr, 4) returns
// the aligned word at addr&^3, Read(addr, 2) returns the
// aligned halfword at addr&^1 zero extended, and
// Read(addr, 1) returns the byte at addr. The GBATEK
// misaligned load rotation lives in the CPU, which is
// also what the conformance corpus expects: its recorded
// bus transactions carry the raw units. GamePak SRAM is
// byte wide, so wide SRAM reads return the addressed
// byte replicated across all lanes and half reads return
// it in both bytes; SRAM writes use only the low byte
// regardless of size. Writes to normal regions force the
// address to the access alignment: Write(addr, 4) stores
// the full word at addr&^3 and Write(addr, 2) stores the
// low halfword at addr&^1.
package bus

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi"
)

// Region sizes in bytes.
const (
	BIOSSize    = 0x4000  // 16 KB
	EWRAMSize   = 0x40000 // 256 KB
	IWRAMSize   = 0x8000  // 32 KB
	IOSize      = 0x400   // 1 KB
	PaletteSize = 0x400   // 1 KB
	VRAMSize    = 0x18000 // 96 KB
	OAMSize     = 0x400   // 1 KB
	SRAMSize    = 0x10000 // 64 KB
)

// Bus is the GBA system bus. The backing stores are
// exported so the system package can serialize them and
// tools can inspect them; ROM is the cartridge image,
// set through SetROM.
type Bus struct {
	BIOS    [BIOSSize]byte
	EWRAM   [EWRAMSize]byte
	IWRAM   [IWRAMSize]byte
	IO      [IOSize]byte
	Palette [PaletteSize]byte
	VRAM    [VRAMSize]byte
	OAM     [OAMSize]byte
	SRAM    [SRAMSize]byte

	ROM []byte

	// IORead and IOWrite, when set by the system, give IO
	// registers behavior: they are consulted for accesses
	// inside the 1 KB IO window before the plain store is.
	// The offset is relative to 0x04000000. A handler that
	// reports false leaves the access to the plain store
	// (which is where behavior-less registers such as
	// WAITCNT continue to live).
	IORead  func(off uint32, size int) (uint32, bool)
	IOWrite func(off uint32, size int, val uint32) bool

	// SaveRead and SaveWrite, when set by the system, give
	// a cartridge save device first claim on its windows:
	// the byte window at the top of the map (0x0E, where
	// flash parts live) and the EEPROM window inside the
	// ROM slot (top byte 0x0D). The hook returns true to
	// claim the access; false lets the normal path run
	// (an EEPROM window offset outside the active range
	// still reads the ROM, and the SRAM window still
	// serves plain battery RAM). The hooks are consulted
	// before the SRAM fast path and the backing stores,
	// so a claimed write never reaches the SRAM store or
	// the read only ROM path. Nil hooks keep the plain
	// GBA-1 behaviour.
	SaveRead  func(addr uint32, size int) (uint32, bool)
	SaveWrite func(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) bool

	// SRAMMask narrows the SRAM window index. Zero (the
	// default) keeps the GBA-1 behaviour: the whole 64 KB
	// store window. The system sets 0x7FFF for cartridges
	// with a 32 KB battery SRAM (and for signature-less
	// cartridges, whose window acts as plain SRAM), so
	// the upper half of the window mirrors the lower half
	// the way the real 32 KB part does.
	SRAMMask uint32

	// last is the open bus value: the last value a read
	// or fetch drove onto the bus.
	last uint32
}

// sramMask is the effective SRAM window index mask.
func (b *Bus) sramMask() uint32 {
	if b.SRAMMask != 0 {
		return b.SRAMMask
	}
	return SRAMSize - 1
}

// Bus must satisfy the CPU's memory interface.
var _ arm7tdmi.Bus = (*Bus)(nil)

// New returns a bus with all stores zeroed and no
// cartridge attached.
func New() *Bus { return &Bus{} }

// SetROM attaches a cartridge ROM image to the GamePak
// ROM windows. A nil or empty image detaches it, and
// reads of the ROM windows then return the open bus
// value.
func (b *Bus) SetROM(rom []byte) { b.ROM = rom }

// OpenBus returns the current open bus value (the last
// value a read or fetch drove).
func (b *Bus) OpenBus() uint32 { return b.last }

// isSRAM reports whether addr lands in the GamePak SRAM
// windows (0x0E and its 0x0F mirror).
func isSRAM(addr uint32) bool {
	top := addr >> 24
	return top == 0x0E || top == 0x0F
}

// decode maps an aligned address in a normal (non SRAM)
// region to its backing store and offset. readOnly marks
// stores that ignore writes (the BIOS and the ROM), and
// isROM marks the GamePak windows, whose reads wrap
// inside the image instead of indexing a fixed store.
// ok is false for unmapped addresses and for ROM windows
// with no image attached.
func (b *Bus) decode(addr uint32) (store []byte, off uint32, readOnly, isROM, ok bool) {
	switch top := addr >> 24; {
	case top == 0x00:
		if addr < BIOSSize {
			return b.BIOS[:], addr, true, false, true
		}
	case top == 0x02:
		return b.EWRAM[:], addr & (EWRAMSize - 1), false, false, true
	case top == 0x03:
		return b.IWRAM[:], addr & (IWRAMSize - 1), false, false, true
	case top == 0x04:
		if addr&0x00FFFFFF < IOSize {
			return b.IO[:], addr & (IOSize - 1), false, false, true
		}
	case top == 0x05:
		return b.Palette[:], addr & (PaletteSize - 1), false, false, true
	case top == 0x06:
		// The 128 KB window with the upper 32 KB mirrored:
		// window offsets 0x18000..0x1FFFF fold back onto
		// 0x10000..0x17FFF, and the window repeats over the
		// slot. (A plain mask cannot express this: it would
		// have to keep bit 15 for offsets below 0x18000 and
		// drop it above, which is exactly the fold below.
		// GBA-4 history: a 0x17FFF mask here dropped bit 15
		// everywhere, sending every access at 0x8000..0xFFFF
		// 32 KB low and scrambling the graphics of any game
		// that uses the upper half of VRAM.)
		off := addr & 0x1FFFF
		if off >= 0x18000 {
			off -= 0x8000
		}
		return b.VRAM[:], off, false, false, true
	case top == 0x07:
		return b.OAM[:], addr & (OAMSize - 1), false, false, true
	case top >= 0x08 && top <= 0x0D:
		if len(b.ROM) == 0 {
			return nil, 0, true, true, false
		}
		return b.ROM, addr & 0x01FFFFFF, true, true, true
	}
	return nil, 0, false, false, false
}

// readROM assembles size bytes starting at window offset
// off, wrapping inside the image so an undersized ROM
// mirrors across the whole window.
func (b *Bus) readROM(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	n := uint32(len(b.ROM))
	var v uint32
	if n&(n-1) == 0 {
		// Power of two image: mirror with a mask.
		for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
			v |= uint32(b.ROM[(off+uint32(i))&(n-1)]) << (8 * i)
		}
		return v
	}
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		v |= uint32(b.ROM[(off+uint32(i))%n]) << (8 * i)
	}
	return v
}

// readAligned reads size bytes from an address already
// aligned down to size, with no rotation applied.
func (b *Bus) readAligned(addr uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	store, off, _, isROM, ok := b.decode(addr)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	if isROM {
		return b.readROM(off, size), true
	}
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		v |= uint32(store[off+uint32(i)]) << (8 * i)
	}
	return v, true
}

// Read implements arm7tdmi.Bus, delivering the raw
// aligned unit (see the package comment for the full
// width contract): a 4-byte read returns the word at
// addr&^3, a 2-byte read returns the halfword at addr&^1
// zero extended, and a 1-byte read returns the byte at
// addr. The CPU applies the GBATEK misaligned rotation
// itself. Any other size returns the open bus value.
func (b *Bus) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1, 2, 4:
	default:
		return b.last
	}
	if addr>>24 == 0x04 && addr&0x00FFFFFF < IOSize && b.IORead != nil {
		if v, ok := b.IORead(addr&(IOSize-1), size); ok {
			b.last = v
			return v
		}
	}
	if b.SaveRead != nil {
		if v, ok := b.SaveRead(addr, size); ok {
			b.last = v
			return v
		}
	}
	if isSRAM(addr) {
		// Byte wide SRAM: the addressed byte is replicated
		// across the bus lanes, so every width returns the
		// replicated byte (a half read returns it in both
		// bytes).
		v := uint32(b.SRAM[addr&b.sramMask()])
		switch size {
		case 1:
			// v already holds just the byte.
		case 2:
			v |= v << 8
		case 4:
			v |= v << 8
			v |= v << 16
		}
		b.last = v
		return v
	}
	aligned := addr
	switch size {
	case 2:
		aligned &^= 1
	case 4:
		aligned &^= 3
	}
	v, ok := b.readAligned(aligned, size)
	if !ok {
		return b.last
	}
	b.last = v
	return v
}

// Fetch implements arm7tdmi.Bus. It behaves exactly like
// Read; keeping it a separate entry point is what lets
// the open bus value track the instruction stream, which
// is what dominates the real hardware's open bus reads.
func (b *Bus) Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	return b.Read(addr, size)
}

// Write implements arm7tdmi.Bus. Unmapped writes and
// writes to the BIOS and ROM windows are ignored. Wide
// writes to SRAM store only the low byte at the
// addressed byte. Writes do not change the open bus
// value in this model: only reads and fetches drive it.
func (b *Bus) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	switch size {
	case 1, 2, 4:
	default:
		return
	}
	if addr>>24 == 0x04 && addr&0x00FFFFFF < IOSize && b.IOWrite != nil {
		if b.IOWrite(addr&(IOSize-1), size, val) {
			return
		}
	}
	if b.SaveWrite != nil && b.SaveWrite(addr, size, val) {
		return
	}
	if isSRAM(addr) {
		b.SRAM[addr&b.sramMask()] = byte(val)
		return
	}
	aligned := addr
	if size == 2 {
		aligned &^= 1
	} else if size == 4 {
		aligned &^= 3
	}
	store, off, readOnly, _, ok := b.decode(aligned)
	if !ok || readOnly {
		return
	}
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		store[off+uint32(i)] = byte(val >> (8 * i))
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/bus/bus_test.go ====================

package bus

import "testing"

func TestMirroring(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		write uint32
		size  int
		val   uint32
		alias uint32 // an address that must mirror the write address
	}{
		{"EWRAM 256 KB mirror", 0x02000100, 4, 0x11223344, 0x02040100},
		{"EWRAM slot top mirror", 0x02000100, 4, 0x55667788, 0x02FC0100},
		{"IWRAM 32 KB mirror", 0x03000040, 4, 0x99AABBCC, 0x03008040},
		{"IWRAM slot top mirror", 0x03000040, 2, 0xBEEF, 0x03FF8040},
		{"palette 1 KB mirror", 0x05000010, 2, 0x7FFF, 0x05000410},
		{"palette slot mirror", 0x05000010, 4, 0x03E07C1F, 0x05010010},
		{"OAM 1 KB mirror", 0x07000020, 4, 0xDEADBEEF, 0x07000420},
		{"OAM slot mirror", 0x07000020, 2, 0x1234, 0x07020020},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			b := New()
			b.Write(c.write, c.size, c.val)
			if got := b.Read(c.alias, c.size); got != c.val {
				t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, %d) = %#08x, want %#08x (mirror of write at %#08x)",
					c.alias, c.size, got, c.val, c.write)
			}
			if got := b.Read(c.write, c.size); got != c.val {
				t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, %d) = %#08x, want %#08x", c.write, c.size, got, c.val)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestVRAMUpperMirror(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	// The top 32 KB of VRAM lives at window offsets
	// 0x10000..0x17FFF and is mirrored at 0x18000..0x1FFFF.
	b.Write(0x06010000, 4, 0xCAFEBABE)
	for _, addr := range []uint32{0x06010000, 0x06018000, 0x06030000, 0x06038000} {
		if got := b.Read(addr, 4); got != 0xCAFEBABE {
			t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, 4) = %#08x, want 0xCAFEBABE", addr, got)
		}
	}
	// The lower 64 KB repeats every 128 KB window too.
	b.Write(0x06000004, 4, 0x0BADF00D)
	for _, addr := range []uint32{0x06000004, 0x06020004, 0x06040004} {
		if got := b.Read(addr, 4); got != 0x0BADF00D {
			t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, 4) = %#08x, want 0x0BADF00D", addr, got)
		}
	}
	// A write through the upper mirror lands in the same
	// backing bytes as the first copy.
	b.Write(0x06018008, 4, 0x11223344)
	if got := b.Read(0x06010008, 4); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Fatalf("Read(0x06010008, 4) = %#08x, want 0x11223344", got)
	}
}

// TestVRAMMiddleBand pins the window offsets
// 0x8000..0xFFFF: they are real VRAM (the second 32 KB
// bank and the OBJ tile area starts right above them),
// NOT aliases of the 32 KB below. A mask-based decode
// once dropped bit 15 for the whole window, folding this
// band onto 0x0000..0x7FFF and scrambling any game that
// places maps or tiles there (found by the Anguna gate
// in GBA-4: its BG2 tilemap at window 0xE000 landed at
// backing offset 0x6000).
func TestVRAMMiddleBand(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	marks := []struct {
		addr uint32
		val  uint32
	}{
		{0x06008000, 0x11111111},
		{0x0600A000, 0x22222222},
		{0x0600E000, 0x33333333},
		{0x0600FFFC, 0x44444444},
	}
	for _, mk := range marks {
		b.Write(mk.addr, 4, mk.val)
	}
	for _, mk := range marks {
		if got := b.Read(mk.addr, 4); got != mk.val {
			t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, 4) = %#08x, want %#08x", mk.addr, got, mk.val)
		}
	}
	// The spots the buggy fold used to hit must be empty.
	for _, addr := range []uint32{0x06000000, 0x06002000, 0x06006000, 0x06007FFC} {
		if got := b.Read(addr, 4); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, 4) = %#08x, want 0 (the middle band must not alias the low band)", addr, got)
		}
	}
	// And the backing store must hold the bytes at the
	// true offsets.
	if got := b.VRAM[0x8000]; got != 0x11 {
		t.Fatalf("VRAM backing at 0x8000 = %#02x, want 0x11", got)
	}
	if got := b.VRAM[0xE000]; got != 0x33 {
		t.Fatalf("VRAM backing at 0xE000 = %#02x, want 0x33", got)
	}
}

func TestROMMirroring(t *testing.T) {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x1000) // 4 KB fake ROM
	for i := range rom {
		rom[i] = byte(i*7 + 3)
	}
	b := New()
	b.SetROM(rom)
	want := b.Read(0x08000040, 4)
	for _, addr := range []uint32{0x08001040, 0x08002040, 0x0A000040, 0x0A003040, 0x0C000040, 0x0C007040} {
		if got := b.Read(addr, 4); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, 4) = %#08x, want %#08x (4 KB ROM mirror)", addr, got, want)
		}
	}
	// Byte reads agree with the image at the base window.
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if got := b.Read(0x08000000+uint32(i), 1); got != uint32(rom[i]) {
			t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, 1) = %#02x, want %#02x", 0x08000000+i, got, rom[i])
		}
	}
	// Writes to the ROM windows are ignored.
	b.Write(0x08000000, 4, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	if got := b.Read(0x08000000, 4); got == 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Fatal("write to ROM window changed the image")
	}
}

func TestSRAMByteReplication(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write(0x0E000000, 1, 0xAB)
	reads := []struct {
		addr uint32
		size int
		want uint32
	}{
		{0x0E000000, 1, 0xAB},
		{0x0E000000, 2, 0xABAB},
		{0x0E000000, 4, 0xABABABAB},
		{0x0E000001, 1, 0x00}, // the next byte is untouched
	}
	for _, r := range reads {
		if got := b.Read(r.addr, r.size); got != r.want {
			t.Fatalf("Read(%#08x, %d) = %#08x, want %#08x", r.addr, r.size, got, r.want)
		}
	}
	// An odd address with its own byte replicates that
	// byte with no rotation applied.
	b.Write(0x0E000001, 1, 0xCD)
	if got := b.Read(0x0E000001, 4); got != 0xCDCDCDCD {
		t.Fatalf("Read(0x0E000001, 4) = %#08x, want 0xCDCDCDCD", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x0E000001, 2); got != 0xCDCD {
		t.Fatalf("Read(0x0E000001, 2) = %#08x, want 0xCDCD", got)
	}
	// The 0x0F window mirrors the same SRAM.
	if got := b.Read(0x0F000000, 1); got != 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("Read(0x0F000000, 1) = %#02x, want 0xAB", got)
	}
}

func TestSRAMWideWritesUseLowByte(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.SRAM[0x11] = 0xEE // neighbor sentinel
	b.Write(0x0E000010, 4, 0x12345678)
	if got := b.SRAM[0x10]; got != 0x78 {
		t.Fatalf("SRAM[0x10] = %#02x, want 0x78 (low byte of wide write)", got)
	}
	if got := b.SRAM[0x11]; got != 0xEE {
		t.Fatalf("SRAM[0x11] = %#02x, want 0xEE (neighbor untouched)", got)
	}
	b.Write(0x0E000020, 2, 0x1234)
	if got := b.Read(0x0E000020, 1); got != 0x34 {
		t.Fatalf("Read(0x0E000020, 1) = %#02x, want 0x34", got)
	}
}

// TestRawAlignedReads pins the exact values the bus
// delivers for the word 0x11223344 stored at an aligned
// EWRAM address: the bus returns the raw aligned unit
// with no rotation (the CPU owns the GBATEK misaligned
// rotation). A word read returns the aligned word for
// every address inside it, a half read returns the
// aligned halfword at addr&^1, and a byte read returns
// the addressed byte.
func TestRawAlignedReads(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write(0x02000000, 4, 0x11223344)
	cases := []struct {
		addr uint32
		size int
		want uint32
	}{
		{0x02000000, 4, 0x11223344},
		{0x02000001, 4, 0x11223344},
		{0x02000002, 4, 0x11223344},
		{0x02000003, 4, 0x11223344},
		{0x02000000, 2, 0x00003344},
		{0x02000001, 2, 0x00003344},
		{0x02000002, 2, 0x00001122},
		{0x02000003, 2, 0x00001122},
		{0x02000000, 1, 0x44},
		{0x02000001, 1, 0x33},
		{0x02000002, 1, 0x22},
		{0x02000003, 1, 0x11},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if got := b.Read(c.addr, c.size); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("Read(%#08x, %d) = %#08x, want %#08x", c.addr, c.size, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestWritesForceAlignment pins the write side of the
// contract: a word write stores at addr&^3 and a half
// write stores the low halfword at addr&^1.
func TestWritesForceAlignment(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write(0x02000002, 4, 0xAABBCCDD)
	if got := b.Read(0x02000000, 4); got != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Fatalf("after unaligned word write, Read(0x02000000, 4) = %#08x, want 0xAABBCCDD", got)
	}
	b.Write(0x02000011, 2, 0x12345678)
	if got := b.Read(0x02000010, 2); got != 0x5678 {
		t.Fatalf("after unaligned half write, Read(0x02000010, 2) = %#08x, want 0x5678", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x02000012, 2); got != 0x0000 {
		t.Fatalf("half write touched the next halfword: Read(0x02000012, 2) = %#08x", got)
	}
}

func TestOpenBus(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	// A fresh bus has driven nothing, and the BIOS store
	// reads back as zeros.
	if got := b.Read(0x01000000, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh open bus Read = %#08x, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x00000000, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BIOS Read = %#08x, want 0 (zero filled store)", got)
	}
	b.Write(0x02000000, 4, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if got := b.Read(0x02000000, 4); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("Read = %#08x, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	// Unused region 0x01 returns the last driven value.
	if got := b.Read(0x01000000, 4); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("open bus Read(0x01000000, 4) = %#08x, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	// Address 0x0D000000 with no cartridge attached: the
	// ROM window has nothing to drive, so it is open bus
	// as well.
	if got := b.Read(0x0D000000, 4); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("open bus Read(0x0D000000, 4) = %#08x, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	// A fetch drives the bus too, and a later open read
	// returns the fetched value.
	b.Write(0x02000004, 4, 0x12345678)
	if got := b.Fetch(0x02000004, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("Fetch = %#08x, want 0x12345678", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x01000000, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("open bus after Fetch = %#08x, want 0x12345678", got)
	}
	if got := b.OpenBus(); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("OpenBus() = %#08x, want 0x12345678", got)
	}
	// Writes to unmapped regions are ignored and do not
	// disturb real stores.
	b.Write(0x01000000, 4, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	if got := b.Read(0x02000004, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("Read after unmapped write = %#08x, want 0x12345678", got)
	}
}

func TestIOStore(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	// WAITCNT lives at 0x04000204; in this slice it is a
	// plain cell of the IO store.
	b.Write(0x04000204, 2, 0x4317)
	if got := b.Read(0x04000204, 2); got != 0x4317 {
		t.Fatalf("WAITCNT Read = %#08x, want 0x4317", got)
	}
	if b.IO[0x204] != 0x17 || b.IO[0x205] != 0x43 {
		t.Fatalf("IO store bytes at 0x204 = %#02x %#02x, want 0x17 0x43", b.IO[0x204], b.IO[0x205])
	}
	b.Write(0x04000000, 4, 0xA5A5A5A5)
	if got := b.Read(0x04000000, 4); got != 0xA5A5A5A5 {
		t.Fatalf("IO Read = %#08x, want 0xA5A5A5A5", got)
	}
	b.Write(0x04000100, 1, 0x5A)
	if got := b.Read(0x04000100, 1); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("IO byte Read = %#08x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
	// Past the 1 KB register store the region is unmapped:
	// the read falls back to the open bus (the last IO
	// byte read, 0x5A).
	if got := b.Read(0x04000400, 4); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("Read past IO store = %#08x, want open bus 0x5A", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/cart/cart.go ====================

// Package cart parses a Game Boy Advance cartridge
// header, written from the published GBATEK cartridge
// header layout:
//
//	0x00  entry point (an ARM branch, 4 bytes)
//	0x04  the 156 byte logo bitmap (never embedded or
//	      checked by this core; it is Nintendo data)
//	0xA0  game title, 12 bytes
//	0xAC  game code, 4 bytes
//	0xB0  maker code, 2 bytes
//	0xB2  fixed byte, must be 0x96
//	0xBC  software version
//	0xBD  header checksum: -(0x19 + sum of 0xA0..0xBC)
//
// The save type is not a header field on GBA cartridges;
// games name their save chip in an ASCII signature string
// embedded in the ROM ("SRAM_V", "FLASH_V", "FLASH512_V",
// "FLASH1M_V", "EEPROM_V", each followed by version
// digits), and Parse finds it by scanning the image the
// way the published documentation describes.
package cart

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// SaveKind classifies the save chip a cartridge's
// signature names.
type SaveKind int

const (
	SaveNone SaveKind = iota
	SaveSRAM
	SaveFlash
	SaveFlash512
	SaveFlash1M
	SaveEEPROM
)

func (k SaveKind) String() string {
	switch k {
	case SaveSRAM:
		return "SRAM"
	case SaveFlash:
		return "FLASH"
	case SaveFlash512:
		return "FLASH512"
	case SaveFlash1M:
		return "FLASH1M"
	case SaveEEPROM:
		return "EEPROM"
	}
	return "none"
}

// saveSignatures are scanned longest first, so the
// longer FLASH512_V and FLASH1M_V signatures win over
// the FLASH_V prefix they share a stem with.
var saveSignatures = []struct {
	sig  string
	kind SaveKind
}{
	{"FLASH512_V", SaveFlash512},
	{"FLASH1M_V", SaveFlash1M},
	{"EEPROM_V", SaveEEPROM},
	{"FLASH_V", SaveFlash},
	{"SRAM_V", SaveSRAM},
}

// Cart is a parsed cartridge image.
type Cart struct {
	ROM []byte // the image exactly as loaded

	EntryPoint uint32 // the word at 0x00 (an ARM branch on real games)
	Title      string // 0xA0, 12 bytes, trailing zeros and spaces trimmed
	GameCode   string // 0xAC, 4 bytes
	MakerCode  string // 0xB0, 2 bytes
	Version    uint8  // 0xBC

	HeaderChecksum      uint8 // the byte stored at 0xBD
	HeaderChecksumValid bool  // whether 0xBD matches the computed checksum

	// ROMSize is the addressable ROM size: the smallest
	// power of two that holds the image, capped at the
	// 32 MB a GamePak window serves. Undersized images
	// mirror across it (see the bus package).
	ROMSize int

	SaveKind SaveKind
	// SaveType is the full signature as found in the
	// image, signature plus its version digits (for
	// example "FLASH1M_V103"), or empty when the image
	// carries no save signature.
	SaveType string
}

// headerChecksum computes the checksum byte for header
// bytes 0xA0..0xBC: chk = -(0x19 + sum of the bytes).
func headerChecksum(rom []byte) uint8 {
	sum := 0x19
	for _, c := range rom[0xA0 : 0xBC+1] {
		sum += int(c)
	}
	return uint8(-sum)
}

// detectSave scans the image for the save signatures,
// longest signature first (see saveSignatures), and
// returns the kind and the full signature string with
// its version digits.
func detectSave(rom []byte) (SaveKind, string) {
	for _, s := range saveSignatures {
		i := bytes.Index(rom, []byte(s.sig))
		if i < 0 {
			continue
		}
		end := i + len(s.sig)
		for end < len(rom) && rom[end] >= '0' && rom[end] <= '9' {
			end++
		}
		return s.kind, string(rom[i:end])
	}
	return SaveNone, ""
}

// Parse validates and describes a cartridge image. It
// refuses images too small to hold a header and images
// whose fixed byte at 0xB2 is not 0x96. A wrong header
// checksum is reported through HeaderChecksumValid
// rather than refused: real world images with damaged
// headers exist, and the caller decides.
func Parse(rom []byte) (*Cart, error) {
	if len(rom) < 0xC0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cart: image too small for a GBA header (%d bytes, need at least %d)", len(rom), 0xC0)
	}
	if rom[0xB2] != 0x96 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cart: fixed byte at 0xB2 is %#02x, want 0x96", rom[0xB2])
	}
	c := &Cart{ROM: rom}
	c.EntryPoint = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(rom[0x00:0x04])
	c.Title = strings.TrimRight(string(rom[0xA0:0xAC]), "\x00 ")
	c.GameCode = string(rom[0xAC:0xB0])
	c.MakerCode = string(rom[0xB0:0xB2])
	c.Version = rom[0xBC]
	c.HeaderChecksum = rom[0xBD]
	c.HeaderChecksumValid = headerChecksum(rom) == rom[0xBD]
	c.ROMSize = 1
	for c.ROMSize < len(rom) && c.ROMSize < 32*1024*1024 {
		c.ROMSize <<= 1
	}
	c.SaveKind, c.SaveType = detectSave(rom)
	return c, nil
}

// Load is Parse under the family name the sibling cores
// use for their cartridge entry point.
func Load(rom []byte) (*Cart, error) { return Parse(rom) }


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/cart/cart_test.go ====================

package cart

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// synthetic builds a minimal valid image of the given
// size with a proper header; fixups sets fields before
// the checksum is computed, and a non-nil checksum
// override writes that byte at 0xBD instead.
func synthetic(size int, fixups func(rom []byte), checksumOverride *uint8) []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, size)
	// Entry: an ARM branch to the code offset past the
	// header, the shape a real image starts with.
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x00:], 0xEA00002E)
	copy(rom[0xA0:], "TESTGAME")
	copy(rom[0xAC:], "ATGE")
	copy(rom[0xB0:], "01")
	rom[0xB2] = 0x96
	rom[0xBC] = 0x03
	if fixups != nil {
		fixups(rom)
	}
	chk := headerChecksum(rom)
	if checksumOverride != nil {
		chk = *checksumOverride
	}
	rom[0xBD] = chk
	return rom
}

func TestParseValid(t *testing.T) {
	rom := synthetic(0x4000, nil, nil)
	c, err := Parse(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Parse: %v", err)
	}
	if c.Title != "TESTGAME" {
		t.Errorf("Title = %q, want TESTGAME", c.Title)
	}
	if c.GameCode != "ATGE" {
		t.Errorf("GameCode = %q, want ATGE", c.GameCode)
	}
	if c.MakerCode != "01" {
		t.Errorf("MakerCode = %q, want 01", c.MakerCode)
	}
	if c.Version != 0x03 {
		t.Errorf("Version = %#02x, want 0x03", c.Version)
	}
	if c.EntryPoint != 0xEA00002E {
		t.Errorf("EntryPoint = %#08x, want 0xEA00002E", c.EntryPoint)
	}
	if !c.HeaderChecksumValid {
		t.Error("HeaderChecksumValid = false on a checksummed header")
	}
	if c.HeaderChecksum != rom[0xBD] {
		t.Errorf("HeaderChecksum = %#02x, want %#02x", c.HeaderChecksum, rom[0xBD])
	}
	if c.ROMSize != 0x4000 {
		t.Errorf("ROMSize = %#x, want 0x4000", c.ROMSize)
	}
	if c.SaveKind != SaveNone || c.SaveType != "" {
		t.Errorf("Save = %v %q, want none", c.SaveKind, c.SaveType)
	}
	if len(c.ROM) != len(rom) {
		t.Errorf("ROM holds %d bytes, want %d", len(c.ROM), len(rom))
	}
}

func TestParseChecksumWrong(t *testing.T) {

	}

func TestROMSizeRounding(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		size int
		want int
	}{
		{0xC0, 0x100},
		{0x100, 0x100},
		{0x101, 0x200},
		{0x12345, 0x20000},
		{32 * 1024 * 1024, 32 * 1024 * 1024},

func TestSaveSignatures(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		sig  string
		kind SaveKind
		want string
	}{
		{"SRAM", "SRAM_V110", SaveSRAM, "SRAM_V110"},
		{"FLASH", "FLASH_V126", SaveFlash, "FLASH_V126"},

		{"FLASH1M", "FLASH1M_V103", SaveFlash1M, "FLASH1M_V103"},
		{"EEPROM", "EEPROM_V124", SaveEEPROM, "EEPROM_V124"},

	for _, tc := range cases {

				copy(r[0x800:], tc.sig)
				copy(r[0x800+len(tc.sig):], "\x00\xff not digits")
			}, nil)

			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("Parse: %v", err)
			}
			if c.SaveKind != tc.kind {
				t.Errorf("SaveKind = %v, want %v", c.SaveKind, tc.kind)
			}
			if c.SaveType != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("SaveType = %q, want %q", c.SaveType, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestSaveSignatureLongestWins puts the FLASH1M signature
// in an image that also carries a bare FLASH_V string, in
// both orders: the longer signature must win either way,
// because scanning checks longer signatures first.
func TestSaveSignatureLongestWins(t *testing.T) {
	for _, order := range []string{"flash-first", "flash1m-first"} {
		rom := synthetic(0x2000, func(r []byte) {
			if order == "flash-first" {
				copy(r[0x800:], "FLASH_V126")
				copy(r[0x1000:], "FLASH1M_V103")
			} else {
				copy(r[0x800:], "FLASH1M_V103")
				copy(r[0x1000:], "FLASH_V126")
			}
		}, nil)
		c, err := Parse(rom)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: Parse: %v", order, err)
		}
		if c.SaveKind != SaveFlash1M || c.SaveType != "FLASH1M_V103" {
			t.Errorf("%s: Save = %v %q, want FLASH1M FLASH1M_V103", order, c.SaveKind, c.SaveType)
		}
		if strings.Contains(c.SaveType, "FLASH_V") && c.SaveKind == SaveFlash {
			t.Errorf("%s: bare FLASH signature won over FLASH1M", order)
		}
	}
	// Same check for FLASH512 against FLASH.
	rom := synthetic(0x2000, func(r []byte) {
		copy(r[0x800:], "FLASH_V126")
		copy(r[0x1000:], "FLASH512_V131")
	}, nil)
	c, err := Parse(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Parse: %v", err)
	}
	if c.SaveKind != SaveFlash512 || c.SaveType != "FLASH512_V131" {
		t.Errorf("Save = %v %q, want FLASH512 FLASH512_V131", c.SaveKind, c.SaveType)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi/arm.go ====================

package arm7tdmi

// execARM executes one ARM-state instruction (the word in the
// execute stage, located at R15-8) and returns its cycle count.
func (c *CPU) execARM(instr uint32) int {
	addr := c.R[15] - 8
	cond := instr >> 28
	if cond != 0xE && !c.condPassed(cond) {
		return 1
	}

	// Branch and exchange: 0001 0010 1111 1111 1111 0001.
	// Bit 0 of the operand selects the new state and is consumed.
	if instr&0x0FFFFFF0 == 0x012FFF10 {
		v := c.R[instr&0xF]
		if v&1 != 0 {
			c.CPSR |= BitT
		} else {
			c.CPSR &^= BitT
		}
		c.branch(v &^ 1)
		return 3
	}

	switch {
	case (instr>>26)&3 == 0 && instr&(1<<25) == 0 && (instr&0x90) == 0x90 && (instr>>5)&3 == 0:
		// Multiply, multiply-long, swap space (bit 7 and bit 4
		// set, shift field zero).
		switch {
		case (instr>>23)&0x1F == 0x1:
			return c.execMultiplyLong(instr)
		case (instr>>22)&0x3F == 0:
			return c.execMultiply(instr)
		case instr&0x0FB00FF0 == 0x01000090:
			return c.execSwap(instr)
		}
		return c.undefined(addr)

	case (instr>>26)&3 == 0 && instr&(1<<25) == 0 && (instr&0x90) == 0x90:
		// Halfword and signed data transfer (bits 6-5 nonzero).
		return c.execHalfword(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>26)&3 == 0:
		return c.execDataProc(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>26)&3 == 1:
		// Single data transfer. A register offset with bit 4 set
		// is undefined on ARMv4.
		if instr&(1<<25) != 0 && instr&(1<<4) != 0 {
			return c.undefined(addr)
		}
		return c.execSingle(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>25)&7 == 4:
		return c.execBlock(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>25)&7 == 5:
		// Branch, branch with link.
		off := int32(instr<<8) >> 8
		target := uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off<<2)
		if instr&(1<<24) != 0 {
			c.R[14] = addr + 4
		}
		c.branch(target)
		return 3

	case (instr>>24)&0xF == 0xF:
		// Software interrupt: the system hook (BIOS HLE) gets
		// first refusal with the raw 24-bit comment field;
		// unhandled calls take the real exception.
		if c.SWIHook != nil {
			if n, ok := c.SWIHook(c, instr&0xFFFFFF); ok {
				return n
			}
		}
		return c.exception(0x08, ModeSVC, addr+4)
	}

	// Coprocessor space and everything left over has no
	// coprocessor to answer on the ARM7TDMI: undefined trap.
	return c.undefined(addr)
}

// writeReg writes an instruction result, refilling the pipeline
// when the destination is the PC.
func (c *CPU) writeReg(rd uint32, v uint32) {
	if rd == 15 {
		c.branch(v)
		return
	}
	c.R[rd] = v
}

func mulCycles(rs uint32) int {
	switch {
	case rs&0xFFFFFF00 == 0 || rs&0xFFFFFF00 == 0xFFFFFF00:
		return 1
	case rs&0xFFFF0000 == 0 || rs&0xFFFF0000 == 0xFFFF0000:
		return 2
	case rs&0xFF000000 == 0 || rs&0xFF000000 == 0xFF000000:
		return 3
	}
	return 4
}

// execMultiply runs MUL and MLA.
func (c *CPU) execMultiply(instr uint32) int {
	acc := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	set := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rd := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rn := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	rs := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
	rm := instr & 0xF
	lhs, rhs := c.memReg(rm), c.memReg(rs)
	var accum uint32
	res := lhs * rhs
	if acc {
		accum = c.memReg(rn)
		res += accum
	}
	if set {
		c.setNZ(res)
		full := tickMultiply(true, rhs)
		c.setCarry(mulCarry(full, false, false, lhs, rhs, accum, 0))
	}
	c.writeReg(rd, res)
	n := 1 + mulCycles(rhs)
	if acc {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// execMultiplyLong runs UMULL, UMLAL, SMULL and SMLAL.
func (c *CPU) execMultiplyLong(instr uint32) int {
	signed := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	acc := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	set := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rdHi := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rdLo := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	rs := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
	rm := instr & 0xF
	lhs, rhs := c.memReg(rm), c.memReg(rs)
	var res uint64
	if signed {
		res = uint64(int64(int32(lhs)) * int64(int32(rhs)))
	} else {
		res = uint64(lhs) * uint64(rhs)
	}
	var accumLo, accumHi uint32
	if acc {
		accumLo = c.memReg(rdLo)
		accumHi = c.memReg(rdHi)
		res += uint64(accumHi)<<32 | uint64(accumLo)
	}
	if set {
		c.CPSR &^= FlagN | FlagZ
		if res>>63 != 0 {
			c.CPSR |= FlagN
		}
		if res == 0 {
			c.CPSR |= FlagZ
		}
		full := tickMultiply(signed, rhs)
		c.setCarry(mulCarry(full, true, signed, lhs, rhs, accumLo, accumHi))
	}
	c.R[rdLo] = uint32(res)
	c.R[rdHi] = uint32(res >> 32)
	if rdHi == 15 {
		c.branch(uint32(res >> 32))
	} else if rdLo == 15 {
		c.branch(uint32(res))
	}
	n := 2 + mulCycles(rhs)
	if acc {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// execSwap runs SWP and SWPB.
func (c *CPU) execSwap(instr uint32) int {
	byteOp := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	rm := instr & 0xF
	// The swap address and the stored operand both read PC as
	// A+12 when they name R15 (the reference implementation
	// reads them after its pipeline increment).
	addr := c.memReg(rn)
	if byteOp {
		tmp := c.Bus.Read(addr, 1)
		c.Bus.Write(addr, 1, c.memReg(rm)&0xFF)
		c.writeReg(rd, tmp)
		return 4
	}
	tmp := c.load(addr, 4, false)
	c.Bus.Write(addr, 4, c.memReg(rm))
	c.writeReg(rd, tmp)
	return 4
}

// decodePSR handles MRS and MSR inside the data-processing space:
// the test-opcode encodings with S clear are the PSR transfers.
func (c *CPU) execPSR(instr uint32, opcode uint32) (int, bool) {
	sBit := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	if sBit {
		return 0, false
	}
	switch opcode {
	case 8, 10: // TST / CMP shape: MRS when Rn=1111 and low bits 0
		if (instr>>16)&0xF != 0xF || instr&0xFFF != 0 {
			return 0, false
		}
		rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
		var v uint32
		if opcode == 10 {
			v = c.curSPSR()
		} else {
			v = c.CPSR
		}
		// MRS writes its destination as a plain register, even
		// when Rd is R15: no pipeline refill follows (the
		// reference behavior advances sequentially).
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 1, true
	case 9, 11: // TEQ / CMN shape: MSR
		fieldMask := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
		var v uint32
		if instr&(1<<25) != 0 {
			rot := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
			v = ror32(instr&0xFF, uint(rot*2))
		} else {
			if instr&0xFF0 != 0 {
				return 0, false
			}
			v = c.R[instr&0xF]
		}
		c.msr(opcode == 11, fieldMask, v)
		return 1, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// execDataProc runs the ARM data-processing group, including the
// PSR transfers that share its encoding space.
func (c *CPU) execDataProc(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	opcode := (instr >> 21) & 0xF
	if n, ok := c.execPSR(instr, opcode); ok {
		return n
	}
	sBit := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	isTest := opcode >= 8 && opcode <= 11

	// Operand 2.
	var op2 uint32
	var shiftCarry bool
	regShift := false
	if instr&(1<<25) != 0 {
		rot := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
		op2 = ror32(instr&0xFF, uint(rot*2))
		if rot == 0 {
			shiftCarry = c.carry()
		} else {
			shiftCarry = op2>>31 != 0
		}
	} else if instr&(1<<4) != 0 {
		regShift = true
		rs := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
		// The shift-amount register reads PC as the plain A+8
		// in the reference implementation (no +12 quirk for
		// Rs), while Rn and Rm do take the +4 adjustment.
		rsVal := c.R[rs]
		rmVal := c.R[instr&0xF]
		if instr&0xF == 15 {
			rmVal += 4
		}
		op2, shiftCarry = c.shifter(rmVal, (instr>>5)&3, rsVal&0xFF, true)
	} else {
		// Immediate shift: an Rm of R15 reads the plain A+8
		// already held in R15, which c.R[instr&0xF] provides.
		amt := (instr >> 7) & 0x1F
		op2, shiftCarry = c.shifter(c.R[instr&0xF], (instr>>5)&3, amt, false)
	}

	rnVal := c.R[rn]
	if rn == 15 && regShift {
		rnVal += 4
	}

	setFlags := sBit || isTest
	var res uint32
	logical := false
	switch opcode {
	case 0, 8: // AND, TST
		res = rnVal & op2
		logical = true
	case 1, 9: // EOR, TEQ
		res = rnVal ^ op2
		logical = true
	case 2, 10: // SUB, CMP
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(rnVal, op2, true)
		} else {
			res = rnVal - op2
		}
	case 3: // RSB
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(op2, rnVal, true)
		} else {
			res = op2 - rnVal
		}
	case 4, 11: // ADD, CMN
		if setFlags {
			res = c.addFlags(rnVal, op2, false)
		} else {
			res = rnVal + op2
		}
	case 5: // ADC
		if setFlags {
			res = c.addFlags(rnVal, op2, c.carry())
		} else {
			res = rnVal + op2
			if c.carry() {
				res++
			}
		}
	case 6: // SBC
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(rnVal, op2, c.carry())
		} else {
			res = rnVal - op2
			if !c.carry() {
				res--
			}
		}
	case 7: // RSC
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(op2, rnVal, c.carry())
		} else {
			res = op2 - rnVal
			if !c.carry() {
				res--
			}
		}
	case 12: // ORR
		res = rnVal | op2
		logical = true
	case 13: // MOV
		res = op2
		logical = true
	case 14: // BIC
		res = rnVal &^ op2
		logical = true
	case 15: // MVN
		res = ^op2
		logical = true
	}
