	if logical && setFlags {
		c.setNZC(res, shiftCarry)
	}

	if isTest {
		// A test-opcode encoding whose Rd field is R15 with S
		// set restores the CPSR from the SPSR after the flag
		// computation, in the reference implementation. In
		// modes without an SPSR the restore reads back the
		// CPSR itself, so the computed flags stand.
		if rd == 15 && sBit {
			c.setCPSR(c.curSPSR())
		}
		return 1 + regShiftCycles(regShift, false)
	}
	if rd == 15 {
		if sBit {
			c.setCPSR(c.curSPSR())
		}
		c.branch(res)
		return 1 + regShiftCycles(regShift, true)
	}
	c.R[rd] = res
	return 1 + regShiftCycles(regShift, false)
}

func regShiftCycles(regShift bool, rdPC bool) int {
	n := 0
	if regShift {
		n++
	}
	if rdPC {
		n += 2
	}
	return n
}

// addrMode computes the effective address and writeback value for
// the P/U/W addressing forms shared by the single and halfword
// transfers. It returns the address to access, the value to write
// back (when doWB), and whether writeback applies.
func addrMode(base, offset uint32, pre, up, w bool) (ea, wb uint32, doWB bool) {
	if pre {
		if up {
			ea = base + offset
		} else {
			ea = base - offset
		}
		return ea, ea, w
	}
	if up {
		wb = base + offset
	} else {
		wb = base - offset
	}
	return base, wb, true
}

// execSingle runs LDR and STR (word and byte forms).
func (c *CPU) execSingle(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	pre := instr&(1<<24) != 0
	up := instr&(1<<23) != 0
	byteOp := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	w := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	load := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF

	var offset uint32
	if instr&(1<<25) != 0 {
		amt := (instr >> 7) & 0x1F
		offset, _ = c.shifter(c.R[instr&0xF], (instr>>5)&3, amt, false)
	} else {
		offset = instr & 0xFFF
	}
	ea, wb, doWB := addrMode(c.R[rn], offset, pre, up, w)

	// A writeback into R15 refills the pipeline at the
	// written-back value plus one unit (the reference
	// implementation computes it from the post-increment PC),
	// unless a load into R15 follows and wins.
	writeback := func() {
		if !doWB {
			return
		}
		if rn == 15 {
			c.branch(wb + 4)
		} else {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
	}

	if load {
		var v uint32
		if byteOp {
			v = c.load(ea, 1, false)
		} else {
			v = c.load(ea, 4, false)
		}
		if rn != rd {
			writeback()
		}
		if rd == 15 {
			c.branch(v)
			return 5
		}
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 3
	}
	data := c.R[rd]
	if rd == 15 {
		data = c.R[15] + 4 // STR of PC stores A+12
	}
	if byteOp {
		c.store(ea, 1, data)
	} else {
		c.store(ea, 4, data)
	}
	writeback()
	return 2
}

// execHalfword runs the halfword and signed transfer group.
// Note the offset-kind bit (22) is inverted relative to the
// single transfers: set means an immediate offset, clear means a
// register offset.
func (c *CPU) execHalfword(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	pre := instr&(1<<24) != 0
	up := instr&(1<<23) != 0
	regOff := instr&(1<<22) == 0
	w := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	load := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	sh := (instr >> 5) & 3

	if !load && sh != 1 {
		return c.undefined(addr)
	}
	var offset uint32
	if regOff {
		offset = c.R[instr&0xF]
	} else {
		offset = ((instr>>8)&0xF)<<4 | (instr & 0xF)
	}
	ea, wb, doWB := addrMode(c.R[rn], offset, pre, up, w)

	if load {
		var v uint32
		switch sh {
		case 1:
			v = c.load(ea, 2, false)
		case 2:
			v = c.load(ea, 1, true)
		case 3:
			v = c.load(ea, 2, true)
		}
		if doWB && rn != rd {
			if rn == 15 {
				c.branch(wb + 4)
			} else {
				c.R[rn] = wb
			}
		}
		if rd == 15 {
			c.branch(v)
			return 5
		}
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 3
	}
	data := c.R[rd]
	if rd == 15 {
		data = c.R[15] + 4
	}
	c.store(ea, 2, data)
	if doWB {
		if rn == 15 {
			c.branch(wb + 4)
		} else {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
	}
	return 2
}

// blockStart returns the address of the first (lowest-address)
// transfer of a block of count words from base, for the four
// addressing modes: increment after, increment before, decrement
// after, decrement before.
func blockStart(base uint32, count int, pre, up bool) uint32 {
	switch {
	case up && !pre:
		return base
	case up && pre:
		return base + 4
	case !up && !pre:
		return base - 4*uint32(count-1)
	default:
		return base - 4*uint32(count)
	}
}

// execBlock runs LDM and STM, all four addressing modes. The
// structure follows the reference implementation: with the S bit
// set the CPU switches to the user register view for the whole
// transfer, except for an S-bit LDM that also loads the PC,
// which transfers into the current view and then restores the
// CPSR from the SPSR. The base writeback is applied when the
// first register of the list is reached, before that register
// is itself transferred. An empty register list transfers R15
// only, with a writeback offset of 0x40.
func (c *CPU) execBlock(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	pre := instr&(1<<24) != 0
	up := instr&(1<<23) != 0
	sBit := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	w := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	load := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	list := uint32(instr & 0xFFFF)
	base := c.R[rn]

	mode := c.Mode()
	transferPC := list&(1<<15) != 0
	switchMode := sBit && (!load || !transferPC) && mode != ModeUSR && mode != ModeSYS

	empty := list == 0
	if empty {
		list = 1 << 15
		transferPC = true
	}
	count := 0
	first := 16
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) != 0 {
			count++
			if first == 16 {
				first = int(i)
			}
		}
	}
	bytes := uint32(count) * 4
	if empty {
		bytes = 0x40
	}
	var wb uint32
	if up {
		wb = base + bytes
	} else {
		wb = base - bytes
	}
	start := blockStart(base, int(bytes/4), pre, up)

	origCPSR := c.CPSR
	if switchMode {
		c.setCPSR(origCPSR&^0x1F | ModeUSR)
	}

	var pcVal uint32
	pcSet := false
	wbApplied := false
	applyWB := func() {
		wbApplied = true
		if rn != 15 {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
	}
	cur := start
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<uint(i)) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if load {
			v := c.Bus.Read(cur, 4)
			if w && i == first {
				// Writeback lands before the destination
				// register is written, so a base register
				// in the list ends with the loaded value.
				applyWB()
			}
			if i == 15 {
				pcVal, pcSet = v, true
			} else {
				c.R[i] = v
			}
		} else {
			var v uint32
			switch {
			case i == 15 && rn == 15 && w && wbApplied:
				v = wb // base is PC and writeback already applied
			case i == 15:
				v = c.R[15] + 4 // STM stores PC as A+12
			default:
				v = c.R[i]
			}
			c.Bus.Write(cur, 4, v)
			if w && i == first {
				// Writeback lands after the first register
				// is stored, so a base register heading the
				// list is stored with its original value.
				applyWB()
			}
		}
		cur += 4
	}

	if switchMode {
		c.setCPSR(origCPSR)
	}
	if load && pcSet {
		if sBit {
			c.setCPSR(c.curSPSR())
		}
		c.branch(pcVal)
		return count + 4
	}
	if w && rn == 15 {
		c.branch(wb)
	}
	if load {
		return count + 2
	}
	return count + 1
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi/arm7tdmi.go ====================

// Package arm7tdmi implements the ARM7TDMI CPU core used by the
// Game Boy Advance: full ARM (ARMv4T) and Thumb instruction sets,
// banked registers for all six exception modes, and cycle counts in
// the ARM7TDMI S/N/I cycle model as published in GBATEK and the
// ARM7TDMI technical reference manual.
//
// The core is written from the published architecture documentation.
// Memory access goes through the Bus interface so the same core runs
// against the GBA system bus and against the transaction-backed
// memory used by the Tom Harte (SingleStepTests) conformance corpus.
package arm7tdmi

// Processor modes, CPSR bits 4-0.
const (
	ModeUSR = 0x10
	ModeFIQ = 0x11
	ModeIRQ = 0x12
	ModeSVC = 0x13
	ModeABT = 0x17
	ModeUND = 0x1B
	ModeSYS = 0x1F
)

// CPSR/SPSR flag bits.
const (
	FlagN = 1 << 31
	FlagZ = 1 << 30
	FlagC = 1 << 29
	FlagV = 1 << 28
	FlagQ = 1 << 27

	BitI = 1 << 7
	BitF = 1 << 6
	BitT = 1 << 5
)

// SPSR slots, in the order the conformance corpus lists them.
const (
	SPSRFIQ = iota
	SPSRSVC
	SPSRABT
	SPSRIRQ
	SPSRUND
	SPSRCount
)

// Bus is the memory interface the CPU executes against. Read and
// Write are data accesses; Fetch is an instruction-stream read.
// Sizes are in bytes: 1, 2 or 4. Read returns the value zero
// extended to 32 bits (the CPU applies rotation and sign extension
// rules itself). Write passes the value in the low bits.
type Bus interface {
	Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32
	Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32)
	Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32
}

// CPU is the complete ARM7TDMI processor state.
//
// R is the register file as seen in the current mode. The banked
// registers of the inactive modes live in the RFIQ/RSVC/RABT/RIRQ/
// RUND/RUSR fields; mode switches swap R8-R14 (and R8-R12 for FIQ)
// between R and the bank fields, so at any moment R plus the bank
// fields together hold every physical register exactly once, with
// one exception: when a mode is active its bank fields are stale
// copies and R is authoritative for that mode.
//
// Pipe holds the two fetched instruction words behind the
// instruction being executed: in ARM state Pipe[0] is the word in
// the decode stage (the next instruction) and Pipe[1] the word in
// the fetch stage; in Thumb state they hold halfwords, zero
// extended. The executing instruction sits at R[15]-8 in ARM state
// and R[15]-4 in Thumb state.
type CPU struct {
	R    [16]uint32
	RFIQ [7]uint32 // R8-R14 of FIQ mode
	RSVC [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of SVC mode
	RABT [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of ABT mode
	RIRQ [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of IRQ mode
	RUND [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of UND mode
	RUSR [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of USR/SYS modes

	CPSR uint32
	SPSR [SPSRCount]uint32

	Pipe [2]uint32

	Bus Bus

	// Halted is set by instructions that stop the core on real
	// hardware paths the GBA never takes out of (unused here; kept
	// in the serialized state for future slices).
	Halted bool

	// IRQLine is the level sensitive interrupt request input.
	// The system drives it from its interrupt controller: while
	// it is set and the CPSR I bit is clear, Step enters the IRQ
	// exception instead of executing the next instruction. It is
	// an external input, not processor state, so it is not
	// serialized.
	IRQLine bool

	// SWIHook, when non-nil, intercepts software interrupts
	// before the SWI exception is taken. It receives the raw SWI
	// comment field (the full 24-bit field in ARM state, the
	// 8-bit field in Thumb state) and reports the cycle count and
	// whether it handled the call. A hook that handles the call
	// is responsible for arranging the continuation, normally by
	// calling Jump with the return address (the SWI address + 4
	// in ARM state, + 2 in Thumb state), or by setting Halted for
	// the calls that wait. It is system wiring, not processor
	// state, so it is not serialized.
	SWIHook func(c *CPU, imm uint32) (int, bool)

	// Executing is the instruction word currently in the execute
	// stage. It is not serialized; it is reloaded from Pipe state
	// on Deserialize via ExecutingValid.
	Executing      uint32
	ExecutingValid bool

	// usr8_12 holds the user bank R8-R12 while FIQ mode is active
	// (they swap with the FIQ bank on mode changes). Serialized.
	usr8_12 [5]uint32

	// flushed marks that the last Step refilled the pipeline, so
	// the normal pipeline advance must be skipped.
	flushed bool

	// spsrDummy absorbs SPSR reads in modes that have no SPSR
	// (USR/SYS); reads there return the CPSR instead and this
	// field is never used. It exists so MSR-to-SPSR in such modes
	// has a harmless sink during development of test code.
	spsrDummy uint32
}

// New returns a CPU in its reset state, bound to bus b.
func New(b Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{Bus: b}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Mode returns the current processor mode bits.
func (c *CPU) Mode() uint32 { return c.CPSR & 0x1F }

// Thumb reports whether the core is in Thumb state.
func (c *CPU) Thumb() bool { return c.CPSR&BitT != 0 }

// Reset puts the CPU in the documented power-on state: SVC mode,
// ARM state, IRQ and FIQ disabled, PC at the reset vector 0x00,
// pipeline refilled from the vector.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	for i := range c.R {
		c.R[i] = 0
	}
	c.RFIQ = [7]uint32{}
	c.RSVC = [2]uint32{}
	c.RABT = [2]uint32{}
	c.RIRQ = [2]uint32{}
	c.RUND = [2]uint32{}
	c.RUSR = [2]uint32{}
	c.SPSR = [SPSRCount]uint32{}
	c.CPSR = ModeSVC | BitI | BitF
	c.usr8_12 = [5]uint32{}
	c.flushed = false
	c.spsrDummy = 0
	c.Halted = false
	c.R[15] = 0
	c.refill(0)
}

// refill loads the pipeline starting at the branch target addr
// and sets R15 so the unit at addr is in the execute position.
// In ARM state the R15 register keeps the target value verbatim
// (no low bits discarded, as the reference behavior shows); in
// Thumb state bit 0 is discarded. Instruction fetches are
// issued at the aligned address either way: word aligned in ARM
// state, halfword aligned in Thumb state.
func (c *CPU) refill(addr uint32) {
	if c.Thumb() {
		fa := addr &^ 1
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch(fa, 2)
		c.Pipe[0] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+2, 2)
		c.Pipe[1] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+4, 2)
		c.R[15] = fa + 4
	} else {
		fa := addr &^ 3
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch(fa, 4)
		c.Pipe[0] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+4, 4)
		c.Pipe[1] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+8, 4)
		c.R[15] = addr + 8
	}
	c.ExecutingValid = true
}

// StateSize is the serialized size of the CPU state in bytes.
const StateSize = (16+7+2+2+2+2+2)*4 + 4 + SPSRCount*4 + 2*4 + 5*4 + 4

// Serialize writes the full CPU state to dst, which must be at
// least StateSize bytes. It returns the number of bytes written.
func (c *CPU) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &stateWriter{b: dst}
	for _, v := range c.R {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RFIQ {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RSVC {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RABT {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RIRQ {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RUND {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RUSR {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.u32(c.CPSR)
	for _, v := range c.SPSR {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.u32(c.Pipe[0])
	w.u32(c.Pipe[1])
	for _, v := range c.usr8_12 {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	var flags uint32
	if c.Halted {
		flags |= 1
	}
	w.u32(flags)
	return w.n
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It reports
// false, leaving the CPU untouched, when src is too short.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < StateSize {
		return false
	}
	r := &stateReader{b: src}
	for i := range c.R {
		c.R[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RFIQ {
		c.RFIQ[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RSVC {
		c.RSVC[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RABT {
		c.RABT[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RIRQ {
		c.RIRQ[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RUND {
		c.RUND[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RUSR {
		c.RUSR[i] = r.u32()
	}
	c.CPSR = r.u32()
	for i := range c.SPSR {
		c.SPSR[i] = r.u32()
	}
	c.Pipe[0] = r.u32()
	c.Pipe[1] = r.u32()
	for i := range c.usr8_12 {
		c.usr8_12[i] = r.u32()
	}
	flags := r.u32()
	c.Halted = flags&1 != 0
	// The executing instruction is the one behind Pipe in the
	// stream: at R15-8 (ARM) or R15-4 (Thumb), the word two units
	// back from the fetch stage. Re-fetch it from the bus so the
	// next Step executes the same instruction the saved core was
	// about to execute.
	if c.Thumb() {
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]-4)&^1, 2)
	} else {
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]-8)&^3, 4)
	}
	c.ExecutingValid = true
	return true
}

type stateWriter struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) {
	w.b[w.n+0] = byte(v)
	w.b[w.n+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	w.b[w.n+2] = byte(v >> 16)
	w.b[w.n+3] = byte(v >> 24)
	w.n += 4
}

type stateReader struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (r *stateReader) u32() uint32 {
	v := uint32(r.b[r.n]) | uint32(r.b[r.n+1])<<8 | uint32(r.b[r.n+2])<<16 | uint32(r.b[r.n+3])<<24
	r.n += 4
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi/conformance_test.go ====================

package arm7tdmi

// The Tom Harte / SingleStepTests ARM7TDMI conformance gate.
//
// The corpus (github.com/SingleStepTests/ARM7TDMI, generated from
// NanoBoyAdvance) ships as binary .json.bin files: a header (magic
// 0xD33DBAE0, test count), then per test an initial state, a final
// state, a transaction list and the opcode with its base address.
// Each state is 40 u32 values: R0-R15, the FIQ bank R8-R14, the
// SVC/ABT/IRQ/UND banked R13-R14 pairs, CPSR, the five SPSRs (fiq,
// svc, abt, irq, und order), two pipeline words, and an access
// field this harness ignores.
//
// The harness installs the initial state, executes one Step
// against a transaction-backed bus, and compares:
//   - R0-R15, CPSR, all five SPSRs;
//   - the banked register storage, verbatim (the corpus dumps the
//     generator's raw bank storage, so the fields compare as
//     stored, not composed through the active mode);
//   - the pipeline as the corpus models it: its pipeline[0] is the
//     executing instruction and pipeline[1] the decode slot, which
//     map to this CPU's Executing and Pipe[0] after the step;
//   - every data read and write, in order: kind, size, address,
//     and the data returned or written.
//
// The corpus does not publish a trustworthy total cycle count
// (its per-transaction cycle field is documented upstream as
// experimental and is not asserted on here), so Step cycle counts
// follow the GBATEK model and are not corpus-compared.
//
// The corpus lives under testroms/tomharte-arm7tdmi in this
// module (gitignored, local evidence only). When it is absent the
// gate skips. Fetch it with:
//
//	git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/SingleStepTests/ARM7TDMI
//	# then copy ARM7TDMI/v1/*.json.bin into testroms/tomharte-arm7tdmi/
//
// The per-file subset size defaults to 2,000 of the 50,000 tests
// (seeded); set GBA_TH_SUBSET=50000 to run everything and
// GBA_TH_SEED to change the seed.

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"math/rand"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"testing"
)

type thState struct {
	R        [16]uint32
	RFIQ     [7]uint32
	RSVC     [2]uint32
	RABT     [2]uint32
	RIRQ     [2]uint32
	RUND     [2]uint32
	CPSR     uint32
	SPSR     [5]uint32
	Pipeline [2]uint32
}

type thTxn struct {
	kind uint32
	size uint32
	addr uint32
	data uint32
}

type thTest struct {
	initial thState
	final   thState
	txns    []thTxn
	opcode  uint32
	base    uint32
}

func parseState(b []byte, off int) thState {
	var s thState
	v := func(i int) uint32 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off+8+i*4:]) }
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		s.R[i] = v(i)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 7; i++ {
		s.RFIQ[i] = v(16 + i)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.RSVC[i] = v(23 + i)
		s.RABT[i] = v(25 + i)
		s.RIRQ[i] = v(27 + i)
		s.RUND[i] = v(29 + i)
	}
	s.CPSR = v(31)
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		s.SPSR[i] = v(32 + i)
	}
	s.Pipeline[0] = v(37)
	s.Pipeline[1] = v(38)
	return s
}

func parseCorpusFile(t *testing.T, path string) []thTest {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(data) < 8 || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data) != 0xD33DBAE0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s: bad magic", path)
	}
	num := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[4:]))
	tests := make([]thTest, 0, num)
	off := 8
	u32 := func(p int) uint32 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[p:]) }
	for i := 0; i < num; i++ {
		recStart := off
		recSize := int(int32(u32(off)))
		off += 4
		var tt thTest
		// Section 1: initial state.
		secSize := int(int32(u32(off)))
		tt.initial = parseState(data, off)
		off += secSize
		// Section 2: final state.
		secSize = int(int32(u32(off)))
		tt.final = parseState(data, off)
		off += secSize
		// Section 3: transactions.
		secSize = int(int32(u32(off)))
		nTxn := int(int32(u32(off + 8)))
		for j := 0; j < nTxn; j++ {
			p := off + 12 + j*24
			tt.txns = append(tt.txns, thTxn{
				kind: u32(p), size: u32(p + 4), addr: u32(p + 8), data: u32(p + 12),
			})
		}
		off += secSize
		// Section 4: opcode and base address.
		tt.opcode = u32(off + 8)
		tt.base = u32(off + 12)
		off += 16
		if off != recStart+recSize {
			t.Fatalf("%s test %d: record walk desync (%d != %d)", path, i, off, recStart+recSize)
		}
		tests = append(tests, tt)
	}
	return tests
}

// corpusBus plays the transaction list back to the CPU.
type corpusBus struct {
	base   uint32
	opcode uint32
	data   []thTxn // kind 1 and 2, in order
	pos    int
	code   []thTxn // kind 0, in order
	codeIx map[[2]uint32]int
	fail   string
}

func newCorpusBus(tt *thTest) *corpusBus {
	b := &corpusBus{base: tt.base, opcode: tt.opcode, codeIx: map[[2]uint32]int{}}
	for _, x := range tt.txns {
		switch x.kind {
		case 1, 2:
			b.data = append(b.data, x)
		case 0:
			// The same address can be fetched at two sizes
			// (a sequential Thumb fetch and a refill word
			// fetch after a state switch); index by both.
			key := [2]uint32{x.addr, x.size}
			if _, dup := b.codeIx[key]; !dup {
				b.codeIx[key] = len(b.code)
			}
			b.code = append(b.code, x)
		}
	}
	return b
}

func (b *corpusBus) setFail(format string, args ...interface{}) {
	if b.fail == "" {
		b.fail = fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
	}
}

func (b *corpusBus) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if b.pos >= len(b.data) {
		b.setFail("unexpected data read addr=%08x size=%d (no transactions left)", addr, size)
		return 0
	}
	x := b.data[b.pos]
	b.pos++
	if x.kind != 1 || x.addr != addr || x.size != uint32(size) {
		b.setFail("data read #%d: cpu read kind=%d addr=%08x size=%d, corpus has kind=%d addr=%08x size=%d",
			b.pos-1, 1, addr, size, x.kind, x.addr, x.size)
	}
	return x.data
}

func (b *corpusBus) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if b.pos >= len(b.data) {
		b.setFail("unexpected data write addr=%08x size=%d val=%08x (no transactions left)", addr, size, val)
		return
	}
	x := b.data[b.pos]
	b.pos++
	if x.kind != 2 || x.addr != addr || x.size != uint32(size) || x.data != val {
		b.setFail("data write #%d: cpu wrote addr=%08x size=%d val=%08x, corpus has kind=%d addr=%08x size=%d data=%08x",
			b.pos-1, addr, size, val, x.kind, x.addr, x.size, x.data)
	}
}

func (b *corpusBus) Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if addr == b.base {
		return b.opcode
	}
	if ix, ok := b.codeIx[[2]uint32{addr, uint32(size)}]; ok {
		return b.code[ix].data
	}
	// Fall back to any fetch recorded at this address.
	for _, x := range b.code {
		if x.addr == addr {
			return x.data
		}
	}
	if size == 2 {
		return addr & 0xFFFF
	}
	return addr
}

func loadState(c *CPU, s *thState, tt *thTest, bus *corpusBus) {
	// The corpus dumps raw bank storage with no swapping: its R
	// array is the user-bank view (R8-R14 as USR sees them) and
	// each mode's banked registers sit in their own arrays, even
	// for the active mode. This CPU keeps the active view in R
	// and swaps banks on mode changes, so loading composes the
	// active registers from the bank arrays of the initial mode,
	// while the bank fields themselves are loaded verbatim.
	mode := s.CPSR & 0x1F
	c.R = s.R
	c.RFIQ = s.RFIQ
	c.RSVC = s.RSVC
	c.RABT = s.RABT
	c.RIRQ = s.RIRQ
	c.RUND = s.RUND
	c.RUSR = [2]uint32{s.R[13], s.R[14]}
	c.usr8_12 = [5]uint32{}
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(c.usr8_12[:], s.R[8:13])
		copy(c.R[8:13], s.RFIQ[0:5])
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RFIQ[5], s.RFIQ[6]
	case ModeSVC:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RSVC[0], s.RSVC[1]
	case ModeABT:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RABT[0], s.RABT[1]
	case ModeIRQ:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RIRQ[0], s.RIRQ[1]
	case ModeUND:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RUND[0], s.RUND[1]
	}
	c.CPSR = s.CPSR
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		c.SPSR[i] = s.SPSR[i]
	}
	c.Executing = tt.opcode
	c.ExecutingValid = true
	c.Pipe[0] = s.Pipeline[1]
	// The fetch-stage slot holds the word the step's own code
	// transaction at the initial R15 returns; when the corpus has
	// no such transaction (control flow refills anyway), fall
	// back to the final pipeline value, which that slot feeds.
	c.Pipe[1] = tt.final.Pipeline[1]
	for _, x := range tt.txns {
		if x.kind == 0 && x.addr == s.R[15] {
			c.Pipe[1] = x.data
			break
		}
	}
	c.Halted = false
	c.flushed = false
}

// composedViews translates the CPU's swap-based state back into
// the corpus's raw bank storage layout, keyed by the final mode:
// the view array shows the user bank, and each bank array shows
// that mode's own registers (taken from the live R view when that
// mode is the active one).
func composedViews(c *CPU) (view [16]uint32, fiq [7]uint32, svc, abt, irq, und [2]uint32) {
	view = c.R
	fiq = c.RFIQ
	svc = c.RSVC
	abt = c.RABT
	irq = c.RIRQ
	und = c.RUND
	switch c.Mode() {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(view[8:13], c.usr8_12[:])
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		copy(fiq[0:5], c.R[8:13])
		fiq[5], fiq[6] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeSVC:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		svc[0], svc[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeABT:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		abt[0], abt[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeIRQ:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		irq[0], irq[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeUND:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		und[0], und[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	}
	return
}

func diffState(c *CPU, tt *thTest, bus *corpusBus) []string {
	var diffs []string
	f := &tt.final
	view, fiq, svc, abt, irq, und := composedViews(c)
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if view[i] != f.R[i] {
			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("R%d: got %08x want %08x", i, view[i], f.R[i]))
		}
	}
	if c.CPSR != f.CPSR {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("CPSR: got %08x want %08x", c.CPSR, f.CPSR))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		if c.SPSR[i] != f.SPSR[i] {
			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("SPSR[%d]: got %08x want %08x", i, c.SPSR[i], f.SPSR[i]))
		}
	}
	banks := []struct {
		name string
		got  []uint32
		want []uint32
	}{
		{"R_fiq", fiq[:], f.RFIQ[:]},
		{"R_svc", svc[:], f.RSVC[:]},
		{"R_abt", abt[:], f.RABT[:]},
		{"R_irq", irq[:], f.RIRQ[:]},
		{"R_und", und[:], f.RUND[:]},
	}
	for _, bk := range banks {
		for i := range bk.got {
			if bk.got[i] != bk.want[i] {
				diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("%s[%d]: got %08x want %08x", bk.name, i, bk.got[i], bk.want[i]))
			}
		}
	}
	if c.Executing != f.Pipeline[0] {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("pipeline[0]: got %08x want %08x", c.Executing, f.Pipeline[0]))
	}
	if c.Pipe[0] != f.Pipeline[1] {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("pipeline[1]: got %08x want %08x", c.Pipe[0], f.Pipeline[1]))
	}
	if bus.fail != "" {
		diffs = append(diffs, "bus: "+bus.fail)
	}
	if bus.pos != len(bus.data) {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("bus: consumed %d of %d data transactions", bus.pos, len(bus.data)))
	}
	return diffs
}

func corpusDir(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "testroms", "tomharte-arm7tdmi")
	if st, err := os.Stat(dir); err != nil || !st.IsDir() {
		t.Skipf("corpus not present at %s", dir)
	}
	return dir
}

func TestTomHarteARM7TDMI(t *testing.T) {
	dir := corpusDir(t)
	files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, "*.json.bin"))
	if err != nil || len(files) == 0 {
		t.Skip("no corpus files")
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	subset := 2000
	if v := os.Getenv("GBA_TH_SUBSET"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &subset)
	}
	seed := int64(0xA7D1)
	if v := os.Getenv("GBA_TH_SEED"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &seed)
	}
	totalRun, totalFail := 0, 0
	for _, path := range files {
		path := path
		name := filepath.Base(path)
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			tests := parseCorpusFile(t, path)
			rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed + int64(len(name))))
			idx := rng.Perm(len(tests))
			if subset < len(idx) {
				idx = idx[:subset]
			}
			fails := 0
			for _, ix := range idx {
				tt := &tests[ix]
				bus := newCorpusBus(tt)
				cpu := &CPU{Bus: bus}
				loadState(cpu, &tt.initial, tt, bus)
				cpu.Step()
				if diffs := diffState(cpu, tt, bus); len(diffs) > 0 {
					fails++
					if fails <= 3 {
						t.Logf("test %d opcode=%08x base=%08x: %v", ix, tt.opcode, tt.base, diffs)
					}
				}
			}
			totalRun += len(idx)
			totalFail += fails
			t.Logf("%s: %d/%d passed", name, len(idx)-fails, len(idx))
			if fails > 0 {
				t.Errorf("%s: %d of %d tests failed", name, fails, len(idx))
			}
		})
	}
	t.Logf("TOTAL: %d/%d passed", totalRun-totalFail, totalRun)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi/exec.go ====================

package arm7tdmi

// Step executes exactly one instruction and returns the number of
// bus cycles it consumed in the ARM7TDMI cycle model.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	// A pending IRQ is taken at the instruction boundary,
	// before the instruction in the execute stage runs, and
	// also while the core is halted: an accepted interrupt
	// is what ends a halt on hardware, so the entry clears
	// Halted and the IRQ handler code actually runs. That
	// matters beyond the halt itself: a BIOS wait (Halt,
	// IntrWait) completes through the BIOS dispatcher, and
	// the dispatcher is IRQ handler code, so leaving
	// Halted set here would freeze the core inside the
	// exception entry with the dispatcher unreachable and
	// the wait undecidable (found by the Anguna gate: the
	// game sat halted in IRQ mode at the vector forever).
	// The link value follows the exception convention: it
	// is the address of the instruction that was about to
	// execute, plus 4, so the handler returns with SUBS PC,
	// LR, #4 to exactly that instruction.
	if c.IRQLine && c.CPSR&BitI == 0 {
		c.Halted = false
		if c.Thumb() {
			return c.exception(0x18, ModeIRQ, c.R[15])
		}
		return c.exception(0x18, ModeIRQ, c.R[15]-4)
	}
	if c.Halted {
		return 1
	}
	instr := c.Executing
	c.flushed = false
	state := c.Thumb()
	var n int
	if state {
		n = c.execThumb(uint16(instr))
	} else {
		n = c.execARM(instr)
	}
	if !c.flushed {
		// The pipeline advances in the state the instruction
		// was fetched in, even if the instruction rewrote the
		// CPSR T bit (an MSR may do that in the reference
		// implementation without disturbing this step).
		c.advance(state)
	}
	return n
}

// advance moves the pipeline one instruction unit forward without
// a control-flow change: the decode-stage unit enters execute and
// a new unit is fetched at the fetch-stage address.
func (c *CPU) advance(thumb bool) {
	if thumb {
		nf := c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]&^1)+2, 2)
		c.Executing = c.Pipe[0]
		c.Pipe[0] = c.Pipe[1]
		c.Pipe[1] = nf
		c.R[15] += 2
		c.ExecutingValid = true
		return
	}
	nf := c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]&^3)+4, 4)
	c.Executing = c.Pipe[0]
	c.Pipe[0] = c.Pipe[1]
	c.Pipe[1] = nf
	c.R[15] += 4
	c.ExecutingValid = true
}

// branch refills the pipeline at addr in the state the CPU is in
// after any CPSR change the instruction already made. Alignment
// is applied inside refill.
func (c *CPU) branch(addr uint32) {
	c.refill(addr)
	c.flushed = true
}

// Jump moves execution to addr, refilling the pipeline there.
// It exists for the system layer and the SWI hook: a handled
// software interrupt completes by jumping to its return
// address, and the BIOS wait routines resume the same way.
func (c *CPU) Jump(addr uint32) {
	c.branch(addr)
}

// condPassed evaluates an ARM condition field against the CPSR
// flags. Condition 0xF (NV) never passes on ARMv4.
func (c *CPU) condPassed(cond uint32) bool {
	n := c.CPSR&FlagN != 0
	z := c.CPSR&FlagZ != 0
	cf := c.CPSR&FlagC != 0
	v := c.CPSR&FlagV != 0
	switch cond {
	case 0x0:
		return z
	case 0x1:
		return !z
	case 0x2:
		return cf
	case 0x3:
		return !cf
	case 0x4:
		return n
	case 0x5:
		return !n
	case 0x6:
		return v
	case 0x7:
		return !v
	case 0x8:
		return cf && !z
	case 0x9:
		return !cf || z
	case 0xA:
		return n == v
	case 0xB:
		return n != v
	case 0xC:
		return !z && n == v
	case 0xD:
		return z || n != v
	case 0xE:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func (c *CPU) setNZ(v uint32) {
	c.CPSR &^= FlagN | FlagZ
	if v&0x80000000 != 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagN
	}
	if v == 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagZ
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setNZC(v uint32, carry bool) {
	c.setNZ(v)
	c.setCarry(carry)
}

func (c *CPU) setCarry(carry bool) {
	c.CPSR &^= FlagC
	if carry {
		c.CPSR |= FlagC
	}
}

// memReg reads a register in a memory-operand position, where
// R15 reads as A+12 (the pipeline value plus one unit). Used for
// swap addressing and operands, and for stored PC values.
func (c *CPU) memReg(i uint32) uint32 {
	if i == 15 {
		return c.R[15] + 4
	}
	return c.R[i]
}

// tickMultiply reports whether the ARM7TDMI multiplier runs the
// full four beats for the given multiplier operand, with no
// early termination. Termination happens when the remaining
// high bytes of the multiplier are all zero, or (for signed
// multiplies) all ones.
func tickMultiply(signed bool, multiplier uint32) bool {
	mask := uint32(0xFFFFFF00)
	for {
		multiplier &= mask
		if multiplier == 0 {
			break
		}
		if signed && multiplier == mask {
			break
		}
		mask <<= 8
	}
	return mask == 0
}

// mulCarry computes the C flag a multiply leaves behind in the
// reference implementation. On the silicon the flag is the
// carry out of the booth multiplier's carry-save adder tree;
// the routines below model that adder. (Booth carry model
// after the published work of zaydlang and calc84maniac on the
// ARM7TDMI multiplier, as also used by NanoBoyAdvance, the
// corpus generator.) An early-terminated multiply takes the
// low-word carry; a full-length one takes the final injected
// booth carry bit for the short forms and the high-word carry
// for the long forms.
func mulCarry(full bool, isLong bool, signExtend bool, multiplicand, multiplier, accumLo, accumHi uint32) bool {
	if full {
		if isLong {
			return mulCarryHi(signExtend, multiplicand, multiplier, accumHi)
		}
		return (multiplier>>30)&3 == 2
	}
	return mulCarryLo(multiplicand, multiplier, accumLo)
}

// mulCarryLo models the carry out of the multiplier's
// carry-save adder for the low result word, processing the
// multiplier in radix-4 booth steps exactly as the hardware
// accumulates it.
func mulCarryLo(multiplicand, multiplier, accum uint32) bool {
	// Setting the low bit of the multiplicand makes negation
	// invert the upper bits; the bit cannot reach the carry.
	multiplicand |= 1

	booth := uint32(int32(multiplier<<31) >> 31)
	carry := multiplicand * booth
	sum := carry + accum

	shift := 29
	for {
		// Four booth iterations cover 8 multiplier bits.
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			nextBooth := uint32(int32(multiplier<<uint(shift)) >> uint(shift))
			factor := nextBooth - booth
			booth = nextBooth
			addend := multiplicand * factor
			// Carry-save accumulation.
			newAccum := accum ^ carry ^ addend
			sum += addend
			carry = sum - newAccum
			accum = newAccum
			shift -= 2
		}
		if booth == multiplier {
			break
		}
	}
	return carry>>31 != 0
}

// mulCarryHi models the carry out of the high result word of a
// long multiply. Only the last three booth iterations can
// influence it, so both operands are reduced to the relevant
// high bits and the carry is propagated through magic marker
// bits, following the published model.
func mulCarryHi(signExtend bool, multiplicand, multiplier, accumHi uint32) bool {
	if signExtend {
		multiplicand = uint32(int32(multiplicand) >> 6)
		multiplier = uint32(int32(multiplier) >> 26)
	} else {
		multiplicand >>= 6
		multiplier >>= 26
	}
	multiplicand |= 1

	carry := ^accumHi & 0x20000000
	accum := accumHi - 0x08000000

	booth0 := uint32(int32(multiplier<<27) >> 27)
	booth1 := uint32(int32(multiplier<<29) >> 29)
	booth2 := uint32(int32(multiplier<<31) >> 31)
	factor0 := multiplier - booth0
	factor1 := booth0 - booth1
	factor2 := booth1 - booth2

	addend := multiplicand * factor2
	accum -= addend & 0x10000000
	addend = multiplicand * factor1
	accum -= addend & 0x40000000

	sum := accum + (addend & 0x20000000)
	accum -= carry

	addend = multiplicand * factor0
	sum += addend & 0x40000000

	return (sum^accum)>>31 != 0
}

func (c *CPU) carry() bool { return c.CPSR&FlagC != 0 }

// addFlags computes a+b+carryIn and sets N, Z, C, V.
func (c *CPU) addFlags(a, b uint32, carryIn bool) uint32 {
	var ci uint64
	if carryIn {
		ci = 1
	}
	sum := uint64(a) + uint64(b) + ci
	res := uint32(sum)
	c.setNZ(res)
	c.CPSR &^= FlagC | FlagV
	if sum > 0xFFFFFFFF {
		c.CPSR |= FlagC
	}
	if (a^res)&(b^res)&0x80000000 != 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagV
	}
	return res
}

// subFlags computes a-b-(1-carryIn) and sets N, Z, C, V, with C
// meaning NOT borrow, as ARM defines it.
func (c *CPU) subFlags(a, b uint32, carryIn bool) uint32 {
	var ci uint64 = 1
	if carryIn {
		ci = 0
	}
	diff := uint64(a) - uint64(b) - ci
	res := uint32(diff)
	c.setNZ(res)
	c.CPSR &^= FlagC | FlagV
	if uint64(a) >= uint64(b)+ci {
		c.CPSR |= FlagC
	}
	if (a^b)&(a^res)&0x80000000 != 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagV
	}
	return res
}

func ror32(v uint32, n uint) uint32 {
	n &= 31
	if n == 0 {
		return v
	}
	return v>>n | v<<(32-n)
}

// shifter runs the ARM barrel shifter for data-processing operand
// 2 in register form. rmVal is the value of Rm (already PC-quirk
// adjusted by the caller), typ is the shift type (0 LSL, 1 LSR,
// 2 ASR, 3 ROR), amount is the shift amount, and byReg reports a
// register-specified shift (amount is Rs&0xFF, encoded cases
// differ). It returns the shifted value and the shifter carry
// out.
func (c *CPU) shifter(rmVal uint32, typ uint32, amount uint32, byReg bool) (uint32, bool) {
	oldC := c.carry()
	if byReg {
		if amount == 0 {
			return rmVal, oldC
		}
		switch typ {
		case 0: // LSL
			if amount < 32 {
				return rmVal << amount, (rmVal>>(32-amount))&1 != 0
			}
			if amount == 32 {
				return 0, rmVal&1 != 0
			}
			return 0, false
		case 1: // LSR
			if amount < 32 {
				return rmVal >> amount, (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
			}
			if amount == 32 {
				return 0, rmVal>>31 != 0
			}
			return 0, false
		case 2: // ASR
			if amount >= 32 {
				if rmVal>>31 != 0 {
					return 0xFFFFFFFF, true
				}
				return 0, false
			}
			return uint32(int32(rmVal) >> amount), (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
		case 3: // ROR
			m := amount & 31
			if m == 0 {
				return rmVal, rmVal>>31 != 0
			}
			return ror32(rmVal, uint(m)), (rmVal>>(m-1))&1 != 0
		}
	}
	// Immediate shift amounts: 0 is special per type.
	switch typ {
	case 0: // LSL #0
		if amount == 0 {
			return rmVal, oldC
		}
		return rmVal << amount, (rmVal>>(32-amount))&1 != 0
	case 1: // LSR #0 means LSR #32
		if amount == 0 {
			return 0, rmVal>>31 != 0
		}
		return rmVal >> amount, (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
	case 2: // ASR #0 means ASR #32
		if amount == 0 {
			if rmVal>>31 != 0 {
				return 0xFFFFFFFF, true
			}
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint32(int32(rmVal) >> amount), (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
	case 3: // ROR #0 means RRX
		if amount == 0 {
			res := rmVal >> 1
			if oldC {
				res |= 0x80000000
			}
			return res, rmVal&1 != 0
		}
		return ror32(rmVal, uint(amount)), (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
	}
	return rmVal, oldC
}

// spsrIndex maps a mode to its SPSR slot, or -1 when the mode has
// no SPSR (USR and SYS).
func spsrIndex(mode uint32) int {
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		return SPSRFIQ
	case ModeSVC:
		return SPSRSVC
	case ModeABT:
		return SPSRABT
	case ModeIRQ:
		return SPSRIRQ
	case ModeUND:
		return SPSRUND
	}
	return -1
}

// curSPSR returns the SPSR of the current mode. In modes without
// an SPSR it returns the CPSR, the value MRS SPSR observes on the
// hardware paths the corpus exercises.
func (c *CPU) curSPSR() uint32 {
	if idx := spsrIndex(c.Mode()); idx >= 0 {
		return c.SPSR[idx]
	}
	return c.CPSR
}

// storeBank parks the R8-R14 values of the given (outgoing) mode
// into its bank fields, restoring the neutral user R8-R12 view
// after a FIQ exit.
func (c *CPU) storeBank(mode uint32) {
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(c.RFIQ[0:5], c.R[8:13])
		c.RFIQ[5] = c.R[13]
		c.RFIQ[6] = c.R[14]
		copy(c.R[8:13], c.usr8_12[0:5])
	case ModeSVC:
		c.RSVC[0], c.RSVC[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeABT:
		c.RABT[0], c.RABT[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeIRQ:
		c.RIRQ[0], c.RIRQ[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeUND:
		c.RUND[0], c.RUND[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	default: // USR, SYS
		c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	}
}

// loadBank brings the R8-R14 values of the given (incoming) mode
// into the live register view.
func (c *CPU) loadBank(mode uint32) {
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(c.usr8_12[0:5], c.R[8:13])
		copy(c.R[8:13], c.RFIQ[0:5])
		c.R[13] = c.RFIQ[5]
		c.R[14] = c.RFIQ[6]
	case ModeSVC:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RSVC[0], c.RSVC[1]
	case ModeABT:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RABT[0], c.RABT[1]
	case ModeIRQ:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RIRQ[0], c.RIRQ[1]
	case ModeUND:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RUND[0], c.RUND[1]
	default:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
	}
}

// setCPSR writes the CPSR, swapping register banks when the mode
// bits change.
func (c *CPU) setCPSR(v uint32) {
	oldMode := c.Mode()
	newMode := v & 0x1F
	if oldMode != newMode {
		c.storeBank(oldMode)
		c.loadBank(newMode)
	}
	c.CPSR = v
}

// msr writes val into the fields of the CPSR or the current SPSR
// selected by fieldMask (bit0 c, bit1 x, bit2 s, bit3 f, from the
// instruction's mask field). CPSR control-field (c) writes
// require a privileged mode.
func (c *CPU) msr(toSPSR bool, fieldMask uint32, val uint32) {
	// Field write mask. In user mode only the flag field of the
	// CPSR is writable; the s, x and c fields require privilege.
	// A CPSR control-field write preserves bit 4 of the mode
	// field (only bits 3-0 of the mode are writable) in the
	// reference implementation, while an SPSR control-field
	// write takes bit 4 from the operand; even the T bit is
	// stored from the operand.
	priv := c.Mode() != ModeUSR
	var m uint32
	if fieldMask&8 != 0 {
		m |= 0xFF000000
	}
	if fieldMask&4 != 0 && (toSPSR || priv) {
		m |= 0x00FF0000
	}
	if fieldMask&2 != 0 && (toSPSR || priv) {
		m |= 0x0000FF00
	}
	if fieldMask&1 != 0 && toSPSR {
		m |= 0x000000FF
	}
	if fieldMask&1 != 0 && !toSPSR && priv {
		m |= 0x000000EF
	}
	if toSPSR {
		idx := spsrIndex(c.Mode())
		if idx < 0 {
			c.spsrDummy = val
			return
		}
		cur := c.SPSR[idx]
		c.SPSR[idx] = cur&^m | val&m
		return
	}
	nv := c.CPSR&^m | val&m
	c.setCPSR(nv)
}

// exception enters an exception mode: SPSR of the new mode saves
// the old CPSR, the mode switches with I set (and F set for FIQ),
// LR of the new mode receives lr, and the pipeline refills at the
// vector. Entry costs 2S+1N = 3 cycles.
func (c *CPU) exception(vector uint32, mode uint32, lr uint32) int {
	if idx := spsrIndex(mode); idx >= 0 {
		c.SPSR[idx] = c.CPSR
	}
	nc := c.CPSR&^0x1F | mode
	nc &^= BitT
	nc |= BitI
	if mode == ModeFIQ {
		nc |= BitF
	}
	c.setCPSR(nc)
	c.R[14] = lr
	c.branch(vector)
	return 3
}

// undefined raises the undefined-instruction exception for the
// instruction at addr (the executing address).
func (c *CPU) undefined(addr uint32) int {
	if c.Thumb() {
		return c.exception(0x04, ModeUND, addr+2)
	}
	return c.exception(0x04, ModeUND, addr+4)
}

// userReg reads register n of the user bank (for the S-bit block
// transfer forms), independent of the current mode.
func (c *CPU) userReg(n uint32) uint32 {
	switch {
	case n < 8:
		return c.R[n]
	case n < 13:
		if c.Mode() == ModeFIQ {
			return c.usr8_12[n-8]
		}
		return c.R[n]
	case n < 15:
		if c.Mode() == ModeUSR || c.Mode() == ModeSYS {
			return c.R[n]
		}
		return c.RUSR[n-13]
	}
	return c.R[15]
}

// userSet writes register n of the user bank.
func (c *CPU) userSet(n uint32, v uint32) {
	switch {
	case n < 8:
		c.R[n] = v
	case n < 13:
		if c.Mode() == ModeFIQ {
			c.usr8_12[n-8] = v
		} else {
			c.R[n] = v
		}
	case n < 15:
		if c.Mode() == ModeUSR || c.Mode() == ModeSYS {
			c.R[n] = v
		} else {
			c.RUSR[n-13] = v
		}
	}
}

// load performs a data load of the given size in bytes. The bus
// returns the raw aligned unit containing addr; the CPU applies
// the ARM alignment rotation: word loads rotate right by the
// byte offset, and a halfword load from an odd address rotates
// the zero-extended halfword right by 8 (the reference behavior,
// which also feeds the signed forms).
func (c *CPU) load(addr uint32, size int, signed bool) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		v := c.Bus.Read(addr, 1)
		if signed {
			return uint32(int32(int8(v)))
		}
		return v
	case 2:
		v := c.Bus.Read(addr, 2)
		if signed && addr&1 != 0 {
			// A misaligned signed halfword load returns the
			// sign-extended byte at addr (the high byte of
			// the aligned halfword read).
			return uint32(int32(int8(v >> 8)))
		}
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			v = ror32(v, 8)
		}
		if signed {
			return uint32(int32(int16(v)))
		}
		return v
	default:
		return ror32(c.Bus.Read(addr, 4), uint((addr&3)*8))
	}
}

// store performs a data store of the given size in bytes,
// masking the value to the transfer width.
func (c *CPU) store(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		val &= 0xFF
	case 2:
		val &= 0xFFFF
	}
	c.Bus.Write(addr, size, val)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi/halt_test.go ====================

package arm7tdmi

import "testing"

// ramBus is a flat word-addressed RAM stub for the halt
// tests: 64 KB at address 0, everything else reads zero.
type ramBus struct {
	mem [0x10000]byte
}

func (b *ramBus) get(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		a := addr + uint32(i)
		if a < uint32(len(b.mem)) {
			v |= uint32(b.mem[a]) << (8 * i)
		}
	}
	return v
}

func (b *ramBus) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32  { return b.get(addr, size) }
func (b *ramBus) Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32 { return b.get(addr, size) }
func (b *ramBus) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		a := addr + uint32(i)
		if a < uint32(len(b.mem)) {
			b.mem[a] = byte(val >> (8 * i))
		}
	}
}

func put32(b *ramBus, addr, w uint32) {
	b.mem[addr] = byte(w)
	b.mem[addr+1] = byte(w >> 8)
	b.mem[addr+2] = byte(w >> 16)
	b.mem[addr+3] = byte(w >> 24)
}

// TestHaltedCPUTakesIRQ pins the wake rule the BIOS waits
// depend on: an accepted interrupt ends a halt, the IRQ
// exception is entered, handler code runs, and its
// SUBS PC, LR, #4 return resumes the interrupted
// instruction. Before this was pinned, Step took the
// exception but left Halted set, so the core froze
// inside the exception entry and no handler ever ran
// (the Anguna deadlock).
func TestHaltedCPUTakesIRQ(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &ramBus{}
	// IRQ vector at 0x18: branch to the handler at 0x100.
	put32(bus, 0x18, 0xEA000038) // B 0x100
	// Handler: count the call in R1, return.
	put32(bus, 0x100, 0xE2811001) // ADD R1, R1, #1
	put32(bus, 0x104, 0xE25EF004) // SUBS PC, LR, #4
	// Main at 0x200: one real instruction, then a branch
	// to self that the interrupt lands in front of.
	put32(bus, 0x200, 0xE3A00055) // MOV R0, #0x55
	put32(bus, 0x204, 0xEAFFFFFE) // B .

	c := New(bus)
	c.setCPSR(ModeUSR)
	c.Jump(0x200)
	c.Step() // MOV executes; the branch sits in execute.
	if got := c.R[0]; got != 0x55 {
		t.Fatalf("R0 = %#08x, want 0x55 (MOV did not run)", got)
	}
	// A halted core with no interrupt request stays put.
	c.Halted = true
	if n := c.Step(); n != 1 || !c.Halted {
		t.Fatalf("halted step without IRQ: cycles %d, halted %v, want 1 and still halted", n, c.Halted)
	}
	// The interrupt arrives: the core must wake into the
	// IRQ exception, not freeze inside the entry.
	c.IRQLine = true
	c.Step()
	if c.Halted {
		t.Fatal("accepted IRQ left the core halted; the handler can never run")
	}
	if mode := c.CPSR & 0x1F; mode != ModeIRQ {
		t.Fatalf("mode after IRQ entry = %#02x, want IRQ (%#02x)", mode, ModeIRQ)
	}
	if got := c.R[15] - 8; got != 0x18 {
		t.Fatalf("executing address after IRQ entry = %#08x, want the vector 0x18", got)
	}
	c.Step() // vector branch
	c.Step() // handler ADD
	if got := c.R[1]; got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("handler ran %d times, want 1", got)
	}
	c.Step() // SUBS return
	if mode := c.CPSR & 0x1F; mode != ModeUSR {
		t.Fatalf("mode after handler return = %#02x, want USR (%#02x)", mode, ModeUSR)
	}
	if got := c.R[15] - 8; got != 0x204 {
		t.Fatalf("resumed at %#08x, want the interrupted instruction 0x204", got)
	}
	c.IRQLine = false
	c.Step() // the interrupted branch finally executes
	if got := c.R[15] - 8; got != 0x204 {
		t.Fatalf("after resume the branch at 0x204 should loop to itself, executing %#08x", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi/thumb.go ====================

package arm7tdmi

// execThumb executes one Thumb-state instruction (the halfword in
// the execute stage, located at R15-4) and returns its cycle
// count.
func (c *CPU) execThumb(op uint16) int {
	addr := c.R[15] - 4

	switch {
	// Format 1 and 2: shifts by immediate, add/subtract.
	case op>>13 == 0 && (op>>11)&3 != 3:
		typ := uint32((op >> 11) & 3)
		amt := uint32((op >> 6) & 0x1F)
		rs := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		res, carry := c.shifter(rs, typ, amt, false)
		c.R[op&7] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 1
	case op>>13 == 0:
		// Format 2: ADD/SUB register or 3-bit immediate. The
		// first operand is the register in bits 5-3; the second
		// operand (a register or the immediate) is in bits 8-6.
		sub := op&(1<<9) != 0
		a := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		var b uint32
		if op&(1<<10) != 0 {
			b = uint32((op >> 6) & 7)
		} else {
			b = c.R[(op>>6)&7]
		}
		var res uint32
		if sub {
			res = c.subFlags(a, b, true)
		} else {
			res = c.addFlags(a, b, false)
		}
		c.R[op&7] = res
		return 1

	// Format 3: move/compare/add/subtract immediate.
	case op>>13 == 1:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		imm := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		switch (op >> 11) & 3 {
		case 0: // MOV
			c.R[rd] = imm
			c.setNZ(imm)
		case 1: // CMP
			c.subFlags(c.R[rd], imm, true)
		case 2: // ADD
			c.R[rd] = c.addFlags(c.R[rd], imm, false)
		case 3: // SUB
			c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(c.R[rd], imm, true)
		}
		return 1

	// Format 4: ALU operations.
	case op>>12 == 4 && (op>>11)&1 == 0 && (op>>10)&1 == 0:
		return c.execThumbALU(op)

	// Format 5: high-register operations and BX.
	case op>>12 == 4 && (op>>11)&1 == 0:
		operation := (op >> 8) & 3
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		rs := uint32((op >> 3) & 7)
		if op&(1<<7) != 0 {
			rd += 8
		}
		if op&(1<<6) != 0 {
			rs += 8
		}
		switch operation {
		case 0: // ADD
			res := c.R[rd] + c.R[rs]
			if rd == 15 {
				c.branch(res)
				return 3
			}
			c.R[rd] = res
		case 1: // CMP
			c.subFlags(c.R[rd], c.R[rs], true)
		case 2: // MOV
			if rd == 15 {
				c.branch(c.R[rs])
				return 3
			}
			c.R[rd] = c.R[rs]
		case 3: // BX (the bit-7 BLX register encoding does not
			// exist on ARM7TDMI; the reference implementation
			// executes it as a plain BX with no LR write)
			v := c.R[rs]
			if v&1 != 0 {
				c.CPSR |= BitT
			} else {
				c.CPSR &^= BitT
			}
			c.branch(v &^ 1)
			return 3
		}
		return 1

	// Format 6: PC-relative load.
	case op>>11 == 0b01001:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		base := c.R[15] &^ 2
		v := c.load(base+uint32(op&0xFF)*4, 4, false)
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 3

	// Formats 7 and 8: load/store with register offset.
	case op>>12 == 5:
		rn := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		ea := rn + c.R[(op>>6)&7]
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		if op&(1<<9) == 0 {
			// Format 7, keyed by bits 11-10 (L, B).
			switch (op >> 10) & 3 {
			case 0:
				c.store(ea, 4, c.R[rd])
			case 1:
				c.store(ea, 1, c.R[rd])
			case 2:
				c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 4, false)
				return 3
			case 3:
				c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 1, false)
				return 3
			}
			return 2
		}
		// Format 8, keyed by bits 11-9.
		switch (op >> 9) & 7 {
		case 1:
			c.store(ea, 2, c.R[rd])
			return 2
		case 3:
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 1, true)
		case 5:
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 2, false)
		case 7:
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 2, true)
		}
		return 3

	// Format 9: load/store with immediate offset.
	case op>>13 == 3:
		imm := uint32((op >> 6) & 0x1F)
		rn := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		load := op&(1<<11) != 0
		if op&(1<<12) != 0 { // byte
			ea := rn + imm
			if load {
				c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 1, false)
				return 3
			}
			c.store(ea, 1, c.R[rd])
			return 2
		}
		ea := rn + imm*4
		if load {
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 4, false)
			return 3
		}
		c.store(ea, 4, c.R[rd])
		return 2

	// Format 10: halfword load/store with immediate offset.
	case op>>12 == 8:
		imm := uint32((op>>6)&0x1F) * 2
		ea := c.R[(op>>3)&7] + imm
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 2, false)
			return 3
		}
		c.store(ea, 2, c.R[rd])
		return 2

	// Format 11: SP-relative load/store.
	case op>>12 == 9:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		ea := c.R[13] + uint32(op&0xFF)*4
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 4, false)
			return 3
		}
		c.store(ea, 4, c.R[rd])
		return 2

	// Format 12: load address.
	case op>>12 == 10:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		var base uint32
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			base = c.R[13]
		} else {
			base = c.R[15] &^ 2
		}
		c.R[rd] = base + uint32(op&0xFF)*4
		return 1

	// Format 13: add offset to stack pointer.
	case op&0xFF00 == 0xB000:
		imm := uint32(op&0x7F) * 4
		if op&(1<<7) != 0 {
			c.R[13] -= imm
		} else {
			c.R[13] += imm
		}
		return 1

	// Format 14: push and pop.
	case op&0xFE00 == 0xB400:
		list := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		if op&(1<<8) != 0 {
			list |= 1 << 14
		}
		return c.thumbPush(list)
	case op&0xFE00 == 0xBC00:
		list := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		if op&(1<<8) != 0 {
			list |= 1 << 15
		}
		return c.thumbPop(list)

	// Format 16: multiple load/store.
	case op>>12 == 12:
		rn := uint32((op >> 8) & 7)
		list := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			return c.thumbBlock(rn, list, true)
		}
		return c.thumbBlock(rn, list, false)

	// Format 15: conditional branch and SWI.
	case op>>12 == 13:
		cond := uint32((op >> 8) & 0xF)
		if cond == 0xF {
			// SWI in Thumb state: the system hook (BIOS HLE)
			// gets first refusal with the 8-bit comment field;
			// unhandled calls take the real exception, whose
			// LR_svc is A+2.
			if c.SWIHook != nil {
				if n, ok := c.SWIHook(c, uint32(op&0xFF)); ok {
					return n
				}
			}
			return c.exception(0x08, ModeSVC, addr+2)
		}
		// Condition 14, undefined in the Thumb encoding, is
		// evaluated as always by the reference implementation
		// (the shared condition table).
		if c.condPassed(cond) {
			off := int32(int8(op&0xFF)) * 2
			c.branch(uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off))
			return 3
		}
		return 1

	// Format 17: unconditional branch.
	case op>>11 == 0b11100:
		off := (int32(op&0x7FF) << 21) >> 21 * 2
		c.branch(uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off))
		return 3

	// Format 18: long branch prefix.
	case op>>11 == 0b11110:
		off := (int32(op&0x7FF) << 21) >> 21
		c.R[14] = uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off<<12)
		return 1

	// Format 19: long branch suffix (BL), and the BLX suffix
	// encoding, which NBA also implements.
	case op>>11 == 0b11111 || op>>11 == 0b11101:
		target := c.R[14] + uint32(op&0x7FF)*2
		if op>>11 == 0b11101 {
			// BLX suffix: bit 0 of LR is part of the pair
			// encoding, not of the target.
			target = (c.R[14] &^ 1) + uint32(op&0x7FF)*2
			c.CPSR &^= BitT
		}
		c.R[14] = (addr + 2) | 1
		c.branch(target)
		return 3
	}

	return c.undefined(addr)
}

// execThumbALU runs format 4, the register-register ALU group.
func (c *CPU) execThumbALU(op uint16) int {
	rd := uint32(op & 7)
	rs := uint32((op >> 3) & 7)
	a := c.R[rd]
	b := c.R[rs]
	switch (op >> 6) & 0xF {
	case 0: // AND
		c.R[rd] = a & b
		c.setNZ(a & b)
	case 1: // EOR
		c.R[rd] = a ^ b
		c.setNZ(a ^ b)
	case 2: // LSL
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 0, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 3: // LSR
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 1, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 4: // ASR
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 2, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 5: // ADC
		c.R[rd] = c.addFlags(a, b, c.carry())
	case 6: // SBC
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(a, b, c.carry())
	case 7: // ROR
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 3, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 8: // TST
		c.setNZ(a & b)
	case 9: // NEG
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(0, b, true)
	case 10: // CMP
		c.subFlags(a, b, true)
	case 11: // CMN
		c.addFlags(a, b, false)
	case 12: // ORR
		c.R[rd] = a | b
		c.setNZ(a | b)
	case 13: // MUL: in the Thumb form the booth multiplier is
		// the destination register's old value and the
		// multiplicand is the source register (the reference
		// implementation's operand order).
		res := a * b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZ(res)
		c.setCarry(mulCarry(tickMultiply(true, a), false, false, b, a, 0, 0))
		return 1 + mulCycles(a)
	case 14: // BIC
		c.R[rd] = a &^ b
		c.setNZ(a &^ b)
	case 15: // MVN
		c.R[rd] = ^b
		c.setNZ(^b)
	}
	return 1
}

// branchRawThumb refills the pipeline at addr like a Thumb
// branch, but keeps the raw target value in R15 (bit 0 not
// discarded). The empty-list LDMIA form loads the PC this way
// in the reference implementation.
func (c *CPU) branchRawThumb(addr uint32) {
	fa := addr &^ 1
	c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch(fa, 2)
	c.Pipe[0] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+2, 2)
	c.Pipe[1] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+4, 2)
	c.R[15] = addr + 4
	c.ExecutingValid = true
	c.flushed = true
}

// thumbPush stores a register list (STMDB SP), always with
// writeback.
func (c *CPU) thumbPush(list uint32) int {
	if list == 0 {
		// Empty list quirk: the PC is stored and the stack
		// pointer moves by the full 0x40.
		c.R[13] -= 0x40
		c.Bus.Write(c.R[13], 4, c.R[15]+2)
		return 2
	}
	count := popcount16(list)
	start := c.R[13] - 4*uint32(count)
	cur := start
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		c.Bus.Write(cur, 4, c.R[i])
		cur += 4
	}
	c.R[13] = start
	return count + 1
}

// thumbPop loads a register list (LDMIA SP), always with
// writeback; a loaded PC branches.
func (c *CPU) thumbPop(list uint32) int {
	if list == 0 {
		// Empty list quirk: the PC is loaded (raw, bit 0
		// kept) and the stack pointer moves by 0x40.
		v := c.Bus.Read(c.R[13], 4)
		c.R[13] += 0x40
		c.branchRawThumb(v)
		return 5
	}
	count := popcount16(list)
	cur := c.R[13]
	var pcVal uint32
	pcSet := false
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		v := c.Bus.Read(cur, 4)
		cur += 4
		if i == 15 {
			pcVal, pcSet = v, true
		} else {
			c.R[i] = v
		}
	}
	c.R[13] += 4 * uint32(count)
	n := count + 2
	if pcSet {
		c.branch(pcVal)
		n += 2
	}
	return n
}

// thumbBlock runs the Thumb LDMIA/STMIA forms (format 16), which
// always write back. A load whose base is in the list keeps the
// loaded value and suppresses writeback; a store whose base is in
// the list stores the old base when first and the new base
// otherwise. An empty list transfers R15 with a 0x40 writeback,
// as on ARM.
func (c *CPU) thumbBlock(rn uint32, list uint32, load bool) int {
	base := c.R[rn]
	empty := list == 0
	if empty {
		list = 1 << 15
	}
	count := popcount16(list)
	wb := base + 4*uint32(count)
	if empty {
		wb = base + 0x40
	}
	if load {
		var pcVal uint32
		pcSet := false
		cur := base
		for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
			if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			v := c.Bus.Read(cur, 4)
			cur += 4
			if i == 15 {
				pcVal, pcSet = v, true
			} else {
				c.R[i] = v
			}
		}
		if list&(1<<rn) == 0 {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
		n := count + 2
		if pcSet {
			if empty {
				// The empty-list LDMIA loads the PC raw.
				c.branchRawThumb(pcVal)
			} else {
				c.branch(pcVal)
			}
			n += 2
		}
		return n
	}
	idx := 0
	rnIdx := -1
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) != 0 {
			if uint32(i) == rn {
				rnIdx = idx
			}
			idx++
		}
	}
	cur := base
	idx = 0
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		v := c.R[i]
		if uint32(i) == rn && rnIdx > 0 {
			v = wb
		}
		if i == 15 {
			v = c.R[15] + 2 // a stored PC reads as A+6 in Thumb state
		}
		c.Bus.Write(cur, 4, v)
		cur += 4
		idx++
	}
	c.R[rn] = wb
	return count + 1
}

func popcount16(list uint32) int {
	n := 0
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) != 0 {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/go.mod ====================

module github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba

go 1.25.7


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/gpu/gpu.go ====================

// Package gpu is the GBA picture processor, built from
// documented register and pixel behaviour. It works one
// scanline at a time: scroll values are latched at the
// start of a line, the whole line is then sampled, and
// the affine reference points advance by their per line
// steps once the line is done.
//
// Pixel selection keeps the top two candidates for each
// output pixel so that colour effects can blend the
// winner with whatever sits directly underneath it.
package gpu

// Screen dimensions in pixels.
const (
	Width  = 240
	Height = 160
)

// Serialized layout, all integers little endian:
//
//	0    96 bytes  stored register bytes, offsets 0x00 to 0x5F
//	96   16 bytes  latched scroll values, H then V for BG0 to BG3
//	112  16 bytes  live affine references, BG2 X/Y then BG3 X/Y
//	128  4 bytes   current line as int32
//	132  1 byte    flags, bit 0 hblank, bit 1 vblank
//	133  3 bytes   zero padding
//	136  rest      framebuffer, Width*Height uint32 pixels
const StateSize = 136 + Width*Height*4

// Layer identifiers, chosen so the identifier is also
// the bit position used by the window and blending
// registers: BG0 to BG3 are 0 to 3, OBJ is 4, and the
// backdrop is 5.
const (
	layerBG0 = 0
	layerOBJ = 4
	layerBD  = 5
)

// Register offsets, relative to the display IO base.
const (
	regDISPCNT  = 0x00
	regDISPSTAT = 0x04
	regVCOUNT   = 0x06
	regBG0CNT   = 0x08
	regMOSAIC   = 0x4C
	regBLDCNT   = 0x50
	regBLDALPHA = 0x52
	regBLDY     = 0x54
)

// GPU is one display unit. The palette, video RAM and
// sprite memory are slices owned by the caller (on real
// wiring, the bus backing stores); the GPU only reads
// them while rendering.
type GPU struct {
	palette []byte
	vram    []byte
	oam     []byte

	regs     [0x60]byte
	latchedH [4]uint16
	latchedV [4]uint16

	// Live affine reference points, held as signed
	// 28 bit values with 8 fractional bits.
	refX [2]int32
	refY [2]int32

	line   int
	hblank bool
	vblank bool

	frame []uint32
}

// New returns a GPU in power-on state reading from the
// given backing stores.
func New(palette, vram, oam []byte) *GPU {
	g := &GPU{palette: palette, vram: vram, oam: oam}
	g.frame = make([]uint32, Width*Height)
	g.Reset()
	return g
}

// Reset clears every register and internal counter and
// returns the framebuffer to opaque black. The external
// backing stores are not touched.
func (g *GPU) Reset() {
	for i := range g.regs {
		g.regs[i] = 0
	}
	for i := range g.latchedH {
		g.latchedH[i] = 0
		g.latchedV[i] = 0
	}
	for i := range g.refX {
		g.refX[i] = 0
		g.refY[i] = 0
	}
	g.line = 0
	g.hblank = false
	g.vblank = false
	if g.frame == nil {
		g.frame = make([]uint32, Width*Height)
	}
	for i := range g.frame {
		g.frame[i] = 0xFF000000
	}
}

// Framebuffer returns the GPU owned pixel buffer in
// XRGB8888 form.
func (g *GPU) Framebuffer() []uint32 { return g.frame }

// Line returns the current scanline number.
func (g *GPU) Line() int { return g.line }

// SetLine sets the current scanline number, which is
// what the VCOUNT register reports.
func (g *GPU) SetLine(line int) { g.line = line }

// SetHBlank drives the hblank status flag.
func (g *GPU) SetHBlank(on bool) { g.hblank = on }

// SetVBlank drives the vblank status flag.
func (g *GPU) SetVBlank(on bool) { g.vblank = on }

// VCountMatch reports whether the current line equals
// the compare value stored in the status register.
func (g *GPU) VCountMatch() bool {
	lyc := int((g.reg16(regDISPSTAT) >> 8) & 0xFF)
	return g.line == lyc
}

// Small register access helpers.

func (g *GPU) reg16(off uint32) uint16 {
	if off+1 >= uint32(len(g.regs)) {
		return 0
	}
	return uint16(g.regs[off]) | uint16(g.regs[off+1])<<8
}

func (g *GPU) setReg16(off uint32, v uint16) {
	if off+1 >= uint32(len(g.regs)) {
		return
	}
	g.regs[off] = byte(v)
	g.regs[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
}

func (g *GPU) reg32(off uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(g.reg16(off)) | uint32(g.reg16(off+2))<<16
}

// sign28 interprets the low 28 bits of v as a signed
// value and returns it sign extended into an int32.
func sign28(v uint32) int32 {
	n := int32(v & 0x0FFFFFFF)
	if n&(1<<27) != 0 {
		n -= 1 << 28
	}
	return n
}

// refInfoFor maps any byte offset inside one of the
// 32 bit affine reference registers to that register:
// its base offset, which background (0 for BG2, 1 for
// BG3) and which coordinate (0 for X, 1 for Y).
func refInfoFor(off uint32) (base uint32, bg int, coord int, ok bool) {
	switch {
	case off >= 0x28 && off < 0x2C:
		return 0x28, 0, 0, true
	case off >= 0x2C && off < 0x30:
		return 0x2C, 0, 1, true
	case off >= 0x38 && off < 0x3C:
		return 0x38, 1, 0, true
	case off >= 0x3C && off < 0x40:
		return 0x3C, 1, 1, true
	}
	return 0, 0, 0, false
}

// syncRef reloads one live reference point from its
// stored 32 bit register value.
func (g *GPU) syncRef(bg, coord int) {
	var base uint32
	switch {
	case bg == 0 && coord == 0:
		base = 0x28
	case bg == 0:
		base = 0x2C
	case coord == 0:
		base = 0x38
	default:
		base = 0x3C
	}
	v := sign28(g.reg32(base))
	if coord == 0 {
		g.refX[bg] = v
	} else {
		g.refY[bg] = v
	}
}

// isRefHalf reports whether a 16 bit register offset is
// one half of an affine reference register.
func isRefHalf(off uint32) bool {
	switch off {
	case 0x28, 0x2A, 0x2C, 0x2E, 0x38, 0x3A, 0x3C, 0x3E:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// read16 resolves one 16 bit register read, applying the
// read restrictions of the status, count, scroll and
// affine reference registers.
func (g *GPU) read16(off uint32) uint16 {
	if off >= 0x60 {
		return 0
	}
	switch {
	case off == regDISPSTAT:
		stored := g.reg16(off) & 0xFF38
		var live uint16
		if g.vblank {
			live |= 1 << 0
		}
		if g.hblank {
			live |= 1 << 1
		}
		if g.VCountMatch() {
			live |= 1 << 2
		}
		return stored | live
	case off == regVCOUNT:
		return uint16(g.line)
	case off >= 0x10 && off < 0x20:
		return 0 // scroll registers read back as zero
	case isRefHalf(off):
		return 0 // affine reference points read back as zero
	}
	return g.reg16(off)
}

// ReadReg reads size bytes (1, 2 or 4) at a register
// offset. Wide and byte reads are composed from the
// underlying 16 bit registers, little endian.
func (g *GPU) ReadReg(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		v := uint32(g.read16(off &^ 1))
		if off&1 != 0 {
			return v >> 8
		}
		return v & 0xFF
	case 2:
		return uint32(g.read16(off))
	case 4:
		return uint32(g.read16(off)) | uint32(g.read16(off+2))<<16
	}
	return 0
}

func (g *GPU) write8(off uint32, val uint32) {
	if off >= 0x60 {
		return
	}
	aligned := off &^ 1
	if aligned == regVCOUNT {
		return
	}
	if aligned == regDISPSTAT {
		if off == regDISPSTAT {
			// Low byte: only the three IRQ enable bits
			// (bits 3 to 5) are stored; the flag bits
			// are driven by the timing setters.
			g.regs[off] = byte(val) & 0x38
		} else {
			// High byte is the line compare value.
			g.regs[off] = byte(val)
		}
		return
	}
	g.regs[off] = byte(val)
	if base, bg, coord, ok := refInfoFor(off); ok {
		_ = base
		g.syncRef(bg, coord)
	}
}

func (g *GPU) write16(off uint32, val uint32) {
	if off >= 0x60 {
		return
	}
	v := uint16(val)
	switch {
	case off == regVCOUNT:
		return
	case off == regDISPSTAT:
		g.setReg16(off, v&0xFF38)
		return
	}
	g.setReg16(off, v)
	if _, bg, coord, ok := refInfoFor(off); ok {
		g.syncRef(bg, coord)
	}
}

// WriteReg writes size bytes (1, 2 or 4) at a register
// offset. Wide writes decompose into 16 bit writes and
// byte writes touch only their own lane, including for
// the write-only scroll and reference registers, whose
// stored values still update.
func (g *GPU) WriteReg(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		g.write8(off, val&0xFF)
	case 2:
		if off&1 != 0 {
			g.write8(off, val&0xFF)
			g.write8(off+1, (val>>8)&0xFF)
			return
		}
		g.write16(off, val&0xFFFF)
	case 4:
		g.WriteReg(off, 2, val&0xFFFF)
		g.WriteReg(off+2, 2, (val>>16)&0xFFFF)
	}
}

// BeginLine latches the text scroll offsets for the
// current line, so changes written part way through a
// line only take effect on the next one.
func (g *GPU) BeginLine() {
	for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
		base := uint32(0x10 + bg*4)
		g.latchedH[bg] = g.reg16(base) & 0x1FF
		g.latchedV[bg] = g.reg16(base+2) & 0x1FF
	}
}

// Serialize writes the full GPU state (see the layout
// documented at StateSize) into dst and returns the
// number of bytes used. It returns 0 if dst is short.
func (g *GPU) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	if len(dst) < StateSize {
		return 0
	}
	put16 := func(off int, v uint16) {
		dst[off] = byte(v)
		dst[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	}
	put32 := func(off int, v uint32) {
		dst[off] = byte(v)
		dst[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
		dst[off+2] = byte(v >> 16)
		dst[off+3] = byte(v >> 24)
	}
	copy(dst[0:96], g.regs[:])
	off := 96
	for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
		put16(off, g.latchedH[bg])
		off += 2
	}
	for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
		put16(off, g.latchedV[bg])
		off += 2
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		put32(off, uint32(g.refX[i]))
		off += 4
		put32(off, uint32(g.refY[i]))
		off += 4
	}
	put32(off, uint32(int32(g.line)))
	off += 4
	var flags byte
	if g.hblank {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if g.vblank {
		flags |= 2
	}
	dst[off] = flags
	off++
	dst[off] = 0
	dst[off+1] = 0
	dst[off+2] = 0
	off += 3
	for i, px := range g.frame {
		put32(off+i*4, px)
	}
	return StateSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
// It reports false when the input is too short.
func (g *GPU) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < StateSize {
		return false
	}
	get16 := func(off int) uint16 {
		return uint16(src[off]) | uint16(src[off+1])<<8
	}
	get32 := func(off int) uint32 {
		return uint32(src[off]) | uint32(src[off+1])<<8 |
			uint32(src[off+2])<<16 | uint32(src[off+3])<<24
	}
	copy(g.regs[:], src[0:96])
	off := 96
	for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
		g.latchedH[bg] = get16(off)
		off += 2
	}
	for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
		g.latchedV[bg] = get16(off)
		off += 2
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		g.refX[i] = int32(get32(off))
		off += 4
		g.refY[i] = int32(get32(off))
		off += 4
	}
	g.line = int(int32(get32(off)))
	off += 4
	flags := src[off]
	off++
	g.hblank = flags&1 != 0
	g.vblank = flags&2 != 0
	off += 3
	if g.frame == nil {
		g.frame = make([]uint32, Width*Height)
	}
	for i := range g.frame {
		g.frame[i] = get32(off + i*4)
	}
	return true
}

package gpu

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"
)

// Test colours in 15 bit form and their packed output
// form, worked out by hand from the channel expansion
// rule (v<<3)|(v>>2).
const (
	c555Red   = 0x001F
	c555Green = 0x03E0
	c555Blue  = 0x7C00
	c555White = 0x7FFF
	c555Yel   = 0x03FF
	c555Cyan  = 0x7FE0
	c555Mag   = 0x7C1F

	pxRed   = 0xFFFF0000
	pxGreen = 0xFF00FF00
	pxBlue  = 0xFF0000FF
	pxWhite = 0xFFFFFFFF
	pxYel   = 0xFFFFFF00
	pxCyan  = 0xFF00FFFF
)

func newRig() (*GPU, []byte, []byte, []byte) {
	pal := make([]byte, 0x400)
	vram := make([]byte, 0x18000)
	oam := make([]byte, 0x400)
	return New(pal, vram, oam), pal, vram, oam
}

func setPal(pal []byte, idx int, val uint16) {
	pal[idx*2] = byte(val)
	pal[idx*2+1] = byte(val >> 8)
}

func setObjPal(pal []byte, idx int, val uint16) {
	off := 0x200 + idx*2
	pal[off] = byte(val)
	pal[off+1] = byte(val >> 8)
}

func putVRAM16(vram []byte, off int, val uint16) {
	vram[off] = byte(val)
	vram[off+1] = byte(val >> 8)
}

func putOAM16(oam []byte, off int, val uint16) {
	oam[off] = byte(val)
	oam[off+1] = byte(val >> 8)
}

// disableSpritesExcept marks every sprite except the
// named one as disabled, since zeroed sprite entries
// are otherwise live sprites stacked at the origin.
func disableSpritesExcept(oam []byte, keep int) {
	for i := 0; i < 128; i++ {
		if i != keep {
			putOAM16(oam, i*8, 1<<9)
		}
	}
}

// renderRow renders one line and returns a copy of that
// row of the framebuffer.
func renderRow(g *GPU, line int) []uint32 {
	g.SetLine(line)
	g.BeginLine()
	g.RenderLine()
	row := make([]uint32, Width)
	copy(row, g.Framebuffer()[line*Width:(line+1)*Width])
	return row
}

// setupTextBG0 points BG0 at screen block 1 with
// character base 0 and feeds it a single screen entry
// for tile 0. prio is the BG0 priority value.
func setupTextBG0(g *GPU, vram []byte, prio uint16) {
	putVRAM16(vram, 0x800, 0) // entry: tile 0, no flips, bank 0
	g.WriteReg(0x08, 2, uint32((1<<8)|prio))
	g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x0100) // mode 0, BG0 on
}

func TestTextTilePixel(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("4bpp pixels and transparency", func(t *testing.T) {
		g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
		setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue) // backdrop
		setPal(pal, 1, c555Red)
		setPal(pal, 2, c555Green)
		// Tile 0, row 0: pixels are indices 1, 2, 0, 0.
		vram[0] = 0x21
		vram[1] = 0x00
		setupTextBG0(g, vram, 0)
		row := renderRow(g, 0)
		if row[0] != pxRed {
			t.Errorf("pixel (0,0) = %#08x, want red %#08x", row[0], pxRed)
		}
		if row[1] != pxGreen {
			t.Errorf("pixel (1,0) = %#08x, want green %#08x", row[1], pxGreen)
		}
		if row[2] != pxBlue {
			t.Errorf("pixel (2,0) = %#08x, want backdrop blue %#08x", row[2], pxBlue)
		}
	})

	t.Run("8bpp tile pixel", func(t *testing.T) {
		g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
		setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
		setPal(pal, 5, c555Yel)
		setPal(pal, 6, c555Cyan)
		vram[0] = 5 // tile 0 texel (0,0) in 8bpp
		vram[1] = 6 // texel (1,0)
		putVRAM16(vram, 0x800, 0)
		g.WriteReg(0x08, 2, (1<<8)|(1<<7)) // screen base 1, 8bpp
		g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x0100)
		row := renderRow(g, 0)
		if row[0] != pxYel {
			t.Errorf("pixel (0,0) = %#08x, want yellow %#08x", row[0], pxYel)
		}
		if row[1] != pxCyan {
			t.Errorf("pixel (1,0) = %#08x, want cyan %#08x", row[1], pxCyan)
		}
	})

	t.Run("4bpp palette bank selection", func(t *testing.T) {
		g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
		setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
		setPal(pal, 3, c555Red)    // bank 0 index 3: the wrong colour
		setPal(pal, 35, c555Green) // bank 2 index 3: the right colour
		vram[0] = 0x03             // texel (0,0) is index 3
		putVRAM16(vram, 0x800, 2<<12)
		g.WriteReg(0x08, 2, 1<<8)
		g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x0100)
		row := renderRow(g, 0)
		if row[0] != pxGreen {
			t.Errorf("pixel (0,0) = %#08x, want bank 2 green %#08x", row[0], pxGreen)
		}
	})
}

func TestPriority(t *testing.T) {
	build := func(bgPrio, objPrio uint16) uint32 {
		g, pal, vram, oam := newRig()
		setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
		setPal(pal, 1, c555Red) // background pixel colour
		setObjPal(pal, 1, c555White)
		vram[0] = 0x01       // BG tile 0 texel (0,0) index 1
		vram[0x10000] = 0x01 // OBJ tile 0 texel (0,0) index 1
		setupTextBG0(g, vram, bgPrio)
		disableSpritesExcept(oam, 0)
		putOAM16(oam, 0, 0)           // attr0: y 0, 8x8, normal
		putOAM16(oam, 2, 0)           // attr1: x 0, size 0
		putOAM16(oam, 4, objPrio<<10) // attr2: tile 0, priority
		g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x1100)   // BG0 and OBJ on, mode 0
		return renderRow(g, 0)[0]
	}
	t.Run("sprite wins on equal priority", func(t *testing.T) {
		if got := build(1, 1); got != pxWhite {
			t.Errorf("pixel = %#08x, want sprite white %#08x", got, pxWhite)
		}
	})
	t.Run("background wins with lower priority number", func(t *testing.T) {
		if got := build(0, 1); got != pxRed {
			t.Errorf("pixel = %#08x, want background red %#08x", got, pxRed)
		}
	})
}

func affineRig(pa, pd uint16) (*GPU, []byte) {
	g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
	setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
	setPal(pal, 2, c555Red)
	setPal(pal, 3, c555Green)
	vram[0x800] = 1           // map entry at (0,0): tile 1
	vram[64] = 2              // tile 1 texel (0,0)
	vram[64+9] = 3            // tile 1 texel (1,1)
	g.WriteReg(0x0C, 2, 1<<8) // BG2CNT: screen base 1, size 0
	g.WriteReg(0x20, 2, uint32(pa))
	g.WriteReg(0x22, 2, 0)
	g.WriteReg(0x24, 2, 0)
	g.WriteReg(0x26, 2, uint32(pd))
	g.WriteReg(0x28, 4, 0)      // BG2X
	g.WriteReg(0x2C, 4, 0)      // BG2Y
	g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x0401) // mode 1, BG2 on
	return g, vram
}

func TestAffineSampling(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("identity samples the expected texel", func(t *testing.T) {
		g, _ := affineRig(0x100, 0x100)
		row := renderRow(g, 0)
		if row[0] != pxRed {
			t.Errorf("pixel (0,0) = %#08x, want texel (0,0) red %#08x", row[0], pxRed)
		}
		if row[1] != pxBlue {
			t.Errorf("pixel (1,0) = %#08x, want transparent texel over backdrop %#08x", row[1], pxBlue)
		}
	})
	t.Run("half scale reaches texel (1,1) at screen (2,2)", func(t *testing.T) {
		g, _ := affineRig(0x80, 0x80)
		renderRow(g, 0)
		renderRow(g, 1)
		row := renderRow(g, 2)
		if row[2] != pxGreen {
			t.Errorf("pixel (2,2) = %#08x, want texel (1,1) green %#08x", row[2], pxGreen)
		}
	})
}

func identityAffine(g *GPU) {
	g.WriteReg(0x20, 2, 0x100)
	g.WriteReg(0x22, 2, 0)
	g.WriteReg(0x24, 2, 0)
	g.WriteReg(0x26, 2, 0x100)
	g.WriteReg(0x28, 4, 0)
	g.WriteReg(0x2C, 4, 0)
}

	identityAffine(g)
	g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x0403) // mode 3, BG2 on
	renderRow(g, 0)
	renderRow(g, 1)
	renderRow(g, 2)
	row := renderRow(g, 3)
	if row[5] != pxYel {

	}
