func TestMode4PageSelect(t *testing.T) {
	build := func(page bool) uint32 {
		g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
		setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
		setPal(pal, 9, c555Red)
		setPal(pal, 7, c555Green)
		vram[0] = 9      // page 0 texel (0,0)
		vram[0xA000] = 7 // page 1 texel (0,0)
		identityAffine(g)
		dc := uint32(0x0404) // mode 4, BG2 on
		if page {
			dc |= 1 << 4
		}
		g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, dc)
		return renderRow(g, 0)[0]
	}
	if got := build(true); got != pxGreen {
		t.Errorf("page 1 pixel = %#08x, want green %#08x", got, pxGreen)
	}
	if got := build(false); got != pxRed {
		t.Errorf("page 0 pixel = %#08x, want red %#08x", got, pxRed)
	}
}

// blendRig builds BG0 over BG1 at pixel (0,0): BG0 uses
// palette index bg0Idx, BG1 uses palette index bg1Idx.
func blendRig(bg0Idx, bg1Idx byte) *GPU {
	g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
	setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
	setPal(pal, 1, c555Red)
	setPal(pal, 2, c555Blue)
	setPal(pal, 3, c555White)
	vram[0] = bg0Idx                     // BG0 tile 0 texel (0,0)
	putVRAM16(vram, 0x800, 0)            // BG0 entry
	vram[0x4000] = bg1Idx                // BG1 tile 0 (char base 1) texel (0,0)
	putVRAM16(vram, 0x1000, 0)           // BG1 entry at screen base 2
	g.WriteReg(0x08, 2, (1<<8)|0)        // BG0CNT: prio 0
	g.WriteReg(0x0A, 2, (2<<8)|(1<<2)|1) // BG1CNT: screen 2, char 1, prio 1
	g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x0300)          // mode 0, BG0 and BG1 on
	return g
}

func TestAlphaBlend(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("half and half average", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := blendRig(1, 2)
		// First target BG0, mode alpha, second target BG1.
		g.WriteReg(0x50, 2, 1|(1<<6)|(1<<9))
		g.WriteReg(0x52, 2, 8|(8<<8)) // EVA 8, EVB 8
		row := renderRow(g, 0)
		// Red (31,0,0) over blue (0,0,31) at 8/16 each:
		// r and b become (31*8)/16 = 15, expanded to
		// (15<<3)|(15>>2) = 123 = 0x7B.
		want := uint32(0xFF7B007B)
		if row[0] != want {
			t.Errorf("pixel = %#08x, want blended %#08x", row[0], want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("full coefficients clamp at 31", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := blendRig(3, 3) // white over white
		g.WriteReg(0x50, 2, 1|(1<<6)|(1<<9))
		g.WriteReg(0x52, 2, 16|(16<<8)) // EVA 16, EVB 16
		row := renderRow(g, 0)
		if row[0] != pxWhite {
			t.Errorf("pixel = %#08x, want clamped white %#08x", row[0], pxWhite)
		}
	})
}

func TestBrightness(t *testing.T) {
	build := func(mode uint16) uint32 {
		g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
		setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
		setPal(pal, 1, 0x4210) // channels 16, 16, 16
		vram[0] = 0x01
		setupTextBG0(g, vram, 0)
		g.WriteReg(0x50, 2, uint32(1|(mode<<6))) // first target BG0
		g.WriteReg(0x54, 2, 16)                  // EVY 16
		return renderRow(g, 0)[0]
	}
	t.Run("brighten to white", func(t *testing.T) {
		// 16 + (31-16)*16/16 = 31 per channel.
		if got := build(2); got != pxWhite {
			t.Errorf("pixel = %#08x, want white %#08x", got, pxWhite)
		}
	})
	t.Run("darken to black", func(t *testing.T) {
		// 16 - 16*16/16 = 0 per channel.
		if got := build(3); got != 0xFF000000 {
			t.Errorf("pixel = %#08x, want black %#08x", got, 0xFF000000)
		}
	})
}

func TestWindowClip(t *testing.T) {
	g, pal, vram, _ := newRig()
	setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
	setPal(pal, 1, c555Red)
	vram[0] = 0x01
	// Fill the whole first tile row of the map with tile 0
	// entries whose pixels are red: entry tile 0 already
	// gives red at index 1 for every texel of row 0 only,
	// so give tile 0 an all-ones row instead.
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		vram[i] = 0x11
	}
	setupTextBG0(g, vram, 0)
	g.WriteReg(0x40, 2, 120)    // WIN0H: left 0, right 120
	g.WriteReg(0x44, 2, 160)    // WIN0V: top 0, bottom 160
	g.WriteReg(0x48, 2, 0x01)   // WININ low: BG0 on inside
	g.WriteReg(0x4A, 2, 0x00)   // WINOUT low: nothing outside
	g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x2100) // BG0 on, window 0 on
	row := renderRow(g, 0)
	if row[10] != pxRed {
		t.Errorf("pixel (10,0) = %#08x, want inside window red %#08x", row[10], pxRed)
	}
	if row[200] != pxBlue {
		t.Errorf("pixel (200,0) = %#08x, want outside window backdrop %#08x", row[200], pxBlue)
	}
}

func TestSemiTransparentSprite(t *testing.T) {
	g, pal, vram, oam := newRig()
	setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
	setPal(pal, 2, c555Blue) // background pixel colour
	setObjPal(pal, 1, c555Red)
	vram[0] = 0x02       // BG texel index 2
	vram[0x10000] = 0x01 // OBJ texel index 1
	setupTextBG0(g, vram, 1)
	disableSpritesExcept(oam, 0)
	putOAM16(oam, 0, 1<<10) // attr0: y 0, semi-transparent mode
	putOAM16(oam, 2, 0)
	putOAM16(oam, 4, 0) // attr2: tile 0, priority 0
	// Second target is BG0; the sprite counts as first
	// target on its own.
	g.WriteReg(0x50, 2, 1<<8)
	g.WriteReg(0x52, 2, 8|(8<<8))
	g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x1100)
	row := renderRow(g, 0)
	want := uint32(0xFF7B007B) // same 15/0/15 mix as the alpha test
	if row[0] != want {
		t.Errorf("pixel = %#08x, want blended %#08x", row[0], want)
	}
}

func TestRegisterBehaviour(t *testing.T) {
	g, _, _, _ := newRig()
	// DISPSTAT: stored bits are the IRQ enables and the
	// line compare value; the flags come from setters.
	g.WriteReg(0x04, 2, 0x1238)
	g.SetLine(18)
	g.SetVBlank(true)
	g.SetHBlank(true)
	if got := g.ReadReg(0x04, 2); got != 0x123F {
		t.Errorf("DISPSTAT = %#04x, want 0x123f", got)
	}
	if !g.VCountMatch() {
		t.Error("VCountMatch false at line 18 with compare 0x12")
	}
	if got := g.ReadReg(0x06, 2); got != 18 {
		t.Errorf("VCOUNT = %d, want 18", got)
	}
	g.WriteReg(0x06, 2, 99) // read only: ignored
	if g.Line() != 18 {
		t.Errorf("Line after VCOUNT write = %d, want 18", g.Line())
	}
	// Scroll registers are write only for reads but keep
	// their stored value.
	g.WriteReg(0x10, 2, 0x01AB)
	if got := g.ReadReg(0x10, 2); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("scroll read = %#04x, want 0", got)
	}
	// Byte write touches only its lane of DISPCNT.
	g.WriteReg(0x00, 2, 0x0100)
	g.WriteReg(0x01, 1, 0x12)
	if got := g.ReadReg(0x00, 2); got != 0x1200 {
		t.Errorf("DISPCNT after byte write = %#04x, want 0x1200", got)
	}
	// Affine reference: reads return zero, and a stored
	// value with bit 27 set is held as a negative
	// internal point (visible in the serialized state).
	g.WriteReg(0x28, 4, 0x0FFFFFFF)
	if got := g.ReadReg(0x28, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("BG2X read = %#08x, want 0", got)
	}
	buf := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if n := g.Serialize(buf); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize returned %d, want %d", n, StateSize)
	}
	// Live references sit at byte 112 in the layout.
	if got := int32(uint32(buf[112]) | uint32(buf[113])<<8 | uint32(buf[114])<<16 | uint32(buf[115])<<24); got != -1 {
		t.Errorf("serialized BG2 ref X = %d, want -1", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	g, pal, vram, oam := newRig()
	setPal(pal, 0, c555Blue)
	setPal(pal, 1, c555Red)
	vram[0] = 0x01
	setupTextBG0(g, vram, 0)
	g.WriteReg(0x10, 2, 3) // BG0 horizontal scroll
	g.WriteReg(0x50, 2, 0x0081)
	g.WriteReg(0x54, 2, 4)
	for line := 0; line < 3; line++ {
		renderRow(g, line)
	}
	first := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if n := g.Serialize(first); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize returned %d, want %d", n, StateSize)
	}
	// Deserialize into a fresh GPU over the same backing stores.
	fresh := New(pal, vram, oam)
	if !fresh.Deserialize(first) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize reported false")
	}
	second := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if n := fresh.Serialize(second); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("second Serialize returned %d, want %d", n, StateSize)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(first, second) {
		t.Error("state bytes differ after a serialize round trip")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(
		func() []byte { b, _ := frameBytes(g); return b }(),
		func() []byte { b, _ := frameBytes(fresh); return b }(),
	) {
		t.Error("framebuffers differ after a serialize round trip")
	}
}

func frameBytes(g *GPU) ([]byte, bool) {
	buf := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if g.Serialize(buf) != StateSize {
		return nil, false
	}
	return buf[136:], true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/gpu/render.go ====================

package gpu

// One scanline of rendering: candidate gathering from
// the background and sprite layers, window masking,
// winner selection, colour effects and output packing.

// candidate is one layer offering a pixel. The colour is
// kept as a raw 15 bit value so effect maths can work
// in 5 bit channels.
type candidate struct {
	present bool
	col     uint16
	layer   int
	prio    int
	semi    bool
}

// candRank orders candidates that share a priority
// number: sprites first, then backgrounds in index
// order, and the backdrop below everything.
func candRank(c candidate) int {
	switch {
	case c.layer == layerOBJ:
		return 0
	case c.layer == layerBD:
		return 99
	default:
		return 1 + c.layer
	}
}

// candBetter reports whether a outranks b.
func candBetter(a, b candidate) bool {
	if a.prio != b.prio {
		return a.prio < b.prio
	}
	return candRank(a) < candRank(b)
}

type picker struct {
	best   candidate
	second candidate
}

func (p *picker) consider(c candidate) {
	if !c.present {
		return
	}
	if !p.best.present || candBetter(c, p.best) {
		p.second = p.best
		p.best = c
		return
	}
	if !p.second.present || candBetter(c, p.second) {
		p.second = c
	}
}

// Backing store reads, all bounds checked.

func (g *GPU) vram8(off int) (byte, bool) {
	if off < 0 || off >= len(g.vram) {
		return 0, false
	}
	return g.vram[off], true
}

func (g *GPU) vram16(off int) (uint16, bool) {
	lo, ok1 := g.vram8(off)
	hi, ok2 := g.vram8(off + 1)
	if !ok1 || !ok2 {
		return 0, false
	}
	return uint16(lo) | uint16(hi)<<8, true
}

func (g *GPU) palAt(byteOff int) uint16 {
	if byteOff < 0 || byteOff+1 >= len(g.palette) {
		if byteOff >= 0 && byteOff < len(g.palette) {
			return uint16(g.palette[byteOff])
		}
		return 0
	}
	return uint16(g.palette[byteOff]) | uint16(g.palette[byteOff+1])<<8
}

// bgPal returns the background palette colour for a
// palette index in the range 0 to 255.
func (g *GPU) bgPal(idx int) uint16 { return g.palAt(idx * 2) }

// objPal returns the sprite palette colour for a
// palette index in the range 0 to 255.
func (g *GPU) objPal(idx int) uint16 { return g.palAt(0x200 + idx*2) }

func (g *GPU) oam16(off int) uint16 {
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(g.oam) {
		return 0
	}
	return uint16(g.oam[off]) | uint16(g.oam[off+1])<<8
}

// Register convenience readers used while rendering.

func (g *GPU) dispcnt() uint16 { return g.reg16(regDISPCNT) }

func (g *GPU) bgcnt(bg int) uint16 {
	return g.reg16(uint32(regBG0CNT + bg*2))
}

// affineParam returns one of the four affine matrix
// values (indices 0 to 3 are PA, PB, PC, PD) for a
// background, as a signed 8.8 fixed point number.
func (g *GPU) affineParam(bg, idx int) int16 {
	base := uint32(0x20)
	if bg == 3 {
		base = 0x30
	}
	return int16(g.reg16(base + uint32(idx*2)))
}

// stepRefs advances both live affine reference points
// by their per line steps, wrapping to signed 28 bits.
func (g *GPU) stepRefs() {
	for i, bg := range []int{2, 3} {
		pb := int32(g.affineParam(bg, 1))
		pd := int32(g.affineParam(bg, 3))
		g.refX[i] = sign28(uint32(g.refX[i] + pb))
		g.refY[i] = sign28(uint32(g.refY[i] + pd))
	}
}

// Positive modulo for wrapping coordinates.
func wrapMod(v, n int) int {
	r := v % n
	if r < 0 {
		r += n
	}
	return r
}

// Text backgrounds.

// textPixel fetches the colour offered by text
// background bg at screen column x on the current line,
// reporting false for a transparent texel.
func (g *GPU) textPixel(bg, x int) (uint16, bool) {
	cnt := g.bgcnt(bg)
	charBase := int((cnt>>2)&3) * 0x4000
	screenBase := int((cnt>>8)&0x1F) * 0x800
	size := (cnt >> 14) & 3

	mapW, mapH := 256, 256
	switch size {
	case 1:
		mapW = 512
	case 2:
		mapH = 512
	case 3:
		mapW, mapH = 512, 512
	}

	mx := wrapMod(x+int(g.latchedH[bg]), mapW)
	my := wrapMod(g.line+int(g.latchedV[bg]), mapH)

	if cnt&(1<<6) != 0 {
		mosaic := g.reg16(regMOSAIC)
		hs := int((mosaic>>8)&0xF) + 1
		vs := int((mosaic>>12)&0xF) + 1
		mx -= mx % hs
		my -= my % vs
	}

	blocksPerRow := mapW / 256
	block := (mx >> 8) + (my>>8)*blocksPerRow
	bx := mx & 0xFF
	by := my & 0xFF
	entryOff := screenBase + block*0x800 + ((by>>3)*32+(bx>>3))*2
	entry, ok := g.vram16(entryOff)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	tile := int(entry & 0x3FF)
	px := mx & 7
	py := my & 7
	if entry&(1<<10) != 0 {
		px = 7 - px
	}
	if entry&(1<<11) != 0 {
		py = 7 - py
	}
	if cnt&(1<<7) != 0 {
		off := charBase + tile*64 + py*8 + px
		idx, ok := g.vram8(off)
		if !ok || idx == 0 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return g.bgPal(int(idx)), true
	}
	off := charBase + tile*32 + py*4 + px/2
	b, ok := g.vram8(off)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	var nib int
	if px&1 == 0 {
		nib = int(b & 0xF)
	} else {
		nib = int(b >> 4)
	}
	if nib == 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	bank := int((entry >> 12) & 0xF)
	return g.bgPal(bank*16 + nib), true
}

// Affine backgrounds.

// affineTex computes the texture coordinates of screen
// column x for an affine background, using the live
// reference point and the per pixel steps PA and PC.
func (g *GPU) affineTex(bg, x int) (int, int) {
	i := bg - 2
	pa := int32(g.affineParam(bg, 0))
	pc := int32(g.affineParam(bg, 2))
	texX := int((g.refX[i] + pa*int32(x)) >> 8)
	texY := int((g.refY[i] + pc*int32(x)) >> 8)
	return texX, texY
}

func (g *GPU) affinePixel(bg, x int) (uint16, bool) {
	cnt := g.bgcnt(bg)
	charBase := int((cnt>>2)&3) * 0x4000
	screenBase := int((cnt>>8)&0x1F) * 0x800
	size := 128 << ((cnt >> 14) & 3)
	wrap := cnt&(1<<13) != 0

	texX, texY := g.affineTex(bg, x)
	if texX < 0 || texX >= size || texY < 0 || texY >= size {
		if !wrap {
			return 0, false
		}
		texX = wrapMod(texX, size)
		texY = wrapMod(texY, size)
	}
	tilesPerRow := size / 8
	entryOff := screenBase + (texY>>3)*tilesPerRow + (texX >> 3)
	tileByte, ok := g.vram8(entryOff)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	off := charBase + int(tileByte)*64 + (texY&7)*8 + (texX & 7)
	idx, ok := g.vram8(off)
	if !ok || idx == 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	return g.bgPal(int(idx)), true
}

// bitmapPixel fetches BG2 in the direct and indexed
// bitmap modes (3, 4 and 5).
func (g *GPU) bitmapPixel(mode, x int) (uint16, bool) {
	cnt := g.bgcnt(2)
	wrap := cnt&(1<<13) != 0
	pageBase := 0
	if g.dispcnt()&(1<<4) != 0 {
		pageBase = 0xA000
	}
	texX, texY := g.affineTex(2, x)
	switch mode {
	case 3:
		if texX < 0 || texX >= 240 || texY < 0 || texY >= 160 {
			if !wrap {
				return 0, false
			}
			texX = wrapMod(texX, 240)
			texY = wrapMod(texY, 160)
		}
		col, ok := g.vram16((texY*240 + texX) * 2)
		if !ok {
			return 0, false
		}
		return col, true
	case 4:
		if texX < 0 || texX >= 240 || texY < 0 || texY >= 160 {
			if !wrap {
				return 0, false
			}
			texX = wrapMod(texX, 240)
			texY = wrapMod(texY, 160)
		}
		idx, ok := g.vram8(pageBase + texY*240 + texX)
		if !ok || idx == 0 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return g.bgPal(int(idx)), true
	case 5:
		if texX < 0 || texX >= 160 || texY < 0 || texY >= 128 {
			if !wrap {
				return 0, false
			}
			texX = wrapMod(texX, 160)
			texY = wrapMod(texY, 128)
		}
		col, ok := g.vram16(pageBase + (texY*160+texX)*2)
		if !ok {
			return 0, false
		}
		return col, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// Sprites.

// Sprite sizes by shape then size index: width, height.
var objSizes = [3][4][2]int{
	{{8, 8}, {16, 16}, {32, 32}, {64, 64}}, // square
	{{16, 8}, {32, 8}, {32, 16}, {64, 32}}, // wide
	{{8, 16}, {8, 32}, {16, 32}, {32, 64}}, // tall
}

type objLine struct {
	pix    [Width]candidate
	winMsk [Width]bool
}

// objTilePixel fetches one source pixel of a sprite.
func (g *GPU) objTilePixel(tileNum, srcX, srcY, widthTiles int, color256 bool, bank int) (uint16, bool) {
	step := 1
	if color256 {
		step = 2
	}
	var tileNumber int
	if g.dispcnt()&(1<<6) != 0 {
		// One dimensional: tile numbers run on through
		// the sprite area row by row.
		tileNumber = tileNum + (srcY>>3)*widthTiles*step + (srcX>>3)*step
	} else {
		// Two dimensional: each sprite row starts 32
		// tile numbers after the previous one.
		tileNumber = tileNum + (srcY>>3)*32 + (srcX>>3)*step
	}
	base := 0x10000
	if mode := g.dispcnt() & 7; mode >= 3 && mode <= 5 {
		base = 0x14000
	}
	off := base + tileNumber*32
	tx := srcX & 7
	ty := srcY & 7
	if color256 {
		idx, ok := g.vram8(off + ty*8 + tx)
		if !ok || idx == 0 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return g.objPal(int(idx)), true
	}
	b, ok := g.vram8(off + ty*4 + tx/2)
	if !ok {
		return 0, false
	}
	var nib int
	if tx&1 == 0 {
		nib = int(b & 0xF)
	} else {
		nib = int(b >> 4)
	}
	if nib == 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	return g.objPal(bank*16 + nib), true
}

// buildObjLine resolves every sprite pixel that lands
// on the current line, and the sprite window mask.
func (g *GPU) buildObjLine() objLine {
	var out objLine
	mode := int(g.dispcnt() & 7)
	_ = mode
	mosaic := g.reg16(regMOSAIC)
	mosH := int(mosaic&0xF) + 1
	mosV := int((mosaic>>4)&0xF) + 1

	for i := 0; i < 128; i++ {
		base := i * 8
		if base+5 >= len(g.oam) {
			break
		}
		attr0 := g.oam16(base)
		attr1 := g.oam16(base + 2)
		attr2 := g.oam16(base + 4)

		affine := attr0&(1<<8) != 0
		flag9 := attr0&(1<<9) != 0
		if flag9 && !affine {
			continue // disabled sprite
		}
		shape := int((attr0 >> 14) & 3)
		if shape == 3 {
			continue
		}
		objMode := int((attr0 >> 10) & 3)
		color256 := attr0&(1<<13) != 0
		mosaicOn := attr0&(1<<12) != 0

		sizeIdx := int((attr1 >> 14) & 3)
		w := objSizes[shape][sizeIdx][0]
		h := objSizes[shape][sizeIdx][1]
		boundW, boundH := w, h
		if affine && flag9 {
			boundW, boundH = w*2, h*2 // double size box
		}

		y := int(attr0 & 0xFF)
		xCoord := int(attr1 & 0x1FF)
		relY := (g.line - y) & 0xFF
		if relY >= boundH {
			continue
		}

		tileNum := int(attr2 & 0x3FF)
		prio := int((attr2 >> 10) & 3)
		bank := int((attr2 >> 12) & 0xF)

		var pa, pb, pc, pd int
		if affine {
			set := int((attr1 >> 9) & 0x1F)
			pa = int(int16(g.oam16(set*0x20 + 0x06)))
			pb = int(int16(g.oam16(set*0x20 + 0x0E)))
			pc = int(int16(g.oam16(set*0x20 + 0x16)))
			pd = int(int16(g.oam16(set*0x20 + 0x1E)))
		}
		hflip := attr1&(1<<12) != 0
		vflip := attr1&(1<<13) != 0

		for px := 0; px < Width; px++ {
			relX := (px - xCoord) & 0x1FF
			if relX >= boundW {
				continue
			}
			var srcX, srcY int
			if affine {
				dx := relX - boundW/2
				dy := relY - boundH/2
				srcX = ((pa*dx + pb*dy) >> 8) + w/2
				srcY = ((pc*dx + pd*dy) >> 8) + h/2
				if srcX < 0 || srcX >= w || srcY < 0 || srcY >= h {
					continue
				}
			} else {
				srcX, srcY = relX, relY
				if hflip {
					srcX = w - 1 - srcX
				}
				if vflip {
					srcY = h - 1 - srcY
				}
			}
			if mosaicOn {
				srcX -= srcX % mosH
				srcY -= srcY % mosV
			}
			col, ok := g.objTilePixel(tileNum, srcX, srcY, w/8, color256, bank)
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			if objMode == 2 {
				out.winMsk[px] = true
				continue
			}
			c := candidate{
				present: true,
				col:     col,
				layer:   layerOBJ,
				prio:    prio,
				semi:    objMode == 1,
			}
			if !out.pix[px].present || prio < out.pix[px].prio {
				out.pix[px] = c
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// Windows.

// windowMask returns the six enable and effect bits in
// force at a pixel: bits 0 to 3 enable BG0 to BG3, bit 4
// enables sprites, bit 5 enables colour effects.
func (g *GPU) windowMask(x int, objWin [Width]bool) uint16 {
	dc := g.dispcnt()
	if dc&0xE000 == 0 {
		return 0x3F // no window active: everything on
	}
	winIn := g.reg16(0x48)
	winOut := g.reg16(0x4A)
	if dc&(1<<13) != 0 && g.inWindow(0, x) {
		return winIn & 0x3F
	}
	if dc&(1<<14) != 0 && g.inWindow(1, x) {
		return (winIn >> 8) & 0x3F
	}
	if dc&(1<<15) != 0 && objWin[x] {
		return (winOut >> 8) & 0x3F
	}
	return winOut & 0x3F
}

// inWindow tests a pixel against one window rectangle,
// applying the dimension rules for empty or oversized
// rectangles: a right edge at or below the (clamped)
// left edge, or past the screen edge, extends to the
// screen edge, and the same for the bottom edge.
func (g *GPU) inWindow(which, x int) bool {
	hv := g.reg16(uint32(0x40 + which*2))
	vv := g.reg16(uint32(0x44 + which*2))
	left := int(hv >> 8)
	right := int(hv & 0xFF)
	top := int(vv >> 8)
	bottom := int(vv & 0xFF)
	if left > Width {
		left = Width
	}
	if top > Height {
		top = Height
	}
	if right <= left || right > Width {
		right = Width
	}
	if bottom <= top || bottom > Height {
		bottom = Height
	}
	return x >= left && x < right && g.line >= top && g.line < bottom
}

// Colour effects.

func clamp16(v int) int {
	if v > 16 {
		return 16
	}
	if v < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return v
}

func channels(col uint16) (int, int, int) {
	return int(col & 31), int((col >> 5) & 31), int((col >> 10) & 31)
}

// applyEffects runs the blending and brightness maths
// for the winning pixel. second may hold the backdrop
// as a stand-in runner-up.
func (g *GPU) applyEffects(best, second candidate) (int, int, int) {
	r, gg, b := channels(best.col)
	bld := g.reg16(regBLDCNT)
	mode := int((bld >> 6) & 3)
	alpha := g.reg16(regBLDALPHA)
	eva := clamp16(int(alpha & 0x1F))
	evb := clamp16(int((alpha >> 8) & 0x1F))
	evy := clamp16(int(g.reg16(regBLDY) & 0x1F))

	blend := func() (int, int, int) {
		sr, sg, sb := channels(second.col)
		mix := func(top, under int) int {
			v := (top*eva + under*evb) / 16
			if v > 31 {
				v = 31
			}
			return v
		}
		return mix(r, sr), mix(gg, sg), mix(b, sb)
	}

	firstTarget := best.layer >= 0 && best.layer <= 5 &&
		(bld>>uint(best.layer))&1 != 0
	secondTarget := second.present &&
		(bld>>(8+uint(second.layer)))&1 != 0

	// A semi-transparent sprite blends with a second
	// target underneath it whatever the mode bits say.
	if best.semi && best.layer == layerOBJ && secondTarget {
		return blend()
	}
	switch mode {
	case 1:
		if firstTarget && secondTarget {
			return blend()
		}
	case 2:
		if firstTarget {
			up := func(c int) int { return c + (31-c)*evy/16 }
			return up(r), up(gg), up(b)
		}
	case 3:
		if firstTarget {
			down := func(c int) int { return c - c*evy/16 }
			return down(r), down(gg), down(b)
		}
	}
	return r, gg, b
}

func packPixel(r, gg, b int) uint32 {
	r8 := uint32((r << 3) | (r >> 2))
	g8 := uint32((gg << 3) | (gg >> 2))
	b8 := uint32((b << 3) | (b >> 2))
	return 0xFF000000 | r8<<16 | g8<<8 | b8
}

// RenderLine renders the current line when it is
// visible, then advances the affine reference points by
// one line step. The step happens even for blanked and
// off screen lines.
func (g *GPU) RenderLine() {
	defer g.stepRefs()
	if g.line < 0 || g.line >= Height {
		return
	}
	row := g.line * Width
	dc := g.dispcnt()
	if dc&(1<<7) != 0 {
		for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
			g.frame[row+x] = 0xFFFFFFFF
		}
		return
	}
	mode := int(dc & 7)
	obj := g.buildObjLine()

	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		mask := g.windowMask(x, obj.winMsk)
		var pick picker
		for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
			if dc&(1<<uint(8+bg)) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			if mask&(1<<uint(bg)) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			var col uint16
			var ok bool
			switch {
			case mode == 0 && bg <= 3:
				col, ok = g.textPixel(bg, x)
			case mode == 1 && bg <= 1:
				col, ok = g.textPixel(bg, x)
			case mode == 1 && bg == 2:
				col, ok = g.affinePixel(bg, x)
			case mode == 2 && (bg == 2 || bg == 3):
				col, ok = g.affinePixel(bg, x)
			case (mode == 3 || mode == 4 || mode == 5) && bg == 2:
				col, ok = g.bitmapPixel(mode, x)
			}
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			pick.consider(candidate{
				present: true,
				col:     col,
				layer:   bg,
				prio:    int(g.bgcnt(bg) & 3),
			})
		}
		if dc&(1<<12) != 0 && mask&(1<<4) != 0 && obj.pix[x].present {
			pick.consider(obj.pix[x])
		}
		backdrop := candidate{
			present: true,
			col:     g.palAt(0),
			layer:   layerBD,
			prio:    99,
		}
		if !pick.best.present {
			pick.best = backdrop
			pick.second = candidate{}
		} else if !pick.second.present {
			pick.second = backdrop
		}
		r, gg, b := channels(pick.best.col)
		if mask&(1<<5) != 0 {
			r, gg, b = g.applyEffects(pick.best, pick.second)
		}
		g.frame[row+x] = packPixel(r, gg, b)
	}
}

// Command libretro builds the Go GBA core as a libretro shared
// library (go build -buildmode=c-shared). It is a thin C ABI shell
// over the system package: the frontend (the iTaK engine) registers
// its callbacks, hands us a ROM, and calls retro_run once per
// frame.
package main

/*

import "C"

import (
	"bytes"
	"hash/fnv"
	"os"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/system"

// libretro constants used here (from the public libretro API).
const (
	envSetPixelFormat  = 10
	pixelFormatXRGB888 = 1
	deviceJoypad       = 1
	joypadB            = 0
	joypadSelect       = 2
	joypadStart        = 3
	joypadUp           = 4
	joypadDown         = 5
	joypadLeft         = 6
	joypadRight        = 7
	joypadA            = 8
	joypadL            = 10
	joypadR            = 11
	regionNTSC         = 0
	gbaFPS             = 16777216.0 / 280896.0 // 59.7275
	gbaAspect          = 1.5                   // 240x160, square pixels
	memSaveRAM         = 0
	defaultAudioRate   = 32768 // SOUNDBIAS power-on rate
)

var sys *system.Machine

// declaredRate is the audio sample rate captured from the
// machine at load time and reported in the AV info. A game can
// change the machine's live rate mid-run by writing SOUNDBIAS;
// the frontend keeps consuming at the declared rate, so the
// shell resamples to it (see drainAudio).
var declaredRate = defaultAudioRate

// Save RAM plumbing. The machine hands out copies of the save
// contents, but the libretro memory interface needs a stable
// buffer the frontend can both read and write. The shell keeps
// one canonical copy: game-side changes are pulled into it
// after every frame, and frontend edits are detected by hash
// and pushed back before the next frame runs.
var (
	saveRAMCache []byte
	saveRAMHash  uint64
)

// resampler state for the SOUNDBIAS rate conversion: leftover
// input samples and the fractional read position within them.
var (
	resBuf   []int16
	resPhase float64
)

func main() {}

//export retro_api_version
func retro_api_version() C.uint { return 1 }

//export retro_init
func retro_init() { sys = system.New() }

//export retro_deinit
func retro_deinit() { sys = nil }

func retro_set_environment(cb C.retro_environment_t) { C.gba_set_environ(cb) }

//export retro_set_video_refresh
func retro_set_video_refresh(cb C.retro_video_refresh_t) { C.gba_set_video(cb) }

func retro_set_input_poll(cb C.retro_input_poll_t) { C.gba_set_input_poll(cb) }

func retro_set_input_state(cb C.retro_input_state_t) { C.gba_set_input_state(cb) }

//export retro_get_system_info

	info.library_name = C.gba_get_name()
	info.library_version = C.gba_get_version()
	info.valid_extensions = C.gba_get_exts()
	info.need_fullpath = false
	info.block_extract = false
}

//export retro_get_system_av_info

	info.geometry.base_width = system.Width
	info.geometry.base_height = system.Height
	info.geometry.max_width = system.Width
	info.geometry.max_height = system.Height
	info.geometry.aspect_ratio = gbaAspect
	info.timing.fps = gbaFPS
	rate := declaredRate
	if rate == 0 {
		rate = defaultAudioRate
	}
	info.timing.sample_rate = C.double(rate)
}

//export retro_get_region
func retro_get_region() C.unsigned { return regionNTSC }

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_gba_game_info) C.bool {
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	} else if info.path != nil {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(C.GoString(info.path))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		data = b
	} else {
		return false
	}
	if sys == nil {
		sys = system.New()
	}
	if err := sys.LoadCart(data); err != nil {
		return false
	}
	declaredRate = sys.AudioSampleRate()
	resBuf = resBuf[:0]
	resPhase = 0
	saveRAMCache = sys.SaveRAM()
	saveRAMHash = hashBytes(saveRAMCache)
	// Ask the frontend for XRGB8888 frames (what the GPU produces).
	fmt888 := C.uint32_t(pixelFormatXRGB888)
	C.gba_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&fmt888))
	return true
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() {
	sys = system.New()
	saveRAMCache = nil
	declaredRate = defaultAudioRate
}

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys != nil {
		// The machine keeps its save device contents across
		// a reset (battery backed); refresh the cache so the
		// two stay in step.
		pushSaveRAMEdits()
		sys.Reset()
		pullSaveRAM()
	}
}

func pressed(port int, id uint) bool {
	return C.gba_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceJoypad, 0, C.unsigned(id)) != 0
}

// pollPad translates libretro joypad state into the GBA button
// mask (GBATEK KEYINPUT order, via the system Button bits).
func pollPad(port int) uint32 {
	var m uint32
	if pressed(port, joypadA) {
		m |= system.ButtonA
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadB) {
		m |= system.ButtonB
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadSelect) {
		m |= system.ButtonSelect
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadStart) {
		m |= system.ButtonStart
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadRight) {
		m |= system.ButtonRight
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadLeft) {
		m |= system.ButtonLeft
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadUp) {
		m |= system.ButtonUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadDown) {
		m |= system.ButtonDown
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadR) {
		m |= system.ButtonR
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadL) {
		m |= system.ButtonL
	}
	return m
}

func hashBytes(b []byte) uint64 {
	h := fnv.New64a()
	_, _ = h.Write(b)
	return h.Sum64()
}

// pushSaveRAMEdits detects frontend edits to the exposed save
// RAM buffer and writes them into the machine.
func pushSaveRAMEdits() {
	if sys == nil || saveRAMCache == nil {
		return
	}
	if hashBytes(saveRAMCache) != saveRAMHash {
		sys.SetSaveRAM(saveRAMCache)
		pullSaveRAM()
	}
}

// pullSaveRAM refreshes the exposed buffer from the machine
// after game-side changes (and after a push, so size changes
// from EEPROM size learning show up too).
func pullSaveRAM() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	cur := sys.SaveRAM()
	if !bytes.Equal(cur, saveRAMCache) {
		saveRAMCache = cur
	}
	saveRAMHash = hashBytes(saveRAMCache)
}

// drainAudio returns this frame's audio at the declared rate.
// When the machine's live rate differs (a game rewrote
// SOUNDBIAS after load), the input is converted with a small
// linear interpolator: a fractional read position advances by
// liveRate/declaredRate per output frame over a carried
// buffer, so the conversion is continuous across frames.
// Linear interpolation is a deliberate simplicity choice for a
// rate change that in practice happens once at a game's audio
// init, before any audible output.
func drainAudio() []int16 {
	in := sys.AudioBuffer()
	live := sys.AudioSampleRate()
	if live == declaredRate || live == 0 || declaredRate == 0 {
		resBuf = resBuf[:0]
		resPhase = 0
		return in
	}
	resBuf = append(resBuf, in...)
	total := len(resBuf) / 2
	step := float64(live) / float64(declaredRate)
	var out []int16
	for resPhase+1 < float64(total) {
		i := int(resPhase)
		frac := resPhase - float64(i)
		l := lerp(resBuf[2*i], resBuf[2*i+2], frac)
		r := lerp(resBuf[2*i+1], resBuf[2*i+3], frac)
		out = append(out, l, r)
		resPhase += step
	}
	consumed := int(resPhase)
	if consumed > 0 {
		resBuf = append(resBuf[:0], resBuf[2*consumed:]...)
		resPhase -= float64(consumed)
	}
	return out
}

func lerp(a, b int16, frac float64) int16 {
	return int16(float64(a) + (float64(b)-float64(a))*frac)
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() {
	if sys == nil || sys.Cart() == nil {
		return
	}
	pushSaveRAMEdits()
	C.gba_input_poll()
	sys.SetButtons(pollPad(0))
	sys.RunFrame()
	pullSaveRAM()

	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) > 0 {
		C.gba_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]),
			C.unsigned(system.Width), C.unsigned(system.Height),
			C.size_t(system.Width*4))
	}
	ab := drainAudio()
	if len(ab) >= 2 {
		frames := len(ab) / 2
		done := int(C.gba_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&ab[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
		for i := done; i < frames; i++ {
			C.gba_audio_sample(C.int16_t(ab[2*i]), C.int16_t(ab[2*i+1]))
		}
	}
}

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.StateSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	if len(state) == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), len(state))
	copy(buf, state)
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.StateSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	cp := make([]byte, size)
	copy(cp, buf)
	if err := sys.Deserialize(cp); err != nil {
		return false
	}
	pullSaveRAM()
	return true
}

// The memory interface exposes the cartridge save contents as
// RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM through the shell-owned cache described
// above. Work RAM is not offered: the GBA's two work RAMs are
// not one contiguous region.

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.unsigned) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil || id != memSaveRAM || len(saveRAMCache) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Pointer(&saveRAMCache[0])
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.unsigned) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil || id != memSaveRAM {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(len(saveRAMCache))
}

//export retro_cheat_reset
func retro_cheat_reset() {}
