==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/periph/dma.go ====================

package periph

// DMA register offsets (relative to 0x04000000). Channel
// n occupies 12 bytes at 0xB0+0xC*n: source address word
// at +0, destination address word at +4, unit count
// halfword (CNT_L) at +8 and control halfword (CNT_H) at
// +0xA. Channels run 0xB0..0xDF overall.
const dmaBase = 0xB0

// DMA control (CNT_H) bits, in the terms used below.
const (
	dmaRepeat  = 1 << 9
	dmaIRQ     = 1 << 14
	dmaEnable  = 1 << 15
	dma32Bit   = 1 << 10
	dmaFIFOCha = 1 // first FIFO capable channel
	dmaFIFOChb = 2 // second FIFO capable channel
)

// dmaChan is one DMA channel: the registers as last
// written, plus the internal latches a transfer actually
// runs from. The latches load from the registers when the
// channel is enabled, and the count (and the destination,
// in reload mode) loads again when a repeat re-arms.
type dmaChan struct {
	sad   uint32 // source address register
	dad   uint32 // destination address register
	cntL  uint16 // unit count register, 0 means maximum
	cntH  uint16 // control register
	src   uint32 // internal source address
	dst   uint32 // internal destination address
	count uint32 // internal remaining units, 0 means idle
}

func (c *dmaChan) enabled() bool { return c.cntH&dmaEnable != 0 }

// timing returns the CNT_H start timing: 0 immediate,
// 1 VBlank, 2 HBlank, 3 special (FIFO for DMA1/DMA2).
func (c *dmaChan) timing() uint16 { return (c.cntH >> 12) & 3 }

// dstAdjust returns the CNT_H destination adjust mode:
// 0 increment, 1 decrement, 2 fixed, 3 increment with
// reload of the destination latch on repeat.
func (c *dmaChan) dstAdjust() uint16 { return (c.cntH >> 5) & 3 }

// srcAdjust returns the CNT_H source adjust mode:
// 0 increment, 1 decrement, 2 fixed. Mode 3 is prohibited
// on hardware and is treated as fixed here.
func (c *dmaChan) srcAdjust() uint16 { return (c.cntH >> 7) & 3 }

// effCount maps a CNT_L register value to the unit count
// it stands for: zero selects the channel maximum, 0x4000
// units for channels 0-2 and 0x10000 units for channel 3.
func effCount(ch int, cntL uint16) uint32 {
	if cntL != 0 {
		return uint32(cntL)
	}
	if ch == 3 {
		return 0x10000
	}
	return 0x4000
}

// adjustStep converts an adjust mode and unit size into
// the signed per unit address delta. Destination mode 3
// steps like increment during a transfer; its reload
// half lives in the repeat handling.
func adjustStep(mode uint16, size uint32) int32 {
	switch mode {
	case 0, 3:
		return int32(size)
	case 1:
		return -int32(size)
	}
	return 0
}

// FIFOSink receives sound FIFO samples from the special
// timing DMA channels. The audio hardware arrives in a
// later slice; the system wires a sink so DMA1 and DMA2
// can already deliver their bursts.
type FIFOSink interface {
	FIFOSample(channel int, value uint32)
}

// DMA is the four channel DMA controller. Transfers copy
// unit by unit through the Memory endpoint. When several
// channels are pending at one trigger, they run in
// channel order: channel 0 first, channel 3 last.
type DMA struct {
	mem  Memory
	irq  *IRQ
	sink FIFOSink
	ch   [4]dmaChan
}

// NewDMA builds a DMA controller bound to the transfer
// memory, the interrupt controller (for completion
// IRQs) and the FIFO sample sink (which may be nil, in
// which case FIFO bursts are dropped).
func NewDMA(mem Memory, irq *IRQ, sink FIFOSink) *DMA {
	return &DMA{mem: mem, irq: irq, sink: sink}
}

// loadLatches copies the registers of channel n into its
// internal address and count latches.
func (d *DMA) loadLatches(n int) {
	c := &d.ch[n]
	c.src = c.sad
	c.dst = c.dad
	c.count = effCount(n, c.cntL)
}

// byteAt returns the register byte at an IO offset in
// 0xB0..0xDF: the address words, then the CNT_L and CNT_H
// halfwords of the owning channel. CNT_L reads return the
// stored register value; on hardware the count register
// is write only and reads return open bus values, so
// returning the register is a deliberate simplification
// of this core. Address registers read back as written.
// Other offsets read as zero.
func (d *DMA) byteAt(addr uint32) byte {
	if addr < dmaBase || addr > dmaBase+0x2F {
		return 0
	}
	rel := addr - dmaBase
	c := &d.ch[rel/0xC]
	r := rel % 0xC
	switch {
	case r < 4:
		return byte(c.sad >> (8 * r))
	case r < 8:
		return byte(c.dad >> (8 * (r - 4)))
	case r < 10:
		return byte(c.cntL >> (8 * (r - 8)))
	default:
		return byte(c.cntH >> (8 * (r - 10)))
	}
}

// writeByte applies one byte of a register write. Only
// the CNT_H high byte carries the enable bit, so the
// enable transition check lives there: when a write sets
// enable on a disabled channel, the internal latches load
// from the registers, and an immediate timing channel
// runs its transfer synchronously inside the write.
func (d *DMA) writeByte(addr uint32, b byte) {
	if addr < dmaBase || addr > dmaBase+0x2F {
		return
	}
	rel := addr - dmaBase
	n := int(rel / 0xC)
	c := &d.ch[n]
	r := rel % 0xC
	switch {
	case r < 4:
		s := 8 * r
		c.sad = (c.sad &^ (0xFF << s)) | uint32(b)<<s
	case r < 8:
		s := 8 * (r - 4)
		c.dad = (c.dad &^ (0xFF << s)) | uint32(b)<<s
	case r < 10:
		if r == 8 {
			c.cntL = (c.cntL & 0xFF00) | uint16(b)
		} else {
			c.cntL = (c.cntL & 0x00FF) | uint16(b)<<8
		}
	case r == 10:
		c.cntH = (c.cntH & 0xFF00) | uint16(b)
	default: // r == 11, the CNT_H high byte
		was := c.enabled()
		c.cntH = (c.cntH & 0x00FF) | uint16(b)<<8
		if !was && c.enabled() {
			d.loadLatches(n)
			if c.timing() == 0 {
				d.runTransfer(n)
			}
		}
	}
}

// ReadReg reads size bytes at off (0xB0..0xDF), composed
// little endian from the register values as last written.
func (d *DMA) ReadReg(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return 0
	}
	return compose(off, size, d.byteAt)
}

// WriteReg writes size bytes at off (0xB0..0xDF),
// decomposed little endian. The write that raises the
// enable bit on a channel loads its latches and, for
// immediate timing, performs the whole transfer before
// returning (see writeByte).
func (d *DMA) WriteReg(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return
	}
	decompose(off, size, val, d.writeByte)
}

// runTransfer performs the pending transfer of channel n
// from its internal latches, unit by unit, then handles
// completion: the completion IRQ is raised when CNT_H
// asks for it; a repeat channel reloads its count (and
// its destination latch when the destination adjust is
// the reload mode) and stays enabled for the next
// trigger, while a one shot channel has its enable bit
// cleared.
func (d *DMA) runTransfer(n int) {
	c := &d.ch[n]
	if d.mem == nil || c.count == 0 {
		return
	}
	size := uint32(2)
	if c.cntH&dma32Bit != 0 {
		size = 4
	}
	srcStep := adjustStep(c.srcAdjust(), size)
	dstStep := adjustStep(c.dstAdjust(), size)
	if c.srcAdjust() == 3 {
		srcStep = 0 // prohibited source mode acts as fixed
	}
	for c.count > 0 {
		v := d.mem.Read(c.src, int(size))
		d.mem.Write(c.dst, int(size), v)
		c.src = uint32(int32(c.src) + srcStep)
		c.dst = uint32(int32(c.dst) + dstStep)
		c.count--
	}
	if c.cntH&dmaIRQ != 0 && d.irq != nil {
		d.irq.Raise(uint16(IRQDMA0 << n))
	}
	if c.cntH&dmaRepeat != 0 {
		c.count = effCount(n, c.cntL)
		if c.dstAdjust() == 3 {
			c.dst = c.dad
		}
	} else {
		c.cntH &^= dmaEnable
	}
}

// trigger runs every enabled channel whose start timing
// is want and whose internal count is loaded, in channel
// order.
func (d *DMA) trigger(want uint16) {
	for n := range d.ch {
		c := &d.ch[n]
		if c.enabled() && c.timing() == want && c.count > 0 {
			d.runTransfer(n)
		}
	}
}

// OnVBlank delivers the vertical blank trigger: enabled
// channels with VBlank timing run their pending
// transfer.
func (d *DMA) OnVBlank() { d.trigger(1) }

// OnHBlank delivers the horizontal blank trigger:
// enabled channels with HBlank timing run their pending
// transfer.
func (d *DMA) OnHBlank() { d.trigger(2) }

// OnFIFO delivers one sound FIFO request for a channel.
// Only DMA1 and DMA2 have FIFO wiring, and only in
// special timing while enabled: each request moves
// exactly four 32 bit words from the internal source
// (advanced by the source adjust mode) to the sink. The
// destination is the fixed FIFO register, so it never
// moves; no completion IRQ fires per burst and the
// channel stays armed for the next request. Anything else
// (DMA0 or DMA3, a disabled channel, a channel in another
// timing) does nothing.
func (d *DMA) OnFIFO(channel int) {
	if channel != dmaFIFOCha && channel != dmaFIFOChb {
		return
	}
	c := &d.ch[channel]
	if !c.enabled() || c.timing() != 3 || d.mem == nil || d.sink == nil {
		return
	}
	step := adjustStep(c.srcAdjust(), 4)
	if c.srcAdjust() == 3 {
		step = 0
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		v := d.mem.Read(c.src, 4)
		d.sink.FIFOSample(channel, v)
		c.src = uint32(int32(c.src) + step)
	}
}

// DMAStateSize is the serialized size of the DMA state:
// 24 bytes per channel times 4 channels.
//
// Layout, per channel at 24n: source register word at 0,
// destination register word at 4, CNT_L halfword at 8,
// CNT_H halfword at 10, internal source word at 12,
// internal destination word at 16, internal count word at
// 20, all little endian.
const DMAStateSize = 4 * 24

// Serialize writes the DMA state to dst, which must be
// at least DMAStateSize bytes, and returns the number of
// bytes written.
func (d *DMA) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	for n := range d.ch {
		c := &d.ch[n]
		o := 24 * n
		put32(dst, o+0, c.sad)
		put32(dst, o+4, c.dad)
		put16(dst, o+8, c.cntL)
		put16(dst, o+10, c.cntH)
		put32(dst, o+12, c.src)
		put32(dst, o+16, c.dst)
		put32(dst, o+20, c.count)
	}
	return DMAStateSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It
// reports false, leaving the state untouched, when src is
// too short.
func (d *DMA) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < DMAStateSize {
		return false
	}
	for n := range d.ch {
		c := &d.ch[n]
		o := 24 * n
		c.sad = get32(src, o+0)
		c.dad = get32(src, o+4)
		c.cntL = get16(src, o+8)
		c.cntH = get16(src, o+10)
		c.src = get32(src, o+12)
		c.dst = get32(src, o+16)
		c.count = get32(src, o+20)
	}
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/periph/irq.go ====================

package periph

// Interrupt source bits, in IE/IF register order.
const (
	IRQVBlank  = 1 << 0
	IRQHBlank  = 1 << 1
	IRQVCount  = 1 << 2
	IRQTimer0  = 1 << 3
	IRQTimer1  = 1 << 4
	IRQTimer2  = 1 << 5
	IRQTimer3  = 1 << 6
	IRQSerial  = 1 << 7
	IRQDMA0    = 1 << 8
	IRQDMA1    = 1 << 9
	IRQDMA2    = 1 << 10
	IRQDMA3    = 1 << 11
	IRQKeypad  = 1 << 12
	IRQGamePak = 1 << 13
)

// irqMask covers the 14 meaningful IE/IF bits.
const irqMask = 0x3FFF

// Register offsets handled by IRQ (relative to 0x04000000).
const (
	regIE  = 0x200
	regIF  = 0x202
	regIME = 0x208
)

// IRQ is the interrupt controller state: the IE enable
// mask, the IF flag register and the IME master switch.
// A source raises its IF bit through Raise; the CPU side
// is interrupted only when the bit is also enabled in IE
// and IME bit 0 is set (see Asserted).
type IRQ struct {
	ie     uint16 // stored masked to irqMask
	iflags uint16
	ime    uint8 // 0 or 1
}

// NewIRQ returns an interrupt controller in power-on
// state: nothing enabled, no flags, master switch off.
func NewIRQ() *IRQ { return &IRQ{} }

// byteAt returns the register byte at an IO offset. The
// offsets owned here are the IE halfword at 0x200, the IF
// halfword at 0x202 and the IME word at 0x208 (whose upper
// three bytes read as zero); anything else reads as zero.
func (q *IRQ) byteAt(addr uint32) byte {
	switch addr {
	case regIE:
		return byte(q.ie)
	case regIE + 1:
		return byte(q.ie >> 8)
	case regIF:
		return byte(q.iflags)
	case regIF + 1:
		return byte(q.iflags >> 8)
	case regIME:
		return q.ime
	}
	return 0
}

// writeByte applies one byte of a register write. IE
// bytes are plain stores. IF bytes follow the hardware
// acknowledge rule: a bit written as 1 clears the flag, a
// bit written as 0 leaves it, so software confirms an
// interrupt by writing back the bits it handled. The IME
// low byte keeps only bit 0.
func (q *IRQ) writeByte(addr uint32, b byte) {
	switch addr {
	case regIE:
		q.ie = (q.ie & 0xFF00) | uint16(b)
		q.ie &= irqMask
	case regIE + 1:
		q.ie = (q.ie & 0x00FF) | uint16(b)<<8
		q.ie &= irqMask
	case regIF:
		q.iflags &^= uint16(b)
	case regIF + 1:
		q.iflags &^= uint16(b) << 8
	case regIME:
		q.ime = b & 1
	}
}

// ReadReg reads size bytes at off, composed little endian
// across the IE/IF pair or the IME word. Offsets outside
// the owned set read as zero.
func (q *IRQ) ReadReg(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return 0
	}
	return compose(off, size, q.byteAt)
}

// WriteReg writes size bytes at off, decomposed little
// endian; the IF lanes acknowledge instead of storing
// (see writeByte). Writes to offsets outside the owned
// set are ignored.
func (q *IRQ) WriteReg(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return
	}
	decompose(off, size, val, q.writeByte)
}

// Raise sets the given IF flag bits. Bits outside the 14
// meaningful ones are dropped.
func (q *IRQ) Raise(mask uint16) {
	q.iflags |= mask & irqMask
}

// Pending returns the flags that are both raised and
// enabled (IE AND IF). The IME switch is not part of this
// value; Asserted folds it in.
func (q *IRQ) Pending() uint16 {
	return q.ie & q.iflags
}

// Asserted reports whether an interrupt should reach the
// CPU: the master switch is on and at least one enabled
// flag is raised.
func (q *IRQ) Asserted() bool {
	return q.ime != 0 && q.Pending() != 0
}

// IRQStateSize is the serialized size of the IRQ state.
//
// Layout: IE as a little endian halfword at 0, IF as a
// little endian halfword at 2, IME (0 or 1) at 4, and one
// reserved zero byte at 5.
const IRQStateSize = 6

// Serialize writes the IRQ state to dst, which must be
// at least IRQStateSize bytes, and returns the number of
// bytes written.
func (q *IRQ) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	put16(dst, 0, q.ie)
	put16(dst, 2, q.iflags)
	dst[4] = q.ime
	dst[5] = 0
	return IRQStateSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It
// reports false, leaving the state untouched, when src is
// too short.
func (q *IRQ) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < IRQStateSize {
		return false
	}
	q.ie = get16(src, 0) & irqMask
	q.iflags = get16(src, 2) & irqMask
	q.ime = src[4] & 1
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/periph/keypad.go ====================

package periph

// Keypad register offsets (relative to 0x04000000):
// KEYINPUT at 0x130, KEYCNT at 0x132.
const (
	regKeyInput = 0x130
	regKeyCnt   = 0x132
)

// keyMask covers the ten button bits, in GBATEK KEYINPUT
// bit order: A, B, Select, Start, Right, Left, Up, Down,
// R, L at bits 0..9.
const keyMask = 0x3FF

// KEYCNT bits, in the terms used below.
const (
	keyCntIRQEnable = 1 << 14
	keyCntAnd       = 1 << 15
)

// Keypad is the controller input state: the pressed
// button mask in pressed set form and the KEYCNT
// interrupt control register. KEYINPUT presents the mask
// active low, as the hardware does.
type Keypad struct {
	buttons     uint32 // pressed set form, low 10 bits
	keycnt      uint16 // stored as written
	lastCond    bool   // condition at the last evaluation
	lastEnabled bool   // KEYCNT IRQ enable at the last evaluation
}

// NewKeypad returns a keypad in power-on state: nothing
// pressed, KEYCNT zero (IRQ off, OR condition).
func NewKeypad() *Keypad { return &Keypad{} }

// inputValue is the KEYINPUT halfword: bits 0-9 are the
// key states active low (0 means pressed), and the
// unused bits 10-15 read as zero.
func (k *Keypad) inputValue() uint16 {
	return uint16(^k.buttons) & keyMask
}

// condition evaluates the KEYCNT interrupt condition
// against the current buttons: with bit 15 clear, any
// selected key pressed is enough (OR); with bit 15 set,
// every selected key must be pressed (AND). Selecting no
// keys never satisfies either form.
func (k *Keypad) condition() bool {
	sel := uint32(k.keycnt) & keyMask
	if sel == 0 {
		return false
	}
	hit := k.buttons & sel
	if k.keycnt&keyCntAnd != 0 {
		return hit == sel
	}
	return hit != 0
}

// SetButtons stores a new pressed mask (GBATEK KEYINPUT
// bit order, set bit means pressed) and evaluates the
// KEYCNT condition: when the interrupt condition as a
// whole (condition true and KEYCNT IRQ enable set) moves
// from false to true, the keypad IRQ is raised. Folding
// the enable bit into the evaluated edge is what lets a
// KEYCNT write that arms the interrupt while keys are
// already held fire on the next SetButtons call, which
// the system makes once per frame. Evaluation therefore
// lags such a write by at most one frame; that latency
// is a deliberate simplification of this core.
func (k *Keypad) SetButtons(mask uint32, irq *IRQ) {
	k.buttons = mask & keyMask
	cond := k.condition()
	enabled := k.keycnt&keyCntIRQEnable != 0
	if cond && enabled && !(k.lastCond && k.lastEnabled) && irq != nil {
		irq.Raise(IRQKeypad)
	}
	k.lastCond = cond
	k.lastEnabled = enabled
}

// Buttons returns the stored pressed mask, in pressed
// set form with only the low 10 bits meaningful.
func (k *Keypad) Buttons() uint32 { return k.buttons }

// byteAt returns the register byte at an IO offset:
// KEYINPUT bytes at 0x130..0x131, KEYCNT bytes at
// 0x132..0x133. Other offsets read as zero.
func (k *Keypad) byteAt(addr uint32) byte {
	switch addr {
	case regKeyInput:
		return byte(k.inputValue())
	case regKeyInput + 1:
		return byte(k.inputValue() >> 8)
	case regKeyCnt:
		return byte(k.keycnt)
	case regKeyCnt + 1:
		return byte(k.keycnt >> 8)
	}
	return 0
}

// writeByte applies one byte of a register write. Only
// KEYCNT is writable; KEYINPUT writes are ignored.
func (k *Keypad) writeByte(addr uint32, b byte) {
	switch addr {
	case regKeyCnt:
		k.keycnt = (k.keycnt & 0xFF00) | uint16(b)
	case regKeyCnt + 1:
		k.keycnt = (k.keycnt & 0x00FF) | uint16(b)<<8
	}
}

// ReadReg reads size bytes at off (0x130 KEYINPUT,
// 0x132 KEYCNT), composed little endian.
func (k *Keypad) ReadReg(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return 0
	}
	return compose(off, size, k.byteAt)
}

// WriteReg writes size bytes at off, decomposed little
// endian. KEYCNT stores; writes to KEYINPUT are ignored.
// The write itself does not evaluate the IRQ condition
// (it has no IRQ handle); SetButtons does, and the
// system calls it every frame (see SetButtons).
func (k *Keypad) WriteReg(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return
	}
	decompose(off, size, val, k.writeByte)
}

// KeypadStateSize is the serialized size of the keypad
// state.
//
// Layout: buttons mask word at 0 (little endian, low 10
// bits meaningful), KEYCNT halfword at 4, and one flags
// byte at 6 (bit 0 the last evaluated condition, bit 1
// the last evaluated IRQ enable), with one reserved zero
// byte at 7.
const KeypadStateSize = 8

// Serialize writes the keypad state to dst, which must
// be at least KeypadStateSize bytes, and returns the
// number of bytes written.
func (k *Keypad) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	put32(dst, 0, k.buttons)
	put16(dst, 4, k.keycnt)
	var flags byte
	if k.lastCond {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if k.lastEnabled {
		flags |= 2
	}
	dst[6] = flags
	dst[7] = 0
	return KeypadStateSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It
// reports false, leaving the state untouched, when src is
// too short.
func (k *Keypad) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < KeypadStateSize {
		return false
	}
	k.buttons = get32(src, 0) & keyMask
	k.keycnt = get16(src, 4)
	k.lastCond = src[6]&1 != 0
	k.lastEnabled = src[6]&2 != 0
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/periph/periph.go ====================

// Package periph implements the GBA interrupt controller,
// the four hardware timers, the four DMA channels and the
// keypad registers for GBA-2, written from GBATEK semantics.
//
// All register offsets in this package are relative to the
// IO base 0x04000000. The system package owns routing: it
// forwards each IO access to the one component that owns
// the offset, with the access size (1, 2 or 4 bytes), and
// multi byte accesses compose little endian across the
// registers of a component. The CPU steps in whole
// instructions and reports cycle counts, so the timers are
// driven by Advance calls with elapsed cycles, and DMA and
// keypad events arrive as explicit trigger calls from the
// system at line and frame boundaries.
package periph

import "encoding/binary"

// Memory is the transfer endpoint DMA works through: the
// system bus, narrowed to plain reads and writes. Read
// returns the raw aligned unit (a 4 byte read returns the
// word at addr&^3, a 2 byte read the halfword at addr&^1
// zero extended); Write stores a unit the same way.
type Memory interface {
	Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32
	Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32)
}

// validSize reports whether size is a routable IO access
// width (byte, halfword or word).
func validSize(size int) bool {
	return size == 1 || size == 2 || size == 4
}

// compose builds a little endian read of size bytes
// starting at off from per byte values.
func compose(off uint32, size int, byteAt func(addr uint32) byte) uint32 {
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		v |= uint32(byteAt(off+uint32(i))) << (8 * i)
	}
	return v
}

// decompose splits a little endian write of size bytes
// starting at off into per byte writes, lowest byte
// first, so side effects that depend on register order
// (a reload write landing before the enable write that
// consumes it, inside one word access) see the same
// sequence the hardware register file would.
func decompose(off uint32, size int, val uint32, writeByte func(addr uint32, b byte)) {
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		writeByte(off+uint32(i), byte(val>>(8*i)))
	}
}

// put16 stores v little endian at dst[i:].
func put16(dst []byte, i int, v uint16) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(dst[i:], v)
}

// put32 stores v little endian at dst[i:].
func put32(dst []byte, i int, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[i:], v)
}

// get16 loads a little endian halfword from src[i:].
func get16(src []byte, i int) uint16 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(src[i:])
}

// get32 loads a little endian word from src[i:].
func get32(src []byte, i int) uint32 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(src[i:])
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/periph/periph_test.go ====================

package periph

import "testing"

// mockMem is a flat Memory for DMA tests: a 256 KB EWRAM
// region at 0x02000000 and a 32 KB IWRAM region at
// 0x03000000, both indexed by masking the address into
// the region. Accesses behave like the bus: wide accesses
// align down and move the unit little endian.
type mockMem struct {
	ew [0x40000]byte
	iw [0x8000]byte
}

func (m *mockMem) byteAt(addr uint32) *byte {
	switch addr >> 24 {
	case 0x02:
		return &m.ew[addr&0x3FFFF]
	case 0x03:
		return &m.iw[addr&0x7FFF]
	}
	return nil
}

func (m *mockMem) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if size == 2 {
		addr &^= 1
	} else if size == 4 {
		addr &^= 3
	}
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		if p := m.byteAt(addr + uint32(i)); p != nil {
			v |= uint32(*p) << (8 * i)
		}
	}
	return v
}

func (m *mockMem) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if size == 2 {
		addr &^= 1
	} else if size == 4 {
		addr &^= 3
	}
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		if p := m.byteAt(addr + uint32(i)); p != nil {
			*p = byte(val >> (8 * i))
		}
	}
}

// fifoSink records FIFO samples in delivery order.
type fifoSample struct {
	channel int
	value   uint32
}

type fifoSink struct {
	samples []fifoSample
}

func (s *fifoSink) FIFOSample(channel int, value uint32) {
	s.samples = append(s.samples, fifoSample{channel, value})
}

// DMA register offsets for channel ch.
func dmaSAD(ch int) uint32  { return uint32(0xB0 + 0xC*ch) }
func dmaDAD(ch int) uint32  { return uint32(0xB4 + 0xC*ch) }
func dmaCntL(ch int) uint32 { return uint32(0xB8 + 0xC*ch) }
func dmaCntH(ch int) uint32 { return uint32(0xBA + 0xC*ch) }

// armDMA programs a channel's registers, control last so
// the enable write sees the full configuration.
func armDMA(d *DMA, ch int, sad, dad uint32, count, cntH uint16) {
	d.WriteReg(dmaSAD(ch), 4, sad)
	d.WriteReg(dmaDAD(ch), 4, dad)
	d.WriteReg(dmaCntL(ch), 2, uint32(count))
	d.WriteReg(dmaCntH(ch), 2, uint32(cntH))
}

const (
	cntHEnable = 1 << 15
	cntHIRQ    = 1 << 14
	cntH32     = 1 << 10
	cntHRepeat = 1 << 9
)

func TestIRQ(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("RaisePendingAssertedGating", func(t *testing.T) {
		q := NewIRQ()
		q.Raise(IRQVBlank)
		if got := q.Pending(); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("Pending with IE clear = %#x, want 0", got)
		}
		if q.Asserted() {
			t.Fatal("Asserted with IE clear, want false")
		}
		q.WriteReg(0x200, 2, IRQVBlank)
		if got := q.Pending(); got != IRQVBlank {
			t.Fatalf("Pending = %#x, want %#x", got, IRQVBlank)
		}
		if q.Asserted() {
			t.Fatal("Asserted with IME clear, want false")
		}
		q.WriteReg(0x208, 2, 1)
		if !q.Asserted() {
			t.Fatal("Asserted with IME set and pending bit, want true")
		}
	})

	t.Run("IFAcknowledgeClearsOnlyWrittenBits", func(t *testing.T) {
		q := NewIRQ()
		q.Raise(IRQVBlank | IRQHBlank | IRQTimer0)
		q.WriteReg(0x202, 2, IRQVBlank|IRQTimer0)
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got != IRQHBlank {
			t.Fatalf("IF after ack = %#x, want %#x", got, IRQHBlank)
		}
		// A zero write changes nothing; a byte write with
		// all ones clears the whole low byte.
		q.WriteReg(0x202, 2, 0)
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got != IRQHBlank {
			t.Fatalf("IF after zero ack = %#x, want %#x", got, IRQHBlank)
		}
		q.WriteReg(0x202, 1, 0xFF)
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("IF after byte ack = %#x, want 0", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("IEMaskingAndComposedAccess", func(t *testing.T) {
		q := NewIRQ()
		q.WriteReg(0x200, 2, 0xFFFF)
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x200, 2); got != 0x3FFF {
			t.Fatalf("IE = %#x, want 0x3FFF", got)
		}
		q.WriteReg(0x200, 2, 0x0003)
		q.Raise(0x0005)
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x200, 4); got != 0x00050003 {
			t.Fatalf("IE/IF word = %#x, want 0x00050003", got)
		}
		// IME keeps bit 0 only and reads back 0 or 1.
		q.WriteReg(0x208, 4, 0xFFFFFFFE)
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x208, 4); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("IME = %#x, want 0", got)
		}
		q.WriteReg(0x208, 4, 0xFFFFFFFF)
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x208, 4); got != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("IME = %#x, want 1", got)
		}
		if got := q.ReadReg(0x204, 2); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("unowned offset read = %#x, want 0", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("SerializeRoundTrip", func(t *testing.T) {
		q := NewIRQ()
		q.WriteReg(0x200, 2, 0x1555)
		q.Raise(IRQTimer2 | IRQKeypad)
		q.WriteReg(0x208, 2, 1)
		buf := make([]byte, IRQStateSize)
		if n := q.Serialize(buf); n != IRQStateSize {
			t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d, want %d", n, IRQStateSize)
		}
		r := NewIRQ()
		if !r.Deserialize(buf) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize returned false")
		}
		if r.ReadReg(0x200, 2) != 0x1555 ||
			r.ReadReg(0x202, 2) != q.ReadReg(0x202, 2) ||
			r.ReadReg(0x208, 2) != 1 {
			t.Fatal("round trip state mismatch")
		}
		if r.Deserialize(buf[:IRQStateSize-1]) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize of short input returned true")
		}
	})
}

func TestTimers(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("Prescaler64", func(t *testing.T) {
		tm := NewTimers()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		tm.WriteReg(0x100, 2, 0xFFF0)    // CNT_L while stopped
		tm.WriteReg(0x102, 2, 0x80|0x01) // enable, prescaler 64
		tm.Advance(64*5, irq)
		if got := tm.Counter(0); got != 0xFFF5 {
			t.Fatalf("counter = %#x, want 0xFFF5", got)
		}
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQTimer0 != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("IF = %#x, timer0 bit set without overflow", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("OverflowReloadsAndRaisesIRQ", func(t *testing.T) {
		tm := NewTimers()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		tm.WriteReg(0x100, 2, 0xFFFE)
		tm.WriteReg(0x102, 2, 0x80|0x40) // enable, IRQ on, period 1
		tm.Advance(2, irq)
		if got := tm.Counter(0); got != 0xFFFE {
			t.Fatalf("counter = %#x, want 0xFFFE (reloaded)", got)
		}
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQTimer0 == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("IF = %#x, want timer0 bit set", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("Cascade", func(t *testing.T) {
		tm := NewTimers()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		tm.WriteReg(0x100, 2, 0xFFFF)    // ch0 reload
		tm.WriteReg(0x102, 2, 0x80)      // ch0 enable, period 1
		tm.WriteReg(0x104, 2, 0x1000)    // ch1 reload
		tm.WriteReg(0x106, 2, 0x80|0x04) // ch1 enable, cascade
		tm.Advance(3, irq)
		if got := tm.Counter(1); got != 0x1003 {
			t.Fatalf("ch1 counter = %#x, want 0x1003", got)
		}
		if got := tm.Counter(0); got != 0xFFFF {
			t.Fatalf("ch0 counter = %#x, want 0xFFFF (reloaded)", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("StoppedTimerAndCNTLPrime", func(t *testing.T) {
		tm := NewTimers()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		tm.WriteReg(0x100, 2, 0x1234)
		if got := tm.Counter(0); got != 0x1234 {
			t.Fatalf("counter after CNT_L write = %#x, want 0x1234", got)
		}
		tm.Advance(100000, irq)
		if got := tm.Counter(0); got != 0x1234 {
			t.Fatalf("stopped counter = %#x, want 0x1234", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("SerializeRoundTripKeepsDivider", func(t *testing.T) {
		tm := NewTimers()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		tm.WriteReg(0x100, 2, 0)
		tm.WriteReg(0x102, 2, 0x80|0x01) // prescaler 64
		tm.Advance(32, irq)              // half a period banked
		buf := make([]byte, TimersStateSize)
		if n := tm.Serialize(buf); n != TimersStateSize {
			t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d, want %d", n, TimersStateSize)
		}
		r := NewTimers()
		if !r.Deserialize(buf) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize returned false")
		}
		r.Advance(32, irq) // completes the banked period
		if got := r.Counter(0); got != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("counter = %d, want 1 (divider survived)", got)
		}
		if r.Deserialize(buf[:TimersStateSize-1]) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize of short input returned true")
		}
	})
}

func TestDMA(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("Immediate32BitCopy", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		irq := NewIRQ()
		d := NewDMA(mem, irq, &fifoSink{})
		want := []uint32{0x11223344, 0x55667788, 0x99AABBCC, 0xDDEEFF00}
		for i, v := range want {
			mem.Write(0x02000000+uint32(4*i), 4, v)
		}
		armDMA(d, 0, 0x02000000, 0x03000000, 4, cntHEnable|cntH32)
		for i, w := range want {
			if got := mem.Read(0x03000000+uint32(4*i), 4); got != w {
				t.Fatalf("dest word %d = %#x, want %#x", i, got, w)
			}
		}
		if got := d.ReadReg(dmaCntH(0), 2); got&cntHEnable != 0 {
			t.Fatal("enable still set after one shot transfer")
		}
		// Registers read back as written.
		if got := d.ReadReg(dmaSAD(0), 4); got != 0x02000000 {
			t.Fatalf("SAD readback = %#x, want 0x02000000", got)
		}
		if got := d.ReadReg(dmaCntL(0), 2); got != 4 {
			t.Fatalf("CNT_L readback = %d, want 4", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("FixedSourceFill", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		d := NewDMA(mem, NewIRQ(), &fifoSink{})
		mem.Write(0x02000100, 4, 0xCAFEBABE)
		// Source adjust 2 (fixed), destination increment.
		armDMA(d, 1, 0x02000100, 0x03000000, 3, cntHEnable|cntH32|(2<<7))
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			if got := mem.Read(0x03000000+uint32(4*i), 4); got != 0xCAFEBABE {
				t.Fatalf("dest word %d = %#x, want 0xCAFEBABE", i, got)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("DecrementDest", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		d := NewDMA(mem, NewIRQ(), &fifoSink{})
		vals := []uint32{0xAAAA0001, 0xBBBB0002, 0xCCCC0003}
		for i, v := range vals {
			mem.Write(0x02000000+uint32(4*i), 4, v)
		}
		// Destination adjust 1 (decrement) from the top slot.
		armDMA(d, 2, 0x02000000, 0x03000008, 3, cntHEnable|cntH32|(1<<5))
		for i, w := range []uint32{vals[2], vals[1], vals[0]} {
			if got := mem.Read(0x03000000+uint32(4*i), 4); got != w {
				t.Fatalf("dest word %d = %#x, want %#x", i, got, w)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("HalfwordUnits", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		d := NewDMA(mem, NewIRQ(), &fifoSink{})
		mem.Write(0x02000000, 2, 0x1234)
		mem.Write(0x02000002, 2, 0x5678)
		armDMA(d, 0, 0x02000000, 0x03000000, 2, cntHEnable) // 16 bit units
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0x56781234 {
			t.Fatalf("dest = %#x, want 0x56781234", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("RepeatHBlankDestReload", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		d := NewDMA(mem, NewIRQ(), &fifoSink{})
		words := []uint32{0x11110000, 0x22220000, 0x33330000, 0x44440000}
		for i, v := range words {
			mem.Write(0x02000000+uint32(4*i), 4, v)
		}
		cntH := cntHEnable | cntHRepeat | cntH32 | (2 << 12) | (3 << 5)
		armDMA(d, 2, 0x02000000, 0x03000000, 2, uint16(cntH))
		d.OnHBlank()
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000000, 4); got != words[0] {
			t.Fatalf("first burst dest[0] = %#x, want %#x", got, words[0])
		}
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000004, 4); got != words[1] {
			t.Fatalf("first burst dest[1] = %#x, want %#x", got, words[1])
		}
		mem.Write(0x03000000, 4, 0)
		mem.Write(0x03000004, 4, 0)
		d.OnHBlank()
		// Destination latch reloaded: the second burst
		// lands at the start again, carrying the next
		// source words.
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000000, 4); got != words[2] {
			t.Fatalf("second burst dest[0] = %#x, want %#x", got, words[2])
		}
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000004, 4); got != words[3] {
			t.Fatalf("second burst dest[1] = %#x, want %#x", got, words[3])
		}
		if got := d.ReadReg(dmaCntH(2), 2); got&cntHEnable == 0 {
			t.Fatal("repeat channel lost its enable bit")
		}
	})

	t.Run("VBlankTimingWaitsForTrigger", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		d := NewDMA(mem, NewIRQ(), &fifoSink{})
		mem.Write(0x02000000, 4, 0xFEEDFACE)
		armDMA(d, 3, 0x02000000, 0x03000000, 1, cntHEnable|cntH32|(1<<12))
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("dest before trigger = %#x, want 0", got)
		}
		d.OnHBlank() // wrong trigger: must not run
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("dest after HBlank = %#x, want 0", got)
		}
		d.OnVBlank()
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0xFEEDFACE {
			t.Fatalf("dest after VBlank = %#x, want 0xFEEDFACE", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("FIFOChannel1", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		sink := &fifoSink{}
		d := NewDMA(mem, NewIRQ(), sink)
		want := []uint32{0x50000001, 0x50000002, 0x50000003, 0x50000004}
		for i, v := range want {
			mem.Write(0x02000000+uint32(4*i), 4, v)
		}
		armDMA(d, 1, 0x02000000, 0x040000A0, 0, cntHEnable|cntH32|(3<<12))
		d.OnFIFO(1)
		if len(sink.samples) != 4 {
			t.Fatalf("FIFO delivered %d samples, want 4", len(sink.samples))
		}
		for i, s := range sink.samples {
			if s.channel != 1 || s.value != want[i] {
				t.Fatalf("sample %d = (%d, %#x), want (1, %#x)", i, s.channel, s.value, want[i])
			}
		}
		// A disabled channel and the non FIFO channels
		// deliver nothing.
		d.OnFIFO(2)
		armDMA(d, 0, 0x02000000, 0x040000A0, 0, cntHEnable|cntH32|(3<<12))
		d.OnFIFO(0)
		if len(sink.samples) != 4 {
			t.Fatalf("FIFO delivered %d samples after dead triggers, want 4", len(sink.samples))
		}
	})

	t.Run("IRQOnCompletion", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		irq := NewIRQ()
		d := NewDMA(mem, irq, &fifoSink{})
		mem.Write(0x02000000, 4, 0x12345678)
		armDMA(d, 0, 0x02000000, 0x03000000, 1, cntHEnable|cntH32|cntHIRQ)
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQDMA0 == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("IF = %#x, want DMA0 bit set", got)
		}
	})

	t.Run("SerializeRoundTrip", func(t *testing.T) {
		mem := &mockMem{}
		irq := NewIRQ()
		d := NewDMA(mem, irq, &fifoSink{})
		mem.Write(0x02000000, 4, 0x0BADF00D)
		armDMA(d, 1, 0x02000000, 0x03000000, 1, cntHEnable|cntH32|(1<<12))
		buf := make([]byte, DMAStateSize)
		if n := d.Serialize(buf); n != DMAStateSize {
			t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d, want %d", n, DMAStateSize)
		}
		r := NewDMA(mem, irq, &fifoSink{})
		if !r.Deserialize(buf) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize returned false")
		}
		r.OnVBlank()
		if got := mem.Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0x0BADF00D {
			t.Fatalf("dest after restored trigger = %#x, want 0x0BADF00D", got)
		}
		if r.Deserialize(buf[:DMAStateSize-1]) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize of short input returned true")
		}
	})
}

func TestKeypad(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("ActiveLowInput", func(t *testing.T) {
		k := NewKeypad()
		if got := k.ReadReg(0x130, 2); got != 0x3FF {
			t.Fatalf("KEYINPUT idle = %#x, want 0x3FF", got)
		}
		k.SetButtons(1<<0|1<<9, NewIRQ()) // A and L
		want := uint32(0x3FF) &^ (1<<0 | 1<<9)
		if got := k.ReadReg(0x130, 2); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("KEYINPUT = %#x, want %#x", got, want)
		}
		if got := k.Buttons(); got != 1<<0|1<<9 {
			t.Fatalf("Buttons = %#x, want %#x", got, 1<<0|1<<9)
		}
		// KEYINPUT ignores writes.
		k.WriteReg(0x130, 2, 0)
		if got := k.ReadReg(0x130, 2); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("KEYINPUT after write = %#x, want %#x", got, want)
		}
	})

	t.Run("ORConditionRaises", func(t *testing.T) {
		k := NewKeypad()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		k.WriteReg(0x132, 2, (1<<0)|(1<<14)) // select A, IRQ on, OR
		k.SetButtons(0, irq)
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQKeypad != 0 {
			t.Fatal("keypad IRQ raised with nothing pressed")
		}
		k.SetButtons(1<<0, irq)
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQKeypad == 0 {
			t.Fatal("keypad IRQ not raised on selected press")
		}
		// Holding the key does not raise twice: acknowledge
		// and re-evaluate, the flag must stay clear.
		irq.WriteReg(0x202, 2, IRQKeypad)
		k.SetButtons(1<<0, irq)
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQKeypad != 0 {
			t.Fatal("keypad IRQ re-raised while key held")
		}
	})

	t.Run("ANDConditionRequiresAll", func(t *testing.T) {
		k := NewKeypad()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		k.WriteReg(0x132, 2, (1<<0)|(1<<1)|(1<<14)|(1<<15)) // A+B, IRQ on, AND
		k.SetButtons(1<<0, irq)
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQKeypad != 0 {
			t.Fatal("keypad IRQ raised with only one of two AND keys")
		}
		k.SetButtons(1<<0|1<<1, irq)
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQKeypad == 0 {
			t.Fatal("keypad IRQ not raised with both AND keys pressed")
		}
	})

	t.Run("NoRaiseWhenIRQDisabled", func(t *testing.T) {
		k := NewKeypad()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		k.WriteReg(0x132, 2, 1<<0) // select A, IRQ enable clear
		k.SetButtons(1<<0, irq)
		if got := irq.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQKeypad != 0 {
			t.Fatal("keypad IRQ raised with KEYCNT bit 14 clear")
		}
	})

	t.Run("SerializeRoundTrip", func(t *testing.T) {
		k := NewKeypad()
		irq := NewIRQ()
		k.WriteReg(0x132, 2, (1<<3)|(1<<14))
		k.SetButtons(1<<3|1<<4, irq) // raises, latching the edge state
		buf := make([]byte, KeypadStateSize)
		if n := k.Serialize(buf); n != KeypadStateSize {
			t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d, want %d", n, KeypadStateSize)
		}
		r := NewKeypad()
		if !r.Deserialize(buf) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize returned false")
		}
		if r.Buttons() != k.Buttons() ||
			r.ReadReg(0x132, 2) != k.ReadReg(0x132, 2) ||
			r.ReadReg(0x130, 2) != k.ReadReg(0x130, 2) {
			t.Fatal("round trip state mismatch")
		}
		// The latched edge survives: the same held buttons
		// must not raise again on the restored keypad.
		irq2 := NewIRQ()
		r.SetButtons(1<<3|1<<4, irq2)
		if got := irq2.ReadReg(0x202, 2); got&IRQKeypad != 0 {
			t.Fatal("restored keypad re-raised for held buttons")
		}
		if r.Deserialize(buf[:KeypadStateSize-1]) {
			t.Fatal("Deserialize of short input returned true")
		}
	})
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/periph/timers.go ====================

package periph

// Timer register offsets (relative to 0x04000000). Channel
// n has its counter/reload halfword at 0x100+4n and its
// control halfword at 0x102+4n.
const timerBase = 0x100

// Timer control (CNT_H) bits, in the terms used below.
const (
	timerEnable  = 1 << 7
	timerCascade = 1 << 2
	timerIRQ     = 1 << 6
)

// prescalerPeriods maps the CNT_H prescaler select (bits
// 0-1) to the number of system cycles per counter tick.
var prescalerPeriods = [4]int{1, 64, 256, 1024}

// timerChan is one timer channel. The divider holds the
// prescaler remainder in cycles, so live counter reads
// reflect every Advance call exactly with no drift.
type timerChan struct {
	reload  uint16
	counter uint16
	control uint16
	divider uint16 // cycles, always below 1024
}

func (c *timerChan) enabled() bool { return c.control&timerEnable != 0 }

// Timers is the set of four GBA timer channels. Channels
// count at a prescaled rate, or, in cascade mode, once per
// overflow of the previous channel.
type Timers struct {
	ch [4]timerChan

	// OnOverflow, when set, is called once per channel
	// overflow during Advance, with the channel index. The
	// sound unit uses it to clock the Direct Sound FIFOs:
	// timers 0 and 1 are the sample rate generators for
	// FIFO channels A and B. It fires whether or not the
	// channel's IRQ enable is set.
	OnOverflow func(ch int)
}

// NewTimers returns the timers in power-on state: all
// channels stopped, reload and counter zero.
func NewTimers() *Timers { return &Timers{} }

// byteAt returns the register byte at an IO offset in
// 0x100..0x10F: the live counter bytes at the CNT_L
// offsets and the stored control bytes at the CNT_H
// offsets. Other offsets read as zero.
func (t *Timers) byteAt(addr uint32) byte {
	if addr < timerBase || addr > timerBase+0xF {
		return 0
	}
	rel := addr - timerBase
	c := &t.ch[rel/4]
	switch rel % 4 {
	case 0:
		return byte(c.counter)
	case 1:
		return byte(c.counter >> 8)
	case 2:
		return byte(c.control)
	default:
		return byte(c.control >> 8)
	}
}

// writeByte applies one byte of a register write.
//
// A CNT_L byte updates the reload value; while the channel
// is stopped the live counter follows the reload value,
// so a stopped channel can be primed by writing CNT_L. A
// CNT_H low byte can flip the enable bit: on a stopped to
// running transition the counter loads from the reload
// value and the prescaler divider restarts.
func (t *Timers) writeByte(addr uint32, b byte) {
	if addr < timerBase || addr > timerBase+0xF {
		return
	}
	rel := addr - timerBase
	c := &t.ch[rel/4]
	switch rel % 4 {
	case 0:
		c.reload = (c.reload & 0xFF00) | uint16(b)
		if !c.enabled() {
			c.counter = c.reload
		}
	case 1:
		c.reload = (c.reload & 0x00FF) | uint16(b)<<8
		if !c.enabled() {
			c.counter = c.reload
		}
	case 2:
		was := c.enabled()
		c.control = (c.control & 0xFF00) | uint16(b)
		if !was && c.enabled() {
			c.counter = c.reload
			c.divider = 0
		}
	case 3:
		c.control = (c.control & 0x00FF) | uint16(b)<<8
	}
}

// ReadReg reads size bytes at off (0x100..0x10F), composed
// little endian. Reading a CNT_L offset returns the live
// counter, not the reload value.
func (t *Timers) ReadReg(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return 0
	}
	return compose(off, size, t.byteAt)
}

// WriteReg writes size bytes at off (0x100..0x10F),
// decomposed little endian. See writeByte for the reload
// and enable rules.
func (t *Timers) WriteReg(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if !validSize(size) {
		return
	}
	decompose(off, size, val, t.writeByte)
}

// Counter returns the live counter of channel ch (0..3),
// as a CNT_L read would report it. Out of range channels
// read as zero.
func (t *Timers) Counter(ch int) uint16 {
	if ch < 0 || ch > 3 {
		return 0
	}
	return t.ch[ch].counter
}

// Advance moves every running channel forward by cycles
// system cycles. Non cascade channels accumulate the
// cycles into their prescaler divider and tick once per
// period. A tick past 0xFFFF reloads the counter from the
// reload value, raises the channel IRQ when CNT_H asks
// for it, and feeds one count into the next channel when
// that channel runs in cascade mode. Channels are
// processed in order within the call, so a cascade chain
// settles completely: a cascading channel can itself
// overflow and feed the next one. Stopped channels do not
// count, and a stopped or non cascade channel breaks a
// cascade chain.
func (t *Timers) Advance(cycles int, irq *IRQ) {
	if cycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	var feed uint32 // overflows handed from channel n-1 to n
	for n := range t.ch {
		c := &t.ch[n]
		var ticks uint32
		switch {
		case !c.enabled():
			// Stopped: no ticks, and the chain stops here.
		case c.control&timerCascade != 0:
			// Cascade mode counts previous overflows; the
			// prescaler select is ignored.
			ticks = feed
		default:
			period := prescalerPeriods[c.control&3]
			total := int(c.divider) + cycles
			ticks = uint32(total / period)
			c.divider = uint16(total % period)
		}
		feed = 0
		for ticks > 0 {
			until := uint32(0x10000) - uint32(c.counter)
			if ticks < until {
				c.counter += uint16(ticks)
				ticks = 0
				break
			}
			ticks -= until
			c.counter = c.reload
			feed++
			if c.control&timerIRQ != 0 && irq != nil {
				irq.Raise(uint16(IRQTimer0 << n))
			}
			if t.OnOverflow != nil {
				t.OnOverflow(n)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TimersStateSize is the serialized size of the timers
// state: 8 bytes per channel times 4 channels.
//
// Layout, per channel at 8n: reload halfword at 0,
// counter halfword at 2, control halfword at 4, prescaler
// divider halfword at 6, all little endian.
const TimersStateSize = 4 * 8

// Serialize writes the timers state to dst, which must
// be at least TimersStateSize bytes, and returns the
// number of bytes written.
func (t *Timers) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	for n := range t.ch {
		c := &t.ch[n]
		put16(dst, 8*n+0, c.reload)
		put16(dst, 8*n+2, c.counter)
		put16(dst, 8*n+4, c.control)
		put16(dst, 8*n+6, c.divider)
	}
	return TimersStateSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It
// reports false, leaving the state untouched, when src is
// too short.
func (t *Timers) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < TimersStateSize {
		return false
	}
	for n := range t.ch {
		c := &t.ch[n]
		c.reload = get16(src, 8*n+0)
		c.counter = get16(src, 8*n+2)
		c.control = get16(src, 8*n+4)
		c.divider = get16(src, 8*n+6)
	}
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/save/save.go ====================

// Package save implements the GBA cartridge save devices
// with a bus protocol, as described in GBATEK: the flash
// parts (64 KB and 128 KB, command driven) and the serial
// EEPROMs (512 byte and 8 KB). A Device is created from
// the cartridge's detected save kind; the system installs
// it behind bus hooks for the windows the device owns:
//
//   - Flash occupies the byte wide window at 0x0E000000,
//     the same window SRAM uses, whenever the cartridge
//     carries a flash part.
//   - EEPROM occupies accesses whose top byte is 0x0D,
//     inside what is normally the ROM window. For ROM
//     images of 16 MB or less the whole window belongs to
//     the EEPROM; for larger images GBATEK restricts it
//     to window offsets 0xFFFF00..0xFFFFFF, and other
//     offsets still read the ROM.
//
// Battery SRAM has no protocol; it stays in the bus,
// where GBA-1 put it: a plain byte store behind the same
// 0x0E000000 window, masked to its 32 KB by the system
// when the cartridge kind calls for it.
package save

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/cart"
)

// Storage sizes in bytes.
const (
	Flash64Size  = 0x10000 // 64 KB flash part
	Flash128Size = 0x20000 // 128 KB flash part (two banks)
	EEPROM512    = 0x200   // 512 byte EEPROM
	EEPROM8K     = 0x2000  // 8 KB EEPROM
	SRAMSize     = 0x8000  // 32 KB battery SRAM
)

// StateSize is the serialized device block: one kind
// byte, the full flash backing, the full EEPROM backing,
// and a fixed region of protocol state.
const StateSize = 1 + Flash128Size + EEPROM8K + 64

// Device is one cartridge's save hardware. The zero
// value is not usable; construct with New.
type Device struct {
	kind    cart.SaveKind
	romSize int

	flash  [Flash128Size]byte // only the part's size is used
	eeprom [EEPROM8K]byte     // only the part's size is used

	// Flash command protocol state.
	fStage  int  // unlock and command stage counter
	fIDMode bool // reads return the ID pair
	fProg   bool // next window write programs one byte
	fBankSw bool // next window write to offset 0 sets the bank
	fBank   int  // current 64 KB bank (128 KB part only)

	// EEPROM size, learned from the first completed
	// transfer's address width (or from a loaded save
	// image's length). Until learned it reports 8 KB.
	eeprom512   bool
	eepromKnown bool

	// EEPROM serial protocol state.
	eState  int    // stream phase, see the ee* constants
	eBits   int    // address bits captured (read requests)
	eAddr   uint32 // read address being served
	eCapN   int    // bits captured (write requests)
	eCapHi  uint64 // captured bits above bit 63
	eCapLo  uint64 // captured bits, low 64
	eOut    uint64 // data block being clocked out
	eOutPos int    // bits clocked out, dummy bits included
}

// EEPROM stream phases.
const (
	eeIdle      = iota // waiting for a start bit
	eeRequest          // waiting for the read/write bit
	eeReadAddr         // capturing read address bits
	eeReadOut          // clocking out dummy then data bits
	eeWriteCap         // capturing address and data bits of a write
	eeWritePend        // 71 bits captured: small-part write or long stream, undecided
)

// New builds the device for a detected save kind. The
// ROM size decides the EEPROM window rule above.
func New(kind cart.SaveKind, romSize int) *Device {
	d := &Device{kind: kind, romSize: romSize}
	d.ResetContents()
	return d
}

// Kind reports the cartridge save kind this device serves.
func (d *Device) Kind() cart.SaveKind { return d.kind }

// ResetContents returns the storage to its power-on
// contents (flash erased to 0xFF, EEPROM zeroed) and the
// protocols to idle. Save data is meant to survive
// console resets, so the system does not call this on a
// machine reset; it exists for construction and tests.
func (d *Device) ResetContents() {
	for i := range d.flash {
		d.flash[i] = 0xFF
	}
	for i := range d.eeprom {
		d.eeprom[i] = 0
	}
	d.ResetProtocol()
}

// ResetProtocol returns both device protocols to idle
// without touching the stored contents.
func (d *Device) ResetProtocol() {
	d.fStage, d.fIDMode, d.fProg, d.fBankSw, d.fBank = 0, false, false, false, 0
	d.eState, d.eBits, d.eAddr = eeIdle, 0, 0
	d.eCapN, d.eCapHi, d.eCapLo = 0, 0, 0
	d.eOut, d.eOutPos = 0, 0
}

// IsFlash reports whether the flash window hook applies.
func (d *Device) IsFlash() bool {
	switch d.kind {
	case cart.SaveFlash, cart.SaveFlash512, cart.SaveFlash1M:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// IsEEPROM reports whether the EEPROM window hook applies.
func (d *Device) IsEEPROM() bool { return d.kind == cart.SaveEEPROM }

// flashSize is the active flash capacity in bytes.
func (d *Device) flashSize() int {
	if d.kind == cart.SaveFlash1M {
		return Flash128Size
	}
	return Flash64Size
}

// EEPROMSize is the active EEPROM capacity in bytes: the
// 512 byte part once a 6 bit address transfer (or a 512
// byte save image) has identified it, otherwise 8 KB.
func (d *Device) EEPROMSize() int {
	if d.eeprom512 {
		return EEPROM512
	}
	return EEPROM8K
}

// learnEEPROMSize records the part size from an address
// width seen on the wire.
func (d *Device) learnEEPROMSize(addrBits int) {
	d.eepromKnown = true
	d.eeprom512 = addrBits == 6
}

// SaveRAM returns a copy of the device contents in the
// form a frontend persists: the flash bytes for a flash
// cartridge, the EEPROM bytes for an EEPROM cartridge.
// It returns nil for kinds this package does not own
// (the system serves SRAM from the bus store instead).
func (d *Device) SaveRAM() []byte {
	switch {
	case d.IsFlash():
		out := make([]byte, d.flashSize())
		copy(out, d.flash[:d.flashSize()])
		return out
	case d.IsEEPROM():
		out := make([]byte, d.EEPROMSize())
		copy(out, d.eeprom[:d.EEPROMSize()])
		return out
	}
	return nil
}

// SetSaveRAM loads device contents saved earlier. A
// length that matches the other size class of the same
// device family is accepted (a 64 KB image on a 128 KB
// part loads into bank 0 with bank 1 erased; a 512 byte
// EEPROM image marks the part as the small one). Other
// lengths are ignored.
func (d *Device) SetSaveRAM(b []byte) {
	switch {
	case d.IsFlash():
		if len(b) == 0 || len(b) > Flash128Size {
			return
		}
		d.ResetContents()
		copy(d.flash[:], b)
	case d.IsEEPROM():
		if len(b) != EEPROM512 && len(b) != EEPROM8K {
			return
		}
		d.ResetContents()
		copy(d.eeprom[:], b)
		d.eeprom512 = len(b) == EEPROM512
		d.eepromKnown = true
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/save/save_eeprom.go ====================

package save

// The EEPROM serial protocol, following GBATEK. The
// chip sits on the data bus at window 0x0D000000 and
// moves one bit per bus access: a write access clocks
// in the bit in bit 0 of the value, a read access clocks
// out one bit, returned in bit 0 (all other bits read
// as zero here).
//
// A transfer starts with a start bit (1) and a request
// bit: 1 for read, 0 for write.
//
//	Read:  address bits, most significant first, then a
//	       stop bit (0) written by the host; the chip
//	       then outputs 4 dummy bits (0) and the 64 data
//	       bits of the addressed block, most significant
//	       first.
//	Write: address bits then 64 data bits, most
//	       significant first, then a stop bit (0). The
//	       chip commits the block when the stop bit
//	       arrives, then needs a programming interval
//	       during which reads return 0 (busy) before
//	       returning 1 (ready).
//
// The address is 6 bits on the 512 byte part and 14 bits
// on the 8 KB part; a block is 8 bytes either way. The
// cartridge signature does not name the size, so the
// device learns it from the first transfer, the way the
// wire allows: a read's address ends where the host
// switches from writing to reading, and a write commits
// when a read poll ends its stream or when the long
// form's 79th bit (its stop) arrives. One residue is
// stated plainly: if the very first transfer a game
// makes is a write to the 8 KB part whose data happens
// to put a 0 then a 1 across the small part's stop
// position, the stream is indistinguishable from a
// small part write followed by a new start bit, and is
// read the second way. Any earlier read, or a save
// image of known length, pins the size first and the
// ambiguity never arises. Until the size is pinned the
// device reports the 8 KB part.
//
// The write programming interval is also collapsed:
// writes complete at the stop bit, so the first ready
// poll already reads 1.

// EEPROMActive reports whether an access at addr hits
// the EEPROM rather than the ROM behind the window: the
// whole window for ROM images up to 16 MB, only offsets
// 0xFFFF00..0xFFFFFF of the window for larger images.
func (d *Device) EEPROMActive(addr uint32) bool {
	if !d.IsEEPROM() {
		return false
	}
	if d.romSize <= 16*1024*1024 {
		return true
	}
	return addr&0xFFFFFF >= 0xFFFF00
}

// EEPROMRead clocks out one bit.
func (d *Device) EEPROMRead() uint32 {
	switch d.eState {
	case eeReadAddr:
		// The host stopped writing: the address is
		// complete. The last captured bit may be the
		// stop bit; accept both shapes.
		bits := d.eBits
		addr := d.eAddr
		if bits == 7 || bits == 15 {
			bits--
			addr >>= 1
		}
		if bits != 6 && bits != 14 {
			d.eState = eeIdle
			return 1
		}
		d.learnEEPROMSize(bits)
		d.eAddr = addr & uint32(d.EEPROMSize()/8-1)
		base := int(d.eAddr) * 8
		var v uint64
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			v |= uint64(d.eeprom[base+i]) << (56 - 8*i)
		}
		d.eOut = v
		d.eOutPos = 0
		d.eState = eeReadOut
		return d.eepromOutBit()
	case eeReadOut:
		return d.eepromOutBit()
	case eeWritePend:
		// The host ended the stream with a poll: the
		// 71 bit capture was a complete small part write.
		d.commitWrite(6)
		d.eState = eeIdle
		return 1
	case eeWriteCap:
		// A read mid-capture aborts the transfer.
		d.eState = eeIdle
		return 1
	}
	// Idle, mid-handshake and busy all read back the
	// ready bit: 1. Writes complete instantly in this
	// model, so the busy interval never shows.
	return 1
}

// eepromOutBit serves one bit of a read: 4 dummy zero
// bits, then the 64 data bits, most significant first.
// After the last data bit the stream ends and later
// reads see the idle ready bit.
func (d *Device) eepromOutBit() uint32 {
	pos := d.eOutPos
	d.eOutPos++
	if pos < 4 {
		return 0
	}
	if pos >= 4+64 {
		d.eState = eeIdle
		return 1
	}
	return uint32(d.eOut >> (63 - (pos - 4)) & 1)
}

// EEPROMWrite clocks in one bit.
func (d *Device) EEPROMWrite(val uint32) {
	bit := val & 1
	switch d.eState {
	case eeIdle:
		if bit == 1 {
			d.eState = eeRequest
		}
	case eeRequest:
		if bit == 1 {
			d.eState = eeReadAddr
			d.eBits, d.eAddr = 0, 0
		} else {
			d.eState = eeWriteCap
			d.eCapN, d.eCapHi, d.eCapLo = 0, 0, 0
		}
	case eeReadAddr:
		d.eAddr = d.eAddr<<1 | bit
		d.eBits++
		if d.eBits > 15 {
			d.eState = eeIdle // runaway stream; drop it
		}
	case eeReadOut:
		// A write during readout starts a new transfer
		// if it is a start bit; anything else ends it.
		if bit == 1 {
			d.eState = eeRequest
		} else {
			d.eState = eeIdle
		}
	case eeWritePend:
		if bit == 0 {
			// A 0 cannot be a start bit: the capture is
			// the long part's stream after all. Fold the
			// bit in as data and keep capturing.
			d.capPush(bit)
			d.eState = eeWriteCap
			return
		}
		// A 1 here is read as a fresh start bit after a
		// completed small part write (the header comment
		// states the indistinguishable case plainly).
		d.commitWrite(6)
		d.eState = eeRequest
	case eeWriteCap:
		d.capPush(bit)
		switch {
		case d.eCapN == 71 && bit == 0:
			if d.eepromKnown && !d.eeprom512 {
				// Size pinned to the long part: bit 71 is
				// data, never a stop. Keep capturing.
			} else if d.eepromKnown {
				d.commitWrite(6)
				d.eState = eeIdle
			} else {
				d.eState = eeWritePend
			}
		case d.eCapN == 79:
			if bit == 0 {
				d.commitWrite(14)
			}
			d.eState = eeIdle
		case d.eCapN > 79:
			d.eState = eeIdle
		}
	}
}

// capPush appends one bit to the write capture.
func (d *Device) capPush(bit uint32) {
	d.eCapHi = d.eCapHi<<1 | d.eCapLo>>63
	d.eCapLo = d.eCapLo<<1 | uint64(bit)
	d.eCapN++
}

// commitWrite splits a captured write stream (address
// bits of the given width, then 64 data bits; the stop
// bit that ends the stream is captured last and belongs
// to neither) and stores the block. The block bytes land
// in stream order: the first data byte clocked in is the
// block's first byte.
func (d *Device) commitWrite(addrBits int) {
	addr := uint32(d.captureBits(0, addrBits))
	data := d.captureBits(addrBits, 64)
	d.learnEEPROMSize(addrBits)
	addr &= uint32(d.EEPROMSize()/8 - 1)
	base := int(addr) * 8
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		d.eeprom[base+i] = byte(data >> (56 - 8*i))
	}
}

// captureBits returns length stream bits starting at
// the given stream position (0 is the first bit clocked
// in) from the capture pair.
func (d *Device) captureBits(start, length int) uint64 {
	total := d.eCapN
	var out uint64
	for i := 0; i < length; i++ {
		// Stream bit (start+i), counted from the head,
		// sits at position total-1-(start+i) from bit 0
		// of the (hi, lo) pair.
		pos := total - 1 - (start + i)
		var b uint64
		if pos >= 64 {
			b = d.eCapHi >> uint(pos-64) & 1
		} else {
			b = d.eCapLo >> uint(pos) & 1
		}
		out = out<<1 | b
	}
	return out
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/save/save_flash.go ====================

package save

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/cart"
)

// Flash window accesses and the command protocol,
// following GBATEK's description of the flash save
// chips.
//
// Command entry always starts with the unlock pair:
// byte 0xAA to window offset 0x5555, then 0x55 to offset
// 0x2AAA. The next byte, written to offset 0x5555, is the
// command:
//
//	0x90  enter ID mode: reads at offsets 0 and 1 return
//	      the manufacturer and device bytes (the pairs
//	      are named in flashID below)
//	0xF0  leave ID mode
//	0xA0  byte program: the very next window write stores
//	      one byte. Flash cells only clear bits, so the
//	      stored byte is the old byte AND the written one;
//	      only an erase sets bits again (to 1, byte 0xFF).
//	0x80  erase setup: a second unlock pair follows, then
//	      0x10 to offset 0x5555 erases the whole part, or
//	      0x30 to any address in a 4 KB sector erases that
//	      sector.
//	0xB0  bank switch (128 KB part only): the next write,
//	      to offset 0, carries the bank number in bit 0.
//
// Hardware programs and erases over milliseconds and
// games poll the byte being written (the documented
// data polling on bit 7). This core completes every
// operation at the write that triggers it, so a polling
// read always sees the final byte immediately; the
// simplification is stated here and in the README.

// FlashRead serves one read from the flash window. The
// window is byte wide: the byte is repeated into every
// lane of the result, exactly as the SRAM window behaves.
func (d *Device) FlashRead(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	off := addr & 0xFFFF
	var b byte
	if d.fIDMode && off <= 1 {
		b = d.flashID(off)
	} else {
		b = d.flash[d.fBank*Flash64Size+int(off)]
	}
	w := uint32(b) * 0x01010101
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return w & 0xFF
	case 2:
		return w & 0xFFFF
	}
	return w
}

// flashID returns the manufacturer (offset 0) or device
// (offset 1) byte for the emulated part: the Sanyo
// LE26FV10N1TS pair (0x62, 0x13) for the 128 KB part,
// the Macronix pair (0xC2, 0x1C) for the 64 KB parts.
func (d *Device) flashID(off uint32) byte {
	if d.kind == cart.SaveFlash1M {
		if off == 0 {
			return 0x62
		}
		return 0x13
	}
	if off == 0 {
		return 0xC2
	}
	return 0x1C
}

// FlashWrite serves one write to the flash window. Only
// the low byte of the value reaches the chip.
func (d *Device) FlashWrite(addr uint32, val uint32) {
	off := addr & 0xFFFF
	b := byte(val)

	// A bank switch write is the byte right after the
	// 0xB0 command, to offset 0.
	if d.fBankSw {
		d.fBankSw = false
		if off == 0 && d.kind == cart.SaveFlash1M {
			d.fBank = int(b & 1)
		}
		return
	}
	// A program write is the byte right after the 0xA0
	// command, to any address.
	if d.fProg {
		d.fProg = false
		cell := d.fBank*Flash64Size + int(off)
		d.flash[cell] &= b // cells only clear bits
		return
	}
	// ID mode ends on a bare 0xF0 write to 0x5555 as well
	// as on the unlocked command; several drivers exit
	// without the full unlock pair.
	if d.fIDMode && d.fStage == 0 && off == 0x5555 && b == 0xF0 {
		d.fIDMode = false
		return
	}

	switch d.fStage {
	case 0: // idle: watch for the unlock
		if off == 0x5555 && b == 0xAA {
			d.fStage = 1
		}
	case 1: // unlock half one seen
		if off == 0x2AAA && b == 0x55 {
			d.fStage = 2
		} else {
			d.fStage = 0
		}
	case 2: // command byte, to offset 0x5555
		d.fStage = 0
		if off != 0x5555 {
			return
		}
		switch b {
		case 0x90:
			d.fIDMode = true
		case 0xF0:
			d.fIDMode = false
		case 0xA0:
			d.fProg = true
		case 0x80:
			d.fStage = 3
		case 0xB0:
			if d.kind == cart.SaveFlash1M {
				d.fBankSw = true
			}
		}
	case 3: // erase setup: second unlock, half one
		if off == 0x5555 && b == 0xAA {
			d.fStage = 4
		} else {
			d.fStage = 0
		}
	case 4: // erase setup: second unlock, half two
		if off == 0x2AAA && b == 0x55 {
			d.fStage = 5
		} else {
			d.fStage = 0
		}
	case 5: // erase target
		d.fStage = 0
		switch {
		case b == 0x10 && off == 0x5555:
			for i := 0; i < d.flashSize(); i++ {
				d.flash[i] = 0xFF
			}
		case b == 0x30:
			base := d.fBank*Flash64Size + int(off&^0xFFF)
			for i := 0; i < 0x1000; i++ {
				d.flash[base+i] = 0xFF
			}
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/save/save_state.go ====================

package save

import "encoding/binary"

// Serialized layout (StateSize bytes total):
//
//	0          1 byte    the cartridge save kind
//	1          128 KB    the flash backing store
//	1+128 KB   8 KB      the EEPROM backing store
//	then       64 bytes  protocol state:
//	  0  flash stage counter
//	  1  flash ID mode flag
//	  2  flash program armed flag
//	  3  flash bank switch armed flag
//	  4  flash current bank
//	  5  EEPROM size flag (1 = the 512 byte part)
//	  6  EEPROM size known flag
//	  7  EEPROM stream phase
//	  8  EEPROM read address bits captured
//	  9  EEPROM read address, little endian 32
//	  13 EEPROM write capture count, little endian 32
//	  17 EEPROM write capture high bits, little endian 64
//	  25 EEPROM write capture low bits, little endian 64
//	  33 EEPROM readout block, little endian 64
//	  41 EEPROM readout position, little endian 32
//	  45..63 zero
//
// The backing stores are serialized at full size for
// every kind: unused regions hold their power-on fill
// (0xFF flash, zero EEPROM) and cost a fixed block in
// every state, which keeps the layout independent of
// the cartridge in the slot.

// protoOff is the offset of the protocol region.
const protoOff = 1 + Flash128Size + EEPROM8K

// Serialize writes the device block into dst and
// returns the number of bytes used, or 0 if dst is short.
func (d *Device) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	if len(dst) < StateSize {
		return 0
	}
	dst[0] = byte(d.kind)
	copy(dst[1:1+Flash128Size], d.flash[:])
	copy(dst[1+Flash128Size:protoOff], d.eeprom[:])
	p := dst[protoOff : protoOff+64]
	for i := range p {
		p[i] = 0
	}
	p[0] = byte(d.fStage)
	p[1] = boolByte(d.fIDMode)
	p[2] = boolByte(d.fProg)
	p[3] = boolByte(d.fBankSw)
	p[4] = byte(d.fBank)
	p[5] = boolByte(d.eeprom512)
	p[6] = boolByte(d.eepromKnown)
	p[7] = byte(d.eState)
	p[8] = byte(d.eBits)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(p[9:13], d.eAddr)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(p[13:17], uint32(d.eCapN))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(p[17:25], d.eCapHi)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(p[25:33], d.eCapLo)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(p[33:41], d.eOut)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(p[41:45], uint32(d.eOutPos))
	return StateSize
}

// Deserialize restores a block written by Serialize. It
// reports false when the input is short or names a
// different save kind than this device serves.
func (d *Device) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < StateSize {
		return false
	}
	if src[0] != byte(d.kind) {
		return false
	}
	copy(d.flash[:], src[1:1+Flash128Size])
	copy(d.eeprom[:], src[1+Flash128Size:protoOff])
	p := src[protoOff : protoOff+64]
	d.fStage = int(p[0])
	d.fIDMode = p[1] != 0
	d.fProg = p[2] != 0
	d.fBankSw = p[3] != 0
	d.fBank = int(p[4])
	d.eeprom512 = p[5] != 0
	d.eepromKnown = p[6] != 0
	d.eState = int(p[7])
	d.eBits = int(p[8])
	d.eAddr = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(p[9:13])
	d.eCapN = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(p[13:17]))
	d.eCapHi = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(p[17:25])
	d.eCapLo = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(p[25:33])
	d.eOut = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(p[33:41])
	d.eOutPos = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(p[41:45]))
	return true
}

func boolByte(b bool) byte {
	if b {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/save/save_test.go ====================

package save

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/cart"
)

// Flash helpers: the window base the bus presents.
const win = 0x0E000000

func fw(d *Device, off uint32, b byte) { d.FlashWrite(win+off, uint32(b)) }
func fr(d *Device, off uint32) byte    { return byte(d.FlashRead(win+off, 1)) }

func unlock(d *Device) {
	fw(d, 0x5555, 0xAA)
	fw(d, 0x2AAA, 0x55)
}

func command(d *Device, c byte) {
	unlock(d)
	fw(d, 0x5555, c)
}

func program(d *Device, off uint32, b byte) {
	command(d, 0xA0)
	fw(d, off, b)
}

func TestFlashIDMode(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveFlash, 0)
	command(d, 0x90)
	if got := fr(d, 0); got != 0xC2 {
		t.Fatalf("64K manufacturer ID = %#02x, want 0xC2 (Macronix)", got)
	}
	if got := fr(d, 1); got != 0x1C {
		t.Fatalf("64K device ID = %#02x, want 0x1C", got)
	}
	// A bare 0xF0 to 0x5555 leaves ID mode.
	fw(d, 0x5555, 0xF0)
	if got := fr(d, 0); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("after ID exit, offset 0 reads %#02x, want erased data 0xFF", got)
	}

	d1 := New(cart.SaveFlash1M, 0)
	command(d1, 0x90)
	if got := fr(d1, 0); got != 0x62 {
		t.Fatalf("128K manufacturer ID = %#02x, want 0x62 (Sanyo)", got)
	}
	if got := fr(d1, 1); got != 0x13 {
		t.Fatalf("128K device ID = %#02x, want 0x13", got)
	}
}

func TestFlashProgramANDSemantics(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveFlash512, 0)
	program(d, 0x1234, 0x3C)
	if got := fr(d, 0x1234); got != 0x3C {
		t.Fatalf("programmed byte = %#02x, want 0x3C", got)
	}
	// Programming can only clear bits: 0x3C AND 0xF0 = 0x30.
	program(d, 0x1234, 0xF0)
	if got := fr(d, 0x1234); got != 0x30 {
		t.Fatalf("second program = %#02x, want 0x30 (AND semantics)", got)
	}
	// And a program of 0xFF changes nothing.
	program(d, 0x1234, 0xFF)
	if got := fr(d, 0x1234); got != 0x30 {
		t.Fatalf("program 0xFF = %#02x, want 0x30", got)
	}
	// Neighbours are untouched.
	if got := fr(d, 0x1235); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("neighbour = %#02x, want 0xFF", got)
	}
}

func TestFlashSectorAndChipErase(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveFlash, 0)
	program(d, 0x0010, 0x11)
	program(d, 0x1010, 0x22)
	// Sector erase: setup, second unlock, 0x30 anywhere
	// inside the sector.
	command(d, 0x80)
	unlock(d)
	fw(d, 0x0ABC, 0x30)
	if got := fr(d, 0x0010); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("sector 0 after erase = %#02x, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	if got := fr(d, 0x1010); got != 0x22 {
		t.Fatalf("sector 1 after sector erase = %#02x, want 0x22 intact", got)
	}
	// Chip erase clears everything.
	command(d, 0x80)
	unlock(d)
	fw(d, 0x5555, 0x10)
	if got := fr(d, 0x1010); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("after chip erase = %#02x, want 0xFF", got)
	}
}

func TestFlashBankSwitch128K(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveFlash1M, 0)
	program(d, 0x0100, 0x11) // bank 0
	command(d, 0xB0)
	fw(d, 0x0000, 1) // bank 1
	if got := fr(d, 0x0100); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("bank 1 fresh byte = %#02x, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	program(d, 0x0100, 0x22)
	command(d, 0xB0)
	fw(d, 0x0000, 0) // back to bank 0
	if got := fr(d, 0x0100); got != 0x11 {
		t.Fatalf("bank 0 byte = %#02x, want 0x11", got)
	}
	sr := d.SaveRAM()
	if len(sr) != Flash128Size {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", len(sr), Flash128Size)
	}
	if sr[0x0100] != 0x11 || sr[0x10100] != 0x22 {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM banks = %#02x/%#02x, want 0x11/0x22", sr[0x0100], sr[0x10100])
	}
	// The 64 KB kinds report the smaller image.
	if got := len(New(cart.SaveFlash, 0).SaveRAM()); got != Flash64Size {
		t.Fatalf("64K SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", got, Flash64Size)
	}
}

func TestFlashStateRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveFlash1M, 0)
	program(d, 0x0042, 0x77)
	command(d, 0xB0)
	fw(d, 0x0000, 1)
	buf := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if n := d.Serialize(buf); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize used %d, want %d", n, StateSize)
	}
	d2 := New(cart.SaveFlash1M, 0)
	if !d2.Deserialize(buf) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize rejected a valid block")
	}
	// Bank 1 is still selected after the round trip.
	if got := fr(d2, 0x0042); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("bank state lost: bank1[0x42] = %#02x, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	command(d2, 0xB0)
	fw(d2, 0x0000, 0)
	if got := fr(d2, 0x0042); got != 0x77 {
		t.Fatalf("restored byte = %#02x, want 0x77", got)
	}
	if d2.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a short block")
	}
}

// EEPROM helpers: clock bits through the serial window.

func ew(d *Device, bit uint32) { d.EEPROMWrite(bit) }
func er(d *Device) uint32      { return d.EEPROMRead() }

// eeWriteBlock clocks one full write transfer and polls
// ready, which must read 1 on the first poll in this
// model (the programming interval is collapsed).
func eeWriteBlock(t *testing.T, d *Device, addr uint32, addrBits int, value uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	ew(d, 1) // start
	ew(d, 0) // write request
	for i := addrBits - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		ew(d, (addr>>uint(i))&1)
	}
	for i := 63; i >= 0; i-- {
		ew(d, uint32(value>>uint(i))&1)
	}
	ew(d, 0) // stop
	if got := er(d); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ready poll after write = %d, want 1", got)
	}
}

// eeReadBlock clocks one full read transfer and returns
// the 64 bit block, checking the 4 dummy bits are zero.
func eeReadBlock(t *testing.T, d *Device, addr uint32, addrBits int) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	ew(d, 1) // start
	ew(d, 1) // read request
	for i := addrBits - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		ew(d, (addr>>uint(i))&1)
	}
	ew(d, 0) // stop
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if got := er(d); got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("dummy bit %d = %d, want 0", i, got)
		}
	}
	var v uint64
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		v = v<<1 | uint64(er(d))
	}
	return v
}

func TestEEPROMRoundTrip8K(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveEEPROM, 8*1024*1024)
	if got := er(d); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("idle read = %d, want ready 1", got)
	}
	const want uint64 = 0x0123456789ABCDEF
	eeWriteBlock(t, d, 0x123, 14, want)
	if got := eeReadBlock(t, d, 0x123, 14); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("read back = %#016x, want %#016x", got, want)
	}
	if got := d.EEPROMSize(); got != EEPROM8K {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROMSize = %d, want %d", got, EEPROM8K)
	}
	if got := len(d.SaveRAM()); got != EEPROM8K {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", got, EEPROM8K)
	}
	// A different block is still zero.
	if got := eeReadBlock(t, d, 0x124, 14); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("untouched block = %#016x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestEEPROMRoundTrip512(t *testing.T) {

	const want uint64 = 0xFEDCBA9876543210
	eeWriteBlock(t, d, 0x2A, 6, want)
	if got := d.EEPROMSize(); got != EEPROM512 {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROMSize = %d, want %d (learned from the 6 bit address)", got, EEPROM512)
	}
	if got := eeReadBlock(t, d, 0x2A, 6); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("read back = %#016x, want %#016x", got, want)

		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", got, EEPROM512)
	}
}

func TestEEPROMBackToBackTransfers(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveEEPROM, 8*1024*1024)
	// A small part write followed IMMEDIATELY by a read
	// transfer (no ready poll in between): the read's
	// start bit lands while the write is still pending.
	ew(d, 1)
	ew(d, 0)
	for i := 5; i >= 0; i-- {
		ew(d, (0x11>>uint(i))&1)
	}
	const want uint64 = 0xA5A5A5A5A5A5A5A5
	for i := 63; i >= 0; i-- {
		ew(d, uint32(want>>uint(i))&1)
	}
	ew(d, 0) // stop: the write is now pending commit
	if got := eeReadBlock(t, d, 0x11, 6); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("back to back read = %#016x, want %#016x", got, want)
	}
}

func TestEEPROMWindowRule(t *testing.T) {
	big := New(cart.SaveEEPROM, 32*1024*1024)
	if big.EEPROMActive(0x0D000000) {
		t.Fatal("32 MB ROM: window offset 0 must not be EEPROM")
	}
	if !big.EEPROMActive(0x0DFFFF00) {
		t.Fatal("32 MB ROM: window offset 0xFFFF00 must be EEPROM")
	}
	if !big.EEPROMActive(0x0DFFFFFF) {
		t.Fatal("32 MB ROM: window offset 0xFFFFFF must be EEPROM")
	}
	small := New(cart.SaveEEPROM, 16*1024*1024)
	if !small.EEPROMActive(0x0D000000) {
		t.Fatal("16 MB ROM: the whole window must be EEPROM")
	}
	none := New(cart.SaveFlash, 8*1024*1024)
	if none.EEPROMActive(0x0D000000) {
		t.Fatal("a flash cartridge must never activate the EEPROM window")
	}
}

func TestEEPROMSetSaveRAMSizePin(t *testing.T) {
	d := New(cart.SaveEEPROM, 8*1024*1024)
	img := make([]byte, EEPROM512)
	img[0x10] = 0x99
	d.SetSaveRAM(img)
	if got := d.EEPROMSize(); got != EEPROM512 {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROMSize after 512 byte image = %d, want %d", got, EEPROM512)
	}
