	if got := eeReadBlock(t, d, 2, 6); got != 0x9900000000000000 {
		t.Fatalf("read block 2 = %#016x, want 0x9900000000000000", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/system/anguna_gate_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"math"
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// The GBA-4 real-game gate: Anguna, a full open-source
// homebrew GBA game (homebrew/anguna.gba, local test
// material only, never shipped), booted and played on the
// core for 3,600 frames. The gate is presence-gated: it
// skips cleanly when the ROM is absent.
//
// The game flow below is what the GBA-4 probe runs
// (system probe logs, October 2026) measured on this
// core, and it matches the game's real behaviour:
//
//	frames 1..~450    intro fade and logo animation
//	frames ~500..900   title screen (static, about 67%
//	                   non-blank)
//	frame 900          Start (held 30 frames) opens the
//	                   menu (about 59% non-blank, the
//	                   display gains a second background)
//	frames 1250, 1600  A walks the menu (cursor steps)
//	frame 2400         A confirms; the game enters its
//	                   first animated scene (about 77%
//	                   non-blank, frame hash changes on
//	                   every sample from here on)
//
// Audio: the gate measures the output and finds digital
// silence for the whole run (RMS 0.0), and that is the
// game's own behaviour, traced exhaustively while
// bringing this gate up, not a core defect:
//
//   - A census of every IO write in the first 120 frames
//     shows the sound hardware written exactly three
//     times, all at boot: SOUNDCNT_H once, SOUNDCNT_X
//     twice (master enable plus the Direct Sound timer
//     select). No channel register is ever written.
//   - A 600 frame trace in gameplay shows the only IO
//     writes are the per-frame DMA3 OAM copy: zero sound
//     register writes, zero FIFO DMA arming.
//   - 1,800 frames of deep play (walking, sword swings,
//     interactions) produce zero sound register writes,
//     zero FIFO samples, and IE never gains a bit beyond
//     vblank, so no sound interrupt is ever unmasked.
//
// The APU itself is proven by the GBA-3 synthetic gates
// (exact tone frequencies, FIFO sine measurement), so a
// silent game stays silent here. The gate therefore pins
// the observed truth: the FIFO counters stay at zero and
// the output RMS stays at the floor. If a future change
// makes this title produce sound, or stops it being
// faithfully silent, the gate fails and a human looks.

const angunaROMPath = "../../../homebrew/anguna.gba"

// angunaPresses is the input script: frame number to the
// buttons held from that frame.
func angunaPresses() map[int]uint32 {
	press := map[int]uint32{}
	hold := func(at int, btn uint32, dur int) {
		for i := 0; i < dur; i++ {
			press[at+i] |= btn
		}
	}
	hold(900, ButtonStart, 30)
	hold(1250, ButtonA, 12)
	hold(1600, ButtonA, 12)
	hold(2400, ButtonA, 12)
	return press
}

func loadAnguna(t *testing.T) (*Machine, []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(angunaROMPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("Anguna ROM not present (%v); gate skipped", err)
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(data); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart(Anguna): %v", err)
	}
	return m, data
}

// fbBytes flattens the framebuffer to little-endian
// bytes for hashing (the conversion the original probe
// used, kept with the gate it evolved into).
func fbBytes(fb []uint32) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, len(fb)*4)
	for i, p := range fb {
		out[4*i] = byte(p)
		out[4*i+1] = byte(p >> 8)
		out[4*i+2] = byte(p >> 16)
		out[4*i+3] = byte(p >> 24)
	}
	return out
}

func frameHash(fb []uint32) [32]byte {
	return sha256.Sum256(fbBytes(fb))
}

func nonblankPct(fb []uint32) float64 {
	n := 0
	for _, p := range fb {
		if p != 0xFF000000 {
			n++
		}
	}
	return 100 * float64(n) / float64(len(fb))
}

func TestAngunaGate(t *testing.T) {
	m, data := loadAnguna(t)
	press := angunaPresses()

	// Anguna's ROM carries no save signature (devkitPro
	// build with an unfixed header), so detection reports
	// SaveNone and the fallback 32 KB SRAM window applies.
	if got := m.Cart().SaveKind.String(); got != "none" {
		t.Fatalf("Anguna save kind = %s, want none (no signature in the image)", got)
	}
	if got := len(m.SaveRAM()); got != 32768 {
		t.Fatalf("Anguna SaveRAM size = %d, want 32768 (fallback SRAM window)", got)
	}

	hashAt := map[int][32]byte{}
	pctAt := map[int]float64{}
	rmsMax := 0.0
	var stateAt2400 []byte
	sampleFrames := map[int]bool{600: true, 899: true, 1200: true, 1800: true, 2400: true, 3000: true, 3300: true, 3600: true}

	// Frames 1..2399: boot, title, Start into the menu.
	for f := 1; f <= 2399; f++ {
		m.SetButtons(press[f])
		m.RunFrame()
		ab := m.AudioBuffer()
		var ss float64
		for _, s := range ab {
			ss += float64(s) * float64(s)
		}
		if len(ab) > 0 {
			if r := math.Sqrt(ss / float64(len(ab))); r > rmsMax {
				rmsMax = r
			}
		}
		if sampleFrames[f] {
			hashAt[f] = frameHash(m.Framebuffer())
			pctAt[f] = nonblankPct(m.Framebuffer())
		}
	}
	stateAt2400 = m.Serialize()

	// The continuation, frames 2400..3600, recorded.
	contHash := map[int][32]byte{}
	contAudio := map[int][]int16{}
	for f := 2400; f <= 3600; f++ {
		m.SetButtons(press[f])
		m.RunFrame()
		ab := m.AudioBuffer()
		contAudio[f] = append([]int16{}, ab...)
		var ss float64
		for _, s := range ab {
			ss += float64(s) * float64(s)
		}
		if len(ab) > 0 {
			if r := math.Sqrt(ss / float64(len(ab))); r > rmsMax {
				rmsMax = r
			}
		}
		if sampleFrames[f] {
			hashAt[f] = frameHash(m.Framebuffer())
			pctAt[f] = nonblankPct(m.Framebuffer())
		}
		if f <= 2519 {
			contHash[f] = frameHash(m.Framebuffer())
		}
	}
	// Video assertions.
	for _, f := range []int{600, 1200, 1800, 2400, 3000, 3600} {
		if pctAt[f] < 25 {
			t.Fatalf("frame %d non-blank = %.1f%%, want a substantially drawn screen (>= 25%%)", f, pctAt[f])
		}
	}
	t.Logf("non-blank: f600 %.1f%% f1200 %.1f%% f1800 %.1f%% f2400 %.1f%% f3000 %.1f%% f3600 %.1f%%",
		pctAt[600], pctAt[1200], pctAt[1800], pctAt[2400], pctAt[3000], pctAt[3600])
	if hashAt[600] == hashAt[3600] {
		t.Fatal("frame at 3600 is identical to frame 600: the game did not progress")
	}
	// Start at frame 900 must leave the title screen: the
	// menu frame at 1200 differs materially from the
	// title frame at 899.
	if hashAt[899] == hashAt[1200] {
		t.Fatal("Start at frame 900 produced no frame change by 1200: title screen did not leave")
	}
	// The scene reached by 3000 is animated: consecutive
	// samples differ.
	if hashAt[3000] == hashAt[3300] {
		t.Fatal("frames 3000 and 3300 are identical: the in-game scene is not animating")
	}

	// Audio assertions: the traced profile documented at
	// the top of this file. RMS floor for this title is
	// the silence ceiling: the game requests no audio.
	if got := m.FIFOSamples(1) + m.FIFOSamples(2); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO samples delivered = %d, want 0 for Anguna's traced profile", got)
	}
	if rmsMax > 1.0 {
		t.Fatalf("audio RMS max = %.2f, want <= 1.0 (Anguna makes no sound; see the header)", rmsMax)
	}
	t.Logf("audio: RMS max %.2f over 3600 frames, FIFO samples 0 (game-side silence, traced)", rmsMax)

	// Save at 2400, restore into a fresh machine, and
	// require the next 120 frames to match byte for byte
	// (framebuffer hashes and audio samples).
	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.LoadCart(data); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart(Anguna, fresh): %v", err)
	}
	if err := m2.Deserialize(stateAt2400); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize at frame 2400: %v", err)
	}
	for f := 2400; f <= 2519; f++ {
		m2.SetButtons(press[f])
		m2.RunFrame()
		ab := m2.AudioBuffer()
		wantHash := contHash[f]
		if got := frameHash(m2.Framebuffer()); got != wantHash {
			t.Fatalf("restored frame %d hash = %x, want %x (continuation diverged)", f, got[:6], wantHash[:6])
		}
		want := contAudio[f]
		if len(ab) != len(want) {
			t.Fatalf("restored frame %d produced %d audio samples, want %d", f, len(ab), len(want))
		}
		for i := range ab {
			if ab[i] != want[i] {
				t.Fatalf("restored frame %d audio sample %d = %d, want %d", f, i, ab[i], want[i])
			}
		}
	}
	t.Logf("save/restore: 120 frames after the frame-2400 state are byte-identical (video and audio)")
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/system/gba2_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// The GBA-2 integration gate. The synthetic program
// below boots through the core's own BIOS stub, installs
// an IRQ handler in ROM, enables the VBlank interrupt
// end to end (DISPSTAT enable, IE, IME, CPSR I bit), and
// idles in a branch loop. The handler increments a
// counter in IWRAM on every interrupt it is called for.
// If any link in the chain (PPU event, interrupt
// controller, CPU IRQ entry, BIOS dispatcher, handler
// return) is broken, the counter does not move.

// armSTRH builds STRH rd, [rn] with a zero immediate
// offset.
func armSTRH(rd, rn uint32) uint32 {
	return 0xE1C000B0 | rn<<16 | rd<<12
}

// irqSceneROM builds a 4 KB image whose main code sits
// at 0xC0 (reached by the standard entry branch) and
// whose IRQ handler sits at ROM offset 0x200.
func irqSceneROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x1000)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x00:], 0xEA00002E)
	copy(rom[0xA0:], "IRQSCENE")
	copy(rom[0xAC:], "ASYE")
	copy(rom[0xB0:], "01")
	rom[0xB2] = 0x96
	rom[0xBC] = 0x01
	sum := 0x19
	for _, c := range rom[0xA0 : 0xBC+1] {
		sum += int(c)
	}
	rom[0xBD] = uint8(-sum)

	var code []uint32
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(0, 0x03007F00)...) // R0 = user stack top
	code = append(code, 0xE1A0D000)                      // MOV SP, R0
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x03007FFC)...) // R1 = handler pointer slot
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(2, 0x08000200)...) // R2 = handler address
	code = append(code, armSTR(2, 1, false))             // STR R2, [R1]
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x04000004)...) // R1 = DISPSTAT
	code = append(code, armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 8))          // MOV R2, #8 (VBlank IRQ enable)
	code = append(code, armSTRH(2, 1))                   // STRH R2, [R1]
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x04000200)...) // R1 = IE
	code = append(code, armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 1))          // MOV R2, #1 (VBlank)
	code = append(code, armSTRH(2, 1))                   // STRH R2, [R1]
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x04000208)...) // R1 = IME
	code = append(code, armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 1))          // MOV R2, #1
	code = append(code, armSTRH(2, 1))                   // STRH R2, [R1]
	code = append(code,
		0xE10F0000,                // MRS R0, CPSR
		armImm(14, 0, 0, 0, 0x80), // BIC R0, R0, #0x80 (IRQ enable)
		0xE121F000,                // MSR CPSR_c, R0
		0xEAFFFFFE,                // B . (idle loop)
	)
	for i, w := range code {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0xC0+4*i:], w)
	}

	// The handler at 0x200: bump the word at
	// IWRAM+0x10, preserving the registers it uses, and
	// return to the dispatcher with BX LR.
	var handler []uint32
	handler = append(handler, 0xE92D0003) // PUSH {R0, R1}
	handler = append(handler, armBuildConst(0, 0x03000010)...)
	handler = append(handler,
		0xE5901000,            // LDR R1, [R0]
		armImm(4, 1, 1, 0, 1), // ADD R1, R1, #1
		0xE5801000,            // STR R1, [R0]
		0xE8BD0003,            // POP {R0, R1}
		0xE12FFF1E,            // BX LR
	)
	for i, w := range handler {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x200+4*i:], w)
	}
	return rom
}

// TestVBlankIRQCount is the interrupt gate: exactly one
// VBlank interrupt must reach the handler per frame.
func TestVBlankIRQCount(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(irqSceneROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03000010, 4); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("VBlank handler ran %d times in 3 frames, want exactly 3", got)
	}
	// The BIOS dispatcher must also have recorded the
	// flags in the interrupt check word.
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03007FF8, 4); got&1 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BIOS check word = %#08x, want the VBlank bit set", got)
	}
}

// setupScene paints the deterministic scene the
// determinism gate renders: a text tile background, one
// sprite on top of it, and an HBlank DMA that rewrites
// the backdrop palette entry every line.
func setupScene(t *testing.T, m *Machine) {
	t.Helper()
	b := m.Bus()
	// BG palette: entry 1 = red (BGR555 0x001F).
	b.Write(0x05000002, 2, 0x001F)
	// OBJ palette: entry 1 = green (BGR555 0x03E0).
	b.Write(0x05000202, 2, 0x03E0)
	// VRAM tile 1 (char base 0): all nibbles = color 1.
	for off := uint32(0); off < 32; off += 4 {
		b.Write(0x06000020+off, 4, 0x11111111)
	}
	// OBJ tile 0 at 0x06010000: all nibbles = color 1.
	for off := uint32(0); off < 32; off += 4 {
		b.Write(0x06010000+off, 4, 0x11111111)
	}
	// Tilemap at screen base 0x800: entries (0,0) and
	// (1,0) show tile 1.
	b.Write(0x06000800, 2, 1)
	b.Write(0x06000802, 2, 1)
	// OAM entry 0: 8x8 sprite at (0,0), tile 0, prio 0.
	b.Write(0x07000000, 2, 0) // attr0: y=0
	b.Write(0x07000002, 2, 0) // attr1: x=0, size 0
	b.Write(0x07000004, 2, 0) // attr2: tile 0
	// BG0CNT: char base 0, screen base block 1.
	b.Write(0x04000008, 2, 0x0100)
	// DISPCNT: mode 0, BG0 on, OBJ on.
	b.Write(0x04000000, 2, 0x1100)
	// HBlank DMA3: EWRAM pattern to the backdrop
	// palette entry, one halfword per line, repeating
	// with destination reload.
	b.Write(0x02000000, 4, 0x00007C00)
	b.Write(0x040000D4, 4, 0x02000000) // DMA3SAD
	b.Write(0x040000D8, 4, 0x05000000) // DMA3DAD
	b.Write(0x040000DC, 2, 1)          // DMA3CNT_L: 1 unit
	b.Write(0x040000DE, 2, 0xA360)     // DMA3CNT_H: enable, HBlank, repeat, fixed src, dst reload
}

// TestSceneDeterminismGate renders the scene, takes a
// save state mid-frame, and requires the continuation
// after a restore into a fresh machine to be identical
// in state bytes and framebuffer to the uninterrupted
// run.
func TestSceneDeterminismGate(t *testing.T) {
	rom := irqSceneROM()
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	setupScene(t, m)
	m.runLines(100) // mid-frame
	save := m.Serialize()
	m.runLines(linesPerFrame - 100)
	m.RunFrame()
	wantState := m.Serialize()
	wantFrame := append([]uint32{}, m.Framebuffer()...)

	// Scene spot checks on the uninterrupted run.
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03000010, 4); got != 2 {
		t.Errorf("VBlank handler count = %d after 2 frames, want 2", got)
	}
	fb := m.Framebuffer()
	if got := fb[0]; got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Errorf("pixel (0,0) = %#08x, want 0xFF00FF00 (sprite green over BG)", got)
	}
	if got := fb[8]; got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Errorf("pixel (8,0) = %#08x, want 0xFFFF0000 (BG red tile)", got)
	}
	if got := fb[100*Width+100]; got != 0xFF0000FF {
		t.Errorf("pixel (100,100) = %#08x, want 0xFF0000FF (DMA blue backdrop)", got)
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x05000000, 2); got != 0x7C00 {
		t.Errorf("backdrop palette entry = %#04x, want 0x7C00 (HBlank DMA wrote it)", got)
	}

	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart (second machine): %v", err)
	}
	if err := m2.Deserialize(save); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	m2.runLines(linesPerFrame - 100)
	m2.RunFrame()
	if got := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Fatal("state after a mid-frame restore and continuation differs from the uninterrupted run")
	}
	got2 := m2.Framebuffer()
	for i := range wantFrame {
		if got2[i] != wantFrame[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d after restore = %#08x, want %#08x", i, got2[i], wantFrame[i])
		}
	}
}

// TestStateVersion4 checks the v4 state shape: version
// byte 4, exact size, and a v3-shaped input rejected
// (the GBA-4 cartridge save device block joined the
// layout, so the older formats no longer load).
func TestStateVersion4(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(irqSceneROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	m.RunFrame()
	s := m.Serialize()
	if len(s) != m.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, StateSize = %d", len(s), m.StateSize())

		t.Fatalf("version byte = %d, want 4", s[0])
	}

	v3[0] = 3
	if err := m.Deserialize(v3); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a version 3 state under the v4 format")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/system/gba3_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// The GBA-3 integration gates: Direct Sound FIFO playback
// end to end (timer 0 as the 8192 Hz sample clock, DMA1
// in FIFO mode feeding FIFO A from a sine table in
// EWRAM), the exposed audio surface (AudioBuffer and
// AudioSampleRate), and mid-playback save state
// determinism with PSG and FIFO sound running together.

// setupFIFOScene loads the idle IRQ scene ROM, then
// programs the sound and DMA registers directly through
// the bus: timer 0 ticks at 8192 Hz, DMA1 runs in FIFO
// mode from a 256 Hz sine table in EWRAM, and FIFO A is
// enabled on both speakers at full volume.
func setupFIFOScene(t *testing.T, m *Machine) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := m.LoadCart(irqSceneROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	b := m.Bus()
	// Sine table: the 32 sample period of a 256 Hz sine
	// at the 8192 Hz sample rate, repeated across 16 KB
	// of EWRAM. The FIFO DMA source pointer only advances,
	// so the table has to cover the whole run: 8192 bytes
	// per second of playback.
	for i := 0; i < 16384; i++ {
		v := int8(math.Round(100 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i%32)/32)))
		b.Write(0x02000000+uint32(i), 1, uint32(byte(v)))
	}
	// Timer 0: reload 0xF800 gives a 2048 cycle period at
	// prescaler 1, which is 8192 Hz; then start it.
	b.Write(0x04000100, 2, 0xF800) // TM0CNT_L
	b.Write(0x04000102, 2, 0x0080) // TM0CNT_H: enable
	// DMA1: source the sine table, destination FIFO_A,
	// enabled in special (FIFO) timing, 32 bit units.
	b.Write(0x040000BC, 4, 0x02000000) // DMA1SAD
	b.Write(0x040000C0, 4, 0x040000A0) // DMA1DAD = FIFO_A
	b.Write(0x040000C4, 2, 0)          // DMA1CNT_L (unused in FIFO mode)
	b.Write(0x040000C6, 2, 0xB400)     // DMA1CNT_H: enable, timing 3, 32 bit
	// Sound: master on, FIFO A full volume on both sides,
	// clocked by timer 0.
	b.Write(0x04000084, 2, 0x0080) // SOUNDCNT_X: master enable
	b.Write(0x04000082, 2, 0x0304) // SOUNDCNT_H: A vol 100%, A L+R on, timer 0
}

// playSquareA4 programs PSG channel 1 through the bus to
// play A4 (frequency register 0x6D6, the documented value
// for 440 Hz) at full envelope volume, 50 percent duty.
func playSquareA4(m *Machine) {
	b := m.Bus()
	b.Write(0x04000084, 2, 0x0080) // SOUNDCNT_X: master enable
	b.Write(0x04000080, 2, 0x1177) // SOUNDCNT_L: ch1 both sides, volumes 7
	b.Write(0x04000082, 2, 0x0306) // SOUNDCNT_H: PSG 100%, FIFO A full, L+R
	b.Write(0x04000062, 2, 0xF080) // SOUND1CNT_H: duty 50%, envelope 15 step 0
	b.Write(0x04000064, 2, 0x86D6) // SOUND1CNT_X: trigger, frequency 0x6D6
}

// TestFIFOSineGate runs the FIFO scene for about a
// second and measures the output: a 256 Hz sine within
// tolerance, and a DMA word count that matches the
// consumption accounting (8192 sample pops per second,
// 16 bytes per refill burst, at most a FIFO of slack).
func TestFIFOSineGate(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	setupFIFOScene(t, m)
	playSquareA4(m)
	// One second of audio is 32768 output frames; run 62
	// frames (about 1.016 s) so the buffer holds at
	// least a full second.
	const frames = 62
	for i := 0; i < frames; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	out := m.AudioBuffer()
	if len(out) < 2*32768 {
		t.Fatalf("audio frames = %d, want at least 32768", len(out)/2)
	}
	if got := m.AudioSampleRate(); got != 32768 {
		t.Fatalf("AudioSampleRate = %d, want 32768", got)
	}
	// FIFO consumption accounting: timer 0 pops one byte
	// per 2048 cycles. In 62 frames the machine advances
	// at least 62*280896 cycles, at least 8500 pops; each
	// refill burst delivers 4 words. Delivered bytes must
	// cover the pops and exceed them by less than the
	// FIFO capacity plus one burst.
	words := m.FIFOSamples(1)
	if words < 2050 || words > 2300 {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO words delivered = %d, want within [2050, 2300] for ~8500 pops", words)
	}
	t.Logf("FIFO words delivered in %d frames: %d (%d bytes for ~8500 sample pops)", frames, words, 4*words)
}

// TestFIFOOnlySineFrequency isolates the FIFO path: no
// PSG channel is programmed, so the left channel carries
// the pure sample-and-hold sine and its positive
// crossings over the drained span must measure 256 Hz.
func TestFIFOOnlySineFrequency(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	setupFIFOScene(t, m)
	const frames = 62
	for i := 0; i < frames; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	out := m.AudioBuffer()
	n := len(out) / 2
	if n < 32768 {
		t.Fatalf("audio frames = %d, want at least 32768", n)
	}
	crossings := 0
	for i := 1; i < n; i++ {
		if out[2*(i-1)] < 0 && out[2*i] >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
	}
	measured := float64(crossings) * 32768.0 / float64(n)
	if measured < 250 || measured > 262 {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO sine measured %.2f Hz over %d frames, want 256 within 6", measured, n)
	}
	// The held sample must actually swing: peak absolute
	// value near the sine table peak (100) scaled by the
	// Direct Sound gain (4 in the output domain, times
	// 64 into int16) is 25600.
	peak := 0
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		v := int(out[2*i])
		if v < 0 {
			v = -v
		}
		if v > peak {
			peak = v
		}
	}
	if peak < 20000 || peak > 26000 {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO sine peak = %d, want near 25600", peak)
	}
	t.Logf("FIFO sine: %d crossings over %d output frames = %.2f Hz, peak %d", crossings, n, measured, peak)
}

// TestAudioDeterminismGate: mid-frame save during PSG
// plus FIFO playback restores and the continuation is
// bit-identical, in output samples and in state bytes.
func TestAudioDeterminismGate(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	setupFIFOScene(t, m)
	playSquareA4(m)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	m.runLines(100) // mid-frame
	m.AudioBuffer() // drain at the save point: pending output is not state
	save := m.Serialize()
	// Continuation: finish the frame, run 6 more frames,
	// draining after the save point.
	m.runLines(linesPerFrame - 100)
	for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	wantAudio := m.AudioBuffer()
	wantState := m.Serialize()
	if len(wantAudio) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("continuation produced no audio")
	}

	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.LoadCart(irqSceneROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart (second machine): %v", err)
	}
	if err := m2.Deserialize(save); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	m2.runLines(linesPerFrame - 100)
	for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
		m2.RunFrame()
	}
	gotAudio := m2.AudioBuffer()
	if len(gotAudio) != len(wantAudio) {
		t.Fatalf("audio after restore: %d samples, want %d", len(gotAudio), len(wantAudio))
	}
	for i := range wantAudio {
		if gotAudio[i] != wantAudio[i] {
			t.Fatalf("audio sample %d after restore = %d, want %d", i, gotAudio[i], wantAudio[i])
		}
	}
	if got := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Fatal("state after a mid-playback restore and continuation differs from the uninterrupted run")
	}
}

// TestSoundRateSelection checks the AudioSampleRate
// surface: power-on default 32768, and a SOUNDBIAS
// resolution write moves it per the documented table.
func TestSoundRateSelection(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(irqSceneROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	if got := m.AudioSampleRate(); got != 32768 {
		t.Fatalf("default AudioSampleRate = %d, want 32768", got)
	}
	m.Bus().Write(0x04000088, 2, 0xC200) // SOUNDBIAS resolution 3
	if got := m.AudioSampleRate(); got != 262144 {
		t.Fatalf("AudioSampleRate at resolution 3 = %d, want 262144", got)
	}
	m.Bus().Write(0x04000088, 2, 0x4200) // SOUNDBIAS resolution 1
	if got := m.AudioSampleRate(); got != 65536 {
		t.Fatalf("AudioSampleRate at resolution 1 = %d, want 65536", got)
	}
}

// TestMasterOffSilencesMachine: with the PSG playing,
// clearing the SOUNDCNT_X master enable silences the
// machine output completely.
func TestMasterOffSilencesMachine(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(irqSceneROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	playSquareA4(m)
	m.RunFrame()
	loud := m.AudioBuffer()
	nonzero := false
	for _, s := range loud {
		if s != 0 {
			nonzero = true
			break
		}
	}
	if !nonzero {
		t.Fatal("PSG produced no sound before master off; gate is meaningless")
	}
	m.Bus().Write(0x04000084, 2, 0x0000) // SOUNDCNT_X: master off
	m.RunFrame()
	quiet := m.AudioBuffer()
	if len(quiet) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no samples generated while master off; the stream must keep its rate")
	}
	for i, s := range quiet {
		if s != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("sample %d = %d with master off, want 0", i, s)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/system/save_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/save"
)

// GBA-4 gates for the cartridge save devices: synthetic
// ROMs whose save signature strings activate each device,
// exercised through the machine's bus windows, plus the
// SaveRAM frontend surface and the device block inside
// save states.

// saveSigROM builds a minimal cartridge image carrying
// the given save signature string, in the scene ROM
// style: a branch at the entry point (never run by these
// tests, which drive the bus directly) and the fixed
// header byte set.
func saveSigROM(sig string) []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x4000)
	rom[0x00] = 0xFE
	rom[0x01] = 0xFF
	rom[0x02] = 0xFF
	rom[0x03] = 0xEA // B .
	rom[0xB2] = 0x96
	copy(rom[0x200:], sig)
	return rom
}

func loadSaveROM(t *testing.T, sig string) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(saveSigROM(sig)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart(%q): %v", sig, err)
	}
	return m
}

func TestSaveKindActivation(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		sig  string
		kind cart.SaveKind
	}{
		{"SRAM_V110", cart.SaveSRAM},
		{"FLASH_V103", cart.SaveFlash},
		{"FLASH512_V101", cart.SaveFlash512},
		{"FLASH1M_V103", cart.SaveFlash1M},
		{"EEPROM_V122", cart.SaveEEPROM},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		m := loadSaveROM(t, c.sig)
		if m.Cart().SaveKind != c.kind {
			t.Fatalf("%s detected as %v, want %v", c.sig, m.Cart().SaveKind, c.kind)
		}
	}
}

func TestSRAMWindowMirrorAndSaveRAM(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadSaveROM(t, "SRAM_V110")
	b := m.Bus()
	b.Write(0x0E001234, 1, 0x5A)
	if got := b.Read(0x0E001234, 1); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("SRAM read back = %#02x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
	// The 32 KB part mirrors at +32 KB.
	if got := b.Read(0x0E009234, 1); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("SRAM mirror read = %#02x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
	sr := m.SaveRAM()
	if len(sr) != save.SRAMSize {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", len(sr), save.SRAMSize)
	}
	if sr[0x1234] != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM[0x1234] = %#02x, want 0x5A", sr[0x1234])
	}
	// Round trip into a fresh machine.
	m2 := loadSaveROM(t, "SRAM_V110")
	m2.SetSaveRAM(sr)
	if got := m2.Bus().Read(0x0E001234, 1); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("restored SRAM byte = %#02x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
}

func TestFlashThroughBus(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadSaveROM(t, "FLASH_V103")
	b := m.Bus()
	w := func(off uint32, v byte) { b.Write(0x0E000000+off, 1, uint32(v)) }
	r := func(off uint32) byte { return byte(b.Read(0x0E000000+off, 1)) }
	w(0x5555, 0xAA)
	w(0x2AAA, 0x55)
	w(0x5555, 0x90)
	if got := r(0); got != 0xC2 {
		t.Fatalf("flash ID manufacturer via bus = %#02x, want 0xC2", got)
	}
	if got := r(1); got != 0x1C {
		t.Fatalf("flash ID device via bus = %#02x, want 0x1C", got)
	}
	w(0x5555, 0xF0)
	w(0x5555, 0xAA)
	w(0x2AAA, 0x55)
	w(0x5555, 0xA0)
	w(0x0200, 0x66)
	if got := r(0x0200); got != 0x66 {
		t.Fatalf("programmed byte via bus = %#02x, want 0x66", got)
	}
	// The bus SRAM store must NOT have taken the writes:
	// the flash hook claimed the window.
	if got := b.SRAM[0x0200]; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("bus SRAM store polluted by flash traffic: %#02x", got)
	}
	if got := len(m.SaveRAM()); got != save.Flash64Size {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", got, save.Flash64Size)
	}
	if got := m.SaveRAM()[0x0200]; got != 0x66 {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM[0x200] = %#02x, want 0x66", got)
	}
}

func TestFlash1MThroughBus(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadSaveROM(t, "FLASH1M_V103")
	if got := len(m.SaveRAM()); got != save.Flash128Size {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", got, save.Flash128Size)
	}
	b := m.Bus()
	w := func(off uint32, v byte) { b.Write(0x0E000000+off, 1, uint32(v)) }
	cmd := func(c byte) {
		w(0x5555, 0xAA)
		w(0x2AAA, 0x55)
		w(0x5555, c)
	}
	cmd(0xA0)
	w(0x0010, 0x0B) // bank 0
	cmd(0xB0)
	w(0x0000, 0x01) // bank 1
	cmd(0xA0)
	w(0x0010, 0x0E) // bank 1
	sr := m.SaveRAM()
	if sr[0x0010] != 0x0B || sr[0x10010] != 0x0E {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM banks = %#02x/%#02x, want 0x0B/0x0E", sr[0x0010], sr[0x10010])
	}
}

// eeBusWriteBlock / eeBusReadBlock drive the EEPROM bit
// protocol through the machine bus with halfword
// accesses at 0x0D000000, the way games do it (usually
// via DMA; one bus access per bit either way).
func eeBusWriteBlock(t *testing.T, m *Machine, addr uint32, addrBits int, value uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	b := m.Bus()
	w := func(bit uint32) { b.Write(0x0D000000, 2, bit) }
	w(1)
	w(0)
	for i := addrBits - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		w((addr >> uint(i)) & 1)
	}
	for i := 63; i >= 0; i-- {
		w(uint32(value>>uint(i)) & 1)
	}
	w(0) // stop
	if got := b.Read(0x0D000000, 2) & 1; got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROM ready poll = %d, want 1", got)
	}
}

func eeBusReadBlock(t *testing.T, m *Machine, addr uint32, addrBits int) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	b := m.Bus()
	w := func(bit uint32) { b.Write(0x0D000000, 2, bit) }
	w(1)
	w(1)
	for i := addrBits - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		w((addr >> uint(i)) & 1)
	}
	w(0) // stop
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if got := b.Read(0x0D000000, 2) & 1; got != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("EEPROM dummy bit %d = %d, want 0", i, got)
		}
	}
	var v uint64
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		v = v<<1 | uint64(b.Read(0x0D000000, 2)&1)
	}
	return v
}

func TestEEPROMThroughBus(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadSaveROM(t, "EEPROM_V122")
	const want uint64 = 0x1122334455667788
	eeBusWriteBlock(t, m, 0x2BC, 14, want)
	if got := eeBusReadBlock(t, m, 0x2BC, 14); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROM block via bus = %#016x, want %#016x", got, want)
	}
	if got := len(m.SaveRAM()); got != save.EEPROM8K {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", got, save.EEPROM8K)
	}
}

func TestEEPROM512ThroughBus(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadSaveROM(t, "EEPROM_V110")
	// Pin the small part the way a frontend would: load a
	// 512 byte save image.
	m.SetSaveRAM(make([]byte, save.EEPROM512))
	const want uint64 = 0x8877665544332211
	eeBusWriteBlock(t, m, 0x15, 6, want)
	if got := eeBusReadBlock(t, m, 0x15, 6); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROM 512 block via bus = %#016x, want %#016x", got, want)
	}
	if got := len(m.SaveRAM()); got != save.EEPROM512 {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM len = %d, want %d", got, save.EEPROM512)
	}
}

func TestSaveDeviceInState(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadSaveROM(t, "FLASH_V103")
	b := m.Bus()
	w := func(off uint32, v byte) { b.Write(0x0E000000+off, 1, uint32(v)) }
	w(0x5555, 0xAA)
	w(0x2AAA, 0x55)
	w(0x5555, 0xA0)
	w(0x0300, 0x42)
	s := m.Serialize()
	m2 := loadSaveROM(t, "FLASH_V103")
	if err := m2.Deserialize(s); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if got := byte(m2.Bus().Read(0x0E000300, 1)); got != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("flash byte after state restore = %#02x, want 0x42", got)
	}
	if got := m2.SaveRAM()[0x0300]; got != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("SaveRAM after state restore = %#02x, want 0x42", got)
	}
	// The SRAM-side contents also ride the state (they
	// live in the bus stores, as before).
	m3 := loadSaveROM(t, "SRAM_V110")
	m3.Bus().Write(0x0E000777, 1, 0x24)
	s3 := m3.Serialize()
	m4 := loadSaveROM(t, "SRAM_V110")
	if err := m4.Deserialize(s3); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize SRAM state: %v", err)
	}
	if got := m4.SaveRAM()[0x777]; got != 0x24 {
		t.Fatalf("SRAM byte after state restore = %#02x, want 0x24", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/system/system.go ====================

// Package system is the whole Game Boy Advance machine:
// the ARM7TDMI CPU from chips/arm7tdmi, the memory map
// from the bus package, a parsed cartridge from the cart
// package, the PPU from the gpu package, the timers, DMA,
// interrupt controller and keypad from the periph package,
// the sound unit from the apu package, and our own BIOS
// code and SWI HLE from the bios package.
//
// Execution model: the frame runs line by line (228
// lines of 1232 cycles: 160 visible, 68 of vertical
// blank). Within a line the CPU runs for the visible
// portion first, the line is rendered by the PPU at the
// start of horizontal blank, line-triggered DMA and
// interrupts fire, and the CPU runs out the remainder of
// the line. Peripherals advance on the cycle counts the
// CPU reports, so timer and DMA behavior is consistent
// with the instruction stream at line granularity.
package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/apu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/bios"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/chips/arm7tdmi"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/gpu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/periph"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/save"
)

// Width and Height are the framebuffer dimensions, in the
// family shape the sibling cores use.
const (
	Width  = 240
	Height = 160
)

// CyclesPerFrame is the RunFrame budget.
const CyclesPerFrame = 280896

// CyclesPerLine is the documented line period.
const CyclesPerLine = 1232

// cyclesVisible is the part of a line before horizontal
// blank begins (cycles 0 to 1005); the rest of the line
// is the horizontal blank window.
const cyclesVisible = 1006

// linesPerFrame is 160 visible lines plus 68 of blank.
const linesPerFrame = 228

// Buttons, in GBATEK KEYINPUT bit order (bits 0 to 9).
// A set bit in the mask handed to SetButtons means the
// button is pressed; the keypad register reports the
// active low form.
const (
	ButtonA      = 1 << 0
	ButtonB      = 1 << 1
	ButtonSelect = 1 << 2
	ButtonStart  = 1 << 3
	ButtonRight  = 1 << 4
	ButtonLeft   = 1 << 5
	ButtonUp     = 1 << 6
	ButtonDown   = 1 << 7
	ButtonR      = 1 << 8
	ButtonL      = 1 << 9

	buttonsMask = 0x3FF // the low 10 bits
)

// stateVersion is the save state format version. Version
// 3 covers the CPU state, the bus stores, the GBA-2
// component states (PPU, interrupt controller, timers,
// DMA, keypad, BIOS wait state), the GBA-3 sound unit
// state, and the machine trailer. Version 4 adds the
// GBA-4 cartridge save device block (contents and
// protocol state, see the save package) between the
// sound unit block and the trailer; version 3 states are
// refused, as version 2 states were before them.
const stateVersion = 4

// machineTrailerSize is the fixed trailer behind the
// component blocks: buttons, current line, and the FIFO
// sink counters and last values for DMA channels 1 and 2.
const machineTrailerSize = 4 + 4 + 2*8 + 2*4

// Machine is one powered-on GBA.
type Machine struct {
	cpu  *arm7tdmi.CPU
	bus  *bus.Bus
	cart *cart.Cart

	gpu    *gpu.GPU
	irq    *periph.IRQ
	timers *periph.Timers
	dma    *periph.DMA
	keys   *periph.Keypad
	apu    *apu.APU
	biosH  *bios.Handler

	// dev is the cartridge save device (flash or EEPROM,
	// per the cartridge's detected kind), installed
	// behind the bus save hooks. SRAM and signature-less
	// cartridges leave it without a window to serve; their
	// contents live in the bus SRAM store.
	dev        *save.Device
	devROMSize int

	buttons uint32
	line    int

	// The FIFO sink counters: every word the FIFO DMA
	// channels deliver is counted per channel and the most
	// recent value kept, alongside being pushed into the
	// sound unit's FIFOs (see FIFOSample).
	fifoCount [2]uint64
	fifoLast  [2]uint32
}

// New builds an empty machine (no cartridge) in its
// power-on state.
func New() *Machine {
	m := &Machine{}
	m.power()
	return m
}

// power rebuilds the bus, installs our BIOS code into the
// BIOS store, recreates the CPU and every component, and
// wires the dispatch hooks. The cartridge (if any) stays
// attached. This is the shared body of construction,
// LoadCart and Reset.
func (m *Machine) power() {
	rom := []byte(nil)
	if m.cart != nil {
		rom = m.cart.ROM
	}
	m.bus = bus.New()
	m.bus.SetROM(rom)
	bios.Install(m.bus.BIOS[:])
	m.cpu = arm7tdmi.New(m.bus)
	m.gpu = gpu.New(m.bus.Palette[:], m.bus.VRAM[:], m.bus.OAM[:])
	m.irq = periph.NewIRQ()
	m.timers = periph.NewTimers()
	m.dma = periph.NewDMA(m.bus, m.irq, m)
	m.keys = periph.NewKeypad()
	m.apu = apu.New()
	m.biosH = bios.New(m.bus)
	// Sound wiring: timer overflows clock the Direct
	// Sound FIFOs (the APU pops one sample per overflow of
	// the timer each FIFO channel selected), and the APU's
	// refill request, raised when a FIFO drops to the
	// documented half-empty level, runs one FIFO DMA burst
	// on the matching channel (DMA1 feeds FIFO A, DMA2
	// feeds FIFO B).
	m.timers.OnOverflow = m.apu.OnTimerOverflow
	m.apu.Refill = func(fifo int) {
		if m.apu.WantsData(fifo) {
			m.dma.OnFIFO(fifo + 1)
		}
	}
	m.cpu.SWIHook = m.biosH.Hook
	m.bus.IORead = m.ioRead
	m.bus.IOWrite = m.ioWrite
	// The cartridge save device. Contents survive a
	// machine reset (a battery does not empty when the
	// console resets), so the device is rebuilt only when
	// the cartridge or its ROM image changes; a plain
	// reset keeps the device and just idles its protocol.
	kind := cart.SaveNone
	romSize := 0
	if m.cart != nil {
		kind = m.cart.SaveKind
		romSize = len(m.cart.ROM)
	}
	if m.dev == nil || m.dev.Kind() != kind || m.devROMSize != romSize {
		m.dev = save.New(kind, romSize)
		m.devROMSize = romSize
	} else {
		m.dev.ResetProtocol()
	}
	m.bus.SaveRead = m.saveRead
	m.bus.SaveWrite = m.saveWrite
	if kind == cart.SaveSRAM || kind == cart.SaveNone {
		// A 32 KB battery part (and the signature-less
		// fallback window): the upper half of the window
		// mirrors the lower half.
		m.bus.SRAMMask = save.SRAMSize - 1
	}
	// The stack pointers the BIOS boot stub also sets,
	// preset here so a CPU primed directly at the
	// cartridge entry (as tools and tests do) still sees
	// the documented stacks.
	m.cpu.R[13] = bios.SVCStackTop
	m.cpu.RSVC[0] = bios.SVCStackTop
	m.cpu.RIRQ[0] = bios.IRQStackTop
	m.cpu.RUSR[0] = bios.UserStackTop
	m.buttons = 0
	m.line = 0
	m.fifoCount = [2]uint64{}
	m.fifoLast = [2]uint32{}
}

// LoadCart parses a cartridge image, attaches it to the
// bus ROM windows, and resets the machine. A parse error
// leaves the previous cartridge (if any) untouched.
func (m *Machine) LoadCart(rom []byte) error {
	c, err := cart.Parse(rom)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	m.cart = c
	m.power()
	return nil
}

// Reset returns the machine to power-on state with the
// current cartridge kept loaded.
func (m *Machine) Reset() { m.power() }

// Cart returns the loaded cartridge, or nil.
func (m *Machine) Cart() *cart.Cart { return m.cart }

// Bus returns the system bus, for tools and tests.
func (m *Machine) Bus() *bus.Bus { return m.bus }

// CPU returns the processor, for tools and tests.
func (m *Machine) CPU() *arm7tdmi.CPU { return m.cpu }

// GPU returns the picture processor, for tools and tests.
func (m *Machine) GPU() *gpu.GPU { return m.gpu }

// Title returns the loaded game's title, or empty.
func (m *Machine) Title() string {
	if m.cart == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return m.cart.Title
}

// FIFOSample is the DMA FIFO sink: words delivered by
// DMA channels 1 and 2 are counted (the GBA-2 counters
// stay as an observability hook) and pushed into the
// sound unit's FIFOs, four sample bytes per word, least
// significant byte first.
func (m *Machine) FIFOSample(channel int, value uint32) {
	if channel < 1 || channel > 2 {
		return
	}
	m.fifoCount[channel-1]++
	m.fifoLast[channel-1] = value
	m.apu.PushFIFO(channel-1, value)
}

// FIFOSamples reports how many FIFO samples a DMA
// channel (1 or 2) has delivered since power-on.
func (m *Machine) FIFOSamples(channel int) uint64 {
	if channel < 1 || channel > 2 {
		return 0
	}
	return m.fifoCount[channel-1]
}

// IO dispatch.

// ioRead routes an IO window read to the component that
// owns the register. Behavior-less registers fall
// through to the bus's plain IO store.
func (m *Machine) ioRead(off uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	switch {
	case off < 0x60:
		return m.gpu.ReadReg(off, size), true
	case off >= 0x60 && off < 0xA8:
		return m.apu.ReadReg(off, size), true
	case off >= 0xB0 && off < 0xE0:
		return m.dma.ReadReg(off, size), true
	case off >= 0x100 && off < 0x110:
		return m.timers.ReadReg(off, size), true
	case off >= 0x130 && off < 0x134:
		return m.keys.ReadReg(off, size), true
	case off >= 0x200 && off < 0x204, off >= 0x208 && off < 0x20C:
		return m.irq.ReadReg(off, size), true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// ioWrite routes an IO window write to the component
// that owns the register.
func (m *Machine) ioWrite(off uint32, size int, val uint32) bool {
	switch {
	case off < 0x60:
		m.gpu.WriteReg(off, size, val)
	case off >= 0x60 && off < 0xA8:
		m.apu.WriteReg(off, size, val)
	case off >= 0xB0 && off < 0xE0:
		m.dma.WriteReg(off, size, val)
	case off >= 0x100 && off < 0x110:
		m.timers.WriteReg(off, size, val)
	case off >= 0x130 && off < 0x134:
		m.keys.WriteReg(off, size, val)
	case off >= 0x200 && off < 0x204, off >= 0x208 && off < 0x20C:
		m.irq.WriteReg(off, size, val)
	default:
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// Save device hooks and the frontend save interface.

// saveRead gives the save device first claim on its
// windows: the top of the map for flash, the 0x0D window
// (when the EEPROM window rule activates the address)
// for EEPROM. Anything else falls through to the bus.
func (m *Machine) saveRead(addr uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	switch addr >> 24 {
	case 0x0E, 0x0F:
		if m.dev.IsFlash() {
			return m.dev.FlashRead(addr, size), true
		}
	case 0x0D:
		if m.dev.EEPROMActive(addr) {
			return m.dev.EEPROMRead(), true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

// saveWrite is the write half of saveRead. EEPROM writes
// clock one protocol bit per access, so DMA driven
// transfers (one bus access per unit) work unchanged.
func (m *Machine) saveWrite(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) bool {
	switch addr >> 24 {
	case 0x0E, 0x0F:
		if m.dev.IsFlash() {
			m.dev.FlashWrite(addr, val)
			return true
		}
	case 0x0D:
		if m.dev.EEPROMActive(addr) {
			m.dev.EEPROMWrite(val)
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// SaveRAM returns a copy of the cartridge's save
// contents, sized by the detected save kind: 32 KB for
// SRAM, 64 or 128 KB for flash, 512 bytes or 8 KB for
// EEPROM (the size the device has identified). A
// cartridge without a save signature gets the fallback
// window: plain 32 KB SRAM behind the save window, which
// is what signature-less homebrew (for example Anguna)
// expects to find there. With no cartridge loaded it
// returns nil.
func (m *Machine) SaveRAM() []byte {
	if m.cart == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if m.dev.IsFlash() || m.dev.IsEEPROM() {
		return m.dev.SaveRAM()
	}
	out := make([]byte, save.SRAMSize)
	copy(out, m.bus.SRAM[:save.SRAMSize])
	return out
}

// SetSaveRAM loads save contents saved earlier, the
// counterpart of SaveRAM. Contents for the wrong family
// or of an unrecognized length are ignored (see the
// save package for the exact acceptance rules); SRAM
// images shorter than 32 KB load with the rest zeroed.
func (m *Machine) SetSaveRAM(b []byte) {
	if m.dev.IsFlash() || m.dev.IsEEPROM() {
		m.dev.SetSaveRAM(b)
		return
	}
	for i := 0; i < save.SRAMSize; i++ {
		m.bus.SRAM[i] = 0
	}
	copy(m.bus.SRAM[:save.SRAMSize], b)
}

// SaveDevice returns the cartridge save device, for
// tools and tests.
func (m *Machine) SaveDevice() *save.Device { return m.dev }

// Execution.

// runCPU steps the CPU for the given cycle budget,
// advancing the timers and the sound unit by the cycles
// each step reports (timer overflows reach the sound
// unit through the timers' OnOverflow hook, and the
// sound unit then advances by the same count) and
// keeping the CPU's IRQ input level current. A BIOS wait
// in progress is polled on every step, not just while the
// CPU is halted: the wait completes through the IRQ
// dispatcher, and the handler's Poll watches both the
// halted side and the return from dispatch (see
// bios.Handler.Poll).
func (m *Machine) runCPU(cycles int) {
	spent := 0
	for spent < cycles {
		if m.biosH.Waiting() {
			m.biosH.Poll(m.cpu)
		}
		m.cpu.IRQLine = m.irq.Asserted()
		n := m.cpu.Step()
		m.timers.Advance(n, m.irq)
		m.apu.Advance(n)
		spent += n
	}
}

// runLines advances the machine by n scanlines. Each
// line: vblank and vcount events are evaluated at the
// line start, the PPU latches its scroll registers, the
// CPU runs the visible portion, the line renders as
// horizontal blank begins, HBlank events fire, and the
// CPU runs the rest of the line.
func (m *Machine) runLines(n int) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		line := m.line
		m.gpu.SetLine(line)
		dispstat := m.gpu.ReadReg(0x04, 2)
		if line == 160 {
			m.gpu.SetVBlank(true)
			if dispstat&0x0008 != 0 {
				m.irq.Raise(periph.IRQVBlank)
			}
			m.dma.OnVBlank()
		}
		if line == 0 {
			m.gpu.SetVBlank(false)
		}
		if m.gpu.VCountMatch() && dispstat&0x0020 != 0 {
			m.irq.Raise(periph.IRQVCount)
		}
		m.gpu.BeginLine()
		m.runCPU(cyclesVisible)
		if line < Height {
			m.gpu.RenderLine()
		}
		m.gpu.SetHBlank(true)
		if dispstat&0x0010 != 0 {
			m.irq.Raise(periph.IRQHBlank)
		}
		if line < Height {
			m.dma.OnHBlank()
		}
		m.runCPU(CyclesPerLine - cyclesVisible)
		m.gpu.SetHBlank(false)
		m.line++
		if m.line >= linesPerFrame {
			m.line = 0
		}
	}
}

// RunFrame advances the machine by one frame: 228 lines
// against the documented per-frame cycle budget.
func (m *Machine) RunFrame() { m.runLines(linesPerFrame) }

// Framebuffer returns the machine frame as Width*Height
// XRGB8888 pixels, owned by the PPU.
func (m *Machine) Framebuffer() []uint32 { return m.gpu.Framebuffer() }

// AudioBuffer drains the sound unit's pending output:
// interleaved stereo int16 samples at the rate
// AudioSampleRate reports. The slice is empty when no
// full output sample has accumulated since the last
// drain.
func (m *Machine) AudioBuffer() []int16 { return m.apu.AudioBuffer() }

// AudioSampleRate returns the current output sample rate
// in Hz, selected by the SOUNDBIAS resolution bits
// (32768 Hz at power-on).
func (m *Machine) AudioSampleRate() int { return m.apu.SampleRate() }

// SetButtons stores the controller mask (see the Button
// constants) and presents it to the keypad register,
// which evaluates its interrupt condition.
func (m *Machine) SetButtons(mask uint32) {
	m.buttons = mask & buttonsMask
	m.keys.SetButtons(m.buttons, m.irq)
}

// Buttons returns the stored controller mask.
func (m *Machine) Buttons() uint32 { return m.buttons }

// Save states.

// StateSize returns the exact byte size of a serialized
// state: the version byte, the CPU block, the seven bus
// stores, the component blocks (PPU, interrupt
// controller, timers, DMA, keypad, BIOS wait state,
// sound unit), the cartridge save device block, and the
// machine trailer.
func (m *Machine) StateSize() int {
	return 1 + arm7tdmi.StateSize +
		bus.EWRAMSize + bus.IWRAMSize + bus.SRAMSize +
		bus.PaletteSize + bus.VRAMSize + bus.OAMSize + bus.IOSize +
		gpu.StateSize + periph.IRQStateSize + periph.TimersStateSize +
		periph.DMAStateSize + periph.KeypadStateSize + bios.HandlerStateSize +
		apu.StateSize + save.StateSize +
		machineTrailerSize
}

// Serialize captures the machine in the layout StateSize
// describes. The BIOS store is not part of the state (it
// holds our own code, reinstalled at power-on) and
// neither is the ROM image.
func (m *Machine) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, m.StateSize())
	out[0] = stateVersion
	off := 1
	off += m.cpu.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += copy(out[off:], m.bus.EWRAM[:])
	off += copy(out[off:], m.bus.IWRAM[:])
	off += copy(out[off:], m.bus.SRAM[:])
	off += copy(out[off:], m.bus.Palette[:])
	off += copy(out[off:], m.bus.VRAM[:])
	off += copy(out[off:], m.bus.OAM[:])
	off += copy(out[off:], m.bus.IO[:])
	off += m.gpu.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += m.irq.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += m.timers.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += m.dma.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += m.keys.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += m.biosH.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += m.apu.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += m.dev.Serialize(out[off:])
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], m.buttons)
	off += 4
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], uint32(m.line))
	off += 4
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(out[off:], m.fifoCount[i])
		off += 8
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], m.fifoLast[i])
		off += 4
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
// The input must be exactly StateSize bytes and carry
// the current version; older versions are rejected by
// that check, as in the sibling cores. The memory stores
// and components are restored before the CPU, because
// the CPU's Deserialize re-fetches its executing
// instruction through the bus.
func (m *Machine) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != m.StateSize() {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d, want %d", len(in), m.StateSize())
	}
	if in[0] != stateVersion {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state version %d, want %d", in[0], stateVersion)
	}
	off := 1 + arm7tdmi.StateSize
	off += copy(m.bus.EWRAM[:], in[off:])
	off += copy(m.bus.IWRAM[:], in[off:])
	off += copy(m.bus.SRAM[:], in[off:])
	off += copy(m.bus.Palette[:], in[off:])
	off += copy(m.bus.VRAM[:], in[off:])
	off += copy(m.bus.OAM[:], in[off:])
	off += copy(m.bus.IO[:], in[off:])
	blocks := []struct {
		size int
		load func([]byte) bool
	}{
		{gpu.StateSize, m.gpu.Deserialize},
		{periph.IRQStateSize, m.irq.Deserialize},
		{periph.TimersStateSize, m.timers.Deserialize},
		{periph.DMAStateSize, m.dma.Deserialize},
		{periph.KeypadStateSize, m.keys.Deserialize},
		{bios.HandlerStateSize, m.biosH.Deserialize},
		{apu.StateSize, m.apu.Deserialize},
		{save.StateSize, m.dev.Deserialize},
	}
	for _, b := range blocks {
		if !b.load(in[off : off+b.size]) {
			return fmt.Errorf("system: component state block at %d rejected", off)
		}
		off += b.size
	}
	m.buttons = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
	off += 4
	m.line = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:]))
	off += 4
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		m.fifoCount[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(in[off:])
		off += 8
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		m.fifoLast[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
	}
	m.keys.SetButtons(m.buttons, m.irq)
	if !m.cpu.Deserialize(in[1 : 1+arm7tdmi.StateSize]) {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: CPU state block too short")
	}
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/system/system_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// Synthetic ROM.

// armImm builds a data processing instruction with an
// immediate operand from its fields: MOV is opcode 13,
// ORR is opcode 12. The operand is imm8 rotated right by
// rot*2 bits, the ARM modified immediate encoding.
func armImm(opcode, rn, rd, rot, imm8 uint32) uint32 {
	return 0xE0000000 | 1<<25 | opcode<<21 | rn<<16 | rd<<12 | rot<<8 | imm8
}

// armBuildConst emits the instructions that load a
// 32-bit constant into register rd: a MOV of the low
// byte followed by one ORR per non-zero higher byte,
// each byte rotated into its position.
func armBuildConst(rd, v uint32) []uint32 {
	out := []uint32{armImm(13, 0, rd, 0, v&0xFF)} // MOV rd, #low byte
	rots := []uint32{0, 12, 8, 4}                 // ROR 0, 24, 16, 8 by byte position
	for i := 1; i < 4; i++ {
		b := (v >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
		if b != 0 {
			out = append(out, armImm(12, rd, rd, rots[i], b)) // ORR rd, rd, #byte in place
		}
	}
	return out
}

// armSTR builds STR rd, [rn] (byte=false) or STRB rd,
// [rn] (byte=true) with a zero immediate offset.
func armSTR(rd, rn uint32, byteOp bool) uint32 {
	w := uint32(0xE5800000) | rn<<16 | rd<<12
	if byteOp {
		w |= 1 << 22
	}
	return w
}

// armBranch builds a branch at code index from to code
// index to, with the given condition field (0xE is
// always, 0x1 is not equal). The offset counts in words
// from the address of the branch plus 8, like hardware.
func armBranch(cond uint32, from, to int) uint32 {
	return cond<<28 | 0x0A000000 | uint32((to-(from+2))&0xFFFFFF)
}

// syntheticROM builds a 4 KB image behind a valid header.
// The entry word at 0x00 is an ARM branch to the code at
// 0xC0: the branch offset is (0xC0 - 8) / 4 = 0x2E words,
// since the program counter reads as the address of the
// branch plus 8, so the word is 0xEA00002E. The code at
// 0xC0 first fills 64 EWRAM words with 0x11223344 + i,
// then loops forever: it sums the 64 words into a
// checksum, stores the checksum at IWRAM+0, the running
// iteration count at IWRAM+4, and the low checksum byte
// at SRAM+0. Because the loop never ends, a save state
// taken mid-run captures live progress, and continuing
// from it must reproduce the uninterrupted run exactly.
func syntheticROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x1000)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x00:], 0xEA00002E)
	copy(rom[0xA0:], "SYNTHTEST")
	copy(rom[0xAC:], "ASYE")
	copy(rom[0xB0:], "01")
	rom[0xB2] = 0x96
	rom[0xBC] = 0x01
	sum := 0x19
	for _, c := range rom[0xA0 : 0xBC+1] {
		sum += int(c)
	}
	rom[0xBD] = uint8(-sum)

	var code []uint32
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(0, 0x02000000)...) // r0 = EWRAM base
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x11223344)...) // r1 = fill pattern
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(4, 0x03000000)...) // r4 = IWRAM base
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(7, 0x0E000000)...) // r7 = SRAM base
	code = append(code, armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 0))          // MOV r2, #0
	fill := len(code)
	code = append(code,
		0xE7801102,             // STR r1, [r0, r2, LSL #2]
		armImm(4, 1, 1, 0, 1),  // ADD r1, r1, #1
		armImm(4, 2, 2, 0, 1),  // ADD r2, r2, #1
		0xE3520040,             // CMP r2, #64
		0,                      // BNE fill (patched below)
		armImm(13, 0, 6, 0, 0), // MOV r6, #0 (iteration count)
	)
	outer := len(code)
	code = append(code,
		armImm(13, 0, 5, 0, 0), // MOV r5, #0 (checksum)
		armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 0), // MOV r2, #0
	)
	sumLoop := len(code)
	code = append(code,
		0xE7903102,            // LDR r3, [r0, r2, LSL #2]
		0xE0855003,            // ADD r5, r5, r3
		armImm(4, 2, 2, 0, 1), // ADD r2, r2, #1
		0xE3520040,            // CMP r2, #64
		0,                     // BNE sumLoop (patched below)
		armSTR(5, 4, false),   // STR r5, [r4]
		0xE5846004,            // STR r6, [r4, #4]
		armSTR(5, 7, true),    // STRB r5, [r7]
		armImm(4, 6, 6, 0, 1), // ADD r6, r6, #1
		0,                     // B outer (patched below)
	)
	code[fill+4] = armBranch(1, fill+4, fill)
	code[sumLoop+4] = armBranch(1, sumLoop+4, sumLoop)
	last := len(code) - 1
	code[last] = armBranch(0xE, last, outer)
	for i, w := range code {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0xC0+4*i:], w)
	}
	return rom
}

// wantChecksum is the sum the synthetic program
// accumulates over its 64 filled EWRAM words.
func wantChecksum() uint32 {
	var s uint32
	for i := uint32(0); i < 64; i++ {
		s += 0x11223344 + i
	}
	return s
}

// assertProgramEffects checks the results the synthetic
// program produces: the filled EWRAM table, the checksum
// and a positive iteration count in IWRAM, and the low
// checksum byte in SRAM.
func assertProgramEffects(t *testing.T, m *Machine) {
	t.Helper()
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x02000000, 4); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("EWRAM word 0 = %#08x, want 0x11223344", got)
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x02000000+63*4, 4); got != 0x11223344+63 {
		t.Errorf("EWRAM word 63 = %#08x, want %#08x", got, 0x11223344+63)
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03000000, 4); got != wantChecksum() {
		t.Errorf("IWRAM checksum = %#08x, want %#08x", got, wantChecksum())
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03000004, 4); got == 0 {
		t.Error("IWRAM iteration count is 0, the checksum loop never stored")
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x0E000000, 1); got != uint32(byte(wantChecksum())) {
		t.Errorf("SRAM byte = %#02x, want %#02x", got, byte(wantChecksum()))
	}
}

func TestLoadCartAndFramebuffer(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(syntheticROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	if m.Title() != "SYNTHTEST" {
		t.Errorf("Title = %q, want SYNTHTEST", m.Title())
	}
	if m.Cart() == nil || m.Cart().GameCode != "ASYE" {
		t.Errorf("Cart header not wired: %+v", m.Cart())
	}
	if Width != 240 || Height != 160 {
		t.Errorf("dimensions = %dx%d, want 240x160", Width, Height)
	}
	fb := m.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) != Width*Height {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer has %d pixels, want %d", len(fb), Width*Height)
	}
	for i, p := range fb {
		if p != 0xFF000000 {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer[%d] = %#08x, want 0xFF000000 (blank)", i, p)
		}
	}
	// RunFrame must return and leave the blank frame.
	m.RunFrame()
	if len(m.Framebuffer()) != Width*Height {
		t.Fatal("framebuffer changed size after RunFrame")
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	rom := syntheticROM()
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	m.RunFrame()
	// Scribble every serialized store with known values.
	m.Bus().Write(0x02000000, 4, 0x11223344)
	m.Bus().Write(0x03000000, 4, 0x55667788)
	m.Bus().Write(0x0E000000, 1, 0xAA)
	m.Bus().Write(0x05000000, 2, 0x7FFF)
	m.Bus().Write(0x06000000, 4, 0xCAFEBABE)
	m.Bus().Write(0x07000000, 4, 0x0BADF00D)
	m.Bus().Write(0x04000204, 2, 0x4317)

	s1 := m.Serialize()
	if len(s1) != m.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize produced %d bytes, StateSize says %d", len(s1), m.StateSize())
	}
	if s1[0] != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("version byte = %d, want 4", s1[0])
	}

	// Deserialize must not depend on cart size or history:
	// a fresh machine with the same cart restores it and
	// serializes back to identical bytes.
	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart (second machine): %v", err)
	}
	if m2.StateSize() != m.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("StateSize differs between machines: %d vs %d", m2.StateSize(), m.StateSize())
	}
	if err := m2.Deserialize(s1); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if s2 := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(s1, s2) {
		t.Fatal("serialize after deserialize differs from the original state")
	}
	// Restoring into the same machine is also a no-op.
	if err := m.Deserialize(s1); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize (same machine): %v", err)
	}
	if s3 := m.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(s1, s3) {
		t.Fatal("same machine round trip differs")
	}
}

func TestDeserializeRejectsBadInput(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(syntheticROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	good := m.Serialize()
	if err := m.Deserialize(good[:len(good)-1]); err == nil {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted a short state")
	}
	if err := m.Deserialize(append(append([]byte{}, good...), 0)); err == nil {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted an oversized state")
	}
	badVersion := append([]byte{}, good...)
	badVersion[0] = 99
	if err := m.Deserialize(badVersion); err == nil {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted version 99")
	}
}

// primeEntry loads the CPU pipeline at the cartridge
// entry point 0x08000000. A powered-on GBA starts in the
// BIOS, which is what normally jumps there; this core
// ships no BIOS (and BIOS SWI HLE is a later slice), so
// the tests perform that jump themselves, in exactly the
// state the CPU's own Reset refill produces for the reset
// vector.
func primeEntry(m *Machine) {
	c := m.CPU()
	const entry = 0x08000000
	c.Executing = m.Bus().Fetch(entry, 4)
	c.Pipe[0] = m.Bus().Fetch(entry+4, 4)
	c.Pipe[1] = m.Bus().Fetch(entry+8, 4)
	c.R[15] = entry + 8
	c.ExecutingValid = true
}

// TestSyntheticROMExecution runs the hand-assembled
// program through the machine and checks the filled
// table, the checksum loop results in IWRAM, and the
// low byte in SRAM.
func TestSyntheticROMExecution(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(syntheticROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	primeEntry(m)
	m.RunFrame()
	assertProgramEffects(t, m)
}

// TestSaveStateContinuation proves the deterministic
// round trip under execution: run the checksum loop,
// save mid-run, run further, and require that a machine
// restored from the mid-run save reaches byte-identical
// state after the same additional frames.
func TestSaveStateContinuation(t *testing.T) {
	rom := syntheticROM()
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	primeEntry(m)
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	s1 := m.Serialize()
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	want := m.Serialize()
	assertProgramEffects(t, m)

	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart (second machine): %v", err)
	}
	if err := m2.Deserialize(s1); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	m2.RunFrame()
	m2.RunFrame()
	if got := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatal("continuation after a mid-run restore differs from the uninterrupted run")
	}
	assertProgramEffects(t, m2)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-gba/system/wait_regression_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// The IntrWait regression gate, added by GBA-4 after the
// Anguna homebrew game exposed the deadlock it covers:
// a game whose main loop sleeps in VBlankIntrWait (SWI
// 0x05) never woke, because the CPU took the VBlank IRQ
// exception while halted but kept its halted flag set,
// freezing the core inside the exception entry with the
// BIOS dispatcher (the code that records the event in
// the check word the wait polls) unreachable.
//
// The synthetic program below boots through the core's
// own BIOS stub, installs a VBlank handler that counts
// its calls in IWRAM, and then loops on VBlankIntrWait,
// counting completed waits beside it. If any link in the
// chain (IRQ wake from halt, dispatcher, check word,
// wait completion) breaks, one of the counters stalls.

// waitSceneROM builds the 4 KB test image: main code at
// 0xC0, IRQ handler at 0x200, in the irqSceneROM layout.
func waitSceneROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x1000)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x00:], 0xEA00002E)
	copy(rom[0xA0:], "WAITSCENE")
	copy(rom[0xAC:], "ASYE")
	copy(rom[0xB0:], "01")
	rom[0xB2] = 0x96
	rom[0xBC] = 0x01
	sum := 0x19
	for _, c := range rom[0xA0 : 0xBC+1] {
		sum += int(c)
	}
	rom[0xBD] = uint8(-sum)

	var code []uint32
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(0, 0x03007F00)...) // R0 = user stack top
	code = append(code, 0xE1A0D000)                      // MOV SP, R0
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x03007FFC)...) // R1 = handler pointer slot
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(2, 0x08000200)...) // R2 = handler address
	code = append(code, armSTR(2, 1, false))             // STR R2, [R1]
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x04000004)...) // R1 = DISPSTAT
	code = append(code, armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 8))          // MOV R2, #8 (VBlank IRQ enable)
	code = append(code, armSTRH(2, 1))                   // STRH R2, [R1]
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x04000200)...) // R1 = IE
	code = append(code, armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 1))          // MOV R2, #1 (VBlank)
	code = append(code, armSTRH(2, 1))                   // STRH R2, [R1]
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(1, 0x04000208)...) // R1 = IME
	code = append(code, armImm(13, 0, 2, 0, 1))          // MOV R2, #1
	code = append(code, armSTRH(2, 1))                   // STRH R2, [R1]
	code = append(code,
		0xE10F0000,                // MRS R0, CPSR
		armImm(14, 0, 0, 0, 0x80), // BIC R0, R0, #0x80 (IRQ enable)
		0xE121F000,                // MSR CPSR_c, R0
	)
	code = append(code, armBuildConst(4, 0x03000020)...) // R4 = progress counter
	swiAt := len(code)
	code = append(code, 0xEF050000) // SWI 0x05: VBlankIntrWait
	code = append(code,
		0xE5941000,            // LDR R1, [R4]
		armImm(4, 1, 1, 0, 1), // ADD R1, R1, #1
		0xE5841000,            // STR R1, [R4]
	)
	branchAddr := uint32(0xC0 + 4*len(code))
	target := uint32(0xC0 + 4*swiAt)
	off := (int32(target) - int32(branchAddr) - 8) / 4
	code = append(code, 0xEA000000|(uint32(off)&0xFFFFFF)) // B back to the SWI
	for i, w := range code {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0xC0+4*i:], w)
	}

	// The handler at 0x200: bump the word at IWRAM+0x10
	// and return to the dispatcher with BX LR.
	var handler []uint32
	handler = append(handler, 0xE92D0003) // PUSH {R0, R1}
	handler = append(handler, armBuildConst(0, 0x03000010)...)
	handler = append(handler,
		0xE5901000,            // LDR R1, [R0]
		armImm(4, 1, 1, 0, 1), // ADD R1, R1, #1
		0xE5801000,            // STR R1, [R0]
		0xE8BD0003,            // POP {R0, R1}
		0xE12FFF1E,            // BX LR
	)
	for i, w := range handler {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x200+4*i:], w)
	}
	return rom
}

// TestVBlankIntrWaitProgress is the core of the gate:
// one handler call and one completed wait per frame,
// with the check word consumed after each wake.
func TestVBlankIntrWaitProgress(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(waitSceneROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03000010, 4); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("VBlank handler ran %d times in 5 frames, want exactly 5", got)
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03000020, 4); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("VBlankIntrWait completed %d times in 5 frames, want exactly 5 (the wait deadlocked or double-woke)", got)
	}
	if got := m.Bus().Read(0x03007FF8, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BIOS check word = %#08x, want 0 (each wake consumes its bit)", got)
	}
}

// TestVBlankIntrWaitMidWaitState covers the save path: a
// state taken while the CPU sits halted inside a wait
// must restore into a wait that still completes, and the
// continuation must be byte identical to the
// uninterrupted run.
func TestVBlankIntrWaitMidWaitState(t *testing.T) {
	rom := waitSceneROM()
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	if !m.cpu.Halted || !m.biosH.Waiting() {
		t.Fatalf("after 3 frames the machine should be halted inside wait 4 (halted %v, waiting %v)",
			m.cpu.Halted, m.biosH.Waiting())
	}
	save := m.Serialize()
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	wantState := m.Serialize()

	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.LoadCart(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCart (second machine): %v", err)
	}
	if err := m2.Deserialize(save); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if !m2.biosH.Waiting() {
		t.Fatal("the restored machine lost the outstanding BIOS wait")
	}
	m2.RunFrame()
	m2.RunFrame()
	if got := m2.Bus().Read(0x03000010, 4); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("restored machine: handler ran %d times in 5 frames, want 5", got)
	}
	if got := m2.Bus().Read(0x03000020, 4); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("restored machine: waits completed %d times in 5 frames, want 5", got)
	}
	if got := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Fatal("state after a mid-wait restore and continuation differs from the uninterrupted run")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/APP_WIRING_PLAN.md ====================

# Wiring the Go Genesis core into the app (recon done 2026-10-12 night)

Goal: Genesis games in the app run on our in-house Go core instead of
Genesis Plus GX, with zero regression.

## Where cores are wired

- Flutter table: flutter_ui/lib/main.dart, kSystems, the genesis entry
  (id 'genesis', exts .md/.gen/.bin) names core 'libgenesis_plus_gx.so'.
- Go backend registry: go_backend/internal/core/types.go line 36
  (SystemGenesis) and line 41 (SystemSegaCD), both naming
  libgenesis_plus_gx.so today.
- Core binaries: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/assets/cores/*.so.
  They are NOT in git. The server pipeline rsync EXCLUDES that dir, so
  staging is a file operation on the server build tree (~/itak-gaming)
  plus the local workspace copy.

## The Sega CD catch

Genesis Plus GX also serves Sega CD (SystemSegaCD, .cue/.iso) in the
backend registry. Our core has no Sega CD yet (roadmap item). So:

- Switch SystemGenesis (both registries) to libgo_genesis.so.
- Sega CD STAYS on libgenesis_plus_gx.so; the binary stays in assets
  for that one system until our Sega CD support lands, then it is
  deleted. Removing Sega CD outright would regress a working system,
  which David's no-regression rule forbids.

## Build the Android core

Target is android-arm (32-bit), per the pipeline's flutter build.
On the server (NDK 26.1 at ~/toolchain/android-sdk/ndk/26.1.10909125,
Go at ~/toolchain/go/bin):

  cd cores/go-genesis
  CGO_ENABLED=1 GOOS=android GOARCH=arm GOARM=7 \
  CC=$NDK/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/armv7a-linux-androideabi24-clang \
  go build -buildmode=c-shared -trimpath \
    -o libgo_genesis.so ./libretro

(The libretro package builds c-shared on linux today; the same entry
must produce the Android .so. Discard the generated .h or keep it out
of assets.) Verify with `file` (ELF 32-bit ARM) and nm -D that the
retro_* exports are present.

==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/README.md ====================

# go-genesis: a Sega Genesis core written in Go

Clean-room Sega Genesis / Mega Drive emulator core for iTaK Gaming, written
in Go and exposed through the libretro API so the iTaK engine can load it
exactly like any other core.

Why this exists: the Genesis Plus GX core bundled today carries a
non-commercial license, which blocks any future monetization of the app.
This core is 100 percent our own code (MIT, same as the rest of iTaK
Gaming), written from published hardware documentation: the Motorola
M68000 Programmer's Reference Manual, the Zilog Z80 manual, and the TI
SN76489 datasheet plus Sega variant notes.

Milestone 1 ran on three MIT-licensed Go chip libraries by John
Schember (go-chip-m68k, go-chip-z80, go-chip-sn76489) while the rest of
the machine was built. Those chips have since been replaced by our own
implementations in `chips/`, each differential-tested against the
library it replaced (used only as a black-box test oracle): the Z80
passed 100 seeds of 60,000 instructions in lockstep with zero
divergence, and the 68000 passed a generated-program sweep of 40 seeds
of 100,000 instructions with zero divergence outside documented
undefined-flag cases. The module now has no external dependencies.

## Layout

- `chips/` our own CPU and sound chips: `m68k/` (Motorola 68000),
  `z80/` (Zilog Z80), `psg/` (TI SN76489)
- `cart/` ROM image + header parsing
- `bus/` the 68k and Z80 address maps, work RAM, I/O ports, Z80 control
- `vdp/` the VDP video chip: registers, VRAM/CRAM/VSRAM, DMA, rendering
- `sound/` YM2612 FM + SN76489 PSG, mixed to 44.1kHz stereo
- `system/` the machine: clocks, scanline loop, interrupts, save states
- `libretro/` cgo c-shared exports of the retro_* API (the actual core .so)

## Build (desktop test core)

```
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -buildmode=c-shared \
  -o go_genesis_libretro.so ./libretro
```

## Status

Milestone 1 DONE (2026-10-12), verified against the engine test rig and
direct frame dumps with Sonic The Hedgehog:

- The game boots (SEGA logo, team card, title screen), Start enters
  Green Hill Zone Act 1 and gameplay runs: planes, sprites, scrolling,
  HUD, DMA, HBlank/VBlank interrupts, the Z80 sound driver executes.
- Save states are byte-exact: serialize, restore, re-serialize produces
  an identical image, and play after a restore is frame-for-frame
  deterministic against the unrestored run.
- Sound: the PSG path is live and unit-tested. The YM2612 FM chip
  started as a register-accurate shell; milestone 2 below replaced it
  with the full FM operator engine.
- Known cosmetic issues: the title screen's water ripple (per-line
  scroll effect) renders noisier than hardware.

Chip swap DONE (2026-10-13): the core now runs entirely on our own
chips. Verified end to end again with Sonic The Hedgehog: SEGA logo,
title screen and Green Hill Zone gameplay render correctly, the save
state round trip is byte-exact (0 bytes differ, state size unchanged
at 206,757 bytes), and play after a restore is deterministic.

Milestone 2 DONE (2026-10-13): the YM2612 FM operator engine is built
in-house (6 channels, 4 operators per channel, envelopes with SSG-EG,
feedback, LFO, channel 3 special mode, DAC channel, hardware timers)
and unit-tested, including a 440.00 Hz frequency check on a keyed
channel. Two wirings completed it: the timers advance from the system
loop at scanline precision (a polling program sees the flag mid-frame;
261 timer services land inside one frame), and register writes are
timestamped, so the sound up to each write's emulated moment renders
before the write lands. A DAC sample stream (the SEGA jingle, about
275 sample writes per frame) now plays at full rate: measured
1,200-1,400 waveform-active samples per frame in the jingle window,
where frame-end rendering managed about 2. The pan registers power on
routed to both sides, as hardware behaves (the jingle never writes
pan first). In the Sonic save test the music window produces 484,644
non-zero samples (was 33,002, PSG only), save states stay byte-exact
at the grown size of 207,149 bytes, and the engine test rig now
reports ALL TESTS PASSED.

Genesis is wired into the app (build 42). Sega CD support is
complete in this core as of SCD-4 (see the SCD-4 section below);
the app swap off Genesis Plus GX is prepared locally and ships
with a later build number assigned at ship time.

## Sega CD support (SCD-1, foundations)

What landed in this slice:

- A second 68000 sub CPU running at 12.5 MHz with its own bus view: boot window, 512 KB PRG-RAM, 256 KB Word RAM, the gate array, and PCM register and wave RAM storage.
- Word RAM 2M and 1M modes with the DMNA/RET ownership handshake between the two CPUs.
- The gate array at 0xA12000 on the main side, mirrored at 0xFF8000 for the sub CPU: reset and bus-request control, comm flags, 8 command words and 8 status words, and the H-INT interval and vector registers.
- H-INT delivered to the main CPU as a level 2 interrupt at the programmed line cadence.
- A CD block layer opening .cue/.bin and .iso images, with cue parsing, MSF/LBA conversion, and Mode 1/Mode 2 data extraction.
- A simplified CDC model: latched LBA, count and destination, DMA-style transfer into PRG-RAM, Word RAM or PCM wave RAM, or a polled data port. Its busy flag clears after two status reads. The CDD is held at a status-response model.

Boot honesty: this core contains NO Sega BIOS code. Both BIOS roles are filled by small hand-written 68k stubs in the scd package. The sub stub performs the documented boot flow: read sector 0, verify the SEGADISCSYSTEM signature, load the initial program from the header fields into PRG-RAM, and jump to it. A main-side stub program releases the sub CPU and runs the comm handshake for CD-only boots. Real Sega CD BIOS call services (the BIOS jump tables games call) were not implemented in this slice; SCD-4 implements them, see the SCD-4 section below.

Save states: cartridge-only states are byte-identical to before and still load. With a disc attached, the state grows by the sub CPU registers, the full CD RAM and register state, and the sub cycle counter: the state size in CD mode is 1,061,509 bytes (cartridge mode is 207,149 bytes). A CD state needs the CD attached to load.

Simplifications, stated plainly:

- The main CPU's own Word RAM window in cartridge space (0x200000) is not routed yet, so cartridge space is completely untouched in this slice. This also keeps SRAM cartridges safe. The ownership model is enforced and tested at the unit level.
- CDC transfers complete instantly apart from the two-read busy window.
- No wait states are charged on sub CPU memory accesses.
- PRG-RAM banking and protection, and the 1M dual-port second window, are not modeled.
- PCM registers and wave RAM are storage only: there is no PCM or CD audio yet.

Remaining slices at the end of SCD-1: SCD-2 (CD-DA and RF5C164 PCM audio, full CDD command set), SCD-3 (graphics scaler/rotator ASIC), SCD-4 (BIOS call services and app wiring so the Sega CD slot swaps off Genesis Plus GX). SCD-2 and SCD-3 have since landed; see the next sections.

## Sega CD support (SCD-2, CDD + CD-DA + PCM + banking)

What landed in this slice:

- The full CDD host interface at its documented sub CPU offsets: fader word at 0xFF8034, control byte (HOCK handshake) written at 0xFF8037, status nibbles RS0-RS9 read at 0xFF8038-0xFF8041, command nibbles TC0-TC9 written at 0xFF8042-0xFF804B. A command executes when TC9 lands and its checksum verifies (the sum of all ten nibbles is 0xF mod 16; a bad checksum is ignored). The response packet becomes visible at the next 75 Hz status tick (an exact accumulator off sub CPU cycles) and raises an interrupt. Commands: get status, stop, TOC info (absolute and relative position, current track, total length, first/last track, per-track start with the data-track flag), read/play, seek, pause, resume, fast forward/reverse (8x position rate, audio muted), open and close tray, plus error rejection of out-of-range and non-BCD targets with no state change. The documented-but-unnamed commands 0x05, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0E and 0x0F answer with a plain status packet.
- CD-DA playback: audio tracks stream from the cue/bin image through Disc.ReadAudio (raw 2352 byte sectors), position tracked in absolute samples (588 stereo frames per sector) with a sub-sector counter, play/pause/seek/stop from the CDD, track end advancing into the next audio track, stop at a data track boundary or at disc end. The fader register scales samples by FD/1024 in integer math (FD = 1024 is unity).
- The RF5C164 PCM chip in full: 8 channels programmed through the register page at 0xFF0000 (ENV gain, PAN with 4 bit left/right gains, FD phase increment, loop start, start address with write-retrigger, CTRL with chip on/off plus the MOD channel/wave-bank select, per-channel ON/OFF), wave RAM window banked in 4 KB pages at 0xFF1000. Output mixes with the documented integer math and resamples to the machine rate.
- Interrupts on the sub CPU: a delivered CDD response raises level 4 and a completed CDC transfer raises level 5, each gated by a mask bit in gate array register 0x03 (bit1 for CDD, bit2 for CDC). Per the published CDD documentation and the sub BIOS interrupt layout, CDD is level 4 and CDC is level 5.
- PRG-RAM banking and protection: the main CPU reaches PRG-RAM through a 128 KB window at 0x420000, banked by memory mode register bits 7:6, with a write protect field (bits 4:2 of the main-written register byte) protecting the first N x 64 KB of physical PRG-RAM against main window writes. The main CPU Word RAM windows are routed on the Genesis bus: 0x200000-0x23FFFF and its 2M decode at 0x600000-0x63FFFF, both enforcing the 2M/1M ownership model, all inert when no CD is attached. Bus request has its acknowledge readback at 0xA12000 bit1.
- Register coexistence: the CDD interface overlaps the SCD-1 CDC latch addresses. Writes to 0xFF8038-0xFF8041 still land in the CDC latches while reads there return CDD status nibbles; the 0xFF8037 read stays the CDC status register while its write is the CDD control byte; the 0xFF8048 read stays the CDC data port while its write is command nibble TC6.
- Save states: the SCD-2 state (CDD machine and positions, PCM channels and control, bank and protection registers, interrupt latches) fits inside the previously reserved tail bytes of the CD block, so the CD mode state size is unchanged at 1,061,509 bytes and cartridge mode is unchanged at 207,149 bytes.
