A determinism gate saves mid-playback (PCM channel plus CD-DA track running) and proves sample-identical continuation audio and byte-identical state after restore.

Measured evidence from the gates (synthetic fixtures, zero crossings unless noted): PCM sine at FD 0x0800 over a 256 byte period measured 127.00 Hz against a 127.16 Hz target; sign-magnitude decode peaks exactly at the documented mix value 15060; CD-DA sines measured 439 Hz and 879 Hz against 440 Hz and 880 Hz targets; one second of playback advanced the position exactly 44,100 samples (75 sectors); fast forward advanced at exactly 8x over the measured window; fader FD 512 versus FD 1024 peak ratio measured exactly 0.5.

Simplifications and honesty notes, stated plainly:

- Fader curve: the manual publishes the fade data as an 11 bit field with 1024 at unity; we apply it as a straight linear gain FD/1024. Hardware fades toward the target over time; we apply the target instantly, so the EFDT bit always reads complete. If the published per-step dB table is located later, the gain function changes in one place.
- PCM rate constant: the RF5C164 steps at 12.5 MHz / 384 = 32,552.08 Hz per the Ricoh documentation of the chip family and the Mega CD manual PCM chapter (not the 31,250 Hz sometimes quoted). Sample format is sign-magnitude with 0xFF as the loop marker byte, per the same sources.
- PCM mixing: ENV is a constant per-channel gain (the chip has no envelope generator, and no separate VOL register exists on it). PAN high nibble is the left gain, low nibble the right gain. The datasheet restriction on CPU wave RAM access while the chip is sounding is not modeled; CPU access is always allowed, which sample-streaming software relies on.
- Wait states: published figures for sub CPU accesses to Word RAM and PRG-RAM are not stated consistently in the material we have, so no wait states are charged; the sub CPU runs at a flat 12.5 MHz, as in SCD-1.
- Play modes: the CDD register level has no documented repeat control (TC8 is documented as unused), so there is none: track end advances to the next audio track and the disc end stops. PLAY against a data track runs the documented data read path, streaming one sector per 75 Hz tick into the CDC buffer.
- The scan rate multiple (8x), the WP field decode (bits 4:2, 64 KB boundary units), and the register 0x03 interrupt mask bits are documented model choices where the published material available to us does not pin the exact bits; each lives in exactly one place in the code.

## Sega CD support (SCD-3, graphics ASIC)

What landed in this slice:

- The rotation and scaling ASIC register file, in the scd package at its documented home: the sub CPU register page only, offsets 0x58 to 0x67 (sub addresses 0xFF8058 to 0xFF8067). Registers: stamp size and status (bit15 GRON drawing-in-progress, bit2 stamp map size SMS, bit1 stamp size STS, bit0 repeat RPT), stamp map base address, image buffer vertical cell size, image buffer start address, image buffer offset (bits 0-2 horizontal dots, bits 3-5 vertical dots), image buffer horizontal dot count (9 bits), image buffer vertical dot count, and the trace table base address. Register values are Word RAM byte addresses divided by 4 with the documented alignment masks per map geometry (256x256 dots with 16x16 or 32x32 stamps; 4096x4096 dots with 16x16 or 32x32 stamps).
- The drawing operation. The trace vectors are not registers: they live in a trace table in Word RAM, one 8 byte entry per output line holding a start X and Y in unsigned 13.3 fixed point and a delta X and Y in signed 5.11 fixed point. Writing the trace table base register starts the operation. Per line the ASIC accumulates the position at 13.11 precision (start shifted left 8, delta added per dot), looks up the stamp map entry (bits 10:0 stamp number, bit15 horizontal flip, bits 14:13 rotation in quarter turns; stamp 0 and, with repeat off, any out-of-map position fetch pixel 0), fetches the 4 bit stamp pixel from the stamp data at Word RAM offset 0 (stamp byte address = number x 128, cells stored column by column like Mega Drive sprites, even dot in the high nibble), applies the flip and rotation transform, and writes the pixel into the image buffer in Word RAM, which uses the same cell layout (line starts step 8 dots, columns jump by the column height in dots). Pixel writes follow the priority mode field (bits 4:3 of the memory mode register word; in this core's register model those bits are shared with the SCD-1 CDC destination select, so software sets the field before whichever operation it runs): mode 0 normal writes the fetched pixel always, mode 1 underwrite writes only into zero nibbles, mode 2 overwrite writes only nonzero pixels, mode 3 writes nothing. The image buffer horizontal and vertical dot counts bound the draw, and all ASIC addressing wraps at the 256 KB Word RAM boundary.
- Word RAM access rule: the render runs only while the sub CPU has Word RAM access (2M mode owned by the sub CPU, or 1M mode, where the sub CPU always holds a half). A trace started without access stays latched: GRON reads 1 and the vertical dot count still reads its programmed value; the draw runs the moment ownership is granted. The ASIC addresses the full physical 256 KB Word RAM in both modes and its writes go to the shared store regardless of which CPU owns it for CPU access. In the common case (sub CPU owns Word RAM) the draw completes synchronously inside the trace base write, so GRON reads 0 on the first poll and the vertical dot count reads 0 after the draw (hardware counts it down line by line).
- Save states: the ASIC registers and the latched-draw flag fit in the previously reserved tail bytes of the CD block (bytes 242 to 254), so the CD mode state size is unchanged at 1,061,509 bytes, cartridge mode is unchanged at 207,149 bytes, and SCD-1 and SCD-2 states load with the ASIC at power-on state. A state gate round-trips a latched (deferred) draw and proves it completes byte-identically after restore.

Gates, all exact byte comparisons against hand-derived expectations: identity trace (buffer bytes equal the stamp bytes), 90 degree rotation trace (dot delta (0, +1), per-line starts stepping (-1, 0)), 2x scale down (delta 2.0), 2x upscale (delta 0.5, each stamp pixel becomes a 2x2 block), stamp entry flip and all four rotation field values, repeat on (wraps at the 256 dot map edge) and repeat off (out-of-map dots fetch 0 and, in overwrite mode, leave the sentinel), all four priority modes including transparent zeros leaving a pre-filled sentinel in overwrite mode while zeros overwrite in normal mode, 32x32 stamp mode including the stamp number masking (entry 7 draws stamp 4), the 4096 dot map geometry, the image buffer offset register, the deferred draw lifecycle, 1M mode rendering, and a system level gate: a hand-assembled sub CPU program on a synthetic disc builds the scene, programs the ASIC, traces it, checksums the buffer (0x1FC0) into the comm registers for the main CPU stub to answer, and a save taken after the trace restores and continues byte-identically.

Published documentation versus the slice brief (the documents won, as in SCD-2):

- Register location: the brief put the ASIC at main side 0xA12010 to 0xA1202F. That window is the communication register area (already implemented in SCD-1). The published register documentation puts the ASIC in the sub CPU page only, at 0xFF8058 to 0xFF8067, with no main CPU access. Implemented per the documents.
- Trace vectors: the brief described separate trace start and delta registers. Only the trace table base is a register; the start and delta vectors are per-line entries in Word RAM in the formats above. The brief's line delta maps to how consecutive entries' starts progress.
- Transparency: the brief said pixel value 0 is always skipped. The documented rule is the priority mode field above; only overwrite mode skips zeros, and normal mode writes them. All four modes are implemented.
- Stamp map entry: the brief described horizontal and vertical flip bits plus priority bits. The documented entry has one flip bit (horizontal) and a two bit rotation field; there is no vertical flip bit (vertical flip is the horizontal flip plus the 180 degree rotation) and no priority bit in the entry. Bits 12:11 are unused.
- Map sizes: the brief's size field description (1x1 up to 16x16 cells) does not match the documented geometry; the two map sizes and two stamp sizes above are what the documents describe.
- 1M mode: the brief said a buffer address bit selects the Word RAM half for the ASIC. No source we found documents an ASIC bank selection; the documented rule is the sub CPU access requirement, and this implementation addresses the full physical array in both modes.

Simplifications, stated plainly:

- Synchronous draw: no cycle timing is charged for rendering, and the hardware level 1 completion interrupt is not generated (this core's SCD-1 register model has no level 1 interrupt mask register). GRON reads 1 only while a draw is latched waiting for Word RAM access.
- Byte write trigger: the operation starts on the write that completes the trace base value (its low byte). A 68k word write therefore starts exactly one operation with the full value, as on hardware.
- The ASIC font conversion registers at sub offsets 0x4C to 0x57 are a separate hardware function and are not implemented in this slice; those offsets keep their SCD-1 behavior.

SCD-4 has since landed; see the next section.

## Sega CD support (SCD-4, BIOS call services, enginetest, shell, app prep): Sega CD COMPLETE

With this slice the Genesis core covers Genesis and Sega CD entirely in-house: every chip, the CD block, the sub BIOS call services, and the backup RAM are our own code written from published documentation. The core contains no Sega BIOS bytes anywhere; the BIOS roles are our synthesized stub plus Go service implementations, exactly as in SCD-1 through SCD-3.

What landed in this slice:

- The stub BIOS grows to a 0x6000 byte image at the published CD system program offsets: exception vectors (autovectors 25 to 31 point at the jump table level entries, other exceptions at a fatal stub that sets sub flag 0xEE), our own ID string at $0100, the SCD-1 boot code at $0200 unchanged in behavior, handler stubs and three family trampolines, and the jump table at $5EE0. Jump table layout (6 byte JMP entries): $5EE0 to $5F04 are _level1 through _level7 (RTE stubs), $5F0A _usercall0, $5F10 _usercall1, $5F16 _buram, $5F1C _usercall2, $5F22 _cdbios, $5F28 _cdboot, $5F2E _usercall3. The _buram ($5F16) and _cdbios ($5F22) addresses match the real firmware's table layout. The table region $5EE0 to $5F3F is RAM backed per unit and initialized from the image, so software can patch the level and usercall entries as the manual describes; the patched bytes are part of the save state.
- Call mechanics: the service implementations live in Go (scd/bios.go). A family entry point is a thin hand-assembled trampoline that saves D0-D7/A0-A6 into a mailbox in PRG-RAM at $025A00 with MOVEM, records the family and the function number (in D0.w per the manual), sets a request byte, and spins. The system services one request per scanline (Unit.BIOSService, called from runSubLine), writes the result registers D0/D1/A0/A1 and the caller's CCR back through the mailbox, and the trampoline restores them (MOVEM does not touch flags, then a MOVE to CCR) and returns. Parameter tables and buffers are read and written through the sub CPU bus, so they work in PRG-RAM or Word RAM.
- Boot handover for the disc's main CPU program: the sub boot stub now also copies sector 0 into Word RAM offset 0 (the documented home of the boot sector, whose user bytes from offset 0x200 are the main CPU program). After the comm handshake, MainStubROM jumps to Word RAM $200208 when the 8 byte marker "ITAKMAIN" sits at $200200; discs without the marker keep the previous idle behavior byte for byte. The marker is our synthesized stub's convention: a real BIOS jumps unconditionally, and the guard keeps every earlier flow identical.
- BIOS coverage. _cdbios ($5F22), synchronous calls: CDBCHK $80, CDBSTAT $81 (writes the 32 byte status table at PRG-RAM $025E80 and returns it in A0), CDBTOCWRITE $82, CDBTOCREAD $83, CDBPAUSE $84, FDRSET $85, FDRCHG $86, CDCSTART $87, CDCSTARTP $88 (same as CDCSTART), CDCSTOP $89, CDCSTAT $8A, CDCREAD $8B, CDCTRN $8C (2048 user bytes plus a zeroed EDC/ECC region, pointers advance per the manual), CDCACK $8D, LEDSET $95, CDCSETMODE $96. Asynchronous calls (queued one deep, execute after one 75 Hz tick, CDBCHK reports busy meanwhile): DRVOPEN $00, MSCSTOP $0A, DRVINIT $10 (with autoplay when the start track byte has bit 7 set), MSCPLAY $11, MSCPLAY1 $12, MSCPLAYR $13, MSCPLAYT $14, MSCSEEK $15, MSCSEEK1 $16, ROMREAD $17, ROMSEEK $18, MSCSEEKT $19, ROMREADN $20 (plus its $21 shared tail), ROMREADE $22. Async slots $01 (stop), $02 (resume), $04 (pause), $06 (fast reverse), $07 (fast forward) are implemented by their firmware-observed behavior; the other $01 to $0C slots are success no-ops. Stubbed by design: SCDINIT $8E, SCDSTART $8F, SCDSTOP $90 are success no-ops and SCDSTAT $91 returns zeros (subcode is not decoded); SCDREAD $92, SCDPQ $93, SCDPQL $94, WONDERREQ $97, WONDERCHK $98 fail with carry set; slots $0D-$0F, $1A-$1F, $23-$2B are rejected like the real firmware's reject stub; any other number fails with carry set and D0 = 0.
- _buram ($5F16): BRMINIT 0, BRMSTAT 1, BRMSERCH 2, BRMREAD 3, BRMWRITE 4, BRMDEL 5, BRMFORMAT 6, BRMDIR 7, BRMVERIFY 8, all implemented over an internal 8 KB backup RAM store. BRMFORMAT writes the documented volume footer exactly (the SEGA_CD_ROM signature block, the file and free counts written four times each, RAM_CARTRIDGE___ at the end); an empty formatted volume reports 125 free blocks of $40 bytes. BRAM contents are part of the CD save state. _cdboot ($5F28): CBTINIT 0, CBTINT 1, CBTOPENDISC 2, CBTOPENSTAT 3, CBTCHKDISC 4, CBTCHKSTAT 5, all implemented (disc type codes: $FFFF not ready, 1 audio only, 2 data without boot signature, 5 bootable game disc).
- Save states grow this time, by design: the unit appends the 8,192 byte BRAM and a 768 byte BIOS state block (queue, fader, read state, TOC override, jump table overlay), taking the unit from 854,272 to 863,232 bytes and the CD mode machine state from 1,061,509 to 1,070,469 bytes. Pre-SCD-4 CD states keep loading: the unit accepts the legacy length with BRAM unformatted and BIOS state at defaults, and the system expands a legacy length CD buffer by inserting the zero sections at the end of the unit block (the state format carries no mode flag byte; the disc attachment plus the exact legacy length identifies a legacy CD state). Cartridge states are unchanged at 207,149 bytes.
- The libretro shell loads discs: the extension list is now bin|gen|md|smd|cue|iso. Routing: a .cue or .iso path goes to LoadDisc by path; content that sniffs as a disc image (SEGADISCSYSTEM at offset 0, or at offset 16 behind the raw sector sync pattern) goes to LoadDisc by path when a path exists, else through a temp file that unload removes; anything else loads as a cartridge exactly as before. The shell outputs the machine AudioBuffer, which since SCD-2 mixes Genesis, CD-DA, and PCM. A CD mode state round-trips through the shell (proven by the harness below).
- App swap preparation, done locally and not yet published: the backend registry (go_backend/internal/core/types.go) binds the Sega CD slot to Go Genesis / libgo_genesis.so with extensions .cue/.iso/.bin, and flutter_ui/lib/main.dart gained a Sega CD entry (id segacd, dir SegaCD, core libgo_genesis.so). The Kotlin activities and tools/autobuild-server.sh never named a core for Sega CD (the name flows from Dart), so they needed no edit. Publishing still needs the libgenesis_plus_gx.so asset deleted on the server, a build number assigned by the parent, and a TV playtest; the pubspec is untouched by this slice. Note: the 32 bit build still bundles mGBA and PCSX ReARMed until the GBA and PS1 swaps ship; Genesis Plus GX is retired from every slot this core covers.

Full-stack enginetest (synthetic cue/bin, the IP written against the BIOS calls):

- TestCDBIOSFullStack (companion cartridge plus disc): the IP finishes in 4 frames with the stage bitmap 0x7F, all seven stages passing: DRVINIT plus CDBTOCREAD track checks, MSCPLAY of track 2 plus CDBSTAT table checks, a PCM tone started through raw registers, ROMREADN with the CDCREAD/CDCTRN/CDCACK family pulling the payload sector (checksum matches, the first bytes spell ITAKBIOS), the BRAM round trip (format, BRMSTAT 125 free, write, 123 free, search, read back byte equal, delete), and an ASIC trace into Word RAM that the main side copies to VRAM. Comm command 1 (main side VRAM readback checksum) is 0xD000, the ASIC buffer checksum inside the trace stage is 0x1FC0, and the framebuffer shows 14,848 non-background pixels. Tone power over the run's last frames (2,943 left samples, Goertzel): CD-DA 440 Hz = 3.80e12, PCM 508.6 Hz = 2.65e14, 1500 Hz control = 3.24e9. A save taken mid-run replays 45 frames byte-identically, including 66,236 compared audio samples, and a legacy 1,061,509 byte state is accepted and keeps running.
- TestCDBIOSDiscOnlyBoot: the same disc with no cartridge (the synthesized MainStubROM path): bitmap 0x7F, checksum 0xD000, 14,848 non-background pixels, frame byte identical 30 frames later.
- The shared harness (go_backend/cmd/enginetest) against the same cue through the built desktop core reports RESULT: ALL TESTS PASSED: video 256x224 non-blank inside the first 120 frames, audio produced 88,313 samples with 91,576 non-silent drained samples, save state 1,070,469 bytes, and the frame hash after restoring the save matches the save point hash exactly (dbb4303c28c2daf2).

Published documentation versus the slice brief (the documents and the code won, as in SCD-2 and SCD-3):

- The brief's CDBTOC is the manual's CDBTOCREAD ($83); CDBTOCWRITE ($82) is its write twin. Both are implemented.
- The brief's CDBPAUSE/CDBRESUME pair does not exist. CDBPAUSE ($84) sets the standby pause time; pause and resume live in the async music and data groups (MSCPAUSEON/OFF, ROMPAUSEON/OFF), mapped by behavior in the async slots above.
- The _buram and _cdboot function numbers follow the manual's own section listing order starting at 0, because the numeric equates in Sega's cabios.i include file were not obtainable from published sources. The _cdbios numbers are cross-verified against the real firmware's dispatch table. The choice is flagged in code comments.
- BRAM directory entries: the manual publishes the volume footer layout and every call contract, but the on-disk directory entry layout is BIOS internal (on hardware the stored names are encoded, not plain). Our 16 byte entries (plain name, flag byte, start block, unit count) are a documented synthesis; the footer is the documented layout, and the 125 free block figure for an empty 8 KB volume matches a hardware-verified description.
- CDCACK: when a bounded read's last sector is acknowledged, the BIOS read state closes but the CDD is not force stopped; the drive finishes its current command at track end (the SCD-2 streaming model). CDCSTOP stops the drive immediately.
- BRM parameter handling accepts both the manual's A0 table layout (name, flag byte, block size word) and a register-carried variant (flag in D1, blocks in D2); BRMWRITE and BRMREAD advance the A1 result by the byte count, following this core's CDCTRN pointer convention. BRMSTAT writes its 12 byte display string through (A1) when a buffer is passed, per the manual; callers must not alias it with live data.

Remaining gaps, consolidated for the whole Sega CD:

- The ASIC font conversion registers at sub offsets $FF804C to $FF8057 keep their SCD-1 passthrough behavior and are not implemented.
- The ASIC level 1 completion interrupt is not generated; draws complete synchronously (or latch until Word RAM is available), as documented in SCD-3.
- Sub CPU wait states are not charged; the sub CPU runs at a flat 12.5 MHz, as in SCD-1.
- The PRG-RAM write protect field decode (bits 4:2 of the main-written register byte, first N x 64 KB protected) is the SCD-2 model choice; the published material available to us does not pin the exact field.
- Fader model: at the CDD register level the fader target still applies instantly and the EFDT bit always reads complete (SCD-2 note); the BIOS layer adds FDRCHG ramping in 75 Hz steps. DRVINIT's roughly 2 second hardware pause is shortened to one 75 Hz tick, and the async queue is one deep (a second async call while one is queued is dropped).
- Subcode is not decoded, so the SCD call family reports no data. MSCPLAY1 and MSCPLAYR collapse to MSCPLAY at the CDD level, and CDCSTARTP is identical to CDCSTART. CDCTRN fills the EDC/ECC region with zeros. BRAM is not mapped on the sub CPU bus; BRMSERCH's returned pointer ($600000 plus the file offset) is informational, and BRMREAD is the access path. A handful of _cdbios async slots ($01 to $0C) are implemented by observed behavior because their manual names are not confirmed, and the exact names of jump table entries 0 to 8 beyond the level and usercall structure follow the manual's layout without firmware confirmation.


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/bus/bus.go ====================

// Package bus wires the Genesis address maps for both CPUs.
//
// 68k map (24-bit):
//
//	0x000000-0x3FFFFF cartridge ROM (bank SRAM window at 0x200000+ when the
//	                  cart has SRAM and ROM is switched out via 0xA130F1)
//	                  With a Sega CD attached (AttachCD), three CD windows
//	                  decode inside and above this space instead: main CPU
//	                  Word RAM at 0x200000-0x23FFFF, the banked PRG-RAM
//	                  window at 0x420000-0x43FFFF, and the 2M Word RAM
//	                  window at 0x600000-0x63FFFF
//	0xA00000-0xA07FFF Z80 address space window
//	0xA04000-0xA04003 YM2612
//	0xA06000          bank register mirror (Z80 view handles the real one)
//	0xA10000-0xA1001F I/O: version, controller data/control, serial
//	0xA12000-0xA120FF Sega CD gate array, only when a unit is attached via AttachCD
//	0xA11100          Z80 bus request (0x0100 = grant/hold, 0x0000 = release)
//	0xA11200          Z80 reset (0x0000 = assert, 0x0100 = release)
//	0xA130F1          SRAM enable / ROM bank switch
//	0xA14000-0xA14003 TMSS register (accepted, ignored)
//	0xC00000-0xDFFFFF VDP ports (mirrored every 0x20) + PSG at 0xC00011
//	0xE00000-0xFFFFFF 64KB work RAM (mirrored)
//
// Z80 map (64KB):
//
//	0x0000-0x1FFF its own 8KB RAM
//	0x4000-0x4003 YM2612
//	0x6000        bank register (9 bits shifted in, selects the 32KB window)
//	0x7F11        PSG
//	0x8000-0xFFFF window into 68k space through the bank register
//
// Pad button bits for SetPad (internal layout, libretro translates):
//
//	Up=1<<0 Down=1<<1 Left=1<<2 Right=1<<3 B=1<<4 C=1<<5 A=1<<6 Start=1<<7 Mode=1<<8
//
// PINNED API (system and libretro are written against this):
//
//	New(c *cart.Cart, v *vdp.VDP, s *sound.Sound) *Bus
//	m68k.Bus: Read8/16/32, Write8/16/32, Reset()
//	z80.Bus: Fetch, Read, Write, In, Out
//	SetPad(player int, mask uint16)
//	Z80Halted() bool     bus requested or reset asserted
//	TakeZ80Reset() bool  true once after reset is released (system resets the Z80)
//	AttachCD(u *scd.Unit) / CDAttached() bool  Sega CD gate array window
//	SerializeSize() int / Serialize / Deserialize (RAM, Z80 RAM, SRAM, IO state)
//
// SetYMClock(fn func(fromZ80 bool) int64) was added after the
// original pin: the system installs an emulated-time source (YM2612
// master clocks since power-on) that timestamps YM2612 writes, so
// the sound section can render the pending FM span before each
// write lands (see writeYM). Without one, writes behave exactly
// as before.
package bus

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/scd"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/sound"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/vdp"
)

// Pad button bits.
const (
	PadUp    = 1 << 0
	PadDown  = 1 << 1
	PadLeft  = 1 << 2
	PadRight = 1 << 3
	PadB     = 1 << 4
	PadC     = 1 << 5
	PadA     = 1 << 6
	PadStart = 1 << 7
	PadMode  = 1 << 8
)

// Bus is the shared address space both CPUs see.
type Bus struct {
	cart  *cart.Cart
	vdp   *vdp.VDP
	sound *sound.Sound
	cd    *scd.Unit

	RAM  [0x10000]uint8 // 68k work RAM
	ZRAM [0x2000]uint8  // Z80 RAM
	SRAM []uint8        // cartridge save RAM (sized from the cart header)

	pads          [2]uint16                // current button state per player (Pad* bits)
	ioData        [3]uint8                 // last values written to the data ports
	ioCtrl        [3]uint8                 // control (direction/TH select) per port
	z80Req        bool                     // 68k holds the Z80 bus (Z80 halted)
	z80Rst        bool                     // Z80 reset asserted
	z80RstPending bool                     // reset was released; system should reset the Z80
	bank          uint32                   // Z80 window bank (9 bits, in 32KB units >> 15)
	sramOn        bool                     // SRAM mapped at 0x200000 instead of ROM
	ymClockFn     func(fromZ80 bool) int64 // emulated time for YM writes, nil = untimestamped
}

// New builds the bus around a cartridge, VDP and sound chip set.
func New(c *cart.Cart, v *vdp.VDP, s *sound.Sound) *Bus {
	b := &Bus{cart: c, vdp: v, sound: s, z80Rst: true, z80RstPending: true}
	if c != nil && c.SRAM {
		n := c.SRAMEnd - c.SRAMStart + 1
		if n == 0 || n > 0x100000 {
			n = 0x10000
		}
		b.SRAM = make([]uint8, n)
		for i := range b.SRAM {
			b.SRAM[i] = 0xFF
		}
	}
	v.SetDMASource(func(addr uint32) uint16 { return b.Read16(addr) })
	return b
}

// AttachCD attaches a Sega CD unit so its gate array answers at
// 0xA12000-0xA120FF on the 68k map.
func (b *Bus) AttachCD(u *scd.Unit) { b.cd = u }

// CDAttached reports whether a Sega CD unit is attached.
func (b *Bus) CDAttached() bool { return b.cd != nil }

// SetPad records the button state for a player (0 or 1).
func (b *Bus) SetPad(player int, mask uint16) {
	if player >= 0 && player < 2 {
		b.pads[player] = mask
	}
}

// SetYMClock installs the emulated-time source used to timestamp
// YM2612 writes: fn reports the current time in YM2612 master
// clocks since power-on for a write coming from the 68000
// (fromZ80 false) or from the Z80 (fromZ80 true). The bus is a
// wiring layer and owns no clock of its own; the system, which
// owns both CPUs, supplies the source. Passing nil (or never
// calling this) leaves writes untimestamped.
func (b *Bus) SetYMClock(fn func(fromZ80 bool) int64) { b.ymClockFn = fn }

// writeYM passes one YM2612 port write to the sound section. When
// a clock source is installed, the FM stream is first rendered up
// to the write's emulated moment, so the register change takes
// effect at its true position inside the frame: a DAC stream
// writing data hundreds of times per frame is rendered as a
// stream, not as its last byte held to frame end.
func (b *Bus) writeYM(addr uint32, val uint8, fromZ80 bool) {
	if b.ymClockFn != nil {
		b.sound.RenderYMTo(b.ymClockFn(fromZ80))
	}
	b.sound.WriteYM(addr, val)
}

// Z80Halted reports whether the Z80 must not run (bus requested by the
// 68k, or reset asserted).
func (b *Bus) Z80Halted() bool { return b.z80Req || b.z80Rst }

// TakeZ80Reset reports true once each time the Z80 leaves reset, so the
// system can reset the CPU at the right moment.
func (b *Bus) TakeZ80Reset() bool {
	if b.z80RstPending && !b.z80Rst {
		b.z80RstPending = false
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// Reset satisfies the m68k Bus interface (bus reset hook; state is owned
// by New and the serialize path, so this is intentionally light).
func (b *Bus) Reset() {}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cartridge window (shared by the 68k map and the Z80 window helper)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// readROMByte resolves a byte in the cartridge window, honoring the SRAM
// overlay. SRAM is a byte-wide device decoded on odd addresses only: odd
// addresses reach the SRAM array (byte index = offset/2), even addresses
// read back open bus.
func (b *Bus) readROMByte(addr uint32) uint8 {
	if b.sramOn && b.cart != nil && b.cart.SRAM &&
		addr >= b.cart.SRAMStart && addr <= b.cart.SRAMEnd {
		if addr&1 == 0 {
			return 0xFF
		}
		if i := (addr - b.cart.SRAMStart) >> 1; int(i) < len(b.SRAM) {
			return b.SRAM[i]
		}
		return 0xFF
	}
	if b.cart == nil {
		return 0xFF
	}
	return b.cart.ReadROM(addr)
}

// readROMWord reads a big-endian word from the cartridge window.
// When the word touches the SRAM overlay it composes from byte
// reads so each byte follows the overlay rules exactly; otherwise
// it reads the ROM image directly in one access.
func (b *Bus) readROMWord(addr uint32) uint16 {
	if b.sramOn && b.cart != nil && b.cart.SRAM &&
		addr <= b.cart.SRAMEnd && addr+1 >= b.cart.SRAMStart {
		return uint16(b.readROMByte(addr))<<8 | uint16(b.readROMByte(addr+1))
	}
	if b.cart == nil {
		return 0xFFFF
	}
	return b.cart.ReadROM16(addr)
}

// writeROMByte stores into the SRAM overlay when it is switched in; plain
// ROM writes are ignored.
func (b *Bus) writeROMByte(addr uint32, val uint8) {
	if b.sramOn && b.cart != nil && b.cart.SRAM &&
		addr >= b.cart.SRAMStart && addr <= b.cart.SRAMEnd {
		if addr&1 == 0 {
			return
		}
		if i := (addr - b.cart.SRAMStart) >> 1; int(i) < len(b.SRAM) {
			b.SRAM[i] = val
		}
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 68k address space
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Read8 reads one byte from the 68k address space.
func (b *Bus) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	addr &= 0xFFFFFF
	// Fast paths for the two regions that dominate execution,
	// cartridge ROM and work RAM, reached only when no Sega CD
	// window decode can claim the address first (the CD windows
	// inside the cartridge range sit at 0x200000-0x23FFFF).
	if addr >= 0xE00000 {
		return b.RAM[addr&0xFFFF]
	}
	if addr < 0x400000 && (b.cd == nil || addr < 0x200000 || addr >= 0x240000) {
		return b.readROMByte(addr)
	}
	switch {
	case b.cd != nil && addr >= 0x200000 && addr < 0x240000:
		// Sega CD main CPU Word RAM window (1M halves / 2M owner view).
		return b.cd.MainWordRead8(addr)
	case b.cd != nil && addr >= 0x420000 && addr < 0x440000:
		// Sega CD PRG-RAM bank window (128 KB, bank from the gate
		// array memory mode register).
		return b.cd.MainPRGRead8(addr)
	case b.cd != nil && addr >= 0x600000 && addr < 0x640000:
		// Sega CD 2M Word RAM window: the same main view as the
		// 0x200000 window, decoded at its documented 2M address.
		return b.cd.MainWordRead8(addr - 0x400000)
	case addr < 0x400000:
		return b.readROMByte(addr)
	case addr >= 0xE00000:
		return b.RAM[addr&0xFFFF]
	case addr >= 0xC00000: // VDP window 0xC00000-0xDFFFFF
		w := b.vdp.ReadPort((addr & 0x1F) &^ 1)
		if addr&1 == 1 {
			return uint8(w)
		}
		return uint8(w >> 8)
	case addr >= 0xA04000 && addr <= 0xA04003: // YM2612
		if addr == 0xA04000 {
			return b.sound.ReadYM()
		}
		return 0
	case addr >= 0xA10000 && addr <= 0xA1001F:
		return b.readIO8(addr)
	case addr == 0xA11100: // Z80 bus request status, high byte: reads 1
		// while the Z80 still owns the bus, 0 once the bus is granted to
		// the 68000. Games poll this bit waiting for it to clear (the
		// stock Sega startup code and Sonic's sound driver loader do).
		if b.Z80Halted() {
			return 0x00
		}
		return 0x01
	case addr == 0xA11101: // Z80 bus request status, low byte
		return 0x00
	case addr == 0xA11200 || addr == 0xA11201: // Z80 reset
		return 0
	case addr >= 0xA14000 && addr <= 0xA14003: // TMSS
		return 0
	case addr >= 0xA12000 && addr <= 0xA120FF:
		if b.cd != nil {
			return b.cd.MainRead8(addr - 0xA12000)
		}
		return 0xFF
	case addr >= 0xA00000: // Z80 window 0xA00000-0xA0FFFF (mirrored decode)
		if a := addr & 0x7FFF; a < 0x2000 {
			return b.ZRAM[a]
		}
		return 0xFF
	}
	return 0xFF
}

// Read16 reads a big-endian word. Device regions with their own word
// semantics (VDP ports, Z80 control, TMSS) are handled directly; the
// cartridge and RAM windows have direct word reads below; all other
// regions compose from byte reads.
func (b *Bus) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	addr &= 0xFFFFFF
	switch {
	case addr >= 0xC00000 && addr < 0xE00000:
		return b.vdp.ReadPort(addr & 0x1F)
	case addr == 0xA11100: // status word: 0x0100 while the Z80 owns the
		// bus, 0x0000 once granted (see the byte read above)
		if b.Z80Halted() {
			return 0x0000
		}
		return 0x0100
	case addr == 0xA11200:
		return 0
	case addr >= 0xA14000 && addr <= 0xA14003:
		return 0
	case addr < 0x3FFFFF && (b.cd == nil || addr < 0x1FFFFF || addr >= 0x240000):
		// Cartridge window, the whole word inside it and clear
		// of the Sega CD Word RAM window (see Read8).
		return b.readROMWord(addr)
	case addr >= 0xE00000 && addr < 0xFFFFFF:
		return uint16(b.RAM[addr&0xFFFF])<<8 | uint16(b.RAM[(addr+1)&0xFFFF])
	}
	return uint16(b.Read8(addr))<<8 | uint16(b.Read8(addr+1))
}

// Read32 reads a big-endian long as two word accesses (which is also how
// a 32-bit VDP access must be decomposed).
func (b *Bus) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(b.Read16(addr))<<16 | uint32(b.Read16(addr+2))
}

// Write8 writes one byte into the 68k address space.
func (b *Bus) Write8(addr uint32, val uint8) {
	addr &= 0xFFFFFF
	if addr >= 0xE00000 {
		// Work RAM mirror range; no device decode reaches here.
		b.RAM[addr&0xFFFF] = val
		return
	}
	switch {
	case b.cd != nil && addr >= 0x200000 && addr < 0x240000:
		b.cd.MainWordWrite8(addr, val)
	case b.cd != nil && addr >= 0x420000 && addr < 0x440000:
		// PRG-RAM bank window; the unit enforces write protection.
		b.cd.MainPRGWrite8(addr, val)
	case b.cd != nil && addr >= 0x600000 && addr < 0x640000:
		b.cd.MainWordWrite8(addr-0x400000, val)
	case addr < 0x400000:
		b.writeROMByte(addr, val)
	case addr >= 0xE00000:
		b.RAM[addr&0xFFFF] = val
	case addr >= 0xC00000: // VDP window 0xC00000-0xDFFFFF
		off := addr & 0x1F
		switch {
		case off == 0x11: // PSG byte lane (0xC00011)
			b.sound.WritePSG(val)
		case off == 0x10: // PSG port high lane: writes are ignored
		case addr&1 == 0:
			b.vdp.WritePort(off, uint16(val)<<8)
		default:
			b.vdp.WritePort(off, uint16(val))
		}
	case addr >= 0xA04000 && addr <= 0xA04003: // YM2612
		b.writeYM(addr&3, val, false)
	case addr >= 0xA130F0 && addr <= 0xA130FF: // SRAM / ROM switch
		b.sramOn = val&1 == 1
	case addr == 0xA11100: // Z80 bus request: bit 0 of the byte is the grant bit
		b.z80Req = val&1 == 1
	case addr == 0xA11200: // Z80 reset
		b.writeZ80Reset(val&1 == 1)
	case addr >= 0xA10000 && addr <= 0xA1001F:
		b.writeIO8(addr, val)
	case addr >= 0xA12000 && addr <= 0xA120FF:
		if b.cd != nil {
			b.cd.MainWrite8(addr-0xA12000, val)
		}
	case addr >= 0xA00000: // Z80 window 0xA00000-0xA0FFFF (mirrored decode)
		if a := addr & 0x7FFF; a < 0x2000 {
			b.ZRAM[a] = val
		}
	}
	// Everything else (TMSS, unmapped): writes are ignored.
}

// writeZ80Reset applies the Z80 reset line level: released=false asserts
// reset; releasing it after an assert arms the one-shot TakeZ80Reset.
func (b *Bus) writeZ80Reset(released bool) {
	if !released {
		b.z80Rst = true
		return
	}
	if b.z80Rst {
		b.z80RstPending = true
	}
	b.z80Rst = false
}

// Write16 writes a big-endian word. The VDP takes word accesses directly;
// every other region decomposes into byte writes, which matches hardware
// bus behavior for the byte-wide devices behind them (YM2612 latches,
// IO ports, the Z80 control registers whose grant bit lives in the high
// byte, and the SRAM switch whose low byte lands last).
func (b *Bus) Write16(addr uint32, val uint16) {
	addr &= 0xFFFFFF
	if addr >= 0xC00000 && addr < 0xE00000 {
		b.vdp.WritePort(addr&0x1F, val)
		return
	}
	if addr >= 0xE00000 && addr < 0xFFFFFF {
		// Work RAM word: the same two byte stores Write8 would
		// make, without the region decode twice.
		b.RAM[addr&0xFFFF] = uint8(val >> 8)
		b.RAM[(addr+1)&0xFFFF] = uint8(val)
		return
	}
	b.Write8(addr, uint8(val>>8))
	b.Write8(addr+1, uint8(val))
}

// Write32 writes a big-endian long as two word accesses.
func (b *Bus) Write32(addr uint32, val uint32) {
	b.Write16(addr, uint16(val>>16))
	b.Write16(addr+2, uint16(val))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 68k I/O ports (0xA10000-0xA1001F)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func (b *Bus) readIO8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	switch addr {
	case 0xA10000: // version register: overseas (export), NTSC, no TMSS
		return 0x80
	case 0xA10003, 0xA10005: // controller data ports 1 and 2
		return b.padValue(int((addr - 0xA10003) / 2))
	case 0xA10007: // expansion port: nothing attached
		return 0xFF
	case 0xA10009, 0xA1000B, 0xA1000D: // control ports
		return b.ioCtrl[(addr-0xA10009)/2]
	}
	return 0xFF
}

func (b *Bus) writeIO8(addr uint32, val uint8) {
	switch addr {
	case 0xA10003, 0xA10005, 0xA10007:
		b.ioData[(addr-0xA10003)/2] = val
	case 0xA10009, 0xA1000B, 0xA1000D:
		b.ioCtrl[(addr-0xA10009)/2] = val
	}
}

// padValue builds the active-low controller byte for one port. TH selects
// which button group is multiplexed onto the direction pins: when the
// control register marks TH as an output, TH is whatever the game wrote
// to data bit 6; when TH is an input it floats high on a standard pad.
func (b *Bus) padValue(p int) uint8 {
	th := uint8(1)
	if b.ioCtrl[p]&0x40 != 0 {
		th = (b.ioData[p] >> 6) & 1
	}
	m := b.pads[p]
	inv := func(bit uint16) uint8 {
		if m&bit == 0 {
			return 1
		}
		return 0
	}
	if th == 1 {
		// ?1CBRLDU: C,B on the button pins, full direction pad.
		return 0x80 | 0x40 |
			inv(PadC)<<5 | inv(PadB)<<4 |
			inv(PadRight)<<3 | inv(PadLeft)<<2 |
			inv(PadDown)<<1 | inv(PadUp)
	}
	// ?0SA00DU: Start,A on the button pins; the Left/Right pins read 0
	// on a 3-button pad in this phase.
	return 0x80 |
		inv(PadStart)<<5 | inv(PadA)<<4 |
		inv(PadDown)<<1 | inv(PadUp)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Z80 address space
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Fetch reads an opcode byte (M1 cycle); identical to Read here.
func (b *Bus) Fetch(addr uint16) uint8 { return b.Read(addr) }

// Read reads one byte from the Z80 address space.
func (b *Bus) Read(addr uint16) uint8 {
	switch {
	case addr < 0x2000:
		return b.ZRAM[addr]
	case addr >= 0x4000 && addr <= 0x4003: // YM2612
		if addr == 0x4000 {
			return b.sound.ReadYM()
		}
		return 0xFF
	case addr >= 0x6000 && addr < 0x8000: // bank register / PSG window: reads float
		return 0xFF
	case addr >= 0x8000: // 32KB window into 68k space
		return b.read68kByte((b.bank << 15) | uint32(addr&0x7FFF))
	}
	return 0xFF
}

// Write writes one byte into the Z80 address space.
func (b *Bus) Write(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	switch {
	case addr < 0x2000:
		b.ZRAM[addr] = val
	case addr >= 0x4000 && addr <= 0x4003: // YM2612
		b.writeYM(uint32(addr&3), val, true)
	case addr == 0x6000: // bank register: shift one bit in, LSB first
		b.bank = (b.bank >> 1) | (uint32(val&1) << 8)
		b.bank &= 0x1FF
	case addr == 0x7F11: // PSG
		b.sound.WritePSG(val)
	}
}

// In reads an I/O port; the Genesis Z80 has no port devices attached.
func (b *Bus) In(port uint16) uint8 { return 0xFF }

// Out writes an I/O port; ignored.
func (b *Bus) Out(port uint16, val uint8) {}

// read68kByte is the Z80 window's view into 68k space. Only the memory
// regions are reachable this way (cartridge window with the SRAM overlay,
// work RAM); device regions read as open bus so the sound CPU can never
// trigger VDP or IO side effects through the window.
func (b *Bus) read68kByte(a uint32) uint8 {
	a &= 0xFFFFFF
	switch {
	case a < 0x400000:
		return b.readROMByte(a)
	case a >= 0xE00000:
		return b.RAM[a&0xFFFF]
	}
	return 0xFF
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Save states
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// sramStateSize is the fixed width of the SRAM field inside a serialized
// state. Carts with more SRAM than this (rare) keep only their first
// 64KB in save states; carts with less are zero padded.
const sramStateSize = 0x10000

// SerializeSize returns the exact serialized state size in bytes:
// work RAM (64KB) + Z80 RAM (8KB) + SRAM length prefix (4) + SRAM field
// (64KB) + trailing bus register block (16).
func (b *Bus) SerializeSize() int {
	return 0x10000 + 0x2000 + 4 + sramStateSize + 16
}

// Serialize writes the bus-owned state (RAM, Z80 RAM, SRAM, IO and Z80
// control state) into buf, which must be at least SerializeSize() bytes.
func (b *Bus) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < b.SerializeSize() {
		return errors.New("bus: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	off := 0
	copy(buf[off:off+0x10000], b.RAM[:])
	off += 0x10000
	copy(buf[off:off+0x2000], b.ZRAM[:])
	off += 0x2000
	n := len(b.SRAM)
	if n > sramStateSize {
		n = sramStateSize
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off:off+4], uint32(n))
	off += 4
	field := buf[off : off+sramStateSize]
	for i := range field {
		field[i] = 0
	}
	copy(field, b.SRAM[:n])
	off += sramStateSize
	blk := buf[off : off+16]
	for i := range blk {
		blk[i] = 0
	}
	copy(blk[0:3], b.ioData[:])
	copy(blk[3:6], b.ioCtrl[:])
	var flags uint8
	if b.z80Req {
		flags |= 1 << 0
	}
	if b.z80Rst {
		flags |= 1 << 1
	}
	if b.z80RstPending {
		flags |= 1 << 2
	}
	if b.sramOn {
		flags |= 1 << 3
	}
	blk[6] = flags
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(blk[7:9], uint16(b.bank))
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores state written by Serialize into the existing RAM
// arrays and SRAM slice (allocating SRAM if this bus has none but the
// state carries some).
func (b *Bus) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < b.SerializeSize() {
		return errors.New("bus: state buffer too small")
	}
	off := 0
	copy(b.RAM[:], buf[off:off+0x10000])
	off += 0x10000
	copy(b.ZRAM[:], buf[off:off+0x2000])
	off += 0x2000
	n := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off : off+4]))
	off += 4
	if n > sramStateSize {
		n = sramStateSize
	}
	if n > 0 {
		if len(b.SRAM) < n {
			b.SRAM = make([]uint8, n)
		}
		copy(b.SRAM[:n], buf[off:off+n])
	}
	off += sramStateSize
	blk := buf[off : off+16]
	copy(b.ioData[:], blk[0:3])
	copy(b.ioCtrl[:], blk[3:6])
	flags := blk[6]
	b.z80Req = flags&(1<<0) != 0
	b.z80Rst = flags&(1<<1) != 0
	b.z80RstPending = flags&(1<<2) != 0
	b.sramOn = flags&(1<<3) != 0
	b.bank = uint32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(blk[7:9])) & 0x1FF
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/bus/bus_test.go ====================

package bus

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/sound"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/vdp"
)

// testCart builds a synthetic 256KB cartridge image with a deterministic
// pattern plus two sentinel bytes inside the bank-3 window page.
func testCart() *cart.Cart {
	data := make([]byte, 0x40000)
	for i := range data {
		data[i] = uint8(i>>3) ^ uint8(i)
	}
	data[0x18000] = 0x5A
	data[0x18001] = 0xA5
	return &cart.Cart{Data: data}
}

func newTestBus(c *cart.Cart) *Bus {
	return New(c, vdp.New(), sound.New())
}

func TestROMReads(t *testing.T) {
	c := testCart()
	b := newTestBus(c)

	if got := b.Read8(0x1234); got != c.Data[0x1234] {
		t.Errorf("Read8 ROM = %02X, want %02X", got, c.Data[0x1234])
	}
	if got, want := b.Read16(0x0100), binary.BigEndian.Uint16(c.Data[0x100:0x102]); got != want {
		t.Errorf("Read16 ROM = %04X, want %04X", got, want)
	}
	if got, want := b.Read32(0x0200), binary.BigEndian.Uint32(c.Data[0x200:0x204]); got != want {
		t.Errorf("Read32 ROM = %08X, want %08X", got, want)
	}
}

func TestRAMMirror(t *testing.T) {
	b := newTestBus(testCart())

	b.Write8(0xE00010, 0xAB)
	if got := b.Read8(0xFF0010); got != 0xAB {
		t.Errorf("RAM mirror byte = %02X, want AB", got)
	}
	b.Write16(0xFF1000, 0xBEEF)
	if got := b.Read16(0xE01000); got != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("RAM mirror word = %04X, want BEEF", got)
	}
	b.Write32(0xE02000, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if got := b.Read32(0xFF2000); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("RAM mirror long = %08X, want DEADBEEF", got)
	}
}

func TestPadProtocol(t *testing.T) {
	b := newTestBus(testCart())

	if got := b.Read8(0xA10000); got != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("version register = %02X, want 80", got)
	}

	// Port 1: TH as output, TH driven high. A, Start and Up are pressed
	// but only Up belongs to the TH-high group.
	b.Write8(0xA10009, 0x40)
	b.Write8(0xA10003, 0x40)
	b.SetPad(0, PadA|PadStart|PadUp)
	if got := b.Read8(0xA10003); got != 0xFE {
		t.Errorf("TH high pad read = %02X, want FE", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0xA10009); got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("control readback = %02X, want 40", got)
	}

	// TH driven low: Start and A appear, Down joins Up, Left/Right read 0.
	b.Write8(0xA10003, 0x00)
	if got := b.Read8(0xA10003); got != 0x82 {
		t.Errorf("TH low pad read = %02X, want 82", got)
	}

	// TH as input floats high regardless of the data latch; with no
	// buttons pressed every active-low bit reads 1.
	b.Write8(0xA10009, 0x00)
	b.SetPad(0, 0)
	if got := b.Read8(0xA10003); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("TH input pad read = %02X, want FF", got)
	}

	// Expansion port floats.
	if got := b.Read8(0xA10007); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("expansion port = %02X, want FF", got)
	}
}

func TestZ80WindowAndBank(t *testing.T) {
	c := testCart()
	b := newTestBus(c)

	// Z80 RAM through the 68k window and its mirror.
	b.Write(0x0010, 0x77)
	if got := b.Read8(0xA00010); got != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("68k sees ZRAM = %02X, want 77", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0xA08010); got != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("68k sees ZRAM mirror = %02X, want 77", got)
	}
	if got := b.Fetch(0x0010); got != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("Fetch = %02X, want 77", got)
	}
	// Window offsets past ZRAM are unmapped from both sides.
	if got := b.Read8(0xA02000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("window hole = %02X, want FF", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x2000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("Z80 hole = %02X, want FF", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x7F11); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("PSG read = %02X, want FF", got)
	}

	// Shift bank 3 into the register (9 bits, LSB first) and read the
	// ROM page it selects through the 0x8000 window.
	for i := 0; i < 9; i++ {
		bit := uint8(0)
		if i < 2 {
			bit = 1
		}
		b.Write(0x6000, bit)
	}
	if b.bank != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("bank = %d, want 3", b.bank)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x8000); got != 0x5A {
		t.Errorf("banked ROM[0] = %02X, want 5A", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x8001); got != 0xA5 {
		t.Errorf("banked ROM[1] = %02X, want A5", got)
	}
}

func TestZ80Control(t *testing.T) {
	b := newTestBus(testCart())

	// Power-on state: reset asserted, so the Z80 is halted and no reset
	// edge is reported yet.
	if !b.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("Z80 should be halted at power-on (reset asserted)")
	}
	if b.TakeZ80Reset() {
		t.Error("TakeZ80Reset fired while reset still asserted")
	}

	// Release reset: the one-shot fires exactly once.
	b.Write16(0xA11200, 0x0100)
	if b.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("Z80 still halted after reset release")
	}
	if !b.TakeZ80Reset() {
		t.Error("TakeZ80Reset did not fire after release")
	}
	if b.TakeZ80Reset() {
		t.Error("TakeZ80Reset fired twice")
	}

	// Bus request by word write. The status reads back 0 once the bus is
	// granted to the 68000: the status bit means "the Z80 still owns the
	// bus", and games poll it waiting for it to clear.
	b.Write16(0xA11100, 0x0100)
	if !b.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("Z80 not halted after bus request")
	}
	if got := b.Read16(0xA11100); got != 0x0000 {
		t.Errorf("bus request readback = %04X, want 0000 (granted)", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0xA11100); got != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("bus request byte readback = %02X, want 00 (granted)", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0xA11101); got != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("bus request low byte = %02X, want 00", got)
	}

	// Release by byte write, re-request by byte write, release by word.
	b.Write8(0xA11100, 0x00)
	if b.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("Z80 halted after byte release of bus request")
	}
	b.Write8(0xA11100, 0x01)
	if !b.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("Z80 not halted after byte bus request")
	}
	b.Write16(0xA11100, 0x0000)
	if b.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("Z80 halted after word release of bus request")
	}
	if got := b.Read16(0xA11100); got != 0x0100 {
		t.Errorf("bus request readback = %04X, want 0100 (Z80 owns the bus again)", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0xA11100); got != 0x01 {
		t.Errorf("bus request byte readback = %02X, want 01 (Z80 owns the bus again)", got)
	}

	// Re-asserting reset halts again without an edge report.
	b.Write16(0xA11200, 0x0000)
	if !b.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("Z80 not halted after reset re-assert")
	}
	if b.TakeZ80Reset() {
		t.Error("TakeZ80Reset fired on assert")
	}
}

func TestSRAMOverlay(t *testing.T) {
	data := make([]byte, 0x400000)
	data[0x200001] = 0x11 // ROM byte behind the SRAM window
	c := &cart.Cart{Data: data, SRAM: true, SRAMStart: 0x200000, SRAMEnd: 0x20FFFF}
	b := newTestBus(c)

	// Switch off: the window reads ROM.
	if got := b.Read8(0x200001); got != 0x11 {
		t.Fatalf("pre-switch read = %02X, want ROM 11", got)
	}

	// Switch on via the byte lane. Even addresses float, odd store.
	b.Write8(0xA130F1, 0x01)
	if got := b.Read8(0x200000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("even SRAM read = %02X, want FF", got)
	}
	b.Write8(0x200000, 0x99)
	b.Write8(0x200001, 0x42)
	b.Write8(0x200003, 0x43)
	if got := b.Read8(0x200001); got != 0x42 {
		t.Errorf("SRAM[0] = %02X, want 42", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0x200003); got != 0x43 {
		t.Errorf("SRAM[1] = %02X, want 43", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0x200000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("even SRAM write leaked: read = %02X, want FF", got)
	}

	// Word writes use the low byte: 0x0000 switches out, 0x0001 back in,
	// and the contents survive the round trip.
	b.Write16(0xA130F0, 0x0000)
	if got := b.Read8(0x200001); got != 0x11 {
		t.Errorf("switched-out read = %02X, want ROM 11", got)
	}
	b.Write16(0xA130F0, 0x0001)
	if got := b.Read8(0x200001); got != 0x42 {
		t.Errorf("switched-in read = %02X, want SRAM 42", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	data := make([]byte, 0x400000)
	data[0x28000] = 0x3C // bank 5 window sentinel
	c := &cart.Cart{Data: data, SRAM: true, SRAMStart: 0x200000, SRAMEnd: 0x20FFFF}
	b := newTestBus(c)

	b.Write8(0xE00010, 0xDE)    // work RAM
	b.Write(0x0010, 0xAD)       // Z80 RAM
	b.Write8(0xA130F1, 0x01)    // SRAM on
	b.Write8(0x200001, 0x77)    // SRAM[0]
	b.Write8(0xA10009, 0x40)    // IO control
	b.Write8(0xA10003, 0x40)    // IO data
	b.Write16(0xA11100, 0x0100) // Z80 bus requested
	b.Write16(0xA11200, 0x0100) // reset released
	b.TakeZ80Reset()            // consume the edge
	for i, bit := range []uint8{1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0} {
		_ = i
		b.Write(0x6000, bit) // bank 5
	}
	if b.bank != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("bank = %d, want 5", b.bank)
	}

	if got, want := b.SerializeSize(), 0x10000+0x2000+4+0x10000+16; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("SerializeSize = %d, want %d", got, want)
	}
	buf := make([]byte, b.SerializeSize())
	if err := b.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	if err := b.Serialize(make([]byte, 8)); err == nil {
		t.Error("Serialize accepted a short buffer")
	}

	b2 := newTestBus(c)
	if err := b2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if err := b2.Deserialize(make([]byte, 8)); err == nil {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted a short buffer")
	}
	if got := b2.Read8(0xE00010); got != 0xDE {
		t.Errorf("RAM round trip = %02X, want DE", got)
	}
	if got := b2.Read(0x0010); got != 0xAD {
		t.Errorf("ZRAM round trip = %02X, want AD", got)
	}
	if got := b2.Read8(0x200001); got != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("SRAM round trip = %02X, want 77", got)
	}
	if got := b2.Read8(0xA10009); got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("ioCtrl round trip = %02X, want 40", got)
	}
	if !b2.Z80Halted() {
		t.Error("z80Req flag lost in round trip")
	}
	if got := b2.Read(0x8000); got != 0x3C {
		t.Errorf("bank round trip: window = %02X, want 3C", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/cart/cart.go ====================

// Package cart loads and describes a Sega Genesis / Mega Drive ROM image.
//
// Written clean-room from the published cartridge header layout. The header
// occupies the bytes at 0x100-0x1FF of every Genesis ROM.
package cart

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"strings"
)

// Cart is a loaded cartridge image plus the facts parsed from its header.
type Cart struct {
	Data       []byte // raw ROM image, big-endian as stored on the cartridge
	Title      string // overseas title (header 0x150)
	TitleJP    string // domestic title (header 0x120)
	Serial     string // serial number (header 0x180)
	Checksum   uint16 // checksum stored in the header (0x18E)
	ChecksumOK bool   // stored checksum matches the computed one
	SRAM       bool   // cartridge carries battery/save RAM
	SRAMStart  uint32 // save RAM window start (usually 0x200000)
	SRAMEnd    uint32 // save RAM window end (inclusive)
	Region     byte   // first region code byte (header 0x1F0): 'J', 'U', 'E'
}

// Load parses a ROM image. data is the whole file contents.
func Load(data []byte) (*Cart, error) {
	if len(data) < 0x200 {
		return nil, errors.New("cart: image too small to hold a Genesis header")
	}
	c := &Cart{Data: data}
	sys := strings.TrimSpace(string(data[0x100:0x110]))
	if !strings.HasPrefix(sys, "SEGA") {
		return nil, errors.New("cart: missing SEGA header at 0x100")
	}
	c.TitleJP = strings.TrimSpace(string(data[0x120:0x150]))
	c.Title = strings.TrimSpace(string(data[0x150:0x180]))
	c.Serial = strings.TrimSpace(string(data[0x180:0x18E]))
	c.Checksum = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[0x18E:0x190])
	c.ChecksumOK = c.Checksum == ComputeChecksum(data)
	if data[0x1B0] == 'R' && data[0x1B1] == 'A' {
		c.SRAM = true
		c.SRAMStart = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[0x1B4:0x1B8])
		c.SRAMEnd = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[0x1B8:0x1BC])
		if c.SRAMStart == 0 {
			c.SRAMStart = 0x200000
		}
		if c.SRAMEnd < c.SRAMStart {
			c.SRAMEnd = c.SRAMStart + 0xFFFF
		}
	}
	c.Region = data[0x1F0]
	return c, nil
}

// ComputeChecksum returns the Genesis header checksum for an image: the
// 16-bit wrapping sum of every word from offset 0x200 to the end.
func ComputeChecksum(data []byte) uint16 {
	var sum uint16
	for i := 0x200; i+1 < len(data); i += 2 {
		sum += binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[i : i+2])
	}
	return sum
}

// ReadROM returns the ROM byte at a 68k address inside the cartridge window
// (0x000000-0x3FFFFF). Images smaller than the window mirror, as they do on
// real hardware when address lines go unconnected.
func (c *Cart) ReadROM(addr uint32) uint8 {
	if len(c.Data) == 0 {
		return 0xFF
	}
	return c.Data[addr%uint32(len(c.Data))]
}

// ReadROM16 returns the big-endian ROM word at addr, applying the
// same mirror wrap as ReadROM to each byte: byte one is the byte
// ReadROM(addr) returns, byte two is ReadROM(addr+1), with a single
// modulo for the pair.
func (c *Cart) ReadROM16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	n := uint32(len(c.Data))
	if n == 0 {
		return 0xFFFF
	}
	i := addr % n
	hi := uint16(c.Data[i])
	i++
	if i == n {
		i = 0
	}
	return hi<<8 | uint16(c.Data[i])
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k/cpu.go ====================

// Package m68k is an original implementation of the Motorola 68000 CPU,
// written from the behavior documented in the M68000 Programmer's
// Reference Manual: the base instruction set, all 14 addressing modes,
// condition-code semantics, the exception model, and the manual's cycle
// count tables (implemented exactly where the manual is exact, and in
// the documented neighborhood elsewhere, which is what a line-budget
// scheduler in a game console core needs).
//
// This is the original 68000 only: no 68010+ instructions (MOVES, MOVEC,
// BKPT, RTD, long CHK, index scaling) exist here, and their encodings
// raise the illegal-instruction exception as they do on real silicon.
//
// Stack model: a[7] always holds the ACTIVE stack pointer; the inactive
// one lives in usp/ssp and is swapped in by setSupervisor whenever the
// S bit of SR changes, exactly as the hardware swaps A7 with USP/SSP.
package m68k

// Bus is the memory interface the CPU drives. Read32/Write32 move a full
// long word in CPU order; the bus owns the byte ordering of its memory.
type Bus interface {
	Read8(addr uint32) uint8
	Read16(addr uint32) uint16
	Read32(addr uint32) uint32
	Write8(addr uint32, val uint8)
	Write16(addr uint32, val uint16)
	Write32(addr uint32, val uint32)
	Reset()
}

// Registers is a snapshot of the programmer-visible CPU state.
type Registers struct {
	D   [8]uint32
	A   [8]uint32
	PC  uint32
	SR  uint16
	USP uint32
	SSP uint32
	IR  uint16
}

// Status register bits.
const (
	srT    = 0x8000 // trace enable
	srS    = 0x2000 // supervisor state
	srMask = 0x0700 // interrupt priority mask (bits 10-8)
	srX    = 0x0010
	srN    = 0x0008
	srZ    = 0x0004
	srV    = 0x0002
	srC    = 0x0001
	srFull = 0xA71F // all bits that exist on a real 68000 SR
)

// Exception vector numbers used by this implementation.
const (
	vecAddressError = 3
	vecIllegal      = 4
	vecDivZero      = 5
	vecCHK          = 6
	vecTRAPV        = 7
	vecPrivilege    = 8
	vecTrace        = 9
	vecLineA        = 10
	vecLineF        = 11
)

// CPU is a Motorola 68000. The zero value is not usable; call New.
type CPU struct {
	bus Bus

	d   [8]uint32
	a   [8]uint32 // a[7] is the active stack pointer
	usp uint32    // user stack pointer (inactive while supervisor)
	ssp uint32    // supervisor stack pointer (inactive while user)
	pc  uint32
	sr  uint16
	ir  uint16 // last opcode fetched (the 68000's instruction register)

	// instrPC is the address of the instruction currently executing.
	// Exceptions raised because an instruction could not execute at
	// all (illegal encoding, line A and F, privilege violation) stack
	// this address, so a handler can inspect the offending word; only
	// exceptions raised by a completed instruction (TRAP, CHK, divide
	// by zero, ...) stack the following address.
	instrPC uint32

	cycles  uint64
	stopped bool // STOP executed; waiting for an acceptable interrupt
	halted  bool // double fault; the processor is dead until Reset

	// Pending (latched) interrupt request. A latched request survives
	// while the SR mask inhibits it and is serviced when the mask drops.
	pendPresent bool
	pendLevel   uint8
	pendVec     uint8
	pendVecOK   bool // an explicit vector was supplied

	tookException bool // set when the current step entered an exception
	inEntry       bool // inside exception entry (double-fault guard)
}

// New creates a CPU attached to bus. Call Reset to power it on.
func New(bus Bus) *CPU {
	return &CPU{bus: bus}
}

// Reset powers the CPU on: SR = 0x2700 (supervisor, mask 7, trace off),
// the supervisor stack pointer is loaded from vector 0 and the PC from
// vector 1, and all pending state is cleared.
//
// Note: CPU reset does not pulse the bus Reset line in this model; the
// surrounding system owns peripheral reset sequencing.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	c.d = [8]uint32{}
	c.a = [8]uint32{}
	c.sr = 0x2700
	c.a[7] = c.bus.Read32(0)
	c.ssp = c.a[7]
	c.usp = 0
	c.pc = c.bus.Read32(4)
	c.ir = 0
	c.cycles = 0
	c.stopped = false
	c.halted = false
	c.pendPresent = false
	c.tookException = false
	c.inEntry = false
}

// Cycles returns the total cycles consumed since Reset (plus any credit
// added with AddCycles).
func (c *CPU) Cycles() uint64 { return c.cycles }

// AddCycles advances the cycle counter without executing anything; the
// caller uses it to account for external bus-hold periods (for example
// DMA seizing the bus) and to restore a saved counter after SetState.
func (c *CPU) AddCycles(n uint64) { c.cycles += n }

// Halted reports whether the CPU has halted (double fault).
func (c *CPU) Halted() bool { return c.halted }

// Registers returns the live programmer-visible state. A[7] is the
// active stack pointer; the USP/SSP fields hold the user/supervisor
// stack pointers, with the active one mirroring A[7].
func (c *CPU) Registers() Registers {
	var r Registers
	r.D = c.d
	r.A = c.a
	if c.sr&srS != 0 {
		r.SSP = c.a[7]
		r.USP = c.usp
	} else {
		r.USP = c.a[7]
		r.SSP = c.ssp
	}
	r.PC = c.pc
	r.SR = c.sr
	r.IR = c.ir
	return r
}

// SetState installs a register snapshot for save-state restore. The
// contract (which the restore path depends on) is: D, SR, USP, SSP, PC
// and IR are copied; A[0..6] are copied; A[7] is NOT taken from the
// argument's A[7] but derived from the mode: SSP when SR bit 13
// (supervisor) is set, USP otherwise. Stopped and halted are cleared,
// pending interrupts are cleared, and the cycle counter is set to 0
// (the caller re-adds any saved count with AddCycles).
func (c *CPU) SetState(r Registers) {
	c.d = r.D
	for i := 0; i < 7; i++ {
		c.a[i] = r.A[i]
	}
	c.pc = r.PC
	c.sr = r.SR & srFull
	c.usp = r.USP
	c.ssp = r.SSP
	if c.sr&srS != 0 {
		c.a[7] = r.SSP
	} else {
		c.a[7] = r.USP
	}
	c.ir = r.IR
	c.stopped = false
	c.halted = false
	c.pendPresent = false
	c.tookException = false
	c.inEntry = false
	c.cycles = 0
}

// RequestInterrupt latches a pending interrupt at the given priority
// level (1-7). vector, when non-nil, is the exception vector number to
// use; nil requests an autovector interrupt (vector 24+level). A latched
// request is not dropped while the SR interrupt mask inhibits it: it is
// serviced at the first instruction boundary after the mask drops below
// the level. Level 7 is non-maskable. A newly arriving request replaces
// a latched one of equal or lower level.
func (c *CPU) RequestInterrupt(level uint8, vector *uint8) {
	if level == 0 || level > 7 || c.halted {
		return
	}
	if c.pendPresent && level < c.pendLevel {
		return
	}
	c.pendPresent = true
	c.pendLevel = level
	if vector != nil {
		c.pendVec = *vector
		c.pendVecOK = true
	} else {
		c.pendVecOK = false
	}
}

// Step executes one instruction, or one exception entry, and returns the
// cycles consumed. While the CPU is stopped (STOP) with no acceptable
// interrupt pending, Step advances time by 4 cycles without executing.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	if c.halted {
		c.cycles += 4
		return 4
	}
	if c.stopped {
		if c.intAcceptable() {
			c.stopped = false
			n := c.safeEntry(c.serviceInterrupt)
			c.cycles += uint64(n)
			return n
		}
		c.cycles += 4
		return 4
	}
	if c.intAcceptable() {
		n := c.safeEntry(c.serviceInterrupt)
		c.cycles += uint64(n)
		return n
	}
	return c.stepExec()
}

// StepCycles executes instructions until at least budget cycles have
// been consumed and returns the total consumed. A stopped or halted CPU
// consumes the whole budget as elapsed time.
func (c *CPU) StepCycles(budget int) int {
	if budget <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if c.halted || (c.stopped && !c.intAcceptable()) {
		c.cycles += uint64(budget)
		return budget
	}
	total := 0
	for total < budget {
		total += c.Step()
	}
	return total
}

// stepExec fetches and executes one instruction, converting internal
// faults (address error, illegal encoding) into exception entries.
func (c *CPU) stepExec() (ret int) {
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			switch f := r.(type) {
			case addrError:
				if c.inEntry {
					c.halted = true
					c.cycles += 4
					ret = 4
					return
				}
				n := c.safeEntry(func() int { return c.enterAddrError(f) })
				c.cycles += uint64(n)
				ret = n
			case illegalEncoding:
				if c.inEntry {
					c.halted = true
					c.cycles += 4
					ret = 4
					return
				}
				n := c.safeEntry(func() int { return c.enterExceptionAt(vecIllegal, c.instrPC, 34) })
				c.cycles += uint64(n)
				ret = n
			default:
				panic(r)
			}
		}
	}()
	trace := c.sr&srT != 0
	c.instrPC = c.pc
	op := c.fetch16()
	c.ir = op
	c.tookException = false
	n := c.execute(op)
	c.cycles += uint64(n)
	ret = n
	if trace && !c.tookException && !c.stopped {
		m := c.safeEntry(func() int { return c.enterException(vecTrace, 34) })
		c.cycles += uint64(m)
		ret += m
	}
	return ret
}

// safeEntry runs an exception-entry routine, converting an address error
// raised inside the entry itself (a fault while stacking, i.e. a double
// fault) into the halted state instead of a panic escape.
func (c *CPU) safeEntry(entry func() int) (ret int) {
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			if _, ok := r.(addrError); ok {
				c.inEntry = false
				c.halted = true
				ret = 4
				return
			}
			panic(r)
		}
	}()
	return entry()
}

// intAcceptable reports whether the latched interrupt may be serviced:
// its level must exceed the SR mask, except level 7, which is
// non-maskable.
func (c *CPU) intAcceptable() bool {
	if !c.pendPresent || c.halted {
		return false
	}
	if c.pendLevel == 7 {
		return true
	}
	return c.pendLevel > uint8((c.sr>>8)&7)
}

// serviceInterrupt performs interrupt entry: the PC and SR are stacked
// on the supervisor stack, S is set, trace is cleared, the mask is
// raised to the interrupt level, and the PC is loaded from the
// interrupt's vector (the requested vector, or the autovector).
// Documented cost: 44 cycles.
func (c *CPU) serviceInterrupt() int {
	level := c.pendLevel
	vec := int(24 + level)
	if c.pendVecOK {
		vec = int(c.pendVec)
	}
	c.pendPresent = false
	oldSR := c.sr
	c.setSupervisor(true)
	c.sr = (oldSR | srS) &^ srT & srFull
	c.sr = (c.sr &^ srMask) | uint16(level)<<8
	c.inEntry = true
	c.push32(c.pc)
	c.push16(oldSR)
	c.inEntry = false
	c.pc = c.bus.Read32(uint32(vec) * 4)
	c.tookException = true
	return 44
}

// enterException performs a software exception entry for an exception
// raised by a completed instruction (TRAP, CHK, divide by zero, ...):
// the address of the next instruction and the SR are stacked on the
// supervisor stack, S is set, trace is cleared, the interrupt mask is
// left unchanged, and the PC is loaded from the vector.
func (c *CPU) enterException(vector int, cycles int) int {
	return c.enterExceptionAt(vector, c.pc, cycles)
}

// enterExceptionAt is enterException with a caller-chosen stacked PC.
// Per the manual, exceptions for instructions that never executed
// (illegal instruction, line A and line F emulation, privilege
// violation) stack the address of the offending instruction itself,
// so a handler can decode the word that caused the exception.
func (c *CPU) enterExceptionAt(vector int, stackPC uint32, cycles int) int {
	c.tookException = true
	oldSR := c.sr
	c.setSupervisor(true)
	c.sr = (oldSR | srS) &^ srT & srFull
	c.inEntry = true
	c.push32(stackPC)
	c.push16(oldSR)
	c.inEntry = false
	c.pc = c.bus.Read32(uint32(vector) * 4)
	return cycles
}

// addrError is an internal fault: a word or long access to an odd
// address. Real hardware raises the address-error exception (vector 3).
type addrError struct {
	addr  uint32
	write bool
}

// illegalEncoding is an internal fault: an opcode bit pattern that the
// decode rejected before any operand fetch (an unassigned EA mode, a
// PC-relative destination, ...). Real hardware raises vector 4.
type illegalEncoding struct{}

// enterAddrError stacks a plausible 68000 group-0 frame: below the
// normal SR/PC frame it places a status word, the instruction register,
// and the access address (the extra information the 68000 stacks for bus
// and address errors). Games should never take this exception; the frame
// layout is a documented simplification.
func (c *CPU) enterAddrError(ae addrError) int {
	c.tookException = true
	oldSR := c.sr
	c.setSupervisor(true)
	c.sr = (oldSR | srS) &^ srT & srFull
	var stat uint16
	if ae.write {
		stat |= 0x10 // read/write indicator, simplified
	}
	c.inEntry = true
	c.push32(ae.addr) // access address
	c.push16(c.ir)    // instruction register
	c.push16(stat)    // status information word
	c.push32(c.instrPC)
	c.push16(oldSR)
	c.inEntry = false
	c.pc = c.bus.Read32(uint32(vecAddressError) * 4)
	return 50
}

// setSupervisor swaps the stack pointers so that a[7] is the stack
// pointer for the requested state. It only swaps the pointers; callers
// manage the S bit of SR themselves.
func (c *CPU) setSupervisor(on bool) {
	cur := c.sr&srS != 0
	if cur == on {
		return
	}
	if on {
		c.usp = c.a[7]
		c.a[7] = c.ssp
	} else {
		c.ssp = c.a[7]
		c.a[7] = c.usp
	}
}

// applySR installs a complete new SR value (MOVE to SR, RTE, STOP),
// swapping stack pointers if the S bit changes.
func (c *CPU) applySR(v uint16) {
	v &= srFull
	c.setSupervisor(v&srS != 0)
	c.sr = v
}

// setCCR installs a new condition-code byte (low byte of SR), preserving
// the rest of SR. Only the flag bits that exist are taken.
func (c *CPU) setCCR(v uint16) {
	c.sr = (c.sr & 0xFF00) | (v & 0x1F)
}

// --- memory access -------------------------------------------------
// Word and long accesses to odd addresses raise the address-error
// exception on the 68000; the helpers below panic with addrError and
// Step converts the fault into an exception entry.

func (c *CPU) rd8(addr uint32) uint8 { return c.bus.Read8(addr) }

func (c *CPU) rd16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr})
	}
	return c.bus.Read16(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) rd32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr})
	}
	return c.bus.Read32(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) wr8(addr uint32, v uint8) { c.bus.Write8(addr, v) }

func (c *CPU) wr16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr, write: true})
	}
	c.bus.Write16(addr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) wr32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr, write: true})
	}
	c.bus.Write32(addr, v)
}

// fetch16 reads the next instruction-stream word and advances the PC.
func (c *CPU) fetch16() uint16 {
	v := c.rd16(c.pc)
	c.pc += 2
	return v
}

// fetch32 reads the next instruction-stream long word.
func (c *CPU) fetch32() uint32 {
	hi := uint32(c.fetch16())
	return hi<<16 | uint32(c.fetch16())
}

// push16/push32 store on the active stack (predecrement);
// pop16/pop32 load from it (postincrement).
func (c *CPU) push16(v uint16) {
	c.a[7] -= 2
	c.wr16(c.a[7], v)
}

func (c *CPU) push32(v uint32) {
	c.a[7] -= 4
	c.wr32(c.a[7], v)
}

func (c *CPU) pop16() uint16 {
	v := c.rd16(c.a[7])
	c.a[7] += 2
	return v
}

func (c *CPU) pop32() uint32 {
	v := c.rd32(c.a[7])
	c.a[7] += 4
	return v
}

// --- condition codes -----------------------------------------------

// Operand size codes used throughout the decoder.
const (
	szB = 0 // byte
	szW = 1 // word
	szL = 2 // long
)

func sizeBytes(size int) int { return 1 << uint(size) }

func sizeMask(size int) uint32 {
	if size == szL {
		return 0xFFFFFFFF
	}
	return (uint32(1) << uint(sizeBytes(size)*8)) - 1
}

func signBit(size int) uint32 { return uint32(1) << uint(sizeBytes(size)*8-1) }

// setNZ sets N and Z from a result of the given size, touching nothing
// else.
func (c *CPU) setNZ(v uint32, size int) {
	v &= sizeMask(size)
	c.sr &^= srN | srZ
	if v == 0 {
		c.sr |= srZ
	}
	if v&signBit(size) != 0 {
		c.sr |= srN
	}
}

// flagsLogic applies the standard logical-instruction flags: N and Z
// from the result, V and C cleared, X preserved.
func (c *CPU) flagsLogic(v uint32, size int) {
	c.setNZ(v, size)
	c.sr &^= srV | srC
}

// flagsAdd computes a + b + xIn (xIn is 0 or 1) at the given size and
// sets X, N, Z, V, C per the manual. With stickyZ (ADDX), a zero result
// leaves Z unchanged instead of setting it. Returns the masked result.
func (c *CPU) flagsAdd(a, b uint32, size int, xIn uint8, stickyZ bool) uint32 {
	mask := sizeMask(size)
	sb := signBit(size)
	a &= mask
	b &= mask
	bEff := (b + uint32(xIn)) & mask
	full := uint64(a) + uint64(b) + uint64(xIn)
	res := uint32(full) & mask
	var f uint16
	if full > uint64(mask) {
		f |= srC | srX
	}
	if (a^res)&(bEff^res)&sb != 0 {
		f |= srV
	}
	if res&sb != 0 {
		f |= srN
	}
	if res == 0 && (!stickyZ || c.sr&srZ != 0) {
		f |= srZ
	}
	c.sr = (c.sr &^ (srX | srN | srZ | srV | srC)) | f
	return res
}

// flagsSub computes a - b - xIn (xIn is 0 or 1) at the given size and
// sets X (to the borrow), N, Z, V, C per the manual. With stickyZ
// (SUBX), a zero result leaves Z unchanged. Returns the masked result.
func (c *CPU) flagsSub(a, b uint32, size int, xIn uint8, stickyZ bool) uint32 {
	mask := sizeMask(size)
	sb := signBit(size)
	a &= mask
	b &= mask
	diff := int64(a) - int64(b) - int64(xIn)
	res := uint32(diff) & mask
	var f uint16
	if diff < 0 {
		f |= srC | srX
	}
	if (a^b)&sb != 0 && (res^a)&sb != 0 {
		f |= srV
	}
	if res&sb != 0 {
		f |= srN
	}
	if res == 0 && (!stickyZ || c.sr&srZ != 0) {
		f |= srZ
	}
	c.sr = (c.sr &^ (srX | srN | srZ | srV | srC)) | f
	return res
}

// flagsCmp applies subtraction flags (for CMP/CMPA/CMPM) while
// preserving X, which compares never affect.
func (c *CPU) flagsCmp(a, b uint32, size int) {
	x := c.sr & srX
	c.flagsSub(a, b, size, 0, false)
	c.sr = (c.sr &^ srX) | x
}

// condTrue evaluates a 68000 condition-code field (Bcc/Scc/DBcc).
func (c *CPU) condTrue(cond int) bool {
	switch cond {
	case 0: // T
		return true
	case 1: // F
		return false
	case 2: // HI: !C && !Z
		return c.sr&(srC|srZ) == 0
	case 3: // LS: C || Z
		return c.sr&(srC|srZ) != 0
	case 4: // CC: !C
		return c.sr&srC == 0
	case 5: // CS: C
		return c.sr&srC != 0
	case 6: // NE: !Z
		return c.sr&srZ == 0
	case 7: // EQ: Z
		return c.sr&srZ != 0
	case 8: // VC: !V
		return c.sr&srV == 0
	case 9: // VS: V
		return c.sr&srV != 0
	case 10: // PL: !N
		return c.sr&srN == 0
	case 11: // MI: N
		return c.sr&srN != 0
	case 12: // GE: N == V
		return (c.sr&srN != 0) == (c.sr&srV != 0)
	case 13: // LT: N != V
		return (c.sr&srN != 0) != (c.sr&srV != 0)
	case 14: // GT: !Z && N == V
		return c.sr&srZ == 0 && (c.sr&srN != 0) == (c.sr&srV != 0)
	case 15: // LE: Z || N != V
		return c.sr&srZ != 0 || (c.sr&srN != 0) != (c.sr&srV != 0)
	}
	return false
}

// xBit returns the current X flag as 0 or 1.
func (c *CPU) xBit() uint8 {
	if c.sr&srX != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k/disasm.go ====================

package m68k

import "fmt"

// Disassemble decodes the instruction at pc, reading instruction words
// through fetch. It returns the mnemonic text and the address of the
// next instruction. The common instruction forms are covered; anything
// unrecognized (or an encoding the decoder rejects) renders as
// "DC.W $XXXX" and advances one word.
func Disassemble(pc uint32, fetch func(addr uint32) uint16) (string, uint32) {
	op := fetch(pc)
	d := &disState{start: pc, cur: pc + 2, fetch: fetch}
	text := d.decode(op)
	if text == "" {
		return fmt.Sprintf("DC.W $%04X", op), pc + 2
	}
	return text, d.cur
}

type disState struct {
	start uint32
	cur   uint32
	fetch func(addr uint32) uint16
}

func (d *disState) w() uint16 {
	v := d.fetch(d.cur)
	d.cur += 2
	return v
}

func (d *disState) l() uint32 {
	hi := uint32(d.w())
	return hi<<16 | uint32(d.w())
}

var disSizeSuffix = []string{".B", ".W", ".L", ""}

var disCond = []string{"T", "F", "HI", "LS", "CC", "CS", "NE", "EQ",
	"VC", "VS", "PL", "MI", "GE", "LT", "GT", "LE"}

// hexDisp formats a signed displacement as $XX or -$XX.
func hexDisp(v int32) string {
	if v < 0 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("-$%X", -v)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("$%X", v)
}

// indexStr formats the register of an index extension word.
func indexStr(ext uint16) string {
	name := byte('D')
	if ext&0x8000 != 0 {
		name = 'A'
	}
	sz := "W"
	if ext&0x0800 != 0 {
		sz = "L"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%c%d.%s", name, (ext>>12)&7, sz)
}

// ea formats an effective-address operand, consuming its extension
// words exactly as the executor's operand resolver does.
func (d *disState) ea(mode, reg, size int) string {
	switch mode {
	case 0:
		return fmt.Sprintf("D%d", reg)
	case 1:
		return fmt.Sprintf("A%d", reg)
	case 2:
		return fmt.Sprintf("(A%d)", reg)
	case 3:
		return fmt.Sprintf("(A%d)+", reg)
	case 4:
		return fmt.Sprintf("-(A%d)", reg)
	case 5:
		disp := int32(int16(d.w()))
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s(A%d)", hexDisp(disp), reg)
	case 6:
		ext := d.w()
		disp := int32(int8(uint8(ext & 0xFF)))
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s(A%d,%s)", hexDisp(disp), reg, indexStr(ext))
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			return fmt.Sprintf("$%04X", d.w())
		case 1:
			return fmt.Sprintf("$%08X", d.l())
		case 2:
			disp := int32(int16(d.w()))
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s(PC)", hexDisp(disp))
		case 3:
			ext := d.w()
			disp := int32(int8(uint8(ext & 0xFF)))
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s(PC,%s)", hexDisp(disp), indexStr(ext))
		case 4:
			switch size {
			case szB:
				return fmt.Sprintf("#$%02X", d.w()&0xFF)
			case szW:
				return fmt.Sprintf("#$%04X", d.w())
			case szL:
				return fmt.Sprintf("#$%08X", d.l())
			}
		}
	}
	return "?"
}

// imm formats a bare immediate operand (line-0 ops read it before the EA).
func (d *disState) imm(size int) string {
	switch size {
	case szB:
		return fmt.Sprintf("#$%02X", d.w()&0xFF)
	case szW:
		return fmt.Sprintf("#$%04X", d.w())
	case szL:
		return fmt.Sprintf("#$%08X", d.l())
	}
	return "#?"
}

func (d *disState) decode(op uint16) string {
	switch op >> 12 {
	case 0x0:
		return d.decodeLine0(op)
	case 0x1:
		return d.decodeMove(op, szB)
	case 0x2:
		return d.decodeMove(op, szL)
	case 0x3:
		return d.decodeMove(op, szW)
	case 0x4:
		return d.decodeLine4(op)
	case 0x5:
		return d.decodeLine5(op)
	case 0x6:
		cond := int((op >> 8) & 0xF)
		base := d.start + 2
		var disp int32
		if op&0xFF == 0 {
			disp = int32(int16(d.w()))
		} else {
			disp = int32(int8(uint8(op & 0xFF)))
		}
		target := uint32(int32(base) + disp)
		switch cond {
		case 0:
			return fmt.Sprintf("BRA $%06X", target)
		case 1:
			return fmt.Sprintf("BSR $%06X", target)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("B%s $%06X", disCond[cond], target)
	case 0x7:
		if op&0x0100 != 0 {
			return ""
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("MOVEQ #$%02X,D%d", op&0xFF, (op>>9)&7)
	case 0x8:
		return d.decodeLine8(op)
	case 0x9:
		return d.decodeLine9D(op, "SUB")
	case 0xA, 0xF:
		return "" // line A/F are exception stubs, not instructions
	case 0xB:
		return d.decodeLineB(op)
	case 0xC:
		return d.decodeLineC(op)
	case 0xD:
		return d.decodeLine9D(op, "ADD")
	case 0xE:
		return d.decodeShifts(op)
	}
	return ""
}

func (d *disState) decodeLine0(op uint16) string {
	hi := (op >> 8) & 0xF
	mode, reg := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	size := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	switch hi {
	case 0x0, 0x2, 0x4, 0x6, 0xA, 0xC:
		names := map[uint16]string{0x0: "ORI", 0x2: "ANDI", 0x4: "SUBI",
			0x6: "ADDI", 0xA: "EORI", 0xC: "CMPI"}
		if size == 3 {
			return ""
		}
		if mode == 7 && reg == 4 && (hi == 0x0 || hi == 0x2 || hi == 0xA) {
			switch size {
			case szB:
				v := d.w()
				return fmt.Sprintf("%s #$%02X,CCR", names[hi], v&0xFF)
			case szW:
				v := d.w()
				return fmt.Sprintf("%s #$%04X,SR", names[hi], v)
			}
			return ""
		}
		imm := d.imm(size)
		dst := d.ea(mode, reg, size)
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s %s,%s", names[hi], disSizeSuffix[size], imm, dst)
	case 0x8:
		bops := []string{"BTST", "BCHG", "BCLR", "BSET"}
		bop := bops[(op>>6)&3]
		bit := d.w() & 0xFF
		dst := d.ea(mode, reg, szB)
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s #$%02X,%s", bop, bit, dst)
	default:
		if mode == 1 {
			// MOVEP
			disp := int32(int16(d.w()))
			sz := ".W"
			if op&0x40 != 0 {
				sz = ".L"
			}
			ea := fmt.Sprintf("%s(A%d)", hexDisp(disp), reg)
			if op&0x80 != 0 {
				return fmt.Sprintf("MOVEP%s D%d,%s", sz, (op>>9)&7, ea)
			}
			return fmt.Sprintf("MOVEP%s %s,D%d", sz, ea, (op>>9)&7)
		}
		bops := []string{"BTST", "BCHG", "BCLR", "BSET"}
		dst := d.ea(mode, reg, szB)
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s D%d,%s", bops[(op>>6)&3], (op>>9)&7, dst)
	}
}

func (d *disState) decodeMove(op uint16, size int) string {
	dstReg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
