	dstMode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	srcMode, srcReg := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	src := d.ea(srcMode, srcReg, size)
	dst := d.ea(dstMode, dstReg, size)
	if dstMode == 1 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("MOVEA%s %s,A%d", disSizeSuffix[size], src, dstReg)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("MOVE%s %s,%s", disSizeSuffix[size], src, dst)
}

// movemList renders a MOVEM register mask as a compact list. rev
// selects the predecrement interpretation of the mask bits.
func movemList(mask uint16, rev bool) string {
	var present [16]bool // index: 0-7 = D0-D7, 8-15 = A0-A7
	for j := 0; j < 16; j++ {
		if mask>>uint(j)&1 == 0 {
			continue
		}
		var kind, idx int
		if rev {
			kind, idx = movemRevReg(j)
		} else {
			kind, idx = movemListReg(j)
		}
		if kind == 0 {
			present[idx] = true
		} else {
			present[8+idx] = true
		}
	}
	name := func(i int) string {
		if i < 8 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("D%d", i)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("A%d", i-8)
	}
	out := ""
	for base := 0; base < 16; base += 8 {
		i := base
		for i < base+8 {
			if !present[i] {
				i++
				continue
			}
			j := i
			for j+1 < base+8 && present[j+1] {
				j++
			}
			if out != "" {
				out += "/"
			}
			if j > i {
				out += name(i) + "-" + name(j)
			} else {
				out += name(i)
			}
			i = j + 1
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (d *disState) decodeLine4(op uint16) string {
	bits86 := (op >> 6) & 7
	mode, reg := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	if bits86 == 6 {
		src := d.ea(mode, reg, szW)
		return fmt.Sprintf("CHK.W %s,D%d", src, (op>>9)&7)
	}
	if bits86 == 7 {
		src := d.ea(mode, reg, szW)
		return fmt.Sprintf("LEA %s,A%d", src, (op>>9)&7)
	}
	fam := (op >> 8) & 0xF
	ss := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	switch fam {
	case 0x0:
		if ss == 3 {
			dst := d.ea(mode, reg, szW)
			return fmt.Sprintf("MOVE SR,%s", dst)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("NEGX%s %s", disSizeSuffix[ss], d.ea(mode, reg, ss))
	case 0x2:
		return fmt.Sprintf("CLR%s %s", disSizeSuffix[ss], d.ea(mode, reg, ss))
	case 0x4:
		if ss == 3 {
			src := d.ea(mode, reg, szW)
			return fmt.Sprintf("MOVE %s,CCR", src)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("NEG%s %s", disSizeSuffix[ss], d.ea(mode, reg, ss))
	case 0x6:
		if ss == 3 {
			src := d.ea(mode, reg, szW)
			return fmt.Sprintf("MOVE %s,SR", src)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("NOT%s %s", disSizeSuffix[ss], d.ea(mode, reg, ss))
	case 0x8:
		if op&0x0080 != 0 && mode != 0 {
			mask := d.w()
			dst := d.ea(mode, reg, szW)
			sz := ".W"
			if op&0x40 != 0 {
				sz = ".L"
			}
			return fmt.Sprintf("MOVEM%s %s,%s", sz, movemList(mask, mode == 4), dst)
		}
		switch ss {
		case 0:
			return fmt.Sprintf("NBCD %s", d.ea(mode, reg, szB))
		case 1:
			if mode == 0 {
				return fmt.Sprintf("SWAP D%d", reg)
			}
			return fmt.Sprintf("PEA %s", d.ea(mode, reg, szW))
		case 2:
			return fmt.Sprintf("EXT.W D%d", reg)
		case 3:
			return fmt.Sprintf("EXT.L D%d", reg)
		}
	case 0xA:
		if ss == 3 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("TAS %s", d.ea(mode, reg, szB))
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("TST%s %s", disSizeSuffix[ss], d.ea(mode, reg, ss))
	case 0xC:
		if op&0x0080 != 0 {
			mask := d.w()
			src := d.ea(mode, reg, szW)
			sz := ".W"
			if op&0x40 != 0 {
				sz = ".L"
			}
			return fmt.Sprintf("MOVEM%s %s,%s", sz, src, movemList(mask, false))
		}
		return ""
	case 0xE:
		switch ss {
		case 1:
			return d.decodeLine4Control(op)
		case 2:
			return fmt.Sprintf("JSR %s", d.ea(mode, reg, szW))
		case 3:
			return fmt.Sprintf("JMP %s", d.ea(mode, reg, szW))
		}
		return ""
	}
	return ""
}

func (d *disState) decodeLine4Control(op uint16) string {
	switch {
	case op&0xFFF0 == 0x4E40:
		return fmt.Sprintf("TRAP #%d", op&0xF)
	case op&0xFFF8 == 0x4E50:
		disp := d.w()
		return fmt.Sprintf("LINK A%d,#$%04X", op&7, disp)
	case op&0xFFF8 == 0x4E58:
		return fmt.Sprintf("UNLK A%d", op&7)
	case op&0xFFF0 == 0x4E60:
		if op&0x8 != 0 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("MOVE.L USP,A%d", op&7)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("MOVE.L A%d,USP", op&7)
	case op == 0x4E70:
		return "RESET"
	case op == 0x4E71:
		return "NOP"
	case op == 0x4E72:
		return fmt.Sprintf("STOP #$%04X", d.w())
	case op == 0x4E73:
		return "RTE"
	case op == 0x4E75:
		return "RTS"
	case op == 0x4E76:
		return "TRAPV"
	case op == 0x4E77:
		return "RTR"
	}
	return ""
}

func (d *disState) decodeLine5(op uint16) string {
	mode, reg := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	cond := int((op >> 8) & 0xF)
	if (op>>6)&3 == 3 {
		if mode == 1 {
			disp := int32(int16(d.w()))
			target := uint32(int32(d.start+2) + disp)
			return fmt.Sprintf("DB%s D%d,$%06X", disCond[cond], reg, target)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("S%s %s", disCond[cond], d.ea(mode, reg, szB))
	}
	data := (op >> 9) & 7
	if data == 0 {
		data = 8
	}
	name := "ADDQ"
	if op&0x0100 != 0 {
		name = "SUBQ"
	}
	size := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s #%d,%s", name, disSizeSuffix[size], data, d.ea(mode, reg, size))
}

// twoOperand formats a line 8/9/B/C/D instruction in its <ea>,Dn form.
func (d *disState) twoReg(op uint16, name string, size int) string {
	mode, reg := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	src := d.ea(mode, reg, size)
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s %s,D%d", name, disSizeSuffix[size], src, (op>>9)&7)
}

// twoMem formats the Dn,<ea> (destination EA) form.
func (d *disState) twoMem(op uint16, name string, size int) string {
	mode, reg := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	dst := d.ea(mode, reg, size)
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s D%d,%s", name, disSizeSuffix[size], (op>>9)&7, dst)
}

// bcdOperands formats the register or predecrement operand pair used by
// ABCD/SBCD/ADDX/SUBX (source first).
func bcdOperands(op uint16) string {
	src := int(op & 7)
	dst := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	if (op>>3)&1 != 0 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("-(A%d),-(A%d)", src, dst)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("D%d,D%d", src, dst)
}

func (d *disState) decodeLine8(op uint16) string {
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	switch {
	case opmode == 3:
		return fmt.Sprintf("DIVU.W %s,D%d", d.ea(mode, r, szW), reg)
	case opmode == 7:
		return fmt.Sprintf("DIVS.W %s,D%d", d.ea(mode, r, szW), reg)
	case opmode >= 4 && mode <= 1:
		return fmt.Sprintf("SBCD %s", bcdOperands(op))
	case opmode <= 2:
		return d.twoReg(op, "OR", opmode)
	default:
		return d.twoMem(op, "OR", opmode-4)
	}
}

func (d *disState) decodeLine9D(op uint16, name string) string {
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	switch {
	case opmode == 3:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%sA.W %s,A%d", name, d.ea(mode, r, szW), reg)
	case opmode == 7:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%sA.L %s,A%d", name, d.ea(mode, r, szL), reg)
	case opmode >= 4 && mode <= 1:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%sX%s %s", name, disSizeSuffix[opmode-4], bcdOperands(op))
	case opmode <= 2:
		return d.twoReg(op, name, opmode)
	default:
		return d.twoMem(op, name, opmode-4)
	}
}

func (d *disState) decodeLineB(op uint16) string {
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	switch {
	case opmode == 3:
		return fmt.Sprintf("CMPA.W %s,A%d", d.ea(mode, r, szW), reg)
	case opmode == 7:
		return fmt.Sprintf("CMPA.L %s,A%d", d.ea(mode, r, szL), reg)
	case opmode <= 2:
		return d.twoReg(op, "CMP", opmode)
	case mode == 1 && opmode >= 4:
		return fmt.Sprintf("CMPM%s (A%d)+,(A%d)+", disSizeSuffix[opmode-4], r, reg)
	default:
		return d.twoMem(op, "EOR", opmode-4)
	}
}

func (d *disState) decodeLineC(op uint16) string {
	switch {
	case op&0xF1F8 == 0xC140:
		return fmt.Sprintf("EXG D%d,D%d", (op>>9)&7, op&7)
	case op&0xF1F8 == 0xC148:
		return fmt.Sprintf("EXG A%d,A%d", (op>>9)&7, op&7)
	case op&0xF1F8 == 0xC188:
		return fmt.Sprintf("EXG D%d,A%d", (op>>9)&7, op&7)
	}
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
	switch {
	case opmode == 3:
		return fmt.Sprintf("MULU.W %s,D%d", d.ea(mode, r, szW), reg)
	case opmode == 7:
		return fmt.Sprintf("MULS.W %s,D%d", d.ea(mode, r, szW), reg)
	case opmode >= 4 && mode <= 1:
		return fmt.Sprintf("ABCD %s", bcdOperands(op))
	case opmode <= 2:
		return d.twoReg(op, "AND", opmode)
	default:
		return d.twoMem(op, "AND", opmode-4)
	}
}

func (d *disState) decodeShifts(op uint16) string {
	names := [4][2]string{
		{"ASR", "ASL"},
		{"LSR", "LSL"},
		{"ROXR", "ROXL"},
		{"ROR", "ROL"},
	}
	if (op>>6)&3 == 3 {
		typ := int((op >> 9) & 3)
		dir := int((op >> 8) & 1)
		mode, reg := int((op>>3)&7), int(op&7)
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s", names[typ][dir], d.ea(mode, reg, szW))
	}
	cntField := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	dir := int((op >> 8) & 1)
	size := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	typ := int((op >> 3) & 3)
	reg := int(op & 7)
	var cnt string
	if op&0x20 != 0 {
		cnt = fmt.Sprintf("D%d", cntField)
	} else {
		n := cntField
		if n == 0 {
			n = 8
		}
		cnt = fmt.Sprintf("#%d", n)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s%s %s,D%d", names[typ][dir], disSizeSuffix[size], cnt, reg)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k/ea.go ====================

package m68k

// Effective-address machinery. The 68000 has 14 addressing modes,
// encoded as a 3-bit mode plus a 3-bit register field:
//
//	000 Dn        data register direct      001 An  address register direct
//	010 (An)      register indirect         011 (An)+   indirect postincrement
//	100 -(An)     indirect predecrement     101 (d16,An)  indirect + displacement
//	110 (d8,An,Xn) indirect + index + disp  111 special: 000 (xxx).W, 001 (xxx).L,
//	                                             010 (d16,PC), 011 (d8,PC,Xn),
//	                                             100 #imm immediate
//
// An operand is resolved once: the address is computed (extension words
// consumed, predecrement applied) and a pending postincrement is
// recorded for the caller to commit after the access, which matches the
// hardware order (a read-modify-write to (An)+ stores to the address
// computed before the increment).

type operand struct {
	mode, reg int
	addr      uint32 // effective address for memory operands
	imm       uint32 // immediate value (mode 7, reg 4)
	post      int    // pending postincrement for the address register
	cyc       int    // documented EA calculation cycles at the operand size
}

// eaFetchCycles is the manual's effective-address calculation time
// table: (byte/word, long) per mode.
func eaFetchCycles(mode, reg int, size int) int {
	long := size == szL
	pick := func(w, l int) int {
		if long {
			return l
		}
		return w
	}
	switch mode {
	case 0, 1:
		return 0
	case 2, 3:
		return pick(4, 8)
	case 4:
		return pick(6, 10)
	case 5:
		return pick(8, 12)
	case 6:
		return pick(10, 14)
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			return pick(8, 12)
		case 1:
			return pick(12, 16)
		case 2:
			return pick(8, 12)
		case 3:
			return pick(10, 14)
		case 4:
			return pick(4, 8)
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// leaCycles is the manual's LEA timing per control mode (also used for
// PEA at +8 and JMP/JSR from their own tables below).
func leaCycles(mode, reg int) int {
	switch mode {
	case 2:
		return 4
	case 5:
		return 8
	case 6:
		return 12
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0, 2: // (xxx).W, (d16,PC)
			return 8
		case 1, 3: // (xxx).L, (d8,PC,Xn)
			return 12
		}
	}
	return 0
}

func jmpCycles(mode, reg int) int {
	switch mode {
	case 2:
		return 8
	case 5:
		return 10
	case 6:
		return 14
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			return 10
		case 1:
			return 12
		case 2:
			return 10
		case 3:
			return 14
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// Addressing-class predicates, from the manual's per-instruction EA
// tables. Instructions reject operands outside their class with the
// illegal-instruction exception before any extension word is read (the
// class is fully determined by the opcode bits).
func eaReadable(mode, reg int) bool { return mode <= 6 || (mode == 7 && reg <= 4) }

func eaAlterableMem(mode, reg int) bool {
	return (mode >= 2 && mode <= 6) || (mode == 7 && reg <= 1)
}

func eaDataAlterable(mode, reg int) bool {
	return mode == 0 || eaAlterableMem(mode, reg)
}

func eaControl(mode, reg int) bool {
	return mode == 2 || mode == 5 || mode == 6 || (mode == 7 && reg <= 3)
}

// indexEA computes the register-indirect-with-index address. base is
// the address register (or PC) value; the extension word is read from
// the instruction stream at the current PC, which for the PC-relative
// form is also the displacement base the hardware uses. Index format
// (brief, the only form the 68000 has): D/A select, register, W/L
// select, three zero bits (no scaling on the 68000), signed 8-bit
// displacement.
func (c *CPU) indexEA(base uint32) uint32 {
	ext := c.fetch16()
	idxReg := (ext >> 12) & 7
	var idx uint32
	if ext&0x8000 != 0 {
		idx = c.a[idxReg]
	} else {
		idx = c.d[idxReg]
	}
	if ext&0x0800 == 0 {
		idx = uint32(int32(int16(uint16(idx)))) // word index, sign-extended
	}
	disp := int32(int8(uint8(ext & 0xFF)))
	return base + uint32(disp) + idx
}

// resolveEA computes an operand at the given size (szB/szW/szL),
// consuming extension words and applying predecrement. It panics with
// illegalEncoding for the nonexistent special modes (111 reg 5+).
func (c *CPU) resolveEA(mode, reg, size int) operand {
	o := operand{mode: mode, reg: reg, cyc: eaFetchCycles(mode, reg, size)}
	switch mode {
	case 0, 1:
		// Register direct: no address.
	case 2:
		o.addr = c.a[reg]
	case 3:
		o.addr = c.a[reg]
		n := sizeBytes(size)
		if reg == 7 && size == szB {
			n = 2 // the stack-pointer byte quirk: A7 always moves by 2
		}
		o.post = n
	case 4:
		n := sizeBytes(size)
		if reg == 7 && size == szB {
			n = 2
		}
		c.a[reg] -= uint32(n)
		o.addr = c.a[reg]
	case 5:
		d := int32(int16(c.fetch16()))
		o.addr = c.a[reg] + uint32(d)
	case 6:
		o.addr = c.indexEA(c.a[reg])
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0: // (xxx).W, sign-extended
			o.addr = uint32(int32(int16(c.fetch16())))
		case 1: // (xxx).L
			o.addr = c.fetch32()
		case 2: // (d16,PC): displacement base is the extension word's address
			extAddr := c.pc
			d := int32(int16(c.fetch16()))
			o.addr = extAddr + uint32(d)
		case 3: // (d8,PC,Xn)
			o.addr = c.indexEA(c.pc)
		case 4: // #imm
			switch size {
			case szB:
				o.imm = uint32(c.fetch16() & 0xFF)
			case szW:
				o.imm = uint32(c.fetch16())
			case szL:
				o.imm = c.fetch32()
			}
		default:
			panic(illegalEncoding{})
		}
	}
	return o
}

// readMem reads a byte/word/long operand from memory.
func (c *CPU) readMem(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case szB:
		return uint32(c.rd8(addr))
	case szW:
		return uint32(c.rd16(addr))
	default:
		return c.rd32(addr)
	}
}

// writeMem writes a byte/word/long operand to memory.
func (c *CPU) writeMem(addr uint32, size int, v uint32) {
	switch size {
	case szB:
		c.wr8(addr, uint8(v))
	case szW:
		c.wr16(addr, uint16(v))
	default:
		c.wr32(addr, v)
	}
}

// opRead reads an operand's value at the given size. Register-direct
// reads return the register masked to the operand size. The pending
// postincrement is NOT applied; use readSrc for source operands, or
// commitPost after a read-modify-write completes.
func (c *CPU) opRead(o operand, size int) uint32 {
	if o.mode == 0 {
		return c.d[o.reg] & sizeMask(size)
	}
	if o.mode == 1 {
		return c.a[o.reg] & sizeMask(size)
	}
	if o.mode == 7 && o.reg == 4 {
		return o.imm
	}
	return c.readMem(o.addr, size)
}

// readSrc reads a source operand and applies its postincrement,
// matching the hardware order for operand fetch.
func (c *CPU) readSrc(o operand, size int) uint32 {
	v := c.opRead(o, size)
	c.commitPost(o)
	return v
}

// opWrite writes a value to an operand at the given size and applies
// its postincrement. Data-register writes merge at byte/word size;
// address-register word writes sign-extend into the full register, as
// the hardware does.
func (c *CPU) opWrite(o operand, size int, v uint32) {
	switch o.mode {
	case 0:
		switch size {
		case szB:
			c.d[o.reg] = (c.d[o.reg] &^ 0xFF) | (v & 0xFF)
		case szW:
			c.d[o.reg] = (c.d[o.reg] &^ 0xFFFF) | (v & 0xFFFF)
		case szL:
			c.d[o.reg] = v
		}
	case 1:
		switch size {
		case szW:
			c.a[o.reg] = uint32(int32(int16(uint16(v))))
		case szL:
			c.a[o.reg] = v
		}
	default:
		c.writeMem(o.addr, size, v)
	}
	c.commitPost(o)
}

// commitPost applies a resolved operand's pending postincrement.
func (c *CPU) commitPost(o operand) {
	if o.post != 0 {
		c.a[o.reg] += uint32(o.post)
	}
}

// signExtend widens a value of the given size to 32 bits, signed.
func signExtend(v uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case szB:
		return uint32(int32(int8(uint8(v))))
	case szW:
		return uint32(int32(int16(uint16(v))))
	default:
		return v
	}
}

// eaFields splits an opcode's low 6 bits into mode and register.
func eaFields(op uint16) (mode, reg int) {
	return int((op >> 3) & 7), int(op & 7)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k/exec.go ====================

package m68k

// Instruction decode and execution. The 68000 opcode space is organized
// in 16 lines by the top nibble; the dispatcher mirrors that map, and
// each line decoder applies the manual's rules for its family,
// including which addressing modes are legal (an operand outside its
// instruction's class raises the illegal-instruction exception).

// execute runs one already-fetched opcode and returns its cycle count.
// Exceptions raised by the instruction itself (TRAP, CHK, divide by
// zero, privilege violation, ...) return their entry cost as the total.
func (c *CPU) execute(op uint16) int {
	switch op >> 12 {
	case 0x0:
		return c.execLine0(op)
	case 0x1:
		return c.execMove(op, szB)
	case 0x2:
		return c.execMove(op, szL)
	case 0x3:
		return c.execMove(op, szW)
	case 0x4:
		return c.execLine4(op)
	case 0x5:
		return c.execLine5(op)
	case 0x6:
		return c.execBranch(op)
	case 0x7:
		return c.execMoveQ(op)
	case 0x8:
		return c.execLine8(op)
	case 0x9:
		return c.execLine9D(op, false) // SUB family
	case 0xA:
		return c.enterExceptionAt(vecLineA, c.instrPC, 34)
	case 0xB:
		return c.execLineB(op)
	case 0xC:
		return c.execLineC(op)
	case 0xD:
		return c.execLine9D(op, true) // ADD family
	case 0xE:
		return c.execShifts(op)
	case 0xF:
		return c.enterExceptionAt(vecLineF, c.instrPC, 34)
	}
	return c.illegal(op)
}

func (c *CPU) illegal(op uint16) int { return c.enterExceptionAt(vecIllegal, c.instrPC, 34) }
func (c *CPU) privilege() int        { return c.enterExceptionAt(vecPrivilege, c.instrPC, 34) }
func (c *CPU) supervisor() bool      { return c.sr&srS != 0 }

// --- line 0: immediate ops, bit ops, MOVEP --------------------------

func (c *CPU) execLine0(op uint16) int {
	hi := (op >> 8) & 0xF // bits 11-8
	mode, reg := eaFields(op)
	size := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	switch hi {
	case 0x0, 0x2, 0xA: // ORI, ANDI, EORI
		if size == 3 {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		return c.execLogicImm(op, hi, mode, reg, size)
	case 0x4, 0x6, 0xC: // SUBI, ADDI, CMPI
		if size == 3 {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		return c.execArithImm(op, hi, mode, reg, size)
	case 0x8: // static bit ops: bit number from an extension word
		bop := int((op >> 6) & 3)
		bitNum := uint32(c.fetch16() & 0xFF)
		return c.execBitOp(op, bop, bitNum, mode, reg, true)
	default: // hi odd: bit 8 set -> MOVEP or dynamic bit op
		if mode == 1 {
			return c.execMoveP(op)
		}
		bop := int((op >> 6) & 3)
		bitNum := c.d[(op>>9)&7]
		return c.execBitOp(op, bop, bitNum, mode, reg, false)
	}
}

// execLogicImm implements ORI/ANDI/EORI, including the immediate-to-CCR
// and immediate-to-SR forms (EA field 111100). The SR forms are
// privileged. kind: 0x0 ORI, 0x2 ANDI, 0xA EORI (bits 11-8 of the opcode).
func (c *CPU) execLogicImm(op uint16, kind uint16, mode, reg, size int) int {
	if mode == 7 && reg == 4 {
		// Immediate operand is the extension word itself; byte size
		// targets the CCR, word size targets the SR.
		switch size {
		case szB:
			v := c.fetch16() & 0xFF
			ccr := uint16(c.sr & 0xFF)
			switch kind {
			case 0x0:
				ccr |= v
			case 0x2:
				ccr &= v
			case 0xA:
				ccr ^= v
			}
			c.setCCR(ccr)
			return 20
		case szW:
			v := c.fetch16()
			if !c.supervisor() {
				return c.privilege()
			}
			var nv uint16
			switch kind {
			case 0x0:
				nv = c.sr | v
			case 0x2:
				nv = c.sr & v
			case 0xA:
				nv = c.sr ^ v
			}
			c.applySR(nv)
			return 20
		}
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	var imm uint32
	switch size {
	case szB:
		imm = uint32(c.fetch16() & 0xFF)
	case szW:
		imm = uint32(c.fetch16())
	case szL:
		imm = c.fetch32()
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	v := c.opRead(o, size)
	var res uint32
	switch kind {
	case 0x0:
		res = v | imm
	case 0x2:
		res = v & imm
	case 0xA:
		res = v ^ imm
	}
	res &= sizeMask(size)
	c.flagsLogic(res, size)
	c.opWrite(o, size, res)
	if mode == 0 {
		if size == szL {
			return 12
		}
		return 8
	}
	if size == szL {
		return 20 + o.cyc
	}
	return 12 + o.cyc
}

// execArithImm implements SUBI/ADDI/CMPI. kind: 0x4 SUBI, 0x6 ADDI,
// 0xC CMPI (bits 11-8 of the opcode).
func (c *CPU) execArithImm(op uint16, kind uint16, mode, reg, size int) int {
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	var imm uint32
	switch size {
	case szB:
		imm = uint32(c.fetch16() & 0xFF)
	case szW:
		imm = uint32(c.fetch16())
	case szL:
		imm = c.fetch32()
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	v := c.opRead(o, size)
	switch kind {
	case 0x4: // SUBI
		res := c.flagsSub(v, imm, size, 0, false)
		c.opWrite(o, size, res)
	case 0x6: // ADDI
		res := c.flagsAdd(v, imm, size, 0, false)
		c.opWrite(o, size, res)
	case 0xC: // CMPI
		c.flagsCmp(v, imm, size)
		c.commitPost(o)
	}
	if mode == 0 {
		if size == szL {
			return 12
		}
		return 8
	}
	if size == szL {
		return 20 + o.cyc
	}
	return 12 + o.cyc
}

// execBitOp implements BTST/BCHG/BCLR/BSET for both the static
// (immediate bit number) and dynamic (register bit number) forms.
// bop: 0 BTST, 1 BCHG, 2 BCLR, 3 BSET. Only Z is affected: it is set to
// the complement of the tested bit.
func (c *CPU) execBitOp(op uint16, bop int, bitNum uint32, mode, reg int, static bool) int {
	if mode == 0 {
		// Data register: the bit number is modulo 32.
		bit := bitNum & 31
		old := c.d[reg]
		c.sr &^= srZ
		if (old>>bit)&1 == 0 {
			c.sr |= srZ
		}
		switch bop {
		case 1:
			old ^= uint32(1) << bit
		case 2:
			old &^= uint32(1) << bit
		case 3:
			old |= uint32(1) << bit
		}
		if bop != 0 {
			c.d[reg] = old
		}
		// Documented: BTST 6 (dynamic) or 10 (static); others 8.
		if bop == 0 {
			if static {
				return 10
			}
			return 6
		}
		return 8
	}
	// Memory: byte operand, bit number modulo 8.
	if bop == 0 {
		if !eaReadable(mode, reg) || (mode == 7 && reg == 4) {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
	} else if !eaAlterableMem(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szB)
	bit := bitNum & 7
	if bop == 0 {
		v := c.readSrc(o, szB)
		c.sr &^= srZ
		if (v>>bit)&1 == 0 {
			c.sr |= srZ
		}
		// Documented: 4 + EA (dynamic) or 8 + EA (static).
		if static {
			return 8 + o.cyc
		}
		return 4 + o.cyc
	}
	v := c.opRead(o, szB)
	c.sr &^= srZ
	if (v>>bit)&1 == 0 {
		c.sr |= srZ
	}
	switch bop {
	case 1:
		v ^= uint32(1) << bit
	case 2:
		v &^= uint32(1) << bit
	case 3:
		v |= uint32(1) << bit
	}
	c.opWrite(o, szB, v)
	return 8 + o.cyc
}

// execMoveP implements MOVEP: a register-to-memory transfer that moves
// a word or long one byte at a time to every other byte address,
// starting at (d16,An). Direction bit 7: 0 = memory to register,
// 1 = register to memory. Size bit 6: 0 = word, 1 = long.
func (c *CPU) execMoveP(op uint16) int {
	dreg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	areg := int(op & 7)
	disp := int32(int16(c.fetch16()))
	addr := c.a[areg] + uint32(disp)
	n := 2
	if op&0x40 != 0 {
		n = 4
	}
	if op&0x80 != 0 {
		// Register to memory, most significant byte first.
		v := c.d[dreg]
		shift := uint((n - 1) * 8)
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			c.wr8(addr+uint32(2*i), uint8(v>>shift))
			shift -= 8
		}
	} else {
		// Memory to register.
		var v uint32
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			v = (v << 8) | uint32(c.rd8(addr+uint32(2*i)))
		}
		if n == 2 {
			c.d[dreg] = (c.d[dreg] &^ 0xFFFF) | v
		} else {
			c.d[dreg] = v
		}
	}
	if n == 4 {
		return 24
	}
	return 16
}

// --- MOVE / MOVEA ----------------------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execMove(op uint16, size int) int {
	dstReg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	dstMode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	srcMode, srcReg := eaFields(op)
	if dstMode == 1 && size == szB {
		return c.illegal(op) // MOVE.B to an address register
	}
	if dstMode == 7 && dstReg > 1 {
		return c.illegal(op) // destination must be alterable memory
	}
	src := c.resolveEA(srcMode, srcReg, size)
	v := c.readSrc(src, size)
	dst := c.resolveEA(dstMode, dstReg, size)
	if dstMode == 1 {
		// MOVEA: no flags; a word source sign-extends.
		if size == szW {
			c.a[dstReg] = uint32(int32(int16(uint16(v))))
		} else {
			c.a[dstReg] = v
		}
		return 4 + src.cyc + dst.cyc
	}
	c.opWrite(dst, size, v)
	c.flagsLogic(v, size)
	return 4 + src.cyc + dst.cyc
}

// --- line 4: the miscellaneous group ---------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execLine4(op uint16) int {
	bits86 := (op >> 6) & 7 // bits 8-6
	mode, reg := eaFields(op)
	if bits86 == 6 {
		return c.execChk(op, mode, reg)
	}
	if bits86 == 7 {
		// LEA
		dstReg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
		if !eaControl(mode, reg) {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
		c.a[dstReg] = o.addr
		return leaCycles(mode, reg)
	}
	fam := (op >> 8) & 0xF
	ss := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	switch fam {
	case 0x0:
		if ss == 3 {
			return c.execMoveFromSR(op, mode, reg)
		}
		return c.execUnary(op, ss, mode, reg, unaryNegx)
	case 0x2:
		return c.execUnary(op, ss, mode, reg, unaryClr)
	case 0x4:
		if ss == 3 {
			return c.execMoveToCCR(op, mode, reg)
		}
		return c.execUnary(op, ss, mode, reg, unaryNeg)
	case 0x6:
		if ss == 3 {
			return c.execMoveToSR(op, mode, reg)
		}
		return c.execUnary(op, ss, mode, reg, unaryNot)
	case 0x8:
		// Bit 7 set with a non-register EA is MOVEM (registers to
		// memory); with a register-direct EA the same bit pattern is
		// EXT.W/EXT.L, whose mode field is always 000.
		if op&0x0080 != 0 && mode != 0 {
			return c.execMovem(op, false)
		}
		switch ss {
		case 0:
			return c.execNBCD(op, mode, reg)
		case 1:
			if mode == 0 {
				// SWAP
				v := c.d[reg]
				v = (v << 16) | (v >> 16)
				c.d[reg] = v
				c.flagsLogic(v, szL)
				return 4
			}
			// PEA
			if !eaControl(mode, reg) {
				return c.illegal(op)
			}
			o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
			c.push32(o.addr)
			return leaCycles(mode, reg) + 8
		case 2: // EXT.W
			if mode != 0 {
				return c.illegal(op)
			}
			v := uint32(int32(int8(uint8(c.d[reg]))))
			c.d[reg] = (c.d[reg] &^ 0xFFFF) | (v & 0xFFFF)
			c.flagsLogic(v, szW)
			return 4
		case 3: // EXT.L
			if mode != 0 {
				return c.illegal(op)
			}
			v := uint32(int32(int16(uint16(c.d[reg]))))
			c.d[reg] = v
			c.flagsLogic(v, szL)
			return 4
		}
	case 0xA:
		if ss == 3 {
			return c.execTAS(op, mode, reg)
		}
		return c.execTST(op, ss, mode, reg)
	case 0xC:
		if op&0x0080 != 0 {
			return c.execMovem(op, true)
		}
		return c.illegal(op)
	case 0xE:
		switch ss {
		case 1:
			return c.execLine4Control(op)
		case 2: // JSR
			if !eaControl(mode, reg) {
				return c.illegal(op)
			}
			o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
			c.push32(c.pc)
			c.pc = o.addr
			return jmpCycles(mode, reg) + 8
		case 3: // JMP
			if !eaControl(mode, reg) {
				return c.illegal(op)
			}
			o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
			c.pc = o.addr
			return jmpCycles(mode, reg)
		}
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	return c.illegal(op)
}

// execLine4Control decodes the 0100 1110 01xx xxxx group: TRAP, LINK,
// UNLK, MOVE to/from USP, and the fixed control instructions.
func (c *CPU) execLine4Control(op uint16) int {
	switch {
	case op&0xFFF0 == 0x4E40: // TRAP #vector
		return c.enterException(32+int(op&0xF), 34)
	case op&0xFFF8 == 0x4E50: // LINK
		reg := int(op & 7)
		disp := int32(int16(c.fetch16()))
		c.push32(c.a[reg])
		c.a[reg] = c.a[7]
		c.a[7] += uint32(disp)
		return 16
	case op&0xFFF8 == 0x4E58: // UNLK
		reg := int(op & 7)
		c.a[7] = c.a[reg]
		c.a[reg] = c.pop32()
		return 12
	case op&0xFFF0 == 0x4E60: // MOVE USP (privileged)
		if !c.supervisor() {
			return c.privilege()
		}
		reg := int(op & 7)
		if op&0x8 != 0 {
			c.a[reg] = c.uspValue()
		} else {
			c.setUSPValue(c.a[reg])
		}
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E70: // RESET (privileged; the external reset line is not modeled)
		if !c.supervisor() {
			return c.privilege()
		}
		return 132
	case op == 0x4E71: // NOP
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E72: // STOP (privileged)
		imm := c.fetch16()
		if !c.supervisor() {
			return c.privilege()
		}
		c.applySR(imm)
		c.stopped = true
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E73: // RTE (privileged)
		if !c.supervisor() {
			return c.privilege()
		}
		newSR := c.rd16(c.a[7])
		newPC := c.rd32(c.a[7] + 2)
		c.a[7] += 6
		c.applySR(newSR)
		c.pc = newPC
		return 20
	case op == 0x4E75: // RTS
		c.pc = c.pop32()
		return 16
	case op == 0x4E76: // TRAPV
		if c.sr&srV != 0 {
			return c.enterException(vecTRAPV, 34)
		}
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E77: // RTR
		ccr := c.pop16()
		c.setCCR(ccr)
		c.pc = c.pop32()
		return 20
	}
	return c.illegal(op)
}

// uspValue/sspValue read and write the inactive-pointer storage,
// treating the active A7 correctly when the CPU is in user mode.
func (c *CPU) uspValue() uint32 {
	if c.sr&srS == 0 {
		return c.a[7]
	}
	return c.usp
}

func (c *CPU) setUSPValue(v uint32) {
	if c.sr&srS == 0 {
		c.a[7] = v
	} else {
		c.usp = v
	}
}

// execChk implements CHK (word form, the only size on the 68000): if
// the low word of Dn is negative or greater than the source operand,
// the CHK exception (vector 6) is taken, with N set exactly when the
// register was negative. The manual leaves Z, V and C undefined for
// CHK; on the trap path they are cleared here so the stacked frame
// is deterministic (this matches the observable behavior of the
// reference implementation the core was differential-tested against).
func (c *CPU) execChk(op uint16, mode, reg int) int {
	dstReg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	if !eaReadable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
	upper := int16(uint16(c.readSrc(o, szW)))
	dv := int16(uint16(c.d[dstReg]))
	if dv < 0 {
		c.sr = (c.sr | srN) &^ (srZ | srV | srC)
		return c.enterException(vecCHK, 44)
	}
	if dv > upper {
		c.sr &^= srN | srZ | srV | srC
		return c.enterException(vecCHK, 44)
	}
	// No trap: N is clear (the value is non-negative here by
	// construction), Z records equality with the bound, and V and C
	// are cleared; X is preserved. The manual leaves CHK's Z, V and C
	// undefined; a flag probe against the reference implementation
	// (grid over values, bounds and preset CCR) showed exactly this
	// rule, including in the stacked frame on the trap path.
	c.sr &^= srN | srZ | srV | srC
	if dv == upper {
		c.sr |= srZ
	}
	return 12 + o.cyc
}

type unaryKind int

const (
	unaryNegx unaryKind = iota
	unaryClr
	unaryNeg
	unaryNot
)

// execUnary implements NEGX, CLR, NEG and NOT against a data-alterable
// operand.
func (c *CPU) execUnary(op uint16, size int, mode, reg int, kind unaryKind) int {
	if size > szL {
		return c.illegal(op) // the ss == 11 encodings are the SR moves, handled by callers
	}
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	v := c.opRead(o, size)
	var res uint32
	switch kind {
	case unaryNegx:
		res = c.flagsSub(0, v, size, c.xBit(), true)
	case unaryClr:
		res = 0
		c.sr = (c.sr &^ (srN | srV | srC)) | srZ
	case unaryNeg:
		res = c.flagsSub(0, v, size, 0, false)
	case unaryNot:
		res = (^v) & sizeMask(size)
		c.flagsLogic(res, size)
	}
	c.opWrite(o, size, res)
	if mode == 0 {
		if size == szL {
			return 6
		}
		return 4
	}
	if size == szL {
		return 12 + o.cyc
	}
	return 8 + o.cyc
}

func (c *CPU) execMoveFromSR(op uint16, mode, reg int) int {
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
	c.opWrite(o, szW, uint32(c.sr))
	if mode == 0 {
		return 6
	}
	return 8 + o.cyc
}

func (c *CPU) execMoveToCCR(op uint16, mode, reg int) int {
	if !eaReadable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
	v := c.readSrc(o, szW)
	c.setCCR(uint16(v))
	return 12 + o.cyc
}

func (c *CPU) execMoveToSR(op uint16, mode, reg int) int {
	if !eaReadable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
	v := c.readSrc(o, szW)
	if !c.supervisor() {
		return c.privilege()
	}
	c.applySR(uint16(v))
	return 12 + o.cyc
}

// execNBCD implements NBCD: 0 - operand - X in BCD.
func (c *CPU) execNBCD(op uint16, mode, reg int) int {
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szB)
	v := c.opRead(o, szB)
	res := c.bcdSub(0, v)
	c.opWrite(o, szB, res)
	if mode == 0 {
		return 6
	}
	return 8 + o.cyc
}

// execTAS implements TAS: test a byte (N/Z from it, V and C cleared)
// and set its high bit. The official ILLEGAL opcode (0x4AFC) shares the
// TAS encoding with an immediate operand and raises vector 4.
func (c *CPU) execTAS(op uint16, mode, reg int) int {
	if mode == 7 && reg == 4 {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szB)
	v := c.opRead(o, szB)
	c.flagsLogic(v, szB)
	c.opWrite(o, szB, v|0x80)
	if mode == 0 {
		return 4
	}
	return 10 + o.cyc
}

// execTST implements TST. On the base 68000 the operand class is data
// registers and alterable memory (no address register, PC-relative, or
// immediate forms).
func (c *CPU) execTST(op uint16, size int, mode, reg int) int {
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	v := c.readSrc(o, size)
	c.flagsLogic(v, size)
	return 4 + o.cyc
}

// --- line 5: ADDQ/SUBQ, Scc, DBcc ------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execLine5(op uint16) int {
	mode, reg := eaFields(op)
	cond := int((op >> 8) & 0xF)
	if (op>>6)&3 == 3 {
		if mode == 1 {
			// DBcc: if the condition is false, decrement the low word
			// of Dn and branch unless it reached -1.
			base := c.pc
			disp := int32(int16(c.fetch16()))
			if c.condTrue(cond) {
				return 12
			}
			low := uint16(c.d[reg]) - 1
			c.d[reg] = (c.d[reg] &^ 0xFFFF) | uint32(low)
			if low != 0xFFFF {
				c.pc = uint32(int32(base) + disp)
				return 10
			}
			return 14
		}
		// Scc
		if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szB)
		var v uint32
		if c.condTrue(cond) {
			v = 0xFF
		}
		c.opWrite(o, szB, v)
		if mode == 0 {
			if v != 0 {
				return 4
			}
			return 6
		}
		return 8 + o.cyc
	}
	// ADDQ/SUBQ
	data := uint32((op >> 9) & 7)
	if data == 0 {
		data = 8
	}
	size := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	sub := op&0x0100 != 0
	if mode == 1 {
		// Quick ops to An: no flags, word and long only.
		if size == szB {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		if sub {
			c.a[reg] -= data
		} else {
			c.a[reg] += data
		}
		if size == szL {
			return 8
		}
		return 4
	}
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	v := c.opRead(o, size)
	var res uint32
	if sub {
		res = c.flagsSub(v, data, size, 0, false)
	} else {
		res = c.flagsAdd(v, data, size, 0, false)
	}
	c.opWrite(o, size, res)
	if mode == 0 {
		if size == szL {
			return 8
		}
		return 4
	}
	if size == szL {
		return 12 + o.cyc
	}
	return 8 + o.cyc
}

// --- line 6: branches -------------------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execBranch(op uint16) int {
	cond := int((op >> 8) & 0xF)
	base := c.pc // displacement base: the word after the opcode
	disp8 := int8(uint8(op & 0xFF))
	var disp int32
	notTaken := 8
	if disp8 == 0 {
		disp = int32(int16(c.fetch16()))
		notTaken = 12
	} else {
		disp = int32(disp8)
	}
	if cond == 1 {
		// BSR: push the return address (after the whole instruction).
		c.push32(c.pc)
		c.pc = uint32(int32(base) + disp)
		return 18
	}
	if c.condTrue(cond) {
		c.pc = uint32(int32(base) + disp)
		return 10
	}
	return notTaken
}

// --- line 7: MOVEQ ----------------------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execMoveQ(op uint16) int {
	if op&0x0100 != 0 {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	v := uint32(int32(int8(uint8(op & 0xFF))))
	c.d[reg] = v
	c.flagsLogic(v, szL)
	return 4
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k/exec2.go ====================

package m68k

// The two-operand lines (8, 9, B, C, D), multiply/divide, BCD, MOVEM,
// and the shift/rotate family. These lines share a three-way opmode
// split:
//
//	opmode 000-010: <ea> is the source, Dn the destination (size = opmode)
//	opmode 011/111: word/long variant instruction (DIV, MUL, SUBA, ...)
//	opmode 100-110: Dn is the source, <ea> the destination (size-100),
//	                except that EA modes 000/001 in this range encode
//	                the register-to-register / memory-to-memory forms
//	                (ADDX, SUBX, ABCD, SBCD, CMPM).

type aluKind int

const (
	aluOr aluKind = iota
	aluAnd
	aluAdd
	aluSub
	aluEor
	aluCmp
)

// applyALU performs a two-operand ALU operation with the manual's flag
// semantics and returns the result (unused for aluCmp).
func (c *CPU) applyALU(kind aluKind, a, b uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch kind {
	case aluOr:
		r := (a | b) & sizeMask(size)
		c.flagsLogic(r, size)
		return r
	case aluAnd:
		r := (a & b) & sizeMask(size)
		c.flagsLogic(r, size)
		return r
	case aluEor:
		r := (a ^ b) & sizeMask(size)
		c.flagsLogic(r, size)
		return r
	case aluAdd:
		return c.flagsAdd(a, b, size, 0, false)
	case aluSub:
		return c.flagsSub(a, b, size, 0, false)
	case aluCmp:
		c.flagsCmp(a, b, size)
		return 0
	}
	return 0
}

// execALUToReg runs the <ea>,Dn form: the source is read, combined with
// Dn, and (except for compares) written back to Dn.
func (c *CPU) execALUToReg(op uint16, dstReg, size, mode, reg int, kind aluKind) int {
	if mode == 1 && size == szB {
		return c.illegal(op) // byte operations cannot use An as a source
	}
	if !eaReadable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	src := c.readSrc(o, size)
	res := c.applyALU(kind, c.d[dstReg], src, size)
	if kind != aluCmp {
		c.opWrite(operand{mode: 0, reg: dstReg}, size, res)
	}
	if size == szL {
		return 6 + o.cyc
	}
	return 4 + o.cyc
}

// execALUToMem runs the Dn,<ea> form: the memory (or, for EOR, register)
// destination is read, combined with Dn, and written back. For SUB the
// computation is <ea> - Dn; the destination supplies the first operand.
func (c *CPU) execALUToMem(op uint16, srcReg, size, mode, reg int, kind aluKind) int {
	if !eaDataAlterable(mode, reg) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	v := c.opRead(o, size)
	res := c.applyALU(kind, v, c.d[srcReg], size)
	c.opWrite(o, size, res)
	if mode == 0 {
		if size == szL {
			return 6
		}
		return 4
	}
	if size == szL {
		return 12 + o.cyc
	}
	return 8 + o.cyc
}

// --- line 8: OR, DIVU, DIVS, SBCD -------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execLine8(op uint16) int {
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := eaFields(op)
	switch {
	case opmode == 3:
		return c.execDiv(op, reg, mode, r, false)
	case opmode == 7:
		return c.execDiv(op, reg, mode, r, true)
	case opmode >= 4 && mode <= 1:
		return c.execBCD(op, reg, mode, r, true) // SBCD
	case opmode <= 2:
		return c.execALUToReg(op, reg, opmode, mode, r, aluOr)
	default:
		return c.execALUToMem(op, reg, opmode-4, mode, r, aluOr)
	}
}

// --- lines 9/D: SUB/ADD families --------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execLine9D(op uint16, isAdd bool) int {
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := eaFields(op)
	kind := aluSub
	if isAdd {
		kind = aluAdd
	}
	switch {
	case opmode == 3 || opmode == 7:
		// SUBA/ADDA: word form sign-extends the source; no flags.
		size := szW
		if opmode == 7 {
			size = szL
		}
		if !eaReadable(mode, r) {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		o := c.resolveEA(mode, r, size)
		v := c.readSrc(o, size)
		if size == szW {
			v = signExtend(v, szW)
			if isAdd {
				c.a[reg] += v
			} else {
				c.a[reg] -= v
			}
			return 8 + o.cyc
		}
		if isAdd {
			c.a[reg] += v
		} else {
			c.a[reg] -= v
		}
		return 6 + o.cyc
	case opmode >= 4 && mode <= 1:
		// SUBX/ADDX, register-to-register or memory-to-memory (both
		// memory operands use predecrement addressing).
		size := opmode - 4
		if (op>>3)&1 != 0 {
			so := c.resolveEA(4, r, size)
			sv := c.opRead(so, size)
			do := c.resolveEA(4, reg, size)
			dv := c.opRead(do, size)
			res := c.flagsX(kind, dv, sv, size)
			c.opWrite(do, size, res)
			if size == szL {
				return 30
			}
			return 18
		}
		res := c.flagsX(kind, c.d[reg], c.d[r], size)
		c.opWrite(operand{mode: 0, reg: reg}, size, res)
		if size == szL {
			return 8
		}
		return 4
	case opmode <= 2:
		return c.execALUToReg(op, reg, opmode, mode, r, kind)
	default:
		return c.execALUToMem(op, reg, opmode-4, mode, r, kind)
	}
}

// flagsX applies ADDX/SUBX arithmetic: the X flag is the carry/borrow
// in, X and C take the carry/borrow out, and Z is sticky (a zero result
// leaves it unchanged).
func (c *CPU) flagsX(kind aluKind, a, b uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if kind == aluAdd {
		return c.flagsAdd(a, b, size, c.xBit(), true)
	}
	return c.flagsSub(a, b, size, c.xBit(), true)
}

// --- line B: CMP, EOR, CMPA, CMPM --------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execLineB(op uint16) int {
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := eaFields(op)
	switch {
	case opmode == 3 || opmode == 7:
		// CMPA: compare the full address register against the
		// (sign-extended for word) source; X is preserved.
		size := szW
		if opmode == 7 {
			size = szL
		}
		if !eaReadable(mode, r) {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		o := c.resolveEA(mode, r, size)
		v := c.readSrc(o, size)
		if size == szW {
			v = signExtend(v, szW)
		}
		c.flagsCmp(c.a[reg], v, szL)
		return 6 + o.cyc
	case opmode <= 2:
		return c.execALUToReg(op, reg, opmode, mode, r, aluCmp)
	case mode == 1 && opmode >= 4:
		// CMPM: compare (An)+ against (An)+.
		size := opmode - 4
		so := c.resolveEA(3, r, size)
		sv := c.readSrc(so, size)
		do := c.resolveEA(3, reg, size)
		dv := c.readSrc(do, size)
		c.flagsCmp(dv, sv, size)
		if size == szL {
			return 20
		}
		return 12
	default:
		return c.execALUToMem(op, reg, opmode-4, mode, r, aluEor)
	}
}

// --- line C: AND, MULU, MULS, ABCD, EXG --------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execLineC(op uint16) int {
	// EXG encodings live inside the AND opcode space; test them first.
	switch {
	case op&0xF1F8 == 0xC140: // EXG Dn,Dn
		a, b := int((op>>9)&7), int(op&7)
		c.d[a], c.d[b] = c.d[b], c.d[a]
		return 6
	case op&0xF1F8 == 0xC148: // EXG An,An
		a, b := int((op>>9)&7), int(op&7)
		c.a[a], c.a[b] = c.a[b], c.a[a]
		return 6
	case op&0xF1F8 == 0xC188: // EXG Dn,An
		a, b := int((op>>9)&7), int(op&7)
		c.d[a], c.a[b] = c.a[b], c.d[a]
		return 6
	}
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	mode, r := eaFields(op)
	switch {
	case opmode == 3:
		return c.execMul(op, reg, mode, r, false)
	case opmode == 7:
		return c.execMul(op, reg, mode, r, true)
	case opmode >= 4 && mode <= 1:
		return c.execBCD(op, reg, mode, r, false) // ABCD
	case opmode <= 2:
		return c.execALUToReg(op, reg, opmode, mode, r, aluAnd)
	default:
		return c.execALUToMem(op, reg, opmode-4, mode, r, aluAnd)
	}
}

// --- multiply and divide ------------------------------------------------

// execDiv implements DIVU/DIVS: a 32-by-16 division producing a 16-bit
// quotient in the low word and the remainder in the high word of Dn. A
// zero divisor raises the divide-by-zero exception (vector 5). On
// quotient overflow the destination is left unchanged and V is set
// (N and Z are undefined by the manual in that case). The remainder
// takes the sign of the dividend, as Go's % does, matching the manual.
func (c *CPU) execDiv(op uint16, reg, mode, r int, signed bool) int {
	if !eaReadable(mode, r) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, r, szW)
	src := c.readSrc(o, szW)
	if signed {
		dvs := int32(int16(uint16(src)))
		if dvs == 0 {
			return c.enterException(vecDivZero, 40)
		}
		dvd := int32(c.d[reg])
		q := dvd / dvs
		rem := dvd % dvs
		if q > 32767 || q < -32768 {
			c.sr = (c.sr &^ srC) | srV
			return 100 + o.cyc
		}
		c.d[reg] = (uint32(uint16(rem)) << 16) | uint32(uint16(q))
		c.flagsLogic(uint32(uint16(q)), szW)
		return 120 + o.cyc
	}
	dvs := src & 0xFFFF
	if dvs == 0 {
		return c.enterException(vecDivZero, 40)
	}
	dvd := c.d[reg]
	q := dvd / dvs
	rem := dvd % dvs
	if q > 0xFFFF {
		c.sr = (c.sr &^ srC) | srV
		return 100 + o.cyc
	}
	c.d[reg] = (rem << 16) | q
	c.flagsLogic(q, szW)
	return 140 + o.cyc
}

// execMul implements MULU/MULS: a 16-by-16 multiply producing a 32-bit
// result in Dn, with N/Z from the full result and V/C cleared.
// Documented time is about 70 cycles plus the source EA fetch.
func (c *CPU) execMul(op uint16, reg, mode, r int, signed bool) int {
	if !eaReadable(mode, r) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, r, szW)
	src := c.readSrc(o, szW)
	var res uint32
	if signed {
		res = uint32(int32(int16(uint16(c.d[reg]))) * int32(int16(uint16(src))))
	} else {
		res = (c.d[reg] & 0xFFFF) * (src & 0xFFFF)
	}
	c.d[reg] = res
	c.flagsLogic(res, szL)
	return 70 + o.cyc
}

// --- BCD ------------------------------------------------------------------

// execBCD implements ABCD (isSub false) and SBCD (isSub true), byte
// only, in register-to-register and memory-to-memory (predecrement)
// forms.
func (c *CPU) execBCD(op uint16, reg, mode, r int, isSub bool) int {
	if (op>>3)&1 != 0 {
		so := c.resolveEA(4, r, szB)
		sv := c.opRead(so, szB)
		do := c.resolveEA(4, reg, szB)
		dv := c.opRead(do, szB)
		var res uint32
		if isSub {
			res = c.bcdSub(dv, sv)
		} else {
			res = c.bcdAdd(dv, sv)
		}
		c.opWrite(do, szB, res)
		return 18
	}
	var res uint32
	if isSub {
		res = c.bcdSub(c.d[reg], c.d[r])
	} else {
		res = c.bcdAdd(c.d[reg], c.d[r])
	}
	c.opWrite(operand{mode: 0, reg: reg}, szB, res)
	return 6
}

// The BCD model below was fitted against a full-space black-box
// probe of the reference implementation (every operand pair and both
// X states, 131072 cases per instruction, result and flags compared).
// The manual leaves the results for invalid BCD digits and the V flag
// undefined, but real code can observe both (DBcc reads V), so the
// silicon behavior is what is implemented:
//
//   - Corrections are applied to the binary sum as separate passes.
//     For ABCD the +0x60 pass and the carry flag are decided on the
//     RAW binary sum (before the +6 pass), not on the corrected sum.
//   - For SBCD the -0x60 result pass is decided on the raw
//     difference, but the carry flag is decided on the difference
//     after the -6 pass.
//   - V is the OR of the signed overflows of the correction passes
//     alone, each computed on byte values; the initial binary pass
//     does not contribute.

// bcdPassVAdd is the signed overflow of one byte addition pass u + k
// producing t.
func bcdPassVAdd(u, k, t uint32) bool {
	return (u^t)&(k^t)&0x80 != 0
}

// bcdPassVSub is the signed overflow of one byte subtraction pass
// u - k producing t.
func bcdPassVSub(u, k, t uint32) bool {
	return (u^k)&(u^t)&0x80 != 0
}

// bcdAdd computes a + b + X as packed BCD. Flags: X and C get the
// decimal carry, N is the result's top bit, Z is sticky (cleared by a
// nonzero result, otherwise unchanged, as for ADDX), V per the model
// above.
func (c *CPU) bcdAdd(a, b uint32) uint32 {
	a &= 0xFF
	b &= 0xFF
	x := uint32(c.xBit())
	raw := a + b + x
	res := raw & 0xFF
	v := false
	if (a&0xF)+(b&0xF)+x > 9 {
		before := res
		res = (res + 6) & 0xFF
		v = v || bcdPassVAdd(before, 6, res)
	}
	carry := false
	if raw > 0x99 {
		before := res
		res = (res + 0x60) & 0xFF
		v = v || bcdPassVAdd(before, 0x60, res)
		carry = true
	}
	c.setBCDFlags(res, carry, v)
	return res
}

// bcdSub computes a - b - X as packed BCD, with the flag rules of the
// model above. NBCD is bcdSub with a = 0.
func (c *CPU) bcdSub(a, b uint32) uint32 {
	a &= 0xFF
	b &= 0xFF
	x := int(c.xBit())
	raw := int(a) - int(b) - x
	res := uint32(raw) & 0xFF
	v := false
	afterLow := raw
	if (a & 0xF) < (b&0xF)+uint32(x) {
		before := res
		res = (res - 6) & 0xFF
		v = v || bcdPassVSub(before, 6, res)
		afterLow = raw - 6
	}
	carry := afterLow < 0
	if raw < 0 {
		before := res
		res = (res - 0x60) & 0xFF
		v = v || bcdPassVSub(before, 0x60, res)
	}
	c.setBCDFlags(res, carry, v)
	return res
}

func (c *CPU) setBCDFlags(res uint32, carry, v bool) {
	c.sr &^= srX | srN | srV | srC
	if carry {
		c.sr |= srX | srC
	}
	if v {
		c.sr |= srV
	}
	if res&0x80 != 0 {
		c.sr |= srN
	}
	if res != 0 {
		c.sr &^= srZ
	}
}

// --- MOVEM ------------------------------------------------------------------

// movemListReg maps a register-list mask bit (normal order) to a
// register: bits 0-7 are D0-D7, bits 8-15 are A0-A7. kind 0 = D, 1 = A.
func movemListReg(j int) (kind, idx int) {
	if j < 8 {
		return 0, j
	}
	return 1, j - 8
}

// movemRevReg maps a mask bit under predecrement addressing, where the
// mask is interpreted in reverse: bit 0 is A7 down to bit 7 = A0, then
// bit 8 is D7 down to bit 15 = D0.
func movemRevReg(j int) (kind, idx int) {
	if j < 8 {
		return 1, 7 - j
	}
	return 0, 15 - j
}

func regValue(snapD, snapA [8]uint32, kind, idx int) uint32 {
	if kind == 0 {
		return snapD[idx]
	}
	return snapA[idx]
}

// execMovem implements MOVEM in both directions. The mask word follows
// the opcode. Register-to-memory permits control modes and
// predecrement (with the reversed mask); memory-to-register permits
// control modes and postincrement. Word transfers to registers
// sign-extend. Documented times: 8 + 4/8 per register stored,
// 12 + 4/8 per register loaded.
func (c *CPU) execMovem(op uint16, memToReg bool) int {
	size := szW
	if op&0x40 != 0 {
		size = szL
	}
	mode, reg := eaFields(op)
	mask := c.fetch16()
	sb := sizeBytes(size)
	if !memToReg {
		// Snapshot first: under predecrement, a base register that is
		// itself in the list is stored with its original value.
		snapD, snapA := c.d, c.a
		if mode == 4 {
			addr := c.a[reg]
			n := 0
			for j := 0; j < 16; j++ {
				if mask>>uint(j)&1 == 0 {
					continue
				}
				addr -= uint32(sb)
				kind, idx := movemRevReg(j)
				c.writeMem(addr, size, regValue(snapD, snapA, kind, idx))
				n++
			}
			c.a[reg] = addr
			return 8 + n*sb*2
		}
		if !(mode == 2 || mode == 5 || mode == 6 || (mode == 7 && reg <= 1)) {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
		addr := o.addr
		n := 0
		for j := 0; j < 16; j++ {
			if mask>>uint(j)&1 == 0 {
				continue
			}
			kind, idx := movemListReg(j)
			c.writeMem(addr, size, regValue(snapD, snapA, kind, idx))
			addr += uint32(sb)
			n++
		}
		return 8 + n*sb*2
	}
	if !(mode == 2 || mode == 3 || mode == 5 || mode == 6 || (mode == 7 && reg <= 1)) {
		return c.illegal(op)
	}
	o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, size)
	addr := o.addr
	n := 0
	for j := 0; j < 16; j++ {
		if mask>>uint(j)&1 == 0 {
			continue
		}
		v := c.readMem(addr, size)
		kind, idx := movemListReg(j)
		if kind == 0 {
			c.d[idx] = signExtend(v, size)
		} else {
			c.a[idx] = signExtend(v, size)
		}
		addr += uint32(sb)
		n++
	}
	if mode == 3 {
		// Postincrement total; a base register in the list ends with
		// the final address, not the loaded value.
		c.a[reg] = addr
	}
	return 12 + n*sb*2
}

// --- shifts and rotates (line E) -------------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) execShifts(op uint16) int {
	if (op>>6)&3 == 3 {
		// Memory form: word only, shift count of one.
		typ := int((op >> 9) & 3)
		dir := int((op >> 8) & 1)
		mode, reg := eaFields(op)
		if !eaAlterableMem(mode, reg) {
			return c.illegal(op)
		}
		o := c.resolveEA(mode, reg, szW)
		v := c.opRead(o, szW)
		res := c.shiftOp(typ, dir, szW, v, 1)
		c.opWrite(o, szW, res)
		return 8 + o.cyc
	}
	cntField := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	dir := int((op >> 8) & 1)
	size := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	typ := int((op >> 3) & 3)
	reg := int(op & 7)
	var count int
	if op&0x20 != 0 {
		count = int(c.d[cntField] & 63) // register counts are modulo 64
	} else {
		count = cntField
		if count == 0 {
			count = 8
		}
	}
	v := c.d[reg] & sizeMask(size)
	res := c.shiftOp(typ, dir, size, v, count)
	c.opWrite(operand{mode: 0, reg: reg}, size, res)
	if size == szL {
		return 8 + 2*count
	}
	return 6 + 2*count
}

// shiftOp performs one arithmetic/logical shift or rotate. typ: 0 AS,
// 1 LS, 2 ROX (through X), 3 RO. dir: 0 right, 1 left.
//
// Flag rules per the manual: N and Z come from the result; C holds the
// last bit shifted out and is cleared when the count is zero; X holds
// the last bit shifted out for AS/LS/ROX and is unaffected for RO and
// when the count is zero; V is set for ASL if the sign bit changes at
// any point during the shift, and is cleared for all other forms.
func (c *CPU) shiftOp(typ, dir, size int, v uint32, count int) uint32 {
	bits := sizeBytes(size) * 8
	mask := sizeMask(size)
	sb := signBit(size)
	v &= mask
	res := v
	carry := uint32(0)
	shifted := false
	vSet := false
	xIn := uint32(0)
	if c.sr&srX != 0 {
		xIn = 1
	}
	if dir == 1 { // left
		switch typ {
		case 0, 1: // ASL, LSL
			for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
				before := res & sb
				carry = 0
				if before != 0 {
					carry = 1
				}
				res = (res << 1) & mask
				if typ == 0 && (res&sb) != before {
					vSet = true
				}
				shifted = true
			}
		case 2: // ROXL
			x := xIn
			for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
				nx := uint32(0)
				if res&sb != 0 {
					nx = 1
				}
				res = ((res << 1) | x) & mask
				x = nx
				carry = nx
				shifted = true
			}
		case 3: // ROL
			for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
				carry = 0
				if res&sb != 0 {
					carry = 1
				}
				res = ((res << 1) | carry) & mask
				shifted = true
			}
		}
	} else { // right
		switch typ {
		case 0: // ASR
			for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
				carry = res & 1
				res = (res >> 1) | (res & sb)
				shifted = true
			}
		case 1: // LSR
			for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
				carry = res & 1
				res >>= 1
				shifted = true
			}
		case 2: // ROXR
			x := xIn
			for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
				nx := res & 1
				res = (res >> 1) | (x << uint(bits-1))
				x = nx
				carry = nx
				shifted = true
			}
		case 3: // ROR
			for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
				carry = res & 1
				res = (res >> 1) | (carry << uint(bits-1))
				shifted = true
			}
		}
	}
	c.sr &^= srN | srZ | srV | srC
	if res&sb != 0 {
		c.sr |= srN
	}
	if res == 0 {
		c.sr |= srZ
	}
	if vSet {
		c.sr |= srV
	}
	if shifted && carry != 0 {
		c.sr |= srC
	}
	if typ != 3 && shifted {
		// AS/LS/ROX load X with the last bit out.
		if carry != 0 {
			c.sr |= srX
		} else {
			c.sr &^= srX
		}
	}
	return res
}

package m68k

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// ramBus is a flat big-endian RAM implementing the CPU's Bus interface.
type ramBus struct{ mem []byte }

func newRAMBus() *ramBus { return &ramBus{mem: make([]byte, 0x10000)} }

func (b *ramBus) Read8(a uint32) uint8       { return b.mem[a] }
func (b *ramBus) Read16(a uint32) uint16     { return binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b.mem[a:]) }
func (b *ramBus) Read32(a uint32) uint32     { return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b.mem[a:]) }
func (b *ramBus) Write8(a uint32, v uint8)   { b.mem[a] = v }
func (b *ramBus) Write16(a uint32, v uint16) { binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(b.mem[a:], v) }
func (b *ramBus) Write32(a uint32, v uint32) { binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b.mem[a:], v) }
func (b *ramBus) Reset()                     {}

const codeBase = 0x1000

// newCPU builds a CPU with the reset vector pointing at codeBase and
// the given instruction words laid out there. Initial SSP is 0xF000.
func newCPU(code ...uint16) (*CPU, *ramBus) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.Write32(0, 0x0000F000)
	bus.Write32(4, codeBase)
	for i, w := range code {
		bus.Write16(codeBase+uint32(2*i), w)
	}
	c := New(bus)
	c.Reset()
	return c, bus
}

// arrange mutates the register file through the public snapshot API.
func arrange(c *CPU, fn func(r *Registers)) {
	r := c.Registers()
	fn(&r)
	c.SetState(r)
}

func flags(t *testing.T, c *CPU, want, clear uint16) {
	t.Helper()
	sr := c.Registers().SR
	if sr&want != want {
		t.Errorf("SR = %04X, want flags %04X set", sr, want)
	}
	if sr&clear != 0 {
		t.Errorf("SR = %04X, want flags %04X clear", sr, clear)
	}
}

func TestReset(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := newCPU(0x4E71)
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.SR != 0x2700 {
		t.Errorf("SR = %04X, want 2700", r.SR)
	}
	if r.A[7] != 0xF000 || r.SSP != 0xF000 {
		t.Errorf("SP = %08X/%08X, want F000", r.A[7], r.SSP)
	}
	if r.PC != codeBase {
		t.Errorf("PC = %08X, want %08X", r.PC, codeBase)
	}
	if c.Cycles() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("cycles = %d, want 0", c.Cycles())
	}
}

func TestAddFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// ADD.W D1,D0 = 0xD041; 0x7FFF + 1 overflows into the sign bit.
	c, _ := newCPU(0xD041)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x7FFF; r.D[1] = 1 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("ADD.W result = %08X, want 8000", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srN|srV, srZ|srC|srX)

	// ADD.B D1,D0 = 0xD001; 0xFF + 1 wraps with carry, upper bytes kept.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xD001)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x123456FF; r.D[1] = 1 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x12345600 {
		t.Errorf("ADD.B result = %08X, want 12345600", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srZ|srC|srX, srN|srV)

	// ADD.L D1,D0 = 0xD081; 0x7FFFFFFF + 1.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xD081)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x7FFFFFFF; r.D[1] = 1 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x80000000 {
		t.Errorf("ADD.L result = %08X, want 80000000", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srN|srV, srZ|srC)
}

func TestSubCmpFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// SUB.W D1,D0 = 0x9041; 0 - 1 borrows.
	c, _ := newCPU(0x9041)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0; r.D[1] = 1 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0xFFFF {
		t.Errorf("SUB.W result = %08X, want FFFF", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srN|srC|srX, srZ|srV)

	// SUB.W overflow: 0x8000 - 1 = 0x7FFF with V set.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x9041)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x8000; r.D[1] = 1 })
	c.Step()
	flags(t, c, srV, srN|srZ|srC)

	// CMP.W D1,D0 = 0xB041 preserves X and writes nothing back.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xB041)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) {
		r.D[0] = 5
		r.D[1] = 5
		r.SR = 0x2700 | srX
	})
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 5 {
		t.Errorf("CMP changed D0 to %08X", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srZ|srX, srN|srV|srC)
}

func TestAddXStickyZ(t *testing.T) {
	// ADDX.W D1,D0 = 0xD141.
	// Case 1: 0 + 0 + X(1) = 1: nonzero result clears Z, no carry out.
	c, _ := newCPU(0xD141)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.SR = 0x2700 | srX | srZ })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("ADDX result = %08X, want 1", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, 0, srZ|srX|srC)

	// Case 2: 0xFFFF + 0 + X(1) = 0 with carry; Z was clear and the
	// sticky-Z rule keeps it clear for a zero result.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xD141)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0xFFFF; r.SR = 0x2700 | srX })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ADDX result = %08X, want 0", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srX|srC, srZ)

	// Case 3: same sum, but Z was set; sticky Z keeps it set.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xD141)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0xFFFF; r.SR = 0x2700 | srX | srZ })
	c.Step()
	flags(t, c, srZ|srX|srC, 0)
}

func TestShifts(t *testing.T) {
	// ASL.W #1,D0 = 0xE340: 0x8001 -> 0x0002, carry out 1, sign changed
	// so V is set.
	c, _ := newCPU(0xE340)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x8001 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x0002 {
		t.Errorf("ASL result = %08X, want 0002", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srC|srX|srV, srN|srZ)

	// ASL.W D1,D0 = 0xE360 with a zero register count: value unchanged,
	// C cleared, X preserved, V clear.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xE360)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x8000; r.D[1] = 0; r.SR = 0x2700 | srX })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("ASL count-0 result = %08X, want 8000", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srN|srX, srC|srV|srZ)

	// LSR.B #1,D0 = 0xE208: 0x03 -> 0x01, carry 1.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xE208)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x03 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x01 {
		t.Errorf("LSR result = %08X, want 01", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srC|srX, srN|srZ|srV)

	// ROXL.W #1,D0 = 0xE350 with X set: 0x8000 -> 0x0001, X stays 1.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xE350)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x8000; r.SR = 0x2700 | srX })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x0001 {
		t.Errorf("ROXL result = %08X, want 0001", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srC|srX, srN|srZ|srV)

	// ASR.L #8,D0 = 0xE080: sign-extends, 0x80000000 -> 0xFF800000,
	// last bit out is 0.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xE080)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x80000000 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0xFF800000 {
		t.Errorf("ASR result = %08X, want FF800000", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srN, srZ|srC|srV)

	// ASL.W (A0) = 0xE1D0 (memory form, count one): 0xC000 -> 0x8000,
	// carry 1, sign unchanged so V clear.
	c, bus := newCPU(0xE1D0)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	bus.Write16(0x2000, 0xC000)
	c.Step()
	if got := bus.Read16(0x2000); got != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("ASL mem result = %04X, want 8000", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srN|srC|srX, srZ|srV)
}

func TestDivide(t *testing.T) {
	// DIVU #10,D0 = 0x80FC: 600000 / 10 = 60000 remainder 0.
	c, _ := newCPU(0x80FC, 0x000A)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 600000 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 60000 {
		t.Errorf("DIVU result = %08X, want 60000 (0000EA60)", got)
	}
	// 60000 = 0xEA60 has the word sign bit set, so N is set.
	flags(t, c, srN, srZ|srV|srC)

	// DIVU overflow: 65536 / 1 does not fit in a word; the destination
	// is unchanged and V is set.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x80FC, 0x0001)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x00010000 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x00010000 {
		t.Errorf("DIVU overflow changed D0 to %08X", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srV, srC)

	// DIVS #-3,D0 = 0x81FC: -100 / -3 = 33 remainder -1 (the remainder
	// takes the dividend's sign).
	c, _ = newCPU(0x81FC, 0xFFFD)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0xFFFFFF9C })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0xFFFF0021 {
		t.Errorf("DIVS result = %08X, want FFFF0021", got)
	}

	// Divide by zero takes exception vector 5: the handler address is
	// stacked-frame reachable and the return PC is the next instruction.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x80FC, 0x0000)
	bus.Write32(5*4, 0x2000)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 42 })
	c.Step()
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.PC != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("div-zero PC = %08X, want handler 2000", r.PC)
	}
	if r.A[7] != 0xF000-6 {
		t.Errorf("div-zero SP = %08X, want EFFA", r.A[7])
	}
	if got := bus.Read16(0xEFFA); got != 0x2700 {
		t.Errorf("stacked SR = %04X, want 2700", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read32(0xEFFC); got != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("stacked PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+4)
	}
}

func TestAddressingModes(t *testing.T) {
	// MOVE.W (A0)+,D0 = 0x3018.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x3018)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	bus.Write16(0x2000, 0xBEEF)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("(A0)+ value = %08X, want BEEF", got)
	}
	if got := c.Registers().A[0]; got != 0x2002 {
		t.Errorf("(A0)+ A0 = %08X, want 2002", got)
	}

	// MOVE.B (A7)+,D0 = 0x101F: the stack-pointer byte quirk moves A7
	// by 2, not 1.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x101F)
	bus.Write8(0xF000, 0x5A)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x5A {
		t.Errorf("(A7)+ value = %08X, want 5A", got)
	}
	if got := c.Registers().A[7]; got != 0xF002 {
		t.Errorf("(A7)+ A7 = %08X, want F002", got)
	}

	// MOVE.W -(A0),D0 = 0x3020.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x3020)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	bus.Write16(0x1FFE, 0x1234)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x1234 {
		t.Errorf("-(A0) value = %08X, want 1234", got)
	}
	if got := c.Registers().A[0]; got != 0x1FFE {
		t.Errorf("-(A0) A0 = %08X, want 1FFE", got)
	}

	// MOVE.B D0,-(A7) = 0x1F00: byte predecrement on A7 also moves by 2.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x1F00)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0xAB })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().A[7]; got != 0xEFFE {
		t.Errorf("-(A7) A7 = %08X, want EFFE", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read8(0xEFFE); got != 0xAB {
		t.Errorf("-(A7) byte = %02X, want AB", got)
	}

	// MOVE.W $10(A0),D0 = 0x3028.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x3028, 0x0010)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	bus.Write16(0x2010, 0x0D0A)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x0D0A {
		t.Errorf("d16(A0) value = %08X, want 0D0A", got)
	}

	// MOVE.W $4(A0,D1.W),D0 = 0x3030, index word 0x1004.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x3030, 0x1004)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000; r.D[1] = 0x10 })
	bus.Write16(0x2014, 0x600D)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x600D {
		t.Errorf("d8(A0,D1.W) value = %08X, want 600D", got)
	}

	// Same with a long index of -16 (sign-extended from the register):
	// index word 0x1804 selects D1.L.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x3030, 0x1804)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000; r.D[1] = 0xFFFFFFF0 })
	bus.Write16(0x1FF4, 0x0BAD)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x0BAD {
		t.Errorf("d8(A0,D1.L) value = %08X, want 0BAD", got)
	}

	// MOVE.W (d16,PC),D0 = 0x303A: the displacement base is the
	// extension word's address (codeBase+2); a displacement of 0x4E
	// reaches codeBase+0x50.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x303A, 0x004E)
	bus.Write16(codeBase+0x50, 0xCAFE)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0xCAFE {
		t.Errorf("d16(PC) value = %08X, want CAFE", got)
	}

	// MOVE.L D0,-(A7) = 0x2F00.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x2F00)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0xDEADBEEF })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().A[7]; got != 0xEFFC {
		t.Errorf("push A7 = %08X, want EFFC", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read32(0xEFFC); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("pushed value = %08X, want DEADBEEF", got)
	}
}

func TestInterruptMaskingAndRTE(t *testing.T) {
	// Program: MOVE.W #$2300,SR then NOPs. Autovector handler (level 4
	// -> vector 28) sits at 0x2000 and is a bare RTE.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x46FC, 0x2300, 0x4E71, 0x4E71)
	bus.Write32(28*4, 0x2000)
	bus.Write16(0x2000, 0x4E73)

	// Mask is 7 after reset, so the level-4 request latches but is not
	// serviced; a lower level-2 request must not displace it.
	c.RequestInterrupt(4, nil)
	c.RequestInterrupt(2, nil)
	c.Step() // executes MOVE to SR (mask drops to 3)
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+4 {
		t.Fatalf("PC after MOVE = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+4)
	}
	c.Step() // now the latched level-4 interrupt is serviced
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.PC != 0x2000 {
		t.Fatalf("interrupt PC = %08X, want handler 2000", r.PC)
	}
	if r.SR != 0x2400 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt SR = %04X, want 2400 (S set, mask = level)", r.SR)
	}
	if got := bus.Read16(0xEFFA); got != 0x2300 {
		t.Errorf("stacked SR = %04X, want 2300", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read32(0xEFFC); got != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("stacked PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+4)
	}
	c.Step() // RTE in the handler
	r = c.Registers()
	if r.PC != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("RTE return PC = %08X, want %08X", r.PC, codeBase+4)
	}
	if r.SR != 0x2300 {
		t.Errorf("RTE restored SR = %04X, want 2300", r.SR)
	}
	if r.A[7] != 0xF000 {
		t.Errorf("RTE restored SP = %08X, want F000", r.A[7])
	}
}

func TestExplicitVectorInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	// A request carrying an explicit vector uses that vector instead of
	// the autovector.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x46FC, 0x2000, 0x4E71) // MOVE.W #$2000,SR: mask 0
	bus.Write32(64*4, 0x2000)
	vec := uint8(64)
	c.RequestInterrupt(3, &vec)
	c.Step() // MOVE to SR executes (mask was 7 at the boundary)
	c.Step() // interrupt serviced through vector 64
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("explicit-vector PC = %08X, want 2000", got)
	}
}

func TestStopWake(t *testing.T) {
	// STOP #$2000 then NOP. Level 6 autovector = 30.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x4E72, 0x2000, 0x4E71)
	bus.Write32(30*4, 0x2000)
	c.Step() // STOP
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+4 {
		t.Fatalf("PC after STOP = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+4)
	}
	if n := c.Step(); n != 4 {
		t.Errorf("stopped Step = %d cycles, want 4", n)
	}
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("stopped PC moved to %08X", got)
	}
	c.RequestInterrupt(6, nil)
	c.Step() // wakes and services
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.PC != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("STOP wake PC = %08X, want 2000", r.PC)
	}
	if got := bus.Read16(0xEFFA); got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("STOP stacked SR = %04X, want 2000", got)
	}

	// STOP with mask 7: a level-6 request cannot wake it, but the
	// non-maskable level 7 (autovector 31) can.
	c2, bus2 := newCPU(0x4E72, 0x2700, 0x4E71)
	bus2.Write32(31*4, 0x2000)
	c2.Step()
	c2.RequestInterrupt(6, nil)
	if n := c2.Step(); n != 4 {
		t.Errorf("masked stopped Step = %d, want 4", n)
	}
	if got := c2.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("masked STOP woke early, PC = %08X", got)
	}
	// StepCycles on a stopped CPU consumes the whole budget as time.
	if n := c2.StepCycles(40); n != 40 {
		t.Errorf("stopped StepCycles = %d, want 40", n)
	}
	c2.RequestInterrupt(7, nil)
	c2.Step()
	if got := c2.Registers().PC; got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("level-7 wake PC = %08X, want 2000", got)
	}
}

func TestSetStateContract(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU(0x4E71)
	bus.Write32(31*4, 0x2000)
	// Burn some cycles so the SetState cycle reset is observable.
	c.Step()
	c.Step()
	if c.Cycles() == 0 {
		t.Fatal("expected nonzero cycles before SetState")
	}
	// Latch an interrupt that SetState must clear.
	c.RequestInterrupt(7, nil)

	c.SetState(Registers{
		D:   [8]uint32{3: 0xDEADBEEF},
		A:   [8]uint32{2: 0x11112222, 7: 0x77777777}, // A[7] must be ignored
		PC:  codeBase,
		SR:  0x2300, // supervisor
		USP: 0x9000,
		SSP: 0x8000,
	})
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.A[7] != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("supervisor A[7] = %08X, want SSP 8000", r.A[7])
	}
	if r.A[2] != 0x11112222 || r.D[3] != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("register copy wrong: A2=%08X D3=%08X", r.A[2], r.D[3])
	}
	if c.Cycles() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("SetState left cycles = %d, want 0", c.Cycles())
	}
	c.AddCycles(1234)
	if c.Cycles() != 1234 {
		t.Errorf("AddCycles: cycles = %d, want 1234", c.Cycles())
	}
	// The pending level-7 request was cleared: Step runs the NOP, not
	// the interrupt handler.
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+2 {
		t.Errorf("PC after cleared-pending Step = %08X, want %08X (NOP ran)", got, codeBase+2)
	}

	// User mode: A[7] comes from USP instead.
	c.SetState(Registers{PC: codeBase, SR: 0x0300, USP: 0x9000, SSP: 0x8000})
	if got := c.Registers().A[7]; got != 0x9000 {
		t.Errorf("user A[7] = %08X, want USP 9000", got)
	}
	if got := c.Registers().SSP; got != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("user-mode SSP field = %08X, want 8000", got)
	}
}

func TestMovem(t *testing.T) {
	// MOVEM.L D0-D2/A0-A1,-(A7) = 0x48E7; under predecrement the mask
	// is read in reverse bit order: D2..D0 land at bits 13..15 and
	// A1..A0 at bits 6..7, hence 0xE0C0.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x48E7, 0xE0C0, 0x4CDF, 0x0307)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) {
		r.D[0], r.D[1], r.D[2] = 0x11111111, 0x22222222, 0x33333333
		r.A[0], r.A[1] = 0x44444444, 0x55555555
	})
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().A[7]; got != 0xF000-20 {
		t.Fatalf("MOVEM store SP = %08X, want %08X", got, 0xF000-20)
	}
	base := uint32(0xF000 - 20)
	want := []uint32{0x11111111, 0x22222222, 0x33333333, 0x44444444, 0x55555555}
	for i, w := range want {
		if got := bus.Read32(base + uint32(4*i)); got != w {
			t.Errorf("MOVEM memory[%d] = %08X, want %08X", i, got, w)
		}
	}
	// Clear the registers (keeping PC and the stack pointer) and load
	// them back with MOVEM.L (A7)+,D0-D2/A0-A1 = 0x4CDF, mask 0x0307.
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) {
		r.D[0], r.D[1], r.D[2] = 0, 0, 0
		r.A[0], r.A[1] = 0, 0
		r.SSP = base
	})
	c.Step()
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.D[0] != want[0] || r.D[1] != want[1] || r.D[2] != want[2] ||
		r.A[0] != want[3] || r.A[1] != want[4] {
		t.Errorf("MOVEM load wrong: D=%08X %08X %08X A=%08X %08X",
			r.D[0], r.D[1], r.D[2], r.A[0], r.A[1])
	}
	if r.A[7] != 0xF000 {
		t.Errorf("MOVEM load SP = %08X, want F000", r.A[7])
	}

	// MOVEM.W (A0),D0 = 0x4C90 sign-extends word loads.
	c2, bus2 := newCPU(0x4C90, 0x0001)
	arrange(c2, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	bus2.Write16(0x2000, 0x8001)
	c2.Step()
	if got := c2.Registers().D[0]; got != 0xFFFF8001 {
		t.Errorf("MOVEM.W load = %08X, want FFFF8001", got)
	}
}

func TestBranchAndDBcc(t *testing.T) {
	// MOVEQ #3,D0; DBF D0,-2 (loops on itself); NOP.
	c, _ := newCPU(0x7003, 0x51C8, 0xFFFE, 0x4E71)
	c.Step() // MOVEQ
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.Step() // DBF runs 4 times total: 3 branches + fall-through
	}
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.PC != codeBase+6 {
		t.Errorf("DBF exit PC = %08X, want %08X", r.PC, codeBase+6)
	}
	if got := r.D[0] & 0xFFFF; got != 0xFFFF {
		t.Errorf("DBF final counter = %04X, want FFFF", got)
	}

	// MOVEQ #0,D0 (sets Z); BEQ +2 skips MOVEQ #5,D1.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x7000, 0x6702, 0x7205, 0x4E71)
	c.Step()
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+6 {
		t.Errorf("BEQ taken PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+6)
	}
	if got := c.Registers().D[1]; got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("BEQ skipped instruction still ran: D1 = %08X", got)
	}

	// MOVEQ #1,D0 (clears Z); BEQ falls through; MOVEQ #5,D1 runs.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x7001, 0x6702, 0x7205, 0x4E71)
	c.Step()
	c.Step()
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[1]; got != 5 {
		t.Errorf("BEQ fall-through D1 = %08X, want 5", got)
	}
}

func TestPrivilegeViolation(t *testing.T) {
	// In user mode, MOVE.W #$2700,SR must take the privilege exception
	// (vector 8), stacking on the supervisor stack.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x46FC, 0x2700)
	bus.Write32(8*4, 0x2000)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) {
		r.SR = 0x0300 // user mode
		r.USP = 0x9000
		r.SSP = 0x8000
	})
	c.Step()
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.PC != 0x2000 {
		t.Fatalf("privilege PC = %08X, want handler 2000", r.PC)
	}
	if r.A[7] != 0x8000-6 {
		t.Errorf("privilege SP = %08X, want %08X", r.A[7], 0x8000-6)
	}
	if got := bus.Read16(0x8000 - 6); got != 0x0300 {
		t.Errorf("stacked SR = %04X, want 0300 (user SR)", got)
	}
	// The stacked PC is the privileged instruction itself, not the
	// next instruction: the instruction never executed, and the manual
	// has the handler inspect the offending word (the same rule as
	// illegal instruction and the line A/F emulation vectors, verified
	// against the reference implementation by differential test).
	if got := bus.Read32(0x8000 - 4); got != codeBase {
		t.Errorf("stacked PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase)
	}
	if r.USP != 0x9000 {
		t.Errorf("USP after switch = %08X, want 9000", r.USP)
	}
}

func TestAddressError(t *testing.T) {
	// MOVE.W $00001001,D0 reads a word at an odd address: vector 3.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x3039, 0x0000, 0x1001)
	bus.Write32(3*4, 0x2000)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("address-error PC = %08X, want handler 2000", got)
	}
	if c.Halted() {
		t.Error("CPU halted on a single address error")
	}
}

func TestChk(t *testing.T) {
	// CHK.W #10,D0 = 0x41BC. In range: no trap.
	c, _ := newCPU(0x41BC, 0x000A, 0x4E71)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 5 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+4 {
		t.Errorf("CHK in-range PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+4)
	}

	// Above the bound: trap to vector 6 with N clear.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x41BC, 0x000A)
	bus.Write32(6*4, 0x2000)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 20 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("CHK trap PC = %08X, want 2000", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, 0, srN)

	// Negative register: trap with N set.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x41BC, 0x000A)
	bus.Write32(6*4, 0x2000)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0xFFFF })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("CHK negative PC = %08X, want 2000", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srN, 0)
}

func TestMoveP(t *testing.T) {
	// MOVEP.L D0,(0,A0) = 0x01C8 spreads the bytes to even addresses.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x01C8, 0x0000)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000; r.D[0] = 0x11223344 })
	c.Step()
	for i, want := range []uint8{0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44} {
		if got := bus.Read8(0x2000 + uint32(2*i)); got != want {
			t.Errorf("MOVEP byte %d = %02X, want %02X", i, got, want)
		}
	}

	// MOVEP.W (0,A0),D1 = 0x0308 gathers them back, high word kept.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x0308, 0x0000)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000; r.D[1] = 0xCAFE0000 })
	bus.Write8(0x2000, 0xAB)
	bus.Write8(0x2002, 0xCD)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[1]; got != 0xCAFEABCD {
		t.Errorf("MOVEP load = %08X, want CAFEABCD", got)
	}
}

func TestBCD(t *testing.T) {
	// ABCD D1,D0 = 0xC101: 0x15 + 0x27 = 0x42.
	c, _ := newCPU(0xC101)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x15; r.D[1] = 0x27 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0] & 0xFF; got != 0x42 {
		t.Errorf("ABCD = %02X, want 42", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, 0, srC|srX)

	// ABCD carry case: 0x99 + 0x01 = 0x00 with carry.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xC101)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x99; r.D[1] = 0x01 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0] & 0xFF; got != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("ABCD carry = %02X, want 00", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srC|srX, srZ) // note: Z is sticky; SR started clear of Z

	// SBCD D1,D0 = 0x8101: 0x42 - 0x15 = 0x27.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x8101)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x42; r.D[1] = 0x15 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0] & 0xFF; got != 0x27 {
		t.Errorf("SBCD = %02X, want 27", got)
	}

	// NBCD D0 = 0x4800: 0 - 1 = 0x99 with borrow.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x4800)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x01 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0] & 0xFF; got != 0x99 {
		t.Errorf("NBCD = %02X, want 99", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srC|srX, 0)
}

func TestBitOpsAndTAS(t *testing.T) {
	// BTST #3,D0 = 0x0800, extension 0x0003: bit set -> Z clear.
	c, _ := newCPU(0x0800, 0x0003)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x08 })
	c.Step()
	flags(t, c, 0, srZ)

	// Bit clear -> Z set.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x0800, 0x0003)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x00 })
	c.Step()
	flags(t, c, srZ, 0)

	// BSET D1,(A0) = 0x03D0: D1 = 9, so bit 1 of the byte at (A0).
	c, bus := newCPU(0x03D0)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000; r.D[1] = 9 })
	c.Step()
	if got := bus.Read8(0x2000); got != 0x02 {
		t.Errorf("BSET byte = %02X, want 02", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srZ, 0) // the bit was clear before the set

	// TAS (A0) = 0x4AD0: tests the byte and sets its high bit.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x4AD0)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	bus.Write8(0x2000, 0x7F)
	c.Step()
	if got := bus.Read8(0x2000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("TAS byte = %02X, want FF", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, 0, srN|srZ|srV|srC)
}

func TestMiscInstructions(t *testing.T) {
	// SWAP D0 = 0x4840.
	c, _ := newCPU(0x4840)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x12345678 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x56781234 {
		t.Errorf("SWAP = %08X, want 56781234", got)
	}

	// EXT.W D0 = 0x4880 then EXT.L D0 = 0x48C0.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x4880, 0x48C0)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0x00000080 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x0000FF80 {
		t.Errorf("EXT.W = %08X, want 0000FF80", got)
	}
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0xFFFFFF80 {
		t.Errorf("EXT.L = %08X, want FFFFFF80", got)
	}

	// ADDQ.W #8,D0 = 0x5040 (data field 0 encodes 8): 0xFFFF + 8.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x5040)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.D[0] = 0xFFFF })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().D[0]; got != 0x0007 {
		t.Errorf("ADDQ = %08X, want 0007", got)
	}
	flags(t, c, srC|srX, srZ)

	// LEA $10(A0),A1 = 0x43E8.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x43E8, 0x0010)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().A[1]; got != 0x2010 {
		t.Errorf("LEA = %08X, want 2010", got)
	}

	// PEA (A0) = 0x4850 pushes the address itself.
	c, bus := newCPU(0x4850)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000 })
	c.Step()
	if got := bus.Read32(0xEFFC); got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("PEA pushed %08X, want 2000", got)
	}
