	// LINK A0,#-4 = 0x4E50 / UNLK A0 = 0x4E58 round trip.
	c, _ = newCPU(0x4E50, 0xFFFC, 0x4E58)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0xAAAA0000 })
	c.Step()
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.A[0] != 0xF000-4 || r.A[7] != 0xF000-8 {
		t.Fatalf("LINK: A0=%08X A7=%08X, want EFFC/EFF8", r.A[0], r.A[7])
	}
	c.Step()
	r = c.Registers()
	if r.A[0] != 0xAAAA0000 || r.A[7] != 0xF000 {
		t.Errorf("UNLK: A0=%08X A7=%08X, want AAAA0000/F000", r.A[0], r.A[7])
	}

	// JSR $00001010 = 0x4EB9 / RTS = 0x4E75.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x4EB9, 0x0000, 0x1010, 0x4E71)
	bus.Write16(0x1010, 0x4E75)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != 0x1010 {
		t.Fatalf("JSR PC = %08X, want 1010", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read32(0xEFFC); got != codeBase+6 {
		t.Errorf("JSR return = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+6)
	}
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+6 {
		t.Errorf("RTS PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+6)
	}

	// TRAP #5 = 0x4E45 goes through vector 37.
	c, bus = newCPU(0x4E45, 0x4E71)
	bus.Write32(37*4, 0x2000)
	c.Step()
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("TRAP PC = %08X, want 2000", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read32(0xEFFC); got != codeBase+2 {
		t.Errorf("TRAP stacked PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+2)
	}

	// CMPM.W (A0)+,(A1)+ = 0xB348 with equal words sets Z.
	c, bus = newCPU(0xB348)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x2000; r.A[1] = 0x3000 })
	bus.Write16(0x2000, 5)
	bus.Write16(0x3000, 5)
	c.Step()
	flags(t, c, srZ, 0)
	r = c.Registers()
	if r.A[0] != 0x2002 || r.A[1] != 0x3002 {
		t.Errorf("CMPM postincrement: A0=%08X A1=%08X, want 2002/3002", r.A[0], r.A[1])
	}

	// CMPA.W #$1000,A0 = 0xB0FC with A0 = 0x1000 sets Z.
	c, _ = newCPU(0xB0FC, 0x1000)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.A[0] = 0x1000 })
	c.Step()
	flags(t, c, srZ, 0)
}

func TestUserSupervisorStacks(t *testing.T) {
	// MOVE.W #$0300,SR in supervisor mode drops to user mode and swaps
	// A7 for the USP. The reset SSP is 0xF000; only USP needs staging.
	c, _ := newCPU(0x46FC, 0x0300)
	arrange(c, func(r *Registers) { r.USP = 0x9000 })
	c.Step()
	r := c.Registers()
	if r.A[7] != 0x9000 {
		t.Errorf("after drop to user, A[7] = %08X, want USP 9000", r.A[7])
	}
	if r.SSP != 0xF000 {
		t.Errorf("SSP field = %08X, want F000 (the stack we left)", r.SSP)
	}
}

func TestCycleAccounting(t *testing.T) {
	code := make([]uint16, 30)
	for i := range code {
		code[i] = 0x4E71 // NOP
	}
	c, _ := newCPU(code...)
	if n := c.Step(); n != 4 {
		t.Errorf("NOP Step = %d cycles, want 4", n)
	}
	if n := c.StepCycles(96); n != 96 {
		t.Errorf("StepCycles(96) = %d, want 96", n)
	}
	if got := c.Cycles(); got != 100 {
		t.Errorf("Cycles = %d, want 100", got)
	}
	if got := c.Registers().PC; got != codeBase+50 {
		t.Errorf("PC = %08X, want %08X", got, codeBase+50)
	}
	// MOVEQ is also 4 cycles.
	c2, _ := newCPU(0x7003)
	if n := c2.Step(); n != 4 {
		t.Errorf("MOVEQ Step = %d cycles, want 4", n)
	}
}

func TestDisassemble(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		code []uint16
		want string
		next int // words consumed
	}{
		{[]uint16{0x3018}, "MOVE.W (A0)+,D0", 1},
		{[]uint16{0xD041}, "ADD.W D1,D0", 1},
		{[]uint16{0x7003}, "MOVEQ #$03,D0", 1},
		{[]uint16{0x6000, 0xFFFC}, "BRA $000FFE", 2},
		{[]uint16{0x51C8, 0xFFFE}, "DBF D0,$001000", 2},
		{[]uint16{0x48E7, 0xE0C0}, "MOVEM.L D0-D2/A0-A1,-(A7)", 2},
		{[]uint16{0x4E75}, "RTS", 1},
		{[]uint16{0x80FC, 0x000A}, "DIVU.W #$000A,D0", 2},
		{[]uint16{0xA000}, "DC.W $A000", 1},
		{[]uint16{0x303A, 0x004E}, "MOVE.W $4E(PC),D0", 2},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		bus := newRAMBus()
		for i, w := range tc.code {
			bus.Write16(codeBase+uint32(2*i), w)
		}
		fetch := func(addr uint32) uint16 { return bus.Read16(addr) }
		got, next := Disassemble(codeBase, fetch)
		if got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("Disassemble(%04X) = %q, want %q", tc.code[0], got, tc.want)
		}
		if want := uint32(codeBase + 2*tc.next); next != want {
			t.Errorf("Disassemble(%04X) next = %08X, want %08X", tc.code[0], next, want)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/psg/psg.go ====================

// Package psg is an original implementation of the Texas Instruments
// SN76489 programmable sound generator, written from the published
// datasheet behavior and the documented Sega variant (as used in the
// Master System, Game Gear and Genesis/Mega Drive).
//
// The chip provides three square-wave tone channels and one noise
// channel. Each channel has a 4-bit attenuation (volume) register:
// 0 is loudest, each step is 2 dB down, and 15 is silent.
//
// Register access uses the chip's latch/data protocol: a byte with
// bit 7 set selects a register and carries its low 4 data bits; a byte
// with bit 7 clear is a data byte for the most recently latched
// register (the high 6 bits for a tone period, the low 4 bits for a
// volume or the noise control).
package psg

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"math/bits"
)

// Config selects chip-variant parameters.
type Config struct {
	// LFSRBits is the width of the noise shift register. The original
	// TI part uses 15 bits; the Sega variant uses 16. Zero means 15.
	LFSRBits int

	// WhiteNoiseTaps is the feedback tap mask for white-noise mode:
	// the feedback bit is the parity of (lfsr & WhiteNoiseTaps).
	// The Sega variant taps bits 0 and 3 (0x0009); the original TI
	// taps are bits 0 and 1 (0x0003), which is the default when zero.
	WhiteNoiseTaps uint32
}

// SerializeSize is the exact size of a serialized chip state.
const SerializeSize = 41

// serializeVersion identifies the state layout written by Serialize.
const serializeVersion = 1

// volumeTable maps a 4-bit attenuation value to a linear amplitude.
// Each step is 2 dB, so the ratio between steps is 10^(-2/20).
var volumeTable = [16]float32{
	1.0, 0.7943, 0.6310, 0.5012,
	0.3981, 0.3162, 0.2512, 0.1995,
	0.1585, 0.1259, 0.1, 0.0794,
	0.0631, 0.0501, 0.0398, 0.0,
}

// noiseRates maps the noise control register's two rate bits to the
// shift period of the rate source, in input clocks, for rates 0-2.
// Rate 3 slaves the noise channel to tone channel 3's output instead.
var noiseRates = [3]int{512, 1024, 2048}

// PSG is a single SN76489 chip instance.
type PSG struct {
	clockFreq  int
	sampleRate int

	// Register file. periods holds the 10-bit tone period registers;
	// volumes holds the 4-bit attenuation for all four channels
	// (index 3 is the noise channel). latched is the register most
	// recently selected by a latch byte, encoded as channel*2+type
	// (type 0 = period/control, 1 = volume).
	periods [3]uint16
	volumes [4]uint8
	latched int

	// Tone generator state: down-counters and output polarity
	// (true = positive half-cycle).
	counters [3]int
	polarity [3]bool

	// Noise generator state.
	noiseCtl uint8 // bit 2: white (1) vs periodic (0); bits 1-0: rate
	lfsr     uint32
	lfsrBits int
	taps     uint32
	// noisePhase advances the fixed-rate clock source (a square wave
	// with the period from noiseRates); noisePrevLevel is the source
	// level seen on the previous input clock, for falling-edge
	// detection.
	noisePhase     int
	noisePrevLevel bool

	// clockDiv counts input clocks toward the next tone tick; the
	// tone counters decrement once per 16 input clocks.
	clockDiv int

	// samplePhase is the fractional sample accumulator, in units of
	// input clocks scaled by sampleRate: it advances by sampleRate
	// per input clock and emits a sample each time it reaches
	// clockFreq, so the long-run sample rate is exact.
	samplePhase int64

	// Output buffer: buffer[:count] holds generated samples not yet
	// drained by the caller.
	buffer []float32
	count  int
}

// New returns a PSG in its power-on state, clocked at clockFreq Hz and
// producing samples at sampleRate Hz into a buffer that holds at most
// bufferSize samples.
//
// Power-on state (the datasheet leaves the register file undefined
// until software writes it; these are the deterministic defaults
// chosen here): periods 0 (which behave as 1024), volumes 15
// (silent), counters loaded with the effective period, tone outputs
// positive, noise control 0, the latch pointing at tone channel 0's
// period register, and the noise register seeded.
func New(clockFreq, sampleRate, bufferSize int, config Config) *PSG {
	if clockFreq <= 0 {
		clockFreq = 3579545 // NTSC color-burst rate used by Sega
	}
	if sampleRate <= 0 {
		sampleRate = 44100
	}
	if bufferSize <= 0 {
		bufferSize = 4096
	}
	lfsrBits := config.LFSRBits
	if lfsrBits == 0 {
		lfsrBits = 15
	}
	if lfsrBits < 2 {
		lfsrBits = 2
	}
	if lfsrBits > 32 {
		lfsrBits = 32
	}
	taps := config.WhiteNoiseTaps
	if taps == 0 {
		taps = 0x0003 // original TI taps: bits 0 and 1
	}
	p := &PSG{
		clockFreq:  clockFreq,
		sampleRate: sampleRate,
		volumes:    [4]uint8{15, 15, 15, 15},
		polarity:   [3]bool{true, true, true},
		lfsrBits:   lfsrBits,
		taps:       taps,
		buffer:     make([]float32, bufferSize),
	}
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		p.counters[ch] = p.effectivePeriod(ch)
	}
	p.resetLFSR()
	p.noisePrevLevel = p.noiseSourceLevel()
	return p
}

// effectivePeriod returns the counter reload value for a tone channel.
// A period register of 0 behaves as 1024 on the Sega variant (the
// 10-bit counter simply counts through the full range).
func (p *PSG) effectivePeriod(ch int) int {
	if p.periods[ch] == 0 {
		return 1024
	}
	return int(p.periods[ch])
}

// resetLFSR seeds the noise shift register with a single bit in the
// top position.
func (p *PSG) resetLFSR() {
	p.lfsr = 1 << uint(p.lfsrBits-1)
}

// lfsrMask trims the shift register to its configured width.
func (p *PSG) lfsrMask() uint32 {
	if p.lfsrBits >= 32 {
		return 0xFFFFFFFF
	}
	return (uint32(1) << uint(p.lfsrBits)) - 1
}

// Write feeds one byte to the chip's control port. A byte with bit 7
// set is a latch/data byte: bits 6-5 select the channel, bit 4 the
// register type (0 = period/control, 1 = volume), and bits 3-0 are
// the low 4 data bits, applied immediately. A byte with bit 7 clear
// is a data byte for the latched register: bits 5-0 supply the high
// 6 bits of a tone period, or replace the low 4 bits of a volume or
// the noise control.
func (p *PSG) Write(value uint8) {
	if value&0x80 != 0 {
		p.latched = int(value>>4) & 0x07
		p.writeRegister(p.latched, value&0x0F, true)
		return
	}
	p.writeRegister(p.latched, value&0x3F, false)
}

// writeRegister applies data to register reg. latch reports whether
// the write came from a latch byte (low 4 bits of data) as opposed to
// a data byte (6 bits).
func (p *PSG) writeRegister(reg int, data uint8, latch bool) {
	channel := reg >> 1
	isVolume := reg&1 != 0
	switch {
	case isVolume:
		p.volumes[channel] = data & 0x0F
	case channel == 3:
		// Noise control. Writing it reseeds the shift register.
		p.noiseCtl = data & 0x0F
		p.resetLFSR()
		// A register write must not itself look like a clock edge:
		// resync the edge detector to the (possibly new) source.
		p.noisePrevLevel = p.noiseSourceLevel()
	default:
		// Tone period: a latch byte loads the low 4 bits, a data
		// byte loads the high 6 bits; the other bits are retained.
		if latch {
			p.periods[channel] = p.periods[channel]&0x3F0 | uint16(data&0x0F)
		} else {
			p.periods[channel] = p.periods[channel]&0x00F | uint16(data&0x3F)<<4
		}
	}
}

// GenerateSamples advances the chip by the given number of input
// clocks and generates output samples into the internal buffer,
// which the caller drains with GetBuffer and ResetBuffer.
//
// Overflow policy: chip time always advances by the full clock count.
// Samples that would exceed the buffer's capacity are still
// generated (the chip state advances identically) but discarded;
// the return value is the number of samples actually stored during
// this call.
func (p *PSG) GenerateSamples(clocks int) int {
	stored := 0
	remaining := clocks
	for remaining > 0 {
		// Clocks until the next output sample: the phase
		// accumulator advances sampleRate per clock and emits
		// when it reaches clockFreq, so the next emission is
		// ceil((clockFreq - phase) / sampleRate) clocks away.
		// Chip state between sample points only matters through
		// the noise channel's edge counting, which advanceClocks
		// handles in bulk, so the span can be crossed at once.
		step := int((int64(p.clockFreq) - p.samplePhase + int64(p.sampleRate) - 1) / int64(p.sampleRate))
		if step > remaining {
			step = remaining
		}
		p.advanceClocks(step)
		remaining -= step
		p.samplePhase += int64(step) * int64(p.sampleRate)
		if p.samplePhase >= int64(p.clockFreq) {
			p.samplePhase -= int64(p.clockFreq)
			if p.count < len(p.buffer) {
				p.buffer[p.count] = p.output()
				p.count++
				stored++
			}
		}
	}
	return stored
}

// GetBuffer returns the sample buffer and the number of valid
// samples at its front.
func (p *PSG) GetBuffer() ([]float32, int) {
	return p.buffer, p.count
}

// ResetBuffer discards all buffered samples.
func (p *PSG) ResetBuffer() {
	p.count = 0
}

// output is the chip's instantaneous analog output. The hardware
// output stage is unipolar: each channel contributes its volume
// while its generator is in the high state and nothing while low
// (for noise, the shift register's bit 0 is that state). The four
// channels are summed and normalized by 4. (Verified against the
// reference chip's observable output in the differential harness:
// bipolar drive differs only by a DC offset and a factor of 2, but
// drop-in equivalence is exact in this convention.)
func (p *PSG) output() float32 {
	var sum float32
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		if p.polarity[ch] {
			sum += volumeTable[p.volumes[ch]]
		}
	}
	if p.lfsr&1 != 0 {
		sum += volumeTable[p.volumes[3]]
	}
	return sum * 0.25
}

// advanceClocks advances the chip by n input clocks, exactly as n
// stepClock calls would, but computed in bulk: the tone counters
// move by whole ticks with arithmetic flip counts, and the noise
// register shifts once per falling edge of its clock source inside
// the span. (The chip used to be stepped one clock at a time,
// some 60,000 calls per emulated frame, almost all of which only
// decremented counters.)
func (p *PSG) advanceClocks(n int) {
	if n <= 0 {
		return
	}
	// Tone ticks land once per 16 input clocks, phased by
	// clockDiv: tick boundaries in the span are the clocks where
	// clockDiv wraps.
	total := p.clockDiv + n
	ticks := total / 16
	p.clockDiv = total % 16
	pol3Before := p.polarity[2]
	flips3 := 0
	if ticks > 0 {
		for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
			if f := p.advanceTone(ch, ticks); ch == 2 {
				flips3 = f
			}
		}
	}
	p.advanceNoise(n, pol3Before, flips3)
}

// advanceTone moves one tone channel forward by the given number
// of tone ticks and returns how many times its output flipped.
// The per-tick rule is: decrement, and on reaching zero reload
// with the effective period and flip. A counter in [1, period]
// first flips after exactly counter ticks, then every period
// ticks. A counter outside that range (only reachable through a
// hand-crafted state) falls back to the literal per-tick walk.
func (p *PSG) advanceTone(ch, ticks int) int {
	c := p.counters[ch]
	per := p.effectivePeriod(ch)
	if c < 1 || c > per {
		flips := 0
		for i := 0; i < ticks; i++ {
			c--
			if c <= 0 {
				c += per
				p.polarity[ch] = !p.polarity[ch]
				flips++
			}
		}
		p.counters[ch] = c
		return flips
	}
	if ticks < c {
		p.counters[ch] = c - ticks
		return 0
	}
	flips := 1 + (ticks-c)/per
	p.counters[ch] = per - (ticks-c)%per
	if flips&1 != 0 {
		p.polarity[ch] = !p.polarity[ch]
	}
	return flips
}

// advanceNoise advances the noise channel over n input clocks.
// Tone channel 3's flip count inside the span is supplied because
// in slaved mode (rate bits 3) that channel's output is the noise
// clock source: each of its high-to-low flips shifts the register
// once. In the fixed-rate modes the source is the phase square
// wave, high while noisePhase*2 < rate after each clock's
// increment; the falling edge is the clock whose increment lands
// the phase on rate/2, which the span crosses a computable number
// of times.
func (p *PSG) advanceNoise(n int, pol3Before bool, flips3 int) {
	if p.noiseCtl&0x03 == 0x03 {
		edges := flips3 / 2
		if pol3Before && flips3&1 != 0 {
			edges++
		}
		for i := 0; i < edges; i++ {
			p.shiftNoise()
		}
		p.noisePrevLevel = p.polarity[2]
		return
	}
	rate := noiseRates[p.noiseCtl&0x03]
	target := rate / 2 // first low phase; rates are even (see noiseRates)
	first := (target - p.noisePhase) % rate
	if first <= 0 {
		first += rate
	}
	if first <= n {
		edges := 1 + (n-first)/rate
		for i := 0; i < edges; i++ {
			p.shiftNoise()
		}
	}
	p.noisePhase = (p.noisePhase + n) % rate
	p.noisePrevLevel = p.noisePhase*2 < rate
}

// noiseSourceLevel reports the current level of the noise clock
// source. The fixed rates are modeled as a square wave with the
// documented period, high for its first half; rate 3 is tone
// channel 3's output polarity.
func (p *PSG) noiseSourceLevel() bool {
	if p.noiseCtl&0x03 == 0x03 {
		return p.polarity[2]
	}
	rate := noiseRates[p.noiseCtl&0x03]
	return p.noisePhase*2 < rate
}

// shiftNoise advances the noise shift register by one step. In white
// noise mode the feedback bit is the parity of the tapped bits; in
// periodic mode the output bit itself rotates back into the top, so
// the seed pattern repeats every LFSRBits shifts and the output bit
// is high once per repetition.
func (p *PSG) shiftNoise() {
	var feedback uint32
	if p.noiseCtl&0x04 != 0 {
		feedback = uint32(bits.OnesCount32(p.lfsr&p.taps) & 1)
	} else {
		feedback = p.lfsr & 1
	}
	p.lfsr = (p.lfsr >> 1) | feedback<<uint(p.lfsrBits-1)
	p.lfsr &= p.lfsrMask()
}

// Serialize writes the complete chip state into buf, which must be
// at least SerializeSize bytes. The state covers every register and
// counter, including the fractional sample timing, so a restored
// chip continues sample-exactly. Samples sitting in the output
// buffer are not part of the state (callers drain before saving);
// a chip restored by Deserialize starts with an empty buffer.
func (p *PSG) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("psg: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	out := buf[:SerializeSize]
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = 0
	}
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[1+2*ch:], p.periods[ch])
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[7+2*ch:], uint16(p.counters[ch]))
	}
	copy(out[13:17], p.volumes[:])
	out[17] = p.noiseCtl
	out[18] = uint8(p.latched)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[19:23], p.lfsr)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[23:25], uint16(p.noisePhase))
	out[25] = uint8(p.clockDiv)
	var flags uint8
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		if p.polarity[ch] {
			flags |= 1 << uint(ch)
		}
	}
	if p.noisePrevLevel {
		flags |= 1 << 3
	}
	out[26] = flags
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(out[27:35], uint64(p.samplePhase))
	out[35] = uint8(p.lfsrBits)
	// Bytes 36-40 are reserved and stay zero.
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. The restoring
// chip should have the same clock/sample rates and variant config;
// the saved shift register is trimmed to this chip's LFSR width.
func (p *PSG) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("psg: deserialize buffer too small")
	}
	in := buf[:SerializeSize]
	if in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("psg: unsupported serialize version")
	}
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		p.periods[ch] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[1+2*ch:]) & 0x3FF
		p.counters[ch] = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[7+2*ch:]))
	}
	for i := range p.volumes {
		p.volumes[i] = in[13+i] & 0x0F
	}
	p.noiseCtl = in[17] & 0x0F
	p.latched = int(in[18]) & 0x07
	p.lfsr = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[19:23]) & p.lfsrMask()
	p.noisePhase = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[23:25]))
	p.clockDiv = int(in[25]) & 0x0F
	flags := in[26]
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		p.polarity[ch] = flags&(1<<uint(ch)) != 0
	}
	p.noisePrevLevel = flags&(1<<3) != 0
	p.samplePhase = int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(in[27:35]))
	p.count = 0
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/psg/psg_test.go ====================

package psg

import (
	"bytes"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

var segaConfig = Config{LFSRBits: 16, WhiteNoiseTaps: 0x0009}

// The latch byte selects a register (bits 6-5 channel, bit 4 type)
// and loads its low 4 data bits at once; a following data byte
// supplies the high 6 bits of a tone period or replaces the low 4
// bits of a volume.
func TestLatchProtocol(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 1024, segaConfig)

	p.Write(0x8A) // latch tone 0 period, low bits 0xA
	if p.latched != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("latched = %d, want 0", p.latched)
	}
	if p.periods[0] != 0x00A {
		t.Fatalf("periods[0] = %#x, want 0x00a", p.periods[0])
	}
	p.Write(0x3F) // data byte: high 6 bits
	if p.periods[0] != 0x3FA {
		t.Fatalf("periods[0] = %#x, want 0x3fa", p.periods[0])
	}
	p.Write(0x85) // latch again: only the low 4 bits change
	if p.periods[0] != 0x3F5 {
		t.Fatalf("periods[0] = %#x, want 0x3f5", p.periods[0])
	}

	p.Write(0x9B) // latch tone 0 volume = 11
	if p.volumes[0] != 11 {
		t.Fatalf("volumes[0] = %d, want 11", p.volumes[0])
	}
	p.Write(0x36) // data byte replaces the volume's low bits
	if p.volumes[0] != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("volumes[0] = %d, want 6", p.volumes[0])
	}

	p.Write(0xA7) // latch tone 1 period, low bits 7
	if p.periods[1] != 0x007 {
		t.Fatalf("periods[1] = %#x, want 0x007", p.periods[1])
	}

	p.Write(0xF9) // latch noise volume = 9
	if p.volumes[3] != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("volumes[3] = %d, want 9", p.volumes[3])
	}
}

// Writing the noise control register applies the low bits and
// reseeds the shift register, for both latch and data byte writes.
func TestNoiseControlWrite(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 256, segaConfig)
	p.Write(0xE4) // white noise, rate 0
	if p.noiseCtl != 0x04 {
		t.Fatalf("noiseCtl = %#x, want 0x04", p.noiseCtl)
	}
	if p.lfsr != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("lfsr = %#x, want seed 0x8000", p.lfsr)
	}
	p.shiftNoise()
	p.shiftNoise()
	if p.lfsr == 0x8000 {
		t.Fatal("lfsr did not advance")
	}
	p.Write(0x07) // data byte to the latched noise control
	if p.noiseCtl != 0x07 {
		t.Fatalf("noiseCtl = %#x, want 0x07", p.noiseCtl)
	}
	if p.lfsr != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("lfsr = %#x, want reseeded 0x8000", p.lfsr)
	}
}

// With sampleRate == clockFreq every input clock yields one sample,
// which exposes the tone waveform directly: the counter decrements
// once per 16 clocks, so with period 4 the output polarity flips
// every 64 samples.
func TestToneWaveform(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(16384, 16384, 4096, segaConfig)
	p.Write(0x84) // tone 0 period low = 4
	p.Write(0x00) // tone 0 period high = 0
	p.Write(0x90) // tone 0 volume = 0 (loudest)
	p.counters[0] = 4
	p.polarity[0] = true

	if n := p.GenerateSamples(200); n != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("GenerateSamples returned %d, want 200", n)
	}
	buf, n := p.GetBuffer()
	if n != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("buffered %d samples, want 200", n)
	}
	// First toggle at clock 64, second at clock 128. Output is
	// unipolar and normalized: high state = volume/4, low = 0.
	for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
		want := float32(0.25)
		if i >= 63 && i < 127 || i >= 191 {
			want = 0
		}
		if buf[i] != want {
			t.Fatalf("sample %d = %v, want %v", i, buf[i], want)
		}
	}
}

// A period register of 0 counts through the full 10-bit range:
// the first toggle takes 1024 counter ticks = 16384 input clocks.
func TestPeriodZeroIs1024(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(16384, 16384, 64, segaConfig)
	// periods[0] is 0 and counters[0] starts at 1024 from New.
	p.GenerateSamples(16383)
	if !p.polarity[0] {
		t.Fatal("polarity toggled before 16384 clocks")
	}
	p.GenerateSamples(1)
	if p.polarity[0] {
		t.Fatal("polarity did not toggle at 16384 clocks")
	}
}

// The attenuation table: 2 dB steps from 1.0 down to silence at 15.
// Output is unipolar and normalized by 4: a channel contributes
// table[vol]/4 while its generator is high, nothing while low.
func TestVolumeTable(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 256, segaConfig)
	close := func(got, want float32) bool {
		return math.Abs(float64(got-want)) < 1e-4
	}
	// Other channels sit at attenuation 15 (amplitude 0), so the
	// output is tone 0 alone.
	p.volumes[0] = 0
	p.polarity[0] = true
	if got := p.output(); got != 0.25 {
		t.Fatalf("output at volume 0 = %v, want 0.25", got)
	}
	for vol, want := range map[uint8]float32{
		1: 0.1986, 2: 0.1578, 5: 0.0791, 10: 0.025, 14: 0.0100, 15: 0.0,
	} {
		p.volumes[0] = vol
		if got := p.output(); !close(got, want) {
			t.Fatalf("output at volume %d = %v, want %v", vol, got, want)
		}
	}
	p.volumes[0] = 0
	p.polarity[0] = false
	if got := p.output(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("output in low state = %v, want 0", got)
	}
	// All four channels loud and in the high state sum to 1.0.
	p.polarity = [3]bool{true, true, true}
	p.volumes = [4]uint8{0, 0, 0, 0}
	p.lfsr |= 1
	if got := p.output(); got != 1.0 {
		t.Fatalf("full sum = %v, want 1.0", got)
	}
}

// The white-noise LFSR sequence for the Sega configuration (16-bit,
// taps on bits 0 and 3), worked out from the documented rule:
// feedback = parity(lfsr & 0x0009), shifting right, seed 0x8000.
func TestNoiseLFSRSequenceWhite(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 256, segaConfig)
	p.Write(0xE4) // white noise, rate 0
	wantStates := []uint32{
		0x8000, 0x4000, 0x2000, 0x1000, 0x0800, 0x0400, 0x0200, 0x0100,
		0x0080, 0x0040, 0x0020, 0x0010, 0x0008, 0x8004, 0x4002, 0x2001,
		0x9000, 0x4800, 0x2400, 0x1200, 0x0900, 0x0480, 0x0240, 0x0120,
		0x0090, 0x0048, 0x8024, 0x4012, 0x2009, 0x1004, 0x0802, 0x0401,
		0x8200,
	}
	// Output bit (bit 0) read at each state, before shifting.
	wantBits := "0000000000000001" + "0000000000001001" + "0"
	gotBits := make([]byte, 0, len(wantStates))
	for i, want := range wantStates {
		if p.lfsr != want {
			t.Fatalf("state %d: lfsr = %#06x, want %#06x", i, p.lfsr, want)
		}
		if p.lfsr&1 != 0 {
			gotBits = append(gotBits, '1')
		} else {
			gotBits = append(gotBits, '0')
		}
		p.shiftNoise()
	}
	if string(gotBits) != wantBits {
		t.Fatalf("output bits = %s, want %s", gotBits, wantBits)
	}
}

// In periodic mode the seed bit rotates through the register: the
// output is high for exactly one shift in every LFSRBits shifts and
// the register returns to the seed after a full rotation.
func TestNoisePeriodic(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 256, segaConfig)
	p.Write(0xE0) // periodic noise, rate 0
	ones := 0
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if p.lfsr&1 != 0 {
			ones++
		}
		p.shiftNoise()
	}
	if ones != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("output high %d times in 16 shifts, want 1", ones)
	}
	if p.lfsr != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("lfsr after full rotation = %#06x, want 0x8000", p.lfsr)
	}
}

// At fixed rate 0 the rate source is a 512-clock square wave, so
// shifts land on its falling edges: clocks 256, 768, ...
func TestNoiseFixedRateTiming(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 8192, segaConfig)
	p.Write(0xE4) // white noise, rate 0
	p.GenerateSamples(255)
	if p.lfsr != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("after 255 clocks lfsr = %#06x, want 0x8000", p.lfsr)
	}
	p.GenerateSamples(1)
	if p.lfsr != 0x4000 {
		t.Fatalf("after 256 clocks lfsr = %#06x, want 0x4000", p.lfsr)
	}
	p.GenerateSamples(511)
	if p.lfsr != 0x4000 {
		t.Fatalf("after 767 clocks lfsr = %#06x, want 0x4000", p.lfsr)
	}
	p.GenerateSamples(1)
	if p.lfsr != 0x2000 {
		t.Fatalf("after 768 clocks lfsr = %#06x, want 0x2000", p.lfsr)
	}
}

// Rate 3 slaves the noise shift to tone channel 3's output: shifts
// happen on its falling edges only.
func TestNoiseSlavedToTone3(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 256, segaConfig)
	p.Write(0xC1) // tone 3 (channel 2) period low = 1
	p.Write(0x00) // period high = 0
	p.counters[2] = 1
	p.polarity[2] = true
	p.Write(0xE7) // white noise, rate 3 (slaved)
	if p.lfsr != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("lfsr = %#06x, want seed 0x8000", p.lfsr)
	}
	// Tone 3 toggles every 16 clocks; falling edges at 16, 48, ...
	p.GenerateSamples(16)
	if p.lfsr != 0x4000 {
		t.Fatalf("after falling edge lfsr = %#06x, want 0x4000", p.lfsr)
	}
	p.GenerateSamples(16)
	if p.lfsr != 0x4000 {
		t.Fatalf("after rising edge lfsr = %#06x, want 0x4000", p.lfsr)
	}
	p.GenerateSamples(16)
	if p.lfsr != 0x2000 {
		t.Fatalf("after second falling edge lfsr = %#06x, want 0x2000", p.lfsr)
	}
}

// Config defaults: zero LFSRBits selects the 15-bit TI register
// (seed 0x4000) and zero taps select the TI taps 0x0003; the Sega
// config seeds 0x8000.
func TestConfigDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(0, 0, 0, Config{})
	if p.clockFreq != 3579545 || p.sampleRate != 44100 {
		t.Fatalf("rate defaults = %d/%d, want 3579545/44100", p.clockFreq, p.sampleRate)
	}
	if len(p.buffer) != 4096 {
		t.Fatalf("buffer size = %d, want 4096", len(p.buffer))
	}
	if p.lfsrBits != 15 || p.taps != 0x0003 {
		t.Fatalf("config defaults = %d bits, taps %#x; want 15, 0x0003", p.lfsrBits, p.taps)
	}
	p.Write(0xE4)
	if p.lfsr != 0x4000 {
		t.Fatalf("15-bit seed = %#06x, want 0x4000", p.lfsr)
	}

	q := New(3579545, 44100, 128, segaConfig)
	q.Write(0xE4)
	if q.lfsr != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("16-bit seed = %#06x, want 0x8000", q.lfsr)
	}
}

// The fractional accumulator must be exact over the long run: one
// second of input clocks produces exactly one second of samples.
func TestSampleRateExact(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 100000, segaConfig)
	if n := p.GenerateSamples(3579545); n != 44100 {
		t.Fatalf("generated %d samples for 1s of clocks, want 44100", n)
	}
	if p.samplePhase != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("residual phase = %d, want 0", p.samplePhase)
	}
}

// Overflow policy: chip time advances in full, samples beyond the
// buffer capacity are discarded, and the return value counts only
// the samples actually stored.
func TestBufferOverflow(t *testing.T) {
	p := New(48000, 48000, 8, segaConfig) // one sample per clock
	if n := p.GenerateSamples(100); n != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("stored %d samples, want 8", n)
	}
	if _, n := p.GetBuffer(); n != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("buffered %d samples, want 8", n)
	}
	if n := p.GenerateSamples(100); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("stored %d samples into a full buffer, want 0", n)
	}
	// Time still advanced: 200 clocks = 12 tone ticks (at 16, 32,
	// ...) plus 8 more clocks, so the counter dropped by 12.
	if p.counters[0] != 1024-12 {
		t.Fatalf("counter = %d, want %d", p.counters[0], 1012)
	}
	p.ResetBuffer()
	if n := p.GenerateSamples(3); n != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("stored %d samples after reset, want 3", n)
	}
}

// A state captured mid-stream must restore exactly: re-serializing
// gives identical bytes and the restored chip generates identical
// samples going forward.
func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	if SerializeSize != 41 {
		t.Fatalf("SerializeSize = %d, want 41", SerializeSize)
	}
	p := New(3579545, 44100, 2048, segaConfig)
	p.Write(0x8C)            // tone 0 period low = 0xC
	p.Write(0x2B)            // tone 0 period high = 0x2B -> period 0x2BC
	p.Write(0x93)            // tone 0 volume = 3
	p.Write(0xA4)            // tone 1 period low = 4
	p.Write(0x06)            // tone 1 period high = 6
	p.Write(0xE5)            // white noise, rate 1
	p.Write(0xF5)            // noise volume = 5
	p.GenerateSamples(12345) // odd counts: fractional state everywhere
	p.ResetBuffer()

	state := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := p.Serialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	q := New(3579545, 44100, 2048, segaConfig)
	if err := q.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	restored := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := q.Serialize(restored); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(state, restored) {
		t.Fatalf("state mismatch after round trip:\n%x\n%x", state, restored)
	}

	np := p.GenerateSamples(5000)
	nq := q.GenerateSamples(5000)
	if np != nq {
		t.Fatalf("sample counts diverge: %d vs %d", np, nq)
	}
	pb, _ := p.GetBuffer()
	qb, _ := q.GetBuffer()
	for i := 0; i < np; i++ {
		if pb[i] != qb[i] {
			t.Fatalf("sample %d diverges: %v vs %v", i, pb[i], qb[i])
		}
	}

	if err := p.Serialize(make([]byte, SerializeSize-1)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Serialize accepted a short buffer")
	}
	if err := q.Deserialize(make([]byte, SerializeSize-1)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a short buffer")
	}
	bad := bytes.Clone(state)
	bad[0] = 0xFF
	if err := q.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted an unknown version")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/z80/cb.go ====================

package z80

// rotShift applies the CB rotate/shift operation selected by y
// (0=RLC, 1=RRC, 2=RL, 3=RR, 4=SLA, 5=SRA, 6=SLL, 7=SRL) to v,
// setting the shift group flags: S/Z/Y/X and parity from the
// result, H and N clear, C holding the bit shifted out.
func (c *CPU) rotShift(y int, v uint8) uint8 {
	oldC := c.f & flagC
	var res, out uint8
	switch y {
	case 0: // RLC
		out = v >> 7
		res = v<<1 | out
	case 1: // RRC
		out = v & 1
		res = v>>1 | out<<7
	case 2: // RL
		out = v >> 7
		res = v<<1 | oldC
	case 3: // RR
		out = v & 1
		res = v>>1 | oldC<<7
	case 4: // SLA
		out = v >> 7
		res = v << 1
	case 5: // SRA
		out = v & 1
		res = v>>1 | (v & 0x80)
	case 6: // SLL (documented undocumented shift: a 1 enters bit 0)
		out = v >> 7
		res = v<<1 | 1
	default: // SRL
		out = v & 1
		res = v >> 1
	}
	c.f = szpFlags(res) | out
	return res
}

// bitTest sets the BIT group flags for bit y of v. yxSource supplies
// the undocumented Y/X bits: the operand itself for register forms,
// or the high byte of the effective address (the WZ register) for
// memory forms. PV mirrors Z, S is set only for bit 7 when set,
// H is set, N clear, C preserved.
func (c *CPU) bitTest(y int, v uint8, yxSource uint8) {
	f := c.f&flagC | flagH
	if v&(1<<uint(y)) == 0 {
		f |= flagZ | flagPV
	}
	if y == 7 && v&0x80 != 0 {
		f |= flagS
	}
	f |= yxSource & (flagY | flagX)
	c.f = f
}

// execCB executes a CB-prefixed opcode. The opcode byte itself is
// fetched here (an M1 cycle, bumping R).
func (c *CPU) execCB() int {
	op := c.fetchOpcode()
	y := int(op>>3) & 7
	z := int(op) & 7
	switch op >> 6 {
	case 0: // rotates and shifts
		if z == 6 {
			hl := c.hl()
			c.bus.Write(hl, c.rotShift(y, c.bus.Read(hl)))
			return 15
		}
		c.setReg(z, c.rotShift(y, c.reg(z)))
		return 8
	case 1: // BIT
		if z == 6 {
			// For (HL), the Y/X bits come from the high byte of
			// the address (WZ = HL).
			c.bitTest(y, c.bus.Read(c.hl()), c.h)
			return 12
		}
		v := c.reg(z)
		c.bitTest(y, v, v)
		return 8
	case 2: // RES
		mask := ^(1 << uint(y))
		if z == 6 {
			hl := c.hl()
			c.bus.Write(hl, c.bus.Read(hl)&uint8(mask))
			return 15
		}
		c.setReg(z, c.reg(z)&uint8(mask))
		return 8
	default: // SET
		mask := uint8(1 << uint(y))
		if z == 6 {
			hl := c.hl()
			c.bus.Write(hl, c.bus.Read(hl)|mask)
			return 15
		}
		c.setReg(z, c.reg(z)|mask)
		return 8
	}
}

// execIndexedCB executes a DDCB/FDCB sequence: the displacement byte
// comes first (a plain read), then the opcode (an M1 cycle). For the
// shift and RES/SET groups, an operand field other than (HL) also
// copies the result into that register, as documented; BIT only
// tests the memory byte. Timing is 23 T-states, 20 for BIT.
func (c *CPU) execIndexedCB(idx *uint16) int {
	d := int8(c.operand())
	op := c.fetchOpcode()
	addr := uint16(int32(*idx) + int32(d))
	y := int(op>>3) & 7
	z := int(op) & 7
	switch op >> 6 {
	case 0: // rotates and shifts on (IX+d), with register copy
		res := c.rotShift(y, c.bus.Read(addr))
		c.bus.Write(addr, res)
		if z != 6 {
			c.setReg(z, res)
		}
		return 23
	case 1: // BIT: no write-back, no register copy
		c.bitTest(y, c.bus.Read(addr), uint8(addr>>8))
		return 20
	case 2: // RES
		res := c.bus.Read(addr) & ^(1 << uint(y))
		c.bus.Write(addr, res)
		if z != 6 {
			c.setReg(z, res)
		}
		return 23
	default: // SET
		res := c.bus.Read(addr) | (1 << uint(y))
		c.bus.Write(addr, res)
		if z != 6 {
			c.setReg(z, res)
		}
		return 23
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/z80/cpu.go ====================

// Package z80 is an original implementation of the Zilog Z80 CPU,
// written from the behaviour documented in the Z80 CPU User Manual
// (instruction set, flag effects, T-state counts) and from publicly
// documented flag research for the undocumented flag bits (z80.info).
//
// The implementation is a straightforward fetch/decode/execute core:
// one Step runs exactly one instruction, one iteration of a repeating
// block instruction (with PC left pointing at the instruction, exactly
// as the hardware re-fetches it), or one 4 T-state HALT idle cycle.
package z80

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Bus is the machine interface the CPU drives. Fetch is used for
// opcode bytes (the M1 cycles), Read/Write for operands and data,
// In/Out for I/O port cycles.
type Bus interface {
	Fetch(addr uint16) uint8
	Read(addr uint16) uint8
	Write(addr uint16, val uint8)
	In(port uint16) uint8
	Out(port uint16, val uint8)
}

// Flag bit positions inside the F register.
const (
	flagS  = 0x80 // sign
	flagZ  = 0x40 // zero
	flagY  = 0x20 // bit 5 of result (undocumented)
	flagH  = 0x10 // half carry
	flagX  = 0x08 // bit 3 of result (undocumented)
	flagPV = 0x04 // parity / signed overflow
	flagN  = 0x02 // last ALU op was a subtraction
	flagC  = 0x01 // carry
)

// Registers is a snapshot of the programmer-visible CPU state.
type Registers struct {
	AF, BC, DE, HL     uint16
	AFShadow, BCShadow uint16
	DEShadow, HLShadow uint16
	IX, IY, SP, PC     uint16
	I, R               uint8
	IFF1, IFF2         bool
	IM                 uint8
	Halted             bool
}

// CPU is the Z80 state. The zero value is not usable; call New.
type CPU struct {
	bus Bus

	a, f uint8
	b, c uint8
	d, e uint8
	h, l uint8

	// Shadow (alternate) register set, swapped by EX AF,AF' and EXX.
	a2, f2 uint8
	b2, c2 uint8
	d2, e2 uint8
	h2, l2 uint8

	ix, iy uint16
	sp, pc uint16

	i, r   uint8 // interrupt vector base, memory refresh counter
	iff1   bool
	iff2   bool
	im     uint8
	halted bool
	cycles uint64

	intLine    bool  // level-triggered INT input
	intData    uint8 // byte the interrupting device puts on the bus
	nmiPending bool  // latched NMI request (edge triggered on real hardware)
	inhibitInt bool  // set by EI: no acceptance until after the next instruction
}

// New returns a CPU in its reset state, attached to bus.
func New(bus Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{bus: bus}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Reset restores the power-on state documented in the manual:
// PC = 0, I = 0, R = 0, interrupts disabled, interrupt mode 0.
// AF and SP take the conventional 0xFFFF initial values.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	c.a, c.f = 0xFF, 0xFF
	c.b, c.c = 0, 0
	c.d, c.e = 0, 0
	c.h, c.l = 0, 0
	c.a2, c.f2 = 0xFF, 0xFF
	c.b2, c.c2 = 0, 0
	c.d2, c.e2 = 0, 0
	c.h2, c.l2 = 0, 0
	c.ix, c.iy = 0, 0
	c.sp = 0xFFFF
	c.pc = 0x0000
	c.i, c.r = 0, 0
	c.iff1, c.iff2 = false, false
	c.im = 0
	c.halted = false
	c.cycles = 0
	c.intLine = false
	c.intData = 0
	c.nmiPending = false
	c.inhibitInt = false
}

// Cycles returns the total number of T-states executed since reset
// (or since the state was loaded), including interrupt responses.
func (c *CPU) Cycles() uint64 { return c.cycles }

// Registers returns a copy of the programmer-visible state.
func (c *CPU) Registers() Registers {
	return Registers{
		AF:       uint16(c.a)<<8 | uint16(c.f),
		BC:       c.bc(),
		DE:       c.de(),
		HL:       c.hl(),
		AFShadow: uint16(c.a2)<<8 | uint16(c.f2),
		BCShadow: uint16(c.b2)<<8 | uint16(c.c2),
		DEShadow: uint16(c.d2)<<8 | uint16(c.e2),
		HLShadow: uint16(c.h2)<<8 | uint16(c.l2),
		IX:       c.ix,
		IY:       c.iy,
		SP:       c.sp,
		PC:       c.pc,
		I:        c.i,
		R:        c.r,
		IFF1:     c.iff1,
		IFF2:     c.iff2,
		IM:       c.im,
		Halted:   c.halted,
	}
}

// SetState replaces the programmer-visible state. Cycle count and
// interrupt line state are not part of Registers and are untouched.
func (c *CPU) SetState(reg Registers) {
	c.a, c.f = uint8(reg.AF>>8), uint8(reg.AF)
	c.setBC(reg.BC)
	c.setDE(reg.DE)
	c.setHL(reg.HL)
	c.a2, c.f2 = uint8(reg.AFShadow>>8), uint8(reg.AFShadow)
	c.b2, c.c2 = uint8(reg.BCShadow>>8), uint8(reg.BCShadow)
	c.d2, c.e2 = uint8(reg.DEShadow>>8), uint8(reg.DEShadow)
	c.h2, c.l2 = uint8(reg.HLShadow>>8), uint8(reg.HLShadow)
	c.ix, c.iy = reg.IX, reg.IY
	c.sp, c.pc = reg.SP, reg.PC
	c.i, c.r = reg.I, reg.R
	c.iff1, c.iff2 = reg.IFF1, reg.IFF2
	c.im = reg.IM
	c.halted = reg.Halted
}

// INT drives the maskable interrupt line. It is level triggered: the
// CPU samples it at the end of each instruction. data is the byte an
// interrupting device would place on the data bus (used by modes 0
// and 2).
func (c *CPU) INT(assert bool, data uint8) {
	c.intLine = assert
	c.intData = data
}

// NMI requests a non-maskable interrupt. The request is latched until
// it is serviced at the next instruction boundary.
func (c *CPU) NMI() { c.nmiPending = true }

// StepCycles executes whole instructions until at least budget
// T-states have been consumed and returns the total consumed.
func (c *CPU) StepCycles(budget int) int {
	total := 0
	for total < budget {
		total += c.Step()
	}
	return total
}

// Step executes one instruction, one iteration of a repeating block
// instruction, or one HALT idle cycle, then services any interrupt
// that is due. It returns the T-states consumed.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	if c.halted {
		switch {
		case c.nmiPending:
			c.halted = false
			t := c.acceptNMI()
			c.cycles += uint64(t)
			return t
		case c.intLine && c.iff1:
			c.halted = false
			t := c.acceptINT()
			c.cycles += uint64(t)
			return t
		case c.intLine:
			// A masked INT still wakes the CPU; execution resumes
			// with the instruction after HALT.
			c.halted = false
		default:
			// Idle in HALT: one refresh cycle, 4 T-states.
			c.incR()
			c.cycles += 4
			return 4
		}
	}

	t := c.execute()

	// Interrupt acceptance point: the end of the instruction. EI
	// inhibits acceptance until the end of the following instruction.
	switch {
	case c.inhibitInt:
		c.inhibitInt = false
	case c.nmiPending:
		t += c.acceptNMI()
	case c.intLine && c.iff1:
		t += c.acceptINT()
	}
	c.cycles += uint64(t)
	return t
}

// acceptNMI runs the non-maskable interrupt sequence: IFF1 is copied
// to IFF2, IFF1 is cleared, PC is pushed and control goes to 0x0066.
func (c *CPU) acceptNMI() int {
	c.nmiPending = false
	c.halted = false
	c.incR() // the interrupt acknowledge M1 cycle refreshes memory
	c.iff2 = c.iff1
	c.iff1 = false
	c.push(c.pc)
	c.pc = 0x0066
	return 11
}

// acceptINT runs the maskable interrupt sequence for the current
// interrupt mode. Both interrupt flip-flops are cleared.
func (c *CPU) acceptINT() int {
	c.halted = false
	c.incR() // acknowledge M1 cycle
	c.iff1 = false
	c.iff2 = false
	switch c.im {
	case 1:
		c.push(c.pc)
		c.pc = 0x0038
		return 13
	case 2:
		c.push(c.pc)
		vec := uint16(c.i)<<8 | uint16(c.intData)
		c.pc = c.read16(vec)
		return 19
	default: // mode 0: execute the byte supplied on the data bus
		b := c.intData
		if b&0xC7 == 0xC7 { // RST p, the usual mode-0 instruction
			c.push(c.pc)
			c.pc = uint16(b & 0x38)
			return 13
		}
		// Any other supplied opcode runs through the normal decoder;
		// the acknowledge adds 2 T-states on top of its cost.
		return c.execOne(b) + 2
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Register pair helpers

func (c *CPU) bc() uint16         { return uint16(c.b)<<8 | uint16(c.c) }
func (c *CPU) de() uint16         { return uint16(c.d)<<8 | uint16(c.e) }
func (c *CPU) hl() uint16         { return uint16(c.h)<<8 | uint16(c.l) }
func (c *CPU) setBC(v uint16)     { c.b, c.c = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v) }
func (c *CPU) setDE(v uint16)     { c.d, c.e = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v) }
func (c *CPU) setHL(v uint16)     { c.h, c.l = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v) }
func pairVal(hi, lo uint8) uint16 { return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo) }

// pair returns register pair n of the LD rr / ADD group:
// 0=BC, 1=DE, 2=HL, 3=SP.
func (c *CPU) pair(n int) uint16 {
	switch n {
	case 0:
		return c.bc()
	case 1:
		return c.de()
	case 2:
		return c.hl()
	default:
		return c.sp
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setPair(n int, v uint16) {
	switch n {
	case 0:
		c.setBC(v)
	case 1:
		c.setDE(v)
	case 2:
		c.setHL(v)
	default:
		c.sp = v
	}
}

// stackPair returns register pair n of the PUSH/POP group:
// 0=BC, 1=DE, 2=HL, 3=AF.
func (c *CPU) stackPair(n int) uint16 {
	switch n {
	case 0:
		return c.bc()
	case 1:
		return c.de()
	case 2:
		return c.hl()
	default:
		return uint16(c.a)<<8 | uint16(c.f)
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setStackPair(n int, v uint16) {
	switch n {
	case 0:
		c.setBC(v)
	case 1:
		c.setDE(v)
	case 2:
		c.setHL(v)
	default:
		c.a, c.f = uint8(v>>8), uint8(v)
	}
}

// reg returns 8-bit register n in the standard encoding
// (0=B, 1=C, 2=D, 3=E, 4=H, 5=L, 7=A). Index 6 means (HL) and is
// always handled by the caller, never passed here.
func (c *CPU) reg(n int) uint8 {
	switch n {
	case 0:
		return c.b
	case 1:
		return c.c
	case 2:
		return c.d
	case 3:
		return c.e
	case 4:
		return c.h
	case 5:
		return c.l
	default:
		return c.a
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setReg(n int, v uint8) {
	switch n {
	case 0:
		c.b = v
	case 1:
		c.c = v
	case 2:
		c.d = v
	case 3:
		c.e = v
	case 4:
		c.h = v
	case 5:
		c.l = v
	case 7:
		c.a = v
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Bus access helpers

// fetch reads the next instruction-stream byte at PC (no refresh).
func (c *CPU) fetch() uint8 {
	v := c.bus.Fetch(c.pc)
	c.pc++
	return v
}

// fetchOpcode reads an opcode byte: an M1 cycle, which also bumps
// the refresh register.
func (c *CPU) fetchOpcode() uint8 {
	c.incR()
	return c.fetch()
}

// operand reads an immediate byte (not an M1 cycle).
func (c *CPU) operand() uint8 {
	v := c.bus.Read(c.pc)
	c.pc++
	return v
}

// operand16 reads a little-endian immediate word.
func (c *CPU) operand16() uint16 {
	lo := c.operand()
	hi := c.operand()
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

func (c *CPU) read16(addr uint16) uint16 {
	lo := c.bus.Read(addr)
	hi := c.bus.Read(addr + 1)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

func (c *CPU) write16(addr, v uint16) {
	c.bus.Write(addr, uint8(v))
	c.bus.Write(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
}

func (c *CPU) push(v uint16) {
	c.sp--
	c.bus.Write(c.sp, uint8(v>>8))
	c.sp--
	c.bus.Write(c.sp, uint8(v))
}

func (c *CPU) pop() uint16 {
	v := c.read16(c.sp)
	c.sp += 2
	return v
}

// incR advances the refresh register: only the low 7 bits count,
// bit 7 is preserved, as documented for the refresh counter.
func (c *CPU) incR() {
	c.r = (c.r & 0x80) | ((c.r + 1) & 0x7F)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Flag helpers

// parityEven reports whether v has an even number of set bits
// (the Z80 P/V flag is set for even parity).
func parityEven(v uint8) bool {
	v ^= v >> 4
	v ^= v >> 2
	v ^= v >> 1
	return v&1 == 0
}

// szpFlags builds the S, Z, Y, X and PV (parity) bits for an 8-bit
// result, in the flag positions.
func szpFlags(v uint8) uint8 {
	f := v & (flagS | flagY | flagX)
	if v == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	if parityEven(v) {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	return f
}

// setSZP sets S, Z, Y, X and PV from an 8-bit result and clears
// H and N. C is preserved.
func (c *CPU) setSZP(v uint8) {
	c.f = c.f&flagC | szpFlags(v)
}

// cond evaluates condition n of the jump/call/return groups:
// 0=NZ, 1=Z, 2=NC, 3=C, 4=PO, 5=PE, 6=P, 7=M.
func (c *CPU) cond(n int) bool {
	switch n & 7 {
	case 0:
		return c.f&flagZ == 0
	case 1:
		return c.f&flagZ != 0
	case 2:
		return c.f&flagC == 0
	case 3:
		return c.f&flagC != 0
	case 4:
		return c.f&flagPV == 0
	case 5:
		return c.f&flagPV != 0
	case 6:
		return c.f&flagS == 0
	default:
		return c.f&flagS != 0
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 8-bit ALU primitives. Each leaves the documented flag pattern in F.

// add8 computes A + v (+ carry if adc) and sets all arithmetic flags.
func (c *CPU) add8(v uint8, adc bool) uint8 {
	a := c.a
	ci := 0
	if adc && c.f&flagC != 0 {
		ci = 1
	}
	sum := int(a) + int(v) + ci
	res := uint8(sum)
	f := szpFlags(res) &^ flagPV // PV means overflow here, not parity
	if (a&0x0F)+(v&0x0F)+uint8(ci) > 0x0F {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if (^(a ^ v) & (a ^ res) & 0x80) != 0 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	if sum > 0xFF {
		f |= flagC
	}
	c.f = f
	return res
}

// sub8 computes A - v (- carry if sbc) and sets all arithmetic flags.
// For CP (cp=true) A is unchanged by the caller, and the undocumented
// Y/X bits come from the operand v rather than from the result.
func (c *CPU) sub8(v uint8, sbc bool, cp bool) uint8 {
	a := c.a
	ci := 0
	if sbc && c.f&flagC != 0 {
		ci = 1
	}
	diff := int(a) - int(v) - ci
	res := uint8(diff)
	f := flagN | (szpFlags(res) &^ flagPV)
	if int(a&0x0F)-int(v&0x0F)-ci < 0 {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if ((a ^ v) & (a ^ res) & 0x80) != 0 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	if diff < 0 {
		f |= flagC
	}
	if cp {
		f = f&^(flagY|flagX) | v&(flagY|flagX)
	}
	c.f = f
	return res
}

// alu runs one operation from the ALU group:
// 0=ADD, 1=ADC, 2=SUB, 3=SBC, 4=AND, 5=XOR, 6=OR, 7=CP.
func (c *CPU) alu(kind int, v uint8) {
	switch kind {
	case 0:
		c.a = c.add8(v, false)
	case 1:
		c.a = c.add8(v, true)
	case 2:
		c.a = c.sub8(v, false, false)
	case 3:
		c.a = c.sub8(v, true, false)
	case 4: // AND: H set, N and C clear, PV = parity
		c.a &= v
		c.f = szpFlags(c.a) | flagH
	case 5: // XOR
		c.a ^= v
		c.f = szpFlags(c.a)
	case 6: // OR
		c.a |= v
		c.f = szpFlags(c.a)
	case 7: // CP: result discarded
		c.sub8(v, false, true)
	}
}

// inc8 implements INC r flag behaviour: C is preserved, PV is set
// when the operand was 0x7F, H on a low-nibble carry, N cleared.
func (c *CPU) inc8(v uint8) uint8 {
	res := v + 1
	f := c.f & flagC
	f |= res & (flagS | flagY | flagX)
	if res == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	if v&0x0F == 0x0F {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if v == 0x7F {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	c.f = f
	return res
}

// dec8 implements DEC r flag behaviour: C is preserved, PV is set
// when the operand was 0x80, H on a low-nibble borrow, N set.
func (c *CPU) dec8(v uint8) uint8 {
	res := v - 1
	f := c.f&flagC | flagN
	f |= res & (flagS | flagY | flagX)
	if res == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	if v&0x0F == 0x00 {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if v == 0x80 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	c.f = f
	return res
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 16-bit arithmetic primitives

// add16 implements ADD HL,rr / ADD IX,rr: only H, N (cleared), C and
// the undocumented Y/X bits (from the high byte of the result) move.
func (c *CPU) add16(a, b uint16) uint16 {
	sum := int(a) + int(b)
	res := uint16(sum)
	f := c.f & (flagS | flagZ | flagPV)
	if (a&0x0FFF)+(b&0x0FFF) > 0x0FFF {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if sum > 0xFFFF {
		f |= flagC
	}
	f |= uint8(res>>8) & (flagY | flagX)
	c.f = f
	return res
}

// adc16 implements ADC HL,rr: a full 16-bit add with carry.
func (c *CPU) adc16(a, b uint16) uint16 {
	ci := int(0)
	if c.f&flagC != 0 {
		ci = 1
	}
	sum := int(a) + int(b) + ci
	res := uint16(sum)
	var f uint8
	if res&0x8000 != 0 {
		f |= flagS
	}
	if res == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	f |= uint8(res>>8) & (flagY | flagX)
	if (a&0x0FFF)+(b&0x0FFF)+uint16(ci) > 0x0FFF {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if (^(a ^ b) & (a ^ res) & 0x8000) != 0 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	if sum > 0xFFFF {
		f |= flagC
	}
	c.f = f
	return res
}

// sbc16 implements SBC HL,rr: a full 16-bit subtract with carry.
func (c *CPU) sbc16(a, b uint16) uint16 {
	ci := int(0)
	if c.f&flagC != 0 {
		ci = 1
	}
	diff := int(a) - int(b) - ci
	res := uint16(diff)
	var f uint8 = flagN
	if res&0x8000 != 0 {
		f |= flagS
	}
	if res == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	f |= uint8(res>>8) & (flagY | flagX)
	if int(a&0x0FFF)-int(b&0x0FFF)-ci < 0 {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if ((a ^ b) & (a ^ res) & 0x8000) != 0 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	if diff < 0 {
		f |= flagC
	}
	c.f = f
	return res
}

// daa implements the decimal adjust accumulator operation using the
// documented correction table: 0x06 fixes the low digit, 0x60 the
// high digit, selected by the H/C flags and the nibble values left
// by the preceding addition or subtraction.
func (c *CPU) daa() {
	a := c.a
	var corr uint8
	carry := c.f&flagC != 0
	if c.f&flagH != 0 || (a&0x0F) > 9 {
		corr |= 0x06
	}
	if carry || a > 0x99 {
		corr |= 0x60
		carry = true
	} else {
		carry = false
	}
	var res uint8
	var half bool
	if c.f&flagN != 0 {
		res = a - corr
		half = (a & 0x0F) < (corr & 0x0F)
	} else {
		res = a + corr
		half = (a&0x0F)+(corr&0x0F) > 0x0F
	}
	c.a = res
	f := szpFlags(res) | (c.f & flagN)
	if half {
		f |= flagH
	}
	if carry {
		f |= flagC
	}
	c.f = f
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Serialization
//
// Layout (37 of the 47 bytes are used, the rest stay zero):
//
//	[0]     version (1)
//	[1:25]  AF, BC, DE, HL, AF', BC', DE', HL', IX, IY, SP, PC (LE16)
//	[25]    I
//	[26]    R
//	[27]    bit flags: IFF1, IFF2, halted, INT line, NMI pending,
//	        EI inhibit, IM in bits 6-7
//	[28]    INT bus data byte
//	[29:37] cycle counter (LE64)

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size in bytes.
const SerializeSize = 47

const serializeVersion = 1

// Serialize writes the full CPU state (including cycle counter and
// interrupt line state) into buf, which must be at least
// SerializeSize bytes long.
func (c *CPU) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("z80: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	for i := 0; i < SerializeSize; i++ {
		buf[i] = 0
	}
	buf[0] = serializeVersion
	pairs := []uint16{
		uint16(c.a)<<8 | uint16(c.f), c.bc(), c.de(), c.hl(),
		uint16(c.a2)<<8 | uint16(c.f2),
		uint16(c.b2)<<8 | uint16(c.c2),
		uint16(c.d2)<<8 | uint16(c.e2),
		uint16(c.h2)<<8 | uint16(c.l2),
		c.ix, c.iy, c.sp, c.pc,
	}
	for i, p := range pairs {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[1+i*2:], p)
	}
	buf[25] = c.i
	buf[26] = c.r
	var bits uint8
	if c.iff1 {
		bits |= 1 << 0
	}
	if c.iff2 {
		bits |= 1 << 1
	}
	if c.halted {
		bits |= 1 << 2
	}
	if c.intLine {
		bits |= 1 << 3
	}
	if c.nmiPending {
		bits |= 1 << 4
	}
	if c.inhibitInt {
		bits |= 1 << 5
	}
	bits |= (c.im & 3) << 6
	buf[27] = bits
	buf[28] = c.intData
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[29:], c.cycles)
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("z80: deserialize buffer too small")
	}
	if buf[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("z80: unsupported serialize version")
	}
	pairAt := func(i int) uint16 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[1+i*2:]) }
	c.a, c.f = uint8(pairAt(0)>>8), uint8(pairAt(0))
	c.setBC(pairAt(1))
	c.setDE(pairAt(2))
	c.setHL(pairAt(3))
	c.a2, c.f2 = uint8(pairAt(4)>>8), uint8(pairAt(4))
	c.b2, c.c2 = uint8(pairAt(5)>>8), uint8(pairAt(5))
	c.d2, c.e2 = uint8(pairAt(6)>>8), uint8(pairAt(6))
	c.h2, c.l2 = uint8(pairAt(7)>>8), uint8(pairAt(7))
	c.ix = pairAt(8)
	c.iy = pairAt(9)
	c.sp = pairAt(10)
	c.pc = pairAt(11)
	c.i = buf[25]
	c.r = buf[26]
	bits := buf[27]
	c.iff1 = bits&(1<<0) != 0
	c.iff2 = bits&(1<<1) != 0
	c.halted = bits&(1<<2) != 0
	c.intLine = bits&(1<<3) != 0
	c.nmiPending = bits&(1<<4) != 0
	c.inhibitInt = bits&(1<<5) != 0
	c.im = (bits >> 6) & 3
	c.intData = buf[28]
	c.cycles = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(buf[29:])
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/z80/ed.go ====================

package z80

// execED executes an ED-prefixed opcode. The opcode byte itself is
// fetched here (an M1 cycle, bumping R). Undefined ED opcodes are
// two-byte NOPs costing 8 T-states.
func (c *CPU) execED() int {
	op := c.fetchOpcode()

	// Block group first: exact opcodes in the 0xA0-0xBB range.
	switch op {
	case 0xA0: // LDI
		return c.blockMove(1, false)
	case 0xA1: // CPI
		return c.blockCompare(1, false)
	case 0xA2: // INI
		return c.blockIn(1, false)
	case 0xA3: // OUTI
		return c.blockOut(1, false)
	case 0xA8: // LDD
		return c.blockMove(-1, false)
	case 0xA9: // CPD
		return c.blockCompare(-1, false)
	case 0xAA: // IND
		return c.blockIn(-1, false)
	case 0xAB: // OUTD
		return c.blockOut(-1, false)
	case 0xB0: // LDIR
		return c.blockMove(1, true)
	case 0xB1: // CPIR
		return c.blockCompare(1, true)
	case 0xB2: // INIR
		return c.blockIn(1, true)
	case 0xB3: // OTIR
		return c.blockOut(1, true)
	case 0xB8: // LDDR
		return c.blockMove(-1, true)
	case 0xB9: // CPDR
		return c.blockCompare(-1, true)
	case 0xBA: // INDR
		return c.blockIn(-1, true)
	case 0xBB: // OTDR
		return c.blockOut(-1, true)
	}

	if op < 0x40 || op > 0x7F {
		return 8 // undefined ED opcode: no operation
	}

	y := int(op>>3) & 7
	z := int(op) & 7
	p := int(op>>4) & 3
	q := int(op>>3) & 1
	switch z {
	case 0: // IN r,(C); op 0x70 is IN (HL),(C): value kept in memory
		v := c.bus.In(c.bc())
		// Documented flags: S/Z/Y/X from the value, H clear,
		// PV = parity, N clear, C preserved.
		c.f = c.f&flagC | szpFlags(v)
		if op == 0x70 {
			c.bus.Write(c.hl(), v)
		} else {
			c.setReg(y, v)
		}
		return 12
	case 1: // OUT (C),r; op 0x71 is OUT (C),0
		if op == 0x71 {
			c.bus.Out(c.bc(), 0)
		} else {
			c.bus.Out(c.bc(), c.reg(y))
		}
		return 12
	case 2: // SBC HL,rr / ADC HL,rr
		if q == 0 {
			c.setHL(c.sbc16(c.hl(), c.pair(p)))
		} else {
			c.setHL(c.adc16(c.hl(), c.pair(p)))
		}
		return 15
	case 3: // LD (nn),rr / LD rr,(nn)
		addr := c.operand16()
		if q == 0 {
			c.write16(addr, c.pair(p))
		} else {
			c.setPair(p, c.read16(addr))
		}
		return 20
	case 4: // NEG (all eight encodings)
		old := c.a
		res := -old
		c.a = res
		f := flagN | (szpFlags(res) &^ flagPV)
		if old&0x0F != 0 {
			f |= flagH
		}
		if old == 0x80 {
			f |= flagPV
		}
		if old != 0 {
			f |= flagC
		}
		c.f = f
		return 8
	case 5: // RETN (all encodings) / RETI (0x4D only)
		c.pc = c.pop()
		if op != 0x4D {
			// RETN restores IFF1 from IFF2; RETI does not.
			c.iff1 = c.iff2
		}
		return 14
	case 6: // IM 0 / 1 / 2
		switch y {
		case 0, 1, 4, 5:
			c.im = 0
		case 2, 6:
			c.im = 1
		case 3, 7:
			c.im = 2
		}
		return 8
	case 7:
		switch op {
		case 0x47: // LD I,A
			c.i = c.a
			return 9
		case 0x4F: // LD R,A
			c.r = c.a
			return 9
		case 0x57: // LD A,I
			c.a = c.i
			c.ldAIRFlags(c.i)
			return 9
		case 0x5F: // LD A,R
			c.a = c.r
			c.ldAIRFlags(c.r)
			return 9
		case 0x67: // RRD
			addr := c.hl()
			t := c.bus.Read(addr)
			c.bus.Write(addr, c.a<<4|(t>>4))
			c.a = (c.a & 0xF0) | (t & 0x0F)
			c.setSZP(c.a)
			return 18
		case 0x6F: // RLD
			addr := c.hl()
			t := c.bus.Read(addr)
			c.bus.Write(addr, (t<<4)|(c.a&0x0F))
			c.a = (c.a & 0xF0) | (t >> 4)
			c.setSZP(c.a)
			return 18
		}
		return 8
	}
	return 8
}

// ldAIRFlags sets the flags for LD A,I and LD A,R: S/Z/Y/X from the
// value, PV holding a copy of IFF2, H and N clear, C preserved.
func (c *CPU) ldAIRFlags(v uint8) {
	f := c.f&flagC | (v & (flagS | flagY | flagX))
	if v == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	if c.iff2 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	c.f = f
}

// addW adds a signed direction (+1 or -1) to a 16-bit register.
func addW(v uint16, dir int) uint16 {
	return uint16(int32(v) + int32(dir))
}

// repeatYX applies the documented flag oddity of the repeating
// block move/compare instructions: while the instruction repeats,
// the Y/X bits are taken from the high byte of the address just
// past the instruction (the WZ register holds PC+2 for these).
func (c *CPU) repeatYX(f uint8) uint8 {
	hb := uint8((c.pc + 2) >> 8) // c.pc was rewound by 2 already
	return f&^(flagY|flagX) | hb&(flagY|flagX)
}

// blockMove performs one LDI/LDD iteration; with repeat set it
// performs one LDIR/LDDR iteration, rewinding PC while BC != 0.
// Flag behaviour: H and N clear, PV set while BC != 0 after the
// decrement, and Y/X from (A + transferred byte): Y is its bit 1,
// X its bit 3. S, Z and C are preserved.
func (c *CPU) blockMove(dir int, repeat bool) int {
	v := c.bus.Read(c.hl())
	c.bus.Write(c.de(), v)
	c.setHL(addW(c.hl(), dir))
	c.setDE(addW(c.de(), dir))
	bc := c.bc() - 1
	c.setBC(bc)

	f := c.f & (flagS | flagZ | flagC)
	if bc != 0 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	n := c.a + v
	f |= (n & 0x02) << 4 // bit 1 -> Y
	f |= n & 0x08        // bit 3 -> X
	if repeat && bc != 0 {
		c.pc -= 2
		c.f = c.repeatYX(f)
		return 21
	}
	c.f = f
	return 16
}

// blockCompare performs one CPI/CPD iteration; with repeat set it
// performs one CPIR/CPDR iteration, rewinding PC while BC != 0 and
// no match was found. Flags are those of CP A,(HL) except that C is
// preserved, PV reports BC != 0, and Y/X come from the difference
// adjusted by the half borrow (bit 1 and bit 3 of it).
func (c *CPU) blockCompare(dir int, repeat bool) int {
	v := c.bus.Read(c.hl())
	c.setHL(addW(c.hl(), dir))
	bc := c.bc() - 1
	c.setBC(bc)

	diff := int(c.a) - int(v)
	res := uint8(diff)
	halfBorrow := (c.a & 0x0F) < (v & 0x0F)
	f := c.f&flagC | flagN
	if res&0x80 != 0 {
		f |= flagS
	}
	if res == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	if halfBorrow {
		f |= flagH
	}
	w := res
	if halfBorrow {
		w--
	}
	f |= (w & 0x02) << 4 // bit 1 -> Y
	f |= w & 0x08        // bit 3 -> X
	if bc != 0 {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	if repeat && bc != 0 && res != 0 {
		c.pc -= 2
		c.f = c.repeatYX(f)
		return 21
	}
	c.f = f
	return 16
}

// blockIn performs one INI/IND iteration; with repeat set it
// performs one INIR/INDR iteration. The port is addressed by the
// value of BC before B is decremented.
//
// Flag behaviour (documented on z80.info): S/Z/Y/X are those of B
// after the decrement; N is bit 7 of the byte read; with
// k = byte + (C + direction), H and C are both set when k > 255 and
// PV is the parity of (k & 7) XOR B.
func (c *CPU) blockIn(dir int, repeat bool) int {
	v := c.bus.In(c.bc()) // old BC
	c.bus.Write(c.hl(), v)
	c.b--
	c.setHL(addW(c.hl(), dir))

	k := int(v) + int(uint8(int16(c.c)+int16(dir)))
	f := c.blockIOFlags(v, k)
	c.f = f
	if repeat && c.b != 0 {
		c.pc -= 2
		c.repeatIOFixup(k > 0xFF, v&0x80 != 0)
		return 21
	}
	return 16
}

// blockOut performs one OUTI/OUTD iteration; with repeat set it
// performs one OTIR/OTDR iteration. B is decremented before the
// port write, so the port is addressed by the new BC.
//
// Flag behaviour mirrors blockIn, except k = byte + L, with L taken
// after HL has been updated.
func (c *CPU) blockOut(dir int, repeat bool) int {
	v := c.bus.Read(c.hl())
	c.b--
	c.bus.Out(c.bc(), v) // new BC
	c.setHL(addW(c.hl(), dir))

	k := int(v) + int(c.l) // L after the HL update
	f := c.blockIOFlags(v, k)
	c.f = f
	if repeat && c.b != 0 {
		c.pc -= 2
		c.repeatIOFixup(k > 0xFF, v&0x80 != 0)
		return 21
	}
	return 16
}

// blockIOFlags builds the flag byte for one block I/O iteration:
// S/Z/Y/X from B (already decremented), N from bit 7 of the
// transferred byte, H and C from k overflowing a byte, PV the
// parity of (k & 7) XOR B.
func (c *CPU) blockIOFlags(v uint8, k int) uint8 {
	f := c.b & (flagS | flagY | flagX)
	if c.b == 0 {
		f |= flagZ
	}
	if v&0x80 != 0 {
		f |= flagN
	}
	if k > 0xFF {
		f |= flagH | flagC
	}
	if parityEven(uint8(k&7) ^ c.b) {
		f |= flagPV
	}
	return f
}

// repeatIOFixup applies the documented extra flag adjustment that
// happens when a block I/O instruction repeats: H and PV are
// recomputed from B alone, or from B+1 / B-1 when the transfer
// raised a carry, depending on the N flag the transfer left.
func (c *CPU) repeatIOFixup(carry, nflag bool) {
	var pvVal uint8
	var h bool
	switch {
	case !carry:
		pvVal = c.b
	case !nflag:
		pvVal = c.b + 1
		h = c.b&0x0F == 0x0F
	default:
		pvVal = c.b - 1
		h = c.b&0x0F == 0x00
	}
	c.f &^= flagH | flagPV
	if h {
		c.f |= flagH
	}
	if parityEven(pvVal) {
		c.f |= flagPV
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/z80/exec.go ====================

package z80

// execute fetches and runs one instruction, including any prefix
// bytes, and returns its T-state cost.
func (c *CPU) execute() int {
	op := c.fetchOpcode()

	// DD/FD prefix handling: the last prefix seen wins; every prefix
	// before it is a wasted 4 T-state M1 cycle, as on hardware.
	prefix := byte(0)
	extra := 0
	for op == 0xDD || op == 0xFD {
		if prefix != 0 {
			extra += 4
		}
		prefix = op
		op = c.fetchOpcode()
	}

	if prefix != 0 {
		idx := &c.ix
		if prefix == 0xFD {
			idx = &c.iy
		}
		switch {
		case op == 0xCB:
			return c.execIndexedCB(idx) + extra
		case op == 0xED:
			// An index prefix in front of an ED instruction is
			// simply wasted.
			return c.execED() + extra + 4
		default:
			return c.execIndexed(op, idx) + extra
		}
	}
	return c.execOne(op)
}

// execOne dispatches a single already-fetched opcode byte with no
// index prefix in effect.
func (c *CPU) execOne(op byte) int {
	switch op {
	case 0xCB:
		return c.execCB()
	case 0xED:
		return c.execED()
	default:
		return c.execBase(op)
	}
}

// execBase executes one unprefixed opcode (not CB/ED/DD/FD) and
// returns its documented T-state cost.
func (c *CPU) execBase(op byte) int {
	// Pattern-coded groups first.
	switch {
	case op&0xCF == 0x01: // LD rr,nn
		c.setPair(int(op>>4)&3, c.operand16())
		return 10
	case op&0xCF == 0x03: // INC rr
		n := int(op>>4) & 3
		c.setPair(n, c.pair(n)+1)
		return 6
	case op&0xCF == 0x0B: // DEC rr
		n := int(op>>4) & 3
		c.setPair(n, c.pair(n)-1)
		return 6
	case op&0xCF == 0x09: // ADD HL,rr
		c.setHL(c.add16(c.hl(), c.pair(int(op>>4)&3)))
		return 11
	case op&0xC7 == 0x04: // INC r / INC (HL)
		if idx := int(op>>3) & 7; idx == 6 {
			hl := c.hl()
			c.bus.Write(hl, c.inc8(c.bus.Read(hl)))
			return 11
		} else {
			c.setReg(idx, c.inc8(c.reg(idx)))
			return 4
		}
	case op&0xC7 == 0x05: // DEC r / DEC (HL)
		if idx := int(op>>3) & 7; idx == 6 {
			hl := c.hl()
			c.bus.Write(hl, c.dec8(c.bus.Read(hl)))
			return 11
		} else {
			c.setReg(idx, c.dec8(c.reg(idx)))
			return 4
		}
	case op&0xC7 == 0x06: // LD r,n / LD (HL),n
		v := c.operand()
		if idx := int(op>>3) & 7; idx == 6 {
			c.bus.Write(c.hl(), v)
			return 10
		} else {
			c.setReg(idx, v)
			return 7
		}
	case op == 0x76: // HALT (the (HL),(HL) slot of the LD matrix)
		c.halted = true
		return 4
	case op >= 0x40 && op <= 0x7F: // LD r,r'
		dst, src := int(op>>3)&7, int(op)&7
		var v uint8
		if src == 6 {
			v = c.bus.Read(c.hl())
		} else {
			v = c.reg(src)
		}
		if dst == 6 {
			c.bus.Write(c.hl(), v)
		} else {
			c.setReg(dst, v)
		}
		if src == 6 || dst == 6 {
			return 7
		}
		return 4
	case op >= 0x80 && op <= 0xBF: // ALU A,r / ALU A,(HL)
		src := int(op) & 7
		if src == 6 {
			c.alu(int(op>>3)&7, c.bus.Read(c.hl()))
			return 7
		}
		c.alu(int(op>>3)&7, c.reg(src))
		return 4
	case op&0xC7 == 0xC0: // RET cc
		if c.cond(int(op>>3) & 7) {
			c.pc = c.pop()
			return 11
		}
		return 5
	case op&0xCF == 0xC1: // POP rr
		c.setStackPair(int(op>>4)&3, c.pop())
		return 10
	case op&0xC7 == 0xC2: // JP cc,nn
		addr := c.operand16()
		if c.cond(int(op>>3) & 7) {
			c.pc = addr
		}
		return 10
	case op&0xC7 == 0xC4: // CALL cc,nn
		addr := c.operand16()
		if c.cond(int(op>>3) & 7) {
			c.push(c.pc)
			c.pc = addr
			return 17
		}
		return 10
	case op&0xCF == 0xC5: // PUSH rr
		c.push(c.stackPair(int(op>>4) & 3))
		return 11
	case op&0xC7 == 0xC6: // ALU A,n
		c.alu(int(op>>3)&7, c.operand())
		return 7
	case op&0xC7 == 0xC7: // RST p
		c.push(c.pc)
		c.pc = uint16(op & 0x38)
		return 11
	}

	// Discrete opcodes.
	switch op {
	case 0x00: // NOP
		return 4
	case 0x02: // LD (BC),A
		c.bus.Write(c.bc(), c.a)
		return 7
	case 0x12: // LD (DE),A
		c.bus.Write(c.de(), c.a)
		return 7
	case 0x0A: // LD A,(BC)
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.bc())
		return 7
	case 0x1A: // LD A,(DE)
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.de())
		return 7
	case 0x07: // RLCA
		out := c.a >> 7
		c.a = c.a<<1 | out
		c.f = c.f&(flagS|flagZ|flagPV) | out | (c.a & (flagY | flagX))
		return 4
	case 0x0F: // RRCA
		out := c.a & 1
		c.a = c.a>>1 | out<<7
		c.f = c.f&(flagS|flagZ|flagPV) | out | (c.a & (flagY | flagX))
		return 4
	case 0x17: // RLA
		out := c.a >> 7
		c.a = c.a<<1 | (c.f & flagC)
		c.f = c.f&(flagS|flagZ|flagPV) | out | (c.a & (flagY | flagX))
		return 4
	case 0x1F: // RRA
		out := c.a & 1
		c.a = c.a>>1 | (c.f&flagC)<<7
		c.f = c.f&(flagS|flagZ|flagPV) | out | (c.a & (flagY | flagX))
		return 4
	case 0x08: // EX AF,AF'
		c.a, c.a2 = c.a2, c.a
		c.f, c.f2 = c.f2, c.f
		return 4
	case 0x10: // DJNZ e
		off := int8(c.operand())
		c.b--
		if c.b != 0 {
			c.pc = uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
			return 13
		}
		return 8
	case 0x18: // JR e
		off := int8(c.operand())
		c.pc = uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
		return 12
	case 0x20, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38: // JR NZ/Z/NC/C,e
		off := int8(c.operand())
		cc := int(op>>3) & 3 // NZ, Z, NC, C are conditions 0..3
		if c.cond(cc) {
			c.pc = uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
			return 12
		}
		return 7
	case 0x22: // LD (nn),HL
		c.write16(c.operand16(), c.hl())
		return 16
	case 0x2A: // LD HL,(nn)
		c.setHL(c.read16(c.operand16()))
		return 16
	case 0x32: // LD (nn),A
		c.bus.Write(c.operand16(), c.a)
		return 13
	case 0x3A: // LD A,(nn)
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.operand16())
		return 13
	case 0x27: // DAA
		c.daa()
		return 4
	case 0x2F: // CPL
		c.a = ^c.a
		c.f |= flagH | flagN
		c.f = c.f&^(flagY|flagX) | (c.a & (flagY | flagX))
		return 4
	case 0x37: // SCF
		// Y/X come from A OR the previous F (the documented quirk the
		// z80test research established for SCF/CCF; found by differential
		// testing, where copying from A alone diverged).
		c.f = c.f&(flagS|flagZ|flagPV) | flagC | ((c.f | c.a) & (flagY | flagX))
		return 4
	case 0x3F: // CCF
		oldC := c.f & flagC
		f := c.f&(flagS|flagZ|flagPV) | ((c.f | c.a) & (flagY | flagX))
		if oldC != 0 {
			f |= flagH // the old carry becomes the half carry
		} else {
			f |= flagC
		}
		c.f = f
		return 4
	case 0xC3: // JP nn
		c.pc = c.operand16()
		return 10
	case 0xC9: // RET
		c.pc = c.pop()
		return 10
	case 0xCD: // CALL nn
		addr := c.operand16()
		c.push(c.pc)
		c.pc = addr
		return 17
	case 0xD3: // OUT (n),A
		c.bus.Out(uint16(c.a)<<8|uint16(c.operand()), c.a)
		return 11
	case 0xDB: // IN A,(n)
		c.a = c.bus.In(uint16(c.a)<<8 | uint16(c.operand()))
		return 11
	case 0xD9: // EXX
		c.b, c.b2 = c.b2, c.b
		c.c, c.c2 = c.c2, c.c
		c.d, c.d2 = c.d2, c.d
		c.e, c.e2 = c.e2, c.e
		c.h, c.h2 = c.h2, c.h
		c.l, c.l2 = c.l2, c.l
		return 4
	case 0xE3: // EX (SP),HL
		v := c.read16(c.sp)
		c.write16(c.sp, c.hl())
		c.setHL(v)
		return 19
	case 0xE9: // JP (HL)
		c.pc = c.hl()
		return 4
	case 0xEB: // EX DE,HL
		c.d, c.h = c.h, c.d
		c.e, c.l = c.l, c.e
		return 4
	case 0xF3: // DI
		c.iff1, c.iff2 = false, false
		c.inhibitInt = false
		return 4
	case 0xF9: // LD SP,HL
		c.sp = c.hl()
		return 6
	case 0xFB: // EI
		c.iff1, c.iff2 = true, true
		c.inhibitInt = true
		return 4
	}
	// Any opcode not decoded above cannot occur: the pattern groups
	// and the discrete table cover the whole base map. Treat a miss
	// as a NOP rather than crashing the machine.
	return 4
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/z80/ix.go ====================

package z80

// Indexed (DD/FD) instruction execution. idx points at the index
// register in use (IX for 0xDD, IY for 0xFD); its halves are
// reachable as the IXh/IXl (IYh/IYl) pseudo-registers wherever the
// base instruction set would use H or L, except when the instruction
// also uses the (IX+d) memory operand, where real H and L apply.
// Opcodes the prefix does not modify fall back to the base
// instruction with a 4 T-state prefix penalty.

// idxAddr computes the effective address IX+d / IY+d, fetching the
// signed displacement byte.
func (c *CPU) idxAddr(idx *uint16) uint16 {
	d := int8(c.operand())
	return uint16(int32(*idx) + int32(d))
}

// idxHalf reads the high (hi=true) or low half of the index register.
func idxHalf(idx *uint16, hi bool) uint8 {
	if hi {
		return uint8(*idx >> 8)
	}
	return uint8(*idx)
}

// setIdxHalf writes one half of the index register.
func setIdxHalf(idx *uint16, hi bool, v uint8) {
	if hi {
		*idx = (*idx & 0x00FF) | uint16(v)<<8
	} else {
		*idx = (*idx & 0xFF00) | uint16(v)
	}
}

// idxRegVal reads operand n in indexed mode: 4 and 5 select the
// index halves, everything else is a plain register. Never called
// with n == 6.
func (c *CPU) idxRegVal(idx *uint16, n int) uint8 {
	switch n {
	case 4:
		return idxHalf(idx, true)
	case 5:
		return idxHalf(idx, false)
	default:
		return c.reg(n)
	}
}

// setIdxReg writes operand n in indexed mode (see idxRegVal).
func (c *CPU) setIdxReg(idx *uint16, n int, v uint8) {
	switch n {
	case 4:
		setIdxHalf(idx, true, v)
	case 5:
		setIdxHalf(idx, false, v)
	default:
		c.setReg(n, v)
	}
}

// execIndexed executes one opcode with a DD/FD prefix in effect and
// returns its documented T-state cost (which includes the prefix).
func (c *CPU) execIndexed(op byte, idx *uint16) int {
	switch {
	case op&0xCF == 0x09: // ADD idx,rr (rr == idx for the 0x29 form)
		var v uint16
		if n := int(op>>4) & 3; n == 2 {
			v = *idx
		} else {
			v = c.pair(n)
		}
		*idx = c.add16(*idx, v)
		return 15
	case op == 0x21: // LD idx,nn
		*idx = c.operand16()
		return 14
	case op == 0x22: // LD (nn),idx
		c.write16(c.operand16(), *idx)
		return 20
	case op == 0x23: // INC idx
		*idx++
		return 10
	case op == 0x2A: // LD idx,(nn)
		*idx = c.read16(c.operand16())
		return 20
	case op == 0x2B: // DEC idx
		*idx--
		return 10
	case op&0xC7 == 0x04 || op&0xC7 == 0x05: // INC/DEC half or (idx+d)
		n := int(op>>3) & 7
		apply := c.inc8
		if op&0xC7 == 0x05 {
			apply = c.dec8
		}
		switch n {
		case 4:
			setIdxHalf(idx, true, apply(idxHalf(idx, true)))
			return 8
		case 5:
			setIdxHalf(idx, false, apply(idxHalf(idx, false)))
			return 8
		case 6:
			addr := c.idxAddr(idx)
			c.bus.Write(addr, apply(c.bus.Read(addr)))
			return 23
		default:
			return c.execBase(op) + 4
		}
	case op&0xC7 == 0x06: // LD half,n / LD (idx+d),n
		n := int(op>>3) & 7
		switch n {
		case 4:
			setIdxHalf(idx, true, c.operand())
			return 11
		case 5:
			setIdxHalf(idx, false, c.operand())
			return 11
		case 6:
			addr := c.idxAddr(idx)
			c.bus.Write(addr, c.operand())
			return 19
		default:
			return c.execBase(op) + 4
		}
	case op == 0x76: // HALT (prefix does not change it)
		c.halted = true
		return 8
	case op >= 0x40 && op <= 0x7F: // LD r,r' with index rules
		dst, src := int(op>>3)&7, int(op)&7
		if src == 6 { // LD r,(idx+d): the register is a plain one
			c.setReg(dst, c.bus.Read(c.idxAddr(idx)))
			return 19
		}
		if dst == 6 { // LD (idx+d),r: likewise
			c.bus.Write(c.idxAddr(idx), c.reg(src))
			return 19
		}
		c.setIdxReg(idx, dst, c.idxRegVal(idx, src))
		return 8
	case op >= 0x80 && op <= 0xBF: // ALU A,operand
		src := int(op) & 7
		kind := int(op>>3) & 7
		switch src {
		case 6:
			c.alu(kind, c.bus.Read(c.idxAddr(idx)))
			return 19
		case 4:
			c.alu(kind, idxHalf(idx, true))
			return 8
		case 5:
			c.alu(kind, idxHalf(idx, false))
			return 8
		default:
			c.alu(kind, c.reg(src))
			return 8
		}
	case op == 0xE1: // POP idx
		*idx = c.pop()
		return 14
	case op == 0xE3: // EX (SP),idx
		v := c.read16(c.sp)
		c.write16(c.sp, *idx)
		*idx = v
		return 23
	case op == 0xE5: // PUSH idx
		c.push(*idx)
		return 15
	case op == 0xE9: // JP (idx)
		c.pc = *idx
		return 8
	case op == 0xF9: // LD SP,idx
		c.sp = *idx
		return 10
	default:
		// The prefix does not modify this instruction.
		return c.execBase(op) + 4
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/chips/z80/z80_test.go ====================

package z80

import "testing"

// ramBus is a flat 64KB memory with scriptable I/O ports.
type ramBus struct {
	mem    [65536]uint8
	inVal  map[uint16]uint8
	outLog []outWrite
}

type outWrite struct {
	port uint16
	val  uint8
}

func (b *ramBus) Fetch(a uint16) uint8    { return b.mem[a] }
func (b *ramBus) Read(a uint16) uint8     { return b.mem[a] }
func (b *ramBus) Write(a uint16, v uint8) { b.mem[a] = v }
func (b *ramBus) In(p uint16) uint8       { return b.inVal[p] }
func (b *ramBus) Out(p uint16, v uint8) {
	b.outLog = append(b.outLog, outWrite{p, v})
}

func newCPU(prog ...byte) (*CPU, *ramBus) {
	bus := &ramBus{inVal: map[uint16]uint8{}}
	copy(bus.mem[:], prog)
	return New(bus), bus
}

func flags(c *CPU) uint8 { return uint8(c.Registers().AF) }
func acc(c *CPU) uint8   { return uint8(c.Registers().AF >> 8) }

func TestADDFlagsOverflow(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, _ := newCPU(0x3E, 0x7F, 0xC6, 0x01) // LD A,0x7F; ADD A,0x01
	cpu.Step()
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("ADD A,n cost = %d, want 7", got)
	}
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("A = %#02x, want 0x80", a)
	}
	// S=1, H=1 (nibble carry), PV=1 (signed overflow), Z/Y/X/N/C=0.
	if f, want := flags(cpu), uint8(flagS|flagH|flagPV); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("F = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
}

func TestSUBFlagsBorrow(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, _ := newCPU(0x3E, 0x00, 0xD6, 0x01) // LD A,0; SUB 0x01
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("A = %#02x, want 0xFF", a)
	}
	// S=1, Y=1, H=1, X=1, N=1, C=1; Z=0, PV=0.
	want := uint8(flagS | flagY | flagH | flagX | flagN | flagC)
	if f := flags(cpu); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("F = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
}

func TestCPFlagsComeFromOperand(t *testing.T) {
	// CP with equal operands: result is 0, but the undocumented
	// Y/X bits must be copied from the operand (0x28), not the result.
	cpu, _ := newCPU(0x3E, 0x28, 0xFE, 0x28) // LD A,0x28; CP 0x28
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0x28 {
		t.Fatalf("CP changed A: %#02x", a)
	}
	want := uint8(flagZ | flagY | flagX | flagN)
	if f := flags(cpu); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("F = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
}

func TestDAA(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		prog  []byte
		wantA uint8
		wantF uint8
	}{
		// 0x15 + 0x27 = 0x3C -> DAA -> 0x42 (15 + 27 = 42 in BCD).
		{"add", []byte{0x3E, 0x15, 0xC6, 0x27, 0x27}, 0x42, flagH | flagPV},
		// 0x99 + 0x99 = 0x32 carry -> DAA -> 0x98, carry stays.
		// 0x98 has bit 3 set, so X is set; parity is odd, so PV clear.
		{"add carry", []byte{0x3E, 0x99, 0xC6, 0x99, 0x27}, 0x98, flagS | flagX | flagC},
		// 0x42 - 0x27 = 0x1B (N) -> DAA -> 0x15.
		{"sub", []byte{0x3E, 0x42, 0xD6, 0x27, 0x27}, 0x15, flagN},
		// 0x00 - 0x01 = 0xFF (N) -> DAA -> 0x99 with carry (borrow).
		// 0x99 = 1001 1001b: S and X set, Y clear, even parity (PV).
		{"sub borrow", []byte{0x3E, 0x00, 0xD6, 0x01, 0x27}, 0x99, flagS | flagX | flagPV | flagN | flagC},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			cpu, _ := newCPU(tc.prog...)
			for range tc.prog {
				if cpu.Registers().PC >= uint16(len(tc.prog)) {
					break
				}
				cpu.Step()
			}
			if a := acc(cpu); a != tc.wantA {
				t.Fatalf("A = %#02x, want %#02x", a, tc.wantA)
			}
			if f := flags(cpu); f != tc.wantF {
				t.Fatalf("F = %#02x, want %#02x", f, tc.wantF)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestINCDECFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// INC B from 0x7F: overflow to 0x80, carry (set by SCF) preserved.
	cpu, _ := newCPU(0x37, 0x06, 0x7F, 0x04) // SCF; LD B,0x7F; INC B
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	if b := cpu.Registers().BC >> 8; b != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("B = %#02x, want 0x80", b)
	}
	if f, want := flags(cpu), uint8(flagS|flagH|flagPV|flagC); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("INC F = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
	// DEC B from 0x80: underflow to 0x7F, PV set, N set, carry kept.
	cpu, _ = newCPU(0x37, 0x06, 0x80, 0x05) // SCF; LD B,0x80; DEC B
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	if b := cpu.Registers().BC >> 8; b != 0x7F {
		t.Fatalf("B = %#02x, want 0x7F", b)
	}
	want := uint8(flagY | flagH | flagX | flagPV | flagN | flagC)
	if f := flags(cpu); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("DEC F = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
}

func TestLDIRBlockTransfer(t *testing.T) {
	prog := []byte{
		0x21, 0x00, 0x20, // LD HL,0x2000
		0x11, 0x00, 0x30, // LD DE,0x3000
		0x01, 0x04, 0x00, // LD BC,0x0004
		0xED, 0xB0, // LDIR
		0x76, // HALT
	}
	cpu, bus := newCPU(prog...)
	copy(bus.mem[0x2000:], []byte{0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44})
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	wantCosts := []int{21, 21, 21, 16}
	for i, want := range wantCosts {
		if got := cpu.Step(); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("LDIR iteration %d cost = %d, want %d", i, got, want)
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if got := bus.mem[0x3000+i]; got != bus.mem[0x2000+i] {
