			t.Fatalf("copied byte %d = %#02x, want %#02x", i, got, bus.mem[0x2000+i])
		}
	}
	reg := cpu.Registers()
	if reg.BC != 0 || reg.HL != 0x2004 || reg.DE != 0x3004 {
		t.Fatalf("end state BC=%#04x HL=%#04x DE=%#04x, want 0/0x2004/0x3004",
			reg.BC, reg.HL, reg.DE)
	}
	if reg.PC != 11 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %d, want 11 (past the LDIR)", reg.PC)
	}
	if flags(cpu)&flagPV != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("PV must be clear when BC reaches 0, F = %#02x", flags(cpu))
	}
	if cpu.Cycles() != 10+10+10+21+21+21+16 {
		t.Fatalf("Cycles = %d, want 109", cpu.Cycles())
	}
}

func TestInterruptMode1(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, bus := newCPU()
	cpu.SetState(Registers{SP: 0xFF00, PC: 0x1000, IM: 1, IFF1: true})
	bus.mem[0x1000] = 0x00 // NOP
	cpu.INT(true, 0x00)
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 4+13 {
		t.Fatalf("Step cost = %d, want 17 (NOP + IM1 response)", got)
	}
	reg := cpu.Registers()
	if reg.PC != 0x0038 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %#04x, want 0x0038", reg.PC)
	}
	if reg.SP != 0xFEFE {
		t.Fatalf("SP = %#04x, want 0xFEFE", reg.SP)
	}
	if pushed := uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFF])<<8 | uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFE]); pushed != 0x1001 {
		t.Fatalf("pushed PC = %#04x, want 0x1001", pushed)
	}
	if reg.IFF1 || reg.IFF2 {
		t.Fatalf("IFF1/IFF2 must be clear after INT acceptance")
	}
}

func TestInterruptMode2Vector(t *testing.T) {

	bus.mem[0x1000] = 0x00

		t.Fatalf("PC = %#04x, want 0x5678 (from vector 0x1234)", pc)
	}
	if pushed := uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFF])<<8 | uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFE]); pushed != 0x1001 {
		t.Fatalf("pushed PC = %#04x, want 0x1001", pushed)
	}
}

func TestNMIAndRETN(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, bus := newCPU()
	cpu.SetState(Registers{SP: 0xFF00, PC: 0x2000, IFF1: true})
	bus.mem[0x2000] = 0x00 // NOP
	bus.mem[0x0066] = 0xED // RETN
	bus.mem[0x0067] = 0x45 //
	cpu.NMI()
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 4+11 {
		t.Fatalf("Step cost = %d, want 15 (NOP + NMI response)", got)
	}
	reg := cpu.Registers()
	if reg.PC != 0x0066 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %#04x, want 0x0066", reg.PC)
	}
	if reg.IFF1 {
		t.Fatal("IFF1 must be clear inside the NMI handler")
	}
	if !reg.IFF2 {
		t.Fatal("IFF2 must hold the pre-NMI IFF1 value")
	}
	if pushed := uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFF])<<8 | uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFE]); pushed != 0x2001 {
		t.Fatalf("pushed PC = %#04x, want 0x2001", pushed)
	}
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 14 {
		t.Fatalf("RETN cost = %d, want 14", got)
	}
	reg = cpu.Registers()
	if reg.PC != 0x2001 || !reg.IFF1 {
		t.Fatalf("after RETN PC = %#04x IFF1 = %v, want 0x2001/true", reg.PC, reg.IFF1)
	}
}

func TestEIDelay(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, bus := newCPU()
	cpu.SetState(Registers{SP: 0xFF00, PC: 0x3000, IM: 1})
	bus.mem[0x3000] = 0xFB // EI
	bus.mem[0x3001] = 0x00 // NOP
	bus.mem[0x3002] = 0x00 // NOP
	cpu.INT(true, 0x00)
	cpu.Step() // EI: the interrupt must NOT be taken yet
	if reg := cpu.Registers(); reg.PC != 0x3001 || reg.SP != 0xFF00 {
		t.Fatalf("after EI: PC = %#04x SP = %#04x, want 0x3001/0xFF00", reg.PC, reg.SP)
	}
	cpu.Step() // NOP: now the pending interrupt is accepted
	reg := cpu.Registers()
	if reg.PC != 0x0038 {
		t.Fatalf("after the instruction following EI: PC = %#04x, want 0x0038", reg.PC)
	}
	if pushed := uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFF])<<8 | uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFE]); pushed != 0x3002 {
		t.Fatalf("pushed PC = %#04x, want 0x3002", pushed)
	}
}

func TestHALTAndWake(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, bus := newCPU()
	cpu.SetState(Registers{SP: 0xFF00, PC: 0x4000, IM: 1, IFF1: true})
	bus.mem[0x4000] = 0x76 // HALT
	bus.mem[0x4001] = 0x00 // NOP
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("HALT cost = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if !cpu.Registers().Halted {
		t.Fatal("CPU must report Halted after HALT")
	}
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("HALT idle cost = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if pc := cpu.Registers().PC; pc != 0x4001 {
		t.Fatalf("PC while halted = %#04x, want 0x4001", pc)
	}
	cpu.INT(true, 0x00)
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 13 {
		t.Fatalf("wake+IM1 cost = %d, want 13", got)
	}
	reg := cpu.Registers()
	if reg.Halted || reg.PC != 0x0038 {
		t.Fatalf("after wake: Halted = %v PC = %#04x, want false/0x0038", reg.Halted, reg.PC)
	}
	if pushed := uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFF])<<8 | uint16(bus.mem[0xFEFE]); pushed != 0x4001 {
		t.Fatalf("pushed PC = %#04x, want 0x4001 (instruction after HALT)", pushed)
	}
}

func TestRefreshRegister(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, bus := newCPU()
	cpu.SetState(Registers{PC: 0x0000, R: 0xFF})
	bus.mem[0x0000] = 0x00 // NOP: one M1 cycle
	cpu.Step()
	if r := cpu.Registers().R; r != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("R = %#02x, want 0x80 (low 7 bits wrap, bit 7 kept)", r)
	}
	// LD A,R is ED 5F: two M1 fetches, so A receives R bumped twice.
	cpu.SetState(Registers{PC: 0x0000, R: 0x80})
	bus.mem[0x0000] = 0xED
	bus.mem[0x0001] = 0x5F
	cpu.Step()
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0x82 {
		t.Fatalf("A after LD A,R = %#02x, want 0x82", a)
	}
}

func TestIOPortFormation(t *testing.T) {
	// OUT (n),A puts A in the high byte of the port address.
	cpu, bus := newCPU(0xD3, 0x10)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{AF: 0xAB00, PC: 0})
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 11 {
		t.Fatalf("OUT (n),A cost = %d, want 11", got)
	}
	if len(bus.outLog) != 1 || bus.outLog[0] != (outWrite{0xAB10, 0xAB}) {
		t.Fatalf("out log = %v, want [{0xAB10 0xAB}]", bus.outLog)
	}
	// IN A,(n) reads through the same address formation.
	cpu, bus = newCPU(0xDB, 0x10)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{AF: 0xAB00, PC: 0})
	bus.inVal[0xAB10] = 0x5A
	cpu.Step()
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("A = %#02x, want 0x5A", a)
	}
	// OUT (C),B uses the full BC pair as the port.
	cpu, bus = newCPU(0xED, 0x41)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{BC: 0x1234, PC: 0})
	cpu.Step()
	if len(bus.outLog) != 1 || bus.outLog[0] != (outWrite{0x1234, 0x12}) {
		t.Fatalf("out log = %v, want [{0x1234 0x12}]", bus.outLog)
	}
	// IN A,(C): flags from the value, carry preserved.
	cpu, bus = newCPU(0xED, 0x78)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{AF: 0x0001, BC: 0x1234, PC: 0}) // C flag set
	bus.inVal[0x1234] = 0x80
	cpu.Step()
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("A = %#02x, want 0x80", a)
	}
	if f, want := flags(cpu), uint8(flagS|flagC); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("IN flags = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
}

func TestINIBlockIOFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// INI with C = 0x10 and input 0xF0: k = 0xF0 + (0x10 + 1) = 0x101,
	// so H and C set; N from bit 7 of the input; B drops to 0 so Z set.
	cpu, bus := newCPU(0xED, 0xA2)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{BC: 0x0110, HL: 0x3000, PC: 0})
	bus.inVal[0x0110] = 0xF0
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("INI cost = %d, want 16", got)
	}
	if bus.mem[0x3000] != 0xF0 {
		t.Fatalf("(HL) = %#02x, want 0xF0", bus.mem[0x3000])
	}
	reg := cpu.Registers()
	if reg.BC != 0x0010 || reg.HL != 0x3001 {
		t.Fatalf("BC = %#04x HL = %#04x, want 0x0010/0x3001", reg.BC, reg.HL)
	}
	want := uint8(flagZ | flagH | flagN | flagC)
	if f := flags(cpu); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("INI flags = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
}

func TestIndexedOps(t *testing.T) {
	// LD (IX+5),0x42 then LD A,(IX+5).
	cpu, bus := newCPU(0xDD, 0x36, 0x05, 0x42, 0xDD, 0x7E, 0x05)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{IX: 0x2000, PC: 0})
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 19 {
		t.Fatalf("LD (IX+d),n cost = %d, want 19", got)

		t.Fatalf("LD A,(IX+d) cost = %d, want 19", got)
	}
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("A = %#02x, want 0x42", a)
	}
	// Index halves: LD IXh,0x33 and LD A,IXh.
	cpu, _ = newCPU(0xDD, 0x26, 0x33, 0xDD, 0x7C)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{IX: 0x2000, PC: 0})
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 11 {
		t.Fatalf("LD IXh,n cost = %d, want 11", got)

	if ix := cpu.Registers().IX; ix != 0x3300 {
		t.Fatalf("IX = %#04x, want 0x3300", ix)
	}
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("LD A,IXh cost = %d, want 8", got)
	}
	if a := acc(cpu); a != 0x33 {
		t.Fatalf("A = %#02x, want 0x33", a)
	}
}

func TestDDCBSetAndBit(t *testing.T) {
	// SET 3,(IX+2) with the register-copy form landing in B (z = 0).
	cpu, bus := newCPU(0xDD, 0xCB, 0x02, 0xD8)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{IX: 0x2000, PC: 0})
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 23 {
		t.Fatalf("DDCB SET cost = %d, want 23", got)
	}
	if bus.mem[0x2002] != 0x08 {
		t.Fatalf("(IX+2) = %#02x, want 0x08", bus.mem[0x2002])
	}
	if b := cpu.Registers().BC >> 8; b != 0x08 {
		t.Fatalf("B (register copy) = %#02x, want 0x08", b)
	}
	// BIT 3,(IX+2): set, so Z clear; cost 20. BIT 2: clear, Z and PV set.
	cpu, _ = newCPU(0xDD, 0xCB, 0x02, 0x5E, 0xDD, 0xCB, 0x02, 0x56)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{IX: 0x2000, PC: 0})
	bus2 := cpu.bus.(*ramBus)
	bus2.mem[0x2002] = 0x08
	if got := cpu.Step(); got != 20 {
		t.Fatalf("DDCB BIT cost = %d, want 20", got)
	}
	if f := flags(cpu); f&flagZ != 0 || f&flagH == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BIT 3 flags = %#02x, want H set and Z clear", f)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	if f := flags(cpu); f&(flagZ|flagPV) != flagZ|flagPV {
		t.Fatalf("BIT 2 flags = %#02x, want Z and PV set", f)
	}
}

func Test16BitArithmeticFlags(t *testing.T) {
	// SBC HL,BC: 0x0000 - 0x0001 -> 0xFFFF with borrow.
	cpu, _ := newCPU(0xED, 0x42)

		t.Fatalf("SBC flags = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
	// ADC HL,BC: 0x7FFF + 0x0001 -> 0x8000, signed overflow.
	cpu, _ = newCPU(0xED, 0x4A)
	cpu.SetState(Registers{HL: 0x7FFF, BC: 0x0001, PC: 0})
	cpu.Step()
	if hl := cpu.Registers().HL; hl != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("HL = %#04x, want 0x8000", hl)
	}
	if f, want := flags(cpu), uint8(flagS|flagH|flagPV); f != want {
		t.Fatalf("ADC flags = %#02x, want %#02x", f, want)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, bus := newCPU(0x06, 0x03, 0x10, 0xFE, 0x76)
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.INT(true, 0x34)
	wantRegs := cpu.Registers()
	wantCycles := cpu.Cycles()

	buf := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := cpu.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	other, _ := newCPU(0x00)
	other.StepCycles(500) // scramble cycles and state
	if err := other.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if got := other.Registers(); got != wantRegs {
		t.Fatalf("registers after round trip:\n got %+v\nwant %+v", got, wantRegs)
	}
	if other.Cycles() != wantCycles {
		t.Fatalf("cycles after round trip = %d, want %d", other.Cycles(), wantCycles)
	}
	buf2 := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if err := other.Serialize(buf2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("re-Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	for i := range buf {
		if buf[i] != buf2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("state byte %d differs after round trip: %#02x != %#02x", i, buf[i], buf2[i])
		}
	}
	_ = bus
	if err := cpu.Serialize(make([]byte, 8)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Serialize into a short buffer must fail")
	}
	bad := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	copy(bad, buf)
	bad[0] = 0x7E
	if err := other.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize with a bad version must fail")
	}
}

func TestStepCyclesBudget(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, _ := newCPU() // all-zero memory: endless NOPs
	if got := cpu.StepCycles(100); got != 100 {
		t.Fatalf("StepCycles(100) = %d, want 100 (25 NOPs at 4 T)", got)
	}
	if cpu.Cycles() != 100 {
		t.Fatalf("Cycles = %d, want 100", cpu.Cycles())
	}
	if got := cpu.StepCycles(6); got != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("StepCycles(6) = %d, want 8 (whole instructions only)", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/cmd/ggdebug/main.go ====================

// Command ggdebug runs the Go Genesis machine directly (no libretro
// shell) and prints where the CPUs spend their time, what reached the
// VDP, and whether the framebuffer ever lights up. A debugging tool for
// core development; not part of the shipped core.
package main

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"hash/fnv"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/png"
	"os"
	"sort"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/sound"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/system"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/vdp"

	m68k "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/chips/z80"
)

const (
	masterFrame = 3420 * 262
	linesTotal  = 262
	z80PerLine  = 228
)

func m68kTarget(line int) uint64 { return uint64(line+1) * masterFrame / 7 / linesTotal }

// dumpPNG writes the visible framebuffer to a PNG file.
func dumpPNG(v *vdp.VDP, path string) {
	w, h := v.DisplayWidth(), v.DisplayHeight()
	img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, w, h))
	fb := v.Framebuffer()
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			px := fb[y*320+x]
			r5 := (px >> 11) & 0x1F
			g6 := (px >> 5) & 0x3F
			b5 := px & 0x1F
			img.Set(x, y, color.RGBA{uint8(r5<<3 | r5>>2), uint8(g6<<2 | g6>>4), uint8(b5<<3 | b5>>2), 0xFF})
		}
	}
	out, err := os.Create(path)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	png.Encode(out, img)
	out.Close()
}

// savetest replays the engine test's exact script against the system
// package and checks save/restore determinism: the frame 2 frames after
// a restore must equal the frame at the save point, and a state that is
// serialized, restored and re-serialized must be byte-identical.
func savetest(romPath string) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	sys := system.New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(data); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	frame := 0
	firstNonBlank := -1
	fbHash := func() uint64 {
		h := fnv.New64a()
		var b [2]byte
		for _, px := range sys.Framebuffer() {
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[:], px)
			h.Write(b[:])
		}
		return h.Sum64()
	}
	audioNZ := 0
	run := func(n int, mask uint16) {
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			sys.SetButtons(0, mask)
			sys.RunFrame()
			frame++
			for _, s := range sys.AudioBuffer() {
				if s != 0 && frame > 400 {
					audioNZ++
				}
			}
			if firstNonBlank < 0 && frame <= 200 {
				for _, px := range sys.Framebuffer() {
					if px != 0 {
						firstNonBlank = frame
						break
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	run(120, 0)
	run(480, 0)
	run(10, bus.PadStart)
	run(120, 0)
	fmt.Printf("first non-blank frame: %d\n", firstNonBlank)
	// Dump the save-point frame (in-level gameplay) as a PNG.
	{
		w, h := sys.Width(), sys.Height()
		img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, w, h))
		fb := sys.Framebuffer()
		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				px := fb[y*320+x]
				r5 := (px >> 11) & 0x1F
				g6 := (px >> 5) & 0x3F
				b5 := px & 0x1F
				img.Set(x, y, color.RGBA{uint8(r5<<3 | r5>>2), uint8(g6<<2 | g6>>4), uint8(b5<<3 | b5>>2), 0xFF})
			}
		}
		out, _ := os.Create("/tmp/gengames/gameplay.png")
		png.Encode(out, img)
		out.Close()
		fmt.Println("gameplay frame dumped to /tmp/gengames/gameplay.png")
	}
	h1 := fbHash()
	state := make([]byte, sys.SerializeSize())
	if err := sys.Serialize(state); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("save point: frame=%d fb=%016x state=%d bytes\n", frame, h1, len(state))
	psgW, ymW := sys.SoundWrites()
	fmt.Printf("audio: %d non-zero samples produced in frames 401-%d; chip writes so far: PSG=%d YM2612=%d\n",
		audioNZ, frame, psgW, ymW)

	run(2, bus.PadDown)
	h732 := fbHash()
	run(8, bus.PadDown)
	run(30, 0)
	fmt.Printf("moved on:   frame=%d fb=%016x (differs: %v)\n", frame, fbHash(), fbHash() != h1)

	if err := sys.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	rt := make([]byte, sys.SerializeSize())
	if err := sys.Serialize(rt); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	regions := []struct {
		name string
		lo   int
		hi   int
	}{
		{"m68k regs", 0, 80},
		{"z80 cpu", 80, 127},
		{"bus", 127, 139411},
		{"vdp", 139411, 205189},
		{"sound", 205189, 207125},
		{"trailer", 207125, len(state)},
	}
	ndiff := 0
	for i := range state {
		if state[i] != rt[i] {
			if ndiff < 5 {
				reg := "?"
				for _, r := range regions {
					if i >= r.lo && i < r.hi {
						reg = r.name
					}
				}
				fmt.Printf("state round-trip diff at byte %d (%s): %02x != %02x\n", i, reg, state[i], rt[i])
			}
			ndiff++
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("state round-trip: %d bytes differ\n", ndiff)

	run(2, bus.PadDown)
	h3 := fbHash()
	fmt.Printf("restored+2: fb=%016x  harness-match(save point)=%v  deterministic-match(frame732)=%v\n",
		h3, h3 == h1, h3 == h732)
}

// playshot runs a game past its title screen, presses Start, plays a
// few seconds and dumps the frame: a visual proof of gameplay.
func playshot(romPath string) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	sys := system.New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(data); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	frame := 0
	dump := func(tag string) {
		colors := map[uint16]bool{}
		for _, px := range sys.Framebuffer() {
			colors[px] = true
		}
		w, h := sys.Width(), sys.Height()
		img := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, w, h))
		fb := sys.Framebuffer()
		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				px := fb[y*320+x]
				r5 := (px >> 11) & 0x1F
				g6 := (px >> 5) & 0x3F
				b5 := px & 0x1F
				img.Set(x, y, color.RGBA{uint8(r5<<3 | r5>>2), uint8(g6<<2 | g6>>4), uint8(b5<<3 | b5>>2), 0xFF})
			}
		}
		out, _ := os.Create("/tmp/gengames/play_" + tag + ".png")
		png.Encode(out, img)
		out.Close()
		fmt.Printf("frame %d (%s): %d distinct colors\n", frame, tag, len(colors))
	}
	run := func(n int, mask uint16) {
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			sys.SetButtons(0, mask)
			sys.RunFrame()
			sys.AudioBuffer()
			frame++
		}
	}
	run(700, 0)
	dump("700")
	run(120, 0)
	dump("820")
	run(10, bus.PadStart) // start the game
	dump("830")
	run(180, 0)
	dump("1010")
	run(150, 0)
	dump("1160")
	run(90, 0)
	dump("1250")
	run(120, 0)
	dump("1370")
}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) >= 3 && os.Args[1] == "-savetest" {
		savetest(os.Args[2])
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) >= 3 && os.Args[1] == "-playshot" {
		playshot(os.Args[2])
		return
	}
	if len(os.Args) < 2 {
		fmt.Println("usage: ggdebug <rom> [frames] | ggdebug -savetest <rom>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(os.Args[1])
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	frames := 180
	if len(os.Args) > 2 {
		fmt.Sscanf(os.Args[2], "%d", &frames)
	}
	c, err := cart.Load(data)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("cart: %q serial=%s checksum ok=%v sram=%v region=%c\n",
		c.Title, c.Serial, c.ChecksumOK, c.SRAM, c.Region)

	v := vdp.New()
	snd := sound.New()
	b := bus.New(c, v, snd)
	cpu := m68k.New(b)
	zcpu := z80.New(b)
	cpu.Reset()
	zcpu.Reset()
	fmt.Printf("boot: SSP=%08X PC=%08X\n", cpu.Registers().A[7], cpu.Registers().PC)

	pcHist := map[uint32]int{}
	var trail []uint32
	run68k := func(target uint64) {
		for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
			cur := cpu.Cycles()
			if cur >= target {
				return
			}
			cpu.StepCycles(int(target - cur))
			pc := cpu.Registers().PC
			pcHist[pc]++
			if pc != 0x71FC4 && pc != 0x71FC6 {
				trail = append(trail, pc)
				if len(trail) > 400 {
					trail = trail[len(trail)-400:]
				}
			}
			if cpu.Cycles() == cur {
				return
			}
		}
	}
	runZ80 := func() {
		if b.TakeZ80Reset() {
			zcpu.Reset()
		}
		if b.Z80Halted() {
			return
		}
		target := zcpu.Cycles() + z80PerLine
		for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
			cur := zcpu.Cycles()
			if cur >= target {
				return
			}
			zcpu.StepCycles(int(target - cur))
			if zcpu.Cycles() == cur {
				return
			}
		}
	}

	startAt := -1
	if s := os.Getenv("START_AT"); s != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d", &startAt)
	}
	for f := 0; f < frames; f++ {
		if f == startAt {
			b.SetPad(0, bus.PadStart)
		}
		if f == startAt+10 {
			b.SetPad(0, 0)
		}
		h := v.DisplayHeight()
		base := uint64(f) * masterFrame / 7
		v.BeginFrame()
		for line := 0; line < linesTotal; line++ {
			if line == 0 {
				v.ExitVBlank()
				zcpu.INT(false, 0)
			}
			run68k(base + m68kTarget(line))
			runZ80()
			if line < h {
				if v.LineIRQ(line) {
					cpu.RequestInterrupt(4, nil)
				}
				v.RenderLine(line)
			}
			if line == h {
				if v.EnterVBlank() {
					cpu.RequestInterrupt(6, nil)
				}
				zcpu.INT(true, 0xFF)
			}
		}
		snd.Produce(736)

		if f%30 == 29 || f == frames-1 {
			vramNZ, cramNZ := 0, 0
			for _, x := range v.VRAM {
				if x != 0 {
					vramNZ++
				}
			}
			for _, x := range v.CRAM {
				if x != 0 {
					cramNZ++
				}
			}
			fb := v.Framebuffer()
			colors := map[uint16]bool{}
			for _, px := range fb {
				colors[px] = true
			}
			if f+1 == 500 {
				dumpPNG(v, "/tmp/gengames/frame500.png")
				fmt.Printf("frame 500 PC=%08X CRAM0=%04X\n", cpu.Registers().PC, uint16(v.CRAM[0])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[1]))
			}
			if f+1 == 210 {
				vals := []int{}
				for px := range colors {
					vals = append(vals, int(px))
				}
				sort.Ints(vals)
				fmt.Printf("frame 210 distinct fb values: %04X\n", vals)
				fmt.Printf("frame 210 CRAM words 0-7: %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X\n",
					uint16(v.CRAM[0])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[1]), uint16(v.CRAM[2])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[3]),
					uint16(v.CRAM[4])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[5]), uint16(v.CRAM[6])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[7]),
					uint16(v.CRAM[8])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[9]), uint16(v.CRAM[10])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[11]),
					uint16(v.CRAM[12])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[13]), uint16(v.CRAM[14])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[15]))
				dumpPNG(v, "/tmp/gengames/frame210.png")
			}
			r := cpu.Registers()
			fmt.Printf("frame %3d: PC=%08X SR=%04X D0=%08X D1=%08X A0=%08X cycles=%d VDP R1=%02X dispW=%d VRAM nz=%d CRAM nz=%d colors=%d Z80 halted=%v Z80 PC=%04X\n",
				f+1, r.PC, r.SR, r.D[0], r.D[1], r.A[0], cpu.Cycles(), v.Regs[1], v.DisplayWidth(), vramNZ, cramNZ, len(colors), b.Z80Halted(), zcpu.Registers().PC)
		}
	}

	type pcCount struct {
		pc uint32
		n  int
	}
	var top []pcCount
	for pc, n := range pcHist {
		top = append(top, pcCount{pc, n})
	}
	sort.Slice(top, func(i, j int) bool { return top[i].n > top[j].n })
	fmt.Println("--- hottest PCs (where the 68000 spends its time):")
	for i := 0; i < len(top) && i < 8; i++ {
		txt, _ := m68k.Disassemble(top[i].pc, func(addr uint32) uint16 {
			return uint16(c.ReadROM(addr))<<8 | uint16(c.ReadROM(addr+1))
		})
		fmt.Printf("  %08X x%-6d %s\n", top[i].pc, top[i].n, txt)
	}
	fmt.Printf("VDP regs: % X\n", v.Regs)

	zramNZ := 0
	for _, x := range b.ZRAM {
		if x != 0 {
			zramNZ++
		}
	}
	ramNZ := 0
	for _, x := range b.RAM {
		if x != 0 {
			ramNZ++
		}
	}
	fmt.Printf("ZRAM nz=%d RAM nz=%d\n", zramNZ, ramNZ)
	fmt.Printf("CRAM words 0-7: %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X\n",
		uint16(v.CRAM[0])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[1]), uint16(v.CRAM[2])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[3]),
		uint16(v.CRAM[4])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[5]), uint16(v.CRAM[6])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[7]),
		uint16(v.CRAM[8])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[9]), uint16(v.CRAM[10])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[11]),
		uint16(v.CRAM[12])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[13]), uint16(v.CRAM[14])<<8|uint16(v.CRAM[15]))

	// Dump the final framebuffer as a PNG we can look at.
	dumpPNG(v, "/tmp/gengames/frame.png")
	fmt.Println("frame dumped to /tmp/gengames/frame.png")

	fmt.Println("--- last distinct PCs before the 0x71FC4 delay loop took over:")
	seen := map[uint32]bool{}
	shown := 0
	for i := len(trail) - 1; i >= 0 && shown < 24; i-- {
		if !seen[trail[i]] {
			seen[trail[i]] = true
			shown++
		}
	}
	// print in forward order, distinct only
	seen = map[uint32]bool{}
	for _, pc := range trail {
		if seen[pc] {
			continue
		}
		seen[pc] = true
		txt, _ := m68k.Disassemble(pc, func(addr uint32) uint16 {
			return uint16(c.ReadROM(addr))<<8 | uint16(c.ReadROM(addr+1))
		})
		fmt.Printf("  %08X  %s\n", pc, txt)
	}

	fmt.Println("--- disassembly 0x71F80-0x72040:")
	for pc := uint32(0x71F80); pc < 0x72040; {
		txt, next := m68k.Disassemble(pc, func(addr uint32) uint16 {
			return uint16(c.ReadROM(addr))<<8 | uint16(c.ReadROM(addr+1))
		})
		fmt.Printf("  %08X  %s\n", pc, txt)
		if next > pc {
			pc = next
		} else if next > 0 {
			pc += next
		} else {
			pc += 2
		}
	}
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/libretro/disc.go ====================

package main

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// Disc routing for retro_load_game. A frontend can hand this core a
// cartridge image, a cue sheet path, an ISO path, or a raw disc image
// with no path at all. These helpers decide which loader the bytes and
// the path belong to; they are pure so they can be unit tested without
// the cgo shell.

// Load routes returned by routeFor.
const (
	routeCartridge = iota
	routeDiscPath
	routeDiscData
)

// discSignature is the boot signature at the start of every Sega CD
// disc's data area.
const discSignature = "SEGADISCSYSTEM"

// sniffDisc reports whether data looks like a Sega CD disc image. A
// 2048 byte sector image carries the signature at offset 0. A raw
// 2352 byte sector image carries the twelve byte sync pattern first
// (0x00, ten 0xFF bytes, 0x00), then a four byte header, so the
// signature lands at offset 16. A Genesis cartridge, which carries
// "SEGA" at offset 0x100 instead, returns false.
func sniffDisc(data []byte) bool {
	if len(data) >= len(discSignature) && string(data[:len(discSignature)]) == discSignature {
		return true
	}
	if len(data) < 16+len(discSignature) {
		return false
	}
	if data[0] != 0x00 || data[11] != 0x00 {
		return false
	}
	for i := 1; i <= 10; i++ {
		if data[i] != 0xFF {
			return false
		}
	}
	return string(data[16:16+len(discSignature)]) == discSignature
}

// routeFor picks the loader for one retro_load_game call. A .cue or
// .iso path always wins: the cue sheet is not the disc data, and an
// ISO is a disc by definition. Otherwise the data decides: a disc
// signature means a disc, loaded from its path when it has one and
// from the bytes themselves when it does not. Anything else is a
// cartridge.
func routeFor(path string, data []byte) int {
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".cue", ".iso":
		return routeDiscPath
	}
	if sniffDisc(data) {
		if path != "" {
			return routeDiscPath
		}
		return routeDiscData
	}
	return routeCartridge
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/libretro/disc_test.go ====================

package main

import "testing"

// discImage2048 returns a one sector 2048 byte image carrying the
// boot signature at offset 0.
func discImage2048() []byte {
	data := make([]byte, 2048)
	copy(data, "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	return data
}

// discImage2352 returns a one sector raw 2352 byte image: the sync
// pattern at offset 0, a four byte header, then the boot signature
// at offset 16.
func discImage2352() []byte {
	data := make([]byte, 2352)
	data[0] = 0x00
	for i := 1; i <= 10; i++ {
		data[i] = 0xFF
	}
	data[11] = 0x00
	copy(data[16:], "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	return data
}

// cartridgeImage returns a small cartridge image carrying "SEGA" at
// offset 0x100, as a Genesis ROM header does.
func cartridgeImage() []byte {
	data := make([]byte, 1024)
	copy(data[0x100:], "SEGA")
	return data
}

func TestSniffDisc(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		data []byte
		want bool
	}{
		{"2048 image", discImage2048(), true},
		{"2352 image", discImage2352(), true},
		{"cartridge header", cartridgeImage(), false},
		{"empty", nil, false},
		{"short", []byte("SEGA"), false},
		{"truncated signature", []byte("SEGADISC"), false},
		{"2352 signature without sync", func() []byte {
			data := make([]byte, 2352)
			copy(data[16:], "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
			return data
		}(), false},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		if got := sniffDisc(tc.data); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: sniffDisc = %v, want %v", tc.name, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestRouteFor(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		path string
		data []byte
		want int
	}{
		{"cue path wins over cartridge data", "game.cue", cartridgeImage(), routeDiscPath},
		{"uppercase cue path", "GAME.CUE", cartridgeImage(), routeDiscPath},
		{"iso path", "game.iso", cartridgeImage(), routeDiscPath},
		{"bin path with disc data", "game.bin", discImage2048(), routeDiscPath},
		{"no path with 2048 disc data", "", discImage2048(), routeDiscData},
		{"no path with 2352 disc data", "", discImage2352(), routeDiscData},
		{"md path with cartridge data", "game.md", cartridgeImage(), routeCartridge},
		{"no path with cartridge data", "", cartridgeImage(), routeCartridge},
		{"bin path with cartridge data", "game.bin", cartridgeImage(), routeCartridge},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		if got := routeFor(tc.path, tc.data); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: routeFor(%q) = %d, want %d", tc.name, tc.path, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/libretro/main.go ====================

// Command libretro builds the Go Genesis core as a libretro shared
// library (go build -buildmode=c-shared). It is a thin C ABI shell over
// the system package: the frontend (the iTaK engine) registers its
// callbacks, hands us a ROM, and calls retro_run once per frame.
package main

/*

static size_t gg_audio_batch(const int16_t *data, size_t frames) { return audio_batch_cb ? audio_batch_cb(data, frames) : 0; }

import "C"

import (
	"os"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/system"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/vdp"

// libretro constants used here (from the public libretro API).
const (
	envSetPixelFormat = 10
	pixelFormatRGB565 = 2
	deviceJoypad      = 1
	joypadB           = 0
	joypadY           = 1
	joypadSelect      = 2
	joypadStart       = 3
	joypadUp          = 4
	joypadDown        = 5
	joypadLeft        = 6
	joypadRight       = 7
	joypadA           = 8
	regionNTSC        = 0
	genesisFPS        = 59.9227
	genesisAspectH40  = 1.3061 // pixel-aspect corrected, matches Genesis Plus GX
	genesisAspectH32  = 1.2152
	sampleRate        = 44100
)

var sys *system.System

// ranFrames distinguishes "loaded but not started yet" from a running
// game for geometry reporting: the VDP powers on in H32 mode, but most
// Genesis games switch to H40 during boot, so before the first frame the
// honest default geometry is 320 wide.
var ranFrames bool

// discTempPath is the temp file written when a frontend hands us disc
// bytes with no path (the routeDiscData route). retro_unload_game
// deletes it.
var discTempPath string

func main() {}

//export retro_api_version
func retro_api_version() C.uint { return 1 }

//export retro_init
func retro_init() { sys = system.New() }

//export retro_deinit
func retro_deinit() { sys = nil }

//export retro_set_environment

//export retro_set_video_refresh
func retro_set_video_refresh(cb C.retro_video_refresh_t) { C.gg_set_video(cb) }

//export retro_set_audio_sample

//export retro_set_audio_sample_batch

//export retro_get_system_info
func retro_get_system_info(info *C.struct_gg_system_info) {
	info.library_name = C.gg_get_name()
	info.library_version = C.gg_get_version()
	info.valid_extensions = C.gg_get_exts()
	info.need_fullpath = false
	info.block_extract = false
}

//export retro_get_system_av_info
func retro_get_system_av_info(info *C.struct_gg_av_info) {
	w, h := 320, 224
	aspect := genesisAspectH40
	if sys != nil && sys.Loaded() && ranFrames {
		w, h = sys.Width(), sys.Height()
		if w == 256 {
			aspect = genesisAspectH32
		}
	}
	info.geometry.base_width = C.unsigned(w)
	info.geometry.base_height = C.unsigned(h)
	info.geometry.max_width = vdp.MaxWidth
	info.geometry.max_height = vdp.MaxHeight
	info.geometry.aspect_ratio = C.float(aspect)
	info.timing.fps = genesisFPS
	info.timing.sample_rate = sampleRate
}

//export retro_get_region
func retro_get_region() C.unsigned { return regionNTSC }

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_gg_game_info) C.bool {
	var path string
	if info.path != nil {
		path = C.GoString(info.path)
	}
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	} else if info.path != nil {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		data = b
	} else {
		return false
	}
	if sys == nil {
		sys = system.New()
	}
	switch routeFor(path, data) {
	case routeDiscPath:
		if err := sys.LoadDisc(path); err != nil {
			return false
		}
	case routeDiscData:
		// LoadDisc works on files, so park the bytes in a temp ISO
		// first. retro_unload_game deletes it.
		f, err := os.CreateTemp("", "itak-disc-*.iso")
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		tmpPath := f.Name()
		if _, err := f.Write(data); err != nil {
			f.Close()
			os.Remove(tmpPath)
			return false
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			os.Remove(tmpPath)
			return false
		}
		if err := sys.LoadDisc(tmpPath); err != nil {
			os.Remove(tmpPath)
			return false
		}
		discTempPath = tmpPath
	default:
		if err := sys.LoadGame(data); err != nil {
			return false
		}
	}
	// Ask the frontend for RGB565 frames (what the VDP produces).
	fmt565 := C.uint32_t(pixelFormatRGB565)
	C.gg_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&fmt565))
	return true
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() {
	if discTempPath != "" {
		os.Remove(discTempPath)
		discTempPath = ""
	}
	sys = system.New()
	ranFrames = false
}

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys != nil {
		sys.Reset()
	}
}

func pressed(port int, id uint) bool {
	return C.gg_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceJoypad, 0, C.unsigned(id)) != 0
}

// pollPad translates libretro joypad state into the bus pad layout.
// 3-button Genesis pad mapping (same as Genesis Plus GX defaults):
// libretro Y = Genesis A, B = B, A = C, Select = Mode, Start = Start.
func pollPad(port int) uint16 {
	var m uint16
	if pressed(port, joypadUp) {
		m |= bus.PadUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadDown) {
		m |= bus.PadDown
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadLeft) {
		m |= bus.PadLeft
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadRight) {
		m |= bus.PadRight
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadY) {
		m |= bus.PadA
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadB) {
		m |= bus.PadB
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadA) {
		m |= bus.PadC
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadStart) {
		m |= bus.PadStart
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadSelect) {
		m |= bus.PadMode
	}
	return m
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() {
	if sys == nil || !sys.Loaded() {
		return
	}
	ranFrames = true
	C.gg_input_poll()
	sys.SetButtons(0, pollPad(0))
	sys.SetButtons(1, pollPad(1))
	sys.RunFrame()

	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) > 0 {
		C.gg_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]),
			C.unsigned(sys.Width()), C.unsigned(sys.Height()),
			C.size_t(vdp.MaxWidth*2))
	}
	ab := sys.AudioBuffer()
	if len(ab) >= 2 {
		frames := len(ab) / 2
		done := int(C.gg_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&ab[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
		for i := done; i < frames; i++ {
			C.gg_audio_sample(C.int16_t(ab[2*i]), C.int16_t(ab[2*i+1]))
		}
	}
}

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.SerializeSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.SerializeSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	return sys.Serialize(buf) == nil
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.SerializeSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	return sys.Deserialize(buf) == nil
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/scd/asic.go ====================

package scd

import "encoding/binary"

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Graphics ASIC (rotation and scaling), SCD-3.
//
// The ASIC register file lives in the sub CPU register page only,
// at offsets 0x58 to 0x67 (sub CPU addresses 0xFF8058 to 0xFF8067).
// The main CPU has no access to it on the documented hardware: the
// main side window at 0xA12010 to 0xA1202F is the communication
// register area (SCD-1), not the ASIC. Register map, from the
// published register documentation (the public Sega CD ASIC
// register list, cross-checked against the homebrew gate array
// headers that name the same offsets):
//
//	0x58  stamp size and status (word): bit15 GRON (read only,
//	      1 while a graphics operation is running), bit2 SMS
//	      (stamp map size), bit1 STS (stamp size), bit0 RPT
//	      (repeat stamp map)
//	0x5A  stamp map base address: Word RAM byte address / 4
//	0x5C  image buffer vertical cell size: low byte is the image
//	      buffer column height in 8 dot cells, minus 1
//	0x5E  image buffer start address: Word RAM byte address / 4
//	0x60  image buffer offset: low byte bits 0-2 horizontal dot
//	      offset, bits 3-5 vertical dot offset
//	0x62  image buffer horizontal dot size (9 bits)
//	0x64  image buffer vertical dot size: low byte; hardware
//	      counts it down per rendered line
//	0x66  trace table base address: Word RAM byte address / 4;
//	      writing it starts the graphics operation
//
// The trace vectors are NOT registers. They live in a trace table
// in Word RAM, one 8 byte entry per output line: start X and
// start Y as unsigned 13.3 fixed point words, then delta X and
// delta Y as signed 5.11 fixed point words. The ASIC walks one
// entry per line, accumulating the position at 13.11 precision
// (the start value shifted left 8) and adding the delta after
// each dot.
//
// Stamp map entries are words: bits 10:0 are the stamp number
// (stamp data byte address = number * 128; with 32x32 stamps the
// low 2 bits are masked out, so numbers are multiples of 4),
// bit15 is the horizontal flip, bits 14:13 are a rotation in
// quarter turns (00 = 0, 01 = 90, 10 = 180, 11 = 270). There is
// no vertical flip bit and no per-entry priority bit: a vertical
// flip is the horizontal flip plus the 180 rotation. Stamp data
// starts at Word RAM offset 0 and stamp 0 is always blank. A
// stamp is a grid of 8x8 cells stored column by column like Mega
// Drive sprites: the cell at column cx, row cy sits at cell index
// cy + cx * (cells per side) inside the stamp, each cell 32
// bytes in standard tile layout, two 4 bit dots per byte with the
// even dot in the high nibble.
//
// The image buffer uses the same cell layout in Word RAM: dots
// are addressed by a dot index that steps across an 8 dot cell
// row, then jumps by the column stride (the column height in
// dots, minus 7) to the next cell column, and the next output
// line starts 8 dots later. Byte offset = dot index / 2.
//
// Pixel writes follow the priority mode field of the memory mode
// register (in this core's register model, bits 4:3 of register
// 0x03, the same two bits the SCD-1 model reads as the CDC
// destination select; software sets the field before whichever
// operation it runs):
//
//	0  normal:    the fetched pixel always replaces the old one
//	1  underwrite: the fetched pixel lands only where the old
//	              nibble is 0
//	2  overwrite: the fetched pixel lands only when it is not 0
//	3  prohibited: nothing is written
//
// A position outside the stamp map (with repeat off) and stamp 0
// both fetch pixel 0, which then goes through the priority rule
// like any other pixel: the brief for this slice said pixel 0 is
// always skipped, but the documented rule is the mode field
// above, and only overwrite mode skips zeros.
//
// Rendering model: the draw runs synchronously when the trace
// table base register is written, except that the ASIC can only
// reach Word RAM while the sub CPU has access to it (2M mode
// owned by the sub CPU, or 1M mode, where the sub CPU always
// holds a half). A trace started without access stays pending:
// GRON reads 1 and the draw runs the moment access is granted.
// While a draw is not pending GRON reads 0, so software polling
// the status bit sees completion immediately in the common case.
// Hardware draw timing (Word RAM access cycles per line) and the
// level 1 completion interrupt are not modeled; this core's
// SCD-1 register model has no level 1 interrupt mask register.
// In 1M mode the ASIC addresses the full physical 256 KB Word
// RAM, as it does in 2M mode; the published material documents
// the access requirement but no bank selection for the ASIC.
// The ASIC also has a font conversion function at offsets 0x4C
// to 0x57 on real hardware; it is a separate feature and is not
// implemented in this slice (those offsets keep their SCD-1
// behavior).
//
// Byte access note: the registers are word wide. In this byte
// oriented bus the trace starts on the write that completes the
// trace base value, its low byte (offset 0x67); a 68k word write
// therefore behaves exactly as on hardware.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// ASICStateSize is the serialized size of the graphics ASIC
// state. It occupies bytes 242 to 254 of the unit's 256 byte
// state block, in the previously reserved tail:
// stamp control byte, stamp map base, image buffer vertical cell
// size, image buffer start, image buffer offset, image buffer
// horizontal dots, image buffer vertical dots, trace table base,
// and the pending flag. SCD-1 and SCD-2 states have zeros there
// and load with the ASIC at its power-on state.
const ASICStateSize = 13

// asicState is the graphics ASIC register file and draw state.
// Registers are stored raw, as written; documented masks are
// applied where the values are used.
type asicState struct {
	stampCtl  uint8  // offset 0x58 low byte: bit2 SMS, bit1 STS, bit0 RPT
	stampMap  uint16 // offset 0x5A: stamp map base, Word RAM bytes / 4
	imgVCell  uint8  // offset 0x5C low byte: column height in cells minus 1
	imgStart  uint16 // offset 0x5E: image buffer start, Word RAM bytes / 4
	imgOffset uint8  // offset 0x60 low byte: bits 0-2 H dots, bits 3-5 V dots
	imgHDots  uint16 // offset 0x62: dots per line (9 bits used)
	imgVDots  uint8  // offset 0x64 low byte: lines to render
	traceBase uint16 // offset 0x66: trace table base, Word RAM bytes / 4
	pending   bool   // a trace is waiting for sub CPU Word RAM access
}

// asicRead reads one ASIC register byte, offsets 0x58 to 0x67.
func (u *Unit) asicRead(off uint8) uint8 {
	a := &u.asic
	switch off {
	case 0x58:
		if a.pending {
			return 0x80 // GRON: a graphics operation is running
		}
		return 0
	case 0x59:
		return a.stampCtl
	case 0x5A:
		return uint8(a.stampMap >> 8)
	case 0x5B:
		return uint8(a.stampMap)
	case 0x5C:
		return 0
	case 0x5D:
		return a.imgVCell
	case 0x5E:
		return uint8(a.imgStart >> 8)
	case 0x5F:
		return uint8(a.imgStart)
	case 0x60:
		return 0
	case 0x61:
		return a.imgOffset
	case 0x62:
		return uint8(a.imgHDots >> 8)
	case 0x63:
		return uint8(a.imgHDots)
	case 0x64:
		return 0
	case 0x65:
		return a.imgVDots
	case 0x66:
		return uint8(a.traceBase >> 8)
	case 0x67:
		return uint8(a.traceBase)
	}
	return 0
}

// asicWrite writes one ASIC register byte, offsets 0x58 to 0x67.
// Writing the trace table base starts the operation. On this
// byte oriented bus the start is the low byte write (offset
// 0x67): a 68k word write stores the high byte first and then
// completes the value with the low byte, so word writes start
// exactly one operation with the full value, as on hardware.
func (u *Unit) asicWrite(off uint8, v uint8) {
	a := &u.asic
	switch off {
	case 0x58:
		// GRON is read-only status; high byte writes are ignored.
	case 0x59:
		a.stampCtl = v
	case 0x5A:
		a.stampMap = a.stampMap&0x00FF | uint16(v)<<8
	case 0x5B:
		a.stampMap = a.stampMap&0xFF00 | uint16(v)
	case 0x5C:
	case 0x5D:
		a.imgVCell = v
	case 0x5E:
		a.imgStart = a.imgStart&0x00FF | uint16(v)<<8
	case 0x5F:
		a.imgStart = a.imgStart&0xFF00 | uint16(v)
	case 0x60:
	case 0x61:
		a.imgOffset = v
	case 0x62:
		a.imgHDots = a.imgHDots&0x00FF | uint16(v)<<8
	case 0x63:
		a.imgHDots = a.imgHDots&0xFF00 | uint16(v)
	case 0x64:
	case 0x65:
		a.imgVDots = v
	case 0x66:
		a.traceBase = a.traceBase&0x00FF | uint16(v)<<8
	case 0x67:
		a.traceBase = a.traceBase&0xFF00 | uint16(v)
		u.startTrace()
	}
}

// ASICBusy reports whether a graphics operation is running: in
// this synchronous model that means a trace is latched and
// waiting for the sub CPU to gain Word RAM access (GRON = 1).
func (u *Unit) ASICBusy() bool { return u.asic.pending }

// ASICLinesRemaining returns the image buffer vertical dot count
// as the register reads it: the programmed line count while a
// trace is pending, and 0 once the draw has run (hardware counts
// it down line by line as it draws).
func (u *Unit) ASICLinesRemaining() int { return int(u.asic.imgVDots) }

// subWordAccess reports whether the sub CPU can reach Word RAM
// right now: always in 1M mode (the sub CPU holds one half), and
// in 2M mode only while it owns the whole array.
func (u *Unit) subWordAccess() bool {
	return u.memMode != 0 || u.wordOwner == 1
}

// startTrace latches a graphics operation and runs it at once if
// the ASIC can reach Word RAM.
func (u *Unit) startTrace() {
	u.asic.pending = true
	u.tryASIC()
}

// tryASIC runs a pending trace once the sub CPU has Word RAM
// access. It is called on trace starts, on memory mode changes
// that can grant access, and on every cycle advance, so a
// deferred draw lands the moment ownership passes.
func (u *Unit) tryASIC() {
	if !u.asic.pending || !u.subWordAccess() {
		return
	}
	u.asic.pending = false
	u.drawTrace()
}

// asicPrioNibble applies one priority mode to a single nibble:
// old is the nibble already in the image buffer, pix the fetched
// pixel.
func asicPrioNibble(pm, old, pix uint8) uint8 {
	switch pm {
	case 0: // normal
		return pix
	case 1: // underwrite
		if old != 0 {
			return old
		}
		return pix
	case 2: // overwrite
		if pix != 0 {
			return pix
		}
		return old
	default: // 3: prohibited
		return old
	}
}

// asicTransform maps a within-stamp destination dot coordinate
// to the source coordinate the ASIC samples, applying a stamp
// map entry's flip and rotation field (hrr: bit2 horizontal
// flip, bits 1:0 rotation in quarter turns). The flip applies
// first, then the rotation components, in the documented
// transform order. mask is stampSize-1 (15 or 31).
func asicTransform(px, py, mask uint32, hrr uint16) (uint32, uint32) {
	if hrr&4 != 0 { // horizontal flip
		px = mask - px
	}
	if hrr&2 != 0 { // rotation bit 1: flip both axes
		px = mask - px
		py = mask - py
	}
	if hrr&1 != 0 { // rotation bit 0: transpose with a flip
		px, py = mask-py, px
	}
	return px, py
}

// drawTrace runs one full graphics operation: every line of the
// image buffer is traced from its trace table entry. All Word
// RAM addressing wraps at the 256 KB boundary.
func (u *Unit) drawTrace() {
	a := &u.asic
	wr := u.wordRAM[:]

	sms := a.stampCtl&0x04 != 0
	sts := a.stampCtl&0x02 != 0
	rpt := a.stampCtl&0x01 != 0

	// Map geometry per (SMS, STS), from the register
	// documentation: dotMask is the stamp map extent in the
	// internal 13.11 dot coordinate space, stampShift converts a
	// dot coordinate to a stamp column, mapShift is log2 of the
	// stamps per map row, and mapAlign masks the stamp map base
	// address to its documented alignment.
	var dotMask, mapAlign uint32
	var stampShift, mapShift uint
	var stampSize uint32 = 16
	switch {
	case !sms && !sts: // 256x256 dots, 16x16 stamps, 16x16 map
		dotMask, stampShift, mapShift, mapAlign = 0x7FFFF, 15, 4, 0x3FE00
	case !sms && sts: // 256x256 dots, 32x32 stamps, 8x8 map
		dotMask, stampShift, mapShift, mapAlign = 0x7FFFF, 16, 3, 0x3FF80
		stampSize = 32
	case sms && !sts: // 4096x4096 dots, 16x16 stamps, 256x256 map
		dotMask, stampShift, mapShift, mapAlign = 0x7FFFFF, 15, 8, 0x20000
	case sms && sts: // 4096x4096 dots, 32x32 stamps, 128x128 map
		dotMask, stampShift, mapShift, mapAlign = 0x7FFFFF, 16, 7, 0x38000
		stampSize = 32
	}
	stampMask := uint32(0x7FF)
	if sts {
		stampMask = 0x7FC // 32x32 stamp numbers are multiples of 4
	}
	cellsPerSide := stampSize / 8

	mapBase := (uint32(a.stampMap) << 2) & mapAlign
	traceAddr := (uint32(a.traceBase) << 2) & 0x3FFF8
	colStride := ((uint32(a.imgVCell&0x1F) + 1) << 6) - 7
	bufStart := (uint32(a.imgStart)<<3)&0x7FFC0 + uint32(a.imgOffset&0x3F)
	width := uint32(a.imgHDots) & 0x1FF
	pm := (u.reg03 >> 3) & 0x03

	lines := int(a.imgVDots)
	bufIdx := bufStart
	for line := 0; line < lines; line++ {
		x := int32(uint32(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(wr[traceAddr:])) << 8)
		y := int32(uint32(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(wr[traceAddr+2:])) << 8)
		dx := int32(int16(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(wr[traceAddr+4:])))
		dy := int32(int16(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(wr[traceAddr+6:])))
		traceAddr = (traceAddr + 8) & 0x3FFFF

		idx := bufIdx
		for d := uint32(0); d < width; d++ {
			ux, uy := uint32(x), uint32(y)
			if rpt {
				ux &= dotMask
				uy &= dotMask
			} else {
				ux &= 0xFFFFFF
				uy &= 0xFFFFFF
			}
			var pix uint8
			if (ux|uy)&^dotMask == 0 {
				mapIdx := (ux >> stampShift) | ((uy >> stampShift) << mapShift)
				entry := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(wr[(mapBase+mapIdx*2)&0x3FFFF:])
				if num := uint32(entry) & stampMask; num != 0 {
					px := (ux >> 11) & (stampSize - 1)
					py := (uy >> 11) & (stampSize - 1)
					tx, ty := asicTransform(px, py, stampSize-1, (entry>>13)&7)
					cellIdx := (ty / 8) + (tx/8)*cellsPerSide
					dotIdx := num<<8 | cellIdx<<6 | (ty&7)<<3 | (tx & 7)
					b := wr[(dotIdx>>1)&0x3FFFF]
					if dotIdx&1 != 0 {
						pix = b & 0x0F
					} else {
						pix = b >> 4
					}
				}
			}
			// Priority mode write of the fetched pixel (or 0)
			// into the image buffer nibble.
			bi := (idx >> 1) & 0x3FFFF
			old := wr[bi]
			if idx&1 != 0 {
				wr[bi] = old&0xF0 | asicPrioNibble(pm, old&0x0F, pix)
			} else {
				wr[bi] = asicPrioNibble(pm, old>>4, pix)<<4 | old&0x0F
			}
			if idx&7 != 7 {
				idx++
			} else {
				idx += colStride
			}
			x += dx
			y += dy
		}
		bufIdx += 8
	}
	a.imgVDots = 0
}

// serializeState writes ASICStateSize bytes into buf.
func (a *asicState) serializeState(buf []byte) {
	buf[0] = a.stampCtl
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(buf[1:3], a.stampMap)
	buf[3] = a.imgVCell
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(buf[4:6], a.imgStart)
	buf[6] = a.imgOffset
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(buf[7:9], a.imgHDots)
	buf[9] = a.imgVDots
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(buf[10:12], a.traceBase)
	buf[12] = 0
	if a.pending {
		buf[12] = 1
	}
}

// deserializeState restores state written by serializeState.
func (a *asicState) deserializeState(buf []byte) {
	a.stampCtl = buf[0]
	a.stampMap = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(buf[1:3])
	a.imgVCell = buf[3]
	a.imgStart = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(buf[4:6])
	a.imgOffset = buf[6]
	a.imgHDots = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(buf[7:9])
	a.imgVDots = buf[9]
	a.traceBase = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(buf[10:12])
	a.pending = buf[12]&1 != 0
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/scd/asic_test.go ====================

package scd

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SCD-3 unit gates: the graphics ASIC. Every gate compares exact
// image buffer bytes against expectations derived from the
// documented trace table, stamp, and buffer cell layout rules,
// never from the renderer itself.
//
// Fixture layout in Word RAM (byte offsets):
//
//	0x0000  stamp data (stamp 1 at byte 128, stamp 4 at byte 512)
//	0x1000  stamp map
//	0x2000  trace table
//	0x4000  image buffer
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const (
	asicTestMapBase   = 0x1000
	asicTestTraceBase = 0x2000
	asicTestBufBase   = 0x4000
)

// asicSetReg writes one ASIC register word through the sub CPU
// register page.
func asicSetReg(u *Unit, off uint32, v uint16) { u.Write16(0xFF8000+off, v) }

// asicGetReg reads one ASIC register word through the sub CPU
// register page.
func asicGetReg(u *Unit, off uint32) uint16 { return u.Read16(0xFF8000 + off) }

// fillStamp writes one stamp into Word RAM stamp data. num is the
// stamp number (256 dots per number), size is 16 or 32, and pix
// gives the pixel at stamp coordinate (x, y). Cells are stored
// column by column: cell index = (y/8) + (x/8) * (size/8).
func fillStamp(wr []byte, num, size int, pix func(x, y int) uint8) {
	cps := size / 8
	for y := 0; y < size; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < size; x++ {
			cell := (y / 8) + (x/8)*cps
			dot := num*256 + cell*64 + (y%8)*8 + (x % 8)
			v := pix(x, y) & 0x0F
			if dot%2 == 0 {
				wr[dot/2] = wr[dot/2]&0x0F | v<<4
			} else {
				wr[dot/2] = wr[dot/2]&0xF0 | v
			}
		}
	}
}

// setMapEntry writes one stamp map entry (row major words).
func setMapEntry(wr []byte, base, idx int, entry uint16) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(wr[base+idx*2:], entry)
}

// setTrace writes one trace table entry: start X and Y in 13.3
// fixed point, delta X and Y as raw signed 5.11 words.
func setTrace(wr []byte, base, line int, sx, sy, dx, dy uint16) {
	o := base + line*8
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(wr[o:], sx)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(wr[o+2:], sy)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(wr[o+4:], dx)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(wr[o+6:], dy)
}

// expectBufBytes packs a raster image of w by h pixels into the
// image buffer cell layout for a buffer whose columns are
// cellsPerCol cells high.
func expectBufBytes(w, h, cellsPerCol int, pix func(x, y int) uint8) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, (w/8)*cellsPerCol*32)
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			dot := (x/8)*cellsPerCol*64 + (y/8)*64 + (y%8)*8 + (x % 8)
			v := pix(x, y) & 0x0F
			if dot%2 == 0 {
				out[dot/2] |= v << 4
			} else {
				out[dot/2] |= v
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// programASIC writes the register block for the fixture layout
// and triggers the draw with the trace base write.
func programASIC(u *Unit, ctl, vcell, offset uint8, hdot uint16, vdot uint8) {
	asicSetReg(u, 0x58, uint16(ctl))
	asicSetReg(u, 0x5A, asicTestMapBase/4)
	asicSetReg(u, 0x5C, uint16(vcell))
	asicSetReg(u, 0x5E, asicTestBufBase/4)
	asicSetReg(u, 0x60, uint16(offset))
	asicSetReg(u, 0x62, hdot)
	asicSetReg(u, 0x64, uint16(vdot))
	asicSetReg(u, 0x66, asicTestTraceBase/4) // trigger
}

// pat16 is the 16x16 test pattern: every pixel nonzero and every
// coordinate identifiable.
func pat16(x, y int) uint8 { return uint8((x+y*16)%15 + 1) }

// pat32 is the 32x32 test pattern.
func pat32(x, y int) uint8 { return uint8((x+y*32)%15 + 1) }

// identityTrace fills the trace table for a straight copy of a
// size by size stamp area at the map origin.
func identityTrace(wr []byte, lines int) {
	for l := 0; l < lines; l++ {
		setTrace(wr, asicTestTraceBase, l, 0, uint16(l<<3), 0x0800, 0)
	}
}

func TestASICIdentityTrace(t *testing.T) {
	u := NewUnit(nil)
	wr := u.WordRAM()
	fillStamp(wr, 1, 16, pat16)
	setMapEntry(wr, asicTestMapBase, 0, 1)
	identityTrace(wr, 16)

	programASIC(u, 0x00, 1, 0, 16, 16)

	// For a 16x16 buffer two cells high, the buffer cell layout
	// and the stamp cell layout coincide, so the buffer bytes
	// must equal the stamp bytes exactly.
	got := wr[asicTestBufBase : asicTestBufBase+128]
	want := wr[128:256]
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("identity buffer differs from stamp bytes:\n got %x\nwant %x", got, want)
	}
	if u.ASICBusy() {
		t.Fatal("ASIC still busy after a synchronous draw")
	}
	if got := u.ASICLinesRemaining(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("lines remaining = %d, want 0 after the draw", got)
	}
	if got := asicGetReg(u, 0x58); got&0x8000 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("GRON reads set after the draw: %#06x", got)
	}
}

func TestASICRotationTrace(t *testing.T) {
	u := NewUnit(nil)
	wr := u.WordRAM()
	fillStamp(wr, 1, 16, pat16)
	setMapEntry(wr, asicTestMapBase, 0, 1)
	// Quarter turn: each output line starts one stamp dot to the
	// left of the previous line's start (line step (-1, 0)) and
	// walks down the stamp (dot delta (0, +1)).
	for l := 0; l < 16; l++ {
		setTrace(wr, asicTestTraceBase, l, uint16((15-l)<<3), 0, 0, 0x0800)
	}

	programASIC(u, 0x00, 1, 0, 16, 16)

	want := expectBufBytes(16, 16, 2, func(x, y int) uint8 {
		return pat16(15-y, x)
	})
	got := wr[asicTestBufBase : asicTestBufBase+len(want)]
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("rotated buffer mismatch:\n got %x\nwant %x", got, want)
	}
}

	}

	}

func TestASICRepeatWrapAndClip(t *testing.T) {
	setup := func(u *Unit) {
		wr := u.WordRAM()
		fillStamp(wr, 1, 16, pat16)
		for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
			setMapEntry(wr, asicTestMapBase, i, 1)
		}
		// Lines start at stamp space x = 250, six dots from the
		// 256 dot map edge, and walk 16 dots.
		for l := 0; l < 16; l++ {
			setTrace(wr, asicTestTraceBase, l, 250<<3, uint16(l<<3), 0x0800, 0)
		}
	}

	// Repeat on: the position wraps at the map edge.
	u := NewUnit(nil)
	setup(u)
	programASIC(u, 0x01, 1, 0, 16, 16)
	want := expectBufBytes(16, 16, 2, func(x, y int) uint8 {
		return pat16((250+x)%16, y)
	})
	if got := u.WordRAM()[asicTestBufBase : asicTestBufBase+len(want)]; !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("repeat wrap buffer mismatch:\n got %x\nwant %x", got, want)
	}

	// Repeat off, overwrite priority: out-of-map dots fetch
	// pixel 0 and leave the sentinel nibbles untouched.
	u2 := NewUnit(nil)
	setup(u2)
	for i := asicTestBufBase; i < asicTestBufBase+128; i++ {
		u2.WordRAM()[i] = 0xEE
	}
	u2.Write8(0xFF8003, 0x10) // priority mode 2 (overwrite)
	programASIC(u2, 0x00, 1, 0, 16, 16)
	want2 := expectBufBytes(16, 16, 2, func(x, y int) uint8 {
		if x < 6 {
			return pat16(10+x, y)
		}
		return 0x0E // sentinel nibble survives
	})
	if got := u2.WordRAM()[asicTestBufBase : asicTestBufBase+len(want2)]; !bytes.Equal(got, want2) {
		t.Fatalf("repeat off buffer mismatch:\n got %x\nwant %x", got, want2)
	}
}

func TestASICPriorityModes(t *testing.T) {
	// Stamp: left half transparent (0), right half nonzero.
	halfZero := func(x, y int) uint8 {
		if x < 8 {
			return 0
		}
		return uint8((x+y)%15 + 1)
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		pm      uint8
		prefill byte
		pix     func(x, y int) uint8
	}{
		{"overwrite skips zeros", 2, 0x33, func(x, y int) uint8 {
			if x < 8 {
				return 3
			}
			return halfZero(x, y)
		}},
		{"normal writes zeros", 0, 0x33, func(x, y int) uint8 {
			return halfZero(x, y)
		}},
		{"underwrite keeps nonzero buffer", 1, 0x44, func(x, y int) uint8 {
			return 4
		}},
		{"prohibited writes nothing", 3, 0x33, func(x, y int) uint8 {
			return 3
		}},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			u := NewUnit(nil)
			wr := u.WordRAM()
			fillStamp(wr, 1, 16, halfZero)
			setMapEntry(wr, asicTestMapBase, 0, 1)
			identityTrace(wr, 16)
			for i := asicTestBufBase; i < asicTestBufBase+128; i++ {
				wr[i] = tc.prefill
			}
			u.Write8(0xFF8003, tc.pm<<3) // priority mode field
			programASIC(u, 0x00, 1, 0, 16, 16)
			want := expectBufBytes(16, 16, 2, tc.pix)
			got := wr[asicTestBufBase : asicTestBufBase+len(want)]
			if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
				t.Fatalf("buffer mismatch:\n got %x\nwant %x", got, want)
			}
		})
	}
}
