// cddMeasureFreq plays a track and measures the rendered left
// channel frequency by positive going zero crossings over one
// second of rendered output.
func cddMeasureFreq(t *testing.T, c *CDD, trackStartLBA int) float64 {
	t.Helper()
	renderMark := trackStartLBA * 588
	var left []int32
	for len(left) < 44100 {
		c.AdvanceCycles(166667)
		now := cddPosTotal(c)
		n := now - renderMark
		if n <= 0 {
			continue
		}
		buf := make([]int32, n*2)
		c.RenderCDDA(buf)
		renderMark = now
		for i := 0; i < n && len(left) < 44100; i++ {
			left = append(left, buf[i*2])
		}
	}
	crossings := 0
	for i := 1; i < len(left); i++ {
		if left[i-1] < 0 && left[i] >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
	}
	return float64(crossings) * 44100.0 / float64(len(left))
}

func TestCDDDAFrequency(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	c := NewCDD(disc)
	cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 10))
	f440 := cddMeasureFreq(t, c, 10)
	t.Logf("measured track 2 frequency: %.2f Hz", f440)
	if f440 < 440*0.98 || f440 > 440*1.02 {
		t.Errorf("track 2 frequency = %.2f Hz, want 440 within 2 percent", f440)
	}
	cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 160))
	f880 := cddMeasureFreq(t, c, 160)
	t.Logf("measured track 3 frequency: %.2f Hz", f880)
	if f880 < 880*0.98 || f880 > 880*1.02 {
		t.Errorf("track 3 frequency = %.2f Hz, want 880 within 2 percent", f880)
	}
}

func cddRenderWindow(t *testing.T, disc *Disc, fd int) []int32 {
	t.Helper()
	c := NewCDD(disc)
	if fd != 1024 {
		word := fd << 4
		c.WriteFaderByte(0, byte(word>>8))
		c.WriteFaderByte(1, byte(word))
		if got := c.FaderFD(); got != fd {
			t.Fatalf("FaderFD = %d, want %d", got, fd)
		}
	}
	cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 10))
	c.AdvanceCycles(6250000)
	n := cddPosTotal(c) - 10*588
	buf := make([]int32, n*2)
	c.RenderCDDA(buf)
	return buf
}

func TestCDDFader(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	full := cddRenderWindow(t, disc, 1024)
	half := cddRenderWindow(t, disc, 512)
	if len(full) != len(half) {
		t.Fatalf("render lengths differ: %d vs %d", len(full), len(half))
	}
	peak := func(buf []int32) int64 {
		var p int64
		for i := 0; i < len(buf); i += 2 {
			v := int64(buf[i])
			if v < 0 {
				v = -v
			}
			if v > p {
				p = v
			}
		}
		return p
	}
	pf, ph := peak(full), peak(half)
	ratio := float64(ph) / float64(pf)
	t.Logf("fader peaks: FD1024 %d, FD512 %d, ratio %.4f", pf, ph, ratio)
	if ratio < 0.475 || ratio > 0.525 {
		t.Errorf("fader ratio = %.4f, want 0.5 within 5 percent", ratio)
	}
	zero := cddRenderWindow(t, disc, 0)
	for i, v := range zero {
		if v != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("FD 0 render nonzero at %d: %d", i, v)
		}
	}
}

func TestCDDTrackEndAdvance(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	c := NewCDD(disc)
	cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 159))
	// The delivery tick inside cddDeliver already advanced one
	// sector of playback, so the remaining advance is 2 seconds
	// of cycles minus that one tick.
	c.AdvanceCycles(25000000 - 166667)
	if c.State() != CDDPlaying {
		t.Errorf("state after crossing into track 3 = %v, want playing", c.State())
	}
	if got := c.PositionLBA(); got < 160 || got >= 310 {
		t.Errorf("position after crossing = LBA %d, want inside track 3", got)
	}

	c2 := NewCDD(disc)
	cddDeliver(t, c2, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 309))
	c2.AdvanceCycles(25000000)
	if c2.State() != CDDStopped || c2.DisplayStatus() != 0x09 {
		t.Errorf("past disc end: state %v display %#x, want stopped 0x09", c2.State(), c2.DisplayStatus())
	}
}

func TestCDDFastForward(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	c := NewCDD(disc)
	cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 10))
	p := cddDeliver(t, c, cddSimpleCommand(0x08))
	if p[0] != 0x03 || c.State() != CDDScanFF {
		t.Errorf("FF packet RS0 %#x state %v, want 0x03 scanning forward", p[0], c.State())
	}
	scanBuf := make([]int32, 200)
	c.RenderCDDA(scanBuf)
	for i, v := range scanBuf {
		if v != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("render during scan nonzero at %d: %d", i, v)
		}
	}
	before := cddPosTotal(c)
	c.AdvanceCycles(3125000)
	delta := cddPosTotal(c) - before
	t.Logf("FF position delta over 0.25 s of cycles: %d samples (want about 88200)", delta)
	if delta < 88200-1176 || delta > 88200+1176 {
		t.Errorf("FF delta = %d samples, want 88200 within 2 sectors", delta)
	}
	// Play returns to normal playback.
	p = cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, c.PositionLBA()))
	if p[0] != 0x01 || c.State() != CDDPlaying {
		t.Errorf("play after FF: RS0 %#x state %v, want 0x01 playing", p[0], c.State())
	}
}

func TestCDDDataReadEvents(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	c := NewCDD(disc)
	nib := cddMSFCommand(0x03, 2)
	cddWriteRaw(c, nib, cddChecksum(nib))
	var got []int
	for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
		ev := c.AdvanceCycles(166667)
		if ev.DataCount > 0 {
			for k := 0; k < ev.DataCount; k++ {
				got = append(got, ev.DataLBA+k)
			}
		}
		if i >= 2 && len(got) >= 3 && got[0] == 2 && got[1] == 3 && got[2] == 4 {
			// First three events verified; keep draining to the
			// end of track 1 below.
		}
		if c.State() == CDDStopped && len(got) > 0 {
			break
		}
	}
	want := []int{2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9}
	if len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("data read events = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	for i := range want {
		if got[i] != want[i] {
			t.Fatalf("data read events = %v, want %v", got, want)
		}
	}
	if c.State() != CDDStopped {
		t.Errorf("state after reading to track end = %v, want stopped", c.State())
	}
	ev := c.AdvanceCycles(166667)
	if ev.DataCount != 0 || ev.DataLBA != -1 {
		t.Errorf("event after read stop = %+v, want none", ev)
	}
}

func TestCDDOpenCloseTray(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	c := NewCDD(disc)
	p := cddDeliver(t, c, cddSimpleCommand(0x0D))
	if p[0] != 0x05 || c.State() != CDDTrayOpen {
		t.Errorf("open: RS0 %#x state %v, want 0x05 tray open", p[0], c.State())
	}
	p = cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 10))
	if c.State() != CDDTrayOpen {
		t.Errorf("play while open changed state to %v", c.State())
	}
	if p[0] != 0x05 {
		t.Errorf("play while open RS0 = %#x, want 0x05", p[0])
	}
	p = cddDeliver(t, c, cddSimpleCommand(0x0C))
	if p[0] != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("close packet RS0 = %#x, want 0x00", p[0])
	}
	if c.State() != CDDStopped || c.DisplayStatus() != 0x09 {
		t.Errorf("after close tick: state %v display %#x, want stopped 0x09", c.State(), c.DisplayStatus())
	}
	p = cddDeliver(t, c, cddSimpleCommand(0x00))
	if p[0] != 0x09 {
		t.Errorf("get status after close RS0 = %#x, want 0x09", p[0])
	}
}

func TestCDDOutOfRangePlay(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	c := NewCDD(disc)
	cddDeliver(t, c, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 400))
	if c.State() != CDDStopped || c.PositionLBA() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("out of range play: state %v LBA %d, want stopped at 0", c.State(), c.PositionLBA())
	}
	// Seconds field 75: invalid MSF.
	nib := [9]uint8{0, 3, 0, 0, 7, 5, 0, 0, 0}
	cddDeliver(t, c, nib)
	if c.State() != CDDStopped || c.PositionLBA() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("invalid seconds play: state %v LBA %d, want stopped at 0", c.State(), c.PositionLBA())
	}
	// A nibble over 9: also invalid BCD.
	nib = [9]uint8{0, 3, 0, 0, 1, 0x0A, 0, 0, 0}
	cddDeliver(t, c, nib)
	if c.State() != CDDStopped {
		t.Errorf("invalid BCD play changed state to %v", c.State())
	}
}

func TestCDDSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	disc, _ := buildCDDFixture(t)
	if CDDStateSize > 56 {
		t.Fatalf("CDDStateSize = %d, want at most 56", CDDStateSize)
	}
	c1 := NewCDD(disc)
	cddDeliver(t, c1, cddMSFCommand(0x03, 10))
	c1.AdvanceCycles(6250000)
	buf := make([]byte, CDDStateSize)
	c1.SerializeState(buf)

	c2 := NewCDD(disc)
	c2.DeserializeState(buf)

	renderBoth := func() ([]int32, []int32) {
		n := cddPosTotal(c1) - 10*588
		b1 := make([]int32, n*2)
		b2 := make([]int32, n*2)
		c1.RenderCDDA(b1)
		c2.RenderCDDA(b2)
		return b1, b2
	}
	c1.AdvanceCycles(6250000)
	c2.AdvanceCycles(6250000)
	b1, b2 := renderBoth()
	if !bytes.Equal(int32Bytes(b1), int32Bytes(b2)) {
		t.Error("rendered buffers differ after serialize round trip")
	}
	if cddPosTotal(c1) != cddPosTotal(c2) {
		t.Errorf("positions differ: %d vs %d", cddPosTotal(c1), cddPosTotal(c2))
	}
	buf1 := make([]byte, CDDStateSize)
	buf2 := make([]byte, CDDStateSize)
	c1.SerializeState(buf1)
	c2.SerializeState(buf2)
	if !bytes.Equal(buf1, buf2) {
		t.Error("re-serialized bytes differ after round trip")
	}
}

func int32Bytes(v []int32) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, len(v)*4)
	for i, x := range v {
		u := uint32(x)
		out[i*4] = byte(u)
		out[i*4+1] = byte(u >> 8)
		out[i*4+2] = byte(u >> 16)
		out[i*4+3] = byte(u >> 24)
	}
	return out
}

func TestCDDReadAudio(t *testing.T) {
	disc, bin := buildCDDFixture(t)
	got, err := disc.ReadAudio(20)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadAudio(20): %v", err)
	}
	if len(got) != 2352 {
		t.Fatalf("ReadAudio(20) len = %d, want 2352", len(got))
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, bin[20*2352:21*2352]) {
		t.Error("ReadAudio(20) does not match the fixture sector bytes")
	}
	if _, err := disc.ReadAudio(310); err == nil {
		t.Error("ReadAudio(310) succeeded, want out of range error")
	}
	if _, err := disc.ReadAudio(-1); err == nil {
		t.Error("ReadAudio(-1) succeeded, want out of range error")
	}

	dir := t.TempDir()
	isoPath := writeTestFile(t, dir, "plain.iso", make([]byte, 4*2048))
	iso := openAndClose(t, isoPath)
	if _, err := iso.ReadAudio(0); err == nil {
		t.Error("ReadAudio on a 2048 byte sector disc succeeded, want error")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/scd/disc.go ====================

// Package scd provides the Sega CD block layer for the Genesis core.
//
// This file covers disc images: it opens user supplied .cue/.bin and
// .iso images, parses cue sheets, and serves 2048 byte user data
// sectors to the CDC model. Only the Go standard library is used.
package scd

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// TrackMode identifies the layout of one track on a disc image.
type TrackMode int

const (
	// TrackMode1_2048 is a Mode 1 data track stored as bare 2048 byte
	// sectors with no sync, header, or error correction bytes.
	TrackMode1_2048 TrackMode = iota
	// TrackMode1_2352 is a Mode 1 data track stored as raw 2352 byte
	// sectors. User data lives at bytes [16:2064] of each sector.
	TrackMode1_2352
	// TrackMode2_2352 is a Mode 2 data track stored as raw 2352 byte
	// sectors. User data lives at bytes [24:2072] of each sector.
	TrackMode2_2352
	// TrackAudio is a Red Book audio track stored as raw 2352 byte
	// sectors. It carries no file system user data.
	TrackAudio
)

// sectorSize returns the on disc byte size of one sector in this mode.
func (m TrackMode) sectorSize() int {
	switch m {
	case TrackMode1_2048:
		return 2048
	case TrackMode1_2352, TrackMode2_2352, TrackAudio:
		return 2352
	default:
		return 0
	}
}

// Track describes one track of a disc image.
type Track struct {
	Number     int       // track number as written in the cue sheet, starting at 1
	Mode       TrackMode // sector layout for this track
	StartLBA   int       // first logical block address of the track
	Sectors    int       // number of sectors in the track
	FileIndex  int       // index into the disc file list that holds this track
	FileOffset int64     // byte offset of the track first sector within its file
	SectorSize int       // bytes per raw sector in the backing file
}

// Disc is an opened disc image. It keeps one file handle open per
// backing file until Close is called.
type Disc struct {
	tracks []Track
	files  []*os.File
	closed bool
}

// MSFToLBA converts a minutes, seconds, frames position to a logical
// block address. There are 75 frames per second and the first data
// sector sits at 00:02:00, which is LBA 0, hence the 150 frame offset.
func MSFToLBA(m, s, f int) int {
	return ((m*60)+s)*75 + f - 150
}

// LBAToMSF converts a logical block address back to a minutes,
// seconds, frames position. It is the inverse of MSFToLBA.
func LBAToMSF(lba int) (m, s, f int) {
	total := lba + 150
	f = total % 75
	total /= 75
	s = total % 60
	m = total / 60
	return m, s, f
}

// OpenDisc opens a disc image at path. The format is chosen from the
// file extension, case insensitively: .cue for a cue sheet with one or
// more binary image files, .iso for a bare MODE1/2048 image, and .bin
// for a bare MODE1/2352 image.
func OpenDisc(path string) (*Disc, error) {
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".iso":
		return openSingleFile(path, TrackMode1_2048)
	case ".bin":
		return openSingleFile(path, TrackMode1_2352)
	case ".cue":
		return openCue(path)
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: unsupported disc image extension %q", filepath.Ext(path))
	}
}

// openSingleFile opens an image that holds exactly one data track and
// no cue sheet. It backs both the .iso and the direct .bin cases.
func openSingleFile(path string, mode TrackMode) (*Disc, error) {
	sectorSize := mode.sectorSize()
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: open disc image: %w", err)
	}
	info, err := f.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		f.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: stat disc image %q: %w", path, err)
	}
	size := info.Size()
	if size == 0 {
		f.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: disc image %q is empty", path)
	}
	if size%int64(sectorSize) != 0 {
		f.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: disc image %q size %d is not a multiple of sector size %d", path, size, sectorSize)
	}
	track := Track{
		Number:     1,
		Mode:       mode,
		StartLBA:   0,
		Sectors:    int(size / int64(sectorSize)),
		FileIndex:  0,
		FileOffset: 0,
		SectorSize: sectorSize,
	}
	return &Disc{tracks: []Track{track}, files: []*os.File{f}}, nil
}

// openCue parses the cue sheet at path, opens every image file it
// names, and derives each track byte offset and sector count.
//
// Simplification: tracks are taken in cue sheet order. A track sector
// count comes from the start of the next track in the same file when
// there is one, otherwise it runs to the end of its own file. A cue
// sheet that spreads one logical track across several files is not
// supported, which matches how Sega CD images are normally shipped.
func openCue(path string) (*Disc, error) {
	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: read cue sheet: %w", err)
	}
	dir := filepath.Dir(path)

	var fileNames []string
	var tracks []Track
	currentTrack := -1

	for lineNo, line := range strings.Split(string(raw), "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		fields := strings.Fields(line)
		keyword := strings.ToUpper(fields[0])
		switch keyword {
		case "FILE":
			name, fileType, err := parseCueFileLine(line)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: %w", lineNo+1, err)
			}
			if !strings.EqualFold(fileType, "BINARY") {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: unsupported file type %q, only BINARY is supported", lineNo+1, fileType)
			}
			if !filepath.IsAbs(name) {
				name = filepath.Join(dir, name)
			}
			fileNames = append(fileNames, name)
		case "TRACK":
			if len(fileNames) == 0 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: TRACK appears before any FILE", lineNo+1)
			}
			if len(fields) < 3 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: malformed TRACK line %q", lineNo+1, line)
			}
			number, err := strconv.Atoi(fields[1])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: bad track number %q", lineNo+1, fields[1])
			}
			mode, err := parseCueTrackMode(fields[2])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: %w", lineNo+1, err)
			}
			tracks = append(tracks, Track{
				Number:     number,
				Mode:       mode,
				StartLBA:   -1,
				FileIndex:  len(fileNames) - 1,
				SectorSize: mode.sectorSize(),
			})
			currentTrack = len(tracks) - 1
		case "INDEX":
			if len(fields) < 3 || fields[1] != "01" {
				// INDEX 00 and any other index points do not set the
				// track start, so they are ignored here.
				continue
			}
			if currentTrack < 0 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: INDEX appears before any TRACK", lineNo+1)
			}
			m, s, fr, err := parseMSF(fields[2])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue line %d: %w", lineNo+1, err)
			}
			tracks[currentTrack].StartLBA = MSFToLBA(m, s, fr)
		default:
			// REM, PREGAP, FLAGS, CATALOG, and every other cue sheet
			// line carry nothing the block layer needs, so they are
			// ignored by design.
			continue
		}
	}

	if len(fileNames) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue sheet %q names no image file", path)
	}
	if len(tracks) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue sheet %q has an empty track list", path)
	}
	for i := range tracks {
		if tracks[i].StartLBA < 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue sheet %q track %d has no INDEX 01", path, tracks[i].Number)
		}
	}

	files := make([]*os.File, 0, len(fileNames))
	fileSizes := make([]int64, 0, len(fileNames))
	closeFiles := func() {
		for _, f := range files {
			f.Close()
		}
	}
	for _, name := range fileNames {
		f, err := os.Open(name)
		if err != nil {
			closeFiles()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: open cue image file %q: %w", name, err)
		}
		info, err := f.Stat()
		if err != nil {
			f.Close()
			closeFiles()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: stat cue image file %q: %w", name, err)
		}
		files = append(files, f)
		fileSizes = append(fileSizes, info.Size())
	}

	// Byte offsets accumulate within each file: a track starts where
	// the previous track in the same file ended, measured in that
	// previous track sector size.
	for i := range tracks {
		prev := previousTrackInFile(tracks, i)
		if prev < 0 {
			tracks[i].FileOffset = 0
			continue
		}
		gap := tracks[i].StartLBA - tracks[prev].StartLBA
		tracks[i].FileOffset = tracks[prev].FileOffset + int64(gap)*int64(tracks[prev].SectorSize)
	}
	for i := range tracks {
		next := nextTrackInFile(tracks, i)
		if next >= 0 {
			tracks[i].Sectors = tracks[next].StartLBA - tracks[i].StartLBA
			continue
		}
		remaining := fileSizes[tracks[i].FileIndex] - tracks[i].FileOffset
		tracks[i].Sectors = int(remaining / int64(tracks[i].SectorSize))
	}
	for i := range tracks {
		if tracks[i].Sectors <= 0 {
			closeFiles()
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: cue sheet %q track %d has no sectors in its image file", path, tracks[i].Number)
		}
	}

	return &Disc{tracks: tracks, files: files}, nil
}

// previousTrackInFile returns the index of the closest track before i
// that lives in the same file as track i, or -1 when there is none.
func previousTrackInFile(tracks []Track, i int) int {
	for j := i - 1; j >= 0; j-- {
		if tracks[j].FileIndex == tracks[i].FileIndex {
			return j
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// nextTrackInFile returns the index of the closest track after i that
// lives in the same file as track i, or -1 when there is none.
func nextTrackInFile(tracks []Track, i int) int {
	for j := i + 1; j < len(tracks); j++ {
		if tracks[j].FileIndex == tracks[i].FileIndex {
			return j
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// parseCueFileLine splits a FILE line into its image name and its
// file type. The name may be quoted, in which case it can contain
// spaces, or it may be a single bare token.
func parseCueFileLine(line string) (name, fileType string, err error) {
	rest := strings.TrimSpace(line[len(strings.Fields(line)[0]):])
	if rest == "" {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("malformed FILE line %q", line)
	}
	if rest[0] == '"' {
		end := strings.Index(rest[1:], `"`)
		if end < 0 {
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("unterminated quoted file name in FILE line %q", line)
		}
		name = rest[1 : 1+end]
		rest = strings.TrimSpace(rest[1+end+1:])
	} else {
		parts := strings.Fields(rest)
		name = parts[0]
		rest = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(rest, name))
	}
	typeFields := strings.Fields(rest)
	if len(typeFields) == 0 {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("FILE line %q has no file type", line)
	}
	return name, typeFields[0], nil
}

// parseCueTrackMode maps a cue sheet track mode token to a TrackMode.
func parseCueTrackMode(token string) (TrackMode, error) {
	switch strings.ToUpper(token) {
	case "MODE1/2048":
		return TrackMode1_2048, nil
	case "MODE1/2352":
		return TrackMode1_2352, nil
	case "MODE2/2352":
		return TrackMode2_2352, nil
	case "AUDIO":
		return TrackAudio, nil
	default:
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("unsupported track mode %q", token)
	}
}

// parseMSF parses an mm:ss:ff cue sheet timestamp.
func parseMSF(text string) (m, s, f int, err error) {
	parts := strings.Split(text, ":")
	if len(parts) != 3 {
		return 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("bad MSF timestamp %q", text)
	}
	values := make([]int, 3)
	for i, part := range parts {
		value, convErr := strconv.Atoi(part)
		if convErr != nil {
			return 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("bad MSF timestamp %q", text)
		}
		values[i] = value
	}
	return values[0], values[1], values[2], nil
}

// Close closes every backing file handle. It is idempotent: calling
// it more than once returns nil after the first call.
func (d *Disc) Close() error {
	if d == nil || d.closed {
		return nil
	}
	d.closed = true
	var firstErr error
	for _, f := range d.files {
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil && firstErr == nil {
			firstErr = err
		}
	}
	return firstErr
}

// NumSectors returns the total number of sectors across all tracks.
func (d *Disc) NumSectors() int {
	total := 0
	for _, track := range d.tracks {
		total += track.Sectors
	}
	return total
}

// Tracks returns a copy of the track list, so callers cannot mutate
// the state the disc reads through.
func (d *Disc) Tracks() []Track {
	out := make([]Track, len(d.tracks))
	copy(out, d.tracks)
	return out
}

// DataTracks returns the number of non audio tracks on the disc.
func (d *Disc) DataTracks() int {
	count := 0
	for _, track := range d.tracks {
		if track.Mode != TrackAudio {
			count++
		}
	}
	return count
}

// ReadData returns exactly 2048 bytes of user data for the sector at
// lba. Audio sectors and out of range addresses return an error. The
// returned slice is freshly allocated on every call.
func (d *Disc) ReadData(lba int) ([]byte, error) {
	if d == nil || d.closed {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: ReadData on a closed disc")
	}
	track := d.trackForLBA(lba)
	if track == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: LBA %d is out of range, disc has %d sectors", lba, d.NumSectors())
	}
	if track.Mode == TrackAudio {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: LBA %d is in audio track %d, audio tracks have no user data", lba, track.Number)
	}
	offset := track.FileOffset + int64(lba-track.StartLBA)*int64(track.SectorSize)
	raw := make([]byte, track.SectorSize)
	if _, err := d.files[track.FileIndex].ReadAt(raw, offset); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: read sector at LBA %d: %w", lba, err)
	}
	out := make([]byte, 2048)
	switch track.Mode {
	case TrackMode1_2048:
		copy(out, raw)
	case TrackMode1_2352:
		copy(out, raw[16:2064])
	case TrackMode2_2352:
		copy(out, raw[24:2072])
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: track %d has unsupported mode %d", track.Number, track.Mode)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// ReadAudio returns a freshly allocated 2352 byte raw sector for
// the sector at lba. It serves any track whose sector size is 2352,
// audio or data. Tracks stored as 2048 byte sectors and out of
// range addresses return an error.
func (d *Disc) ReadAudio(lba int) ([]byte, error) {
	if d == nil || d.closed {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: ReadAudio on a closed disc")
	}
	track := d.trackForLBA(lba)
	if track == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: LBA %d is out of range, disc has %d sectors", lba, d.NumSectors())
	}
	if track.SectorSize != 2352 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: LBA %d is in track %d with sector size %d, want 2352", lba, track.Number, track.SectorSize)
	}
	offset := track.FileOffset + int64(lba-track.StartLBA)*int64(track.SectorSize)
	out := make([]byte, 2352)
	if _, err := d.files[track.FileIndex].ReadAt(out, offset); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("scd: read audio sector at LBA %d: %w", lba, err)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// trackForLBA finds the track that owns lba, or nil when no track does.
func (d *Disc) trackForLBA(lba int) *Track {
	for i := range d.tracks {
		track := &d.tracks[i]
		if lba >= track.StartLBA && lba < track.StartLBA+track.Sectors {
			return track
		}
	}
	return nil
}

package scd

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// writeTestFile writes data to dir/name and returns the full path.
func writeTestFile(t *testing.T, dir, name string, data []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, name)
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", name, err)
	}
	return path
}

// fillSector returns one raw sector of the given size where the user
// data window [userStart:userStart+2048] is filled with value and
// every other byte is junk, so a read that lands on the wrong window
// cannot accidentally pass.
func fillSector(size, userStart int, value byte) []byte {
	sector := make([]byte, size)
	for i := range sector {
		sector[i] = 0xEE
	}
	// Twelve sync style bytes and a short header pattern sit in front
	// of the user data on raw sector layouts.
	for i := 0; i < userStart && i < size; i++ {
		sector[i] = byte(i)
	}
	for i := userStart; i < userStart+2048 && i < size; i++ {
		sector[i] = value
	}
	return sector
}

// buildRawBin assembles a bin image from per sector fill values using
// fillSector for each sector.
func buildRawBin(sectorSize, userStart int, values []byte) []byte {
	var bin []byte
	for _, value := range values {
		bin = append(bin, fillSector(sectorSize, userStart, value)...)
	}
	return bin
}

// wantUserData builds the expected 2048 byte block filled with value.
func wantUserData(value byte) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 2048)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = value
	}
	return out
}

// openAndClose opens a disc and registers its Close with Cleanup.
func openAndClose(t *testing.T, path string) *Disc {
	t.Helper()
	disc, err := OpenDisc(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenDisc(%s): %v", path, err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		if err := disc.Close(); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("Close: %v", err)
		}
	})
	return disc
}

func TestMSFLBARoundTrips(t *testing.T) {
	if got := MSFToLBA(0, 2, 0); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("MSFToLBA(0, 2, 0) = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	m, s, f := LBAToMSF(0)
	if m != 0 || s != 2 || f != 0 {
		t.Errorf("LBAToMSF(0) = %02d:%02d:%02d, want 00:02:00", m, s, f)
	}

	// A mid disc position: 12 minutes, 34 seconds, 56 frames.
	const wantLBA = ((12*60)+34)*75 + 56 - 150
	if got := MSFToLBA(12, 34, 56); got != wantLBA {
		t.Errorf("MSFToLBA(12, 34, 56) = %d, want %d", got, wantLBA)
	}
	m, s, f = LBAToMSF(wantLBA)
	if m != 12 || s != 34 || f != 56 {
		t.Errorf("LBAToMSF(%d) = %02d:%02d:%02d, want 12:34:56", wantLBA, m, s, f)
	}

	for _, lba := range []int{0, 1, 74, 75, 449, 450, 12345, 269999} {
		m, s, f := LBAToMSF(lba)
		if got := MSFToLBA(m, s, f); got != lba {
			t.Errorf("round trip LBA %d gave %d via %02d:%02d:%02d", lba, got, m, s, f)
		}
	}
}

func TestOpenISO(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	data := make([]byte, 8*2048)
	for sector := 0; sector < 8; sector++ {
		for i := 0; i < 2048; i++ {
			data[sector*2048+i] = byte(sector)
		}
	}
	copy(data, "SEGA CD TEST MARKER")
	path := writeTestFile(t, dir, "game.iso", data)

	disc := openAndClose(t, path)
	if got := disc.NumSectors(); got != 8 {
		t.Errorf("NumSectors = %d, want 8", got)
	}
	tracks := disc.Tracks()
	if len(tracks) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("len(Tracks) = %d, want 1", len(tracks))
	}
	track := tracks[0]
	if track.Mode != TrackMode1_2048 || track.SectorSize != 2048 || track.Sectors != 8 || track.StartLBA != 0 {
		t.Errorf("track = %+v, want MODE1/2048 with 8 sectors of 2048 bytes at LBA 0", track)
	}
	if got := disc.DataTracks(); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("DataTracks = %d, want 1", got)
	}

	sector0, err := disc.ReadData(0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadData(0): %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.HasPrefix(sector0, []byte("SEGA CD TEST MARKER")) {
		t.Errorf("ReadData(0) lost the sector 0 marker, starts with %q", sector0[:19])
	}

	sector3, err := disc.ReadData(3)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadData(3): %v", err)
	}
	if len(sector3) != 2048 {
		t.Fatalf("len(ReadData(3)) = %d, want 2048", len(sector3))
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(sector3, wantUserData(3)) {
		t.Errorf("ReadData(3) is not 2048 bytes of value 3")
	}

	if _, err := disc.ReadData(8); err == nil {
		t.Error("ReadData(8) succeeded, want an out of range error")
	}
	if _, err := disc.ReadData(-1); err == nil {
		t.Error("ReadData(-1) succeeded, want an out of range error")
	}
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/scd/pcm.go ====================

package scd

// This file implements the Ricoh RF5C164 PCM engine of the Sega CD.
//
// The facts below come from the Ricoh RF5C68A datasheet summary and
// from the PCM chapter of the Mega CD hardware manual, as reproduced
// in public documentation.
//
// The chip plays eight channels from a shared 64 KB wave RAM and
// produces one mixed stereo output sample every 384 sub CPU clocks.
// The sub CPU clock is 12,500,000 Hz, so the native output rate is
// 12,500,000 / 384 = 32552.08 Hz.
//
// Wave RAM samples are 8 bit sign-magnitude values. Bit 7 is the
// sign (1 means positive and 0 means negative) and bits 6 to 0 are
// the magnitude, from 0 to 127. The byte 0xFF is not a sample at
// all: when a channel fetch reads 0xFF the channel jumps to its loop
// start address and fetches again there. If the byte at the loop
// start is also 0xFF the channel outputs silence for that tick.
// Because 0xFF is the loop marker, a positive 127 is not a legal
// sample, while a negative 127 (0x7F) is legal.
//
// This model does sample-and-hold resampling to 44,100 Hz in
// RenderFrame. The real chip does no interpolation, so a held native
// sample is repeated until the next chip tick produces a new one.
// The exact ratio accumulator keeps the long term rate exact.
//
// The datasheet restricts CPU access to wave RAM while the chip is
// sounding. That restriction is not modeled here: CPU wave RAM
// access through the bank window is unrestricted in the Unit, and
// this engine only reports the selected bank through WaveBank.

import "encoding/binary"

// PCMStateSize is the exact serialized size of a PCM engine, in
// bytes. The layout is 11 bytes per channel for the eight channels
// (88 bytes, channel major, in the field order ENV, PAN, FD low,
// FD high, loop start low, loop start high, start, and the four
// address counter bytes in big-endian order), followed by 19 global
// bytes: CTRL, the selected channel, the wave bank, the on and off
// byte, the seven mirror bytes for register offsets 9 to 15, the
// four resample accumulator bytes in big-endian order, and the held
// left and right outputs as big-endian signed words.
const PCMStateSize = 8*11 + 19

// Chip timing and output constants.
const (
	pcmSubClockHz   = 12500000 // sub CPU clock, in Hz
	pcmClocksPerOut = 384      // sub CPU clocks per native output sample
	pcmOutputHz     = 44100    // RenderFrame output rate, in Hz
)

// pcmChannel holds the register and playback state of one of the
// eight RF5C164 channels. The current sample byte is not part of the
// serialized state: it is refetched from wave RAM on restore, using
// the same loop marker rule as a normal fetch.
type pcmChannel struct {
	env  uint8  // offset 0x00: constant gain, called envelope in the manual
	pan  uint8  // offset 0x01: bits 7 to 4 left gain, bits 3 to 0 right gain
	fd   uint16 // offsets 0x02 and 0x03: 5.11 fixed point phase increment
	ls   uint16 // offsets 0x04 and 0x05: loop start address
	st   uint8  // offset 0x06: start address high byte, start is st << 8
	addr uint32 // 27 bit phase counter: 16 integer bits and 11 fraction bits
	cur  uint8  // current fetched sample byte, or 0 for a double loop marker
}

// PCM is the RF5C164 engine. It borrows the caller owned 64 KB wave
// RAM slice and keeps every other piece of state internally.
type PCM struct {
	wave     []byte
	channels [8]pcmChannel

	ctrl       uint8    // offset 0x07 raw byte: bit 7 master on, bit 6 MOD
	curChannel int      // channel selected by the last MOD 1 CTRL write
	waveBank   int      // wave bank selected by the last MOD 0 CTRL write
	onOff      uint8    // offset 0x08: bit i enables channel i
	mirror     [7]uint8 // offsets 0x09 to 0x0F: store and read back only

	resampleAccum uint32 // exact ratio accumulator for RenderFrame
	holdL         int16  // held mixed left output of the last chip tick
	holdR         int16  // held mixed right output of the last chip tick
}

// NewPCM builds an engine over wave, which the caller owns and which
// is expected to be the 64 KB wave RAM. The slice reference is kept,
// so caller writes to wave RAM are heard by the engine. Power-on
// state is all zero: the chip master is off, channel 0 is selected,
// wave bank 0 is selected, and no channel is enabled.
func NewPCM(wave []byte) *PCM {
	return &PCM{wave: wave}
}

// waveAt reads one wave RAM byte. Indexes outside the slice read as
// zero, which keeps a short or missing wave RAM silent instead of
// faulting. A full engine always runs over the full 64 KB.
func (p *PCM) waveAt(idx int) uint8 {
	if idx < 0 || idx >= len(p.wave) {
		return 0
	}
	return p.wave[idx]
}

// fetchCurrent refetches the current sample of ch from the wave RAM
// position its address counter points at. A 0xFF byte is the loop
// marker: the counter jumps to the loop start address and the fetch
// repeats there. A second 0xFF at the loop start means the current
// sample is silence, stored as zero, which decodes to a magnitude of
// zero on either sign.
func (p *PCM) fetchCurrent(ch *pcmChannel) {
	idx := int(ch.addr >> 11)
	b := p.waveAt(idx)
	if b != 0xFF {
		ch.cur = b
		return
	}
	ch.addr = uint32(ch.ls) << 11
	b = p.waveAt(int(ch.ls))
	if b == 0xFF {
		ch.cur = 0
		return
	}
	ch.cur = b
}

// holdAtStart parks ch at its start address, which is where an
// inactive channel counter constantly sits. The current sample is
// refreshed from the start position so a channel that turns on later
// starts from the start sample, but the loop marker jump is not
// applied here: the counter itself must stay at the start address
// for as long as the channel is inactive. A marker byte at the start
// position reads as silence.
func (p *PCM) holdAtStart(ch *pcmChannel) {
	ch.addr = uint32(ch.st) << 19
	b := p.waveAt(int(ch.st) << 8)
	if b == 0xFF {
		ch.cur = 0
		return
	}
	ch.cur = b
}

// masterOn reports whether the chip master bit (CTRL bit 7) is set.
func (p *PCM) masterOn() bool { return p.ctrl&0x80 != 0 }

// WriteReg writes one byte of the register page at offset off, which
// ranges from 0x00 to 0x0F. Offsets 0x00 to 0x06 write the currently
// selected channel. Offset 0x07 is CTRL, offset 0x08 is the channel
// on and off byte, and offsets 0x09 to 0x0F are mirror bytes that are
// stored and read back with no other effect. Offsets outside the
// page are ignored.
func (p *PCM) WriteReg(off uint8, v uint8) {
	switch {
	case off <= 0x06:
		ch := &p.channels[p.curChannel]
		switch off {
		case 0x00:
			ch.env = v
		case 0x01:
			ch.pan = v
		case 0x02:
			ch.fd = ch.fd&0xFF00 | uint16(v)
		case 0x03:
			ch.fd = ch.fd&0x00FF | uint16(v)<<8
		case 0x04:
			ch.ls = ch.ls&0xFF00 | uint16(v)
		case 0x05:
			ch.ls = ch.ls&0x00FF | uint16(v)<<8
		case 0x06:
			// Writing the start register reloads the address
			// counter and refetches the current sample at once,
			// whether or not the channel is currently on. This
			// is the channel retrigger.
			ch.st = v
			ch.addr = uint32(v) << 19
			p.fetchCurrent(ch)
		}
	case off == 0x07:
		p.ctrl = v
		if v&0x40 != 0 {
			// MOD 1: bits 2 to 0 select the current channel.
			// The wave bank selection is left untouched.
			p.curChannel = int(v & 0x07)
		} else {
			// MOD 0: bits 3 to 0 select the wave RAM bank shown
			// in the CPU window. The channel selection is left
			// untouched.
			p.waveBank = int(v & 0x0F)
		}
	case off == 0x08:
		p.onOff = v
	case off >= 0x09 && off <= 0x0F:
		p.mirror[off-0x09] = v
	}
}

// ReadReg reads one byte of the register page at offset off.
// Offsets 0x00 to 0x06 return the currently selected channel values,
// offset 0x07 returns the raw CTRL byte, offset 0x08 returns the on
// and off byte, and offsets 0x09 to 0x0F return the mirror bytes.
// Offsets outside the page read as zero.
func (p *PCM) ReadReg(off uint8) uint8 {
	switch {
	case off <= 0x06:
		ch := &p.channels[p.curChannel]
		switch off {
		case 0x00:
			return ch.env
		case 0x01:
			return ch.pan
		case 0x02:
			return uint8(ch.fd)
		case 0x03:
			return uint8(ch.fd >> 8)
		case 0x04:
			return uint8(ch.ls)
		case 0x05:
			return uint8(ch.ls >> 8)
		case 0x06:
			return ch.st
		}
	case off == 0x07:
		return p.ctrl
	case off == 0x08:
		return p.onOff
	case off >= 0x09 && off <= 0x0F:
		return p.mirror[off-0x09]
	}
	return 0
}

// WaveBank returns the wave RAM bank, from 0 to 15, that the CPU
// window currently shows. It is set by MOD 0 CTRL writes and is 0 at
// power-on.
func (p *PCM) WaveBank() int { return p.waveBank }

// Selected returns the currently selected channel, from 0 to 7. It is
// set by MOD 1 CTRL writes and is 0 at power-on.
func (p *PCM) Selected() int { return p.curChannel }

// OnOff returns the channel on and off byte: bit i enables channel i.
func (p *PCM) OnOff() uint8 { return p.onOff }

// Ctrl returns the raw CTRL byte last written to offset 0x07.
func (p *PCM) Ctrl() uint8 { return p.ctrl }

// ChannelAddr returns the 27 bit address counter of channel ch, or
// zero when ch is out of range. The sample index into wave RAM is
// the counter shifted right by 11.
func (p *PCM) ChannelAddr(ch int) uint32 {
	if ch < 0 || ch >= len(p.channels) {
		return 0
	}
	return p.channels[ch].addr & 0x7FFFFFF
}

// ChannelSample returns the current fetched sample byte of channel
// ch, or zero when ch is out of range. A channel whose fetch found
// the loop marker twice in a row reports zero, for silence.
func (p *PCM) ChannelSample(ch int) uint8 {
	if ch < 0 || ch >= len(p.channels) {
		return 0
	}
	return p.channels[ch].cur
}

// Tick advances the engine by one chip tick and recomputes the held
// mixed output. With the chip master off the held output is zero, no
// channel advances, and every channel counter is parked at its start
// address, because the master off state makes every channel
// inactive. With the master on, an enabled channel advances its
// address counter by its FD increment, wraps in 27 bits, and
// refetches its current sample with the loop marker rule. A disabled
// channel is parked at its start address and contributes nothing.
func (p *PCM) Tick() {
	if !p.masterOn() {
		for i := range p.channels {
			p.holdAtStart(&p.channels[i])
		}
		p.holdL = 0
		p.holdR = 0
		return
	}
	var sumL, sumR int
	for i := range p.channels {
		ch := &p.channels[i]
		if p.onOff&(1<<uint(i)) == 0 {
			p.holdAtStart(ch)
			continue
		}
		ch.addr = (ch.addr + uint32(ch.fd)) & 0x7FFFFFF
		p.fetchCurrent(ch)
		mag := int(ch.cur & 0x7F)
		if mag == 0 {
			continue
		}
		sign := 1
		if ch.cur&0x80 == 0 {
			sign = -1
		}
		env := int(ch.env)
		sumL += sign * ((mag * env * int(ch.pan>>4)) >> 5)
		sumR += sign * ((mag * env * int(ch.pan&0x0F)) >> 5)
	}
	p.holdL = clampInt16(sumL)
	p.holdR = clampInt16(sumR)
}

// clampInt16 clamps v to the signed 16 bit range.
func clampInt16(v int) int16 {
	if v > 32767 {
		return 32767
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return -32768
	}
	return int16(v)
}

// RenderFrame returns one stereo output frame at 44,100 Hz. The
// exact ratio accumulator adds the sub CPU clock rate on every call
// and runs one chip tick for every 384 times 44,100 accumulated
// units, so the long term tick rate is exactly the native chip rate
// and no drift builds up. The returned sample is the held output of
// the most recent chip tick, repeated unchanged between ticks,
// because the chip itself does no interpolation.
func (p *PCM) RenderFrame() (l, r int16) {
	p.resampleAccum += pcmSubClockHz
	for p.resampleAccum >= pcmClocksPerOut*pcmOutputHz {
		p.resampleAccum -= pcmClocksPerOut * pcmOutputHz
		p.Tick()
	}
	return p.holdL, p.holdR
}

// SerializeState writes exactly PCMStateSize bytes into buf, in the
// layout documented on PCMStateSize. The caller supplies a buffer of
// at least that size.
func (p *PCM) SerializeState(buf []byte) {
	off := 0
	for i := range p.channels {
		ch := &p.channels[i]
		buf[off+0] = ch.env
		buf[off+1] = ch.pan
		buf[off+2] = uint8(ch.fd)
		buf[off+3] = uint8(ch.fd >> 8)
		buf[off+4] = uint8(ch.ls)
		buf[off+5] = uint8(ch.ls >> 8)
		buf[off+6] = ch.st
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(buf[off+7:off+11], ch.addr&0x7FFFFFF)
		off += 11
	}
	buf[off+0] = p.ctrl
	buf[off+1] = uint8(p.curChannel)
	buf[off+2] = uint8(p.waveBank)
	buf[off+3] = p.onOff
	copy(buf[off+4:off+11], p.mirror[:])
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(buf[off+11:off+15], p.resampleAccum)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(buf[off+15:off+17], uint16(p.holdL))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(buf[off+17:off+19], uint16(p.holdR))
}

// DeserializeState restores state written by SerializeState. After
// the registers and counters are restored, every channel current
// sample is refetched from wave RAM with the same loop marker rule a
// normal fetch uses, so a restored engine renders identically to the
// engine that was serialized.
func (p *PCM) DeserializeState(buf []byte) {
	off := 0
	for i := range p.channels {
		ch := &p.channels[i]
		ch.env = buf[off+0]
		ch.pan = buf[off+1]
		ch.fd = uint16(buf[off+2]) | uint16(buf[off+3])<<8
		ch.ls = uint16(buf[off+4]) | uint16(buf[off+5])<<8
		ch.st = buf[off+6]
		ch.addr = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(buf[off+7:off+11]) & 0x7FFFFFF
		off += 11
	}
	p.ctrl = buf[off+0]
	p.curChannel = int(buf[off+1]) & 0x07
	p.waveBank = int(buf[off+2]) & 0x0F
	p.onOff = buf[off+3]
	copy(p.mirror[:], buf[off+4:off+11])
	p.resampleAccum = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(buf[off+11 : off+15])
	p.holdL = int16(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(buf[off+15 : off+17]))
	p.holdR = int16(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(buf[off+17 : off+19]))
	for i := range p.channels {
		p.fetchCurrent(&p.channels[i])
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/scd/pcm_test.go ====================

package scd

import (
	"bytes"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// pcmSelectChannel selects ch through a MOD 1 CTRL write with the
// chip master on, which is the normal way test setups change the
// current channel.
func pcmSelectChannel(p *PCM, ch int) {
	p.WriteReg(0x07, 0xC0|uint8(ch))
}

// pcmSetupChannel programs the currently selected channel with the
// given register values. The loop start is written before the start
// register, because the start write retriggers the channel and its
// refetch can use the loop start.
func pcmSetupChannel(p *PCM, env, pan uint8, fd, ls uint16, st uint8) {
	p.WriteReg(0x00, env)
	p.WriteReg(0x01, pan)
	p.WriteReg(0x02, uint8(fd))
	p.WriteReg(0x03, uint8(fd>>8))
	p.WriteReg(0x04, uint8(ls))
	p.WriteReg(0x05, uint8(ls>>8))
	p.WriteReg(0x06, st)
}

// signMag encodes v as a sign-magnitude wave byte. Positive values
// clamp to 126 because a positive 127 would be the 0xFF loop marker.
func signMag(v int) uint8 {
	if v > 126 {
		v = 126
	}
	if v < -127 {
		v = -127
	}
	if v >= 0 {
		return 0x80 | uint8(v)
	}
	return uint8(-v)
}

func TestPCMFrequency(t *testing.T) {
	wave := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		v := int(math.Round(126 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/256)))
		wave[i] = signMag(v)
	}
	for i := 256; i < 288; i++ {
		wave[i] = 0xFF
	}
	p := NewPCM(wave)
	pcmSelectChannel(p, 0)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 255, 0xFF, 0x0800, 0, 0)
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x01)

	crossings := 0
	prevSign := 0
	for i := 0; i < 44100; i++ {
		l, _ := p.RenderFrame()
		sign := 0
		if l > 0 {
			sign = 1
		} else if l < 0 {
			sign = -1
		}
		if sign != 0 {
			if prevSign != 0 && sign != prevSign {
				crossings++
			}
			prevSign = sign
		}
	}
	// 44,100 frames at 44,100 Hz is exactly one second, and a sine
	// crosses zero twice per period, so half the crossing count is
	// the measured frequency in Hz.
	measured := float64(crossings) / 2
	want := 32552.08 / 256
	t.Logf("measured frequency %.2f Hz from %d zero crossings, want %.2f Hz", measured, crossings, want)
	if math.Abs(measured-want) > 0.03*want {
		t.Fatalf("measured frequency %.2f Hz, want %.2f Hz within 3 percent", measured, want)
	}
}

func TestPCMLoopWrap(t *testing.T) {
	wave := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	for i := 0; i < 128; i++ {
		wave[i] = 0x80 | 100 // positive constant, magnitude 100
	}
	for i := 128; i < 256; i++ {
		wave[i] = 100 // negative constant, magnitude 100
	}
	wave[256] = 0xFF
	p := NewPCM(wave)
	pcmSelectChannel(p, 0)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 255, 0xFF, 0x0800, 128, 0)
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x01)

	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		p.Tick()
	}
	if got := p.ChannelSample(0); got != 0x80|100 {
		t.Fatalf("sample before the loop region = %#02x, want %#02x", got, 0x80|100)
	}
	for i := 10; i < 255; i++ {
		p.Tick()
	}
	if got := p.ChannelAddr(0) >> 11; got != 255 {
		t.Fatalf("sample index after 255 ticks = %d, want 255", got)
	}
	p.Tick() // tick 256 fetches the marker at 256 and jumps to 128
	if got := p.ChannelAddr(0) >> 11; got != 128 {
		t.Fatalf("sample index at the wrap tick = %d, want 128 (the loop start)", got)
	}
	if got := p.ChannelSample(0); got != 100 {
		t.Fatalf("sample after wrapping = %#02x, want %#02x (the negative constant)", got, 100)
	}
}

func TestPCMTwoChannelsSum(t *testing.T) {
	wave := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	wave[0] = 0xFE // positive 126
	p := NewPCM(wave)
	pcmSelectChannel(p, 0)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 128, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0)
	pcmSelectChannel(p, 1)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 128, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0)

	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x01)
	p.Tick()
	singleL, singleR := p.RenderFrame()
	// One channel contributes (126 * 128 * 15) >> 5 = 7560 per side.
	if singleL != 7560 || singleR != 7560 {
		t.Fatalf("single channel output = %d, %d, want 7560, 7560", singleL, singleR)
	}
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x03)
	p.Tick()
	doubleL, doubleR := p.RenderFrame()
	// Exact equality holds here: both channels produce the identical
	// per channel term, and the documented truncation is applied per
	// channel before the sum, so the two channel sum is exactly
	// twice the single channel value with no rounding difference.
	if doubleL != 2*singleL || doubleR != 2*singleR {
		t.Fatalf("two channel output = %d, %d, want exactly twice %d, %d", doubleL, doubleR, singleL, singleR)
	}
}

func TestPCMPanFullLeft(t *testing.T) {
	wave := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	wave[0] = 0xFE
	p := NewPCM(wave)
	pcmSelectChannel(p, 0)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 255, 0xF0, 0, 0, 0)
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x01)

	nonzeroLeft := 0
	for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
		l, r := p.RenderFrame()
		if r != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("frame %d: right output = %d, want exactly 0 with full left pan", i, r)
		}
		if l != 0 {
			nonzeroLeft++
		}
	}
	if nonzeroLeft == 0 {
		t.Fatal("left output was never nonzero with full left pan")
	}
}

func TestPCMStartRetrigger(t *testing.T) {
	wave := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	p := NewPCM(wave)
	pcmSelectChannel(p, 0)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 255, 0xFF, 0x0800, 0, 2)
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x01)

	start := uint32(2) << 19
	if got := p.ChannelAddr(0); got != start {
		t.Fatalf("address after the start write = %d, want %d", got, start)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		p.Tick()
	}
	if got := p.ChannelAddr(0); got != start+5*0x0800 {
		t.Fatalf("address after 5 ticks = %d, want %d", got, start+5*0x0800)
	}
	p.WriteReg(0x06, 2) // write the start register again: retrigger
	if got := p.ChannelAddr(0); got != start {
		t.Fatalf("address after the start rewrite = %d, want %d", got, start)
	}
}

func TestPCMOffSilences(t *testing.T) {
	wave := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	wave[0] = 0xFE
	p := NewPCM(wave)
	pcmSelectChannel(p, 0)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 255, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0)

	// Channel off: the on and off bit for channel 0 stays clear.
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x00)
	for i := 0; i < 50; i++ {
		if l, r := p.RenderFrame(); l != 0 || r != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("channel off, frame %d: output = %d, %d, want 0, 0", i, l, r)
		}
	}
	// Chip master off: the channel is enabled but CTRL bit 7 is
	// clear. A MOD 1 CTRL write with bit 7 clear selects channel 0
	// and keeps the master off.
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x01)
	p.WriteReg(0x07, 0x40)
	for i := 0; i < 50; i++ {
		if l, r := p.RenderFrame(); l != 0 || r != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("master off, frame %d: output = %d, %d, want 0, 0", i, l, r)
		}
	}
}

	pcmSelectChannel(p, 0)
	pcmSetupChannel(p, 255, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0)
	p.WriteReg(0x08, 0x01)
