package scd

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k"
)

// makeISO builds a two sector temp .iso for tests: sector 0 is a
// Sega CD style header sector carrying the SEGADISCSYSTEM
// signature at offset 0, the IP start LBA (1) at offset 0x30 and
// the IP size at offset 0x34, and sector 1 is the IP padded to
// 2048 bytes. It returns the image path.
func makeISO(t *testing.T, ip []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	img := make([]byte, 2*2048)
	copy(img[0:], "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0x30:], 1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0x34:], uint32(len(ip)))
	copy(img[2048:], ip)
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "test.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, img, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write ISO: %v", err)
	}
	return path
}

// openISO opens a disc for a test and closes it at test end.
func openISO(t *testing.T, ip []byte) *Disc {
	t.Helper()
	d, err := OpenDisc(makeISO(t, ip))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenDisc: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { d.Close() })
	return d
}

// pollCDC reads the sub CPU CDC status register until the
// transfer complete bit sets, and returns the final status byte.
func pollCDC(t *testing.T, u *Unit) uint8 {
	t.Helper()
	var st uint8
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		st = u.Read8(0xFF8037)
		if st&0x02 != 0 {
			return st
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("CDC transfer never completed, last status %#04x", st)
	return st
}

func TestGateArrayCommAndFlags(t *testing.T) {
	u := NewUnit(nil)

	// Comm command 3 = 0xCAFE, written by the main CPU one byte
	// lane at a time (offset 0x16 = high byte, 0x17 = low byte).
	u.MainWrite8(0x16, 0xCA)
	u.MainWrite8(0x17, 0xFE)
	if got := u.CommCommand(3); got != 0xCAFE {
		t.Fatalf("CommCommand(3) = %#06x, want 0xCAFE", got)
	}
	if got := u.Read8(0xFF8016); got != 0xCA {
		t.Fatalf("sub read of comm command 3 high byte = %#04x, want 0xCA", got)
	}
	if got := u.Read8(0xFF8017); got != 0xFE {
		t.Fatalf("sub read of comm command 3 low byte = %#04x, want 0xFE", got)
	}

	// Comm status 5 and the sub flag are written by the sub CPU
	// and read back by the main CPU.
	u.Write8(0xFF802A, 0x12)
	u.Write8(0xFF802B, 0x34)
	if got := u.CommStatus(5); got != 0x1234 {
		t.Fatalf("CommStatus(5) = %#06x, want 0x1234", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainRead8(0x2A); got != 0x12 {
		t.Fatalf("main read of comm status 5 high byte = %#04x, want 0x12", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainRead8(0x2B); got != 0x34 {
		t.Fatalf("main read of comm status 5 low byte = %#04x, want 0x34", got)
	}
	u.Write8(0xFF800F, 0x5A)
	if got := u.SubFlag(); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("SubFlag() = %#04x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainRead8(0x0F); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("main read of sub flag = %#04x, want 0x5A", got)
	}

	// The main flag is written by the main CPU and read by the sub.
	u.MainWrite8(0x0E, 0xA5)
	if got := u.MainFlag(); got != 0xA5 {
		t.Fatalf("MainFlag() = %#04x, want 0xA5", got)
	}
	if got := u.Read8(0xFF800E); got != 0xA5 {
		t.Fatalf("sub read of main flag = %#04x, want 0xA5", got)
	}

	// Write protection: the sub CPU cannot write the main flag,
	// the main CPU cannot write the sub flag, the comm status
	// words, or the CD block offsets at or above 0x30.
	u.Write8(0xFF800E, 0x00)
	if got := u.MainFlag(); got != 0xA5 {
		t.Fatalf("sub write changed MainFlag to %#04x, want 0xA5", got)
	}
	u.MainWrite8(0x0F, 0x00)
	if got := u.SubFlag(); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("main write changed SubFlag to %#04x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
	u.MainWrite8(0x2A, 0xFF)
	if got := u.CommStatus(5); got != 0x1234 {
		t.Fatalf("main write changed CommStatus(5) to %#06x, want 0x1234", got)
	}
	u.Write8(0xFF8016, 0x00)
	if got := u.CommCommand(3); got != 0xCAFE {
		t.Fatalf("sub write changed CommCommand(3) to %#06x, want 0xCAFE", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainRead8(0x30); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("main read of offset 0x30 = %#04x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestWordRAMOwnership(t *testing.T) {
	u := NewUnit(nil)

	// Power-on: 2M mode, sub CPU owns Word RAM.
	if !u.WordOwnerSub() {
		t.Fatal("power-on Word RAM owner is not the sub CPU")
	}
	u.Write8(0x200000, 0x5A)
	if got := u.WordRAM()[0]; got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("WordRAM()[0] = %#04x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainWordRead8(0x200000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("main Word RAM read while sub owns = %#04x, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	u.MainWordWrite8(0x200000, 0x99)
	if got := u.WordRAM()[0]; got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("main Word RAM write while sub owns landed: %#04x", got)
	}

	// A non-owner DMNA write is ignored in 2M mode.
	u.MainWrite8(0x02, 0x02)
	if !u.WordOwnerSub() {
		t.Fatal("non-owner DMNA transferred Word RAM ownership")
	}

	// The owner gives: ownership flips to the main CPU and the
	// main side RET flag sets.
	u.Write8(0xFF8002, 0x02)
	if u.WordOwnerSub() {
		t.Fatal("owner DMNA did not transfer Word RAM ownership")
	}
	if got := u.MainWordRead8(0x200000); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("main Word RAM read after transfer = %#04x, want 0x5A", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainRead8(0x02); got&0x04 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("main read of 0x02 = %#04x, want RET bit set", got)
	}
	if got := u.Read8(0x200000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("sub Word RAM read while main owns = %#04x, want 0xFF", got)
	}

	// Switch to 1M with a combined MODE plus DMNA write from the
	// owner (main) side: mode becomes 1M and the halves swap, so
	// the sub CPU now owns the second 128 KB half.
	u.MainWrite8(0x02, 0x03)
	if got := u.MainRead8(0x02); got&0x01 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mode readback = %#04x, want 1M mode bit set", got)
	}
	u.Write8(0x200000, 0xA5) // sub half: physical 0x20000
	if got := u.WordRAM()[0x20000]; got != 0xA5 {
		t.Fatalf("WordRAM()[0x20000] = %#04x, want 0xA5 (sub 1M half)", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainWordRead8(0x200000); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("main 1M window read = %#04x, want its own half byte 0x5A", got)
	}
	u.MainWordWrite8(0x200000, 0x11) // main half: physical 0
	if got := u.WordRAM()[0]; got != 0x11 {
		t.Fatalf("WordRAM()[0] = %#04x, want 0x11 (main 1M half)", got)
	}

	// A 1M DMNA swap exchanges the halves: each side now sees the
	// byte the other side wrote.
	u.MainWrite8(0x02, 0x03)
	if got := u.MainWordRead8(0x200000); got != 0xA5 {
		t.Fatalf("main window after 1M swap = %#04x, want sub byte 0xA5", got)
	}
	if got := u.Read8(0x200000); got != 0x11 {
		t.Fatalf("sub window after 1M swap = %#04x, want main byte 0x11", got)
	}
}

func TestCDCPolledAndDMA(t *testing.T) {
	ip := []byte{0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04}
	disc := openISO(t, ip)
	u := NewUnit(disc)

	// DMA transfer of sector 1 (the IP) into PRG-RAM at sub
	// address 0x00030000, destination type PRG-RAM (DDT = 1).
	u.Write8(0xFF8003, 0x08)
	u.Write32(0xFF8038, 1)          // LBA latch
	u.Write32(0xFF803E, 0x00030000) // destination latch
	u.Write16(0xFF803C, 1)          // sector count
	u.Write8(0xFF8036, 0x01)        // start
	st := pollCDC(t, u)
	if st&0x08 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("CDC status %#04x has the error bit set", st)
	}
	base := 0x30000 - 0x20000
	for i, want := range ip {
		if got := u.PRGRAM()[base+i]; got != want {
			t.Fatalf("PRGRAM()[%#x] = %#04x, want IP byte %#04x", base+i, got, want)
		}
	}

	// Buffer-only transfer (DDT = 0) of sector 0, then stream it
	// out of the CDC data port.
	u.Write8(0xFF8003, 0x00)
	u.Write32(0xFF8038, 0)
	u.Write32(0xFF803E, 0)
	u.Write16(0xFF803C, 1)
	u.Write8(0xFF8036, 0x01)
	st = pollCDC(t, u)
	if st&0x04 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("CDC status %#04x does not report data ready", st)
	}
	got := make([]byte, 14)
	for i := range got {
		got[i] = u.Read8(0xFF8048)
	}
	if string(got) != "SEGADISCSYSTEM" {
		t.Fatalf("data port stream = %q, want SEGADISCSYSTEM", got)
	}
}

func TestBootStubBootsIP(t *testing.T) {
	// IP program: MOVE.W #0x600D, 0xFF8020.l (comm status 0),
	// then BRA . to idle. The absolute long encoding is 0x33FC
	// followed by the immediate word and the 32 bit address.
	ip := []byte{
		0x33, 0xFC, 0x60, 0x0D, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x20,
		0x60, 0xFE,
	}
	disc := openISO(t, ip)
	u := NewUnit(disc)
	cpu := m68k.New(u)

	// The reset one-shot does not report while RES = 0, and the
	// arm survives the early call.
	if u.TakeSubReset() {
		t.Fatal("TakeSubReset reported a reset before release")
	}
	if !u.SubHalted() {
		t.Fatal("sub CPU is not halted at power-on")
	}
	u.MainWrite8(0x00, 0x01) // RES = 1: release the sub CPU
	if u.SubHalted() {
		t.Fatal("sub CPU is still halted after RES = 1")
	}
	if !u.TakeSubReset() {
		t.Fatal("TakeSubReset did not report the release")
	}
	if u.TakeSubReset() {
		t.Fatal("TakeSubReset reported the same release twice")
	}

	cpu.Reset()
	for i := 0; i < 200 && u.SubFlag() != 1; i++ {
		cpu.StepCycles(1000)
	}
	if got := u.SubFlag(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("SubFlag() = %#04x, want 1 (boot OK) after boot stub run", got)
	}
	if got := u.CommStatus(0); got != 0x600D {
		t.Fatalf("CommStatus(0) = %#06x, want 0x600D written by the IP (the stub wrote 0xB007 first)", got)
	}
	if cpu.Halted() {
		t.Fatal("sub CPU halted during boot")
	}
}

func TestUnitSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	ip := []byte{0x10, 0x20, 0x30}
	disc := openISO(t, ip)
	u := NewUnit(disc)

	// Dirty every piece of serialized state.
	u.PRGRAM()[0] = 0xAA
	u.PRGRAM()[0x7FFFF] = 0xBB
	u.WordRAM()[0] = 0xCC
	u.WordRAM()[0x3FFFF] = 0xDD
	u.Write8(0xFF0003, 0x42) // PCM register
	u.Write8(0xFF1000, 0x77) // PCM wave RAM through its window
	u.MainWrite8(0x00, 0x01) // control: RES = 1
	u.MainWrite8(0x01, 0x24) // LED
	u.Write8(0xFF8002, 0x02) // DMNA: Word RAM to main, RET main
	u.Write8(0xFF8003, 0x08) // CDC destination PRG-RAM
	u.MainWrite8(0x04, 0x06) // H-INT interval
	u.MainWrite8(0x05, 0x00) // H-INT vector (autovector)
	u.MainWrite8(0x0E, 0xE0) // main flag
	u.Write8(0xFF800F, 0x0F) // sub flag
	u.MainWrite8(0x12, 0x12) // comm command 1 = 0x1234
	u.MainWrite8(0x13, 0x34)
	u.Write8(0xFF8024, 0xAB) // comm status 2 = 0xABCD
	u.Write8(0xFF8025, 0xCD)
	u.Write8(0xFF8030, 0x00) // CDD command, refreshes response
	u.Write8(0xFF8031, 0x99) // CDD parameter
	u.Write32(0xFF8038, 7)   // CDC LBA latch
	u.Write16(0xFF803C, 3)   // CDC count latch
	u.Write32(0xFF803E, 0x00026000)
	// Run one buffer transfer so the sector buffer, data pointer
	// and CDC state are all nonzero in the saved state.
	u.Write8(0xFF8003, 0x00)
	u.Write32(0xFF8038, 1)
	u.Write16(0xFF803C, 1)
	u.Write8(0xFF8036, 0x01)
	pollCDC(t, u)
	_ = u.Read8(0xFF8048) // advance the data port pointer
	_ = u.Read8(0xFF8048)

	buf1 := make([]byte, u.SerializeSize())
	if err := u.Serialize(buf1); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize: %v", err)
	}

	u2 := NewUnit(disc)
	if err := u2.Deserialize(buf1); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	buf2 := make([]byte, u2.SerializeSize())
	if err := u2.Serialize(buf2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("re-Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(buf1, buf2) {
		t.Fatal("serialize, deserialize, serialize did not round trip byte for byte")
	}
	if got := u2.CommStatus(2); got != 0xABCD {
		t.Fatalf("restored CommStatus(2) = %#06x, want 0xABCD", got)
	}
	if got := u2.SubFlag(); got != 0x0F {
		t.Fatalf("restored SubFlag() = %#04x, want 0x0F", got)
	}
}

func TestBootStubImageVectors(t *testing.T) {
	img := BootStubImage()
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(img[0:]); got != 0x000A0000 {
		t.Fatalf("boot stub SSP = %#010x, want 0x000A0000", got)
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(img[4:]); got != 0x00000200 {
		t.Fatalf("boot stub PC = %#010x, want 0x00000200", got)
	}
	if !bytes.Contains(img, []byte("SEGADISCSYSTEM")) {
		t.Fatal("boot stub image does not embed the SEGADISCSYSTEM signature")
	}

	rom := MainStubROM()
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(rom[4:]); got != 0x00000200 {
		t.Fatalf("main stub PC = %#010x, want 0x00000200", got)
	}
	if got := string(rom[0x100 : 0x100+4]); got != "SEGA" {
		t.Fatalf("main stub header at 0x100 = %q, want SEGA prefix", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/scd/stub.go ====================

package scd

import "encoding/binary"

// This file builds the two hand-written boot programs for the Sega
// CD unit. Neither contains any Sega BIOS code: both are original
// programs written for this core with the tiny two-pass 68000
// assembler below.
//
// Encoding note: the absolute destination forms of MOVE use the
// absolute long destination encodings 0x13FC (MOVE.B immediate),
// 0x33FC (MOVE.W immediate) and 0x33C0 (MOVE.W from Dn), followed
// by a full 32 bit address. The absolute short forms (0x11FC,
// 0x31FC, 0x31C0) sign extend a 16 bit address and cannot reach the
// main CPU gate array window at 0xA12000, and the IP test program
// in scd_test.go uses the matching absolute long form (0x33FC with
// a 32 bit address) for its comm status write. The repository
// system test documents the same encoding: 0x13FC is move.b #imm,
// addr.l, where the mode 7 destination register field 001 selects
// absolute long.

// Branch condition codes used by the assembler.
const (
	ccBRA = 0
	ccBNE = 6
	ccBEQ = 7
	ccBGT = 14
	ccBLE = 15
)

// asmFixup is one pending branch displacement word.
type asmFixup struct {
	pos   int    // buffer offset of the displacement word
	label string // target label name
}

// asm is a minimal two-pass 68000 assembler: a byte buffer, a
// label map and a fixup list. Label addresses and branch
// displacements use absolute addresses: the assembler is created
// with the address its first emitted byte will run at, and a
// branch displacement is target minus (address of the opcode word
// plus 2), stored as the word after the opcode word (the 16 bit
// displacement form, selected by a zero low byte in the opcode).
type asm struct {
	base   int
	buf    []byte
	labels map[string]int
	fixups []asmFixup
}

func newAsm(base int) *asm {
	return &asm{base: base, labels: make(map[string]int)}
}

// mark records the current position as a label.
func (a *asm) mark(name string) {
	a.labels[name] = a.base + len(a.buf)
}

// addr returns the absolute address a label will have, or 0 if it
// has not been marked yet. Callers that need a forward address
// assemble twice (measure, then rebuild with the known value).
func (a *asm) addr(name string) uint32 {
	return uint32(a.labels[name])
}

func (a *asm) emit16(v uint16) {
	a.buf = append(a.buf, byte(v>>8), byte(v))
}

func (a *asm) emit32(v uint32) {
	a.buf = append(a.buf, byte(v>>24), byte(v>>16), byte(v>>8), byte(v))
}

// finish resolves all branch fixups and returns the code bytes.
func (a *asm) finish() []byte {
	for _, f := range a.fixups {
		target, ok := a.labels[f.label]
		if !ok {
			panic("scd: assembler fixup to unknown label " + f.label)
		}
		// The displacement word sits at base+f.pos, which is also
		// the address of the opcode word plus 2.
		disp := target - (a.base + f.pos)
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(a.buf[f.pos:f.pos+2], uint16(int16(disp)))
	}
	return a.buf
}

// branch emits an opcode word with a zero low byte (16 bit
// displacement form) and records a fixup for the word after it.
func (a *asm) branchWord(opcode uint16, label string) {
	a.emit16(opcode)
	a.fixups = append(a.fixups, asmFixup{pos: len(a.buf), label: label})
	a.emit16(0)
}

func (a *asm) nop() { a.emit16(0x4E71) }
func (a *asm) rts() { a.emit16(0x4E75) }

func (a *asm) moveq(v int, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x7000 | uint16(dn)<<9 | uint16(v&0xFF))
}

func (a *asm) movelImm(v uint32, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x203C | uint16(dn)<<9)
	a.emit32(v)
}

func (a *asm) moveaImm(v uint32, an int) {
	a.emit16(0x207C | uint16(an)<<9)
	a.emit32(v)
}

func (a *asm) leaAbs(addr uint32, an int) {
	a.emit16(0x41F9 | uint16(an)<<9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

// movebImmToAbs emits MOVE.B #v, addr.l (absolute long form).
func (a *asm) movebImmToAbs(v uint8, addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x13FC)
	a.emit16(uint16(v))
	a.emit32(addr)
}

// movewImmToAbs emits MOVE.W #v, addr.l (absolute long form).
func (a *asm) movewImmToAbs(v uint16, addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x33FC)
	a.emit16(v)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *asm) movelDnToAbs(dn int, addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x23C0 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *asm) movelAbsToDn(addr uint32, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x2039 | uint16(dn)<<9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *asm) movebAbsToDn(addr uint32, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x1039 | uint16(dn)<<9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *asm) movebPostIncToDn(an int, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x1000 | uint16(dn)<<9 | 0x18 | uint16(an))
}

// cmpbDn emits CMP.B srcDn, dstDn (computes dst minus src).
func (a *asm) cmpbDn(srcDn int, dstDn int) {
	a.emit16(0xB000 | uint16(dstDn)<<9 | uint16(srcDn))
}

// btstDn emits BTST #bit, Dn (static bit number form).
func (a *asm) btstDn(bit int, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x0800 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit16(uint16(bit))
}

func (a *asm) tstL(dn int) { a.emit16(0x4A80 | uint16(dn)) }

func (a *asm) addqL(n int, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x5080 | uint16(n&7)<<9 | uint16(dn))
}

func (a *asm) addiL(v uint32, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x0680 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit32(v)
}

func (a *asm) subiL(v uint32, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x0480 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit32(v)
}

func (a *asm) branch(cond int, label string) {
	a.branchWord(0x6000|uint16(cond)<<8|0x00, label)
}

func (a *asm) bsr(label string) {
	a.branchWord(0x6100, label)
}

func (a *asm) dbra(dn int, label string) {
	a.branchWord(0x51C8|uint16(dn), label)
}

func (a *asm) jmpAbs(addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x4EF9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *asm) rte() { a.emit16(0x4E73) }

// movemRegToAbs emits MOVEM.L <mask>, addr.l (register to memory,
// absolute long destination): opcode 0x48F9, mask word, address.
func (a *asm) movemRegToAbs(mask uint16, addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x48F9)
	a.emit16(mask)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

// movemAbsToReg emits MOVEM.L addr.l, <mask> (memory to register,
// absolute long source): opcode 0x4CF9, mask word, address.
func (a *asm) movemAbsToReg(mask uint16, addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x4CF9)
	a.emit16(mask)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

// tstbAbs emits TST.B addr.l (absolute long): opcode 0x4A39.
func (a *asm) tstbAbs(addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x4A39)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

// moveToCCRFromAbs emits MOVE addr.l, CCR (absolute long source):
// opcode 0x44F9.
func (a *asm) moveToCCRFromAbs(addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x44F9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *asm) movewAbsToDn(addr uint32, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x3039 | uint16(dn)<<9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *asm) cmpiw(v uint16, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x0C40 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit16(v)
}

// cmpil emits CMPI.L #imm32, Dn.
func (a *asm) cmpil(v uint32, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x0C80 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit32(v)
}

func (a *asm) notw(dn int) { a.emit16(0x4640 | uint16(dn)) }

// movewDnToAbs emits MOVE.W Dn, addr.l (absolute long form).
func (a *asm) movewDnToAbs(dn int, addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x33C0 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit32(addr)
}

// bootStubCode assembles the sub CPU boot program. sigAddr is the
// absolute address of the embedded signature string; it is a
// parameter because the string sits right after the code, so its
// address depends on the code length. The code length does not
// depend on sigAddr, so callers assemble once with 0 to measure,
// then again with the true value.
func bootStubCode(sigAddr uint32) []byte {
	a := newAsm(0x200)

	a.mark("start")
	a.movebImmToAbs(0x08, 0xFF8003) // CDC destination = PRG-RAM, H-INT off
	a.moveq(0, 0)                   // D0 = LBA 0
	a.movelImm(0x00020400, 2)       // D2 = PRG-RAM scratch destination
	a.bsr("readsec")
	a.leaAbs(0x00020400, 0) // A0 = scratch (sector 0 image)
	a.leaAbs(sigAddr, 1)    // A1 = embedded signature
	a.moveq(13, 3)          // D3 = 14 bytes minus 1, for DBRA
	a.mark("chk")
	a.movebPostIncToDn(0, 0) // D0 = next scratch byte
	a.movebPostIncToDn(1, 1) // D1 = next signature byte
	a.cmpbDn(1, 0)
	a.branch(ccBNE, "fail")
	a.dbra(3, "chk")
	// Copy sector 0 into Word RAM offset 0, so the main program in
	// the boot sector user bytes from offset 0x200 onward lands at
	// main window address 0x200200. For DDT 2 the destination latch
	// is a Word RAM offset, not a bus address.
	a.movebImmToAbs(0x10, 0xFF8003) // CDC destination = Word RAM
	a.moveq(0, 0)                   // D0 = LBA 0
	a.moveq(0, 2)                   // D2 = Word RAM offset 0
	a.bsr("readsec")
	a.movebImmToAbs(0x08, 0xFF8003) // CDC destination = PRG-RAM again
	a.movelAbsToDn(0x00020430, 0)   // D0 = IP start LBA (header offset 0x30)
	a.movelAbsToDn(0x00020434, 4)   // D4 = IP size in bytes (offset 0x34)
	a.movelImm(0x00026000, 2)       // D2 = IP destination address
	a.mark("load")
	a.tstL(4)
	a.branch(ccBLE, "done")
	a.bsr("readsec")
	a.addqL(1, 0)     // next LBA
	a.addiL(0x800, 2) // next destination sector
	a.subiL(0x800, 4) // bytes remaining
	a.branch(ccBRA, "load")
	a.mark("done")
	a.movebImmToAbs(0x01, 0xFF800F)   // sub flag: boot OK
	a.movewImmToAbs(0xB007, 0xFF8020) // comm status 0: boot signature
	a.jmpAbs(0x00026000)              // enter the IP
	a.mark("fail")
	a.movebImmToAbs(0xEE, 0xFF800F) // sub flag: signature mismatch
	a.branch(ccBRA, "fail")
	a.mark("readsec")
	a.movelDnToAbs(0, 0xFF8038)       // CDC LBA latch = D0
	a.movelDnToAbs(2, 0xFF803E)       // CDC destination latch = D2
	a.movewImmToAbs(0x0001, 0xFF803C) // CDC sector count = 1
	a.movebImmToAbs(0x01, 0xFF8036)   // CDC control: start transfer
	a.mark("poll")
	a.movebAbsToDn(0xFF8037, 1) // D1 = CDC status
	a.btstDn(1, 1)              // test transfer complete bit
	a.branch(ccBEQ, "poll")
	a.rts()
	return a.finish()
}

// BIOS mailbox addresses in PRG-RAM (sub CPU absolute). The
// trampolines below save the caller register image here, and the
// Go BIOS services in bios.go read it and write the result block.
const (
	mbRequestAddr = 0x00025A00 // request byte: 0 idle, 1 pending
	mbFamilyAddr  = 0x00025A01 // family byte: 0 cdbios, 1 buram, 2 cdboot
	mbImageAddr   = 0x00025A04 // 15 longs: D0..D7, A0..A6
	mbResultAddr  = 0x00025A40 // 4 longs: D0, D1, A0, A1
	mbCCRAddr     = 0x00025A50 // result CCR word (low byte is the CCR)
)

// handlerStubCode assembles the BIOS handler block that lives
// right after the boot code and its signature string in the stub
// image: an RTE stub, an RTS stub, a fatal stub (sets the sub
// flag to 0xEE and spins, mirroring the boot fail path), and the
// three family trampolines for the jump table. A trampoline
// saves D0-D7/A0-A6 into the mailbox register image with MOVEM,
// stores its family byte, sets the request byte last, spins on
// the request byte until the Go service clears it, restores
// D0/D1/A0/A1 from the result block with MOVEM, loads the saved
// CCR word into CCR (MOVEM does not touch CCR, so the CCR load
// comes last), and returns. The block uses only relative branches
// and absolute mailbox addresses, so its bytes do not depend on
// where it is placed; base is still passed for label resolution.
// It returns the code and the absolute addresses of each stub.
func handlerStubCode(base int) (code []byte, rteAddr, rtsAddr, fatalAddr uint32, trampAddrs [3]uint32) {
	a := newAsm(base)
	a.mark("rte")
	a.rte()
	a.mark("rts")
	a.rts()
	a.mark("fatal")
	a.movebImmToAbs(0xEE, 0xFF800F) // sub flag: fatal stub entry
	a.branch(ccBRA, "fatal")
	spinNames := [3]string{"spin0", "spin1", "spin2"}
	trampNames := [3]string{"tramp0", "tramp1", "tramp2"}
	for fam := 0; fam < 3; fam++ {
		a.mark(trampNames[fam])
		a.movemRegToAbs(0x7FFF, mbImageAddr) // save D0-D7/A0-A6
		a.movebImmToAbs(uint8(fam), mbFamilyAddr)
		a.movebImmToAbs(0x01, mbRequestAddr) // request byte set last
		a.mark(spinNames[fam])
		a.tstbAbs(mbRequestAddr)
		a.branch(ccBNE, spinNames[fam])
		a.movemAbsToReg(0x0303, mbResultAddr) // restore D0/D1/A0/A1
		a.moveToCCRFromAbs(mbCCRAddr)
		a.rts()
	}
	code = a.finish()
	rteAddr = a.addr("rte")
	rtsAddr = a.addr("rts")
	fatalAddr = a.addr("fatal")
	for fam := 0; fam < 3; fam++ {
		trampAddrs[fam] = a.addr(trampNames[fam])
	}
	return code, rteAddr, rtsAddr, fatalAddr, trampAddrs
}

// JumpTableBase is the sub CPU address of the BIOS jump table in
// the stub image. The table holds 14 six byte JMP absolute long
// entries from 0x5EE0 to 0x5F33, and the RAM overlay window the
// Unit serves for it spans 0x5EE0 to 0x5F3F (jumpTableSize
// bytes). The _buram entry at 0x5F16 and the _cdbios entry at
// 0x5F22 are the documented hard addresses real software calls.
const JumpTableBase = 0x5EE0

const jumpTableSize = 0x60 // 96 bytes: 0x5EE0..0x5F3F

// BootStubImage builds the sub CPU boot stub image based at sub
// CPU address 0. The image is 0x6000 bytes: vectors at 0 (SSP =
// 0x000A0000, at the top of PRG-RAM) and 4 (PC = 0x00000200), an
// ASCII ID string at 0x100, the boot code at offset 0x200 with
// the 14 byte signature string SEGADISCSYSTEM embedded right
// after it, the BIOS handler block (RTE and RTS stubs, a fatal
// stub, and the three family trampolines) after the signature,
// and the BIOS jump table at 0x5EE0. Vectors 2..23 and 32..63
// point at the fatal stub, vector 24 (spurious) points at the
// RTE stub, and autovectors 25..31 point at the jump table
// level entries. Everything else is zero.
//
// The program is our own hand-written boot code, not a copy of
// any Sega BIOS: it programs the CDC for PRG-RAM destination,
// reads sector 0 into a PRG-RAM scratch page, verifies the
// SEGADISCSYSTEM signature from the sector against its embedded
// copy, copies sector 0 into Word RAM offset 0 with the CDC
// destination set to Word RAM and then restored to PRG-RAM,
// loads the IP (initial program) sectors named by the
// sector 0 header fields at offsets 0x30 (start LBA) and 0x34
// (size in bytes) to sub address 0x026000, sets the sub comm flag
// to 1 and comm status 0 to 0xB007, and jumps to the IP. On a
// signature mismatch it sets the sub flag to 0xEE and spins.
func BootStubImage() []byte {
	img := make([]byte, 0x6000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0:], 0x000A0000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[4:], 0x00000200)
	copy(img[0x100:], "iTaK CD BIOS")

	measure := bootStubCode(0)
	sigAddr := uint32(0x200 + len(measure))
	handlerBase := int(sigAddr) + len("SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	hcode, rteAddr, rtsAddr, fatalAddr, trampAddrs := handlerStubCode(handlerBase)

	putVec := func(n int, addr uint32) {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[n*4:], addr)
	}
	for v := 2; v <= 23; v++ {
		putVec(v, fatalAddr)
	}
	putVec(24, rteAddr) // spurious interrupt: just return
	levelEntries := [7]uint32{0x5EE0, 0x5EE6, 0x5EEC, 0x5EF2, 0x5EF8, 0x5EFE, 0x5F04}
	for i, entry := range levelEntries {
		putVec(25+i, entry) // autovectors 25..31: levels 1..7
	}
	for v := 32; v <= 63; v++ {
		putVec(v, fatalAddr)
	}

	code := bootStubCode(sigAddr)
	copy(img[0x200:], code)
	copy(img[sigAddr:], "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	copy(img[handlerBase:], hcode)

	// Jump table at 0x5EE0: JMP absolute long entries.
	entries := [14]uint32{
		rteAddr,       // 0x5EE0 _level1
		rteAddr,       // 0x5EE6 _level2
		rteAddr,       // 0x5EEC _level3
		rteAddr,       // 0x5EF2 _level4
		rteAddr,       // 0x5EF8 _level5
		rteAddr,       // 0x5EFE _level6
		rteAddr,       // 0x5F04 _level7
		rtsAddr,       // 0x5F0A _usercall0
		rtsAddr,       // 0x5F10 _usercall1
		trampAddrs[1], // 0x5F16 _buram (hard address)
		rtsAddr,       // 0x5F1C _usercall2
		trampAddrs[0], // 0x5F22 _cdbios (hard address)
		trampAddrs[2], // 0x5F28 _cdboot
		rtsAddr,       // 0x5F2E _usercall3
	}
	for i, target := range entries {
		off := JumpTableBase + i*6
		img[off] = 0x4E
		img[off+1] = 0xF9
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[off+2:], target)
	}
	return img
}

// MainStubROM builds a 0x10000 byte Genesis cartridge image for
// CD-only mode. Vectors: SSP = 0x00FFFE00 at offset 0 and PC =
// 0x00000200 at offset 4. The header at 0x100 holds the 16 bytes
// SEGA GENESIS followed by spaces, which is what the cartridge
// loader checks for. The code at 0x200 releases the sub CPU
// (gate array RES = 1 at 0xA12000), waits for comm status 0 at
// 0xA12020 to read 0x600D (the running IP), echoes the inverted
// comm status 1 word into comm command 0 at 0xA12010, sets the
// main comm flag at 0xA1200E, and then hands over to a disc main
// program when one is present, otherwise it idles.
//
// Disc main program convention for this synthesized stub: the
// main program lives at boot sector offset 0x200, which is the
// documented boot sector layout. The boot stub copies sector 0
// into Word RAM, so that program sits at main window address
// 0x200200. This stub requires the 8 byte marker ITAKMAIN at
// 0x200200 before jumping to the program entry at 0x200208, so
// discs without the marker keep the legacy idle behavior.
func MainStubROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0:], 0x00FFFE00)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[4:], 0x00000200)
	copy(rom[0x100:], "SEGA GENESIS    ")

	a := newAsm(0x200)
	a.mark("start")
	a.movebImmToAbs(0x01, 0xA12000) // RES = 1, BRQ = 0: release sub CPU
	a.mark("wait")
	a.movewAbsToDn(0xA12020, 0) // D0 = comm status 0
	a.cmpiw(0x600D, 0)
	a.branch(ccBNE, "wait")
	a.movewAbsToDn(0xA12022, 0) // D0 = comm status 1
	a.notw(0)
	a.movewDnToAbs(0, 0xA12010)     // comm command 0 = inverted status 1
	a.movebImmToAbs(0x01, 0xA1200E) // main comm flag = 1
	a.movelAbsToDn(0x00200200, 0)   // D0 = first marker longword
	a.cmpil(0x4954414B, 0)          // "ITAK"
	a.branch(ccBNE, "idle")
	a.movelAbsToDn(0x00200204, 0) // D0 = second marker longword
	a.cmpil(0x4D41494E, 0)        // "MAIN"
	a.branch(ccBNE, "idle")
	a.jmpAbs(0x00200208) // disc main program entry
	a.mark("idle")
	a.branch(ccBRA, "idle")
	copy(rom[0x200:], a.finish())
	return rom
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/sound/sound.go ====================

// Package sound is the Genesis sound section: a Yamaha YM2612 FM chip and
// the TI SN76489 PSG (the Sega variant built into the VDP's silicon, with
// the 16-bit LFSR and 0x0009 noise taps), mixed to 44.1kHz stereo.
//
// The PSG is our own SN76489 (cores/go-genesis/chips/psg), written
// from the TI datasheet and the Sega variant documentation. The
// YM2612 FM engine (ym2612.go) is written from Yamaha's published
// documentation: full six-channel FM with operators, envelopes,
// SSG-EG, LFO, timers and the DAC path. Milestone 1 shipped the
// YM2612 as a register shell; milestone 2 is the real engine.
//
// PINNED API (bus and system are written against this):
//
//	New() *Sound
//	WriteYM(addr uint32, val uint8)   addr 0-3: 0=addr port A, 1=data A, 2=addr port B, 3=data B
//	ReadYM() uint8                    status byte (busy + timer flags)
//	WritePSG(val uint8)
//	Produce(frames int) []int16       interleaved stereo, advances the PSG
//	SerializeSize() int / Serialize / Deserialize
//
// AdvanceClocks(cycles uint32) was added after the original pin:
// it steps only the YM2612 timers, in master clocks, so the system
// can move them at scanline boundaries; Produce accounts for the
// stepped time through a serialized ledger (see AdvanceClocks).
//
// RenderYMTo(clock int64) was added for timestamped register
// writes: it renders the pending FM span up to an emulated moment
// (YM2612 master clocks since power-on), so a write that lands
// right after it, driven by the bus with a CPU clock, takes
// effect at its true position inside the frame instead of at
// frame end. DAC sample streams depend on it.
package sound

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"math"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/chips/psg"
)

// SampleRate is the core's audio output rate.
const SampleRate = 44100

// YM2612 master clock on the Genesis (NTSC): 7,670,454 Hz.
const ymClock = 7670454

// PSG clock on the Genesis (NTSC): 3,579,545 Hz.
const psgClock = 3579545

// Sound holds both chips and the mix state.
type Sound struct {
	psg *psg.PSG

	ymAddrA  uint8
	ymAddrB  uint8
	ymRegsA  [256]uint8
	ymRegsB  [256]uint8
	ymStatus uint8 // YM2612 timer flags: bit0 = timer A, bit1 = timer B (busy is never set)
	ym       ymState

	// ymRegGen counts YM2612 register data writes; ymPrep holds
	// per-channel render constants derived from the register file
	// (see ym2612.go), rebuilt lazily whenever the generation has
	// moved since the channel was last prepared. Register changes
	// only ever arrive between render spans, so constants derived
	// at a generation stay valid for a whole span.
	ymRegGen uint64
	ymPrep   [6]ymChanPrep

	psgCarry float64 // fractional PSG clocks owed to the next Produce call
	out      []int16 // reusable mix buffer

	// FM resampler state: fmBuf holds native-rate stereo samples,
	// fmPrev is the last native sample of the previous batch and
	// fmAcc is how far (in native samples, 0..1) the next output
	// frame's position has advanced past it. preRendered counts
	// the samples at the head of fmBuf that timestamped writes
	// (RenderYMTo) already generated for the next Produce window;
	// it is always zero between frames, when states are taken, so
	// it is not serialized (the samples themselves are regenerated
	// identically from the serialized engine and stream state).
	fmBuf       []float32
	fmPrevL     float32
	fmPrevR     float32
	fmAcc       float64
	preRendered int

	psgWrites int // diagnostic counters: chip register writes seen
	ymWrites  int
}

// WriteCounts returns how many PSG and YM2612 writes the chips have
// received since power-on. Diagnostic aid: it separates a game that
// never touches a chip from one whose sound is genuinely broken.
func (s *Sound) WriteCounts() (psg, ym int) { return s.psgWrites, s.ymWrites }

// New returns the sound section in power-on state.
func New() *Sound {
	s := &Sound{
		psg: psg.New(psgClock, SampleRate, 4096, psg.Config{
			LFSRBits:       16,     // Sega variant
			WhiteNoiseTaps: 0x0009, // bits 0 and 3
		}),
	}
	// Operators power on silent: envelope at full attenuation,
	// stage off (the zero values of the ymState fields).
	for ch := range s.ym.ops {
		for op := range s.ym.ops[ch] {
			s.ym.ops[ch][op].levelFP = ymMaxFP
		}
	}
	// Pan powers on routed to BOTH sides on real hardware, even
	// though the register value reads as zero: the registers are
	// write-only, and games prove the routing every boot. Sonic 1
	// streams the SEGA jingle through the DAC without ever writing
	// channel 6's pan register first, and it is audible on hardware.
	// An explicit pan write (including 0x00, full mute) still takes
	// effect exactly as written.
	for _, bank := range []*[256]uint8{&s.ymRegsA, &s.ymRegsB} {
		bank[0xB4] = 0xC0
		bank[0xB5] = 0xC0
		bank[0xB6] = 0xC0
	}
	return s
}

// WritePSG passes a byte to the PSG.
func (s *Sound) WritePSG(val uint8) { s.psgWrites++; s.psg.Write(val) }

// serializeSize is the fixed save-state size of the sound section.
// The first 1544 bytes are the milestone 1 layout; the FM engine
// state (milestone 2) is appended after it:
//
//	ymAddrA(1) + ymAddrB(1) + ymStatus(1) + pad(1) + ymRegsA(256) +
//	ymRegsB(256) + psgLen(4, little endian) + psg state (1024 max) +
//	psgCarry f64(8) + fmAcc f64(8) + fmPrev f32x2(8) + lfoPhase(4) +
//	timerAAcc(4) + timerBAcc(4) + egDiv(1) + prev27(1) + pad(2) +
//	per-channel feedback history f32x2 x6(48) +
//	per-operator state x24(12 each: phase(4) + levelFP(4) +
//	stage(1) + flags(1: keyOn, ssgDown, ssgHold) + pad(2)) +
//	advLedger i64(8): timer clocks the system stepped ahead of the
//	render loop (see AdvanceClocks); without it a restore would
//	step that span of timer time a second time or not at all.
//	genClock i64(8): emulated time the render stream has reached
//	(see RenderYMTo); without it a restore could not place
//	timestamped writes against the stream and would skip or
//	double-render the span around the save point.
const serializeSize = 1936

// psgStateOffset is the offset of the PSG state region in the layout.
const psgStateOffset = 520

// ymStateOffset is the offset of the appended FM engine state.
const ymStateOffset = 1544

// WriteYM handles a write to one of the YM2612's four ports: address
// latch or data for bank A (channels 1-3 plus the global registers)
// or bank B (channels 4-6). Data writes land in the register file,
// which the engine reads live, and the two registers with immediate
// side effects act at once: 0x27 resets timer flags and starts or
// stops the timers through its load bits, 0x28 keys operators on
// and off.
func (s *Sound) WriteYM(addr uint32, val uint8) {
	s.ymWrites++
	switch addr {
	case 0: // bank A address latch
		s.ymAddrA = val
	case 1: // bank A data
		s.ymRegsA[s.ymAddrA] = val
		s.ymRegGen++
		switch s.ymAddrA {
		case 0x27:
			// Timer mode: bit4 (0x10) resets the timer A flag,
			// bit5 (0x20) resets the timer B flag.
			if val&0x10 != 0 {
				s.ymStatus &^= 0x01
			}
			if val&0x20 != 0 {
				s.ymStatus &^= 0x02
			}
			// A rising load bit restarts that timer's count.
			if val&0x01 != 0 && s.ym.prev27&0x01 == 0 {
				s.ym.timerAAcc = 0
			}
			if val&0x02 != 0 && s.ym.prev27&0x02 == 0 {
				s.ym.timerBAcc = 0
			}
			s.ym.prev27 = val
		case 0x28:
			s.ymKey(val)
		}
	case 2: // bank B address latch
		s.ymAddrB = val
	case 3: // bank B data
		s.ymRegsB[s.ymAddrB] = val
		s.ymRegGen++
	}
}

// ReadYM returns the YM2612 status byte: bit7 busy (always 0 here, port
// writes complete instantly), bit1 timer B flag, bit0 timer A flag.
func (s *Sound) ReadYM() uint8 {
	return s.ymStatus & 0x03
}

// AdvanceClocks steps the YM2612 timers forward by the given
// number of master clocks, outside the render path. On the
// Genesis the YM2612 clock (master / 7) equals the 68000 clock, so
// callers pass elapsed 68000 cycles. The system calls this at
// scanline boundaries so a CPU polling the status port sees timer
// flags flip mid-frame, the way DAC sample playback is paced,
// instead of only after the frame's audio renders. The stepped
// clocks are recorded in the engine's advance ledger and Produce
// renders past them without stepping a second time, so a span of
// emulated time moves the timers exactly once. Only the timers
// move here; envelopes and phase still render in Produce.
func (s *Sound) AdvanceClocks(cycles uint32) {
	if cycles == 0 {
		return
	}
	s.ymAdvanceTimers(cycles)
	s.ym.advLedger += int64(cycles)
}

// RenderYMTo renders the FM stream forward to the given emulated
// moment, in YM2612 master clocks since power-on (on the Genesis
// the YM2612 clock equals the 68000 clock). The bus calls this
// with the writing CPU's current time just before a register
// write lands, so the pending span is rendered with the register
// values that were in force during it and the write takes effect
// at its true position inside the frame. Without it, a DAC
// stream writing register 0x2A hundreds of times per frame would
// be heard as only its last byte, held for the whole frame.
// Rendering happens in whole native samples (144 clocks); a
// sub-sample remainder stays pending for the next call, so many
// small advances cost nothing until a full sample is owed.
// Timers ride along through the render loop's ledger accounting,
// exactly as if Produce had generated the span. A clock at or
// behind the rendered position renders nothing.
func (s *Sound) RenderYMTo(clock int64) {
	pending := clock - s.ym.genClock
	if pending < 144 {
		return
	}
	s.ymGenerate(int(pending / 144))
}

// Produce advances both chips by the time owed for frames output
// frames and returns exactly frames interleaved stereo pairs. The
// PSG runs as it always has (native samples at the output rate,
// mono duplicated to both channels). The YM2612 runs at its native
// rate (master / 144) and is linear-interpolated down to the output
// rate; the interpolation position and the previous native sample
// carry across calls and are part of the save state, so a restore
// resumes the FM stream sample-exactly.
func (s *Sound) Produce(frames int) []int16 {
	if frames < 0 {
		frames = 0
	}
	total := s.psgCarry + float64(frames)*psgClock/SampleRate
	whole := int(total)
	s.psgCarry = total - float64(whole)

	s.psg.GenerateSamples(whole)
	buf, count := s.psg.GetBuffer()
	s.psg.ResetBuffer()

	// Generate the native-rate FM samples this call spans, on top
	// of any already rendered into the head of the buffer by
	// timestamped writes (RenderYMTo). The next output frame sits
	// at native position -fmAcc relative to the first sample of
	// the window, with the previous batch's last sample at
	// position -1.
	n := 0
	if frames > 0 {
		n = int(float64(frames)*ymRatio-s.fmAcc) + 1
		if n < 0 {
			n = 0
		}
		if s.preRendered < n {
			s.ymGenerate(n - s.preRendered)
		}
	}

	need := frames * 2
	if cap(s.out) < need {
		s.out = make([]int16, need)
	}
	s.out = s.out[:need]
	for i := 0; i < frames; i++ {
		var f float32
		if i < count {
			f = buf[i]
		}
		if f > 1 {
			f = 1
		} else if f < -1 {
			f = -1
		}

		// Linear interpolation of the FM stream at this frame's
		// native position.
		pos := -s.fmAcc + float64(i)*ymRatio
		k := int(pos)
		if pos < 0 && float64(k) != pos {
			k-- // floor for negative positions
		}
		frac := float32(pos - float64(k))
		var l0, r0 float32
		if k < 0 {
			l0, r0 = s.fmPrevL, s.fmPrevR
		} else {
			l0, r0 = s.fmBuf[2*k], s.fmBuf[2*k+1]
		}
		l1, r1 := s.fmBuf[2*(k+1)], s.fmBuf[2*(k+1)+1]
		fl := l0 + (l1-l0)*frac
		fr := r0 + (r1-r0)*frac

		s.out[2*i] = clamp16(f*24000 + fl*12000)
		s.out[2*i+1] = clamp16(f*24000 + fr*12000)
	}
	if n > 0 {
		s.fmPrevL = s.fmBuf[2*(n-1)]
		s.fmPrevR = s.fmBuf[2*(n-1)+1]
		s.fmAcc = float64(n) + s.fmAcc - float64(frames)*ymRatio
		// Samples the timestamped writes rendered past this
		// window (their emulated moment falls inside the next
		// one) carry over as the head of the next window; the
		// rest of the buffer is scratch.
		if left := s.preRendered - n; left > 0 {
			copy(s.fmBuf, s.fmBuf[2*n:2*(n+left)])
			s.preRendered = left
		} else {
			s.preRendered = 0
		}
	}
	return s.out
}

// clamp16 converts a mixed float sample to int16 with saturation.
func clamp16(v float32) int16 {
	if v > 32767 {
		return 32767
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return -32768
	}
	return int16(v)
}

// SerializeSize returns the fixed save-state size of the sound section.
func (s *Sound) SerializeSize() int { return serializeSize }

// Serialize writes the sound section state into buf (layout documented at
// serializeSize). The PSG state goes into the 1024-byte region at the
// tail. Observed chip behavior: psg.Serialize needs only
// psg.SerializeSize (41) bytes, so with a 1024-byte scratch it never
// errors; if it ever did, psgLen is written as 0 and the region left
// zeroed instead of failing the whole state.
func (s *Sound) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < serializeSize {
		return errors.New("sound: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	buf[0] = s.ymAddrA
	buf[1] = s.ymAddrB
	buf[2] = s.ymStatus
	buf[3] = 0
	copy(buf[4:260], s.ymRegsA[:])
	copy(buf[260:516], s.ymRegsB[:])

	region := buf[psgStateOffset:serializeSize]
	for i := range region {
		region[i] = 0
	}
	psgLen := 0
	var scratch [1024]byte
	if err := s.psg.Serialize(scratch[:]); err == nil {
		psgLen = psg.SerializeSize
		copy(region, scratch[:psgLen])
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[516:520], uint32(psgLen))

	// FM engine state (milestone 2), layout at serializeSize.
	b := buf[ymStateOffset:]
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(b[0:8], math.Float64bits(s.psgCarry))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(b[8:16], math.Float64bits(s.fmAcc))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[16:20], math.Float32bits(s.fmPrevL))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[20:24], math.Float32bits(s.fmPrevR))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[24:28], s.ym.lfoPhase)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[28:32], s.ym.timerAAcc)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[32:36], s.ym.timerBAcc)
	b[36] = s.ym.egDiv
	b[37] = s.ym.prev27
	b[38], b[39] = 0, 0
	off := 40
	for ch := range s.ym.chans {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[off:off+4], math.Float32bits(s.ym.chans[ch].fb0))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[off+4:off+8], math.Float32bits(s.ym.chans[ch].fb1))
		off += 8
	}
	for ch := range s.ym.ops {
		for op := range s.ym.ops[ch] {
			o := &s.ym.ops[ch][op]
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[off:off+4], o.phase)
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[off+4:off+8], uint32(o.levelFP))
			b[off+8] = o.stage
			var flags uint8
			if o.keyOn {
				flags |= 1
			}
			if o.ssgDown {
				flags |= 2
			}
			if o.ssgHold {
				flags |= 4
			}
			b[off+9] = flags
			b[off+10], b[off+11] = 0, 0
			off += 12
		}
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(b[off:off+8], uint64(s.ym.advLedger))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(b[off+8:off+16], uint64(s.ym.genClock))
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores state written by Serialize.
func (s *Sound) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < serializeSize {
		return errors.New("sound: deserialize buffer too small")
	}
	s.ymAddrA = buf[0]
	s.ymAddrB = buf[1]
	s.ymStatus = buf[2] & 0x03
	copy(s.ymRegsA[:], buf[4:260])
	copy(s.ymRegsB[:], buf[260:516])

	psgLen := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[516:520]))
	if psgLen > ymStateOffset-psgStateOffset {
		return errors.New("sound: corrupt PSG state length")
	}
	if psgLen > 0 {
		if err := s.psg.Deserialize(buf[psgStateOffset : psgStateOffset+psgLen]); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	// FM engine state (milestone 2), layout at serializeSize.
	b := buf[ymStateOffset:]
	s.psgCarry = math.Float64frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(b[0:8]))
	s.fmAcc = math.Float64frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(b[8:16]))
	s.fmPrevL = math.Float32frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[16:20]))
	s.fmPrevR = math.Float32frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[20:24]))
	s.ym.lfoPhase = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[24:28])
	s.ym.timerAAcc = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[28:32])
	s.ym.timerBAcc = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[32:36])
	s.ym.egDiv = b[36]
	s.ym.prev27 = b[37]
	off := 40
	for ch := range s.ym.chans {
		s.ym.chans[ch].fb0 = math.Float32frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off : off+4]))
		s.ym.chans[ch].fb1 = math.Float32frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off+4 : off+8]))
		off += 8
	}
	for ch := range s.ym.ops {
		for op := range s.ym.ops[ch] {
			o := &s.ym.ops[ch][op]
			o.phase = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off : off+4])
			o.levelFP = int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off+4 : off+8]))
			o.stage = b[off+8]
			flags := b[off+9]
			o.keyOn = flags&1 != 0
			o.ssgDown = flags&2 != 0
			o.ssgHold = flags&4 != 0
			off += 12
		}
	}
	s.ym.advLedger = int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(b[off : off+8]))
	s.ym.genClock = int64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(b[off+8 : off+16]))
	// fmBuf content is scratch and preRendered is always zero at
	// frame boundaries, where states are taken; make that true
	// here too so a mid-stream restore cannot resurrect stale
	// pending samples.
	s.preRendered = 0
	// The register file was replaced wholesale: force every
	// channel's prepared render constants to rebuild.
	s.ymRegGen++
	return nil
}
