package sound

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/chips/psg"
)

// setTone writes an audible channel 0 tone to the PSG: period 0xEE (238,
// about 470 Hz) at maximum volume.
func setTone(s *Sound) {
	s.WritePSG(0x8E) // latch: channel 0, tone, low 4 bits of period = 0xE
	s.WritePSG(0x0E) // data: high 6 bits of period = 0x0E
	s.WritePSG(0x90) // latch: channel 0, volume, value 0 = loudest
}

func countNonzero(out []int16) int {
	n := 0
	for _, v := range out {
		if v != 0 {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

func TestWriteYMLatchAndData(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()

	s.WriteYM(0, 0x2A) // bank A latch: DAC data register
	s.WriteYM(1, 0x55) // bank A data
	if s.ymAddrA != 0x2A {
		t.Fatalf("ymAddrA = %#02x, want 0x2a", s.ymAddrA)
	}
	if got := s.ymRegsA[0x2A]; got != 0x55 {
		t.Fatalf("ymRegsA[0x2a] = %#02x, want 0x55", got)
	}

	// A second data write without re-latching hits the same register.
	s.WriteYM(1, 0x66)
	if got := s.ymRegsA[0x2A]; got != 0x66 {
		t.Fatalf("ymRegsA[0x2a] = %#02x after second data write, want 0x66", got)
	}

	s.WriteYM(2, 0x10) // bank B latch
	s.WriteYM(3, 0xAB) // bank B data
	if s.ymAddrB != 0x10 {
		t.Fatalf("ymAddrB = %#02x, want 0x10", s.ymAddrB)
	}
	if got := s.ymRegsB[0x10]; got != 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("ymRegsB[0x10] = %#02x, want 0xab", got)
	}
	if got := s.ymRegsA[0x10]; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("bank B write leaked into bank A: ymRegsA[0x10] = %#02x", got)
	}
	if got := s.ymRegsB[0x2A]; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("bank A write leaked into bank B: ymRegsB[0x2a] = %#02x", got)
	}
}

func TestWriteYMTimerRegistersStored(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	s.WriteYM(0, 0x24)
	s.WriteYM(1, 0xF0) // timer A period high 8 bits
	s.WriteYM(0, 0x25)
	s.WriteYM(1, 0x03) // timer A period low 2 bits in top bits
	s.WriteYM(0, 0x26)
	s.WriteYM(1, 0x7E) // timer B period
	if s.ymRegsA[0x24] != 0xF0 || s.ymRegsA[0x25] != 0x03 || s.ymRegsA[0x26] != 0x7E {
		t.Fatalf("timer regs = %02x %02x %02x, want f0 03 7e",
			s.ymRegsA[0x24], s.ymRegsA[0x25], s.ymRegsA[0x26])
	}
}

func TestWriteYMReg27ClearsTimerFlags(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	s.ymStatus = 0x03 // pretend both timer flags are raised

	s.WriteYM(0, 0x27)
	s.WriteYM(1, 0x10) // reset timer A flag only
	if s.ymStatus != 0x02 {
		t.Fatalf("ymStatus = %#02x after 0x27 reset A, want 0x02", s.ymStatus)
	}
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got != 0x02 {
		t.Fatalf("ReadYM = %#02x, want 0x02", got)
	}

	s.WriteYM(1, 0x20) // reset timer B flag (address still latched to 0x27)
	if s.ymStatus != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("ymStatus = %#02x after 0x27 reset B, want 0x00", s.ymStatus)
	}
	if got := s.ymRegsA[0x27]; got != 0x20 {
		t.Fatalf("ymRegsA[0x27] = %#02x, want the raw value 0x20 stored", got)
	}
}

func TestReadYMBusyClear(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	st := s.ReadYM()
	if st&0x80 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("busy bit set on fresh chip: status %#02x", st)
	}
	if st != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh status = %#02x, want 0 (no timer flags)", st)
	}
}

func TestProducePSGTone(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	setTone(s)

	out := s.Produce(735)
	if len(out) != 1470 {
		t.Fatalf("len(Produce(735)) = %d, want 1470", len(out))
	}
	if n := countNonzero(out); n == 0 {
		t.Fatal("Produce returned all silence with an audible tone set")
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(out); i += 2 {
		if out[i] != out[i+1] {
			t.Fatalf("stereo pair %d differs: %d != %d", i/2, out[i], out[i+1])
		}
	}
}

func TestProduceSilentByDefault(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	out := s.Produce(735)
	if len(out) != 1470 {
		t.Fatalf("len(Produce(735)) = %d, want 1470", len(out))
	}
	if n := countNonzero(out); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh chip produced %d nonzero samples, want silence", n)
	}
}

func TestSerializeSizeAndRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	s.WriteYM(0, 0x24)
	s.WriteYM(1, 0xF0)
	s.WriteYM(2, 0x30)
	s.WriteYM(3, 0x71)
	setTone(s)
	s.Produce(100) // run the PSG so its state is mid-stream

	if got := s.SerializeSize(); got != 1936 {
		t.Fatalf("SerializeSize() = %d, want 1936", got)
	}
	buf := make([]byte, s.SerializeSize())
	if err := s.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	if buf[0] != s.ymAddrA || buf[1] != s.ymAddrB || buf[2] != s.ymStatus {
		t.Fatalf("header bytes = %02x %02x %02x, want %02x %02x %02x",
			buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], s.ymAddrA, s.ymAddrB, s.ymStatus)
	}
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[516:520]); got != psg.SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("psgLen = %d, want %d (psg.SerializeSize)", got, psg.SerializeSize)
	}

	s2 := New()
	if err := s2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if s2.ymRegsA != s.ymRegsA {
		t.Fatal("ymRegsA did not survive the round trip")
	}
	if s2.ymRegsB != s.ymRegsB {
		t.Fatal("ymRegsB did not survive the round trip")
	}
	if s2.ymAddrA != s.ymAddrA || s2.ymAddrB != s.ymAddrB || s2.ymStatus != s.ymStatus {
		t.Fatalf("latches/status = %02x %02x %02x, want %02x %02x %02x",
			s2.ymAddrA, s2.ymAddrB, s2.ymStatus, s.ymAddrA, s.ymAddrB, s.ymStatus)
	}

	// The restored PSG still has its tone: Produce works and is audible.
	out := s2.Produce(735)
	if len(out) != 1470 {
		t.Fatalf("len(Produce(735)) after Deserialize = %d, want 1470", len(out))
	}
	if n := countNonzero(out); n == 0 {
		t.Fatal("PSG tone lost across the serialize round trip")
	}
}

func TestSerializeBuffersTooSmall(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	if err := s.Serialize(make([]byte, serializeSize-1)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Serialize accepted a short buffer")
	}
	if err := s.Deserialize(make([]byte, serializeSize-1)); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a short buffer")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/sound/ym2612.go ====================

package sound

import "math"

// YM2612 FM engine (milestone 2), written from Yamaha's published
// YM2612 documentation: the register map, the phase and envelope
// generator behavior, the eight algorithm connection diagrams, the
// SSG-EG pattern set and the timer formulas. No third-party emulator
// source was consulted; where the datasheet gives behavior as tables
// this implementation follows the documented shape and says so.
//
// Model summary:
//
//   - The chip runs at its native sample rate, master clock / 144
//     (about 53,267 Hz on the Genesis). Produce generates native-rate
//     stereo into a reusable buffer and linear-interpolates down to
//     the 44.1 kHz output rate.
//   - Operator phase is a 32-bit accumulator whose cycle length is
//     2^21 counts, so the documented increment (F-number << block)
//     at multiple 1 is exact and multiple 0 (the 0.5x case) keeps a
//     fractional bit. The sine table index is the top 10 bits.
//   - Operator output is sine times a log amplitude: attenuation is
//     tracked in the chip's own units, 1024 steps spanning 96 dB,
//     with total level adding 8 steps per count (0.75 dB), key
//     scaling and AM from the LFO added on top.
//   - The envelope generator ticks once every 3 native samples, as
//     on the chip. Its full-range time follows the datasheet rate
//     table shape (time doubles every 4 effective rate steps).
//     Attack is the documented exponential approach to full volume;
//     decay, sustain decay and release advance linearly in dB.
//   - Timers A and B count master clocks with the documented
//     periods, (1024 - NA) * 18 and (256 - NB) * 288 clocks, set
//     their status flags on expiry when the matching enable bit in
//     register 0x27 is set, and auto-reload while loaded.
//   - Channel 3 special mode (register 0x27 bits 6-7 nonzero) gives
//     operators 2, 3 and 4 their own F-number and block from the
//     0xA8-0xAE registers. CSM mode is approximated as normal
//     keying: the hardware would key channel 3 from timer A, which
//     almost no Genesis game uses, and the difference is documented
//     here rather than hidden.
//   - When register 0x2B bit 7 is set, channel 6 outputs the DAC
//     sample from register 0x2A (unsigned, 0x80 is the center)
//     instead of FM, through channel 6's pan controls.

// ymNativeRate is the YM2612 output sample rate on the Genesis:
// master clock divided by 144.
const ymNativeRate = float64(ymClock) / 144.0

// ymRatio is native samples per 44.1 kHz output frame.
const ymRatio = ymNativeRate / SampleRate

// ymMaxFP is the envelope attenuation ceiling in fixed point:
// 1023 attenuation steps (silence) shifted up by 20 fractional bits.
const ymMaxFP = 1023 << 20

// Envelope generator stages.
const (
	egOff = iota
	egAttack
	egDecay
	egSustain
	egRelease
	egSSG
)

// ymOp is one FM operator's runtime state. Only state that affects
// future output lives here, and all of it is serialized.
type ymOp struct {
	phase   uint32 // phase accumulator, one cycle is 2^21 counts
	levelFP int32  // envelope attenuation, 0 loudest, ymMaxFP silent
	stage   uint8  // eg stage (egOff, egAttack, ...)
	keyOn   bool   // current key state from register 0x28
	ssgDown bool   // SSG-EG: current leg runs toward silence
	ssgHold bool   // SSG-EG: pattern finished, holding its level
}

// ymChan is one channel's runtime state beyond its registers.
type ymChan struct {
	fb0 float32 // operator 1 output, previous sample (feedback)
	fb1 float32 // operator 1 output, two samples ago
}

// ymState is the whole FM engine state.
type ymState struct {
	ops   [6][4]ymOp // [channel][operator in logical order 1-4]
	chans [6]ymChan

	lfoPhase  uint32 // LFO phase accumulator, one cycle is 2^32
	timerAAcc uint32 // master clocks accumulated toward timer A expiry
	timerBAcc uint32 // master clocks accumulated toward timer B expiry
	egDiv     uint8  // envelope divider counter, ticks every 3 samples
	prev27    uint8  // last register 0x27 value, for timer load edges
	// genClock is the emulated time, in YM2612 master clocks, the
	// render stream has reached: 144 clocks per native sample
	// generated, counted from power-on. RenderYMTo compares write
	// timestamps against it to decide how much pending span to
	// render before a register change lands. Serialized: without
	// it a restore could not tell rendered time from unrendered
	// time and timestamped writes would skip or double-render a
	// span around the save point.
	genClock int64
	// advLedger is the master clocks of timer time the system has
	// already stepped through AdvanceClocks but the render loop has
	// not yet accounted for. ymGenerate consumes it instead of
	// stepping the timers a second time for the same span, so a
	// span of emulated time is never counted twice. Serialized:
	// without it a restore would re-step (or skip) timer time and
	// the flag pattern after the restore would drift.
	advLedger int64
}

// opSlot maps between logical operator index (0..3 for OP1..OP4) and
// register slot index. The YM2612 register file stores the operators
// in the order OP1, OP3, OP2, OP4, so the map is its own inverse:
// slot = opSlot[op] and op = opSlot[slot].
var opSlot = [4]int{0, 2, 1, 3}

// modMask[algo][op] is the bitmask of earlier operators whose outputs
// modulate this operator, from the documented algorithm diagrams.
var modMask = [8][4]uint8{
	{0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x4}, // 0: 1-2-3-4 chain
	{0, 0x0, 0x3, 0x4}, // 1: 1+2 into 3, 3 into 4
	{0, 0x0, 0x1, 0x6}, // 2: 1 into 3, 3+2 into 4
	{0, 0x1, 0x0, 0x6}, // 3: 1 into 2, 2+3 into 4
	{0, 0x1, 0x0, 0x4}, // 4: 1 into 2, 3 into 4
	{0, 0x1, 0x1, 0x1}, // 5: 1 into 2, 3 and 4
	{0, 0x1, 0x0, 0x0}, // 6: 1 into 2
	{0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0}, // 7: four independent carriers
}

// carrierMask[algo] is the bitmask of operators that reach the
// channel output.
var carrierMask = [8]uint8{0x8, 0x8, 0x8, 0x8, 0xA, 0xE, 0xE, 0xF}

// carrierGain normalizes channel loudness by carrier count.
var carrierGain = [8]float32{1, 1, 1, 1, 0.7, 0.55, 0.55, 0.45}

// fbScale[fb] is the operator 1 feedback depth in sine table index
// units at full-scale output, doubling per step as documented.
var fbScale = [8]float32{0, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048}

// lfoFreqTable is the documented LFO frequency table (Hz) for
// register 0x22 bits 0-2.
var lfoFreqTable = [8]float64{3.98, 5.56, 6.02, 6.37, 6.88, 9.63, 48.1, 72.2}

// pmsCents[pms] is the documented pitch modulation depth in cents
// (peak deviation) for register 0xB4 bits 0-2.
var pmsCents = [8]float64{0, 3.4, 6.7, 10, 14, 20, 40, 80}

// amsSteps[ams] is the documented AM depth in attenuation steps
// (0, 1.4, 5.9, 11.8 dB) for register 0xB4 bits 4-5.
var amsSteps = [4]int32{0, 15, 63, 126}

// slSteps[sl] is the sustain level in attenuation steps from the
// datasheet table; note the documented jump at 15.
var slSteps = [16]int32{0, 32, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 288, 320, 352, 384, 416, 448, 992}

// Tables built once at package load; the sample loop only reads.
var (
	sinTable [1024]float32
	// ampTable[a] is the linear amplitude for a attenuation steps,
	// a in 0..2175 (EG 1023 + TL 1016 + AM 126, plus headroom).
	ampTable   [2176]float32
	egTicks    [64]int32 // EG ticks for a full-range sweep per effective rate
	egIncFP    [64]int32 // fixed-point attenuation step per EG tick
	lfoIncTab  [8]uint32 // LFO phase increment per native sample
	ymInitDone = buildYMTables()
)

func buildYMTables() bool {
	for i := range sinTable {
		sinTable[i] = float32(math.Sin(2 * math.Pi * float64(i) / 1024))
	}
	for i := range ampTable {
		db := float64(i) * (96.0 / 1024.0)
		ampTable[i] = float32(math.Pow(10, -db/20))
	}
	for er := 0; er < 64; er++ {
		// Datasheet rate table shape: the full-range time doubles
		// every 4 rate steps, about 0.34 ms at rate 63.
		t := int32(6.2*math.Pow(2, float64(63-er)/4) + 0.5)
		if t < 1 {
			t = 1
		}
		egTicks[er] = t
		inc := int32(ymMaxFP) / t
		if inc < 1 {
			inc = 1
		}
		egIncFP[er] = inc
	}
	for i, f := range lfoFreqTable {
		lfoIncTab[i] = uint32(f / ymNativeRate * 4294967296.0)
	}
	return true
}

// ymBank returns the register bank and channel offset for a channel:
// channels 0-2 live in bank A, channels 3-5 in bank B.
func (s *Sound) ymBank(ch int) (*[256]uint8, int) {
	if ch < 3 {
		return &s.ymRegsA, ch
	}
	return &s.ymRegsB, ch - 3
}

// ymOpFreq returns the effective F-number and block for an operator,
// honoring channel 3 special mode (per-operator frequency registers
// 0xA8-0xAE; operator 1 keeps the normal channel registers).
func (s *Sound) ymOpFreq(ch, op int) (fnum, block int) {
	if ch == 2 && (s.ymRegsA[0x27]>>6)&3 != 0 {
		switch op {
		case 1:
			return ymFreqPair(s.ymRegsA[0xA8], s.ymRegsA[0xAC])
		case 2:
			return ymFreqPair(s.ymRegsA[0xA9], s.ymRegsA[0xAD])
		case 3:
			return ymFreqPair(s.ymRegsA[0xAA], s.ymRegsA[0xAE])
		}
	}
	bank, off := s.ymBank(ch)
	return ymFreqPair(bank[0xA0+off], bank[0xA4+off])
}

func ymFreqPair(lo, hi uint8) (fnum, block int) {
	return (int(hi&0x07) << 8) | int(lo), int(hi>>3) & 0x07
}

// ymKey applies a key on/off register (0x28) write: bits 4-7 key the
// operators in register slot order, bits 0-2 select the channel
// (0,1,2,4,5,6; 3 and 7 are not channels). Only transitions act:
// key on starts the attack from the current level, key off starts
// the release. The phase accumulator is not reset, as on the chip.
func (s *Sound) ymKey(val uint8) {
	var ch int
	switch sel := val & 0x07; {
	case sel < 3:
		ch = int(sel)
	case sel >= 4 && sel <= 6:
		ch = int(sel) - 1
	default:
		return
	}
	mask := (val >> 4) & 0x0F
	for slot := 0; slot < 4; slot++ {
		o := &s.ym.ops[ch][opSlot[slot]]
		if mask&(1<<uint(slot)) != 0 {
			if !o.keyOn {
				o.keyOn = true
				o.stage = egAttack
				o.ssgHold = false
			}
		} else if o.keyOn {
			o.keyOn = false
			o.stage = egRelease
		}
	}
}

// ymAdvanceTimers advances timers A and B by the given number of
// master clocks and sets the status flags for expiries whose
// enable bit in register 0x27 is set. A timer only counts while
// its load bit is set; the accumulator restarts when the load bit
// rises, which WriteYM handles through prev27. Expiry drains whole
// periods off the accumulator, so the timers auto-reload and any
// chunk size (one native sample of 144 clocks from the render
// loop, a scanline of 68000 cycles from the system) behaves the
// same.
func (s *Sound) ymAdvanceTimers(clocks uint32) {
	r27 := s.ymRegsA[0x27]
	if r27&0x01 != 0 { // timer A load
		na := (int(s.ymRegsA[0x24]) << 2) | (int(s.ymRegsA[0x25]) >> 6)
		period := uint32(18 * (1024 - na))
		s.ym.timerAAcc += clocks
		for s.ym.timerAAcc >= period {
			s.ym.timerAAcc -= period
			if r27&0x04 != 0 { // timer A enable
				s.ymStatus |= 0x01
			}
		}
	}
	if r27&0x02 != 0 { // timer B load
		period := uint32(288 * (256 - int(s.ymRegsA[0x26])))
		s.ym.timerBAcc += clocks
		for s.ym.timerBAcc >= period {
			s.ym.timerBAcc -= period
			if r27&0x08 != 0 { // timer B enable
				s.ymStatus |= 0x02
			}
		}
	}
}

// ymEffRate computes the effective envelope rate for a rate register
// value with key scaling: rate = 2*R + keycode addend, clamped to
// 63. The keycode derives from the operator's own pitch.
func ymEffRate(r int, ks, kc int) int {
	add := 0
	if ks > 0 {
		add = kc >> uint(3-ks)
	}
	er := 2*r + add
	if er > 63 {
		er = 63
	}
	return er
}

// ymEGAfterAttack picks the stage that follows a completed attack:
// the SSG-EG pattern stage when SSG-EG is enabled for the operator,
// otherwise the first decay.
func (s *Sound) ymEGAfterAttack(o *ymOp, ssgReg uint8) {
	if ssgReg&0x08 != 0 {
		o.stage = egSSG
		o.ssgDown = (ssgReg & 0x07) < 4
		o.ssgHold = false
	} else {
		o.stage = egDecay
	}
}

// ymTickEG advances every operator's envelope by one EG tick.
func (s *Sound) ymTickEG() {
	for ch := 0; ch < 6; ch++ {
		bank, off := s.ymBank(ch)
		for op := 0; op < 4; op++ {
			o := &s.ym.ops[ch][op]
			if o.stage == egOff {
				continue
			}
			s.ymTickOp(bank, off, ch, op, o)
		}
	}
}

// ymTickOp advances one operator's envelope by one EG tick.
func (s *Sound) ymTickOp(bank *[256]uint8, off, ch, op int, o *ymOp) {
	slot := opSlot[op]
	ksReg := bank[0x50+slot*4+off]
	ks := int(ksReg >> 6)
	fnum, block := s.ymOpFreq(ch, op)
	kc := (block << 2) | (fnum >> 9)
	rate := func(r int) int { return ymEffRate(r, ks, kc) }

	switch o.stage {
	case egAttack:
		er := rate(int(ksReg & 0x1F))
		div := egTicks[er] / 4
		if div < 1 {
			div = 1
		}
		// Exponential approach: each tick removes a fraction of
		// the remaining attenuation, plus one unit so the tail
		// always lands.
		step := o.levelFP/div + 1
		if step >= o.levelFP {
			o.levelFP = 0
			s.ymEGAfterAttack(o, bank[0x90+slot*4+off])
		} else {
			o.levelFP -= step
		}
	case egDecay:
		er := rate(int(bank[0x60+slot*4+off] & 0x1F))
		o.levelFP += egIncFP[er]
		slFP := slSteps[bank[0x80+slot*4+off]>>4] << 20
		if o.levelFP >= slFP {
			o.stage = egSustain
		}
		if o.levelFP > ymMaxFP {
			o.levelFP = ymMaxFP
		}
	case egSustain:
		er := rate(int(bank[0x70+slot*4+off] & 0x1F))
		o.levelFP += egIncFP[er]
		if o.levelFP >= ymMaxFP {
			o.levelFP = ymMaxFP
			o.stage = egOff
		}
	case egRelease:
		// Documented release rate is 2*RR + 1 before key scaling.
		rr := int(bank[0x80+slot*4+off] & 0x0F)
		add := 0
		if ks > 0 {
			add = kc >> uint(3-ks)
		}
		er := 2*rr + 1 + add
		if er > 63 {
			er = 63
		}
		o.levelFP += egIncFP[er]
		if o.levelFP >= ymMaxFP {
			o.levelFP = ymMaxFP
			o.stage = egOff
		}
	case egSSG:
		if o.ssgHold {
			return
		}
		pat := bank[0x90+slot*4+off] & 0x07
		er := rate(int(bank[0x60+slot*4+off] & 0x1F)) // SSG-EG cycles at D1R
		if o.ssgDown {
			o.levelFP += egIncFP[er]
			if o.levelFP >= ymMaxFP {
				o.levelFP = ymMaxFP
				s.ymSSGBound(o, pat, true)
			}
		} else {
			div := egTicks[er] / 4
			if div < 1 {
				div = 1
			}
			step := o.levelFP/div + 1
			if step >= o.levelFP {
				o.levelFP = 0
				s.ymSSGBound(o, pat, false)
			} else {
				o.levelFP -= step
			}
		}
	}
}

// ymSSGBound applies an SSG-EG pattern boundary: the level just
// reached the bottom (full attenuation, atBottom true) or the top
// (zero attenuation). Patterns follow the documented SSG shapes:
// 0 repeat decay, 1 decay then hold at bottom, 2 alternate, 3 decay
// then hold at top, 4 repeat attack, 5 attack then hold at top,
// 6 alternate, 7 attack then hold at bottom.
func (s *Sound) ymSSGBound(o *ymOp, pat uint8, atBottom bool) {
	switch pat {
	case 0: // repeat decay: jump back to the top and keep decaying
		if atBottom {
			o.levelFP = 0
		}
	case 1: // decay once, hold at the bottom
		if atBottom {
			o.ssgHold = true
		}
	case 2, 6: // alternate direction at each bound
		o.ssgDown = !atBottom
	case 3: // decay once, jump to the top and hold
		if atBottom {
			o.levelFP = 0
			o.ssgHold = true
		}
	case 4: // repeat attack: jump to the bottom and keep attacking
		if !atBottom {
			o.levelFP = ymMaxFP
		}
	case 5: // attack once, hold at the top
		if !atBottom {
			o.ssgHold = true
		}
	case 7: // attack once, jump to the bottom and hold
		if !atBottom {
			o.levelFP = ymMaxFP
			o.ssgHold = true
		}
	}
}

// ymOpStep computes the phase increment for one operator: the
// documented (F-number << block) base, detune offset, multiple
// scaling (multiple 0 is the 0.5x case), and LFO pitch modulation.
func ymOpStep(fnum, block, dt, mul int, pmFactor float64) uint32 {
	base := int32(fnum) << uint(block)
	if mag := dt & 3; mag != 0 && base != 0 {
		// Detune: the datasheet table's offset grows with pitch
		// (keycode) and with the detune magnitude. This follows
		// that shape, up to about 5 percent at the top of the
		// range; it is an approximation of the printed table.
		kc := (block << 2) | (fnum >> 9)
		off := (base * int32(mag) * int32(kc+1)) >> 11
		if dt&4 != 0 {
			base -= off
		} else {
			base += off
		}
		if base < 0 {
			base = 0
		}
	}
	mul2 := int32(2 * mul)
	if mul == 0 {
		mul2 = 1 // documented 0.5x case
	}
	step := base * mul2 >> 1
	if pmFactor != 1 {
		step = int32(float64(step) * pmFactor)
	}
	if step < 0 {
		step = 0
	}
	return uint32(step)
}

// ymChanPrep holds one FM channel's render constants derived from
// the register file: everything ymChannel used to recompute from
// registers on every native sample (some 6,000 times per frame per
// channel). A channel is re-prepared lazily when the register
// generation (Sound.ymRegGen) has moved since its last prepare;
// register writes only land between render spans, so a prepared
// channel is exact for the whole span it serves.
type ymChanPrep struct {
	gen   uint64
	ready bool
	pan   uint8
	dacOn bool
	algo  int
	fb    int
	ams   int
	pms   int
	// Per operator, in render order: the phase step before LFO
	// pitch modulation, the total-level contribution to the
	// attenuation index, and the AM enable bit.
	stepPre [4]uint32
	tlAtt   [4]int
	amOn    [4]bool
}

// ymPrepChannel rebuilds one channel's prepared constants from the
// current register file.
func (s *Sound) ymPrepChannel(ch int, p *ymChanPrep) {
	bank, off := s.ymBank(ch)
	p.pan = bank[0xB4+off]
	p.dacOn = ch == 5 && s.ymRegsA[0x2B]&0x80 != 0
	p.algo = int(bank[0xB0+off] & 0x07)
	p.fb = int((bank[0xB0+off] >> 3) & 0x07)
	p.ams = int((bank[0xB4+off] >> 4) & 0x03)
	p.pms = int(bank[0xB4+off] & 0x07)
	for op := 0; op < 4; op++ {
		slot := opSlot[op]
		fnum, block := s.ymOpFreq(ch, op)
		dtMul := bank[0x30+slot*4+off]
		p.stepPre[op] = ymOpStep(fnum, block, int(dtMul>>4)&0x07, int(dtMul&0x0F), 1)
		p.tlAtt[op] = int(bank[0x40+slot*4+off]&0x7F) * 8
		p.amOn[op] = bank[0x60+slot*4+off]&0x80 != 0
	}
	p.gen = s.ymRegGen
	p.ready = true
}

// ymChannel renders one native-rate stereo pair's worth of one FM
// channel into the l/r accumulators, applying pan. DAC mode on
// channel 6 replaces the FM output.
func (s *Sound) ymChannel(ch int, lfoSigned, lfoTri float64, lfoOn bool, acc *[2]float32) {
	p := &s.ymPrep[ch]
	if !p.ready || p.gen != s.ymRegGen {
		s.ymPrepChannel(ch, p)
	}

	pmFactor := 1.0
	if lfoOn && p.pms != 0 {
		pmFactor = math.Pow(2, lfoSigned*pmsCents[p.pms]/1200)
	}
	amAtt := int32(0)
	if lfoOn {
		amAtt = int32(float64(amsSteps[p.ams]) * lfoTri)
	}

	var outs [4]float32
	for op := 0; op < 4; op++ {
		o := &s.ym.ops[ch][op]

		// Modulation input from earlier operators plus, for
		// operator 1, its feedback history.
		var mod float32
		m := modMask[p.algo][op]
		for src := 0; src < op; src++ {
			if m&(1<<uint(src)) != 0 {
				mod += outs[src]
			}
		}
		idxOff := int32(mod * 512)
		if op == 0 {
			avg := (s.ym.chans[ch].fb0 + s.ym.chans[ch].fb1) * 0.5
			idxOff += int32(avg * fbScale[p.fb])
		}
		idx := (int32(o.phase>>11) + idxOff) & 1023

		// The prepared step already carries detune, multiple
		// and the negative clamp; pitch modulation scales it
		// exactly as ymOpStep's pmFactor path did (the product
		// of a non-negative step and a positive factor cannot
		// go negative, so the clamp cannot re-trigger).
		step := p.stepPre[op]
		if pmFactor != 1 {
			step = uint32(int32(float64(step) * pmFactor))
		}
		o.phase += step

		atten := int(o.levelFP>>20) + p.tlAtt[op]
		if p.amOn[op] { // AM enable for this operator
			atten += int(amAtt)
		}
		if atten > len(ampTable)-1 {
			atten = len(ampTable) - 1
		} else if atten < 0 {
			atten = 0
		}
		outs[op] = sinTable[idx] * ampTable[atten]
	}
	s.ym.chans[ch].fb1 = s.ym.chans[ch].fb0
	s.ym.chans[ch].fb0 = outs[0]

	var v float32
	if p.dacOn {
		// DAC sample: unsigned 8-bit data, 0x80 is the center.
		// The data register is read live, not from the prep: a
		// DAC write bumps the generation and re-prepares, but
		// the byte itself is the stream.
		v = float32(int(s.ymRegsA[0x2A])-128) / 128 * 0.75
	} else {
		cm := carrierMask[p.algo]
		for op := 0; op < 4; op++ {
			if cm&(1<<uint(op)) != 0 {
				v += outs[op]
			}
		}
		v *= carrierGain[p.algo]
	}

	if p.pan&0x80 != 0 {
		acc[0] += v
	}
	if p.pan&0x40 != 0 {
		acc[1] += v
	}
}

// ymGenerate renders n native-rate stereo samples, appending
// them to the pending stream in s.fmBuf after any samples already
// rendered there by RenderYMTo (s.preRendered of them). Each sample
// advances genClock by 144 master clocks; rendering in pieces, as
// timestamped writes drive it, produces the same state evolution
// as rendering the whole span at once, with register changes
// landing at their true positions inside the span.
func (s *Sound) ymGenerate(n int) {
	start := s.preRendered
	total := start + n
	need := 2 * total
	if cap(s.fmBuf) < need {
		grown := make([]float32, need)
		copy(grown, s.fmBuf[:2*start])
		s.fmBuf = grown
	}
	s.fmBuf = s.fmBuf[:need]

	lfoReg := s.ymRegsA[0x22]
	lfoOn := lfoReg&0x08 != 0
	lfoInc := lfoIncTab[lfoReg&0x07]

	for i := start; i < total; i++ {
		// Timer time for this native sample (144 master clocks):
		// whatever the system already stepped through
		// AdvanceClocks is consumed from the ledger instead of
		// being stepped again; only the uncovered remainder is
		// stepped here, so total timer time tracks emulated time
		// exactly once no matter who drove it.
		switch {
		case s.ym.advLedger >= 144:
			s.ym.advLedger -= 144
		case s.ym.advLedger > 0:
			s.ymAdvanceTimers(uint32(144 - s.ym.advLedger))
			s.ym.advLedger = 0
		default:
			s.ymAdvanceTimers(144)
		}

		var lfoSigned, lfoTri float64
		if lfoOn {
			s.ym.lfoPhase += lfoInc
			ph := float64(s.ym.lfoPhase) / 4294967296.0
			if ph < 0.5 {
				lfoTri = ph * 2
			} else {
				lfoTri = 2 - ph*2
			}
			lfoSigned = lfoTri*2 - 1
		}

		s.ym.egDiv++
		if s.ym.egDiv >= 3 {
			s.ym.egDiv = 0
			s.ymTickEG()
		}

		var acc [2]float32
		for ch := 0; ch < 6; ch++ {
			s.ymChannel(ch, lfoSigned, lfoTri, lfoOn, &acc)
		}
		s.fmBuf[2*i] = acc[0]
		s.fmBuf[2*i+1] = acc[1]
	}
	s.preRendered = total
	s.ym.genClock += int64(n) * 144
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/sound/ym2612_test.go ====================

package sound

import (
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// ymWriteA writes one bank A register (latch then data).
func ymWriteA(s *Sound, addr, val uint8) {
	s.WriteYM(0, addr)
	s.WriteYM(1, val)
}

// ymWriteB writes one bank B register (latch then data).
func ymWriteB(s *Sound, addr, val uint8) {
	s.WriteYM(2, addr)
	s.WriteYM(3, val)
}

// ymWriteCh writes a channel register on the bank that owns ch.
func ymWriteCh(s *Sound, ch int, addr, val uint8) {
	if ch < 3 {
		ymWriteA(s, addr, val)
	} else {
		ymWriteB(s, addr, val)
	}
}

// ymPatchSine programs one channel as a plain sine: operator 1 only,
// algorithm 7 (independent carriers), total level 0, fastest attack,
// no decay, both output sides on. Other operators stay unkeyed and
// therefore silent whatever their registers hold.
func ymPatchSine(s *Sound, ch, fnum, block int) {
	off := uint8(ch % 3)
	w := func(addr, val uint8) { ymWriteCh(s, ch, addr, val) }
	w(0x30+off, 0x01) // OP1: DT 0, MUL 1
	w(0x40+off, 0x00) // OP1: TL 0
	w(0x50+off, 0x1F) // OP1: KS 0, AR 31
	w(0x60+off, 0x00) // OP1: AM off, D1R 0
	w(0x70+off, 0x00) // OP1: D2R 0
	w(0x80+off, 0x00) // OP1: SL 0, RR 0
	w(0xA0+off, uint8(fnum&0xFF))
	w(0xA4+off, uint8(block<<3|fnum>>8))
	w(0xB0+off, 0x07) // FB 0, algorithm 7
	w(0xB4+off, 0xC0) // L+R on, AMS 0, PMS 0
}

// ymKey writes the key on/off register: slotMask bit s keys the
// operator in register slot s (slot 0 is OP1). ch is 0-based.
func ymKey(s *Sound, ch int, slotMask uint8) {
	sel := ch
	if ch >= 3 {
		sel = ch + 1
	}
	ymWriteA(s, 0x28, slotMask<<4|uint8(sel))
}

// produceAll runs Produce in frame-sized chunks and concatenates.
func produceAll(s *Sound, frames int) []int16 {
	var out []int16
	for frames > 0 {
		n := frames
		if n > 735 {
			n = 735
		}
		out = append(out, s.Produce(n)...)
		frames -= n
	}
	return out
}

func rmsRange(out []int16, from, to int) float64 {
	if from < 0 {
		from = 0
	}
	if to > len(out) {
		to = len(out)
	}
	var sum float64
	for _, v := range out[from:to] {
		sum += float64(v) * float64(v)
	}
	if to <= from {
		return 0
	}
	return math.Sqrt(sum / float64(to-from))
}

func TestYMKeyOnProducesSound(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymPatchSine(s, 0, 1083, 4)
	ymKey(s, 0, 0x1) // OP1 on

	out := s.Produce(735)
	if len(out) != 1470 {
		t.Fatalf("len(Produce(735)) = %d, want 1470", len(out))
	}
	if n := countNonzero(out); n < 1000 {
		t.Fatalf("keyed-on FM channel produced only %d nonzero samples of 1470", n)
	}
}

func TestYMFrequencyA4(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	// F-number 1083, block 4 is 440.1 Hz by the documented
	// frequency formula.
	ymPatchSine(s, 0, 1083, 4)
	ymKey(s, 0, 0x1)

	out := produceAll(s, 15435) // 0.35 s
	// Rising zero crossings of the left channel between 0.10 s
	// and 0.30 s (attack long settled, sustain crawl negligible).
	from, to := 4410*2, 13230*2
	crossings := 0
	for i := from; i+2 < to && i+2 < len(out); i += 2 {
		if out[i] < 0 && out[i+2] >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
	}
	freq := float64(crossings) / 0.20
	if freq < 415 || freq > 465 {
		t.Fatalf("measured %.1f Hz from %d crossings, want about 440", freq, crossings)
	}
}

func TestYMEnvelopeDecay(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymPatchSine(s, 0, 1083, 4)
	// Fast first decay to a deep sustain level: D1R 16, SL 15.
	ymWriteCh(s, 0, 0x60, 0x10)
	ymWriteCh(s, 0, 0x80, 0xF0)
	ymKey(s, 0, 0x1)

	out := produceAll(s, 11025)            // 0.25 s
	early := rmsRange(out, 88*2, 265*2)    // 2-6 ms: still loud
	late := rmsRange(out, 8820*2, 11025*2) // 200-250 ms: decayed away
	if early < 500 {
		t.Fatalf("early RMS = %.1f, want a loud note right after attack", early)
	}
	if late > early*0.05 {
		t.Fatalf("late RMS = %.1f, want under 5%% of early %.1f after decay", late, early)
	}
}

func TestYMKeyOffRelease(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymPatchSine(s, 0, 1083, 4)
	ymWriteCh(s, 0, 0x80, 0x0F) // SL 0, RR 15 (fast release)
	ymKey(s, 0, 0x1)

	out := produceAll(s, 4410) // 0.1 s of sustain
	if got := rmsRange(out, 2205*2, 4410*2); got < 1000 {
		t.Fatalf("sustaining RMS = %.1f, want a loud held note", got)
	}

	ymKey(s, 0, 0x0)           // key off
	out = produceAll(s, 13230) // 0.3 s
	max := 0
	for _, v := range out[11025*2:] { // final 50 ms
		if v < 0 {
			v = -v
		}
		if int(v) > max {
			max = int(v)
		}
	}
	if max > 1 {
		t.Fatalf("max sample after release = %d, want silence (<= 1)", max)
	}
}

func TestYMTimerAFlag(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymWriteA(s, 0x24, 0xFF)
	ymWriteA(s, 0x25, 0xC0) // NA = 1023: period 18 master clocks
	ymWriteA(s, 0x27, 0x05) // load + enable timer A
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag set before any time passed: %#02x", got)
	}
	s.Produce(16)
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag not set after its period: %#02x", got)
	}
	ymWriteA(s, 0x27, 0x10) // reset the flag (drops load bits too)
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag not cleared by the 0x27 reset bit: %#02x", got)
	}

	// A long period must not fire early: NA = 0 is 18432 clocks.
	s2 := New()
	ymWriteA(s2, 0x24, 0x00)
	ymWriteA(s2, 0x25, 0x00)
	ymWriteA(s2, 0x27, 0x05)
	s2.Produce(10) // about 1700 clocks
	if got := s2.ReadYM(); got&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A fired early at period 18432: %#02x", got)
	}
	s2.Produce(200) // about 36,000 clocks total
	if got := s2.ReadYM(); got&0x01 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A never fired at period 18432: %#02x", got)
	}
}

func TestYMAdvanceClocksTimerA(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymWriteA(s, 0x24, 0xFA)
	ymWriteA(s, 0x25, 0x00) // NA = 1000: period 18*24 = 432 master clocks
	ymWriteA(s, 0x27, 0x05) // load + enable timer A
	// No Produce call anywhere: the flag must move on stepped
	// clocks alone, at exactly the accumulated period.
	s.AdvanceClocks(431)
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag set after 431 of 432 clocks: %#02x", got)
	}
	s.AdvanceClocks(1)
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag not set at 432 clocks: %#02x", got)
	}
	ymWriteA(s, 0x27, 0x10) // reset bit still clears it
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag not cleared by the 0x27 reset bit: %#02x", got)
	}
}

func TestYMAdvanceClocksLedger(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymWriteA(s, 0x24, 0xFA)
	ymWriteA(s, 0x25, 0x00) // period 432 master clocks
	ymWriteA(s, 0x27, 0x05) // load + enable timer A
	s.AdvanceClocks(400)
	// One rendered output frame from a fresh chip generates two
	// native samples (288 clocks), all inside the 400 already
	// stepped. If Produce stepped them again the total would be
	// 688 and the flag would be up; it must stay down.
	s.Produce(1)
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag set: Produce double-stepped system time: %#02x", got)
	}

	// The ledger is part of the save state: a chip restored here
	// agrees on the remaining distance to the flag.
	buf := make([]byte, s.SerializeSize())
	if err := s.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	s2 := New()
	if err := s2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	s2.AdvanceClocks(31) // 431 total
	if got := s2.ReadYM(); got&0x01 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("restored chip: timer A flag set after 431 clocks: %#02x", got)
	}
	s.AdvanceClocks(31)
	s.AdvanceClocks(1)
	s2.AdvanceClocks(1)
	if got := s.ReadYM(); got&0x01 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer A flag not set at 432 clocks: %#02x", got)
	}
	if got := s2.ReadYM(); got&0x01 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("restored chip: timer A flag not set at 432 clocks: %#02x", got)
	}
}

func TestYMDACMode(t *testing.T) {

	ymWriteA(s, 0x2B, 0x80) // DAC enable: channel 6 becomes the DAC
	ymWriteB(s, 0xB6, 0xC0) // channel 6 pan: L+R

		}

			t.Fatalf("DAC output not steady: sample %d = %d, sample 200 = %d", i, out[i], out[200])
		}
	}
}

func TestYMDACPanPowerOnDefault(t *testing.T) {

	ymWriteA(s, 0x2B, 0x80) // DAC enable: channel 6 becomes the DAC

	out := s.Produce(400)

// A DAC stream is register writes at audio rate: this drives the
// timestamp seam the bus uses (RenderYMTo, then the write) and
// proves one Produce window holds a genuine step, low byte for
// its true duration then high byte, not the last byte held for
// the whole window and not a blend.
func TestYMDACStreamStep(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymWriteA(s, 0x2B, 0x80) // DAC enable: channel 6 becomes the DAC
	ymWriteA(s, 0x2A, 0x00) // DAC data low: (0-128)/128*0.75 = -0.75

	// A 735-frame Produce spans 888 native samples (127,872
	// clocks). Render half of that span with the low byte in
	// force, then land the high byte, as a stream would.
	s.RenderYMTo(63936)
	ymWriteA(s, 0x2A, 0xFF) // DAC data high: +0.744

	out := s.Produce(735)
	if len(out) != 1470 {
		t.Fatalf("len(Produce(735)) = %d, want 1470", len(out))
	}
	// The step sits at native sample 444, near output frame 368.
	// Average regions well clear of it: frames 10-100 must sit at
	// the low steady value (about -9000 after the mix gain) and
	// frames 635-725 at the high one (about +8929). Frame-end
	// rendering would put both at the high value; a blend would
	// put both near zero.
	mean := func(from, to int) float64 {
		sum := 0.0
		for _, v := range out[from*2 : to*2] {
			sum += float64(v)
		}
		return sum / float64((to-from)*2)
	}
	if got := mean(10, 100); got < -9500 || got > -8500 {
		t.Fatalf("early mean = %.0f, want about -9000 (low byte held for its span)", got)
	}
	if got := mean(635, 725); got < 8400 || got > 9500 {
		t.Fatalf("late mean = %.0f, want about +8929 (high byte after the step)", got)
	}
}

func TestYMSerializeDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	ymPatchSine(s, 0, 1083, 4)
	ymWriteCh(s, 0, 0x60, 0x10) // some decay so the EG is mid-flight
	ymWriteCh(s, 0, 0x80, 0xF0)
	ymKey(s, 0, 0x1)
	s.Produce(1000)

	buf := make([]byte, s.SerializeSize())
	if err := s.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	s2 := New()
	if err := s2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}

	// A state restored and immediately re-serialized is
	// byte-identical to the state that was saved.
	buf2 := make([]byte, s2.SerializeSize())
	if err := s2.Serialize(buf2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("re-Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	for i := range buf {
		if buf[i] != buf2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("re-serialized state differs at byte %d: %02x vs %02x", i, buf[i], buf2[i])
		}
	}

	// And the restored chip produces exactly the samples the
	// original produces from the same point.
	outA := s.Produce(500)
	outB := s2.Produce(500)
	if len(outA) != len(outB) {
		t.Fatalf("post-restore lengths differ: %d vs %d", len(outA), len(outB))
	}
	for i := range outA {
		if outA[i] != outB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("post-restore sample %d differs: %d vs %d", i, outA[i], outB[i])
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/system/sonic_bench_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"hash/fnv"
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// sonicBenchROM is the local probe copy of Sonic 1 used by the
// bridge benchmark in go_backend. It is never committed; every
// entry point here skips when the file is absent.
const sonicBenchROM = "/tmp/sonic_probe.md"

func loadSonicBench(tb testing.TB) *System {
	tb.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(sonicBenchROM)
	if err != nil {
		tb.Skip("sonic probe ROM not present")
	}
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(data); err != nil {
		tb.Fatalf("LoadGame: %v", err)
	}
	return sys
}

// frameHash is a 64-bit FNV-1a over the framebuffer in little
// endian byte order. It is the pixel-stability gate for the
// speed work: optimizations must not change it.
func frameHash(sys *System) uint64 {
	h := fnv.New64a()
	var buf [2]byte
	for _, px := range sys.Framebuffer() {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[:], px)
		h.Write(buf[:])
	}
	return h.Sum64()
}

// TestSonicFrame730Hash records the framebuffer hash after 730
// frames of Sonic 1 from power-on (the long-standing proof gate
// point) and logs it for comparison across optimizations.
func TestSonicFrame730Hash(t *testing.T) {
	sys := loadSonicBench(t)
	for i := 0; i < 730; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		sys.AudioBuffer()
	}
	t.Logf("frame 730 hash: %016x size %dx%d", frameHash(sys), sys.Width(), sys.Height())
}

// BenchmarkSonicFrame mirrors the bridge benchmark: 300 warmup
// frames from power-on, then timed frames, draining audio each
// frame the way the native bridge does.
func BenchmarkSonicFrame(b *testing.B) {
	sys := loadSonicBench(b)
	for i := 0; i < 300; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		sys.AudioBuffer()
	}
	b.ResetTimer()
	for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		sys.AudioBuffer()
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/system/system.go ====================

// Package system wires the parts of the Genesis into a running machine:
// the two CPUs, the bus, the VDP and the sound section, clocked and
// interrupted the way the real hardware does it (NTSC timing).
//
// Timing model: the NTSC master clock is 53,693,175 Hz, divided by 7 for
// the 68000 (7.67 MHz) and by 15 for the Z80 (3.58 MHz). One frame is 3420
// master cycles x 262 lines = 896,040 master cycles (59.92 fps). The CPUs
// run in per-scanline budgets; the VDP renders each visible line after the
// CPUs have run for it, raises the HBlank interrupt during the line
// sequence and the VBlank interrupt (level 6) plus the Z80 interrupt at
// the start of the blanking period.
package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"math"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/scd"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/sound"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/vdp"

	m68k "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/chips/m68k"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/chips/z80"
)

const (
	masterHz      = 53693175
	masterPerLine = 3420
	linesTotal    = 262
	masterFrame   = masterPerLine * linesTotal // 896,040
	z80PerLine    = 228                        // 896,040 / 15 / 262, exact
)

// subFrameCycles is the number of sub CPU cycles in one frame: the
// Sega CD sub CPU runs at 12.5 MHz.
const subFrameCycles = 12500000 * masterFrame / masterHz

// subTarget is the sub CPU cycle count at the end of the given line.
func subTarget(line int) uint64 {
	return uint64(line+1) * subFrameCycles / linesTotal
}

// System is one Genesis console.
type System struct {
	cart  *cart.Cart
	vdp   *vdp.VDP
	sound *sound.Sound
	bus   *bus.Bus
	cpu   *m68k.CPU
	zcpu  *z80.CPU
	cd    *scd.Unit
	scpu  *m68k.CPU
	disc  *scd.Disc

	audio    []int16 // samples produced since the last AudioBuffer call
	audioAcc float64 // fractional samples owed
	frame    uint64  // frames run since power-on (drives cumulative cycle targets)
	loaded   bool

	// Anchors for timestamping Z80 writes to the YM2612 (see the
	// SetYMClock closure in LoadGame): the YM time at the start of
	// the scanline whose Z80 budget is currently running, and the
	// Z80 cycle counter at that moment. Recomputed at every line
	// before any Z80 write can occur, so they never need to be
	// serialized.
	z80LineYM     int64
	z80LineCycles uint64
}

// New returns an empty machine; call LoadGame before RunFrame.
func New() *System { return &System{} }

// LoadGame builds the machine around a cartridge image and powers it on.
// Loading a cartridge powers the machine on fresh: any Sega CD
// attachment is cleared before the new bus is built, and any disc
// must be loaded again afterwards with LoadDisc.
func (s *System) LoadGame(data []byte) error {
	c, err := cart.Load(data)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.cd = nil
	s.scpu = nil
	if s.disc != nil {
		s.disc.Close()
		s.disc = nil
	}
	s.cart = c
	s.vdp = vdp.New()
	s.sound = sound.New()
	s.bus = bus.New(c, s.vdp, s.sound)
	s.cpu = m68k.New(s.bus)
	s.zcpu = z80.New(s.bus)
	// Timestamp source for YM2612 writes, so the sound section
	// can render the pending FM span before a write lands (the
	// bus calls it at the write's emulated moment). The YM2612
	// clock equals the 68000 clock (both master / 7), so a 68000
	// write is stamped with the CPU's own counter, which both
	// CPUs charge after each instruction: a stamp is the time at
	// the start of the executing instruction, instruction
	// granularity (a few cycles, far inside the ~465-clock
	// spacing of a DAC stream). A Z80 write is stamped from the
	// line anchors set in RunFrame: the line's start time plus
	// the Z80 cycles elapsed in the line, converted at the fixed
	// ratio (one Z80 cycle is 15/7 YM clocks; the conversion is
	// computed from the anchor each call, so no fractional
	// remainder ever accumulates). One imprecision is inherent
	// to the frame loop's shape: the 68000 runs a whole line
	// before the Z80 runs its share, so within one scanline a
	// Z80 stamp can fall up to a line (~489 clocks, ~3.4 native
	// samples) behind 68000 time already rendered; the sound
	// section clamps such spans to nothing, and the relative
	// spacing of writes from one CPU, which is what a sample
	// stream is made of, stays exact.
	s.bus.SetYMClock(func(fromZ80 bool) int64 {
		if fromZ80 {
			return s.z80LineYM + int64((s.zcpu.Cycles()-s.z80LineCycles)*15/7)
		}
		return int64(s.cpu.Cycles())
	})
	s.audio = nil
	s.audioAcc = 0
	s.frame = 0
	s.loaded = true
	s.cpu.Reset()  // reads SSP + PC from the cartridge vectors
	s.zcpu.Reset() // held in reset by the bus until the game releases it
	return nil
}

// Loaded reports whether a game is in the machine.
func (s *System) Loaded() bool { return s.loaded }

// LoadDisc opens a disc image and attaches a Sega CD unit. With no
// cartridge loaded, the machine powers on around the built-in main
// stub program so a CD-only boot works; with a cartridge loaded, the
// CD attaches alongside and the cartridge stays in control (it must
// release the sub CPU itself through the gate array, as on hardware).
// Loading a cartridge afterwards clears the attachment, so a disc
// must be loaded again after LoadGame.
func (s *System) LoadDisc(path string) error {
	disc, err := scd.OpenDisc(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !s.loaded {
		if err := s.LoadGame(scd.MainStubROM()); err != nil {
			disc.Close()
			return err
		}
	}
	if s.disc != nil {
		s.disc.Close()
	}
	s.disc = disc
	s.cd = scd.NewUnit(disc)
	s.scpu = m68k.New(s.cd)
	s.bus.AttachCD(s.cd)
	return nil
}

// CDAttached reports whether a Sega CD unit is attached.
func (s *System) CDAttached() bool { return s.cd != nil }

// CDUnit returns the attached Sega CD unit, or nil when detached.
func (s *System) CDUnit() *scd.Unit { return s.cd }

// Reset is the console reset button: the 68000 restarts from its vectors.
// RAM, VRAM and cartridge save RAM survive, as they do on hardware.
func (s *System) Reset() {
	if !s.loaded {
		return
	}
	s.cpu.Reset()
	if s.cd != nil {
		s.cd.ForceSubReset()
	}
}

// Title returns the cartridge's overseas title, for logs and UIs.
func (s *System) Title() string {
	if s.cart == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return s.cart.Title
}

// SetButtons records pad state for a player, in bus.Pad* bit layout.
func (s *System) SetButtons(player int, mask uint16) {
	if s.loaded {
		s.bus.SetPad(player, mask)
	}
}

// Framebuffer returns the VDP's RGB565 frame (stride vdp.MaxWidth).
func (s *System) Framebuffer() []uint16 {
	if !s.loaded {
		return nil
	}
	return s.vdp.Framebuffer()
}

// Width is the current display width in pixels (256 or 320).
func (s *System) Width() int {
	if !s.loaded {
		return 320
	}
	return s.vdp.DisplayWidth()
}

// Height is the current display height in pixels (224 or 240).
func (s *System) Height() int {
	if !s.loaded {
		return 224
	}
	return s.vdp.DisplayHeight()
}

// SystemRAM exposes the 64KB work RAM (libretro memory interface).
func (s *System) SystemRAM() []uint8 {
	if !s.loaded {
		return nil
	}
	return s.bus.RAM[:]
}

// SaveRAM exposes the cartridge save RAM, if the cartridge has any.
func (s *System) SaveRAM() []uint8 {
	if !s.loaded {
		return nil
	}
	return s.bus.SRAM
}

// SoundWrites reports how many PSG and YM2612 register writes the game
// has made (diagnostics; see sound.WriteCounts).
func (s *System) SoundWrites() (psg, ym int) {
	if !s.loaded {
		return 0, 0
	}
	return s.sound.WriteCounts()
}

// AudioBuffer drains the samples produced by the last RunFrame.
func (s *System) AudioBuffer() []int16 {
	out := s.audio
	s.audio = nil
	return out
}

// m68kTarget is the 68000 cycle count at the end of the given line.
func m68kTarget(line int) uint64 {
	return uint64(line+1) * masterFrame / 7 / linesTotal
}

// run68k advances the 68000 toward target cycles. A CPU parked in STOP
// makes no progress; it wakes when an interrupt lands at a line boundary.
func (s *System) run68k(target uint64) {
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		cur := s.cpu.Cycles()
		if cur >= target {
			return
		}
		s.cpu.StepCycles(int(target - cur))
		if s.cpu.Cycles() == cur {
			return
		}
	}
}

// runSubLine advances the Sega CD sub CPU by one scanline of cycles,
// honoring the gate array reset and halt lines the main CPU controls.
func (s *System) runSubLine(line int) {
	if s.cd == nil {
		return
	}
	if s.cd.TakeSubReset() {
		s.scpu.Reset()
	}
	if s.cd.SubHalted() {
		return
	}
	base := s.frame * subFrameCycles
	target := base + subTarget(line)
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		cur := s.scpu.Cycles()
		if cur >= target {
			break
		}
		s.scpu.StepCycles(int(target - cur))
		if s.scpu.Cycles() == cur {
			break
		}
	}
	// SCD-4: service any sub BIOS request the stepping above
	// queued (see scd BIOSPending and BIOSService). The service
	// runs once per line, after the sub CPU has had its cycles.
	s.cd.BIOSService()
}

// runZ80Line advances the Z80 by one scanline of cycles, honoring the
// bus-request and reset lines the 68000 controls. lineStartYM is the
// scanline's start time in YM2612 clocks; it and the Z80 counter at
// entry anchor the timestamps of any YM2612 writes the Z80 makes
// during the line (see the SetYMClock closure in LoadGame).
func (s *System) runZ80Line(lineStartYM int64) {
	if s.bus.TakeZ80Reset() {
		s.zcpu.Reset()
	}
	s.z80LineYM = lineStartYM
	s.z80LineCycles = s.zcpu.Cycles()
	if s.bus.Z80Halted() {
		return
	}
	target := s.zcpu.Cycles() + z80PerLine
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		cur := s.zcpu.Cycles()
		if cur >= target {
			return
		}
		s.zcpu.StepCycles(int(target - cur))
		if s.zcpu.Cycles() == cur {
			return
		}
	}
}

// RunFrame runs one whole video frame: 262 scanlines of CPU time, VDP
// rendering and interrupts, then produces the frame's audio.
func (s *System) RunFrame() {
	if !s.loaded {
		return
	}
	h := s.vdp.DisplayHeight()
	// The CPU cycle counter is cumulative since power-on, so line targets
	// must be too: base this frame's targets on the frames already run.
	base := s.frame * masterFrame / 7
	s.vdp.BeginFrame()
	// clocked is the cumulative 68000-cycle target the YM2612
	// timers have been advanced to. The YM2612 clock equals the
	// 68000 clock (both master / 7), so line-target deltas are YM
	// master clocks one to one. Advancing at each line boundary
	// lets a CPU polling the YM status port see timer flags flip
	// mid-frame; Produce accounts for the stepped time through the
	// sound section's ledger and never steps it twice. The deltas
	// depend only on the line number, not the frame base, so a
	// restored machine replays the exact same advance sequence.
	clocked := base
	for line := 0; line < linesTotal; line++ {
		if line == 0 {
			s.vdp.ExitVBlank()
			s.zcpu.INT(false, 0)
		}
		s.run68k(base + m68kTarget(line))
		// The line starts, in 68000 (and YM2612) cycles, at the
		// previous line's cumulative target.
		s.runZ80Line(int64(base + uint64(line)*masterFrame/7/linesTotal))
		s.runSubLine(line)
		if s.cd != nil {
			// Advance the CD block (CDD 75 Hz tick, CD-DA and data
			// read progression) by this line's sub CPU cycle budget.
			// The delta depends only on the line number, so a
			// restored machine replays the exact same advance
			// sequence. Completed CDD commands raise level 4 on
			// the sub CPU and completed CDC transfers level 5,
			// each gated by its gate array interrupt mask bit.
			delta := subTarget(line)
			if line > 0 {
				delta -= subTarget(line - 1)
			}
			s.cd.AdvanceCycles(int(delta))
			if s.cd.TakeCDDInterrupt() {
				s.scpu.RequestInterrupt(4, nil)
			}
			if s.cd.TakeCDCInterrupt() {
				s.scpu.RequestInterrupt(5, nil)
			}
			if fire, vec := s.cd.LineTick(line); fire {
				s.cpu.RequestInterrupt(2, vec)
			}
		}
		target := base + m68kTarget(line)
		s.sound.AdvanceClocks(uint32(target - clocked))
		clocked = target
		if line < h {
			if s.vdp.LineIRQ(line) {
				s.cpu.RequestInterrupt(4, nil)
			}
			s.vdp.RenderLine(line)
		}
		if line == h {
			if s.vdp.EnterVBlank() {
				s.cpu.RequestInterrupt(6, nil)
			}
			s.zcpu.INT(true, 0xFF)
		}
	}
	s.frame++
	// 44,100 Hz at 59.92 fps is ~735.9 samples per frame; carry the fraction.
	s.audioAcc += float64(sound.SampleRate) * masterFrame / masterHz
	n := int(s.audioAcc)
	s.audioAcc -= float64(n)
	gen := s.sound.Produce(n)
	if s.cd != nil {
		// Mix the Sega CD audio (CD-DA through the fader plus the
		// RF5C164 PCM mix, both already at the machine rate) into
		// the Genesis output with saturation.
		cdAudio := s.cd.RenderAudio(n)
		for i := range gen {
			if i >= len(cdAudio) {
				break
			}
			v := int32(gen[i]) + int32(cdAudio[i])
			if v > 32767 {
				v = 32767
			} else if v < -32768 {
				v = -32768
			}
			gen[i] = int16(v)
		}
	}
	s.audio = append(s.audio, gen...)
}

// --- save states ---------------------------------------------------------

const m68kStateSize = 80 // D[8]+A[8] u32, PC u32, SR u16, USP u32, SSP u32, IR u16

// trailerSize holds the machine-level bookkeeping appended after the
// component states: frame counter (u64), 68000 cycle counter (u64) and
// the audio fraction accumulator (f64 bits). The cycle counter MUST be
// saved: the CPU's SetState zeroes it, and this system's frame
// timing is derived from it, so losing it fast-forwards the machine on
// the first frame after a restore.
const trailerSize = 24

// writeM68kState writes one 68000 register snapshot (m68kStateSize
// bytes) into buf.
func writeM68kState(buf []byte, cpu *m68k.CPU) {
	off := 0
	r := cpu.Registers()
	// The CPU's SetState ignores the A[7] slot and derives the
	// active stack pointer from SSP (supervisor) or USP (user) instead,
	// while its Registers() can report a stale SSP/USP next to the live
	// A[7]. Fold the live A[7] into whichever stack pointer is active so
	// a restore lands on the exact stack the game was using. (Genesis
	// games always run in supervisor mode.)
	if r.SR&0x2000 != 0 {
		r.SSP = r.A[7]
	} else {
		r.USP = r.A[7]
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off:], r.D[i])
		off += 4
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off:], r.A[i])
		off += 4
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off:], r.PC)
	off += 4
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[off:], r.SR)
	off += 2
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off:], r.USP)
	off += 4
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[off:], r.SSP)
	off += 4
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[off:], r.IR)
}

// readM68kState parses one 68000 register snapshot from buf and
// installs it into cpu.
func readM68kState(buf []byte, cpu *m68k.CPU) {
	off := 0
	var r m68k.Registers
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		r.D[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off:])
		off += 4
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		r.A[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off:])
		off += 4
	}
	r.PC = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off:])
	off += 4
	r.SR = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[off:])
	off += 2
	r.USP = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off:])
	off += 4
	r.SSP = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(buf[off:])
	off += 4
	r.IR = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[off:])
	cpu.SetState(r)
}

// SerializeSize is the total save-state size in bytes.
//
// Versioning choice: the cartridge-only layout is unchanged and old
// cartridge states still load in cartridge mode; CD states carry an
// appended CD section and loading one requires the CD attached (a
// cartridge-sized buffer in CD mode fails the existing size check).
func (s *System) SerializeSize() int {
	if !s.loaded {
		return 0
	}
	n := m68kStateSize + z80.SerializeSize +
		s.bus.SerializeSize() + s.vdp.SerializeSize() + s.sound.SerializeSize() +
		trailerSize
	if s.cd != nil {
		n += m68kStateSize + s.cd.SerializeSize() + 8
	}
	return n
}

// Serialize writes the full machine state into buf.
//
// Note: a pending-but-unserviced 68000 interrupt is not part of the CPU
// library's register snapshot. Interrupts re-fire every frame (VBlank) or
// are re-requested by the game, so a restore at worst shifts one interrupt
// by a frame.
func (s *System) Serialize(buf []byte) error {
	if !s.loaded {
		return errors.New("system: no game loaded")
	}
	if len(buf) < s.SerializeSize() {
		return errors.New("system: serialize buffer too small")
	}
	off := 0
	writeM68kState(buf[off:], s.cpu)
	off += m68kStateSize

	if err := s.zcpu.Serialize(buf[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += z80.SerializeSize
	if err := s.bus.Serialize(buf[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += s.bus.SerializeSize()
	if err := s.vdp.Serialize(buf[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += s.vdp.SerializeSize()
	if err := s.sound.Serialize(buf[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += s.sound.SerializeSize()
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[off:], s.frame)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[off+8:], s.cpu.Cycles())
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[off+16:], math.Float64bits(s.audioAcc))
	off += trailerSize
	if s.cd != nil {
		writeM68kState(buf[off:], s.scpu)
		off += m68kStateSize
		if err := s.cd.Serialize(buf[off:]); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		off += s.cd.SerializeSize()
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(buf[off:], s.scpu.Cycles())
	}
	return nil
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
//
// SCD-4 legacy rule: a CD state written before the sub BIOS
// sections existed is exactly scd.BRAMSize + scd.BIOSStateSize
// bytes shorter than a current CD state. When a disc is
// attached and the buffer has exactly that legacy length, the
// missing sections are treated as zero: the state is expanded
// with zero bytes and the normal path runs. The state format
// carries no mode flag byte; the attachment plus the exact
// legacy length identifies a legacy CD state (no cartridge
// state has this length). The expansion inserts the zeros at the
// end of the CD unit block, which is where Serialize appends the
// unit growth; the unit block is not quite the end of the whole
// state, because the 8 byte sub CPU cycle trailer follows it, so
// a plain append at the end of the buffer would misalign both
// the unit block and the trailer. Every other length mismatch
// keeps failing exactly as before.
func (s *System) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if !s.loaded {
		return errors.New("system: no game loaded")
	}
	data := buf
	if s.cd != nil && len(buf) == s.SerializeSize()-(scd.BRAMSize+scd.BIOSStateSize) {
		expanded := make([]byte, 0, s.SerializeSize())
		insertAt := len(buf) - 8 // end of the CD unit block, before the cycle trailer
		expanded = append(expanded, buf[:insertAt]...)
		expanded = append(expanded, make([]byte, scd.BRAMSize+scd.BIOSStateSize)...)
		expanded = append(expanded, buf[insertAt:]...)
		data = expanded
	}
	if len(data) < s.SerializeSize() {
		return errors.New("system: state too small")
	}
	off := 0
	readM68kState(data[off:], s.cpu)
	off += m68kStateSize

	if err := s.zcpu.Deserialize(data[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += z80.SerializeSize
	if err := s.bus.Deserialize(data[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += s.bus.SerializeSize()
	if err := s.vdp.Deserialize(data[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += s.vdp.SerializeSize()
	if err := s.sound.Deserialize(data[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += s.sound.SerializeSize()
	s.frame = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(data[off:])
	// SetState zeroed the CPU's cycle counter; put it back so the frame
	// timing base and the counter agree again.
	s.cpu.AddCycles(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(data[off+8:]))
	s.audioAcc = math.Float64frombits(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(data[off+16:]))
	off += trailerSize
	if s.cd != nil {
		readM68kState(data[off:], s.scpu)
		off += m68kStateSize
		if err := s.cd.Deserialize(data[off:]); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		off += s.cd.SerializeSize()
		s.scpu.AddCycles(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(data[off:]))
	}
	return nil
}

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SCD-2 system gates: main CPU CD windows through the real bus, and
// the save/restore audio determinism gate.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// TestCDWindowsRequireAttachment proves the CD windows in cartridge
// space (0x200000 Word RAM, 0x420000 PRG-RAM bank, 0x600000 Word RAM)
// stay inert when no CD is attached, so cartridge behavior is
// untouched.
func TestCDWindowsRequireAttachment(t *testing.T) {
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(ymTimerROM(0x05)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame: %v", err)
	}
	if got := sys.bus.Read8(0x420000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("bus read 0x420000 without CD = %#04x, want 0xFF (open bus)", got)
	}
	if got := sys.bus.Read8(0x600000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("bus read 0x600000 without CD = %#04x, want 0xFF (open bus)", got)
	}
	// 0x200000 without a CD is cartridge space: the timer ROM is
	// small, so this reads the ROM mirror/open value, never a CD
	// window. The ROM's own read path must not be disturbed; just
	// assert the machine still runs its program.
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(sys.SystemRAM()[0:4]); got != ymTimerMagic {
		t.Fatalf("RAM magic = %#08x, want %#08x", got, ymTimerMagic)
	}
}

// TestCDMainWindowsAndBanking drives the SCD-2 main CPU windows
// through the real Genesis bus: Word RAM at 0x200000 and its 2M
// alias at 0x600000, and the banked, write-protected PRG-RAM window
// at 0x420000.
func TestCDMainWindowsAndBanking(t *testing.T) {
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadDisc(makeSCDISO(t, cdTestIP)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	u := sys.CDUnit()

	// Word RAM starts owned by the sub CPU in 2M mode: the main
	// window reads open bus (0xFF) and writes are dropped.
	if got := sys.bus.Read8(0x201000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("main Word RAM read while sub owns = %#04x, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	sys.bus.Write8(0x201000, 0x77)
	if got := u.WordRAM()[0x1000]; got != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("main Word RAM write while sub owns landed: %#04x", got)
	}

	// The sub CPU hands Word RAM to the main CPU (DMNA).
	u.Write8(0xFF8002, 0x02)
	sys.bus.Write8(0x201000, 0x77)
	if got := u.WordRAM()[0x1000]; got != 0x77 {
		t.Fatalf("WordRAM[0x1000] = %#04x, want 0x77 written through the main window", got)
	}
	if got := sys.bus.Read8(0x201000); got != 0x77 {
		t.Fatalf("main Word RAM readback = %#04x, want 0x77", got)
	}
	// The 2M alias at 0x600000 shows the same byte.
	if got := sys.bus.Read8(0x601000); got != 0x77 {
		t.Fatalf("2M alias read = %#04x, want 0x77", got)
	}
	sys.bus.Write8(0x601001, 0x88)
	if got := u.WordRAM()[0x1001]; got != 0x88 {
		t.Fatalf("WordRAM[0x1001] = %#04x, want 0x88 written through the 2M alias", got)
	}

	// PRG-RAM bank window at 0x420000: default bank 0.
	sys.bus.Write8(0x420100, 0xB0)
	if got := u.PRGRAM()[0x100]; got != 0xB0 {
		t.Fatalf("PRGRAM[0x100] = %#04x, want 0xB0 (bank 0 window write)", got)
	}
	// Select bank 2 (memory mode bits 7:6 = 2) and write a
	// different byte at the same window offset.
	sys.bus.Write8(0xA12002, 0x80)
	sys.bus.Write8(0x420100, 0xB2)
	if got := u.PRGRAM()[0x40100]; got != 0xB2 {
		t.Fatalf("PRGRAM[0x40100] = %#04x, want 0xB2 (bank 2 window write)", got)
	}
	if got := u.PRGRAM()[0x100]; got != 0xB0 {
		t.Fatalf("PRGRAM[0x100] = %#04x, want 0xB0 undisturbed by the bank 2 write", got)
	}
	// Back to bank 0: the window shows the bank 0 byte again.
	sys.bus.Write8(0xA12002, 0x00)
	if got := sys.bus.Read8(0x420100); got != 0xB0 {
		t.Fatalf("bank 0 window readback = %#04x, want 0xB0", got)
	}

	// Write protection: WP field 2 (bits 4:2 of the memory mode
	// byte as written by the main CPU) protects the first 128 KB
	// of physical PRG-RAM against main window writes.
	sys.bus.Write8(0xA12002, 0x08) // bank 0, WP = 2
	sys.bus.Write8(0x420100, 0xEE)
	if got := u.PRGRAM()[0x100]; got != 0xB0 {
		t.Fatalf("protected write landed: PRGRAM[0x100] = %#04x, want 0xB0", got)
	}
	// Bank 1 offset 0x100 is physical 0x20100, outside the
	// protected region: the write lands.
	sys.bus.Write8(0xA12002, 0x48) // bank 1, WP = 2
	sys.bus.Write8(0x420100, 0xB1)
	if got := u.PRGRAM()[0x20100]; got != 0xB1 {
		t.Fatalf("PRGRAM[0x20100] = %#04x, want 0xB1 (unprotected bank 1 write)", got)
	}
	// Clearing WP lets the bank 0 write through.
	sys.bus.Write8(0xA12002, 0x00)
	sys.bus.Write8(0x420100, 0xEE)
	if got := u.PRGRAM()[0x100]; got != 0xEE {
		t.Fatalf("PRGRAM[0x100] = %#04x, want 0xEE after WP cleared", got)
	}
}

// cdAudioIP is the SCD-2 determinism gate's initial program. It
// fills PCM wave RAM bank 0 with one square period (128 bytes of
// +126, 128 bytes of -126, then 32 loop markers), programs PCM
// channel 0 (ENV and PAN full, FD = 0x0800, start 0), turns the
// chip and the channel on, issues a CDD PLAY for the audio track
// starting at LBA 2 (MSF 00:02:02) through the TC nibble registers
// with a valid checksum, publishes the boot magic 0x600D as comm
// status 0, and idles. Encodings follow the absolute long forms
// used by the other hand-assembled test programs in this repo.
var cdAudioIP = []byte{
	0x41, 0xF9, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x10, 0x00, // lea $FF1000, a0 (wave window)
	0x70, 0xFE, // moveq #-2, d0 (byte 0xFE = +126 sign-magnitude)
	0x32, 0x3C, 0x00, 0x7F, // move.w #127, d1
	0x10, 0xC0, // fillA: move.b d0, (a0)+
	0x51, 0xC9, 0xFF, 0xFC, // dbra d1, fillA
	0x70, 0x7E, // moveq #126, d0 (byte 0x7E = -126)
	0x32, 0x3C, 0x00, 0x7F, // move.w #127, d1
	0x10, 0xC0, // fillB: move.b d0, (a0)+
	0x51, 0xC9, 0xFF, 0xFC, // dbra d1, fillB
	0x70, 0xFF, // moveq #-1, d0 (0xFF loop markers)
	0x32, 0x3C, 0x00, 0x1F, // move.w #31, d1
	0x10, 0xC0, // fillC: move.b d0, (a0)+
	0x51, 0xC9, 0xFF, 0xFC, // dbra d1, fillC
	// PCM channel 0 setup. CTRL first: 0xC0 = chip on, MOD = 1,
	// channel 0 selected.
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0xC0, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x07, // move.b #$C0, $FF0007
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00, // ENV = 0xFF
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x01, // PAN = 0xFF
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x02, // FD.L = 0x00
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x08, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x03, // FD.H = 0x08 (FD = 0x0800)
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x06, // ST = 0 (retrigger)
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x08, // ON/OFF: channel 0 on
	// CDD PLAY at MSF 00:02:02: TC nibbles 0,3, 0,0, 0,2, 0,2, 0,
	// checksum 8 (nibbles sum to 7, checksum is the complement).
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x42, // TC0 = 0
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x03, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x43, // TC1 = 3 (PLAY)
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x44, // TC2 = 0
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x45, // TC3 = 0
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x46, // TC4 = 0
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x47, // TC5 = 2
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x48, // TC6 = 0
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x49, // TC7 = 2
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x4A, // TC8 = 0
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x08, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x4B, // TC9 = 8 (checksum)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x60, 0x0D, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x20, // comm status 0 = 0x600D
	0x60, 0xFE, // idle: bra idle
}

// makeCDAudioCue builds a three track cue/bin fixture: track 1 is
// two MODE1/2352 data sectors (boot header + the IP), track 2 is
// 150 audio sectors of a 440 Hz sine, track 3 is 150 audio sectors
// of an 880 Hz sine. It returns the cue path.
func makeCDAudioCue(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	bin := make([]byte, 0, 302*2352)

	// Track 1, sector 0: raw MODE1/2352 sector whose user area
	// (bytes 16..2064) is the boot header.
	sec0 := make([]byte, 2352)
	user := sec0[16:2064]
	copy(user, "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(user[0x30:], 1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(user[0x34:], uint32(len(cdAudioIP)))
	bin = append(bin, sec0...)
	// Track 1, sector 1: the IP in the user area.
	sec1 := make([]byte, 2352)
	copy(sec1[16:2064], cdAudioIP)
	bin = append(bin, sec1...)

	// Audio tracks: stereo sine, same value on both channels.
	sine := func(freq float64, sectors int) {
		for s := 0; s < sectors; s++ {
			sec := make([]byte, 2352)
			for f := 0; f < 588; f++ {
				idx := s*588 + f
				v := int16(10000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*freq*float64(idx)/44100))
				binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[f*4:], uint16(v))
				binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[f*4+2:], uint16(v))
			}
			bin = append(bin, sec...)
		}
	}
	sine(440, 150)
	sine(880, 150)

	binPath := filepath.Join(dir, "audio.bin")
	if err := os.WriteFile(binPath, bin, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write bin: %v", err)
	}
	cue := "FILE \"audio.bin\" BINARY\n" +
		"  TRACK 01 MODE1/2352\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 00:02:00\n" +
		"  TRACK 02 AUDIO\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 00:02:02\n" +
		"  TRACK 03 AUDIO\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 00:04:02\n"
	cuePath := filepath.Join(dir, "audio.cue")
	if err := os.WriteFile(cuePath, []byte(cue), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write cue: %v", err)
	}
	return cuePath
}

// TestCDAudioDeterminism is the SCD-2 determinism gate: the IP
// starts a PCM channel and a CD-DA track, the machine is saved
// mid-playback, and a restored machine must continue with
// byte-identical state and sample-identical audio.
func TestCDAudioDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	cue := makeCDAudioCue(t)

	a := New()
	if err := a.LoadDisc(cue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc A: %v", err)
	}
	// Boot and let the IP set up PCM + CD-DA, then play for a
	// while before saving.
	for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
		a.RunFrame()
	}
	_ = a.AudioBuffer() // drain pre-save audio
	u := a.CDUnit()
	if !u.CDDPlaying() {
		t.Fatalf("CDD is not playing after IP PLAY command (state %d)", u.CDDState())
	}
	posAtSave := u.CDDPositionLBA()
	if posAtSave <= 2 {
		t.Fatalf("CDD position LBA = %d, want past the track 2 start (2)", posAtSave)
	}
	sA := make([]byte, a.SerializeSize())
	if err := a.Serialize(sA); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize A: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		a.RunFrame()
	}
	audioA := a.AudioBuffer()
	sA2 := make([]byte, a.SerializeSize())
	if err := a.Serialize(sA2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize A2: %v", err)
	}

	// The mixed audio must actually contain signal (CD-DA sine
	// plus the PCM square), not silence.
	nonzero := 0
	for _, s := range audioA {
		if s != 0 {
			nonzero++
		}
	}
	if nonzero < len(audioA)/4 {
		t.Fatalf("only %d of %d continuation samples are nonzero, want real CD audio in the mix", nonzero, len(audioA))
	}

	b := New()
	if err := b.LoadDisc(cue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc B: %v", err)
	}
	if err := b.Deserialize(sA); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize B: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	audioB := b.AudioBuffer()
	sB2 := make([]byte, b.SerializeSize())
	if err := b.Serialize(sB2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize B2: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(sA2, sB2) {
		t.Fatal("state after restore plus 30 frames differs from the unrestored run")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(int16sToBytes(audioA), int16sToBytes(audioB)) {
		t.Fatal("continuation audio after restore differs from the unrestored run")
	}
	t.Logf("continuation audio: %d samples compared byte for byte, CDD position at save = LBA %d", len(audioA), posAtSave)
}

func int16sToBytes(in []int16) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 2*len(in))
	for i, v := range in {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[2*i:], uint16(v))
	}
	return out
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/system/system_cd3_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SCD-3 system gate: a hand-assembled sub CPU initial program
// builds a stamp scene in Word RAM, programs the graphics ASIC
// through its register page, traces a 16x16 identity scene into
// the image buffer, checksums the buffer into the comm registers,
// and completes the comm handshake with the main stub. A save
// taken after the trace restores and continues byte-identically.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// cdASICIP is loaded to sub address 0x026000 by the boot stub.
// It fills stamp 1 (Word RAM bytes 128..255) with byte values
// 0..127 (so stamped byte k holds value k), sets stamp map entry
// (0,0) to stamp 1, builds a 16 line identity trace table at
// Word RAM 0x2000 (start (0, line), dot delta 1.0), programs the
// ASIC (map at 0x1000, buffer at 0x4000, 16x16 dots), triggers
// the draw, polls GRON clear, checksums the 128 buffer bytes
// (0+1+...+127 = 0x1FC0) into comm status 1, publishes the done
// magic as comm status 0, then stores the main CPU ack (comm
// status 1 XOR 0xFFFF = 0xE03F) at PRG-RAM 0x020500, sets sub
// flag 2 and idles.
var cdASICIP = []byte{
	0x41, 0xF9, 0x00, 0x20, 0x01, 0x00, // lea $200100, a0
	0x30, 0x3C, 0x00, 0x7F, // move.w #$7F, d0
	0x11, 0x00, // fill: move.b d0, -(a0)
	0x51, 0xC8, 0xFF, 0xFC, // dbra d0, fill
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x20, 0x10, 0x00, // move.w #1, $201000
	0x41, 0xF9, 0x00, 0x20, 0x20, 0x00, // lea $202000, a0
	0x70, 0x00, // moveq #0, d0
	0x72, 0x00, // moveq #0, d1
	0x34, 0x3C, 0x00, 0x0F, // move.w #15, d2
	0x30, 0xC0, // tloop: move.w d0, (a0)+  (start X)
	0x30, 0xC1, // move.w d1, (a0)+          (start Y)
	0x30, 0xFC, 0x08, 0x00, // move.w #$0800, (a0)+ (delta X = 1.0)
	0x30, 0xC0, // move.w d0, (a0)+          (delta Y = 0)
	0x06, 0x41, 0x00, 0x08, // addi.w #8, d1
	0x51, 0xCA, 0xFF, 0xF0, // dbra d2, tloop
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x58, // move.w #0, $FF8058 (stamp ctl)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x5A, // move.w #$400, $FF805A (map base)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x5C, // move.w #1, $FF805C (vcell)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x10, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x5E, // move.w #$1000, $FF805E (img start)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x60, // move.w #0, $FF8060 (offset)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x62, // move.w #16, $FF8062 (h dots)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x64, // move.w #16, $FF8064 (v dots)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x08, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x66, // move.w #$800, $FF8066 (trace base: starts)
	0x10, 0x39, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x58, // poll: move.b $FF8058, d0 (GRON)
	0x4A, 0x00, // tst.b d0
	0x66, 0xF6, // bne.b poll
	0x41, 0xF9, 0x00, 0x20, 0x40, 0x00, // lea $204000, a0
	0x74, 0x00, // moveq #0, d2
	0x76, 0x00, // moveq #0, d3 (byte accumulator: high byte must start 0)
	0x32, 0x3C, 0x00, 0x7F, // move.w #$7F, d1
	0x16, 0x18, // csum: move.b (a0)+, d3
	0xD4, 0x43, // add.w d3, d2
	0x51, 0xC9, 0xFF, 0xFA, // dbra d1, csum
	0x33, 0xC2, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x22, // move.w d2, $FF8022 (comm status 1)
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x60, 0x0D, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x20, // move.w #$600D, $FF8020
	0x10, 0x39, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x0E, // wait: move.b $FF800E, d0
	0x0C, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, // cmpi.b #1, d0
	0x66, 0x00, 0xFF, 0xF4, // bne.w wait
	0x30, 0x39, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x10, // move.w $FF8010, d0
	0x33, 0xC0, 0x00, 0x02, 0x05, 0x00, // move.w d0, $020500
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x0F, // move.b #2, $FF800F
	0x60, 0xFE, // idle: bra idle
}

func TestCDASICTrace(t *testing.T) {
	iso := makeSCDISO(t, cdASICIP)

	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadDisc(iso); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if got, want := sys.SerializeSize(), 1070469; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("CD mode SerializeSize = %d, want %d (SCD-4 size: SCD-3 size plus BRAM and BIOS sections)", got, want)
	}
	if !runUntilSubDone(sys, 180) {
		t.Fatalf("sub flag = %#02x after 180 frames, want 2 (ASIC handshake never completed)", sys.CDUnit().SubFlag())
	}
	u := sys.CDUnit()

	// The image buffer holds the stamp bytes exactly (the 16x16
	// identity trace with matching buffer geometry copies them).
	for i := 0; i < 128; i++ {
		if got := u.WordRAM()[0x4000+i]; got != byte(i) {
			t.Fatalf("image buffer byte %d = %#02x, want %#02x", i, got, byte(i))
		}
	}
	// The sub CPU checksummed the buffer and published it; the
	// main stub answered with its inverse in comm command 0, and
	// the IP stored that ack in PRG-RAM.
	if got := u.CommStatus(1); got != 0x1FC0 {
		t.Fatalf("comm status 1 = %#06x, want 0x1FC0 (buffer checksum)", got)
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(u.PRGRAM()[0x500:0x502]); got != 0xE03F {
		t.Fatalf("ack cell = %#06x, want 0xE03F (checksum XOR 0xFFFF)", got)
	}
	if u.ASICBusy() {
		t.Fatal("ASIC busy after the completed trace")
	}
	if got := u.ASICLinesRemaining(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ASIC lines remaining = %d, want 0", got)
	}

	// Save after the trace, restore into a fresh machine, and
	// the continuation is byte-identical.
	sA := make([]byte, sys.SerializeSize())
	if err := sys.Serialize(sA); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize A: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 15; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
	}
	sA2 := make([]byte, sys.SerializeSize())
	if err := sys.Serialize(sA2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize A2: %v", err)
	}
	b := New()
	if err := b.LoadDisc(iso); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc B: %v", err)
	}
	if err := b.Deserialize(sA); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize B: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 15; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	sB2 := make([]byte, b.SerializeSize())
	if err := b.Serialize(sB2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize B2: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(sA2, sB2) {
		t.Fatal("state after restore plus 15 frames differs from the unrestored run")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/system/system_cd4_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/scd"
)

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SCD-4 system gate: the full-stack enginetest. A custom Genesis
// ROM (built below) releases the sub CPU; the sub CPU boot stub
// loads the test IP from a synthetic cue/bin disc; the IP drives
// the sub BIOS services (_cdbios at $5F22, _buram at $5F16) through
// their published stages: DRVINIT and TOC reads, MSCPLAY plus
// CDBSTAT, a raw-register RF5C164 tone, the ROMREADN sector read
// flow, backup RAM format/write/search/read/delete, and the
// SCD-3 ASIC identity trace, then hands Word RAM to the main CPU,
// which programs the VDP, copies the traced image buffer into
// VRAM tiles plus a 16x16 cell tile map, and checksums the VRAM
// readback into comm command 1. The Go side asserts the stage
// bitmap, the checksums, the rendered frame, both audio tones,
// save/restore determinism at 45 frames, and legacy CD state
// acceptance.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Branch condition codes for the assembler below.
const (
	cd4BRA = 0
	cd4BHI = 2
	cd4BCC = 4
	cd4BCS = 5
	cd4BNE = 6
	cd4BEQ = 7
	cd4BGE = 12
	cd4BLT = 13
	cd4BGT = 14
	cd4BLE = 15
)

// MOVE size codes (bits 13-12 of the opcode word).
const (
	cd4SizeB = 1
	cd4SizeW = 3
	cd4SizeL = 2
)

// cd4Fixup is one pending patch: a word branch displacement or a
// 32 bit absolute address.
type cd4Fixup struct {
	pos   int
	label string
	abs32 bool
}

// cd4asm is a small two-pass 68000 assembler local to this test
// file, in the spirit of the scd package assembler: labels,
// branches, and the MOVE and JSR forms the two test programs
// need. Addresses are absolute: the assembler is created with the
// address its first byte will run at.
type cd4asm struct {
	base   int
	buf    []byte
	labels map[string]int
	fixups []cd4Fixup
}

func newCD4Asm(base int) *cd4asm {
	return &cd4asm{base: base, labels: make(map[string]int)}
}

func (a *cd4asm) mark(name string) { a.labels[name] = a.base + len(a.buf) }

func (a *cd4asm) emit16(v uint16) {
	a.buf = append(a.buf, byte(v>>8), byte(v))
}
