func (a *cd4asm) emit32(v uint32) {
	a.buf = append(a.buf, byte(v>>24), byte(v>>16), byte(v>>8), byte(v))
}

func (a *cd4asm) emitBytes(b []byte) { a.buf = append(a.buf, b...) }

func (a *cd4asm) finish() []byte {
	for _, f := range a.fixups {
		target, ok := a.labels[f.label]
		if !ok {
			panic("cd4asm: fixup to unknown label " + f.label)
		}
		if f.abs32 {
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(a.buf[f.pos:f.pos+4], uint32(target))
			continue
		}
		disp := target - (a.base + f.pos)
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(a.buf[f.pos:f.pos+2], uint16(int16(disp)))
	}
	return a.buf
}

// move emits a generic MOVE: opcode size bits, destination reg
// and mode, source mode and reg, then the source extension words
// followed by the destination extension words.
func (a *cd4asm) move(size, srcMode, srcReg int, srcExt []uint16, dstReg, dstMode int, dstExt []uint16) {
	a.emit16(uint16(size)<<12 | uint16(dstReg)<<9 | uint16(dstMode)<<6 | uint16(srcMode)<<3 | uint16(srcReg))
	for _, e := range srcExt {
		a.emit16(e)
	}
	for _, e := range dstExt {
		a.emit16(e)
	}
}

func ext32(v uint32) []uint16 { return []uint16{uint16(v >> 16), uint16(v)} }

func (a *cd4asm) moveq(v int, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x7000 | uint16(dn)<<9 | uint16(v&0xFF))
}

func (a *cd4asm) leaAbs(addr uint32, an int) {
	a.emit16(0x41F9 | uint16(an)<<9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *cd4asm) leaLabel(name string, an int) {
	a.emit16(0x41F9 | uint16(an)<<9)
	a.fixups = append(a.fixups, cd4Fixup{pos: len(a.buf), label: name, abs32: true})
	a.emit32(0)
}

func (a *cd4asm) moveImmToDn(size int, v uint32, dn int) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeB: 0x103C, cd4SizeW: 0x303C, cd4SizeL: 0x203C}[size]
	a.emit16(op | uint16(dn)<<9)
	if size == cd4SizeL {
		a.emit32(v)
	} else {
		a.emit16(uint16(v))
	}
}

func (a *cd4asm) moveImmToAbs(size int, v uint32, addr uint32) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeB: 0x13FC, cd4SizeW: 0x33FC, cd4SizeL: 0x23FC}[size]
	a.emit16(op)
	if size == cd4SizeL {
		a.emit32(v)
	} else {
		a.emit16(uint16(v))
	}
	a.emit32(addr)
}

// moveImmToPostInc emits MOVE #imm, (An)+ (used for VDP map and
// ASIC trace table entries).
func (a *cd4asm) moveImmToPostInc(size int, v uint32, an int) {
	var srcExt []uint16
	if size == cd4SizeL {
		srcExt = ext32(v)
	} else {
		srcExt = []uint16{uint16(v)}
	}
	a.move(size, 7, 4, srcExt, an, 3, nil)
}

func (a *cd4asm) moveDnToAbs(size int, dn int, addr uint32) {
	a.move(size, 0, dn, nil, 1, 7, ext32(addr))
}

func (a *cd4asm) moveAbsToDn(size int, addr uint32, dn int) {
	a.move(size, 7, 1, ext32(addr), dn, 0, nil)
}

func (a *cd4asm) moveDnToAn(size int, dn int, an int) {
	a.move(size, 0, dn, nil, an, 2, nil)
}

func (a *cd4asm) moveDnToPostInc(size int, dn int, an int) {
	a.move(size, 0, dn, nil, an, 3, nil)
}

func (a *cd4asm) moveDnToPreDec(size int, dn int, an int) {
	a.move(size, 0, dn, nil, an, 4, nil)
}

func (a *cd4asm) movePostIncToDn(size int, an int, dn int) {
	a.move(size, 3, an, nil, dn, 0, nil)
}

func (a *cd4asm) movePostIncToPostInc(size int, anSrc, anDst int) {
	a.move(size, 3, anSrc, nil, anDst, 3, nil)
}

// moveDispToDn emits MOVE (disp, An), Dn.
func (a *cd4asm) moveDispToDn(size int, disp int, an int, dn int) {
	a.move(size, 5, an, []uint16{uint16(int16(disp))}, dn, 0, nil)
}

func (a *cd4asm) cmpi(size int, v uint32, dn int) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeB: 0x0C00, cd4SizeW: 0x0C40, cd4SizeL: 0x0C80}[size]
	a.emit16(op | uint16(dn))
	if size == cd4SizeL {
		a.emit32(v)
	} else {
		a.emit16(uint16(v))
	}
}

// cmpbDn emits CMP.B srcDn, dstDn.
func (a *cd4asm) cmpbDn(srcDn, dstDn int) {
	a.emit16(0xB000 | uint16(dstDn)<<9 | uint16(srcDn))
}

func (a *cd4asm) tstDn(size int, dn int) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeB: 0x4A00, cd4SizeW: 0x4A40, cd4SizeL: 0x4A80}[size]
	a.emit16(op | uint16(dn))
}

func (a *cd4asm) btstImm(bit int, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x0800 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit16(uint16(bit))
}

func (a *cd4asm) bsetImm(bit int, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x08C0 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit16(uint16(bit))
}

func (a *cd4asm) addq(size int, n int, dn int) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeB: 0x5000, cd4SizeW: 0x5040, cd4SizeL: 0x5080}[size]
	a.emit16(op | uint16(n&7)<<9 | uint16(dn))
}

func (a *cd4asm) subq(size int, n int, dn int) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeB: 0x5100, cd4SizeW: 0x5140, cd4SizeL: 0x5180}[size]
	a.emit16(op | uint16(n&7)<<9 | uint16(dn))
}

func (a *cd4asm) addiW(v uint16, dn int) {
	a.emit16(0x0640 | uint16(dn))
	a.emit16(v)
}

func (a *cd4asm) addDn(size int, srcDn, dstDn int) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeW: 0xD040, cd4SizeL: 0xD080}[size]
	a.emit16(op | uint16(dstDn)<<9 | uint16(srcDn))
}

func (a *cd4asm) clrDn(size int, dn int) {
	op := map[int]uint16{cd4SizeW: 0x4240, cd4SizeL: 0x4280}[size]
	a.emit16(op | uint16(dn))
}

func (a *cd4asm) jsrAbs(addr uint32) {
	a.emit16(0x4EB9)
	a.emit32(addr)
}

func (a *cd4asm) branch(cond int, label string) {
	a.emit16(0x6000 | uint16(cond)<<8)
	a.fixups = append(a.fixups, cd4Fixup{pos: len(a.buf), label: label})
	a.emit16(0)
}

func (a *cd4asm) bra(label string) { a.branch(cd4BRA, label) }

func (a *cd4asm) dbra(dn int, label string) {
	a.emit16(0x51C8 | uint16(dn))
	a.fixups = append(a.fixups, cd4Fixup{pos: len(a.buf), label: label})
	a.emit16(0)
}

// pollCDBCHK emits a bounded CDBCHK poll loop: it calls _cdbios
// with D0.w = $80 until the trampoline reports carry clear, or
// the iteration budget runs out and control falls to failLabel.
// The budget counts jsr round trips; a trampoline that blocks
// until the per-line BIOSService completes the request resolves
// in one trip, and a purely polled one resolves as soon as the
// queued work drains.
func (a *cd4asm) pollCDBCHK(loopLabel string, failLabel string) {
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeL, 20000, 6)
	a.mark(loopLabel)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x80, 0) // CDBCHK
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.branch(cd4BCC, loopLabel+"ok")
	a.subq(cd4SizeL, 1, 6)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, loopLabel)
	a.bra(failLabel)
	a.mark(loopLabel + "ok")
}

func bcd(v int) uint32 {
	return uint32(v/10)<<4 | uint32(v%10)
}

// tocLong returns the expected CDBTOCREAD result for a track: BCD
// minute, second and frame bytes (frame bit 7 set for a data
// track) over the track number byte.
func tocLong(lba int, track int, data bool) uint32 {
	m, s, f := scd.LBAToMSF(lba)
	fr := bcd(f)
	if data {
		fr |= 0x80
	}
	return bcd(m)<<24 | bcd(s)<<16 | fr<<8 | uint32(track)
}

// headerLong returns the expected CDCREAD header long for a data
// sector: BCD minute, second, frame and the mode byte 1.
func headerLong(lba int) uint32 {
	m, s, f := scd.LBAToMSF(lba)
	return bcd(m)<<24 | bcd(s)<<16 | bcd(f)<<8 | 0x01
}

// payloadByte is the fixture payload pattern at byte i of the
// LBA 8 sector user area: (i*7+3) mod 251, with the first eight
// bytes replaced by the ASCII marker ITAKBIOS.
func payloadByte(i int) byte {
	if i < 8 {
		return "ITAKBIOS"[i]
	}
	return byte((i*7 + 3) % 251)
}

// payloadSum is the word checksum of the 2048 payload user bytes.
func payloadSum() uint16 {
	var sum uint16
	for i := 0; i < 2048; i++ {
		sum += uint16(payloadByte(i))
	}
	return sum
}

// scd4Info carries the fixture constants the IP is assembled
// against and the gate asserts.
type scd4Info struct {
	track1Sectors int
	track2Start   int
	track3Start   int
	tocTrack1     uint32
	tocTrack3     uint32
	payloadLBA    int
	payloadSum    uint16
	headerLBA8    uint32
}

// dataSector builds one raw MODE1/2352 sector for lba: the sync
// pattern, a BCD MSF plus mode 1 header, and the 2048 user bytes.
func dataSector(lba int, user []byte) []byte {
	sec := make([]byte, 2352)
	sec[0] = 0x00
	for i := 1; i <= 10; i++ {
		sec[i] = 0xFF
	}
	sec[11] = 0x00
	m, s, f := scd.LBAToMSF(lba)
	sec[12] = byte(bcd(m))
	sec[13] = byte(bcd(s))
	sec[14] = byte(bcd(f))
	sec[15] = 0x01
	copy(sec[16:2064], user)
	return sec
}

// makeSCDBIOSCue builds the SCD-4 fixture disc: track 1 is 32
// MODE1/2352 data sectors (boot sector at LBA 0, the IP in the
// sectors from LBA 1, the known payload sector at LBA 8), track 2
// is 150 audio sectors of a 440 Hz sine starting right after
// track 1, and track 3 is 150 audio sectors of an 880 Hz sine.
// INDEX lines are computed from the actual sector counts. When
// the environment variable SCD4_FIXTURE_DIR is set, the cue and
// bin are written there (so the shell enginetest can share the
// fixture); otherwise a fresh temporary directory is used.
func makeSCDBIOSCue(t *testing.T) (string, scd4Info) {
	t.Helper()
	info := scd4Info{
		track1Sectors: 32,
		payloadLBA:    8,
		payloadSum:    payloadSum(),
	}
	info.track2Start = info.track1Sectors
	info.track3Start = info.track2Start + 150
	info.tocTrack1 = tocLong(0, 1, true)
	info.tocTrack3 = tocLong(info.track3Start, 3, false)
	info.headerLBA8 = headerLong(info.payloadLBA)

	ip := buildSCD4IP(info)
	if len(ip) > 7*2048 {
		t.Fatalf("SCD-4 IP is %d bytes, want at most %d so it stays clear of the payload sector at LBA %d", len(ip), 7*2048, info.payloadLBA)
	}

	// The disc main program: the same main side program the
	// companion cartridge runs, assembled at its Word RAM entry
	// 0x200208. It must fit in the boot sector user bytes from
	// offset 0x208 to the end of the 2048 byte user area.
	mainProg := buildSCD4MainProgram(0x200208)
	if len(mainProg) > 0x800-0x208 {
		t.Fatalf("SCD-4 disc main program is %d bytes, want at most %d so it fits in boot sector user bytes 0x208..0x800", len(mainProg), 0x800-0x208)
	}
	t.Logf("SCD-4 disc main program: %d bytes (limit %d)", len(mainProg), 0x800-0x208)

	bin := make([]byte, 0, 332*2352)
	// Track 1 sector 0: the boot header, plus the disc main
	// program at user offset 0x200 behind the ITAKMAIN marker.
	user0 := make([]byte, 2048)
	copy(user0, "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(user0[0x30:], 1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(user0[0x34:], uint32(len(ip)))
	copy(user0[0x200:], "ITAKMAIN")
	copy(user0[0x208:], mainProg)
	bin = append(bin, dataSector(0, user0)...)
	// Track 1 sectors 1 to 31: zeros, with the payload pattern at
	// LBA 8. The IP is overlaid into LBAs 1.. afterwards.
	for lba := 1; lba < info.track1Sectors; lba++ {
		user := make([]byte, 2048)
		if lba == info.payloadLBA {
			for i := range user {
				user[i] = payloadByte(i)
			}
		}
		bin = append(bin, dataSector(lba, user)...)
	}
	// Overlay the IP: the boot stub loads consecutive LBAs from
	// LBA 1 into $026000, so IP chunk k (0 based) sits in disc
	// LBA 1+k. The size cap asserted above (at most 7 sectors,
	// payload at load sector 7 counting from LBA 1) keeps every
	// chunk on LBAs 1..7, clear of the payload sector.
	for k := 0; k*2048 < len(ip); k++ {
		lba := 1 + k
		if lba >= info.payloadLBA {
			t.Fatalf("SCD-4 IP chunk %d would land on payload LBA %d", k, info.payloadLBA)
		}
		off := lba * 2352
		chunk := ip[k*2048:]
		if len(chunk) > 2048 {
			chunk = chunk[:2048]
		}
		copy(bin[off+16:off+16+len(chunk)], chunk)
	}

	// Audio tracks: stereo sine, same value on both channels.
	sine := func(freq float64, sectors int) {
		for s := 0; s < sectors; s++ {
			sec := make([]byte, 2352)
			for f := 0; f < 588; f++ {
				idx := s*588 + f
				v := int16(10000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*freq*float64(idx)/44100))
				binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[f*4:], uint16(v))
				binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[f*4+2:], uint16(v))
			}
			bin = append(bin, sec...)
		}
	}
	sine(440, 150)
	sine(880, 150)

	dir := t.TempDir()
	if env := os.Getenv("SCD4_FIXTURE_DIR"); env != "" {
		dir = env
		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("SCD4_FIXTURE_DIR mkdir: %v", err)
		}
	}
	binPath := filepath.Join(dir, "bios.bin")
	if err := os.WriteFile(binPath, bin, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write bin: %v", err)
	}
	msf := func(lba int) string {
		m, s, f := scd.LBAToMSF(lba)
		return fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%02d:%02d", m, s, f)
	}
	cue := "FILE \"bios.bin\" BINARY\n" +
		"  TRACK 01 MODE1/2352\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 " + msf(0) + "\n" +
		"  TRACK 02 AUDIO\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 " + msf(info.track2Start) + "\n" +
		"  TRACK 03 AUDIO\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 " + msf(info.track3Start) + "\n"
	cuePath := filepath.Join(dir, "bios.cue")
	if err := os.WriteFile(cuePath, []byte(cue), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write cue: %v", err)
	}
	return cuePath, info
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The sub CPU initial program, loaded at $026000 by the boot stub.
// It runs stages a to h from the task brief, maintaining a stage
// bitmap in D7 (bit per stage) that it mirrors into the PRG-RAM
// results cell at $025000 after every stage and finally into comm
// status 1. A failing sub-check stores a distinct detail code in
// the PRG-RAM cell at $025002 (stage letter in the high nibble
// pattern 0xA0 to 0xF0 and 0x60, sub-check in the low bits) and
// the stage bit stays clear. Argument tables and data patterns
// are staged in PRG-RAM by the Go side before the run (see
// stageSCD4Tables), at these sub CPU addresses:
//
//	$025010 DRVINIT table {1, $FF}
//	$025012 MSCPLAY argument word (track 2)
//	$025014 CDBTOCREAD argument word (track 3)
//	$025016 CDBTOCREAD argument word (track 1)
//	$025020 ROMREADN arguments {sector.l = 8, count.l = 1}
//	$02A000 BRM parameter block: filename at +0 (11 bytes),
//	        flag byte at +11, block size word at +12, with a
//	        data address long at +16 and a byte count long at
//	        +20 as extra fields
//	$02B000 BRM write source data (64 bytes)
//	$02C000 BRM read destination (64 bytes)
//
// BIOS register conventions used (the published table style):
// _cdbios functions take their parameter block at A0 when they
// have one (DRVINIT, MSCPLAY, ROMREADN), CDBTOCREAD also takes
// the track number in D1.w, CDCSETMODE takes its mode in D1.w,
// CDCTRN takes the data buffer in A0 and the header buffer in
// A1. _buram calls take the file parameter block at A0, the data
// buffer in A1, the flag in D1.w, the block count in D2.w and
// the byte count in D3.l.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func buildSCD4IP(info scd4Info) []byte {
	a := newCD4Asm(0x26000)

	storeBitmap := func() { a.moveDnToAbs(cd4SizeW, 7, 0x025000) }
	detail := func(code uint16) { a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, uint32(code), 0x025002) }

	// Stage a: DRVINIT {start 1, end $FF}, poll CDBCHK.
	a.mark("stageA")
	a.leaAbs(0x025010, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x10, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.pollCDBCHK("pollA", "failA")
	a.bsetImm(0, 7)
	a.bra("stageAend")
	a.mark("failA")
	detail(0xA1)
	a.mark("stageAend")
	storeBitmap()

	// Stage b: CDBTOCREAD for tracks 3 and 1.
	a.mark("stageB")
	a.leaAbs(0x025014, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 3, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x83, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeL, info.tocTrack3, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failB1")
	a.leaAbs(0x025016, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x83, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeL, info.tocTrack1, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failB2")
	a.bsetImm(1, 7)
	a.bra("stageBend")
	a.mark("failB1")
	detail(0xB1)
	a.bra("stageBend")
	a.mark("failB2")
	detail(0xB2)
	a.mark("stageBend")
	storeBitmap()

	// Stage c: MSCPLAY track 2, poll, CDBSTAT table checks.
	a.mark("stageC")
	a.leaAbs(0x025012, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 2, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x11, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.pollCDBCHK("pollC", "failC1")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x81, 0) // CDBSTAT: A0 = status table
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.moveDispToDn(cd4SizeB, 7, 0, 0) // BP3: current track
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeB, 2, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failC2")
	a.moveDispToDn(cd4SizeB, 1, 0, 0) // MSC status byte: 1 = playing
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeB, 1, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failC3")
	a.bsetImm(2, 7)
	a.bra("stageCend")
	a.mark("failC1")
	detail(0xC1)
	a.bra("stageCend")
	a.mark("failC2")
	detail(0xC2)
	a.bra("stageCend")
	a.mark("failC3")
	detail(0xC3)
	a.mark("stageCend")
	storeBitmap()

	// Stage d: PCM tone through raw registers only. A 128 byte
	// sine period (sign-magnitude, amplitude 120) goes to wave
	// RAM bank 0 with a loop marker at byte 128 and loop start 0;
	// FD = $1000 advances 2 samples per chip tick, so the tone is
	// (12500000/384) * 2 / 128 = about 508.6 Hz.
	a.mark("stageD")
	a.leaLabel("sinetab", 1)
	a.leaAbs(0xFF1000, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 127, 4)
	a.mark("loopD")
	a.movePostIncToPostInc(cd4SizeB, 1, 0)
	a.dbra(4, "loopD")
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0xFF, 0xFF1080) // loop marker
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0xC0, 0xFF0007) // CTRL: on, MOD 1, channel 0
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0xFF, 0xFF0000) // ENV
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0xFF, 0xFF0001) // PAN
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0x00, 0xFF0002) // FD low
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0x10, 0xFF0003) // FD high: FD = $1000
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0x00, 0xFF0004) // loop start low
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0x00, 0xFF0005) // loop start high
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0x00, 0xFF0006) // start = 0 (retrigger)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0x01, 0xFF0008) // channel 0 on
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeB, 0xFF0007, 0)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeB, 0xC0, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failD1")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeB, 0xFF0003, 0)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeB, 0x10, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failD2")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeB, 0xFF0008, 0)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeB, 0x01, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failD3")
	a.bsetImm(3, 7)
	a.bra("stageDend")
	a.mark("failD1")
	detail(0xD1)
	a.bra("stageDend")
	a.mark("failD2")
	detail(0xD2)
	a.bra("stageDend")
	a.mark("failD3")
	detail(0xD3)
	a.mark("stageDend")
	storeBitmap()

	// Stage e: the ROMREADN sector read flow for LBA 8.
	a.mark("stageE")
	a.leaAbs(0x025020, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeL, 8, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeL, 1, 2)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x20, 0) // ROMREADN
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.pollCDBCHK("pollE", "failE1")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x96, 0) // CDCSETMODE, D1.w = 0
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0, 1)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeL, 20000, 6)
	a.mark("statE")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x8A, 0) // CDCSTAT
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.branch(cd4BCC, "statEok")
	a.subq(cd4SizeL, 1, 6)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "statE")
	a.bra("failE2")
	a.mark("statEok")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x8B, 0) // CDCREAD: header long in D0
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeL, info.headerLBA8, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failE3")
	a.leaAbs(0x027000, 0) // CDCTRN data buffer
	a.leaAbs(0x028000, 1) // CDCTRN header buffer
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x8C, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x8D, 0) // CDCACK
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F22)
	a.leaAbs(0x027000, 0)
	a.clrDn(cd4SizeL, 2)
	a.moveq(0, 3)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 2047, 1)
	a.mark("sumE")
	a.movePostIncToDn(cd4SizeB, 0, 3)
	a.addDn(cd4SizeW, 3, 2)
	a.dbra(1, "sumE")
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, uint32(info.payloadSum), 2)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failE4")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeL, 0x027000, 0)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeL, 0x4954414B, 0) // "ITAK"
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failE5")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeL, 0x027004, 0)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeL, 0x42494F53, 0) // "BIOS"
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failE5")
	a.bsetImm(4, 7)
	a.bra("stageEend")
	a.mark("failE1")
	detail(0xE1)
	a.bra("stageEend")
	a.mark("failE2")
	detail(0xE2)
	a.bra("stageEend")
	a.mark("failE3")
	detail(0xE3)
	a.bra("stageEend")
	a.mark("failE4")
	detail(0xE4)
	a.bra("stageEend")
	a.mark("failE5")
	detail(0xE5)
	a.mark("stageEend")
	storeBitmap()

	// Stage f: backup RAM through _buram.
	a.mark("stageF")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 6, 0) // BRMFORMAT
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.branch(cd4BCS, "failF1")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 0) // BRMSTAT
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 125, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failF2")
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 0, 1)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failF3")
	a.leaAbs(0x02A000, 0) // BRMWRITE
	a.leaAbs(0x02B000, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0, 1) // flag 0
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 2) // 1 block
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeL, 64, 3)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 4, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.branch(cd4BCS, "failF4")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 0) // BRMSTAT: 123 free after 1 file
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 123, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failF5")
	a.leaAbs(0x02A000, 0) // BRMSERCH
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 2, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.branch(cd4BCS, "failF6")
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 1, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failF7")
	a.leaAbs(0x02A000, 0) // BRMREAD
	a.leaAbs(0x02C000, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 2)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 3, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.branch(cd4BCS, "failF8")
	// The compare reads the reference copy at $02D000, not the
	// write source at $02B000: BRMSTAT writes its 12 byte display
	// string through (A1), and A1 still pointed at the source
	// buffer during the second BRMSTAT above, so the source
	// buffer's first bytes are clobbered by design of the call.
	a.leaAbs(0x02D000, 0)
	a.leaAbs(0x02C000, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 63, 4)
	a.mark("cmpF")
	a.movePostIncToDn(cd4SizeB, 0, 5)
	a.movePostIncToDn(cd4SizeB, 1, 3)
	a.cmpbDn(3, 5)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failF9")
	a.dbra(4, "cmpF")
	a.leaAbs(0x02A000, 0) // BRMDEL
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 5, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.branch(cd4BCS, "failFA")
	a.leaAbs(0x02A000, 0) // BRMSERCH again: expect carry set
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 2, 0)
	a.jsrAbs(0x5F16)
	a.branch(cd4BCC, "failFB")
	a.bsetImm(5, 7)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF1")
	detail(0xF1)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF2")
	detail(0xF2)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF3")
	detail(0xF3)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF4")
	detail(0xF4)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF5")
	detail(0xF5)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF6")
	detail(0xF6)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF7")
	detail(0xF7)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF8")
	detail(0xF8)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failF9")
	detail(0xF9)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failFA")
	detail(0xFA)
	a.bra("stageFend")
	a.mark("failFB")
	detail(0xFB)
	a.mark("stageFend")
	storeBitmap()

	// Stage g: the SCD-3 ASIC identity trace, then DMNA.
	a.mark("stageG")
	a.leaAbs(0x200100, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x7F, 0)
	a.mark("fillG")
	a.moveDnToPreDec(cd4SizeB, 0, 0)
	a.dbra(0, "fillG")
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 1, 0x201000)
	a.leaAbs(0x202000, 0)
	a.moveq(0, 0)
	a.moveq(0, 1)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 15, 2)
	a.mark("tloopG")
	a.moveDnToPostInc(cd4SizeW, 0, 0)
	a.moveDnToPostInc(cd4SizeW, 1, 0)
	a.moveImmToPostInc(cd4SizeW, 0x0800, 0)
	a.moveDnToPostInc(cd4SizeW, 0, 0)
	a.addiW(8, 1)
	a.dbra(2, "tloopG")
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0, 0xFF8058)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x0400, 0xFF805A)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 1, 0xFF805C)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x1000, 0xFF805E)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0, 0xFF8060)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 16, 0xFF8062)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 16, 0xFF8064)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x0800, 0xFF8066)
	a.mark("pollG")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeB, 0xFF8058, 0)
	a.tstDn(cd4SizeB, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "pollG")
	a.leaAbs(0x204000, 0)
	a.moveq(0, 2)
	a.moveq(0, 3)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x7F, 1)
	a.mark("csumG")
	a.movePostIncToDn(cd4SizeB, 0, 3)
	a.addDn(cd4SizeW, 3, 2)
	a.dbra(1, "csumG")
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 0x1FC0, 2)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "failG")
	a.bsetImm(6, 7)
	a.bra("stageGend")
	a.mark("failG")
	detail(0x60)
	a.mark("stageGend")
	storeBitmap()
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 0x02, 0xFF8002) // DMNA: Word RAM to main

	// Stage h: publish results and idle.
	a.mark("stageH")
	a.moveDnToAbs(cd4SizeW, 7, 0xFF8022) // comm status 1 = bitmap
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x600D, 0xFF8020)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 2, 0xFF800F) // sub flag 2
	a.mark("idle")
	a.bra("idle")

	// The stage d sine table: one 128 byte sign-magnitude sine
	// period, amplitude 120.
	a.mark("sinetab")
	tab := make([]byte, 128)
	for i := range tab {
		v := int(math.Round(120 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/128)))
		if v >= 0 {
			tab[i] = 0x80 | byte(v)
		} else {
			tab[i] = byte(-v)
		}
	}
	a.emitBytes(tab)
	return a.finish()
}

// stageSCD4Tables writes the IP argument tables and BRM data into
// PRG-RAM before the first frame runs (the sub CPU is still held
// in reset, so nothing races it).
func stageSCD4Tables(sys *System) {
	prg := sys.CDUnit().PRGRAM()
	prg[0x5010] = 1                             // DRVINIT start track
	prg[0x5011] = 0xFF                          // DRVINIT end track
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(prg[0x5012:], 2) // MSCPLAY track
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(prg[0x5014:], 3) // CDBTOCREAD track 3
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(prg[0x5016:], 1) // CDBTOCREAD track 1
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(prg[0x5020:], 8) // ROMREADN sector
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(prg[0x5024:], 1) // ROMREADN count
	blk := prg[0xA000:]
	copy(blk[0:11], "ITAKTEST___")
	blk[11] = 0                                    // flag byte
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(blk[12:], 1)        // block size word
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(blk[16:], 0x02B000) // data address (extra field)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(blk[20:], 64)       // byte count (extra field)
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		prg[0xB000+i] = byte(i*5 + 0x41) // BRM write source
		prg[0xD000+i] = byte(i*5 + 0x41) // pristine reference copy
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The main CPU program, used both as a custom Genesis ROM and
// as the disc main program embedded in boot sector 0. It releases the sub
// CPU, waits for comm status 0 = $600D and for its RET flag, then
// programs the VDP (display on, plane A at $2000, H32, plane B at
// $E000, sprite table at $3000, scroll table at $4000), writes a
// 16 entry palette, copies the Word RAM image buffer at $204000
// into VRAM tiles 1 to 4 with a CPU loop through the data port,
// fills the plane A map with the blank tile 0 and overwrites a
// 16x16 cell region with tiles 1 to 4 cycling by column plus row,
// reads the tiles back through the VDP and stores the word
// checksum in comm command 1, sets the main flag, and idles.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// buildSCD4MainProgram assembles the main CPU program at the
// given base address: 0x200 for the companion cartridge variant
// and 0x200208 for the disc variant embedded in boot sector 0
// behind the ITAKMAIN marker. The program is position dependent
// only through its palette table label, which the assembler
// resolves from the base, so the same bytes logic runs from ROM
// or from Word RAM.
func buildSCD4MainProgram(base int) []byte {
	a := newCD4Asm(base)
	a.mark("start")
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 1, 0xA12000) // RES = 1: release sub CPU
	a.mark("wait600d")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeW, 0xA12020, 0)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 0x600D, 0)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "wait600d")
	a.mark("waitret")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeB, 0xA12002, 0)
	a.btstImm(2, 0) // RET flag: Word RAM owned by main
	a.branch(cd4BEQ, "waitret")

	regs := [][2]uint32{
		{1, 0x40},  // display on
		{2, 0x08},  // plane A name table at $2000
		{3, 0x00},  // window table at $0000 (window disabled by edges)
		{4, 0x07},  // plane B name table at $E000
		{5, 0x18},  // sprite table at $3000
		{7, 0x00},  // backdrop: palette 0 color 0
		{12, 0x00}, // H32 (256 px)
		{13, 0x10}, // horizontal scroll table at $4000
		{15, 0x02}, // auto-increment 2
		{16, 0x00}, // planes 32x32 cells
	}
	for _, r := range regs {
		a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x8000|r[0]<<8|r[1], 0xC00004)
	}

	// Palette: CRAM write at address 0, 16 words from the table.
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0xC000, 0xC00004)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x0000, 0xC00004)
	a.leaLabel("cramtab", 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 15, 1)
	a.mark("cramloop")
	a.movePostIncToDn(cd4SizeW, 0, 0)
	a.moveDnToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0, 0xC00000)
	a.dbra(1, "cramloop")

	// Tiles: VRAM write at $0020 (tile 1), 64 words copied from
	// the Word RAM image buffer through the main window.
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x4020, 0xC00004)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x0000, 0xC00004)
	a.leaAbs(0x204000, 0)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 63, 1)
	a.mark("copyloop")
	a.movePostIncToDn(cd4SizeW, 0, 0)
	a.moveDnToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0, 0xC00000)
	a.dbra(1, "copyloop")

	// Map: fill all 32x32 plane A entries with tile 0 (blank,
	// since tile 0 pattern bytes are never written), then write
	// the 16x16 pattern region, one VRAM address set per row.
	// The pattern region runs as nested loops rather than an
	// unrolled write per cell, so the same program also fits in
	// the boot sector user bytes for the disc variant: cell
	// (row, column) gets tile 1+((column+row)&3). D3 counts rows,
	// D4 holds the VRAM control low word for the current row
	// (0x6000 plus 0x40 per row, since plane A starts at 0x2000
	// and each row is 32 cells at 2 bytes), D5 counts columns,
	// and D6 holds the current tile. Writing 16 cells advances
	// D6 through a whole cycle of 4 and back to the row start
	// tile, so one extra advance before the next row gives that
	// row its start tile.
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x6000, 0xC00004)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x0000, 0xC00004)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1023, 1)
	a.mark("fillloop")
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0, 0xC00000)
	a.dbra(1, "fillloop")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 0x6000, 4)
	a.moveq(0, 3)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 6)
	a.mark("rowloop")
	a.moveDnToAbs(cd4SizeW, 4, 0xC00004)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0, 0xC00004)
	a.moveq(0, 5)
	a.mark("colloop")
	a.moveDnToAbs(cd4SizeW, 6, 0xC00000)
	a.addq(cd4SizeW, 1, 6)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 5, 6)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "colnowrap")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 6)
	a.mark("colnowrap")
	a.addq(cd4SizeL, 1, 5)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeL, 16, 5)
	a.branch(cd4BLT, "colloop")
	a.addq(cd4SizeW, 1, 6)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeW, 5, 6)
	a.branch(cd4BNE, "rownowrap")
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 1, 6)
	a.mark("rownowrap")
	a.addiW(0x40, 4)
	a.addq(cd4SizeL, 1, 3)
	a.cmpi(cd4SizeL, 16, 3)
	a.branch(cd4BLT, "rowloop")

	// Readback: VRAM read at $0020, sum 64 words, publish.
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x0020, 0xC00004)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeW, 0x0000, 0xC00004)
	a.moveq(0, 2)
	a.moveImmToDn(cd4SizeW, 63, 1)
	a.mark("rdloop")
	a.moveAbsToDn(cd4SizeW, 0xC00000, 0)
	a.addDn(cd4SizeW, 0, 2)
	a.dbra(1, "rdloop")
	a.moveDnToAbs(cd4SizeW, 2, 0xA12012) // comm command 1
	a.moveq(1, 0)                        // leave D0 odd (see header comment)
	a.moveImmToAbs(cd4SizeB, 1, 0xA1200E)
	a.mark("idle")
	a.bra("idle")

	// Palette words: index i maps to red = i&7, green = (i>>1)&7,
	// blue = (i>>2)&7 in the VDP 9 bit BGR word layout, which is
	// injective over 0..15, so all sixteen colors are distinct.
	a.mark("cramtab")
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		r := i & 7
		g := (i >> 1) & 7
		b := (i >> 2) & 7
		a.emit16(uint16(r<<1 | g<<5 | b<<9))
	}
	return a.finish()
}

// buildSCD4ROM builds the companion cartridge variant of the
// main program: a Genesis ROM whose code at 0x200 is the main
// program assembled at base 0x200. The cartridge ignores the
// boot sector main program copy in Word RAM.
func buildSCD4ROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0:], 0x00FFFE00)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[4:], 0x00000200)
	copy(rom[0x100:], "SEGA GENESIS    ")
	copy(rom[0x200:], buildSCD4MainProgram(0x200))
	return rom
}

// goertzelPower returns the single-bin DFT power of samples at
// freq Hz over a rate Hz stream.
func goertzelPower(samples []int16, freq, rate float64) float64 {
	if len(samples) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	k := 2 * math.Pi * freq / rate
	coeff := 2 * math.Cos(k)
	var s1, s2 float64
	for _, v := range samples {
		s0 := float64(v) + coeff*s1 - s2
		s2 = s1
		s1 = s0
	}
	return s1*s1 + s2*s2 - coeff*s1*s2
}

func fbBytes(fb []uint16) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 2*len(fb))
	for i, v := range fb {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[2*i:], v)
	}
	return out
}

func TestCDBIOSFullStack(t *testing.T) {
	cue, info := makeSCDBIOSCue(t)

	// Fixture sanity: the disc TOC matches the computed layout.
	disc, err := scd.OpenDisc(cue)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: OpenDisc: %v", err)
	}
	tracks := disc.Tracks()
	disc.Close()
	if len(tracks) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: %d tracks, want 3", len(tracks))
	}
	if tracks[0].StartLBA != 0 || tracks[0].Sectors != info.track1Sectors {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: track 1 at LBA %d with %d sectors, want LBA 0 with %d", tracks[0].StartLBA, tracks[0].Sectors, info.track1Sectors)
	}
	if tracks[1].StartLBA != info.track2Start || tracks[1].Sectors != 150 {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: track 2 at LBA %d with %d sectors, want LBA %d with 150", tracks[1].StartLBA, tracks[1].Sectors, info.track2Start)
	}
	if tracks[2].StartLBA != info.track3Start || tracks[2].Sectors != 150 {
		t.Fatalf("fixture: track 3 at LBA %d with %d sectors, want LBA %d with 150", tracks[2].StartLBA, tracks[2].Sectors, info.track3Start)
	}

	rom := buildSCD4ROM()
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sys.LoadDisc(cue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if got, want := sys.SerializeSize(), 1070469; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("CD mode SerializeSize = %d, want %d (SCD-4 size with BRAM and BIOS sections)", got, want)
	}
	stageSCD4Tables(sys)
	u := sys.CDUnit()

	// Run until the IP publishes sub flag 2, collecting audio
	// per frame for the tone analysis.
	framesAudio := make([][]int16, 0, 256)
	done := false
	framesRun := 0
	for i := 0; i < 1200; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		framesRun++
		framesAudio = append(framesAudio, sys.AudioBuffer())
		if u.SubFlag() == 2 {
			done = true
			break
		}
	}
	bitmapCell := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(u.PRGRAM()[0x5000:0x5002])
	detail := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(u.PRGRAM()[0x5002:0x5004])
	if !done {
		t.Fatalf("stage h: sub flag = %#02x after %d frames, want 2 (IP never finished); stage bitmap cell = %#04x, detail code = %#04x, comm status 0 = %#06x",
			u.SubFlag(), framesRun, bitmapCell, detail, u.CommStatus(0))
	}
	t.Logf("IP finished in %d frames", framesRun)

	// Stage bitmap: bits a to g all set, in comm status 1 and in
	// the PRG-RAM results cell.
	if got := u.CommStatus(1); got != 0x7F {
		t.Fatalf("stage bitmap: comm status 1 = %#04x, want 0x7f (stages a to g all passed); PRG detail code = %#04x", got, detail)
	}
	if bitmapCell != 0x7F {
		t.Fatalf("stage bitmap: PRG results cell = %#04x, want 0x7f; PRG detail code = %#04x", bitmapCell, detail)
	}

	// Main side: the VRAM readback checksum in comm command 1
	// must equal the word sum of the image buffer the ASIC
	// traced into Word RAM.
	wr := u.WordRAM()[0x4000:0x4080]
	var wantVRAMSum uint16
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		wantVRAMSum += uint16(wr[2*i])<<8 | uint16(wr[2*i+1])
	}
	if got := u.CommCommand(1); got != wantVRAMSum {
		t.Fatalf("main VDP: comm command 1 = %#06x, want %#06x (VRAM tile readback checksum)", got, wantVRAMSum)
	}
	if got := u.MainFlag(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("main VDP: main flag = %#02x, want 1 (main program finished)", got)
	}

	// Let two full frames render with the final VDP state: the
	// main CPU finished its VDP work partway through the frame
	// the IP completed in, so the pattern rows of that frame
	// were still rendered as backdrop.
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		_ = sys.AudioBuffer()
	}

	// Framebuffer: the 16x16 cell pattern region shows the image
	// buffer tiles. Every image byte contributes its two nibbles
	// as pixels; 233 of the 256 nibbles in bytes 0..127 are
	// nonzero and each tile is shown 64 times across the region,
	// so thousands of pixels must differ from the backdrop.
	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	nonblank := 0
	for y := 0; y < sys.Height(); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < sys.Width(); x++ {
			if fb[y*320+x] != 0 {
				nonblank++
			}
		}
	}
	t.Logf("framebuffer non-background pixels: %d", nonblank)
	if nonblank < 2000 {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer: %d non-background pixels, want at least 2000 from the 16x16 tile pattern", nonblank)
	}

	// Audio tones: analyze the last up to 45 frames of audio
	// from the initial run (both MSCPLAY CD-DA at 440 Hz and the
	// PCM tone at about 508.6 Hz are running by then).
	start := 0
	if len(framesAudio) > 45 {
		start = len(framesAudio) - 45
	}
	var left []int16
	for _, fr := range framesAudio[start:] {
		for i := 0; i+1 < len(fr); i += 2 {
			left = append(left, fr[i])
		}
	}
	const pcmHz = 12500000.0 / 384 * 2 / 128 // FD $1000, 128 sample period
	p440 := goertzelPower(left, 440, 44100)
	pPCM := goertzelPower(left, pcmHz, 44100)
	pCtl := goertzelPower(left, 1500, 44100)
	t.Logf("tone powers over %d samples: 440 Hz = %.4g, PCM %.1f Hz = %.4g, control 1500 Hz = %.4g", len(left), p440, pcmHz, pPCM, pCtl)
	if !(p440 > 4*pCtl) {
		t.Fatalf("audio stage c: 440 Hz CD-DA power %.4g does not exceed 4x the 1500 Hz control power %.4g", p440, pCtl)
	}
	if !(pPCM > 4*pCtl) {
		t.Fatalf("audio stage d: PCM %.1f Hz power %.4g does not exceed 4x the 1500 Hz control power %.4g", pcmHz, pPCM, pCtl)
	}

	// Determinism leg at a mid-playback frame. The playback
	// still running at this point is the stage d PCM tone: the
	// stage e read flow ends its bounded read with a CDD stop
	// (CDCACK), so the CDD itself is stopped by design here
	// (position LBA 9, one sector past the payload). The PCM
	// channel is never stopped, so the save is taken while it
	// is sounding and the continuation audio must carry it.
	t.Logf("determinism save point: CDD state %d at LBA %d (stopped after the stage e read), PCM tone running", u.CDDState(), u.CDDPositionLBA())
	sMid := make([]byte, sys.SerializeSize())
	if err := sys.Serialize(sMid); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism: Serialize: %v", err)
	}
	var audioA []int16
	for i := 0; i < 45; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		audioA = append(audioA, sys.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	// The unrestored continuation audio must carry the PCM
	// tone, proving the save point was mid-playback.
	var leftA []int16
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(audioA); i += 2 {
		leftA = append(leftA, audioA[i])
	}
	pPCMA := goertzelPower(leftA, pcmHz, 44100)
	pCtlA := goertzelPower(leftA, 1500, 44100)
	if !(pPCMA > 4*pCtlA) {
		t.Fatalf("determinism: PCM tone power %.4g in the continuation audio does not exceed 4x the control %.4g; the save point was not mid-playback", pPCMA, pCtlA)
	}
	sAEnd := make([]byte, sys.SerializeSize())
	if err := sys.Serialize(sAEnd); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism: Serialize A end: %v", err)
	}
	fbA := fbBytes(sys.Framebuffer())

	b := New()
	if err := b.LoadGame(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism: LoadGame B: %v", err)
	}
	if err := b.LoadDisc(cue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism: LoadDisc B: %v", err)
	}
	if err := b.Deserialize(sMid); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism: Deserialize B: %v", err)
	}
	var audioB []int16
	for i := 0; i < 45; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
		audioB = append(audioB, b.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	sBEnd := make([]byte, b.SerializeSize())
	if err := b.Serialize(sBEnd); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism: Serialize B end: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(sAEnd, sBEnd) {
		t.Fatal("determinism: state after restore plus 45 frames differs from the unrestored run")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(int16sToBytes(audioA), int16sToBytes(audioB)) {
		t.Fatal("determinism: audio after restore plus 45 frames differs from the unrestored run")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(fbA, fbBytes(b.Framebuffer())) {
		t.Fatal("determinism: framebuffer after restore plus 45 frames differs from the unrestored run")
	}
	t.Logf("determinism: 45 frames replayed byte-identically, %d audio samples compared", len(audioA))

	// Legacy leg: build a pre-SCD-4 CD state from the current
	// one. Serialize's layout puts the CD unit block before an
	// 8 byte sub CPU cycle trailer, so the unit growth is not at
	// the very end of the state: the legacy state is the current
	// state with the last scd.BRAMSize + scd.BIOSStateSize bytes
	// of the unit block removed, keeping the trailer.
	growth := scd.BRAMSize + scd.BIOSStateSize
	if growth != 8960 {
		t.Fatalf("legacy: BRAMSize + BIOSStateSize = %d, want 8960", growth)
	}
	legacy := make([]byte, 0, len(sMid)-growth)
	legacy = append(legacy, sMid[:len(sMid)-8-growth]...)
	legacy = append(legacy, sMid[len(sMid)-8:]...)
	if len(legacy) != 1061509 {
		t.Fatalf("legacy: constructed legacy state is %d bytes, want 1061509", len(legacy))
	}
	c := New()
	if err := c.LoadGame(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("legacy: LoadGame C: %v", err)
	}
	if err := c.LoadDisc(cue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("legacy: LoadDisc C: %v", err)
	}
	if err := c.Deserialize(legacy); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("legacy: Deserialize of the legacy-sized CD state failed: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		c.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := c.CDUnit().SubFlag(); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("legacy: sub flag = %#02x after 5 frames on the restored legacy state, want 2 (machine did not keep running)", got)
	}
	// A buffer one byte short of the legacy length must keep
	// failing: only the exact legacy length is expanded.
	legacyBad := legacy[:len(legacy)-1]
	d := New()
	if err := d.LoadGame(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("legacy negative: LoadGame D: %v", err)
	}
	if err := d.LoadDisc(cue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("legacy negative: LoadDisc D: %v", err)
	}
	if err := d.Deserialize(legacyBad); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("legacy negative: Deserialize accepted a truncated legacy-sized state, want an error")
	}
	t.Logf("legacy: %d byte legacy state accepted and ran; truncated variant rejected", len(legacy))
}

// TestCDBIOSDiscOnlyBoot is the disc only variant of the SCD-4
// gate: no cartridge is loaded, so the system synthesizes
// MainStubROM itself. The boot stub copies boot sector 0 into
// Word RAM, the main stub finds the ITAKMAIN marker at 0x200200
// and jumps to the embedded main program at 0x200208, and that
// program programs the VDP exactly as the companion cartridge
// variant does.
func TestCDBIOSDiscOnlyBoot(t *testing.T) {
	cue, _ := makeSCDBIOSCue(t)

	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadDisc(cue); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	stageSCD4Tables(sys)
	u := sys.CDUnit()

	done := false
	framesRun := 0
	for i := 0; i < 1200; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		framesRun++
		_ = sys.AudioBuffer()
		if u.SubFlag() == 2 {
			done = true
			break
		}
	}
	detail := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(u.PRGRAM()[0x5002:0x5004])
	if !done {
		t.Fatalf("disc only: sub flag = %#02x after %d frames, want 2 (IP never finished); PRG detail code = %#04x, comm status 0 = %#06x",
			u.SubFlag(), framesRun, detail, u.CommStatus(0))
	}
	t.Logf("disc only: IP finished in %d frames", framesRun)

	if got := u.CommStatus(1); got != 0x7F {
		t.Fatalf("disc only: comm status 1 = %#04x, want 0x7f (stages a to g all passed); PRG detail code = %#04x", got, detail)
	}
	if got := u.CommCommand(1); got != 0xD000 {
		t.Fatalf("disc only: comm command 1 = %#06x, want 0xd000 (VRAM tile readback checksum)", got)
	}
	if got := u.MainFlag(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("disc only: main flag = %#02x, want 1 (main program finished)", got)
	}

	// Let two full frames render with the final VDP state, as in
	// the companion cartridge gate.
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		_ = sys.AudioBuffer()
	}
	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	nonblank := 0
	for y := 0; y < sys.Height(); y++ {
		for x := 0; x < sys.Width(); x++ {
			if fb[y*320+x] != 0 {
				nonblank++
			}
		}
	}
	t.Logf("disc only: framebuffer non-background pixels: %d", nonblank)
	if nonblank < 2000 {
		t.Fatalf("disc only: framebuffer: %d non-background pixels, want at least 2000 from the 16x16 tile pattern", nonblank)
	}

	// Stability: 30 more frames must leave the framebuffer
	// byte identical.
	before := fbBytes(sys.Framebuffer())
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		_ = sys.AudioBuffer()
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(before, fbBytes(sys.Framebuffer())) {
		t.Fatal("disc only: framebuffer changed over 30 extra frames, want byte identical stability")
	}
	if got := u.SubFlag(); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("disc only: sub flag = %#02x after 30 extra frames, want 2 (machine did not stay stable)", got)
	}
	t.Logf("disc only: framebuffer stable over 30 extra frames, %d non-background pixels", nonblank)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/system/system_cd_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// makeSCDISO writes a minimal two sector disc image: sector 0 is
// the boot header (SEGADISCSYSTEM signature, IP LBA and IP size in
// the header fields at 0x30 and 0x34) and sector 1 holds the IP.
func makeSCDISO(t *testing.T, ip []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	img := make([]byte, 4096)
	copy(img[0:], "SEGADISCSYSTEM")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0x30:], 1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0x34:], uint32(len(ip)))
	copy(img[2048:], ip)
	path := t.TempDir() + "/test.iso"
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, img, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write ISO: %v", err)
	}
	return path
}

// cdTestIP is the initial program loaded to sub address 0x026000 by
// the boot stub. It fills the first 256 bytes of Word RAM with the
// descending sequence 255 down to 0 (so byte i of Word RAM ends up
// holding value i), copies that block through to PRG-RAM at
// 0x028000, records both checksums (0+1+...+255 = 0x7F80) in
// PRG-RAM cells, publishes the copy checksum as comm status 1 and
// the done magic 0x600D as comm status 0, then waits for the main
// CPU comm flag, stores the main CPU acknowledgement from comm
// command 0 (the main stub sends comm status 1 XOR 0xFFFF, which is
// 0x807F), sets sub flag 2 and idles.
var cdTestIP = []byte{
	0x41, 0xF9, 0x00, 0x20, 0x01, 0x00, // lea $200100, a0
	0x74, 0x00, // moveq #0, d2
	0x30, 0x3C, 0x00, 0xFF, // move.w #$FF, d0
	0x11, 0x00, // fill: move.b d0, -(a0)
	0xD4, 0x40, // add.w d0, d2
	0x51, 0xC8, 0xFF, 0xFA, // dbra d0, fill
	0x41, 0xF9, 0x00, 0x20, 0x00, 0x00, // lea $200000, a0
	0x43, 0xF9, 0x00, 0x02, 0x80, 0x00, // lea $028000, a1
	0x76, 0x00, // moveq #0, d3
	0x78, 0x00, // moveq #0, d4
	0x32, 0x3C, 0x00, 0xFF, // move.w #$FF, d1
	0x18, 0x18, // copy: move.b (a0)+, d4
	0x12, 0xC4, // move.b d4, (a1)+
	0xD6, 0x44, // add.w d4, d3
	0x51, 0xC9, 0xFF, 0xF8, // dbra d1, copy
	0x23, 0xC2, 0x00, 0x02, 0x05, 0x00, // move.l d2, $020500
	0x23, 0xC3, 0x00, 0x02, 0x05, 0x10, // move.l d3, $020510
	0x33, 0xC3, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x22, // move.w d3, $FF8022
	0x33, 0xFC, 0x60, 0x0D, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x20, // move.w #$600D, $FF8020
	0x10, 0x39, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x0E, // poll: move.b $FF800E, d0
	0x0C, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, // cmpi.b #1, d0
	0x66, 0x00, 0xFF, 0xF4, // bne poll
	0x30, 0x39, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x10, // move.w $FF8010, d0
	0x33, 0xC0, 0x00, 0x02, 0x05, 0x08, // move.w d0, $020508
	0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x0F, // move.b #2, $FF800F
	0x60, 0xFE, // idle: bra idle
}

// runUntilSubDone runs frames until the IP sets sub flag 2 and
// reports whether that happened within maxFrames.
func runUntilSubDone(sys *System, maxFrames int) bool {
	for i := 0; i < maxFrames; i++ {
		if sys.CDUnit().SubFlag() == 2 {
			return true
		}
		sys.RunFrame()
	}
	return sys.CDUnit().SubFlag() == 2
}

// TestCDBootHandshake boots a disc with no cartridge loaded: the
// main stub releases the sub CPU, the boot stub loads the IP, and
// the two sides complete the comm handshake.
func TestCDBootHandshake(t *testing.T) {
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadDisc(makeSCDISO(t, cdTestIP)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if !sys.CDAttached() {
		t.Fatalf("CDAttached = false after LoadDisc")
	}
	if !runUntilSubDone(sys, 180) {
		t.Fatalf("sub flag = %#02x after 180 frames, want 2 (boot handshake never completed)", sys.CDUnit().SubFlag())
	}
	u := sys.CDUnit()
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		if got := u.WordRAM()[i]; got != byte(i) {
			t.Fatalf("WordRAM[%d] = %#02x, want %#02x", i, got, byte(i))
		}
		if got := u.PRGRAM()[0x8000+i]; got != byte(i) {
			t.Fatalf("PRGRAM[%#x] = %#02x, want %#02x", 0x8000+i, got, byte(i))
		}
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(u.PRGRAM()[0x500:0x504]); got != 0x7F80 {
		t.Fatalf("fill checksum cell = %#08x, want 0x7F80", got)
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(u.PRGRAM()[0x510:0x514]); got != 0x7F80 {
		t.Fatalf("copy checksum cell = %#08x, want 0x7F80", got)
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(u.PRGRAM()[0x508:0x50A]); got != 0x807F {
		t.Fatalf("ack cell = %#04x, want 0x807F", got)
	}
}

// TestCDStateDeterminism proves a CD mode save state restores into
// a fresh machine and continues byte-identically.
func TestCDStateDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	iso := makeSCDISO(t, cdTestIP)

	a := New()
	if err := a.LoadDisc(iso); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc A: %v", err)
	}
	if !runUntilSubDone(a, 180) {
		t.Fatalf("machine A: sub flag = %#02x, want 2", a.CDUnit().SubFlag())
	}
	sA := make([]byte, a.SerializeSize())
	if err := a.Serialize(sA); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize A: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 15; i++ {
		a.RunFrame()
	}
	sA2 := make([]byte, a.SerializeSize())
	if err := a.Serialize(sA2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize A2: %v", err)
	}

	b := New()
	if err := b.LoadDisc(iso); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc B: %v", err)
	}
	if err := b.Deserialize(sA); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize B: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 15; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	sB2 := make([]byte, b.SerializeSize())
	if err := b.Serialize(sB2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize B2: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(sA2, sB2) {
		t.Fatalf("state after restore plus 15 frames differs from the unrestored run")
	}

	cartSys := New()
	if err := cartSys.LoadGame(ymTimerROM(0x05)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame cart: %v", err)
	}
	if cartSys.SerializeSize() >= a.SerializeSize() {
		t.Fatalf("cartridge SerializeSize %d, want smaller than CD mode %d", cartSys.SerializeSize(), a.SerializeSize())
	}
	cartSized := make([]byte, cartSys.SerializeSize())
	if err := a.Deserialize(cartSized); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize of a cartridge-sized buffer in CD mode succeeded, want an error")
	}
}

// TestCDInertWithCartridge proves that attaching a disc alongside a
// cartridge leaves the cartridge fully in control: the sub CPU is
// never released, so the CD side stays at its power-on state.
func TestCDInertWithCartridge(t *testing.T) {
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(ymTimerROM(0x05)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sys.LoadDisc(makeSCDISO(t, cdTestIP)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(sys.SystemRAM()[0:4]); got != ymTimerMagic {
		t.Fatalf("RAM magic = %#08x, want %#08x: the cartridge program was disturbed by the CD attachment", got, ymTimerMagic)
	}
	u := sys.CDUnit()
	if got := u.SubFlag(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("SubFlag = %#02x, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := u.CommStatus(0); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("CommStatus(0) = %#04x, want 0", got)
	}
	for i, v := range u.PRGRAM() {
		if v != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("PRGRAM[%#x] = %#02x, want all zeros (sub CPU was never released)", i, v)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/system/system_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// ymTimerROM builds a synthetic cartridge whose 68000 programs
// YM2612 timer A with a 432 master-clock period (NA = 1000), then
// polls the status port in a tight loop and writes a magic value
// to work RAM the moment it sees the timer A flag. reg27 is the
// value written to the timer mode register: 0x05 loads and enables
// timer A, 0x04 enables without loading (the timer never counts).
//
// The encodings are plain absolute-long moves: 0x13FC is
// move.b #imm, addr.l; 0x0839 is btst #imm, addr.l; 0x23FC is
// move.l #imm, addr.l. (In the mode-7 destination field the
// register bits select the sub-mode, and absolute long is 001.)
func ymTimerROM(reg27 byte) []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x10000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0:], 0x00FFFE00) // initial SSP
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[4:], 0x00000200) // reset PC
	copy(rom[0x100:], "SEGA GENESIS    ")

	var code []byte
	pair := func(reg, val byte) { // select register, write data port
		code = append(code, 0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, reg, 0x00, 0xA0, 0x40, 0x00)
		code = append(code, 0x13, 0xFC, 0x00, val, 0x00, 0xA0, 0x40, 0x01)
	}
	pair(0x24, 0xFA) // timer A period high bits
	pair(0x25, 0x00) // NA = 1000, period 18*(1024-1000) = 432 clocks
	pair(0x27, reg27)
	poll := len(code)
	code = append(code, 0x08, 0x39, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xA0, 0x40, 0x00) // btst #0, status
	code = append(code, 0x67, byte(poll-(len(code)+2)))                 // beq.s poll
	code = append(code, 0x23, 0xFC, 0x1B, 0xAD, 0xB0, 0x02,
		0x00, 0xFF, 0x00, 0x00) // move.l #0x1BADB002, $FF0000.l
	code = append(code, 0x60, 0xFE) // bra.s *
	copy(rom[0x200:], code)
	return rom
}

const ymTimerMagic = 0x1BADB002

// TestYMTimerFlagVisibleMidFrame proves the system steps the
// YM2612 timers while the frame runs: a 68000 polling the status
// port sees the timer A flag during the first frame and reacts.
// If the timers only moved inside the frame-end audio render, the
// poll loop would still be spinning when the frame ends and the
// magic would not be in RAM yet.
func TestYMTimerFlagVisibleMidFrame(t *testing.T) {
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(ymTimerROM(0x05)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame: %v", err)
	}
	sys.RunFrame()
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(sys.SystemRAM()[0:4]); got != ymTimerMagic {
		t.Fatalf("RAM magic after one frame = %#08x, want %#08x: the polling 68000 never saw the timer A flag mid-frame", got, ymTimerMagic)
	}
}

// TestYMTimerFlagNeedsLoad is the control: with the load bit clear
// the timer never counts, the flag never rises, and the magic
// must stay out of RAM. It guards against the test above passing
// for a reason other than real timer expiry.
func TestYMTimerFlagNeedsLoad(t *testing.T) {
	sys := New()
	if err := sys.LoadGame(ymTimerROM(0x04)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame: %v", err)
	}
	sys.RunFrame()
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(sys.SystemRAM()[0:4]); got == ymTimerMagic {
		t.Fatalf("RAM magic present with timer A never loaded: the flag rose without the timer counting")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-genesis/vdp/vdp.go ====================

// Package vdp emulates the Sega Genesis VDP (video display processor).
//
// Clean-room implementation from published hardware documentation
// (the Genesis VDP register map, command protocol and tile formats are
// documented in Sega's Genesis Technical Overview and Charles MacDonald's
// VDP notes).
//
// PINNED API (bus, system and libretro are written against this; do not
// change signatures):
//
//	New() *VDP
//	SetDMASource(f func(addr uint32) uint16)
//	ReadPort(off uint32) uint16      off = 68k address & 0x1F within 0xC00000 window
//	WritePort(off uint32, val uint16)
//	BeginFrame()
//	RenderLine(y int)                renders visible line y (0..DisplayHeight()-1)
//	EnterVBlank() bool               sets the vblank flag; true if IRQ6 is enabled
//	ExitVBlank()
//	LineIRQ(y int) bool              true when an HBlank IRQ4 fires on line y
//	Framebuffer() []uint16           RGB565 pixels, Width() x Height()
//	DisplayWidth() int               256 (H32) or 320 (H40)
//	DisplayHeight() int              224 (NTSC) or 240
//	SerializeSize() int
//	Serialize(buf []byte) error
//	Deserialize(buf []byte) error
//
// Port offsets (off): 0x00/0x02 data, 0x04/0x06 control (read = status),
// 0x08-0x0E HV counter, 0x10/0x11 PSG write (bus forwards those to sound),
// 0x18 debug register (ignore), others mirror.
package vdp

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Frame geometry maxima.
const (
	MaxWidth  = 320
	MaxHeight = 240
)

// accessTarget identifies the memory selected by a VDP command code.
// The low command bits encode VRAM as 0, CRAM as 1 (bit 1 set) and
// VSRAM as 2 (bit 2 set); bit 0 distinguishes a write (1) from a read (0).
type accessTarget int

const (
	targetVRAM accessTarget = iota
	targetCRAM
	targetVSRAM
)

// VDP holds the full video chip state.
type VDP struct {
	Regs [24]uint8 // control registers 0-23

	VRAM  [0x10000]uint8 // 64KB video RAM (patterns, name tables, sprite table, hscroll)
	CRAM  [128]uint8     // 64 colors x 2 bytes (9-bit BGR)
	VSRAM [80]uint8      // vertical scroll, 40 entries x 2 bytes

	// Command state
	addr    uint32 // current VRAM/CRAM/VSRAM address (17 bits used)
	code    uint8  // access type from the two control writes
	pending bool   // first control word latched
	first   uint16 // latched first control word

	// Status / timing
	vblank    bool
	dmaBusy   bool
	dmaFill   bool
	dmaSrc    uint32
	dmaLen    uint16
	hintCtr   int // scanlines remaining before the next HBlank interrupt
	readBuf   uint16
	currentLn int // last line handed to RenderLine, for the HV counter
	frames    int // completed frames (kept for timing/debug state)

	dmaSource func(addr uint32) uint16

	fb []uint16 // framebuffer, MaxWidth*MaxHeight RGB565

	// Palette cache: the 64 CRAM entries converted to RGB565.
	// Rendering used to run the conversion (with its multiplies
	// and divides) once per pixel; the cache is rebuilt only when
	// the CRAM bytes actually change, detected by comparing
	// against palShadow at the start of each rendered line.
	palCache  [64]uint16
	palShadow [128]uint8
	palValid  bool
}

// New returns a VDP in power-on state.
func New() *VDP {
	return &VDP{fb: make([]uint16, MaxWidth*MaxHeight)}
}

// SetDMASource installs the reader the VDP uses for DMA transfers from
// 68k address space (word reads).
func (v *VDP) SetDMASource(f func(addr uint32) uint16) { v.dmaSource = f }

// ReadPort reads one of the VDP ports. off is the offset within the
// 0xC00000 window, already masked to 0x1F by the caller (we mask again
// defensively so mirrors behave the same).
func (v *VDP) ReadPort(off uint32) uint16 {
	switch off & 0x1F {
	case 0x00, 0x02:
		return v.readData()
	case 0x04, 0x06:
		return v.readStatus()
	case 0x08, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0E:
		return v.readHV()
	default:
		// PSG, debug register and unused mirrors read back as zero.
		return 0
	}
}

// WritePort writes one of the VDP ports.
func (v *VDP) WritePort(off uint32, val uint16) {
	switch off & 0x1F {
	case 0x00, 0x02:
		v.writeData(val)
	case 0x04, 0x06:
		v.writeControl(val)
	default:
		// HV counter is read-only; PSG writes are forwarded to the
		// sound section by the bus; the debug register is ignored.
	}
}

// readStatus composes the status register. The top bits are the fixed
// open-bus pattern (0x3400), bit 9 reports an empty FIFO, and bit 4 is
// the vertical blank flag. Reading the status also clears the latched
// first command word; games depend on that side effect.
func (v *VDP) readStatus() uint16 {
	status := uint16(0x3400) | 0x0200 // FIFO empty
	if v.vblank {
		status |= 0x0010
	}
	if v.dmaBusy {
		status |= 0x0004
	}
	v.pending = false
	return status
}

// readHV returns the horizontal/vertical counter pair. Milestone 1 has
// no cycle-level beam position, so the horizontal counter reports a
// fixed mid-line value; the vertical counter tracks the last rendered
// line, or the first vertical blank line while in vblank.
func (v *VDP) readHV() uint16 {
	line := v.currentLn
	if v.vblank {
		line = 224
	}
	if line < 0 {
		line = 0
	}
	const hcount = 0x80
	return uint16(line&0xFF)<<8 | (hcount >> 1)
}

// writeControl runs the two-word command latch and the single-word
// register write encoding.
func (v *VDP) writeControl(word uint16) {
	if !v.pending {
		// A first word of the form 100xxxxx xxxxxxxx is a register
		// write: bits 12-8 select the register, the low byte is the
		// value. It leaves no pending command behind.
		if word&0xE000 == 0x8000 {
			if reg := (word >> 8) & 0x1F; reg < uint16(len(v.Regs)) {
				v.Regs[reg] = uint8(word)
			}
			v.pending = false
			return
		}
		// Otherwise this is the first command word: the low 14 bits
		// are address bits A0-A13 and bits 15/14 are CD1/CD0, which
		// land in code bits 1/0.
		v.first = word
		v.pending = true
		v.addr = uint32(word & 0x3FFF)
		v.code = uint8((word >> 14) & 0x03)
		return
	}

	// Second command word: bits 1-0 are address bits A14-A15 and
	// bits 7-4 are CD5-CD2, which land in code bits 5-2.
	v.pending = false
	v.addr |= uint32(word&0x03) << 14
	v.code |= uint8((word & 0xF0) >> 2)
	v.finishCommand()
}

// finishCommand acts on a completed command word pair: DMA commands run
// (or, for a fill, arm) immediately, and read commands prefetch the
// first word into the read buffer.
func (v *VDP) finishCommand() {
	v.dmaFill = false
	if v.code&0x20 != 0 {
		v.handleDMACommand()
		return
	}
	if v.code&0x01 == 0 {
		v.readBuf = v.readTargetWord(targetForCode(v.code), v.addr)
	}
}

// targetForCode decodes the memory selected by a command code.
func targetForCode(code uint8) accessTarget {
	switch {
	case code&0x04 != 0:
		return targetVSRAM
	case code&0x02 != 0:
		return targetCRAM
	default:
		return targetVRAM
	}
}

// normalizeAddr applies the wrap rules of the selected memory to an
// internal address after an increment.
func normalizeAddr(target accessTarget, addr uint32) uint32 {
	switch target {
	case targetCRAM:
		return addr & 0x7F
	case targetVSRAM:
		return addr % 80
	default:
		return addr & 0xFFFF
	}
}

// readTargetWord reads one 16-bit word from the selected memory at a
// byte address, using the storage byte order of that memory: VRAM words
// are stored low byte first (the byte-swap quirk described at
// writeTargetWord), CRAM and VSRAM words are stored big-endian.
func (v *VDP) readTargetWord(target accessTarget, addr uint32) uint16 {
	switch target {
	case targetCRAM:
		a := addr & 0x7F
		return uint16(v.CRAM[a])<<8 | uint16(v.CRAM[(a+1)&0x7F])
	case targetVSRAM:
		a := addr % 80
		return uint16(v.VSRAM[a])<<8 | uint16(v.VSRAM[(a+1)%80])
	default:
		a := addr & 0xFFFF
		return uint16(v.VRAM[a]) | uint16(v.VRAM[(a+1)&0xFFFF])<<8
	}
}

// writeTargetWord stores one 16-bit word into the selected memory at a
// byte address. VRAM stores the word byte-swapped (low byte at addr,
// high byte at addr+1): the 68k data bus is wired to the VDP so that a
// word written by the CPU lands swapped in VRAM, and tile patterns are
// consequently read back linearly from VRAM when rendering. CRAM and
// VSRAM store the word big-endian, with no swap.
func (v *VDP) writeTargetWord(target accessTarget, addr uint32, val uint16) {
	switch target {
	case targetCRAM:
		a := addr & 0x7F
		v.CRAM[a] = uint8(val >> 8)
		v.CRAM[(a+1)&0x7F] = uint8(val)
	case targetVSRAM:
		a := addr % 80
		v.VSRAM[a] = uint8(val >> 8)
		v.VSRAM[(a+1)%80] = uint8(val)
	default:
		a := addr & 0xFFFF
		v.VRAM[a] = uint8(val)
		v.VRAM[(a+1)&0xFFFF] = uint8(val >> 8)
	}
}

// readData services a data port read. The first read after a read
// command returns the prefetched word; each read then advances the
// address by the auto-increment register and prefetches the next word.
func (v *VDP) readData() uint16 {
	if v.code&0x20 != 0 || v.code&0x01 != 0 {
		// Not a read command; the buffer still holds its last value.
		return v.readBuf
	}
	target := targetForCode(v.code)
	result := v.readBuf
	v.addr = normalizeAddr(target, v.addr+uint32(v.Regs[15]))
	v.readBuf = v.readTargetWord(target, v.addr)
	return result
}

// writeData services a data port write. If a VRAM fill DMA is armed, the
// written word is the fill data and triggers the fill instead.
func (v *VDP) writeData(val uint16) {
	if v.dmaFill {
		v.dmaFill = false
		v.performFill(val)
		return
	}
	if v.code&0x20 != 0 || v.code&0x01 == 0 {
		// DMA commands and read commands do not take data writes.
		return
	}
	target := targetForCode(v.code)
	v.writeTargetWord(target, v.addr, val)
	v.addr = normalizeAddr(target, v.addr+uint32(v.Regs[15]))
}

// dmaLengthWords returns the DMA length in words from registers 19/20;
// a programmed length of zero means 0x10000 words.
func (v *VDP) dmaLengthWords() int {
	n := int(v.Regs[19]) | int(v.Regs[20])<<8
	if n == 0 {
		return 0x10000
	}
	return n
}

// dmaSourceByteAddr returns the DMA source as a byte address: registers
// 21/22/23 hold a word address, so the byte address is that value
// shifted left by one. mask limits the high register to the bits that
// are address (0x7F normally; register 23's top two bits are the DMA
// mode, so a VRAM copy uses 0x3F).
func (v *VDP) dmaSourceByteAddr(mask uint8) uint32 {
	raw := uint32(v.Regs[21]) |
		uint32(v.Regs[22])<<8 |
		uint32(v.Regs[23]&mask)<<16
	return raw << 1
}

// handleDMACommand dispatches a completed DMA command (command code bit
// CD5 set) on the mode bits in register 23. DMA does nothing unless
// register 1 bit 4 (DMA enable) is set.
func (v *VDP) handleDMACommand() {
	if v.Regs[1]&0x10 == 0 {
		return
	}
	switch mode := v.Regs[23]; {
	case mode&0x80 == 0:
		v.perform68kDMA()
	case mode&0x40 == 0:
		// VRAM fill: the transfer waits for the next data port write,
		// which supplies the fill word. The length is latched now.
		if targetForCode(v.code) != targetVRAM {
			return
		}
		v.dmaLen = uint16(v.Regs[19]) | uint16(v.Regs[20])<<8
		v.dmaFill = true
	default:
		v.performCopyDMA()
	}
}

// perform68kDMA copies the programmed number of words from 68k address
// space (through the DMA source callback) into the selected memory.
// The destination advances by two bytes per word with the target's
// wrap rules; the auto-increment register does not apply to DMA.
func (v *VDP) perform68kDMA() {
	target := targetForCode(v.code)
	src := v.dmaSourceByteAddr(0x7F)
	v.dmaSrc = src
	v.dmaBusy = true
	for i, n := 0, v.dmaLengthWords(); i < n; i++ {
		var word uint16
		if v.dmaSource != nil {
			word = v.dmaSource(src)
		}
		v.writeTargetWord(target, v.addr, word)
		src += 2
		v.addr = normalizeAddr(target, v.addr+2)
	}
	v.dmaBusy = false
}

// performFill runs an armed VRAM fill: the supplied word is stored,
// byte-swapped like every VRAM word, at consecutive word addresses for
// the latched length.
func (v *VDP) performFill(fillWord uint16) {
	n := int(v.dmaLen)
	if n == 0 {
		n = 0x10000
	}
	v.dmaBusy = true
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		v.writeTargetWord(targetVRAM, v.addr, fillWord)
		v.addr = normalizeAddr(targetVRAM, v.addr+2)
	}
	v.dmaBusy = false
}

// performCopyDMA copies words within VRAM from the DMA source address
// to the command address. Bytes move in stored order, so the copy is
// exact regardless of the VRAM word byte-swap.
func (v *VDP) performCopyDMA() {
	src := v.dmaSourceByteAddr(0x3F)
	v.dmaSrc = src
	v.dmaBusy = true
	for i, n := 0, v.dmaLengthWords(); i < n; i++ {
		s := src & 0xFFFF
		d := v.addr & 0xFFFF
		b0 := v.VRAM[s]
		b1 := v.VRAM[(s+1)&0xFFFF]
		v.VRAM[d] = b0
		v.VRAM[(d+1)&0xFFFF] = b1
		src += 2
		v.addr = normalizeAddr(targetVRAM, v.addr+2)
	}
	v.dmaBusy = false
}

// BeginFrame starts a new frame: the horizontal interrupt counter
// reloads from register 10.
func (v *VDP) BeginFrame() {
	v.hintCtr = int(v.Regs[10])
}

// EnterVBlank marks the start of vertical blank and reports whether the
// vertical blank interrupt (IRQ6) is enabled in register 1 bit 5.
func (v *VDP) EnterVBlank() bool {
	v.vblank = true
	return v.Regs[1]&0x20 != 0
}

// ExitVBlank marks the end of vertical blank.
func (v *VDP) ExitVBlank() {
	v.vblank = false
	v.frames++
}

// LineIRQ reports whether a horizontal blank interrupt (IRQ4) fires on
// scanline y. The counter reloads to register 10 each time it fires, so
// interrupts occur every register 10 + 1 active lines. The system calls
// this once per line; only active display lines count.
func (v *VDP) LineIRQ(y int) bool {
	if v.Regs[0]&0x04 == 0 {
		return false
	}
	if y < 0 || y >= v.DisplayHeight() {
		return false
	}
	if v.hintCtr == 0 {
		v.hintCtr = int(v.Regs[10])
		return true
	}
	v.hintCtr--
	return false
}

// DisplayWidth returns the horizontal resolution: 320 in H40 mode
// (register 12 bits 7 and 0 both set), otherwise 256.
func (v *VDP) DisplayWidth() int {
	if v.Regs[12]&0x81 == 0x81 {
		return 320
	}
	return 256
}

// DisplayHeight returns 240 when register 1 bit 3 selects the 240-line
// mode, otherwise 224.
func (v *VDP) DisplayHeight() int {
	if v.Regs[1]&0x08 != 0 {
		return 240
	}
	return 224
}

// Framebuffer returns the RGB565 frame. It is always MaxWidth wide; the
// system crops each line to DisplayWidth when presenting.
func (v *VDP) Framebuffer() []uint16 {
	return v.fb
}

// cramColor converts a CRAM palette index (0-63) to RGB565. A CRAM word
// is laid out 0000 BBB0 GGG0 RRR0: three bits per channel, scaled to
// the RGB565 channel ranges.
func (v *VDP) cramColor(index int) uint16 {
	a := (index * 2) & 0x7F
	word := uint16(v.CRAM[a])<<8 | uint16(v.CRAM[(a+1)&0x7F])
	r := uint32((word >> 1) & 0x07)
	g := uint32((word >> 5) & 0x07)
	b := uint32((word >> 9) & 0x07)
	return uint16(r*31/7)<<11 | uint16(g*63/7)<<5 | uint16(b*31/7)
}

// refreshPalette rebuilds the RGB565 palette cache when the CRAM
// contents differ from the shadow copy taken at the last rebuild.
// It runs once per rendered line; CRAM writes are rare compared to
// the hundreds of thousands of pixel lookups the cache serves.
func (v *VDP) refreshPalette() {
	if v.palValid && v.palShadow == v.CRAM {
		return
	}
	v.palShadow = v.CRAM
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		v.palCache[i] = v.cramColor(i)
	}
	v.palValid = true
}

// backdropColor returns the color behind every layer, selected by
// register 7 (palette in bits 5-4, color in bits 3-0).
func (v *VDP) backdropColor() uint16 {
	index := int((v.Regs[7]>>4)&0x03)*16 + int(v.Regs[7]&0x0F)
	return v.palCache[index]
}

// vramWord reads a 16-bit word from VRAM in CPU order: because data
// port writes store VRAM words byte-swapped (low byte first), the word
// a program wrote is recovered as low | high<<8.
func (v *VDP) vramWord(addr int) uint16 {
	a := uint32(addr) & 0xFFFF
	return uint16(v.VRAM[a]) | uint16(v.VRAM[(a+1)&0xFFFF])<<8
}

// planeCells decodes register 16 into the plane size in cells. The
// encoding is 0=32, 1=64, 2=invalid (treated as 128), 3=128 for both
// the width (bits 1-0) and the height (bits 5-4).
func (v *VDP) planeCells() (wCells, hCells int) {
	sizes := [4]int{32, 64, 128, 128}
	return sizes[v.Regs[16]&0x03], sizes[(v.Regs[16]>>4)&0x03]
}

// hScroll returns the horizontal scroll offset for a plane on line y.
// The scroll table holds one pair of words (plane A, then plane B) per
// row; register 11 bits 1-0 select full-screen (row 0), per-cell (one
// row per 8 lines) or per-line scrolling. The convention used here:
// screen pixel x shows plane pixel x + scroll, where scroll is the
// negated table value (the table stores the shift as a two's complement
// value that the hardware subtracts).
func (v *VDP) hScroll(planeB bool, y int) int {
	row := 0
	switch v.Regs[11] & 0x03 {
	case 2:
		row = y &^ 7
	case 3:
		row = y
	}
	base := int(v.Regs[13]&0x3F) << 10
	off := base + row*4
	if planeB {
		off += 2
	}
	return -int(int16(v.vramWord(off)))
}

// vScroll returns the vertical scroll offset for a plane at screen
// column x. Register 11 bit 2 selects full-screen scrolling (VSRAM
// entries 0 and 1) or per-16-pixel-column scrolling (entry pairs per
// column). Only the low 10 bits of each entry are significant. The
// entry index is at most 39 (20 columns times 2, plus the plane B
// offset), so its byte offset is at most 78 and the big-endian word
// read never wraps the 80-byte VSRAM.
func (v *VDP) vScroll(planeB bool, x int) int {
	entry := 0
	if v.Regs[11]&0x04 != 0 {
		entry = (x / 16) * 2
	}
	if planeB {
		entry++
	}
	a := entry * 2
	return int((uint16(v.VSRAM[a])<<8 | uint16(v.VSRAM[a+1])) & 0x3FF)
}

// tileRowIndices decodes one 8-pixel row of a tile into palette
// indices (0-15). The entry's vertical flip selects the mirrored
// row; its horizontal flip reverses the decoded order. Pattern
// bytes are read through the byte-swapped VRAM storage (see
// writeTargetWord): the byte holding pixel pair p of a row lives
// at the pair's address XOR 1, with the even pixel in the high
// nibble.
func (v *VDP) tileRowIndices(entry uint16, ty int, out *[8]uint8) {
	if entry&0x1000 != 0 { // vertical flip
		ty = 7 - ty
	}
	rowAddr := int(entry&0x07FF)*32 + ty*4
	for p := 0; p < 4; p++ {
		b := v.VRAM[((rowAddr+p)^1)&0xFFFF]
		out[2*p] = b >> 4
		out[2*p+1] = b & 0x0F
	}
	if entry&0x0800 != 0 { // horizontal flip
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			out[i], out[7-i] = out[7-i], out[i]
		}
	}
}

// tilePixel resolves one pixel of a tile given its name table entry and
// the pixel's position (0-7) inside the tile, applying the entry's flip
// bits. It returns the RGB565 color, the priority bit, and whether the
// pixel is opaque (palette index 0 of any palette is transparent).
// The scanline renderer works a tile row at a time through
// tileRowIndices; this per-pixel form stays as the reference for the
// same semantics.
func (v *VDP) tilePixel(entry uint16, tx, ty int) (uint16, bool, bool) {
	var row [8]uint8
	v.tileRowIndices(entry, ty, &row)
	nibble := row[tx]
	if nibble == 0 {
		return 0, false, false
	}
	palette := (entry >> 13) & 0x03
	return v.cramColor(int(palette)*16 + int(nibble)), entry&0x8000 != 0, true
}

// renderPlaneLine resolves one scanline of a background plane into
// the color, priority and opacity arrays. It walks the line in
// segments that never cross a tile boundary or a 16-pixel vertical
// scroll column boundary, so within a segment the name table entry,
// the decoded tile row and the vertical scroll are all constant and
// are resolved once instead of once per pixel. For plane A the
// window overlay is applied afterwards by renderWindowLine.
func (v *VDP) renderPlaneLine(planeB bool, y, width int, col *[MaxWidth]uint16, pri, ok *[MaxWidth]bool) {
	wCells, hCells := v.planeCells()
	planeW, planeH := wCells*8, hCells*8
	var base int
	if planeB {
		base = int(v.Regs[4]&0x07) << 13
	} else {
		base = int(v.Regs[2]&0x38) << 10
	}
	// The horizontal scroll is a function of the line only, in
	// every scroll mode, so it is read once here. Screen pixel x
	// shows plane pixel x + scroll (see hScroll). The plane
	// dimensions are always powers of two (32, 64 or 128 cells),
	// so wrapping a coordinate is a mask, not a modulo; for the
	// possibly negative scroll the two's complement mask gives
	// the same result as the mathematical mod.
	sx := v.hScroll(planeB, y) & (planeW - 1)
	colMode := v.Regs[11]&0x04 != 0 // per-column vertical scrolling
	var row [8]uint8
	for x := 0; x < width; {
		srcY := (y + v.vScroll(planeB, x)) & (planeH - 1)
		entry := v.vramWord(base + ((srcY/8)*wCells+(sx/8))*2)
		v.tileRowIndices(entry, srcY&7, &row)
		palBase := int((entry>>13)&0x03) * 16
		prio := entry&0x8000 != 0
		tx := sx & 7
		n := 8 - tx
		if colMode {
			// A segment must not cross a vertical scroll
			// column boundary: the scroll can change there,
			// giving the rest of the tile a different row.
			if rem := 16 - (x & 15); n > rem {
				n = rem
			}
		}
		if n > width-x {
			n = width - x
		}
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			if nib := row[tx+i]; nib != 0 {
				col[x+i] = v.palCache[palBase+int(nib)]
				pri[x+i] = prio
				ok[x+i] = true
			}
		}
		x += n
		sx += n
		if sx >= planeW {
			sx -= planeW
		}
	}
	if !planeB {
		v.renderWindowLine(y, width, col, pri, ok)
	}
}

// renderWindowLine overlays the window plane onto plane A's arrays
// for one scanline. Register 17 sets the horizontal edge in
// 16-pixel units (bit 7: the window extends rightward from the edge
// instead of leftward from 0); register 18 sets the vertical edge
// in 8-line units (bit 7: downward instead of upward). For a given
// line the window therefore covers one contiguous x range aligned
// to whole tile cells. The window plane is not scrolled; its name
// table has a fixed row stride: 64 cells in H40, 32 in H32. A
// transparent window pixel clears plane A's pixel, matching the
// old per-pixel rule that the window result replaced plane A's
// whenever the pixel fell inside the window rectangle.
func (v *VDP) renderWindowLine(y, width int, col *[MaxWidth]uint16, pri, ok *[MaxWidth]bool) {
	hEdge := int(v.Regs[17]&0x1F) * 16
	vEdge := int(v.Regs[18]&0x1F) * 8
	inY := y < vEdge
	if v.Regs[18]&0x80 != 0 {
		inY = y >= vEdge
	}
	if !inY {
		return
	}
	x0, x1 := 0, hEdge
	if v.Regs[17]&0x80 != 0 {
		x0, x1 = hEdge, width
	}
	if x1 > width {
		x1 = width
	}
	if x0 >= x1 {
		return
	}
	mask := uint8(0x7C)
	stride := 64
	if width == 256 {
		mask = 0x78
		stride = 32
	}
	base := int(v.Regs[3]&mask) << 10
	var row [8]uint8
	for x := x0; x < x1; x += 8 {
		entry := v.vramWord(base + ((y/8)*stride+(x/8))*2)
		v.tileRowIndices(entry, y&7, &row)
		palBase := int((entry>>13)&0x03) * 16
		prio := entry&0x8000 != 0
		for i := 0; i < 8 && x+i < x1; i++ {
			if nib := row[i]; nib != 0 {
				col[x+i] = v.palCache[palBase+int(nib)]
				pri[x+i] = prio
				ok[x+i] = true
			} else {
				ok[x+i] = false
			}
		}
	}
}

// renderSprites draws one scanline of sprites into the low and high
// priority sprite layers. Sprites are visited in link-chain order
// starting from sprite 0; within a priority layer the earliest sprite
// wins a pixel, as on hardware. Per line at most 20 sprites (H40) or
// 16 (H32) are drawn, loosely applying the hardware sprite pixel
// budget of one display width.
//
// Sprite attribute format (8 bytes per sprite, read here as four
// words): word 0 is the Y position (bits 9-0, biased by 128); word 1
// holds the size byte in its high half (bits 11-10 horizontal cells-1,
// bits 9-8 vertical cells-1) and the link byte in its low half (bits
// 6-0, the next sprite's index); word 2 is the pattern attribute
// (bit 15 priority, bits 14-13 palette, bit 12 vertical flip, bit 11
// horizontal flip, bits 10-0 first tile); word 3 is the X position
// (bits 8-0, biased by 128). Tiles inside a sprite are arranged
// column-major: the tile index increases down a column first.
func (v *VDP) renderSprites(y int, low, high *[MaxWidth]uint16, lowOK, highOK *[MaxWidth]bool) {
	width := v.DisplayWidth()
	maxSprites, lineLimit := 80, 20
	if width == 256 {
		maxSprites, lineLimit = 64, 16
	}
	base := int(v.Regs[5]&0x7E) << 9
	pixelBudget := width
	drawn := 0

	var visited [80]bool
	index := 0
	for n := 0; n < maxSprites; n++ {
		if index < 0 || index >= maxSprites || visited[index] {
			break
		}
		visited[index] = true
		entryBase := base + index*8
		yWord := v.vramWord(entryBase)
		sizeLink := v.vramWord(entryBase + 2)
		attr := v.vramWord(entryBase + 4)
		xWord := v.vramWord(entryBase + 6)
		link := int(sizeLink & 0x7F)

		hCells := int((sizeLink>>10)&0x03) + 1
		vCells := int((sizeLink>>8)&0x03) + 1
		top := int(yWord&0x03FF) - 128
		left := int(xWord&0x01FF) - 128
		sprW, sprH := hCells*8, vCells*8

		if y >= top && y < top+sprH && left < width && left+sprW > 0 {
			drawn++
			if drawn > lineLimit {
				break
			}
			layer, layerOK := low, lowOK
			if attr&0x8000 != 0 {
				layer, layerOK = high, highOK
			}
			sy := y - top
			// Work in unflipped sprite space so flips move
			// both the tile order and the pixels inside a
			// tile, as the hardware does. The row's pixels
			// are decoded once into unflipped order (tiles
			// inside a sprite are column-major: the tile
			// index increases down a column first); the loop
			// below then only mirrors the lookup coordinate.
			srcY := sy
			if attr&0x1000 != 0 { // vertical flip
				srcY = sprH - 1 - sy
			}
			var rowPix [32]uint8
			for tc := 0; tc < hCells; tc++ {
				tile := int(attr&0x07FF) + tc*vCells + srcY/8
				rowAddr := tile*32 + (srcY&7)*4
				for p := 0; p < 4; p++ {
					b := v.VRAM[((rowAddr+p)^1)&0xFFFF] // byte-swapped storage, as in tileRowIndices
					rowPix[tc*8+2*p] = b >> 4
					rowPix[tc*8+2*p+1] = b & 0x0F
				}
			}
			palBase := int((attr>>13)&0x03) * 16
			for sx := 0; sx < sprW && pixelBudget > 0; sx++ {
				pixelBudget--
				screenX := left + sx
				if screenX < 0 || screenX >= width {
					continue
				}
				srcX := sx
				if attr&0x0800 != 0 { // horizontal flip
					srcX = sprW - 1 - sx
				}
				nibble := rowPix[srcX]
				if nibble == 0 || layerOK[screenX] {
					continue
				}
				layer[screenX] = v.palCache[palBase+int(nibble)]
				layerOK[screenX] = true
			}
			if pixelBudget <= 0 {
				break
			}
		}

		if link == index {
			break
		}
		index = link
	}
}

// RenderLine renders one visible scanline into the framebuffer. Layers
// compose back to front in priority order: backdrop, plane B low,
// plane A low, sprites low, plane B high, plane A high, sprites high;
// a layer pixel covers what is below only when it is opaque.
func (v *VDP) RenderLine(y int) {
	if y < 0 || y >= MaxHeight || y >= v.DisplayHeight() {
		return
	}
	v.currentLn = y
	v.refreshPalette()
	width := v.DisplayWidth()
	line := v.fb[y*MaxWidth : y*MaxWidth+MaxWidth]
	backdrop := v.backdropColor()
