package r4300

import (
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// COP1 encoders.
func mtc1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 4<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11 }
func mfc1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 0<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11 }
func dmtc1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x11<<26 | 5<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11
}
func dmfc1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x11<<26 | 1<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11
}
func ctc1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 6<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11 }
func fpArith(fmt, ft, fs, fd, funct uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x11<<26 | fmt<<21 | ft<<16 | fs<<11 | fd<<6 | funct
}
func bc1f(off int16) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 8<<21 | 0<<16 | uint32(uint16(off)) }
func bc1t(off int16) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 8<<21 | 1<<16 | uint32(uint16(off)) }

func f32bits(f float32) uint32 { return math.Float32bits(f) }

func TestFPURegisterPairFR0(t *testing.T) {
	// With FR=0, a double lives in the low words of an
	// even/odd pair: 1.5 = 0x3FF8000000000000, so $f0 gets
	// the low word 0 and $f1 the high word 0x3FF80000.
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		lui(rT0, 0x3FF8),
		mtc1(rT0, 1),            // $f1 = high word
		mtc1(rZero, 0),          // $f0 = low word 0
		dmfc1(rT1, 0),           // t1 = 1.5 as raw double
		fpArith(17, 0, 0, 2, 0), // add.d $f2, $f0, $f0 = 3.0
		dmfc1(rT2, 2),
	)
	run(c, 6)
	if c.Reg[rT1] != 0x3FF8000000000000 {
		t.Errorf("pair read: got %x", c.Reg[rT1])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT2] != 0x4008000000000000 {
		t.Errorf("add.d: got %x", c.Reg[rT2])
	}
}

func TestFPURegisterFR1(t *testing.T) {
	// With FR=1 a double occupies one whole register.
	c2, _ := setupCPU(
		dmtc1(rT0, 3),
		dmfc1(rT1, 3),
		fpArith(16, 3, 3, 4, 6), // mov.s $f4, $f3 (single view of low word)
		mfc1(rT2, 4),
	)
	c2.CP0[Cp0Status] |= StatusFR
	c2.Reg[rT0] = 0x3FF8000000000000
	run(c2, 4)
	if c2.Reg[rT1] != 0x3FF8000000000000 {
		t.Errorf("fr1 dmtc1/dmfc1: got %x", c2.Reg[rT1])
	}
	if uint32(c2.Reg[rT2]) != 0x00000000 {
		t.Errorf("fr1 single view of 1.5 low word: got %x", uint32(c2.Reg[rT2]))
	}
}

func TestFPURoundingModesConvert(t *testing.T) {
	// CVT.W.S honors FCSR RM: values 2.5 and -2.5.
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		rm   uint32
		in   float32
		want int32
	}{
		{0, 2.5, 2}, // RN ties to even
		{0, 3.5, 4}, // RN ties to even
		{1, 2.5, 2}, // RZ
		{1, -2.5, -2},
		{2, 2.5, 3}, // RP
		{2, -2.5, -2},
		{3, 2.5, 2}, // RM
		{3, -2.5, -3},
	} {
		c, _ := setupCPU(
			mtc1(rT0, 0),
			fpArith(16, 0, 0, 2, 36), // cvt.w.s $f2, $f0
			mfc1(rT1, 2),
		)
		c.Reg[rT0] = uint64(f32bits(tc.in))
		c.FCSR = tc.rm
		run(c, 3)
		if int32(c.Reg[rT1]) != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("cvt.w.s rm=%d in=%v: got %d want %d",
				tc.rm, tc.in, int32(c.Reg[rT1]), tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestFPUAddSingleRoundingModes(t *testing.T) {
	// 1.0 + 2^-24 is exactly halfway between 1.0 and the
	// next single (spacing 2^-23): RN keeps 1.0 (ties to
	// even), RP steps up, RZ and RM keep 1.0.
	const tiny = 0x33800000 // 2^-24
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		rm   uint32
		want uint32
	}{
		{0, 0x3F800000},
		{1, 0x3F800000},
		{2, 0x3F800001},
		{3, 0x3F800000},
	} {
		c, _ := setupCPU(
			mtc1(rT0, 0),
			mtc1(rT1, 1),
			fpArith(16, 1, 0, 2, 0), // add.s $f2, $f0, $f1
			mfc1(rT2, 2),
		)
		c.Reg[rT0] = uint64(f32bits(1.0))
		c.Reg[rT1] = uint64(tiny)
		c.FCSR = tc.rm
		run(c, 4)
		if uint32(c.Reg[rT2]) != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("add.s rm=%d: got %08x want %08x",
				tc.rm, uint32(c.Reg[rT2]), tc.want)
		}
	}
	// -1.0 + -2^-24 under RM steps away from zero.
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		mtc1(rT0, 0),
		mtc1(rT1, 1),
		fpArith(16, 1, 0, 2, 0),
		mfc1(rT2, 2),
	)
	c.Reg[rT0] = uint64(f32bits(-1.0))
	c.Reg[rT1] = uint64(0xB3800000) // -2^-24
	c.FCSR = 3
	run(c, 4)
	if uint32(c.Reg[rT2]) != 0xBF800001 {
		t.Errorf("add.s rm negative: got %08x", uint32(c.Reg[rT2]))
	}
}

func TestFPUCompareAndBranch(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		mtc1(rT0, 0),
		mtc1(rT1, 1),
		fpArith(16, 1, 0, 0, 50), // c.eq.s $f0, $f1 (funct 48+2)
		bc1t(2),                  // taken: target is index 6
		addiu(rT2, rZero, 111),   // delay slot: still executes
		addiu(rT2, rZero, 999),   // skipped by the taken branch
		addiu(rT3, rZero, 5),     // branch target
	)
	c.Reg[rT0] = uint64(f32bits(2.0))
	c.Reg[rT1] = uint64(f32bits(2.0))
	run(c, 6)
	if !c.Cond[0] {
		t.Error("c.eq.s did not set FCC")
	}
	if c.Reg[rT2] != 111 {
		t.Errorf("bc1t delay slot: t2=%d want 111 (delay slot ran, 999 skipped)", c.Reg[rT2])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT3] != 5 {
		t.Errorf("bc1t target: t3=%d want 5", c.Reg[rT3])
	}
}

func TestFPUConversionsAndTrunc(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		dmtc1(rT0, 0),            // $f0 = -2.9 double
		fpArith(17, 0, 0, 2, 13), // trunc.w.d $f2, $f0 -> -2
		mfc1(rT1, 2),
		fpArith(17, 0, 0, 4, 32), // cvt.s.d $f4, $f0
		mfc1(rT2, 4),
		mtc1(rT3, 6),             // $f6 = int pattern 7 (via cvt path below)
		fpArith(20, 0, 6, 8, 33), // cvt.d.w $f8, $f6 -> 7.0
		dmfc1(rT4, 8),
	)
	c.Reg[rT0] = math.Float64bits(-2.9)
	c.Reg[rT3] = 7
	run(c, 8)
	if int32(c.Reg[rT1]) != -2 {
		t.Errorf("trunc.w.d: got %d", int32(c.Reg[rT1]))
	}
	if uint32(c.Reg[rT2]) != f32bits(-2.9) {
		t.Errorf("cvt.s.d: got %08x", uint32(c.Reg[rT2]))
	}
	if c.Reg[rT4] != math.Float64bits(7.0) {
		t.Errorf("cvt.d.w: got %x", c.Reg[rT4])
	}
}

func TestFPUDivideByZeroFlag(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		mtc1(rT0, 0),
		mtc1(rT1, 1),
		fpArith(16, 1, 0, 2, 3), // div.s $f2, $f0, $f1
		mfc1(rT2, 2),
	)
	c.Reg[rT0] = uint64(f32bits(1.0))
	c.Reg[rT1] = 0
	run(c, 4)
	if !math.IsInf(float64(math.Float32frombits(uint32(c.Reg[rT2]))), 1) {
		t.Errorf("1/0: got %x", uint32(c.Reg[rT2]))
	}
	if c.FCSR&fcsrFlagZ == 0 {
		t.Error("divide-by-zero flag not set in FCSR")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/r4300/r4300.go ====================

// Package r4300 is an original implementation of the NEC
// VR4300 CPU (MIPS III with 64-bit extensions) used in the
// Nintendo 64, written from the published MIPS64 architecture
// manuals and the VR4300 hardware manual. It implements the
// full integer instruction set, the CP1 floating point unit's
// core operations, CP0 with a 32-entry TLB, exceptions with
// correct vector selection, and branch delay slots.
//
// The CPU talks to the machine through the Bus interface in
// physical addresses: virtual translation (TLB plus the KSEG
// direct maps) happens inside the CPU, exactly as on the
// hardware, and every load, store, and instruction fetch is
// checked for alignment, segment permission, and TLB state
// before the bus is touched.
//
// Cycle counting is a flat published-style model: one cycle
// per simple instruction, two for loads and stores, and flat
// class totals for multiply, divide, and floating point
// operations. The Count register advances at half the cycle
// rate, as on the hardware. The README lists the totals.
package r4300

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"math/bits"
)

// Bus is the physical-address memory interface the CPU uses.
// Sizes are in bytes (1, 2, 4, or 8) and transfers are
// big-endian: Read returns the value right-justified, Write
// stores the low size bytes of val.
type Bus interface {
	Read(addr uint32, size int) uint64
	Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint64)
}

// CP0 register indices.
const (
	Cp0Index    = 0
	Cp0Random   = 1
	Cp0EntryLo0 = 2
	Cp0EntryLo1 = 3
	Cp0Context  = 4
	Cp0PageMask = 5
	Cp0Wired    = 6
	Cp0BadVAddr = 8
	Cp0Count    = 9
	Cp0EntryHi  = 10
	Cp0Compare  = 11
	Cp0Status   = 12
	Cp0Cause    = 13
	Cp0EPC      = 14
	Cp0PRId     = 15
	Cp0Config   = 16
	Cp0LLAddr   = 17
	Cp0WatchLo  = 18
	Cp0WatchHi  = 19
	Cp0XContext = 20
	Cp0ECC      = 26
	Cp0CacheErr = 27
	Cp0TagLo    = 28
	Cp0TagHi    = 29
	Cp0ErrorEPC = 30
)

// Status register bits.
const (
	StatusIE  = 1 << 0
	StatusEXL = 1 << 1
	StatusERL = 1 << 2
	StatusKSU = 3 << 3
	StatusUX  = 1 << 5
	StatusSX  = 1 << 6
	StatusKX  = 1 << 7
	StatusIM  = 0xFF << 8
	StatusDE  = 1 << 16
	StatusCE  = 1 << 17
	StatusCH  = 1 << 18
	StatusSR  = 1 << 20
	StatusFR  = 1 << 21
	StatusBEV = 1 << 22
	StatusTS  = 1 << 23
	StatusITS = 1 << 24
	StatusRE  = 1 << 25
	StatusRP  = 1 << 27
	StatusCU0 = 1 << 28
	StatusCU1 = 1 << 29
	StatusCU2 = 1 << 30
	StatusCU3 = 1 << 31
)

// Cause register fields.
const (
	CauseExcCode = 0x1F << 2
	CauseIP      = 0xFF << 8
	CauseIPSW    = 0x03 << 8 // software-writable IP0/IP1
	CauseIV      = 1 << 23
	CauseCE      = 3 << 28
	CauseBD      = 1 << 31
)

// Exception codes (Cause ExcCode values).
const (
	ExcInterrupt = 0
	ExcTLBMod    = 1
	ExcTLBL      = 2
	ExcTLBS      = 3
	ExcAdEL      = 4
	ExcAdES      = 5
	ExcBusFetch  = 6
	ExcBusData   = 7
	ExcSyscall   = 8
	ExcBreak     = 9
	ExcReserved  = 10
	ExcCpU       = 11
	ExcOverflow  = 12
	ExcTrap      = 13
	ExcFPE       = 15
)

// TLBEntry is one decoded TLB entry. The raw CP0-format
// values are kept so TLBR can hand them back exactly.
type TLBEntry struct {
	PageMask uint64 // raw PageMask register value
	EntryHi  uint64 // raw EntryHi register value
	EntryLo0 uint64 // raw EntryLo0 register value
	EntryLo1 uint64 // raw EntryLo1 register value
}

// EntryLo bit fields.
const (
	entryLoG = 1 << 0
	entryLoV = 1 << 1
	entryLoD = 1 << 2
)

// Access kinds for translation.
const (
	accFetch = iota
	accRead
	accWrite
)

// Privilege modes.
const (
	modeKernel = iota
	modeSupervisor
	modeUser
)

// CPU is the VR4300 core. Registers are exported so tests and
// the system package can inspect and seed state.
type CPU struct {
	Reg [32]uint64
	HI  uint64
	LO  uint64
	PC  uint64 // address of the next instruction to execute
	NPC uint64 // address of the instruction after PC

	FPR  [32]uint64 // raw FPU register storage
	FCSR uint32     // FCR31: rounding mode, flags, enables, cause, conditions
	Cond [8]bool    // FPU condition bits (Cond[0] is FCC in FCSR bit 23)

	CP0 [32]uint64
	TLB [32]TLBEntry

	LLBit  bool
	LLAddr uint32

	Cycles uint64 // total cycles executed (flat model)

	bus       Bus
	delaySlot bool // the instruction at PC sits in a branch delay slot
	nullify   bool // next instruction is nullified (branch-likely not taken)
	countFrac uint64
	ipLine    uint8 // external interrupt lines driven by the machine (IP2..IP6)
	err       error
}

// New returns a CPU in its reset state, attached to bus.
func New(bus Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{bus: bus}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Reset applies the power-on state: the CPU starts at the
// reset vector in kernel mode with BEV and ERL set.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	for i := range c.Reg {
		c.Reg[i] = 0
	}
	c.HI, c.LO = 0, 0
	c.PC = 0xFFFFFFFFBFC00000
	c.NPC = c.PC + 4
	for i := range c.FPR {
		c.FPR[i] = 0
	}
	c.FCSR = 0
	for i := range c.Cond {
		c.Cond[i] = false
	}
	for i := range c.CP0 {
		c.CP0[i] = 0
	}
	// Power-on CP0 values per the VR4300 manual. Config's
	// cache-geometry fields are informational only; caches
	// are not modeled.
	c.CP0[Cp0Status] = StatusBEV | StatusERL | StatusCU0 | StatusRP
	c.CP0[Cp0PRId] = 0x00000B22
	c.CP0[Cp0Config] = 0x6E46303F
	c.CP0[Cp0Random] = 31
	for i := range c.TLB {
		c.TLB[i] = TLBEntry{}
	}
	c.LLBit = false
	c.LLAddr = 0
	c.Cycles = 0
	c.delaySlot = false
	c.nullify = false
	c.countFrac = 0
	c.err = nil
}

// SetBus attaches or replaces the memory bus.
func (c *CPU) SetBus(b Bus) { c.bus = b }

// SetInterruptLine drives the external interrupt input the
// machine connects to Cause IP2 (the RCP interrupt on the
// N64). Other IP bits are internal (software IP0/IP1 and the
// Count/Compare timer on IP7).
func (c *CPU) SetInterruptLine(active bool) {
	if active {
		c.ipLine |= 1 << 2
	} else {
		c.ipLine &^= 1 << 2
	}
}

// status is the CP0 Status register as a uint32.
func (c *CPU) status() uint32 { return uint32(c.CP0[Cp0Status]) }

// cause is the CP0 Cause register as a uint32.
func (c *CPU) cause() uint32 { return uint32(c.CP0[Cp0Cause]) }

// privMode reports the current privilege mode.
func (c *CPU) privMode() int {
	st := c.status()
	if st&(StatusEXL|StatusERL) != 0 {
		return modeKernel
	}
	switch (st & StatusKSU) >> 3 {
	case 0:
		return modeKernel
	case 1:
		return modeSupervisor
	default:
		return modeUser
	}
}

// seg64 reports whether 64-bit addressing is enabled for the
// current privilege mode (KX/SX/UX).
func (c *CPU) seg64() bool {
	st := c.status()
	switch c.privMode() {
	case modeKernel:
		return st&StatusKX != 0
	case modeSupervisor:
		return st&StatusSX != 0
	default:
		return st&StatusUX != 0
	}
}

// allow64Ops reports whether 64-bit integer instructions may
// execute. In kernel mode the full MIPS III operation set is
// available; supervisor and user modes require SX/UX. This
// matches how the N64's kernel (which runs with KX clear)
// uses 64-bit operations.
func (c *CPU) allow64Ops() bool {
	switch c.privMode() {
	case modeKernel:
		return true
	case modeSupervisor:
		return c.status()&StatusSX != 0
	default:
		return c.status()&StatusUX != 0
	}
}

// signExtend32 sign-extends a 32-bit value into 64 bits.
func signExtend32(v uint32) uint64 { return uint64(int64(int32(v))) }

// exc is an exception being raised by an operation.
type exc struct {
	code    int
	ce      int
	badAddr uint64
	refill  bool // TLB miss (no matching entry), selects the refill vector
	addrErr bool // BadVAddr/Context update applies
}

var errHalt = errors.New("r4300: halted")

// raiseException enters an exception for the instruction at
// instrAddr. inDelay reports whether that instruction sits in
// a branch delay slot.
func (c *CPU) raiseException(e exc, instrAddr uint64, inDelay bool) {
	st := c.status()
	cause := c.cause() &^ (CauseExcCode | CauseCE | CauseBD)
	cause |= uint32(e.code&0x1F) << 2
	cause |= uint32(e.ce&3) << 28
	if e.addrErr || e.code == ExcTLBL || e.code == ExcTLBS || e.code == ExcTLBMod {
		c.CP0[Cp0BadVAddr] = e.badAddr
		// Context and XContext record the faulting VPN2.
		ctx := (c.CP0[Cp0Context] &^ 0x7FFFF0) | (uint64((e.badAddr>>13)&0x7FFFF) << 4)
		c.CP0[Cp0Context] = ctx
		xctx := (c.CP0[Cp0XContext] &^ 0x1FFFFFFF0) | (uint64((e.badAddr>>13)&0x1FFFFFFF) << 4)
		c.CP0[Cp0XContext] = xctx
		hi := (c.CP0[Cp0EntryHi] & 0xFF) | (e.badAddr &^ 0x1FFF)
		c.CP0[Cp0EntryHi] = hi
	}
	erl := st&StatusERL != 0
	exl := st&StatusEXL != 0
	if erl {
		c.CP0[Cp0ErrorEPC] = instrAddr
		if inDelay {
			c.CP0[Cp0ErrorEPC] = instrAddr - 4
		}
	} else if !exl {
		epc := instrAddr
		if inDelay {
			epc = instrAddr - 4
			cause |= CauseBD
		}
		c.CP0[Cp0EPC] = epc
	}
	// When EPC is not updated (EXL or ERL already set), BD
	// keeps its old value too.
	if erl || exl {
		cause = (cause &^ CauseBD) | (c.cause() & CauseBD)
	}
	c.CP0[Cp0Cause] = uint64(cause)
	if !erl {
		c.CP0[Cp0Status] = uint64(st | StatusEXL)
	}
	c.LLBit = false

	base := uint64(0xFFFFFFFF80000000)
	if st&StatusBEV != 0 {
		base = 0xFFFFFFFFBFC00000
	}
	var off uint64 = 0x180
	if e.refill && !exl && !erl {
		if c.seg64() {
			off = 0x080 // XTLB refill
		} else {
			off = 0x000 // TLB refill
		}
	} else if e.code == ExcInterrupt && cause&CauseIV != 0 && st&StatusBEV == 0 {
		off = 0x200 // special interrupt vector
	}
	vec := base + off
	c.PC = vec
	c.NPC = vec + 4
	c.delaySlot = false
	c.nullify = false
}

// interruptPending reports whether an enabled interrupt is
// waiting (Cause IP against Status IM, IE set, EXL/ERL clear).
func (c *CPU) interruptPending() bool {
	st := c.status()
	if st&StatusIE == 0 || st&(StatusEXL|StatusERL) != 0 {
		return false
	}
	ip := uint32(c.cause()&CauseIP) | uint32(c.ipLine)<<8
	return ip&uint32(st&StatusIM) != 0
}

// tlbLookup translates through the TLB. On success it returns
// the physical address. On failure it returns the exception
// to raise.
func (c *CPU) tlbLookup(vaddr uint64, write bool, fetch bool) (uint32, *exc) {
	asid := uint8(c.CP0[Cp0EntryHi] & 0xFF)
	code := ExcTLBL
	if write {
		code = ExcTLBS
	}
	for i := range c.TLB {
		e := &c.TLB[i]
		mask := (e.PageMask >> 13) & 0xFFF
		shift := uint(bits.Len64(mask+1)) + 12 // log2(2*pageSize)
		if (vaddr >> shift) != (e.EntryHi >> shift) {
			continue
		}
		global := e.EntryLo0&entryLoG != 0 && e.EntryLo1&entryLoG != 0
		if !global && uint8(e.EntryHi&0xFF) != asid {
			continue
		}
		half := (vaddr >> (shift - 1)) & 1
		lo := e.EntryLo0
		if half == 1 {
			lo = e.EntryLo1
		}
		if lo&entryLoV == 0 {
			return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
		}
		if write && lo&entryLoD == 0 {
			return 0, &exc{code: ExcTLBMod, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
		}
		pageSize := (mask + 1) << 12
		pfn := (lo >> 6) & 0xFFFFFFFFF
		paddr := (pfn << 12) | (vaddr & (uint64(pageSize) - 1))
		return uint32(paddr), nil
	}
	return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, refill: true, addrErr: true}
}

// translate converts a virtual address to a physical address
// for the given access kind, applying segment permissions.
func (c *CPU) translate(vaddr uint64, access int) (uint32, *exc) {
	write := access == accWrite
	code := ExcAdEL
	if write {
		code = ExcAdES
	}
	mode := c.privMode()
	if vaddr == signExtend32(uint32(vaddr)) {
		lo32 := uint32(vaddr)
		switch {
		case lo32 < 0x80000000: // kuseg: TLB mapped, all modes
			return c.tlbLookup(vaddr, write, access == accFetch)
		case lo32 < 0xA0000000: // kseg0: direct, kernel
			if mode != modeKernel {
				return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
			}
			return lo32 - 0x80000000, nil
		case lo32 < 0xC0000000: // kseg1: direct, kernel
			if mode != modeKernel {
				return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
			}
			return lo32 - 0xA0000000, nil
		case lo32 < 0xE0000000: // kseg2/ksseg: TLB, kernel or supervisor
			if mode == modeUser {
				return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
			}
			return c.tlbLookup(vaddr, write, access == accFetch)
		default: // kseg3: TLB, kernel
			if mode != modeKernel {
				return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
			}
			return c.tlbLookup(vaddr, write, access == accFetch)
		}
	}
	// True 64-bit segments require the mode's 64-bit enable.
	if !c.seg64() {
		return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
	}
	switch {
	case vaddr <= 0x0000FFFFFFFFFFFF: // xkuseg: TLB
		return c.tlbLookup(vaddr, write, access == accFetch)
	case vaddr >= 0x4000000000000000 && vaddr <= 0x4000FFFFFFFFFFFF: // xkseg: TLB, kernel
		if mode != modeKernel {
			return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
		}
		return c.tlbLookup(vaddr, write, access == accFetch)
	case vaddr >= 0x8000000000000000 && vaddr <= 0xBFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF: // xkphys: direct
		if mode != modeKernel {
			return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
		}
		return uint32(vaddr), nil
	}
	return 0, &exc{code: code, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}
}

// readMem reads size bytes at a virtual address.
func (c *CPU) readMem(vaddr uint64, size int, instrAddr uint64, inDelay bool) (uint64, bool) {
	if size > 1 && vaddr&(uint64(size)-1) != 0 {
		c.raiseException(exc{code: ExcAdEL, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}, instrAddr, inDelay)
		return 0, false
	}
	paddr, e := c.translate(vaddr, accRead)
	if e != nil {
		c.raiseException(*e, instrAddr, inDelay)
		return 0, false
	}
	return c.bus.Read(paddr, size), true
}

// writeMem writes size bytes at a virtual address.
func (c *CPU) writeMem(vaddr uint64, size int, val uint64, instrAddr uint64, inDelay bool) bool {
	if size > 1 && vaddr&(uint64(size)-1) != 0 {
		c.raiseException(exc{code: ExcAdES, badAddr: vaddr, addrErr: true}, instrAddr, inDelay)
		return false
	}
	paddr, e := c.translate(vaddr, accWrite)
	if e != nil {
		c.raiseException(*e, instrAddr, inDelay)
		return false
	}
	c.bus.Write(paddr, size, val)
	return true
}

// tick advances the Count/Compare timer by the cycles an
// instruction consumed and decrements Random.
func (c *CPU) tick(cycles int) {
	c.Cycles += uint64(cycles)
	c.countFrac += uint64(cycles)
	delta := c.countFrac / 2
	c.countFrac %= 2
	if delta > 0 {
		prev := uint64(uint32(c.CP0[Cp0Count]))
		next := prev + delta
		cmp := uint64(uint32(c.CP0[Cp0Compare]))
		c.CP0[Cp0Count] = uint64(uint32(next))
		if cmp != 0 && prev < cmp && next >= cmp {
			c.CP0[Cp0Cause] |= 1 << 15 // IP7 timer interrupt
		} else if cmp == 0 && uint32(next) == 0 && prev != 0 {
			// Compare of 0 matches on wrap.
		}
	}
	// Random decrements once per instruction (flat model),
	// wrapping between Wired and 31.
	r := int32(c.CP0[Cp0Random])
	wired := int32(c.CP0[Cp0Wired])
	r--
	if r < wired || r > 31 {
		r = 31
	}
	c.CP0[Cp0Random] = uint64(uint32(r))
}

// Step executes one instruction (or takes a pending
// interrupt) and returns the flat cycle count consumed.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	if c.nullify {
		// Branch-likely not taken: the delay slot instruction
		// is nullified, execution resumes after it.
		c.nullify = false
		c.PC = c.NPC
		c.NPC = c.PC + 4
		c.delaySlot = false
	}
	if c.interruptPending() {
		c.raiseException(exc{code: ExcInterrupt}, c.PC, c.delaySlot)
		c.tick(1)
		return 1
	}
	instrAddr := c.PC
	inDelay := c.delaySlot
	c.PC = c.NPC
	c.NPC = c.PC + 4
	c.delaySlot = false

	if instrAddr&3 != 0 {
		c.raiseException(exc{code: ExcAdEL, badAddr: instrAddr, addrErr: true}, instrAddr, inDelay)
		c.tick(1)
		return 1
	}
	paddr, e := c.translate(instrAddr, accFetch)
	if e != nil {
		c.raiseException(*e, instrAddr, inDelay)
		c.tick(1)
		return 1
	}
	instr := uint32(c.bus.Read(paddr, 4))
	cycles := c.execute(instr, instrAddr, inDelay)
	c.Reg[0] = 0
	c.tick(cycles)
	return cycles
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed byte size of a serialized CPU.
const SerializeSize = 32*8 + 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 + // GPRs, HI, LO, PC, NPC
	32*8 + 4 + 4 + // FPRs, FCSR, cond mask
	32*8 + // CP0
	32*4*8 + // TLB
	8 + 8 + 4 + 4 // Cycles, countFrac, LLAddr, flags

// Serialize writes the complete CPU state into dst, which
// must be at least SerializeSize bytes.
func (c *CPU) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &stateWriter{b: dst}
	for _, r := range c.Reg {
		w.u64(r)
	}
	w.u64(c.HI)
	w.u64(c.LO)
	w.u64(c.PC)
	w.u64(c.NPC)
	for _, r := range c.FPR {
		w.u64(r)
	}
	w.u32(c.FCSR)
	var cond uint32
	for i, b := range c.Cond {
		if b {
			cond |= 1 << uint(i)
		}
	}
	w.u32(cond)
	for _, r := range c.CP0 {
		w.u64(r)
	}
	for _, t := range c.TLB {
		w.u64(t.PageMask)
		w.u64(t.EntryHi)
		w.u64(t.EntryLo0)
		w.u64(t.EntryLo1)
	}
	w.u64(c.Cycles)
	w.u64(c.countFrac)
	w.u32(c.LLAddr)
	var flags uint32
	if c.LLBit {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if c.delaySlot {
		flags |= 2
	}
	if c.nullify {
		flags |= 4
	}
	w.u32(flags)
	return w.off
}

// Deserialize restores a CPU state written by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(src []byte) error {
	if len(src) < SerializeSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("r4300: state too short: %d", len(src))
	}
	r := &stateReader{b: src}
	for i := range c.Reg {
		c.Reg[i] = r.u64()
	}
	c.HI = r.u64()
	c.LO = r.u64()
	c.PC = r.u64()
	c.NPC = r.u64()
	for i := range c.FPR {
		c.FPR[i] = r.u64()
	}
	c.FCSR = r.u32()
	cond := r.u32()
	for i := range c.Cond {
		c.Cond[i] = cond&(1<<uint(i)) != 0
	}
	for i := range c.CP0 {
		c.CP0[i] = r.u64()
	}
	for i := range c.TLB {
		c.TLB[i].PageMask = r.u64()
		c.TLB[i].EntryHi = r.u64()
		c.TLB[i].EntryLo0 = r.u64()
		c.TLB[i].EntryLo1 = r.u64()
	}
	c.Cycles = r.u64()
	c.countFrac = r.u64()
	c.LLAddr = r.u32()
	flags := r.u32()
	c.LLBit = flags&1 != 0
	c.delaySlot = flags&2 != 0
	c.nullify = flags&4 != 0
	return r.err
}

type stateWriter struct {
	b   []byte
	off int
}

func (w *stateWriter) u64(v uint64) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(w.b[w.off:], v)
	w.off += 8
}

func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(w.b[w.off:], v)
	w.off += 4
}

type stateReader struct {
	b   []byte
	off int
	err error
}

func (r *stateReader) u64() uint64 {
	v := binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(r.b[r.off:])
	r.off += 8
	return v
}

func (r *stateReader) u32() uint32 {
	v := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(r.b[r.off:])
	r.off += 4
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/r4300/r4300_test.go ====================

package r4300

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// testBus is a flat 16 MB physical RAM for CPU tests.
type testBus struct{ mem []byte }

func newTestBus() *testBus { return &testBus{mem: make([]byte, 16<<20)} }

func (b *testBus) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint64 {
	var v uint64
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		v = v<<8 | uint64(b.mem[addr+uint32(i)])
	}
	return v
}

func (b *testBus) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint64) {
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		b.mem[addr+uint32(i)] = byte(val >> (8 * uint(size-1-i)))
	}
}

func (b *testBus) load32(paddr uint32, instr uint32) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b.mem[paddr:], instr)
}

// Assembler helpers.
func rr(rs, rt, rd, sa, funct uint32) uint32 {
	return rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | sa<<6 | funct
}
func ii(op, rs, rt uint32, imm uint16) uint32 {
	return op<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(imm)
}
func lui(rt uint32, imm uint16) uint32 { return ii(0x0F, 0, rt, imm) }
func ori(rt, rs uint32, imm uint16) uint32 {
	return ii(0x0D, rs, rt, imm)
}
func addiu(rt, rs uint32, imm int16) uint32 { return ii(0x09, rs, rt, uint16(imm)) }
func addi(rt, rs uint32, imm int16) uint32  { return ii(0x08, rs, rt, uint16(imm)) }
func lw(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32    { return ii(0x23, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func sw(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32    { return ii(0x2B, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func beq(rs, rt uint32, off int16) uint32   { return ii(0x04, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func bne(rs, rt uint32, off int16) uint32   { return ii(0x05, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func mtc0(rt, rd uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x10<<26 | 4<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11
}
func mfc0(rt, rd uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x10<<26 | 0<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11
}
func nop() uint32 { return 0 }

const (
	rZero = 0
	rV0   = 2
	rA0   = 4
	rT0   = 8
	rT1   = 9
	rT2   = 10
	rT3   = 11
	rT4   = 12
	rS0   = 16
	rS1   = 17
	rRA   = 31
)

const progBase = 0x80000000 // kseg0, physical 0

// setupCPU returns a CPU with kernel-mode Status (BEV
// clear), the program loaded at physical 0, PC at progBase.
func setupCPU(prog ...uint32) (*CPU, *testBus) {
	bus := newTestBus()
	for i, in := range prog {
		bus.load32(uint32(i*4), in)
	}
	c := New(bus)
	c.CP0[Cp0Status] = StatusCU0 | StatusCU1
	c.PC = signExtend32(progBase)
	c.NPC = c.PC + 4
	return c, bus
}

func run(c *CPU, steps int) {
	for i := 0; i < steps; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
}

func TestArithmeticVectors(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		lui(rT0, 0x1234),
		ori(rT0, rT0, 0x5678),       // t0 = 0x12345678
		rr(rT0, rT0, rT1, 0, 0x21),  // addu t1 = 0x2468ACF0
		rr(rT0, rT0, rT2, 0, 0x2D),  // daddu t2 = 0x2468ACF0
		addiu(rT3, rZero, -1),       // t3 = -1
		rr(rT3, rT0, rT4, 0, 0x2C),  // dadd t4 = 0x12345677
		rr(rT0, rT0, rT0, 16, 0x38), // dsll t0 = 0x123456780000
	)
	run(c, 7)
	if c.Reg[rT1] != 0x2468ACF0 {
		t.Errorf("addu: got %x", c.Reg[rT1])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT2] != 0x2468ACF0 {
		t.Errorf("daddu: got %x", c.Reg[rT2])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT4] != 0x12345677 {
		t.Errorf("dadd: got %x", c.Reg[rT4])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT0] != 0x123456780000 {
		t.Errorf("dsll: got %x", c.Reg[rT0])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT3] != 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("addiu sign extension: got %x", c.Reg[rT3])
	}
}

func TestMultiplyDivideVectors(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		addiu(rT0, rZero, -3),
		addiu(rT1, rZero, 7),
		rr(rT0, rT1, 0, 0, 0x18), // mult: -21
		rr(0, 0, rT2, 0, 0x12),   // mflo
		rr(0, 0, rT3, 0, 0x10),   // mfhi = -1 (sign extended)
		rr(rT0, rT1, 0, 0, 0x1C), // dmult
		rr(0, 0, rT4, 0, 0x12),   // mflo
		rr(rT1, rT0, 0, 0, 0x1F), // ddivu 7 / 0xFFFF...FD
	)
	run(c, 8)
	if int64(c.Reg[rT2]) != -21 {
		t.Errorf("mult lo: got %d", int64(c.Reg[rT2]))
	}
	if c.Reg[rT3] != 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("mult hi: got %x", c.Reg[rT3])
	}
	if int64(c.Reg[rT4]) != -21 {
		t.Errorf("dmult lo: got %d", int64(c.Reg[rT4]))
	}
}

func TestDivideByZeroDocumented(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		addiu(rT0, rZero, 42),
		addiu(rT1, rZero, 0),
		rr(rT0, rT1, 0, 0, 0x1A), // div by zero
		rr(0, 0, rT2, 0, 0x12),   // mflo = -1 (dividend >= 0)
		rr(0, 0, rT3, 0, 0x10),   // mfhi = 42
	)
	run(c, 5)
	if c.Reg[rT2] != 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("div0 lo: got %x", c.Reg[rT2])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT3] != 42 {
		t.Errorf("div0 hi: got %x", c.Reg[rT3])
	}
}

func TestAddOverflowTraps(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		lui(rT0, 0x7FFF),
		ori(rT0, rT0, 0xFFFF), // t0 = 0x7FFFFFFF
		addi(rT1, rT0, 1),     // overflow
	)
	run(c, 2)
	c.Step() // overflow raises
	if got := (c.CP0[Cp0Cause] & CauseExcCode) >> 2; got != ExcOverflow {
		t.Errorf("cause: got %d want overflow", got)
	}
	if c.CP0[Cp0EPC] != signExtend32(progBase+8) {
		t.Errorf("epc: got %x", c.CP0[Cp0EPC])
	}
	if c.PC != signExtend32(0x80000180) {
		t.Errorf("vector: got %x", c.PC)
	}
}

func TestDelaySlotExecutes(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		addiu(rT0, rZero, 1),
		beq(rZero, rZero, 2), // to index 4
		addiu(rT0, rT0, 10),  // delay slot: t0 = 11
		addiu(rT0, rT0, 100), // skipped
		addiu(rT1, rT0, 1),   // t1 = 12
	)
	run(c, 4)
	if c.Reg[rT0] != 11 {
		t.Errorf("delay slot: t0 = %d, want 11", c.Reg[rT0])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT1] != 12 {
		t.Errorf("delay slot: t1 = %d, want 12", c.Reg[rT1])
	}
}

func TestBranchLikelyNullifies(t *testing.T) {
	// A not-taken branch-likely nullifies its delay slot.
	c2, _ := setupCPU(
		addiu(rT0, rZero, 1),
		ii(0x15, rT0, rT0, 2), // bnel t0, t0: equal, not taken, nullify next
		addiu(rT0, rT0, 10),   // nullified
		addiu(rT1, rT0, 1),    // executes: t1 = 2
	)
	run(c2, 4)
	if c2.Reg[rT0] != 1 || c2.Reg[rT1] != 2 {
		t.Errorf("likely nullify: t0=%d t1=%d", c2.Reg[rT0], c2.Reg[rT1])
	}
}

	c, _ := setupCPU(
		beq(rZero, rZero, 1), // to index 2
		0x0000000C,           // syscall in the delay slot
		nop(),

	if c.CP0[Cp0EPC] != signExtend32(progBase) {
		t.Errorf("epc should be the branch: got %x", c.CP0[Cp0EPC])
	}
	if c.CP0[Cp0Cause]&CauseBD == 0 {
		t.Error("BD not set in Cause")
	}
	if got := (c.CP0[Cp0Cause] & CauseExcCode) >> 2; got != ExcSyscall {
		t.Errorf("cause: got %d", got)
	}
}

func TestUserModeSegmentFaultAndCpU(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := setupCPU(
		lui(rT0, 0x8000),
		lw(rT1, rT0, 0),
	)
	// Drop to user mode: KSU=2 (user), EXL/ERL clear.
	// Even fetching from kseg0 faults in user mode.
	c.CP0[Cp0Status] = StatusCU1 | 2<<3
	run(c, 2)
	if got := (c.CP0[Cp0Cause] & CauseExcCode) >> 2; got != ExcAdEL {
		t.Errorf("user kseg0: cause %d want AdEL", got)
	}
	// COP0 in user mode is unusable. The instruction must
	// be fetched from kuseg, so map VA 0 -> PA 0 through
	// the TLB and place the mfc0 at VA 0x100.
	c2, bus2 := setupCPU(nop())
	c2.TLB[0] = TLBEntry{
		PageMask: 0,
		EntryHi:  0,    // VPN2 0, ASID 0
		EntryLo0: 0x1F, // PFN 0, C=3, D, V, G
		EntryLo1: 0x405F,
	}
	bus2.load32(0x100, mfc0(rT0, Cp0Status))
	c2.CP0[Cp0Status] = StatusCU1 | 2<<3
	c2.PC = 0x100
	c2.NPC = 0x104
	run(c2, 1)
	if got := (c2.CP0[Cp0Cause] & CauseExcCode) >> 2; got != ExcCpU {
		t.Errorf("user cop0: cause %d want CpU", got)
	}
	if ce := (c2.CP0[Cp0Cause] & CauseCE) >> 28; ce != 0 {
		t.Errorf("user cop0: CE %d want 0", ce)
	}
}

func TestCountCompareInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := setupCPU(nop(), nop(), nop(), nop())
	_ = bus
	// Handler at the special interrupt vector 0x80000200:
	// record v0 = 0x600D and eret.
	handler := []uint32{
		addiu(rV0, rZero, 0x600D&0x7FFF),
		0x42000018, // eret
	}
	for i, in := range handler {
		bus.load32(0x200+uint32(i*4), in)
	}
	c.CP0[Cp0Cause] = CauseIV
	c.CP0[Cp0Status] = StatusCU0 | StatusIE | (1 << 15) // IM7
	c.CP0[Cp0Count] = 0
	c.CP0[Cp0Compare] = 3
	run(c, 12)
	if c.Reg[rV0] != 0x600D {
		t.Errorf("timer interrupt handler did not run: v0=%x cause=%x count=%d",
			c.Reg[rV0], c.CP0[Cp0Cause], c.CP0[Cp0Count])
	}
}

func TestLLSC(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := setupCPU(
		lui(rT0, 0x8000),
		ii(0x30, rT0, rT1, 0x40), // ll t1, 0x40(t0)
		addiu(rT1, rT1, 1),
		ii(0x38, rT0, rT1, 0x40), // sc t1: succeeds, t1=1
		ii(0x38, rT0, rT2, 0x40), // sc t2 without ll: fails, t2=0
	)
	// Seed the linked cell at physical 0x40 with 41.
	bus.Write(0x40, 4, 41)
	run(c, 5)
	if c.Reg[rT1] != 1 {
		t.Errorf("sc after ll: t1=%d want 1", c.Reg[rT1])
	}
	if c.Reg[rT2] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("sc without ll: t2=%d want 0", c.Reg[rT2])
	}
	if got := bus.Read(0x40, 4); got != 42 {
		t.Errorf("cell after sc: got %d want 42", got)
	}
}

func TestLoadStorePartialBigEndian(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := setupCPU(
		lui(rT0, 0x8000),
		// Store 0xAABBCCDD at phys 0x100.
		lui(rT1, 0xAABB),
		ori(rT1, rT1, 0xCCDD),
		sw(rT1, rT0, 0x100),
		// LWL at 0x101 into zeroed t2: bytes  BB CC DD fill top.
		ii(0x22, rT0, rT2, 0x101), // lwl t2, 0x101(t0)
		// LWR at 0x102: bytes AA BB CC fill bottom of t3 (t3 starts 0xFF.. marker via lui).
		lui(rT3, 0xFF00),
		ii(0x26, rT0, rT3, 0x102), // lwr t3, 0x102(t0)
		// SWL of 0x11223344 at 0x201: stores 11 22 33 at 0x201..0x203.
		lui(rT4, 0x1122),
		ori(rT4, rT4, 0x3344),
		ii(0x2A, rT0, rT4, 0x201), // swl t4, 0x201(t0)
		// SWR of 0x11223344 at 0x302: the low bytes of the
		// register fill memory from the unit start, so
		// 0x300 gets 0x22, 0x301 gets 0x33, 0x302 gets 0x44.
		ii(0x2E, rT0, rT4, 0x302), // swr t4, 0x302(t0)
	)
	run(c, 11)
	if got := bus.Read(0x100, 4); got != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Fatalf("seed store: %08x", got)
	}
	if got := uint32(c.Reg[rT2]); got != 0xBBCCDD00 {
		t.Errorf("lwl: got %08x want BBCCDD00", got)
	}
	if got := uint32(c.Reg[rT3]); got != 0xFFAABBCC {
		t.Errorf("lwr: got %08x want FFAABBCC", got)
	}
	// SWL at 0x201 (k=1): stores rt's top 3 bytes (11 22 33)
	// at 0x201,0x202,0x203.
	if got := bus.Read(0x200, 4); got != 0x00112233 {
		t.Errorf("swl bytes: got %08x want 00112233", got)
	}
	// SWR at 0x302 (k=2): mem[0x300]=0x22, mem[0x301]=0x33,
	// mem[0x302]=0x44 (the byte at the address is the
	// register's lowest byte).
	if got := bus.Read(0x300, 4); got != 0x22334400 {
		t.Errorf("swr bytes: got %08x want 22334400", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	prog := []uint32{
		lui(rT0, 0x1111),
		ori(rT0, rT0, 0x2222),
		rr(rT0, rT0, rT1, 0, 0x2D), // daddu t1, t0, t0
		lui(rT2, 0x8000),
		sw(rT0, rT2, 0x80),
	}
	c1, b1 := setupCPU(prog...)
	run(c1, 2)
	state := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if n := c1.Serialize(state); n != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("serialize size %d want %d", n, SerializeSize)
	}
	run(c1, 3)
	c2, b2 := setupCPU(prog...)
	if err := c2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	run(c2, 3)
	for i := range c1.Reg {
		if c1.Reg[i] != c2.Reg[i] {
			t.Errorf("reg %d: %x != %x", i, c1.Reg[i], c2.Reg[i])
		}
	}
	if b1.Read(0x80, 4) != b2.Read(0x80, 4) {
		t.Error("memory diverged after restore")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/r4300/tlb_test.go ====================

package r4300

import "testing"

// programTLB installs, by executing real CP0 instructions,
// a 4 KB page pair at index 0: VA 0x00400000 -> PA
// 0x00100000 (even page, EntryLo0) and VA 0x00401000 -> PA
// 0x00101000 (odd page, EntryLo1). lo0/lo1 are parameters so
// tests can vary Valid and Dirty.
func programTLB(lo0, lo1 uint32) []uint32 {
	return []uint32{
		lui(rT0, 0x0040),         // t0 = 0x00400000
		mtc0(rT0, Cp0EntryHi),    // VPN2 = 0x200, ASID 0
		mtc0(rZero, Cp0PageMask), // 4 KB pages
		addiu(rT1, rZero, int16(lo0)),
		mtc0(rT1, Cp0EntryLo0),
		addiu(rT1, rZero, int16(lo1)),
		mtc0(rT1, Cp0EntryLo1),
		mtc0(rZero, Cp0Index),
		0x42000002, // tlbwi
	}
}

const (
	loEven = 0x401F // PFN 0x100, C=3, D=1, V=1, G=1
	loOdd  = 0x405F // PFN 0x101, C=3, D=1, V=1, G=1
)

func TestTLBMappedStoreAndLoad(t *testing.T) {
	prog := append(programTLB(loEven, loOdd),
		lui(rT2, 0x1234),
		ori(rT2, rT2, 0x5678),
		sw(rT2, rT0, 0),      // VA 0x00400000 -> PA 0x00100000
		lw(rT3, rT0, 0),      // read back through the TLB
		sw(rT2, rT0, 0x1000), // odd page -> PA 0x00101000
	)
	c, bus := setupCPU(prog...)
	run(c, len(prog))
	if got := bus.Read(0x100000, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("even page store: phys %08x", got)
	}
	if got := bus.Read(0x101000, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("odd page store: phys %08x", got)
	}
	if c.Reg[rT3] != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("tlb load: got %x", c.Reg[rT3])
	}
}

func TestTLBRefillVectorAndRegisters(t *testing.T) {
	prog := []uint32{
		lui(rT0, 0x0080), // VA 0x00800000, unmapped
		sw(rT0, rT0, 0),
	}
	c, _ := setupCPU(prog...)
	run(c, 2)
	if got := (c.CP0[Cp0Cause] & CauseExcCode) >> 2; got != ExcTLBS {
		t.Errorf("cause: got %d want TLBS", got)
	}
	// Refill with EXL clear uses vector offset 0.
	if c.PC != signExtend32(0x80000000) {
		t.Errorf("refill vector: got %x", c.PC)
	}
	if c.CP0[Cp0BadVAddr] != signExtend32(0x00800000) {
		t.Errorf("badvaddr: got %x", c.CP0[Cp0BadVAddr])
	}
	if c.CP0[Cp0Status]&StatusEXL == 0 {
		t.Error("EXL not set after refill")
	}
	if got := (c.CP0[Cp0Context] >> 4) & 0x7FFFF; got != 0x00800000>>13 {
		t.Errorf("context vpn: got %x", got)
	}
}

		t.Errorf("cause: got %d want TLBL", got)

	if c.PC != signExtend32(0x80000180) {
		t.Errorf("invalid vector: got %x want general", c.PC)
	}
}

	}
