func TestTLBProbe(t *testing.T) {
	prog := append(programTLB(loEven, loOdd),
		lui(rT0, 0x0040),
		mtc0(rT0, Cp0EntryHi),
		0x42000008, // tlbp: hit at index 0
		mfc0(rT4, Cp0Index),
		lui(rT0, 0x0060), // unmapped VPN
		mtc0(rT0, Cp0EntryHi),
		0x42000008, // tlbp: miss, P bit set
		mfc0(rS0, Cp0Index),
	)
	c, _ := setupCPU(prog...)
	run(c, len(prog))
	if c.Reg[rT4] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("tlbp hit: index %x want 0", c.Reg[rT4])
	}
	if c.Reg[rS0]&0x80000000 == 0 {
		t.Errorf("tlbp miss: P bit not set in %x", c.Reg[rS0])
	}
}

func TestTLBLargerPage(t *testing.T) {
	// 16 KB pages: PageMask = 3<<13. Pair covers 32 KB:
	// VA 0x00400000..0x00407FFF. EntryHi VPN2 key is
	// vaddr>>15, so EntryHi = 0x00400000 still encodes it
	// (the low bits masked by the compare shift).
	prog := []uint32{
		lui(rT0, 0x0040),
		mtc0(rT0, Cp0EntryHi),
		addiu(rT1, rZero, 0x6000), // PageMask field value 3<<13 = 0x6000
		mtc0(rT1, Cp0PageMask),
		addiu(rT1, rZero, int16(loEven)),
		mtc0(rT1, Cp0EntryLo0),
		addiu(rT1, rZero, int16(loOdd)),
		mtc0(rT1, Cp0EntryLo1),
		mtc0(rZero, Cp0Index),
		0x42000002, // tlbwi
		lui(rT2, 0x0BAD),
		sw(rT2, rT0, 0x4000), // VA 0x00404000: odd half (16K page 1) -> PA 0x101000 + 0x0? offset within page
		lw(rT3, rT0, 0x4000),
	}
	c, bus := setupCPU(prog...)
	run(c, len(prog))
	// VA 0x00404000: half = (vaddr>>14)&1 = 1 -> EntryLo1,
	// PA = 0x101000 + (0x4000 & 0x3FFF) = 0x101000.
	if got := bus.Read(0x101000, 4); got != 0x0BAD0000 {
		t.Errorf("16k page store: phys %08x at 0x101000", got)
	}
	if c.Reg[rT3] != 0x0BAD0000 {
		t.Errorf("16k page load: got %x", c.Reg[rT3])
	}
}

func TestERETReturnsAndClearsEXL(t *testing.T) {
	prog := []uint32{
		0x0000000C, // syscall
	}
	c, bus := setupCPU(prog...)
	// Handler at the general vector: bump a counter cell,
	// then eret.
	handler := []uint32{
		lui(rT0, 0x8000),
		lw(rT1, rT0, 0x40),
		addiu(rT1, rT1, 1),
		sw(rT1, rT0, 0x40),
		0x42000018, // eret
	}
	for i, in := range handler {
		bus.load32(0x180+uint32(i*4), in)
	}
	run(c, 1) // syscall -> vector
	if c.PC != signExtend32(0x80000180) {
		t.Fatalf("no vector: pc %x", c.PC)
	}
	run(c, 5) // handler + eret -> back to EPC (progBase) with EXL clear
	if c.CP0[Cp0Status]&StatusEXL != 0 {
		t.Error("EXL still set after eret")
	}
	if got := bus.Read(0x40, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("handler ran %d times", got)
	}
	if c.PC != signExtend32(progBase) {
		t.Errorf("eret target: got %x", c.PC)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/rsp/exec.go ====================

package rsp

import "encoding/binary"

// Step executes one instruction and returns 1 (the flat
// RSP cycle cost in this model). A halted RSP executes
// nothing and returns 0. There are no exceptions: BREAK
// sets the broke flag and halts, and any encoding outside
// the documented RSP subset executes as a NOP.
func (r *RSP) Step() int {
	if r.halted {
		return 0
	}
	pc := r.PC
	instr := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(r.IMEM[pc&0xFFF:])
	nextNPC := (r.NPC + 4) & 0xFFF
	r.exec(instr, pc, &nextNPC)
	r.PC = r.NPC
	r.NPC = nextNPC
	r.Reg[0] = 0
	return 1
}

// exec decodes and executes one instruction word. taken
// branches rewrite *nextNPC (the address after the delay
// slot), giving the standard MIPS delay-slot flow with a
// 12-bit IMEM wrap.
func (r *RSP) exec(instr uint32, pc uint32, nextNPC *uint32) {
	op := instr >> 26
	rs := (instr >> 21) & 0x1F
	rt := (instr >> 16) & 0x1F
	rd := (instr >> 11) & 0x1F
	sa := (instr >> 6) & 0x1F
	funct := instr & 0x3F
	imm := instr & 0xFFFF
	simm := int32(int16(imm))
	branch := func(cond bool) {
		if cond {
			*nextNPC = (pc + 4 + uint32(simm<<2)) & 0xFFF
		}
	}

	switch op {
	case 0x00: // SPECIAL
		a, b := r.Reg[rs], r.Reg[rt]
		switch funct {
		case 0x00: // SLL
			r.Reg[rd] = b << sa
		case 0x02: // SRL
			r.Reg[rd] = b >> sa
		case 0x03: // SRA
			r.Reg[rd] = uint32(int32(b) >> sa)
		case 0x04: // SLLV
			r.Reg[rd] = b << (a & 0x1F)
		case 0x06: // SRLV
			r.Reg[rd] = b >> (a & 0x1F)
		case 0x07: // SRAV
			r.Reg[rd] = uint32(int32(b) >> (a & 0x1F))
		case 0x08: // JR
			*nextNPC = a & 0xFFC
		case 0x09: // JALR
			r.Reg[rd] = (pc + 8) & 0xFFF
			*nextNPC = a & 0xFFC
		case 0x0D: // BREAK: set broke, halt, interrupt if enabled
			r.broke = true
			r.halted = true
			if r.intrOnBreak {
				r.setInterrupt(true)
			}
		case 0x0F: // SYNC: no-op on the RSP
		case 0x10: // MFHI
			r.Reg[rd] = r.HI
		case 0x11: // MTHI
			r.HI = a
		case 0x12: // MFLO
			r.Reg[rd] = r.LO
		case 0x13: // MTLO
			r.LO = a
		case 0x18: // MULT
			p := int64(int32(a)) * int64(int32(b))
			r.LO, r.HI = uint32(p), uint32(p>>32)
		case 0x19: // MULTU
			p := uint64(a) * uint64(b)
			r.LO, r.HI = uint32(p), uint32(p>>32)
		case 0x1A: // DIV
			r.div(int32(a), int32(b))
		case 0x1B: // DIVU
			r.divu(a, b)
		case 0x20, 0x21: // ADD, ADDU (no overflow trap on the RSP)
			r.Reg[rd] = a + b
		case 0x22, 0x23: // SUB, SUBU
			r.Reg[rd] = a - b
		case 0x24: // AND
			r.Reg[rd] = a & b
		case 0x25: // OR
			r.Reg[rd] = a | b
		case 0x26: // XOR
			r.Reg[rd] = a ^ b
		case 0x27: // NOR
			r.Reg[rd] = ^(a | b)
		case 0x2A: // SLT
			r.Reg[rd] = bool32(int32(a) < int32(b))
		case 0x2B: // SLTU
			r.Reg[rd] = bool32(a < b)
		}
	case 0x01: // REGIMM
		switch rt {
		case 0x00: // BLTZ
			branch(int32(r.Reg[rs]) < 0)
		case 0x01: // BGEZ
			branch(int32(r.Reg[rs]) >= 0)
		case 0x10: // BLTZAL (link written either way, MIPS I style)
			r.Reg[31] = (pc + 8) & 0xFFF
			branch(int32(r.Reg[rs]) < 0)
		case 0x11: // BGEZAL
			r.Reg[31] = (pc + 8) & 0xFFF
			branch(int32(r.Reg[rs]) >= 0)
		}
	case 0x02: // J
		*nextNPC = (instr & 0x3FFFFFF) << 2 & 0xFFC
	case 0x03: // JAL
		r.Reg[31] = (pc + 8) & 0xFFF
		*nextNPC = (instr & 0x3FFFFFF) << 2 & 0xFFC
	case 0x04: // BEQ
		branch(r.Reg[rs] == r.Reg[rt])
	case 0x05: // BNE
		branch(r.Reg[rs] != r.Reg[rt])
	case 0x06: // BLEZ
		branch(int32(r.Reg[rs]) <= 0)
	case 0x07: // BGTZ
		branch(int32(r.Reg[rs]) > 0)
	case 0x08, 0x09: // ADDI, ADDIU (identical on the RSP)
		r.Reg[rt] = r.Reg[rs] + uint32(simm)
	case 0x0A: // SLTI
		r.Reg[rt] = bool32(int32(r.Reg[rs]) < simm)
	case 0x0B: // SLTIU
		r.Reg[rt] = bool32(r.Reg[rs] < uint32(simm))
	case 0x0C: // ANDI
		r.Reg[rt] = r.Reg[rs] & imm
	case 0x0D: // ORI
		r.Reg[rt] = r.Reg[rs] | imm
	case 0x0E: // XORI
		r.Reg[rt] = r.Reg[rs] ^ imm
	case 0x0F: // LUI
		r.Reg[rt] = imm << 16
	case 0x10: // COP0: the SP register set
		switch rs {
		case 0: // MFC0
			r.Reg[rt] = r.ReadCP0(int(rd))
		case 4: // MTC0
			r.WriteCP0(int(rd), r.Reg[rt])
		}
	case 0x12: // COP2: vector unit moves and computation
		r.execCOP2(instr)
	case 0x20: // LB
		r.Reg[rt] = uint32(int32(int8(r.loadByte(r.Reg[rs], simm))))
	case 0x21: // LH
		r.Reg[rt] = uint32(int32(int16(r.loadHalf(r.Reg[rs], simm))))
	case 0x23: // LW
		r.Reg[rt] = r.loadWord(r.Reg[rs], simm)
	case 0x24: // LBU
		r.Reg[rt] = uint32(r.loadByte(r.Reg[rs], simm))
	case 0x25: // LHU
		r.Reg[rt] = uint32(r.loadHalf(r.Reg[rs], simm))
	case 0x22: // LWL
		r.loadWordLeft(rt, r.Reg[rs], simm, true)
	case 0x26: // LWR
		r.loadWordLeft(rt, r.Reg[rs], simm, false)
	case 0x28: // SB
		r.setDMEMByte(addrOf(r.Reg[rs], simm), byte(r.Reg[rt]))
	case 0x29: // SH
		r.storeHalf(r.Reg[rs], simm, uint16(r.Reg[rt]))
	case 0x2B: // SW
		r.storeWord(r.Reg[rs], simm, r.Reg[rt])
	case 0x2A: // SWL
		r.storeWordLeft(rt, r.Reg[rs], simm, true)
	case 0x2E: // SWR
		r.storeWordLeft(rt, r.Reg[rs], simm, false)
	case 0x32: // LWC2: vector loads
		r.execLoadStore(instr, true)
	case 0x3A: // SWC2: vector stores
		r.execLoadStore(instr, false)
	}
	// Every other encoding is a NOP on the RSP, including
	// COP1 (no floating point unit) and the 64-bit forms.
}

// div performs a signed divide with the common MIPS
// divide-by-zero convention (the architecture leaves the
// result undefined; the RSP documentation does not pin
// it either).
func (r *RSP) div(a, b int32) {
	if b == 0 {
		if a >= 0 {
			r.LO = 0xFFFFFFFF
		} else {
			r.LO = 1
		}
		r.HI = uint32(a)
		return
	}
	if a == -1<<31 && b == -1 {
		r.LO, r.HI = uint32(a), 0
		return
	}
	r.LO = uint32(a / b)
	r.HI = uint32(a % b)
}

// divu performs an unsigned divide (divide by zero keeps
// the same convention as the signed form).
func (r *RSP) divu(a, b uint32) {
	if b == 0 {
		r.LO = 0xFFFFFFFF
		r.HI = a
		return
	}
	r.LO = a / b
	r.HI = a % b
}

func bool32(b bool) uint32 {
	if b {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// addrOf forms a DMEM effective address: base plus
// sign-extended offset, low 12 bits used.
func addrOf(base uint32, off int32) uint32 {
	return (base + uint32(off)) & 0xFFF
}

func (r *RSP) loadByte(base uint32, off int32) byte {
	return r.dmemByte(addrOf(base, off))
}

func (r *RSP) loadHalf(base uint32, off int32) uint16 {
	a := addrOf(base, off)
	return uint16(r.dmemByte(a))<<8 | uint16(r.dmemByte(a+1))
}

func (r *RSP) loadWord(base uint32, off int32) uint32 {
	a := addrOf(base, off)
	return uint32(r.dmemByte(a))<<24 | uint32(r.dmemByte(a+1))<<16 |
		uint32(r.dmemByte(a+2))<<8 | uint32(r.dmemByte(a+3))
}

func (r *RSP) storeHalf(base uint32, off int32, v uint16) {
	a := addrOf(base, off)
	r.setDMEMByte(a, byte(v>>8))
	r.setDMEMByte(a+1, byte(v))
}

func (r *RSP) storeWord(base uint32, off int32, v uint32) {
	a := addrOf(base, off)
	r.setDMEMByte(a, byte(v>>24))
	r.setDMEMByte(a+1, byte(v>>16))
	r.setDMEMByte(a+2, byte(v>>8))
	r.setDMEMByte(a+3, byte(v))
}

// regByte views a scalar register as big-endian bytes,
// index 0 most significant.
func regByte(v uint32, i int) byte { return byte(v >> (8 * uint(3-i))) }

func setRegByte(v uint32, i int, b byte) uint32 {
	sh := 8 * uint(3-i)
	return v&^(0xFF<<sh) | uint32(b)<<sh
}

// loadWordLeft implements the big-endian LWL (left=true)
// and LWR (left=false) byte merges into register rt.
func (r *RSP) loadWordLeft(rt, base uint32, off int32, left bool) {
	addr := addrOf(base, off)
	v := r.Reg[rt]
	if left {
		n := 4 - int(addr&3)
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			v = setRegByte(v, k, r.dmemByte(addr+uint32(k)))
		}
	} else {
		n := int(addr&3) + 1
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			v = setRegByte(v, 4-n+k, r.dmemByte(addr-uint32(n-1)+uint32(k)))
		}
	}
	r.Reg[rt] = v
}

// storeWordLeft implements the big-endian SWL/SWR byte
// merges from register rt.
func (r *RSP) storeWordLeft(rt, base uint32, off int32, left bool) {
	addr := addrOf(base, off)
	v := r.Reg[rt]
	if left {
		n := 4 - int(addr&3)
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			r.setDMEMByte(addr+uint32(k), regByte(v, k))
		}
	} else {
		n := int(addr&3) + 1
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			r.setDMEMByte(addr-uint32(n-1)+uint32(k), regByte(v, 4-n+k))
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/rsp/rsp.go ====================

// Package rsp implements the Nintendo 64 Reality Signal
// Processor: the scalar MIPS I core, the SP register set
// and DMA engine, and the vector unit (COP2). It is
// original code written from the published RSP
// documentation (the SGI/Nintendo RSP Programmer's Guide,
// used here as a factual reference for register layouts,
// instruction encodings, and operation semantics).
//
// The RSP owns its DMEM (4 KB) and IMEM (4 KB). The main
// CPU sees both through the SP memory window on the bus,
// and the SP registers through the SP register page. DMA
// between RDRAM and SP memory executes atomically when a
// length register is written, so the DMA busy and full
// flags always read clear; that simplification is stated
// in the README.
//
// The scalar core implements the documented MIPS I subset
// with no exceptions: overflow does not trap, illegal
// encodings execute as NOPs, and BREAK is the only stop
// condition besides the halt flag. Data accesses use the
// low 12 bits of the effective address into DMEM, exactly
// as the documented instruction pseudocode specifies.
package rsp

import "encoding/binary"

// CP0 register numbers on the RSP (also the CPU-visible
// SP register page order at 0x04040000).
const (
	CP0MemAddr   = 0 // SP_MEM_ADDR: bit 12 selects IMEM, bits 11..0 offset
	CP0DramAddr  = 1 // SP_DRAM_ADDR: 24-bit RDRAM address
	CP0RdLen     = 2 // SP_RD_LEN: write starts a DRAM to SP transfer
	CP0WrLen     = 3 // SP_WR_LEN: write starts an SP to DRAM transfer
	CP0Status    = 4 // SP_STATUS
	CP0DMAFull   = 5 // SP_DMA_FULL (read-only)
	CP0DMABusy   = 6 // SP_DMA_BUSY (read-only)
	CP0Semaphore = 7 // SP_SEMAPHORE
	// 8..15 are the DP registers. They route to the RDP
	// in the rdp package through the DPRead and DPWrite
	// hooks below; with no hook attached they read as 0
	// and ignore writes.
)

// SP_STATUS read bits.
const (
	StatusHalt        = 1 << 0
	StatusBroke       = 1 << 1
	StatusDMABusy     = 1 << 2
	StatusDMAFull     = 1 << 3
	StatusIOFull      = 1 << 4
	StatusSingleStep  = 1 << 5
	StatusIntrOnBreak = 1 << 6
	// Bits 7..14 are signals 0..7.
)

// RSP is the signal processor state.
type RSP struct {
	Reg [32]uint32
	HI  uint32
	LO  uint32
	PC  uint32 // IMEM address of the next instruction (12 bits)
	NPC uint32 // IMEM address after PC (12 bits)

	DMEM [4096]byte
	IMEM [4096]byte

	V   [32][8]uint16 // vector registers, element 0 first (big-endian order)
	ACC [8]int64      // 48-bit accumulator lanes, kept sign-extended
	VCC uint16        // compare code: low byte results, high byte clip codes
	VCO uint16        // low byte carry/borrow, high byte not-equal
	VCE uint8         // clip extend flags

	halted      bool
	broke       bool
	sstep       bool
	intrOnBreak bool
	signals     uint8
	intr        bool // MI SP interrupt line level driven by this chip

	memAddr   uint32 // SP_MEM_ADDR raw (bit 12 bank, 11..0 offset)
	dramAddr  uint32 // SP_DRAM_ADDR raw (24 bits)
	rdLen     uint32 // last value written to SP_RD_LEN
	wrLen     uint32 // last value written to SP_WR_LEN
	semaphore uint32 // 0 or 1

	divIn  int32 // latched reciprocal input (high half set by the H forms)
	divOut int32 // latched reciprocal result (read by the H forms)

	dram []byte // attached RDRAM, nil until AttachDRAM

	// OnInterrupt, when set, is called when the RSP
	// interrupt output changes level. The bus wires it to
	// the MI SP interrupt bit.
	OnInterrupt func(active bool)

	// DPRead and DPWrite route CP0 registers 8..15 (the
	// DP command registers) to the RDP. The bus attaches
	// them; the argument is the CP0 register number.
	DPRead  func(reg int) uint32
	DPWrite func(reg int, val uint32)
}

// New returns an RSP in its power-on state: halted, PC 0,
// SP_STATUS reads 0x0001.
func New() *RSP {
	return &RSP{halted: true}
}

// AttachDRAM gives the DMA engine its RDRAM backing store.
func (r *RSP) AttachDRAM(dram []byte) { r.dram = dram }

// Halted reports whether the scalar core is stopped.
func (r *RSP) Halted() bool { return r.halted }

// Status returns the SP_STATUS register value.
func (r *RSP) Status() uint32 {
	var s uint32
	if r.halted {
		s |= StatusHalt
	}
	if r.broke {
		s |= StatusBroke
	}
	// DMA busy, DMA full, and IO full always read 0: DMA
	// completes atomically on the length-register write.
	if r.sstep {
		s |= StatusSingleStep
	}
	if r.intrOnBreak {
		s |= StatusIntrOnBreak
	}
	s |= uint32(r.signals) << 7
	return s
}

// setInterrupt drives the MI SP interrupt output.
func (r *RSP) setInterrupt(on bool) {
	if r.intr == on {
		return
	}
	r.intr = on
	if r.OnInterrupt != nil {
		r.OnInterrupt(on)
	}
}

// writeStatus applies the documented SP_STATUS write-bit
// semantics (used by both the CPU register page and the
// RSP's own MTC0): each function has a clear bit and a
// set bit; a write with neither changes nothing.
func (r *RSP) writeStatus(v uint32) {
	if v&0x001 != 0 { // clear halt
		r.halted = false
	}
	if v&0x002 != 0 { // set halt
		r.halted = true
	}
	if v&0x004 != 0 { // clear broke
		r.broke = false
	}
	if v&0x008 != 0 { // clear RSP interrupt
		r.setInterrupt(false)
	}
	if v&0x010 != 0 { // set RSP interrupt
		r.setInterrupt(true)
	}
	if v&0x020 != 0 { // clear single step
		r.sstep = false
	}
	if v&0x040 != 0 { // set single step
		r.sstep = true
	}
	if v&0x080 != 0 { // clear interrupt-on-break enable
		r.intrOnBreak = false
	}
	if v&0x100 != 0 { // set interrupt-on-break enable
		r.intrOnBreak = true
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if v&(1<<uint(9+2*i)) != 0 { // clear signal i
			r.signals &^= 1 << uint(i)
		}
		if v&(1<<uint(10+2*i)) != 0 { // set signal i
			r.signals |= 1 << uint(i)
		}
	}
}

// ReadCP0 reads an RSP coprocessor 0 register (the SP
// register set). Reading the semaphore performs the
// documented test-and-set.
func (r *RSP) ReadCP0(reg int) uint32 {
	switch reg {
	case CP0MemAddr:
		return r.memAddr
	case CP0DramAddr:
		return r.dramAddr
	case CP0RdLen:
		return r.rdLen
	case CP0WrLen:
		return r.wrLen
	case CP0Status:
		return r.Status()
	case CP0DMAFull, CP0DMABusy:
		return 0 // transfers complete atomically in this model
	case CP0Semaphore:
		v := r.semaphore
		r.semaphore = 1
		return v
	}
	if reg >= 8 && reg <= 15 && r.DPRead != nil {
		return r.DPRead(reg)
	}
	return 0
}

// WriteCP0 writes an RSP coprocessor 0 register. Writing
// a length register starts the DMA transfer immediately.
// Writing the semaphore clears it (the documented
// release operation writes 0).
func (r *RSP) WriteCP0(reg int, val uint32) {
	switch reg {
	case CP0MemAddr:
		r.memAddr = val & 0x1FFF
	case CP0DramAddr:
		r.dramAddr = val & 0xFFFFFF
	case CP0RdLen:
		r.rdLen = val
		r.dma(true, val)
	case CP0WrLen:
		r.wrLen = val
		r.dma(false, val)
	case CP0Status:
		r.writeStatus(val)
	case CP0DMAFull, CP0DMABusy:
		// Read-only status.
	case CP0Semaphore:
		r.semaphore = 0
	default:
		if reg >= 8 && reg <= 15 && r.DPWrite != nil {
			r.DPWrite(reg, val)
		}
	}
}

// ReadRegister reads a CPU-visible SP register by byte
// offset from 0x04040000 (0x00..0x1C).
func (r *RSP) ReadRegister(off uint32) uint32 {
	return r.ReadCP0(int(off / 4))
}

// WriteRegister writes a CPU-visible SP register by byte
// offset from 0x04040000 (0x00..0x1C).
func (r *RSP) WriteRegister(off uint32, val uint32) {
	r.WriteCP0(int(off/4), val)
}

// ReadPC reads the SP_PC register for the CPU.
func (r *RSP) ReadPC() uint32 { return r.PC }

// WritePC writes the SP_PC register. Per the
// documentation the write takes effect only while the
// RSP is halted.
func (r *RSP) WritePC(val uint32) {
	if !r.halted {
		return
	}
	r.PC = val & 0xFFF
	r.NPC = (r.PC + 4) & 0xFFF
}

// decodeDMAFields splits a DMA length register value
// into the row size in bytes, the row count, and the
// per-row DRAM skip in bytes. The length field holds
// bytes-per-row minus 1 with the low 3 bits ignored (as
// if set), the count field holds rows minus 1.
func decodeDMAFields(raw uint32) (rowBytes, rows, skip int) {
	rowBytes = int(raw&0xFF8) + 8
	rows = int((raw>>12)&0xFF) + 1
	skip = int((raw >> 20) & 0xFFF)
	return
}

// dma performs one SP DMA transfer atomically. DRAM to SP
// when toSP is true (SP_RD_LEN write), SP to DRAM when
// false (SP_WR_LEN write). The SP address advances by the
// row length and wraps inside the selected 4 KB bank; the
// DRAM address advances by length plus skip per row and
// wraps in 24 bits. Both address registers are left
// holding their advanced values.
func (r *RSP) dma(toSP bool, lenRaw uint32) {
	rowBytes, rows, skip := decodeDMAFields(lenRaw)
	bank := r.memAddr & 0x1000
	off := r.memAddr & 0xFFF
	daddr := r.dramAddr
	for row := 0; row < rows; row++ {
		for i := 0; i < rowBytes; i++ {
			spIdx := bank | ((off + uint32(i)) & 0xFFF)
			dIdx := (daddr + uint32(i)) & 0xFFFFFF
			if toSP {
				r.setSPByte(spIdx, r.dramByte(dIdx))
			} else {
				r.setDRAMByte(dIdx, r.spByte(spIdx))
			}
		}
		off = (off + uint32(rowBytes)) & 0xFFF
		daddr = (daddr + uint32(rowBytes) + uint32(skip)) & 0xFFFFFF
	}
	r.memAddr = bank | off
	r.dramAddr = daddr
}

// spByte reads SP memory at a 13-bit index (bit 12
// selects IMEM over DMEM).
func (r *RSP) spByte(idx uint32) byte {
	if idx&0x1000 != 0 {
		return r.IMEM[idx&0xFFF]
	}
	return r.DMEM[idx&0xFFF]
}

// setSPByte writes SP memory at a 13-bit index.
func (r *RSP) setSPByte(idx uint32, v byte) {
	if idx&0x1000 != 0 {
		r.IMEM[idx&0xFFF] = v
	} else {
		r.DMEM[idx&0xFFF] = v
	}
}

// dramByte reads attached RDRAM; with no DRAM attached it
// reads 0.
func (r *RSP) dramByte(idx uint32) byte {
	if len(r.dram) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return r.dram[idx&(uint32(len(r.dram))-1)]
}

// setDRAMByte writes attached RDRAM.
func (r *RSP) setDRAMByte(idx uint32, v byte) {
	if len(r.dram) == 0 {
		return
	}
	r.dram[idx&(uint32(len(r.dram))-1)] = v
}

// dmemByte reads DMEM with 12-bit wrap; scalar and vector
// accesses are DMEM-only per the documented pseudocode.
func (r *RSP) dmemByte(addr uint32) byte { return r.DMEM[addr&0xFFF] }

// setDMEMByte writes DMEM with 12-bit wrap.
func (r *RSP) setDMEMByte(addr uint32, v byte) { r.DMEM[addr&0xFFF] = v }

// Run executes up to n instructions, stopping early at a
// halt. It returns the number of instructions executed.
func (r *RSP) Run(n int) int {
	done := 0
	for done < n && !r.halted {
		r.Step()
		done++
	}
	return done
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed byte size of a serialized
// RSP.
const SerializeSize = 32*4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + // GPRs, HI, LO, PC, NPC
	4096 + 4096 + // DMEM, IMEM
	32*8*2 + // vector registers
	8*8 + // accumulator
	2 + 2 + 1 + 8 + // VCC, VCO, VCE, state flags
	4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + // semaphore, mem addr, dram addr, rd len, wr len
	4 + 4 // reciprocal latch state

// Serialize writes the full RSP state into dst, which
// must be at least SerializeSize bytes, and returns the
// number of bytes written.
func (r *RSP) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &stateWriter{b: dst}
	for _, v := range r.Reg {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.u32(r.HI)
	w.u32(r.LO)
	w.u32(r.PC)
	w.u32(r.NPC)
	w.bytes(r.DMEM[:])
	w.bytes(r.IMEM[:])
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
			w.u16(r.V[i][j])
		}
	}
	for _, a := range r.ACC {
		w.u64(uint64(a))
	}
	w.u16(r.VCC)
	w.u16(r.VCO)
	w.u8(r.VCE)
	var flags uint64
	if r.halted {
		flags |= 1 << 0
	}
	if r.broke {
		flags |= 1 << 1
	}
	if r.sstep {
		flags |= 1 << 2
	}
	if r.intrOnBreak {
		flags |= 1 << 3
	}
	if r.intr {
		flags |= 1 << 4
	}
	flags |= uint64(r.signals) << 8
	w.u64(flags)
	w.u32(r.semaphore)
	w.u32(r.memAddr)
	w.u32(r.dramAddr)
	w.u32(r.rdLen)
	w.u32(r.wrLen)
	w.u32(uint32(r.divIn))
	w.u32(uint32(r.divOut))
	return w.n
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (r *RSP) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) < SerializeSize {
		return errShortState
	}
	rd := &stateReader{b: in}
	for i := range r.Reg {
		r.Reg[i] = rd.u32()
	}
	r.HI = rd.u32()
	r.LO = rd.u32()
	r.PC = rd.u32()
	r.NPC = rd.u32()
	copy(r.DMEM[:], rd.bytes(4096))
	copy(r.IMEM[:], rd.bytes(4096))
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
			r.V[i][j] = rd.u16()
		}
	}
	for i := range r.ACC {
		r.ACC[i] = acc48(int64(rd.u64()))
	}
	r.VCC = rd.u16()
	r.VCO = rd.u16()
	r.VCE = rd.u8()
	flags := rd.u64()
	r.halted = flags&(1<<0) != 0
	r.broke = flags&(1<<1) != 0
	r.sstep = flags&(1<<2) != 0
	r.intrOnBreak = flags&(1<<3) != 0
	r.intr = flags&(1<<4) != 0
	r.signals = uint8(flags >> 8)
	r.semaphore = rd.u32()
	r.memAddr = rd.u32()
	r.dramAddr = rd.u32()
	r.rdLen = rd.u32()
	r.wrLen = rd.u32()
	r.divIn = int32(rd.u32())
	r.divOut = int32(rd.u32())
	return nil
}

// acc48 masks and sign-extends a value to 48 bits, the
// accumulator storage invariant.
func acc48(v int64) int64 {
	v &= (1 << 48) - 1
	if v&(1<<47) != 0 {
		v |= ^int64(0) << 48
	}
	return v
}

var errShortState = errShort{}

type errShort struct{}

func (errShort) Error() string { return "rsp: state too short" }

// stateWriter appends fixed-width big-endian values.
type stateWriter struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (w *stateWriter) u8(v uint8)   { w.b[w.n] = v; w.n++ }
func (w *stateWriter) u16(v uint16) { binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(w.b[w.n:], v); w.n += 2 }
func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) { binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w.b[w.n:], v); w.n += 4 }
func (w *stateWriter) u64(v uint64) { binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(w.b[w.n:], v); w.n += 8 }
func (w *stateWriter) bytes(p []byte) {
	copy(w.b[w.n:], p)
	w.n += len(p)
}

// stateReader reads fixed-width big-endian values.
type stateReader struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (s *stateReader) u8() uint8   { v := s.b[s.n]; s.n++; return v }
func (s *stateReader) u16() uint16 { v := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(s.b[s.n:]); s.n += 2; return v }
func (s *stateReader) u32() uint32 { v := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(s.b[s.n:]); s.n += 4; return v }
func (s *stateReader) u64() uint64 { v := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(s.b[s.n:]); s.n += 8; return v }
func (s *stateReader) bytes(n int) []byte {
	v := s.b[s.n : s.n+n]
	s.n += n
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/rsp/rsp_test.go ====================

package rsp

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// Small assembler helpers for hand-derived test programs.
func rr(rs, rt, rd, sa, funct uint32) uint32 {
	return rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | sa<<6 | funct
}
func ii(op, rs, rt uint32, imm uint16) uint32 {
	return op<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(imm)
}
func addiu(rt, rs uint32, imm int16) uint32 { return ii(0x09, rs, rt, uint16(imm)) }
func lui(rt uint32, imm uint16) uint32      { return ii(0x0F, 0, rt, imm) }
func ori(rt, rs uint32, imm uint16) uint32  { return ii(0x0D, rs, rt, imm) }
func sw(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32    { return ii(0x2B, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func lw(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32    { return ii(0x23, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }

const breakInstr = 0x0000000D

func loadProgram(r *RSP, words []uint32) {
	for i, w := range words {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(r.IMEM[i*4:], w)
	}
}

// start clears the halt flag and runs until the RSP stops
// (BREAK or budget exhausted).
func start(r *RSP) {
	r.WriteCP0(CP0Status, 0x001) // clear halt
	r.Run(100000)
}

func runProgram(t *testing.T, words []uint32) *RSP {
	t.Helper()
	r := New()
	loadProgram(r, words)
	start(r)
	if !r.Halted() {
		t.Fatal("program did not halt (no BREAK reached?)")
	}
	return r
}

func dmemWord(r *RSP, off int) uint32 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(r.DMEM[off:])
}

func TestScalarArithmeticAndMemory(t *testing.T) {
	// DMEM fixture for the LWL/LWR checks.
	r := New()
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(r.DMEM[0x200:], 0xAABBCCDD)
	r.DMEM[0x204] = 0xEE
	loadProgram(r, []uint32{
		addiu(8, 0, 7),         // t0 = 7
		addiu(9, 0, 5),         // t1 = 5
		rr(8, 9, 0, 0, 0x18),   // mult t0, t1
		rr(0, 0, 10, 0, 0x12),  // mflo t2 = 35
		sw(10, 0, 0x100),       // DMEM[0x100] = 35
		lui(11, 0x1122),        // t3 = 0x11220000
		ori(11, 11, 0x3344),    // t3 = 0x11223344
		ii(0x22, 0, 11, 0x201), // lwl t3, 0x201($0): top 3 bytes from DMEM
		sw(11, 0, 0x104),       // store merged value
		ii(0x26, 0, 11, 0x204), // lwr t3, 0x204($0): low byte from DMEM
		sw(11, 0, 0x108),       // store again
		addiu(12, 0, -17),      // t4 = -17
		addiu(13, 0, 5),        // t5 = 5
		rr(12, 13, 0, 0, 0x1A), // div t4, t5
		rr(0, 0, 14, 0, 0x12),  // mflo t6 = -3
		rr(0, 0, 15, 0, 0x10),  // mfhi t7 = -2
		sw(14, 0, 0x10C),
		sw(15, 0, 0x110),
		breakInstr,
	})
	start(r)
	if got := dmemWord(r, 0x100); got != 35 {
		t.Errorf("mult/mflo/sw: %d", got)
	}
	// LWL at 0x201 merges BB CC DD over the top bytes,
	// keeping the low byte 0x44.
	if got := dmemWord(r, 0x104); got != 0xBBCCDD44 {
		t.Errorf("lwl merge: %08x", got)
	}
	// LWR at 0x204 then replaces the low byte with 0xEE.
	if got := dmemWord(r, 0x108); got != 0xBBCCDDEE {
		t.Errorf("lwr merge: %08x", got)
	}
	if got := dmemWord(r, 0x10C); got != 0xFFFFFFFD {
		t.Errorf("div quotient: %08x", got)
	}
	if got := dmemWord(r, 0x110); got != 0xFFFFFFFE {
		t.Errorf("div remainder: %08x", got)
	}
}

func TestBranchLinkAndDelaySlot(t *testing.T) {
	// jal to a subroutine that adds 1 and returns; the
	// delay slot of the jal must execute exactly once, and
	// jr's delay slot too.
	r := runProgram(t, []uint32{
		addiu(8, 0, 40),       // 0x00
		ii(0x03, 0, 0, 5),     // 0x04: jal 0x14
		addiu(8, 8, 1),        // 0x08: delay slot, t0 = 41
		sw(8, 0, 0x100),       // 0x0C: after return, store
		breakInstr,            // 0x10
		addiu(8, 8, 1),        // 0x14: subroutine: t0 = 42
		rr(31, 0, 0, 0, 0x08), // 0x18: jr $ra
		addiu(9, 0, 7),        // 0x1C: jr delay slot
	})
	if got := dmemWord(r, 0x100); got != 42 {
		t.Errorf("jal/jr flow: %d", got)
	}
	if r.Reg[9] != 7 {
		t.Errorf("jr delay slot not executed: %d", r.Reg[9])
	}
	if r.Reg[31] != 0x0C {
		t.Errorf("link register: %x", r.Reg[31])
	}
}

func TestStatusWriteSemantics(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	if got := r.Status(); got != StatusHalt {
		t.Fatalf("power-on status: %08x", got)
	}
	// Set interrupt-on-break (bit 8) and signal 3 set
	// (bit 10 + 2*3 = bit 16).
	r.WriteRegister(0x10, 0x100|(1<<16))
	st := r.Status()
	if st&StatusIntrOnBreak == 0 {
		t.Error("interrupt-on-break not set")
	}
	if st&(1<<10) == 0 { // signal 3 reads at bit 7+3
		t.Error("signal 3 not set")
	}
	// Clear signal 3 (bit 9 + 2*3 = bit 15).
	r.WriteRegister(0x10, 1<<15)
	if r.Status()&(1<<10) != 0 {
		t.Error("signal 3 not cleared")
	}
	// Set halt stops execution; PC writes are ignored
	// while running.
	r.WriteRegister(0x10, 0x001) // clear halt
	if r.Halted() {
		t.Fatal("halt not cleared")
	}
	r.WritePC(0x40)
	if r.PC != 0 {
		t.Errorf("PC write while running took effect: %x", r.PC)
	}
	r.WriteRegister(0x10, 0x002) // set halt
	r.WritePC(0x40)
	if r.PC != 0x40 || r.NPC != 0x44 {
		t.Errorf("PC write while halted: PC %x NPC %x", r.PC, r.NPC)
	}
}

func TestSemaphore(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	if got := r.ReadRegister(0x1C); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("first semaphore read: %d", got)
	}
	if got := r.ReadRegister(0x1C); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("second semaphore read (test-and-set): %d", got)
	}
	r.WriteRegister(0x1C, 0) // documented release: write clears
	if got := r.ReadRegister(0x1C); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("semaphore after release: %d", got)
	}
	// Same through the RSP's own CP0 view.
	if got := r.ReadCP0(CP0Semaphore); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("CP0 semaphore read after set: %d", got)
	}
}

func TestDMARowsAndSkip(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	dram := make([]byte, 4096)
	for i := range dram {
		dram[i] = byte(i)
	}
	r.AttachDRAM(dram)
	// DRAM 0x40 -> DMEM 0x100, two 16-byte rows, skip 16.
	r.WriteCP0(CP0MemAddr, 0x100)
	r.WriteCP0(CP0DramAddr, 0x40)
	r.WriteCP0(CP0RdLen, 8|(1<<12)|(16<<20))
	for k := 0; k < 16; k++ {
		if r.DMEM[0x100+k] != byte(0x40+k) {
			t.Fatalf("row 0 byte %d: %02x", k, r.DMEM[0x100+k])
		}
		if r.DMEM[0x110+k] != byte(0x60+k) {
			t.Fatalf("row 1 byte %d: %02x", k, r.DMEM[0x110+k])
		}
	}
	if got := r.ReadCP0(CP0MemAddr); got != 0x120 {
		t.Errorf("SP_MEM_ADDR after DMA: %x", got)
	}
	if got := r.ReadCP0(CP0DramAddr); got != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("SP_DRAM_ADDR after DMA: %x", got)
	}
	if got := r.ReadCP0(CP0DMABusy); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("DMA busy after atomic transfer: %d", got)
	}
	// And back out: DMEM 0x100 -> DRAM 0x200, one row.
	r.WriteCP0(CP0MemAddr, 0x100)
	r.WriteCP0(CP0DramAddr, 0x200)
	r.WriteCP0(CP0WrLen, 8)
	for k := 0; k < 16; k++ {
		if dram[0x200+k] != byte(0x40+k) {
			t.Fatalf("write-back byte %d: %02x", k, dram[0x200+k])
		}
	}
	// IMEM bank select (bit 12) reaches IMEM, not DMEM.
	r.WriteCP0(CP0MemAddr, 0x1000)
	r.WriteCP0(CP0DramAddr, 0x40)
	r.WriteCP0(CP0RdLen, 8)
	if r.IMEM[0] != 0x40 || r.IMEM[15] != 0x4F {
		t.Errorf("IMEM DMA: %02x %02x", r.IMEM[0], r.IMEM[15])
	}
	if r.DMEM[0] == 0x40 && r.DMEM[1] == 0x41 {
		t.Error("IMEM DMA leaked into DMEM")
	}
}

func TestCP0DrivenDMA(t *testing.T) {
	// The RSP starts a DMA itself with MTC0, exactly as
	// microcode does, then reads back DMA_BUSY as 0.
	dram := make([]byte, 1024)
	for i := range dram {
		dram[i] = byte(0x80 + i)
	}
	mtc0 := func(rt, rd uint32) uint32 { return 0x10<<26 | 4<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 }
	mfc0 := func(rt, rd uint32) uint32 { return 0x10<<26 | 0<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 }
	r := New()
	r.AttachDRAM(dram)
	loadProgram(r, []uint32{
		addiu(8, 0, 0x80),
		mtc0(8, CP0MemAddr),
		addiu(8, 0, 0x20),
		mtc0(8, CP0DramAddr),
		addiu(8, 0, 8), // 16 bytes, one row
		mtc0(8, CP0RdLen),
		mfc0(9, CP0DMABusy),
		sw(9, 0, 0x100),
		breakInstr,
	})
	start(r)
	for k := 0; k < 16; k++ {
		if r.DMEM[0x80+k] != byte(0xA0+k) {
			t.Fatalf("CP0 DMA byte %d: %02x", k, r.DMEM[0x80+k])
		}
	}
	if got := dmemWord(r, 0x100); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("DMA_BUSY readback: %d", got)
	}
}

func TestBreakInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	fired := false
	r.OnInterrupt = func(on bool) { fired = on }
	r.WriteCP0(CP0Status, 0x100) // interrupt on break
	loadProgram(r, []uint32{breakInstr})
	start(r)
	if !fired {
		t.Error("BREAK with interrupt-on-break did not assert the interrupt")
	}
	if r.Status()&StatusBroke == 0 {
		t.Error("broke bit not set after BREAK")
	}
	// Clearing the interrupt through the status write
	// drops the output.
	r.WriteCP0(CP0Status, 0x008)
	if fired {
		t.Error("interrupt not cleared by status write")
	}
	// Without interrupt-on-break, BREAK stays quiet.
	r2 := New()
	fired2 := false
	r2.OnInterrupt = func(on bool) { fired2 = on }
	loadProgram(r2, []uint32{breakInstr})
	start(r2)
	if fired2 {
		t.Error("BREAK asserted interrupt without interrupt-on-break")
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	dram := make([]byte, 256)
	r.AttachDRAM(dram)
	loadProgram(r, []uint32{
		addiu(8, 0, 1234),
		sw(8, 0, 0x40),
		breakInstr,
	})
	r.V[3][5] = 0xBEEF
	r.ACC[2] = -123456789
	r.VCC, r.VCO, r.VCE = 0xCAFE, 0x0FF0, 0xA5
	start(r)
	buf := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if n := r.Serialize(buf); n != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("serialize wrote %d, SerializeSize %d", n, SerializeSize)
	}
	r2 := New()
	if err := r2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	buf2 := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	r2.Serialize(buf2)
	if !bytes.Equal(buf, buf2) {
		t.Error("serialize/deserialize/serialize not byte identical")
	}
	if r2.DMEM[0x43] != 0xD2 { // 1234 = 0x04D2, low byte at 0x43
		t.Errorf("DMEM not restored: %02x", r2.DMEM[0x43])
	}
	if r2.V[3][5] != 0xBEEF || r2.ACC[2] != -123456789 || r2.VCC != 0xCAFE || r2.VCE != 0xA5 {
		t.Error("vector state not restored")
	}
	if !r2.Halted() {
		t.Error("halt state not restored")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/rsp/vector.go ====================

package rsp

import "math"

// This file implements COP2: the vector computational
// instructions, the vector loads and stores (LWC2/SWC2),
// and the scalar/vector moves. Semantics follow the
// documented Operation pseudocode for each instruction,
// summarized in our own words in the per-op comments.
//
// Two documented judgment calls, both flagged in the
// README:
//
//   - The plain compares (VLT/VEQ/VNE/VGE) combine with a
//     preceding VSUBC exactly as the chapter prose
//     describes: they read the borrow (VCO low byte) and
//     not-equal (VCO high byte) flags VSUBC leaves, and
//     clear VCO and VCE on output. In single precision
//     (VCO clear) they reduce to the plain signed
//     comparison, as documented.
//   - The clip compares write VCC with the le (vs <= -vt)
//     bit for element i at bit i and the ge (vs >= vt) bit
//     at bit i+8, following the guide's register-format
//     figure and the VCH/VCL Operation sections (one
//     prose sentence in the guide swaps them).

// elemIndex maps a destination lane i to the source
// element of vt for the documented element encodings:
// 0..1 whole vector, 2..3 scalar quarter (one of each
// element pair broadcast within the pair), 4..7 scalar
// half (one of each group of four broadcast within the
// group), 8..15 scalar whole (one element broadcast to
// all lanes).
func elemIndex(e, i int) int {
	switch {
	case e < 2:
		return i
	case e < 4:
		return (e & 1) + (i & 6)
	case e < 8:
		return (e & 3) + (i & 4)
	default:
		return e & 7
	}
}

// vByte reads byte b (0 = most significant) of a vector
// register.
func (r *RSP) vByte(reg, b int) byte {
	return byte(r.V[reg][b>>1] >> (8 * uint(1-(b&1))))
}

// setVByte writes byte b of a vector register.
func (r *RSP) setVByte(reg, b int, v byte) {
	if b&1 == 0 {
		r.V[reg][b>>1] = r.V[reg][b>>1]&0x00FF | uint16(v)<<8
	} else {
		r.V[reg][b>>1] = r.V[reg][b>>1]&0xFF00 | uint16(v)
	}
}

// execCOP2 handles the COP2 opcode space: moves between
// the scalar and vector files (rs 0/2/4/6) and vector
// computation (rs bit 4 set, the element field rides in
// the low rs bits).
func (r *RSP) execCOP2(instr uint32) {
	rs := (instr >> 21) & 0x1F
	rt := (instr >> 16) & 0x1F
	vd := (instr >> 11) & 0x1F
	elem := (instr >> 7) & 0xF
	switch {
	case rs == 0: // MFC2: sign-extended 16-bit element at byte offset elem
		v := uint16(r.vByte(int(vd), int(elem)))<<8 |
			uint16(r.vByte(int(vd), int((elem+1)&0xF)))
		r.Reg[rt] = uint32(int32(int16(v)))
	case rs == 2: // CFC2: control register selected by the rd field
		var v uint16
		switch vd {
		case 0:
			v = r.VCO
		case 1:
			v = r.VCC
		case 2:
			v = uint16(r.VCE)
		}
		r.Reg[rt] = uint32(int32(int16(v)))
	case rs == 4: // MTC2: low 16 bits of rt stored at byte offset elem
		v := uint16(r.Reg[rt])
		r.setVByte(int(vd), int(elem), byte(v>>8))
		r.setVByte(int(vd), int((elem+1)&0xF), byte(v))
	case rs == 6: // CTC2
		switch vd {
		case 0:
			r.VCO = uint16(r.Reg[rt])
		case 1:
			r.VCC = uint16(r.Reg[rt])
		case 2:
			r.VCE = uint8(r.Reg[rt])
		}
	case rs&0x10 != 0: // vector computation
		r.execVector(instr)
	}
}

// execVector decodes and runs one vector computational
// instruction.
func (r *RSP) execVector(instr uint32) {
	e := int((instr >> 21) & 0xF)
	vt := int((instr >> 16) & 0x1F)
	vs := int((instr >> 11) & 0x1F)
	vd := int((instr >> 6) & 0x1F)
	funct := instr & 0x3F

	var vsA, vtA [8]uint16
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		vsA[i] = r.V[vs][i]
		vtA[i] = r.V[vt][elemIndex(e, i)]
	}

	switch {
	case funct < 0x10: // multiply family
		r.vecMultiply(vd, vs, vsA, vtA, funct)
	case funct < 0x18 || funct == 0x1D: // add family (VSAR lives at 0x1D)
		r.vecAdd(vd, vs, vsA, vtA, e, funct)
	case funct < 0x20: // reserved in the add group: NOP
	case funct < 0x28: // select family
		r.vecSelect(vd, vsA, vtA, funct)
	case funct < 0x30: // logical family
		r.vecLogical(vd, vsA, vtA, funct)
	default: // divide family
		r.vecDivide(vd, vt, vs, e, funct)
	}
}

// clamp16s clamps a 32-bit value to a signed 16-bit
// result.
func clamp16s(v int32) uint16 {
	if v > 32767 {
		return 0x7FFF
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return 0x8000
	}
	return uint16(v)
}

// clampHiSigned reads accumulator bits 31..16 with the
// documented signed saturation (VMULF/VMACF read-out and
// the M/H partial-product read-outs).
func clampHiSigned(acc int64) uint16 {
	v := acc >> 16
	if v > 32767 {
		return 0x7FFF
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return 0x8000
	}
	return uint16(v)
}

// clampHiUnsigned is clampHiSigned with unsigned
// saturation (VMULU/VMACU read-out).
func clampHiUnsigned(acc int64) uint16 {
	if acc < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	v := acc >> 16
	if v > 0xFFFF {
		return 0xFFFF
	}
	return uint16(v)
}

// clampLowSigned reads accumulator bits 15..0 with the
// documented signed saturation for the L/N partial
// products: the raw low half passes through when the
// accumulator fits in 32 bits; a genuine 48-bit overflow
// saturates by sign.
func clampLowSigned(acc int64) uint16 {
	if acc == int64(int32(acc)) {
		return uint16(acc)
	}
	if acc < 0 {
		return 0x8000
	}
	return 0x7FFF
}

// clampQ reads accumulator bits 32..17 with signed
// saturation and masks to the documented 0xFFF0 result
// (VMULQ/VMACQ read-out).
func clampQ(acc int64) uint16 {
	v := acc >> 17
	if v > 32767 {
		v = 32767
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		v = -32768
	}
	return uint16(v) & 0xFFF0
}

// vecMultiply implements the multiply group. The funct
// low three bits select the format (F, U, RND, Q, L, M,
// N, H) and bit 3 selects accumulate over load. Products
// and clamps follow the documented multiply table.
func (r *RSP) vecMultiply(vd, vsField int, vsA, vtA [8]uint16, funct uint32) {
	accum := funct&0x08 != 0
	format := funct & 0x07
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		s := int32(int16(vsA[i]))
		t := int32(int16(vtA[i]))
		su := uint32(vsA[i])
		tu := uint32(vtA[i])
		switch format {
		case 0, 1: // F: signed fraction; U: same product, unsigned clamp
			prod := int64(s) * int64(t)
			if accum {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(r.ACC[i] + (prod << 1))
			} else {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48((prod << 1) + 0x8000)
			}
			if format == 0 {
				r.V[vd][i] = clampHiSigned(r.ACC[i])
			} else {
				r.V[vd][i] = clampHiUnsigned(r.ACC[i])
			}
		case 2: // RND: conditionally add vt to the accumulator
			shift := uint(0)
			if vsField == 1 { // the vs instruction field, not a register
				shift = 16
			}
			add := int64(t) << shift
			if !accum { // VRNDN: add when accumulator is negative
				if r.ACC[i] < 0 {
					r.ACC[i] = acc48(r.ACC[i] + add)
				}
			} else { // VRNDP: add when accumulator is positive
				if r.ACC[i] > 0 {
					r.ACC[i] = acc48(r.ACC[i] + add)
				}
			}
			r.V[vd][i] = clampHiSigned(r.ACC[i])
		case 3: // Q: MPEG quantization multiply / oddification
			if !accum { // VMULQ
				prod := int64(s) * int64(t)
				acc := prod << 16
				if prod < 0 {
					acc += 31 << 16
				}
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(acc)
			} else { // VMACQ: oddify the accumulator in place
				acc := r.ACC[i]
				if acc < 0 && (acc>>21)&1 == 0 {
					acc += 1 << 21
				} else if acc > 0 && (acc>>21)&1 == 0 && (acc>>21) != 0 {
					acc -= 1 << 21
				}
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(acc)
			}
			r.V[vd][i] = clampQ(r.ACC[i])
		case 4: // L: unsigned x unsigned, product shifted right 16
			prod := uint64(su) * uint64(tu)
			delta := int64(prod >> 16)
			if accum {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(r.ACC[i] + delta)
			} else {
				r.ACC[i] = delta
			}
			r.V[vd][i] = clampLowSigned(r.ACC[i])
		case 5: // M: signed x unsigned, full product
			prod := int64(s) * int64(tu)
			if accum {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(r.ACC[i] + prod)
			} else {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(prod)
			}
			r.V[vd][i] = clampHiSigned(r.ACC[i])
		case 6: // N: unsigned x signed, full product
			prod := int64(su) * int64(t)
			if accum {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(r.ACC[i] + prod)
			} else {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(prod)
			}
			r.V[vd][i] = clampLowSigned(r.ACC[i])
		case 7: // H: signed x signed, product shifted left 16
			prod := int64(s) * int64(t)
			delta := prod << 16
			if accum {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(r.ACC[i] + delta)
			} else {
				r.ACC[i] = acc48(delta)
			}
			r.V[vd][i] = clampHiSigned(r.ACC[i])
		}
	}
}

// vecAdd implements the add group: VADD, VSUB, VABS,
// VADDC, VSUBC, and VSAR. VADD/VSUB consume the VCO low
// byte as carry/borrow in and clear VCO; VADDC/VSUBC
// produce it.
func (r *RSP) vecAdd(vd, vs int, vsA, vtA [8]uint16, e int, funct uint32) {
	switch funct {
	case 0x10, 0x11: // VADD, VSUB
		vco := r.VCO
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			var res int32
			if funct == 0x10 {
				res = int32(int16(vsA[i])) + int32(int16(vtA[i])) + int32((vco>>uint(i))&1)
			} else {
				res = int32(int16(vsA[i])) - int32(int16(vtA[i])) - int32((vco>>uint(i))&1)
			}
			r.ACC[i] = int64(res)
			r.V[vd][i] = clamp16s(res)
		}
		r.VCO = 0
	case 0x13: // VABS: negate vt by the sign of vs
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			var res uint16
			switch s := int16(vsA[i]); {
			case s < 0:
				res = uint16(-int32(int16(vtA[i])))
			case s == 0:
				res = 0
			default:
				res = vtA[i]
			}
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(res))
			r.V[vd][i] = res
		}
	case 0x14: // VADDC
		var vco uint16
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			sum := uint32(vsA[i]) + uint32(vtA[i])
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(uint16(sum)))
			r.V[vd][i] = uint16(sum)
			if sum > 0xFFFF {
				vco |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
			// The not-equal bit is written 0 by VADDC per
			// the documented Operation.
		}
		r.VCO = vco
	case 0x15: // VSUBC
		var vco uint16
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			d := int32(vsA[i]) - int32(vtA[i])
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(uint16(d)))
			r.V[vd][i] = uint16(d)
			if d < 0 {
				vco |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
			if d != 0 {
				vco |= 1 << uint(i+8)
			}
		}
		r.VCO = vco
	case 0x1D: // VSAR: read one accumulator slice, write vs into it
		if e > 2 {
			return
		}
		shift := uint((2 - e) * 16)
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			r.V[vd][i] = uint16(r.ACC[i] >> shift)
			u := uint64(r.ACC[i]) & ((1 << 48) - 1)
			u = u&^(0xFFFF<<shift) | uint64(r.V[vs][i])<<shift
			r.ACC[i] = acc48(int64(u))
		}
	}
}

// vecSelect implements the select group: the plain
// compares, the VCH/VCL/VCR clip family, and VMRG.
func (r *RSP) vecSelect(vd int, vsA, vtA [8]uint16, funct uint32) {
	switch funct {
	case 0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23: // VLT, VEQ, VNE, VGE
		vco := r.VCO
		var vcc uint16
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			s, t := int16(vsA[i]), int16(vtA[i])
			borrow := (vco >> uint(i)) & 1
			ne := (vco >> uint(i+8)) & 1
			var c bool
			switch funct {
			case 0x20: // VLT
				c = s < t || (s == t && borrow != 0)
			case 0x21: // VEQ
				c = s == t && ne == 0
			case 0x22: // VNE
				c = s != t || (s == t && ne != 0)
			case 0x23: // VGE
				c = s > t || (s == t && borrow == 0)
			}
			sel := vtA[i]
			if c {
				sel = vsA[i]
				vcc |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(sel))
			r.V[vd][i] = sel
		}
		r.VCC = vcc
		r.VCO = 0
		r.VCE = 0
	case 0x25: // VCH: clip test, high half
		var vcc, vco uint16
		var vce uint8
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			s := int32(int16(vsA[i]))
			t := int32(int16(vtA[i]))
			sign := (vsA[i]^vtA[i])&0x8000 != 0
			var ge, le, isVCE, eq bool
			var di int32
			if sign {
				ge = t < 0
				sum := s + t
				le = sum <= 0
				isVCE = sum == -1
				eq = sum == 0
				if le {
					di = -t
				} else {
					di = s
				}
			} else {
				le = t < 0
				d := s - t
				ge = d >= 0
				eq = d == 0
				if ge {
					di = t
				} else {
					di = s
				}
			}
			res := uint16(di)
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(res))
			r.V[vd][i] = res
			if ge {
				vcc |= 1 << uint(i+8)
			}
			if le {
				vcc |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
			if sign {
				vco |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
			if !eq {
				vco |= 1 << uint(i+8)
			}
			if isVCE {
				vce |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
		}
		r.VCC, r.VCO, r.VCE = vcc, vco, vce
	case 0x24: // VCL: clip test, low half (consumes VCH state)
		vccIn, vcoIn, vceIn := r.VCC, r.VCO, r.VCE
		var vcc uint16
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			le := (vccIn>>uint(i))&1 != 0
			ge := (vccIn>>uint(i+8))&1 != 0
			vce := (vceIn>>uint(i))&1 != 0
			eq := (vcoIn>>uint(i+8))&1 == 0
			sign := (vcoIn>>uint(i))&1 != 0
			var di uint16
			if sign {
				sum := uint32(vsA[i]) + uint32(vtA[i])
				carry := sum > 0xFFFF
				if eq {
					if vce {
						le = (sum&0xFFFF) == 0 || !carry
					} else {
						le = (sum&0xFFFF) == 0 && !carry
					}
				}
				if le {
					di = -vtA[i]
				} else {
					di = vsA[i]
				}
			} else {
				d := int32(int16(vsA[i])) - int32(int16(vtA[i]))
				if eq {
					ge = d >= 0
				}
				if ge {
					di = vtA[i]
				} else {
					di = vsA[i]
				}
			}
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(di))
			r.V[vd][i] = di
			if le {
				vcc |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
			if ge {
				vcc |= 1 << uint(i+8)
			}
		}
		r.VCC = vcc
		r.VCO = 0
		r.VCE = 0
	case 0x26: // VCR: ones-complement clip test
		var vcc uint16
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			s := int32(int16(vsA[i]))
			t := int32(int16(vtA[i]))
			sign := (vsA[i]^vtA[i])&0x8000 != 0
			var ge, le bool
			var di uint16
			if sign {
				ge = t < 0
				le = s+t+1 <= 0
				if le {
					di = ^vtA[i]
				} else {
					di = vsA[i]
				}
			} else {
				le = t < 0
				ge = s-t >= 0
				if ge {
					di = vtA[i]
				} else {
					di = vsA[i]
				}
			}
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(di))
			r.V[vd][i] = di
			if ge {
				vcc |= 1 << uint(i+8)
			}
			if le {
				vcc |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
		}
		r.VCC = vcc
		r.VCO = 0
		r.VCE = 0
	case 0x27: // VMRG: merge by VCC low byte
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			sel := vtA[i]
			if (r.VCC>>uint(i))&1 != 0 {
				sel = vsA[i]
			}
			r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(sel))
			r.V[vd][i] = sel
		}
	}
}

// vecLogical implements the logical group. Results also
// land in the accumulator low halves, per the documented
// Operation sections.
func (r *RSP) vecLogical(vd int, vsA, vtA [8]uint16, funct uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		var res uint16
		switch funct {
		case 0x28: // VAND
			res = vsA[i] & vtA[i]
		case 0x29: // VNAND
			res = ^(vsA[i] & vtA[i])
		case 0x2A: // VOR
			res = vsA[i] | vtA[i]
		case 0x2B: // VNOR
			res = ^(vsA[i] | vtA[i])
		case 0x2C: // VXOR
			res = vsA[i] ^ vtA[i]
		case 0x2D: // VNXOR
			res = ^(vsA[i] ^ vtA[i])
		}
		r.ACC[i] = int64(int16(res))
		r.V[vd][i] = res
	}
}

// vecDivide implements the divide group: VRCP, VRCPL,
// VRCPH, VRSQ, VRSQL, VRSQH, VMOV, VNOP. The destination
// element comes from the vs instruction field and the
// source element from the element field, per the
// documentation. The H forms latch the input high half
// and write out the previously computed result's high
// half; the L forms combine with the latched high half.
//
// Reciprocals are computed exactly (integer arithmetic
// for RCP, float64 for RSQ) in the documented formats:
// single precision reads the element as an S1.15 fraction
// and returns S16.15; double precision reads the latched
// 32-bit input as S15.16 and returns S16.15. The hardware
// uses a 1024-entry lookup table with about 10 bits of
// precision, so hardware low bits can differ; see the
// README precision note. Negative inputs produce the
// ones complement of the positive result, and zero
// saturates to 0x7FFFFFFF, both per the documentation.
func (r *RSP) vecDivide(vd, vt, vsField, e int, funct uint32) {
	de := vsField & 7
	elem := r.V[vt][e&7]
	switch funct {
	case 0x30, 0x34: // VRCP, VRSQ (single precision)
		mag, neg := abs16(elem)
		res := recipResult(mag, 15, funct == 0x34)
		if neg {
			res = ^res
		}
		r.divOut = res
		r.V[vd][de] = uint16(res)
		r.recipAccSideEffect(elem)
	case 0x31, 0x35: // VRCPL, VRSQL (double precision, low half in)
		d := (r.divIn &^ 0xFFFF) | int32(elem)
		r.divIn = d
		mag, neg := abs32(d)
		res := recipResult(mag, 16, funct == 0x35)
		if neg {
			res = ^res
		}
		r.divOut = res
		r.V[vd][de] = uint16(res)
		r.recipAccSideEffect(elem)
	case 0x32, 0x36: // VRCPH, VRSQH (latch high half, write prior high)
		r.divIn = (int32(int16(elem)) << 16) | (r.divIn & 0xFFFF)
		r.V[vd][de] = uint16(r.divOut >> 16)
		r.recipAccSideEffect(elem)
	case 0x33: // VMOV
		r.V[vd][de] = elem
	case 0x37: // VNOP
	}
}

// recipAccSideEffect writes the source element into the
// low 16 bits of every accumulator lane, the documented
// side effect of the reciprocal instructions.
func (r *RSP) recipAccSideEffect(elem uint16) {
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		r.ACC[i] = (r.ACC[i] &^ 0xFFFF) | int64(elem)
	}
}

func abs16(v uint16) (uint32, bool) {
	s := int32(int16(v))
	if s < 0 {
		return uint32(-s), true
	}
	return uint32(s), false
}

func abs32(v int32) (uint32, bool) {
	if v < 0 {
		return uint32(-(int64(v))), true
	}
	return uint32(v), false
}

// recipResult computes a reciprocal (rsq=false) or
// reciprocal square root (rsq=true) of the positive
// magnitude mag, where the input value is mag / 2^frac
// and the result is in S16.15 format.
func recipResult(mag uint32, frac uint, rsq bool) int32 {
	if mag == 0 {
		return 0x7FFFFFFF
	}
	if !rsq {
		num := uint64(1) << (15 + frac)
		v := (num + uint64(mag)/2) / uint64(mag)
		if v > 0x7FFFFFFF {
			v = 0x7FFFFFFF
		}
		return int32(v)
	}
	d := float64(mag) / float64(uint64(1)<<frac)
	v := math.Floor(32768.0/math.Sqrt(d) + 0.5)
	if v > 0x7FFFFFFF {
		v = 0x7FFFFFFF
	}
	return int32(v)
}

// loadStoreShift gives the offset scale for each vector
// load/store op (the rd-field encoding).
var loadStoreShift = [12]uint{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4}

// execLoadStore implements LWC2 (load=true) and SWC2
// (load=false). The rd field selects the transfer kind,
// the element field is a byte index into the vector
// register, and the 7-bit offset is sign-extended and
// scaled by the per-op shift. All addresses wrap in the
// 4 KB DMEM.
func (r *RSP) execLoadStore(instr uint32, load bool) {
	base := (instr >> 21) & 0x1F
	vt := int((instr >> 16) & 0x1F)
	op := (instr >> 11) & 0x1F
	elem := int((instr >> 7) & 0xF)
	off7 := int32(instr & 0x7F)
	if off7&0x40 != 0 {
		off7 -= 0x80
	}
	if op > 11 {
		return
	}
	addr := (r.Reg[base] + uint32(off7<<loadStoreShift[op])) & 0xFFF

	// memByte and regByte move one byte in the transfer
	// direction.
	get := func(a uint32) byte { return r.dmemByte(a) }
	put := func(a uint32, v byte) { r.setDMEMByte(a, v) }

	switch op {
	case 0: // LBV / SBV
		if load {
			r.setVByte(vt, elem, get(addr))
		} else {
			put(addr, r.vByte(vt, elem))
		}
	case 1, 2, 3: // LSV/SSV (2), LLV/SLV (4), LDV/SDV (8)
		n := 2 << (op - 1)
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			if load {
				r.setVByte(vt, (elem+k)&0xF, get(addr+uint32(k)))
			} else {
				put(addr+uint32(k), r.vByte(vt, (elem+k)&0xF))
			}
		}
	case 4: // LQV / SQV: from addr to the end of its 16-byte block
		n := 16 - int(addr&0xF)
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			if load {
				r.setVByte(vt, (elem+k)&0xF, get(addr+uint32(k)))
			} else {
				put(addr+uint32(k), r.vByte(vt, (elem+k)&0xF))
			}
		}
	case 5: // LRV / SRV: the tail of the block into the register tail
		n := int(addr & 0xF)
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			a := addr - uint32(n) + uint32(k)
			if load {
				r.setVByte(vt, 16-n+k, get(a))
			} else {
				put(a, r.vByte(vt, 16-n+k))
			}
		}
	case 6, 7: // LPV/SPV (bits 15..8), LUV/SUV (bits 14..7)
		shift := uint(8)
		if op == 7 {
			shift = 7
		}
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if load {
				r.V[vt][i] = uint16(get(addr+uint32(i))) << shift
			} else {
				put(addr+uint32(i), byte(r.V[vt][i]>>shift))
			}
		}
	case 8: // LHV / SHV: every second byte, bits 14..7
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			a := addr + uint32(2*i)
			if load {
				r.V[vt][i] = uint16(get(a)) << 7
			} else {
				put(a, byte(r.V[vt][i]>>7))
			}
		}
	case 9: // LFV / SFV: every fourth byte into lanes (elem/2 + i)
		base0 := elem >> 1 // documented element is 0 or 8, giving lanes 0..3 or 4..7
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			a := addr + uint32(4*i)
			if load {
				r.V[vt][base0+i] = uint16(get(a)) << 7
			} else {
				put(a, byte(r.V[vt][base0+i]>>7))
			}
		}
	case 10: // SWV (store only): the register rotated by elem/2 lanes
		if load {
			return
		}
		block := addr &^ 0xF
		for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
			v := r.V[vt][(j+(elem>>1))&7]
			put(block+uint32(2*j), byte(v>>8))
			put(block+uint32(2*j)+1, byte(v))
		}
	case 11: // LTV / STV: transpose across an 8-register group
		block := addr &^ 0xF
		lane := elem >> 1
		for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
			reg := (vt & 0x18) | ((j + lane) & 7)
			a := block + uint32(2*j)
			if load {
				r.V[reg][lane] = uint16(get(a))<<8 | uint16(get(a+1))
			} else {
				v := r.V[reg][lane]
				put(a, byte(v>>8))
				put(a+1, byte(v))
			}
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/chips/rsp/vector_test.go ====================

package rsp

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// vop encodes a COP2 computational instruction:
// opcode COP2, bit 25 set, element, vt, vs, vd, funct.
func vop(funct, e, vt, vs, vd uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x12<<26 | 1<<25 | e<<21 | vt<<16 | vs<<11 | vd<<6 | funct
}

// step1 executes a single instruction placed at IMEM 0
// (a BREAK sits in the next slot and is not executed).
func step1(r *RSP, instr uint32) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(r.IMEM[0:], instr)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(r.IMEM[4:], breakInstr)
	r.PC, r.NPC = 0, 4
	r.halted = false
	r.Step()
}

// cfc2 runs a CFC2 into scalar register rt and returns
// its new value. sel: 0 = VCO, 1 = VCC, 2 = VCE.
func cfc2(r *RSP, rt, sel uint32) uint32 {
	step1(r, 0x12<<26|2<<21|rt<<16|sel<<11)
	return r.Reg[rt]
}

// fill sets every lane of a vector register.
func fill(r *RSP, reg int, v uint16) {
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		r.V[reg][i] = v
	}
}

func TestVMULFCornerAndValues(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	fill(r, 1, 0x8000)
	fill(r, 2, 0x8000)
	step1(r, vop(0x00, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vmulf v3, v1, v2
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if r.V[3][i] != 0x7FFF {
			t.Errorf("lane %d: %04x, want 7fff (saturated)", i, r.V[3][i])
		}
		if r.ACC[i] != 0x80008000 {
			t.Errorf("acc lane %d: %x, want 80008000", i, r.ACC[i])
		}
	}
	// Read the accumulator back through VSAR slices:
	// element 1 = mid, 0 = high, 2 = low.
	step1(r, vop(0x1D, 1, 0, 0, 4)) // vsar v4, v0, [1]
	step1(r, vop(0x1D, 0, 0, 0, 5)) // vsar v5, v0, [0]
	step1(r, vop(0x1D, 2, 0, 0, 6)) // vsar v6, v0, [2]
	if r.V[4][0] != 0x8000 || r.V[5][0] != 0x0000 || r.V[6][0] != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("vsar readback: mid %04x high %04x low %04x",
			r.V[4][0], r.V[5][0], r.V[6][0])
	}

	// Ordinary fractions: 0.5*0.5, 0.25*0.5, -0.25*0.5,
	// and the near-1.0 product.
	r.V[1] = [8]uint16{0x4000, 0x2000, 0xE000, 0x7FFF}
	r.V[2] = [8]uint16{0x4000, 0x4000, 0x4000, 0x4000}
	step1(r, vop(0x00, 0, 2, 1, 3))
	want := [8]uint16{0x2000, 0x1000, 0xF000, 0x4000}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if r.V[3][i] != want[i] {
			t.Errorf("vmulf lane %d: %04x want %04x", i, r.V[3][i], want[i])
		}
	}
	// VMULU clamps the same corner to the unsigned result.
	fill(r, 1, 0x8000)
	fill(r, 2, 0x8000)
	step1(r, vop(0x01, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vmulu
	if r.V[3][0] != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("vmulu corner: %04x want 8000", r.V[3][0])
	}
}

func TestVMACChainSaturates(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	fill(r, 1, 0x7FFF)
	fill(r, 2, 0x7FFF)
	step1(r, vop(0x00, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vmulf: ACC = 0x7FFE8002
	if r.V[3][0] != 0x7FFE {
		t.Fatalf("vmulf: %04x", r.V[3][0])
	}
	step1(r, vop(0x08, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vmacf: ACC = 0x7FFE8002 + 0x7FFE0002
	if got := r.ACC[0]; got != 0xFFFC8004 {
		t.Fatalf("acc after vmacf: %x", got)
	}
	if r.V[3][0] != 0x7FFF {
		t.Fatalf("vmacf read-out not saturated: %04x", r.V[3][0])
	}
	step1(r, vop(0x08, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vmacf again
	if got := r.ACC[0]; got != 0x17FFA8006 {
		t.Errorf("acc after second vmacf: %x", got)
	}
	if r.V[3][0] != 0x7FFF {
		t.Errorf("still saturated: %04x", r.V[3][0])
	}
}

func TestQuarterBroadcast(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	// vt lanes; quarter element 1 (e=3) broadcasts vt[1],
	// vt[3], vt[5], vt[7] within their pairs. vs = 0.5 in
	// every lane, so each result is exactly vt/2.
	r.V[2] = [8]uint16{0x1000, 0x2000, 0x3000, 0x4000, 0x5000, 0x6000, 0x7000, 0x7F00}
	fill(r, 1, 0x4000)
	step1(r, vop(0x00, 3, 2, 1, 3)) // vmulf v3, v1, v2[1q]
	want := [8]uint16{0x1000, 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x2000, 0x3000, 0x3000, 0x3F80, 0x3F80}
	if r.V[3] != want {
		t.Errorf("quarter broadcast: %04x want %04x", r.V[3], want)
	}
	// Half broadcast (e=6 -> vt[2] and vt[6]) and whole
	// broadcast (e=8+5 -> vt[5]) for contrast.
	fill(r, 1, 0x4000)
	step1(r, vop(0x00, 6, 2, 1, 3))
	wantH := [8]uint16{0x1800, 0x1800, 0x1800, 0x1800, 0x3800, 0x3800, 0x3800, 0x3800}
	if r.V[3] != wantH {
		t.Errorf("half broadcast: %04x want %04x", r.V[3], wantH)
	}
	step1(r, vop(0x00, 13, 2, 1, 3))
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if r.V[3][i] != 0x3000 {
			t.Errorf("whole broadcast lane %d: %04x", i, r.V[3][i])
		}
	}
}

func TestVADDCVSUBCCarryChain(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	// VSUBC on the low halves: 0x0000 - 0x0001 borrows
	// and is not equal, setting VCO = 0xFF00 (NE byte)
	// plus borrow bits 0x00FF... borrow is bit i, NE is
	// bit i+8: all lanes borrow, so VCO = 0xFFFF.
	fill(r, 1, 0x0000)
	fill(r, 2, 0x0001)
	step1(r, vop(0x15, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vsubc v3, v1, v2
	if r.V[3][0] != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("vsubc result: %04x", r.V[3][0])
	}
	if got := cfc2(r, 5, 0); got != 0xFFFFFFFF { // sign-extended 0xFFFF
		t.Errorf("cfc2 vco after vsubc: %08x", got)
	}
	// VADD on the high halves consumes the borrow:
	// 5 - 3 - 1 = 1 (32-bit: 0x00050000 - 0x00030001 =
	// 0x0001FFFF).
	fill(r, 1, 5)
	fill(r, 2, 3)
	step1(r, vop(0x11, 0, 2, 1, 4)) // vsub v4, v1, v2 (uses VCO borrow)
	if r.V[4][0] != 1 {
		t.Errorf("vsub with borrow in: %04x", r.V[4][0])
	}
	if r.VCO != 0 {
		t.Errorf("vsub did not clear VCO: %04x", r.VCO)
	}
	// VADDC carry: 0xFFFF + 0x0001 carries in every lane;
	// its not-equal byte is written 0 per the documented
	// Operation, so VCO = 0x00FF.
	fill(r, 1, 0xFFFF)
	fill(r, 2, 0x0001)
	step1(r, vop(0x14, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vaddc
	if r.V[3][0] != 0x0000 {
		t.Errorf("vaddc result: %04x", r.V[3][0])
	}
	if got := cfc2(r, 5, 0); got != 0x000000FF {
		t.Errorf("cfc2 vco after vaddc: %08x", got)
	}
}

func TestCompareCombineWithVSUBC(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	// Double-precision VEQ: low halves equal via VSUBC,
	// high halves equal, so VEQ reports true.
	fill(r, 1, 0x1234)
	fill(r, 2, 0x1234)
	step1(r, vop(0x15, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vsubc: result 0, NE = 0
	fill(r, 1, 0x0007)
	fill(r, 2, 0x0007)
	step1(r, vop(0x21, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // veq
	if r.VCC != 0x00FF {
		t.Errorf("veq combined: VCC %04x", r.VCC)
	}
	if r.V[3][0] != 0x0007 { // true selects vs
		t.Errorf("veq select: %04x", r.V[3][0])
	}
	// Same highs, but low halves differ (NE = 1): VEQ
	// reports false and selects vt.
	fill(r, 1, 0x1234)
	fill(r, 2, 0x1235)
	step1(r, vop(0x15, 0, 2, 1, 3))
	fill(r, 1, 0x0007)
	fill(r, 2, 0x0007)
	step1(r, vop(0x21, 0, 2, 1, 3))
	if r.VCC != 0 {
		t.Errorf("veq with NE lows: VCC %04x", r.VCC)
	}
	// VMRG merges by the VCC a compare leaves.
	fill(r, 1, 10)
	fill(r, 2, 20)
	step1(r, vop(0x20, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vlt: 10 < 20 true
	fill(r, 1, 0xAAAA)
	fill(r, 2, 0xBBBB)
	step1(r, vop(0x27, 0, 2, 1, 4)) // vmrg
	if r.V[4][0] != 0xAAAA {
		t.Errorf("vmrg: %04x", r.V[4][0])
	}
}

func TestVCHVCLClip(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	// Equal values: ge set, VD = vt.
	fill(r, 1, 100)
	fill(r, 2, 100)
	step1(r, vop(0x25, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vch
	if r.V[3][0] != 100 || r.VCC != 0xFF00 || r.VCO != 0 || r.VCE != 0 {
		t.Errorf("vch equal: vd %04x vcc %04x vco %04x vce %02x",
			r.V[3][0], r.VCC, r.VCO, r.VCE)
	}
	// Above range, same sign: clamped to +vt.
	fill(r, 1, 200)
	fill(r, 2, 100)
	step1(r, vop(0x25, 0, 2, 1, 3))
	if r.V[3][0] != 100 || r.VCC != 0xFF00 {
		t.Errorf("vch clamp high: vd %04x vcc %04x", r.V[3][0], r.VCC)
	}
	// Below range, signs differ: clamped to -vt, le set.
	fill(r, 1, 0xFF38) // -200
	fill(r, 2, 100)
	step1(r, vop(0x25, 0, 2, 1, 3))
	if r.V[3][0] != 0xFF9C || r.VCC != 0x00FF {
		t.Errorf("vch clamp low: vd %04x vcc %04x", r.V[3][0], r.VCC)
	}
	// Inside range: unchanged.
	fill(r, 1, 50)
	fill(r, 2, 100)
	step1(r, vop(0x25, 0, 2, 1, 3))
	if r.V[3][0] != 50 || r.VCC != 0x0000 {
		t.Errorf("vch inside: vd %04x vcc %04x", r.V[3][0], r.VCC)
	}

	// Double precision: value (100, 1) against bound
	// (100, 0) is just above the bound and must clamp to
	// exactly (100, 0): VCH on the highs ties (ge, eq),
	// then VCL on the lows resolves with the difference.
	r2 := New()
	fill(r2, 1, 100)                 // vs high
	fill(r2, 2, 100)                 // vt high
	step1(r2, vop(0x25, 0, 2, 1, 3)) // vch -> VD high
	hi := r2.V[3]
	fill(r2, 1, 0x0001)              // vs low
	fill(r2, 2, 0x0000)              // vt low
	step1(r2, vop(0x24, 0, 2, 1, 4)) // vcl -> VD low
	if hi[0] != 100 || r2.V[4][0] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("vch/vcl clamp: high %04x low %04x", hi[0], r2.V[4][0])
	}
	if r2.VCO != 0 || r2.VCE != 0 {
		t.Errorf("vcl did not clear VCO/VCE: %04x %02x", r2.VCO, r2.VCE)
	}
	// And (99, 0xFFFF) against (100, 0) is inside: the
	// low half passes through untouched.
	fill(r2, 1, 99)
	fill(r2, 2, 100)
	step1(r2, vop(0x25, 0, 2, 1, 3))
	fill(r2, 1, 0xFFFF)
	fill(r2, 2, 0x0000)
	step1(r2, vop(0x24, 0, 2, 1, 4))
	if r2.V[4][0] != 0xFFFF {
		t.Errorf("vcl inside: low %04x", r2.V[4][0])
	}
}

func TestReciprocals(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	// VRCP of 0.5 (element 0x4000) is exactly 2.0:
	// combined result 0x00010000 across VRCP + VRCPH.
	r.V[5][3] = 0x4000
	step1(r, vop(0x30, 11, 5, 0, 6)) // vrcp v6[0], v5[3]
	lo := r.V[6][0]
	step1(r, vop(0x32, 8, 0, 1, 6)) // vrcph v6[1], v0[0]
	combined := uint32(r.V[6][1])<<16 | uint32(lo)
	if combined != 0x00010000 {
		t.Errorf("vrcp(0.5): %08x want 00010000", combined)
	}
	// VRCP of 0x7FFF (the closest S1.15 value to 1.0):
	// 2^30/32767 = 32768.99997 in exact arithmetic,
	// rounding to 0x8001 in S16.15. The exact 0.5 input
	// 0x8000 gives exactly 1.0 (0x8000).
	r.V[5][3] = 0x7FFF
	step1(r, vop(0x30, 11, 5, 0, 6))
	step1(r, vop(0x32, 8, 0, 1, 6))
	combined = uint32(r.V[6][1])<<16 | uint32(r.V[6][0])
	if combined != 0x00008001 {
		t.Errorf("vrcp(~1.0): %08x want 00008001", combined)
	}
	// Negative input: ones complement of the positive
	// result. vrcp(-0.5): positive is 0x00010000, result
	// 0xFFFEFFFF.
	r.V[5][3] = 0xC000
	step1(r, vop(0x30, 11, 5, 0, 6))
	step1(r, vop(0x32, 8, 0, 1, 6))
	combined = uint32(r.V[6][1])<<16 | uint32(r.V[6][0])
	if combined != 0xFFFEFFFF {
		t.Errorf("vrcp(-0.5): %08x want fffeffff", combined)
	}
	// VRSQ of 0.5 is sqrt(2): 1.41421 * 32768 = 46341.
	r.V[5][3] = 0x4000
	step1(r, vop(0x34, 11, 5, 0, 6)) // vrsq
	if got := r.V[6][0]; got != 0xB505 {
		t.Errorf("vrsq(0.5) low: %04x want b505", got)
	}
	// Double precision: vrcph latches the high half of
	// 1.0 (S15.16 0x00010000), vrcpl the low half; the
	// reciprocal is 1.0 in S16.15 (0x00008000).
	r.V[5][0] = 0x0001
	step1(r, vop(0x32, 8, 5, 0, 6)) // vrcph v6[0], v5[0]
	r.V[5][0] = 0x0000
	step1(r, vop(0x31, 8, 5, 0, 6)) // vrcpl v6[0], v5[0]
	if got := r.V[6][0]; got != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("vrcp dp 1.0 low: %04x want 8000", got)
	}
	step1(r, vop(0x32, 8, 0, 1, 6)) // vrcph writes the high half
	if got := r.V[6][1]; got != 0x0000 {
		t.Errorf("vrcp dp 1.0 high: %04x", got)
	}
	// Divide by zero saturates.
	r.V[5][3] = 0
	step1(r, vop(0x30, 11, 5, 0, 6))
	step1(r, vop(0x32, 8, 0, 1, 6))
	combined = uint32(r.V[6][1])<<16 | uint32(r.V[6][0])
	if combined != 0x7FFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("vrcp(0): %08x want 7fffffff", combined)
	}
}

func TestMovesAndControlRegs(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	r.Reg[5] = 0x1234BEEF
	// MTC2 stores the low half of rt at byte element 4
	// of v7 (lane 2).
	step1(r, 0x12<<26|4<<21|5<<16|7<<11|4<<7)
	if r.V[7][2] != 0xBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("mtc2: %04x", r.V[7][2])
	}
	// MFC2 sign-extends the element back out.
	step1(r, 0x12<<26|0<<21|6<<16|7<<11|4<<7)
	if r.Reg[6] != 0xFFFFBEEF {
		t.Errorf("mfc2: %08x", r.Reg[6])
	}
	// An odd byte element merges halves of two lanes:
	// element 5 of v7 is low byte of lane 2 then high
	// byte of lane 3.
	r.V[7][3] = 0xCA00
	step1(r, 0x12<<26|0<<21|6<<16|7<<11|5<<7)
	if r.Reg[6] != 0xFFFFEFCA {
		t.Errorf("mfc2 odd element: %08x", r.Reg[6])
	}
	// CTC2/CFC2 round trip on VCO.
	r.Reg[5] = 0x0000ABCD
	step1(r, 0x12<<26|6<<21|5<<16|0<<11) // ctc2 vco
	if r.VCO != 0xABCD {
		t.Fatalf("ctc2 vco: %04x", r.VCO)
	}
	if got := cfc2(r, 6, 0); got != 0xFFFFABCD {
		t.Errorf("cfc2 vco: %08x", got)
	}
	// VMOV copies one element; VNOP changes nothing.
	r.V[2][5] = 0x7777
	step1(r, vop(0x33, 13, 2, 1, 3)) // vmov v3[1], v2[5]
	if r.V[3][1] != 0x7777 {
		t.Errorf("vmov: %04x", r.V[3][1])
	}
	before := r.V[3]
	step1(r, vop(0x37, 0, 0, 0, 3)) // vnop
	if r.V[3] != before {
		t.Error("vnop modified state")
	}
}

func TestLQVUnalignedAndLRVPair(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		r.DMEM[0x100+i] = 0xA0 + byte(i)
		r.DMEM[0x110+i] = 0xB0 + byte(i)
	}
	fill(r, 1, 0xEEEE)
	// LQV at 0x104 loads 12 bytes (to the end of the
	// 16-byte block) into register bytes 0..11; bytes
	// 12..15 keep the old value.
	r.Reg[2] = 4
	step1(r, 0x32<<26|2<<21|1<<16|4<<11|0<<7|0x10) // lqv v1, 0x100($2) -> addr 0x104
	if got := r.vByte(1, 0); got != 0xA4 {
		t.Errorf("lqv byte 0: %02x", got)
	}
	if got := r.vByte(1, 11); got != 0xAF {
		t.Errorf("lqv byte 11: %02x", got)
	}
	if got := r.vByte(1, 12); got != 0xEE {
		t.Errorf("lqv overwrote byte 12: %02x", got)
	}
	// LRV at 0x114 loads the first 4 bytes of the next
	// block into register bytes 12..15, completing the
	// unaligned 16-byte load.
	step1(r, 0x32<<26|2<<21|1<<16|5<<11|0<<7|0x11) // lrv v1, 0x110($2) -> addr 0x114
	for k := 0; k < 4; k++ {
		if got := r.vByte(1, 12+k); got != 0xB0+byte(k) {
			t.Errorf("lrv byte %d: %02x", 12+k, got)
		}
	}
	// SQV stores the same span back out.
	for i := range r.DMEM {
		r.DMEM[i] = 0
	}
	r.Reg[2] = 4
	step1(r, 0x3A<<26|2<<21|1<<16|4<<11|0<<7|0x10) // sqv v1, 0x100($2)
	if r.DMEM[0x104] != 0xA4 || r.DMEM[0x10F] != 0xAF || r.DMEM[0x110] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("sqv: %02x %02x %02x", r.DMEM[0x104], r.DMEM[0x10F], r.DMEM[0x110])
	}
}

func TestTransposeStore(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	// A 4x4 matrix in the low lanes of v0..v3: A[r][c].
	for row := 0; row < 4; row++ {
		for col := 0; col < 4; col++ {
			r.V[row][col] = uint16(row*4 + col + 1)
		}
	}
	// STV at lane c writes the group column starting at
	// register c (the documented start-element rotation):
	// block c short j is A[(j+c)&7][c], with the lanes of
	// registers 4..7 reading as zero here. The four
	// blocks are the transpose in rotated form.
	r.Reg[2] = 0
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		off := uint32(0x20 + c*2) // field: addr = off << 4 = 0x200 + c*0x20
		step1(r, 0x3A<<26|2<<21|0<<16|11<<11|uint32(2*c)<<7|off)
	}
	for c := 0; c < 4; c++ {
		base := 0x200 + c*0x20
		for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
			got := uint16(r.DMEM[base+2*j])<<8 | uint16(r.DMEM[base+2*j+1])
			row := (j + c) & 7
			var want uint16
			if row < 4 {
				want = uint16(row*4 + c + 1) // A[row][c]
			}
			if got != want {
				t.Errorf("transpose block %d short %d: %04x want %04x", c, j, got, want)
			}
		}
	}
	// LTV with the same lane rotation loads the diagonal
	// back: from block 0 (lane 0) register v(j) lane 0
	// receives short j rotated by the lane.
	r2 := New()
	for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(r2.DMEM[0x200+2*j:], uint16(j+1))
	}
	r2.Reg[2] = 0
	step1(r2, 0x32<<26|2<<21|0<<16|11<<11|0<<7|0x20) // ltv v0[0], 0x200($2)
	for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
		if got := r2.V[j][0]; got != uint16(j+1) {
			t.Errorf("ltv lane 0 reg %d: %04x", j, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestPackedLoadsStores(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		r.DMEM[0x300+i] = byte(i + 1)
	}
	// LPV/LUV reach 0x300 through the base register (the
	// 7-bit signed offset field cannot express it at
	// their shift). LHV/LFV shift by 4, field 0x30.
	r.Reg[2] = 0x300
	// LPV: byte i becomes lane i << 8.
	step1(r, 0x32<<26|2<<21|1<<16|6<<11|0<<7|0)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if r.V[1][i] != uint16(i+1)<<8 {
			t.Errorf("lpv lane %d: %04x", i, r.V[1][i])
		}
	}
	// LUV: byte i becomes lane i << 7.
	step1(r, 0x32<<26|2<<21|2<<16|7<<11|0<<7|0)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if r.V[2][i] != uint16(i+1)<<7 {
			t.Errorf("luv lane %d: %04x", i, r.V[2][i])
		}
	}
	// LHV: every second byte (offsets 0,2,4,...) << 7.
	r.Reg[2] = 0
	step1(r, 0x32<<26|2<<21|3<<16|8<<11|0<<7|0x30)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if r.V[3][i] != uint16(2*i+1)<<7 {
			t.Errorf("lhv lane %d: %04x", i, r.V[3][i])
		}
	}
	// SHV stores bits 14..7 back to every second byte.
	for i := range r.DMEM {
		r.DMEM[i] = 0
	}
	step1(r, 0x3A<<26|2<<21|3<<16|8<<11|0<<7|0x30)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if r.DMEM[0x300+2*i] != byte(2*i+1) {
			t.Errorf("shv byte %d: %02x", 2*i, r.DMEM[0x300+2*i])
		}
	}
	// LFV: every fourth byte into lanes 0..3 (element 0).
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		r.DMEM[0x300+i] = byte(0x40 + i)
	}
	step1(r, 0x32<<26|2<<21|4<<16|9<<11|0<<7|0x30)
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if r.V[4][i] != uint16(0x40+4*i)<<7 {
			t.Errorf("lfv lane %d: %04x", i, r.V[4][i])
		}
	}
}

// shared library (go build -buildmode=c-shared). It is
// a thin C ABI shell over the system package: the
// frontend (the iTaK engine) registers its callbacks,
// hands us a ROM, and calls retro_run once per frame.

//	gon64_expansion_pak:  On | Off
//

// do not declare their save device in the ROM header

import (
	"os"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/cart"

// libretro constants used here (from the public libretro API).
const (
	envSetPixelFormat  = 10
	pixelFormatXRGB888 = 1
	deviceJoypad       = 1
	deviceAnalog       = 2
	analogLeft         = 0
	analogRight        = 1
	analogX            = 0
	analogY            = 1
	joypadB            = 0
	joypadY            = 1
	joypadStart        = 3
	joypadUp           = 4
	joypadDown         = 5
	joypadLeft         = 6
	joypadRight        = 7
	joypadA            = 8
	joypadX            = 9
	joypadL            = 10
	joypadR            = 11
	joypadL2           = 12
	regionNTSC         = 0
	n64FPS             = 60.0    // NTSC field rate, simplified to 60 for AV info
	n64Aspect          = 1.33333 // 4:3

func variable(key string) string {
	ck := C.CString(key)
	defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(ck))
	v := C.gon64_variable_value(ck)
	if v == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return C.GoString(v)
}

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_gon64_game_info) C.bool {
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	} else if info.path != nil {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(C.GoString(info.path))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		data = b
	} else {
		return false
	}
	expansion := variable("gon64_expansion_pak") != "Off"
	s, err := system.NewWithOptions(data, expansion)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	switch variable("gon64_save_type") {
	case "EEPROM 4K":
		s.SetSaveType(cart.SaveEEPROM4K)
	case "EEPROM 16K":
		s.SetSaveType(cart.SaveEEPROM16K)
	case "SRAM":
		s.SetSaveType(cart.SaveSRAM)
	case "Flash":
		s.SetSaveType(cart.SaveFlash)
	}
	sys = s
	rsReset()
	sys.Start()
	fmt888 := C.uint32_t(pixelFormatXRGB888)
	C.gon64_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&fmt888))
	return true
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() { sys = nil }

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys != nil {
		sys.Start() // a reset reboots through the HLE boot
	}
}

func pressed(port int, id uint) bool {
	return C.gon64_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceJoypad, 0, C.unsigned(id)) != 0
}

func axis(port int, index, id uint) int16 {
	return int16(C.gon64_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceAnalog, C.unsigned(index), C.unsigned(id)))
}

// stickAxis scales a libretro analog axis (-32768..32767)
// to the N64 stick range (-80..80).
func stickAxis(v int16) int8 {
	n := int(v) * 80 / 32768
	if n > 80 {
		n = 80
	}
	if n < -80 {
		n = -80
	}
	return int8(n)
}

// pollPad translates one port's libretro state into the
// N64 controller state. The mapping (documented in the
// README): A and B are the face buttons, Z is on L2,
// the C buttons sit on the right analog stick past a
// threshold plus X for C-up and Y for C-left.
func pollPad(port int) {
	var m uint16
	if pressed(port, joypadA) {
		m |= system.ButtonA
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadB) {
		m |= system.ButtonB
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadStart) {
		m |= system.ButtonStart
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadUp) {
		m |= system.ButtonDUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadDown) {
		m |= system.ButtonDDown
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadLeft) {
		m |= system.ButtonDLeft
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadRight) {
		m |= system.ButtonDRight
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadL) {
		m |= system.ButtonL
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadR) {
		m |= system.ButtonR
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadL2) {
		m |= system.ButtonZ
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadX) {
		m |= system.ButtonCUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadY) {
		m |= system.ButtonCLeft
	}
	rx := axis(port, analogRight, analogX)
	ry := axis(port, analogRight, analogY)
	if rx < -cThreshold {
		m |= system.ButtonCLeft
	}
	if rx > cThreshold {
		m |= system.ButtonCRight
	}
	if ry < -cThreshold {
		m |= system.ButtonCUp
	}
	if ry > cThreshold {
		m |= system.ButtonCDown
	}
	sys.SetButtonsPort(port, m)
	sys.SetStick(port,
		stickAxis(axis(port, analogLeft, analogX)),
		stickAxis(axis(port, analogLeft, analogY)))
}

// The audio resampler: the shell declares 44,100 Hz and
// converts the AI's stream (at its programmed DAC rate)
// with linear interpolation, carrying the fractional
// phase and the last source frame across calls.
var (
	rsPrev  [2]int16
	rsPhase float64
)

func rsReset() {
	rsPrev = [2]int16{}
	rsPhase = 0
}

func resample(src []int16, rate int) []int16 {
	if len(src) < 2 || rate <= 0 || rate == n64SampleRate {
		return src
	}
	srcFrames := len(src) / 2
	ext := make([]int16, 0, len(src)+2)
	ext = append(ext, rsPrev[0], rsPrev[1])
	ext = append(ext, src...)
	total := srcFrames + 1 // ext frames: prev + src
	step := float64(rate) / n64SampleRate
	out := make([]int16, 0, srcFrames*2)
	pos := rsPhase
	for pos < float64(total-1) {
		i := int(pos)
		frac := pos - float64(i)
		for ch := 0; ch < 2; ch++ {
			a := float64(ext[2*i+ch])
			b := float64(ext[2*i+2+ch])
			out = append(out, int16(a+(b-a)*frac))
		}
		pos += step
	}
	rsPhase = pos - float64(total-1)
	rsPrev = [2]int16{src[len(src)-2], src[len(src)-1]}
	return out
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	C.gon64_input_poll()
	for port := 0; port < 4; port++ {
		pollPad(port)
	}
	sys.RunFrame()

	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	w, h := sys.FramebufferSize()
	if len(fb) > 0 {
		C.gon64_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]),
			C.unsigned(w), C.unsigned(h), C.size_t(w*4))
	}
	ab := resample(sys.AudioBuffer(), sys.AudioRate())
	if len(ab) >= 2 {
		frames := len(ab) / 2
		done := int(C.gon64_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&ab[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
		for i := done; i < frames; i++ {
			C.gon64_audio_sample(C.int16_t(ab[2*i]), C.int16_t(ab[2*i+1]))
		}
	}
}

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.SerializeSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), len(state))
	copy(buf, state)
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.SerializeSize()
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	cp := make([]byte, size)
	copy(cp, buf)
	return sys.Deserialize(cp) == nil
}

// The memory interface exposes the active save device
// as SAVE_RAM and RDRAM as SYSTEM_RAM.

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.unsigned) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var ram []uint8
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		ram = sys.SaveRAM()
	case memSystemRAM:
		ram = sys.Mem.RDRAM
	}
	if len(ram) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Pointer(&ram[0])
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.unsigned) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SaveRAM()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.Mem.RDRAM))
	}
	return 0
}
