func retro_cheat_set(index C.unsigned, enabled C.bool, code *C.char) {}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/pif/pif.go ====================

// Package pif implements the N64 PIF (peripheral
// interface) as seen through the serial interface: the
// 64-byte PIF RAM holding Joybus frames for the four
// controller channels and the cartridge channel, the
// frame parsing and execution model, the Joybus command
// set for controllers, controller paks, and the
// cartridge EEPROM, and the two Joybus checksums. It is
// original code written from the published N64
// documentation (n64brew PIF-NUS and Joybus Protocol
// pages).
//
// The documented processing model has two phases. When
// the command byte (PIF RAM offset 0x3F) is written with
// bit 0x01 set, the PIF parses the frame in PIF RAM and
// records each channel's handshake. When the CPU then
// reads PIF RAM through an SI DMA, the PIF executes the
// handshakes (channels in reverse order, 4 down to 0)
// and the replies land in PIF RAM before the DMA copies
// it out. A frame can be executed repeatedly after one
// parse.
//
// Simplifications, stated plainly: the PIF boot security
// exchange with the CIC (including the 6105
// challenge/response) is modeled as passed. The command
// bits 0x20/0x40 (acquire and run the IPL2 checksum) are
// accepted and reported complete without reproducing
// the PIF ROM's checksum comparison, and bit 0x02 (the
// 6105 challenge) leaves the challenge bytes untouched.
// No PIF ROM code is embedded anywhere in this core.
package pif

// RAMSize is the size of PIF RAM in bytes.
const RAMSize = 0x40

// Command byte bits (PIF RAM offset 0x3F).
const (
	cmdJoybusFrame = 0x01 // parse the Joybus frame in RAM
	cmdChallenge   = 0x02 // 6105 challenge/response (modeled: no-op)
	cmdTerminate   = 0x08 // game signals boot termination
	cmdLockROM     = 0x10 // lock the PIF ROM (modeled: no-op)
	cmdAcquireSum  = 0x20 // CPU hands over its IPL2 checksum
	cmdRunSum      = 0x40 // PIF verifies the IPL2 checksum
	cmdDone        = 0x80 // PIF sets: boot data ready / sum acquired
)

// Escape codes in place of a handshake TX byte.
const (
	escSkipChannel = 0x00
	escReset       = 0xFD
	escEndOfFrame  = 0xFE
	escNop         = 0xFF
)

// RX byte error flags, set by the PIF after execution.
const (
	rxNoDevice = 0x80
	rxTimeout  = 0x40
)

// Joybus command bytes.
const (
	joyInfo        = 0x00
	joyInfoAlt     = 0xFF
	joyReadState   = 0x01
	joyPakRead     = 0x02
	joyPakWrite    = 0x03
	joyEEPromRead  = 0x04
	joyEEPromWrite = 0x05
	joyRTCInfo     = 0x06
	joyRTCRead     = 0x07
	joyRTCWrite    = 0x08
)

// PakKind identifies the accessory in a controller.
type PakKind int

const (
	PakNone PakKind = iota
	PakMemory
	PakRumble
)

// PakSize is the controller pak storage size.
const PakSize = 32 << 10

// CartChannel is the cartridge-side Joybus device on
// channel 4: the save EEPROM. The cart package's
// SaveStore satisfies it; RTC commands are answered by
// the PIF itself (no RTC is fitted in this core).
type CartChannel interface {
	EEPROMInfoID() (uint16, bool)
	EEPROMRead(block byte) ([8]byte, bool)
	EEPROMWrite(block byte, data [8]byte) bool
}

// channelState is the runtime state of one controller
// port.
type channelState struct {
	attached bool
	buttons  uint16
	stickX   int8
	stickY   int8

	pak     PakKind
	pakData [PakSize]byte
	// pakFresh is true while an inserted pak has not
	// yet been reported by an Info command (status 3).
	// While fresh, the pak behaves as absent, per the
	// documented Joybus rules.
	pakFresh bool
	rumbleOn bool
	// checksumError is set when the last pak access
	// carried a bad address checksum; the next Info
	// reply reports it in status bit 2.
	checksumError bool
}

// handshake is one parsed Joybus exchange in PIF RAM.
type handshake struct {
	off    int  // offset of the TX byte
	txLen  int  // bytes to transmit (bits 0..5 of TX)
	rxLen  int  // bytes to receive (bits 0..5 of RX)
	skip   bool // TX bit 7: skip this channel at execution
	device bool // whether a handshake was parsed at all
}

// PIF is the peripheral interface device.
type PIF struct {
	RAM [RAMSize]byte

	channels [4]channelState
	cart     CartChannel

	frame    [5]handshake // parsed frame, per channel
	parsed   bool
	bootDone bool
}

// New builds a PIF with a controller attached to every
// port, no paks inserted, and no cartridge device.
func New() *PIF {
	p := &PIF{}
	for i := range p.channels {
		p.channels[i].attached = true
	}
	return p
}

// SetAttached models plugging or unplugging a
// controller. An unplugged port answers every command
// with the no-device error.
func (p *PIF) SetAttached(port int, attached bool) {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return
	}
	p.channels[port].attached = attached
}

// AttachCart connects the cartridge channel device
// (channel 4). Passing nil detaches it.
func (p *PIF) AttachCart(c CartChannel) { p.cart = c }

// SetController records a controller port's live input
// state (button bit layout per the system package's
// Button constants, stick in the -80..80 range).
func (p *PIF) SetController(port int, buttons uint16, stickX, stickY int8) {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return
	}
	c := &p.channels[port]
	c.buttons = buttons
	c.stickX = stickX
	c.stickY = stickY
}

// InsertPak puts an accessory into a controller port.
// A memory pak's storage starts zeroed (games format
// it themselves). A freshly inserted pak reports
// status 3 on the next Info command and behaves as
// absent until then, per the documented rules.
func (p *PIF) InsertPak(port int, kind PakKind) {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return
	}
	c := &p.channels[port]
	c.pak = kind
	c.pakFresh = kind != PakNone
	c.rumbleOn = false
	if kind == PakMemory {
		c.pakData = [PakSize]byte{}
	}
}

// PakKind returns the accessory fitted in a port.
func (p *PIF) PakKind(port int) PakKind {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return PakNone
	}
	return p.channels[port].pak
}

// PakData returns a port's memory pak storage (the
// live array; the system uses it for save states).
func (p *PIF) PakData(port int) []byte {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return nil
	}
	return p.channels[port].pakData[:]
}

// RumbleOn reports a rumble pak's motor state.
func (p *PIF) RumbleOn(port int) bool {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return false
	}
	return p.channels[port].rumbleOn
}

// BootTerminated reports whether the game has sent the
// documented boot termination command (bit 0x08).
func (p *PIF) BootTerminated() bool { return p.bootDone }

// AfterWrite must be called after any host write into
// PIF RAM (SI DMA write or direct CPU write). When the
// command byte carries the joybus frame bit, the frame
// is parsed; the other documented command bits are
// serviced and cleared.
func (p *PIF) AfterWrite() {
	cmd := p.RAM[0x3F]
	if cmd&cmdJoybusFrame != 0 {
		p.parseFrame()
		p.RAM[0x3F] &^= cmdJoybusFrame
	}
	if cmd&cmdAcquireSum != 0 {
		// The CPU's 6-byte IPL2 checksum sits at offset
		// 0x32; the PIF takes it in and clears the area.
		for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
			p.RAM[0x32+i] = 0
		}
		p.RAM[0x3F] &^= cmdAcquireSum
		p.RAM[0x3F] |= cmdDone
	}
	if cmd&cmdRunSum != 0 {
		// Modeled as passed (see the package comment).
		p.RAM[0x3F] &^= cmdRunSum
	}
	if cmd&cmdLockROM != 0 {
		p.RAM[0x3F] &^= cmdLockROM
	}
	if cmd&cmdChallenge != 0 {
		// Modeled: the challenge bytes are left as they
		// are and the bit is cleared.
		p.RAM[0x3F] &^= cmdChallenge
	}
	if cmd&cmdTerminate != 0 {
		p.bootDone = true
		p.RAM[0x3F] &^= cmdTerminate
	}
}

// parseFrame decodes the Joybus frame in PIF RAM into
// per-channel handshakes, following the documented
// escape codes. A handshake that would run past the
// end of RAM aborts the parse (remaining channels keep
// no handshake).
func (p *PIF) parseFrame() {
	for i := range p.frame {
		p.frame[i] = handshake{}
	}
	pos := 0
	for ch := 0; ch < 5; ch++ {
		if pos >= 0x3F {
			break
		}
		b := p.RAM[pos]
		switch b {
		case escEndOfFrame:
			p.parsed = true
			return
		case escSkipChannel, escReset:
			pos++
			continue
		case escNop:
			pos++
			ch-- // a nop does not consume a channel
			continue
		}
		txLen := int(b & 0x3F)
		if txLen == 0 || pos+1 >= RAMSize {
			p.parsed = true
			return
		}
		rxLen := int(p.RAM[pos+1] & 0x3F)
		if pos+2+txLen+rxLen > RAMSize {
			p.parsed = true
			return // incomplete handshake: parsing aborts
		}
		p.frame[ch] = handshake{
			off:    pos,
			txLen:  txLen,
			rxLen:  rxLen,
			skip:   b&0x80 != 0,
			device: true,
		}
		pos += 2 + txLen + rxLen
	}
	p.parsed = true
}

// Execute runs the parsed frame's handshakes against
// the channel devices, in reverse channel order as the
// real PIF does, writing replies into PIF RAM and the
// documented error flags into each RX byte. The SI
// calls it when the CPU DMAs PIF RAM out.
func (p *PIF) Execute() {
	if !p.parsed {
		return
	}
	for ch := 4; ch >= 0; ch-- {
		h := p.frame[ch]
		if !h.device || h.skip {
			continue
		}
		rxOff := h.off + 1
		// The PIF clears the RX flag bits before the
		// exchange, then sets error flags as needed.
		p.RAM[rxOff] &^= rxNoDevice | rxTimeout
		tx := p.RAM[h.off+2 : h.off+2+h.txLen]
		rx := p.RAM[h.off+2+h.txLen : h.off+2+h.txLen+h.rxLen]
		reply, outcome := p.dispatch(ch, tx)
		switch outcome {
		case outcomeNoDevice:
			p.RAM[rxOff] |= rxNoDevice
		case outcomeSilent:
			p.RAM[rxOff] |= rxTimeout
		default:
			if len(reply) < h.rxLen {
				p.RAM[rxOff] |= rxTimeout
			}
			copy(rx, reply)
		}
	}
}

// dispatch outcomes for one Joybus exchange.
const (
	outcomeAnswered = iota // the device replied
	outcomeSilent          // a device is there but did not reply (timeout)
	outcomeNoDevice        // nothing is attached to the channel
)

// dispatch routes one Joybus command to a channel's
// device.
func (p *PIF) dispatch(ch int, tx []byte) ([]byte, int) {
	if len(tx) == 0 {
		return nil, outcomeSilent
	}
	if ch == 4 {
		return p.dispatchCart(tx)
	}
	return p.dispatchController(ch, tx)
}

// controllerInfo builds the 3-byte Info reply for a
// controller channel: device 0x0500 plus the accessory
// status byte (1 inserted, 2 absent, 3 newly inserted,
// with bit 2 reporting a previous checksum error).
func (p *PIF) controllerInfo(ch int) []byte {
	c := &p.channels[ch]
	status := byte(0x02)
	if c.pak != PakNone {
		if c.pakFresh {
			status = 0x03
			c.pakFresh = false
		} else {
			status = 0x01
		}
	}
	if c.checksumError {
		status |= 0x04
		c.checksumError = false
	}
	return []byte{0x05, 0x00, status}
}

func (p *PIF) dispatchController(ch int, tx []byte) ([]byte, int) {
	c := &p.channels[ch]
	if !c.attached {
		return nil, outcomeNoDevice
	}
	switch tx[0] {
	case joyInfo, joyInfoAlt:
		return p.controllerInfo(ch), outcomeAnswered
	case joyReadState:
		return []byte{
			byte(c.buttons >> 8), byte(c.buttons),
			byte(c.stickX), byte(c.stickY),
		}, outcomeAnswered
	case joyPakRead, joyPakWrite:
		return p.pakAccess(c, tx)
	}
	return nil, outcomeSilent // unknown command: the device stays silent
}

// pakAccess serves controller pak read and write
// commands. The address is the 16-bit value in tx[1..2]
// whose low 5 bits carry the address checksum; the
// data area is 32 bytes. An absent or still-fresh pak
// behaves as documented: reads return zero-filled data
// with a complemented CRC, writes answer only the
// complemented CRC.
func (p *PIF) pakAccess(c *channelState, tx []byte) ([]byte, int) {
	isWrite := tx[0] == joyPakWrite
	if len(tx) < 3 || (isWrite && len(tx) < 35) {
		return nil, outcomeSilent
	}
	addr := uint16(tx[1])<<8 | uint16(tx[2])
	if uint16(AddressChecksum(addr)) != addr&0x1F {
		c.checksumError = true
		return nil, outcomeSilent // bad address checksum: no reply
	}
	base := int(addr & 0xFFE0)
	absent := c.pak == PakNone || c.pakFresh
	if isWrite {
		data := tx[3:35]
		crc := DataCRC(data)
		if absent {
			return []byte{^crc}, outcomeAnswered
		}
		if c.pak == PakMemory {
			copy(c.pakData[base&0x7FFF:], data)
		} else if c.pak == PakRumble && base == 0x8000 {
			c.rumbleOn = data[0]&1 != 0
		}
		return []byte{crc}, outcomeAnswered
	}
	// Read.
	if absent {
		out := make([]byte, 33)
		out[32] = 0xFF // CRC of 32 zero bytes is 0; complemented
		return out, outcomeAnswered
	}
	out := make([]byte, 33)
	if c.pak == PakMemory {
		copy(out, c.pakData[base&0x7FFF:])
	}
	out[32] = DataCRC(out[:32])
	return out, outcomeAnswered
}

// dispatchCart serves channel 4: the cartridge EEPROM
// (and the RTC commands, which have no device here).
func (p *PIF) dispatchCart(tx []byte) ([]byte, int) {
	switch tx[0] {
	case joyInfo, joyInfoAlt:
		if p.cart != nil {
			if id, ok := p.cart.EEPROMInfoID(); ok {
				return []byte{byte(id >> 8), byte(id), 0x00}, outcomeAnswered
			}
		}
		return []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00}, outcomeAnswered
	case joyEEPromRead:
		if p.cart == nil || len(tx) < 2 {
			return nil, outcomeSilent
		}
		blk, ok := p.cart.EEPROMRead(tx[1])
		if !ok {
			return nil, outcomeSilent
		}
		return blk[:], outcomeAnswered
	case joyEEPromWrite:
		if p.cart == nil || len(tx) < 10 {
			return nil, outcomeSilent
		}
		var blk [8]byte
		copy(blk[:], tx[2:10])
		if !p.cart.EEPROMWrite(tx[1], blk) {
			return nil, outcomeSilent
		}
		return []byte{0x00}, outcomeAnswered
	case joyRTCInfo:
		// No RTC is fitted: the documented answer is
		// three zero bytes.
		return []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00}, outcomeAnswered
	}
	return nil, outcomeSilent
}

// DataCRC is the Joybus data checksum: CRC-8 with
// polynomial 0x85 and initial value 0x00, computed
// MSB-first, as documented for the pak read/write
// commands.
func DataCRC(data []byte) byte {
	crc := byte(0)
	for _, b := range data {
		crc ^= b
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if crc&0x80 != 0 {
				crc = crc<<1 ^ 0x85
			} else {
				crc <<= 1
			}
		}
	}
	return crc
}

// addressChecksumTable holds the documented per-bit
// XOR values for address bits 15 down to 5.
var addressChecksumTable = [11]byte{
	0x01, 0x1A, 0x0D, 0x1C, 0x0E, 0x07, 0x19, 0x16, 0x0B, 0x1F, 0x15,
}

// AddressChecksum computes the 5-bit Joybus address
// checksum over the top 11 bits of addr (not a CRC: a
// positional XOR, per the documentation).
func AddressChecksum(addr uint16) byte {
	var sum byte
	for i := 0; i < 11; i++ {
		bit := 15 - i
		if addr&(1<<uint(bit)) != 0 {
			sum ^= addressChecksumTable[i]
		}
	}
	return sum & 0x1F
}

// StateSize is the fixed byte size of the PIF runtime
// block in a system save state: the four paks' storage,
// per-channel accessory runtime flags, the global flags
// byte, and the parsed frame (so a state saved between
// a frame's parse and its execution restores exactly).
//
// Layout: 4 x 32768 bytes of pak data, then per channel
// one flags byte (bits 0..1 pak kind, bit 2 fresh, bit
// 3 rumble on, bit 4 checksum error, bit 5 detached),
// then the parsed and boot-done flags byte, then per
// channel four frame bytes (PIF RAM offset, TX length,
// RX length, flags: bit 0 parsed, bit 1 skip).
const StateSize = 4*PakSize + 4 + 1 + 5*4

// Serialize writes the PIF runtime state (PIF RAM
// itself is serialized by the bus owner; here: pak
// storage and accessory flags) into out.
func (p *PIF) Serialize(out []byte) {
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		copy(out[ch*PakSize:], p.channels[ch].pakData[:])
		var flags byte
		flags |= byte(p.channels[ch].pak) & 0x03
		if p.channels[ch].pakFresh {
			flags |= 0x04
		}
		if p.channels[ch].rumbleOn {
			flags |= 0x08
		}
		if p.channels[ch].checksumError {
			flags |= 0x10
		}
		if !p.channels[ch].attached {
			flags |= 0x20
		}
		out[4*PakSize+ch] = flags
	}
	var f byte
	if p.parsed {
		f |= 0x01
	}
	if p.bootDone {
		f |= 0x02
	}
	out[4*PakSize+4] = f
	for ch := 0; ch < 5; ch++ {
		h := p.frame[ch]
		base := 4*PakSize + 5 + ch*4
		out[base] = byte(h.off)
		out[base+1] = byte(h.txLen)
		out[base+2] = byte(h.rxLen)
		var hf byte
		if h.device {
			hf |= 0x01
		}
		if h.skip {
			hf |= 0x02
		}
		out[base+3] = hf
	}
}

// Deserialize restores the PIF runtime state,
// including the parsed frame.
func (p *PIF) Deserialize(in []byte) {
	for ch := 0; ch < 4; ch++ {
		copy(p.channels[ch].pakData[:], in[ch*PakSize:])
		flags := in[4*PakSize+ch]
		p.channels[ch].pak = PakKind(flags & 0x03)
		p.channels[ch].pakFresh = flags&0x04 != 0
		p.channels[ch].rumbleOn = flags&0x08 != 0
		p.channels[ch].checksumError = flags&0x10 != 0
		p.channels[ch].attached = flags&0x20 == 0
	}
	f := in[4*PakSize+4]
	p.parsed = f&0x01 != 0
	p.bootDone = f&0x02 != 0
	for ch := 0; ch < 5; ch++ {
		base := 4*PakSize + 5 + ch*4
		hf := in[base+3]
		p.frame[ch] = handshake{
			off:    int(in[base]),
			txLen:  int(in[base+1]),
			rxLen:  int(in[base+2]),
			device: hf&0x01 != 0,
			skip:   hf&0x02 != 0,
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/pif/pif_test.go ====================

package pif

import "testing"

// Checksums pinned against hand-computed values.

// CRC-8 (poly 0x85, init 0) computed by hand:
//   - 32 zero bytes: 0x00
//   - the single byte 0x01: 0x85 (after 8 shifts the
//     lone bit reaches the top and folds once)
//   - the single byte 0xFF: 0x8D
//   - "123456789" ASCII: 0xFE? (verified against the
//     CRC-8/SMBUS variant table: poly 0x85 reflected
//     differs; the MSB-first value for this string
//     under poly 0x85 init 0 is computed in the test
//     comment from the bit algorithm: it is 0x3D.)
func TestDataCRCPinned(t *testing.T) {
	if got := DataCRC(make([]byte, 32)); got != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("CRC(zeros) = %#02x, want 0x00", got)
	}
	if got := DataCRC([]byte{0x01}); got != 0x85 {
		t.Errorf("CRC(0x01) = %#02x, want 0x85", got)
	}
	if got := DataCRC([]byte{0xFF}); got != 0x8D {
		t.Errorf("CRC(0xFF) = %#02x, want 0x8D", got)
	}
}

// Address checksum: the documented example is address
// 0x0020 encoding checksum 10101b = 0x15 (only bit 5
// set, whose table value is 0x15). Address 0 has
// checksum 0. Address 0x8000 (only bit 15) is 0x01.
func TestAddressChecksumPinned(t *testing.T) {
	if got := AddressChecksum(0x0020); got != 0x15 {
		t.Errorf("checksum(0x0020) = %#02x, want 0x15", got)
	}
	if got := AddressChecksum(0x0000); got != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("checksum(0) = %#02x, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := AddressChecksum(0x8000); got != 0x01 {
		t.Errorf("checksum(0x8000) = %#02x, want 0x01", got)
	}
	// Bits 6 and 5: 0x1F ^ 0x15 = 0x0A.
	if got := AddressChecksum(0x0060); got != 0x0A {
		t.Errorf("checksum(0x0060) = %#02x, want 0x0A", got)
	}
}

// fakeCart is a channel-4 EEPROM backed by a map.
type fakeCart struct {
	id    uint16
	there bool
	store [2048]byte
}

func (f *fakeCart) EEPROMInfoID() (uint16, bool) { return f.id, f.there }
func (f *fakeCart) EEPROMRead(block byte) ([8]byte, bool) {
	var out [8]byte
	if !f.there {
		return out, false
	}
	copy(out[:], f.store[int(block)*8:])
	return out, true
}
func (f *fakeCart) EEPROMWrite(block byte, data [8]byte) bool {
	if !f.there {
		return false
	}
	copy(f.store[int(block)*8:], data[:])
	return true
}

// loadFrame writes a frame into PIF RAM, sets the
// command bit, and parses (as an SI DMA write would).
func loadFrame(p *PIF, frame []byte) {
	copy(p.RAM[:], frame)
	p.RAM[0x3F] = 0x01
	p.AfterWrite()
}

func TestControllerInfoAndState(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	p.SetController(0, 0x8010, -5, 42) // A + Start, stick
	// Frame: ch0 state read (tx1 rx4 cmd 0x01), ch1-3
	// skipped, ch4 info (tx1 rx3 cmd 0x00), FE.
	frame := []byte{
		0x01, 0x04, 0x01, 0, 0, 0, 0,
		0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
		0x01, 0x03, 0x00, 0, 0, 0,
		0xFE,
	}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[3] != 0x80 || p.RAM[4] != 0x10 {
		t.Errorf("buttons = %02x %02x, want 80 10", p.RAM[3], p.RAM[4])
	}
	if int8(p.RAM[5]) != -5 || int8(p.RAM[6]) != 42 {
		t.Errorf("stick = %d,%d", int8(p.RAM[5]), int8(p.RAM[6]))
	}
	// Ch4 info with no cart device: zero signature.
	if p.RAM[13] != 0 || p.RAM[14] != 0 || p.RAM[15] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ch4 info = %02x %02x %02x", p.RAM[13], p.RAM[14], p.RAM[15])
	}
	// No error flags anywhere.
	if p.RAM[1]&0xC0 != 0 || p.RAM[11]&0xC0 != 0 {
		t.Errorf("rx flags set: %02x %02x", p.RAM[1], p.RAM[11])
	}
}

func TestControllerInfoPakLifecycle(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	info := func() byte {
		frame := []byte{0x01, 0x03, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0, 0xFE}
		loadFrame(p, frame)
		p.Execute()
		return p.RAM[5]
	}
	if s := info(); s != 0x02 {
		t.Fatalf("no pak status = %#02x, want 0x02", s)
	}
	p.InsertPak(0, PakMemory)
	if s := info(); s != 0x03 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh pak status = %#02x, want 0x03", s)
	}
	if s := info(); s != 0x01 {
		t.Fatalf("settled pak status = %#02x, want 0x01", s)
	}
}

func TestPakRoundTripAndAbsentBehavior(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	addr := uint16(0x0020)
	addr |= uint16(AddressChecksum(addr))
	pakWrite := func(data []byte) byte {
		frame := []byte{0x23, 0x01, 0x03, byte(addr >> 8), byte(addr)}
		frame = append(frame, data...)
		frame = append(frame, 0, 0xFE) // rx space + end
		loadFrame(p, frame)
		p.Execute()
		return p.RAM[37]
	}
	pakRead := func() []byte {
		frame := []byte{0x03, 0x21, 0x02, byte(addr >> 8), byte(addr)}
		frame = append(frame, make([]byte, 33)...)
		frame = append(frame, 0xFE)
		loadFrame(p, frame)
		p.Execute()
		return p.RAM[5:38]
	}
	data := make([]byte, 32)
	for i := range data {
		data[i] = byte(i*3 + 1)
	}
	// Absent pak: write answers the complemented CRC,
	// read returns zeros with CRC 0xFF.
	if crc := pakWrite(data); crc != ^DataCRC(data) {
		t.Errorf("absent write crc = %#02x, want %#02x", crc, ^DataCRC(data))
	}
	got := pakRead()
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if got[i] != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("absent read byte %d = %#02x", i, got[i])
		}
	}
	if got[32] != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("absent read crc = %#02x, want 0xFF", got[32])
	}
	// Insert a pak: while fresh it still behaves
	// absent; an Info settles it.
	p.InsertPak(0, PakMemory)
	if crc := pakWrite(data); crc != ^DataCRC(data) {
		t.Errorf("fresh write crc = %#02x, want complemented", crc)
	}
	frame := []byte{0x01, 0x03, 0x00, 0, 0, 0, 0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if crc := pakWrite(data); crc != DataCRC(data) {
		t.Errorf("write crc = %#02x, want %#02x", crc, DataCRC(data))
	}
	got = pakRead()
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if got[i] != data[i] {
			t.Fatalf("read byte %d = %#02x, want %#02x", i, got[i], data[i])
		}
	}
	if got[32] != DataCRC(data) {
		t.Errorf("read crc = %#02x, want %#02x", got[32], DataCRC(data))
	}
}

func TestPakBadAddressChecksum(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	p.InsertPak(0, PakMemory)
	frame := []byte{0x01, 0x03, 0x00, 0, 0, 0, 0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute() // settle the pak
	// Address 0x0020 with a deliberately wrong checksum
	// (0x00 instead of 0x15): no reply (timeout flag),
	// and the next Info reports the checksum error bit.
	bad := []byte{0x03, 0x21, 0x02, 0x00, 0x20}
	bad = append(bad, make([]byte, 33)...)
	bad = append(bad, 0xFE)
	loadFrame(p, bad)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[1]&rxTimeout == 0 {
		t.Errorf("bad checksum did not time out: rx byte %#02x", p.RAM[1])
	}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[5] != 0x01|0x04 {
		t.Errorf("info after bad checksum = %#02x, want 0x05", p.RAM[5])
	}
}

func TestEEPROMChannel(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	fc := &fakeCart{id: 0x0080, there: true}
	p.AttachCart(fc)
	// ch4 write block 7 (skip ch0..3 first).
	frame := []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
		0x0A, 0x01, 0x05, 0x07, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 0xEE,
		0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[16] != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("eeprom write reply = %#02x", p.RAM[16])
	}
	// Read it back.
	frame = []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
		0x02, 0x08, 0x04, 0x07, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,
		0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if p.RAM[8+i] != byte(i+1) {
			t.Fatalf("eeprom byte %d = %#02x", i, p.RAM[8+i])
		}
	}
	// Info on ch4 returns the EEPROM signature.
	frame = []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x03, 0xFF, 0, 0, 0, 0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[7] != 0x00 || p.RAM[8] != 0x80 || p.RAM[9] != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("eeprom info = %02x %02x %02x", p.RAM[7], p.RAM[8], p.RAM[9])
	}
	// RTC info with no RTC: three zero bytes, no error.
	frame = []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x03, 0x06, 0, 0, 0, 0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[5]&0xC0 != 0 {
		t.Errorf("rtc info flagged an error: %#02x", p.RAM[5])
	}
	if p.RAM[7] != 0 || p.RAM[8] != 0 || p.RAM[9] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("rtc info bytes nonzero")
	}
}

func TestNoDeviceChannelAndSkipBit(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	// All five channels ask an EEPROM read; only ch4
	// exists in this PIF's world when a cart is
	// attached without EEPROM... instead: use an
	// unknown command 0x42 on ch0 (device stays
	// silent) and check the timeout flag, then a
	// skipped handshake (TX bit 7) leaves RAM alone.
	frame := []byte{0x01, 0x02, 0x42, 0xAA, 0xBB, 0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[1]&rxTimeout == 0 {
		t.Errorf("unknown command: rx = %#02x, want timeout", p.RAM[1])
	}
	if p.RAM[3] != 0xAA || p.RAM[4] != 0xBB {
		t.Error("timeout wrote into the receive space")
	}
	frame = []byte{0x81, 0x04, 0x01, 0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC, 0xCC, 0xFE}
	loadFrame(p, frame)
	p.Execute()
	if p.RAM[3] != 0xCC {
		t.Error("skipped handshake executed")
	}
}

func TestCommandBits(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	p.RAM[0x3F] = 0x20 // acquire checksum
	copy(p.RAM[0x32:], []byte{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6})
	p.AfterWrite()
	if p.RAM[0x32] != 0 {
		t.Error("checksum area not cleared by acquire")
	}
	if p.RAM[0x3F]&0x80 == 0 {
		t.Error("done bit not set after acquire")
	}
	p.RAM[0x3F] = 0x08 // terminate boot
	p.AfterWrite()
	if !p.BootTerminated() {
		t.Error("terminate bit did not register")
	}
	if p.RAM[0x3F]&0x08 != 0 {
		t.Error("terminate bit not cleared")
	}
}

func TestPIFStateRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	p.InsertPak(1, PakMemory)
	copy(p.PakData(1)[100:], []byte{9, 8, 7})
	buf := make([]byte, StateSize)
	p.Serialize(buf)
	p2 := New()
	p2.Deserialize(buf)
	if p2.PakKind(1) != PakMemory {
		t.Fatalf("pak kind = %v", p2.PakKind(1))
	}
	if !p2.channels[1].pakFresh {
		t.Error("fresh flag lost")
	}
	if p2.PakData(1)[100] != 9 || p2.PakData(1)[102] != 7 {
		t.Error("pak data lost")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/rdp/cmds.go ====================

package rdp

// State command handlers. Field layouts follow the
// published RDP command summary; each handler decodes
// its 64-bit word into the registers it owns.

// dispatchState decodes the single-word state and setup
// commands. w is the full command word.
func (r *RDP) dispatchState(op int, w uint64) {
	switch op {
	case CmdSetColorImg:
		r.colorImg = decodeImage(w)
	case CmdSetTexImage:
		r.texImg = decodeImage(w)
	case CmdSetZImage:
		r.zAddr = uint32(w & 0x3FFFFFF)
	case CmdSetTile:
		idx := int((w >> 24) & 7)
		t := &r.tiles[idx]
		t.Format = int((w >> 53) & 7)
		t.Size = int((w >> 51) & 3)
		t.Line = int((w >> 41) & 0x1FF)
		t.TMem = int((w >> 32) & 0x1FF)
		t.Palette = int((w >> 20) & 0xF)
		t.ClampT = (w>>19)&1 != 0
		t.MirrorT = (w>>18)&1 != 0
		t.MaskT = int((w >> 14) & 0xF)
		t.ShiftT = int((w >> 10) & 0xF)
		t.ClampS = (w>>9)&1 != 0
		t.MirrorS = (w>>8)&1 != 0
		t.MaskS = int((w >> 4) & 0xF)
		t.ShiftS = int(w & 0xF)
	case CmdSetTileSize, CmdLoadTile, CmdLoadTLUT:
		sl := int((w >> 44) & 0xFFF)
		tl := int((w >> 32) & 0xFFF)
		idx := int((w >> 24) & 7)
		sh := int((w >> 12) & 0xFFF)
		th := int(w & 0xFFF)
		t := &r.tiles[idx]
		t.SL, t.TL, t.SH, t.TH = sl, tl, sh, th
		switch op {
		case CmdLoadTile:
			r.loadTile(idx)
		case CmdLoadTLUT:
			r.loadTLUT(idx)
		}
	case CmdLoadBlock:
		idx := int((w >> 24) & 7)
		sl := int((w >> 44) & 0xFFF)
		tl := int((w >> 32) & 0xFFF)
		sh := int((w >> 12) & 0xFFF)
		dxt := int(w & 0xFFF)
		t := &r.tiles[idx]
		t.SL, t.TL, t.SH = sl, tl, sh
		r.loadBlock(idx, dxt)
	case CmdSetOtherMode:
		r.otherModes = w & 0x00FFFFFFFFFFFFFF
	case CmdSetCombine:
		r.combineReg = w & 0x00FFFFFFFFFFFFFF
	case CmdSetPrimColor:
		r.primMinLvl = int((w >> 40) & 0x1F)
		r.primLvlFrc = int((w >> 32) & 0xFF)
		r.primColor = decodeColor(w)
	case CmdSetEnvColor:
		r.envColor = decodeColor(w)
	case CmdSetBlendCol:
		r.blendColor = decodeColor(w)
	case CmdSetFogColor:
		r.fogColor = decodeColor(w)
	case CmdSetFillColor:
		r.fillColor = uint32(w)
	case CmdSetPrimDepth:
		r.primZ = uint16((w >> 16) & 0xFFFF)
		r.primDZ = uint16(w & 0xFFFF)
	case CmdSetScissor:
		r.sciX0 = int((w >> 44) & 0xFFF)
		r.sciY0 = int((w >> 32) & 0xFFF)
		r.sciField = (w>>25)&1 != 0
		r.sciOdd = (w>>24)&1 != 0
		r.sciX1 = int((w >> 12) & 0xFFF)
		r.sciY1 = int(w & 0xFFF)
	case CmdSetConvert:
		for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
			v := int32((w >> uint(45-9*i)) & 0x1FF)
			if v&0x100 != 0 {
				v -= 0x200
			}
			r.conv[i] = v
		}
		// Power-on typical values if a list never sets
		// them are NOT assumed here; New leaves them
		// zero and games always program them. Tests set
		// the documented typical set explicitly.
	case CmdSetKeyR:
		r.keyR = keyChan{
			Width:  int((w >> 16) & 0xFFF),
			Center: int((w >> 8) & 0xFF),
			Scale:  int(w & 0xFF),
		}
	case CmdSetKeyGB:
		r.keyGB = keyGBRegs{
			WidthG:  int((w >> 44) & 0xFFF),
			WidthB:  int((w >> 32) & 0xFFF),
			CenterG: int((w >> 24) & 0xFF),
			ScaleG:  int((w >> 16) & 0xFF),
			CenterB: int((w >> 8) & 0xFF),
			ScaleB:  int(w & 0xFF),
		}
	case CmdFillRect:
		r.fillRect(w)
	}
}

// decodeImage decodes a Set Color/Texture Image word.
func decodeImage(w uint64) Image {
	return Image{
		Format: int((w >> 53) & 7),
		Size:   int((w >> 51) & 3),
		Width:  int((w>>32)&0x3FF) + 1,
		Addr:   uint32(w & 0x3FFFFFF),
	}
}

// decodeColor pulls the RGBA byte set out of the low 32
// bits of a color-set command word.
func decodeColor(w uint64) RGBA {
	return RGBA{
		R: uint8(w >> 24),
		G: uint8(w >> 16),
		B: uint8(w >> 8),
		A: uint8(w),
	}
}

// Other-mode field accessors (see the bit map in the
// package documentation lineage: the other-modes
// register as the RDP receives it, with the high and
// low halves already merged by the microcode upstream).

func (r *RDP) omCycleType() int  { return int((r.otherModes >> 52) & 3) }
func (r *RDP) omPerspTex() bool  { return (r.otherModes>>51)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omDetailTex() bool { return (r.otherModes>>50)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omSharpenTex() bool {
	return (r.otherModes>>49)&1 != 0
}
func (r *RDP) omTexLOD() bool      { return (r.otherModes>>48)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omEnTLUT() bool      { return (r.otherModes>>47)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omTLUTType() int     { return int((r.otherModes >> 46) & 1) }
func (r *RDP) omSampleType() int   { return int((r.otherModes >> 45) & 1) }
func (r *RDP) omMidTexel() bool    { return (r.otherModes>>44)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omBiLerp0() bool     { return (r.otherModes>>43)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omBiLerp1() bool     { return (r.otherModes>>42)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omConvertOne() bool  { return (r.otherModes>>41)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omKeyEn() bool       { return (r.otherModes>>40)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omRGBDither() int    { return int((r.otherModes >> 38) & 3) }
func (r *RDP) omAlphaDither() int  { return int((r.otherModes >> 36) & 3) }
func (r *RDP) omForceBlend() bool  { return (r.otherModes>>14)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omAlphaCvgSel() bool { return (r.otherModes>>13)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omCvgTimesAlpha() bool {
	return (r.otherModes>>12)&1 != 0
}
func (r *RDP) omZMode() int        { return int((r.otherModes >> 10) & 3) }
func (r *RDP) omCvgDest() int      { return int((r.otherModes >> 8) & 3) }
func (r *RDP) omColorOnCvg() bool  { return (r.otherModes>>7)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omImageRead() bool   { return (r.otherModes>>6)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omZUpdate() bool     { return (r.otherModes>>5)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omZCompare() bool    { return (r.otherModes>>4)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omAntialias() bool   { return (r.otherModes>>3)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omZSourcePrim() bool { return (r.otherModes>>2)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omDitherAlpha() bool { return (r.otherModes>>1)&1 != 0 }
func (r *RDP) omAlphaCompare() bool {
	return r.otherModes&1 != 0
}

// Blender mux fields for one cycle. cycle 0 uses the
// _0 field group, cycle 1 the _1 group.
func (r *RDP) omBlendMux(cycle, which int) int {
	// which: 0 m1a, 1 m1b, 2 m2a, 3 m2b
	base := [2][4]int{
		{30, 26, 22, 18}, // cycle 0: m1a_0 is bits 31..30
		{28, 24, 20, 16}, // cycle 1
	}
	return int((r.otherModes >> uint(base[cycle][which])) & 3)
}

// fillRect executes the Fill Rectangle command. Field
// layout: XL (55..44), YL (43..32) in the high word,
// XH (23..12), YH (11..0) in the low positions, all in
// 10.2 fixed point. The fill color is written directly;
// in fill and copy cycle modes both corners are
// included, in 1-cycle and 2-cycle modes the lower
// right corner follows the exclusive rule of the other
// primitives.
func (r *RDP) fillRect(w uint64) {
	xl := int((w>>44)&0xFFF) >> 2
	yl := int((w>>32)&0xFFF) >> 2
	xh := int((w>>12)&0xFFF) >> 2
	yh := int(w&0xFFF) >> 2
	if ct := r.omCycleType(); ct == 0 || ct == 1 {
		xl--
		yl--
	}
	r.fillSpan(xh, yh, xl, yl)
}

// fillSpan writes the fill color over the rectangle
// from (x0, y0) to (x1, y1) with both corners included.
// The scissor box clips the writes.
func (r *RDP) fillSpan(x0, y0, x1, y1 int) {
	for y := y0; y <= y1; y++ {
		if !r.inScissorY(y) {
			continue
		}
		for x := x0; x <= x1; x++ {
			if x < r.sciX0>>2 || x >= r.sciX1>>2 {
				continue
			}
			r.writeFillPixel(x, y)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/rdp/rast.go ====================

package rdp

// Triangle and texture rectangle rasterization. The
// plane-evaluation model and the stepping rules are
// described at the top of render.go.

// sext14 sign-extends a 14-bit Y coordinate (11.2).
func sext14(v uint32) int32 {
	x := int32(v & 0x3FFF)
	if x&0x2000 != 0 {
		x -= 0x4000
	}
	return x
}

// sext16 sign-extends a 16-bit field.
func sext16(v uint32) int32 {
	x := int32(v & 0xFFFF)
	if x&0x8000 != 0 {
		x -= 0x10000
	}
	return x
}

// pairFrac rebuilds a 32-bit 16.16 value whose integer
// half sits in one word and whose fraction half sits in
// a paired word, at the same 16-bit lane (lane 0 is the
// topmost, bits 63..48).
func pairFrac(intWord, fracWord uint64, lane int) int32 {
	shift := uint(48 - 16*lane)
	i := uint32(intWord>>shift) & 0xFFFF
	f := uint32(fracWord>>shift) & 0xFFFF
	return int32(i<<16 | f)
}

// triCmd is a decoded triangle command.
type triCmd struct {
	lft   bool
	level int
	tile  int

	yh, ym, yl int32 // 11.2 subpixel units
	// Edge coefficients, 16.16.
	xh, dxhdy int32
	xm, dxmdy int32
	xl, dxldy int32

	shaded    bool
	tex, hasZ bool

	// Shade attributes at the top vertex, 16.16 in
	// 0..255 color units (colQ) and derivatives.
	col    [4]int32 // R,G,B,A
	dColDx [4]int32
	dColDe [4]int32
	dColDy [4]int32

	// Texture attributes at the top vertex, 16.16 raw.
	s, t, w int32
	dsDx    int32
	dtDx    int32
	dwDx    int32
	dsDe    int32
	dtDe    int32
	dwDe    int32
	dsDy    int32
	dtDy    int32
	dwDy    int32

	z    int32 // 16.16
	dzDx int32
	dzDe int32
	dzDy int32
}

// cmdTriangle decodes and rasterizes one triangle
// command. words holds the full command (edge group,
// then shade, texture, and z groups as present).
func (r *RDP) cmdTriangle(op int, words []uint64) {
	var tc triCmd
	tc.shaded = op&0x04 != 0
	tc.tex = op&0x02 != 0
	tc.hasZ = op&0x01 != 0

	w0 := words[0]
	tc.lft = (w0>>55)&1 != 0
	tc.level = int((w0 >> 51) & 7)
	tc.tile = int((w0 >> 48) & 7)
	tc.yl = sext14(uint32(w0 >> 32))
	tc.ym = sext14(uint32(w0 >> 16))
	tc.yh = sext14(uint32(w0))

	tc.xh = int32(words[1] >> 32)
	tc.dxhdy = int32(words[1])
	tc.xm = int32(words[2] >> 32)
	tc.dxmdy = int32(words[2])
	tc.xl = int32(words[3] >> 32)
	tc.dxldy = int32(words[3])

	wi := 4
	if tc.shaded {
		// Lanes: 0=R, 1=G, 2=B, 3=A.
		for lane := 0; lane < 4; lane++ {
			tc.col[lane] = pairFrac(words[wi+0], words[wi+2], lane)
			tc.dColDx[lane] = pairFrac(words[wi+1], words[wi+3], lane)
			tc.dColDe[lane] = pairFrac(words[wi+4], words[wi+6], lane)
			tc.dColDy[lane] = pairFrac(words[wi+5], words[wi+7], lane)
		}
		wi += 8
	}
	if tc.tex {
		// Lanes: 0=S, 1=T, 2=W.
		tc.s = pairFrac(words[wi+0], words[wi+2], 0)
		tc.t = pairFrac(words[wi+0], words[wi+2], 1)
		tc.w = pairFrac(words[wi+0], words[wi+2], 2)
		tc.dsDx = pairFrac(words[wi+1], words[wi+3], 0)
		tc.dtDx = pairFrac(words[wi+1], words[wi+3], 1)
		tc.dwDx = pairFrac(words[wi+1], words[wi+3], 2)
		tc.dsDe = pairFrac(words[wi+4], words[wi+6], 0)
		tc.dtDe = pairFrac(words[wi+4], words[wi+6], 1)
		tc.dwDe = pairFrac(words[wi+4], words[wi+6], 2)
		tc.dsDy = pairFrac(words[wi+5], words[wi+7], 0)
		tc.dtDy = pairFrac(words[wi+5], words[wi+7], 1)
		tc.dwDy = pairFrac(words[wi+5], words[wi+7], 2)
		wi += 8
	}
	if tc.hasZ {
		tc.z = int32(words[wi] >> 32)
		tc.dzDx = int32(words[wi])
		tc.dzDe = int32(words[wi+1] >> 32)
		tc.dzDy = int32(words[wi+1])
	}

	r.rasterTri(&tc)
}

// plane evaluates an attribute plane at pixel (x, line)
// anchored at (xhTop, yh): attr(x, y) = a0 + Dx*(x -
// xhTop) + Dy*(ySub - yh)/4, with ySub = line*4, all in
// 16.16 fixed point. xhTop is the major edge position
// at the top vertex's height, in 16.16.
func plane(a0, dx, dy int32, xPix int, xhTop int32, lineSub, yh int32) int32 {
	dxTerm := (int64(dx) * (int64(int32(xPix))<<16 - int64(xhTop))) >> 16
	dyTerm := (int64(dy) * int64(lineSub-yh)) >> 2
	return a0 + int32(dxTerm) + int32(dyTerm)
}

// ceilDiv4 returns ceil(v/4) for the 11.2 domain.
func ceilDiv4(v int32) int32 { return (v + 3) >> 2 }

// rasterTri walks the triangle scanline by scanline.
func (r *RDP) rasterTri(tc *triCmd) {
	firstLine := int(ceilDiv4(tc.yh))
	lastLine := int(ceilDiv4(tc.yl)) // exclusive
	midLine := int(ceilDiv4(tc.ym))
	if lastLine <= firstLine {
		return
	}
	prevLine := int32(firstLine - 1)
	// Major edge position at the top vertex height:
	// the given XH sits at prevLine, so step it to YH.
	xhTop := tc.xh + int32((int64(tc.dxhdy)*int64(tc.yh-prevLine*4))>>2)

	// LOD setup for textured triangles.
	lodLevel, lodFrac := 0, r.primLvlFrc
	persp := r.omPerspTex()
	if tc.tex {
		lodLevel, lodFrac = r.triLOD(tc, xhTop, persp)
		if lodLevel > tc.level {
			lodLevel = tc.level
		}
		if lodLevel < r.primMinLvl {
			lodLevel = r.primMinLvl
			lodFrac = r.primLvlFrc
		}
	}

	for y := firstLine; y < lastLine; y++ {
		// Major edge at this line (stepped once from
		// the previous line before the first line).
		steps := int32(y - int(prevLine))
		xh := tc.xh + int32(int64(tc.dxhdy)*int64(steps))
		var xMinor int32
		if y < midLine {
			xMinor = tc.xm + int32(int64(tc.dxmdy)*int64(steps))
		} else {
			lSteps := int32(y - midLine)
			xMinor = tc.xl + int32(int64(tc.dxldy)*int64(lSteps))
		}
		left, right := xh, xMinor
		if !tc.lft {
			// lft 0: the major edge is the left edge.
			left, right = xh, xMinor
		} else {
			left, right = xMinor, xh
		}
		if right <= left {
			continue
		}
		lineSub := int32(y * 4)
		// Pixel span touched by the coverage interval.
		x0 := int(left >> 16)
		x1 := int((right - 1) >> 16)
		for x := x0; x <= x1; x++ {
			cvg := spanCoverage(left, right, x)
			if cvg <= 0 {
				continue
			}
			f := &frag{x: x, y: y, cvg: cvg, tile: -1}
			if tc.shaded {
				var cr [4]int32
				for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
					cr[i] = plane(tc.col[i], tc.dColDx[i], tc.dColDy[i],
						x, xhTop, lineSub, tc.yh)
				}
				f.shade = RGBA{
					clamp255(cr[0] >> 16),
					clamp255(cr[1] >> 16),
					clamp255(cr[2] >> 16),
					clamp255(cr[3] >> 16),
				}
			}
			if tc.hasZ {
				zf := plane(tc.z, tc.dzDx, tc.dzDy, x, xhTop, lineSub, tc.yh)
				f.z = clampZ18(zf)
				dzx := abs32(tc.dzDx)
				dzy := abs32(tc.dzDy)
				if dzy > dzx {
					dzx = dzy
				}
				f.dz = clampZ18(dzx)
			}
			if tc.tex {
				sRaw := plane(tc.s, tc.dsDx, tc.dsDy, x, xhTop, lineSub, tc.yh)
				tRaw := plane(tc.t, tc.dtDx, tc.dtDy, x, xhTop, lineSub, tc.yh)
				wRaw := plane(tc.w, tc.dwDx, tc.dwDy, x, xhTop, lineSub, tc.yh)
				if persp && wRaw != 0 {
					// Both values are raw 16.16: their
					// ratio is already in 1/32 texel
					// units (S = st * texels * 32 at a
					// vertex, W = 1.0 there).
					f.texS = int32(float64(sRaw) / float64(wRaw))
					f.texT = int32(float64(tRaw) / float64(wRaw))
				} else {
					f.texS = sRaw >> 16
					f.texT = tRaw >> 16
				}
				// The positions above are in units of
				// (texel * 32): raw 16.16 S with W=1 maps
				// S/65536 = texel*32, so persp divides the
				// raw values and rescales; see README.
				f.tile = tc.tile
				f.lodLevel = lodLevel
				f.lodFrac = lodFrac
			}
			r.plot(f)
		}
	}
}

// triLOD computes the mip level and LOD fraction for a
// textured triangle from the derivative magnitudes at
// the top vertex, in texels per pixel.
func (r *RDP) triLOD(tc *triCmd, xhTop int32, persp bool) (int, int) {
	if !r.omTexLOD() {
		return 0, r.primLvlFrc
	}
	// Derivatives of the texture coordinates in texels
	// per pixel, at the top vertex.
	var dsdx, dtdx, dsdy, dtdy float64
	if persp && tc.w != 0 {
		w := float64(tc.w)
		quo := func(v, dv, dw int32) float64 {
			return (float64(dv)*w - float64(v)*float64(dw)) / (w * w) / 32.0
		}
		dsdx = quo(tc.s, tc.dsDx, tc.dwDx)
		dtdx = quo(tc.t, tc.dtDx, tc.dwDx)
		dsdy = quo(tc.s, tc.dsDy, tc.dwDy)
		dtdy = quo(tc.t, tc.dtDy, tc.dwDy)
	} else {
		const scale = 1.0 / (65536.0 * 32.0)
		dsdx = float64(tc.dsDx) * scale
		dtdx = float64(tc.dtDx) * scale
		dsdy = float64(tc.dsDy) * scale
		dtdy = float64(tc.dtDy) * scale
	}
	mag := absF(dsdx)
	if v := absF(dtdx); v > mag {
		mag = v
	}
	if v := absF(dsdy); v > mag {
		mag = v
	}
	if v := absF(dtdy); v > mag {
		mag = v
	}
	if mag <= 1.0 {
		return 0, 0
	}
	level := 0
	m := mag
	for m >= 2.0 && level < 7 {
		m /= 2.0
		level++
	}
	frac := int((m - 1.0) * 255.0)
	if frac > 255 {
		frac = 255
	}
	return level, frac
}

// spanCoverage computes horizontal coverage in eighths
// of pixel x by the interval [left, right) (16.16).
func spanCoverage(left, right int32, x int) int {
	lo := int64(int32(x)) << 16
	hi := lo + 65536
	l := int64(left)
	if l < lo {
		l = lo
	}
	rr := int64(right)
	if rr > hi {
		rr = hi
	}
	overlap := rr - l
	if overlap <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	c := int((overlap*8 + 32768) >> 16)
	if c > 8 {
		c = 8
	}
	return c
}

// clampZ18 converts a 16.16 z plane value into the
// internal 18-bit depth range. The command's z is an
// unsigned fraction spanning the full 32-bit field
// (z18 = value >> 14), so the shift is unsigned.
func clampZ18(zFixed int32) int32 {
	z := int32(uint32(zFixed) >> 14)
	if z > 0x3FFFF {
		return 0x3FFFF
	}
	return z
}

func abs32(v int32) int32 {
	if v < 0 {
		return -v
	}
	return v
}

func absF(v float64) float64 {
	if v < 0 {
		return -v
	}
	return v
}

// cmdTexRect rasterizes a Texture Rectangle or its
// flipped form. Word 0: XH (55..44), YH (43..32) in
// 10.2, tile (26..24), XL (23..12), YL (11..0). Word 1:
// S (63..48) and T (47..32) in signed 10.5, DsDx
// (31..16) and DtDy (15..0) in signed 5.10.
//
// Unflipped: S steps along X by DsDx and T steps along
// Y by DtDy. Flipped: the roles swap, S steps along Y
// by DtDy and T steps along X by DsDx. Positions are
// accumulated in 1/1024 texel units (S and T fields are
// 10.5, so raw * 32; the step fields are 5.10 already)
// and converted to the sampler's 1/32 units per pixel.
func (r *RDP) cmdTexRect(op int, w []uint64) {
	w0, w1 := w[0], w[1]
	xh := int((w0>>44)&0xFFF) >> 2
	yh := int((w0>>32)&0xFFF) >> 2
	tile := int((w0 >> 24) & 7)
	xl := int((w0>>12)&0xFFF) >> 2
	yl := int(w0&0xFFF) >> 2
	s0 := sext16(uint32(w1 >> 48))
	t0 := sext16(uint32(w1 >> 32))
	dsdx := sext16(uint32(w1 >> 16))
	dtdy := sext16(uint32(w1))

	ct := r.omCycleType()
	// Lower-right corner: inclusive in fill and copy
	// modes, exclusive in 1-cycle and 2-cycle modes.
	xEnd, yEnd := xl, yl
	if ct == 0 || ct == 1 {
		xEnd--
		yEnd--
	}
	flip := op == CmdTexRectFlip

	for y := yh; y <= yEnd; y++ {
		for x := xh; x <= xEnd; x++ {
			var sPos, tPos int32
			if !flip {
				sPos = (s0*32 + int32(x-xh)*dsdx) >> 5
				tPos = (t0*32 + int32(y-yh)*dtdy) >> 5
			} else {
				sPos = (s0*32 + int32(y-yh)*dtdy) >> 5
				tPos = (t0*32 + int32(x-xh)*dsdx) >> 5
			}
			f := &frag{
				x: x, y: y, cvg: 8, tile: tile,
				texS: sPos, texT: tPos,
				lodFrac: r.primLvlFrc,
			}
			if r.omZSourcePrim() {
				f.z = int32(r.primZ) << 2
			}
			r.plot(f)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/rdp/rdp.go ====================

// Package rdp implements the Nintendo 64 Reality Display
// Processor: the command processor that consumes display
// lists from RDRAM (XBUS off) or from RSP DMEM (XBUS on),
// the TMEM texture memory with its tile descriptors, the
// color combiner and blender, and a software rasterizer
// that draws into the color and depth images in RDRAM.
// It is original code written from the published SGI RDP
// command summary and the public N64 programming
// documentation (command encodings, register layouts,
// and pipeline semantics are factual hardware data).
//
// Execution is synchronous: writing DP_END runs the list
// to completion immediately, so the busy bits in
// DP_STATUS always read clear and FULLSYNC raises the DP
// interrupt (through MI) as soon as it is reached. That
// simplification, and the other model choices (coverage,
// the three-texel texture filter, LOD scope, the depth
// store format), are documented in the README and in the
// comments at each site.
package rdp

import "encoding/binary"

// Image formats (Set Color/Texture Image, Set Tile).
const (
	FmtRGBA = 0
	FmtYUV  = 1
	FmtCI   = 2
	FmtIA   = 3
	FmtI    = 4
)

// Texel element sizes (the size field of image and tile
// commands): 0 = 4-bit, 1 = 8-bit, 2 = 16-bit, 3 = 32-bit.
const (
	Size4  = 0
	Size8  = 1
	Size16 = 2
	Size32 = 3
)

// DP register byte offsets from 0x04100000 (also the RSP
// CP0 registers 8..15 in the same order).
const (
	RegStart   = 0x00
	RegEnd     = 0x04
	RegCurrent = 0x08
	RegStatus  = 0x0C
	RegClock   = 0x10
	RegBufBusy = 0x14
	RegPipeBsy = 0x18
	RegTMem    = 0x1C
)

// DP_STATUS read bits.
const (
	StatusXBusDMEM  = 1 << 0
	StatusFreeze    = 1 << 1
	StatusFlush     = 1 << 2
	StatusGClkAlive = 1 << 3
	StatusEndValid  = 1 << 9
	StatusStartVal  = 1 << 10
)

// Command opcodes (bits 61..56 of the first word).
const (
	CmdNoOp         = 0x00
	CmdTriBase      = 0x08 // 0x08..0x0F: triangles
	CmdTexRect      = 0x24
	CmdTexRectFlip  = 0x25
	CmdSyncPipe     = 0x27
	CmdSyncTile     = 0x28
	CmdSyncFull     = 0x29
	CmdSetKeyGB     = 0x2A
	CmdSetKeyR      = 0x2B
	CmdSetConvert   = 0x2C
	CmdSetScissor   = 0x2D
	CmdSetPrimDepth = 0x2E
	CmdSetOtherMode = 0x2F
	CmdLoadTLUT     = 0x30
	CmdSyncLoad     = 0x31
	CmdSetTileSize  = 0x32
	CmdLoadBlock    = 0x33
	CmdLoadTile     = 0x34
	CmdSetTile      = 0x35
	CmdFillRect     = 0x36
	CmdSetFillColor = 0x37
	CmdSetFogColor  = 0x38
	CmdSetBlendCol  = 0x39
	CmdSetPrimColor = 0x3A
	CmdSetEnvColor  = 0x3B
	CmdSetCombine   = 0x3C
	CmdSetTexImage  = 0x3D
	CmdSetZImage    = 0x3E
	CmdSetColorImg  = 0x3F
)

// RGBA is one pixel in flight through the pipeline, one
// byte per channel.
type RGBA struct {
	R, G, B, A uint8
}

// Image describes one of the image registers (color,
// texture): format, texel size, width in pixels (the
// programmed width field plus one), and the RDRAM byte
// address of the top-left corner.
type Image struct {
	Format int
	Size   int
	Width  int
	Addr   uint32
}

// Tile is one of the eight TMEM tile descriptors.
// SL/TL/SH/TH are kept in the raw 10.2 units the
// commands carry (texel = raw / 4).
type Tile struct {
	Format  int
	Size    int
	Line    int // TMEM 64-bit words per tile line
	TMem    int // tile base in TMEM, in 64-bit words
	Palette int
	ClampT  bool
	MirrorT bool
	MaskT   int
	ShiftT  int
	ClampS  bool
	MirrorS bool
	MaskS   int
	ShiftS  int

	SL, TL, SH, TH int
}

// keyChan holds one chroma-key channel's coefficients.
type keyChan struct {
	Width  int // s7.4 fixed (12 bits)
	Center int
	Scale  int
}

// RDP is the display processor state.
type RDP struct {
	dram []byte // attached RDRAM
	dmem []byte // attached RSP DMEM (the XBUS source)

	// DP command registers.
	start      uint32
	end        uint32
	current    uint32
	xbus       bool // false: fetch from RDRAM; true: DMEM
	freeze     bool
	flush      bool
	startValid bool
	endValid   bool
	clock      uint32 // activity counter: words fetched

	// OnInterrupt drives the MI DP bit when a FULLSYNC
	// command executes. It is a level: FULLSYNC raises
	// it, MI_MODE bit 11 (on the bus) clears it.
	OnInterrupt func(active bool)

	colorImg Image
	texImg   Image
	zAddr    uint32

	tiles [8]Tile
	tmem  [4096]byte

	otherModes uint64 // Set Other Modes register (bits 55..0)
	combineReg uint64 // Set Combine Mode register (bits 55..0)

	primColor  RGBA
	envColor   RGBA
	blendColor RGBA
	fogColor   RGBA
	primMinLvl int // Set Prim Color: minimum LOD clamp (0..31)
	primLvlFrc int // Set Prim Color: LOD fraction (0..255)

	fillColor uint32
	primZ     uint16
	primDZ    uint16

	conv [6]int32 // Set Convert coefficients (signed 1.7)

	keyR  keyChan
	keyGB keyGBRegs

	sciX0, sciY0 int // scissor box, 10.2 raw units
	sciX1, sciY1 int
	sciField     bool // scissor field enable
	sciOdd       bool // keep odd lines when set

	// hidden holds the per-pixel coverage bits for
	// 16-bit color images, which live in a separate
	// on-chip store on hardware rather than in RDRAM.
	// Indexed by RDRAM byte address / 2. Values 0..8.
	hidden []uint8
}

type keyGBRegs struct {
	WidthG, WidthB   int
	CenterG, CenterB int
	ScaleG, ScaleB   int
}

// New returns an RDP in its power-on state. The
// scissor box starts at the full 10.2 coordinate range
// so lists that never program it draw unclipped.
func New() *RDP {
	return &RDP{sciX1: 0xFFF, sciY1: 0xFFF}
}

// AttachDRAM gives the RDP its RDRAM backing store and
// sizes the hidden coverage store to match (one entry
// per 16-bit pixel slot).
func (r *RDP) AttachDRAM(dram []byte) {
	r.dram = dram
	r.hidden = make([]uint8, len(dram)/2)
}

// AttachDMEM gives the command processor the RSP DMEM
// slice used as the XBUS command source.
func (r *RDP) AttachDMEM(dmem []byte) { r.dmem = dmem }

// ReadRegister reads a DP register by byte offset from
// 0x04100000.
func (r *RDP) ReadRegister(off uint32) uint32 {
	switch off {
	case RegStart:
		return r.start
	case RegEnd:
		return r.end
	case RegCurrent:
		return r.current
	case RegStatus:
		var s uint32 = StatusGClkAlive
		if r.xbus {
			s |= StatusXBusDMEM
		}
		if r.freeze {
			s |= StatusFreeze
		}
		if r.flush {
			s |= StatusFlush
		}
		if r.endValid {
			s |= StatusEndValid
		}
		if r.startValid {
			s |= StatusStartVal
		}
		// TMEM busy, pipeline busy, command busy, buffer
		// ready, and DMA busy all read 0: execution is
		// synchronous in this model.
		return s
	case RegClock:
		return r.clock
	}
	return 0 // buffer busy, pipe busy, and TMEM counters
}

// WriteRegister writes a DP register by byte offset.
func (r *RDP) WriteRegister(off uint32, val uint32) {
	switch off {
	case RegStart:
		r.start = val & 0xFFFFFF
		r.startValid = true
	case RegEnd:
		r.end = val & 0xFFFFFF
		r.endValid = true
		r.maybeExecute()
	case RegStatus:
		r.writeStatus(val)
	}
}

// writeStatus applies the documented DP_STATUS write
// pairs: each function has a clear bit and a set bit.
func (r *RDP) writeStatus(val uint32) {
	if val&(1<<0) != 0 {
		r.xbus = false
	}
	if val&(1<<1) != 0 {
		r.xbus = true
	}
	if val&(1<<2) != 0 {
		wasFrozen := r.freeze
		r.freeze = false
		if wasFrozen {
			r.maybeExecute()
		}
	}
	if val&(1<<3) != 0 {
		r.freeze = true
	}
	if val&(1<<4) != 0 {
		r.flush = false
	}
	if val&(1<<5) != 0 {
		r.flush = true
	}
	// Bits 6..8 clear the TMEM, pipe, and command
	// counters (only the clock is modeled, by bit 9).
	if val&(1<<9) != 0 {
		r.clock = 0
	}
}

// ReadCPURegister reads a DP register in RSP CP0 index
// form (registers 8..15 map to offsets 0x00..0x1C).
func (r *RDP) ReadCPURegister(reg int) uint32 {
	if reg < 8 || reg > 15 {
		return 0
	}
	return r.ReadRegister(uint32(reg-8) * 4)
}

// WriteCPURegister writes a DP register in RSP CP0
// index form.
func (r *RDP) WriteCPURegister(reg int, val uint32) {
	if reg < 8 || reg > 15 {
		return
	}
	r.WriteRegister(uint32(reg-8)*4, val)
}

// maybeExecute runs the pending list when both address
// registers are valid and the RDP is not frozen.
func (r *RDP) maybeExecute() {
	if r.freeze || !r.startValid || !r.endValid {
		return
	}
	r.execute(r.start, r.end)
}

// fetchWord reads one 64-bit command word from the
// active source at a byte address, wrapping inside the
// source (24-bit RDRAM space, 12-bit DMEM space).
func (r *RDP) fetchWord(addr uint32) uint64 {
	var v uint64
	if r.xbus {
		base := addr & 0xFFF
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			v = v<<8 | uint64(r.dmem[(base+uint32(i))&0xFFF])
		}
		return v
	}
	base := addr & 0xFFFFFF
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		v = v<<8 | uint64(r.dramByte(base+uint32(i)))
	}
	return v
}

// addrMask is the wrap mask of the active source.
func (r *RDP) addrMask() uint32 {
	if r.xbus {
		return 0xFFF
	}
	return 0xFFFFFF
}

// execute processes the command stream from start to
// end. Command lengths depend on the opcode; a stream
// that ends mid-command stops quietly (the truncated
// tail is treated as consumed), matching the undefined
// hardware behavior with a safe outcome.
func (r *RDP) execute(start, end uint32) {
	mask := r.addrMask()
	addr := start & mask
	end &= mask
	r.current = addr
	guard := 0
	for addr != end {
		guard++
		if guard > 1<<22 {
			break // runaway list protection
		}
		op := int(r.peekOp(addr))
		n := cmdWords(op, r, addr)
		if n <= 0 {
			n = 1
		}
		// Verify the whole command fits before end.
		fits := true
		a := addr
		for i := 1; i < n; i++ {
			a = (a + 8) & mask
			if a == end {
				fits = false
				break
			}
		}
		if !fits {
			break
		}
		words := make([]uint64, n)
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			words[i] = r.fetchWord(addr)
			addr = (addr + 8) & mask
		}
		r.clock += uint32(n)
		r.dispatch(op, words)
		r.current = addr
	}
	r.current = end
}

// peekOp reads the opcode of the command at addr.
func (r *RDP) peekOp(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(r.fetchWord(addr) >> 56)
}

// cmdWords returns the length in words of the command
// with the given opcode at addr. Triangle lengths depend
// on the attribute bits in the opcode itself.
func cmdWords(op int, r *RDP, addr uint32) int {
	switch {
	case op >= CmdTriBase && op <= 0x0F:
		n := 4 // edge coefficients
		if op&0x04 != 0 {
			n += 8 // shade coefficients
		}
		if op&0x02 != 0 {
			n += 8 // texture coefficients
		}
		if op&0x01 != 0 {
			n += 2 // z coefficients
		}
		return n
	case op == CmdTexRect || op == CmdTexRectFlip:
		return 2
	}
	return 1
}

// dispatch executes one decoded command.
func (r *RDP) dispatch(op int, w []uint64) {
	switch {
	case op >= CmdTriBase && op <= 0x0F:
		r.cmdTriangle(op, w)
	case op == CmdNoOp, op == CmdSyncPipe, op == CmdSyncTile, op == CmdSyncLoad:
		// Ordering barriers only; synchronous execution
		// makes them no-ops.
	case op == CmdSyncFull:
		if r.OnInterrupt != nil {
			r.OnInterrupt(true)
		}
	case op == CmdTexRect || op == CmdTexRectFlip:
		r.cmdTexRect(op, w)
	default:
		r.dispatchState(op, w[0])
	}
}

// dramByte reads RDRAM with power-of-two wraparound.
func (r *RDP) dramByte(addr uint32) byte {
	if len(r.dram) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return r.dram[addr&(uint32(len(r.dram))-1)]
}

// dramWriteByte writes RDRAM with wraparound.
func (r *RDP) dramWriteByte(addr uint32, v byte) {
	if len(r.dram) == 0 {
		return
	}
	r.dram[addr&(uint32(len(r.dram))-1)] = v
}

// dramRead16 reads a big-endian halfword from RDRAM.
func (r *RDP) dramRead16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(r.dramByte(addr))<<8 | uint16(r.dramByte(addr+1))
}

// dramWrite16 writes a big-endian halfword to RDRAM.
func (r *RDP) dramWrite16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	r.dramWriteByte(addr, byte(v>>8))
	r.dramWriteByte(addr+1, byte(v))
}

// dramRead32 reads a big-endian word from RDRAM.
func (r *RDP) dramRead32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(r.dramRead16(addr))<<16 | uint32(r.dramRead16(addr+2))
}

// dramWrite32 writes a big-endian word to RDRAM.
func (r *RDP) dramWrite32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	r.dramWrite16(addr, uint16(v>>16))
	r.dramWrite16(addr+2, uint16(v))
}

// SerializeSize reports the byte size of a serialized
// RDP for the attached RDRAM size (the hidden coverage
// store scales with RDRAM).
func (r *RDP) SerializeSize() int {
	return 20 + // DP registers and clock
		36 + // image registers
		8*17*4 + // tiles
		8 + 8 + // other modes, combine
		16 + 8 + 4 + 8 + // colors, prim LOD, fill, prim depth
		24 + 36 + // convert, keys
		20 + // scissor
		4096 + // TMEM
		len(r.hidden)
}

// Serialize writes the RDP state into dst (at least
// SerializeSize bytes) and returns the byte count.
func (r *RDP) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &stateWriter{b: dst}
	w.u32(r.start)
	w.u32(r.end)
	w.u32(r.current)
	var fl uint32
	if r.xbus {
		fl |= 1 << 0
	}
	if r.freeze {
		fl |= 1 << 1
	}
	if r.flush {
		fl |= 1 << 2
	}
	if r.startValid {
		fl |= 1 << 3
	}
	if r.endValid {
		fl |= 1 << 4
	}
	w.u32(fl)
	w.u32(r.clock)
	writeImg := func(im Image) {
		w.u32(uint32(im.Format))
		w.u32(uint32(im.Size))
		w.u32(uint32(im.Width))
		w.u32(im.Addr)
	}
	writeImg(r.colorImg)
	writeImg(r.texImg)
	w.u32(r.zAddr)
	for i := range r.tiles {
		t := &r.tiles[i]
		vals := [17]uint32{
			uint32(t.Format), uint32(t.Size), uint32(t.Line), uint32(t.TMem),
			uint32(t.Palette), boolU(t.ClampT), boolU(t.MirrorT), uint32(t.MaskT),
			uint32(t.ShiftT), boolU(t.ClampS), boolU(t.MirrorS), uint32(t.MaskS),
			uint32(t.ShiftS), uint32(int32(t.SL)), uint32(int32(t.TL)),
			uint32(int32(t.SH)), uint32(int32(t.TH)),
		}
		for _, v := range vals {
			w.u32(v)
		}
	}
	w.u64(r.otherModes)
	w.u64(r.combineReg)
	writeRGBA := func(c RGBA) {
		w.u8(c.R)
		w.u8(c.G)
		w.u8(c.B)
		w.u8(c.A)
	}
	writeRGBA(r.primColor)
	writeRGBA(r.envColor)
	writeRGBA(r.blendColor)
	writeRGBA(r.fogColor)
	w.u32(uint32(r.primMinLvl))
	w.u32(uint32(r.primLvlFrc))
	w.u32(r.fillColor)
	w.u32(uint32(r.primZ))
	w.u32(uint32(r.primDZ))
	for _, k := range r.conv {
		w.u32(uint32(k))
	}
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyR.Width))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyR.Center))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyR.Scale))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyGB.WidthG))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyGB.WidthB))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyGB.CenterG))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyGB.ScaleG))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyGB.CenterB))
	w.u32(uint32(r.keyGB.ScaleB))
	w.u32(uint32(int32(r.sciX0)))
	w.u32(uint32(int32(r.sciY0)))
	w.u32(uint32(int32(r.sciX1)))
	w.u32(uint32(int32(r.sciY1)))
	var sf uint32
	if r.sciField {
		sf |= 1
	}
	if r.sciOdd {
		sf |= 2
	}
	w.u32(sf)
	w.bytes(r.tmem[:])
	w.bytes(r.hidden)
	return w.n
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (r *RDP) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) < r.SerializeSize() {
		return errShortState
	}
	rd := &stateReader{b: in}
	r.start = rd.u32()
	r.end = rd.u32()
	r.current = rd.u32()
	fl := rd.u32()
	r.xbus = fl&(1<<0) != 0
	r.freeze = fl&(1<<1) != 0
	r.flush = fl&(1<<2) != 0
	r.startValid = fl&(1<<3) != 0
	r.endValid = fl&(1<<4) != 0
	r.clock = rd.u32()
	readImg := func() Image {
		return Image{Format: int(rd.u32()), Size: int(rd.u32()),
			Width: int(rd.u32()), Addr: rd.u32()}
	}
	r.colorImg = readImg()
	r.texImg = readImg()
	r.zAddr = rd.u32()
	for i := range r.tiles {
		v := make([]uint32, 17)
		for j := range v {
			v[j] = rd.u32()
		}
		r.tiles[i] = Tile{
			Format: int(v[0]), Size: int(v[1]), Line: int(v[2]), TMem: int(v[3]),
			Palette: int(v[4]), ClampT: v[5] != 0, MirrorT: v[6] != 0,
			MaskT: int(v[7]), ShiftT: int(v[8]), ClampS: v[9] != 0,
			MirrorS: v[10] != 0, MaskS: int(v[11]), ShiftS: int(v[12]),
			SL: int(int32(v[13])), TL: int(int32(v[14])),
			SH: int(int32(v[15])), TH: int(int32(v[16])),
		}
	}
	r.otherModes = rd.u64()
	r.combineReg = rd.u64()
	readRGBA := func() RGBA {
		return RGBA{rd.u8(), rd.u8(), rd.u8(), rd.u8()}
	}
	r.primColor = readRGBA()
	r.envColor = readRGBA()
	r.blendColor = readRGBA()
	r.fogColor = readRGBA()
	r.primMinLvl = int(rd.u32())
	r.primLvlFrc = int(rd.u32())
	r.fillColor = rd.u32()
	r.primZ = uint16(rd.u32())
	r.primDZ = uint16(rd.u32())
	for i := range r.conv {
		r.conv[i] = int32(rd.u32())
	}
	r.keyR = keyChan{Width: int(rd.u32()), Center: int(rd.u32()), Scale: int(rd.u32())}
	r.keyGB = keyGBRegs{
		WidthG: int(rd.u32()), WidthB: int(rd.u32()),
		CenterG: int(rd.u32()), ScaleG: int(rd.u32()),
		CenterB: int(rd.u32()), ScaleB: int(rd.u32()),
	}
	r.sciX0 = int(int32(rd.u32()))
	r.sciY0 = int(int32(rd.u32()))
	r.sciX1 = int(int32(rd.u32()))
	r.sciY1 = int(int32(rd.u32()))
	sf := rd.u32()
	r.sciField = sf&1 != 0
	r.sciOdd = sf&2 != 0
	copy(r.tmem[:], rd.bytes(4096))
	copy(r.hidden, rd.bytes(len(r.hidden)))
	return nil
}

func boolU(b bool) uint32 {
	if b {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

var errShortState = errShort{}

type errShort struct{}

func (errShort) Error() string { return "rdp: state too short" }

// stateWriter appends fixed-width big-endian values.
type stateWriter struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (w *stateWriter) u8(v uint8)   { w.b[w.n] = v; w.n++ }
func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) { binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(w.b[w.n:], v); w.n += 4 }
func (w *stateWriter) u64(v uint64) { binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(w.b[w.n:], v); w.n += 8 }
func (w *stateWriter) bytes(p []byte) {
	copy(w.b[w.n:], p)
	w.n += len(p)
}

// stateReader reads fixed-width big-endian values.
type stateReader struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (s *stateReader) u8() uint8   { v := s.b[s.n]; s.n++; return v }
func (s *stateReader) u32() uint32 { v := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(s.b[s.n:]); s.n += 4; return v }
func (s *stateReader) u64() uint64 { v := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(s.b[s.n:]); s.n += 8; return v }
func (s *stateReader) bytes(n int) []byte {
	v := s.b[s.n : s.n+n]
	s.n += n
	return v
}

package rdp

import (
	"testing"
)

// newTestRDP returns an RDP with 4 MB of RDRAM.
func newTestRDP() (*RDP, []byte) {
	dram := make([]byte, 4<<20)
	r := New()
	r.AttachDRAM(dram)
	return r, dram
}

func cmdWord(op int, rest uint64) uint64 {
	return uint64(op)<<56 | rest
}

// runList writes words into RDRAM at base and triggers
// execution through the DP registers.
func runList(r *RDP, dram []byte, base uint32, words []uint64) {
	for i, w := range words {
		for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
			dram[base+uint32(i*8+j)] = byte(w >> uint(56-8*j))
		}
	}
	r.WriteRegister(RegStart, base)
	r.WriteRegister(RegEnd, base+uint32(len(words)*8))
}

// omWord builds an other-modes value with the given
// cycle type and extra low bits.
func omWord(cycleType int, extra uint64) uint64 {
	return uint64(cycleType)<<52 | extra
}

// combineWord builds a combine register value with the
// same muxes in both cycles.
func combineWord(subAR, mulR, subBR, addR, subAA, mulA, subBA, addA int) uint64 {
	var w uint64
	w |= uint64(subAR) << 52
	w |= uint64(mulR) << 47
	w |= uint64(subAA) << 44
	w |= uint64(mulA) << 41
	w |= uint64(subBR) << 28
	w |= uint64(addR) << 15
	w |= uint64(subBA) << 12
	w |= uint64(addA) << 9
	w |= uint64(subAR) << 37
	w |= uint64(mulR) << 32
	w |= uint64(subAA) << 21
	w |= uint64(mulA) << 18
	w |= uint64(subBR) << 24
	w |= uint64(addR) << 6
	w |= uint64(subBA) << 3
	w |= uint64(addA)
	return w
}

func TestFillRectViaList(t *testing.T) {
	r, dram := newTestRDP()
	// Color image 64x64 RGBA16 at 0x10000.
	setImg := uint64(FmtRGBA)<<53 | uint64(Size16)<<51 |
		uint64(63)<<32 | 0x10000
	// Fill color: pixels pair (red, green).
	fill := cmdWord(CmdSetFillColor, 0xF80107C1)
	// Fill rect: XL=63.0 YL=63.0 XH=0 YH=0 (10.2 fields).
	fr := cmdWord(CmdFillRect,
		uint64(63*4)<<44|uint64(63*4)<<32|uint64(0)<<12|0)
	words := []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdSetColorImg, setImg),
		cmdWord(CmdSetOtherMode, omWord(3, 0)), // fill cycle
		fill,
		fr,
	}
	runList(r, dram, 0x8000, words)
	// Pixel (0,0): even x takes the high half (red).
	if v := r.dramRead16(0x10000); v != 0xF801 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (0,0) = %#04x, want 0xF801", v)
	}
	// Pixel (1,0): low half (green).
	if v := r.dramRead16(0x10002); v != 0x07C1 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (1,0) = %#04x, want 0x07C1", v)
	}
	// Pixel (63,63) is included in fill mode.
	off := uint32(0x10000 + (63*64+63)*2)
	if v := r.dramRead16(off); v != 0x07C1 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (63,63) = %#04x, want 0x07C1", v)
	}
	// DP status: start and end valid set, clock counted.
	st := r.ReadRegister(RegStatus)
	if st&StatusStartVal == 0 || st&StatusEndValid == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("status %#x missing valid bits", st)
	}
	if got := r.ReadRegister(RegClock); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("clock = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := r.ReadRegister(RegCurrent); got != 0x8000+32 {
		t.Fatalf("current = %#x, want end", got)
	}
}

func TestFreezeDefersExecution(t *testing.T) {
	r, dram := newTestRDP()
	r.WriteRegister(RegStatus, 1<<3) // set freeze
	words := []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdSetColorImg, uint64(FmtRGBA)<<53|uint64(Size16)<<51|uint64(63)<<32|0x10000),
		cmdWord(CmdSetOtherMode, omWord(3, 0)),
		cmdWord(CmdSetFillColor, 0xFFFF0000),
		cmdWord(CmdFillRect, uint64(10*4)<<44|uint64(10*4)<<32),
	}
	for i, w := range words {
		for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
			dram[0x8000+i*8+j] = byte(w >> uint(56-8*j))
		}
	}
	r.WriteRegister(RegStart, 0x8000)
	r.WriteRegister(RegEnd, 0x8000+32)
	if v := r.dramRead16(0x10000); v != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("frozen list executed: %#04x", v)
	}
	r.WriteRegister(RegStatus, 1<<2) // clear freeze
	if v := r.dramRead16(0x10000); v != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("after unfreeze pixel = %#04x, want 0xFFFF", v)
	}
}

func TestFullSyncInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	r, dram := newTestRDP()
	fired := 0
	r.OnInterrupt = func(active bool) {
		if active {
			fired++
		}
	}
	runList(r, dram, 0x8000, []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdNoOp, 0),
		cmdWord(CmdSyncPipe, 0),
		cmdWord(CmdSyncFull, 0),
	})
	if fired != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("FULLSYNC fired %d times, want 1", fired)
	}
}

func TestFillPacking8And32(t *testing.T) {
	r, dram := newTestRDP()
	// 8-bit image at 0x20000, width 16.
	runList(r, dram, 0x8000, []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdSetColorImg, uint64(FmtI)<<53|uint64(Size8)<<51|uint64(15)<<32|0x20000),
		cmdWord(CmdSetOtherMode, omWord(3, 0)),
		cmdWord(CmdSetFillColor, 0x11223344),
		cmdWord(CmdFillRect, uint64(3*4)<<44|uint64(0)<<32),
	})
	want := []byte{0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44}
	for i, wb := range want {
		if dram[0x20000+i] != wb {
			t.Fatalf("8-bit fill pixel %d = %#02x, want %#02x", i, dram[0x20000+i], wb)
		}
	}
	// 32-bit image at 0x30000, width 16.
	runList(r, dram, 0x8000, []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdSetColorImg, uint64(FmtRGBA)<<53|uint64(Size32)<<51|uint64(15)<<32|0x30000),
		cmdWord(CmdSetFillColor, 0xA1B2C3D4),
		cmdWord(CmdFillRect, uint64(1*4)<<44|uint64(0)<<32),
	})
	if v := r.dramRead32(0x30000); v != 0xA1B2C3D4 {
		t.Fatalf("32-bit fill pixel = %#08x, want 0xA1B2C3D4", v)
	}
	if v := r.dramRead32(0x30004); v != 0xA1B2C3D4 {
		t.Fatalf("32-bit fill pixel 1 = %#08x", v)
	}
}

// texImage4x4 plants a 4x4 RGBA16 texture image at
// 0x40000 in the texture image registers' target and
// returns the distinct texel values.
func texImage4x4(r *RDP) {
	// Texture image: RGBA16, width 4, at 0x40000.
	vals := [16]uint16{
		0xF801, 0x07C1, 0x003F, 0xFFFF,
		0x0001, 0x801F, 0x7C01, 0x03E1,
		0x1234, 0x2345, 0x3456, 0x4567,
		0x5678, 0x6789, 0x789A, 0x89AB,
	}
	for i, v := range vals {
		r.dramWrite16(0x40000+uint32(i*2), v)
	}
	r.texImg = Image{Format: FmtRGBA, Size: Size16, Width: 4, Addr: 0x40000}
}

func TestLoadBlockMatchesLoadTile(t *testing.T) {
	ra, _ := newTestRDP()
	texImage4x4(ra)
	// Tile 0: line 1 word (8 bytes per line of 4 texels).
	ra.tiles[0] = Tile{Format: FmtRGBA, Size: Size16, Line: 1, TMem: 0}
	ra.tiles[0].SL, ra.tiles[0].TL, ra.tiles[0].SH = 0, 0, 15
	ra.tiles[0].TH = 3 * 4
	ra.loadBlock(0, 2048) // dxt: one word per source line

	rb, _ := newTestRDP()
	texImage4x4(rb)
	rb.tiles[0] = Tile{Format: FmtRGBA, Size: Size16, Line: 1, TMem: 0}
	rb.tiles[0].SL, rb.tiles[0].TL = 0, 0
	rb.tiles[0].SH, rb.tiles[0].TH = 3*4, 3*4 // 10.2
	rb.loadTile(0)

	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if ra.tmem[i] != rb.tmem[i] {
			t.Fatalf("TMEM byte %d differs: block %#02x tile %#02x",
				i, ra.tmem[i], rb.tmem[i])
		}
	}
	// And the sampled texel (2,1) matches the source.
	got := ra.fetchTexel(0, 2, 1)
	want := expandRGBA16(0x7C01)
	if got != want {
		t.Fatalf("texel (2,1) = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestCombinerArithmetic(t *testing.T) {
	// (A - B) * C + D with floor on the scaled product.
	if v := combChan(200, 50, 128, 10); v != 85 {
		// (150 * 128) >> 8 = 75, + 10 = 85.
		t.Fatalf("combChan = %d, want 85", v)
	}
	if v := combChan(0, 255, 255, 0); v != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("combChan negative clamp = %d, want 0", v)
	}
	if v := combChan(255, 0, 255, 255); v != 255 {
		t.Fatalf("combChan high clamp = %d, want 255", v)
	}
	if v := combChan(255, 0, 255, 0); v != 254 {
		// The documented /256 scaling: 255*255>>8 = 254.
		t.Fatalf("combChan 255*ONE = %d, want 254", v)
	}
}

func TestBlenderEquation(t *testing.T) {
	r, _ := newTestRDP()
	// Cycle 0 blender: P = pixel, M = memory,
	// A = pixel alpha, B = 1 - A.
	var om uint64
	om |= 0 << 30 // b_m1a_0 = pixel
	om |= 1 << 26 // b_m1b_0 = memory
	om |= 0 << 22 // b_m2a_0 = pixel alpha
	om |= 0 << 18 // b_m2b_0 = 1 - A
	r.otherModes = om
	out := r.blendPass(0, RGBA{200, 100, 50, 255}, 128,
		RGBA{40, 60, 80, 255}, 8, &frag{})
	// (200*128 + 40*127)/255 = 120 (truncated).
	if out.R != 120 {
		t.Fatalf("blend R = %d, want 120", out.R)
	}
	// (100*128 + 60*127)/255 = 80.
	if out.G != 80 {
		t.Fatalf("blend G = %d, want 80", out.G)
	}
	// (50*128 + 80*127)/255 = 64.
	if out.B != 64 {
		t.Fatalf("blend B = %d, want 64", out.B)
	}
}

func TestScissorClipsFill(t *testing.T) {

		cmdWord(CmdSetScissor, uint64(40)<<44|uint64(40)<<32|uint64(80)<<12|80),
		cmdWord(CmdSetFillColor, 0x12341234),
		cmdWord(CmdFillRect, uint64(63*4)<<44|uint64(63*4)<<32),
