	}
	off = uint32(0x10000 + (20*64+20)*2)
	if v := r.dramRead16(off); v != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("scissor lower-right (exclusive) written: %#04x", v)
	}
}

func TestCI4TLUTAndFormats(t *testing.T) {
	r, _ := newTestRDP()
	// TLUT in the texture image: 16 RGBA16 entries at
	// 0x50000; entry 3 is pure red.
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		r.dramWrite16(0x50000+uint32(i*2), 0x0000)
	}
	r.dramWrite16(0x50000+6, 0xF801)
	r.texImg = Image{Format: FmtRGBA, Size: Size16, Width: 16, Addr: 0x50000}
	r.tiles[7] = Tile{Format: FmtRGBA, Size: Size16, Line: 1, TMem: 256}
	r.tiles[7].SL, r.tiles[7].TL = 0, 0
	r.tiles[7].SH = 15 * 4
	r.loadTLUT(7)
	// Enable TLUT (bit 47) and fetch a CI4 texel with
	// index 3 through tile 0.
	r.otherModes = 1 << 47
	r.tiles[0] = Tile{Format: FmtCI, Size: Size4, Line: 1, TMem: 0}
	r.tiles[0].SH, r.tiles[0].TH = 3*4, 0
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 0, 0, 3)
	got := r.fetchTexel(0, 0, 0)
	if got != (RGBA{255, 0, 0, 255}) {
		t.Fatalf("CI4 TLUT texel = %+v, want red", got)
	}
	// IA8: intensity high nibble, alpha low nibble.
	r.tiles[1] = Tile{Format: FmtIA, Size: Size8, Line: 1, TMem: 32}
	r.tiles[1].SH, r.tiles[1].TH = 3*4, 0
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[1], 0, 0, 0xAB)
	got = r.fetchTexel(1, 0, 0)
	if got != (RGBA{170, 170, 170, 187}) {
		t.Fatalf("IA8 texel = %+v, want (170,170,170,187)", got)
	}
	// I4: nibble * 17.
	r.tiles[2] = Tile{Format: FmtI, Size: Size4, Line: 1, TMem: 64}
	r.tiles[2].SH, r.tiles[2].TH = 3*4, 0
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[2], 0, 0, 9)
	got = r.fetchTexel(2, 0, 0)
	if got != (RGBA{153, 153, 153, 255}) {
		t.Fatalf("I4 texel = %+v, want 153 gray", got)
	}
}

func TestYUVConversion(t *testing.T) {
	r, _ := newTestRDP()
	// Documented typical convert coefficients.
	r.otherModes = 0 // TLUT off
	conv := []int32{175, -43, -89, 222, 114, 42}
	var w uint64
	for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
		w |= uint64(uint32(conv[i])&0x1FF) << uint(45-9*i)
	}
	r.dispatchState(CmdSetConvert, cmdWord(CmdSetConvert, w))
	// YUV red: Y=76, U=85, V=255 in a 16-bit pair.
	r.tiles[0] = Tile{Format: FmtYUV, Size: Size16, Line: 1, TMem: 0}
	r.tiles[0].SH, r.tiles[0].TH = 3*4, 0
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 0, 0, uint32(76)<<8|85)
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 1, 0, uint32(76)<<8|255)
	got := r.fetchTexel(0, 0, 0)
	if got != (RGBA{255, 0, 0, 255}) {
		t.Fatalf("YUV red = %+v, want (255,0,0,255)", got)
	}
}

func TestThreeTexelFilter(t *testing.T) {
	r, _ := newTestRDP()
	// 2x2 mode on, bilerp path requested by the caller.
	r.otherModes = 1 << 45 // sample_type = 2x2
	r.tiles[0] = Tile{Format: FmtRGBA, Size: Size32, Line: 1, TMem: 0}
	r.tiles[0].SH, r.tiles[0].TH = 4*4, 4*4 // clamp range
	// RGBA32 texels: (0,0) black, (1,0) R=64,
	// (0,1) G=128, (1,1) white.
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 0, 0, 0x000000FF)
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 1, 0, 0x400000FF)
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 0, 1, 0x008000FF)
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 1, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	// Half-texel position: fx = fy = 16 (of 32):
	// weights (0, 16, 16, 0) over the diagonal split.
	got := r.fetchFiltered(0, 16, 16, true)
	want := RGBA{32, 64, 0, 255}
	if got != want {
		t.Fatalf("triangle filter = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
	// Point mode at the same position returns (0,0).
	got = r.fetchFiltered(0, 16, 16, false)
	if got != (RGBA{0, 0, 0, 255}) {
		t.Fatalf("point sample = %+v, want black", got)
	}
}

func TestPrimDepthAndZ(t *testing.T) {
	r, dram := newTestRDP()
	// Clear the z image (at 0x18000) to max depth by
	// filling it through the color image register.
	runList(r, dram, 0x8000, []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdSetZImage, 0x18000),
		cmdWord(CmdSetColorImg, uint64(FmtRGBA)<<53|uint64(Size16)<<51|uint64(63)<<32|0x18000),
		cmdWord(CmdSetOtherMode, omWord(3, 0)),
		cmdWord(CmdSetFillColor, 0xFFFFFFFF),
		cmdWord(CmdFillRect, uint64(63*4)<<44|uint64(63*4)<<32),
		cmdWord(CmdSetColorImg, uint64(FmtRGBA)<<53|uint64(Size16)<<51|uint64(63)<<32|0x10000),
	})
	// A 1x1 white texture in tile 0.
	r.tiles[0] = Tile{Format: FmtRGBA, Size: Size16, Line: 1, TMem: 0}
	r.tiles[0].SH, r.tiles[0].TH = 0, 0
	r.writeTMEMRaw(&r.tiles[0], 0, 0, 0xFFFF)
	// 1-cycle, z compare + update on, z source = prim.
	om := omWord(0, (1<<4)|(1<<5)|(1<<2))
	// TEXRECT x 8..24, y 8..24 (lower right exclusive),
	// S = T = 0, DsDx = DtDy = 0 (the 1x1 clamps).
	rect := []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdTexRect, uint64(8*4)<<44|uint64(8*4)<<32|
			uint64(24*4)<<12|24*4),
		0,
	}
	words := []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdSetOtherMode, om),
		cmdWord(CmdSetCombine, combineWord(1, 16, 8, 1, 1, 7, 7, 1)),
		cmdWord(CmdSetPrimDepth, 0x8000<<16),
	}
	words = append(words, rect...)
	words = append(words, cmdWord(CmdSetPrimDepth, 0xC000<<16))
	words = append(words, rect...)
	runList(r, dram, 0x8000, words)
	// Pixel (12,12): the near rect (z 0x8000) drew
	// white; the farther rect (z 0xC000) lost the test.
	off := uint32(0x10000 + (12*64+12)*2)
	if v := r.dramRead16(off); v != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("prim-depth pixel = %#04x, want 0xFFFF (near wins)", v)
	}
	// Stored z at that pixel: z18 = primZ << 2.
	z, _ := r.readZ(12, 12)
	if z != 0x20000 {
		t.Fatalf("stored z = %#x, want 0x20000", z)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	r, dram := newTestRDP()
	runList(r, dram, 0x8000, []uint64{
		cmdWord(CmdSetColorImg, uint64(FmtRGBA)<<53|uint64(Size16)<<51|uint64(63)<<32|0x10000),
		cmdWord(CmdSetOtherMode, omWord(1, 0)),
		cmdWord(CmdSetPrimColor, 0x30<<40|0x40<<32|0x11223344),
		cmdWord(CmdSetTile, 0),
	})
	buf := make([]byte, r.SerializeSize())
	n := r.Serialize(buf)
	if n != r.SerializeSize() {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d, size says %d", n, r.SerializeSize())
	}
	r2, _ := newTestRDP()
	if err := r2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if r2.colorImg != r.colorImg || r2.primColor != r.primColor {
		t.Fatalf("round trip mismatch: %+v vs %+v", r2.colorImg, r.colorImg)
	}
	buf2 := make([]byte, r2.SerializeSize())
	r2.Serialize(buf2)
	for i := range buf {
		if buf[i] != buf2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("state byte %d differs after round trip", i)
		}
	}
	if err := r2.Deserialize(buf[:10]); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("short state accepted")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/rdp/render.go ====================

package rdp

// The rasterizer and the per-pixel pipeline: combiner,
// blender, z test, coverage bookkeeping, and the color
// and depth image accesses in RDRAM.
//
// Model notes (all stated in the README as well):
//   - Y coordinates are 11.2 fixed point, so the
//     rasterizer is exact at quarter-pixel steps. Edge
//     X positions and slopes are 16.16.
//   - The given XH and XM edge positions sit at the
//     scanline above the first rendered one; the major
//     and upper minor edges step once before the first
//     rendered line. XL is given at the first scanline
//     at or below the mid vertex and steps after each
//     line from there; the mid line itself belongs to
//     the lower edge.
//   - Attributes (shade, texture, z) are evaluated with
//     the exact plane equations anchored at the top
//     vertex, using the command's Dx and Dy derivatives
//     (De is then implied; hardware steps De along the
//     major edge and gets the same plane).
//   - Coverage comes from horizontal fractional
//     coverage in eighths; vertical coverage is treated
//     as full because edges are line-snapped in this
//     model.
//   - Depth: internal z is 18-bit (z18). The stored
//     RDRAM word holds (z18 >> 2) in the high 14 bits
//     and a 2-bit dz code; the code decodes through
//     the table {16, 64, 256, 1024} in z18 units. That
//     dz compression is exact at only those four
//     magnitudes (documented approximation).

// frag carries one rasterized fragment into the pixel
// pipeline.
type frag struct {
	x, y int
	cvg  int // coverage 0..8

	shade RGBA

	texS, texT int32 // texture position, 1/32 texel units (pre-shift)
	lodLevel   int
	lodFrac    int // 0..255
	tile       int

	z  int32 // z18
	dz int32 // dz in z18 units

	keyScale int // chroma-key scale 0..255, valid when keyEn
}

// scissorYOK reports whether a line passes the field
// scissor rule.
func (r *RDP) inScissorY(y int) bool {
	if !r.sciField {
		return true
	}
	return (y&1 != 0) == r.sciOdd
}

// inScissor reports whether (x, y) is inside the
// scissor box. Coordinates in the box are 10.2; pixel
// bounds are [XH>>2, XL>>2) by [YH>>2, YL>>2).
func (r *RDP) inScissor(x, y int) bool {
	return x >= r.sciX0>>2 && x < r.sciX1>>2 &&
		y >= r.sciY0>>2 && y < r.sciY1>>2 && r.inScissorY(y)
}

// plot runs the full per-pixel pipeline for one
// fragment. fillMode writes the fill color directly
// (already handled by writeFillPixel); plot handles the
// 1-cycle, 2-cycle, and copy cycle types.
func (r *RDP) plot(f *frag) {
	if !r.inScissor(f.x, f.y) {
		return
	}
	ct := r.omCycleType()
	if ct == 3 { // fill
		r.writeFillPixel(f.x, f.y)
		return
	}

	// Texture fetch. texel0 uses the tile selected by
	// the LOD level when texture LOD is on; texel1 is
	// the next descriptor, fetched for 2-cycle mode.
	var tex0, tex1 RGBA
	needTex := f.tile >= 0
	if needTex {
		tile0 := f.tile
		if r.omTexLOD() {
			tile0 += f.lodLevel
			if tile0 > 7 {
				tile0 = 7
			}
		}
		t0 := r.tiles[tile0]
		tex0 = r.fetchFiltered(tile0,
			f.texS>>uint(t0.ShiftS), f.texT>>uint(t0.ShiftT),
			r.omBiLerp0())
		if ct == 1 {
			tile1 := tile0 + 1
			if tile1 > 7 {
				tile1 = 7
			}
			t1 := r.tiles[tile1]
			tex1 = r.fetchFiltered(tile1,
				f.texS>>uint(t1.ShiftS), f.texT>>uint(t1.ShiftT),
				r.omBiLerp1())
		}
	}

	if ct == 2 { // copy mode: texel straight to memory
		if r.omAlphaCompare() && int(tex0.A) < r.alphaThreshold(f) {
			return
		}
		r.writeColor(f.x, f.y, tex0, 8)
		return
	}

	// Chroma key: the filtered texel's alpha is replaced
	// by the key result, which also feeds KEYSCALE.
	if r.omKeyEn() && needTex {
		ka := r.keyAlpha(tex0)
		tex0.A = ka
		f.keyScale = int(ka)
	}

	cyc0, cyc1 := r.combine(f, tex0, tex1)
	out := cyc0
	if ct == 1 {
		out = cyc1
	}

	// Alpha compare discards under the blend color
	// alpha (or the dither value when alpha dither is
	// the noise mode).
	if r.omAlphaCompare() && int(out.A) < r.alphaThreshold(f) {
		return
	}

	// Z test.
	zPass := true
	var zPix, dzPix int32
	if r.omZSourcePrim() {
		zPix = int32(r.primZ) << 2
		dzPix = int32(r.primDZ) << 2
		if dzPix > 0x3FFFF {
			dzPix = 0x3FFFF
		}
	} else {
		zPix = f.z
		dzPix = f.dz
	}
	if r.omZCompare() {
		zOld, _ := r.readZ(f.x, f.y)
		switch r.omZMode() {
		case 0: // opaque
			zPass = zPix < zOld
		case 1, 3: // interpenetrating, decal
			zPass = zPix <= zOld+dzPix
		case 2: // transparent
			zPass = zPix < zOld
		}
	}
	if !zPass {
		return
	}

	// Read the destination.
	mem, memCvg := r.readColor(f.x, f.y)

	// Pixel alpha after the coverage adjustments the
	// blender sees.
	adjAlpha := func(c RGBA) int {
		a := int(c.A)
		if r.omCvgTimesAlpha() {
			a = a * f.cvg / 8
		} else if r.omAlphaCvgSel() {
			a = f.cvg * 255 / 8
		}
		return a
	}

	final := out
	if r.omImageRead() || r.omForceBlend() {
		passes := 1
		if ct == 1 {
			passes = 2
		}
		cur := mem
		curCvg := memCvg
		cycleCols := [2]RGBA{cyc0, cyc1}
		for p := 0; p < passes; p++ {
			pc := cycleCols[p]
			if p == 1 {
				// Second blend cycle: memory is the
				// first pass result with full coverage.
				curCvg = 8
			}
			final = r.blendPass(p, pc, adjAlpha(pc), cur, curCvg, f)
			cur = final
		}
	}

	// Coverage algebra at the destination.
	newCvg := combineCvg(memCvg, f.cvg, r.omCvgDest())

	colorWrite := true
	if r.omColorOnCvg() && newCvg < 8 {
		colorWrite = false // coverage only this pixel
	}
	if colorWrite {
		r.writeColor(f.x, f.y, final, newCvg)
	} else {
		r.storeCvg(f.x, f.y, newCvg)
	}

	if r.omZUpdate() {
		r.writeZ(f.x, f.y, zPix, dzPix)
	}
}

// alphaThreshold is the alpha-compare threshold for a
// fragment: the blend color alpha, or the per-pixel
// noise value when alpha dither selects noise.
func (r *RDP) alphaThreshold(f *frag) int {
	if r.omDitherAlpha() && r.omAlphaDither() == 2 {
		return int(noiseByte(f.x, f.y))
	}
	return int(r.blendColor.A)
}

// combineCvg folds incoming coverage into stored
// coverage per the cvg_dest mode.
func combineCvg(old, inc, dest int) int {
	switch dest {
	case 0: // clamp
		if old+inc > 8 {
			return 8
		}
		return old + inc
	case 1: // wrap
		return (old + inc) & 7
	case 2: // zap (full)
		return 8
	case 3: // save (unchanged)
		return old
	}
	return old + inc
}

// keyAlpha computes the chroma-key alpha for a texel
// from the Set Key registers. A channel whose width
// exceeds 1.0 (raw above 16 in s7.4) does not take part.
func (r *RDP) keyAlpha(c RGBA) uint8 {
	key := 255
	apply := func(v uint8, kc keyChan) {
		if kc.Width > 16 {
			return
		}
		diff := (int(v) - kc.Center) * kc.Scale / 255
		if diff < 0 {
			diff = -diff
		}
		ka := kc.Width*255/16 - diff
		if ka < key {
			key = ka
		}
	}
	apply(c.R, r.keyR)
	apply(c.G, keyChan{r.keyGB.WidthG, r.keyGB.CenterG, r.keyGB.ScaleG})
	apply(c.B, keyChan{r.keyGB.WidthB, r.keyGB.CenterB, r.keyGB.ScaleB})
	if key < 0 {
		key = 0
	}
	return uint8(key)
}

// combine runs the color combiner for both cycles and
// returns the two cycle outputs. In 1-cycle mode the
// second output equals the first.
func (r *RDP) combine(f *frag, tex0, tex1 RGBA) (RGBA, RGBA) {
	cw := r.combineReg
	fields := func(cycle int) (subAR, mulR, subBR, addR, subAA, mulA, subBA, addA int) {
		if cycle == 0 {
			return int((cw >> 52) & 0xF), int((cw >> 47) & 0x1F),
				int((cw >> 28) & 0xF), int((cw >> 15) & 7),
				int((cw >> 44) & 7), int((cw >> 41) & 7),
				int((cw >> 12) & 7), int((cw >> 9) & 7)
		}
		return int((cw >> 37) & 0xF), int((cw >> 32) & 0x1F),
			int((cw >> 24) & 0xF), int((cw >> 6) & 7),
			int((cw >> 21) & 7), int((cw >> 18) & 7),
			int((cw >> 3) & 7), int(cw & 7)
	}

	rgbIn := func(sel int, combined RGBA, haveCombined bool) RGBA {
		switch sel {
		case 0:
			if haveCombined {
				return combined
			}
			return RGBA{}
		case 1:
			return tex0
		case 2:
			return tex1
		case 3:
			return r.primColor
		case 4:
			return f.shade
		case 5:
			return r.envColor
		case 6:
			return RGBA{255, 255, 255, 255}
		case 7:
			n := noiseByte(f.x, f.y)
			return RGBA{n, n, n, n}
		}
		return RGBA{}
	}
	rgbMul := func(sel int, combined RGBA, haveCombined bool) RGBA {
		switch sel {
		case 0:
			if haveCombined {
				return combined
			}
			return RGBA{}
		case 1:
			return tex0
		case 2:
			return tex1
		case 3:
			return r.primColor
		case 4:
			return f.shade
		case 5:
			return r.envColor
		case 6:
			k := uint8(f.keyScale)
			return RGBA{k, k, k, k}
		case 7:
			if haveCombined {
				return gray(combined.A)
			}
			return RGBA{}
		case 8:
			return gray(tex0.A)
		case 9:
			return gray(tex1.A)
		case 10:
			return gray(r.primColor.A)
		case 11:
			return gray(f.shade.A)
		case 12:
			return gray(r.envColor.A)
		case 13:
			return gray(uint8(f.lodFrac))
		case 14:
			return gray(uint8(r.primLvlFrc))
		case 15:
			return gray(uint8(r.conv[5] << 1))
		}
		return RGBA{}
	}
	alphaIn := func(sel int, combined RGBA, haveCombined bool) int {
		switch sel {
		case 0:
			if haveCombined {
				return int(combined.A)
			}
			return 0
		case 1:
			return int(tex0.A)
		case 2:
			return int(tex1.A)
		case 3:
			return int(r.primColor.A)
		case 4:
			return int(f.shade.A)
		case 5:
			return int(r.envColor.A)
		case 6:
			return 255
		}
		return 0
	}
	alphaMul := func(sel int, combined RGBA, haveCombined bool) int {
		switch sel {
		case 0:
			return f.lodFrac
		case 1:
			return int(tex0.A)
		case 2:
			return int(tex1.A)
		case 3:
			return int(r.primColor.A)
		case 4:
			return int(f.shade.A)
		case 5:
			return int(r.envColor.A)
		case 6:
			return r.primLvlFrc
		}
		return 0
	}

	run := func(cycle int, combined RGBA, haveCombined bool) RGBA {
		subAR, mulR, subBR, addR, subAA, mulA, subBA, addA := fields(cycle)
		a := rgbIn(subAR, combined, haveCombined)
		b := rgbIn(subBR, combined, haveCombined)
		c := rgbMul(mulR, combined, haveCombined)
		d := rgbIn(addR, combined, haveCombined)
		aa := alphaIn(subAA, combined, haveCombined)
		ab := alphaIn(subBA, combined, haveCombined)
		ac := alphaMul(mulA, combined, haveCombined)
		ad := alphaIn(addA, combined, haveCombined)
		return RGBA{
			combChan(int(a.R), int(b.R), int(c.R), int(d.R)),
			combChan(int(a.G), int(b.G), int(c.G), int(d.G)),
			combChan(int(a.B), int(b.B), int(c.B), int(d.B)),
			combChan(aa, ab, ac, ad),
		}
	}

	c0 := run(0, RGBA{}, false)
	if r.omCycleType() != 1 {
		return c0, c0
	}
	c1 := run(1, c0, true)
	return c0, c1
}

// combChan is one combiner channel: clamp((A-B)*C/256
// + D, 0, 255) with floor semantics on the product.
func combChan(a, b, c, d int) uint8 {
	v := ((a-b)*c)>>8 + d
	if v < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if v > 255 {
		return 255
	}
	return uint8(v)
}

func gray(v uint8) RGBA { return RGBA{v, v, v, v} }

// blendPass runs one blender pass: out = (P*A + M*B) /
// (A + B) per channel over the mux-selected inputs.
// When A + B is zero the result is P unchanged.
func (r *RDP) blendPass(cycle int, pixel RGBA, pixelAlpha int, mem RGBA, memCvg int, f *frag) RGBA {
	selC := func(sel int) RGBA {
		switch sel {
		case 0:
			return pixel
		case 1:
			return mem
		case 2:
			return r.blendColor
		case 3:
			return r.fogColor
		}
		return RGBA{}
	}
	p := selC(r.omBlendMux(cycle, 0))
	m := selC(r.omBlendMux(cycle, 1))
	var a int
	switch r.omBlendMux(cycle, 2) {
	case 0:
		a = pixelAlpha
	case 1:
		a = int(r.fogColor.A)
	case 2:
		a = int(f.shade.A)
	case 3:
		a = 0
	}
	var b int
	switch r.omBlendMux(cycle, 3) {
	case 0:
		b = 255 - a
	case 1:
		// Memory alpha: coverage for 16-bit images,
		// the stored alpha byte for 32-bit images.
		if r.colorImg.Size == Size16 {
			b = memCvg * 255 / 8
		} else {
			b = int(mem.A)
		}
	case 2:
		b = 255
	case 3:
		b = 0
	}
	if a+b == 0 {
		return p
	}
	mix := func(pc, mc uint8) uint8 {
		return uint8((int(pc)*a + int(mc)*b) / (a + b))
	}
	return RGBA{mix(p.R, m.R), mix(p.G, m.G), mix(p.B, m.B), mix(p.A, m.A)}
}

// noiseByte is the deterministic per-pixel noise used
// by the NOISE combiner input and the noise dither
// modes, so save/restore stays bit-identical (hardware
// noise comes from a free-running counter and is not
// reproducible even there).
func noiseByte(x, y int) uint8 {
	n := uint32(x)*374761393 + uint32(y)*668265263
	n = (n ^ (n >> 13)) * 1274126177
	return uint8((n >> 16) & 0xFF)
}

// readColor reads the destination pixel of the color
// image plus its coverage.
func (r *RDP) readColor(x, y int) (RGBA, int) {
	img := r.colorImg
	addr := img.Addr + uint32(y*img.Width+x)*uint32(texelBytes2(img.Size))/2
	switch img.Size {
	case Size16:
		v := r.dramRead16(addr)
		c := expandRGBA16(v)
		cvg := 8
		if idx := int(addr / 2); idx < len(r.hidden) {
			cvg = int(r.hidden[idx])
		}
		return c, cvg
	case Size32:
		v := r.dramRead32(addr)
		c := RGBA{uint8(v >> 24), uint8(v >> 16), uint8(v >> 8), uint8(v)}
		cvg := 8
		if r.omCvgDest() != 3 {
			cvg = int(v & 7)
			if cvg == 7 {
				cvg = 8
			}
		}
		return c, cvg
	case Size8:
		v := r.dramByte(addr)
		cvg := 8
		if idx := int(addr / 2); idx < len(r.hidden) {
			cvg = int(r.hidden[idx])
		}
		return RGBA{v, v, v, 255}, cvg
	}
	return RGBA{}, 8
}

// writeColor stores a pixel into the color image with
// its coverage, applying the programmed RGB dither when
// quantizing to 5-bit channels.
func (r *RDP) writeColor(x, y int, c RGBA, cvg int) {
	img := r.colorImg
	addr := img.Addr + uint32(y*img.Width+x)*uint32(texelBytes2(img.Size))/2
	switch img.Size {
	case Size16:
		d := r.ditherAdd(x, y)
		enc := func(v uint8) uint16 {
			return uint16(clamp255(int32(v)+d)) >> 3
		}
		a := uint16(0)
		if c.A >= 128 {
			a = 1
		}
		r.dramWrite16(addr, enc(c.R)<<11|enc(c.G)<<6|enc(c.B)<<1|a)
		r.storeCvg(x, y, cvg)
	case Size32:
		a := c.A
		if r.omCvgDest() != 3 {
			bits := uint8(cvg)
			if bits > 7 {
				bits = 7
			}
			a = a&^7 | bits
		}
		r.dramWrite32(addr, uint32(c.R)<<24|uint32(c.G)<<16|uint32(c.B)<<8|uint32(a))
	case Size8:
		r.dramWriteByte(addr, c.R)
		r.storeCvg(x, y, cvg)
	}
}

// storeCvg writes coverage alone (the color-on-coverage
// case and 16/8-bit pixels written by other paths).
func (r *RDP) storeCvg(x, y int, cvg int) {
	img := r.colorImg
	if img.Size == Size32 {
		addr := img.Addr + uint32(y*img.Width+x)*4
		v := r.dramRead32(addr)
		bits := uint32(cvg)
		if bits > 7 {
			bits = 7
		}
		r.dramWrite32(addr, v&^7|bits)
		return
	}
	addr := img.Addr + uint32(y*img.Width+x)*uint32(texelBytes2(img.Size))/2
	if idx := int(addr / 2); idx < len(r.hidden) {
		r.hidden[idx] = uint8(cvg)
	}
}

// writeFillPixel writes the packed fill color at one
// pixel, following the documented fill packing: for a
// 16-bit image the 32-bit fill word holds two adjacent
// pixels (even x takes the high half), for an 8-bit
// image four pixels (first pixel in the top byte), and
// for a 32-bit image the word is the pixel.
func (r *RDP) writeFillPixel(x, y int) {
	img := r.colorImg
	switch img.Size {
	case Size16:
		addr := img.Addr + uint32(y*img.Width+x)*2
		// Fill writes the full word-pair atomically in
		// hardware; here a single pixel write places
		// its half from the fill word, and r.fillSpan
		// covers both halves across the span.
		var v uint16
		if x%2 == 0 {
			v = uint16(r.fillColor >> 16)
		} else {
			v = uint16(r.fillColor)
		}
		r.dramWrite16(addr, v)
		if idx := int(addr / 2); idx < len(r.hidden) {
			r.hidden[idx] = 8
		}
	case Size32:
		addr := img.Addr + uint32(y*img.Width+x)*4
		r.dramWrite32(addr, r.fillColor)
	case Size8:
		addr := img.Addr + uint32(y*img.Width+x)
		shift := uint(24 - 8*(x%4))
		r.dramWriteByte(addr, byte(r.fillColor>>shift))
		if idx := int(addr / 2); idx < len(r.hidden) {
			r.hidden[idx] = 8
		}
	}
}

// ditherAdd returns the dither offset (in 8-bit channel
// units, 0..7 range scaled) for the RGB dither mode at
// a pixel: magic-square matrix for mode 0, Bayer for
// mode 1, noise for mode 2, none for mode 3. The offset
// is added before the 8 to 5 bit truncation by the
// caller. Only applied to 16-bit image writes.
func (r *RDP) ditherAdd(x, y int) int32 {
	switch r.omRGBDither() {
	case 0:
		return int32(magicSquare[y&3][x&3]) >> 2 // 0..15 -> 0..3
	case 1:
		return int32(bayer4[y&3][x&3]) >> 2
	case 2:
		return int32(noiseByte(x, y) >> 6) // 0..3
	}
	return 0
}

var bayer4 = [4][4]uint8{
	{0, 8, 2, 10},
	{12, 4, 14, 6},
	{3, 11, 1, 9},
	{15, 7, 13, 5},
}

var magicSquare = [4][4]uint8{
	{0, 14, 3, 13},
	{11, 5, 8, 6},
	{12, 2, 15, 1},
	{7, 9, 4, 10},
}

// dzTable decodes the 2-bit stored dz code to z18
// units.
var dzTable = [4]int32{16, 64, 256, 1024}

// readZ reads the stored depth at a pixel: the internal
// 18-bit z and the stored dz (decoded).
func (r *RDP) readZ(x, y int) (int32, int32) {
	addr := r.zAddr + uint32(y*r.colorImg.Width+x)*2
	w := r.dramRead16(addr)
	z := int32(w&0xFFFC) << 2
	return z, dzTable[w&3]
}

// writeZ stores a pixel depth with its dz compressed
// to the 2-bit code (the smallest code whose value is
// at least the dz, or the largest code).
func (r *RDP) writeZ(x, y int, z, dz int32) {
	addr := r.zAddr + uint32(y*r.colorImg.Width+x)*2
	code := 3
	for i, tv := range dzTable {
		if dz <= tv {
			code = i
			break
		}
	}
	w := uint16((z >> 2) & 0xFFFC)
	r.dramWrite16(addr, w|uint16(code))
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/rdp/tmem.go ====================

package rdp

// TMEM loads and texture sampling. TMEM is 4 KB,
// addressed in 64-bit words (0..511). The documented
// odd-line 32-bit half interleave is a TMEM banking
// artifact that only matters to software that pokes
// texture memory and expects the pattern back; loads
// here write the logical texel layout and fetches read
// the same layout, so Load Tile and Load Block agree
// and sampling is exact for normal images. That
// simplification is stated in the README.

// texelBytes returns the byte width of one texel of a
// size class, as a numerator over 2 (4-bit counts half).
func texelBytes2(size int) int {
	switch size {
	case Size4:
		return 1 // 1/2 byte
	case Size8:
		return 2 // 1 byte
	case Size16:
		return 4 // 2 bytes
	case Size32:
		return 8 // 4 bytes
	}
	return 2
}

// imgByteOffset converts a texel index in a line-major
// image of the given width (pixels) and size to a byte
// offset.
func imgByteOffset(idx, size int) int {
	return idx * texelBytes2(size) / 2
}

// loadBlock implements Load Block. The image span of
// (SH - SL + 1) texels starting at (SL, TL) in the
// texture image is copied into TMEM at the tile base.
// DxT (unsigned 1.11) is the amount the source T
// coordinate advances per 8 TMEM bytes written; each
// time the accumulated T crosses an integer, the source
// moves to the next image line at the same SL. DxT is
// programmed as the ceiling of the true reciprocal of
// the line length in 64-bit words for full-width loads,
// which makes the walk land line-exact.
func (r *RDP) loadBlock(tileIdx, dxt int) {
	t := &r.tiles[tileIdx]
	img := r.texImg
	if img.Width <= 0 {
		return
	}
	texels := t.SH - t.SL + 1
	if texels <= 0 {
		return
	}
	totalBytes := texels * texelBytes2(img.Size) / 2
	lineBytes := imgByteOffset(img.Width, img.Size)
	srcRow := imgByteOffset(t.TL*img.Width+t.SL, img.Size)
	dst := t.TMem * 8
	tAcc := 0
	srcInRow := 0 // bytes consumed in the current source row
	for written := 0; written < totalBytes; written += 8 {
		n := totalBytes - written
		if n > 8 {
			n = 8
		}
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			r.tmem[(dst+written+i)&0xFFF] =
				r.dramByte(img.Addr + uint32(srcRow+srcInRow+i))
		}
		srcInRow += 8
		if dxt > 0 {
			tAcc += dxt
			if tAcc >= 0x800 {
				tAcc -= 0x800
				srcRow += lineBytes
				srcInRow = 0
			}
		}
	}
}

// loadTile implements Load Tile: the rectangle of the
// texture image at the tile's SL/TL..SH/TH (10.2 units,
// so texel bounds are the raw values shifted right by
// 2) is copied into TMEM in the tile's own format and
// size, laid out by the tile's line stride.
func (r *RDP) loadTile(tileIdx int) {
	t := &r.tiles[tileIdx]
	img := r.texImg
	sl, tl := t.SL>>2, t.TL>>2
	sh, th := t.SH>>2, t.TH>>2
	sameFormat := t.Format == img.Format && t.Size == img.Size
	for ty := tl; ty <= th; ty++ {
		for sx := sl; sx <= sh; sx++ {
			if sameFormat {
				// The normal case: a straight texel move.
				r.writeTMEMRaw(t, sx-sl, ty-tl,
					r.readImageRaw(img, sx, ty))
			} else {
				v := r.readImageTexel(img, sx, ty)
				r.writeTMEMTexel(t, sx-sl, ty-tl, v)
			}
		}
	}
}

// loadTLUT implements Load TLUT. The palette entries
// starting at (SL>>2, TL>>2) in the texture image are
// stored in TMEM at the tile base. Following the
// documented quadrication, each 16-bit entry occupies
// a full 64-bit word with the value repeated in all
// four halfword slots; fetches read the first slot.
func (r *RDP) loadTLUT(tileIdx int) {
	t := &r.tiles[tileIdx]
	img := r.texImg
	count := (t.SH >> 2) - (t.SL >> 2) + 1
	if count <= 0 {
		return
	}
	base := imgByteOffset((t.TL>>2)*img.Width+(t.SL>>2), img.Size)
	dst := t.TMem * 8
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		entry := r.dramRead16(img.Addr + uint32(base+i*2))
		for k := 0; k < 4; k++ {
			off := (dst + i*8 + k*2) & 0xFFF
			r.tmem[off] = byte(entry >> 8)
			r.tmem[off+1] = byte(entry)
		}
	}
}

// readImageTexel reads one texel of an image in RDRAM
// and returns it expanded to RGBA in the image's own
// format and size, without TLUT lookup (a CI image
// expands its index through the palette only on the
// sampling path) and with YUV kept in component form.
func (r *RDP) readImageTexel(img Image, x, y int) RGBA {
	return r.expandSample(img.Format, img.Size,
		r.readImageRaw(img, x, y), 0, 0, true)
}

// readImageRaw reads the packed texel bits of one image
// texel: for 4-bit sizes the low bits hold the texel
// value, for 8-bit the byte, for 16-bit the halfword,
// for 32-bit the word.
func (r *RDP) readImageRaw(img Image, x, y int) uint32 {
	off := imgByteOffset(y*img.Width+x, img.Size)
	switch img.Size {
	case Size4:
		b := r.dramByte(img.Addr + uint32(off))
		if (y*img.Width+x)%2 == 0 {
			return uint32(b >> 4)
		}
		return uint32(b & 0xF)
	case Size8:
		return uint32(r.dramByte(img.Addr + uint32(off)))
	case Size16:
		return uint32(r.dramRead16(img.Addr + uint32(off)))
	case Size32:
		return r.dramRead32(img.Addr + uint32(off))
	}
	return 0
}

// writeTMEMTexel stores one texel (already expanded to
// RGBA from its source format) into TMEM through the
// tile's format and size packing, at tile-relative
// coordinates.
func (r *RDP) writeTMEMTexel(t *Tile, x, y int, c RGBA) {
	v := packTexel(t.Format, t.Size, c)
	r.writeTMEMRaw(t, x, y, v)
}

// writeTMEMRaw packs a raw texel value into TMEM at
// tile-relative coordinates.
func (r *RDP) writeTMEMRaw(t *Tile, x, y int, v uint32) {
	switch t.Size {
	case Size4:
		idx := y*(t.Line*16) + x
		off := t.TMem*8 + idx/2
		b := r.tmem[off&0xFFF]
		if idx%2 == 0 {
			b = b&0x0F | byte(v)<<4
		} else {
			b = b&0xF0 | byte(v&0xF)
		}
		r.tmem[off&0xFFF] = b
	case Size8:
		off := t.TMem*8 + y*(t.Line*8) + x
		r.tmem[off&0xFFF] = byte(v)
	case Size16:
		off := t.TMem*8 + (y*(t.Line*4)+x)*2
		r.tmem[off&0xFFF] = byte(v >> 8)
		r.tmem[(off+1)&0xFFF] = byte(v)
	case Size32:
		off := t.TMem*8 + (y*(t.Line*2)+x)*4
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			r.tmem[(off+i)&0xFFF] = byte(v >> uint(24-8*i))
		}
	}
}

// readTMEMRaw reads a raw texel value from TMEM at
// tile-relative coordinates.
func (r *RDP) readTMEMRaw(t *Tile, x, y int) uint32 {
	switch t.Size {
	case Size4:
		idx := y*(t.Line*16) + x
		b := r.tmem[(t.TMem*8+idx/2)&0xFFF]
		if idx%2 == 0 {
			return uint32(b >> 4)
		}
		return uint32(b & 0xF)
	case Size8:
		return uint32(r.tmem[(t.TMem*8+y*(t.Line*8)+x)&0xFFF])
	case Size16:
		off := t.TMem*8 + (y*(t.Line*4)+x)*2
		return uint32(r.tmem[off&0xFFF])<<8 | uint32(r.tmem[(off+1)&0xFFF])
	case Size32:
		off := t.TMem*8 + (y*(t.Line*2)+x)*4
		var v uint32
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			v = v<<8 | uint32(r.tmem[(off+i)&0xFFF])
		}
		return v
	}
	return 0
}

// packTexel quantizes an RGBA color back to a format
// and size's packed bits (used by Load Tile when the
// source format differs, and by 32-bit image writes).
func packTexel(format, size int, c RGBA) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case Size32:
		return uint32(c.R)<<24 | uint32(c.G)<<16 | uint32(c.B)<<8 | uint32(c.A)
	case Size16:
		if format == FmtIA {
			return uint32(c.R)<<8 | uint32(c.A)
		}
		a := uint32(0)
		if c.A >= 128 {
			a = 1
		}
		return uint32(c.R>>3)<<11 | uint32(c.G>>3)<<6 | uint32(c.B>>3)<<1 | a
	case Size8:
		if format == FmtIA {
			return uint32(c.R&0xF0) | uint32(c.A>>4)
		}
		return uint32(c.R)
	case Size4:
		if format == FmtIA {
			return uint32(c.R>>5)<<1 | uint32(c.A>>7)
		}
		return uint32(c.R >> 4)
	}
	return 0
}

// expandSample expands a raw TMEM or image texel to
// sampling path, including TLUT lookup and the YUV
// conversion. yuvPartner carries the paired texel's
// raw value for YUV chroma sharing when needed.
func (r *RDP) expandSample(format, size int, raw uint32, palette int, partner uint32, forLoad bool) RGBA {
	switch format {
	case FmtRGBA:
		if size == Size16 {
			return expandRGBA16(uint16(raw))
		}
		return RGBA{uint8(raw >> 24), uint8(raw >> 16), uint8(raw >> 8), uint8(raw)}
	case FmtYUV:
		// 16-bit YUYV pairs: even texel holds Y0 in the
		// high byte, odd holds Y1; U and V are shared.
		y := uint8(raw >> 8)
		u := uint8(raw)
		v := uint8(partner)
		if forLoad {
			return RGBA{y, u, v, 255}
		}
		return r.convertYUV(y, u, v)
	case FmtCI:
		idx := raw
		if !r.omEnTLUT() {
			// Index shown as intensity (games always
			// enable the TLUT for CI; this keeps the
			// result defined).
			g := uint8(idx)
			if size == Size4 {
				g = uint8(idx * 17)
			}
			return RGBA{g, g, g, 255}
		}
		var entryAddr int
		if size == Size4 {
			entryAddr = 2048 + (palette*16+int(idx))*8
		} else {
			entryAddr = 2048 + int(idx)*8
		}
		entry := uint16(r.tmem[entryAddr&0xFFF])<<8 | uint16(r.tmem[(entryAddr+1)&0xFFF])
		if r.omTLUTType() == 1 {
			return RGBA{uint8(entry >> 8), uint8(entry >> 8), uint8(entry >> 8), uint8(entry)}
		}
		return expandRGBA16(entry)
	case FmtIA:
		switch size {
		case Size4:
			i3 := (raw >> 1) & 7
			inten := uint8((i3 << 5) | (i3 << 2) | (i3 >> 1))
			a := uint8(0)
			if raw&1 != 0 {
				a = 255
			}
			return RGBA{inten, inten, inten, a}
		case Size8:
			i := uint8((raw >> 4) * 17)
			a := uint8((raw & 0xF) * 17)
			return RGBA{i, i, i, a}
		case Size16:
			i := uint8(raw >> 8)
			return RGBA{i, i, i, uint8(raw)}
		}
	case FmtI:
		if size == Size4 {
			g := uint8(raw * 17)
			return RGBA{g, g, g, 255}
		}
		g := uint8(raw)
		return RGBA{g, g, g, 255}
	}
	return RGBA{}
}

// expandRGBA16 expands an RGBA5551 halfword.
func expandRGBA16(v uint16) RGBA {
	r5 := uint8((v >> 11) & 31)
	g5 := uint8((v >> 6) & 31)
	b5 := uint8((v >> 1) & 31)
	a := uint8(0)
	if v&1 != 0 {
		a = 255
	}
	return RGBA{(r5 << 3) | (r5 >> 2), (g5 << 3) | (g5 >> 2), (b5 << 3) | (b5 >> 2), a}
}

// convertYUV applies the documented two-stage YUV to
// RGB conversion: the texture-filter stage forms
// R' = Y + K0*V, G' = Y + K1*U + K2*V, B' = Y + K3*U
// with U and V centered on zero, and the combiner
// stage forms out = (in - K4) * K5 + in per channel.
// The K coefficients are signed 1.7 fixed point.
func (r *RDP) convertYUV(y, u, v uint8) RGBA {
	uc := int32(u) - 128
	vc := int32(v) - 128
	yi := int32(y)
	rp := yi + (r.conv[0]*vc)>>7
	gp := yi + (r.conv[1]*uc)>>7 + (r.conv[2]*vc)>>7
	bp := yi + (r.conv[3]*uc)>>7
	stage2 := func(c int32) uint8 {
		o := ((c - r.conv[4]) * r.conv[5]) >> 7
		return clamp255(c + o)
	}
	return RGBA{stage2(rp), stage2(gp), stage2(bp), 255}
}

// clamp255 clamps an int32 to the byte range.
func clamp255(v int32) uint8 {
	if v < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if v > 255 {
		return 255
	}
	return uint8(v)
}

// wrapCoord applies one axis' addressing mode to an
// integer texel coordinate. With a zero mask the
// coordinate clamps to the tile's own coordinate range
// [lo, hi] (the Set Tile Size bounds). With a mask the
// coordinate wraps modulo 2^mask, mirror flips alternate
// blocks, and the clamp bit (when set) clamps the
// result to [lo, hi] afterwards.
func wrapCoord(c, mask int, clampEn, mirrorEn bool, lo, hi int) int {
	if mask == 0 {
		if c < lo {
			return lo
		}
		if c > hi {
			return hi
		}
		return c
	}
	span := 1 << uint(mask)
	v := c & (span - 1)
	if mirrorEn && (c&(span)) != 0 {
		v = span - 1 - v
	}
	if clampEn {
		if v < lo {
			v = lo
		}
		if v > hi {
			v = hi
		}
	}
	return v
}

// fetchTexel reads one fully expanded texel of the tile
// at possibly out-of-range integer coordinates, applying
// the tile's wrap and mirror modes. This is the nearest
// (point) fetch; the filter builds on it.
func (r *RDP) fetchTexel(tileIdx, s, t int) RGBA {
	tile := &r.tiles[tileIdx]
	lo := tile.SL >> 2
	hi := tile.SH >> 2
	s = wrapCoord(s, tile.MaskS, tile.ClampS, tile.MirrorS, lo, hi)
	lo = tile.TL >> 2
	hi = tile.TH >> 2
	t = wrapCoord(t, tile.MaskT, tile.ClampT, tile.MirrorT, lo, hi)
	// Tile-relative coordinates into TMEM.
	rs := s - (tile.SL >> 2)
	rt := t - (tile.TL >> 2)

	if tile.Format == FmtYUV {
		// Chroma is shared across the horizontal pair:
		// the even texel's raw holds Y0,U and the odd
		// texel's holds Y1,V in the 16-bit packing used
		// here (Y in the high byte; the second byte of
		// the pair word is U for even, V for odd).
		evenRaw := r.readTMEMRaw(tile, rs&^1, rt)
		oddRaw := r.readTMEMRaw(tile, rs|1, rt)
		y := uint8(evenRaw >> 8)
		if rs&1 != 0 {
			y = uint8(oddRaw >> 8)
		}
		return r.expandSample(FmtYUV, tile.Size,
			uint32(y)<<8|uint32(uint8(evenRaw)), tile.Palette,
			uint32(uint8(oddRaw)), false)
	}
	raw := r.readTMEMRaw(tile, rs, rt)
	return r.expandSample(tile.Format, tile.Size, raw, tile.Palette, 0, false)
}

// fetchFiltered samples a tile at a position given in
// 1/32 texel units (already shifted by the tile's shift
// fields by the caller). sampleType selects the hardware
// 2x2 mode; bilerp selects whether the filter runs the
// three-texel triangle blend for this pass or the
// color-convert operation (modeled as point sampling
// for non-YUV formats; YUV conversion happens in the
// fetch itself).
func (r *RDP) fetchFiltered(tileIdx int, sPos, tPos int32, bilerp bool) RGBA {
	if r.omSampleType() == 0 || !bilerp || r.omCycleType() == 3 {
		return r.fetchTexel(tileIdx, floorDiv32(sPos), floorDiv32(tPos))
	}
	// Three-texel triangle filter: the 2x2 block around
	// the sample center contributes its three texels on
	// the sample's side of the diagonal, weighted by
	// the fractional position (in 1/32 units).
	s0 := floorDiv32(sPos)
	t0 := floorDiv32(tPos)
	fx := int(sPos - int32(s0)*32)
	fy := int(tPos - int32(t0)*32)
	p00 := r.fetchTexel(tileIdx, s0, t0)
	p10 := r.fetchTexel(tileIdx, s0+1, t0)
	p01 := r.fetchTexel(tileIdx, s0, t0+1)
	p11 := r.fetchTexel(tileIdx, s0+1, t0+1)
	blend3 := func(w00, w10, w01, w11 int, get func(RGBA) uint8) uint8 {
		sum := w00*int(get(p00)) + w10*int(get(p10)) +
			w01*int(get(p01)) + w11*int(get(p11))
		return uint8((sum + 16) >> 5)
	}
	if fx+fy <= 32 {
		return RGBA{
			blend3(32-fx-fy, fx, fy, 0, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.R }),
			blend3(32-fx-fy, fx, fy, 0, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.G }),
			blend3(32-fx-fy, fx, fy, 0, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.B }),
			blend3(32-fx-fy, fx, fy, 0, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.A }),
		}
	}
	return RGBA{
		blend3(0, 32-fy, 32-fx, fx+fy-32, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.R }),
		blend3(0, 32-fy, 32-fx, fx+fy-32, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.G }),
		blend3(0, 32-fy, 32-fx, fx+fy-32, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.B }),
		blend3(0, 32-fy, 32-fx, fx+fy-32, func(c RGBA) uint8 { return c.A }),
	}
}

// floorDiv32 floors a 1/32-unit position to its texel.
func floorDiv32(v int32) int {
	if v >= 0 {
		return int(v >> 5)
	}
	return int(-(((-v) + 31) >> 5))
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/system/boot.go ====================

package system

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/chips/r4300"
)

// The HLE boot (slice N64-4). This core contains no PIF
// boot ROM and no CIC code: the boot below is an
// original reimplementation of the documented process
// (n64brew PIF-NUS "Console startup" and Initial
// Program Load pages), reduced to the effects the rest
// of the chain depends on:
//
//   - The CIC family (detected from the ROM's own boot
//     area by the cart package, or set with SetCIC, or
//     the 6102 default) selects the documented seed.
//   - The IPL3 checksum is computed over the ROM's own
//     bytes (0x1000..0x101000, the published algorithm)
//     and compared with the header words at 0x10/0x14.
//     The result is reported through BootChecksumOK and
//     never enforced: like common emulators, boot
//     proceeds either way.
//   - The PIF's side of the exchange (the CIC seed
//     handshake and the IPL2 checksum verification) is
//     modeled as passed: PIF RAM carries the documented
//     post-boot state (boot info word at 0x24 with the
//     region and both seeds, command byte 0x80 up),
//     without reproducing the PIF ROM's challenge math.
//   - The ROM's first 0x1000 bytes (header + IPL3) are
//     placed in RSP DMEM exactly as IPL2 leaves them,
//     and the CPU starts at the documented IPL3 entry
//     0xA4000040 with the documented entry state: CP0
//     Status 0x34000000 and Config 0x0006E463 (IPL1's
//     initialization), stack at 0xA4001FF0, the IPL3
//     seed in $s6, and the TV type (NTSC = 1; this
//     core's console region is NTSC) in $s4.
//
// A ROM whose IPL3 is the genuine article therefore
// runs it on this core's CPU and RSP, the standard
// HLE-boot arrangement used by multiple emulators;
// the IPL3 then performs the documented 1 MB copy to
// the header entry address itself.

// Start resets the machine and runs the HLE boot: the
// CPU is left executing the cartridge's IPL3 from RSP
// DMEM. LoadROM alone does not boot (it leaves the
// machine at the reset vector for low-level tests).
func (s *System) Start() {
	s.Reset()
	s.boot()
}

// Booted reports whether Start has run the boot.
func (s *System) Booted() bool { return s.booted }

// BootCIC returns the CIC family the boot used (after
// detection, SetCIC, and the 6102 default resolve).
func (s *System) BootCIC() cart.CIC { return s.bootCIC }

// BootChecksum returns the IPL3 checksum words computed
// at boot over the ROM's own bytes.
func (s *System) BootChecksum() (uint32, uint32) { return s.bootCRC1, s.bootCRC2 }

// BootChecksumOK reports whether the computed IPL3
// checksum matched the header words. Boot proceeds
// regardless; this is a report, not a gate.
func (s *System) BootChecksumOK() bool { return s.bootChecksumOK }

// SetCIC overrides the CIC family for the next boot.
// Real cartridges are identified by the cart package's
// CRC32 detection over the ROM's own boot code, which
// a synthetic ROM cannot reproduce (its boot area is
// original code, not the copyrighted original), so
// tests and homebrew can name the family explicitly.
// Without detection or an override the boot defaults
// to CIC 6102, the family the large majority of
// cartridges use.
func (s *System) SetCIC(c cart.CIC) {
	s.cicOverride = c
	s.cicSet = true
}

func (s *System) boot() {
	cic := s.Cart.CIC
	if s.cicSet {
		cic = s.cicOverride
	}
	if cic == cart.CICUnknown {
		cic = cart.CIC6102
	}
	s.bootCIC = cic
	seed, _ := cart.CICSeed(cic)

	if c1, c2, ok := cart.IPL3Checksum(s.Cart.ROM, cic); ok {
		s.bootCRC1, s.bootCRC2 = c1, c2
		s.bootChecksumOK = c1 == s.Cart.CRC1 && c2 == s.Cart.CRC2
	}

	// PIF RAM post-boot state: the boot info word at
	// 0x24 carries the region (0x01 = NTSC) and the two
	// CIC seeds, and the command byte raises 0x80 to
	// signal the data is available. The exact byte
	// packing of the info word beyond its documented
	// contents (region + both seeds in this word) is
	// this core's HLE arrangement.
	p := s.Mem.PIF
	for i := range p.RAM {
		p.RAM[i] = 0
	}
	p.RAM[0x24] = 0x01 // region: NTSC
	p.RAM[0x25] = seed // IPL2 seed
	p.RAM[0x26] = seed // IPL3 seed (the same byte in every known variant)
	p.RAM[0x3F] = 0x80

	// IPL3 placement: DMEM gets the ROM's first
	// 0x1000 bytes (the header at 0x00, the boot code
	// at 0x40), as IPL2 leaves it.
	n := 0x1000
	if len(s.Cart.ROM) < n {
		n = len(s.Cart.ROM)
	}
	copy(s.RSP.DMEM[:], s.Cart.ROM[:n])

	// CPU entry state (documented on IPL3 entry).
	cpu := s.CPU
	cpu.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status] = 0x34000000
	cpu.CP0[r4300.Cp0Config] = 0x0006E463
	cpu.Reg[29] = 0xFFFFFFFFA4001FF0 // sp, top of DMEM
	cpu.Reg[22] = uint64(seed)       // $s6: IPL3 seed
	cpu.Reg[20] = 1                  // $s4: TV type, NTSC
	cpu.PC = 0xFFFFFFFFA4000040      // IPL3 entry in DMEM
	cpu.NPC = cpu.PC + 4
	s.booted = true
}

package system

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/chips/r4300"
)

// TestN64SystemtestReportOnly is a report-only harness for
// the open-source n64-systemtest homebrew ROM. It is NOT a
// gate: the ROM normally boots through the PIF/CIC process,
// which lands in slice N64-4, and the project's official
// GitHub offers no prebuilt ROM (no releases; the Rust
// source needs a MIPS toolchain to build). If a legally
// obtained build is ever placed at
// testroms/n64-systemtest.z64, this harness boots it in raw
// CPU mode (IPL3-style: the ROM image from offset 0x1000 is
// copied to RDRAM 0x400 and the CPU starts at the header
// boot address) and logs how far execution gets.
func TestN64SystemtestReportOnly(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join("..", "testroms", "n64-systemtest.z64")
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("n64-systemtest ROM not present (%v); report-only harness idle", err)
	}
	sys, err := New(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse: %v", err)
	}
	t.Logf("cart: name=%q cic=%s boot=%08x", sys.Cart.Name, sys.Cart.CIC, sys.Cart.BootAddress)
	// IPL3-style raw load: copy ROM[0x1000:] to RDRAM 0x400.
	copy(sys.Mem.RDRAM[0x400:], sys.Cart.ROM[0x1000:])
	sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status] = r4300.StatusCU0 | r4300.StatusCU1
	sys.CPU.Reg[29] = 0xFFFFFFFF803FFFF0 // stack near top of RDRAM (kseg0)
	entry := sys.Cart.BootAddress
	if entry == 0 {
		entry = 0x80000400
	}
	sys.CPU.PC = uint64(int64(int32(entry)))
	sys.CPU.NPC = sys.CPU.PC + 4
	const budget = 3000000
	steps := 0
	lastPC := sys.CPU.PC
	stall := 0
	for steps < budget {
		sys.CPU.Step()
		steps++
		if sys.CPU.PC == lastPC {
			stall++
		} else {
			stall = 0
			lastPC = sys.CPU.PC
		}
		if stall > 200000 {
			break
		}
	}
	t.Logf("ran %d steps, final PC %x, cycles %d, stall-run %d",
		steps, sys.CPU.PC, sys.CPU.Cycles, stall)
	t.Logf("cause=%08x epc=%x status=%08x",
		sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Cause], sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0EPC], sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status])
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/system/system.go ====================

// Package system wires the VR4300 CPU, the RSP, the
// RDP/VI/AI output devices, the physical memory bus,
// the PIF, and a parsed cartridge into the machine the
// libretro shell drives. Slice N64-2 adds the RSP: it
// executes from IMEM under the interleave model
// described on RunCycles. Slice N64-3 adds the RDP
// rasterizer, the VI presentation, and AI audio output.
// Slice N64-4 adds the PIF with controllers and paks,
// the cartridge save devices, the real SI DMA, and the
// HLE boot (see boot.go): Start boots a cartridge
// through its own IPL3. Bare code loaded directly into
// memory still runs without booting, which the
// low-level test harness uses.
package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/ai"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/chips/r4300"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/chips/rsp"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/pif"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/vi"
)

// Frame geometry and timing (NTSC): the VR4300 runs at
// 93.75 MHz; a 60 Hz frame budget is 1,562,500 cycles.
const (
	Width          = 320
	Height         = 240
	CyclesPerFrame = 93750000 / 60
)

// Controller button bits in the standard N64 controller
// data layout (the order the PIF reports them).
const (
	ButtonA      = 1 << 15
	ButtonB      = 1 << 14
	ButtonZ      = 1 << 13
	ButtonStart  = 1 << 12
	ButtonDUp    = 1 << 11
	ButtonDDown  = 1 << 10
	ButtonDLeft  = 1 << 9
	ButtonDRight = 1 << 8
	ButtonL      = 1 << 5
	ButtonR      = 1 << 4
	ButtonCUp    = 1 << 3
	ButtonCDown  = 1 << 2
	ButtonCLeft  = 1 << 1
	ButtonCRight = 1 << 0
)

// System is the N64 machine.
type System struct {
	CPU  *r4300.CPU
	RSP  *rsp.RSP
	Mem  *bus.Memory
	Cart *cart.Cart

	expansion bool
	pads      [4]padState
	fb        []uint32
	rspFrac   int // leftover RSP budget numerator (of 3 per CPU cycle)

	cicOverride    cart.CIC
	cicSet         bool
	bootCIC        cart.CIC
	bootCRC1       uint32
	bootCRC2       uint32
	bootChecksumOK bool
	booted         bool
}

// padState is one controller port's host-side input.
type padState struct {
	buttons uint16
	stickX  int8
	stickY  int8
}

// New builds a machine around a raw cartridge dump.
func New(rom []byte) (*System, error) {
	return NewWithOptions(rom, false)
}

// NewWithOptions builds a machine; expansion selects the
// 8 MB Expansion Pak memory size instead of the stock 4 MB.
func NewWithOptions(rom []byte, expansion bool) (*System, error) {
	s := &System{expansion: expansion, fb: make([]uint32, Width*Height)}
	for i := range s.fb {
		s.fb[i] = 0xFF000000 // opaque black
	}
	if err := s.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return s, nil
}

// LoadROM parses a cartridge dump and resets the machine
// around it. A Controller Pak starts inserted in port 1
// (the common case; games that use one work without any
// host setup). The save device starts as none: select
// one with SetSaveType.
func (s *System) LoadROM(rom []byte) error {
	c, err := cart.Parse(rom)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.Cart = c
	s.Mem = bus.New(c.ROM, s.expansion)
	s.RSP = s.Mem.RSP
	s.CPU = r4300.New(s.Mem)
	s.Mem.OnMIChange = func(active bool) {
		s.CPU.SetInterruptLine(active)
	}
	s.Mem.PIF.InsertPak(0, pif.PakMemory)
	s.pads = [4]padState{}
	s.booted = false
	s.Reset()
	return nil
}

// Reset returns the machine to its power-on state: the
// CPU resets and the RDP, VI, and AI are rebuilt fresh.
// Reset does not boot the cartridge; Start does. Test
// code that seeds PC and memory directly uses Reset's
// state, as it did before the boot existed.
func (s *System) Reset() {
	s.Mem.ResetDevices()
	s.CPU.Reset()
	s.booted = false
}

// RunCycles executes the CPU for at least the given
// number of flat cycles, interleaving the RSP. The RSP
// runs at 62.5 MHz against the CPU's 93.75 MHz, a 2:3
// ratio: after every CPU step the RSP is credited 2
// cycles per 3 CPU cycles (the fractional remainder is
// carried exactly) and runs that many instructions,
// stopping early when halted. A CPU write that sets the
// halt flag therefore stops the RSP at the next system
// step boundary.
func (s *System) RunCycles(cycles int) {
	n := 0
	for n < cycles {
		c := s.CPU.Step()
		n += c
		s.rspFrac += 2 * c
		steps := s.rspFrac / 3
		s.rspFrac -= steps * 3
		if steps > 0 {
			s.RSP.Run(steps)
		}
	}
	// The VI and AI advance on the cycles actually
	// consumed: device timing granularity is the
	// RunCycles call.
	s.Mem.VI.Advance(n)
	s.Mem.AI.Advance(n)
}

// RunFrame executes one 60 Hz frame budget of CPU cycles.
func (s *System) RunFrame() {
	s.RunCycles(CyclesPerFrame)
}

// Framebuffer returns the current video output: the VI
// presentation of the programmed color image when the
// VI is on, otherwise the blank 320x240 buffer.
func (s *System) Framebuffer() []uint32 {
	if fb, _, _ := s.Mem.VI.Present(s.Mem.RDRAM); fb != nil {
		return fb
	}
	return s.fb
}

// FramebufferSize reports the VI output geometry when
// the VI is presenting (width, height), or the blank
// buffer's 320x240 when it is not.
func (s *System) FramebufferSize() (int, int) {
	if _, w, h := s.Mem.VI.Present(s.Mem.RDRAM); w > 0 {
		return w, h
	}
	return Width, Height
}

// AudioBuffer drains the AI's produced samples:
// interleaved signed 16-bit stereo at AudioRate.
func (s *System) AudioBuffer() []int16 { return s.Mem.AI.Drain() }

// AudioRate reports the AI's current DAC sample rate in
// Hz, from the programmed DACRATE register.
func (s *System) AudioRate() int { return s.Mem.AI.SampleRate() }

// SetButtons records player 1's controller state. The
// state reaches games through the PIF on their next
// Joybus poll.
func (s *System) SetButtons(mask uint16) { s.SetButtonsPort(0, mask) }

// SetButtonsPort records one port's button state
// (port 0 is player 1).
func (s *System) SetButtonsPort(port int, mask uint16) {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return
	}
	s.pads[port].buttons = mask
	s.pushPad(port)
}

// SetStick records one port's analog stick position
// (each axis in the -80..80 hardware range; out of
// range values are clamped).
func (s *System) SetStick(port int, x, y int8) {
	if port < 0 || port > 3 {
		return
	}
	s.pads[port].stickX = clampStick(x)
	s.pads[port].stickY = clampStick(y)
	s.pushPad(port)
}

func clampStick(v int8) int8 {
	if v > 80 {
		return 80
	}
	if v < -80 {
		return -80
	}
	return v
}

func (s *System) pushPad(port int) {
	p := s.pads[port]
	s.Mem.PIF.SetController(port, p.buttons, p.stickX, p.stickY)
}

// Buttons returns player 1's recorded controller state.
func (s *System) Buttons() uint16 { return s.pads[0].buttons }

// InsertPak puts an accessory (memory pak or rumble
// pak) into a controller port; pif.PakNone removes it.
func (s *System) InsertPak(port int, kind pif.PakKind) {
	s.Mem.PIF.InsertPak(port, kind)
}

// SetSaveType selects the cartridge save device
// (EEPROM 4K/16K, SRAM, or Flash). Cartridges do not
// declare a save device in their headers and this core
// keeps no database, so the host picks: the libretro
// shell exposes it as the gon64_save_type core option
// and tests set it directly. Switching discards the
// previous device's contents.
func (s *System) SetSaveType(t cart.SaveType) { s.Mem.Saves.Configure(t) }

// SaveType returns the selected save device.
func (s *System) SaveType() cart.SaveType { return s.Mem.Saves.Type }

// SaveRAM returns the active save device's contents
// (the libretro SAVE_RAM image), or nil when no device
// is fitted.
func (s *System) SaveRAM() []byte { return s.Mem.Saves.Data() }

// SetSaveRAM loads a host save image into the active
// save device.
func (s *System) SetSaveRAM(b []byte) { s.Mem.Saves.SetData(b) }

// Title returns the cartridge name from its header.
func (s *System) Title() string {
	if s.Cart == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return s.Cart.Name
}

const stateVersion = 4

// SerializeSize reports the byte size of a serialized
// system for this machine's RDRAM configuration.
func (s *System) SerializeSize() int {
	return 2 + r4300.SerializeSize + len(s.Mem.RDRAM) + rsp.SerializeSize + 8 + 8 +
		s.Mem.DP.SerializeSize() + vi.SerializeSize + ai.SerializeSize +
		8 + pif.RAMSize + pif.StateSize + cart.SaveStateSize
}

// Serialize writes the full machine state: version byte,
// option flags, the CPU block, RDRAM, the RSP block, the
// MI interrupt and mask registers, the RSP interleave
// remainder, the RDP, VI, and AI blocks, and (version
// 4) the SI registers, PIF RAM, the PIF runtime block
// (pak storage and accessory flags), and the cartridge
// save device block.
func (s *System) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, s.SerializeSize())
	out[0] = stateVersion
	if s.expansion {
		out[1] = 1
	}
	n := s.CPU.Serialize(out[2:])
	off := 2 + n
	copy(out[off:], s.Mem.RDRAM)
	off += len(s.Mem.RDRAM)
	off += s.RSP.Serialize(out[off:])
	intr, mask := s.Mem.MIState()
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], intr)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off+4:], mask)
	off += 8
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[off:], uint64(int64(s.rspFrac)))
	off += 8
	off += s.Mem.DP.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += s.Mem.VI.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += s.Mem.AI.Serialize(out[off:])
	dramAddr, status := s.Mem.SIState()
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], dramAddr)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off+4:], status)
	off += 8
	copy(out[off:], s.Mem.PIF.RAM[:])
	off += pif.RAMSize
	s.Mem.PIF.Serialize(out[off:])
	off += pif.StateSize
	s.Mem.Saves.Serialize(out[off:])
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (s *System) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != s.SerializeSize() {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d, want %d", len(in), s.SerializeSize())
	}
	if in[0] != stateVersion {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state version %d", in[0])
	}
	if (in[1] == 1) != s.expansion {
		return errors.New("system: Expansion Pak configuration mismatch")
	}
	if err := s.CPU.Deserialize(in[2:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off := 2 + r4300.SerializeSize
	copy(s.Mem.RDRAM, in[off:])
	off += len(s.Mem.RDRAM)
	if err := s.RSP.Deserialize(in[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += rsp.SerializeSize
	intr := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
	mask := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off+4:])
	s.Mem.RestoreMI(intr, mask)
	off += 8
	s.rspFrac = int(int64(binary.BigEndian.Uint64(in[off:])))
	off += 8
	if err := s.Mem.DP.Deserialize(in[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += s.Mem.DP.SerializeSize()
	if err := s.Mem.VI.Deserialize(in[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += vi.SerializeSize
	if err := s.Mem.AI.Deserialize(in[off:]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += ai.SerializeSize
	dramAddr := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
	siStatus := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[off+4:])
	s.Mem.RestoreSI(dramAddr, siStatus)
	off += 8
	copy(s.Mem.PIF.RAM[:], in[off:])
	off += pif.RAMSize
	s.Mem.PIF.Deserialize(in[off:])
	off += pif.StateSize
	s.Mem.Saves.Deserialize(in[off:])
	s.CPU.SetInterruptLine(s.Mem.MIInterrupt())
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/system/system_n64_3_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"math"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/chips/r4300"
)

// N64-3 gates: RDP display lists (RDRAM and DMEM
// sources), VI presentation, AI audio, and mid-run
// determinism across the new devices.

func n64Cmd(op int, rest uint64) uint64 { return uint64(op)<<56 | rest }

// triWord0 builds a triangle command's first word.
func triWord0(lft bool, level, tile int, yl, ym, yh int32) uint64 {
	var w uint64
	if lft {
		w |= 1 << 55
	}
	w |= uint64(level&7) << 51
	w |= uint64(tile&7) << 48
	w |= uint64(uint32(yl)&0x3FFF) << 32
	w |= uint64(uint32(ym)&0x3FFF) << 16
	w |= uint64(uint32(yh) & 0x3FFF)
	return w
}

func edgeWord(x, dxdy int32) uint64 {
	return uint64(uint32(x))<<32 | uint64(uint32(dxdy))
}

// shadeWords builds the 8 shade coefficient words for a
// constant color plus an optional per-pixel G slope.
// Color components are 0..255 in the integer lanes.
func shadeWords(r, g, b, a int, dGdx int32) []uint64 {
	w := make([]uint64, 8)
	w[0] = uint64(r)<<48 | uint64(g)<<32 | uint64(b)<<16 | uint64(a)
	if dGdx != 0 {
		// dDx integer word: G lane holds the slope's
		// integer part (the derivative is 16.16 in units
		// of color per pixel; dGdx here is already the
		// 16.16 value with fraction 0).
		w[1] = uint64(uint32(dGdx>>16)) << 32
	}
	return w
}

// zWords builds the 2 z coefficient words for a
// constant depth given as an 18-bit value.
func zWords(z18 int32) []uint64 {
	z32 := uint32(z18) << 14
	return []uint64{uint64(z32) << 32, 0}
}

// plantTexture writes the 32x32 RGBA16 test texture at
// RDRAM 0x200000: texel (s,t) = s<<11 | t<<6 | 0x21.
func plantTexture(sys *System) {
	for t := 0; t < 32; t++ {
		for s := 0; s < 32; s++ {
			v := uint64(s<<11 | t<<6 | 0x21)
			sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x200000+(t*32+s)*2), 2, v)
		}
	}
}

// sceneList builds the gate display list: fill the
// background, clear depth, draw a shaded z triangle,
// draw a closer magenta z triangle, draw a farther
// green z triangle over the same spot (must lose), draw
// a point-sampled textured rect, FULLSYNC.
func sceneList() []uint64 {
	img320 := uint64(0) // format RGBA
	setColor := n64Cmd(0x3F, img320<<53|uint64(2)<<51|uint64(319)<<32|0x100000)
	setZ := n64Cmd(0x3E, 0x180000)
	omFill := n64Cmd(0x2F, 3<<52)
	bg := uint64(0x2221) // RGB (32,64,128) in RGBA5551 + alpha
	fillFull := n64Cmd(0x36, uint64(319*4)<<44|uint64(239*4)<<32)
	setColorZ := n64Cmd(0x3F, uint64(2)<<51|uint64(319)<<32|0x180000)

	words := []uint64{
		setColor,
		setZ,
		omFill,
		n64Cmd(0x37, bg<<16|bg), // SETFILLCOLOR
		fillFull,                // FILLRECT background
		setColorZ,
		n64Cmd(0x37, 0xFFFFFFFF),
		fillFull, // FILLRECT depth clear
		setColor, // color image back
		n64Cmd(0x3D, uint64(2)<<51|uint64(31)<<32|0x200000), // SETTIMG
		// SETTILE tile 0: RGBA16, line 8 words, tmem 0.
		n64Cmd(0x35, uint64(2)<<51|uint64(8)<<41),
		// SETTILESIZE tile 0: 0,0 .. 31,31 (10.2).
		n64Cmd(0x32, uint64(124)<<12|124),
		// LOADBLOCK tile 0: 1024 texels, dxt 256.
		n64Cmd(0x33, uint64(1023)<<12|256),
	}
	// Triangles: 1-cycle, z compare + update, no dither.
	omTri := n64Cmd(0x2F, (3<<38)|(1<<4)|(1<<5))
	combShade := uint64(0)
	{
		// (SHADE - 0) * 0 + SHADE for RGB and alpha.
		c := combineGate(4, 16, 8, 4, 4, 7, 7, 4)
		combShade = c
	}
	words = append(words, omTri, n64Cmd(0x3C, combShade))
	// Shaded triangle (40,40) (200,40) (40,160), z 0.5.
	// G is 0 at the anchor (the H vertex at x=40) with
	// a slope of one color unit per pixel, so
	// G(x) = x - 40 across the triangle.
	{
		w := []uint64{triWord0(false, 0, 0, 640, 160, 160),
			edgeWord(40<<16, 0), edgeWord(40<<16, 0),
			edgeWord(200<<16, -87381)}
		w[0] |= uint64(0x0D) << 56
		w = append(w, shadeWords(200, 0, 50, 255, 1<<16)...)
		w = append(w, zWords(0x20000)...)
		words = append(words, w...)
	}
	// Magenta triangle (80,60) (160,60) (80,140), z 0.25.
	{
		w := []uint64{triWord0(false, 0, 0, 560, 240, 240),
			edgeWord(80<<16, 0), edgeWord(80<<16, 0),
			edgeWord(160<<16, -65536)}
		w[0] |= uint64(0x0D) << 56
		w = append(w, shadeWords(255, 0, 255, 255, 0)...)
		w = append(w, zWords(0x10000)...)
		words = append(words, w...)
	}
	// Green triangle, same geometry, z 0.75 (must lose).
	{
		w := []uint64{triWord0(false, 0, 0, 560, 240, 240),
			edgeWord(80<<16, 0), edgeWord(80<<16, 0),
			edgeWord(160<<16, -65536)}
		w[0] |= uint64(0x0D) << 56
		w = append(w, shadeWords(0, 255, 0, 255, 0)...)
		w = append(w, zWords(0x30000)...)
		words = append(words, w...)
	}
	// Textured rect (220,20)-(251,51), point sampled.
	omRect := n64Cmd(0x2F, 3<<38)
	combTex := combineGate(1, 16, 8, 1, 1, 7, 7, 1)
	words = append(words, omRect, n64Cmd(0x3C, combTex))
	words = append(words,
		n64Cmd(0x24, uint64(220*4)<<44|uint64(20*4)<<32|
			uint64(252*4)<<12|uint64(52*4)),
		uint64(1024)<<16|1024, // S=0, T=0, DsDx=DtDy=1.0 (5.10)
	)
	words = append(words, n64Cmd(0x29, 0)) // SYNCFULL
	return words
}

// combineGate builds a combine register image with the
// same muxes in both cycles (mirrors the rdp test
// helper's layout).
func combineGate(subAR, mulR, subBR, addR, subAA, mulA, subBA, addA int) uint64 {
	var w uint64
	w |= uint64(subAR) << 52
	w |= uint64(mulR) << 47
	w |= uint64(subAA) << 44
	w |= uint64(mulA) << 41
	w |= uint64(subBR) << 28
	w |= uint64(addR) << 15
	w |= uint64(subBA) << 12
	w |= uint64(addA) << 9
	w |= uint64(subAR) << 37
	w |= uint64(mulR) << 32
	w |= uint64(subAA) << 21
	w |= uint64(mulA) << 18
	w |= uint64(subBR) << 24
	w |= uint64(addR) << 6
	w |= uint64(subBA) << 3
	w |= uint64(addA)
	return w
}

// plantList writes a display list into RDRAM at base.
func plantList(sys *System, base uint32, words []uint64) {
	for i, w := range words {
		sys.Mem.Write(base+uint32(i*8), 8, w)
	}
}

// programVI points the VI at the scene's color image:
// 320x240 RGBA5551, 1:1 scales, interrupt at line 2.
func programVI(sys *System) {
	w := func(off uint32, v uint64) { sys.Mem.Write(0x04400000+off, 4, v) }
	w(0x00, 2)        // CTRL: type 16-bit
	w(0x04, 0x100000) // ORIGIN
	w(0x08, 320)      // WIDTH
	w(0x0C, 2)        // V_INTR
	w(0x18, 524)      // V_TOTAL (525 half-lines)
	w(0x24, 320)      // H_VIDEO: start 0, end 320
	w(0x28, 480)      // V_VIDEO: start 0, end 480
	w(0x30, 0x400)    // X_SCALE 1.0
	w(0x34, 0x400)    // Y_SCALE 1.0
}

// dpHandler plants the DP interrupt handler at the
// general exception vector: it increments the counter
// at RDRAM 0x310 and clears the DP interrupt through
// MI_MODE bit 11.
func dpHandler(sys *System) {
	handler := []uint32{
		lui(26, 0x8000),     // k0 = RDRAM kseg0
		lw(27, 26, 0x310),   // k1 = count
		addiu(27, 27, 1),    // count++
		sw(27, 26, 0x310),   // store
		lui(26, 0xA430),     // MI page
		addiu(27, 0, 0x800), // MI_MODE bit 11: clear DP
		sw(27, 26, 0),       // MI_MODE
		0x42000018,          // eret
	}
	for i, in := range handler {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x180+i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
}

// bootSceneMachine builds a machine whose CPU program
// unmasks the DP interrupt, triggers the scene list
// through the DP registers, and polls the handler
// counter at RDRAM 0x310.
func bootSceneMachine(t *testing.T) *System {
	t.Helper()
	sys, err := New(testROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	plantTexture(sys)
	words := sceneList()
	plantList(sys, 0x40000, words)
	programVI(sys)
	dpHandler(sys)
	end := 0x40000 + len(words)*8
	prog := []uint32{
		lui(s0, 0xA430),          // 0: MI page
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x800),      // 1: DP mask set bit
		sw(t0, s0, 0xC),          // 2: MI_MASK
		lui(s0, 0xA410),          // 3: DP page
		lui(t0, 0x0004),          // 4: DP_START = 0x40000
		sw(t0, s0, 0),            // 5
		lui(t0, uint16(end>>16)), // 6
		ori(t0, t0, uint16(end)), // 7: DP_END
		sw(t0, s0, 4),            // 8: execute
		lui(t2, 0x8000),          // 9
		lw(t3, t2, 0x310),        // 10: poll count
		ii(0x04, t3, 0, 0xFFFF),  // 11: beq t3, $0, 10 (off -2)
		0,                        // 12: nop
		0x0800000D,               // 13: j self
		0,                        // 14: nop
	}
	// Fix the poll branch offset: from index 11 back to
	// index 10 is -1 in branch units... branch offset is
	// relative to the next instruction: target 10 from
	// 11 gives offset -2.
	prog[11] = ii(0x04, t3, 0, 0xFFFE)
	for i, in := range prog {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status] = r4300.StatusCU0 | r4300.StatusCU1 | 0x400 | 0x1
	sys.CPU.PC = 0xFFFFFFFF80000000
	sys.CPU.NPC = sys.CPU.PC + 4
	return sys
}

func px16(sys *System, x, y int) uint16 {
	return uint16(sys.Mem.Read(uint32(0x100000+(y*320+x)*2), 2))
}

func TestDisplayListGate(t *testing.T) {
	sys := bootSceneMachine(t)
	for i := 0; i < 20000 && sys.Mem.Read(0x310, 4) == 0; i++ {
		sys.RunCycles(10)
	}
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x310, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("DP interrupt count = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	// Background corners (fill).
	if v := px16(sys, 0, 0); v != 0x2221 {
		t.Errorf("bg (0,0) = %#04x, want 0x2221", v)
	}
	if v := px16(sys, 319, 239); v != 0x2221 {
		t.Errorf("bg (319,239) = %#04x, want 0x2221", v)
	}
	// Shaded triangle interior: (60,50): R 200, G
	// 20 (x - 40 by the gradient), B 50 -> 0xC88D.
	if v := px16(sys, 60, 50); v != 0xC88D {
		t.Errorf("shaded (60,50) = %#04x, want 0xC88D", v)
	}
	// Z winner at the overlap (100,80): magenta (the
	if v := px16(sys, 100, 80); v != 0xF83F {
		t.Errorf("overlap (100,80) = %#04x, want 0xF83F (magenta)", v)
	}
	// Textured rect probes.
	if v := px16(sys, 225, 27); v != 0x29E1 {
		t.Errorf("texrect (225,27) = %#04x, want 0x29E1", v)
	}
	if v := px16(sys, 251, 51); v != 0xFFE1 {
		t.Errorf("texrect (251,51) = %#04x, want 0xFFE1", v)
	}
	if v := px16(sys, 219, 27); v != 0x2221 {
		t.Errorf("left of rect (219,27) = %#04x, want bg 0x2221", v)
	}
	// VI presentation matches at the probe points.
	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) != 320*240 {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer size %d", len(fb))
	}
	probes := []struct {
		x, y int
		want uint32
	}{
		{0, 0, 0xFF214284},     // bg (32,64,128) expanded
		{100, 80, 0xFFFF00FF},  // magenta
		{225, 27, 0xFF293984},  // texel (5,7) expanded
		{60, 50, 0xFFCE1031},   // shaded (206,16,49)
		{319, 239, 0xFF214284}, // bg corner
	}
	for _, p := range probes {
		if got := fb[p.y*320+p.x]; got != p.want {
			t.Errorf("fb (%d,%d) = %#08x, want %#08x", p.x, p.y, got, p.want)
		}
	}
}

// TestDisplayListDMEMGate runs a short list out of RSP
// DMEM: an RSP program DMAs the list into DMEM, sets the
// XBUS/DMEM bit through its CP0 DP window, and starts
// the list from there.
func TestDisplayListDMEMGate(t *testing.T) {
	sys, err := New(testROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Short list at RDRAM 0x40000: fill the scene
	// background color and sync.
	words := []uint64{
		n64Cmd(0x3F, uint64(2)<<51|uint64(319)<<32|0x100000),
		n64Cmd(0x2F, 3<<52),
		n64Cmd(0x37, 0x22212221),
		n64Cmd(0x36, uint64(319*4)<<44|uint64(239*4)<<32),
		n64Cmd(0x29, 0),
	}
	plantList(sys, 0x40000, words)
	dpHandler(sys)
	// RSP program at RDRAM 0x2000 (11 instructions).
	rspProg := []uint32{
		mtc0(0, 0),       // MEM_ADDR = DMEM 0
		lui(t0, 0x0004),  // DRAM_ADDR = 0x40000
		mtc0(t0, 1),      //
		addiu(t0, 0, 39), // RD_LEN: 40 bytes
		mtc0(t0, 2),      // DMA fires
		addiu(t0, 0, 2),  // DP_STATUS write: set XBUS
		mtc0(t0, 11),     //
		mtc0(0, 8),       // DP_START = 0 (DMEM)
		addiu(t0, 0, 40), //
		mtc0(t0, 9),      // DP_END = 40: execute
		0x0000000D,       // break
	}
	for i, in := range rspProg {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x2000+i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	cpuProg := []uint32{
		lui(s0, 0xA404),      // SP registers
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x1000), // MEM_ADDR = IMEM
		sw(t0, s0, 0),
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x2000), // DRAM_ADDR = 0x2000
		sw(t0, s0, 4),
		addiu(t0, 0, 43), // RD_LEN: 44 bytes
		sw(t0, s0, 8),
		lui(t1, 0xA408),     // SP_PC page
		sw(0, t1, 0),        // SP_PC = 0
		lui(t1, 0xA430),     // MI page
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x800), // DP mask
		sw(t0, t1, 0xC),     // MI_MASK
		addiu(t0, 0, 1),     // clear halt only
		sw(t0, s0, 0x10),    // SP_STATUS: RSP runs
		lui(t2, 0x8000),
		lw(t3, t2, 0x310), // poll DP count
		ii(0x04, t3, 0, 0xFFFE),
		0,
		0x08000012, // j self (index 18)
		0,
	}
	for i, in := range cpuProg {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status] = r4300.StatusCU0 | r4300.StatusCU1 | 0x400 | 0x1
	sys.CPU.PC = 0xFFFFFFFF80000000
	sys.CPU.NPC = sys.CPU.PC + 4
	for i := 0; i < 40000 && sys.Mem.Read(0x310, 4) == 0; i++ {
		sys.RunCycles(10)
	}
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x310, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("DP interrupt count (DMEM list) = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if v := px16(sys, 0, 0); v != 0x2221 {
		t.Errorf("DMEM fill (0,0) = %#04x, want 0x2221", v)
	}
	if v := px16(sys, 200, 100); v != 0x2221 {
		t.Errorf("DMEM fill (200,100) = %#04x, want 0x2221", v)
	}
}

// TestAIGate plays a 1 kHz sine through the AI with two
// queued transfers and checks the measured frequency,
// the per-start interrupt count, and the LENGTH
// readback behavior.
func TestAIGate(t *testing.T) {
	sys, err := New(testROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Sine: 32 frames per period, amplitude 12000.
	// 12800 frames (400 periods) per buffer.
	plant := func(base uint32) {
		for i := 0; i < 12800; i++ {
			v := int16(12000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i%32)/32))
			sys.Mem.Write(base+uint32(i*4), 2, uint64(uint16(v)))
			sys.Mem.Write(base+uint32(i*4+2), 2, uint64(uint16(v)))
		}
	}
	plant(0x50000)
	plant(0x60000)
	// AI interrupt handler at 0x180: count at 0x318,
	// ack by writing AI STATUS.
	handler := []uint32{
		lui(26, 0x8000),
		lw(27, 26, 0x318),
		addiu(27, 27, 1),
		sw(27, 26, 0x318),
		lui(26, 0xA450), // AI page
		sw(0, 26, 0xC),  // STATUS write: ack
		0x42000018,      // eret
	}
	for i, in := range handler {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x180+i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	prog := []uint32{
		lui(s1, 0xA430),    // MI page
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x20), // AI mask set (bit 5)
		sw(t0, s1, 0xC),    // MI_MASK
		lui(s0, 0xA450),    // AI page
		addiu(t0, 0, 1520), // DACRATE (32006 Hz)
		sw(t0, s0, 0x10),
		addiu(t0, 0, 15), // BITRATE
		sw(t0, s0, 0x14),
		lui(t0, 0x0005), // DRAM_ADDR = 0x50000
		sw(t0, s0, 0),
		addiu(t0, 0, 1), // CONTROL: DMA enable
		sw(t0, s0, 8),
		ori(t0, 0, 0xC800), // LENGTH: 51200 bytes
		sw(t0, s0, 4),      // transfer 1 starts
		lui(t0, 0x0006),    // DRAM_ADDR = 0x60000
		sw(t0, s0, 0),
		ori(t0, 0, 0xC800),
		sw(t0, s0, 4), // transfer 2 queued (51200)
		0x08000012,    // j self (index 18)
		0,
	}
	for i, in := range prog {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status] = r4300.StatusCU0 | r4300.StatusCU1 | 0x400 | 0x1
	sys.CPU.PC = 0xFFFFFFFF80000000
	sys.CPU.NPC = sys.CPU.PC + 4

	// One frame in: the CPU has programmed the AI, so
	// the rate reads back, transfer 1 is playing, and
	// the LENGTH readback decreases over time.
	sys.RunFrame()
	if got := sys.AudioRate(); got != 32006 {
		t.Fatalf("AudioRate = %d, want 32006", got)
	}
	len1 := sys.Mem.Read(0x04500004, 4)
	sys.RunFrame()
	len2 := sys.Mem.Read(0x04500004, 4)
	if !(len1 > 0 && len2 < len1 && len1 <= 51200) {
		t.Fatalf("LENGTH readback not decreasing: %d then %d", len1, len2)
	}
	// Run a full second of emulated time (60 frames
	// total), draining audio as it comes.
	var samples []int16
	samples = append(samples, sys.AudioBuffer()...)
	for i := 0; i < 58; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		samples = append(samples, sys.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	frames := len(samples) / 2
	if frames < 24000 {
		t.Fatalf("only %d stereo frames from two 51200-byte transfers", frames)
	}
	// Positive-going zero crossings on the left channel.
	crossings := 0
	for i := 1; i < frames; i++ {
		if samples[2*(i-1)] < 0 && samples[2*i] >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
	}
	seconds := float64(frames) / float64(sys.AudioRate())
	freq := float64(crossings) / seconds
	if freq < 970 || freq > 1030 {
		t.Fatalf("measured sine = %.1f Hz, want about 1000", freq)
	}
	// Both transfers started: exactly 2 AI interrupts.
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x318, 4); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("AI interrupt count = %d, want 2", got)
	}
}

// TestN64_3Determinism runs the scene and audio, saves
// mid-run, restores into a fresh machine, and requires
// byte-identical continuation.
func TestN64_3Determinism(t *testing.T) {
	setup := func() *System {
		sys := bootTestMachine(t)
		plantTexture(sys)
		plantList(sys, 0x40000, sceneList())
		programVI(sys)
		// Execute the list through the bus DP page.
		sys.Mem.Write(0x04100000, 4, 0x40000)
		sys.Mem.Write(0x04100004, 4, 0x40000+uint64(len(sceneList())*8))
		// AI: a long sine transfer.
		for i := 0; i < 3200; i++ {
			v := int16(12000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i%32)/32))
			sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x50000+i*4), 2, uint64(uint16(v)))
			sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x50000+i*4+2), 2, uint64(uint16(v)))
		}
		sys.Mem.Write(0x04500010, 4, 1520)    // DACRATE
		sys.Mem.Write(0x04500014, 4, 15)      // BITRATE
		sys.Mem.Write(0x04500000, 4, 0x50000) // DRAM_ADDR
		sys.Mem.Write(0x04500008, 4, 1)       // CONTROL
		sys.Mem.Write(0x04500004, 4, 12800)   // LENGTH
		return sys
	}
	a := setup()
	a.RunCycles(200000)
	_ = a.AudioBuffer() // drain pre-save output
	state := a.Serialize()
	a.RunCycles(100000)
	audioA := a.AudioBuffer()
	stateA := a.Serialize()
	fbA := append([]uint32(nil), a.Framebuffer()...)

	b := setup()
	if err := b.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	b.RunCycles(100000)
	audioB := b.AudioBuffer()
	stateB := b.Serialize()
	fbB := append([]uint32(nil), b.Framebuffer()...)

	if !bytes.Equal(stateA, stateB) {
		t.Error("states diverged after N64-3 restore")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(int16s(audioA), int16s(audioB)) {
		t.Error("audio diverged after N64-3 restore")
	}
	if len(audioA) == 0 {
		t.Error("no audio produced in the continuation window")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(uint32s(fbA), uint32s(fbB)) {
		t.Error("framebuffers diverged after N64-3 restore")
	}
	if fbA[80*320+100] != 0xFFFF00FF {
		t.Errorf("restored framebuffer probe = %#08x, want magenta", fbA[80*320+100])
	}
}

func int16s(v []int16) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 2*len(v))
	for i, s := range v {
		out[2*i] = byte(uint16(s) >> 8)
		out[2*i+1] = byte(uint16(s))
	}
	return out
}

func uint32s(v []uint32) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 4*len(v))
	for i, s := range v {
		out[4*i] = byte(s >> 24)
		out[4*i+1] = byte(s >> 16)
		out[4*i+2] = byte(s >> 8)
		out[4*i+3] = byte(s)
	}
	return out
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/system/system_n64_4_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/chips/r4300"
)

// N64-4 swap-class gate: a synthetic ROM whose
// hand-written IPL3 runs the documented boot chain
// (PIF post-boot state, IPL3 from DMEM, game entry),
// after which the game payload exercises the RDP, the
// AI, the PIF/SI controller path, a Controller Pak
// round trip, and the cartridge EEPROM, setting
// milestone flags in RDRAM as it goes. The gate boots
// only through LoadROM + Start: no seeding.
//
// Milestone and detail words live in RDRAM at 0x300:
//   0x310 DP interrupt count    0x318 AI interrupt count
//   0x31C SI interrupt count
//   0x320..0x334 milestone flags 1..6, set in order
//   0x340/0x344 controller reply words from the poll
//   0x348 EEPROM check (0x600D ok, 0x0BADxxxx fail)
//   0x34C pak check (0x600D ok, 0x0BAD fail)
//   0x350 spin loop counter
//   0x354 ch4 info check (0x600D ok, else the word seen)
//   0x358 pak info status byte (3 while fresh, then 1)
//   0x360/0x364 video/audio wait timeout details
//   0x3F0 the CIC seed byte recorded from $s6 at entry

// Extra register numbers for the guest assembler.
const (
	at = 1
	v0 = 2
	a0 = 4
	a1 = 5
	a2 = 6
	a3 = 7
	s3 = 19
	s4 = 20
	s5 = 21
	s6 = 22
	s7 = 23
	t8 = 24
	t9 = 25
	k0 = 26
	k1 = 27
	sp = 29
	ra = 31
)

// guestAsm is a tiny two-pass MIPS assembler for the
// fixture code: instructions are emitted with the
// package's encoding helpers, and branch/jump targets
// are named and patched in finish.
type guestAsm struct {
	base   uint32
	code   []uint32
	labels map[string]int
	fix    []guestFix
}

type guestFix struct {
	at   int
	name string
	jump bool
}

func newGuestAsm(base uint32) *guestAsm {
	return &guestAsm{base: base, labels: map[string]int{}}
}

func (a *guestAsm) mark(name string) { a.labels[name] = len(a.code) }

func (a *guestAsm) emit(w uint32) { a.code = append(a.code, w) }

func (a *guestAsm) branch(op, rs, rt uint32, name string) {
	a.fix = append(a.fix, guestFix{at: len(a.code), name: name})
	a.emit(op<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16)
}

func (a *guestAsm) beq(rs, rt uint32, name string) { a.branch(0x04, rs, rt, name) }
func (a *guestAsm) bne(rs, rt uint32, name string) { a.branch(0x05, rs, rt, name) }

func (a *guestAsm) jump(op uint32, name string) {
	a.fix = append(a.fix, guestFix{at: len(a.code), name: name, jump: true})
	a.emit(op << 26)
}

func (a *guestAsm) j(name string)   { a.jump(0x02, name) }
func (a *guestAsm) jal(name string) { a.jump(0x03, name) }

func (a *guestAsm) finish() []uint32 {
	for _, f := range a.fix {
		target, ok := a.labels[f.name]
		if !ok {
			panic("guestAsm: unknown label " + f.name)
		}
		if f.jump {
			addr := (a.base + uint32(4*target)) >> 2 & 0x3FFFFFF
			a.code[f.at] |= addr
		} else {
			off := int16(target - (f.at + 1))
			a.code[f.at] |= uint32(uint16(off))
		}
	}
	return a.code
}

// sb, lbu, srl, sll, addu, and, xor encodings used by
// the fixture (the rest come from the package helpers).
func sb(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32  { return ii(0x28, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func lbu(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32 { return ii(0x24, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func andi(rt, rs uint32, imm uint16) uint32 {
	return ii(0x0C, rs, rt, imm)
}
func xori(rt, rs uint32, imm uint16) uint32 {
	return ii(0x0E, rs, rt, imm)
}
func srl(rd, rt uint32, sa uint32) uint32 { return rr(0, rt, rd, sa, 0x02) }
func sll(rd, rt uint32, sa uint32) uint32 { return rr(0, rt, rd, sa, 0x00) }
func addu(rd, rs, rt uint32) uint32       { return rr(rs, rt, rd, 0, 0x21) }
func and_(rd, rs, rt uint32) uint32       { return rr(rs, rt, rd, 0, 0x24) }
func xor_(rd, rs, rt uint32) uint32       { return rr(rs, rt, rd, 0, 0x26) }
func jr(rs uint32) uint32                 { return rr(rs, 0, 0, 0, 0x08) }

// Payload image layout (offsets within the 0x2000-byte
// payload the IPL3 copies to the entry address).
const (
	imgHandlerOff = 0x800
	imgListOff    = 0x900
	imgSineOff    = 0x1000
	imgPayloadLen = 0x2000
	imgEntryAddr  = 0x80000400
)

// engineIPL3 assembles the fixture's IPL3: it reads the
// entry address and the payload length from the header
// copy in DMEM (offsets 0x08 and 0x18), copies the
// payload from the cartridge window to the entry
// address, and jumps to it. This is the documented
// IPL3 job, in original code.
func engineIPL3() []uint32 {
	a := newGuestAsm(0xA4000040)
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0xA400))     // DMEM base
	a.emit(lw(t1, t0, 8))       // entry address
	a.emit(lw(t2, t0, 0x18))    // payload length
	a.emit(lui(t3, 0xB000))     //
	a.emit(ori(t3, t3, 0x1000)) // src = cart 0x1000 (kseg1)
	a.emit(addu(t4, t1, 0))     // dst = entry
	a.mark("copy")
	a.emit(lw(t5, t3, 0))
	a.emit(sw(t5, t4, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, t3, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(t4, t4, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -4))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "copy")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(jr(t1))
	a.emit(0)
	return a.finish()
}

// engineHandler assembles the interrupt handler the
// payload plants at RDRAM 0x180: it counts DP, AI, and
// SI interrupts (at 0x310/0x318/0x31C) and acknowledges
// each at its source.
func engineHandler() []uint32 {
	a := newGuestAsm(0x80000180)
	count := func(tag string, intrBit uint16, counterOff int16, ack func()) {
		a.emit(lui(k0, 0xA430)) // MI page
		a.emit(lw(k1, k0, 8))   // MI_INTR
		a.emit(andi(at, k1, intrBit))
		a.beq(at, 0, "next"+tag)
		a.emit(0)
		a.emit(lui(at, 0x8000))
