		a.emit(lw(k1, at, counterOff))
		a.emit(addiu(k1, k1, 1))
		a.emit(sw(k1, at, counterOff))
		ack()
		a.mark("next" + tag)
	}
	count("dp", 0x20, 0x310, func() { // DP: clear via MI_MODE bit 11
		a.emit(ori(k1, 0, 0x800))
		a.emit(sw(k1, k0, 0))
	})
	count("ai", 0x04, 0x318, func() { // AI: status write
		a.emit(lui(k0, 0xA450))
		a.emit(sw(0, k0, 0xC))
	})
	count("si", 0x02, 0x31C, func() { // SI: status write
		a.emit(lui(k0, 0xA480))
		a.emit(sw(0, k0, 0x1C))
	})
	a.emit(0x42000018) // eret
	return a.finish()
}

// engineROM builds the synthetic cartridge: header with
// the fixture payload length at 0x18, the assembled
// IPL3 at 0x40, and the payload image at 0x1000. The
// header checksum words are filled with the published
// IPL3 checksum for the 6102 family so the boot's
// report-only verification passes.
func engineROM(t *testing.T) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	handler := engineHandler()
	payload := enginePayload(t, len(handler))
	// The handler words live inside the payload image.
	for i, w := range handler {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(payload[imgHandlerOff+i*4:], w)
	}
	rom := make([]byte, 0x101000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x00:], 0x80371240)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x08:], imgEntryAddr)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x18:], imgPayloadLen)
	copy(rom[0x20:], "GON64 ENGINE TEST   ")
	rom[0x3B] = 'N'
	rom[0x3E] = 'E'
	for i, w := range engineIPL3() {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x40+i*4:], w)
	}
	copy(rom[0x1000:], payload)
	c1, c2, ok := cart.IPL3Checksum(rom, cart.CIC6102)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("checksum not computable")
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x10:], c1)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x14:], c2)
	return rom
}

// enginePayload assembles the game program and lays out
// the payload image: code at 0, the display list (the
// N64-3 gate scene) at imgListOff, the sine table at
// imgSineOff. The interrupt handler words are patched
// in by engineROM at imgHandlerOff.
func enginePayload(t *testing.T, handlerWords int) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	list := sceneList()
	listBytes := len(list) * 8
	a := newGuestAsm(imgEntryAddr)

	// ---- entry and setup ----
	a.emit(lui(sp, 0x8008))     // sp = 0x80080000
	a.emit(lui(s7, 0x8000))     // s7 = RDRAM base (kseg0)
	a.emit(sw(s6, s7, 0x3F0))   // record the CIC seed from $s6
	a.emit(lui(t8, 0x8000))     //
	a.emit(ori(t8, t8, 0x9000)) // t8 = PIF frame block 0x80009000
	// Plant the interrupt handler at 0x180.
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0x8000))
	a.emit(ori(t0, t0, 0x0400+imgHandlerOff)) // src = image handler
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x8000))
	a.emit(ori(t1, t1, 0x0180)) // dst = vector area
	a.emit(addiu(t2, 0, int16(handlerWords)))
	a.mark("copyHandler")
	a.emit(lw(t3, t0, 0))
	a.emit(sw(t3, t1, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(t1, t1, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "copyHandler")
	a.emit(0)
	// Enable interrupts: Status CU0|CU1|IM2|IE.
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0x3000))
	a.emit(ori(t0, t0, 0x0401))
	a.emit(mtc0(t0, r4300.Cp0Status))
	// MI_MASK: unmask DP, AI, SI.
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0xA430))
	a.emit(ori(t1, 0, 0x828))
	a.emit(sw(t1, t0, 0xC))
	// Milestone 0: boot reached the payload.
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x320))
	// Terminate the PIF boot (command byte bit 0x08).
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0xBFC0))
	a.emit(ori(t0, t0, 0x07FF))
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 8))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t0, 0))

	// ---- milestone 1: VI + display list ----
	a.emit(lui(s0, 0xA440)) // VI page
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 2))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x00)) // CTRL: 16-bit
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x0010))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x04)) // ORIGIN 0x100000
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 320))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x08)) // WIDTH
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 2))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x0C)) // V_INTR
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 524))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x18)) // V_TOTAL
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 320))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x24)) // H_VIDEO
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 480))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x28)) // V_VIDEO
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x400))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x30)) // X_SCALE
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x34)) // Y_SCALE
	a.emit(lui(s0, 0xA410))  // DP page
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x400+imgListOff))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0)) // DP_START
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x400+imgListOff+int16(listBytes)))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 4))   // DP_END: execute
	a.emit(lui(t2, 0x0010)) // wait cap: 1M polls
	a.mark("waitDP")
	a.emit(lw(t0, s7, 0x310))
	a.bne(t0, 0, "dpDone")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "waitDP")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x0BAD))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x360)) // timeout detail
	a.j("afterVideo")
	a.emit(0)
	a.mark("dpDone")
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 2))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x324)) // milestone 1
	a.mark("afterVideo")

	// ---- milestone 2: AI sine ----
	// Fill the buffer at 0x50000 from the 32-entry table.
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0x8005)) // dst = 0x80050000
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x8000))
	a.emit(ori(t1, t1, 0x0400+imgSineOff)) // table in image
	a.emit(addiu(t2, 0, 12800))
	a.mark("fillSine")
	a.emit(addiu(t4, 0, 31))
	a.emit(and_(t3, t2, t4))
	a.emit(sll(t3, t3, 2))
	a.emit(addu(t5, t1, t3))
	a.emit(lw(t6, t5, 0))
	a.emit(sw(t6, t0, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "fillSine")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lui(s0, 0xA450)) // AI page
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1520))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x10)) // DACRATE (32006 Hz)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 15))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x14)) // BITRATE
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x0005))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x00)) // DRAM_ADDR 0x50000
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x08)) // CONTROL: enable
	a.emit(ori(t1, 0, 0xC800))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s0, 0x04)) // LENGTH 51200: starts
	a.emit(lui(t2, 0x0010))
	a.mark("waitAI")
	a.emit(lw(t0, s7, 0x318))
	a.bne(t0, 0, "aiDone")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "waitAI")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x0BAD))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x364)) // timeout detail
	a.j("afterAudio")
	a.emit(0)
	a.mark("aiDone")
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 3))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x328)) // milestone 2
	a.mark("afterAudio")

	// ---- milestone 3: controller poll + cart info ----
	a.jal("pollPad")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lw(t0, t8, 0))
	a.emit(sw(t0, s7, 0x340)) // reply word 0 (TX/RX/cmd/button hi)
	a.emit(lw(t0, t8, 4))
	a.emit(sw(t0, s7, 0x344)) // reply word 1 (button lo/stick)
	a.emit(lw(t0, t8, 12))
	a.emit(ori(t1, 0, 0x8000))
	a.bne(t0, t1, "infoBad")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x600D))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x354))
	a.j("infoDone")
	a.emit(0)
	a.mark("infoBad")
	a.emit(sw(t0, s7, 0x354)) // the word actually seen
	a.mark("infoDone")
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 4))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x32C)) // milestone 3

	// ---- milestone 4: controller pak round trip ----
	// Info on channel 0 first: a fresh pak behaves as
	// absent until an Info reports status 3.
	a.jal("zeroFrame")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0)) // TX
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 3))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 1)) // RX
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0xFF))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 2)) // cmd info
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0x3F)) // command byte
	a.jal("siExchange")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lw(t0, t8, 4))
	a.emit(srl(t0, t0, 16))
	a.emit(andi(t0, t0, 0xFF))
	a.emit(sw(t0, s7, 0x358)) // pak info status byte
	// Write 32 pattern bytes to pak address 0x0020 (the
	// encoded address carries its checksum: 0x0035).
	a.jal("zeroFrame")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x23))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0)) // TX = 35
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 1)) // RX = 1 (the CRC)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 3))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 2)) // cmd write
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x35))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 4)) // address low byte (high is 0)
	a.emit(addiu(t2, 0, 32))
	a.emit(addu(t0, t8, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 5))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, 0, 0))
	a.mark("pakPat")
	a.emit(sll(t4, t3, 1))
	a.emit(addu(t4, t4, t3))
	a.emit(addiu(t4, t4, 1)) // value = i*3+1
	a.emit(sb(t4, t0, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, t3, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "pakPat")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0x3F))
	a.jal("siExchange")
	a.emit(0)
	// Read the block back.
	a.jal("zeroFrame")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 3))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0)) // TX = 3
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x21))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 1)) // RX = 33 (data + CRC)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 2))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 2)) // cmd read
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x35))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0x3F))
	a.jal("siExchange")
	a.emit(0)
	// Verify data against the pattern while accumulating
	// the documented Joybus CRC-8 (poly 0x85).
	a.emit(addiu(t2, 0, 32))
	a.emit(addu(t0, t8, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 5))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, 0, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(s1, 0, 0)) // crc
	a.mark("pakVerify")
	a.emit(lbu(t4, t0, 0))
	a.emit(sll(t5, t3, 1))
	a.emit(addu(t5, t5, t3))
	a.emit(addiu(t5, t5, 1))
	a.bne(t4, t5, "pakFail")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(xor_(s1, s1, t4))
	a.emit(addiu(t6, 0, 8))
	a.mark("pakCRCbit")
	a.emit(andi(t5, s1, 0x80))
	a.emit(sll(s1, s1, 1))
	a.beq(t5, 0, "pakCRCnoFold")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(xori(s1, s1, 0x85))
	a.mark("pakCRCnoFold")
	a.emit(addiu(t6, t6, -1))
	a.bne(t6, 0, "pakCRCbit")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(andi(s1, s1, 0xFF))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, t3, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "pakVerify")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lbu(t4, t8, 37)) // the CRC byte after the data
	a.bne(t4, s1, "pakFail")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x600D))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x34C))
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 5))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x330)) // milestone 4
	a.j("pakDone")
	a.emit(0)
	a.mark("pakFail")
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x0BAD))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x34C))
	a.mark("pakDone")

	// ---- milestone 5: EEPROM block round trip ----
	a.jal("zeroFrame")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x0A))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 4)) // ch4 TX = 10
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 5)) // RX = 1
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 5))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 6)) // cmd write
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 7)) // block 5
	a.emit(addiu(t2, 0, 8))
	a.emit(addu(t0, t8, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 8))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, 0, 0))
	a.mark("eePat")
	a.emit(addiu(t4, t3, 0xA0)) // value = 0xA0 + i
	a.emit(sb(t4, t0, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, t3, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "eePat")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0x3F))
	a.jal("siExchange")
	a.emit(0)
	a.jal("zeroFrame")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 2))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 4)) // TX = 2
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 8))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 5)) // RX = 8
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 4))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 6)) // cmd read
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 5))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 7)) // block 5
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0x3F))
	a.jal("siExchange")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t2, 0, 8))
	a.emit(addu(t0, t8, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 8))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, 0, 0))
	a.mark("eeVerify")
	a.emit(lbu(t4, t0, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t5, t3, 0xA0))
	a.bne(t4, t5, "eeFail")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t3, t3, 1))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "eeVerify")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 0x600D))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x348))
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 6))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x334)) // milestone 5
	a.j("eeDone")
	a.emit(0)
	a.mark("eeFail")
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x0BAD))
	a.emit(sw(t1, s7, 0x348))
	a.mark("eeDone")

	// ---- spin: count loops, keep the AI fed, and keep
	// polling the pad ----
	a.mark("spin")
	a.emit(lw(t0, s7, 0x350))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 1))
	a.emit(sw(t0, s7, 0x350))
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0xA450))
	a.emit(lw(t1, t0, 4)) // AI_LENGTH: 0 means drained
	a.bne(t1, 0, "spinPolled")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x0005))
	a.emit(sw(t1, t0, 0)) // DRAM_ADDR
	a.emit(ori(t1, 0, 0xC800))
	a.emit(sw(t1, t0, 4)) // LENGTH: restart the sine
	a.mark("spinPolled")
	a.jal("pollPad")
	a.emit(0)
	a.j("spin")
	a.emit(0)

	// ---- subroutines ----
	a.mark("zeroFrame")
	a.emit(addiu(t2, 0, 16))
	a.emit(addu(t0, t8, 0))
	a.mark("zfLoop")
	a.emit(sw(0, t0, 0))
	a.emit(addiu(t0, t0, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(t2, t2, -1))
	a.bne(t2, 0, "zfLoop")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(jr(ra))
	a.emit(0)

	a.mark("siExchange")
	a.emit(lui(t0, 0xA480)) // SI page
	a.emit(ori(t1, 0, 0x9000))
	a.emit(sw(t1, t0, 0)) // SI_DRAM_ADDR
	a.emit(lui(t1, 0x1FC0))
	a.emit(ori(t1, t1, 0x07C0)) // PIF RAM address
	a.emit(sw(t1, t0, 0x10))    // WR64B: frame to PIF (parses)
	a.emit(sw(t1, t0, 0x04))    // RD64B: execute + read back
	a.emit(jr(ra))
	a.emit(0)

	a.mark("pollPad")
	a.emit(addiu(sp, sp, -8))
	a.emit(sw(ra, sp, 4))
	a.jal("zeroFrame")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0)) // ch0 TX = 1
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 4))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 1)) // ch0 RX = 4
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 2)) // cmd: read state
	// Channels 1..3 stay zeroed (skip), channel 4 asks
	// for its info signature.
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 10)) // ch4 TX = 1
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 3))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 11)) // ch4 RX = 3
	a.emit(addiu(t1, 0, 1))
	a.emit(sb(t1, t8, 0x3F)) // command byte
	a.jal("siExchange")
	a.emit(0)
	a.emit(lw(ra, sp, 4))
	a.emit(addiu(sp, sp, 8))
	a.emit(jr(ra))
	a.emit(0)

	code := a.finish()
	if len(code)*4 > imgHandlerOff {
		t.Fatalf("payload code is %d bytes, over the %d budget", len(code)*4, imgHandlerOff)
	}
	if listBytes > imgSineOff-imgListOff {
		t.Fatalf("display list is %d bytes, over budget", listBytes)
	}
	img := make([]byte, imgPayloadLen)
	for i, w := range code {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[i*4:], w)
	}
	for i, w := range list {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(img[imgListOff+i*8:], w)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		v := int16(12000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/32))
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[imgSineOff+i*4:], uint32(uint16(v))<<16|uint32(uint16(v)))
	}
	return img
}

// TestEngineBootGate is the N64-4 swap gate. It boots
// the synthetic ROM through LoadROM + Start only, and
// asserts every milestone in order, the video and
// audio evidence, the pak and EEPROM internal checks,
// and byte-identical continuation across a mid-run
// save/restore.
func TestEngineBootGate(t *testing.T) {
	rom := engineROM(t)
	sys, err := New(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// The synthetic boot area is original code, so the
	// CRC32 detection cannot name its CIC family: the
	// boot must fall back to the documented 6102
	// default.
	if sys.Cart.CIC != cart.CICUnknown {
		t.Fatalf("synthetic CIC detected as %s (test premise broken)", sys.Cart.CIC)
	}
	sys.SetSaveType(cart.SaveEEPROM4K)
	sys.SetButtons(ButtonA | ButtonStart)
	sys.Start()

	// Post-boot PIF state, before the payload's own SI
	// traffic overwrites PIF RAM.
	pram := sys.Mem.PIFRAM()
	if pram[0x3F] != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("PIF command byte after boot = %#02x, want 0x80", pram[0x3F])
	}
	if pram[0x25] != 0x3F || pram[0x26] != 0x3F {
		t.Errorf("boot info seeds = %#02x/%#02x, want 0x3F", pram[0x25], pram[0x26])
	}
	if !sys.Booted() || sys.BootCIC() != cart.CIC6102 {
		t.Errorf("boot cic = %s, booted = %v", sys.BootCIC(), sys.Booted())
	}
	if !sys.BootChecksumOK() {
		c1, c2 := sys.BootChecksum()
		t.Errorf("IPL3 checksum report: computed %08x/%08x, header %08x/%08x",
			c1, c2, sys.Cart.CRC1, sys.Cart.CRC2)
	}
	// IPL3 sits in DMEM where IPL2 would leave it.
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x04000040, 4); got == 0 {
		t.Error("DMEM holds no IPL3 at 0x40")
	}

	// Run until all milestones land, recording the
	// order they appear in. Audio is collected from
	// the first frame: the payload's transfer is a
	// finite 0.4 seconds of sine.
	rd32 := func(addr uint32) uint32 { return uint32(sys.Mem.Read(addr, 4)) }
	order := []int{}
	seen := map[uint32]bool{}
	var samples []int16
	deadline := 400 // frames
	for frame := 0; frame < deadline && len(order) < 6; frame++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		samples = append(samples, sys.AudioBuffer()...)
		for m := 0; m < 6; m++ {
			addr := uint32(0x320 + 4*m)
			if !seen[addr] && rd32(addr) == uint32(m+1) {
				seen[addr] = true
				order = append(order, m+1)
			}
		}
	}
	if len(order) < 6 {
		t.Fatalf("milestones reached: %v (flags %08x %08x %08x %08x %08x %08x, "+
			"details: info %08x pak %08x ee %08x vto %08x ato %08x, spin %d, pc %x)",
			order,
			rd32(0x320), rd32(0x324), rd32(0x328), rd32(0x32C), rd32(0x330), rd32(0x334),
			rd32(0x354), rd32(0x34C), rd32(0x348), rd32(0x360), rd32(0x364),
			rd32(0x350), sys.CPU.PC)
	}
	for i, m := range order {
		if m != i+1 {
			t.Fatalf("milestones out of order: %v", order)
		}
	}
	// The seed IPL3 received in $s6 is the 6102 seed.
	if got := rd32(0x3F0); got != 0x3F {
		t.Errorf("seed at entry = %#x, want 0x3F", got)
	}
	// The PIF boot was terminated by the payload.
	if !sys.Mem.PIF.BootTerminated() {
		t.Error("PIF boot termination command never arrived")
	}
	// Controller evidence: A + Start in the button
	// bytes the payload copied out of its poll.
	w0, w1 := rd32(0x340), rd32(0x344)
	// Frame word 0 bytes are TX, RX, command, button
	// high byte.
	if byte(w0>>24) != 0x01 || byte(w0>>16) != 0x04 || byte(w0>>8) != 0x01 {
		t.Errorf("poll frame head = %08x (TX/RX/cmd bytes wrong)", w0)
	}
	buttons := uint16(w0&0xFF)<<8 | uint16(w1>>24)
	if buttons != ButtonA|ButtonStart {
		t.Errorf("polled buttons = %#04x, want %#04x", buttons, uint16(ButtonA|ButtonStart))
	}
	if got := rd32(0x354); got != 0x600D {
		t.Errorf("ch4 info check = %08x, want 0x600D", got)
	}
	if got := rd32(0x358); got != 3 {
		t.Errorf("pak fresh status = %d, want 3", got)
	}
	if got := rd32(0x34C); got != 0x600D {
		t.Errorf("pak round trip = %08x, want 0x600D", got)
	}
	if got := rd32(0x348); got != 0x600D {
		t.Errorf("eeprom round trip = %08x, want 0x600D", got)
	}
	// The EEPROM block the payload wrote is in the
	// save device now.
	if sys.SaveRAM()[5*8] != 0xA0 || sys.SaveRAM()[5*8+7] != 0xA7 {
		t.Errorf("eeprom block 5 = %02x..%02x", sys.SaveRAM()[40], sys.SaveRAM()[47])
	}
	// Video evidence: the scene's probes through the
	// VI presentation.
	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if got := fb[80*320+100]; got != 0xFFFF00FF {
		t.Errorf("triangle probe = %#08x, want magenta 0xFFFF00FF", got)
	}
	if got := fb[0]; got != 0xFF214284 {
		t.Errorf("background probe = %#08x, want 0xFF214284", got)
	}

	// Audio evidence: run out the rest of the
	// payload's sine transfer and measure it (32
	// frames per period at a 32006 Hz DAC rate is
	// 1000.19 Hz ideal).
	for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		samples = append(samples, sys.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	frames := len(samples) / 2
	if frames < 10000 {
		t.Fatalf("only %d audio frames produced", frames)
	}
	crossings := 0
	for i := 1; i < frames; i++ {
		if samples[2*(i-1)] < 0 && samples[2*i] >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
	}
	freq := float64(crossings) / (float64(frames) / float64(sys.AudioRate()))
	if freq < 970 || freq > 1030 {
		t.Errorf("measured sine = %.2f Hz, want about 1000", freq)
	} else {
		t.Logf("sine measured %.2f Hz (ideal 1000.19)", freq)
	}

	// Mid-run save/restore: byte-identical continuation.
	_ = sys.AudioBuffer()
	state := sys.Serialize()
	sys.RunCycles(300000)
	audioA := sys.AudioBuffer()
	stateA := sys.Serialize()
	fbA := append([]uint32(nil), sys.Framebuffer()...)

	sys2, err := New(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sys2.SetSaveType(cart.SaveEEPROM4K)
	sys2.SetButtons(ButtonA | ButtonStart)
	sys2.Start()
	if err := sys2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sys2.RunCycles(300000)
	audioB := sys2.AudioBuffer()
	stateB := sys2.Serialize()
	fbB := append([]uint32(nil), sys2.Framebuffer()...)
	if string(stateA) != string(stateB) {
		t.Error("continuation states diverged after restore")
	}
	if string(int16s(audioA)) != string(int16s(audioB)) {
		t.Error("continuation audio diverged after restore")
	}
	if len(audioA) == 0 {
		t.Error("no audio in the continuation window")
	}
	for i := range fbA {
		if fbA[i] != fbB[i] {
			t.Errorf("continuation framebuffer diverged at pixel %d", i)
			break
		}
	}
	if got := uint32(sys2.Mem.Read(0x350, 4)); got == 0 {
		t.Error("spin counter did not resume after restore")
	}
	t.Logf("state size v4 = %d bytes", sys.SerializeSize())
}

// TestBootChecksumMismatchReportedOnly proves the boot
// proceeds on a bad header checksum and merely
// reports it.
func TestBootChecksumMismatchReportedOnly(t *testing.T) {
	rom := engineROM(t)
	rom[0x10] ^= 0xFF // corrupt the stored checksum word
	sys, err := New(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sys.Start()
	if sys.BootChecksumOK() {
		t.Error("corrupted checksum reported OK")
	}
	// Boot still ran: the payload's first milestone
	// lands within a few frames.
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		sys.RunFrame()
		if sys.Mem.Read(0x320, 4) == 1 {
			return
		}
	}
	t.Error("payload never started on a checksum-mismatched ROM")
}

// TestWriteEngineROM materializes the synthetic engine
// ROM for the cross-platform harness
// (go_backend/cmd/enginetest). It runs only when
// GON64_ENGINE_ROM_OUT names the output path:
//
//	GON64_ENGINE_ROM_OUT=/tmp/gon64-engine.z64 go test ./system -run TestWriteEngineROM
func TestWriteEngineROM(t *testing.T) {
	out := os.Getenv("GON64_ENGINE_ROM_OUT")
	if out == "" {
		t.Skip("GON64_ENGINE_ROM_OUT not set")
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(out, engineROM(t), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/system/system_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-n64/chips/r4300"
)

// Assembler helpers (kept local to the test).
func rr(rs, rt, rd, sa, funct uint32) uint32 {
	return rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | sa<<6 | funct
}
func ii(op, rs, rt uint32, imm uint16) uint32 {
	return op<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(imm)
}
func lui(rt uint32, imm uint16) uint32 { return ii(0x0F, 0, rt, imm) }
func ori(rt, rs uint32, imm uint16) uint32 {
	return ii(0x0D, rs, rt, imm)
}
func addiu(rt, rs uint32, imm int16) uint32 { return ii(0x09, rs, rt, uint16(imm)) }
func lw(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32    { return ii(0x23, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func sw(rt, rs uint32, off int16) uint32    { return ii(0x2B, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func bne(rs, rt uint32, off int16) uint32   { return ii(0x05, rs, rt, uint16(off)) }
func mtc0(rt, rd uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x10<<26 | 4<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11
}

const (
	t0 = 8
	t1 = 9
	t2 = 10
	t3 = 11
	t4 = 12
	t5 = 13
	t6 = 14
	t7 = 15
	s0 = 16
	s1 = 17
	s2 = 18
)

// testROM builds a 1 MB cartridge image whose bytes from
// offset 0x1000 follow byte(i) = i*3+5.
func testROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 1<<20)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x00:], 0x80371240)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x08:], 0x80000400)
	copy(rom[0x20:], "GO-N64 TEST CART    ")
	for i := 0x1000; i < len(rom); i++ {
		rom[i] = byte(i*3 + 5)
	}
	return rom
}

// testProgram installs a TLB mapping (VA 0x00400000 -> PA
// 0x00100000), stores a word through it, runs a 64-byte PI
// DMA from ROM offset 0x1000 to RDRAM 0x200000, sums the 16
// transferred words, and writes the sum and the TLB word to
// RDRAM 0x300/0x304 before spinning.
func testProgram() []uint32 {
	return []uint32{
		lui(t0, 0x0040),         // 0: t0 = 0x00400000
		mtc0(t0, 10),            // 1: EntryHi
		mtc0(0, 5),              // 2: PageMask = 0
		addiu(t1, 0, 0x401F),    // 3
		mtc0(t1, 2),             // 4: EntryLo0
		addiu(t1, 0, 0x405F),    // 5
		mtc0(t1, 3),             // 6: EntryLo1
		mtc0(0, 0),              // 7: Index = 0
		0x42000002,              // 8: tlbwi
		lui(t2, 0x1234),         // 9
		ori(t2, t2, 0x5678),     // 10
		sw(t2, t0, 0),           // 11: store via TLB
		lui(s0, 0xA460),         // 12: PI registers (kseg1)
		lui(t3, 0x0020),         // 13
		sw(t3, s0, 0),           // 14: PI_DRAM_ADDR = 0x200000
		lui(t3, 0x1000),         // 15
		ori(t3, t3, 0x1000),     // 16
		sw(t3, s0, 4),           // 17: PI_CART_ADDR = 0x10001000
		addiu(t3, 0, 63),        // 18
		sw(t3, s0, 8),           // 19: PI_RD_LEN -> DMA
		lui(t4, 0x8020),         // 20: KSEG0 0x80200000
		addiu(t5, 0, 16),        // 21: counter
		rr(0, 0, s1, 0, 0x2D),   // 22: s1 = 0 (daddu)
		ii(0x27, t4, t6, 0),     // 23: loop: lwu t6, 0(t4)
		rr(s1, t6, s1, 0, 0x2D), // 24: daddu s1, s1, t6
		addiu(t4, t4, 4),        // 25
		addiu(t5, t5, -1),       // 26
		bne(t5, 0, -5),          // 27: -> 23
		lw(s2, t0, 0),           // 28: read back TLB word
		lui(t7, 0x8000),         // 29
		sw(s1, t7, 0x300),       // 30: sum low word
		rr(0, s1, t6, 0, 0x3E),  // 31: dsrl32 t6 = s1 >> 32
		sw(t6, t7, 0x304),       // 32: sum high word
		sw(s2, t7, 0x308),       // 33: TLB word
		0x0A000022,              // 34: j self (0x80000088)
		0,                       // 35: nop
	}
}

// bootTestMachine loads the test ROM, plants the program at
// RDRAM 0, and points the CPU at it in kernel mode.
func bootTestMachine(t *testing.T) *System {
	t.Helper()
	sys, err := New(testROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	prog := testProgram()
	for i, in := range prog {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status] = r4300.StatusCU0 | r4300.StatusCU1
	sys.CPU.PC = 0xFFFFFFFF80000000
	sys.CPU.NPC = sys.CPU.PC + 4
	return sys
}

func expectedSum() uint64 {
	var sum uint64
	for w := 0; w < 16; w++ {
		var word uint64
		for b := 0; b < 4; b++ {
			i := 0x1000 + w*4 + b
			word = word<<8 | uint64(byte(i*3+5))
		}
		sum += word
	}
	return sum
}

func TestProgramTLBAndPIDMA(t *testing.T) {
	sys := bootTestMachine(t)
	for i := 0; i < 200; i++ {
		sys.CPU.Step()
	}
	// TLB store reached physical 0x100000.
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x100000, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("tlb store: %08x", got)
	}
	// PI DMA landed the ROM bytes at RDRAM 0x200000.
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		if sys.Mem.RDRAM[0x200000+i] != byte((0x1000+i)*3+5) {
			t.Fatalf("dma byte %d wrong", i)
		}
	}
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x300, 4) | sys.Mem.Read(0x304, 4)<<32; got != expectedSum() {
		t.Errorf("sum: got %x want %x", got, expectedSum())
	}
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x308, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("tlb word cell: got %08x", got)
	}
}

func TestMidRunSaveRestoreDeterministic(t *testing.T) {
	a := bootTestMachine(t)
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ { // stop mid-loop, after the DMA
		a.CPU.Step()
	}
	state := a.Serialize()
	for i := 0; i < 170; i++ {
		a.CPU.Step()
	}

	b := bootTestMachine(t)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ { // different history, then adopt A's state
		b.CPU.Step()
	}
	if err := b.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 170; i++ {
		b.CPU.Step()
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(a.Mem.RDRAM, b.Mem.RDRAM) {
		t.Error("RDRAM diverged after restore")
	}
	if a.CPU.Reg != b.CPU.Reg {
		t.Error("registers diverged after restore")
	}
	if a.CPU.PC != b.CPU.PC || a.CPU.Cycles != b.CPU.Cycles {
		t.Error("pc/cycles diverged after restore")
	}
	if got := b.Mem.Read(0x300, 4) | b.Mem.Read(0x304, 4)<<32; got != expectedSum() {
		t.Errorf("restored run sum: %x want %x", got, expectedSum())
	}
}

func TestSerializeValidation(t *testing.T) {
	sys := bootTestMachine(t)
	state := sys.Serialize()
	if len(state) != sys.SerializeSize() {
		t.Fatalf("size %d want %d", len(state), sys.SerializeSize())
	}
	bad := append([]byte(nil), state...)
	bad[0] = 99
	if err := sys.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Error("bad version accepted")
	}
	if err := sys.Deserialize(state[:len(state)-1]); err == nil {
		t.Error("truncated state accepted")
	}
	exp, err := NewWithOptions(testROM(), true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := exp.Deserialize(state); err == nil {
		t.Error("expansion mismatch accepted")
	}
}

func TestFramebufferBlankAndButtons(t *testing.T) {
	sys := bootTestMachine(t)
	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) != Width*Height {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer %d", len(fb))
	}
	for i, px := range fb {
		if px != 0xFF000000 {
			t.Fatalf("pixel %d = %08x, want opaque black", i, px)
		}
	}
	sys.SetButtons(ButtonStart | ButtonA)
	if sys.Buttons() != ButtonStart|ButtonA {
		t.Error("buttons not recorded")
	}
	if sys.Title() != "GO-N64 TEST CART" {
		t.Errorf("title %q", sys.Title())
	}
}

func TestRunFrameBudget(t *testing.T) {
	sys := bootTestMachine(t)
	sys.RunFrame()
	if sys.CPU.Cycles < CyclesPerFrame {
		t.Errorf("frame consumed %d cycles, want at least %d", sys.CPU.Cycles, CyclesPerFrame)
	}
}

// --- N64-2: RSP execution through the system ---

// rspVInstr encodes an RSP COP2 computational instruction.
func rspVInstr(funct, e, vt, vs, vd uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x12<<26 | 1<<25 | e<<21 | vt<<16 | vs<<11 | vd<<6 | funct
}

// rspLS encodes an RSP LWC2/SWC2 instruction.
func rspLS(store bool, base, vt, op, elem uint32, off int32) uint32 {
	opc := uint32(0x32)
	if store {
		opc = 0x3A
	}
	return opc<<26 | base<<21 | vt<<16 | op<<11 | elem<<7 | (uint32(off) & 0x7F)
}

// rspDotProgram is the RSP microcode for the gate: load
// two 8-lane S1.15 vectors from DMEM 0x000/0x010, multiply
// (VMULF), pull the per-lane products out of the
// accumulator mid slice, sum them in scalar registers,
// store the dot product to DMEM 0x100, and BREAK.
func rspDotProgram() []uint32 {
	prog := []uint32{
		rspLS(false, 0, 0, 4, 0, 0), // lqv v0, 0($0)
		rspLS(false, 0, 1, 4, 0, 1), // lqv v1, 16($0)
		rspVInstr(0x00, 0, 1, 0, 2), // vmulf v2, v0, v1
		rspVInstr(0x1D, 1, 0, 0, 3), // vsar v3, v0, [1] (acc mid)
	}
	for lane := 0; lane < 8; lane++ {
		prog = append(prog, 0x12<<26|uint32(lane+1)<<16|3<<11|uint32(2*lane)<<7) // mfc2 $lane+1, v3[2*lane]
	}
	prog = append(prog, rr(1, 2, 9, 0, 0x21)) // add $9, $1, $2
	for reg := uint32(3); reg <= 8; reg++ {
		prog = append(prog, rr(9, reg, 9, 0, 0x21)) // add $9, $9, $reg
	}
	prog = append(prog,
		ii(0x2B, 0, 9, 0x100), // sw $9, 0x100($0)
		0x0000000D,            // break
	)
	return prog
}

// bootRSPMachine builds a machine where the CPU program
// DMAs the RSP dot-product program and its vectors from
// RDRAM into IMEM/DMEM, starts the RSP with
// interrupt-on-break enabled, and waits for the MI SP
// interrupt handler (planted at the exception vector) to
// flag completion before copying the result and the SP
// status out to RDRAM cells.
func bootRSPMachine(t *testing.T) *System {
	t.Helper()
	sys, err := New(testROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cpuProg := []uint32{
		lui(s0, 0xA404),         // 0: SP register page (kseg1)
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x1000),    // 1: MEM_ADDR = IMEM + 0
		sw(t0, s0, 0),           // 2
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x1000),    // 3: DRAM_ADDR = 0x1000
		sw(t0, s0, 4),           // 4
		addiu(t0, 0, 80),        // 5: RD_LEN: 88 bytes, 1 row
		sw(t0, s0, 8),           // 6: DMA program to IMEM
		addiu(t0, 0, 0),         // 7: MEM_ADDR = DMEM + 0
		sw(t0, s0, 0),           // 8
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x2000),    // 9: DRAM_ADDR = 0x2000
		sw(t0, s0, 4),           // 10
		addiu(t0, 0, 24),        // 11: RD_LEN: 32 bytes
		sw(t0, s0, 8),           // 12: DMA vectors to DMEM
		lui(t1, 0xA408),         // 13: SP_PC page
		sw(0, t1, 0),            // 14: SP_PC = 0
		lui(t1, 0xA430),         // 15: MI page
		addiu(t0, 0, 2),         // 16: set SP interrupt mask
		sw(t0, t1, 0xC),         // 17: MI_MASK
		addiu(t0, 0, 0x101),     // 18: clr halt + set intr-on-break
		sw(t0, s0, 0x10),        // 19: SP_STATUS: RSP starts
		lui(t2, 0x8000),         // 20: RDRAM kseg0
		lw(t3, t2, 0x300),       // 21: poll the handler flag
		ii(0x04, t3, 0, 0xFFFE), // 22: beq t3, $0, 21
		0,                       // 23: nop
		lui(t1, 0xA400),         // 24: SP memory window
		lw(t4, t1, 0x100),       // 25: dot product in DMEM
		sw(t4, t2, 0x304),       // 26: result cell
		lw(t5, s0, 0x10),        // 27: SP_STATUS
		sw(t5, t2, 0x308),       // 28: status cell
		0x0800001D,              // 29: j self
		0,                       // 30: nop
	}
	for i, in := range cpuProg {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	// Interrupt handler at the general exception vector
	// (physical 0x180): flag completion, clear the RSP
	// interrupt, return.
	handler := []uint32{
		lui(26, 0x8000),      // k0 = RDRAM kseg0
		addiu(27, 0, 0x600D), // k1 = done magic
		sw(27, 26, 0x300),    // flag word
		lui(26, 0xA404),      // SP register page
		addiu(27, 0, 8),      // clr interrupt
		sw(27, 26, 0x10),     // SP_STATUS
		0x42000018,           // eret
	}
	for i, in := range handler {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x180+i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	// RSP program image at RDRAM 0x1000.
	for i, in := range rspDotProgram() {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x1000+i*4), 4, uint64(in))
	}
	// Vectors at RDRAM 0x2000: A in S1.15, B all 0.5.
	a := []uint16{0x4000, 0x2000, 0x1000, 0x0800, 0x4000, 0x2000, 0x1000, 0x0800}
	for i, v := range a {
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x2000+i*2), 2, uint64(v))
		sys.Mem.Write(uint32(0x2010+i*2), 2, 0x4000)
	}
	sys.CPU.CP0[r4300.Cp0Status] = r4300.StatusCU0 | r4300.StatusCU1 | 0x400 | 0x1 // CU0|CU1|IM2|IE
	sys.CPU.PC = 0xFFFFFFFF80000000
	sys.CPU.NPC = sys.CPU.PC + 4
	return sys
}

func runUntilFlag(t *testing.T, sys *System) {
	t.Helper()
	for i := 0; i < 20000 && sys.Mem.Read(0x300, 4) == 0; i++ {
		sys.RunCycles(10)
	}
	if sys.Mem.Read(0x300, 4) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("RSP completion flag never arrived (interrupt path broken?)")
	}
}

func TestRSPExecutionGate(t *testing.T) {
	sys := bootRSPMachine(t)
	if got := sys.SerializeSize(); got != 6604438 {
		t.Errorf("state size at 4 MB: %d want 6604438", got)
	}
	runUntilFlag(t, sys)
	for i := 0; i < 50; i++ { // let the CPU copy the cells out
		sys.RunCycles(10)
	}
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x300, 4); got != 0x600D {
		t.Errorf("handler flag: %08x", got)
	}
	// Dot product: 2*(0.25 + 0.125 + 0.0625 + 0.03125)
	// = 0.9375 = 0x7800 in S1.15.
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x304, 4); got != 0x7800 {
		t.Errorf("dot product cell: %08x want 7800", got)
	}
	// SP_STATUS: halt (bit 0) + broke (bit 1) +
	// interrupt-on-break enabled (bit 6).
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(0x308, 4); got != 0x43 {
		t.Errorf("status cell: %08x want 43", got)
	}
	// The handler cleared the interrupt, so the MI SP
	// line is down again.
	if sys.Mem.MIInterrupt() {
		t.Error("MI interrupt still asserted after handler cleared it")
	}
}

func TestRSPMidRunSaveRestoreDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	a := bootRSPMachine(t)
	// Step one cycle at a time until the RSP is caught
	// mid-program, then save.
	mid := false
	for i := 0; i < 100000 && !mid; i++ {
		a.RunCycles(1)
		if !a.RSP.Halted() && a.RSP.PC >= 8 && a.RSP.PC <= 72 {
			mid = true
		}
	}
	if !mid {
		t.Fatal("never caught the RSP mid-program")
	}
	state := a.Serialize()
	finish := func(s *System) {
		for i := 0; i < 20000 && s.Mem.Read(0x300, 4) == 0; i++ {
			s.RunCycles(10)
		}
		for i := 0; i < 100; i++ { // settle into the spin loop
			s.RunCycles(10)
		}
	}
	finish(a)
	b := bootRSPMachine(t)
	if err := b.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	finish(b)
	if !bytes.Equal(a.Serialize(), b.Serialize()) {
		t.Error("full states diverged after mid-run RSP restore")
	}
	if got := b.Mem.Read(0x304, 4); got != 0x7800 {
		t.Errorf("restored dot product: %08x", got)
	}
}

func TestSemaphoreThroughBus(t *testing.T) {
	sys, err := New(testROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	const sem = 0x0404001C // SP_SEMAPHORE
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(sem, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("first read: %d", got)
	}
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(sem, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("second read (test-and-set): %d", got)
	}
	sys.Mem.Write(sem, 4, 0) // CPU write releases
	if got := sys.Mem.Read(sem, 4); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("read after release: %d", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/vi/vi.go ====================

// Package vi implements the Nintendo 64 Video Interface.
//
// The VI scans a framebuffer out of RDRAM on a fixed field
// cadence and raises an interrupt when the scan reaches a
// programmed half-line. This package models the register
// file, the half-line timing, the interrupt level, and the
// final picture sampling (Present) that turns the RDRAM
// framebuffer into an XRGB8888 frame for the host. RDP
// rendering into RDRAM is a separate package; the VI only
// reads what is already there.
//
// Model choices, stated plainly:
//
//   - A field lasts exactly 1,562,500 CPU cycles (the
//     93.75 MHz CPU divided by 60 Hz). That budget is
//     spread evenly over the field's half-lines with an
//     exact rational accumulator, so long runs have no
//     timing drift.
//   - The total half-line count is V_TOTAL plus one,
//     except that a V_TOTAL field of 0 selects the NTSC
//     default of 525 half-lines.
//   - An even half-line total means interlaced output:
//     the field flag toggles at every field wrap. An odd
//     total means progressive output: the field flag
//     never toggles. The SERRATE bit is stored but does
//     not change this model.
//   - In progressive mode the low bit of both the
//     interrupt target and the line counter is ignored
//     for the interrupt comparison, because a progressive
//     field has no distinct odd and even half-lines.
//   - When CTRL TYPE is 0 the VI is off: the counter is
//     frozen at 0, V_CURRENT reads 0, no interrupt fires,
//     and Present returns no frame.
//   - The interrupt is a level. OnInterrupt is called
//     with true when a field reaches the target half-line
//     and with false when a write to V_CURRENT clears
//     the pending flag.
package vi

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"math"
)

// Register byte offsets from the VI base at 0x04400000.
const (
	RegCtrl     = 0x00
	RegOrigin   = 0x04
	RegWidth    = 0x08
	RegVIntr    = 0x0C
	RegVCurrent = 0x10
	RegBurst    = 0x14
	RegVTotal   = 0x18
	RegHTotal   = 0x1C
	RegHLeap    = 0x20
	RegHVideo   = 0x24
	RegVVideo   = 0x28
	RegVBurst   = 0x2C
	RegXScale   = 0x30
	RegYScale   = 0x34
)

// CTRL register bits and fields.
const (
	CtrlTypeMask     = 0x0003 // bits 1-0: 0 off, 2 is 16-bit, 3 is 32-bit
	CtrlGammaDither  = 1 << 2
	CtrlGamma        = 1 << 3
	CtrlDivot        = 1 << 4
	CtrlVBusClock    = 1 << 5
	CtrlSerrate      = 1 << 6
	CtrlTestMode     = 1 << 7
	CtrlAAModeMask   = 0x0300 // bits 9-8
	CtrlKillWE       = 1 << 11
	CtrlPixelAdvMask = 0xF000 // bits 15-12
	CtrlDedither     = 1 << 16
)

// cyclesPerField is the CPU cycle budget of one field:
// 93,750,000 cycles per second divided by 60 fields.
const cyclesPerField = 1562500

// defaultHalfLines is the half-line count used when the
// V_TOTAL field reads 0 (NTSC timing, 525 half-lines).
const defaultHalfLines = 525

// VI is the video interface device.
type VI struct {
	ctrl   uint32
	origin uint32 // stored masked to 24 bits
	width  uint32
	vIntr  uint32
	burst  uint32
	vTotal uint32
	hTotal uint32
	hLeap  uint32
	hVideo uint32
	vVideo uint32
	vBurst uint32
	xScale uint32
	yScale uint32

	counter uint32 // current half-line, 0 to totalHalf-1
	acc     uint64 // rational timing remainder, in units of half-line cycles
	fld     int    // current field: 0 or 1
	pending bool   // interrupt level currently asserted

	// OnInterrupt, when set, is called when the interrupt
	// level changes: true when a field reaches the target
	// half-line, false when a V_CURRENT write clears it.
	// The coordinator wires it to the MI VI interrupt bit.
	OnInterrupt func(active bool)
}

// New returns a VI in its power-on state: TYPE 0 (off),
// all registers zero, counter at half-line 0, field 0.
func New() *VI {
	return &VI{}
}

// totalHalf returns the number of half-lines in a field.
func (v *VI) totalHalf() int {
	f := int(v.vTotal & 0x3FF)
	if f == 0 {
		return defaultHalfLines
	}
	return f + 1
}

// interlaced reports whether the current timing is
// interlaced (an even half-line total).
func (v *VI) interlaced() bool {
	return v.totalHalf()%2 == 0
}

// framebufferType returns the CTRL TYPE field.
func (v *VI) framebufferType() uint32 {
	return v.ctrl & CtrlTypeMask
}

// ReadRegister reads the 32-bit register at the given byte
// offset. Plain registers read back what was written.
// V_CURRENT reads the computed counter value.
func (v *VI) ReadRegister(off uint32) uint32 {
	switch off {
	case RegCtrl:
		return v.ctrl
	case RegOrigin:
		return v.origin
	case RegWidth:
		return v.width
	case RegVIntr:
		return v.vIntr
	case RegVCurrent:
		return v.Current()
	case RegBurst:
		return v.burst
	case RegVTotal:
		return v.vTotal
	case RegHTotal:
		return v.hTotal
	case RegHLeap:
		return v.hLeap
	case RegHVideo:
		return v.hVideo
	case RegVVideo:
		return v.vVideo
	case RegVBurst:
		return v.vBurst
	case RegXScale:
		return v.xScale
	case RegYScale:
		return v.yScale
	}
	return 0
}

// WriteRegister writes the 32-bit register at the given
// byte offset. ORIGIN is masked to its 24-bit field;
// every other plain register is stored raw. Any write to
// V_CURRENT clears the interrupt, whatever the value.
func (v *VI) WriteRegister(off uint32, val uint32) {
	switch off {
	case RegCtrl:
		v.ctrl = val
	case RegOrigin:
		v.origin = val & 0xFFFFFF
	case RegWidth:
		v.width = val
	case RegVIntr:
		v.vIntr = val
	case RegVCurrent:
		v.pending = false
		if v.OnInterrupt != nil {
			v.OnInterrupt(false)
		}
	case RegBurst:
		v.burst = val
	case RegVTotal:
		v.vTotal = val
	case RegHTotal:
		v.hTotal = val
	case RegHLeap:
		v.hLeap = val
	case RegHVideo:
		v.hVideo = val
	case RegVVideo:
		v.vVideo = val
	case RegVBurst:
		v.vBurst = val
	case RegXScale:
		v.xScale = val
	case RegYScale:
		v.yScale = val
	}
}

// Current returns the V_CURRENT register value: bits 9-1
// hold the current line (half-line counter divided by 2)
// and bit 0 holds the field flag. When the VI is off the
// value reads 0.
func (v *VI) Current() uint32 {
	if v.framebufferType() == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return ((v.counter >> 1) << 1) | uint32(v.fld)
}

// Field returns the current field flag, 0 or 1. In
// progressive mode it stays 0; in interlaced mode it
// toggles at every field wrap.
func (v *VI) Field() int {
	return v.fld
}

// Pending reports whether the VI interrupt is asserted.
// It is a test and integration helper; the level itself
// is delivered through OnInterrupt.
func (v *VI) Pending() bool {
	return v.pending
}

// Advance runs the half-line timing for the given number
// of CPU cycles.
//
// The accumulator keeps the timing exact: each call adds
// cpuCycles times totalHalf to the numerator, converts
// whole multiples of cyclesPerField into half-line steps,
// and keeps the remainder. The counter steps one half-line
// at a time so the interrupt comparison sees every line.
//
// The interrupt fires when a step takes the counter onto
// the target: in interlaced mode the counter must equal
// the target, in progressive mode the counters divided by
// 2 must become equal where they were not equal on the
// previous half-line (so the paired half-line does not
// fire a second time). A target of 0 therefore fires at
// the field wrap. When the VI is off the cycles are
// discarded and the counter stays at 0.
func (v *VI) Advance(cpuCycles int) {
	if cpuCycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	if v.framebufferType() == 0 {
		v.counter = 0
		v.acc = 0
		return
	}
	total := v.totalHalf()
	inter := total%2 == 0
	target := v.vIntr & 0x3FF

	matches := func(c uint32) bool {
		if inter {
			return c == target
		}
		return c>>1 == target>>1
	}

	v.acc += uint64(cpuCycles) * uint64(total)
	steps := v.acc / cyclesPerField
	v.acc -= steps * cyclesPerField

	for s := uint64(0); s < steps; s++ {
		prev := v.counter
		v.counter++
		if int(v.counter) >= total {
			v.counter = 0
			if inter {
				v.fld ^= 1
			}
		}
		if matches(v.counter) && !matches(prev) {
			v.pending = true
			if v.OnInterrupt != nil {
				v.OnInterrupt(true)
			}
		}
	}
}

// gammaTable maps a channel byte through the VI gamma
// curve (a square root), computed once with the formula
// byte(sqrt(c/255) * 255 + 0.5).
var gammaTable [256]byte

func init() {
	for c := 0; c < 256; c++ {
		gammaTable[c] = byte(math.Sqrt(float64(c)/255.0)*255.0 + 0.5)
	}
}

// Present samples the RDRAM framebuffer into an XRGB8888
// frame (alpha in the top byte) and returns it with its
// width and height. It returns nil, 0, 0 when the VI is
// off (TYPE 0), when TYPE is a reserved value, or when
// WIDTH is 0.
//
// Geometry comes from the video window registers: the
// width is H_END minus H_START from H_VIDEO (falling back
// to WIDTH when that is out of range) and the height is
// (V_END minus V_START) divided by 2 from V_VIDEO, since
// those values are in half-lines (falling back to 240).
// Width is capped at 640 and height at 480.
//
// Each output pixel maps back into the framebuffer
// through the X_SCALE and Y_SCALE registers, which hold a
// 2.10 fixed point scale and offset: the source coordinate
// is (offset + output * scale) shifted right by 10. In
// interlaced mode the source line is doubled and offset
// by the current field, so each field presents its own
// lines of the framebuffer. Pixels whose source x is
// outside WIDTH, or whose address falls outside RDRAM,
// read as opaque black.
func (v *VI) Present(dram []byte) (fb []uint32, w, h int) {
	typ := v.framebufferType()
	if typ != 2 && typ != 3 {
		return nil, 0, 0
	}
	if v.width == 0 {
		return nil, 0, 0
	}

	hStart := int((v.hVideo >> 16) & 0x3FF)
	hEnd := int(v.hVideo & 0x3FF)
	w = hEnd - hStart
	if w <= 0 || w > 640 {
		w = int(v.width)
	}
	if w > 640 {
		w = 640
	}
	if w <= 0 {
		return nil, 0, 0
	}

	vStart := int((v.vVideo >> 16) & 0x3FF)
	vEnd := int(v.vVideo & 0x3FF)
	h = (vEnd - vStart) / 2
	if h <= 0 || h > 480 {
		h = 240
	}
	if h > 480 {
		h = 480
	}

	xScale := int(v.xScale & 0xFFF)
	xOff := int((v.xScale >> 16) & 0xFFF)
	if xScale == 0 {
		xScale = 1024
	}
	yScale := int(v.yScale & 0xFFF)
	yOff := int((v.yScale >> 16) & 0xFFF)
	if yScale == 0 {
		yScale = 1024
	}

	bpp := 2
	if typ == 3 {
		bpp = 4
	}
	inter := v.interlaced()
	origin := int(v.origin & 0xFFFFFF)
	width := int(v.width)
	gamma := v.ctrl&CtrlGamma != 0

	fb = make([]uint32, w*h)
	for oy := 0; oy < h; oy++ {
		sy := (yOff + oy*yScale) >> 10
		srcLine := sy
		if inter {
			srcLine = sy*2 + v.fld
		}
		for ox := 0; ox < w; ox++ {
			sx := (xOff + ox*xScale) >> 10
			px := uint32(0xFF000000)
			if sx >= 0 && sx < width {
				addr := origin + (srcLine*width+sx)*bpp
				if addr >= 0 && addr+bpp <= len(dram) {
					px = v.fetchPixel(dram, addr, typ, gamma)
				}
			}
			fb[oy*w+ox] = px
		}
	}
	return fb, w, h
}

// fetchPixel decodes one framebuffer pixel at a byte
// address in RDRAM into XRGB8888.
func (v *VI) fetchPixel(dram []byte, addr int, typ uint32, gamma bool) uint32 {
	var r, g, b, a uint32
	if typ == 2 {
		p := uint32(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(dram[addr:]))
		r5 := (p >> 11) & 31
		g5 := (p >> 6) & 31
		b5 := (p >> 1) & 31
		r = (r5 << 3) | (r5 >> 2)
		g = (g5 << 3) | (g5 >> 2)
		b = (b5 << 3) | (b5 >> 2)
		if p&1 != 0 {
			a = 255
		}
	} else {
		r = uint32(dram[addr])
		g = uint32(dram[addr+1])
		b = uint32(dram[addr+2])
		a = uint32(dram[addr+3])
	}
	if gamma {
		r = uint32(gammaTable[r])
		g = uint32(gammaTable[g])
		b = uint32(gammaTable[b])
	}
	return a<<24 | r<<16 | g<<8 | b
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed byte size of a serialized VI.
//
// Layout, all big-endian:
//
//	 0: 13 register words: CTRL, ORIGIN, WIDTH, V_INTR,
//	    BURST, V_TOTAL, H_TOTAL, H_LEAP, H_VIDEO, V_VIDEO,
//	    V_BURST, X_SCALE, Y_SCALE (52 bytes)
//	52: half-line counter, uint32
//	56: timing accumulator, uint64
//	64: field flag byte
//	65: interrupt pending byte
//	66: 2 pad bytes
const SerializeSize = 13*4 + 4 + 8 + 4

// Serialize writes the VI state into dst, which must be
// at least SerializeSize bytes, and returns the number of
// bytes written. The layout is documented on
// SerializeSize. The OnInterrupt callback is not part of
// the state; the coordinator rewires it after a restore.
func (v *VI) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	regs := [13]uint32{
		v.ctrl, v.origin, v.width, v.vIntr, v.burst,
		v.vTotal, v.hTotal, v.hLeap, v.hVideo, v.vVideo,
		v.vBurst, v.xScale, v.yScale,
	}
	for i, r := range regs {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(dst[i*4:], r)
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(dst[52:], v.counter)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(dst[56:], v.acc)
	dst[64] = byte(v.fld)
	if v.pending {
		dst[65] = 1
	} else {
		dst[65] = 0
	}
	dst[66] = 0
	dst[67] = 0
	return SerializeSize
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (v *VI) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("vi: state too short")
	}
	regs := make([]uint32, 13)
	for i := range regs {
		regs[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[i*4:])
	}
	v.ctrl = regs[0]
	v.origin = regs[1]
	v.width = regs[2]
	v.vIntr = regs[3]
	v.burst = regs[4]
	v.vTotal = regs[5]
	v.hTotal = regs[6]
	v.hLeap = regs[7]
	v.hVideo = regs[8]
	v.vVideo = regs[9]
	v.vBurst = regs[10]
	v.xScale = regs[11]
	v.yScale = regs[12]
	v.counter = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(in[52:])
	v.acc = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(in[56:])
	v.fld = int(in[64] & 1)
	v.pending = in[65] != 0
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-n64/vi/vi_test.go ====================

package vi

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// programNTSC240p sets up the standard test timing: a
// 16-bit framebuffer, 525 half-lines (progressive 240p),
// interrupt at half-line 2, and 1.0 scaling on both axes.
func programNTSC240p(v *VI) {
	v.WriteRegister(RegCtrl, 2) // TYPE 2, 16-bit
	v.WriteRegister(RegVTotal, 524)
	v.WriteRegister(RegVIntr, 2)
	v.WriteRegister(RegWidth, 320)
	v.WriteRegister(RegHVideo, 108<<16|428)
	v.WriteRegister(RegVVideo, 37<<16|517)
	v.WriteRegister(RegXScale, 0x400)
	v.WriteRegister(RegYScale, 0x400)
}

func TestNTSC240pInterruptOncePerField(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	fires := 0
	clears := 0
	v.OnInterrupt = func(active bool) {
		if active {
			fires++
		} else {
			clears++
		}
	}
	programNTSC240p(v)

	v.Advance(1562500) // exactly one field
	if fires != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("interrupt fired %d times in one field, want 1", fires)
	}
	if !v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("interrupt not pending after the field")
	}
	if c := v.Current(); c > 2 {
		t.Fatalf("counter %d after a full field, want near 0", c)
	}
	if v.Field() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("field %d in progressive mode, want 0", v.Field())
	}

	v.WriteRegister(RegVCurrent, 0)
	if v.Pending() {
		t.Fatal("interrupt still pending after a V_CURRENT write")
	}
	if clears != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("clear callback ran %d times, want 1", clears)
	}
}

func TestRegisterReadback(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	v.WriteRegister(RegOrigin, 0xFF123456)
	if got := v.ReadRegister(RegOrigin); got != 0x123456 {
		t.Fatalf("ORIGIN read %#x, want 0x123456 (24-bit mask)", got)
	}
	v.WriteRegister(RegBurst, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if got := v.ReadRegister(RegBurst); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("BURST read %#x, want the raw written value", got)
	}

	programNTSC240p(v)
	if got := v.Current(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Current at reset %d, want 0", got)
	}
	// 10,000 cycles at 525 half-lines per 1,562,500 cycles
	// is exactly 3 half-lines plus a remainder.
	v.Advance(10000)
	if got := v.Current(); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("Current after 3 half-lines %d, want 2 (counter 3, field 0)", got)
	}
	if got := v.ReadRegister(RegVCurrent); got != v.Current() {
		t.Fatalf("V_CURRENT read %d, want Current %d", got, v.Current())
	}

	// Interlaced timing: an even half-line total toggles
	// the field flag at the wrap, and the flag is bit 0
	// of V_CURRENT.
	v2 := New()
	programNTSC240p(v2)
	v2.WriteRegister(RegVTotal, 525) // 526 half-lines, interlaced
	v2.Advance(1562500)
	if v2.Field() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("field after an interlaced field %d, want 1", v2.Field())
	}
	if got := v2.Current(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("Current after interlaced wrap %d, want 1 (counter 0, field 1)", got)
	}
	v2.Advance(1562500)
	if v2.Field() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("field after two interlaced fields %d, want 0", v2.Field())
	}
}

func TestVIOffFreezesCounter(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	fires := 0
	v.OnInterrupt = func(active bool) {
		if active {
			fires++
		}
	}
	v.WriteRegister(RegVTotal, 524)
	v.WriteRegister(RegVIntr, 2)
	v.Advance(1562500) // TYPE is still 0
	if fires != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("interrupt fired %d times while off, want 0", fires)
	}
	if got := v.Current(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Current while off %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if _, w, h := v.Present(make([]byte, 1<<20)); w != 0 || h != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Present while off gave %dx%d, want 0x0", w, h)
	}
}

func putPixel16(dram []byte, width, x, y int, val uint16) {
	addr := (y*width + x) * 2
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(dram[addr:], val)
}

func TestPresent16Bit(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	programNTSC240p(v)
	v.WriteRegister(RegOrigin, 0)

	dram := make([]byte, 320*240*2)
	putPixel16(dram, 320, 0, 0, 0xF801) // pure red, alpha 1
	putPixel16(dram, 320, 1, 0, 0x07C1) // pure green, alpha 1
	putPixel16(dram, 320, 0, 2, 0x003F) // pure blue, alpha 1
	putPixel16(dram, 320, 2, 0, 0xF800) // red with alpha 0

	fb, w, h := v.Present(dram)
	if w != 320 || h != 240 {
		t.Fatalf("Present geometry %dx%d, want 320x240", w, h)
	}
	if fb == nil || len(fb) != w*h {
		t.Fatalf("Present returned %d pixels, want %d", len(fb), w*h)
	}
	if got := fb[0]; got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (0,0) %#08x, want 0xFFFF0000", got)
	}
	if got := fb[1]; got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (1,0) %#08x, want 0xFF00FF00", got)
	}
	if got := fb[2*w]; got != 0xFF0000FF {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (0,2) %#08x, want 0xFF0000FF", got)
	}
	if got := fb[2]; got != 0x00FF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (2,0) %#08x, want 0x00FF0000 (alpha 0 keeps the channels)", got)
	}

	v.WriteRegister(RegCtrl, 0)
	fb, w, h = v.Present(dram)
	if fb != nil || w != 0 || h != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Present with TYPE 0 gave %v %dx%d, want nil 0x0", fb, w, h)
	}
}

func TestPresent32BitAndGamma(t *testing.T) {
	v := New()
	programNTSC240p(v)
	v.WriteRegister(RegCtrl, 3) // TYPE 3, 32-bit
	dram := make([]byte, 320*240*4)
	copy(dram[0:], []byte{0x10, 0x20, 0x30, 0x40})
	fb, _, _ := v.Present(dram)
	if fb == nil {
		t.Fatal("Present returned nil for TYPE 3")
	}
	if got := fb[0]; got != 0x40102030 {
		t.Fatalf("32-bit pixel %#08x, want 0x40102030", got)
	}

	// Gamma brightens mid values through the square root
	// curve: 0x40 (64) maps to 128.
	v.WriteRegister(RegCtrl, 3|CtrlGamma)
	copy(dram[0:], []byte{0x40, 0x40, 0x40, 0xFF})
	fb, _, _ = v.Present(dram)
	if got := fb[0]; got != 0xFF808080 {
		t.Fatalf("gamma pixel %#08x, want 0xFF808080", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	if SerializeSize != 68 {
		t.Fatalf("SerializeSize %d, want 68", SerializeSize)
	}
	v := New()
	programNTSC240p(v)
	v.Advance(10000)

	buf := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	if n := v.Serialize(buf); n != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d bytes, want %d", n, SerializeSize)
	}

	v2 := New()
	if err := v2.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if v2.Current() != v.Current() {
		t.Fatalf("restored Current %d, want %d", v2.Current(), v.Current())
	}
	if got := v2.ReadRegister(RegWidth); got != 320 {
		t.Fatalf("restored WIDTH %d, want 320", got)
	}

	fires1, fires2 := 0, 0
	v.OnInterrupt = func(active bool) {
		if active {
			fires1++
		}
	}
	v2.OnInterrupt = func(active bool) {
		if active {
			fires2++
		}
	}
	// Run both to just past the field wrap; the target at
	// half-line 2 must fire exactly once in the new field
	// on both machines.
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		v.Advance(156250)
		v2.Advance(156250)
		if v.Current() != v2.Current() {
			t.Fatalf("step %d: Current diverged, %d vs %d", i, v.Current(), v2.Current())
		}
	}
	if fires1 != 1 || fires2 != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("fires after restore %d and %d, want 1 and 1", fires1, fires2)
	}

	if err := v2.Deserialize(buf[:10]); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize accepted a short state")
	}
}
