==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/README.md ====================

# go-nds: a from-scratch Go Nintendo DS core

Part of iTaK Gaming. This module is a clean-room Nintendo DS
emulator core written in Go from the published hardware
documentation (the ARM architecture manuals and GBATEK). It
bundles no BIOS, no firmware, and no game data, and it has zero
third-party Go dependencies.

DS-1 delivered both CPUs, the dual bus, cartridge header
foundations, and the system skeleton. DS-2 added both 2D
video engines with VRAM bank assignment and display capture,
timers, both DMA engines, IPC, per-CPU interrupt controllers,
the game card command model, the documented minimal stubs
(touchscreen, RTC, AUX SPI save memory, and a generated
firmware image), and the full direct boot. DS-3 added the
3D geometry and rendering engine feeding engine A's BG0,
the 16-channel sound unit with capture, and the
microphone path through the touchscreen ADC. DS-4 (this
slice) completes the core: the libretro shell, the
full-stack enginetest through guest ARM9 and ARM7
programs and through the built shell library in the
shared harness, and the android-64bit app wiring
preparation. Wireless stays a documented stub (below).

## Package layout

- `chips/armcore`: one configurable ARM execution core. The two
  DS processors share an architecture lineage, so a single
  implementation is configured as ARMv4T or ARMv5TE.
- `chips/arm7`: the ARM7TDMI (ARMv4T) as used by the DS for
  sound, touchscreen, and wireless work.
- `chips/arm9`: the ARM946E-S (ARMv5TE, "ARM9") that runs the
  main game code: CLZ, the saturating Q arithmetic group, the
  signed halfword multiplies, LDRD/STRD, BLX, BKPT, PLD as a
  no-op, and the CP15 system control coprocessor with register
  storage, high exception vectors, and fault registers (FSR and
  FAR) set on aborts.
- `bus`: the DS memory system as two CPU views over shared
  backing stores. Main RAM 4 MB at 0x02000000 (mirrored), ITCM
  32 KB and DTCM with CP15-configured base and size honored,
  shared WRAM 32 KB under the WRAMCNT ownership mapping
  (enforced per bank, per CPU), ARM7 private WRAM 64 KB at
  0x03800000, per-side IO pages (the ARM9 page is 8 KB so the
  engine B page at 0x04001000 is mapped), VRAM banks A to I as
  LCDC backing stores, the palette store (2 KB: both engines'
  BG and OBJ palettes) and OAM store (2 KB: 1 KB per engine),
  the GBA slot SRAM window, and the cartridge window gated by
  the EXMEMCNT ownership bit. Banks C and D assigned as ARM7
  WRAM (VRAMCNT MST 2) are decoded in the ARM7 view at
  0x06000000. When the system installs its `IOHook`, IO page
  accesses and the 0x04100000 window (IPC FIFO receive port,
  card data port) are offered to the DS-2 devices first and
  fall back to storage for offsets they do not claim; a bare
  bus behaves exactly as slice 1.
- `cart`: DS ROM header parsing and validation (title, game
  code, maker code, unit code, encryption seed select byte,
  capacity, both binaries' ROM offsets, entry and load
  addresses, icon offset, secure area CRC field, header CRC
  reported as a validity flag rather than a hard failure).
- `periph`: the DS-2 device registers behind the bus hook.
  Per-CPU interrupt controllers (IME/IE/IF with
  write-1-to-acknowledge IF), four GBA-style timers per CPU
  (prescalers, cascade, IRQ), ARM9 DMA (immediate, VBlank,
  HBlank, display-start, main-memory-display, card, GBA cart,
  and geometry FIFO timing; the FIFO port itself is claimed
  by the system hook for the gx package since DS-3), ARM7 DMA (GBA modes; the special
  timing has no source in this module and completes cleanly),
  IPCSYNC and the 16-word IPC FIFOs with their IRQ
  conditions, the game card command unit (see the card note
  under Honesty), an AUX SPI 512-byte EEPROM save memory
  exposed as `Machine.SaveRAM()`, the ARM7 SPI bus (power
  stub, generated firmware flash, touchscreen ADC whose aux
  channel 6 is the microphone input since DS-3), and the RTC
  stub.
- `gx`: the 3D geometry and rendering engine (DS-3). The
  packed GXFIFO port and the direct command ports feed a
  256-entry FIFO plus 4-entry pipe drained by an executor
  implementing the full documented command set: the matrix
  unit (four current matrices, projection and texture stacks
  of 1, position/vector stacks of 31 plus the documented
  entry-31 overflow behavior), polygon and vertex assembly
  (2048 polygons, 6144 vertices, with the GXSTAT and
  RAM_COUNT overflow reporting), the 4-light lighting model
  evaluated per vertex at NORMAL time, all eight texture
  formats including 4x4 compressed, and the test commands
  with their result readbacks. SWAP_BUFFERS defers to the
  next VBlank, where the rendering engine draws the swapped
  list into a 256x192 layer (clipping, viewport, per-span
  perspective texture interpolation, 24-bit depth, the
  documented translucent blending and fog) that the video
  package consumes as engine A's BG0 through the `Line3D`
  provider.
- `audio`: the DS sound unit (DS-3) on the ARM7 IO page: 16
  channels (PCM8, PCM16, IMA ADPCM with the documented step
  and index tables, PSG squares on channels 8 to 13, noise
  on 14 and 15), the stereo mixer at 32,768 Hz with master
  volume, per-side source selects, and SOUNDBIAS, and the
  two sound capture units writing the mix back to memory.
- `video`: both 2D engines and display capture. Engines fetch
  through the VRAMCNT bank assignment layer (BG A/B, OBJ A/B,
  extended palette spaces, and the texture spaces, all built
  from the VRAMCNT bytes). Text, affine, affine-extended, and
  bitmap backgrounds including the mode 6 large bitmap, OBJ
  with bitmap sprites and extended palettes, windows, alpha
  blending and brightness, per-engine master brightness, the
  display modes (off, graphics, VRAM display, main RAM
  display), POWCNT1 display swap, DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, and
  DISPCAPCNT capture into a VRAM bank. Timing: 263 lines per
  frame (VCOUNT 0-262), 192 visible, rendered per scanline;
  the ARM9 line budget splits 1536 visible plus 594 hblank
  cycles and the ARM7 budget 768 plus 297, which reproduces
  the frame budgets of 560,190 and 280,095 cycles exactly.
- `system`: the machine. `LoadROM` performs the full direct
  boot (below); `Start`, `Start9`, and `Start7` jump the CPUs
  to the header entry points; `RunFrame` steps the machine at
  scanline granularity, raising the LCD interrupt sources and
  DMA triggers at the documented points; `Framebuffer`
  returns the two 256x192 XRGB8888 screens in POWCNT1 order
  (top, bottom); `SetButtons` and `SetTouch` drive the
  KEYINPUT/EXTKEYIN registers, the keypad interrupt, the
  touchscreen ADC, and the pen-down interrupt; `Serialize`
  and `Deserialize` implement version 3 save states of
  6,071,376 bytes (version 2 states are rejected; each CPU
  state is 8,388 bytes); `SaveRAM` and `SetSaveRAM` expose
  the AUX SPI save backing.
- `libretro`: the shell (DS-4). Core name "iTaK GoDS",
  extension nds, in the family C ABI shape. Both screens
  are presented in one 256x384 XRGB8888 frame, top screen
  in rows 0-191 and bottom screen in rows 192-383, in
  `Framebuffer` order (which already honors the POWCNT1
  display swap); the app crops or scales as it likes.
  The declared rate is the machine's own quotient,
  33,513,982 Hz over 560,190 ARM9 cycles per frame =
  59.8261 fps, and the audio rate is the sound unit's
  32,768 Hz. The libretro pointer device drives the
  touchscreen: coordinates span the presented frame, a
  press in the bottom half becomes `SetTouch` pixel
  coordinates in the bottom screen, and a press in the
  top half (or no press) lifts the pen. The microphone
  is not wired to a frontend source; `SetMicrophone`
  remains available to in-process hosts. SAVE_RAM is the
  512-byte AUX SPI EEPROM backing and SYSTEM_RAM is
  main RAM. A reset re-runs the direct boot from the
  loaded image. Load accepts a path or content.

## Conformance gates

The SingleStepTests ARM7TDMI corpus (generated from
NanoBoyAdvance) is the CPU gate. There is no ARM9 corpus: the
SingleStepTests/ProcessorTests tree has no ARM directory at all
(checked 2026-10-13), and the ARM7TDMI set lives in its own
repository. The corpus files are local test evidence only,
under `testroms/` (gitignored, never committed).

- ARM7 configuration: 2,250,000 of 2,250,000 tests pass (45
  files, full size). The default `go test` subset is 2,000 per
  file (90,000 tests), also 100 percent; set
  `NDS_TH_SUBSET=50000` for the full run and `NDS_TH_SEED` to
  change the seed. The harness compares registers, CPSR, all
  SPSRs, banked storage, the pipeline model, and every data
  read and write in order, by kind, size, address, and data.
  The corpus does not publish a trustworthy total cycle count,
  so cycle counts follow the published model and are not
  corpus-compared.
- ARM9 configuration: 66,000 of 66,000 gated tests pass (33
  files at the default subset). One file (`arm_mcr_mrc`) is
  excluded because CP15 exists on the ARM9, so those encodings
  are register transfers instead of the undefined trap the ARM7
  corpus expects. Eleven files are run in report-only mode
  (20,479 of 22,000 pass): every divergence in them is the
  documented ARMv5 interworking change (a value written to the
  PC selects the instruction state from bit 0, and the Thumb
  BLX register form writes LR), which the ARMv4T generator does
  not model. The counts stay visible in the test log rather
  than being hidden.
- The ARMv5TE additions are pinned by hand-derived unit vectors
  from the architecture documentation (`armcore_test.go`): CLZ
  edges (0, all-ones top bit, mid-word), QADD/QSUB saturation
  with a sticky Q flag, QDADD/QDSUB with first-stage doubling
  saturation, SMUL/SMLA half selection and sign, SMLA wrap with
  Q set and no clamping, SMULW/SMLAW shifted products, SMLALxy
  64-bit accumulation, LDRD/STRD round trip, MCR/MRC round
  trips including DTCM configuration and the high-vectors bit,
  BKPT prefetch abort with FSR/FAR, and serialize round trips.
- System gate: a synthetic cartridge whose ARM9 program writes
  a magic word into shared WRAM and whose ARM7 program reads,
  increments, and returns it under WRAMCNT ownership changes.
  A mid-run save state restores to a byte-identical
  continuation (shared WRAM and full state compared).
- DS-2 gates (all synthetic, no game data): per-engine text
  BG pixel probes (engine A red/green tiles, an independent
  engine B scene), affine and extended bitmap BG probes,
  bitmap OBJ probe, master brightness up and down to the
  exact 6-bit values, alpha blend to the exact blended value,
  VRAM display mode reading a bank directly, capture writing
  a blended copy into the target bank (verified by reading
  the bank back: 0xBC0F for red blended with blue at
  EVA=EVB=8), a VRAMCNT bank moved between assignments
  changing extended palette rendering, timer counts exact
  over long advances plus cascade, ARM9 DMA immediate and
  GX FIFO sink counts, IPC FIFO loopback in both directions
  with IRQ flags, IPCSYNC nibble with IRQ, card chip ID and
  card DMA reads from the loaded image, AUX SPI EEPROM
  write/read round trip, touchscreen ADC values derived from
  SetTouch (X=100 reads 0x67D through the documented map),
  firmware settings block CRC, and an RTC that ticks one
  second per 60 frames. System gates: the direct-boot gate
  (ARM9 program verifies the boot flag at 0x027FFFFA and its
  installed stack pointer; ARM7 verifies its entry state and
  answers through the IPC FIFO), an ARM9 IRQ handler in ITCM
  counting exactly one VBlank per frame, ARM7 timer IRQ
  asserted while the ARM9 controller stays masked, display
  swap exchanging the Framebuffer order, and a determinism
  gate: direct boot, a two-engine scene with a capture pass,
  a mid-run save, and a restored continuation with identical
  dual framebuffers and identical state bytes.

- DS-3 gates (all synthetic): identity clip matrix readback
  bit-exact against the loaded matrix, POS_TEST matching a
  hand-computed transform, matrix stack pointer and overflow
  behavior across 32 pushes, packed GXFIFO command decode,
  FIFO IRQ mode conditions, RAM_COUNT and the swap pause, a
  red triangle covering the screen center and not a corner,
  textured quads sampling exact texels (256-color palette,
  A3I5 alpha blended over the clear color to the documented
  values, a 4x4 compressed block rendering its four
  hand-computed colors), nearer-quad depth wins, the
  equal-depth flag drawing a second polygon the plain case
  rejects, wireframe edges with a transparent interior, toon
  table shading, fog at full density, the clear image bitmap
  rear plane, a PCM16 loop tone measured within 2 percent,
  ADPCM decode of an encoded sine with bounded error, a PSG
  square pitch measured within 2 percent, pan full-left
  zeroing the right channel, capture RAM matching the drained
  output sample for sample, microphone ADC values through
  the SPI path including the idle center, and the DS-3
  determinism gate: two quads (flat translucent near,
  textured far) with fog on, a PCM loop tone plus a PSG
  square, a mid-run save, and a restored continuation with
  identical dual framebuffers, identical next 2,048 stereo
  audio samples (4,382 int16 values compared), and identical
  state bytes.

## Boot approach: no BIOS, ever

No DS BIOS or firmware image is shipped, needed, or accepted
by this module. Boot is the documented direct-boot path:
`LoadROM` stages the ARM9 binary with WRAMCNT = 3 and the
ARM7 binary with WRAMCNT = 0 (leaving WRAMCNT = 0: at boot
the shared WRAM belongs to the ARM7 and games reprogram it),
copies the 0x200-byte header to 0x027FFE00, writes the chip
ID to 0x027FF800 and 0x027FF804, the header bytes 0x20-0x3F
to 0x027FFC00, and the boot flag halfword 0x0001 to
0x027FFFFA, sets POWCNT1 to 0x020F, and installs each CPU's
entry register state: CPSR = system mode, SVC stack
0x03007FE0 and IRQ stack 0x03007FA0 on the ARM9 (0x0380FDC0
and 0x0380FD80 on the ARM7), user stack at the end of the
ARM9 binary's load region (0x0380FE00 on the ARM7), and
r12 = r14 = the header entry point. The CPUs stay halted
until `Start`. The chip ID is a synthetic constant of this
module (0x00001FC2, in the documented format); real chip IDs
belong to manufactured cartridges. Reads of the hardware
BIOS windows (ARM9 at 0xFFFF0000, ARM7 at 0x00000000) return
the side's open-bus value, the documented approximation:
there are no dumped BIOS bytes in this design, by policy.
One consequence: ARM9 interrupt delivery is fully testable
(its vectors fetch from ITCM), while the ARM7's vectors fetch
from its BIOS window, so ARM7 interrupt correctness is gated
at the IF/IRQ-line level in this slice; the real BIOS
dispatch through the RAM handler pointer is a DS-4 shell
concern.

## Encryption scope

The header parser performs no decryption, embeds no keys,
and reads the secure area CRC field without interpreting the
secure area. DS-2's card command unit is always in the plain
(unencrypted command) state: our boot path never runs the
KEY1/KEY2 encryption setup, and real games only encrypt
after talking to a real BIOS, which this module does not
have. Commands are parsed plain and that is stated here
rather than hidden: the documented data read commands
(0x00 and 0xB7) read from the loaded image, the chip ID
command (0xB8) answers the module's synthetic chip ID, the
KEY1 activation marker (0x3C) is accepted without changing
state, and any other command returns a zero-filled block.

## Honesty notes and approximations

- Caches are NOT simulated. CP15 cache and MPU configuration
  registers are stored, but accesses go straight to backing
  memory and no memory protection is enforced (protection
  enforced: none). The TCM windows are real: the bus decodes
  them from the live CP15 registers. The physical DTCM backing
  store is 32 KB; a configured region larger than the store
  wraps within it (the DS part is 16 KB, so real software
  stays inside).
- Cycle model is flat. Both CPUs use the ARM7TDMI S/N/I cycle
  counts; the ARM9's improved multiplier timing and cache
  timing are not modeled. Timing is budgeted per frame.
- The C flag left by a flag-setting multiply follows the
  ARM7TDMI Booth carry model on both CPUs (the published
  carry-save adder model, as used by the corpus generator).
  The ARM9 architecture leaves that flag unaffected; the value
  is unpredictable on ARMv4, so conforming programs cannot
  observe the difference.
- Architecturally unpredictable forms (multiply or swap into
  the PC, and friends) follow the corpus reference behavior.
  The Thumb condition-14 branch encoding, architecturally
  undefined, evaluates as always, matching the reference.
- The cartridge image is mapped linearly in the 0x08000000
  window for foundation work. A real DS game card streams
  through a serial command interface; direct boot here works
  from the parsed image and never executes from that window.
- Data aborts are raised through the CPU API (and by BKPT for
  prefetch aborts); the bus never faults, so the FSR values
  written on abort are simple status codes, to be refined
  when a faulting bus device exists.
- DS-2 video simplifications, all deliberate: display mode 3
  (main RAM display) reads 15bpp pixels from main RAM at the
  address latched by the DISP_MMEM_FIFO register; the display
  FIFO itself is not modeled. Capture source A is engine A's
  composed line before master brightness (the hardware's
  3D+2D mix; since DS-3 the 3D layer takes part through the
  same BG0 composition); source B is read from a VRAM bank
  at the same coordinates the write offset addresses;
  capture completes at the end of the last captured line. On
  engine A a BG0 selected as the 3D layer (DISPCNT bit 3) is
  filled by the gx package through the `Video.Line3D`
  provider, and the condition stays exposed as
  `Video.BG0Is3D`.
  Mode 6 on engine B behaves as mode 5, and the mode 6 large
  bitmap reads from BG space offset 0. Mosaic quantizes the
  fetch coordinates (a simplification of the hardware's
  sample-and-hold). LCDC CPU access to the physical VRAM
  banks stays mapped regardless of the engine assignments.
  The published VRAMCNT tables for banks F and G carry
  overlapping mode encodings; the resolution used here is
  documented in `video/vram.go`.
- Correction found in DS-3: DS-2 decoded the VRAMCNT byte
  layout shifted by one bit (its enable was bit 0 and its
  MST bits 1-2, with fixtures written in that same private
  convention, so its gates passed self-consistently). The
  published GBATEK bank table puts MST at bits 0-2, OFS at
  bits 3-4, and the enable at bit 7 (a BG A texture bank is
  0x81, not 0x03). DS-3 rewrote the decode and the fixtures
  to the published layout, including bank C MST 4 (BG B),
  bank D MST 4 (OBJ B), the F/G extended-palette slot pairs,
  banks A/B MST 2 (OBJ A only, at the OFS-selected 128 KB),
  and bank I MST 2 (OBJ B at offset 0). Published
  documentation wins over the earlier code, per this
  module's standing rule.
- DS-3 geometry and rendering model choices: the geometry
  engine executes commands eagerly as they are written (the
  hardware's execution timing is not modeled); the
  rendering engine draws the whole display list at the
  VBlank swap rather than per scanline, so mid-frame GX
  register changes apply from the next frame. Clipping is
  standard homogeneous clipping against the six view-volume
  planes (the hardware's near-plane behavior simplified, as
  briefed); a polygon crossing the far plane with
  POLYGON_ATTR bit 12 clear is dropped whole, and clipped
  strip remainders stay part of their polygon. RAM_COUNT
  counts the buffer being built (the counts reset at the
  swap, as documented). TEXIMAGE_PARAM and PLTT_BASE latch
  into each polygon at BEGIN_VTXS. Lighting evaluates the
  documented equations in float64 with 0..1 components and
  rounds to 5-bit (the hardware's fixed-point rounding may
  differ by one LSB); with the shininess table disabled the
  raw squared specular level is used, which GBATEK
  describes as equivalent to the table holding linearly
  increasing values. Shadow shading mode falls back to
  modulation. EDGE_COLOR is stored only (edge marking is
  not drawn); DISP_1DOT_DEPTH drives the documented 1-dot
  polygon rule (a failing 1-dot polygon is skipped whole;
  the hardware nuance of rendering it with its first
  vertex's attributes is not implemented). The equal-depth
  tolerance is GBATEK's fixed plus/minus 0x200 of the 24-bit
  depth (it is not derived from DISP_1DOT_DEPTH; the DS-3
  brief's guess there was wrong and the document wins).
  SWAP_BUFFERS bit 1 follows GBATEK (0 selects Z depth, 1
  selects W depth), the reverse of the brief's reading; the
  Z depth is ((z+w) times 0xFFFFFF)/(2w) and the W depth is
  w shifted left 8 (W = 1.0 maps to 0x100000), both clamped
  to 24 bits. Translucent Y-sorting uses the polygon's
  maximum screen Y ascending, stable for ties. The span
  rules follow GBATEK's polygon-size notes: opaque polygons
  without edge marking or anti-aliasing exclude their lower
  and right edges; translucent, edge-marked, and
  anti-aliased polygons render full size; anti-aliasing
  itself is not computed (it changes only the size rule).
  GXSTAT bit 15 written set clears the stack error and
  resets the projection and texture stack pointers (GBATEK
  says the projection pointer, probably also texture).
  SHININESS (command 0x34) is implemented: GBATEK's
  invalid-command list omits it while its own command table
  documents it, and the table wins.
- DS-3 audio model choices: SAD, TMR, PNT, and LEN latch at
  channel start (volume, pan, duty, format, and repeat are
  read live). The channel sample value is held between
  steps with no interpolation. Channel rates use GBATEK's
  formula 16,756,991/(65536 minus TMR) exactly with a
  rational step accumulator (the brief's halved formula was
  wrong). The mixer produces exactly 32,768 samples per
  16,756,991 cycles (GBATEK's nominal figure; the raw clock
  division gives 32,728.5, a 0.12 percent discrepancy inside
  GBATEK's rounded numbers, stated rather than hidden).
  SOUNDBIAS carries only the bias on the DS (the amplitude
  bits the brief mentioned are a GBA feature). The output
  source selects name channels 1 and 3 (the brief said 1
  and 2; the document wins), and capture pairs are channel
  0 (capture 0) and channel 2 (capture 1) with the
  associated channel added in. Capture runs at the mixer
  rate (GBATEK times it from the channel 1 and 3 timers;
  that sharing is not modeled), captures the final post-bias
  output for the mixer source (so captured samples equal the
  drained output exactly under this model), clamps instead
  of emulating the two documented hardware capture bugs,
  and stores PCM8 captures as byte(value shifted right 8
  plus 128). Noise polarity: positive when the LFSR output
  bit is 0. The output buffer is capped at 65,536 stereo
  samples and drops new samples on overflow. The sound unit
  raises no interrupts (there is no per-channel IRQ). The
  microphone consumes one host sample per SPI aux-channel
  read; with no stream (or an exhausted one) the ADC reads
  the idle center value 0x800.
- DS-2 device simplifications: immediate DMA transfers run
  synchronously inside the register write. The ARM7 DMA
  special timing (sound FIFO and card/wifi triggers) has no
  source in this module and completes cleanly; the ARM9
  GBA-cart timing runs immediately against the open-bus
  window. Writing a timer's CNT_L loads its counter
  immediately. Reading an empty IPC FIFO returns 0 (hardware
  returns the last received word). The wifi interrupt bit
  exists with no source.
- The touchscreen, RTC, and firmware are documented minimal
  stubs. The touchscreen ADC uses a linear map consistent
  with the generated calibration (edge 0x100, far edge
  0xF00), and the pen-up ADC reads 0. The RTC is a simplified
  byte model (the real chip is bit-serial) ticking from the
  fixed epoch 2000-01-01 00:00:00 at one second per 60
  frames. The firmware flash image is generated in code in
  the documented format, never dumped: erased 0xFF fill with
  two user settings blocks (empty nickname, default
  calibration, settings CRC16 at offset 0x70 over bytes
  [0:0x70], this module's internally consistent placement);
  SPI flash write commands are ignored. The AUX SPI save
  memory models the 512-byte EEPROM class.

## Roadmap

- DS-2: done.
- DS-3: done.
- DS-4: done (this slice). The libretro shell is built
  as `libgo_ds.so` (see the `libretro` package notes
  above for the presentation, pointer, and rate
  contract). The enginetest gate
  (`system.TestDS4EngineGate`) runs synthetic guest
  programs on both CPUs: the ARM9 boots through the
  real direct boot (milestone 1), uploads VRAM data
  and programs both 2D engines plus a GX scene (a
  textured far quad under a flat near quad, with a 2D
  text tile composited over the 3D layer) and swaps
  buffers (2), starts a PCM loop tone on the ARM7 via
  the IPC FIFO (3), and has the ARM7 poll the
  touchscreen over SPI (4). The milestone log reads
  [1 2 3 4] in order; the touch ADC values are exactly
  0x67D and 0x565 for a pen at (100, 60); stacked
  frame probes are exact (2D tile magenta over the 3D
  layer, textured texels red and green at their
  documented positions, near quad green, engine B tile
  white over a black backdrop); the tone measures
  442.37 Hz against the 442.28 Hz the documented
  channel formula predicts; a mid-run save restores to
  byte-identical framebuffers, continuation audio, and
  state bytes. The same ROM then went through the
  shared harness (`go_backend/cmd/enginetest`) against
  the built shell library: ALL TESTS PASSED (256x384
  non-blank video, non-silent audio, save state of
  exactly 6,071,376 bytes, restore hash equal to the
  save-point hash). App wiring preparation (nothing
  pushed): the DS slot in
  `go_backend/internal/core/types.go` and the DS entry
  in `flutter_ui/lib/main.dart` now name iTaK GoDS and
  `libgo_ds.so`; `tools/autobuild-server.sh` has no
  64-bit branch or core list yet, so the script side
  waits on the parent's pipeline branch. The core is
  complete. Remaining honest gaps: wifi is a documented
  stub with no source behind its interrupt bit; the
  retail encrypted card protocol (KEY1/KEY2 secure
  area) is out of scope and the card model stays in
  the plain command state; the GX executes commands
  eagerly and draws the whole list at the swap rather
  than per scanline (DS-3 model); lighting is computed
  in float64 and rounded to 5-bit color (possible
  1-LSB differences from hardware fixed point); the
  ARM9 CPU cannot write the 0x06000000 BG VRAM window
  (CPU VRAM writes go through the LCDC window, a DS-1
  bus simplification the DS-4 guest is written
  against). The DS-2 boot gate failure DS-3 observed
  once at `system/ds2_test.go:151` has not reproduced:
  DS-4 ran the system package at `-count=10` (ten
  consecutive full passes including the boot gate),
  on top of DS-3's and the parent's earlier green
  runs.

==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/audio/audio.go ====================

// Package audio implements the Nintendo DS sound unit from
// the published GBATEK documentation: sixteen channels with
// PCM8, PCM16 and IMA ADPCM playback, PSG square waves on
// channels 8 to 13, noise on channels 14 and 15, a stereo
// mixer with master volume and bias, and two sound capture
// units that write back into memory.
//
// Stated model choices and simplifications:
//
//   - The channel sample value is held between channel steps,
//     with no interpolation.
//   - Volume, divider, pan, duty, repeat mode and format are
//     read from the live control register, while SAD, TMR,
//     PNT and LEN are latched when a channel starts. GBATEK
//     does not document live reload of those address and
//     timing registers, so this package latches them, and a
//     register write takes effect on the next start.
//   - Capture runs at the mixer rate of 32768 Hz, one sample
//     per output sample. GBATEK shares the channel 1 and 3
//     timers for capture timing; this package does not model
//     that sharing.
//   - The two documented hardware capture bugs (an all
//     negative result case and an overflow wrap case) are not
//     emulated. Captured values are clamped instead.
//   - PCM8 capture stores byte(value shifted right 8 plus
//     128), so a captured byte round trips with the PCM8
//     playback scale used here.
//   - Noise polarity: a generated sample is positive when the
//     LFSR output bit is 0 and negative when it is 1.
//   - The internal output buffer is capped at 65536 stereo
//     samples. On overflow the new samples are dropped.
//
// The unit raises no interrupts: the DS sound unit has no
// per channel interrupt source.
package audio

// Memory is the byte addressed memory the sound unit reads
// sample data from and writes captured data to. Read16 and
// Write16 are little endian.
type Memory interface {
	Read8(addr uint32) uint8
	Read16(addr uint32) uint16
	Write8(addr uint32, v uint8)
	Write16(addr uint32, v uint16)
}

const (
	clockHz   = 16756991
	outRate   = 32768
	numChan   = 16
	outCap    = 65536
	regBase   = 0x400
	regEnd    = 0x520
	cntStart  = 1 << 31
	cntHold   = 1 << 15
	sndEnable = 1 << 15
)

// adpcmStep is the standard IMA ADPCM step table. It has 89
// entries, for step indices 0 to 88.
var adpcmStep = [...]int32{
	7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17,
	19, 21, 23, 25, 28, 31, 34, 37, 41, 45,
	50, 55, 60, 66, 73, 80, 88, 97, 107, 118,
	130, 143, 157, 173, 190, 209, 230, 253, 279, 307,
	337, 371, 408, 449, 494, 544, 598, 658, 724, 796,
	876, 963, 1060, 1166, 1282, 1411, 1552, 1707, 1878, 2066,
	2272, 2499, 2749, 3024, 3327, 3660, 4026, 4428, 4871, 5358,
	5894, 6484, 7132, 7845, 8630, 9493, 10442, 11487, 12635, 13899,
	15289, 16818, 18500, 20350, 22385, 24623, 27086, 29794, 32767,
}

// adpcmIndex adjusts the step index from the low three bits
// of a data nibble.
var adpcmIndex = [...]int32{-1, -1, -1, -1, 2, 4, 6, 8}

func init() {
	if len(adpcmStep) != 89 {
		panic("audio: ADPCM step table must have 89 entries")
	}
	if len(adpcmIndex) != 8 {
		panic("audio: ADPCM index table must have 8 entries")
	}
}

var divShift = [...]uint{0, 1, 2, 4}

type channel struct {
	idx int

	// Live and stored registers.
	cnt    uint32
	sadReg uint32
	tmrReg uint16
	pntReg uint16
	lenReg uint32

	// Registers latched at channel start.
	lSad uint32
	lTmr uint16
	lPnt uint16
	lLen uint32

	busy       bool
	hang       bool
	holdActive bool

	pos uint64
	acc uint64

	pred      int32
	index     int32
	snapPred  int32
	snapIndex int32
	snapTaken bool

	lfsr  uint16
	phase uint8

	cur  int32
	hold int32
}

type captureUnit struct {
	cntReg uint8
	dadReg uint32
	lenReg uint16

	busy      bool
	lDad      uint32
	lLenWords uint32
	lCnt      uint8
	posBytes  uint32
}

// Sound is the whole DS sound unit.
type Sound struct {
	mem      Memory
	ch       [numChan]channel
	caps     [2]captureUnit
	soundCnt uint32
	bias     uint32
	phase    uint64
	out      []int16
}

// New builds a sound unit reading and writing through mem.
// The bias register starts at its power on value 0x200 and
// every other register starts at zero.
func New(mem Memory) *Sound {
	s := &Sound{mem: mem, bias: 0x200}
	for i := range s.ch {
		s.ch[i].idx = i
		s.ch[i].lfsr = 0x7FFF
	}
	return s
}

func clamp16(v int32) int32 {
	if v > 32767 {
		return 32767
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return -32768
	}
	return v
}

// getU32 extracts the unit of the given size at the byte lane
// of off from a 32-bit register value.
func getU32(v uint32, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return (v >> ((off & 3) * 8)) & 0xFF
	case 2:
		return (v >> ((off & 2) * 8)) & 0xFFFF
	}
	return v
}

// putU32 merges a written unit of the given size at the byte
// lane of off into a 32-bit register value.
func putU32(v uint32, off uint32, size int, val uint32) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		sh := (off & 3) * 8
		return v&^(0xFF<<sh) | (val&0xFF)<<sh
	case 2:
		sh := (off & 2) * 8
		return v&^(0xFFFF<<sh) | (val&0xFFFF)<<sh
	}
	return val
}

// writeTouches reports whether a write starting at off and
// spanning size bytes includes the byte at addr.
func writeTouches(off uint32, size int, addr uint32) bool {
	if size <= 0 {
		return false
	}
	return off <= addr && addr < off+uint32(size)
}

func (s *Sound) capCntWord() uint32 {
	var w uint32
	for i := range s.caps {
		b := uint32(s.caps[i].cntReg & 0x7F)
		if s.caps[i].busy {
			b |= 0x80
		}
		w |= b << (8 * uint(i))
	}
	return w
}

// ReadIO claims ARM7 IO offsets 0x400 to 0x51F.
func (s *Sound) ReadIO(off uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	if off < regBase || off >= regEnd {
		return 0, false
	}
	base := off &^ 3
	var word uint32
	switch {
	case base < 0x500:
		idx := (base - regBase) / 16
		rel := (base - regBase) % 16
		ch := &s.ch[idx]
		switch rel {
		case 0:
			word = ch.cnt &^ cntStart
			if ch.busy {
				word |= cntStart
			}
		case 4:
			word = ch.sadReg
		case 8:
			word = uint32(ch.tmrReg) | uint32(ch.pntReg)<<16
		case 12:
			word = ch.lenReg
		}
	case base == 0x500:
		word = s.soundCnt
	case base == 0x504:
		word = s.bias
	case base == 0x508:
		word = s.capCntWord()
	case base == 0x510:
		word = s.caps[0].dadReg
	case base == 0x514:
		word = uint32(s.caps[0].lenReg)
	case base == 0x518:
		word = s.caps[1].dadReg
	case base == 0x51C:
		word = uint32(s.caps[1].lenReg)
	}
	return getU32(word, off, size), true
}

// WriteIO claims ARM7 IO offsets 0x400 to 0x51F.
func (s *Sound) WriteIO(off uint32, size int, val uint32) bool {
	if off < regBase || off >= regEnd {
		return false
	}
	switch {
	case off < 0x500:
		rel := off - regBase
		idx := rel / 16
		r := rel % 16
		ch := &s.ch[idx]
		switch {
		case r < 4:
			ch.cnt = putU32(ch.cnt, off, size, val)
			startAddr := regBase + idx*16 + 3
			if writeTouches(off, size, startAddr) {
				if ch.cnt&cntStart != 0 {
					s.startChannel(int(idx))
				} else {
					s.stopChannel(ch)
				}
			}
		case r < 8:
			ch.sadReg = putU32(ch.sadReg, off, size, val) & 0x07FFFFFC
		case r < 12:
			w := uint32(ch.tmrReg) | uint32(ch.pntReg)<<16
			w = putU32(w, off, size, val)
			ch.tmrReg = uint16(w)
			ch.pntReg = uint16(w >> 16)
		default:
			ch.lenReg = putU32(ch.lenReg, off, size, val) & 0x003FFFFF
		}
	case off < 0x504:
		s.soundCnt = putU32(s.soundCnt, off, size, val)
	case off < 0x508:
		s.bias = putU32(s.bias, off, size, val)
	case off < 0x50C:
		old := uint32(s.caps[0].cntReg) | uint32(s.caps[1].cntReg)<<8
		nw := putU32(old, off, size, val)
		for i := range s.caps {
			byteAddr := uint32(0x508 + i)
			if writeTouches(off, size, byteAddr) {
				s.caps[i].cntReg = uint8(nw >> (8 * uint(i)))
				if s.caps[i].cntReg&0x80 != 0 {
					s.startCapture(i)
				} else {
					s.caps[i].busy = false
				}
			}
		}
	case off < 0x510:
		// Unused gap between the capture control bytes and
		// the capture destination registers. Writes land
		// nowhere, but the offset is claimed.
	case off < 0x514:
		s.caps[0].dadReg = putU32(s.caps[0].dadReg, off, size, val)
	case off < 0x518:
		s.caps[0].lenReg = uint16(putU32(uint32(s.caps[0].lenReg), off, size, val))
	case off < 0x51C:
		s.caps[1].dadReg = putU32(s.caps[1].dadReg, off, size, val)
	default:
		s.caps[1].lenReg = uint16(putU32(uint32(s.caps[1].lenReg), off, size, val))
	}
	return true
}

func (ch *channel) format() uint32 {
	return (ch.cnt >> 29) & 3
}

func (ch *channel) totalWords() uint64 {
	return uint64(ch.lPnt) + uint64(ch.lLen)
}

func (ch *channel) totalSamples(format uint32) uint64 {
	tw := ch.totalWords()
	switch format {
	case 0:
		return tw * 4
	case 1:
		return tw * 2
	case 2:
		if tw == 0 {
			return 0
		}
		return 8 * (tw - 1)
	}
	return 0
}

func (ch *channel) loopStartSample(format uint32) uint64 {
	switch format {
	case 0:
		return uint64(ch.lPnt) * 4
	case 1:
		return uint64(ch.lPnt) * 2
	case 2:
		if ch.lPnt == 0 {
			return 0
		}
		return 8 * (uint64(ch.lPnt) - 1)
	}
	return 0
}

// startChannel latches SAD, TMR, PNT and LEN, resets the
// playback position and loads the first sample immediately.
// A total length below four words hangs the channel for the
// sample formats: it stays busy and outputs nothing until a
// control write stops it.
func (s *Sound) startChannel(idx int) {
	ch := &s.ch[idx]
	ch.busy = true
	ch.holdActive = false
	ch.acc = 0
	ch.pos = 0
	ch.lSad = ch.sadReg & 0x07FFFFFC
	ch.lTmr = ch.tmrReg
	ch.lPnt = ch.pntReg
	ch.lLen = ch.lenReg & 0x003FFFFF
	ch.pred = 0
	ch.index = 0
	ch.snapPred = 0
	ch.snapIndex = 0
	ch.snapTaken = false
	ch.lfsr = 0x7FFF
	ch.phase = 0
	ch.cur = 0
	ch.hold = 0
	ch.hang = false

	format := ch.format()
	if format == 3 {
		if idx >= 14 {
			ch.stepNoise()
		}
		return
	}
	if ch.totalWords() < 4 {
		ch.hang = true
		return
	}
	if format == 2 {
		s.loadADPCMHeader(ch)
		if ch.loopStartSample(format) == 0 {
			ch.snapPred = ch.pred
			ch.snapIndex = ch.index
			ch.snapTaken = true
		}
	}
	s.loadSample(ch)
}

// stopChannel stops a channel from a control write with the
// start bit clear. The hold bit in the new control value
// decides whether the last value keeps sounding.
func (s *Sound) stopChannel(ch *channel) {
	var raw int32
	if ch.busy {
		raw = ch.rawCurrent()
	} else if ch.holdActive {
		raw = ch.hold
	}
	ch.busy = false
	if ch.cnt&cntHold != 0 {
		ch.holdActive = true
		ch.hold = raw
	} else {
		ch.holdActive = false
	}
}

func (s *Sound) loadADPCMHeader(ch *channel) {
	lo := s.mem.Read16(ch.lSad)
	hi := s.mem.Read16(ch.lSad + 2)
	hdr := uint32(lo) | uint32(hi)<<16
	ch.pred = int32(int16(uint16(hdr)))
	idx := int32((hdr >> 16) & 0x7F)
	if idx > 88 {
		idx = 88
	}
	ch.index = idx
}

func (s *Sound) loadSample(ch *channel) {
	switch ch.format() {
	case 0:
		b := s.mem.Read8(ch.lSad + uint32(ch.pos))
		ch.cur = (int32(b) - 128) << 8
	case 1:
		v := s.mem.Read16(ch.lSad + uint32(ch.pos)*2)
		ch.cur = int32(int16(v))
	case 2:
		addr := ch.lSad + 4 + uint32(ch.pos/2)
		b := s.mem.Read8(addr)
		var nib uint32
		if ch.pos%2 == 0 {
			nib = uint32(b & 0x0F)
		} else {
			nib = uint32(b >> 4)
		}
		s.decodeADPCM(ch, nib)
	}
}

// decodeADPCM applies one nibble to the predictor and step
// index. The emitted sample is the predictor after the
// nibble has been applied.
func (s *Sound) decodeADPCM(ch *channel, nib uint32) {
	step := adpcmStep[ch.index]
	diff := step >> 3
	if nib&1 != 0 {
		diff += step >> 2
	}
	if nib&2 != 0 {
		diff += step >> 1
	}
	if nib&4 != 0 {
		diff += step
	}
	pred := ch.pred
	if nib&8 != 0 {
		pred -= diff
	} else {
		pred += diff
	}
	ch.pred = clamp16(pred)
	idx := ch.index + adpcmIndex[nib&7]
	if idx < 0 {
		idx = 0
	}
	if idx > 88 {
		idx = 88
	}
	ch.index = idx
	ch.cur = ch.pred
}

// stepNoise advances the 15 bit LFSR once and generates the
// next noise sample. Polarity choice: the sample is positive
// when the output bit taken from the LFSR is 0 and negative
// when it is 1.
func (ch *channel) stepNoise() {
	outBit := ch.lfsr & 1
	ch.lfsr >>= 1
	if outBit != 0 {
		ch.lfsr ^= 0x6000
	}
	if outBit == 0 {
		ch.cur = 32512
	} else {
		ch.cur = -32512
	}
}

// rawCurrent is the sample value before volume and pan.
func (ch *channel) rawCurrent() int32 {
	if ch.format() == 3 && ch.idx >= 8 && ch.idx <= 13 {
		duty := (ch.cnt >> 24) & 7
		if uint32(ch.phase) < duty+1 {
			return 32512
		}
		return -32512
	}
	return ch.cur
}

// monoValue is the channel value after the volume multiplier
// and divisor, before pan. Capture and the direct channel 1
// and 3 outputs use this value.
func (ch *channel) monoValue() int32 {
	if ch.hang && ch.busy {
		return 0
	}
	var raw int32
	if ch.busy {
		raw = ch.rawCurrent()
	} else if ch.holdActive {
		raw = ch.hold
	} else {
		return 0
	}
	vol := int32(ch.cnt & 0x7F)
	v := (raw * vol) >> 7
	v >>= divShift[(ch.cnt>>8)&3]
	return v
}

// stepChannel advances a running channel by one channel
// sample, handling the end of the data: a loop wrap restores
// the loop start (and, for ADPCM, the snapshot taken when
// playback first reached the loop word; a loop start at word
// zero re-reads the header), and the manual, one shot and
// prohibited repeat modes stop the channel, honouring hold.
func (s *Sound) stepChannel(ch *channel) {
	format := ch.format()
	if format == 3 {
		switch {
		case ch.idx >= 8 && ch.idx <= 13:
			ch.phase = (ch.phase + 1) & 7
			ch.pos++
		case ch.idx >= 14:
			ch.pos++
			ch.stepNoise()
		}
		return
	}
	total := ch.totalSamples(format)
	ch.pos++
	if ch.pos >= total {
		repeat := (ch.cnt >> 27) & 3
		if repeat == 1 {
			ch.pos = ch.loopStartSample(format)
			if format == 2 {
				if ch.lPnt == 0 {
					s.loadADPCMHeader(ch)
					ch.snapPred = ch.pred
					ch.snapIndex = ch.index
					ch.snapTaken = true
				} else if ch.snapTaken {
					ch.pred = ch.snapPred
					ch.index = ch.snapIndex
				}
			}
			if ch.pos < total {
				s.loadSample(ch)
			}
			return
		}
		ch.busy = false
		if ch.cnt&cntHold != 0 {
			ch.holdActive = true
			ch.hold = ch.cur
		} else {
			ch.holdActive = false
		}
		return
	}
	if format == 2 && !ch.snapTaken && ch.pos == ch.loopStartSample(format) {
		// The position has just crossed into the loop word.
		// Snapshot the decoder state before this sample is
		// decoded, so a later wrap can restore it and replay
		// the loop region identically.
		ch.snapPred = ch.pred
		ch.snapIndex = ch.index
		ch.snapTaken = true
	}
	s.loadSample(ch)
}

// Advance runs the unit for the given number of ARM7 cycles.
func (s *Sound) Advance(cycles uint64) {
	s.phase += cycles * outRate
	n := s.phase / clockHz
	s.phase %= clockHz
	var i uint64
	for i = 0; i < n; i++ {
		s.produce()
	}
}

// produce mixes one output sample from the current channel
// values, appends the stereo result to the output buffer,
// runs the capture units for that sample, and then steps
// every running channel toward the next output sample. The
// first sample loaded at channel start is therefore the
// first sample heard.
func (s *Sound) produce() {
	var mono [numChan]int32
	for i := range s.ch {
		mono[i] = s.ch[i].monoValue()
	}

	add0 := s.caps[0].busy && s.caps[0].lCnt&1 != 0
	add1 := s.caps[1].busy && s.caps[1].lCnt&1 != 0

	var mixL, mixR int64
	for i := range s.ch {
		ch := &s.ch[i]
		v := int64(mono[i])
		switch i {
		case 0:
			if add0 {
				v += int64(mono[1])
			}
		case 1:
			if add0 || s.soundCnt&(1<<12) != 0 {
				continue
			}
		case 2:
			if add1 {
				v += int64(mono[3])
			}
		case 3:
			if add1 || s.soundCnt&(1<<13) != 0 {
				continue
			}
		}
		pan := int64((ch.cnt >> 16) & 0x7F)
		mixL += v * (127 - pan) / 127
		mixR += v * pan / 127
	}

	left := s.mixOut(selectSource((s.soundCnt>>8)&3, mixL, &mono))
	right := s.mixOut(selectSource((s.soundCnt>>10)&3, mixR, &mono))

	if len(s.out)/2 < outCap {
		s.out = append(s.out, left, right)
	}
	s.runCapture(0, left, right, &mono)
	s.runCapture(1, left, right, &mono)

	for i := range s.ch {
		ch := &s.ch[i]
		if !ch.busy || ch.hang {
			continue
		}
		ch.acc += clockHz
		threshold := uint64(65536-uint32(ch.lTmr)) * outRate
		for ch.busy && ch.acc >= threshold {
			ch.acc -= threshold
			s.stepChannel(ch)
		}
	}
}

func selectSource(code uint32, mix int64, mono *[numChan]int32) int64 {
	switch code {
	case 1:
		return int64(mono[1])
	case 2:
		return int64(mono[3])
	case 3:
		return int64(mono[1]) + int64(mono[3])
	}
	return mix
}

// mixOut applies the master volume and the bias to one
// selected side value and returns the final output sample.
// With the master enable clear the selected value is muted
// and only the bias contributes.
func (s *Sound) mixOut(sel int64) int16 {
	var t int64
	if s.soundCnt&sndEnable != 0 {
		t = (sel * int64(s.soundCnt&0x7F)) >> 7
		t >>= 6
		if t > 511 {
			t = 511
		}
		if t < -512 {
			t = -512
		}
	}
	out := (t + int64(s.bias&0x3FF) - 0x200) << 6
	if out > 32767 {
		out = 32767
	}
	if out < -32768 {
		out = -32768
	}
	return int16(out)
}

func (s *Sound) startCapture(i int) {
	cap := &s.caps[i]
	cap.busy = true
	cap.posBytes = 0
	cap.lDad = cap.dadReg
	words := uint32(cap.lenReg)
	if words == 0 {
		words = 1
	}
	cap.lLenWords = words
	cap.lCnt = cap.cntReg
}

// runCapture writes one captured sample for a capture unit.
// The mixer source is the final output sample for the side;
// the channel source is the channel mono value, plus the
// associated channel mono value when the addition bit is
// set, clamped to int16 range.
func (s *Sound) runCapture(i int, left int16, right int16, mono *[numChan]int32) {
	cap := &s.caps[i]
	if !cap.busy {
		return
	}
	var val int32
	if cap.lCnt&(1<<1) == 0 {
		if i == 0 {
			val = int32(left)
		} else {
			val = int32(right)
		}
	} else {
		if i == 0 {
			val = mono[0]
			if cap.lCnt&1 != 0 {
				val += mono[1]
			}
		} else {
			val = mono[2]
			if cap.lCnt&1 != 0 {
				val += mono[3]
			}
		}
		val = clamp16(val)
	}
	total := cap.lLenWords * 4
	addr := cap.lDad + cap.posBytes
	if cap.lCnt&(1<<3) == 0 {
		s.mem.Write16(addr, uint16(int16(val)))
		cap.posBytes += 2
	} else {
		b := uint8((clamp16(val) >> 8) + 128)
		s.mem.Write8(addr, b)
		cap.posBytes++
	}
	if cap.posBytes >= total {
		if cap.lCnt&(1<<2) == 0 {
			cap.posBytes %= total
		} else {
			cap.busy = false
			cap.posBytes = total
		}
	}
}

// Drain returns the buffered stereo output samples,
// interleaved left then right, and clears the buffer.
func (s *Sound) Drain() []int16 {
	out := s.out
	s.out = nil
	if out == nil {
		return []int16{}
	}
	return out
}

package audio_test

import (
	"math"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/audio"
)

// fakeMem is a byte backed Memory for the tests.
type fakeMem struct {
	b []byte
}

func newFakeMem() *fakeMem {
	return &fakeMem{b: make([]byte, 1<<20)}
}

func (m *fakeMem) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	if int(addr) >= len(m.b) {
		return 0
	}
	return m.b[addr]
}

func (m *fakeMem) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(m.Read8(addr)) | uint16(m.Read8(addr+1))<<8
}

func (m *fakeMem) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	if int(addr) < len(m.b) {
		m.b[addr] = v
	}
}

func (m *fakeMem) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	m.Write8(addr, uint8(v))
	m.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
}

func put(t *testing.T, s *audio.Sound, off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	t.Helper()
	if !s.WriteIO(off, size, val) {
		t.Fatalf("WriteIO offset %#x not claimed", off)
	}
}

func get(t *testing.T, s *audio.Sound, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	t.Helper()
	v, ok := s.ReadIO(off, size)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("ReadIO offset %#x not claimed", off)
	}
	return v
}

func masterOn(t *testing.T, s *audio.Sound) {
	t.Helper()
	put(t, s, 0x500, 4, 0x8000|127)
}

// chanRegs writes the address, timer, loop point and length
// registers of a channel. Call it before the control write
// that starts the channel, because those registers latch at
// start.
func chanRegs(t *testing.T, s *audio.Sound, ch int, sad uint32, divisor uint32, pnt uint32, words uint32) {
	t.Helper()
	base := uint32(0x400 + ch*16)
	put(t, s, base+4, 4, sad)
	put(t, s, base+8, 2, 65536-divisor)
	put(t, s, base+0xA, 2, pnt)
	put(t, s, base+0xC, 4, words)
}

func cntValue(pan uint32, repeat uint32, format uint32) uint32 {
	return 127 | pan<<16 | repeat<<27 | format<<29 | 1<<31
}

// fillSine16 writes one period of a PCM16 sine of the given
// number of samples and amplitude into memory.
func fillSine16(m *fakeMem, base uint32, samples int, amp float64) {
	for i := 0; i < samples; i++ {
		v := int16(amp * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/float64(samples)))
		m.Write16(base+uint32(i)*2, uint16(v))
	}
}

func leftChannel(stereo []int16) []int16 {
	out := make([]int16, len(stereo)/2)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = stereo[2*i]
	}
	return out
}

// Gate 1: a PCM16 loop tone comes out at the expected pitch
// and level.
func TestPCM16LoopTone(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	const base = 0x1000
	const period = 256
	fillSine16(m, base, period, 30000)
	s := audio.New(m)
	masterOn(t, s)
	chanRegs(t, s, 0, base, 511, 0, period/2)
	put(t, s, 0x400, 4, cntValue(64, 1, 1))
	s.Advance(16756991)
	stereo := s.Drain()
	if len(stereo) != 32768*2 {
		t.Fatalf("drained %d samples, want %d", len(stereo), 32768*2)
	}
	left := leftChannel(stereo)
	rate := 16756991.0 / 511.0
	wantFreq := rate / period
	cross := 0
	for i := 1; i < len(left); i++ {
		if left[i-1] < 0 && left[i] >= 0 {
			cross++
		}
	}
	gotFreq := float64(cross)
	if math.Abs(gotFreq-wantFreq)/wantFreq > 0.02 {
		t.Fatalf("frequency %v Hz from %d crossings, want %v Hz within 2 percent", gotFreq, cross, wantFreq)
	}
	var peak int
	var sumSq float64
	for _, v := range left {
		a := int(v)
		if a < 0 {
			a = -a
		}
		if a > peak {
			peak = a
		}
		sumSq += float64(v) * float64(v)
	}
	rms := math.Sqrt(sumSq / float64(len(left)))
	if peak < 10000 || peak > 20000 {
		t.Fatalf("peak %d, want between 10000 and 20000", peak)
	}
	if rms < 8000 || rms > 14000 {
		t.Fatalf("rms %v, want between 8000 and 14000", rms)
	}
}

func runPan(t *testing.T, pan uint32) []int16 {

// Gate 3: pan hard left silences the right side and pan hard

func TestPan(t *testing.T) {

		}

		}
	}

// IMA tables duplicated in the test so the reference encoder
// below stands on the published tables alone.
var testStep = [...]int32{
	7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17,
	19, 21, 23, 25, 28, 31, 34, 37, 41, 45,
	50, 55, 60, 66, 73, 80, 88, 97, 107, 118,
	130, 143, 157, 173, 190, 209, 230, 253, 279, 307,
	337, 371, 408, 449, 494, 544, 598, 658, 724, 796,
	876, 963, 1060, 1166, 1282, 1411, 1552, 1707, 1878, 2066,
	2272, 2499, 2749, 3024, 3327, 3660, 4026, 4428, 4871, 5358,
	5894, 6484, 7132, 7845, 8630, 9493, 10442, 11487, 12635, 13899,
	15289, 16818, 18500, 20350, 22385, 24623, 27086, 29794, 32767,
}

var testIndex = [...]int32{-1, -1, -1, -1, 2, 4, 6, 8}

func decodeNibble(pred int32, idx int32, nib uint32) (int32, int32) {
	step := testStep[idx]
	diff := step >> 3
	if nib&1 != 0 {
		diff += step >> 2
	}
	if nib&2 != 0 {
		diff += step >> 1
	}
	if nib&4 != 0 {
		diff += step
	}
	if nib&8 != 0 {
		pred -= diff
	} else {
		pred += diff
	}
	if pred > 32767 {
		pred = 32767
	}
	if pred < -32768 {
		pred = -32768
	}
	idx += testIndex[nib&7]
	if idx < 0 {
		idx = 0
	}
	if idx > 88 {
		idx = 88
	}
	return pred, idx
}

// Gate 4: ADPCM data encoded by a reference encoder in the
// test decodes through the package close to the source sine.
func TestADPCM(t *testing.T) {
	if len(testStep) != 89 {
		t.Fatalf("step table has %d entries, want 89", len(testStep))
	}
	m := newFakeMem()
	const base = 0x3000
	const period = 128
	const nsamp = 2048
	const amp = 12000.0
	pred := int32(0)
	idx := int32(30)
	m.Write16(base, 0)
	m.Write8(base+2, uint8(idx))
	m.Write8(base+3, 0)
	for i := 0; i < nsamp; i++ {
		target := int32(amp * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/period))
		best := uint32(0)
		var bestPred, bestIdx int32
		bestErr := int32(-1)
		var nib uint32
		for nib = 0; nib < 16; nib++ {
			p, ix := decodeNibble(pred, idx, nib)
			err := p - target
			if err < 0 {
				err = -err
			}
			if bestErr < 0 || err < bestErr {
				bestErr = err
				best = nib
				bestPred = p
				bestIdx = ix
			}
		}
		pred, idx = bestPred, bestIdx
		addr := base + 4 + uint32(i)/2
		if i%2 == 0 {
			m.Write8(addr, uint8(best))
		} else {
			m.Write8(addr, m.Read8(addr)|uint8(best)<<4)
		}
	}

	s := audio.New(m)
	masterOn(t, s)
	chanRegs(t, s, 0, base, 511, 0, 1+nsamp/8)
	put(t, s, 0x400, 4, cntValue(64, 1, 2))
	s.Advance(16756991)
	left := leftChannel(s.Drain())
	if len(left) < 20000 {
		t.Fatalf("drained %d left samples, want at least 20000", len(left))
	}
	rate := 16756991.0 / 511.0
	var maxErr, sumSq float64
	n := 0
	for out := 1000; out < 20000; out++ {
		pos := float64(out) * rate / 32768.0
		want := amp * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*pos/period)
		est := float64(left[out]) * 128.0 / 63.0
		err := math.Abs(est - want)
		if err > maxErr {
			maxErr = err
		}
		d := est - want
		sumSq += d * d
		n++
	}
	rms := math.Sqrt(sumSq / float64(n))
	t.Logf("ADPCM max error %v, rms error %v over %d samples", maxErr, rms, n)
	if maxErr >= 6000 {
		t.Fatalf("max error %v, want below 6000", maxErr)
	}
	if rms > 2500 {
		t.Fatalf("rms error %v, want at most 2500", rms)
	}
	var peak int
	for _, v := range left {
		a := int(v)
		if a < 0 {
			a = -a
		}
		if a > peak {
			peak = a
		}
	}
	if peak < 2000 {
		t.Fatalf("peak %d, ADPCM output looks silent", peak)
	}
}

// Gate 5: capture 0 on the mixer source writes exactly the
// samples that Drain returns for the same interval.
func TestCaptureMixerExact(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	const base = 0x1000
	const period = 256
	fillSine16(m, base, period, 30000)
	s := audio.New(m)
	masterOn(t, s)
	chanRegs(t, s, 0, base, 511, 0, period/2)
	put(t, s, 0x400, 4, cntValue(64, 1, 1))

	const dad = 0x8000
	const capWords = 64
	put(t, s, 0x510, 4, dad)
	put(t, s, 0x514, 2, capWords)
	// One shot, PCM16, mixer source, start.
	put(t, s, 0x508, 1, 0x80|0x04)
	s.Advance(200000)
	stereo := s.Drain()
	nsamp := capWords * 2
	if len(stereo)/2 < nsamp {
		t.Fatalf("only %d output samples, capture needs %d", len(stereo)/2, nsamp)
	}
	for i := 0; i < nsamp; i++ {
		got := int16(m.Read16(dad + uint32(i)*2))
		want := stereo[2*i]
		if got != want {
			t.Fatalf("captured sample %d is %d, drained left sample is %d", i, got, want)
		}
	}
	if v := get(t, s, 0x508, 1); v&0x80 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("capture still busy after one shot, cnt %#x", v)
	}
}

// Gate 6: a serialized scene continues bit identically in a
// fresh unit, including the undrained output buffer.
func TestStateRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	const base = 0x1000
	fillSine16(m, base, 256, 30000)
	build := func() *audio.Sound {
		s := audio.New(m)
		masterOn(t, s)
		chanRegs(t, s, 0, base, 511, 0, 128)
		put(t, s, 0x400, 4, cntValue(64, 1, 1))
		const ch = 9
		b9 := uint32(0x400 + ch*16)
		chanRegs(t, s, ch, 0, 700, 0, 0)
		cnt := uint32(100) | 90<<16 | 5<<24 | 3<<29 | 1<<31
		put(t, s, b9, 4, cnt)
		return s
	}
	orig := build()
	orig.Advance(5000000)
	blob := make([]byte, audio.StateSize)
	if n := orig.Serialize(blob); n != audio.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize returned %d, want %d", n, audio.StateSize)
	}
	fresh := audio.New(m)
	if n := fresh.Deserialize(blob); n != audio.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize returned %d, want %d", n, audio.StateSize)
	}
	orig.Advance(3000000)
	fresh.Advance(3000000)
	a := orig.Drain()
	b := fresh.Drain()
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		t.Fatalf("drain lengths differ: %d and %d", len(a), len(b))
	}
	if len(a) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("scene produced no output")
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			t.Fatalf("sample %d differs: %d and %d", i, a[i], b[i])
		}
	}
	blobA := make([]byte, audio.StateSize)
	blobB := make([]byte, audio.StateSize)
	orig.Serialize(blobA)
	fresh.Serialize(blobB)
	for i := range blobA {
		if blobA[i] != blobB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("re-serialized byte %d differs: %d and %d", i, blobA[i], blobB[i])
		}
	}
}

// Gate 7: register readback, including the busy bit.
func TestRegisterReadback(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	const base = 0x1000
	fillSine16(m, base, 256, 20000)
	s := audio.New(m)
	if _, ok := s.ReadIO(0x3FC, 4); ok {
		t.Fatal("ReadIO below 0x400 claimed")
	}
	if _, ok := s.ReadIO(0x520, 4); ok {
		t.Fatal("ReadIO at 0x520 claimed")
	}
	if s.WriteIO(0x520, 4, 0) {
		t.Fatal("WriteIO at 0x520 claimed")
	}
	masterOn(t, s)
	if v := get(t, s, 0x500, 4); v != 0x8000|127 {
		t.Fatalf("SOUNDCNT readback %#x, want %#x", v, 0x8000|127)
	}
	if v := get(t, s, 0x504, 4); v != 0x200 {
		t.Fatalf("SOUNDBIAS power on readback %#x, want 0x200", v)
	}
	put(t, s, 0x504, 2, 0x123)
	if v := get(t, s, 0x504, 4); v != 0x123 {
		t.Fatalf("SOUNDBIAS readback %#x, want 0x123", v)
	}
	put(t, s, 0x504, 2, 0x200)

	chanRegs(t, s, 0, base, 511, 0, 128)
	if v := get(t, s, 0x404, 4); v != base {
		t.Fatalf("SAD readback %#x, want %#x", v, base)
	}
	put(t, s, 0x400, 4, cntValue(64, 1, 1))
	if v := get(t, s, 0x400, 4); v&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("CNT busy bit clear while playing, cnt %#x", v)
	}
	s.Advance(100000)
	if v := get(t, s, 0x400, 4); v&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("CNT busy bit clear mid loop, cnt %#x", v)
	}
	put(t, s, 0x400, 4, 0)
	if v := get(t, s, 0x400, 4); v&(1<<31) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("CNT busy bit set after stop, cnt %#x", v)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/audio/state.go ====================

package audio

// StateSize is the serialized size of the sound unit: a
// fixed layout holding every channel register and playback
// field, both capture units, the master registers, the mixer
// phase accumulator, and the output buffer as a count plus a
// fixed capacity array of samples.
//
// Per channel 75 bytes, times 16: 1200.
// Per capture unit 21 bytes, times 2: 42.
// Master registers and the mixer phase: 16.
// Output buffer count: 4.
// Output buffer samples: 65536 stereo samples at 2 channels
// and 2 bytes each: 262144.
const StateSize = 16*75 + 2*21 + 16 + 4 + 65536*4

// Serialize writes exactly StateSize bytes into dst and
// returns StateSize.
func (s *Sound) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &stateWriter{b: dst}
	for i := range s.ch {
		ch := &s.ch[i]
		w.u32(ch.cnt)
		w.u32(ch.sadReg)
		w.u16(ch.tmrReg)
		w.u16(ch.pntReg)
		w.u32(ch.lenReg)
		w.u32(ch.lSad)
		w.u16(ch.lTmr)
		w.u16(ch.lPnt)
		w.u32(ch.lLen)
		w.u64(ch.pos)
		w.u64(ch.acc)
		w.u32(uint32(ch.pred))
		w.u32(uint32(ch.index))
		w.u32(uint32(ch.snapPred))
		w.u32(uint32(ch.snapIndex))
		w.flag(ch.snapTaken)
		w.u16(ch.lfsr)
		w.u8(ch.phase)
		w.flag(ch.busy)
		w.flag(ch.hang)
		w.flag(ch.holdActive)
		w.u32(uint32(ch.cur))
		w.u32(uint32(ch.hold))
	}
	for i := range s.caps {
		cap := &s.caps[i]
		w.u8(cap.cntReg)
		w.u32(cap.dadReg)
		w.u16(cap.lenReg)
		w.flag(cap.busy)
		w.u32(cap.lDad)
		w.u32(cap.lLenWords)
		w.u8(cap.lCnt)
		w.u32(cap.posBytes)
	}
	w.u32(s.soundCnt)
	w.u32(s.bias)
	w.u64(s.phase)
	count := len(s.out) / 2
	w.u32(uint32(count))
	total := outCap * 2
	for i := 0; i < total; i++ {
		if i < len(s.out) {
			w.u16(uint16(s.out[i]))
		} else {
			w.u16(0)
		}
	}
	return w.n
}

// Deserialize restores the state written by Serialize and
// returns the byte count consumed.
func (s *Sound) Deserialize(src []byte) int {
	r := &stateReader{b: src}
	for i := range s.ch {
		ch := &s.ch[i]
		ch.idx = i
		ch.cnt = r.u32()
		ch.sadReg = r.u32()
		ch.tmrReg = r.u16()
		ch.pntReg = r.u16()
		ch.lenReg = r.u32()
		ch.lSad = r.u32()
		ch.lTmr = r.u16()
		ch.lPnt = r.u16()
		ch.lLen = r.u32()
		ch.pos = r.u64()
		ch.acc = r.u64()
		ch.pred = int32(r.u32())
		ch.index = int32(r.u32())
		ch.snapPred = int32(r.u32())
		ch.snapIndex = int32(r.u32())
		ch.snapTaken = r.flag()
		ch.lfsr = r.u16()
		ch.phase = r.u8()
		ch.busy = r.flag()
		ch.hang = r.flag()
		ch.holdActive = r.flag()
		ch.cur = int32(r.u32())
		ch.hold = int32(r.u32())
	}
	for i := range s.caps {
		cap := &s.caps[i]
		cap.cntReg = r.u8()
		cap.dadReg = r.u32()
		cap.lenReg = r.u16()
		cap.busy = r.flag()
		cap.lDad = r.u32()
		cap.lLenWords = r.u32()
		cap.lCnt = r.u8()
		cap.posBytes = r.u32()
	}
	s.soundCnt = r.u32()
	s.bias = r.u32()
	s.phase = r.u64()
	count := int(r.u32())
	if count > outCap {
		count = outCap
	}
	if count < 0 {
		count = 0
	}
	out := make([]int16, 0, count*2)
	total := outCap * 2
	for i := 0; i < total; i++ {
		v := int16(r.u16())
		if i < count*2 {
			out = append(out, v)
		}
	}
	s.out = out
	return r.n
}

// stateWriter and stateReader are byte cursors for the state
// blob, in the style of the sibling packages.
type stateWriter struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (w *stateWriter) u8(v uint8) { w.b[w.n] = v; w.n++ }
func (w *stateWriter) u16(v uint16) {
	w.u8(uint8(v))
	w.u8(uint8(v >> 8))
}
func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) {
	w.u16(uint16(v))
	w.u16(uint16(v >> 16))
}
func (w *stateWriter) u64(v uint64) {
	w.u32(uint32(v))
	w.u32(uint32(v >> 32))
}
func (w *stateWriter) flag(b bool) {
	if b {
		w.u8(1)
	} else {
		w.u8(0)
	}
}

type stateReader struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (r *stateReader) u8() uint8 {
	v := r.b[r.n]
	r.n++
	return v
}
func (r *stateReader) u16() uint16 {
	return uint16(r.u8()) | uint16(r.u8())<<8
}
func (r *stateReader) u32() uint32 {
	return uint32(r.u16()) | uint32(r.u16())<<16
}
func (r *stateReader) u64() uint64 {
	return uint64(r.u32()) | uint64(r.u32())<<32
}
func (r *stateReader) flag() bool { return r.u8() != 0 }


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/bus/bus.go ====================

// Package bus implements the Nintendo DS memory system as two
// CPU-facing views over one set of backing stores. The ARM9 view
// honors the CP15-configured ITCM and DTCM windows; both views
// see the shared WRAM window through the WRAMCNT ownership
// mapping and the cartridge window through the EXMEMCNT
// ownership bit.
//
// Slice 1 simplifications, stated plainly:
//   - The instruction and data caches are NOT simulated. The
//     CP15 cache configuration registers exist as storage in the
//     CPU, but every access goes straight to backing memory.
//   - No DS or GBA BIOS bytes exist anywhere in this module (and
//     none may be added: no dumps). Reads of the BIOS windows
//     return the side's open-bus value, the documented
//     approximation for code that reads unmapped space.
//   - VRAM banks are backing stores mapped at their LCDC
//     addresses. The VRAMCNT bank assignment registers are plain
//     IO storage; the 2D engines in the video package consume
//     the assignments. Banks C and D assigned as ARM7 WRAM
//     (MST 2) appear in the ARM7 view at 0x06000000, as on
//     hardware.
//   - DS-2 device registers (timers, DMA, IPC, interrupts, the
//     card ports) are not plain storage. When the system
//     installs an IOHook, accesses to the IO pages are offered
//     to it first and fall back to storage for the offsets it
//     does not claim. A bare bus (unit tests) has no hook and
//     behaves exactly as slice 1.
//   - The cartridge image is mapped linearly in the
//     0x08000000 window for foundation work. The real DS game
//     card streams through a serial command interface; direct
//     boot staging in the system package loads binaries from the
//     parsed image into RAM and does not execute from this
//     window.
package bus

import "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/chips/armcore"

// Memory region sizes.
const (
	MainRAMSize = 4 << 20
	ITCMSize    = 32 << 10
	DTCMSize    = 32 << 10
	SharedSize  = 32 << 10
	ARM7RAMSize = 64 << 10
	VRAMSize    = 0xA4000 // banks A-I at their LCDC offsets
	PaletteSize = 2 << 10 // BG/OBJ palettes for both engines
	OAMSize     = 2 << 10 // 1 KB of OAM per engine
	GBASRAMSize = 64 << 10
	IOSize      = 0x1000 // one side's IO page (the ARM7 page)
	IO9Size     = 0x2000 // ARM9 IO: its page plus the engine B page
)

// IO offsets of the shared registers, within the 0x04000000 page.
const (
	ioEXMEMCNT = 0x204 // 16-bit, in the ARM9 IO page
	ioWRAMCNT  = 0x247 // 8-bit, in the ARM9 IO page
)

// VRAMCNT byte offsets in the ARM9 IO page, one per bank A-I.
// Banks C and D (offsets 0x242 and 0x243) with MST 2 assign the
// bank as ARM7 WRAM, decoded in the ARM7 view.
const (
	ioVRAMCNTC = 0x242
	ioVRAMCNTD = 0x243
)

// IOHook is the device-register dispatcher the system installs
// for DS-2 hardware. ReadIO and WriteIO receive the side, an
// offset in the hook offset space, and the access size in bytes.
// The offset space is the IO page offset (0x0000-0x1FFF on the
// ARM9 side, which includes the engine B page at 0x1000-0x1FFF;
// 0x0000-0x0FFF on the ARM7 side) plus the 0x04100000 window
// remapped to 0x2000-0x2FFF (the IPC FIFO receive port at
// 0x2000 and the card data port at 0x2010). A false return
// means the offset is plain storage and the bus handles the
// access itself.
type IOHook interface {
	ReadIO(nine bool, off uint32, size int) (uint32, bool)
	WriteIO(nine bool, off uint32, size int, val uint32) bool
}

// hookOffset maps an address to the hook offset space, if the
// address belongs to a hooked window for that side.
func hookOffset(nine bool, addr uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	switch {
	case addr >= 0x04000000 && addr < 0x04001000:
		return addr & 0xFFF, true
	case nine && addr >= 0x04001000 && addr < 0x04002000:
		return addr & 0x1FFF, true
	case addr >= 0x04100000 && addr < 0x04101000:
		return 0x2000 + (addr & 0xFFF), true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// Bus holds every DS backing store and hands out the two CPU
// views. Construct with New, then AttachCPU9 so the ARM9 view can
// decode the CP15 TCM configuration.
type Bus struct {
	MainRAM  []byte
	ITCM     []byte
	DTCM     []byte
	Shared   []byte
	ARM7WRAM []byte
	VRAM     []byte
	Palette  []byte
	OAM      []byte
	GBASRAM  []byte
	IO9      []byte
	IO7      []byte

	rom   []byte
	cpu9  *armcore.CPU
	hook  IOHook
	open9 uint32
	open7 uint32
}

// New returns a zeroed DS memory system.
func New() *Bus {
	return &Bus{
		MainRAM:  make([]byte, MainRAMSize),
		ITCM:     make([]byte, ITCMSize),
		DTCM:     make([]byte, DTCMSize),
		Shared:   make([]byte, SharedSize),
		ARM7WRAM: make([]byte, ARM7RAMSize),
		VRAM:     make([]byte, VRAMSize),
		Palette:  make([]byte, PaletteSize),
		OAM:      make([]byte, OAMSize),
		GBASRAM:  make([]byte, GBASRAMSize),
		IO9:      make([]byte, IO9Size),
		IO7:      make([]byte, IOSize),
	}
}

// SetIOHook installs the device-register dispatcher. The system
// calls it once at construction; unit tests leave it nil.
func (b *Bus) SetIOHook(h IOHook) { b.hook = h }

// AttachCPU9 binds the ARM9 CPU whose CP15 TCM registers the
// ARM9 view decodes against.
func (b *Bus) AttachCPU9(c *armcore.CPU) { b.cpu9 = c }

// SetROM installs the cartridge image used by the ROM window.
// The bytes are kept by reference.
func (b *Bus) SetROM(rom []byte) { b.rom = rom }

// ROMImage returns the installed cartridge image.
func (b *Bus) ROMImage() []byte { return b.rom }

// WRAMCNT returns the shared WRAM ownership register (ARM9 IO).
func (b *Bus) WRAMCNT() uint32 { return uint32(b.IO9[ioWRAMCNT]) }

// SetWRAMCNT stores the shared WRAM ownership register.
func (b *Bus) SetWRAMCNT(v uint32) { b.IO9[ioWRAMCNT] = byte(v) }

// EXMEMCNT returns the external memory control register.
func (b *Bus) EXMEMCNT() uint32 {
	return uint32(b.IO9[ioEXMEMCNT]) | uint32(b.IO9[ioEXMEMCNT+1])<<8
}

// cartOwner9 reports whether the ARM9 owns the cartridge window:
// EXMEMCNT bit 7 clear means ARM9, set means ARM7.
func (b *Bus) cartOwner9() bool { return b.EXMEMCNT()&(1<<7) == 0 }

// View is one CPU's window onto the bus.
type View struct {
	b    *Bus
	nine bool
}

// ARM9 returns the ARM9 bus view.
func (b *Bus) ARM9() View { return View{b: b, nine: true} }

// ARM7 returns the ARM7 bus view.
func (b *Bus) ARM7() View { return View{b: b, nine: false} }

// bankOwnedBy9 reports whether shared WRAM bank (0 or 1) belongs
// to the ARM9 under the WRAMCNT mapping: mode 0 both ARM7,
// mode 1 bank 0 ARM7 and bank 1 ARM9, mode 2 bank 0 ARM9 and
// bank 1 ARM7, mode 3 both ARM9.
func bankOwnedBy9(mode, bank uint32) bool {
	switch mode & 3 {
	case 0:
		return false
	case 1:
		return bank == 1
	case 2:
		return bank == 0
	default:
		return true
	}
}

// sharedWindow translates an address in the 0x03000000 shared
// WRAM window to the shared backing store for one CPU side, or
// reports the access unmapped when the bank belongs to the other
// CPU.
func (b *Bus) sharedWindow(nine bool, addr uint32) ([]byte, uint32, bool) {
	win := addr & 0x7FFF
	bank := win >> 14
	if bankOwnedBy9(b.WRAMCNT(), bank) != nine {
		return nil, 0, false
	}
	rank := uint32(0)
	for i := uint32(0); i < bank; i++ {
		if bankOwnedBy9(b.WRAMCNT(), i) == nine {
			rank++
		}
	}
	return b.Shared, rank<<14 | (win & 0x3FFF), true
}

// decode9 resolves an ARM9 address to a backing store and
// offset. ok=false means open bus.
func (b *Bus) decode9(addr uint32, fetch bool) ([]byte, uint32, bool) {
	if b.cpu9 != nil {
		if base, size, en := b.cpu9.DTCMRegion(); en && size > 0 && addr-base < size {
			return b.DTCM, (addr - base) % uint32(len(b.DTCM)), true
		}
		if base, size, en := b.cpu9.ITCMRegion(); en && size > 0 {
			// The ITCM mirrors across 0x00000000-0x01FFFFFF.
			if rel := addr - base; addr < 0x02000000 && rel < 0x02000000 {
				off := rel % size
				if off < uint32(len(b.ITCM)) {
					return b.ITCM, off, true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	switch {
	case addr >= 0x02000000 && addr < 0x03000000:
		return b.MainRAM, addr & (MainRAMSize - 1), true
	case addr >= 0x03000000 && addr < 0x03008000:
		return b.sharedWindow(true, addr)
	case addr >= 0x04000000 && addr < 0x04002000:
		return b.IO9, addr & 0x1FFF, true
	case addr >= 0x05000000 && addr < 0x05001000:
		return b.Palette, addr & (PaletteSize - 1), true
	case addr >= 0x06800000 && addr < 0x06800000+VRAMSize:
		return b.VRAM, addr - 0x06800000, true
	case addr >= 0x07000000 && addr < 0x07001000:
		return b.OAM, addr & (OAMSize - 1), true
	case addr >= 0x08000000 && addr < 0x0A000000:
		if b.cartOwner9() && len(b.rom) > 0 {
			return b.rom, (addr - 0x08000000) % uint32(len(b.rom)), true
		}
	case addr >= 0x0A000000 && addr < 0x0B000000:
		if b.cartOwner9() {
			return b.GBASRAM, addr & (GBASRAMSize - 1), true
		}
	}
	return nil, 0, false
}

// decode7 resolves an ARM7 address to a backing store and
// offset. ok=false means open bus (which covers its 16 KB BIOS
// window at 0x00000000: no BIOS bytes exist in this module).
func (b *Bus) decode7(addr uint32) ([]byte, uint32, bool) {
	switch {
	case addr >= 0x02000000 && addr < 0x03000000:
		return b.MainRAM, addr & (MainRAMSize - 1), true
	case addr >= 0x03000000 && addr < 0x03008000:
		return b.sharedWindow(false, addr)
	case addr >= 0x03800000 && addr < 0x04000000:
		return b.ARM7WRAM, addr & (ARM7RAMSize - 1), true
	case addr >= 0x06000000 && addr < 0x06040000:
		// VRAM banks C and D assigned as ARM7 WRAM (VRAMCNT
		// MST 2) appear here: bank C or D at 0x06000000 plus
		// 0x20000 times its OFS low bit.
		for i, cntOff := range []int{ioVRAMCNTC, ioVRAMCNTD} {
			cnt := uint32(b.IO9[cntOff])
			if cnt&0x80 != 0 && cnt&7 == 2 && uint32(addr-0x06000000)>>17 == (cnt>>3)&1 {
				return b.VRAMBank(2 + i), addr & 0x1FFFF, true
			}
		}
		return nil, 0, false
	case addr >= 0x04000000 && addr < 0x04001000:
		// The ARM7 reads EXMEMCNT and WRAMCNT from the ARM9 page;
		// its writes to them are ignored.
		if off := addr & 0xFFF; off == ioEXMEMCNT || off == ioEXMEMCNT+1 || off == ioWRAMCNT {
			return b.IO9, off, true
		}
		return b.IO7, addr & 0xFFF, true
	case addr >= 0x08000000 && addr < 0x0A000000:
		if !b.cartOwner9() && len(b.rom) > 0 {
			return b.rom, (addr - 0x08000000) % uint32(len(b.rom)), true
		}
	case addr >= 0x0A000000 && addr < 0x0B000000:
		if !b.cartOwner9() {
			return b.GBASRAM, addr & (GBASRAMSize - 1), true
		}
	}
	return nil, 0, false
}

func readBytes(mem []byte, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		v |= uint32(mem[(off+uint32(i))%uint32(len(mem))]) << (8 * i)
	}
	return v
}

func writeBytes(mem []byte, off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		mem[(off+uint32(i))%uint32(len(mem))] = byte(val >> (8 * i))
	}
}

func (v View) open() *uint32 {
	if v.nine {
		return &v.b.open9
	}
	return &v.b.open7
}

// Read implements armcore.Bus for this side.
func (v View) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if v.b.hook != nil {
		if off, in := hookOffset(v.nine, addr); in {
			if val, handled := v.b.hook.ReadIO(v.nine, off, size); handled {
				*v.open() = val
				return val
			}
		}
	}
	var mem []byte
	var off uint32
	var ok bool
	if v.nine {
		mem, off, ok = v.b.decode9(addr, false)
	} else {
		mem, off, ok = v.b.decode7(addr)
	}
	if !ok {
		o := *v.open()
		switch size {
		case 1:
			return o & 0xFF
		case 2:
			return o & 0xFFFF
		}
		return o
	}
	val := readBytes(mem, off, size)
	*v.open() = val
	return val
}

// Fetch implements armcore.Bus for this side. Fetches see the
// same map as reads on the ARM9 side (ITCM first), which is the
// slice 1 model.
func (v View) Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if !v.nine {
		return v.Read(addr, size)
	}
	mem, off, ok := v.b.decode9(addr, true)
	if !ok {
		return v.Read(addr, size)
	}
	val := readBytes(mem, off, size)
	v.b.open9 = val
	return val
}

// Write implements armcore.Bus for this side. ARM7 writes to the
// shared control registers are dropped (decode7 routes their
// reads to the ARM9 page, so writes must not land there).
func (v View) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if !v.nine && addr >= 0x04000000 && addr < 0x04001000 {
		if off := addr & 0xFFF; off >= ioEXMEMCNT && off <= ioEXMEMCNT+1 || off == ioWRAMCNT {
			return
		}
	}
	if v.b.hook != nil {
		if off, in := hookOffset(v.nine, addr); in {
			if v.b.hook.WriteIO(v.nine, off, size, val) {
				*v.open() = val
				return
			}
		}
	}
	var mem []byte
	var off uint32
	var ok bool
	if v.nine {
		mem, off, ok = v.b.decode9(addr, false)
	} else {
		mem, off, ok = v.b.decode7(addr)
	}
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	writeBytes(mem, off, size, val)
	*v.open() = val
}

// LoadBytes copies data into the memory map through one side's
// view (used by cartridge staging, which writes into windows the
// owning CPU will read). It returns how many bytes were placed.
func (b *Bus) LoadBytes(nine bool, addr uint32, data []byte) int {
	n := 0
	for i, x := range data {
		var mem []byte
		var off uint32
		var ok bool
		if nine {
			mem, off, ok = b.decode9(addr+uint32(i), false)
		} else {
			mem, off, ok = b.decode7(addr + uint32(i))
		}
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		mem[off] = x
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// VRAMBank returns the backing store of one VRAM bank (0=A ..
// 8=I) at its LCDC offset within the flat VRAM array.
func (b *Bus) VRAMBank(i int) []byte {
	offs := []struct{ at, size int }{
		{0x00000, 128 << 10}, // A
		{0x20000, 128 << 10}, // B
		{0x40000, 128 << 10}, // C
		{0x60000, 128 << 10}, // D
		{0x80000, 64 << 10},  // E
		{0x90000, 16 << 10},  // F
		{0x94000, 16 << 10},  // G
		{0x98000, 32 << 10},  // H
		{0xA0000, 16 << 10},  // I
	}
	if i < 0 || i >= len(offs) {
		return nil
	}
	o := offs[i]
	return b.VRAM[o.at : o.at+o.size]
}

// StateSize is the serialized size of the whole memory system.
const StateSize = MainRAMSize + ITCMSize + DTCMSize + SharedSize + ARM7RAMSize +
	VRAMSize + PaletteSize + OAMSize + GBASRAMSize + IO9Size + IOSize + 8

// Serialize writes every backing store, plus the two open-bus
// values, to dst (at least StateSize bytes).
func (b *Bus) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	n := 0
	put := func(src []byte) {
		copy(dst[n:], src)
		n += len(src)
	}
	put(b.MainRAM)
	put(b.ITCM)
	put(b.DTCM)
	put(b.Shared)
	put(b.ARM7WRAM)
	put(b.VRAM)
	put(b.Palette)
	put(b.OAM)
	put(b.GBASRAM)
	put(b.IO9)
	put(b.IO7)
	for _, v := range []uint32{b.open9, b.open7} {
		dst[n] = byte(v)
		dst[n+1] = byte(v >> 8)
		dst[n+2] = byte(v >> 16)
		dst[n+3] = byte(v >> 24)
		n += 4
	}
	return n
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (b *Bus) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < StateSize {
		return false
	}
	n := 0
	get := func(dst []byte) {
		copy(dst, src[n:n+len(dst)])
		n += len(dst)
	}
	get(b.MainRAM)
	get(b.ITCM)
	get(b.DTCM)
	get(b.Shared)
	get(b.ARM7WRAM)
	get(b.VRAM)
	get(b.Palette)
	get(b.OAM)
	get(b.GBASRAM)
	get(b.IO9)
	get(b.IO7)
	rd := func() uint32 {
		v := uint32(src[n]) | uint32(src[n+1])<<8 | uint32(src[n+2])<<16 | uint32(src[n+3])<<24
		n += 4
		return v
	}
	b.open9 = rd()
	b.open7 = rd()
	return true
}
