package bus

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/chips/armcore"
)

func TestMainRAMSharedAndMirrored(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.ARM9().Write(0x02000004, 4, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x02000004, 4); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 main RAM read: got %08x", got)
	}
	// 4 MB mirrored across the 16 MB window.
	if got := b.ARM9().Read(0x02400004, 4); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("main RAM mirror: got %08x", got)
	}
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x02C00004, 4); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("main RAM mirror 2: got %08x", got)
	}
}

func TestSharedWRAMOwnership(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	// Mode 3: ARM9 owns both banks.
	b.SetWRAMCNT(3)
	b.ARM9().Write(0x03000000, 4, 0x11111111)
	b.ARM9().Write(0x03004000, 4, 0x22222222)
	if b.Shared[0] != 0x11 || b.Shared[0x4000] != 0x22 {
		t.Fatalf("shared backing: %02x %02x", b.Shared[0], b.Shared[0x4000])
	}
	// ARM7 sees open bus, not the ARM9 values.
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x03000000, 4); got == 0x11111111 {
		t.Error("ARM7 read an ARM9-owned bank")
	}
	// Mode 0: ARM7 owns both banks, same backing cells.
	b.SetWRAMCNT(0)
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0x11111111 {
		t.Errorf("mode 0 ARM7 read bank 0: got %08x", got)
	}
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x03004000, 4); got != 0x22222222 {
		t.Errorf("mode 0 ARM7 read bank 1: got %08x", got)
	}
	if got := b.ARM9().Read(0x03000000, 4); got == 0x11111111 {
		t.Error("ARM9 read an ARM7-owned bank")
	}
	// Mode 1: split, bank 0 ARM7, bank 1 ARM9. Each side's
	// window packs its own bank at offset 0.
	b.SetWRAMCNT(1)
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0x11111111 {
		t.Errorf("mode 1 ARM7 bank: got %08x", got)
	}
	if got := b.ARM9().Read(0x03000000, 4); got != 0x22222222 {
		t.Errorf("mode 1 ARM9 packed bank: got %08x", got)
	}
}

func TestTCMWindows(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	cpu := armcore.NewARM9(b.ARM9())
	b.AttachCPU9(cpu)
	// Reset config: ITCM 32 KB at 0, DTCM 16 KB at 0x00800000.
	b.ARM9().Write(0x00000100, 4, 0xAAAA0001)
	if got := readWord(b.ITCM, 0x100); got != 0xAAAA0001 {
		t.Errorf("ITCM write landed at %08x", got)
	}
	b.ARM9().Write(0x00800040, 4, 0xBBBB0002)
	if got := readWord(b.DTCM, 0x40); got != 0xBBBB0002 {
		t.Errorf("DTCM write landed at %08x", got)
	}
	// The ARM7 cannot see the ITCM window: its 0x00000100 is the
	// BIOS window, which reads open bus.
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x00000100, 4); got == 0xAAAA0001 {
		t.Error("ARM7 read into the ARM9 ITCM")
	}
	// Reprogramming the DTCM base through CP15 moves the window.
	cpu.CP15Write(9, 1, 0, 0x02000000|5<<1)
	b.ARM9().Write(0x02000080, 4, 0xCCCC0003)
	if got := readWord(b.DTCM, 0x80); got != 0xCCCC0003 {
		t.Errorf("moved DTCM write landed at %08x", got)
	}
	if got := readWord(b.MainRAM, 0x80); got == 0xCCCC0003 {
		t.Error("moved DTCM shadowed by main RAM write")
	}
}

func TestCartWindowOwnership(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	rom := []byte{0x10, 0x20, 0x30, 0x40, 0x50, 0x60, 0x70, 0x80}
	b.SetROM(rom)
	// Default EXMEMCNT: ARM9 owns the window.
	if got := b.ARM9().Read(0x08000000, 4); got != 0x40302010 {
		t.Errorf("ARM9 cart read: got %08x", got)
	}
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x08000000, 4); got == 0x40302010 {
		t.Error("ARM7 read the cart window while ARM9 owns it")
	}
	// Hand ownership to the ARM7: EXMEMCNT bit 7 set. A fresh
	// bus is used for the ARM9 denial check so the ARM9 open-bus
	// value cannot coincidentally equal the ROM contents.
	b.IO9[ioEXMEMCNT] = 0x80
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x08000000, 4); got != 0x40302010 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 cart read: got %08x", got)
	}
	b2 := New()
	b2.SetROM(rom)
	b2.IO9[ioEXMEMCNT] = 0x80
	if got := b2.ARM9().Read(0x08000000, 4); got == 0x40302010 {
		t.Error("ARM9 read the cart window while ARM7 owns it")
	}
	// The ARM7 reads the same EXMEMCNT value from its own page.
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x04000204, 2); got != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 EXMEMCNT read: got %04x", got)
	}
	// And cannot change it.
	b.ARM7().Write(0x04000204, 2, 0)
	if b.EXMEMCNT() != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 wrote EXMEMCNT: now %04x", b.EXMEMCNT())
	}
}

func TestARM7PrivateWRAMAndIO(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.ARM7().Write(0x03800100, 4, 0x77777777)
	if got := readWord(b.ARM7WRAM, 0x100); got != 0x77777777 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 WRAM: got %08x", got)
	}
	// Mirrored across its 8 MB window.
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x03840100, 4); got != 0x77777777 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 WRAM mirror: got %08x", got)
	}
	// Sound registers are plain IO storage on the ARM7 page.
	b.ARM7().Write(0x04000400, 4, 0x12345678)
	if got := b.ARM7().Read(0x04000400, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 IO storage: got %08x", got)
	}
	// DISPCNT is plain IO storage on the ARM9 page.
	b.ARM9().Write(0x04000000, 4, 0x00020001)
	if got := b.ARM9().Read(0x04000000, 4); got != 0x00020001 {
		t.Errorf("ARM9 IO storage: got %08x", got)
	}
	// VRAM bank B lands in the flat store at its LCDC offset.
	b.ARM9().Write(0x06820000, 4, 0x99999999)
	if got := readWord(b.VRAMBank(1), 0); got != 0x99999999 {
		t.Errorf("VRAM bank B: got %08x", got)
	}
}

func TestBusSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.ARM9().Write(0x02000000, 4, 0x13572468)
	b.SetWRAMCNT(2)
	buf := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if n := b.Serialize(buf); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d, StateSize %d", n, StateSize)
	}
	d := New()
	if !d.Deserialize(buf) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize refused")
	}
	if got := d.ARM9().Read(0x02000000, 4); got != 0x13572468 {
		t.Errorf("main RAM round trip: %08x", got)
	}
	if d.WRAMCNT() != 2 {
		t.Errorf("WRAMCNT round trip: %d", d.WRAMCNT())
	}
	if d.Deserialize(buf[:StateSize-1]) {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted a short state")
	}
}

func readWord(mem []byte, off int) uint32 {
	return uint32(mem[off]) | uint32(mem[off+1])<<8 | uint32(mem[off+2])<<16 | uint32(mem[off+3])<<24
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/cart/cart.go ====================

// Package cart parses the Nintendo DS ROM header: the fixed
// 0x200-byte layout at the start of every DS cartridge image,
// documented in GBATEK. Slice 1 reads fields only. It does not
// decrypt anything: retail images carry an encrypted secure
// area whose KEY1/KEY2 scheme (documented in the manuals) is
// implemented by a later slice if direct boot of retail images
// requires it. No keys are embedded here.
package cart

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// Header is the parsed DS ROM header.
type Header struct {
	Title          string // 12 bytes at 0x000, ASCII, NUL padded
	GameCode       string // 4 bytes at 0x00C
	MakerCode      string // 2 bytes at 0x010
	UnitCode       byte   // 0x012: 0 = DS, 2 = DS/DSi, 3 = DSi
	SeedSelect     byte   // 0x013: encryption seed select
	Capacity       byte   // 0x014: device capacity (128KB << n)
	ARM9Offset     uint32 // 0x020: ROM offset of the ARM9 binary
	ARM9Entry      uint32 // 0x024: ARM9 entry address
	ARM9Load       uint32 // 0x028: ARM9 load address
	ARM9Size       uint32 // 0x02C: ARM9 binary size
	ARM7Offset     uint32 // 0x030
	ARM7Entry      uint32 // 0x034
	ARM7Load       uint32 // 0x038
	ARM7Size       uint32 // 0x03C
	IconOffset     uint32 // 0x068: icon/title structure offset
	SecureCRC      uint16 // 0x06C: secure area CRC field (read only here)
	LogoCRC        uint16 // 0x15C: stored CRC of the logo area
	HeaderCRC      uint16 // 0x15E: stored header CRC
	HeaderCRCValid bool   // computed CRC16 over 0x000-0x15D matches HeaderCRC
}

// MinHeaderSize is the smallest image that can hold a header.
const MinHeaderSize = 0x160

// ErrShortImage reports an image too small to contain a header.
var ErrShortImage = errors.New("cart: image smaller than a DS header")

// crc16 computes the CRC used by the DS header: polynomial
// 0x8005 reflected (0xA001), initial value 0xFFFF.
func crc16(data []byte) uint16 {
	crc := uint32(0xFFFF)
	for _, x := range data {
		crc ^= uint32(x)
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if crc&1 != 0 {
				crc = (crc >> 1) ^ 0xA001
			} else {
				crc >>= 1
			}
		}
	}
	return uint16(crc)
}

// Parse reads the header from the start of a ROM image. It fails
// only on structural problems: an image too small, or ARM9/ARM7
// binary extents outside the image. A bad header CRC is reported
// in HeaderCRCValid, not as an error, because homebrew images in
// the wild carry stale CRCs.
func Parse(rom []byte) (*Header, error) {
	if len(rom) < MinHeaderSize {
		return nil, ErrShortImage
	}
	le := binary.LittleEndian
	trim := func(s string) string {
		return strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00 ")
	}
	h := &Header{
		Title:      trim(string(rom[0x000:0x00C])),
		GameCode:   string(rom[0x00C:0x010]),
		MakerCode:  string(rom[0x010:0x012]),
		UnitCode:   rom[0x012],
		SeedSelect: rom[0x013],
		Capacity:   rom[0x014],
		ARM9Offset: le.Uint32(rom[0x020:]),
		ARM9Entry:  le.Uint32(rom[0x024:]),
		ARM9Load:   le.Uint32(rom[0x028:]),
		ARM9Size:   le.Uint32(rom[0x02C:]),
		ARM7Offset: le.Uint32(rom[0x030:]),
		ARM7Entry:  le.Uint32(rom[0x034:]),
		ARM7Load:   le.Uint32(rom[0x038:]),
		ARM7Size:   le.Uint32(rom[0x03C:]),
		IconOffset: le.Uint32(rom[0x068:]),
		SecureCRC:  le.Uint16(rom[0x06C:]),
		LogoCRC:    le.Uint16(rom[0x15C:]),
		HeaderCRC:  le.Uint16(rom[0x15E:]),
	}
	h.HeaderCRCValid = crc16(rom[:0x15E]) == h.HeaderCRC
	if err := h.checkExtent("ARM9", h.ARM9Offset, h.ARM9Size, len(rom)); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := h.checkExtent("ARM7", h.ARM7Offset, h.ARM7Size, len(rom)); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return h, nil
}

func (h *Header) checkExtent(name string, off, size uint32, romLen int) error {
	if size == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	if uint64(off)+uint64(size) > uint64(romLen) {
		return fmt.Errorf("cart: %s binary [%08x, +%08x) exceeds image size %08x",
			name, off, size, romLen)
	}
	return nil
}

// ARM9Binary returns the ARM9 program bytes from the image.
func (h *Header) ARM9Binary(rom []byte) []byte {
	return rom[h.ARM9Offset : h.ARM9Offset+h.ARM9Size]
}

// ARM7Binary returns the ARM7 program bytes from the image.
func (h *Header) ARM7Binary(rom []byte) []byte {
	return rom[h.ARM7Offset : h.ARM7Offset+h.ARM7Size]
}

// CapacityBytes returns the cartridge capacity class in bytes
// from the header capacity byte (128 KB shifted by n).
func (h *Header) CapacityBytes() uint32 {
	return 128 << 10 << h.Capacity
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/cart/cart_test.go ====================

package cart

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// syntheticROM builds a minimal well-formed DS image: a 0x200
// byte header region, an ARM9 binary at 0x1000 and an ARM7
// binary at 0x2000, with a valid header CRC stamped.
func syntheticROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x4000)
	copy(rom[0x000:], "DS1 UNITTEST")
	copy(rom[0x00C:], "ADSE")
	copy(rom[0x010:], "01")
	rom[0x012] = 0 // unit code: DS
	rom[0x013] = 1 // encryption seed select
	rom[0x014] = 2 // capacity: 512 KB class
	le := binary.LittleEndian
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x020:], 0x1000)     // ARM9 offset
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x024:], 0x02000000) // ARM9 entry
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x028:], 0x02000000) // ARM9 load
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x02C:], 16)         // ARM9 size
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x030:], 0x2000)     // ARM7 offset
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x034:], 0x03800000) // ARM7 entry
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x038:], 0x03800000) // ARM7 load
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x03C:], 20)         // ARM7 size
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x068:], 0x3000)     // icon offset
	le.PutUint16(rom[0x06C:], 0xBEEF)     // secure area CRC field
	le.PutUint16(rom[0x15E:], crc16(rom[:0x15E]))
	return rom
}

func TestParseSynthetic(t *testing.T) {
	h, err := Parse(syntheticROM())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if h.Title != "DS1 UNITTEST" || h.GameCode != "ADSE" || h.MakerCode != "01" {
		t.Errorf("identity: %q %q %q", h.Title, h.GameCode, h.MakerCode)
	}
	if h.UnitCode != 0 || h.SeedSelect != 1 || h.Capacity != 2 {
		t.Errorf("unit/seed/capacity: %d %d %d", h.UnitCode, h.SeedSelect, h.Capacity)
	}
	if h.ARM9Offset != 0x1000 || h.ARM9Entry != 0x02000000 || h.ARM9Load != 0x02000000 || h.ARM9Size != 16 {
		t.Errorf("ARM9 fields: %+v", h)
	}
	if h.ARM7Offset != 0x2000 || h.ARM7Entry != 0x03800000 || h.ARM7Load != 0x03800000 || h.ARM7Size != 20 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 fields: %+v", h)
	}
	if h.IconOffset != 0x3000 || h.SecureCRC != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("icon/secure: %08x %04x", h.IconOffset, h.SecureCRC)
	}
	if !h.HeaderCRCValid {
		t.Error("stamped header CRC should validate")
	}
	if h.CapacityBytes() != 512<<10 {
		t.Errorf("CapacityBytes: %d", h.CapacityBytes())
	}
}

func TestParseRejects(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := Parse(make([]byte, 0x100)); err == nil {
		t.Error("short image accepted")
	}
	rom := syntheticROM()
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rom[0x02C:], 0xFFFFF) // ARM9 size out of range
	if _, err := Parse(rom); err == nil {
		t.Error("out-of-range ARM9 extent accepted")
	}
}

func TestParseBadCRCIsNotFatal(t *testing.T) {
	rom := syntheticROM()
	rom[0x40] ^= 0xFF // corrupt a reserved byte after stamping
	h, err := Parse(rom)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if h.HeaderCRCValid {
		t.Error("corrupted header should report CRC invalid")
	}
}

// Package arm9 exposes the DS module's ARM946E-S processor (the
// "ARM9"): the ARMv5TE core that runs the main game code on the
// Nintendo DS. Over the ARMv4T base it adds CLZ, the saturating
// Q arithmetic, the signed halfword multiplies, LDRD/STRD, BLX,
// BKPT, and the CP15 system control coprocessor with its ITCM
// and DTCM configuration registers. It is the ARMv5TE
// configuration of the module's shared ARM core (chips/armcore).
//
// In this slice CP15 cache and MPU registers are stored but not
// acted on: no cache is simulated and no memory protection is
// enforced. The TCM base/size registers are live, because the
// system bus decodes the TCM windows from them.

// of armcore.CPU; see that package for the state layout.
type CPU = armcore.CPU

// New returns an ARM946E-S in its reset state, bound to bus b,
// with the DS power-on CP15 TCM configuration installed.
func New(b Bus) *CPU {
	return armcore.NewARM9(b)
}

// StateSize is the serialized size of the CPU state in bytes.
const StateSize = armcore.StateSize


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/chips/armcore/arm.go ====================

package armcore

import "math/bits"

// execARM executes one ARM-state instruction (the word in the
// execute stage, located at R15-8) and returns its cycle count.
func (c *CPU) execARM(instr uint32) int {
	addr := c.R[15] - 8
	cond := instr >> 28
	if cond != 0xE && !c.condPassed(cond) {
		return 1
	}
	v5 := c.Config.V5

	// Branch and exchange: bit 0 of the operand selects the new
	// state and is consumed.
	if instr&0x0FFFFFF0 == 0x012FFF10 {
		v := c.R[instr&0xF]
		if v&1 != 0 {
			c.CPSR |= BitT
		} else {
			c.CPSR &^= BitT
		}
		c.branch(v &^ 1)
		return 3
	}
	// BLX register (ARMv5): as BX, but LR is set first.
	if instr&0x0FFFFFF0 == 0x012FFF30 {
		if !v5 {
			return c.undefined(addr)
		}
		v := c.R[instr&0xF]
		c.R[14] = addr + 4
		if v&1 != 0 {
			c.CPSR |= BitT
		} else {
			c.CPSR &^= BitT
		}
		c.branch(v &^ 1)
		return 3
	}
	// BKPT (ARMv5): with no debugger attached the core takes a
	// prefetch abort.
	if v5 && instr&0x0FF000F0 == 0x01200070 {
		return c.PrefetchAbort(addr)
	}
	// CLZ (ARMv5): count leading zeros.
	if v5 && instr&0x0FFF0FF0 == 0x016F0F10 {
		rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
		c.R[rd] = uint32(bits.LeadingZeros32(c.R[instr&0xF]))
		return 1
	}
	// Saturating arithmetic (ARMv5): QADD, QSUB, QDADD, QDSUB.
	// Operand order per the architecture: the result is
	// Rm op Rn, with Rn the doubled operand for the QD forms.
	if v5 && instr&0x0F900FF0 == 0x01000050 {
		return c.execQOp(instr)
	}
	// Signed halfword multiplies (ARMv5): SMLAxy, SMLAWy,
	// SMULWy, SMLALxy, SMULxy. They sit in the multiply space
	// with S clear, opcode (bits 24-21) 8..11, bit 7 set and
	// bit 4 clear. With S set the same field pattern is the
	// data-processing test space, so the S check keeps the two
	// apart; with S clear the data-processing space holds only
	// the PSR transfers, whose operand patterns exclude bit 7.
	if v5 && (instr>>25)&7 == 0 && instr&(1<<20) == 0 &&
		(instr>>21)&0xF >= 8 && (instr>>21)&0xF <= 11 && instr&0x90 == 0x80 {
		return c.execDSPMultiply(instr)
	}

	switch {
	case (instr>>26)&3 == 0 && instr&(1<<25) == 0 && (instr&0x90) == 0x90 && (instr>>5)&3 == 0:
		// Multiply, multiply-long, swap space (bits 7-4 = 1001).
		op := (instr >> 21) & 0xF
		switch {
		case op <= 1:
			return c.execMultiply(instr)
		case op >= 4 && op <= 7:
			return c.execMultiplyLong(instr)
		case instr&0x0FB00FF0 == 0x01000090:
			return c.execSwap(instr)
		}
		return c.undefined(addr)

	case (instr>>26)&3 == 0 && instr&(1<<25) == 0 && (instr&0x90) == 0x90:
		// Halfword, signed and (ARMv5) doubleword transfers.
		return c.execHalfword(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>26)&3 == 0:
		return c.execDataProc(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>26)&3 == 1:
		// Single data transfer. A register offset with bit 4 set
		// is undefined.
		if instr&(1<<25) != 0 && instr&(1<<4) != 0 {
			return c.undefined(addr)
		}
		return c.execSingle(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>25)&7 == 4:
		return c.execBlock(instr, addr)

	case (instr>>25)&7 == 5:
		// Branch, branch with link.
		off := int32(instr<<8) >> 8
		target := uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off<<2)
		if instr&(1<<24) != 0 {
			c.R[14] = addr + 4
		}
		c.branch(target)
		return 3

	case (instr>>24)&0xF == 0xF:
		// Software interrupt.
		return c.exception(VectorSWI, ModeSVC, addr+4)

	case (instr>>24)&0xF == 0xE && instr&(1<<4) != 0:
		// Coprocessor register transfers. Only CP15 on the
		// ARM9 answers; everything else is an undefined trap.
		return c.execCPTransfer(instr, addr)
	}

	// Coprocessor data operations and loads/stores, and every
	// other leftover encoding: no coprocessor answers.
	return c.undefined(addr)
}

// execQOp runs the ARMv5 saturating arithmetic group. Results
// are clamped to the signed 32-bit range and the sticky Q flag
// is set when any stage saturates (for the QD forms the doubling
// is saturated first, even if the final result would have fit).
func (c *CPU) execQOp(instr uint32) int {
	op := (instr >> 21) & 3
	rn := int64(int32(c.R[(instr>>16)&0xF]))
	rm := int64(int32(c.R[instr&0xF]))
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	var res uint32
	var sat bool
	switch op {
	case 0: // QADD
		res, sat = saturate32(rm + rn)
	case 1: // QSUB
		res, sat = saturate32(rm - rn)
	case 2: // QDADD
		d, s1 := saturate32(rn * 2)
		res, sat = saturate32(rm + int64(int32(d)))
		sat = sat || s1
	case 3: // QDSUB
		d, s1 := saturate32(rn * 2)
		res, sat = saturate32(rm - int64(int32(d)))
		sat = sat || s1
	}
	c.setQ(sat)
	c.R[rd] = res
	return 1
}

// halfOf extracts one signed halfword of v: the low half when top
// is false, the high half when top is true.
func halfOf(v uint32, top bool) int64 {
	if top {
		return int64(int16(v >> 16))
	}
	return int64(int16(v))
}

// execDSPMultiply runs the ARMv5 signed halfword multiply group.
// In the encoding, bit 6 (y) selects the Rs half and bit 5 (x)
// selects the Rm half; for the W forms bit 5 instead selects
// between SMLAWy (0) and SMULWy (1). The 32-bit accumulate forms
// wrap on overflow and set Q (the result is not clamped); the
// 64-bit form never touches Q.
func (c *CPU) execDSPMultiply(instr uint32) int {
	op := (instr >> 21) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rn := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	rs := c.R[(instr>>8)&0xF]
	rm := c.R[instr&0xF]
	y := instr&(1<<6) != 0
	x := instr&(1<<5) != 0
	switch op {
	case 8: // SMLAxy
		sum := int64(int32(c.R[rn])) + halfOf(rm, x)*halfOf(rs, y)
		_, sat := saturate32(sum)
		c.setQ(sat)
		c.R[rd] = uint32(sum)
		return 2
	case 9: // SMLAWy / SMULWy
		prod := (int64(int32(rm)) * halfOf(rs, y)) >> 16
		if x { // SMULWy: no accumulate, Rn field unused
			c.R[rd] = uint32(prod)
			return 2
		}
		sum := int64(int32(c.R[rn])) + prod
		_, sat := saturate32(sum)
		c.setQ(sat)
		c.R[rd] = uint32(sum)
		return 2
	case 10: // SMLALxy
		acc := int64(uint64(c.R[rd])<<32 | uint64(c.R[rn]))
		acc += halfOf(rm, x) * halfOf(rs, y)
		c.R[rn] = uint32(acc)
		c.R[rd] = uint32(acc >> 32)
		return 3
	case 11: // SMULxy
		c.R[rd] = uint32(halfOf(rm, x) * halfOf(rs, y))
		return 2
	}
	return 1
}

// execCPTransfer runs MRC and MCR. On the ARM9, CP15 registers
// are stored in the CPU; MRC into R15 loads the CPSR flag nibble
// only, and MCR from R15 passes PC+12, per the architecture. Any
// other coprocessor (and every coprocessor on the ARM7) traps as
// undefined.
func (c *CPU) execCPTransfer(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	cp := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
	if !c.Config.V5 || cp != 15 {
		return c.undefined(addr)
	}
	crn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	opc2 := (instr >> 5) & 7
	crm := instr & 0xF
	if instr&(1<<20) != 0 { // MRC: coprocessor to ARM
		v := c.CP15Read(crn, crm, opc2)
		if rd == 15 {
			c.CPSR = c.CPSR&0x0FFFFFFF | v&0xF0000000
		} else {
			c.R[rd] = v
		}
		return 3
	}
	// MCR: ARM to coprocessor.
	v := c.R[rd]
	if rd == 15 {
		v = c.R[15] + 4
	}
	c.CP15Write(crn, crm, opc2, v)
	return 2
}

// writeReg writes an instruction result, refilling the pipeline
// when the destination is the PC. Used by the multiply and swap
// forms, whose PC destinations are architecturally unpredictable
// and follow the reference behavior (a raw refill, no state
// selection from bit 0). Defined interworking loads and results
// use branchPC instead.
func (c *CPU) writeReg(rd uint32, v uint32) {
	if rd == 15 {
		c.branch(v)
		return
	}
	c.R[rd] = v
}

func mulCycles(rs uint32) int {
	switch {
	case rs&0xFFFFFF00 == 0 || rs&0xFFFFFF00 == 0xFFFFFF00:
		return 1
	case rs&0xFFFF0000 == 0 || rs&0xFFFF0000 == 0xFFFF0000:
		return 2
	case rs&0xFF000000 == 0 || rs&0xFF000000 == 0xFF000000:
		return 3
	}
	return 4
}

// execMultiply runs MUL and MLA. Operands read in the
// memory-operand position (R15 reads as A+12).
func (c *CPU) execMultiply(instr uint32) int {
	acc := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	set := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rd := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rn := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	rs := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
	rm := instr & 0xF
	lhs, rhs := c.memReg(rm), c.memReg(rs)
	var accum uint32
	res := lhs * rhs
	if acc {
		accum = c.memReg(rn)
		res += accum
	}
	if set {
		c.setNZ(res)
		full := tickMultiply(true, rhs)
		c.setCarry(mulCarry(full, false, false, lhs, rhs, accum, 0))
	}
	c.writeReg(rd, res)
	n := 1 + mulCycles(rhs)
	if acc {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// execMultiplyLong runs UMULL, UMLAL, SMULL and SMLAL.
func (c *CPU) execMultiplyLong(instr uint32) int {
	signed := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	acc := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	set := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rdHi := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rdLo := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	rs := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
	rm := instr & 0xF
	lhs, rhs := c.memReg(rm), c.memReg(rs)
	var res uint64
	if signed {
		res = uint64(int64(int32(lhs)) * int64(int32(rhs)))
	} else {
		res = uint64(lhs) * uint64(rhs)
	}
	var accumLo, accumHi uint32
	if acc {
		accumLo = c.memReg(rdLo)
		accumHi = c.memReg(rdHi)
		res += uint64(accumHi)<<32 | uint64(accumLo)
	}
	if set {
		c.CPSR &^= FlagN | FlagZ
		if res>>63 != 0 {
			c.CPSR |= FlagN
		}
		if res == 0 {
			c.CPSR |= FlagZ
		}
		full := tickMultiply(signed, rhs)
		c.setCarry(mulCarry(full, true, signed, lhs, rhs, accumLo, accumHi))
	}
	c.R[rdLo] = uint32(res)
	c.R[rdHi] = uint32(res >> 32)
	if rdHi == 15 {
		c.branch(uint32(res >> 32))
	} else if rdLo == 15 {
		c.branch(uint32(res))
	}
	n := 2 + mulCycles(rhs)
	if acc {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// execSwap runs SWP and SWPB. The swap address and the stored
// operand both read PC as A+12 when they name R15.
func (c *CPU) execSwap(instr uint32) int {
	byteOp := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	rm := instr & 0xF
	addr := c.memReg(rn)
	if byteOp {
		tmp := c.Bus.Read(addr, 1)
		c.Bus.Write(addr, 1, c.memReg(rm)&0xFF)
		c.writeReg(rd, tmp)
		return 4
	}
	tmp := c.load(addr, 4, false)
	c.Bus.Write(addr, 4, c.memReg(rm))
	c.writeReg(rd, tmp)
	return 4
}

// execPSR handles MRS and MSR inside the data-processing space:
// the test-opcode encodings with S clear are the PSR transfers.
func (c *CPU) execPSR(instr uint32, opcode uint32) (int, bool) {
	sBit := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	if sBit {
		return 0, false
	}
	switch opcode {
	case 8, 10: // TST / CMP shape: MRS when Rn=1111 and low bits 0
		if (instr>>16)&0xF != 0xF || instr&0xFFF != 0 {
			return 0, false
		}
		rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
		var v uint32
		if opcode == 10 {
			v = c.curSPSR()
		} else {
			v = c.CPSR
		}
		// MRS writes its destination as a plain register, even
		// when Rd is R15: no pipeline refill follows.
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 1, true
	case 9, 11: // TEQ / CMN shape: MSR
		fieldMask := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
		var v uint32
		if instr&(1<<25) != 0 {
			rot := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
			v = ror32(instr&0xFF, uint(rot*2))
		} else {
			if instr&0xFF0 != 0 {
				return 0, false
			}
			v = c.R[instr&0xF]
		}
		c.msr(opcode == 11, fieldMask, v)
		return 1, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// execDataProc runs the ARM data-processing group, including the
// PSR transfers that share its encoding space.
func (c *CPU) execDataProc(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	opcode := (instr >> 21) & 0xF
	if n, ok := c.execPSR(instr, opcode); ok {
		return n
	}
	sBit := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	isTest := opcode >= 8 && opcode <= 11

	// Operand 2.
	var op2 uint32
	var shiftCarry bool
	regShift := false
	if instr&(1<<25) != 0 {
		rot := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
		op2 = ror32(instr&0xFF, uint(rot*2))
		if rot == 0 {
			shiftCarry = c.carry()
		} else {
			shiftCarry = op2>>31 != 0
		}
	} else if instr&(1<<4) != 0 {
		regShift = true
		rs := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
		rsVal := c.R[rs]
		rmVal := c.R[instr&0xF]
		if instr&0xF == 15 {
			rmVal += 4
		}
		op2, shiftCarry = c.shifter(rmVal, (instr>>5)&3, rsVal&0xFF, true)
	} else {
		amt := (instr >> 7) & 0x1F
		op2, shiftCarry = c.shifter(c.R[instr&0xF], (instr>>5)&3, amt, false)
	}

	rnVal := c.R[rn]
	if rn == 15 && regShift {
		rnVal += 4
	}

	setFlags := sBit || isTest
	var res uint32
	logical := false
	switch opcode {
	case 0, 8: // AND, TST
		res = rnVal & op2
		logical = true
	case 1, 9: // EOR, TEQ
		res = rnVal ^ op2
		logical = true
	case 2, 10: // SUB, CMP
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(rnVal, op2, true)
		} else {
			res = rnVal - op2
		}
	case 3: // RSB
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(op2, rnVal, true)
		} else {
			res = op2 - rnVal
		}
	case 4, 11: // ADD, CMN
		if setFlags {
			res = c.addFlags(rnVal, op2, false)
		} else {
			res = rnVal + op2
		}
	case 5: // ADC
		if setFlags {
			res = c.addFlags(rnVal, op2, c.carry())
		} else {
			res = rnVal + op2
			if c.carry() {
				res++
			}
		}
	case 6: // SBC
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(rnVal, op2, c.carry())
		} else {
			res = rnVal - op2
			if !c.carry() {
				res -= 1
			}
		}
	case 7: // RSC
		if setFlags {
			res = c.subFlags(op2, rnVal, c.carry())
		} else {
			res = op2 - rnVal
			if !c.carry() {
				res -= 1
			}
		}
	case 12: // ORR
		res = rnVal | op2
		logical = true
	case 13: // MOV
		res = op2
		logical = true
	case 14: // BIC
		res = rnVal &^ op2
		logical = true
	case 15: // MVN
		res = ^op2
		logical = true
	}
	if logical && setFlags {
		c.setNZC(res, shiftCarry)
	}

	if isTest {
		// A test-opcode encoding whose Rd field is R15 with S
		// set restores the CPSR from the SPSR after the flag
		// computation.
		if rd == 15 && sBit {
			c.setCPSR(c.curSPSR())
		}
		return 1 + regShiftCycles(regShift, false)
	}
	if rd == 15 {
		if sBit {
			// Exception return form: CPSR comes back from the
			// SPSR, then the pipeline refills at the result in
			// the restored state.
			c.setCPSR(c.curSPSR())
			c.branch(res)
		} else {
			c.branchPC(res)
		}
		return 1 + regShiftCycles(regShift, true)
	}
	c.R[rd] = res
	return 1 + regShiftCycles(regShift, false)
}

func regShiftCycles(regShift bool, rdPC bool) int {
	n := 0
	if regShift {
		n++
	}
	if rdPC {
		n += 2
	}
	return n
}

// addrMode computes the effective address and writeback value for
// the P/U/W addressing forms shared by the single, halfword and
// doubleword transfers.
func addrMode(base, offset uint32, pre, up, w bool) (ea, wb uint32, doWB bool) {
	if pre {
		if up {
			ea = base + offset
		} else {
			ea = base - offset
		}
		return ea, ea, w
	}
	if up {
		wb = base + offset
	} else {
		wb = base - offset
	}
	return base, wb, true
}

// execSingle runs LDR and STR (word and byte forms).
func (c *CPU) execSingle(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	pre := instr&(1<<24) != 0
	up := instr&(1<<23) != 0
	byteOp := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	w := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	load := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF

	var offset uint32
	if instr&(1<<25) != 0 {
		amt := (instr >> 7) & 0x1F
		offset, _ = c.shifter(c.R[instr&0xF], (instr>>5)&3, amt, false)
	} else {
		offset = instr & 0xFFF
	}
	ea, wb, doWB := addrMode(c.R[rn], offset, pre, up, w)

	// A writeback into R15 refills the pipeline at the
	// written-back value plus one unit (the reference behavior
	// computes it from the post-increment PC), unless a load
	// into R15 follows and wins.
	writeback := func() {
		if !doWB {
			return
		}
		if rn == 15 {
			c.branch(wb + 4)
		} else {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
	}

	if load {
		var v uint32
		if byteOp {
			v = c.load(ea, 1, false)
		} else {
			v = c.load(ea, 4, false)
		}
		if rn != rd {
			writeback()
		}
		if rd == 15 {
			c.branchPC(v)
			return 5
		}
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 3
	}
	data := c.R[rd]
	if rd == 15 {
		data = c.R[15] + 4 // STR of PC stores A+12
	}
	if byteOp {
		c.store(ea, 1, data)
	} else {
		c.store(ea, 4, data)
	}
	writeback()
	return 2
}

// execHalfword runs the halfword and signed transfer group, plus
// the ARMv5 doubleword forms that share the encoding space: in
// the store class (L clear), opcode 2 is LDRD and opcode 3 is
// STRD; in the load class, opcodes 2 and 3 are the signed byte
// and signed halfword loads. The offset-kind bit (22) is inverted
// relative to the single transfers: set means an immediate
// offset, clear means a register offset.
func (c *CPU) execHalfword(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	pre := instr&(1<<24) != 0
	up := instr&(1<<23) != 0
	regOff := instr&(1<<22) == 0
	w := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	load := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF
	sh := (instr >> 5) & 3

	if !load && sh != 1 {
		if c.Config.V5 && (sh == 2 || sh == 3) {
			return c.execDouble(instr, sh == 3)
		}
		return c.undefined(addr)
	}
	var offset uint32
	if regOff {
		offset = c.R[instr&0xF]
	} else {
		offset = ((instr>>8)&0xF)<<4 | (instr & 0xF)
	}
	ea, wb, doWB := addrMode(c.R[rn], offset, pre, up, w)

	writeback := func() {
		if !doWB {
			return
		}
		if rn == 15 {
			c.branch(wb + 4)
		} else {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
	}

	if load {
		var v uint32
		switch sh {
		case 1:
			v = c.load(ea, 2, false)
		case 2:
			v = c.load(ea, 1, true)
		case 3:
			v = c.load(ea, 2, true)
		}
		if rn != rd {
			writeback()
		}
		if rd == 15 {
			c.branchPC(v)
			return 5
		}
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 3
	}
	data := c.R[rd]
	if rd == 15 {
		data = c.R[15] + 4
	}
	c.store(ea, 2, data)
	writeback()
	return 2
}

// execDouble runs LDRD (store flag false) and STRD (true), the
// ARMv5 doubleword transfers. Rd names the even register of the
// pair; the address is expected doubleword aligned.
func (c *CPU) execDouble(instr uint32, store bool) int {
	pre := instr&(1<<24) != 0
	up := instr&(1<<23) != 0
	regOff := instr&(1<<22) == 0
	w := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	rd := (instr >> 12) & 0xF

	var offset uint32
	if regOff {
		offset = c.R[instr&0xF]
	} else {
		offset = ((instr>>8)&0xF)<<4 | (instr & 0xF)
	}
	ea, wb, doWB := addrMode(c.R[rn], offset, pre, up, w)

	writeback := func() {
		if !doWB {
			return
		}
		if rn == 15 {
			c.branch(wb + 4)
		} else {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
	}

	if store {
		c.store(ea, 4, c.R[rd])
		c.store(ea+4, 4, c.R[rd+1])
		writeback()
		return 2
	}
	lo := c.load(ea, 4, false)
	hi := c.load(ea+4, 4, false)
	if rn != rd && rn != rd+1 {
		writeback()
	}
	c.R[rd] = lo
	c.R[rd+1] = hi
	return 3
}

// blockStart returns the address of the first (lowest-address)
// transfer of a block covering count words from base, for the
// four addressing modes.
func blockStart(base uint32, count int, pre, up bool) uint32 {
	switch {
	case up && !pre:
		return base
	case up && pre:
		return base + 4
	case !up && !pre:
		return base - 4*uint32(count-1)
	default:
		return base - 4*uint32(count)
	}
}

// execBlock runs LDM and STM, all four addressing modes. With
// the S bit set the CPU switches to the user register view for
// the whole transfer, except for an S-bit LDM that also loads
// the PC, which transfers into the current view and then
// restores the CPSR from the SPSR (the exception return). The
// base writeback is applied when the first register of the list
// is reached: before that register is loaded (so a base in the
// list ends with the loaded value) and after it is stored (so a
// base heading the list is stored with its original value). An
// empty register list transfers R15 only, with a writeback
// offset of 0x40.
func (c *CPU) execBlock(instr uint32, addr uint32) int {
	pre := instr&(1<<24) != 0
	up := instr&(1<<23) != 0
	sBit := instr&(1<<22) != 0
	w := instr&(1<<21) != 0
	load := instr&(1<<20) != 0
	rn := (instr >> 16) & 0xF
	list := uint32(instr & 0xFFFF)
	base := c.R[rn]

	mode := c.Mode()
	transferPC := list&(1<<15) != 0
	switchMode := sBit && (!load || !transferPC) && mode != ModeUSR && mode != ModeSYS

	empty := list == 0
	if empty {
		list = 1 << 15
		transferPC = true
	}
	count := 0
	first := 16
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) != 0 {
			count++
			if first == 16 {
				first = int(i)
			}
		}
	}
	bytes := uint32(count) * 4
	if empty {
		bytes = 0x40
	}
	var wb uint32
	if up {
		wb = base + bytes
	} else {
		wb = base - bytes
	}
	start := blockStart(base, int(bytes/4), pre, up)

	origCPSR := c.CPSR
	if switchMode {
		c.setCPSR(origCPSR&^0x1F | ModeUSR)
	}

	var pcVal uint32
	pcSet := false
	wbApplied := false
	applyWB := func() {
		wbApplied = true
		if rn != 15 {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
	}
	cur := start
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<uint(i)) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if load {
			v := c.Bus.Read(cur, 4)
			if w && i == first {
				applyWB()
			}
			if i == 15 {
				pcVal, pcSet = v, true
			} else {
				c.R[i] = v
			}
		} else {
			var v uint32
			switch {
			case i == 15 && rn == 15 && w && wbApplied:
				v = wb // base is PC and writeback already applied
			case i == 15:
				v = c.R[15] + 4 // STM stores PC as A+12
			default:
				v = c.R[i]
			}
			c.Bus.Write(cur, 4, v)
			if w && i == first {
				applyWB()
			}
		}
		cur += 4
	}

	if switchMode {
		c.setCPSR(origCPSR)
	}
	if load && pcSet {
		if sBit {
			// Exception return: the CPSR comes back from the
			// SPSR, and the pipeline refills at the loaded PC
			// in the restored state.
			c.setCPSR(c.curSPSR())
			c.branch(pcVal)
		} else {
			c.branchPC(pcVal)
		}
		return count + 4
	}
	if w && rn == 15 {
		c.branch(wb)
	}
	if load {
		return count + 2
	}
	return count + 1
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/chips/armcore/armcore.go ====================

// Package armcore is the shared ARM execution core behind the DS
// module's two processors. One implementation is configured two
// ways: ARMv4T (the DS ARM7TDMI) and ARMv5TE (the DS ARM946E-S,
// "ARM9" here), matching how the two silicon blocks share one
// architecture lineage. The chips/arm7 and chips/arm9 packages
// expose the two configurations under their own names.
//
// The core is written from the published ARM architecture
// documentation and GBATEK. Memory access goes through the Bus
// interface so the same core runs against the DS system bus and
// against the transaction-backed memory used by the
// SingleStepTests ARM7TDMI conformance corpus.
package armcore

// Processor modes, CPSR bits 4-0.
const (
	ModeUSR = 0x10
	ModeFIQ = 0x11
	ModeIRQ = 0x12
	ModeSVC = 0x13
	ModeABT = 0x17
	ModeUND = 0x1B
	ModeSYS = 0x1F
)

// CPSR/SPSR flag and control bits.
const (
	FlagN = 1 << 31
	FlagZ = 1 << 30
	FlagC = 1 << 29
	FlagV = 1 << 28
	FlagQ = 1 << 27

	BitI = 1 << 7
	BitF = 1 << 6
	BitT = 1 << 5
)

// SPSR slots, in the order the conformance corpus lists them.
const (
	SPSRFIQ = iota
	SPSRSVC
	SPSRABT
	SPSRIRQ
	SPSRUND
	SPSRCount
)

// Exception vectors, offsets from the vector base (0x00000000, or
// 0xFFFF0000 on the ARM9 when the CP15 control V bit is set).
const (
	VectorReset  = 0x00
	VectorUndef  = 0x04
	VectorSWI    = 0x08
	VectorPAbort = 0x0C
	VectorDAbort = 0x10
	VectorIRQ    = 0x18
	VectorFIQ    = 0x1C
)

// Bus is the memory interface the CPU executes against. Read and
// Write are data accesses; Fetch is an instruction-stream read.
// Sizes are in bytes: 1, 2 or 4. Read returns the value zero
// extended to 32 bits (the CPU applies rotation and sign extension
// rules itself). Write passes the value in the low bits.
type Bus interface {
	Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32
	Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32)
	Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32
}

// Config selects the architecture generation of a CPU instance.
type Config struct {
	// V5 enables the ARMv5TE additions: CLZ, the saturating
	// Q arithmetic, the signed halfword multiplies, LDRD/STRD,
	// BLX, BKPT, PLD handling, load-to-PC state selection from
	// bit 0, and the CP15 system control coprocessor.
	V5 bool
	// Name is "ARM7TDMI" or "ARM946E-S" for diagnostics.
	Name string
}

// cp15Index flattens a CP15 register address (CRn, CRm, opcode2)
// into the storage array.
func cp15Index(crn, crm, opc2 uint32) int {
	return int(crn<<7 | crm<<3 | opc2)
}

// CP15 register addresses used by this core, precomputed.
const (
	cp15ID       = 0 // c0, c0, 0: main ID register
	cp15Control  = 1 << 7
	cp15FSR      = 5 << 7      // c5, c0, 0: fault status
	cp15FAR      = 6 << 7      // c6, c0, 0: fault address
	cp15DTCM     = 9<<7 | 1<<3 // c9, c1, 0: data TCM base/size
	cp15ITCM     = 9<<7 | 1<<3 | 1
	cp15ControlV = 1 << 13 // high exception vectors
	cp15DTCMEn   = 1 << 16
	cp15ITCMEn   = 1 << 18
)

// CPU is the complete processor state for one configured core.
//
// R is the register file as seen in the current mode. The banked
// registers of the inactive modes live in the RFIQ/RSVC/RABT/RIRQ/
// RUND/RUSR fields; mode switches swap R8-R14 (and R8-R12 for FIQ)
// between R and the bank fields, so at any moment R plus the bank
// fields together hold every physical register exactly once, with
// one exception: when a mode is active its bank fields are stale
// copies and R is authoritative for that mode.
//
// Pipe holds the two fetched instruction words behind the
// instruction being executed: in ARM state Pipe[0] is the word in
// the decode stage (the next instruction) and Pipe[1] the word in
// the fetch stage; in Thumb state they hold halfwords, zero
// extended. The executing instruction sits at R[15]-8 in ARM state
// and R[15]-4 in Thumb state.
type CPU struct {
	Config Config

	R    [16]uint32
	RFIQ [7]uint32 // R8-R14 of FIQ mode
	RSVC [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of SVC mode
	RABT [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of ABT mode
	RIRQ [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of IRQ mode
	RUND [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of UND mode
	RUSR [2]uint32 // R13-R14 of USR/SYS modes

	CPSR uint32
	SPSR [SPSRCount]uint32

	// CP15 is the ARM9 system control register file, stored raw
	// (2048 words). It is meaningful only on the V5 configuration;
	// the ARM7 configuration never touches it. Cache and MPU
	// registers are storage only in this slice: no protection or
	// caching behavior is enforced from them.
	CP15 [2048]uint32

	// FSR and FAR mirror the ARM9 CP15 fault registers; they are
	// also kept as plain fields so aborts can be raised before
	// CP15 plumbing exists in a test harness.
	FSR uint32
	FAR uint32

	Pipe [2]uint32

	Bus Bus

	// Halted stops the core (used by the system to park a CPU
	// until its boot staging is complete).
	Halted bool

	// IRQLine and FIQLine are the interrupt input levels. They
	// are sampled at instruction boundaries.
	IRQLine bool
	FIQLine bool

	// Executing is the instruction word currently in the execute
	// stage. It is not serialized; it is reloaded from the bus on
	// Deserialize.
	Executing      uint32
	ExecutingValid bool

	// usr8_12 holds the user bank R8-R12 while FIQ mode is active
	// (they swap with the FIQ bank on mode changes). Serialized.
	usr8_12 [5]uint32

	// flushed marks that the last Step refilled the pipeline, so
	// the normal pipeline advance must be skipped.
	flushed bool

	// spsrDummy absorbs MSR-to-SPSR writes in modes that have no
	// SPSR (USR/SYS), where the write is architecturally ignored.
	spsrDummy uint32
}

// NewARM7 returns an ARM7TDMI (ARMv4T) CPU in its reset state.
func NewARM7(b Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{Config: Config{V5: false, Name: "ARM7TDMI"}, Bus: b}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// NewARM9 returns an ARM946E-S (ARMv5TE) CPU in its reset state,
// with the DS power-on CP15 TCM configuration installed.
func NewARM9(b Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{Config: Config{V5: true, Name: "ARM946E-S"}, Bus: b}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Mode returns the current processor mode bits.
func (c *CPU) Mode() uint32 { return c.CPSR & 0x1F }

// Thumb reports whether the core is in Thumb state.
func (c *CPU) Thumb() bool { return c.CPSR&BitT != 0 }

// VectorBase returns the exception vector base for this CPU: the
// high vector address on the ARM9 when CP15 control bit 13 is
// set, otherwise zero.
func (c *CPU) VectorBase() uint32 {
	if c.Config.V5 && c.CP15[cp15Control]&cp15ControlV != 0 {
		return 0xFFFF0000
	}
	return 0
}

// Reset puts the CPU in the documented power-on state: SVC mode,
// ARM state, IRQ and FIQ disabled, PC at the reset vector,
// pipeline refilled from the vector. On the ARM9 it also installs
// the DS CP15 defaults: instruction TCM 32 KB at 0x00000000 and
// data TCM 16 KB at 0x00800000, both enabled (the state DS
// software expects to find and reprogram).
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	for i := range c.R {
		c.R[i] = 0
	}
	c.RFIQ = [7]uint32{}
	c.RSVC = [2]uint32{}
	c.RABT = [2]uint32{}
	c.RIRQ = [2]uint32{}
	c.RUND = [2]uint32{}
	c.RUSR = [2]uint32{}
	c.SPSR = [SPSRCount]uint32{}
	c.CP15 = [2048]uint32{}
	c.FSR, c.FAR = 0, 0
	c.CPSR = ModeSVC | BitI | BitF
	c.usr8_12 = [5]uint32{}
	c.flushed = false
	c.spsrDummy = 0
	c.Halted = false
	c.IRQLine, c.FIQLine = false, false
	if c.Config.V5 {
		c.CP15[cp15ID] = 0x41059461 // ARM946E-S ID
		c.CP15[cp15Control] = cp15DTCMEn | cp15ITCMEn
		c.CP15[cp15DTCM] = 0x00800000 | 5<<1 // base 0x00800000, 16 KB
		c.CP15[cp15ITCM] = 6 << 1            // base 0x00000000, 32 KB
	}
	c.R[15] = 0
	c.refill(c.VectorBase())
}

// Jump refills the pipeline at addr in the current state. The
// system uses it to start a CPU at a cartridge entry point after
// boot staging.
func (c *CPU) Jump(addr uint32) {
	c.refill(addr)
	c.Halted = false
}

// refill loads the pipeline starting at the branch target addr
// and sets R15 so the unit at addr is in the execute position.
// In ARM state the R15 register keeps the target value verbatim
// (no low bits discarded, as the reference behavior shows); in
// Thumb state bit 0 is discarded. Instruction fetches are
// issued at the aligned address either way: word aligned in ARM
// state, halfword aligned in Thumb state.
func (c *CPU) refill(addr uint32) {
	if c.Thumb() {
		fa := addr &^ 1
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch(fa, 2)
		c.Pipe[0] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+2, 2)
		c.Pipe[1] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+4, 2)
		c.R[15] = fa + 4
	} else {
		fa := addr &^ 3
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch(fa, 4)
		c.Pipe[0] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+4, 4)
		c.Pipe[1] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+8, 4)
		c.R[15] = addr + 8
	}
	c.ExecutingValid = true
}

// TCMRegion decodes one TCM configuration register value into
// base and size in bytes. The size field encodes the region size
// as 512 bytes shifted left by the field value.
func TCMRegion(reg uint32) (base, size uint32) {
	base = reg & 0xFFFFF000
	field := (reg >> 1) & 0x1F
	if field > 15 {
		field = 15
	}
	size = 512 << field
	return base, size
}

// DTCMRegion returns the configured data TCM window and whether
// the data TCM is enabled in the CP15 control register.
func (c *CPU) DTCMRegion() (base, size uint32, enabled bool) {
	base, size = TCMRegion(c.CP15[cp15DTCM])
	return base, size, c.CP15[cp15Control]&cp15DTCMEn != 0
}

// ITCMRegion returns the configured instruction TCM window and
// whether the instruction TCM is enabled.
func (c *CPU) ITCMRegion() (base, size uint32, enabled bool) {
	base, size = TCMRegion(c.CP15[cp15ITCM])
	return base, size, c.CP15[cp15Control]&cp15ITCMEn != 0
}

// CP15Read returns the stored CP15 register at the given address.
// Reads of the fault registers return the live FSR/FAR fields.
func (c *CPU) CP15Read(crn, crm, opc2 uint32) uint32 {
	switch cp15Index(crn, crm, opc2) {
	case cp15FSR:
		return c.FSR
	case cp15FAR:
		return c.FAR
	}
	return c.CP15[cp15Index(crn, crm, opc2)]
}

// CP15Write stores a CP15 register. Writes to the fault registers
// update the live FSR/FAR fields as well as the storage.
func (c *CPU) CP15Write(crn, crm, opc2, val uint32) {
	switch cp15Index(crn, crm, opc2) {
	case cp15FSR:
		c.FSR = val
	case cp15FAR:
		c.FAR = val
	}
	c.CP15[cp15Index(crn, crm, opc2)] = val
}

// StateSize is the serialized size of the CPU state in bytes.
const StateSize = (16 + 7 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + SPSRCount + 2 + 5 + 1 + 2048 + 2) * 4

// Serialize writes the full CPU state to dst, which must be at
// least StateSize bytes. It returns the number of bytes written.
func (c *CPU) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &stateWriter{b: dst}
	for _, v := range c.R {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RFIQ {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RSVC {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RABT {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RIRQ {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RUND {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	for _, v := range c.RUSR {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.u32(c.CPSR)
	for _, v := range c.SPSR {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.u32(c.Pipe[0])
	w.u32(c.Pipe[1])
	for _, v := range c.usr8_12 {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	var flags uint32
	if c.Halted {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if c.IRQLine {
		flags |= 2
	}
	if c.FIQLine {
		flags |= 4
	}
	w.u32(flags)
	for _, v := range c.CP15 {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.u32(c.FSR)
	w.u32(c.FAR)
	return w.n
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize. It reports
// false, leaving the CPU untouched, when src is too short.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < StateSize {
		return false
	}
	r := &stateReader{b: src}
	for i := range c.R {
		c.R[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RFIQ {
		c.RFIQ[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RSVC {
		c.RSVC[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RABT {
		c.RABT[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RIRQ {
		c.RIRQ[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RUND {
		c.RUND[i] = r.u32()
	}
	for i := range c.RUSR {
		c.RUSR[i] = r.u32()
	}
	c.CPSR = r.u32()
	for i := range c.SPSR {
		c.SPSR[i] = r.u32()
	}
	c.Pipe[0] = r.u32()
	c.Pipe[1] = r.u32()
	for i := range c.usr8_12 {
		c.usr8_12[i] = r.u32()
	}
	flags := r.u32()
	c.Halted = flags&1 != 0
	c.IRQLine = flags&2 != 0
	c.FIQLine = flags&4 != 0
	for i := range c.CP15 {
		c.CP15[i] = r.u32()
	}
	c.FSR = r.u32()
	c.FAR = r.u32()
	// The executing instruction is the one behind Pipe in the
	// stream: at R15-8 (ARM) or R15-4 (Thumb). Re-fetch it from
	// the bus so the next Step executes the same instruction the
	// saved core was about to execute.
	if c.Thumb() {
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]-4)&^1, 2)
	} else {
		c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]-8)&^3, 4)
	}
	c.ExecutingValid = true
	return true
}

type stateWriter struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) {
	w.b[w.n+0] = byte(v)
	w.b[w.n+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	w.b[w.n+2] = byte(v >> 16)
	w.b[w.n+3] = byte(v >> 24)
	w.n += 4
}

type stateReader struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (r *stateReader) u32() uint32 {
	v := uint32(r.b[r.n]) | uint32(r.b[r.n+1])<<8 | uint32(r.b[r.n+2])<<16 | uint32(r.b[r.n+3])<<24
	r.n += 4
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/chips/armcore/armcore_test.go ====================

package armcore

// Hand-derived ARMv5TE unit vectors, worked out from the ARM
// architecture reference encodings and semantics (the ARM7TDMI
// corpus cannot cover any of these: it predates the E
// extensions). Each test assembles one instruction word from its
// documented bit fields and checks the architectural result,
// including the Q flag behavior the task calls out.

import "testing"

type ramBus struct{ mem [1 << 16]byte }

func (b *ramBus) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	addr &= 0xFFFF
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		v |= uint32(b.mem[(addr+uint32(i))&0xFFFF]) << (8 * i)
	}
	return v
}

func (b *ramBus) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	addr &= 0xFFFF
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		b.mem[(addr+uint32(i))&0xFFFF] = byte(val >> (8 * i))
	}
}

func (b *ramBus) Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32 { return b.Read(addr, size) }

func newTestCPU(v5 bool) (*CPU, *ramBus) {
	b := &ramBus{}
	if v5 {
		return NewARM9(b), b
	}
	return NewARM7(b), b
}

// execARMWord places word at addr, jumps there, and steps once.
func execARMWord(c *CPU, b *ramBus, addr, word uint32) {
	b.Write(addr, 4, word)
	c.Jump(addr)
	c.Step()
}

func TestCLZEdges(t *testing.T) {
	c, b := newTestCPU(true)
	clz := func(rm uint32) uint32 { return 0xE16F0F10 | rm }
	cases := []struct{ in, want uint32 }{
		{0, 32},
		{0x80000000, 0},
		{0x00010000, 15},
		{0x00000001, 31},
		{0x00F00000, 8},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		c.R[1] = tc.in
		execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, clz(1))
		if c.R[0] != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("CLZ(%08x): got %d want %d", tc.in, c.R[0], tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestQOps(t *testing.T) {
	// Encodings: base 0xE1000050 (QADD), opcode bits 23-20 step
	// by 2 per operation; Rn at bits 19-16, Rd at bits 15-12,
	// Rm at bits 3-0.
	const qadd = 0xE1000050
	const qsub = 0xE1200050
	const qdadd = 0xE1400050
	const qdsub = 0xE1600050
	mk := func(base uint32) uint32 { return base | 2<<16 | 0<<12 | 1 } // Rd=R0, Rm=R1, Rn=R2

	c, b := newTestCPU(true)
	// QADD saturation high.
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 0x7FFFFFFF, 1
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, mk(qadd))
	if c.R[0] != 0x7FFFFFFF || c.CPSR&FlagQ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("QADD sat: R0=%08x Q=%v", c.R[0], c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0)
	}
	// Q flag is sticky: a clean QADD leaves it set.
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 3, 4
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, mk(qadd))
	if c.R[0] != 7 || c.CPSR&FlagQ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("QADD clean after sat: R0=%08x Q=%v", c.R[0], c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0)
	}
	c.CPSR &^= FlagQ
	// QSUB saturation low.
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 0x80000000, 1
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, mk(qsub))
	if c.R[0] != 0x80000000 || c.CPSR&FlagQ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("QSUB sat: R0=%08x Q=%v", c.R[0], c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0)
	}
	c.CPSR &^= FlagQ
	// QDADD: the doubling saturates first (Rn=0x40000000 doubles
	// past the range), Q set, final result saturates too.
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 10, 0x40000000
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, mk(qdadd))
	if c.R[0] != 0x7FFFFFFF || c.CPSR&FlagQ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("QDADD: R0=%08x Q=%v", c.R[0], c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0)
	}
	c.CPSR &^= FlagQ
	// QDSUB: doubling saturates (Q set) but the subtraction
	// itself lands in range.
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 0, 0x40000000
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, mk(qdsub))
	if c.R[0] != 0x80000001 || c.CPSR&FlagQ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("QDSUB: R0=%08x Q=%v", c.R[0], c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0)
	}
	// QDADD in range: 5 + 2*7 = 19, Q stays clear.
	c.CPSR &^= FlagQ
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 5, 7
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, mk(qdadd))
	if c.R[0] != 19 || c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0 {
		t.Errorf("QDADD clean: R0=%08x Q=%v", c.R[0], c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0)
	}
	// NZCV must be untouched by Q ops.
	c.CPSR |= FlagN | FlagV
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 1, 2
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, mk(qadd))
	if c.CPSR&FlagN == 0 || c.CPSR&FlagV == 0 {
		t.Errorf("QADD clobbered NZCV: CPSR=%08x", c.CPSR)
	}
}

func TestDSPMultiplies(t *testing.T) {
	c, b := newTestCPU(true)
	// SMULBB R0, R1, R2: opcode 1011, halves from bits 6 (y, Rs)
	// and 5 (x, Rm); base includes bit 7 set, bit 4 clear.
	smulbb := uint32(0xE1600281)
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 0x00030004, 0x00050006
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smulbb)
	if c.R[0] != 24 {
		t.Errorf("SMULBB: got %d want 24", c.R[0])
	}
	// SMULTT: both top halves: 3 * 5 = 15.
	smultt := uint32(0xE16002E1)
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smultt)
	if c.R[0] != 15 {
		t.Errorf("SMULTT: got %d want 15", c.R[0])
	}
	// SMULBB with negative halves: low halves are 0xFFFE (-2)
	// and 0x0003 (3): product -6.
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 0x0000FFFE, 0x00000003
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smulbb)
	if int32(c.R[0]) != -6 {
		t.Errorf("SMULBB neg: got %d want -6", int32(c.R[0]))
	}
	// SMLABB R0, R1, R2, R3: 4*6 + 100 = 124.
	smlabb := uint32(0xE1003281)
	c.R[1], c.R[2], c.R[3] = 0x00030004, 0x00050006, 100
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smlabb)
	if c.R[0] != 124 {
		t.Errorf("SMLABB: got %d want 124", c.R[0])
	}
	// SMLA overflow wraps and sets Q without clamping:
	// low halves 0x7FFF * 0x7FFF = 0x3FFF0001, plus Rn
	// 0x7FFFFFFF wraps negative.
	c.CPSR &^= FlagQ
	c.R[1], c.R[2], c.R[3] = 0x00007FFF, 0x00007FFF, 0x7FFFFFFF
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smlabb)
	want := uint32(int64(0x3FFF0001) + int64(0x7FFFFFFF))
	if c.R[0] != want || c.CPSR&FlagQ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("SMLA wrap: R0=%08x want %08x Q=%v", c.R[0], want, c.CPSR&FlagQ != 0)
	}
	// SMULWT R0, R1, R2: (0x00020000 * 4) >> 16 = 8.
	smulwt := uint32(0xE12002E1)
	c.R[1], c.R[2] = 0x00020000, 0x00040000
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smulwt)
	if c.R[0] != 8 {
		t.Errorf("SMULWT: got %d want 8", c.R[0])
	}
	// SMLAWB R0, R1, R2, R3: (0x00010000 * 3) >> 16 + 10 = 13.
	smlawb := uint32(0xE1203281)
	c.R[1], c.R[2], c.R[3] = 0x00010000, 0x00000003, 10
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smlawb)
	if c.R[0] != 13 {
		t.Errorf("SMLAWB: got %d want 13", c.R[0])
	}
	// SMLALBB R1:R0 pair (RdHi=R0 at bits 19-16, RdLo=R1 at
	// bits 15-12), Rm=R2, Rs=R3: 5 + 3*4 = 17.
	smlalbb := uint32(0xE1401382)
	c.R[0], c.R[1] = 0, 5
	c.R[2], c.R[3] = 3, 4
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, smlalbb)
	if c.R[1] != 17 || c.R[0] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("SMLALBB: pair=%08x:%08x want 0:17", c.R[0], c.R[1])
	}
}

func TestDoublewordTransfers(t *testing.T) {
	c, b := newTestCPU(true)
	// STRD R0, [R4] = 0xE1C400F0; LDRD R0, [R4] = 0xE1C400D0.
	c.R[4] = 0x200
	c.R[0], c.R[1] = 0xAABBCCDD, 0x11223344
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xE1C400F0)
	if got := b.Read(0x200, 4); got != 0xAABBCCDD {
		t.Fatalf("STRD low word: got %08x", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read(0x204, 4); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Fatalf("STRD high word: got %08x", got)
	}
	c.R[0], c.R[1] = 0, 0
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xE1C400D0)
	if c.R[0] != 0xAABBCCDD || c.R[1] != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("LDRD: got %08x:%08x", c.R[1], c.R[0])
	}
}

func TestCP15RoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	c, b := newTestCPU(true)
	// MCR p15, 0, R0, c1, c0, 0 (control) = 0xEE010F10.
	// MRC p15, 0, R1, c1, c0, 0 = 0xEE111F10.
	c.R[0] = 0x00052078
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xEE010F10)
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xEE111F10)
	if c.R[1] != 0x00052078 {
		t.Errorf("CP15 control round trip: got %08x", c.R[1])
	}
	// High vectors bit drives the vector base.
	if c.VectorBase() != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Errorf("VectorBase with V set: got %08x", c.VectorBase())
	}
	// DTCM config: MCR p15, 0, R0, c9, c1, 0 = 0xEE090F11.
	// Value: base 0x02000000, size field 6 (32 KB).
	c.R[0] = 0x02000000 | 6<<1
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xEE090F11)
	base, size, en := c.DTCMRegion()
	if base != 0x02000000 || size != 32768 || !en {
		t.Errorf("DTCMRegion: base=%08x size=%d en=%v", base, size, en)
	}
	// MRC into R15 loads only the flag nibble of the CPSR.
	c.CP15Write(0, 0, 0, 0xF0000000)
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xEE10FF10) // MRC p15,0,R15,c0,c0,0
	if c.CPSR&0xF0000000 != 0xF0000000 {
		t.Errorf("MRC to R15: CPSR=%08x", c.CPSR)
	}
}

func TestCoprocessorUndefinedOnARM7(t *testing.T) {
	c, b := newTestCPU(false)
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xEE010F10) // MCR on ARMv4T: no CP15
	if c.Mode() != ModeUND {
		t.Errorf("MCR on ARM7 should trap undefined, mode=%02x", c.Mode())
	}
	if c.R[14] != 0x104 {
		t.Errorf("UND LR: got %08x want 104", c.R[14])
	}
}

func TestBKPTPrefetchAbort(t *testing.T) {
	c, b := newTestCPU(true)
	execARMWord(c, b, 0x100, 0xE1200070) // BKPT #0
	if c.Mode() != ModeABT {
		t.Fatalf("BKPT should enter ABT mode, mode=%02x", c.Mode())
	}
	if c.R[14] != 0x104 {
		t.Errorf("ABT LR after BKPT: got %08x want 104", c.R[14])
	}
	if c.FAR != 0x100 {
		t.Errorf("FAR after BKPT: got %08x want 100", c.FAR)
	}
	if got := c.CP15Read(5, 0, 0); got != c.FSR {
		t.Errorf("CP15 FSR mirror: got %08x want %08x", got, c.FSR)
	}
	if got := c.CP15Read(6, 0, 0); got != 0x100 {
		t.Errorf("CP15 FAR: got %08x", got)
	}
}
