	if c.Mode() != ModeABT || c.FAR != 0x02000004 || c.FSR == 0 {
		t.Errorf("DataAbort: mode=%02x FAR=%08x FSR=%08x", c.Mode(), c.FAR, c.FSR)
	}
}

func TestThumbBLXRegister(t *testing.T) {
	c, b := newTestCPU(true)
	b.Write(0x100, 2, 0x4788) // BLX R1
	c.CPSR |= BitT
	c.Jump(0x100)
	c.R[1] = 0x200
	c.Step()
	if c.Thumb() {
		t.Error("BLX register should leave Thumb state for an even target")
	}
	if c.R[14] != 0x103 {
		t.Errorf("BLX LR: got %08x want 103", c.R[14])
	}
	if c.R[15] != 0x208 {
		t.Errorf("BLX target R15: got %08x want 208", c.R[15])
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := newTestCPU(true)
	c.R[3] = 0xCAFEBABE
	c.R[13] = 0x02004000
	c.CP15Write(1, 0, 0, 0x00052078)
	c.FSR, c.FAR = 0x5, 0x2000
	buf := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if n := c.Serialize(buf); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize wrote %d bytes, StateSize=%d", n, StateSize)
	}
	d, _ := newTestCPU(true)
	if !d.Deserialize(buf) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize refused a full state")
	}
	if d.R[3] != 0xCAFEBABE || d.R[13] != 0x02004000 {
		t.Errorf("registers did not round trip: R3=%08x R13=%08x", d.R[3], d.R[13])
	}
	if d.CP15Read(1, 0, 0) != 0x00052078 {
		t.Errorf("CP15 did not round trip: %08x", d.CP15Read(1, 0, 0))
	}
	if d.FSR != 0x5 || d.FAR != 0x2000 {
		t.Errorf("FSR/FAR did not round trip: %08x %08x", d.FSR, d.FAR)
	}
	if d.Deserialize(buf[:StateSize-1]) {
		t.Error("Deserialize accepted a short state")
	}
}

func TestResetDefaultsARM9(t *testing.T) {
	c, _ := newTestCPU(true)
	if c.Mode() != ModeSVC || c.Thumb() {
		t.Errorf("reset state: mode=%02x CPSR=%08x", c.Mode(), c.CPSR)
	}
	base, size, en := c.ITCMRegion()
	if base != 0 || size != 32768 || !en {
		t.Errorf("ITCM reset: base=%08x size=%d en=%v", base, size, en)
	}
	base, size, en = c.DTCMRegion()
	if base != 0x00800000 || size != 16384 || !en {
		t.Errorf("DTCM reset: base=%08x size=%d en=%v", base, size, en)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/chips/armcore/conformance_test.go ====================

package armcore

// The SingleStepTests ARM7TDMI conformance gate.
//
// The corpus (github.com/SingleStepTests/ARM7TDMI, generated
// from NanoBoyAdvance) ships as binary .json.bin files: a header
// (magic 0xD33DBAE0, test count), then per test an initial
// state, a final state, a transaction list and the opcode with
// its base address. Each state is 40 u32 values: R0-R15, the FIQ
// bank R8-R14, the SVC/ABT/IRQ/UND banked R13-R14 pairs, CPSR,
// the five SPSRs (fiq, svc, abt, irq, und order), two pipeline
// words, and an access field this harness ignores.
//
// There is no ARM9 set in SingleStepTests/ProcessorTests (its
// root listing has no ARM directory at all, checked 2026-10-13),
// so this ARM7TDMI corpus is the only published single-step gate
// available for either DS processor. It gates:
//   - the ARM7 configuration in full (TestSingleStepARM7);
//   - the ARM9 configuration over the ARMv4T-shared instruction
//     space (TestSingleStepARM9Shared), excluding the MCR/MRC
//     file: on the ARM9, CP15 exists, so those encodings are
//     register transfers there instead of the undefined trap the
//     ARM7 corpus expects. Eleven further files are run in
//     report-only mode for the ARM9: every divergence in them is
//     the documented ARMv5 interworking change (PC writes
//     select the instruction state from bit 0; Thumb BLX
//     register writes LR), which the ARMv4T generator does not
//     model. ARMv5TE-only behavior is covered by the
//     hand-derived vectors in armcore_test.go instead.
//
// The harness installs the initial state, executes one Step
// against a transaction-backed bus, and compares registers,
// CPSR, SPSRs, bank storage, the pipeline model, and every data
// read and write in order. The corpus does not publish a
// trustworthy total cycle count, so Step cycle counts follow
// the published cycle model and are not corpus-compared.
//
// The corpus lives under testroms/tomharte-arm7tdmi in this
// module (gitignored, local evidence only). When it is absent
// the gates skip. The per-file subset defaults to 2,000 of the
// 50,000 tests (seeded); set NDS_TH_SUBSET=50000 to run
// everything and NDS_TH_SEED to change the seed.

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"math/rand"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"testing"
)

type thState struct {
	R        [16]uint32
	RFIQ     [7]uint32
	RSVC     [2]uint32
	RABT     [2]uint32
	RIRQ     [2]uint32
	RUND     [2]uint32
	CPSR     uint32
	SPSR     [5]uint32
	Pipeline [2]uint32
}

type thTxn struct {
	kind uint32
	size uint32
	addr uint32
	data uint32
}

type thTest struct {
	initial thState
	final   thState
	txns    []thTxn
	opcode  uint32
	base    uint32
}

func parseState(b []byte, off int) thState {
	var s thState
	v := func(i int) uint32 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[off+8+i*4:]) }
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		s.R[i] = v(i)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 7; i++ {
		s.RFIQ[i] = v(16 + i)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.RSVC[i] = v(23 + i)
		s.RABT[i] = v(25 + i)
		s.RIRQ[i] = v(27 + i)
		s.RUND[i] = v(29 + i)
	}
	s.CPSR = v(31)
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		s.SPSR[i] = v(32 + i)
	}
	s.Pipeline[0] = v(37)
	s.Pipeline[1] = v(38)
	return s
}

func parseCorpusFile(t *testing.T, path string) []thTest {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(data) < 8 || binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data) != 0xD33DBAE0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s: bad magic", path)
	}
	num := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[4:]))
	tests := make([]thTest, 0, num)
	off := 8
	u32 := func(p int) uint32 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[p:]) }
	for i := 0; i < num; i++ {
		recStart := off
		recSize := int(int32(u32(off)))
		off += 4
		var tt thTest
		secSize := int(int32(u32(off)))
		tt.initial = parseState(data, off)
		off += secSize
		secSize = int(int32(u32(off)))
		tt.final = parseState(data, off)
		off += secSize
		secSize = int(int32(u32(off)))
		nTxn := int(int32(u32(off + 8)))
		for j := 0; j < nTxn; j++ {
			p := off + 12 + j*24
			tt.txns = append(tt.txns, thTxn{
				kind: u32(p), size: u32(p + 4), addr: u32(p + 8), data: u32(p + 12),
			})
		}
		off += secSize
		tt.opcode = u32(off + 8)
		tt.base = u32(off + 12)
		off += 16
		if off != recStart+recSize {
			t.Fatalf("%s test %d: record walk desync (%d != %d)", path, i, off, recStart+recSize)
		}
		tests = append(tests, tt)
	}
	return tests
}

// corpusBus plays the transaction list back to the CPU.
type corpusBus struct {
	base   uint32
	opcode uint32
	data   []thTxn // kind 1 and 2, in order
	pos    int
	code   []thTxn // kind 0, in order
	codeIx map[uint32]int
	fail   string
}

func newCorpusBus(tt *thTest) *corpusBus {
	b := &corpusBus{base: tt.base, opcode: tt.opcode, codeIx: map[uint32]int{}}
	for _, x := range tt.txns {
		switch x.kind {
		case 1, 2:
			b.data = append(b.data, x)
		case 0:
			if _, dup := b.codeIx[x.addr]; !dup {
				b.codeIx[x.addr] = len(b.code)
			}
			b.code = append(b.code, x)
		}
	}
	return b
}

func (b *corpusBus) setFail(format string, args ...interface{}) {
	if b.fail == "" {
		b.fail = fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
	}
}

func (b *corpusBus) Read(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	if b.pos >= len(b.data) {
		b.setFail("unexpected data read addr=%08x size=%d (no transactions left)", addr, size)
		return 0
	}
	x := b.data[b.pos]
	b.pos++
	if x.kind != 1 || x.addr != addr || x.size != uint32(size) {
		b.setFail("data read #%d: cpu read kind=%d addr=%08x size=%d, corpus has kind=%d addr=%08x size=%d",
			b.pos-1, 1, addr, size, x.kind, x.addr, x.size)
	}
	return x.data
}

func (b *corpusBus) Write(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	if b.pos >= len(b.data) {
		b.setFail("unexpected data write addr=%08x size=%d val=%08x (no transactions left)", addr, size, val)
		return
	}
	x := b.data[b.pos]
	b.pos++
	if x.kind != 2 || x.addr != addr || x.size != uint32(size) || x.data != val {
		b.setFail("data write #%d: cpu wrote addr=%08x size=%d val=%08x, corpus has kind=%d addr=%08x size=%d data=%08x",
			b.pos-1, addr, size, val, x.kind, x.addr, x.size, x.data)
	}
}

func (b *corpusBus) Fetch(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	// Code transactions are keyed by address AND size: a state
	// switch at the branch target can record a Thumb fetch and
	// an ARM fetch at the same address in one test.
	fallback := -1
	for i, x := range b.code {
		if x.addr != addr {
			continue
		}
		if int(x.size) == size {
			return x.data
		}
		if fallback < 0 {
			fallback = i
		}
	}
	if fallback >= 0 {
		return b.code[fallback].data
	}
	if size == 2 {
		return addr & 0xFFFF
	}
	return addr
}

func loadState(c *CPU, s *thState, tt *thTest) {
	// The corpus dumps raw bank storage with no swapping: its R
	// array is the user-bank view (R8-R14 as USR sees them) and
	// each mode's banked registers sit in their own arrays, even
	// for the active mode. This CPU keeps the active view in R
	// and swaps banks on mode changes, so loading composes the
	// active registers from the bank arrays of the initial mode,
	// while the bank fields themselves are loaded verbatim.
	mode := s.CPSR & 0x1F
	c.R = s.R
	c.RFIQ = s.RFIQ
	c.RSVC = s.RSVC
	c.RABT = s.RABT
	c.RIRQ = s.RIRQ
	c.RUND = s.RUND
	c.RUSR = [2]uint32{s.R[13], s.R[14]}
	c.usr8_12 = [5]uint32{}
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(c.usr8_12[:], s.R[8:13])
		copy(c.R[8:13], s.RFIQ[0:5])
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RFIQ[5], s.RFIQ[6]
	case ModeSVC:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RSVC[0], s.RSVC[1]
	case ModeABT:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RABT[0], s.RABT[1]
	case ModeIRQ:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RIRQ[0], s.RIRQ[1]
	case ModeUND:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = s.RUND[0], s.RUND[1]
	}
	c.CPSR = s.CPSR
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		c.SPSR[i] = s.SPSR[i]
	}
	c.Executing = tt.opcode
	c.ExecutingValid = true
	c.Pipe[0] = s.Pipeline[1]
	// The fetch-stage slot holds the word the step's own code
	// transaction at the initial R15 returns; when the corpus has
	// no such transaction (control flow refills anyway), fall
	// back to the final pipeline value, which that slot feeds.
	c.Pipe[1] = tt.final.Pipeline[1]
	for _, x := range tt.txns {
		if x.kind == 0 && x.addr == s.R[15] {
			c.Pipe[1] = x.data
			break
		}
	}
	c.Halted = false
	c.flushed = false
}

// composedViews translates the CPU's swap-based state back into
// the corpus's raw bank storage layout, keyed by the final mode.
func composedViews(c *CPU) (view [16]uint32, fiq [7]uint32, svc, abt, irq, und [2]uint32) {
	view = c.R
	fiq = c.RFIQ
	svc = c.RSVC
	abt = c.RABT
	irq = c.RIRQ
	und = c.RUND
	switch c.Mode() {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(view[8:13], c.usr8_12[:])
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		copy(fiq[0:5], c.R[8:13])
		fiq[5], fiq[6] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeSVC:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		svc[0], svc[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeABT:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		abt[0], abt[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeIRQ:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		irq[0], irq[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeUND:
		view[13], view[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
		und[0], und[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	}
	return
}

func diffState(c *CPU, tt *thTest, bus *corpusBus) []string {
	var diffs []string
	f := &tt.final
	view, fiq, svc, abt, irq, und := composedViews(c)
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if view[i] != f.R[i] {
			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("R%d: got %08x want %08x", i, view[i], f.R[i]))
		}
	}
	if c.CPSR != f.CPSR {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("CPSR: got %08x want %08x", c.CPSR, f.CPSR))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		if c.SPSR[i] != f.SPSR[i] {
			diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("SPSR[%d]: got %08x want %08x", i, c.SPSR[i], f.SPSR[i]))
		}
	}
	banks := []struct {
		name string
		got  []uint32
		want []uint32
	}{
		{"R_fiq", fiq[:], f.RFIQ[:]},
		{"R_svc", svc[:], f.RSVC[:]},
		{"R_abt", abt[:], f.RABT[:]},
		{"R_irq", irq[:], f.RIRQ[:]},
		{"R_und", und[:], f.RUND[:]},
	}
	for _, bk := range banks {
		for i := range bk.got {
			if bk.got[i] != bk.want[i] {
				diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("%s[%d]: got %08x want %08x", bk.name, i, bk.got[i], bk.want[i]))
			}
		}
	}
	if c.Executing != f.Pipeline[0] {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("pipeline[0]: got %08x want %08x", c.Executing, f.Pipeline[0]))
	}
	if c.Pipe[0] != f.Pipeline[1] {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("pipeline[1]: got %08x want %08x", c.Pipe[0], f.Pipeline[1]))
	}
	if bus.fail != "" {
		diffs = append(diffs, "bus: "+bus.fail)
	}
	if bus.pos != len(bus.data) {
		diffs = append(diffs, fmt.Sprintf("bus: consumed %d of %d data transactions", bus.pos, len(bus.data)))
	}
	return diffs
}

func corpusDir(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "testroms", "tomharte-arm7tdmi")
	if st, err := os.Stat(dir); err != nil || !st.IsDir() {
		t.Skipf("corpus not present at %s", dir)
	}
	return dir
}

func corpusSubset() (subset int, seed int64) {
	subset = 2000
	if v := os.Getenv("NDS_TH_SUBSET"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &subset)
	}
	seed = 0xA7D1
	if v := os.Getenv("NDS_TH_SEED"); v != "" {
		fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &seed)
	}
	return subset, seed
}

func runCorpus(t *testing.T, v5 bool, exclude, soft map[string]bool) (run, fail, softRun, softFail int) {
	t.Helper()
	dir := corpusDir(t)
	files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, "*.json.bin"))
	if err != nil || len(files) == 0 {
		t.Skip("no corpus files")
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	subset, seed := corpusSubset()
	for _, path := range files {
		name := filepath.Base(path)
		if exclude[name] {
			t.Logf("%s: excluded from this configuration's gate", name)
			continue
		}
		tests := parseCorpusFile(t, path)
		rng := rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed + int64(len(name))))
		idx := rng.Perm(len(tests))
		if subset < len(idx) {
			idx = idx[:subset]
		}
		fails := 0
		for _, ix := range idx {
			tt := &tests[ix]
			bus := newCorpusBus(tt)
			cpu := &CPU{Bus: bus}
			cpu.Config = Config{V5: v5, Name: "corpus"}
			loadState(cpu, &tt.initial, tt)
			cpu.Step()
			if diffs := diffState(cpu, tt, bus); len(diffs) > 0 {
				fails++
				if fails <= 3 {
					t.Logf("%s test %d opcode=%08x base=%08x: %v", name, ix, tt.opcode, tt.base, diffs)
				}
			}
		}
		if soft[name] {
			softRun += len(idx)
			softFail += fails
			t.Logf("%s: %d/%d passed (report only: ARMv5 interworking divergence)", name, len(idx)-fails, len(idx))
			continue
		}
		run += len(idx)
		fail += fails
		t.Logf("%s: %d/%d passed", name, len(idx)-fails, len(idx))
		if fails > 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s: %d of %d tests failed", name, fails, len(idx))
		}
	}
	return run, fail, softRun, softFail
}

func TestSingleStepARM7(t *testing.T) {
	run, fail, _, _ := runCorpus(t, false, nil, nil)
	t.Logf("ARM7TDMI TOTAL: %d/%d passed", run-fail, run)
}

func TestSingleStepARM9Shared(t *testing.T) {
	// On the ARM9 the MCR/MRC encodings reach a real CP15
	// instead of the undefined trap the ARM7 corpus expects, so
	// that one file is excluded here; ARMv5 CP15 behavior is
	// pinned by the unit vectors in armcore_test.go.
	exclude := map[string]bool{"arm_mcr_mrc.json.bin": true}
	// The files below are run and reported but not gated: every
	// divergence in them is the documented ARMv5 interworking
	// change (a value written to the PC selects the instruction
	// state from its bit 0, and the Thumb BLX register form
	// writes LR), which the ARMv4T generator does not model.
	// The unit vectors pin the ARM9 behavior; the report keeps
	// the counts visible.
	soft := map[string]bool{
		"arm_data_proc_immediate.json.bin":       true,
		"arm_data_proc_immediate_shift.json.bin": true,
		"arm_data_proc_register_shift.json.bin":  true,
		"arm_ldm_stm.json.bin":                   true,
		"arm_ldr_str_immediate_offset.json.bin":  true,
		"arm_ldr_str_register_offset.json.bin":   true,
		"arm_ldrh_strh.json.bin":                 true,
		"arm_ldrsb_ldrsh.json.bin":               true,
		"thumb_add_cmp_mov_hi.json.bin":          true,
		"thumb_bx.json.bin":                      true,
		"thumb_push_pop.json.bin":                true,
	}
	run, fail, softRun, softFail := runCorpus(t, true, exclude, soft)
	t.Logf("ARM946E-S shared-space TOTAL: %d/%d passed (gated)", run-fail, run)
	t.Logf("ARM946E-S interworking files: %d/%d passed (report only)", softRun-softFail, softRun)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/chips/armcore/exec.go ====================

package armcore

// Step executes exactly one instruction and returns the number of
// bus cycles it consumed. Cycle counts follow the published
// ARM7TDMI S/N/I model and are used flat for the ARM9 as well in
// this slice (the DS system timing is budgeted per frame, not per
// bus transaction). Pending interrupt lines are sampled first.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	if c.Halted {
		return 1
	}
	if n, taken := c.pollInterrupts(); taken {
		return n
	}
	instr := c.Executing
	c.flushed = false
	state := c.Thumb()
	var n int
	if state {
		n = c.execThumb(uint16(instr))
	} else {
		n = c.execARM(instr)
	}
	if !c.flushed {
		// The pipeline advances in the state the instruction
		// was fetched in, even if the instruction rewrote the
		// CPSR T bit (an MSR may do that without disturbing
		// this step in the reference behavior).
		c.advance(state)
	}
	return n
}

// pollInterrupts enters IRQ or FIQ when a line is asserted and
// the corresponding CPSR mask bit is clear. The link register
// receives the address of the next instruction plus 4, per the
// architecture definition (PC plus 4 at the point of entry).
func (c *CPU) pollInterrupts() (int, bool) {
	if c.FIQLine && c.CPSR&BitF == 0 {
		lr := c.R[15]
		if !c.Thumb() {
			lr -= 4
		}
		return c.exception(VectorFIQ, ModeFIQ, lr), true
	}
	if c.IRQLine && c.CPSR&BitI == 0 {
		lr := c.R[15]
		if !c.Thumb() {
			lr -= 4
		}
		return c.exception(VectorIRQ, ModeIRQ, lr), true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// advance moves the pipeline one instruction unit forward without
// a control-flow change: the decode-stage unit enters execute and
// a new unit is fetched at the fetch-stage address. The unit size
// follows the state the executing instruction was fetched in.
func (c *CPU) advance(thumb bool) {
	if thumb {
		nf := c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]&^1)+2, 2)
		c.Executing = c.Pipe[0]
		c.Pipe[0] = c.Pipe[1]
		c.Pipe[1] = nf
		c.R[15] += 2
		c.ExecutingValid = true
		return
	}
	nf := c.Bus.Fetch((c.R[15]&^3)+4, 4)
	c.Executing = c.Pipe[0]
	c.Pipe[0] = c.Pipe[1]
	c.Pipe[1] = nf
	c.R[15] += 4
	c.ExecutingValid = true
}

// branch refills the pipeline at addr in the state the CPU is in
// after any CPSR change the instruction already made.
func (c *CPU) branch(addr uint32) {
	c.refill(addr)
	c.flushed = true
}

// branchPC handles an instruction writing a value into the PC
// through the normal register-write path (loads and data
// processing results). On ARMv5 the low bit of the value selects
// the instruction state; on ARMv4 the state is unchanged.
func (c *CPU) branchPC(v uint32) {
	if c.Config.V5 {
		if v&1 != 0 {
			c.CPSR |= BitT
		} else {
			c.CPSR &^= BitT
		}
		c.branch(v &^ 1)
		return
	}
	c.branch(v)
}

// condPassed evaluates an ARM condition field against the CPSR
// flags. Condition 0xF never passes here: on ARMv5 the encodings
// that use it (PLD and friends) are no-ops for this core, which
// the false result reproduces.
func (c *CPU) condPassed(cond uint32) bool {
	n := c.CPSR&FlagN != 0
	z := c.CPSR&FlagZ != 0
	cf := c.CPSR&FlagC != 0
	v := c.CPSR&FlagV != 0
	switch cond {
	case 0x0:
		return z
	case 0x1:
		return !z
	case 0x2:
		return cf
	case 0x3:
		return !cf
	case 0x4:
		return n
	case 0x5:
		return !n
	case 0x6:
		return v
	case 0x7:
		return !v
	case 0x8:
		return cf && !z
	case 0x9:
		return !cf || z
	case 0xA:
		return n == v
	case 0xB:
		return n != v
	case 0xC:
		return !z && n == v
	case 0xD:
		return z || n != v
	case 0xE:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func (c *CPU) setNZ(v uint32) {
	c.CPSR &^= FlagN | FlagZ
	if v&0x80000000 != 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagN
	}
	if v == 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagZ
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setNZC(v uint32, carry bool) {
	c.setNZ(v)
	c.setCarry(carry)
}

func (c *CPU) setCarry(carry bool) {
	c.CPSR &^= FlagC
	if carry {
		c.CPSR |= FlagC
	}
}

// memReg reads a register in a memory-operand position, where
// R15 reads as A+12 (the pipeline value plus one unit). Used for
// swap addressing and operands, multiply operands, and stored PC
// values.
func (c *CPU) memReg(i uint32) uint32 {
	if i == 15 {
		return c.R[15] + 4
	}
	return c.R[i]
}

// tickMultiply reports whether the multiplier runs the full four
// beats for the given multiplier operand, with no early
// termination. Termination happens when the remaining high bytes
// of the multiplier are all zero, or (for signed multiplies) all
// ones.
func tickMultiply(signed bool, multiplier uint32) bool {
	mask := uint32(0xFFFFFF00)
	for {
		multiplier &= mask
		if multiplier == 0 {
			break
		}
		if signed && multiplier == mask {
			break
		}
		mask <<= 8
	}
	return mask == 0
}

// mulCarry computes the C flag a flag-setting multiply leaves
// behind. On the silicon the flag is the carry out of the booth
// multiplier's carry-save adder tree; the routines below model
// that adder, following the published ARM7TDMI multiplier work
// (zaydlang and calc84maniac, as also used by the corpus
// generator). This core applies the same model on both DS CPUs:
// on the ARM9 the architecture leaves the flag unaffected by
// multiplies, but the value is unpredictable on ARMv4, so no
// conforming program can observe the difference. An
// early-terminated multiply takes the low-word carry; a
// full-length one takes the final injected booth carry bit for
// the short forms and the high-word carry for the long forms.
func mulCarry(full bool, isLong bool, signExtend bool, multiplicand, multiplier, accumLo, accumHi uint32) bool {
	if full {
		if isLong {
			return mulCarryHi(signExtend, multiplicand, multiplier, accumHi)
		}
		return (multiplier>>30)&3 == 2
	}
	return mulCarryLo(multiplicand, multiplier, accumLo)
}

// mulCarryLo models the carry out of the multiplier's
// carry-save adder for the low result word, processing the
// multiplier in radix-4 booth steps exactly as the hardware
// accumulates it.
func mulCarryLo(multiplicand, multiplier, accum uint32) bool {
	// Setting the low bit of the multiplicand makes negation
	// invert the upper bits; the bit cannot reach the carry.
	multiplicand |= 1

	booth := uint32(int32(multiplier<<31) >> 31)
	carry := multiplicand * booth
	sum := carry + accum

	shift := 29
	for {
		// Four booth iterations cover 8 multiplier bits.
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			nextBooth := uint32(int32(multiplier<<uint(shift)) >> uint(shift))
			factor := nextBooth - booth
			booth = nextBooth
			addend := multiplicand * factor
			// Carry-save accumulation.
			newAccum := accum ^ carry ^ addend
			sum += addend
			carry = sum - newAccum
			accum = newAccum
			shift -= 2
		}
		if booth == multiplier {
			break
		}
	}
	return carry>>31 != 0
}

// mulCarryHi models the carry out of the high result word of a
// long multiply. Only the last three booth iterations can
// influence it, so both operands are reduced to the relevant
// high bits and the carry is propagated through marker bits,
// following the published model.
func mulCarryHi(signExtend bool, multiplicand, multiplier, accumHi uint32) bool {
	if signExtend {
		multiplicand = uint32(int32(multiplicand) >> 6)
		multiplier = uint32(int32(multiplier) >> 26)
	} else {
		multiplicand >>= 6
		multiplier >>= 26
	}
	multiplicand |= 1

	carry := ^accumHi & 0x20000000
	accum := accumHi - 0x08000000

	booth0 := uint32(int32(multiplier<<27) >> 27)
	booth1 := uint32(int32(multiplier<<29) >> 29)
	booth2 := uint32(int32(multiplier<<31) >> 31)
	factor0 := multiplier - booth0
	factor1 := booth0 - booth1
	factor2 := booth1 - booth2

	addend := multiplicand * factor2
	accum -= addend & 0x10000000
	addend = multiplicand * factor1
	accum -= addend & 0x40000000

	sum := accum + (addend & 0x20000000)
	accum -= carry

	addend = multiplicand * factor0
	sum += addend & 0x40000000

	return (sum^accum)>>31 != 0
}

func (c *CPU) carry() bool { return c.CPSR&FlagC != 0 }

// addFlags computes a+b+carryIn and sets N, Z, C, V.
func (c *CPU) addFlags(a, b uint32, carryIn bool) uint32 {
	var ci uint64
	if carryIn {
		ci = 1
	}
	sum := uint64(a) + uint64(b) + ci
	res := uint32(sum)
	c.setNZ(res)
	c.CPSR &^= FlagC | FlagV
	if sum > 0xFFFFFFFF {
		c.CPSR |= FlagC
	}
	if (a^res)&(b^res)&0x80000000 != 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagV
	}
	return res
}

// subFlags computes a-b-(1-carryIn) and sets N, Z, C, V, with C
// meaning NOT borrow, as ARM defines it.
func (c *CPU) subFlags(a, b uint32, carryIn bool) uint32 {
	var ci uint64 = 1
	if carryIn {
		ci = 0
	}
	diff := uint64(a) - uint64(b) - ci
	res := uint32(diff)
	c.setNZ(res)
	c.CPSR &^= FlagC | FlagV
	if uint64(a) >= uint64(b)+ci {
		c.CPSR |= FlagC
	}
	if (a^b)&(a^res)&0x80000000 != 0 {
		c.CPSR |= FlagV
	}
	return res
}

// saturate32 clamps a signed 64-bit value to the signed 32-bit
// range, reporting whether clamping happened (the caller sets the
// Q flag).
func saturate32(v int64) (uint32, bool) {
	if v > 0x7FFFFFFF {
		return 0x7FFFFFFF, true
	}
	if v < -0x80000000 {
		return 0x80000000, true
	}
	return uint32(v), false
}

// setQ marks the sticky Q flag after a saturating operation
// overflowed.
func (c *CPU) setQ(saturated bool) {
	if saturated {
		c.CPSR |= FlagQ
	}
}

func ror32(v uint32, n uint) uint32 {
	n &= 31
	if n == 0 {
		return v
	}
	return v>>n | v<<(32-n)
}

// shifter runs the ARM barrel shifter for data-processing operand
// 2 in register form. typ is the shift type (0 LSL, 1 LSR, 2 ASR,
// 3 ROR), amount is the shift amount, and byReg reports a
// register-specified shift (amount is Rs&0xFF; the encoded cases
// differ). It returns the shifted value and the shifter carry out.
func (c *CPU) shifter(rmVal uint32, typ uint32, amount uint32, byReg bool) (uint32, bool) {
	oldC := c.carry()
	if byReg {
		if amount == 0 {
			return rmVal, oldC
		}
		switch typ {
		case 0: // LSL
			if amount < 32 {
				return rmVal << amount, (rmVal>>(32-amount))&1 != 0
			}
			if amount == 32 {
				return 0, rmVal&1 != 0
			}
			return 0, false
		case 1: // LSR
			if amount < 32 {
				return rmVal >> amount, (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
			}
			if amount == 32 {
				return 0, rmVal>>31 != 0
			}
			return 0, false
		case 2: // ASR
			if amount >= 32 {
				if rmVal>>31 != 0 {
					return 0xFFFFFFFF, true
				}
				return 0, false
			}
			return uint32(int32(rmVal) >> amount), (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
		case 3: // ROR
			m := amount & 31
			if m == 0 {
				return rmVal, rmVal>>31 != 0
			}
			return ror32(rmVal, uint(m)), (rmVal>>(m-1))&1 != 0
		}
	}
	// Immediate shift amounts: 0 is special per type.
	switch typ {
	case 0: // LSL #0
		if amount == 0 {
			return rmVal, oldC
		}
		return rmVal << amount, (rmVal>>(32-amount))&1 != 0
	case 1: // LSR #0 means LSR #32
		if amount == 0 {
			return 0, rmVal>>31 != 0
		}
		return rmVal >> amount, (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
	case 2: // ASR #0 means ASR #32
		if amount == 0 {
			if rmVal>>31 != 0 {
				return 0xFFFFFFFF, true
			}
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint32(int32(rmVal) >> amount), (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
	case 3: // ROR #0 means RRX
		if amount == 0 {
			res := rmVal >> 1
			if oldC {
				res |= 0x80000000
			}
			return res, rmVal&1 != 0
		}
		return ror32(rmVal, uint(amount)), (rmVal>>(amount-1))&1 != 0
	}
	return rmVal, oldC
}

// spsrIndex maps a mode to its SPSR slot, or -1 when the mode has
// no SPSR (USR and SYS).
func spsrIndex(mode uint32) int {
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		return SPSRFIQ
	case ModeSVC:
		return SPSRSVC
	case ModeABT:
		return SPSRABT
	case ModeIRQ:
		return SPSRIRQ
	case ModeUND:
		return SPSRUND
	}
	return -1
}

// curSPSR returns the SPSR of the current mode. In modes without
// an SPSR it returns the CPSR, the value MRS SPSR observes on the
// hardware paths the corpus exercises.
func (c *CPU) curSPSR() uint32 {
	if idx := spsrIndex(c.Mode()); idx >= 0 {
		return c.SPSR[idx]
	}
	return c.CPSR
}

// storeBank parks the R8-R14 values of the given (outgoing) mode
// into its bank fields, restoring the neutral user R8-R12 view
// after a FIQ exit.
func (c *CPU) storeBank(mode uint32) {
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(c.RFIQ[0:5], c.R[8:13])
		c.RFIQ[5] = c.R[13]
		c.RFIQ[6] = c.R[14]
		copy(c.R[8:13], c.usr8_12[0:5])
	case ModeSVC:
		c.RSVC[0], c.RSVC[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeABT:
		c.RABT[0], c.RABT[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeIRQ:
		c.RIRQ[0], c.RIRQ[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	case ModeUND:
		c.RUND[0], c.RUND[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	default: // USR, SYS
		c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1] = c.R[13], c.R[14]
	}
}

// loadBank brings the R8-R14 values of the given (incoming) mode
// into the live register view.
func (c *CPU) loadBank(mode uint32) {
	switch mode {
	case ModeFIQ:
		copy(c.usr8_12[0:5], c.R[8:13])
		copy(c.R[8:13], c.RFIQ[0:5])
		c.R[13] = c.RFIQ[5]
		c.R[14] = c.RFIQ[6]
	case ModeSVC:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RSVC[0], c.RSVC[1]
	case ModeABT:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RABT[0], c.RABT[1]
	case ModeIRQ:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RIRQ[0], c.RIRQ[1]
	case ModeUND:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RUND[0], c.RUND[1]
	default:
		c.R[13], c.R[14] = c.RUSR[0], c.RUSR[1]
	}
}

// setCPSR writes the CPSR, swapping register banks when the mode
// bits change.
func (c *CPU) setCPSR(v uint32) {
	oldMode := c.Mode()
	newMode := v & 0x1F
	if oldMode != newMode {
		c.storeBank(oldMode)
		c.loadBank(newMode)
	}
	c.CPSR = v
}

// msr writes val into the fields of the CPSR or the current SPSR
// selected by fieldMask (bit0 c, bit1 x, bit2 s, bit3 f, from the
// instruction's mask field). In user mode only the flag field of
// the CPSR is writable; the s, x and c fields require privilege.
// A CPSR control-field write preserves bit 4 of the mode field
// (only bits 3-0 of the mode are writable) in the reference
// behavior, while an SPSR control-field write takes bit 4 from
// the operand.
func (c *CPU) msr(toSPSR bool, fieldMask uint32, val uint32) {
	priv := c.Mode() != ModeUSR
	var m uint32
	if fieldMask&8 != 0 {
		m |= 0xFF000000
	}
	if fieldMask&4 != 0 && (toSPSR || priv) {
		m |= 0x00FF0000
	}
	if fieldMask&2 != 0 && (toSPSR || priv) {
		m |= 0x0000FF00
	}
	if fieldMask&1 != 0 && toSPSR {
		m |= 0x000000FF
	}
	if fieldMask&1 != 0 && !toSPSR && priv {
		m |= 0x000000EF
	}
	if toSPSR {
		idx := spsrIndex(c.Mode())
		if idx < 0 {
			c.spsrDummy = val
			return
		}
		cur := c.SPSR[idx]
		c.SPSR[idx] = cur&^m | val&m
		return
	}
	nv := c.CPSR&^m | val&m
	c.setCPSR(nv)
}

// exception enters an exception mode: the SPSR of the new mode
// saves the old CPSR, the mode switches with I set (and F set for
// FIQ and reset), LR of the new mode receives lr, and the
// pipeline refills at the vector (relocated by the CP15 high
// vectors bit on the ARM9). Entry costs 3 cycles.
func (c *CPU) exception(vector uint32, mode uint32, lr uint32) int {
	if idx := spsrIndex(mode); idx >= 0 {
		c.SPSR[idx] = c.CPSR
	}
	nc := c.CPSR&^0x1F | mode
	nc &^= BitT
	nc |= BitI
	if mode == ModeFIQ {
		nc |= BitF
	}
	c.setCPSR(nc)
	c.R[14] = lr
	c.branch(c.VectorBase() + vector)
	return 3
}

// undefined raises the undefined-instruction exception for the
// instruction at addr (the executing address).
func (c *CPU) undefined(addr uint32) int {
	if c.Thumb() {
		return c.exception(VectorUndef, ModeUND, addr+2)
	}
	return c.exception(VectorUndef, ModeUND, addr+4)
}

// PrefetchAbort raises the prefetch abort exception (BKPT with
// no debugger attached, or a fetch fault signalled by the
// system): the fault address is recorded in FAR and the status in
// FSR on the ARM9, and LR receives the faulting address plus 4.
func (c *CPU) PrefetchAbort(addr uint32) int {
	if c.Config.V5 {
		c.FAR = addr
		c.FSR = 0x0D // terminal fault, prefetch (domain field unused here)
		c.CP15[cp15FSR] = c.FSR
		c.CP15[cp15FAR] = c.FAR
	}
	lr := addr + 4
	return c.exception(VectorPAbort, ModeABT, lr)
}

// DataAbort raises the data abort exception for a data access to
// faultAddr: FAR and FSR are set on the ARM9 and LR in abort mode
// receives the address of the faulting instruction plus 8, which
// this core expresses from the current pipeline position.
func (c *CPU) DataAbort(faultAddr uint32) int {
	if c.Config.V5 {
		c.FAR = faultAddr
		c.FSR = 0x05 // alignment-style terminal fault status slot
		c.CP15[cp15FSR] = c.FSR
		c.CP15[cp15FAR] = c.FAR
	}
	lr := c.R[15] // ARM: executing address + 8
	if c.Thumb() {
		lr += 4 // Thumb: executing address + 8 via R15+4
	}
	return c.exception(VectorDAbort, ModeABT, lr)
}

// load performs a data load of the given size in bytes. The bus
// returns the raw unit at addr; the CPU applies the ARM alignment
// rules: word loads rotate right by the byte offset, a halfword
// load from an odd address rotates the zero-extended halfword
// right by 8, and a signed halfword load from an odd address
// instead returns the sign-extended byte at addr (the high byte
// of the halfword read), matching the reference behavior.
func (c *CPU) load(addr uint32, size int, signed bool) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		v := c.Bus.Read(addr, 1)
		if signed {
			return uint32(int32(int8(v)))
		}
		return v
	case 2:
		v := c.Bus.Read(addr, 2)
		if signed && addr&1 != 0 {
			return uint32(int32(int8(v >> 8)))
		}
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			v = ror32(v, 8)
		}
		if signed {
			return uint32(int32(int16(v)))
		}
		return v
	default:
		return ror32(c.Bus.Read(addr, 4), uint((addr&3)*8))
	}
}

// store performs a data store of the given size in bytes,
// masking the value to the transfer width.
func (c *CPU) store(addr uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		val &= 0xFF
	case 2:
		val &= 0xFFFF
	}
	c.Bus.Write(addr, size, val)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/chips/armcore/thumb.go ====================

package armcore

// execThumb executes one Thumb-state instruction (the halfword in
// the execute stage, located at R15-4) and returns its cycle
// count.
func (c *CPU) execThumb(op uint16) int {
	addr := c.R[15] - 4

	// BKPT (ARMv5): with no debugger attached the core takes a
	// prefetch abort.
	if c.Config.V5 && op&0xFF00 == 0xBE00 {
		return c.PrefetchAbort(addr)
	}

	switch {
	// Format 1 and 2: shifts by immediate, add/subtract.
	case op>>13 == 0 && (op>>11)&3 != 3:
		typ := uint32((op >> 11) & 3)
		amt := uint32((op >> 6) & 0x1F)
		rs := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		res, carry := c.shifter(rs, typ, amt, false)
		c.R[op&7] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 1
	case op>>13 == 0:
		// Format 2: ADD/SUB register or 3-bit immediate. The
		// first operand is the register in bits 5-3; the second
		// operand (a register or the immediate) is in bits 8-6.
		sub := op&(1<<9) != 0
		a := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		var b uint32
		if op&(1<<10) != 0 {
			b = uint32((op >> 6) & 7)
		} else {
			b = c.R[(op>>6)&7]
		}
		var res uint32
		if sub {
			res = c.subFlags(a, b, true)
		} else {
			res = c.addFlags(a, b, false)
		}
		c.R[op&7] = res
		return 1

	// Format 3: move/compare/add/subtract immediate.
	case op>>13 == 1:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		imm := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		switch (op >> 11) & 3 {
		case 0: // MOV
			c.R[rd] = imm
			c.setNZ(imm)
		case 1: // CMP
			c.subFlags(c.R[rd], imm, true)
		case 2: // ADD
			c.R[rd] = c.addFlags(c.R[rd], imm, false)
		case 3: // SUB
			c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(c.R[rd], imm, true)
		}
		return 1

	// Format 4: ALU operations.
	case op>>12 == 4 && (op>>11)&1 == 0 && (op>>10)&1 == 0:
		return c.execThumbALU(op)

	// Format 5: high-register operations and BX/BLX register.
	case op>>12 == 4 && (op>>11)&1 == 0:
		operation := (op >> 8) & 3
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		rs := uint32((op >> 3) & 7)
		if op&(1<<7) != 0 {
			rd += 8
		}
		if op&(1<<6) != 0 {
			rs += 8
		}
		switch operation {
		case 0: // ADD
			res := c.R[rd] + c.R[rs]
			if rd == 15 {
				c.branchPC(res)
				return 3
			}
			c.R[rd] = res
		case 1: // CMP
			c.subFlags(c.R[rd], c.R[rs], true)
		case 2: // MOV
			if rd == 15 {
				c.branchPC(c.R[rs])
				return 3
			}
			c.R[rd] = c.R[rs]
		case 3: // BX, and BLX register on the ARM9
			v := c.R[rs]
			if op&(1<<7) != 0 && c.Config.V5 {
				// BLX register: LR receives the return
				// address with the Thumb bit set. On the
				// ARM7TDMI configuration the same encoding
				// executes as a plain BX in the reference
				// behavior, with no LR write.
				c.R[14] = (addr + 2) | 1
			}
			if v&1 != 0 {
				c.CPSR |= BitT
			} else {
				c.CPSR &^= BitT
			}
			c.branch(v &^ 1)
			return 3
		}
		return 1

	// Format 6: PC-relative load.
	case op>>11 == 0b01001:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		base := c.R[15] &^ 2
		v := c.load(base+uint32(op&0xFF)*4, 4, false)
		c.R[rd] = v
		return 3

	// Formats 7 and 8: load/store with register offset.
	case op>>12 == 5:
		rn := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		ea := rn + c.R[(op>>6)&7]
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		if op&(1<<9) == 0 {
			// Format 7, keyed by bits 11-10 (L, B).
			switch (op >> 10) & 3 {
			case 0:
				c.store(ea, 4, c.R[rd])
			case 1:
				c.store(ea, 1, c.R[rd])
			case 2:
				c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 4, false)
				return 3
			case 3:
				c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 1, false)
				return 3
			}
			return 2
		}
		// Format 8, keyed by bits 11-9.
		switch (op >> 9) & 7 {
		case 1:
			c.store(ea, 2, c.R[rd])
			return 2
		case 3:
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 1, true)
		case 5:
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 2, false)
		case 7:
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 2, true)
		}
		return 3

	// Format 9: load/store with immediate offset.
	case op>>13 == 3:
		imm := uint32((op >> 6) & 0x1F)
		rn := c.R[(op>>3)&7]
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		load := op&(1<<11) != 0
		if op&(1<<12) != 0 { // byte
			ea := rn + imm
			if load {
				c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 1, false)
				return 3
			}
			c.store(ea, 1, c.R[rd])
			return 2
		}
		ea := rn + imm*4
		if load {
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 4, false)
			return 3
		}
		c.store(ea, 4, c.R[rd])
		return 2

	// Format 10: halfword load/store with immediate offset.
	case op>>12 == 8:
		imm := uint32((op>>6)&0x1F) * 2
		ea := c.R[(op>>3)&7] + imm
		rd := uint32(op & 7)
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 2, false)
			return 3
		}
		c.store(ea, 2, c.R[rd])
		return 2

	// Format 11: SP-relative load/store.
	case op>>12 == 9:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		ea := c.R[13] + uint32(op&0xFF)*4
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			c.R[rd] = c.load(ea, 4, false)
			return 3
		}
		c.store(ea, 4, c.R[rd])
		return 2

	// Format 12: load address.
	case op>>12 == 10:
		rd := (op >> 8) & 7
		var base uint32
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			base = c.R[13]
		} else {
			base = c.R[15] &^ 2
		}
		c.R[rd] = base + uint32(op&0xFF)*4
		return 1

	// Format 13: add offset to stack pointer.
	case op&0xFF00 == 0xB000:
		imm := uint32(op&0x7F) * 4
		if op&(1<<7) != 0 {
			c.R[13] -= imm
		} else {
			c.R[13] += imm
		}
		return 1

	// Format 14: push and pop.
	case op&0xFE00 == 0xB400:
		list := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		if op&(1<<8) != 0 {
			list |= 1 << 14
		}
		return c.thumbPush(list)
	case op&0xFE00 == 0xBC00:
		list := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		if op&(1<<8) != 0 {
			list |= 1 << 15
		}
		return c.thumbPop(list)

	// Format 16: multiple load/store.
	case op>>12 == 12:
		rn := uint32((op >> 8) & 7)
		list := uint32(op & 0xFF)
		if op&(1<<11) != 0 {
			return c.thumbBlock(rn, list, true)
		}
		return c.thumbBlock(rn, list, false)

	// Format 15: conditional branch and SWI.
	case op>>12 == 13:
		cond := uint32((op >> 8) & 0xF)
		if cond == 0xF {
			// SWI in Thumb state: LR_svc is A+2.
			return c.exception(VectorSWI, ModeSVC, addr+2)
		}
		// Condition 14 is undefined in the Thumb encoding, but
		// the corpus reference evaluates it through the shared
		// condition table (as always); this core matches the
		// reference.
		if c.condPassed(cond) {
			off := int32(int8(op&0xFF)) * 2
			c.branch(uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off))
			return 3
		}
		return 1

	// Format 17: unconditional branch.
	case op>>11 == 0b11100:
		off := (int32(op&0x7FF) << 21) >> 21 * 2
		c.branch(uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off))
		return 3

	// Format 18: long branch prefix.
	case op>>11 == 0b11110:
		off := (int32(op&0x7FF) << 21) >> 21
		c.R[14] = uint32(int32(c.R[15]) + off<<12)
		return 1

	// Format 19: long branch suffix. The 11111 suffix is BL
	// (stay in Thumb); the 11101 suffix is BLX immediate: the
	// target is ARM state, formed from LR with its bit 0 (part
	// of the pair encoding) cleared, exactly as the reference
	// implementation composes it.
	case op>>11 == 0b11111 || op>>11 == 0b11101:
		target := c.R[14] + uint32(op&0x7FF)*2
		if op>>11 == 0b11101 {
			target = (c.R[14] &^ 1) + uint32(op&0x7FF)*2
			c.CPSR &^= BitT
		}
		c.R[14] = (addr + 2) | 1
		c.branch(target)
		return 3
	}

	return c.undefined(addr)
}

// execThumbALU runs format 4, the register-register ALU group.
func (c *CPU) execThumbALU(op uint16) int {
	rd := uint32(op & 7)
	rs := uint32((op >> 3) & 7)
	a := c.R[rd]
	b := c.R[rs]
	switch (op >> 6) & 0xF {
	case 0: // AND
		c.R[rd] = a & b
		c.setNZ(a & b)
	case 1: // EOR
		c.R[rd] = a ^ b
		c.setNZ(a ^ b)
	case 2: // LSL
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 0, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 3: // LSR
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 1, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 4: // ASR
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 2, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 5: // ADC
		c.R[rd] = c.addFlags(a, b, c.carry())
	case 6: // SBC
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(a, b, c.carry())
	case 7: // ROR
		res, carry := c.shifter(a, 3, b&0xFF, true)
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZC(res, carry)
		return 2
	case 8: // TST
		c.setNZ(a & b)
	case 9: // NEG
		c.R[rd] = c.subFlags(0, b, true)
	case 10: // CMP
		c.subFlags(a, b, true)
	case 11: // CMN
		c.addFlags(a, b, false)
	case 12: // ORR
		c.R[rd] = a | b
		c.setNZ(a | b)
	case 13: // MUL: the multiplier for the flag and timing
		// model is the destination register's old value, the
		// multiplicand is the source register.
		res := a * b
		c.R[rd] = res
		c.setNZ(res)
		c.setCarry(mulCarry(tickMultiply(true, a), false, false, b, a, 0, 0))
		return 1 + mulCycles(a)
	case 14: // BIC
		c.R[rd] = a &^ b
		c.setNZ(a &^ b)
	case 15: // MVN
		c.R[rd] = ^b
		c.setNZ(^b)
	}
	return 1
}

// branchRawThumb refills the pipeline at addr like a Thumb
// branch, but keeps the raw target value in R15 (bit 0 not
// discarded). The empty-list LDMIA form loads the PC this way in
// the reference behavior.
func (c *CPU) branchRawThumb(addr uint32) {
	fa := addr &^ 1
	c.Executing = c.Bus.Fetch(fa, 2)
	c.Pipe[0] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+2, 2)
	c.Pipe[1] = c.Bus.Fetch(fa+4, 2)
	c.R[15] = addr + 4
	c.ExecutingValid = true
	c.flushed = true
}

// thumbPush stores a register list (STMDB SP), always with
// writeback. An empty list stores the PC and moves the stack
// pointer by the full 0x40, as on ARM.
func (c *CPU) thumbPush(list uint32) int {
	if list == 0 {
		c.R[13] -= 0x40
		c.Bus.Write(c.R[13], 4, c.R[15]+2)
		return 2
	}
	count := popcount16(list)
	start := c.R[13] - 4*uint32(count)
	cur := start
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		c.Bus.Write(cur, 4, c.R[i])
		cur += 4
	}
	c.R[13] = start
	return count + 1
}

// thumbPop loads a register list (LDMIA SP), always with
// writeback; a loaded PC branches. An empty list loads the PC
// raw (bit 0 kept in R15, state unchanged) and moves the stack
// pointer by 0x40.
func (c *CPU) thumbPop(list uint32) int {
	if list == 0 {
		v := c.Bus.Read(c.R[13], 4)
		c.R[13] += 0x40
		c.branchRawThumb(v)
		return 5
	}
	count := popcount16(list)
	cur := c.R[13]
	var pcVal uint32
	pcSet := false
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		v := c.Bus.Read(cur, 4)
		cur += 4
		if i == 15 {
			pcVal, pcSet = v, true
		} else {
			c.R[i] = v
		}
	}
	c.R[13] += 4 * uint32(count)
	n := count + 2
	if pcSet {
		c.branchPC(pcVal)
		n += 2
	}
	return n
}

// thumbBlock runs the Thumb LDMIA/STMIA forms (format 16), which
// always write back. A load whose base is in the list keeps the
// loaded value and suppresses writeback; a store whose base is
// in the list stores the old base when first and the new base
// otherwise. An empty list transfers R15 with a 0x40 writeback,
// as on ARM.
func (c *CPU) thumbBlock(rn uint32, list uint32, load bool) int {
	base := c.R[rn]
	empty := list == 0
	if empty {
		list = 1 << 15
	}
	count := popcount16(list)
	wb := base + 4*uint32(count)
	if empty {
		wb = base + 0x40
	}
	if load {
		var pcVal uint32
		pcSet := false
		cur := base
		for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
			if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			v := c.Bus.Read(cur, 4)
			cur += 4
			if i == 15 {
				pcVal, pcSet = v, true
			} else {
				c.R[i] = v
			}
		}
		if list&(1<<rn) == 0 {
			c.R[rn] = wb
		}
		n := count + 2
		if pcSet {
			if empty {
				// The empty-list LDMIA loads the PC raw.
				c.branchRawThumb(pcVal)
			} else {
				c.branchPC(pcVal)
			}
			n += 2
		}
		return n
	}
	idx := 0
	rnIdx := -1
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) != 0 {
			if uint32(i) == rn {
				rnIdx = idx
			}
			idx++
		}
	}
	cur := base
	idx = 0
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		v := c.R[i]
		if uint32(i) == rn && rnIdx > 0 {
			v = wb
		}
		if i == 15 {
			v = c.R[15] + 2 // a stored PC reads as A+6 in Thumb state
		}
		c.Bus.Write(cur, 4, v)
		cur += 4
		idx++
	}
	c.R[rn] = wb
	return count + 1
}

func popcount16(list uint32) int {
	n := 0
	for i := uint(0); i < 16; i++ {
		if list&(1<<i) != 0 {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

go 1.25.7


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/gx/gx.go ====================

// Package gx implements the DS 3D geometry engine and
// rendering engine per GBATEK: the GXFIFO command port and the
// direct command ports, the matrix unit with its three
// stacks, per-vertex lighting with four lights, polygon
// assembly into the double-buffered polygon and vertex RAM,
// and the rendering engine that rasterizes the swapped list
// into the 256x192 layer the video package composites as
// engine A BG0.
//
// Execution model (stated): commands execute eagerly, as soon
// as their parameter set is complete, matching this core
// family's synchronous device style. The FIFO is modeled as
// the entry queue between the port parser and the executor;
// its GXSTAT level counts entries not yet consumed. A
// SWAP_BUFFERS command pauses the executor until the next
// VBlank (the hardware halts the geometry engine the same
// way), when the buffers exchange and the rendering engine
// draws the new display list. POS_TEST, VEC_TEST and BOX_TEST
// therefore complete instantly and the test-busy bit reads 0.
//
// Fixed point: matrix elements and clip coordinates are
// signed 32-bit with 12 fractional bits; multiplies
// accumulate in 64-bit and shift right by 12 (wrapping to 32
// bits), the documented matrix arithmetic shape.
package gx

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
)

// Screen geometry of the rendered layer.
const (
	Width  = 256
	Height = 192
)

// Polygon and vertex RAM capacities (GBATEK).
const (
	MaxPolys = 2048
	MaxVerts = 6144
)

// IO offsets (hook offset space, ARM9 page) claimed here.
const (
	offEdgeColor  = 0x330
	offAlphaRef   = 0x340
	offClearColor = 0x350
	offClearDepth = 0x354
	offFogColor   = 0x358
	offFogOffset  = 0x35C
	offFogTable   = 0x360
	offToonTable  = 0x380
	offGXFIFO     = 0x400
	offPorts      = 0x440
	offPortsEnd   = 0x600
	offGXSTAT     = 0x600
	offRAMCount   = 0x604
	offDotDepth   = 0x610
	offPOSResult  = 0x620
	offVECResult  = 0x630
	offClipResult = 0x640
	offVecMtxRes  = 0x680
	offEnd        = 0x6B0
	offDISP3DCNT  = 0x060
)

// paramCount gives the number of 32-bit parameters per
// documented command ID, or -1 for an invalid command (which
// the hardware ignores, fetching no parameters). GBATEK's
// invalid-command list omits 34h (SHININESS) even though its
// own command table documents it with 32 parameters; 34h is
// implemented as valid here.
func paramCount(cmd uint8) int {
	switch cmd {
	case 0x11, 0x15, 0x41: // MTX_PUSH, MTX_IDENTITY, END_VTXS
		return 0
	case 0x16, 0x18: // MTX_LOAD_4x4, MTX_MULT_4x4
		return 16
	case 0x17, 0x19: // MTX_LOAD_4x3, MTX_MULT_4x3
		return 12
	case 0x1A: // MTX_MULT_3x3
		return 9
	case 0x1B, 0x1C, 0x70: // MTX_SCALE, MTX_TRANS, BOX_TEST
		return 3
	case 0x23, 0x71: // VTX_16, POS_TEST
		return 2
	case 0x34: // SHININESS
		return 32
	case 0x10, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14, // matrix mode/pop/store/restore
		0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x24, 0x25, 0x26, 0x27, 0x28, // vertex group
		0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B, // polygon attr, teximage, pltt base
		0x30, 0x31, 0x32, 0x33, // lighting group
		0x40, 0x50, 0x60, 0x72: // begin, swap, viewport, vec test
		return 1
	}
	return -1
}

// fifoEntry is one 40-bit FIFO entry as the hardware stores
// it: a command byte plus one parameter word. A command with
// N parameters occupies N entries (a parameterless command
// occupies one entry with an unused parameter word).
type fifoEntry struct {
	cmd   uint8
	param uint32
}

// GX is the geometry and rendering engine.
type GX struct {
	bus *bus.Bus

	// FIFOWords counts 32-bit words written to the GXFIFO
	// port (0x04000400 and its mirrors), the DS-3 successor
	// of the DS-2 counting sink.
	FIFOWords uint32

	// Port parser: packed command IDs waiting to be
	// decompressed into entries, and the command currently
	// being decompressed (its parameters arrive as GXFIFO
	// writes).
	idQueue   []uint8
	decCmd    uint8
	decRemain int

	// Entry queue between parser and executor, capped at the
	// documented FIFO+PIPE capacity. The hardware stalls the
	// writer when full; this model drops excess entries
	// instead (only reachable while the executor is paused
	// at a swap with a full frame of queued commands).
	queue []fifoEntry

	// Executor assembly state.
	execCmd    uint8
	execHave   int
	execParams [32]uint32
	executing  bool

	// GXSTAT fields.
	stackErr  bool
	irqMode   uint32 // GXSTAT bits 30-31
	boxResult bool

	// RE plain registers and tables (write-only on hardware;
	// reads here return 0 except ALPHA_TEST_REF).
	alphaRef   uint32
	clearColor uint32
	clearDepth uint32 // 15-bit value in bits 0-14
	clrImgOff  uint32 // CLRIMAGE_OFFSET
	fogColor   uint32
	fogOffset  uint32 // 15-bit
	fogTable   [32]uint8
	toonTable  [32]uint16
	edgeColor  [8]uint16
	dotDepth   uint32 // DISP_1DOT_DEPTH, 15-bit W value

	// Matrix unit.
	mtxMode int
	curProj mat
	curPos  mat
	curVec  mat
	curTex  mat
	projStk [1]mat
	posStk  [32]mat
	vecStk  [32]mat
	texStk  [1]mat
	spProj  int
	spPos   int // 6-bit
	spTex   int

	// Vertex pipeline state.
	curR, curG, curB uint8 // current vertex color, 6-bit channels
	curS, curT       int32 // current texcoord, raw 4-frac domain
	lastX, lastY     int32
	lastZ            int32

	// Lighting state.
	diffuse   uint32 // raw DIF_AMB parameter
	ambient   uint32
	specular  uint32 // raw SPE_EMI parameter
	emission  uint32
	shineOn   bool
	shineTbl  [128]uint8
	lightVec  [4][3]int32 // transformed at LIGHT_VECTOR, 9-frac
	lightHalf [4][3]int32
	lightCol  [4]uint32 // RGB15 in bits 0-14

	// Latched command registers.
	pendAttr   uint32 // last POLYGON_ATTR written
	normalAttr uint32 // attr in effect for lighting (latched at NORMAL)
	beginAttr  uint32 // attr in effect for the current primitive
	texParam   uint32 // last TEXIMAGE_PARAM written
	plttBase   uint32 // last PLTT_BASE written
	viewport   uint32 // last VIEWPORT written

	// Test results.
	posResult [4]int32
	vecResult [3]int32

	// Polygon assembly.
	primType  int
	primCount int // vertices fed into the current primitive group
	primOpen  bool
	build     listBuf
	display   listBuf

	// Swap state. curSwapBits govern the list being built;
	// renderBits were latched for the display list at its
	// SWAP_BUFFERS.
	swapPending bool
	curManual   bool
	curZBuf     bool
	rndManual   bool
	rndZBuf     bool

	// Rendering engine output: rgb6 color with the 5-bit
	// alpha in bits 18-22, per pixel; 0 means fully
	// transparent (nothing rendered there).
	fb []uint32

	// Rendering scratch buffers (color, alpha, 24-bit
	// depth, fog flag, polygon ID), fully rewritten by
	// every render, so they are not serialized.
	fbC     []uint32
	fbA     []uint8
	fbDepth []uint32
	fbAttr  []uint8
	fbID    []uint8

	// Texture fetch spaces, rebuilt when VRAMCNT changes.
	texImg   [0x80000]byte
	texPal   [0x18000]byte
	texCache [9]byte
	texValid bool
}

// New builds the engine over the shared bus.
func New(b *bus.Bus) *GX {
	g := &GX{bus: b, fb: make([]uint32, Width*Height),
		fbC: make([]uint32, Width*Height), fbA: make([]uint8, Width*Height),
		fbDepth: make([]uint32, Width*Height), fbAttr: make([]uint8, Width*Height),
		fbID: make([]uint8, Width*Height)}
	g.curProj = identityMat()
	g.curPos = identityMat()
	g.curVec = identityMat()
	g.curTex = identityMat()
	return g
}

// disp3dcnt reads DISP3DCNT (0x04000060) from the ARM9 IO
// page storage.
func (g *GX) disp3dcnt() uint32 {
	return uint32(g.bus.IO9[offDISP3DCNT]) | uint32(g.bus.IO9[offDISP3DCNT+1])<<8
}

// setOverflow sets or clears the polygon/vertex RAM overflow
// flag (DISP3DCNT bit 13) in IO storage.
func (g *GX) setOverflow() {
	g.bus.IO9[offDISP3DCNT+1] |= 0x20
}

// FIFOLevel returns the number of FIFO entries not yet
// consumed by the executor: queued entries plus the
// parameters buffered for the command being assembled.
func (g *GX) FIFOLevel() int {
	return len(g.queue) + g.execHave
}

// FIFOBusy reports the GXSTAT geometry-busy condition:
// entries pending, a command mid-assembly, or the executor
// paused at a swap.
func (g *GX) FIFOBusy() bool {
	return len(g.queue) > 0 || g.executing || g.swapPending || len(g.idQueue) > 0 || g.decRemain > 0
}

// FIFOIRQCondition reports whether the GXSTAT FIFO IRQ mode
// currently asserts the ARM9 geometry FIFO interrupt (mode 1:
// less than half full, mode 2: empty, mode 3: never, per
// GBATEK).
func (g *GX) FIFOIRQCondition() bool {
	switch g.irqMode {
	case 1:
		return g.FIFOLevel() < 128
	case 2:
		return g.FIFOLevel() == 0 && !g.FIFOBusy()
	}
	return false
}

// pushEntry appends one entry, dropping it when the queue is
// at the documented capacity (see the queue field comment).
func (g *GX) pushEntry(e fifoEntry) {
	if len(g.queue) >= 260 {
		return
	}
	g.queue = append(g.queue, e)
}

// writeFIFO handles one 32-bit write to the GXFIFO port.
func (g *GX) writeFIFO(val uint32) {
	g.FIFOWords++
	if g.decRemain > 0 {
		// The word is a parameter for the command being
		// decompressed.
		g.pushEntry(fifoEntry{g.decCmd, val})
		g.decRemain--
		if g.decRemain == 0 {
			g.drainIDs()
		}
		g.pump()
		return
	}
	// The word packs up to four command IDs (low byte first);
	// a zero byte is no command.
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if id := uint8(val >> (8 * i)); id != 0 {
			g.idQueue = append(g.idQueue, id)
		}
	}
	g.drainIDs()
	g.pump()
}

// drainIDs decompresses queued command IDs into entries
// until one needs parameters from future writes.
func (g *GX) drainIDs() {
	for len(g.idQueue) > 0 && g.decRemain == 0 {
		id := g.idQueue[0]
		g.idQueue = g.idQueue[1:]
		n := paramCount(id)
		if n < 0 {
			continue // invalid command: ignored, no parameters
		}
		if n == 0 {
			g.pushEntry(fifoEntry{id, 0})
			continue
		}
		g.decCmd = id
		g.decRemain = n
	}
}

// writePort handles one write to a direct command port
// (0x04000440 onward): the value becomes an entry tagged with
// the port's command. For parameterless commands the value is
// a dummy.
func (g *GX) writePort(off uint32, val uint32) {
	cmd := uint8((off - offGXFIFO) >> 2)
	if paramCount(cmd) < 0 {
		return
	}
	g.pushEntry(fifoEntry{cmd, val})
	g.pump()
}

// pump runs the executor until the queue empties, a command
// is left mid-assembly, or a swap pauses execution.
func (g *GX) pump() {
	for len(g.queue) > 0 {
		if g.swapPending {
			return
		}
		e := g.queue[0]
		g.queue = g.queue[1:]
		if !g.executing {
			n := paramCount(e.cmd)
			if n < 0 {
				continue
			}
			g.execCmd = e.cmd
			g.execHave = 0
			if n == 0 {
				g.execute(e.cmd, g.execParams[:0])
				continue
			}
			g.executing = true
		}
		g.execParams[g.execHave] = e.param
		g.execHave++
		if g.execHave == paramCount(g.execCmd) {
			g.executing = false
			g.execute(g.execCmd, g.execParams[:g.execHave])
			g.execHave = 0
		}
	}
}

// execute dispatches one fully assembled command.
func (g *GX) execute(cmd uint8, p []uint32) {
	switch {
	case cmd >= 0x10 && cmd <= 0x1C:
		g.execMatrix(cmd, p)
	case cmd == 0x20:
		g.cmdColor(p[0])
	case cmd == 0x21:
		g.cmdNormal(p[0])
	case cmd == 0x22:
		g.cmdTexcoord(p[0])
	case cmd >= 0x23 && cmd <= 0x28:
		g.cmdVertex(cmd, p)
	case cmd == 0x29:
		g.pendAttr = p[0]
	case cmd == 0x2A:
		g.texParam = p[0]
	case cmd == 0x2B:
		g.plttBase = p[0]
	case cmd == 0x30:
		g.diffuse = p[0] & 0x7FFF
		g.ambient = (p[0] >> 16) & 0x7FFF
		if p[0]&0x8000 != 0 {
			// The diffuse color doubles as the vertex color.
			g.setVertexColor(g.diffuse)
		}
	case cmd == 0x31:
		g.specular = p[0] & 0x7FFF
		g.emission = (p[0] >> 16) & 0x7FFF
		g.shineOn = p[0]&0x8000 != 0
	case cmd == 0x32:
		g.cmdLightVector(p[0])
	case cmd == 0x33:
		g.lightCol[(p[0]>>30)&3] = p[0] & 0x7FFF
	case cmd == 0x34:
		for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
			for k := 0; k < 4; k++ {
				g.shineTbl[i*4+k] = uint8(p[i] >> (8 * k))
			}
		}
	case cmd == 0x40:
		g.beginVtxs(p[0])
	case cmd == 0x41:
		g.primOpen = false
	case cmd == 0x50:
		g.rndManual = g.curManual
		g.rndZBuf = g.curZBuf
		g.curManual = p[0]&1 != 0
		g.curZBuf = p[0]&2 != 0
		g.swapPending = true
	case cmd == 0x60:
		g.viewport = p[0]
	case cmd == 0x70:
		g.cmdBoxTest(p)
	case cmd == 0x71:
		g.cmdPosTest(p)
	case cmd == 0x72:
		g.cmdVecTest(p[0])
	}
}

// OnVBlank performs the deferred buffer swap (when a
// SWAP_BUFFERS is pending) and renders the display list into
// the frame buffer. The system calls it at line 192. Without
// a pending swap the same display list is rendered again, so
// rear-plane register changes still appear.
func (g *GX) OnVBlank() {
	if g.swapPending {
		g.display, g.build = g.build, listBuf{}
		g.swapPending = false
	}
	g.render()
	g.pump()
}

// ReadIO implements the read side of the claimed ARM9
// offsets: 0x320 (RDLINES_COUNT, reads 0 in this model), the
// RE register block 0x330-0x3BF, the command port range
// (write-only, reads 0), and the status/result block
// 0x600-0x6AF.
func (g *GX) ReadIO(off uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	switch {
	case off == 0x320:
		return 0, true
	case off >= offEdgeColor && off < offToonTable+0x40:
		if off >= offAlphaRef && off < offAlphaRef+4 {
			return getLanes(g.alphaRef, off, size), true
		}
		return 0, true
	case off >= offGXFIFO && off < offPortsEnd:
		return 0, true
	case off == offGXSTAT || off == offGXSTAT+2:
		return getLanes(g.gxstat(), off, size), true
	case off == offRAMCount || off == offRAMCount+2:
		return getLanes(g.ramCount(), off, size), true
	case off == offDotDepth || off == offDotDepth+2:
		return 0, true
	case off >= offPOSResult && off < offPOSResult+16:
		i := (off - offPOSResult) / 4
		return getLanes(uint32(g.posResult[i]), off, size), true
	case off >= offVECResult && off < offVECResult+12:
		i := (off - offVECResult) / 4
		return getLanes(uint32(g.vecResult[i]), off, size), true
	case off >= offClipResult && off < offClipResult+64:
		i := (off - offClipResult) / 4
		clip := g.clipMatrix()
		return getLanes(uint32(clip[i]), off, size), true
	case off >= offVecMtxRes && off < offVecMtxRes+36:
		i := (off - offVecMtxRes) / 4
		vm := [9]int32{g.curVec[0], g.curVec[1], g.curVec[2],
			g.curVec[4], g.curVec[5], g.curVec[6],
			g.curVec[8], g.curVec[9], g.curVec[10]}
		return getLanes(uint32(vm[i]), off, size), true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// WriteIO implements the write side of the claimed offsets.
func (g *GX) WriteIO(off uint32, size int, val uint32) bool {
	switch {
	case off >= offEdgeColor && off < offToonTable+0x40:
		g.writeREReg(off, size, val)
		return true
	case off >= offGXFIFO && off < offPorts:
		if size == 4 {
			g.writeFIFO(val)
		}
		return true
	case off >= offPorts && off < offPortsEnd:
		if size == 4 && off&3 == 0 {
			g.writePort(off, val)
		}
		return true
	case off == offGXSTAT || off == offGXSTAT+2:
		g.writeGXSTAT(off, size, val)
		return true
	case off == offDotDepth || off == offDotDepth+2:
		if size == 4 || off == offDotDepth {
			g.dotDepth = putLanes(g.dotDepth, off, size, val) & 0x7FFF
		}
		return true
	case off >= offPOSResult && off < offEnd:
		return true // result registers are read-only
	}
	return false
}

// writeREReg merges a write into the RE register block:
// byte-lane tables (edge colors, fog table, toon table) and
// the plain registers between them.
func (g *GX) writeREReg(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	// bytewise merges one written unit into a halfword table.
	bytewise := func(tbl []uint16, base uint32) {
		for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
			pos := off - base + uint32(i)
			b := uint16(byte(val >> (8 * i)))
			if pos%2 == 0 {
				tbl[pos/2] = tbl[pos/2]&0xFF00 | b
			} else {
				tbl[pos/2] = tbl[pos/2]&0x00FF | b<<8
			}
		}
	}
	switch {
	case off >= offEdgeColor && off < offEdgeColor+16:
		bytewise(g.edgeColor[:], offEdgeColor)
	case off >= offAlphaRef && off < offAlphaRef+4:
		g.alphaRef = putLanes(g.alphaRef, off, size, val) & 0x1F
	case off >= offClearColor && off < offClearColor+4:
		g.clearColor = putLanes(g.clearColor, off, size, val)
	case off >= offClearDepth && off < offClearDepth+2:
		g.clearDepth = putLanes(g.clearDepth, off, size, val) & 0x7FFF
		if size == 4 {
			// The high half of a 32-bit write is
			// CLRIMAGE_OFFSET.
			g.clrImgOff = val >> 16
		}
	case off >= offClearDepth+2 && off < offClearDepth+4:
		g.clrImgOff = putLanes(g.clrImgOff, off, size, val)
	case off >= offFogColor && off < offFogColor+4:
		g.fogColor = putLanes(g.fogColor, off, size, val)
	case off >= offFogOffset && off < offFogOffset+4:
		g.fogOffset = putLanes(g.fogOffset, off, size, val) & 0x7FFF
	case off >= offFogTable && off < offFogTable+32:
		for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
			g.fogTable[off-offFogTable+uint32(i)] = byte(val >> (8 * i))
		}
	case off >= offToonTable && off < offToonTable+64:
		bytewise(g.toonTable[:], offToonTable)
	}
}

// writeGXSTAT handles GXSTAT writes: bits 30-31 set the FIFO
// IRQ mode; writing bit 15 set clears the stack error flag
// and resets the projection (and, per GBATEK's "probably",
// texture) stack pointer.
func (g *GX) writeGXSTAT(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	merged := putLanes(g.irqMode<<30, off, size, val)
	g.irqMode = merged >> 30
	if merged&(1<<15) != 0 {
		g.stackErr = false
		g.spProj = 0
		g.spTex = 0
	}
}

// gxstat composes the GXSTAT register.
func (g *GX) gxstat() uint32 {
	var s uint32
	if g.boxResult {
		s |= 1 << 1
	}
	s |= uint32(g.spPos&31) << 8
	s |= uint32(g.spProj&1) << 13
	if g.stackErr {
		s |= 1 << 15
	}
	lvl := g.FIFOLevel()
	s |= uint32(lvl) << 16
	if lvl < 128 {
		s |= 1 << 25
	}
	if lvl == 0 && !g.FIFOBusy() {
		s |= 1 << 26
	}
	if g.FIFOBusy() {
		s |= 1 << 27
	}
	s |= g.irqMode << 30
	return s
}

// ramCount composes RAM_COUNT from the build buffer: polygon
// count in bits 0-11, vertex count in bits 16-28.
func (g *GX) ramCount() uint32 {
	return uint32(len(g.build.polys)) | uint32(len(g.build.verts))<<16
}

// getLanes extracts the unit of the given size at the byte
// lane of off from a 32-bit value (same convention as the
// system hook).
func getLanes(v uint32, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return (v >> ((off & 3) * 8)) & 0xFF
	case 2:
		return (v >> ((off & 2) * 8)) & 0xFFFF
	}
	return v
}

// putLanes merges a written unit into a 32-bit value.
func putLanes(v uint32, off uint32, size int, val uint32) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		sh := (off & 3) * 8
		return v&^(0xFF<<sh) | (val&0xFF)<<sh
	case 2:
		sh := (off & 2) * 8
		return v&^(0xFFFF<<sh) | (val&0xFFFF)<<sh
	}
	return val
}
