package gx_test

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/gx"
)

// rig drives the engine through its IO interface over a bus.
type rig struct {
	b *bus.Bus
	g *gx.GX
}

func newRig() *rig {
	b := bus.New()
	return &rig{b: b, g: gx.New(b)}
}

// cmd sends one command through its direct port.
func (r *rig) cmd(id uint8, params ...uint32) {
	port := uint32(0x400) + uint32(id)*4
	if len(params) == 0 {
		r.g.WriteIO(port, 4, 0)
		return
	}
	for _, p := range params {
		r.g.WriteIO(port, 4, p)
	}
}

func (r *rig) rd(off uint32) uint32 {
	v, ok := r.g.ReadIO(off, 4)
	if !ok {
		panic("unclaimed read")
	}
	return v
}

// identity sets identity projection and position matrices
// and a full-screen viewport.
func (r *rig) identity() {
	r.cmd(0x10, 0) // MTX_MODE projection
	r.cmd(0x15)    // MTX_IDENTITY
	r.cmd(0x10, 1) // MTX_MODE position
	r.cmd(0x15)
	r.cmd(0x60, 0xBFFF0000) // VIEWPORT (0,0)-(255,191)
}

func TestClipMatrixReadbackExact(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	// Load a distinctive projection matrix, identity position.
	m := [16]uint32{0x1000, 0x0800, 0xFFFFF000, 3,
		0x2000, 0x1000, 0, 0xFFFFE000,
		1, 2, 3, 4,
		0x3000, 0xFFFFC000, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x1000}
	r.cmd(0x10, 0)
	p := make([]uint32, 16)
	copy(p, m[:])
	r.cmd(0x16, p...)
	r.cmd(0x10, 1)
	r.cmd(0x15)
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if got := r.rd(0x640 + uint32(i*4)); got != m[i] {
			t.Fatalf("CLIPMTX_RESULT[%d] = %08x want %08x", i, got, m[i])
		}
	}
}

func TestPosTestHandComputed(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.identity()
	// Translate the position matrix by (0.5, -0.25, 2.0).
	r.cmd(0x1C, 0x0800, 0xFFFFFC00, 0x2000)
	// POS_TEST (1.0, 0, 0): expect (1.5, -0.25, 2.0, 1.0).
	r.cmd(0x71, 0x1000, 0)
	want := [4]uint32{0x1800, 0xFFFFFC00, 0x2000, 0x1000}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if got := r.rd(0x620 + uint32(i*4)); got != want[i] {
			t.Fatalf("POS_RESULT[%d] = %08x want %08x", i, got, want[i])
		}
	}
}

func TestVecTestIdentity(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.identity()
	// Direction (0.5, -0.5, 0) in 9-frac packed 10-bit fields:
	// 256, -256 (0x300), 0.
	r.cmd(0x72, 256|0x300<<10)
	if got := r.rd(0x630); got != 256 {
		t.Fatalf("VEC_RESULT X = %d want 256", int32(got))
	}
	if got := r.rd(0x634); got != uint32(0xFFFFFF00) {
		t.Fatalf("VEC_RESULT Y = %08x want FFFFFF00 (-256)", got)
	}
	if got := r.rd(0x638); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("VEC_RESULT Z = %d want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestMatrixStackOverflow(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.cmd(0x10, 1) // position mode
	for i := 0; i < 31; i++ {
		r.cmd(0x11) // PUSH
	}
	st := r.rd(0x600)
	if st&(1<<15) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("stack error after 31 pushes")
	}
	if got := (st >> 8) & 31; got != 31 {
		t.Fatalf("stack pointer = %d want 31", got)
	}
	r.cmd(0x11) // 32nd push: entry 31, error flag
	st = r.rd(0x600)
	if st&(1<<15) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("stack error missing after 32nd push")
	}
	// Writing GXSTAT bit 15 clears the error.
	r.g.WriteIO(0x600, 4, 1<<15)
	if st := r.rd(0x600); st&(1<<15) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("stack error not cleared by GXSTAT write")
	}
	// POP 1 from SP 32 lands at 31 (also an error entry).
	r.cmd(0x12, 1)
	if st := r.rd(0x600); (st>>8)&31 != 31 {
		t.Fatalf("stack pointer after pop = %d want 31", (st>>8)&31)
	}
}

func TestPackedFIFOCommands(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	// One packed word: MTX_MODE (0x10) + MTX_IDENTITY (0x15),
	// then the MTX_MODE parameter word (mode 0).
	r.g.WriteIO(0x400, 4, 0x10|0x15<<8)
	r.g.WriteIO(0x400, 4, 0)
	if lvl := r.g.FIFOLevel(); lvl != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO level = %d want 0", lvl)
	}
	if r.g.FIFOBusy() {
		t.Fatal("geometry busy after drain")
	}
	if got := r.g.FIFOWords; got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("FIFOWords = %d want 2", got)
	}
	// GXSTAT: empty flag set, less-than-half set.
	st := r.rd(0x600)
	if st&(1<<26) == 0 || st&(1<<25) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("GXSTAT empty/half flags: %08x", st)
	}
	// IRQ modes: mode 2 (empty) asserts, mode 0 never does.
	r.g.WriteIO(0x600, 4, 2<<30)
	if !r.g.FIFOIRQCondition() {
		t.Fatal("FIFO IRQ condition false in empty mode")
	}
	r.g.WriteIO(0x600, 4, 0)
	if r.g.FIFOIRQCondition() {
		t.Fatal("FIFO IRQ condition true in never mode")
	}
}

func TestRAMCountAndSwapPause(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.identity()
	r.cmd(0x29, 31<<16|0xC0) // POLYGON_ATTR: alpha 31, both faces
	r.cmd(0x40, 0)           // BEGIN_VTXS triangles
	// One triangle via VTX_16.
	r.cmd(0x23, 0x0000F000, 0) // (0, -1)
	r.cmd(0x23, 0x00001000, 0) // (0, 1)
	r.cmd(0x23, 0x10001000, 0) // (1, 1)
	if got := r.rd(0x604); got != 1|3<<16 {
		t.Fatalf("RAM_COUNT = %08x want 1 poly, 3 verts", got)
	}
	r.cmd(0x50, 0) // SWAP_BUFFERS
	// Commands after the swap are paused until VBlank.
	r.cmd(0x40, 0)
	r.cmd(0x23, 0x0000F000, 0)
	if got := r.rd(0x604); got != 1|3<<16 {
		t.Fatalf("RAM_COUNT moved while paused: %08x", got)
	}
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	// The paused BEGIN+VTX now executed into the new build
	// buffer: 1 vertex, no polygon yet.
	if got := r.rd(0x604); got != 0|1<<16 {
		t.Fatalf("RAM_COUNT after vblank = %08x want 0 polys, 1 vert", got)
	}
}

func TestBoxTestResult(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.identity()
	// A box well inside the view volume: result bit set.
	r.cmd(0x70, 0x00000000, 0x00000000, 0x00080008) // origin 0, size (8,8,8) in 12-frac/16 units
	if st := r.rd(0x600); st&2 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BOX_TEST inside: GXSTAT = %08x, result bit clear", st)
	}
	// A box fully beyond the right plane (X = 2.0, past
	// +W): result bit clear.
	r.cmd(0x70, 0x00002000, 0x00000000, 0x00080008)
	if st := r.rd(0x600); st&2 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BOX_TEST outside: GXSTAT = %08x, result bit set", st)
	}
}

func TestGXStateRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.identity()
	r.cmd(0x29, 31<<16|0xC0)
	r.cmd(0x40, 0)
	r.cmd(0x23, 0x0000F000, 0)
	r.cmd(0x23, 0x00001000, 0)
	r.cmd(0x23, 0x10001000, 0)
	r.cmd(0x50, 0)
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	blob := make([]byte, gx.StateSize)
	if n := r.g.Serialize(blob); n != gx.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("serialize n = %d want %d", n, gx.StateSize)
	}
	r2 := newRig()
	if n := r2.g.Deserialize(blob); n != gx.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("deserialize n = %d want %d", n, gx.StateSize)
	}
	blob2 := make([]byte, gx.StateSize)
	r2.g.Serialize(blob2)
	for i := range blob {
		if blob[i] != blob2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("state bytes differ at %d", i)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/gx/matrix.go ====================

package gx

// The matrix unit: four current matrices (projection,
// position, directional/vector, texture), three stacks, and
// the MTX command group. Matrices are 4x4, row-major,
// elements signed with 12 fractional bits; vertices are row
// vectors, so the clip transform is v * (Position *
// Projection) per GBATEK's written order, and MTX_MULT
// composes C = M * C (the new matrix applies first, in the
// vertex's local space).

type mat [16]int32

func identityMat() mat {
	var m mat
	m[0], m[5], m[10], m[15] = 0x1000, 0x1000, 0x1000, 0x1000
	return m
}

// matMul returns a*b with 64-bit accumulation and a 12-bit
// fractional shift per output element, wrapping to 32 bits.
func matMul(a, b mat) mat {
	var out mat
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
			var acc int64
			for k := 0; k < 4; k++ {
				acc += int64(a[i*4+k]) * int64(b[k*4+j])
			}
			out[i*4+j] = int32(acc >> 12)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// xform applies m to the row vector (x, y, z, w), all in the
// 12-fraction domain.
func xform(m mat, x, y, z, w int32) (int32, int32, int32, int32) {
	v := [4]int32{x, y, z, w}
	var out [4]int32
	for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
		var acc int64
		for k := 0; k < 4; k++ {
			acc += int64(v[k]) * int64(m[k*4+j])
		}
		out[j] = int32(acc >> 12)
	}
	return out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3]
}

// xformDir applies the upper 3x3 of m to a direction vector
// in the 9-fraction domain (normals, light vectors, VEC_TEST).
func xformDir(m mat, x, y, z int32) (int32, int32, int32) {
	v := [3]int32{x, y, z}
	var out [3]int32
	for j := 0; j < 3; j++ {
		var acc int64
		for k := 0; k < 3; k++ {
			acc += int64(v[k]) * int64(m[k*4+j])
		}
		out[j] = int32(acc >> 12)
	}
	return out[0], out[1], out[2]
}

// clipMatrix is Position * Projection, recomputed on demand.
func (g *GX) clipMatrix() mat { return matMul(g.curPos, g.curProj) }

// targets returns pointers to the current matrices a load or
// multiply applies to, per the matrix mode. Mode 2 applies to
// both position and vector.
func (g *GX) targets() []*mat {
	switch g.mtxMode {
	case 0:
		return []*mat{&g.curProj}
	case 2:
		return []*mat{&g.curPos, &g.curVec}
	case 3:
		return []*mat{&g.curTex}
	}
	return []*mat{&g.curPos}
}

// execMatrix runs the MTX command group (0x10-0x1C).
func (g *GX) execMatrix(cmd uint8, p []uint32) {
	switch cmd {
	case 0x10: // MTX_MODE
		g.mtxMode = int(p[0] & 3)
	case 0x11: // MTX_PUSH
		g.stackPush()
	case 0x12: // MTX_POP
		g.stackPop(p[0])
	case 0x13: // MTX_STORE
		g.stackStore(p[0])
	case 0x14: // MTX_RESTORE
		g.stackRestore(p[0])
	case 0x15: // MTX_IDENTITY
		for _, t := range g.targets() {
			*t = identityMat()
		}
	case 0x16, 0x17: // MTX_LOAD_4x4 / 4x3
		m := loadMat(p, cmd == 0x16)
		for _, t := range g.targets() {
			*t = m
		}
	case 0x18, 0x19: // MTX_MULT_4x4 / 4x3
		m := loadMat(p, cmd == 0x18)
		for _, t := range g.targets() {
			*t = matMul(m, *t)
		}
	case 0x1A: // MTX_MULT_3x3
		m := embed3x3(p)
		for _, t := range g.targets() {
			*t = matMul(m, *t)
		}
	case 0x1B: // MTX_SCALE: position only in mode 2
		var s mat
		s[0], s[5], s[10], s[15] = int32(p[0]), int32(p[1]), int32(p[2]), 0x1000
		ts := g.targets()
		if g.mtxMode == 2 {
			ts = []*mat{&g.curPos}
		}
		for _, t := range ts {
			*t = matMul(s, *t)
		}
	case 0x1C: // MTX_TRANS
		var tr mat
		tr[0], tr[5], tr[10], tr[15] = 0x1000, 0x1000, 0x1000, 0x1000
		tr[12], tr[13], tr[14] = int32(p[0]), int32(p[1]), int32(p[2])
		for _, t := range g.targets() {
			*t = matMul(tr, *t)
		}
	}
}

// loadMat builds a 4x4 matrix from a 4x4 load (16 words) or a
// 4x3 load (12 words; the fourth column is 0,0,0,1).
func loadMat(p []uint32, full bool) mat {
	var m mat
	if full {
		for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
			m[i] = int32(p[i])
		}
		return m
	}
	for i := 0; i < 12; i++ {
		m[i] = int32(p[i])
	}
	m[15] = 0x1000
	return m
}

// embed3x3 builds the 4x4 embedding of a 3x3 load: the 3x3
// block plus a zero fourth row/column and m[15] = 1.0, which
// leaves the current matrix's translation column unchanged
// under multiplication.
func embed3x3(p []uint32) mat {
	var m mat
	for r := 0; r < 3; r++ {
		for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
			m[r*4+c] = int32(p[r*3+c])
		}
	}
	m[15] = 0x1000
	return m
}

// stackPush implements MTX_PUSH per stack rules: projection
// and texture stacks hold one entry (the pointer is one bit
// and wraps, the entry mirroring, with the error flag set on
// access to entry 1); the position/vector stacks share the
// 6-bit pointer over 32 physical entries, entries addressed
// 31 and up setting the error flag (entry 31 physically
// exists and is written).
func (g *GX) stackPush() {
	switch g.mtxMode {
	case 0:
		if g.spProj == 1 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.projStk[0] = g.curProj
		g.spProj = (g.spProj + 1) & 1
	case 3:
		if g.spTex == 1 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.texStk[0] = g.curTex
		g.spTex = (g.spTex + 1) & 1
	default: // modes 1 and 2 act on both stacks
		if g.spPos >= 31 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.posStk[g.spPos&31] = g.curPos
		g.vecStk[g.spPos&31] = g.curVec
		g.spPos = (g.spPos + 1) & 63
	}
}

// stackPop implements MTX_POP: the position stack pointer
// moves by the signed 6-bit offset before the load; the
// projection and texture stacks always use offset +1.
func (g *GX) stackPop(param uint32) {
	switch g.mtxMode {
	case 0:
		g.spProj = (g.spProj - 1) & 1
		if g.spProj == 1 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.curProj = g.projStk[0]
	case 3:
		g.spTex = (g.spTex - 1) & 1
		if g.spTex == 1 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.curTex = g.texStk[0]
	default:
		n := int32(int8(param<<2)) >> 2 // sign-extend 6 bits
		g.spPos = int((int32(g.spPos) - n) & 63)
		if g.spPos >= 31 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.curPos = g.posStk[g.spPos&31]
		g.curVec = g.vecStk[g.spPos&31]
	}
}

// stackStore implements MTX_STORE. On the single-entry stacks
// the parameter is ignored.
func (g *GX) stackStore(param uint32) {
	switch g.mtxMode {
	case 0:
		g.projStk[0] = g.curProj
	case 3:
		g.texStk[0] = g.curTex
	default:
		n := int(param & 31)
		if n == 31 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.posStk[n] = g.curPos
		g.vecStk[n] = g.curVec
	}
}

// stackRestore implements MTX_RESTORE.
func (g *GX) stackRestore(param uint32) {
	switch g.mtxMode {
	case 0:
		g.curProj = g.projStk[0]
	case 3:
		g.curTex = g.texStk[0]
	default:
		n := int(param & 31)
		if n == 31 {
			g.stackErr = true
		}
		g.curPos = g.posStk[n]
		g.curVec = g.vecStk[n]
	}
}

// cmdPosTest transforms the given vertex by the clip matrix
// into POS_RESULT.
func (g *GX) cmdPosTest(p []uint32) {
	x := int32(int16(p[0]))
	y := int32(int16(p[0] >> 16))
	z := int32(int16(p[1]))
	cx, cy, cz, cw := xform(g.clipMatrix(), x, y, z, 0x1000)
	g.posResult = [4]int32{cx, cy, cz, cw}
}

// cmdVecTest transforms the packed 10-bit direction by the
// vector matrix into VEC_RESULT (9-fraction results).
func (g *GX) cmdVecTest(param uint32) {
	nx := sext10(param)
	ny := sext10(param >> 10)
	nz := sext10(param >> 20)
	rx, ry, rz := xformDir(g.curVec, nx, ny, nz)
	g.vecResult = [3]int32{rx, ry, rz}
}

// cmdBoxTest transforms the eight box corners by the clip
// matrix and reports whether any part of the box can be
// inside the view volume: the box is outside only when all
// corners fall outside one common clip plane.
func (g *GX) cmdBoxTest(p []uint32) {
	x := int32(int16(p[0]))
	y := int32(int16(p[0] >> 16))
	z := int32(int16(p[1]))
	sx := int32(int16(p[1] >> 16))
	sy := int32(int16(p[2]))
	sz := int32(int16(p[2] >> 16))
	clip := g.clipMatrix()
	var corners [8][4]int32
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		cx, cy := x, y
		if i&1 != 0 {
			cx += sx
		}
		if i&2 != 0 {
			cy += sy
		}
		cz := z
		if i&4 != 0 {
			cz += sz
		}
		a, b, c, w := xform(clip, cx, cy, cz, 0x1000)
		corners[i] = [4]int32{a, b, c, w}
	}
	outside := false
	for plane := 0; plane < 6; plane++ {
		all := true
		for _, c := range corners {
			if planeDist(c, plane) >= 0 {
				all = false
				break
			}
		}
		if all {
			outside = true
			break
		}
	}
	g.boxResult = !outside
}

// planeDist returns the signed distance of a clip-space
// vertex from clip plane p (0 left, 1 right, 2 bottom, 3 top,
// 4 near, 5 far); non-negative means inside.
func planeDist(c [4]int32, p int) int64 {
	x, y, z, w := int64(c[0]), int64(c[1]), int64(c[2]), int64(c[3])
	switch p {
	case 0:
		return x + w
	case 1:
		return w - x
	case 2:
		return y + w
	case 3:
		return w - y
	case 4:
		return z + w
	}
	return w - z
}

// sext10 sign-extends a 10-bit field.
func sext10(v uint32) int32 {
	v &= 0x3FF
	if v&0x200 != 0 {
		return int32(v) - 0x400
	}
	return int32(v)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/gx/polygon.go ====================

package gx

import "math"

// The vertex pipeline: COLOR, NORMAL, TEXCOORD and the VTX
// command forms feed the primitive assembler, which appends
// transformed vertices to vertex RAM and completed polygons
// to polygon RAM (the build half of the double buffer).
// Lighting is evaluated at NORMAL time per GBATEK's
// equations, in float64 with components in the 0..1 range
// (a stated numeric choice; results are rounded to 5-bit
// and expanded to the engine's 6-bit color domain like the
// COLOR command).

// vertex is one vertex-RAM entry: the clip coordinates
// computed at VTX time, the 6-bit vertex color, and the
// texcoord in the raw 4-fraction domain.
type vertex struct {
	x, y, z, w int32
	r, g, b    uint8
	s, t       int32
}

// polygon is one polygon-RAM entry: up to four vertex
// indices with the attribute, texture parameter, and
// palette base latched at BEGIN_VTXS.
type polygon struct {
	idx  [4]int32
	n    int
	attr uint32
	tex  uint32
	pltt uint32
}

// listBuf is one half of the double-buffered polygon and
// vertex RAM.
type listBuf struct {
	verts []vertex
	polys []polygon
}

// expandGX expands a 5-bit color channel to the geometry
// engine's 6-bit domain: 0 stays 0, anything else becomes
// 2*x+1 (GBATEK's texture-blending chapter expansion).
func expandGX(x uint32) uint32 {
	if x == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return 2*x + 1
}

// setVertexColor sets the current vertex color from an
// RGB15 value, expanded to 6-bit channels.
func (g *GX) setVertexColor(rgb15 uint32) {
	g.curR = uint8(expandGX(rgb15 & 31))
	g.curG = uint8(expandGX((rgb15 >> 5) & 31))
	g.curB = uint8(expandGX((rgb15 >> 10) & 31))
}

// cmdColor implements COLOR.
func (g *GX) cmdColor(p uint32) { g.setVertexColor(p & 0x7FFF) }

// cmdTexcoord implements TEXCOORD, including the mode-1
// (texcoord source) texture transform, computed here with
// the documented (S, T, 1/16, 1/16) input vector against the
// first two columns of the texture matrix.
func (g *GX) cmdTexcoord(p uint32) {
	s := int32(int16(p))
	t := int32(int16(p >> 16))
	if g.texParam>>30 == 1 {
		m := g.curTex
		ns := (int64(s)*int64(m[0]) + int64(t)*int64(m[4]) + int64(m[8]) + int64(m[12])) >> 12
		nt := (int64(s)*int64(m[1]) + int64(t)*int64(m[5]) + int64(m[9]) + int64(m[13])) >> 12
		s, t = int32(int16(ns)), int32(int16(nt))
	}
	g.curS, g.curT = s, t
}

// cmdNormal implements NORMAL: the normal is transformed by
// the vector matrix, the vertex color is recomputed by the
// lighting model, and in texture transform mode 2 the
// texcoord is recomputed from the transformed normal.
func (g *GX) cmdNormal(p uint32) {
	g.normalAttr = g.pendAttr
	nx, ny, nz := xformDir(g.curVec, sext10(p), sext10(p>>10), sext10(p>>20))
	if g.texParam>>30 == 2 {
		m := g.curTex
		// Inputs in the 21-fraction domain: normal terms are
		// 9-frac by 12-frac; the last-row terms use the
		// current texcoord (4-frac by 12-frac, shifted up).
		s := (int64(nx)*int64(m[0]) + int64(ny)*int64(m[4]) + int64(nz)*int64(m[8]) +
			(int64(g.curS)*int64(m[12]))<<5) >> 17
		t := (int64(nx)*int64(m[1]) + int64(ny)*int64(m[5]) + int64(nz)*int64(m[9]) +
			(int64(g.curT)*int64(m[13]))<<5) >> 17
		g.curS, g.curT = int32(int16(s)), int32(int16(t))
	}
	g.computeLighting(nx, ny, nz)
}

// computeLighting evaluates the documented per-vertex
// lighting: the color starts at the emission, and each
// enabled light adds specular, diffuse, and ambient terms.
// Light vectors and half vectors were transformed when
// LIGHT_VECTOR executed; the half vector uses the fixed
// line of sight (0, 0, -1), which the hardware never rotates
// by the projection matrix.
func (g *GX) computeLighting(nx, ny, nz int32) {
	n := [3]float64{float64(nx) / 512, float64(ny) / 512, float64(nz) / 512}
	mat5 := func(rgb uint32) [3]float64 {
		return [3]float64{
			float64(rgb&31) / 31,
			float64((rgb>>5)&31) / 31,
			float64((rgb>>10)&31) / 31,
		}
	}
	dif := mat5(g.diffuse)
	amb := mat5(g.ambient)
	spec := mat5(g.specular)
	col := mat5(g.emission)
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if g.normalAttr&(1<<uint(i)) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		lc := mat5(g.lightCol[i])
		lv := g.lightVec[i]
		hv := g.lightHalf[i]
		d := -(float64(lv[0])*n[0] + float64(lv[1])*n[1] + float64(lv[2])*n[2]) / 512
		if d < 0 {
			d = 0
		}
		s := -(float64(hv[0])*n[0] + float64(hv[1])*n[1] + float64(hv[2])*n[2]) / 512
		if s < 0 {
			s = 0
		}
		s *= s
		if g.shineOn {
			idx := int(s * 128)
			if idx > 127 {
				idx = 127
			}
			s = float64(g.shineTbl[idx]) / 255
		}
		for c := 0; c < 3; c++ {
			col[c] += spec[c]*lc[c]*s + dif[c]*lc[c]*d + amb[c]*lc[c]
		}
	}
	g.curR = uint8(expandGX(round31(col[0])))
	g.curG = uint8(expandGX(round31(col[1])))
	g.curB = uint8(expandGX(round31(col[2])))
}

// round31 clamps a 0..1 float to a rounded 5-bit value.
func round31(f float64) uint32 {
	if f <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if f >= 1 {
		return 31
	}
	return uint32(math.Floor(f*31 + 0.5))
}

// cmdLightVector implements LIGHT_VECTOR: the packed
// direction (10-bit fields, 9 fractional bits) is transformed
// by the current vector matrix when the command executes;
// the half vector against the fixed line of sight (0, 0, -1)
// is derived from the transformed vector.
func (g *GX) cmdLightVector(p uint32) {
	i := (p >> 30) & 3
	x, y, z := xformDir(g.curVec, sext10(p), sext10(p>>10), sext10(p>>20))
	g.lightVec[i] = [3]int32{x, y, z}
	g.lightHalf[i] = [3]int32{x / 2, y / 2, (z - 512) / 2}
}

// cmdVertex implements the VTX command forms. Coordinates
// enter in the 12-fraction domain: VTX_16 fields are used as
// read, VTX_10 fields (6 fractional bits) shift left by 6,
// VTX_DIFF deltas (9 fractional bits) shift left by 3 and add
// to the previous vertex.
func (g *GX) cmdVertex(cmd uint8, p []uint32) {
	var x, y, z int32
	switch cmd {
	case 0x23: // VTX_16
		x = int32(int16(p[0]))
		y = int32(int16(p[0] >> 16))
		z = int32(int16(p[1]))
	case 0x24: // VTX_10
		x = sext10(p[0]) << 6
		y = sext10(p[0]>>10) << 6
		z = sext10(p[0]>>20) << 6
	case 0x25: // VTX_XY
		x = int32(int16(p[0]))
		y = int32(int16(p[0] >> 16))
		z = g.lastZ
	case 0x26: // VTX_XZ
		x = int32(int16(p[0]))
		z = int32(int16(p[0] >> 16))
		y = g.lastY
	case 0x27: // VTX_YZ
		y = int32(int16(p[0]))
		z = int32(int16(p[0] >> 16))
		x = g.lastX
	case 0x28: // VTX_DIFF
		x = g.lastX + sext10(p[0])<<3
		y = g.lastY + sext10(p[0]>>10)<<3
		z = g.lastZ + sext10(p[0]>>20)<<3
	}
	g.lastX, g.lastY, g.lastZ = x, y, z
	s, t := g.curS, g.curT
	if g.texParam>>30 == 3 {
		// Vertex-source texture transform: the input vector
		// is the vertex position with the last row replaced
		// by the current texcoord. Terms are computed in
		// the 24-fraction domain.
		m := g.curTex
		ns := (int64(x)*int64(m[0]) + int64(y)*int64(m[4]) + int64(z)*int64(m[8]) +
			(int64(g.curS)*int64(m[12]))<<8) >> 20
		nt := (int64(x)*int64(m[1]) + int64(y)*int64(m[5]) + int64(z)*int64(m[9]) +
			(int64(g.curT)*int64(m[13]))<<8) >> 20
		s, t = int32(int16(ns)), int32(int16(nt))
	}
	cx, cy, cz, cw := xform(g.clipMatrix(), x, y, z, 0x1000)
	v := vertex{x: cx, y: cy, z: cz, w: cw,
		r: g.curR, g: g.curG, b: g.curB, s: s, t: t}
	g.pushVertex(v)
}

// beginVtxs implements BEGIN_VTXS: the pending polygon
// attribute, texture parameter, and palette base latch for
// the new primitive.
func (g *GX) beginVtxs(param uint32) {
	g.beginAttr = g.pendAttr
	g.primType = int(param & 3)
	g.primCount = 0
	g.primOpen = true
}

// pushVertex appends one transformed vertex to vertex RAM
// and feeds the primitive assembler. Vertices beyond the RAM
// capacity are dropped and set the overflow flag.
func (g *GX) pushVertex(v vertex) {
	if len(g.build.verts) >= MaxVerts {
		g.setOverflow()
		return
	}
	idx := int32(len(g.build.verts))
	g.build.verts = append(g.build.verts, v)
	if g.primOpen {
		g.assemble(idx)
	}
}

// assemble folds one new vertex index into the current
// primitive, emitting a polygon whenever a group completes.
// Strips reuse the trailing vertices of the previous group;
// in a triangle strip the winding alternates so all
// triangles keep the same facing.
func (g *GX) assemble(idx int32) {
	g.primCount++
	verts := g.build.verts
	recent := func(k int) int32 {
		return int32(len(verts)) - 1 - int32(k)
	}
	emit := func(idxs ...int32) {
		if len(g.build.polys) >= MaxPolys {
			g.setOverflow()
			return
		}
		var pl polygon
		pl.n = len(idxs)
		copy(pl.idx[:], idxs)
		pl.attr = g.beginAttr
		pl.tex = g.texParam
		pl.pltt = g.plttBase
		g.build.polys = append(g.build.polys, pl)
	}
	switch g.primType {
	case 0: // separate triangles
		if g.primCount%3 == 0 {
			emit(recent(2), recent(1), recent(0))
		}
	case 1: // separate quads
		if g.primCount%4 == 0 {
			emit(recent(3), recent(2), recent(1), recent(0))
		}
	case 2: // triangle strip
		if g.primCount >= 3 {
			if g.primCount%2 == 1 {
				emit(recent(2), recent(1), recent(0))
			} else {
				emit(recent(1), recent(2), recent(0))
			}
		}
	case 3: // quad strip: pairs of vertices per quad
		if g.primCount >= 4 && g.primCount%2 == 0 {
			emit(recent(3), recent(2), recent(1), recent(0))
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/gx/render.go ====================

package gx

import (
	"math"
	"sort"
)

// The rendering engine. At each VBlank it draws the display
// list into the frame buffers: rear plane first, then opaque
// polygons in submission order, then translucent polygons
// (Y-sorted unless the swap selected manual order), then the
// fog post-pass. Rasterization interpolates S, T, the vertex
// color, and 1/W linearly per span and divides per pixel
// (the documented perspective approach); depth interpolates
// linearly in X per span. Interpolation runs in float64; the
// depth buffer stores the rounded 24-bit result.
//
// Clipping is standard homogeneous clipping against the six
// view-volume planes (a stated simplification of the
// hardware's near-plane behavior). A polygon whose vertices
// all have W <= 0, or that still has a W <= 0 vertex after
// clipping, is not drawn.

// cvert is a clip-space vertex during clipping.
type cvert struct {
	x, y, z, w int32
	r, g, b    float64 // 6-bit color domain
	s, t       int32
}

// rvert is a screen-space vertex ready to rasterize.
type rvert struct {
	fx, fy float64 // pixel coordinates (top-down rows)
	depth  float64 // 24-bit depth value
	q      float64 // 1/W
	sq, tq float64 // texel-unit S and T times q
	rq, gq float64
	bq     float64
}

// render draws the current display list.
func (g *GX) render() {
	g.rebuildTex()
	disp3d := g.disp3dcnt()
	g.resetRear(disp3d)
	// Prepare polygons: cull, clip, project.
	type prepared struct {
		verts  []rvert
		poly   polygon
		maxY   float64
		wire   bool
		fullSz bool
	}
	var opaque, trans []prepared
	vp := g.viewport
	x1 := float64(vp & 0xFF)
	y1 := float64((vp >> 8) & 0xFF)
	x2 := float64((vp >> 16) & 0xFF)
	y2 := float64((vp >> 24) & 0xFF)
	vw, vh := x2-x1+1, y2-y1+1
	texOn := disp3d&1 != 0
	for _, pl := range g.display.polys {
		// Face culling by the clip-space winding.
		var area2 int64
		n := pl.n
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			a := g.display.verts[pl.idx[i]]
			b := g.display.verts[pl.idx[(i+1)%n]]
			area2 += int64(a.x)*int64(b.y) - int64(b.x)*int64(a.y)
		}
		if area2 == 0 {
			continue // degenerate: occupies RAM, draws nothing
		}
		if area2 > 0 && pl.attr&(1<<7) == 0 {
			continue // front face (CCW) not enabled
		}
		if area2 < 0 && pl.attr&(1<<6) == 0 {
			continue // back face (CW) not enabled
		}
		// The 1-dot depth rule: a polygon no larger than one
		// pixel in each dimension is hidden when its first
		// vertex's W is behind DISP_1DOT_DEPTH, unless the
		// attr bit allows it.
		// (Extent is measured after projection, below.)
		cv := make([]cvert, 0, n+4)
		allNegW := true
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			v := g.display.verts[pl.idx[i]]
			if v.w > 0 {
				allNegW = false
			}
			cv = append(cv, cvert{x: v.x, y: v.y, z: v.z, w: v.w,
				r: float64(v.r), g: float64(v.g), b: float64(v.b), s: v.s, t: v.t})
		}
		if allNegW {
			continue
		}
		// Far-plane crossing polygons are hidden whole when
		// the attr far-plane bit is clear.
		if pl.attr&(1<<12) == 0 {
			in, out := false, false
			for _, c := range cv {
				if int64(c.z) <= int64(c.w) {
					in = true
				} else {
					out = true
				}
			}
			if in && out {
				continue
			}
		}
		cv = clipPoly(cv)
		if len(cv) < 3 {
			continue
		}
		rv := make([]rvert, 0, len(cv))
		bad := false
		var minFx, maxFx, minFy, maxFy float64
		for i, c := range cv {
			if c.w <= 0 {
				bad = true
				break
			}
			sv := project(c, x1, y1, vw, vh, g.rndZBuf)
			rv = append(rv, sv)
			if i == 0 {
				minFx, maxFx, minFy, maxFy = sv.fx, sv.fx, sv.fy, sv.fy
			} else {
				minFx = math.Min(minFx, sv.fx)
				maxFx = math.Max(maxFx, sv.fx)
				minFy = math.Min(minFy, sv.fy)
				maxFy = math.Max(maxFy, sv.fy)
			}
		}
		if bad {
			continue
		}
		if maxFx-minFx <= 1 && maxFy-minFy <= 1 && pl.attr&(1<<13) == 0 {
			first := g.display.verts[pl.idx[0]]
			if int32(first.w>>9) > int32(g.dotDepth) {
				continue
			}
		}
		pp := prepared{verts: rv, poly: pl, maxY: maxFy,
			wire:   (pl.attr>>16)&31 == 0,
			fullSz: disp3d&0x30 != 0, // edge marking or anti-aliasing on
		}
		alpha := (pl.attr >> 16) & 31
		if alpha == 31 || pp.wire {
			opaque = append(opaque, pp)
		} else {
			pp.fullSz = true // translucent polygons render full size
			trans = append(trans, pp)
		}
	}
	for _, pp := range opaque {
		g.rasterize(pp.verts, pp.poly, disp3d, texOn, pp.wire, pp.fullSz)
	}
	if !g.rndManual {
		sort.SliceStable(trans, func(i, j int) bool { return trans[i].maxY < trans[j].maxY })
	}
	for _, pp := range trans {
		g.rasterize(pp.verts, pp.poly, disp3d, texOn, pp.wire, pp.fullSz)
	}
	g.applyFog(disp3d)
	// Compose the output buffer: rgb6 with alpha in bits
	// 18-22; fully transparent pixels read as 0.
	for i := range g.fb {
		if g.fbA[i] == 0 {
			g.fb[i] = 0
		} else {
			g.fb[i] = g.fbC[i] | uint32(g.fbA[i])<<18
		}
	}
}

// project maps one clipped vertex to screen space. The
// viewport formula follows GBATEK: sx = X1 + (x+w)*(X2-X1+1)
// /(2w); the Y axis is converted from the documented
// bottom-up viewport to top-down rows. Depth is the 24-bit Z
// value by default, or the normalized W value when the swap
// selected W buffering.
func project(c cvert, x1, y1, vw, vh float64, wBuf bool) rvert {
	wf := float64(c.w)
	sx := x1 + (float64(c.x)+wf)*vw/(2*wf)
	syBottom := y1 + (float64(c.y)+wf)*vh/(2*wf)
	fy := float64(Height) - syBottom
	var depth float64
	if wBuf {
		depth = wf * 256
	} else {
		depth = (float64(c.z) + wf) * 16777215.0 / (2 * wf)
	}
	if depth < 0 {
		depth = 0
	}
	if depth > 0xFFFFFF {
		depth = 0xFFFFFF
	}
	q := 4096.0 / wf // 1/W in real terms (W = w / 4096)
	return rvert{
		fx: sx, fy: fy, depth: depth, q: q,
		sq: float64(c.s) / 16 * q,
		tq: float64(c.t) / 16 * q,
		rq: c.r * q, gq: c.g * q, bq: c.b * q,
	}
}

// clipPoly clips a polygon against the six view-volume
// planes, interpolating all attributes linearly in clip
// space.
func clipPoly(in []cvert) []cvert {
	out := in
	for plane := 0; plane < 6; plane++ {
		if len(out) == 0 {
			return out
		}
		next := make([]cvert, 0, len(out)+1)
		for i := range out {
			a := out[i]
			b := out[(i+1)%len(out)]
			da := planeDist([4]int32{a.x, a.y, a.z, a.w}, plane)
			db := planeDist([4]int32{b.x, b.y, b.z, b.w}, plane)
			if da >= 0 {
				next = append(next, a)
			}
			if (da >= 0) != (db >= 0) {
				t := float64(da) / float64(da-db)
				next = append(next, lerpCvert(a, b, t))
			}
		}
		out = next
	}
	return out
}

func lerpCvert(a, b cvert, t float64) cvert {
	li := func(x, y int32) int32 {
		return int32(float64(x) + (float64(y)-float64(x))*t + 0.5)
	}
	lf := func(x, y float64) float64 { return x + (y-x)*t }
	return cvert{
		x: li(a.x, b.x), y: li(a.y, b.y), z: li(a.z, b.z), w: li(a.w, b.w),
		r: lf(a.r, b.r), g: lf(a.g, b.g), b: lf(a.b, b.b),
		s: li(a.s, b.s), t: li(a.t, b.t),
	}
}

// resetRear initializes the frame buffers from the rear
// plane: the clear color/depth registers, or the clear image
// bitmaps (texture slots 2 and 3, scrolled by
// CLRIMAGE_OFFSET with wraparound) when DISP3DCNT bit 14
// selects the bitmap rear plane.
func (g *GX) resetRear(disp3d uint32) {
	cc := g.clearColor
	id := uint8((cc >> 24) & 0x3F)
	clearD := expandDepth(uint32(g.clearDepth))
	if disp3d&(1<<14) != 0 {
		xo := int(g.clrImgOff & 0xFF)
		yo := int((g.clrImgOff >> 8) & 0xFF)
		for y := 0; y < Height; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
				i := y*Width + x
				src := uint32(((y+yo)&0xFF)*256 + ((x + xo) & 0xFF))
				cv := g.texHalf(0x40000 + src*2)
				dv := g.texHalf(0x60000 + src*2)
				g.fbC[i] = rgb6c(expandGX(uint32(cv&31)),
					expandGX(uint32((cv>>5)&31)), expandGX(uint32((cv>>10)&31)))
				if cv&0x8000 != 0 {
					g.fbA[i] = 31
				} else {
					g.fbA[i] = 0
				}
				g.fbDepth[i] = expandDepth(uint32(dv & 0x7FFF))
				g.fbAttr[i] = uint8(dv >> 15)
				g.fbID[i] = id
			}
		}
		return
	}
	rgb := rgb6c(expandGX(cc&31), expandGX((cc>>5)&31), expandGX((cc>>10)&31))
	alpha := uint8((cc >> 16) & 31)
	fog := uint8((cc >> 15) & 1)
	for i := range g.fbC {
		g.fbC[i] = rgb
		g.fbA[i] = alpha
		g.fbDepth[i] = clearD
		g.fbAttr[i] = fog
		g.fbID[i] = id
	}
}

// expandDepth expands a 15-bit depth to 24 bits by the
// documented formula X*0x200 plus 0x1FF when X is 0x7FFF.
func expandDepth(x uint32) uint32 {
	return x*0x200 + ((x+1)>>15)*0x1FF
}

func rgb6c(r, g, b uint32) uint32 { return r | g<<6 | b<<12 }

// rasterize fills one prepared convex polygon.
func (g *GX) rasterize(vs []rvert, pl polygon, disp3d uint32, texOn, wire, fullSz bool) {
	// Scanline range by the pixel-center rule. The normal
	// size rule excludes the bottom edge; full-size polygons
	// (translucent, edge-marked, anti-aliased) include it.
	minY, maxY := vs[0].fy, vs[0].fy
	for _, v := range vs[1:] {
		minY = math.Min(minY, v.fy)
		maxY = math.Max(maxY, v.fy)
	}
	yStart := int(math.Ceil(minY - 0.5))
	yEnd := int(math.Ceil(maxY - 0.5)) // exclusive
	if fullSz || wire {
		yEnd = int(math.Floor(maxY-0.5)) + 1
	}
	if yStart < 0 {
		yStart = 0
	}
	if yEnd > Height {
		yEnd = Height
	}
	type isect struct {
		x     float64
		attrs rvert
	}
	for y := yStart; y < yEnd; y++ {
		yc := float64(y) + 0.5
		var hits []isect
		for i := range vs {
			a := vs[i]
			b := vs[(i+1)%len(vs)]
			if (a.fy <= yc && yc < b.fy) || (b.fy <= yc && yc < a.fy) {
				t := (yc - a.fy) / (b.fy - a.fy)
				hits = append(hits, isect{
					x:     a.fx + (b.fx-a.fx)*t,
					attrs: lerpRvert(a, b, t),
				})
			}
		}
		if len(hits) < 2 {
			continue
		}
		lo, hi := hits[0], hits[0]
		for _, h := range hits[1:] {
			if h.x < lo.x {
				lo = h
			}
			if h.x > hi.x {
				hi = h
			}
		}
		xs := int(math.Ceil(lo.x - 0.5))
		xe := int(math.Ceil(hi.x - 0.5)) // exclusive
		if fullSz || wire {
			xe = int(math.Floor(hi.x-0.5)) + 1
		}
		if xs < 0 {
			xs = 0
		}
		if xe > Width {
			xe = Width
		}
		span := hi.x - lo.x
		for x := xs; x < xe; x++ {
			if wire && x != xs && x != xe-1 && y != yStart && y != yEnd-1 {
				continue
			}
			t := 0.0
			if span > 0 {
				t = (float64(x) + 0.5 - lo.x) / span
			}
			rv := lerpRvert(lo.attrs, hi.attrs, t)
			g.plot(x, y, rv, pl, disp3d, texOn, wire)
		}
	}
}

func lerpRvert(a, b rvert, t float64) rvert {
	l := func(x, y float64) float64 { return x + (y-x)*t }
	return rvert{
		depth: l(a.depth, b.depth), q: l(a.q, b.q),
		sq: l(a.sq, b.sq), tq: l(a.tq, b.tq),
		rq: l(a.rq, b.rq), gq: l(a.gq, b.gq), bq: l(a.bq, b.bq),
	}
}

// plot evaluates one pixel: texture sample and blend, alpha
// test, depth test, and the framebuffer write rules.
func (g *GX) plot(x, y int, rv rvert, pl polygon, disp3d uint32, texOn, wire bool) {
	i := y*Width + x
	depth := uint32(math.Floor(rv.depth + 0.5))
	old := g.fbDepth[i]
	diff := int64(depth) - int64(old)
	equalOK := pl.attr&(1<<14) != 0 && diff >= -0x200 && diff <= 0x200
	if diff >= 0 && !equalOK {
		return
	}
	// Vertex color at this pixel (perspective-divided).
	vc := vertex{
		r: clamp63(rv.rq / rv.q),
		g: clamp63(rv.gq / rv.q),
		b: clamp63(rv.bq / rv.q),
	}
	var tx texel
	if texOn {
		s := int(math.Floor(rv.sq / rv.q))
		t := int(math.Floor(rv.tq / rv.q))
		tx = g.sampleTexture(pl.tex, pl.pltt, s, t)
	}
	r, gg, b, a := g.blendTexture(tx, vc, pl.attr, disp3d)
	if wire {
		a = 31
	}
	if disp3d&4 != 0 && uint32(a) <= g.alphaRef {
		return // alpha test: draw only when alpha exceeds the reference
	}
	if a == 0 {
		return // fully transparent pixels update nothing
	}
	rgb := rgb6c(uint32(r), uint32(gg), uint32(b))
	translucent := a < 31
	if !translucent {
		g.fbC[i] = rgb
		g.fbA[i] = 31
		g.fbDepth[i] = depth
		g.fbAttr[i] = uint8((pl.attr >> 15) & 1)
		g.fbID[i] = uint8((pl.attr >> 24) & 0x3F)
		return
	}
	// Translucent write: alpha blending when enabled and
	// the old pixel is not fully transparent, else the
	// documented overwrite bypass.
	if disp3d&8 != 0 && g.fbA[i] > 0 {
		na := uint32(a)
		bl := func(p, o uint32) uint32 { return (p*(na+1) + o*(31-na)) / 32 }
		g.fbC[i] = rgb6c(
			bl(uint32(r), g.fbC[i]&63),
			bl(uint32(gg), g.fbC[i]>>6&63),
			bl(uint32(b), g.fbC[i]>>12&63))
		if a > g.fbA[i] {
			g.fbA[i] = a
		}
	} else {
		g.fbC[i] = rgb
		g.fbA[i] = a
	}
	if pl.attr&(1<<11) != 0 {
		g.fbDepth[i] = depth
		g.fbID[i] = uint8((pl.attr >> 24) & 0x3F)
	}
	// Fog flag: a translucent write can only clear it.
	g.fbAttr[i] &= uint8((pl.attr >> 15) & 1)
}

func clamp63(f float64) uint8 {
	if f <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if f >= 63 {
		return 63
	}
	return uint8(math.Floor(f + 0.5))
}

// applyFog runs the fog post-pass over flagged pixels: the
// density is interpolated between the documented depth
// boundaries (FOG_OFFSET plus FOG_STEP multiples, FOG_STEP
// = 0x400 shifted right by the DISP3DCNT fog shift) in the
// pixel depth's top 15 bits, then blended toward FOG_COLOR
// by (fog*density + color*(128-density))/128, density 127
// counting as 128. DISP3DCNT bit 6 selects alpha-only fog.
func (g *GX) applyFog(disp3d uint32) {
	if disp3d&(1<<7) == 0 {
		return
	}
	shift := (disp3d >> 8) & 0xF
	step := 0x400 >> shift
	fr := expandGX(g.fogColor & 31)
	fg := expandGX((g.fogColor >> 5) & 31)
	fb := expandGX((g.fogColor >> 10) & 31)
	fa := (g.fogColor >> 16) & 31
	alphaOnly := disp3d&(1<<6) != 0
	blend := func(c, f, density uint32) uint32 {
		return (f*density + c*(128-density)) / 128
	}
	for i := range g.fbC {
		if g.fbAttr[i]&1 == 0 {
			continue
		}
		d := int64(g.fbDepth[i] >> 9)
		var density uint32
		switch {
		case step == 0:
			if d <= int64(g.fogOffset) {
				density = uint32(g.fogTable[0])
			} else {
				density = uint32(g.fogTable[31])
			}
		case d <= int64(g.fogOffset)+int64(step):
			density = uint32(g.fogTable[0])
		default:
			// Find the boundary pair containing d.
			rel := d - int64(g.fogOffset)
			n := int(rel / int64(step)) // boundary index (1-based segment)
			if n > 31 {
				density = uint32(g.fogTable[31])
			} else {
				lo := int64(g.fogOffset) + int64(step)*int64(n)
				frac := d - lo
				d0 := int64(g.fogTable[n-1])
				d1 := int64(g.fogTable[n])
				density = uint32(d0 + (d1-d0)*frac/int64(step))
			}
		}
		if density == 127 {
			density = 128
		}
		if !alphaOnly {
			g.fbC[i] = rgb6c(
				blend(g.fbC[i]&63, fr, density),
				blend(g.fbC[i]>>6&63, fg, density),
				blend(g.fbC[i]>>12&63, fb, density))
		}
		g.fbA[i] = uint8(blend(uint32(g.fbA[i]), fa, density))
	}
}

// Line3D is the video package's 3D layer provider: it fills
// dst with one scanline of the rendered layer (rgb6 with the
// alpha in bits 18-22, 0 = transparent). The horizontal BG0
// scroll applies with the documented 512-pixel wrap (the
// second 256 pixels are transparent), and POWCNT1 bit 2
// (rendering engine enable) gates the output.
func (g *GX) Line3D(y int, dst *[Width]uint32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = 0
	}
	pow := uint32(g.bus.IO9[0x304]) | uint32(g.bus.IO9[0x305])<<8
	if pow&4 == 0 {
		return
	}
	scroll := int(g.bus.IO9[0x10]) | int(g.bus.IO9[0x11]&1)<<8
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		sx := x + scroll
		if sx >= 512 {
			sx -= 512
		}
		if sx >= Width {
			continue
		}
		dst[x] = g.fb[y*Width+sx]
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/gx/render_test.go ====================

package gx_test

import (
	"testing"
)

func (r *rig) line(x, y int) uint32 {
	var dst [256]uint32
	r.g.Line3D(y, &dst)
	return dst[x]
}

// prep installs the power bits Line3D needs, the identity
// transform, and the far clear depth real software uses.
func (r *rig) prep() {
	r.b.IO9[0x304] = 0x0F // LCD + engine A + 3D render + geometry
	r.g.WriteIO(0x354, 4, 0x7FFF)
	r.identity()
}

// vtx emits one VTX_16 vertex (12-frac coordinates).
func (r *rig) vtx(x, y, z int) {
	r.cmd(0x23, uint32(uint16(x))|uint32(uint16(y))<<16, uint32(uint16(z)))
}

// vtxST emits a texcoord then a vertex at z = 0.
func (r *rig) vtxST(x, y, s, t int) {
	r.cmd(0x22, uint32(uint16(s))|uint32(uint16(t))<<16)
	r.vtx(x, y, 0)
}

// quad emits a full quad primitive (NDC corners, z fixed).
func (r *rig) quad(x0, y0, x1, y1, z int) {
	r.cmd(0x40, 1) // BEGIN_VTXS quads
	r.vtx(x0, y0, z)
	r.vtx(x1, y0, z)
	r.vtx(x1, y1, z)
	r.vtx(x0, y1, z)
}

const attrBothOpaque = 31<<16 | 0xC0

func TestRedTriangleCenter(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.prep()
	r.cmd(0x29, attrBothOpaque)
	r.cmd(0x20, 0x001F) // COLOR red
	r.cmd(0x40, 0)      // triangles
	r.vtx(-0x800, -0x800, 0)
	r.vtx(0x800, -0x800, 0)
	r.vtx(0, 0x800, 0)
	r.cmd(0x50, 0)
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	if got := r.line(128, 96); got != 63|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("center = %08x want red opaque", got)
	}
	if got := r.line(2, 2); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("corner = %08x want transparent", got)
	}
}

	r := newRig()
	r.prep()
	r.cmd(0x29, attrBothOpaque)
	r.cmd(0x20, 0x001F) // red, far
	r.quad(-0xC00, -0xC00, 0xC00, 0xC00, 0x800)
	r.cmd(0x20, 0x03E0) // green, near
	r.quad(-0x600, -0x600, 0x600, 0x600, -0x800)
	r.cmd(0x50, 0)
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	if got := r.line(128, 96); got != 63<<6|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("overlap = %08x want green", got)
	}
	if got := r.line(204, 38); got != 63|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("far-only = %08x want red", got)
	}

func TestEqualDepthFlag(t *testing.T) {
	draw := func(equal bool) uint32 {
		r := newRig()
		r.prep()
		r.cmd(0x29, attrBothOpaque)
		r.cmd(0x20, 0x001F)
		r.quad(-0x800, -0x800, 0x800, 0x800, 0)
		attr := uint32(attrBothOpaque)
		if equal {
			attr |= 1 << 14
		}
		r.cmd(0x29, attr)
		r.cmd(0x20, 0x03E0)
		r.quad(-0x800, -0x800, 0x800, 0x800, 0)
		r.cmd(0x50, 0)
		r.g.OnVBlank()
		return r.line(128, 96)
	}
	if got := draw(false); got != 63|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("plain equal depth = %08x want red (second rejected)", got)
	}
	if got := draw(true); got != 63<<6|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("equal-flag depth = %08x want green (second drawn)", got)
	}
}

// texRig assigns bank A as texture slot 0 and bank E as the
// texture palette, enables texture mapping, and sets a white
// vertex color.
func (r *rig) texRig() {
	r.b.IO9[0x240] = 0x83 // bank A: texture image slot 0
	r.b.IO9[0x244] = 0x83 // bank E: texture palette slots 0-3
	r.b.IO9[0x60] = 0x01  // DISP3DCNT: texture mapping on
	r.cmd(0x29, attrBothOpaque)
	r.cmd(0x20, 0x7FFF) // white
}

// texQuad draws a full-screen quad mapping the whole texture.
func (r *rig) texQuad() {
	r.cmd(0x40, 1)
	r.vtxST(-0x1000, -0x1000, 0, 128)
	r.vtxST(0x1000, -0x1000, 128, 128)
	r.vtxST(0x1000, 0x1000, 128, 0)
	r.vtxST(-0x1000, 0x1000, 0, 0)
}

func TestTexturedQuadPalette256(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.prep()
	r.texRig()
	a := r.b.VRAMBank(0)
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		a[i] = 1
	}
	e := r.b.VRAMBank(4)
	e[2], e[3] = 0x1F, 0x00 // palette entry 1 = red
	r.cmd(0x2A, 4<<26)      // TEXIMAGE_PARAM: 8x8, 256-color palette
	r.cmd(0x2B, 0)          // PLTT_BASE 0
	r.texQuad()
	r.cmd(0x50, 0)
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	if got := r.line(128, 96); got != 63|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("textured center = %08x want red", got)
	}
}

func TestA3I5BlendOverClear(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.prep()
	r.texRig()
	r.b.IO9[0x60] = 0x09 // + alpha blending enable
	r.g.WriteIO(0x350, 4, 0x7C00|31<<16)
	a := r.b.VRAMBank(0)
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		a[i] = 0x81 // index 1, alpha 3-bit 4 (5-bit 18)
	}
	e := r.b.VRAMBank(4)
	e[2], e[3] = 0x1F, 0x00
	r.cmd(0x2A, 1<<26) // A3I5
	r.cmd(0x2B, 0)
	r.texQuad()
	r.cmd(0x50, 0)
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	got := r.line(128, 96)
	// Blend: R (63*19 + 0*13)/32 = 37, B (0*19 + 63*13)/32
	// = 25, alpha max(18, 31) = 31.
	if got != 37|25<<12|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("A3I5 blend = %08x want (37,0,25) opaque", got)
	}
}

func TestCompressedTextureBlock(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.prep()
	r.texRig()
	r.b.IO9[0x241] = 0x8B // bank B: texture image slot 1 (index data)
	a := r.b.VRAMBank(0)
	// Block (0,0): every row texels 0,1,2,3 = byte 0xE4.
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		a[i] = 0xE4
	}
	// Index header for block (0,0) sits at slot-1 offset 0
	// (bank B start): palette offset 0, mode 0. It is
	// already zero. Palette entries: black, red, green,
	// blue.
	e := r.b.VRAMBank(4)
	e[2], e[3] = 0x1F, 0x00
	e[4], e[5] = 0xE0, 0x03
	e[6], e[7] = 0x00, 0x7C
	r.cmd(0x2A, 5<<26) // 4x4 compressed
	r.cmd(0x2B, 0)
	r.texQuad()
	r.cmd(0x50, 0)
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	// Block (0,0) covers screen x 0..127 (texels 0..3 of
	// 8), rows near the top (T = 0 at the top).
	if got := r.line(16, 12); got != 31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("texel 0 = %08x want black opaque", got)
	}
	if got := r.line(48, 12); got != 63|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("texel 1 = %08x want red", got)
	}
	if got := r.line(80, 12); got != 63<<6|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("texel 2 = %08x want green", got)
	}
	if got := r.line(112, 12); got != 63<<12|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("texel 3 = %08x want blue", got)
	}
}

func TestClearImageBitmap(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.prep()
	r.texRig()                       // banks A (slot 0) and E assigned; slots follow
	r.b.IO9[0x242] = 0x80 | 3 | 2<<3 // bank C: texture slot 2
	r.b.IO9[0x243] = 0x80 | 3 | 3<<3 // bank D: texture slot 3
	r.b.IO9[0x60] = 0x01             // texture on
	r.b.IO9[0x61] = 0x40             // DISP3DCNT bit 14: bitmap rear plane
	// Color bitmap entry (0,0): red with alpha bit set.
	c := r.b.VRAMBank(2)
	c[0], c[1] = 0x1F, 0x80
	// Depth bitmap entry (0,0): 0x7FFF (far) is fine.
	d := r.b.VRAMBank(3)
	d[0], d[1] = 0xFF, 0x7F
	r.cmd(0x50, 0)
	r.g.OnVBlank()
	if got := r.line(0, 0); got != 63|31<<18 {
		t.Fatalf("clear image pixel = %08x want red", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/gx/state.go ====================

package gx

// Save state. The layout is fixed: header scalars, the RE
// registers and tables, the matrix unit (current matrices,
// stacks, pointers), the vertex and lighting state, the FIFO
// parser/executor state, the two polygon/vertex RAM buffers,
// and the rendered frame buffer. The depth/attribute/ID
// scratch buffers are not stored: every render rewrites them
// completely.

const (
	matBytes   = 64
	vertBytes  = 28 // 4 coords + 3 color + 1 pad + s,t
	polyBytes  = 32 // 4 indices + count + attr + tex + pltt
	queueBytes = 260 * 5
	fbBytes    = Width * Height * 4
	stackBytes = (1 + 32 + 32 + 1) * matBytes
	bufBytes   = 4 + MaxVerts*vertBytes + 4 + MaxPolys*polyBytes
)

// StateSize is the exact serialized size of the engine state.
const StateSize = 4 + 8 + // FIFOWords, flags, irqMode, mtxMode
	24 + 32 + 64 + 16 + 4 + // RE registers and tables
	4*matBytes + stackBytes + 4 + // matrices, stacks, pointers
	24 + // vertex color and texcoord state
	16 + 4 + 128 + 48 + 48 + 16 + // lighting
	24 + 16 + 12 + // latched registers and test results
	16 + // primitive and swap state
	17 + queueBytes + 128 + // FIFO and executor
	2*bufBytes +
	fbBytes

type sw struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (w *sw) u8(v uint8)   { w.b[w.n] = v; w.n++ }
func (w *sw) u16(v uint16) { w.u8(uint8(v)); w.u8(uint8(v >> 8)) }
func (w *sw) u32(v uint32) { w.u16(uint16(v)); w.u16(uint16(v >> 16)) }
func (w *sw) flag(f bool) {
	if f {
		w.u8(1)
	} else {
		w.u8(0)
	}
}
func (w *sw) mat(m mat) {
	for _, v := range m {
		w.u32(uint32(v))
	}
}
func (w *sw) buf(l *listBuf) {
	w.u32(uint32(len(l.verts)))
	for i := 0; i < MaxVerts; i++ {
		var v vertex
		if i < len(l.verts) {
			v = l.verts[i]
		}
		w.u32(uint32(v.x))
		w.u32(uint32(v.y))
		w.u32(uint32(v.z))
		w.u32(uint32(v.w))
		w.u8(v.r)
		w.u8(v.g)
		w.u8(v.b)
		w.u8(0)
		w.u32(uint32(v.s))
		w.u32(uint32(v.t))
	}
	w.u32(uint32(len(l.polys)))
	for i := 0; i < MaxPolys; i++ {
		var p polygon
		if i < len(l.polys) {
			p = l.polys[i]
		}
		for _, ix := range p.idx {
			w.u32(uint32(ix))
		}
		w.u32(uint32(p.n))
		w.u32(p.attr)
		w.u32(p.tex)
		w.u32(p.pltt)
	}
}

type sr struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (r *sr) u8() uint8 { v := r.b[r.n]; r.n++; return v }
func (r *sr) u16() uint16 {
	v := uint16(r.u8()) | uint16(r.u8())<<8
	return v
}
func (r *sr) u32() uint32 { v := uint32(r.u16()) | uint32(r.u16())<<16; return v }
func (r *sr) flag() bool  { return r.u8() != 0 }
func (r *sr) mat() mat {
	var m mat
	for i := range m {
		m[i] = int32(r.u32())
	}
	return m
}
func (r *sr) buf() listBuf {
	var l listBuf
	nv := int(r.u32())
	l.verts = make([]vertex, 0, nv)
	for i := 0; i < MaxVerts; i++ {
		v := vertex{x: int32(r.u32()), y: int32(r.u32()), z: int32(r.u32()), w: int32(r.u32())}
		v.r, v.g, v.b = r.u8(), r.u8(), r.u8()
		r.u8()
		v.s, v.t = int32(r.u32()), int32(r.u32())
		if i < nv {
			l.verts = append(l.verts, v)
		}
	}
	np := int(r.u32())
	l.polys = make([]polygon, 0, np)
	for i := 0; i < MaxPolys; i++ {
		var p polygon
		for j := range p.idx {
			p.idx[j] = int32(r.u32())
		}
		p.n = int(r.u32())
		p.attr, p.tex, p.pltt = r.u32(), r.u32(), r.u32()
		if i < np {
			l.polys = append(l.polys, p)
		}
	}
	return l
}

// Serialize writes the engine state into dst (at least
// StateSize bytes) and returns the byte count.
func (g *GX) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &sw{b: dst}
	w.u32(g.FIFOWords)
	w.flag(g.stackErr)
	w.flag(g.boxResult)
	w.u8(uint8(g.mtxMode))
	w.u8(0)
	w.u32(g.irqMode)
	w.u32(g.alphaRef)
	w.u32(g.clearColor)
	w.u32(g.clearDepth)
	w.u32(g.clrImgOff)
	w.u32(g.fogColor)
	w.u32(g.fogOffset)
	for _, v := range g.fogTable {
		w.u8(v)
	}
	for _, v := range g.toonTable {
		w.u16(v)
	}
	for _, v := range g.edgeColor {
		w.u16(v)
	}
	w.u32(g.dotDepth)
	w.mat(g.curProj)
	w.mat(g.curPos)
	w.mat(g.curVec)
	w.mat(g.curTex)
	for _, m := range g.projStk {
		w.mat(m)
	}
	for _, m := range g.posStk {
		w.mat(m)
	}
	for _, m := range g.vecStk {
		w.mat(m)
	}
	for _, m := range g.texStk {
		w.mat(m)
	}
	w.u8(uint8(g.spProj))
	w.u8(uint8(g.spPos))
	w.u8(uint8(g.spTex))
	w.u8(0)
	w.u8(g.curR)
	w.u8(g.curG)
	w.u8(g.curB)
	w.u8(0)
	w.u32(uint32(g.curS))
	w.u32(uint32(g.curT))
	w.u32(uint32(g.lastX))
	w.u32(uint32(g.lastY))
	w.u32(uint32(g.lastZ))
	w.u32(g.diffuse)
	w.u32(g.ambient)
	w.u32(g.specular)
	w.u32(g.emission)
	w.flag(g.shineOn)
	w.u8(0)
	w.u8(0)
	w.u8(0)
	for _, v := range g.shineTbl {
		w.u8(v)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		for _, v := range g.lightVec[i] {
			w.u32(uint32(v))
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		for _, v := range g.lightHalf[i] {
			w.u32(uint32(v))
		}
	}
	for _, v := range g.lightCol {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.u32(g.pendAttr)
	w.u32(g.normalAttr)
	w.u32(g.beginAttr)
	w.u32(g.texParam)
	w.u32(g.plttBase)
	w.u32(g.viewport)
	for _, v := range g.posResult {
		w.u32(uint32(v))
	}
	for _, v := range g.vecResult {
		w.u32(uint32(v))
	}
	w.u8(uint8(g.primType))
	w.u8(0)
	w.u16(0)
	w.u32(uint32(g.primCount))
	w.flag(g.primOpen)
	w.flag(g.swapPending)
	w.flag(g.curManual)
	w.flag(g.curZBuf)
	w.flag(g.rndManual)
	w.flag(g.rndZBuf)
	w.u8(0)
	w.u8(0)
	// FIFO and executor.
	w.u8(uint8(len(g.idQueue)))
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if i < len(g.idQueue) {
			w.u8(g.idQueue[i])
		} else {
			w.u8(0)
		}
	}
	w.u8(g.decCmd)
	w.u8(uint8(g.decRemain))
	w.u8(g.execCmd)
	w.u8(uint8(g.execHave))
	w.flag(g.executing)
	w.u8(0)
	w.u16(uint16(len(g.queue)))
	for i := 0; i < 260; i++ {
		var e fifoEntry
		if i < len(g.queue) {
			e = g.queue[i]
		}
		w.u8(e.cmd)
		w.u32(e.param)
	}
	for _, v := range g.execParams {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.buf(&g.build)
	w.buf(&g.display)
	for _, v := range g.fb {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	return w.n
}

// Deserialize restores the engine state and returns the byte
// count consumed.
func (g *GX) Deserialize(src []byte) int {
	r := &sr{b: src}
	g.FIFOWords = r.u32()
	g.stackErr = r.flag()
	g.boxResult = r.flag()
	g.mtxMode = int(r.u8())
	r.u8()
	g.irqMode = r.u32()
	g.alphaRef = r.u32()
	g.clearColor = r.u32()
	g.clearDepth = r.u32()
	g.clrImgOff = r.u32()
	g.fogColor = r.u32()
	g.fogOffset = r.u32()
	for i := range g.fogTable {
		g.fogTable[i] = r.u8()
	}
	for i := range g.toonTable {
		g.toonTable[i] = r.u16()
	}
	for i := range g.edgeColor {
		g.edgeColor[i] = r.u16()
	}
	g.dotDepth = r.u32()
	g.curProj = r.mat()
	g.curPos = r.mat()
	g.curVec = r.mat()
	g.curTex = r.mat()
	for i := range g.projStk {
		g.projStk[i] = r.mat()
	}
	for i := range g.posStk {
		g.posStk[i] = r.mat()
	}
	for i := range g.vecStk {
		g.vecStk[i] = r.mat()
	}
	for i := range g.texStk {
		g.texStk[i] = r.mat()
	}
	g.spProj = int(r.u8())
	g.spPos = int(r.u8())
	g.spTex = int(r.u8())
	r.u8()
	g.curR, g.curG, g.curB = r.u8(), r.u8(), r.u8()
	r.u8()
	g.curS = int32(r.u32())
	g.curT = int32(r.u32())
	g.lastX = int32(r.u32())
	g.lastY = int32(r.u32())
	g.lastZ = int32(r.u32())
	g.diffuse = r.u32()
	g.ambient = r.u32()
	g.specular = r.u32()
	g.emission = r.u32()
	g.shineOn = r.flag()
	r.u8()
	r.u8()
	r.u8()
	for i := range g.shineTbl {
		g.shineTbl[i] = r.u8()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		for j := range g.lightVec[i] {
			g.lightVec[i][j] = int32(r.u32())
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		for j := range g.lightHalf[i] {
			g.lightHalf[i][j] = int32(r.u32())
		}
	}
	for i := range g.lightCol {
		g.lightCol[i] = r.u32()
	}
	g.pendAttr = r.u32()
	g.normalAttr = r.u32()
	g.beginAttr = r.u32()
	g.texParam = r.u32()
	g.plttBase = r.u32()
	g.viewport = r.u32()
	for i := range g.posResult {
		g.posResult[i] = int32(r.u32())
	}
	for i := range g.vecResult {
		g.vecResult[i] = int32(r.u32())
	}
	g.primType = int(r.u8())
	r.u8()
	r.u16()
	g.primCount = int(r.u32())
	g.primOpen = r.flag()
	g.swapPending = r.flag()
	g.curManual = r.flag()
	g.curZBuf = r.flag()
	g.rndManual = r.flag()
	g.rndZBuf = r.flag()
	r.u8()
	r.u8()
	nID := int(r.u8())
	g.idQueue = g.idQueue[:0]
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		v := r.u8()
		if i < nID {
			g.idQueue = append(g.idQueue, v)
		}
	}
	g.decCmd = r.u8()
	g.decRemain = int(r.u8())
	g.execCmd = r.u8()
	g.execHave = int(r.u8())
	g.executing = r.flag()
	r.u8()
	nq := int(r.u16())
	g.queue = g.queue[:0]
	for i := 0; i < 260; i++ {
		e := fifoEntry{cmd: r.u8(), param: r.u32()}
		if i < nq {
			g.queue = append(g.queue, e)
		}
	}
	for i := range g.execParams {
		g.execParams[i] = r.u32()
	}
	g.build = r.buf()
	g.display = r.buf()
	for i := range g.fb {
		g.fb[i] = r.u32()
	}
	g.texValid = false
	return r.n
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/gx/texture.go ====================

package gx

// Texture fetch: the texture image space (four 128 KB slots,
// banks A-D assigned with VRAMCNT MST 3, the OFS field
// selecting the slot) and the texture palette space (up to
// six 16 KB slots: bank E with MST 3 covers slots 0-3, banks
// F and G with MST 3 cover slot (OFS bit 0) + (OFS bit 1)*4),
// decoded from the same VRAMCNT bytes the video package uses
// (GBATEK layout: MST bits 0-2, OFS bits 3-4, enable bit 7).
// The spaces are rebuilt when the VRAMCNT bytes change.

// rebuildTex rebuilds the texture spaces if VRAMCNT changed.
func (g *GX) rebuildTex() {
	var cur [9]byte
	copy(cur[:7], g.bus.IO9[0x240:0x247])
	cur[7] = g.bus.IO9[0x248]
	cur[8] = g.bus.IO9[0x249]
	if g.texValid && cur == g.texCache {
		return
	}
	g.texCache = cur
	g.texValid = true
	for i := range g.texImg {
		g.texImg[i] = 0
	}
	for i := range g.texPal {
		g.texPal[i] = 0
	}
	for bank := 0; bank < 9; bank++ {
		cnt := cur[bank]
		if cnt&0x80 == 0 || cnt&7 != 3 {
			continue
		}
		ofs := (cnt >> 3) & 3
		data := g.bus.VRAMBank(bank)
		switch bank {
		case 0, 1, 2, 3: // texture image slot OFS
			copy(g.texImg[uint32(ofs)*0x20000:], data)
		case 4: // E: texture palette slots 0-3
			copy(g.texPal[0:], data)
		case 5, 6: // F, G: texture palette slot (OFS.0) + (OFS.1)*4
			slot := uint32(ofs&1) + uint32(ofs>>1)*4
			copy(g.texPal[slot*0x4000:], data)
		}
	}
}

func (g *GX) texByte(addr uint32) uint8 {
	return g.texImg[addr&0x7FFFF]
}

func (g *GX) texHalf(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(g.texByte(addr)) | uint16(g.texByte(addr+1))<<8
}

func (g *GX) palHalf(addr uint32) uint16 {
	a := addr % 0x18000
	return uint16(g.texPal[a]) | uint16(g.texPal[(a+1)%0x18000])<<8
}

// texel is one decoded texture sample: RGB15 color and a
// 5-bit alpha.
type texel struct {
	rgb   uint16
	alpha uint8
	ok    bool // false: no texture (format 0 or mapping off)
}

// wrapCoord applies the wrap mode of one axis to a texel
// coordinate: clamp to the edge, repeat modulo the size, or
// flip (mirror every second repeat, which requires repeat;
// without repeat the flip bit is ignored and the coordinate
// clamps).
func wrapCoord(c, size int, repeat, flip bool) int {
	if repeat {
		if flip {
			m := c % (2 * size)
			if m < 0 {
				m += 2 * size
			}
			if m >= size {
				m = 2*size - 1 - m
			}
			return m
		}
		m := c % size
		if m < 0 {
			m += size
		}
		return m
	}
	if c < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if c >= size {
		return size - 1
	}
	return c
}

// sampleTexture fetches the texel at integer texel
// coordinates (s, t) for a polygon with the given latched
// TEXIMAGE_PARAM and PLTT_BASE values.
func (g *GX) sampleTexture(tex, pltt uint32, s, t int) texel {
	format := (tex >> 26) & 7
	if format == 0 {
		return texel{}
	}
	w := 8 << ((tex >> 20) & 7)
	h := 8 << ((tex >> 23) & 7)
	s = wrapCoord(s, w, tex&0x10000 != 0, tex&0x40000 != 0)
	t = wrapCoord(t, h, tex&0x20000 != 0, tex&0x80000 != 0)
	base := (tex & 0xFFFF) * 8
	color0Trans := tex&(1<<29) != 0
	palBase := func() uint32 {
		if format == 2 {
			return (pltt & 0x1FFF) * 8
		}
		return (pltt & 0x1FFF) * 16
	}
	switch format {
	case 1, 6: // A3I5, A5I3: one byte per texel
		b := g.texByte(base + uint32(t*w+s))
		if format == 1 {
			a := uint32(b >> 5)
			return texel{rgb: g.palHalf(palBase() + uint32(b&31)*2),
				alpha: uint8(a*4 + a/2), ok: true}
		}
		return texel{rgb: g.palHalf(palBase() + uint32(b&7)*2),
			alpha: b >> 3, ok: true}
	case 2: // 4-color palette, 2bpp
		b := g.texByte(base + uint32(t*(w/4)+s/4))
		idx := uint32((b >> (uint(s&3) * 2)) & 3)
		return palTexel(g.palHalf(palBase()+uint32(idx)*2), idx, color0Trans)
	case 3: // 16-color palette, 4bpp
		b := g.texByte(base + uint32(t*(w/2)+s/2))
		idx := uint32((b >> (uint(s&1) * 4)) & 15)
		return palTexel(g.palHalf(palBase()+uint32(idx)*2), idx, color0Trans)
	case 4: // 256-color palette, 8bpp
		idx := g.texByte(base + uint32(t*w+s))
		return palTexel(g.palHalf(palBase()+uint32(idx)*2), uint32(idx), color0Trans)
	case 5: // 4x4 compressed
		return g.sampleCompressed(base, palBase(), w, s, t)
	case 7: // direct color
		v := g.texHalf(base + uint32(t*w+s)*2)
		a := uint8(0)
		if v&0x8000 != 0 {
			a = 31
		}
		return texel{rgb: v & 0x7FFF, alpha: a, ok: true}
	}
	return texel{}
}

// palTexel applies the color-0 transparency rule of the
// palette formats.
func palTexel(rgb uint16, idx uint32, color0Trans bool) texel {
	a := uint8(31)
	if idx == 0 && color0Trans {
		a = 0
	}
	return texel{rgb: rgb, alpha: a, ok: true}
}

// sampleCompressed fetches one texel of a 4x4 compressed
// texture. The 32-bit texel blocks live in texture slot 0 or
// 2; the 16-bit palette-index header for each block lives in
// slot 1 at half the block's in-slot offset (plus 0x10000 for
// slot 2), per GBATEK. Header bits 0-13 give the palette
// offset in 4-byte steps from the palette base, bits 14-15
// the interpolation mode.
func (g *GX) sampleCompressed(base, palBase uint32, w, s, t int) texel {
	blockIdx := uint32((t/4)*(w/4) + s/4)
	blockAddr := base + blockIdx*4
	word := uint32(g.texByte(blockAddr)) | uint32(g.texByte(blockAddr+1))<<8 |
		uint32(g.texByte(blockAddr+2))<<16 | uint32(g.texByte(blockAddr+3))<<24
	var hdrAddr uint32
	if blockAddr < 0x20000 {
		hdrAddr = 0x20000 + blockAddr/2
	} else {
		hdrAddr = 0x20000 + (blockAddr-0x40000)/2 + 0x10000
	}
	hdr := g.texHalf(hdrAddr)
	mode := hdr >> 14
	palAddr := palBase + uint32(hdr&0x3FFF)*4
	row := (word >> (uint(t&3) * 8)) & 0xFF
	idx := (row >> (uint(s&3) * 2)) & 3
	c0 := g.palHalf(palAddr)
	c1 := g.palHalf(palAddr + 2)
	switch mode {
	case 0, 2: // four palette colors
		return texel{rgb: g.palHalf(palAddr + uint32(idx)*2), alpha: 31, ok: true}
	case 1: // c0, c1, average, transparent
		switch idx {
		case 0:
			return texel{rgb: c0, alpha: 31, ok: true}
		case 1:
			return texel{rgb: c1, alpha: 31, ok: true}
		case 2:
			return texel{rgb: avg15(c0, c1, 1, 1, 2), alpha: 31, ok: true}
		}
		return texel{rgb: 0, alpha: 0, ok: true}
	case 3: // c0, c1, and the 5/8 and 3/8 interpolations
		switch idx {
		case 0:
			return texel{rgb: c0, alpha: 31, ok: true}
		case 1:
			return texel{rgb: c1, alpha: 31, ok: true}
		case 2:
			return texel{rgb: avg15(c0, c1, 5, 3, 8), alpha: 31, ok: true}
		}
		return texel{rgb: avg15(c0, c1, 3, 5, 8), alpha: 31, ok: true}
	}
	return texel{}
}

// avg15 blends two RGB15 colors per channel with integer
// weights over a power-of-two denominator (truncating).
func avg15(a, b uint16, wa, wb, den uint32) uint16 {
	ch := func(x, y uint32) uint32 { return (x*wa + y*wb) / den }
	return uint16(ch(uint32(a&31), uint32(b&31)) |
		ch(uint32((a>>5)&31), uint32((b>>5)&31))<<5 |
		ch(uint32((a>>10)&31), uint32((b>>10)&31))<<10)
}

// blendTexture combines a sampled texel with a vertex color
// per the polygon mode, in the 6-bit domain with GBATEK's
// formulas. Vertex alpha comes only from POLYGON_ATTR.
// Modes: 0 modulation, 1 decal, 2 toon or highlight (the
// DISP3DCNT shading select picks), 3 shadow (rendered as
// modulation in this module; true shadow volumes need the
// polygon ID buffer test, stated in the README).
func (g *GX) blendTexture(tx texel, v vertex, attr uint32, disp3d uint32) (uint8, uint8, uint8, uint8) {
	av := uint8((attr >> 16) & 31)
	if !tx.ok {
		return v.r, v.g, v.b, av
	}
	tr := expandGX(uint32(tx.rgb & 31))
	tg := expandGX(uint32((tx.rgb >> 5) & 31))
	tb := expandGX(uint32((tx.rgb >> 10) & 31))
	vr, vg, vb := uint32(v.r), uint32(v.g), uint32(v.b)
	mod := func(t6, v6 uint32) uint32 { return ((t6+1)*(v6+1) - 1) / 64 }
	mode := (attr >> 4) & 3
	switch mode {
	case 1: // decal
		at := uint32(tx.alpha)
		if at == 0 {
			return v.r, v.g, v.b, av
		}
		if at == 31 {
			return uint8(tr), uint8(tg), uint8(tb), av
		}
		a6 := 2*at + 1
		dec := func(t6, v6 uint32) uint32 { return (t6*a6 + v6*(63-a6)) / 64 }
		return uint8(dec(tr, vr)), uint8(dec(tg, vg)), uint8(dec(tb, vb)), av
	case 2: // toon / highlight
		tt := g.toonTable[v.r>>1]
		tr2 := expandGX(uint32(tt & 31))
		tg2 := expandGX(uint32((tt >> 5) & 31))
		tb2 := expandGX(uint32((tt >> 10) & 31))
		if disp3d&2 != 0 { // highlight: modulation plus table color
			return uint8(min63(mod(tr, vr) + tr2)),
				uint8(min63(mod(tg, vg) + tg2)),
				uint8(min63(mod(tb, vb) + tb2)),
				blendAlpha(tx.alpha, av)
		}
		return uint8(mod(tr, tr2)), uint8(mod(tg, tg2)), uint8(mod(tb, tb2)),
			blendAlpha(tx.alpha, av)
	}
	// Modulation (and the shadow fallback).
	return uint8(mod(tr, vr)), uint8(mod(tg, vg)), uint8(mod(tb, vb)),
		blendAlpha(tx.alpha, av)
}

// blendAlpha combines texel and vertex alpha in the 6-bit
// formula domain and returns the 5-bit result.
func blendAlpha(at, av uint8) uint8 {
	a6 := ((expandGX(uint32(at))+1)*(expandGX(uint32(av))+1) - 1) / 64
	return uint8(a6 >> 1)
}

func min63(v uint32) uint32 {
	if v > 63 {
		return 63
	}
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/libretro/main.go ====================

// Command libretro builds the Go DS core as a libretro
// shared library (go build -buildmode=c-shared). It is a
// thin C ABI shell over the system package: the frontend
// (the iTaK engine) registers its callbacks, hands us a
// ROM, and calls retro_run once per frame.
//
// Presentation: the DS has two 256x192 screens. The shell
// presents BOTH in one 256x384 frame, stacked vertically:
// rows 0-191 are the system's top screen and rows 192-383
// the bottom screen, in the order Machine.Framebuffer
// returns them (which already honors the POWCNT1 display
// swap). The touchscreen is the libretro pointer device:
// a press in the bottom half maps into bottom-screen pixel
// coordinates and feeds Machine.SetTouch; a press in the
// top half (the non-touch screen) lifts the pen. The
// microphone is not wired to any frontend source in this
// shell: Machine.SetMicrophone stays available to hosts
// that drive the core in-process.
package main

/*

#include <stdlib.h>

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_gods_game_info) C.bool {
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	} else if info.path != nil {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(C.GoString(info.path))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		data = b
	} else {
		return false
	}
	m := system.New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(data); err != nil {
		return false
	}
	sys = m
	rom = data
	sys.Start()
	// Ask the frontend for XRGB8888 frames (what the
	// video engines produce).
	fmt888 := C.uint32_t(pixelFormatXRGB888)
	C.gods_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&fmt888))
	return true
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() { sys = nil }

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys == nil || rom == nil {
		return
	}
	// A reset re-runs the direct boot from the loaded
	// image: LoadROM stages the binaries and installs
	// the entry state again.
	m := system.New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		return
	}
	sys = m
	sys.Start()
}

func pressed(port int, id uint) bool {
	return C.gods_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceJoypad, 0, C.unsigned(id)) != 0
}

// pollPad translates libretro joypad state into the DS
// button mask (Machine.SetButtons bit order).
func pollPad(port int) uint32 {
	var m uint32
	if pressed(port, joypadA) {
		m |= btnA
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadB) {
		m |= btnB
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadSelect) {
		m |= btnSelect
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadStart) {
		m |= btnStart
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadRight) {
		m |= btnRight
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadLeft) {
		m |= btnLeft
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadUp) {
		m |= btnUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadDown) {
		m |= btnDown
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadR) {
		m |= btnR
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadL) {
		m |= btnL
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadX) {
		m |= btnX
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadY) {
		m |= btnY
	}
	return m
}

// pollTouch translates the libretro pointer into the DS
// touchscreen state. Pointer coordinates span the whole
// presented frame (-0x8000..0x7FFF over 256x384); only
// the bottom half is the touch screen. A press in the
// top half, or no press at all, lifts the pen.
func pollTouch(port int) {
	st := func(id uint) int {
		return int(C.gods_input_state(C.unsigned(port), devicePointer, 0, C.unsigned(id)))
	}
	if st(pointerPressed) == 0 {
		sys.SetTouch(0, 0, false)
		return
	}
	px := (st(pointerX) + 0x8000) * frameWidth / 0x10000
	py := (st(pointerY) + 0x8000) * frameHeight / 0x10000
	if px < 0 {
		px = 0
	}
	if px > frameWidth-1 {
		px = frameWidth - 1
	}
	if py < system.ScreenHeight {
		sys.SetTouch(0, 0, false)
		return
	}
	py -= system.ScreenHeight
	if py > system.ScreenHeight-1 {
		py = system.ScreenHeight - 1
	}
	sys.SetTouch(uint16(px), uint16(py), true)
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	C.gods_input_poll()
	sys.SetButtons(pollPad(0))
	pollTouch(0)
	sys.RunFrame()

	top, bottom := sys.Framebuffer()
	copy(frame[:frameWidth*system.ScreenHeight], top)
	copy(frame[frameWidth*system.ScreenHeight:], bottom)
	C.gods_video(unsafe.Pointer(&frame[0]),
		frameWidth, frameHeight, C.size_t(frameWidth*4))

	ab := sys.AudioSamples()
	if len(ab) >= 2 {
		frames := len(ab) / 2
		done := int(C.gods_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&ab[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
		for i := done; i < frames; i++ {
			C.gods_audio_sample(C.int16_t(ab[2*i]), C.int16_t(ab[2*i+1]))
		}
	}
}

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(system.StateSize)
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), len(state))
	copy(buf, state)
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), system.StateSize)
	cp := make([]byte, system.StateSize)
	copy(cp, buf)
	return C.bool(sys.Deserialize(cp))
}

// The memory interface exposes the cartridge save memory
// (the AUX SPI EEPROM backing) as SAVE_RAM and main RAM
// as SYSTEM_RAM, the standard libretro memory map ids.

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.unsigned) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var ram []uint8
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		ram = sys.SaveRAM()
	case memSystemRAM:
		ram = sys.Bus.MainRAM
	}
	if len(ram) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Pointer(&ram[0])
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.unsigned) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SaveRAM()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.Bus.MainRAM))
	}
	return 0
}
