==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/auxspi.go ====================

package periph

// AuxSPI is the cartridge backup memory on the AUX SPI bus,
// modeled as a small serial EEPROM (the 512-byte class used by
// early DS games) behind AUXSPICNT (0x040001A0) and AUXSPIDATA
// (0x040001A2). The protocol follows the documented small
// EEPROM command set: WREN (0x06) sets the write-enable latch,
// WRDI (0x04) clears it, RDSR (0x05) streams the status byte
// (bit 0 write-in-progress, always 0 here since writes are
// instant; bit 1 write-enable latch), READ (0x03) and WRITE
// (0x02) take one address byte (address bit 8 rides in command
// bit 3) and then stream data bytes. A transaction ends when
// AUXSPICNT is written with the chip-select hold bit (bit 6)
// clear, or when a fresh command byte arrives in command
// state; ending a transaction after a write phase clears the
// latch. The backing buffer is part of the machine state and
// is exposed to the system as the cartridge save RAM.
type AuxSPI struct {
	cnt   uint16
	save  [512]byte
	state uint8 // 0 command, 1 address, 2 read data, 3 write data, 4 status
	addr  uint32
	hi    uint32 // address bit 8 from the command byte
	wr    bool   // current transaction writes
	wel   bool
}

func (a *AuxSPI) read(rel, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch rel {
	case 0:
		return getU32(uint32(a.cnt), off, size)
	case 2:
		switch a.state {
		case 2: // read data streams on data reads
			return uint32(a.nextRead())
		case 4: // status streams after RDSR
			return uint32(a.status())
		}
		return 0
	}
	return 0
}

func (a *AuxSPI) status() byte {
	if a.wel {
		return 0x02
	}
	return 0
}

func (a *AuxSPI) nextRead() byte {
	b := a.save[a.addr&0x1FF]
	a.addr++
	return b
}

func (a *AuxSPI) write(rel, off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	switch rel {
	case 0: // AUXSPICNT
		a.cnt = uint16(putU32(uint32(a.cnt), off, size, val))
		if a.cnt&(1<<6) == 0 {
			a.end()
		}
	case 2: // AUXSPIDATA: one byte per write
		a.byteIn(byte(val))
	}
}

// end closes the current transaction.
func (a *AuxSPI) end() {
	if a.state == 3 {
		a.wel = false
	}
	a.state = 0
}

// byteIn feeds one transmitted byte into the EEPROM protocol.
func (a *AuxSPI) byteIn(b byte) {
	switch a.state {
	case 0: // command byte
		switch {
		case b == 0x06: // WREN
			a.wel = true
		case b == 0x04: // WRDI
			a.wel = false
		case b == 0x05: // RDSR
			a.state = 4
		case b&0x07 == 0x03: // READ (bit 3 = address bit 8)
			a.hi = uint32(b>>3) & 1
			a.wr = false
			a.state = 1
		case b&0x07 == 0x02: // WRITE
			a.hi = uint32(b>>3) & 1
			a.wr = true
			a.state = 1
		}
	case 1: // address byte
		a.addr = a.hi<<8 | uint32(b)
		if a.wr {
			a.state = 3
		} else {
			a.state = 2
		}
	case 3: // write data
		if a.wel {
			a.save[a.addr&0x1FF] = b
		}
		a.addr++
	case 2, 4:
		// Transmitting during a read phase just clocks the
		// stream forward.
		if a.state == 2 {
			a.nextRead()
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/card.go ====================

package periph

// ChipID is the value the card unit reports for the documented
// Get ROM Chip ID command. It is a synthetic constant of this
// module (real chip IDs belong to manufactured cartridges; ours
// follows the documented 32-bit format with the DS media type
// byte). The direct-boot block writes the same value into main
// RAM where games read their chip ID after boot.
const ChipID uint32 = 0x00001FC2

// Card is the minimal game card command model. The card is
// always in the plain (unencrypted command) state: our boot
// path never runs the KEY1/KEY2 encryption setup, and real
// games only encrypt after talking to the real BIOS, which
// this module does not have. Commands are therefore parsed
// plain, which is stated here and in the README rather than
// hidden.
//
// On a ROMCTRL write with the transfer-start bit set, the
// 8-byte command in ROMCMD is latched and a data block is
// prepared synchronously: command 0x00 and 0xB7 read ROM bytes
// at the 24-bit big-endian address in command bytes 1-3,
// command 0xB8 returns the chip ID repeated, command 0x3C (the
// KEY1 activation marker) and anything else return a zero
// block. Preparing a block raises the card-data-ready
// interrupt and fires armed card-timing DMA channels; reading
// the data port past the end raises transfer complete.
type Card struct {
	cmd     [8]byte
	romctrl uint32

	buf    []byte // prepared block, re-derived on deserialize
	pos    int
	srcOff uint32
	srcLen uint32
	kind   uint8 // 0 none, 1 ROM data, 2 chip ID, 3 zeros
	active bool
}

var cardBlockSizes = [8]uint32{0, 0x200, 0x400, 0x800, 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x4000, 0x10000}

// start latches the command and prepares the block.
func (c *Card) start(s *Set) {
	size := cardBlockSizes[(c.romctrl>>24)&7]
	c.pos = 0
	c.srcLen = size
	switch c.cmd[0] {
	case 0x00, 0xB7:
		c.kind = 1
		c.srcOff = uint32(c.cmd[1])<<16 | uint32(c.cmd[2])<<8 | uint32(c.cmd[3])
	case 0xB8:
		c.kind = 2
	default:
		c.kind = 3
	}
	c.rebuild(s.rom())
	c.active = size > 0
	if c.active {
		s.Raise(true, IRQCardData)
		s.TriggerDMA(TrigCard)
	}
}

// rebuild regenerates the prepared block from the ROM image.
func (c *Card) rebuild(rom []byte) {
	n := int(c.srcLen)
	c.buf = make([]byte, n)
	switch c.kind {
	case 1:
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			if int(c.srcOff)+i < len(rom) {
				c.buf[i] = rom[c.srcOff+uint32(i)]
			}
		}
	case 2:
		id := ChipID
		for i := 0; i+4 <= n; i += 4 {
			c.buf[i] = byte(id)
			c.buf[i+1] = byte(id >> 8)
			c.buf[i+2] = byte(id >> 16)
			c.buf[i+3] = byte(id >> 24)
		}
	}
}

// readROMCTRL returns ROMCTRL with the live status bits: bit
// 23 is data-ready, bit 31 reads as busy during a transfer.
func (c *Card) readROMCTRL() uint32 {
	v := c.romctrl &^ (1<<23 | 1<<31)
	if c.active {
		v |= 1 << 31
		if c.pos < len(c.buf) {
			v |= 1 << 23
		}
	}
	return v
}

// readData serves one word from the data port at 0x04100010.
// The second return reports that this read drained the block,
// so the caller raises the transfer-complete interrupt.
func (c *Card) readData() (uint32, bool) {
	if !c.active || c.pos >= len(c.buf) {
		return 0, false
	}
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < 4 && c.pos+i < len(c.buf); i++ {
		v |= uint32(c.buf[c.pos+i]) << (8 * i)
	}
	c.pos += 4
	if c.pos >= len(c.buf) {
		c.active = false
		return v, true
	}
	return v, false
}

func (c *Card) readCmd(rel uint32, size int) uint32 {
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < size && int(rel)+i < 8; i++ {
		v |= uint32(c.cmd[rel+uint32(i)]) << (8 * i)
	}
	return v
}

func (c *Card) writeCmd(rel uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < size && int(rel)+i < 8; i++ {
		c.cmd[rel+uint32(i)] = byte(val >> (8 * i))
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/dma.go ====================

package periph

// TriggerKind selects which DMA start condition the system or a
// device fires.
type TriggerKind int

const (
	TrigVBlank      TriggerKind = iota // frame start of vblank (line 192)
	TrigHBlank                         // per visible line
	TrigDisplayLine                    // display start + main-memory display
	TrigCard                           // a card block is ready
	TrigGX                             // frame start, geometry FIFO timing
)

// stepAddr applies a DMA address adjust mode: 0 increment,
// 1 decrement, 2 fixed, 3 increment (the destination reload
// mode also increments during the transfer).
func stepAddr(a uint32, mode uint32, unit int) uint32 {
	switch mode {
	case 0, 3:
		return a + uint32(unit)
	case 1:
		return a - uint32(unit)
	}
	return a
}

// --- ARM9 DMA -------------------------------------------------
//
// Registers at 0x0B0 + 16 per channel: SAD, DAD, CNT. CNT
// fields: bits 0-20 unit count (0 means 0x200000 units),
// 21-22 destination adjust, 23-24 source adjust, 25 repeat,
// 26 unit size (0 = 16-bit, 1 = 32-bit), 27-29 start timing,
// 30 IRQ on completion, 31 enable. Timing 0 is immediate and
// runs synchronously inside the register write; that is a
// documented simplification of the hardware's pipelined start.
// The geometry FIFO timing (7) fires once per frame.

type dma9Chan struct {
	sad, dad, cnt uint32
	src, dst      uint32
	remain        uint32
	armed         bool
}

func dma9Count(cnt uint32) uint32 {
	if n := cnt & 0x1FFFFF; n != 0 {
		return n
	}
	return 0x200000
}

func (s *Set) writeDMA9(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	ch := &s.dm9[off/16]
	rel := off % 16
	switch rel / 4 {
	case 0:
		ch.sad = putU32(ch.sad, rel, size, val)
	case 1:
		ch.dad = putU32(ch.dad, rel, size, val)
	case 2:
		ch.cnt = putU32(ch.cnt, rel, size, val)
		s.enableDMA9(int(off/16), ch)
	}
}

func (s *Set) readDMA9(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	ch := &s.dm9[off/16]
	rel := off % 16
	switch rel / 4 {
	case 0:
		return getU32(ch.sad, rel, size)
	case 1:
		return getU32(ch.dad, rel, size)
	}
	return getU32(ch.cnt, rel, size)
}

// enableDMA9 runs or arms the channel after a CNT write with
// the enable bit set.
func (s *Set) enableDMA9(idx int, ch *dma9Chan) {
	if ch.cnt&(1<<31) == 0 {
		ch.armed = false
		return
	}
	timing := (ch.cnt >> 27) & 7
	switch timing {
	case 0:
		ch.src, ch.dst = ch.sad, ch.dad
		ch.remain = dma9Count(ch.cnt)
		s.runDMA9(idx, ch)
	case 5:
		// Card timing: run at once if a block is waiting,
		// otherwise arm for the card unit to fire.
		ch.src, ch.dst = ch.sad, ch.dad
		ch.remain = dma9Count(ch.cnt)
		if s.crd.active {
			s.runDMA9(idx, ch)
		} else {
			ch.armed = true
		}
	case 6:
		// GBA cart timing: no slot device exists in this
		// module; the transfer runs immediately, reading the
		// open-bus cart window, and completes cleanly.
		ch.src, ch.dst = ch.sad, ch.dad
		ch.remain = dma9Count(ch.cnt)
		s.runDMA9(idx, ch)
	default:
		ch.src, ch.dst = ch.sad, ch.dad
		ch.remain = dma9Count(ch.cnt)
		ch.armed = true
	}
}

func (s *Set) runDMA9(idx int, ch *dma9Chan) {
	unit := 2
	if ch.cnt&(1<<26) != 0 {
		unit = 4
	}
	view := s.view9
	for ch.remain > 0 {
		v := view.Read(ch.src, unit)
		view.Write(ch.dst, unit, v)
		ch.src = stepAddr(ch.src, (ch.cnt>>23)&3, unit)
		ch.dst = stepAddr(ch.dst, (ch.cnt>>21)&3, unit)
		ch.remain--
	}
	if ch.cnt&(1<<30) != 0 {
		s.Raise(true, IRQDMA0+uint(idx))
	}
	if ch.cnt&(1<<25) != 0 {
		ch.remain = dma9Count(ch.cnt)
		if (ch.cnt>>21)&3 == 3 {
			ch.dst = ch.dad
		}
		ch.armed = true
	} else {
		ch.cnt &^= 1 << 31
		ch.armed = false
	}
}

// fireDMA9 runs every armed channel with the given timing code.
func (s *Set) fireDMA9(timing uint32) {
	for i := range s.dm9 {
		ch := &s.dm9[i]
		if ch.armed && (ch.cnt>>27)&7 == timing {
			ch.armed = false
			s.runDMA9(i, ch)
		}
	}
}

// --- ARM7 DMA -------------------------------------------------
//
// GBA register layout at 0x0B0 + 12 per channel: SAD, DAD,
// CNT_L (unit count, 16-bit, 0 means 0x10000), CNT_H: bits 5-6
// destination adjust, 7-8 source adjust, 9 repeat, 10 unit
// size, 11-12 timing (0 immediate, 1 vblank, 2 hblank,
// 3 special), 14 IRQ, 15 enable. The special timing covers the
// DS sound FIFO and card/wifi triggers on the ARM7; none has a
// real source in this module, so a special-timing transfer
// completes cleanly on enable without moving data (documented).

type dma7Chan struct {
	sad, dad   uint32
	cntL, cntH uint16
	src, dst   uint32
	remain     uint32
	armed      bool
}

func dma7Count(cntL uint16) uint32 {
	if n := uint32(cntL); n != 0 {
		return n
	}
	return 0x10000
}

func (s *Set) writeDMA7(off uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	ch := &s.dm7[off/12]
	rel := off % 12
	switch {
	case rel < 4:
		ch.sad = putU32(ch.sad, rel, size, val)
	case rel < 8:
		ch.dad = putU32(ch.dad, rel, size, val)
	case rel < 10:
		ch.cntL = uint16(putU32(uint32(ch.cntL), rel, size, val))
	default:
		ch.cntH = uint16(putU32(uint32(ch.cntH)<<16, rel, size, val) >> 16)
		s.enableDMA7(int(off/12), ch)
	}
}

func (s *Set) readDMA7(off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	ch := &s.dm7[off/12]
	rel := off % 12
	switch {
	case rel < 4:
		return getU32(ch.sad, rel, size)
	case rel < 8:
		return getU32(ch.dad, rel, size)
	case rel < 10:
		return getU32(uint32(ch.cntL), rel, size)
	}
	return getU32(uint32(ch.cntH)<<16, rel, size)
}

func (s *Set) enableDMA7(idx int, ch *dma7Chan) {
	if ch.cntH&0x8000 == 0 {
		ch.armed = false
		return
	}
	timing := (ch.cntH >> 11) & 3
	switch timing {
	case 0:
		ch.src, ch.dst = ch.sad, ch.dad
		ch.remain = dma7Count(ch.cntL)
		s.runDMA7(idx, ch)
	case 3:
		// Special timing: no source. Complete cleanly.
		ch.remain = 0
		if ch.cntH&0x4000 != 0 {
			s.Raise(false, IRQDMA0+uint(idx))
		}
		if ch.cntH&0x0200 == 0 {
			ch.cntH &^= 0x8000
		}
	default:
		ch.src, ch.dst = ch.sad, ch.dad
		ch.remain = dma7Count(ch.cntL)
		ch.armed = true
	}
}

func (s *Set) runDMA7(idx int, ch *dma7Chan) {
	unit := 2
	if ch.cntH&0x0400 != 0 {
		unit = 4
	}
	view := s.view7
	for ch.remain > 0 {
		v := view.Read(ch.src, unit)
		view.Write(ch.dst, unit, v)
		ch.src = stepAddr(ch.src, uint32(ch.cntH>>7)&3, unit)
		ch.dst = stepAddr(ch.dst, uint32(ch.cntH>>5)&3, unit)
		ch.remain--
	}
	if ch.cntH&0x4000 != 0 {
		s.Raise(false, IRQDMA0+uint(idx))
	}
	if ch.cntH&0x0200 != 0 {
		ch.remain = dma7Count(ch.cntL)
		if (ch.cntH>>5)&3 == 3 {
			ch.dst = ch.dad
		}
		ch.armed = true
	} else {
		ch.cntH &^= 0x8000
		ch.armed = false
	}
}

func (s *Set) fireDMA7(timing uint32) {
	for i := range s.dm7 {
		ch := &s.dm7[i]
		if ch.armed && uint32(ch.cntH>>11)&3 == timing {
			ch.armed = false
			s.runDMA7(i, ch)
		}
	}
}

// TriggerDMA fires a DMA start condition across both CPUs. The
// system calls it at the video timing points; the card unit
// calls the card trigger itself when a block is ready.
func (s *Set) TriggerDMA(k TriggerKind) {
	switch k {
	case TrigVBlank:
		s.fireDMA9(1)
		s.fireDMA7(1)
	case TrigHBlank:
		s.fireDMA9(2)
		s.fireDMA7(2)
	case TrigDisplayLine:
		s.fireDMA9(3)
		s.fireDMA9(4)
	case TrigCard:
		s.fireDMA9(5)
	case TrigGX:
		s.fireDMA9(7)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/firmware.go ====================

package periph

// FirmwareSize is the size of the generated firmware flash
// image the ARM7 SPI firmware device serves.
const FirmwareSize = 512 << 10

// SettingsOffset is the documented offset of the first user
// settings block in the firmware flash. A duplicate block sits
// 0x100 bytes later.
const SettingsOffset = 0x3FE00

// buildFirmware generates the minimal firmware image in code.
// It is NOT a dump of any real firmware: the image is filled
// with the erased value (0xFF) and only the two user settings
// blocks are populated, in the documented format, with a
// zeroed identity (empty nickname and message, default
// birthday and color) and a default touchscreen calibration
// matching the ADC map in spi.go. The settings block carries
// its CRC16 at offset 0x70 computed over bytes [0:0x70] with
// the reflected polynomial 0xA001 and initial value 0xFFFF,
// the CRC family of the cartridge header CRC in the cart
// package; that placement is this module's own internally
// consistent choice.
func buildFirmware() []byte {
	fw := make([]byte, FirmwareSize)
	for i := range fw {
		fw[i] = 0xFF
	}
	writeSettings(fw[SettingsOffset : SettingsOffset+0x100])
	writeSettings(fw[SettingsOffset+0x100 : SettingsOffset+0x200])
	return fw
}

func writeSettings(b []byte) {
	for i := range b {
		b[i] = 0
	}
	b[0] = 5 // settings version
	b[1] = 0 // favorite color
	b[2] = 1 // birthday month
	b[3] = 1 // birthday day
	// Nickname (UTF-16 at 0x04, length byte at 0x1A) and the
	// message area stay zeroed: empty.
	putU16(b, 0x58, 0x0200) // touch calibration: ADC X1
	putU16(b, 0x5A, 0x0200) // ADC Y1
	b[0x5C] = 0             // screen X1
	b[0x5D] = 0             // screen Y1
	putU16(b, 0x5E, 0x0E00) // ADC X2
	putU16(b, 0x60, 0x0E00) // ADC Y2
	b[0x62] = 254           // screen X2
	b[0x63] = 190           // screen Y2
	putU16(b, 0x70, crc16Settings(b[:0x70]))
}

func putU16(b []byte, off int, v uint16) {
	b[off] = byte(v)
	b[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
}

func crc16Settings(data []byte) uint16 {
	crc := uint16(0xFFFF)
	for _, c := range data {
		crc ^= uint16(c)
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if crc&1 != 0 {
				crc = crc>>1 ^ 0xA001
			} else {
				crc >>= 1
			}
		}
	}
	return crc
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/ipc.go ====================

package periph

// IPC implements IPCSYNC and the IPC FIFO pair. Each side has a
// 16-word send FIFO that the other side receives from. IRQ
// conditions follow the control register: send FIFO empty,
// receive FIFO not empty, plus the IPCSYNC nibble exchange.
// Overflow and underflow set the side's error flag.
type IPC struct {
	syncOut        [2]uint8
	syncIRQEn      [2]bool
	fifo           [2][16]uint32 // fifo[s] is written by side s
	head           [2]int
	count          [2]int
	cntEn          [2]bool
	sendEmptyIE    [2]bool
	recvNotEmptyIE [2]bool
	err            [2]bool
}

func sideNine(side int) bool { return side == 0 }

// read serves IPCSYNC (rel 0) and IPCFIFOCNT (rel 4).
func (p *IPC) read(side int, rel, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	other := 1 - side
	var v uint32
	switch rel / 4 {
	case 0: // IPCSYNC
		v = uint32(p.syncOut[other]) | uint32(p.syncOut[side])<<8
		if p.syncIRQEn[side] {
			v |= 1 << 13
		}
	case 1: // IPCFIFOCNT
		if p.count[side] == 0 {
			v |= 1 << 0
		}
		if p.count[side] == 16 {
			v |= 1 << 1
		}
		if p.sendEmptyIE[side] {
			v |= 1 << 2
		}
		if p.count[other] == 0 {
			v |= 1 << 8
		}
		if p.count[other] == 16 {
			v |= 1 << 9
		}
		if p.recvNotEmptyIE[side] {
			v |= 1 << 10
		}
		if p.err[side] {
			v |= 1 << 14
		}
		if p.cntEn[side] {
			v |= 1 << 15
		}
	}
	return getU32(v, off, size)
}

// writeCnt serves writes to IPCSYNC and IPCFIFOCNT. Writing a
// new output nibble raises the other side's sync IRQ when that
// side enabled it (its IPCSYNC bit 13).
func (p *IPC) writeCnt(side int, rel, off uint32, size int, val uint32, s *Set) {
	other := 1 - side
	switch rel / 4 {
	case 0: // IPCSYNC
		if coversBit(off, size, 8) {
			merged := putU32(uint32(p.syncOut[side])<<8, off, size, val)
			newOut := uint8(merged >> 8 & 0xF)
			if newOut != p.syncOut[side] {
				p.syncOut[side] = newOut
				if p.syncIRQEn[other] {
					s.Raise(sideNine(other), IRQIPCSync)
				}
			}
		}
		if coversBit(off, size, 13) {
			p.syncIRQEn[side] = putU32(0, off, size, val)&(1<<13) != 0
		}
	case 1: // IPCFIFOCNT
		merged := putU32(0, off, size, val)
		// Only the writable bits the write actually covered
		// change; test the covered lanes via the raw value.
		p.applyCnt(side, off, size, merged)
		if coversBit(off, size, 3) && merged&(1<<3) != 0 {
			p.head[side], p.count[side] = 0, 0
			if p.sendEmptyIE[side] {
				s.Raise(sideNine(side), IRQIPCSend)
			}
		}
	}
}

// applyCnt updates the side's FIFO control enables from the
// lanes the CPU wrote.
func (p *IPC) applyCnt(side int, off uint32, size int, merged uint32) {
	if coversBit(off, size, 2) {
		p.sendEmptyIE[side] = merged&(1<<2) != 0
	}
	if coversBit(off, size, 10) {
		p.recvNotEmptyIE[side] = merged&(1<<10) != 0
	}
	if coversBit(off, size, 14) && merged&(1<<14) != 0 {
		p.err[side] = false // writing 1 clears the error flag
	}
	if coversBit(off, size, 15) {
		p.cntEn[side] = merged&(1<<15) != 0
	}
}

// coversBit reports whether a write of the given size at byte
// lane off touches register bit b.
func coversBit(off uint32, size int, b uint) bool {
	lo := uint((off & 3) * 8)
	hi := lo + uint(size*8)
	return lo <= b && b < hi
}

// send pushes one word into the side's send FIFO.
func (p *IPC) send(side int, v uint32, s *Set) {
	if !p.cntEn[side] {
		return
	}
	if p.count[side] == 16 {
		p.err[side] = true
		return
	}
	p.fifo[side][(p.head[side]+p.count[side])%16] = v
	p.count[side]++
	other := 1 - side
	if p.recvNotEmptyIE[other] {
		s.Raise(sideNine(other), IRQIPCRecv)
	}
}

// recv pops one word from the other side's send FIFO. Reading
// an empty FIFO sets the error flag and returns 0 (hardware
// returns the last word; 0 is our documented simplification).
// Draining the sender's FIFO raises the sender's send-empty
// IRQ when the sender enabled it.
func (p *IPC) recv(side int, s *Set) uint32 {
	other := 1 - side
	if p.count[other] == 0 {
		p.err[side] = true
		return 0
	}
	v := p.fifo[other][p.head[other]]
	p.head[other] = (p.head[other] + 1) % 16
	p.count[other]--
	if p.count[other] == 0 && p.sendEmptyIE[other] {
		s.Raise(sideNine(other), IRQIPCSend)
	}
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/periph.go ====================

// Package periph implements the DS device registers that are
// not plain storage: the per-CPU interrupt controllers, timers,
// DMA engines, the IPC sync and FIFO unit, the game card
// command port, the AUX SPI save memory, the ARM7 SPI bus
// (power, firmware flash, touchscreen with the microphone aux
// channel), and the RTC stub. The
// system installs a Set as the bus IOHook; offsets the Set does
// not claim fall back to plain IO storage in the bus.
//
// Offset space: the bus hook offsets (IO page offset, plus the
// 0x04100000 window at 0x2000). Side index 0 is the ARM9, side
// index 1 is the ARM7, matching sideIdx.
package periph

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
)

// Interrupt source bits in IE/IF (GBATEK). Bit 7 is the RTC on
// the ARM7 only; bit 21 is the geometry FIFO on the ARM9 and
// unused on the ARM7; bits 22-24 are ARM7 only (pen down,
// wifi (no source in this module), SPI).
const (
	IRQVBlank   = 0
	IRQHBlank   = 1 // raised by the system, not this package
	IRQVCount   = 2 // raised by the system, not this package
	IRQTimer0   = 3
	IRQTimer1   = 4
	IRQTimer2   = 5
	IRQTimer3   = 6
	IRQRTC      = 7
	IRQDMA0     = 8
	IRQDMA1     = 9
	IRQDMA2     = 10
	IRQDMA3     = 11
	IRQKeys     = 12
	IRQCartSlot = 13 // GBA slot: no source in this module
	IRQIPCSync  = 16
	IRQIPCSend  = 17
	IRQIPCRecv  = 18
	IRQCardData = 19
	IRQCardIO   = 20
	IRQPendown  = 22
	IRQWifi     = 23 // no source in this module
	IRQSPI      = 24
)

// GXFIFOAddr is the geometry command FIFO port. In DS-3 the
// system hook routes writes there to the gx package; the
// DS-2 counting sink that lived here is gone.
const GXFIFOAddr = 0x04000400

// IO offsets (hook offset space) of the registers claimed here.
const (
	offDMA9   = 0x0B0
	offDMA7   = 0x0B0
	offTimers = 0x100
	offKeyIn  = 0x130
	offExtKey = 0x136
	offRTC    = 0x138
	offIPC    = 0x180
	offAuxSPI = 0x1A0
	offROMCtl = 0x1A4
	offROMCmd = 0x1A8
	offIME    = 0x208
	offIE     = 0x210
	offIF     = 0x214
	offSPI    = 0x1C0

	extFIFORecv = 0x2000 // 0x04100000
	extCardData = 0x2010 // 0x04100010
)

func sideIdx(nine bool) int {
	if nine {
		return 0
	}
	return 1
}

// irqCtl is one CPU's IME/IE/IF register set. IF bits are set
// by devices through raise and cleared by the CPU writing 1s.
type irqCtl struct {
	ime    uint32
	ie     uint32
	iflags uint32
}

// Set is the whole DS-2 peripheral set behind the bus hook.
type Set struct {
	bus   *bus.Bus
	view9 bus.View
	view7 bus.View
	rom   func() []byte
	keys  func() uint32
	touch func() (uint16, uint16, bool)
	mic   func() (int16, bool)
	penDn bool

	irq [2]irqCtl
	tim [2][4]Timer
	dm9 [4]dma9Chan
	dm7 [4]dma7Chan
	ipc IPC
	crd Card
	aux AuxSPI
	spi SPI
	rtc RTC
}

// New builds the peripheral set. The callbacks reach the parts
// of the machine the devices touch: the cartridge image, the
// button state, and the touchscreen state.
func New(b *bus.Bus, rom func() []byte, keys func() uint32, touch func() (uint16, uint16, bool)) *Set {
	s := &Set{
		bus:   b,
		view9: b.ARM9(),
		view7: b.ARM7(),
		rom:   rom,
		keys:  keys,
		touch: touch,
	}
	s.spi.fw = buildFirmware()
	return s
}

// Raise sets an interrupt flag on one side.
func (s *Set) Raise(nine bool, bit uint) {
	s.irq[sideIdx(nine)].iflags |= 1 << bit
}

// PendingIRQ reports whether the side's IRQ line should be
// asserted: master enable set and at least one enabled source
// pending.
func (s *Set) PendingIRQ(nine bool) bool {
	c := &s.irq[sideIdx(nine)]
	return c.ime&1 != 0 && c.ie&c.iflags != 0
}

// IFlags returns the side's pending interrupt flags (tests and
// the system's keypad evaluation read them here).
func (s *Set) IFlags(nine bool) uint32 { return s.irq[sideIdx(nine)].iflags }

// SetPenDown records the touchscreen pen state; a transition to
// down raises the ARM7 pen-down interrupt.
func (s *Set) SetPenDown(down bool) {
	if down && !s.penDn {
		s.Raise(false, IRQPendown)
	}
	s.penDn = down
}

// SetMicrophoneSource installs the machine's microphone
// sample source for the touchscreen ADC aux channel (DS-3).
// Each call of the source consumes one sample; ok=false means
// no sample is available and the ADC reads its idle value.
func (s *Set) SetMicrophoneSource(fn func() (int16, bool)) { s.mic = fn }

// SaveRAM returns the cartridge save memory (the AUX SPI
// EEPROM backing).
func (s *Set) SaveRAM() []byte { return s.aux.save[:] }

// ReadIO implements bus.IOHook for the offsets this package
// claims.
func (s *Set) ReadIO(nine bool, off uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	side := sideIdx(nine)
	switch {
	case off >= offDMA9 && off < offDMA9+0x40 && nine:
		return s.readDMA9(off-offDMA9, size), true
	case off >= offDMA7 && off < offDMA7+0x38 && !nine:
		return s.readDMA7(off-offDMA7, size), true
	case off >= offTimers && off < offTimers+0x10:
		return s.tim[side][(off-offTimers)/4].readReg(off&3, size), true
	case off == offKeyIn:
		return getU32(0xFFFF&^(s.keys()&0x3FF), off, size), true
	case off == offExtKey && !nine:
		v := uint32(0xFFFF)
		if s.keys()&0x400 != 0 {
			v &^= 1 << 0 // X
		}
		if s.keys()&0x800 != 0 {
			v &^= 1 << 1 // Y
		}
		if _, _, down := s.touch(); down {
			v &^= 1 << 6 // pen down
		}
		return getU32(v, off, size), true
	case off == offRTC && !nine:
		return uint32(s.rtc.read()), true
	case off == offIPC || off == offIPC+4 || off == offIPC+8:
		return s.ipc.read(side, off-offIPC, off, size), true
	case off == offAuxSPI || off == offAuxSPI+2:
		return s.aux.read(off-offAuxSPI, off, size), true
	case off == offROMCtl && nine:
		return getU32(s.crd.readROMCTRL(), off, size), true
	case off >= offROMCmd && off < offROMCmd+8 && nine:
		return s.crd.readCmd(off-offROMCmd, size), true
	case off == offSPI || off == offSPI+2:
		if nine {
			return 0, false
		}
		return s.spi.read(off-offSPI, off, size), true
	case off >= offIME && off < offIME+4, off >= offIE && off < offIE+4, off >= offIF && off < offIF+4:
		c := &s.irq[side]
		var v uint32
		switch {
		case off < offIME+4:
			v = c.ime
		case off < offIE+4:
			v = c.ie
		default:
			v = c.iflags
		}
		return getU32(v, off, size), true
	case !nine && (off == 0x204 || off == 0x205 || off == 0x247):
		// The ARM7 reads EXMEMCNT and WRAMCNT from the ARM9
		// page (the DS-1 bus routes these reads itself when no
		// hook is installed; with the hook we serve them).
		v := uint32(s.bus.IO9[off])
		if size >= 2 && off == 0x204 {
			v |= uint32(s.bus.IO9[0x205]) << 8
		}
		return v, true
	case off == extFIFORecv:
		return s.ipc.recv(side, s), true
	case off == extCardData && nine:
		v, done := s.crd.readData()
		if done {
			s.Raise(true, IRQCardIO)
		}
		return v, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// WriteIO implements bus.IOHook for the offsets this package
// claims.
func (s *Set) WriteIO(nine bool, off uint32, size int, val uint32) bool {
	side := sideIdx(nine)
	switch {
	case off >= offDMA9 && off < offDMA9+0x40 && nine:
		s.writeDMA9(off-offDMA9, size, val)
		return true
	case off >= offDMA7 && off < offDMA7+0x38 && !nine:
		s.writeDMA7(off-offDMA7, size, val)
		return true
	case off >= offTimers && off < offTimers+0x10:
		s.tim[side][(off-offTimers)/4].writeReg(off&3, size, val)
		return true
	case off == offRTC && !nine:
		s.rtc.write()
		return true
	case off == offIPC || off == offIPC+4:
		s.ipc.writeCnt(side, off-offIPC, off, size, val, s)
		return true
	case off == offIPC+8:
		// IPCFIFOSEND is a full-word port; partial writes are
		// ignored on hardware.
		if size == 4 {
			s.ipc.send(side, val, s)
		}
		return true
	case off == offAuxSPI || off == offAuxSPI+2:
		s.aux.write(off-offAuxSPI, off, size, val)
		return true
	case off == offROMCtl && nine:
		s.crd.romctrl = putU32(s.crd.romctrl, off, size, val)
		if merged := s.crd.romctrl; merged&(1<<31) != 0 {
			s.crd.start(s)
		}
		return true
	case off >= offROMCmd && off < offROMCmd+8 && nine:
		s.crd.writeCmd(off-offROMCmd, size, val)
		return true
	case (off == offSPI || off == offSPI+2) && !nine:
		s.spi.write(off-offSPI, off, size, val, s)
		return true
	case off >= offIME && off < offIME+4:
		c := &s.irq[side]
		c.ime = putU32(c.ime, off, size, val) & 1
		return true
	case off >= offIE && off < offIE+4:
		c := &s.irq[side]
		c.ie = putU32(c.ie, off, size, val)
		return true
	case off >= offIF && off < offIF+4:
		// Writing 1s acknowledges (clears) the written flags.
		c := &s.irq[side]
		c.iflags &^= putU32(0, off, size, val)
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// FrameTick advances the frame-based devices (the RTC) by one
// video frame. The system calls it once per RunFrame.
func (s *Set) FrameTick() {
	if s.rtc.tick() {
		s.Raise(false, IRQRTC)
	}
}

// getU32 extracts the unit of the given size at byte lane
// (off&3) from a 32-bit register value.
func getU32(v uint32, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return (v >> ((off & 3) * 8)) & 0xFF
	case 2:
		return (v >> ((off & 2) * 8)) & 0xFFFF
	}
	return v
}

// putU32 merges a written unit of the given size at byte lane
// (off&3) into a 32-bit register value and returns the result.
func putU32(v uint32, off uint32, size int, val uint32) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		sh := (off & 3) * 8
		return v&^(0xFF<<sh) | (val&0xFF)<<sh
	case 2:
		sh := (off & 2) * 8
		return v&^(0xFFFF<<sh) | (val&0xFFFF)<<sh
	}
	return val
}

// stateWriter and stateReader are byte cursors for the device
// state blob, in the armcore style.
type stateWriter struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (w *stateWriter) u8(v uint8)   { w.b[w.n] = v; w.n++ }
func (w *stateWriter) u16(v uint16) { w.u8(uint8(v)); w.u8(uint8(v >> 8)) }
func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) {
	w.u16(uint16(v))
	w.u16(uint16(v >> 16))
}
func (w *stateWriter) u64(v uint64) { w.u32(uint32(v)); w.u32(uint32(v >> 32)) }
func (w *stateWriter) bytes(p []byte) {
	copy(w.b[w.n:], p)
	w.n += len(p)
}
func (w *stateWriter) flag(b bool) {
	if b {
		w.u8(1)
	} else {
		w.u8(0)
	}
}

type stateReader struct {
	b []byte
	n int
}

func (r *stateReader) u8() uint8 { v := r.b[r.n]; r.n++; return v }
func (r *stateReader) u16() uint16 {
	v := uint16(r.u8()) | uint16(r.u8())<<8
	return v
}
func (r *stateReader) u32() uint32 {
	v := uint32(r.u16()) | uint32(r.u16())<<16
	return v
}
func (r *stateReader) u64() uint64 {
	v := uint64(r.u32()) | uint64(r.u32())<<32
	return v
}
func (r *stateReader) bytes(p []byte) {
	copy(p, r.b[r.n:r.n+len(p)])
	r.n += len(p)
}
func (r *stateReader) flag() bool { return r.u8() != 0 }


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/periph_test.go ====================

package periph

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
)

// rig wires a Set onto a bare bus, the way the system does.
type rig struct {
	b   *bus.Bus
	s   *Set
	v9  bus.View
	v7  bus.View
	rom []byte
}

func newRig() *rig {
	r := &rig{rom: make([]byte, 0x8000)}
	for i := range r.rom {
		r.rom[i] = byte(i*7 + 3)
	}
	r.b = bus.New()
	r.b.SetROM(r.rom)
	keys := uint32(0)
	r.s = New(r.b,
		func() []byte { return r.rom },
		func() uint32 { return keys },
		func() (uint16, uint16, bool) { return 100, 50, true })
	r.b.SetIOHook(r.s)
	r.v9 = r.b.ARM9()
	r.v7 = r.b.ARM7()
	return r
}

func TestIRQControlAndAck(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.s.Raise(true, IRQVBlank)
	if r.s.PendingIRQ(true) {
		t.Fatal("pending with IME clear")
	}
	r.v9.Write(0x04000210, 4, 1) // IE = VBlank
	r.v9.Write(0x04000208, 4, 1) // IME = 1
	if !r.s.PendingIRQ(true) {
		t.Fatal("not pending with IME+IE+IF set")
	}
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x04000214, 4); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("IF readback: %08x", got)
	}
	r.v9.Write(0x04000214, 4, 1) // ack
	if r.s.PendingIRQ(true) || r.s.IFlags(true) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("IF ack failed")
	}
	// ARM7 side is independent.
	if r.s.IFlags(false) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("ARM7 IF polluted")
	}
}

func TestTimersExactAndCascade(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	// Timer 0 (ARM9): reload for a 547-tick period at F/1024.
	r.v9.Write(0x04000100, 2, 64989)
	r.v9.Write(0x04000102, 2, 0xC3) // start, IRQ on, F/1024
	r.s.AdvanceTimers(true, 5601900)
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x04000100, 2); got != 64989 {
		t.Fatalf("counter after 10 exact periods: %d want 64989", got)
	}
	if r.s.IFlags(true)&(1<<IRQTimer0) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer overflow IRQ not raised")
	}
	r.v9.Write(0x04000214, 4, 1<<IRQTimer0) // ack
	// Remainder is 620 cycles; 547*1024-620 more gives exactly
	// one more overflow, landing back on the reload value.
	r.s.AdvanceTimers(true, 547*1024-620)
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x04000100, 2); got != 64989 {
		t.Fatalf("counter after 11th period: %d want 64989", got)
	}
	if r.s.IFlags(true)&(1<<IRQTimer0) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("11th overflow IRQ not raised")
	}
	// Cascade: timer 2 period 1 tick (reload 0xFFFF) at F/1024,
	// timer 3 cascades from it.
	r.v9.Write(0x04000108, 2, 0xFFFF)
	r.v9.Write(0x0400010A, 2, 0xC3)
	r.v9.Write(0x0400010C, 2, 100)
	r.v9.Write(0x0400010E, 2, 0x84) // start, cascade
	r.s.AdvanceTimers(true, 1024*5)
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x0400010C, 2); got != 105 {
		t.Fatalf("cascade counter: %d want 105", got)
	}
}

func TestDMA9Immediate(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	src := []byte{1, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 3, 0, 0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 0}
	r.b.LoadBytes(true, 0x02001000, src)
	r.v9.Write(0x040000B0, 4, 0x02001000) // SAD
	r.v9.Write(0x040000B4, 4, 0x02002000) // DAD
	r.v9.Write(0x040000B8, 4, 0x84000004) // enable, 32-bit, 4 units
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		got := r.v9.Read(0x02002000+uint32(i*4), 4)
		if got != uint32(i+1) {
			t.Fatalf("DMA word %d: %08x", i, got)
		}
	}
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x040000B8, 4); got&(1<<31) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("enable bit not cleared after immediate transfer")
	}
}

func TestIPCLoopbackAndSync(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.v9.Write(0x04000184, 4, 0x8000) // ARM9 FIFO enable
	r.v7.Write(0x04000184, 4, 0x8400) // ARM7 enable + recv IRQ
	r.v9.Write(0x04000188, 4, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if r.s.IFlags(false)&(1<<IRQIPCRecv) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("ARM7 receive IRQ not raised")
	}
	if got := r.v7.Read(0x04100000, 4); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO ARM9 to ARM7: %08x", got)
	}
	r.v9.Write(0x04000184, 4, 0x8400)
	r.v7.Write(0x04000188, 4, 0x12345678)
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x04100000, 4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO ARM7 to ARM9: %08x", got)
	}
	// IPCSYNC: ARM9 enables its sync IRQ, ARM7 sends nibble 5.
	r.v9.Write(0x04000180, 2, 1<<13)
	r.v7.Write(0x04000180, 2, 0x0500)
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x04000180, 2); got&0xF != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("sync nibble: %04x", got)
	}
	if r.s.IFlags(true)&(1<<IRQIPCSync) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("sync IRQ not raised")
	}
	// Underflow sets the error flag.
	r.v7.Read(0x04100000, 4)
	if got := r.v7.Read(0x04000184, 4); got&(1<<14) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("FIFO error flag not set on underflow")
	}
}

func TestCardCommandsAndDMA(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	// Chip ID command (0xB8), block size code 1 (0x200).
	r.v9.Write(0x040001A8, 4, 0xB8)
	r.v9.Write(0x040001A4, 4, 0x81000000)
	if r.s.IFlags(true)&(1<<IRQCardData) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("card data-ready IRQ not raised")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if got := r.v9.Read(0x04100010, 4); got != ChipID {
			t.Fatalf("chip ID word %d: %08x", i, got)
		}
	}
	// Data read 0xB7 at ROM offset 0x1000, drained by DMA.
	r.v9.Write(0x040001A8, 4, 0xB7)
	r.v9.Write(0x040001AC, 4, 0x00100000) // addr bytes big-endian in cmd[1..3]
	r.v9.Write(0x040001A4, 4, 0x81000000)
	r.v9.Write(0x040000B0, 4, 0x04100010)
	r.v9.Write(0x040000B4, 4, 0x02004000)
	r.v9.Write(0x040000B8, 4, 0xAD000080) // enable, card timing, fixed source, 32-bit, 128 words
	for i := 0; i < 0x200; i++ {
		if r.b.MainRAM[0x4000+i] != r.rom[0x1000+i] {
			t.Fatalf("card DMA byte %d: %02x want %02x", i, r.b.MainRAM[0x4000+i], r.rom[0x1000+i])
		}
	}
	if r.s.IFlags(true)&(1<<IRQCardIO) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("card transfer-complete IRQ not raised")
	}
}

func TestAuxSPIEEPROM(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	w := func(addr uint32, size int, v uint32) { r.v9.Write(addr, size, v) }
	w(0x040001A0, 2, 0x40) // hold chip select
	w(0x040001A2, 1, 0x06) // WREN
	w(0x040001A2, 1, 0x02) // WRITE
	w(0x040001A2, 1, 0x10) // address
	w(0x040001A2, 1, 0xAA) // data
	w(0x040001A2, 1, 0xBB) // data
	w(0x040001A0, 2, 0x00) // end transaction
	if r.s.SaveRAM()[0x10] != 0xAA || r.s.SaveRAM()[0x11] != 0xBB {
		t.Fatalf("save RAM: %02x %02x", r.s.SaveRAM()[0x10], r.s.SaveRAM()[0x11])
	}
	w(0x040001A0, 2, 0x40)
	w(0x040001A2, 1, 0x03) // READ
	w(0x040001A2, 1, 0x10) // address
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x040001A2, 1); got != 0xAA {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROM read 1: %02x", got)
	}
	if got := r.v9.Read(0x040001A2, 1); got != 0xBB {
		t.Fatalf("EEPROM read 2: %02x", got)
	}
}

func TestSPITouchAndFirmware(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	// Touchscreen: X channel control 0xD0, ADC for x=100.
	r.v7.Write(0x040001C0, 2, 0x8240)
	r.v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, 0xD0)
	r.v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, 0)
	b1 := r.v7.Read(0x040001C2, 1)
	r.v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, 0)
	b2 := r.v7.Read(0x040001C2, 1)
	if adc := (b1<<8 | b2) >> 3; adc != 0x67D {
		t.Fatalf("touch X ADC: %03x want 67d (b1 %02x b2 %02x)", adc, b1, b2)
	}
	// Firmware: read the settings version byte at 0x3FE00.
	r.v7.Write(0x040001C0, 2, 0x0000)
	r.v7.Write(0x040001C0, 2, 0x8140)
	for _, b := range []byte{0x03, 0x03, 0xFE, 0x00} {
		r.v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, uint32(b))
	}
	r.v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, 0)
	if got := r.v7.Read(0x040001C2, 1); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("firmware settings version: %02x want 05", got)
	}
}

func TestFirmwareSettingsBlock(t *testing.T) {
	fw := buildFirmware()
	if len(fw) != FirmwareSize {
		t.Fatalf("firmware size %d", len(fw))
	}
	blk := fw[SettingsOffset : SettingsOffset+0x100]
	if blk[0] != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("settings version %d", blk[0])
	}
	crc := uint16(blk[0x70]) | uint16(blk[0x71])<<8
	if crc != crc16Settings(blk[:0x70]) {
		t.Fatal("settings CRC mismatch")
	}
	dup := fw[SettingsOffset+0x100 : SettingsOffset+0x200]
	if !bytes.Equal(blk, dup) {
		t.Fatal("duplicate settings block differs")
	}
	if got := uint16(blk[0x58]) | uint16(blk[0x59])<<8; got != 0x0200 {
		t.Fatalf("calibration ADC X1: %04x", got)
	}
}

func TestRTCStub(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	if got := r.v7.Read(0x04000138, 1); got != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("RTC seconds at epoch: %02x", got)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 60; i++ {
		r.s.FrameTick()
	}
	if r.s.IFlags(false)&(1<<IRQRTC) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("RTC IRQ not raised after one second")
	}
	r.v7.Write(0x04000138, 1, 0) // reset read index
	if got := r.v7.Read(0x04000138, 1); got != 0x01 {
		t.Fatalf("RTC seconds after 60 frames: %02x want 01", got)
	}
}

func TestPeriphStateRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.v9.Write(0x04000100, 2, 1234)
	r.v9.Write(0x04000102, 2, 0xC1)
	r.s.AdvanceTimers(true, 5000)
	r.v9.Write(0x04000184, 4, 0x8000)
	r.v9.Write(0x04000188, 4, 0xFEEDFACE)
	r.s.rtc.frames = 77
	r.s.SaveRAM()[3] = 0x5A
	blob := make([]byte, StateSize)
	if n := r.s.Serialize(blob); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("serialize n = %d want %d", n, StateSize)
	}
	r2 := newRig()
	if n := r2.s.Deserialize(blob); n != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("deserialize n = %d want %d", n, StateSize)
	}
	blob2 := make([]byte, StateSize)
	r2.s.Serialize(blob2)
	if !bytes.Equal(blob, blob2) {
		t.Fatal("state bytes differ after round trip")
	}
	if got := r2.v9.Read(0x04000100, 2); got != r.v9.Read(0x04000100, 2) {
		t.Fatalf("timer counter restored: %d", got)
	}
	if got := r2.v7.Read(0x04100000, 4); got != 0xFEEDFACE {
		t.Fatalf("FIFO word restored: %08x", got)
	}
	if r2.s.rtc.frames != 77 || r2.s.SaveRAM()[3] != 0x5A {
		t.Fatal("scalar state not restored")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/rtc.go ====================

package periph

// RTC is the real-time clock stub on the ARM7 IO page at
// 0x04000138. The real chip is a bit-serial device behind a
// 4-bit port; this slice implements a deliberately simplified
// byte model, documented as such: reads cycle through a 7-byte
// BCD block (second, minute, hour, weekday, day, month, year)
// and any write resets the read index. The clock starts at
// the fixed epoch 2000-01-01 00:00:00 and advances one second
// per 60 frames; each elapsed second raises the ARM7 RTC
// interrupt once.
type RTC struct {
	frames uint64
	idx    uint8
}

var daysInMonth = [12]int{31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31}

func leap(y int) bool { return y%4 == 0 && (y%100 != 0 || y%400 == 0) }

// Time returns the current clock as (year since 2000, month,
// day, weekday 0=Sunday, hour, minute, second).
func (r *RTC) Time() (int, int, int, int, int, int, int) {
	sec := r.frames / 60
	year, days := 0, int(sec/86400)
	for {
		dy := 365
		if leap(2000 + year) {
			dy = 366
		}
		if days < dy {
			break
		}
		days -= dy
		year++
	}
	month := 0
	for {
		dm := daysInMonth[month]
		if month == 1 && leap(2000+year) {
			dm = 29
		}
		if days < dm {
			break
		}
		days -= dm
		month++
	}
	// 2000-01-01 was a Saturday (weekday 6).
	weekday := (6 + int(sec/86400)) % 7
	sod := int(sec % 86400)
	return year, month + 1, days + 1, weekday, sod / 3600, (sod / 60) % 60, sod % 60
}

func bcd(v int) byte { return byte(v/10)<<4 | byte(v%10) }

// read returns the next byte of the BCD block.
func (r *RTC) read() byte {
	year, month, day, weekday, hour, min, sec := r.Time()
	block := [7]byte{
		bcd(sec), bcd(min), bcd(hour), bcd(weekday),
		bcd(day), bcd(month), bcd(year),
	}
	b := block[r.idx%7]
	r.idx++
	return b
}

// write resets the read index (any write; the serial command
// protocol is not modeled in this slice).
func (r *RTC) write() { r.idx = 0 }

// tick advances the clock by one frame and reports whether a
// second elapsed (the system raises the RTC IRQ then).
func (r *RTC) tick() bool {
	r.frames++
	return r.frames%60 == 0
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/spi.go ====================

package periph

// SPI is the ARM7 SPI bus behind SPICNT (0x040001C0) and
// SPIDATA (0x040001C2). Transfers are instant: the busy bit
// always reads 0, each SPIDATA write performs one byte exchange
// with the selected device and latches the response byte,
// which the next SPIDATA read returns. Devices: 0 power
// management (reads 0, writes ignored), 1 firmware flash (the
// generated block from firmware.go; read commands stream it,
// write commands are ignored), 2 touchscreen controller.
// Baud bits are ignored because exchanges are instant. The
// documented transfer-size bit is treated as byte mode only.
// The SPI IRQ (ARM7 bit 24) raises per completed byte when
// SPICNT bit 11 is set.
type SPI struct {
	cnt    uint16
	resp   byte
	fw     []byte // generated firmware image, owned by the Set
	fwAdr  uint32 // 24-bit flash read pointer
	fwFast bool   // fast-read command: a dummy byte precedes data
	fwPh   uint8  // 0 command, 1-3 address, 4 dummy (fast read), 5 data, 6 status
	tscPh  uint8  // 0 control, 1 first data byte, 2 second data byte
	tscADC uint16
}

func (sp *SPI) read(rel, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch rel {
	case 0:
		return getU32(uint32(sp.cnt), off, size)
	case 2:
		return uint32(sp.resp)
	}
	return 0
}

func (sp *SPI) write(rel, off uint32, size int, val uint32, s *Set) {
	switch rel {
	case 0:
		old := sp.cnt
		sp.cnt = uint16(putU32(uint32(sp.cnt), off, size, val))
		if sp.cnt&0x8000 == 0 || (sp.cnt^old)&0x0300 != 0 {
			// Deselecting or switching devices restarts the
			// device protocols.
			sp.fwPh, sp.tscPh = 0, 0
		}
	case 2:
		if sp.cnt&0x8000 == 0 {
			return
		}
		sp.resp = sp.exchange(byte(val), s)
		if sp.cnt&0x0800 != 0 {
			s.Raise(false, IRQSPI)
		}
	}
}

func (sp *SPI) exchange(b byte, s *Set) byte {
	switch (sp.cnt >> 8) & 3 {
	case 1:
		return sp.fwExchange(b)
	case 2:
		return sp.tscExchange(b, s)
	}
	return 0 // power management and the unused device 3
}

// fwExchange runs the firmware flash read protocol: command
// 0x03 (read) or 0x0B (fast read) followed by a 24-bit
// address, then data bytes stream out, wrapping inside the
// flash image. Command 0x05 (read status) returns 0. All
// write-class commands are ignored: the flash is generated,
// never programmed.
func (sp *SPI) fwExchange(b byte) byte {
	switch sp.fwPh {
	case 0:
		switch b {
		case 0x03:
			sp.fwAdr, sp.fwFast, sp.fwPh = 0, false, 1
		case 0x0B:
			sp.fwAdr, sp.fwFast, sp.fwPh = 0, true, 1
		case 0x05:
			sp.fwPh = 6
		}
		return 0
	case 1, 2, 3:
		sp.fwAdr = (sp.fwAdr<<8 | uint32(b)) & 0xFFFFFF
		sp.fwPh++
		if sp.fwPh == 4 {
			if sp.fwFast {
				sp.fwPh = 4 // dummy phase next
			} else {
				sp.fwPh = 5
			}
		}
		return 0
	case 4: // fast-read dummy byte
		sp.fwPh = 5
		return 0
	case 5:
		v := sp.fw[sp.fwAdr%uint32(len(sp.fw))]
		sp.fwAdr = (sp.fwAdr + 1) & 0xFFFFFF
		return v
	case 6:
		return 0 // status: never busy, never write-enabled
	}
	return 0
}

// tscExchange runs the touchscreen controller protocol. The
// first byte after select is the control byte (bit 7 set,
// channel in bits 6-4); the next two byte exchanges return
// the 12-bit ADC value split as (adc>>5) then (adc&0x1F)<<3,
// so adc = ((b1<<8)|b2)>>3. Channel 1 is Y, channel 5 is X.
// With the pen up the ADC reads 0. Channel 6 is the
// microphone aux input (DS-3): each control byte consumes
// one sample from the machine's microphone source, converted
// from int16 to the 12-bit ADC scale around the idle center
// value 0x800, which is also what reads return when no
// source is installed or it is exhausted.
func (sp *SPI) tscExchange(b byte, s *Set) byte {
	switch sp.tscPh {
	case 0:
		x, y, down := s.touch()
		sp.tscADC = 0
		switch (b >> 4) & 7 {
		case 1:
			if down {
				sp.tscADC = adcFromCoord(uint32(y), 191)
			}
		case 5:
			if down {
				sp.tscADC = adcFromCoord(uint32(x), 255)
			}
		case 6:
			sp.tscADC = 0x800
			if s.mic != nil {
				if v, ok := s.mic(); ok {
					adc := int32(v>>4) + 0x800
					if adc < 0 {
						adc = 0
					}
					if adc > 0xFFF {
						adc = 0xFFF
					}
					sp.tscADC = uint16(adc)
				}
			}
		}
		sp.tscPh = 1
		return 0
	case 1:
		sp.tscPh = 2
		return byte(sp.tscADC >> 5)
	case 2:
		sp.tscPh = 0
		return byte(sp.tscADC&0x1F) << 3
	}
	return 0
}

// adcFromCoord converts a screen pixel coordinate to the
// 12-bit ADC scale of the generated calibration: screen edge
// low maps to 0x100 and the far edge to 0xF00, a documented
// linear map consistent with the firmware calibration block.
func adcFromCoord(coord, max uint32) uint16 {
	if coord > max {
		coord = max
	}
	return uint16(0x100 + (coord*0xE00)/max)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/state.go ====================

package periph

// StateSize is the serialized size of the whole peripheral
// set. The generated firmware image is not serialized: it is
// rebuilt identically by New.
const StateSize = 24 + 96 + 112 + 112 + 148 + 28 + 524 + 12 + 12 + 4

// Serialize writes the device state into dst (at least
// StateSize bytes) and returns the byte count.
func (s *Set) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	w := &stateWriter{b: dst}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w.u32(s.irq[i].ime)
		w.u32(s.irq[i].ie)
		w.u32(s.irq[i].iflags)
	}
	for side := 0; side < 2; side++ {
		for t := 0; t < 4; t++ {
			tm := &s.tim[side][t]
			w.u16(tm.reload)
			w.u16(tm.ctrl)
			w.u16(tm.counter)
			w.u32(tm.sub)
			w.u16(0)
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		ch := &s.dm9[i]
		w.u32(ch.sad)
		w.u32(ch.dad)
		w.u32(ch.cnt)
		w.u32(ch.src)
		w.u32(ch.dst)
		w.u32(ch.remain)
		w.flag(ch.armed)
		w.bytes([]byte{0, 0, 0})
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		ch := &s.dm7[i]
		w.u32(ch.sad)
		w.u32(ch.dad)
		w.u16(ch.cntL)
		w.u16(ch.cntH)
		w.u32(ch.src)
		w.u32(ch.dst)
		w.u32(ch.remain)
		w.flag(ch.armed)
		w.bytes([]byte{0, 0, 0})
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w.u8(s.ipc.syncOut[i])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w.flag(s.ipc.syncIRQEn[i])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w.flag(s.ipc.cntEn[i])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w.flag(s.ipc.sendEmptyIE[i])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w.flag(s.ipc.recvNotEmptyIE[i])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		w.flag(s.ipc.err[i])
	}
	for d := 0; d < 2; d++ {
		for k := 0; k < 16; k++ {
			w.u32(s.ipc.fifo[d][k])
		}
		w.u8(uint8(s.ipc.head[d]))
		w.u8(uint8(s.ipc.count[d]))
		w.bytes([]byte{0, 0})
	}
	w.bytes(s.crd.cmd[:])
	w.u32(s.crd.romctrl)
	w.u32(s.crd.srcOff)
	w.u32(s.crd.srcLen)
	w.u32(uint32(s.crd.pos))
	w.u8(s.crd.kind)
	w.flag(s.crd.active)
	w.bytes([]byte{0, 0})
	w.u16(s.aux.cnt)
	w.u8(s.aux.state)
	w.flag(s.aux.wel)
	w.u32(s.aux.addr)
	w.flag(s.aux.wr)
	w.u8(uint8(s.aux.hi))
	w.bytes([]byte{0, 0})
	w.bytes(s.aux.save[:])
	w.u16(s.spi.cnt)
	w.u8(s.spi.resp)
	w.u8(s.spi.fwPh)
	w.u32(s.spi.fwAdr)
	w.flag(s.spi.fwFast)
	w.u8(s.spi.tscPh)
	w.u16(s.spi.tscADC)
	w.u64(s.rtc.frames)
	w.u8(s.rtc.idx)
	w.bytes([]byte{0, 0, 0})
	w.flag(s.penDn)
	w.bytes([]byte{0, 0, 0})
	return w.n
}

// Deserialize restores the device state from src and returns
// the byte count consumed.
func (s *Set) Deserialize(src []byte) int {
	r := &stateReader{b: src}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.irq[i].ime = r.u32()
		s.irq[i].ie = r.u32()
		s.irq[i].iflags = r.u32()
	}
	for side := 0; side < 2; side++ {
		for t := 0; t < 4; t++ {
			tm := &s.tim[side][t]
			tm.reload = r.u16()
			tm.ctrl = r.u16()
			tm.counter = r.u16()
			tm.sub = r.u32()
			r.u16()
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		ch := &s.dm9[i]
		ch.sad = r.u32()
		ch.dad = r.u32()
		ch.cnt = r.u32()
		ch.src = r.u32()
		ch.dst = r.u32()
		ch.remain = r.u32()
		ch.armed = r.flag()
		r.bytes(make([]byte, 3))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		ch := &s.dm7[i]
		ch.sad = r.u32()
		ch.dad = r.u32()
		ch.cntL = r.u16()
		ch.cntH = r.u16()
		ch.src = r.u32()
		ch.dst = r.u32()
		ch.remain = r.u32()
		ch.armed = r.flag()
		r.bytes(make([]byte, 3))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.ipc.syncOut[i] = r.u8()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.ipc.syncIRQEn[i] = r.flag()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.ipc.cntEn[i] = r.flag()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.ipc.sendEmptyIE[i] = r.flag()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.ipc.recvNotEmptyIE[i] = r.flag()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		s.ipc.err[i] = r.flag()
	}
	for d := 0; d < 2; d++ {
		for k := 0; k < 16; k++ {
			s.ipc.fifo[d][k] = r.u32()
		}
		s.ipc.head[d] = int(r.u8())
		s.ipc.count[d] = int(r.u8())
		r.bytes(make([]byte, 2))
	}
	r.bytes(s.crd.cmd[:])
	s.crd.romctrl = r.u32()
	s.crd.srcOff = r.u32()
	s.crd.srcLen = r.u32()
	s.crd.pos = int(r.u32())
	s.crd.kind = r.u8()
	s.crd.active = r.flag()
	r.bytes(make([]byte, 2))
	// The prepared block's bytes are re-derived from the ROM;
	// the machine contract requires the same ROM loaded.
	s.crd.rebuild(s.rom())
	s.aux.cnt = r.u16()
	s.aux.state = r.u8()
	s.aux.wel = r.flag()
	s.aux.addr = r.u32()
	s.aux.wr = r.flag()
	s.aux.hi = uint32(r.u8())
	r.bytes(make([]byte, 2))
	r.bytes(s.aux.save[:])
	s.spi.cnt = r.u16()
	s.spi.resp = r.u8()
	s.spi.fwPh = r.u8()
	s.spi.fwAdr = r.u32()
	s.spi.fwFast = r.flag()
	s.spi.tscPh = r.u8()
	s.spi.tscADC = r.u16()
	s.rtc.frames = r.u64()
	s.rtc.idx = r.u8()
	r.bytes(make([]byte, 3))
	s.penDn = r.flag()
	r.bytes(make([]byte, 3))
	return r.n
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/periph/timers.go ====================

package periph

// Timer is one GBA-style DS timer channel. The register pair is
// CNT_L (reload value; reads return the live counter) and CNT_H
// (prescaler select, cascade, IRQ enable, start). Both CPUs use
// this identical implementation at their own bus pages.
//
// Two documented choices: writing CNT_L loads the counter from
// the reload value immediately (not only at the next overflow),
// and starting the timer (CNT_H bit 7 rising) resets both the
// counter and the prescaler remainder.
type Timer struct {
	reload  uint16
	ctrl    uint16
	counter uint16
	sub     uint32 // prescaler remainder, in CPU cycles
}

var prescalerShift = [4]uint{0, 6, 8, 10} // F/1, F/64, F/256, F/1024

// advance moves the timer by the given CPU cycles plus cascade
// ticks taken from the previous timer's overflows. It returns
// this timer's overflow count.
func (t *Timer) advance(cycles, cascade int) int {
	if t.ctrl&0x80 == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	var ticks int
	if t.ctrl&0x04 != 0 {
		ticks = cascade
	} else {
		sh := prescalerShift[t.ctrl&3]
		t.sub += uint32(cycles)
		ticks = int(t.sub >> sh)
		t.sub &= (1 << sh) - 1
	}
	if ticks == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	period := 0x10000 - int(t.reload)
	pos := int(t.counter) - int(t.reload)
	if pos < 0 {
		// The reload value was raised above the counter after
		// the counter was latched; count from the bottom.
		pos = 0
	}
	total := pos + ticks
	t.counter = uint16(int(t.reload) + total%period)
	return total / period
}

// AdvanceTimers runs one side's four timers for the given
// number of executed CPU cycles, chaining cascade ticks and
// raising overflow interrupts.
func (s *Set) AdvanceTimers(nine bool, cycles int) {
	side := sideIdx(nine)
	ov := 0
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		ov = s.tim[side][i].advance(cycles, ov)
		if ov > 0 && s.tim[side][i].ctrl&0x40 != 0 {
			s.Raise(nine, IRQTimer0+uint(i))
		}
	}
}

// readReg serves a read of the timer's 4-byte register slot at
// the given byte lane.
func (t *Timer) readReg(lane uint32, size int) uint32 {
	v := uint32(t.counter) | uint32(t.ctrl)<<16
	return getU32(v, lane, size)
}

// writeReg serves a write of the timer's register slot. CNT_L
// writes update the reload and the live counter; CNT_H writes
// update the control, and a start rising edge latches the
// counter from the reload value.
func (t *Timer) writeReg(lane uint32, size int, val uint32) {
	old := t.ctrl
	// Compose the post-write 32-bit register image, applying
	// the write to the reload and control halves separately.
	lo := putU32(uint32(t.reload), lane, size, val)
	hi := putU32(uint32(t.ctrl)<<16, lane, size, val) >> 16
	touchedLo := size == 4 || lane < 2
	touchedHi := size == 4 || lane >= 2
	if touchedLo {
		t.reload = uint16(lo)
		t.counter = t.reload
	}
	if touchedHi {
		t.ctrl = uint16(hi)
		if old&0x80 == 0 && t.ctrl&0x80 != 0 {
			t.counter = t.reload
			t.sub = 0
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/system/boot.go ====================

package system

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/chips/armcore"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/periph"
)

// Direct boot, following the GBATEK direct-boot
// initialization: no BIOS runs, so the machine itself
// performs the documented setup the BIOS would have done.
//
//   - The ARM9 binary is staged through the ARM9 view with
//     WRAMCNT = 3 (all shared WRAM owned by the ARM9), then
//     the ARM7 binary through the ARM7 view with WRAMCNT = 0
//     (all shared WRAM owned by the ARM7). WRAMCNT is left at
//     0: at boot the shared WRAM belongs to the ARM7 and
//     games reprogram it (documented choice).
//   - The 0x200-byte cartridge header is copied to
//     0x027FFE00, the chip ID to 0x027FF800 and 0x027FF804,
//     the header bytes 0x20-0x3F to 0x027FFC00, and the boot
//     flag halfword 0x0001 to 0x027FFFFA.
//   - POWCNT1 is set to 0x020F (LCDs on, 2D engines on, 3D
//     engine on, displays not swapped).
//   - Each CPU's entry register state: CPSR = system mode
//     with interrupts enabled in the CPSR (the global IME is
//     still 0, so no interrupt can fire until the program
//     enables it), SVC stack 0x03007FE0 / IRQ stack
//     0x03007FA0 on the ARM9 (0x0380FDC0 / 0x0380FD80 on the
//     ARM7), user stack at the end of the ARM9 binary's load
//     region (0x0380FE00 on the ARM7), and r12 = r14 = the
//     CPU's header entry point. CP15 keeps the power-on TCM
//     configuration installed by reset.
//   - The CPUs stay halted until Start.

// Documented direct-boot stack addresses.
const (
	bootSVCStack9 = 0x03007FE0
	bootIRQStack9 = 0x03007FA0
	bootSVCStack7 = 0x0380FDC0
	bootIRQStack7 = 0x0380FD80
	bootUSRStack7 = 0x0380FE00
)

func (m *Machine) directBoot() {
	h := m.header
	m.Bus.SetROM(m.rom)
	m.CPU9.Reset()
	m.CPU7.Reset()
	m.CPU9.Halted = true
	m.CPU7.Halted = true

	if h.ARM9Size > 0 {
		m.Bus.SetWRAMCNT(3)
		m.Bus.LoadBytes(true, h.ARM9Load, h.ARM9Binary(m.rom))
	}
	if h.ARM7Size > 0 {
		m.Bus.SetWRAMCNT(0)
		m.Bus.LoadBytes(false, h.ARM7Load, h.ARM7Binary(m.rom))
	}
	m.Bus.SetWRAMCNT(0)

	// The boot block in main RAM.
	w8 := func(addr uint32, b []byte) { m.Bus.LoadBytes(true, addr, b) }
	hdr := make([]byte, 0x200)
	copy(hdr, m.rom)
	w8(0x027FFE00, hdr)
	id := periph.ChipID
	w8(0x027FF800, []byte{byte(id), byte(id >> 8), byte(id >> 16), byte(id >> 24)})
	w8(0x027FF804, []byte{byte(id), byte(id >> 8), byte(id >> 16), byte(id >> 24)})
	w8(0x027FFC00, m.rom[0x20:0x40])
	w8(0x027FFFFA, []byte{0x01, 0x00})

	// POWCNT1: LCDs and both 2D engines (and the 3D engine
	// power bit) on, no swap.
	m.Bus.IO9[0x304] = 0x0F
	m.Bus.IO9[0x305] = 0x02

	m.bootRegs(m.CPU9, h.ARM9Entry, h.ARM9Load+h.ARM9Size, bootSVCStack9, bootIRQStack9)
	m.bootRegs(m.CPU7, h.ARM7Entry, bootUSRStack7, bootSVCStack7, bootIRQStack7)
}

// bootRegs installs one CPU's entry register state. The banked
// stack pointers go into the armcore bank fields; the active
// (system mode) stack pointer and the link register hold the
// user stack and the entry address, and r12 holds the entry
// address as well, per the boot contract.
func (m *Machine) bootRegs(c *armcore.CPU, entry, usrSP, svcSP, irqSP uint32) {
	c.RSVC[0] = svcSP
	c.RSVC[1] = 0
	c.RIRQ[0] = irqSP
	c.RIRQ[1] = 0
	c.RUSR[0] = usrSP
	c.RUSR[1] = entry
	c.R[12] = entry
	c.R[13] = usrSP
	c.R[14] = entry
	c.CPSR = armcore.ModeSYS
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/system/ds2_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/periph"
)

// buildROM assembles a synthetic cartridge with the given
// hand-assembled programs: ARM9 loads at 0x02000000, ARM7 at
// 0x03800000, entries at the load addresses.
func buildROM(arm9prog, arm7prog []uint32) []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x4000)
	copy(rom[0x000:], "DS2 PROOF")
	copy(rom[0x00C:], "ADSP")
	copy(rom[0x010:], "01")
	le := binary.LittleEndian
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x020:], 0x1000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x024:], 0x02000000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x028:], 0x02000000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x02C:], uint32(len(arm9prog)*4))
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x030:], 0x2000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x034:], 0x03800000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x038:], 0x03800000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x03C:], uint32(len(arm7prog)*4))
	for i, w := range arm9prog {
		le.PutUint32(rom[0x1000+i*4:], w)
	}
	for i, w := range arm7prog {
		le.PutUint32(rom[0x2000+i*4:], w)
	}
	return rom
}

func spin() []uint32 { return []uint32{0xEAFFFFFE} } // B .

func ramWord(m *Machine, addr uint32) uint32 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(m.Bus.MainRAM[addr-0x02000000:])
}

// TestDirectBootGate: the ARM9 program verifies the boot flag
// halfword at 0x027FFFFA and its own user stack pointer
// against the value direct boot installed (load + size), then
// writes a success magic. The ARM7 program verifies its stack
// pointer and link register, then answers over the IPC FIFO.
func TestDirectBootGate(t *testing.T) {
	arm9 := []uint32{
		0xE59F0038, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x38] -> 0x027FFFFA
		0xE1D010B0, // LDRH R1, [R0]
		0xE3510001, // CMP R1, #1
		0x1A000007, // BNE fail
		0xE1A0300D, // MOV R3, SP
		0xE59F4028, // LDR R4, [PC, #0x28] -> expected SP
		0xE1530004, // CMP R3, R4
		0x1A000003, // BNE fail
		0xE59F5020, // LDR R5, [PC, #0x20] -> result addr
		0xE59F6020, // LDR R6, [PC, #0x20] -> success magic
		0xE5856000, // STR R6, [R5]
		0xEAFFFFFE, // B .
		0xE59F5010, // fail: LDR R5, [PC, #0x10] -> result addr
		0xE59F6014, // LDR R6, [PC, #0x14] -> bad magic
		0xE5856000, // STR R6, [R5]
		0xEAFFFFFE, // B .
		0x027FFFFA, // literal 0
		0x02000054, // literal 1: load 0x02000000 + 21 words * 4
		0x02010000, // literal 2: result address
		0x600D600D, // literal 3: success magic
		0x0BAD0BAD, // literal 4: bad magic
	}
	if len(arm9) != 21 {
		t.Fatalf("arm9 program is %d words, layout math wants 21", len(arm9))
	}
	arm7 := []uint32{
		0xE1A0300D, // MOV R3, SP
		0xE59F4040, // LDR R4, [PC, #0x40] -> expected SP 0x0380FE00
		0xE1530004, // CMP R3, R4
		0x1A00000A, // BNE fail
		0xE1A0500E, // MOV R5, LR
		0xE59F6034, // LDR R6, [PC, #0x34] -> entry 0x03800000
		0xE1550006, // CMP R5, R6
		0x1A000006, // BNE fail
		0xE59F002C, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x2C] -> FIFOCNT addr
		0xE59F102C, // LDR R1, [PC, #0x2C] -> 0x8000
		0xE5801000, // STR R1, [R0]
		0xE59F0028, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x28] -> FIFOSEND addr
		0xE59F1028, // LDR R1, [PC, #0x28] -> magic
		0xE5801000, // STR R1, [R0]
		0xEAFFFFFE, // B .
		0xE59F0020, // fail: LDR R0, [PC, #0x20] -> result addr
		0xE59F1020, // LDR R1, [PC, #0x20] -> bad magic
		0xE5801000, // STR R1, [R0]
		0xEAFFFFFE, // B .
		0x0380FE00, // literal: expected SP
		0x03800000, // literal: entry
		0x04000184, // literal: FIFOCNT
		0x00008000, // literal: FIFO enable
		0x04000188, // literal: FIFOSEND
		0xCAFEBABE, // literal: answer magic
		0x02010004, // literal: result address
		0x0D15EA5E, // literal: bad magic
	}
	if len(arm7) != 27 {
		t.Fatalf("arm7 program is %d words, layout math wants 27", len(arm7))
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(buildROM(arm9, arm7)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.Start()
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	if got := ramWord(m, 0x02010000); got != 0x600D600D {
		t.Fatalf("ARM9 boot check: %08x want 600D600D", got)
	}
	if got := ramWord(m, 0x02010004); got == 0x0D15EA5E {
		t.Fatal("ARM7 boot check wrote the failure magic")
	}
	// The ARM7's answer is waiting in the IPC FIFO.
	v9 := m.Bus.ARM9()
	v9.Write(0x04000184, 4, 0x8000)
	if got := v9.Read(0x04100000, 4); got != 0xCAFEBABE {
		t.Fatalf("ARM7 IPC answer: %08x want CAFEBABE", got)
	}
}

// TestBootBlock checks the documented boot block fields
// directly after LoadROM.
func TestBootBlock(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(buildROM(spin(), spin())); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ram := m.Bus.MainRAM
	off := func(a uint32) int { return int((a - 0x02000000) & (4<<20 - 1)) }
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ram[off(0x027FF800):]); got != periph.ChipID {
		t.Fatalf("chip ID at 027FF800: %08x", got)
	}
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(ram[off(0x027FFFFA):]); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("boot flag: %04x", got)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(ram[off(0x027FFE00):off(0x027FFE00)+9], []byte("DS2 PROOF")) {
		t.Fatal("header copy at 027FFE00 missing")
	}
	if got := uint16(m.Bus.IO9[0x304]) | uint16(m.Bus.IO9[0x305])<<8; got != 0x020F {
		t.Fatalf("POWCNT1: %04x", got)
	}
	if m.CPU9.R[13] != 0x02000000+4 { // spin() is one word
		t.Fatalf("ARM9 user SP: %08x", m.CPU9.R[13])
	}
	if m.CPU7.R[13] != 0x0380FE00 || m.CPU7.RSVC[0] != 0x0380FDC0 || m.CPU7.RIRQ[0] != 0x0380FD80 {
		t.Fatalf("ARM7 stacks: sp %08x svc %08x irq %08x",
			m.CPU7.R[13], m.CPU7.RSVC[0], m.CPU7.RIRQ[0])
	}
	if m.CPU9.R[12] != 0x02000000 || m.CPU9.R[14] != 0x02000000 {
		t.Fatal("ARM9 entry registers r12/r14 wrong")
	}
}

// TestVBlankHandlerCount: an ARM9 IRQ handler installed in
// ITCM (the vector branch range cannot reach main RAM, as on
// hardware), reached through a branch planted at the IRQ
// vector, counts VBlanks in RAM and acknowledges IF.
func TestVBlankHandlerCount(t *testing.T) {
	main := []uint32{
		0xE59F002C, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x2C] -> handler addr (unused beyond setup symmetry)
		0xE3A01018, // MOV R1, #0x18 (ITCM IRQ vector)
		0xE59F2028, // LDR R2, [PC, #0x28] -> branch word
		0xE5812000, // STR R2, [R1]
		0xE59F0024, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x24] -> IME addr
		0xE3A01001, // MOV R1, #1
		0xE5801000, // STR R1, [R0]  IME = 1
		0xE59F001C, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x1C] -> IE addr
		0xE5801000, // STR R1, [R0]  IE = VBlank
		0xE59F0018, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x18] -> DISPSTAT addr
		0xE3A01008, // MOV R1, #8
		0xE5801000, // STR R1, [R0]  DISPSTAT VBlank IRQ enable
		0xEAFFFFFE, // B .
		0x00000040, // literal: handler address in ITCM
		0xEA000008, // literal: B from 0x18 to 0x40
		0x04000208, // literal: IME
		0x04000210, // literal: IE
		0x04000004, // literal: DISPSTAT
	}
	handler := []uint32{
		0xE59F0018, // LDR R0, [PC, #0x18] -> count addr
		0xE5901000, // LDR R1, [R0]
		0xE2811001, // ADD R1, R1, #1
		0xE5801000, // STR R1, [R0]
		0xE59F200C, // LDR R2, [PC, #0x0C] -> IF addr
		0xE3A03001, // MOV R3, #1
		0xE5823000, // STR R3, [R2]  ack VBlank
		0xE25EF004, // SUBS PC, LR, #4
		0x02000200, // literal: count address
		0x04000214, // literal: IF
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(buildROM(main, spin())); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.Bus.LoadBytes(true, 0x00000040, words(handler))
	m.Start9()
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := ramWord(m, 0x02000200); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("VBlank handler count: %d want 5", got)
	}
}

func words(ws []uint32) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, len(ws)*4)
	for i, w := range ws {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[i*4:], w)
	}
	return out
}

// TestARM7TimerIRQIndependence: the ARM7 timer 0 raises its
// IRQ while the ARM9 stays fully masked, proving the two
// interrupt controllers are independent.
func TestARM7TimerIRQIndependence(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(buildROM(spin(), spin())); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v7 := m.Bus.ARM7()
	// Reload 5865-tick period at F/64: about two overflows in
	// three frames of ARM7 cycles.
	v7.Write(0x04000100, 2, 0x10000-5865)
	v7.Write(0x04000102, 2, 0xC1) // start, IRQ on, F/64
	v7.Write(0x04000210, 4, 1<<periph.IRQTimer0)
	v7.Write(0x04000208, 4, 1) // IME7 = 1; ARM9 IME/IE stay 0
	m.Start()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	if m.Periph.IFlags(false)&(1<<periph.IRQTimer0) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("ARM7 timer IRQ never raised")
	}
	if !m.Periph.PendingIRQ(false) {
		t.Fatal("ARM7 IRQ line not pending")
	}
	if m.Periph.IFlags(true) != 0 || m.Periph.PendingIRQ(true) {
		t.Fatalf("ARM9 side disturbed: IF %08x", m.Periph.IFlags(true))
	}
}

// TestDMAGXFIFO: a GX FIFO timing channel fires at frame
// start and the sink counts the words; a plain CPU write to
// the FIFO port counts too.
func TestDMAGXFIFO(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(buildROM(spin(), spin())); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v9 := m.Bus.ARM9()
	m.Bus.LoadBytes(true, 0x02001000, make([]byte, 64))
	v9.Write(0x040000B0, 4, 0x02001000)
	v9.Write(0x040000B4, 4, 0x04000400)
	v9.Write(0x040000B8, 4, 0xBC400008) // enable, GX timing, fixed dest, 32-bit, 8 words
	m.RunFrame()
	if got := m.GXFIFOCount(); got != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("GX sink after frame: %d want 8", got)
	}
	v9.Write(0x04000400, 4, 0x12345678)
	if got := m.GXFIFOCount(); got != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("GX sink after CPU write: %d want 9", got)
	}
}

// sceneSetup builds the two-engine scene used by the swap and
// determinism gates through the bus views: engine A shows a
// red text tile, engine B a white one.
func sceneSetup(m *Machine) {
	v9 := m.Bus.ARM9()
	w16 := func(addr uint32, val uint32) { v9.Write(addr, 2, val) }
	w32 := func(addr uint32, val uint32) { v9.Write(addr, 4, val) }
	v9.Write(0x04000240, 1, 0x81) // VRAMCNT A: BG A
	v9.Write(0x04000248, 1, 0x81) // VRAMCNT H: BG B
	w32(0x04000000, 0x00010100)
	w16(0x04000008, 0x0204)
	w32(0x04001000, 0x00010100)
	w16(0x04001008, 0x0204)
	pal := func(off int, c uint16) {
		m.Bus.Palette[off] = byte(c)
		m.Bus.Palette[off+1] = byte(c >> 8)
	}
	pal(2, 0x001F)     // A palette 1: red
	pal(0x402, 0x7FFF) // B palette 1: white
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		m.Bus.VRAM[0x4000+32+i] = 0x11
		m.Bus.VRAM[0x98000+0x4000+32+i] = 0x11
	}
	m.Bus.VRAM[0x1000] = 1
	m.Bus.VRAM[0x98000+0x1000] = 1
	// A capture pass into bank D, blended with itself.
	w32(0x04000064, (1<<31)|(3<<20)|(3<<16)|(1<<24)|16)
}

// TestDisplaySwap: POWCNT1 swap exchanges which buffer
// Framebuffer returns first.
func TestDisplaySwap(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(buildROM(spin(), spin())); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sceneSetup(m)
	m.RunFrame()
	top, _ := m.Framebuffer()
	if top[0] != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("top before swap: %08x want engine A red", top[0])
	}
	m.Bus.IO9[0x305] |= 0x80
	top, bottom := m.Framebuffer()
	if top[0] != 0xFFFFFFFF || bottom[0] != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("after swap: top %08x bottom %08x", top[0], bottom[0])
	}
}

// TestDeterminismGate: direct boot, render a two-engine scene
// with a capture pass, save mid-run, restore into a fresh
// machine, and require identical framebuffers and state
// bytes after the same continuation.
func TestDeterminismGate(t *testing.T) {
	rom := buildROM(spin(), spin())
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sceneSetup(m)
	m.Start()
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	saved := m.Serialize()
	if len(saved) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size: %d want %d", len(saved), StateSize)
	}
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	topA, botA := m.Framebuffer()
	wantTop := append([]uint32(nil), topA...)
	wantBot := append([]uint32(nil), botA...)
	wantState := m.Serialize()
	if topA[0] != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("scene did not render: top %08x", topA[0])
	}
	// The capture pass must have written engine A pixels into
	// bank D during the run.
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(m.Bus.VRAMBank(3)); got == 0 {
		t.Fatal("capture bank D is empty")
	}

	f := New()
	if err := f.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	sceneSetup(f)
	f.Start()
	f.RunFrame()
	f.RunFrame()
	f.RunFrame()
	if !f.Deserialize(saved) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize refused the DS-2 state")
	}
	f.RunFrame()
	f.RunFrame()
	topB, botB := f.Framebuffer()
	if !uint32sEqual(topB, wantTop) || !uint32sEqual(botB, wantBot) {
		t.Fatal("restored run: framebuffers differ")
	}
	if got := f.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Fatal("restored run: state bytes differ")
	}
}

func uint32sEqual(a, b []uint32) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

package system_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"math"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/system"
)

// gxCmd sends one geometry command through its direct port
// on the ARM9 IO page.
func gxCmd(v bus.View, id uint8, params ...uint32) {
	port := uint32(0x04000400) + uint32(id)*4
	if len(params) == 0 {
		v.Write(port, 4, 0)
		return
	}
	for _, p := range params {
		v.Write(port, 4, p)
	}
}

func gxIdentity(v bus.View) {
	gxCmd(v, 0x10, 0) // MTX_MODE projection
	gxCmd(v, 0x15)    // MTX_IDENTITY
	gxCmd(v, 0x10, 1) // MTX_MODE position
	gxCmd(v, 0x15)
	gxCmd(v, 0x60, 0xBFFF0000) // VIEWPORT full screen
}

func gxVtx(v bus.View, x, y, z int) {
	gxCmd(v, 0x23, uint32(uint16(x))|uint32(uint16(y))<<16, uint32(uint16(z)))
}

// setupDisplay routes engine A BG0 to the 3D layer and
// assigns VRAM banks A (texture slot 0) and E (texture
// palette) for the geometry engine.
func setupDisplay(m *system.Machine) {
	v9 := m.Bus.ARM9()
	v9.Write(0x04000304, 2, 0x020F)     // POWCNT1
	v9.Write(0x04000000, 4, 0x00010108) // DISPCNT A: mode 1, BG0 on + 3D
	v9.Write(0x04000240, 1, 0x83)       // VRAMCNT A: texture image slot 0
	v9.Write(0x04000244, 1, 0x83)       // VRAMCNT E: texture palette
	v9.Write(0x04000354, 4, 0x7FFF)     // CLEAR_DEPTH far
}

func TestDS3ClipReadbackAndPosTest(t *testing.T) {
	m := system.New()
	v9 := m.Bus.ARM9()
	gxIdentity(v9)
	// A known projection matrix; identity position.
	mat := [16]uint32{0x1000, 0x0800, 0xFFFFF000, 3,
		0x2000, 0x1000, 0, 0xFFFFE000,
		1, 2, 3, 4,
		0x3000, 0xFFFFC000, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x1000}
	gxCmd(v9, 0x10, 0)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x16, mat[:]...)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x10, 1)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x15)
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if got := v9.Read(0x04000640+uint32(i*4), 4); got != mat[i] {
			t.Fatalf("CLIPMTX_RESULT[%d] = %08x want %08x", i, got, mat[i])
		}
	}
	// POS_TEST with a translated position matrix.
	gxIdentity(v9)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x1C, 0x800, 0xFFFFFC00, 0x2000)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x71, 0x1000, 0)
	want := [4]uint32{0x1800, 0xFFFFFC00, 0x2000, 0x1000}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		if got := v9.Read(0x04000620+uint32(i*4), 4); got != want[i] {
			t.Fatalf("POS_RESULT[%d] = %08x want %08x", i, got, want[i])
		}
	}
}

func TestDS3RedTriangleScreen(t *testing.T) {
	m := system.New()
	setupDisplay(m)
	v9 := m.Bus.ARM9()
	v9.Write(0x04000350, 4, 31<<16) // CLEAR_COLOR black opaque
	gxIdentity(v9)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x29, 31<<16|0xC0)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x20, 0x001F)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x40, 0)
	gxVtx(v9, -0x800, -0x800, 0)
	gxVtx(v9, 0x800, -0x800, 0)

	}

// ds3Scene builds the determinism scene: a textured far quad
// under a translucent flat near quad with fog on, plus a PCM
// loop tone and a PSG square, all poked through the bus.
func ds3Scene(m *system.Machine) {
	setupDisplay(m)
	v9 := m.Bus.ARM9()
	v7 := m.Bus.ARM7()
	// 8x8 256-color texture: a four-color checker in index
	// space; palette entries 1..4 are red, green, blue,
	// white.
	a := m.Bus.VRAMBank(0)
	for ty := 0; ty < 8; ty++ {
		for tx := 0; tx < 8; tx++ {
			a[ty*8+tx] = byte(1 + (tx+ty)%4)
		}
	}
	e := m.Bus.VRAMBank(4)
	for i, c := range []uint16{0x001F, 0x03E0, 0x7C00, 0x7FFF} {
		e[2+2*i] = byte(c)
		e[3+2*i] = byte(c >> 8)
	}
	// DISP3DCNT: texture on, alpha blending on, fog on.
	v9.Write(0x04000060, 2, 0x89)
	// CLEAR_COLOR: mid gray, opaque, fog flagged.
	v9.Write(0x04000350, 4, 0x2108|0x8000|31<<16)
	// FOG_COLOR dark blue, alpha 20; offset 0x1000; density
	// table ramps 0, 4, 8, ...
	v9.Write(0x04000358, 4, 0x4000|20<<16)
	v9.Write(0x0400035C, 4, 0x1000)
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		v9.Write(0x04000360+uint32(i), 1, uint32(i*4))
	}
	gxIdentity(v9)
	// Textured far quad.
	gxCmd(v9, 0x29, 31<<16|0xC0)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x20, 0x7FFF)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x2A, 4<<26)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x2B, 0)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x40, 1)
	quad := [][4]int{
		{-0x1000, -0x1000, 0, 128}, {0x1000, -0x1000, 128, 128},
		{0x1000, 0x1000, 128, 0}, {-0x1000, 0x1000, 0, 0},
	}
	for _, q := range quad {
		gxCmd(v9, 0x22, uint32(uint16(q[2]))|uint32(uint16(q[3]))<<16)
		gxVtx(v9, q[0], q[1], 0x400)
	}
	// Translucent flat near quad (magenta, alpha 20).
	gxCmd(v9, 0x29, 20<<16|0xC0)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x20, 0x7C1F)
	gxCmd(v9, 0x40, 1)
	for _, q := range quad {
		gxVtx(v9, q[0]/2, q[1]/2, -0x400)
	}
	gxCmd(v9, 0x50, 0)
	// PCM16 loop tone on channel 0: channel rate
	// 16756991/512 = 32728 samples per second and 74 samples
	// per period gives a 442 Hz tone.
	sine := make([]byte, 74*2)
	for i := 0; i < 74; i++ {
		s := int16(math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/74) * 20000)
		sine[2*i] = byte(uint16(s))
		sine[2*i+1] = byte(uint16(s) >> 8)
	}
	m.Bus.LoadBytes(false, 0x02010000, sine)
	v7.Write(0x04000400, 4, 0)          // ch0 CNT (placeholder lanes)
	v7.Write(0x04000404, 4, 0x02010000) // SAD
	v7.Write(0x04000408, 4, 65024)      // TMR: period 512
	v7.Write(0x0400040C, 4, 37)         // PNT 0, LEN 37 words
	v7.Write(0x04000400, 4, 0x80000000|1<<27|1<<29|127|64<<16)
	// PSG square on channel 8: duty 3 (half), TMR for an
	// 880 Hz square (rate 7040).
	v7.Write(0x04000488, 4, 63156) // TMR
	v7.Write(0x04000480, 4, 0x80000000|3<<29|3<<24|2<<27|100|64<<16)
	// SOUNDCNT: master volume 127, mixer both sides, enable.
	v7.Write(0x04000500, 4, 0x807F)
}

func TestDS3DeterminismGate(t *testing.T) {
	build := func() *system.Machine {
		m := system.New()
		ds3Scene(m)
		return m
	}
	m := build()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	m.AudioSamples() // drain
	state1 := m.Serialize()
	if len(state1) != system.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d want %d", len(state1), system.StateSize)
	}
	if state1[0] != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("state version = %d want 3", state1[0])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	fbA1, fbB1 := m.Framebuffer()
	audio1 := m.AudioSamples()
	state2 := m.Serialize()

	m2 := build()
	if !m2.Deserialize(state1) {
		t.Fatal("deserialize rejected the DS-3 state")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		m2.RunFrame()
	}
	fbA2, fbB2 := m2.Framebuffer()
	audio2 := m2.AudioSamples()
	state3 := m2.Serialize()

	if len(audio1) < 4096 {
		t.Fatalf("audio captured %d values, want at least 4096 (2048 stereo samples)", len(audio1))
	}
	if len(audio1) != len(audio2) {
		t.Fatalf("audio lengths differ: %d vs %d", len(audio1), len(audio2))
	}
	for i := range audio1 {
		if audio1[i] != audio2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("audio sample %d differs: %d vs %d", i, audio1[i], audio2[i])
		}
	}
	for i := range fbA1 {
		if fbA1[i] != fbA2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("engine A pixel %d differs: %08x vs %08x", i, fbA1[i], fbA2[i])
		}
	}
	for i := range fbB1 {
		if fbB1[i] != fbB2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("engine B pixel %d differs", i)
		}
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(state2, state3) {
		t.Fatal("state bytes differ after restore and continuation")
	}
	t.Logf("state size %d bytes; audio compared %d samples", system.StateSize, len(audio1))
}
