func TestDS3PCMToneThroughMachine(t *testing.T) {
	m := system.New()
	v7 := m.Bus.ARM7()
	const n = 74
	sine := make([]byte, n*2)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		s := int16(math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/n) * 20000)
		sine[2*i] = byte(uint16(s))
		sine[2*i+1] = byte(uint16(s) >> 8)
	}
	m.Bus.LoadBytes(false, 0x02010000, sine)
	v7.Write(0x04000404, 4, 0x02010000)
	v7.Write(0x04000408, 4, 65024)
	v7.Write(0x0400040C, 4, 37)
	v7.Write(0x04000500, 4, 0x807F)
	v7.Write(0x04000400, 4, 0x80000000|1<<27|1<<29|127|64<<16)
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	samples := m.AudioSamples()
	// Count positive zero crossings on the left channel.
	cross := 0
	prev := int16(0)
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(samples); i += 2 {
		s := samples[i]
		if prev <= 0 && s > 0 {
			cross++
		}
		prev = s
	}
	secs := float64(len(samples)/2) / 32768.0
	freq := float64(cross) / secs
	rate := 16756991.0 / 512.0
	expect := rate / n
	if math.Abs(freq-expect)/expect > 0.02 {
		t.Fatalf("tone freq = %.2f Hz want %.2f (rate %.1f / %d)", freq, expect, rate, n)
	}
}

func TestDS3PanAndCaptureThroughMachine(t *testing.T) {
	m := system.New()
	v7 := m.Bus.ARM7()
	// Constant DC PCM16 on channel 0, pan full left.
	dc := make([]byte, 8*2)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		dc[2*i] = byte(10000 & 0xFF)
		dc[2*i+1] = byte(10000 >> 8)
	}
	m.Bus.LoadBytes(false, 0x02010000, dc)
	v7.Write(0x04000404, 4, 0x02010000)
	v7.Write(0x04000408, 4, 27452)
	v7.Write(0x0400040C, 4, 4) // 8 samples looped
	v7.Write(0x04000500, 4, 0x807F)
	v7.Write(0x04000400, 4, 0x80000000|1<<27|1<<29|127) // pan 0
	// Capture 0: mixer left source, PCM16, one-shot, 512
	// samples (256 words).
	v7.Write(0x04000510, 4, 0x02018000) // DAD
	v7.Write(0x04000514, 4, 256)        // LEN words
	v7.Write(0x04000508, 1, 0x84)       // start, one-shot
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	out := m.AudioSamples()
	if len(out) < 1024 {
		t.Fatalf("drained %d values, want at least 1024", len(out))
	}
	// Pan full left: the right channel stays at the bias
	// center, which is exactly 0 with bias 0x200.
	for i := 1; i < len(out); i += 2 {
		if out[i] != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("right sample %d = %d want 0 (pan full left)", i/2, out[i])
		}
	}
	if out[0] == 0 {
		t.Fatal("left channel silent with pan full left")
	}
	// Capture RAM holds the same left samples the drain
	// returned (the stated capture model).
	vm := m.Bus.ARM7()
	for i := 0; i < 512; i++ {
		got := int16(vm.Read(0x02018000+uint32(2*i), 2))
		if got != out[2*i] {
			t.Fatalf("captured sample %d = %d want drained %d", i, got, out[2*i])
		}
	}
}

func TestDS3Microphone(t *testing.T) {
	m := system.New()
	m.SetMicrophone([]int16{0x4000, -0x4000})
	v7 := m.Bus.ARM7()
	readADC := func() uint16 {
		v7.Write(0x040001C0, 2, 0x8200) // SPICNT: enable, touchscreen
		v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, 0xE0)   // control: channel 6 (microphone)
		v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, 0)
		b1 := v7.Read(0x040001C2, 1)
		v7.Write(0x040001C2, 1, 0)
		b2 := v7.Read(0x040001C2, 1)
		return uint16((b1<<8 | b2) >> 3)
	}
	if got := readADC(); got != 0xC00 {
		t.Fatalf("mic sample 1 ADC = %03x want C00", got)
	}
	if got := readADC(); got != 0x400 {
		t.Fatalf("mic sample 2 ADC = %03x want 400", got)
	}
	if got := readADC(); got != 0x800 {
		t.Fatalf("mic idle ADC = %03x want 800 (center)", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/system/ds4_test.go ====================

package system_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/system"
)

// DS-4 enginetest: a synthetic cartridge whose ARM9 and
// ARM7 guest programs drive the whole machine the way a
// game would. The ARM9 boots through the real direct
// boot, uploads VRAM data and programs both 2D engines,
// submits a GX scene (a textured far quad under a flat
// near quad) plus a 2D text tile on engine A, swaps
// buffers, then asks the ARM7 over the IPC FIFO to start
// a PCM loop tone, and finally to poll the touchscreen
// over SPI and report the ADC values. Milestones land in
// a sequence log in main RAM in completion order.
//
// The guests are built with the tiny two-pass assembler
// below (the DS-2 gate hand-writes its words; the DS-4
// programs are long enough that encoding helpers pay
// off). Data uploads and register programming on the
// ARM9 side run through one (address, value) word table
// executed by a short copy loop, the same table the GX
// command stream is expressed in (GX direct ports are
// just word writes to 0x04000400 + command*4).

const (
	ds4LogAddr   = 0x0201F000 // milestone sequence log
	ds4FailAddr  = 0x0201F080 // guest failure magic lands here
	ds4TouchXAdr = 0x0201F100 // ARM7 stores the touch ADC X here
	ds4TouchYAdr = 0x0201F104 // and Y here

	ds4CmdTone   = 0x544F4E45 // "TONE"
	ds4AckTone   = 0x41434B54 // "ACKT"
	ds4CmdTouch  = 0x544F5543 // "TOUC"
	ds4AckTouch  = 0x41434B55 // "ACKU"
	ds4FailMagic = 0x0BAD0BAD
)

// ---- tiny ARM assembler --------------------------------

type ds4Fix struct {
	at     int
	label  string
	branch bool
	addr   bool // the word itself is patched to the label address
}

type ds4Asm struct {
	base   uint32
	w      []uint32
	labels map[string]int
	fix    []ds4Fix
}

func newDS4Asm(base uint32) *ds4Asm {
	return &ds4Asm{base: base, labels: map[string]int{}}
}

func (a *ds4Asm) label(name string) { a.labels[name] = len(a.w) }

func (a *ds4Asm) emit(w uint32) { a.w = append(a.w, w) }

// dataWord appends a raw word (literal pool entry or a
// data table entry) under a label.
func (a *ds4Asm) dataWord(name string, v uint32) {
	a.label(name)
	a.emit(v)
}

// addrWord appends a word whose value becomes the
// address of the named label, patched at build time.
func (a *ds4Asm) addrWord(name, target string) {
	a.label(name)
	a.fix = append(a.fix, ds4Fix{at: len(a.w), label: target, addr: true})
	a.emit(0)
}

func (a *ds4Asm) ldrLit(rd int, label string) {
	a.fix = append(a.fix, ds4Fix{at: len(a.w), label: label})
	a.emit(0xE59F0000 | uint32(rd)<<12)
}

func (a *ds4Asm) b(cond uint32, label string) {
	a.fix = append(a.fix, ds4Fix{at: len(a.w), label: label, branch: true})
	a.emit(cond<<28 | 0x0A000000)
}

func (a *ds4Asm) build(t *testing.T) []uint32 {
	for _, f := range a.fix {
		idx, ok := a.labels[f.label]
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("assembler: unknown label %q", f.label)
		}
		switch {
		case f.addr:
			a.w[f.at] = a.base + uint32(idx*4)
		case f.branch:
			off := idx - (f.at + 2)
			a.w[f.at] |= uint32(off) & 0xFFFFFF
		default: // LDR literal
			off := (idx - (f.at + 2)) * 4
			if off < 0 || off > 4095 {
				t.Fatalf("assembler: literal %q out of range (%d)", f.label, off)
			}
			a.w[f.at] |= uint32(off)
		}
	}
	return a.w
}

const (
	ds4EQ = 0x0
	ds4NE = 0x1
)

// ds4RotImm returns the ARM rotated-immediate encoding
// of v, or false when v is not representable.
func ds4RotImm(v uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	for rot := uint(0); rot < 16; rot++ {
		// imm8 = v ROL (2*rot)
		var imm uint32
		if rot == 0 {
			imm = v
		} else {
			imm = v<<(2*rot) | v>>(32-2*rot)
		}
		if imm <= 0xFF {
			return uint32(rot)<<8 | imm, true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

func (a *ds4Asm) immOp(op uint32, rd, rn int, v uint32) {
	enc, ok := ds4RotImm(v)
	if !ok {
		panic("immediate not encodable")
	}
	a.emit(op | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12 | enc)
}

func (a *ds4Asm) movImm(rd int, v uint32) { a.immOp(0xE3A00000, rd, 0, v) }
func (a *ds4Asm) cmpImm(rn int, v uint32) { a.immOp(0xE3500000, 0, rn, v) }
func (a *ds4Asm) tstImm(rn int, v uint32) { a.immOp(0xE3100000, 0, rn, v) }
func (a *ds4Asm) subsImm(rd, rn int, v uint32) {
	a.immOp(0xE2500000, rd, rn, v)
}
func (a *ds4Asm) movReg(rd, rm int) {
	a.emit(0xE1A00000 | uint32(rd)<<12 | uint32(rm))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) cmpReg(rn, rm int) {
	a.emit(0xE1500000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rm))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) ldr(rd, rn, off int) {
	a.emit(0xE5900000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12 | uint32(off))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) ldrPost(rd, rn, off int) {
	a.emit(0xE4900000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12 | uint32(off))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) str(rd, rn int) {
	a.emit(0xE5800000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12)
}
func (a *ds4Asm) strPost(rd, rn, off int) {
	a.emit(0xE4800000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12 | uint32(off))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) ldrb(rd, rn int) {
	a.emit(0xE5D00000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12)
}
func (a *ds4Asm) strb(rd, rn int) {
	a.emit(0xE5C00000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12)
}
func (a *ds4Asm) strh(rd, rn int) {
	a.emit(0xE1C000B0 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12)
}
func (a *ds4Asm) ldrh(rd, rn int) {
	a.emit(0xE1D000B0 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12)
}
func (a *ds4Asm) lslImm(rd, rm, n int) {
	a.emit(0xE1A00000 | uint32(rd)<<12 | uint32(n)<<7 | uint32(rm))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) lsrImm(rd, rm, n int) {
	a.emit(0xE1A00020 | uint32(rd)<<12 | uint32(n)<<7 | uint32(rm))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) orrReg(rd, rn, rm int) {
	a.emit(0xE1800000 | uint32(rn)<<16 | uint32(rd)<<12 | uint32(rm))
}
func (a *ds4Asm) spin() { a.emit(0xEAFFFFFE) } // B .

// log appends one milestone to the sequence log (r8 is
// the log cursor on the ARM9).
func (a *ds4Asm) log(stage uint32) {
	a.movImm(0, stage)
	a.strPost(0, 8, 4)
}

// fail writes the failure magic and parks the CPU.
func (a *ds4Asm) fail() {
	a.label("fail")
	a.ldrLit(0, "fail_addr")
	a.ldrLit(1, "fail_magic")
	a.str(1, 0)
	a.spin()
}

// waitFIFO polls FIFOCNT until the receive FIFO is
// non-empty, then pops one word into rd and compares it
// against the expected literal; mismatch branches to
// the named label (the ARM9 passes "fail", the ARM7
// loops back to its wait).
func (a *ds4Asm) waitFIFO(rd int, want string, badLabel string, tag string) {
	a.label("wait_" + tag)
	a.ldrLit(0, "fifocnt")
	a.ldr(2, 0, 0)
	a.tstImm(2, 0x100) // receive-empty bit
	a.b(ds4NE, "wait_"+tag)
	a.ldrLit(0, "fiforecv")
	a.ldr(rd, 0, 0)
	a.ldrLit(1, want)
	a.cmpReg(rd, 1)
	a.b(ds4NE, badLabel)
}

// sendFIFO pushes the named literal word to the peer.
func (a *ds4Asm) sendFIFO(what string) {
	a.ldrLit(0, "fifosend")
	a.ldrLit(1, what)
	a.str(1, 0)
}

// enableFIFO turns this side's IPC FIFO unit on.
func (a *ds4Asm) enableFIFO() {
	a.ldrLit(0, "fifocnt")
	a.ldrLit(1, "v8000")
	a.str(1, 0)
}

// ---- the ARM9 guest ------------------------------------

// ds4GXPort is the direct command port of a GX command.
func ds4GXPort(id uint32) uint32 { return 0x04000400 + id*4 }

// ds4IOTable is the (address, value) word-write table the
// ARM9 guest executes: VRAM uploads through the LCDC
// window, palette entries, VRAMCNT assignment, both
// engines' display registers, the GX clear registers,
// and the whole GX command stream for the scene. It
// mirrors, write for write, the bus pokes of the DS-3
// gates (setupDisplay and the textured/near quad gate).
func ds4IOTable() [][2]uint32 {
	var tab [][2]uint32
	put := func(addr, val uint32) { tab = append(tab, [2]uint32{addr, val}) }

	// 8x8 256-color texture in bank A (LCDC 0x06800000):
	// a four-color checker, index 1+(tx+ty)%4.
	rows := []uint32{0x04030201, 0x01040302, 0x02010403, 0x03020104}
	for ty := 0; ty < 8; ty++ {
		put(0x06800000+uint32(ty*8), rows[ty%4])
		put(0x06800004+uint32(ty*8), rows[ty%4])
	}
	// Texture palette in bank E (LCDC 0x06880000):
	// entry 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 white.
	put(0x06880000, 0x001F0000)
	put(0x06880004, 0x7C0003E0)
	put(0x06880008, 0x00007FFF)
	// Engine A BG1 tile 1 (filled with color index 1)
	// and map entry 0 in bank B (LCDC 0x06820000).
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		put(0x06824020+uint32(i*4), 0x11111111)
	}
	put(0x06821000, 1)
	// Engine B BG0 tile 1 and map entry 0 in bank H
	// (LCDC 0x06898000).
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		put(0x0689C020+uint32(i*4), 0x11111111)
	}
	put(0x06899000, 1)
	// BG palettes: engine A entry 1 magenta (a color the
	// texture palette does not contain, so the 2D probe
	// is unambiguous), engine B entry 1 white.
	put(0x05000000, 0x7C1F0000)
	put(0x05000400, 0x7FFF0000)
	// VRAMCNT: A texture slot 0, B = BG A, E texture
	// palette, H = BG B (WRAMCNT byte preserved as 0).
	put(0x04000240, 0x00008183)
	put(0x04000244, 0x00000083)
	put(0x04000248, 0x00000081)
	// Engine A: graphics display, BG0 = 3D (priority 1),
	// BG1 text (priority 0, char base 1, screen base 2).
	put(0x04000000, 0x00010308) // DISPCNT A
	put(0x04000008, 0x02040001) // BG1CNT << 16 | BG0CNT
	put(0x04000060, 0x00000001) // DISP3DCNT: texture on
	// Engine B: graphics display, BG0 text.
	put(0x04001000, 0x00010100) // DISPCNT B
	put(0x04001008, 0x00000204) // BG0CNT B
	// GX rear plane.
	put(0x04000350, 31<<16) // CLEAR_COLOR black, alpha 31
	put(0x04000354, 0x7FFF) // CLEAR_DEPTH far
	// GX command stream (direct ports).
	gx := func(id uint32, params ...uint32) {
		if len(params) == 0 {
			put(ds4GXPort(id), 0)
			return
		}
		for _, p := range params {
			put(ds4GXPort(id), p)
		}
	}
	gx(0x10, 0)          // MTX_MODE projection
	gx(0x15)             // MTX_IDENTITY
	gx(0x10, 1)          // MTX_MODE position
	gx(0x15)             // MTX_IDENTITY
	gx(0x60, 0xBFFF0000) // VIEWPORT full screen
	// Textured far quad.
	gx(0x29, 31<<16|0xC0) // POLYGON_ATTR
	gx(0x20, 0x7FFF)      // COLOR white
	gx(0x2A, 4<<26)       // TEXIMAGE_PARAM 256-color
	gx(0x2B, 0)           // PLTT_BASE
	gx(0x40, 1)           // BEGIN_VTXS quads
	vtx := func(s, t, x, y, z int) {
		gx(0x22, uint32(uint16(s))|uint32(uint16(t))<<16)
		gx(0x23, uint32(uint16(x))|uint32(uint16(y))<<16, uint32(uint16(z)))
	}
	vtx(0, 128, -0x1000, -0x1000, 0x400)
	vtx(128, 128, 0x1000, -0x1000, 0x400)
	vtx(128, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, 0x400)
	vtx(0, 0, -0x1000, 0x1000, 0x400)
	// Flat green near quad (half size, closer).
	gx(0x2A, 0)      // TEXIMAGE_PARAM off
	gx(0x20, 0x03E0) // COLOR green
	gx(0x40, 1)      // BEGIN_VTXS quads
	fvtx := func(x, y, z int) {
		gx(0x23, uint32(uint16(x))|uint32(uint16(y))<<16, uint32(uint16(z)))
	}
	fvtx(-0x800, -0x800, -0x400)
	fvtx(0x800, -0x800, -0x400)
	fvtx(0x800, 0x800, -0x400)
	fvtx(-0x800, 0x800, -0x400)
	gx(0x50, 0) // SWAP_BUFFERS
	return tab
}

func ds4ARM9Program(t *testing.T) []uint32 {
	a := newDS4Asm(0x02000000)
	// Stage 1: the direct boot flag halfword reads 1.
	a.ldrLit(0, "bootflag")
	a.ldrh(1, 0)
	a.cmpImm(1, 1)
	a.b(ds4NE, "fail")
	a.ldrLit(8, "log_base")
	a.log(1)
	// Stage 2: display setup, VRAM uploads, GX scene,
	// swap buffers (one table copy loop).
	a.ldrLit(0, "io_table_lit")
	a.ldrLit(1, "io_table_end_lit")
	a.label("tabloop")
	a.cmpReg(0, 1)
	a.b(ds4EQ, "tabdone")
	a.ldrPost(2, 0, 4)
	a.ldrPost(3, 0, 4)
	a.str(3, 2)
	a.b(0xE, "tabloop") // AL
	a.label("tabdone")
	a.log(2)
	// Stage 3: IPC tone handshake with the ARM7.
	a.enableFIFO()
	a.sendFIFO("cmd_tone")
	a.waitFIFO(3, "ack_tone", "fail", "tone")
	a.log(3)
	// Stage 4: IPC touch handshake; the ARM7 leaves the
	// ADC values in main RAM.
	a.sendFIFO("cmd_touch")
	a.waitFIFO(3, "ack_touch", "fail", "touch")
	a.log(4)
	a.spin()
	a.fail()
	// Literal pool.
	a.dataWord("bootflag", 0x027FFFFA)
	a.dataWord("log_base", ds4LogAddr)
	a.dataWord("fail_addr", ds4FailAddr)
	a.dataWord("fail_magic", ds4FailMagic)
	a.dataWord("fifocnt", 0x04000184)
	a.dataWord("fifosend", 0x04000188)
	a.dataWord("fiforecv", 0x04100000)
	a.dataWord("v8000", 0x8000)
	a.dataWord("cmd_tone", ds4CmdTone)
	a.dataWord("ack_tone", ds4AckTone)
	a.dataWord("cmd_touch", ds4CmdTouch)
	a.dataWord("ack_touch", ds4AckTouch)
	// The table start/end literals: pool words holding
	// the table's own start and end addresses.
	a.addrWord("io_table_lit", "io_table")
	a.addrWord("io_table_end_lit", "io_table_end")
	a.label("io_table")
	for _, e := range ds4IOTable() {
		a.emit(e[0])
		a.emit(e[1])
	}
	a.label("io_table_end")
	return a.build(t)
}

// ---- the ARM7 guest ------------------------------------

// ds4SPIRead emits one touchscreen ADC read for the
// given control byte (channel in bits 6-4, bit 7 set),
// leaving the 12-bit ADC value in r4. It mirrors the
// byte sequence of the DS-3 microphone gate.
func ds4SPIRead(a *ds4Asm, ctrl uint32) {
	a.ldrLit(0, "spicnt")
	a.ldrLit(1, "spicnt_val")
	a.strh(1, 0)
	a.ldrLit(0, "spidata")
	a.movImm(1, ctrl)
	a.strb(1, 0)
	a.movImm(1, 0)
	a.strb(1, 0)
	a.ldrb(2, 0) // first data byte (adc >> 5)
	a.strb(1, 0)
	a.ldrb(3, 0) // second data byte ((adc & 0x1F) << 3)
	a.lslImm(2, 2, 8)
	a.orrReg(2, 2, 3)
	a.lsrImm(4, 2, 3)
}

func ds4ARM7Program(t *testing.T) []uint32 {
	a := newDS4Asm(0x03800000)
	// Wait for the tone command.
	a.enableFIFO()
	a.waitFIFO(3, "cmd_tone", "wait_tone", "tone")
	// Copy the sine table into main RAM (the address
	// the sound channel will stream from).
	a.ldrLit(0, "sine_ptr")
	a.ldrLit(1, "ram_sine")
	a.movImm(2, 37)
	a.label("cpy")
	a.ldrPost(3, 0, 4)
	a.strPost(3, 1, 4)
	a.subsImm(2, 2, 1)
	a.b(ds4NE, "cpy")
	// Program sound channel 0 and the mixer, mirroring
	// the DS-3 machine gate's register writes; the CNT
	// write (with the enable bit) comes last.
	a.ldrLit(0, "snd_sad")
	a.ldrLit(1, "ram_sine")
	a.str(1, 0)
	a.ldrLit(0, "snd_tmr")
	a.ldrLit(1, "tmr_val")
	a.str(1, 0)
	a.ldrLit(0, "snd_len")
	a.movImm(1, 37)
	a.str(1, 0)
	a.ldrLit(0, "snd_main")
	a.ldrLit(1, "main_val")
	a.str(1, 0)
	a.ldrLit(0, "snd_cnt")
	a.ldrLit(1, "cnt_val")
	a.str(1, 0)
	a.sendFIFO("ack_tone")
	// Wait for the touch command, then poll the
	// touchscreen over SPI: channel 5 is X, channel 1
	// is Y.
	a.waitFIFO(3, "cmd_touch", "wait_touch", "touch")
	ds4SPIRead(a, 0xD0) // X
	a.ldrLit(0, "touch_x")
	a.str(4, 0)
	ds4SPIRead(a, 0x90) // Y
	a.ldrLit(0, "touch_y")
	a.str(4, 0)
	a.sendFIFO("ack_touch")
	a.spin()
	// Literal pool.
	a.dataWord("fifocnt", 0x04000184)
	a.dataWord("fifosend", 0x04000188)
	a.dataWord("fiforecv", 0x04100000)
	a.dataWord("v8000", 0x8000)
	a.dataWord("cmd_tone", ds4CmdTone)
	a.dataWord("ack_tone", ds4AckTone)
	a.dataWord("cmd_touch", ds4CmdTouch)
	a.dataWord("ack_touch", ds4AckTouch)
	a.dataWord("ram_sine", 0x02010000)
	a.dataWord("snd_sad", 0x04000404)
	a.dataWord("snd_tmr", 0x04000408)
	a.dataWord("snd_len", 0x0400040C)
	a.dataWord("snd_cnt", 0x04000400)
	a.dataWord("snd_main", 0x04000500)
	a.dataWord("tmr_val", 65024) // period 512: 16,756,991/512 per second
	a.dataWord("cnt_val", 0xA840007F)
	a.dataWord("main_val", 0x807F)
	a.dataWord("spicnt", 0x040001C0)
	a.dataWord("spidata", 0x040001C2)
	a.dataWord("spicnt_val", 0x8200)
	a.dataWord("touch_x", ds4TouchXAdr)
	a.dataWord("touch_y", ds4TouchYAdr)
	a.addrWord("sine_ptr", "sine_data")
	// The 74-sample PCM16 sine table (37 words), the
	// same table the DS-3 tone gates use.
	a.label("sine_data")
	for i := 0; i < 37; i++ {
		s0 := int16(math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(2*i)/74) * 20000)
		s1 := int16(math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(2*i+1)/74) * 20000)
		a.emit(uint32(uint16(s0)) | uint32(uint16(s1))<<16)
	}
	return a.build(t)
}

// ---- the gate ------------------------------------------

// buildDS4ROM assembles the synthetic DS-4 cartridge
// (the DS-2 builder's layout: ARM9 at 0x02000000, ARM7
// at 0x03800000, entries at the load addresses).
func buildDS4ROM(arm9prog, arm7prog []uint32) []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x4000)
	copy(rom[0x000:], "DS4 PROOF")
	copy(rom[0x00C:], "ADSE")
	copy(rom[0x010:], "01")
	le := binary.LittleEndian
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x020:], 0x1000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x024:], 0x02000000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x028:], 0x02000000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x02C:], uint32(len(arm9prog)*4))
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x030:], 0x2000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x034:], 0x03800000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x038:], 0x03800000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x03C:], uint32(len(arm7prog)*4))
	for i, w := range arm9prog {
		le.PutUint32(rom[0x1000+i*4:], w)
	}
	for i, w := range arm7prog {
		le.PutUint32(rom[0x2000+i*4:], w)
	}
	return rom
}

func ds4Word(m *system.Machine, addr uint32) uint32 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(m.Bus.MainRAM[addr-0x02000000:])
}

// ds4Stacked composes the two screens exactly as the
// libretro shell presents them: top screen in rows
// 0-191, bottom screen in rows 192-383.
func ds4Stacked(m *system.Machine) []uint32 {
	top, bottom := m.Framebuffer()
	out := make([]uint32, 256*384)
	copy(out[:256*192], top)
	copy(out[256*192:], bottom)
	return out
}

func TestDS4EngineGate(t *testing.T) {
	rom := buildDS4ROM(ds4ARM9Program(t), ds4ARM7Program(t))
	// Leave the ROM next to the built shell library so
	// the shared enginetest harness can run the same
	// image through the real .so.
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join("..", "builds"), 0o755); err == nil {
		p := filepath.Join("..", "builds", "enginetest.nds")
		if err := os.WriteFile(p, rom, 0o644); err != nil {
			t.Logf("writing harness ROM: %v", err)
		} else {
			t.Logf("harness ROM at %s", p)
		}
	}

	m := system.New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// The pen is down at (100, 60) before anything runs;
	// the ARM7's SPI poll must see exactly this point.
	m.SetTouch(100, 60, true)
	m.Start()
	frames := 0
	var log []uint32
	for frames = 0; frames < 30; frames++ {
		m.RunFrame()
		log = log[:0]
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if w := ds4Word(m, ds4LogAddr+uint32(4*i)); w != 0 {
				log = append(log, w)
			}
		}
		if len(log) >= 4 {
			break
		}
	}
	if got := ds4Word(m, ds4FailAddr); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("guest failure magic %08x after %d frames", got, frames)
	}
	if len(log) != 4 || log[0] != 1 || log[1] != 2 || log[2] != 3 || log[3] != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("milestone log = %v after %d frames, want [1 2 3 4]", log, frames)
	}
	// Touch ADC values: the documented linear map of
	// (100, 60) from the DS-2/DS-3 gates.
	if got := ds4Word(m, ds4TouchXAdr); got != 0x67D {
		t.Fatalf("touch ADC X = %03x want 67D", got)
	}
	if got := ds4Word(m, ds4TouchYAdr); got != 0x565 {
		t.Fatalf("touch ADC Y = %03x want 565", got)
	}

	// The GX swap renders at the next VBlank edge (the
	// DS-3 model), so give the presented frame two more
	// frames to settle before probing pixels.
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()

	// Shell-presented stacked frame probes.
	fb := ds4Stacked(m)
	probe := func(x, y int, want uint32, what string) {
		if got := fb[y*256+x]; got != want {
			t.Fatalf("stacked (%d,%d) %s = %08x want %08x", x, y, what, got, want)
		}
	}
	probe(4, 4, 0xFFFF00FF, "engine A BG1 tile (2D over 3D)")
	probe(10, 10, 0xFFFF0000, "textured quad texel (0,0) red")
	probe(40, 20, 0xFF00FF00, "textured quad texel (1,0) green")
	probe(128, 96, 0xFF00FF00, "near flat quad green")
	probe(200, 150, 0xFFFF0000, "textured quad texel (6,6) red")
	probe(4, 196, 0xFFFFFFFF, "engine B BG0 tile white")
	probe(100, 292, 0xFF000000, "engine B backdrop black")

	// Audio: the PCM loop tone the ARM7 started. Keep
	// running so at least half a second of output is
	// available, then measure the left channel's pitch
	// by positive zero crossings (the DS-3 method).
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	samples := m.AudioSamples()
	cross := 0
	prev := int16(0)
	nonSilent := 0
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(samples); i += 2 {
		s := samples[i]
		if s != 0 {
			nonSilent++
		}
		if prev <= 0 && s > 0 {
			cross++
		}
		prev = s
	}
	if nonSilent == 0 {
		t.Fatal("audio is silent after the IPC tone start")
	}
	secs := float64(len(samples)/2) / 32768.0
	freq := float64(cross) / secs
	expect := (16756991.0 / 512.0) / 74.0
	if math.Abs(freq-expect)/expect > 0.02 {
		t.Fatalf("tone freq = %.2f Hz want %.2f (within 2%%)", freq, expect)
	}
	t.Logf("milestones in %d frames; tone %.2f Hz (expect %.2f); %d audio values",
		frames, freq, expect, len(samples))

	// Determinism: drain, save mid-run, continue on this
	// machine and on a fresh one restored from the save;
	// framebuffers, continuation audio, and final state
	// bytes must be identical.
	m.AudioSamples()
	saved := m.Serialize()
	if len(saved) != system.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d want %d", len(saved), system.StateSize)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	topA, botA := m.Framebuffer()
	audioA := m.AudioSamples()
	stateA := m.Serialize()

	m2 := system.New()
	if err := m2.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m2.SetTouch(100, 60, true)
	if !m2.Deserialize(saved) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize refused the DS-4 state")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		m2.RunFrame()
	}
	topB, botB := m2.Framebuffer()
	audioB := m2.AudioSamples()
	stateB := m2.Serialize()
	if len(audioA) == 0 || len(audioA) != len(audioB) {
		t.Fatalf("continuation audio lengths: %d vs %d", len(audioA), len(audioB))
	}
	for i := range audioA {
		if audioA[i] != audioB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("continuation audio value %d differs: %d vs %d", i, audioA[i], audioB[i])
		}
	}
	for i := range topA {
		if topA[i] != topB[i] || botA[i] != botB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d differs after restore", i)
		}
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(stateA, stateB) {
		t.Fatal("state bytes differ after restore and continuation")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/system/hook.go ====================

package system

// The machine is the bus IOHook. It dispatches the DS-2 device
// offsets between the video package (DISPSTAT, VCOUNT, and the
// main-memory display FIFO address) and the peripheral set
// (everything else), so neither package imports the other.

// getLanes extracts the unit of the given size at the byte
// lane of off from a 32-bit value.
func getLanes(v uint32, off uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return (v >> ((off & 3) * 8)) & 0xFF
	case 2:
		return (v >> ((off & 2) * 8)) & 0xFFFF
	}
	return v
}

// putLanes merges a written unit into a 32-bit value.
func putLanes(v uint32, off uint32, size int, val uint32) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		sh := (off & 3) * 8
		return v&^(0xFF<<sh) | (val&0xFF)<<sh
	case 2:
		sh := (off & 2) * 8
		return v&^(0xFFFF<<sh) | (val&0xFFFF)<<sh
	}
	return val
}

// ReadIO implements bus.IOHook.
func (m *Machine) ReadIO(nine bool, off uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	if nine && off >= 0x004 && off < 0x008 {
		word := uint32(m.Video.DISPSTAT()) | uint32(uint16(m.Video.VCount()))<<16
		return getLanes(word, off, size), true
	}
	if nine && off == 0x068 {
		return 0, true // DISP_MMEM_FIFO reads back 0
	}
	if nine && (off == 0x320 || off >= 0x330 && off < 0x3C0 || off >= 0x400 && off < 0x6B0) {
		// RDLINES_COUNT, the RE register block, the GX
		// command ports, and the GX status/result block.
		return m.GX.ReadIO(off, size)
	}
	if !nine && off >= 0x400 && off < 0x520 {
		return m.Audio.ReadIO(off, size)
	}
	return m.Periph.ReadIO(nine, off, size)
}

// WriteIO implements bus.IOHook.
func (m *Machine) WriteIO(nine bool, off uint32, size int, val uint32) bool {
	if nine && off >= 0x004 && off < 0x006 {
		merged := putLanes(uint32(m.Video.DISPSTAT()), off, size, val)
		m.Video.SetDISPSTAT(uint16(merged))
		return true
	}
	if nine && off >= 0x006 && off < 0x008 {
		return true // VCOUNT is read-only
	}
	if nine && off == 0x068 {
		m.Video.SetMainDispAddr(val)
		return true
	}
	if nine && (off == 0x320 || off >= 0x330 && off < 0x3C0 || off >= 0x400 && off < 0x6B0) {
		return m.GX.WriteIO(off, size, val)
	}
	if !nine && off >= 0x400 && off < 0x520 {
		return m.Audio.WriteIO(off, size, val)
	}
	return m.Periph.WriteIO(nine, off, size, val)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/system/system.go ====================

// Package system is the Nintendo DS machine: the two CPUs on
// the dual bus, the 2D video engines, the 3D geometry and
// rendering engine, the sound unit, the peripherals, full
// direct boot, scanline-stepped execution, and save states.
//
// Boot approach (deliberately no BIOS): no DS BIOS or firmware
// image exists in this module and none is required. LoadROM
// performs the documented direct-boot initialization: it
// stages both binaries at their header load addresses, writes
// the boot block games read in main RAM, installs the entry
// register state (stacks per the direct-boot table, CPSR =
// system mode, r12/r13/r14 at the entry contract), and leaves
// the CPUs halted until Start. The firmware the ARM7 can read
// over SPI is a generated minimal image (periph package), not
// a dump.
package system

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/audio"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/cart"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/chips/arm7"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/chips/arm9"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/chips/armcore"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/gx"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/periph"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/video"
)

// Frame budgets in CPU cycles. The ARM9 runs at 33.5 MHz and
// the ARM7 at half that; one 60 Hz frame is 560,190 ARM9 cycles
// and 280,095 ARM7 cycles. The line split (video package)
// reproduces these totals exactly over 263 lines.
const (
	CyclesPerFrame9 = 560190
	CyclesPerFrame7 = 280095
)

// Screen geometry of one DS display.
const (
	ScreenWidth  = 256
	ScreenHeight = 192
)

// Machine is one DS console.
type Machine struct {
	Bus    *bus.Bus
	CPU9   *armcore.CPU
	CPU7   *armcore.CPU
	Periph *periph.Set
	Video  *video.Video
	GX     *gx.GX
	Audio  *audio.Sound

	header *cart.Header
	rom    []byte

	started9 bool
	started7 bool

	buttons uint32

	touchX    uint16
	touchY    uint16
	touchDown bool

	micSamples []int16
	micIdx     int
}

// New returns a machine with both CPUs halted and no cartridge.
func New() *Machine {
	b := bus.New()
	m := &Machine{Bus: b}
	m.CPU7 = arm7.New(b.ARM7())
	m.CPU9 = arm9.New(b.ARM9())
	b.AttachCPU9(m.CPU9)
	m.CPU9.Halted = true
	m.CPU7.Halted = true
	m.Video = video.New(b)
	m.Periph = periph.New(b,
		func() []byte { return m.rom },
		func() uint32 { return m.buttons },
		func() (uint16, uint16, bool) { return m.touchX, m.touchY, m.touchDown })
	m.GX = gx.New(b)
	m.Audio = audio.New(audioMem{v: b.ARM7()})
	m.Video.Line3D = m.GX.Line3D
	m.Periph.SetMicrophoneSource(m.micNext)
	b.SetIOHook(m)
	return m
}

// audioMem adapts the ARM7 bus view to the sound unit's
// memory interface.
type audioMem struct{ v bus.View }

func (a audioMem) Read8(addr uint32) uint8     { return uint8(a.v.Read(addr, 1)) }
func (a audioMem) Read16(addr uint32) uint16   { return uint16(a.v.Read(addr, 2)) }
func (a audioMem) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) { a.v.Write(addr, 1, uint32(v)) }
func (a audioMem) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	a.v.Write(addr, 2, uint32(v))
}

// LoadROM parses the cartridge header and performs the full
// direct-boot initialization (see boot.go), leaving both CPUs
// halted with their entry state installed. Call Start (or
// Start9/Start7) to run them.
func (m *Machine) LoadROM(rom []byte) error {
	h, err := cart.Parse(rom)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	m.header = h
	m.rom = rom
	m.started9 = false
	m.started7 = false
	m.directBoot()
	return nil
}

// Header returns the parsed cartridge header, or nil before
// LoadROM.
func (m *Machine) Header() *cart.Header { return m.header }

// Start9 starts the ARM9 at its header entry point.
func (m *Machine) Start9() {
	if m.header == nil {
		return
	}
	m.CPU9.Jump(m.header.ARM9Entry)
	m.started9 = true
}

// Start7 starts the ARM7 at its header entry point.
func (m *Machine) Start7() {
	if m.header == nil {
		return
	}
	m.CPU7.Jump(m.header.ARM7Entry)
	m.started7 = true
}

// Start starts both CPUs at their header entry points.
func (m *Machine) Start() {
	m.Start9()
	m.Start7()
}

// RunFrame advances the machine by one frame, stepped at
// scanline granularity: 263 lines, each running the visible
// cycle chunk, the hblank point (HBlank flags, DMA triggers),
// and the hblank cycle chunk. Video renders per line from the
// register state at line start. VBlank begins at line 192,
// which also latches the affine reference points and fires the
// VBlank DMA triggers and interrupt sources.
func (m *Machine) RunFrame() {
	m.Periph.TriggerDMA(periph.TrigGX)
	m.Video.BeginFrame()
	for line := 0; line < video.LinesTotal; line++ {
		m.Video.SetLine(line)
		if line == m.Video.LYC() && m.Video.IRQEnabled(2) {
			m.Periph.Raise(true, periph.IRQVCount)
			m.Periph.Raise(false, periph.IRQVCount)
		}
		if line == video.Height {
			if m.Video.IRQEnabled(0) {
				m.Periph.Raise(true, periph.IRQVBlank)
				m.Periph.Raise(false, periph.IRQVBlank)
			}
			// The geometry engine's deferred swap and render
			// happen at the VBlank edge.
			m.GX.OnVBlank()
			m.Periph.TriggerDMA(periph.TrigVBlank)
			m.Video.LatchAffine()
		}
		if line < video.Height {
			m.Periph.TriggerDMA(periph.TrigDisplayLine)
			m.Video.RenderLine(line)
			m.Video.CaptureLine(line)
		}
		m.runChunk(video.CyclesLineA9, video.CyclesLineA7)
		m.Video.SetHBlank(true)
		if line < video.Height && m.Video.IRQEnabled(1) {
			m.Periph.Raise(true, periph.IRQHBlank)
			m.Periph.Raise(false, periph.IRQHBlank)
		}
		if line < video.Height {
			m.Periph.TriggerDMA(periph.TrigHBlank)
		}
		m.runChunk(video.CyclesLineB9, video.CyclesLineB7)
		m.Video.SetHBlank(false)
		if line < video.Height {
			m.Video.AdvanceAffine()
		}
	}
	m.Periph.FrameTick()
}

// runChunk steps each started CPU for up to its chunk budget,
// then advances its timers by the cycles actually executed
// and evaluates the keypad interrupt. Each CPU's IRQ line is
// resampled from the interrupt controller after every step,
// so a handler that acknowledges its interrupt source
// deasserts the line at the next instruction boundary instead
// of re-entering until the chunk ends.
// irqGXFIFO is the ARM9 geometry FIFO interrupt bit (21); it
// is level-triggered by the GXSTAT FIFO IRQ mode, so the
// system re-asserts it whenever the condition holds.
const irqGXFIFO = 21

func (m *Machine) runChunk(n9, n7 int) {
	if m.GX.FIFOIRQCondition() {
		m.Periph.Raise(true, irqGXFIFO)
	}
	if m.started9 {
		m.CPU9.IRQLine = m.Periph.PendingIRQ(true)
		n := 0
		for n < n9 {
			n += m.CPU9.Step()
			m.CPU9.IRQLine = m.Periph.PendingIRQ(true)
		}
		m.Periph.AdvanceTimers(true, n)
		m.evalKeyIRQ(true, 0x132)
	}
	if m.started7 {
		m.CPU7.IRQLine = m.Periph.PendingIRQ(false)
		n := 0
		for n < n7 {
			n += m.CPU7.Step()
			m.CPU7.IRQLine = m.Periph.PendingIRQ(false)
		}
		m.Periph.AdvanceTimers(false, n)
		m.Audio.Advance(uint64(n))
		m.evalKeyIRQ(false, 0x132)
	} else {
		// The sound unit is free-running even while the
		// ARM7 is halted.
		m.Audio.Advance(uint64(n7))
	}
}

// evalKeyIRQ evaluates a side's KEYCNT condition against the
// button state and raises the keypad interrupt on a match.
func (m *Machine) evalKeyIRQ(nine bool, off int) {
	io := m.Bus.IO7
	if nine {
		io = m.Bus.IO9
	}
	kc := uint32(io[off]) | uint32(io[off+1])<<8
	if kc&(1<<14) == 0 {
		return
	}
	sel := kc & 0x3FF
	pressed := m.buttons & 0x3FF
	match := false
	if kc&(1<<15) != 0 {
		match = sel != 0 && pressed&sel == sel
	} else {
		match = pressed&sel != 0
	}
	if match {
		m.Periph.Raise(nine, periph.IRQKeys)
	}
}

// Framebuffer returns the top and bottom screen buffers in
// POWCNT1 assignment order: with the swap bit clear engine A
// is the top screen; set, engine A is the bottom screen.
func (m *Machine) Framebuffer() (top, bottom []uint32) {
	if m.Video.Swapped() {
		return m.Video.B, m.Video.A
	}
	return m.Video.A, m.Video.B
}

// SetButtons stores the DS button state: bits 0-9 are A, B,
// Select, Start, Right, Left, Up, Down, R, L in the KEYINPUT
// order, bits 10-11 are X and Y.
func (m *Machine) SetButtons(mask uint32) { m.buttons = mask }

// Buttons returns the stored button state.
func (m *Machine) Buttons() uint32 { return m.buttons }

// SetTouch stores the touchscreen state (pixel coordinates and
// pen-down), feeding both the SPI touchscreen device and the
// ARM7 pen-down interrupt.
func (m *Machine) SetTouch(x, y uint16, down bool) {
	m.touchX, m.touchY, m.touchDown = x, y, down
	m.Periph.SetPenDown(down)
}

// Touch returns the stored touchscreen state.
func (m *Machine) Touch() (x, y uint16, down bool) {
	return m.touchX, m.touchY, m.touchDown
}

// SaveRAM returns the cartridge save memory (the AUX SPI
// EEPROM backing, 512 bytes in this slice).
func (m *Machine) SaveRAM() []byte { return m.Periph.SaveRAM() }

// SetSaveRAM replaces the cartridge save memory contents
// (the AUX SPI EEPROM backing), truncating or zero-padding
// data to the backing size.
func (m *Machine) SetSaveRAM(data []byte) { copy(m.Periph.SaveRAM(), data) }

// GXFIFOCount returns the number of 32-bit words written to
// the geometry FIFO port (the DS-3 geometry engine drains
// them for real; see the gx package).
func (m *Machine) GXFIFOCount() uint32 { return m.GX.FIFOWords }

// AudioSamples drains the sound unit's stereo output buffer
// (interleaved L,R int16 at 32,768 Hz).
func (m *Machine) AudioSamples() []int16 { return m.Audio.Drain() }

// SetMicrophone installs the microphone sample stream. The
// ARM7 reads samples through the SPI touchscreen ADC aux
// channel, one sample per read; with no stream installed (or
// once it is exhausted) the ADC returns its idle center
// value.
func (m *Machine) SetMicrophone(samples []int16) {
	m.micSamples = samples
	m.micIdx = 0
}

// micNext consumes one microphone sample for the SPI path.
func (m *Machine) micNext() (int16, bool) {
	if m.micIdx >= len(m.micSamples) {
		return 0, false
	}
	v := m.micSamples[m.micIdx]
	m.micIdx++
	return v, true
}

// stateVersion is the save-state format version. Version 3
// adds the geometry engine and sound unit blocks; version 2
// states are rejected.
const stateVersion = 3

// trailerSize is the fixed machine-state block after the
// device states.
const trailerSize = 32

// StateSize is the exact serialized size of a machine state.
const StateSize = 1 + bus.StateSize + 2*armcore.StateSize +
	periph.StateSize + video.StateSize + gx.StateSize +
	audio.StateSize + trailerSize

// Serialize writes the full machine state. The cartridge
// image itself is not part of the state; Deserialize expects
// a machine that already loaded the same ROM.
func (m *Machine) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	out[0] = stateVersion
	n := 1
	n += m.Bus.Serialize(out[n:])
	n += m.CPU9.Serialize(out[n:])
	n += m.CPU7.Serialize(out[n:])
	n += m.Periph.Serialize(out[n:])
	n += m.Video.Serialize(out[n:])
	n += m.GX.Serialize(out[n:])
	n += m.Audio.Serialize(out[n:])
	t := out[n:]
	if m.started9 {
		t[0] |= 1
	}
	if m.started7 {
		t[0] |= 2
	}
	put32 := func(at int, v uint32) {
		t[at] = byte(v)
		t[at+1] = byte(v >> 8)
		t[at+2] = byte(v >> 16)
		t[at+3] = byte(v >> 24)
	}
	put32(4, m.buttons)
	t[8] = byte(m.touchX)
	t[9] = byte(m.touchX >> 8)
	t[10] = byte(m.touchY)
	t[11] = byte(m.touchY >> 8)
	if m.touchDown {
		t[12] = 1
	}
	put32(16, uint32(m.micIdx))
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize into this
// machine, which must already have loaded the same cartridge.
func (m *Machine) Deserialize(src []byte) bool {
	if len(src) < StateSize || src[0] != stateVersion {
		return false
	}
	n := 1
	if !m.Bus.Deserialize(src[n:]) {
		return false
	}
	n += bus.StateSize
	if !m.CPU9.Deserialize(src[n:]) {
		return false
	}
	n += armcore.StateSize
	if !m.CPU7.Deserialize(src[n:]) {
		return false
	}
	n += armcore.StateSize
	n += m.Periph.Deserialize(src[n:])
	n += m.Video.Deserialize(src[n:])
	n += m.GX.Deserialize(src[n:])
	n += m.Audio.Deserialize(src[n:])
	t := src[n:]
	m.started9 = t[0]&1 != 0
	m.started7 = t[0]&2 != 0
	m.buttons = uint32(t[4]) | uint32(t[5])<<8 | uint32(t[6])<<16 | uint32(t[7])<<24
	m.touchX = uint16(t[8]) | uint16(t[9])<<8
	m.touchY = uint16(t[10]) | uint16(t[11])<<8
	m.touchDown = t[12] != 0
	m.micIdx = int(uint32(t[16]) | uint32(t[17])<<8 | uint32(t[18])<<16 | uint32(t[19])<<24)
	return true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/system/system_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// syntheticROM builds the DS-1 proof cartridge: the ARM9 program
// writes a magic word into shared WRAM bank 0, and the ARM7
// program reads it back, increments it, and writes the result to
// the next word. Both programs are hand-assembled below.
//
//	ARM9 (loads at 0x02000000):
//	  MOV R1, #0x03000000    E3A01403
//	  MOV R2, #0xAB000000    E3A024AB
//	  STR R2, [R1]           E5812000
//	  B .                    EAFFFFFE
//
//	ARM7 (loads at 0x03800000):
//	  MOV R1, #0x03000000    E3A01403
//	  LDR R2, [R1]           E5912000
//	  ADD R2, R2, #1         E2822001
//	  STR R2, [R1, #4]       E5812004
//	  B .                    EAFFFFFE
func syntheticROM() []byte {
	rom := make([]byte, 0x4000)
	copy(rom[0x000:], "DS1 PROOF")
	copy(rom[0x00C:], "ADSP")
	copy(rom[0x010:], "01")
	le := binary.LittleEndian
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x020:], 0x1000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x024:], 0x02000000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x028:], 0x02000000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x02C:], 16)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x030:], 0x2000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x034:], 0x03800000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x038:], 0x03800000)
	le.PutUint32(rom[0x03C:], 20)
	arm9prog := []uint32{0xE3A01403, 0xE3A024AB, 0xE5812000, 0xEAFFFFFE}
	for i, w := range arm9prog {
		le.PutUint32(rom[0x1000+i*4:], w)
	}
	arm7prog := []uint32{0xE3A01403, 0xE5912000, 0xE2822001, 0xE5812004, 0xEAFFFFFE}
	for i, w := range arm7prog {
		le.PutUint32(rom[0x2000+i*4:], w)
	}
	return rom
}

func sharedWord(m *Machine, off int) uint32 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(m.Bus.Shared[off:])
}

// TestDualCPUDeterminism is the DS-1 system gate: the two CPUs
// communicate through shared WRAM under WRAMCNT ownership, and a
// mid-run save state restores to a byte-identical continuation.
func TestDualCPUDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	rom := syntheticROM()

	// Phase 1: ARM9 owns both shared banks and writes the magic.
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.Bus.SetWRAMCNT(3)
	m.Start9()
	m.RunFrame()
	if got := sharedWord(m, 0); got != 0xAB000000 {
		t.Fatalf("phase 1: shared word 0 = %08x, want AB000000", got)
	}

	// Save mid-run, with the ARM7 not yet started.
	saved := m.Serialize()
	if len(saved) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size: got %d want %d", len(saved), StateSize)
	}

	// Phase 2: hand both banks to the ARM7 and let it answer.
	m.Bus.SetWRAMCNT(0)
	m.Start7()
	m.RunFrame()
	if got := sharedWord(m, 4); got != 0xAB000001 {
		t.Fatalf("phase 2: shared word 1 = %08x, want AB000001", got)
	}
	wantShared := append([]byte(nil), m.Bus.Shared...)
	wantState := m.Serialize()

	// Restore the mid-run state into a fresh machine and replay
	// phase 2: the outcome must be byte-identical.
	f := New()
	if err := f.LoadROM(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !f.Deserialize(saved) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize refused the mid-run state")
	}
	f.Bus.SetWRAMCNT(0)
	f.Start7()
	f.RunFrame()
	if !bytes.Equal(f.Bus.Shared, wantShared) {
		t.Fatal("restored run: shared WRAM differs from the direct run")
	}
	if got := f.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Fatal("restored run: full state differs from the direct run")
	}
}

func TestLoadROMStaging(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadROM(syntheticROM()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(m.Bus.MainRAM[0:]); got != 0xE3A01403 {
		t.Errorf("ARM9 binary not staged in main RAM: %08x", got)
	}
	if got := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(m.Bus.ARM7WRAM[0:]); got != 0xE3A01403 {
		t.Errorf("ARM7 binary not staged in ARM7 WRAM: %08x", got)
	}
	if m.CPU9.R[15] != 8 && !m.CPU9.Halted {
		t.Error("CPU9 should sit halted after staging")
	}
	h := m.Header()
	if h == nil || h.Title != "DS1 PROOF" {
		t.Errorf("header: %+v", h)
	}
	if err := New().LoadROM([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Error("tiny image accepted")
	}
}

func TestFramebufferAndInputs(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	top, bottom := m.Framebuffer()
	if len(top) != ScreenWidth*ScreenHeight || len(bottom) != ScreenWidth*ScreenHeight {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer sizes: %d %d", len(top), len(bottom))
	}
	for i, v := range top {
		if v != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("top buffer not blank at %d: %08x", i, v)
		}
	}
	m.SetButtons(0x201)
	if m.Buttons() != 0x201 {
		t.Errorf("buttons: %08x", m.Buttons())
	}
	m.SetTouch(100, 50, true)
	if x, y, down := m.Touch(); x != 100 || y != 50 || !down {
		t.Errorf("touch: %d %d %v", x, y, down)
	}
	// Inputs ride along in the save state.
	st := m.Serialize()
	f := New()
	if !f.Deserialize(st) {
		t.Fatal("Deserialize refused")
	}
	if f.Buttons() != 0x201 {
		t.Errorf("restored buttons: %08x", f.Buttons())
	}
	if x, y, down := f.Touch(); x != 100 || y != 50 || !down {
		t.Errorf("restored touch: %d %d %v", x, y, down)
	}
	if f.Deserialize([]byte{9}) {
		t.Error("garbage state accepted")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/video/capture.go ====================

package video

// Display capture (DISPCAPCNT at 0x04000064), with the
// documented simplifications: source A is engine A's
// composed line before master brightness (the hardware's
// 3D+2D mix; the 3D layer takes part since DS-3), source B
// is read as
// 15bpp pixels from a VRAM bank at the same coordinates the
// write offset addresses (the hardware's separate source
// addressing is not modeled), and capture completes at the
// end of the last captured line, clearing enable and busy.
// Sizes: 0 = 128x128, 1 = 256x64, 2 = 256x128, 3 = 256x192.
// The write offset (bits 18-19) is in 32 KB units; the source
// select (bit 25) applies when the blend bit (24) is clear.

var capSizes = [4][2]int{{128, 128}, {256, 64}, {256, 128}, {256, 192}}

// CaptureLine runs one line of an armed capture. The system
// calls it after rendering each visible line.
func (v *Video) CaptureLine(y int) {
	if !v.capOn {
		return
	}
	cap := v.rd32(0x064)
	w, h := capSizes[(cap>>20)&3][0], capSizes[(cap>>20)&3][1]
	if y >= h {
		return
	}
	dst := v.bus.VRAMBank(int(cap>>16) & 3)
	srcB := v.bus.VRAMBank(int(cap>>26) & 3)
	writeOff := int(cap>>18&3) * 0x8000
	blendAB := cap&(1<<24) != 0
	selB := cap&(1<<25) != 0
	eva := int(cap & 0x1F)
	evb := int(cap >> 8 & 0x1F)
	to5 := func(c uint32) (uint32, uint32, uint32) {
		return (c >> 1) & 31, (c >> 7) & 31, (c >> 13) & 31
	}
	for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
		addr := writeOff + (y*w+x)*2
		if addr+2 > len(dst) {
			break
		}
		ar, ag, ab := to5(v.lineA[x])
		var r, g, b uint32
		if blendAB || selB {
			sw := uint16(srcB[addr]) | uint16(srcB[addr+1])<<8
			br, bg, bb := uint32(sw&31), uint32(sw>>5&31), uint32(sw>>10&31)
			if blendAB {
				mix := func(a, s uint32) uint32 {
					val := (int(a)*eva + int(s)*evb) >> 4
					if val > 31 {
						val = 31
					}
					return uint32(val)
				}
				r, g, b = mix(ar, br), mix(ag, bg), mix(ab, bb)
			} else {
				r, g, b = br, bg, bb
			}
		} else {
			r, g, b = ar, ag, ab
		}
		w16 := uint16(r) | uint16(g)<<5 | uint16(b)<<10 | 0x8000
		dst[addr] = byte(w16)
		dst[addr+1] = byte(w16 >> 8)
	}
	v.capLine++
	if y == h-1 {
		v.capOn = false
		cap = v.rd32(0x064)
		v.wr32(0x064, cap&^(1<<31|1<<29))
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/video/composite.go ====================

package video

// Per-line compositing: priority merge of the four BGs and the
// OBJ layer over the backdrop, window masking, and the DS
// color effects (alpha blending and brightness up/down via
// BLDCNT/BLDALPHA/BLDY), in rgb6 space. Master brightness is
// applied by the caller after compositing; display capture
// takes this pre-brightness line.

type cand struct {
	c      uint32
	on     bool
	layer  int // 0-3 BG, 4 OBJ, 5 backdrop
	prio   int
	semi   bool
	target int // BLDCNT bit index of this layer
}

// composite merges the rendered layers for one line.
func (lc *lineCtx) composite() [Width]uint32 {
	v := lc.v
	var out [Width]uint32
	bgPrio := [4]int{}
	for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
		bgPrio[bg] = int(v.rd16(lc.base+8+2*bg) & 3)
		lc.bgOn[bg] = false
		for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
			if lc.bg[bg][x].ok {
				lc.bgOn[bg] = true
				break
			}
		}
	}
	winEn := lc.dispcnt & 0xE000
	bld := v.rd16(lc.base + 0x50)
	bldMode := (bld >> 6) & 3
	eva := int(v.rd16(lc.base+0x52) & 0x1F)
	evb := int(v.rd16(lc.base+0x52) >> 8 & 0x1F)
	bldy := int(v.rd16(lc.base+0x54) & 0x1F)
	if eva > 16 {
		eva = 16
	}
	if evb > 16 {
		evb = 16
	}
	if bldy > 16 {
		bldy = 16
	}
	backdrop := v.stdPal(lc.e, false, 0)
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		mask := uint32(0x3F)
		if winEn != 0 {
			mask = lc.windowMask(x)
		}
		// Collect present candidates in layer order and pick
		// the top two by (priority, layer order).
		var cs [6]cand
		n := 0
		for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
			if lc.bg[bg][x].ok && mask&(1<<uint(bg)) != 0 {
				cs[n] = cand{c: lc.bg[bg][x].c, on: true, layer: bg, prio: bgPrio[bg], target: bg}
				n++
			}
		}
		if lc.obj[x].ok && mask&0x10 != 0 {
			cs[n] = cand{c: lc.obj[x].c, on: true, layer: 4, prio: int(lc.obj[x].prio), semi: lc.obj[x].semi, target: 4}
			n++
		}
		cs[n] = cand{c: backdrop, on: true, layer: 5, prio: 4, target: 5}
		n++
		top, second := cs[0], cand{}
		for _, c := range cs[1:n] {
			if c.prio < top.prio || c.prio == top.prio && c.layer < top.layer {
				second, top = top, c
			} else if !second.on || c.prio < second.prio || c.prio == second.prio && c.layer < second.layer {
				second = c
			}
		}
		c := top.c
		// A translucent 3D BG0 pixel on top blends over the
		// second candidate with its own per-pixel alpha
		// (EVA = A/2, EVB = 16 - A/2 in the blend's terms),
		// independent of BLDCNT and of the window color
		// effect bit: the documented 3D alpha path.
		blended3D := false
		if top.layer == 0 && lc.has3D && second.on {
			if a := int(lc.alpha3D[x]); a > 0 && a < 31 {
				c = blend(c, second.c, a/2, 16-a/2)
				blended3D = true
			}
		}
		if !blended3D && mask&0x20 != 0 {
			t1 := bld&(1<<uint(top.target)) != 0
			var t2 bool
			if second.on {
				t2 = bld&(1<<uint(8+second.target)) != 0
			}
			forceAlpha := top.semi && second.on && t2
			switch {
			case bldMode == 1 && t1 && t2 || forceAlpha:
				c = blend(c, second.c, eva, evb)
			case bldMode == 2 && t1:
				c = brighten(c, bldy, true)
			case bldMode == 3 && t1:
				c = brighten(c, bldy, false)
			}
		}
		out[x] = c
	}
	return out
}

// windowMask resolves the WININ/WINOUT layer mask for one
// pixel: WIN0 inside wins first, then WIN1, then the OBJ
// window, then outside.
func (lc *lineCtx) windowMask(x int) uint32 {
	v := lc.v
	inRect := func(n int) bool {
		wh := v.rd16(lc.base + 0x40 + 2*n)
		wv := v.rd16(lc.base + 0x44 + 2*n)
		x1, x2 := int(wh>>8), int(wh&0xFF)
		y1, y2 := int(wv>>8), int(wv&0xFF)
		inX := (x2 > x1 && x >= x1 && x < x2) || (x2 <= x1 && (x >= x1 || x < x2))
		inY := (y2 > y1 && lc.y >= y1 && lc.y < y2) || (y2 <= y1 && (lc.y >= y1 || lc.y < y2))
		return inX && inY
	}
	winIn := v.rd16(lc.base + 0x48)
	winOut := v.rd16(lc.base + 0x4A)
	if lc.dispcnt&0x2000 != 0 && inRect(0) {
		return uint32(winIn & 0x3F)
	}
	if lc.dispcnt&0x4000 != 0 && inRect(1) {
		return uint32(winIn >> 8 & 0x3F)
	}
	if lc.dispcnt&0x8000 != 0 && lc.objWin[x] {
		return uint32(winOut >> 8 & 0x3F)
	}
	return uint32(winOut & 0x3F)
}

func blend(a, b uint32, eva, evb int) uint32 {
	ch := func(x, y uint32) uint32 {
		v := (int(x)*eva + int(y)*evb) >> 4
		if v > 63 {
			v = 63
		}
		return uint32(v)
	}
	return rgb6(ch(a&63, b&63), ch(a>>6&63, b>>6&63), ch(a>>12&63, b>>12&63))
}

func brighten(c uint32, y int, up bool) uint32 {
	ch := func(v uint32) uint32 {
		if up {
			return v + (63-v)*uint32(y)>>4
		}
		return v - v*uint32(y)>>4
	}
	return rgb6(ch(c&63), ch(c>>6&63), ch(c>>12&63))
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/video/obj.go ====================

package video

// OBJ (sprite) rendering per engine, GBA entry format with the
// DS additions: OBJ mode 3 bitmap OBJs (direct color from the
// OBJ VRAM space at (attr2&0x3FF)*128 bytes per the documented
// 128-byte boundary, alpha bit 15), OBJ extended palettes for
// 8bpp OBJs, affine parameter sets with the double-size flag,
// and mosaic. The lowest OAM index wins a pixel.

var objSizes = [4][4][2]int{
	// shape 0: square
	{{8, 8}, {16, 16}, {32, 32}, {64, 64}},
	// shape 1: wide
	{{16, 8}, {32, 8}, {32, 16}, {64, 32}},
	// shape 2: tall
	{{8, 16}, {8, 32}, {16, 32}, {32, 64}},
	// shape 3: prohibited, treated as square
	{{8, 8}, {16, 16}, {32, 32}, {64, 64}},
}

func (v *Video) renderOBJ(lc *lineCtx) {
	sp := v.objSpace(lc.e)
	oam := v.bus.OAM[lc.e*0x400:]
	oneD := lc.dispcnt&0x10 != 0
	mosH, _ := lc.mosaic(true)
	for i := 127; i >= 0; i-- {
		attr0 := uint16(oam[i*8]) | uint16(oam[i*8+1])<<8
		attr1 := uint16(oam[i*8+2]) | uint16(oam[i*8+3])<<8
		attr2 := uint16(oam[i*8+4]) | uint16(oam[i*8+5])<<8
		affine := attr0&0x100 != 0
		if !affine && attr0&0x200 != 0 {
			continue // disabled
		}
		w, h := objSizes[attr0>>14][attr1>>14][0], objSizes[attr0>>14][attr1>>14][1]
		dw, dh := w, h
		if attr0&0x200 != 0 { // double-size (affine only)
			dw, dh = 2*w, 2*h
		}
		x0 := int(attr1 & 0x1FF)
		if x0 >= 256 {
			x0 -= 512
		}
		dy := (lc.y - int(attr0&0xFF)) & 0xFF
		if dy >= dh {
			continue
		}
		mode := (attr0 >> 10) & 3
		prio := uint8(attr2 >> 10 & 3)
		// Affine parameters (also fetched for the
		// non-affine path only when needed).
		var pa, pb, pc, pd int32
		if affine {
			g := int(attr1>>9) & 0x1F
			rd := func(k int) int32 {
				off := 6 + g*32 + k*8
				return int32(int16(uint16(oam[off]) | uint16(oam[off+1])<<8))
			}
			pa, pb, pc, pd = rd(0), rd(1), rd(2), rd(3)
		}
		for dx := 0; dx < dw; dx++ {
			sx := x0 + dx
			if sx < 0 || sx >= Width {
				continue
			}
			fdx := dx
			if attr0&0x1000 != 0 && mosH > 1 {
				fdx = dx - dx%mosH
			}
			var ox, oy int
			if affine {
				rx, ry := fdx-dw/2, dy-dh/2
				ox = int((pa*int32(rx)+pb*int32(ry))>>8) + w/2
				oy = int((pc*int32(rx)+pd*int32(ry))>>8) + h/2
				if ox < 0 || oy < 0 || ox >= w || oy >= h {
					continue
				}
			} else {
				ox, oy = fdx, dy
				if attr1&0x1000 != 0 {
					ox = w - 1 - ox
				}
				if attr1&0x2000 != 0 {
					oy = h - 1 - oy
				}
			}
			c, idx, ok := v.objPixel(lc, sp, attr0, attr2, ox, oy, w, oneD)
			if !ok || idx == 0 && mode != 3 {
				continue
			}
			if mode == 2 {
				lc.objWin[sx] = true
				continue
			}
			lc.obj[sx] = objPx{c: c, ok: true, semi: mode == 1, prio: prio}
		}
	}
}

// objPixel fetches one OBJ source pixel. It returns the rgb6
// color, the raw color index (for the OBJ window test), and
// whether the pixel is present at all.
func (v *Video) objPixel(lc *lineCtx, sp *space, attr0, attr2 uint16, ox, oy, w int, oneD bool) (uint32, int, bool) {
	tile := uint32(attr2 & 0x3FF)
	palNum := int(attr2 >> 12)
	if (attr0>>10)&3 == 3 {
		// Bitmap OBJ: direct color, 128 bytes per tile index
		// unit (the documented boundary simplification).
		addr := tile*128 + uint32(oy*w+ox)*2
		w16 := sp.get16(addr)
		if w16&0x8000 == 0 {
			return 0, 0, false
		}
		return rgb6From15(w16), 1, true
	}
	charsWide, rowChars := 1, 32
	if attr0&0x2000 != 0 {
		charsWide = 2
	}
	if oneD {
		rowChars = (w >> 3) * charsWide
	}
	charIdx := tile + uint32((oy>>3)*rowChars+(ox>>3)*charsWide)
	if attr0&0x2000 != 0 { // 8bpp
		idx := int(sp.get(charIdx*32 + uint32((oy&7)*8+(ox&7))))
		if idx == 0 {
			return 0, 0, false
		}
		if lc.dispcnt&(1<<31) != 0 {
			return rgb6From15(v.extOBJ[lc.e].get16(uint32(palNum*0x200 + idx*2))), idx, true
		}
		return v.stdPal(lc.e, true, idx), idx, true
	}
	b := sp.get(charIdx*32 + uint32((oy&7)*4+(ox&7)/2))
	nib := int(b & 15)
	if ox&1 != 0 {
		nib = int(b >> 4)
	}
	if nib == 0 {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	return v.stdPal(lc.e, true, palNum*16+nib), nib, true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/video/render.go ====================

package video

// Per-scanline renderer. Colors are carried internally as
// rgb6 (three 6-bit channels packed r | g<<6 | b<<12) and
// expanded to XRGB8888 only at the framebuffer.
//
// Layer kinds per (BG mode, engine, BG number), per the
// documented mode tables:
//
//	mode 0: text, text, text, text
//	mode 1: text, text, text, affine
//	mode 2: text, text, affine, affine
//	mode 3: text, text, text, extended
//	mode 4: text, text, affine, extended
//	mode 5: text, text, extended, extended
//	mode 6: engine A: BG2 large bitmap only; engine B: as 5
//
// On engine A, a BG0 with DISPCNT bit 3 set is the 3D layer:
// the gx package fills it through the Line3D provider
// (DS-3); BG0Is3D exposes the condition.

const (
	kindNone = iota
	kindText
	kindAffine
	kindExtended
	kindLarge
)

func bgKind(mode uint32, e, bg int) int {
	if bg == 0 || bg == 1 {
		return kindText
	}
	switch mode {
	case 0:
		return kindText
	case 1:
		if bg == 2 {
			return kindText
		}
		return kindAffine
	case 2:
		return kindAffine
	case 3:
		if bg == 2 {
			return kindText
		}
		return kindExtended
	case 4:
		if bg == 2 {
			return kindAffine
		}
		return kindExtended
	case 5:
		return kindExtended
	case 6:
		if e == 0 {
			if bg == 2 {
				return kindLarge
			}
			return kindNone
		}
		return kindExtended
	}
	return kindNone
}

type px struct {
	c  uint32
	ok bool
}

type objPx struct {
	c    uint32
	ok   bool
	semi bool
	prio uint8
}

type lineCtx struct {
	v       *Video
	e       int
	base    int // IO offset of the engine's register page
	y       int
	dispcnt uint32
	bg      [4][Width]px
	bgOn    [4]bool
	obj     [Width]objPx
	objWin  [Width]bool
	line3D  [Width]uint32 // packed 3D provider output for this line
	alpha3D [Width]uint8  // per-pixel alpha of the 3D BG0 layer
	has3D   bool          // BG0 is the 3D layer on this line
}

func (v *Video) bgSpace(e int) *space {
	if e == 0 {
		return v.bgA
	}
	return v.bgB
}

func (v *Video) objSpace(e int) *space {
	if e == 0 {
		return v.objA
	}
	return v.objB
}

// stdPal reads a standard (non-extended) palette entry: BG at
// +0x000/+0x400 per engine, OBJ at +0x200/+0x600.
func (v *Video) stdPal(e int, obj bool, idx int) uint32 {
	base := e * 0x400
	if obj {
		base += 0x200
	}
	off := base + idx*2
	return rgb6From15(uint16(v.bus.Palette[off]) | uint16(v.bus.Palette[off+1])<<8)
}

// pal256 returns the 256-color palette entry for a BG layer,
// honoring the extended palette slot when BG extended
// palettes are enabled.
func (v *Video) pal256(lc *lineCtx, bg, idx int) uint32 {
	if lc.dispcnt&(1<<30) != 0 {
		return rgb6From15(lc.v.extBG[lc.e].get16(uint32(bg*0x2000 + idx*2)))
	}
	return lc.v.stdPal(lc.e, false, idx)
}

// RenderLine renders line y of both engines into the A and B
// framebuffers and records engine A's composed line (before
// master brightness) for display capture.
func (v *Video) RenderLine(y int) {
	v.maybeRebuildMaps()
	v.renderEngine(0, y, v.A)
	v.renderEngine(1, y, v.B)
}

func (v *Video) renderEngine(e, y int, out []uint32) {
	base := e * 0x1000
	row := out[y*Width : (y+1)*Width]
	pow := v.powcnt()
	dispcnt := v.rd32(base)
	engineOn := pow&1 != 0 && (e == 0 && pow&2 != 0 || e == 1 && pow&0x200 != 0)
	fill := func(c6 uint32) {
		w := xrgb(c6)
		for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
			row[x] = w
			if e == 0 {
				v.lineA[x] = c6
			}
		}
	}
	if !engineOn {
		fill(0) // powered down: black
		return
	}
	mode := (dispcnt >> 16) & 3
	if dispcnt&0x80 != 0 || mode == 0 {
		fill(rgb6(63, 63, 63)) // forced blank / display off: white
		return
	}
	switch mode {
	case 2: // VRAM display: raw 15bpp from the selected bank
		bank := v.bus.VRAMBank(int(dispcnt>>18) & 3)
		for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
			off := (y*Width + x) * 2
			c := rgb6From15(uint16(bank[off]) | uint16(bank[off+1])<<8)
			row[x] = xrgb(c)
			if e == 0 {
				v.lineA[x] = c
			}
		}
		return
	case 3: // main RAM display at the latched address
		for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
			off := (v.mainAdr + uint32(y*Width+x)*2) & (4<<20 - 1)
			c := rgb6From15(uint16(v.bus.MainRAM[off]) | uint16(v.bus.MainRAM[off+1])<<8)
			row[x] = xrgb(c)
			if e == 0 {
				v.lineA[x] = c
			}
		}
		return
	}
	lc := &lineCtx{v: v, e: e, base: base, y: y, dispcnt: dispcnt}
	lc.renderLayers()
	comp := lc.composite()
	mb := v.rd16(base + 0x6C)
	f := int(mb & 0x3F)
	if f > 16 {
		f = 16
	}
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		c := comp[x]
		if e == 0 {
			v.lineA[x] = c
		}
		row[x] = xrgb(applyMaster(c, mb>>14&3, f))
	}
}

// applyMaster applies one MASTER_BRIGHT mode (1 up, 2 down)
// with the clamped factor to an rgb6 pixel.
func applyMaster(c uint32, mode uint16, f int) uint32 {
	if mode != 1 && mode != 2 {
		return c
	}
	ch := func(v uint32) uint32 {
		if mode == 1 {
			return v + (63-v)*uint32(f)>>4
		}
		return v - v*uint32(f)>>4
	}
	return rgb6(ch(c&63), ch(c>>6&63), ch(c>>12&63))
}

func (lc *lineCtx) renderLayers() {
	v := lc.v
	mode := lc.dispcnt & 7
	for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
		if lc.dispcnt&(1<<uint(8+bg)) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		if bg == 0 && lc.e == 0 && lc.dispcnt&8 != 0 {
			// The 3D layer: fill BG0 from the rendering
			// engine's line provider when one is installed;
			// without one it stays transparent.
			if v.Line3D != nil {
				lc.has3D = true
				v.Line3D(lc.y, &lc.line3D)
				for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
					packed := lc.line3D[x]
					a := uint8(packed >> 18)
					if a == 0 {
						continue
					}
					lc.bg[0][x] = px{c: packed & 0x3FFFF, ok: true}
					lc.alpha3D[x] = a
				}
			}
			continue
		}
		switch bgKind(mode, lc.e, bg) {
		case kindText:
			v.renderTextBG(lc, bg)
		case kindAffine:
			v.renderAffineBG(lc, bg)
		case kindExtended:
			v.renderExtendedBG(lc, bg)
		case kindLarge:
			v.renderLargeBG(lc, bg)
		}
	}
	if lc.dispcnt&0x1000 != 0 {
		v.renderOBJ(lc)
	}
}

// mosaicH returns the horizontal mosaic size for a layer class
// (BG or OBJ) from the engine's MOSAIC register.
func (lc *lineCtx) mosaic(isOBJ bool) (int, int) {
	m := lc.v.rd16(lc.base + 0x4C)
	if isOBJ {
		return int(m>>8&0xF) + 1, int(m>>12&0xF) + 1
	}
	return int(m&0xF) + 1, int(m>>4&0xF) + 1
}

// renderTextBG renders one text-mode background line (GBA
// semantics: 4bpp/8bpp tiles, screen block layout, flips,
// palette banks), with mosaic quantization of the fetch
// coordinates.
func (v *Video) renderTextBG(lc *lineCtx, bg int) {
	sp := v.bgSpace(lc.e)
	cnt := v.rd16(lc.base + 8 + 2*bg)
	charBase := uint32(cnt>>2&0x1F) * 0x4000
	scrBase := uint32(cnt>>8&0x1F) * 0x800
	wTiles := 32 << (cnt >> 14 & 1)
	sx := int(v.rd16(lc.base+0x10+4*bg) & 0x1FF)
	sy := int(v.rd16(lc.base+0x12+4*bg) & 0x1FF)
	mh, mv := 1, 1
	if cnt&0x40 != 0 {
		mh, mv = lc.mosaic(false)
	}
	fy := lc.y + sy
	if mv > 1 {
		fy -= fy % mv
	}
	tileY := fy >> 3
	blockRow := (tileY >> 5) * (wTiles >> 5)
	eightBit := cnt&0x80 != 0
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		fx := x + sx
		if mh > 1 {
			fx -= fx % mh
		}
		tileX := fx >> 3
		block := scrBase + uint32(blockRow+(tileX>>5))*0x800
		entry := sp.get16(block + uint32((tileY&31)*32+(tileX&31))*2)
		tile := uint32(entry & 0x3FF)
		pxx, pyy := fx&7, fy&7
		if entry&0x400 != 0 {
			pxx = 7 - pxx
		}
		if entry&0x800 != 0 {
			pyy = 7 - pyy
		}
		var idx int
		if eightBit {
			idx = int(sp.get(charBase + tile*64 + uint32(pyy*8+pxx)))
			if idx == 0 {
				continue
			}
			lc.bg[bg][x] = px{c: v.pal256(lc, bg, idx), ok: true}
		} else {
			b := sp.get(charBase + tile*32 + uint32(pyy*4+pxx/2))
			nib := int(b>>4) & 15
			if pxx&1 == 0 {
				nib = int(b & 15)
			}
			if nib == 0 {
				continue
			}
			lc.bg[bg][x] = px{c: v.stdPal(lc.e, false, int(entry>>12)*16+nib), ok: true}
		}
	}
}

// affineSample computes the source pixel for screen x of an
// affine layer: the reference point advanced by the matrix.
// ok=false means the sample falls outside the layer bounds
// with wrap disabled.
func (lc *lineCtx) affineSample(bg int, x int, sizePx int, wrap bool) (int, int, bool) {
	base := lc.base + 0x20 + (bg-2)*0x10
	pa := int32(int16(lc.v.rd16(base)))
	refX := lc.v.refX[lc.e][bg] + pa*int32(x)
	refY := lc.v.refY[lc.e][bg] + int32(int16(lc.v.rd16(base+4)))*int32(x)
	tx, ty := int(refX>>8), int(refY>>8)
	if wrap {
		tx &= sizePx - 1
		ty &= sizePx - 1
		return tx, ty, true
	}
	if tx < 0 || ty < 0 || tx >= sizePx || ty >= sizePx {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	return tx, ty, true
}

// renderAffineBG renders one affine background line (8bpp
// tiles over a square map).
func (v *Video) renderAffineBG(lc *lineCtx, bg int) {
	sp := v.bgSpace(lc.e)
	cnt := v.rd16(lc.base + 8 + 2*bg)
	charBase := uint32(cnt>>2&0x1F) * 0x4000
	scrBase := uint32(cnt>>8&0x1F) * 0x800
	mapTiles := 16 << (cnt >> 14 & 3)
	wrap := cnt&0x2000 != 0
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		tx, ty, ok := lc.affineSample(bg, x, mapTiles*8, wrap)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		tile := sp.get(scrBase + uint32((ty>>3)*mapTiles+(tx>>3)))
		idx := int(sp.get(charBase + uint32(tile)*64 + uint32((ty&7)*8+(tx&7))))
		if idx == 0 {
			continue
		}
		lc.bg[bg][x] = px{c: v.pal256(lc, bg, idx), ok: true}
	}
}

// renderExtendedBG renders one extended background line:
// affine-extended tile mode (BGxCNT bit 2 clear) or bitmap
// mode (bit 2 set), per the documented decode in the header
// of this slice's design notes.
func (v *Video) renderExtendedBG(lc *lineCtx, bg int) {
	sp := v.bgSpace(lc.e)
	cnt := v.rd16(lc.base + 8 + 2*bg)
	wrap := cnt&0x2000 != 0
	if cnt&4 == 0 {
		// Affine-extended tiles: 16-bit map entries (tile
		// 0-13, H flip 14, V flip 15), 8bpp tile data.
		charBase := uint32(cnt>>2&0x1F) * 0x4000
		scrBase := uint32(cnt>>8&0x1F) * 0x800
		mapTiles := 16 << (cnt >> 14 & 3)
		for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
			tx, ty, ok := lc.affineSample(bg, x, mapTiles*8, wrap)
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			entry := sp.get16(scrBase + uint32((ty>>3)*mapTiles+(tx>>3))*2)
			pxx, pyy := tx&7, ty&7
			if entry&0x4000 != 0 {
				pxx = 7 - pxx
			}
			if entry&0x8000 != 0 {
				pyy = 7 - pyy
			}
			idx := int(sp.get(charBase + uint32(entry&0x3FFF)*64 + uint32(pyy*8+pxx)))
			if idx == 0 {
				continue
			}
			lc.bg[bg][x] = px{c: v.pal256(lc, bg, idx), ok: true}
		}
		return
	}
	// Bitmap mode.
	sizes := [4][2]int{{128, 128}, {256, 256}, {512, 256}, {512, 512}}
	w, h := sizes[cnt>>14&3][0], sizes[cnt>>14&3][1]
	dataBase := uint32(cnt>>8&0x1F) * 0x4000
	direct := cnt&0x80 != 0
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		tx, ty, ok := lc.affineSampleWH(bg, x, w, h, wrap)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		if direct {
			w16 := sp.get16(dataBase + uint32(ty*w+tx)*2)
			if w16&0x8000 == 0 {
				continue
			}
			lc.bg[bg][x] = px{c: rgb6From15(w16), ok: true}
		} else {
			idx := int(sp.get(dataBase + uint32(ty*w+tx)))
			if idx == 0 {
				continue
			}
			lc.bg[bg][x] = px{c: rgb6From15(v.extBG[lc.e].get16(uint32(bg*0x2000 + idx*2))), ok: true}
		}
	}
}

// affineSampleWH is affineSample for rectangular layers.
func (lc *lineCtx) affineSampleWH(bg, x, w, h int, wrap bool) (int, int, bool) {
	base := lc.base + 0x20 + (bg-2)*0x10
	pa := int32(int16(lc.v.rd16(base)))
	refX := lc.v.refX[lc.e][bg] + pa*int32(x)
	refY := lc.v.refY[lc.e][bg] + int32(int16(lc.v.rd16(base+4)))*int32(x)
	tx, ty := int(refX>>8), int(refY>>8)
	if wrap {
		tx = ((tx % w) + w) % w
		ty = ((ty % h) + h) % h
		return tx, ty, true
	}
	if tx < 0 || ty < 0 || tx >= w || ty >= h {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	return tx, ty, true
}

// renderLargeBG renders engine A's mode-6 BG2 large bitmap
// (direct color, affine parameters apply, data base 0 of the
// BG A space; a documented simplification of the hardware's
// base-offset selection).
func (v *Video) renderLargeBG(lc *lineCtx, bg int) {
	sp := v.bgSpace(lc.e)
	cnt := v.rd16(lc.base + 8 + 2*bg)
	sizes := [4][2]int{{512, 1024}, {1024, 512}, {512, 512}, {1024, 1024}}
	w, h := sizes[cnt>>14&3][0], sizes[cnt>>14&3][1]
	wrap := cnt&0x2000 != 0
	for x := 0; x < Width; x++ {
		tx, ty, ok := lc.affineSampleWH(bg, x, w, h, wrap)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		w16 := sp.get16(uint32(ty*w+tx) * 2)
		if w16&0x8000 == 0 {
			continue
		}
		lc.bg[bg][x] = px{c: rgb6From15(w16), ok: true}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/video/state.go ====================

package video

// StateSize is the serialized size of the video unit's own
// state (VRAM, palette, and OAM contents live in the bus
// stores and serialize there; the framebuffers are rebuilt by
// rendering).
const StateSize = 80

// Serialize writes the video state into dst.
func (v *Video) Serialize(dst []byte) int {
	n := 0
	put16 := func(x uint16) { dst[n] = byte(x); dst[n+1] = byte(x >> 8); n += 2 }
	put32 := func(x uint32) { put16(uint16(x)); put16(uint16(x >> 16)) }
	put16(v.lyc)
	dst[n] = v.dsEn
	n++
	dst[n] = 0
	n++
	put16(uint16(v.vcount))
	if v.hblank {
		dst[n] = 1
	}
	n++
	dst[n] = 0
	n++
	for e := 0; e < 2; e++ {
		for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
			put32(uint32(v.refX[e][bg]))
			put32(uint32(v.refY[e][bg]))
		}
	}
	if v.capOn {
		dst[n] = 1
	}
	n++
	put16(uint16(v.capLine))
	dst[n] = 0
	n++
	put32(v.mainAdr)
	return n
}

// Deserialize restores the video state and marks the VRAM
// assignment maps for rebuild.
func (v *Video) Deserialize(src []byte) int {
	n := 0
	get16 := func() uint16 { x := uint16(src[n]) | uint16(src[n+1])<<8; n += 2; return x }
	get32 := func() uint32 { return uint32(get16()) | uint32(get16())<<16 }
	v.lyc = get16()
	v.dsEn = src[n]
	n += 2
	v.vcount = int(get16())
	v.hblank = src[n] != 0
	n += 2
	for e := 0; e < 2; e++ {
		for bg := 0; bg < 4; bg++ {
			v.refX[e][bg] = int32(get32())
			v.refY[e][bg] = int32(get32())
		}
	}
	v.capOn = src[n] != 0
	n++
	v.capLine = int(get16())
	n++
	v.mainAdr = get32()
	v.mapsDirty = true
	return n
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/video/video.go ====================

// Package video implements the two DS 2D engines (A and B),
// the VRAM bank assignment layer the engines fetch through,
// DISPSTAT and VCOUNT, display capture, and the display
// timing model the system drives.
//
// Timing model (stated in the README): a frame is 263 lines
// (VCOUNT 0-262), 192 of them visible. The ARM9 cycle budget
// splits as 1536 cycles of visible dots plus 594 cycles of
// horizontal blank per line, and the ARM7 budget as 768 plus
// 297, which reproduces the DS-1 frame budgets of 560,190 and
// 280,095 cycles exactly. Rendering happens per scanline from
// the register and VRAM state at line start, like the rest of
// this core family. The main-memory display FIFO is not
// modeled; display mode 3 reads main RAM at a latched address.
package video

import (
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
)

// Screen geometry and timing.
const (
	Width        = 256
	Height       = 192
	LinesTotal   = 263
	CyclesLineA9 = 1536 // visible portion of a line, ARM9 cycles
	CyclesLineB9 = 594  // hblank portion
	CyclesLineA7 = 768
	CyclesLineB7 = 297
)

// space is one VRAM fetch space: an array of chunks aliased
// into the physical banks, indexed by address. Unassigned
// chunks read as 0.
type space struct {
	chunks [][]byte
	shift  uint
	size   uint32
}

func newSpace(chunks int, shift uint, size uint32) *space {
	return &space{chunks: make([][]byte, chunks), shift: shift, size: size}
}

func (s *space) get(addr uint32) byte {
	addr &= s.size - 1
	c := s.chunks[addr>>s.shift]
	if c == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return c[addr&((1<<s.shift)-1)]
}

func (s *space) get16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(s.get(addr)) | uint16(s.get(addr+1))<<8
}

func (s *space) put(addr uint32, data []byte) {
	n := 1 << s.shift
	for off := 0; off+n <= len(data); off += n {
		s.chunks[(addr+uint32(off))>>s.shift] = data[off : off+n]
	}
}

func (s *space) clear() {
	for i := range s.chunks {
		s.chunks[i] = nil
	}
}

// Video owns both engines' render state.
type Video struct {
	bus *bus.Bus
	A   []uint32 // engine A framebuffer, XRGB8888
	B   []uint32 // engine B framebuffer, XRGB8888

	// Line3D, when set, fills one scanline of the 3D layer
	// for engine A BG0: rgb6 colors with the 5-bit alpha in
	// bits 18-22; a zero entry is fully transparent. The
	// system installs the gx package's provider (DS-3).
	Line3D func(y int, dst *[Width]uint32)

	bgA, bgB   *space
	objA, objB *space
	extBG      [2]*space
	extOBJ     [2]*space
	cntCache   [9]byte
	mapsDirty  bool

	vcount  int
	hblank  bool
	lyc     uint16
	dsEn    uint8 // DISPSTAT IRQ enables: vblank, hblank, vcount
	refX    [2][4]int32
	refY    [2][4]int32
	lineA   [Width]uint32 // engine A composed line (rgb6), for capture
	capOn   bool
	capLine int
	mainAdr uint32 // latched main-RAM display address
}

// New builds the video unit over the shared bus.
func New(b *bus.Bus) *Video {
	v := &Video{
		bus:       b,
		A:         make([]uint32, Width*Height),
		B:         make([]uint32, Width*Height),
		bgA:       newSpace(32, 14, 0x80000),
		bgB:       newSpace(8, 14, 0x20000),
		objA:      newSpace(16, 14, 0x40000),
		objB:      newSpace(16, 14, 0x40000),
		mapsDirty: true,
	}
	v.extBG[0] = newSpace(4, 13, 0x8000)
	v.extBG[1] = newSpace(4, 13, 0x8000)
	v.extOBJ[0] = newSpace(2, 13, 0x4000)
	v.extOBJ[1] = newSpace(2, 13, 0x4000)
	return v
}

// IO read helpers over the ARM9 IO page (both engine pages live
// there).
func (v *Video) rd16(off int) uint16 {
	return uint16(v.bus.IO9[off]) | uint16(v.bus.IO9[off+1])<<8
}
func (v *Video) rd32(off int) uint32 {
	return uint32(v.rd16(off)) | uint32(v.rd16(off+2))<<16
}
func (v *Video) wr16(off int, val uint16) {
	v.bus.IO9[off] = byte(val)
	v.bus.IO9[off+1] = byte(val >> 8)
}
func (v *Video) wr32(off int, val uint32) {
	v.wr16(off, uint16(val))
	v.wr16(off+2, uint16(val>>16))
}

// POWCNT1 (IO9 0x304): bit 0 LCDs on, bit 1 engine A 2D on,
// bit 9 engine B 2D on, bit 15 swap displays (engine A on the
// bottom screen).
func (v *Video) powcnt() uint16 { return v.rd16(0x304) }

// Swapped reports the POWCNT1 display assignment.
func (v *Video) Swapped() bool { return v.powcnt()&0x8000 != 0 }

// BG0Is3D reports whether engine A's BG0 is selected as the 3D
// layer (DISPCNT bit 3). The gx package renders the layer
// through the Line3D provider.
func (v *Video) BG0Is3D() bool { return v.rd32(0)&8 != 0 }

// DISPSTAT returns the composed DISPSTAT halfword: live flags
// in bits 0-2 (VBlank, HBlank, VCount match), the stored IRQ
// enables in bits 3-5, and the 9-bit LYC in bits 8-15 plus
// bit 7.
func (v *Video) DISPSTAT() uint16 {
	var s uint16
	if v.vcount >= Height {
		s |= 1
	}
	if v.hblank {
		s |= 2
	}
	if uint16(v.vcount) == v.lyc {
		s |= 4
	}
	s |= uint16(v.dsEn&7) << 3
	s |= (v.lyc & 0x100) >> 1
	s |= (v.lyc & 0xFF) << 8
	return s
}

// SetDISPSTAT stores the writable DISPSTAT fields (IRQ enables
// and LYC) from a CPU write.
func (v *Video) SetDISPSTAT(val uint16) {
	v.dsEn = uint8(val >> 3 & 7)
	v.lyc = (val>>8)&0xFF | (val&0x80)<<1
}

// IRQEnabled reports whether a DISPSTAT source (0 VBlank,
// 1 HBlank, 2 VCount) has its IRQ enable set.
func (v *Video) IRQEnabled(kind int) bool { return v.dsEn>>uint(kind)&1 != 0 }

// LYC returns the VCount compare value.
func (v *Video) LYC() int { return int(v.lyc) }

// SetLine sets the current scanline (VCOUNT).
func (v *Video) SetLine(n int) { v.vcount = n }

// VCount returns the current scanline.
func (v *Video) VCount() int { return v.vcount }

// SetHBlank sets the hblank phase flag.
func (v *Video) SetHBlank(b bool) { v.hblank = b }

// SetMainDispAddr latches the main-RAM display address written
// to DISP_MMEM_FIFO (0x04000068).
func (v *Video) SetMainDispAddr(a uint32) { v.mainAdr = a }

// LatchAffine reloads both engines' affine reference points
// from their registers. The system calls it at the start of
// VBlank (line 192).
func (v *Video) LatchAffine() {
	for e := 0; e < 2; e++ {
		for bg := 2; bg < 4; bg++ {
			x, y := v.regRef(e, bg)
			v.refX[e][bg], v.refY[e][bg] = x, y
		}
	}
}

// regRef reads an affine BG's reference point registers as
// sign-extended 28-bit fixed-point values (8 fractional bits).
func (v *Video) regRef(e, bg int) (int32, int32) {
	base := e*0x1000 + 0x20 + (bg-2)*0x10
	x := int32(v.rd32(base + 8))
	y := int32(v.rd32(base + 12))
	if x&0x08000000 != 0 {
		x |= ^0x0FFFFFFF
	}
	if y&0x08000000 != 0 {
		y |= ^0x0FFFFFFF
	}
	return x, y
}

// AdvanceAffine steps both engines' affine reference points by
// their vertical parameters after a rendered line.
func (v *Video) AdvanceAffine() {
	for e := 0; e < 2; e++ {
		for bg := 2; bg < 4; bg++ {
			base := e*0x1000 + 0x20 + (bg-2)*0x10
			v.refX[e][bg] += int32(int16(v.rd16(base + 2))) // PB (dmx)
			v.refY[e][bg] += int32(int16(v.rd16(base + 6))) // PD (dmy)
		}
	}
}

// BeginFrame arms display capture if DISPCAPCNT enable is set.
func (v *Video) BeginFrame() {
	cap := v.rd32(0x064)
	if cap&(1<<31) != 0 && !v.capOn {
		v.capOn = true
		v.capLine = 0
		v.wr32(0x064, cap|(1<<29)) // busy
	}
}

// rgb6 packs three 6-bit channels.
func rgb6(r, g, b uint32) uint32 { return r | g<<6 | b<<12 }

// rgb6From15 converts a 15-bit palette color to rgb6 by the
// documented 5-to-6 expansion (c<<1)|(c>>4).
func rgb6From15(c uint16) uint32 {
	r := uint32(c & 31)
	g := uint32(c >> 5 & 31)
	b := uint32(c >> 10 & 31)
	return rgb6(r<<1|r>>4, g<<1|g>>4, b<<1|b>>4)
}

// xrgb expands an rgb6 pixel to XRGB8888 (6-to-8 by
// (c<<2)|(c>>4) per channel).
func xrgb(c uint32) uint32 {
	r := c & 63
	g := c >> 6 & 63
	b := c >> 12 & 63
	return 0xFF000000 | (r<<2|r>>4)<<16 | (g<<2|g>>4)<<8 | (b<<2 | b>>4)
}

package video_test

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nds/video"
)

// rig: a bus plus video unit with both engines powered
// (POWCNT1 = 0x020F) and bank A assigned to BG A.
type rig struct {
	b *bus.Bus
	v *video.Video
}

func newRig() *rig {
	b := bus.New()
	r := &rig{b: b, v: video.New(b)}
	r.w16(0x304, 0x020F)
	return r
}

func (r *rig) w16(off int, v uint16) {
	r.b.IO9[off] = byte(v)
	r.b.IO9[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
}
func (r *rig) w32(off int, v uint32) {
	r.w16(off, uint16(v))
	r.w16(off+2, uint16(v>>16))
}

// pal sets one standard palette entry (15bpp) for an engine
// palette page offset.
func (r *rig) pal(off int, c uint16) {
	r.b.Palette[off] = byte(c)
	r.b.Palette[off+1] = byte(c >> 8)
}

// solidTile4 fills a 4bpp tile (32 bytes) with one nibble.
func solidTile4(r *rig, bankOff int, nib byte) {
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		r.b.VRAM[bankOff+i] = nib | nib<<4
	}
}

// textSceneA builds the reusable engine A text scene: bank A
// to BG A, BG0 4bpp, tile 1 solid palette-1 at screen (0,0),
// tile 2 solid palette-2 at (1,0).
func textSceneA(r *rig) {
	r.b.IO9[0x240] = 0x81 // VRAMCNT A: BG A at 0
	r.w32(0x000, 0x00010100)
	r.w16(0x008, 0x0204) // BG0CNT: char base 0x4000, screen base 0x1000
	r.pal(0, 0x0000)
	r.pal(2, 0x001F) // palette 1: red
	r.pal(4, 0x03E0) // palette 2: green
	solidTile4(r, 0x4000+32, 1)
	solidTile4(r, 0x4000+64, 2)
	r.b.VRAM[0x1000] = 1 // screen entry (0,0) = tile 1
	r.b.VRAM[0x1002] = 2 // screen entry (1,0) = tile 2
}

func TestTextBGEngineA(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	textSceneA(r)
	r.v.RenderLine(0)
	if got := r.v.A[0]; got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("A pixel (0,0): %08x want FFFF0000 (red)", got)
	}
	if got := r.v.A[8]; got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Fatalf("A pixel (8,0): %08x want FF00FF00 (green)", got)
	}
	if got := r.v.A[16]; got != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Fatalf("A pixel (16,0): %08x want backdrop black", got)
	}
}
