func TestExtPaletteAssignment(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.b.IO9[0x240] = 0x81
	r.w32(0x000, 0x40010100) // BG0, graphics, BG ext palettes on
	r.w16(0x008, 0x0284)     // BG0CNT: 8bpp, char base 0x4000, screen base 0x1000
	r.pal(0, 0x7FFF)         // backdrop white
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		r.b.VRAM[0x4000+64+i] = 1 // 8bpp tile 1: index 1
	}
	r.b.VRAM[0x1000] = 1
	// No extended palette bank assigned: tiles read the empty
	// extended palette and come out black on white.
	r.v.RenderLine(0)
	if got := r.v.A[0]; got != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Fatalf("no ext pal: %08x want black", got)
	}
	if got := r.v.A[8]; got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("backdrop: %08x want white", got)
	}
	// Assign bank E as BG extended palette A with entry 1 red.
	r.b.VRAM[0x80000+2] = 0x1F
	r.b.VRAM[0x80000+3] = 0x00
	r.b.IO9[0x244] = 0x84 // VRAMCNT E: MST 4 (BG ext palette A)
	r.v.RenderLine(0)
	if got := r.v.A[0]; got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("ext pal assigned: %08x want red", got)
	}
	// Move bank E to OBJ A: the extended palette goes away.
	r.b.IO9[0x244] = 0x82
	r.v.RenderLine(0)
	if got := r.v.A[0]; got != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Fatalf("ext pal removed: %08x want black", got)
	}
}

func TestVideoStateRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRig()
	r.v.SetDISPSTAT(0xFF08) // LYC 0xFF... plus enables
	r.v.SetLine(100)
	r.v.LatchAffine()
	blob := make([]byte, video.StateSize)
	if n := r.v.Serialize(blob); n != video.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("serialize n = %d want %d", n, video.StateSize)
	}
	r2 := newRig()
	if n := r2.v.Deserialize(blob); n != video.StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("deserialize n = %d want %d", n, video.StateSize)
	}
	if r2.v.LYC() != r.v.LYC() || r2.v.VCount() != 100 {
		t.Fatal("video scalars not restored")
	}
	blob2 := make([]byte, video.StateSize)
	r2.v.Serialize(blob2)
	for i := range blob {
		if blob[i] != blob2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("video state bytes differ at %d", i)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nds/video/vram.go ====================

package video

// VRAM bank assignment. The engines never fetch from the flat
// LCDC store directly; they fetch through five assignment
// spaces (BG A, BG B, OBJ A, OBJ B, and the extended palette
// spaces) built from the VRAMCNT bytes A-I (IO9 0x240-0x24A)
// per the documented mapping tables. LCDC CPU access to the
// physical banks in the bus is unaffected. Texture image and
// texture palette slots are decoded from the same bytes by
// the gx package (DS-3).
//
// VRAMCNT byte layout (GBATEK): bits 0-2 MST, bits 3-4 OFS,
// bit 7 enable. (DS-2 originally decoded enable at bit 0 and
// MST at bits 1-2; that layout contradicts GBATEK and was
// corrected in DS-3, with the DS-2 fixtures updated to the
// documented byte values.)
//
// Bank rules implemented (GBATEK):
//   - Banks A/B (128 KB): MST 1 = BG A at OFS*128 KB;
//     MST 2 = OBJ A at (OFS bit 0)*128 KB; MST 3 = texture
//     slot OFS (consumed by gx).
//   - Banks C/D (128 KB): MST 1 = BG A as above; MST 2 =
//     ARM7 WRAM image (decoded in the bus, not here); MST 3 =
//     texture slot (gx); MST 4 = BG B at 0 (bank C) or OBJ B
//     at 0 (bank D).
//   - Bank E (64 KB): MST 1 = BG A at 0; MST 2 = OBJ A at 0;
//     MST 3 = texture palette slots 0-3 (gx); MST 4 = BG
//     extended palette A, first 32 KB.
//   - Banks F/G (16 KB): MST 1 = BG A, MST 2 = OBJ A, both
//     at (OFS bit 0)*4 KB + (OFS bit 1)*64 KB; MST 3 =
//     texture palette slot (OFS bit 0) + (OFS bit 1)*4 (gx);
//     MST 4 = BG extended palette A slot pair selected by
//     OFS bit 0 (the 16 KB bank covers two 8 KB slots);
//     MST 5 = OBJ extended palette A (8 KB used).
//   - Bank H (32 KB): MST 1 = BG B at 0; MST 2 = BG extended
//     palette B (all 32 KB).
//   - Bank I (16 KB): MST 1 = BG B at 8 KB; MST 2 = OBJ B at
//     0; MST 3 = OBJ extended palette B.
//
// Later banks in A-I order overwrite earlier chunks in the
// same space.

// maybeRebuildMaps rebuilds the fetch spaces when the
// VRAMCNT bytes changed. The nine bank bytes are gathered
// explicitly: WRAMCNT sits at 0x247, between VRAMCNT G
// (0x246) and H (0x248).
func (v *Video) maybeRebuildMaps() {
	var cur [9]byte
	copy(cur[:7], v.bus.IO9[0x240:0x247])
	cur[7] = v.bus.IO9[0x248]
	cur[8] = v.bus.IO9[0x249]
	if !v.mapsDirty && cur == v.cntCache {
		return
	}
	v.cntCache = cur
	v.mapsDirty = false
	v.bgA.clear()
	v.bgB.clear()
	v.objA.clear()
	v.objB.clear()
	v.extBG[0].clear()
	v.extBG[1].clear()
	v.extOBJ[0].clear()
	v.extOBJ[1].clear()
	for bank := 0; bank < 9; bank++ {
		cnt := cur[bank]
		if cnt&0x80 == 0 {
			continue
		}
		data := v.bus.VRAMBank(bank)
		mst := cnt & 7
		ofs := (cnt >> 3) & 3
		switch bank {
		case 0, 1: // A, B: 128 KB
			switch mst {
			case 1:
				v.bgA.put(uint32(ofs)*0x20000, data)
			case 2:
				v.objA.put(uint32(ofs&1)*0x20000, data)
			}
		case 2, 3: // C, D: 128 KB
			switch mst {
			case 1:
				v.bgA.put(uint32(ofs)*0x20000, data)
			case 4:
				if bank == 2 {
					v.bgB.put(0, data)
				} else {
					v.objB.put(0, data)
				}
			}
		case 4: // E: 64 KB
			switch mst {
			case 1:
				v.bgA.put(0, data)
			case 2:
				v.objA.put(0, data)
			case 4:
				v.extBG[0].put(0, data[:0x8000])
			}
		case 5, 6: // F, G: 16 KB
			off14 := uint32(ofs&1)*0x4000 + uint32(ofs>>1)*0x10000
			switch mst {
			case 1:
				v.bgA.put(off14, data)
			case 2:
				v.objA.put(off14, data)
			case 4:
				v.extBG[0].put(uint32(ofs&1)*0x4000, data)
			case 5:
				// OBJ extended palette A (8 KB of the
				// bank used).
				v.extOBJ[0].put(0, data[:0x2000])
			}
		case 7: // H: 32 KB
			switch mst {
			case 1:
				v.bgB.put(0, data)
			case 2:
				v.extBG[1].put(0, data)
			}
		case 8: // I: 16 KB
			switch mst {
			case 1:
				v.bgB.put(0x8000, data)
			case 2:
				v.objB.put(0, data)
			case 3:
				v.extOBJ[1].put(0, data)
			}
		}
	}
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/README.md ====================

# go-nes: a Nintendo Entertainment System core written in Go

Clean-room NES emulator core for iTaK Gaming, written in Go and
exposed through the libretro API so the iTaK engine can load it
exactly like any other core.

Why this exists: the FCEUmm core bundled today is fine license-wise,
but David's standing rule for iTaK Gaming is that every system gets
its own from-scratch Go core, 100 percent our own code (MIT, same as
the rest of iTaK Gaming), written from published hardware
documentation: the MOS 6502 datasheet behavior as the NES's Ricoh
2A03 variant runs it (no decimal arithmetic), the documented
unofficial opcode behavior collected on the NESdev wiki, the
documented iNES and NES 2.0 header formats, and the documented
mapper (MMC1, MMC3, and friends) behavior.

Conformance is proven the standard way: Kevin Horton's nestest
(automated mode at $C000, result bytes at $0002/$0003 plus a
trace comparison against the golden log), and Blargg's test ROM
suites (the $6000 status and text protocol, the older
screen-report shells, and the 2005 RAM-code shell), run headless
against the system package in this module. The test ROMs are
public conformance suites, kept locally under `testroms/` and
never committed to the repository.

## Status

- NES-1: module skeleton, the 6502 CPU (`chips/cpu6502`,
  official plus documented unofficial opcodes, cycle counts from
  bus accesses), cartridge header parsing and mappers 0, 1, 2,
  3, 4, 7, 11, 66 (`cart`). Gates: nestest full pass, all 18
  Blargg instr_test-v5 ROMs pass.
- NES-2 (this slice): the PPU (`ppu/`, dot-stepped 341x262 NTSC
  timing with the odd-frame dot skip, the full register file
  with the loopy scroll machinery, background and sprite
  rendering with sprite 0 hit and the buggy overflow behavior,
  the published 64-color NTSC palette with emphasis, open-bus
  latch decay, and palette RAM with its mirrors) and the real
  machine in `system/`: the CPU steps cycle by cycle at 3 PPU
  dots per cycle with the access interleaved two dots in, NMI
  driven by the PPU's derived output line, OAM DMA at 513/514
  cycles by CPU parity, both controller ports, and the MMC3
  IRQ clocked from the PPU's A12 line through the documented
  glitch filter. Whole-machine save states serialize the CPU,
  cartridge and mapper state, the full PPU (registers, internal
  latches, pipeline and evaluation state, frame parity), RAM,
  the open bus byte, and the controller state; a determinism
  test proves a frame hash is identical across a
  serialize/restore boundary. The APU register space stayed
  inert through this slice and comes alive in NES-3.
- NES-3 (this slice, completing the core): the APU in
  `sound/` (two pulse channels with duty, sweep with the
  per-channel negate quirk, envelopes and length counters;
  the triangle with its linear counter; noise with both
  LFSR modes; the DMC with DMA sample fetches that stall the
  CPU through the bus, the output level unit, loop mode and
  its IRQ; the frame sequencer at APU rate with the 3-or-4
  cycle $4017 reset delay and the triple frame IRQ set at
  the sequence end; the $4015 status read that clears only
  the frame IRQ flag; and the published non-linear pulse/tnd
  mixer formulas rendered at 44100 Hz, mono duplicated to
  stereo), the libretro shell in `libretro/` mirroring
  go-gameboy's (24 retro_* exports, XRGB8888 256x240, 60.0988
  fps, 4/3 aspect), and the app wiring that points the NES
  row at libgo_nes.so. Save states grew a version-2 block
  carrying the full APU state; a state saved by this core
  restores byte-exact, proven on a real MMC3 game through
  the engine bridge (below).

## NES-2 conformance results

Hard gates (all passing): ppu_open_bus; the 2005 ppu tests
palette_ram, sprite_ram, vram_access, vbl_clear_time (through
the shell's RAM code); sprite_hit_tests 01-08 plus the
timing-grade 09-11 logged passing; sprite_overflow_tests 1 and
2 plus 3-5 logged passing; mmc3_irq_tests 1.Clocking,
3.A12_clocking, 6.MMC3_rev_B; ppu_vbl_nmi singles 01, 04, 05,
07, 08, 09, 10; vbl_nmi_timing 1, 6, 7. The older mmc3_test
set logs 1, 2, 3, 5 passing.

Report-only, with the reason on the test in
`system/conformance_test.go`: ppu_vbl_nmi 02, 03, 06 and the
combined ROM, and vbl_nmi_timing 2, 3, 4, 5 (a one-dot sync
residue tradeoff: the value family and the NMI-timing family
provably want the sync_vbl exit residue one dot apart under
any single $2002 read rule; the shipped rule is the
documented one, a read whose capture races the set dot
reports the flag clear). mmc3_irq_tests 2.Details case 7 and
4.Scanline_timing case 2, and mmc3_test 4-scanline_timing
case 2 (the pre-render line's first background fetch rise,
which follows the vblank-long A12 low, is counted by this
filter model: 242 clocks in the measured frame against the
expected 241, so the IRQ lands one clock early; every other
line and pattern-table arrangement counts exactly).
power_up_palette (palette RAM powers up cleared here rather
than with the measured hardware contents). cpu_timing_test
produces no verdict even given 900 million cycles (about
30,000 frames): it never reads $4015, its NMI handler is
entered and its timing counters advance, but its measurement
sequence never completes here; the precise verdict is on
TestCPUTimingReport. instr_timing 1/2 waited for NES-3
(they time against the APU length counters); both are hard
gates now, see the NES-3 results below.

## NES-3 conformance results

Hard gates (all passing): Blargg's apu_test singles, all
eight: 1-len_ctr, 2-len_table, 3-irq_flag, 4-jitter,
5-len_timing, 6-irq_flag_timing, 7-dmc_basics, 8-dmc_rates.
The last three are the cycle-grade ones: they pin the frame
sequencer's APU-rate stepping, the $4017 reset delay of 3
or 4 cycles by divider phase, and the frame IRQ flag's
triple set on the last three CPU cycles of the 4-step
sequence. Blargg's instr_timing 1 and 2, deferred from
NES-1 because they time against the APU length counters,
are hard gates now and pass. Unit gates in `sound/` cover
the sweep target overflow mute, the period-below-8 mute,
the envelope decay schedule, length halt and $4015 disable
behavior, DMC playback, loop restart and IRQ, and a
byte-exact APU serialize round trip whose restored copy
produces identical samples. A pulse channel playing A4
(period 253) measures 441.00 Hz, 3.9 cents sharp of 440
(the period's true pitch is 440.29 Hz; the reading is the
zero-crossing count over one second).

Report-only: Blargg's apu_mixer set (square, triangle,
noise, dmc). Each ROM runs its full tone and cancellation
sequence to the shell's done state here, but the verdict is
a human listening for near-silence between the beeps, so
there is no CPU-visible result to gate on; the test logs
the final status and the audio activity for the record.

Real games, through the iTaK engine bridge and the
from-scratch core (enginetest): Super Mario Bros. 3 (USA)
(MMC3) loads, renders non-blank 256x240 video, produces
non-silent audio, and writes a 15,063-byte save state; its
one harness flag (the frame 2 frames after a restore
differs from the save-point frame) is the harness's
static-screen premise, adjudicated the same way as the
Game Boy core's: the state re-saved immediately after the
restore differs from the saved state in 0 of 15,063 bytes,
and a 300-frame continuation from the restored state lands
byte-identical to the original continuation. Super Mario
Bros. (Japan, USA) (NROM) passes the full harness with no
flags: ALL TESTS PASSED, 15,050-byte states, the restored
frame matching the save point exactly.

## Layout

- `chips/cpu6502/` the Ricoh 2A03 CPU core (a MOS 6502 with the
  decimal flag wired off), pure Go, with exact flag behavior,
  interrupt polling at the documented poll point (sampled at
  every bus access, latched at the second-to-last), the NMI
  hijack of BRK, cycle counting by bus access, an RDY stall
  hook for DMA, and save-state serialization
- `cart/` iNES and NES 2.0 header parsing plus the memory
  mappers: NROM, MMC1, UxROM, CNROM, MMC3, AxROM, Color Dreams,
  GxROM
- `ppu/` the 2C02 picture processing unit: dot-stepped timing
  and rendering, the register file, and save-state
  serialization
- `sound/` the 2A03 APU: pulse, triangle, noise and DMC
  channels, the frame sequencer, the non-linear mixer, and
  save-state serialization
- `system/` the assembled machine: CPU, PPU, cartridge, RAM,
  controllers, DMA, and whole-machine save states, in the
  go-gameboy core's shape (RunFrame, Framebuffer,
  Serialize/Deserialize, SetButtons)
- `libretro/` the libretro C ABI shell (24 retro_* exports),
  mirroring the go-gameboy core's shell


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/cart/cart.go ====================

// Package cart loads and describes an NES cartridge image in the
// iNES and NES 2.0 formats, and implements the memory mappers
// (bank controllers) that page PRG and CHR memory through the
// CPU and PPU address spaces.
//
// Written clean-room from the published header layouts and the
// mapper behavior documented on the NESdev wiki. Cartridge RAM
// contents live in Cart's PRG RAM slice, which the system owns
// for battery persistence; mapper bank registers are kept in the
// mapper and serialized with it.
//
// NES-1 implements mappers 0 (NROM), 1 (MMC1), 2 (UxROM),
// 3 (CNROM), 4 (MMC3), 7 (AxROM), 11 (Color Dreams), and
// 66 (GxROM). The MMC3 IRQ counter is fully implemented here;
// the system clocks it from PPU address line A12 starting in
// NES-2.
package cart

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// Mirror describes a nametable mirroring arrangement. The header
// sets the default; several mappers override it dynamically.
type Mirror int

const (
	MirrorHorizontal Mirror = iota
	MirrorVertical
	MirrorSingle0
	MirrorSingle1
	MirrorFourScreen
)

func (m Mirror) String() string {
	switch m {
	case MirrorHorizontal:
		return "horizontal"
	case MirrorVertical:
		return "vertical"
	case MirrorSingle0:
		return "single screen (low)"
	case MirrorSingle1:
		return "single screen (high)"
	case MirrorFourScreen:
		return "four screen"
	}
	return "unknown"
}

// Header is the parsed cartridge header.
type Header struct {
	Mapper    int
	Submapper int
	NES2      bool // the image carries a NES 2.0 header

	PRGSize    int // PRG ROM bytes
	CHRSize    int // CHR ROM bytes (0 means CHR RAM)
	PRGRAMDecl int // CPU $6000-$7FFF RAM bytes the header declares
	CHRRAMDecl int // CHR RAM bytes the header declares

	Mirror     Mirror // as the header declares it
	Battery    bool
	Trainer    bool
	VS         bool // VS. System cartridge
	PlayChoice bool // PlayChoice-10 cartridge
}

// Cart is a loaded cartridge image.
type Cart struct {
	Header Header

	prg    []uint8 // PRG ROM
	chr    []uint8 // CHR ROM, or CHR RAM when chrIsRAM
	chrRAM bool
	prgRAM []uint8

	mapper mapper

	// cycle is the CPU cycle count of the most recent access,
	// fed by the system through SetCycle. MMC1 consults it for
	// the consecutive-write ignore quirk.
	cycle int64

	// a12Clocks counts ClockA12 calls (diagnostic).
	a12Clocks int64

	// Flat read fast paths for the unbanked NROM layout (the
	// only mapper that is a plain baseMapper): ReadPRG and
	// ReadCHR then index the ROM directly instead of paying
	// an interface dispatch and a modulo per access. prgMask
	// is len(prg)-1, valid because the flat path is armed
	// only for power-of-two PRG sizes; flatCHR requires the
	// fixed 8 KB CHR window.
	flatPRG bool
	prgMask int
	flatCHR bool

	// irqPossible is armed only for MMC3, the one mapper
	// whose irqPending can ever return true. syncLines on
	// the system polls IRQPending once per CPU cycle.
	irqPossible bool

	// Mirror mode memo: MirrorMode is polled by the PPU on
	// every nametable access (tens of thousands per frame),
	// and the answer changes only on a cartridge register
	// write or a state load, both of which clear mirrorOK.
	mirrorCache Mirror
	mirrorOK    bool
}

// mapper is the bank controller interface. Read and write at the
// PRG side cover $8000-$FFFF (the system routes $6000-$7FFF RAM
// through ramEnabled and Cart's own slice); the CHR side covers
// $0000-$1FFF.
type mapper interface {
	readPRG(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8
	writePRG(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8)
	readCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8
	writeCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8)
	mirror() (Mirror, bool) // ok false: use the header's
	ramEnabled() bool
	irqPending() bool
	clockA12()
	state() []byte
	setState([]byte) error
}

// baseMapper provides the NROM behavior plus the defaults every
// simple mapper shares: linear CHR, RAM enabled, no IRQ.
type baseMapper struct{}

func (baseMapper) readPRG(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	return c.prg[int(addr-0x8000)%len(c.prg)]
}
func (baseMapper) writePRG(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) {}
func (baseMapper) readCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	return c.chr[int(addr)%len(c.chr)]
}
func (baseMapper) writeCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if c.chrRAM {
		c.chr[int(addr)%len(c.chr)] = val
	}
}
func (baseMapper) mirror() (Mirror, bool) { return 0, false }
func (baseMapper) ramEnabled() bool       { return true }
func (baseMapper) irqPending() bool       { return false }
func (baseMapper) clockA12()              {}
func (baseMapper) state() []byte          { return nil }
func (baseMapper) setState([]byte) error  { return nil }

// bankOff returns the byte offset of a bank of the given unit
// size inside a ROM image, wrapping the bank number modulo the
// number of banks the image holds, as the hardware's unconnected
// high address lines do.
func bankOff(bank, unit, size int) int {
	n := size / unit
	b := bank % n
	if b < 0 {
		b += n
	}
	return b * unit
}

func (c *Cart) prgOff(bank, unit int) int { return bankOff(bank, unit, len(c.prg)) }
func (c *Cart) chrOff(bank, unit int) int { return bankOff(bank, unit, len(c.chr)) }

// New parses a cartridge image and builds its mapper.
func New(data []byte) (*Cart, error) {
	h, off, err := parseHeader(data)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	need := off + h.PRGSize + h.CHRSize
	if len(data) < need {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cart: image truncated: have %d bytes, header promises %d", len(data), need)
	}
	c := &Cart{Header: h}
	c.prg = append(c.prg, data[off:off+h.PRGSize]...)
	if h.CHRSize > 0 {
		c.chr = append(c.chr, data[off+h.PRGSize:need]...)
	} else {
		ram := h.CHRRAMDecl
		if ram <= 0 {
			ram = 8192
		}
		c.chr = make([]uint8, ram)
		c.chrRAM = true
	}
	if h.PRGSize == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("cart: image has no PRG ROM")
	}
	if h.PRGAMSize() > 0 {
		c.prgRAM = make([]uint8, h.PRGAMSize())
	}
	m, err := newMapper(h.Mapper)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c.mapper = m
	if _, ok := m.(*mmc3); ok {
		c.irqPossible = true
	}
	if _, ok := m.(baseMapper); ok {
		if n := len(c.prg); n > 0 && n&(n-1) == 0 {
			c.flatPRG = true
			c.prgMask = n - 1
		}
		if len(c.chr) == 0x2000 {
			c.flatCHR = true
		}
	}
	return c, nil
}

// PRGAMSize is the amount of CPU work RAM at $6000-$7FFF. A
// header that declares RAM wins. Otherwise an iNES header means
// the standard 8 KB: iNES has no way to declare the RAM absent,
// and the format's cartridges (the public test ROMs included)
// assume it is there. NES 2.0 declares exact sizes including
// zero, and there zero is honored.
func (h Header) PRGAMSize() int {
	if h.PRGRAMDecl > 0 {
		return h.PRGRAMDecl
	}
	if h.NES2 {
		return 0
	}
	return 8192
}

func newMapper(num int) (mapper, error) {
	switch num {
	case 0:
		return baseMapper{}, nil
	case 1:
		return newMMC1(), nil
	case 2:
		return &uxrom{}, nil
	case 3:
		return &cnrom{}, nil
	case 4:
		return newMMC3(), nil
	case 7:
		return &axrom{}, nil
	case 11:
		return &colorDreams{}, nil
	case 66:
		return &gxrom{}, nil
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("cart: mapper %d not implemented in this core yet", num)
}

// parseHeader decodes the 16-byte header and returns the offset
// of the PRG ROM (past the header and any trainer).
func parseHeader(data []byte) (Header, int, error) {
	var h Header
	if len(data) < 16 {
		return h, 0, errors.New("cart: image shorter than a header")
	}
	if data[0] != 'N' || data[1] != 'E' || data[2] != 'S' || data[3] != 0x1A {
		return h, 0, errors.New("cart: missing iNES magic")
	}
	flags6, flags7 := data[6], data[7]
	h.NES2 = flags7&0x0C == 0x08
	h.Mapper = int(flags6>>4) | int(flags7&0xF0)
	h.Battery = flags6&0x02 != 0
	h.Trainer = flags6&0x04 != 0
	if flags6&0x08 != 0 {
		h.Mirror = MirrorFourScreen
	} else if flags6&0x01 != 0 {
		h.Mirror = MirrorVertical
	} else {
		h.Mirror = MirrorHorizontal
	}

	if h.NES2 {
		h.Mapper |= int(data[8]&0x0F) << 8
		h.Submapper = int(data[8] >> 4)
		h.PRGSize = nes2Size(data[4], data[9]&0x0F, 16384)
		h.CHRSize = nes2Size(data[5], data[9]>>4, 8192)
		h.PRGRAMDecl = nes2ShiftSize(data[10]&0x0F, data[10]>>4)
		h.CHRRAMDecl = nes2ShiftSize(data[11]&0x0F, data[11]>>4)
		switch data[7] & 0x03 {
		case 1:
			h.VS = true
		case 2:
			h.PlayChoice = true
		}
	} else {
		h.PRGSize = int(data[4]) * 16384
		h.CHRSize = int(data[5]) * 8192
		if data[8] > 0 {
			h.PRGRAMDecl = int(data[8]) * 8192
		}
		h.VS = flags7&0x01 != 0
		h.PlayChoice = flags7&0x02 != 0
	}
	off := 16
	if h.Trainer {
		off += 512
	}
	return h, off, nil
}

// nes2Size decodes a NES 2.0 ROM size field: either a plain
// 12-bit count of units, or, when the high nibble is 0xF, the
// exponent-multiplier form 2^E * (2*M + 1) bytes.
func nes2Size(lo byte, hi byte, unit int) int {
	if hi == 0x0F {
		exp := int(lo >> 2)
		mult := int(lo&0x03)*2 + 1
		return (1 << exp) * mult
	}
	return (int(hi)<<8 | int(lo)) * unit
}

// nes2ShiftSize decodes a NES 2.0 RAM size field pair (volatile
// and non-volatile shift counts). The cart uses the larger of the
// two as its RAM size; each nonzero shift means 64 << shift bytes.
func nes2ShiftSize(volatile, nonvolatile byte) int {
	size := 0
	for _, s := range []byte{volatile, nonvolatile} {
		if s > 0 {
			if n := 64 << s; n > size {
				size = n
			}
		}
	}
	return size
}

// SetCycle records the CPU cycle of the current access. The
// system calls it from its bus accessors so cycle-sensitive
// mapper behavior (the MMC1 consecutive-write quirk) sees
// realistic spacing.
func (c *Cart) SetCycle(cycle int64) { c.cycle = cycle }

// ReadPRG reads the CPU-side cartridge space, $6000-$FFFF.
// Addresses below $6000 are expansion space and read as zero
// here; the system owns that range.
func (c *Cart) ReadPRG(addr uint16) uint8 {
	if addr >= 0x6000 && addr < 0x8000 {
		if len(c.prgRAM) > 0 && c.mapper.ramEnabled() {
			return c.prgRAM[int(addr-0x6000)%len(c.prgRAM)]
		}
		return 0
	}
	if addr < 0x8000 {
		return 0
	}
	if c.flatPRG {
		return c.prg[int(addr-0x8000)&c.prgMask]
	}
	return c.mapper.readPRG(c, addr)
}

// WritePRG writes the CPU-side cartridge space, $6000-$FFFF.
func (c *Cart) WritePRG(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if addr >= 0x6000 && addr < 0x8000 {
		if len(c.prgRAM) > 0 && c.mapper.ramEnabled() {
			c.prgRAM[int(addr-0x6000)%len(c.prgRAM)] = val
		}
		return
	}
	if addr < 0x8000 {
		return
	}
	c.mirrorOK = false
	c.mapper.writePRG(c, addr, val)
}

// ReadCHR reads the PPU-side pattern space, $0000-$1FFF.
func (c *Cart) ReadCHR(addr uint16) uint8 {
	if c.flatCHR {
		return c.chr[addr&0x1FFF]
	}
	return c.mapper.readCHR(c, addr&0x1FFF)
}

// WriteCHR writes the PPU-side pattern space. Writes land only
// when the cartridge carries CHR RAM.
func (c *Cart) WriteCHR(addr uint16, val uint8) { c.mapper.writeCHR(c, addr&0x1FFF, val) }

// MirrorMode reports the cartridge's current nametable
// mirroring, honoring the mapper's dynamic override.
func (c *Cart) MirrorMode() Mirror {
	if c.mirrorOK {
		return c.mirrorCache
	}
	m := c.Header.Mirror
	if mm, ok := c.mapper.mirror(); ok {
		m = mm
	}
	c.mirrorCache, c.mirrorOK = m, true
	return m
}

// IRQPending reports whether the mapper is asserting its IRQ
// output (the MMC3 counter, in this slice).
func (c *Cart) IRQPending() bool {
	if !c.irqPossible {
		return false
	}
	return c.mapper.irqPending()
}

// ClockA12 clocks the MMC3 IRQ counter the way a rising edge of
// PPU address line A12 does. NES-1 tests drive it directly; NES-2
// calls it from the PPU.
func (c *Cart) ClockA12() {
	c.a12Clocks++
	c.mapper.clockA12()
}

// UsesA12IRQ reports whether the loaded mapper clocks an IRQ
// counter from PPU A12 edges. Among the implemented mappers
// only MMC3 does; the PPU uses this to skip its per-dot A12
// sampling entirely for cartridges that cannot observe it.
func (c *Cart) UsesA12IRQ() bool {
	_, ok := c.mapper.(*mmc3)
	return ok
}

// A12Clocks returns how many filtered A12 rising edges the
// cartridge has been clocked with since power-on. Diagnostic;
// the MMC3 conformance ROMs count these per frame.
func (c *Cart) A12Clocks() int64 { return c.a12Clocks }

// PRGRAM exposes the cartridge RAM contents for battery
// persistence (load) and save-file extraction.
func (c *Cart) PRGRAM() []uint8 { return c.prgRAM }

// LoadPRGRAM installs saved cartridge RAM contents.
func (c *Cart) LoadPRGRAM(data []byte) {
	copy(c.prgRAM, data)
}

// Serialize writes the cartridge state: a format byte, the
// mapper number, the PRG RAM contents, and the mapper's own
// register state.
func (c *Cart) Serialize() []byte {
	out := []byte{1, uint8(c.Header.Mapper), uint8(c.Header.Mapper >> 8)}
	out = append(out, c.prgRAM...)
	out = append(out, c.mapper.state()...)
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *Cart) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) < 3 || in[0] != 1 {
		return errors.New("cart: bad state")
	}
	if int(in[1])|int(in[2])<<8 != c.Header.Mapper {
		return errors.New("cart: state is for a different mapper")
	}
	rest := in[3:]
	if len(rest) < len(c.prgRAM) {
		return errors.New("cart: state truncated")
	}
	copy(c.prgRAM, rest[:len(c.prgRAM)])
	c.mirrorOK = false
	return c.mapper.setState(rest[len(c.prgRAM):])
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/cart/cart_test.go ====================

package cart

import "testing"

// buildImage makes an iNES image whose PRG bytes identify their
// 8 KB chunk (byte value = chunk index) and whose CHR bytes
// identify their 1 KB chunk, so bank checks read the pattern back.
func buildImage(mapper int, prgKB, chrKB int, flags byte) []byte {
	img := []byte{'N', 'E', 'S', 0x1A,
		byte(prgKB / 16), byte(chrKB / 8),
		byte(mapper<<4) | flags, byte(mapper & 0xF0),
		0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
	for i := 0; i < prgKB*1024; i++ {
		img = append(img, byte(i/8192))
	}
	for i := 0; i < chrKB*1024; i++ {
		img = append(img, byte(i/1024))
	}
	return img
}

func mustCart(t *testing.T, img []byte) *Cart {
	t.Helper()
	c, err := New(img)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("New: %v", err)
	}
	return c
}

// writeBits feeds an MMC1 register through the serial port, one
// value bit per write, LSB first, with generous cycle spacing.
func writeBits(c *Cart, addr uint16, v uint8, cycle *int64) {
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		*cycle += 10
		c.SetCycle(*cycle)
		c.WritePRG(addr, (v>>uint(i))&1)
	}
}

func TestHeaderParse(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(4, 32, 8, 0x03)) // battery + vertical
	h := c.Header
	if h.Mapper != 4 || h.PRGSize != 32768 || h.CHRSize != 8192 {
		t.Fatalf("header = %+v", h)
	}
	if h.Mirror != MirrorVertical || !h.Battery {
		t.Fatalf("header mirror/battery = %v/%v", h.Mirror, h.Battery)
	}
	if h.PRGAMSize() != 8192 {
		t.Fatalf("battery RAM = %d, want 8192", h.PRGAMSize())
	}
}

func TestHeaderNES2(t *testing.T) {
	// A NES 2.0 header with a 12-bit mapper and an
	// exponent-encoded PRG size: E=10, M=1 gives 2^10 * 3 = 3072.
	img := []byte{'N', 'E', 'S', 0x1A, 41, 0, 0x40, 0x08, 0x31, 0x0F,
		0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
	h, _, err := parseHeader(img)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !h.NES2 {
		t.Fatalf("NES2 flag not detected")
	}
	if h.Mapper != 0x104 || h.Submapper != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("mapper/submapper = %X/%X, want 104/3", h.Mapper, h.Submapper)
	}
	if h.PRGSize != 3072 {
		t.Fatalf("PRGSize = %d, want 3072 (exponent form)", h.PRGSize)
	}
}

func TestHeaderGarbage(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := New([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("short image accepted")
	}
	bad := buildImage(0, 16, 8, 0)
	bad[0] = 'X'
	if _, err := New(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("bad magic accepted")
	}
	trunc := buildImage(0, 32, 8, 0)
	if _, err := New(trunc[:len(trunc)-100]); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("truncated image accepted")
	}
	if _, err := New(buildImage(5, 16, 8, 0)); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("unimplemented mapper accepted")
	}
}

func TestNROMMirror(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(0, 16, 8, 0))
	// A 16 KB PRG repeats at $C000.
	if c.ReadPRG(0x8000) != c.ReadPRG(0xC000) {
		t.Fatalf("16 KB mirror broken: %02X vs %02X", c.ReadPRG(0x8000), c.ReadPRG(0xC000))
	}
	if c.ReadPRG(0x8000) != 0 || c.ReadPRG(0xA000) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("NROM pattern wrong")
	}
}

func TestUxROM(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(2, 128, 8, 0)) // 8 PRG chunks of 8 KB
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 2)                      // bank 2 = chunks 4,5
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("$8000 chunk = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0xC000); got != 14 { // last 16 KB bank = 8K chunks 14,15
		t.Fatalf("$C000 chunk = %d, want 14", got)
	}
}

func TestCNROM(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(3, 32, 32, 0))
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 2)
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0); got != 16 { // CHR bank 2 starts at 1 KB chunk 16
		t.Fatalf("CHR chunk = %d, want 16", got)
	}
}

func TestAxROM(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(7, 128, 8, 0))
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 3)
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 12 { // 32 KB bank 3 = chunk 12
		t.Fatalf("AxROM chunk = %d, want 12", got)
	}
	if c.MirrorMode() != MirrorSingle0 {
		t.Fatalf("mirror = %v, want single low", c.MirrorMode())
	}
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 0x10|3)
	if c.MirrorMode() != MirrorSingle1 {
		t.Fatalf("mirror = %v, want single high", c.MirrorMode())
	}
}

func TestLatchMappers(t *testing.T) {
	cd := mustCart(t, buildImage(11, 128, 64, 0))
	cd.WritePRG(0x8000, 0x21) // PRG bank 1, CHR bank 2
	if got := cd.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("Color Dreams PRG chunk = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := cd.ReadCHR(0); got != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("Color Dreams CHR chunk = %d, want 16", got)
	}
	gx := mustCart(t, buildImage(66, 128, 32, 0))
	gx.WritePRG(0x8000, 0x21)
	if got := gx.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("GxROM PRG chunk = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := gx.ReadCHR(0); got != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("GxROM CHR chunk = %d, want 16", got)
	}
}

func TestMMC1Banking(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(1, 64, 32, 0x02)) // battery: PRG RAM present
	var cycle int64
	// Reset the shift register, then write control $1E:
	// horizontal? No: bits 0-1 = 2 (vertical), PRG mode 3,
	// CHR mode 1 (two 4 KB banks).
	cycle += 10
	c.SetCycle(cycle)
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 0x80)
	writeBits(c, 0x8000, 0x1E, &cycle)
	if c.MirrorMode() != MirrorVertical {
		t.Fatalf("MMC1 mirror = %v, want vertical", c.MirrorMode())
	}
	// PRG bank 2 in the low window; the high window is fixed to
	// the last bank (chunks 6,7).
	writeBits(c, 0xE000, 2, &cycle)
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("MMC1 low window chunk = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0xC000); got != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("MMC1 high window chunk = %d, want 6", got)
	}
	// CHR bank 3 in the low 4 KB: the pattern marks 1 KB chunks,
	// so bank 3 reads back as chunk 12.
	writeBits(c, 0xA000, 3, &cycle)
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0); got != 12 {
		t.Fatalf("MMC1 CHR chunk = %d, want 12", got)
	}
}

func TestMMC1ResetWrite(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(1, 64, 32, 0))
	var cycle int64
	// Start a control write, abandon it halfway, reset, and
	// write a full value: only the post-reset bits may land.
	for _, bit := range []uint8{1, 1, 1} {
		cycle += 10
		c.SetCycle(cycle)
		c.WritePRG(0x8000, bit)
	}
	cycle += 10
	c.SetCycle(cycle)
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 0x80) // reset
	if c.MirrorMode() == MirrorHorizontal && false {
		t.Fatal("unreachable")
	}
	writeBits(c, 0x8000, 0x1C, &cycle) // vertical? bits: mirroring 0 → single low
	if c.MirrorMode() != MirrorSingle0 {
		t.Fatalf("after reset write, mirror = %v, want single low", c.MirrorMode())
	}
}

func TestMMC1ConsecutiveWriteIgnored(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(1, 64, 32, 0))
	// Write control $12 (vertical, PRG mode 0, CHR 4 KB mode),
	// but deliver bit 1 one cycle after bit 0: that write must
	// be dropped, so the remaining bits only commit when the
	// sixth write arrives.
	bits := []struct {
		cycle int64
		bit   uint8
	}{
		{100, 0}, // bit 0 of $12
		{101, 1}, // bit 1, consecutive: ignored
		{110, 1}, // bit 1 again
		{120, 0}, // bit 2
		{130, 0}, // bit 3
		{140, 1}, // bit 4: commits $12
	}
	for _, w := range bits {
		c.SetCycle(w.cycle)
		c.WritePRG(0x8000, w.bit)
	}
	// CHR mode is 4 KB: CHR bank register 3 shows at $0000 as
	// 1 KB chunk 12. If the consecutive write had counted,
	// control would be $06 (8 KB CHR) and the same register
	// would show 8 KB bank 1, chunk 8.
	var cycle int64 = 1000
	writeBits(c, 0xA000, 3, &cycle)
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0); got != 12 {
		t.Fatalf("CHR chunk = %d, want 12 (consecutive write was not ignored?)", got)
	}
}

func TestMMC1RAMGate(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(1, 64, 32, 0x02))
	var cycle int64
	writeBits(c, 0xE000, 0x10, &cycle) // PRG register bit 4: RAM disabled
	c.WritePRG(0x6000, 0xAB)
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x6000); got == 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("write landed while RAM disabled")
	}
	writeBits(c, 0xE000, 0x00, &cycle)
	c.WritePRG(0x6000, 0xAB)
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x6000); got != 0xAB {
		t.Fatalf("RAM read = %02X, want AB", got)
	}
}

func TestMMC3Banking(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(4, 64, 32, 0x02))
	// R6 = 5 at $8000 (mode 0), R7 = 2 at $A000.
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 6)
	c.WritePRG(0x8001, 5)
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 7)
	c.WritePRG(0x8001, 2)
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("$8000 bank = %d, want 5", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0xA000); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("$A000 bank = %d, want 2", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0xC000); got != 6 { // second to last
		t.Fatalf("$C000 bank = %d, want 6", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0xE000); got != 7 { // last
		t.Fatalf("$E000 bank = %d, want 7", got)
	}
	// PRG mode 1 moves R6 to $C000 and the fixed bank to $8000.
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 0x40|6)
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0xC000); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("mode 1 $C000 bank = %d, want 5", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("mode 1 $8000 bank = %d, want 6", got)
	}
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 6)
	// CHR: R0 = 4 is a 2 KB window at $0000-$07FF (its second
	// half reads as chunk 5), R1 = 6 covers $0800-$0FFF, and
	// R2 = 9 sits at $1000.
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 0)
	c.WritePRG(0x8001, 4)
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 1)
	c.WritePRG(0x8001, 6)
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 2)
	c.WritePRG(0x8001, 9)
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0x0000); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("CHR $0000 bank = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0x0400); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("CHR $0400 bank = %d, want 5 (R0 second half)", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0x0800); got != 6 {
		t.Fatalf("CHR $0800 bank = %d, want 6 (R1)", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0x1000); got != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("CHR $1000 bank = %d, want 9", got)
	}
	// CHR inversion swaps the window sets: R0 lands at $1000.
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 0x80)
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0x1000); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("inverted CHR $1000 bank = %d, want 4", got)
	}
	if got := c.ReadCHR(0x0000); got != 9 {
		t.Fatalf("inverted CHR $0000 bank = %d, want 9 (R2)", got)
	}
	// Mirroring register: 0 vertical, 1 horizontal.
	if c.MirrorMode() != MirrorVertical {
		t.Fatalf("MMC3 mirror = %v, want vertical", c.MirrorMode())
	}
	c.WritePRG(0xA000, 1)
	if c.MirrorMode() != MirrorHorizontal {
		t.Fatalf("MMC3 mirror = %v, want horizontal", c.MirrorMode())
	}
}

func TestMMC3IRQCounter(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(4, 64, 32, 0))
	c.WritePRG(0xC000, 2) // latch = 2
	c.WritePRG(0xC001, 0) // reload on the next clock
	c.WritePRG(0xE001, 0) // enable
	c.ClockA12()          // reload: counter = 2
	if c.IRQPending() {
		t.Fatalf("IRQ fired on the reload clock")
	}
	c.ClockA12() // 2 to 1
	if c.IRQPending() {
		t.Fatalf("IRQ fired early")
	}
	c.ClockA12() // 1 to 0: fire
	if !c.IRQPending() {
		t.Fatalf("IRQ did not fire at zero")
	}
	c.WritePRG(0xE000, 0) // disable acknowledges
	if c.IRQPending() {
		t.Fatalf("IRQ still pending after disable")
	}
}

func TestMMC3RAMProtectRegisters(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(4, 64, 32, 0x02))
	c.WritePRG(0x6000, 0x5A)
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x6000); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("MMC3 RAM read = %02X, want 5A", got)
	}
	c.WritePRG(0xA001, 0x00) // RAM enable bit clear
	c.WritePRG(0x6000, 0x11)
	c.WritePRG(0xA001, 0x80) // enabled again
	if got := c.ReadPRG(0x6000); got != 0x5A {
		t.Fatalf("MMC3 RAM = %02X after disable window, want 5A", got)
	}
}

func TestCartSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	c := mustCart(t, buildImage(4, 64, 32, 0x02))
	c.WritePRG(0x8000, 6)
	c.WritePRG(0x8001, 3)
	c.WritePRG(0x6000, 0x77)
	state := c.Serialize()
	c2 := mustCart(t, buildImage(4, 64, 32, 0x02))
	if err := c2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := c2.ReadPRG(0x8000); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("restored $8000 bank = %d, want 3", got)
	}
	if got := c2.ReadPRG(0x6000); got != 0x77 {
		t.Fatalf("restored RAM = %02X, want 77", got)
	}
	if err := c2.Deserialize([]byte{9, 9, 9}); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("bad state accepted")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/cart/mapper.go ====================

package cart

import (
	"errors"
)

// --- Mapper 2: UxROM ---
//
// A latch selects which 16 KB bank sits at $8000-$BFFF; the last
// bank is fixed at $C000-$FFFF. Any write to $8000-$FFFF sets the
// latch. (Real boards have bus conflicts, the write value ANDed
// with the ROM byte under the address; games are not supposed to
// depend on them and this core does not model them, here or in
// the other latch mappers.)

type uxrom struct {
	baseMapper
	bank uint8
}

func (m *uxrom) readPRG(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	if addr < 0xC000 {
		return c.prg[c.prgOff(int(m.bank), 16384)+int(addr-0x8000)]
	}
	return c.prg[c.prgOff(-1, 16384)+int(addr-0xC000)]
}
func (m *uxrom) writePRG(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) { m.bank = val }
func (m *uxrom) state() []byte                            { return []byte{m.bank} }
func (m *uxrom) setState(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != 1 {
		return errors.New("cart: bad UxROM state")
	}
	m.bank = in[0]
	return nil
}

// --- Mapper 3: CNROM ---
//
// One latch selects the 8 KB CHR bank; PRG is plain NROM. Any
// write to $8000-$FFFF sets the latch.

type cnrom struct {
	baseMapper
	chrBank uint8
}

func (m *cnrom) readCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	return c.chr[c.chrOff(int(m.chrBank), 8192)+int(addr)]
}
func (m *cnrom) writePRG(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) { m.chrBank = val }
func (m *cnrom) state() []byte                            { return []byte{m.chrBank} }
func (m *cnrom) setState(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != 1 {
		return errors.New("cart: bad CNROM state")
	}
	m.chrBank = in[0]
	return nil
}

// --- Mapper 7: AxROM ---
//
// One latch selects a whole 32 KB PRG bank and, in bit 4, which
// single nametable page is shown (AxROM boards carry one physical
// nametable and switch its CIRAM address line).

type axrom struct {
	baseMapper
	latch uint8
}

func (m *axrom) readPRG(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	return c.prg[c.prgOff(int(m.latch&0x07), 32768)+int(addr-0x8000)]
}
func (m *axrom) writePRG(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) { m.latch = val }
func (m *axrom) mirror() (Mirror, bool) {
	if m.latch&0x10 != 0 {
		return MirrorSingle1, true
	}
	return MirrorSingle0, true
}
func (m *axrom) state() []byte { return []byte{m.latch} }
func (m *axrom) setState(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != 1 {
		return errors.New("cart: bad AxROM state")
	}
	m.latch = in[0]
	return nil
}

// --- Mapper 11: Color Dreams ---

type colorDreams struct {

func (m *colorDreams) readPRG(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {

}

	return nil
}

	if len(in) != 1 {
