// --- Mapper 1: MMC1 ---
//
// The MMC1 is programmed through a serial shift register: each
// write to $8000-$FFFF shifts bit 0 of the value in, and the
// fifth consecutive write commits the accumulated five bits to
// the register the write address selects. A write with bit 7 set
// resets the shift register and sets the control register's two
// PRG-mode bits. Two hardware quirks are modeled:
//
//   - Writes on consecutive CPU cycles are ignored entirely: the
//     chip cannot keep up. The system feeds the cart the cycle of
//     each access through SetCycle; the mapper remembers the
//     cycle of its last accepted write and drops a write that
//     lands exactly one cycle later. (This is the state-level
//     model; a write sequence driven without cycle information,
//     such as unit tests that never call SetCycle, sees constant
//     spacing and nothing is dropped.)
//   - The PRG bank register's bit 4 disables cartridge RAM on
//     the MMC1B and later revisions when set.

type mmc1 struct {
	baseMapper
	shift   uint8
	count   int
	control uint8 // mirroring, PRG mode, CHR mode
	chr0    uint8
	chr1    uint8
	prgReg  uint8

	lastWriteCycle int64
	haveLastWrite  bool

	// Resolved window bases, as in the MMC3: the byte
	// offset of each 16 KB PRG window and each 4 KB CHR
	// window under the current banking, recomputed lazily
	// after any write or state load dirties them.
	prgWin [2]int
	chrWin [2]int
	winOK  bool
}

func newMMC1() *mmc1 {
	return &mmc1{control: 0x0C} // power-on: PRG mode 3, like the reset state
}

func (m *mmc1) writePRG(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	m.winOK = false
	if m.haveLastWrite && c.cycle == m.lastWriteCycle+1 {
		return // consecutive-cycle write: ignored
	}
	m.haveLastWrite = true
	m.lastWriteCycle = c.cycle
	if val&0x80 != 0 {
		m.shift = 0
		m.count = 0
		m.control |= 0x0C
		return
	}
	m.shift |= (val & 1) << uint(m.count)
	m.count++
	if m.count < 5 {
		return
	}
	v := m.shift & 0x1F
	m.shift = 0
	m.count = 0
	switch {
	case addr < 0xA000:
		m.control = v
	case addr < 0xC000:
		m.chr0 = v
	case addr < 0xE000:
		m.chr1 = v
	default:
		m.prgReg = v
	}
}

// resolveWins recomputes the MMC1 window bases from the
// control and bank registers.
func (m *mmc1) resolveWins(c *Cart) {
	last := len(c.prg)/16384 - 1
	switch (m.control >> 2) & 3 {
	case 0, 1: // 32 KB switch at $8000
		bank := int(m.prgReg&0x0F) >> 1
		m.prgWin[0] = c.prgOff(bank*2, 16384)
		m.prgWin[1] = c.prgOff(bank*2+1, 16384)
	case 2: // $8000 fixed to bank 0, $C000 switches
		m.prgWin[0] = c.prgOff(0, 16384)
		m.prgWin[1] = c.prgOff(int(m.prgReg&0x0F), 16384)
	default: // $8000 switches, $C000 fixed to the last bank
		m.prgWin[0] = c.prgOff(int(m.prgReg&0x0F), 16384)
		m.prgWin[1] = c.prgOff(last, 16384)
	}
	if m.control&0x10 == 0 { // one 8 KB CHR bank
		m.chrWin[0] = c.chrOff(int(m.chr0>>1)*2, 4096)
		m.chrWin[1] = c.chrOff(int(m.chr0>>1)*2+1, 4096)
	} else {
		m.chrWin[0] = c.chrOff(int(m.chr0), 4096)
		m.chrWin[1] = c.chrOff(int(m.chr1), 4096)
	}
	m.winOK = true
}

func (m *mmc1) readPRG(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	if !m.winOK {
		m.resolveWins(c)
	}
	return c.prg[m.prgWin[(addr>>14)&1]+int(addr&0x3FFF)]
}

func (m *mmc1) readCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	if !m.winOK {
		m.resolveWins(c)
	}
	return c.chr[m.chrWin[(addr>>12)&1]+int(addr&0x0FFF)]
}

func (m *mmc1) writeCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if !c.chrRAM {
		return
	}
	if !m.winOK {
		m.resolveWins(c)
	}
	c.chr[m.chrWin[(addr>>12)&1]+int(addr&0x0FFF)] = val
}

func (m *mmc1) mirror() (Mirror, bool) {
	switch m.control & 3 {
	case 0:
		return MirrorSingle0, true
	case 1:
		return MirrorSingle1, true
	case 2:
		return MirrorVertical, true
	default:
		return MirrorHorizontal, true
	}
}

func (m *mmc1) ramEnabled() bool { return m.prgReg&0x10 == 0 }

func (m *mmc1) state() []byte {
	return []byte{m.shift, uint8(m.count), m.control, m.chr0, m.chr1, m.prgReg}
}
func (m *mmc1) setState(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != 6 {
		return errors.New("cart: bad MMC1 state")
	}
	m.shift, m.count = in[0], int(in[1])
	m.control, m.chr0, m.chr1, m.prgReg = in[2], in[3], in[4], in[5]
	m.winOK = false
	return nil
}

// --- Mapper 4: MMC3 ---
//
// The MMC3 pages PRG in 8 KB banks through six window registers
// (two switchable PRG windows whose positions swap with the PRG
// mode bit) and CHR in 1 KB and 2 KB windows whose layout flips
// with the CHR inversion bit. Its scanline counter is clocked by
// PPU A12 rising edges: on each edge, if a reload is pending or
// the counter is zero, the counter reloads from the latch,
// otherwise it decrements; a counter that reaches zero with
// interrupts enabled asserts the IRQ output until software
// acknowledges it by writing the disable register.

type mmc3 struct {
	baseMapper
	bankSelect uint8
	regs       [8]uint8
	mirrorReg  uint8
	ramEnable  bool
	ramProtect bool

	irqLatch   uint8
	irqCounter uint8
	irqReload  bool
	irqEnabled bool
	irqAssert  bool

	// Resolved window bases: the byte offset of each 8 KB
	// PRG window and each 1 KB CHR window under the current
	// banking. Reads index through these instead of
	// resolving bank numbers per byte (a switch plus a
	// modulo division each). Any register write or state
	// load dirties them; the next read resolves again.
	prgWin [4]int
	chrWin [8]int
	winOK  bool
}

func newMMC3() *mmc3 {
	m := &mmc3{ramEnable: true}
	m.regs[6] = 0
	m.regs[7] = 1
	return m
}

func (m *mmc3) prgWindow(c *Cart, addr uint16) (bank int) {
	total := len(c.prg) / 8192
	secondLast := total - 2
	mode := (m.bankSelect >> 6) & 1
	switch {
	case addr < 0xA000:
		if mode == 0 {
			return int(m.regs[6])
		}
		return secondLast
	case addr < 0xC000:
		return int(m.regs[7])
	case addr < 0xE000:
		if mode == 0 {
			return secondLast
		}
		return int(m.regs[6])
	default:
		return total - 1
	}
}

// resolveWins recomputes the window bases by evaluating the
// original bank resolution at each window's first address,
// so the cached values are the original ones by construction.
func (m *mmc3) resolveWins(c *Cart) {
	for w := 0; w < 4; w++ {
		m.prgWin[w] = c.prgOff(m.prgWindow(c, uint16(0x8000+w*8192)), 8192)
	}
	for s := 0; s < 8; s++ {
		m.chrWin[s] = m.chrOffset(c, uint16(s*1024))
	}
	m.winOK = true
}

func (m *mmc3) readPRG(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	if !m.winOK {
		m.resolveWins(c)
	}
	return c.prg[m.prgWin[(addr>>13)&3]+int(addr&0x1FFF)]
}

func (m *mmc3) readCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16) uint8 {
	if !m.winOK {
		m.resolveWins(c)
	}
	return c.chr[m.chrWin[addr>>10]+int(addr&0x03FF)]
}

func (m *mmc3) writeCHR(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if c.chrRAM {
		if !m.winOK {
			m.resolveWins(c)
		}
		c.chr[m.chrWin[addr>>10]+int(addr&0x03FF)] = val
	}
}

// chrOffset resolves a CHR address to a byte offset under the
// current banking: two 2 KB windows and four 1 KB windows, with
// the CHR inversion bit swapping which set sits low.
func (m *mmc3) chrOffset(c *Cart, addr uint16) int {
	invert := m.bankSelect&0x80 != 0
	if !invert {
		switch {
		case addr < 0x0800:
			return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[0]&0xFE), 1024) + int(addr)
		case addr < 0x1000:
			return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[1]&0xFE), 1024) + int(addr-0x0800)
		case addr < 0x1400:
			return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[2]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
		case addr < 0x1800:
			return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[3]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
		case addr < 0x1C00:
			return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[4]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
		default:
			return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[5]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
		}
	}
	switch {
	case addr < 0x0400:
		return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[2]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
	case addr < 0x0800:
		return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[3]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
	case addr < 0x0C00:
		return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[4]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
	case addr < 0x1000:
		return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[5]), 1024) + int(addr&0x03FF)
	case addr < 0x1800:
		return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[0]&0xFE), 1024) + int(addr-0x1000)
	default:
		return c.chrOff(int(m.regs[1]&0xFE), 1024) + int(addr-0x1800)
	}
}

func (m *mmc3) writePRG(c *Cart, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	m.winOK = false
	even := addr&1 == 0
	switch {
	case addr < 0xA000:
		if even {
			m.bankSelect = val & 0xC7
		} else {
			m.regs[m.bankSelect&7] = val
		}
	case addr < 0xC000:
		if even {
			m.mirrorReg = val & 1
		} else {
			m.ramEnable = val&0x80 != 0
			m.ramProtect = val&0x40 != 0
		}
	case addr < 0xE000:
		if even {
			m.irqLatch = val
		} else {
			m.irqReload = true
		}
	default:
		if even {
			m.irqEnabled = false
			m.irqAssert = false
		} else {
			m.irqEnabled = true
		}
	}
}

func (m *mmc3) mirror() (Mirror, bool) {
	if m.mirrorReg&1 != 0 {
		return MirrorHorizontal, true
	}
	return MirrorVertical, true
}

func (m *mmc3) ramEnabled() bool { return m.ramEnable }

// clockA12 advances the IRQ counter on one filtered A12
// rising edge. The counter reloads from the latch when a
// reload is pending (a $C001 write) or when it sits at zero;
// otherwise it decrements. The IRQ asserts whenever the
// counter is at zero after the clock and IRQs are enabled:
// on a decrement into zero, on a reload that loads zero,
// and on a clock that finds the counter resting at zero
// (the revision B behavior the test suites pin).
func (m *mmc3) clockA12() {
	if m.irqReload || m.irqCounter == 0 {
		m.irqCounter = m.irqLatch
		m.irqReload = false
	} else {
		m.irqCounter--
	}
	if m.irqCounter == 0 && m.irqEnabled {
		m.irqAssert = true
	}
}

func (m *mmc3) irqPending() bool { return m.irqAssert }

func (m *mmc3) state() []byte {
	var flags byte
	if m.ramEnable {
		flags |= 1
	}
	if m.ramProtect {
		flags |= 2
	}
	if m.irqReload {
		flags |= 4
	}
	if m.irqEnabled {
		flags |= 8
	}
	if m.irqAssert {
		flags |= 16
	}
	out := []byte{m.bankSelect}
	out = append(out, m.regs[:]...)
	out = append(out, m.mirrorReg, m.irqLatch, m.irqCounter, flags)
	return out
}

func (m *mmc3) setState(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != 13 {
		return errors.New("cart: bad MMC3 state")
	}
	m.bankSelect = in[0]
	copy(m.regs[:], in[1:9])
	m.mirrorReg = in[9]
	m.irqLatch = in[10]
	m.irqCounter = in[11]
	m.winOK = false
	flags := in[12]
	m.ramEnable = flags&1 != 0
	m.ramProtect = flags&2 != 0
	m.irqReload = flags&4 != 0
	m.irqEnabled = flags&8 != 0
	m.irqAssert = flags&16 != 0
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/chips/cpu6502/cpu6502.go ====================

// Package cpu6502 is an original implementation of the MOS 6502
// CPU as the NES's Ricoh 2A03 runs it, written from the published
// datasheet behavior and the documented results collected on the
// NESdev wiki (including the unofficial opcode page).
//
// The Ricoh variant differs from a stock 6502 in one way that
// matters to software: the decimal flag still exists and can be
// set and cleared, but ADC and SBC always compute in binary. The
// interrupt lines also differ: the 2A03 adds an edge-triggered
// NMI input driven by the PPU alongside the level-triggered IRQ.
//
// Cycle counting is by bus access: every byte the CPU reads or
// writes takes exactly one cycle, and the addressing-mode helpers
// perform the hardware's dummy reads and dummy writes in the
// documented order, so the accesses a machine observes happen in
// the same order and at the same count as on hardware. Internal
// cycles are modeled as dummy reads, again like the hardware,
// which mostly spends them re-reading the byte at PC. A machine
// that hangs timing-sensitive devices off the bus (the PPU, the
// MMC3 IRQ counter, DMA) can therefore watch the accesses go by.
//
// Interrupts are polled the way the hardware polls them: once
// per instruction, just before the instruction's last bus
// access. The CPU records the interrupt lines before every
// access, and at the end of each Step the sample taken before
// the last access becomes the decision the next Step acts on.
// That one mechanism produces the documented behavior with no
// special cases: an interrupt that lands during the final
// access waits for the next instruction, CLI/SEI/PLP/RTI give
// IRQ a one-instruction delay because the deciding sample
// predates the flag write, and an NMI enabled during vblank is
// serviced after one more instruction. NMI is an edge latch
// with priority over IRQ, IRQ is masked by the I flag, and BRK
// and IRQ sequences check the NMI latch again when they reach
// their vector fetch, which is how a mid-sequence NMI hijacks
// to the NMI vector while keeping the bytes already pushed.
// Devices on the bus raise the latch mid-instruction through
// SetNMILine; the sample ordering sorts out the rest.
package cpu6502

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Bus is the machine interface the CPU drives. Every access is one
// CPU cycle, in order.
type Bus interface {
	Read(addr uint16) uint8
	Write(addr uint16, val uint8)
}

// lineSyncer is the optional bus extension a timing-exact
// machine implements so the CPU can resolve its interrupt poll
// at the end of each Step. The machine advances its devices
// lazily and drives the interrupt lines through them; the CPU
// calls SyncPoll just before latching the poll decision (the
// driven point is the sync point of the access before the
// Step's last access, which is the sample the hardware poll
// semantics use), SyncFinal after latching (driving through
// the last access's own sync point, where the next Step's
// samples and edge latches pick the levels up), and SyncLatch
// at the mid-sequence points where the CPU reads the NMI latch
// directly (the BRK and interrupt vector hijack checks).
// A bus that does not implement it (the unit tests' flat RAM)
// leaves the lines exactly where the test drove them, and the
// poll falls back to the levels as they stand.
type lineSyncer interface {
	SyncPoll()
	SyncFinal()
	SyncLatch()
}

// Status register bit masks. Bit 5 (the "unused" bit) has no
// storage in the hardware: it reads as 1 in every byte pushed to
// the stack, and the B flag (bit 4) exists only in those pushed
// bytes; the live register keeps bit 5 set and bit 4 clear at all
// times.
const (
	FlagC = 0x01 // carry
	FlagZ = 0x02 // zero
	FlagI = 0x04 // interrupt disable
	FlagD = 0x08 // decimal (present but inert on the NES CPU)
	FlagB = 0x10 // break (stack copies only)
	FlagU = 0x20 // always 1 in pushed copies
	FlagV = 0x40 // overflow
	FlagN = 0x80 // negative
)

// Vector addresses.
const (
	VectorNMI   = 0xFFFA
	VectorReset = 0xFFFC
	VectorIRQ   = 0xFFFE // shared by IRQ and BRK
)

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size in bytes.
const SerializeSize = 21

const serializeVersion = 1

// Registers is a snapshot of the programmer-visible CPU state. P
// is the live status register as the CPU keeps it (bit 5 set, the
// B bit clear).
type Registers struct {
	A, X, Y, SP, P uint8
	PC             uint16
}

// CPU is a single 6502 instance.
type CPU struct {
	bus Bus

	a, x, y, sp, p uint8
	pc             uint16

	cycles uint64

	nmiLine    bool // current level of the NMI pin
	nmiPending bool // falling-to-rising edge latched, awaiting service
	irqLine    bool // current level of the IRQ pin (true asserts)

	stall  int  // pending RDY stall cycles (OAM DMA and friends)
	jammed bool // a KIL opcode has halted the CPU until reset

	// Interrupt poll state (see the package comment): the
	// samples are refreshed before every bus access, and the
	// takes are the decision latched at the end of each Step.
	smpNMI  bool // NMI latch as sampled before the last access
	smpIRQ  bool // IRQ recognizable as sampled before the last access
	pollI   bool // I flag clear, as sampled before the last access
	takeNMI bool // the next Step enters the NMI sequence
	takeIRQ bool // the next Step enters the IRQ sequence
}

// New returns a CPU in its power-on state: registers zeroed,
// cycles zeroed, interrupt lines low. Call Reset (with a bus
// attached) to run the reset sequence.
func New() *CPU {
	return &CPU{}
}

// Attach wires the CPU to a bus. The machine owns this; the CPU
// never changes buses on its own.
func (c *CPU) Attach(bus Bus) { c.bus = bus }

// Reset runs the hardware reset sequence: seven cycles, the stack
// pointer drops by three without writes, the I flag sets, the
// pending NMI latch clears (the reset input suppresses it), and PC
// loads from the reset vector. A, X, and Y survive a reset on real
// hardware and survive here too; from power-on they are zero.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	// Three stack reads that decrement SP without storing, two
	// internal cycles, then the vector fetch: seven cycles in
	// all, modeled as reads like the hardware performs.
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		c.read(0x0100 | uint16(c.sp))
		c.sp--
	}
	c.read(c.pc)
	c.read(c.pc)
	c.p = (c.p | FlagI | FlagU) &^ FlagB
	c.nmiPending = false
	c.jammed = false
	c.smpNMI, c.smpIRQ = false, false
	c.takeNMI, c.takeIRQ = false, false
	lo := c.read(VectorReset)
	hi := c.read(VectorReset + 1)
	c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// Regs returns a snapshot of the programmer-visible registers.
func (c *CPU) Regs() Registers {
	return Registers{A: c.a, X: c.x, Y: c.y, SP: c.sp, P: c.p, PC: c.pc}
}

// SetRegs installs a register snapshot. P is normalized to the
// live register's invariant (bit 5 set, B clear).
func (c *CPU) SetRegs(r Registers) {
	c.a, c.x, c.y, c.sp = r.A, r.X, r.Y, r.SP
	c.p = (r.P | FlagU) &^ FlagB
	c.pc = r.PC
}

// PC returns the current program counter.
func (c *CPU) PC() uint16 { return c.pc }

// Cycles returns the total cycles executed since power-on,
// including reset and stall cycles.
func (c *CPU) Cycles() uint64 { return c.cycles }

// SetNMILine drives the NMI pin. The input is edge triggered: a
// low-to-high transition latches a pending NMI that the CPU
// services at the next poll point. The latch survives the pin
// dropping again.
func (c *CPU) SetNMILine(high bool) {
	if high && !c.nmiLine {
		c.nmiPending = true
	}
	c.nmiLine = high
}

// SetIRQLine drives the IRQ pin. The input is level triggered and
// is honored only while the I flag is clear.
func (c *CPU) SetIRQLine(asserted bool) { c.irqLine = asserted }

// NMIPending reports whether an NMI edge is latched and awaiting
// service. Machines use it for diagnostics; the CPU clears it when
// the interrupt is taken or on reset.
func (c *CPU) NMIPending() bool { return c.nmiPending }

// Stall adds RDY stall cycles. A DMA engine (OAM DMA in NES-2)
// calls this when it seizes the bus: Step then burns the cycles
// one dummy read at a time before the next instruction, which is
// the state-level hook. Hardware stalls reads only and aligns to
// the clock phase; the NES-2 machine computes the 513 or 514 the
// hardware would spend and hands the total here.
func (c *CPU) Stall(n int) {
	if n > 0 {
		c.stall += n
	}
}

// Jammed reports whether a KIL opcode has halted the CPU. Only a
// reset recovers.
func (c *CPU) Jammed() bool { return c.jammed }

// sampleInterrupts records the I-flag half of the interrupt
// poll as it stands before a bus access. The poll point for
// an instruction is the sample taken before its last access,
// and the flag half must be captured there because CLI, SEI,
// PLP, and RTI change the flag after their last access, which
// is exactly the one-instruction recognition delay the
// hardware shows. The line half of the poll is resolved in
// finishStep: the machine drives the lines through the point
// this sample describes (see lineSyncer), so the levels the
// decision uses are the levels at this same moment.
func (c *CPU) sampleInterrupts() {
	c.pollI = c.p&FlagI == 0
}

// finishStep resolves the interrupt poll at the end of a Step
// unit and latches the decision the next Step acts on. It runs
// at the end of every Step unit (instruction, interrupt
// sequence, stall cycle, jammed cycle).
func (c *CPU) finishStep() {
	if s, ok := c.bus.(lineSyncer); ok {
		s.SyncPoll()
	}
	c.smpNMI = c.nmiPending
	c.smpIRQ = c.irqLine && c.pollI
	c.latchPoll()
	if s, ok := c.bus.(lineSyncer); ok {
		s.SyncFinal()
	}
}

// syncLatch asks the machine to drive the interrupt lines
// through the last completed access's sync point, so a direct
// read of the NMI latch mid-sequence (the vector hijack
// checks) sees the level the per-access sync would have left.
func (c *CPU) syncLatch() {
	if s, ok := c.bus.(lineSyncer); ok {
		s.SyncLatch()
	}
}

// latchPoll moves the latest samples into the decision the
// next Step acts on. It runs at the end of every Step unit
// (instruction, interrupt sequence, stall cycle, jammed
// cycle).
func (c *CPU) latchPoll() {
	c.takeNMI = c.smpNMI
	c.takeIRQ = c.smpIRQ
}

// read performs one bus read and charges one cycle.
func (c *CPU) read(addr uint16) uint8 {
	c.sampleInterrupts()
	v := c.bus.Read(addr)
	c.cycles++
	return v
}

// write performs one bus write and charges one cycle.
func (c *CPU) write(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	c.sampleInterrupts()
	c.bus.Write(addr, val)
	c.cycles++
}

// fetch reads the byte at PC and advances PC.
func (c *CPU) fetch() uint8 {
	v := c.read(c.pc)
	c.pc++
	return v
}

// dummy charges an internal cycle the way the hardware spends it:
// a read whose value is discarded, usually at PC.
func (c *CPU) dummy(addr uint16) { c.read(addr) }

func (c *CPU) push(v uint8) {
	c.write(0x0100|uint16(c.sp), v)
	c.sp--
}

func (c *CPU) pull() uint8 {
	c.sp++
	return c.read(0x0100 | uint16(c.sp))
}

// statusByte renders P the way an interrupt or BRK pushes it:
// bit 5 always set, B set only for BRK and PHP.
func (c *CPU) statusByte(brk bool) uint8 {
	p := c.p | FlagU
	if brk {
		p |= FlagB
	} else {
		p &^= FlagB
	}
	return p
}

// setP installs a pulled status byte, restoring the live
// register's invariant.
func (c *CPU) setP(v uint8) {
	c.p = (v | FlagU) &^ FlagB
}

// Step executes one instruction, one interrupt sequence, one
// stall cycle, or one jammed cycle, and returns the cycles it
// consumed.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	start := c.cycles
	if c.jammed {
		// The hardware jams reading the KIL opcode forever.
		c.read(c.pc)
		c.finishStep()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	if c.stall > 0 {
		c.stall--
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.finishStep()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	// Interrupt decision latched at the previous Step's poll
	// point. NMI wins over IRQ.
	if c.takeNMI {
		c.takeNMI = false
		c.nmiPending = false
		c.interrupt(VectorNMI)
		c.finishStep()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	if c.takeIRQ {
		c.takeIRQ = false
		c.interrupt(VectorIRQ)
		c.finishStep()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	op := c.fetch()
	c.exec(op)
	c.finishStep()
	return int(c.cycles - start)
}

// interrupt runs the seven-cycle hardware interrupt sequence: two
// internal cycles with PC held (the fetched opcode is discarded),
// the return address and a B-clear status byte pushed, I set, and
// PC loaded from the vector. BRK shares the shape but pushes its
// own bytes; see execBRK. An NMI latched after the sequence
// began hijacks the vector fetch to the NMI vector.
func (c *CPU) interrupt(vector uint16) {
	c.dummy(c.pc)
	c.dummy(c.pc)
	c.push(uint8(c.pc >> 8))
	c.push(uint8(c.pc))
	c.push(c.statusByte(false))
	c.p |= FlagI
	c.syncLatch()
	if vector != VectorNMI && c.nmiPending {
		c.nmiPending = false
		vector = VectorNMI
	}
	lo := c.read(vector)
	hi := c.read(vector + 1)
	c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// Serialize writes the CPU state in this package's fixed layout.
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	out[1] = c.a
	out[2] = c.x
	out[3] = c.y
	out[4] = c.sp
	out[5] = c.p
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[6:], c.pc)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(out[8:], c.cycles)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[16:], uint16(c.stall))
	var lines uint8
	if c.nmiLine {
		lines |= 1
	}
	if c.nmiPending {
		lines |= 2
	}
	if c.irqLine {
		lines |= 4
	}
	if c.jammed {
		lines |= 8
	}
	out[18] = lines
	// Byte 19 carries the interrupt poll state; byte 20 is
	// reserved and stays zero in version 1.
	var poll uint8
	if c.takeNMI {
		poll |= 1
	}
	if c.takeIRQ {
		poll |= 2
	}
	if c.smpNMI {
		poll |= 4
	}
	if c.smpIRQ {
		poll |= 8
	}
	out[19] = poll
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("cpu6502: bad state size")
	}
	if in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("cpu6502: unsupported state version")
	}
	c.a, c.x, c.y, c.sp = in[1], in[2], in[3], in[4]
	c.setP(in[5])
	c.pc = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[6:])
	c.cycles = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(in[8:])
	c.stall = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[16:]))
	lines := in[18]
	c.nmiLine = lines&1 != 0
	c.nmiPending = lines&2 != 0
	c.irqLine = lines&4 != 0
	c.jammed = lines&8 != 0
	poll := in[19]
	c.takeNMI = poll&1 != 0
	c.takeIRQ = poll&2 != 0
	c.smpNMI = poll&4 != 0
	c.smpIRQ = poll&8 != 0
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/chips/cpu6502/cpu6502_test.go ====================

package cpu6502

import "testing"

// flatBus is a 64 KB RAM with no devices: every address reads
// back what was written, which is all the CPU unit tests need.
type flatBus struct{ mem [65536]uint8 }

func (b *flatBus) Read(a uint16) uint8     { return b.mem[a] }
func (b *flatBus) Write(a uint16, v uint8) { b.mem[a] = v }

// newCPUAt returns a CPU reset into a program placed at start.
func newCPUAt(bus *flatBus, start uint16, prog ...uint8) *CPU {
	bus.mem[VectorReset] = uint8(start)
	bus.mem[VectorReset+1] = uint8(start >> 8)
	copy(bus.mem[start:], prog)
	c := New()
	c.Attach(bus)
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// stepCycles runs one step and reports its cycle cost.
func stepCycles(c *CPU) int {
	before := c.Cycles()
	c.Step()
	return int(c.Cycles() - before)
}

func TestADCBinaryEvenWithDecimalFlag(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	// SED; LDA #$50; ADC #$50. In binary: $A0, V set, C clear.
	// If decimal arithmetic leaked in, the result would be $00
	// with C set, which is exactly what nestest checks for.
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0xF8, 0xA9, 0x50, 0x69, 0x50)
	c.Step() // SED
	c.Step() // LDA
	c.Step() // ADC
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.A != 0xA0 {
		t.Fatalf("A = %02X, want A0 (binary ADC with D set)", r.A)
	}
	if r.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("C set, want clear")
	}
	if r.P&FlagV == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("V clear, want set")
	}
	if r.P&FlagD == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("D flag itself should still read as set")
	}
}

func TestSBCBinaryEvenWithDecimalFlag(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	// SED; LDA #$00; SEC; SBC #$01: binary $FF with borrow.
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0xF8, 0xA9, 0x00, 0x38, 0xE9, 0x01)
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.A != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("A = %02X, want FF (binary SBC with D set)", r.A)
	}
	if r.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("C set, want clear (borrow)")
	}
}

func TestIndexedPageCrossCycles(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	// LDX #$02; LDA $80FF,X crosses into $8101: 5 cycles.
	// With X = 0 the same instruction costs 4.
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0xA2, 0x02, 0xBD, 0xFF, 0x80)
	c.Step()
	if got := stepCycles(c); got != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("LDA abs,X crossing cost %d, want 5", got)
	}
	bus2 := &flatBus{}
	c2 := newCPUAt(bus2, 0x8000, 0xA2, 0x00, 0xBD, 0xFF, 0x80)
	c2.Step()
	if got := stepCycles(c2); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("LDA abs,X not crossing cost %d, want 4", got)
	}
}

func TestBranchCyclePenalties(t *testing.T) {
	// Not taken: 2 cycles. Taken same page: 3. Taken across a
	// page boundary: 4.
	bus := &flatBus{}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0xD0, 0x10) // BNE +16, Z set after reset? P=$24: Z clear
	stepCycles(c)                          // Z is clear, so BNE is taken, same page
	if c.PC() != 0x8012 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %04X, want 8012", c.PC())
	}
	bus2 := &flatBus{}
	c2 := newCPUAt(bus2, 0x8000, 0xF0, 0x10) // BEQ +16, Z clear: not taken
	if got := stepCycles(c2); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("branch not taken cost %d, want 2", got)
	}
	bus3 := &flatBus{}
	c3 := newCPUAt(bus3, 0x80F0, 0xD0, 0x20) // BNE +32 from $80F2 to $8112: page cross
	if got := stepCycles(c3); got != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("branch taken crossing cost %d, want 4", got)
	}
	bus4 := &flatBus{}
	c4 := newCPUAt(bus4, 0x8000, 0xD0, 0x10)
	if got := stepCycles(c4); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("branch taken cost %d, want 3", got)
	}
}

func TestJMPIndirectPageWrapBug(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	bus.mem[0x02FF] = 0x34
	bus.mem[0x0200] = 0x80 // high byte must come from $0200, not $0300
	bus.mem[0x0300] = 0x99
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0x6C, 0xFF, 0x02)
	c.Step()
	if c.PC() != 0x8034 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %04X, want 8034 (the wrap bug)", c.PC())
	}
}

func TestBRKPushesBreakStatus(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	bus.mem[VectorIRQ] = 0x00
	bus.mem[VectorIRQ+1] = 0x90
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0x00)
	if got := stepCycles(c); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("BRK cost %d, want 7", got)
	}
	// Stack after reset (SP $FD): pushes land at $01FD (PCH),
	// $01FC (PCL), $01FB (status).
	if bus.mem[0x01FB] != 0x34 { // live P $24, plus B and U
		t.Fatalf("BRK status byte = %02X, want 34", bus.mem[0x01FB])
	}
	if c.PC() != 0x9000 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %04X, want 9000", c.PC())
	}
	if c.Regs().P&FlagI == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BRK must set I")
	}
}

func TestInterruptPushesClearBreakStatus(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	bus.mem[VectorIRQ] = 0x00
	bus.mem[VectorIRQ+1] = 0x90
	// CLI, then NOPs. Interrupts are polled just before an
	// instruction's last bus access, so a line asserted after
	// CLI has retired is first recognized at the NOP's poll
	// point: the NOP executes, and the interrupt sequence
	// follows it.
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0x58, 0xEA, 0xEA)
	c.Step() // CLI: P goes to $20
	c.SetIRQLine(true)
	if got := stepCycles(c); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("NOP before the interrupt cost %d, want 2", got)
	}
	if got := stepCycles(c); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("interrupt sequence cost %d, want 7", got)
	}
	if bus.mem[0x01FB]&FlagB != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("hardware interrupt status byte has B set: %02X", bus.mem[0x01FB])
	}
	if bus.mem[0x01FB]&FlagU == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("hardware interrupt status byte lost the U bit")
	}
	if c.PC() != 0x9000 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %04X, want 9000", c.PC())
	}
	// Return address is past the executed NOP: $8002.
	if bus.mem[0x01FD] != 0x80 || bus.mem[0x01FC] != 0x02 {
		t.Fatalf("return address pushed = %02X%02X, want 8002", bus.mem[0x01FD], bus.mem[0x01FC])
	}
}

// hijackBus raises the NMI line the moment the CPU pushes BRK's
// return address, simulating a PPU vblank landing mid-BRK.
type hijackBus struct {
	flatBus
	cpu *CPU
}

func (b *hijackBus) Write(a uint16, v uint8) {
	b.flatBus.Write(a, v)
	if a == 0x01FD && b.cpu != nil {
		b.cpu.SetNMILine(true)
	}
}

func TestNMIHijacksBRK(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &hijackBus{}
	bus.mem[VectorIRQ] = 0x00
	bus.mem[VectorIRQ+1] = 0x90
	bus.mem[VectorNMI] = 0x00
	bus.mem[VectorNMI+1] = 0xA0
	bus.mem[VectorReset] = 0x00
	bus.mem[VectorReset+1] = 0x80
	bus.mem[0x8000] = 0x00 // BRK
	c := New()
	c.Attach(bus)
	bus.cpu = c
	c.Reset()
	c.Step()
	if c.PC() != 0xA000 {
		t.Fatalf("PC = %04X, want A000 (NMI vector, hijacked)", c.PC())
	}
	// The pushed bytes are still BRK's: B-set status, return past
	// the padding byte.
	if bus.mem[0x01FB] != 0x34 {
		t.Fatalf("status byte = %02X, want 34 (BRK bytes)", bus.mem[0x01FB])
	}
	if c.NMIPending() {
		t.Fatalf("NMI latch should be consumed by the hijack")
	}
}

func TestPHPAndPLPBitRules(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	// LDA #$00 (Z set), PHP, SEC, CLC... then PLP restores.
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000,
		0xA9, 0x00, // LDA #$00: P = U|Z = $26 after reset's $24 loses I? (I stays) P=$26
		0x08, // PHP
		0x38, // SEC
		0x28, // PLP
	)
	c.Step()
	c.Step() // PHP
	pushed := bus.mem[0x01FD]
	if pushed&FlagB == 0 || pushed&FlagU == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("PHP byte %02X must carry B and U", pushed)
	}
	c.Step() // SEC
	if c.Regs().P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("SEC did not set C")
	}
	c.Step() // PLP
	r := c.Regs()
	if r.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("PLP should have restored C clear")
	}
	if r.P&FlagB != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("live P must never carry B")
	}
	if r.P&FlagU == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("live P must always carry U")
	}
}

func TestUnofficialComposites(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	bus.mem[0x0010] = 0x81
	// SLO $10: memory becomes $02 with C set, A = A OR $02.
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0x07, 0x10)
	c.Step()
	if bus.mem[0x0010] != 0x02 {
		t.Fatalf("SLO memory = %02X, want 02", bus.mem[0x0010])
	}
	if c.Regs().A != 0x02 || c.Regs().P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("SLO result A=%02X P=%02X, want A=02 C set", c.Regs().A, c.Regs().P)
	}

	bus2 := &flatBus{}
	bus2.mem[0x0020] = 0x05
	// LDA #$05; DCP $20: memory $04, compare A with $04: C set, Z clear.
	c2 := newCPUAt(bus2, 0x8000, 0xA9, 0x05, 0xC7, 0x20)
	c2.Step()
	c2.Step()
	if bus2.mem[0x0020] != 0x04 {
		t.Fatalf("DCP memory = %02X, want 04", bus2.mem[0x0020])
	}
	if c2.Regs().P&FlagC == 0 || c2.Regs().P&FlagZ != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("DCP flags P=%02X, want C set Z clear", c2.Regs().P)
	}

	bus3 := &flatBus{}
	// LDA #$FF; TAX; AXS #$01: (A&X)=$0F? No: TAX copies $FF.
	// Use LDA #$1F; TAX; AXS #$01: A&X=$1F, X=$1E, C set.
	c3 := newCPUAt(bus3, 0x8000, 0xA9, 0x1F, 0xAA, 0xCB, 0x01)
	c3.Step()
	c3.Step()
	c3.Step()
	if c3.Regs().X != 0x1E || c3.Regs().P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("AXS result X=%02X P=%02X, want X=1E C set", c3.Regs().X, c3.Regs().P)
	}

	bus4 := &flatBus{}
	// LDA #$80; ANC #$FF: A=$80, C copies N (set).
	c4 := newCPUAt(bus4, 0x8000, 0xA9, 0x80, 0x0B, 0xFF)
	c4.Step()
	c4.Step()
	if c4.Regs().A != 0x80 || c4.Regs().P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ANC result A=%02X P=%02X, want A=80 C set", c4.Regs().A, c4.Regs().P)
	}

	bus5 := &flatBus{}
	// LDA #$81; CLC; ARR #$FF: A&$FF=$81, ROR with C clear gives
	// $40; C is bit 6 (set), V is bit6 XOR bit5 (set).
	c5 := newCPUAt(bus5, 0x8000, 0xA9, 0x81, 0x18, 0x6B, 0xFF)
	c5.Step()
	c5.Step()
	c5.Step()
	r5 := c5.Regs()
	if r5.A != 0x40 || r5.P&FlagC == 0 || r5.P&FlagV == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ARR result A=%02X P=%02X, want A=40 C and V set", r5.A, r5.P)
	}

	bus6 := &flatBus{}
	// LDA #$01; SEC; ARR #$01: AND gives $01, ROR with C set
	// gives $80. C and V must both be clear (bits 6 and 5 of
	// $80 are both 0) even though bit 7 is set. This is the case
	// Blargg's checksum sweep catches.
	c6 := newCPUAt(bus6, 0x8000, 0xA9, 0x01, 0x38, 0x6B, 0x01)
	c6.Step()
	c6.Step()
	c6.Step()
	r6 := c6.Regs()
	if r6.A != 0x80 || r6.P&FlagC != 0 || r6.P&FlagV != 0 || r6.P&FlagN == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ARR result A=%02X P=%02X, want A=80 N set, C and V clear", r6.A, r6.P)
	}
}

func TestJamAndStall(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0x02, 0xEA) // KIL, NOP
	c.Step()
	if !c.Jammed() {
		t.Fatalf("KIL did not jam the CPU")
	}
	pc := c.PC()
	c.Step()
	if c.PC() != pc {
		t.Fatalf("jammed CPU moved PC to %04X", c.PC())
	}
	c.Reset()
	if c.Jammed() {
		t.Fatalf("reset must clear the jam")
	}

	bus2 := &flatBus{}
	c2 := newCPUAt(bus2, 0x8000, 0xEA)
	c2.Stall(3)
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		if got := stepCycles(c2); got != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("stall step cost %d, want 1", got)
		}
		if c2.PC() != 0x8000 {
			t.Fatalf("stall burned an instruction, PC=%04X", c2.PC())
		}
	}
	c2.Step() // the NOP finally executes
	if c2.PC() != 0x8001 {
		t.Fatalf("PC after stall = %04X, want 8001", c2.PC())
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	bus := &flatBus{}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, 0xA9, 0x42, 0xAA, 0xE8, 0x8D, 0x00, 0x02)
	c.Step()
	c.Step()
	snap := c.Serialize()
	want := c.Regs()
	wantCycles := c.Cycles()
	// Scramble and restore.
	c.Step()
	c.Step()
	c.Step()
	if err := c.Deserialize(snap); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if c.Regs() != want || c.Cycles() != wantCycles {
		t.Fatalf("restored %+v cycles %d, want %+v cycles %d", c.Regs(), c.Cycles(), want, wantCycles)
	}
	if err := c.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("short state accepted")
	}
	bad := append([]byte{}, snap...)
	bad[0] = 99
	if err := c.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("bad version accepted")
	}
}

// TestOpcodeSpaceCoverage steps every opcode once on a flat RAM
// bus and checks that the disassembler's instruction length
// agrees with the executor's PC advance (control-flow opcodes
// excluded; they land where they land), and that exactly the KIL
// set jams.
func TestOpcodeSpaceCoverage(t *testing.T) {
	controlFlow := map[uint8]bool{
		0x00: true, // BRK
		0x20: true, // JSR
		0x40: true, // RTI
		0x60: true, // RTS
		0x4C: true, // JMP abs
		0x6C: true, // JMP ind
	}
	kil := map[uint8]bool{}
	for _, op := range []uint8{0x02, 0x12, 0x22, 0x32, 0x42, 0x52, 0x62, 0x72, 0x92, 0xB2, 0xD2, 0xF2} {
		kil[op] = true
	}
	for op := 0; op < 256; op++ {
		bus := &flatBus{}
		c := newCPUAt(bus, 0x8000, uint8(op), 0x00, 0x00)
		c.Step()
		if c.Jammed() != kil[uint8(op)] {
			t.Fatalf("opcode %02X jammed=%v, want %v", op, c.Jammed(), kil[uint8(op)])
		}
		if controlFlow[uint8(op)] || kil[uint8(op)] {
			continue
		}
		want := uint16(disLen(disOf(uint8(op)).mode))
		if got := c.PC() - 0x8000; got != want {
			t.Fatalf("opcode %02X advanced PC by %d, disassembler says %d", op, got, want)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/chips/cpu6502/disasm.go ====================

package cpu6502

import "fmt"

// Disassembly support, in the format the nestest golden log uses
// (the Nintendulator trace format). Kept beside the CPU because
// it must agree with the decoder about every opcode's length and
// addressing mode; a test cross-checks the two over the whole
// opcode space.

// disMode is a disassembly addressing mode. It mirrors addrMode
// but adds the implied, relative, and JMP-indirect shapes the
// execution grid handles outside decode.
type disMode int

const (
	dmImp disMode = iota
	dmAcc
	dmImm
	dmZP
	dmZPX
	dmZPY
	dmAbs
	dmAbsX
	dmAbsY
	dmIndX
	dmIndY
	dmInd
	dmRel
)

// disInfo describes one opcode for the disassembler.
type disInfo struct {
	name       string
	mode       disMode
	unofficial bool
}

// disLen returns the instruction length in bytes for a mode.
func disLen(m disMode) int {
	switch m {
	case dmImp, dmAcc:
		return 1
	case dmAbs, dmAbsX, dmAbsY, dmInd:
		return 3
	default:
		return 2
	}
}

var disSpecials = map[uint8]disInfo{
	0x00: {"BRK", dmImp, false},
	0x20: {"JSR", dmAbs, false},
	0x40: {"RTI", dmImp, false},
	0x60: {"RTS", dmImp, false},
	0x4C: {"JMP", dmAbs, false},
	0x6C: {"JMP", dmInd, false},
	0x08: {"PHP", dmImp, false},
	0x48: {"PHA", dmImp, false},
	0x28: {"PLP", dmImp, false},
	0x68: {"PLA", dmImp, false},
	0x18: {"CLC", dmImp, false},
	0x38: {"SEC", dmImp, false},
	0x58: {"CLI", dmImp, false},
	0x78: {"SEI", dmImp, false},
	0xB8: {"CLV", dmImp, false},
	0xD8: {"CLD", dmImp, false},
	0xF8: {"SED", dmImp, false},
	0x88: {"DEY", dmImp, false},
	0x8A: {"TXA", dmImp, false},
	0x98: {"TYA", dmImp, false},
	0x9A: {"TXS", dmImp, false},
	0xA8: {"TAY", dmImp, false},
	0xAA: {"TAX", dmImp, false},
	0xBA: {"TSX", dmImp, false},
	0xC8: {"INY", dmImp, false},
	0xCA: {"DEX", dmImp, false},
	0xE8: {"INX", dmImp, false},
	0xEA: {"NOP", dmImp, false},
	0x1A: {"NOP", dmImp, true},
	0x3A: {"NOP", dmImp, true},
	0x5A: {"NOP", dmImp, true},
	0x7A: {"NOP", dmImp, true},
	0xDA: {"NOP", dmImp, true},
	0xFA: {"NOP", dmImp, true},
	0x02: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x12: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x22: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x32: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x42: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x52: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x62: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x72: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x92: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0xB2: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0xD2: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0xF2: {"KIL", dmImp, true},
	0x80: {"NOP", dmImm, true},
	0x82: {"NOP", dmImm, true},
	0x89: {"NOP", dmImm, true},
	0xC2: {"NOP", dmImm, true},
	0xE2: {"NOP", dmImm, true},
}

var branchNames = [...]string{"BPL", "BMI", "BVC", "BVS", "BCC", "BCS", "BNE", "BEQ"}

// disOf returns the disassembly description of an opcode,
// following the same grid decode as the executor.
func disOf(op uint8) disInfo {
	if info, ok := disSpecials[op]; ok {
		return info
	}
	if op&0x1F == 0x10 {
		return disInfo{branchNames[(op>>5)&7], dmRel, false}
	}
	cc := op & 3
	aaa := (op >> 5) & 7
	bbb := (op >> 2) & 7
	gridModes := [...]disMode{dmIndX, dmZP, dmImm, dmAbs, dmIndY, dmZPX, dmAbsY, dmAbsX}
	switch cc {
	case 1:
		names := [...]string{"ORA", "AND", "EOR", "ADC", "STA", "LDA", "CMP", "SBC"}
		return disInfo{names[aaa], gridModes[bbb], false}
	case 3:
		if bbb == 2 {
			names := [...]string{"ANC", "ANC", "ALR", "ARR", "XAA", "LXA", "AXS", "SBC"}
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmImm, true}
		}
		names := [...]string{"SLO", "RLA", "SRE", "RRA", "SAX", "LAX", "DCP", "ISB"}
		m := gridModes[bbb]
		if bbb == 7 && aaa == 5 {
			m = dmAbsY // LAX absolute is Y-indexed
		}
		switch op {
		case 0x93, 0x9F:
			return disInfo{"AHX", m, true}
		case 0x9B:
			return disInfo{"TAS", dmAbsY, true}
		case 0xBB:
			return disInfo{"LAS", dmAbsY, true}
		}
		if (aaa == 4 || aaa == 5) && m == dmZPX {
			m = dmZPY
		}
		return disInfo{names[aaa], m, true}
	case 2:
		names := [...]string{"ASL", "ROL", "LSR", "ROR", "STX", "LDX", "DEC", "INC"}
		switch bbb {
		case 0:
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmImm, false}
		case 1:
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmZP, false}
		case 2:
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmAcc, false}
		case 3:
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmAbs, false}
		case 5:
			if aaa == 4 || aaa == 5 {
				return disInfo{names[aaa], dmZPY, false}
			}
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmZPX, false}
		case 7:
			if aaa == 5 {
				return disInfo{names[aaa], dmAbsY, false}
			}
			if aaa == 4 {
				return disInfo{"SHX", dmAbsY, true}
			}
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmAbsX, false}
		}
		return disInfo{"KIL", dmImp, true}
	default: // cc 0
		switch bbb {
		case 0:
			names := [...]string{"", "", "", "", "", "LDY", "CPY", "CPX"}
			return disInfo{names[aaa], dmImm, false}
		case 1:
			switch aaa {
			case 1:
				return disInfo{"BIT", dmZP, false}
			case 4:
				return disInfo{"STY", dmZP, false}
			case 5:
				return disInfo{"LDY", dmZP, false}
			case 6:
				return disInfo{"CPY", dmZP, false}
			case 7:
				return disInfo{"CPX", dmZP, false}
			}
			return disInfo{"NOP", dmZP, true}
		case 3:
			switch aaa {
			case 1:
				return disInfo{"BIT", dmAbs, false}
			case 4:
				return disInfo{"STY", dmAbs, false}
			case 5:
				return disInfo{"LDY", dmAbs, false}
			case 6:
				return disInfo{"CPY", dmAbs, false}
			case 7:
				return disInfo{"CPX", dmAbs, false}
			}
			return disInfo{"NOP", dmAbs, true}
		case 5:
			switch aaa {
			case 4:
				return disInfo{"STY", dmZPX, false}
			case 5:
				return disInfo{"LDY", dmZPX, false}
			}
			return disInfo{"NOP", dmZPX, true}
		case 7:
			if aaa == 5 {
				return disInfo{"LDY", dmAbsX, false}
			}
			if op == 0x9C {
				return disInfo{"SHY", dmAbsX, true}
			}
			return disInfo{"NOP", dmAbsX, true}
		}
		return disInfo{"KIL", dmImp, true}
	}
}

// FormatTrace renders one nestest golden-log line for the
// instruction at pc, using peek for side-effect-free memory reads
// and the CPU state as it stands BEFORE the instruction executes
// (r is that state; cycles is the cycle count at the same
// moment). It also returns the address whose value fills the
// line's trailing "= XX" annotation, so a comparer can tell a
// real divergence from an annotation about stub IO space.
func FormatTrace(peek func(uint16) uint8, pc uint16, r Registers, cycles uint64) (line string, annAddr uint16, hasAnn bool) {
	op := peek(pc)
	info := disOf(op)
	b1 := peek(pc + 1)
	b2 := peek(pc + 2)

	var bytesField string
	switch disLen(info.mode) {
	case 1:
		bytesField = fmt.Sprintf("%02X", op)
	case 2:
		bytesField = fmt.Sprintf("%02X %02X", op, b1)
	default:
		bytesField = fmt.Sprintf("%02X %02X %02X", op, b1, b2)
	}

	// The golden format reserves the first operand column for
	// the unofficial marker: unofficial mnemonics start with *,
	// official ones with a space.
	name := " " + info.name
	if info.unofficial {
		name = "*" + info.name
	}
	zpPtr := func(t uint8) uint16 {
		lo := peek(uint16(t))
		hi := peek(uint16(t + 1))
		return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
	}
	absAddr := uint16(b2)<<8 | uint16(b1)
	var operand string
	switch info.mode {
	case dmImp:
		operand = name
	case dmAcc:
		operand = name + " A"
	case dmImm:
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s #$%02X", name, b1)
	case dmZP:
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%02X = %02X", name, b1, peek(uint16(b1)))
		annAddr, hasAnn = uint16(b1), true
	case dmZPX:
		eff := b1 + r.X
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%02X,X @ %02X = %02X", name, b1, eff, peek(uint16(eff)))
		annAddr, hasAnn = uint16(eff), true
	case dmZPY:
		eff := b1 + r.Y
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%02X,Y @ %02X = %02X", name, b1, eff, peek(uint16(eff)))
		annAddr, hasAnn = uint16(eff), true
	case dmAbs:
		if info.name == "JMP" || info.name == "JSR" {
			operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%04X", name, absAddr)
		} else {
			operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%04X = %02X", name, absAddr, peek(absAddr))
			annAddr, hasAnn = absAddr, true
		}
	case dmAbsX:
		eff := absAddr + uint16(r.X)
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%04X,X @ %04X = %02X", name, absAddr, eff, peek(eff))
		annAddr, hasAnn = eff, true
	case dmAbsY:
		eff := absAddr + uint16(r.Y)
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%04X,Y @ %04X = %02X", name, absAddr, eff, peek(eff))
		annAddr, hasAnn = eff, true
	case dmIndX:
		zp := b1 + r.X
		ptr := zpPtr(zp)
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s ($%02X,X) @ %02X = %04X = %02X", name, b1, zp, ptr, peek(ptr))
		annAddr, hasAnn = ptr, true
	case dmIndY:
		ptr := zpPtr(b1)
		eff := ptr + uint16(r.Y)
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s ($%02X),Y = %04X @ %04X = %02X", name, b1, ptr, eff, peek(eff))
		annAddr, hasAnn = eff, true
	case dmInd:
		lo := peek(absAddr)
		hi := peek((absAddr & 0xFF00) | uint16(uint8(absAddr)+1))
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s ($%04X) = %04X", name, absAddr, uint16(hi)<<8|uint16(lo))
	case dmRel:
		target := uint16(int32(pc) + 2 + int32(int8(b1)))
		operand = fmt.Sprintf("%s $%04X", name, target)
	}

	ppu := cycles * 3
	line = fmt.Sprintf("%04X  %-9s%-32s A:%02X X:%02X Y:%02X P:%02X SP:%02X PPU:%3d,%3d CYC:%d",
		pc, bytesField, operand, r.A, r.X, r.Y, r.P, r.SP,
		(ppu/341)%262, ppu%341, cycles)
	return line, annAddr, hasAnn
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/chips/cpu6502/exec.go ====================

package cpu6502

// Instruction execution. The opcode space is decoded the way the
// hardware lays it out (the aaabbbcc bit fields), with an explicit
// special-case switch in exec for the instructions that live
// outside the grid: branches, jumps, returns, stack and register
// operations, the KIL jams, and the one-byte NOPs. The grid slots
// that look empty on a datasheet are not empty on the silicon:
// they hold the unofficial opcodes (the grid's third column is
// almost entirely unofficial), and real NES games use several of
// them, so they are implemented to their documented behavior from
// the NESdev wiki's unofficial opcode reference.
//
// Cycle counts fall out of the addressing helpers below: each one
// performs the same bus accesses in the same order as the
// hardware, including the dummy read at the unfixed address on
// indexed accesses (charged always for stores and read-modify-
// write, and on reads only when the index crosses a page, because
// without a crossing the unfixed address IS the target) and the
// dummy write of the old value in read-modify-write instructions.

// operation identifies an instruction's action.
type operation int

const (
	opInvalid operation = iota
	opORA
	opAND
	opEOR
	opADC
	opSTA
	opLDA
	opCMP
	opSBC
	opASL
	opROL
	opLSR
	opROR
	opSTX
	opLDX
	opDEC
	opINC
	opBIT
	opSTY
	opLDY
	opCPY
	opCPX
	// Unofficial operations.
	opSLO // ASL memory, then ORA
	opRLA // ROL memory, then AND
	opSRE // LSR memory, then EOR
	opRRA // ROR memory, then ADC
	opSAX // store A AND X
	opLAX // load A and X together
	opDCP // DEC memory, then CMP
	opISC // INC memory, then SBC (also called ISB)
	opNOP // the multi-byte NOPs: fetch and discard
	opANC // AND, then copy N to C
	opALR // AND, then LSR on A
	opARR // AND, then ROR on A, with the special V and C rules
	opXAA // A = (A OR magic) AND X AND immediate (unstable on hardware)
	opAXS // X = (A AND X) minus immediate, CMP-style flags (also SBX)
	opLXA // A and X = (A OR magic) AND immediate (also ATX)
	opAHX // store A AND X AND (address high byte + 1)
	opTAS // SP = A AND X, then store SP AND (high byte + 1)
	opSHX // store X AND (high byte + 1)
	opSHY // store Y AND (high byte + 1)
	opLAS // A, X, SP = memory AND SP
	opKIL // jam the CPU until reset
)

// addrMode identifies an addressing mode.
type addrMode int

const (
	modeInvalid addrMode = iota
	modeImm
	modeZP
	modeZPX
	modeZPY
	modeAbs
	modeAbsX
	modeAbsY
	modeIndX
	modeIndY
	modeAcc
)

// magic is the OR constant the unstable XAA and LXA opcodes pick
// up from the floating bus. The value varies between machines and
// moments on real hardware (it depends on the data bus state),
// which is why these two opcodes are called unstable. Blargg's
// instr_test-v5 checksum, calibrated on NES hardware, pins LXA
// down: with 0xFF the operation loads the operand outright and
// the checksum passes, while the often-quoted 0xEE fails it, so
// 0xFF is what this core uses. Games that rely on a different
// value are relying on luck either way.
const unstableMagic = 0xFF

// decode maps a grid opcode to its operation and addressing mode.
// exec handles the off-grid opcodes first, so decode only sees
// opcodes that follow the aaabbbcc layout.
func decode(op uint8) (operation, addrMode) {
	cc := op & 3
	aaa := (op >> 5) & 7
	bbb := (op >> 2) & 7

	gridModes := [...]addrMode{modeIndX, modeZP, modeImm, modeAbs, modeIndY, modeZPX, modeAbsY, modeAbsX}

	switch cc {
	case 1: // the ALU grid
		ops := [...]operation{opORA, opAND, opEOR, opADC, opSTA, opLDA, opCMP, opSBC}
		return ops[aaa], gridModes[bbb]

	case 3: // the unofficial grid (same layout, third column)
		if bbb == 2 {
			// The immediate column holds the one-off unofficial
			// immediate instructions, plus the duplicate SBC.
			imm := [...]operation{opANC, opANC, opALR, opARR, opXAA, opLXA, opAXS, opSBC}
			return imm[aaa], modeImm
		}
		ops := [...]operation{opSLO, opRLA, opSRE, opRRA, opSAX, opLAX, opDCP, opISC}
		o := ops[aaa]
		switch op {
		case 0x93: // the SAX (indirect),Y slot is AHX
			return opAHX, modeIndY
		case 0x9F: // the SAX absolute,X slot position holds AHX absolute,Y
			return opAHX, modeAbsY
		case 0x9B: // the SAX absolute-Y slot at bbb 6 is TAS
			return opTAS, modeAbsY
		case 0xBB: // the LAX absolute-Y slot at bbb 6 is LAS
			return opLAS, modeAbsY
		}
		m := gridModes[bbb]
		// SAX and LAX index zero page by Y where the rest of the
		// grid indexes by X.
		if (o == opSAX || o == opLAX) && m == modeZPX {
			m = modeZPY
		}
		// LAX absolute is likewise Y-indexed (0xBF), unlike the
		// cc=01 grid's absolute,X column.
		if o == opLAX && bbb == 7 {
			m = modeAbsY
		}
		return o, m

	case 2: // the shift and X grid
		ops := [...]operation{opASL, opROL, opLSR, opROR, opSTX, opLDX, opDEC, opINC}
		o := ops[aaa]
		switch bbb {
		case 0:
			return o, modeImm // only LDX reaches here; the rest are handled in exec
		case 1:
			return o, modeZP
		case 2:
			return o, modeAcc // the shifts; TAX and friends are handled in exec
		case 3:
			return o, modeAbs
		case 5:
			if o == opSTX || o == opLDX {
				return o, modeZPY
			}
			return o, modeZPX
		case 7:
			if o == opLDX {
				return o, modeAbsY
			}
			if o == opSTX {
				return opSHX, modeAbsY // 0x9E is SHX, not a store
			}
			return o, modeAbsX
		}
		return opKIL, modeInvalid // bbb 4 and 6 are the KIL and implied slots

	default: // cc 0: BIT, the stores and loads of Y, the compares
		switch bbb {
		case 0:
			switch aaa {
			case 5:
				return opLDY, modeImm
			case 6:
				return opCPY, modeImm
			case 7:
				return opCPX, modeImm
			}
		case 1:
			switch aaa {
			case 1:
				return opBIT, modeZP
			case 4:
				return opSTY, modeZP
			case 5:
				return opLDY, modeZP
			case 6:
				return opCPY, modeZP
			case 7:
				return opCPX, modeZP
			}
			return opNOP, modeZP
		case 3:
			switch aaa {
			case 1:
				return opBIT, modeAbs
			case 4:
				return opSTY, modeAbs
			case 5:
				return opLDY, modeAbs
			case 6:
				return opCPY, modeAbs
			case 7:
				return opCPX, modeAbs
			}
			return opNOP, modeAbs
		case 5:
			switch aaa {
			case 4:
				return opSTY, modeZPX
			case 5:
				return opLDY, modeZPX
			}
			return opNOP, modeZPX
		case 7:
			if aaa == 5 {
				return opLDY, modeAbsX
			}
			if op == 0x9C {
				return opSHY, modeAbsX
			}
			return opNOP, modeAbsX
		}
		return opKIL, modeInvalid
	}
}

// --- flag and ALU helpers ---

func (c *CPU) setFlag(mask uint8, on bool) {
	if on {
		c.p |= mask
	} else {
		c.p &^= mask
	}
}

func (c *CPU) setZN(v uint8) {
	c.setFlag(FlagZ, v == 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x80 != 0)
}

func (c *CPU) ora(v uint8) { c.a |= v; c.setZN(c.a) }
func (c *CPU) and(v uint8) { c.a &= v; c.setZN(c.a) }
func (c *CPU) eor(v uint8) { c.a ^= v; c.setZN(c.a) }

// adc adds with carry, always in binary: on the NES CPU the
// decimal flag is a flag like any other but the arithmetic unit
// never looks at it.
func (c *CPU) adc(v uint8) {
	carry := uint16(0)
	if c.p&FlagC != 0 {
		carry = 1
	}
	sum := uint16(c.a) + uint16(v) + carry
	c.setFlag(FlagV, (c.a^uint8(sum))&(v^uint8(sum))&0x80 != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagC, sum > 0xFF)
	c.a = uint8(sum)
	c.setZN(c.a)
}

// sbc subtracts with borrow by adding the ones' complement, the
// hardware's own trick.
func (c *CPU) sbc(v uint8) { c.adc(v ^ 0xFF) }

func (c *CPU) cmp(reg, v uint8) {
	c.setFlag(FlagC, reg >= v)
	c.setZN(reg - v)
}

func (c *CPU) asl(v uint8) uint8 {
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x80 != 0)
	v <<= 1
	c.setZN(v)
	return v
}

func (c *CPU) rol(v uint8) uint8 {
	old := c.p&FlagC != 0
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x80 != 0)
	v <<= 1
	if old {
		v |= 1
	}
	c.setZN(v)
	return v
}

func (c *CPU) lsr(v uint8) uint8 {
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&1 != 0)
	v >>= 1
	c.setZN(v)
	return v
}

func (c *CPU) ror(v uint8) uint8 {
	old := c.p&FlagC != 0
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&1 != 0)
	v >>= 1
	if old {
		v |= 0x80
	}
	c.setZN(v)
	return v
}

// shiftFn returns the single-operand transform an operation
// applies to memory (or, for the accumulator forms, to A).
func (c *CPU) shiftFn(o operation) func(uint8) uint8 {
	switch o {
	case opASL, opSLO:
		return c.asl
	case opROL, opRLA:
		return c.rol
	case opLSR, opSRE:
		return c.lsr
	case opROR, opRRA:
		return c.ror
	case opINC, opISC:
		return func(v uint8) uint8 { v++; c.setZN(v); return v }
	case opDEC, opDCP:
		return func(v uint8) uint8 { v--; c.setZN(v); return v }
	}
	return func(v uint8) uint8 { return v }
}

// --- addressing helpers ---
//
// Each helper starts after the opcode fetch and performs the
// operand accesses in hardware order. Read-class indexed helpers
// return the value directly when the index did not cross a page
// (the dummy read at the unfixed address already fetched it) and
// report haveVal false when a crossing means the caller must read
// the fixed address itself.

// eaZP fetches a zero-page operand address.
func (c *CPU) eaZP() uint16 { return uint16(c.fetch()) }

// eaZPIdx fetches a zero-page address and indexes it. The add
// cycle reads the un-indexed zero-page address, and the sum wraps
// inside the page: zero-page indexing can never cross into page 1.
func (c *CPU) eaZPIdx(idx uint8) uint16 {
	t := c.fetch()
	c.dummy(uint16(t))
	return uint16(t + idx)
}

// eaAbs fetches a 16-bit operand address.
func (c *CPU) eaAbs() uint16 {
	lo := c.fetch()
	hi := c.fetch()
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// indexed applies an index to a base address with the hardware's
// unfixed-address dummy read. For write-class accesses the dummy
// is charged unconditionally; for read-class accesses the dummy
// read is the data read when the page does not cross.
func (c *CPU) indexed(base uint16, idx uint8, writeClass bool) (addr uint16, val uint8, haveVal bool) {
	addr = base + uint16(idx)
	unfixed := (base & 0xFF00) | (addr & 0x00FF)
	v := c.read(unfixed)
	if writeClass || addr&0xFF00 != base&0xFF00 {
		return addr, 0, false
	}
	return addr, v, true
}

func (c *CPU) eaAbsIdx(idx uint8, writeClass bool) (uint16, uint8, bool) {
	return c.indexed(c.eaAbs(), idx, writeClass)
}

// eaIndX resolves (indirect,X): the add cycle reads the pointer's
// own zero-page address, and both pointer bytes wrap in page 0.
func (c *CPU) eaIndX() uint16 {
	t := c.fetch()
	c.dummy(uint16(t))
	p := t + c.x
	lo := c.read(uint16(p))
	hi := c.read(uint16(p + 1))
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// eaIndYBase fetches the (indirect),Y pointer (wrapping in page 0)
// and returns the base address; the caller applies the index.
func (c *CPU) eaIndYBase() uint16 {
	t := c.fetch()
	lo := c.read(uint16(t))
	hi := c.read(uint16(t + 1))
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

func (c *CPU) eaIndY(idx uint8, writeClass bool) (uint16, uint8, bool) {
	return c.indexed(c.eaIndYBase(), idx, writeClass)
}

// eaJmpInd resolves the JMP (indirect) pointer, including the
// famous page-wrap bug: the high byte comes from the start of the
// pointer's own page, not the next page.
func (c *CPU) eaJmpInd() uint16 {
	p := c.eaAbs()
	lo := c.read(p)
	hi := c.read((p & 0xFF00) | uint16(uint8(p)+1))
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// readVal finishes a read-class indexed access.
func (c *CPU) readVal(addr uint16, val uint8, haveVal bool) uint8 {
	if haveVal {
		return val
	}
	return c.read(addr)
}

// rmw runs a read-modify-write at addr: read the value, write the
// old value back (the dummy write the hardware performs), then
// write the transformed value.
func (c *CPU) rmw(addr uint16, f func(uint8) uint8) uint8 {
	v := c.read(addr)
	c.write(addr, v)
	nv := f(v)
	c.write(addr, nv)
	return nv
}

// branch executes a conditional branch opcode; the offset byte
// has already been read as part of the fetch sequence here. A
// taken branch costs one extra cycle reading the fall-through
// address with the old high byte, plus another when the target
// crosses into a different page.
func (c *CPU) branch(op uint8) {
	off := int8(c.fetch())
	var flag uint8
	switch (op >> 6) & 3 {
	case 0:
		flag = FlagN
	case 1:
		flag = FlagV
	case 2:
		flag = FlagC
	default:
		flag = FlagZ
	}
	taken := (c.p&flag != 0) == (op&0x20 != 0)
	if !taken {
		return
	}
	target := uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
	unfixed := (c.pc & 0xFF00) | (target & 0x00FF)
	c.dummy(unfixed)
	if unfixed != target {
		c.dummy(target)
	}
	c.pc = target
}

// indexedRaw performs the indexed dummy read and reports the
// effective address and whether the index crossed a page. The
// unstable stores use it directly: their stored value can replace
// the address's high byte on a crossing.
func (c *CPU) indexedRaw(base uint16, idx uint8) (addr uint16, crossed bool) {
	addr = base + uint16(idx)
	unfixed := (base & 0xFF00) | (addr & 0x00FF)
	c.read(unfixed)
	return addr, addr&0xFF00 != base&0xFF00
}

// eaWrite resolves an address for a store or read-modify-write,
// charging the write-class dummy reads.
func (c *CPU) eaWrite(m addrMode) uint16 {
	switch m {
	case modeZP:
		return c.eaZP()
	case modeZPX:
		return c.eaZPIdx(c.x)
	case modeZPY:
		return c.eaZPIdx(c.y)
	case modeAbs:
		return c.eaAbs()
	case modeAbsX:
		addr, _, _ := c.eaAbsIdx(c.x, true)
		return addr
	case modeAbsY:
		addr, _, _ := c.eaAbsIdx(c.y, true)
		return addr
	case modeIndX:
		return c.eaIndX()
	case modeIndY:
		addr, _, _ := c.eaIndY(c.y, true)
		return addr
	}
	return 0
}

// readOperand fetches the operand value for a read-class
// instruction in the given mode.
func (c *CPU) readOperand(m addrMode) uint8 {
	switch m {
	case modeImm:
		return c.fetch()
	case modeZP:
		return c.read(c.eaZP())
	case modeZPX:
		return c.read(c.eaZPIdx(c.x))
	case modeZPY:
		return c.read(c.eaZPIdx(c.y))
	case modeAbs:
		return c.read(c.eaAbs())
	case modeAbsX:
		addr, v, have := c.eaAbsIdx(c.x, false)
		return c.readVal(addr, v, have)
	case modeAbsY:
		addr, v, have := c.eaAbsIdx(c.y, false)
		return c.readVal(addr, v, have)
	case modeIndX:
		return c.read(c.eaIndX())
	case modeIndY:
		addr, v, have := c.eaIndY(c.y, false)
		return c.readVal(addr, v, have)
	}
	return 0
}

// applyRead applies a read-class operation to a fetched value.
func (c *CPU) applyRead(o operation, v uint8) {
	switch o {
	case opORA:
		c.ora(v)
	case opAND:
		c.and(v)
	case opEOR:
		c.eor(v)
	case opADC:
		c.adc(v)
	case opSBC:
		c.sbc(v)
	case opCMP:
		c.cmp(c.a, v)
	case opLDA:
		c.a = v
		c.setZN(v)
	case opLAX:
		c.a = v
		c.x = v
		c.setZN(v)
	case opLDX:
		c.x = v
		c.setZN(v)
	case opLDY:
		c.y = v
		c.setZN(v)
	case opCPX:
		c.cmp(c.x, v)
	case opCPY:
		c.cmp(c.y, v)
	case opBIT:
		c.setFlag(FlagZ, c.a&v == 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x80 != 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, v&0x40 != 0)
	case opLAS:
		nv := v & c.sp
		c.a, c.x, c.sp = nv, nv, nv
		c.setZN(nv)
	case opNOP:
		// The operand was fetched and discarded.
	}
}

// storeVal returns the byte a store operation writes.
func (c *CPU) storeVal(o operation) uint8 {
	switch o {
	case opSTX:
		return c.x
	case opSTY:
		return c.y
	case opSAX:
		return c.a & c.x
	default: // opSTA
		return c.a
	}
}

// rmwPost applies the second half of a composite unofficial
// read-modify-write: the ALU operation on the value just written.
func (c *CPU) rmwPost(o operation, nv uint8) {
	switch o {
	case opSLO:
		c.ora(nv)
	case opRLA:
		c.and(nv)
	case opSRE:
		c.eor(nv)
	case opRRA:
		c.adc(nv)
	case opDCP:
		c.cmp(c.a, nv)
	case opISC:
		c.sbc(nv)
	}
}

// applyUnstableStore executes AHX, TAS, SHX, and SHY: the stored
// byte is ANDed with the base address's high byte plus one, and
// when the index crosses a page the address's high byte is
// replaced by the stored byte (the carry into the high byte is
// ANDed the same way). TAS also updates SP first.
func (c *CPU) applyUnstableStore(o operation, m addrMode) {
	var base uint16
	var idx uint8
	switch m {
	case modeAbsX:
		base, idx = c.eaAbs(), c.x
	case modeAbsY:
		base, idx = c.eaAbs(), c.y
	case modeIndY:
		base, idx = c.eaIndYBase(), c.y
	}
	addr, crossed := c.indexedRaw(base, idx)
	h := uint8(base>>8) + 1
	var v uint8
	switch o {
	case opAHX:
		v = c.a & c.x & h
	case opSHX:
		v = c.x & h
	case opSHY:
		v = c.y & h
	case opTAS:
		c.sp = c.a & c.x
		v = c.sp & h
	}
	if crossed {
		addr = (addr & 0x00FF) | (uint16(v) << 8)
	}
	c.write(addr, v)
}

// apply executes a grid operation once its mode is known.
func (c *CPU) apply(o operation, m addrMode) {
	switch o {
	// The unofficial immediate one-offs.
	case opANC:
		v := c.fetch()
		c.a &= v
		c.setZN(c.a)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, c.p&FlagN != 0)
	case opALR:
		v := c.fetch()
		c.a = c.lsr(c.a & v)
	case opARR:
		v := c.fetch()
		t := c.a & v
		r := t >> 1
		if c.p&FlagC != 0 {
			r |= 0x80
		}
		c.a = r
		c.setZN(r)
		// ARR's documented flags: C is bit 6 of the result, V is
		// bit 6 XOR bit 5.
		c.setFlag(FlagC, r&0x40 != 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, (r&0x40 != 0) != (r&0x20 != 0))
	case opXAA:
		v := c.fetch()
		c.a = (c.a | unstableMagic) & c.x & v
		c.setZN(c.a)
	case opLXA:
		v := c.fetch()
		c.a = (c.a | unstableMagic) & v
		c.x = c.a
		c.setZN(c.a)
	case opAXS:
		v := c.fetch()
		t := uint16(c.a & c.x)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, t >= uint16(v))
		c.x = uint8(t - uint16(v))
		c.setZN(c.x)

	case opAHX, opTAS, opSHX, opSHY:
		c.applyUnstableStore(o, m)

	case opSTA, opSTX, opSTY, opSAX:
		c.write(c.eaWrite(m), c.storeVal(o))

	case opASL, opROL, opLSR, opROR, opDEC, opINC,
		opSLO, opRLA, opSRE, opRRA, opDCP, opISC:
		if m == modeAcc {
			c.dummy(c.pc)
			c.a = c.shiftFn(o)(c.a)
			return
		}
		addr := c.eaWrite(m)
		nv := c.rmw(addr, c.shiftFn(o))
		c.rmwPost(o, nv)

	default: // read class, including opNOP (fetch and discard)
		c.applyRead(o, c.readOperand(m))
	}
}

// execBRK runs the BRK instruction: the padding byte is read and
// skipped, PC (pointing past it) and a B-set status byte are
// pushed, and the vector is fetched. An NMI latched by vector
// time hijacks the sequence to the NMI vector while keeping BRK's
// pushed bytes; the IRQ input shares BRK's vector anyway, so only
// NMI changes the outcome.
func (c *CPU) execBRK() {
	c.dummy(c.pc)
	c.pc++
	c.push(uint8(c.pc >> 8))
	c.push(uint8(c.pc))
	c.push(c.statusByte(true))
	c.p |= FlagI
	vector := uint16(VectorIRQ)
	c.syncLatch()
	if c.nmiPending {
		c.nmiPending = false
		vector = VectorNMI
	}
	lo := c.read(vector)
	hi := c.read(vector + 1)
	c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// exec runs one instruction whose opcode byte has been fetched.
func (c *CPU) exec(op uint8) {
	switch op {
	case 0x00: // BRK
		c.execBRK()
		return
	case 0x20: // JSR
		lo := c.fetch()
		c.dummy(0x0100 | uint16(c.sp))
		c.push(uint8(c.pc >> 8))
		c.push(uint8(c.pc))
		hi := c.read(c.pc)
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		return
	case 0x40: // RTI
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.dummy(0x0100 | uint16(c.sp))
		c.setP(c.pull())
		lo := c.pull()
		hi := c.pull()
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		return
	case 0x60: // RTS
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.dummy(0x0100 | uint16(c.sp))
		lo := c.pull()
		hi := c.pull()
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.pc++
		return
	case 0x4C: // JMP absolute
		c.pc = c.eaAbs()
		return
	case 0x6C: // JMP indirect
		c.pc = c.eaJmpInd()
		return

	// Stack operations.
	case 0x08: // PHP
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.push(c.statusByte(true))
		return
	case 0x48: // PHA
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.push(c.a)
		return
	case 0x28: // PLP
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.dummy(0x0100 | uint16(c.sp))
		c.setP(c.pull())
		return
	case 0x68: // PLA
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.dummy(0x0100 | uint16(c.sp))
		c.a = c.pull()
		c.setZN(c.a)
		return

	// Flag operations.
	case 0x18:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, false)
		return
	case 0x38:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, true)
		return
	case 0x58:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.setFlag(FlagI, false)
		return
	case 0x78:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.setFlag(FlagI, true)
		return
	case 0xB8:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, false)
		return
	case 0xD8:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.setFlag(FlagD, false)
		return
	case 0xF8:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.setFlag(FlagD, true)
		return

	// Register transfers and increments.
	case 0x88: // DEY
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.y--
		c.setZN(c.y)
		return
	case 0x8A: // TXA
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.a = c.x
		c.setZN(c.a)
		return
	case 0x98: // TYA
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.a = c.y
		c.setZN(c.a)
		return
	case 0x9A: // TXS (no flags)
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.sp = c.x
		return
	case 0xA8: // TAY
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.y = c.a
		c.setZN(c.y)
		return
	case 0xAA: // TAX
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.x = c.a
		c.setZN(c.x)
		return
	case 0xBA: // TSX
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.x = c.sp
		c.setZN(c.x)
		return
	case 0xC8: // INY
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.y++
		c.setZN(c.y)
		return
	case 0xCA: // DEX
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.x--
		c.setZN(c.x)
		return
	case 0xE8: // INX
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		c.x++
		c.setZN(c.x)
		return

	// NOP, official and the unofficial one-byte forms.
	case 0xEA, 0x1A, 0x3A, 0x5A, 0x7A, 0xDA, 0xFA:
		c.dummy(c.pc)
		return

	// KIL: the CPU jams until reset. PC steps back onto the
	// opcode so the Step loop's jam reads hit it, like the bus
	// does on hardware.
	case 0x02, 0x12, 0x22, 0x32, 0x42, 0x52,
		0x62, 0x72, 0x92, 0xB2, 0xD2, 0xF2:
		c.jammed = true
		c.pc--
		return

	// DOP: the two-byte NOPs in the immediate slots the grid
	// cannot use (STA immediate, ASL immediate, and friends).
	case 0x80, 0x82, 0x89, 0xC2, 0xE2:
		c.fetch()
		return
	}

	if op&0x1F == 0x10 { // the branch column
		c.branch(op)
		return
	}
	o, m := decode(op)
	c.apply(o, m)
}

// Command libretro builds the Go NES core as a libretro shared
// library (go build -buildmode=c-shared). It is a thin C ABI shell
// over the system package: the frontend (the iTaK engine) registers
// its callbacks, hands us a ROM, and calls retro_run once per
// frame.
package main

	"os"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nes/ppu"

// libretro constants used here (from the public libretro API).
const (
	envSetPixelFormat  = 10
	pixelFormatXRGB888 = 1
	deviceJoypad       = 1
	joypadB            = 0
	joypadY            = 1
	joypadSelect       = 2
	joypadStart        = 3
	joypadUp           = 4
	joypadDown         = 5
	joypadLeft         = 6
	joypadRight        = 7
	joypadA            = 8
	joypadX            = 9
	regionNTSC         = 0
	nesFPS             = 60.0988 // NTSC NES frame rate
	nesAspect          = 1.33333 // 4/3, the app convention for NES
	memSaveRAM         = 0
	memSystemRAM       = 1
)

// NES controller mask bits, the order SetButtons expects
// (the order the console's shift register clocks them out).
const (
	btnA      = 1 << 0
	btnB      = 1 << 1
	btnSelect = 1 << 2
	btnStart  = 1 << 3
	btnUp     = 1 << 4
	btnDown   = 1 << 5
	btnLeft   = 1 << 6
	btnRight  = 1 << 7
)

var sys *system.System

func main() {}

//export retro_api_version
func retro_api_version() C.uint { return 1 }

//export retro_init
func retro_init() {}

//export retro_deinit
func retro_deinit() { sys = nil }

//export retro_set_environment
func retro_set_environment(cb C.retro_environment_t) { C.nes_set_environ(cb) }

//export retro_set_video_refresh
func retro_set_video_refresh(cb C.retro_video_refresh_t) { C.nes_set_video(cb) }

//export retro_set_audio_sample
func retro_set_audio_sample(cb C.retro_audio_sample_t) { C.nes_set_audio(cb) }

//export retro_set_audio_sample_batch

	info.library_name = C.nes_get_name()
	info.library_version = C.nes_get_version()
	info.valid_extensions = C.nes_get_exts()
	info.need_fullpath = false
	info.block_extract = false

	info.geometry.base_width = ppu.Width
	info.geometry.base_height = ppu.Height
	info.geometry.max_width = ppu.Width
	info.geometry.max_height = ppu.Height
	info.geometry.aspect_ratio = nesAspect
	info.timing.fps = nesFPS
	info.timing.sample_rate = sound.SampleRate
}

//export retro_get_region
func retro_get_region() C.unsigned { return regionNTSC }

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_nes_game_info) C.bool {
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	} else if info.path != nil {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(C.GoString(info.path))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		data = b
	} else {
		return false
	}
	s, err := system.New(data)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	sys = s
	// Ask the frontend for XRGB8888 frames (what the PPU produces).
	fmt888 := C.uint32_t(pixelFormatXRGB888)
	C.nes_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&fmt888))
	return true
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() { sys = nil }

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys != nil {
		sys.Reset()
	}
}

func pressed(port int, id uint) bool {
	return C.nes_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceJoypad, 0, C.unsigned(id)) != 0
}

// pollPad translates libretro joypad state into the NES button
// mask. Libretro A and X are the console A, B and Y are the
// console B (the usual map).
func pollPad(port int) uint8 {
	var m uint8
	if pressed(port, joypadA) || pressed(port, joypadX) {
		m |= btnA
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadB) || pressed(port, joypadY) {
		m |= btnB
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadSelect) {
		m |= btnSelect
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadStart) {
		m |= btnStart
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadUp) {
		m |= btnUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadDown) {
		m |= btnDown
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadLeft) {
		m |= btnLeft
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadRight) {
		m |= btnRight
	}
	return m
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	C.nes_input_poll()
	sys.SetButtons(0, pollPad(0))
	sys.SetButtons(1, pollPad(1))
	sys.RunFrame()

	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) > 0 {
		C.nes_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]),
			C.unsigned(ppu.Width), C.unsigned(ppu.Height),
			C.size_t(ppu.Width*4))
	}
	ab := sys.AudioBuffer()
	if len(ab) >= 2 {
		frames := len(ab) / 2
		done := int(C.nes_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&ab[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
		for i := done; i < frames; i++ {
			C.nes_audio_sample(C.int16_t(ab[2*i]), C.int16_t(ab[2*i+1]))
		}
	}
}

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.StateSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	if len(state) == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), len(state))
	copy(buf, state)
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.StateSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	cp := make([]byte, size)
	copy(cp, buf)
	return sys.Deserialize(cp) == nil
}

// The memory interface exposes cartridge RAM as SAVE_RAM and the
// console's internal RAM as SYSTEM_RAM, the standard libretro
// memory map ids.

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.unsigned) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var ram []uint8
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		ram = sys.Cart().PRGRAM()
	case memSystemRAM:
		ram = sys.SystemRAM()
	}
	if len(ram) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Pointer(&ram[0])
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.unsigned) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.Cart().PRGRAM()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SystemRAM()))
	}
	return 0
}

// hooks yet.

//export retro_cheat_reset
func retro_cheat_reset() {}

//export retro_cheat_set

==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/ppu/palette.go ====================

package ppu

// The NTSC palette: the 64 RGB colors the PPU's composite
// output produces for its 64 palette entries, as published in
// the standard references (the NESdev wiki's palette table, the
// values most emulators ship as their default). The PPU itself
// stores only 6-bit color indices; this table is the fixed
// translation the core applies when it produces the XRGB8888
// framebuffer, so games see the same colors on any host.
var ntscPalette = [64][3]uint8{
	{84, 84, 84}, {0, 30, 116}, {8, 16, 144}, {48, 0, 136},
	{68, 0, 100}, {92, 0, 48}, {84, 4, 0}, {60, 24, 0},
	{32, 42, 0}, {8, 58, 0}, {0, 64, 0}, {0, 60, 0},
	{0, 50, 60}, {0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 0},

	{152, 150, 152}, {8, 76, 196}, {48, 50, 236}, {92, 30, 228},
	{136, 20, 176}, {160, 20, 100}, {152, 34, 32}, {120, 60, 0},
	{84, 90, 0}, {40, 114, 0}, {8, 124, 0}, {0, 118, 40},
	{0, 102, 120}, {0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 0},

	{236, 238, 236}, {76, 154, 236}, {120, 124, 236}, {176, 98, 236},
	{228, 84, 236}, {236, 88, 180}, {236, 106, 100}, {212, 136, 32},
	{160, 170, 0}, {116, 196, 0}, {76, 208, 32}, {56, 204, 108},
	{56, 180, 204}, {60, 60, 60}, {0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 0},

	{236, 238, 236}, {168, 204, 236}, {188, 188, 236}, {212, 178, 236},
	{236, 174, 236}, {236, 164, 212}, {236, 180, 176}, {228, 196, 144},
	{204, 210, 120}, {180, 222, 120}, {168, 226, 144}, {152, 226, 180},
	{160, 214, 228}, {160, 162, 160}, {0, 0, 0}, {0, 0, 0},
}

// emphasisScale returns the per-channel multiplier (as a
// fraction out of 256) for the $2001 emphasis bits: emphasizing
// one channel attenuates the other two. On hardware the factors
// come from the composite signal levels; the published
// approximation used across emulators is about 0.75 for the
// attenuated channels.
func emphasisScale(emphasis uint8, channel int) int {
	if emphasis == 0 {
		return 256
	}
	if emphasis&(1<<uint(channel)) != 0 {
		return 256
	}
	return 192 // 0.75
}

// rgbTable resolves (emphasis, color index) to a packed
// XRGB8888 pixel. The output stage asks for one pixel per dot
// (about 61 thousand per frame), and the answer depends only
// on the 6-bit color index and the three emphasis bits, so the
// full 512-entry table is built once at startup with exactly
// the arithmetic colorRGB used to do per pixel.
var rgbTable [8][64]uint32

func init() {
	for e := 0; e < 8; e++ {
		for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
			c := ntscPalette[i]
			r := int(c[0]) * emphasisScale(uint8(e), 0) >> 8
			g := int(c[1]) * emphasisScale(uint8(e), 1) >> 8
			b := int(c[2]) * emphasisScale(uint8(e), 2) >> 8
			rgbTable[e][i] = 0xFF000000 | uint32(r)<<16 | uint32(g)<<8 | uint32(b)
		}
	}
}

// colorRGB resolves a 6-bit PPU palette index under the current
// emphasis bits to a packed XRGB8888 pixel.
func (p *PPU) colorRGB(index uint8) uint32 {
	emph := (p.mask >> 5) & 7 // $2001 bits 5,6,7: red, green, blue
	return rgbTable[emph][index&0x3F]
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-nes/ppu/ppu.go ====================

// Package ppu is an original implementation of the NES's
// Ricoh 2C02 picture processing unit, written from the behavior
// published on the NESdev wiki: the dot-level rendering timing,
// the loopy v/t/x scrolling registers, sprite evaluation with
// its overflow bug, and the open-bus behavior of the register
// file.
//
// The PPU advances one dot at a time (341 dots per scanline,
// 262 scanlines per NTSC frame, three dots per CPU cycle). The
// machine drives it in three-dot ticks from its CPU bus
// accessors, so every CPU-visible event (the vblank flag, sprite
// 0 hits, the MMC3's A12 clocks) lands on the same dot it does
// on hardware. Rendering state that software cannot observe
// directly (the exact byte inside a two-dot fetch, the order of
// secondary OAM writes inside the clear window) is handled at
// the granularity the published timing pins down, and the
// simplifications are documented where they live.
package ppu

import "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nes/cart"

// Width and Height are the framebuffer dimensions in pixels.
const (
	Width  = 256
	Height = 240
)

// Timing constants for the NTSC 2C02.
const (
	dotsPerLine   = 341
	linesPerFrame = 262
	dotsPerFrame  = dotsPerLine * linesPerFrame // 89342, even frames

	vblSetLine = 241 // vblank flag sets at dot 1 of this line
	preLine    = 261 // pre-render line: flags clear at dot 1
)

// Memory is the cartridge side of the PPU bus: pattern memory
// and the mirroring mode, plus the A12 hook the MMC3's IRQ
// counter hangs off.
type Memory interface {
	ReadCHR(addr uint16) uint8
	WriteCHR(addr uint16, val uint8)
	MirrorMode() cart.Mirror
	ClockA12()
}

// a12MinLowDots is the glitch filter on the cartridge's A12
// line: the MMC3 only clocks its IRQ counter on a rising edge
// of A12 when the line has been low for at least this many
// consecutive dots. During rendering, A12 (bit 12 of the fetch
// address) toggles with four-dot low runs inside each tile and
// sprite fetch group, while the one edge that matters per
// scanline, the transition between the background and sprite
// fetch phases in the standard pattern-table arrangements, is
// preceded by a low run tens of dots long. This threshold sits
// between those two regimes; the Blargg mmc3_irq suite (which
// counts exactly 241 clocks per rendered frame) pins it down.
const a12MinLowDots = 9

// decayLifetimeDots is how long each bit of the IO latch holds
// a stored 1 before it decays to 0, per bit position. On
// hardware the latch is a small dynamic store whose bits fade
// at slightly different rates on a scale of somewhat under a
// second; Blargg's ppu_open_bus requires every bit gone by one
// second and intact after tens of milliseconds. One second is
// about 5.37 million dots at the NTSC dot rate.
var decayLifetimeDots = [8]uint32{
	3_600_000, 3_750_000, 3_900_000, 4_050_000,
	4_200_000, 4_350_000, 4_500_000, 4_650_000,
}

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size in bytes: version
// byte, CIRAM, OAM, palette, then the registers and pipeline
// state in this package's private layout.
const SerializeSize = 1 + 4096 + 256 + 32 + 192

const serializeVersion = 1

// PPU is a single 2C02 instance.
type PPU struct {
	mem Memory

	// Register file and scrolling state.
	ctrl    uint8 // $2000
	mask    uint8 // $2001
	oamAddr uint8 // $2003
	v       uint16
	t       uint16
	x       uint8 // fine X scroll, 0-7
	w       bool  // $2005/$2006 write toggle

	readBuf uint8 // $2007 read buffer

	// IO latch (open bus) with per-bit decay. Decay itself is
	// accounted lazily: decayDebt counts the dots elapsed
	// since the countdowns were last brought up to date, and
