==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/README.md ====================

# go-ps1

A from-scratch PlayStation (PS1) core in Go for iTaK
Gaming, built the same way as the go-genesis,
go-gameboy, go-nes and go-snes cores in this
repository: every chip is our own code, written from
published hardware documentation (the MIPS I manuals
and the psx-spx hardware notes), proven against test
evidence kept as local files only, and wrapped in a
libretro-compatible shell for the app when it is
ready. No third-party Go dependencies. No Sony BIOS
and no game images are ever part of this repository.

## Status

**PS1-4: the core is complete and app-ready. The
libretro shell (libretro/main.go, core name "iTaK
GoPS1") loads discs and PS-X EXEs, boots discs
through their SYSTEM.CNF the way the console does,
and drives the machine at its native display size
with analog pad, rumble and memory card exposed to
the frontend. The shell passes the repository's
shared enginetest harness on both payload forms
(synthetic .cue/.bin disc and bare .exe): ALL
TESTS PASSED, details in the PS1-4 section below.
PS1-3 (SPU, GTE, CD controller, MDEC, pads and
card, BIOS HLE), PS1-2 (GPU, timers, DMA, interrupt
controller) and PS1-1 (CPU, memory map, CD image
foundations) are underneath and their gates still
pass, with the reconciliations listed at the
bottom. What is NOT proven yet is stated plainly
in the honesty section: no commercial game has run
on this core.**

- `chips/r3000a`: the MIPS I R3000A CPU, as in
  PS1-1/PS1-2, plus the PS1-3 coprocessor stall
  model: GTE commands charge their documented cycle
  counts (from the psx-spx opcode summary) into the
  instruction cost at instruction granularity, and
  an exported CommitPendingLoad lets the BIOS
  interception return without stranding a delay-slot
  load.
- `chips/gte`: the full GTE. All 22 commands in the
  psx-spx dispatch table are implemented with the
  documented fixed-point semantics: RTPS (0x01),
  NCLIP (0x06), OP (0x0C), DPCS (0x10), INTPL (0x11),
  MVMVA (0x12), NCDS (0x13), CDP (0x14), NCDT (0x16),
  NCCS (0x1B), CC (0x1C), NCS (0x1E), NCT (0x20),
  SQR (0x28), DCPL (0x29), DPCT (0x2A), AVSZ3 (0x2D),
  AVSZ4 (0x2E), RTPT (0x30), GPF (0x3D), GPL (0x3E),
  NCCT (0x3F). (The psx-spx table is the checklist;
  names that appear in secondary sources but not in
  it, such as RTIR and NCAS, are not GTE opcodes and
  return the unknown-command error, pinned by a
  test.) Division inside RTPS/RTPT uses the
  documented UNR reciprocal algorithm; the gate
  measures its error against exact division over
  20,000 deterministic pseudo-random pairs (15,003
  in the non-overflow, non-saturating range): the
  measured maximum error is 2.703 quotient units
  and the gate bound is 3. The SXY FIFO (SXY0/1/2 plus the SXYP push
  register), IRGB/ORGB conversions and LZCS/LZCR
  leading-zero counts follow the docs. FLAG bit 31
  is the sticky OR of the error bits (bits 30-24 and
  18-13); the MAC0 overflow bits 23/22 are reported
  but, per the doc, are not part of the bit-31 error
  set. Saturation of IR1-3 honors the lm flag per
  command. Command cycle counts are charged to the
  CPU coprocessor stall model.
- `bus`: as in PS1-2 (2 MB RAM mirrored, 1 KB
  scratchpad, the IODevice hook on the register
  page).
- `gpu`, `timers`, `dma`: as in PS1-2 (full GP0/GP1
  rasterizer with pixel probes, exact root counters
  from machine position, 7-channel DMA with GPU
  linked lists and the psx-spx OTC worked example).
  DMA channels 0 and 1 now reach the real MDEC codec
  instead of the PS1-2 stubs.
- `spu`: the full SPU per the psx-spx SPU chapter.
  24 voices: volume L/R with the documented sweep
  modes, pitch with the documented clamp at 0x4000
  and the pitch-modulation (FM) formula driven by
  the previous voice's post-envelope output when its
  PMON bit is set (including the documented sign
  glitch for pitch values above 0x7FFF), ADPCM
  decode with the four documented filter pairs (the
  XA chapter table the SPU chapter defers to) and
  the published 4-tap gaussian interpolation table
  from psx-spx (each tap summed with its own
  arithmetic shift by 15, per the doc formula),
  ADSR with the documented rate tables and
  exponential curves, noise mode per voice, reverb
  send per voice, KON/KOFF with ENDX status, and
  the loop-address IRQ (IRQA) raising the SPU
  interrupt. All SPU addresses (SSA, LSAX, IRQA,
  ESA, TSA) are in 8-byte units. The reverb network
  implements the documented equations (input gains,
  the comb and allpass stages at the documented tap
  offsets scaled by the work area, output gains)
  with its work buffer inside SPU RAM at ESA. CD
  audio mixes at CD volume; the four 1 KB capture
  buffers in the first 4 KB of SPU RAM are written
  per the documented map (CD left at 0x000, CD right
  at 0x400, voice 1 at 0x800, voice 3 at 0xC00).
  Output is interleaved stereo int16 at 44,100 Hz
  through an exact ratio accumulator (768 CPU cycles
  per sample, exactly). Measured gates: an ADPCM
  tone built in the test from the documented encoder
  math measures exactly 440.0 Hz at pitch 0x1000
  (220 crossings in 0.5 s) and 882.0 Hz at pitch
  0x2000; ADSR attack and release hit
  their computed checkpoints; a loop sets ENDX and
  fires the IRQA interrupt (count 1 in the gate);
  FM raises the carrier's crossing count from 220
  to 328 (the documented factor of about 1.49 for
  the gate's modulator level), with 22,048 of 22,050
  samples differing; a reverb impulse returns its
  first echo at sample 142 (computed window about
  140) at peak 17,212 after a silent gap; master
  volume at half measures peaks 5,977 against
  11,954 at full, a ratio of exactly 0.500.
- `cd`: the PS1-1 image layer plus the full
  controller. The documented command set is
  implemented: Getstat (0x01), Setloc (0x02), Play
  (0x03), Forward (0x04), Backward (0x05), ReadN
  (0x06), MotorOn (0x07), Stop (0x08), Pause (0x09),
  Init (0x0A), Mute (0x0B), Demute (0x0C), Setfilter
  (0x0D), Setmode (0x0E), Getparam (0x0F), GetlocL
  (0x10), GetlocP (0x11), SetSession (0x12), GetTN
  (0x13), GetTD (0x14), SeekL (0x15), SeekP (0x16),
  Test (0x19, including the published version
  response), GetID (0x1A, with its delayed second
  response), ReadS (0x1B), Reset (0x1C), GetQ
  (0x1D, subchannel Q generated per the documented
  format with the CRC-16 computed by the documented
  polynomial), ReadTOC (0x1E). Timing model: with
  the exception of status reads, commands complete
  over modeled cycle delays driven by the machine
  advance: a seek costs a 120,000 cycle base (or a
  3,000,000 cycle settle when the drive starts from
  a stopped state) plus 900 cycles per sector of
  distance, that term capped at 6,000,000 cycles,
  and sectors then arrive one per sector period
  (451,584 cycles at 1x speed, 225,792 at 2x).
  Completion interrupts (seek INT2, data INT1) fire
  only through that advance. CD-DA playback streams
  samples to the SPU CD input through PullCDSample;
  Mode 2 Form 2 XA-ADPCM sectors decode with the XA
  filter table (different from the SPU table) and
  route to the same input when Setmode XA is on;
  Setfilter file/channel filtering applies to data
  reads. Error responses carry the documented bytes
  (INT5 with 0x10 for bad parameters, 0x80 for no
  disc).
- `mdec`: the macroblock codec per psx-spx: VLC
  bitstream parsing with the published DC and AC
  tables and escape codes, dequantization with the
  stream's quant tables, the fixed-point IDCT with
  the published coefficient set, YUV to RGB per the
  documented formula, output in 24-bit, 15-bit (STP
  bit from the control word) and 4-bit/8-bit
  monochrome modes, and DMA0-in/DMA1-out wiring in
  the documented word order. Gates: a DC-only
  luminance block decodes to the exact uniform
  value, a 4:2:0 macroblock in 15-bit mode produces
  the expected solid color at probed pixels, one AC
  coefficient lands within plus/minus 2 of an
  independent float IDCT reference (the DC path is
  exact), and a quant table change alters output as
  documented. State size 198,912 bytes. The
  package also carries a BS Huffman layer (the
  software format of STR movies and BS picture
  files) as an extension, selected by an otherwise
  unused command bit; real software performs that
  decode on the CPU, never through the MDEC ports.
  Its v3 DC reconstruction multiplies the decoded
  category value (base + index) by 4 per the
  transcription in bs.go; that scaling has not
  been verified against a real BS v3 stream and is
  flagged in the test that covers it.
- `pad`: the SIO0 joypad and memory card controller
  per psx-spx, with immediate byte completion (the
  stated timing simplification): JOY_DATA/STAT/MODE/
  CTRL/BAUD at their documented sizes, IRQ on the
  documented acknowledge conditions. Digital pad
  (ID 0x41) poll 0x42 returns active-low button
  bytes from SetButtons; config mode (0x43), mode
  set (0x44) enables the analog response (ID 0x73)
  with stick bytes from SetAnalog; the info commands
  0x45 to 0x48 and 0x4C answer the documented
  constants; rumble mapping (0x4D) is stored and the
  mapped poll bytes drive Motors(). Memory card
  behind address 0x81: read (0x52), write (0x57) and
  get ID (0x53; 0x59 is accepted identically, the
  two published sources disagree) with 128-byte
  frames, the XOR checksum over address plus data,
  the documented end bytes (0x47 good, 0x4E bad
  checksum, 0xFF bad sector; a bad-checksum write is
  not stored) and the FLAG byte semantics (starts
  0x08, bit 3 clears on a completed write, bit 2
  surfaces after a failed write). The card image is
  a raw 128 KB store; its directory is game-managed,
  we implement the raw protocol only. An absent card
  answers all 0xFF with no acknowledge. State size
  131,584 bytes including the card image.
- `system`: the wired machine, state version 3.
  PS-X EXE loading (LoadEXE) per the documented
  header: text copied to t_addr, PC = pc0, GP = gp0,
  SP and FP = s_addr + s_size when s_addr is
  nonzero, else the documented default stack top
  0x801FFF00; saved-register header fields are
  ignored. Disc boot (PS1-4, boot.go): BootDisc
  reads the loaded disc's ISO9660 filesystem, takes
  the executable path from SYSTEM.CNF's BOOT line,
  and LoadEXEs it, the console's own boot sequence
  minus the boot ROM; only the BOOT line is
  honored (TCB, EVENT and STACK lines configure
  the real kernel's tables, which the HLE allocates
  on demand). Diagnostics (PS1-4, diag.go):
  Machine.Diagnostics aggregates the
  not-implemented tally since machine creation:
  unimplemented BIOS calls, unknown CD controller
  commands, and unknown GP1 commands, each with a
  total count and the distinct offenders. The HLE BIOS (bios.go) intercepts the
  call vectors at 0xA0/0xB0/0xC0 and the
  critical-section syscalls. Implemented calls:
  A(44h) FlushCache, A(48h) SendGP1Command, A(49h)
  GPU_cw, A(4Ah) GPU_cwp, A(4Dh) GetGPUStatus;
  B(02h) init_timer, B(03h) get_timer, B(04h)
  enable_timer_irq, B(05h) disable_timer_irq,
  B(06h) restart_timer, B(07h) DeliverEvent, B(08h)
  OpenEvent, B(09h) CloseEvent, B(0Ah) WaitEvent,
  B(0Bh) TestEvent, B(0Ch) EnableEvent, B(0Dh)
  DisableEvent, B(12h) InitPAD2, B(13h) StartPAD2,
  B(14h) StopPAD2, B(20h) UnDeliverEvent; C(04h)
  get_free_EvCB_slot, C(08h) SysInitMemory, C(09h)
  SysInitKernelVariables, C(0Ah) ChangeClearRCnt,
  C(19h) SetRCnt, C(1Ah) GetRCnt, C(1Bh) ResetRCnt
  (the SDK root-counter names, at the slots the
  PS1-3 brief named; psx-spx defines the root
  counter API as the B(02h) to B(06h) set above, and
  both are implemented); SYS(01h)
  EnterCriticalSection and SYS(02h)
  ExitCriticalSection through the syscall
  instruction. Any other call is logged (the machine
  exposes UnimplementedBIOSCalls and its count) and
  returns $v0 = 0xFFFFFFFF; it never crashes.
  Events: 16 slots, handles 0xF1000000 and up, open
  disabled; mode 0x2000 marks ready for TestEvent,
  mode 0x1000 queues a callback invoked at a Step
  boundary through a synthetic frame with the full
  context saved and restored. InitPAD2 buffers are
  filled on VBlank once StartPAD2 has run. The
  slice gate is the enginetest in
  system/system_ps3_test.go: the generator in the
  homebrew package builds a PS-X EXE from
  hand-assembled MIPS that
  opens and enables the VBlank event through the
  BIOS and counts three deliveries, initializes the
  GPU through GPU_cw, DMA-uploads a texture and
  draws a textured quad, DMA-loads an ADPCM tone
  into SPU RAM and plays it, issues Setloc and ReadN
  and DMA-checksums the sector, runs RTPS through
  the GTE, and writes a PASS magic last. The test
  asserts the magic and all six stage markers, the
  framebuffer probes (the four texture quadrants
  render red, green, blue and white at (48,48),
  (80,48), (48,80) and (80,80)), the tone in the
  audio output (exactly 440.0 Hz, 220 crossings in
  0.5 s), the sector checksum (0xFFFFFF00 for the
  synthetic disc), the GTE results (SXYP (160,120)
  exact for the centered point, (226,86) for the
  offset point, FLAG bit 31 clear), and a mid-run
  save/restore continuation that is byte-identical
  in state, framebuffer (76,800 pixels), result
  area and the next 5,208 audio samples. Save states are version 3 (version
  2 states are rejected): CPU, RAM, scratchpad, GPU,
  GTE, timers, DMA, interrupt controller, SPU, CD
  controller, MDEC, pad and card, the BIOS HLE block
  and the machine misc block: 4,115,149 bytes.

## Timing and model notes (PS1-3)

- The two PS1-2 frame models still coexist exactly:
  RunFrame spends the rational CPU budget (565,045
  cycles average) while the display frame is about
  566,078 CPU cycles, so VBlank tracks display
  frames.
- WaitEvent is non-blocking in the HLE (it returns
  the current readiness): HLE time advances only
  while the CPU executes, so a blocking wait could
  never be satisfied. This is the one deliberate
  BIOS semantic deviation.
- BIOS event delivery follows the I_STAT latch, not
  I_MASK: on hardware a masked interrupt never
  reaches the kernel handler.
- The SPU KON delay is a fixed 5 output samples.
  The reverb path replaces the documented 39-tap
  resampling FIR with plain decimation at half rate
  (the reverb itself runs every second output
  sample, as documented); the feedback equations
  are the documented ones.
- Reading the MDEC register at 0x1F801820 returns a
  pending output word when status bit 31 (data-out
  request) is set, and the status register
  otherwise; the two share the address on hardware
  in the same way, disambiguated by that bit here.
- CD model constants are stated with the cd package
  above. CDROM DMA pads zeros if the data FIFO runs
  dry (hardware would stall the channel).
- GTE command timing is charged per command at
  instruction granularity; there is no cycle-exact
  coprocessor pipeline model.
- Pad and card transfers complete immediately on
  the JOY_DATA write; JOY_STAT TX-ready bits read 1
  and the baud timer bits read zero.

## PS1-2 gate reconciliations in PS1-3

- The cd package tests and the system CD gate now
  advance the machine (or the controller) past the
  modeled seek/settle delay and one sector period
  before asserting data; every content assertion is
  unchanged. The PS1-2 controller delivered sectors
  immediately; the PS1-3 timing model is the
  documented behavior the slice required.
- The SPU transfer port moved to the documented
  register map: PS1-2 carried the address register
  at 0x1F801DA4 in 4-byte units and the data port at
  0x1F801DA6; the documented map is IRQA at
  0x1F801DA4, TSA at 0x1F801DA6 in 8-byte units, and
  the data port at 0x1F801DA8. The PS1-2 transfer
  tests were updated to the documented addresses
  and units with their content assertions unchanged.

## The BIOS approach

There is no Sony BIOS in this core and there never
will be. The BIOS window exists in the memory map
and its reads return zero words (a NOP sled, so the
reset vector at 0xBFC00000 executes harmlessly), and
the documented call vectors are serviced by our own
HLE implementation (see the system section above).
User-supplied BIOS files are not read by this core.

## PS1-4: the libretro shell and app readiness

- `libretro`: the shell, core name "iTaK GoPS1",
  version "0.1", valid extensions cue|bin|iso|exe,
  loading by path (need_fullpath). Discs boot
  through BootDisc; a disc with no bootable
  SYSTEM.CNF is rejected at load. A bare .exe
  boots through LoadEXE. Video: the GPU framebuffer
  in XRGB8888, presented at the machine's current
  native display size each frame with a
  SET_GEOMETRY notice on size changes; base
  geometry 320x240, max 640x480, aspect 4:3, 59.94
  fps. Audio: 44,100 Hz stereo from the SPU, batch
  callback with per-sample fallback (the iTaK
  bridge registers only the batch callback). Input:
  the standard libretro joypad map onto the PS1
  pad; analog sticks from the libretro analog axes;
  the pad is forced into analog mode at load (see
  below). Rumble: SET_RUMBLE_INTERFACE wired to
  the pad motors when the frontend offers it
  (weak = small motor on/off, strong = large motor
  byte times 0x101); the iTaK bridge does not offer
  the interface, so rumble is inert inside the app
  for now. Memory: RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM is the
  128 KB memory card image, RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM
  is the 2 MB main RAM. Serialize forwards to the
  version 3 machine states.
- Analog mode choice: the shell always presents an
  analog pad. Frontends of this era assume one;
  games that poll a digital pad read the same
  buttons either way, and games that use the
  sticks need the 73h poll form, which only analog
  mode produces. The guest can still switch modes
  itself through the config sequence; a frontend
  reset restores the shell's choice.
- `homebrew`: the shared synthetic fixtures: the
  MIPS assembler, the enginetest guest program as
  a PS-X EXE, and ISO9660 plus cue/bin disc images
  carrying it. PS1-3's test generator moved here
  unchanged in behavior so the system gates, the
  shell gates and the harness all run the identical
  guest bytes.
- Shell enginetest: the repository's shared
  harness (go_backend/cmd/enginetest, the
  production Go bridge) ran against the desktop
  build (builds/libgo_ps1.so, gitignored) with
  both payloads. Verbatim verdicts: the .exe run
  reported non-silent audio (48,000 of 48,000
  samples), a save-point frame hash e25b3a53, and
  "RESULT: ALL TESTS PASSED"; the .cue disc run
  reported non-silent audio (48,000 of 48,000
  samples), a save-point frame hash c2a085d8, a
  restored frame matching the save point, and
  "RESULT: ALL TESTS PASSED". Inside the harness's
  750 frames the disc guest completes all six
  enginetest stages (its PASS magic is asserted by
  the in-process gates); the bare-.exe guest has no
  disc for its CD stage, so it parks in its
  documented timeout spin after stage 4 with the
  quad on screen and the tone playing, which is
  what the harness checks. In-process shell gates
  (libretro/main_test.go) cover the same loads,
  the full PASS through the .cue, the state round
  trip, the memory region sizes, and clean
  rejection of a bad EXE, a missing cue and an
  unbootable ISO.
- Disc boot gate (system/boot_test.go): the
  synthetic ISO boots end to end (all six guest
  stages, PASS magic, zero unimplemented BIOS
  calls, empty diagnostics), and bad discs fail
  with errors, not hangs.
- First-real-game diagnostics: at unload (and at
  retro_deinit, which the iTaK bridge calls without
  an unload), the shell prints the machine's
  not-implemented tally through the frontend log
  interface, once per loaded game, when it is
  nonzero: the unimplemented BIOS calls by table
  and function, the unknown CD command bytes, and
  the unknown GP1 command bytes, each with counts.
  The iTaK bridge prints core log lines to stderr
  with a "[core] " prefix. A real game that fails
  will name what it needs in the log.

## Roadmap: closed

PS1-1 through PS1-4 are done; the core is
app-ready and the app swap off PCSX ReARMed is
prepared in the app tree (binding, frontend slot
and release notes; the swap ships under a build
number assigned at release time). Future accuracy
work, none of it blocking: verify the MDEC BS v3
DC scaling against a real BS v3 stream; replace
the XA sample-and-hold rate conversion with the
hardware resampler; restore the documented reverb
FIR in place of half-rate decimation; real-game
compatibility passes driven by the diagnostics
above.

## Honesty notes

What is proven:

- Every subsystem gate from PS1-1 to PS1-3:
  documentation-derived suites per package, the
  GTE differential measurement (UNR max error
  2.703 quotient units), the SPU measurements
  (440.0 Hz and 882.0 Hz exact, reverb and ADSR
  measured), the CD command and timing model, the
  MDEC codec including its bitstream writer, pad
  and memory card poll bytes, and the BIOS HLE
  implemented set.
- The homebrew enginetest guest completes end to
  end in-process and through the shell from both a
  bare PS-X EXE (with a disc attached in-process)
  and a synthetic disc booted from SYSTEM.CNF,
  with zero unimplemented BIOS calls, exact
  framebuffer probes, exactly 440.0 Hz audio, and
  byte-identical save/restore continuation.
- The libretro shell loads, runs, saves and
  restores through the production bridge and the
  shared harness on both payload forms: ALL TESTS
  PASSED, twice.

What is NOT proven:

- No commercial game has run on this core. Not
  one. Every gate above is homebrew, synthetic
  fixtures, or documentation-derived unit tests.
- The BIOS HLE covers the calls the homebrew
  exercises plus the documented implemented set
  listed in this README. Real games will call
  more: other A/B/C functions, the CD file API
  family (CdSearchFile and friends), the pad and
  card libraries, and kernel paths this HLE does
  not have. Those calls are logged and return
  0xFFFFFFFF today; the diagnostics exist so the
  first real-game failure says which ones matter.
- Disc boot covers ISO9660 discs with a SYSTEM.CNF
  BOOT line, the standard retail layout. Discs
  with subchannel tricks, multi-disc sets, CD-DA
  heavy layouts, and copy-protection checks are
  untested territory.
- The swap decision belongs with a real-game check
  against a real disc library; the harness results
  above are necessary evidence, not sufficient
  evidence.

Standing notes:

- Conformance: the TomHarte/ProcessorTests tree has
  no MIPS or PSX single-step set. The gates are the
  documentation-derived suites in each package plus
  the enginetest; all fixtures are synthetic and
  built inside the tests. No Sony data, BIOS bytes
  or game images appear anywhere in this module.
- Cycle counting is instruction-level, not
  cycle-exact: most instructions cost 1, loads and
  stores 2, the HI/LO busy model applies, and GTE
  commands charge their documented counts. Cache
  hits, memory wait states and the instruction
  cache are not simulated.
- The CD controller, SPU, GTE, MDEC and pad/card
  approximations are stated in their sections
  above, not hidden.


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/bus/bus.go ====================

// Package bus is the PlayStation memory map for the
// go-ps1 core, written from the psx-spx memory map.
//
// Virtual segments follow the R3000 fixed map: KUSEG
// (0x00000000-0x7FFFFFFF) is physical, KSEG0 and KSEG1
// strip their high bits to the same physical space,
// and KSEG2 holds the cache control register at
// 0xFFFE0130. Physical regions:
//
//   - main RAM: 2 MB at physical 0, mirrored four times
//     across the 8 MB window 0x000000-0x7FFFFF.
//   - scratchpad: 1 KB at 0x1F800000.
//   - hardware registers: 0x1F801000-0x1F802FFF, stored
//     stubs by default; when the system attaches an
//     IODevice (PS1-2), accesses to the behavioral
//     windows (GPU, timers, DMA, CD, SPU transfer
//     ports, interrupt control) route to it and only
//     unclaimed addresses use the stored page.
//   - expansion regions: reads return all ones, the
//     open-bus value used for unpopulated space.
//   - BIOS window: 512 KB mirrored across
//     0x1FC00000-0x1FFFFFFF. There is no Sony BIOS in
//     this core and none ever will be: reads return
//     zero words (a NOP sled) in this slice, and the
//     project's HLE BIOS behavior arrives in a later
//     slice (see the core README).
//
// The memory control register RAM_SIZE (0x1F801060)
// resets to its documented 2 MB value 0x00000B88. The
// cache control register at 0xFFFE0130 is stored.
package bus

const (
	RAMSize        = 2 * 1024 * 1024
	ScratchpadSize = 1024
	IOSize         = 0x2000 // 0x1F801000-0x1F802FFF

	ramWindow    = 0x00800000 // RAM mirrors span 8 MB
	scratchBase  = 0x1F800000
	ioBase       = 0x1F801000
	exp1Base     = 0x1F000000
	exp1Size     = 0x00800000
	biosBase     = 0x1FC00000
	biosWindow   = 0x00400000
	cacheCtrlAdr = 0xFFFE0130

	ramSizeReset = 0x00000B88 // documented reset value for 2 MB
	ramSizeOff   = 0x60       // offset of RAM_SIZE from 0x1F801000
)

// IODevice is a behavioral peripheral attached to the
// hardware register page. Read and Write receive the
// physical address and the access size in bytes (1, 2
// or 4) and report whether they handled the access;
// unhandled accesses fall back to the stored stub
// page. The system package installs one multiplexer
// covering the GPU, timers, DMA, CD and SPU windows;
// a Bus without a device keeps the PS1-1 stored-stub
// behavior everywhere.
type IODevice interface {
	ReadIO(addr uint32, size int) (uint32, bool)
	WriteIO(addr uint32, size int, v uint32) bool
}

// Bus is the whole physical address space.
type Bus struct {
	ram        [RAMSize]byte
	scratchpad [ScratchpadSize]byte
	io         [IOSize]byte
	cacheCtrl  uint32
	dev        IODevice
}

// SetIODevice attaches (or clears, with nil) the
// behavioral peripheral multiplexer for the register
// page.
func (b *Bus) SetIODevice(d IODevice) { b.dev = d }

// ioAccess consults the attached device for a
// register-page access at byte offset off.
func (b *Bus) ioAccess(off uint32, size int, write bool, v uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	if b.dev == nil || off >= IOSize {
		return 0, false
	}
	addr := ioBase + off
	if write {
		return 0, b.dev.WriteIO(addr, size, v)
	}
	return b.dev.ReadIO(addr, size)
}

// New returns a bus in reset state.
func New() *Bus {
	b := &Bus{}
	b.Reset()
	return b
}

// Reset clears RAM, scratchpad and the register page,
// and restores the documented memory-control reset
// values.
func (b *Bus) Reset() {
	b.ram = [RAMSize]byte{}
	b.scratchpad = [ScratchpadSize]byte{}
	b.io = [IOSize]byte{}
	b.cacheCtrl = 0
	b.Write32(ioBase+ramSizeOff, ramSizeReset)
}

// RAM returns the live main RAM store (for save states
// and tools).
func (b *Bus) RAM() []byte { return b.ram[:] }

// Scratchpad returns the live scratchpad store.
func (b *Bus) Scratchpad() []byte { return b.scratchpad[:] }

// CacheControl returns the stored cache control
// register (0xFFFE0130).
func (b *Bus) CacheControl() uint32 { return b.cacheCtrl }

// region identifies a physical region and the offset
// inside it.
type region int

const (
	regionRAM region = iota
	regionScratchpad
	regionIO
	regionBIOS
	regionOpenBus
)

// decode maps a virtual address to its region and the
// byte offset or value source inside it.
func decode(addr uint32) (region, uint32) {
	if addr >= cacheCtrlAdr && addr < cacheCtrlAdr+4 {
		// The cache control word lives in a sentinel
		// slot just past the IO page: offsets IOSize+0..3
		// are its four bytes, little-endian.
		return regionIO, IOSize + (addr - cacheCtrlAdr)
	}
	phys := addr
	switch {
	case addr >= 0x80000000 && addr < 0xA0000000: // KSEG0
		phys = addr - 0x80000000
	case addr >= 0xA0000000 && addr < 0xC0000000: // KSEG1
		phys = addr - 0xA0000000
	case addr >= 0xC0000000: // KSEG2 other than the cache register
		return regionOpenBus, 0
	}
	switch {
	case phys < ramWindow:
		return regionRAM, phys & (RAMSize - 1)
	case phys >= scratchBase && phys < scratchBase+ScratchpadSize:
		return regionScratchpad, phys - scratchBase
	case phys >= ioBase && phys < ioBase+IOSize:
		return regionIO, phys - ioBase
	case phys >= biosBase && phys < biosBase+biosWindow:
		return regionBIOS, phys - biosBase
	}
	return regionOpenBus, phys
}

// Read8 reads one byte from the virtual address.
func (b *Bus) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	reg, off := decode(addr)
	switch reg {
	case regionRAM:
		return b.ram[off]
	case regionScratchpad:
		return b.scratchpad[off]
	case regionIO:
		if off >= IOSize {
			return uint8(b.cacheCtrl >> (8 * (off - IOSize)))
		}
		if v, ok := b.ioAccess(off, 1, false, 0); ok {
			return uint8(v)
		}
		return b.io[off]
	case regionBIOS:
		// HLE stub pattern: zero bytes. Zero words are
		// NOPs, so a CPU reset into the window slides
		// harmlessly until the HLE slice lands.
		return 0
	}
	return 0xFF // expansion and unmapped space read as open bus
}

// Read16 reads a little-endian halfword.
func (b *Bus) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	if reg, off := decode(addr); reg == regionIO && off < IOSize {
		if v, ok := b.ioAccess(off, 2, false, 0); ok {
			return uint16(v)
		}
	}
	return uint16(b.Read8(addr)) | uint16(b.Read8(addr+1))<<8
}

// Read32 reads a little-endian word.
func (b *Bus) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	if reg, off := decode(addr); reg == regionIO && off < IOSize {
		if v, ok := b.ioAccess(off, 4, false, 0); ok {
			return v
		}
	}
	return uint32(b.Read8(addr)) | uint32(b.Read8(addr+1))<<8 |
		uint32(b.Read8(addr+2))<<16 | uint32(b.Read8(addr+3))<<24
}

// Write8 writes one byte. BIOS and expansion writes
// are dropped, as on hardware with nothing there.
func (b *Bus) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	reg, off := decode(addr)
	switch reg {
	case regionRAM:
		b.ram[off] = v
	case regionScratchpad:
		b.scratchpad[off] = v
	case regionIO:
		if off >= IOSize {
			shift := 8 * (off - IOSize)
			b.cacheCtrl = (b.cacheCtrl &^ (0xFF << shift)) | uint32(v)<<shift
		} else if _, ok := b.ioAccess(off, 1, true, uint32(v)); !ok {
			b.io[off] = v
		}
	}
}

// Write16 writes a little-endian halfword.
func (b *Bus) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	if reg, off := decode(addr); reg == regionIO && off < IOSize {
		if _, ok := b.ioAccess(off, 2, true, uint32(v)); ok {
			return
		}
	}
	b.Write8(addr, uint8(v))
	b.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
}

// Write32 writes a little-endian word.
func (b *Bus) Write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	if reg, off := decode(addr); reg == regionIO && off < IOSize {
		if _, ok := b.ioAccess(off, 4, true, v); ok {
			return
		}
	}
	b.Write8(addr, uint8(v))
	b.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
	b.Write8(addr+2, uint8(v>>16))
	b.Write8(addr+3, uint8(v>>24))
}

package bus

import "testing"

func TestRAMMirrorsAcrossSegments(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write32(0x00001000, 0xAABBCCDD)
	for _, addr := range []uint32{0x00001000, 0x00201000, 0x00401000, 0x00601000, 0x80001000, 0x80201000, 0xA0201000} {
		if got := b.Read32(addr); got != 0xAABBCCDD {
			t.Errorf("Read32(0x%08X) = 0x%08X, want 0xAABBCCDD (RAM mirror)", addr, got)
		}
	}
	b.Write8(0x00000000, 0x11)
	if got := b.Read8(0x00200000); got != 0x11 {
		t.Errorf("Read8(0x00200000) = 0x%02X, want 0x11 (2 MB wrap)", got)
	}
}

func TestScratchpad(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write32(0x1F800000, 0x11223344)
	if got := b.Read32(0x9F800000); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("KSEG0 scratchpad read = 0x%08X, want 0x11223344", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read32(0xBF800000); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("KSEG1 scratchpad read = 0x%08X, want 0x11223344", got)
	}
	// The last scratchpad word does not bleed into the
	// register page.
	b.Write32(0x1F8003FC, 0x55667788)
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F8003FC); got != 0x55667788 {
		t.Errorf("scratchpad top word = 0x%08X, want 0x55667788", got)
	}
}

func TestBIOSWindowIsStub(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	if got := b.Read32(0xBFC00000); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("BIOS reset vector read = 0x%08X, want 0 (HLE stub pattern)", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read32(0x1FC00180); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("BIOS exception vector read = 0x%08X, want 0", got)
	}
	b.Write32(0xBFC00000, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	if got := b.Read32(0xBFC00000); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("BIOS write was not dropped: read 0x%08X", got)
	}
}

func TestIORegisterStubsAndResetValues(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F801060); got != ramSizeReset {
		t.Errorf("RAM_SIZE = 0x%08X, want documented reset 0x%08X", got, uint32(ramSizeReset))
	}
	// Interrupt control and a DMA channel register are
	// plain stored stubs in this slice.
	b.Write32(0x1F801070, 0x00001234)
	b.Write32(0x1F8010A0, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F801070); got != 0x1234 {
		t.Errorf("I_STAT stub = 0x%08X, want 0x1234", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F8010A0); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("DMA stub = 0x%08X, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	b.Write16(0x1F801814, 0xBEEF) // inside the GPU register window
	if got := b.Read16(0x1F801814); got != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("GPU window stub = 0x%04X, want 0xBEEF", got)
	}
}

func TestCacheControlRegister(t *testing.T) {
	bus := New()
	bus.Write32(cacheCtrlAdr, 0xDEADBEEF)
	if got := bus.Read32(cacheCtrlAdr); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("cache control read = 0x%08X, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	if bus.CacheControl() != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("CacheControl() = 0x%08X, want 0xDEADBEEF", bus.CacheControl())
	}
	bus.Write8(cacheCtrlAdr+1, 0x00)
	if got := bus.Read32(cacheCtrlAdr); got != 0xDEAD00EF {
		t.Errorf("cache control byte write: read 0x%08X, want 0xDEAD00EF", got)
	}
}

func TestExpansionReadsOpenBus(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F000000); got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("expansion 1 read = 0x%08X, want 0xFFFFFFFF (open bus)", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read8(0x1FA00000); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("expansion byte read = 0x%02X, want 0xFF", got)
	}
	b.Write32(0x1F000000, 0)
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F000000); got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("expansion write changed the open bus value: 0x%08X", got)
	}
}

func TestResetClearsStores(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write32(0x00002000, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	b.Write32(0x1F800000, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	b.Reset()
	if got := b.Read32(0x00002000); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("RAM after reset = 0x%08X, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F800000); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("scratchpad after reset = 0x%08X, want 0", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read32(0x1F801060); got != ramSizeReset {
		t.Errorf("RAM_SIZE after reset = 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", got, uint32(ramSizeReset))
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/cd/audio.go ====================

package cd

// CD audio output for the SPU, per the psx-spx
// CD-ROM format and XA chapters.
//
// PullCDSample is called once per 44,100 Hz output
// sample.
//
// CD-DA: while playing, it returns the raw sector
// samples (2352-byte sectors, 588 stereo int16
// frames, little-endian) in order, advancing the
// play position by 1 frame at single speed or 2 at
// double speed (Setmode bit 7). Sectors on data
// tracks are treated as silence, as the doc notes
// for Play on data sectors. At a track boundary the
// Setmode autopause bit decides: autopause on
// pauses with INT4 at the end of the old track;
// off, playback continues into the next track, and
// at the end of the disc it stops (motor off) with
// INT4. While Forward/Backward scanning, and while
// muted, it returns silence (position is moved by
// Advance for scanning; by this pull for play).
//
// XA-ADPCM: a ReadN/ReadS stream with the Setmode
// XA bit on delivers Mode 2 Form 2 audio sectors
// to the decoder in deliverSector (via
// tryXAOrFilter) instead of the data FIFO. Decoded
// samples are queued and served sample-and-hold at
// the ratio of their rate to 44,100 Hz: each source
// sample is held until a fractional accumulator
// (rate added per output sample) crosses 44,100.
// That replaces the doc's 25-point zigzag
// resampler with the simpler hold the task
// specifies. At 37,800 Hz the hold pattern repeats
// one source sample in every 7 outputs (37,800 x 7
// = 44,100 x 6); at 18,900 Hz the ratio is 7:3.
//
// XA sector layout (raw sector): sync (12), header
// (4), subheader (4: file, channel, submode,
// codinginfo) plus its copy (4), then 0x900 bytes
// of ADPCM data in 18 portions of 128 bytes, each
// portion holding 16 header bytes and 28 data
// words. A 2336-byte raw sector is the same sector
// without sync and header: subheader at offset 0,
// ADPCM data at offset 8.

var syncPattern = []byte{0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x00}

func hasSync(raw []byte) bool {
	if len(raw) < 16 {
		return false
	}
	for i, b := range syncPattern {
		if raw[i] != b {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// parseMode2 reports the subheader of a raw sector
// when it is a Mode 2 sector, and records the
// sector header/subheader in lastHdr for GetlocL.
func (c *Controller) parseMode2(raw []byte) (file, channel, submode, coding uint8, ok bool) {
	var subOff, hdrOff int
	switch {
	case hasSync(raw) && len(raw) >= 24:
		if raw[15] != 2 {
			return 0, 0, 0, 0, false
		}
		hdrOff, subOff = 12, 16
	case len(raw) == 2336:
		subOff = 0
		hdrOff = -1
	default:
		return 0, 0, 0, 0, false
	}
	sub := raw[subOff : subOff+4]
	if hdrOff >= 0 {
		c.lastHdr = [8]byte{raw[hdrOff], raw[hdrOff+1], raw[hdrOff+2], raw[hdrOff+3],
			sub[0], sub[1], sub[2], sub[3]}
	} else {
		m, s, f := LBAToMSF(c.nextLBA)
		c.lastHdr = [8]byte{toBCD(m), toBCD(s), toBCD(f), 2, sub[0], sub[1], sub[2], sub[3]}
	}
	return sub[0], sub[1], sub[2], sub[3], true
}

// tryXAOrFilter decides, for one streamed sector,
// whether it is consumed without data delivery:
// skipped by the Setfilter rule, or decoded as XA
// audio. It also keeps lastHdr current for sectors
// it parses.
func (c *Controller) tryXAOrFilter(lba int) bool {
	raw, err := c.disc.ReadSector(lba, true)
	if err != nil || len(raw) < 2048 {
		c.updateLastHdrSynth(lba)
		return false
	}
	file, channel, submode, coding, ok := c.parseMode2(raw)
	if !ok {
		c.updateLastHdrSynth(lba)
		return false
	}
	if c.mode&0x08 != 0 && (file != c.filterFile || channel != c.filterChannel) {
		// XA filter on (Setmode bit 3): non-matching
		// sectors are skipped entirely (the task's
		// stated simplification).
		return true
	}
	isAudio := submode&0x20 != 0 && submode&0x04 != 0 && submode&0x40 != 0
	if c.mode&0x40 != 0 && isAudio {
		if c.decodeXASector(raw, coding) {
			c.xaActive = true
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// XA filter tables from the format chapter (only
// filters 0..3 exist for XA; entry 4 is the SPU's).
var (
	xaPosTable = [5]int{0, 60, 115, 98, 122}
	xaNegTable = [5]int{0, 0, -52, -55, -60}
)

// xaExpand shifts a signed sample by the (possibly
// negative) net shift without a negative shift
// count: shift is 12-shiftCode for 4-bit samples
// (expand by 12, then shift down by the code) and
// 8-shiftCode for 8-bit samples.
func xaExpand(t, shift int) int {
	if shift >= 0 {
		return t << uint(shift)
	}
	return t >> uint(-shift)
}

func (c *Controller) xaSample(t, shift, filter int, old, older *int) int16 {
	s := xaExpand(t, shift) + ((*old*xaPosTable[filter] + *older*xaNegTable[filter] + 32) >> 6)
	if s < -32768 {
		s = -32768
	}
	if s > 32767 {
		s = 32767
	}
	*older = *old
	*old = s
	return int16(s)
}

// decodeXASector decodes one XA audio sector's
// 0x900 ADPCM bytes into the sample queue. coding
// is the subheader codinginfo byte: bits 0-1
// mono/stereo, bit 2 sample rate (0=37.8 kHz,
// 1=18.9 kHz), bits 4-5 bits per sample
// (0=4-bit, 1=8-bit).
func (c *Controller) decodeXASector(raw []byte, coding uint8) bool {
	dataOff := 24
	if len(raw) == 2336 {
		dataOff = 8
	}
	if len(raw) < dataOff+0x900 {
		return false
	}
	data := raw[dataOff : dataOff+0x900]
	c.xaStereo = coding&0x03 == 1
	c.xaBits8 = (coding>>4)&0x03 == 1
	c.xaRate = 37800
	if coding&0x04 != 0 {
		c.xaRate = 18900
	}
	for portion := 0; portion < 18; portion++ {
		p := data[portion*128 : portion*128+128]
		if c.xaBits8 {
			c.decodeXAPortion8(p)
		} else {
			c.decodeXAPortion4(p)
		}
	}
	return true
}

// decodeXAPortion4 decodes one 128-byte portion in
// 4-bit format: 8 blocks of 28 samples, the blocks'
// samples packed as nibbles across the 28 data
// words (block b is nibble b of each word).
func (c *Controller) decodeXAPortion4(p []byte) {
	var blocks [8][28]int16
	for b := 0; b < 8; b++ {
		hdr := p[4+b]
		shiftCode := int(hdr & 0x0F)
		if shiftCode >= 13 {
			shiftCode = 9 // doc: reserved codes act as 9
		}
		shift := 12 - shiftCode
		filter := int(hdr>>4) & 0x03
		// Filter state is per logical channel: mono
		// runs all blocks through one state in time
		// order; stereo runs even blocks through the
		// left state and odd blocks through the
		// right state. Decoding block by block keeps
		// each channel's state in time order.
		for j := 0; j < 28; j++ {
			byt := p[16+j*4+b/2]
			nib := byt & 0x0F
			if b%2 == 1 {
				nib = byt >> 4
			}
			t := int(nib)
			if t >= 8 {
				t -= 16
			}
			switch {
			case !c.xaStereo:
				blocks[b][j] = c.xaSample(t, shift, filter, &c.xaOldM, &c.xaOlderM)
			case b%2 == 0:
				blocks[b][j] = c.xaSample(t, shift, filter, &c.xaOldL, &c.xaOlderL)
			default:
				blocks[b][j] = c.xaSample(t, shift, filter, &c.xaOldR, &c.xaOlderR)
			}
		}
	}
	c.emitXABlocks(blocks[:], 8)
}

// decodeXAPortion8 decodes one 128-byte portion in
// 8-bit format: 4 blocks of 28 samples, one byte
// per block in each data word.
func (c *Controller) decodeXAPortion8(p []byte) {
	var blocks [4][28]int16
	for b := 0; b < 4; b++ {
		hdr := p[4+b]
		shiftCode := int(hdr & 0x0F)
		if shiftCode >= 13 {
			shiftCode = 9
		}
		shift := 8 - shiftCode
		filter := int(hdr>>4) & 0x03
		for j := 0; j < 28; j++ {
			t := int(int8(p[16+j*4+b]))
			switch {
			case !c.xaStereo:
				blocks[b][j] = c.xaSample(t, shift, filter, &c.xaOldM, &c.xaOlderM)
			case b%2 == 0:
				blocks[b][j] = c.xaSample(t, shift, filter, &c.xaOldL, &c.xaOlderL)
			default:
				blocks[b][j] = c.xaSample(t, shift, filter, &c.xaOldR, &c.xaOlderR)
			}
		}
	}
	c.emitXABlocks(blocks[:], 4)
}

// emitXABlocks appends decoded blocks to the queue
// in time order: mono blocks are sequential;
// stereo blocks alternate left/right in pairs.
func (c *Controller) emitXABlocks(blocks [][28]int16, n int) {
	push := func(l, r int16) {
		if len(c.xaQueue) < xaQueueCap {
			c.xaQueue = append(c.xaQueue, [2]int16{l, r})
		}
	}
	if !c.xaStereo {
		for b := 0; b < n; b++ {
			for j := 0; j < 28; j++ {
				push(blocks[b][j], blocks[b][j])
			}
		}
		return
	}
	for pair := 0; pair+1 < n; pair += 2 {
		for j := 0; j < 28; j++ {
			push(blocks[pair][j], blocks[pair+1][j])
		}
	}
}

// pullXA serves the XA queue sample-and-hold, as
// described at the top of this file.
func (c *Controller) pullXA() (int16, int16) {
	if c.xaRate == 0 {
		c.xaRate = 37800
	}
	if c.xaNeedNext && len(c.xaQueue) > 0 {
		c.xaHoldL, c.xaHoldR = c.xaQueue[0][0], c.xaQueue[0][1]
		c.xaQueue = c.xaQueue[1:]
		c.xaHoldValid = true
		c.xaNeedNext = false
	}
	if !c.xaHoldValid {
		if len(c.xaQueue) == 0 {
			return 0, 0
		}
		c.xaHoldL, c.xaHoldR = c.xaQueue[0][0], c.xaQueue[0][1]
		c.xaQueue = c.xaQueue[1:]
		c.xaHoldValid = true
	}
	l, r := c.xaHoldL, c.xaHoldR
	c.xaAcc += c.xaRate
	if c.xaAcc >= 44100 {
		c.xaAcc -= 44100
		c.xaNeedNext = true
	}
	if c.muted {
		return 0, 0
	}
	return l, r
}

func (c *Controller) loadPlayBuf() {
	buf := make([]byte, 2352)
	if c.disc != nil {
		if tr, ok := c.trackAt(c.playLBA); ok && tr.Mode == TrackAudio {
			if raw, err := c.disc.ReadSector(c.playLBA, true); err == nil {
				copy(buf, raw)
			}
		}
		// Data track sectors play as silence, per the
		// doc's note on Play over data sectors.
	}
	c.playBuf = buf
	c.playBufLBA = c.playLBA
	c.playBufValid = true
}

// PullCDSample returns one 44,100 Hz stereo sample
// of CD audio: CD-DA while playing, XA-ADPCM while
// an XA stream is active, else silence.
func (c *Controller) PullCDSample() (int16, int16) {
	if c.playing && !c.seeking {
		if c.scanDir != 0 {
			return 0, 0 // scanning is muted; Advance moves the position
		}
		if c.playOff >= 588 {
			return 0, 0 // parked at a track end by autopause
		}
		if !c.playBufValid || c.playBufLBA != c.playLBA {
			c.loadPlayBuf()
		}
		off := c.playOff * 4
		l := int16(uint16(c.playBuf[off]) | uint16(c.playBuf[off+1])<<8)
		r := int16(uint16(c.playBuf[off+2]) | uint16(c.playBuf[off+3])<<8)
		steps := 1
		if c.mode&0x80 != 0 {
			steps = 2 // double speed: 2 source frames per output sample
		}
		for i := 0; i < steps; i++ {
			c.advancePlayFrame()
		}
		if c.muted {
			return 0, 0
		}
		return l, r
	}
	if c.xaActive {
		return c.pullXA()
	}
	return 0, 0
}

// advancePlayFrame moves the play position by one
// CD-DA frame, handling sector, track, and disc
// boundaries.
func (c *Controller) advancePlayFrame() {
	c.playOff++
	if c.playOff < 588 {
		return
	}
	c.playOff = 0
	c.playLBA++
	c.curLBA = c.playLBA
	c.playBufValid = false
	if c.mode&0x04 != 0 && c.playLBA%10 == 0 {
		c.reportFrame()
	}
	total := c.totalSectors()
	if c.playLBA >= total {
		// End of disc: INT4, playback stops, motor
		// off, per the doc.
		c.playing = false
		c.motorOn = false
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte())
		c.raiseIRQ(irqDataEnd)
		return
	}
	prevTr, pok := c.trackAt(c.playLBA - 1)
	nextTr, nok := c.trackAt(c.playLBA)
	if pok && nok && nextTr.Number != prevTr.Number && c.mode&0x02 != 0 {
		// Autopause: INT4 and pause at the END of
		// the old track (position stays there).
		c.playLBA--
		c.curLBA = c.playLBA
		c.playOff = 588
		c.playing = false
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte())
		c.raiseIRQ(irqDataEnd)
	}
}

// reportFrame emits one Play report INT1 (Setmode
// report bit): stat, track, index, then absolute
// or track-relative MSF depending on the sector,
// then peak lo/hi (modeled as 0).
func (c *Controller) reportFrame() {
	pos := c.positionBytes()
	resp := []byte{c.statusByte(), pos[0], pos[1], pos[5], pos[6], pos[7], 0, 0}
	if c.playLBA%20 >= 10 {
		resp[3] = pos[2]
		resp[4] = pos[3] | 0x80 // relative form sets the ss high bit, per the doc
		resp[5] = pos[4]
	}
	c.pushResp(resp...)
	c.raiseIRQ(irqDataReady)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/cd/cd.go ====================

// Package cd reads PlayStation disc images supplied by
// the user at runtime: .cue/.bin pairs and single-file
// .iso images. No disc image is ever part of this
// repository; this package only parses and reads files
// it is handed.
//
// Sector model: a cue sheet describes tracks made of
// fixed-size sectors. Data tracks expose 2048 bytes of
// user data per sector at a mode-dependent offset;
// audio tracks are raw 2352-byte sectors. ReadSector
// returns either the raw sector or the user data, with
// MSF/LBA conversion helpers alongside.
//
// Cue positions (INDEX times) are frame counts inside
// their file: MSFToSector converts them with no 150
// frame disc offset. Disc LBAs are zero-based from the
// first track. LBAToMSF converts a disc LBA back to an
// absolute MSF time, which includes the standard 150
// frame (2 second) lead-in offset.
package cd

import (
	"bufio"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// TrackMode classifies a track's sector layout.
type TrackMode int

const (
	TrackData  TrackMode = iota // 2048 bytes of user data per sector
	TrackAudio                  // raw 2352-byte audio sectors
)

// Track is one cue track laid out on the disc.
type Track struct {
	Number     int
	Mode       TrackMode
	SectorSize int // bytes per sector in the file
	UserOffset int // offset of user data inside a raw sector
	UserSize   int // user bytes per sector
	StartLBA   int // first disc sector of the track, including any pregap
	DataLBA    int // disc sector where INDEX 01 data begins
	Length     int // total disc sectors, including any pregap
	Pregap     int // pregap sectors (DataLBA - StartLBA)

	file          int  // index into Image.sources
	dataSector    int  // file sector of DataLBA
	storedPregap  bool // pregap lives in the file (INDEX 00 present)
	generatedPrep bool // pregap is silence (PREGAP command)
}

// Reader is what the system package consumes: a disc
// that reports its tracks and serves sectors.
type Reader interface {
	Tracks() []Track
	// ReadSector returns the raw sector when raw is
	// true, else the sector's user data.
	ReadSector(lba int, raw bool) ([]byte, error)
	Close() error
}

// Image is an opened disc image (one or more files).
type Image struct {
	tracks  []Track
	sources []io.ReaderAt
	closers []io.Closer
}

var _ Reader = (*Image)(nil)

// Tracks returns a copy of the track layout.
func (im *Image) Tracks() []Track {
	out := make([]Track, len(im.tracks))
	copy(out, im.tracks)
	return out
}

// Close closes the underlying files.
func (im *Image) Close() error {
	var first error
	for _, cl := range im.closers {
		if err := cl.Close(); err != nil && first == nil {
			first = err
		}
	}
	return first
}

// trackAt finds the track containing a disc LBA.
func (im *Image) trackAt(lba int) (Track, bool) {
	for _, t := range im.tracks {
		if lba >= t.StartLBA && lba < t.StartLBA+t.Length {
			return t, true
		}
	}
	return Track{}, false
}

// ReadSector returns the raw sector bytes (raw=true)
// or the user data bytes for a disc LBA. Generated
// pregap sectors read as zeros.
func (im *Image) ReadSector(lba int, raw bool) ([]byte, error) {
	t, ok := im.trackAt(lba)
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: LBA %d outside image (%d tracks)", lba, len(im.tracks))
	}
	size := t.UserSize
	off := t.UserOffset
	if raw {
		size = t.SectorSize
		off = 0
	}
	out := make([]byte, size)
	if t.generatedPrep && lba < t.DataLBA {
		return out, nil // pregap silence
	}
	fileSector := t.dataSector + (lba - t.DataLBA)
	src := im.sources[t.file]
	buf := make([]byte, t.SectorSize)
	if _, err := src.ReadAt(buf, int64(fileSector)*int64(t.SectorSize)); err != nil && err != io.EOF {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: reading LBA %d: %w", lba, err)
	}
	copy(out, buf[off:off+size])
	return out, nil
}

// MSFToSector converts a cue position (minutes,
// seconds, frames at 75 per second) to a sector count
// inside a file.
func MSFToSector(m, s, f int) int {
	return ((m*60)+s)*75 + f
}

// SectorToMSF converts a sector count to minutes,
// seconds, frames.
func SectorToMSF(sector int) (m, s, f int) {
	m = sector / (60 * 75)
	rem := sector % (60 * 75)
	s = rem / 75
	f = rem % 75
	return m, s, f
}

// LBAToMSF converts a zero-based disc LBA to an
// absolute MSF time, adding the standard 150 frame
// lead-in.
func LBAToMSF(lba int) (m, s, f int) {
	return SectorToMSF(lba + 150)
}

// sectorLayout resolves a cue mode string to sizes.
func sectorLayout(mode string) (sectorSize, userOff, userSize int, tm TrackMode, err error) {
	switch strings.ToUpper(mode) {
	case "AUDIO":
		return 2352, 0, 2352, TrackAudio, nil
	case "MODE1/2048":
		return 2048, 0, 2048, TrackData, nil
	case "MODE1/2352":
		return 2352, 16, 2048, TrackData, nil
	case "MODE2/2048":
		return 2048, 0, 2048, TrackData, nil
	case "MODE2/2336":
		return 2336, 8, 2048, TrackData, nil
	case "MODE2/2352":
		return 2352, 24, 2048, TrackData, nil
	}
	return 0, 0, 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("cd: unsupported track mode %q", mode)
}

// Open opens a disc image by path: .cue (with its
// referenced files), .bin (single raw Mode 2 track),
// or .iso / .img (single 2048-byte-sector data track).
func Open(path string) (*Image, error) {
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".cue":
		return openCue(path)
	case ".iso", ".img":
		return openFlat(path, 2048, 0, 2048, TrackData)
	case ".bin":
		// A lone .bin is treated as one raw Mode 2
		// track when it divides by 2352, else as flat
		// 2048-byte sectors.
		fi, err := os.Stat(path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if fi.Size()%2352 == 0 {
			return openFlat(path, 2352, 24, 2048, TrackData)
		}
		return openFlat(path, 2048, 0, 2048, TrackData)
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: unsupported image extension for %q", path)
}

func openFlat(path string, sectorSize, userOff, userSize int, tm TrackMode) (*Image, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	fi, err := f.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		f.Close()
		return nil, err
	}
	n := int(fi.Size()) / sectorSize
	if n == 0 {
		f.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %q holds no full %d-byte sectors", path, sectorSize)
	}
	tr := Track{
		Number: 1, Mode: tm, SectorSize: sectorSize,
		UserOffset: userOff, UserSize: userSize,
		StartLBA: 0, DataLBA: 0, Length: n,
		file: 0, dataSector: 0,
	}
	return &Image{
		tracks:  []Track{tr},
		sources: []io.ReaderAt{f},
		closers: []io.Closer{f},
	}, nil
}

// cueTrack is the parser's working record for one
// track before disc layout is computed.
type cueTrack struct {
	track      Track
	idx0, idx1 int
	hasIdx0    bool
	hasIdx1    bool
	pregapCmd  int // PREGAP frames, -1 when absent
	fileSize   int64
}

func openCue(path string) (*Image, error) {
	cf, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer cf.Close()
	dir := filepath.Dir(path)

	im := &Image{}
	var parsed []cueTrack
	var cur *cueTrack
	var fileSizes []int64
	curFile := -1

	sc := bufio.NewScanner(cf)
	sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 1024*1024), 1024*1024)
	lineNo := 0
	for sc.Scan() {
		lineNo++
		line := strings.TrimSpace(sc.Text())
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		fields := cueFields(line)
		if len(fields) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		switch strings.ToUpper(fields[0]) {
		case "FILE":
			if len(fields) < 2 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: FILE without a name", path, lineNo)
			}
			name := fields[1]
			fp := name
			if !filepath.IsAbs(fp) {
				fp = filepath.Join(dir, name)
			}
			f, err := os.Open(fp)
			if err != nil {
				return nil, err
			}
			fi, err := f.Stat()
			if err != nil {
				f.Close()
				return nil, err
			}
			im.sources = append(im.sources, f)
			im.closers = append(im.closers, f)
			curFile = len(im.sources) - 1
			cur = nil
			// Remember the file size on the next track
			// records via parsed entries; store it on a
			// side table keyed by file index.
			fileSizes = append(fileSizes, fi.Size())
		case "TRACK":
			if curFile < 0 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: TRACK before FILE", path, lineNo)
			}
			if len(fields) < 3 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: malformed TRACK", path, lineNo)
			}
			num, err := strconv.Atoi(fields[1])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: bad track number: %w", path, lineNo, err)
			}
			ss, uo, us, tm, err := sectorLayout(fields[2])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: %w", path, lineNo, err)
			}
			parsed = append(parsed, cueTrack{
				track: Track{
					Number: num, Mode: tm, SectorSize: ss,
					UserOffset: uo, UserSize: us, file: curFile,
				},
				pregapCmd: -1,
				fileSize:  fileSizes[curFile],
			})
			cur = &parsed[len(parsed)-1]
		case "INDEX":
			if cur == nil || len(fields) < 3 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: INDEX outside TRACK", path, lineNo)
			}
			which, err := strconv.Atoi(fields[1])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: bad INDEX number: %w", path, lineNo, err)
			}
			sec, err := parseMSF(fields[2])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: %w", path, lineNo, err)
			}
			switch which {
			case 0:
				cur.idx0, cur.hasIdx0 = sec, true
			case 1:
				cur.idx1, cur.hasIdx1 = sec, true
			}
		case "PREGAP":
			if cur == nil || len(fields) < 2 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: PREGAP outside TRACK", path, lineNo)
			}
			sec, err := parseMSF(fields[1])
			if err != nil {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %s:%d: %w", path, lineNo, err)
			}
			cur.pregapCmd = sec
		default:
			// REM, FLAGS, ISRC, PERFORMER, TITLE and the
			// rest carry nothing the reader needs.
		}
	}
	if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(parsed) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %q declares no tracks", path)
	}

	// Lay the tracks out on the disc. File boundaries
	// for each track end where the next track in the
	// same file starts (its INDEX 00 if it has one,
	// else INDEX 01), or at the end of the file.
	discLBA := 0
	for i := range parsed {
		ct := &parsed[i]
		if !ct.hasIdx1 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: track %d has no INDEX 01", ct.track.Number)
		}
		t := ct.track
		boundary := int(ct.fileSize) / t.SectorSize // file end, in sectors
		for j := i + 1; j < len(parsed); j++ {
			if parsed[j].track.file == t.file {
				if parsed[j].hasIdx0 {
					boundary = parsed[j].idx0
				} else {
					boundary = parsed[j].idx1
				}
				break
			}
		}
		switch {
		case ct.hasIdx0:
			// Pregap is stored in the file.
			t.storedPregap = true
			t.StartLBA = discLBA
			t.Pregap = ct.idx1 - ct.idx0
			t.DataLBA = discLBA + t.Pregap
			t.dataSector = ct.idx1
			t.Length = t.Pregap + (boundary - ct.idx1)
		case ct.pregapCmd > 0:
			// Pregap is generated silence.
			t.generatedPrep = true
			t.StartLBA = discLBA
			t.Pregap = ct.pregapCmd
			t.DataLBA = discLBA + t.Pregap
			t.dataSector = ct.idx1
			t.Length = t.Pregap + (boundary - ct.idx1)
		default:
			t.StartLBA = discLBA
			t.DataLBA = discLBA
			t.dataSector = ct.idx1
			t.Length = boundary - ct.idx1
		}
		if t.Length <= 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: track %d computes to %d sectors", t.Number, t.Length)
		}
		discLBA += t.Length
		im.tracks = append(im.tracks, t)
	}
	return im, nil
}

// cueFields splits a cue line, keeping a quoted file
// name (which may contain spaces) as one field.
func cueFields(line string) []string {
	var out []string
	i := 0
	for i < len(line) {
		for i < len(line) && (line[i] == ' ' || line[i] == '\t') {
			i++
		}
		if i >= len(line) {
			break
		}
		if line[i] == '"' {
			j := strings.IndexByte(line[i+1:], '"')
			if j < 0 {
				out = append(out, line[i+1:])
				break
			}
			out = append(out, line[i+1:i+1+j])
			i += j + 2
			continue
		}
		j := i
		for j < len(line) && line[j] != ' ' && line[j] != '\t' {
			j++
		}
		out = append(out, line[i:j])
		i = j
	}
	return out
}

// parseMSF parses an mm:ss:ff cue time into a sector
// count.
func parseMSF(s string) (int, error) {
	parts := strings.Split(s, ":")
	if len(parts) != 3 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("cd: bad MSF time %q", s)
	}
	var n [3]int
	for i, p := range parts {
		v, err := strconv.Atoi(p)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("cd: bad MSF time %q", s)
		}
		n[i] = v
	}
	return MSFToSector(n[0], n[1], n[2]), nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/cd/cd_test.go ====================

package cd

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestMSFConversion(t *testing.T) {
	if got := MSFToSector(1, 2, 3); got != 4653 {
		t.Errorf("MSFToSector(1,2,3) = %d, want 4653", got)
	}
	m, s, f := SectorToMSF(4653)
	if m != 1 || s != 2 || f != 3 {
		t.Errorf("SectorToMSF(4653) = %d:%02d:%02d, want 1:02:03", m, s, f)
	}
	m, s, f = LBAToMSF(0)
	if m != 0 || s != 2 || f != 0 {
		t.Errorf("LBAToMSF(0) = %d:%02d:%02d, want 0:02:00 (150 frame lead-in)", m, s, f)
	}
}

// writeCueFixture builds a two-track bin/cue in dir: a
// 4-sector Mode 2 data track whose user bytes are
// filled with 0x10+sector, and a 3-sector audio track
// filled with 0xA0+sector, with a 2-sector generated
// pregap in front of the audio.
func writeCueFixture(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	var bin []byte
	for s := 0; s < 4; s++ {
		sec := make([]byte, 2352)
		sec[0] = byte(s) // raw marker
		for i := 24; i < 24+2048; i++ {
			sec[i] = byte(0x10 + s)
		}
		bin = append(bin, sec...)
	}
	for s := 0; s < 3; s++ {
		sec := make([]byte, 2352)
		for i := range sec {
			sec[i] = byte(0xA0 + s)
		}
		bin = append(bin, sec...)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "game.bin"), bin, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cue := "FILE \"game.bin\" BINARY\n" +
		"  TRACK 01 MODE2/2352\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 00:00:00\n" +
		"  TRACK 02 AUDIO\n" +
		"    PREGAP 00:00:02\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 00:00:04\n"
	cuePath := filepath.Join(dir, "game.cue")
	if err := os.WriteFile(cuePath, []byte(cue), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return cuePath
}

func TestCueLayoutAndSectors(t *testing.T) {
	im, err := Open(writeCueFixture(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()
	tracks := im.Tracks()
	if len(tracks) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("tracks = %d, want 2", len(tracks))
	}
	d, a := tracks[0], tracks[1]
	if d.Mode != TrackData || d.StartLBA != 0 || d.DataLBA != 0 || d.Length != 4 {
		t.Errorf("data track = %+v, want data at 0, length 4", d)
	}
	if a.Mode != TrackAudio || a.StartLBA != 4 || a.DataLBA != 6 || a.Pregap != 2 || a.Length != 5 {
		t.Errorf("audio track = start %d data %d pregap %d length %d, want 4/6/2/5",
			a.StartLBA, a.DataLBA, a.Pregap, a.Length)
	}

	user, err := im.ReadSector(0, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(user) != 2048 || !bytes.Equal(user, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x10}, 2048)) {
		t.Errorf("sector 0 user data: len %d, first bytes %v, want 2048 of 0x10", len(user), user[:4])
	}
	raw, err := im.ReadSector(2, true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(raw) != 2352 || raw[0] != 2 || raw[24] != 0x12 {
		t.Errorf("sector 2 raw: len %d marker 0x%02X user start 0x%02X, want 2352/0x02/0x12",
			len(raw), raw[0], raw[24])
	}
	// Generated pregap reads as silence.
	for _, lba := range []int{4, 5} {
		sec, err := im.ReadSector(lba, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !bytes.Equal(sec, make([]byte, 2352)) {
			t.Errorf("pregap LBA %d not silent", lba)
		}
	}
	audio, err := im.ReadSector(6, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(audio, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xA0}, 2352)) {
		t.Errorf("audio sector 6: want 2352 bytes of 0xA0")
	}
	last, err := im.ReadSector(8, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(last, bytes.Repeat([]byte{0xA2}, 2352)) {
		t.Errorf("audio sector 8: want 2352 bytes of 0xA2")
	}
	if _, err := im.ReadSector(9, false); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("LBA 9 read succeeded, want out-of-range error")
	}
}

func TestFlatISOOpen(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	data := make([]byte, 2048*3)
	data[2048] = 0x77
	p := filepath.Join(dir, "flat.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	im, err := Open(p)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()
	tracks := im.Tracks()
	if len(tracks) != 1 || tracks[0].Length != 3 || tracks[0].Mode != TrackData {
		t.Fatalf("tracks = %+v, want one 3-sector data track", tracks)
	}
	sec, err := im.ReadSector(1, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if sec[0] != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("sector 1 first byte = 0x%02X, want 0x77", sec[0])
	}
}

func TestCueErrors(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	p := filepath.Join(dir, "bad.cue")
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte("FILE \"missing.bin\" BINARY\n  TRACK 01 MODE2/2352\n    INDEX 01 00:00:00\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := Open(p); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("cue with missing bin opened, want error")
	}
	if _, err := Open(filepath.Join(dir, "nope.xyz")); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("unknown extension opened, want error")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/cd/ctrl.go ====================

// CD-ROM controller, per the psx-spx CD-ROM drive
// chapter: registers at 0x1F801800-0x1F801803, the
// full documented command set, subchannel Q, and
// CD-DA / XA-ADPCM audio output for the SPU.
//
// Timing model (a model, stated plainly, built from
// the magnitudes in the psx-spx response timings
// chapter):
//
//   - Commands are written instantly. The FIRST
//     response (INT3 ack, or INT5 error) is delivered
//     immediately on the command write.
//   - A command issued while another command's
//     completion (second response) is still pending
//     is queued, one deep, and executed when that
//     completion fires in Advance; this is the
//     doc's busy rule, simplified. Getstat is exempt
//     (the doc has software poll it during seeks).
//   - All completion work is scheduled in CPU cycles
//     and processed by Advance(cycles), which the
//     system calls every CPU step.
//   - Seek delay, in cycles at 33,868,800 Hz:
//     seekDelay = settle + 900 per sector of
//     distance (the distance term capped at
//     6,000,000), where settle is 3,000,000 cycles
//     when the drive starts from a stopped (parked)
//     state, the state after disc load, reset, Stop
//     completion, or Init standby, and 120,000
//     cycles when the drive is already active. So
//     the first sector of a read from a stopped
//     state lands at 3,000,000 + the distance term
//     + one sector period.
//   - ReadN/ReadS: first sector after seekDelay
//     plus exactly one sector period; subsequent
//     sectors one sector period apart. A sector
//     period is 33,868,800/75 = 451,584 cycles at
//     single speed, half that at double speed
//     (Setmode bit 7). Each delivered sector raises
//     INT1 with a stat response byte.
//   - Play: playback starts after seekDelay (the
//     spin-up/settle model above). Pause second
//     response after 5 sector periods when active
//     (the doc's measured average is about that),
//     or 7,666 cycles when already paused. Stop
//     second response after 13,856,714 cycles when
//     spinning (the doc's measured average) or
//     7,547 when stopped. MotorOn second response
//     after the spin-up delay. Init second response
//     after 81,038 cycles. GetID second response
//     after 18,944 cycles. GetQ second response
//     after one sector period. ReadTOC second
//     response after 33,868,800 cycles (the doc
//     says about 1 second). Reset (1Ch) completes
//     silently after 0x400000 cycles (the doc's
//     stated software delay), holding the busy
//     queue for that long.
//   - Forward/Backward scan (a model of the doc's
//     fixed skipping rate): the play position moves
//     10 sectors per sector period, audio muted.
//
// Setfilter simplification (stated per the task):
// when the Setmode XA-filter bit is on, a Mode 2
// sector whose subheader file/channel does not
// match the filter is skipped entirely, for both
// data delivery and XA decode. The doc's two-pass
// data delivery quirk is not modeled.
//
// The interrupt model is unchanged from PS1-2: a
// type is recorded in the flag register when it
// occurs, and OnIRQ fires on the 0-to-1 transition
// of (flag AND enable). Writing the flag register
// acknowledges the written bits; writing bit 6
// resets the parameter/response FIFOs and flags.

package cd

import "fmt"

// IRQ types recorded in the flag register.
const (
	irqDataReady = 1
	irqComplete  = 2
	irqAck       = 3
	irqDataEnd   = 4
	irqError     = 5
)

// Timing model constants, in CPU cycles.
const (
	cpuClockHz          = 33868800
	sectorPeriod1x      = cpuClockHz / 75 // 451,584
	spinUpSettleCycles  = 3000000         // settle/spin-up from a stopped state
	seekBaseCycles      = 120000
	seekPerSectorCycles = 900
	seekTermCapCycles   = 6000000
	pauseSecondIdle     = 7666
	stopSecondSpinning  = 13856714
	stopSecondStopped   = 7547
	initSecondDelay     = 81038
	getIDSecondDelay    = 18944
	readTOCSecondDelay  = cpuClockHz // about 1 second
	resetDoneDelay      = 0x400000
	scanSectorsPerStep  = 10
)

// sectorPeriodCycles returns the current sector
// period for a Setmode byte.
func sectorPeriodCycles(mode uint8) int {
	if mode&0x80 != 0 {
		return sectorPeriod1x / 2
	}
	return sectorPeriod1x
}

// seekDelayCycles is the seek model: a per-sector
// distance term (capped), on top of a 3,000,000
// cycle settle when the drive starts from a
// stopped (parked) state, or a 120,000 cycle base
// when the drive is already active.
func seekDelayCycles(dist int, stopped bool) int {
	if dist < 0 {
		dist = -dist
	}
	term := dist * seekPerSectorCycles
	if term > seekTermCapCycles {
		term = seekTermCapCycles
	}
	if stopped {
		return spinUpSettleCycles + term
	}
	return seekBaseCycles + term
}

// Event kinds for scheduled completion work.
const (
	evSector = iota + 1
	evSeek
	evPlayStart
	evPauseSecond
	evStopSecond
	evMotorSecond
	evInitSecond
	evTOCSecond
	evSessionSecond
	evSessionError
	evSecondResp // precomputed bytes + IRQ (GetID, GetQ)
	evResetDone  // silent completion, busy hold only
)

type cdEvent struct {
	at     int64
	kind   uint8
	irq    uint8
	flag   uint8 // evSeek: 0=SeekL, 1=SeekP
	target int
	resp   []byte
}

// Controller is the CD-ROM controller.
type Controller struct {
	disc Reader

	index    int
	params   []byte
	response []byte
	data     []byte

	irqEnable uint8
	irqFlag   uint8
	irqHot    bool

	mode      uint8
	statError bool
	seekError bool
	idError   bool

	motorOn   bool
	stopped   bool // parked state: disc load, reset, Stop done, Init standby
	seeking   bool
	streaming bool
	playing   bool
	muted     bool

	pendingLBA    int  // Setloc target
	setlocPending bool // Setloc not yet consumed
	nextLBA       int  // next sector to stream
	curLBA        int  // head position (last seek/delivered sector)
	resumeLBA     int  // most recently delivered sector

	filterFile    uint8
	filterChannel uint8
	session       uint8

	// Host-side diagnostic: command bytes rejected
	// as invalid, kept across Reset, never
	// serialized.
	unknownCmds []uint8
	unknownCmdN int

	events []cdEvent
	now    int64

	// Queued command under the busy rule.
	hasQueued    bool
	queuedCmd    uint8
	queuedParams []byte

	// Play (CD-DA) state.
	playLBA      int
	playOff      int // sample frame within the sector, 0..588
	playBuf      []byte
	playBufLBA   int
	playBufValid bool
	scanDir      int // 0, +1 forward, -1 backward
	scanAcc      int

	// XA-ADPCM state.
	xaActive    bool
	xaQueue     [][2]int16
	xaHoldL     int16
	xaHoldR     int16
	xaHoldValid bool
	xaNeedNext  bool
	xaAcc       int
	xaRate      int
	xaStereo    bool
	xaBits8     bool
	xaOldL      int
	xaOlderL    int
	xaOldR      int
	xaOlderR    int
	xaOldM      int
	xaOlderM    int

	// Last delivered sector header/subheader, for
	// GetlocL: amm, ass, asect, mode, file, channel,
	// submode, codinginfo.
	lastHdr [8]byte

	scexTotal   uint8
	scexSuccess uint8

	// OnIRQ, when set, is called on the 0-to-1
	// transition of (irqFlag AND irqEnable).
	OnIRQ func()
}

// NewController returns a controller with no disc.
func NewController() *Controller { return &Controller{xaRate: 37800, stopped: true} }

// SetDisc attaches the disc image sectors are
// streamed from (nil detaches). Attaching a disc
// spins the motor up, as at door close.
func (c *Controller) SetDisc(r Reader) {
	c.disc = r
	if r == nil {
		c.motorOn = false
		c.streaming = false
		c.playing = false
		return
	}
	c.motorOn = true
	c.stopped = true
	c.scexTotal, c.scexSuccess = 0, 0
	for _, t := range r.Tracks() {
		if t.Mode == TrackData {
			c.scexTotal, c.scexSuccess = 1, 1
			break
		}
	}
	c.updateLastHdrSynth(c.curLBA)
}

// Reset returns the controller to power-on state.
// The attached disc is kept.
func (c *Controller) Reset() {
	disc := c.disc
	onIRQ := c.OnIRQ
	unk, unkN := c.unknownCmds, c.unknownCmdN
	*c = Controller{disc: disc, OnIRQ: onIRQ, xaRate: 37800, stopped: true,
		unknownCmds: unk, unknownCmdN: unkN}
	if disc != nil {
		c.SetDisc(disc)
	}
}

// UnknownCommands returns the distinct command bytes
// this controller has rejected as invalid (INT5
// code 40h), in first-seen order. It is a host-side
// diagnostic: the log survives Reset and is not part
// of the serialized state.
func (c *Controller) UnknownCommands() []uint8 {
	out := make([]uint8, len(c.unknownCmds))
	copy(out, c.unknownCmds)
	return out
}

// UnknownCommandCount returns the total number of
// invalid commands received, repeats included.
func (c *Controller) UnknownCommandCount() int { return c.unknownCmdN }

func (c *Controller) noteUnknownCmd(cmd uint8) {
	c.unknownCmdN++
	for _, u := range c.unknownCmds {
		if u == cmd {
			return
		}
	}
	c.unknownCmds = append(c.unknownCmds, cmd)
}

// DataLen returns the number of bytes waiting in the
// data FIFO.
func (c *Controller) DataLen() int { return len(c.data) }

// Streaming reports whether a read stream is active.
func (c *Controller) Streaming() bool { return c.streaming }

// Mode returns the stored Setmode byte.
func (c *Controller) Mode() uint8 { return c.mode }

// statusByte builds the documented stat byte:
//
//	7 Play, 6 Seek, 5 Read (only one of these three)
//	4 ShellOpen, 3 IdError, 2 SeekError,
//	1 Spindle Motor, 0 Error
func (c *Controller) statusByte() uint8 {
	var b uint8
	if c.statError {
		b |= 0x01
	}
	if c.motorOn {
		b |= 0x02
	}
	if c.seekError {
		b |= 0x04
	}
	if c.idError {
		b |= 0x08
	}
	if c.disc == nil {
		b |= 0x10
	}
	switch {
	case c.playing:
		b |= 0x80
	case c.seeking:
		b |= 0x40
	case c.streaming:
		b |= 0x20
	}
	return b
}

// StatusRegister returns the value read from
// 0x1F801800.
func (c *Controller) StatusRegister() uint8 {
	var b uint8 = uint8(c.index & 3)
	if len(c.params) == 0 {
		b |= 0x08 // PRMEMPT: parameter FIFO empty
	}
	if len(c.params) < 16 {
		b |= 0x10 // PRMWRDY: parameter FIFO not full
	}
	if len(c.response) > 0 {
		b |= 0x20 // RSLRRDY: response ready
	}
	if len(c.data) > 0 {
		b |= 0x40 // DRQSTS: data FIFO not empty
	}
	return b
}

func (c *Controller) raiseIRQ(typ uint8) {
	c.irqFlag |= typ
	hot := c.irqFlag&c.irqEnable != 0
	if hot && !c.irqHot && c.OnIRQ != nil {
		c.OnIRQ()
	}
	c.irqHot = hot
}

func (c *Controller) pushResp(bs ...byte) { c.response = append(c.response, bs...) }

// errorResp delivers the documented error form: a
// stat byte with the error bit set, then the error
// code byte, with INT5.
func (c *Controller) errorResp(code uint8) {
	c.pushResp(c.statusByte()|0x01, code)
	c.statError = true
	c.raiseIRQ(irqError)
}

func (c *Controller) ackResp(bs ...byte) {
	c.pushResp(bs...)
	c.raiseIRQ(irqAck)
}

// ReadReg reads one of the four controller
// registers (offset 0-3).
func (c *Controller) ReadReg(off uint32) uint8 {
	switch off & 3 {
	case 0:
		return c.StatusRegister()
	case 1:
		if len(c.response) == 0 {
			return 0
		}
		v := c.response[0]
		c.response = c.response[1:]
		return v
	case 2:
		return c.popDataByte()
	case 3:
		if c.index == 1 {
			return c.irqFlag
		}
		return c.irqEnable
	}
	return 0
}

// WriteReg writes one of the four controller
// registers.
func (c *Controller) WriteReg(off uint32, v uint8) {
	switch off & 3 {
	case 0:
		c.index = int(v & 3)
	case 1:
		if c.index == 0 {
			c.command(v)
		}
	case 2:
		if c.index == 0 && len(c.params) < 16 {
			c.params = append(c.params, v)
		}
	case 3:
		if c.index == 1 {
			if v&0x40 != 0 {
				c.params = nil
				c.response = nil
				c.irqFlag = 0
				c.irqHot = false
			} else {
				c.irqFlag &^= v & 0x1F
				c.irqHot = c.irqFlag&c.irqEnable != 0
			}
		} else {
			c.irqEnable = v & 0x1F
			hot := c.irqFlag&c.irqEnable != 0
			if hot && !c.irqHot && c.OnIRQ != nil {
				c.OnIRQ()
			}
			c.irqHot = hot
		}
	}
}

// Advance processes scheduled completion work for
// the given number of CPU cycles.
func (c *Controller) Advance(cycles int) {
	if cycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	end := c.now + int64(cycles)
	for i := 0; i < 1000000; i++ {
		idx := -1
		for j := range c.events {
			if c.events[j].at <= end && (idx < 0 || c.events[j].at < c.events[idx].at) {
				idx = j
			}
		}
		if idx < 0 {
			break
		}
		ev := c.events[idx]
		c.events = append(c.events[:idx], c.events[idx+1:]...)
		c.now = ev.at
		c.fireEvent(ev)
		if ev.kind != evSector && c.hasQueued {
			cmd, params := c.queuedCmd, c.queuedParams
			c.hasQueued, c.queuedCmd, c.queuedParams = false, 0, nil
			c.params = params
			c.execCommand(cmd)
		}
	}
	c.now = end
	if c.scanDir != 0 && c.playing {
		c.scanAcc += cycles
		period := sectorPeriodCycles(c.mode)
		for c.scanAcc >= period && c.scanDir != 0 {
			c.scanAcc -= period
			c.scanStep()
		}
	}
}

func (c *Controller) schedule(at int64, ev cdEvent) {
	ev.at = at
	c.events = append(c.events, ev)
}

func (c *Controller) cancelEvents(kinds ...uint8) {
	kept := c.events[:0]
	for _, ev := range c.events {
		drop := false
		for _, k := range kinds {
			if ev.kind == k {
				drop = true
			}
		}
		if !drop {
			kept = append(kept, ev)
		}
	}
	c.events = kept
}

// pendingCompletion reports whether a command's
// second response (or silent completion) is still
// outstanding. Sector deliveries do not count.
func (c *Controller) pendingCompletion() bool {
	for _, ev := range c.events {
		if ev.kind != evSector {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (c *Controller) fireEvent(ev cdEvent) {
	switch ev.kind {
	case evSector:
		c.deliverSector()
	case evSeek:
		c.seeking = false
		if ev.flag == 0 {
			if tr, ok := c.trackAt(ev.target); ok && tr.Mode == TrackAudio {
				// SeekL on an audio track: the doc's
				// second response is a seek error and
				// the motor stops.
				c.seekError = true
				c.motorOn = false
				c.pushResp(c.statusByte()|0x04, 0x04)
				c.raiseIRQ(irqError)
				return
			}
		}
		c.curLBA = ev.target
		c.resumeLBA = ev.target
		c.updateLastHdrSynth(ev.target)
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte())
		c.raiseIRQ(irqComplete)
	case evPlayStart:
		c.seeking = false
		c.playing = true
		c.playLBA = ev.target
		c.playOff = 0
		c.playBufValid = false
		c.curLBA = ev.target
		c.resumeLBA = ev.target
	case evPauseSecond, evInitSecond, evTOCSecond, evSessionSecond:
		if ev.kind == evSessionSecond {
			c.session = 1
			c.curLBA = 0
		}
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte())
		c.raiseIRQ(irqComplete)
	case evStopSecond:
		c.motorOn = false
		c.stopped = true
		c.curLBA = 0
		c.playLBA = 0
		c.playOff = 0
		c.playBufValid = false
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte())
		c.raiseIRQ(irqComplete)
	case evMotorSecond:
		c.motorOn = true
		c.stopped = false
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte())
		c.raiseIRQ(irqComplete)
	case evSessionError:
		c.seekError = true
		c.motorOn = false
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte()|0x04, 0x40)
		c.raiseIRQ(irqError)
	case evSecondResp:
		c.pushResp(ev.resp...)
		c.raiseIRQ(ev.irq)
	case evResetDone:
		// Silent: only held the busy queue.
	}
}

func (c *Controller) scanStep() {
	total := c.totalSectors()
	c.playLBA += c.scanDir * scanSectorsPerStep
	c.playOff = 0
	c.playBufValid = false
	if c.scanDir > 0 && c.playLBA >= total {
		c.playLBA = total
		c.scanDir = 0
		c.playing = false
		c.motorOn = false
		c.pushResp(c.statusByte())
		c.raiseIRQ(irqDataEnd)
		return
	}
	if c.scanDir < 0 && c.playLBA <= 0 {
		// Backward switches to Play at the begin of
		// track 1, per the doc.
		c.playLBA = 0
		c.scanDir = 0
	}
	if c.playLBA < 0 {
		c.playLBA = 0
	}
	c.curLBA = c.playLBA
}

// stopActivities aborts streaming, playing and
// scanning, and cancels their scheduled work. The
// motor and the data FIFO are left alone.
func (c *Controller) stopActivities() {
	c.streaming = false
	c.playing = false
	c.seeking = false
	c.scanDir = 0
	c.xaActive = false
	c.cancelEvents(evSector, evPlayStart)
}

func bcdVal(b uint8) int { return int(b>>4)*10 + int(b&0x0F) }

func bcdValid(b uint8) bool { return b>>4 <= 9 && b&0x0F <= 9 }

func toBCD(n int) uint8 {
	if n < 0 {
		n = 0
	}
	if n > 99 {
		n = 99
	}
	return uint8(n/10)<<4 | uint8(n%10)
}

func (c *Controller) tracks() []Track {
	if c.disc == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return c.disc.Tracks()
}

func (c *Controller) trackAt(lba int) (Track, bool) {
	for _, t := range c.tracks() {
		if lba >= t.StartLBA && lba < t.StartLBA+t.Length {
			return t, true
		}
	}
	return Track{}, false
}

func (c *Controller) totalSectors() int {
	total := 0
	for _, t := range c.tracks() {
		if end := t.StartLBA + t.Length; end > total {
			total = end
		}
	}
	return total
}

// headPos is the position GetlocP/GetQ report: the
// play position while playing, else the head.
func (c *Controller) headPos() int {
	if c.playing {
		return c.playLBA
	}
	return c.curLBA
}

func (c *Controller) updateLastHdrSynth(lba int) {
	m, s, f := LBAToMSF(lba)
	modeByte := uint8(0x02)
	if tr, ok := c.trackAt(lba); ok && tr.SectorSize == 2048 && tr.UserOffset == 0 {
		modeByte = 0x01
	}
	c.lastHdr = [8]byte{toBCD(m), toBCD(s), toBCD(f), modeByte, 0, 0, 0x08, 0}
}
