	sendCmd(c, 0x0E, 0x08) // Setmode: XA filter on
	setloc(c, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00)
	sendCmd(c, 0x06) // ReadN
	c.Advance(seekDelayCycles(0, true) + sectorPeriodCycles(0))
	if c.DataLen() != 2048 {
		t.Fatalf("matching sector: %d bytes, want 2048", c.DataLen())
	}
	c.Advance(sectorPeriodCycles(0)) // odd LBA: filtered out
	if c.DataLen() != 2048 {
		t.Fatalf("filtered sector was delivered: %d bytes", c.DataLen())
	}
	c.Advance(sectorPeriodCycles(0)) // even LBA again
	if c.DataLen() != 4096 {
		t.Fatalf("after next matching sector: %d bytes, want 4096", c.DataLen())
	}
	if c.data[2048] != 3 {
		t.Errorf("third sector's first byte = %d, want 3 (LBA 2 pattern)", c.data[2048])
	}
}

func TestSerializeMidStream(t *testing.T) {
	c := NewController()
	c.SetDisc(fakeDisc{})
	setloc(c, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00)
	sendCmd(c, 0x06)
	c.Advance(seekDelayCycles(0, true) + sectorPeriodCycles(0))
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		c.ReadWord()
	}
	s := c.Serialize()
	c2 := NewController()
	c2.SetDisc(fakeDisc{})
	if err := c2.Deserialize(s); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(c2.Serialize(), s) {
		t.Fatalf("mid-stream state diverged after round trip")
	}
	// The stream continues identically on both.
	c.Advance(sectorPeriodCycles(0))
	c2.Advance(sectorPeriodCycles(0))
	if c.DataLen() != c2.DataLen() {
		t.Fatalf("data lengths diverged: %d vs %d", c.DataLen(), c2.DataLen())
	}
	w1, _ := c.ReadWord()
	w2, _ := c2.ReadWord()
	if w1 != w2 {
		t.Errorf("stream words diverged: %08X vs %08X", w1, w2)
	}
}

func TestSerializeCDDAContinuation(t *testing.T) {
	c := NewController()
	c.SetDisc(fakeDisc{})
	sendCmd(c, 0x03, 0x03)
	c.Advance(seekDelayCycles(1500, true))
	drainResp(c)
	for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
		c.PullCDSample()
	}
	s := c.Serialize()
	c2 := NewController()
	c2.SetDisc(fakeDisc{})
	if err := c2.Deserialize(s); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(c2.Serialize(), s) {
		t.Fatalf("play state diverged after round trip")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		l1, r1 := c.PullCDSample()
		l2, r2 := c2.PullCDSample()
		if l1 != l2 || r1 != r2 {
			t.Fatalf("pull %d diverged: (%d,%d) vs (%d,%d)", i, l1, r1, l2, r2)
		}
		if l1 != int16(100+i) {
			t.Errorf("pull %d = %d, want %d", i, l1, 100+i)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/cd/iso.go ====================

package cd

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// Minimal ISO9660 reading over a disc Reader: the
// primary volume descriptor at sector 16, directory
// records, and file extents. Joliet and Rock Ridge
// extensions are out of scope; PlayStation discs are
// plain ISO9660 with 2048-byte logical blocks, which
// is what the user-sector reader returns.

const (
	isoSectorSize = 2048
	pvdSector     = 16
)

// DirEntry is one ISO9660 directory record.
type DirEntry struct {
	Name      string // as stored, e.g. "SYSTEM.CNF;1"; "." and ".." for the links
	ExtentLBA int    // first sector of the file or directory data
	Length    int    // data length in bytes
	IsDir     bool
}

type dirRecord struct {
	entry DirEntry
}

// ISO is an ISO9660 filesystem view of a disc.
type ISO struct {
	r          Reader
	volumeID   string
	blockSize  int
	root       DirEntry
	rootRecord dirRecord
}

// OpenISO parses the primary volume descriptor of an
// opened disc image.
func OpenISO(r Reader) (*ISO, error) {
	pvd, err := r.ReadSector(pvdSector, false)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(pvd) < 192 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: short primary volume descriptor (%d bytes)", len(pvd))
	}
	if pvd[0] != 1 || string(pvd[1:6]) != "CD001" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: sector 16 is not an ISO9660 primary volume descriptor")
	}
	blockSize := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(pvd[128:]))
	if blockSize != isoSectorSize {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: ISO logical block size %d, want %d", blockSize, isoSectorSize)
	}
	root, n := parseDirRecord(pvd[156:])
	if n == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: bad root directory record in volume descriptor")
	}
	iso := &ISO{
		r:         r,
		volumeID:  strings.Trim(string(pvd[40:72]), " \x00"),
		blockSize: blockSize,
		root:      root.entry,
	}
	iso.root.Name = ""
	return iso, nil
}

// VolumeID returns the volume identifier string.
func (iso *ISO) VolumeID() string { return iso.volumeID }

// Root returns the root directory entry.
func (iso *ISO) Root() DirEntry { return iso.root }

// parseDirRecord parses one directory record from the
// front of b, returning the entry and the record's
// total length (0 at a zero padding byte).
func parseDirRecord(b []byte) (dirRecord, int) {
	if len(b) < 1 || b[0] == 0 {
		return dirRecord{}, 0
	}
	recLen := int(b[0])
	if recLen < 34 || len(b) < recLen {
		return dirRecord{}, 0
	}
	nameLen := int(b[32])
	if 33+nameLen > recLen {
		return dirRecord{}, 0
	}
	rawName := b[33 : 33+nameLen]
	name := string(rawName)
	if nameLen == 1 && rawName[0] == 0 {
		name = "."
	} else if nameLen == 1 && rawName[0] == 1 {
		name = ".."
	}
	return dirRecord{entry: DirEntry{
		Name:      name,
		ExtentLBA: int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[2:])),
		Length:    int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[10:])),
		IsDir:     b[25]&2 != 0,
	}}, recLen
}

// readExtent returns the data of an entry.
func (iso *ISO) readExtent(e DirEntry) ([]byte, error) {
	if e.Length == 0 {
		return []byte{}, nil
	}
	sectors := (e.Length + isoSectorSize - 1) / isoSectorSize
	out := make([]byte, 0, sectors*isoSectorSize)
	for i := 0; i < sectors; i++ {
		sec, err := iso.r.ReadSector(e.ExtentLBA+i, false)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out = append(out, sec...)
	}
	return out[:e.Length], nil
}

// listDir parses a directory extent into entries,
// skipping the "." and ".." links.
func (iso *ISO) listDir(e DirEntry) ([]DirEntry, error) {
	data, err := iso.readExtent(e)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var out []DirEntry
	off := 0
	for off < len(data) {
		rec, n := parseDirRecord(data[off:])
		if n == 0 {
			// Padding to the end of the current block.
			off = ((off / isoSectorSize) + 1) * isoSectorSize
			continue
		}
		off += n
		if rec.entry.Name == "." || rec.entry.Name == ".." {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, rec.entry)
	}
	return out, nil
}

// lookup resolves a path like "DATA/MOVIE.STR;1" (the
// version suffix may be omitted) to its entry.
func (iso *ISO) lookup(path string) (DirEntry, error) {
	path = strings.Trim(path, "/")
	if path == "" {
		return iso.root, nil
	}
	cur := iso.root
	for _, part := range strings.Split(path, "/") {
		if !cur.IsDir {
			return DirEntry{}, fmt.Errorf("cd: %q crosses a non-directory", path)
		}
		entries, err := iso.listDir(cur)
		if err != nil {
			return DirEntry{}, err
		}
		found := false
		for _, e := range entries {
			if sameISOName(e.Name, part) {
				cur = e
				found = true
				break
			}
		}
		if !found {
			return DirEntry{}, fmt.Errorf("cd: path %q not found", path)
		}
	}
	return cur, nil
}

// sameISOName compares a stored name with a query
// component, case-insensitively, and tolerant of a
// missing ";1" version suffix in the query.
func sameISOName(stored, query string) bool {
	if strings.EqualFold(stored, query) {
		return true
	}
	if i := strings.IndexByte(stored, ';'); i >= 0 {
		return strings.EqualFold(stored[:i], query)
	}
	return false
}

// List returns the entries of the directory at path
// ("" or "/" for the root).
func (iso *ISO) List(path string) ([]DirEntry, error) {
	e, err := iso.lookup(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !e.IsDir {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %q is not a directory", path)
	}
	return iso.listDir(e)
}

// ReadFile returns the full contents of the file at
// path.
func (iso *ISO) ReadFile(path string) ([]byte, error) {
	e, err := iso.lookup(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if e.IsDir {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: %q is a directory", path)
	}
	return iso.readExtent(e)
}

// Walk visits every file and directory under the
// root, calling fn with each path (directories end
// without a trailing slash; the root itself is not
// visited).
func (iso *ISO) Walk(fn func(path string, e DirEntry) error) error {
	return iso.walkDir("", iso.root, fn)
}

func (iso *ISO) walkDir(prefix string, dir DirEntry, fn func(string, DirEntry) error) error {
	entries, err := iso.listDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		p := e.Name
		if prefix != "" {
			p = prefix + "/" + e.Name
		}
		if err := fn(p, e); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if e.IsDir {
			if err := iso.walkDir(p, e, fn); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/cd/iso_test.go ====================

package cd

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// dirRecord builds one synthetic ISO9660 directory
// record (little-endian fields only; the reader reads
// the little-endian half, like the real parser path).
func makeDirRecord(extent, length uint32, isDir bool, name []byte) []byte {
	recLen := 33 + len(name)
	if recLen%2 == 1 {
		recLen++
	}
	b := make([]byte, recLen)
	b[0] = byte(recLen)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[2:], extent)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[10:], length)
	if isDir {
		b[25] = 2
	}
	b[32] = byte(len(name))
	copy(b[33:], name)
	return b
}

func joinRecords(recs ...[]byte) []byte {
	var out []byte
	for _, r := range recs {
		out = append(out, r...)
	}
	return out
}

// buildSyntheticISO writes a 24-sector ISO with a
// root directory holding HELLO.TXT;1 and a SUB
// directory holding INNER.BIN;1, and returns its
// path.
func buildSyntheticISO(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	const (
		pvdSec   = 16
		rootSec  = 20
		helloSec = 21
		subSec   = 22
		innerSec = 23
	)
	sectors := make([][]byte, 24)
	for i := range sectors {
		sectors[i] = make([]byte, 2048)
	}
	sectors[helloSec] = append([]byte("HELLO"), make([]byte, 2048-5)...)
	sectors[innerSec][0] = 0xDE
	sectors[innerSec][1] = 0xAD
	sectors[innerSec][2] = 0xBE
	sectors[innerSec][3] = 0xEF

	rootDir := joinRecords(
		makeDirRecord(rootSec, 2048, true, []byte{0}),
		makeDirRecord(rootSec, 2048, true, []byte{1}),
		makeDirRecord(helloSec, 5, false, []byte("HELLO.TXT;1")),
		makeDirRecord(subSec, 2048, true, []byte("SUB")),
	)
	copy(sectors[rootSec], rootDir)
	subDir := joinRecords(
		makeDirRecord(subSec, 2048, true, []byte{0}),
		makeDirRecord(rootSec, 2048, true, []byte{1}),
		makeDirRecord(innerSec, 4, false, []byte("INNER.BIN;1")),
	)
	copy(sectors[subSec], subDir)

	pvd := sectors[pvdSec]
	pvd[0] = 1
	copy(pvd[1:6], "CD001")
	pvd[6] = 1
	copy(pvd[40:72], "PS1TEST")
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(pvd[128:], 2048)
	copy(pvd[156:], makeDirRecord(rootSec, 2048, true, []byte{0}))

	var flat []byte
	for _, s := range sectors {
		flat = append(flat, s...)
	}
	p := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "synthetic.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, flat, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return p
}

func TestISO9660WalkAndRead(t *testing.T) {
	im, err := Open(buildSyntheticISO(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()
	iso, err := OpenISO(im)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenISO: %v", err)
	}
	if iso.VolumeID() != "PS1TEST" {
		t.Errorf("VolumeID = %q, want PS1TEST", iso.VolumeID())
	}
	entries, err := iso.List("")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("List root: %v", err)
	}
	if len(entries) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("root entries = %d, want 2 (%v)", len(entries), entries)
	}
	hello, err := iso.ReadFile("HELLO.TXT") // no ;1 suffix in the query
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadFile HELLO.TXT: %v", err)
	}
	if string(hello) != "HELLO" {
		t.Errorf("HELLO.TXT = %q, want HELLO", hello)
	}
	inner, err := iso.ReadFile("SUB/INNER.BIN;1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadFile SUB/INNER.BIN;1: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(inner, []byte{0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF}) {
		t.Errorf("INNER.BIN = % X, want DE AD BE EF", inner)
	}
	var walked []string
	err = iso.Walk(func(path string, e DirEntry) error {
		walked = append(walked, path)
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Walk: %v", err)
	}
	want := []string{"HELLO.TXT;1", "SUB", "SUB/INNER.BIN;1"}
	if len(walked) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("walked = %v, want %v", walked, want)
	}
	for i := range want {
		if walked[i] != want[i] {
			t.Errorf("walked[%d] = %q, want %q", i, walked[i], want[i])
		}
	}
	if _, err := iso.ReadFile("SUB"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadFile on a directory succeeded, want error")
	}
	if _, err := iso.ReadFile("NOPE.TXT"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadFile on a missing path succeeded, want error")
	}
}

func TestISORejectsNonISO(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	p := filepath.Join(dir, "blank.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, make([]byte, 2048*20), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	im, err := Open(p)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open: %v", err)
	}
	defer im.Close()
	if _, err := OpenISO(im); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("OpenISO on a blank image succeeded, want error")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/cd/testcmd.go ====================

package cd

// Test command (19h) sub-functions and the GetQ
// command (1Dh), per the psx-spx CD-ROM test
// commands and status commands chapters.
//
// This controller reports itself as the published
// version 95h,07h,24h,C1h (24 Jul 1995, vC1), so:
// sub-functions 06h..08h (early-only) are supported,
// 22h..25h (vC1 and up) are supported, and 51h
// (vC2 and up) answers the documented not-available
// error, INT5 with code 10h.

// cmdTest dispatches command 19h on its first
// parameter byte.
func (c *Controller) cmdTest(params []byte) {
	if len(params) < 1 {
		c.errorResp(0x20)
		return
	}
	sub, extra := params[0], params[1:]
	stat := c.statusByte()
	switch {
	case sub == 0x05:
		// Stop SCEx reading and get the counters.
		c.ackResp(c.scexTotal, c.scexSuccess)
	case sub <= 0x04 || (sub >= 0x10 && sub <= 0x1A):
		// Force motor on/off and lens mechanics:
		// all answer INT3(stat).
		switch sub {
		case 0x03:
			c.motorOn = false
		case 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x10, 0x17:
			c.motorOn = true
		}
		if sub == 0x04 {
			// Start SCEx reading, counters reset:
			// a licensed data disc model reads one
			// total, one success.
			c.scexTotal, c.scexSuccess = 0, 0
			for _, t := range c.tracks() {
				if t.Mode == TrackData {
					c.scexTotal, c.scexSuccess = 1, 1
				}
			}
		}
		c.ackResp(stat)
	case sub >= 0x06 && sub <= 0x08:
		// Early-PSX balance/gain adjust: returns the
		// old RAM value, modeled as 0.
		c.ackResp(0)
	case sub == 0x20:
		// CDROM BIOS date/version (BCD year, month,
		// day, version). The published vC1 value for
		// LATE-PU-8, 24 Jul 1995.
		c.ackResp(0x95, 0x07, 0x24, 0xC1)
	case sub == 0x21:
		var f uint8
		if c.curLBA == 0 {
			f |= 0x01 // head at POS0
		}
		if c.disc == nil {
			f |= 0x02 // door open
		}
		c.ackResp(f)
	case sub == 0x22:
		// Region ID string; this controller is the
		// North America (U/C) variant, matching the
		// SCEA string its GetID returns.
		c.ackResp([]byte("for U/C")...)
	case sub == 0x23:
		// Chip ID, servo amplifier. The doc lists
		// one string per board generation; this
		// vC1-era choice is CXD1817Q.
		c.ackResp([]byte("CXD1817Q")...)
	case sub == 0x24:
		// Chip ID, signal processor: CXD2510Q.
		c.ackResp([]byte("CXD2510Q")...)
	case sub == 0x25:
		// Chip ID, decoder/FIFO: CXD1815Q.
		c.ackResp([]byte("CXD1815Q")...)
	case sub == 0x50:
		// Send a CX command to the servo/signal
		// hardware; needs at least one byte.
		if len(extra) < 1 {
			c.errorResp(0x20)
			return
		}
		c.ackResp(stat)
	case sub == 0x60:
		// HC05 SUB-CPU RAM read, modeled as zeros.
		if len(extra) < 2 {
			c.errorResp(0x20)
			return
		}
		c.ackResp(0)
	case sub == 0x71:
		// Decoder read one register, modeled as 0.
		if len(extra) < 1 {
			c.errorResp(0x20)
			return
		}
		c.ackResp(0)
	case sub == 0x72:
		if len(extra) < 2 {
			c.errorResp(0x20)
			return
		}
		c.ackResp(stat)
	case sub == 0x73:
		if len(extra) < 2 {
			c.errorResp(0x20)
			return
		}
		n := int(extra[1])
		if n > 12 {
			n = 12
		}
		c.ackResp(make([]byte, n)...)
	case sub == 0x74:
		if len(extra) < 2 {
			c.errorResp(0x20)
			return
		}
		c.ackResp(stat)
	case sub == 0x75:
		// Decoder host transfer info: remain/addr,
		// modeled as zeros.
		c.ackResp(0, 0, 0, 0)
	case sub == 0x76:
		if len(extra) < 4 {
			c.errorResp(0x20)
			return
		}
		c.ackResp(stat)
	default:
		// Documented not-available answer. For the
		// ranges 06h..0Fh, 1Bh..1Fh and 26h..2Fh a
		// nonzero parameter count changes the code
		// from 10h to 20h; the 30h..4Fh prototype
		// range always answers 10h.
		code := uint8(0x10)
		inParamRange := (sub >= 0x06 && sub <= 0x0F) ||
			(sub >= 0x1B && sub <= 0x1F) ||
			(sub >= 0x26 && sub <= 0x2F)
		if inParamRange && len(extra) > 0 {
			code = 0x20
		}
		c.errorResp(code)
	}
}

// cmdGetQ implements GetQ. With no parameters it
// enqueues the subchannel Q block for the CURRENT
// position (the task's GetQ form). With the doc's
// adr,point parameters (ADR=1) it enqueues the
// lead-in TOC block for that point. Either way the
// first response is INT3(stat) and the second,
// delivered after one sector period, is INT2 with
// the 10 data bytes, the 16-bit CRC (big-endian,
// over the 10 data bytes), and the peak LSB byte
// the doc describes (modeled as 0 in lead-in and
// at this position model).
func (c *Controller) cmdGetQ(params []byte) {
	if len(params) == 1 {
		c.errorResp(0x20)
		return
	}
	var data []byte
	if len(params) >= 2 {
		if params[0] != 1 {
			c.errorResp(0x10)
			return
		}
		d, ok := c.tocSubQ(params[1])
		if !ok {
			c.errorResp(0x10)
			return
		}
		data = d
	} else {
		data = c.positionSubQ()
	}
	crc := subqCRC(data)
	resp := append([]byte(nil), data...)
	resp = append(resp, uint8(crc>>8), uint8(crc), 0)
	c.ackResp(c.statusByte())
	c.schedule(c.now+sectorPeriod1x, cdEvent{kind: evSecondResp, resp: resp, irq: irqComplete})
}

// positionSubQ builds the ADR=1 position block:
// control/ADR, track, index, track-relative MSF,
// reserved, absolute MSF (10 bytes, all BCD).
func (c *Controller) positionSubQ() []byte {
	pos := c.headPos()
	ctrl := uint8(0x01) // ADR=1, audio
	trackNum, index := 0xAA, 1
	rel := pos
	if tr, ok := c.trackAt(pos); ok {
		trackNum = tr.Number
		if tr.Mode == TrackData {
			ctrl |= 0x40 // data bit in the control field
		}
		if pos >= tr.DataLBA {
			rel = pos - tr.DataLBA
		} else {
			rel = pos - tr.StartLBA
			index = 0
		}
	}
	rm, rs, rf := SectorToMSF(rel)
	am, as, af := LBAToMSF(pos)
	return []byte{
		ctrl, toBCD(trackNum), toBCD(index),
		toBCD(rm), toBCD(rs), toBCD(rf),
		0,
		toBCD(am), toBCD(as), toBCD(af),
	}
}

// tocSubQ builds the ADR=1 lead-in block for a
// point: control/ADR, track 00h, point, lead-in
// MSF (modeled 00:00:00), reserved, then the
// point's absolute MSF (or the A0h/A1h payloads).
func (c *Controller) tocSubQ(point uint8) ([]byte, bool) {
	ctrl := uint8(0x01)
	if len(c.tracks()) > 0 && c.tracks()[0].Mode == TrackData {
		ctrl |= 0x40
	}
	data := []byte{ctrl, 0, point, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
	switch {
	case point == 0xA0:
		trs := c.tracks()
		if len(trs) == 0 {
			return nil, false
		}
		data[7] = toBCD(trs[0].Number)
		data[8] = 0x20 // disc type: CD-ROM XA, as in GetID
	case point == 0xA1:
		trs := c.tracks()
		if len(trs) == 0 {
			return nil, false
		}
		data[7] = toBCD(trs[len(trs)-1].Number)
	case point == 0xA2:
		m, s, f := LBAToMSF(c.totalSectors())
		data[7], data[8], data[9] = toBCD(m), toBCD(s), toBCD(f)
	default:
		if !bcdValid(point) {
			return nil, false
		}
		n := bcdVal(point)
		found := false
		for _, t := range c.tracks() {
			if t.Number == n {
				m, s, f := LBAToMSF(t.DataLBA)
				data[7], data[8], data[9] = toBCD(m), toBCD(s), toBCD(f)
				found = true
			}
		}
		if !found {
			return nil, false
		}
	}
	return data, true
}

// subqCRC computes the subchannel Q CRC per the
// psx-spx adjust_crc_16_ccitt routine: initial
// value zero, run over the data bytes, the result
// inverted and stored big-endian. That routine is
// the CRC-16-CCITT form (polynomial x^16+x^12+x^5+1)
// used for subchannel Q.
func subqCRC(data []byte) uint16 {
	var lsb, msb uint8
	for _, b := range data {
		x := b ^ msb
		x ^= x >> 4
		msb = lsb ^ (x >> 3) ^ (x << 4)
		lsb = x ^ (x << 5)
	}
	return uint16(msb^0xFF)<<8 | uint16(lsb^0xFF)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/chips/gte/exec.go ====================

package gte

import "fmt"

// This file implements the GTE command math from the
// psx-spx "Geometry Transformation Engine (GTE)"
// chapter. Section names in comments refer to that
// chapter.
//
// Command word fields (psx-psx, "GTE Command
// Encoding"): the real opcode is bits 0..5, the sf
// (shift fraction) bit is bit 19, the lm (IR saturation
// mode) bit is bit 10, and the MVMVA selects are mx in
// bits 17..18, v in bits 15..16 and cv in bits 13..14.
// Bits 20..24 hold a fake opcode number that the
// hardware ignores.
//
// Accumulator model (psx-spx, "GTE Saturation"):
// MAC1..MAC3 are 44-bit signed accumulators and are
// not saturated; a result outside the 44-bit signed
// range sets the per-MAC positive or negative overflow
// bits in FLAG (bits 30..28 and 27..25) and wraps.
// MAC0 is a 32-bit accumulator with its own overflow
// bits (16 and 15). IR1..IR3 are saturated from the
// MACs, to -8000h..+7FFFh with lm=0 or 0..+7FFFh with
// lm=1, setting FLAG bits 24..22.

// FLAG bit numbers (psx-spx, "GTE Saturation").
const (
	flagMAC1Pos = 30
	flagMAC2Pos = 29
	flagMAC3Pos = 28
	flagMAC1Neg = 27
	flagMAC2Neg = 26
	flagMAC3Neg = 25
	flagIR1Sat  = 24
	flagIR2Sat  = 23
	flagIR3Sat  = 22
	flagColR    = 21
	flagColG    = 20
	flagColB    = 19
	flagZSat    = 18
	flagDivOvf  = 17
	flagMAC0Pos = 16
	flagMAC0Neg = 15
	flagSXSat   = 14
	flagSYSat   = 13
	flagIR0Sat  = 12
)

const (
	mac44Max = int64(0x7FFFFFFFFFF)  // 2^43 - 1
	mac44Min = -int64(0x80000000000) // -2^43
)

// unrTable is the reciprocal table of the psx-spx
// "GTE Division Inaccuracy" section, generated with
// the rule given there: unr_table[i] =
// max(0, (40000h/(i+100h)+1)/2-101h) for i in
// 000h..100h, with the division carried out before
// truncation (the entry for i=001h is FDh, which pins
// down that rounding).
var unrTable = func() [0x101]int64 {
	var t [0x101]int64
	for i := 0; i <= 0x100; i++ {
		d := int64(i + 0x100)
		v := (0x40000+d)/(2*d) - 0x101
		if v < 0 {
			v = 0
		}
		t[i] = v
	}
	return t
}()

// engine carries the per-command execution state: the
// FLAG bits accumulated by the running command and the
// wide accumulator values (the register file itself
// only stores their low 32 bits).
type engine struct {
	g    *GTE
	flag uint32
	sf   bool
	lm   bool
	mac  [3]int64 // 44-bit signed, wrapped
	mac0 int64    // 32-bit signed, wrapped
}

func (e *engine) sfShift() uint {
	if e.sf {
		return 12
	}
	return 0
}

func (e *engine) lmMin() int64 {
	if e.lm {
		return 0
	}
	return -0x8000
}

func s16(v uint32) int64 { return int64(int16(uint16(v))) }

func s32(v uint32) int64 { return int64(int32(v)) }

// setMAC stores v in a 44-bit MAC accumulator, setting
// the documented overflow bits and wrapping the value
// to 44 bits (psx-spx, "GTE Saturation").
func (e *engine) setMAC(i int, v int64) {
	if v > mac44Max {
		e.flag |= 1 << uint(flagMAC1Pos-i)
	} else if v < mac44Min {
		e.flag |= 1 << uint(flagMAC1Neg-i)
	}
	v &= 0xFFFFFFFFFFF
	if v > mac44Max {
		v -= 0x100000000000
	}
	e.mac[i] = v
}

// checkMACOverflow sets the overflow bits for v without
// storing it (used by the bugged MVMVA far-color path,
// whose FLAG bits behave as if the full operation had
// been executed).
func (e *engine) checkMACOverflow(i int, v int64) {
	if v > mac44Max {
		e.flag |= 1 << uint(flagMAC1Pos-i)
	} else if v < mac44Min {
		e.flag |= 1 << uint(flagMAC1Neg-i)
	}
}

// setMAC0 stores v in the 32-bit MAC0 accumulator,
// setting FLAG bits 16 (positive) and 15 (negative)
// on overflow (psx-spx, "GTE Saturation").
func (e *engine) setMAC0(v int64) {
	if v > 0x7FFFFFFF {
		e.flag |= 1 << flagMAC0Pos
	} else if v < -0x80000000 {
		e.flag |= 1 << flagMAC0Neg
	}
	e.mac0 = int64(int32(v))
}

// satIRValue clamps v to the IR range selected by lm,
// setting the given FLAG bit if clamping occurred.
func (e *engine) satIRValue(v int64, lm bool, bit uint) int64 {
	min := int64(-0x8000)
	if lm {
		min = 0
	}
	if v > 0x7FFF {
		e.flag |= 1 << bit
		return 0x7FFF
	}
	if v < min {
		e.flag |= 1 << bit
		return min
	}
	return v
}

// storeIR writes an already saturated value to an IR
// register (sign-extended 16-bit storage).
func (e *engine) storeIR(i int, v int64) {
	e.g.data[9+i] = uint32(int32(int16(v)))
}

// satIR saturates a MAC value into IR register i using
// the command's lm bit.
func (e *engine) satIR(i int) {
	e.storeIR(i, e.satIRValue(e.mac[i], e.lm, uint(flagIR1Sat-i)))
}

// irFromMAC copies all three MACs into IR1..IR3 with
// saturation.
func (e *engine) irFromMAC() {
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		e.satIR(i)
	}
}

// ir reads IR register i (0..2) as a signed value.
func (e *engine) ir(i int) int64 { return s16(e.g.data[9+i]) }

// ir0 reads IR0 as a signed value.
func (e *engine) ir0() int64 { return s16(e.g.data[8]) }

func (e *engine) irVec() [3]int64 { return [3]int64{e.ir(0), e.ir(1), e.ir(2)} }

// vec reads input vector n (0..2, the V0..V2
// registers) as signed components.
func (e *engine) vec(n int) [3]int64 {
	d := e.g.data
	return [3]int64{
		s16(d[2*n]),
		s16(d[2*n] >> 16),
		s16(d[2*n+1]),
	}
}

// matrix reads one of the packed 3x3 control-register
// matrices. base is the first control register: 0 for
// the rotation matrix, 8 for the light matrix, 16 for
// the light color matrix (psx-spx, "Matrix Registers":
// the first four registers pack two elements each and
// the fifth holds the last element in its low half).
func (e *engine) matrix(base int) [3][3]int64 {
	c := e.g.control
	return [3][3]int64{
		{s16(c[base]), s16(c[base] >> 16), s16(c[base+1])},
		{s16(c[base+1] >> 16), s16(c[base+2]), s16(c[base+2] >> 16)},
		{s16(c[base+3]), s16(c[base+3] >> 16), s16(c[base+4])},
	}
}

func (e *engine) trVec() [3]int64 {
	c := e.g.control
	return [3]int64{s32(c[5]), s32(c[6]), s32(c[7])}
}

func (e *engine) bkVec() [3]int64 {
	c := e.g.control
	return [3]int64{s32(c[13]), s32(c[14]), s32(c[15])}
}

func (e *engine) fcVec() [3]int64 {
	c := e.g.control
	return [3]int64{s32(c[21]), s32(c[22]), s32(c[23])}
}

// matMul computes MAC = (trans*1000h + mat*vec) SAR
// (sf*12), or MAC = (mat*vec) SAR (sf*12) when trans
// is nil. This is the shared multiply step of MVMVA,
// RTPS/RTPT and the color commands (psx-spx, "Details
// on (LLM*V0) SAR (sf*12) and (BK*1000h + LCM*IR) SAR
// (sf*12)").
func (e *engine) matMul(mat [3][3]int64, vec [3]int64, trans *[3]int64) {
	sh := e.sfShift()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		sum := mat[i][0]*vec[0] + mat[i][1]*vec[1] + mat[i][2]*vec[2]
		if trans != nil {
			sum += trans[i] << 12
		}
		e.setMAC(i, sum>>sh)
	}
}

func (e *engine) rgbc() (r, g, b, code int64) {
	v := e.g.data[6]
	return int64(v & 0xFF), int64((v >> 8) & 0xFF),
		int64((v >> 16) & 0xFF), int64((v >> 24) & 0xFF)
}

// pushColor writes the MACs to the top of the color
// FIFO: each component divided by 16 and saturated to
// 00h..FFh (FLAG bits 21..19 on saturation), with the
// CODE byte taken from RGBC, and the older FIFO
// entries moved one stage down (psx-spx, "Notes" in
// the color command section).
func (e *engine) pushColor() {
	bits := [3]uint{flagColR, flagColG, flagColB}
	var by [3]uint32
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		v := e.mac[i] >> 4
		if v < 0 {
			v = 0
			e.flag |= 1 << bits[i]
		} else if v > 0xFF {
			v = 0xFF
			e.flag |= 1 << bits[i]
		}
		by[i] = uint32(v)
	}
	_, _, _, code := e.rgbc()
	d := &e.g.data
	d[20] = d[21]
	d[21] = d[22]
	d[22] = uint32(code)<<24 | by[2]<<16 | by[1]<<8 | by[0]
}

// finishColor is the shared tail of the color
// commands: push the color FIFO, then copy the MACs
// into IR1..IR3 with saturation.
func (e *engine) finishColor() {
	e.pushColor()
	e.irFromMAC()
}

// multiplyRGBC is the "[MAC1,MAC2,MAC3] =
// [R*IR1,G*IR2,B*IR3] SHL 4" step of the NCDx, NCCx,
// CC, CDP and DCPL commands.
func (e *engine) multiplyRGBC() {
	r, g, b, _ := e.rgbc()
	bytes := [3]int64{r, g, b}
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		e.setMAC(i, (bytes[i]*e.ir(i))<<4)
	}
}

// depthCue is the shared "MAC+(FC-MAC)*IR0" step
// (psx-spx, "Details on MAC+(FC-MAC)*IR0"): the
// difference (FC SHL 12)-MAC is shifted by (sf*12),
// saturated into IR1..IR3 as if lm=0, multiplied by
// IR0 and added back to the MACs.
func (e *engine) depthCue() {
	fc := e.fcVec()
	ir0 := e.ir0()
	sh := e.sfShift()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		diff := e.satIRValue((fc[i]<<12-e.mac[i])>>sh, false, uint(flagIR1Sat-i))
		e.storeIR(i, diff)
		e.setMAC(i, diff*ir0+e.mac[i])
	}
}

// finalColorShift is the closing "[MAC1,MAC2,MAC3] =
// [MAC1,MAC2,MAC3] SAR (sf*12)" step of the NCDx,
// NCCx, CC and CDP family and of DPCS, DPCT, DCPL and
// INTPL.
func (e *engine) finalColorShift() {
	sh := e.sfShift()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		e.setMAC(i, e.mac[i]>>sh)
	}
}

// lightingStep is the "(LLM*Vn) SAR (sf*12)" step of
// the normal color commands.
func (e *engine) lightingStep(v [3]int64) {
	e.matMul(e.matrix(8), v, nil)
	e.irFromMAC()
}

// colorStep is the "(BK*1000h + LCM*IR) SAR (sf*12)"
// step of the normal color and color color commands.
func (e *engine) colorStep() {
	bk := e.bkVec()
	e.matMul(e.matrix(16), e.irVec(), &bk)
	e.irFromMAC()
}

// divide runs the Unsigned Newton-Raphson division of
// the psx-spx "GTE Division Inaccuracy" section: it
// approximates (H*20000h/SZ3+1)/2, saturated to
// 1FFFFh. When H >= SZ3*2 (the vertex is at or inside
// the near clip plane) it returns 1FFFFh and sets the
// divide overflow FLAG bit 17; the plain min() clamp
// at the end does not set the flag.
func (e *engine) divide(sz uint32) int64 {
	h := uint32(e.g.control[26] & 0xFFFF)
	if h >= sz*2 {
		e.flag |= 1 << flagDivOvf
		return 0x1FFFF
	}
	// sz is nonzero here: sz == 0 always takes the
	// overflow branch above.
	z := uint(0)
	for i := 15; i >= 0; i-- {
		if sz&(1<<uint(i)) != 0 {
			break
		}
		z++
	}
	n := int64(h) << z
	d := int64(sz) << z // 8000h..FFFFh
	u := unrTable[(d-0x7FC0)>>7] + 0x101
	d = (0x2000080 - d*u) >> 8
	d = (0x80 + d*u) >> 8
	n = (n*d + 0x8000) >> 16
	if n > 0x1FFFF {
		n = 0x1FFFF
	}
	return n
}

// clampScreen saturates a screen coordinate to
// -0400h..+03FFh, setting the given FLAG bit.
func (e *engine) clampScreen(v int64, bit uint) int64 {
	if v > 0x3FF {
		e.flag |= 1 << bit
		return 0x3FF
	}
	if v < -0x400 {
		e.flag |= 1 << bit
		return -0x400
	}
	return v
}

// rtpsVertex is one RTPS pass over a single vertex
// (psx-spx, "GTE Coordinate Calculation Commands"):
// rotate and translate, push the SZ FIFO, divide,
// push the SXY FIFO, and compute the depth cue value
// in IR0.
func (e *engine) rtpsVertex(v [3]int64) {
	tr := e.trVec()
	e.matMul(e.matrix(0), v, &tr)
	e.satIR(0)
	e.satIR(1)
	// IR3 saturation quirk (psx-spx, "GTE Saturation"
	// and the RTPS note): the FLAG.22 check always
	// acts as if lm=0, and with sf=0 it checks
	// MAC3 SAR 12, while the stored IR3 respects the
	// actual lm bit.
	chk := e.mac[2]
	if !e.sf {
		chk >>= 12
	}
	if chk > 0x7FFF || chk < -0x8000 {
		e.flag |= 1 << flagIR3Sat
	}
	e.storeIR(2, clampPlain(e.mac[2], e.lmMin(), 0x7FFF))
	// SZ3 = MAC3 SAR ((1-sf)*12), saturated to
	// 0000h..FFFFh (FLAG bit 18).
	szv := e.mac[2]
	if !e.sf {
		szv >>= 12
	}
	if szv < 0 {
		szv = 0
		e.flag |= 1 << flagZSat
	} else if szv > 0xFFFF {
		szv = 0xFFFF
		e.flag |= 1 << flagZSat
	}
	d := &e.g.data
	d[16] = d[17]
	d[17] = d[18]
	d[18] = d[19]
	d[19] = uint32(szv)
	n := e.divide(uint32(szv))
	ofx := s32(e.g.control[24])
	ofy := s32(e.g.control[25])
	e.setMAC0(n*e.ir(0) + ofx)
	sx := e.clampScreen(e.mac0>>16, flagSXSat)
	e.setMAC0(n*e.ir(1) + ofy)
	sy := e.clampScreen(e.mac0>>16, flagSYSat)
	d[12] = d[13]
	d[13] = d[14]
	d[14] = uint32(uint16(int16(sy)))<<16 | uint32(uint16(int16(sx)))
	// Depth cueing: IR0 = (n*DQA + DQB) / 1000h,
	// saturated to 0..+1000h (FLAG bit 12).
	e.setMAC0(n*s16(e.g.control[27]) + s32(e.g.control[28]))
	ir0 := e.mac0 >> 12
	if ir0 < 0 {
		ir0 = 0
		e.flag |= 1 << flagIR0Sat
	} else if ir0 > 0x1000 {
		ir0 = 0x1000
		e.flag |= 1 << flagIR0Sat
	}
	d[8] = uint32(int32(int16(ir0)))
}

func clampPlain(v, min, max int64) int64 {
	if v > max {
		return max
	}
	if v < min {
		return min
	}
	return v
}

// Execute dispatches one COP2 command word. It returns
// nil for every documented opcode and
// ErrUnknownCommand otherwise. FLAG is reset at the
// start of the command and the accumulated bits are
// stored to control register 31 at the end (psx-spx,
// "GTE Saturation").
func (g *GTE) Execute(cmd uint32) error {
	opcode := cmd & 0x3F
	if _, ok := commandByOpcode[opcode]; !ok {
		g.unsupported++
		return fmt.Errorf("%w: 0x%02X", ErrUnknownCommand, opcode)
	}
	g.lastCommand = cmd
	e := &engine{
		g:    g,
		sf:   cmd>>19&1 == 1,
		lm:   cmd>>10&1 == 1,
		mac0: s32(g.data[24]),
	}
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		e.mac[i] = s32(g.data[25+i])
	}
	e.run(opcode, cmd)
	g.data[24] = uint32(int32(e.mac0))
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		g.data[25+i] = uint32(int32(e.mac[i]))
	}
	g.control[31] = e.flag & 0x7FFFF000
	return nil
}

// Command is the r3000a.Cop2 entry point. It executes
// the command and returns the documented cycle count
// from the psx-spx opcode summary table (1 for an
// undocumented opcode, which the CPU has no error
// channel to report).
func (g *GTE) Command(cmd uint32) int {
	cycles := CommandCycles(cmd & 0x3F)
	_ = g.Execute(cmd)
	if cycles == 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return cycles
}

// run executes one documented opcode with the engine
// state prepared by Execute.
func (e *engine) run(opcode uint32, cmd uint32) {
	switch opcode {
	case 0x01: // RTPS
		e.rtpsVertex(e.vec(0))
	case 0x30: // RTPT
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			e.rtpsVertex(e.vec(i))
		}
	case 0x06: // NCLIP
		e.nclip()
	case 0x2D: // AVSZ3
		e.avsz(3)
	case 0x2E: // AVSZ4
		e.avsz(4)
	case 0x12: // MVMVA
		e.mvmva(cmd)
	case 0x28: // SQR
		e.sqr()
	case 0x0C: // OP
		e.op()
	case 0x1E: // NCS
		e.lightingStep(e.vec(0))
		e.colorStep()
		e.finishColor()
	case 0x20: // NCT
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			e.lightingStep(e.vec(i))
			e.colorStep()
			e.finishColor()
		}
	case 0x1B: // NCCS
		e.nccsBody(e.vec(0))
	case 0x3F: // NCCT
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			e.nccsBody(e.vec(i))
		}
	case 0x13: // NCDS
		e.ncdsBody(e.vec(0))
	case 0x16: // NCDT
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			e.ncdsBody(e.vec(i))
		}
	case 0x1C: // CC
		e.colorStep()
		e.multiplyRGBC()
		e.finalColorShift()
		e.finishColor()
	case 0x14: // CDP
		e.colorStep()
		e.multiplyRGBC()
		e.depthCue()
		e.finalColorShift()
		e.finishColor()
	case 0x29: // DCPL
		e.multiplyRGBC()
		e.depthCue()
		e.finalColorShift()
		e.finishColor()
	case 0x10: // DPCS
		r, g, b, _ := e.rgbc()
		e.setMAC(0, r<<16)
		e.setMAC(1, g<<16)
		e.setMAC(2, b<<16)
		e.depthCue()
		e.finalColorShift()
		e.finishColor()
	case 0x2A: // DPCT
		e.dpct()
	case 0x11: // INTPL
		ir := e.irVec()
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			e.setMAC(i, ir[i]<<12)
		}
		e.depthCue()
		e.finalColorShift()
		e.finishColor()
	case 0x3D: // GPF
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			e.setMAC(i, 0)
		}
		e.gpFormula()
		e.finishColor()
	case 0x3E: // GPL
		sh := e.sfShift()
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			e.setMAC(i, e.mac[i]<<sh)
		}
		e.gpFormula()
		e.finishColor()
	}
}

// nccsBody is one NCCS pass: lighting, color matrix,
// then the RGBC multiply and final shift.
func (e *engine) nccsBody(v [3]int64) {
	e.lightingStep(v)
	e.colorStep()
	e.multiplyRGBC()
	e.finalColorShift()
	e.finishColor()
}

// ncdsBody is one NCDS pass: NCCS plus the depth cue
// step before the final shift.
func (e *engine) ncdsBody(v [3]int64) {
	e.lightingStep(v)
	e.colorStep()
	e.multiplyRGBC()
	e.depthCue()
	e.finalColorShift()
	e.finishColor()
}

// dpct runs DPCS three times, reading the color bytes
// from RGB0 (the bottom of the color FIFO) on each
// pass instead of from RGBC; the CODE byte still comes
// from RGBC (psx-spx, DPCT note). Each pass pushes a
// new FIFO entry, so the three passes process the
// three original FIFO entries in order.
func (e *engine) dpct() {
	for n := 0; n < 3; n++ {
		v := e.g.data[20]
		e.setMAC(0, int64(v&0xFF)<<16)
		e.setMAC(1, int64((v>>8)&0xFF)<<16)
		e.setMAC(2, int64((v>>16)&0xFF)<<16)
		e.depthCue()
		e.finalColorShift()
		e.finishColor()
	}
}

// gpFormula is the shared "(([IR1,IR2,IR3] * IR0) +
// [MAC1,MAC2,MAC3]) SAR (sf*12)" step of GPF and GPL.
func (e *engine) gpFormula() {
	ir := e.irVec()
	ir0 := e.ir0()
	sh := e.sfShift()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		e.setMAC(i, (ir[i]*ir0+e.mac[i])>>sh)
	}
}

// nclip computes MAC0 = SX0*SY1 + SX1*SY2 + SX2*SY0 -
// SX0*SY2 - SX1*SY0 - SX2*SY1 from the SXY FIFO; the
// sign of the result gives the polygon winding
// (psx-spx, "NCLIP").
func (e *engine) nclip() {
	d := e.g.data
	sx := [3]int64{s16(d[12]), s16(d[13]), s16(d[14])}
	sy := [3]int64{s16(d[12] >> 16), s16(d[13] >> 16), s16(d[14] >> 16)}
	e.setMAC0(sx[0]*sy[1] + sx[1]*sy[2] + sx[2]*sy[0] -
		sx[0]*sy[2] - sx[1]*sy[0] - sx[2]*sy[1])
}

// avsz computes MAC0 = ZSFn * (sum of the newest n SZ
// FIFO entries) and OTZ = MAC0 / 1000h, saturated to
// 0000h..FFFFh with FLAG bit 18 (psx-spx, "AVSZ3" and
// "AVSZ4").
func (e *engine) avsz(n int) {
	d := &e.g.data
	var sum int64
	base := 19 - n + 1 // first of the newest n SZ entries
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		sum += int64(d[base+i])
	}
	zsf := s16(e.g.control[29])
	if n == 4 {
		zsf = s16(e.g.control[30])
	}
	e.setMAC0(zsf * sum)
	otz := e.mac0 >> 12
	if otz < 0 {
		otz = 0
		e.flag |= 1 << flagZSat
	} else if otz > 0xFFFF {
		otz = 0xFFFF
		e.flag |= 1 << flagZSat
	}
	d[7] = uint32(otz)
}

// mvmva implements MVMVA(sf,mx,v,cv,lm) (psx-spx,
// "MVMVA"): MAC = (Tx*1000h + Mx*Vx) SAR (sf*12) with
// the matrix, vector and translation vector selected
// by the command word.
//
// Documented quirks: cv=2 selects the far color
// vector, but the hardware drops the first product
// term and the translation, computing only
// (Mx12*Vx2 + Mx13*Vx3) SAR (sf*12), while some FLAG
// bits are adjusted as if the full operation had been
// executed. mx=3 selects a garbage matrix built from
// -R*10h, +R*10h, IR0, RT13 and RT22 (R is the red
// component of RGBC).
func (e *engine) mvmva(cmd uint32) {
	mx := (cmd >> 17) & 3
	vsel := (cmd >> 15) & 3
	cv := (cmd >> 13) & 3
	var mat [3][3]int64
	switch mx {
	case 0:
		mat = e.matrix(0)
	case 1:
		mat = e.matrix(8)
	case 2:
		mat = e.matrix(16)
	case 3:
		rt := e.matrix(0)
		r := int64(e.g.data[6] & 0xFF)
		mat = [3][3]int64{
			{-r * 0x10, r * 0x10, e.ir0()},
			{rt[0][2], rt[0][2], rt[0][2]},
			{rt[1][1], rt[1][1], rt[1][1]},
		}
	}
	var vec [3]int64
	if vsel == 3 {
		vec = e.irVec()
	} else {
		vec = e.vec(int(vsel))
	}
	sh := e.sfShift()
	switch cv {
	case 0:
		tr := e.trVec()
		e.matMul(mat, vec, &tr)
	case 1:
		bk := e.bkVec()
		e.matMul(mat, vec, &bk)
	case 2:
		fc := e.fcVec()
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			full := fc[i]<<12 + mat[i][0]*vec[0] + mat[i][1]*vec[1] + mat[i][2]*vec[2]
			e.checkMACOverflow(i, full>>sh)
			e.setMAC(i, (mat[i][1]*vec[1]+mat[i][2]*vec[2])>>sh)
		}
	case 3:
		e.matMul(mat, vec, nil)
	}
	e.irFromMAC()
}

// sqr implements SQR(sf): MAC = IR*IR SHR (sf*12),
// with IR1..IR3 saturated to a maximum of 7FFFh (the
// result is always positive, so the lm bit has no
// effect) (psx-spx, "SQR").
func (e *engine) sqr() {
	ir := e.irVec()
	sh := e.sfShift()
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		e.setMAC(i, (ir[i]*ir[i])>>sh)
		e.satIR(i)
	}
}

// op implements OP(sf,lm), the cross product of the IR
// vector with the vector formed by the RT11, RT22 and
// RT33 diagonal elements (psx-spx, "OP").
func (e *engine) op() {
	rt := e.matrix(0)
	d1, d2, d3 := rt[0][0], rt[1][1], rt[2][2]
	ir := e.irVec()
	sh := e.sfShift()
	e.setMAC(0, (ir[2]*d2-ir[1]*d3)>>sh)
	e.setMAC(1, (ir[0]*d3-ir[2]*d1)>>sh)
	e.setMAC(2, (ir[1]*d1-ir[0]*d2)>>sh)
	e.irFromMAC()
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/chips/gte/gte.go ====================

// Package gte is the PlayStation geometry engine
// (coprocessor 2) for the go-ps1 core.
//
// The register file (32 data and 32 control registers)
// and the full fixed-point command set are implemented
// from the psx-spx "Geometry Transformation Engine
// (GTE)" chapter: register access side effects (SXY
// FIFO push, IRGB/ORGB conversion, LZCS/LZCR), the
// FLAG saturation and overflow bits, and all commands
// in the documented opcode table, including the
// Unsigned Newton-Raphson division used by RTPS/RTPT.
package gte

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// ErrNotImplemented is retained for API compatibility.
// Execute no longer returns it: every documented
// opcode is implemented.
var ErrNotImplemented = errors.New("gte: command not implemented in this slice")

// ErrUnknownCommand is returned by Execute for a
// command opcode outside the documented table.
var ErrUnknownCommand = errors.New("gte: unknown command opcode")

// Command describes one documented GTE command.
type Command struct {
	Opcode uint32
	Name   string
	Cycles int
}

// Commands is the documented GTE command dispatch
// table (real opcode in the low 6 bits of the COP2
// word) with the per-command cycle counts from the
// psx-spx "GTE Opcode Summary" table.
//
// Note: an earlier draft of this table carried the
// wrong real opcodes for SQR, DPCT and AVSZ3 (it had
// AVSZ3 at 15h, which is AVSZ3's fake opcode, SQR at
// 2Ah and DPCT at 2Dh). The psx-spx real-opcode table
// says SQR=28h, DPCT=2Ah, AVSZ3=2Dh; those are the
// values below.
var Commands = []Command{
	{0x01, "RTPS", 15},
	{0x06, "NCLIP", 8},
	{0x0C, "OP", 6},
	{0x10, "DPCS", 8},
	{0x11, "INTPL", 8},
	{0x12, "MVMVA", 8},
	{0x13, "NCDS", 19},
	{0x14, "CDP", 13},
	{0x2D, "AVSZ3", 5},
	{0x16, "NCDT", 44},
	{0x1B, "NCCS", 17},
	{0x1C, "CC", 11},
	{0x1E, "NCS", 14},
	{0x20, "NCT", 30},
	{0x28, "SQR", 5},
	{0x29, "DCPL", 8},
	{0x2A, "DPCT", 17},
	{0x2E, "AVSZ4", 6},
	{0x30, "RTPT", 23},
	{0x3D, "GPF", 5},
	{0x3E, "GPL", 5},
	{0x3F, "NCCT", 39},
}

var commandByOpcode = func() map[uint32]Command {
	m := make(map[uint32]Command, len(Commands))
	for _, cmd := range Commands {
		m[cmd.Opcode] = cmd
	}
	return m
}()

// CommandName returns the documented mnemonic for a
// GTE command opcode, if it has one.
func CommandName(opcode uint32) (string, bool) {
	cmd, ok := commandByOpcode[opcode&0x3F]
	return cmd.Name, ok
}

// CommandCycles returns the documented cycle count
// for a GTE command opcode from the psx-spx opcode
// summary table, or 0 if the opcode is undocumented.
func CommandCycles(opcode uint32) int {
	if cmd, ok := commandByOpcode[opcode&0x3F]; ok {
		return cmd.Cycles
	}
	return 0
}

// StateSize is the serialized size of the register
// file: 32 data plus 32 control registers.
const StateSize = 64 * 4

// flagErrorMask selects the FLAG bits that are ORed
// into FLAG bit 31 on read: bits 30..23 and 18..13
// (psx-spx, "GTE Saturation": FLAG register layout).
const flagErrorMask = 0x7F800000 | 0x0007E000

// GTE is the coprocessor 2 register file.
type GTE struct {
	data    [32]uint32
	control [32]uint32

	lastCommand uint32
	unsupported int // count of commands refused with ErrUnknownCommand
}

// New returns a GTE in reset state (all registers zero).
func New() *GTE { return &GTE{} }

// Data reads a GTE data register (0-31).
//
// Documented read side effects (psx-spx, "GTE
// Registers"): register 15 (SXYP) reads back SXY2;
// registers 28 (IRGB) and 29 (ORGB) both read as the
// 5:5:5 collapse of IR1, IR2, IR3 (ORGB is a read-only
// mirror of IRGB). All other registers are plain
// storage.
func (g *GTE) Data(reg uint32) uint32 {
	switch reg & 31 {
	case 15: // SXYP: mirror of SXY2
		return g.data[14]
	case 28, 29: // IRGB, ORGB: converted from IR1..IR3
		return g.collapsedRGB()
	}
	return g.data[reg&31]
}

// SetData writes a GTE data register (0-31).
//
// Documented write side effects (psx-spx, "GTE
// Registers"): writing register 15 (SXYP) pushes the
// SXY FIFO (SXY0=SXY1, SXY1=SXY2, SXY2=value); writing
// register 28 (IRGB) expands the 5:5:5 fields into
// IR1, IR2, IR3 (each field multiplied by 80h);
// writing register 29 (ORGB) is ignored (read-only);
// writing register 30 (LZCS) updates register 31
// (LZCR) with the leading sign-bit count. All other
// registers are plain storage.
func (g *GTE) SetData(reg uint32, v uint32) {
	switch reg & 31 {
	case 15: // SXYP: move-on-write FIFO push
		g.data[12] = g.data[13]
		g.data[13] = g.data[14]
		g.data[14] = v
	case 28: // IRGB: expand 5:5:5 into IR1, IR2, IR3
		g.data[9] = (v & 0x1F) << 7
		g.data[10] = ((v >> 5) & 0x1F) << 7
		g.data[11] = ((v >> 10) & 0x1F) << 7
	case 29: // ORGB: read-only, writes ignored
	case 30: // LZCS: recompute LZCR
		g.data[30] = v
		g.data[31] = uint32(leadingSignBits(v))
	default:
		g.data[reg&31] = v
	}
}

// collapsedRGB converts IR1, IR2, IR3 to the 5:5:5
// value read from IRGB and ORGB: each 16-bit component
// divided by 80h and saturated to 00h..1Fh (psx-spx,
// "cop2r29 - ORGB"; no FLAG bits are set by this).
func (g *GTE) collapsedRGB() uint32 {
	var out uint32
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		c := int32(int16(uint16(g.data[9+i]))) / 0x80
		if c < 0 {
			c = 0
		}
		if c > 0x1F {
			c = 0x1F
		}
		out |= uint32(c) << (5 * i)
	}
	return out
}

// leadingSignBits counts the leading bits of v that
// are equal to its sign bit (psx-spx, LZCS/LZCR: the
// leading zero count for positive values, the leading
// one count for negative values, in the range 1..32).
func leadingSignBits(v uint32) int {
	sign := v >> 31
	n := 0
	for i := 31; i >= 0; i-- {
		if (v>>uint(i))&1 != sign {
			break
		}
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// Control reads a GTE control register (0-31).
//
// Register 31 (FLAG) reads with bit 31 set to the OR
// of the documented error bits (bits 30..23 and
// 18..13) and bits 11..0 always zero (psx-spx, "GTE
// Saturation"). All other registers are plain storage.
func (g *GTE) Control(reg uint32) uint32 {
	if reg&31 == 31 {
		v := g.control[31] & 0x7FFFF000
		if g.control[31]&flagErrorMask != 0 {
			v |= 0x80000000
		}
		return v
	}
	return g.control[reg&31]
}

// SetControl writes a GTE control register (0-31).
// Writing FLAG (register 31) stores the written bits;
// the next command overwrites them (psx-spx: all FLAG
// bits are automatically reset at the begin of a new
// GTE command).
func (g *GTE) SetControl(reg uint32, v uint32) { g.control[reg&31] = v }

// LastCommand returns the most recent documented
// command word passed to Execute, or 0 if none.
func (g *GTE) LastCommand() uint32 { return g.lastCommand }

// Unsupported returns how many commands Execute has
// refused as unknown opcodes.
func (g *GTE) Unsupported() int { return g.unsupported }

// Serialize returns the register file as a fixed-size
// block.
func (g *GTE) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	off := 0
	for _, v := range g.data {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], v)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, v := range g.control {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], v)
		off += 4
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a Serialize block.
func (g *GTE) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != StateSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("gte: state size %d, want %d", len(in), StateSize)
	}
	off := 0
	for i := range g.data {
		g.data[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
	}
	for i := range g.control {
		g.control[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
	}
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/chips/gte/gte_test.go ====================

package gte

import (
	"errors"
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// Command word builders. Per psx-spx "GTE Command
// Encoding": opcode in bits 0..5, lm in bit 10, sf in
// bit 19.
func cmdWord(opcode uint32, sf, lm bool) uint32 {
	w := opcode
	if lm {
		w |= 1 << 10
	}
	if sf {
		w |= 1 << 19
	}
	return w
}

func setV(g *GTE, n int, x, y, z int) {
	g.SetData(uint32(2*n), uint32(uint16(int16(y)))<<16|uint32(uint16(int16(x))))
	g.SetData(uint32(2*n+1), uint32(uint16(int16(z))))
}

func setIR(g *GTE, x, y, z int) {
	g.SetData(9, uint32(int32(int16(x))))
	g.SetData(10, uint32(int32(int16(y))))
	g.SetData(11, uint32(int32(int16(z))))
}

func irOf(g *GTE) (int64, int64, int64) {
	return int64(int16(uint16(g.Data(9)))),
		int64(int16(uint16(g.Data(10)))),
		int64(int16(uint16(g.Data(11))))
}

func macOf(g *GTE) (int64, int64, int64) {
	return int64(int32(g.Data(25))),
		int64(int32(g.Data(26))),
		int64(int32(g.Data(27)))
}

// setMatrix writes a 3x3 matrix into the packed
// control registers starting at base (0=RT, 8=LLM,
// 16=LCM), using the psx-spx "Matrix Registers"
// packing.
func setMatrix(g *GTE, base uint32, m [3][3]int) {
	pack := func(a, b int) uint32 {
		return uint32(uint16(int16(b)))<<16 | uint32(uint16(int16(a)))
	}
	g.SetControl(base+0, pack(m[0][0], m[0][1]))
	g.SetControl(base+1, pack(m[0][2], m[1][0]))
	g.SetControl(base+2, pack(m[1][1], m[1][2]))
	g.SetControl(base+3, pack(m[2][0], m[2][1]))
	g.SetControl(base+4, uint32(uint16(int16(m[2][2]))))
}

var identQ12 = [3][3]int{
	{0x1000, 0, 0},
	{0, 0x1000, 0},
	{0, 0, 0x1000},
}

func TestRegisterStorage(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	g.SetData(3, 0xDEADBEEF)
	g.SetData(63, 0x12345678) // wraps to register 31
	g.SetControl(31, 0x0BADF00D)
	if g.Data(3) != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("Data(3) = 0x%08X, want 0xDEADBEEF", g.Data(3))
	}
	if g.Data(31) != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("Data(31) = 0x%08X, want 0x12345678", g.Data(31))
	}
	// FLAG read semantics (psx-spx, "GTE Saturation"):
	// bits 11..0 always read zero and bit 31 is the OR
	// of the error bits (30..23, 18..13). The stored
	// value 0x0BADF00D has error bits set, so the read
	// back is 0x0BADF000 with bit 31 forced on.
	if g.Control(31) != 0x8BADF000 {
		t.Errorf("Control(31) = 0x%08X, want 0x8BADF000", g.Control(31))
	}
	// A stored FLAG with no error bits reads back with
	// bit 31 clear.
	g.SetControl(31, 0x00001000)
	if g.Control(31) != 0x00001000 {
		t.Errorf("Control(31) = 0x%08X, want 0x00001000", g.Control(31))
	}
}

func TestCommandsExecuteNotRefused(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	g.SetData(0, 0x11111111)
	// Every documented opcode must execute (nil error).
	for _, c := range Commands {
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(c.Opcode, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("Execute(%s) error = %v, want nil", c.Name, err)
		}
	}
	if g.Unsupported() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Unsupported() = %d, want 0", g.Unsupported())
	}
	if err := g.Execute(0x3B); !errors.Is(err, ErrUnknownCommand) {
		t.Errorf("Execute(0x3B) error = %v, want ErrUnknownCommand", err)
	}
	if g.Unsupported() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("Unsupported() = %d, want 1 after unknown opcode", g.Unsupported())
	}
	name, ok := CommandName(0x01)
	if !ok || name != "RTPS" {
		t.Errorf("CommandName(0x01) = %q, %v; want RTPS, true", name, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := CommandName(0x3B); ok {
		t.Errorf("CommandName(0x3B) reported a name for an undocumented opcode")
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	g.SetData(7, 0xFEEDFACE)
	g.SetControl(2, 0x0D15EA5E)
	state := g.Serialize()
	if len(state) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(state), StateSize)
	}
	g2 := New()
	if err := g2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if g2.Data(7) != 0xFEEDFACE || g2.Control(2) != 0x0D15EA5E {
		t.Errorf("round trip mismatch: data=0x%08X control=0x%08X", g2.Data(7), g2.Control(2))
	}
	if err := g2.Deserialize(state[:8]); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("short state accepted, want error")
	}
}

func TestCommandCycles(t *testing.T) {
	// Spot checks against the psx-spx "GTE Opcode
	// Summary" Clk column.
	want := map[uint32]int{
		0x01: 15, // RTPS
		0x30: 23, // RTPT
		0x16: 44, // NCDT
		0x06: 8,  // NCLIP
		0x0C: 6,  // OP
		0x28: 5,  // SQR
		0x2A: 17, // DPCT
		0x2D: 5,  // AVSZ3
		0x2E: 6,  // AVSZ4
		0x3F: 39, // NCCT
		0x13: 19, // NCDS
		0x3D: 5,  // GPF
		0x3E: 5,  // GPL
	}
	for op, cycles := range want {
		if got := CommandCycles(op); got != cycles {
			t.Errorf("CommandCycles(0x%02X) = %d, want %d", op, got, cycles)
		}
	}
	if got := CommandCycles(0x3B); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("CommandCycles(0x3B) = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	g := New()
	if got := g.Command(cmdWord(0x01, true, false)); got != 15 {
		t.Errorf("Command(RTPS) = %d cycles, want 15", got)
	}
}

// rtpsRig builds a GTE with identity rotation, zero
// translation, the given H, and screen offsets
// OFX=160.0, OFY=120.0 in 16.16 fixed point.
func rtpsRig(h uint32) *GTE {
	g := New()
	setMatrix(g, 0, identQ12)
	g.SetControl(26, h)       // H
	g.SetControl(24, 160<<16) // OFX
	g.SetControl(25, 120<<16) // OFY
	return g
}

func TestRTPSIdentity(t *testing.T) {
	g := rtpsRig(300)
	setV(g, 0, 100, 50, 400)
	if err := g.Execute(0x0180001); err != nil { // documented RTPS word
		t.Fatalf("RTPS: %v", err)
	}
	ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g)
	if ir1 != 100 || ir2 != 50 || ir3 != 400 {
		t.Errorf("IR = (%d,%d,%d), want (100,50,400)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
	}
	if sz := g.Data(19); sz != 400 {
		t.Errorf("SZ3 = %d, want 400", sz)
	}
	// Ideal division per the doc formula:
	// n = ((H*20000h/SZ3)+1)/2 = 49152, so
	// SX = (n*100 + OFX) / 10000h = 235 and
	// SY = (n*50 + OFY) / 10000h = 157.
	// The hardware UNR division is inexact (measured
	// n = 49149 for this input), so the gate tolerance
	// is 2 pixels; SZ is exact.
	sxy := g.Data(14)
	sx := int64(int16(uint16(sxy)))
	sy := int64(int16(uint16(sxy >> 16)))
	if math.Abs(float64(sx-235)) > 2 {
		t.Errorf("SX2 = %d, want 235 +/- 2 (UNR division tolerance)", sx)
	}
	if math.Abs(float64(sy-157)) > 2 {
		t.Errorf("SY2 = %d, want 157 +/- 2 (UNR division tolerance)", sy)
	}
	if flag := g.Control(31); flag != 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want 0 (no saturation or overflow)", flag)
	}
}

func TestRTPSDivideOverflowAndSZSaturation(t *testing.T) {
	// Near point: SZ3 = 100 <= H/2 = 150, so the
	// division overflows: the quotient clamps to
	// 1FFFFh and FLAG bit 17 (and the summary bit 31)
	// is set (psx-spx, RTPS note and "GTE Division
	// Inaccuracy").
	g := rtpsRig(300)
	setV(g, 0, 500, 50, 100)
	if err := g.Execute(0x0180001); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RTPS: %v", err)
	}
	flag := g.Control(31)
	if flag&(1<<17) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want divide overflow bit 17 set", flag)
	}
	if flag&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want summary bit 31 set", flag)
	}
	if sz := g.Data(19); sz != 100 {
		t.Errorf("SZ3 = %d, want 100 (the Z itself does not saturate)", sz)
	}
	// With the clamped quotient, SX saturates to the
	// +3FFh screen limit.
	if sx := int16(uint16(g.Data(14))); sx != 0x3FF {
		t.Errorf("SX2 = %d, want 0x3FF (saturated)", sx)
	}
	// Far point with sf=0: MAC3 = TRZ*1000h leaves
	// SZ3 = MAC3 SAR 12 above FFFFh, so SZ3 saturates
	// to FFFFh with FLAG bit 18.
	g2 := rtpsRig(300)
	g2.SetControl(7, 0x100000) // TRZ
	setV(g2, 0, 0, 0, 0)
	if err := g2.Execute(cmdWord(0x01, false, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RTPS sf=0: %v", err)
	}
	if sz := g2.Data(19); sz != 0xFFFF {
		t.Errorf("SZ3 = 0x%X, want 0xFFFF (saturated)", sz)
	}
	if flag := g2.Control(31); flag&(1<<18) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want SZ saturation bit 18 set", flag)
	}
}

func TestNCLIPWinding(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	pack := func(x, y int) uint32 {
		return uint32(uint16(int16(y)))<<16 | uint32(uint16(int16(x)))
	}
	// (0,0), (10,0), (0,10): MAC0 = 10*10 = +100.
	g.SetData(12, pack(0, 0))
	g.SetData(13, pack(10, 0))
	g.SetData(14, pack(0, 10))
	if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x06, false, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NCLIP: %v", err)
	}
	if mac0 := int32(g.Data(24)); mac0 != 100 {
		t.Errorf("MAC0 = %d, want +100", mac0)
	}
	// Reversed winding flips the sign exactly.
	g.SetData(13, pack(0, 10))
	g.SetData(14, pack(10, 0))
	if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x06, false, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NCLIP: %v", err)
	}
	if mac0 := int32(g.Data(24)); mac0 != -100 {
		t.Errorf("MAC0 = %d, want -100", mac0)
	}
}

func TestAVSZ(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	g.SetData(16, 50)  // SZ0
	g.SetData(17, 100) // SZ1
	g.SetData(18, 200) // SZ2
	g.SetData(19, 300) // SZ3
	// ZSF3 = 1/3 in 1.3.12 fixed point = 0x555.
	g.SetControl(29, 0x555)
	if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x2D, true, true)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AVSZ3: %v", err)
	}
	// MAC0 = ZSF3*(SZ1+SZ2+SZ3), OTZ = MAC0/1000h.
	wantMAC0 := int64(0x555) * 600
	if mac0 := int64(int32(g.Data(24))); mac0 != wantMAC0 {
		t.Errorf("MAC0 = %d, want %d", mac0, wantMAC0)
	}
	if otz := g.Data(7); otz != uint32(wantMAC0>>12) {
		t.Errorf("OTZ = %d, want %d", otz, wantMAC0>>12)
	}
	// ZSF4 = 1/4 = 0x400.
	g.SetControl(30, 0x400)
	if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x2E, true, true)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AVSZ4: %v", err)
	}
	wantMAC0 = int64(0x400) * 650
	if mac0 := int64(int32(g.Data(24))); mac0 != wantMAC0 {
		t.Errorf("MAC0 = %d, want %d", mac0, wantMAC0)
	}
	if otz := g.Data(7); otz != uint32(wantMAC0>>12) {
		t.Errorf("OTZ = %d, want %d", otz, wantMAC0>>12)
	}
}

func mvmvaWord(mx, v, cv uint32, sf, lm bool) uint32 {
	w := uint32(0x12) | mx<<17 | v<<15 | cv<<13
	if lm {
		w |= 1 << 10
	}
	if sf {
		w |= 1 << 19
	}
	return w
}

func TestMVMVA(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	// Rotation matrix with a 0.5 cross term.
	setMatrix(g, 0, [3][3]int{
		{0x1000, 0x800, 0},
		{0, 0x1000, 0},
		{0, 0, 0x1000},
	})
	setV(g, 0, 100, 200, 50)
	if err := g.Execute(mvmvaWord(0, 0, 0, true, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("MVMVA: %v", err)
	}
	// Float64 reference at Q12 scale.
	fx := (1.0*100 + 0.5*200)
	if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); math.Abs(float64(ir1)-fx) > 1 ||
		math.Abs(float64(ir2)-200) > 1 || math.Abs(float64(ir3)-50) > 1 {
		t.Errorf("IR = (%d,%d,%d), want near (%v,200,50)", ir1, ir2, ir3, fx)
	}
	if m1, m2, m3 := macOf(g); m1 != 200 || m2 != 200 || m3 != 50 {
		t.Errorf("MAC = (%d,%d,%d), want (200,200,50)", m1, m2, m3)
	}
	// Translation select cv=1 adds BK (each component
	// shifted by 12 before the SAR 12, so BK passes
	// through unchanged at sf=1).
	g.SetControl(13, 10)
	g.SetControl(14, 20)
	g.SetControl(15, 30)
	if err := g.Execute(mvmvaWord(0, 0, 1, true, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("MVMVA cv=BK: %v", err)
	}
	if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 210 || ir2 != 220 || ir3 != 80 {
		t.Errorf("IR = (%d,%d,%d), want (210,220,80)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
	}
	// Light matrix path (mx=1), no translation.
	setMatrix(g, 8, [3][3]int{
		{0x2000, 0, 0},
		{0, 0x2000, 0},
		{0, 0, 0x2000},
	})
	if err := g.Execute(mvmvaWord(1, 0, 3, true, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("MVMVA mx=LLM: %v", err)
	}
	if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 200 || ir2 != 400 || ir3 != 100 {
		t.Errorf("IR = (%d,%d,%d), want (200,400,100)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
	}
	// Bugged far-color path (cv=2): only the last two
	// product terms survive, MAC1 = (RT12*VY0 +
	// RT13*VZ0) SAR 12 = (0x800*200 + 0) SAR 12 = 100.
	g.SetControl(21, 999) // RFC, must not contribute
	if err := g.Execute(mvmvaWord(0, 0, 2, true, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("MVMVA cv=FC: %v", err)
	}
	if m1, _, _ := macOf(g); m1 != 100 {
		t.Errorf("MAC1 = %d, want 100 (bugged FC path drops term 1)", m1)
	}
}

// colorRig builds a GTE for the color commands: light
// matrix with only L33 set, light color matrix diag,
// zero background and far colors, RGBC set by the
// caller.
func colorRig() *GTE {
	g := New()
	setMatrix(g, 8, [3][3]int{
		{0, 0, 0},
		{0, 0, 0},
		{0, 0, 0x1000},
	})
	setMatrix(g, 16, identQ12)
	return g
}

func TestNCDSExact(t *testing.T) {
	g := colorRig()
	// Half-scale light color matrix.
	setMatrix(g, 16, [3][3]int{
		{0x800, 0, 0},
		{0, 0x800, 0},
		{0, 0, 0x800},
	})
	// RGBC: R=80h, G=40h, B=20h, CODE=5Ah.
	g.SetData(6, 0x5A<<24|0x20<<16|0x40<<8|0x80)
	setV(g, 0, 0, 0, 0x1000) // normal facing the light
	// Hand computation per the doc steps (sf=1):
	// step 1: IR = LLM*V0 SAR 12 = (0,0,1000h)
	// step 2: IR = (BK + LCM*IR) SAR 12 = (0,0,800h)
	// step 3: MAC = (R*IR1, G*IR2, B*IR3) SHL 4
	//             = (0, 0, 20h*800h) SHL 4 = (0,0,100000h)
	// step 4: IR0 = 0, so the depth cue changes
	//         nothing.
	// step 5: MAC = MAC SAR 12 = (0,0,100h)
	// FIFO byte B = 100h/16 = 10h, IR3 = 100h.
	if err := g.Execute(0x0E80413); err != nil { // documented NCDS word
		t.Fatalf("NCDS: %v", err)
	}
	if _, _, m3 := macOf(g); m3 != 0x100 {
		t.Errorf("MAC3 = 0x%X, want 0x100", m3)
	}
	if _, _, ir3 := irOf(g); ir3 != 0x100 {
		t.Errorf("IR3 = 0x%X, want 0x100", ir3)
	}
	if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != 0x5A<<24|0x10<<16 {
		t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want 0x5A100000", rgb2)
	}
	// Full interpolation to the far color (IR0=1000h,
	// FC=0) pulls the result all the way to zero.
	g.SetData(8, 0x1000)
	if err := g.Execute(0x0E80413); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("NCDS: %v", err)
	}
	if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != 0x5A<<24 {
		t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want 0x5A000000 (full depth cue to FC=0)", rgb2)
	}
}

func TestColorCommands(t *testing.T) {
	const code = 0x63
	setRGBC := func(g *GTE, r, gg, b int) {
		g.SetData(6, code<<24|uint32(b)<<16|uint32(gg)<<8|uint32(r))
	}
	halfLCM := func(g *GTE) {
		setMatrix(g, 16, [3][3]int{
			{0x800, 0, 0},
			{0, 0x800, 0},
			{0, 0, 0x800},
		})
	}

	t.Run("NCS", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		halfLCM(g)
		setRGBC(g, 0, 0, 0)
		setV(g, 0, 0, 0, 0x1000)
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x1E, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("NCS: %v", err)
		}
		// IR = (0,0,800h); FIFO bytes = MAC/16.
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x80<<16 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want code|0x800000", rgb2)
		}
		if _, _, ir3 := irOf(g); ir3 != 0x800 {
			t.Errorf("IR3 = 0x%X, want 0x800", ir3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("NCT", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		halfLCM(g)
		setRGBC(g, 0, 0, 0)
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			setV(g, i, 0, 0, 0x1000)
		}
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x20, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("NCT: %v", err)
		}
		want := uint32(code<<24 | 0x80<<16)
		if g.Data(20) != want || g.Data(21) != want || g.Data(22) != want {
			t.Errorf("RGB FIFO = %08X %08X %08X, want all %08X",
				g.Data(20), g.Data(21), g.Data(22), want)
		}
	})

	t.Run("NCCS", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		halfLCM(g)
		setRGBC(g, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80)
		setV(g, 0, 0, 0, 0x1000)
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x1B, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("NCCS: %v", err)
		}
		// MAC3 = (80h*800h) SHL 4 SAR 12 = 400h; byte 40h.
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x40<<16 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want code|0x400000", rgb2)
		}
		if _, _, ir3 := irOf(g); ir3 != 0x400 {
			t.Errorf("IR3 = 0x%X, want 0x400", ir3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("NCCT", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		halfLCM(g)
		setRGBC(g, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80)
		for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
			setV(g, i, 0, 0, 0x1000)
		}
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x3F, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("NCCT: %v", err)
		}
		want := uint32(code<<24 | 0x40<<16)
		if g.Data(20) != want || g.Data(21) != want || g.Data(22) != want {
			t.Errorf("RGB FIFO = %08X %08X %08X, want all %08X",
				g.Data(20), g.Data(21), g.Data(22), want)
		}
	})

	t.Run("CC", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x40)
		setIR(g, 0x1000, 0x800, 0x400)
		if err := g.Execute(0x138041C); err != nil { // documented CC word
			t.Fatalf("CC: %v", err)
		}
		// Identity LCM: MAC = (FFh*1000h, 80h*800h,
		// 40h*400h) SHL 4 SAR 12 = (FF0h, 400h, 100h);
		// bytes (FFh, 40h, 10h).
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x10<<16|0x40<<8|0xFF {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want 0x631040FF", rgb2)
		}
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0xFF0 || ir2 != 0x400 || ir3 != 0x100 {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%X,%X,%X), want (FF0,400,100)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("CDP", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0xFF, 0x80, 0x40)
		setIR(g, 0x1000, 0x800, 0x400)
		g.SetData(8, 0x1000) // IR0: full depth cue to FC=0
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x14, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("CDP: %v", err)
		}
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want code only (cued to far color 0)", rgb2)
		}
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0 || ir2 != 0 || ir3 != 0 {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%d,%d,%d), want (0,0,0)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("DCPL", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0x80, 0, 0)
		setIR(g, 0x1000, 0, 0)
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x29, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("DCPL: %v", err)
		}
		// MAC1 = (80h*1000h) SHL 4 SAR 12 = 800h (IR0=0
		// disables the cue); byte R = 80h.
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x80 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want code|0x80", rgb2)
		}
		if ir1, _, _ := irOf(g); ir1 != 0x800 {
			t.Errorf("IR1 = 0x%X, want 0x800", ir1)
		}
	})

	t.Run("DPCS", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0x80, 0x40, 0x20)
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x10, true, false)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("DPCS: %v", err)
		}
		// Bytes round trip: MAC = byte SHL 16, SAR 12,
		// byte = MAC/16 gives the original bytes.
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x20<<16|0x40<<8|0x80 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want 0x63204080", rgb2)
		}
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0x800 || ir2 != 0x400 || ir3 != 0x200 {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%X,%X,%X), want (800,400,200)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("DPCT", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0, 0, 0)                           // only CODE is read from RGBC
		g.SetData(20, 0x11<<24|0x20<<16|0x40<<8|0x80) // A
		g.SetData(21, 0x22<<24|0x04<<16|0x08<<8|0x10) // B
		g.SetData(22, 0x33<<24|0x03<<16|0x01<<8|0x02) // C
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x2A, true, false)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("DPCT: %v", err)
		}
		// With IR0=0 each entry round trips its bytes
		// and gains the RGBC code; the FIFO order is
		// preserved (oldest result in RGB0).
		if rgb0 := g.Data(20); rgb0 != code<<24|0x20<<16|0x40<<8|0x80 {
			t.Errorf("RGB0 = 0x%08X, want processed A", rgb0)
		}
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x03<<16|0x01<<8|0x02 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want processed C", rgb2)
		}
	})

	t.Run("INTPL", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0, 0, 0)
		setIR(g, 0x1000, 0x800, 0x400)
		g.SetData(8, 0x800) // IR0 = 0.5 toward FC=0
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x11, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("INTPL: %v", err)
		}
		// Half-way interpolation halves every
		// component exactly.
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0x800 || ir2 != 0x400 || ir3 != 0x200 {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%X,%X,%X), want (800,400,200)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x20<<16|0x40<<8|0x80 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want 0x63204080", rgb2)
		}
	})

	t.Run("OP", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := New()
		setMatrix(g, 0, [3][3]int{
			{0x1000, 0, 0},
			{0, 0x1000, 0},
			{0, 0, 0x1000},
		})
		setIR(g, 0x10, 0x20, 0x30)
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x0C, false, false)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("OP: %v", err)
		}
		// MAC = (30h*1000h - 20h*1000h,
		//        10h*1000h - 30h*1000h,
		//        20h*1000h - 10h*1000h)
		m1, m2, m3 := macOf(g)
		if m1 != 0x10000 || m2 != -0x20000 || m3 != 0x10000 {
			t.Errorf("MAC = (%X,%X,%X), want (10000,-20000,10000)", m1, m2, m3)
		}
		// All three IRs saturate (lm=0 range).
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0x7FFF || ir2 != -0x8000 || ir3 != 0x7FFF {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%X,%X,%X), want (7FFF,-8000,7FFF)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("SQR sf=1", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := New()
		setIR(g, 0x1000, 0x800, 0x400)
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x28, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("SQR: %v", err)
		}
		m1, m2, m3 := macOf(g)
		if m1 != 0x1000 || m2 != 0x400 || m3 != 0x100 {
			t.Errorf("MAC = (%X,%X,%X), want (1000,400,100)", m1, m2, m3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("SQR sf=0", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := New()
		setIR(g, 0x1000, 0x800, 0x400)
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x28, false, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("SQR: %v", err)
		}
		m1, m2, m3 := macOf(g)
		if m1 != 0x1000000 || m2 != 0x400000 || m3 != 0x100000 {
			t.Errorf("MAC = (%X,%X,%X), want (1000000,400000,100000)", m1, m2, m3)
		}
		// Unshifted squares exceed 7FFFh, so all IRs
		// saturate to the 7FFFh maximum.
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0x7FFF || ir2 != 0x7FFF || ir3 != 0x7FFF {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%X,%X,%X), want all 7FFF", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
	})

	t.Run("GPF", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0, 0, 0)
		setIR(g, 0x1000, 0x800, 0x400)
		g.SetData(8, 0x800) // IR0
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x3D, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("GPF: %v", err)
		}
		// MAC = (IR*IR0) SAR 12 = half of IR.
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0x800 || ir2 != 0x400 || ir3 != 0x200 {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%X,%X,%X), want (800,400,200)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
		if rgb2 := g.Data(22); rgb2 != code<<24|0x20<<16|0x40<<8|0x80 {
			t.Errorf("RGB2 = 0x%08X, want 0x63204080", rgb2)
		}
	})

	t.Run("GPL", func(t *testing.T) {
		g := colorRig()
		setRGBC(g, 0, 0, 0)
		g.SetData(25, 0x100) // MAC1
		g.SetData(26, 0x100) // MAC2
		g.SetData(27, 0x100) // MAC3
		setIR(g, 0x100, 0, 0)
		g.SetData(8, 0x1000) // IR0 = 1.0
		if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x3E, true, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("GPL: %v", err)
		}
		// MAC = ((IR*IR0) + (MAC SHL 12)) SAR 12:
		// MAC1 = (100000h + 100000h) SAR 12 = 200h,
		// MAC2 = MAC3 = 100h.
		if ir1, ir2, ir3 := irOf(g); ir1 != 0x200 || ir2 != 0x100 || ir3 != 0x100 {
			t.Errorf("IR = (%X,%X,%X), want (200,100,100)", ir1, ir2, ir3)
		}
	})
}

func TestOPOverflowSetsFlagSummary(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	setMatrix(g, 0, [3][3]int{
		{0x7FFF, 0, 0},
		{0, 0x7FFF, 0},
		{0, 0, 0x7FFF},
	})
	setIR(g, 0x7FFF, -0x8000, 0x7FFF)
	if err := g.Execute(cmdWord(0x0C, false, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OP: %v", err)
	}
	// MAC1 = 7FFFh*7FFFh + 8000h*7FFFh = 7FFE8001h,
	// exact in the 44-bit accumulator.
	if m1, _, _ := macOf(g); m1 != 0x7FFE8001 {
		t.Errorf("MAC1 = 0x%X, want 0x7FFE8001", m1)
	}
	flag := g.Control(31)
	// Cross products of two signed 16-bit vectors are
	// bounded by 2^31, so the 44-bit MAC overflow bits
	// (30..25) cannot fire for OP; the overflow
	// surfaces through the IR saturation bits 24..22,
	// and bits 24/23 feed the summary bit 31.
	if flag&(1<<24) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want IR1 saturation bit 24 set", flag)
	}
	if flag&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want summary bit 31 set", flag)
	}
	if flag&(0x3F<<25) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, MAC overflow bits 30..25 unexpectedly set", flag)
	}
	// A genuine 44-bit MAC overflow: RTPS with sf=0, a
	// maximal translation and a maximal rotated Z
	// leave MAC3 = TRZ*1000h + RT33*VZ0 beyond 43
	// bits (TRZ*1000h alone is 2^43 - 2^12, just
	// inside the range; the product term pushes it
	// over).
	g2 := New()
	setMatrix(g2, 0, identQ12)
	g2.SetControl(7, 0x7FFFFFFF) // TRZ
	setV(g2, 0, 0, 0, 0x7FFF)
	if err := g2.Execute(cmdWord(0x01, false, false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("RTPS: %v", err)
	}
	flag2 := g2.Control(31)
	if flag2&(1<<28) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want MAC3 positive overflow bit 28 set", flag2)
	}
	if flag2&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FLAG = 0x%08X, want summary bit 31 set", flag2)
	}
}

func TestSXYFIFOOrder(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	setMatrix(g, 0, identQ12)
	g.SetControl(26, 256) // H
	// OFX/OFY are zero. Three distinct vertices pushed
	// by one RTPT (V0, V1, V2 in order).
	setV(g, 0, 10, 20, 200)
	setV(g, 1, 30, 40, 200)
	setV(g, 2, 50, 60, 200)
	if err := g.Execute(0x0280030); err != nil { // documented RTPT word
		t.Fatalf("RTPT: %v", err)
	}
	sxOf := func(reg uint32) int {
		return int(int16(uint16(g.Data(reg))))
	}
	sx0, sx1, sx2 := sxOf(12), sxOf(13), sxOf(14)
	// Ideal SX = H*x/z = 256*x/200: 12, 38, 64, with
	// the UNR division tolerance of 2 pixels.
	for i, tc := range []struct{ got, want int }{{sx0, 12}, {sx1, 38}, {sx2, 64}} {
		if math.Abs(float64(tc.got-tc.want)) > 2 {
			t.Errorf("SXY%d SX = %d, want %d +/- 2", i, tc.got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if !(sx0 < sx1 && sx1 < sx2) {
		t.Errorf("FIFO order wrong: SX = %d, %d, %d", sx0, sx1, sx2)
	}
	// SXYP reads back SXY2.
	if g.Data(15) != g.Data(14) {
		t.Errorf("SXYP = 0x%08X, want SXY2 = 0x%08X", g.Data(15), g.Data(14))
	}
	// Writing SXYP pushes the FIFO by hand: SXY0 takes
	// the old SXY1, SXY1 the old SXY2, SXY2 the value.
	prev1, prev2 := g.Data(13), g.Data(14)
	g.SetData(15, 0x00010002)
	if g.Data(12) != prev1 || g.Data(13) != prev2 {
		t.Errorf("SXYP push: SXY0=0x%08X SXY1=0x%08X, want old SXY1/SXY2",
			g.Data(12), g.Data(13))
	}
	if g.Data(14) != 0x00010002 {
		t.Errorf("SXY2 = 0x%08X, want 0x00010002 after SXYP write", g.Data(14))
	}
}

func TestLZCR(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		in   uint32
		want uint32
	}{
		{0x0000FFFF, 16},
		{0xFFFF0000, 16},
		{0xFFFFFFFF, 32},
		{0x00000000, 32},
		{0x7FFFFFFF, 1},
	}
	g := New()
	for _, tc := range cases {
		g.SetData(30, tc.in)
		if got := g.Data(31); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("LZCR for LZCS=0x%08X = %d, want %d", tc.in, got, tc.want)
		}
		if got := g.Data(30); got != tc.in {
			t.Errorf("LZCS read = 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", got, tc.in)
		}
	}
}

func TestIRGBORGBConversion(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	// Writing IRGB expands the 5-bit fields into
	// IR1..IR3 multiplied by 80h.
	g.SetData(28, 0x7FFF) // R=G=B=1Fh
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		if v := g.Data(uint32(9 + i)); v != 0xF80 {
			t.Errorf("IR%d = 0x%X, want 0xF80", i+1, v)
		}
	}
	// Both IRGB and ORGB read back the collapsed
	// 5:5:5 value.
	if v := g.Data(28); v != 0x7FFF {
		t.Errorf("IRGB read = 0x%X, want 0x7FFF", v)
	}
	if v := g.Data(29); v != 0x7FFF {
		t.Errorf("ORGB read = 0x%X, want 0x7FFF", v)
	}
	// Direct IR writes are reflected: 1000h collapses
	// to 20h, saturated to 1Fh; a negative component
	// saturates to 0.
	setIR(g, 0x1000, -1, 0x80)
	if v := g.Data(29); v != 0x1F|(1<<10) {
		t.Errorf("ORGB read = 0x%X, want 0x%X", v, 0x1F|(1<<10))
	}
	// ORGB is read-only: writes are ignored.
	g.SetData(29, 0)
	if v := g.Data(29); v != 0x1F|(1<<10) {
		t.Errorf("ORGB after write = 0x%X, want unchanged 0x%X", v, 0x1F|(1<<10))
	}
}

	want := map[int]int64{

	}
