		}
	}
}

func TestUNRErrorBound(t *testing.T) {
	// The UNR division error bound, gated against
	// exact division over 20,000 deterministic
	// pseudo-random (H, SZ) pairs in the
	// non-overflow, non-saturating range: the exact
	// documented value is (H*20000h/SZ+1)/2, which is
	// H*10000h/SZ + 0.5. Pairs whose exact value
	// reaches the 1FFFFh saturation are skipped
	// (that path is pinned by the overflow test).
	e := &engine{g: New()}
	rng := uint32(0x12345678)
	next := func() uint32 {
		rng = rng*1664525 + 1013904223
		return rng >> 8
	}
	maxErr := 0.0
	tested := 0
	for i := 0; i < 20000; i++ {
		h := next()&0xFFFF + 1
		sz := next()&0xFFFF + 1
		if h >= sz*2 {
			continue // overflow branch
		}
		exact := float64(h)*65536.0/float64(sz) + 0.5
		if exact >= 0x1FFFF {
			continue // saturation path
		}
		e.g.control[26] = h
		e.flag = 0
		got := e.divide(sz)
		d := float64(got) - exact
		if d < 0 {
			d = -d
		}
		if d > maxErr {
			maxErr = d
		}
		tested++
	}
	if tested < 10000 {
		t.Fatalf("only %d pairs in range, want at least 10000", tested)
	}
	if maxErr > 3.0 {
		t.Errorf("UNR max error = %.3f over %d pairs, want <= 3.0", maxErr, tested)
	}
	t.Logf("UNR error bound: max %.3f over %d pairs", maxErr, tested)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/chips/r3000a/conformance_test.go ====================

package r3000a

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// TestTomHarteMIPSCorpus is the family-pattern
// presence-gated conformance slot. For PS1-1 the check
// was made against the TomHarte/ProcessorTests tree:
// it contains 6502, 65816, 680x0, 8088, spc700 and
// 65C02 variants, and no MIPS or PSX single-step set.
// If a corpus directory ever appears under testroms,
// this test says so instead of passing silently; the
// CPU is meanwhile gated on the documentation-derived
// unit tests in this package.
func TestTomHarteMIPSCorpus(t *testing.T) {
	candidates := []string{
		"../../testroms/tomharte-mips",
		"../../testroms/tomharte-psx",
		"../../testroms/mips",
		"../../testroms/psx",
	}
	for _, d := range candidates {
		if st, err := os.Stat(d); err == nil && st.IsDir() {
			t.Skipf("corpus directory %s exists, but PS1-1 ships no harness for its schema; see the core README", d)
		}
	}
	t.Skip("no MIPS single-step corpus present: TomHarte/ProcessorTests has no mips or psx set (checked for PS1-1); CPU gated on unit tests")
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/chips/r3000a/exec.go ====================

package r3000a

// Instruction execution for the R3000A. Register writes
// go through setReg/setLoad so the load-delay and
// cancellation rules in Step see every write. Any
// instruction that can fault checks its fault condition
// before producing side effects, so a faulting
// instruction has no architectural effect.

func sext16(v uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(int32(int16(v)))
}

func (c *CPU) raise(code, addr, ce uint32) *raisedException {
	return &raisedException{code: code, addr: addr, ce: ce}
}

func (c *CPU) execute(op uint32, instrPC uint32) (int, bool, *raisedException) {
	primary := op >> 26
	rs := (op >> 21) & 31
	rt := (op >> 16) & 31
	rd := (op >> 11) & 31
	shamt := (op >> 6) & 31
	funct := op & 63
	imm := op & 0xFFFF
	simm := sext16(imm)
	cycles := 1

	switch primary {
	case 0x00: // SPECIAL
		switch funct {
		case 0x00: // SLL
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rt]<<shamt)
		case 0x02: // SRL
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rt]>>shamt)
		case 0x03: // SRA
			c.setReg(rd, uint32(int32(c.Regs[rt])>>shamt))
		case 0x04: // SLLV
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rt]<<(c.Regs[rs]&31))
		case 0x06: // SRLV
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rt]>>(c.Regs[rs]&31))
		case 0x07: // SRAV
			c.setReg(rd, uint32(int32(c.Regs[rt])>>(c.Regs[rs]&31)))
		case 0x08: // JR
			c.NextPC = c.Regs[rs]
			return cycles, true, nil
		case 0x09: // JALR
			target := c.Regs[rs]
			c.setReg(rd, c.NextPC) // NextPC is instrPC+8 here
			c.NextPC = target
			return cycles, true, nil
		case 0x0C: // SYSCALL
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcSys, 0, 0)
		case 0x0D: // BREAK
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcBp, 0, 0)
		case 0x10: // MFHI
			cycles += c.stallHiLo()
			c.setReg(rd, c.HI)
		case 0x11: // MTHI
			cycles += c.stallHiLo()
			c.HI = c.Regs[rs]
		case 0x12: // MFLO
			cycles += c.stallHiLo()
			c.setReg(rd, c.LO)
		case 0x13: // MTLO
			cycles += c.stallHiLo()
			c.LO = c.Regs[rs]
		case 0x18: // MULT
			prod := int64(int32(c.Regs[rs])) * int64(int32(c.Regs[rt]))
			c.HI = uint32(uint64(prod) >> 32)
			c.LO = uint32(prod)
			c.busySet = multBusyCycles
		case 0x19: // MULTU
			prod := uint64(c.Regs[rs]) * uint64(c.Regs[rt])
			c.HI = uint32(prod >> 32)
			c.LO = uint32(prod)
			c.busySet = multBusyCycles
		case 0x1A: // DIV
			a := int32(c.Regs[rs])
			b := int32(c.Regs[rt])
			switch {
			case b == 0:
				// Documented R3000A divide-by-zero result:
				// remainder is the dividend, quotient is
				// -1 for a non-negative dividend, +1 for a
				// negative one.
				c.HI = uint32(a)
				if a < 0 {
					c.LO = 1
				} else {
					c.LO = 0xFFFFFFFF
				}
			case a == -1<<31 && b == -1:
				c.LO = uint32(a)
				c.HI = 0
			default:
				c.LO = uint32(a / b)
				c.HI = uint32(a % b)
			}
			c.busySet = divBusyCycles
		case 0x1B: // DIVU
			a := c.Regs[rs]
			b := c.Regs[rt]
			if b == 0 {
				c.HI = a
				c.LO = 0xFFFFFFFF
			} else {
				c.LO = a / b
				c.HI = a % b
			}
			c.busySet = divBusyCycles
		case 0x20: // ADD
			r := int64(int32(c.Regs[rs])) + int64(int32(c.Regs[rt]))
			if r > 0x7FFFFFFF || r < -0x80000000 {
				return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcOv, 0, 0)
			}
			c.setReg(rd, uint32(r))
		case 0x21: // ADDU
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rs]+c.Regs[rt])
		case 0x22: // SUB
			r := int64(int32(c.Regs[rs])) - int64(int32(c.Regs[rt]))
			if r > 0x7FFFFFFF || r < -0x80000000 {
				return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcOv, 0, 0)
			}
			c.setReg(rd, uint32(r))
		case 0x23: // SUBU
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rs]-c.Regs[rt])
		case 0x24: // AND
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rs]&c.Regs[rt])
		case 0x25: // OR
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rs]|c.Regs[rt])
		case 0x26: // XOR
			c.setReg(rd, c.Regs[rs]^c.Regs[rt])
		case 0x27: // NOR
			c.setReg(rd, ^(c.Regs[rs] | c.Regs[rt]))
		case 0x2A: // SLT
			if int32(c.Regs[rs]) < int32(c.Regs[rt]) {
				c.setReg(rd, 1)
			} else {
				c.setReg(rd, 0)
			}
		case 0x2B: // SLTU
			if c.Regs[rs] < c.Regs[rt] {
				c.setReg(rd, 1)
			} else {
				c.setReg(rd, 0)
			}
		default:
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcRI, 0, 0)
		}
		return cycles, false, nil

	case 0x01: // REGIMM branches
		v := int32(c.Regs[rs])
		target := c.PC + (simm << 2) // PC is instrPC+4 here
		switch rt {
		case 0x00: // BLTZ
			if v < 0 {
				c.NextPC = target
			}
		case 0x01: // BGEZ
			if v >= 0 {
				c.NextPC = target
			}
		case 0x10: // BLTZAL: link is unconditional on the R3000A
			c.setReg(31, c.NextPC)
			if v < 0 {
				c.NextPC = target
			}
		case 0x11: // BGEZAL: link is unconditional on the R3000A
			c.setReg(31, c.NextPC)
			if v >= 0 {
				c.NextPC = target
			}
		default:
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcRI, 0, 0)
		}
		return cycles, true, nil

	case 0x02: // J
		c.NextPC = (c.PC & 0xF0000000) | ((op & 0x03FFFFFF) << 2)
		return cycles, true, nil

	case 0x03: // JAL
		c.setReg(31, c.NextPC)
		c.NextPC = (c.PC & 0xF0000000) | ((op & 0x03FFFFFF) << 2)
		return cycles, true, nil

	case 0x04: // BEQ
		if c.Regs[rs] == c.Regs[rt] {
			c.NextPC = c.PC + (simm << 2)
		}
		return cycles, true, nil

	case 0x05: // BNE
		if c.Regs[rs] != c.Regs[rt] {
			c.NextPC = c.PC + (simm << 2)
		}
		return cycles, true, nil

	case 0x06: // BLEZ
		if rt != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcRI, 0, 0)
		}
		if int32(c.Regs[rs]) <= 0 {
			c.NextPC = c.PC + (simm << 2)
		}
		return cycles, true, nil

	case 0x07: // BGTZ
		if rt != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcRI, 0, 0)
		}
		if int32(c.Regs[rs]) > 0 {
			c.NextPC = c.PC + (simm << 2)
		}
		return cycles, true, nil

	case 0x08: // ADDI
		r := int64(int32(c.Regs[rs])) + int64(int32(simm))
		if r > 0x7FFFFFFF || r < -0x80000000 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcOv, 0, 0)
		}
		c.setReg(rt, uint32(r))
	case 0x09: // ADDIU
		c.setReg(rt, c.Regs[rs]+simm)
	case 0x0A: // SLTI
		if int32(c.Regs[rs]) < int32(simm) {
			c.setReg(rt, 1)
		} else {
			c.setReg(rt, 0)
		}
	case 0x0B: // SLTIU (immediate is sign-extended, compared unsigned)
		if c.Regs[rs] < simm {
			c.setReg(rt, 1)
		} else {
			c.setReg(rt, 0)
		}
	case 0x0C: // ANDI
		c.setReg(rt, c.Regs[rs]&imm)
	case 0x0D: // ORI
		c.setReg(rt, c.Regs[rs]|imm)
	case 0x0E: // XORI
		c.setReg(rt, c.Regs[rs]^imm)
	case 0x0F: // LUI
		c.setReg(rt, imm<<16)

	case 0x10: // COP0
		return c.execCOP0(op, rs, rt, rd, funct)
	case 0x11: // COP1: no FPU on the PSX
		return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcCpU, 0, 1)
	case 0x12: // COP2: the GTE
		return c.execCOP2(op, rs, rt, rd)
	case 0x13: // COP3: not present
		return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcCpU, 0, 3)

	case 0x20, 0x21, 0x22, 0x23, 0x24, 0x25, 0x26, // loads
		0x28, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B, 0x2E, // stores
		0x32, 0x3A: // LWC2 / SWC2
		return c.execLoadStore(primary, rs, rt, simm)

	case 0x30, 0x31, 0x33: // LWC0/1/3
		return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcCpU, 0, primary-0x30)
	case 0x38, 0x39, 0x3B: // SWC0/1/3
		return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcCpU, 0, primary-0x38)

	default:
		return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcRI, 0, 0)
	}
	return cycles, false, nil
}

// execCOP0 handles MFC0, MTC0, BC0 and RFE.
func (c *CPU) execCOP0(op, rs, rt, rd, funct uint32) (int, bool, *raisedException) {
	switch {
	case rs == 0x00: // MFC0: a delayed load, like memory loads
		c.setLoad(rt, c.readCP0(rd))
		return 2, false, nil
	case rs == 0x04: // MTC0
		c.writeCP0(rd, c.Regs[rt])
		return 1, false, nil
	case rs == 0x08: // BC0F/BC0T: the CP0 condition input is tied false on the PSX
		return 1, true, nil
	case rs >= 0x10 && funct == 0x10: // RFE
		c.SR = (c.SR &^ 0x0F) | ((c.SR >> 2) & 0x0F)
		return 1, false, nil
	}
	return 1, false, c.raise(ExcRI, 0, 0)
}

// execCOP2 handles the GTE register moves and command
// issue. Register reads are delayed loads, matching
// the load-delay family.
func (c *CPU) execCOP2(op, rs, rt, rd uint32) (int, bool, *raisedException) {
	if c.CP2 == nil {
		return 1, false, c.raise(ExcCpU, 0, 2)
	}
	switch {
	case rs == 0x00: // MFC2
		c.setLoad(rt, c.CP2.Data(rd))
		return 2, false, nil
	case rs == 0x02: // CFC2
		c.setLoad(rt, c.CP2.Control(rd))
		return 2, false, nil
	case rs == 0x04: // MTC2
		c.CP2.SetData(rd, c.Regs[rt])
		return 1, false, nil
	case rs == 0x06: // CTC2
		c.CP2.SetControl(rd, c.Regs[rt])
		return 1, false, nil
	case rs == 0x08: // BC2F/BC2T: the GTE raises no branch condition
		return 1, true, nil
	case rs >= 0x10: // GTE command: the GTE charges
		// its documented execution cycles.
		cyc := c.CP2.Command(op)
		if cyc < 1 {
			cyc = 1
		}
		return cyc, false, nil
	}
	return 1, false, c.raise(ExcRI, 0, 0)
}

// mergeBase returns the value an LWL/LWR merge starts
// from: the pending load's value when a load to the
// same register is in its delay slot (the merge reads
// late, after that load lands), else the register.
func (c *CPU) mergeBase(rt uint32) uint32 {
	if c.pending.valid && uint32(c.pending.reg) == rt {
		return c.pending.value
	}
	return c.Regs[rt]
}

// execLoadStore implements every integer load and
// store, including the unaligned merge instructions.
func (c *CPU) execLoadStore(primary, rs, rt, simm uint32) (int, bool, *raisedException) {
	addr := c.Regs[rs] + simm
	const cycles = 2
	switch primary {
	case 0x20: // LB
		v := c.readData8(addr)
		c.setLoad(rt, uint32(int32(int8(v))))
	case 0x24: // LBU
		c.setLoad(rt, uint32(c.readData8(addr)))
	case 0x21: // LH
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcAdEL, addr, 0)
		}
		c.setLoad(rt, uint32(int32(int16(c.readData16(addr)))))
	case 0x25: // LHU
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcAdEL, addr, 0)
		}
		c.setLoad(rt, uint32(c.readData16(addr)))
	case 0x23: // LW
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcAdEL, addr, 0)
		}
		c.setLoad(rt, c.readData32(addr))
	case 0x22: // LWL (little-endian merge, documented shifts)
		word := c.readData32(addr &^ 3)
		old := c.mergeBase(rt)
		var v uint32
		switch addr & 3 {
		case 0:
			v = (old & 0x00FFFFFF) | (word << 24)
		case 1:
			v = (old & 0x0000FFFF) | (word << 16)
		case 2:
			v = (old & 0x000000FF) | (word << 8)
		case 3:
			v = word
		}
		c.setLoad(rt, v)
	case 0x26: // LWR
		word := c.readData32(addr &^ 3)
		old := c.mergeBase(rt)
		var v uint32
		switch addr & 3 {
		case 0:
			v = word
		case 1:
			v = (old & 0xFF000000) | (word >> 8)
		case 2:
			v = (old & 0xFFFF0000) | (word >> 16)
		case 3:
			v = (old & 0xFFFFFF00) | (word >> 24)
		}
		c.setLoad(rt, v)
	case 0x28: // SB
		c.writeData8(addr, uint8(c.Regs[rt]))
	case 0x29: // SH
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcAdES, addr, 0)
		}
		c.writeData16(addr, uint16(c.Regs[rt]))
	case 0x2B: // SW
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcAdES, addr, 0)
		}
		c.writeData32(addr, c.Regs[rt])
	case 0x2A: // SWL (read-modify-write of the aligned word)
		a := addr &^ 3
		word := c.readData32(a)
		v := c.Regs[rt]
		var merged uint32
		switch addr & 3 {
		case 0:
			merged = (word & 0xFFFFFF00) | (v >> 24)
		case 1:
			merged = (word & 0xFFFF0000) | (v >> 16)
		case 2:
			merged = (word & 0xFF000000) | (v >> 8)
		case 3:
			merged = v
		}
		c.writeData32(a, merged)
	case 0x2E: // SWR
		a := addr &^ 3
		word := c.readData32(a)
		v := c.Regs[rt]
		var merged uint32
		switch addr & 3 {
		case 0:
			merged = v
		case 1:
			merged = (word & 0x000000FF) | (v << 8)
		case 2:
			merged = (word & 0x0000FFFF) | (v << 16)
		case 3:
			merged = (word & 0x00FFFFFF) | (v << 24)
		}
		c.writeData32(a, merged)
	case 0x32: // LWC2
		if c.CP2 == nil {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcCpU, 0, 2)
		}
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcAdEL, addr, 0)
		}
		c.CP2.SetData(rt, c.readData32(addr))
	case 0x3A: // SWC2
		if c.CP2 == nil {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcCpU, 0, 2)
		}
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return cycles, false, c.raise(ExcAdES, addr, 0)
		}
		c.writeData32(addr, c.CP2.Data(rt))
	}
	return cycles, false, nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/chips/r3000a/r3000a.go ====================

// Package r3000a is a from-scratch MIPS I R3000A CPU, the
// processor of the PlayStation, written from the MIPS I
// architecture manuals and the psx-spx hardware notes.
//
// The two pipeline behaviors that define this chip are
// modeled exactly:
//
//   - Load delay: a load (memory load, MFC0, MFC2) executed
//     by instruction N does not write its destination
//     register until instruction N+1 has executed. N+1
//     reads the old value. If N+1 writes the same
//     register with an ordinary write (an ALU result or
//     a link write), the pending load is cancelled and
//     never lands: the younger write wins, which is the
//     documented R3000 cancellation rule. A second load
//     to the same register does not cancel it: the
//     first load lands on schedule and the second takes
//     its place, so back-to-back loads deliver their
//     values one instruction apart. LWL and LWR merges
//     read the pending value when one targets their
//     register, because the merge happens late in the
//     pipeline; that is how unaligned load pairs
//     compose.
//   - Branch delay: the instruction after any branch or
//     jump always executes before control transfers. If
//     it faults, EPC points at the branch and Cause.BD
//     is set.
//
// Multiply and divide run in the async HI/LO unit: the
// instruction issues in one cycle and sets a busy count
// (12 cycles for multiply, 36 for divide, the documented
// R3000A figures). Independent instructions proceed;
// an MFHI/MFLO/MTHI/MTLO that arrives early stalls for
// the remaining count, which Step charges to it.
//
// Cache control: when SR.Isc is set, data loads and
// stores are redirected into an internal isolation
// store and never touch the bus; when SR.SwC is also
// set, instruction fetches come from that store too.
// Line, tag and writeback behavior of the real caches
// is not modeled in this slice (see the core README).
package r3000a

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
)

// Bus is the CPU's view of memory. Read16 and Read32
// return little-endian values. The CPU only issues
// aligned Read32 calls for word loads; unaligned access
// goes through the LWL/LWR/SWL/SWR merge paths or byte
// accesses.
type Bus interface {
	Read8(addr uint32) uint8
	Read16(addr uint32) uint16
	Read32(addr uint32) uint32
	Write8(addr uint32, v uint8)
	Write16(addr uint32, v uint16)
	Write32(addr uint32, v uint32)
}

// Cop2 is the interface the CPU uses for the GTE. The
// system package wires chips/gte into it. Command is
// the COP2 instruction word; it executes the command
// and returns the cycles the GTE charges for it (the
// documented per-command execution time from the
// psx-spx GTE command table), which Step adds to the
// instruction's cost. That is this core's coprocessor
// stall model: command timing at instruction
// granularity, with no partial-overlap modeling.
type Cop2 interface {
	Data(reg uint32) uint32
	SetData(reg uint32, v uint32)
	Control(reg uint32) uint32
	SetControl(reg uint32, v uint32)
	Command(cmd uint32) int
}

// Exception codes for Cause.ExcCode.
const (
	ExcInt  = 0  // interrupt
	ExcAdEL = 4  // address error, load or fetch
	ExcAdES = 5  // address error, store
	ExcIBE  = 6  // instruction bus error
	ExcDBE  = 7  // data bus error
	ExcSys  = 8  // syscall
	ExcBp   = 9  // breakpoint
	ExcRI   = 10 // reserved instruction
	ExcCpU  = 11 // coprocessor unusable
	ExcOv   = 12 // arithmetic overflow
)

// CP0 register numbers used by this core.
const (
	cp0BadVAddr = 8
	cp0SR       = 12
	cp0Cause    = 13
	cp0EPC      = 14
	cp0PRId     = 15
)

// SR bits.
const (
	srIEc     = 0x00000001
	srStack   = 0x0000003F // KU/IE three-deep stack, bits 0-5
	srIMMask  = 0x0000FF00
	srIsc     = 0x00010000
	srSwC     = 0x00020000
	srBEV     = 0x00400000
	srWriteOK = 0xF7FFFFFF
)

// ResetVector is where execution starts after reset,
// in the BIOS window.
const ResetVector = 0xBFC00000

const (
	generalVectorBEV    = 0xBFC00180
	generalVectorNoBEV  = 0x80000000
	causeIPMask         = 0x0000FF00
	causeSWIP           = 0x00000300 // Cause bits 8-9, software writable
	externalIP2         = 0x00000400 // Cause bit 10, the PSX interrupt line
	multBusyCycles      = 12
	divBusyCycles       = 36
	isolationStoreBytes = 4096
)

// pendingLoad is one delayed load waiting out its delay
// slot.
type pendingLoad struct {
	reg   uint8
	value uint32
	valid bool
}

type raisedException struct {
	code uint32
	addr uint32 // faulting address for BadVAddr, else 0
	ce   uint32 // coprocessor number for ExcCpU
}

// CPU is one R3000A.
type CPU struct {
	Regs   [32]uint32
	HI, LO uint32
	PC     uint32 // address of the next instruction to execute
	NextPC uint32 // address after PC (the branch target path)

	// CP0 registers with architectural behavior. Other
	// CP0 registers read as zero and ignore writes in
	// this slice.
	SR       uint32
	Cause    uint32
	EPC      uint32
	BadVAddr uint32

	// CP2 is the GTE, wired by the system. It may be
	// nil in CPU-only tests; COP2 instructions then
	// raise coprocessor unusable like a missing chip.
	CP2 Cop2

	bus Bus

	pending   pendingLoad // load executed by the previous instruction
	newLoad   pendingLoad // load executed by the current instruction
	curWrites uint32      // bitmask of GPRs the current instruction wrote with non-load writes
	busySet   int         // HI/LO busy count set by the current instruction, -1 for none
	hiLoBusy  int         // remaining HI/LO unit busy cycles
	delaySlot bool        // the instruction at PC sits in a branch delay slot

	isolation [isolationStoreBytes]byte

	cycles uint64
}

// StateSize is the fixed serialized size of the CPU.
const StateSize = 32*4 + // GPRs
	4*4 + // HI, LO, PC, NextPC
	4*4 + // SR, Cause, EPC, BadVAddr
	4 + // pending reg/valid/delaySlot pad
	4 + // pending value
	4 + // hiLoBusy
	8 + // cycles
	isolationStoreBytes

// New returns a CPU in reset state attached to bus.
func New(bus Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{bus: bus}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Reset applies the hardware reset state: PC at the
// BIOS reset vector, SR with BEV set and interrupts
// off, everything else zero.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	c.Regs = [32]uint32{}
	c.HI, c.LO = 0, 0
	c.PC = ResetVector
	c.NextPC = ResetVector + 4
	c.SR = srBEV
	c.Cause = 0
	c.EPC = 0
	c.BadVAddr = 0
	c.pending = pendingLoad{}
	c.newLoad = pendingLoad{}
	c.curWrites = 0
	c.busySet = -1
	c.hiLoBusy = 0
	c.delaySlot = false
	c.isolation = [isolationStoreBytes]byte{}
	c.cycles = 0
}

// Cycles returns the total cycles Step has charged.
func (c *CPU) Cycles() uint64 { return c.cycles }

// SetInterrupt drives the external interrupt line (the
// PSX interrupt controller output, Cause IP2). The
// interrupt is taken at the next instruction boundary
// if SR enables it.
func (c *CPU) SetInterrupt(on bool) {
	if on {
		c.Cause |= externalIP2
	} else {
		c.Cause &^= externalIP2
	}
}

func (c *CPU) interruptPending() bool {
	return c.SR&srIEc != 0 && c.SR&c.Cause&causeIPMask != 0
}

// commitPending lands the previous instruction's
// delayed load unconditionally. Used when the current
// instruction will not execute (exception or
// interrupt), where the older load has completed its
// delay in program order.
func (c *CPU) commitPending() {
	if c.pending.valid && c.pending.reg != 0 {
		c.Regs[c.pending.reg] = c.pending.value
	}
	c.pending = pendingLoad{}
}

// CommitPendingLoad lands the previous instruction's
// delayed load immediately. The system uses it when
// it intercepts execution outside the normal Step
// flow (the BIOS HLE vectors): a load sitting in the
// delay slot of the call has completed its delay in
// program order when the callee starts, exactly as
// enterException treats it.
func (c *CPU) CommitPendingLoad() { c.commitPending() }

// Step executes one instruction (or takes a pending
// interrupt) and returns the cycles charged.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	if c.bus == nil {
		return 0
	}
	if c.interruptPending() {
		c.commitPending()
		c.enterException(ExcInt, c.PC, 0, 0, c.delaySlot)
		c.cycles++
		return 1
	}
	instrPC := c.PC
	if instrPC&3 != 0 {
		c.commitPending()
		c.enterException(ExcAdEL, instrPC, instrPC, 0, c.delaySlot)
		c.cycles++
		return 1
	}
	inDelay := c.delaySlot
	op := c.fetch(instrPC)
	c.PC = c.NextPC
	c.NextPC = c.PC + 4

	c.newLoad = pendingLoad{}
	c.curWrites = 0
	c.busySet = -1
	cycles, isCTI, exc := c.execute(op, instrPC)
	if cycles < 1 {
		cycles = 1
	}
	if exc != nil {
		// The faulting instruction has no architectural
		// effect; the older delayed load completes.
		c.commitPending()
		c.enterException(exc.code, instrPC, exc.addr, exc.ce, inDelay)
		c.cycles += uint64(cycles)
		return cycles
	}
	// Land the previous load unless this instruction
	// wrote the same register with a non-load write
	// (the R3000 cancellation rule). A fresh load to
	// the same register does not cancel it: the old
	// load lands here and the new one becomes pending.
	if c.pending.valid {
		mask := uint32(1) << c.pending.reg
		if c.curWrites&mask == 0 && c.pending.reg != 0 {
			c.Regs[c.pending.reg] = c.pending.value
		}
	}
	c.pending = c.newLoad
	c.delaySlot = isCTI
	if c.busySet >= 0 {
		c.hiLoBusy = c.busySet
	} else if c.hiLoBusy > 0 {
		c.hiLoBusy -= cycles
		if c.hiLoBusy < 0 {
			c.hiLoBusy = 0
		}
	}
	c.Regs[0] = 0
	c.cycles += uint64(cycles)
	return cycles
}

// enterException performs the R3000 exception entry:
// the KU/IE stack shifts, EPC and Cause are loaded
// (EPC points at the branch when the faulting
// instruction is in its delay slot, with Cause.BD
// set), and control goes to the general exception
// vector selected by SR.BEV.
func (c *CPU) enterException(code, instrPC, badAddr, ce uint32, inDelay bool) {
	epc := instrPC
	cause := c.Cause & causeIPMask
	cause |= code << 2
	if inDelay {
		epc = instrPC - 4
		cause |= 1 << 31 // BD
	}
	if code == ExcCpU {
		cause |= ce << 28
	}
	c.Cause = cause
	c.EPC = epc
	switch code {
	case ExcAdEL, ExcAdES, ExcIBE, ExcDBE:
		c.BadVAddr = badAddr
	}
	// Push the mode stack: old becomes previous,
	// previous becomes current's source, current is
	// kernel mode with interrupts disabled.
	c.SR = (c.SR &^ srStack) | ((c.SR & 0x0F) << 2)
	if c.SR&srBEV != 0 {
		c.PC = generalVectorBEV
	} else {
		c.PC = generalVectorNoBEV
	}
	c.NextPC = c.PC + 4
	c.delaySlot = false
	c.pending = pendingLoad{}
}

// fetch reads one instruction word, honoring the
// swapped-cache isolation mode.
func (c *CPU) fetch(addr uint32) uint32 {
	if c.SR&srIsc != 0 && c.SR&srSwC != 0 {
		return c.isoRead32(addr)
	}
	return c.bus.Read32(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) isoRead8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	return c.isolation[addr&(isolationStoreBytes-1)]
}

func (c *CPU) isoRead32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		v |= uint32(c.isoRead8(addr+uint32(i))) << (8 * i)
	}
	return v
}

func (c *CPU) isoWrite8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	c.isolation[addr&(isolationStoreBytes-1)] = v
}

// readData8/16/32 and writeData8/16/32 route through
// the isolation store when SR.Isc is set, else the bus.
func (c *CPU) readData8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	if c.SR&srIsc != 0 {
		return c.isoRead8(addr)
	}
	return c.bus.Read8(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) readData16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	if c.SR&srIsc != 0 {
		return uint16(c.isoRead8(addr)) | uint16(c.isoRead8(addr+1))<<8
	}
	return c.bus.Read16(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) readData32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	if c.SR&srIsc != 0 {
		return c.isoRead32(addr)
	}
	return c.bus.Read32(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) writeData8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	if c.SR&srIsc != 0 {
		c.isoWrite8(addr, v)
		return
	}
	c.bus.Write8(addr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) writeData16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	if c.SR&srIsc != 0 {
		c.isoWrite8(addr, uint8(v))
		c.isoWrite8(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
		return
	}
	c.bus.Write16(addr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) writeData32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	if c.SR&srIsc != 0 {
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			c.isoWrite8(addr+uint32(i), uint8(v>>(8*i)))
		}
		return
	}
	c.bus.Write32(addr, v)
}

// setReg writes a general register immediately and
// records the write for the load-cancellation rule.
func (c *CPU) setReg(reg uint32, v uint32) {
	if reg == 0 {
		return
	}
	c.Regs[reg] = v
	c.curWrites |= uint32(1) << reg
}

// setLoad schedules a delayed load. It deliberately
// does not mark curWrites: a load in the delay slot of
// another load to the same register does not cancel
// the older load (see the package comment).
func (c *CPU) setLoad(reg uint32, v uint32) {
	if reg == 0 {
		return
	}
	c.newLoad = pendingLoad{reg: uint8(reg), value: v, valid: true}
}

// stallHiLo charges the remaining HI/LO busy time to a
// HI/LO access and clears it.
func (c *CPU) stallHiLo() int {
	n := c.hiLoBusy
	c.hiLoBusy = 0
	return n
}

// readCP0 returns a CP0 register. PRId is the
// documented R3000A value 0x00000002.
func (c *CPU) readCP0(reg uint32) uint32 {
	switch reg {
	case cp0BadVAddr:
		return c.BadVAddr
	case cp0SR:
		return c.SR
	case cp0Cause:
		return c.Cause
	case cp0EPC:
		return c.EPC
	case cp0PRId:
		return 0x00000002
	}
	return 0
}

// writeCP0 writes a CP0 register with the documented
// writability rules: BadVAddr and PRId ignore writes,
// and Cause only accepts its two software interrupt
// bits from MTC0.
func (c *CPU) writeCP0(reg uint32, v uint32) {
	switch reg {
	case cp0SR:
		c.SR = v & srWriteOK
	case cp0Cause:
		c.Cause = (c.Cause &^ causeSWIP) | (v & causeSWIP)
	case cp0EPC:
		c.EPC = v
	case cp0BadVAddr, cp0PRId:
		// Read-only in practice; writes are dropped.
	}
}

// Serialize returns the full CPU state as a fixed-size
// block (see StateSize).
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	off := 0
	for _, r := range c.Regs {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], r)
		off += 4
	}
	for _, v := range []uint32{c.HI, c.LO, c.PC, c.NextPC, c.SR, c.Cause, c.EPC, c.BadVAddr} {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], v)
		off += 4
	}
	meta := byte(0)
	if c.pending.valid {
		meta = c.pending.reg
		out[off] = meta
		out[off+1] = 1
	}
	if c.delaySlot {
		out[off+2] = 1
	}
	off += 4
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], c.pending.value)
	off += 4
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], uint32(int32(c.hiLoBusy)))
	off += 4
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(out[off:], c.cycles)
	off += 8
	copy(out[off:], c.isolation[:])
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != StateSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("r3000a: state size %d, want %d", len(in), StateSize)
	}
	off := 0
	for i := range c.Regs {
		c.Regs[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
	}
	vals := make([]uint32, 8)
	for i := range vals {
		vals[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
	}
	c.HI, c.LO, c.PC, c.NextPC = vals[0], vals[1], vals[2], vals[3]
	c.SR, c.Cause, c.EPC, c.BadVAddr = vals[4], vals[5], vals[6], vals[7]
	c.pending = pendingLoad{reg: in[off], valid: in[off+1] != 0}
	c.delaySlot = in[off+2] != 0
	off += 4
	c.pending.value = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
	if !c.pending.valid {
		c.pending = pendingLoad{}
	}
	off += 4
	c.hiLoBusy = int(int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])))
	off += 4
	c.cycles = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(in[off:])
	off += 8
	copy(c.isolation[:], in[off:off+isolationStoreBytes])
	c.newLoad = pendingLoad{}
	c.curWrites = 0
	c.busySet = -1
	c.Regs[0] = 0
	return nil
}

package r3000a

import "testing"

// ramBus is a flat little-endian test memory. Addresses
// are masked into the store, so programs can use any
// segment.
type ramBus struct{ mem []byte }

func newRAMBus() *ramBus { return &ramBus{mem: make([]byte, 1<<20)} }

func (b *ramBus) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 { return b.mem[addr&(uint32(len(b.mem))-1)] }
func (b *ramBus) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(b.Read8(addr)) | uint16(b.Read8(addr+1))<<8
}
func (b *ramBus) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(b.Read8(addr)) | uint32(b.Read8(addr+1))<<8 |
		uint32(b.Read8(addr+2))<<16 | uint32(b.Read8(addr+3))<<24
}
func (b *ramBus) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) { b.mem[addr&(uint32(len(b.mem))-1)] = v }
func (b *ramBus) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	b.Write8(addr, uint8(v))
	b.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
}
func (b *ramBus) Write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	b.Write8(addr, uint8(v))
	b.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
	b.Write8(addr+2, uint8(v>>16))
	b.Write8(addr+3, uint8(v>>24))
}
func (b *ramBus) load(base uint32, words []uint32) {
	for i, w := range words {
		b.Write32(base+4*uint32(i), w)
	}
}

// Register numbers used below.
const (
	zero = 0
	t0   = 8
	t1   = 9
	t2   = 10
	t3   = 11
	t4   = 12
	t5   = 13
	t6   = 14
	t7   = 15
	s0   = 16
	s1   = 17
	s2   = 18
	s3   = 19
	s4   = 20
	s5   = 21
	s6   = 22
	s7   = 23
	ra   = 31
)

func rI(op, rs, rt, imm uint32) uint32 { return op<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | (imm & 0xFFFF) }
func rR(rs, rt, rd, sh, fn uint32) uint32 {
	return rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | sh<<6 | fn
}
func rJ(op, target uint32) uint32 { return op<<26 | (target>>2)&0x03FFFFFF }
func cop0(rs, rt, rd uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x10<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11
}

const nop = 0

func newCPUAt(bus *ramBus, words []uint32, base uint32) *CPU {
	bus.load(base, words)
	c := New(bus)
	c.PC = base
	c.NextPC = base + 4
	return c
}

func stepN(c *CPU, n int) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
}

func TestArithmeticAndLogic(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 40),     // addiu t0, 40
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 2),      // addiu t1, 2
		rR(t0, t1, t2, 0, 0x21),    // addu t2 = 42
		rR(t0, t1, t3, 0, 0x23),    // subu t3 = 38
		rR(0, t1, t4, 3, 0x00),     // sll t4 = 16
		rR(0, t0, t5, 2, 0x02),     // srl t5 = 10
		rI(0x09, zero, t6, 0xFFF0), // addiu t6, -16
		rR(0, t6, t7, 2, 0x03),     // sra t7 = -4
		rR(t1, t0, s0, 0, 0x2A),    // slt s0 = 1
		rR(t0, t1, s1, 0, 0x2B),    // sltu s1 = 0
		rR(t0, t1, s2, 0, 0x24),    // and s2 = 0
		rR(t0, t1, s3, 0, 0x25),    // or s3 = 42
		rR(t0, t1, s4, 0, 0x26),    // xor s4 = 42
		rR(t0, t1, s5, 0, 0x27),    // nor s5 = ^42
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x18),     // mult
		rR(0, 0, s6, 0, 0x12),      // mflo s6 = 80
		rR(0, 0, s7, 0, 0x10),      // mfhi s7 = 0
		rI(0x0F, zero, s0, 0x12),   // lui s0, 0x12
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, len(words))
	want := map[uint32]uint32{
		t0: 40, t1: 2, t2: 42, t3: 38, t4: 16, t5: 10,
		t6: 0xFFFFFFF0, t7: 0xFFFFFFFC,
		s1: 0, s2: 0, s3: 42, s4: 42, s5: ^uint32(42),
		s6: 80, s7: 0, s0: 0x00120000,
	}
	for reg, v := range want {
		if c.Regs[reg] != v {
			t.Errorf("r%d = 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", reg, c.Regs[reg], v)
		}
	}
	if c.Regs[zero] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("r0 = 0x%08X, want 0", c.Regs[zero])
	}
}

func TestLoadDelayBasic(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.Write32(0x2000, 0xDEADBEEF)
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0x2000), // addiu t0, 0x2000
		rI(0x23, t0, t1, 0),        // lw t1, 0(t0)
		rR(t1, zero, t2, 0, 0x21),  // addu t2, t1 (delay slot: old value 0)
		rR(t1, zero, t3, 0, 0x21),  // addu t3, t1 (loaded value)
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 4)
	if c.Regs[t2] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("delay slot read t2 = 0x%08X, want 0", c.Regs[t2])
	}
	if c.Regs[t3] != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("post delay read t3 = 0x%08X, want 0xDEADBEEF", c.Regs[t3])
	}
}

func TestLoadDelayCancellationByWrite(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.Write32(0x2000, 0xDEADBEEF)
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0x2000),
		rI(0x23, t0, t1, 0),       // lw t1 (pending)
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 7),     // addiu t1, 7: writes t1, load is cancelled
		rR(t1, zero, t2, 0, 0x21), // addu t2 = 7
		rR(t1, zero, t3, 0, 0x21), // addu t3 = 7, the load never lands
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 5)
	if c.Regs[t2] != 7 || c.Regs[t3] != 7 {
		t.Errorf("t2=0x%08X t3=0x%08X, want 7 and 7 (load cancelled)", c.Regs[t2], c.Regs[t3])
	}
}

func TestLoadDelayBackToBackLoads(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.Write32(0x2000, 111)
	bus.Write32(0x2004, 222)
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0x2000),
		rI(0x23, t0, t1, 0),       // lw t1 = 111 (pending)
		rI(0x23, t0, t1, 4),       // lw t1 = 222 (delay slot load; does not cancel the first)
		rR(t1, zero, t2, 0, 0x21), // addu t2: reads the first load, 111
		rR(t1, zero, t3, 0, 0x21), // addu t3: reads the second load, 222
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 5)
	if c.Regs[t2] != 111 {
		t.Errorf("t2 = %d, want 111 (first of two back-to-back loads lands on schedule)", c.Regs[t2])
	}
	if c.Regs[t3] != 222 {
		t.Errorf("t3 = %d, want 222", c.Regs[t3])
	}
}

func TestBranchDelayAndJal(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	words := []uint32{
		rJ(0x03, 20),                 // 0: jal 20
		rI(0x09, zero, s0, 1),        // 1: delay slot
		rI(0x09, zero, s1, 2),        // 2: return address lands here
		rI(0x04, zero, zero, 0xFFFF), // 3: beq zero, zero, -1 (halt loop)
		nop,                          // 4
		rI(0x09, zero, s2, 3),        // 5: subroutine at byte 20
		rR(ra, 0, 0, 0, 0x08),        // 6: jr ra
		rI(0x09, zero, s3, 4),        // 7: jr delay slot
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0)
	stepN(c, 12)
	if c.Regs[ra] != 8 {
		t.Errorf("ra = 0x%X, want 8", c.Regs[ra])
	}
	for reg, v := range map[uint32]uint32{s0: 1, s1: 2, s2: 3, s3: 4} {
		if c.Regs[reg] != v {
			t.Errorf("r%d = %d, want %d", reg, c.Regs[reg], v)
		}
	}
}

func TestBranchAndLinkUnconditionalLink(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	// bltzal with a non-negative source is NOT taken,
	// but the R3000A writes the link register anyway.
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 5), // addiu t0, 5
		rI(0x01, t0, 0x10, 4), // bltzal t0, +4 words (not taken)
		nop,                   // delay slot
		rI(0x09, zero, s0, 1), // fall-through marker
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 4)
	if c.Regs[ra] != 0x100C {
		t.Errorf("ra = 0x%08X, want 0x100C (link written despite not-taken branch)", c.Regs[ra])
	}
	if c.Regs[s0] != 1 {
		t.Errorf("s0 = %d, want 1 (fell through)", c.Regs[s0])
	}
}

func TestUnalignedLoadStore(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.Write32(0x1000, 0x11223344)
	bus.Write32(0x1004, 0x55667788)
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0x1000), // base
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 0),      // t1 = 0
		rI(0x22, t0, t1, 4),        // lwl t1, 4(t0)
		rI(0x26, t0, t1, 1),        // lwr t1, 1(t0)
		nop,                        // load delay
		rR(t1, zero, t2, 0, 0x21),  // addu t2 = unaligned word at 0x1001
		rI(0x09, zero, t3, 0x2000), // dest base
		rI(0x2A, t3, t1, 4),        // swl t1, 4(t3)
		rI(0x2E, t3, t1, 1),        // swr t1, 1(t3)
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x4000)
	stepN(c, len(words))
	if c.Regs[t2] != 0x88112233 {
		t.Errorf("unaligned load = 0x%08X, want 0x88112233", c.Regs[t2])
	}
	for off, want := range map[uint32]uint8{0x2001: 0x33, 0x2002: 0x22, 0x2003: 0x11, 0x2004: 0x88} {
		if got := bus.Read8(off); got != want {
			t.Errorf("mem[0x%X] = 0x%02X, want 0x%02X", off, got, want)
		}
	}
	if bus.Read8(0x2000) != 0 || bus.Read8(0x2005) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("unaligned store touched bytes outside 0x2001-0x2004")
	}
}

func TestMultiplyDivideResults(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0xFFFA), // addiu t0, -6
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 7),
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x18), // mult: -42
		rR(0, 0, t2, 0, 0x12),  // mflo = -42
		rR(0, 0, t3, 0, 0x10),  // mfhi = -1
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 100),
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x1A), // div 100/7
		rR(0, 0, t4, 0, 0x12),  // mflo = 14
		rR(0, 0, t5, 0, 0x10),  // mfhi = 2
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 0),
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x1B),     // divu 100/0
		rR(0, 0, t6, 0, 0x12),      // mflo = 0xFFFFFFFF
		rR(0, 0, t7, 0, 0x10),      // mfhi = 100
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0xFFFB), // addiu t0, -5
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x1A),     // div -5/0
		rR(0, 0, s0, 0, 0x12),      // mflo = 1
		rR(0, 0, s1, 0, 0x10),      // mfhi = -5
		rI(0x0F, zero, t0, 0x8000), // t0 = 0x80000000
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 0xFFFF), // addiu t1, -1
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x1A),     // div INT_MIN/-1
		rR(0, 0, s2, 0, 0x12),      // mflo = 0x80000000
		rR(0, 0, s3, 0, 0x10),      // mfhi = 0
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, len(words))
	want := map[uint32]uint32{
		t2: 0xFFFFFFD6, t3: 0xFFFFFFFF, t4: 14, t5: 2,
		t6: 0xFFFFFFFF, t7: 100, s0: 1, s1: 0xFFFFFFFB,
		s2: 0x80000000, s3: 0,
	}
	for reg, v := range want {
		if c.Regs[reg] != v {
			t.Errorf("r%d = 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", reg, c.Regs[reg], v)
		}
	}
}

func TestHiLoStallTiming(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	// Immediate consumer stalls for the busy count.
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 6),
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 7),
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x18), // mult
		rR(0, 0, t2, 0, 0x12),  // mflo
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 3)
	if got := c.Step(); got != 1+multBusyCycles {
		t.Errorf("mflo right after mult charged %d cycles, want %d", got, 1+multBusyCycles)
	}
	if c.Regs[t2] != 42 {
		t.Errorf("mflo = %d, want 42", c.Regs[t2])
	}
	// Spaced consumer does not stall.
	bus2 := newRAMBus()
	spaced := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 6),
		rI(0x09, zero, t1, 7),
		rR(t0, t1, 0, 0, 0x18), // mult
	}
	for i := 0; i < multBusyCycles; i++ {
		spaced = append(spaced, nop)
	}
	spaced = append(spaced, rR(0, 0, t2, 0, 0x12)) // mflo
	c3 := newCPUAt(bus2, spaced, 0x1000)
	stepN(c3, len(spaced)-1)
	if got := c3.Step(); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("mflo after %d spacing instructions charged %d cycles, want 1", multBusyCycles, got)
	}
}

func TestOverflowException(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x0F, zero, t0, 0x7FFF), // lui t0, 0x7FFF
		rI(0x0D, t0, t0, 0xFFFF),   // ori t0, 0xFFFF -> 0x7FFFFFFF
		rI(0x08, t0, t1, 1),        // addi t1, t0, 1 -> overflow
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 3)
	if c.PC != generalVectorBEV {
		t.Errorf("PC = 0x%08X, want exception vector 0x%08X", c.PC, uint32(generalVectorBEV))
	}
	if c.EPC != 0x1008 {
		t.Errorf("EPC = 0x%08X, want 0x1008", c.EPC)
	}
	if code := (c.Cause >> 2) & 0x1F; code != ExcOv {
		t.Errorf("ExcCode = %d, want %d (overflow)", code, ExcOv)
	}
	if c.Regs[t1] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("t1 = 0x%08X, want 0 (faulting instruction has no effect)", c.Regs[t1])
	}
}

func TestSyscallAndInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	c := newCPUAt(bus, []uint32{rR(0, 0, 0, 0, 0x0C)}, 0x1000)
	c.Step()
	if code := (c.Cause >> 2) & 0x1F; code != ExcSys {
		t.Errorf("syscall ExcCode = %d, want %d", code, ExcSys)
	}
	if c.EPC != 0x1000 || c.PC != generalVectorBEV {
		t.Errorf("syscall EPC/PC = 0x%08X/0x%08X, want 0x1000/0x%08X", c.EPC, c.PC, uint32(generalVectorBEV))
	}

	bus2 := newRAMBus()
	c2 := newCPUAt(bus2, []uint32{rI(0x09, zero, t0, 1)}, 0x1000)
	c2.SR = 0x00000401 // IEc + IM for IP2
	c2.SetInterrupt(true)
	c2.Step()
	if c2.Regs[t0] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt taken after the instruction ran; t0 = %d, want 0", c2.Regs[t0])
	}
	if c2.EPC != 0x1000 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt EPC = 0x%08X, want 0x1000", c2.EPC)
	}
	if code := (c2.Cause >> 2) & 0x1F; code != ExcInt {
		t.Errorf("interrupt ExcCode = %d, want 0", code)
	}
}

func TestMFC0LoadDelay(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 1),     // addiu t0, 1
		cop0(0x04, t0, cp0SR),     // mtc0 t0, SR
		cop0(0x00, t1, cp0SR),     // mfc0 t1, SR (delayed)
		rR(t1, zero, t2, 0, 0x21), // addu t2: old t1 = 0
		rR(t1, zero, t3, 0, 0x21), // addu t3: SR = 1
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 5)
	if c.Regs[t2] != 0 || c.Regs[t3] != 1 {
		t.Errorf("t2=%d t3=%d, want 0 and 1 (mfc0 has a load delay)", c.Regs[t2], c.Regs[t3])
	}
	if got := c.readCP0(cp0PRId); got != 0x00000002 {
		t.Errorf("PRId = 0x%08X, want 0x00000002", got)
	}
}

func TestCacheIsolation(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0x2000), // base
		rI(0x0F, zero, t1, 0xCAFE), // lui
		rI(0x0D, t1, t1, 0xBABE),   // ori -> 0xCAFEBABE
		rI(0x2B, t0, t1, 0),        // sw
		rI(0x23, t0, t2, 0),        // lw
		nop,
		rR(t2, zero, t3, 0, 0x21), // addu t3
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	c.SR = 0x00010000 // Isc: isolate the data cache
	stepN(c, len(words))
	if c.Regs[t3] != 0xCAFEBABE {
		t.Errorf("isolated load = 0x%08X, want 0xCAFEBABE", c.Regs[t3])
	}
	if bus.Read32(0x2000) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("isolated store leaked to the bus: mem = 0x%08X", bus.Read32(0x2000))
	}
	// A second CPU without isolation sees the (empty) bus.
	c2 := newCPUAt(bus, []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0x2000),
		rI(0x23, t0, t2, 0),
		nop,
		rR(t2, zero, t3, 0, 0x21),
	}, 0x1000)
	stepN(c2, 4)
	if c2.Regs[t3] != 0 {
		t.Errorf("non-isolated load = 0x%08X, want 0", c2.Regs[t3])
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTripWithPendingLoad(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.Write32(0x2000, 0x12345678)
	words := []uint32{
		rI(0x09, zero, t0, 0x2000),
		rI(0x23, t0, t1, 0),       // lw t1 (pending at save time)
		rR(t1, zero, t2, 0, 0x21), // addu t2 (delay slot)
		rR(t1, zero, t3, 0, 0x21), // addu t3 (loaded value)
	}
	c := newCPUAt(bus, words, 0x1000)
	stepN(c, 2) // the load is now pending, not yet landed
	state := c.Serialize()
	if len(state) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(state), StateSize)
	}
	c2 := New(bus)
	if err := c2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	stepN(c, 2)
	stepN(c2, 2)
	if c.Regs != c2.Regs {
		t.Errorf("registers diverged after restore: %v vs %v", c.Regs, c2.Regs)
	}
	if c2.Regs[t3] != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("restored pending load produced t3 = 0x%08X, want 0x12345678", c2.Regs[t3])
	}
	if err := c2.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("short state accepted, want error")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/dma/dma.go ====================

// Package dma implements the PlayStation DMA
// controller from the psx-spx DMA documentation:
// seven channels (0 MDEC-in, 1 MDEC-out, 2 GPU,
// 3 CDROM, 4 SPU, 5 PIO, 6 OTC), the DPCR control
// register and the DICR interrupt register.
//
// Channel registers live at 0x1F801080 + n*0x10:
// MADR (base address), BCR (block control), CHCR
// (channel control). CHCR bits used here:
//
//	bit 0      transfer direction (0 = device to
//	           RAM, 1 = RAM to device)
//	bit 1      address step (0 = +4, 1 = -4)
//	bit 2      chopping enable
//	bits 9-10  sync mode (0 = all at once on start,
//	           1 = in blocks on request/trigger,
//	           2 = linked list)
//	bits 16-18 chopping DMA window size (2^n words)
//	bits 20-22 chopping CPU window size
//	bit 24     start/busy
//	bit 25     start/trigger for sync mode 1
//
// Transfers complete inside the call that starts
// them: this core has no DMA timing model (PS1-2
// states this in the core README). Chopping is
// honored structurally: a chopped transfer runs in
// bursts of the programmed DMA window size with the
// CPU windows in between, but because execution is
// immediate the moved data is identical; only the
// burst count is observable, through BurstCount.
//
// DICR follows the documentation precisely: channel
// IRQ flags (bits 24-30) are set on completion ONLY
// when the channel's IRQ enable (bits 16-22) is set;
// bit 15 is the bus error flag; bit 31 reads as
// b15 OR (master enable b23 AND any enabled flag);
// on the 0-to-1 transition of bit 31 the OnIRQ
// callback fires (the system latches I_STAT IRQ3).
// Flags are acknowledged by writing 1s to them.
package dma

// Channel indices in hardware order.
const (
	ChMDECIn  = 0
	ChMDECOut = 1
	ChGPU     = 2
	ChCDROM   = 3
	ChSPU     = 4
	ChPIO     = 5
	ChOTC     = 6

	Channels = 7
)

// Memory is the DMA engine's view of main memory
// (the system bus; DMA does not pass through CPU
// cache isolation).
type Memory interface {
	Read32(addr uint32) uint32
	Write32(addr uint32, v uint32)
}

// Devices are the channel endpoints. GP0Write feeds
// a word to the GPU command port and GPURead pulls
// a word from GPUREAD. CDReadWord pulls the next
// word from the CD data FIFO (ok=false when the
// FIFO cannot supply one). SPUReadWord/SPUWriteWord
// go through the SPU transfer port. MDECInWrite
// sinks a word into the MDEC stub and MDECOutRead
// sources one; the codec itself is PS1-3.
type Devices interface {
	GP0Write(w uint32)
	GPURead() uint32
	CDReadWord() (uint32, bool)
	SPUReadWord() uint32
	SPUWriteWord(w uint32)
	MDECInWrite(w uint32)
	MDECOutRead() uint32
}

// Channel holds one channel's registers.
type Channel struct {
	MADR uint32
	BCR  uint32
	CHCR uint32

	bursts int // bursts used by the last transfer
}

// Controller is the DMA controller.
type Controller struct {
	Ch   [Channels]Channel
	DPCR uint32

	dicrLow   uint32 // bits 0-14 (stored)
	forceIRQ  bool   // bit 15 (bus error flag storage name in docs: force/bus-error)
	irqEnable uint32 // bits 16-22
	masterEn  bool   // bit 23
	irqFlags  uint32 // bits 24-30
	irqLine   bool   // computed bit 31

	Mem Memory
	Dev Devices

	// OnIRQ fires on the 0-to-1 transition of the
	// DICR master flag (bit 31).
	OnIRQ func()
}

// New returns a controller in reset state: DPCR
// holds its documented reset value 0x07654321 and
// DICR is clear.
func New() *Controller {
	c := &Controller{}
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Reset restores the reset register values.
func (c *Controller) Reset() {
	c.Ch = [Channels]Channel{}
	c.DPCR = 0x07654321
	c.dicrLow = 0
	c.forceIRQ = false
	c.irqEnable = 0
	c.masterEn = false
	c.irqFlags = 0
	c.irqLine = false
}

// DICR returns the interrupt register as read by
// the CPU.
func (c *Controller) DICR() uint32 {
	v := c.dicrLow | (c.irqEnable << 16) | (c.irqFlags << 24)
	if c.forceIRQ {
		v |= 1 << 15
	}
	if c.masterEn {
		v |= 1 << 23
	}
	if c.irqLine {
		v |= 1 << 31
	}
	return v
}

// WriteDICR stores a CPU write to DICR: control
// bits are stored, flag bits written as 1 are
// acknowledged (cleared).
func (c *Controller) WriteDICR(v uint32) {
	c.dicrLow = v & 0x3FFF
	c.forceIRQ = v&(1<<15) != 0
	c.irqEnable = (v >> 16) & 0x7F
	c.masterEn = v&(1<<23) != 0
	ack := (v >> 24) & 0x7F
	c.irqFlags &^= ack
	c.updateLine()
}

func (c *Controller) updateLine() {
	line := c.forceIRQ || (c.masterEn && (c.irqFlags&c.irqEnable) != 0)
	if line && !c.irqLine && c.OnIRQ != nil {
		c.OnIRQ()
	}
	c.irqLine = line
}

// IRQLine returns the current DICR bit 31 value.
func (c *Controller) IRQLine() bool { return c.irqLine }

// ReadReg reads a DMA register by physical address
// (0x1F801080-0x1F8010FF).
func (c *Controller) ReadReg(addr uint32) uint32 {
	if addr == 0x1F8010F0 {
		return c.DPCR
	}
	if addr == 0x1F8010F4 {
		return c.DICR()
	}
	n, off := channelAddr(addr)
	if n < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	switch off {
	case 0:
		return c.Ch[n].MADR
	case 4:
		return c.Ch[n].BCR
	case 8:
		return c.Ch[n].CHCR
	}
	return 0
}

// WriteReg writes a DMA register; writing CHCR can
// start a transfer.
func (c *Controller) WriteReg(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	if addr == 0x1F8010F0 {
		c.DPCR = v
		return
	}
	if addr == 0x1F8010F4 {
		c.WriteDICR(v)
		return
	}
	n, off := channelAddr(addr)
	if n < 0 {
		return
	}
	switch off {
	case 0:
		c.Ch[n].MADR = v & 0x00FFFFFF
	case 4:
		c.Ch[n].BCR = v
	case 8:
		if n == ChOTC {
			// OTC CHCR has only bits 24, 28 and 30
			// writable; bit 1 (backward step) always
			// reads 1 and the rest read 0.
			c.Ch[n].CHCR = v & (1<<24 | 1<<28 | 1<<30)
		} else {
			c.Ch[n].CHCR = v
		}
		c.maybeStart(n)
	}
}

func channelAddr(addr uint32) (int, uint32) {
	if addr < 0x1F801080 || addr > 0x1F8010EC {
		return -1, 0
	}
	off := addr - 0x1F801080
	return int(off >> 4), off & 0xC
}

// channelEnabled reports the DPCR master enable for
// a channel (bit 3 of its nibble).
func (c *Controller) channelEnabled(n int) bool {
	return c.DPCR&(1<<uint(4*n+3)) != 0
}

// maybeStart runs a transfer if the CHCR write
// armed one and the channel is enabled in DPCR.
func (c *Controller) maybeStart(n int) {
	ch := &c.Ch[n]
	if ch.CHCR&(1<<24) == 0 || !c.channelEnabled(n) {
		return
	}
	sync := (ch.CHCR >> 9) & 3
	if n == ChOTC {
		c.runOTC(n)
		c.complete(n)
		return
	}
	switch sync {
	case 0:
		c.runBlock(n, c.sync0Words(n))
		c.complete(n)
	case 1:
		if ch.CHCR&(1<<25) == 0 {
			return // armed, waiting for the trigger bit
		}
		ch.CHCR &^= 1 << 25
		bs := int(ch.BCR & 0xFFFF)
		if bs == 0 {
			bs = 0x10000
		}
		bc := int(ch.BCR >> 16)
		if bc == 0 {
			bc = 1
		}
		c.runBlock(n, bs*bc)
		c.complete(n)
	case 2:
		if n == ChGPU {
			c.runLinkedList(n)
			c.complete(n)
		}
	}
}

// sync0Words is the sync mode 0 word count: the low
// halfword of BCR, with 0 meaning 0x10000.
func (c *Controller) sync0Words(n int) int {
	w := int(c.Ch[n].BCR & 0xFFFF)
	if w == 0 {
		w = 0x10000
	}
	return w
}

// complete finishes a channel: busy clears and the
// DICR flag is set if the channel IRQ is enabled
// (the documented rule: flags set only when
// enabled).
func (c *Controller) complete(n int) {
	c.Ch[n].CHCR &^= 1 << 24
	if c.irqEnable&(1<<uint(n)) != 0 {
		c.irqFlags |= 1 << uint(n)
	}
	c.updateLine()
}

// transferWord moves one word between memory at
// addr and channel n's device, honoring CHCR
// direction (bit 0: 1 = RAM to device).
func (c *Controller) transferWord(n int, addr uint32) {
	fromRAM := c.Ch[n].CHCR&1 != 0
	switch n {
	case ChGPU:
		if fromRAM {
			c.Dev.GP0Write(c.Mem.Read32(addr))
		} else {
			c.Mem.Write32(addr, c.Dev.GPURead())
		}
	case ChCDROM:
		if fromRAM {
			_ = c.Mem.Read32(addr) // CD has no data-in path in this subset; words are dropped
		} else {
			w, ok := c.Dev.CDReadWord()
			if !ok {
				w = 0 // FIFO dry: hardware would stall; we pad (see README)
			}
			c.Mem.Write32(addr, w)
		}
	case ChSPU:
		if fromRAM {
			c.Dev.SPUWriteWord(c.Mem.Read32(addr))
		} else {
			c.Mem.Write32(addr, c.Dev.SPUReadWord())
		}
	case ChMDECIn:
		if fromRAM {
			c.Dev.MDECInWrite(c.Mem.Read32(addr))
		}
	case ChMDECOut:
		if !fromRAM {
			c.Mem.Write32(addr, c.Dev.MDECOutRead())
		}
	case ChPIO:
		if fromRAM {
			_ = c.Mem.Read32(addr) // PIO unused: sink
		} else {
			c.Mem.Write32(addr, 0)
		}
	}
}

// runBlock moves words words for channel n from its
// MADR with the programmed address step, in bursts
// when chopping is enabled.
func (c *Controller) runBlock(n int, words int) {
	ch := &c.Ch[n]
	step := int32(4)
	if ch.CHCR&0x2 != 0 {
		step = -4
	}
	burst := words
	if ch.CHCR&0x4 != 0 {
		burst = 1 << ((ch.CHCR >> 16) & 7)
	}
	ch.bursts = 0
	addr := ch.MADR
	done := 0
	for done < words {
		nb := burst
		if nb > words-done {
			nb = words - done
		}
		for i := 0; i < nb; i++ {
			c.transferWord(n, addr)
			addr = uint32(int32(addr) + step)
			done++
		}
		ch.bursts++
	}
	ch.MADR = addr & 0x00FFFFFF
}

// runLinkedList executes a GPU linked list: each
// node starts with a header word (top byte = number
// of data words that follow, low 24 bits = address
// of the next node); the list ends when the next
// address is 0xFFFFFF. A generous node cap guards
// against corrupt lists looping forever.
func (c *Controller) runLinkedList(n int) {
	ch := &c.Ch[n]
	addr := ch.MADR
	for nodes := 0; nodes < (1 << 20); nodes++ {
		header := c.Mem.Read32(addr)
		count := int(header >> 24)
		next := header & 0x00FFFFFF
		for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
			addr += 4
			c.Dev.GP0Write(c.Mem.Read32(addr))
		}
		if next == 0x00FFFFFF {
			break
		}
		addr = next
	}
	ch.MADR = addr & 0x00FFFFFF
}

// runOTC builds the ordering table for channel 6:
// BCR holds the entry count; starting at MADR (the
// LAST entry) and stepping down, each entry receives
// the address of the previous entry, and the first
// (lowest) entry receives the terminator 0x00FFFFFF.
// This reproduces the documented DMA6 example table
// word for word.
func (c *Controller) runOTC(n int) {
	ch := &c.Ch[n]
	count := int(ch.BCR & 0xFFFF)
	if count == 0 {
		count = int(ch.BCR >> 16)
	}
	addr := ch.MADR
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		var v uint32
		if i == count-1 {
			v = 0x00FFFFFF
		} else {
			v = (addr - 4) & 0x00FFFFFF
		}
		c.Mem.Write32(addr, v)
		addr -= 4
	}
	ch.MADR = addr & 0x00FFFFFF
}

// BurstCount reports how many bursts the channel's
// last transfer used (1 unless chopping split it).
func (c *Controller) BurstCount(n int) int { return c.Ch[n].bursts }

// StateSize is the serialized controller size.
const StateSize = Channels*16 + 16

// Serialize writes the controller state.
func (c *Controller) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	for i := range c.Ch {
		o := out[i*16:]
		put32(o[0:], c.Ch[i].MADR)
		put32(o[4:], c.Ch[i].BCR)
		put32(o[8:], c.Ch[i].CHCR)
	}
	o := out[Channels*16:]
	put32(o[0:], c.DPCR)
	put32(o[4:], c.DICR())
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (c *Controller) Deserialize(in []byte) {
	for i := range c.Ch {
		o := in[i*16:]
		c.Ch[i].MADR = get32(o[0:])
		c.Ch[i].BCR = get32(o[4:])
		c.Ch[i].CHCR = get32(o[8:])
		c.Ch[i].bursts = 0
	}
	o := in[Channels*16:]
	c.DPCR = get32(o[0:])
	dicr := get32(o[4:])
	c.dicrLow = dicr & 0x3FFF
	c.forceIRQ = dicr&(1<<15) != 0
	c.irqEnable = (dicr >> 16) & 0x7F
	c.masterEn = dicr&(1<<23) != 0
	c.irqFlags = (dicr >> 24) & 0x7F
	c.irqLine = dicr&(1<<31) != 0
}

func put32(b []byte, v uint32) {
	b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3] = byte(v), byte(v>>8), byte(v>>16), byte(v>>24)
}
func get32(b []byte) uint32 {
	return uint32(b[0]) | uint32(b[1])<<8 | uint32(b[2])<<16 | uint32(b[3])<<24
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/dma/dma_test.go ====================

package dma

import "testing"

type fakeMem struct{ m map[uint32]uint32 }

func newFakeMem() *fakeMem                    { return &fakeMem{m: map[uint32]uint32{}} }
func (f *fakeMem) Read32(a uint32) uint32     { return f.m[a] }
func (f *fakeMem) Write32(a uint32, v uint32) { f.m[a] = v }

type fakeDev struct {
	gp0     []uint32
	gpuRead []uint32
	cdWords []uint32
	spuIn   []uint32
	spuOut  []uint32
	spuIdx  int
	mdecIn  []uint32
}

func (d *fakeDev) GP0Write(w uint32) { d.gp0 = append(d.gp0, w) }
func (d *fakeDev) GPURead() uint32 {
	if len(d.gpuRead) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	v := d.gpuRead[0]
	d.gpuRead = d.gpuRead[1:]
	return v
}
func (d *fakeDev) CDReadWord() (uint32, bool) {
	if len(d.cdWords) == 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	v := d.cdWords[0]
	d.cdWords = d.cdWords[1:]
	return v, true
}
func (d *fakeDev) SPUReadWord() uint32 {
	if d.spuIdx >= len(d.spuOut) {
		return 0
	}
	v := d.spuOut[d.spuIdx]
	d.spuIdx++
	return v
}
func (d *fakeDev) SPUWriteWord(w uint32) { d.spuIn = append(d.spuIn, w) }
func (d *fakeDev) MDECInWrite(w uint32)  { d.mdecIn = append(d.mdecIn, w) }
func (d *fakeDev) MDECOutRead() uint32   { return 0xABCD0000 }

func newRig() (*Controller, *fakeMem, *fakeDev) {
	c := New()
	m := newFakeMem()
	d := &fakeDev{}
	c.Mem = m
	c.Dev = d
	return c, m, d
}

func TestSync0RAMtoGPU(t *testing.T) {
	c, m, d := newRig()
	m.m[0x1000] = 0x11223344
	m.m[0x1004] = 0x55667788
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800) // enable ch2 (nibble bit 3 at 4*2+3=11)
	if c.DPCR != 0x0800 {
		t.Fatalf("DPCR = 0x%08X", c.DPCR)
	}
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A0, 0x1000)     // MADR
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A4, 2)          // BCR: 2 words
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000001) // dir from RAM, sync 0, start
	if len(d.gp0) != 2 || d.gp0[0] != 0x11223344 || d.gp0[1] != 0x55667788 {
		t.Errorf("gp0 words = %v", d.gp0)
	}
	if got := c.ReadReg(0x1F8010A8); got&(1<<24) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("CHCR busy bit still set: 0x%08X", got)
	}
	if c.ReadReg(0x1F8010A0) != 0x1008 {
		t.Errorf("MADR after = 0x%X, want 0x1008", c.ReadReg(0x1F8010A0))
	}
}

func TestLinkedListThreeNodes(t *testing.T) {
	c, m, d := newRig()
	// Node A at 0x2000: 2 words, next 0x2100.
	m.m[0x2000] = 0x02002100
	m.m[0x2004] = 0xAAAA0001
	m.m[0x2008] = 0xAAAA0002
	// Node B at 0x2100: 1 word, next 0x2200.
	m.m[0x2100] = 0x01002200
	m.m[0x2104] = 0xBBBB0001
	// Node C at 0x2200: 3 words, terminator.
	m.m[0x2200] = 0x03FFFFFF
	m.m[0x2204] = 0xCCCC0001
	m.m[0x2208] = 0xCCCC0002
	m.m[0x220C] = 0xCCCC0003
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A0, 0x2000)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000401) // sync 2, from RAM, start
	want := []uint32{0xAAAA0001, 0xAAAA0002, 0xBBBB0001, 0xCCCC0001, 0xCCCC0002, 0xCCCC0003}
	if len(d.gp0) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("gp0 = %v, want %v", d.gp0, want)
	}
	for i := range want {
		if d.gp0[i] != want[i] {
			t.Errorf("gp0[%d] = 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", i, d.gp0[i], want[i])
		}
	}
}

func TestOTCBuildsDocumentedTable(t *testing.T) {
	c, m, _ := newRig()
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010F0, 0x8000000) // enable ch6 (bit 4*6+3 = 27)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010E0, 0x12300C)  // MADR = last entry
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010E4, 4)         // BCR = 4 entries
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010E8, 0x01000000)
	want := map[uint32]uint32{
		0x123000: 0x00FFFFFF,
		0x123004: 0x00123000,
		0x123008: 0x00123004,
		0x12300C: 0x00123008,
	}
	for a, v := range want {
		if m.m[a] != v {
			t.Errorf("table[0x%X] = 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", a, m.m[a], v)
		}
	}
}

func TestDICRFlagRuleAndInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	c, m, _ := newRig()
	m.m[0x4000] = 0x99
	irqs := 0
	c.OnIRQ = func() { irqs++ }
	// Completion WITHOUT the channel IRQ enable must
	// not raise the flag (documented rule).
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A0, 0x4000)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A4, 1)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000001)
	if c.DICR()&(1<<26) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("DICR flag set without enable: 0x%08X", c.DICR())
	}
	if irqs != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("irq fired without enable")
	}
	// Enable ch2 IRQ + master; transfer again.
	c.WriteDICR(1<<18 | 1<<23)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A0, 0x4000)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A4, 1)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000001)
	d := c.DICR()
	if d&(1<<26) == 0 || d&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("DICR = 0x%08X, want flag bit 26 and master bit 31 set", d)
	}
	if irqs != 1 {
		t.Errorf("irq callbacks = %d, want 1", irqs)
	}
	// Acknowledge by writing 1 to the flag bit.
	c.WriteDICR(1<<18 | 1<<23 | 1<<26)
	if c.DICR()&(1<<31) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("DICR master still set after ack: 0x%08X", c.DICR())
	}
}

func TestCDROMChannelPullsFIFO(t *testing.T) {
	c, m, d := newRig()
	d.cdWords = []uint32{0x11111111, 0x22222222}
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010F0, 0x8000) // enable ch3 (bit 15)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010B0, 0x8000)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010B4, 2)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010B8, 0x01000000) // to RAM, sync 0, start
	if m.m[0x8000] != 0x11111111 || m.m[0x8004] != 0x22222222 {
		t.Errorf("RAM got 0x%08X 0x%08X", m.m[0x8000], m.m[0x8004])
	}
}

func TestSync1NeedsTriggerBit(t *testing.T) {
	c, m, d := newRig()
	m.m[0x3000] = 0x77
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A0, 0x3000)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A4, 0x00010001) // block size 1, count 1
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000201) // sync 1, start, NO trigger
	if len(d.gp0) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("sync mode 1 moved data without the trigger bit")
	}
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A8, 0x03000201) // now with trigger bit 25
	if len(d.gp0) != 1 || d.gp0[0] != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("gp0 = %v after trigger", d.gp0)
	}
}

func TestChoppingBursts(t *testing.T) {
	c, m, _ := newRig()
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		m.m[0x5000+uint32(4*i)] = uint32(i)
	}
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A0, 0x5000)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A4, 16)
	// Chopping on, DMA window 2^2 = 4 words.
	c.WriteReg(0x1F8010A8, 0x01020005)
	if got := c.BurstCount(2); got != 4 {
		t.Errorf("bursts = %d, want 4", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	c, _, _ := newRig()
	c.WriteDICR(1<<18 | 1<<23)
	c.Ch[2].MADR = 0x1234
	s := c.Serialize()
	c2 := New()
	c2.Deserialize(s)
	if c2.DICR() != c.DICR() || c2.Ch[2].MADR != 0x1234 || c2.DPCR != c.DPCR {
		t.Errorf("DMA state diverged after round trip")
	}
}

// Package gpu implements the PlayStation GPU from
// the psx-spx GPU documentation: the GP0/GP1 command
// interface, the 1024x512 16-bit VRAM, immediate-mode
// software rasterization of every documented drawing
// primitive, semi-transparency, texture mapping with
// CLUT lookup, dithering, and conversion of the
// display area to an XRGB8888 framebuffer at the
// native display resolution.
//
// Rendering model (stated in the core README):
// commands render immediately in WriteGP0 order;
// there is no command FIFO delay or polygon timing
// model in this slice. The line walker is a standard
// integer Bresenham; psx-spx names the endpoints-
// inclusive behavior but does not pin the walker's
// subpixel phase, so exact mid-line pixel choice on
// near-diagonal lines is the one documented
// under-specification carried by this package.
// Everything else (scan conversion, edge exclusion,
// blending arithmetic, dither matrix, transfer
// parameter masking) follows the documentation as
// written.
package gpu

// VRAM dimensions in 16-bit entries.
const (
	VRAMWidth  = 1024
	VRAMHeight = 512
)

// Display size limits: width is one of 256, 320,
// 368, 512 or 640 by display mode; height is 240 or
// 480 (interlaced).
const (
	MaxWidth  = 640
	MaxHeight = 480
)

// ditherTable is the documented 4x4 dither matrix,
// indexed [y&3][x&3], added to 8-bit color channels
// before quantization to 5 bits.
var ditherTable = [4][4]int{
	{-4, 0, -3, 1},
	{2, -2, 3, -1},
	{-3, 1, -4, 0},
	{3, -1, 2, -2},
}

// texPage holds a texture page attribute set (from
// GP0(E1) or from a textured primitive's own texpage
// word).
type texPage struct {
	xBase    int // in halfwords: bits 0-3 times 64
	yBase    int // 0 or 256 (plus the 2 MB VRAM bit, ignored)
	semiMode int // bits 5-6 of E1
	colorFmt int // 0=4bit, 1=8bit, 2=15bit
}

// GPU is the graphics processor state.
type GPU struct {
	vram [VRAMWidth * VRAMHeight]uint16

	// Draw mode (GP0 E1) and environment.
	page       texPage
	dither     bool
	drawToDisp bool
	texDisable bool
	rectFlipX  bool
	rectFlipY  bool
	winMaskX   int
	winMaskY   int
	winOffX    int
	winOffY    int
	drawX1     int
	drawY1     int
	drawX2     int
	drawY2     int
	offX       int
	offY       int
	maskSet    bool
	maskCheck  bool
	texWindow  uint32 // raw E2 value, for GP1(10)

	// Display state (GP1).
	dispEnable bool
	dmaDir     int
	dispX      int
	dispY      int
	rangeX1    int
	rangeX2    int
	rangeY1    int
	rangeY2    int
	hres2      bool
	hres1      int
	vres480    bool
	pal        bool
	depth24    bool
	interlace  bool
	reverse    bool

	// Beam state, fed by the system timing model:
	// drives GPUSTAT bits 13 (field) and 31
	// (drawing odd lines).
	Field    int
	LineOdd  bool
	OddFrame bool // 480i frame parity: the field on display

	irq       bool // GPUSTAT bit 24
	readLatch uint32

	// Host-side diagnostic: GP1 command bytes with
	// no implemented case, kept across resets, never
	// serialized. (GP0 has no unknown commands: every
	// opcode byte names a documented command class.)
	unknownGP1  []uint8
	unknownGP1N int

	// GP0 command assembly.
	buf     [20]uint32
	bufLen  int
	bufNeed int
	cmd     uint8

	// Polyline capture.
	polyline    bool
	polyGouraud bool
	polyStage   int // 0 = group start word, 1 = vertex after a gouraud color
	polyPrevX   int
	polyPrevY   int
	polyPrevC   [3]int
	polyColor   [3]int

	// VRAM transfer state.
	xferActive bool
	xferRead   bool // true: VRAM to CPU
	xferX      int
	xferY      int
	xferW      int
	xferH      int
	xferCol    int
	xferRow    int
	xferHalf   bool   // low halfword of the current word consumed
	xferPend   uint16 // pending low halfword for CPU to VRAM writes
	xferHasLo  bool

	displayBuf []uint32
}

// New returns a GPU in its power-on state (the
// documented GP1(00) reset defaults).
func New() *GPU {
	g := &GPU{}
	g.Reset()
	return g
}

// Reset applies the documented GP1(00) reset
// defaults: display off, DMA off, display area at 0,
// horizontal range 0x200 to 0xC00, vertical range
// 0x10 to 0x100, display mode 0, and all GP0
// environment registers cleared. GPUSTAT then reads
// 0x14802000. VRAM contents are preserved, as on
// hardware.
func (g *GPU) Reset() {
	vram := g.vram
	unk, unkN := g.unknownGP1, g.unknownGP1N
	*g = GPU{vram: vram, unknownGP1: unk, unknownGP1N: unkN}
	g.dispEnable = false
	g.rangeX1 = 0x200
	g.rangeX2 = 0x200 + 256*10
	g.rangeY1 = 0x010
	g.rangeY2 = 0x010 + 240
	g.displayBuf = make([]uint32, MaxWidth*MaxHeight)
}

// VRAM exposes the framebuffer memory (row major,
// VRAMWidth entries per row).
func (g *GPU) VRAM() []uint16 { return g.vram[:] }

// VRAMAt reads one VRAM entry (coordinates wrap).
func (g *GPU) VRAMAt(x, y int) uint16 {
	return g.vram[(y&(VRAMHeight-1))*VRAMWidth+(x&(VRAMWidth-1))]
}

// SetVRAM writes one VRAM entry directly (test and
// transfer helper; coordinates wrap).
func (g *GPU) SetVRAM(x, y int, v uint16) {
	g.vram[(y&(VRAMHeight-1))*VRAMWidth+(x&(VRAMWidth-1))] = v
}

// IRQRequested reports GPUSTAT bit 24.
func (g *GPU) IRQRequested() bool { return g.irq }

// DisplayEnabled reports whether the display is on.
func (g *GPU) DisplayEnabled() bool { return g.dispEnable }

// PAL reports the display mode video standard.
func (g *GPU) PAL() bool { return g.pal }

// DisplayWidth returns the native horizontal
// resolution from the display mode.
func (g *GPU) DisplayWidth() int {
	if g.hres2 {
		return 368
	}
	switch g.hres1 {
	case 0:
		return 256
	case 1:
		return 320
	case 2:
		return 512
	default:
		return 640
	}
}

// DotDivider is the video clock divider producing
// the dotclock for the current horizontal
// resolution (256: /10, 320: /8, 368: /7, 512: /5,
// 640: /4).
func (g *GPU) DotDivider() int {
	switch g.DisplayWidth() {
	case 256:
		return 10
	case 320:
		return 8
	case 368:
		return 7
	case 512:
		return 5
	default:
		return 4
	}
}

// DisplayHeight returns 480 in interlaced vertical
// 480 mode, else 240.
func (g *GPU) DisplayHeight() int {
	if g.vres480 && g.interlace {
		return 480
	}
	return 240
}

// HDisplayRange returns the horizontal display range
// in video clock units (for the system timing model).
func (g *GPU) HDisplayRange() (int, int) { return g.rangeX1, g.rangeX2 }

// VDisplayRange returns the vertical display range
// in scanlines.
func (g *GPU) VDisplayRange() (int, int) { return g.rangeY1, g.rangeY2 }

// DisplayAreaStart returns the display area origin
// in VRAM halfwords/lines.
func (g *GPU) DisplayAreaStart() (int, int) { return g.dispX, g.dispY }

// Status builds GPUSTAT.
func (g *GPU) Status() uint32 {
	var s uint32
	s |= uint32(g.page.xBase/64) & 0xF
	if g.page.yBase&256 != 0 {
		s |= 1 << 4
	}
	s |= uint32(g.page.semiMode&3) << 5
	s |= uint32(g.page.colorFmt&3) << 7
	if g.dither {
		s |= 1 << 9
	}
	if g.drawToDisp {
		s |= 1 << 10
	}
	if g.maskSet {
		s |= 1 << 11
	}
	if g.maskCheck {
		s |= 1 << 12
	}
	// Bit 13: interlace field; on this GPU version it
	// reads 1 when interlace is off.
	if !g.interlace || g.Field == 1 {
		s |= 1 << 13
	}
	if g.reverse {
		s |= 1 << 14
	}
	if g.page.yBase&512 != 0 {
		s |= 1 << 15
	}
	if g.hres2 {
		s |= 1 << 16
	}
	s |= uint32(g.hres1&3) << 17
	if g.vres480 {
		s |= 1 << 19
	}
	if g.pal {
		s |= 1 << 20
	}
	if g.depth24 {
		s |= 1 << 21
	}
	if g.interlace {
		s |= 1 << 22
	}
	if !g.dispEnable {
		s |= 1 << 23
	}
	if g.irq {
		s |= 1 << 24
	}
	// Ready bits in the immediate model: the GPU is
	// ready to receive commands and DMA blocks unless
	// a VRAM to CPU transfer is pending readback
	// (bit 27 is set exactly while it is).
	pendingRead := g.xferActive && g.xferRead
	readyCmd := !pendingRead
	readyDMA := readyCmd
	if pendingRead {
		s |= 1 << 27
	}
	if readyCmd {
		s |= 1 << 26
	}
	if readyDMA {
		s |= 1 << 28
	}
	// Bit 25 (data request) follows the DMA
	// direction: off = always 0, FIFO = FIFO not full
	// (always in this model), CPU to GP0 = bit 28,
	// GPUREAD to CPU = bit 27.
	switch g.dmaDir {
	case 1:
		s |= 1 << 25
	case 2:
		if readyDMA {
			s |= 1 << 25
		}
	case 3:
		if pendingRead {
			s |= 1 << 25
		}
	}
	s |= uint32(g.dmaDir&3) << 29
	if g.LineOdd {
		s |= 1 << 31
	}
	return s
}

// UnknownGP1Commands returns the distinct GP1
// command bytes received that have no implemented
// case, in first-seen order. Host-side diagnostic
// only: the log survives resets and is not part of
// the serialized state.
func (g *GPU) UnknownGP1Commands() []uint8 {
	out := make([]uint8, len(g.unknownGP1))
	copy(out, g.unknownGP1)
	return out
}

// UnknownGP1Count returns the total number of
// unimplemented GP1 commands received, repeats
// included.
func (g *GPU) UnknownGP1Count() int { return g.unknownGP1N }

func (g *GPU) noteUnknownGP1(cmd uint8) {
	g.unknownGP1N++
	for _, u := range g.unknownGP1 {
		if u == cmd {
			return
		}
	}
	g.unknownGP1 = append(g.unknownGP1, cmd)
}

// WriteGP1 executes a GP1 command word.
func (g *GPU) WriteGP1(w uint32) {
	cmd := w >> 24
	param := w & 0xFFFFFF
	switch cmd {
	case 0x00: // reset
		vram := g.vram
		disp := g.displayBuf
		unk, unkN := g.unknownGP1, g.unknownGP1N
		*g = GPU{vram: vram, displayBuf: disp, unknownGP1: unk, unknownGP1N: unkN}
		g.dispEnable = false
		g.rangeX1 = 0x200
		g.rangeX2 = 0x200 + 256*10
		g.rangeY1 = 0x010
		g.rangeY2 = 0x010 + 240
	case 0x01: // reset command buffer
		g.bufLen = 0
		g.bufNeed = 0
		g.polyline = false
		g.xferActive = false
	case 0x02: // acknowledge interrupt
		g.irq = false
	case 0x03: // display enable (bit 0: 0 on, 1 off)
		g.dispEnable = param&1 == 0
	case 0x04: // DMA direction
		g.dmaDir = int(param & 3)
	case 0x05: // display area start
		g.dispX = int(param & 0x3FF)
		g.dispY = int((param >> 10) & 0x1FF)
	case 0x06: // horizontal display range
		g.rangeX1 = int(param & 0xFFF)
		g.rangeX2 = int((param >> 12) & 0xFFF)
	case 0x07: // vertical display range
		g.rangeY1 = int(param & 0x3FF)
		g.rangeY2 = int((param >> 10) & 0x3FF)
	case 0x08: // display mode
		g.hres1 = int(param & 3)
		g.vres480 = param&4 != 0
		g.pal = param&8 != 0
		g.depth24 = param&16 != 0
		g.interlace = param&32 != 0
		g.hres2 = param&64 != 0
		g.reverse = param&128 != 0
	case 0x09: // VRAM size (v2 register, stored only in hardware effect)
		// Accepted and ignored: our VRAM is always 1 MB.
	case 0x10: // read internal register
		switch param & 0xF {
		case 2:
			g.readLatch = g.texWindow
		case 3:
			g.readLatch = uint32(g.drawX1) | uint32(g.drawY1)<<10
		case 4:
			g.readLatch = uint32(g.drawX2) | uint32(g.drawY2)<<10
		case 5:
			g.readLatch = uint32(g.offX&0x7FF) | uint32(g.offY&0x7FF)<<11
		case 7:
			g.readLatch = 2 // GPU version (v2)
		}
	default:
		// Not a documented GP1 command for this
		// GPU: ignored, but recorded for the
		// host-side diagnostic log.
		g.noteUnknownGP1(uint8(cmd))
	}
}

// ReadData services GPUREAD: VRAM to CPU transfer
// words first, then the GP1(10) latch.
func (g *GPU) ReadData() uint32 {
	if g.xferActive && g.xferRead {
		lo := g.xferNextHalf()
		hi := g.xferNextHalf()
		return uint32(lo) | uint32(hi)<<16
	}
	return g.readLatch
}

// xferNextHalf returns the next halfword of a VRAM
// to CPU transfer and advances its cursor; when the
// last halfword is consumed the transfer ends.
func (g *GPU) xferNextHalf() uint16 {
	v := g.VRAMAt(g.xferX+g.xferCol, g.xferY+g.xferRow)
	g.xferCol++
	if g.xferCol >= g.xferW {
		g.xferCol = 0
		g.xferRow++
		if g.xferRow >= g.xferH {
			g.xferActive = false
		}
	}
	return v
}

// Framebuffer renders the display area into an
// XRGB8888 slice at native resolution and returns
// it along with its dimensions. In interlaced 480
// mode the full 480 lines are returned, starting at
// the display area offset by the current field
// parity (the simplification stated in the README).
// A disabled display returns black.
func (g *GPU) Framebuffer() ([]uint32, int, int) {
	w, h := g.DisplayWidth(), g.DisplayHeight()
	out := g.displayBuf[:w*h]
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = 0xFF000000
	}
	if !g.dispEnable {
		return out, w, h
	}
	yOff := 0
	if g.interlace && g.vres480 && g.OddFrame {
		yOff = 1
	}
	if g.depth24 {
		g.blit24(out, w, h, yOff)
	} else {
		g.blit15(out, w, h, yOff)
	}
	return out, w, h
}

func (g *GPU) blit15(out []uint32, w, h, yOff int) {
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		sy := (g.dispY + yOff + y) & (VRAMHeight - 1)
		row := sy * VRAMWidth
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			sx := (g.dispX + x) & (VRAMWidth - 1)
			out[y*w+x] = expand15(g.vram[row+sx])
		}
	}
}

func expand15(v uint16) uint32 {
	r := uint32(v & 0x1F)
	gr := uint32((v >> 5) & 0x1F)
	b := uint32((v >> 10) & 0x1F)
	r = (r << 3) | (r >> 2)
	gr = (gr << 3) | (gr >> 2)
	b = (b << 3) | (b >> 2)
	return 0xFF000000 | r<<16 | gr<<8 | b
}

func (g *GPU) blit24(out []uint32, w, h, yOff int) {
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		sy := (g.dispY + yOff + y) & (VRAMHeight - 1)
		base := sy * VRAMWidth * 2 // byte offset of the VRAM row
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			off := base + g.dispX*2 + x*3
			r := g.vramByte(off)
			gr := g.vramByte(off + 1)
			b := g.vramByte(off + 2)
			out[y*w+x] = 0xFF000000 | uint32(r)<<16 | uint32(gr)<<8 | uint32(b)
		}
	}
}

// vramByte reads one byte of VRAM by byte offset,
// wrapping at 1 MB.
func (g *GPU) vramByte(off int) uint8 {
	off &= (VRAMWidth * VRAMHeight * 2) - 1
	hw := g.vram[off>>1]
	if off&1 == 0 {
		return uint8(hw)
	}
	return uint8(hw >> 8)
}

func packColor(c [3]int) uint32 {
	return uint32(c[0]) | uint32(c[1])<<8 | uint32(c[2])<<16
}

func unpackColor(w uint32) [3]int {
	return [3]int{int(w & 0xFF), int((w >> 8) & 0xFF), int((w >> 16) & 0xFF)}
}

// StateSize is the serialized size of the GPU:
// VRAM plus a fixed field block.
const StateSize = VRAMWidth*VRAMHeight*2 + 2048

// Serialize writes the GPU state.
func (g *GPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	for i, v := range g.vram {
		out[2*i] = byte(v)
		out[2*i+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	}
	o := out[VRAMWidth*VRAMHeight*2:]
	put16 := func(off int, v uint16) { o[off], o[off+1] = byte(v), byte(v>>8) }
	put32 := func(off int, v uint32) {
		o[off], o[off+1], o[off+2], o[off+3] = byte(v), byte(v>>8), byte(v>>16), byte(v>>24)
	}
	put32(0, g.texWindow)
	put32(4, uint32(g.page.xBase)|uint32(g.page.yBase)<<16)
	o[8] = byte(g.page.semiMode) | byte(g.page.colorFmt)<<2
	flags := byte(0)
	set := func(bit byte, on bool) {
		if on {
			flags |= 1 << bit
		}
	}
	set(0, g.dither)
	set(1, g.drawToDisp)
	set(2, g.texDisable)
	set(3, g.rectFlipX)
	set(4, g.rectFlipY)
	set(5, g.maskSet)
	set(6, g.maskCheck)
	set(7, g.dispEnable)
	o[9] = flags
	put16(10, uint16(g.winMaskX)|uint16(g.winMaskY)<<8)
	put16(12, uint16(g.winOffX)|uint16(g.winOffY)<<8)
	put16(14, uint16(g.drawX1))
	put16(16, uint16(g.drawY1))
	put16(18, uint16(g.drawX2))
	put16(20, uint16(g.drawY2))
	put16(22, uint16(g.offX))
	put16(24, uint16(g.offY))
	put16(26, uint16(g.dispX))
	put16(28, uint16(g.dispY))
	put16(30, uint16(g.rangeX1))
	put16(32, uint16(g.rangeX2))
	put16(34, uint16(g.rangeY1))
	put16(36, uint16(g.rangeY2))
	o[38] = byte(g.dmaDir) | byte(g.hres1)<<2
	f2 := byte(0)
	set2 := func(bit byte, on bool) {
		if on {
			f2 |= 1 << bit
		}
	}
	set2(0, g.hres2)
	set2(1, g.vres480)
	set2(2, g.pal)
	set2(3, g.depth24)
	set2(4, g.interlace)
	set2(5, g.reverse)
	set2(6, g.irq)
	set2(7, g.OddFrame)
	o[39] = f2
	put32(40, g.readLatch)
	o[44] = byte(g.bufLen)
	o[45] = byte(g.bufNeed)
	o[46] = g.cmd
	for i := 0; i < g.bufLen && i < len(g.buf); i++ {
		put32(48+i*4, g.buf[i])
	}
	o[128] = 0
	if g.polyline {
		o[128] |= 1
	}
	if g.polyGouraud {
		o[128] |= 2
	}
	o[129] = byte(g.polyStage)
	put16(130, uint16(g.polyPrevX))
	put16(132, uint16(g.polyPrevY))
	put32(134, packColor(g.polyPrevC))
	put32(156, packColor(g.polyColor))
	o[138] = 0
	if g.xferActive {
		o[138] |= 1
	}
	if g.xferRead {
		o[138] |= 2
	}
	if g.xferHasLo {
		o[138] |= 4
	}
	put16(140, uint16(g.xferX))
	put16(142, uint16(g.xferY))
	put16(144, uint16(g.xferW))
	put16(146, uint16(g.xferH))
	put16(148, uint16(g.xferCol))
	put16(150, uint16(g.xferRow))
	put16(152, g.xferPend)
	o[154] = byte(g.Field)
	if g.LineOdd {
		o[155] = 1
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (g *GPU) Deserialize(in []byte) {
	for i := range g.vram {
		g.vram[i] = uint16(in[2*i]) | uint16(in[2*i+1])<<8
	}
	o := in[VRAMWidth*VRAMHeight*2:]
	get16 := func(off int) uint16 { return uint16(o[off]) | uint16(o[off+1])<<8 }
	get32 := func(off int) uint32 {
		return uint32(o[off]) | uint32(o[off+1])<<8 | uint32(o[off+2])<<16 | uint32(o[off+3])<<24
	}
	g.texWindow = get32(0)
	p := get32(4)
	g.page.xBase = int(p & 0xFFFF)
	g.page.yBase = int(p >> 16)
	g.page.semiMode = int(o[8] & 3)
	g.page.colorFmt = int((o[8] >> 2) & 3)
	flags := o[9]
	g.dither = flags&1 != 0
	g.drawToDisp = flags&2 != 0
	g.texDisable = flags&4 != 0
	g.rectFlipX = flags&8 != 0
	g.rectFlipY = flags&16 != 0
	g.maskSet = flags&32 != 0
	g.maskCheck = flags&64 != 0
	g.dispEnable = flags&128 != 0
	m := get16(10)
	g.winMaskX, g.winMaskY = int(m&0xFF), int(m>>8)
	m = get16(12)
	g.winOffX, g.winOffY = int(m&0xFF), int(m>>8)
	g.drawX1 = int(get16(14))
	g.drawY1 = int(get16(16))
	g.drawX2 = int(get16(18))
	g.drawY2 = int(get16(20))
	g.offX = int(int16(get16(22)))
	g.offY = int(int16(get16(24)))
	g.dispX = int(get16(26))
	g.dispY = int(get16(28))
	g.rangeX1 = int(get16(30))
	g.rangeX2 = int(get16(32))
	g.rangeY1 = int(get16(34))
	g.rangeY2 = int(get16(36))
	g.dmaDir = int(o[38] & 3)
	g.hres1 = int((o[38] >> 2) & 3)
	f2 := o[39]
	g.hres2 = f2&1 != 0
	g.vres480 = f2&2 != 0
	g.pal = f2&4 != 0
	g.depth24 = f2&8 != 0
	g.interlace = f2&16 != 0
	g.reverse = f2&32 != 0
	g.irq = f2&64 != 0
	g.OddFrame = f2&128 != 0
	g.readLatch = get32(40)
	g.bufLen = int(o[44])
	g.bufNeed = int(o[45])
	g.cmd = o[46]
	for i := range g.buf {
		g.buf[i] = 0
	}
	for i := 0; i < g.bufLen && i < len(g.buf); i++ {
		g.buf[i] = get32(48 + i*4)
	}
	g.polyline = o[128]&1 != 0
	g.polyGouraud = o[128]&2 != 0
	g.polyStage = int(o[129])
	g.polyPrevX = int(int16(get16(130)))
	g.polyPrevY = int(int16(get16(132)))
	g.polyPrevC = unpackColor(get32(134))
	g.polyColor = unpackColor(get32(156))
	g.xferActive = o[138]&1 != 0
	g.xferRead = o[138]&2 != 0
	g.xferHasLo = o[138]&4 != 0
	g.xferX = int(get16(140))
	g.xferY = int(get16(142))
	g.xferW = int(get16(144))
	g.xferH = int(get16(146))
	g.xferCol = int(get16(148))
	g.xferRow = int(get16(150))
	g.xferPend = get16(152)
	g.Field = int(o[154])
	g.LineOdd = o[155] != 0
}
