package gpu

import "testing"

func gp0(g *GPU, words ...uint32) {
	for _, w := range words {
		g.WriteGP0(w)
	}
}

func gp1(g *GPU, w uint32) { g.WriteGP1(w) }

// fullDraw sets the drawing area to the whole VRAM
// and the offset to 0.
func fullDraw(g *GPU) {
	gp0(g,
		0xE3000000, // E3 top-left (0,0)
		0xE407FFFF, // E4 bottom-right (1023,511)
		0xE5000000, // E5 offset (0,0)
	)
}

func countColor(g *GPU, col uint16) int {
	n := 0
	for _, v := range g.VRAM() {
		if v == col {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

func TestResetStatus(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	if s := g.Status(); s != 0x14802000 {
		t.Errorf("GPUSTAT after reset = 0x%08X, want 0x14802000", s)
	}
}

func TestFlatTriangleCoverageRule(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	// Right triangle (0,0),(8,0),(0,8), pure red.
	gp0(g, 0x200000FF, 0x00000000, 0x00000008, 0x00080000)
	if n := countColor(g, 0x001F); n != 36 {
		t.Errorf("red pixels = %d, want 36 (lower-right edges excluded)", n)
	}
	if g.VRAMAt(7, 0) != 0x001F || g.VRAMAt(0, 7) != 0x001F || g.VRAMAt(0, 0) != 0x001F {
		t.Errorf("top/left edge pixels missing")
	}
	if g.VRAMAt(8, 0) != 0 || g.VRAMAt(0, 8) != 0 || g.VRAMAt(4, 4) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("lower-right edge pixels drawn but must be excluded")
	}
}

func TestGouraudInterpolationExact(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	// (0,0) red, (9,0) green, (0,9) blue.
	gp0(g,
		0x300000FF, 0x00000000, // cmd+color0, v0
		0x0000FF00, 0x00000009, // color1, v1
		0x00FF0000, 0x00090000, // color2, v2
	)
	// Barycentric weights at (2,2) are 45/18/18 of 81:
	// r=142, g=57, b=57 in 8-bit space, quantized to
	// 17/7/7.
	if got := g.VRAMAt(2, 2); got != 0x1CF1 {
		t.Errorf("pixel (2,2) = 0x%04X, want 0x1CF1", got)
	}
}

func TestQuadSplitsAsTwoTriangles(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	// Quad (0,0),(8,0),(0,8),(8,8) green.
	gp0(g, 0x2800FF00, 0x00000000, 0x00000008, 0x00080000, 0x00080008)
	// Union of triangles (0,0)(8,0)(0,8) and
	// (8,0)(0,8)(8,8): only the shared-diagonal
	// pixels and the outer lower-right corners are
	// excluded; spot check interior pixels.
	for _, pt := range [][2]int{{0, 0}, {7, 1}, {1, 7}, {7, 7}, {4, 4}} {
		if g.VRAMAt(pt[0], pt[1]) != 0x03E0 {
			t.Errorf("quad pixel %v = 0x%04X, want 0x03E0", pt, g.VRAMAt(pt[0], pt[1]))
		}
	}
	if g.VRAMAt(8, 0) != 0 || g.VRAMAt(0, 8) != 0 || g.VRAMAt(8, 8) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("quad outer lower-right corners drawn but must be excluded")
	}
}

func TestSemiTransparencyModes(t *testing.T) {
	backdrop := uint16(0x294A) // (10,10,10)
	front := uint32(0x00F8F8F8)
	want := []uint16{
		0x5294, // B/2 + F/2: 5 + 15 = 20 per channel
		0x7FFF, // B + F clamped: 31
		0x0000, // B - F clamped: 0
		0x4631, // B + F/4: 10 + 7 = 17
	}
	for mode := 0; mode < 4; mode++ {
		g := New()
		fullDraw(g)
		gp0(g, 0xE1000000|uint32(mode)<<5) // E1 semi mode
		g.SetVRAM(2, 2, backdrop)
		g.SetVRAM(3, 2, backdrop)
		g.SetVRAM(2, 3, backdrop)
		// Semi-transparent flat triangle (cmd 0x22)
		// over (2,2),(3,2),(2,3).
		gp0(g, 0x22000000|front, 0x00020002, 0x00020003, 0x00030002)
		if got := g.VRAMAt(2, 2); got != want[mode] {
			t.Errorf("mode %d: pixel = 0x%04X, want 0x%04X", mode, got, want[mode])
		}
	}
}

func TestFillMaskingRules(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	// Height parameter 512 masks to 0: nothing fills.
	gp0(g, 0x02FFFFFF, 0x00000000, 0x02000010)
	if n := countColor(g, 0x7FFF); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("fill with height 512 drew %d pixels, want 0", n)
	}
	// X position 0x123 masks to 0x120; width 17 rounds
	// up to 32; color low bits are dropped (0xFFFFFF
	// becomes channels of 31 = 0x7FFF, mask bit 0).
	gp0(g, 0x02FFFFFF, 0x00000123, 0x00010011)
	if g.VRAMAt(0x120, 0) != 0x7FFF || g.VRAMAt(0x120+31, 0) != 0x7FFF {
		t.Errorf("fill span wrong: [0x120]=0x%04X [0x13F]=0x%04X",
			g.VRAMAt(0x120, 0), g.VRAMAt(0x13F, 0))
	}
	if g.VRAMAt(0x120+32, 0) != 0 || g.VRAMAt(0x11F, 0) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("fill leaked outside the masked span")
	}
	if g.VRAMAt(0x120, 0)&0x8000 != 0 {
		t.Errorf("fill set the mask bit; it is forced to 0")
	}
}

func TestTexturedRect4BitCLUTRaw(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	// CLUT at (0,256): entries 1,2,3 colored, 0
	// transparent.
	g.SetVRAM(1, 256, 0x001F)
	g.SetVRAM(2, 256, 0x03E0)
	g.SetVRAM(3, 256, 0x7C00)
	// Texture row: nibbles for u=0..3 are 1,2,3,0.
	g.SetVRAM(0, 0, 0x0321)
	// Raw textured variable rect (0x65) at (10,10),
	// 4x1; the UV word's high halfword is the CLUT
	// coordinate (0,256): 256<<6 in the high half.
	gp0(g, 0x65000000, 0x000A000A, 0x40000000, 0x00010004)
	want := []uint16{0x001F, 0x03E0, 0x7C00, 0x0000}
	for i, wv := range want {
		if got := g.VRAMAt(10+i, 10); got != wv {
			t.Errorf("pixel (%d,10) = 0x%04X, want 0x%04X", 10+i, got, wv)
		}
	}
}

func TestTexturedRectBlendedModulation(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	g.SetVRAM(1, 256, 0x001F) // CLUT[1] = red 31
	g.SetVRAM(0, 0, 0x0111)   // nibbles: u=0,1,2 all index CLUT 1
	// Blended textured variable-size rect (0x64)
	// with a 1x1 size word. Neutral color 0x80
	// leaves the texel unchanged.
	gp0(g, 0x64008080, 0x00140014, 0x40000000, 0x00010001)
	if got := g.VRAMAt(20, 20); got != 0x001F {
		t.Errorf("neutral modulation = 0x%04X, want 0x001F", got)
	}
	// Color 0x40 halves it: 255*64>>7 = 127, >>3 = 15.
	gp0(g, 0x64004040, 0x00140015, 0x40000000, 0x00010001)
	if got := g.VRAMAt(21, 20); got != 0x000F {
		t.Errorf("half modulation = 0x%04X, want 0x000F", got)
	}
}

}

func TestSemiTexturedBlendsOnlySTP(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	gp0(g, 0xE1000000)      // semi mode 0
	g.SetVRAM(0, 0, 0x001F) // texel A: red, STP clear
	g.SetVRAM(1, 0, 0x801F) // texel B: red, STP set
	g.SetVRAM(40, 40, 0x7FFF)
	g.SetVRAM(41, 40, 0x7FFF)
	// Semi blended triangle (0x26) (40,40),(42,40),
	// (40,42), UVs (0,0),(2,0),(0,2), 15-bit page.
	gp0(g,
		0x26808080,
		0x00280028, 0x00000000,
		0x0028002A, 0x01000002,
		0x002A0028, 0x00000200,
	)
	// Neutral modulation (0x80) reproduces the texel
	// exactly; STP clear means opaque write.
	if got := g.VRAMAt(40, 40); got != 0x001F {
		t.Errorf("STP-clear pixel = 0x%04X, want opaque 0x001F", got)
	}
	// STP set blends B/2+F/2 over white: (15+15,
	// 15+0, 15+0) = 0x3DFE, and the texel STP bit is
	// written into the pixel mask bit, giving 0xBDFE.
	if got := g.VRAMAt(41, 40); got != 0xBDFE {
		t.Errorf("STP-set pixel = 0x%04X, want 0xBDFE", got)
	}
}

	}
}

func TestDitherRules(t *testing.T) {
	// Gouraud triangle with all vertex colors 0x80:
	// dither on produces the matrix pattern.
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	gp0(g, 0xE1000200) // E1 dither on
	gp0(g,
		0x30808080, 0x00000000,
		0x00808080, 0x00000007,
		0x00808080, 0x00070000,
	)
	want := []uint16{0x3DEF, 0x4210, 0x3DEF, 0x4210} // (128-4)>>3=15, 128>>3=16, (128-3)>>3=15, (128+1)>>3=16
	for x, wv := range want {
		if got := g.VRAMAt(x, 0); got != wv {
			t.Errorf("dithered pixel (%d,0) = 0x%04X, want 0x%04X", x, got, wv)
		}
	}
	// Monochrome triangles never dither.
	g2 := New()
	fullDraw(g2)
	gp0(g2, 0xE1000200)
	gp0(g2, 0x20808080, 0x00000000, 0x00000007, 0x00070000)
	for x := 0; x < 4; x++ {
		if got := g2.VRAMAt(x, 0); got != 0x4210 {
			t.Errorf("mono pixel (%d,0) = 0x%04X, want undithered 0x4210", x, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestLinesAndPolyline(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	// Horizontal mono line (0,30)-(4,30), white.
	gp0(g, 0x40FFFFFF, 0x001E0000, 0x001E0004)
	for x := 0; x <= 4; x++ {
		if g.VRAMAt(x, 30) != 0x7FFF {
			t.Errorf("line pixel (%d,30) = 0x%04X", x, g.VRAMAt(x, 30))
		}
	}
	if g.VRAMAt(5, 30) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("line overran its endpoint")
	}
	// Diagonal (0,32)-(4,36).
	gp0(g, 0x40FFFFFF, 0x00200000, 0x00240004)
	for i := 0; i <= 4; i++ {
		if g.VRAMAt(i, 32+i) != 0x7FFF {
			t.Errorf("diagonal pixel (%d,%d) missing", i, 32+i)
		}
	}
	// Polyline: (0,40) to (4,40) to (4,44), then the
	// terminator word.
	gp0(g, 0x48FFFFFF, 0x00280000, 0x00280004, 0x002C0004, 0x50005000)
	if g.VRAMAt(2, 40) != 0x7FFF || g.VRAMAt(4, 42) != 0x7FFF {
		t.Errorf("polyline segments missing: (2,40)=0x%04X (4,42)=0x%04X",
			g.VRAMAt(2, 40), g.VRAMAt(4, 42))
	}
	// The command stream still works after the
	// terminator: a fill must land.
	gp0(g, 0x0200FF00, 0x00320032, 0x00020002)
	if g.VRAMAt(50, 50) != 0x03E0 {
		t.Errorf("post-terminator fill failed: 0x%04X", g.VRAMAt(50, 50))
	}
}

	}
}

func TestOverspanPrimitiveSkipped(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	// X span of 1123 exceeds 1023: not drawn.
	// Vertices: (-100,0), (1023,0), (0,10); -100 in
	// 11-bit two's complement is 0x79C.
	gp0(g, 0x200000FF, 0x0000079C, 0x000003FF, 0x000A0000)
	if n := countColor(g, 0x001F); n != 0 {
		t.Errorf("overspan triangle drew %d pixels, want 0", n)
	}
}

func TestVRAMTransfers(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	// CPU to VRAM: 2 halfwords at (0,0).
	gp0(g, 0xA0000000, 0x00000000, 0x00010002, 0xBBBBAAAA)
	if g.VRAMAt(0, 0) != 0xAAAA || g.VRAMAt(1, 0) != 0xBBBB {
		t.Fatalf("CPU to VRAM landed wrong: 0x%04X 0x%04X", g.VRAMAt(0, 0), g.VRAMAt(1, 0))
	}
	// VRAM to VRAM: copy (0,0)-(1,0) to (10,5).
	gp0(g, 0x80000000, 0x00000000, 0x0005000A, 0x00010002)
	if g.VRAMAt(10, 5) != 0xAAAA || g.VRAMAt(11, 5) != 0xBBBB {
		t.Errorf("VRAM to VRAM copy wrong: 0x%04X 0x%04X", g.VRAMAt(10, 5), g.VRAMAt(11, 5))
	}
	// VRAM to CPU: arm and read back.
	gp0(g, 0xC0000000, 0x00000000, 0x00010002)
	if g.Status()&(1<<27) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("GPUSTAT bit 27 (VRAM read ready) clear during readback")
	}
	if got := g.ReadData(); got != 0xBBBBAAAA {
		t.Errorf("GPUREAD = 0x%08X, want 0xBBBBAAAA", got)
	}
	if g.Status()&(1<<27) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("GPUSTAT bit 27 still set after readback drained")
	}
}

func TestGP0IRQCommand(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	gp0(g, 0x1F000000)
	if g.Status()&(1<<24) == 0 || !g.IRQRequested() {
		t.Errorf("GP0(1F) did not set the GPU interrupt bit")
	}
	gp1(g, 0x02000000) // GP1(02) acknowledge
	if g.Status()&(1<<24) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("GP1(02) did not clear the GPU interrupt bit")
	}
}

func TestDisplayOutput(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	g.SetVRAM(0, 0, 0x001F) // red
	g.SetVRAM(1, 0, 0x8000) // non-transparent black
	gp1(g, 0x05000000)      // display area (0,0)
	gp1(g, 0x08000000)      // mode 0: 256x240 15-bit
	gp1(g, 0x03000000)      // display on
	fb, w, h := g.Framebuffer()
	if w != 256 || h != 240 || len(fb) != 256*240 {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer = %dx%d len %d", w, h, len(fb))
	}
	if fb[0] != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Errorf("fb[0] = 0x%08X, want 0xFFFF0000", fb[0])
	}
	if fb[1] != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Errorf("fb[1] = 0x%08X, want 0xFF000000", fb[1])
	}
	// Display off: black.
	gp1(g, 0x03000001)
	fb, _, _ = g.Framebuffer()
	if fb[0] != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Errorf("display-off framebuffer not black: 0x%08X", fb[0])
	}
}

	gp1(g, 0x05000000)

		t.Fatalf("DisplayHeight = %d, want 480", g.DisplayHeight())
	}
	g.OddFrame = false
	fb, w, _ := g.Framebuffer()
	if fb[w] != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Errorf("even frame line 1 = 0x%08X, want green", fb[w])
	}
	g.OddFrame = true
	fb, _, _ = g.Framebuffer()
	if fb[0] != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Errorf("odd frame line 0 = 0x%08X, want green (field offset applied)", fb[0])
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	g := New()
	fullDraw(g)
	gp0(g, 0xE1000100)
	gp0(g, 0x200000FF, 0x00000000, 0x00000008, 0x00080000)
	gp1(g, 0x08000001) // 320 wide
	gp1(g, 0x03000000)
	s := g.Serialize()
	if len(s) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state = %d, want %d", len(s), StateSize)
	}
	g2 := New()
	g2.Deserialize(s)
	if g2.Status() != g.Status() {
		t.Errorf("status diverged: 0x%08X vs 0x%08X", g2.Status(), g.Status())
	}
	fb1, w1, h1 := g.Framebuffer()
	fb2, w2, h2 := g2.Framebuffer()
	if w1 != w2 || h1 != h2 {
		t.Fatalf("display size diverged")
	}
	for i := range fb1 {
		if fb1[i] != fb2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer diverged at pixel %d", i)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/gpu/raster.go ====================

package gpu

// Rasterization: pixel plotting with the drawing
// area clip, display-area rule, mask rules and
// semi-transparency; texture sampling; scan
// conversion for triangles and lines.

// prim carries the per-primitive rendering
// attributes shared by the polygon, line and
// rectangle paths.
type prim struct {
	textured bool
	semi     bool
	raw      bool
	page     texPage
	clutX    int
	clutY    int
	ditherOK bool // this primitive class dithers when enabled
}

// inDisplayArea reports whether a VRAM pixel falls
// inside the currently displayed rectangle (used by
// the GP0(E1) draw-to-display rule).
func (g *GPU) inDisplayArea(x, y int) bool {
	dx := x - g.dispX
	dy := y - g.dispY
	return dx >= 0 && dx < g.DisplayWidth() && dy >= 0 && dy < g.DisplayHeight()
}

// plot writes one shaded pixel (15-bit color in col,
// whose bit 15 is the source STP bit for textured
// primitives and 0 otherwise) at VRAM coordinates,
// applying clipping, the draw-to-display rule, the
// mask rules and, when blend is set, semi-transparent
// blending with the existing pixel per mode.
func (g *GPU) plot(x, y int, col uint16, blend bool, mode int) {
	if x < g.drawX1 || x > g.drawX2 || y < g.drawY1 || y > g.drawY2 {
		return
	}
	if x < 0 || x >= VRAMWidth || y < 0 || y >= VRAMHeight {
		return
	}
	// The draw-to-display prohibition protects the
	// area being scanned out; with the display
	// disabled there is no scanout to protect, so the
	// rule applies only while the display is on (see
	// the README model notes).
	if g.dispEnable && !g.drawToDisp && g.inDisplayArea(x, y) {
		return
	}
	idx := y*VRAMWidth + x
	dst := g.vram[idx]
	if g.maskCheck && dst&0x8000 != 0 {
		return
	}
	out := col & 0x7FFF
	if blend {
		out = blend15(dst&0x7FFF, out, mode)
	}
	if g.maskSet || col&0x8000 != 0 {
		out |= 0x8000
	}
	g.vram[idx] = out
}

// blend15 applies one semi-transparency mode to
// 5-bit channels: mode 0 = B/2 + F/2, mode 1 = B + F
// (clamped), mode 2 = B - F (clamped at 0),
// mode 3 = B + F/4 (clamped).
func blend15(backdrop, front uint16, mode int) uint16 {
	var out uint16
	for shift := 0; shift < 15; shift += 5 {
		b := int((backdrop >> shift) & 0x1F)
		f := int((front >> shift) & 0x1F)
		var v int
		switch mode {
		case 0:
			v = (b >> 1) + (f >> 1)
		case 1:
			v = b + f
			if v > 31 {
				v = 31
			}
		case 2:
			v = b - f
			if v < 0 {
				v = 0
			}
		default:
			v = b + (f >> 2)
			if v > 31 {
				v = 31
			}
		}
		out |= uint16(v) << shift
	}
	return out
}

// quantize converts an 8-bit-space shaded color to a
// 15-bit VRAM color, adding the dither matrix value
// first when dither applies.
func (g *GPU) quantize(c vertex, x, y int, dither bool) uint16 {
	r, gg, b := c.r, c.g, c.b
	if dither {
		d := ditherTable[y&3][x&3]
		r += d
		gg += d
		b += d
	}
	return uint16(clamp5(r)) | uint16(clamp5(gg))<<5 | uint16(clamp5(b))<<10
}

func clamp5(v int) int {
	v >>= 3
	if v < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if v > 31 {
		return 31
	}
	return v
}

// applyWindow maps a texture coordinate through the
// GP0(E2) texture window in one axis.
func (g *GPU) applyWindow(t, mask, off int) int {
	if mask == 0 {
		return t
	}
	return (t & ((mask * 8) - 1)) | ((off & mask) * 8)
}

// sample fetches and shades one texel. It returns
// the 15-bit color (bit 15 = texel STP), whether the
// texel is drawn at all (texel 0x0000 is fully
// transparent), and the STP bit. Raw mode returns
// the texel unmodified. Blended mode modulates the
// texel by the vertex color in 8-bit space,
// saturating like the v2 GPU, and dithers when the
// draw-mode dither flag is on and the primitive
// class allows it.
func (g *GPU) sample(p prim, u, v int, shade vertex, x, y int) (uint16, bool, bool) {
	u = g.applyWindow(u, g.winMaskX, g.winOffX)
	v = g.applyWindow(v, g.winMaskY, g.winOffY)
	page := p.page
	var tex uint16
	switch page.colorFmt {
	case 0: // 4-bit CLUT
		w := g.VRAMAt(page.xBase+(u>>2), page.yBase+v)
		idx := (w >> (uint(u&3) * 4)) & 0xF
		tex = g.VRAMAt(p.clutX+int(idx), p.clutY)
	case 1: // 8-bit CLUT
		w := g.VRAMAt(page.xBase+(u>>1), page.yBase+v)
		idx := (w >> (uint(u&1) * 8)) & 0xFF
		tex = g.VRAMAt(p.clutX+int(idx), p.clutY)
	default: // 15-bit direct
		tex = g.VRAMAt(page.xBase+u, page.yBase+v)
	}
	if tex == 0 {
		return 0, false, false
	}
	stp := tex&0x8000 != 0
	if p.raw {
		return tex, true, stp
	}
	vr := modulate(int(tex&0x1F), shade.r)
	vg := modulate(int((tex>>5)&0x1F), shade.g)
	vb := modulate(int((tex>>10)&0x1F), shade.b)
	col := g.quantize(vertex{r: vr, g: vg, b: vb}, x, y, g.dither && p.ditherOK)
	if stp {
		col |= 0x8000
	}
	return col, true, stp
}

// modulate applies texture modulation: the 5-bit
// texel channel is expanded to 8 bits and multiplied
// by the 8-bit vertex color with 0x80 as neutral,
// saturating at 255.
func modulate(tex5, color8 int) int {
	t8 := (tex5 << 3) | (tex5 >> 2)
	out := (t8 * color8) >> 7
	if out > 255 {
		out = 255
	}
	return out
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Triangles
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

// edgeFn is the edge function for the directed edge
// a to b evaluated at (x,y).
func edgeFn(ax, ay, bx, by, x, y int64) int64 {
	return (bx-ax)*(y-ay) - (by-ay)*(x-ax)
}

// topLeft reports whether the directed edge a to b
// is a top or left edge under the hardware rule that
// lower-right polygon edges are not drawn: boundary
// pixels on top and left edges belong to the
// polygon, boundary pixels on bottom and right edges
// do not.
func topLeft(ax, ay, bx, by int64) bool {
	if by == ay {
		return bx > ax // top edge runs left to right
	}
	return by < ay // left edge runs bottom to top
}

// drawTri scan-converts one triangle with barycentric
// interpolation of color and texture coordinates.
// Screen coordinates are the vertex coordinates plus
// the drawing offset.
func (g *GPU) drawTri(v0, v1, v2 vertex, p prim) {
	// Work in screen space.
	v0.x += g.offX
	v0.y += g.offY
	v1.x += g.offX
	v1.y += g.offY
	v2.x += g.offX
	v2.y += g.offY
	area := edgeFn(int64(v0.x), int64(v0.y), int64(v1.x), int64(v1.y), int64(v2.x), int64(v2.y))
	if area == 0 {
		return
	}
	if area < 0 {
		v1, v2 = v2, v1
		area = -area
	}
	// After the swap the winding gives positive edge
	// functions inside.
	x0 := minI(minI(v0.x, v1.x), v2.x)
	x1 := maxI(maxI(v0.x, v1.x), v2.x)
	y0 := minI(minI(v0.y, v1.y), v2.y)
	y1 := maxI(maxI(v0.y, v1.y), v2.y)
	// Clip the bounding box to the drawing area and
	// VRAM.
	x0 = maxI(x0, maxI(g.drawX1, 0))
	y0 = maxI(y0, maxI(g.drawY1, 0))
	x1 = minI(x1, minI(g.drawX2, VRAMWidth-1))
	y1 = minI(y1, minI(g.drawY2, VRAMHeight-1))
	if x0 > x1 || y0 > y1 {
		return
	}
	tl0 := topLeft(int64(v1.x), int64(v1.y), int64(v2.x), int64(v2.y))
	tl1 := topLeft(int64(v2.x), int64(v2.y), int64(v0.x), int64(v0.y))
	tl2 := topLeft(int64(v0.x), int64(v0.y), int64(v1.x), int64(v1.y))
	half := area / 2
	for y := y0; y <= y1; y++ {
		for x := x0; x <= x1; x++ {
			w0 := edgeFn(int64(v1.x), int64(v1.y), int64(v2.x), int64(v2.y), int64(x), int64(y))
			w1 := edgeFn(int64(v2.x), int64(v2.y), int64(v0.x), int64(v0.y), int64(x), int64(y))
			w2 := edgeFn(int64(v0.x), int64(v0.y), int64(v1.x), int64(v1.y), int64(x), int64(y))
			if !inside(w0, tl0) || !inside(w1, tl1) || !inside(w2, tl2) {
				continue
			}
			c := vertex{
				r: int((w0*int64(v0.r) + w1*int64(v1.r) + w2*int64(v2.r) + half) / area),
				g: int((w0*int64(v0.g) + w1*int64(v1.g) + w2*int64(v2.g) + half) / area),
				b: int((w0*int64(v0.b) + w1*int64(v1.b) + w2*int64(v2.b) + half) / area),
			}
			if p.textured {
				u := int((w0*int64(v0.u) + w1*int64(v1.u) + w2*int64(v2.u) + half) / area)
				v := int((w0*int64(v0.v) + w1*int64(v1.v) + w2*int64(v2.v) + half) / area)
				col, ok, stp := g.sample(p, u, v, c, x, y)
				if !ok {
					continue
				}
				g.plot(x, y, col, p.semi && stp, p.page.semiMode)
			} else {
				col := g.quantize(c, x, y, g.dither && p.ditherOK)
				g.plot(x, y, col, p.semi, p.page.semiMode)
			}
		}
	}
}

func inside(w int64, topLeftEdge bool) bool {
	return w > 0 || (w == 0 && topLeftEdge)
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Lines
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

// drawLine rasterizes one line segment, both
// endpoints inclusive, interpolating color along the
// major axis. The walker is a 16.16 fixed point DDA
// on the minor axis; psx-spx documents the endpoint
// behavior and shading but not the walker's exact
// subpixel phase (see the package comment).
func (g *GPU) drawLine(a, b vertex, p prim) {
	ax, ay := a.x+g.offX, a.y+g.offY
	bx, by := b.x+g.offX, b.y+g.offY
	dx := bx - ax
	dy := by - ay
	steps := maxI(absI(dx), absI(dy))
	if steps == 0 {
		col := g.quantize(a, ax, ay, g.dither && p.ditherOK)
		g.plot(ax, ay, col, p.semi, p.page.semiMode)
		return
	}
	if steps > 1023 {
		return // documented span limit behavior for lines as for polygons
	}
	xAcc := int64(ax) << 16
	yAcc := int64(ay) << 16
	xStep := (int64(dx) << 16) / int64(steps)
	yStep := (int64(dy) << 16) / int64(steps)
	rStep := (int64(b.r-a.r) << 16) / int64(steps)
	ggStep := (int64(b.g-a.g) << 16) / int64(steps)
	bStep := (int64(b.b-a.b) << 16) / int64(steps)
	rAcc := int64(a.r) << 16
	gAcc := int64(a.g) << 16
	bAcc := int64(a.b) << 16
	for i := 0; i <= steps; i++ {
		x := int(xAcc >> 16)
		y := int(yAcc >> 16)
		c := vertex{r: int(rAcc >> 16), g: int(gAcc >> 16), b: int(bAcc >> 16)}
		col := g.quantize(c, x, y, g.dither && p.ditherOK)
		g.plot(x, y, col, p.semi, p.page.semiMode)
		xAcc += xStep
		yAcc += yStep
		rAcc += rStep
		gAcc += ggStep
		bAcc += bStep
	}
}

func minI(a, b int) int {
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}
func maxI(a, b int) int {
	if a > b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}
func absI(a int) int {
	if a < 0 {
		return -a
	}
	return a
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/gpu/render.go ====================

package gpu

// GP0 command processing and software rasterization.
// See the package comment for the rendering model and
// the one under-specified step (line walker phase).

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Command intake
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

// WriteGP0 feeds one word to the GP0 port: commands
// are assembled and executed immediately; CPU to
// VRAM transfer data words are consumed directly.
func (g *GPU) WriteGP0(w uint32) {
	if g.polyline {
		g.feedPolyline(w)
		return
	}
	if g.xferActive && !g.xferRead {
		g.feedTransfer(w)
		return
	}
	if g.bufLen == 0 {
		cmd := uint8(w >> 24)
		if immediateCommand(cmd) {
			g.execImmediate(w)
			return
		}
		g.cmd = cmd
		g.buf[0] = w
		g.bufLen = 1
		g.bufNeed = commandLength(cmd)
		if g.bufNeed <= 1 {
			g.execBuffered()
			g.bufLen = 0
		}
		return
	}
	// Polyline commands start streaming after their
	// first vertex word.
	if g.bufLen < len(g.buf) {
		g.buf[g.bufLen] = w
	}
	g.bufLen++
	if isPolylineCmd(g.cmd) && g.bufLen == 2 {
		g.startPolyline()
		return
	}
	if g.bufLen >= g.bufNeed {
		g.execBuffered()
		g.bufLen = 0
	}
}

// immediateCommand reports whether a command word is
// complete in one word: environment commands, the
// IRQ request command and 1-word misc commands.
func immediateCommand(cmd uint8) bool {
	if cmd >= 0xE0 {
		return true // environment block
	}
	if cmd == 0x1F {
		return true // interrupt request
	}
	if cmd < 0x20 {
		return cmd != 0x02 // misc, except fill (3 words)
	}
	return false
}

// commandLength returns the total word count of a
// buffered GP0 command, including the command word.
func commandLength(cmd uint8) int {
	switch {
	case cmd < 0x20: // fill rectangle (0x02)
		return 3
	case cmd < 0x40: // polygons
		verts := 3
		if cmd&0x08 != 0 {
			verts = 4
		}
		n := 1 + verts
		if cmd&0x10 != 0 { // gouraud: a color before each extra vertex
			n += verts - 1
		}
		if cmd&0x04 != 0 { // textured: a UV word per vertex
			n += verts
		}
		return n
	case cmd < 0x60: // lines
		if cmd&0x08 != 0 {
			return 2 // polyline: command + first vertex, then streams
		}
		if cmd&0x10 != 0 {
			return 4
		}
		return 3
	case cmd < 0x80: // rectangles
		n := 2
		if cmd&0x04 != 0 {
			n++
		}
		if (cmd>>3)&3 == 0 {
			n++ // variable size word
		}
		return n
	case cmd < 0xA0: // VRAM to VRAM
		return 4
	case cmd < 0xC0: // CPU to VRAM: 3 header words then data
		return 3
	default: // VRAM to CPU
		return 3
	}
}

func isPolylineCmd(cmd uint8) bool {
	return cmd >= 0x40 && cmd < 0x60 && cmd&0x08 != 0
}

// execImmediate runs a single-word command.
func (g *GPU) execImmediate(w uint32) {
	cmd := uint8(w >> 24)
	p := w & 0xFFFFFF
	switch {
	case cmd == 0x1F: // interrupt request
		g.irq = true
	case cmd >= 0xE0:
		g.execEnv(cmd, p)
	}
	// Other one-word misc commands (0x00 nop, 0x01
	// clear cache, 0x03-0x1E) have no visible effect.
}

// execEnv runs the GP0 environment commands E1-E6.
func (g *GPU) execEnv(cmd uint8, p uint32) {
	switch cmd {
	case 0xE1: // draw mode
		g.page.xBase = int(p&0xF) * 64
		g.page.yBase = int((p>>4)&1) * 256
		g.page.semiMode = int((p >> 5) & 3)
		g.page.colorFmt = int((p >> 7) & 3)
		g.dither = p&(1<<9) != 0
		g.drawToDisp = p&(1<<10) != 0
		if p&(1<<11) != 0 {
			g.page.yBase |= 512
		}
		g.texDisable = p&(1<<15) != 0
		g.rectFlipX = p&(1<<12) != 0
		g.rectFlipY = p&(1<<13) != 0
	case 0xE2: // texture window
		g.texWindow = p & 0xFFFFF
		g.winMaskX = int(p & 0x1F)
		g.winMaskY = int((p >> 5) & 0x1F)
		g.winOffX = int((p >> 10) & 0x1F)
		g.winOffY = int((p >> 15) & 0x1F)
	case 0xE3: // drawing area top-left
		g.drawX1 = int(p & 0x3FF)
		g.drawY1 = int((p >> 10) & 0x1FF)
	case 0xE4: // drawing area bottom-right
		g.drawX2 = int(p & 0x3FF)
		g.drawY2 = int((p >> 10) & 0x1FF)
	case 0xE5: // drawing offset
		g.offX = signExtend(int(p&0x7FF), 11)
		g.offY = signExtend(int((p>>11)&0x7FF), 11)
	case 0xE6: // mask bit
		g.maskSet = p&1 != 0
		g.maskCheck = p&2 != 0
	}
}

func signExtend(v, bits int) int {
	if v&(1<<(bits-1)) != 0 {
		return v - (1 << bits)
	}
	return v
}

// decodeVertex unpacks a vertex word: X in bits 0-10
// signed, Y in bits 16-26 signed.
func decodeVertex(w uint32) (int, int) {
	return signExtend(int(w&0x7FF), 11), signExtend(int((w>>16)&0x7FF), 11)
}

// decodeColor unpacks a 24-bit color word to 8-bit
// channels.
func decodeColor(w uint32) (int, int, int) {
	return int(w & 0xFF), int((w >> 8) & 0xFF), int((w >> 16) & 0xFF)
}

// execBuffered runs a fully assembled command.
func (g *GPU) execBuffered() {
	b := g.buf
	cmd := g.cmd
	switch {
	case cmd == 0x02:
		g.cmdFill(b)
	case cmd < 0x40:
		g.cmdPolygon(b)
	case cmd < 0x60:
		g.cmdLine(b)
	case cmd < 0x80:
		g.cmdRect(b)
	case cmd < 0xA0:
		g.cmdBlitVRAM(b)
	case cmd < 0xC0:
		g.startTransfer(b, false)
	default:
		g.startTransfer(b, true)
	}
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Primitive parameter decoding
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

type vertex struct {
	x, y    int
	r, g, b int
	u, v    int
}

// cmdPolygon decodes and draws a triangle or quad.
func (g *GPU) cmdPolygon(b [20]uint32) {
	cmd := g.cmd
	textured := cmd&0x04 != 0
	gouraud := cmd&0x10 != 0
	semi := cmd&0x02 != 0
	raw := cmd&0x01 != 0
	verts := 3
	if cmd&0x08 != 0 {
		verts = 4
	}
	vs := make([]vertex, verts)
	r, gg, bl := decodeColor(b[0])
	idx := 1
	var clutX, clutY int
	page := g.page
	for i := 0; i < verts; i++ {
		x, y := decodeVertex(b[idx])
		idx++
		vs[i].x, vs[i].y = x, y
		vs[i].r, vs[i].g, vs[i].b = r, gg, bl
		if textured {
			uvw := b[idx]
			idx++
			vs[i].u = int(uvw & 0xFF)
			vs[i].v = int((uvw >> 8) & 0xFF)
			if i == 0 {
				// The CLUT coordinate rides in the high
				// halfword of the first UV word.
				clutX = int((uvw>>16)&0x3F) * 16
				clutY = int((uvw >> 22) & 0x1FF)
			}
			if i == 1 {
				page = texPageFromWord(uvw, page)
			}
		}
		if gouraud && i < verts-1 {
			r, gg, bl = decodeColor(b[idx])
			idx++
		}
	}
	// Hardware span limits: primitives spanning more
	// than 1023 horizontally or 511 vertically are
	// not drawn.
	minX, maxX, minY, maxY := vs[0].x, vs[0].x, vs[0].y, vs[0].y
	for _, v := range vs[1:] {
		minX, maxX = minI(minX, v.x), maxI(maxX, v.x)
		minY, maxY = minI(minY, v.y), maxI(maxY, v.y)
	}
	if maxX-minX > 1023 || maxY-minY > 511 {
		return
	}
	p := prim{
		textured: textured && !g.texDisable,
		semi:     semi,
		raw:      raw,
		page:     page,
		clutX:    clutX,
		clutY:    clutY,
		// Dithering applies to gouraud-shaded and
		// texture-modulated polygons, never to
		// monochrome ones.
		ditherOK: textured || gouraud,
	}
	g.drawTri(vs[0], vs[1], vs[2], p)
	if verts == 4 {
		// Quads split as (1,2,3) and (2,3,4).
		g.drawTri(vs[1], vs[2], vs[3], p)
	}
}

// texPageFromWord extracts the texpage attribute
// carried in a textured primitive's second UV word.
func texPageFromWord(uvw uint32, cur texPage) texPage {
	tp := int((uvw >> 16) & 0xFFFF)
	out := cur
	out.xBase = int(tp&0xF) * 64
	out.yBase = int((tp>>4)&1) * 256
	out.semiMode = int((tp >> 5) & 3)
	out.colorFmt = int((tp >> 7) & 3)
	if tp&(1<<11) != 0 {
		out.yBase |= 512
	}
	return out
}

func (g *GPU) cmdLine(b [20]uint32) {
	gouraud := g.cmd&0x10 != 0
	semi := g.cmd&0x02 != 0
	r, gg, bl := decodeColor(b[0])
	x0, y0 := decodeVertex(b[1])
	x1, y1 := decodeVertex(b[2])
	r1, g1, b1 := r, gg, bl
	if gouraud {
		r1, g1, b1 = decodeColor(b[2])
		x1, y1 = decodeVertex(b[3])
	}
	p := prim{semi: semi, ditherOK: true}
	g.drawLine(
		vertex{x: x0, y: y0, r: r, g: gg, b: bl},
		vertex{x: x1, y: y1, r: r1, g: g1, b: b1}, p)
}

func (g *GPU) startPolyline() {
	g.polyline = true
	g.polyGouraud = g.cmd&0x10 != 0
	g.polyStage = 0
	r, gg, bl := decodeColor(g.buf[0])
	x, y := decodeVertex(g.buf[1])
	g.polyPrevX, g.polyPrevY = x, y
	g.polyPrevC = [3]int{r, gg, bl}
	g.bufLen = 0
}

// feedPolyline consumes one streaming polyline word.
func (g *GPU) feedPolyline(w uint32) {
	terminator := w&0xF000F000 == 0x50005000
	switch g.polyStage {
	case 0: // a group-start word: color (gouraud) or vertex
		if terminator {
			g.polyline = false
			return
		}
		if g.polyGouraud {
			r, gg, bl := decodeColor(w)
			g.polyColor = [3]int{r, gg, bl}
			g.polyStage = 1
			return
		}
		x, y := decodeVertex(w)
		g.lineTo(x, y, g.polyPrevC)
	case 1: // vertex word after a gouraud color
		x, y := decodeVertex(w)
		g.lineTo(x, y, g.polyColor)
		g.polyStage = 0
	}
}

// lineTo draws one polyline segment from the
// previous vertex to (x,y) with end color c.
func (g *GPU) lineTo(x, y int, c [3]int) {
	semi := g.cmd&0x02 != 0
	p := prim{semi: semi, ditherOK: true}
	g.drawLine(
		vertex{x: g.polyPrevX, y: g.polyPrevY, r: g.polyPrevC[0], g: g.polyPrevC[1], b: g.polyPrevC[2]},
		vertex{x: x, y: y, r: c[0], g: c[1], b: c[2]}, p)
	g.polyPrevX, g.polyPrevY = x, y
	g.polyPrevC = c
}

func (g *GPU) cmdRect(b [20]uint32) {
	cmd := g.cmd
	textured := cmd&0x04 != 0
	semi := cmd&0x02 != 0
	raw := cmd&0x01 != 0
	sizeCode := (cmd >> 3) & 3
	r, gg, bl := decodeColor(b[0])
	vx, vy := decodeVertex(b[1])
	idx := 2
	u0, v0, clutX, clutY := 0, 0, 0, 0
	if textured {
		uvw := b[idx]
		idx++
		u0 = int(uvw & 0xFF)
		v0 = int((uvw >> 8) & 0xFF)
		// The CLUT coordinate rides in the high
		// halfword of the UV word.
		clutX = int((uvw>>16)&0x3F) * 16
		clutY = int((uvw >> 22) & 0x1FF)
	}
	w, h := 1, 1
	switch sizeCode {
	case 0:
		w = int(b[idx] & 0x3FF)
		if w == 0 {
			w = 1024
		}
		h = int((b[idx] >> 16) & 0x1FF)
		if h == 0 {
			h = 512
		}
	case 2:
		w, h = 8, 8
	case 3:
		w, h = 16, 16
	}
	if w > 1024 || h > 512 {
		return
	}
	p := prim{
		textured: textured && !g.texDisable,
		semi:     semi,
		raw:      raw,
		page:     g.page,
		clutX:    clutX,
		clutY:    clutY,
		ditherOK: false, // rectangles are never dithered
	}
	sx := vx + g.offX
	sy := vy + g.offY
	for dy := 0; dy < h; dy++ {
		for dx := 0; dx < w; dx++ {
			x, y := sx+dx, sy+dy
			if !p.textured {
				g.plot(x, y, g.quantize(vertex{r: r, g: gg, b: bl}, x, y, false), semi, g.page.semiMode)
				continue
			}
			tu, tv := dx, dy
			if g.rectFlipX {
				tu = w - 1 - dx
			}
			if g.rectFlipY {
				tv = h - 1 - dy
			}
			col, ok, stp := g.sample(p, (u0+tu)&0xFF, (v0+tv)&0xFF,
				vertex{r: r, g: gg, b: bl}, x, y)
			if !ok {
				continue
			}
			g.plot(x, y, col, semi && stp, p.page.semiMode)
		}
	}
}

// cmdFill draws the fill rectangle (GP0 0x02): the
// documented parameter masking applies and the mask
// settings and drawing area do not.
func (g *GPU) cmdFill(b [20]uint32) {
	c := b[0] & 0xFFFFFF
	col := uint16((c>>19)&0x1F)<<10 | uint16((c>>11)&0x1F)<<5 | uint16((c>>3)&0x1F)
	x := int(b[1]&0xFFFF) & 0x3F0
	y := int(b[1]>>16) & 0x1FF
	w := (int(b[2]&0xFFFF) & 0x3FF)
	w = (w + 0xF) &^ 0xF
	h := int(b[2]>>16) & 0x1FF
	if w == 0 || h == 0 {
		return
	}
	for yy := 0; yy < h; yy++ {
		row := ((y + yy) & (VRAMHeight - 1)) * VRAMWidth
		for xx := 0; xx < w; xx++ {
			g.vram[row+((x+xx)&(VRAMWidth-1))] = col
		}
	}
}

// cmdBlitVRAM performs a VRAM to VRAM copy.
func (g *GPU) cmdBlitVRAM(b [20]uint32) {
	sx, sy := blitCoord(b[1])
	dx, dy := blitCoord(b[2])
	w, h := blitSize(b[3])
	for yy := 0; yy < h; yy++ {
		for xx := 0; xx < w; xx++ {
			src := g.VRAMAt(sx+xx, sy+yy)
			dst := g.VRAMAt(dx+xx, dy+yy)
			if g.maskCheck && dst&0x8000 != 0 {
				continue
			}
			v := src & 0x7FFF
			if g.maskSet || src&0x8000 != 0 {
				v |= 0x8000
			}
			g.vram[((dy+yy)&(VRAMHeight-1))*VRAMWidth+((dx+xx)&(VRAMWidth-1))] = v
		}
	}
}

func blitCoord(w uint32) (int, int) {
	return int(w & 0x3FF), int((w >> 16) & 0x1FF)
}

// blitSize applies the documented size rule: a
// stored size of 0 means the full width/height.
func blitSize(w uint32) (int, int) {
	sx := int(w & 0xFFFF)
	sy := int(w >> 16)
	return ((sx - 1) & 0x3FF) + 1, ((sy - 1) & 0x1FF) + 1
}

// startTransfer arms a CPU to VRAM or VRAM to CPU
// transfer from its parameter words.
func (g *GPU) startTransfer(b [20]uint32, read bool) {
	x, y := blitCoord(b[1])
	w, h := blitSize(b[2])
	g.xferActive = true
	g.xferRead = read
	g.xferX, g.xferY = x, y
	g.xferW, g.xferH = w, h
	g.xferCol, g.xferRow = 0, 0
}

// feedTransfer consumes one word of CPU to VRAM
// data: two halfwords, low first, honoring the mask
// rules; the transfer ends after W*H halfwords.
func (g *GPU) feedTransfer(w uint32) {
	for _, half := range [2]uint16{uint16(w), uint16(w >> 16)} {
		if !g.xferActive {
			return
		}
		x := g.xferX + g.xferCol
		y := g.xferY + g.xferRow
		dst := g.VRAMAt(x, y)
		if !(g.maskCheck && dst&0x8000 != 0) {
			v := half & 0x7FFF
			if g.maskSet || half&0x8000 != 0 {
				v |= 0x8000
			}
			g.vram[(y&(VRAMHeight-1))*VRAMWidth+(x&(VRAMWidth-1))] = v
		}
		g.xferCol++
		if g.xferCol >= g.xferW {
			g.xferCol = 0
			g.xferRow++
			if g.xferRow >= g.xferH {
				g.xferActive = false
			}
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/homebrew/disc.go ====================

package homebrew

// Synthetic disc images carrying the enginetest EXE:
// a plain ISO9660 image and a cue/bin pair wrapping
// the same sectors. The image layout is fixed:
//
//	sectors 0 to 15   system area (zeros)
//	sector 16         primary volume descriptor
//	sector 20         root directory
//	sector 21         SYSTEM.CNF;1
//	sector 22 onward  ENGTEST.EXE;1
//
// SYSTEM.CNF names the EXE on its BOOT line, the way
// a real PlayStation disc does, so the system's
// BootDisc path (ISO9660 walk, SYSTEM.CNF parse, EXE
// load) is the exact code a commercial disc would
// take. The sector contents are otherwise inert: the
// guest's CD stage reads sector 0 and records a
// checksum of whatever is there, it does not compare
// it against a fixed value at runtime.

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

const (
	isoSectorSize  = 2048
	isoPVDSector   = 16
	isoRootSector  = 20
	isoCNFSector   = 21
	isoEXESector   = 22
	isoVolumeID    = "ITAK_ENGTEST"
	engtestCNFName = "SYSTEM.CNF;1"
	engtestEXEName = "ENGTEST.EXE;1"
)

// SystemCNF is the boot configuration file content:
// the BOOT line the disc boot parses, plus the
// customary TCB, EVENT and STACK lines.
func SystemCNF() string {
	return "BOOT = cdrom:\\ENGTEST.EXE;1\r\n" +
		"TCB = 4\r\n" +
		"EVENT = 16\r\n" +
		"STACK = 801FFF00\r\n"
}

// both16 writes a both-endian 16-bit value (little
// first, then big), the ISO9660 multi-byte format.
func both16(b []byte, v uint16) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[0:], v)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(b[2:], v)
}

// both32 writes a both-endian 32-bit value.
func both32(b []byte, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[0:], v)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[4:], v)
}

// dirRecord builds one ISO9660 directory record.
// name is the raw stored name; a one-byte name is
// "\x00" for "." and "\x01" for "..".
func dirRecord(name string, extent, size int, isDir bool) []byte {
	nameLen := len(name)
	recLen := 33 + nameLen
	if recLen%2 != 0 {
		recLen++
	}
	b := make([]byte, recLen)
	b[0] = byte(recLen)
	both32(b[2:], uint32(extent))
	both32(b[10:], uint32(size))
	// Recording date: 2026-10-13, GMT. Only the year,
	// month and day are plausible; parsers ignore it.
	b[18] = 126 // years since 1900
	b[19] = 10
	b[20] = 13
	if isDir {
		b[25] = 2
	}
	both16(b[28:], 1) // volume sequence number
	b[32] = byte(nameLen)
	copy(b[33:], name)
	return b
}

// EnginetestISO builds the ISO9660 image carrying
// exe as its boot file. The image is a multiple of
// the 2048-byte sector size.
func EnginetestISO(exe []byte) []byte {
	exeSectors := (len(exe) + isoSectorSize - 1) / isoSectorSize
	total := isoEXESector + exeSectors
	img := make([]byte, total*isoSectorSize)

	// Primary volume descriptor at sector 16.
	pvd := img[isoPVDSector*isoSectorSize:]
	pvd[0] = 1
	copy(pvd[1:6], "CD001")
	pvd[6] = 1
	vid := isoVolumeID + strings.Repeat(" ", 32-len(isoVolumeID))
	copy(pvd[40:72], vid)
	both32(pvd[80:], uint32(total)) // volume space size
	both16(pvd[120:], 1)            // volume set size
	both16(pvd[124:], 1)            // volume sequence number
	both16(pvd[128:], isoSectorSize)
	rootRec := dirRecord("\x00", isoRootSector, isoSectorSize, true)
	copy(pvd[156:], rootRec)

	// Root directory at sector 20.
	root := img[isoRootSector*isoSectorSize:]
	off := 0
	put := func(r []byte) {
		copy(root[off:], r)
		off += len(r)
	}
	put(dirRecord("\x00", isoRootSector, isoSectorSize, true)) // .
	put(dirRecord("\x01", isoRootSector, isoSectorSize, true)) // ..
	put(dirRecord(engtestCNFName, isoCNFSector, len(SystemCNF()), false))
	put(dirRecord(engtestEXEName, isoEXESector, len(exe), false))

	// Files.
	copy(img[isoCNFSector*isoSectorSize:], SystemCNF())
	copy(img[isoEXESector*isoSectorSize:], exe)
	return img
}

// EnginetestDisc returns the cue sheet text and the
// bin contents for the enginetest disc: the ISO
// image as one MODE1/2048 track. The cue references
// "ENGTEST.BIN", so the two files belong side by
// side under that name.
func EnginetestDisc(exe []byte) (cue string, bin []byte) {
	bin = EnginetestISO(exe)
	cue = fmt.Sprintf("FILE \"ENGTEST.BIN\" BINARY\r\n  TRACK 01 MODE1/2048\r\n    INDEX 01 00:00:00\r\n")
	return cue, bin
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/homebrew/homebrew.go ====================

package homebrew

// Homebrew fixtures for the go-ps1 core: a small MIPS
// assembler, the PS1-3 enginetest guest program (a
// PS-X EXE that drives the BIOS event system, a GPU
// textured quad, SPU ADPCM playback, a CD sector read
// and GTE projection, then writes a PASS magic), and
// synthetic disc images carrying that EXE. The system
// package gates use the in-process builders; the
// libretro shell gates use the file forms. Everything
// here is synthetic: no Sony code, no game data.

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
)

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Register numbers used by the assembler.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

const (
	Zero = 0
	V0   = 2
	A0   = 4
	A1   = 5
	A2   = 6
	A3   = 7
	T0   = 8
	T1   = 9
	T2   = 10
	T3   = 11
	T4   = 12
	T5   = 13
	T6   = 14
	T7   = 15
	S0   = 16
	S1   = 17
	S2   = 18
	S4   = 20
	RA   = 31
)

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// A small MIPS assembler with label fixups.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

const (
	patchBranch = iota
	patchJAL
	patchLoadHi
	patchLoadLo
)

type patch struct {
	idx   int
	kind  int
	label string
}

type Asm struct {
	words   []uint32
	labels  map[string]int
	patches []patch
}

func NewAsm() *Asm {
	return &Asm{labels: map[string]int{}}
}

func (a *Asm) Emit(w uint32) int {
	a.words = append(a.words, w)
	return len(a.words) - 1
}

func (a *Asm) Label(name string) { a.labels[name] = len(a.words) }

func (a *Asm) LabelAt(name string, idx int) { a.labels[name] = idx }

func (a *Asm) Nop() { a.Emit(0x00000000) }

func (a *Asm) Lui(rt, imm uint32) {
	a.Emit(0x3C000000 | rt<<16 | (imm & 0xFFFF))
}

func (a *Asm) Ori(rt, rs, imm uint32) {
	a.Emit(0x34000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | (imm & 0xFFFF))
}

// li loads a 32-bit constant in one or two words.
func (a *Asm) Li(rt, v uint32) {
	switch {
	case v>>16 == 0:
		a.Ori(rt, Zero, v)
	case v&0xFFFF == 0:
		a.Lui(rt, v>>16)
	default:
		a.Lui(rt, v>>16)
		a.Ori(rt, rt, v)
	}
}

// liLabel loads the absolute address of a label.
func (a *Asm) LiLabel(rt uint32, name string) {
	idx := a.Emit(0x3C000000 | rt<<16)
	a.patches = append(a.patches, patch{idx: idx, kind: patchLoadHi, label: name})
	idx = a.Emit(0x34000000 | rt<<21 | rt<<16)
	a.patches = append(a.patches, patch{idx: idx, kind: patchLoadLo, label: name})
}

func (a *Asm) Addiu(rt, rs uint32, imm int) {
	a.Emit(0x24000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(uint16(imm)))
}

func (a *Asm) Addu(rd, rs, rt uint32) {
	a.Emit(0x00000021 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11)
}

func (a *Asm) Andi(rt, rs, imm uint32) {
	a.Emit(0x30000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | (imm & 0xFFFF))
}

func (a *Asm) Lw(rt uint32, off int, rs uint32) {
	a.Emit(0x8C000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(uint16(off)))
}

func (a *Asm) Sw(rt uint32, off int, rs uint32) {
	a.Emit(0xAC000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(uint16(off)))
}

func (a *Asm) Lbu(rt uint32, off int, rs uint32) {
	a.Emit(0x90000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(uint16(off)))
}

func (a *Asm) Sb(rt uint32, off int, rs uint32) {
	a.Emit(0xA0000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(uint16(off)))
}

func (a *Asm) Sh(rt uint32, off int, rs uint32) {
	a.Emit(0xA4000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | uint32(uint16(off)))
}

func (a *Asm) Beq(rs, rt uint32, label string) {
	idx := a.Emit(0x10000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16)
	a.patches = append(a.patches, patch{idx: idx, kind: patchBranch, label: label})
}

func (a *Asm) Bne(rs, rt uint32, label string) {
	idx := a.Emit(0x14000000 | rs<<21 | rt<<16)
	a.patches = append(a.patches, patch{idx: idx, kind: patchBranch, label: label})
}

func (a *Asm) JalAbs(addr uint32) {
	a.Emit(0x0C000000 | ((addr >> 2) & 0x3FFFFFF))
}

func (a *Asm) Jr(rs uint32) { a.Emit(0x00000008 | rs<<21) }

func (a *Asm) Syscall() { a.Emit(0x0000000C) }

// callBIOS emits a vector call: function number in
// $t1, jal to the vector, NOP in the delay slot (the
// HLE intercepts when the PC reaches the vector,
// after the delay slot has executed).
func (a *Asm) CallBIOS(vector uint32, fn int) {
	a.Addiu(T1, Zero, fn)
	a.JalAbs(vector)
	a.Nop()
}

// storeWordAbs stores a constant to an absolute
// address, using $t5 and $t6 as scratch.
func (a *Asm) StoreWordAbs(addr, val uint32) {
	a.Li(T5, addr)
	a.Li(T6, val)
	a.Sw(T6, 0, T5)
}

// storeWordLabelAbs stores a label address to an
// absolute address.
func (a *Asm) StoreWordLabelAbs(addr uint32, label string) {
	a.Li(T5, addr)
	a.LiLabel(T6, label)
	a.Sw(T6, 0, T5)
}

// storeHalfAbs stores a constant halfword to an
// absolute address.
func (a *Asm) StoreHalfAbs(addr, val uint32) {
	a.Li(T5, addr)
	a.Li(T6, val)
	a.Sh(T6, 0, T5)
}

// marker records stage completion: the stage number
// goes to the shared marker word at result+0x100.
// $s0 must hold the result base 0x80020000.
func (a *Asm) Marker(n int) {
	a.Li(T1, uint32(n))
	a.Sw(T1, 0x100, S0)
}

// gpuCW sends one GP0 word through BIOS GPU_cw.
func (a *Asm) GpuCW(w uint32) {
	a.Li(A0, w)
	a.CallBIOS(0xA0, 0x49)
}

func (a *Asm) Mtc2(rt, rd uint32) { a.Emit(0x48800000 | rt<<16 | rd<<11) }
func (a *Asm) Ctc2(rt, rd uint32) { a.Emit(0x48C00000 | rt<<16 | rd<<11) }

// mfc2Store reads a GTE data register into $t0 (with
// the load delay NOP) and stores it at off($s0).
func (a *Asm) Mfc2Store(rd uint32, off int) {
	a.Emit(0x48000000 | T0<<16 | rd<<11) // mfc2 t0, rd
	a.Nop()
	a.Sw(T0, off, S0)
}

// cfc2Store reads a GTE control register the same
// way as mfc2Store.
func (a *Asm) Cfc2Store(rd uint32, off int) {
	a.Emit(0x48400000 | T0<<16 | rd<<11) // cfc2 t0, rd
	a.Nop()
	a.Sw(T0, off, S0)
}

// build resolves all patches against base (the
// address word 0 lands at) and returns the words.
func (a *Asm) Build(base uint32) []uint32 {
	out := append([]uint32(nil), a.words...)
	for _, p := range a.patches {
		li, ok := a.labels[p.label]
		if !ok {
			panic("homebrew: unknown label " + p.label)
		}
		switch p.kind {
		case patchBranch:
			off := li - (p.idx + 1)
			if off < -32768 || off > 32767 {
				panic("homebrew: branch out of range to " + p.label)
			}
			out[p.idx] |= uint32(uint16(off))
		case patchJAL:
			addr := base + uint32(4*li)
			out[p.idx] |= (addr >> 2) & 0x3FFFFFF
		case patchLoadHi:
			addr := base + uint32(4*li)
			out[p.idx] |= (addr >> 16) & 0xFFFF
		case patchLoadLo:
			addr := base + uint32(4*li)
			out[p.idx] |= addr & 0xFFFF
		}
	}
	return out
}

// spin emits an endless self loop with its NOP
// delay slot.
func (a *Asm) Spin(name string) {
	a.Label(name)
	a.Beq(Zero, Zero, name)
	a.Nop()
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// Fixtures: the 16x16 texture table and the ADPCM
// tone (encoder copied in shape from the spu package
// tests, which document the decoder math from the
// psx-spx XA chapter).
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

// textureWords builds the 128 data words of the
// 16x16 texture: two halfword pixels per word, low
// first, with one solid color per quadrant.
func textureWords() []uint32 {
	color := func(x, y int) uint32 {
		switch {
		case x < 8 && y < 8:
			return 0x001F // red
		case x >= 8 && y < 8:
			return 0x03E0 // green
		case x < 8:
			return 0x7C00 // blue
		default:
			return 0x7FFF // white
		}
	}
	out := make([]uint32, 0, 128)
	for wi := 0; wi < 128; wi++ {
		var w uint32
		for half := 0; half < 2; half++ {
			p := wi*2 + half
			w |= color(p%16, p/16) << (16 * half)
		}
		out = append(out, w)
	}
	return out
}

var ps3EncF0 = [5]int32{0, 60, 115, 98, 122}
var ps3EncF1 = [5]int32{0, 0, -52, -55, -60}

func encRecon(nib, shift, f0, f1, old, older int32) int32 {
	s := (nib<<12)>>uint(shift) + (old*f0+older*f1+32)/64
	if s > 0x7FFF {
		s = 0x7FFF
	}
	if s < -0x8000 {
		s = -0x8000
	}
	return s
}

func encodeBlock(pcm []int16, old, older int32) ([16]byte, int32, int32) {
	var best [16]byte
	bestErr := int64(-1)
	var bestOld, bestOlder int32
	for filter := 0; filter <= 4; filter++ {
		for shift := 0; shift <= 12; shift++ {
			var blk [16]byte
			blk[0] = byte(filter<<4 | shift)
			o, oo := old, older
			err := int64(0)
			var nibs [28]int32
			for i := 0; i < 28; i++ {
				target := int32(pcm[i])
				bn, be := int32(0), int64(-1)
				for nib := int32(-8); nib <= 7; nib++ {
					r := encRecon(nib, int32(shift), ps3EncF0[filter], ps3EncF1[filter], o, oo)
					d := int64(r - target)
					if be < 0 || d*d < be {
						be, bn = d*d, nib
					}
				}
				r := encRecon(bn, int32(shift), ps3EncF0[filter], ps3EncF1[filter], o, oo)
				oo, o = o, r
				err += be
				nibs[i] = bn
			}
			if bestErr < 0 || err < bestErr {
				bestErr, bestOld, bestOlder = err, o, oo
				copy(best[:], blk[:])
				for i := 0; i < 28; i++ {
					u := uint8(nibs[i] & 0xF)
					if i&1 == 0 {
						best[2+i/2] |= u
					} else {
						best[2+i/2] |= u << 4
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return best, bestOld, bestOlder
}

// EncodeLoop encodes pcm as a seamlessly looping
// ADPCM stream: three encoding passes so the decoder
// state at the end matches the start, then the loop
// start flag on block 0 and loop end plus repeat on
// the last block.
func EncodeLoop(pcm []int16) []byte {
	var out []byte
	var old, older int32
	for pass := 0; pass < 3; pass++ {
		out = nil
		for i := 0; i+28 <= len(pcm); i += 28 {
			blk, o, oo := encodeBlock(pcm[i:i+28], old, older)
			old, older = o, oo
			out = append(out, blk[:]...)
		}
	}
	out[1] |= 4           // loop start on first block
	out[len(out)-15] |= 3 // loop end + repeat on last block
	return out
}

// SinePCM makes a sine: 2800 samples with 28
// periods is 441 Hz at the 44100 Hz sample rate.
func SinePCM(n, periods int, amp float64) []int16 {
	out := make([]int16, n)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = int16(amp * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(periods)*float64(i)/float64(n)))
	}
	return out
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// PS-X EXE builder.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

func BuildEXE(text []uint32) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 0x800+4*len(text))
	copy(out[0:8], "PS-X EXE")
	put := func(off int, v uint32) { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], v) }
	put(0x10, 0x80010000) // pc0
	put(0x14, 0)          // gp0
	put(0x18, 0x80010000) // t_addr
	put(0x1C, uint32(4*len(text)))
	put(0x30, 0x800F0000) // s_addr, so SP = 0x80100000
	put(0x34, 0x10000)    // s_size
	for i, w := range text {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[0x800+4*i:], w)
	}
	return out
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// The enginetest guest program. Result area base
// 0x80020000 ($s0): PASS magic at +0x00, stage marker
// at +0x100, CD checksum at +0x104, GTE results at
// +0x108 onward. CD buffer at 0x80030000.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

func EngineWords(tone []byte) []uint32 {
	a := NewAsm()
	a.Lui(S0, 0x8002) // result base 0x80020000

	// Stage A: critical section plus VBlank events.
	a.Li(A0, 1)
	a.Syscall() // EnterCriticalSection
	a.Li(A0, 0xF0000001)
	a.Li(A1, 0x1000)
	a.Li(A2, 0x2000)
	a.Li(A3, 0)
	a.CallBIOS(0xB0, 0x08) // OpenEvent(VBlank, IRQ spec, ready mode, no func)
	a.Addu(S1, V0, Zero)
	a.Addu(A0, S1, Zero)
	a.CallBIOS(0xB0, 0x0C) // EnableEvent(handle)
	a.Li(A0, 2)
	a.Syscall()                   // ExitCriticalSection
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F801074, 1) // I_MASK = VBlank
	a.Marker(1)
	a.Addiu(S2, Zero, 0) // delivery count
	a.Label("pollA")
	a.Addu(A0, S1, Zero)
	a.CallBIOS(0xB0, 0x0B) // TestEvent(handle)
	a.Beq(V0, Zero, "pollA")
	a.Nop()
	a.Addiu(S2, S2, 1)
	a.Addiu(T0, Zero, 3)
	a.Bne(S2, T0, "pollA")
	a.Nop()
	a.Marker(2)

	// Stage B: GPU display setup, texture upload,
	// textured quad.
	for _, w := range []uint32{0x00000000, 0x06C60260, 0x07041020, 0x08000001, 0x05000000} {
		a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F801814, w) // GP1 direct
	}
	// The display enable GP1 word (0x03000000) is
	// deferred until after the quad is drawn, below:
	// gpu.plot suppresses drawing into the display
	// area while the display is enabled and the E1
	// draw-to-display bit is clear, so enabling first
	// would make the quad undrawable by design.
	for _, w := range []uint32{0xE1000000, 0xE3000000, 0xE403BD3F, 0xE5000000, 0xE6000000} {
		a.GpuCW(w)
	}
	a.GpuCW(0xA0000000) // CPU to VRAM transfer
	a.GpuCW(0x01000000) // dest (0,256): (256<<16)|0
	a.GpuCW(0x00100010) // size 16x16: (16<<16)|16
	a.LiLabel(A0, "texTable")
	a.Li(A1, 128)
	a.CallBIOS(0xA0, 0x4A) // GPU_cwp(table, 128)
	for _, w := range []uint32{
		0x2C808080, // textured quad, neutral color
		0x00200020, // v0 (32,32)
		0x00000000, // uv0 (0,0)
		0x00200060, // v1 (96,32)
		0x01100010, // uv1: texpage 0x0110 in high half, u=16, v=0
		0x00600020, // v2 (32,96)
		0x00001000, // uv2: u=0, v=16
		0x00600060, // v3 (96,96)
		0x00001010, // uv3: u=16, v=16
	} {
		a.GpuCW(w)
	}
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F801814, 0x03000000) // GP1 display enable, after the draw
	a.Marker(3)

	// Stage C: SPU. The tone goes to SPU RAM byte
	// 0x1000 (TSA 0x200 in 8-byte units) through DMA
	// channel 4, then voice 0 plays it looped.
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801DA6, 0x200)           // TSA
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F8010F0, 0x80000)         // DPCR: channel 4 enable (bit 19)
	a.StoreWordLabelAbs(0x1F8010C0, "toneData") // DMA4 MADR
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F8010C4, 400)             // DMA4 BCR: 1600 bytes in words
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F8010C8, 0x01000001)      // DMA4 CHCR: from RAM, sync 0, start
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801C00, 0x3FFF)          // voice 0 VOLL
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801C02, 0x3FFF)          // voice 0 VOLR
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801C04, 0x1000)          // voice 0 pitch (44100 Hz)
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801C06, 0x200)           // voice 0 SSA (byte 0x1000)
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801C08, 0x000F)          // voice 0 ADSR1: fast attack, sustain 15
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801C0A, 0x1FDF)          // voice 0 ADSR2: sustain never steps
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801D80, 0x7FFF)          // main volume L
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801D82, 0x7FFF)          // main volume R
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801DB0, 0)               // CD volume L
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801DB2, 0)               // CD volume R
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801DAA, 0xC000)          // SPUCNT: on, unmuted
	a.StoreHalfAbs(0x1F801D88, 1)               // KON voice 0
	a.Marker(4)

	// Stage D: CD sector 0 into RAM, checksummed.
	a.Lui(S4, 0x1F80) // CD register base
	a.Sb(Zero, 0x1800, S4)
	a.Li(T0, 0x1F)
	a.Sb(T0, 0x1803, S4) // IRQ enable (index 0)
	a.Sb(Zero, 0x1802, S4)
	a.Li(T0, 0x02)
	a.Sb(T0, 0x1802, S4)
	a.Sb(Zero, 0x1802, S4) // Setloc params 00:02:00 (LBA 0)
	a.Li(T0, 0x02)
	a.Sb(T0, 0x1801, S4) // Setloc command
	a.Lbu(T7, 0x1801, S4)
	a.Li(T0, 0x06)
	a.Sb(T0, 0x1801, S4) // ReadN command
	a.Li(T2, 0)
	a.Li(T3, 20000000) // poll cap
	a.Label("cdPoll")
	a.Lbu(T0, 0x1800, S4)
	a.Nop() // load delay before consuming $t0
	a.Andi(T0, T0, 0x40)
	a.Bne(T0, Zero, "cdReady")
	a.Nop()
	a.Addiu(T2, T2, 1)
	a.Bne(T2, T3, "cdPoll")
	a.Nop()
	a.Beq(Zero, Zero, "cdTimeout")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("cdTimeout")
	a.Li(T1, 0xEE)
	a.Sw(T1, 0x100, S0)
	a.Spin("cdSpin")
	a.Label("cdReady")
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F8010F0, 0x8000) // DPCR: channel 3 enable
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F8010B0, 0x80030000)
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F8010B4, 512)
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F8010B8, 0x01000000) // CHCR: to RAM, sync 0, start
	a.Li(T0, 0x80030000)
	a.Addiu(T1, Zero, 0)
	a.Li(T2, 512)
	a.Addiu(T3, Zero, 0)
	a.Label("cdSum")
	a.Lw(T4, 0, T0)
	a.Nop() // load delay before consuming $t4
	a.Addu(T3, T3, T4)
	a.Addiu(T0, T0, 4)
	a.Addiu(T1, T1, 1)
	a.Bne(T1, T2, "cdSum")
	a.Nop()
	a.Sw(T3, 0x104, S0)
	a.Marker(5)

	// Stage E: GTE RTPS under the identity rotation.
	for _, cr := range []struct {
		reg uint32
		val uint32
	}{
		{0, 0x00001000},  // R11=1.0 (low), R12=0 (high)
		{1, 0x00000000},  // R13=0, R21=0
		{2, 0x00001000},  // R22=1.0 (low), R23=0
		{3, 0x00000000},  // R31=0, R32=0
		{4, 0x00001000},  // R33=1.0
		{24, 0x00A00000}, // OFX = 160 in 16.16
		{25, 0x00780000}, // OFY = 120 in 16.16
		{26, 200},        // H
		{27, 0},          // DQA
		{28, 0},          // DQB
	} {
		a.Li(T0, cr.val)
		a.Ctc2(T0, cr.reg)
	}
	a.Li(T0, 0)
	a.Mtc2(T0, 0) // V0 X=0, Y=0
	a.Li(T0, 300)
	a.Mtc2(T0, 1) // V0 Z=300
	// COP2 command word: rs field 0x10 selects a GTE
	// command in r3000a execCOP2, low bits carry the
	// command with sf (bit 19) set and opcode 0x01
	// (RTPS).
	a.Emit(0x4A080001)
	a.Nop()
	a.Nop()
	a.Mfc2Store(15, 0x108) // SXYP
	a.Mfc2Store(19, 0x10C) // SZ3
	a.Cfc2Store(31, 0x110) // FLAG
	a.Li(T0, 0xFFCE0064)
	a.Mtc2(T0, 0) // V0 X=100, Y=-50
	a.Li(T0, 300)
	a.Mtc2(T0, 1) // V0 Z=300
	a.Emit(0x4A080001)
	a.Nop()
	a.Nop()
	a.Mfc2Store(15, 0x114) // SXYP, second point
	a.Marker(6)

	// PASS magic, written last.
	a.Li(T1, 0x600DF00D)
	a.Sw(T1, 0, S0)
	a.Spin("spin")

	// Embedded data: the texture table, then the
	// ADPCM tone (100 blocks, 1600 bytes, 400 words).
	a.LabelAt("texTable", len(a.words))
	text := append([]uint32(nil), a.words...)
	text = append(text, textureWords()...)
	a.LabelAt("toneData", len(text))
	for i := 0; i+4 <= len(tone); i += 4 {
		text = append(text, binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(tone[i:]))
	}
	// Patch resolution needs the final label table
	// with the data labels in place, so stash the
	// appended words back and build for real.
	a.words = text
	return a.Build(0x80010000)
}

// Len returns the number of words emitted so far.
// Tests pad programs to fixed offsets with it.
func (a *Asm) Len() int { return len(a.words) }

// EnginetestEXE returns the canonical enginetest
// guest: the engine program playing the 440 Hz
// ADPCM tone (2,800 samples, 28 periods, amplitude
// 12,000; the encoded loop is exactly 1,600 bytes,
// 100 ADPCM blocks), wrapped as a PS-X EXE.
func EnginetestEXE() []byte {
	tone := EncodeLoop(SinePCM(2800, 28, 12000))
	return BuildEXE(EngineWords(tone))
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/libretro/main.go ====================

// Command libretro is the libretro shell for the
// from-scratch Go PlayStation core (PS1-4). It
// follows the family pattern set by the SNES and
// Genesis shells: a c-shared package main exporting
// the retro_* C ABI, with the machine behind it in
// the system package.
//
// Choices specific to this core:
//
//   - Content loads by path (need_fullpath): discs
//     (.cue, .bin, .iso, .img) open through the cd
//     image layer and boot through SYSTEM.CNF, the
//     way the console boots them; a bare .exe is an
//     HLE-booted PS-X executable. A disc with no
//     bootable SYSTEM.CNF is rejected, like the
//     third-party core it replaces rejects it.
//   - The guest framebuffer is presented at the
//     machine's current native display size every
//     frame (PlayStation games change resolution
//     mid-game), with a SET_GEOMETRY notice when the
//     size changes. Base geometry 320x240, max
//     640x480, aspect 4:3 (the app convention).
//   - The pad is forced into analog mode at load:
//     this shell always presents an analog pad. The
//     digital buttons still read digitally; the
//     sticks come from the libretro analog axes.
//   - Rumble is wired to the pad motor state through
//     SET_RUMBLE_INTERFACE when the frontend offers
//     it: the weak effect is the small motor (on or
//     off), the strong effect is the large motor
//     byte scaled to 16 bits. Frontends that do not
//     offer the interface (the iTaK Go bridge does
//     not) simply never rumble.
//   - At unload, the machine's not-implemented
//     diagnostics (unimplemented BIOS calls, unknown
//     CD and GP1 commands) are printed through the
//     frontend log interface when any were seen, so
//     a real game failing on the TV names exactly
//     what it called that this core does not have.
package main

/*
#cgo CFLAGS: -std=c11

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef bool (*ps1_environ_cb_t)(unsigned cmd, void *data);
typedef void (*ps1_video_refresh_cb_t)(const void *data, unsigned width, unsigned height, size_t pitch);
typedef void (*ps1_audio_sample_cb_t)(int16_t left, int16_t right);
typedef size_t (*ps1_audio_sample_batch_cb_t)(const int16_t *data, size_t frames);
typedef void (*ps1_input_poll_cb_t)(void);
typedef int16_t (*ps1_input_state_cb_t)(unsigned port, unsigned device, unsigned index, unsigned id);
typedef void (*ps1_log_printf_t)(int level, const char *fmt, ...);
typedef bool (*ps1_set_rumble_state_t)(unsigned port, int effect, uint16_t strength);

static ps1_environ_cb_t ps1_environ_cb;
static ps1_video_refresh_cb_t ps1_video_cb;
static ps1_audio_sample_cb_t ps1_audio_cb;
static ps1_audio_sample_batch_cb_t ps1_audio_batch_cb;
static ps1_input_poll_cb_t ps1_input_poll_cb;
static ps1_input_state_cb_t ps1_input_state_cb;
static ps1_log_printf_t ps1_log_fn;
static ps1_set_rumble_state_t ps1_rumble_fn;

static void ps1_set_environ_cb(ps1_environ_cb_t cb) { ps1_environ_cb = cb; }
static void ps1_set_video_cb(ps1_video_refresh_cb_t cb) { ps1_video_cb = cb; }
static void ps1_set_audio_cb(ps1_audio_sample_cb_t cb) { ps1_audio_cb = cb; }
static void ps1_set_audio_batch_cb(ps1_audio_sample_batch_cb_t cb) { ps1_audio_batch_cb = cb; }
static void ps1_set_input_poll_cb(ps1_input_poll_cb_t cb) { ps1_input_poll_cb = cb; }
static void ps1_set_input_state_cb(ps1_input_state_cb_t cb) { ps1_input_state_cb = cb; }

static bool ps1_call_environ(unsigned cmd, void *data) {
	if (!ps1_environ_cb) return false;
	return ps1_environ_cb(cmd, data);
}
static void ps1_call_video(const void *data, unsigned w, unsigned h, size_t pitch) {
	if (ps1_video_cb) ps1_video_cb(data, w, h, pitch);
}
static void ps1_call_audio(int16_t l, int16_t r) {
	if (ps1_audio_cb) ps1_audio_cb(l, r);
}
static size_t ps1_call_audio_batch(const int16_t *data, size_t frames) {
	if (!ps1_audio_batch_cb) return 0;
	return ps1_audio_batch_cb(data, frames);
}
static void ps1_call_input_poll(void) {
	if (ps1_input_poll_cb) ps1_input_poll_cb();
}
static int16_t ps1_call_input_state(unsigned port, unsigned device, unsigned index, unsigned id) {
	if (!ps1_input_state_cb) return 0;
	return ps1_input_state_cb(port, device, index, id);
}

struct ps1_log_callback { ps1_log_printf_t log; };
static void ps1_grab_log(void *data) {
	struct ps1_log_callback *lc = (struct ps1_log_callback *)data;
	if (ps1_call_environ(27, data)) { // GET_LOG_INTERFACE
		ps1_log_fn = lc->log;
	}
}
static void ps1_log_msg(int level, const char *msg) {
	if (ps1_log_fn) ps1_log_fn(level, "%s", msg);
}

struct ps1_rumble_interface { ps1_set_rumble_state_t set_rumble_state; };
static void ps1_grab_rumble(void *data) {
	struct ps1_rumble_interface *ri = (struct ps1_rumble_interface *)data;
	if (ps1_call_environ(23, data)) { // SET_RUMBLE_INTERFACE
		ps1_rumble_fn = ri->set_rumble_state;
	}
}
static void ps1_call_rumble(unsigned port, int effect, uint16_t strength) {
	if (ps1_rumble_fn) ps1_rumble_fn(port, effect, strength);
}

struct ps1_game_info {
	const char *path;
	const void *data;
	size_t size;
	const char *meta;
};

struct ps1_system_info {
	const char *library_name;
	const char *library_version;
	const char *valid_extensions;
	bool need_fullpath;
	bool block_extract;
};

struct ps1_game_geometry {
	unsigned base_width;
	unsigned base_height;
	unsigned max_width;
	unsigned max_height;
	float aspect_ratio;
};

struct ps1_system_timing {
	double fps;
	double sample_rate;
};

struct ps1_system_av_info {
	struct ps1_game_geometry geometry;
	struct ps1_system_timing timing;
};

static const char *ps1_core_name(void) { return "iTaK GoPS1"; }
static const char *ps1_core_version(void) { return "0.1"; }
static const char *ps1_core_extensions(void) { return "cue|bin|iso|exe"; }
*/
import "C"

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/system"
)

// libretro constants used by this shell.
const (
	envSetPixelFormat     = 10
	envGetLogInterface    = 27 // handled inside the C helper
	envSetRumbleInterface = 23 // handled inside the C helper
	envSetGeometry        = 37

	pixelFormatXRGB8888 = 1

	deviceJoypad = 1
	deviceAnalog = 5

	rumbleStrong = 0
	rumbleWeak   = 1

	logInfo = 1
	logWarn = 2

	memSaveRAM   = 0 // RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM
	memSystemRAM = 1 // RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM
)

var (
	sys        *system.Machine
	videoW     int
	videoH     int
	diagLogged bool
	lastSmall  bool
	lastBig    uint8
)

// joypadMap pairs libretro joypad ids with the PS1
// pad bits they drive: the standard libretro pad
// layout mapped onto the PlayStation pad.
var joypadMap = []struct {
	id  uint
	bit uint32
}{
	{0, system.ButtonCross},  // B
	{1, system.ButtonSquare}, // Y
	{2, system.ButtonSelect}, // Select
	{3, system.ButtonStart},  // Start
	{4, system.ButtonUp},     // Up
	{5, system.ButtonDown},   // Down
	{6, system.ButtonLeft},   // Left
	{7, system.ButtonRight},  // Right
	{8, system.ButtonCircle}, // A
	{9, system.ButtonTri},    // X
	{10, system.ButtonL1},    // L
	{11, system.ButtonR1},    // R
	{12, system.ButtonL2},    // L2
	{13, system.ButtonR2},    // R2
	{14, system.ButtonL3},    // L3
	{15, system.ButtonR3},    // R3
}

// ps1Log prints one line through the frontend log
// interface when one was offered.
func ps1Log(level int, msg string) {
	cmsg := C.CString(msg)
	C.ps1_log_msg(C.int(level), cmsg)
	C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cmsg))
}

// logDiagnostics emits the machine's
// not-implemented tally, once per loaded game, when
// anything unimplemented was seen. The iTaK bridge
// prints core log lines to stderr; RetroArch shows
// them in its log.
func logDiagnostics() {
	if sys == nil || diagLogged {
		return
	}
	diagLogged = true
	d := sys.Diagnostics()
	if d.Empty() {
		return
	}
	ps1Log(logWarn, "[GoPS1] not-implemented report: "+d.String())
}

// loadPath loads content from a filesystem path:
// discs boot through SYSTEM.CNF, .exe files boot
// directly. It is the Go-level core of
// retro_load_game, kept plainly typed so the shell
// test can drive it in-process.
func loadPath(path string, data []byte) bool {
	m := system.New()
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".exe":
		if len(data) == 0 {
			b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
			if err != nil {
				ps1Log(logWarn, "[GoPS1] cannot read "+path)
				return false
			}
			data = b
		}
		if err := m.LoadEXE(data); err != nil {
			ps1Log(logWarn, "[GoPS1] bad PS-X EXE: "+err.Error())
			return false
		}
	case ".cue", ".bin", ".iso", ".img":
		if err := m.OpenDisc(path); err != nil {
			ps1Log(logWarn, "[GoPS1] cannot open disc image: "+err.Error())
			return false
		}
		if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
			ps1Log(logWarn, "[GoPS1] disc does not boot: "+err.Error())
			return false
		}
	default:
		// A data-only load with no usable path: a
		// PS-X EXE is recognizable by its magic.
		if len(data) >= 8 && string(data[:8]) == "PS-X EXE" {
			if err := m.LoadEXE(data); err != nil {
				ps1Log(logWarn, "[GoPS1] bad PS-X EXE: "+err.Error())
				return false
			}
			break
		}
		ps1Log(logWarn, "[GoPS1] unsupported content: "+path)
		return false
	}
	pf := C.int(pixelFormatXRGB8888)
	C.ps1_call_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&pf))
	// The shell always presents an analog pad (see
	// the package comment).
	m.SetAnalogMode(true)
	sys = m
	diagLogged = false
	lastSmall, lastBig = false, 0
	videoW, videoH = m.DisplayWidth(), m.DisplayHeight()
	ps1Log(logInfo, "[GoPS1] loaded "+path)
	return true
}

// axis reads one libretro analog axis as an
// unsigned stick byte, 128 centered.
func axis(index, id uint) uint8 {
	v := int(C.ps1_call_input_state(0, deviceAnalog, C.uint(index), C.uint(id)))
	return uint8((v >> 8) + 128)
}

// runFrame advances the loaded machine one frame,
// presenting video and audio. It is the Go-level
// core of retro_run.
func runFrame() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	C.ps1_call_input_poll()
	var mask uint32
	for _, b := range joypadMap {
		if C.ps1_call_input_state(0, deviceJoypad, 0, C.uint(b.id)) != 0 {
			mask |= b.bit
		}
	}
	sys.SetButtons(mask)
	// SetAnalog takes (rx, ry, lx, ly): right stick
	// is analog index 1, left stick index 0.
	sys.SetAnalog(axis(1, 0), axis(1, 1), axis(0, 0), axis(0, 1))
	sys.RunFrame()

	// Rumble follows the pad motor state when the
	// frontend offered the interface.
	small, big := sys.PAD.Motors()
	if small != lastSmall || big != lastBig {
		lastSmall, lastBig = small, big
		weak := uint16(0)
		if small {
			weak = 0xFFFF
		}
		C.ps1_call_rumble(0, rumbleWeak, C.uint16_t(weak))
		C.ps1_call_rumble(0, rumbleStrong, C.uint16_t(uint16(big)*0x101))
	}

	w, h := sys.DisplayWidth(), sys.DisplayHeight()
	if w != videoW || h != videoH {
		videoW, videoH = w, h
		geom := C.struct_ps1_game_geometry{
			base_width:   C.uint(w),
			base_height:  C.uint(h),
			max_width:    640,
			max_height:   480,
			aspect_ratio: 4.0 / 3.0,
		}
		C.ps1_call_environ(envSetGeometry, unsafe.Pointer(&geom))
	}
	if fb := sys.Framebuffer(); len(fb) >= w*h && w > 0 && h > 0 {
		C.ps1_call_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]), C.uint(w), C.uint(h), C.size_t(w*4))
	}
	samples := sys.AudioBuffer()
	if len(samples) == 0 {
		return
	}
	frames := len(samples) / 2
	done := int(C.ps1_call_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&samples[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
	for i := done * 2; i+1 < len(samples); i += 2 {
		C.ps1_call_audio(C.int16_t(samples[i]), C.int16_t(samples[i+1]))
	}
}

//export retro_api_version
func retro_api_version() C.uint { return 1 }

func retro_deinit() {
	// The iTaK bridge calls retro_deinit without a
	// preceding retro_unload_game; emit the
	// diagnostics here too (guarded to once).
	logDiagnostics()
	sys = nil
}

	info.geometry.max_width = 640

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_ps1_game_info) bool {
	if info == nil {
		return false
	}
	path := ""
	if info.path != nil {
		path = C.GoString(info.path)
	}
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	}
	return loadPath(path, data)
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() {
	logDiagnostics()
	sys = nil
}

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	sys.Reset()
	// Reset restores the pad to digital; the shell's
	// analog choice is reapplied (the machine also
	// reapplies its stored host choice).
	sys.SetAnalogMode(true)
	videoW, videoH = sys.DisplayWidth(), sys.DisplayHeight()
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() { runFrame() }

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.StateSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) bool {
	if sys == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	if int(size) < len(state) {
		return false
	}
	C.memcpy(data, unsafe.Pointer(&state[0]), C.size_t(len(state)))
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) bool {
	if sys == nil {
		return false
	}
	return sys.Deserialize(C.GoBytes(data, C.int(size))) == nil
}

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.uint) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		// The 128 KB memory card image.
		return unsafe.Pointer(&sys.CardImage()[0])
	case memSystemRAM:
		return unsafe.Pointer(&sys.SystemRAM()[0])
	}
	return nil
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.uint) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.CardImage()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SystemRAM()))
	}
	return 0
}
