==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/libretro/main_test.go ====================

package main

// In-process shell gates. The payloads are the
// homebrew enginetest EXE and the synthetic cue/bin
// disc carrying it, driven through the same Go-level
// load and run functions the retro_* exports wrap.
// The literal C ABI is gated end to end by the
// shared enginetest harness (go_backend), which
// loads the built .so through the production bridge;
// this test exists so go test alone catches shell
// regressions: load by extension, boot, PASS magic,
// save state round trip, memory regions, clean
// rejection of bad content.

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/homebrew"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/system"
)

func runUntilPass(t *testing.T) bool {
	t.Helper()
	if sys == nil {
		t.Fatal("no machine loaded")
	}
	for frame := 0; frame < 180; frame++ {
		runFrame()
		if frame%10 == 9 && sys.Bus.Read32(0x80020000) == 0x600DF00D {
			return true
		}
	}
	return sys.Bus.Read32(0x80020000) == 0x600DF00D
}

// runUntilStage advances until the guest's stage
// marker (result +0x100) reaches want, or the frame
// budget runs out.
func runUntilStage(want uint32, maxFrames int) bool {
	for frame := 0; frame < maxFrames; frame++ {
		runFrame()
		if frame%10 == 9 && sys.Bus.Read32(0x80020100) >= want {
			return true
		}
	}
	return sys.Bus.Read32(0x80020100) >= want
}

func TestShellEXE(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	exe := homebrew.EnginetestEXE()
	exePath := filepath.Join(dir, "engtest.exe")
	if err := os.WriteFile(exePath, exe, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !loadPath(exePath, exe) {
		t.Fatal("loadPath(.exe) returned false")
	}
	defer func() { sys = nil }()
	if sys == nil {
		t.Fatal("machine not set after load")
	}
	if !sys.AnalogMode() {
		t.Error("analog mode actual false after shell load, want forced on")
	}
	// A bare .exe load has no disc attached, and
	// this guest's stage D reads a CD sector: with
	// nothing to read it parks in its timeout spin
	// after stage 4 (its CD poll cap). The full PASS
	// run needs the disc, which TestShellDisc does
	// through the .cue. Here the gate is: the BIOS
	// event stage, GPU stage and SPU stage all
	// complete (marker 4) and the quad is on screen.
	if !runUntilStage(4, 180) {
		t.Fatalf("guest stage marker actual %d through the shell (EXE), want 4", sys.Bus.Read32(0x80020100))
	}
	if w, h := sys.DisplayWidth(), sys.DisplayHeight(); w != 320 || h != 240 {
		t.Errorf("display size after the guest's GP1 setup actual %dx%d, want 320x240", w, h)
	}
	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	nonblack := 0
	for _, px := range fb {
		if px != 0xFF000000 {
			nonblack++
		}
	}
	if nonblack == 0 {
		t.Error("framebuffer is all black after the GPU stage")
	}
	if got := sys.UnimplementedBIOSCallCount(); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("unimplemented BIOS calls actual %d, want 0", got)
	}

	// Save state round trip through the machine the
	// shell wraps (retro_serialize forwards here).
	saved := sys.Serialize()
	if len(saved) != sys.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state length actual %d, want StateSize %d", len(saved), sys.StateSize())
	}
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	m2 := system.New()
	if err := m2.Deserialize(saved); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if again := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(saved, again) {
		t.Error("state bytes differ after a serialize/deserialize round trip")
	}

	// Memory regions the shell exposes: the card is
	// 128 KB, main RAM is 2 MB.
	if got := len(sys.CardImage()); got != 128*1024 {
		t.Errorf("card image length actual %d, want %d", got, 128*1024)
	}
	if got := len(sys.SystemRAM()); got != 2*1024*1024 {
		t.Errorf("system RAM length actual %d, want %d", got, 2*1024*1024)
	}
}

func TestShellDisc(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	exe := homebrew.EnginetestEXE()
	cue, bin := homebrew.EnginetestDisc(exe)
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "ENGTEST.BIN"), bin, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cuePath := filepath.Join(dir, "engtest.cue")
	if err := os.WriteFile(cuePath, []byte(cue), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !loadPath(cuePath, []byte(cue)) {
		t.Fatal("loadPath(.cue) returned false")
	}
	defer func() { sys = nil }()
	if !runUntilPass(t) {
		t.Fatal("guest PASS magic not reached through the shell (disc)")
	}
}

func TestShellRejectsBadContent(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	bogus := filepath.Join(dir, "bogus.exe")
	if err := os.WriteFile(bogus, []byte("definitely not a PS-X EXE"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if loadPath(bogus, nil) {
		t.Error("loadPath accepted a non-EXE .exe file")
	}
	missing := filepath.Join(dir, "missing.cue")
	if loadPath(missing, nil) {
		t.Error("loadPath accepted a missing .cue file")
	}
	// A readable image with no SYSTEM.CNF does not
	// boot and is rejected.
	raw := filepath.Join(dir, "data.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(raw, make([]byte, 40*2048), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if loadPath(raw, nil) {
		t.Error("loadPath accepted an unbootable .iso")
	}
	if sys != nil {
		t.Error("a rejected load left a machine behind")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/mdec/bs.go ====================

package mdec

// BS Huffman layer (extension, not hardware).
//
// Sections 13.19 to 13.21 describe the BS bitstream
// format used by STR movies and BS picture files:
// software Huffman decodes a BS stream into the same
// 16 bit run length codes that the MDEC hardware then
// consumes. Real software does that decoding on the
// CPU (often with the GTE) and never sends Huffman
// data to the MDEC ports. This file implements that
// documented software layer inside the package as an
// extension so it is testable on its own terms:
//
//   - It is selected only when bit 24 of the MDEC(1)
//     command word is set. Bit 24 is one of the bits
//     section 6.2 lists as not used (should be zero),
//     so no documented hardware stream can select it
//     by accident. With bit 24 clear, WriteWord is
//     pure hardware behavior.
//   - In BS mode the parameter words start with the
//     BS v1/v2/v3 header of section 13.19, packed as
//     two words: word 0 holds the MDEC size divided
//     by 4 in its low halfword and the file ID 3800h
//     in its high halfword (the size and ID are read
//     and otherwise unused), word 1 holds the quant
//     value in its low halfword and the version in
//     its high halfword.
//   - The bitstream follows, MSB first inside each
//     16 bit halfword, halfwords in low first order
//     inside each word (the good for PSX arrangement
//     of section 13.11: first bit in bit 15 of the
//     first halfword).
//   - Version 1 and 2 use raw signed 10 bit DC values
//     with the 0111111111b end of frame code, and
//     version 3 uses the Huffman DC offsets of
//     section 13.20, per section 13.20's DC v1/v2 and
//     DC v3 entries. AC values for all of v1, v2 and
//     v3 use the Huffman table of section 13.21.
//   - Each decoded DC or AC symbol is turned into the
//     equivalent run length code and fed through the
//     same startBlock and acStep path as hardware
//     input, so dequantization, IDCT, color
//     conversion and output are shared, not forked.

// bsWriteWord handles one parameter word in BS mode.
func (d *MDEC) bsWriteWord(w uint32) {
	switch d.bsStage {
	case 0:
		// BS header word 0: size/4 and file ID
		// 3800h. Both are accepted as documented
		// and not otherwise used.
		d.bsStage = 1
	case 1:
		d.bsQuant = int(uint16(w)) & 0x3F
		d.bsVersion = int(uint16(w >> 16))
		d.bsStage = 2
	default:
		if d.bsEnded {
			return
		}
		d.bitQ = append(d.bitQ, uint16(w), uint16(w>>16))
		d.bsPump()
	}
}

// availBits returns the number of unconsumed bits in
// the bit queue.
func (d *MDEC) availBits() int {
	n := (len(d.bitQ)-d.bitHead)*16 - d.bitPos
	if n < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return n
}

// peekBits returns the next n bits (n at most 24)
// without consuming them, MSB first, or false when
// fewer than n bits are queued.
func (d *MDEC) peekBits(n int) (uint32, bool) {
	if d.availBits() < n {
		return 0, false
	}
	var out uint32
	idx := d.bitHead
	pos := d.bitPos
	rem := n
	for rem > 0 {
		h := d.bitQ[idx]
		take := 16 - pos
		if take > rem {
			take = rem
		}
		seg := (uint32(h) >> uint(16-pos-take)) & ((1 << uint(take)) - 1)
		out = out<<uint(take) | seg
		pos += take
		rem -= take
		if pos == 16 {
			idx++
			pos = 0
		}
	}
	return out, true
}

// consumeBits drops n bits from the bit queue.
func (d *MDEC) consumeBits(n int) {
	d.bitPos += n
	for d.bitPos >= 16 {
		d.bitPos -= 16
		d.bitHead++
	}
	if d.bitHead > 1024 {
		d.bitQ = append([]uint16(nil), d.bitQ[d.bitHead:]...)
		d.bitHead = 0
	}
}

// bsDecodeResult classifies one BS decode attempt.
type bsResult int

const (
	bsNeedMore bsResult = iota
	bsOK
	bsEndedFrame
	bsSkipped
)

// bsPump decodes as many complete symbols as the
// queued bits allow. It returns when the next symbol
// is incomplete; the rest of the symbol stays queued
// for the next parameter word.
func (d *MDEC) bsPump() {
	for !d.bsEnded {
		if d.blkState == blkNeedDC {
			if res := d.bsDecodeDC(); res == bsNeedMore {
				return
			} else if res == bsEndedFrame {
				d.bsEnded = true
				return
			}
		} else {
			if res := d.bsDecodeAC(); res == bsNeedMore {
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

// bsIsChroma reports whether the block currently
// being decoded is a Cr or Cb block.
func (d *MDEC) bsIsChroma() bool {
	return !d.mono() && d.mbIdx < 2
}

// bsDecodeDC decodes one DC value in BS mode and
// starts the block with the synthesized run length DC
// code (quant scale from the BS header in bits 15 to
// 10, DC in bits 9 to 0), which is the QuantDC form
// of section 13.20.
func (d *MDEC) bsDecodeDC() bsResult {
	if d.bsVersion == 3 {
		// End of frame: ten 1 bits, checked at the
		// DC position (section 13.20).
		if bits, ok := d.peekBits(10); ok && bits == 0x3FF {
			d.consumeBits(10)
			return bsEndedFrame
		}
		off, res := d.bsDecodeDCv3Offset()
		if res != bsOK {
			return res
		}
		// Differential accumulation per component:
		// Cr, Cb and Y have separate previous DC
		// values, starting at 0 for the first
		// macroblock (section 13.20). The result
		// wraps inside the 10 bit range, the newer
		// decoder behavior the document describes
		// (QuantDC uses DC AND 3FFh).
		var acc *int32
		switch {
		case d.mono() || d.mbIdx >= 2:
			acc = &d.dcY
		case d.mbIdx == 0:
			acc = &d.dcCr
		default:
			acc = &d.dcCb
		}
		*acc = wrap10(*acc + off)
		code := uint16(d.bsQuant<<10) | uint16(*acc&0x3FF)
		d.startBlock(code)
		return bsOK
	}
	// v1, v2 (and any other version value, treated
	// as v2): raw signed 10 bit DC, with the value
	// 0111111111b as the end of frame code
	// (section 13.20, DC v1/v2).
	bits, ok := d.peekBits(10)
	if !ok {
		return bsNeedMore
	}
	d.consumeBits(10)
	if bits == 0x1FF {
		return bsEndedFrame
	}
	code := uint16(d.bsQuant<<10) | uint16(bits&0x3FF)
	d.startBlock(code)
	return bsOK
}

func wrap10(v int32) int32 {
	v %= 1024
	if v > 511 {
		v -= 1024
	} else if v < -512 {
		v += 1024
	}
	return v
}

// bsDecodeDCv3Offset decodes one Huffman DC offset
// from the category table in tables.go. The pattern
// for a category is prefix, then a sign bit, then
// index bits. Prefixes inside one component table are
// not prefixes of each other (checked against the
// printed patterns), so a prefix match selects the
// category.
func (d *MDEC) bsDecodeDCv3Offset() (int32, bsResult) {
	chroma := d.bsIsChroma()
	for _, cat := range dcCategories {
		pre := cat.lumaPre
		if chroma {
			pre = cat.chromaPre
		}
		bits, ok := d.peekBits(len(pre))
		if !ok {
			return 0, bsNeedMore
		}
		if bits != parseBitPattern(pre) {
			continue
		}
		if cat.base == 0 {
			d.consumeBits(len(pre))
			return 0, bsOK
		}
		total := len(pre) + 1 + cat.indexBits
		all, ok := d.peekBits(total)
		if !ok {
			return 0, bsNeedMore
		}
		sign := (all >> uint(cat.indexBits)) & 1
		idx := all & ((1 << uint(cat.indexBits)) - 1)
		d.consumeBits(total)
		mag := int32(cat.base) + int32(idx)
		if sign == 1 {
			return mag * 4, bsOK
		}
		return -mag * 4, bsOK
	}
	// No category matched. The patterns the document
	// lists as unused (111111110 and 1111111110)
	// land here when not enough bits follow them to
	// form the longest category; consume one bit so
	// the pump makes progress and keeps looking,
	// which treats stray padding as skippable.
	if d.availBits() == 0 {
		return 0, bsNeedMore
	}
	d.consumeBits(1)
	return 0, bsSkipped
}

// bsDecodeAC decodes one AC symbol in BS mode and
// feeds the equivalent run length code. The end of
// block code 10 and the escape code 000001 followed
// by a raw 16 bit code are handled before the table
// (section 13.21). The escape encoding exists for run
// and level pairs that have no table entry; the raw
// code after it is used verbatim.
func (d *MDEC) bsDecodeAC() bsResult {
	if bits, ok := d.peekBits(2); ok && bits == 0x2 {
		// 10: end of block.
		d.consumeBits(2)
		d.acStep(0xFE00)
		return bsOK
	}
	if bits, ok := d.peekBits(6); ok && bits == 0x01 {
		// 000001: escape, raw 16 bit code follows.
		if d.availBits() < 22 {
			return bsNeedMore
		}
		d.consumeBits(6)
		raw, _ := d.peekBits(16)
		d.consumeBits(16)
		d.acStep(uint16(raw))
		return bsOK
	}
	for _, e := range acTable {
		bits, ok := d.peekBits(len(e.pattern))
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		idx, sign, match := matchACPattern(e.pattern, bits)
		if !match {
			continue
		}
		d.consumeBits(len(e.pattern))
		if e.unused {
			// The unused all zero pattern is
			// consumed and treated as the end of
			// the block, so a damaged or padded
			// stream terminates the block instead
			// of looping. This is a choice for a
			// case the document only marks unused.
			d.acStep(0xFE00)
			return bsOK
		}
		code := e.values[idx]
		if sign == 1 {
			run := code >> 10
			lvl := sign10(code)
			code = (run << 10) | uint16(-lvl&0x3FF)
		}
		d.acStep(code)
		return bsOK
	}
	if d.availBits() == 0 {
		return bsNeedMore
	}
	// Unknown prefix: consume one bit and retry, so
	// the pump cannot spin forever on damaged data.
	d.consumeBits(1)
	return bsSkipped
}

// parseBitPattern converts a string of 0 and 1
// characters to its numeric value.
func parseBitPattern(s string) uint32 {
	var v uint32
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		v <<= 1
		if s[i] == '1' {
			v |= 1
		}
	}
	return v
}

// matchACPattern matches a peeked bit field against
// one AC table pattern and extracts the index bits
// (letter x, in order) and the sign bit (letter s).
func matchACPattern(pattern string, bits uint32) (idx int, sign int, match bool) {
	n := len(pattern)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		bit := int((bits >> uint(n-1-i)) & 1)
		switch pattern[i] {
		case '0':
			if bit != 0 {
				return 0, 0, false
			}
		case '1':
			if bit != 1 {
				return 0, 0, false
			}
		case 'x':
			idx = idx<<1 | bit
		case 's':
			sign = bit
		}
	}
	return idx, sign, true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/mdec/color.go ====================

package mdec

import "math"

// Output assembly: color conversion and pixel packing
// for one finished macroblock, per sections 6.3 and
// 6.4.
//
// Colored macroblocks are emitted as four 8x8
// quadrants in Y1, Y2, Y3, Y4 order (the 8x8 bitmap
// order of the data port, section 6.1), each quadrant
// left to right and top to bottom. Monochrome
// macroblocks are a single 8x8 block in the same
// order.
//
// Color conversion follows yuv_to_rgb in section
// 6.3: with R holding the Cr sample and B holding the
// Cb sample for the pixel,
//
//	R = 1.402 * R
//	G = -0.3437 * B - 0.7143 * R
//	B = 1.772 * B
//
// and each output channel is the luma sample plus
// that term, saturated to the signed range -128..127.
// The chroma sample for a pixel comes from the
// quadrant formula in the document, Cr and Cb block
// index ((x+xx)/2) + ((y+yy)/2)*8, where (xx, yy) is
// the quadrant origin inside the 16x16 macroblock.
// The document states the exact fixed point
// resolution of this stage is unknown; this
// implementation computes in float64, saturates, and
// then rounds to the nearest integer, which is the
// choice recorded here and used by the tests. For
// unsigned output 128 is added to each channel (the
// document writes this as an xor with 808080h on the
// signed byte). For signed output the channel byte is
// the two complement byte of the signed value.
//
// Packing: 24 bit output is a byte stream of R, G, B
// per pixel (the document names the pixel value BGR,
// stored little endian), packed into words low byte
// first. 15 bit output is one halfword per pixel,
// bit 15 from the command STP flag, then blue, green
// and red in 5 bits each taken from the top 5 bits of
// the channel byte, packed low halfword first. 8 bit
// mono is one byte per pixel packed low byte first.
// 4 bit mono is one nibble per pixel, the top 4 bits
// of the gray byte, packed low nibble first.

var quadrantOrigin = [4][2]int{{0, 0}, {8, 0}, {0, 8}, {8, 8}}

func (d *MDEC) channelByte(signedVal int32) uint8 {
	if d.signedOut {
		return uint8(int8(signedVal))
	}
	return uint8(signedVal + 128)
}

func yuvChannel(y, cr, cb int32) (r, g, b int32) {
	rf := float64(y) + 1.402*float64(cr)
	gf := float64(y) - 0.3437*float64(cb) - 0.7143*float64(cr)
	bf := float64(y) + 1.772*float64(cb)
	r = clampI32(int32(math.Round(rf)), -128, 127)
	g = clampI32(int32(math.Round(gf)), -128, 127)
	b = clampI32(int32(math.Round(bf)), -128, 127)
	return r, g, b
}

func (d *MDEC) assembleColor() {
	if d.depth == 2 {
		data := make([]byte, 0, 256*3)
		for q := 0; q < 4; q++ {
			xx, yy := quadrantOrigin[q][0], quadrantOrigin[q][1]
			for py := 0; py < 8; py++ {
				for px := 0; px < 8; px++ {
					ci := (px+xx)/2 + ((py+yy)/2)*8
					y := clip9(d.yBlk[q][px+py*8])
					cr := clip9(d.crBlk[ci])
					cb := clip9(d.cbBlk[ci])
					r, g, b := yuvChannel(y, cr, cb)
					data = append(data, d.channelByte(r), d.channelByte(g), d.channelByte(b))
				}
			}
		}
		words := make([]uint32, 0, wordsPerMB(2))
		for i := 0; i < len(data); i += 4 {
			var w uint32
			for j := 0; j < 4 && i+j < len(data); j++ {
				w |= uint32(data[i+j]) << (8 * j)
			}
			words = append(words, w)
		}
		d.enqueue(words, 2)
		return
	}
	// 15 bit depth.
	halfs := make([]uint16, 0, 256)
	for q := 0; q < 4; q++ {
		xx, yy := quadrantOrigin[q][0], quadrantOrigin[q][1]
		for py := 0; py < 8; py++ {
			for px := 0; px < 8; px++ {
				ci := (px+xx)/2 + ((py+yy)/2)*8
				y := clip9(d.yBlk[q][px+py*8])
				cr := clip9(d.crBlk[ci])
				cb := clip9(d.cbBlk[ci])
				r, g, b := yuvChannel(y, cr, cb)
				var hw uint16
				if d.stp {
					hw |= 1 << 15
				}
				hw |= uint16(d.channelByte(b)>>3) << 10
				hw |= uint16(d.channelByte(g)>>3) << 5
				hw |= uint16(d.channelByte(r) >> 3)
				halfs = append(halfs, hw)
			}
		}
	}
	words := make([]uint32, 0, wordsPerMB(3))
	for i := 0; i < len(halfs); i += 2 {
		words = append(words, uint32(halfs[i])|uint32(halfs[i+1])<<16)
	}
	d.enqueue(words, 3)
}

func (d *MDEC) assembleMono() {
	gray := make([]uint8, 64)
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		v := clip9(d.yBlk[0][i])
		gray[i] = d.channelByte(v)
	}
	if d.depth == 1 {
		words := make([]uint32, 0, wordsPerMB(1))
		for i := 0; i < 64; i += 4 {
			var w uint32
			for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
				w |= uint32(gray[i+j]) << (8 * j)
			}
			words = append(words, w)
		}
		d.enqueue(words, 1)
		return
	}
	// 4 bit depth: top nibble of each gray byte,
	// low nibble of each output byte first.
	words := make([]uint32, 0, wordsPerMB(0))
	for i := 0; i < 64; i += 8 {
		var w uint32
		for j := 0; j < 8; j++ {
			w |= uint32(gray[i+j]>>4) << (4 * j)
		}
		words = append(words, w)
	}
	d.enqueue(words, 0)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/mdec/mdec.go ====================

// Package mdec implements the PlayStation MDEC macroblock
// decoder as documented in the psx-spx MDEC chapter
// (sections 6.1 to 6.4), plus the BS Huffman layer from
// sections 13.19 to 13.21 as an explicitly marked
// extension (see bs.go).
//
// Hardware input format (section 6.4): a block is a
// sequence of 16 bit run length codes. The first code
// carries a 6 bit quant scale in bits 15 to 10 and a
// signed 10 bit DC value in bits 9 to 0. Following codes
// carry a 6 bit run of zero coefficients and a signed
// 10 bit AC level. The code FE00h is the end of block
// code and is also ignored when it appears where a new
// block is expected (padding between blocks, section
// 6.4, dummy halfwords). Codes are packed into 32 bit
// words, low halfword first.
//
// Important source note: the MDEC hardware itself has
// no Huffman or VLC stage and no bit reader. The
// Huffman coding (BS v1, v2, v3) lives in the CDROM
// file format layer above the MDEC: software decodes
// it into exactly the run length codes above and then
// feeds those to this hardware. This package therefore
// defaults to the hardware run length format, and the
// BS layer is available only through the extension in
// bs.go so that the two documented layers are not
// silently conflated.
package mdec

// Command kinds stored in the active field.
const (
	cmdNone   = 0
	cmdDecode = 1
	cmdQuant  = 2
	cmdScale  = 3
)

// Block decode states.
const (
	blkNeedDC = 0
	blkInAC   = 1
)

// MDEC is the macroblock decoder state.
type MDEC struct {
	// Control register (0x1F801824 write) stored bits.
	ctrlIn  bool // bit 30: enable data in request
	ctrlOut bool // bit 29: enable data out request

	// Status register stored fields (0x1F801824 read).
	statCopy   uint32 // command bits 28 to 25, shown at status bits 26 to 23
	curBlock   uint32 // status bits 18 to 16
	paramField uint32 // status bits 15 to 0
	dataInFull bool   // status bit 30

	// Current command intake.
	active     int // cmdNone, cmdDecode, cmdQuant or cmdScale
	cmdTotal   int // parameter words expected for the active command
	cmdRecv    int // parameter words received so far
	paramIdx   int // byte index (quant) or halfword index (scale)
	quantColor bool

	// Decode command format, from the command word.
	depth     int  // 0 = 4 bit mono, 1 = 8 bit mono, 2 = 24 bit, 3 = 15 bit
	signedOut bool // command bit 26
	stp       bool // command bit 25
	bsMode    bool // extension only, command bit 24, see bs.go

	// Tables loaded by MDEC(2) and MDEC(3).
	qY    [64]uint8
	qUV   [64]uint8
	scale [64]int16

	// Run length block decoder state.
	blkState int // blkNeedDC or blkInAC
	mbIdx    int // block inside the macroblock: 0 Cr, 1 Cb, 2..5 Y1..Y4; mono always 0
	scanK    int // scan position of the last stored coefficient
	qScale   int // quant scale from the current block DC code
	cur      [64]int32

	// Decoded (post IDCT) blocks of the current macroblock.
	crBlk [64]int32
	cbBlk [64]int32
	yBlk  [4][64]int32

	// BS extension state (bs.go).
	dcCr, dcCb, dcY int32 // BS v3 differential DC accumulators
	bsStage         int   // 0 header word 0, 1 header word 1, 2 bitstream
	bsEnded         bool
	bsQuant         int
	bsVersion       int
	bitQ            []uint16 // pending bitstream halfwords
	bitHead         int      // index of the current halfword in bitQ
	bitPos          int      // bits already consumed in bitQ[bitHead], from bit 15 down

	// Output FIFO. ReadWord pops from outHead.
	out       []uint32
	outHead   int
	outMBs    []mbInfo // one entry per queued macroblock, in order
	outIntoMB int      // words already read from the first queued macroblock
}

// mbInfo describes one queued macroblock in the output FIFO.
type mbInfo struct {
	words int // total output words for this macroblock
	depth int // output depth of the command that produced it
}

// New returns an MDEC in reset state.
func New() *MDEC {
	d := &MDEC{}
	d.Reset()
	return d
}

// Reset restores the power on state: tables cleared, no
// command active, output empty, and the status register
// reads 80040000h (data out FIFO empty, current block
// field 4), matching the value the document gives for a
// control reset in section 6.1.
func (d *MDEC) Reset() {
	keep := MDEC{curBlock: 4}
	*d = keep
}

// Control returns the stored control register bits:
// bit 30 (data in request enable) and bit 29 (data out
// request enable). The reset bit 31 is momentary and
// reads back as zero.
func (d *MDEC) Control() uint32 {
	var v uint32
	if d.ctrlIn {
		v |= 1 << 30
	}
	if d.ctrlOut {
		v |= 1 << 29
	}
	return v
}

// WriteControl handles a write to 0x1F801824.
// Bit 31 aborts any active command, clears the output
// FIFO and the input state, and restores the status
// fields to the reset value from section 6.1. The
// quant and scale tables survive a control reset (the
// document describes an abort, not a table clear).
// Bits 30 and 29 store the DMA request enables.
func (d *MDEC) WriteControl(w uint32) {
	if w&(1<<31) != 0 {
		d.active = cmdNone
		d.cmdRecv = 0
		d.cmdTotal = 0
		d.blkState = blkNeedDC
		d.mbIdx = 0
		d.scanK = 0
		d.qScale = 0
		d.out = nil
		d.outHead = 0
		d.outMBs = nil
		d.outIntoMB = 0
		d.bitQ = nil
		d.bitHead = 0
		d.bitPos = 0
		d.bsStage = 0
		d.bsEnded = false
		d.dcCr, d.dcCb, d.dcY = 0, 0, 0
		d.statCopy = 0
		d.curBlock = 4
		d.paramField = 0
		d.dataInFull = false
	}
	d.ctrlIn = w&(1<<30) != 0
	d.ctrlOut = w&(1<<29) != 0
}

// Status returns the status register read from
// 0x1F801824, with the bit layout of section 6.1:
//
//	31    data out FIFO empty
//	30    data in FIFO full (set here when the last
//	      parameter word of a command was received)
//	29    command busy (receiving or processing)
//	28    data in request (DMA in enabled)
//	27    data out request (DMA out enabled and data
//	      is pending)
//	26-23 output depth, signed and bit15 flags copied
//	      from command bits 28 to 25
//	22-19 zero
//	18-16 current block (0..3 Y1..Y4, 4 Cr, 5 Cb;
//	      mono always 4)
//	15-0  parameter words remaining minus 1 while a
//	      command is being received, FFFFh when a
//	      command has completed its intake, the value
//	      0 after reset, and the raw low bits after a
//	      no function command (see WriteWord)
func (d *MDEC) Status() uint32 {
	var s uint32
	if d.outLen() == 0 {
		s |= 1 << 31
	}
	if d.dataInFull {
		s |= 1 << 30
	}
	if d.active != cmdNone {
		s |= 1 << 29
	}
	if d.ctrlIn {
		s |= 1 << 28
	}
	if d.ctrlOut && d.outLen() > 0 {
		s |= 1 << 27
	}
	s |= (d.statCopy & 0xF) << 23
	s |= (d.curBlock & 7) << 16
	s |= d.paramField & 0xFFFF
	return s
}

// WriteWord handles a write to 0x1F801820 (also the
// DMA channel 0 entry point). When idle the word is a
// command word (section 6.2); otherwise it is the next
// parameter word of the active command.
func (d *MDEC) WriteWord(w uint32) {
	if d.active == cmdNone {
		d.startCommand(w)
		return
	}
	d.cmdRecv++
	switch d.active {
	case cmdQuant:
		// 64 unsigned bytes per table, packed into
		// words low byte first (16 words per table).
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			b := uint8(w >> (8 * i))
			if d.paramIdx < 64 {
				d.qY[d.paramIdx] = b
			} else {
				d.qUV[d.paramIdx-64] = b
			}
			d.paramIdx++
		}
	case cmdScale:
		// 64 signed halfwords, low halfword first
		// (32 words).
		d.scale[d.paramIdx] = int16(uint16(w))
		d.scale[d.paramIdx+1] = int16(uint16(w >> 16))
		d.paramIdx += 2
	case cmdDecode:
		if d.bsMode {
			d.bsWriteWord(w)
		} else {
			d.feedHalfword(uint16(w))
			d.feedHalfword(uint16(w >> 16))
		}
	}
	d.updateParamField()
	if d.cmdRecv >= d.cmdTotal {
		d.finishIntake()
	}
}

// startCommand decodes a command word (section 6.2).
func (d *MDEC) startCommand(w uint32) {
	// All commands copy bits 28 to 25 into status
	// bits 26 to 23.
	d.statCopy = (w >> 25) & 0xF
	d.dataInFull = false
	switch cmd := w >> 29; cmd {
	case 1: // decode macroblocks
		d.depth = int((w >> 27) & 3)
		d.signedOut = (w>>26)&1 == 1
		d.stp = (w>>25)&1 == 1
		d.bsMode = (w>>24)&1 == 1
		d.resetDecodeStream()
		total := int(w & 0xFFFF)
		if total == 0 {
			d.paramField = 0xFFFF
			return
		}
		d.active = cmdDecode
		d.cmdTotal = total
		d.cmdRecv = 0
		d.paramField = uint32(total - 1)
	case 2: // set quant tables
		d.quantColor = w&1 == 1
		total := 16
		if d.quantColor {
			total = 32
		}
		d.active = cmdQuant
		d.cmdTotal = total
		d.cmdRecv = 0
		d.paramIdx = 0
		d.paramField = uint32(total - 1)
	case 3: // set scale table
		d.active = cmdScale
		d.cmdTotal = 32
		d.cmdRecv = 0
		d.paramIdx = 0
		d.paramField = 31
	default:
		// MDEC(0) has no function and MDEC(4..7) are
		// invalid and act identical to MDEC(0), per
		// section 6.2: no parameters are expected,
		// bits 25 to 28 were reflected above, and
		// bits 0 to 15 are reflected into the status
		// low field without the minus 1 effect used
		// by MDEC(1). Unknown commands therefore do
		// nothing and never become busy.
		d.active = cmdNone
		d.paramField = w & 0xFFFF
	}
}

// updateParamField maintains status bits 15 to 0 while
// a command is being received: parameter words
// remaining minus 1.
func (d *MDEC) updateParamField() {
	rem := d.cmdTotal - d.cmdRecv
	if rem <= 0 {
		d.paramField = 0xFFFF
	} else {
		d.paramField = uint32(rem - 1)
	}
}

// finishIntake runs when the last parameter word of a
// command arrived. A partially decoded block at the
// end of a decode command is discarded.
func (d *MDEC) finishIntake() {
	d.active = cmdNone
	d.paramField = 0xFFFF
	d.dataInFull = true
	d.blkState = blkNeedDC
	d.mbIdx = 0
	d.bitQ = nil
	d.bitHead = 0
	d.bitPos = 0
	d.bsEnded = false
	d.bsStage = 0
}

// resetDecodeStream clears the per stream decoder
// state at the start of a decode command.
func (d *MDEC) resetDecodeStream() {
	d.blkState = blkNeedDC
	d.mbIdx = 0
	d.scanK = 0
	d.qScale = 0
	d.curBlock = 4 // Cr first, and mono is always 4
	d.dcCr, d.dcCb, d.dcY = 0, 0, 0
	d.bsStage = 0
	d.bsEnded = false
	d.bsQuant = 0
	d.bsVersion = 2
	d.bitQ = nil
	d.bitHead = 0
	d.bitPos = 0
}

func (d *MDEC) mono() bool { return d.depth == 0 || d.depth == 1 }

// quantTable returns the quant table for the block
// currently being decoded: color blocks (Cr, Cb) use
// the color table, luma blocks use the luminance
// table (section 6.2, MDEC(2)).
func (d *MDEC) quantTable() *[64]uint8 {
	if !d.mono() && d.mbIdx < 2 {
		return &d.qUV
	}
	return &d.qY
}

// blockStatusCode maps the internal macroblock block
// index to the status current block field of
// section 6.1.
func blockStatusCode(mbIdx int, mono bool) uint32 {
	if mono {
		return 4
	}
	switch mbIdx {
	case 0:
		return 4 // Cr
	case 1:
		return 5 // Cb
	default:
		return uint32(mbIdx - 2) // Y1..Y4 are 0..3
	}
}

func sign10(v uint16) int32 {
	v &= 0x3FF
	if v&0x200 != 0 {
		return int32(v) - 0x400
	}
	return int32(v)
}

func clampI32(v, lo, hi int32) int32 {
	if v < lo {
		return lo
	}
	if v > hi {
		return hi
	}
	return v
}

// feedHalfword is the hardware run length entry point:
// one 16 bit code from the decode parameter stream.
func (d *MDEC) feedHalfword(h uint16) {
	if d.blkState == blkNeedDC {
		if h == 0xFE00 {
			// Padding at the start of a block is
			// ignored (section 6.4).
			return
		}
		d.startBlock(h)
		return
	}
	d.acStep(h)
}

// startBlock consumes the first code of a block: the
// DC code (section 6.3, rl_decode_block). qt index 0
// is used without the quant scale; the special scale
// zero mode uses the raw value times 2 and no zigzag,
// as in the published pseudocode.
func (d *MDEC) startBlock(h uint16) {
	d.qScale = int(h>>10) & 0x3F
	raw := sign10(h)
	var v int32
	if d.qScale == 0 {
		v = raw * 2
	} else {
		v = raw * int32(d.quantTable()[0])
	}
	v = clampI32(v, -0x400, 0x3FF)
	d.cur = [64]int32{}
	d.cur[0] = v
	d.scanK = 0
	d.blkState = blkInAC
	d.curBlock = blockStatusCode(d.mbIdx, d.mono())
}

// acStep consumes one AC code (or the end of block
// code) inside a block, following rl_decode_block in
// section 6.3: the run field advances the scan
// position, and a position past 63 ends the block
// (which is how FE00h, with run field 63, acts as the
// end of block code).
func (d *MDEC) acStep(h uint16) {
	run := int(h>>10) & 0x3F
	newK := d.scanK + run + 1
	if newK > 63 {
		d.finishBlock()
		return
	}
	d.scanK = newK
	raw := sign10(h)
	var v int32
	if d.qScale == 0 {
		// Special mode without quant table and
		// without zigzag reordering.
		v = clampI32(raw*2, -0x400, 0x3FF)
		d.cur[d.scanK] = v
		return
	}
	qt := d.quantTable()
	v = (raw*int32(qt[d.scanK])*int32(d.qScale) + 4) / 8
	v = clampI32(v, -0x400, 0x3FF)
	d.cur[zagzig[d.scanK]] = v
}

// finishBlock runs the IDCT on the current block,
// stores it in its macroblock slot, and assembles and
// enqueues a macroblock when its last block arrived.
// Block order in a colored macroblock is Cr, Cb, Y1,
// Y2, Y3, Y4 (section 6.3); monochrome macroblocks
// consist of a single Y block.
func (d *MDEC) finishBlock() {
	spatial := d.idct(d.cur)
	d.blkState = blkNeedDC
	d.scanK = 0
	if d.mono() {
		d.yBlk[0] = spatial
		d.assembleMono()
		d.curBlock = 4
		return
	}
	switch d.mbIdx {
	case 0:
		d.crBlk = spatial
	case 1:
		d.cbBlk = spatial
	default:
		d.yBlk[d.mbIdx-2] = spatial
	}
	if d.mbIdx == 5 {
		d.assembleColor()
		d.mbIdx = 0
	} else {
		d.mbIdx++
	}
	d.curBlock = blockStatusCode(d.mbIdx, false)
}

// idct is the low level IDCT of section 6.3
// (real_idct_core): two passes of dst = src times the
// scale table, with the source processed column by
// column (diagonally mirrored, as the document puts
// it). Each pass computes
//
//	dst[x+y*8] = (sum + 0FFFh) / 2000h
//	sum = Sigma src[y+z*8] * (scaletable[x+z*8] / 8)
//
// The document itself marks the rounding with
// "or so?" and notes the hardware result is not
// perfect; this implementation uses Go integer
// division (truncation toward zero) for both the
// scale division by 8 (which also implements the
// documented use of only the upper 13 bits of the
// scale values) and the final division by 2000h, and
// 64 bit accumulation. That choice is the documented
// ambiguity for this stage; the tests allow for it
// with a plus or minus 2 tolerance against a float
// reference where the exact integer path is not
// asserted.
func (d *MDEC) idct(blk [64]int32) [64]int32 {
	var buf [64]int32
	src := blk
	dst := &buf
	for pass := 0; pass < 2; pass++ {
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
				var sum int64
				for z := 0; z < 8; z++ {
					sum += int64(src[y+z*8]) * int64(int32(d.scale[x+z*8])/8)
				}
				dst[x+y*8] = int32((sum + 0xFFF) / 0x2000)
			}
		}
		tmp := src
		src = *dst
		*dst = tmp
	}
	return src
}

// clip9 interprets the low 9 bits of a sample as a
// signed 9 bit value and saturates it to the signed
// 8 bit range, as in the y_to_mono pseudocode of
// section 6.3. It is applied to luma and chroma
// samples before color conversion as well; the
// document notes a 9 bit limit probably exists there
// too.
func clip9(v int32) int32 {
	v = int32(int16((v&0x1FF)<<7) >> 7)
	return clampI32(v, -128, 127)
}

// outLen returns the number of queued output words.
func (d *MDEC) outLen() int { return len(d.out) - d.outHead }

// enqueue appends one finished macroblock of output
// words to the output FIFO.
func (d *MDEC) enqueue(words []uint32, depth int) {
	if d.outHead > 0 && d.outHead == len(d.out) {
		d.out = d.out[:0]
		d.outHead = 0
	}
	d.out = append(d.out, words...)
	d.outMBs = append(d.outMBs, mbInfo{words: len(words), depth: depth})
}

// wordsPerMB returns the documented output word count
// of one macroblock for an output depth: 24 bit color
// has 256 pixels at 3 bytes (192 words), 15 bit color
// has 256 pixels at 2 bytes (128 words), 8 bit mono
// has 64 pixels (16 words) and 4 bit mono has 64
// pixels at 4 bits (8 words).
func wordsPerMB(depth int) int {
	switch depth {
	case 2:
		return 192
	case 3:
		return 128
	case 1:
		return 16
	default:
		return 8
	}
}

// ReadWord pulls one decoded output word (the data
// port read and the DMA channel 1 entry point).
// Output is produced in 8x8 block order: for colored
// macroblocks the four quadrants are emitted in Y1,
// Y2, Y3, Y4 order, each row by row left to right and
// top to bottom, which is the 8x8 bitmap order the
// document describes for this port in section 6.1
// (DMA channel 1 reorders macroblocks in RAM).
// When no output is pending ReadWord returns 0; the
// document says the hardware returns garbage in that
// case, and returning 0 is the defined behavior of
// this implementation.
func (d *MDEC) ReadWord() uint32 {
	if d.outLen() == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	v := d.out[d.outHead]
	d.outHead++
	d.outIntoMB++
	if len(d.outMBs) > 0 {
		mb := d.outMBs[0]
		if d.outIntoMB >= mb.words {
			d.outMBs = d.outMBs[1:]
			d.outIntoMB = 0
		} else if mb.depth == 2 || mb.depth == 3 {
			// While output is pending the current
			// block field names the output block:
			// quadrant index 0..3 for Y1..Y4.
			perQuadrant := mb.words / 4
			d.curBlock = uint32(d.outIntoMB / perQuadrant)
		} else {
			d.curBlock = 4
		}
	}
	if d.outHead == len(d.out) {
		d.out = d.out[:0]
		d.outHead = 0
	}
	return v
}

package mdec

import (
	"math"
	"testing"
)

// Test fixtures are synthetic and built in this file
// from the documented formats: run length halfwords
// for hardware mode (section 6.4), the standard scale
// table printed in section 6.3, and BS bitstreams for
// the BS extension (sections 13.19 to 13.21).
// Expected values are computed here from the
// documented math: a float64 IDCT reference and the
// YUV to RGB formula of section 6.3.

// stdScaleWords is the standard scale table printed
// in section 6.3 under set_scale_table, row by row,
// transcribed as unsigned hex halfwords.
var stdScaleWords = [64]uint16{
	0x5A82, 0x5A82, 0x5A82, 0x5A82, 0x5A82, 0x5A82, 0x5A82, 0x5A82,
	0x7D8A, 0x6A6D, 0x471C, 0x18F8, 0xE707, 0xB8E3, 0x9592, 0x8275,
	0x7641, 0x30FB, 0xCF04, 0x89BE, 0x89BE, 0xCF04, 0x30FB, 0x7641,
	0x6A6D, 0xE707, 0x8275, 0xB8E3, 0x471C, 0x7D8A, 0x18F8, 0x9592,
	0x5A82, 0xA57D, 0xA57D, 0x5A82, 0x5A82, 0xA57D, 0xA57D, 0x5A82,
	0x471C, 0x8275, 0x18F8, 0x6A6D, 0x9592, 0xE707, 0x7D8A, 0xB8E3,
	0x30FB, 0x89BE, 0x7641, 0xCF04, 0xCF04, 0x7641, 0x89BE, 0x30FB,
	0x18F8, 0xB8E3, 0x6A6D, 0x8275, 0x7D8A, 0x9592, 0x471C, 0xE707,
}

func allQuant(v byte) [64]byte {
	var q [64]byte
	for i := range q {
		q[i] = v
	}
	return q
}

func sendQuant(d *MDEC, color bool, qy, quv [64]byte) {
	cmd := uint32(2) << 29
	var seq []byte
	seq = append(seq, qy[:]...)
	if color {
		cmd |= 1
		seq = append(seq, quv[:]...)
	}
	d.WriteWord(cmd)
	for i := 0; i < len(seq); i += 4 {
		var w uint32
		for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
			w |= uint32(seq[i+j]) << (8 * j)
		}
		d.WriteWord(w)
	}
}

func sendScale(d *MDEC, tab [64]uint16) {
	d.WriteWord(uint32(3) << 29)
	for i := 0; i < 64; i += 2 {
		d.WriteWord(uint32(tab[i]) | uint32(tab[i+1])<<16)
	}
}

func loaded(t *testing.T) *MDEC {
	t.Helper()
	d := New()
	sendQuant(d, true, allQuant(8), allQuant(8))
	sendScale(d, stdScaleWords)
	if d.Status()&(1<<29) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("decoder still busy after table loads: %08x", d.Status())
	}
	return d
}

func dcCode(q int, dc int) uint16 {
	return uint16(q<<10) | uint16(dc&0x3FF)
}

func rlAC(run int, lvl int) uint16 {
	return uint16(run<<10) | uint16(lvl&0x3FF)
}

const eob = 0xFE00

func packWords(halfs []uint16) []uint32 {
	words := make([]uint32, 0, (len(halfs)+1)/2)
	for i := 0; i < len(halfs); i += 2 {
		hi := uint16(eob)
		if i+1 < len(halfs) {
			hi = halfs[i+1]
		}
		words = append(words, uint32(halfs[i])|uint32(hi)<<16)
	}
	return words
}

func decodeCmdWord(depth int, signed, stp, bs bool, total int) uint32 {
	w := uint32(1)<<29 | uint32(depth)<<27 | uint32(total)
	if signed {
		w |= 1 << 26
	}
	if stp {
		w |= 1 << 25
	}
	if bs {
		w |= 1 << 24
	}
	return w
}

func runRL(t *testing.T, d *MDEC, depth int, signed, stp bool, halfs []uint16) []uint32 {
	t.Helper()
	words := packWords(halfs)
	d.WriteWord(decodeCmdWord(depth, signed, stp, false, len(words)))
	for _, w := range words {
		d.WriteWord(w)
	}
	return drain(t, d)
}

func drain(t *testing.T, d *MDEC) []uint32 {
	t.Helper()
	var out []uint32
	for i := 0; i < 100000; i++ {
		if d.Status()&(1<<31) != 0 {
			return out
		}
		out = append(out, d.ReadWord())
	}
	t.Fatalf("output FIFO never drained")
	return out
}

// floatIDCT is the independent float64 reference for
// the two dimensional inverse DCT, in the standard
// JPEG form. in and out are indexed x + y*8, with x
// the horizontal frequency or position.
func floatIDCT(in [64]float64) [64]float64 {
	var out [64]float64
	for y := 0; y < 8; y++ {
		for x := 0; x < 8; x++ {
			var sum float64
			for v := 0; v < 8; v++ {
				cv := 1.0
				if v == 0 {
					cv = 1 / math.Sqrt2
				}
				for u := 0; u < 8; u++ {
					cu := 1.0
					if u == 0 {
						cu = 1 / math.Sqrt2
					}
					sum += cu * cv * in[v*8+u] *
						math.Cos(float64(2*x+1)*float64(u)*math.Pi/16) *
						math.Cos(float64(2*y+1)*float64(v)*math.Pi/16)
				}
			}
			out[y*8+x] = sum / 4
		}
	}
	return out
}

// refRGB applies the section 6.3 YUV to RGB formula
// to one pixel in float64, saturates, rounds, and
// converts to unsigned bytes.
func refRGB(y, cr, cb float64) (uint8, uint8, uint8) {
	clamp := func(v float64) int {
		if v < -128 {
			v = -128
		}
		if v > 127 {
			v = 127
		}
		return int(math.Round(v)) + 128
	}
	r := clamp(y + 1.402*cr)
	g := clamp(y - 0.3437*cb - 0.7143*cr)
	b := clamp(y + 1.772*cb)
	return uint8(r), uint8(g), uint8(b)
}

// solidColorMB builds the run length stream for one
// colored macroblock whose six blocks are DC only:
// Cr, Cb, then Y1..Y4, with q scale 1.
func solidColorMB(crDC, cbDC, yDC int) []uint16 {
	var halfs []uint16
	for _, dc := range []int{crDC, cbDC, yDC, yDC, yDC, yDC} {
		halfs = append(halfs, dcCode(1, dc), eob)
	}
	return halfs
}

// solidColorExpected computes, through the float
// reference, the spatial block values and the RGB
// bytes of the solid macroblock built by
// solidColorMB with all quant entries equal to 8.
func solidColorExpected(crDC, cbDC, yDC int) (uint8, uint8, uint8) {
	spatial := func(dc int) float64 {
		var in [64]float64
		in[0] = float64(dc * 8) // DC dequant: DC times quant[0]
		return floatIDCT(in)[0]
	}
	return refRGB(spatial(yDC), spatial(crDC), spatial(cbDC))
}

func TestQuantAndScaleLoadsAndUse(t *testing.T) {
	d := New()

	// Quant load (both tables): status parameter
	// field starts at words remaining minus 1 and
	// decreases as words are written.
	d.WriteWord(uint32(2)<<29 | 1)
	if got := d.Status() & 0xFFFF; got != 31 {
		t.Fatalf("quant param field after command = %04x, want 1f", got)
	}
	if d.Status()&(1<<29) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("quant load should be busy")
	}
	qy, quv := allQuant(8), allQuant(8)
	seq := append(append([]byte{}, qy[:]...), quv[:]...)
	for wi := 0; wi < 32; wi++ {
		var w uint32
		for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
			w |= uint32(seq[wi*4+j]) << (8 * j)
		}
		d.WriteWord(w)
		if wi == 0 {
			if got := d.Status() & 0xFFFF; got != 30 {
				t.Fatalf("quant param field after 1 word = %04x, want 1e", got)
			}
		}
	}
	if got := d.Status() & 0xFFFF; got != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("quant param field after last word = %04x, want ffff", got)
	}
	if d.Status()&(1<<29) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("quant load should be done")
	}
	sendScale(d, stdScaleWords)

	base := runRL(t, d, 1, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(1, 16), eob})
	baseByte := int(byte(base[0]))

	// Changing one quant entry (luma table entry 0)
	// changes the DC output in the documented
	// direction and magnitude: the DC dequant is
	// DC times quant[0], so doubling quant[0] from 8
	// to 16 doubles the dequantized DC and adds
	// about (256-128)/8 = 16 to the spatial value.
	qy2 := allQuant(8)
	qy2[0] = 16
	sendQuant(d, false, qy2, allQuant(8))
	changed := runRL(t, d, 1, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(1, 16), eob})
	changedByte := int(byte(changed[0]))
	if diff := changedByte - baseByte; diff < 15 || diff > 17 {
		t.Fatalf("quant[0] 8 to 16 changed DC byte by %d, want about 16 (%d to %d)", diff, baseByte, changedByte)
	}

	// The scale table is used too: an all zero scale
	// table makes the IDCT output all zero, so the
	// mono byte is the unsigned zero level 128.
	sendScale(d, [64]uint16{})
	zeroed := runRL(t, d, 1, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(1, 16), eob})
	for _, w := range zeroed {
		if w != 0x80808080 {
			t.Fatalf("zero scale decode word = %08x, want 80808080", w)
		}
	}
}

func TestDCOnlyLuminance(t *testing.T) {
	d := loaded(t)
	// One monochrome macroblock: a single luma block
	// whose only coefficient is the DC value 16,
	// quant scale 1, quant[0] = 8.
	out := runRL(t, d, 1, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(1, 16), eob})
	if len(out) != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("mono 8 bit macroblock words = %d, want 16", len(out))
	}
	// Documented DC path: dequantized DC is
	// 16 * 8 = 128; the IDCT DC gain from the float
	// reference is 1/8, so the uniform sample is 16
	// and the unsigned byte is 144, within the plus
	// or minus 1 rounding tolerance of the integer
	// IDCT path.
	var ref [64]float64
	ref[0] = 128
	want := int(math.Round(floatIDCT(ref)[0])) + 128
	first := int(byte(out[0]))
	if first < want-1 || first > want+1 {
		t.Fatalf("DC byte = %d, want %d plus or minus 1", first, want)
	}
	for wi, w := range out {
		for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
			if b := int(byte(w >> (8 * j))); b != first {
				t.Fatalf("block not uniform: word %d byte %d = %d, want %d", wi, j, b, first)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestFullMacroblock15Bit(t *testing.T) {
	d := loaded(t)
	out := runRL(t, d, 3, false, true, solidColorMB(16, 16, 32))
	if len(out) != 128 {
		t.Fatalf("15 bit macroblock words = %d, want 128", len(out))
	}
	r, g, b := solidColorExpected(16, 16, 32)
	var hw uint32 = 1 << 15
	hw |= uint32(b>>3) << 10
	hw |= uint32(g>>3) << 5
	hw |= uint32(r >> 3)
	want := hw | hw<<16
	for _, idx := range []int{0, 1, 31, 32, 64, 127} {
		if out[idx] != want {
			t.Fatalf("15 bit word %d = %08x, want %08x (RGB %d %d %d)", idx, out[idx], want, r, g, b)
		}
	}
	for i, w := range out {
		if w != want {
			t.Fatalf("15 bit macroblock not solid: word %d = %08x, want %08x", i, w, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestACSingleCoefficient(t *testing.T) {
	d := loaded(t)
	// One AC coefficient: scan position 1, run 0,
	// level 16, quant scale 8, quant[1] = 8.
	// Dequantized value (16*8*8+4)/8 = 128 at raster
	// position zagzig[1] = 1.
	out := runRL(t, d, 1, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(8, 0), rlAC(0, 16), eob})
	if len(out) != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("mono words = %d, want 16", len(out))
	}
	var coeff [64]float64
	coeff[1] = 128
	ref := floatIDCT(coeff)
	// Tolerance: plus or minus 2 per sample between
	// the integer IDCT path and the float reference,
	// as recorded in the package documentation.
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		got := int(byte(out[i/4] >> (8 * (i % 4))))
		want := int(math.Round(ref[i])) + 128
		if got < want-2 || got > want+2 {
			t.Fatalf("sample %d = %d, float reference %d, tolerance plus or minus 2", i, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func Test24BitPacking(t *testing.T) {
	d := loaded(t)
	out := runRL(t, d, 2, false, false, solidColorMB(16, 16, 32))
	if len(out) != 192 {
		t.Fatalf("24 bit macroblock words = %d, want 192", len(out))
	}
	r, g, b := solidColorExpected(16, 16, 32)
	cycle := []uint8{r, g, b}
	// Every byte of the stream must follow the R, G,
	// B per pixel byte order.
	for i := 0; i < 256*3; i++ {
		got := byte(out[i/4] >> (8 * (i % 4)))
		if got != cycle[i%3] {
			t.Fatalf("24 bit byte %d = %d, want %d (RGB %d %d %d)", i, got, cycle[i%3], r, g, b)
		}
	}
	// The first word packs bytes R, G, B, R low byte
	// first, and the second quadrant starts at word
	// 48 with the same alignment (192 bytes per
	// quadrant is a multiple of 3).
	want0 := uint32(r) | uint32(g)<<8 | uint32(b)<<16 | uint32(r)<<24
	if out[0] != want0 {
		t.Fatalf("24 bit word 0 = %08x, want %08x", out[0], want0)
	}
	if out[48] != want0 {
		t.Fatalf("24 bit word 48 = %08x, want %08x", out[48], want0)
	}
}

func TestMono8And4BitModes(t *testing.T) {
	d := loaded(t)
	out8 := runRL(t, d, 1, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(1, 8), eob})
	if len(out8) != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("8 bit mono words = %d, want 16", len(out8))
	}
	// DC 8 with quant[0] 8 gives spatial value 8,
	// unsigned byte 136 (plus or minus 1 rounding).
	for _, w := range out8 {
		for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
			if b := int(byte(w >> (8 * j))); b < 135 || b > 137 {
				t.Fatalf("8 bit mono byte = %d, want about 136", b)
			}
		}
	}
	out4 := runRL(t, d, 0, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(1, 16), eob})
	if len(out4) != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("4 bit mono words = %d, want 8", len(out4))
	}
	// Gray byte 144 (plus or minus 1) has top nibble
	// 9, so every packed nibble is 9.
	for _, w := range out4 {
		if w != 0x99999999 {
			t.Fatalf("4 bit mono word = %08x, want 99999999", w)
		}
	}
}

func TestFEPaddingIgnored(t *testing.T) {
	clean := runRL(t, loaded(t), 1, false, false, []uint16{dcCode(1, 16), eob})
	padded := runRL(t, loaded(t), 1, false, false,
		[]uint16{eob, dcCode(1, 16), eob, eob, eob})
	if len(clean) != len(padded) {
		t.Fatalf("padding changed output length %d vs %d", len(clean), len(padded))
	}
	for i := range clean {
		if clean[i] != padded[i] {
			t.Fatalf("padding changed word %d: %08x vs %08x", i, clean[i], padded[i])
		}
	}
}

func TestStatusDecode(t *testing.T) {
	d := loaded(t)
	if got := New().Status(); got != 0x80040000 {
		t.Fatalf("status after reset = %08x, want 80040000", got)
	}
	// The data out FIFO empty flag (bit 31) reads set
	// at reset, per the document.
	if d.Status()&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("data out empty flag not set after reset")
	}
	words := packWords([]uint16{dcCode(1, 16), eob})
	d.WriteWord(decodeCmdWord(1, false, false, false, len(words)))
	if got := d.Status() & 0xFFFF; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("remaining field at decode start = %04x, want 0000 (1 word minus 1)", got)
	}
	if d.Status()&(1<<29) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("decode should read busy while receiving")
	}
	d.WriteWord(words[0])
	if got := d.Status() & 0xFFFF; got != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("remaining field after final word = %04x, want ffff", got)
	}
	if d.Status()&(1<<29) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("decode should not read busy after final word")
	}
	out := drain(t, d)
	if len(out) != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("mono macroblock output words = %d, want the documented 16", len(out))
	}
}

func TestControlResetAndUnknownCommands(t *testing.T) {
	d := New()
	d.WriteControl(1<<30 | 1<<29)
	if got := d.Control(); got != 1<<30|1<<29 {
		t.Fatalf("control readback = %08x", got)
	}
	if d.Status()&(1<<28) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("data in request should read set with DMA in enabled and idle")
	}
	// Command 5 is invalid and acts as MDEC(0): no
	// function, no parameters, and the low bits are
	// reflected into the status low field.
	d.WriteWord(uint32(5)<<29 | 0x1234)
	if got := d.Status() & 0xFFFF; got != 0x1234 {
		t.Fatalf("unknown command reflection = %04x, want 1234", got)
	}
	if d.Status()&(1<<29) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unknown command must not be busy")
	}
	// Control reset aborts and restores the reset
	// status value.
	d.WriteWord(decodeCmdWord(1, false, false, false, 4))
	if d.Status()&(1<<29) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("decode should be busy before abort")
	}
	d.WriteControl(1 << 31)
	if got := d.Status(); got != 0x80040000 {
		t.Fatalf("status after control reset = %08x, want 80040000", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeMidDecode(t *testing.T) {
	halfs := solidColorMB(16, 16, 32)
	words := packWords(halfs)
	ref := runRL(t, loaded(t), 3, false, true, halfs)

	// Mid decode: serialize after 3 of 6 input
	// words, restore into a fresh decoder (tables
	// come from the serialized state), finish the
	// stream, and compare byte for byte.
	d := loaded(t)
	d.WriteWord(decodeCmdWord(3, false, true, false, len(words)))
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		d.WriteWord(words[i])
	}
	state := d.Serialize()
	if len(state) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(state), StateSize)
	}
	d2 := New()
	if err := d2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 3; i < len(words); i++ {
		d2.WriteWord(words[i])
	}
	got := drain(t, d2)
	if len(got) != len(ref) {
		t.Fatalf("restored decode words = %d, want %d", len(got), len(ref))
	}
	for i := range ref {
		if got[i] != ref[i] {
			t.Fatalf("restored decode word %d = %08x, want %08x", i, got[i], ref[i])
		}
	}

	// Output partially drained: serialize after
	// reading 5 output words, restore, and the rest
	// must match the uninterrupted run exactly.
	d3 := loaded(t)
	d3.WriteWord(decodeCmdWord(3, false, true, false, len(words)))
	for _, w := range words {
		d3.WriteWord(w)
	}
	var joined []uint32
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		joined = append(joined, d3.ReadWord())
	}
	d4 := New()
	if err := d4.Deserialize(d3.Serialize()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("deserialize partial drain: %v", err)
	}
	joined = append(joined, drain(t, d4)...)
	if len(joined) != len(ref) {
		t.Fatalf("partial drain total = %d, want %d", len(joined), len(ref))
	}
	for i := range ref {
		if joined[i] != ref[i] {
			t.Fatalf("partial drain word %d = %08x, want %08x", i, joined[i], ref[i])
		}
	}

	if err := New().Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("short state should fail")
	}
	bad := New().Serialize()
	bad[0] ^= 0xFF
	if err := New().Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("bad magic state should fail")
	}
}

// bitWriter builds a BS bitstream: MSB first inside
// each halfword.
type bitWriter struct {
	halfs []uint16
	cur   uint16
	n     int
}

func (b *bitWriter) bits(v uint32, count int) {
	for i := count - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if (v>>uint(i))&1 == 1 {
			b.cur |= 1 << uint(15-b.n)
		}
		b.n++
		if b.n == 16 {
			b.halfs = append(b.halfs, b.cur)
			b.cur = 0
			b.n = 0
		}
	}
}

// pattern writes a code pattern of fixed bits plus
// letter s (sign) and letter x or n (index bits in
// order, most significant first).
func (b *bitWriter) pattern(pat string, sign, idx int) {
	total := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(pat); i++ {
		if pat[i] == 'x' || pat[i] == 'n' {
			total++
		}
	}
	seen := 0
	for i := 0; i < len(pat); i++ {
		switch pat[i] {
		case '0':
			b.bits(0, 1)
		case '1':
			b.bits(1, 1)
		case 's':
			b.bits(uint32(sign), 1)
		case 'x', 'n':
			b.bits(uint32((idx>>uint(total-1-seen))&1), 1)
			seen++
		}
	}
}

// finish pads the final halfword with 1 bits and then
// pads to a whole number of words with FF FFh
// halfwords. The pad loop runs while a partial
// halfword is open (n != 0): bits() resets n to 0
// when the halfword flushes at 16, so a "n < 16"
// condition would never terminate.
func (b *bitWriter) finish() []uint16 {
	for b.n != 0 {
		b.bits(1, 1)
	}
	if len(b.halfs)%2 == 1 {
		b.halfs = append(b.halfs, 0xFFFF)
	}
	return b.halfs
}

func runBS(t *testing.T, d *MDEC, depth int, stp bool, version, quant int, bw *bitWriter) []uint32 {
	t.Helper()
	halfs := bw.finish()
	words := packWords(halfs)
	total := 2 + len(words)
	d.WriteWord(decodeCmdWord(depth, false, stp, true, total))
	d.WriteWord(0x3800<<16 | 0x0010)                 // header: size/4, file ID 3800h
	d.WriteWord(uint32(version)<<16 | uint32(quant)) // header: quant, version
	for _, w := range words {
		d.WriteWord(w)
	}
	return drain(t, d)
}

func TestBSEscapeVersusInTable(t *testing.T) {
	// BS v2, monochrome. DC is a raw 10 bit value.
	// One AC pair (run 0, level 1) encoded in the
	// table as 11s with s = 0, and again via the
	// escape code 000001 followed by the raw 16 bit
	// MDEC code 0001h. Both must decode identically.
	build := func(escape bool) *bitWriter {
		bw := &bitWriter{}
		bw.bits(20, 10) // DC value 20
		if escape {
			bw.bits(0x01, 6)    // 000001 escape
			bw.bits(0x0001, 16) // raw MDEC code
		} else {
			bw.pattern("11s", 0, 0)
		}
		bw.bits(0x2, 2)    // end of block: 10
		bw.bits(0x1FF, 10) // end of frame: 0111111111
		return bw
	}
	a := runBS(t, loaded(t), 1, false, 2, 1, build(false))
	b := runBS(t, loaded(t), 1, false, 2, 1, build(true))
	if len(a) != 16 || len(b) != 16 {
		t.Fatalf("BS mono words = %d and %d, want 16", len(a), len(b))
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			t.Fatalf("escape decode differs at word %d: %08x vs %08x", i, a[i], b[i])
		}
	}
	// Sanity: DC 20 with quant[0] 8 is spatial 20,
	// so the first byte is about 148.
	if got := int(byte(a[0])); got < 146 || got > 150 {
		t.Fatalf("BS mono first byte = %d, want about 148", got)
	}
}

func TestBSv3DifferentialDC(t *testing.T) {
	// BS v3, 15 bit color. DC values are Huffman
	// offsets against the previous DC of the same
	// component. Per the section 13.20 transcription
	// in bs.go, a category decodes to the signed
	// value (base + index) * 4, so the offsets below
	// accumulate to Cr +128, Cb -64, and Y +96 on Y1,
	// with Y2..Y4 holding there through the zero
	// offset code (which only gives a solid
	// macroblock if the Y accumulator is shared
	// across the four Y blocks, and the Cr and Cb
	// accumulators are separate). NOTE: the *4
	// reconstruction in bs.go is the transcription
	// this package ships; it has not been verified
	// against a real BS v3 stream, and an earlier
	// draft of this fixture assumed unscaled
	// offsets. The category table structure itself
	// (prefixes, sign bit, index bits) is not in
	// question here.
	bw := &bitWriter{}
	bw.pattern("111110snnnnn", 1, 0) // Cr: base 32, index 0, +128 scaled
	bw.bits(0x2, 2)                  // EOB
	bw.pattern("11110snnnn", 0, 0)   // Cb: base 16, index 0, -64 scaled
	bw.bits(0x2, 2)                  // EOB
	bw.pattern("1110snnnn", 1, 8)    // Y1: base 16, index 8, +96 scaled
	bw.bits(0x2, 2)                  // EOB
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		bw.pattern("100", 0, 0) // Y offset 0
		bw.bits(0x2, 2)         // EOB
	}
	bw.bits(0x3FF, 10) // end of frame: ten 1 bits
	out := runBS(t, loaded(t), 3, true, 3, 1, bw)
	if len(out) != 128 {
		t.Fatalf("BS v3 macroblock words = %d, want 128", len(out))
	}
	r, g, b := refRGB(96, 128, -64)
	want := [3]int{int(b >> 3), int(g >> 3), int(r >> 3)}
	// Per channel tolerance of one 5 bit step: the
	// fixed point IDCT rounds a DC only block to
	// within a step of the exact value (the same
	// tolerance the AC gate uses).
	for i, w := range out {
		for _, hw := range [2]uint32{w, w >> 16} {
			if hw>>15&1 != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("BS v3 word %d half %08x: STP bit not set", i, hw)
			}
			got := [3]int{int(hw >> 10 & 0x1F), int(hw >> 5 & 0x1F), int(hw & 0x1F)}
			for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
				if got[ch] < want[ch]-1 || got[ch] > want[ch]+1 {
					t.Fatalf("BS v3 word %d channel %d = %d, want %d +/- 1 (RGB %d %d %d)",
						i, ch, got[ch], want[ch], r, g, b)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestBSSerializeMidStream(t *testing.T) {
	build := func() (*bitWriter, []uint32) {
		bw := &bitWriter{}
		bw.bits(20, 10)
		bw.pattern("11s", 0, 0)
		bw.bits(0x2, 2)
		bw.bits(0x1FF, 10)
		return bw, nil
	}
	bwRef, _ := build()
	ref := runBS(t, loaded(t), 1, false, 2, 1, bwRef)

	bw, _ := build()
	halfs := bw.finish()
	words := packWords(halfs)
	total := 2 + len(words)
	d := loaded(t)
	d.WriteWord(decodeCmdWord(1, false, false, true, total))
	d.WriteWord(0x3800<<16 | 0x0010)
	d.WriteWord(2<<16 | 1)
	d.WriteWord(words[0]) // first bitstream word only
	d2 := New()
	if err := d2.Deserialize(d.Serialize()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("deserialize mid BS: %v", err)
	}
	for _, w := range words[1:] {
		d2.WriteWord(w)
	}
	got := drain(t, d2)
	if len(got) != len(ref) {
		t.Fatalf("restored BS words = %d, want %d", len(got), len(ref))
	}
	for i := range ref {
		if got[i] != ref[i] {
			t.Fatalf("restored BS word %d = %08x, want %08x", i, got[i], ref[i])
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/mdec/serialize.go ====================

package mdec

import "fmt"

// Serialization layout (all integers little endian).
// StateSize is fixed; queues are stored up to the
// capacities below, which are far above anything a
// single realistic decode burst needs. If a queue is
// longer than its capacity when Serialize is called,
// it is truncated to the capacity; that limitation is
// stated here rather than hidden.
//
//	0..255     header: 64 uint32 slots (see below)
//	256..319   luminance quant table (64 bytes)
//	320..383   color quant table (64 bytes)
//	384..511   scale table (64 int16)
//	512..767   current block coefficients (64 int32)
//	768..1023  Cr block (64 int32)
//	1024..1279 Cb block (64 int32)
//	1280..2303 Y blocks (4 x 64 int32)
//	2304..35071   BS bit queue (16384 uint16)
//	35072..166143 output queue (32768 uint32)
//	166144..198911 output macroblock infos (4096 x 2 uint32)
//
// Header slots:
//
//	0 magic 0x4D444543, 1 control enables, 2 status
//	copy nibble, 3 current block, 4 parameter field,
//	5 data in full flag, 6 active command kind,
//	7 command total words, 8 command received words,
//	9 parameter index, 10 quant color flag,
//	11 output depth, 12 signed output flag,
//	13 STP flag, 14 BS mode flag, 15 block state,
//	16 macroblock block index, 17 scan position,
//	18 quant scale, 19 DC Cr accumulator,
//	20 DC Cb accumulator, 21 DC Y accumulator,
//	22 BS stage, 23 BS ended flag, 24 BS quant,
//	25 BS version, 26 bit queue count,
//	27 bit queue head bit position, 28 output count,
//	29 output words read in current macroblock,
//	30 output macroblock info count, 31 active
//	decode format word (depth, signed, STP and BS
//	mode re-packed), 32..63 reserved zero.
const (
	serHdrSize   = 256
	serQYOff     = 256
	serQUVOff    = 320
	serScaleOff  = 384
	serCurOff    = 512
	serCrOff     = 768
	serCbOff     = 1024
	serYOff      = 1280
	serBitQOff   = 2304
	serBitQCap   = 16384 // halfwords
	serOutOff    = serBitQOff + serBitQCap*2
	serOutCap    = 32768 // words
	serMBOff     = serOutOff + serOutCap*4
	serMBCap     = 4096
	serTotalSize = serMBOff + serMBCap*8
)

// StateSize is the serialized MDEC state size.
const StateSize = serTotalSize

const serMagic = 0x4D444543

func put32(b []byte, off int, v uint32) {
	b[off] = byte(v)
	b[off+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	b[off+2] = byte(v >> 16)
	b[off+3] = byte(v >> 24)
}

func get32(b []byte, off int) uint32 {
	return uint32(b[off]) | uint32(b[off+1])<<8 | uint32(b[off+2])<<16 | uint32(b[off+3])<<24
}

func putI32(b []byte, off int, v int32) { put32(b, off, uint32(v)) }
func getI32(b []byte, off int) int32    { return int32(get32(b, off)) }

func boolU32(v bool) uint32 {
	if v {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// Serialize captures the full internal state: tables,
// the run length block decoder position (including a
// partially decoded block), the BS bit reader
// position within a partially consumed stream, the
// current command intake counters, the DC
// accumulators, and the output queue contents and
// drain position, so a save and restore in the
// middle of a decode command continues identically.
func (d *MDEC) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	slot := func(i int, v uint32) { put32(out, i*4, v) }
	slot(0, serMagic)
	slot(1, boolU32(d.ctrlIn)<<30|boolU32(d.ctrlOut)<<29)
	slot(2, d.statCopy)
	slot(3, d.curBlock)
	slot(4, d.paramField)
	slot(5, boolU32(d.dataInFull))
	slot(6, uint32(d.active))
	slot(7, uint32(d.cmdTotal))
	slot(8, uint32(d.cmdRecv))
	slot(9, uint32(d.paramIdx))
	slot(10, boolU32(d.quantColor))
	slot(11, uint32(d.depth))
	slot(12, boolU32(d.signedOut))
	slot(13, boolU32(d.stp))
	slot(14, boolU32(d.bsMode))
	slot(15, uint32(d.blkState))
	slot(16, uint32(d.mbIdx))
	slot(17, uint32(d.scanK))
	slot(18, uint32(d.qScale))
	slot(19, uint32(d.dcCr))
	slot(20, uint32(d.dcCb))
	slot(21, uint32(d.dcY))
	slot(22, uint32(d.bsStage))
	slot(23, boolU32(d.bsEnded))
	slot(24, uint32(d.bsQuant))
	slot(25, uint32(d.bsVersion))
	copy(out[serQYOff:serQYOff+64], d.qY[:])
	copy(out[serQUVOff:serQUVOff+64], d.qUV[:])
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		out[serScaleOff+i*2] = byte(uint16(d.scale[i]))
		out[serScaleOff+i*2+1] = byte(uint16(d.scale[i]) >> 8)
		putI32(out, serCurOff+i*4, d.cur[i])
		putI32(out, serCrOff+i*4, d.crBlk[i])
		putI32(out, serCbOff+i*4, d.cbBlk[i])
		for q := 0; q < 4; q++ {
			putI32(out, serYOff+(q*64+i)*4, d.yBlk[q][i])
		}
	}
	// Bit queue, stored from the head.
	nb := 0
	for i := d.bitHead; i < len(d.bitQ) && nb < serBitQCap; i++ {
		v := d.bitQ[i]
		out[serBitQOff+nb*2] = byte(v)
		out[serBitQOff+nb*2+1] = byte(v >> 8)
		nb++
	}
	slot(26, uint32(nb))
	slot(27, uint32(d.bitPos))
	// Output queue, stored from the head.
	no := 0
	for i := d.outHead; i < len(d.out) && no < serOutCap; i++ {
		put32(out, serOutOff+no*4, d.out[i])
		no++
	}
	slot(28, uint32(no))
	slot(29, uint32(d.outIntoMB))
	nm := 0
	for _, mb := range d.outMBs {
		if nm >= serMBCap {
			break
		}
		put32(out, serMBOff+nm*8, uint32(mb.words))
		put32(out, serMBOff+nm*8+4, uint32(mb.depth))
		nm++
	}
	slot(30, uint32(nm))
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
// It returns an error when the input has the wrong
// size or does not carry the MDEC state magic.
func (d *MDEC) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != StateSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("mdec: state size %d, want %d", len(in), StateSize)
	}
	if get32(in, 0) != serMagic {
		return fmt.Errorf("mdec: bad state magic %08x", get32(in, 0))
	}
	slot := func(i int) uint32 { return get32(in, i*4) }
	ctrl := slot(1)
	d.ctrlIn = ctrl&(1<<30) != 0
	d.ctrlOut = ctrl&(1<<29) != 0
	d.statCopy = slot(2)
	d.curBlock = slot(3)
	d.paramField = slot(4)
	d.dataInFull = slot(5) != 0
	d.active = int(slot(6))
	d.cmdTotal = int(slot(7))
	d.cmdRecv = int(slot(8))
	d.paramIdx = int(slot(9))
	d.quantColor = slot(10) != 0
	d.depth = int(slot(11))
	d.signedOut = slot(12) != 0
	d.stp = slot(13) != 0
	d.bsMode = slot(14) != 0
	d.blkState = int(slot(15))
	d.mbIdx = int(slot(16))
	d.scanK = int(slot(17))
	d.qScale = int(slot(18))
	d.dcCr = int32(slot(19))
	d.dcCb = int32(slot(20))
	d.dcY = int32(slot(21))
	d.bsStage = int(slot(22))
	d.bsEnded = slot(23) != 0
	d.bsQuant = int(slot(24))
	d.bsVersion = int(slot(25))
	copy(d.qY[:], in[serQYOff:serQYOff+64])
	copy(d.qUV[:], in[serQUVOff:serQUVOff+64])
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		d.scale[i] = int16(uint16(in[serScaleOff+i*2]) | uint16(in[serScaleOff+i*2+1])<<8)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 64; i++ {
		d.cur[i] = getI32(in, serCurOff+i*4)
		d.crBlk[i] = getI32(in, serCrOff+i*4)
		d.cbBlk[i] = getI32(in, serCbOff+i*4)
		for q := 0; q < 4; q++ {
			d.yBlk[q][i] = getI32(in, serYOff+(q*64+i)*4)
		}
	}
	nb := int(slot(26))
	if nb > serBitQCap {
		nb = serBitQCap
	}
	d.bitQ = make([]uint16, nb)
	for i := 0; i < nb; i++ {
		d.bitQ[i] = uint16(in[serBitQOff+i*2]) | uint16(in[serBitQOff+i*2+1])<<8
	}
	d.bitHead = 0
	d.bitPos = int(slot(27))
	no := int(slot(28))
	if no > serOutCap {
		no = serOutCap
	}
	d.out = make([]uint32, no)
	for i := 0; i < no; i++ {
		d.out[i] = get32(in, serOutOff+i*4)
	}
	d.outHead = 0
	d.outIntoMB = int(slot(29))
	nm := int(slot(30))
	if nm > serMBCap {
		nm = serMBCap
	}
	d.outMBs = make([]mbInfo, nm)
	for i := 0; i < nm; i++ {
		d.outMBs[i] = mbInfo{
			words: int(get32(in, serMBOff+i*8)),
			depth: int(get32(in, serMBOff+i*8+4)),
		}
	}
	return nil
}
