package mdec

// Tables transcribed from the psx-spx document.
//
// zigzag is from section 6.3 (MDEC Decompression),
// the list headed "zigzag[0..63]". zagzig is its
// inverse, built with the rule the document gives:
// for i in 0..63, zagzig[zigzag[i]] = i.

var zigzag = [64]int{
	0, 1, 5, 6, 14, 15, 27, 28,
	2, 4, 7, 13, 16, 26, 29, 42,
	3, 8, 12, 17, 25, 30, 41, 43,
	9, 11, 18, 24, 31, 40, 44, 53,
	10, 19, 23, 32, 39, 45, 52, 54,
	20, 22, 33, 38, 46, 51, 55, 60,
	21, 34, 37, 47, 50, 56, 59, 61,
	35, 36, 48, 49, 57, 58, 62, 63,
}

var zagzig = buildZagzig()

func buildZagzig() [64]int {
	var z [64]int
	for i, v := range zigzag {
		z[v] = i
	}
	return z
}

// The standard scale table for MDEC(3) is not built
// into the hardware: software loads it with the set
// scale command. The usual values (printed in
// section 6.3 under set_scale_table) are transcribed
// in the tests, which load them through MDEC(3)
// exactly as software would.
//
// BS AC Huffman table, from section 13.21 (CDROM File
// Video BS Compression AC Values), the table headed
// "Huffman codes for AC values BS v1/v2/v3/iki". Each
// entry gives the code pattern and the 16 bit MDEC run
// length codes it maps to. In a pattern, 0 and 1 are
// fixed bits, the letter x bits form the index into
// the value list (first x is the most significant
// index bit), and the final letter s is the sign bit:
// when s is 1 the level in the low 10 bits of the MDEC
// code is negated, as the section states.
//
// Two codes are handled separately in bs.go: the end
// of block code 10 (MDEC code FE00h) and the escape
// code 000001, which is followed by a raw 16 bit MDEC
// code. The all zero 12 bit pattern is listed in the
// document as unused; it is included here marked as
// unused so the decoder can consume it deliberately
// instead of looping.

type acCode struct {
	pattern string
	values  []uint16
	unused  bool
}

var acTable = []acCode{
	{pattern: "11s", values: []uint16{0x0001}},
	{pattern: "011s", values: []uint16{0x0401}},
	{pattern: "010xs", values: []uint16{0x0002, 0x0801}},
	{pattern: "0011xs", values: []uint16{0x1001, 0x0C01}},
	{pattern: "00101s", values: []uint16{0x0003}},
	{pattern: "00100xxxs", values: []uint16{0x3401, 0x0006, 0x3001, 0x2C01, 0x0C02, 0x0403, 0x0005, 0x2801}},
	{pattern: "0001xxs", values: []uint16{0x1C01, 0x1801, 0x0402, 0x1401}},
	{pattern: "00001xxs", values: []uint16{0x0802, 0x2401, 0x0004, 0x2001}},
	{pattern: "0000001xxxs", values: []uint16{0x4001, 0x1402, 0x0007, 0x0803, 0x0404, 0x3C01, 0x3801, 0x1002}},
	{pattern: "00000001xxxxs", values: []uint16{0x000B, 0x2002, 0x1003, 0x000A, 0x0804, 0x1C02, 0x5401, 0x5001, 0x0009, 0x4C01, 0x4801, 0x0405, 0x0C03, 0x0008, 0x1802, 0x4401}},
	{pattern: "000000001xxxxs", values: []uint16{0x2802, 0x2402, 0x1403, 0x0C04, 0x0805, 0x0407, 0x0406, 0x000F, 0x000E, 0x000D, 0x000C, 0x6801, 0x6401, 0x6001, 0x5C01, 0x5801}},
	{pattern: "0000000001xxxxs", values: []uint16{0x001F, 0x001E, 0x001D, 0x001C, 0x001B, 0x001A, 0x0019, 0x0018, 0x0017, 0x0016, 0x0015, 0x0014, 0x0013, 0x0012, 0x0011, 0x0010}},
	{pattern: "00000000001xxxxs", values: []uint16{0x0028, 0x0027, 0x0026, 0x0025, 0x0024, 0x0023, 0x0022, 0x0021, 0x0020, 0x040E, 0x040D, 0x040C, 0x040B, 0x040A, 0x0409, 0x0408}},
	{pattern: "000000000001xxxxs", values: []uint16{0x0412, 0x0411, 0x0410, 0x040F, 0x1803, 0x4002, 0x3C02, 0x3802, 0x3402, 0x3002, 0x2C02, 0x7C01, 0x7801, 0x7401, 0x7001, 0x6C01}},
	{pattern: "000000000000", unused: true},
}

// BS v3 DC Huffman categories, from section 13.20
// (CDROM File Video BS Compression DC Values), the
// table headed "DC v3". Each row is one magnitude
// category: a fixed prefix for chroma (Cr and Cb) and
// a fixed prefix for luma (Y1..Y4), followed (except
// for the zero row) by a sign bit s and by index bits
// that select the magnitude inside the category
// range. The offset added to the previous DC of the
// same component is plus or minus (base + index)
// times 4, with s equal to 0 for negative and 1 for
// positive, as the section states. The number of
// index bits is the base 2 logarithm of the category
// range size, which matches the count of index bits
// printed in the document patterns.
//
// The end of frame code (ten 1 bits), and the two
// patterns the document lists as unused (111111110
// and 1111111110), are handled in bs.go before this
// table is consulted for the end of frame case; an
// unused pattern that is followed by enough bits is
// indistinguishable from the longest category with
// sign bit 0 and is decoded as that category, which
// is the documented ambiguity choice made here.

type dcCategory struct {
	base      int // first magnitude of the category (0, 1, 2, 4, ...)
	indexBits int // number of index bits after the sign bit
	chromaPre string
	lumaPre   string
}

var dcCategories = []dcCategory{
	{base: 0, indexBits: 0, chromaPre: "00", lumaPre: "100"},
	{base: 1, indexBits: 0, chromaPre: "01", lumaPre: "00"},
	{base: 2, indexBits: 1, chromaPre: "10", lumaPre: "01"},
	{base: 4, indexBits: 2, chromaPre: "110", lumaPre: "101"},
	{base: 8, indexBits: 3, chromaPre: "1110", lumaPre: "110"},
	{base: 16, indexBits: 4, chromaPre: "11110", lumaPre: "1110"},
	{base: 32, indexBits: 5, chromaPre: "111110", lumaPre: "11110"},
	{base: 64, indexBits: 6, chromaPre: "1111110", lumaPre: "111110"},
	{base: 128, indexBits: 7, chromaPre: "11111110", lumaPre: "1111110"},
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/pad/pad.go ====================

// Package pad implements the PlayStation controller and memory card
// ports (the JOY registers at 1F801040h to 1F80104Fh), built from the
// psx-spx "Controllers and Memory Cards" chapters.
//
// Serial model simplification: real hardware clocks one bit at a time
// at the baud rate set in JOY_BAUD, and the /ACK pulse and IRQ7 arrive
// roughly 100 cycles after a byte completes. This package simplifies
// that to immediate byte completion: a byte written to JOY_DATA is
// transferred at once, the response byte is placed in the RX FIFO
// immediately, JOY_STAT reports TX ready at all times, RX-not-empty
// reflects the FIFO, the /ACK level bit reflects whether the byte just
// transferred was acknowledged, and OnIRQ fires synchronously from the
// write when the JOY_CTRL interrupt settings request it. Everything
// above the byte layer (the pad command set, config mode, rumble
// mapping, and the memory card read/write/ID protocols with their XOR
// checksums and end bytes) follows the document byte for byte.
//
// One pad (port 1) and one memory card are modelled. The JOY_CTRL slot
// bit is stored but both slots reach the same devices, matching how
// the system package wires a single controller.
//
// Memory card notes from the document:
//   - The card holds 128 Kbytes in 1024 sectors of 128 bytes. Erased
//     (unformatted) storage reads as FFh, so a fresh card image is
//     FFh-filled. The image is raw: directory management is left to
//     games, exactly as on hardware.
//   - The FLAG byte returned with every command starts at 08h on
//     power-up and card insertion. Bit3 means the directory has not
//     been read yet; per the document it is cleared by writing, not by
//     reading. Bit2 reports a write error on the next command.
//   - A write whose checksum does not match the XOR of the address
//     and data bytes is NOT stored, and the transfer ends with the
//     BadChecksum end byte 4Eh. A write or read to a sector above
//     3FFh ends with FFh (bad sector) for writes, and reads answer
//     FFFFh as the confirmed address and abort without data.
//   - With no card inserted, the card answers nothing: every response
//     byte reads FFh and no /ACK (and therefore no IRQ) is produced.
package pad

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// Register addresses (absolute).
const (
	addrData = 0x1F801040
	addrStat = 0x1F801044
	addrMode = 0x1F801048
	addrCtrl = 0x1F80104A
	addrBaud = 0x1F80104E
)

// JOY_CTRL bit masks used by this package.
const (
	ctrlTXEnable  = 1 << 0
	ctrlSelect    = 1 << 1 // /JOYn output low: port selected
	ctrlAck       = 1 << 4 // write 1: reset JOY_STAT bits 3 and 9
	ctrlReset     = 1 << 6 // write 1: reset most JOY registers to zero
	ctrlTXIRQEn   = 1 << 10
	ctrlRXIRQEn   = 1 << 11
	ctrlAckIRQEn  = 1 << 12
	ctrlSlotMask  = 1 << 13
	ctrlStoreMask = 0x3FFF &^ (ctrlAck | ctrlReset | 1<<7)
)

// Device selectors for the first byte of a transfer.
const (
	devNone byte = 0
	devPad  byte = 1
	devCard byte = 2
)

// Pad command bytes.
const (
	padCmdPoll   = 0x42
	padCmdConfig = 0x43
	padCmdLED    = 0x44
	padCmdInfo   = 0x45
	padCmdInfoA  = 0x46
	padCmdInfoC  = 0x47
	padCmdUnk48  = 0x48
	padCmdInfoB  = 0x4C
	padCmdRumble = 0x4D
)

// Memory card command bytes. The document names 52h "R" (read), 57h
// "W" (write), and 53h "S" (get ID). Some references name the get ID
// command 59h; both values are accepted here and answered identically.
const (
	cardCmdRead  = 0x52
	cardCmdWrite = 0x57
	cardCmdID    = 0x53
	cardCmdIDAlt = 0x59
)

const (
	cardSize    = 128 * 1024
	cardSectors = 1024
	sectorSize  = 128
)

// Controller is the JOY port block: registers, one digital/analog pad,
// and one memory card.
type Controller struct {
	// OnIRQ is fired when an acknowledge completes a byte transfer and
	// the JOY_CTRL interrupt settings request an IRQ for it. The
	// system package maps this to I_STAT bit 7.
	OnIRQ func()

	mode uint16
	ctrl uint16
	baud uint16

	rxFIFO  []byte
	statIRQ bool
	ackLow  bool

	// Host supplied pad inputs.
	buttons uint32 // bit set means pressed; see SetButtons
	rx, ry  uint8
	lx, ly  uint8

	// Pad state.
	analogMode       bool
	configMode       bool
	ledLock          bool
	motorMap         [6]byte // 4Dh mapping; FFh means unmapped
	rumbleConfigured bool
	motorSmall       bool
	motorBig         uint8

	// Card state.
	cardPresent bool
	cardFlag    byte // FLAG byte base value; starts at 08h
	cardErrNext bool // set bit2 of the next FLAG after a failed write
	card        []byte

	// In-flight transfer state.
	dev      byte
	cmd      byte
	pos      int // index of the byte currently being transferred
	total    int // total bytes in the transfer, address byte included
	curID    byte
	startCfg bool // transfer started in config mode
	iiVal    byte // config command index byte captured at pos 3
	motXX    byte // first motor byte, for the old one-motor method

	pendNewMap    [6]byte
	pendNewMapOK  bool
	pendMode      int8 // 0 none, 1 enter config, 2 exit config
	pendLED       int8 // 0 none, 1 set digital, 2 set analog
	pendLock      int8 // 0 none, 1 unlock, 2 lock
	lastSent      byte
	cardMSB       byte
	cardLSB       byte
	cardRecvChk   byte
	cardWriteOK   bool
	cardSectorBad bool
	cardWriteBuf  [sectorSize]byte
}

// New returns a Controller in its power-up state: digital mode, motors
// unmapped, card inserted and erased (FFh-filled), FLAG byte 08h.
func New() *Controller {
	c := &Controller{card: make([]byte, cardSize)}
	for i := range c.card {
		c.card[i] = 0xFF
	}
	c.cardPresent = true
	c.Reset()
	return c
}

// Reset resets the JOY registers and the protocol state machines, and
// returns the pad to digital non-config mode with rumble unmapped.
// The card image is preserved (a console reset does not erase the
// card), but the card FLAG byte returns to its power-up value 08h.
func (c *Controller) Reset() {
	c.mode, c.ctrl, c.baud = 0, 0, 0
	c.rxFIFO = c.rxFIFO[:0]
	c.statIRQ = false
	c.ackLow = false
	c.analogMode = false
	c.configMode = false
	c.ledLock = false
	for i := range c.motorMap {
		c.motorMap[i] = 0xFF
	}
	c.rumbleConfigured = false
	c.motorSmall = false
	c.motorBig = 0
	c.rx, c.ry, c.lx, c.ly = 0x80, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80
	c.cardFlag = 0x08
	c.cardErrNext = false
	c.resetTransfer()
}

func (c *Controller) resetTransfer() {
	c.dev = devNone
	c.cmd = 0
	c.pos = 0
	c.total = 0
	c.curID = 0
	c.startCfg = false
	c.iiVal = 0
	c.pendNewMapOK = false
	c.pendMode = 0
	c.pendLED = 0
	c.pendLock = 0
	c.cardWriteOK = false
	c.cardSectorBad = false
}

// SetButtons sets the pressed buttons. Bit layout: bit0 Select,
// bit1 L3, bit2 R3, bit3 Start, bit4 Up, bit5 Right, bit6 Down,
// bit7 Left, bit8 L2, bit9 R2, bit10 L1, bit11 R1, bit12 Triangle,
// bit13 Circle, bit14 Cross, bit15 Square. Set bits mean pressed;
// the wire format is active low and is derived from this mask.
func (c *Controller) SetButtons(mask uint32) { c.buttons = mask & 0xFFFF }

// SetAnalog sets the four stick axes as reported by analog polls:
// right stick X/Y, then left stick X/Y.
func (c *Controller) SetAnalog(rx, ry, lx, ly uint8) { c.rx, c.ry, c.lx, c.ly = rx, ry, lx, ly }

// SetAnalogMode forces the pad's analog mode from the host side.
// Guest software normally enters analog mode through the config
// sequence (the 44h LED command); a frontend that always presents
// an analog pad sets it here instead. Poll responses then carry
// the 73h ID and the stick bytes, and the digital buttons still
// read normally.
func (c *Controller) SetAnalogMode(b bool) { c.analogMode = b }

// AnalogMode reports whether the pad answers polls as an analog
// pad (73h) or a digital pad (41h).
func (c *Controller) AnalogMode() bool { return c.analogMode }

// CardImage returns the live 128 KB card image. Mutations made by the
// card protocol are visible to the caller and vice versa.
func (c *Controller) CardImage() []byte { return c.card }

// SetCardPresent inserts or removes the memory card. Inserting a card
// restores the FLAG byte to its power-up value 08h, as the document
// describes for re-insertion.
func (c *Controller) SetCardPresent(b bool) {
	if b && !c.cardPresent {
		c.cardFlag = 0x08
		c.cardErrNext = false
	}
	c.cardPresent = b
	if !b && c.dev == devCard {
		c.resetTransfer()
	}
}

// Motors returns the last vibration state commanded through the poll
// bytes selected by the 4Dh rumble mapping (or the old one-motor
// method before any 4Dh mapping is installed): the small motor is a
// digital on/off, the big motor an analog level.
func (c *Controller) Motors() (small bool, big uint8) { return c.motorSmall, c.motorBig }

// ReadReg reads a JOY register. Only the documented access sizes are
// claimed: JOY_DATA byte reads (a 32-bit read returns the FIFO head in
// the low byte and previews of the next entries above it, popping
// only the head), JOY_STAT 32-bit, JOY_MODE/JOY_CTRL/JOY_BAUD 16-bit.
func (c *Controller) ReadReg(addr uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	switch addr {
	case addrData:
		switch size {
		case 1:
			return uint32(c.popRX()), true
		case 4:
			var v uint32
			for i := 0; i < 4 && i < len(c.rxFIFO); i++ {
				v |= uint32(c.rxFIFO[i]) << (8 * i)
			}
			c.popRX()
			return v, true
		}
		return 0, false
	case addrStat:
		if size != 4 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return c.stat(), true
	case addrMode:
		if size != 2 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint32(c.mode), true
	case addrCtrl:
		if size != 2 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint32(c.ctrl), true
	case addrBaud:
		if size != 2 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint32(c.baud), true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// WriteReg writes a JOY register. JOY_DATA accepts byte writes and
// word writes (the low byte is sent, per the contract). JOY_MODE,
// JOY_CTRL, and JOY_BAUD accept halfword writes.
func (c *Controller) WriteReg(addr uint32, size int, v uint32) bool {
	switch addr {
	case addrData:
		if size != 1 && size != 4 {
			return false
		}
		c.writeData(byte(v))
		return true
	case addrMode:
		if size != 2 {
			return false
		}
		c.mode = uint16(v)
		return true
	case addrCtrl:
		if size != 2 {
			return false
		}
		c.writeCtrl(uint16(v))
		return true
	case addrBaud:
		if size != 2 {
			return false
		}
		c.baud = uint16(v)
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func (c *Controller) stat() uint32 {
	var s uint32
	s |= 1 << 0 // TX Ready Flag 1: ready (immediate completion model)
	if len(c.rxFIFO) > 0 {
		s |= 1 << 1 // RX FIFO Not Empty
	}
	s |= 1 << 2 // TX Ready Flag 2: finished
	// Bit3 RX parity error: never set (8-bit no-parity transfers).
	if c.ackLow {
		s |= 1 << 7 // /ACK Input Level: low
	}
	if c.statIRQ {
		s |= 1 << 9 // Interrupt Request (sticky until JOY_CTRL bit4)
	}
	// Bits 11-31 baudrate timer: reads zero in this model.
	return s
}

func (c *Controller) writeCtrl(v uint16) {
	old := c.ctrl
	if v&ctrlReset != 0 {
		// Reset most JOY registers to zero. Pad and card device state
		// reached through completed transfers is left alone.
		c.mode, c.ctrl, c.baud = 0, 0, 0
		c.rxFIFO = c.rxFIFO[:0]
		c.statIRQ = false
		c.ackLow = false
		c.resetTransfer()
		return
	}
	if v&ctrlAck != 0 {
		c.statIRQ = false // also clears the parity bit, which is never set
	}
	c.ctrl = v & ctrlStoreMask
	// Deselecting the port, or switching slots mid-transfer, resets
	// the addressed device state machine.
	if old&ctrlSelect != 0 && v&ctrlSelect == 0 {
		c.resetTransfer()
	}
	if (old^v)&ctrlSlotMask != 0 && c.pos > 0 {
		c.resetTransfer()
	}
	if v&ctrlSelect == 0 && c.pos > 0 {
		c.resetTransfer()
	}
}

func (c *Controller) popRX() byte {
	if len(c.rxFIFO) == 0 {
		return 0xFF
	}
	b := c.rxFIFO[0]
	c.rxFIFO = c.rxFIFO[1:]
	return b
}

// writeData runs one byte transfer. Bytes are ignored when JOY_CTRL
// does not enable the transfer (TX enable and port select both set),
// as the document prescribes.
func (c *Controller) writeData(b byte) {
	if c.ctrl&ctrlTXEnable == 0 || c.ctrl&ctrlSelect == 0 {
		return
	}
	resp, ack := c.transferByte(b)
	// The response byte is stored in the RX FIFO (the port is
	// selected, which is the normal receive-enable condition).
	if len(c.rxFIFO) < 8 {
		c.rxFIFO = append(c.rxFIFO, resp)
	}
	c.ackLow = ack
	// Interrupt generation, per the JOY_CTRL mode bits: ACK interrupt
	// (bit12) when the byte was acknowledged, RX interrupt (bit11)
	// when the FIFO reaches the count selected by bits 8-9, TX
	// interrupt (bit10) when TX is ready after a transfer.
	fire := false
	if ack && c.ctrl&ctrlAckIRQEn != 0 {
		fire = true
	}
	if c.ctrl&ctrlRXIRQEn != 0 {
		need := 1 << ((c.ctrl >> 8) & 3) // 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes
		if len(c.rxFIFO) >= need {
			fire = true
		}
	}
	if c.ctrl&ctrlTXIRQEn != 0 {
		fire = true
	}
	if fire {
		c.statIRQ = true
		if c.OnIRQ != nil {
			c.OnIRQ()
		}
	}
}

// transferByte processes one sent byte and returns the simultaneously
// received byte and whether the device acknowledged it. Per the
// document, the last byte of a transfer gets no /ACK.
func (c *Controller) transferByte(b byte) (resp byte, ack bool) {
	prev := c.lastSent
	c.lastSent = b
	if c.pos == 0 {
		switch b {
		case 0x01:
			c.dev = devPad
			c.pos = 1
			return 0xFF, true // Hi-Z dummy response, pad present
		case 0x81:
			if !c.cardPresent {
				return 0xFF, false // absent card answers nothing
			}
			c.dev = devCard
			c.pos = 1
			return 0xFF, true
		default:
			return 0xFF, false
		}
	}
	if c.dev == devPad {
		return c.padByte(b)
	}
	return c.cardByte(b, prev)
}

// finishTransfer applies deferred side effects and re-arms the state
// machine for the next address byte.
func (c *Controller) finishTransfer() {
	if c.pendMode == 1 {
		c.configMode = true
	} else if c.pendMode == 2 {
		c.configMode = false
	}
	if c.pendLED == 1 {
		c.analogMode = false
	} else if c.pendLED == 2 {
		c.analogMode = true
	}
	if c.pendLock == 1 {
		c.ledLock = false
	} else if c.pendLock == 2 {
		c.ledLock = true
	}
	if c.pendNewMapOK {
		c.motorMap = c.pendNewMap
		c.rumbleConfigured = true
	}
	c.resetTransfer()
}

// --- Pad protocol ---

func (c *Controller) padID() byte {
	if c.analogMode {
		return 0x73
	}
	return 0x41
}

// pollTotal is the transfer length of a poll-shaped response with the
// current mode and rumble mapping. Mapping a motor onto a poll byte
// beyond the digital payload extends the transfer (and therefore the
// low nibble of the digital ID), as the 4Dh chapter describes.
func (c *Controller) pollTotal() int {
	if c.configMode || c.analogMode {
		return 9
	}
	total := 5
	for j := 0; j < 6; j++ {
		if c.motorMap[j] != 0xFF && j+4 > total {
			total = j + 4
		}
	}
	return total
}

func (c *Controller) padByte(b byte) (byte, bool) {
	pos := c.pos
	if pos == 1 {
		c.cmd = b
		c.startCfg = c.configMode
		switch {
		case c.configMode:
			c.total = 9
			c.curID = 0xF3
		case b == padCmdPoll || b == padCmdConfig:
			c.total = c.pollTotal()
			c.curID = c.padID()
			if !c.analogMode && c.total != 5 {
				c.curID = 0x40 | byte((c.total-3)/2)
			}
		default:
			// Unknown command in normal mode: answer the ID byte,
			// then end the transfer so the machine cannot hang.
			c.total = 2
			c.curID = c.padID()
		}
		c.pos = 2
		if c.total <= 2 {
			resp := c.curID
			c.finishTransfer()
			return resp, false
		}
		return c.curID, true
	}
	// Data positions: capture side effects first, then respond.
	c.padData(pos, b)
	resp := c.padResponse(pos)
	done := pos >= c.total-1
	c.pos++
	if done {
		c.finishTransfer()
		return resp, false
	}
	return resp, true
}

// padData records the side effects of a sent byte at position pos
// (pos 2 is the first byte after the command byte).
func (c *Controller) padData(pos int, b byte) {
	if pos == 3 {
		c.iiVal = b
	}
	switch c.cmd {
	case padCmdPoll:
		c.pollMotor(pos, b)
	case padCmdConfig:
		if c.startCfg {
			if pos == 3 {
				if b == 0 {
					c.pendMode = 2 // exit config mode
				} else if b == 1 {
					c.pendMode = 0 // stay in config mode
				}
			}
		} else {
			c.pollMotor(pos, b)
			if pos == 3 && b == 1 {
				c.pendMode = 1 // enter config mode
			}
		}
	case padCmdLED:
		if c.startCfg {
			if pos == 3 {
				if b == 0 {
					c.pendLED = 1
				} else if b == 1 {
					c.pendLED = 2
				}
			}
			if pos == 4 {
				eff := b
				if b > 3 {
					eff = b & 3 // 04h..FFh acts as Key AND 03h
				}
				if eff == 3 {
					c.pendLock = 2
				} else {
					c.pendLock = 1
				}
			}
		}
	case padCmdRumble:
		if c.startCfg && pos >= 3 && pos <= 8 {
			c.pendNewMap[pos-3] = b
			if pos == 8 {
				c.pendNewMapOK = true
			}
		}
	}
}

// pollMotor applies one sent poll byte to the rumble motors, using
// the 4Dh mapping once installed, and the old one-motor method before
// that (the byte at pos 3 in 40h..7Fh together with an odd byte at
// pos 4 switches the small motor).
func (c *Controller) pollMotor(pos int, b byte) {
	idx := pos - 3 // poll bytes at pos 3..8 map to aa..ff
	if idx < 0 || idx > 5 {
		return
	}
	if c.rumbleConfigured {
		switch c.motorMap[idx] {
		case 0x00:
			c.motorSmall = b&1 != 0
		case 0x01:
			c.motorBig = b
		}
		return
	}
	if pos == 3 {
		c.motXX = b
	}
	if pos == 4 {
		c.motorSmall = c.motXX >= 0x40 && c.motXX <= 0x7F && b&1 != 0
	}
}

// padResponse returns the pad byte sent back while the host clocks
// out the byte at position pos (pos 2 answers 5Ah, pos 3 and up are
// the payload).
func (c *Controller) padResponse(pos int) byte {
	if pos == 2 {
		return 0x5A
	}
	j := pos - 3 // payload index
	buttons := uint16(c.buttons)
	btnLo := byte(^buttons)
	btnHi := byte(^(buttons >> 8))
	pollPayload := []byte{btnLo, btnHi, c.rx, c.ry, c.lx, c.ly}
	if !c.startCfg && !c.analogMode && c.cmd == padCmdPoll {
		// Digital poll: payload past the buttons is padding, except
		// for bytes that exist only because a motor is mapped there.
		if j >= 2 {
			return 0x00
		}
	}
	switch c.cmd {
	case padCmdPoll:
		if j < len(pollPayload) {
			return pollPayload[j]
		}
		return 0
	case padCmdConfig:
		if c.startCfg {
			return 0 // config-mode exit/stay answers zero payload
		}
		if j < len(pollPayload) {
			return pollPayload[j]
		}
		return 0
	case padCmdLED:
		return 0 // payload includes the Err byte, 00h on this pad class
	case padCmdInfo:
		led := byte(0)
		if c.analogMode {
			led = 1
		}
		info := []byte{0x01, 0x02, led, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00}
		if j < len(info) {
			return info[j]
		}
		return 0
	case padCmdInfoA:
		var fnc, sub, siz, pwr byte
		switch c.iiVal {
		case 0:
			fnc, sub, siz, pwr = 0x01, 0x02, 0x00, 0x0A // small motor
		case 1:
			fnc, sub, siz, pwr = 0x01, 0x01, 0x01, 0x14 // big motor
		}
		info := []byte{0x00, 0x00, fnc, sub, siz, pwr}
		if j < len(info) {
			return info[j]
		}
		return 0
	case padCmdInfoC:
		var info []byte
		if c.iiVal == 0 {
			info = []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00}
		} else {
			info = []byte{0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00}
		}
		if j < len(info) {
			return info[j]
		}
		return 0
	case padCmdUnk48:
		ee := byte(0)
		if c.iiVal <= 1 && j == 4 {
			ee = 0x01
		}
		return ee
	case padCmdInfoB:
		var cc, dd byte
		switch c.iiVal {
		case 0:
			cc, dd = 0x00, 0x04
		case 1:
			cc, dd = 0x00, 0x07
		}
		info := []byte{0x00, 0x00, cc, dd, 0x00, 0x00}
		if j < len(info) {
			return info[j]
		}
		return 0
	case padCmdRumble:
		// Answers the OLD mapping while the new one is being sent.
		if j < 6 {
			return c.motorMap[j]
		}
		return 0
	default:
		// Unused and unknown commands in config mode answer the
		// documented dummy pattern: ID F3h, 5Ah, then zero bytes.
		return 0
	}
}

// --- Memory card protocol ---

func (c *Controller) cardFlagByte() byte {
	f := c.cardFlag
	if c.cardErrNext {
		f |= 0x04
		c.cardErrNext = false
	}
	return f
}

func (c *Controller) cardSector() int {
	return int(c.cardMSB)<<8 | int(c.cardLSB)
}

func (c *Controller) cardChecksum() byte {
	chk := c.cardMSB ^ c.cardLSB
	off := c.cardSector() * sectorSize
	if c.cardSector() < cardSectors {
		for _, d := range c.card[off : off+sectorSize] {
			chk ^= d
		}
	}
	return chk
}

func (c *Controller) cardByte(b byte, prev byte) (byte, bool) {
	pos := c.pos
	if pos == 1 {
		c.cmd = b
		switch b {
		case cardCmdRead:
			c.total = 140
		case cardCmdWrite:
			c.total = 138
		case cardCmdID, cardCmdIDAlt:
			c.total = 10
		default:
			// Invalid command: answer FLAG, then abort the transfer.
			resp := c.cardFlagByte()
			c.resetTransfer()
			return resp, false
		}
		resp := c.cardFlagByte()
		c.pos = 2
		return resp, true
	}
	var resp byte
	done := false
	switch c.cmd {
	case cardCmdRead:
		switch {
		case pos == 2:
			resp = 0x5A
		case pos == 3:
			resp = 0x5D
		case pos == 4:
			c.cardMSB = b
			resp = 0x00
		case pos == 5:
			c.cardLSB = b
			c.cardSectorBad = c.cardSector() >= cardSectors
			resp = prev // (pre): echoes the MSB
		case pos == 6:
			resp = 0x5C
		case pos == 7:
			resp = 0x5D
		case pos == 8:
			if c.cardSectorBad {
				resp = 0xFF
			} else {
				resp = c.cardMSB
			}
		case pos == 9:
			if c.cardSectorBad {
				resp = 0xFF
				done = true // FFFFh confirmed address, then abort
			} else {
				resp = c.cardLSB
			}
		case pos >= 10 && pos <= 137:
			off := c.cardSector()*sectorSize + (pos - 10)
			resp = c.card[off]
		case pos == 138:
			resp = c.cardChecksum()
		case pos == 139:
			resp = 0x47 // "G": good
			done = true
		}
	case cardCmdWrite:
		switch {
		case pos == 2:
			resp = 0x5A
		case pos == 3:
			resp = 0x5D
		case pos == 4:
			c.cardMSB = b
			resp = 0x00
		case pos == 5:
			c.cardLSB = b
			c.cardSectorBad = c.cardSector() >= cardSectors
			resp = prev
		case pos >= 6 && pos <= 133:
			c.cardWriteBuf[pos-6] = b
			resp = prev
		case pos == 134:
			c.cardRecvChk = b
			resp = prev
			// Verify before storing: the checksum covers the
			// address bytes and all 128 data bytes.
			chk := c.cardMSB ^ c.cardLSB
			for _, d := range c.cardWriteBuf {
				chk ^= d
			}
			c.cardWriteOK = chk == b && !c.cardSectorBad
			if c.cardWriteOK {
				off := c.cardSector() * sectorSize
				copy(c.card[off:off+sectorSize], c.cardWriteBuf[:])
			}
		case pos == 135:
			resp = 0x5C
		case pos == 136:
			resp = 0x5D
		case pos == 137:
			switch {
			case c.cardSectorBad:
				resp = 0xFF // bad sector
			case !c.cardWriteOK:
				resp = 0x4E // "N": bad checksum
			default:
				resp = 0x47 // "G": good
			}
			// Any completed write clears FLAG bit3 (the document's
			// dummy-write trick relies on this); a checksum failure
			// raises bit2 on the next command instead.
			c.cardFlag &^= 0x08
			if !c.cardWriteOK && !c.cardSectorBad {
				c.cardErrNext = true
			}
			done = true
		}
	case cardCmdID, cardCmdIDAlt:
		switch pos {
		case 2:
			resp = 0x5A
		case 3:
			resp = 0x5D
		case 4:
			resp = 0x5C
		case 5:
			resp = 0x5D
		case 6:
			resp = 0x04
		case 7, 8:
			resp = 0x00
		case 9:
			resp = 0x80
			done = true
		}
	}
	c.pos++
	if done {
		c.resetTransfer()
		return resp, false
	}
	return resp, true
}

// --- Serialization ---

// StateSize is the fixed serialized size: a 512-byte header holding
// the JOY registers, protocol state, pad mode and config state, and
// the in-flight transfer, followed by the full 128 KB card image.
const StateSize = 512 + cardSize

const stateMagic = "PS1PAD01"

var errBadState = errors.New("pad: bad serialized state")

// Serialize returns the full controller state, exactly StateSize
// bytes, including the card image.
func (c *Controller) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	copy(out[0:8], stateMagic)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[8:10], c.mode)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[10:12], c.ctrl)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[12:14], c.baud)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[16:20], c.buttons)
	out[20], out[21], out[22], out[23] = c.rx, c.ry, c.lx, c.ly
	var fl byte
	if c.configMode {
		fl |= 1 << 0
	}
	if c.analogMode {
		fl |= 1 << 1
	}
	if c.ledLock {
		fl |= 1 << 2
	}
	if c.cardPresent {
		fl |= 1 << 3
	}
	if c.statIRQ {
		fl |= 1 << 4
	}
	if c.ackLow {
		fl |= 1 << 5
	}
	if c.motorSmall {
		fl |= 1 << 6
	}
	out[24] = fl
	if c.rumbleConfigured {
		out[25] = 1
	}
	out[26] = c.motorBig
	out[27] = c.cardFlag
	copy(out[28:34], c.motorMap[:])
	out[34] = c.dev
	out[35] = c.cmd
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[36:38], uint16(c.pos))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[38:40], uint16(c.total))
	out[40] = c.curID
	if c.startCfg {
		out[41] = 1
	}
	out[42] = c.iiVal
	out[43] = c.motXX
	out[44] = c.lastSent
	out[45] = c.cardMSB
	out[46] = c.cardLSB
	out[47] = c.cardRecvChk
	out[48] = byte(len(c.rxFIFO))
	copy(out[49:57], c.rxFIFO)
	copy(out[57:185], c.cardWriteBuf[:])
	copy(out[185:191], c.pendNewMap[:])
	if c.pendNewMapOK {
		out[191] = 1
	}
	out[192] = byte(c.pendMode)
	out[193] = byte(c.pendLED)
	out[194] = byte(c.pendLock)
	if c.cardWriteOK {
		out[195] = 1
	}
	if c.cardSectorBad {
		out[196] = 1
	}
	if c.cardErrNext {
		out[197] = 1
	}
	copy(out[512:512+cardSize], c.card)
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (c *Controller) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != StateSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("pad: state size %d, want %d", len(in), StateSize)
	}
	if string(in[0:8]) != stateMagic {
		return errBadState
	}
	c.mode = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[8:10])
	c.ctrl = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[10:12])
	c.baud = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[12:14])
	c.buttons = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[16:20])
	c.rx, c.ry, c.lx, c.ly = in[20], in[21], in[22], in[23]
	fl := in[24]
	c.configMode = fl&(1<<0) != 0
	c.analogMode = fl&(1<<1) != 0
	c.ledLock = fl&(1<<2) != 0
	c.cardPresent = fl&(1<<3) != 0
	c.statIRQ = fl&(1<<4) != 0
	c.ackLow = fl&(1<<5) != 0
	c.motorSmall = fl&(1<<6) != 0
	c.rumbleConfigured = in[25] != 0
	c.motorBig = in[26]
	c.cardFlag = in[27]
	copy(c.motorMap[:], in[28:34])
	c.dev = in[34]
	c.cmd = in[35]
	c.pos = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[36:38]))
	c.total = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[38:40]))
	c.curID = in[40]
	c.startCfg = in[41] != 0
	c.iiVal = in[42]
	c.motXX = in[43]
	c.lastSent = in[44]
	c.cardMSB = in[45]
	c.cardLSB = in[46]
	c.cardRecvChk = in[47]
	n := int(in[48])
	if n > 8 {
		n = 8
	}
	c.rxFIFO = append(c.rxFIFO[:0], in[49:49+n]...)
	copy(c.cardWriteBuf[:], in[57:185])
	copy(c.pendNewMap[:], in[185:191])
	c.pendNewMapOK = in[191] != 0
	c.pendMode = int8(in[192])
	c.pendLED = int8(in[193])
	c.pendLock = int8(in[194])
	c.cardWriteOK = in[195] != 0
	c.cardSectorBad = in[196] != 0
	c.cardErrNext = in[197] != 0
	copy(c.card, in[512:512+cardSize])
	return nil
}

package pad

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"
)

// selectPort enables transfers on port 1, with optional extra JOY_CTRL
// bits (for example interrupt enables).
func selectPort(c *Controller, extra uint16) {
	if ok := c.WriteReg(0x1F80104A, 2, uint32(0x0003|extra)); !ok {
		panic("JOY_CTRL write not claimed")
	}
}

func deselect(c *Controller) {
	c.WriteReg(0x1F80104A, 2, 0x0000)
}

// xfer clocks one byte through JOY_DATA and returns the response.
func xfer(t *testing.T, c *Controller, b byte) byte {
	t.Helper()
	if ok := c.WriteReg(0x1F801040, 1, uint32(b)); !ok {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_DATA write of %02X not claimed", b)
	}
	v, ok := c.ReadReg(0x1F801040, 1)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_DATA read not claimed")
	}
	return byte(v)
}

// run clocks a full transfer and returns all response bytes,
// including the dummy response to the address byte.
func run(t *testing.T, c *Controller, send ...byte) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	selectPort(c, 0)
	out := make([]byte, len(send))
	for i, b := range send {
		out[i] = xfer(t, c, b)
	}
	deselect(c)
	return out
}

func statReg(t *testing.T, c *Controller) uint32 {
	t.Helper()
	v, ok := c.ReadReg(0x1F801044, 4)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("JOY_STAT read not claimed")
	}
	return v
}

func enterConfig(t *testing.T, c *Controller) {
	t.Helper()
	got := run(t, c, 0x01, 0x43, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00)
	if got[1] != 0x41 && got[1] != 0x73 {
		t.Fatalf("enter config response ID = %02X, want normal ID", got[1])
	}
}

func exitConfig(t *testing.T, c *Controller) {
	t.Helper()
	got := run(t, c, 0x01, 0x43, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want := []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("exit config = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
}

func TestPollDigital(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	// Start (bit3) + Cross (bit14) + Up (bit4).
	c.SetButtons(1<<3 | 1<<14 | 1<<4)
	got := run(t, c, 0x01, 0x42, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	// Buttons are active low: low byte covers bits 0..7 (Start and Up
	// pressed), high byte bits 8..15 (Cross pressed).
	want := []byte{0xFF, 0x41, 0x5A, 0xE7, 0xBF}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("poll = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
}

func TestAnalogMode(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	c.SetAnalog(0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44)
	enterConfig(t, c)
	// Set analog mode (LED on) and lock it.
	got := run(t, c, 0x01, 0x44, 0x00, 0x01, 0x03, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want := []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("set LED = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	// Command 45h reports Typ 01, Num 02, Led 01 (analog), Act 02,
	// Com 01.
	got = run(t, c, 0x01, 0x45, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want = []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0x01, 0x02, 0x01, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("get LED = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	exitConfig(t, c)
	// Poll now returns ID 73h and the four stick bytes in order.
	c.SetButtons(0)
	got = run(t, c, 0x01, 0x42, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want = []byte{0xFF, 0x73, 0x5A, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("analog poll = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
}

func TestConfigInfoCommands(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	enterConfig(t, c)
	// 46h with ii=0 (small motor) and ii=1 (big motor).
	got := run(t, c, 0x01, 0x46, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want := []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x00, 0x0A}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("46h ii=0 = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	got = run(t, c, 0x01, 0x46, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want = []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01, 0x14}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("46h ii=1 = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	// 47h with ii=0 returns the combiner list constants.
	got = run(t, c, 0x01, 0x47, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want = []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0x00, 0x00, 0x02, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("47h = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	// 4Ch with ii=0 and ii=1.
	got = run(t, c, 0x01, 0x4C, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want = []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x04, 0x00, 0x00}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("4Ch ii=0 = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	got = run(t, c, 0x01, 0x4C, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want = []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x07, 0x00, 0x00}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("4Ch ii=1 = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	exitConfig(t, c)
}

func TestVibrationMapping(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	enterConfig(t, c)
	// Map small motor to poll byte aa, big motor to bb. The response
	// echoes the OLD mapping (all FFh = unmapped).
	got := run(t, c, 0x01, 0x4D, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
	want := []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("4Dh = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	exitConfig(t, c)
	// Poll with motor bytes at the mapped positions: small on (bit0),
	// big at A5h.
	run(t, c, 0x01, 0x42, 0x00, 0x01, 0xA5)
	small, big := c.Motors()
	if !small || big != 0xA5 {
		t.Fatalf("Motors = (%v, %02X), want (true, A5)", small, big)
	}
	// Poll again with both off.
	run(t, c, 0x01, 0x42, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	small, big = c.Motors()
	if small || big != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Motors = (%v, %02X), want (false, 00)", small, big)
	}
}

func xorBytes(bs ...byte) byte {
	var x byte
	for _, b := range bs {
		x ^= b
	}
	return x
}

func cardWrite(t *testing.T, c *Controller, sector uint16, data []byte, corrupt bool) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	chk := xorBytes(byte(sector>>8), byte(sector))
	for _, d := range data {
		chk ^= d
	}
	if corrupt {
		chk ^= 0xFF
	}
	send := []byte{0x81, 0x57, 0x00, 0x00, byte(sector >> 8), byte(sector)}
	send = append(send, data...)
	send = append(send, chk, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	return run(t, c, send...)
}

func cardRead(t *testing.T, c *Controller, sector uint16) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	send := []byte{0x81, 0x52, 0x00, 0x00, byte(sector >> 8), byte(sector)}
	send = append(send, make([]byte, 134)...)
	return run(t, c, send...)
}

func TestCardWriteRead(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	data := make([]byte, 128)
	for i := range data {
		data[i] = byte(i*3 + 7)
	}
	got := cardWrite(t, c, 0, data, false)
	// FLAG starts at 08h; IDs 5Ah 5Dh; end byte 47h (good).
	if got[1] != 0x08 || got[2] != 0x5A || got[3] != 0x5D {
		t.Fatalf("write head = % X, want FLAG 08, 5A, 5D", got[:4])
	}
	if got[len(got)-1] != 0x47 {
		t.Fatalf("write end = %02X, want 47", got[len(got)-1])
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(c.CardImage()[0:128], data) {
		t.Fatal("card image does not match written sector")
	}
	// FLAG bit3 is cleared by writing, so the read sees FLAG 00h.
	got = cardRead(t, c, 0)
	if got[1] != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("read FLAG = %02X, want 00 after a write", got[1])
	}
	if got[2] != 0x5A || got[3] != 0x5D || got[6] != 0x5C || got[7] != 0x5D {
		t.Fatalf("read head = % X", got[:8])
	}
	if got[8] != 0x00 || got[9] != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("confirmed address = %02X %02X, want 00 00", got[8], got[9])
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(got[10:138], data) {
		t.Fatal("read data does not match written data")
	}
	wantChk := xorBytes(0x00, 0x00)
	for _, d := range data {
		wantChk ^= d
	}
	if got[138] != wantChk {
		t.Fatalf("read checksum = %02X, want %02X", got[138], wantChk)
	}
	if got[139] != 0x47 {
		t.Fatalf("read end = %02X, want 47", got[139])
	}
	// A non-zero sector round trips too, through CardImage directly.
	c.CardImage()[5*128] = 0xAB
	got = cardRead(t, c, 5)
	if got[10] != 0xAB || got[8] != 0x00 || got[9] != 0x05 {
		t.Fatalf("sector 5 read: data %02X addr %02X %02X", got[10], got[8], got[9])
	}
}

func TestCardBadChecksum(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	good := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x11}, 128)
	cardWrite(t, c, 2, good, false)
	bad := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0x99}, 128)
	got := cardWrite(t, c, 2, bad, true)
	if got[len(got)-1] != 0x4E {
		t.Fatalf("bad checksum end = %02X, want 4E", got[len(got)-1])
	}
	// The corrupted write must not be stored.
	if !bytes.Equal(c.CardImage()[2*128:3*128], good) {
		t.Fatal("bad checksum write overwrote the sector")
	}
	// The next command reports the write error in FLAG bit2.
	got = run(t, c, 0x81, 0x53, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	if got[1]&0x04 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("FLAG after bad write = %02X, want bit2 set", got[1])
	}
}

func TestCardGetID(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	// Both the documented 53h "S" and the 59h alias answer the same
	// sequence. Get ID is not a write, so FLAG stays 08h for both.
	for _, cmd := range []byte{0x53, 0x59} {
		got := run(t, c, 0x81, cmd, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
		want := []byte{0xFF, 0x08, 0x5A, 0x5D, 0x5C, 0x5D, 0x04, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80}
		if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Fatalf("card ID cmd %02X = % X, want % X", cmd, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestCardAbsent(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	c.SetCardPresent(false)
	selectPort(c, 0x1000) // ACK IRQ enabled: absent card must not IRQ
	irq := 0
	c.OnIRQ = func() { irq++ }
	for _, b := range []byte{0x81, 0x52, 0x00, 0x00} {
		if got := xfer(t, c, b); got != 0xFF {
			t.Fatalf("absent card response = %02X, want FF", got)
		}
	}
	deselect(c)
	if irq != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("absent card raised %d IRQs, want 0", irq)
	}
	if s := statReg(t, c); s&(1<<7) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_STAT /ACK low for absent card: %08X", s)
	}
}

func TestStatAndIRQ(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	irq := 0
	c.OnIRQ = func() { irq++ }
	selectPort(c, 0x1000) // TXEN + select + ACK interrupt enable
	if ok := c.WriteReg(0x1F801040, 1, 0x01); !ok {
		t.Fatal("JOY_DATA write not claimed")
	}
	if irq != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("OnIRQ fired %d times, want 1", irq)
	}
	s := statReg(t, c)
	// TX ready bits set, RX not empty, /ACK low, IRQ request set.
	if s&(1<<0) == 0 || s&(1<<2) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_STAT TX ready bits clear: %08X", s)
	}
	if s&(1<<1) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_STAT RX-not-empty clear: %08X", s)
	}
	if s&(1<<7) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_STAT /ACK bit clear: %08X", s)
	}
	if s&(1<<9) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_STAT IRQ bit clear: %08X", s)
	}
	// Reading JOY_DATA drains the RX byte.
	v, _ := c.ReadReg(0x1F801040, 1)
	if byte(v) != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("address response = %02X, want FF (Hi-Z)", byte(v))
	}
	if s = statReg(t, c); s&(1<<1) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_STAT still RX-not-empty after drain: %08X", s)
	}
	// Acknowledging through JOY_CTRL bit4 clears JOY_STAT bit9.
	c.WriteReg(0x1F80104A, 2, 0x1003|(1<<4))
	if s = statReg(t, c); s&(1<<9) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_STAT IRQ bit still set after ack: %08X", s)
	}
	deselect(c)
	// With transfers disabled, TX bytes are ignored: no IRQ, no FIFO.
	irq = 0
	c.WriteReg(0x1F801040, 1, 0x01)
	if irq != 0 {
		t.Fatal("IRQ fired while port deselected")
	}
	if s = statReg(t, c); s&(1<<1) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("RX FIFO filled while port deselected")
	}
}

func TestUnknownCommandInConfig(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	enterConfig(t, c)
	got := run(t, c, 0x01, 0x99, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want := []byte{0xFF, 0xF3, 0x5A, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("unknown config cmd = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
	// The state machine is still alive: exit and poll work.
	exitConfig(t, c)
	c.SetButtons(1 << 3)
	got = run(t, c, 0x01, 0x42, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	want = []byte{0xFF, 0x41, 0x5A, 0xF7, 0xFF}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("poll after unknown cmd = % X, want % X", got, want)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	data := make([]byte, 128)
	for i := range data {
		data[i] = byte(0xA0 + i)
	}
	cardWrite(t, c, 3, data, false)
	enterConfig(t, c)
	if len(c.Serialize()) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize size = %d, want %d", len(c.Serialize()), StateSize)
	}
	d := New()
	if err := d.Deserialize(c.Serialize()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Still in config mode on the restored controller: 45h answers
	// with the config ID, and exit works.
	got := run(t, d, 0x01, 0x45, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
	if got[1] != 0xF3 {
		t.Fatalf("restored config ID = %02X, want F3", got[1])
	}
	exitConfig(t, d)
	// The written sector survived.
	got = cardRead(t, d, 3)
	if !bytes.Equal(got[10:138], data) {
		t.Fatal("restored card sector mismatch")
	}
	if err := d.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("short state accepted")
	}
	bad := c.Serialize()
	bad[0] ^= 0xFF
	if err := d.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("bad magic accepted")
	}
}

func TestRegisterClaiming(t *testing.T) {
	c := New()
	// Wrong sizes are not claimed, so the bus can fall back.
	if _, ok := c.ReadReg(0x1F801044, 2); ok {
		t.Fatal("JOY_STAT halfword read claimed")
	}
	if _, ok := c.ReadReg(0x1F801048, 4); ok {
		t.Fatal("JOY_MODE word read claimed")
	}
	if ok := c.WriteReg(0x1F801040, 2, 0x42); ok {
		t.Fatal("JOY_DATA halfword write claimed")
	}
	if _, ok := c.ReadReg(0x1F801050, 1); ok {
		t.Fatal("SIO address claimed by JOY block")
	}
	// Word write to JOY_DATA sends the low byte.
	selectPort(c, 0)
	if ok := c.WriteReg(0x1F801040, 4, 0x12345601); !ok {
		t.Fatal("JOY_DATA word write not claimed")
	}
	v, _ := c.ReadReg(0x1F801040, 1)
	if byte(v) != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("word write response = %02X, want FF", byte(v))
	}
	deselect(c)
	// MODE and BAUD are plain storage.
	c.WriteReg(0x1F801048, 2, 0x000D)
	c.WriteReg(0x1F80104E, 2, 0x0088)
	if v, _ := c.ReadReg(0x1F801048, 2); v != 0x000D {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_MODE = %04X, want 000D", v)
	}
	if v, _ := c.ReadReg(0x1F80104E, 2); v != 0x0088 {
		t.Fatalf("JOY_BAUD = %04X, want 0088", v)
	}
	// Fresh card image is the erased value FFh throughout.
	img := New().CardImage()
	if len(img) != 128*1024 {
		t.Fatalf("card image size = %d", len(img))
	}
	for i, b := range img {
		if b != 0xFF {
			t.Fatalf("card image[%d] = %02X, want FF (erased)", i, b)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/envelope.go ====================

package spu

// The envelope step model follows the psx-spx
// "Envelope Operation depending on
// Shift/Step/Mode/Direction" pseudocode: a step size
// derived from the step field (with the sign flip for
// decreasing or phase negative modes), shifted by
// the shift field, applied when a counter that
// accumulates 8000h shifted by the shift field
// reaches 8000h. Exponential increase slows down
// above level 6000h; exponential decrease scales the
// step by the current level. A rate whose shift and
// step fields are all ones never steps.

type envParams struct {
	shift    int
	stepVal  int
	exp      bool
	decrease bool
	phaseNeg bool
	allOnes  bool // shift/step fields are all ones: never steps
}

// envApply advances one 44.1 kHz envelope tick and
// returns the new level.
func envApply(level int32, counter *int32, p envParams) int32 {
	step := int32(7 - p.stepVal)
	if p.decrease != p.phaseNeg {
		step = ^step // +7..+4 becomes -8..-5
	}
	var inc int32
	if p.shift <= 11 {
		step <<= uint(11 - p.shift)
		inc = 0x8000
	} else {
		inc = int32(0x8000) >> uint(p.shift-11)
	}
	if p.exp && !p.decrease && level > 0x6000 {
		if p.shift < 10 {
			step >>= 2
		} else if p.shift >= 11 {
			inc >>= 2
		} else {
			step >>= 1
			inc >>= 1
		}
	} else if p.exp && p.decrease {
		step = step * level / 0x8000
	}
	if inc == 0 && !p.allOnes {
		inc = 1
	}
	*counter += inc
	if *counter < 0x8000 {
		return level
	}
	*counter -= 0x8000
	level += step
	if !p.decrease {
		if level > 0x7FFF {
			level = 0x7FFF
		}
		if level < -0x8000 {
			level = -0x8000
		}
	} else if p.phaseNeg {
		if level > 0 {
			level = 0
		}
		if level < -0x8000 {
			level = -0x8000
		}
	} else {
		if level < 0 {
			level = 0
		}
	}
	return level
}

// sweepParams extracts the sweep fields from a
// volume register value in sweep mode.
func sweepParams(raw uint16) envParams {
	return envParams{
		shift:    int(raw>>2) & 0x1F,
		stepVal:  int(raw) & 3,
		exp:      raw&0x4000 != 0,
		decrease: raw&0x2000 != 0,
		phaseNeg: raw&0x1000 != 0,
		allOnes:  raw&0x7C == 0x7C && raw&3 == 3,
	}
}

func (v *voice) sustainLevel() int32 {
	lvl := int32((v.adsrLo&0xF)+1)<<11 - 1
	if lvl > 0x7FFF {
		lvl = 0x7FFF
	}
	return lvl
}

// runEnvelope advances the ADSR envelope by one
// output sample.
func (v *voice) runEnvelope() {
	switch v.phase {
	case phaseAttack:
		p := envParams{
			shift:   int(v.adsrLo>>10) & 0x1F,
			stepVal: int(v.adsrLo>>8) & 3,
			exp:     v.adsrLo&0x8000 != 0,
			allOnes: v.adsrLo&0x7C00 == 0x7C00 && (v.adsrLo>>8)&3 == 3,
		}
		v.envLevel = envApply(v.envLevel, &v.envCounter, p)
		if v.envLevel >= 0x7FFF {
			v.envLevel = 0x7FFF
			v.phase = phaseDecay
			v.envCounter = 0
		}
	case phaseDecay:
		p := envParams{
			shift:    int(v.adsrLo>>4) & 0xF,
			stepVal:  0, // fixed step "-8" after the sign flip
			exp:      true,
			decrease: true,
		}
		v.envLevel = envApply(v.envLevel, &v.envCounter, p)
		if v.envLevel <= v.sustainLevel() {
			// Decay decreases until the sustain
			// level: a step that undershoots stops
			// at the level instead of below it.
			v.envLevel = v.sustainLevel()
			v.phase = phaseSustain
			v.envCounter = 0
		}
	case phaseSustain:
		p := envParams{
			shift:    int(v.adsrHi>>8) & 0x1F,
			stepVal:  int(v.adsrHi>>6) & 3,
			exp:      v.adsrHi&0x8000 != 0,
			decrease: v.adsrHi&0x4000 != 0,
			allOnes:  v.adsrHi&0x1F00 == 0x1F00 && (v.adsrHi>>6)&3 == 3,
		}
		v.envLevel = envApply(v.envLevel, &v.envCounter, p)
	case phaseRelease:
		p := envParams{
			shift:    int(v.adsrHi) & 0x1F,
			stepVal:  0,
			exp:      v.adsrHi&0x20 != 0,
			decrease: true,
			allOnes:  v.adsrHi&0x1F == 0x1F,
		}
		v.envLevel = envApply(v.envLevel, &v.envCounter, p)
		if v.envLevel <= 0 {
			v.envLevel = 0
			v.phase = phaseOff
			v.active = false
		}
	}
}

// runSweep advances one volume sweep channel by one
// output sample and returns the new level.
func runSweep(level int32, counter *int32, raw uint16) int32 {
	return envApply(level, counter, sweepParams(raw))
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/mix.go ====================

package spu

// Advance advances the SPU by CPU cycles (CPU clock
// 33868800 Hz) and generates output samples at
// 44100 Hz. The ratio is exact (768 CPU cycles per
// sample); the remainder is kept in cycleAcc so the
// conversion is fully deterministic. cd is called
// exactly once per generated sample to fetch the CD
// input sample; a nil cd is silence.
func (s *SPU) Advance(cycles int, cd func() (int16, int16)) {
	if cycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	s.cycleAcc += int64(cycles) * 44100
	n := s.cycleAcc / 33868800
	s.cycleAcc -= n * 33868800
	for i := int64(0); i < n; i++ {
		s.genSample(cd)
	}
}

// AudioBuffer drains the pending interleaved stereo
// output samples (left, right pairs).
func (s *SPU) AudioBuffer() []int16 {
	if len(s.audio) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := s.audio
	s.audio = nil
	return out
}

// genSample generates one 44100 Hz output sample.
func (s *SPU) genSample(cd func() (int16, int16)) {
	var cdL, cdR int16
	if cd != nil {
		cdL, cdR = cd()
	}
	s.runNoise()

	enabled := s.spucnt&0x8000 != 0
	unmuted := s.spucnt&0x4000 != 0

	var dryL, dryR, sendL, sendR int32
	var capV1, capV3 int32
	var prevOutx int32
	for n := 0; n < numVoices; n++ {
		outx := s.voiceSample(n, prevOutx)
		prevOutx = outx
		if n == 1 {
			capV1 = outx
		}
		if n == 3 {
			capV3 = outx
		}
		if !enabled || !unmuted {
			continue
		}
		v := &s.voices[n]
		cL := mul15(outx, v.curVolL)
		cR := mul15(outx, v.curVolR)
		dryL += cL
		dryR += cR
		if s.eon>>uint(n)&1 != 0 {
			sendL += cL
			sendR += cR
		}
	}
	// CD input, at CD volume, when enabled in
	// SPUCNT (bit 0). CD is not affected by the SPU
	// enable or mute bits per the document.
	if s.spucnt&0x1 != 0 {
		cL := mul15(int32(cdL), s.cdVolL)
		cR := mul15(int32(cdR), s.cdVolR)
		dryL += cL
		dryR += cR
		if s.spucnt&0x4 != 0 {
			sendL += cL
			sendR += cR
		}
	}
	// Reverb at half rate, on every second sample.
	if !s.revPhase {
		s.runReverb(sendL, sendR)
	}
	s.revPhase = !s.revPhase
	wetL, wetR := int32(0), int32(0)
	if unmuted {
		wetL, wetR = s.revOutL, s.revOutR
	}
	// Main volume sweeps.
	if s.mainSweepOnL {
		s.mainCurL = runSweep(s.mainCurL, &s.mainSweepCntL, s.mainRawL)
	}
	if s.mainSweepOnR {
		s.mainCurR = runSweep(s.mainCurR, &s.mainSweepCntR, s.mainRawR)
	}
	outL := clamp16(mul15(dryL+wetL, s.mainCurL))
	outR := clamp16(mul15(dryR+wetR, s.mainCurR))

	// Capture buffers: CD left at 00000h, CD right
	// at 00400h, voice 1 at 00800h, voice 3 at
	// 00C00h, position from the output sample
	// counter modulo 512 samples.
	pos := uint32(s.totalSamples&0x1FF) * 2
	put := func(base uint32, v int32) {
		u := uint16(int16(clamp16(v)))
		s.RAM[base+pos] = byte(u)
		s.RAM[base+pos+1] = byte(u >> 8)
	}
	put(0x000, int32(cdL))
	put(0x400, int32(cdR))
	put(0x800, capV1)
	put(0xC00, capV3)

	s.audio = append(s.audio, int16(outL), int16(outR))
	s.totalSamples++
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/regs.go ====================

package spu

// Register interface over 1F801C00h..1F801DFFh.
// The DAx block follows the psx-spx documented map:
// 1F801DA2h ESA, 1F801DA4h IRQA, 1F801DA6h TSA,
// 1F801DA8h DATA, 1F801DAAh ATTR/SPUCNT, 1F801DACh
// RAM transfer control, 1F801DAEh STATX.

// ReadReg reads size bytes at an absolute SPU
// address. Size 2 is one halfword access, size 4 is
// two halfword accesses (low at addr, high at
// addr+2). Size 1 and out of window addresses are
// not claimed.
func (s *SPU) ReadReg(addr uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	if size == 2 {
		v, ok := s.readHalf(addr)
		return uint32(v), ok
	}
	if size == 4 {
		lo, ok1 := s.readHalf(addr)
		hi, ok2 := s.readHalf(addr + 2)
		if !ok1 || !ok2 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint32(lo) | uint32(hi)<<16, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// WriteReg writes size bytes at an absolute SPU
// address, with the same size rules as ReadReg.
func (s *SPU) WriteReg(addr uint32, size int, v uint32) bool {
	if size == 2 {
		return s.writeHalf(addr, uint16(v))
	}
	if size == 4 {
		ok1 := s.writeHalf(addr, uint16(v))
		ok2 := s.writeHalf(addr+2, uint16(v>>16))
		return ok1 && ok2
	}
	return false
}

func inWindow(addr uint32) bool {
	return addr >= regBase && addr <= regTop && addr&1 == 0
}

func (s *SPU) readHalf(addr uint32) (uint16, bool) {
	if !inWindow(addr) {
		return 0, false
	}
	switch addr {
	case 0x1F801DA4: // IRQA
		return s.irqAddr, true
	case 0x1F801DA6: // TSA (stored value; does not increment)
		return s.AddrReg, true
	case 0x1F801DA8: // DATA port
		return s.ReadData(), true
	case 0x1F801DAE:
		return s.statusReg(), true
	case 0x1F801D9C:
		return uint16(s.endx), true
	case 0x1F801D9E:
		return uint16(s.endx >> 16), true
	case 0x1F801DB8:
		return uint16(s.mainCurL), true
	case 0x1F801DBA:
		return uint16(s.mainCurR), true
	}
	if addr >= 0x1F801C00 && addr < 0x1F801D80 {
		n := int(addr-0x1F801C00) >> 4
		v := &s.voices[n]
		switch (addr - 0x1F801C00) & 0xF {
		case 0x0:
			return v.volLRaw, true
		case 0x2:
			return v.volRRaw, true
		case 0x4:
			return v.pitch, true
		case 0x6:
			return v.ssa, true
		case 0x8:
			return v.adsrLo, true
		case 0xA:
			return v.adsrHi, true
		case 0xC:
			return uint16(v.envLevel), true
		case 0xE:
			return v.lsax, true
		}
	}
	return s.shadow[(addr-regBase)/2], true
}

func (s *SPU) statusReg() uint16 {
	st := uint16(s.spucnt & 0x3F)
	if s.spucnt&0x20 != 0 {
		st |= 0x80 // DMA request, mirrors SPUCNT bit 5 per the document
	}
	if s.irqFlag {
		st |= 0x40
	}
	if (s.totalSamples & 0x100) != 0 {
		st |= 0x800 // writing to second half of capture buffers
	}
	return st
}

func (s *SPU) writeHalf(addr uint32, val uint16) bool {
	if !inWindow(addr) {
		return false
	}
	s.shadow[(addr-regBase)/2] = val
	switch {
	case addr >= 0x1F801C00 && addr < 0x1F801D80:
		n := int(addr-0x1F801C00) >> 4
		v := &s.voices[n]
		switch (addr - 0x1F801C00) & 0xF {
		case 0x0:
			v.volLRaw = val
			v.curVolL, v.sweepOnL = applyVolumeWrite(v.curVolL, val)
		case 0x2:
			v.volRRaw = val
			v.curVolR, v.sweepOnR = applyVolumeWrite(v.curVolR, val)
		case 0x4:
			v.pitch = val
		case 0x6:
			v.ssa = val
		case 0x8:
			v.adsrLo = val
		case 0xA:
			v.adsrHi = val
		case 0xC:
			v.envLevel = int32(int16(val))
		case 0xE:
			v.lsax = val
			v.repeatWritten = true
		}
		return true
	case addr >= 0x1F801DC0 && addr <= 0x1F801DFE:
		s.rev[(addr-0x1F801DC0)/2] = val
		return true
	}
	switch addr {
	case 0x1F801D80:
		s.mainRawL = val
		s.mainCurL, s.mainSweepOnL = applyMainVolumeWrite(s.mainCurL, val)
	case 0x1F801D82:
		s.mainRawR = val
		s.mainCurR, s.mainSweepOnR = applyMainVolumeWrite(s.mainCurR, val)
	case 0x1F801D84:
		s.evolL = int32(int16(val))
	case 0x1F801D86:
		s.evolR = int32(int16(val))
	case 0x1F801D88:
		for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
			if val>>uint(i)&1 != 0 {
				s.keyOn(i)
			}
		}
	case 0x1F801D8A:
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if val>>uint(i)&1 != 0 {
				s.keyOn(16 + i)
			}
		}
	case 0x1F801D8C:
		for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
			if val>>uint(i)&1 != 0 {
				s.keyOff(i)
			}
		}
	case 0x1F801D8E:
		for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
			if val>>uint(i)&1 != 0 {
				s.keyOff(16 + i)
			}
		}
	case 0x1F801D90:
		s.pmon = (s.pmon & 0xFFFF0000) | uint32(val)
	case 0x1F801D92:
		s.pmon = (s.pmon & 0xFFFF) | uint32(val)<<16
		s.pmon &= 0xFFFFFF
	case 0x1F801D94:
		s.non = (s.non & 0xFFFF0000) | uint32(val)
	case 0x1F801D96:
		s.non = (s.non & 0xFFFF) | uint32(val)<<16
		s.non &= 0xFFFFFF
	case 0x1F801D98:
		s.eon = (s.eon & 0xFFFF0000) | uint32(val)
	case 0x1F801D9A:
		s.eon = (s.eon & 0xFFFF) | uint32(val)<<16
		s.eon &= 0xFFFFFF
	case 0x1F801DA2:
		s.esa = val
		s.revBuf = uint32(val) << 3
	case 0x1F801DA4: // IRQA
		s.irqAddr = val
	case 0x1F801DA6: // TSA
		s.SetAddress(val)
	case 0x1F801DA8: // DATA port
		s.WriteData(val)
	case 0x1F801DAA:
		s.spucnt = val
		if val&0x40 == 0 {
			s.irqFlag = false // acknowledge / disable
		}
	case 0x1F801DAC:
		s.ramCtrl = val
	case 0x1F801DB0:
		s.cdVolL = int32(int16(val))
	case 0x1F801DB2:
		s.cdVolR = int32(int16(val))
	case 0x1F801DB4:
		s.extVolL = int32(int16(val))
	case 0x1F801DB6:
		s.extVolR = int32(int16(val))
	}
	return true
}

// applyVolumeWrite handles a voice volume register
// write: direct mode (bit15=0) sets the current
// volume immediately, sweep mode (bit15=1) keeps the
// current volume and starts sweeping from it.
func applyVolumeWrite(cur int32, raw uint16) (int32, bool) {
	if raw&0x8000 == 0 {
		v := int32(raw & 0x7FFF)
		if v >= 0x4000 {
			v -= 0x8000
		}
		return v * 2, false
	}
	return cur, true
}

// applyMainVolumeWrite is the main volume variant:
// the main registers carry a plain signed 16-bit
// volume in direct mode (0x7FFF is full, 0x3FFF is
// half), and a sweep parameter set in sweep mode.
func applyMainVolumeWrite(cur int32, raw uint16) (int32, bool) {
	if raw&0x8000 == 0 {
		return int32(int16(raw)), false
	}
	return cur, true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/reverb.go ====================

package spu

// The reverb network follows the documented formula
// in the psx-spx SPU chapter: input gains, same side
// and different side reflections, four comb filters,
// two all pass filters, output gains, all in signed
// 16-bit sound RAM with multiplications divided by
// 8000h, running at half the output rate. Register
// indices into s.rev, in document order starting at
// 1F801DC0h.
const (
	rvDAPF1 = iota
	rvDAPF2
	rvVIIR
	rvVCOMB1
	rvVCOMB2
	rvVCOMB3
	rvVCOMB4
	rvVWALL
	rvVAPF1
	rvVAPF2
	rvMLSAME
	rvMRSAME
	rvMLCOMB1
	rvMRCOMB1
	rvMLCOMB2
	rvMRCOMB2
	rvDLSAME
	rvDRSAME
	rvMLDIFF
	rvMRDIFF
	rvMLCOMB3
	rvMRCOMB3
	rvMLCOMB4
	rvMRCOMB4
	rvDLDIFF
	rvDRDIFF
	rvMLAPF1
	rvMRAPF1
	rvMLAPF2
	rvMRAPF2
	rvVLIN
	rvVRIN
)

func (s *SPU) revReg(i int) int32 {
	return int32(int16(s.rev[i]))
}

// revAddr resolves a reverb address register (in
// 8-byte units, relative to the current buffer
// address) to a byte address in sound RAM, wrapped
// inside the work area ESA..7FFFEh.
func (s *SPU) revAddr(rel int32) uint32 {
	esa := int32(s.esa) << 3
	size := int32(RAMSize) - esa
	if size <= 0 {
		return uint32(esa) & (RAMSize - 1)
	}
	a := int32(s.revBuf) + rel
	a = (a-esa)%size + esa
	if a < esa {
		a += size
	}
	return uint32(a)
}

func (s *SPU) revRead(rel int32) int32 {
	a := s.revAddr(rel)
	return int32(int16(uint16(s.RAM[a]) | uint16(s.RAM[a+1])<<8))
}

func (s *SPU) revWrite(rel int32, v int32, store bool) {
	if !store {
		return
	}
	a := s.revAddr(rel)
	v = clamp16(v)
	s.RAM[a] = byte(uint16(int16(v)))
	s.RAM[a+1] = byte(uint16(int16(v)) >> 8)
}

// runReverb performs one 22050 Hz reverb cycle with
// the documented equations. inL/inR are the mixed
// reverb send of the current output sample. When the
// reverb master enable (SPUCNT bit 7) is clear, the
// documented behaviour is that buffer writes become
// reads, so nothing is stored but output is still
// produced from the buffer contents; the SAME/DIFF
// stages are skipped in that case per the document.
func (s *SPU) runReverb(inL, inR int32) {
	enabled := s.spucnt&0x80 != 0
	store := enabled
	lin := mul15(s.revReg(rvVLIN), inL)
	rin := mul15(s.revReg(rvVRIN), inR)
	if enabled {
		// Same side reflections.
		mL := int32(s.rev[rvMLSAME]) << 3
		mR := int32(s.rev[rvMRSAME]) << 3
		prevL := s.revRead(mL - 2)
		prevR := s.revRead(mR - 2)
		nL := mul15(s.revReg(rvVIIR), lin+mul15(s.revReg(rvVWALL), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvDLSAME])<<3))-prevL) + prevL
		nR := mul15(s.revReg(rvVIIR), rin+mul15(s.revReg(rvVWALL), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvDRSAME])<<3))-prevR) + prevR
		s.revWrite(mL, nL, store)
		s.revWrite(mR, nR, store)
		// Different side reflections.
		mLd := int32(s.rev[rvMLDIFF]) << 3
		mRd := int32(s.rev[rvMRDIFF]) << 3
		prevLd := s.revRead(mLd - 2)
		prevRd := s.revRead(mRd - 2)
		nLd := mul15(s.revReg(rvVIIR), lin+mul15(s.revReg(rvVWALL), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvDRDIFF])<<3))-prevLd) + prevLd
		nRd := mul15(s.revReg(rvVIIR), rin+mul15(s.revReg(rvVWALL), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvDLDIFF])<<3))-prevRd) + prevRd
		s.revWrite(mLd, nLd, store)
		s.revWrite(mRd, nRd, store)
	}
	// Early echo: comb filters.
	lout := mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB1), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMLCOMB1])<<3)) +
		mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB2), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMLCOMB2])<<3)) +
		mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB3), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMLCOMB3])<<3)) +
		mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB4), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMLCOMB4])<<3))
	rout := mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB1), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMRCOMB1])<<3)) +
		mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB2), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMRCOMB2])<<3)) +
		mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB3), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMRCOMB3])<<3)) +
		mul15(s.revReg(rvVCOMB4), s.revRead(int32(s.rev[rvMRCOMB4])<<3))
	// Late reverb APF1 and APF2.
	lout = s.runAPF(lout, int32(s.rev[rvMLAPF1])<<3, int32(s.rev[rvDAPF1])<<3, s.revReg(rvVAPF1), store)
	rout = s.runAPF(rout, int32(s.rev[rvMRAPF1])<<3, int32(s.rev[rvDAPF1])<<3, s.revReg(rvVAPF1), store)
	lout = s.runAPF(lout, int32(s.rev[rvMLAPF2])<<3, int32(s.rev[rvDAPF2])<<3, s.revReg(rvVAPF2), store)
	rout = s.runAPF(rout, int32(s.rev[rvMRAPF2])<<3, int32(s.rev[rvDAPF2])<<3, s.revReg(rvVAPF2), store)
	s.revOutL = mul15(lout, s.evolL)
	s.revOutR = mul15(rout, s.evolR)
	// Advance the buffer address.
	nb := (s.revBuf + 2) & 0x7FFFE
	if nb < uint32(s.esa)<<3 {
		nb = uint32(s.esa) << 3
	}
	s.revBuf = nb
}

// runAPF performs one documented all pass stage:
// out = in - v*[addr-disp]; [addr] = out;
// out = out*v + [addr-disp] (the old value).
func (s *SPU) runAPF(in, addr, disp, v int32, store bool) int32 {
	delayed := s.revRead(addr - disp)
	out := in - mul15(v, delayed)
	s.revWrite(addr, out, store)
	return mul15(out, v) + delayed
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/spu.go ====================

// Package spu is the PlayStation SPU: 512 KB sound
// RAM with its transfer port (from PS1-2), plus the
// full chip per the psx-spx SPU chapter: 24 ADPCM
// voices with pitch modulation, gaussian
// interpolation, ADSR envelopes and volume sweeps,
// the noise generator, KON/KOFF/ENDX flags, the
// sample address interrupt, CD mixing, the Schroeder
// reverb network, and the capture buffers in the
// first 4 KB of sound RAM.
//
// Register interface: ReadReg/WriteReg cover absolute
// addresses 1F801C00h..1F801DFFh as halfwords; a
// 32-bit access is two halfword accesses, low first.
// The DAx block follows the psx-spx documented map
// (SPU Memory Access, SPU Interrupt, SPU Control and
// SPU Reverb Registers sections): 1F801DA0h unused,
// 1F801DA2h ESA (reverb work area start), 1F801DA4h
// IRQA (IRQ address), 1F801DA6h TSA (transfer start
// address), 1F801DA8h DATA (data port FIFO),
// 1F801DAAh ATTR/SPUCNT, 1F801DACh RAM transfer
// control, 1F801DAEh STATX. ESA, IRQA and TSA are
// all in 8-byte units. The transfer address unit
// changed in PS1-3 from the 4-byte units used in
// PS1-2 to the documented 8-byte units, so
// SetAddress(v) loads the internal byte address
// v<<3 (AddrReg still stores the raw written value).
//
// KON delay simplification: the document implies key
// on takes effect on a later SPU cycle but gives no
// exact count here; this core uses a fixed delay of
// konDelaySamples output samples between KON and the
// first envelope step.
//
// Capture simplification: the four capture buffers
// are written every output sample at the position
// given by the output sample counter modulo 512
// samples (voice 1 and voice 3 post-envelope mono,
// CD left and right pre-volume), exactly per the
// documented memory map. Capture IRQ and reverb IRQ
// sources are not modelled; only voice reads of the
// IRQ address raise the interrupt.
//
// Reverb simplification: the documented 39-tap
// resampling FIR on the reverb path is replaced by
// plain decimation (the reverb runs at half rate on
// every second output sample, as documented); the
// feedback equations themselves are the documented
// ones. Repeat address written-flag: a software
// write to the repeat address register sets a flag
// that stops a Loop Start header from overwriting
// it until the next KON; the document does not name
// this flag, this is the behaviour other references
// describe for the register.
//
// Serialized layout: sound RAM first, then the
// original 8-byte transfer tail (AddrReg and the
// internal byte address), then appended blocks:
// register shadow, global scalars, reverb registers,
// per-voice state, and the pending audio buffer. The
// RAM plus old tail prefix is unchanged from PS1-2.
package spu

// RAMSize is the sound RAM size in bytes.
const RAMSize = 512 * 1024

const numVoices = 24

// konDelaySamples is the fixed key on delay, in
// output samples (see package comment).
const konDelaySamples = 5

const (
	regBase = 0x1F801C00
	regTop  = 0x1F801DFF
)

// envelope phases
const (
	phaseOff = iota
	phaseAttack
	phaseDecay
	phaseSustain
	phaseRelease
)

// adpcmFilterF0 and adpcmFilterF1 are the published
// SPU/XA ADPCM predictor coefficients from the
// psx-spx CDROM XA chapter (the SPU chapter defers
// to it): f0 = 0,60,115,98,122 and f1 = 0,0,-52,-55,-60
// for filters 0..4.
var adpcmFilterF0 = [5]int32{0, 60, 115, 98, 122}
var adpcmFilterF1 = [5]int32{0, 0, -52, -55, -60}

// voice holds one channel of the SPU.
type voice struct {
	// registers
	volLRaw, volRRaw uint16
	pitch            uint16
	ssa              uint16
	adsrLo, adsrHi   uint16
	lsax             uint16

	// volume sweep state
	curVolL, curVolR     int32
	sweepCntL, sweepCntR int32
	sweepOnL, sweepOnR   bool

	// envelope state
	envLevel   int32
	envCounter int32
	phase      int
	konDelay   int
	active     bool

	// ADPCM runtime
	addr          uint32 // current block byte address
	pitchCounter  uint32
	decOld        int32
	decOlder      int32
	block         [28]int16
	blockFlags    uint8
	blockLoaded   bool
	pos           int
	hist          [4]int32 // oldest, older, old, new
	outx          int32    // latest post-envelope sample
	repeatWritten bool
}

// SPU is the whole sound chip.
type SPU struct {
	RAM     [RAMSize]byte
	AddrReg uint16 // last value written to TSA at 0x1F801DA6
	addr    uint32 // current byte address inside RAM

	// OnIRQ is called on the 0-to-1 transition of
	// the SPU interrupt condition.
	OnIRQ func()

	voices [numVoices]voice
	shadow [256]uint16 // register readback shadow, index = (addr-regBase)/2

	pmon uint32 // pitch modulation mask, bits per voice
	non  uint32 // noise mask
	eon  uint32 // reverb send mask
	endx uint32 // end reached mask

	spucnt  uint16
	ramCtrl uint16
	esa     uint16 // reverb work area start, in 8-byte units
	irqAddr uint16 // IRQ address, in 8-byte units

	cdVolL, cdVolR   int32
	extVolL, extVolR int32
	evolL, evolR     int32

	mainRawL, mainRawR uint16
	mainCurL, mainCurR int32
	mainSweepCntL      int32
	mainSweepCntR      int32
	mainSweepOnL       bool
	mainSweepOnR       bool

	rev              [32]uint16
	revBuf           uint32 // current reverb buffer byte address
	revOutL, revOutR int32
	revPhase         bool // false: run reverb on next sample

	noiseLevel int32
	noiseTimer int32

	irqFlag bool

	cycleAcc     int64 // CPU cycles not yet turned into samples
	totalSamples uint64
	audio        []int16
}

// New returns an SPU in reset state.
func New() *SPU { return &SPU{} }

// Reset clears sound RAM, all registers and runtime
// state. The OnIRQ callback is preserved.
func (s *SPU) Reset() {
	cb := s.OnIRQ
	*s = SPU{}
	s.OnIRQ = cb
}

// SetAddress writes the transfer address register
// (TSA, 1F801DA6h) and loads the internal byte
// address. The register value is in 8-byte units per
// the psx-spx SPU Memory Access section (PS1-2 used
// 4-byte units; changed in PS1-3).
func (s *SPU) SetAddress(v uint16) {
	s.AddrReg = v
	s.addr = (uint32(v) << 3) & (RAMSize - 1)
}

// Address returns the current byte address.
func (s *SPU) Address() uint32 { return s.addr }

// ReadData reads the halfword at the transfer
// address and advances it.
func (s *SPU) ReadData() uint16 {
	v := uint16(s.RAM[s.addr]) | uint16(s.RAM[s.addr+1])<<8
	s.addr = (s.addr + 2) & (RAMSize - 1)
	return v
}

// WriteData writes a halfword at the transfer
// address and advances it.
func (s *SPU) WriteData(v uint16) {
	s.RAM[s.addr] = byte(v)
	s.RAM[s.addr+1] = byte(v >> 8)
	s.addr = (s.addr + 2) & (RAMSize - 1)
}

// ReadWord performs a DMA word read (two halfword
// port accesses, low first).
func (s *SPU) ReadWord() uint32 {
	lo := s.ReadData()
	hi := s.ReadData()
	return uint32(lo) | uint32(hi)<<16
}

// WriteWord performs a DMA word write.
func (s *SPU) WriteWord(w uint32) {
	s.WriteData(uint16(w))
	s.WriteData(uint16(w >> 16))
}

// VoiceEnvelope returns the current envelope level of
// a voice, on the 0..7FFFh scale.
func (s *SPU) VoiceEnvelope(voice int) int {
	if voice < 0 || voice >= numVoices {
		return 0
	}
	l := s.voices[voice].envLevel
	if l < 0 {
		l = 0
	}
	if l > 0x7FFF {
		l = 0x7FFF
	}
	return int(l)
}

// VoicePlaying reports whether a voice is keyed on
// and has not finished its release (or an end+mute
// block).
func (s *SPU) VoicePlaying(voice int) bool {
	if voice < 0 || voice >= numVoices {
		return false
	}
	v := &s.voices[voice]
	return v.active && v.phase != phaseOff
}

func clamp16(v int32) int32 {
	if v > 0x7FFF {
		return 0x7FFF
	}
	if v < -0x8000 {
		return -0x8000
	}
	return v
}

// mul15 multiplies two signed values with the
// documented division by 8000h.
func mul15(a, b int32) int32 {
	return int32((int64(a) * int64(b)) >> 15)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/spu_test.go ====================

package spu

import (
	"math"
	"testing"
)

func TestTransferPortSequential(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	// The transfer address is in documented 8-byte
	// units (psx-spx SPU Memory Access: TSA is the
	// address in the sound buffer divided by eight),
	// so SetAddress(0x0010) means byte address 0x80.
	// PS1-2 used 4-byte units here; corrected in
	// PS1-3.
	s.SetAddress(0x0010) // byte address 0x80
	s.WriteData(0xBEEF)
	s.WriteData(0xCAFE)
	if s.Address() != 0x84 {
		t.Fatalf("address = 0x%X, want 0x84", s.Address())
	}
	s.SetAddress(0x0010)
	if v := s.ReadData(); v != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("read = 0x%04X, want 0xBEEF", v)
	}
	if v := s.ReadData(); v != 0xCAFE {
		t.Errorf("read = 0x%04X, want 0xCAFE", v)
	}
	// The bytes landed in RAM at the register-derived
	// address.
	if s.RAM[0x80] != 0xEF || s.RAM[0x81] != 0xBE {
		t.Errorf("RAM bytes = %02X %02X, want EF BE", s.RAM[0x80], s.RAM[0x81])
	}
}

// TestTransferPortRegisters drives the transfer port
// through the documented register addresses: TSA at
// 1F801DA6h, DATA at 1F801DA8h, IRQA at 1F801DA4h.
func TestTransferPortRegisters(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DA6, 0x0010) // TSA: byte address 0x80
	if got := s.Address(); got != 0x80 {
		t.Fatalf("Address after TSA write = 0x%X, want 0x80", got)
	}
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DA8, 0xBEEF) // DATA port
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DA8, 0xCAFE)
	if got := s.Address(); got != 0x84 {
		t.Fatalf("Address after DATA writes = 0x%X, want 0x84", got)
	}
	if s.RAM[0x80] != 0xEF || s.RAM[0x81] != 0xBE || s.RAM[0x82] != 0xFE || s.RAM[0x83] != 0xCA {
		t.Errorf("RAM at 0x80 = %02X %02X %02X %02X, want EF BE FE CA",
			s.RAM[0x80], s.RAM[0x81], s.RAM[0x82], s.RAM[0x83])
	}
	// TSA readback returns the stored register value
	// (it does not increment during transfers).
	if v := rd(t, s, 0x1F801DA6); v != 0x0010 {
		t.Errorf("TSA readback = 0x%04X, want 0x0010", v)
	}
	if v := rd(t, s, 0x1F801DA4); v != 0 {
		t.Errorf("IRQA readback before write = 0x%04X, want 0", v)
	}
	// Read back through TSA + DATA at the documented
	// addresses.
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DA6, 0x0010)
	if v := rd(t, s, 0x1F801DA8); v != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("DATA read = 0x%04X, want 0xBEEF", v)
	}
	if v := rd(t, s, 0x1F801DA8); v != 0xCAFE {
		t.Errorf("DATA read = 0x%04X, want 0xCAFE", v)
	}
	// IRQA at DA4 stores its own value and must not
	// disturb the transfer address.
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DA4, 0x0200)
	if v := rd(t, s, 0x1F801DA4); v != 0x0200 {
		t.Errorf("IRQA readback = 0x%04X, want 0x0200", v)
	}
	if got := s.Address(); got != 0x84 {
		t.Errorf("Address after IRQA write = 0x%X, want 0x84 (unchanged)", got)
	}
}

func TestWordAccess(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	s.SetAddress(0)
	s.WriteWord(0xDEADBEEF)
	s.SetAddress(0)
	if v := s.ReadWord(); v != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("word = 0x%08X, want 0xDEADBEEF", v)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	s.SetAddress(0x0100)
	s.WriteWord(0x11223344)
	b := s.Serialize()
	if len(b) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state = %d, want %d", len(b), StateSize)
	}
	s2 := New()
	s2.Deserialize(b)
	if s2.RAM != s.RAM || s2.Address() != s.Address() || s2.AddrReg != s.AddrReg {
		t.Errorf("SPU state diverged after round trip")
	}
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// PS1-3 full chip gates. All fixtures are synthetic:
// ADPCM data is built here with an encoder that uses
// the documented decoder math (filter pairs
// 0/60/115/98/122 and 0/0/-52/-55/-60 from the
// psx-spx XA chapter, sample = (nibble<<12)>>shift +
// (old*f0 + older*f1 + 32)/64, clamped to int16).
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

var encF0 = [5]int32{0, 60, 115, 98, 122}
var encF1 = [5]int32{0, 0, -52, -55, -60}

func encRecon(nib, shift, f0, f1, old, older int32) int32 {
	s := (nib<<12)>>uint(shift) + (old*f0+older*f1+32)/64
	if s > 0x7FFF {
		s = 0x7FFF
	}
	if s < -0x8000 {
		s = -0x8000
	}
	return s
}

// encodeBlock encodes 28 PCM samples into one
// 16-byte ADPCM block, greedily choosing the
// filter/shift/nibbles that minimize squared error
// under the documented decoder.
func encodeBlock(pcm []int16, old, older int32) ([16]byte, int32, int32) {
	var best [16]byte
	bestErr := int64(-1)
	var bestOld, bestOlder int32
	for filter := 0; filter <= 4; filter++ {
		for shift := 0; shift <= 12; shift++ {
			var blk [16]byte
			blk[0] = byte(filter<<4 | shift)
			o, oo := old, older
			err := int64(0)
			var nibs [28]int32
			for i := 0; i < 28; i++ {
				target := int32(pcm[i])
				bn, be := int32(0), int64(-1)
				for nib := int32(-8); nib <= 7; nib++ {
					r := encRecon(nib, int32(shift), encF0[filter], encF1[filter], o, oo)
					d := int64(r - target)
					if be < 0 || d*d < be {
						be, bn = d*d, nib
					}
				}
				r := encRecon(bn, int32(shift), encF0[filter], encF1[filter], o, oo)
				oo, o = o, r
				err += be
				nibs[i] = bn
			}
			if bestErr < 0 || err < bestErr {
				bestErr, bestOld, bestOlder = err, o, oo
				copy(best[:], blk[:])
				for i := 0; i < 28; i++ {
					u := uint8(nibs[i] & 0xF)
					if i&1 == 0 {
						best[2+i/2] |= u
					} else {
						best[2+i/2] |= u << 4
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return best, bestOld, bestOlder
}

// encodeStream encodes pcm (a multiple of 28) into
// consecutive blocks, carrying decoder state.
func encodeStream(pcm []int16) []byte {
	var out []byte
	var old, older int32
	for i := 0; i+28 <= len(pcm); i += 28 {
		blk, o, oo := encodeBlock(pcm[i:i+28], old, older)
		old, older = o, oo
		out = append(out, blk[:]...)
	}
	return out
}

// encodeLoop encodes pcm as a seamlessly looping
// stream: several encoding passes around the loop so
// the decoder state at the end matches the start,
// then loop start/end flags are set on the first and
// last blocks.
func encodeLoop(pcm []int16) []byte {
	var out []byte
	var old, older int32
	for pass := 0; pass < 3; pass++ {
		out = nil
		for i := 0; i+28 <= len(pcm); i += 28 {
			blk, o, oo := encodeBlock(pcm[i:i+28], old, older)
			old, older = o, oo
			out = append(out, blk[:]...)
		}
	}
	out[1] |= 4           // loop start on first block
	out[len(out)-15] |= 3 // loop end + repeat on last block
	return out
}

func sinePCM(n, periods int, amp float64) []int16 {
	out := make([]int16, n)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = int16(amp * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(periods)*float64(i)/float64(n)))
	}
	return out
}

func wr(t *testing.T, s *SPU, addr uint32, v uint16) {
	t.Helper()
	if !s.WriteReg(addr, 2, uint32(v)) {
		t.Fatalf("WriteReg(%#x) not claimed", addr)
	}
}

func rd(t *testing.T, s *SPU, addr uint32) uint16 {
	t.Helper()
	v, ok := s.ReadReg(addr, 2)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("ReadReg(%#x) not claimed", addr)
	}
	return uint16(v)
}

// adsrFastHold: attack shift 0 step 0 (full in a few
// samples), decay shift 0, sustain level 15, sustain
// shift 31 step 3 (all-ones rate, never steps),
// release shift 31.
const adsrFastHoldLo = 0x000F
const adsrFastHoldHi = 0x1FDF

func setupChip(t *testing.T, mainVol uint16) *SPU {
	t.Helper()
	s := New()
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D80, mainVol)
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D82, mainVol)
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DB0, 0) // CD volume 0
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DB2, 0)
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DAA, 0xC000) // SPU on, unmuted
	return s
}

func setupVoice(t *testing.T, s *SPU, n int, addrBytes uint32, pitch, adsrLo, adsrHi uint16) {
	t.Helper()
	base := uint32(0x1F801C00 + n*0x10)
	wr(t, s, base+0, 0x3FFF) // VOLL full (direct mode)
	wr(t, s, base+2, 0x3FFF) // VOLR full
	wr(t, s, base+4, pitch)
	wr(t, s, base+6, uint16(addrBytes/8))
	wr(t, s, base+8, adsrLo)
	wr(t, s, base+0xA, adsrHi)
}

func keyOn(t *testing.T, s *SPU, mask uint32) {
	t.Helper()
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D88, uint16(mask))
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D8A, uint16(mask>>16))
}

func advanceSamples(s *SPU, n int) {
	s.Advance(n*768, nil)
}

func leftChannel(s *SPU) []int16 {
	buf := s.AudioBuffer()
	out := make([]int16, len(buf)/2)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = buf[2*i]
	}
	return out
}

func posCrossings(x []int16) int {
	c := 0
	for i := 1; i < len(x); i++ {
		if x[i-1] < 0 && x[i] >= 0 {
			c++
		}
	}
	return c
}

func maxAbs(x []int16) int {
	m := 0
	for _, v := range x {
		if int(v) < 0 {
			if -int(v) > m {
				m = -int(v)
			}
		} else if int(v) > m {
			m = int(v)
		}
	}
	return m
}

func TestADPCMTone440(t *testing.T) {
	// 2800 samples, 28 periods: 441 Hz at 44100 Hz.
	data := encodeLoop(sinePCM(2800, 28, 12000))
	measure := func(pitch uint16) float64 {
		s := setupChip(t, 0x7FFF)
		copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], data)
		setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, pitch, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
		keyOn(t, s, 1)
		advanceSamples(s, 44100)
		l := leftChannel(s)
		win := l[len(l)-22050:]
		f := float64(posCrossings(win)) / 0.5
		t.Logf("pitch %#x: crossings %d in 0.5s = %.1f Hz, peak %d",
			pitch, posCrossings(win), f, maxAbs(win))
		return f
	}
	f1 := measure(0x1000)
	if f1 < 430 || f1 > 450 {
		t.Errorf("440 Hz gate: measured %.1f Hz, want 440 +/- 10", f1)
	}
