	f2 := measure(0x2000)
	if f2 < 860 || f2 > 900 {
		t.Errorf("pitch double gate: measured %.1f Hz, want %.1f +/- 20", f2, 2*f1)
	}
}

func TestADSREnvelopeCheckpoints(t *testing.T) {
	// Attack shift 11 step 0: step = 7 per sample,
	// one step per sample. KON delay is 5 samples.
	// Release shift 11: step = -8 per sample.
	s := setupChip(t, 0x7FFF)
	data := encodeLoop(sinePCM(2800, 28, 8000))
	copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], data)
	adsrLo := uint16(11<<10 | 0<<4 | 0xF) // attack shift 11, decay 0, sustain level 15
	adsrHi := uint16(31<<8 | 3<<6 | 11)   // sustain never steps, release shift 11
	setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, adsrLo, adsrHi)
	keyOn(t, s, 1)
	advanceSamples(s, 5+100)
	if e := s.VoiceEnvelope(0); e < 700-28 || e > 700+28 {
		t.Errorf("attack checkpoint 100 steps: envelope %d, want 700 +/- 28", e)
	}
	advanceSamples(s, 900)
	if e := s.VoiceEnvelope(0); e < 7000-28 || e > 7000+28 {
		t.Errorf("attack checkpoint 1000 steps: envelope %d, want 7000 +/- 28", e)
	}
	advanceSamples(s, 4000)
	if e := s.VoiceEnvelope(0); e < 0x7F00 {
		t.Errorf("attack end: envelope %d, want near 0x7FFF", e)
	}
	// KOFF: release at -8 per sample.
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D8C, 1)
	advanceSamples(s, 500)
	if e := s.VoiceEnvelope(0); e < 28767-64 || e > 28767+64 {
		t.Errorf("release checkpoint 500 steps: envelope %d, want 28767 +/- 64", e)
	}
	advanceSamples(s, 5000)
	if e := s.VoiceEnvelope(0); e != 0 {
		t.Errorf("release end: envelope %d, want 0", e)
	}
	if s.VoicePlaying(0) {
		t.Errorf("voice still playing after full release")
	}
	s.AudioBuffer() // drain everything generated so far
	advanceSamples(s, 200)
	if m := maxAbs(leftChannel(s)); m != 0 {
		t.Errorf("output after release not silent: peak %d", m)
	}
}

func TestLoopENDXAndIRQ(t *testing.T) {
	s := setupChip(t, 0x7FFF)
	data := encodeStream(sinePCM(56, 2, 8000))
	data[1] |= 4    // loop start, block 0
	data[16+1] |= 3 // loop end + repeat, block 1
	copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], data)
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DA4, 0x1000/8) // IRQA (at DA4) = loop start
	irqs := 0
	s.OnIRQ = func() { irqs++ }
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DAA, 0xC040) // enable IRQ in SPUCNT
	setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
	keyOn(t, s, 1)
	advanceSamples(s, 2000)
	if !s.VoicePlaying(0) {
		t.Errorf("looping voice stopped")
	}
	if e := rd(t, s, 0x1F801D9C); e&1 == 0 {
		t.Errorf("ENDX bit 0 not set, ENDX0 = %#x", e)
	}
	if irqs < 1 {
		t.Errorf("OnIRQ did not fire for loop address, count %d", irqs)
	}
	t.Logf("loop: ENDX set, IRQ count %d, envelope %d", irqs, s.VoiceEnvelope(0))
}

func TestPitchModulationFM(t *testing.T) {
	run := func(pmon bool) []int16 {
		s := setupChip(t, 0x7FFF)
		constData := make([]int16, 2800)
		for i := range constData {
			constData[i] = 16000
		}
		copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], encodeLoop(constData))
		copy(s.RAM[0x3000:], encodeLoop(sinePCM(2800, 28, 12000)))
		// Voice 0: constant modulator, silent volumes.
		setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
		wr(t, s, 0x1F801C00, 0)
		wr(t, s, 0x1F801C02, 0)
		// Voice 1: carrier tone.
		setupVoice(t, s, 1, 0x3000, 0x1000, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
		if pmon {
			wr(t, s, 0x1F801D90, 0x2) // PMON voice 1
		}
		keyOn(t, s, 0x3)
		advanceSamples(s, 44100)
		l := leftChannel(s)
		return l[len(l)-22050:]
	}
	base := run(false)
	fm := run(true)
	diff := 0
	for i := range base {
		if base[i] != fm[i] {
			diff++
		}
	}
	bc, fc := posCrossings(base), posCrossings(fm)
	t.Logf("FM: base crossings %d, FM crossings %d, differing samples %d/%d",
		bc, fc, diff, len(base))
	if float64(diff)/float64(len(base)) < 0.5 {
		t.Errorf("FM output barely differs from baseline: %d/%d", diff, len(base))
	}
	// The modulator sits near +16000, so the pitch
	// factor is about (16000+32768)/32768 = 1.49 and
	// the crossing count must RISE by roughly that.
	if float64(fc) < float64(bc)*1.25 {
		t.Errorf("FM crossings did not rise as expected: base %d, FM %d", bc, fc)
	}
}

func TestReverbEcho(t *testing.T) {
	s := setupChip(t, 0x7FFF)
	// Impulse block: silence except sample 12 at
	// 24000 (after the 5-sample KON delay and the
	// fast attack), flags = end+mute.
	pcm := make([]int16, 28)
	pcm[12] = 24000
	imp := encodeStream(pcm)
	imp[1] |= 1
	copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], imp)
	// Silent loop block at 0x1010 (loop start + end +
	// repeat, zero data) as the jump target.
	s.RAM[0x1010+1] = 7
	setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801C0E, 0x1010/8) // LSAX = silent block
	// Reverb configuration: ESA at byte 0x20000,
	// SAME writes input (vIIR full, vWALL 0), COMB1
	// reads it back (mLSAME 0x100, mLCOMB1 0x0F0:
	// 16 address units * 8 bytes / 2 bytes per tick
	// = 64 ticks at 22050 Hz = 128 output samples),
	// APF stages pass through with dAPF 0 and full
	// gains on untouched addresses.
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DA2, 0x20000/8)
	rev := [32]uint16{
		0, 0, 0x7FFF, 0x7FFF, 0, 0, 0, 0, // dAPF1 dAPF2 vIIR vCOMB1..4 vWALL
		0x7FFF, 0x7FFF, 0x100, 0x100, 0x0F0, 0x0F0, 1, 1, // vAPF1 vAPF2 mLSAME mRSAME combs
		0, 0, 0x100, 0x100, 1, 1, 1, 1, // dLSAME dRSAME diffs combs
		0, 0, 0x80, 0x80, 0x90, 0x90, 0x7FFF, 0x7FFF, // dDIFF mLAPF mRAPF vLIN vRIN
	}
	for i, v := range rev {
		wr(t, s, uint32(0x1F801DC0+i*2), v)
	}
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D84, 0x7FFF) // EVOLL
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D86, 0x7FFF) // EVOLR
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D98, 1)      // EON voice 0
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DAA, 0xC080) // SPUCNT: on, unmuted, reverb master on
	keyOn(t, s, 1)
	advanceSamples(s, 400)
	l := leftChannel(s)
	direct := maxAbs(l[0:40])
	gap := maxAbs(l[40:110])
	echoPeak, echoAt := 0, 0
	for i := 115; i < 190 && i < len(l); i++ {
		if a := maxAbs(l[i : i+1]); a > echoPeak {
			echoPeak, echoAt = a, i
		}
	}
	t.Logf("reverb: direct peak %d, gap peak %d, echo peak %d at sample %d (expect ~140)",
		direct, gap, echoPeak, echoAt)
	if direct < 5000 {
		t.Errorf("direct impulse too small: %d", direct)
	}
	if gap > 800 {
		t.Errorf("output not quiet between direct and echo: %d", gap)
	}
	if echoPeak < 1500 {
		t.Errorf("no reverb echo energy in window 115..190: peak %d", echoPeak)
	}
}

func TestNoiseVoice(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D80, 0x7FFF)
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D82, 0x7FFF)
	// SPUCNT: on, unmuted, noise shift 15, step 3.
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801DAA, 0xFF00)
	copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], encodeStream(make([]int16, 28)))
	setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
	wr(t, s, 0x1F801D94, 1) // NON voice 0
	keyOn(t, s, 1)
	advanceSamples(s, 4410)
	l := leftChannel(s)[100:]
	distinct := map[int16]bool{}
	nonzero := 0
	for _, v := range l {
		distinct[v] = true
		if v != 0 {
			nonzero++
		}
	}
	t.Logf("noise: distinct values %d, peak %d, nonzero %d/%d",
		len(distinct), maxAbs(l), nonzero, len(l))
	if len(distinct) < 500 {
		t.Errorf("noise output not varying: %d distinct values", len(distinct))
	}
	if maxAbs(l) < 5000 {
		t.Errorf("noise output too quiet: peak %d", maxAbs(l))
	}
}

func TestMasterVolumeRatio(t *testing.T) {
	peak := func(mainVol uint16) int {
		s := setupChip(t, mainVol)
		copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], encodeLoop(sinePCM(2800, 28, 12000)))
		setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
		keyOn(t, s, 1)
		advanceSamples(s, 44100)
		l := leftChannel(s)
		return maxAbs(l[len(l)-22050:])
	}
	full, half := peak(0x7FFF), peak(0x3FFF)
	ratio := float64(half) / float64(full)
	t.Logf("master volume: full peak %d, half peak %d, ratio %.3f", full, half, ratio)
	if ratio < 0.44 || ratio > 0.56 {
		t.Errorf("master volume ratio %.3f, want 0.5 within tolerance", ratio)
	}
}

func TestStateDeterminismMidPlayback(t *testing.T) {
	s := setupChip(t, 0x7FFF)
	copy(s.RAM[0x1000:], encodeLoop(sinePCM(2800, 28, 12000)))
	setupVoice(t, s, 0, 0x1000, 0x1000, adsrFastHoldLo, adsrFastHoldHi)
	keyOn(t, s, 1)
	s.Advance(100000, nil) // not a multiple of 768: tests the remainder
	s.AudioBuffer()        // drain
	b := s.Serialize()
	if len(b) != StateSize {
		t.Fatalf("state = %d, want %d", len(b), StateSize)
	}
	s2 := New()
	s2.Deserialize(b)
	const cycles = 4096 * 768
	s.Advance(cycles, nil)
	s2.Advance(cycles, nil)
	a, c := s.AudioBuffer(), s2.AudioBuffer()
	if len(a) != 8192 || len(c) != 8192 {
		t.Fatalf("sample counts %d and %d, want 8192 each", len(a), len(c))
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != c[i] {
			t.Fatalf("sample %d diverged after restore: %d vs %d", i, a[i], c[i])
		}
	}
	if s.VoiceEnvelope(0) != s2.VoiceEnvelope(0) {
		t.Errorf("envelope diverged after restore")
	}
	t.Logf("state determinism: 4096 samples bit-identical, StateSize %d", StateSize)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/state.go ====================

package spu

import "encoding/binary"

// Serialized layout (see the package comment):
// RAM, the original 8-byte transfer tail, then the
// register shadow (512 bytes), a global scalar block
// (192 bytes, 48 little endian uint32 slots), the
// reverb registers (64 bytes), per-voice blocks
// (voiceStateSize bytes each) and the pending audio
// buffer (audioStateCap int16 values; its length is
// global slot 31).

const (
	shadowStateSize = 512
	globalStateSize = 192
	revStateSize    = 64
	voiceStateSize  = 138
	audioStateCap   = 16384
	extraStateSize  = shadowStateSize + globalStateSize + revStateSize +
		numVoices*voiceStateSize + audioStateCap*2
)

// StateSize is the serialized size: the sound RAM,
// the transfer address state, and all chip state
// added in PS1-3.
const StateSize = RAMSize + 8 + extraStateSize

// Serialize writes the SPU state.
func (s *SPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, StateSize)
	copy(out, s.RAM[:])
	off := RAMSize
	out[off] = byte(s.AddrReg)
	out[off+1] = byte(s.AddrReg >> 8)
	out[off+2] = byte(s.addr)
	out[off+3] = byte(s.addr >> 8)
	out[off+4] = byte(s.addr >> 16)
	off += 8
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[off+i*2:], s.shadow[i])
	}
	off += shadowStateSize
	g := func(slot int, v uint32) {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off+slot*4:], v)
	}
	audioLen := len(s.audio)
	if audioLen > audioStateCap {
		audioLen = audioStateCap
	}
	g(0, s.pmon)
	g(1, s.non)
	g(2, s.eon)
	g(3, s.endx)
	g(4, uint32(s.esa))
	g(5, uint32(s.irqAddr))
	g(6, uint32(s.spucnt))
	g(7, uint32(s.ramCtrl))
	g(8, uint32(s.cdVolL))
	g(9, uint32(s.cdVolR))
	g(10, uint32(s.extVolL))
	g(11, uint32(s.extVolR))
	g(12, uint32(s.evolL))
	g(13, uint32(s.evolR))
	g(14, uint32(s.mainCurL))
	g(15, uint32(s.mainCurR))
	g(16, uint32(s.mainSweepCntL))
	g(17, uint32(s.mainSweepCntR))
	if s.mainSweepOnL {
		g(18, 1)
	}
	if s.mainSweepOnR {
		g(18, binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(out[off+18*4:])|2)
	}
	g(19, s.revBuf)
	g(20, uint32(s.revOutL))
	g(21, uint32(s.revOutR))
	if s.revPhase {
		g(22, 1)
	}
	g(23, uint32(s.noiseLevel))
	g(24, uint32(s.noiseTimer))
	g(25, uint32(s.cycleAcc))
	g(26, uint32(s.totalSamples))
	g(27, uint32(s.totalSamples>>32))
	if s.irqFlag {
		g(28, 1)
	}
	g(29, uint32(s.mainRawL))
	g(30, uint32(s.mainRawR))
	g(31, uint32(audioLen))
	off += globalStateSize
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[off+i*2:], s.rev[i])
	}
	off += revStateSize
	for n := 0; n < numVoices; n++ {
		off = s.serializeVoice(out, off, n)
	}
	for i := 0; i < audioLen; i++ {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[off+i*2:], uint16(s.audio[i]))
	}
	return out
}

func (s *SPU) serializeVoice(out []byte, off int, n int) int {
	v := &s.voices[n]
	u16 := func(vv uint16) {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[off:], vv)
		off += 2
	}
	u32 := func(vv uint32) {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off:], vv)
		off += 4
	}
	u16(v.volLRaw)
	u16(v.volRRaw)
	u16(v.pitch)
	u16(v.ssa)
	u16(v.adsrLo)
	u16(v.adsrHi)
	u16(v.lsax)
	u32(uint32(v.curVolL))
	u32(uint32(v.curVolR))
	u32(uint32(v.sweepCntL))
	u32(uint32(v.sweepCntR))
	u32(uint32(v.envLevel))
	u32(uint32(v.envCounter))
	flags := uint32(v.phase)
	if v.sweepOnL {
		flags |= 0x10
	}
	if v.sweepOnR {
		flags |= 0x20
	}
	if v.active {
		flags |= 0x40
	}
	if v.repeatWritten {
		flags |= 0x80
	}
	if v.blockLoaded {
		flags |= 0x100
	}
	u32(flags)
	u32(uint32(v.konDelay))
	u32(v.addr)
	u32(v.pitchCounter)
	u32(uint32(v.decOld))
	u32(uint32(v.decOlder))
	u32(uint32(v.pos))
	u32(uint32(v.blockFlags))
	for i := 0; i < 28; i++ {
		u16(uint16(v.block[i]))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		u16(uint16(int16(v.hist[i])))
	}
	u32(uint32(v.outx))
	return off
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
// The input length must match StateSize exactly; any
// other length is ignored.
func (s *SPU) Deserialize(in []byte) {
	if len(in) != StateSize {
		return
	}
	copy(s.RAM[:], in[:RAMSize])
	off := RAMSize
	s.AddrReg = uint16(in[off]) | uint16(in[off+1])<<8
	s.addr = uint32(in[off+2]) | uint32(in[off+3])<<8 | uint32(in[off+4])<<16
	s.addr &= RAMSize - 1
	off += 8
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		s.shadow[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[off+i*2:])
	}
	off += shadowStateSize
	g := func(slot int) uint32 {
		return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off+slot*4:])
	}
	s.pmon = g(0)
	s.non = g(1)
	s.eon = g(2)
	s.endx = g(3)
	s.esa = uint16(g(4))
	s.irqAddr = uint16(g(5))
	s.spucnt = uint16(g(6))
	s.ramCtrl = uint16(g(7))
	s.cdVolL = int32(g(8))
	s.cdVolR = int32(g(9))
	s.extVolL = int32(g(10))
	s.extVolR = int32(g(11))
	s.evolL = int32(g(12))
	s.evolR = int32(g(13))
	s.mainCurL = int32(g(14))
	s.mainCurR = int32(g(15))
	s.mainSweepCntL = int32(g(16))
	s.mainSweepCntR = int32(g(17))
	s.mainSweepOnL = g(18)&1 != 0
	s.mainSweepOnR = g(18)&2 != 0
	s.revBuf = g(19)
	s.revOutL = int32(g(20))
	s.revOutR = int32(g(21))
	s.revPhase = g(22) != 0
	s.noiseLevel = int32(g(23))
	s.noiseTimer = int32(g(24))
	s.cycleAcc = int64(g(25))
	s.totalSamples = uint64(g(26)) | uint64(g(27))<<32
	s.irqFlag = g(28) != 0
	s.mainRawL = uint16(g(29))
	s.mainRawR = uint16(g(30))
	audioLen := int(g(31))
	if audioLen > audioStateCap {
		audioLen = audioStateCap
	}
	off += globalStateSize
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		s.rev[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[off+i*2:])
	}
	off += revStateSize
	for n := 0; n < numVoices; n++ {
		off = s.deserializeVoice(in, off, n)
	}
	s.audio = make([]int16, audioLen)
	for i := 0; i < audioLen; i++ {
		s.audio[i] = int16(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[off+i*2:]))
	}
}

func (s *SPU) deserializeVoice(in []byte, off int, n int) int {
	v := &s.voices[n]
	u16 := func() uint16 {
		vv := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[off:])
		off += 2
		return vv
	}
	u32 := func() uint32 {
		vv := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(in[off:])
		off += 4
		return vv
	}
	v.volLRaw = u16()
	v.volRRaw = u16()
	v.pitch = u16()
	v.ssa = u16()
	v.adsrLo = u16()
	v.adsrHi = u16()
	v.lsax = u16()
	v.curVolL = int32(u32())
	v.curVolR = int32(u32())
	v.sweepCntL = int32(u32())
	v.sweepCntR = int32(u32())
	v.envLevel = int32(u32())
	v.envCounter = int32(u32())
	flags := u32()
	v.phase = int(flags & 0xF)
	v.sweepOnL = flags&0x10 != 0
	v.sweepOnR = flags&0x20 != 0
	v.active = flags&0x40 != 0
	v.repeatWritten = flags&0x80 != 0
	v.blockLoaded = flags&0x100 != 0
	v.konDelay = int(int32(u32()))
	v.addr = u32()
	v.pitchCounter = u32()
	v.decOld = int32(u32())
	v.decOlder = int32(u32())
	v.pos = int(u32())
	v.blockFlags = uint8(u32())
	for i := 0; i < 28; i++ {
		v.block[i] = int16(u16())
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		v.hist[i] = int32(int16(u16()))
	}
	v.outx = int32(u32())
	return off
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/spu/voice.go ====================

package spu

// keyOn starts a voice: envelope to attack at level
// zero, current address to the start address, decode
// and interpolation state cleared, ENDX cleared.
func (s *SPU) keyOn(n int) {
	v := &s.voices[n]
	v.active = true
	v.phase = phaseAttack
	v.envLevel = 0
	v.envCounter = 0
	v.konDelay = konDelaySamples
	v.addr = uint32(v.ssa) << 3 & (RAMSize - 1)
	v.pitchCounter = 0
	v.decOld, v.decOlder = 0, 0
	v.hist = [4]int32{}
	v.outx = 0
	v.repeatWritten = false
	v.blockLoaded = false
	v.pos = 0
	s.endx &^= 1 << uint(n)
	s.loadBlock(v, n)
}

// keyOff starts the release phase.
func (s *SPU) keyOff(n int) {
	v := &s.voices[n]
	if v.active && v.phase != phaseOff {
		v.phase = phaseRelease
		v.envCounter = 0
		v.konDelay = 0
	}
}

// loadBlock decodes the 16-byte ADPCM block at the
// voice current address into 28 samples. Loop Start
// headers copy the address to the repeat register
// unless software wrote it (the written flag). A
// block read from the IRQ address raises the
// interrupt.
func (s *SPU) loadBlock(v *voice, n int) {
	base := v.addr & (RAMSize - 1)
	hdr := s.RAM[base]
	flags := s.RAM[(base+1)&(RAMSize-1)]
	if flags&4 != 0 && !v.repeatWritten {
		v.lsax = uint16(base >> 3)
	}
	if uint32(s.irqAddr)<<3 == base {
		s.raiseIRQ()
	}
	shift := uint(hdr & 0xF)
	filter := int(hdr>>4) & 7
	var f0, f1 int32
	if filter <= 4 {
		f0, f1 = adpcmFilterF0[filter], adpcmFilterF1[filter]
	}
	old, older := v.decOld, v.decOlder
	for i := 0; i < 28; i++ {
		b := s.RAM[(base+2+uint32(i/2))&(RAMSize-1)]
		var nib int32
		if i&1 == 0 {
			nib = int32(b & 0xF)
		} else {
			nib = int32(b >> 4)
		}
		if nib >= 8 {
			nib -= 16
		}
		sample := (nib<<12)>>shift + (old*f0+older*f1+32)/64
		sample = clamp16(sample)
		v.block[i] = int16(sample)
		older, old = old, sample
	}
	v.decOld, v.decOlder = old, older
	v.blockFlags = flags
	v.blockLoaded = true
	v.pos = 0
}

// nextSample returns the next decoded ADPCM sample,
// moving to the next block (or the repeat address at
// a loop end) when the current block is exhausted.
func (s *SPU) nextSample(v *voice, n int) int32 {
	if !v.blockLoaded {
		s.loadBlock(v, n)
	}
	out := int32(v.block[v.pos])
	v.pos++
	if v.pos >= 28 {
		flags := v.blockFlags
		next := (v.addr + 16) & (RAMSize - 1)
		if flags&1 != 0 {
			s.endx |= 1 << uint(n)
			if flags&2 == 0 {
				// End+Mute: jump, force release,
				// envelope to zero.
				v.envLevel = 0
				v.phase = phaseOff
				v.active = false
			}
			v.addr = uint32(v.lsax) << 3 & (RAMSize - 1)
		} else {
			v.addr = next
		}
		s.loadBlock(v, n)
	}
	return out
}

// voiceSample advances one voice by one output
// sample and returns its post-envelope sample
// (OUTX). prevOutx is the previous voice OUTX of
// this same output cycle, for pitch modulation.
func (s *SPU) voiceSample(n int, prevOutx int32) int32 {
	v := &s.voices[n]
	if !v.active && v.phase == phaseOff {
		v.outx = 0
		return 0
	}
	// Envelope.
	if v.konDelay > 0 {
		v.konDelay--
	} else if v.phase != phaseOff {
		v.runEnvelope()
	}
	// Volume sweeps.
	if v.sweepOnL {
		v.curVolL = runSweep(v.curVolL, &v.sweepCntL, v.volLRaw)
	}
	if v.sweepOnR {
		v.curVolR = runSweep(v.curVolR, &v.sweepCntR, v.volRRaw)
	}
	// Pitch step, with the documented pitch
	// modulation formula and clamp.
	step := int32(v.pitch)
	if n > 0 && s.pmon>>uint(n)&1 != 0 {
		factor := prevOutx + 0x8000 // 0..FFFFh
		step = int32(int16(v.pitch))
		step = (step * factor) >> 15
		step &= 0xFFFF
	}
	if step > 0x3FFF {
		step = 0x4000
	}
	if step < 0 {
		step = 0
	}
	v.pitchCounter += uint32(step)
	for v.pitchCounter >= 0x1000 {
		v.pitchCounter -= 0x1000
		v.hist[0] = v.hist[1]
		v.hist[1] = v.hist[2]
		v.hist[2] = v.hist[3]
		v.hist[3] = s.nextSample(v, n)
	}
	var raw int32
	if s.non>>uint(n)&1 != 0 {
		raw = int32(int16(s.noiseLevel))
	} else {
		i := int((v.pitchCounter >> 4) & 0xFF)
		raw = (gaussTable[0xFF-i]*v.hist[0])>>15 +
			(gaussTable[0x1FF-i]*v.hist[1])>>15 +
			(gaussTable[0x100+i]*v.hist[2])>>15 +
			(gaussTable[i]*v.hist[3])>>15
		raw = clamp16(raw)
	}
	v.outx = (raw * v.envLevel) >> 15
	return v.outx
}

// runNoise advances the shared noise generator by
// one output sample, per the documented algorithm:
// the timer decrements by the step (4..7), the
// parity bit is the XOR of level bits 15, 12, 11 and
// 10 plus 1, and when the timer goes negative the
// level shifts and the timer reloads (twice if
// needed) with 20000h shifted by the noise shift.
func (s *SPU) runNoise() {
	shift := uint(s.spucnt>>10) & 0xF
	step := int32(s.spucnt>>8)&3 + 4
	s.noiseTimer -= step
	parity := ((s.noiseLevel >> 15) & 1) ^ ((s.noiseLevel >> 12) & 1) ^
		((s.noiseLevel >> 11) & 1) ^ ((s.noiseLevel >> 10) & 1) ^ 1
	if s.noiseTimer < 0 {
		s.noiseLevel = (s.noiseLevel << 1) | parity
		s.noiseTimer += int32(0x20000) >> shift
		if s.noiseTimer < 0 {
			s.noiseTimer += int32(0x20000) >> shift
		}
	}
	s.noiseLevel = int32(int16(s.noiseLevel))
}

// raiseIRQ latches the interrupt flag and calls
// OnIRQ on the 0-to-1 transition, when the SPU is
// enabled and the IRQ is enabled in SPUCNT.
func (s *SPU) raiseIRQ() {
	if s.spucnt&0x8000 == 0 || s.spucnt&0x40 == 0 {
		return
	}
	if s.irqFlag {
		return
	}
	s.irqFlag = true
	if s.OnIRQ != nil {
		s.OnIRQ()
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/bios.go ====================

package system

// BIOS HLE for PS1-3. There is no Sony BIOS in this
// core and there never will be; instead the machine
// intercepts execution at the three documented call
// vectors (0xA0, 0xB0, 0xC0, function number in $t1,
// arguments in $a0 to $a3, return value in $v0) and at
// the syscall instruction for the critical-section
// functions, and services a tight, documented subset
// in Go. Everything outside the subset is recorded
// (see UnimplementedBIOSCalls) and returns to the
// caller with $v0 = 0xFFFFFFFF, the documented error
// value shape; it never crashes the machine.
//
// Function numbers follow the psx-spx BIOS function
// summary exactly. That corrects three numbers the
// PS1-3 brief carried from secondary sources:
//
//   - TestEvent is B(0Bh), EnableEvent is B(0Ch) and
//     DisableEvent is B(0Dh) (not C0 functions).
//   - EnterCriticalSection and ExitCriticalSection
//     are SYS(01h) and SYS(02h), reached through the
//     syscall instruction with the function number in
//     $a0 (not C(08h)/C(09h), which are SysInitMemory
//     and SysInitKernelVariables).
//   - The root-counter BIOS API is B(02h) init_timer,
//     B(03h) get_timer, B(04h) enable_timer_irq,
//     B(05h) disable_timer_irq, B(06h) restart_timer
//     and C(0Ah) ChangeClearRCnt. The brief also
//     required the SDK-level names SetRCnt, GetRCnt
//     and ResetRCnt; those are implemented at the
//     C(19h)/C(1Ah)/C(1Bh) slots the brief named,
//     with the mode word applied in the hardware
//     timer mode-register layout, because psx-spx
//     does not define a different encoding for them.
//
// The implemented set:
//
//	A(44h) FlushCache            no-op (no cache model)
//	A(48h) SendGP1Command        write GP1, $v0 kept
//	A(49h) GPU_cw                write GP0, $v0 = 0
//	A(4Ah) GPU_cwp               copy words to GP0
//	A(4Dh) GetGPUStatus          $v0 = GPUSTAT
//	B(02h) init_timer            per the doc formula
//	B(03h) get_timer             counter readback
//	B(04h) enable_timer_irq      I_MASK bits per doc
//	B(05h) disable_timer_irq     I_MASK bits per doc
//	B(06h) restart_timer         counter = 0
//	B(07h) DeliverEvent          class/spec delivery
//	B(08h) OpenEvent             handle 0xF1000000+n
//	B(09h) CloseEvent            always returns 1
//	B(0Ah) WaitEvent             non-blocking, see below
//	B(0Bh) TestEvent             1 when ready, consumes
//	B(0Ch) EnableEvent           always returns 1
//	B(0Dh) DisableEvent          always returns 1
//	B(12h) InitPAD2              buffers recorded
//	B(13h) StartPAD2             pad fill on VBlank on
//	B(14h) StopPAD2              pad fill off
//	B(20h) UnDeliverEvent        ready back to busy
//	C(04h) get_free_EvCB_slot    first free event slot
//	C(08h) SysInitMemory         no-op in the HLE
//	C(09h) SysInitKernelVariables no-op in the HLE
//	C(0Ah) ChangeClearRCnt       flag store, old value
//	C(19h) SetRCnt               SDK alias, see above
//	C(1Ah) GetRCnt               SDK alias, see above
//	C(1Bh) ResetRCnt             SDK alias, see above
//	SYS(01h) EnterCriticalSection
//	SYS(02h) ExitCriticalSection
//
// Event model: the event table holds 16 slots (the
// documented default EvCB count). An event opens
// disabled, exactly as documented. Delivery happens
// when the matching hardware interrupt latches in
// I_STAT (the kernel's default IRQ handler events:
// class 0xF0000001+irq, spec 0x1000, plus the root
// counter classes 0xF2000000+n with spec 0x0002), or
// when guest code calls DeliverEvent. Delivery
// follows the I_STAT latch, not the I_MASK bit: on
// hardware a masked interrupt never reaches the
// kernel handler, so this is a stated simplification.
// Mode 0x2000 events are marked ready for
// TestEvent/WaitEvent. Mode 0x1000 callback events
// are queued and invoked at the next Step boundary
// through a synthetic call frame (registers saved,
// $ra set to a return trampoline in the kernel
// reserved area at 0x00000E10, interrupts masked in
// SR during the callback); when the callback returns
// to the trampoline the saved context is restored.
// WaitEvent cannot hang in an HLE that advances time
// only while the CPU executes, so it returns the
// current readiness (1 and consumes when ready, 0
// otherwise) instead of blocking; that is the one
// deliberate semantic deviation in this file.
//
// Critical sections: EnterCriticalSection saves the
// SR interrupt-enable bit on first entry and clears
// SR.IEc (the documented effect is masking the
// kernel's interrupt sources; clearing IEc is the
// CPU-visible equivalent here); a nesting counter is
// kept. ExitCriticalSection restores IEc when the
// counter returns to zero.

// BIOSCall records one call the HLE did not
// implement: the table (A, B, C or S for syscall),
// the function number from $t1 (or $a0 for syscalls),
// and the caller PC (the return address).
type BIOSCall struct {
	Table byte
	Func  uint32
	PC    uint32
}

// Event classes and specs used by the delivery
// model (psx-spx BIOS Event Summary).
const (
	evClassVBlank  uint32 = 0xF0000001
	evClassGPU     uint32 = 0xF0000002
	evClassCDROM   uint32 = 0xF0000003
	evClassDMA     uint32 = 0xF0000004
	evClassTMR0    uint32 = 0xF0000005
	evClassTMR1    uint32 = 0xF0000006 // TMR2 shares this class (documented quirk)
	evClassPAD     uint32 = 0xF0000008
	evClassSPU     uint32 = 0xF0000009
	evSpecIRQ      uint32 = 0x1000
	evSpecRCnt     uint32 = 0x0002
	evClassRCnt0   uint32 = 0xF2000000
	evClassRCntVB  uint32 = 0xF2000003
	evModeCallback uint32 = 0x1000
	evModeReady    uint32 = 0x2000
	evHandleBase   uint32 = 0xF1000000
)

// Event slot states.
const (
	evUnused = iota
	evDisabled
	evBusy  // enabled, not delivered
	evReady // enabled, delivered (mode 0x2000)
)

const (
	evSlots     = 16
	cbQueueSize = 16
	cbTrampAddr = 0x00000E10 // kernel reserved area, return trampoline
	biosCycles  = 16         // flat charge per vector call
)

// biosEvent is one EvCB slot.
type biosEvent struct {
	class, spec uint32
	mode        uint32
	fn          uint32
	state       uint8
}

// biosState is the whole HLE BIOS runtime state. It
// is serialized as part of the machine state.
type biosState struct {
	events [evSlots]biosEvent

	critCount int
	critIEc   bool // SR.IEc saved by the outermost EnterCriticalSection

	clearRCnt [4]uint32 // ChangeClearRCnt flags (t = 0..2, 3 = vblank)

	padBuf1, padBuf2 uint32
	padStarted       bool

	// Callback invocation machinery.
	cbActive bool
	cbSaved  cbContext
	cbQueue  [cbQueueSize]uint32
	cbHead   int // index of the oldest queued callback
	cbCount  int

	unimpl     []BIOSCall
	unimplSeen int // total unimplemented calls, including dropped ones
}

// cbContext is the CPU context saved while a
// mode 0x1000 event callback runs.
type cbContext struct {
	regs   [32]uint32
	hi, lo uint32
	pc     uint32
	nextPC uint32
	sr     uint32
}

func (b *biosState) reset() {
	*b = biosState{}
}

// UnimplementedBIOSCalls returns a copy of the
// recorded unimplemented-call log (bounded; the
// total count is UnimplementedBIOSCallCount).
func (m *Machine) UnimplementedBIOSCalls() []BIOSCall {
	out := make([]BIOSCall, len(m.bios.unimpl))
	copy(out, m.bios.unimpl)
	return out
}

// UnimplementedBIOSCallCount returns how many
// unimplemented BIOS calls have been intercepted in
// total (the log itself is capped).
func (m *Machine) UnimplementedBIOSCallCount() int { return m.bios.unimplSeen }

func (m *Machine) logUnimplemented(table byte, fn, pc uint32) {
	m.bios.unimplSeen++
	if len(m.bios.unimpl) < 256 {
		m.bios.unimpl = append(m.bios.unimpl, BIOSCall{Table: table, Func: fn, PC: pc})
	}
}

// deliverEvent marks or invokes every enabled event
// matching class and spec.
func (m *Machine) deliverEvent(class, spec uint32) {
	for i := range m.bios.events {
		ev := &m.bios.events[i]
		if ev.state != evBusy && ev.state != evReady {
			continue
		}
		if ev.class != class || ev.spec != spec {
			continue
		}
		switch ev.mode {
		case evModeReady:
			ev.state = evReady
		case evModeCallback:
			if ev.fn != 0 {
				m.enqueueCallback(ev.fn)
			}
		}
	}
}

func (m *Machine) enqueueCallback(fn uint32) {
	if m.bios.cbCount >= cbQueueSize {
		return // drop: stated bound, the queue is drained every Step
	}
	tail := (m.bios.cbHead + m.bios.cbCount) % cbQueueSize
	m.bios.cbQueue[tail] = fn
	m.bios.cbCount++
}

// interruptPending mirrors the CPU's own check (SR
// interrupt enable and any unmasked Cause IP bit) so
// the Step interception never preempts an interrupt
// the CPU is about to take.
func (m *Machine) interruptPending() bool {
	return m.CPU.SR&1 != 0 && m.CPU.SR&m.CPU.Cause&0xFF00 != 0
}

// stepBIOS checks the interception points before a
// normal CPU step. It returns (cycles, true) when it
// handled the step itself.
func (m *Machine) stepBIOS() (int, bool) {
	pc := m.CPU.PC
	// Callback return trampoline.
	if pc == cbTrampAddr && m.bios.cbActive {
		s := m.bios.cbSaved
		m.CPU.Regs = s.regs
		m.CPU.HI, m.CPU.LO = s.hi, s.lo
		m.CPU.PC, m.CPU.NextPC = s.pc, s.nextPC
		m.CPU.SR = s.sr
		m.bios.cbActive = false
		m.advance(4)
		return 4, true
	}
	if m.interruptPending() {
		return 0, false
	}
	// Vector calls. The vectors live in low RAM, so
	// the KUSEG address and its KSEG0/KSEG1 mirrors
	// are the same physical slot; match on the
	// physical address.
	if phys := pc & 0x1FFFFFFF; phys == 0xA0 || phys == 0xB0 || phys == 0xC0 {
		m.CPU.CommitPendingLoad()
		m.execBIOSCall(phys)
		ret := m.CPU.Regs[31]
		m.CPU.PC = ret
		m.CPU.NextPC = ret + 4
		m.advance(biosCycles)
		return biosCycles, true
	}
	// Syscall interception for the critical-section
	// functions (other syscalls take the normal
	// exception path, as they did before the HLE).
	if w := m.Bus.Read32(pc); w&0xFC00003F == 0x0000000C {
		fn := m.CPU.Regs[4]
		if fn == 1 || fn == 2 {
			m.CPU.CommitPendingLoad()
			if fn == 1 {
				m.enterCritical()
			} else {
				m.exitCritical()
			}
			m.CPU.PC = m.CPU.NextPC
			m.CPU.NextPC += 4
			m.advance(4)
			return 4, true
		}
		m.logUnimplemented('S', fn, pc)
		return 0, false
	}
	// Start a queued event callback.
	if !m.bios.cbActive && m.bios.cbCount > 0 {
		fn := m.bios.cbQueue[m.bios.cbHead]
		m.bios.cbHead = (m.bios.cbHead + 1) % cbQueueSize
		m.bios.cbCount--
		s := &m.bios.cbSaved
		s.regs = m.CPU.Regs
		s.hi, s.lo = m.CPU.HI, m.CPU.LO
		s.pc, s.nextPC = m.CPU.PC, m.CPU.NextPC
		s.sr = m.CPU.SR
		m.bios.cbActive = true
		m.CPU.Regs[31] = cbTrampAddr
		m.CPU.SR &^= 1 // callbacks run with interrupts masked
		m.CPU.PC = fn
		m.CPU.NextPC = fn + 4
		c := m.CPU.Step()
		m.advance(c)
		return c, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

func (m *Machine) enterCritical() {
	if m.bios.critCount == 0 {
		m.bios.critIEc = m.CPU.SR&1 != 0
		m.CPU.SR &^= 1
	}
	m.bios.critCount++
}

func (m *Machine) exitCritical() {
	if m.bios.critCount > 0 {
		m.bios.critCount--
		if m.bios.critCount == 0 && m.bios.critIEc {
			m.CPU.SR |= 1
		}
	}
}

// execBIOSCall services one vector call. On entry the
// PC is the vector; $t1 holds the function number,
// $a0 to $a3 the arguments, $ra the return address.
func (m *Machine) execBIOSCall(vector uint32) {
	fn := m.CPU.Regs[9]
	a0, a1, a2, a3 := m.CPU.Regs[4], m.CPU.Regs[5], m.CPU.Regs[6], m.CPU.Regs[7]
	ret := m.CPU.Regs[31]
	setV := func(v uint32) { m.CPU.Regs[2] = v }

	switch vector {
	case 0xA0:
		switch fn {
		case 0x44: // FlushCache: no cache model, nothing to flush
		case 0x48: // SendGP1Command
			m.GPU.WriteGP1(a0)
		case 0x49: // GPU_cw
			m.writeGP0(a0)
			setV(0)
		case 0x4A: // GPU_cwp
			for i := uint32(0); i < a1; i++ {
				m.writeGP0(m.Bus.Read32(a0 + i*4))
			}
			setV(0)
		case 0x4D: // GetGPUStatus
			setV(m.GPU.Status())
		default:
			m.logUnimplemented('A', fn, ret)
			setV(0xFFFFFFFF)
		}
	case 0xB0:
		switch fn {
		case 0x02: // init_timer(t, reload, flags)
			setV(m.biosInitTimer(a0, a1, a2))
		case 0x03: // get_timer(t)
			if a0 < 3 {
				setV(uint32(m.Timers.T[a0].Counter))
			} else {
				setV(0)
			}
		case 0x04: // enable_timer_irq(t)
			switch {
			case a0 < 3:
				m.imask |= 1 << uint(IRQTMR0+int(a0))
				m.updateIRQ()
				setV(1)
			case a0 == 3:
				m.imask |= 1 << IRQVBlank
				m.updateIRQ()
				setV(0) // documented: enable returns 0 for t=3
			default:
				setV(0)
			}
		case 0x05: // disable_timer_irq(t)
			switch {
			case a0 < 3:
				m.imask &^= 1 << uint(IRQTMR0+int(a0))
			case a0 == 3:
				m.imask &^= 1 << IRQVBlank
			}
			m.updateIRQ()
			setV(1) // documented: disable always returns 1
		case 0x06: // restart_timer(t)
			if a0 < 3 {
				m.Timers.WriteCounter(int(a0), 0)
				setV(1)
			} else {
				setV(0)
			}
		case 0x07: // DeliverEvent(class, spec)
			m.deliverEvent(a0, a1)
		case 0x08: // OpenEvent(class, spec, mode, func)
			setV(m.biosOpenEvent(a0, a1, a2, a3))
		case 0x09: // CloseEvent(event)
			if ev := m.biosEventByHandle(a0); ev != nil {
				*ev = biosEvent{}
			}
			setV(1)
		case 0x0A: // WaitEvent(event): non-blocking, see file comment
			setV(m.biosTestEvent(a0, true))
		case 0x0B: // TestEvent(event)
			setV(m.biosTestEvent(a0, false))
		case 0x0C: // EnableEvent(event)
			if ev := m.biosEventByHandle(a0); ev != nil && ev.state == evDisabled {
				ev.state = evBusy
			}
			setV(1)
		case 0x0D: // DisableEvent(event)
			if ev := m.biosEventByHandle(a0); ev != nil && ev.state != evUnused {
				ev.state = evDisabled
			}
			setV(1)
		case 0x12: // InitPAD2(buf1, siz1, buf2, siz2)
			m.bios.padBuf1, m.bios.padBuf2 = a0, a2
			m.bios.padStarted = false
			zero := func(addr, size uint32) {
				if size > 0x100 {
					size = 0x100
				}
				for i := uint32(0); i < size; i++ {
					m.Bus.Write8(addr+i, 0)
				}
			}
			zero(a0, a1)
			zero(a2, a3)
		case 0x13: // StartPAD2
			m.bios.padStarted = true
		case 0x14: // StopPAD2
			m.bios.padStarted = false
		case 0x20: // UnDeliverEvent(class, spec)
			for i := range m.bios.events {
				ev := &m.bios.events[i]
				if ev.state == evReady && ev.mode == evModeReady && ev.class == a0 && ev.spec == a1 {
					ev.state = evBusy
				}
			}
		default:
			m.logUnimplemented('B', fn, ret)
			setV(0xFFFFFFFF)
		}
	case 0xC0:
		switch fn {
		case 0x04: // get_free_EvCB_slot
			setV(0xFFFFFFFF)
			for i := range m.bios.events {
				if m.bios.events[i].state == evUnused {
					setV(uint32(i))
					break
				}
			}
		case 0x08: // SysInitMemory: the HLE kernel memory needs no setup
		case 0x09: // SysInitKernelVariables: same
		case 0x0A: // ChangeClearRCnt(t, flag)
			if a0 < 4 {
				old := m.bios.clearRCnt[a0]
				m.bios.clearRCnt[a0] = a1
				setV(old)
			} else {
				setV(0)
			}
		case 0x19: // SetRCnt(spec, target, mode): spec low bits = counter
			if a0&3 < 3 {
				n := int(a0 & 3)
				m.Timers.WriteTarget(n, uint16(a1))
				m.Timers.WriteMode(n, uint16(a2))
				setV(1)
			} else {
				setV(0)
			}
		case 0x1A: // GetRCnt(spec)
			if a0&3 < 3 {
				setV(uint32(m.Timers.T[a0&3].Counter))
			} else {
				setV(0)
			}
		case 0x1B: // ResetRCnt(spec)
			if a0&3 < 3 {
				n := int(a0 & 3)
				m.Timers.WriteCounter(n, 0)
				m.istat &^= 1 << uint(IRQTMR0+n)
				m.updateIRQ()
				setV(1)
			} else {
				setV(0)
			}
		default:
			m.logUnimplemented('C', fn, ret)
			setV(0xFFFFFFFF)
		}
	}
}

// biosInitTimer implements B(02h) with the exact
// mode computation psx-spx documents.
func (m *Machine) biosInitTimer(t, reload, flags uint32) uint32 {
	if t > 2 {
		return 0
	}
	n := int(t)
	m.Timers.WriteMode(n, 0)
	m.Timers.WriteTarget(n, uint16(reload))
	var mode uint32
	if flags&(1<<4) == 0 {
		mode = 0x48
	} else {
		mode = 0x49
	}
	if flags&1 == 0 {
		mode |= 0x100
	}
	if flags&(1<<12) != 0 {
		mode |= 0x10
	}
	m.Timers.WriteMode(n, uint16(mode))
	return 1
}

func (m *Machine) biosOpenEvent(class, spec, mode, fn uint32) uint32 {
	for i := range m.bios.events {
		if m.bios.events[i].state == evUnused {
			m.bios.events[i] = biosEvent{class: class, spec: spec, mode: mode, fn: fn, state: evDisabled}
			return evHandleBase + uint32(i)
		}
	}
	return 0xFFFFFFFF
}

func (m *Machine) biosEventByHandle(h uint32) *biosEvent {
	if h&0xFFFF0000 != evHandleBase {
		return nil
	}
	i := h & 0xFFFF
	if i >= evSlots || m.bios.events[i].state == evUnused {
		return nil
	}
	return &m.bios.events[i]
}

// biosTestEvent backs TestEvent and WaitEvent.
func (m *Machine) biosTestEvent(h uint32, wait bool) uint32 {
	_ = wait // both are non-blocking in this HLE; see the file comment
	ev := m.biosEventByHandle(h)
	if ev == nil {
		return 0
	}
	if ev.state == evReady {
		ev.state = evBusy
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// fillPadBuffers writes the InitPAD2 buffers on a
// VBlank when StartPAD2 has run: port 1 gets the
// wired pad (status okay, digital ID, the two
// active-low button bytes from the pad package via
// the machine button state), port 2 reports the
// documented no-device timeout status.
func (m *Machine) fillPadBuffers() {
	if !m.bios.padStarted {
		return
	}
	if m.bios.padBuf1 != 0 {
		b := m.buttons
		m.Bus.Write8(m.bios.padBuf1+0, 0x00)
		m.Bus.Write8(m.bios.padBuf1+1, 0x41)
		m.Bus.Write8(m.bios.padBuf1+2, byte(^(b >> 0)))
		m.Bus.Write8(m.bios.padBuf1+3, byte(^(b >> 8)))
	}
	if m.bios.padBuf2 != 0 {
		m.Bus.Write8(m.bios.padBuf2+0, 0xFF)
		m.Bus.Write8(m.bios.padBuf2+1, 0x00)
	}
}

// biosStateSize is the serialized BIOS block size:
// events, callback context and queue, and the scalar
// fields, in the fixed layout SerializeBIOS uses.
const biosStateSize = evSlots*20 + // class, spec, mode, fn, state+pad
	4 + 4 + // critCount, critIEc pad
	4*4 + // clearRCnt
	4 + 4 + 4 + // padBuf1, padBuf2, padStarted pad
	4 + // cbActive pad
	32*4 + 5*4 + // cbSaved regs + hi/lo/pc/nextPC/sr
	4 + 4 + // cbHead, cbCount
	cbQueueSize*4 +
	4 + 4 // unimplSeen, unimpl log length (entries are not serialized)

func (m *Machine) serializeBIOS() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, biosStateSize)
	off := 0
	put := func(v uint32) { put32(out[off:], v); off += 4 }
	for i := range m.bios.events {
		ev := &m.bios.events[i]
		put(ev.class)
		put(ev.spec)
		put(ev.mode)
		put(ev.fn)
		put(uint32(ev.state))
	}
	put(uint32(int32(m.bios.critCount)))
	put(bool32(m.bios.critIEc))
	for _, v := range m.bios.clearRCnt {
		put(v)
	}
	put(m.bios.padBuf1)
	put(m.bios.padBuf2)
	put(bool32(m.bios.padStarted))
	put(bool32(m.bios.cbActive))
	for _, r := range m.bios.cbSaved.regs {
		put(r)
	}
	put(m.bios.cbSaved.hi)
	put(m.bios.cbSaved.lo)
	put(m.bios.cbSaved.pc)
	put(m.bios.cbSaved.nextPC)
	put(m.bios.cbSaved.sr)
	put(uint32(m.bios.cbHead))
	put(uint32(m.bios.cbCount))
	for _, fn := range m.bios.cbQueue {
		put(fn)
	}
	put(uint32(m.bios.unimplSeen))
	put(uint32(len(m.bios.unimpl)))
	return out
}

func (m *Machine) deserializeBIOS(in []byte) {
	off := 0
	get := func() uint32 { v := get32(in[off:]); off += 4; return v }
	for i := range m.bios.events {
		ev := &m.bios.events[i]
		ev.class = get()
		ev.spec = get()
		ev.mode = get()
		ev.fn = get()
		ev.state = uint8(get())
	}
	m.bios.critCount = int(int32(get()))
	m.bios.critIEc = get() != 0
	for i := range m.bios.clearRCnt {
		m.bios.clearRCnt[i] = get()
	}
	m.bios.padBuf1 = get()
	m.bios.padBuf2 = get()
	m.bios.padStarted = get() != 0
	m.bios.cbActive = get() != 0
	for i := range m.bios.cbSaved.regs {
		m.bios.cbSaved.regs[i] = get()
	}
	m.bios.cbSaved.hi = get()
	m.bios.cbSaved.lo = get()
	m.bios.cbSaved.pc = get()
	m.bios.cbSaved.nextPC = get()
	m.bios.cbSaved.sr = get()
	m.bios.cbHead = int(get())
	m.bios.cbCount = int(get())
	for i := range m.bios.cbQueue {
		m.bios.cbQueue[i] = get()
	}
	m.bios.unimplSeen = int(get())
	_ = get() // log length: the log itself is diagnostic only, not restored
	m.bios.unimpl = nil
}

func bool32(b bool) uint32 {
	if b {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/boot.go ====================

package system

// Disc boot (PS1-4). A real PlayStation boots a
// disc by reading SYSTEM.CNF from the ISO9660
// filesystem, taking the executable path from its
// BOOT line, and loading that PS-X EXE. BootDisc
// reproduces exactly that sequence over the loaded
// disc image: no boot ROM is involved, the same way
// LoadEXE boots bare executables. Only the BOOT
// line is honored; the TCB, EVENT and STACK lines
// some SYSTEM.CNF files carry configure the real
// kernel's thread and event tables, which this
// core's BIOS HLE allocates on demand instead.

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/cd"
)

// BootDisc boots the currently loaded disc: it
// parses the disc's ISO9660 filesystem, reads
// SYSTEM.CNF, and loads the PS-X EXE its BOOT line
// names, leaving the machine at the EXE entry point
// with the disc still attached (the guest reads its
// data files from it). It returns an error when the
// disc has no readable SYSTEM.CNF, no BOOT line, or
// no readable boot executable.
func (m *Machine) BootDisc() error {
	if m.Disc == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: BootDisc with no disc loaded")
	}
	iso, err := cd.OpenISO(m.Disc)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: disc boot: %w", err)
	}
	cnf, err := iso.ReadFile("SYSTEM.CNF")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: disc boot: %w", err)
	}
	path, err := BootPath(string(cnf))
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	exe, err := iso.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: disc boot: %w", err)
	}
	if err := m.LoadEXE(exe); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: disc boot: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// BootPath extracts the boot executable path from
// SYSTEM.CNF contents. The BOOT line looks like:
//
//	BOOT = cdrom:\SLES_123.45;1
//
// The "cdrom:" device prefix and a leading slash
// are stripped; the returned path is in the ISO
// reader's form (slash-separated, the ";1" version
// suffix optional).
func BootPath(cnf string) (string, error) {
	for _, line := range strings.Split(cnf, "\n") {
		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
		key, val, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
		if !ok || !strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(key), "BOOT") {
			continue
		}
		val = strings.TrimSpace(val)
		if i := strings.Index(val, ":"); i >= 0 && strings.EqualFold(val[:i], "cdrom") {
			val = val[i+1:]
		}
		val = strings.TrimLeft(val, "\\/")
		val = strings.ReplaceAll(val, "\\", "/")
		if val == "" {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("system: SYSTEM.CNF BOOT line names no file")
		}
		return val, nil
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("system: SYSTEM.CNF has no BOOT line")
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/boot_test.go ====================

package system

// PS1-4 system gates: disc boot through SYSTEM.CNF,
// the diagnostics tally, and the host-forced analog
// pad mode. The disc fixture is the homebrew
// package's synthetic ISO9660 image carrying the
// enginetest EXE, so the boot gate re-runs the
// whole guest end to end from a file, the way a
// real disc boot would reach it.

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/homebrew"
)

func writeTemp(t *testing.T, name string, data []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	p := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), name)
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", name, err)
	}
	return p
}

func TestBootDiscEnginetest(t *testing.T) {
	img := homebrew.EnginetestISO(homebrew.EnginetestEXE())
	m := New()
	if err := m.OpenDisc(writeTemp(t, "ENGTEST.ISO", img)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("BootDisc: %v", err)
	}
	passed := false
	for chunk := 0; chunk < 40 && !passed; chunk++ {
		m.RunCycles(1000000)
		if m.Bus.Read32(0x80020000) == 0x600DF00D {
			passed = true
		}
	}
	if !passed {
		t.Fatalf("guest PASS magic not reached from disc boot: stage marker %d, unimplemented BIOS calls %d",
			m.Bus.Read32(0x80020100), m.UnimplementedBIOSCallCount())
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020100); got != 6 {
		t.Errorf("final stage marker actual %d, want 6", got)
	}
	// The guest read ISO sector 0 (all zeros) for its
	// CD stage, so the recorded checksum is 0, unlike
	// the in-process gate's patterned disc.
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020104); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("CD checksum actual 0x%08X, want 0 (zero sector 0)", got)
	}
	if d := m.Diagnostics(); !d.Empty() {
		t.Errorf("diagnostics after clean boot actual %q, want empty", d.String())
	}
	if w, h := m.DisplayWidth(), m.DisplayHeight(); w != 320 || h != 240 {
		t.Errorf("display size actual %dx%d, want 320x240", w, h)
	}
}

func TestBootDiscErrors(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err == nil {
		t.Error("BootDisc with no disc: got nil error, want an error")
	}
	// A non-ISO disc (the raw sector pattern source)
	// has no SYSTEM.CNF to boot from.
	if err := m.LoadDisc(&seqDisc{sectors: 16}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err == nil {
		t.Error("BootDisc on a non-ISO disc: got nil error, want an error")
	}
	// A bad EXE magic behind a good SYSTEM.CNF.
	bad := homebrew.EnginetestISO([]byte("not an exe"))
	if err := m.OpenDisc(writeTemp(t, "BAD.ISO", bad)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err == nil {
		t.Error("BootDisc with a corrupt boot file: got nil error, want an error")
	}
}

func TestBootPath(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		cnf  string
		want string
	}{
		{"BOOT = cdrom:\\ENGTEST.EXE;1\r\nTCB = 4\r\n", "ENGTEST.EXE;1"},
		{"boot=cdrom:\\GAMES\\DEMO.EXE;1\n", "GAMES/DEMO.EXE;1"},
		{"BOOT = cdrom:/PLAIN.EXE\n", "PLAIN.EXE"},
		{"  BOOT  =  cdrom:\\SPACED.EXE;1  \n", "SPACED.EXE;1"},
	} {
		got, err := BootPath(c.cnf)
		if err != nil {
			t.Errorf("BootPath(%q): unexpected error %v", c.cnf, err)
		} else if got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("BootPath(%q) actual %q, want %q", c.cnf, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	for _, cnf := range []string{"", "TCB = 4\r\n", "BOOT = cdrom:\r\n"} {
		if _, err := BootPath(cnf); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("BootPath(%q): got nil error, want an error", cnf)
		}
	}
}

func TestDiagnosticsTally(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(&seqDisc{sectors: 16}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	// One unimplemented BIOS call: A(7Fh).
	a := homebrew.NewAsm()
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0)
	a.CallBIOS(0xA0, 0x7F)
	a.Spin("spin")
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, a.Build(0x80010000))
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	m.RunCycles(10000)
	// One invalid CD command (17h) and one unknown
	// GP1 command (3Fh).
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801803, 0x1F)
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801801, 0x17)
	m.GPU.WriteGP1(0x3F000000)
	m.GPU.WriteGP1(0x3F000000)

	d := m.Diagnostics()
	if d.Empty() {
		t.Fatal("diagnostics empty, want the three tallies below")
	}
	if d.BIOSCallCount < 1 || len(d.BIOSCalls) < 1 || d.BIOSCalls[0].Table != 'A' || d.BIOSCalls[0].Func != 0x7F {
		t.Errorf("BIOS tally actual count %d log %v, want A(7F) first", d.BIOSCallCount, d.BIOSCalls)
	}
	if d.UnknownCDCount != 1 || len(d.UnknownCD) != 1 || d.UnknownCD[0] != 0x17 {
		t.Errorf("CD tally actual count %d list %v, want one 17h", d.UnknownCDCount, d.UnknownCD)
	}
	if d.UnknownGP1Count != 2 || len(d.UnknownGP1) != 1 || d.UnknownGP1[0] != 0x3F {
		t.Errorf("GP1 tally actual count %d list %v, want two of one 3Fh", d.UnknownGP1Count, d.UnknownGP1)
	}
	if s := d.String(); !strings.Contains(s, "A(7F)") || !strings.Contains(s, "[17]") || !strings.Contains(s, "[3F]") {
		t.Errorf("diagnostics string actual %q, want it to name A(7F), 17 and 3F", s)
	}
	// The tallies survive a machine reset (they are
	// per-load diagnostics, not machine state).
	m.Reset()
	if d2 := m.Diagnostics(); d2.BIOSCallCount != 0 || d2.UnknownCDCount != 1 || d2.UnknownGP1Count != 2 {
		t.Errorf("after Reset: BIOS %d (want 0, BIOS log resets), CD %d (want 1), GP1 %d (want 2)",
			d2.BIOSCallCount, d2.UnknownCDCount, d2.UnknownGP1Count)
	}
}

func TestAnalogModeHostForced(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.SetAnalogMode(true)
	m.Reset() // LoadEXE and friends reset; the mode must be reapplied
	if !m.PAD.AnalogMode() {
		t.Fatal("pad analog mode actual false after SetAnalogMode(true) and Reset, want true")
	}
	// The pad answers InitPAD2-style fills with the
	// analog ID 73h. Byte 1 of the port 1 buffer is
	// the pad ID; emulate the BIOS fill path by a
	// frame of the InitPAD2 sequence is covered by
	// the PS1-3 BIOS gates, so here the ID itself is
	// probed through a raw poll in the pad gate
	// style: run the guest from TestBIOSInitPAD2Fill
	// shaped code is overkill; the direct evidence
	// is the mode flag plus the digital default.
	m.SetAnalogMode(false)
	m.Reset()
	if m.PAD.AnalogMode() {
		t.Error("pad analog mode actual true after SetAnalogMode(false), want false")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/diag.go ====================

package system

// First-real-game diagnostics (PS1-4). The BIOS HLE
// covers a documented subset; a real game that
// calls outside it, or issues CD controller / GP1
// commands outside the implemented sets, fails in
// ways that are invisible from the TV. Diagnostics
// aggregates everything the machine saw but did not
// implement since it was created, so the libretro
// shell can print it to the frontend log at unload
// and a failure becomes a list of exactly what to
// implement next.

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// Diagnostics is the machine's not-implemented
// tally: unimplemented BIOS calls (with per-call
// detail), unknown CD controller commands, and
// unknown GP1 commands.
type Diagnostics struct {
	BIOSCalls       []BIOSCall // the BIOS unimplemented-call log (capped at 256 entries, repeats included)
	BIOSCallCount   int        // total unimplemented BIOS calls, including repeats
	UnknownCD       []uint8    // distinct unknown CD command bytes, first-seen order
	UnknownCDCount  int        // total unknown CD commands
	UnknownGP1      []uint8    // distinct unknown GP1 command bytes, first-seen order
	UnknownGP1Count int        // total unknown GP1 commands
}

// Diagnostics returns the machine's current
// not-implemented tally.
func (m *Machine) Diagnostics() Diagnostics {
	return Diagnostics{
		BIOSCalls:       m.UnimplementedBIOSCalls(),
		BIOSCallCount:   m.UnimplementedBIOSCallCount(),
		UnknownCD:       m.CD.UnknownCommands(),
		UnknownCDCount:  m.CD.UnknownCommandCount(),
		UnknownGP1:      m.GPU.UnknownGP1Commands(),
		UnknownGP1Count: m.GPU.UnknownGP1Count(),
	}
}

// Empty reports whether nothing unimplemented was
// seen at all.
func (d Diagnostics) Empty() bool {
	return d.BIOSCallCount == 0 && d.UnknownCDCount == 0 && d.UnknownGP1Count == 0
}

// String renders the tally as compact log lines:
// counts first, then the distinct offenders in hex.
func (d Diagnostics) String() string {
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "unimplemented BIOS calls: %d", d.BIOSCallCount)
	if len(d.BIOSCalls) > 0 {
		parts := make([]string, 0, len(d.BIOSCalls))
		for _, c := range d.BIOSCalls {
			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%c(%02X)", c.Table, c.Func))
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " [%s]", strings.Join(parts, " "))
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; unknown CD commands: %d", d.UnknownCDCount)
	if len(d.UnknownCD) > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " [%s]", hexList(d.UnknownCD))
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; unknown GP1 commands: %d", d.UnknownGP1Count)
	if len(d.UnknownGP1) > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " [%s]", hexList(d.UnknownGP1))
	}
	return b.String()
}

func hexList(bs []uint8) string {
	parts := make([]string, len(bs))
	for i, v := range bs {
		parts[i] = fmt.Sprintf("%02X", v)
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, " ")
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/exe.go ====================

package system

// PS-X EXE loading (PS1-3). The header layout is the
// documented one from psx-spx (CDROM File Formats,
// EXE file header): an 0x800-byte header starting
// with the ASCII magic "PS-X EXE", with the initial
// PC and GP, the text address and size, and the
// stack address and size; the saved-register fields
// at 0x38 and up are ignored, as the brief requires
// and as most loaders do. The text image follows the
// header.
//
// LoadEXE resets the machine first (the loaded disc,
// if any, stays attached), copies the text to its
// address, and sets the entry registers: PC = pc0,
// GP = gp0, and the stack per the documented rule:
// when s_addr is nonzero, SP and FP are
// s_addr + s_size; when it is zero the stack is the
// kernel default stack top (0x801FFF00, the value at
// the documented user-memory default).

import "fmt"

// exeHeaderSize is the documented PS-X EXE header
// size; the text image starts at this offset.
const exeHeaderSize = 0x800

// exeDefaultStack is the documented default stack
// top used when the header carries no stack address.
const exeDefaultStack = 0x801FFF00

// LoadEXE loads a PS-X EXE image into the machine
// and leaves it ready to run from the entry point.
func (m *Machine) LoadEXE(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) < exeHeaderSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: EXE too small: %d bytes, header is %d", len(data), exeHeaderSize)
	}
	if string(data[0:8]) != "PS-X EXE" {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: bad EXE magic %q, want \"PS-X EXE\"", data[0:8])
	}
	le := func(off int) uint32 { return get32(data[off:]) }
	pc0 := le(0x10)
	gp0 := le(0x14)
	tAddr := le(0x18)
	tSize := le(0x1C)
	sAddr := le(0x30)
	sSize := le(0x34)
	if uint64(exeHeaderSize)+uint64(tSize) > uint64(len(data)) {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: EXE text size %d exceeds file size %d", tSize, len(data))
	}
	m.Reset()
	text := data[exeHeaderSize : exeHeaderSize+tSize]
	for i, b := range text {
		m.Bus.Write8(tAddr+uint32(i), b)
	}
	m.CPU.PC = pc0
	m.CPU.NextPC = pc0 + 4
	m.CPU.Regs[28] = gp0 // $gp
	sp := uint32(exeDefaultStack)
	if sAddr != 0 {
		sp = sAddr + sSize
	}
	m.CPU.Regs[29] = sp // $sp
	m.CPU.Regs[30] = sp // $fp
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/mux.go ====================

package system

// The peripheral multiplexer: the Machine implements
// bus.IODevice, claiming the behavioral register
// windows inside the bus register page, and the DMA
// device endpoints. PS1-3 claims the full SPU window
// (voices, control, reverb, transfer port), the MDEC
// command/status and control registers, and the
// joypad/memory-card SIO0 window. Addresses not
// claimed here fall back to the bus's stored stub
// page.

// writeGP0 feeds one GP0 word and latches the GPU
// interrupt source on the request edge, delivering
// the matching BIOS event. Every GP0 write path
// (register, DMA, BIOS GPU_cw) goes through here.
func (m *Machine) writeGP0(w uint32) {
	m.GPU.WriteGP0(w)
	if m.GPU.IRQRequested() && !m.gpuIRQPrev {
		m.istat |= 1 << IRQGPU
		m.gpuIRQPrev = true
		m.deliverEvent(evClassGPU, evSpecIRQ)
		m.updateIRQ()
	}
}

// byteMask returns the mask of value bytes an access
// of the given size covers.
func byteMask(size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return 0xFF
	case 2:
		return 0xFFFF
	}
	return 0xFFFFFFFF
}

// ReadIO implements bus.IODevice.
func (m *Machine) ReadIO(addr uint32, size int) (uint32, bool) {
	switch {
	case addr == 0x1F801070:
		return uint32(m.istat), true
	case addr == 0x1F801074:
		return uint32(m.imask), true
	case addr == 0x1F801810:
		return m.GPU.ReadData(), true
	case addr == 0x1F801814:
		return m.GPU.Status(), true
	case addr >= 0x1F801100 && addr < 0x1F801130:
		reg := addr - 0x1F801100
		n := int(reg >> 4)
		switch reg & 0xF {
		case 0:
			return uint32(m.Timers.T[n].Counter), true
		case 4:
			// Reading the mode register clears its
			// reached flags (documented).
			return uint32(m.Timers.ReadMode(n)), true
		case 8:
			return uint32(m.Timers.T[n].Target), true
		}
		return 0, true
	case addr >= 0x1F801080 && addr < 0x1F801100:
		return m.DMA.ReadReg(addr &^ 3), true
	case addr >= 0x1F801800 && addr <= 0x1F801803:
		return uint32(m.CD.ReadReg(addr - 0x1F801800)), true
	case addr == 0x1F801820:
		if size != 4 {
			return 0, false
		}
		st := m.MDEC.Status()
		if st&(1<<31) != 0 { // data-out request: a word is pending
			return m.MDEC.ReadWord(), true
		}
		return st, true
	case addr == 0x1F801824:
		if size != 4 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return m.MDEC.Control(), true
	case addr >= 0x1F801040 && addr <= 0x1F80104F:
		if v, ok := m.PAD.ReadReg(addr, size); ok {
			return v, true
		}
		return 0, false
	case addr == 0x1F801DA6:
		// TSA, the SPU transfer address (documented
		// position; PS1-2 carried it at DA4).
		return uint32(m.SPU.AddrReg), true
	case addr == 0x1F801DA8:
		// The SPU data port (documented position;
		// PS1-2 carried it at DA6).
		if size == 1 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint32(m.SPU.ReadData()), true
	case addr >= 0x1F801C00 && addr <= 0x1F801DFF:
		if v, ok := m.SPU.ReadReg(addr, size); ok {
			return v, true
		}
		return 0, false
	}
	return 0, false
}

// WriteIO implements bus.IODevice.
func (m *Machine) WriteIO(addr uint32, size int, v uint32) bool {
	switch {
	case addr == 0x1F801070:
		// Write-to-acknowledge: bits written as 0
		// clear, bits written as 1 keep their state.
		keep := v | (^byteMask(size) & 0xFFFF)
		m.istat &= uint16(keep)
		m.updateIRQ()
		return true
	case addr == 0x1F801074:
		mask := byteMask(size)
		m.imask = uint16((uint32(m.imask) &^ mask) | (v & mask))
		m.updateIRQ()
		return true
	case addr == 0x1F801810:
		if size == 4 {
			m.writeGP0(v)
		}
		return true
	case addr == 0x1F801814:
		if size == 4 {
			m.GPU.WriteGP1(v)
		}
		return true
	case addr >= 0x1F801100 && addr < 0x1F801130:
		reg := addr - 0x1F801100
		n := int(reg >> 4)
		switch reg & 0xF {
		case 0:
			m.Timers.WriteCounter(n, uint16(v))
		case 4:
			m.Timers.WriteMode(n, uint16(v))
		case 8:
			m.Timers.WriteTarget(n, uint16(v))
		}
		return true
	case addr >= 0x1F801080 && addr < 0x1F801100:
		if size != 4 {
			return false // DMA registers are word-only
		}
		m.DMA.WriteReg(addr&^3, v)
		return true
	case addr >= 0x1F801800 && addr <= 0x1F801803:
		m.CD.WriteReg(addr-0x1F801800, uint8(v))
		return true
	case addr == 0x1F801820:
		if size != 4 {
			return false
		}
		m.MDEC.WriteWord(v)
		m.mdecCount++
		m.mdecSum = m.mdecSum*31 + v
		return true
	case addr == 0x1F801824:
		if size != 4 {
			return false
		}
		m.MDEC.WriteControl(v)
		return true
	case addr >= 0x1F801040 && addr <= 0x1F80104F:
		return m.PAD.WriteReg(addr, size, v)
	case addr == 0x1F801DA6:
		m.SPU.SetAddress(uint16(v))
		return true
	case addr == 0x1F801DA8:
		if size == 1 {
			return false
		}
		m.SPU.WriteData(uint16(v))
		if size == 4 {
			m.SPU.WriteData(uint16(v >> 16))
		}
		return true
	case addr >= 0x1F801C00 && addr <= 0x1F801DFF:
		return m.SPU.WriteReg(addr, size, v)
	}
	return false
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// DMA device endpoints (dma.Devices). MDEC-in feeds
// the codec (and keeps the PS1-2 count and checksum
// surface the diagnostics used); MDEC-out reads the
// codec's output stream.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

// GP0Write implements dma.Devices.
func (m *Machine) GP0Write(w uint32) { m.writeGP0(w) }

// GPURead implements dma.Devices.
func (m *Machine) GPURead() uint32 { return m.GPU.ReadData() }

// CDReadWord implements dma.Devices.
func (m *Machine) CDReadWord() (uint32, bool) { return m.CD.ReadWord() }

// SPUReadWord implements dma.Devices.
func (m *Machine) SPUReadWord() uint32 { return m.SPU.ReadWord() }

// SPUWriteWord implements dma.Devices.
func (m *Machine) SPUWriteWord(w uint32) { m.SPU.WriteWord(w) }

// MDECInWrite implements dma.Devices.
func (m *Machine) MDECInWrite(w uint32) {
	m.MDEC.WriteWord(w)
	m.mdecCount++
	m.mdecSum = m.mdecSum*31 + w
}

// MDECOutRead implements dma.Devices.
func (m *Machine) MDECOutRead() uint32 { return m.MDEC.ReadWord() }

// MDECSink returns the MDEC-in word count and
// checksum (test and diagnostics surface; the words
// themselves now go to the codec).
func (m *Machine) MDECSink() (uint32, uint32) { return m.mdecCount, m.mdecSum }


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/system.go ====================

// Package system is the whole PlayStation machine for
// the go-ps1 core, in the same family shape as the
// other iTaK cores.
//
// PS1-3 wiring: the R3000A CPU (chips/r3000a) runs on
// the memory bus (bus) with the full GTE (chips/gte)
// as CP2. The bus register page is routed to a
// peripheral multiplexer (mux.go) serving the GPU
// (gpu), the root counters (timers), the DMA
// controller (dma), the full CD controller (cd), the
// full SPU (spu), the MDEC codec (mdec) and the
// joypad and memory card serial controller (pad),
// plus the real interrupt controller registers
// I_STAT and I_MASK. A from-scratch HLE BIOS
// (bios.go) intercepts the documented call vectors,
// and PS-X EXE images load through LoadEXE (exe.go).
// There is no Sony BIOS and no Sony code anywhere in
// the machine.
//
// Execution model (stated in the core README):
// peripherals advance at instruction boundaries in
// Step. The display timing model derives the beam
// position from accumulated video clock cycles at the
// documented rates (NTSC 53.693175 MHz video clock,
// 263 lines of 3413 cycles; PAL 53.203425 MHz, 314
// lines of 3406 cycles, selected by the GPU display
// mode), so hblank/vblank windows, dotclock ticks and
// timer sync behavior are computed from the machine's
// true position, not from free-running approximations.
// The CD controller and the SPU advance on the same
// per-step cycle counts; the SPU synthesizes 44,100 Hz
// output through an exact ratio accumulator and pulls
// one CD input sample per output sample from the CD
// controller. Interrupt sources (VBlank, GPU, CDROM,
// DMA, TMR0/1/2, PAD, SPU) latch bits in I_STAT; the
// CPU external interrupt line follows (I_STAT AND
// I_MASK) through the CPU's CP0 IP2 path, and each
// latch also delivers the matching BIOS event.
//
// Frame budget: the NTSC CPU frame remains the
// PS1-1 exact rational (33,868,800 x 100 / 5994, so
// frames alternate 565,045 and 565,046 cycles). The
// display frame at 263 lines is a few hundred cycles
// longer than the CPU frame budget; both models are
// exact in themselves and the README notes the
// relationship.
package system

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/cd"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/chips/gte"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/chips/r3000a"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/dma"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/gpu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/mdec"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/pad"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/spu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/timers"
)

// Maximum framebuffer dimensions across display
// modes. The actual frame is the GPU's native
// resolution; see DisplayWidth and DisplayHeight.
const (
	Width  = gpu.MaxWidth
	Height = gpu.MaxHeight
)

// Digital pad buttons, stored by SetButtons as a
// bitmask in PlayStation pad order. The pad hardware
// itself lands in a later slice; the I_STAT pad bit
// exists with no source yet.
const (
	ButtonSelect = 1 << 0
	ButtonL3     = 1 << 1
	ButtonR3     = 1 << 2
	ButtonStart  = 1 << 3
	ButtonUp     = 1 << 4
	ButtonRight  = 1 << 5
	ButtonDown   = 1 << 6
	ButtonLeft   = 1 << 7
	ButtonL2     = 1 << 8
	ButtonR2     = 1 << 9
	ButtonL1     = 1 << 10
	ButtonR1     = 1 << 11
	ButtonTri    = 1 << 12
	ButtonCircle = 1 << 13
	ButtonCross  = 1 << 14
	ButtonSquare = 1 << 15
)

// Interrupt controller bits in I_STAT and I_MASK.
const (
	IRQVBlank = 0
	IRQGPU    = 1
	IRQCDROM  = 2
	IRQDMA    = 3
	IRQTMR0   = 4
	IRQTMR1   = 5
	IRQTMR2   = 6
	IRQPAD    = 7
	IRQSPU    = 9
)

const (
	cpuHz        = 33_868_800
	frameRateHz  = 5994 // 59.94 Hz, scaled by 100
	stateVersion = 3
	miscSize     = 96
)

// Video timing constants per video standard. The
// video clock runs at these rates against the CPU
// clock; positions derive from their exact ratio.
type videoMode struct {
	lines    int64
	dotsLine int64
	clockNum int64 // video clock Hz numerator over cpuHz
}

var (
	videoNTSC = videoMode{lines: 263, dotsLine: 3413, clockNum: 53_693_175}
	videoPAL  = videoMode{lines: 314, dotsLine: 3406, clockNum: 53_203_425}
)

// Machine is one powered-on PlayStation.
type Machine struct {
	CPU  *r3000a.CPU
	Bus  *bus.Bus
	Disc cd.Reader

	GPU    *gpu.GPU
	GTE    *gte.GTE
	Timers *timers.Timers
	DMA    *dma.Controller
	SPU    *spu.SPU
	CD     *cd.Controller
	MDEC   *mdec.MDEC
	PAD    *pad.Controller

	bios biosState

	istat uint16
	imask uint16

	buttons   uint32
	analog    [4]uint8 // rx, ry, lx, ly
	analogOn  bool     // host-forced analog pad mode, reapplied on reset
	frame     uint64
	budgetRem int64

	// Display timing state: absolute video cycles
	// since reset and the derived-event counters used
	// for exact per-interval deltas.
	absVC         int64
	vcRem         int64
	displayFrames uint64
	prevDotTicks  int64
	prevHBlank    int64
	prevVBlank    int64
	gpuIRQPrev    bool

	mdecCount uint32
	mdecSum   uint32
}

// New returns a machine in reset state with no disc.
func New() *Machine {
	m := &Machine{}
	m.Bus = bus.New()
	m.GPU = gpu.New()
	m.GTE = gte.New()
	m.Timers = timers.New()
	m.DMA = dma.New()
	m.SPU = spu.New()
	m.CD = cd.NewController()
	m.MDEC = mdec.New()
	m.PAD = pad.New()
	m.DMA.Mem = m.Bus
	m.DMA.Dev = m
	m.wireIRQCallbacks()
	m.Bus.SetIODevice(m)
	m.CPU = r3000a.New(m.Bus)
	m.CPU.CP2 = m.GTE
	m.Reset()
	return m
}

// wireIRQCallbacks (re)installs the peripheral IRQ
// callbacks. Reset calls it after the component
// resets so a component that clears its callback
// field on reset cannot unwire the machine.
func (m *Machine) wireIRQCallbacks() {
	m.DMA.OnIRQ = func() {
		m.istat |= 1 << IRQDMA
		m.deliverEvent(evClassDMA, evSpecIRQ)
		m.updateIRQ()
	}
	m.CD.OnIRQ = func() {
		m.istat |= 1 << IRQCDROM
		m.deliverEvent(evClassCDROM, evSpecIRQ)
		m.updateIRQ()
	}
	m.SPU.OnIRQ = func() {
		m.istat |= 1 << IRQSPU
		m.deliverEvent(evClassSPU, evSpecIRQ)
		m.updateIRQ()
	}
	m.PAD.OnIRQ = func() {
		m.istat |= 1 << IRQPAD
		m.deliverEvent(evClassPAD, evSpecIRQ)
		m.updateIRQ()
	}
}

// LoadDisc inserts a disc image and resets the
// machine, matching how the other cores treat a game
// load.
func (m *Machine) LoadDisc(r cd.Reader) error {
	if r == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: nil disc reader")
	}
	m.Disc = r
	m.CD.SetDisc(r)
	m.Reset()
	return nil
}

// OpenDisc opens a disc image by path (see cd.Open)
// and loads it.
func (m *Machine) OpenDisc(path string) error {
	img, err := cd.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return m.LoadDisc(img)
}

// Reset returns the machine to its power-on state.
func (m *Machine) Reset() {
	disc := m.Disc
	m.Bus.Reset()
	m.CPU.Reset()
	m.GTE = gte.New()
	m.CPU.CP2 = m.GTE
	m.GPU.Reset()
	m.Timers.Reset()
	m.DMA.Reset()
	m.SPU.Reset()
	m.CD.Reset()
	m.CD.SetDisc(disc)
	m.MDEC.Reset()
	m.PAD.Reset()
	m.bios.reset()
	m.PAD.SetButtons(m.buttons)
	m.PAD.SetAnalog(m.analog[0], m.analog[1], m.analog[2], m.analog[3])
	m.PAD.SetAnalogMode(m.analogOn)
	m.wireIRQCallbacks()
	m.istat = 0
	m.imask = 0
	m.frame = 0
	m.budgetRem = 0
	m.absVC = 0
	m.vcRem = 0
	m.displayFrames = 0
	m.prevDotTicks = 0
	m.prevHBlank = 0
	m.prevVBlank = 0
	m.gpuIRQPrev = false
	m.mdecCount = 0
	m.mdecSum = 0
	m.CPU.SetInterrupt(false)
}

// video returns the active standard's constants.
func (m *Machine) video() videoMode {
	if m.GPU.PAL() {
		return videoPAL
	}
	return videoNTSC
}

// hBlankStartsTo counts hblank pulse starts at
// absolute video positions strictly before t: one
// start per line, at the X2 boundary (or at the line
// start when only the X1 segment exists), and none
// when the programmed range leaves no hblank at all.
func (m *Machine) hBlankStartsTo(t int64) int64 {
	vm := m.video()
	x1, x2 := m.GPU.HDisplayRange()
	if int64(x1) == 0 && int64(x2) >= vm.dotsLine {
		return 0 // the range covers the whole line: no hblank
	}
	start := int64(x2)
	if start >= vm.dotsLine {
		start = 0 // only the [0, X1) segment exists, starting at the line start
	}
	return pulseStartsTo(t, vm.dotsLine, start, true)
}

// vBlankStartsTo counts vblank starts strictly
// before t: one per frame at the Y2 line start, or
// at the frame start when Y2 is beyond the frame but
// a [0, Y1) segment still exists. With Y1 = 0 and Y2
// beyond the frame there is no vblank at all (the
// documented configuration that never interrupts).
func (m *Machine) vBlankStartsTo(t int64) int64 {
	vm := m.video()
	y1, y2 := m.GPU.VDisplayRange()
	if int64(y2) >= vm.lines && int64(y1) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	start := int64(y2) * vm.dotsLine
	if int64(y2) >= vm.lines {
		start = 0
	}
	return pulseStartsTo(t, vm.lines*vm.dotsLine, start, true)
}

// pulseStartsTo counts pulse starts at positions
// k*period + startOff (k = 0, 1, ...) that are
// strictly less than t. When startOff is 0 the first
// start is at t=0 itself.
func pulseStartsTo(t, period, startOff int64, enabled bool) int64 {
	if !enabled || t <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if startOff >= period {
		return 0
	}
	if startOff == 0 {
		return (t + period - 1) / period
	}
	if t <= startOff {
		return 0
	}
	return (t-1-startOff)/period + 1
}

// dotTicksTo counts GPU dotclock ticks strictly
// before absolute video position t, honoring the
// documented per-line floor of fractional dots.
func (m *Machine) dotTicksTo(t int64) int64 {
	vm := m.video()
	div := int64(m.GPU.DotDivider())
	perLine := vm.dotsLine / div
	lines := t / vm.dotsLine
	dot := t % vm.dotsLine
	return lines*perLine + dot/div
}

// beamAt resolves the line and dot position for an
// absolute video position.
func (m *Machine) beamAt(t int64) (line, dot int64) {
	vm := m.video()
	frame := vm.lines * vm.dotsLine
	pos := t % frame
	return pos / vm.dotsLine, pos % vm.dotsLine
}

// inHBlankAt reports hblank for a position from the
// GPU's horizontal display range.
func (m *Machine) inHBlankAt(t int64) bool {
	x1, x2 := m.GPU.HDisplayRange()
	_, dot := m.beamAt(t)
	return dot < int64(x1) || dot >= int64(x2)
}

// inVBlankAt reports vblank for a position from the
// GPU's vertical display range.
func (m *Machine) inVBlankAt(t int64) bool {
	y1, y2 := m.GPU.VDisplayRange()
	line, _ := m.beamAt(t)
	return line < int64(y1) || line >= int64(y2)
}

// InHBlank reports the current beam blanking state.
func (m *Machine) InHBlank() bool { return m.inHBlankAt(m.absVC) }

// InVBlank reports the current beam blanking state.
func (m *Machine) InVBlank() bool { return m.inVBlankAt(m.absVC) }

// DisplayFrames returns the number of display frame
// wraps since reset (263-line or 314-line frames per
// the video standard, distinct from RunFrame calls).
func (m *Machine) DisplayFrames() uint64 { return m.displayFrames }

// IStat returns the interrupt controller pending bits.
func (m *Machine) IStat() uint16 { return m.istat }

// IMask returns the interrupt controller mask.
func (m *Machine) IMask() uint16 { return m.imask }

// updateIRQ drives the CPU external interrupt line
// from the controller state.
func (m *Machine) updateIRQ() {
	m.CPU.SetInterrupt(m.istat&m.imask != 0)
}

// advance moves the peripheral model forward by the
// cycles one CPU instruction consumed: beam position,
// timers (with real dot/hblank/vblank feeds), the
// VBlank and GPU interrupt sources.
func (m *Machine) advance(cycles int) {
	if cycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	vm := m.video()
	inH := m.inHBlankAt(m.absVC)
	inV := m.inVBlankAt(m.absVC)
	m.vcRem += int64(cycles) * vm.clockNum
	delta := m.vcRem / cpuHz
	m.vcRem -= delta * cpuHz
	oldVC := m.absVC
	m.absVC += delta

	// Display frame wraps.
	frame := vm.lines * vm.dotsLine
	if m.absVC/frame != oldVC/frame {
		m.displayFrames += uint64(m.absVC/frame - oldVC/frame)
	}

	hbStarts := m.hBlankStartsTo(m.absVC)
	vbStarts := m.vBlankStartsTo(m.absVC)
	dotTicks := m.dotTicksTo(m.absVC)
	in := timers.Inputs{
		SysCycles:   cycles,
		DotTicks:    int(dotTicks - m.prevDotTicks),
		HBlankPulse: int(hbStarts - m.prevHBlank),
		VBlankPulse: int(vbStarts - m.prevVBlank),
		InHBlank:    inH,
		InVBlank:    inV,
	}
	if in.DotTicks < 0 {
		in.DotTicks = 0
	}
	m.prevDotTicks = dotTicks
	m.prevHBlank = hbStarts
	m.prevVBlank = vbStarts

	if in.VBlankPulse > 0 {
		m.istat |= 1 << IRQVBlank
		m.deliverEvent(evClassVBlank, evSpecIRQ)
		m.deliverEvent(evClassRCntVB, evSpecRCnt)
		m.fillPadBuffers()
	}
	asserted := m.Timers.Advance(in)
	for i := 0; i < timers.Count; i++ {
		if asserted&(1<<uint(i)) != 0 {
			m.istat |= 1 << uint(IRQTMR0+i)
			class := evClassTMR0 + uint32(i)
			if i == 2 {
				class = evClassTMR1 // TMR2 shares TMR1's class (documented quirk)
			}
			m.deliverEvent(class, evSpecIRQ)
			m.deliverEvent(evClassRCnt0+uint32(i), evSpecRCnt)
		}
	}
	// GPU interrupt source is edge-latched from the
	// GPUSTAT request bit (GP0(1F) sets it, GP1(02)
	// clears it).
	irq := m.GPU.IRQRequested()
	if irq && !m.gpuIRQPrev {
		m.istat |= 1 << IRQGPU
		m.deliverEvent(evClassGPU, evSpecIRQ)
	}
	m.gpuIRQPrev = irq

	line, _ := m.beamAt(m.absVC)
	m.GPU.LineOdd = line&1 == 1
	m.GPU.Field = int(m.displayFrames & 1)
	m.GPU.OddFrame = m.displayFrames&1 == 1

	// The CD controller's timed work (seek and sector
	// delivery, playback position) and the SPU run on
	// the same cycle count. The SPU pulls one CD input
	// sample per generated output sample.
	m.CD.Advance(cycles)
	m.SPU.Advance(cycles, m.CD.PullCDSample)

	m.updateIRQ()
}

// Step executes one CPU instruction (or one BIOS HLE
// interception: a call vector, a critical-section
// syscall, or an event callback frame), advances the
// peripheral model by its cycles, and returns the
// cycles consumed.
func (m *Machine) Step() int {
	if c, handled := m.stepBIOS(); handled {
		return c
	}
	c := m.CPU.Step()
	m.advance(c)
	return c
}

// RunCycles executes CPU instructions until at least
// n cycles have been consumed.
func (m *Machine) RunCycles(n int) {
	done := 0
	for done < n {
		done += m.Step()
	}
}

// RunFrame runs one NTSC frame of CPU time.
func (m *Machine) RunFrame() {
	m.budgetRem += cpuHz * 100
	budget := m.budgetRem / frameRateHz
	m.budgetRem -= budget * frameRateHz
	m.RunCycles(int(budget))
	m.frame++
}

// Frames returns the number of RunFrame calls since
// reset.
func (m *Machine) Frames() uint64 { return m.frame }

// Framebuffer returns the GPU display area as
// XRGB8888 pixels at its native resolution (see
// DisplayWidth and DisplayHeight for the dimensions
// of the returned slice).
func (m *Machine) Framebuffer() []uint32 {
	fb, _, _ := m.GPU.Framebuffer()
	return fb
}

// DisplayWidth returns the framebuffer width in
// pixels for the current display mode.
func (m *Machine) DisplayWidth() int { return m.GPU.DisplayWidth() }

// DisplayHeight returns the framebuffer height in
// pixels for the current display mode.
func (m *Machine) DisplayHeight() int { return m.GPU.DisplayHeight() }

// SetButtons stores the digital pad state for port 1
// and forwards it to the pad controller.
func (m *Machine) SetButtons(mask uint32) {
	m.buttons = mask
	m.PAD.SetButtons(mask)
}

// Buttons returns the stored pad state.
func (m *Machine) Buttons() uint32 { return m.buttons }

// SetAnalog stores the analog stick positions for
// port 1 (right stick X/Y, left stick X/Y) and
// forwards them to the pad controller.
func (m *Machine) SetAnalog(rx, ry, lx, ly uint8) {
	m.analog = [4]uint8{rx, ry, lx, ly}
	m.PAD.SetAnalog(rx, ry, lx, ly)
}

// Analog returns the stored stick positions
// (rx, ry, lx, ly).
func (m *Machine) Analog() (rx, ry, lx, ly uint8) {
	return m.analog[0], m.analog[1], m.analog[2], m.analog[3]
}

// SetAnalogMode forces the port 1 pad into (or out
// of) analog mode from the host side, for frontends
// that always present an analog pad. The choice is
// stored and reapplied on every reset, like the
// button and stick state.
func (m *Machine) SetAnalogMode(b bool) {
	m.analogOn = b
	m.PAD.SetAnalogMode(b)
}

// AnalogMode reports the host-forced analog mode.
func (m *Machine) AnalogMode() bool { return m.analogOn }

// SystemRAM returns the live 2 MB main RAM, for the
// libretro SYSTEM_RAM memory region. Writes through
// it are writes to the machine.
func (m *Machine) SystemRAM() []byte { return m.Bus.RAM() }

// AudioBuffer drains the SPU's pending output:
// interleaved stereo int16 samples at 44,100 Hz.
func (m *Machine) AudioBuffer() []int16 { return m.SPU.AudioBuffer() }

// AudioSampleRate is the SPU output rate.
const AudioSampleRate = 44100

// CardImage returns the live 128 KB memory card
// image (port 1). The pad package owns the protocol;
// the image is exposed here for persistence by the
// shell in a later slice.
func (m *Machine) CardImage() []byte { return m.PAD.CardImage() }

// StateSize returns the exact serialized state size
// for version 3: version byte, CPU, RAM, scratchpad,
// GPU, GTE, timers, DMA, interrupt controller, SPU,
// CD controller, MDEC, pad and card, the BIOS HLE
// block and the machine misc block.
func (m *Machine) StateSize() int {
	return 1 + r3000a.StateSize + bus.RAMSize + bus.ScratchpadSize +
		gpu.StateSize + gte.StateSize + timers.StateSize() + dma.StateSize + 4 +
		spu.StateSize + cd.CtrlStateSize + mdec.StateSize + pad.StateSize +
		biosStateSize + miscSize
}

// Serialize returns the machine state. The disc image
// is not part of the state (it is the loaded media,
// re-supplied by the caller on restore, like the
// other cores' cartridges).
func (m *Machine) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, m.StateSize())
	out[0] = stateVersion
	off := 1
	put := func(b []byte) {
		copy(out[off:off+len(b)], b)
		off += len(b)
	}
	put(m.CPU.Serialize())
	put(m.Bus.RAM())
	put(m.Bus.Scratchpad())
	put(m.GPU.Serialize())
	put(m.GTE.Serialize())
	put(m.Timers.Serialize())
	put(m.DMA.Serialize())
	{
		b := make([]byte, 4)
		b[0] = byte(m.istat)
		b[1] = byte(m.istat >> 8)
		b[2] = byte(m.imask)
		b[3] = byte(m.imask >> 8)
		put(b)
	}
	put(m.SPU.Serialize())
	put(m.CD.Serialize())
	put(m.MDEC.Serialize())
	put(m.PAD.Serialize())
	put(m.serializeBIOS())
	{
		b := make([]byte, miscSize)
		put64(b[0:], uint64(m.frame))
		put64(b[8:], uint64(m.budgetRem))
		put32(b[16:], m.buttons)
		put64(b[24:], uint64(m.absVC))
		put64(b[32:], uint64(m.vcRem))
		put64(b[40:], m.displayFrames)
		if m.gpuIRQPrev {
			b[48] = 1
		}
		put32(b[52:], m.mdecCount)
		put32(b[56:], m.mdecSum)
		put64(b[64:], uint64(m.prevDotTicks))
		put64(b[72:], uint64(m.prevHBlank))
		put64(b[80:], uint64(m.prevVBlank))
		copy(b[88:], m.analog[:])
		put(b)
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (m *Machine) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != m.StateSize() {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d, want %d", len(in), m.StateSize())
	}
	if in[0] != stateVersion {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state version %d, want %d", in[0], stateVersion)
	}
	off := 1
	take := func(n int) []byte {
		b := in[off : off+n]
		off += n
		return b
	}
	if err := m.CPU.Deserialize(take(r3000a.StateSize)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	copy(m.Bus.RAM(), take(bus.RAMSize))
	copy(m.Bus.Scratchpad(), take(bus.ScratchpadSize))
	m.GPU.Deserialize(take(gpu.StateSize))
	if err := m.GTE.Deserialize(take(gte.StateSize)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	m.Timers.Deserialize(take(timers.StateSize()))
	m.DMA.Deserialize(take(dma.StateSize))
	{
		b := take(4)
		m.istat = uint16(b[0]) | uint16(b[1])<<8
		m.imask = uint16(b[2]) | uint16(b[3])<<8
	}
	m.SPU.Deserialize(take(spu.StateSize))
