	if err := m.CD.Deserialize(take(cd.CtrlStateSize)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := m.MDEC.Deserialize(take(mdec.StateSize)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := m.PAD.Deserialize(take(pad.StateSize)); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	m.deserializeBIOS(take(biosStateSize))
	{
		b := take(miscSize)
		m.frame = get64(b[0:])
		m.budgetRem = int64(get64(b[8:]))
		m.buttons = get32(b[16:])
		m.absVC = int64(get64(b[24:]))
		m.vcRem = int64(get64(b[32:]))
		m.displayFrames = get64(b[40:])
		m.gpuIRQPrev = b[48] != 0
		m.mdecCount = get32(b[52:])
		m.mdecSum = get32(b[56:])
		m.prevDotTicks = int64(get64(b[64:]))
		m.prevHBlank = int64(get64(b[72:]))
		m.prevVBlank = int64(get64(b[80:]))
		copy(m.analog[:], b[88:92])
	}
	m.PAD.SetButtons(m.buttons)
	m.PAD.SetAnalog(m.analog[0], m.analog[1], m.analog[2], m.analog[3])
	m.updateIRQ()
	return nil
}

func put32(b []byte, v uint32) {
	b[0], b[1], b[2], b[3] = byte(v), byte(v>>8), byte(v>>16), byte(v>>24)
}
func get32(b []byte) uint32 {
	return uint32(b[0]) | uint32(b[1])<<8 | uint32(b[2])<<16 | uint32(b[3])<<24
}
func put64(b []byte, v uint64) {
	put32(b, uint32(v))
	put32(b[4:], uint32(v>>32))
}
func get64(b []byte) uint64 {
	return uint64(get32(b)) | uint64(get32(b[4:]))<<32
}

package system

// PS1-2 system gates: display timing, timers through
// the register page, DMA through the machine, the
// interrupt controller with real CPU programs, the CD
// DMA path, and the full determinism gate.

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/cd"
)

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// MIPS program helpers (hand assembled, our own code)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

func loadProg(m *Machine, addr uint32, words []uint32) {
	for i, w := range words {
		m.Bus.Write32(addr+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
}

func setPC(m *Machine, addr uint32) {
	m.CPU.PC = addr
	m.CPU.NextPC = addr + 4
}

// installCounterHandler writes an interrupt handler
// at 0x80000000 that increments the word at
// counterAddr, acknowledges I_STAT with ackValue,
// and returns through EPC/RFE. NOPs sit after the
// load and after mfc0: both results land a cycle
// late on the R3000, so the next instruction must
// not consume them.
//
//	lui k0, hi(counter) ; lw k1, lo(k0) ; nop
//	addiu k1, k1, 1 ; sw k1, lo(k0)
//	lui k0, 0x1F80 ; lui k1, hi(ack) ; ori k1, lo(ack)
//	sw k1, 0x1070(k0) ; mfc0 k0, EPC ; nop
//	jr k0 ; rfe
func installCounterHandler(m *Machine, counterAddr, ackValue uint32) {
	hi := counterAddr >> 16
	lo := counterAddr & 0xFFFF
	words := []uint32{
		0x3C1A0000 | hi,                  // lui k0, hi
		0x8F5B0000 | lo,                  // lw k1, lo(k0)
		0x00000000,                       // nop (load delay)
		0x277B0001,                       // addiu k1, k1, 1
		0xAF5B0000 | lo,                  // sw k1, lo(k0)
		0x3C1A1F80,                       // lui k0, 0x1F80
		0x3C1B0000 | (ackValue >> 16),    // lui k1, hi(ack)
		0x377B0000 | (ackValue & 0xFFFF), // ori k1, k1, lo(ack)
		0xAF5B1070,                       // sw k1, 0x1070(k0)  I_STAT ack
		0x401A7000,                       // mfc0 k0, EPC
		0x00000000,                       // nop (COP0 delay)
		0x03400008,                       // jr k0
		0x42000010,                       // rfe
	}
	loadProg(m, 0x80000000, words)
}

// spinProgram enables interrupts (SR = IEc + IM
// external) and loops forever. Setup words before
// the loop are supplied by the test.
func spinProgram(setup []uint32) []uint32 {
	prog := append([]uint32{}, setup...)
	prog = append(prog,
		0x24090401, // addiu t1, zero, 0x401
		0x40896000, // mtc0 t1, SR
		0x1000FFFF, // beq zero, zero, -1
		0x00000000, // nop (delay slot)
	)
	return prog
}

func TestVBlankInterruptProgram(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	counter := uint32(0x80012000)
	installCounterHandler(m, counter, 0xFFFFFFFE) // ack bit 0 only
	// I_MASK = VBlank only.
	prog := spinProgram([]uint32{
		0x3C081F80, // lui t0, 0x1F80
		0x24090001, // addiu t1, zero, 1
		0xAD091074, // sw t1, 0x1074(t0)
	})
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, prog)
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(counter); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("vblank handler count over 3 frames = %d, want 3", got)
	}
	// Masking at the controller stops delivery even
	// though the source keeps latching I_STAT.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801074, 0)
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(counter); got != 3 {
		t.Errorf("count after masking = %d, want still 3", got)
	}
	if m.IStat()&(1<<IRQVBlank) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("I_STAT vblank bit not latched while masked")
	}
}

func TestTimerInterruptThroughISTAT(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, []uint32{0x1000FFFF, 0x00000000})
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	// Timer 0: target 100, reset at target, IRQ at
	// target, repeat. Configured through the real
	// register page.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801074, 1<<IRQTMR0) // I_MASK
	m.Bus.Write16(0x1F801108, 100)        // target
	m.Bus.Write16(0x1F801104, 0x0058)     // mode
	m.RunCycles(950)
	if m.IStat()&(1<<IRQTMR0) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("timer 0 IRQ never reached I_STAT: I_STAT=0x%04X", m.IStat())
	}
	// Acknowledge: write with the bit 0 clears it.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801070, 0xFFFFFFEF)
	if m.IStat()&(1<<IRQTMR0) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("I_STAT timer bit not cleared by ack write")
	}
	// Counter kept counting from the mode write:
	// after 950 cycles with period 100 it wrapped 9
	// times and reads 50 (reads happen at the last
	// instruction boundary, allow the final partial
	// instruction of slack).
	ctr := m.Bus.Read16(0x1F801100)
	if ctr < 45 || ctr > 55 {
		t.Errorf("timer 0 counter = %d, want about 50", ctr)
	}
}

func TestHBlankTimerExactOverDisplayFrame(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, []uint32{0x1000FFFF, 0x00000000})
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	// Timer 1 clocked by hblank.
	m.Bus.Write16(0x1F801114, 0x0100)
	base := m.DisplayFrames()
	// Step in small increments and stop just past the
	// wrap: the overshoot into the next frame stays a
	// fraction of a line, far from the next hblank
	// pulse at dot 3072, so the count is exact.
	for m.DisplayFrames() == base {
		m.RunCycles(100)
	}
	// One hblank pulse per line, 263 lines, exactly:
	// the beam overshoot into the next frame is a
	// fraction of one line and cannot reach the next
	// pulse at dot 3072.
	if got := m.Timers.T[1].Counter; got != 263 {
		t.Errorf("timer 1 hblank count = %d, want 263", got)
	}
}

func TestHBlankTimerPAL(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, []uint32{0x1000FFFF, 0x00000000})
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801814, 0x08000008) // GP1 mode: PAL
	m.Bus.Write16(0x1F801114, 0x0100)     // timer 1: hblank clock
	for m.DisplayFrames() == 0 {
		m.RunCycles(100)
	}
	if got := m.Timers.T[1].Counter; got != 314 {
		t.Errorf("PAL timer 1 hblank count = %d, want 314", got)
	}
}

func TestDMAGPUFillGate(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	// Draw area wide open.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, 0xE3000000)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, 0xE407FFFF)
	// Packet in RAM: one GP0 fill (green, 4x4 at
	// (60,60)).
	const pkt = 0x80015000
	loadProg(m, pkt, []uint32{0x0200FF00, 0x003C003C, 0x00040004})
	// DICR: enable ch2 IRQ + master.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010F4, (1<<18)|(1<<23))
	// DPCR: enable ch2.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010A0, pkt)        // MADR
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010A4, 3)          // BCR: 3 words
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000001) // CHCR: from RAM, sync 0, start
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(60, 60); got != 0x03E0 {
		t.Errorf("fill pixel = 0x%04X, want 0x03E0 (DMA fed the fill)", got)
	}
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(63, 63); got != 0x03E0 {
		t.Errorf("fill corner = 0x%04X, want 0x03E0", got)
	}
	dicr := m.Bus.Read32(0x1F8010F4)
	if dicr&(1<<26) == 0 || dicr&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("DICR = 0x%08X, want ch2 flag (bit 26) and master (bit 31)", dicr)
	}
	if m.IStat()&(1<<IRQDMA) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("DMA completion did not reach I_STAT bit 3")
	}
}

func TestDMALinkedListGate(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, 0xE3000000)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, 0xE407FFFF)
	// Three nodes, each one fill command (3 words).
	loadProg(m, 0x80016000, []uint32{
		0x03016100, 0x020000FF, 0x00640064, 0x00020002, // node A -> B, red at (100,100)
	})
	loadProg(m, 0x80016100, []uint32{
		0x03016200, 0x0200FF00, 0x006E006E, 0x00020002, // node B -> C, green at (110,110)
	})
	loadProg(m, 0x80016200, []uint32{
		0x03FFFFFF, 0x02FF0000, 0x00780078, 0x00020002, // node C end, blue at (120,120)
	})
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010A0, 0x80016000)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000401) // sync 2 linked list, from RAM, start
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(100, 100); got != 0x001F {
		t.Errorf("node A fill = 0x%04X, want 0x001F", got)
	}
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(110, 110); got != 0x03E0 {
		t.Errorf("node B fill = 0x%04X, want 0x03E0", got)
	}
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(120, 120); got != 0x7C00 {
		t.Errorf("node C fill = 0x%04X, want 0x7C00", got)
	}
}

func TestDMAInterruptProgram(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, 0xE3000000)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, 0xE407FFFF)
	const pkt = 0x80017000
	loadProg(m, pkt, []uint32{0x0200FF00, 0x003C003C, 0x00040004})
	counter := uint32(0x80012008)
	installCounterHandler(m, counter, 0xFFFFFFF7) // ack bit 3 only
	prog := spinProgram([]uint32{
		0x3C081F80, // lui t0, 0x1F80
		0x24090008, // addiu t1, zero, 8 (DMA mask)
		0xAD091074, // sw t1, I_MASK
		0x24090800, // addiu t1, zero, 0x800 (DPCR ch2 enable)
		0xAD0910F0, // sw t1, DPCR
		0x3C090084, // lui t1, 0x0084 (DICR en ch2 + master)
		0xAD0910F4, // sw t1, DICR
		0x3C098001, // lui t1, 0x8001
		0x35297000, // ori t1, 0x7000 (packet address)
		0xAD0910A0, // sw t1, MADR
		0x24090003, // addiu t1, zero, 3
		0xAD0910A4, // sw t1, BCR
		0x3C090100, // lui t1, 0x0100
		0x35290001, // ori t1, 1 (CHCR start, from RAM, sync 0)
		0xAD0910A8, // sw t1, CHCR: triggers the transfer
	})
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, prog)
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	m.RunCycles(100000)
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(counter); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("DMA handler count = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(60, 60); got != 0x03E0 {
		t.Errorf("DMA fill pixel = 0x%04X, want 0x03E0", got)
	}
}

// seqDisc is a synthetic cd.Reader for the system
// gates: sector LBA n is filled with the pattern
// byte(i) = byte(i>>2) + byte(n), so word w of
// sector 0 reads as 0xWWWWWWWW for w < 256.
type seqDisc struct{ sectors int }

func (d *seqDisc) Tracks() []cd.Track {
	return []cd.Track{{Number: 1, Mode: cd.TrackData, SectorSize: 2048, UserSize: 2048, Length: d.sectors}}
}
func (d *seqDisc) ReadSector(lba int, raw bool) ([]byte, error) {
	if lba < 0 || lba >= d.sectors {
		return nil, errLBA
	}
	out := make([]byte, 2048)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = byte(i>>2) + byte(lba)
	}
	return out, nil
}
func (d *seqDisc) Close() error { return nil }

var errLBA = errorString("lba out of range")

type errorString string

func (e errorString) Error() string { return string(e) }

func TestCDROMDMAGate(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	disc := &seqDisc{sectors: 16}
	if err := m.LoadDisc(disc); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	// CD: enable IRQ types, Setloc 00:02:00 (LBA 0),
	// ReadN.
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801803, 0x1F) // irq enable (index 0)
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801802, 0x00) // param mm
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801802, 0x02) // param ss
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801802, 0x00) // param ff
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801801, 0x02) // Setloc
	m.Bus.Read8(0x1F801801)        // drain response
	m.Bus.Write8(0x1F801801, 0x06) // ReadN
	// PS1-3 timing reconciliation: the full CD
	// controller delivers the first sector only after
	// its modeled settle delay plus one sector period
	// (3,000,000 + 451,584 cycles from a stopped
	// state), driven by the machine clock. Run the
	// machine past that point; the content assertions
	// below are unchanged from PS1-2.
	m.RunCycles(3_600_000)
	if m.CD.DataLen() != 2048 {
		t.Fatalf("CD data FIFO = %d bytes, want 2048", m.CD.DataLen())
	}
	if m.IStat()&(1<<IRQCDROM) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("CD IRQ did not reach I_STAT bit 2")
	}
	// DMA ch3 pulls the sector into RAM at 0x80013000.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010F0, 0x8000) // DPCR ch3 enable
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010B0, 0x80013000)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010B4, 512) // one sector of words
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010B8, 0x01000000)
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x80013000 + 12); got != 0x03030303 {
		t.Errorf("DMA word 3 = 0x%08X, want 0x03030303", got)
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x80013000 + 255*4); got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("DMA word 255 = 0x%08X, want 0xFFFFFFFF", got)
	}
}

// setupDeterminismMachine builds the determinism
// gate machine: a 4x4 15-bit texture in VRAM, a
// linked-list DMA packet holding one textured quad
// command stream, the DMA executed, and a CPU
// program spinning on timer 0 target IRQs.
func setupDeterminismMachine(t *testing.T) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	m := New()
	gp0 := func(words ...uint32) {
		for _, w := range words {
			m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, w)
		}
	}
	gp0(0xE3000000, 0xE407FFFF) // drawing area full
	// Upload the 4x4 texture (halfword i = 0x1000+i)
	// to VRAM (0,0) via a CPU to VRAM transfer.
	gp0(0xA0000000, 0x00000000, 0x00040004)
	for w := 0; w < 8; w++ {
		lo := uint32(0x1000 + 2*w)
		hi := uint32(0x1000 + 2*w + 1)
		gp0(lo | hi<<16)
	}
	// Linked list node at 0x80014000: one textured
	// quad (9 words) blended with neutral color.
	loadProg(m, 0x80014000, []uint32{
		0x09FFFFFF,             // header: 9 words, end of list
		0x2C808080,             // textured quad, color 0x808080
		0x00100010, 0x00000000, // v0 (16,16), uv0
		0x00100014, 0x01000003, // v1 (20,16), uv1 u=3 + 15-bit page
		0x00140010, 0x00000300, // v2 (16,20), uv2 v=3
		0x00140014, 0x00000303, // v3 (20,20), uv3
	})
	// GP1: DMA direction CPU to GP0; DPCR enable ch2;
	// run the linked list.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801814, 0x04000002)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010F0, 0x0800)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010A0, 0x80014000)
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F8010A8, 0x01000401)
	// The quad must already be drawn, with exact
	// texel colors (neutral modulation).
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(16, 16); got != 0x1000 {
		t.Fatalf("quad texel (0,0) = 0x%04X, want 0x1000", got)
	}
	// (19,19) interpolates to texel (2,2) under the
	// barycentric rule; (16,19) lands on texel (0,2).
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(19, 19); got != 0x100A {
		t.Fatalf("quad texel at (19,19) = 0x%04X, want 0x100A (texel 2,2)", got)
	}
	if got := m.GPU.VRAMAt(16, 19); got != 0x1008 {
		t.Fatalf("quad texel at (16,19) = 0x%04X, want 0x1008 (texel 0,2)", got)
	}
	// CPU program: timer 0 target IRQ every 5000
	// cycles, handler counts them.
	installCounterHandler(m, 0x8001200C, 0xFFFFFFEF)
	prog := spinProgram([]uint32{
		0x3C081F80, // lui t0, 0x1F80
		0x24090010, // addiu t1, zero, 16 (timer 0 mask)
		0xAD091074, // sw t1, I_MASK
		0x24091388, // addiu t1, zero, 5000
		0xAD091108, // sw t1, timer 0 target
		0x24090058, // addiu t1, zero, 0x58 (reset at target, IRQ, repeat)
		0xAD091104, // sw t1, timer 0 mode
	})
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, prog)
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	return m
}

func TestDeterminismGate(t *testing.T) {
	m := setupDeterminismMachine(t)
	m.RunCycles(60000)
	irqCount := m.Bus.Read32(0x8001200C)
	if irqCount < 5 {
		t.Fatalf("timer IRQ count after 60000 cycles = %d, want at least 5 (spinning on IRQ works)", irqCount)
	}
	mid := m.Serialize()
	m.RunCycles(30000)
	wantState := m.Serialize()
	wantFB := append([]uint32(nil), m.Framebuffer()...)
	wantCount := m.Bus.Read32(0x8001200C)

	m2 := setupDeterminismMachine(t)
	if err := m2.Deserialize(mid); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize mid-frame state: %v", err)
	}
	m2.RunCycles(30000)
	if got := m2.Bus.Read32(0x8001200C); got != wantCount {
		t.Errorf("restored IRQ count = %d, want %d", got, wantCount)
	}
	gotFB := m2.Framebuffer()
	if len(gotFB) != len(wantFB) {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer size diverged")
	}
	for i := range wantFB {
		if gotFB[i] != wantFB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d diverged: 0x%08X vs 0x%08X", i, gotFB[i], wantFB[i])
		}
	}
	if got := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Errorf("state after identical continuation diverged")
	}
}

func TestGPUInterruptSource(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	// GP0(1F) through the GP0 port latches I_STAT
	// bit 1 without any CPU step.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801810, 0x1F000000)
	if m.IStat()&(1<<IRQGPU) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("GP0 IRQ command did not latch I_STAT bit 1")
	}
	// GP1(02) clears the GPUSTAT request, I_STAT
	// stays latched until acknowledged by write.
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801814, 0x02000000)
	if m.GPU.IRQRequested() {
		t.Errorf("GP1(02) did not clear GPUSTAT irq")
	}
	m.Bus.Write32(0x1F801070, 0xFFFFFFFD)
	if m.IStat()&(1<<IRQGPU) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("I_STAT GPU bit not acked")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/system_ps3_test.go ====================

package system

// PS1-3 system gates: a full PS-X EXE enginetest that
// drives the BIOS event system, the GPU textured quad
// path, SPU ADPCM playback through DMA, a CD sector
// read through DMA with a checksum, and GTE RTPS
// projection, all from one guest program, plus a
// determinism leg across Serialize and Deserialize,
// and focused BIOS HLE unit tests.
//
// Deviations from the original slice plan, each one
// resolved in favor of the code as built (the plan
// itself instructed this):
//
//   - DMA channel enable bits in DPCR are bit 4*n+3
//     per dma.Controller.channelEnabled, so channel 4
//     (SPU) is 0x80000, not 0x10000. Channel 3 (CD) is
//     0x8000 as planned.
//   - DMA CHCR direction: dma.transferWord treats
//     CHCR bit 0 set as RAM to device, so the SPU
//     upload uses CHCR 0x01000001. The CD channel
//     moves device to RAM and uses 0x01000000 as
//     planned.
//   - The RTPS CPU word is 0x4A080001, not the draft
//     0x4A000001: chips/r3000a execCOP2 dispatches a
//     GTE command when the rs field is 0x10 or more
//     and passes the whole instruction word to the
//     GTE, whose opcode is bits 0 to 5 and whose sf
//     bit is bit 19. The draft word has sf clear,
//     which would shift the Z result; 0x4A080001 has
//     sf set, matching the documented RTPS word form
//     the gte package tests use (0x0180001 as a bare
//     command).
//   - The textured quad second vertex UV carries
//     u=16, not u=0: vertex 1 is the top right corner
//     (96,32) of a quad mapping a 16 texel wide
//     texture, and the framebuffer probes below are
//     only satisfiable with u=16 there. The texpage
//     halfword is 0x0110, matching
//     gpu.texPageFromWord: x base 0, y base bit at
//     bit 4 (VRAM y 256), color format bits 7 to 8
//     equal 2 (15-bit direct).
//   - The GP1 display enable word is written after
//     the textured quad, not before it: gpu.plot
//     suppresses any drawing into the display area
//     while the display is enabled and the E1
//     draw-to-display bit is clear, and the quad
//     covers display pixels by design. All planned
//     GP1 words are still written, in stage B.
//   - Stage markers share one word at result+0x100,
//     written with the stage number as each stage
//     completes (the plan's simpler option), because
//     per-stage slots at result+0x100+4*stage would
//     collide with the CD checksum at +0x104 and the
//     GTE results at +0x108 onward.

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/homebrew"
)

// ----------------------------------------------------------------
// The enginetest gate.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------

func ps3SX(w uint32) int { return int(int16(w & 0xFFFF)) }
func ps3SY(w uint32) int { return int(int16(w >> 16)) }

func TestPS1Enginetest(t *testing.T) {
	tone := homebrew.EncodeLoop(homebrew.SinePCM(2800, 28, 12000))
	if len(tone) != 1600 {
		t.Fatalf("tone size actual %d bytes, want 1600 (100 ADPCM blocks)", len(tone))
	}
	exe := homebrew.BuildEXE(homebrew.EngineWords(tone))

	m := New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(&seqDisc{sectors: 16}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if err := m.LoadEXE(exe); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadEXE: %v", err)
	}
	var audio []int16
	passed := false
	for chunk := 0; chunk < 40 && !passed; chunk++ {
		m.RunCycles(1000000)
		audio = append(audio, m.AudioBuffer()...)
		if m.Bus.Read32(0x80020000) == 0x600DF00D {
			passed = true
		}
	}
	if !passed {
		t.Fatalf("PASS magic not reached: stage marker actual %d, want 6; PASS word actual 0x%08X, want 0x600DF00D; unimplemented BIOS calls actual %d, want 0",
			m.Bus.Read32(0x80020100), m.Bus.Read32(0x80020000), m.UnimplementedBIOSCallCount())
	}
	// Keep the tone playing so the audio analysis
	// below has well over a second of output: the
	// looped voice keeps sounding while the guest
	// spins on its PASS loop.
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		m.RunCycles(1000000)
		audio = append(audio, m.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020100); got != 6 {
		t.Errorf("final stage marker actual %d, want 6", got)
	}
	if got := m.UnimplementedBIOSCallCount(); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("unimplemented BIOS calls actual %d, want 0 (log %v)", got, m.UnimplementedBIOSCalls())
	}

	// GPU probes: one framebuffer pixel per texture
	// quadrant.
	if w, h := m.DisplayWidth(), m.DisplayHeight(); w != 320 || h != 240 {
		t.Errorf("display size actual %dx%d, want 320x240", w, h)
	}
	fb := m.Framebuffer()
	fw := m.DisplayWidth()
	for _, p := range []struct {
		x, y int
		want uint32
	}{
		{48, 48, 0xFFFF0000},
		{80, 48, 0xFF00FF00},
		{48, 80, 0xFF0000FF},
		{80, 80, 0xFFFFFFFF},
	} {
		if got := fb[p.y*fw+p.x]; got != p.want {
			t.Errorf("framebuffer pixel (%d,%d) actual 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", p.x, p.y, got, p.want)
		}
	}

	// CD checksum: the expected sum comes straight
	// from the seqDisc sector 0 pattern, byte i
	// equal to byte(i>>2), packed little endian.
	var wantSum uint32
	for i := 0; i < 2048; i += 4 {
		var w uint32
		for k := 0; k < 4; k++ {
			w |= uint32(byte((i+k)>>2)) << (8 * k)
		}
		wantSum += w
	}
	gotSum := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020104)
	if gotSum != wantSum {
		t.Errorf("CD sector checksum actual 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", gotSum, wantSum)
	}

	// GTE results.
	sxyp1 := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020108)
	if ps3SX(sxyp1) != 160 || ps3SY(sxyp1) != 120 {
		t.Errorf("RTPS centered point actual (%d,%d), want (160,120) exactly (SXYP word 0x%08X)",
			ps3SX(sxyp1), ps3SY(sxyp1), sxyp1)
	}
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x8002010C); got != 300 {
		t.Errorf("RTPS SZ3 actual %d, want 300", got)
	}
	if flag := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020110); flag&(1<<31) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("RTPS FLAG actual 0x%08X, want bit 31 clear", flag)
	}
	sxyp2 := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020114)
	if sx, sy := ps3SX(sxyp2), ps3SY(sxyp2); sx < 223 || sx > 229 || sy < 84 || sy > 90 {
		t.Errorf("RTPS second point actual (%d,%d), want SX in [223,229] and SY in [84,90] (SXYP word 0x%08X)", sx, sy, sxyp2)
	}

	// Audio: skip the first 0.25 s, count positive
	// zero crossings on the left channel over the
	// next 0.5 s.
	pairs := len(audio) / 2
	if pairs < 11025+22050 {
		t.Fatalf("audio length actual %d sample pairs, want at least %d for the analysis window", pairs, 11025+22050)
	}
	crossings := 0
	prev := int16(0)
	for i := 0; i < 22050; i++ {
		cur := audio[2*(11025+i)]
		if i > 0 && prev < 0 && cur >= 0 {
			crossings++
		}
		prev = cur
	}
	freq := float64(crossings) / 0.5
	t.Logf("enginetest: stage marker 6, CD checksum 0x%08X, SXYP1 (%d,%d), SXYP2 (%d,%d), audio %d crossings in 0.5 s = %.1f Hz",
		gotSum, ps3SX(sxyp1), ps3SY(sxyp1), ps3SX(sxyp2), ps3SY(sxyp2), crossings, freq)
	if freq < 415 || freq > 465 {
		t.Errorf("audio frequency actual %.1f Hz, want in [415,465]", freq)
	}

	// Determinism leg: a fixed cycle run, a mid
	// Serialize, then identical continuations on the
	// original machine and on a fresh machine that
	// only Deserializes the mid state. Pending audio
	// is drained and discarded on both sides of the
	// restore point, because the serialized SPU audio
	// buffer is capped and the original machine would
	// otherwise carry a longer pending tail.
	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.LoadDisc(&seqDisc{sectors: 16}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if err := m2.LoadEXE(exe); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism LoadEXE: %v", err)
	}
	m2.RunCycles(12000000)
	mid := m2.Serialize()
	_ = m2.AudioBuffer() // discard pending, see above
	m2.RunCycles(2000000)
	audio2 := m2.AudioBuffer()
	wantState := m2.Serialize()
	wantFB := append([]uint32(nil), m2.Framebuffer()...)
	wantRes := make([]uint32, 128)
	for i := range wantRes {
		wantRes[i] = m2.Bus.Read32(0x80020000 + uint32(4*i))
	}
	if wantRes[0] != 0x600DF00D {
		t.Fatalf("determinism leg: m2 PASS word actual 0x%08X, want 0x600DF00D after 14M cycles (stage marker %d)",
			wantRes[0], m2.Bus.Read32(0x80020100))
	}

	m3 := New()
	if err := m3.LoadDisc(&seqDisc{sectors: 16}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism LoadDisc m3: %v", err)
	}
	if err := m3.Deserialize(mid); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("determinism Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	_ = m3.AudioBuffer() // discard restored pending
	m3.RunCycles(2000000)
	audio3 := m3.AudioBuffer()
	if len(audio3) != len(audio2) {
		t.Fatalf("determinism audio length actual %d, want %d", len(audio3), len(audio2))
	}
	for i := range audio2 {
		if audio3[i] != audio2[i] {
			t.Fatalf("determinism audio sample %d actual %d, want %d", i, audio3[i], audio2[i])
		}
	}
	if got := m3.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Errorf("determinism state after identical continuation diverged: actual %d bytes vs want %d bytes, byte equal false", len(got), len(wantState))
		for i := range wantState {
			if got[i] != wantState[i] {
				t.Logf("first divergent state byte at offset %d: actual 0x%02X, want 0x%02X", i, got[i], wantState[i])
				break
			}
		}
	}
	gotFB := m3.Framebuffer()
	if len(gotFB) != len(wantFB) {
		t.Fatalf("determinism framebuffer size actual %d, want %d", len(gotFB), len(wantFB))
	}
	for i := range wantFB {
		if gotFB[i] != wantFB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("determinism framebuffer pixel %d actual 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", i, gotFB[i], wantFB[i])
		}
	}
	for i := range wantRes {
		if got := m3.Bus.Read32(0x80020000 + uint32(4*i)); got != wantRes[i] {
			t.Fatalf("determinism result word %d actual 0x%08X, want 0x%08X", i, got, wantRes[i])
		}
	}
	t.Logf("determinism: state bytes equal %v, audio samples after restore %d, framebuffer pixels %d",
		bytes.Equal(m3.Serialize(), wantState), len(audio2), len(wantFB))
}

func TestBIOSUnimplementedLogged(t *testing.T) {
	a := homebrew.NewAsm()
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0)
	a.Li(homebrew.A1, 0)
	a.Li(homebrew.A2, 0)
	a.Li(homebrew.A3, 0)
	a.CallBIOS(0xA0, 0x7F) // unimplemented A function
	a.Lui(homebrew.T0, 0x8002)
	a.Sw(homebrew.V0, 0x210, homebrew.T0)
	a.Spin("spin")
	m := New()
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, a.Build(0x80010000))
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	m.RunCycles(10000)
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020210); got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("unimplemented call return actual 0x%08X, want 0xFFFFFFFF", got)
	}
	if got := m.UnimplementedBIOSCallCount(); got < 1 {
		t.Fatalf("unimplemented call count actual %d, want at least 1", got)
	}
	calls := m.UnimplementedBIOSCalls()
	if len(calls) < 1 {
		t.Fatalf("unimplemented call log length actual %d, want at least 1", len(calls))
	}
	if calls[0].Table != 'A' || calls[0].Func != 0x7F {
		t.Errorf("unimplemented call log entry actual {%c, 0x%02X}, want {A, 0x7F}", calls[0].Table, calls[0].Func)
	}
}

func TestBIOSCallbackEvent(t *testing.T) {
	a := homebrew.NewAsm()
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0xF0000001)
	a.Li(homebrew.A1, 0x1000)
	a.Li(homebrew.A2, 0x1000) // callback mode
	a.LiLabel(homebrew.A3, "callback")
	a.CallBIOS(0xB0, 0x08) // OpenEvent
	a.Addu(homebrew.S1, homebrew.V0, homebrew.Zero)
	a.Addu(homebrew.A0, homebrew.S1, homebrew.Zero)
	a.CallBIOS(0xB0, 0x0C)        // EnableEvent
	a.StoreWordAbs(0x1F801074, 1) // I_MASK = VBlank
	a.Label("spin")
	a.Lui(homebrew.T2, 0x8002)
	a.Lw(homebrew.T0, 0x204, homebrew.T2)
	a.Nop() // load delay
	a.Addiu(homebrew.T0, homebrew.T0, 1)
	a.Sw(homebrew.T0, 0x204, homebrew.T2)
	a.Beq(homebrew.Zero, homebrew.Zero, "spin")
	a.Nop()
	for a.Len() < 64 {
		a.Nop()
	}
	a.Label("callback") // at 0x80010100
	a.Lui(homebrew.T0, 0x8002)
	a.Lw(homebrew.T1, 0x200, homebrew.T0)
	a.Nop() // load delay
	a.Addiu(homebrew.T1, homebrew.T1, 1)
	a.Sw(homebrew.T1, 0x200, homebrew.T0)
	a.Jr(homebrew.RA)
	a.Nop()
	m := New()
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, a.Build(0x80010000))
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		m.RunFrame()
	}
	got := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020200)
	t.Logf("callback event: counter %d after 3 frames", got)
	if got < 2 {
		t.Errorf("callback counter actual %d, want at least 2 after 3 frames", got)
	}
	h1 := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020204)
	m.RunCycles(100000)
	h2 := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020204)
	if h2 == h1 {
		t.Errorf("main spin heartbeat actual %d after more cycles, want a value different from %d (spin still alive)", h2, h1)
	}
}

func TestBIOSSetRCntRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	a := homebrew.NewAsm()
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0)
	a.Li(homebrew.A1, 1234)
	a.Li(homebrew.A2, 0x0058)
	a.CallBIOS(0xC0, 0x19) // SetRCnt(0, 1234, 0x0058)
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0)
	a.CallBIOS(0xC0, 0x1A) // GetRCnt(0)
	a.Lui(homebrew.T0, 0x8002)
	a.Sw(homebrew.V0, 0x220, homebrew.T0)
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0)
	a.CallBIOS(0xC0, 0x1B) // ResetRCnt(0)
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0)
	a.CallBIOS(0xC0, 0x1A) // GetRCnt(0)
	a.Lui(homebrew.T0, 0x8002)
	a.Sw(homebrew.V0, 0x224, homebrew.T0)
	a.Spin("spin")
	m := New()
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, a.Build(0x80010000))
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	m.RunCycles(10000)
	if got := m.Timers.T[0].Target; got != 1234 {
		t.Errorf("timer 0 target actual %d, want 1234", got)
	}
	if got := m.Timers.T[0].Mode; got != 0x0058 {
		t.Errorf("timer 0 mode actual 0x%04X, want 0x0058", got)
	}
	first := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020220)
	second := m.Bus.Read32(0x80020224)
	t.Logf("SetRCnt round trip: first GetRCnt %d, second GetRCnt after reset %d", first, second)
	if first > 1234 {
		t.Errorf("first GetRCnt actual %d, want at most 1234", first)
	}
	if !(second < first || second < 100) {
		t.Errorf("second GetRCnt actual %d, want less than first (%d) or less than 100", second, first)
	}
}

func TestBIOSInitPAD2Fill(t *testing.T) {
	a := homebrew.NewAsm()
	a.Li(homebrew.A0, 0x80020300)
	a.Li(homebrew.A1, 0x22)
	a.Li(homebrew.A2, 0x80020340)
	a.Li(homebrew.A3, 0x22)
	a.CallBIOS(0xB0, 0x12) // InitPAD2
	a.CallBIOS(0xB0, 0x13) // StartPAD2
	a.Spin("spin")
	m := New()
	loadProg(m, 0x80010000, a.Build(0x80010000))
	setPC(m, 0x80010000)
	m.SetButtons(ButtonStart | ButtonCross)
	m.RunFrame()
	m.RunFrame()
	for _, c := range []struct {
		addr uint32
		want uint8
	}{
		{0x80020300, 0x00}, // port 1 status okay
		{0x80020301, 0x41}, // digital pad ID
		{0x80020302, 0xF7}, // low buttons: Start is bit 3, byte = ^0x08
		{0x80020303, 0xBF}, // high buttons: Cross is bit 14, byte = ^0x40
		{0x80020340, 0xFF}, // port 2: no device
	} {
		if got := m.Bus.Read8(c.addr); got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("PAD buffer byte at 0x%08X actual 0x%02X, want 0x%02X", c.addr, got, c.want)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/system/system_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func rI(op, rs, rt, imm uint32) uint32 { return op<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | (imm & 0xFFFF) }
func rR(rs, rt, rd, sh, fn uint32) uint32 {
	return rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | sh<<6 | fn
}

const (
	t0 = 8
	t1 = 9
	t2 = 10
	t3 = 11
	t4 = 12
	t5 = 13
	t6 = 14
)

// checksumProgram sums 16 words at 0x80011000 into
// 0x80012000, then spins. Register plan: t0 = base
// 0x80010000, t1 = count, t2 = sum, t3 = i.
func checksumProgram() []uint32 {
	return []uint32{
		rI(0x0F, 0, t0, 0x8001),  // lui t0, 0x8001
		rI(0x09, 0, t1, 16),      // addiu t1, 16
		rI(0x09, 0, t2, 0),       // addiu t2, 0
		rI(0x09, 0, t3, 0),       // addiu t3, 0
		rR(0, t3, t5, 2, 0x00),   // loop: sll t5, t3, 2
		rR(t0, t5, t6, 0, 0x21),  // addu t6, t0, t5
		rI(0x23, t6, t4, 0x1000), // lw t4, 0x1000(t6)
		0,                        // nop (load delay)
		rR(t2, t4, t2, 0, 0x21),  // addu t2, t2, t4
		rI(0x09, t3, t3, 1),      // addiu t3, 1
		rI(0x05, t3, t1, 0xFFF9), // bne t3, t1, loop (-7)
		0,                        // nop
		rI(0x2B, t0, t2, 0x2000), // sw t2, 0x2000(t0)
		rI(0x04, 0, 0, 0xFFFF),   // spin: beq zero, zero, -1
		0,                        // nop
	}
}

func loadChecksumMachine(t *testing.T) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	m := New()
	for i, w := range checksumProgram() {
		m.Bus.Write32(0x80010000+4*uint32(i), w)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		m.Bus.Write32(0x80011000+4*uint32(i), uint32(i+1))
	}
	m.CPU.PC = 0x80010000
	m.CPU.NextPC = 0x80010004
	return m
}

func TestSyntheticChecksumAndSaveState(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadChecksumMachine(t)
	for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
		m.Step()
	}
	save := m.Serialize()
	if len(save) != m.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(save), m.StateSize())
	}
	m.RunCycles(2000)
	result := m.Bus.Read32(0x80012000)
	if result != 136 {
		t.Fatalf("checksum = %d, want 136 (sum of 1..16)", result)
	}
	finalState := m.Serialize()

	m2 := New()
	if err := m2.Deserialize(save); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	m2.RunCycles(2000)
	if got := m2.Bus.Read32(0x80012000); got != result {
		t.Errorf("restored checksum = %d, want %d", got, result)
	}
	if m2.CPU.Regs != m.CPU.Regs {
		t.Errorf("registers diverged after restore")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(m2.Serialize(), finalState) {
		t.Errorf("full state diverged after restore and identical continuation")
	}
}

func TestMachineBasics(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	// PS1-2 contract change: the framebuffer is the
	// GPU display area at native resolution (the
	// documented reset default is 256x240, display
	// off), not the fixed 640x480 blank of PS1-1.
	fb := m.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) != m.DisplayWidth()*m.DisplayHeight() {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer = %d pixels, want %d (native display)", len(fb), m.DisplayWidth()*m.DisplayHeight())
	}
	if fb[0] != 0xFF000000 || fb[len(fb)-1] != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Errorf("framebuffer not blank black")
	}
	m.SetButtons(ButtonStart | ButtonCross)
	if m.Buttons() != ButtonStart|ButtonCross {
		t.Errorf("Buttons = 0x%X, want 0x%X", m.Buttons(), uint32(ButtonStart|ButtonCross))
	}
	if err := m.LoadDisc(nil); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("LoadDisc(nil) accepted, want error")
	}
	if err := m.Deserialize([]byte{1}); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("short state accepted, want error")
	}
	bad := m.Serialize()
	bad[0] = 99
	if err := m.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("bad version state accepted, want error")
	}
}

func TestRunFrameBudget(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	m.RunFrame()
	if m.Frames() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("Frames = %d, want 1", m.Frames())
	}
	// NTSC frame budget: 33,868,800 / 59.94 = 565,045.04
	// cycles; RunCycles may overshoot by one instruction.
	c := m.CPU.Cycles()
	if c < 565045 || c > 565045+8 {
		t.Errorf("frame consumed %d CPU cycles, want about 565045", c)
	}
}

func TestOpenDiscFromFile(t *testing.T) {
	p := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "flat.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, make([]byte, 2048*20), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m := New()
	if err := m.OpenDisc(p); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if m.Disc == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Disc is nil after OpenDisc")
	}
	tracks := m.Disc.Tracks()
	if len(tracks) != 1 || tracks[0].Length != 20 {
		t.Errorf("tracks = %+v, want one 20-sector track", tracks)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-ps1/timers/timers.go ====================

// Package timers implements the three PlayStation
// root counters (timers 0, 1 and 2) from the psx-spx
// timer documentation.
//
// Each timer has a 16-bit counter, a mode register
// and a 16-bit target. The mode register layout:
//
//	bit 0     synchronization enable
//	bits 1-2  synchronization mode
//	bit 3     reset counter at target (else at 0xFFFF)
//	bit 4     IRQ when counter reaches target
//	bit 5     IRQ when counter reaches 0xFFFF
//	bit 6     IRQ once / repeatedly
//	bit 7     IRQ pulse / toggle
//	bits 8-9  clock source
//	bit 10    interrupt request, INVERTED: reads 0
//	          while a request is pending, 1 when idle;
//	          set back to 1 by any mode write
//	bit 11    reached target (cleared by reading mode)
//	bit 12    reached 0xFFFF (cleared by reading mode)
//
// Clock sources: timer 0 takes the system clock or
// the GPU dotclock; timer 1 the system clock or the
// hblank pulse train; timer 2 the system clock or
// the system clock divided by 8.
//
// Synchronization modes (bit 0 set): timer 0 syncs
// to hblank, timer 1 to vblank:
//
//	0  pause the counter during blanking
//	1  reset the counter to 0 at each blank pulse
//	2  reset at each pulse and count only while the
//	   blanking signal is active
//	3  pause until the first pulse, then free run
//
// Timer 2 with synchronization enabled stops forever
// in modes 0 and 3 and free runs in modes 1 and 2.
//
// The timers do not own a clock: the system feeds
// elapsed ticks through Advance, computed from the
// machine cycle position, so counter readback is
// exact for a given number of consumed ticks. IRQ
// delivery is reported as events: in pulse mode an
// IRQ condition asserts the output once; in toggle
// mode the INTF bit flips per condition and the
// output asserts only on the 1-to-0 flip, matching
// the documented behavior.
package timers

// Count is the number of root counters.
const Count = 3

// Inputs carries the tick sources for one Advance
// call, all measured over the same elapsed interval.
// InHBlank and InVBlank describe the blanking state
// during the interval (sampled at its start); sync
// modes that pause use them, and sync resets use the
// pulse counts.
type Inputs struct {
	SysCycles   int  // system clock ticks
	DotTicks    int  // GPU dotclock ticks (timer 0)
	HBlankPulse int  // hblank pulses (timer 1 clock, timer 0 sync)
	VBlankPulse int  // vblank pulses (timer 1 sync)
	InHBlank    bool // hblank active during the interval
	InVBlank    bool // vblank active during the interval
}

// Timer is one root counter.
type Timer struct {
	Counter uint16
	Mode    uint16 // stored control bits 0-9
	Target  uint16

	intf          bool // mode bit 10 as read: true = no request pending
	reachedTarget bool
	reachedFFFF   bool
	oneShotUsed   bool
	sync3Armed    bool // sync mode 3 has seen its first pulse
	div8Rem       int  // timer 2 clock divider remainder
}

// Timers is the set of three root counters.
type Timers struct {
	T [Count]Timer
}

// New returns the timers in reset state.
func New() *Timers {
	t := &Timers{}
	t.Reset()
	return t
}

// Reset clears all counters and modes.
func (t *Timers) Reset() {
	for i := range t.T {
		t.T[i] = Timer{intf: true}
	}
}

// WriteCounter sets a counter's current value.
func (t *Timers) WriteCounter(i int, v uint16) { t.T[i].Counter = v }

// WriteTarget sets a counter's target value.
func (t *Timers) WriteTarget(i int, v uint16) { t.T[i].Target = v }

// WriteMode stores a mode register value. Per the
// documentation, writing the mode resets the counter
// to zero, sets INTF back to "no request", clears
// the reached flags and re-arms one-shot IRQ
// delivery and sync mode 3.
func (t *Timers) WriteMode(i int, v uint16) {
	tm := &t.T[i]
	tm.Mode = v & 0x03FF
	tm.Counter = 0
	tm.intf = true
	tm.reachedTarget = false
	tm.reachedFFFF = false
	tm.oneShotUsed = false
	tm.sync3Armed = false
	tm.div8Rem = 0
}

// ReadMode returns the mode register as the CPU sees
// it (stored bits, live INTF, reached flags) and
// then clears the two reached flags, per the
// documented read-and-clear behavior.
func (t *Timers) ReadMode(i int) uint16 {
	tm := &t.T[i]
	v := tm.Mode
	if tm.intf {
		v |= 1 << 10
	}
	if tm.reachedTarget {
		v |= 1 << 11
	}
	if tm.reachedFFFF {
		v |= 1 << 12
	}
	tm.reachedTarget = false
	tm.reachedFFFF = false
	return v
}

// syncGate decides, for timer i, whether source
// ticks pass this interval and applies sync resets
// from the pulse counts in in.
func (t *Timers) syncGate(i int, in Inputs) bool {
	tm := &t.T[i]
	if tm.Mode&0x0001 == 0 {
		return true // synchronization disabled: free run
	}
	mode := (tm.Mode >> 1) & 3
	if i == 2 {
		// Timer 2: modes 0 and 3 stop forever, modes
		// 1 and 2 free run.
		return mode == 1 || mode == 2
	}
	pulses := in.HBlankPulse
	inBlank := in.InHBlank
	if i == 1 {
		pulses = in.VBlankPulse
		inBlank = in.InVBlank
	}
	switch mode {
	case 0: // pause during blanking
		return !inBlank
	case 1: // reset at each pulse, else free
		if pulses > 0 {
			tm.Counter = 0
		}
		return true
	case 2: // reset at each pulse, count only in blanking
		if pulses > 0 {
			tm.Counter = 0
		}
		return inBlank
	case 3: // pause until first pulse, then free run
		if pulses > 0 {
			tm.sync3Armed = true
		}
		return tm.sync3Armed
	}
	return true
}

// sourceTicks selects the tick count for timer i
// from the interval inputs, applying timer 2's
// divide-by-8 with its remainder.
func (t *Timers) sourceTicks(i int, in Inputs) int {
	tm := &t.T[i]
	src := (tm.Mode >> 8) & 3
	switch i {
	case 0:
		if src == 1 || src == 3 {
			return in.DotTicks
		}
		return in.SysCycles
	case 1:
		if src == 1 || src == 3 {
			return in.HBlankPulse
		}
		return in.SysCycles
	default: // timer 2
		if src == 2 || src == 3 {
			total := tm.div8Rem + in.SysCycles
			tm.div8Rem = total % 8
			return total / 8
		}
		return in.SysCycles
	}
}

// irq fires one IRQ condition on timer tm and
// reports whether the timer's interrupt output
// asserts (pulse mode: always; toggle mode: only
// when INTF flips 1 to 0). One-shot mode suppresses
// every condition after the first until the mode
// register is written again.
func (tm *Timer) irq() bool {
	if tm.Mode&0x0040 == 0 && tm.oneShotUsed {
		return false
	}
	tm.oneShotUsed = true
	if tm.Mode&0x0080 != 0 { // toggle
		tm.intf = !tm.intf
		return !tm.intf
	}
	// Pulse: the request shows in INTF until the
	// condition passes; the output asserts once.
	tm.intf = false
	return true
}

// tick advances timer i by one source tick, applying
// target/overflow rules, and reports an asserted
// interrupt output.
func (t *Timers) tick(i int) bool {
	tm := &t.T[i]
	nc := uint32(tm.Counter) + 1
	wrapped := nc > 0xFFFF
	if wrapped {
		nc = 0
	}
	assert := false
	targetHit := tm.Target != 0 && !wrapped && uint16(nc) == tm.Target
	if tm.Target == 0 && wrapped && tm.Mode&0x0008 != 0 {
		// Target 0 with reset-at-target behaves as a
		// period of 0x10000 ticks.
		targetHit = true
	}
	if targetHit {
		tm.reachedTarget = true
		if tm.Mode&0x0010 != 0 && tm.irq() {
			assert = true
		}
		if tm.Mode&0x0008 != 0 {
			tm.Counter = 0
			return assert
		}
	}
	if !wrapped && nc == 0xFFFF {
		tm.reachedFFFF = true
		if tm.Mode&0x0020 != 0 && tm.irq() {
			assert = true
		}
	}
	tm.Counter = uint16(nc)
	return assert
}

// Advance feeds one interval of ticks to all timers
// and returns a bitmask of the timers whose
// interrupt output asserted during the interval
// (bit i = timer i), for the interrupt controller.
func (t *Timers) Advance(in Inputs) uint32 {
	var asserted uint32
	for i := 0; i < Count; i++ {
		if !t.syncGate(i, in) {
			continue
		}
		n := t.sourceTicks(i, in)
		for k := 0; k < n; k++ {
			if t.tick(i) {
				asserted |= 1 << uint(i)
			}
		}
		if t.T[i].Mode&0x0080 == 0 {
			// Pulse mode: the INTF dip is momentary
			// (a few clocks on hardware); by the end of
			// the interval it reads idle again. The
			// assertion event above is what the
			// interrupt controller latches.
			t.T[i].intf = true
		}
	}
	return asserted
}

// TimerStateSize is the serialized size of one timer.
const TimerStateSize = 16

// Serialize writes the full timer set state.
func (t *Timers) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, Count*TimerStateSize)
	for i := range t.T {
		tm := &t.T[i]
		o := out[i*TimerStateSize:]
		put16(o[0:], tm.Counter)
		put16(o[2:], tm.Mode)
		put16(o[4:], tm.Target)
		put16(o[6:], uint16(tm.div8Rem))
		flags := byte(0)
		if tm.intf {
			flags |= 1
		}
		if tm.reachedTarget {
			flags |= 2
		}
		if tm.reachedFFFF {
			flags |= 4
		}
		if tm.oneShotUsed {
			flags |= 8
		}
		if tm.sync3Armed {
			flags |= 16
		}
		o[8] = flags
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (t *Timers) Deserialize(in []byte) {
	for i := range t.T {
		tm := &t.T[i]
		o := in[i*TimerStateSize:]
		tm.Counter = get16(o[0:])
		tm.Mode = get16(o[2:])
		tm.Target = get16(o[4:])
		tm.div8Rem = int(get16(o[6:]))
		f := o[8]
		tm.intf = f&1 != 0
		tm.reachedTarget = f&2 != 0
		tm.reachedFFFF = f&4 != 0
		tm.oneShotUsed = f&8 != 0
		tm.sync3Armed = f&16 != 0
	}
}

// StateSize is the serialized size of the timer set.
func StateSize() int { return Count * TimerStateSize }

func put16(b []byte, v uint16) { b[0], b[1] = byte(v), byte(v>>8) }
func get16(b []byte) uint16    { return uint16(b[0]) | uint16(b[1])<<8 }

package timers

import "testing"

func sysTicks(n int) Inputs { return Inputs{SysCycles: n} }

func TestFreeRunCounterExact(t *testing.T) {
	tm := New()
	tm.WriteMode(2, 0x0000) // system clock, free run
	if got := tm.Advance(sysTicks(1000)); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("asserted = %b, want 0", got)
	}
	if tm.T[2].Counter != 1000 {
		t.Errorf("counter = %d, want 1000", tm.T[2].Counter)
	}
	tm.Advance(sysTicks(64536))
	if tm.T[2].Counter != 0 {
		t.Errorf("counter after wrap = %d, want 0", tm.T[2].Counter)
	}
	m := tm.ReadMode(2)
	if m&(1<<12) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("reachedFFFF not set after wrap: mode %04X", m)
	}
	if m2 := tm.ReadMode(2); m2&(1<<12) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("reachedFFFF not cleared by read: mode %04X", m2)
	}
}

func TestTargetResetPeriodExact(t *testing.T) {
	tm := New()
	// Timer 2: reset at target, IRQ at target, repeat, pulse.
	tm.WriteMode(2, 0x0008|0x0010|0x0040)
	tm.WriteTarget(2, 100)
	periods := 0
	for p := 0; p < 10; p++ {
		a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(100))
		if a != 1<<2 {
			t.Fatalf("period %d: asserted = %b, want timer2", p, a)
		}
		if tm.T[2].Counter != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("period %d: counter = %d, want 0 after reset", p, tm.T[2].Counter)
		}
		periods++
	}
	if periods != 10 {
		t.Fatalf("periods = %d, want 10", periods)
	}
	// A partial interval leaves the exact remainder.
	tm.Advance(sysTicks(37))
	if tm.T[2].Counter != 37 {
		t.Errorf("counter = %d, want 37", tm.T[2].Counter)
	}
	m := tm.ReadMode(2)
	if m&(1<<11) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("reachedTarget not set: mode %04X", m)
	}
	if m&(1<<10) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("INTF should read idle (1) in pulse mode after the interval: mode %04X", m)
	}
}

func TestOneShotSuppressesSecondIRQ(t *testing.T) {
	tm := New()
	tm.WriteMode(0, 0x0008|0x0010) // one-shot (bit 6 clear)
	tm.WriteTarget(0, 10)
	if a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(10)); a != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("first target: asserted = %b, want timer0", a)
	}
	if a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(10)); a != 0 {
		t.Errorf("second target in one-shot: asserted = %b, want 0", a)
	}
	// A mode write re-arms one-shot delivery.
	tm.WriteMode(0, 0x0008|0x0010)
	tm.WriteTarget(0, 10)
	if a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(10)); a != 1 {
		t.Errorf("after mode rewrite: asserted = %b, want timer0", a)
	}
}

func TestToggleModeAssertsEverySecondCondition(t *testing.T) {
	tm := New()
	tm.WriteMode(1, 0x0008|0x0010|0x0040|0x0080) // repeat + toggle
	tm.WriteTarget(1, 5)
	if a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(5)); a != 1<<1 {
		t.Fatalf("first toggle: asserted = %b, want timer1 (INTF 1 to 0)", a)
	}
	if a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(5)); a != 0 {
		t.Errorf("second toggle: asserted = %b, want 0 (INTF 0 to 1)", a)
	}
	if a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(5)); a != 1<<1 {
		t.Errorf("third toggle: asserted = %b, want timer1", a)
	}
}

func TestSyncMode3WaitsForFirstPulse(t *testing.T) {

	tm.Advance(sysTicks(100))
	if tm.T[1].Counter != 0 {
		t.Errorf("counter = %d, want 0 before first vblank", tm.T[1].Counter)
	}
	tm.Advance(Inputs{SysCycles: 50, VBlankPulse: 1})
	if tm.T[1].Counter != 50 {
		t.Errorf("counter = %d, want 50 after arming pulse", tm.T[1].Counter)
	}

func TestTimer2SyncStop(t *testing.T) {
	tm := New()
	tm.WriteMode(2, 0x0001) // sync enable, mode 0: stop forever
	tm.Advance(sysTicks(10000))
	if tm.T[2].Counter != 0 {
		t.Errorf("counter = %d, want 0 (stopped)", tm.T[2].Counter)
	}
	tm.WriteMode(2, 0x0001|0x0002) // mode 1: free run
	tm.Advance(sysTicks(25))
	if tm.T[2].Counter != 25 {
		t.Errorf("counter = %d, want 25 (free run)", tm.T[2].Counter)
	}
}

func TestModeWriteResetsCounter(t *testing.T) {
	tm := New()
	tm.Advance(sysTicks(777))
	if tm.T[0].Counter != 777 {
		t.Fatalf("counter = %d, want 777", tm.T[0].Counter)
	}
	tm.WriteMode(0, 0)
	if tm.T[0].Counter != 0 {
		t.Errorf("counter = %d after mode write, want 0 (documented reset)", tm.T[0].Counter)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	tm := New()
	tm.WriteMode(0, 0x0008|0x0010|0x0040)
	tm.WriteTarget(0, 55)
	tm.WriteMode(2, 0x0200)
	tm.Advance(Inputs{SysCycles: 1234, DotTicks: 42})
	s := tm.Serialize()
	if len(s) != StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(s), StateSize())
	}
	tm2 := New()
	tm2.Deserialize(s)
	if tm2.T != tm.T {
		t.Errorf("timers diverged after round trip")
	}
	// Continuation must be identical.
	a := tm.Advance(sysTicks(100))
	b := tm2.Advance(sysTicks(100))
	if a != b || tm2.T != tm.T {
		t.Errorf("continuation diverged: asserted %b vs %b", a, b)
	}
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/README.md ====================

# go-psp: a from-scratch Go PSP core

A PlayStation Portable emulator core written in Go from published
documentation (the MIPS32 architecture manuals and the PSP hardware
documentation written by the homebrew community). No Sony code, firmware,
BIOS or module dumps are used anywhere in this project, and no game data
is decrypted: PGD-encrypted content is out of scope.

PSP software is an operating environment, not a bare ROM. The eventual
game path for this core is HLE of the PSP kernel and syscalls (slice
PSP-3), the same approach the homebrew toolchain targets, not a
low-level boot of Sony firmware.

## Status: COMPLETE (PSP-4: sceAudio, libretro shell, enginetest)

PSP-1 delivered the CPU, memory, media foundations and the machine
skeleton (kept below). PSP-2 added the VFPU and the GE (kept below,
with corrections in the PSP-3 section). PSP-3 adds the software
environment homebrew actually runs against:

- `load`: the ELF32/PRX module loader (audited, see below).
- `kernel`: the HLE kernel: UID objects, memory partitions, a
  cooperative thread scheduler over one shared Allegrex CPU, sync
  objects, delays and vblank, and the syscall registry the loader's
  stubs dispatch into.
- `system` kernel mode: `LoadExecutable(data)` boots an ELF or PRX
  into the kernel; states version 3 carry the kernel in kernel mode.
- PSP-4 completes the core: the sceAudio HLE and mixed output
  drain, the Media Engine decision (not emulated, documented in
  the PSP-4 section), the libretro shell, the synthetic
  bootable-ISO enginetest, and the app wiring prep.

### Loader audit outcome (PSP-3)

The pre-existing loader was audited against the uofw PRX
documentation and the corpus binaries. Two real bugs were found and
fixed: the stub table pointer names the first stub directly (stub j
is the 8 bytes at funcTable + 8j, a JR $ra word plus the syscall
word the kernel patches at StubAddr+4; the old code misread the
table), and the probe extent for ET_EXEC was computed wrong (now the
max segment end minus the min vaddr). Relocation r_info carries
three fields (type bits 0..7, OFS_BASE bits 8..15, ADDR_BASE bits
16..23) and all three are honored; the supported types are
R_MIPS_32, R_MIPS_26, R_MIPS_HI16/LO16 (with the documented AHL
addend combination), and R_MIPS_GPREL16 (validated and skipped: GP
relative entries are invariant under a uniform base shift). Any
other type is a load error naming the type. The loader was then
exonerated against a real corpus PRX by an independent Python ELF
parse: all 11 relocation sections of cpu_alu.prx use only the
modeled forms, and loaded memory matches the file word for word.
Unknown NIDs load fine; calling one returns SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_ERROR
(0x80020001, the model value) and is recorded in
`Kernel.UnknownCalls()` with module and NID. Loader tests are
synthetic ET_EXEC and PRX generators (including the HI16/LO16
sign-carry case) in `load/load_test.go`.

### Kernel model (PSP-3)

- UIDs: a sequential counter with a kind tag in the low byte
  (thread 0x01, sema 0x02, mutex 0x03, eventflag 0x04, memblock
  0x05, callback 0x06, lwmutex 0x07; the first object is 0x101).
- Partitions: user partition 2 at 0x08800000, 24 MB, first-fit with
  256-byte rounding; module images load at partition base + 0x4000
  (the load reserve the corpus binaries' layout requires).
- Threads: one Allegrex CPU time-shared across threads; the full
  CPU state (including the VFPU) is swapped per dispatch. New
  threads start with Status = CU1 | 0x11 and FCSR 0x00000E00.
  Cooperative scheduler: switches on blocking HLE calls and yields,
  reschedules on a higher-priority wakeup, documented
  10,000-instruction timeslice. When every runnable thread blocks,
  time fast-forwards to the next delay deadline or the frame end.
  `RunFrame` consumes its cycle budget across all threads, then
  delivers vblank (waiters wake in priority order, frame counter
  per frame).
- Sync objects: semaphores (microsecond timeouts converted at
  222 MHz), mutexes (recursive per attribute), event flags (AND/OR
  wait modes and clear modes), and the LwMutex family, whose lock
  state lives in a 32-byte guest workarea in the documented layout.
- Delays are microseconds (sceKernelDelayThread) and SysClock counts
  (sceKernelDelaySysClockThread; the SysClock unit is the
  microsecond count read from the cycle counter). The RTC tick is
  62135596800000000 plus the SysClock microseconds, so the clock
  boots at the Unix epoch.
- Boot: the main thread is "root", priority 0x20, 256 KB stack;
  a0 = 5 (the length of "umd0:"), a1 = the boot path string in the
  partition, $gp from the module info, $ra = 0 (the exit
  trampoline). Model values: devkit version 0x06060010 (firmware
  6.60), total memory 32 MB, sceGeEdramGetAddr returns 0x04000000,
  CPU clock 222 MHz.
- Console and IO: sceKernelPrintf (format subset %d %i %u %x %X %c
  %s %p %% with width and zero padding) and fd 1/2 writes go to the
  kernel console buffer. The virtual FS routes umd0:/disc0:
  read-only to the mounted ISO, ms0: and host0: to an in-memory
  store (`system.SetMemoryStickFiles`; host0: is the psplink device
  the corpus framework writes its output file to). The Stdio fd
  getters return 0/1/2 under their legacy (pre-SHA-1) NIDs.

### HLE coverage (PSP-3)

Registered (module, NID) handlers: ThreadManForUser thread set
(Create, Start, Exit, ExitDelete, Delete, GetThreadId,
ReferThreadStatus subset, RotateThreadReadyQueue), delays,
semaphores, mutexes, event flags, callbacks (registered, never
dispatched), LwMutex under both Kernel_Library and
ThreadManForUser; SysMemForUser partition allocation set and
memory queries; the time/RTC/power queries; LoadExecForUser exit
(sceKernelExitGame, and sceKernelSelfStopUnloadModule registered as
exit in the documented single-module approximation); StdioForUser
printf and the fd getters; IoFileMgrForUser (Open, Read, Write,
Close, Lseek, Getstat over the virtual FS; sceIoDevctl returns
invalid argument); sceCtrl (buffer reads/peeks fill SceCtrlData
from the host input state; sampling mode stored); sceDisplay
(SetMode stored, SetFrameBuf routed to the system display,
WaitVblankStart, GetVcount, IsVblank); sceGE (ListEnQueue executes
through the system GE synchronously, ListSync, DrawSync, Break,
EdramGetAddr); scePower (222 MHz, PowerTick no-op); sceRtc tick
queries; sceUtilityGetSystemParamInt (writes 0, returns 0); cache
writeback/invalidate calls are no-op successes. Anything else takes
the unknown-NID path (logged, error returned).

### States (PSP-3)

Version 3 = the version 2 body plus the kernel blob (objects,
partitions, thread contexts, console, sysclock), written only in
kernel mode. A fresh machine serializes to 35,674,041 bytes in
non-kernel mode (version 2) and 35,677,402 bytes just after a
kernel boot (version 3). Version 2 states still load in non-kernel
mode; a version 2 state loaded into a kernel-mode machine is
rejected, version 1 is rejected everywhere. Kernel state
serialization is deterministic: the round trip is byte-identical,
pinned by test.

### Synthetic gates (PSP-3, all pass)

Generator-built ET_EXEC and PRX binaries (hand-assembled MIPS)
cover: (a) hello: printf plus IoWrite emit exactly
"vfpu=1073741824,1077936128,0,0\nhello io\n"; (b) threads: two
priorities sharing a semaphore-guarded counter, console exactly
"start\ncount=2000 sum=95 len=10\n" with the trace order asserted;
(c) a 1,000 microsecond delay and a vblank waiter waking in the
asserted order across frames; (d) a synthetic ISO whose DATA.BIN
checksum the guest prints and matches; (e) a relocatable PRX
(HI16/LO16/R_MIPS_32) loading at 0x08804000, printing through a
resolved stub; (f) determinism: save mid-run, restore, byte
identical console and state; (g) an unknown NID returning the
logged error with the end marker printed; (h) mutex/eventflag/
partition semantics printing exactly
"mx 0 0 800201c5\nev 800201a8 800201af 0\npat 0 res 3\n".

### pspautotests corpus (PSP-3)

The open pspautotests suite is present locally (gitignored, never
committed) and wired through a presence-gated harness. Results
(byte compare after line-ending normalization):

- cpu_alu: 4/4 PASS (the gating group).
- fpu: 6/7. fpu_branch_hazard fails on one line: a bc1f in the
  delay slot of a compare reads the new FCC here; hardware reads
  the stale one. Documented pipeline hazard gap.
- icache: 0/1 on the tail byte only: the content lines match; the
  expected file ends without a trailing newline, a capture
  artifact of the original recording (the same artifact appears
  in lsu). Separately, the machine is cache coherent by
  construction, so cache-maintenance measurements cannot match.
- lsu: 1/3 (llsc passes). lsu's content matches to the same
  trailing-newline artifact; cacheop measures the cache model
  above.
- vfpu: 11/26 pass outright (callout, colors, convert,
  convert_scaled, minmax, minmax_tie, minmax_zero, overlap,
  prefix_branch, prefix_ctrl, vbranch). The other 15 fail only in
  documented classes:
  - The hardware approximation class: the VFPU function units
    (vrcp/vrsq/vsqrt/vlog2/vexp2 family, vsin/vcos/vasin, vrot)
    are low-bit approximations on hardware; this core evaluates
    the true functions. Results differ by 1-3 ULP with signs,
    zeros, NaNs and structure exact. Covers exact (from line 17),
    prefix_sat, specials (vrot rows only), vrot, vector's vasin
    rows, and gum's checkGlRotate sine residual sign (the
    residual magnitude matches exactly; the rest of gum passes,
    including all sceGum matrix ops).
  - prefix_consume: all prefix readbacks and all follow-up
    (then=) values are exact; 30 of 85 op result lines differ in
    per-op prefix roles that are not modeled (which operands
    some ops read raw, scalar prefix routing, product zero
    signs, vcst/vidt writing more than lane 0).
  - prefix_unpack: 11 of 34 lines differ by the prefix unit's
    stale-latch replay, whose update rule the test's own header
    records as not understood (zero is substituted, as the
    author suggests).
  - The operand layout paradox class: vregs Upgrade/Combine,
    the prefixes R-name prints, and matrix's vmidt section
    (which loads four quads from one address) are cases where
    the corpus's own witnesses disagree under any single
    field-based operand walk; the rule satisfying the majority
    of witnesses is kept and these sections differ.
  - overlap_vcrsp: the test's own header documents that the op
    does not read-before-write on hardware (an in-place hazard)
    and uses a size form assemblers refuse; not modeled.
  - vbranch_hazard: an mtvc CC write is visible to a branch 6
    instructions later on hardware, stale at +0/+1/+2; this core
    commits immediately. The plain vbranch test passes fully,
    including vcmp in the delay slot.
  - vavg: lanes 1-3 of the expected file are the recording
    machine's uninitialized register state; the controlled
    witness (specials) shows the ops write lane 0 only.
  - vrnd: seed expansion and the RCX readback path are exact;
    the draw recurrence is modeled, not solved.
  - vector: the guest prints 3309 of 5330 lines (the produced
    region differs only in the vasin approximation rows), then
    its PC loops in an SDK string routine. The tail sections
    (including checkConstants) are unverified; see the VFPU
    flag status.

### PSP-3 corrections to the PSP-2 VFPU

The corpus refuted the PSP-2 build's VFPU operand layout, which
was self-consistent but invented. PSP-3 replaces it, from corpus
witnesses: the arithmetic operand layout (matrix from bits [4:2],
singles and vectors as documented in the source header), the
load/store field layout with LVL.Q/LVR.Q window semantics derived
from the corpus unaligned rows (primary opcode 0x35 is LVL.Q/
LVR.Q; the LDC1 reading PSP-2 assumed does not exist on
Allegrex), MFV/MTV versus MFVC/MTVC split by word bit 7 with the
control index in the low byte, BC2's imm3 CC-bit select, the
planar prefix layout and constant table {0, 1, 2, 1/2, 3, 1/3,
1/4, 1/6}, prefix power-on 0xE4, the prefix consumption reset
(every compute op resets all three prefix registers; an out of
range swizzle lane poisons the op's result to zero), the VFPU
NaN pattern (sign over 0x7F800001, with per-op sign rules the
exact test pins), the hardware half-float truncation/flush
algorithms, the sort/butterfly block with its equal-value tie
collapse, the pack/unpack family with its size-bit and
destination placement rules, VCST's own 19-entry constant
table, vscmp, vsbn/vwbn, vsbz/vlgb, vrot, the reduction ops
(vfad/vavg write lane 0 only), and the matrix operand decode:
vtfm/vhtfm dot the matrix columns with the vector and write a
strided row; vmmul decodes each slot's anchor from its own bits
(no slot transposes; see matrixOriginVmmul) and stores the
product transposed; vmscl reads its matrix with bit 5 cleared.
Scalar VV operands read at the scalar position the dot family
uses (offset = low field bits + high field bits), which the
minmax_tie, vbranch, overlap and prefix_ctrl witnesses jointly
pin. Also corrected in the CPU: the branch-likely family,
Allegrex MAX/MIN, multiply-accumulate and CLZ/CLO placement
(SPECIAL, not SPECIAL2; the SPECIAL2 forms are kept as a
documented superset), the DIVU by-zero rule, WSBW completing the
BSHFL map, the LWL/SWL shift forms, the LL/SC reservation
lifetime (a syscall or thread switch breaks it, a successful SC
does not), the FPU compare predicate formula, the BC1 tf/nd bit
layout, thread Status modeling, CVT.W.S saturation and NaN
rules, the FS-bit denormal model, scalar NaN propagation, exact
add/sub via a residual-checked rational path, FPU
cause/flags maintenance, and the fcr31 writable mask
0x0181FFFF. Primary opcode 0x3F executes as a no-op: the word
0xFFFF0000 appears inside the SDK printf float path linked into
the corpus binaries, and neither published opcode map assigns
0x3F; the encoding stays flagged as an open question in the
source.

VFPU cross-check flag status: the RCX range 136-143 is
corroborated and closed (seeding, form, and mfvc readback all
match the corpus). VCST is implemented from the hardware
constant list and exercised by the corpus's vector tests, but
its dedicated checkConstants section sits in vector's
unproduced tail, so it stays exercised, not adjudicated. The
fill-group encodings are confirmed from the corpus matrix
binary's own words (f 3 vmidt, 6 vmzero, 7 vmone). VREPL/VSPLT
stay flagged: no corpus binary uses them, so the PSP-2 slots
and semantics remain unverified. The VRND draw recurrence and
the RCX shift-window dynamics stay modeled, not solved.

## PSP-4 (sceAudio, Media Engine decision, libretro shell, enginetest)

PSP-4 completes the core: the audio HLE, the shell the frontends
load, a synthetic end-to-end enginetest, and the app wiring prep
(local only, like the other coordinators' swaps; the parent
verifies and pushes).

### sceAudio

The kernel gains the documented sceAudio set (27 new registry
entries; the (module, NID) registry now holds 154). The model
follows the published driver behavior (pspsdk pspaudio.h
constants and the behavior the open test literature records):

- 8 channels, 16-bit samples, stereo (format 0) or mono (0x10)
  per channel, output at 44,100 Hz. A channel is reserved with
  a per-call sample count of 64..65472 frames, a multiple of
  64. sceAudioChReserve with a negative channel takes the first
  free channel searching downward from channel 7, where free
  means no reservation and no buffer still playing out.
- One buffer per channel, no queue. Output calls hand the
  channel a guest address; the mixer reads the samples straight
  out of guest memory as they are consumed (a guest that
  rewrites a playing buffer hears the rewrite, as on hardware;
  the gates double-buffer for exactly this reason). A null
  buffer pointer is accepted and records a full buffer of rest
  length with nothing playing, which is where
  sceAudioGetChannelRestLen (counts it) and
  sceAudioGetChannelRestLength (does not) disagree; gate (d)
  pins the disagreement.
- A non-blocking output on a busy channel fails
  SCE_ERROR_AUDIO_CHANNEL_BUSY (0x80260002). A blocking output
  parks the caller instead (one parked thread per channel; a
  second blocking caller is turned away BUSY). When the playing
  buffer runs out, the parked buffer starts and the caller
  wakes with the channel sample count, the same value an
  immediate enqueue returns. Validation orders match the
  documented driver: outputs check the volume before the
  channel, sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking ORs its volume pair so
  a negative fails there while the other calls read a negative
  volume as "leave that side unchanged", reserve checks the
  sample count before the format, SetChannelDataLen checks its
  length before the reservation. Volumes apply as
  (sample * vol) >> 15 into a wide accumulator with one int16
  clamp; unity is 0x8000. sceAudioChRelease drops only the
  reservation: an in-flight buffer plays to the end.
- Consumption is a pure function of the kernel cycle clock:
  frames due at cycle C is floor(C * 44100 / 222 MHz), exactly
  735 stereo frames per 3,700,000-cycle frame. Mixing is lazy
  (it advances at every scheduler wait-expiry pass and when the
  host drains), so playback is deterministic and a save state
  resumes the stream at the exact frame. A parked blocking
  caller's wait deadline is the cycle its channel's buffer runs
  out, so the scheduler fast-forward lands there and the buffer
  completes: a guest whose only thread blocks on audio output
  forever cannot deadlock the machine (gate (c) proves it).
  One simplification, stated: consumption is phased to the
  boot-time clock rather than re-phasing to the first enqueue
  the way the hardware DMA start does; totals, rates, and
  per-buffer boundaries are unaffected.
- system.AudioBuffer() drains the mixed stream in kernel mode
  (stereo int16 at 44,100 Hz); outside kernel mode it returns
  nil, the PSP-2 behavior. The undrained ring is capped at
  8192 frames (over ten seconds); samples past the cap drop.
- sceAudioInput is the documented silence model: this core has
  no microphone source, so InputInit succeeds, reads fill the
  buffer with zeros and report every requested sample, a null
  buffer returns -1, and GetInputLength returns 0. The routing
  pair is stored state with the documented defaults (mode 1,
  volume mode 1) and set-returns-previous semantics.
  sceAudioSetFrequency accepts the documented 44100 and 48000;
  the output stream itself stays 44,100 Hz.
- Not implemented, by decision: the sceAudioOutput2 and
  sceAudioSRCCh families. They share one hardware channel whose
  documented behavior includes arbitrary input sample rates
  with sample rate conversion and a two-descriptor DMA queue,
  which is not simple documented semantics, and no corpus test
  exercises them. Their NIDs stay unregistered, so calls land
  on the PSP-3 unknown path (0x80020001 plus a
  Kernel.UnknownCalls entry); gate (d) pins exactly that.

Gates (system/psp4_gate_test.go, synthetic guests in the PSP-3
gate builder style, host measures the drained stream):

- (a) One channel plays a 100-frame-period cosine (441 Hz,
  amplitude 12000) through 40 blocking calls of 1024 frames:
  the drained span is exactly 40,960 frames, every sample equal
  to the table value at unity volume, silence outside the span,
  measured frequency 440.35 Hz from rising zero crossings
  (within 2 percent of 441). A second run saves mid-playback
  (20 calls done, a buffer in flight) and the restored
  continuation is byte-identical to the uninterrupted run:
  stream, console, and final state.
- (b) Two channels (7 and 6, the documented downward search)
  mix the same static buffer: 10,240 frames of exact doubled
  table values starting in lockstep, then two buffers of
  +30000 per channel clamped to 32767 for 2,048 frames, then
  two of -30000 clamped to -32768 for 2,048 frames: 14,336
  frames exact.
- (c) A guest that only plays audio (its main thread loops on
  OutputBlocking forever) still advances: 30 frames run, vcount
  30, exactly 44,100 samples drained (30 x 735 stereo frames),
  22 blocking calls completed, and every played frame matches
  the replayed buffer pattern exactly. No deadlock.
- (d) Edge semantics: one guest records 34 return values
  covering the validation orders and error codes above (invalid
  channel 0x80260003, not aligned 0x80260006, invalid format
  0x80260007, not init 0x80260001, invalid volume 0x8026000B,
  invalid frequency 0x8026000A, not reserved 0x80260008, busy
  0x80260002), the RestLen/RestLength disagreement (1024 vs 0
  after a null output), the input silence model, the routing
  defaults, the two unimplemented reserves returning 0x80020001
  and appearing in UnknownCalls, a release with a buffer in
  flight, and a oneshot landing on channel 6 with rest 512
  because channel 7's released buffer is still playing out.
  The corpus harness is unchanged by PSP-4 (cpu_alu still 4/4).

Audio state serializes in the kernel blob (its internal
version is now 3): channels, parked waiters by thread UID,
mixer position, the undrained ring, and the routing pair. A
fresh machine in kernel mode just after boot serializes
35,677,708 bytes (35,677,402 in PSP-3; the audio block adds
306).

### Media Engine decision

The Media Engine is not emulated, and no second CPU will be
built. Reasoning: the ME is a second Allegrex-class processor
with its own boot sequence and shared-memory mailbox protocol;
nothing in the fetched corpus gates it (no pspautotests binary
exercises it); and retail software reaches it through firmware
modules (the sceMe/sceVlme/sceMeAudio libraries and the module
stack above them) that this HLE kernel does not load, so there
is no guest code path in scope that could drive an emulated ME
even if one existed. The stance: any sceMe, sceVlme, or
sceMeAudio-style NID stays on the logged-unknown path
(0x80020001 with a Kernel.UnknownCalls entry). No ME-adjacent
query exists in the implemented sceKernel set today, so nothing
answers with a synthetic value; if one is added it takes the
documented not-available value. No published evidence showed a
small documented subset with simple semantics that real boot
code needs, so none is implemented.

### libretro shell

libretro/ is the family C ABI shell, core name "iTaK GoPSP".
Load paths: .iso opens through the umd layer and boots
PSP_GAME/SYSDR/BOOT.BIN, falling back to EBOOT.BIN beside it
per the documented UMD layout (system.BootUMD); if neither
exists the load fails cleanly. .elf and .prx load directly
through system.LoadExecutable. Declared extensions: iso|elf|prx,
need_fullpath set. Geometry 480x272 XRGB8888, aspect from the
geometry (1.7647). Timing declares fps 60.0, which is the
machine's own quotient (222 MHz over the 3,700,000 cycle frame
budget is exactly 60), and audio 44,100 Hz stereo from the
system drain. Input maps by position (Cross=B, Circle=A,
Square=Y, Triangle=X, Start, Select, L, R, dpad) through
SetButtons and the left analog stick through SetAnalog.
RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM is the 32 MB main RAM.
RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM returns nil/0: PSP saves flow through
the IoFileMgr ms0: store the host installs with
SetMemoryStickFiles, which is a host-owned map with no stable
fixed backing slice to expose, and the iTaK frontend does not
consume libretro SAVE_RAM for PSP. Serialize forwards to system
states (v3 in kernel mode); retro_reset re-boots the loaded
content. Shell gates (libretro/main_test.go) cover both load
paths, the info and AV contract, the memory regions, a
serialize round trip plus reset re-boot, and clean rejection
of bad images (garbage ISO, truncated ISO, ISO with no boot
executable, garbage ELF, empty PRX, wrong extension).

### Enginetest

The enginetest package builds the synthetic bootable ISO: a
hand-assembled guest at PSP_GAME/SYSDR/BOOT.BIN (with a
PARAM.SFO carrying the title "PSP4 Engine Test") that prints
"PSP4 ENGINE OK" through the kernel console, submits a GE list
(clear color 0xFF302010 plus one green sprite at (8,8)-(16,12)),
starts the 441 Hz sceAudio sine in its first frames and keeps
it playing with no input, polls sceCtrl and records the host
buttons, writes milestones 1..5 in order to 0x08900000, and
loops on vblank waits. The in-process gate (system/
psp4_enginetest_test.go) asserts the milestones in order, the
console string, exact pixels (clear, sprite, and the pixel
just past the sprite), the recorded buttons equal to the host
set Start|Down, at least 8 audio calls and 30 vblank waits in
100 frames, vcount equal to the frames run, and the tone exact
from stream frame 6 (147,000 samples over 100 frames). A
mid-run save restores byte-identical continuation: state,
framebuffer, and the 30-frame audio block after the save
point. The same ISO through the built desktop core
(builds/libgo_psp.so, builds/ is gitignored) under
go_backend/cmd/enginetest reports, verbatim:

    === iTaK Gaming engine test (linux/amd64) ===
    core loaded
    game loaded
    AV: aspect=1.7647 fps=60.00 audio=44100 Hz pixelFormat=1
    video: 480x272, frames=120, non-blank=true
    audio: produced=88200 drained=96000 non-silent=94068
    save state: 35939883 bytes at frame hash 103c4fc882f647c1
    save manager: wrote one state each for players dad and kid
    after moving on: hash 103c4fc882f647c1 (differs from save point: false)
    after restoring save: hash 103c4fc882f647c1 (save point 103c4fc882f647c1)
    RESULT: ALL TESTS PASSED

(The core and rom path lines are omitted from the quote; they
name the local builds/ paths. "produced=88200" is exactly 120
frames x 735; the frame hash is stable across the save,
continued running, and the restore because the guest frame is
static once drawn.)

### Wiring prep (local, not pushed)

go_backend/internal/core/types.go: the Cores64BitOnly PSP
entry now names "iTaK GoPSP" / libgo_psp.so with extensions
.iso/.elf/.prx. flutter_ui/lib/main.dart: the PSP SystemInfo
core string is libgo_psp.so with the same extensions (it
already carried requires64: true). Only the PSP entries were
touched; the backend still builds. tools/autobuild-server.sh
is untouched (it has no 64-bit branch; that is the parent's
pipeline task), and no pubspec change was made. The 64-bit
Android build of libgo_psp.so through that pipeline is still
ahead; the wiring names the artifact the pipeline will
produce.

### Honest gaps carried forward

- The parked PSP-3 corpus divergence classes, unchanged: the
  hardware VFPU transcendentals are low-bit approximations
  while this core computes true values (1-3 ULP differences);
  prefix_consume leaves 30 of 85 op result lines differing in
  per-op prefix roles not modeled; prefix_unpack leaves 11 of
  34 lines differing by the prefix unit's stale-latch replay;
  the operand-layout paradox files (vregs Upgrade/Combine,
  prefixes R-name prints, matrix vmidt) stay unresolvable
  under any single field-based walk; overlap_vcrsp's in-place
  hazard is documented by the test's own header and not
  modeled; the vbranch and fpu branch hazards (delayed CC
  visibility) are not modeled; vavg's expected lanes 1-3 are
  the recording machine's uninitialized state; the VRND draw
  recurrence is modeled (xorshift32), not solved, while its
  seed expansion and RCX readback are exact; the corpus vector
  guest still stalls after 3309 of 5330 lines in an SDK string
  routine, so its tail (including checkConstants) is
  unverified and VCST stays exercised, not adjudicated;
  VREPL/VSPLT remain uncorroborated by any corpus binary.
- Callbacks are registered but never dispatched (PSP-3).
- The Media Engine is absent (decision above). The
  sceAudioOutput2 and sceAudioSRCCh families are absent
  (decision above).
- No PGD decryption: encrypted retail content cannot load.
- Primary opcode 0x3F still executes as a no-op; the encoding
  stays flagged open (PSP-3).
- And the standing note: no retail game has been booted on
  this core. Every proof is the published corpus, synthetic
  guests, and documentation gates.

## PSP-2 (VFPU, GE display list processor, system integration)

PSP-2 adds the two coprocessor-class units (the VFPU text below
is the PSP-2 build's; PSP-3 corrected its operand encodings
against the corpus, see the PSP-3 corrections above):

- `chips/allegrex` (VFPU): the full VFPU lives in the CPU package. The
  register file is 128 singles organized as 8 matrices of 4x4 with the
  documented row/column operand decode for S/P/T/Q sizes. Encodings
  follow the published VFPU instruction tables (the uofw PSP hardware
  documentation and the davidgfnet VFPU instruction set documentation):
  VV arithmetic under primary opcodes 0x18/0x19/0x1B, the unary and
  conversion families under 0x34, matrix operations under 0x3C, prefix
  instructions under 0x37, loads/stores on the COP2 load/store opcodes,
  and COP2 (0x12) itself holding only the register moves and the
  condition branch. Implemented families: VADD/VSUB/VMUL/VDIV,
  VMIN/VMAX, VDOT/VHDP/VCRS/VDET, the scalar helpers (VSCL, VSBN), the
  unary set (VMOV, VABS, VNEG, VSGN, VSAT0/VSAT1, VZERO/VONE, VIDT),
  the float function set (VSQRT, VRCP, VRSQ, VNRCP, VEXP2, VREXP2,
  VLOG2, VSIN/VCOS/VNSIN, VASIN), conversions (VF2H/VH2F half float,
  VF2IN/VF2IZ/VF2IU/VF2ID with the published scale field, VI2F, VI2UC/
  VI2S packs, VCST constants), matrix ops (VMMUL, VMSCL, VTFM/VHTFM
  2/3/4, VMZERO/VMIDT matrix forms), VCMP with the full 16-entry
  condition table writing the VFPU condition code (per-lane bits plus
  any/all aggregates), VCMOVT/VCMOVF (carved out of the VI2F encoding
  space by the published marker values), VREPL/VSPLT replication, the
  VPFXS/VPFXT/VPFXD prefix instructions with full prefix semantics
  (source swizzle/abs/negate/constant substitution from the documented
  constant table, destination saturation and write masks, one-shot
  consumption), random support (VRNDS seed, VRNDI integer output and
  the float forms), loads/stores LV.S/SV.S and LV.Q/SV.Q with the
  LVL.Q/LVR.Q/SVL.Q/SVR.Q unaligned merge semantics, and the control
  register moves MFC2/MTC2/CFC2/CTC2/MFVC/MTVC (index 131 is the
  condition code, 135 the read-only revision, 136 to 143 the random
  state). VFPU float math follows the same model as the scalar FPU:
  operands pass through the denormal-flushing input helper, arithmetic
  runs in float64, results are rounded once to single. Genuinely
  unimplemented encodings still raise Reserved Instruction and are
  counted in VFPUFaultCount; every documented family above executes.
