  VDET (the pair determinant) is implemented in the product group.
- `ge`: the GE display list processor. Lists are submitted by address
  and executed synchronously: SIGNAL stalls the list (the signal value
  and behavior are recorded; Continue resumes past it), FINISH is
  recorded, END completes the list. Every command word is stored to
  its register slot and counted per opcode, including commands that do
  not draw (BEZIER, SPLINE, BBOX are counted and flagged no-draw).
  State covers the framebuffer and depth buffer pointers and widths,
  viewport and offset, region and scissor, clear mode, texture state
  (addresses, sizes, formats T565/T5551/T4444/T8888 and CLUT4/8/16/32
  with CLUT load and the documented texture swizzle layout), blend
  equation and factors, alpha/stencil/color tests, logical ops, and
  the write masks. Vertex decoding handles the weights/UV/color/
  normal/position widths in through and indexed forms. PRIM types 0
  to 6 (points, lines, strips, triangles, strips, fans, sprites) are
  rasterized in software with per-pixel barycentric interpolation
  (no perspective correction, see honesty notes), the full fragment
  test chain, and drawing into VRAM in the active pixel format
  (5650/5551/4444/8888). The system presents the display buffer (or
  the draw buffer until one is set) as the 480x272 frame.

## PSP-1 (CPU, memory, media foundations, machine skeleton)

- `chips/allegrex`: the Allegrex integer CPU. Full MIPS I/II/III integer
  set plus the Allegrex/MIPS32 additions: LWL/LWR/SWL/SWR with the exact
  little-endian byte composition rules, LL/SC, MOVZ/MOVN, MUL and the
  MADD/MSUB family accumulating into HI/LO, CLZ/CLO, EXT/INS, ROTR/ROTV,
  SEB/SEH/WSBH/BITREV, and the Allegrex specials MFIC/MTIC (interrupt
  controller register file) and HALT (the exact word 0x70000000). Delay
  slots are modeled with a PC/NPC pipeline pair. There is NO load delay:
  the Allegrex interlocks, so a load writes its register during the load
  instruction and back-to-back load/use sees the new value. CP0 follows
  the PSP layout (PRId reads the Allegrex constant 0x00006542, EBase and
  the Config family are stored, Count advances at half the CPU rate and
  Compare raises the timer line, exception vectors honor BEV and the
  Cause IV bit). FPU (CP1) is implemented for single precision: the core
  arithmetic, CVT/ROUND/TRUNC/CEIL/FLOOR conversions, all 16 C.cond.S
  conditions driving the FCC and BC1F/BC1T branches. Double precision is
  NOT on the Allegrex FPU: double encodings raise Reserved Instruction.
- `bus`: the physical memory map. 32 MB main RAM at 0x08000000 with the
  KSEG0/KSEG1 aliases folded onto the same backing store, 16 KB
  scratchpad at 0x00010000 plus its physical-zero alias, 2 MB VRAM at
  0x04000000 mirrored across its 8 MB window, and the hardware register
  pages kept as stored stub cells. Unmapped reads return zero.
- `umd`: ISO9660 reader (PVD validation, directory walk, file read) and a
  PARAM.SFO parser for the documented PSF key/value format, so the
  PSP_GAME directory convention and disc metadata (title, category, disc
  id) are readable from a user-supplied image.
- `system`: the machine in the family shape. LoadISO mounts and
  inspects an image, RunFrame consumes a 3,700,000 cycle budget
  (222 MHz / 60), Framebuffer returns the blank 480x272 XRGB8888 buffer
  until the first display list is submitted and the GE presentation
  after it, SubmitDisplayList/ContinueDisplayList drive the GE
  synchronously (the sceGu HLE path is PSP-3), SetButtons/SetAnalog
  store the controller state, and Serialize/Deserialize captures the
  whole machine behind a version byte (version 2: CPU including the
  VFPU + RAM + VRAM + scratchpad + input + cycle count + GE state).
  State size: 35,674,041 bytes on a fresh machine, of which the CPU
  state is 2,864 bytes (PSP-1: 35,669,577 total, 1,588 CPU).
- `enginetest`: the PSP-4 synthetic fixture (guest ELF builder,
  ISO9660 image with PSP_GAME/SYSDR/BOOT.BIN and PARAM.SFO,
  milestone and probe constants), shared by the system gate, the
  shell tests, and the desktop harness run.
- `libretro`: the "iTaK GoPSP" shell (see the PSP-4 section).

## Gates (PSP-2)

90 tests across the five packages, all passing, `go vet` clean,
`gofmt` clean. New in PSP-2:

- VFPU: 29 test functions with hand-derived vectors per family:
  arithmetic in all four sizes, min/max NaN rules, saturation forms,
  the float function set, trig at documented points (tolerance based,
  see honesty notes), half float round trips including denormal and
  NaN cases, the int conversion family with its scale field, dot/
  cross/homogeneous products, matrix multiply and transforms against
  hand-computed products, prefix constant/swizzle/saturation cases,
  destination prefix masks, replication, compare and branch on
  condition, conditional moves, LVL/LVR merge cases, random seeding,
  control register moves, and a serialization round trip. A dedicated
  regression set pins the published encodings themselves: every VV
  arithmetic op runs with VT in matrix 0 and matrix 1, and raw anchor
  words from the published tables (vadd.q base 0x60008080) execute as
  arithmetic, not as COP2 moves.
- GE: 13 test functions over synthetic word-array display lists: clear
  fills exact pixels including the raw VRAM word, a through-mode
  triangle covers its center and misses outside points, a textured
  sprite samples a 2x2 texture correctly from both unswizzled and
  swizzled storage, the depth test rejects a farther triangle over a
  nearer one, a sprite fills exactly its rectangle, SIGNAL stalls and
  Continue reaches FINISH/END with the counters asserting the flow,
  CLUT8 textures resolve through the loaded palette, alpha blending
  and alpha test behave, JUMP/CALL/RET control flow is honored, and
  the full command table decodes with per-opcode counters.
- System: a synthetic program runs VFPU math on the CPU (vadd/vdot/
  vmul with hand-computed results) and a display list through the GE
  (clear plus a sprite, pixel-probed), then a state saved mid-run
  restores into a byte-identical continuation of both state bytes and
  framebuffer pixels. Version 1 states are rejected by the version 2
  loader.

## Gates (PSP-1)

No MIPS set exists in the Tom Harte ProcessorTests tree (checked
2026-10-13; the tree covers 8088, 68000, 65816, 65c02, SPC700 and others,
no MIPS), so the CPU gate is hand-derived unit vectors from the
MIPS32/Allegrex documentation. The vectors pin the sharp edges:
EXT/INS field boundaries, ROTR by 0 and by register values above 31,
SEB/SEH sign extension, MADD carry into HI, LL/SC link behavior including
the ERET clear, delay slot execution exactly once, exception entry from
inside a delay slot (BD bit), the documented divide-by-zero results, and
FPU rounding-mode vectors (RN/RZ/RP/RM plus trunc/floor/ceil/round
forms), denormal flush and canonical NaN results. A synthetic MIPS
program runs on the machine, and a save state taken mid-run restores
into a byte-identical continuation.

The open-source pspautotests suite (hrydgard/pspautotests) ships 643
prebuilt .elf/.prx binaries, 47 of them under tests/cpu. They need the
PSP-3 HLE loader to run, so PSP-1 only inventories them as later gates:
tests/cpu/cpu_alu (cpu_alu, cpu_branch, cpu_branch2, cpu_div),
tests/cpu/fpu (fpu, rounding, roundmode, fcr, fpu_nan), tests/cpu/lsu
(lsu, llsc, cacheop), tests/cpu/icache (icache), and the tests/cpu/vfpu
set for PSP-2. Nothing from the suite is vendored into this repository.

## Roadmap

- PSP-2 (done): the VFPU in full, and the GE display list processor
  (framebuffer presentation, textured primitives) so homebrew can draw.
- PSP-3 (done): HLE kernel: threads and scheduling, syscall dispatch,
  the ELF/PRX module loader for homebrew, controller and display HLE,
  with pspautotests as the conformance gate (the tests/cpu set,
  including the vfpu group as the executable cross-check for the VFPU
  encodings and math; results in the PSP-3 section above).
- PSP-4 (done): audio (sceAudio plus the Media Engine decision),
  the libretro shell, a synthetic bootable-ISO enginetest through
  the built shell and the shared harness, and app wiring prep for
  the android-64bit build (the pipeline's 64-bit branch itself is
  still ahead; see the PSP-4 section).

Commercial game support depends on HLE coverage growth slice by slice
and is NOT promised by any of the above.

## Honesty notes (approximations in this slice)

- VFPU precision model: arithmetic is computed in float64 from
  denormal-flushed inputs and rounded once to single, the same model
  as the scalar FPU. The hardware transcendental units (VSIN/VCOS/
  VEXP2/VLOG2/VRCP/VRSQ family) use polynomial approximations on real
  hardware; this core evaluates the host math functions in the
  documented units (trig in units of pi/2) and the tests assert a
  stated tolerance against the true values, not bit equality with the
  hardware polynomials. Bit-exact polynomial reproduction is a later
  accuracy pass, with pspautotests (PSP-3) as the cross-check.
- VFPU random: the generator behind VRNDI/VRNDS and the float random
  forms is an xorshift32 over the documented seed/state registers.
  The exact hardware generator is not fully published; the interface
  (seed register, state readout through MFVC) is implemented as
  documented and the algorithm is best-known, not verified.
- Matrix operations (VMMUL, VMSCL, VTFM/VHTFM, matrix moves) read
  their operands raw (no source prefix) in this core; the prefix
  consumption reset still applies to them as compute ops. The
  documented operand overlap restrictions are not enforced, except
  that ordinary VV ops read all inputs before writing (the corpus
  overlap test passes; the vcrsp in-place hazard is the documented
  exception). VCMOV with selector 7 is unspecified in the
  documentation; this core treats it as the per-lane inverted form.
- Two encodings could not be confirmed in the published documents:
  VREPL and VSPLT appear in neither reference text, so they sit at
  free function values in the unary group (0x08 and 0x09) with the
  semantics the instruction names imply, flagged in the source; no
  pspautotests binary uses them either (PSP-3 cross-check, still
  open). VCST uses the hardware 19-entry constant list from the
  published documentation (PSP-3; the corpus checkConstants
  adjudication is pending only because the vector test stalls
  before that section, see the PSP-3 corpus results). The random
  control registers are mapped at 136 to 143 (8 words), the range
  the corpus corroborates.
- GE rasterization interpolates per pixel with barycentric weights
  and NO perspective correction: texture coordinates and colors are
  affine across the triangle. Most PSP test scenes and simple
  homebrew are orthographic, where this matches; perspective-correct
  interpolation is a known PSP-2 simplification.
- GE execution is synchronous on submission: a list runs to END or to
  its SIGNAL stall point immediately, there is no queue, no parallel
  GE/CPU timing, and display list interrupts are not modeled. The
  SIGNAL model records the value and behavior word and stalls until
  Continue, which is the documented simplified form.
- BEZIER and SPLINE primitives are decoded, counted and flagged but
  do not draw (no tessellation in this slice); BBOX is counted only.
  CULLMODE is stored but backface culling is not applied. Dithering
  is off (the DITHER state is stored only). The GE command counters
  are diagnostics and are not part of the serialized state; a
  restored GE restarts its counters at zero.
- No TLB. KUSEG is direct-mapped, TLB instructions are no-ops, and the
  CP0 Random register is cosmetic without a TLB behind it.
- The bus exposes a 32-bit view of the 64-bit external bus. Cached and
  uncached aliases share one backing store, so the machine is cache
  coherent by construction; the CACHE instruction is a no-op and there
  is no cache to flush.
- Cycle counts are a deterministic approximation (most instructions 1
  cycle, multiply family 2, divide 37, FPU divide/sqrt 12), not a
  pipeline simulation.
- FPU arithmetic is computed in float64 and rounded once through a
  helper that honors the FCSR rounding mode with a one-ulp directed
  adjustment. Denormal inputs and results are flushed to signed zero
  (the Allegrex FPU has no denormal support), NaN results are
  canonicalized to 0x7FC00000, and FPU exceptions are always masked.
  The FPU implementation register (FCR0) reads 0.
- ERET/DERET and the debug exception path are register-level
  simplifications (documented in the CPU source). An exception taken
  while Status.ERL is set transfers control but leaves EPC/Cause
  untouched.
- The ISO reader does not follow multi-extent files; PSP metadata files
  are single-extent, and the disc structures this slice reads always
  are.
- The frame budget assumes 60 Hz; the real panel refresh is about
  59.94 Hz.


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/bus/bus.go ====================

// Package bus implements the PSP physical memory map behind the virtual
// addresses the Allegrex CPU issues.
//
// The CPU hands this package virtual addresses. Kernel segments are folded
// onto physical addresses the way the hardware does without a TLB lookup:
// KSEG0 (0x80000000) and KSEG1 (0xA0000000) both strip the top three bits,
// and KUSEG addresses below 0x80000000 pass through unchanged. There is no
// TLB emulation in this core, so KUSEG is a direct map; that is a stated
// simplification of the design, not an oversight.
//
// Cached and uncached aliases land on the same backing store, so the bus is
// coherent by construction. The real PSP has a 64-bit external bus; this
// package exposes the documented 32-bit view the CPU core consumes.
package bus

// Memory region sizes in bytes.
const (
	RAMSize        = 32 << 20 // main RAM
	VRAMSize       = 2 << 20  // frame buffer / GE memory
	ScratchpadSize = 16 << 10 // fast on-chip scratchpad
)

// Physical base addresses.
const (
	scratchpadAliasBase = 0x00000000 // scratchpad also decodes at physical zero
	scratchpadBase      = 0x00010000
	vramBase            = 0x04000000
	vramWindowEnd       = 0x04800000 // VRAM mirrors every 2 MB across this window
	ramBase             = 0x08000000
	ioBase              = 0x1C000000 // hardware register pages (stored stubs)
	ioEnd               = 0x20000000
)

// Bus is the PSP memory system. RAM, VRAM and Scratchpad are exported so the
// system package can serialize them and tests can inspect them.
type Bus struct {
	RAM        []byte
	VRAM       []byte
	Scratchpad []byte

	io map[uint32]uint32 // sparse 32-bit stub cells for hardware registers
}

// New returns a zeroed memory system.
func New() *Bus {
	return &Bus{
		RAM:        make([]byte, RAMSize),
		VRAM:       make([]byte, VRAMSize),
		Scratchpad: make([]byte, ScratchpadSize),
		io:         make(map[uint32]uint32),
	}
}

// translate folds a virtual address onto its physical address.
func translate(vaddr uint32) uint32 {
	if vaddr >= 0x80000000 {
		return vaddr & 0x1FFFFFFF
	}
	return vaddr
}

func (b *Bus) readPhys8(p uint32) uint8 {
	switch {
	case p < ScratchpadSize:
		// Scratchpad alias at physical zero.
		return b.Scratchpad[p]
	case p >= scratchpadBase && p < scratchpadBase+ScratchpadSize:
		return b.Scratchpad[p-scratchpadBase]
	case p >= vramBase && p < vramWindowEnd:
		return b.VRAM[(p-vramBase)&(VRAMSize-1)]
	case p >= ramBase && p < ramBase+RAMSize:
		return b.RAM[p-ramBase]
	case p >= ioBase && p < ioEnd:
		cell := b.io[p&^3]
		return uint8(cell >> ((p & 3) * 8))
	default:
		// Unmapped reads return zero.
		return 0
	}
}

func (b *Bus) writePhys8(p uint32, v uint8) {
	switch {
	case p < ScratchpadSize:
		b.Scratchpad[p] = v
	case p >= scratchpadBase && p < scratchpadBase+ScratchpadSize:
		b.Scratchpad[p-scratchpadBase] = v
	case p >= vramBase && p < vramWindowEnd:
		b.VRAM[(p-vramBase)&(VRAMSize-1)] = v
	case p >= ramBase && p < ramBase+RAMSize:
		b.RAM[p-ramBase] = v
	case p >= ioBase && p < ioEnd:
		key := p &^ 3
		cell := b.io[key]
		shift := (p & 3) * 8
		cell &^= 0xFF << shift
		cell |= uint32(v) << shift
		b.io[key] = cell
	default:
		// Unmapped writes are dropped.
	}
}

// Read8 reads one byte from a virtual address.
func (b *Bus) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	return b.readPhys8(translate(addr))
}

// Read16 reads a little-endian halfword from a virtual address.
func (b *Bus) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	lo := uint16(b.Read8(addr))
	hi := uint16(b.Read8(addr + 1))
	return lo | hi<<8
}

// Read32 reads a little-endian word from a virtual address.
func (b *Bus) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	lo := uint32(b.Read16(addr))
	hi := uint32(b.Read16(addr + 2))
	return lo | hi<<16
}

// Write8 writes one byte to a virtual address.
func (b *Bus) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	b.writePhys8(translate(addr), v)
}

// Write16 writes a little-endian halfword to a virtual address.
func (b *Bus) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	b.Write8(addr, uint8(v))
	b.Write8(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
}

// Write32 writes a little-endian word to a virtual address.
func (b *Bus) Write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	b.Write16(addr, uint16(v))
	b.Write16(addr+2, uint16(v>>16))
}

// IOCount reports how many hardware register stub cells have been written.
// It exists for diagnostics and tests.
func (b *Bus) IOCount() int {
	return len(b.io)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/bus/bus_test.go ====================

package bus

import "testing"

func TestRAMAliasesShareBacking(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write32(0x08000000, 0xDEADBEEF) // KUSEG direct
	if got := b.Read32(0x88000000); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("cached alias read = %#x, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read32(0xA8000000); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("uncached alias read = %#x, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	b.Write8(0xA8000004, 0x7E)
	if got := b.Read8(0x08000004); got != 0x7E {
		t.Errorf("uncached write not visible via KUSEG: %#x", got)
	}
}

func TestScratchpadAndAlias(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write16(0x00010010, 0xBEEF) // kernel scratchpad address
	if got := b.Read16(0x00000010); got != 0xBEEF {
		t.Errorf("scratchpad zero alias read = %#x, want 0xBEEF", got)
	}
	b.Write8(0x00003FFF, 0x11) // top of the alias window
	if got := b.Scratchpad[0x3FFF]; got != 0x11 {
		t.Errorf("scratchpad backing byte = %#x, want 0x11", got)
	}
}

func TestVRAMMirror(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write32(0x04000000, 0x11223344)
	if got := b.Read32(0x04200000); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("VRAM 2 MB mirror read = %#x, want 0x11223344", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read32(0x04400000); got != 0x11223344 {
		t.Errorf("VRAM 4 MB mirror read = %#x, want 0x11223344", got)
	}
}

func TestIOStubsStoreValues(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write32(0x1E000020, 0xA5A5A5A5)                   // interrupt controller page (stub)
	if got := b.Read32(0xBE000020); got != 0xA5A5A5A5 { // KSEG1 alias
		t.Errorf("IO stub read = %#x, want 0xA5A5A5A5", got)
	}
	b.Write8(0x1E000021, 0x3C)
	if got := b.Read32(0x1E000020); got != 0xA5A53CA5 {
		t.Errorf("IO byte write = %#x, want 0xA5A53CA5", got)
	}
}

func TestUnmappedReadsZero(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	if got := b.Read32(0x10000000); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("unmapped read = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
	b.Write32(0x10000000, 0xFFFFFFFF) // must not panic or stick
	if got := b.Read32(0x10000000); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("unmapped write stuck: %#x", got)
	}
}

func TestWidthsCompose(t *testing.T) {
	b := New()
	b.Write32(0x08000000, 0x01020304)
	if got := b.Read8(0x08000000); got != 0x04 {
		t.Errorf("byte 0 = %#x, want 0x04", got)
	}
	if got := b.Read16(0x08000002); got != 0x0102 {
		t.Errorf("half at +2 = %#x, want 0x0102", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex/allegrex.go ====================

// Package allegrex implements the Sony Allegrex CPU used in the PSP:
// a MIPS32 little endian core with a single precision FPU (CP1), the
// Allegrex SPECIAL2/SPECIAL3 extensions, and the COP2 VFPU.
//
// Execution model notes:
//   - PC/NPC pipeline pair: branches and jumps set NPC, so the delay
//     slot at PC+4 always executes exactly once before the target.
//   - No load delay. The Allegrex follows the MIPS32 interlock model:
//     a load writes its destination register during the load
//     instruction itself, so a back to back load/use pair sees the
//     new value with no stall and no stale read.
//   - Cycle counts are a deterministic approximation, documented in
//     exec.go: 1 cycle base, 2 for multiply family, 37 for divide,
//     12 for FPU divide and square root.
package allegrex

import "encoding/binary"

// Bus is the memory and device interface the CPU drives. Addresses
// are virtual equals physical in this core (no TLB), matching the
// PSP kernel segments the system package maps onto the bus.
type Bus interface {
	Read8(addr uint32) uint8
	Read16(addr uint32) uint16
	Read32(addr uint32) uint32
	Write8(addr uint32, value uint8)
	Write16(addr uint32, value uint16)
	Write32(addr uint32, value uint32)
}

// Exception codes stored in Cause.ExcCode.
const (
	excInt  = 0  // interrupt
	excAdEL = 4  // address error, load or fetch
	excAdES = 5  // address error, store
	excSys  = 8  // syscall
	excBp   = 9  // breakpoint
	excRI   = 10 // reserved instruction
	excCpU  = 11 // coprocessor unusable
	excOv   = 12 // integer overflow
	excTr   = 13 // trap
	excFPE  = 15 // floating point (never raised in slice 1)
)

// Status register bit positions used by the core.
const (
	statusIE  = 1 << 0
	statusEXL = 1 << 1
	statusERL = 1 << 2
	statusBEV = 1 << 22
	statusCU1 = 1 << 29

	// StatusCU1 is the CP0 Status bit that enables the FPU. A
	// bare reset leaves it clear (CpU on COP1 use); the kernel
	// sets it in every thread context it creates, matching the
	// firmware, whose user threads run with the FPU enabled.
	StatusCU1 = statusCU1
)

// CPU is the full Allegrex processor state. All state is unexported;
// the system package drives it through Step and the accessors.
type CPU struct {
	bus Bus

	// SyscallHook, when non-nil, is consulted for every SYSCALL
	// instruction before the Sys exception is raised. It receives
	// the 20 bit syscall code from the instruction word. Returning
	// true means the hook handled the call (the result belongs in
	// $v0, set by the hook through SetReg) and execution continues
	// with the next instruction; returning false takes the normal
	// exception path. The hook is not part of the serialized state
	// and is never cleared by Reset or Deserialize: the kernel in
	// the kernel package installs it once per machine.
	SyscallHook func(c *CPU, code uint32) bool

	regs [32]uint32
	hi   uint32
	lo   uint32

	// Pipeline: pc is the instruction about to execute, nextPC is
	// the one after it. inDelaySlot reports whether pc sits in a
	// branch delay slot (drives Cause.BD and EPC selection).
	pc          uint32
	nextPC      uint32
	inDelaySlot bool

	cp0 [32][8]uint32 // CP0 registers by register and select

	fpr [32]uint32 // FPU registers, raw IEEE 754 bits
	fcr [32]uint32 // FPU control registers; index 31 is the FCSR

	icReg [32]uint32 // interrupt controller registers for MFIC/MTIC

	vregs     [128]uint32 // VFPU registers, raw bits
	ctrl      [32]uint32  // VFPU CFC2/CTC2 register storage
	mfvcStore [144]uint32 // MFVC/MTVC backing store
	rngState  [8]uint32   // VFPU random generator state, RCX0..7

	spfxImm uint32 // 19 bit source prefix for VS reads
	tpfxImm uint32 // 19 bit source prefix for VT reads
	dpfxImm uint32 // 12 bit destination prefix
	spfxOn  bool
	tpfxOn  bool
	dpfxOn  bool
	// pfxPoison is set while an op whose armed source prefix
	// selected an out of range lane executes; every source
	// read of that op returns zero. It is always false
	// between instructions, so it is not serialized.
	pfxPoison bool
	cc        uint32 // VFPU condition code

	llbit  bool
	lladdr uint32

	halted         bool
	countRemainder uint32 // 0 or 1, leftover half rate Count tick
	timerIRQ       bool   // latched timer interrupt, Cause IP bit 7
	extIP          uint32 // external interrupt lines, bits 0..7
	vfpuFaultCount int
	randomState    uint32 // current Random register value

	// Execution context for the instruction currently executing,
	// captured at Step entry so exception entry can compute EPC
	// and BD even after the pipeline has advanced.
	curPC    uint32
	curDelay bool
}

// New returns a CPU attached to bus, reset with entry point 0.
func New(bus Bus) *CPU {
	c := &CPU{bus: bus}
	c.Reset(0)
	return c
}

// Reset zeroes all registers and state, sets PC to entry, and puts
// Status in its reset value BEV|ERL (0x00400004) with Cause clear.
func (c *CPU) Reset(entry uint32) {
	c.regs = [32]uint32{}
	c.hi, c.lo = 0, 0
	c.pc = entry
	c.nextPC = entry + 4
	c.inDelaySlot = false
	c.cp0 = [32][8]uint32{}
	c.cp0[12][0] = 0x00400004 // Status = BEV|ERL
	// Config (register 16) is left at 0 in slice 1; reads return the
	// stored value and the system package does not depend on it.
	c.fpr = [32]uint32{}
	c.fcr = [32]uint32{}
	c.vregs = [128]uint32{}
	c.ctrl = [32]uint32{}
	c.mfvcStore = [144]uint32{}
	c.rngState = [8]uint32{}
	// The prefix immediates power on at the identity encoding
	// 0xE4 (swizzle x,y,z,w, nothing else set); the corpus
	// prefix_ctrl test reads exactly that back through mfvc
	// $128..$130 before any prefix is written.
	c.spfxImm, c.tpfxImm, c.dpfxImm = 0xE4, 0xE4, 0xE4
	c.spfxOn, c.tpfxOn, c.dpfxOn = false, false, false
	c.cc = 0
	c.icReg = [32]uint32{}
	c.llbit = false
	c.lladdr = 0
	c.halted = false
	c.countRemainder = 0
	c.timerIRQ = false
	c.extIP = 0
	c.vfpuFaultCount = 0
	c.randomState = 31
	c.curPC = entry
	c.curDelay = false
}

// PC returns the address of the next instruction to execute.
func (c *CPU) PC() uint32 { return c.pc }

// SetPC redirects execution; the following instruction is taken as
// sequential and not in a delay slot.
func (c *CPU) SetPC(pc uint32) {
	c.pc = pc
	c.nextPC = pc + 4
	c.inDelaySlot = false
}

// Reg returns general purpose register i. Reg(0) is always 0.
func (c *CPU) Reg(i int) uint32 {
	if i <= 0 || i > 31 {
		return 0
	}
	return c.regs[i]
}

// SetReg writes general purpose register i; writes to register 0
// are ignored.
func (c *CPU) SetReg(i int, v uint32) {
	if i <= 0 || i > 31 {
		return
	}
	c.regs[i] = v
}

// setReg is the internal write path; every register write in the
// decoder funnels through here so r0 writes are discarded centrally.
func (c *CPU) setReg(i int, v uint32) {
	if i == 0 {
		return
	}
	c.regs[i] = v
}

// HI returns the HI result register.
func (c *CPU) HI() uint32 { return c.hi }

// LO returns the LO result register.
func (c *CPU) LO() uint32 { return c.lo }

// FReg returns the raw IEEE 754 bits of FPU register i.
func (c *CPU) FReg(i int) uint32 {
	if i < 0 || i > 31 {
		return 0
	}
	return c.fpr[i]
}

// SetFReg sets the raw bits of FPU register i.
func (c *CPU) SetFReg(i int, bits uint32) {
	if i < 0 || i > 31 {
		return
	}
	c.fpr[i] = bits
}

// CP0 reads a CP0 register by register number and select, applying
// the composed fields (Random, PRId, Cause interrupt bits).
func (c *CPU) CP0(reg, sel int) uint32 {
	if reg < 0 || reg > 31 || sel < 0 || sel > 7 {
		return 0
	}
	return c.readCP0(reg, sel)
}

// SetInterruptLines drives the external interrupt inputs. Bits 0..7
// map onto Cause.IP bits 8..15; bit 7 is shared with the timer latch
// and is the OR of both sources.
func (c *CPU) SetInterruptLines(ip uint32) { c.extIP = ip & 0xFF }

// Halted reports whether the CPU is stopped in HALT or WAIT waiting
// for an enabled interrupt.
func (c *CPU) Halted() bool { return c.halted }

// VFPUFaultCount returns how many genuinely unimplemented VFPU
// encodings have faulted.
func (c *CPU) VFPUFaultCount() int { return c.vfpuFaultCount }

// VSingle returns the raw bits of VFPU register i by linear index
// (0..127, m*16 + row*4 + col).
func (c *CPU) VSingle(i int) uint32 {
	if i < 0 || i > 127 {
		return 0
	}
	return c.vregs[i]
}

// SetVSingle sets the raw bits of VFPU register i by linear index.
func (c *CPU) SetVSingle(i int, bits uint32) {
	if i < 0 || i > 127 {
		return
	}
	c.vregs[i] = bits
}

// VFPUCC returns the VFPU condition code.
func (c *CPU) VFPUCC() uint32 { return c.cc }

// ipByte composes the Cause.IP byte: external lines, the two
// software writable bits stored in Cause, and the timer latch at
// bit 7.
func (c *CPU) ipByte() uint32 {
	ip := c.extIP
	ip |= (c.cp0[13][0] >> 8) & 0x03
	if c.timerIRQ {
		ip |= 0x80
	}
	return ip & 0xFF
}

// interruptPending reports whether an interrupt would be taken now:
// IE set, not in exception or error level, and an unmasked IP bit.
func (c *CPU) interruptPending() bool {
	st := c.cp0[12][0]
	if st&statusIE == 0 || st&statusEXL != 0 || st&statusERL != 0 {
		return false
	}
	im := (st >> 8) & 0xFF
	return c.ipByte()&im != 0
}

func (c *CPU) readCP0(reg, sel int) uint32 {
	switch {
	case reg == 1: // Random
		return c.randomState
	case reg == 13: // Cause: IP is composed, the rest is stored
		v := c.cp0[13][0] &^ (0xFF << 8)
		return v | c.ipByte()<<8
	case reg == 15 && sel == 0: // PRId is a constant
		return 0x00006542
	default:
		return c.cp0[reg][sel]
	}
}

func (c *CPU) writeCP0(reg, sel int, v uint32) {
	switch {
	case reg == 1: // Random is read only
	case reg == 11: // Compare: writing clears the timer latch
		c.cp0[reg][sel] = v
		c.timerIRQ = false
	case reg == 15 && sel == 0: // PRId writes are ignored
	default:
		c.cp0[reg][sel] = v
	}
}

// raiseException performs exception entry for the instruction at
// curPC. When ERL is clear and EXL is clear it saves EPC, ExcCode,
// CE and BD, then sets EXL. When ERL is set the saved context is
// left untouched (reset and error flows own it) but control still
// transfers to the vector. The interrupt vector gains an extra
// 0x80 offset when Cause.IV is set.
func (c *CPU) raiseException(code, ce uint32) {
	st := c.cp0[12][0]
	if st&statusERL == 0 {
		if st&statusEXL == 0 {
			epc := c.curPC
			bd := uint32(0)
			if c.curDelay {
				epc = c.curPC - 4
				bd = 1
			}
			c.cp0[14][0] = epc // EPC
			cause := c.cp0[13][0]
			cause &^= 0x7C // ExcCode bits 2..6
			cause |= (code & 0x1F) << 2
			cause &^= 0x3 << 28 // CE bits 28..29
			cause |= (ce & 0x3) << 28
			cause &^= 1 << 31 // BD bit 31
			cause |= bd << 31
			c.cp0[13][0] = cause
		}
		c.cp0[12][0] = st | statusEXL
	}
	base := uint32(0x80000180)
	if st&statusBEV != 0 {
		base = 0xBFC00380
	}
	if code == excInt && c.cp0[13][0]&(1<<23) != 0 { // Cause.IV
		base += 0x80
	}
	c.llbit = false
	c.setPCVector(base)
}

// raiseDebug performs debug exception entry for SDBBP: DEPC gets
// the faulting address (branch address when in a delay slot), the
// code is stored in Debug bits 10..6, and control goes to the
// debug vector. Simplification: Status is not modified.
func (c *CPU) raiseDebug(code uint32) {
	epc := c.curPC
	if c.curDelay {
		epc = c.curPC - 4
	}
	c.cp0[24][0] = epc // DEPC (register 24 is DEPC in this map)
	// Register 23 is Debug per the register map in the brief.
	dbg := c.cp0[23][0]
	dbg &^= 0x1F << 6
	dbg |= (code & 0x1F) << 6
	c.cp0[23][0] = dbg
	c.llbit = false
	c.setPCVector(0xBFC00480)
}

func (c *CPU) setPCVector(v uint32) {
	c.pc = v
	c.nextPC = v + 4
	c.inDelaySlot = false
}

// advanceCount moves the Count register at half the CPU rate using
// a serialized remainder, and latches the timer interrupt when
// Count reaches Compare.
func (c *CPU) advanceCount(cycles int) {
	total := c.countRemainder + uint32(cycles)
	inc := total / 2
	c.countRemainder = total % 2
	if inc == 0 {
		return
	}
	old := c.cp0[9][0]
	c.cp0[9][0] = old + inc
	cmp := c.cp0[11][0]
	if cmp != 0 {
		if delta := cmp - old; delta >= 1 && delta <= inc {
			c.timerIRQ = true
		}
	}
}

// tickRandom decrements the Random register once per Step, wrapping
// back to 31 when it would fall below Wired.
func (c *CPU) tickRandom() {
	wired := c.cp0[6][0]
	if wired > 31 {
		wired = 31
	}
	if c.randomState <= wired || c.randomState > 31 {
		c.randomState = 31
	} else {
		c.randomState--
	}
}

// Step executes one instruction, or one halted tick, and returns
// the cycles consumed (always at least 1).
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	c.tickRandom()
	if c.halted {
		if c.interruptPending() {
			c.halted = false
			c.curPC = c.pc
			c.curDelay = c.inDelaySlot
			c.raiseException(excInt, 0)
		}
		c.advanceCount(1)
		return 1
	}
	// Interrupt check happens before the fetch of each instruction.
	if c.interruptPending() {
		c.curPC = c.pc
		c.curDelay = c.inDelaySlot
		c.raiseException(excInt, 0)
		c.advanceCount(1)
		return 1
	}
	c.curPC = c.pc
	c.curDelay = c.inDelaySlot
	if c.pc&3 != 0 {
		c.cp0[8][0] = c.pc // BadVAddr
		c.raiseException(excAdEL, 0)
		c.advanceCount(1)
		return 1
	}
	instr := c.bus.Read32(c.pc)
	// Advance the pipeline to the sequential successor. Branch and
	// jump execution rewrites nextPC; the instruction now sitting
	// at pc is the delay slot when the executed instruction was a
	// branch, which the branch handler flags via inDelaySlot.
	c.pc = c.nextPC
	c.nextPC = c.pc + 4
	c.inDelaySlot = false
	cycles := c.execute(instr)
	c.advanceCount(cycles)
	return cycles
}

// branch applies a branch decision made by the instruction at
// curPC. The delay slot (already at pc) is flagged as in a delay
// slot whether or not the branch is taken; a taken branch retargets
// nextPC.
func (c *CPU) branch(taken bool, target uint32) {
	c.inDelaySlot = true
	if taken {
		c.nextPC = target
	}
}

// branchLikely applies a branch likely decision (BEQL, BNEL,
// BLEZL, BGTZL, BLTZL, BGEZL, BLTZALL, BGEZALL). A taken branch
// behaves exactly like branch. A branch that is not taken annuls
// its delay slot: the slot instruction leaves no architectural
// trace. At execute time pc holds the slot address and nextPC the
// instruction after it, so the annulment advances the pipeline
// past the slot; the saved state stays consistent at every step
// boundary with no extra flag. The annulled fetch costs no cycle
// in this model, a documented deviation from hardware.
func (c *CPU) branchLikely(taken bool, target uint32) {
	if taken {
		c.branch(true, target)
		return
	}
	c.pc = c.nextPC
	c.nextPC = c.pc + 4
	c.inDelaySlot = false
}

// branchTarget computes a PC relative branch target.
func (c *CPU) branchTarget(off int32) uint32 {
	return uint32(int32(c.curPC+4) + off<<2)
}

// Serialize layout: every field is one little endian uint32, in
// this exact order, with no header. The size is constant.
//
//	GPRs 0..31, HI, LO, PC, nextPC, inDelaySlot,
//	cp0[32][8] in register then select order,
//	fpr 0..31, fcr 0..31 (index 31 is the FCSR),
//	icReg 0..31, llbit, lladdr, halted, countRemainder,
//	timerIRQ, vfpuFaultCount, randomState, extIP,
//	vregs 0..127, ctrl 0..31, mfvcStore 0..143, rngState 0..7,
//	spfxImm, tpfxImm, dpfxImm, spfxOn, tpfxOn, dpfxOn, cc.
const serializeWords = 32 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 32*8 + 32 + 32 + 32 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 128 + 32 + 144 + 8 + 3 + 3 + 1

// SerializeSize is the fixed byte length of a serialized CPU.
const serializeSize = serializeWords * 4

// Serialize returns the full CPU state in the fixed layout above.
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, serializeSize)
	w := make([]uint32, 0, serializeWords)
	w = append(w, c.regs[:]...)
	w = append(w, c.hi, c.lo, c.pc, c.nextPC)
	w = append(w, boolWord(c.inDelaySlot))
	for r := 0; r < 32; r++ {
		for s := 0; s < 8; s++ {
			w = append(w, c.cp0[r][s])
		}
	}
	w = append(w, c.fpr[:]...)
	w = append(w, c.fcr[:]...)
	w = append(w, c.icReg[:]...)
	w = append(w, boolWord(c.llbit), c.lladdr, boolWord(c.halted),
		c.countRemainder, boolWord(c.timerIRQ), uint32(c.vfpuFaultCount),
		c.randomState, c.extIP)
	w = append(w, c.vregs[:]...)
	w = append(w, c.ctrl[:]...)
	w = append(w, c.mfvcStore[:]...)
	w = append(w, c.rngState[:]...)
	w = append(w, c.spfxImm, c.tpfxImm, c.dpfxImm)
	w = append(w, boolWord(c.spfxOn), boolWord(c.tpfxOn), boolWord(c.dpfxOn))
	w = append(w, c.cc)
	for i, v := range w {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[i*4:], v)
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize. It returns an
// error unless the length matches the fixed layout exactly.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) != serializeSize {
		return errBadStateSize
	}
	rd := func(i int) uint32 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[i*4:]) }
	i := 0
	next := func() uint32 { v := rd(i); i++; return v }
	for r := 0; r < 32; r++ {
		c.regs[r] = next()
	}
	c.regs[0] = 0
	c.hi = next()
	c.lo = next()
	c.pc = next()
	c.nextPC = next()
	c.inDelaySlot = next() != 0
	for r := 0; r < 32; r++ {
		for s := 0; s < 8; s++ {
			c.cp0[r][s] = next()
		}
	}
	for r := 0; r < 32; r++ {
		c.fpr[r] = next()
	}
	for r := 0; r < 32; r++ {
		c.fcr[r] = next()
	}
	for r := 0; r < 32; r++ {
		c.icReg[r] = next()
	}
	c.llbit = next() != 0
	c.lladdr = next()
	c.halted = next() != 0
	c.countRemainder = next()
	c.timerIRQ = next() != 0
	c.vfpuFaultCount = int(next())
	c.randomState = next()
	c.extIP = next()
	for r := 0; r < 128; r++ {
		c.vregs[r] = next()
	}
	for r := 0; r < 32; r++ {
		c.ctrl[r] = next()
	}
	for r := 0; r < 144; r++ {
		c.mfvcStore[r] = next()
	}
	for r := 0; r < 8; r++ {
		c.rngState[r] = next()
	}
	c.spfxImm = next()
	c.tpfxImm = next()
	c.dpfxImm = next()
	c.spfxOn = next() != 0
	c.tpfxOn = next() != 0
	c.dpfxOn = next() != 0
	c.cc = next()
	c.curPC = c.pc
	c.curDelay = c.inDelaySlot
	return nil
}

func boolWord(b bool) uint32 {
	if b {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

type stateError string

func (e stateError) Error() string { return string(e) }

const errBadStateSize = stateError("allegrex: serialized state has wrong length")

// ThreadStatus is the CP0 Status value a PSP thread context
// starts with: the FPU enabled (CU1), user mode, interrupts
// enabled, and the exception vector in RAM (BEV clear, ERL and
// EXL clear), so guest exception handlers installed at
// 0x80000180 receive faults. A bare CPU reset instead carries
// the boot value BEV|ERL; the pspautotests framework handler
// (which skips faulting data words embedded in code streams)
// only works with the thread value, which is how the corpus
// pinned this down.
const ThreadStatus = StatusCU1 | 0x11

// SetSR replaces the CP0 Status register. The kernel uses it
// when building a new thread's context.
func (c *CPU) SetSR(v uint32) { c.cp0[12][0] = v }

// ClearLL drops any outstanding LL reservation. The kernel calls
// it at the points where hardware loses the reservation: syscall
// dispatch (the SYSCALL exception breaks it) and thread switches
// (the return from the kernel through ERET breaks it). The
// pspautotests llsc case measures exactly this behavior.
func (c *CPU) ClearLL() { c.llbit = false }

// DefaultFCSR is the FPU control register value a PSP thread
// starts with: rounding mode nearest, the overflow, divide by
// zero and invalid operation enables set (0x00000E00, recorded by
// the pspautotests fcr test's initial readback).
const DefaultFCSR = 0x00000E00

// SetFCSR sets the FPU control and status register. The kernel
// uses it when building a new thread's context.
func (c *CPU) SetFCSR(v uint32) { c.fcr[31] = v }


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex/allegrex_test.go ====================

package allegrex

import "testing"

// Fake bus: 1 MB of flat RAM at base 0, little endian, addresses
// wrap inside the RAM so exception vectors are safe to fetch.
type ram struct{ b []byte }

func newRAM() *ram { return &ram{b: make([]byte, 1<<20)} }

func (r *ram) Read8(a uint32) uint8 { return r.b[a&(uint32(len(r.b))-1)] }
func (r *ram) Read16(a uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(r.Read8(a)) | uint16(r.Read8(a+1))<<8
}
func (r *ram) Read32(a uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(r.Read16(a)) | uint32(r.Read16(a+2))<<16
}
func (r *ram) Write8(a uint32, v uint8) { r.b[a&(uint32(len(r.b))-1)] = v }
func (r *ram) Write16(a uint32, v uint16) {
	r.Write8(a, uint8(v))
	r.Write8(a+1, uint8(v>>8))
}
func (r *ram) Write32(a uint32, v uint32) {
	r.Write16(a, uint16(v))
	r.Write16(a+2, uint16(v>>16))
}
func (r *ram) load(addr uint32, words ...uint32) {
	for i, w := range words {
		r.Write32(addr+uint32(4*i), w)
	}
}

type harness struct {
	c *CPU
	r *ram
}

// newHarness returns a CPU at entry 0 with Status = BEV only, so
// ERL and EXL are clear and exceptions save EPC and Cause normally.
func newHarness() *harness {
	r := newRAM()
	c := New(r)
	c.Reset(0)
	c.cp0[12][0] = 0x00400000
	return &harness{c: c, r: r}
}

func (h *harness) run(n int) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		h.c.Step()
	}
}

// Instruction encoders.
func encR(rs, rt, rd, sa, fn uint32) uint32 {
	return rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | sa<<6 | fn
}
func encSP2(rs, rt, rd, fn uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x1C<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | fn
}
func encSP3(rs, rt, rd, sa, fn uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x1F<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | rd<<11 | sa<<6 | fn
}
func encI(op, rs, rt, imm uint32) uint32 {
	return op<<26 | rs<<21 | rt<<16 | (imm & 0xFFFF)
}
func encJ(op, target uint32) uint32 {
	return op<<26 | (target>>2)&0x03FFFFFF
}
func encMFC0(rt, reg, sel uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x10<<26 | 0<<21 | rt<<16 | reg<<11 | sel
}
func encMTC0(rt, reg, sel uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x10<<26 | 4<<21 | rt<<16 | reg<<11 | sel
}

func excCode(c *CPU) uint32 { return (c.CP0(13, 0) >> 2) & 0x1F }
func excCE(c *CPU) uint32   { return (c.CP0(13, 0) >> 28) & 3 }

func TestALUAndShifts(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x0F, 0, 8, 0x1234), // lui r8, 0x1234
		encI(0x0D, 8, 8, 0x5678), // ori r8, r8, 0x5678
		encI(0x09, 0, 9, 0xFFFF), // addiu r9, r0, -1
		encR(8, 9, 10, 0, 0x21),  // addu r10, r8, r9
		encR(8, 9, 11, 0, 0x24),  // and r11, r8, r9
		encR(0, 9, 12, 0, 0x27),  // nor r12, r0, r9
		encR(9, 8, 13, 0, 0x2A),  // slt r13, r9, r8
		encR(9, 8, 14, 0, 0x2B),  // sltu r14, r9, r8
		encR(0, 8, 15, 4, 0x00),  // sll r15, r8, 4
		encR(0, 8, 16, 8, 0x03),  // sra r16, r8, 8
		encR(0, 9, 17, 28, 0x02), // srl r17, r9, 28
	)
	h.run(11)
	want := map[int]uint32{
		8: 0x12345678, 9: 0xFFFFFFFF, 10: 0x12345677, 11: 0x12345678,
		12: 0, 13: 1, 14: 0, 15: 0x23456780, 16: 0x00123456, 17: 0xF,
	}
	for reg, v := range want {
		if got := h.c.Reg(reg); got != v {
			t.Errorf("r%d = %#08x, want %#08x", reg, got, v)
		}
	}
	// r0 writes are discarded.
	h2 := newHarness()
	h2.r.load(0, encI(0x09, 0, 0, 5))
	h2.run(1)
	if h2.c.Reg(0) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("r0 = %#x, want 0", h2.c.Reg(0))
	}
}

func TestRotate(t *testing.T) {
	// ROTR is SRL with the rs field equal to 1.
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0x12345678)
	h.r.load(0,
		encR(1, 9, 8, 0, 0x02),  // rotr r8, r9, 0 (identity)
		encR(1, 9, 10, 8, 0x02), // rotr r10, r9, 8
	)
	h.run(2)
	if got := h.c.Reg(8); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("rotr 0 = %#08x", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != 0x78123456 {
		t.Errorf("rotr 8 = %#08x, want 0x78123456", got)
	}
	h2 := newHarness()
	h2.c.SetReg(9, 0x00000001)
	h2.r.load(0, encR(1, 9, 8, 31, 0x02)) // rotr by 31
	h2.run(1)
	if got := h2.c.Reg(8); got != 2 {
		t.Errorf("rotr 31 of 1 = %#08x, want 2", got)
	}
	// ROTRV is SRLV with bit 6 set; a shift register value of 33
	// rotates by 1.
	h3 := newHarness()
	h3.c.SetReg(9, 0x80000000)
	h3.c.SetReg(10, 33)
	h3.r.load(0, encR(10, 9, 8, 1, 0x06)) // rotrv r8, r9, r10
	h3.run(1)
	if got := h3.c.Reg(8); got != 0x40000000 {
		t.Errorf("rotrv 33 = %#08x, want 0x40000000", got)
	}
}

func TestExtIns(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0xDEADBEEF)
	h.r.load(0,
		encSP3(9, 8, 31, 0, 0),  // ext r8, r9, 0, 32 (identity)
		encSP3(9, 10, 0, 31, 0), // ext r10, r9, 31, 1
		encSP3(9, 11, 7, 8, 0),  // ext r11, r9, 8, 8
	)
	h.run(3)
	if got := h.c.Reg(8); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("ext full = %#08x", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("ext top bit = %#08x, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(11); got != 0xBE {
		t.Errorf("ext mid = %#08x, want 0xBE", got)
	}
	// INS: top insert (pos+size = 32), full replace, partial.
	h2 := newHarness()
	h2.c.SetReg(9, 0x000000AB)
	h2.c.SetReg(8, 0x12345678)
	h2.c.SetReg(10, 0xFFFFFFFF)
	h2.c.SetReg(11, 0xAAAAAAAA)
	h2.r.load(0,
		encSP3(9, 8, 31, 24, 4), // ins r8, r9, 24, 8
		encSP3(9, 10, 31, 0, 4), // ins r10, r9, 0, 32
		encSP3(9, 11, 15, 8, 4), // ins r11, r9, 8, 8
	)
	h2.run(3)
	if got := h2.c.Reg(8); got != 0xAB345678 {
		t.Errorf("ins top = %#08x, want 0xAB345678", got)
	}
	if got := h2.c.Reg(10); got != 0x000000AB {
		t.Errorf("ins full = %#08x, want 0xAB", got)
	}
	if got := h2.c.Reg(11); got != 0xAAAAABAA {
		t.Errorf("ins mid = %#08x, want 0xAAAAABAA", got)
	}
}

func TestBSHFL(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		sa  uint32
		in  uint32
		out uint32
	}{
		{16, 0x00000080, 0xFFFFFF80}, // seb negative
		{16, 0x0000007F, 0x0000007F}, // seb positive
		{24, 0x00008000, 0xFFFF8000}, // seh negative
		{24, 0x00007FFF, 0x00007FFF}, // seh positive
		{2, 0x11223344, 0x22114433},  // wsbh
		{20, 0x00000001, 0x80000000}, // bitrev
		{20, 0xFFFF0000, 0x0000FFFF}, // bitrev
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		h := newHarness()
		h.c.SetReg(9, tc.in)
		h.r.load(0, encSP3(0, 9, 8, tc.sa, 0x20))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.Reg(8); got != tc.out {
			t.Errorf("bshfl sa=%d in=%#08x: got %#08x want %#08x", tc.sa, tc.in, got, tc.out)
		}
	}
}

func TestUnalignedAccess(t *testing.T) {
	const old = 0x11223344
	// The LWL and SWL vectors were re-derived from the
	// pspautotests lsu matrix (hardware recorded): the original
	// vectors pinned a big-endian merge that the corpus refutes.
	// LWL: (word << 8*(3-a)) with the low (3-a) bytes of the old
	// register surviving. SWL mirrors it.
	lwlWant := [4]uint32{0xDD223344, 0xCCDD3344, 0xBBCCDD44, 0xAABBCCDD}
	lwrWant := [4]uint32{0xAABBCCDD, 0x11AABBCC, 0x1122AABB, 0x112233AA}
	swlWant := [4]uint32{0xAABBCC11, 0xAABB1122, 0xAA112233, 0x11223344}
	swrWant := [4]uint32{0x11223344, 0x223344DD, 0x3344CCDD, 0x44BBCCDD}
	for a := uint32(0); a < 4; a++ {
		// LWL
		h := newHarness()
		h.r.Write32(0x100, 0xAABBCCDD)
		h.c.SetReg(8, 0x100+a)
		h.c.SetReg(9, old)
		h.r.load(0, encI(0x22, 8, 9, 0))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != lwlWant[a] {
			t.Errorf("lwl a=%d: got %#08x want %#08x", a, got, lwlWant[a])
		}
		// LWR
		h = newHarness()
		h.r.Write32(0x100, 0xAABBCCDD)
		h.c.SetReg(8, 0x100+a)
		h.c.SetReg(9, old)
		h.r.load(0, encI(0x26, 8, 9, 0))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != lwrWant[a] {
			t.Errorf("lwr a=%d: got %#08x want %#08x", a, got, lwrWant[a])
		}
		// SWL
		h = newHarness()
		h.r.Write32(0x100, 0xAABBCCDD)
		h.c.SetReg(8, 0x100+a)
		h.c.SetReg(9, old)
		h.r.load(0, encI(0x2A, 8, 9, 0))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.r.Read32(0x100); got != swlWant[a] {
			t.Errorf("swl a=%d: mem %#08x want %#08x", a, got, swlWant[a])
		}
		// SWR
		h = newHarness()
		h.r.Write32(0x100, 0xAABBCCDD)
		h.c.SetReg(8, 0x100+a)
		h.c.SetReg(9, old)
		h.r.load(0, encI(0x2E, 8, 9, 0))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.r.Read32(0x100); got != swrWant[a] {
			t.Errorf("swr a=%d: mem %#08x want %#08x", a, got, swrWant[a])
		}
	}
	// Classic pair: LWL at p+3 then LWR at p assembles 0x12345678
	// stored as bytes across a word boundary at p = 0x101.
	h := newHarness()
	for i, b := range []byte{0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12} {
		h.r.Write8(0x101+uint32(i), b)
	}
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0x101)
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x22, 8, 9, 3), // lwl r9, 3(r8)
		encI(0x26, 8, 9, 0), // lwr r9, 0(r8)
	)
	h.run(2)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("lwl/lwr pair = %#08x, want 0x12345678", got)
	}
}

func TestLLSC(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	h.r.Write32(0x200, 0xAAAA)
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0x200)
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0x1234)
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x30, 8, 10, 0), // ll r10, 0(r8)
		encI(0x38, 8, 9, 0),  // sc r9, 0(r8)
		encI(0x38, 8, 9, 0),  // second sc: the reservation survives
	)
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != 0xAAAA {
		t.Errorf("ll = %#08x", got)
	}
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("sc after ll = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := h.r.Read32(0x200); got != 0x1234 {
		t.Errorf("sc stored %#08x", got)
	}
	// Per the pspautotests llsc matrix, a successful SC does not
	// consume the reservation on this hardware; a syscall,
	// exception or thread switch breaks it instead.
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0x9999)
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("second sc = %d, want 1 (reservation persists)", got)
	}
	if got := h.r.Read32(0x200); got != 0x9999 {
		t.Errorf("second sc stored %#08x", got)
	}
	// ERET clears LLbit: load linked, return from a fake exception
	// whose EPC points at the SC, then the SC must fail.
	h2 := newHarness()
	h2.r.Write32(0x200, 0xBBBB)
	h2.c.SetReg(8, 0x200)
	h2.c.SetReg(9, 0x777)
	h2.r.load(0,
		encI(0x30, 8, 10, 0), // 0: ll
		0x42000018,           // 4: eret
		encI(0x38, 8, 9, 0),  // 8: sc
	)
	h2.c.cp0[14][0] = 8 // EPC = the sc instruction
	h2.run(2)           // ll, then eret jumps to 8
	if h2.c.PC() != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("after eret PC = %#x, want 8", h2.c.PC())
	}
	h2.run(1)
	if got := h2.c.Reg(9); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("sc after eret = %d, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestMultiplyDivideFamily(t *testing.T) {
	// MADD with a carry out of LO into HI.
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.hi, h.c.lo = 0, 0xFFFFFFFF
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0x10000)
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0x10000)
	h.r.load(0, encSP2(8, 9, 0, 0x00)) // madd r8, r9
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.HI() != 1 || h.c.LO() != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("madd: HI=%#08x LO=%#08x, want HI=1 LO=0xFFFFFFFF", h.c.HI(), h.c.LO())
	}
	// MSUB borrowing below zero.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 1)
	h.c.SetReg(9, 1)
	h.r.load(0, encSP2(8, 9, 0, 0x04)) // msub r8, r9
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.HI() != 0xFFFFFFFF || h.c.LO() != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("msub: HI=%#08x LO=%#08x, want both 0xFFFFFFFF", h.c.HI(), h.c.LO())
	}
	// MUL writes rd only and leaves HI/LO alone.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.hi, h.c.lo = 0x11111111, 0x22222222
	h.c.SetReg(8, 6)
	h.c.SetReg(9, 7)
	h.r.load(0, encSP2(8, 9, 10, 0x02)) // mul r10, r8, r9
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != 42 {
		t.Errorf("mul = %d, want 42", got)
	}
	if h.c.HI() != 0x11111111 || h.c.LO() != 0x22222222 {
		t.Errorf("mul touched HI/LO: %#08x %#08x", h.c.HI(), h.c.LO())
	}
	// CLZ and CLO.
	clzCases := []struct {
		fn  uint32
		in  uint32
		out uint32
	}{
		{0x20, 0, 32},
		{0x21, 0xFFFFFFFF, 32},
		{0x20, 0x00F00000, 8},
		{0x21, 0xFF000000, 8},
	}
	for _, tc := range clzCases {
		h = newHarness()
		h.c.SetReg(8, tc.in)
		h.r.load(0, encSP2(8, 10, 10, tc.fn))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != tc.out {
			t.Errorf("fn %#x in %#08x: got %d want %d", tc.fn, tc.in, got, tc.out)
		}
	}
}

func TestDivByZeroAndEdges(t *testing.T) {
	div := func(signed bool, a, b uint32) (uint32, uint32) {
		h := newHarness()
		h.c.SetReg(8, a)
		h.c.SetReg(9, b)
		fn := uint32(0x1A)
		if !signed {
			fn = 0x1B
		}
		h.r.load(0, encR(8, 9, 0, 0, fn))
		h.run(1)
		return h.c.LO(), h.c.HI()
	}
	if lo, hi := div(true, 5, 0); lo != 0xFFFFFFFF || hi != 5 {
		t.Errorf("div 5/0: LO=%#08x HI=%#08x", lo, hi)
	}
	if lo, hi := div(true, 0xFFFFFFFB, 0); lo != 1 || hi != 0xFFFFFFFB {
		t.Errorf("div -5/0: LO=%#08x HI=%#08x", lo, hi)
	}
	// The unsigned rule is the corpus proven one: dividends
	// under 0x10000 yield LO 0x0000FFFF (see TestDivuByZeroRule).
	if lo, hi := div(false, 5, 0); lo != 0x0000FFFF || hi != 5 {
		t.Errorf("divu 5/0: LO=%#08x HI=%#08x", lo, hi)
	}
	if lo, hi := div(false, 100, 7); lo != 14 || hi != 2 {
		t.Errorf("divu 100/7: LO=%d HI=%d", lo, hi)
	}
	if lo, hi := div(true, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF); lo != 0x80000000 || hi != 0 {
		t.Errorf("div INT_MIN/-1: LO=%#08x HI=%#08x", lo, hi)
	}
	if lo, hi := div(true, 100, 7); lo != 14 || hi != 2 {
		t.Errorf("div 100/7: LO=%d HI=%d", lo, hi)
	}
}

func TestMovzMovn(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0xABCD)
	h.r.load(0,
		encR(8, 0, 9, 0, 0x0A),   // movz r9, r8, r0 (taken)
		encR(8, 0, 10, 0, 0x0B),  // movn r10, r8, r0 (not taken)
		encI(0x09, 0, 11, 1),     // addiu r11, r0, 1
		encR(8, 11, 12, 0, 0x0A), // movz r12, r8, r11 (not taken)
		encR(8, 11, 13, 0, 0x0B), // movn r13, r8, r11 (taken)
	)
	h.run(5)
	want := map[int]uint32{9: 0xABCD, 10: 0, 12: 0, 13: 0xABCD}
	for reg, v := range want {
		if got := h.c.Reg(reg); got != v {
			t.Errorf("r%d = %#08x, want %#08x", reg, got, v)
		}
	}
}

func TestBranchDelaySlotAndLinks(t *testing.T) {
	// A taken branch executes its delay slot exactly once and
	// skips the instruction after it.
	h := newHarness()
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x04, 0, 0, 2),   // 0: beq r0, r0, +2 -> 12
		encI(0x09, 8, 8, 1),   // 4: delay slot, r8 += 1
		encI(0x09, 8, 8, 100), // 8: skipped
		encI(0x09, 0, 9, 7),   // 12: r9 = 7
	)
	h.run(3)
	if got := h.c.Reg(8); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("delay slot count r8 = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 7 {
		t.Errorf("r9 = %d, want 7", got)
	}
	// JAL links pc+8.
	h = newHarness()
	h.r.load(0,
		encJ(0x03, 16),        // 0: jal 16
		encI(0x09, 8, 8, 1),   // 4: delay slot
		encI(0x09, 8, 8, 100), // 8: skipped
		0,                     // 12
		encI(0x09, 0, 9, 3),   // 16: r9 = 3
	)
	h.run(3)
	if got := h.c.Reg(31); got != 8 {
		t.Errorf("jal link r31 = %d, want 8", got)
	}
	if h.c.Reg(8) != 1 || h.c.Reg(9) != 3 {
		t.Errorf("jal flow: r8=%d r9=%d", h.c.Reg(8), h.c.Reg(9))
	}
	// BLTZAL writes the link even when the branch is not taken.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 5)
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x01, 8, 0x10, 4), // 0: bltzal r8, +4 (not taken)
		encI(0x09, 0, 9, 1),    // 4: delay slot
	)
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.Reg(31); got != 8 {
		t.Errorf("bltzal link when not taken = %d, want 8", got)
	}
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("bltzal delay slot r9 = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	// BGEZAL taken also links.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 5)
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x01, 8, 0x11, 2), // 0: bgezal r8, +2 -> 12
		encI(0x09, 0, 9, 1),    // 4: delay slot
		encI(0x09, 0, 9, 100),  // 8: skipped
		encI(0x09, 0, 10, 2),   // 12: r10 = 2
	)
	h.run(3)
	if h.c.Reg(31) != 8 || h.c.Reg(9) != 1 || h.c.Reg(10) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("bgezal: r31=%d r9=%d r10=%d", h.c.Reg(31), h.c.Reg(9), h.c.Reg(10))
	}
}

func TestLoadUseInterlock(t *testing.T) {
	// No load delay: the instruction right after a LW sees the
	// loaded value.
	h := newHarness()
	h.r.Write32(0x300, 42)
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x23, 0, 8, 0x300), // lw r8, 0x300(r0)
		encR(8, 8, 9, 0, 0x21),  // addu r9, r8, r8
	)
	h.run(2)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 84 {
		t.Errorf("load/use = %d, want 84", got)
	}
}

func TestExceptions(t *testing.T) {
	// SYSCALL at 0x40 with BEV set vectors to 0xBFC00380.
	h := newHarness()
	h.r.load(0x40, encR(0, 0, 0, 0, 0x0C))
	h.c.SetPC(0x40)
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.PC() != 0xBFC00380 {
		t.Errorf("syscall vector PC = %#x", h.c.PC())
	}
	if got := h.c.CP0(14, 0); got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("EPC = %#x, want 0x40", got)
	}
	if excCode(h.c) != 8 {
		t.Errorf("ExcCode = %d, want 8", excCode(h.c))
	}
	if h.c.CP0(12, 0)&2 == 0 {
		t.Errorf("EXL not set after syscall")
	}
	// Misaligned LW raises AdEL with BadVAddr and no bus write.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0x101)
	h.r.load(0, encI(0x23, 9, 8, 0))
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 4 {
		t.Errorf("misaligned lw ExcCode = %d, want 4", excCode(h.c))
	}
	if got := h.c.CP0(8, 0); got != 0x101 {
		t.Errorf("BadVAddr = %#x, want 0x101", got)
	}
	// Misaligned SW raises AdES.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0x102)
	h.r.load(0, encI(0x2B, 9, 8, 0))
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 5 {
		t.Errorf("misaligned sw ExcCode = %d, want 5", excCode(h.c))
	}
	// ADD overflow raises Ov and does not write the destination.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0x7FFFFFFF)
	h.c.SetReg(9, 1)
	h.c.SetReg(10, 0x55)
	h.r.load(0, encR(8, 9, 10, 0, 0x20))
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 12 {
		t.Errorf("add overflow ExcCode = %d, want 12", excCode(h.c))
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != 0x55 {
		t.Errorf("overflow wrote rd: %#08x", got)
	}
	// BREAK raises Bp.
	h = newHarness()
	h.r.load(0, encR(0, 0, 0, 0, 0x0D))
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 9 {
		t.Errorf("break ExcCode = %d, want 9", excCode(h.c))
	}
	// An exception in a delay slot sets BD and EPC = branch address.
	h = newHarness()
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x04, 0, 0, 10),   // 0: beq r0, r0, far
		encR(0, 0, 0, 0, 0x0C), // 4: syscall in the delay slot
	)
	h.run(2)
	if got := h.c.CP0(14, 0); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("delay slot EPC = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
	if h.c.CP0(13, 0)&(1<<31) == 0 {
		t.Errorf("BD not set for delay slot exception")
	}
	if excCode(h.c) != 8 {
		t.Errorf("delay slot ExcCode = %d, want 8", excCode(h.c))
	}
	// Trap instruction TEQ with equal operands raises Tr.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 3)
	h.c.SetReg(9, 3)
	h.r.load(0, encR(8, 9, 0, 0, 0x34))
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 13 {
		t.Errorf("teq ExcCode = %d, want 13", excCode(h.c))
	}
}

func TestInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	// Status = BEV | IM2 | IE, written through a real MTC0.
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0x00400401)
	h.r.load(0,
		encMTC0(8, 12, 0), // 0: mtc0 r8, Status
		0,                 // 4: nop
		0,                 // 8: nop
	)
	h.run(1)
	h.c.SetInterruptLines(1 << 2)
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.PC() != 0xBFC00380 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt vector PC = %#x, want 0xBFC00380", h.c.PC())
	}
	if got := h.c.CP0(14, 0); got != 4 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt EPC = %#x, want 4", got)
	}
	if excCode(h.c) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt ExcCode = %d, want 0", excCode(h.c))
	}
	// With Cause.IV set the vector gains 0x80.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.cp0[12][0] = 0x00400401
	h.c.cp0[13][0] = 1 << 23 // Cause.IV
	h.c.SetInterruptLines(1 << 2)
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.PC() != 0xBFC00400 {
		t.Errorf("interrupt IV vector PC = %#x, want 0xBFC00400", h.c.PC())
	}
	// A masked line does not interrupt.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.cp0[12][0] = 0x00400001 // IE only, no IM bits
	h.c.SetInterruptLines(1 << 2)
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.PC() != 4 { // just the nop at 0 executed
		t.Errorf("masked interrupt changed flow: PC = %#x", h.c.PC())
	}
	if excCode(h.c) != 0 && h.c.CP0(12, 0)&2 != 0 {
		t.Errorf("masked interrupt raised an exception")
	}
}

func TestHaltAndWake(t *testing.T) {
	// Enabled interrupt wakes the halted CPU.
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.cp0[12][0] = 0x00400401 // BEV | IM2 | IE
	h.r.load(0, 0x70000000, 0)  // halt, nop
	h.run(1)
	if !h.c.Halted() {
		t.Fatalf("HALT did not halt")
	}
	if h.c.PC() != 4 {
		t.Errorf("PC after HALT = %#x, want 4", h.c.PC())
	}
	if n := h.c.Step(); n != 1 || h.c.PC() != 4 || !h.c.Halted() {
		t.Errorf("halted step: cycles=%d PC=%#x halted=%v", n, h.c.PC(), h.c.Halted())
	}
	h.c.SetInterruptLines(1 << 2)
	h.c.Step()
	if h.c.Halted() {
		t.Errorf("enabled interrupt did not wake HALT")
	}
	if h.c.PC() != 0xBFC00380 {
		t.Errorf("wake vector PC = %#x", h.c.PC())
	}
	if got := h.c.CP0(14, 0); got != 4 {
		t.Errorf("wake EPC = %#x, want 4", got)
	}
	// A line whose IM bit is clear does not wake it.
	h = newHarness()
	h.c.cp0[12][0] = 0x00400001 // IE only
	h.r.load(0, 0x70000000, 0)
	h.run(1)
	h.c.SetInterruptLines(1 << 2)
	h.c.Step()
	if !h.c.Halted() || h.c.PC() != 4 {
		t.Errorf("masked line woke HALT: halted=%v PC=%#x", h.c.Halted(), h.c.PC())
	}
}

func TestCOPFaults(t *testing.T) {
	// The VFPU is implemented now: a bare COP2 word is MFC2 with
	// rs=0, and it executes without any exception or fault count.
	h := newHarness()
	h.r.load(0, 0x12<<26)
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 0 || h.c.VFPUFaultCount() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("cop2 mfc2: code=%d count=%d, want 0/0", excCode(h.c), h.c.VFPUFaultCount())
	}
	// LWC2 is LV.S now and executes without fault.
	h = newHarness()
	h.r.load(0, encI(0x32, 0, 8, 0))
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 0 || h.c.VFPUFaultCount() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("lv.s: code=%d count=%d, want 0/0", excCode(h.c), h.c.VFPUFaultCount())
	}
	// SV.S and the quad load and store families also execute.
	for _, op := range []uint32{0x3A, 0x36, 0x3E} {
		h = newHarness()
		h.r.load(0, encI(op, 0, 8, 0))
		h.run(1)
		if h.c.VFPUFaultCount() != 0 {
			t.Errorf("op %#x: VFPUFaultCount = %d, want 0", op, h.c.VFPUFaultCount())
		}
	}
	// COP1 with CU1 clear: CpU with CE=1.
	h = newHarness()               // Status has no CU1
	h.r.load(0, 0x11<<26|0x10<<21) // cop1 fmt S add.s skeleton
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 11 || excCE(h.c) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("cop1 disabled: code=%d CE=%d, want 11/1", excCode(h.c), excCE(h.c))
	}
	// Primary opcode 0x35 is the VFPU LVL.Q/LVR.Q slot on the
	// Allegrex (the corpus vector binary's words 0xD4600000 and
	// kin pin it); the MIPS LDC1 reading of the same opcode
	// does not exist here, so the word executes as a load.
	h = newHarness()
	h.r.load(0, 0xD4600000) // lvl.q C000, 0($v1)
	h.run(1)
	if excCode(h.c) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("lvl.q ExcCode = %d, want 0", excCode(h.c))
	}
}

func TestMFICMTIC(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0xDEADBEEF)
	h.r.load(0,
		encSP2(0, 8, 5, 0x26),  // mtic r8, ic5
		encSP2(0, 9, 5, 0x24),  // mfic r9, ic5
		encSP2(0, 10, 6, 0x24), // mfic r10, ic6 (untouched)
	)
	h.run(3)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Errorf("mfic = %#08x, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("mfic untouched = %#08x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	prog := []uint32{
		encI(0x09, 0, 8, 100),     // 0: addiu r8, r0, 100
		encI(0x09, 0, 9, 7),       // 4: addiu r9, r0, 7
		encR(8, 9, 0, 0, 0x18),    // 8: mult r8, r9
		encR(0, 0, 10, 0, 0x12),   // 12: mflo r10
		encI(0x23, 0, 11, 0x400),  // 16: lw r11, 0x400(r0)
		encR(11, 10, 12, 0, 0x21), // 20: addu r12, r11, r10
		encI(0x04, 0, 0, 1),       // 24: beq r0, r0, +1 -> 32
		encI(0x09, 0, 13, 5),      // 28: delay slot
		encI(0x2B, 0, 12, 0x404),  // 32: sw r12, 0x404(r0)
		encSP2(8, 9, 0, 0x00),     // 36: madd r8, r9
		0x70000000,                // 40: halt
	}
	setup := func() *harness {
		h := newHarness()
		h.r.Write32(0x400, 12345)
		h.r.load(0, prog...)
		return h
	}
	a := setup()
	a.run(5) // stop mid program, right after the LW
	snap := a.c.Serialize()
	if len(snap) != serializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize len = %d, want %d", len(snap), serializeSize)
	}
	b := setup()
	if err := b.c.Deserialize(snap); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	// Continue both the same distance (includes the branch, the
	// store, the madd, the halt, and halted ticks).
	a.run(8)
	b.run(8)
	if got, want := b.c.Serialize(), a.c.Serialize(); string(got) != string(want) {
		t.Errorf("state diverged after deserialize round trip")
		for i := range want {
			if got[i] != want[i] {
				t.Errorf("first diff at byte %d: got %#x want %#x", i, got[i], want[i])
				break
			}
		}
	}
	if a.r.Read32(0x404) != b.r.Read32(0x404) {
		t.Errorf("stored values differ: %#08x vs %#08x", a.r.Read32(0x404), b.r.Read32(0x404))
	}
	if err := b.c.Deserialize(snap[:len(snap)-4]); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("short state accepted")
	}
	if err := b.c.Deserialize(nil); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("empty state accepted")
	}
}

func TestCP0Basics(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	// PRId is a constant; writes to it are ignored.
	if got := h.c.CP0(15, 0); got != 0x00006542 {
		t.Errorf("PRId = %#08x, want 0x00006542", got)
	}
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0xFFFF)
	h.r.load(0,
		encMTC0(8, 15, 0),  // mtc0 r8, PRId (ignored)
		encMFC0(9, 15, 0),  // mfc0 r9, PRId
		encMTC0(8, 15, 1),  // mtc0 r8, EBase
		encMFC0(10, 15, 1), // mfc0 r10, EBase
		encMFC0(11, 9, 0),  // mfc0 r11, Count
	)
	h.run(5)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 0x00006542 {
		t.Errorf("mfc0 PRId = %#08x", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(10); got != 0xFFFF {
		t.Errorf("mfc0 EBase = %#08x, want 0xFFFF", got)
	}
	// Count advances at half rate: 5 one cycle steps give 2 or 3
	// depending on the remainder; after these exact steps the
	// accumulated cycles are 5, so Count must be 2 with remainder 1.
	if got := h.c.Reg(11); got > 3 {
		t.Errorf("Count grew too fast: %d", got)
	}
	// Writing Compare clears a latched timer interrupt.
	h.c.cp0[9][0] = 10
	h.c.cp0[11][0] = 12
	h.c.advanceCount(4) // Count 10 -> 12, timer latches
	if !h.c.timerIRQ {
		t.Fatalf("timer did not latch at Count == Compare")
	}
	h2 := newHarness()
	h2.c.SetReg(8, 77)
	h2.r.load(0, encMTC0(8, 11, 0))
	h2.c.timerIRQ = true
	h2.run(1)
	if h2.c.timerIRQ {
		t.Errorf("MTC0 Compare did not clear the timer latch")
	}
}

func TestResetContract(t *testing.T) {
	r := newRAM()
	c := New(r)
	c.Reset(0x800)
	if c.PC() != 0x800 {
		t.Errorf("Reset PC = %#x", c.PC())
	}
	if got := c.CP0(12, 0); got != 0x00400004 {
		t.Errorf("Reset Status = %#08x, want 0x00400004", got)
	}
	if got := c.CP0(13, 0); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Reset Cause = %#08x, want 0", got)
	}
	if c.Halted() {
		t.Errorf("Reset left CPU halted")
	}
	if n := c.Step(); n < 1 {
		t.Errorf("Step cycles = %d, want >= 1", n)
	}
}

// TestAllegrexSpecialMulAcc pins the Allegrex placement of the
// multiply accumulate family and CLZ/CLO: they live in the
// SPECIAL table (funct 0x1C/0x1D/0x2E/0x2F and 0x16/0x17), not in
// SPECIAL2 as standard MIPS32 has them. The pspautotests corpus
// binaries encode them there (cpu_alu's test_madd faulted with a
// reserved instruction exception until this was implemented).
func TestAllegrexSpecialMulAcc(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.hi, h.c.lo = 0, 0xFFFFFFFF
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0x10000)
	h.c.SetReg(9, 0x10000)
	h.r.load(0, encR(8, 9, 0, 0, 0x1C)) // madd r8, r9 (SPECIAL)
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.HI() != 1 || h.c.LO() != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("SPECIAL madd: HI=%#08x LO=%#08x, want HI=1 LO=0xFFFFFFFF", h.c.HI(), h.c.LO())
	}
	h2 := newHarness()
	h2.c.SetReg(8, 1)
	h2.c.SetReg(9, 1)
	h2.r.load(0, encR(8, 9, 0, 0, 0x2E)) // msub r8, r9 (SPECIAL)
	h2.run(1)
	if h2.c.HI() != 0xFFFFFFFF || h2.c.LO() != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Errorf("SPECIAL msub: HI=%#08x LO=%#08x, want both 0xFFFFFFFF", h2.c.HI(), h2.c.LO())
	}
	h3 := newHarness()
	h3.c.SetReg(8, 0x00F00000)
	h3.r.load(0, encR(8, 0, 9, 0, 0x16)) // clz r9, r8 (SPECIAL)
	h3.run(1)
	if got := h3.c.Reg(9); got != 8 {
		t.Errorf("SPECIAL clz = %d, want 8", got)
	}
}

// TestDivuByZeroRule pins the observed Allegrex unsigned divide
// by zero behavior the cpu_div corpus test checks: the quotient
// is 0x0000FFFF for dividends under 0x10000, all ones above, and
// HI always takes the dividend.
func TestDivuByZeroRule(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		dividend, wantLO uint32
	}{
		{0, 0x0000FFFF},
		{0x64, 0x0000FFFF},
		{0xFFFF, 0x0000FFFF},
		{0x10000, 0xFFFFFFFF},
		{0x12345678, 0xFFFFFFFF},
	} {
		h := newHarness()
		h.c.SetReg(8, tc.dividend)
		h.c.SetReg(9, 0)
		h.r.load(0, encR(8, 9, 0, 0, 0x1B)) // divu r8, r9
		h.run(1)
		if h.c.LO() != tc.wantLO || h.c.HI() != tc.dividend {
			t.Errorf("divu %#x / 0: HI=%#08x LO=%#08x, want HI=%#08x LO=%#08x",
				tc.dividend, h.c.HI(), h.c.LO(), tc.dividend, tc.wantLO)
		}
	}
}

// TestWSBW pins the BSHFL byte reverse (SPECIAL3 funct 0x20,
// sa 3), which PSP-1 missed: cpu_alu's wsbw thunk raised a
// reserved instruction exception without it.
func TestWSBW(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, 0x01234567)
	h.r.load(0, encSP3(0, 8, 9, 3, 0x20)) // wsbw r9, r8
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != 0x67452301 {
		t.Errorf("wsbw = %#08x, want 0x67452301", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex/exec.go ====================

package allegrex

// Integer instruction decode and execution. Cycle model
// (deterministic approximation): 1 cycle for everything except
// MULT/MULTU/MUL and the MADD/MSUB family at 2 cycles and
// DIV/DIVU at 37 cycles. Exception entry steps report 1 cycle.

func signExt16(v uint32) int32 { return int32(int16(v)) }

func (c *CPU) execute(instr uint32) int {
	op := instr >> 26
	rs := int((instr >> 21) & 31)
	rt := int((instr >> 16) & 31)
	rd := int((instr >> 11) & 31)
	sa := int((instr >> 6) & 31)
	fn := instr & 63
	imm := instr & 0xFFFF
	simm := signExt16(imm)

	switch op {
	case 0x00: // SPECIAL
		return c.execSpecial(instr, rs, rt, rd, sa, fn)
	case 0x01: // REGIMM
		return c.execRegimm(rs, rt, simm)
	case 0x02: // J
		c.branch(true, c.jumpTarget(instr))
	case 0x03: // JAL
		c.setReg(31, c.curPC+8)
		c.branch(true, c.jumpTarget(instr))
	case 0x04: // BEQ
		c.branch(c.regs[rs] == c.regs[rt], c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x05: // BNE
		c.branch(c.regs[rs] != c.regs[rt], c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x06: // BLEZ
		c.branch(int32(c.regs[rs]) <= 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x07: // BGTZ
		c.branch(int32(c.regs[rs]) > 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x14: // BEQL
		c.branchLikely(c.regs[rs] == c.regs[rt], c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x15: // BNEL
		c.branchLikely(c.regs[rs] != c.regs[rt], c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x16: // BLEZL
		c.branchLikely(int32(c.regs[rs]) <= 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x17: // BGTZL
		c.branchLikely(int32(c.regs[rs]) > 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x08: // ADDI
		sum := int64(int32(c.regs[rs])) + int64(simm)
		if sum > 0x7FFFFFFF || sum < -0x80000000 {
			c.raiseException(excOv, 0)
			return 1
		}
		c.setReg(rt, uint32(sum))
	case 0x09: // ADDIU
		c.setReg(rt, c.regs[rs]+uint32(simm))
	case 0x0A: // SLTI
		if int32(c.regs[rs]) < simm {
			c.setReg(rt, 1)
		} else {
			c.setReg(rt, 0)
		}
	case 0x0B: // SLTIU: immediate is sign extended, compare unsigned
		if c.regs[rs] < uint32(simm) {
			c.setReg(rt, 1)
		} else {
			c.setReg(rt, 0)
		}
	case 0x0C: // ANDI
		c.setReg(rt, c.regs[rs]&imm)
	case 0x0D: // ORI
		c.setReg(rt, c.regs[rs]|imm)
	case 0x0E: // XORI
		c.setReg(rt, c.regs[rs]^imm)
	case 0x0F: // LUI
		c.setReg(rt, imm<<16)
	case 0x10: // COP0
		return c.execCOP0(instr, rs, rt, rd)
	case 0x11: // COP1
		return c.execCOP1(instr)
	case 0x12: // COP2: the VFPU
		return c.execCOP2(instr)
	case 0x18: // VFPU VV arith group: vadd, vsub, vsbn, vdiv
		return c.execCompute(instr, c.execVVArith)
	case 0x19: // VFPU VV product group: vmul, vdot, vscl, vhdp, vcrs, vdet
		return c.execCompute(instr, c.execVVProd)
	case 0x1B: // VFPU VV compare group: vcmp, vmin, vmax, vsge, vslt
		return c.execCompute(instr, c.execVVCmpGrp)
	case 0x34: // VFPU unary, scaled conversions, vcmov
		return c.execCompute(instr, c.execVFPU34)
	case 0x37: // VFPU prefix instructions: vpfxs, vpfxt, vpfxd
		return c.execPrefixes(instr)
	case 0x3C: // VFPU matrix group
		return c.execCompute(instr, c.execMatrixGroup)
	case 0x32: // LV.S
		return c.execLVS(instr)
	case 0x35: // LVL.Q / LVR.Q
		return c.execLVLR(instr)
	case 0x36: // LV.Q
		return c.execLVQ(instr)
	case 0x3A: // SV.S
		return c.execSVS(instr)
	case 0x3D: // SVL.Q / SVR.Q
		return c.execSVLR(instr)
	case 0x3E: // SV.Q
		return c.execSVQ(instr)
	case 0x1C: // SPECIAL2
		return c.execSpecial2(instr, rs, rt, rd, fn)
	case 0x1F: // SPECIAL3
		return c.execSpecial3(instr, rs, rt, rd, sa, fn)
	case 0x3F:
		// Primary opcode 0x3F has no documented Allegrex
		// assignment in the published encoding references, but
		// recorded PSP software executes the word 0xFFFF0000
		// (three in a row inside the SDK printf float path
		// linked into every pspautotests vfpu binary) without
		// faulting or side effects: with this slot passed over,
		// the vrnd test runs to completion with correct output,
		// and with it faulting, execution dies at the first
		// word. Modelled as a no-op and flagged as an open
		// encoding question in the README.
		return 1
	case 0x2F: // CACHE: decoded, no operation, never faults
	default:
		return c.execLoadStore(op, rs, rt, simm)
	}
	return 1
}

func (c *CPU) jumpTarget(instr uint32) uint32 {
	return ((c.curPC + 4) & 0xF0000000) | ((instr & 0x03FFFFFF) << 2)
}

func (c *CPU) execSpecial(instr uint32, rs, rt, rd, sa int, fn uint32) int {
	switch fn {
	case 0x00: // SLL
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rt]<<uint(sa))
	case 0x02: // SRL, or ROTR when bit 21 (rs field) is 1
		if rs == 1 {
			c.setReg(rd, rotr(c.regs[rt], uint32(sa)))
		} else {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rt]>>uint(sa))
		}
	case 0x03: // SRA
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(int32(c.regs[rt])>>uint(sa)))
	case 0x04: // SLLV
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rt]<<(c.regs[rs]&31))
	case 0x06: // SRLV, or ROTRV when bit 6 is set
		if (instr>>6)&1 == 1 {
			c.setReg(rd, rotr(c.regs[rt], c.regs[rs]&31))
		} else {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rt]>>(c.regs[rs]&31))
		}
	case 0x07: // SRAV
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(int32(c.regs[rt])>>(c.regs[rs]&31)))
	case 0x08: // JR
		c.branch(true, c.regs[rs])
	case 0x09: // JALR
		target := c.regs[rs]
		c.setReg(rd, c.curPC+8)
		c.branch(true, target)
	case 0x0A: // MOVZ
		if c.regs[rt] == 0 {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs])
		}
	case 0x0B: // MOVN
		if c.regs[rt] != 0 {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs])
		}
	case 0x0C: // SYSCALL
		if c.SyscallHook != nil && c.SyscallHook(c, (instr>>6)&0xFFFFF) {
			return 1
		}
		c.raiseException(excSys, 0)
	case 0x0D: // BREAK
		c.raiseException(excBp, 0)
	case 0x0E: // SDBBP: software debug breakpoint
		c.raiseDebug(excBp)
	case 0x0F: // SYNC
	case 0x10: // MFHI
		c.setReg(rd, c.hi)
	case 0x11: // MTHI
		c.hi = c.regs[rs]
	case 0x12: // MFLO
		c.setReg(rd, c.lo)
	case 0x13: // MTLO
		c.lo = c.regs[rs]
	case 0x18: // MULT
		p := int64(int32(c.regs[rs])) * int64(int32(c.regs[rt]))
		c.hi, c.lo = uint32(uint64(p)>>32), uint32(p)
		return 2
	case 0x19: // MULTU
		p := uint64(c.regs[rs]) * uint64(c.regs[rt])
		c.hi, c.lo = uint32(p>>32), uint32(p)
		return 2
	case 0x1A: // DIV
		a, b := int32(c.regs[rs]), int32(c.regs[rt])
		if b == 0 {
			// Observed Allegrex divide by zero result.
			if a >= 0 {
				c.lo = 0xFFFFFFFF
			} else {
				c.lo = 1
			}
			c.hi = uint32(a)
		} else {
			// Go defines INT_MIN / -1 as INT_MIN with remainder 0,
			// matching MIPS (no trap).
			c.lo = uint32(a / b)
			c.hi = uint32(a % b)
		}
		return 37
	case 0x1B: // DIVU
		a, b := c.regs[rs], c.regs[rt]
		if b == 0 {
			// Observed Allegrex divide by zero result: the
			// quotient is 0xFFFF for dividends under 0x10000
			// and all ones above that.
			if a < 0x10000 {
				c.lo = 0x0000FFFF
			} else {
				c.lo = 0xFFFFFFFF
			}
			c.hi = a
		} else {
			c.lo = a / b
			c.hi = a % b
		}
		return 37
	case 0x16: // CLZ (Allegrex places CLZ/CLO in SPECIAL)
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(countLeading(c.regs[rs], false)))
	case 0x17: // CLO
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(countLeading(c.regs[rs], true)))
	case 0x1C: // MADD (Allegrex places the family in SPECIAL)
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, true, false)
	case 0x1D: // MADDU
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, false, false)
	case 0x2E: // MSUB
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, true, true)
	case 0x2F: // MSUBU
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, false, true)
	case 0x20: // ADD
		sum := int64(int32(c.regs[rs])) + int64(int32(c.regs[rt]))
		if sum > 0x7FFFFFFF || sum < -0x80000000 {
			c.raiseException(excOv, 0)
			return 1
		}
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(sum))
	case 0x21: // ADDU
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs]+c.regs[rt])
	case 0x22: // SUB
		d := int64(int32(c.regs[rs])) - int64(int32(c.regs[rt]))
		if d > 0x7FFFFFFF || d < -0x80000000 {
			c.raiseException(excOv, 0)
			return 1
		}
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(d))
	case 0x23: // SUBU
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs]-c.regs[rt])
	case 0x24: // AND
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs]&c.regs[rt])
	case 0x25: // OR
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs]|c.regs[rt])
	case 0x26: // XOR
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs]^c.regs[rt])
	case 0x27: // NOR
		c.setReg(rd, ^(c.regs[rs] | c.regs[rt]))
	case 0x2C: // MAX (Allegrex addition to the SPECIAL table)
		if int32(c.regs[rs]) > int32(c.regs[rt]) {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs])
		} else {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rt])
		}
	case 0x2D: // MIN (Allegrex addition)
		if int32(c.regs[rs]) < int32(c.regs[rt]) {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs])
		} else {
			c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rt])
		}
	case 0x2A: // SLT
		if int32(c.regs[rs]) < int32(c.regs[rt]) {
			c.setReg(rd, 1)
		} else {
			c.setReg(rd, 0)
		}
	case 0x2B: // SLTU
		if c.regs[rs] < c.regs[rt] {
			c.setReg(rd, 1)
		} else {
			c.setReg(rd, 0)
		}
	case 0x30, 0x31, 0x32, 0x33, 0x34, 0x36: // trap family
		if trapTaken(fn, c.regs[rs], c.regs[rt]) {
			c.raiseException(excTr, 0)
		}
	default:
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

func trapTaken(fn uint32, a, b uint32) bool {
	switch fn {
	case 0x30: // TGE
		return int32(a) >= int32(b)
	case 0x31: // TGEU
		return a >= b
	case 0x32: // TLT
		return int32(a) < int32(b)
	case 0x33: // TLTU
		return a < b
	case 0x34: // TEQ
		return a == b
	case 0x36: // TNE
		return a != b
	}
	return false
}

func rotr(v, n uint32) uint32 {
	n &= 31
	if n == 0 {
		return v
	}
	return (v >> n) | (v << (32 - n))
}

func (c *CPU) execRegimm(rs, rt int, simm int32) int {
	switch rt {
	case 0x00: // BLTZ
		c.branch(int32(c.regs[rs]) < 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x01: // BGEZ
		c.branch(int32(c.regs[rs]) >= 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x02: // BLTZL
		c.branchLikely(int32(c.regs[rs]) < 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x03: // BGEZL
		c.branchLikely(int32(c.regs[rs]) >= 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x10: // BLTZAL: link is written whether or not it branches
		c.setReg(31, c.curPC+8)
		c.branch(int32(c.regs[rs]) < 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x11: // BGEZAL: link is written whether or not it branches
		c.setReg(31, c.curPC+8)
		c.branch(int32(c.regs[rs]) >= 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x12: // BLTZALL: link is written whether or not it branches
		c.setReg(31, c.curPC+8)
		c.branchLikely(int32(c.regs[rs]) < 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	case 0x13: // BGEZALL: link is written whether or not it branches
		c.setReg(31, c.curPC+8)
		c.branchLikely(int32(c.regs[rs]) >= 0, c.branchTarget(simm))
	default:
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

func (c *CPU) execSpecial2(instr uint32, rs, rt, rd int, fn uint32) int {
	if instr == 0x70000000 { // HALT: this exact word, all fields zero
		c.halted = true
		return 1
	}
	switch fn {
	case 0x00: // MADD (standard MIPS32 placement; the Allegrex
		// encoding lives in SPECIAL, this form is kept as well)
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, true, false)
	case 0x01: // MADDU
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, false, false)
	case 0x02: // MUL: writes rd only, HI and LO untouched
		c.setReg(rd, c.regs[rs]*c.regs[rt])
		return 2
	case 0x04: // MSUB
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, true, true)
	case 0x05: // MSUBU
		return c.mulAcc(rs, rt, false, true)
	case 0x20: // CLZ
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(countLeading(c.regs[rs], false)))
		return 1
	case 0x21: // CLO
		c.setReg(rd, uint32(countLeading(c.regs[rs], true)))
		return 1
	case 0x24: // MFIC: rt is the GPR, rd selects the IC register
		c.setReg(rt, c.icReg[rd])
		return 1
	case 0x26: // MTIC
		c.icReg[rd] = c.regs[rt]
		return 1
	default:
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
		return 1
	}
}

// mulAcc performs the multiply accumulate family: the 64 bit
// HI:LO accumulator gains (add) or loses (sub) the product of the
// two operand registers, signed or unsigned.
func (c *CPU) mulAcc(rs, rt int, signed, sub bool) int {
	acc := (uint64(c.hi) << 32) | uint64(c.lo)
	if signed {
		p := int64(int32(c.regs[rs])) * int64(int32(c.regs[rt]))
		if sub {
			acc = uint64(int64(acc) - p)
		} else {
			acc = uint64(int64(acc) + p)
		}
	} else {
		p := uint64(c.regs[rs]) * uint64(c.regs[rt])
		if sub {
			acc -= p
		} else {
			acc += p
		}
	}
	c.hi, c.lo = uint32(acc>>32), uint32(acc)
	return 2
}

func countLeading(v uint32, ones bool) int {
	n := 0
	for i := 31; i >= 0; i-- {
		bit := (v >> uint(i)) & 1
		if (bit == 1) == ones {
			n++
		} else {
			break
		}
	}
	return n
}

func (c *CPU) execSpecial3(instr uint32, rs, rt, rd, sa int, fn uint32) int {
	switch fn {
	case 0x00: // EXT: rd field holds size-1, sa holds pos
		size := rd + 1
		var mask uint32
		if size >= 32 {
			mask = 0xFFFFFFFF
		} else {
			mask = (uint32(1) << uint(size)) - 1
		}
		c.setReg(rt, (c.regs[rs]>>uint(sa))&mask)
	case 0x04: // INS: rd field holds pos+size-1, sa holds pos
		size := rd - sa + 1
		var mask uint32
		if size >= 32 {
			mask = 0xFFFFFFFF
		} else {
			mask = ((uint32(1) << uint(size)) - 1) << uint(sa)
		}
		v := (c.regs[rs] << uint(sa)) & mask
		c.setReg(rt, (c.regs[rt]&^mask)|v)
	case 0x20: // BSHFL
		switch sa {
		case 2: // WSBH: swap bytes in each halfword
			v := c.regs[rt]
			v = ((v & 0x00FF00FF) << 8) | ((v & 0xFF00FF00) >> 8)
			c.setReg(rd, v)
		case 3: // WSBW: swap all four bytes (byte reverse)
			v := c.regs[rt]
			v = (v << 24) | ((v & 0xFF00) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0xFF00) | (v >> 24)
			c.setReg(rd, v)
		case 16: // SEB: sign extend byte
