			c.setReg(rd, uint32(int32(int8(c.regs[rt]))))
		case 20: // BITREV: reverse all 32 bits
			v := c.regs[rt]
			var r uint32
			for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
				if v&(1<<uint(i)) != 0 {
					r |= 1 << uint(31-i)
				}
			}
			c.setReg(rd, r)
		case 24: // SEH: sign extend halfword
			c.setReg(rd, uint32(int32(int16(c.regs[rt]))))
		default:
			c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
		}
	default:
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

func (c *CPU) execCOP0(instr uint32, rs, rt, rd int) int {
	sel := int(instr & 7)
	switch {
	case rs == 0x00: // MFC0
		c.setReg(rt, c.readCP0(rd, sel))
	case rs == 0x04: // MTC0
		c.writeCP0(rd, sel, c.regs[rt])
	case rs >= 0x10: // CO function field
		switch instr & 0x3F {
		case 0x01, 0x02, 0x06, 0x08: // TLBR, TLBWI, TLBWR, TLBP
			// No TLB exists in this core; these decode as no-ops.
		case 0x18: // ERET
			if c.cp0[12][0]&statusERL != 0 {
				c.cp0[12][0] &^= statusERL
				c.setPCVector(c.cp0[30][0]) // ErrorEPC
			} else {
				c.cp0[12][0] &^= statusEXL
				c.setPCVector(c.cp0[14][0]) // EPC
			}
			c.llbit = false
		case 0x1F: // DERET: simplification, jump to DEPC only
			c.setPCVector(c.cp0[24][0])
		case 0x20: // WAIT: like HALT, sleep until an enabled interrupt
			c.halted = true
		default:
			c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
		}
	default:
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

// addrError raises the given address error with BadVAddr set and
// performs no bus access.
func (c *CPU) addrError(code uint32, addr uint32) int {
	c.cp0[8][0] = addr
	c.raiseException(code, 0)
	return 1
}

func (c *CPU) execLoadStore(op uint32, rs, rt int, simm int32) int {
	addr := c.regs[rs] + uint32(simm)
	switch op {
	case 0x20: // LB
		c.setReg(rt, uint32(int32(int8(c.bus.Read8(addr)))))
	case 0x24: // LBU
		c.setReg(rt, uint32(c.bus.Read8(addr)))
	case 0x21: // LH
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdEL, addr)
		}
		c.setReg(rt, uint32(int32(int16(c.bus.Read16(addr)))))
	case 0x25: // LHU
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdEL, addr)
		}
		c.setReg(rt, uint32(c.bus.Read16(addr)))
	case 0x23, 0x30: // LW, LL
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdEL, addr)
		}
		c.setReg(rt, c.bus.Read32(addr))
		if op == 0x30 {
			c.llbit = true
			c.lladdr = addr
		}
	case 0x22: // LWL: the aligned word shifts into the high end
		// of rt; the low (3-a) bytes survive. (Shift form, pinned
		// against the pspautotests lsu matrix: the byte loop this
		// replaces merged in big-endian order.)
		w := c.bus.Read32(addr &^ 3)
		shift := uint(8 * (3 - (addr & 3)))
		keep := uint32((uint64(1) << shift) - 1)
		c.setReg(rt, (w<<shift)|(c.regs[rt]&keep))
	case 0x26: // LWR
		w := c.bus.Read32(addr &^ 3)
		a := addr & 3
		v := c.regs[rt]
		for j := uint32(0); j <= 3-a; j++ {
			v = putByte(v, j, getByte(w, a+j))
		}
		c.setReg(rt, v)
	case 0x28: // SB
		c.bus.Write8(addr, uint8(c.regs[rt]))
	case 0x29: // SH
		if addr&1 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdES, addr)
		}
		c.bus.Write16(addr, uint16(c.regs[rt]))
	case 0x2B: // SW
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdES, addr)
		}
		c.bus.Write32(addr, c.regs[rt])
	case 0x2A: // SWL: read modify write of the aligned word; the
		// low (a+1) bytes of the word take rt's high bytes (the
		// mirror of LWL, same shift).
		aligned := addr &^ 3
		w := c.bus.Read32(aligned)
		a := addr & 3
		shift := uint(8 * (3 - a))
		mask := uint32((uint64(1) << (8 * (a + 1))) - 1)
		w = (w &^ mask) | ((c.regs[rt] >> shift) & mask)
		c.bus.Write32(aligned, w)
	case 0x2E: // SWR
		aligned := addr &^ 3
		w := c.bus.Read32(aligned)
		a := addr & 3
		for j := uint32(0); j <= 3-a; j++ {
			w = putByte(w, a+j, getByte(c.regs[rt], j))
		}
		c.bus.Write32(aligned, w)
	case 0x38: // SC: succeeds while the LL reservation stands.
		// The reservation is NOT consumed by a successful SC on
		// this hardware: the pspautotests llsc matrix has a
		// second SC to the reserved address succeed as well.
		// Syscalls, exceptions and thread switches are what
		// break it (see ClearLL).
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdES, addr)
		}
		v := c.regs[rt]
		if c.llbit {
			c.bus.Write32(addr, v)
			c.setReg(rt, 1)
		} else {
			c.setReg(rt, 0)
		}
	case 0x31: // LWC1
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdEL, addr)
		}
		c.fpr[rt] = c.bus.Read32(addr)
	case 0x39: // SWC1
		if addr&3 != 0 {
			return c.addrError(excAdES, addr)
		}
		c.bus.Write32(addr, c.fpr[rt])
	default:
		// Includes LDC1 (0x35) and SDC1 (0x3D): the Allegrex FPU
		// has no double precision, so they are reserved. COP2
		// loads and stores are handled in execute before here.
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

// getByte returns byte j of w, where byte 0 is the least significant.
func getByte(w, j uint32) uint32 { return (w >> (8 * j)) & 0xFF }

func putByte(w, j, b uint32) uint32 {
	w &^= 0xFF << (8 * j)
	return w | (b&0xFF)<<(8*j)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex/fpu.go ====================

package allegrex

import (
	"math"
	"math/big"
)

// COP1 (FPU) implementation, single precision only.
//
// Arithmetic approach: Go float32 arithmetic rounds to nearest even
// only, and the Allegrex FCSR exposes all four MIPS rounding modes.
// Every operation is therefore computed in float64 and passed once
// through roundToSingle, which applies the FCSR rounding mode with
// a one ulp adjustment when the float64 value is not exactly
// representable in single precision. Caveat: division and square
// root are correctly rounded to float64 first and then rounded
// again to float32, a double rounding that can differ from true
// single precision rounding in rare edge cases; it is exact for
// the unit vectors this core is validated against.
//
// Denormal policy (flush to zero, matching the Allegrex): denormal
// inputs are treated as signed zero before an ARITHMETIC operation,
// and denormal results are flushed to signed zero. Scalar compares
// are the exception: they see the true operand values (the
// pspautotests fpu_branch loop counts on 0 < denormal being true).
// Any NaN result is canonicalized to 0x7FC00000. FPU arithmetic
// never raises the FPE exception in slice 1; traps are masked and
// results follow IEEE 754 through the rules above.

const canonicalNaN = 0x7FC00000

// fcr31Mask is the set of FCSR bits a CTC1 write can change and
// a CFC1 read exposes: the rounding mode, flags, enables and
// cause fields (bits 0..16), FCC0 (bit 23) and FS (bit 24). The
// pspautotests fcr matrix pins the rest: writes to the FO and FN
// bits (22 and 21), the FCC1-7 slots (bits 25..31) and the
// unassigned bits are dropped, and FCC1-7 read back as zero even
// though the condition codes themselves work (they are kept in
// the same array bits internally, just never exposed).
const fcr31Mask = 0x0181FFFF

// fcsr returns the FPU control and status register (fcr31) as
// software reads it.
func (c *CPU) fcsr() uint32 { return c.fcr[31] & fcr31Mask }

func (c *CPU) roundingMode() uint32 { return c.fcr[31] & 3 }

// fccRead returns condition code bit cc: cc 0 lives at FCSR bit 23,
// cc 1..7 at FCSR bits 25..31.
func (c *CPU) fccRead(cc int) bool {
	if cc == 0 {
		return c.fcr[31]&(1<<23) != 0
	}
	return c.fcr[31]&(1<<uint(24+cc)) != 0
}

func (c *CPU) fccWrite(cc int, v bool) {
	if cc == 0 {
		if v {
			c.fcr[31] |= 1 << 23
		} else {
			c.fcr[31] &^= 1 << 23
		}
		return
	}
	if v {
		c.fcr[31] |= 1 << uint(24+cc)
	} else {
		c.fcr[31] &^= 1 << uint(24+cc)
	}
}

// fpInput converts raw register bits to the float64 operand value,
// flushing denormals to signed zero. NaN and Inf pass through.
func fpInput(bits uint32) float64 {
	exp := (bits >> 23) & 0xFF
	man := bits & 0x7FFFFF
	if exp == 0 && man != 0 {
		// Denormal input: signed zero.
		if bits>>31 != 0 {
			return math.Copysign(0, -1)
		}
		return 0
	}
	return float64(math.Float32frombits(bits))
}

func isNaNBits(bits uint32) bool {
	return (bits>>23)&0xFF == 0xFF && bits&0x7FFFFF != 0
}

// flushZero reports the FCSR FS bit: when set, the scalar FPU
// flushes denormal inputs and results to signed zero; when
// clear, denormals keep their true values. The pspautotests fpu
// matrix pins both halves (a min-normal times 0.5 yields the
// denormal with FS=0 and zero with FS=1). The VFPU always
// flushes and does not consult this bit.
func (c *CPU) flushZero() bool { return c.fcr[31]>>24&1 != 0 }

// fpIn reads a scalar FPU operand under the FS rule.
func (c *CPU) fpIn(bits uint32) float64 {
	if c.flushZero() {
		return fpInput(bits)
	}
	return float64(math.Float32frombits(bits))
}

// roundToSingle rounds x to a single precision bit pattern under
// the given MIPS rounding mode (0 RN, 1 RZ, 2 RP, 3 RM), flushing
// denormal results to signed zero and canonicalizing NaNs.
func roundToSingle(x float64, mode uint32) uint32 {
	return roundToSingleFlush(x, mode, true)
}

// roundToSingleFlush is roundToSingle with the denormal result
// flush made conditional (the scalar FPU flushes only under FS).
func roundToSingleFlush(x float64, mode uint32, flush bool) uint32 {
	if math.IsNaN(x) {
		return canonicalNaN
	}
	if math.IsInf(x, 0) {
		if x < 0 {
			return 0xFF800000
		}
		return 0x7F800000
	}
	if x == 0 {
		if math.Signbit(x) {
			return 0x80000000
		}
		return 0
	}
	f := float32(x) // round to nearest even baseline
	fb := math.Float32bits(f)
	fx := float64(f)
	switch mode {
	case 1: // RZ: truncate toward zero. From the round to
		// nearest baseline that means stepping down in value for
		// a positive result and UP in value for a negative one
		// (an earlier build stepped down for both, which the
		// roundmode int to float matrix catches at -16777219).
		if fb == 0x7F800000 {
			fb = 0x7F7FFFFF
		} else if fb == 0xFF800000 {
			fb = 0xFF7FFFFF
		} else if x > 0 && fx > x {
			fb = nextDownBits(fb, x)
		} else if x < 0 && fx < x {
			fb = nextUpBits(fb)
		}
	case 2: // RP: toward plus infinity
		if fx < x {
			fb = nextUpBits(fb)
		}
	case 3: // RM: toward minus infinity
		if fx > x {
			fb = nextDownBits(fb, x)
		}
	}
	// Flush a denormal result to signed zero when asked.
	if flush && (fb>>23)&0xFF == 0 && fb&0x7FFFFF != 0 {
		return fb & 0x80000000
	}
	return fb
}

// nextUpBits returns the next float32 bit pattern above the given
// one in value. Sign magnitude encoding makes this bits+1 for
// positive values and bits-1 for negative ones.
func nextUpBits(b uint32) uint32 {
	if b == 0x7F800000 || b == 0xFF800000 {
		return b
	}
	if b>>31 == 0 {
		return b + 1
	}
	return b - 1
}

// nextDownBits returns the next float32 bit pattern below the given
// one in value. Stepping down from an infinity produced by overflow
// of a finite x lands on the largest finite value, which is the
// correct directed rounding result.
func nextDownBits(b uint32, x float64) uint32 {
	if b == 0x7F800000 { // +Inf from a finite x
		return 0x7F7FFFFF
	}
	if b == 0xFF800000 { // -Inf
		if x > -math.MaxFloat32*2 {
			return 0xFF7FFFFF
		}
		return b
	}
	if b>>31 == 0 {
		if b == 0 {
			return 0x80000001
		}
		return b - 1
	}
	return b + 1
}

func (c *CPU) execCOP1(instr uint32) int {
	if c.cp0[12][0]&statusCU1 == 0 {
		c.raiseException(excCpU, 1)
		return 1
	}
	rs := int((instr >> 21) & 31) // fmt field
	rt := int((instr >> 16) & 31) // ft, or GPR for moves
	fs := int((instr >> 11) & 31)
	fd := int((instr >> 6) & 31)
	fn := instr & 63

	switch rs {
	case 0x00: // MFC1
		c.setReg(rt, c.fpr[fs])
	case 0x02: // CFC1: fcr0 reads the FPU implementation ID,
		// fcr31 reads the FCSR through the readback mask,
		// fcr25..28 read 0.
		if fs == 0 {
			c.setReg(rt, 0x00003351)
		} else if fs == 31 {
			c.setReg(rt, c.fcsr())
		} else {
			c.setReg(rt, c.fcr[fs])
		}
	case 0x04: // MTC1
		c.fpr[fs] = c.regs[rt]
	case 0x06: // CTC1: only fcr31 (the FCSR) is writable, and
		// only through the writable mask; the internal FCC1-7
		// bits survive a CTC1 write.
		if fs == 31 {
			c.fcr[31] = c.fcr[31]&^fcr31Mask | c.regs[rt]&fcr31Mask
		}
	case 0x08: // BC1F/BC1T and the likely forms
		cc := int((instr >> 18) & 7)
		// Encoding: bits 20..18 cc, bit 17 nd (the likely flag:
		// annul the delay slot when the branch is not taken),
		// bit 16 tf. PSP-1 had tf and nd swapped, which the
		// pspautotests fpu_branch matrix refutes (bc1t never
		// branched, bc1fl annulled the wrong way).
		tf := (instr>>16)&1 != 0
		likely := (instr>>17)&1 != 0
		taken := c.fccRead(cc) == tf
		if likely {
			c.branchLikely(taken, c.branchTarget(signExt16(instr&0xFFFF)))
		} else {
			c.branch(taken, c.branchTarget(signExt16(instr&0xFFFF)))
		}
	case 0x10: // fmt S
		return c.execFPUS(instr, rt, fs, fd, fn)
	case 0x14: // fmt W
		if fn == 0x20 { // CVT.S.W
			v := float64(int32(c.fpr[fs]))
			c.fpr[fd] = roundToSingleFlush(v, c.roundingMode(), c.flushZero())
			return 1
		}
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	default:
		// Includes fmt D and COP1X style encodings: reserved here.
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

// nanOperand returns the quieted bits of a NaN operand and true,
// or false for a non-NaN. Scalar arithmetic propagates a NaN
// operand's own bit pattern (sign and payload kept, quiet bit
// set) instead of canonicalizing, the behavior the pspautotests
// roundmode arithmetic matrix records (ffc00000 in gives
// ffc00000 out; the signaling 7f800001 gives 7fc00001). Only a
// NaN GENERATED by an invalid operation on non-NaN inputs takes
// the canonical 0x7FC00000.
func nanOperand(bits uint32) (uint32, bool) {
	if isNaNBits(bits) {
		return bits | 0x00400000, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// addSubExact rounds the exact sum or difference of two FPU
// operands (already FS adjusted to float64; aNeg flips the second
// operand's sign for subtraction) to single precision under mode.
// The float64 sum is used when it is exact (the usual case); when
// the float64 rounding leaves a residual, the exact value is
// rebuilt with big.Rat and rounded once. Directed modes need the
// exact value: 2^-126 minus 0.5 truncates to 0xBEFFFFFF on
// hardware, but the float64 difference rounds to exactly 0.5
// first and the truncation is lost (the roundmode matrix pins
// this line).
func addSubExact(a, b float64, neg bool, mode uint32, flush bool) (uint32, *big.Rat) {
	bb := b
	if neg {
		bb = -b
	}
	s := a + bb
	if s == 0 {
		// IEEE zero sign rules, which the roundmode matrix's
		// mode 3 section pins (1.1 - 1.1 is -0 under RM, +0 in
		// the other modes): an exact cancellation is +0 except
		// under round toward minus infinity; a sum of two zeros
		// keeps the common sign, and mixed zeros follow the
		// same RM rule.
		neg := false
		if a == 0 && bb == 0 {
			neg = math.Signbit(a) && math.Signbit(bb)
			if math.Signbit(a) != math.Signbit(bb) {
				neg = mode == 3
			}
		} else {
			neg = mode == 3
		}
		bits := uint32(0)
		if neg {
			bits = 0x80000000
		}
		return bits, new(big.Rat)
	}
	if math.IsInf(a, 0) || math.IsInf(bb, 0) || math.IsNaN(s) {
		// Infinite operands: the float64 result (an infinity,
		// or NaN for Inf against -Inf) is already final, and
		// has no exact rational form.
		return roundToSingleFlush(s, mode, flush), nil
	}
	// TwoSum residual: exact when s does not overflow, which
	// float32 range operands guarantee.
	bv := s - a
	err := (a - (s - bv)) + (bb - bv)
	if err == 0 || math.IsInf(s, 0) {
		return roundToSingleFlush(s, mode, flush), new(big.Rat).SetFloat64(s)
	}
	ra := new(big.Rat).SetFloat64(a)
	rb := new(big.Rat).SetFloat64(bb)
	ra.Add(ra, rb)
	return ratToSingle(ra, mode, flush), ra
}

// Condition bit positions shared by the FCSR Cause field (bits
// 12..16) and Flags field (bits 2..6): I, U, O, Z, V from bit 0.
const (
	condI = 1 << iota
	condU
	condO
	condZ
	condV
)

// setFPUConditions records one operation's IEEE conditions: the
// Cause field is replaced, the Flags field accumulates (sticky).
func (c *CPU) setFPUConditions(cond uint32) {
	c.fcr[31] = c.fcr[31]&^(0x1F<<12) | (cond&0x1F)<<12
	c.fcr[31] |= (cond & 0x1F) << 2
}

// fpuValueConditions derives the overflow, underflow and inexact
// conditions of a finite exact result x (as a float64; for add
// and sub the caller passes the float64 view of the exact
// rational, which only feeds the comparisons here) from the
// rounded result bits.
func fpuValueConditions(x float64, bits uint32) uint32 {
	var cond uint32
	if math.IsInf(x, 0) {
		return condO | condI
	}
	ax := math.Abs(x)
	if ax > math.MaxFloat32 {
		cond |= condO | condI
		return cond
	}
	res := math.Abs(float64(math.Float32frombits(bits)))
	if res != ax {
		cond |= condI
		if ax < 0x1p-126 {
			cond |= condU
		}
	}
	return cond
}

// ratToSingle rounds an exact rational to a float32 bit pattern
// under a MIPS rounding mode, with the FS denormal flush applied
// when flush is set. The rational must be finite and nonzero
// handling is done by the caller for zero (sign rules differ).
func ratToSingle(r *big.Rat, mode uint32, flush bool) uint32 {
	if r.Sign() == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	sign := uint32(0)
	num := new(big.Int).Set(r.Num())
	if r.Sign() < 0 {
		sign = 0x80000000
		num.Abs(num)
	}
	den := r.Denom()
	// Find e with 2^e <= |r| < 2^(e+1): start from bit lengths
	// and correct by one comparison.
	e := num.BitLen() - den.BitLen()
	// compare |r| against 2^e: num/den vs 2^e
	cmp := 0
	if e >= 0 {
		cmp = num.Cmp(new(big.Int).Lsh(den, uint(e)))
	} else {
		cmp = new(big.Int).Lsh(num, uint(-e)).Cmp(den)
	}
	if cmp < 0 {
		e--
	}
	// Round |r| / 2^(e-23) to an integer mantissa with remainder.
	roundTo := func(exp int) (uint64, *big.Int, *big.Int) {
		// value = num/den / 2^(exp-23); return quotient, rem num, rem den
		shift := exp - 23
		n := new(big.Int).Set(num)
		d := new(big.Int).Set(den)
		if shift >= 0 {
			d.Lsh(d, uint(shift))
		} else {
			n.Lsh(n, uint(-shift))
		}
		q, rem := new(big.Int).QuoRem(n, d, new(big.Int))
		return q.Uint64(), rem, d
	}
	applyRound := func(q uint64, rem, d *big.Int) uint64 {
		if rem.Sign() == 0 {
			return q
		}
		up := false
		switch mode {
		case 0: // RN, ties to even
			twice := new(big.Int).Lsh(rem, 1)
			c := twice.Cmp(d)
			up = c > 0 || (c == 0 && q&1 == 1)
		case 1: // RZ
			up = false
		case 2: // RP: magnitude up only for positive values
			up = sign == 0
		case 3: // RM: magnitude up only for negative values
			up = sign != 0
		}
		if up {
			q++
		}
		return q
	}
	if e >= -126 {
		q, rem, d := roundTo(e)
		q = applyRound(q, rem, d)
		if q == 1<<24 {
			q >>= 1
			e++
		}
		if e > 127 {
			// Overflow: infinity under RN, largest finite
			// under directed modes toward zero, per sign.
			switch mode {
			case 0:
				return sign | 0x7F800000
			case 1:
				return sign | 0x7F7FFFFF
			case 2:
				if sign == 0 {
					return 0x7F800000
				}
				return sign | 0x7F7FFFFF
			case 3:
				if sign != 0 {
					return sign | 0x7F800000
				}
				return sign | 0x7F7FFFFF
			}
		}
		return sign | uint32(e+127)<<23 | uint32(q&0x7FFFFF)
	}
	// Subnormal range: roundTo(-126) yields the mantissa at
	// 2^-149 granularity directly.
	q2, rem3, d3 := roundTo(-126)
	q2 = applyRound(q2, rem3, d3)
	if q2 == 0 {
		// Underflow to zero; directed modes away from zero
		// produce the smallest denormal.
		if (mode == 2 && sign == 0) || (mode == 3 && sign != 0) {
			if flush {
				return sign
			}
			return sign | 1
		}
		return sign
	}
	if flush {
		return sign
	}
	if q2 >= 1<<23 {
		// Rounded up into the smallest normal.
		return sign | 0x00800000
	}
	return sign | uint32(q2)
}

func (c *CPU) execFPUS(instr uint32, ft, fs, fd int, fn uint32) int {
	mode := c.roundingMode()
	switch fn {
	case 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03: // ADD.S SUB.S MUL.S DIV.S
		if nb, ok := nanOperand(c.fpr[fs]); ok {
			c.fpr[fd] = nb
			c.setFPUConditions(condV)
		} else if nb, ok := nanOperand(c.fpr[ft]); ok {
			c.fpr[fd] = nb
			c.setFPUConditions(condV)
		} else {
			a, b := c.fpIn(c.fpr[fs]), c.fpIn(c.fpr[ft])
			switch fn {
			case 0x00, 0x01:
				bits, exact := addSubExact(a, b, fn == 0x01, mode, c.flushZero())
				c.fpr[fd] = bits
				if exact == nil {
					// Infinite operand: NaN result means the
					// invalid Inf against -Inf form.
					if isNaNBits(bits) {
						c.setFPUConditions(condV)
					} else {
						c.setFPUConditions(0)
					}
					break
				}
				xf, _ := exact.Float64()
				c.setFPUConditions(fpuValueConditions(xf, bits))
			case 0x02:
				x := a * b
				bits := roundToSingleFlush(x, mode, c.flushZero())
				c.fpr[fd] = bits
				cond := fpuValueConditions(x, bits)
				if (a == 0 && math.IsInf(b, 0)) || (b == 0 && math.IsInf(a, 0)) {
					cond = condV
				}
				c.setFPUConditions(cond)
			case 0x03:
				x := a / b
				bits := roundToSingleFlush(x, mode, c.flushZero())
				c.fpr[fd] = bits
				cond := uint32(0)
				switch {
				case a == 0 && b == 0, math.IsInf(a, 0) && math.IsInf(b, 0):
					cond = condV
				case b == 0 && a != 0 && !math.IsInf(a, 0):
					cond = condZ
				default:
					cond = fpuValueConditions(x, bits)
				}
				c.setFPUConditions(cond)
			}
		}
		if fn == 0x03 {
			return 12
		}
	case 0x04: // SQRT.S
		if nb, ok := nanOperand(c.fpr[fs]); ok {
			c.fpr[fd] = nb
			c.setFPUConditions(condV)
		} else {
			a := c.fpIn(c.fpr[fs])
			x := math.Sqrt(a)
			bits := roundToSingleFlush(x, mode, c.flushZero())
			c.fpr[fd] = bits
			if a < 0 {
				c.setFPUConditions(condV)
			} else {
				c.setFPUConditions(fpuValueConditions(x, bits))
			}
		}
		return 12
	case 0x05: // ABS.S
		c.fpr[fd] = c.fpr[fs] & 0x7FFFFFFF
	case 0x06: // MOV.S
		c.fpr[fd] = c.fpr[fs]
	case 0x07: // NEG.S
		c.fpr[fd] = c.fpr[fs] ^ 0x80000000
	case 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x0F: // ROUND.W.S TRUNC.W.S CEIL.W.S FLOOR.W.S
		m := []uint32{0, 1, 2, 3}[fn-0x0C]
		c.fpr[fd] = cvtToWord(c.fpIn(c.fpr[fs]), m)
	case 0x10, 0x11: // MOVF.S / MOVT.S
		// Slice encoding: cc is taken from the ft field bits
		// 20..18 (the same slot BC1 uses), fn bit 0 is tf, fd is
		// the destination and fs the source.
		cc := int((instr >> 18) & 7)
		want := fn&1 != 0
		if c.fccRead(cc) == want {
			c.fpr[fd] = c.fpr[fs]
		}
	case 0x24: // CVT.W.S uses the FCSR rounding mode
		c.fpr[fd] = cvtToWord(c.fpIn(c.fpr[fs]), mode)
	default:
		if fn >= 0x30 { // C.cond.S
			c.execCompare(instr, ft, fs, fn&0xF)
			return 1
		}
		// MOVZ.S/MOVN.S and everything else: reserved here.
		c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	}
	return 1
}

// cvtToWord converts a float register to an int32 bit pattern under
// an explicit rounding mode. The conversion saturates by sign:
// results at or past the positive limit produce 0x7FFFFFFF and
// results past the negative limit produce 0x80000000. NaN of
// either sign produces 0x7FFFFFFF. That is the Allegrex behavior
// the pspautotests roundmode and fpu matrices record. An earlier
// build returned 0x80000000 for every invalid case on a
// "documented MIPS convention" claim the corpus refutes.
func cvtToWord(v float64, mode uint32) uint32 {
	if math.IsNaN(v) {
		return 0x7FFFFFFF
	}
	var r float64
	switch mode {
	case 0: // RN, ties to even
		r = math.RoundToEven(v)
	case 1: // RZ
		r = math.Trunc(v)
	case 2: // RP
		r = math.Ceil(v)
	case 3: // RM
		r = math.Floor(v)
	}
	if r >= 2147483648.0 {
		return 0x7FFFFFFF
	}
	if r < -2147483648.0 {
		return 0x80000000
	}
	return uint32(int32(r))
}

// execCompare implements C.cond.S. The cond bits are
// [orUnordered, less, equal, signaling] from bit 3 down to bit 0.
// The signaling bit only selects exception behavior, which is
// masked in slice 1, so it changes nothing numerically.
func (c *CPU) execCompare(instr uint32, ft, fs int, cond uint32) {
	aBits, bBits := c.fpr[fs], c.fpr[ft]
	unord := isNaNBits(aBits) || isNaNBits(bBits)
	// Compares see operands under the same FS rule as
	// arithmetic; with FS clear (the thread default) denormal
	// inputs keep their true values. The pspautotests
	// fpu_branch loop pins this (c.lt.s of 0 against a positive
	// denormal is true on hardware, and its bc1tl loop counts 4;
	// an earlier build flushed compare inputs unconditionally
	// and the loop never branched).
	a := c.fpIn(aBits)
	b := c.fpIn(bBits)
	lt := a < b
	eq := a == b
	// The 4-bit condition selects predicate terms: bit 0 adds
	// "or unordered", bit 1 adds equality, bit 2 adds less-than.
	// That one formula covers all sixteen C.cond forms (F, UN,
	// EQ, UEQ, OLT, ULT, OLE, ULE and the signaling set SF, NGLE,
	// SEQ, NGL, LT, NGE, LE, NGT, whose value bits mirror the
	// quiet set). An earlier build gated the unordered term on
	// bit 3, so C.UN.S never reported unordered (and C.SF.S
	// wrongly did); the pspautotests fpu matrix caught it.
	res := (unord && cond&1 != 0) || (lt && cond&4 != 0) || (eq && cond&2 != 0)
	cc := int((instr >> 8) & 7)
	c.fccWrite(cc, res)
}

package allegrex

import "testing"

// FPU test harness: same as newHarness plus CU1 enabled.
func newFPUHarness() *harness {
	h := newHarness()
	h.c.cp0[12][0] = 0x20400000 // BEV | CU1
	return h
}

// encFP builds a COP1 fmt S instruction: ft, fs, fd, funct.
func encFP(ft, fs, fd, fn uint32) uint32 {
	return 0x11<<26 | 0x10<<21 | ft<<16 | fs<<11 | fd<<6 | fn
}
func encMFC1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 0<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11 }
func encMTC1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 4<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11 }
func encCFC1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 2<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11 }
func encCTC1(rt, fs uint32) uint32 { return 0x11<<26 | 6<<21 | rt<<16 | fs<<11 }

// encBC1 builds a BC1 branch: cc in bits 20..18, nd (likely)
// bit 17, tf bit 16 (the hardware layout; an earlier version of
// this helper had tf and nd swapped to match a swapped decoder).
func encBC1(cc uint32, tf bool, off uint32) uint32 {
	w := 0x11<<26 | 8<<21 | cc<<18 | (off & 0xFFFF)
	if tf {
		w |= 1 << 16
	}
	return w
}

// IEEE 754 bit patterns used below.
const (
	fOne   = 0x3F800000 // 1.0
	fOne5  = 0x3FC00000 // 1.5
	fTwo   = 0x40000000 // 2.0
	fTwo25 = 0x40100000 // 2.25
	fThree = 0x40400000 // 3.0
)

func TestFPUArithmetic(t *testing.T) {
	h := newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne5)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fTwo25)
	h.r.load(0,
		encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x00), // add.s f3, f1, f2 = 3.75
		encFP(2, 1, 4, 0x02), // mul.s f4, f1, f2 = 3.375
		encFP(2, 1, 5, 0x01), // sub.s f5, f1, f2 = -0.75
		encFP(1, 2, 6, 0x07), // neg.s f6, f2
		encFP(0, 5, 7, 0x05), // abs.s f7, f5
	)
	h.run(5)
	want := map[int]uint32{
		3: 0x40700000, // 3.75
		4: 0x40580000, // 3.375
		5: 0xBF400000, // -0.75
		6: 0xC0100000, // -2.25
		7: 0x3F400000, // 0.75
	}
	for reg, v := range want {
		if got := h.c.FReg(reg); got != v {
			t.Errorf("f%d = %#08x, want %#08x", reg, got, v)
		}
	}
}

func TestFPUDivSqrt(t *testing.T) {
	h := newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fThree)
	h.c.SetFReg(3, fTwo)
	h.r.load(0,
		encFP(2, 1, 4, 0x03), // div.s f4, f1, f2 = 1/3
		encFP(0, 3, 5, 0x04), // sqrt.s f5, f3 = sqrt(2)
	)
	if n := h.c.Step(); n != 12 {
		t.Errorf("div.s cycles = %d, want 12", n)
	}
	if got := h.c.FReg(4); got != 0x3EAAAAAB {
		t.Errorf("1/3 = %#08x, want 0x3EAAAAAB", got)
	}
	if n := h.c.Step(); n != 12 {
		t.Errorf("sqrt.s cycles = %d, want 12", n)
	}
	if got := h.c.FReg(5); got != 0x3FB504F3 {
		t.Errorf("sqrt(2) = %#08x, want 0x3FB504F3", got)
	}
}

func TestFPUSpecialValues(t *testing.T) {
	// Denormal input flushes to zero: denormal + 1.0 = 1.0.
	h := newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0x00000001) // smallest denormal
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fOne)
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x00))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != fOne {
		t.Errorf("denormal + 1.0 = %#08x, want 1.0", got)
	}
	// 1.0 / 0.0 = +Inf.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, 0)
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x03))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0x7F800000 {
		t.Errorf("1/0 = %#08x, want +Inf", got)
	}
	// 0.0 / 0.0 = canonical NaN.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, 0)
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x03))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0x7FC00000 {
		t.Errorf("0/0 = %#08x, want canonical NaN", got)
	}
	// Denormal results follow the FCSR FS bit (pinned by the
	// pspautotests fpu matrix): with FS clear the product
	// 2^-70 * 2^-70 = 2^-140 keeps its denormal bits, with FS
	// set it flushes to signed zero.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0x1C800000) // 2^-70
	h.c.SetFReg(2, 0x1C800000) // 2^-70
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x02))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0x00000200 {
		t.Errorf("denormal product (FS=0) = %#08x, want 0x00000200", got)
	}
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFCSR(0x01000000) // FS set
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0x1C800000)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, 0x1C800000)
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x02))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("denormal product (FS=1) = %#08x, want flushed 0", got)
	}
	// A NaN operand propagates its own quieted bits (roundmode
	// matrix), it is not canonicalized.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0xFFC00000) // negative quiet NaN
	h.c.SetFReg(2, 0x3F800000) // 1.0
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x00))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0xFFC00000 {
		t.Errorf("add.s NaN propagation = %#08x, want 0xffc00000", got)
	}
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0x7F800001) // signaling NaN, payload 1
	h.c.SetFReg(2, 0x3F800000)
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x02))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0x7FC00001 {
		t.Errorf("mul.s sNaN propagation = %#08x, want 0x7fc00001", got)
	}
}

func TestFPUConvertModes(t *testing.T) {
	// CVT.W.S of 2.5 under each FCSR rounding mode:
	// RN 2, RZ 2, RP 3, RM 2.
	modes := []struct {
		mode uint32
		want uint32
	}{
		{0, 2}, {1, 2}, {2, 3}, {3, 2},
	}
	for _, tc := range modes {
		h := newFPUHarness()
		h.c.fcr[31] = tc.mode
		h.c.SetFReg(1, 0x40200000)        // 2.5
		h.r.load(0, encFP(0, 1, 2, 0x24)) // cvt.w.s f2, f1
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.FReg(2); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("cvt.w.s 2.5 mode %d = %#08x, want %d", tc.mode, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	// Explicit variants on -2.5.
	explicit := []struct {
		fn   uint32
		want uint32
	}{
		{0x0C, 0xFFFFFFFE}, // round.w.s: -2 (ties to even)
		{0x0D, 0xFFFFFFFE}, // trunc.w.s: -2
		{0x0E, 0xFFFFFFFE}, // ceil.w.s: -2
		{0x0F, 0xFFFFFFFD}, // floor.w.s: -3
	}
	for _, tc := range explicit {
		h := newFPUHarness()
		h.c.SetFReg(1, 0xC0200000) // -2.5
		h.r.load(0, encFP(0, 1, 2, tc.fn))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.FReg(2); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("fn %#x of -2.5 = %#08x, want %#08x", tc.fn, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	// CVT.W.S saturates by sign (Allegrex behavior, per the
	// pspautotests roundmode and fpu matrices): positive
	// overflow gives 0x7FFFFFFF, negative overflow gives
	// 0x80000000, and NaN of either sign gives 0x7FFFFFFF.
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		in, want uint32
	}{
		{0x7FC00000, 0x7FFFFFFF}, // positive NaN
		{0xFFC00000, 0x7FFFFFFF}, // negative NaN
		{0x4F000000, 0x7FFFFFFF}, // exactly 2^31
		{0x7F800000, 0x7FFFFFFF}, // +Inf
		{0xCF000001, 0x80000000}, // negative, out of range
		{0xFF800000, 0x80000000}, // -Inf
	} {
		h := newFPUHarness()
		h.c.SetFReg(1, tc.in)
		h.r.load(0, encFP(0, 1, 2, 0x24))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.FReg(2); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("cvt.w.s %#08x = %#08x, want %#08x", tc.in, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	// CVT.S.W of -3 is -3.0.
	h := newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0xFFFFFFFD)                           // int32 -3 as raw bits
	h.r.load(0, 0x11<<26|0x14<<21|0<<16|1<<11|2<<6|0x20) // cvt.s.w f2, f1
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(2); got != 0xC0400000 {
		t.Errorf("cvt.s.w -3 = %#08x, want 0xC0400000 (-3.0)", got)
	}
}

func TestFPUCompareAndBranch(t *testing.T) {
	// C.LT.S (cond 4: less bit) sets FCC, BC1T branches, BC1F does
	// not, and the delay slot still executes for the non likely
	// forms.
	h := newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fTwo)
	h.r.load(0,
		encFP(2, 1, 0, 0x30|4), // 0: c.lt.s f1, f2 (true)
		encBC1(0, true, 2),     // 4: bc1t +2 -> 16
		encI(0x09, 9, 9, 1),    // 8: delay slot, r9 += 1
		encI(0x09, 0, 8, 99),   // 12: skipped
		encI(0x09, 0, 10, 7),   // 16: r10 = 7
	)
	h.run(1)
	if !h.c.fccRead(0) {
		t.Fatalf("c.lt.s 1.0 < 2.0 did not set FCC")
	}
	h.run(3)
	if h.c.Reg(9) != 1 || h.c.Reg(8) != 0 || h.c.Reg(10) != 7 {
		t.Errorf("bc1t flow: r8=%d r9=%d r10=%d", h.c.Reg(8), h.c.Reg(9), h.c.Reg(10))
	}
	// C.EQ.S false, BC1F branches.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fTwo)
	h.r.load(0,
		encFP(2, 1, 0, 0x30|2), // 0: c.eq.s f1, f2 (false)
		encBC1(0, false, 2),    // 4: bc1f +2 -> 16
		encI(0x09, 9, 9, 1),    // 8: delay slot
		encI(0x09, 0, 8, 99),   // 12: skipped
		encI(0x09, 0, 10, 7),   // 16: r10 = 7
	)
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.fccRead(0) {
		t.Fatalf("c.eq.s 1.0 == 2.0 set FCC")
	}
	h.run(3)
	if h.c.Reg(9) != 1 || h.c.Reg(8) != 0 || h.c.Reg(10) != 7 {
		t.Errorf("bc1f flow: r8=%d r9=%d r10=%d", h.c.Reg(8), h.c.Reg(9), h.c.Reg(10))
	}
	// Unordered compare: C.ULT.S (cond 5: unordered or less) with
	// a NaN operand is true; ordered C.LT.S (cond 4) is false.
	// (PSP-1 encoded the predicates with the unordered term on
	// bit 3; the hardware condition field puts it on bit 0.)
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0x7FC00000) // NaN
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fOne)
	h.r.load(0,
		encFP(2, 1, 0, 0x30|5),    // c.ult.s
		encFP(2, 1, 1<<2, 0x30|4), // c.lt.s into fcc1 via cc bits
	)
	h.run(1)
	if !h.c.fccRead(0) {
		t.Errorf("unordered compare with NaN did not set FCC")
	}
	h.run(1)
	if h.c.fccRead(1) {
		t.Errorf("ordered c.lt.s with NaN set FCC1")
	}
}

func TestFPUMovesAndControl(t *testing.T) {
	h := newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetReg(8, fOne5)
	h.r.load(0,
		encMTC1(8, 1),        // mtc1 r8, f1
		encMFC1(9, 1),        // mfc1 r9, f1
		encI(0x09, 0, 10, 2), // addiu r10, r0, 2 (rounding RP)
		encCTC1(10, 31),      // ctc1 r10, fcsr
		encCFC1(11, 31),      // cfc1 r11, fcsr
		encCFC1(12, 0),       // cfc1 r12, fcr0 = implementation ID
	)
	h.run(6)
	if got := h.c.FReg(1); got != fOne5 {
		t.Errorf("mtc1 f1 = %#08x", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(9); got != fOne5 {
		t.Errorf("mfc1 r9 = %#08x", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(11); got != 2 {
		t.Errorf("cfc1 fcsr = %#08x, want 2", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.Reg(12); got != 0x00003351 {
		t.Errorf("cfc1 fcr0 = %#08x, want 0x00003351", got)
	}
	// LWC1 and SWC1 round trip through memory.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(3, 0x40580000)
	h.r.load(0,
		encI(0x39, 0, 3, 0x500), // swc1 f3, 0x500(r0)
		encI(0x31, 0, 5, 0x500), // lwc1 f5, 0x500(r0)
	)
	h.run(2)
	if got := h.c.FReg(5); got != 0x40580000 {
		t.Errorf("lwc1/swc1 round trip = %#08x", got)
	}
	// MOVT.S moves when FCC is set, MOVF.S does not.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fTwo)
	h.c.SetFReg(3, 0xDEADBEEF)
	h.c.SetFReg(4, 0x12345678)
	h.r.load(0,
		encFP(2, 1, 0, 0x30|4), // c.lt.s: FCC = true
		encFP(0, 1, 3, 0x11),   // movt.s f3, f1
		encFP(0, 1, 4, 0x10),   // movf.s f4, f1 (no move)
	)
	h.run(3)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != fOne {
		t.Errorf("movt.s f3 = %#08x, want 1.0 bits", got)
	}
	if got := h.c.FReg(4); got != 0x12345678 {
		t.Errorf("movf.s f4 = %#08x, want unchanged", got)
	}
}

func TestFPURoundingModesArithmetic(t *testing.T) {
	// 1.5 * 1.5 = 2.25 exactly in every mode.
	for mode := uint32(0); mode < 4; mode++ {
		h := newFPUHarness()
		h.c.fcr[31] = mode
		h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne5)
		h.c.SetFReg(2, fOne5)
		h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x02))
		h.run(1)
		if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0x40100000 {
			t.Errorf("mode %d: 1.5*1.5 = %#08x, want 2.25 bits", mode, got)
		}
	}
	// 1/3 under RZ truncates the RN result by one ulp:
	// RN 0x3EAAAAAB, RZ 0x3EAAAAAA.
	h := newFPUHarness()
	h.c.fcr[31] = 1 // RZ
	h.c.SetFReg(1, fOne)
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fThree)
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x03))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0x3EAAAAAA {
		t.Errorf("RZ 1/3 = %#08x, want 0x3EAAAAAA", got)
	}
	// RP goes the other way from RN for a value below the RN result
	// is wrong way check: use -1/3: RN = 0xBEAAAAAB, RP (toward
	// +Inf) must be 0xBEAAAAAA.
	h = newFPUHarness()
	h.c.fcr[31] = 2            // RP
	h.c.SetFReg(1, 0xBF800000) // -1.0
	h.c.SetFReg(2, fThree)
	h.r.load(0, encFP(2, 1, 3, 0x03))
	h.run(1)
	if got := h.c.FReg(3); got != 0xBEAAAAAA {
		t.Errorf("RP -1/3 = %#08x, want 0xBEAAAAAA", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex/vfpu.go ====================

package allegrex

import "math"

// VFPU (COP2) implementation.
//
// Layout: 8 matrices, each 4 rows by 4 columns. The linear index of
// an element is m*16 + row*4 + col.
//
// Register field layouts (all three pinned by the pspautotests
// binaries, whose assemblers encode named registers; PSP-2 used an
// invented layout that its own unit tests echoed back, and every
// corpus test disagreed):
//
//   - Arithmetic fields (vd at [6:0], vs at [14:8], vt at [22:16])
//     and the mfv/mtv operand: bits [4:2] are the matrix. A single
//     takes its row from bits [1:0] and its column from bits [6:5]
//     (vcst.s S010 is field 1, S001 is 32, S100 is 4). A vector
//     takes its fixed coordinate from bits [1:0] (the column, or
//     the row when bit 5, the transpose flag, is set) and walks
//     the other coordinate from 0, or from 4-n when bit 6 (the end
//     anchor) is set: C010 is 1, R000 is 32, C001 (a triple over
//     rows 1..3 of column 0) is 64.
//   - Matrix operands (vmmul, vtfm, vmscl, ...): bits [4:2] are
//     the matrix in every slot. vtfm and vhtfm read the matrix
//     in the plain layout and dot its columns with the vector.
//     vmmul decodes each slot's anchor from its own bits (see
//     matrixOriginVmmul): with b6, b5, b1 the field's bits 6, 5,
//     and 1, vs anchors at (b6, b1), vt at (b1 AND NOT b5,
//     b5 OR b6), vd at (b6 XOR b5, b5 OR b1), anchors scale by
//     (4-n) and swap for triples, and the product is stored
//     transposed. vmscl reads its matrix with bit 5 cleared.
//   - Load/store fields (bits [20:16] giving the high five bits,
//     bits [1:0] the low two): the field is (matrix << 4) |
//     (fixed << 2) | start, with bit 0 the transpose flag and the
//     fixed coordinate at bits [3:2] of the field: lv.q C010 and
//     lv.q R001 are both field 4, told apart by the flag in bit 0
//     of the word. A single (lv.s/sv.s) takes its column from the
//     fixed bits and its row from the low two bits.
//
// Prefixes: the source prefix (spfx for VS reads, tpfx for VT reads)
// swizzles, takes absolute value, negates, or substitutes a constant
// per component. The destination prefix (dpfx) saturates or masks
// per component on a VD write. Each prefix is one shot: it is
// consumed by the first matching read or write that uses it.
// Matrix operations (vmmul, vmscl, matrix vmov) do not apply any
// prefix; that is a documented simplification of this slice.
// Conversions read their source with the source prefix applied but
// write their destination raw, with no destination prefix.
// The VFPU trig unit is pi/2: vsin(x) is sin(x * pi/2) and likewise
// for vcos and vnsin.

// The prefix constant table, pinned by the corpus prefix_ctrl
// readbacks: index (swizzle | abs<<2) selects 0, 1, 2, 1/2, 3,
// 1/3, 1/4, 1/6 in that order.
var vfpuConstTable = [8]float32{0, 1, 2, 1.0 / 2.0, 3, 1.0 / 3.0, 1.0 / 4.0, 1.0 / 6.0}

// vecIndices decodes a 7 bit register field r for an operand of
// size n lanes (1 single, 2 pair, 3 triple, 4 quad) and returns the
// linear indices of its elements; the first n entries are valid.
// See the layout notes at the top of the file.
func vecIndices(r uint32, n int) [4]int {
	m := int((r >> 2) & 7)
	var out [4]int
	if n == 1 {
		row := int(r & 3)
		col := int((r >> 5) & 3)
		out[0] = m*16 + row*4 + col
		return out
	}
	fixed := int(r & 3)
	tr := (r>>5)&1 != 0
	start := 0
	if (r>>6)&1 != 0 {
		start = 4 - n
	}
	for i := 0; i < n && i < 4; i++ {
		if tr {
			out[i] = m*16 + fixed*4 + start + i
		} else {
			out[i] = m*16 + (start+i)*4 + fixed
		}
	}
	return out
}

// singleIndex decodes a 7 bit field as a single element.
func singleIndex(r uint32) int {
	return vecIndices(r, 1)[0]
}

// dotDestIndex decodes a scalar VV operand position (the
// dot product family's destination, the vscl scalar, scalar
// VV reads generally). The corpus witnesses pin the offset
// within the matrix to (low field bits) + (high field
// bits): field 3 lands at 3 (overlap), field 5 at 17
// (minmax_tie vmin.s VT), field 32 at 1 (vbranch vcmp.s
// VT), field 36 at 17 (prefix_ctrl). The plain vector
// layout (low bits strided) and its transpose each fail one
// of those; the sum fits all of them. The VFPU5 single
// writes (VIIM and VFIM) keep the vecIndices layout, which
// the corpus vregs Filled print pins for writes.
func dotDestIndex(r uint32) int {
	m := int((r >> 2) & 7)
	return m*16 + int(r&3) + int((r>>5)&3)
}

// matIndex returns the linear index of matrix m element (i, j),
// where i is the row and j is the column.
func matIndex(m, i, j int) int { return m*16 + i*4 + j }

// matrixOrigin decodes a matrix operand field: the matrix from
// bits [4:2], the transpose flag from bit 5, the anchor row from
// bits [1:0] and the anchor column from bit 6 (blocks anchor at
// even columns).
func matrixOrigin(r uint32) (m int, tr bool, row0, col0 int) {
	m = int((r >> 2) & 7)
	tr = (r>>5)&1 != 0
	row0 = int(r & 3)
	col0 = int((r>>6)&1) << 1
	return m, tr, row0, col0
}

// matSlot identifies which operand slot of a matrix group
// instruction a field sits in.
type matSlot int

const (
	slotVD matSlot = iota
	slotVS
	slotVT
)

// matrixOriginVmmul decodes a vmmul operand field. The three
// slots do NOT share one encoding: the corpus matrix test pins
// each slot's anchor bits separately (the same register name
// encodes differently per slot; the assembler's M000 is 32 in
// the vs field and 0 in the vt field, per the corpus
// _checkSquare4 word). Writing b6, b5, b1 for field bits 6, 5
// and 1, the anchor in block units (R, C) is:
//
//	vs: R = b6,          C = b1
//	vt: R = b1 AND NOT b5, C = b5 OR b6
//	vd: R = b6 XOR b5,   C = b5 OR b1
//
// fitted on every witnessed operand: the .q word (8, 32, 4),
// the .p series (8, 32, 4), (72, 96, 38), (104, 34, 6),
// (74, 66, 70) whose four products and placements the expected
// output fixes exactly, and the .t destination 72 whose block
// lands at file rows 0..2, cols 1..3 (the pair swaps on the
// triple grid). No slot transposes in vmmul: every witnessed
// product is the plain product of the anchored blocks. The
// matrix number is bits [4:2] in all slots.
func matrixOriginVmmul(r uint32, n int, slot matSlot) (m, row0, col0 int) {
	m = int((r >> 2) & 7)
	b6 := (r >> 6) & 1
	b5 := (r >> 5) & 1
	b1 := (r >> 1) & 1
	var R, C uint32
	switch slot {
	case slotVS:
		R, C = b6, b1
	case slotVT:
		R, C = b1&^b5, b5|b6
	default: // slotVD
		R, C = b6^b5, b5|b1
	}
	if n == 3 {
		return m, int(C), int(R)
	}
	return m, int(R) * (4 - n), int(C) * (4 - n)
}

// readMatrixAt reads the size n block anchored at (row0, col0)
// of matrix m, with no prefix and no transpose.
func (c *CPU) readMatrixAt(m, row0, col0, n int) [4][4]float64 {
	var out [4][4]float64
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
			out[i][j] = fpInput(c.vregs[matIndex(m, row0+i, col0+j)])
		}
	}
	return out
}

// writeMatrixAt writes vals into the size n block anchored at
// (row0, col0) of matrix m, with no prefix and no transpose.
func (c *CPU) writeMatrixAt(m, row0, col0, n int, vals [4][4]float64) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
			c.vregs[matIndex(m, row0+i, col0+j)] = roundToSingleVFPU(vals[i][j])
		}
	}
}

// matrixFilePos maps a logical matrix element (i, j) of a size n
// block to its file position (row, col): the block anchors at
// (row0, col0), and a transposed operand reads its elements
// swapped.
func matrixFilePos(r uint32, n, i, j int) (int, int, int) {
	m, tr, row0, col0 := matrixOrigin(r)
	if !tr {
		return m, row0 + i, col0 + j
	}
	return m, row0 + j, col0 + i
}

// readMatrix reads a size n matrix operand raw, with no prefix.
func (c *CPU) readMatrix(r uint32, n int) [4][4]float64 {
	var out [4][4]float64
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
			m, row, col := matrixFilePos(r, n, i, j)
			out[i][j] = fpInput(c.vregs[matIndex(m, row, col)])
		}
	}
	return out
}

// writeMatrix writes a size n matrix operand raw, with no prefix.
func (c *CPU) writeMatrix(r uint32, n int, vals [4][4]float64) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
			m, row, col := matrixFilePos(r, n, i, j)
			c.vregs[matIndex(m, row, col)] = roundToSingleVFPU(vals[i][j])
		}
	}
}

// writeMatrixRawBits writes a size n matrix of raw bit patterns.
func (c *CPU) writeMatrixRawBits(r uint32, n int, vals [4][4]uint32) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		for j := 0; j < n; j++ {
			m, row, col := matrixFilePos(r, n, i, j)
			c.vregs[matIndex(m, row, col)] = vals[i][j]
		}
	}
}

// applySourcePrefix applies a source prefix immediate to a
// padded source vector. The immediate is planar, pinned by the
// corpus prefix_ctrl readbacks: bits [7:0] hold the per lane
// swizzle (2 bits each), bits [11:8] the per lane absolute
// flags, bits [15:12] the per lane constant select, and bits
// [19:16] the per lane negate flags. A constant lane reads
// vfpuConstTable[swizzle | abs<<2], negated when its negate
// flag is set (the abs flag doubles as the constant index's
// high bit); any other lane reads the swizzled source lane
// with abs and negate applied.
func applySourcePrefix(padded [4]float64, imm uint32, n int) [4]float64 {
	var out [4]float64
	for i := 0; i < n && i < 4; i++ {
		swizzle := int((imm >> uint(2*i)) & 3)
		abs := (imm>>uint(8+i))&1 != 0
		cst := (imm>>uint(12+i))&1 != 0
		neg := (imm>>uint(16+i))&1 != 0
		if cst {
			idx := swizzle
			if abs {
				idx |= 4
			}
			v := float64(vfpuConstTable[idx])
			if neg {
				v = -v
			}
			out[i] = v
			continue
		}
		v := padded[swizzle]
		if abs {
			v = math.Abs(v)
		}
		if neg {
			v = -v
		}
		out[i] = v
	}
	return out
}

// resetPrefixes restores all three prefix registers to their
// power on defaults (source identity swizzle 0xE4, dest 0) and
// disarms them. The corpus prefix_consume test pins this: after
// any VFPU compute op executes, MFVC reads the defaults back,
// even for prefixes the op itself did not use (vmov resets the
// target prefix too, vzero resets all three). Ops that do not
// compute (loads, stores, moves, vnop, vsync, vflush, plain
// integer instructions) leave armed prefixes untouched.
func (c *CPU) resetPrefixes() {
	c.spfxImm = 0xE4
	c.tpfxImm = 0xE4
	c.dpfxImm = 0
	c.spfxOn = false
	c.tpfxOn = false
	c.dpfxOn = false
	c.pfxPoison = false
}

// readRawPrefixed returns the source operand's raw bit
// patterns with the source prefix applied bitwise, the model
// the corpus prefix_unpack test documents for the integer
// pack and unpack family: a constant lane substitutes the
// constant's float encoding, negate flips the sign bit, abs
// clears it, and the swizzle selects among the operand's own
// lanes. A select outside the operand's lanes yields zero: on
// hardware it replays a stale prefix unit latch whose update
// rule the test itself records as not understood, and the
// test's author calls zero the reasonable substitute.
func (c *CPU) readRawPrefixed(vs uint32, n int) []uint32 {
	idx := vecIndices(vs, n)
	if n == 1 {
		// A single source reads at the transposed single
		// position, the same decode the dot family uses
		// (the corpus overlap vuc2ifs.s S030 case).
		idx[0] = dotDestIndex(vs)
	}
	in := make([]uint32, n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		in[i] = c.vregs[idx[i]]
	}
	if !c.spfxOn {
		return in
	}
	imm := c.spfxImm
	c.spfxOn = false
	out := make([]uint32, n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		swizzle := int((imm >> uint(2*i)) & 3)
		abs := (imm>>uint(8+i))&1 != 0
		cst := (imm>>uint(12+i))&1 != 0
		neg := (imm>>uint(16+i))&1 != 0
		if cst {
			ci := swizzle
			if abs {
				ci |= 4
			}
			b := math.Float32bits(vfpuConstTable[ci])
			if neg {
				b ^= 0x80000000
			}
			out[i] = b
			continue
		}
		var b uint32
		if swizzle < n {
			b = in[swizzle]
		}
		if abs {
			b &^= 0x80000000
		}
		if neg {
			b ^= 0x80000000
		}
		out[i] = b
	}
	return out
}

// applyDestSaturation applies an armed dest prefix's
// saturation to raw result patterns, treating them as floats
// (the corpus prefix_unpack D cases: a huge positive pattern
// clamps to 1.0, a negative one to 0). The write mask is the
// writers' business, not this function's.
func (c *CPU) applyDestSaturation(out []uint32) {
	if !c.dpfxOn {
		return
	}
	imm := c.dpfxImm
	for i := range out {
		sat := (imm >> uint(2*i)) & 3
		if sat != 1 && sat != 3 {
			continue
		}
		if isNaNBits(out[i]) {
			out[i] = 0x7F800001
			continue
		}
		v := float64(math.Float32frombits(out[i]))
		if sat == 1 {
			if v < 0 {
				v = 0
			} else if v > 1 {
				v = 1
			}
		} else {
			if v < -1 {
				v = -1
			} else if v > 1 {
				v = 1
			}
		}
		out[i] = math.Float32bits(float32(v))
	}
}

// execCompute runs one VFPU compute op and, when it executed
// without faulting, resets the prefix registers (see
// resetPrefixes). A faulting op leaves the prefixes as they
// were, matching the exception path.
func (c *CPU) execCompute(instr uint32, op func(uint32) int) int {
	faults := c.vfpuFaultCount
	r := op(instr)
	if c.vfpuFaultCount == faults {
		c.resetPrefixes()
	}
	return r
}

// paddedFloats builds the padded float vector for a raw read: the
// operand lanes through fpInput, zeros beyond the size.
func (c *CPU) paddedFloats(r uint32, n int) [4]float64 {
	idx := vecIndices(r, n)
	if n == 1 {
		// A scalar VV operand reads at the transposed single
		// position (the dotDestIndex decode): the corpus
		// minmax_tie vmin.s reads its VT single (field 5)
		// from the position the C110 quad load wrote, which
		// is 17, not the 20 the vector layout gives. Vector
		// operands (n >= 2) and the VFPU5 single writes keep
		// the layout of vecIndices.
		idx[0] = dotDestIndex(r)
	}
	var out [4]float64
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		out[i] = fpInput(c.vregs[idx[i]])
	}
	return out
}

// prefixOutOfRange reports whether an armed source prefix
// selects, for some used lane, a non-constant lane beyond the
// op size. On hardware such a prefix poisons the whole op:
// every source read of the op returns zero, so the result is
// the zero combination (the corpus prefix_ctrl OUTSIDE cases
// and the prefix_unpack latch vadd case, where an out of
// range swizzle on a scalar op zeroes even the operand whose
// own prefix is unarmed).
func prefixOutOfRange(imm uint32, n int) bool {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		if (imm>>(12+uint(i)))&1 == 1 {
			continue
		}
		if int((imm>>(2*uint(i)))&3) >= n {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// readVS reads the VS operand of size n, consuming the source
// prefix if one is armed.
func (c *CPU) readVS(r uint32, n int) [4]float64 {
	if c.spfxOn {
		c.spfxOn = false
		if c.pfxPoison || prefixOutOfRange(c.spfxImm, n) {
			c.pfxPoison = true
			return [4]float64{}
		}
		return applySourcePrefix(c.paddedFloats(r, n), c.spfxImm, n)
	}
	if c.pfxPoison {
		return [4]float64{}
	}
	return c.paddedFloats(r, n)
}

// readVT reads the VT operand of size n, consuming the target
// prefix if one is armed.
func (c *CPU) readVT(r uint32, n int) [4]float64 {
	if c.tpfxOn {
		c.tpfxOn = false
		if c.pfxPoison || prefixOutOfRange(c.tpfxImm, n) {
			c.pfxPoison = true
			return [4]float64{}
		}
		return applySourcePrefix(c.paddedFloats(r, n), c.tpfxImm, n)
	}
	if c.pfxPoison {
		return [4]float64{}
	}
	return c.paddedFloats(r, n)
}

// readVSRaw reads the VS operand raw with no prefix and no consume.
func (c *CPU) readVSRaw(r uint32, n int) [4]float64 {
	return c.paddedFloats(r, n)
}

// applySPFXNow applies and consumes the source prefix on an
// already converted float vector. Used by vh2f and vi2f, whose
// sources are not floats in the register file.
func (c *CPU) applySPFXNow(vals [4]float64, n int) [4]float64 {
	if c.spfxOn {
		c.spfxOn = false
		return applySourcePrefix(vals, c.spfxImm, n)
	}
	return vals
}

// writeVD writes float values to the VD operand of size n,
// consuming the destination prefix if one is armed: saturation
// clamps per lane, masked lanes keep their old value.
func (c *CPU) writeVD(r uint32, n int, vals [4]float64) {
	idx := vecIndices(r, n)
	var imm uint32
	on := c.dpfxOn
	if on {
		imm = c.dpfxImm
		c.dpfxOn = false
	}
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		v := vals[i]
		if on {
			// Planar dest prefix, pinned by the corpus
			// prefix_ctrl readbacks: bits [7:0] hold the
			// per lane saturation (2 bits each: 1 clamps
			// to [0, 1], 3 clamps to [-1, 1]) and bits
			// [11:8] the per lane write mask (set skips
			// the lane).
			sat := (imm >> uint(2*i)) & 3
			if (imm>>uint(8+i))&1 != 0 {
				continue
			}
			if sat == 1 || sat == 3 {
				if math.IsNaN(v) {
					// Saturation writes the fixed positive
					// VFPU NaN pattern for a NaN of either
					// sign (corpus prefix_sat).
					c.vregs[idx[i]] = 0x7F800001
					continue
				}
				lo := 0.0
				if sat == 3 {
					lo = -1
				}
				if v < lo {
					v = lo
				} else if v > 1 {
					v = 1
				}
			}
		}
		c.vregs[idx[i]] = roundToSingleVFPU(v)
	}
}

// roundToSingleVFPU rounds like roundToSingle (RN, flush to
// zero) except that a NaN result takes the VFPU pattern: the
// sign bit over 0x7F800001. Every VFPU float result the corpus
// records (vrcp, vsin, vsqrt of a negative, vdiv with a NaN
// operand) carries that pattern rather than the canonical
// quiet NaN the scalar FPU produces.
func roundToSingleVFPU(x float64) uint32 {
	if math.IsNaN(x) {
		if math.Signbit(x) {
			return 0xFF800001
		}
		return 0x7F800001
	}
	return roundToSingle(x, 0)
}

// writeRawVec writes raw bit patterns to an operand of size n with
// no destination prefix and no consumption of it.
func (c *CPU) writeRawVec(r uint32, n int, vals [4]uint32) {
	idx := vecIndices(r, n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		c.vregs[idx[i]] = vals[i]
	}
}

// writeRawFloats converts float values to bits and writes them raw.
func (c *CPU) writeRawFloats(r uint32, n int, vals [4]float64) {
	var bits [4]uint32
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		bits[i] = roundToSingleVFPU(vals[i])
	}
	c.writeRawVec(r, n, bits)
}

// vfpuUnimplemented faults a genuinely unimplemented VFPU encoding.
func (c *CPU) vfpuUnimplemented() int {
	c.vfpuFaultCount++
	c.raiseException(excRI, 0)
	return 1
}

// vfpuCtrlRead reads a VFPU control index for MFVC.
func (c *CPU) vfpuCtrlRead(idx uint32) uint32 {
	switch {
	case idx == 128:
		return c.spfxImm & 0xFFFFF
	case idx == 129:
		return c.tpfxImm & 0xFFFFF
	case idx == 130:
		return c.dpfxImm & 0xFFF
	case idx == 131:
		return c.cc
	case idx == 132:
		return 0xFFFFFFFF
	case idx == 135:
		return 0x00003351
	case idx >= 136 && idx <= 143:
		return c.rngState[idx-136]
	default:
		if idx < 144 {
			return c.mfvcStore[idx]
		}
		return 0
	}
}

// vfpuCtrlWrite writes a VFPU control index for MTVC. Writing a
// prefix index arms that prefix.
func (c *CPU) vfpuCtrlWrite(idx uint32, v uint32) {
	switch {
	case idx == 128:
		c.spfxImm = v & 0xFFFFF
		c.spfxOn = true
	case idx == 129:
		c.tpfxImm = v & 0xFFFFF
		c.tpfxOn = true
	case idx == 130:
		c.dpfxImm = v & 0xFFF
		c.dpfxOn = true
	case idx == 131:
		// The CC register holds six bits; the vbranch corpus
		// test branches on immediates 6 and 7 and reads them
		// as clear even after writing all ones.
		c.cc = v & 0x3F
	case idx == 132, idx == 135:
		// Ignored: read only registers.
	case idx >= 136 && idx <= 143:
		c.rngState[idx-136] = v
	default:
		if idx < 144 {
			c.mfvcStore[idx] = v
		}
	}
}

// execCOP2 dispatches COP2 instructions. COP2 now holds only the
// moves between the GPRs and the VFPU and the BC2 branch; every
// arithmetic encoding lives under its own primary opcode. Any
// other rs value is a reserved instruction.
func (c *CPU) execCOP2(instr uint32) int {
	rs := (instr >> 21) & 31
	rt := int((instr >> 16) & 31)
	switch rs {
	case 0x00: // MFC2
		reg7 := ((instr>>11)&31)<<2 | ((instr >> 6) & 3)
		c.setReg(rt, c.vregs[singleIndex(reg7)])
	case 0x02: // CFC2
		rd := (instr >> 11) & 31
		v := c.ctrl[rd]
		if rd == 0 {
			v = 0x00003351
		}
		c.setReg(rt, v)
	case 0x03: // MFV / MFVC share rs 3: bit 7 of the word
		// separates them. Clear: MFV, the operand is the 7 bit
		// register field in the low bits (mfv $t3, S100 is
		// 0x486B0004). Set: MFVC, the operand is the control
		// index in the low byte (mfvc $t0, $136 is 0x48680088;
		// PSP-2 read bits 15..8, which made every RCX
		// readback return slot 0).
		if instr&0x80 != 0 {
			c.setReg(rt, c.vfpuCtrlRead(instr&0xFF))
		} else {
			c.setReg(rt, c.vregs[singleIndex(instr&0x7F)])
		}
	case 0x04: // MTC2
		reg7 := ((instr>>11)&31)<<2 | ((instr >> 6) & 3)
		c.vregs[singleIndex(reg7)] = c.regs[rt]
	case 0x06: // CTC2
		rd := (instr >> 11) & 31
		if rd != 0 {
			c.ctrl[rd] = c.regs[rt]
		}
	case 0x07: // MTV / MTVC share rs 7, separated by bit 7
		// exactly as MFV / MFVC (mtv $v1, S100 is 0x48E30004,
		// mtvc $88 is 0x48E80088).
		if instr&0x80 != 0 {
			c.vfpuCtrlWrite(instr&0xFF, c.regs[rt])
		} else {
			c.vregs[singleIndex(instr&0x7F)] = c.regs[rt]
		}
	case 0x08: // BC2: rt is (imm3 << 2) | (likely << 1) | tf,
		// where imm3 selects the CC bit under test (the vbranch
		// corpus binary's words 0x49000002.. pin the layout;
		// PSP-2 always tested bit 0).
		condTrue := (c.cc>>(uint(rt)>>2))&1 != 0
		taken := (rt&1 != 0) == condTrue
		if (rt&2) != 0 && !taken {
			// Likely form: annul the delay slot.
			c.pc = c.nextPC
			c.nextPC = c.pc + 4
			c.inDelaySlot = false
		} else {
			c.branch(taken, c.branchTarget(signExt16(instr&0xFFFF)))
		}
	default:
		return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
	}
	return 1
}

// vvFields decodes the shared VV operand fields. The size enum is
// split across bit 7 and bit 15: 0 single, 1 pair, 2 triple,
// 3 quad. The group field G is bits 25:23.
func vvFields(instr uint32) (vd, vs, vt uint32, sizeEnum uint32, n int, g uint32) {
	vd = instr & 0x7F
	vs = (instr >> 8) & 0x7F
	vt = (instr >> 16) & 0x7F
	sizeEnum = (instr>>7)&1 | ((instr>>15)&1)<<1
	n = int(sizeEnum) + 1
	g = (instr >> 23) & 7
	return vd, vs, vt, sizeEnum, n, g
}

// vvBinary applies an element wise binary float operation over
// the VS and VT operands and writes VD.
func (c *CPU) vvBinary(vd, vs, vt uint32, n int, f func(a, b float64) float64) int {
	a := c.readVS(vs, n)
	b := c.readVT(vt, n)
	var out [4]float64
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		out[i] = f(a[i], b[i])
	}
	c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
	return 1
}

// execVVArith dispatches opcode 0x18: G=0 vadd, G=1 vsub,
// G=2 vsbn, G=7 vdiv.
func (c *CPU) execVVArith(instr uint32) int {
	vd, vs, vt, _, n, g := vvFields(instr)
	switch g {
	case 0:
		return c.vvBinary(vd, vs, vt, n, func(a, b float64) float64 { return a + b })
	case 1:
		return c.vvBinary(vd, vs, vt, n, func(a, b float64) float64 { return a - b })
	case 2: // vsbn, single only: set the exponent of VS from VT
		if n != 1 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		src := c.vregs[singleIndex(vs)]
		exp := int32(c.vregs[singleIndex(vt)])
		out := src
		v := fpInput(src)
		if v != 0 && !math.IsNaN(v) && !math.IsInf(v, 0) {
			out = (src & 0x807FFFFF) | uint32((exp+127)&0xFF)<<23
		}
		var bits [4]uint32
		bits[0] = out
		c.writeRawVec(vd, 1, bits)
		return 1
	case 7:
		return c.vvBinary(vd, vs, vt, n, func(a, b float64) float64 {
			r := a / b
			if math.IsNaN(r) {
				// The result NaN takes the XOR of the operand
				// signs (the corpus prefix_sat vdiv rows: -NaN
				// divided by a negative is a positive NaN).
				if math.Signbit(a) != math.Signbit(b) {
					return -math.NaN()
				}
				return math.NaN()
			}
			return r
		})
	}
	return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
}

// execVVProd dispatches opcode 0x19: G=0 vmul, G=1 vdot,
// G=2 vscl, G=4 vhdp, G=5 vcrs, G=6 vdet.
func (c *CPU) execVVProd(instr uint32) int {
	vd, vs, vt, _, n, g := vvFields(instr)
	switch g {
	case 0:
		return c.vvBinary(vd, vs, vt, n, func(a, b float64) float64 {
			r := a * b
			if math.IsNaN(r) {
				if math.Signbit(a) != math.Signbit(b) {
					return -math.NaN()
				}
				return math.NaN()
			}
			return r
		})
	case 1: // vdot, pair and up
		if n < 2 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		a := c.readVS(vs, n)
		b := c.readVT(vt, n)
		sum := 0.0
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			sum += a[i] * b[i]
		}
		c.vregs[dotDestIndex(vd)] = roundToSingleVFPU(sum)
		return 1
	case 2: // vscl: scale VS by the VT scalar, read raw
		a := c.readVS(vs, n)
		s := fpInput(c.vregs[dotDestIndex(vt)])
		var out [4]float64
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			out[i] = a[i] * s
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 4: // vhdp, pair and up: dot of all but the last lane,
		// plus the last VT lane on its own
		if n < 2 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		a := c.readVS(vs, n)
		b := c.readVT(vt, n)
		sum := 0.0
		for i := 0; i < n-1; i++ {
			sum += a[i] * b[i]
		}
		sum += b[n-1]
		c.vregs[dotDestIndex(vd)] = roundToSingleVFPU(sum)
		return 1
	case 5: // vcrs, triple only: partial cross product
		if n != 3 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		a := c.readVS(vs, 3)
		b := c.readVT(vt, 3)
		var out [4]float64
		out[0] = a[1] * b[2]
		out[1] = a[2] * b[0]
		out[2] = a[0] * b[1]
		c.writeVD(vd, 3, out)
		return 1
	case 6: // vdet, pair only: 2x2 determinant to a single
		if n != 2 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		a := c.readVS(vs, 2)
		b := c.readVT(vt, 2)
		c.vregs[dotDestIndex(vd)] = roundToSingleVFPU(a[0]*b[1] - a[1]*b[0])
		return 1
	}
	return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
}

// execVVCmpGrp dispatches opcode 0x1B: G=0 vcmp, G=2 vmin,
// G=3 vmax, G=6 vsge, G=7 vslt.
func (c *CPU) execVVCmpGrp(instr uint32) int {
	vd, vs, vt, _, n, g := vvFields(instr)
	switch g {
	case 0:
		return c.execVCMP(instr)
	case 2, 3:
		if !c.spfxOn && !c.tpfxOn && !c.dpfxOn {
			// Raw path: the hardware orders the operand bit
			// patterns in float totalOrder, in which a
			// negative NaN sorts below every value and a
			// positive NaN above every value, and the winning
			// pattern is stored unchanged (the corpus minmax
			// test's both-NaN cases pin this: vmin of +NaN
			// and -NaN is the -NaN pattern 0xFFBFFFFF).
			ai := vecIndices(vs, n)
			bi := vecIndices(vt, n)
			if n == 1 {
				ai[0] = dotDestIndex(vs)
				bi[0] = dotDestIndex(vt)
			}
			var out [4]uint32
			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
				out[i] = vfpuMinMaxBits(c.vregs[ai[i]], c.vregs[bi[i]], g == 3)
			}
			c.writeRawVec(vd, n, out)
			return 1
		}
		return c.vvBinary(vd, vs, vt, n, func(a, b float64) float64 {
			return vfpuMinMax(a, b, g == 3)
		})
	case 5: // vscmp: three way compare, -1, 0 or +1 per lane
		return c.vvBinary(vd, vs, vt, n, func(a, b float64) float64 {
			switch {
			case a < b:
				return -1
			case a > b:
				return 1
			}
			return 0
		})
	case 6, 7:
		return c.vvBinary(vd, vs, vt, n, func(a, b float64) float64 {
			ok := a >= b
			if g == 7 {
				ok = a < b
			}
			if ok {
				return 1
			}
			return 0
		})
	}
	return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
}

// vfpuMinMaxBits orders two float bit patterns by the float
// totalOrder (sign magnitude key) and returns the winning
// pattern unchanged.
func vfpuMinMaxBits(a, b uint32, isMax bool) uint32 {
	if fpInput(a) == fpInput(b) {
		// A flushed value tie: the two zeros, and denormals
		// against the zero they flush to, compare equal on
		// hardware, and the winner is the second (VT)
		// pattern, stored raw (the corpus minmax_tie and
		// minmax_zero rows). NaN never ties (NaN != NaN), so
		// the NaN totalOrder below is untouched. The sort
		// ops never reach this arm: their equal float
		// collapse fires first.
		return b
	}
	key := func(x uint32) uint32 {
		if x>>31 != 0 {
			return ^x
		}
		return x | 0x80000000
	}
	ka, kb := key(a), key(b)
	if isMax {
		if kb > ka {
			return b
		}
		return a
	}
	if kb < ka {
		return b
	}
	return a
}

// vfpuMinMax is the shared vmin and vmax lane operation: a NaN
// operand yields the other operand, two NaNs yield a NaN.
func vfpuMinMax(a, b float64, isMax bool) float64 {
	if a == 0 && b == 0 {
		// A signed zero tie takes the VT operand, as in
		// the raw path (the corpus minmax_tie rows run with
		// a prefix armed, so they land here).
		return b
	}
	if math.IsNaN(a) && math.IsNaN(b) {
		return math.NaN()
	}
	if math.IsNaN(a) {
		return b
	}
	if math.IsNaN(b) {
		return a
	}
	if isMax {
		if a > b {
			return a
		}
		return b
	}
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

// nextRand steps the VFPU xorshift generator once and returns
// the new state word. The hardware RCX bank visibly keeps float
// form after draws (the seed 0 corpus block shows RCX0 taking
// the draw's low half and RCX4 its high half, both under a
// 0x3F800000 exponent), so the bank is updated in that form
// rather than with the raw word; the true state recurrence is
// a wider linear structure that stays modelled, see the README.
func (c *CPU) nextRand() uint32 {
	x := c.rngState[0]
	if x == 0 {
		x = 0x1
	}
	x ^= x << 13
	x ^= x >> 17
	x ^= x << 5
	c.rngState[0] = 0x3F800000 | (x & 0xFFFF)
	c.rngState[4] = 0x3F800000 | (x >> 16)
	return x
}

// randUnit returns the next generator output as a value in
// [0, 1), using the top 24 bits of the state.
func (c *CPU) randUnit() float64 {
	return float64(c.nextRand()>>8) * (1.0 / 16777216.0)
}

// execVFPU34 dispatches opcode 0x34 by its group field, bits
// 25:23: group 0 is the unary group, group 4 the scaled float to
// int conversions, group 5 the scaled int to float conversion
// plus the vcmov carve out.
func (c *CPU) execVFPU34(instr uint32) int {
	vd, vs, _, _, n, g := vvFields(instr)
	f := (instr >> 16) & 0x7F
	switch g {
	case 0:
		return c.execVFPUUnary(instr, vd, vs, n, f)
	case 4:
		return c.execVF2I(vd, vs, n, f)
	case 5:
		return c.execVI2FOrCmov(vd, vs, n, f)
	case 6, 7:
		// vwbn.s: the immediate scale form. Its encoding
		// shares opcode 0x34 with bits [25:24] = 3, so it
		// lands in groups 6 and 7 here by the immediate's
		// top bit; the immediate itself is bits [23:16].
		// The operation (the hardware's exponent modulus,
		// per the published VFPU documentation, restated):
		// take the source's significand with its implicit
		// leading bit, shift it right by (imm - exp) mod 16
		// when imm exceeds the exponent field, left by
		// (exp - imm) mod 16 otherwise, then reassemble
		// with the exponent field replaced by imm; zero,
		// Inf and NaN inputs keep their pattern with the
		// exponent field ORed with imm.
		imm := (instr >> 16) & 0xFF
		src := c.vregs[singleIndex(vs)]
		exp := (src >> 23) & 0xFF
		var out uint32
		if exp == 0 || exp == 0xFF {
			out = src | (imm << 23)
		} else {
			m := (src & 0x7FFFFF) | 0x800000
			if imm > exp {
				m >>= (imm - exp) & 0xF
			} else {
				m <<= (exp - imm) & 0xF
			}
			out = (src & 0x80000000) | (m & 0x7FFFFF) | (imm << 23)
		}
		c.writeRawMasked(vd, 1, []uint32{out})
		return 1
	}
	return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
}

// execVFPUUnary dispatches the opcode 0x34 group 0 unary and
// conversion functions, F = bits 22:16.
func (c *CPU) execVFPUUnary(instr uint32, vd, vs uint32, n int, f uint32) int {
	switch f {
	case 0x04, 0x05: // vsat0 / vsat1
		if !c.spfxOn && !c.dpfxOn {
			// Raw saturating copy: NaN patterns pass through
			// unchanged and denormals are not flushed (both
			// pinned by the corpus prefix_sat rows); only the
			// clamp itself is numeric.
			idx := vecIndices(vs, n)
			var bits [4]uint32
			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
				b := c.vregs[idx[i]]
				if isNaNBits(b) {
					bits[i] = b
					continue
				}
				v := float64(math.Float32frombits(b))
				lo := 0.0
				if f == 0x05 {
					lo = -1
				}
				if v < lo || (f == 0x04 && v == 0) {
					// The v == 0 arm is vsat0 rewriting a
					// negative zero as positive zero (the
					// corpus row 0,-0,denorm,-denorm).
					v = lo
				} else if v > 1 {
					v = 1
				}
				bits[i] = math.Float32bits(float32(v))
			}
			c.writeRawVec(vd, n, bits)
			return 1
		}
		a := c.readVS(vs, n)
		var out [4]float64
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			out[i] = vfpuUnaryOp(f, a[i])
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13,
		0x14, 0x15, 0x16, 0x17, 0x18, 0x1A, 0x1C, 0x4A:
		a := c.readVS(vs, n)
		var out [4]float64
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			out[i] = vfpuUnaryOp(f, a[i])
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 0x03: // vidt: identity matrix, raw write, no source
		var id [4][4]float64
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			id[i][i] = 1
		}
		c.writeMatrix(vd, n, id)
		return 1
	case 0x06: // vzero
		var out [4]float64
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 0x07: // vone
		var out [4]float64
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = 1
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 0x08: // vrepl: raw source single, no prefix. This
		// encoding could not be confirmed in the published docs;
		// it sits at a free group 0 F value, see the report.
		v := fpInput(c.vregs[singleIndex(vs)])
		var out [4]float64
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = v
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 0x09: // vsplt: same unconfirmed status as vrepl.
		a := c.readVS(vs, n)
		lane := int(vs & 3)
		if lane >= n {
			lane = n - 1
		}
		var out [4]float64
		for i := range out {
			out[i] = a[lane]
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 0x20: // vrnds: seed the generator from the raw VS bits.
		// The seeding expansion is pinned exactly by the
		// pspautotests vrnd recordings for six seeds: each RCX
		// word becomes 1.0f whose mantissa carries one seed
		// nibble (RCXk takes nibble k) above the seed half the
		// word indexes (low half for RCX0..3, high half for
		// RCX4..7). The draw recurrence itself is only modelled
		// (see nextRand); the corpus state sequences after draws
		// do not match this simple generator, an open item the
		// README flags.
		seed := c.vregs[singleIndex(vs)]
		for k := 0; k < 8; k++ {
			half := seed & 0xFFFF
			if k >= 4 {
				half = (seed >> 16) & 0xFFFF
			}
			nib := (seed >> (4 * k)) & 0xF
			c.rngState[k] = 0x3F800000 | (nib << 16) | half
		}
		return 1
	case 0x21: // vrndi: raw random words per lane
		var bits [4]uint32
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			bits[i] = c.nextRand()
		}
		c.writeRawVec(vd, n, bits)
		return 1
	case 0x22, 0x23: // vrndf1 in [1, 2), vrndf2 in [2, 4)
		var out [4]float64
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			u := c.randUnit()
			if f == 0x22 {
				out[i] = 1 + u
			} else {
				out[i] = 2 + 2*u
			}
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
		return 1
	case 0x32: // vf2h
		return c.execVF2H(vd, vs, n)
	case 0x33: // vh2f
		return c.execVH2F(vd, vs, n)
	case 0x36: // vsbz.s: rescale the source into [1, 2) by
		// replacing its exponent field with 127 and dropping
		// the sign; zero and NaN patterns pass unchanged (the
		// published VFPU documentation; the same effect as
		// vsbn with a zero scale register). Scalar only.
		if n != 1 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		a := c.readVS(vs, 1)
		b := math.Float32bits(float32(a[0]))
		if e := (b >> 23) & 0xFF; e != 0 && !isNaNBits(b) {
			b = (b & 0x7FFFFF) | 0x3F800000
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, 1, [4]float64{float64(math.Float32frombits(b))})
		return 1
	case 0x37: // vlgb.s: the source's unbiased exponent as a
		// float (logB); zero and denormal inputs give -Inf,
		// Inf gives +Inf, NaN gives NaN (documented). Scalar
		// only.
		if n != 1 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		a := c.readVS(vs, 1)
		b := math.Float32bits(float32(a[0]))
		var out float64
		switch e := (b >> 23) & 0xFF; {
		case isNaNBits(b):
			out = math.NaN()
		case e == 0xFF:
			out = math.Inf(1)
		case e == 0:
			out = math.Inf(-1)
		default:
			out = float64(int(e) - 127)
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, 1, [4]float64{out})
		return 1
	case 0x38, 0x39, 0x3A, 0x3B, 0x3D, 0x3E:
		// The integer pack and unpack family. Semantics are
		// the hardware's own (the davidgfnet VFPU document's
		// bit formulas, cross checked against the corpus
		// convert rows): the unsigned unpack shifts one bit
		// less and drops the sign, and the unsigned packs
		// clamp negative results to zero after an arithmetic
		// shift one bit shorter than the signed form.
		in := c.readRawPrefixed(vs, n)
		var out []uint32
		switch f {
		case 0x38: // vuc2ifs.s: byte replicated into a float pattern
			out = make([]uint32, 4)
			for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
				b := (in[0] >> uint(8*j)) & 0xFF
				out[j] = b<<23 | b<<15 | b<<7 | b>>1
			}
		case 0x39: // vc2i.s: byte into the top of the word
			out = make([]uint32, 4)
			for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
				out[j] = ((in[0] >> uint(8*j)) & 0xFF) << 24
			}
		case 0x3A: // vus2i: half at bits [30:15], sign dropped
			out = make([]uint32, 2*len(in))
			for i, w := range in {
				out[2*i] = (w << 15) & 0x7FFFFFFF
				out[2*i+1] = (w >> 16 << 15) & 0x7FFFFFFF
			}
		case 0x3B: // vs2i: half into the top of the word
			out = make([]uint32, 2*len(in))
			for i, w := range in {
				out[2*i] = w << 16
				out[2*i+1] = w & 0xFFFF0000
			}
		case 0x3D: // vi2c: pack ints to bytes (top bytes)
			out = make([]uint32, n/4)
			for i := range out {
				for j := 0; j < 4; j++ {
					out[i] |= ((in[4*i+j] >> 24) & 0xFF) << uint(8*j)
				}
			}
		case 0x3E: // vi2us: pack ints to unsigned shorts
			out = make([]uint32, n/2)
			for i := range out {
				out[i] = packHalfU(in[2*i]) | packHalfU(in[2*i+1])<<16
			}
		}
		c.applyDestSaturation(out)
		if f == 0x3D || f == 0x3E {
			// The packs land in the quad's lanes (see
			// writeRawQuadLanes).
			c.writeRawQuadLanes(vd, out)
		} else {
			c.writeRawMasked(vd, len(out), out)
		}
		return 1
	case 0x40, 0x41, 0x48, 0x49: // vsrt1, vsrt2, vsrt3, vsrt4
		// (quad only): sorting passes over the source quad.
		// The min/max picks are the unit's totalOrder ones
		// (the vfpuMinMaxBits rule); the source prefix does
		// not apply. F values from the published bit
		// diagrams: vsrt1 0x40, vsrt2 0x41, vsrt3 0x48,
		// vsrt4 0x49.
		if n != 4 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		idx := vecIndices(vs, 4)
		var s [4]uint32
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			s[i] = c.vregs[idx[i]]
		}
		mn := func(a, b uint32) uint32 { return vfpuMinMaxBits(a, b, false) }
		mx := func(a, b uint32) uint32 { return vfpuMinMaxBits(a, b, true) }
		// When the two (denormal flushed) values compare
		// equal as floats, the pair collapses: the min
		// sorts put the first operand in both slots, the
		// max sorts the second (the corpus specials zero
		// and denormal rows pin this; distinct values and
		// NaNs order by the totalOrder rule).
		sortPair := func(a, b uint32, maxSort bool) (uint32, uint32) {
			if fpInput(a) == fpInput(b) {
				if maxSort {
					return b, b
				}
				return a, a
			}
			if maxSort {
				return mx(a, b), mn(a, b)
			}
			return mn(a, b), mx(a, b)
		}
		var out [4]uint32
		switch f {
		case 0x40: // vsrt1: pairs (0,1) and (2,3), min first
			out[0], out[1] = sortPair(s[0], s[1], false)
			out[2], out[3] = sortPair(s[2], s[3], false)
		case 0x41: // vsrt2: pairs (0,3) and (1,2), min first
			lo03, hi03 := sortPair(s[0], s[3], false)
			lo12, hi12 := sortPair(s[1], s[2], false)
			out = [4]uint32{lo03, lo12, hi12, hi03}
		case 0x48: // vsrt3: pairs (0,1) and (2,3), max first
			out[0], out[1] = sortPair(s[0], s[1], true)
			out[2], out[3] = sortPair(s[2], s[3], true)
		case 0x49: // vsrt4: pairs (0,3) and (1,2), max first
			hi03, lo03 := sortPair(s[0], s[3], true)
			hi12, lo12 := sortPair(s[1], s[2], true)
			out = [4]uint32{hi03, hi12, lo12, lo03}
		}
		c.writeRawMasked(vd, 4, out[:])
		return 1
	case 0x42, 0x43: // vbfy1 (pair/quad), vbfy2 (quad):
		// butterfly sums and differences; no source prefix.
		{
			idx := vecIndices(vs, n)
			var a [4]float64
			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
				a[i] = fpInput(c.vregs[idx[i]])
			}
			var out [4]float64
			switch {
			case f == 0x42 && n == 2:
				out[0], out[1] = a[0]+a[1], a[0]-a[1]
			case f == 0x42 && n == 4:
				out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3] = a[0]+a[1], a[0]-a[1], a[2]+a[3], a[2]-a[3]
			case f == 0x43 && n == 4:
				out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3] = a[0]+a[2], a[1]+a[3], a[0]-a[2], a[1]-a[3]
			default:
				return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
			}
			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
				if math.IsNaN(out[i]) {
					// A butterfly NaN is always the
					// positive pattern on hardware
					// (the corpus specials rows, for
					// both Inf sums and NaN inputs).
					out[i] = math.NaN()
				}
			}
			c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
			return 1
		}
	case 0x44: // vocp: element wise 1 - x; no source prefix.
		{
			idx := vecIndices(vs, n)
			var out [4]float64
			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
				out[i] = 1 - fpInput(c.vregs[idx[i]])
				if math.IsNaN(out[i]) {
					// Like the butterflies, a vocp NaN
					// is the positive pattern (the
					// corpus specials rows).
					out[i] = math.NaN()
				}
			}
			c.writeVD(vd, n, out)
			return 1
		}
	case 0x45: // vsocp.p: one's complement pair splat with saturation
		if n != 2 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		sIdx := vecIndices(vs, n)
		clamp01 := func(v float64) uint32 {
			if math.IsNaN(v) {
				// A NaN through the saturating complement
				// is the positive NaN pattern (the corpus
				// specials rows).
				return 0x7F800001
			}
			if v == 0 {
				v = 0 // a negative zero clamps to +0
			} else if v < 0 {
				v = 0
			} else if v > 1 {
				v = 1
			}
			return math.Float32bits(float32(v))
		}
		a := fpInput(c.vregs[sIdx[0]])
		b := fpInput(c.vregs[sIdx[1]])
		c.writeRawMasked(vd, 4, []uint32{clamp01(1 - a), clamp01(a), clamp01(1 - b), clamp01(b)})
		return 1
	case 0x46, 0x47: // vfad, vavg: reductions to a single
		a := c.readVS(vs, n)
		sum := 0.0
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			sum += a[i]
		}
		if f == 0x47 {
			sum /= float64(n)
		}
		if math.IsNaN(sum) {
			// A reduction NaN is the positive pattern
			// (Inf cancellation included; the corpus
			// specials rows).
			sum = math.NaN()
		}
		c.writeVD(vd, 1, [4]float64{sum})
		// Only lane 0 is written. (The vavg corpus test
		// prints NaN in the other lanes, but those are the
		// recording machine's uninitialized register state:
		// its main never resets the register file. The
		// specials test, whose wrapper pre-zeroes the
		// destination quad, shows the lanes untouched.)
		return 1
	case 0x59, 0x5A, 0x5B: // vt4444, vt5551, vt5650 color conversions
		if n != 4 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		sIdx := vecIndices(vs, n)
		in := [4]uint32{c.vregs[sIdx[0]], c.vregs[sIdx[1]], c.vregs[sIdx[2]], c.vregs[sIdx[3]]}
		var conv func(a, b uint32) uint32
		switch f {
		case 0x59: // vt4444
			conv = func(a, b uint32) uint32 {
				return (a >> 4 & 0xF) | (a >> 8 & 0xF0) | (a >> 12 & 0xF00) | (a >> 16 & 0xF000) |
					(b << 12 & 0xF0000) | (b << 8 & 0xF00000) | (b << 4 & 0xF000000) | (b & 0xF0000000)
			}
		case 0x5A: // vt5551
			conv = func(a, b uint32) uint32 {
				return (a >> 3 & 0x1F) | (a >> 6 & 0x3E0) | (a >> 9 & 0x7C00) | (a >> 16 & 0x8000) |
					(b << 13 & 0x1F0000) | (b << 10 & 0x3E00000) | (b << 7 & 0x7C000000) | (b & 0x80000000)
			}
		case 0x5B: // vt5650
			conv = func(a, b uint32) uint32 {
				return (a >> 3 & 0x1F) | (a >> 5 & 0x7E0) | (a >> 8 & 0xF800) |
					(b << 13 & 0x1F0000) | (b << 11 & 0x7E00000) | (b << 8 & 0xF8000000)
			}
		}
		c.writeRawMasked(vd, 2, []uint32{conv(in[0], in[1]), conv(in[2], in[3])})
		return 1
	case 0x3C: // vi2uc, quad only: pack the top byte of each
		// int, clamping negatives to zero, into one single
		if n != 4 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		in := c.readRawPrefixed(vs, 4)
		var word uint32
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			raw := in[i]
			var b uint32
			if int32(raw) >= 0 {
				b = (raw >> 23) & 0xFF
			}
			word |= b << uint(8*i)
		}
		packed := []uint32{word}
		c.applyDestSaturation(packed)
		c.writeRawQuadLanes(vd, packed)
		return 1
	case 0x3F: // vi2s, pair or quad: pack the top halfword of
		// each int
		if n != 2 && n != 4 {
			return c.vfpuUnimplemented()
		}
		in := c.readRawPrefixed(vs, n)
		var bits [4]uint32
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			h := (in[i] >> 16) & 0xFFFF
			bits[i/2] |= h << uint(16*(i%2))
		}
		packed := bits[:n/2]
		c.applyDestSaturation(packed)
		c.writeRawQuadLanes(vd, packed)
		return 1
	}
	if f >= 0x60 { // vcst: constant index is the low 5 bits of F
		idx := f & 0x1F
		// The hardware VCST table (the davidgfnet VFPU
		// document's constant list), indexed from 1: index 1
		// is the huge value, 2 sqrt(2), and so on. Index 0
		// and indices past the documented list read as zero
		// here; the corpus vector test exercises the listed
