// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 3: textured sprite, unswizzled and swizzled
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestTexturedSprite(t *testing.T) {
	texel := func(x, y int) uint32 {
		switch {
		case x == 0 && y == 0:
			return rgbaWord(255, 0, 0, 255) // red
		case x == 1 && y == 0:
			return rgbaWord(0, 255, 0, 255) // green
		case x == 0 && y == 1:
			return rgbaWord(0, 0, 255, 255) // blue
		default:
			return rgbaWord(255, 255, 255, 255) // white
		}
	}
	for _, swizzled := range []bool{false, true} {
		m := newFakeMem()
		g := New(m)
		texBase := uint32(0x08004000)
		for y := 0; y < 2; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < 2; x++ {
				var off int
				if swizzled {
					// Independent computation of the documented swizzle
					// formula for a 2 texel wide 8888 texture:
					// rowBytes = 8, off = (y>>3)*rowBytes*8 +
					// ((x*4)>>4)*128 + (y&7)*16 + (x*4 & 15).
					rowBytes := 2 * 4
					off = (y>>3)*rowBytes*8 + ((x*4)>>4)*128 + (y&7)*16 + (x * 4 & 15)
				} else {
					off = (y*2 + x) * 4
				}
				m.Write32(texBase+uint32(off), texel(x, y))
			}
		}
		vbase := uint32(0x08003000)
		white := rgbaWord(255, 255, 255, 255)
		writeVertTex(m, vbase, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, white)
		writeVertTex(m, vbase+18, 2, 2, 0, 1, 1, white)
		texMode := uint32(0)
		if swizzled {
			texMode = 1
		}
		putList(m, listAddr, withFB(
			cmd(0x14, 0x080000),           // ORIGIN
			cmd(0xA0, 0x4000),             // TEXADDR0
			cmd(0xB8, 1|(1<<8)),           // TEXSIZE0: 2x2
			cmd(0xA8, 2),                  // TEXBUFWIDTH0
			cmd(0xC5, 3),                  // TEXFORMAT 8888
			cmd(0xC0, float24(1)),         // TEXSCALEU
			cmd(0xC1, float24(1)),         // TEXSCALEV
			cmd(0x53, 1),                  // TEXENABLE
			cmd(0xC4, texMode),            // TEXMODE swizzle flag
			cmd(0x12, vtypeThroughTexPos), // VTYPE
			cmd(0x01, 0x3000),             // VADDR
			cmd(0x04, (6<<16)|2),          // PRIM sprites, 2
			cmd(0x0C, 0),                  // END
		)...)
		if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
			t.Fatalf("swizzled=%v: state = %v, want Completed", swizzled, st)
		}
		assertPixel(t, g, 0, 0, 255, 0, 0, 255)
		assertPixel(t, g, 1, 0, 0, 255, 0, 255)
		assertPixel(t, g, 0, 1, 0, 0, 255, 255)
		assertPixel(t, g, 1, 1, 255, 255, 255, 255)
	}
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 4: depth test
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestDepth(t *testing.T) {
	// Geometry note: with the z buffer at byte offset 0x8000 and a
	// 512 wide 8888 framebuffer, a large clear region or triangle would
	// make color and depth writes overlap in VRAM. The gate therefore
	// uses a small corner region and triangle, where the prescribed
	// layout does not collide: color bytes for pixels in rows 0..15 end
	// below offset 0x8000, and depth bytes start at 0x8000.
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	// Clear color (black) and depth (0xFFFF) together.
	putList(m, listAddr, withFB(
		cmd(0x9E, 0x8000),      // ZBUFPTR
		cmd(0x9F, 512),         // ZBUFWIDTH
		cmd(0xD4, 3),           // ZTESTENABLE test+write
		cmd(0xD5, 4),           // ZFUNC Less
		cmd(0x15, 0),           // REGION1 (0,0)
		cmd(0x16, 15|(15<<10)), // REGION2 (15,15)
		cmd(0xC9, 0),           // CLEARCOLOR black
		cmd(0xCA, 0xFF),        // CLEARALPHA
		cmd(0xCB, 0xFFFF),      // CLEARDEPTH
		cmd(0xCC, 0x1|0x2|0x8), // CLEAR enable|color|depth
		cmd(0x04, (3<<16)|3),   // PRIM (runs the clear)
		cmd(0x0C, 0),           // END
	)...)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("clear state = %v", st)
	}
	draw := func(z uint16, color uint32) {
		base := uint32(0x08002000)
		writeVertColorPos(m, base, 0, 0, z, color)
		writeVertColorPos(m, base+10, 8, 0, z, color)
		writeVertColorPos(m, base+20, 0, 8, z, color)
		putList(m, listAddr, triList()...)
		if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
			t.Fatalf("draw state = %v", st)
		}
	}
	red := rgbaWord(255, 0, 0, 255)
	green := rgbaWord(0, 255, 0, 255)
	draw(40000, red)   // far first
	draw(10000, green) // near wins
	assertPixel(t, g, 2, 2, 0, 255, 0, 255)
	draw(40000, red) // far again: must be rejected
	assertPixel(t, g, 2, 2, 0, 255, 0, 255)
	// Stored depth at the center is the near value.
	depthAddr := uint32(0x04008000) + uint32((2*512+2)*2)
	if d := m.Read16(depthAddr); d != 10000 {
		t.Errorf("stored depth = %d, want 10000", d)
	}
}

func TestSprite(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	blue := rgbaWord(0, 0, 255, 255)
	base := uint32(0x08002000)
	writeVertColorPos(m, base, 0, 0, 0, blue)

	putList(m, listAddr, withFB(

	)...)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("state = %v", st)

		assertPixel(t, g, p[0], p[1], 0, 0, 255, 255)
	}
	for _, p := range [][2]int{{4, 0}, {0, 3}} {
		r, gr, b, a := g.FramebufferPixel(p[0], p[1])
		if r != 0 || gr != 0 || b != 0 || a != 0 {

		}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 6: SIGNAL stall and FINISH on Continue
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestSignalFinish(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	putList(m, listAddr,
		cmd(0x00, 0),            // NOP
		cmd(0x0E, 0x2A|(3<<16)), // SIGNAL value 0x2A, behavior 3
		cmd(0x0F, 0),            // FINISH (after the signal)
		cmd(0x0C, 0),            // END
	)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateStalled {
		t.Fatalf("state = %v, want Stalled", st)
	}
	value, behavior, finished := g.SignalInfo()
	if value&0xFFFF != 0x2A {
		t.Errorf("SignalValue = %#x, want low bits 0x2a", value)
	}
	if behavior != 3 {
		t.Errorf("SignalBehavior = %d, want 3", behavior)
	}
	if finished {
		t.Error("FinishedSeen = true before Continue, want false")
	}
	if st := g.Continue(); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("after Continue state = %v, want Completed", st)
	}
	if !g.FinishedSeen {
		t.Error("FinishedSeen = false after Continue, want true")
	}
	for op, want := range map[int]uint64{0x0E: 1, 0x0F: 1, 0x0C: 1} {
		if got := g.CmdCount(op); got != want {
			t.Errorf("CmdCount(%#02x) = %d, want %d", op, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 7: CLUT8 texture
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestCLUT(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	// 2x1 CLUT8 texture: indices [1, 0] at RAM offset 0x4000.
	texBase := uint32(0x08004000)
	m.Write8(texBase, 1)
	m.Write8(texBase+1, 0)
	// Palette at RAM offset 0x5000: entry 0 white, entry 1 magenta.
	clutBase := uint32(0x08005000)
	m.Write32(clutBase, rgbaWord(255, 255, 255, 255))
	m.Write32(clutBase+4, rgbaWord(255, 0, 255, 255))
	// Sprite vertices.
	vbase := uint32(0x08003000)
	white := rgbaWord(255, 255, 255, 255)
	writeVertTex(m, vbase, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, white)
	writeVertTex(m, vbase+18, 2, 1, 0, 1, 1, white)
	putList(m, listAddr, withFB(
		cmd(0x14, 0x080000),           // ORIGIN
		cmd(0xA0, 0x4000),             // TEXADDR0
		cmd(0xB8, 1),                  // TEXSIZE0: w=2, h=1
		cmd(0xA8, 2),                  // TEXBUFWIDTH0
		cmd(0xC5, 5),                  // TEXFORMAT CLUT8
		cmd(0xB0, 0x5000),             // CLUTADDR
		cmd(0xB1, 3|(31<<8)),          // CLUTFORMAT 8888, shift 0, mask 31, start 0
		cmd(0xB2, 1),                  // CLUTLOAD 1 block = 8 entries
		cmd(0xC0, float24(1)),         // TEXSCALEU
		cmd(0xC1, float24(1)),         // TEXSCALEV
		cmd(0x53, 1),                  // TEXENABLE
		cmd(0x12, vtypeThroughTexPos), // VTYPE
		cmd(0x01, 0x3000),             // VADDR
		cmd(0x04, (6<<16)|2),          // PRIM sprites, 2
		cmd(0x0C, 0),                  // END
	)...)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("state = %v", st)
	}
	// Index 1 is magenta, index 0 is white.
	assertPixel(t, g, 0, 0, 255, 0, 255, 255)
	assertPixel(t, g, 1, 0, 255, 255, 255, 255)
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 8: blending
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestBlend(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	putList(m, listAddr, clearList(0x0000FF)...) // opaque red destination
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("clear state = %v", st)
	}
	writeTestTri(m, 0, rgbaWord(0, 255, 0, 128)) // green, alpha 128
	putList(m, listAddr, withFB(
		cmd(0xCC, 0),               // CLEAR mode off
		cmd(0xD6, 1),               // BLENDENABLE
		cmd(0xD7, 0|(4<<4)|(5<<8)), // BLENDFUNC Add, SrcAlpha, OneMinusSrcAlpha
		cmd(0x14, 0x080000),
		cmd(0x12, vtypeThroughColorPos),
		cmd(0x01, 0x2000),
		cmd(0x04, (3<<16)|3),
		cmd(0x0C, 0),
	)...)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("draw state = %v", st)
	}
	r, gr, _, _ := g.FramebufferPixel(20, 20)
	// r = 255 * (1 - 128/255) = 127, g = 255 * 128/255 = 128.
	if r < 126 || r > 128 {
		t.Errorf("blended r = %d, want about 127", r)
	}
	if gr < 127 || gr > 129 {
		t.Errorf("blended g = %d, want about 128", gr)
	}
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 9: alpha test
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestAlphaTest(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	putList(m, listAddr, clearList(0x0000FF)...) // red destination
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("clear state = %v", st)
	}
	writeTestTri(m, 0, rgbaWord(0, 255, 0, 0)) // alpha 0: must be dropped
	putList(m, listAddr, withFB(
		cmd(0xCC, 0),
		cmd(0xDA, 1),                     // ALPHATESTENABLE
		cmd(0xDB, 2|(255<<8)|(0xFF<<16)), // ALPHAFUNC Equal, ref 255, mask 0xFF
		cmd(0x14, 0x080000),
		cmd(0x12, vtypeThroughColorPos),
		cmd(0x01, 0x2000),
		cmd(0x04, (3<<16)|3),
		cmd(0x0C, 0),
	)...)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("draw state = %v", st)
	}
	assertPixel(t, g, 20, 20, 255, 0, 0, 255) // still the clear color
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 10: JUMP, CALL, RET
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestJumpCallRet(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	putList(m, listAddr,
		cmd(0x10, listAddr>>8), // BASE: basePtr = listAddr
		cmd(0x08, 12),          // JUMP to word index 3, skipping the SIGNAL
		cmd(0x0E, 0x99),        // SIGNAL 0x99: must never execute
		cmd(0x0A, 0x100),       // CALL subroutine at listAddr+0x100
		cmd(0x0C, 0),           // END
	)
	putList(m, listAddr+0x100,
		cmd(0x0E, 0x77), // SIGNAL 0x77: stalls inside the subroutine
		cmd(0x0B, 0),    // RET
	)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateStalled {
		t.Fatalf("state = %v, want Stalled (subroutine SIGNAL)", st)
	}
	if g.SignalValue&0xFFFF != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("SignalValue = %#x, want 0x77", g.SignalValue)
	}
	if got := g.CmdCount(0x0E); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("CmdCount(SIGNAL) = %d, want 1 (the jumped-over SIGNAL never ran)", got)
	}
	if st := g.Continue(); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("after Continue state = %v, want Completed", st)
	}
	for op, want := range map[int]uint64{0x08: 1, 0x0A: 1, 0x0B: 1, 0x0C: 1} {
		if got := g.CmdCount(op); got != want {
			t.Errorf("CmdCount(%#02x) = %d, want %d", op, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Gate 11: viewport transform with float positions
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestViewportFloat(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	green := rgbaWord(0, 255, 0, 255)
	base := uint32(0x08002000)
	writeVertFloat(m, base, 10, 10, 0, green)
	writeVertFloat(m, base+16, 100, 10, 0, green)
	writeVertFloat(m, base+32, 10, 100, 0, green)
	putList(m, listAddr, withFB(
		cmd(0x14, 0x080000),      // ORIGIN
		cmd(0x4A, float24(1)),    // VPXSCALE = 1.0
		cmd(0x4B, float24(1)),    // VPYSCALE = 1.0
		cmd(0x4C, 0),             // VPXCENTER = 0
		cmd(0x4D, 0),             // VPYCENTER = 0
		cmd(0x12, vtypeFloatPos), // VTYPE float positions, not through
		cmd(0x01, 0x2000),        // VADDR
		cmd(0x04, (3<<16)|3),     // PRIM triangles, 3
		cmd(0x0C, 0),             // END
	)...)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("state = %v", st)
	}
	assertPixel(t, g, 20, 20, 0, 255, 0, 255)
	r, gr, b, _ := g.FramebufferPixel(90, 90)
	if r != 0 || gr != 0 || b != 0 {
		t.Errorf("pixel (90,90) = (%d,%d,%d), want black (outside triangle)", r, gr, b)
	}
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Extra gates: counted no-draw commands, serialization round trip
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func TestCountedNoDrawCommands(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	putList(m, listAddr,
		cmd(0x05, 0x1234), // BEZIER: counted, no draw
		cmd(0x06, 0x55),   // SPLINE: counted, no draw
		cmd(0x07, 0x66),   // BBOX: counted, no draw
		cmd(0x09, 0x77),   // BJUMP: counted, never jumps
		cmd(0x00, 0),      // NOP
		cmd(0x0C, 0),      // END
	)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("state = %v", st)
	}
	for _, op := range []int{0x05, 0x06, 0x07, 0x09} {
		if got := g.CmdCount(op); got != 1 {
			t.Errorf("CmdCount(%#02x) = %d, want 1", op, got)
		}
	}
	if got := g.TotalCommands(); got != 6 {
		t.Errorf("TotalCommands = %d, want 6", got)
	}
	if got := g.Reg(0x05); got != 0x1234 {
		t.Errorf("Reg(BEZIER) = %#x, want 0x1234 (every command stores its arg)", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	m := newFakeMem()
	g := New(m)
	putList(m, listAddr, clearList(0x0000FF)...)
	if st := g.Submit(listAddr); st != StateCompleted {
		t.Fatalf("state = %v", st)
	}
	data := g.Serialize()
	g2 := New(m)
	if err := g2.Deserialize(data); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if got := g2.Reg(0xC9); got != 0x0000FF {
		t.Errorf("restored Reg(CLEARCOLOR) = %#x, want 0xff", got)
	}
	if g2.State() != StateCompleted {
		t.Errorf("restored state = %v, want Completed", g2.State())
	}
	assertPixel(t, g2, 240, 136, 255, 0, 0, 255)
	if again := g2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(again, data) {
		t.Error("re-serialized state differs from the original bytes")
	}
	if err := g2.Deserialize(data[:len(data)-1]); err == nil {
		t.Error("Deserialize of truncated data: want error, got nil")
	}
	// ConvertDisplay returns 4 bytes per pixel of RGBA8.
	img := g.ConvertDisplay(2, 1)
	if len(img) != 8 || img[0] != 255 || img[3] != 255 {
		t.Errorf("ConvertDisplay(2,1) = %v, want red opaque first pixel", img)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/ge/raster.go ====================

package ge

import "math"

// This file holds the fixed function pixel path: pixel format
// conversion, vertex fetching and transformation, primitive assembly,
// rasterization, texturing, and the fragment pipeline.
//
// Loud documentation note: triangle attribute interpolation is plain
// linear interpolation in screen space at pixel centers. There is NO
// perspective correction in this slice, and NO backface culling
// (CULLMODE is stored only).

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Pixel formats
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// rgba8 is one decoded pixel, 8 bits per channel.
type rgba8 struct{ r, g, b, a uint8 }

// fcolor is a float color with channels in the 0..255 range, used for
// interpolation and blending before the final rounding at write time.
type fcolor struct{ r, g, b, a float64 }

func (c rgba8) f() fcolor {
	return fcolor{float64(c.r), float64(c.g), float64(c.b), float64(c.a)}
}

func (c fcolor) bytes() rgba8 {
	return rgba8{roundByte(c.r), roundByte(c.g), roundByte(c.b), roundByte(c.a)}
}

// roundByte rounds to nearest and clamps to [0,255].
func roundByte(v float64) uint8 {
	v = math.Floor(v + 0.5)
	if v < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if v > 255 {
		return 255
	}
	return uint8(v)
}

// bytesPerPixel for a pixel format code (0=5650, 1=5551, 2=4444, 3=8888).
func bytesPerPixel(format int) int {
	if format == 3 {
		return 4
	}
	return 2
}

// unpack16 decodes a 16 bit pixel in formats 0 (5650), 1 (5551), or
// 2 (4444). Bit layouts are documented in the package spec: red sits in
// the low bits.
func unpack16(v uint16, format int) rgba8 {
	switch format {
	case 0: // 5650
		r5 := uint32(v & 0x1F)
		g6 := uint32((v >> 5) & 0x3F)
		b5 := uint32((v >> 11) & 0x1F)
		return rgba8{
			uint8((r5 << 3) | (r5 >> 2)),
			uint8((g6 << 2) | (g6 >> 4)),
			uint8((b5 << 3) | (b5 >> 2)),
			255,
		}
	case 1: // 5551
		r5 := uint32(v & 0x1F)
		g5 := uint32((v >> 5) & 0x1F)
		b5 := uint32((v >> 10) & 0x1F)
		a := uint8(0)
		if v&0x8000 != 0 {
			a = 255
		}
		return rgba8{
			uint8((r5 << 3) | (r5 >> 2)),
			uint8((g5 << 3) | (g5 >> 2)),
			uint8((b5 << 3) | (b5 >> 2)),
			a,
		}
	default: // 4444, nibble n expands to n<<4 | n
		r := uint32(v & 0xF)
		gr := uint32((v >> 4) & 0xF)
		b := uint32((v >> 8) & 0xF)
		a := uint32((v >> 12) & 0xF)
		return rgba8{
			uint8(r<<4 | r), uint8(gr<<4 | gr),
			uint8(b<<4 | b), uint8(a<<4 | a),
		}
	}
}

// unpack8888 decodes a 32 bit pixel: R in bits 7:0, G 15:8, B 23:16,
// A 31:24.
func unpack8888(v uint32) rgba8 {
	return rgba8{uint8(v), uint8(v >> 8), uint8(v >> 16), uint8(v >> 24)}
}

// packPixel converts RGBA8 down to a pixel format by truncating high
// bits (5 bit fields take r>>3, 6 bit fields g>>2, 4444 takes v>>4, and
// 5551 alpha is a >= 128).
func packPixel(c rgba8, format int) uint32 {
	switch format {
	case 0: // 5650
		return uint32(c.r>>3) | uint32(c.g>>2)<<5 | uint32(c.b>>3)<<11
	case 1: // 5551
		v := uint32(c.r>>3) | uint32(c.g>>3)<<5 | uint32(c.b>>3)<<10
		if c.a >= 128 {
			v |= 1 << 15
		}
		return v
	case 2: // 4444
		return uint32(c.r>>4) | uint32(c.g>>4)<<4 | uint32(c.b>>4)<<8 | uint32(c.a>>4)<<12
	default: // 8888
		return uint32(c.r) | uint32(c.g)<<8 | uint32(c.b)<<16 | uint32(c.a)<<24
	}
}

// readPixelAt reads one pixel in the given format from a buffer whose
// rows are width pixels apart. Out of range reads return zero.
func (g *GE) readPixelAt(addr uint32, width, format, x, y int) rgba8 {
	if g.mem == nil || width <= 0 || x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= width {
		return rgba8{}
	}
	off := addr + uint32((y*width+x)*bytesPerPixel(format))
	if format == 3 {
		return unpack8888(g.mem.Read32(off))
	}
	return unpack16(g.mem.Read16(off), format)
}

// writePixelAt packs and stores one pixel.
func (g *GE) writePixelAt(addr uint32, width, format, x, y int, c rgba8) {
	if g.mem == nil || width <= 0 || x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= width {
		return
	}
	off := addr + uint32((y*width+x)*bytesPerPixel(format))
	if format == 3 {
		g.mem.Write32(off, packPixel(c, format))
	} else {
		g.mem.Write16(off, uint16(packPixel(c, format)))
	}
}

func (g *GE) readDrawPixel(x, y int) rgba8 {
	return g.readPixelAt(g.fbAddr, g.fbWidth(), g.pixelFormat(), x, y)
}

// readDepth reads the 16 bit depth value at a pixel.
func (g *GE) readDepth(x, y int) uint16 {
	if g.mem == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return g.mem.Read16(g.zAddr + uint32((y*g.zWidth()+x)*2))
}

// writeDepth stores a 16 bit depth value at a pixel.
func (g *GE) writeDepth(x, y int, v uint16) {
	if g.mem == nil {
		return
	}
	g.mem.Write16(g.zAddr+uint32((y*g.zWidth()+x)*2), v)
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Register derived draw state
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func (g *GE) fbWidth() int {
	w := int(g.regs[opFRAMEBUFWIDTH] & 0xFFFF)
	if w == 0 {
		return 512
	}
	return w
}

func (g *GE) zWidth() int {
	w := int(g.regs[0x9F] & 0xFFFF)
	if w == 0 {
		return g.fbWidth()
	}
	return w
}

func (g *GE) pixelFormat() int { return int(g.regs[0xE8] & 3) }

// scissorRect returns the effective scissor rectangle, inclusive on
// both ends. A SCISSOR2 of (0,0) counts as never set and falls back to
// the full framebuffer width and the 512 row limit.
func (g *GE) scissorRect() (x1, y1, x2, y2 int) {
	a := g.regs[0xD0]
	b := g.regs[0xD1]
	x1, y1 = int(a&1023), int((a>>10)&1023)
	x2, y2 = int(b&1023), int((b>>10)&1023)
	if x2 == 0 && y2 == 0 {
		x2 = g.fbWidth() - 1
		if x2 < 0 {
			x2 = 0
		}
		y2 = fbMaxHeight - 1
	}
	return
}

// regionRect returns the effective REGION rectangle, inclusive. A
// REGION2 of (0,0) counts as never set and falls back to the scissor
// rectangle, which itself falls back to (fbWidth-1, 511).
func (g *GE) regionRect() (x1, y1, x2, y2 int) {
	a := g.regs[0x15]
	b := g.regs[0x16]
	x1, y1 = int(a&1023), int((a>>10)&1023)
	x2, y2 = int(b&1023), int((b>>10)&1023)
	if x2 == 0 && y2 == 0 {
		_, _, x2, y2 = g.scissorRect()
	}
	return
}

// stencilAt returns the stencil plane, allocating it on first use at
// fbWidth*512 bytes as the spec fixes it.
func (g *GE) stencilAt() []byte {
	if g.stencil == nil {
		size := g.fbWidth() * fbMaxHeight
		if size <= 0 {
			size = fbMaxHeight * fbMaxHeight
		}
		g.stencil = make([]byte, size)
	}
	return g.stencil
}

func (g *GE) stencilIndex(x, y int) (int, bool) {
	if x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= g.fbWidth() || y >= fbMaxHeight {
		return 0, false
	}
	idx := y*g.fbWidth() + x
	if idx >= len(g.stencilAt()) {
		return 0, false
	}
	return idx, true
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Compare, stencil ops, blend, logic
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// comparePass applies the shared compare function set: 0 Never,
// 1 Always, 2 Equal, 3 NotEqual, 4 Less, 5 LessEqual, 6 Greater,
// 7 GreaterEqual. It answers whether "a compared to b" passes.
func comparePass(fn, a, b int) bool {
	switch fn & 7 {
	case 0:
		return false
	case 1:
		return true
	case 2:
		return a == b
	case 3:
		return a != b
	case 4:
		return a < b
	case 5:
		return a <= b
	case 6:
		return a > b
	case 7:
		return a >= b
	}
	return false
}

// applyStencilOp computes the new stencil value for op:
// 0 Keep, 1 Zero, 2 Replace (with ref), 3 Invert, 4 Increment
// saturating, 5 Decrement saturating, 6 Increment wrapping,
// 7 Decrement wrapping.
func applyStencilOp(op, stored, ref int) int {
	switch op & 15 {
	case 0:
		return stored
	case 1:
		return 0
	case 2:
		return ref & 0xFF
	case 3:
		return (^stored) & 0xFF
	case 4:
		if stored >= 255 {
			return 255
		}
		return stored + 1
	case 5:
		if stored <= 0 {
			return 0
		}
		return stored - 1
	case 6:
		return (stored + 1) & 0xFF
	case 7:
		return (stored - 1) & 0xFF
	}
	return stored
}

// doStencilOp applies op at a pixel when the stencil test is enabled.
func (g *GE) doStencilOp(which, x, y int) {
	reg := g.regs[0xDE]
	var op int
	switch which {
	case 0: // sfail
		op = int(reg & 15)
	case 1: // zfail
		op = int((reg >> 4) & 15)
	default: // zpass
		op = int((reg >> 8) & 15)
	}
	idx, ok := g.stencilIndex(x, y)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	ref := int((g.regs[0xDD] >> 8) & 0xFF)
	plane := g.stencilAt()
	plane[idx] = uint8(applyStencilOp(op, int(plane[idx]), ref))
}

// factorVector returns the per channel blend factor in [0,1] floats.
// For the alpha channel, color based factors use their alpha component.
// Factor 10 (Fixed) uses the fixed color handed in by the caller:
// FIXEDA when computing the source factor, FIXEDB for the destination.
func factorVector(f int, src, dst, fixed fcolor) (fr, fg, fb, fa float64) {
	sn := func(v float64) float64 { return v / 255 }
	switch f {
	case 0: // Zero
		return 0, 0, 0, 0
	case 1: // One
		return 1, 1, 1, 1
	case 2: // SrcColor
		return sn(src.r), sn(src.g), sn(src.b), sn(src.a)
	case 3: // OneMinusSrcColor
		return 1 - sn(src.r), 1 - sn(src.g), 1 - sn(src.b), 1 - sn(src.a)
	case 4: // SrcAlpha
		s := sn(src.a)
		return s, s, s, s
	case 5: // OneMinusSrcAlpha
		s := 1 - sn(src.a)
		return s, s, s, s
	case 6: // DstAlpha
		s := sn(dst.a)
		return s, s, s, s
	case 7: // OneMinusDstAlpha
		s := 1 - sn(dst.a)
		return s, s, s, s
	case 8: // DstColor
		return sn(dst.r), sn(dst.g), sn(dst.b), sn(dst.a)
	case 9: // OneMinusDstColor
		return 1 - sn(dst.r), 1 - sn(dst.g), 1 - sn(dst.b), 1 - sn(dst.a)
	case 10: // Fixed
		return sn(fixed.r), sn(fixed.g), sn(fixed.b), sn(fixed.a)
	}
	return 1, 1, 1, 1 // unknown factors act as One in this slice
}

// blend applies the blend equation to src over dst. Fixed colors are
// 24 bit RGB arguments with alpha forced to 255 (the argument is only
// 24 bits, so there is no alpha byte to read).
func (g *GE) blend(src, dst fcolor) fcolor {
	reg := g.regs[0xD7]
	op := int(reg & 15)
	sf := int((reg >> 4) & 15)
	df := int((reg >> 8) & 15)
	fixedA := rgba8{
		uint8(g.regs[0xD8]), uint8(g.regs[0xD8] >> 8), uint8(g.regs[0xD8] >> 16), 255,
	}.f()
	fixedB := rgba8{
		uint8(g.regs[0xD9]), uint8(g.regs[0xD9] >> 8), uint8(g.regs[0xD9] >> 16), 255,
	}.f()
	sfr, sfg, sfb, sfa := factorVector(sf, src, dst, fixedA)
	dfr, dfg, dfb, dfa := factorVector(df, src, dst, fixedB)
	ch := func(s, d, fs, fd float64) float64 {
		switch op {
		case 0: // Add
			return s*fs + d*fd
		case 1: // Subtract
			return s*fs - d*fd
		case 2: // ReverseSubtract
			return d*fd - s*fs
		case 3: // Min, factors ignored
			return math.Min(s, d)
		case 4: // Max, factors ignored
			return math.Max(s, d)
		case 5: // AbsDiff, factors ignored
			return math.Abs(s - d)
		}
		return s*fs + d*fd
	}
	return fcolor{
		ch(src.r, dst.r, sfr, dfr),
		ch(src.g, dst.g, sfg, dfg),
		ch(src.b, dst.b, sfb, dfb),
		ch(src.a, dst.a, sfa, dfa),
	}
}

// logicOp applies a logical op per RGB channel between the current
// fragment (src) and the framebuffer value (dst), in whole bytes. The
// alpha channel takes the source alpha, except for the NoOp and Invert
// family entries (ops 5 and 10), which keep the destination alpha.
func logicOp(op int, src, dst rgba8) rgba8 {
	ch := func(s, d uint8) uint8 {
		switch op & 15 {
		case 0: // Clear
			return 0
		case 1: // And
			return s & d
		case 2: // AndReverse
			return s &^ d
		case 3: // Copy
			return s
		case 4: // AndInverted
			return (^s) & d
		case 5: // NoOp
			return d
		case 6: // Xor
			return s ^ d
		case 7: // Or
			return s | d
		case 8: // Nor
			return ^(s | d)
		case 9: // Equiv
			return ^(s ^ d)
		case 10: // Invert
			return ^d
		case 11: // OrReverse
			return s | (^d)
		case 12: // CopyInverted
			return ^s
		case 13: // OrInverted
			return (^s) | d
		case 14: // Nand
			return ^(s & d)
		case 15: // Set
			return 0xFF
		}
		return s
	}
	out := rgba8{ch(src.r, dst.r), ch(src.g, dst.g), ch(src.b, dst.b), src.a}
	if op&15 == 5 || op&15 == 10 {
		out.a = dst.a
	}
	return out
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Vertex fetching and transformation
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// vertex is one decoded and transformed vertex.
type vertex struct {
	sx, sy, sz float64 // screen position and depth (z already clamped)
	u, v       float64 // texture coordinates, pre texture transform
	col        fcolor  // RGBA in 0..255 floats
}

func compSize(code int) int {
	switch code {
	case 1:
		return 1
	case 2:
		return 2
	case 3:
		return 4
	}
	return 0
}

// vtype decodes the VTYPE register (0x12).
type vtype struct {
	tcCode, colorCode, normalCode, posCode int
	weightCode, weightCount                int
	indexCode                              int
	through                                bool
}

func (g *GE) vertexType() vtype {
	a := g.regs[opVTYPE]
	vt := vtype{
		tcCode:     int(a & 3),
		colorCode:  int((a >> 2) & 7),
		normalCode: int((a >> 5) & 3),
		posCode:    int((a >> 7) & 3),
		weightCode: int((a >> 9) & 3),
		indexCode:  int((a >> 21) & 3),
		through:    (a>>23)&1 != 0,
	}
	if vt.weightCode != 0 {
		vt.weightCount = int((a>>14)&15) + 1
	}
	return vt
}

// stride is the exact byte size of one vertex: weights, texcoord,
// color, normal, position, in memory order, with no alignment padding.
// That no-padding choice is a documented simplification of this slice.
// Color codes 5..7 are treated as 8888 sized.
func (vt vtype) stride() int {
	n := vt.weightCount * compSize(vt.weightCode)
	n += 2 * compSize(vt.tcCode)
	switch {
	case vt.colorCode == 0:
	case vt.colorCode <= 3:
		n += 2
	default:
		n += 4
	}
	n += 3 * compSize(vt.normalCode)
	pos := vt.posCode
	if pos == 0 {
		pos = 2 // position code 0 is treated as s16
	}
	n += 3 * compSize(pos)
	return n
}

// readTCScalar reads one texcoord component in the given size code.
func (g *GE) readTCScalar(addr uint32, code int) float64 {
	switch code {
	case 1:
		return float64(g.mem.Read8(addr)) / 255
	case 2:
		return float64(g.mem.Read16(addr)) / 65535
	case 3:
		return float64(math.Float32frombits(g.mem.Read32(addr)))
	}
	return 0
}

// fetchVertex decodes the vertex stored at addr per the current VTYPE
// and transforms it to screen space.
func (g *GE) fetchVertex(addr uint32, vt vtype) vertex {
	off := uint32(0)
	// Weights: read for layout only, skinning is not in this slice.
	off += uint32(vt.weightCount * compSize(vt.weightCode))

	var out vertex
	out.col = fcolor{255, 255, 255, 255} // no color field means white
	if vt.tcCode != 0 {
		out.u = g.readTCScalar(addr+off, vt.tcCode)
		out.v = g.readTCScalar(addr+off+uint32(compSize(vt.tcCode)), vt.tcCode)
		off += uint32(2 * compSize(vt.tcCode))
	}
	if vt.colorCode != 0 {
		switch {
		case vt.colorCode <= 3:
			out.col = unpack16(g.mem.Read16(addr+off), vt.colorCode-1).f()
			off += 2
		default: // 8888 (codes 4..7)
			out.col = unpack8888(g.mem.Read32(addr + off)).f()
			off += 4
		}
	}
	// Normal: read for layout only.
	off += uint32(3 * compSize(vt.normalCode))

	posCode := vt.posCode
	if posCode == 0 {
		posCode = 2
	}
	ps := uint32(compSize(posCode))
	var raw [3]float64 // signed or float value per component
	var rawU [3]uint32 // raw unsigned bits per component
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		a := addr + off + uint32(i)*ps
		switch posCode {
		case 1:
			v := g.mem.Read8(a)
			rawU[i] = uint32(v)
			raw[i] = float64(int8(v))
		case 3:
			raw[i] = float64(math.Float32frombits(g.mem.Read32(a)))
		default: // s16
			v := g.mem.Read16(a)
			rawU[i] = uint32(v)
			raw[i] = float64(int16(v))
		}
	}

	if vt.through {
		switch posCode {
		case 3: // float: x and y are pixels, z clamps to depth range
			out.sx, out.sy = raw[0], raw[1]
			out.sz = clampF(raw[2], 0, 65535)
		case 1: // s8: values are pixels, z is the unsigned byte
			out.sx, out.sy = raw[0], raw[1]
			out.sz = float64(rawU[2])
		default: // s16: x and y are 12.4 fixed point, z is raw uint16
			out.sx = float64(int32(int16(uint16(rawU[0]))) >> 4)
			out.sy = float64(int32(int16(uint16(rawU[1]))) >> 4)
			out.sz = float64(rawU[2])
		}
		return out
	}

	// Model to screen through the viewport registers. Positions feed
	// the transform as their decoded numeric values.
	out.sx = raw[0]*g.floatReg(0x4A) + g.floatReg(0x4C) + g.floatReg(0x50)
	out.sy = raw[1]*g.floatReg(0x4B) + g.floatReg(0x4D) + g.floatReg(0x51)
	sz := raw[2]*g.floatReg(0x4E) + g.floatReg(0x4F)
	near := float64(g.regs[0xD2] & 0xFFFF)
	far := float64(g.regs[0xD3] & 0xFFFF)
	if (near != 0 || far != 0) && far >= near {
		out.sz = clampF(sz, near, far)
	} else {
		out.sz = clampF(sz, 0, 65535)
	}
	return out
}

func clampF(v, lo, hi float64) float64 {
	if v < lo {
		return lo
	}
	if v > hi {
		return hi
	}
	return v
}

// fetchVertices reads count vertices for a PRIM, honoring the index
// stream when VTYPE declares one.
func (g *GE) fetchVertices(count int, vt vtype) []vertex {
	stride := vt.stride()
	out := make([]vertex, 0, count)
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		addr := g.vertexPtr + uint32(i*stride)
		if vt.indexCode != 0 {
			isize := compSize(vt.indexCode)
			ia := g.indexPtr + uint32(i*isize)
			var idx uint32
			switch vt.indexCode {
			case 1:
				idx = uint32(g.mem.Read8(ia))
			case 2:
				idx = uint32(g.mem.Read16(ia))
			case 3:
				idx = g.mem.Read32(ia)
			}
			addr = g.vertexPtr + idx*uint32(stride)
		}
		out = append(out, g.fetchVertex(addr, vt))
	}
	return out
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Texture sampling
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

func (g *GE) texSize() (w, h int) {
	a := g.regs[0xB8]
	return 1 << (a & 31), 1 << ((a >> 8) & 31)
}

func (g *GE) texBufWidth() int {
	w := int(g.regs[0xA8] & 0xFFFF)
	if w == 0 {
		tw, _ := g.texSize()
		return tw
	}
	return w
}

// texScale reads a TEXSCALE register; never written means 1.0.
func (g *GE) texScale(op int) float64 {
	if g.regs[op] == 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return g.floatReg(op)
}

// texelIndex resolves a texel space index for one axis under the
// axis wrap mode: only mode 1 clamps, everything else repeats.
func texelIndex(i, size, mode int) int {
	if size <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if mode == 1 {
		if i < 0 {
			return 0
		}
		if i > size-1 {
			return size - 1
		}
		return i
	}
	i %= size
	if i < 0 {
		i += size
	}
	return i
}

// fetchTexel reads the texel at integer coordinates (already resolved
// through texelIndex) in the current texture format.
func (g *GE) fetchTexel(x, y int) rgba8 {
	format := int(g.regs[0xC5] & 7)
	bw := g.texBufWidth()
	swizzled := g.regs[0xC4]&1 != 0

	if format == 4 { // CLUT4: two indices per byte
		var raw uint8
		if swizzled {
			byteX := x >> 1
			off := (y>>3)*(bw/2)*8 + (byteX>>4)*128 + (y&7)*16 + (byteX & 15)
			raw = g.mem.Read8(g.texAddr + uint32(off))
		} else {
			raw = g.mem.Read8(g.texAddr + uint32((y*bw+x)/2))
		}
		var v uint32
		if x&1 != 0 {
			v = uint32(raw >> 4)
		} else {
			v = uint32(raw & 0xF)
		}
		return g.clutLookup(v)
	}

	bpp := 1
	switch format {
	case 0, 1, 2, 6: // 5650, 5551, 4444, CLUT16
		bpp = 2
	case 3, 7: // 8888, CLUT32
		bpp = 4
	}
	var off int
	if swizzled {
		rowBytes := bw * bpp
		off = (y>>3)*rowBytes*8 + ((x*bpp)>>4)*128 + (y&7)*16 + ((x * bpp) & 15)
	} else {
		off = (y*bw + x) * bpp
	}
	addr := g.texAddr + uint32(off)
	switch format {
	case 0, 1, 2:
		return unpack16(g.mem.Read16(addr), format)
	case 3:
		return unpack8888(g.mem.Read32(addr))
	case 5: // CLUT8
		return g.clutLookup(uint32(g.mem.Read8(addr)))
	case 6: // CLUT16
		return g.clutLookup(uint32(g.mem.Read16(addr)))
	case 7: // CLUT32
		return g.clutLookup(g.mem.Read32(addr))
	}
	return rgba8{}
}

// clutLookup maps a raw texture index through the CLUT shift, mask,
// and start fields. Out of range indices are transparent black.
func (g *GE) clutLookup(v uint32) rgba8 {
	_, shift, mask, start := g.clutParams()
	idx := start + int((v>>uint(shift))&uint32(mask))
	if idx < 0 || idx >= 512 {
		return rgba8{}
	}
	return unpack8888(g.clut[idx])
}

// sampleTexture samples the current texture at (u, v) with the
// TEXSCALE/TEXOFFSET transform, wrap modes, and filter selection.
func (g *GE) sampleTexture(u, v float64) rgba8 {
	tw, th := g.texSize()
	wrap := g.regs[0xC7]
	uMode, vMode := int(wrap&7), int((wrap>>8)&7)

	// Filter: linear when either the MIN or MAG selection is 1 or 5
	// (linear or linear-mipmap style codes). No mipmaps in this slice.
	freg := g.regs[0xC6]
	minF, magF := int(freg&7), int((freg>>8)&7)
	linear := minF == 1 || minF == 5 || magF == 1 || magF == 5

	sampleAxis := func(t, scale, offset float64, size, mode int) (int, int, float64) {
		n := t*scale + offset
		if mode == 1 {
			n = clampF(n, 0, 1)
		} else {
			n = n - math.Floor(n)
		}
		s := n * float64(size)
		if !linear {
			return texelIndex(int(math.Floor(s)), size, mode), 0, 0
		}
		s2 := s - 0.5
		i0 := int(math.Floor(s2))
		frac := s2 - float64(i0)
		return texelIndex(i0, size, mode), texelIndex(i0+1, size, mode), frac
	}

	x0, x1, fx := sampleAxis(u, g.texScale(0xC0), g.floatReg(0xC2), tw, uMode)
	y0, y1, fy := sampleAxis(v, g.texScale(0xC1), g.floatReg(0xC3), th, vMode)
	if !linear {
		return g.fetchTexel(x0, y0)
	}
	c00 := g.fetchTexel(x0, y0).f()
	c10 := g.fetchTexel(x1, y0).f()
	c01 := g.fetchTexel(x0, y1).f()
	c11 := g.fetchTexel(x1, y1).f()
	mix := func(a, b, t float64) float64 { return a + (b-a)*t }
	return fcolor{
		mix(mix(c00.r, c10.r, fx), mix(c01.r, c11.r, fx), fy),
		mix(mix(c00.g, c10.g, fx), mix(c01.g, c11.g, fx), fy),
		mix(mix(c00.b, c10.b, fx), mix(c01.b, c11.b, fx), fy),
		mix(mix(c00.a, c10.a, fx), mix(c01.a, c11.a, fx), fy),
	}.bytes()
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Fragment pipeline
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// plot runs one fragment through the whole pipeline and writes it if
// it survives. Steps, in order: scissor and bounds clip, alpha test,
// color test, stencil test, depth test, stencil zpass op, texture
// combine, blend, logical op, masked write.
func (g *GE) plot(x, y int, z float64, col fcolor, u, v float64) {
	// 1. Clip to scissor and framebuffer bounds.
	sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2 := g.scissorRect()
	if x < sx1 || x > sx2 || y < sy1 || y > sy2 {
		return
	}
	if x < 0 || y < 0 || x >= g.fbWidth() || y >= fbMaxHeight {
		return
	}

	src := col.bytes()

	// 2. Alpha test: (srcA & mask) vs (ref & mask).
	if g.regs[0xDA]&1 != 0 {
		reg := g.regs[0xDB]
		fn := int(reg & 7)
		ref := int((reg >> 8) & 0xFF)
		mask := int((reg >> 16) & 0xFF)
		if !comparePass(fn, int(src.a)&mask, ref&mask) {
			return
		}
	}

	// 3. Color test: 24 bit (srcRGB & mask) vs (ref & mask).
	if g.regs[0xDF]&1 != 0 {
		fn := int(g.regs[0xE0] & 7)
		ref := int(g.regs[0xE1] & 0xFFFFFF)
		mask := int(g.regs[0xE2] & 0xFFFFFF)
		srcRGB := int(src.r) | int(src.g)<<8 | int(src.b)<<16
		if !comparePass(fn, srcRGB&mask, ref&mask) {
			return
		}
	}

	stencilOn := g.regs[0xDC]&1 != 0

	// 4. Stencil test: (ref & mask) vs (stored & mask). A failure
	// applies the sfail op and drops the fragment.
	if stencilOn {
		reg := g.regs[0xDD]
		fn := int(reg & 7)
		ref := int((reg >> 8) & 0xFF)
		mask := int((reg >> 16) & 0xFF)
		stored := 0
		if idx, ok := g.stencilIndex(x, y); ok {
			stored = int(g.stencilAt()[idx])
		}
		if !comparePass(fn, ref&mask, stored&mask) {
			g.doStencilOp(0, x, y)
			return
		}
	}

	// 5. Depth test. When ZTESTENABLE bit0 is clear, no depth reads or
	// writes happen at all. A pass writes depth only when bit1 is set
	// and DEPTHMASK bit0 is clear.
	if g.regs[0xD4]&1 != 0 {
		fn := int(g.regs[0xD5] & 7)
		zi := int(math.Floor(z + 0.5))
		if zi < 0 {
			zi = 0
		}
		if zi > 65535 {
			zi = 65535
		}
		stored := int(g.readDepth(x, y))
		if !comparePass(fn, zi, stored) {
			if stencilOn {
				g.doStencilOp(1, x, y)
			}
			return
		}
		if g.regs[0xD4]&2 != 0 && g.regs[0xE7]&1 == 0 {
			g.writeDepth(x, y, uint16(zi))
		}
	}

	// 6. Stencil zpass op, now that every test passed.
	if stencilOn {
		g.doStencilOp(2, x, y)
	}

	// 7. Texture combine.
	out := col
	if g.regs[0x53]&1 != 0 {
		texel := g.sampleTexture(u, v).f()
		switch int(g.regs[0xC8] & 7) {
		case 1: // decal: texel RGB, source alpha
			out = fcolor{texel.r, texel.g, texel.b, col.a}
		case 3: // replace
			out = texel
		case 4: // add
			out = fcolor{
				clampF(col.r+texel.r, 0, 255),
				clampF(col.g+texel.g, 0, 255),
				clampF(col.b+texel.b, 0, 255),
				clampF(col.a+texel.a, 0, 255),
			}
		default: // 0 modulate, 2 blend (acts as modulate in this slice),
			// and anything else
			out = fcolor{
				col.r * texel.r / 255,
				col.g * texel.g / 255,
				col.b * texel.b / 255,
				col.a * texel.a / 255,
			}
		}
	}

	old := g.readDrawPixel(x, y)

	// 8. Blend.
	if g.regs[0xD6]&1 != 0 {
		out = g.blend(out, old.f())
	}

	// 9. Logical op, between the current fragment color and the
	// framebuffer value, in whole bytes.
	final := out.bytes()
	if g.regs[0xE3]&1 != 0 {
		final = logicOp(int(g.regs[0xE4]&15), final, old)
	}

	// 10. Masked write. Never written masks read as fully open.
	rgbMask := g.regs[0xE5]
	if rgbMask == 0 {
		rgbMask = 0xFFFFFF
	}
	aMask := g.regs[0xE6] & 0xFF
	if aMask == 0 {
		aMask = 0xFF
	}
	final = rgba8{
		(final.r & uint8(rgbMask)) | (old.r &^ uint8(rgbMask)),
		(final.g & uint8(rgbMask>>8)) | (old.g &^ uint8(rgbMask>>8)),
		(final.b & uint8(rgbMask>>16)) | (old.b &^ uint8(rgbMask>>16)),
		(final.a & uint8(aMask)) | (old.a &^ uint8(aMask)),
	}
	g.writePixelAt(g.fbAddr, g.fbWidth(), g.pixelFormat(), x, y, final)
}

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PRIM
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

// prim implements PRIM (0x04), including the CLEAR mode path.
func (g *GE) prim(arg uint32) {
	// Clear mode: while CLEAR bit0 is set, PRIM ignores its vertices
	// and fills the region intersect scissor rectangle instead.
	if g.regs[0xCC]&1 != 0 {
		g.clearFill()
		return
	}
	primType := int((arg >> 16) & 7)
	count := int(arg & 0xFFFF)
	if count == 0 {
		return
	}
	vt := g.vertexType()
	verts := g.fetchVertices(count, vt)

	switch primType {
	case 0: // points
		for _, v := range verts {
			g.plot(roundCoord(v.sx), roundCoord(v.sy), v.sz, v.col, v.u, v.v)
		}
	case 1: // lines, in pairs
		for i := 0; i+1 < len(verts); i += 2 {
			g.line(verts[i], verts[i+1])
		}
	case 2: // line strip
		for i := 0; i+1 < len(verts); i++ {
			g.line(verts[i], verts[i+1])
		}
	case 3: // triangles, in triples
		for i := 0; i+2 < len(verts); i += 3 {
			g.triangle(verts[i], verts[i+1], verts[i+2])
		}
	case 4: // triangle strip
		for i := 0; i+2 < len(verts); i++ {
			g.triangle(verts[i], verts[i+1], verts[i+2])
		}
	case 5: // triangle fan around verts[0]
		for i := 1; i+1 < len(verts); i++ {
			g.triangle(verts[0], verts[i], verts[i+1])
		}
	case 6: // sprites, in pairs
		for i := 0; i+1 < len(verts); i += 2 {
			g.sprite(verts[i], verts[i+1])
		}
	default:
		// Primitive type 7 is not defined in this slice: counted, not drawn.
	}
}

// clearFill fills region intersect scissor with the clear values. Color
// goes through the masked write path but bypasses blend, logic, and
// all tests; depth and stencil are written directly.
func (g *GE) clearFill() {
	mode := g.regs[0xCC]
	rx1, ry1, rx2, ry2 := g.regionRect()
	sx1, sy1, sx2, sy2 := g.scissorRect()
	x1, y1 := max(rx1, sx1), max(ry1, sy1)
	x2, y2 := min(rx2, sx2), min(ry2, sy2)
	if x1 < 0 {
		x1 = 0
	}
	if y1 < 0 {
		y1 = 0
	}
	if x2 >= g.fbWidth() {
		x2 = g.fbWidth() - 1
	}
	if y2 >= fbMaxHeight {
		y2 = fbMaxHeight - 1
	}
	cc := g.regs[0xC9]
	clearCol := rgba8{uint8(cc), uint8(cc >> 8), uint8(cc >> 16), uint8(g.regs[0xCA])}
	stencilVal := uint8(g.regs[0xCA] >> 8)
	depthVal := uint16(g.regs[0xCB] & 0xFFFF)
	rgbMask := g.regs[0xE5]
	if rgbMask == 0 {
		rgbMask = 0xFFFFFF
	}
	aMask := g.regs[0xE6] & 0xFF
	if aMask == 0 {
		aMask = 0xFF
	}
	for y := y1; y <= y2; y++ {
		for x := x1; x <= x2; x++ {
			if mode&2 != 0 { // target color
				old := g.readDrawPixel(x, y)
				c := rgba8{
					(clearCol.r & uint8(rgbMask)) | (old.r &^ uint8(rgbMask)),
					(clearCol.g & uint8(rgbMask>>8)) | (old.g &^ uint8(rgbMask>>8)),
					(clearCol.b & uint8(rgbMask>>16)) | (old.b &^ uint8(rgbMask>>16)),
					(clearCol.a & uint8(aMask)) | (old.a &^ uint8(aMask)),
				}
				g.writePixelAt(g.fbAddr, g.fbWidth(), g.pixelFormat(), x, y, c)
			}
			if mode&4 != 0 { // target alpha/stencil plane
				if idx, ok := g.stencilIndex(x, y); ok {
					g.stencilAt()[idx] = stencilVal
				}
			}
			if mode&8 != 0 { // target depth
				g.writeDepth(x, y, depthVal)
			}
		}
	}
}

// roundCoord rounds a screen coordinate to the nearest pixel index.
func roundCoord(v float64) int {
	return int(math.Floor(v + 0.5))
}

// line rasterizes one line with Bresenham steps, interpolating z, uv,
// and color by t along the line.
func (g *GE) line(a, b vertex) {
	x0, y0 := roundCoord(a.sx), roundCoord(a.sy)
	x1, y1 := roundCoord(b.sx), roundCoord(b.sy)
	dx := abs(x1 - x0)
	dy := -abs(y1 - y0)
	stepX, stepY := 1, 1
	if x0 > x1 {
		stepX = -1
	}
	if y0 > y1 {
		stepY = -1
	}
	err := dx + dy
	steps := max(dx, -dy)
	if steps < 1 {
		steps = 1
	}
	x, y := x0, y0
	for step := 0; ; step++ {
		t := float64(step) / float64(steps)
		g.plot(x, y,
			lerp(a.sz, b.sz, t),
			lerpColor(a.col, b.col, t),
			lerp(a.u, b.u, t), lerp(a.v, b.v, t))
		if x == x1 && y == y1 {
			break
		}
		e2 := 2 * err
		if e2 >= dy {
			err += dy
			x += stepX
		}
		if e2 <= dx {
			err += dx
			y += stepY
		}
	}
}

// triangle rasterizes one triangle with barycentric interpolation at
// pixel centers. Interpolation is affine in screen space: NO
// perspective correction in this slice. Both windings are accepted
// because there is no backface culling.
func (g *GE) triangle(a, b, c vertex) {
	area := edge(a.sx, a.sy, b.sx, b.sy, c.sx, c.sy)
	if area == 0 {
		return
	}
	minX := int(math.Floor(math.Min(a.sx, math.Min(b.sx, c.sx))))
	maxX := int(math.Ceil(math.Max(a.sx, math.Max(b.sx, c.sx))))
	minY := int(math.Floor(math.Min(a.sy, math.Min(b.sy, c.sy))))
	maxY := int(math.Ceil(math.Max(a.sy, math.Max(b.sy, c.sy))))
	for y := minY; y <= maxY; y++ {
		for x := minX; x <= maxX; x++ {
			px, py := float64(x)+0.5, float64(y)+0.5
			w0 := edge(b.sx, b.sy, c.sx, c.sy, px, py) / area
			w1 := edge(c.sx, c.sy, a.sx, a.sy, px, py) / area
			w2 := edge(a.sx, a.sy, b.sx, b.sy, px, py) / area
			if w0 < 0 || w1 < 0 || w2 < 0 {
				continue
			}
			g.plot(x, y,
				w0*a.sz+w1*b.sz+w2*c.sz,
				fcolor{
					w0*a.col.r + w1*b.col.r + w2*c.col.r,
					w0*a.col.g + w1*b.col.g + w2*c.col.g,
					w0*a.col.b + w1*b.col.b + w2*c.col.b,
					w0*a.col.a + w1*b.col.a + w2*c.col.a,
				},
				w0*a.u+w1*b.u+w2*c.u,
				w0*a.v+w1*b.v+w2*c.v)
		}
	}
}

// edge is the 2D cross product of (b-a) and (p-a), the signed area
// kernel for barycentric weights.
func edge(ax, ay, bx, by, px, py float64) float64 {
	return (px-bx)*(ay-by) - (ax-bx)*(py-by)
}

// sprite fills the half open rectangle [x0,x1) by [y0,y1) from two
// corner vertices. UVs interpolate linearly across the rectangle with
// the step formula from the spec; z and color come from the first
// corner.
func (g *GE) sprite(a, b vertex) {
	x0, y0 := roundCoord(a.sx), roundCoord(a.sy)
	x1, y1 := roundCoord(b.sx), roundCoord(b.sy)
	if x1 <= x0 || y1 <= y0 {
		return
	}
	for y := y0; y < y1; y++ {
		v := a.v + (b.v-a.v)*(float64(y-y0)+0.5)/float64(y1-y0)
		for x := x0; x < x1; x++ {
			u := a.u + (b.u-a.u)*(float64(x-x0)+0.5)/float64(x1-x0)
			g.plot(x, y, a.sz, a.col, u, v)
		}
	}
}

func lerp(a, b, t float64) float64 { return a + (b-a)*t }

func lerpColor(a, b fcolor, t float64) fcolor {
	return fcolor{lerp(a.r, b.r, t), lerp(a.g, b.g, t), lerp(a.b, b.b, t), lerp(a.a, b.a, t)}
}

func abs(v int) int {
	if v < 0 {
		return -v
	}
	return v
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/audio.go ====================

package kernel

// The sceAudio output engine (PSP-4). The model follows the
// published documentation for the PSP audio driver (the pspsdk
// pspaudio.h constants and the behavior the open PSP test
// literature records):
//
//   - 8 hardware channels. A channel is reserved with a fixed
//     per-call sample count (the buffer length, 64..65472 frames,
//     a multiple of 64) and a format (stereo 0, mono 0x10).
//   - One buffer per channel, no queue behind it. An output call
//     hands the channel a guest buffer address; the mixer reads
//     the samples straight out of guest memory as they are
//     consumed, it never copies on the way in. A null buffer
//     pointer is accepted: the channel records a full buffer of
//     remaining samples but plays nothing, and a later output
//     call succeeds immediately against it.
//   - A non-blocking output on a channel with a buffer in flight
//     fails with SCE_ERROR_AUDIO_CHANNEL_BUSY. A blocking output
//     parks the caller instead (one parked thread per channel; a
//     second blocking caller is turned away BUSY). When the
//     playing buffer runs out, the parked caller's buffer starts
//     playing and the caller wakes with the channel sample count
//     as its result, the same value a successful immediate
//     enqueue returns.
//   - Volumes are per call (panned or single). A negative volume
//     leaves that side unchanged, except in
//     sceAudioOutputPannedBlocking, where the documented check
//     ORs the pair so a negative fails as an invalid volume.
//     Unity gain is 0x8000; mixing applies (sample * vol) >> 15
//     per channel into a wide accumulator and clamps once to
//     int16 at the end.
//   - sceAudioChRelease clears only the reservation: a buffer
//     already in flight keeps playing to the end.
//
// Consumption runs on the kernel cycle clock at exactly 44,100
// stereo frames per second: frames due at a cycle count C is
// floor(C * 44100 / 222 MHz), a pure function of the sysclock,
// so mixing is deterministic and save states resume the stream
// at the exact frame. Mixing itself is lazy: it advances
// whenever the scheduler looks for expired waits (every
// scheduling decision and every timeslice check) and when the
// host drains the output. A guest whose only thread blocks on
// audio output forever cannot deadlock the machine: the parked
// thread's wait deadline is the cycle its channel's buffer runs
// out, so the scheduler fast-forward reaches it, the buffer
// completes, the parked buffer starts, and the cycle repeats
// inside the frame budget.

const (
	audioChannels     = 8
	audioRate         = 44100
	audioVolumeMax    = 0x8000
	audioSampleMin    = 64
	audioSampleMax    = 65472
	audioFormatStereo = 0
	audioFormatMono   = 0x10
	// audioOutCap bounds the undrained output ring, in stereo
	// frames. At the 735 frames a frame budget produces, the cap
	// is over ten seconds of audio; samples past it are dropped
	// (the host is expected to drain every frame).
	audioOutCap = 8192
)

// audioChan is one hardware channel's state.
type audioChan struct {
	reserved    bool
	sampleCount uint32 // frames per output call; 0 after release (and on oneshot-only channels)
	format      uint32
	leftVol     int32
	rightVol    int32

	addr      uint32 // guest address of the playing buffer; 0 = nothing playing
	remaining uint32 // frames left in the playing buffer

	waiter       *Thread // the one parked blocking caller, if any
	waitAddr     uint32
	waitLeftVol  int32
	waitRightVol int32
}

// audioFramesDue is the number of output frames the stream has
// produced by the given kernel cycle count.
func audioFramesDue(cycles uint64) uint64 {
	return cycles * audioRate / ClockHz
}

// audioCycleForFrame is the first kernel cycle count at which
// output frame f has been produced.
func audioCycleForFrame(f uint64) uint64 {
	return (f*ClockHz + audioRate - 1) / audioRate
}

func audioApplyVolume(sample int16, vol int32) int64 {
	return int64(sample) * int64(vol) >> 15
}

func audioClamp(v int64) int16 {
	if v > 32767 {
		return 32767
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return -32768
	}
	return int16(v)
}

// audioAdvance mixes every output frame the cycle clock has
// reached since the last advance, appending stereo int16 frames
// to the output ring and completing channel buffers (which can
// wake parked blocking callers).
func (k *Kernel) audioAdvance() {
	due := audioFramesDue(k.cycles)
	for k.audioMixed < due {
		var accL, accR int64
		for i := range k.audioChans {
			c := &k.audioChans[i]
			if c.addr == 0 || c.remaining == 0 {
				continue
			}
			if c.format == audioFormatMono {
				s := int16(k.mem.Read16(c.addr))
				accL += audioApplyVolume(s, c.leftVol)
				accR += audioApplyVolume(s, c.rightVol)
				c.addr += 2
			} else {
				sl := int16(k.mem.Read16(c.addr))
				sr := int16(k.mem.Read16(c.addr + 2))
				accL += audioApplyVolume(sl, c.leftVol)
				accR += audioApplyVolume(sr, c.rightVol)
				c.addr += 4
			}
			c.remaining--
			if c.remaining == 0 {
				k.audioFinishChannel(i)
			}
		}
		if len(k.audioOut)/2 < audioOutCap {
			k.audioOut = append(k.audioOut, audioClamp(accL), audioClamp(accR))
		}
		k.audioMixed++
	}
}

// audioFinishChannel retires a channel's spent buffer: the
// channel goes idle, and a parked blocking caller's buffer takes
// its place, waking the caller with the sample count.
func (k *Kernel) audioFinishChannel(i int) {
	c := &k.audioChans[i]
	c.addr = 0
	c.remaining = 0
	w := c.waiter
	if w == nil {
		return
	}
	addr, lv, rv := c.waitAddr, c.waitLeftVol, c.waitRightVol
	c.waiter = nil
	if w.state != thWait || w.wait != waitAudio {
		return // the waiter left on its own (deleted or cancelled)
	}
	// Enqueue the parked buffer under the same rules as a fresh
	// output call: a null address leaves the channel idle but
	// holding a buffer's worth of rest length.
	c.remaining = c.sampleCount
	if lv >= 0 {
		c.leftVol = lv
	}
	if rv >= 0 {
		c.rightVol = rv
	}
	c.addr = addr
	k.completeWait(w, int32(c.sampleCount))
	k.maybePreempt(w)
}

// audioEnqueue hands a buffer to a channel under the one-buffer
// model and returns the value the output calls return: the
// channel sample count, or an SCE_ERROR_AUDIO code.
func (k *Kernel) audioEnqueue(c *audioChan, addr uint32, lv, rv int32) uint32 {
	if !c.reserved {
		return ErrAudioChannelNotInit
	}
	if c.addr != 0 {
		return ErrAudioChannelBusy
	}
	c.remaining = c.sampleCount
	if lv >= 0 {
		c.leftVol = lv
	}
	if rv >= 0 {
		c.rightVol = rv
	}
	c.addr = addr
	return c.sampleCount
}

// audioOutputBlocking is the shared body of the two blocking
// output calls: enqueue, or park the caller until the playing
// buffer runs out.
func (k *Kernel) audioOutputBlocking(th *Thread, idx int, addr uint32, lv, rv int32) syscallAction {
	c := &k.audioChans[idx]
	if res := k.audioEnqueue(c, addr, lv, rv); res != ErrAudioChannelBusy {
		k.ret(th, res)
		return actNone
	}
	if c.waiter != nil {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioChannelBusy)
		return actNone
	}
	c.waiter = th
	c.waitAddr = addr
	c.waitLeftVol = lv
	c.waitRightVol = rv
	// The deadline is the cycle at which the playing buffer's
	// last frame is produced; the scheduler fast-forward lands
	// there and audioAdvance completes the wait with the real
	// result (the deadline itself never delivers a timeout:
	// expireWaits has no timeout case for waitAudio).
	finishFrame := k.audioMixed + uint64(c.remaining)
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitAudio, uint32(idx), audioCycleForFrame(finishFrame))
}

// audioRestLen is sceAudioGetChannelRestLen: frames left in the
// playing buffer, plus a full buffer while a blocking caller is
// parked (its buffer counts as queued behind the playing one).
func (k *Kernel) audioRestLen(c *audioChan) int32 {
	rest := int32(c.remaining)
	if c.waiter != nil {
		rest += int32(c.sampleCount)
	}
	return rest
}

// DrainAudio advances mixing to the current kernel cycle count
// and returns every mixed-but-undrained sample (stereo int16)
// in stream order, clearing the ring.
func (k *Kernel) DrainAudio() []int16 {
	k.audioAdvance()
	out := k.audioOut
	k.audioOut = nil
	return out
}

// AudioMixedFrames returns the total number of output frames
// mixed since boot (735 per frame budget), for hosts and gates
// that account for the stream.
func (k *Kernel) AudioMixedFrames() uint64 { return k.audioMixed }

// come from the published pspsdk NID tables. Most user library
// NIDs are the low 32 bits of the SHA-1 of the function name (the
// documented NID generation scheme); this table was cross-checked
// against that computation and against the import tables of the
// open pspautotests corpus. A handful of firmware era NIDs
// predate the scheme (noted where used).

func hleGetCurrentPriority(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, uint32(th.priority))
	return actNone
}

// write64 stores a 64 bit value into guest memory.
func (k *Kernel) write64(addr uint32, v uint64) {
	k.mem.Write32(addr, uint32(v))
	k.mem.Write32(addr+4, uint32(v>>32))
}

// SysClock: the documented kernel time base is a microsecond
// count (sceKernelSysClock2USec divides by 1,000,000), derived
// here from the CPU cycle counter at 222 MHz.

// rtcTickBase is the microsecond tick of 1970-01-01 in the RTC's
// year-1 based reckoning. The RTC starts at the Unix epoch at
// boot in this model.

	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAllocPartitionMemory(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	partitionID := k.arg(th, 0)
	name := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 1), 32)
	typ := k.arg(th, 2)
	size := k.arg(th, 3)
	addr := k.stackArg(th, 4) // the fifth argument rides the stack in o32
	if partitionID != UserPartitionID {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalPartition)
		return actNone
	}
	if typ > allocHighAligned {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalMemBlockType)
		return actNone
	}
	// For the aligned types the fifth argument is the alignment,
	// for the address type the exact address: validate the shape
	// the partition allocator itself enforces.
	if (typ == allocLowAligned || typ == allocHighAligned) && (addr == 0 || addr&(addr-1) != 0) {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalAlignment)
		return actNone
	}
	uid, _, err := k.part.allocInternal(k, name, int(typ), size, addr)
	if err != nil {
		k.ret(th, ErrMemBlockAllocFailed)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleFreePartitionMemory(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	if !k.part.free(uid) {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownUID)
		return actNone
	}
	k.removeObject(uid)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleGetBlockHeadAddr(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	b := k.part.blockByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if b == nil {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownUID)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, b.addr)
	return actNone
}

func hleTotalFreeMemSize(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, k.part.totalFree())
	return actNone
}

func hleMaxFreeMemSize(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, k.part.maxFree())
	return actNone
}

func hleTotalMemSize(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, 32<<20) // PSP main RAM size reported by the firmware call
	return actNone
}

func hlePrintf(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	s := k.kernelPrintf(th, k.arg(th, 0))
	k.writeConsole([]byte(s))
	k.ret(th, uint32(len(s)))
	return actNone

func hleStdoutFd(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction { k.ret(th, 1); return actNone }
func hleStderrFd(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction { k.ret(th, 2); return actNone }

func hleStdoutWrite(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ptr := k.arg(th, 0)
	length := int(k.arg(th, 1))
	if ptr == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if length <= 0 || length > 1<<20 {
		s := k.readCString(ptr, 8192)
		k.writeConsole([]byte(s))
		k.ret(th, uint32(len(s)))
		return actNone
	}
	k.writeConsole(k.readBytes(ptr, length))
	k.ret(th, uint32(length))
	return actNone
}

// hleUtilityGetSystemParamInt answers sceUtility system parameter
// queries with the model's values: every integer parameter reads
// 0 (language Japanese, timezone offset 0, 24h clock unset, and
// so on). Runtime startup code asks during init; nothing in the
// test corpus branches on the values.
func hleUtilityGetSystemParamInt(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	if ptr := k.arg(th, 1); ptr != 0 {
		k.write32(ptr, 0)
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/hle_audio.go ====================

package kernel

// sceAudio handlers (PSP-4). NIDs and semantics come from the
// published pspsdk tables and the documented behavior of the
// PSP audio driver (see audio.go for the channel model and the
// README for the coverage table, including the families that
// deliberately stay on the unknown-NID path: sceAudioOutput2
// and sceAudioSRCCh share one hardware channel whose documented
// behavior includes arbitrary input sample rates with sample
// rate conversion and a two-descriptor DMA queue, which is not
// the simple documented semantics this slice implements).
//
// Argument and validation orders mirror the documented driver
// behavior the open test literature records: the classic output
// calls check the volume before the channel, reserve checks the
// sample count before the format, and sceAudioSetChannelDataLen
// checks its length before the reservation.

func hleAudioInit(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioEnd(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioSetFrequency(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// The documented call accepts 44,100 and 48,000. This
	// core's output stream is fixed at 44,100 Hz (see the
	// README), so the value is validated and accepted and the
	// rate does not change.
	switch k.arg(th, 0) {
	case 44100, 48000:
		k.ret(th, 0)
	default:
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidFrequency)
	}
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioOutput(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	vol := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if vol > 0xFFFF {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidVolume)
		return actNone
	}
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, k.audioEnqueue(&k.audioChans[ch], k.arg(th, 2), vol, vol))
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioOutputBlocking(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	vol := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if vol > 0xFFFF {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidVolume)
		return actNone
	}
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	return k.audioOutputBlocking(th, int(ch), k.arg(th, 2), vol, vol)
}

func hleAudioOutputPanned(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	lv := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	rv := int32(k.arg(th, 2))
	if lv > 0xFFFF || rv > 0xFFFF {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidVolume)
		return actNone
	}
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, k.audioEnqueue(&k.audioChans[ch], k.arg(th, 3), lv, rv))
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioOutputPannedBlocking(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	lv := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	rv := int32(k.arg(th, 2))
	// The panned blocking call ORs the volume pair before its
	// range check, so a negative volume fails here where the
	// other calls read it as "leave unchanged".
	if uint32(lv|rv) > 0xFFFF {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidVolume)
		return actNone
	}
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	return k.audioOutputBlocking(th, int(ch), k.arg(th, 3), lv, rv)
}

// audioFreeChannel finds a channel for a -1 reserve: the search
// runs downward from channel 7, and a channel counts as free
// only when nothing is reserved into it (sample count 0) and no
// buffer is still playing out.
func (k *Kernel) audioFreeChannel() int {
	for i := audioChannels - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if k.audioChans[i].sampleCount == 0 && k.audioChans[i].addr == 0 {
			return i
		}
	}
	return -1
}

func audioValidSampleCount(n uint32) bool {
	return n != 0 && n&63 == 0 && n <= audioSampleMax
}

func audioValidFormat(f uint32) bool {
	return f == audioFormatStereo || f == audioFormatMono
}

func hleAudioChReserve(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ch := int32(k.arg(th, 0))
	if ch < 0 {
		ch = int32(k.audioFreeChannel())
		if ch < 0 {
			k.ret(th, ErrAudioNoChannels)
			return actNone
		}
	}
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	c := &k.audioChans[ch]
	if c.reserved {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	sampleCount := k.arg(th, 1)
	if !audioValidSampleCount(sampleCount) {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioSampleNotAligned)
		return actNone
	}
	format := k.arg(th, 2)
	if !audioValidFormat(format) {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidFormat)
		return actNone
	}
	c.reserved = true
	c.sampleCount = sampleCount
	c.format = format
	c.leftVol = 0
	c.rightVol = 0
	k.ret(th, uint32(ch))
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioChRelease(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	c := &k.audioChans[ch]
	if !c.reserved {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioChannelNotReserved)
		return actNone
	}
	if c.waiter != nil {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioChannelBusy)
		return actNone
	}
	// Only the reservation goes away; a buffer in flight keeps
	// playing (see audio.go).
	c.reserved = false
	c.sampleCount = 0
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioGetChannelRestLen(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, uint32(k.audioRestLen(&k.audioChans[ch])))
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioGetChannelRestLength(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	c := &k.audioChans[ch]
	// Unlike RestLen, this one reads zero when no buffer is
	// really playing: after a null-pointer output the two
	// disagree by exactly the recorded rest length.
	rest := int32(0)
	if c.addr != 0 {
		rest = int32(c.remaining)
	}
	if c.waiter != nil {
		rest += int32(c.sampleCount)
	}
	k.ret(th, uint32(rest))
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioSetChannelDataLen(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	len := k.arg(th, 1)
	if !audioValidSampleCount(len) {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioSampleNotAligned)
		return actNone
	}
	c := &k.audioChans[ch]
	if c.waiter != nil {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioChannelBusy)
		return actNone
	}
	if !c.reserved {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioChannelNotInit)
		return actNone
	}
	c.sampleCount = len
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioChangeChannelConfig(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	c := &k.audioChans[ch]
	if c.waiter != nil || c.addr != 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioChannelBusy)
		return actNone
	}
	if !c.reserved {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioChannelNotReserved)
		return actNone
	}
	format := k.arg(th, 1)
	if !audioValidFormat(format) {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidFormat)
		return actNone
	}
	c.format = format
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioChangeChannelVolume(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	lv := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	rv := int32(k.arg(th, 2))
	if lv > 0xFFFF || rv > 0xFFFF {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidVolume)
		return actNone
	}
	ch := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ch >= audioChannels {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	// No reservation check: the volumes land on the channel
	// either way, and a negative side leaves that side alone.
	c := &k.audioChans[ch]
	if lv >= 0 {
		c.leftVol = lv
	}
	if rv >= 0 {
		c.rightVol = rv
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioOneshotOutput(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// (ch, sampleCount, format, leftvol, rightvol, buf);
	// the last two arguments ride the stack.
	lv := int32(k.arg(th, 3))
	rv := int32(k.stackArg(th, 4))
	buf := k.stackArg(th, 5)
	if uint32(lv) > 0xFFFF || uint32(rv) > 0xFFFF {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidVolume)
		return actNone
	}
	ch := int32(k.arg(th, 0))
	if ch < 0 {
		ch = int32(k.audioFreeChannel())
		if ch < 0 {
			k.ret(th, ErrAudioNoChannels)
			return actNone
		}
	} else if ch >= audioChannels || k.audioChans[ch].reserved {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidChannel)
		return actNone
	}
	sampleCount := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if sampleCount <= 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioSampleNotAligned)
		return actNone
	}
	format := k.arg(th, 2)
	if !audioValidFormat(format) {
		k.ret(th, ErrAudioInvalidFormat)
		return actNone
	}
	// No reservation and no busy check: a second oneshot
	// replaces the buffer in flight. The channel's sample
	// count stays 0, which is what frees the channel for a
	// -1 reserve once this buffer runs out.
	c := &k.audioChans[ch]
	c.format = format
	c.leftVol = lv
	c.rightVol = rv
	c.remaining = uint32(sampleCount)
	c.addr = buf
	k.ret(th, uint32(ch))
	return actNone
}

// --- sceAudioInput: the documented silence stub -----------------
//
// This core has no microphone source. The published semantics
// of the input calls are a sample count of mono 16-bit input;
// with no device attached the honest model is a silent one:
// init succeeds, reads fill the buffer with zeros and report
// every requested sample delivered, and nothing ever pends.

func hleAudioInputInit(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioInput(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	samples := k.arg(th, 0)
	buf := k.arg(th, 2)
	if buf == 0 {
		k.ret(th, 0xFFFFFFFF)
		return actNone
	}
	for i := uint32(0); i < samples; i++ {
		k.mem.Write16(buf+2*i, 0)
	}
	k.ret(th, samples)
	return actNone
}

func hleAudioGetInputLength(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}
