package kernel

import "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/ge"

// Display, controller and GE handlers. The display and GE work
// goes through the GEHost the system installs, since the GE
// engine and the presented framebuffer live in the system
// package (PSP-2).

func hleDisplaySetMode(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// (mode, width, height): stored in the kernel's display fields.
	k.dispMode = [3]uint32{k.arg(th, 1), k.arg(th, 2), k.arg(th, 0)}
	k.dispSet = true
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleDisplaySetFrameBuf(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	topAddr := k.arg(th, 0)
	bufferWidth := int(k.arg(th, 1))
	pixelFormat := int(k.arg(th, 2))
	// arg 3 is the sync mode; presentation is immediate here.
	k.host.PresentFrameBuffer(topAddr, bufferWidth, pixelFormat)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleDisplayWaitVblankStart(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	if k.inVblank {
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitVblank, 0, 0)
}

func hleDisplayGetVcount(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, uint32(k.vcount))
	return actNone
}

func hleDisplayIsVblank(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	if k.inVblank {
		k.ret(th, 1)
	} else {
		k.ret(th, 0)
	}
	return actNone
}

// SceCtrlData (24 bytes): TimeStamp u32, Buttons u32, Lx u8,
// Ly u8, Rsrv[6], plus the analog extension fields this kernel
// leaves zeroed (the documented structure's first 16 bytes are
// what the corpus and the brief exercise).
const (
	ctrlButtonSelect   = 0x000001
	ctrlButtonStart    = 0x000008
	ctrlButtonUp       = 0x000010
	ctrlButtonRight    = 0x000020
	ctrlButtonDown     = 0x000040
	ctrlButtonLeft     = 0x000080
	ctrlButtonLTrigger = 0x000100
	ctrlButtonRTrigger = 0x000200
	ctrlButtonTriangle = 0x001000
	ctrlButtonCircle   = 0x002000
	ctrlButtonCross    = 0x004000
	ctrlButtonSquare   = 0x008000
	ctrlButtonHold     = 0x200000
)

func hleCtrlRead(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	bufPtr := k.arg(th, 0)
	count := int(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count < 1 {
		count = 1
	}
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		w := &guestWriter{k: k, addr: bufPtr + uint32(i*24)}
		w.u32(uint32(k.SysClockMicros())) // TimeStamp
		w.u32(k.host.Buttons())
		lx, ly := k.host.Analog()
		w.u32(uint32(lx) | uint32(ly)<<8)
		// Rsrv[4..6] and the remaining pad words of the 24 byte
		// structure: zero.
		for j := 0; j < 3; j++ {
			w.u32(0)
		}
	}
	k.ret(th, uint32(count))
	return actNone
}

func hleCtrlSetSamplingMode(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.samplingCtl = k.arg(th, 0)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

// --- sceGe ---

// geList tracks one enqueued display list for the sync calls.
type geList struct {
	id        int32
	state     ge.ListState
	stallAddr uint32
}

// geListStates are the documented PspGeListStates values.
const (
	geListCompleted = 0
	geListQueued    = 1
	geListDrawing   = 2
	geListStalled   = 3
	geListPaused    = 4
)

func geListStateCode(s ge.ListState) int32 {
	switch s {
	case ge.StateReady:
		return geListCompleted
	case ge.StateStalled:
		return geListStalled
	case ge.StateDrawing:
		return geListDrawing
	case ge.StateCompleted:
		return geListCompleted
	}
	return geListCompleted
}

func hleGeEdramGetAddr(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// Returns the GE EDRAM base as a GE local address (0x04000000
	// folded to the GE's own address space origin): the
	// documented form is the raw EDRAM pointer guests translate
	// with sceGeEdramGetAddr's contract, 0x04000000.
	k.ret(th, 0x04000000)
	return actNone
}

func hleGeListEnQueue(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	listAddr := k.arg(th, 0)
	stallAddr := k.arg(th, 1)
	// arg 2 is a callback id, arg 3 a callback argument pointer;
	// callbacks are not dispatched in this model (documented).
	id := k.nextGeID
	k.nextGeID++
	st := k.host.SubmitDisplayList(listAddr)
	k.geLists[id] = &geList{id: id, state: st, stallAddr: stallAddr}
	k.ret(th, uint32(id))
	return actNone
}

func hleGeListSync(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	id := int32(k.arg(th, 0))
	syncType := k.arg(th, 1)
	l, ok := k.geLists[id]
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrError)
		return actNone
	}
	if syncType == 0 && l.state == ge.StateStalled {
		// PSP_GE_LIST_SYNC: wait for the list, which in the
		// synchronous model means run it past its stall point.
		l.state = k.host.ContinueDisplayList()
	}
	k.ret(th, uint32(geListStateCode(l.state)))
	return actNone
}

func hleGeDrawSync(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	syncType := k.arg(th, 0)
	if syncType == 0 {
		for _, l := range k.geLists {
			if l.state == ge.StateStalled {
				l.state = k.host.ContinueDisplayList()
			}
		}
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleGeBreak(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// Mode 1 cancels pending lists; the synchronous model has
	// nothing in flight beyond stalls, which are dropped.
	for _, l := range k.geLists {
		l.state = ge.StateCompleted
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleGeContinue(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	for _, l := range k.geLists {
		if l.state == ge.StateStalled {
			l.state = k.host.ContinueDisplayList()
		}
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/hle_io.go ====================

package kernel

import (
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/umd"
)

// The virtual file system behind IoFileMgrForUser. Devices:
//
//   - umd0: and disc0: route read-only to the mounted ISO9660
//     image (the host's umd.ISO).
//   - ms0: routes to the in-memory Memory Stick store the host
//     provides (read and write).
//   - host0: routes to the same store under host0: keys. This is
//     the psplink debug device: homebrew test frameworks (the
//     pspautotests corpus among them) write their results to
//     host0:/__testoutput.txt, so the store doubles as the test
//     result channel for the harness.
//   - fds 0, 1 and 2 are stdin (always EOF), stdout and stderr
//     (both append to the kernel console).
//
// Relative paths resolve against umd0:/ in this model. sceIo
// failures return the errno style kernel error codes.

const (
	fdConsoleIn  = 0
	fdConsoleOut = 1
	fdConsoleErr = 2
	firstUserFD  = 3
)

type fileDesc struct {
	isDir   bool
	writing bool

	// File backing (exactly one of isoPath / msKey is set).
	isoPath string
	msKey   string
	pos     int64

	// Directory backing.
	fromMS    bool
	keyPrefix string // store key prefix ("ms0:" or "host0:")
	dirNames  []string
	dirIdx    int
	dirPath   string
}

func splitDevice(path string) (device, rest string) {
	path = strings.ReplaceAll(path, "\\", "/")
	i := strings.IndexByte(path, ':')
	if i < 0 {
		return "umd0", path
	}
	return strings.ToLower(path[:i]), path[i+1:]
}

func cleanVPath(p string) string {
	if !strings.HasPrefix(p, "/") {
		p = "/" + p
	}
	parts := []string{}
	for _, seg := range strings.Split(p, "/") {
		switch seg {
		case "", ".":
		case "..":
			if len(parts) > 0 {
				parts = parts[:len(parts)-1]
			}
		default:
			parts = append(parts, seg)
		}
	}
	return "/" + strings.Join(parts, "/")
}

// isoStat resolves a path inside the mounted image to its entry.
func isoStat(iso *umd.ISO, path string) (umd.Entry, bool) {
	if path == "/" {
		return umd.Entry{Name: "/", Directory: true}, true
	}
	parent, name := splitParent(path)
	entries, err := iso.List(parent)
	if err != nil {
		return umd.Entry{}, false
	}
	for _, e := range entries {
		if strings.EqualFold(e.Name, name) {
			return e, true
		}
	}
	return umd.Entry{}, false
}

func splitParent(path string) (dir, name string) {
	i := strings.LastIndexByte(path, '/')
	if i <= 0 {
		return "/", strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/")
	}
	return path[:i], path[i+1:]
}

// msFiles returns the host's memory stick store, creating the
// kernel's view when the host has none.
func (k *Kernel) msFiles() map[string][]byte {
	return k.host.MemoryStickFiles()
}

func (k *Kernel) openFile(path string, flags uint32) (*fileDesc, uint32) {
	device, rest := splitDevice(path)
	rest = cleanVPath(rest)
	write := flags&0x0003 != 0x0001 // PSP_O_RDONLY is 1; 2 and 3 write
	switch device {
	case "umd0", "disc0":
		iso := k.host.ISO()
		if iso == nil {
			return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
		}
		info, ok := isoStat(iso, rest)
		if !ok {
			return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
		}
		if info.Directory || write {
			return nil, ErrErrnoInvalidArgument // directories and writes are refused
		}
		return &fileDesc{isoPath: rest}, 0
	case "ms0", "host0":
		files := k.msFiles()
		if files == nil {
			return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
		}
		key := device + ":" + rest
		if _, exists := files[key]; !exists {
			if flags&0x0200 == 0 { // PSP_O_CREAT
				return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
			}
			files[key] = []byte{}
		}
		fd := &fileDesc{msKey: key, writing: true, fromMS: true}
		if flags&0x0400 != 0 { // PSP_O_TRUNC
			files[key] = files[key][:0]
		}
		if flags&0x0100 != 0 { // PSP_O_APPEND
			fd.pos = int64(len(files[key]))
		}
		return fd, 0
	}
	return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
}

func (k *Kernel) openDir(path string) (*fileDesc, uint32) {
	device, rest := splitDevice(path)
	rest = cleanVPath(rest)
	switch device {
	case "umd0", "disc0":
		iso := k.host.ISO()
		if iso == nil {
			return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
		}
		info, ok := isoStat(iso, rest)
		if !ok || !info.Directory {
			return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
		}
		entries, err := iso.List(rest)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
		}
		names := make([]string, 0, len(entries))
		for _, e := range entries {
			names = append(names, e.Name)
		}
		return &fileDesc{isDir: true, dirNames: names, dirPath: rest}, 0
	case "ms0", "host0":
		prefix := device + ":" + rest
		if !strings.HasSuffix(prefix, "/") {
			prefix += "/"
		}
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		names := []string{}
		for key := range k.msFiles() {
			if strings.HasPrefix(key, prefix) {
				name := strings.TrimPrefix(key, prefix)
				if i := strings.IndexByte(name, '/'); i >= 0 {
					name = name[:i]
				}
				if name != "" && !seen[name] {
					seen[name] = true
					names = append(names, name)
				}
			}
		}
		sort.Strings(names)
		return &fileDesc{isDir: true, dirNames: names, dirPath: rest, fromMS: true, keyPrefix: device + ":"}, 0
	}
	return nil, ErrErrnoFileNotFound
}

func (k *Kernel) addFD(fd *fileDesc) int {
	id := k.nextFD
	k.nextFD++
	k.fds[id] = fd
	return id
}

// fileData returns the current bytes behind an open file.
func (k *Kernel) fileData(f *fileDesc) []byte {
	if f.msKey != "" {
		return k.msFiles()[f.msKey]
	}
	if f.isoPath != "" {
		if iso := k.host.ISO(); iso != nil {
			data, err := iso.ReadFile(f.isoPath)
			if err == nil {
				return data
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// fillStat writes a SceIoStat (0x58 bytes) at ptr: mode and attr in
// the documented FIO forms, a 64 bit size, and zeroed timestamps.
func (k *Kernel) fillStat(ptr uint32, isDir bool, size uint32) {
	w := &guestWriter{k: k, addr: ptr}
	if isDir {
		w.u32(0x1000 | 0755) // st_mode: FIO_S_IFDIR | rwxr-xr-x
		w.u32(0x10)          // st_attr: FIO_SO_IFDIR
	} else {
		w.u32(0x2000 | 0644) // st_mode: FIO_S_IFREG | rw-r--r--
		w.u32(0x20)          // st_attr: FIO_SO_IFREG
	}
	w.u32(size)
	w.u32(0) // st_size high word
	for i := 0; i < 12; i++ {
		w.u32(0) // ctime, atime, mtime (16 byte ScePspDateTime each)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 6; i++ {
		w.u32(0) // st_private
	}
}

func hleIoOpen(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	path := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 1024)
	flags := k.arg(th, 1)
	fd, ecode := k.openFile(path, flags)
	if fd == nil {
		k.ret(th, ecode)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, uint32(k.addFD(fd)))
	return actNone
}

func hleIoClose(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	fd := int(k.arg(th, 0))
	if fd >= 0 && fd < firstUserFD {
		k.ret(th, 0) // closing stdio is a no-op success
		return actNone
	}
	if _, ok := k.fds[fd]; !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoBadFd)
		return actNone
	}
	delete(k.fds, fd)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleIoRead(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	fd := int(k.arg(th, 0))
	buf := k.arg(th, 1)
	count := int(k.arg(th, 2))
	if fd == fdConsoleIn {
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	f, ok := k.fds[fd]
	if !ok || f.isDir {
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoBadFd)
		return actNone
	}
	data := k.fileData(f)
	if f.pos >= int64(len(data)) {
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	n := count
	if int64(n) > int64(len(data))-f.pos {
		n = int(int64(len(data)) - f.pos)
	}
	k.writeBytes(buf, data[f.pos:f.pos+int64(n)])
	f.pos += int64(n)
	k.ret(th, uint32(n))
	return actNone
}

func hleIoWrite(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	fd := int(k.arg(th, 0))
	buf := k.arg(th, 1)
	count := int(k.arg(th, 2))
	if fd == fdConsoleOut || fd == fdConsoleErr {
		k.writeConsole(k.readBytes(buf, count))
		k.ret(th, uint32(count))
		return actNone
	}
	f, ok := k.fds[fd]
	if !ok || f.isDir || f.msKey == "" {
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoBadFd)
		return actNone
	}
	files := k.msFiles()
	data := files[f.msKey]
	end := f.pos + int64(count)
	if end > int64(len(data)) {
		grown := make([]byte, end)
		copy(grown, data)
		data = grown
	}
	copy(data[f.pos:end], k.readBytes(buf, count))
	files[f.msKey] = data
	f.pos = end
	k.ret(th, uint32(count))
	return actNone
}

func seekFD(k *Kernel, f *fileDesc, off int64, whence uint32) (int64, bool) {
	size := int64(len(k.fileData(f)))
	var np int64
	switch whence {
	case 0: // SEEK_SET
		np = off
	case 1: // SEEK_CUR
		np = f.pos + off
	case 2: // SEEK_END
		np = size + off
	default:
		return 0, false
	}
	if np < 0 {
		np = 0
	}
	f.pos = np
	return np, true
}

func hleIoLseek(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// o32 packing for (fd, SceOff, whence): the fd takes $a0, the
	// 64 bit offset the aligned $a2/$a3 pair, whence the first
	// stack slot at $sp+16.
	fd := int(k.arg(th, 0))
	off := int64(uint64(k.cpu.Reg(6)) | uint64(k.cpu.Reg(7))<<32)
	whence := k.mem.Read32(k.cpu.Reg(29) + 16)
	f, ok := k.fds[fd]
	if !ok || f.isDir {
		k.ret64(th, ^uint64(0))
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoBadFd)
		return actNone
	}
	np, valid := seekFD(k, f, off, whence)
	if !valid {
		k.ret64(th, ^uint64(0))
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoInvalidArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret64(th, uint64(np))
	return actNone
}

func hleIoLseek32(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	fd := int(k.arg(th, 0))
	off := int64(int32(k.arg(th, 1)))
	whence := k.arg(th, 2)
	f, ok := k.fds[fd]
	if !ok || f.isDir {
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoBadFd)
		return actNone
	}
	np, valid := seekFD(k, f, off, whence)
	if !valid {
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoInvalidArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, uint32(np))
	return actNone
}

func hleIoGetstat(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	path := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 1024)
	statPtr := k.arg(th, 1)
	device, rest := splitDevice(path)
	rest = cleanVPath(rest)
	switch device {
	case "umd0", "disc0":
		iso := k.host.ISO()
		if iso == nil {
			k.ret(th, ErrErrnoFileNotFound)
			return actNone
		}
		info, ok := isoStat(iso, rest)
		if !ok {
			k.ret(th, ErrErrnoFileNotFound)
			return actNone
		}
		k.fillStat(statPtr, info.Directory, info.Size)
		k.ret(th, 0)
	case "ms0", "host0":
		data, ok := k.msFiles()[device+":"+rest]
		if !ok {
			k.ret(th, ErrErrnoFileNotFound)
			return actNone
		}
		k.fillStat(statPtr, false, uint32(len(data)))
		k.ret(th, 0)
	default:
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoFileNotFound)
	}
	return actNone
}

func hleIoDevctl(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// No device command is implemented in this model; the
	// documented invalid argument error is returned.
	k.ret(th, ErrErrnoInvalidArgument)
	return actNone
}

func hleIoDopen(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	path := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 1024)
	fd, ecode := k.openDir(path)
	if fd == nil {
		k.ret(th, ecode)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, uint32(k.addFD(fd)))
	return actNone
}

func hleIoDread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	fd := int(k.arg(th, 0))
	direntPtr := k.arg(th, 1)
	f, ok := k.fds[fd]
	if !ok || !f.isDir {
		k.ret(th, ErrErrnoBadFd)
		return actNone
	}
	if f.dirIdx >= len(f.dirNames) {
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	name := f.dirNames[f.dirIdx]
	f.dirIdx++
	// SceIoDirent: a SceIoStat (0x58 bytes) then d_name[256].
	child := f.dirPath + "/" + name
	if f.dirPath == "/" {
		child = "/" + name
	}
	isDir := false
	var size uint32
	if !f.fromMS {
		if iso := k.host.ISO(); iso != nil {
			if info, ok := isoStat(iso, child); ok {
				isDir = info.Directory
				size = info.Size
			}
		}
	} else if data, ok := k.msFiles()[f.keyPrefix+child]; ok {
		size = uint32(len(data))
	} else {
		isDir = true // an intermediate memory stick directory
	}
	k.fillStat(direntPtr, isDir, size)
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		b := byte(0)
		if i < len(name) {
			b = name[i]
		}
		k.mem.Write8(direntPtr+0x58+uint32(i), b)
	}
	k.ret(th, 1)
	return actNone
}

func hleIoDclose(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	return hleIoClose(k, th)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/hle_lwmutex.go ====================

package kernel

// Lightweight mutexes (sceKernel* LwMutex). Runtime libraries use
// these for their internal locks (the pspsdk libc locks its stdio,
// malloc, and environment state with them), so real programs call
// them constantly. The lock state lives in the guest workarea; see
// sync.go for the layout. Calls reach here under both the
// Kernel_Library and ThreadManForUser import names: pspsdk builds
// import them from ThreadManForUser, other documentation places
// them in Kernel_Library, so both are registered.

func (k *Kernel) lwMutexByWorkarea(workarea uint32) (*lwMutexObj, bool) {
	if workarea == 0 {
		return nil, false
	}
	uid := k.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffUID)
	if uid == lwNoSuchUID {
		return nil, false
	}
	o, ok := k.lookup(uid)
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	l, ok := o.(*lwMutexObj)
	return l, ok
}

func hleCreateLwMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	workarea := k.arg(th, 0)
	name := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 1), 32)
	attr := k.arg(th, 2)
	initCount := int32(k.arg(th, 3))
	if workarea == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if initCount < 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalCount)
		return actNone
	}
	l := &lwMutexObj{
		uid:       k.NewUID(kindLwMutex),
		name:      name,
		attr:      attr,
		initCount: initCount,
		workarea:  workarea,
	}
	k.registerObject(l.uid, l)
	// Initialize the workarea in place: level, owner (the creator
	// when starting locked), attr, waiter count, uid, zeroed pad.
	var owner uint32
	if initCount > 0 {
		owner = th.uid
	}
	k.lwSetState(l, initCount, owner)
	k.write32(workarea+lwOffAttr, attr)
	k.write32(workarea+lwOffWaits, 0)
	k.write32(workarea+lwOffUID, l.uid)
	k.write32(workarea+20, 0)
	k.write32(workarea+24, 0)
	k.write32(workarea+28, 0)
	k.ret(th, l.uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleDeleteLwMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	workarea := k.arg(th, 0)
	l, ok := k.lwMutexByWorkarea(workarea)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrLwMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	for _, w := range l.waiters {
		if w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitLwMutex {
			k.completeWait(w, errResult(ErrWaitDelete))
		}
	}
	l.waiters = nil
	k.removeObject(l.uid)
	// The workarea is cleared: level 0, owner and uid marked gone.
	k.lwSetState(l, 0, lwNoSuchUID)
	k.write32(workarea+lwOffUID, lwNoSuchUID)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

// lwLockCheck validates a lock request against the workarea state
// and returns a kernel error code, or ErrOK when the caller may
// acquire immediately or block.
func (k *Kernel) lwLockCheck(l *lwMutexObj, th *Thread, count int32) uint32 {
	if count <= 0 {
		return ErrIllegalCount
	}
	recursive := l.attr&lwMutexRecursiveMask != 0
	if count > 1 && !recursive {
		return ErrIllegalCount
	}
	level := k.lwLevel(l)
	if level+count < level {
		return ErrLwMutexLockOverflow
	}
	if level != 0 && k.lwOwner(l) == th.uid && !recursive {
		return ErrLwMutexRecursiveDeny
	}
	return ErrOK
}

func (k *Kernel) lwTryAcquire(l *lwMutexObj, th *Thread, count int32) bool {
	level := k.lwLevel(l)
	if level == 0 {
		k.lwSetState(l, count, th.uid)
		return true
	}
	if k.lwOwner(l) == th.uid && l.attr&lwMutexRecursiveMask != 0 {
		k.lwSetState(l, level+count, th.uid)
		return true
	}
	return false
}

func hleLockLwMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	workarea := k.arg(th, 0)
	l, ok := k.lwMutexByWorkarea(workarea)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrLwMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if ec := k.lwLockCheck(l, th, count); ec != ErrOK {
		k.ret(th, ec)
		return actNone
	}
	if k.lwTryAcquire(l, th, count) {
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	deadline, _, poll := k.deadlineFromTimeout(th, k.arg(th, 2))
	if poll {
		k.ret(th, ErrWaitTimeout)
		return actNone
	}
	th.waitCount = count
	l.waiters = append(l.waiters, th)
	k.lwSetWaitCount(l)
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitLwMutex, l.uid, deadline)
}

func hleTryLockLwMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	workarea := k.arg(th, 0)
	l, ok := k.lwMutexByWorkarea(workarea)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrLwMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if ec := k.lwLockCheck(l, th, count); ec != ErrOK {
		k.ret(th, ec)
		return actNone
	}
	if k.lwTryAcquire(l, th, count) {
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	// A failed try-lock reports the plain mutex try-lock error.
	k.ret(th, ErrMutexLocked)
	return actNone
}

func hleUnlockLwMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	workarea := k.arg(th, 0)
	l, ok := k.lwMutexByWorkarea(workarea)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrLwMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count <= 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalCount)
		return actNone
	}
	if count > 1 && l.attr&lwMutexRecursiveMask == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalCount)
		return actNone
	}
	level := k.lwLevel(l)
	if level == 0 || k.lwOwner(l) != th.uid {
		k.ret(th, ErrLwMutexUnlocked)
		return actNone
	}
	if level < count {
		k.ret(th, ErrLwMutexUnlockUnder)
		return actNone
	}
	level -= count
	if level == 0 {
		k.lwSetState(l, 0, 0)
		k.wakeLwMutexWaiter(l)
	} else {
		k.lwSetState(l, level, th.uid)
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/hle_sync.go ====================

package kernel

// Semaphore, mutex and event flag handlers (ThreadManForUser).

func (k *Kernel) semaByUID(uid uint32) (*semaObj, bool) {
	o, ok := k.lookup(uid)
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	s, ok := o.(*semaObj)
	return s, ok
}

func (k *Kernel) mutexByUID(uid uint32) (*mutexObj, bool) {
	o, ok := k.lookup(uid)
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	m, ok := o.(*mutexObj)
	return m, ok
}

func (k *Kernel) evfByUID(uid uint32) (*eventFlagObj, bool) {
	o, ok := k.lookup(uid)
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	e, ok := o.(*eventFlagObj)
	return e, ok
}

// --- Semaphores ---

func hleCreateSema(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	name := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 32)
	attr := k.arg(th, 1)
	initVal := int32(k.arg(th, 2))
	maxVal := int32(k.arg(th, 3))
	if maxVal <= 0 || initVal < 0 || initVal > maxVal {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	s := &semaObj{
		uid:     k.NewUID(kindSema),
		name:    name,
		attr:    attr,
		initVal: initVal,
		maxVal:  maxVal,
		cur:     initVal,
	}
	k.registerObject(s.uid, s)
	k.ret(th, s.uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleWaitSema(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	s, ok := k.semaByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownSemid)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count <= 0 || count > s.maxVal {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if tryAcquireSema(s, count) {
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	deadline, _, poll := k.deadlineFromTimeout(th, k.arg(th, 2))
	if poll {
		k.ret(th, ErrWaitTimeout)
		return actNone
	}
	th.waitCount = count
	s.waiters = append(s.waiters, th)
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitSema, s.uid, deadline)
}

func hlePollSema(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	s, ok := k.semaByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownSemid)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count <= 0 || count > s.maxVal {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if tryAcquireSema(s, count) {
		k.ret(th, 0)
	} else {
		k.ret(th, ErrSemaZero)
	}
	return actNone
}

func hleSignalSema(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	s, ok := k.semaByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownSemid)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count < 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if s.cur+count > s.maxVal {
		k.ret(th, ErrSemaOvf)
		return actNone
	}
	s.cur += count
	k.wakeSemaWaiters(s)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleDeleteSema(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	s, ok := k.semaByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownSemid)
		return actNone
	}
	for _, w := range s.waiters {
		if w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitSema {
			k.completeWait(w, errResult(ErrWaitDelete))
		}
	}
	s.waiters = nil
	k.removeObject(s.uid)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleReferSemaStatus(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	s, ok := k.semaByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownSemid)
		return actNone
	}
	infoPtr := k.arg(th, 1)
	if infoPtr == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	w := &guestWriter{k: k, addr: infoPtr}
	w.u32(56)
	w.str(s.name, 32)
	w.u32(s.attr)
	w.i32(s.initVal)
	w.i32(s.cur)
	w.i32(s.maxVal)
	w.i32(int32(len(s.waiters)))
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

// --- Mutexes ---

func hleCreateMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	name := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 32)
	attr := k.arg(th, 1)
	initCount := int32(k.arg(th, 2))
	if initCount < 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	m := &mutexObj{
		uid:       k.NewUID(kindMutex),
		name:      name,
		attr:      attr,
		initCount: initCount,
	}
	if initCount > 0 {
		m.owner = th
		m.lockCount = initCount
	}
	k.registerObject(m.uid, m)
	k.ret(th, m.uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleLockMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	m, ok := k.mutexByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count <= 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if m.lockCount == 0 {
		m.owner = th
		m.lockCount = count
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	if m.owner == th {
		if m.attr&mutexAttrRecursive == 0 {
			k.ret(th, ErrMutexRecursiveDenied)
			return actNone
		}
		m.lockCount += count
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	deadline, _, poll := k.deadlineFromTimeout(th, k.arg(th, 2))
	if poll {
		k.ret(th, ErrWaitTimeout)
		return actNone
	}
	th.waitCount = count
	m.waiters = append(m.waiters, th)
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitMutex, m.uid, deadline)
}

func hleTryLockMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	m, ok := k.mutexByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count <= 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if m.lockCount == 0 {
		m.owner = th
		m.lockCount = count
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	if m.owner == th && m.attr&mutexAttrRecursive != 0 {
		m.lockCount += count
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, ErrMutexLocked)
	return actNone
}

func hleUnlockMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	m, ok := k.mutexByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	count := int32(k.arg(th, 1))
	if count <= 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if m.lockCount == 0 || m.owner != th {
		k.ret(th, ErrMutexUnlocked)
		return actNone
	}
	if count > m.lockCount {
		k.ret(th, ErrMutexUnlockUnderflow)
		return actNone
	}
	m.lockCount -= count
	if m.lockCount == 0 {
		m.owner = nil
		k.wakeMutexWaiter(m)
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleDeleteMutex(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	m, ok := k.mutexByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	for _, w := range m.waiters {
		if w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitMutex {
			k.completeWait(w, errResult(ErrWaitDelete))
		}
	}
	m.waiters = nil
	k.removeObject(m.uid)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleReferMutexStatus(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	m, ok := k.mutexByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrMutexNotFound)
		return actNone
	}
	infoPtr := k.arg(th, 1)
	if infoPtr == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	var ownerUID uint32
	if m.owner != nil {
		ownerUID = m.owner.uid
	}
	w := &guestWriter{k: k, addr: infoPtr}
	w.u32(56)
	w.str(m.name, 32)
	w.u32(m.attr)
	w.i32(m.initCount)
	w.i32(m.lockCount)
	w.u32(ownerUID)
	w.i32(int32(len(m.waiters)))
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

// --- Event flags ---

func hleCreateEventFlag(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	name := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 32)
	attr := k.arg(th, 1)
	initPat := k.arg(th, 2)
	e := &eventFlagObj{
		uid:     k.NewUID(kindEventF),
		name:    name,
		attr:    attr,
		initPat: initPat,
		pattern: initPat,
	}
	k.registerObject(e.uid, e)
	k.ret(th, e.uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleWaitEventFlag(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	e, ok := k.evfByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownEvfid)
		return actNone
	}
	pattern := k.arg(th, 1)
	mode := k.arg(th, 2)
	resultPtr := k.arg(th, 3)
	if pattern == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrEvfIlpat)
		return actNone
	}
	if evfSatisfied(e.pattern, pattern, mode) {
		result := e.pattern
		if mode&evfWaitClearAll != 0 {
			e.pattern = 0
		} else if mode&evfWaitClearPat != 0 {
			e.pattern &^= pattern
		}
		if resultPtr != 0 {
			k.write32(resultPtr, result)
		}
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	timeoutPtr := k.stackArg(th, 4) // the fifth argument rides the stack in o32
	deadline, _, poll := k.deadlineFromTimeout(th, timeoutPtr)
	if poll {
		if resultPtr != 0 {
			k.write32(resultPtr, e.pattern)
		}
		k.ret(th, ErrWaitTimeout)
		return actNone
	}
	th.waitPattern = pattern
	th.waitMode = mode
	th.waitResultAt = resultPtr
	e.waiters = append(e.waiters, th)
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitEventFlag, e.uid, deadline)
}

func hlePollEventFlag(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	e, ok := k.evfByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownEvfid)
		return actNone
	}
	pattern := k.arg(th, 1)
	mode := k.arg(th, 2)
	resultPtr := k.arg(th, 3)
	if pattern == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrEvfIlpat)
		return actNone
	}
	if resultPtr != 0 {
		k.write32(resultPtr, e.pattern)
	}
	if !evfSatisfied(e.pattern, pattern, mode) {
		k.ret(th, ErrEvfCond)
		return actNone
	}
	if mode&evfWaitClearAll != 0 {
		e.pattern = 0
	} else if mode&evfWaitClearPat != 0 {
		e.pattern &^= pattern
	}
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleSetEventFlag(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	e, ok := k.evfByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownEvfid)
		return actNone
	}
	e.pattern |= k.arg(th, 1)
	k.wakeEventFlagWaiters(e)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleClearEventFlag(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	e, ok := k.evfByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownEvfid)
		return actNone
	}
	e.pattern &^= k.arg(th, 1)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleDeleteEventFlag(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	e, ok := k.evfByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownEvfid)
		return actNone
	}
	for _, w := range e.waiters {
		if w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitEventFlag {
			k.deliverEventFlagResult(w, e.pattern)
			k.completeWait(w, errResult(ErrWaitDelete))
		}
	}
	e.waiters = nil
	k.removeObject(e.uid)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleReferEventFlagStatus(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	e, ok := k.evfByUID(k.arg(th, 0))
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownEvfid)
		return actNone
	}
	infoPtr := k.arg(th, 1)
	if infoPtr == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	w := &guestWriter{k: k, addr: infoPtr}
	w.u32(52)
	w.str(e.name, 32)
	w.u32(e.attr)
	w.u32(e.initPat)
	w.u32(e.pattern)
	w.i32(int32(len(e.waiters)))
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/hle_thread.go ====================

package kernel

// ThreadManForUser handlers. Argument order follows the pspsdk
// pspthreadman.h prototypes; arguments arrive in $a0..$a3 then
// $t0.. as the Allegrex calling convention packs them.

func hleCreateThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	name := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 32)
	entry := k.arg(th, 1)
	priority := int32(k.arg(th, 2))
	stackSize := k.arg(th, 3)
	attr := k.stackArg(th, 4) // the fifth argument rides the stack in o32
	nt, err := k.createThread(name, entry, priority, stackSize, attr)
	if err == nil {
		// A new thread inherits the creator's $gp (the module's
		// small data base). Runtime startup code relies on this:
		// the crt0 spawns user_main and its stdio setup does
		// $gp-relative loads before anything sets $gp itself.
		ctxSetReg(nt.ctx, 28, k.cpu.Reg(28))
	}
	if err != nil {
		if ec, ok := err.(errCode); ok {
			k.ret(th, uint32(ec))
		} else {
			k.ret(th, ErrError)
		}
		return actNone
	}
	k.ret(th, nt.uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleStartThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	target, ok := k.threadByUID(uid)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownThid)
		return actNone
	}
	if target.state != thDormant {
		k.ret(th, ErrNotDormant)
		return actNone
	}
	argsSize := k.arg(th, 1)
	argPtr := k.arg(th, 2)
	sp := ctxReg(target.ctx, 29)
	a1 := uint32(0)
	if argsSize > 0 && argPtr != 0 {
		aligned := (argsSize + 3) &^ 3
		sp -= aligned
		k.writeBytes(sp, k.readBytes(argPtr, int(argsSize)))
		a1 = sp
		ctxSetReg(target.ctx, 29, sp)
	}
	ctxSetReg(target.ctx, 4, argsSize)
	ctxSetReg(target.ctx, 5, a1)
	target.state = thReady
	target.seq = k.nextSeq()
	k.maybePreempt(target)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleExitThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.exitThread(th, int32(k.arg(th, 0)), false)
	return actBlock // never actually resumes; the thread is dead
}

func hleExitDeleteThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.exitThread(th, int32(k.arg(th, 0)), true)
	return actBlock
}

func hleDeleteThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	target, ok := k.threadByUID(uid)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownThid)
		return actNone
	}
	if target == th {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	if target.state != thDormant && target.state != thDead {
		k.ret(th, ErrDormant)
		return actNone
	}
	k.deleteThreadObject(target)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleTerminateThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	target, ok := k.threadByUID(uid)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownThid)
		return actNone
	}
	if target.state == thDead {
		k.ret(th, ErrThreadTerminated)
		return actNone
	}
	if target.state == thWait {
		k.detachWaiter(target)
	}
	wasSelf := target == th
	k.exitThread(target, -1, false)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	if wasSelf {
		return actBlock
	}
	return actNone
}

func hleTerminateDeleteThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	target, ok := k.threadByUID(uid)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownThid)
		return actNone
	}
	if target.state == thDead {
		k.deleteThreadObject(target)
		k.ret(th, 0)
		return actNone
	}
	if target.state == thWait {
		k.detachWaiter(target)
	}
	wasSelf := target == th
	k.exitThread(target, -1, true)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	if wasSelf {
		return actBlock
	}
	return actNone
}

func hleWaitThreadEnd(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	target, ok := k.threadByUID(uid)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownThid)
		return actNone
	}
	if target == th {
		k.ret(th, ErrWaitCancel) // a thread cannot wait on itself in this model
		return actNone
	}
	if target.state == thDead {
		k.ret(th, uint32(target.exitStatus))
		return actNone
	}
	deadline, _, poll := k.deadlineFromTimeout(th, k.arg(th, 1))
	if poll {
		k.ret(th, ErrWaitTimeout)
		return actNone
	}
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitThreadEnd, uid, deadline)
}

func hleDelayThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	us := k.arg(th, 0)
	if us == 0 {
		return actResched // a zero delay is a yield on the real kernel path
	}
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitDelay, 0, k.cycles+uint64(us)*CyclesPerMicro)
}

func hleDelaySysClockThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	ptr := k.arg(th, 0)
	if ptr == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	// SceKernelSysClock is a 64 bit microsecond count.
	us := uint64(k.mem.Read32(ptr)) | uint64(k.mem.Read32(ptr+4))<<32
	if us == 0 {
		return actResched
	}
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitDelay, 0, k.cycles+us*CyclesPerMicro)
}

func hleSleepThread(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	return k.blockCurrent(th, waitSleep, 0, 0)
}

func hleRotateReadyQueue(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actResched
}

func hleGetThreadId(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	k.ret(th, th.uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleChangeCurrentThreadAttr(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	// Attributes are stored; none of them change behavior in this
	// model beyond what createThread recorded.
	th.attr = (th.attr &^ k.arg(th, 0)) | (k.arg(th, 1) & k.arg(th, 0))
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func hleReferThreadStatus(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	infoPtr := k.arg(th, 1)
	target := th
	if uid != 0 {
		t, ok := k.threadByUID(uid)
		if !ok {
			k.ret(th, ErrUnknownThid)
			return actNone
		}
		target = t
	}
	if infoPtr == 0 {
		k.ret(th, ErrIllegalArgument)
		return actNone
	}
	w := &guestWriter{k: k, addr: infoPtr}
	w.u32(104) // size
	w.str(target.name, 32)
	w.u32(target.attr)
	w.u32(threadStatusBits(target.state))
	w.u32(target.entry)
	w.u32(target.stackAddr)
	w.u32(target.stackSize)
	w.u32(ctxReg(target.ctx, 28)) // gpReg: the saved context's $gp
	w.i32(target.initPriority)
	w.i32(target.priority)
	w.i32(waitTypeCode(target.wait))
	w.u32(waitUIDForStatus(target))
	w.i32(0) // wakeupCount
	if target.state == thDead {
		w.i32(target.exitStatus)
	} else {
		w.i32(0)
	}
	w.u64(target.runCycles / CyclesPerMicro) // runClocks as a SysClock
	w.u32(0)                                 // intrPreemptCount
	w.u32(0)                                 // threadPreemptCount
	w.u32(0)                                 // releaseCount
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}

func threadStatusBits(s threadState) uint32 {
	switch s {
	case thRun:
		return 0x01
	case thReady:
		return 0x02
	case thWait:
		return 0x04
	case thDormant:
		return 0x10
	case thDead:
		return 0x20
	}
	return 0
}

// waitTypeCode maps the internal wait kinds to the status codes
// this kernel reports (a stated model subset of the kernel's
// internal wait type numbering).
func waitTypeCode(w waitKind) int32 {
	switch w {
	case waitNone:
		return 0
	case waitSema:
		return 1
	case waitMutex:
		return 2
	case waitEventFlag:
		return 3
	case waitVblank:
		return 4
	case waitThreadEnd:
		return 5
	case waitDelay:
		return 6
	case waitSleep:
		return 7
	}
	return 0
}

func waitUIDForStatus(th *Thread) uint32 {
	if th.state == thWait {
		return th.waitUID
	}
	return 0
}

// guestWriter writes a structure into guest memory field by field.
type guestWriter struct {
	k    *Kernel
	addr uint32
}

func (w *guestWriter) u32(v uint32) {
	w.k.mem.Write32(w.addr, v)
	w.addr += 4
}

func (w *guestWriter) i32(v int32) { w.u32(uint32(v)) }

func (w *guestWriter) u64(v uint64) {
	w.k.mem.Write32(w.addr, uint32(v))
	w.k.mem.Write32(w.addr+4, uint32(v>>32))
	w.addr += 8
}

func (w *guestWriter) str(s string, size int) {
	for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
		b := byte(0)
		if i < len(s) {
			b = s[i]
		}
		w.k.mem.Write8(w.addr+uint32(i), b)
	}
	w.addr += uint32(size)
}

// Kernel callbacks (ThreadManForUser). They are registered and
// deleted like the real objects, but this slice has no event
// source that dispatches them (documented in the README).

func hleCreateCallback(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	name := k.readCString(k.arg(th, 0), 32)
	cb := &callbackObj{
		uid:    k.NewUID(kindCallback),
		name:   name,
		fn:     k.arg(th, 1),
		arg:    k.arg(th, 2),
		thread: th,
	}
	k.registerObject(cb.uid, cb)
	k.ret(th, cb.uid)
	return actNone
}

func hleDeleteCallback(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction {
	uid := k.arg(th, 0)
	o, ok := k.lookup(uid)
	if !ok {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownUID)
		return actNone
	}
	if _, isCB := o.(*callbackObj); !isCB {
		k.ret(th, ErrUnknownCBID)
		return actNone
	}
	k.removeObject(uid)
	k.ret(th, 0)
	return actNone
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/kernel.go ====================

// Package kernel is the PSP-3 HLE kernel: a deterministic subset
// of the PSP system software, implemented from the published
// pspsdk headers and the uofw documentation. It loads ELF and PRX
// modules through the load package, assigns a syscall number to
// every imported (module, NID) pair and patches it into the import
// stub's delay slot word, and dispatches SYSCALL instructions on
// the shared Allegrex CPU through the CPU's SyscallHook.
//
// Threading is cooperative with priority preemption at defined
// scheduling points: a thread runs until it blocks in an HLE call,
// exits, yields, a higher priority thread is unblocked by one of
// its calls, or it exhausts a 10,000 instruction timeslice check
// and an equal or higher priority thread is ready. One Allegrex
// CPU is shared by all threads; a thread's full CPU state (the
// PSP-2 serialized form, 2,864 bytes including the VFPU) is swapped
// in and out on every switch.
//
// Object ids (SceUID) are sequential with a type tag: the low byte
// is the object kind, the remaining bytes a per-kernel sequence
// number starting at 1, so the first object created is 0x101,
// 0x201, and so on in creation order across all kinds.
package kernel

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/ge"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/load"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/umd"
)

// ClockHz is the Allegrex clock the kernel times against: the
// documented default 222 MHz. One microsecond is 222 cycles.
const ClockHz = 222_000_000

// CyclesPerMicro is the number of CPU cycles in one microsecond.
const CyclesPerMicro = ClockHz / 1_000_000

// Kernel error codes returned in $v0, from the published PSP

	ErrLwMutexLockOverflow  = 0x800201CD // SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_LWMUTEX_LOCK_OVERFLOW
	ErrLwMutexUnlockUnder   = 0x800201CE // SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_LWMUTEX_UNLOCK_UNDERFLOW

// Host is what the kernel needs from the machine that owns it. The
// system package implements it.
type Host interface {
	// Memory is the guest address space (the bus).
	Memory() load.Memory
	// CPU is the single shared Allegrex the threads time-share.
	SharedCPU() *allegrex.CPU
	// SubmitDisplayList runs a GE display list synchronously.
	SubmitDisplayList(addr uint32) ge.ListState
	// ContinueDisplayList resumes a SIGNAL-stalled list.
	ContinueDisplayList() ge.ListState
	// PresentFrameBuffer makes the GE present the given buffer.
	PresentFrameBuffer(addr uint32, width, format int)
	// Buttons and Analog expose the current controller state.
	Buttons() uint32
	Analog() (byte, byte)
	// ISO returns the mounted UMD image, or nil.
	ISO() *umd.ISO
	// MemoryStickFiles is the in-memory ms0: store (may be nil).
	MemoryStickFiles() map[string][]byte
}

// UnknownCall records one distinct unimplemented (module, NID)
// pair the guest called, with how many times it fired.
type UnknownCall struct {
	Module string
	NID    uint32
	Count  int
}

// Object kinds, stored in the low byte of every SceUID.
const (
	kindThread   = 0x01
	kindSema     = 0x02
	kindMutex    = 0x03
	kindEventF   = 0x04
	kindMemBlock = 0x05
	kindCallback = 0x06
	kindLwMutex  = 0x07
)

type object interface {
	objKind() uint32
}

// syscallAction tells the scheduler what an HLE handler did to the
// calling thread.
type syscallAction int

const (
	actNone    syscallAction = iota // keep running
	actBlock                        // the handler parked the thread in a wait
	actResched                      // re-run the scheduler pick after this call
)

type syscallFunc func(k *Kernel, th *Thread) syscallAction

type syscallEntry struct {
	module string
	nid    uint32
	name   string
	fn     syscallFunc
}

type modNid struct {
	module string
	nid    uint32
}

// Kernel is the HLE kernel state. It is created once per loaded
// module (one module per boot in this slice).
type Kernel struct {
	host Host
	mem  load.Memory
	cpu  *allegrex.CPU

	uidSeq  uint32
	objects map[uint32]object
	threads map[uint32]*Thread
	order   []*Thread // creation order, for deterministic scans
	current *Thread
	seq     uint64 // ready/wait ordering counter

	part *partition

	cycles   uint64 // sysclock in CPU cycles; mirrors the machine cycle count
	vcount   uint32
	exited   bool
	exitCode int32

	console []byte
	unknown map[modNid]*UnknownCall

	codes    map[uint32]*syscallEntry // assigned syscall number -> handler
	assigned map[modNid]uint32        // (module, NID) -> assigned syscall number
	nextCode uint32

	moduleBlockUID uint32
	moduleBase     uint32
	moduleSize     uint32
	bootPath       string

	exitCallbackUID uint32
	sdkVersion      uint32 // set by the sceKernelSetCompiledSdkVersion family

	dispMode    [3]uint32 // width, height, type from sceDisplaySetMode
	dispSet     bool
	samplingCtl uint32 // sceCtrl sampling mode, stored
	inVblank    bool   // true only while NotifyVblank is waking waiters

	geLists  map[int32]*geList
	nextGeID int32

	fds    map[int]*fileDesc
	nextFD int

	// sceAudio state (PSP-4; the engine lives in audio.go).
	audioChans          [audioChannels]audioChan
	audioMixed          uint64 // output frames mixed since boot
	audioOut            []int16
	audioRoutingMode    int32
	audioRoutingVolMode int32

	resched bool // an HLE call asked for a scheduler re-pick
}

// New creates a kernel bound to host and installs the syscall hook
// on the host CPU.
func New(host Host) *Kernel {
	k := &Kernel{
		host:     host,
		mem:      host.Memory(),
		cpu:      host.SharedCPU(),
		objects:  make(map[uint32]object),
		threads:  make(map[uint32]*Thread),
		part:     newPartition(UserPartitionBase, UserPartitionSize),
		unknown:  make(map[modNid]*UnknownCall),
		codes:    make(map[uint32]*syscallEntry),
		assigned: make(map[modNid]uint32),
		nextCode: 0x100,
		geLists:  make(map[int32]*geList),
		fds:      make(map[int]*fileDesc),
		nextFD:   3,
		bootPath: "umd0:",
		// The routing pair powers on in the speaker-on mode.
		audioRoutingMode:    1,
		audioRoutingVolMode: 1,
	}
	k.cpu.SyscallHook = k.handleSyscall
	return k
}

// NewUID allocates the next sequential UID with the kind tag.
func (k *Kernel) NewUID(kind uint32) uint32 {
	k.uidSeq++
	return k.uidSeq<<8 | kind
}

func (k *Kernel) registerObject(uid uint32, o object) { k.objects[uid] = o }

func (k *Kernel) lookup(uid uint32) (object, bool) {
	o, ok := k.objects[uid]
	return o, ok
}

func (k *Kernel) removeObject(uid uint32) { delete(k.objects, uid) }

// Cycles returns the kernel sysclock in CPU cycles.
func (k *Kernel) Cycles() uint64 { return k.cycles }

// SysClockMicros returns the sysclock in microseconds: cycles at
// 222 cycles per microsecond, truncated.
func (k *Kernel) SysClockMicros() uint64 { return k.cycles / CyclesPerMicro }

// Vcount returns the number of vblanks notified so far.
func (k *Kernel) Vcount() uint32 { return k.vcount }

// Exited reports whether the guest asked to exit (sceKernelExitGame)
// or every thread died.
func (k *Kernel) Exited() bool { return k.exited }

// ExitCode returns the status from sceKernelExitGame.
func (k *Kernel) ExitCode() int32 { return k.exitCode }

// ConsoleText returns everything written to the kernel console so
// far (sceKernelPrintf, sceIoWrite to fds 1 and 2, StdoutWrite).
func (k *Kernel) ConsoleText() string { return string(k.console) }

func (k *Kernel) writeConsole(b []byte) { k.console = append(k.console, b...) }

// UnknownCalls returns the unimplemented (module, NID) pairs the
// guest has called, sorted for determinism.
func (k *Kernel) UnknownCalls() []UnknownCall {
	out := make([]UnknownCall, 0, len(k.unknown))
	for _, u := range k.unknown {
		out = append(out, *u)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].Module != out[j].Module {
			return out[i].Module < out[j].Module
		}
		return out[i].NID < out[j].NID
	})
	return out
}

// CurrentThread returns the running thread, or nil between dispatches.
func (k *Kernel) CurrentThread() *Thread { return k.current }

// ModuleBase returns the load base of the booted module (0 for a
// fixed ET_EXEC image).
func (k *Kernel) ModuleBase() uint32 { return k.moduleBase }

// UserPartitionFree returns total and largest free bytes in the
// user partition, for tests and diagnostics.
func (k *Kernel) UserPartitionFree() (total, max uint32) {
	return k.part.totalFree(), k.part.maxFree()
}

// LoadModule loads an ELF or PRX image into the user partition,
// patches every import stub with its assigned syscall number, and
// creates (but does not start) the main thread at the module
// entry. Defaults follow the published boot model: priority 0x20
// and a 256 KB stack. SceModuleInfo carries no thread fields (the
// toolchain's crt0 owns those), so the defaults always apply here.
func (k *Kernel) LoadModule(data []byte) error {
	size, relocatable, err := load.Probe(data)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var base uint32
	if relocatable {
		// The module block starts at the partition base, but the
		// image loads moduleLoadReserve bytes in: the first 16 KB
		// of the user partition stay reserved, which is where the
		// reference loaders place PRX images (the pspautotests
		// .expected files embed absolute addresses that pin the
		// image base at partition base + 0x4000).
		uid, addr, err := k.part.allocInternal(k, "module", allocLow, size+moduleLoadReserve, 0)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("kernel: module does not fit in the user partition: %w", err)
		}
		k.moduleBlockUID = uid
		base = addr + moduleLoadReserve
	} else {
		// A fixed ET_EXEC image sits at its linked addresses,
		// inside the user partition by construction.
		base = 0
		k.moduleBase = 0
	}
	mod, err := load.Load(k.mem, data, base)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	k.moduleBase = mod.Base
	k.moduleSize = mod.Size

	for _, im := range mod.Imports {
		if im.IsVar {
			// Variable imports have no stub to patch; resolving
			// them is outside this slice (none of the gates or
			// the pspautotests cpu set use them).
			continue
		}
		code := k.assignSyscall(im.Module, im.NID)
		// The stub is JR $ra with the syscall in its delay slot:
		// the SYSCALL word goes at StubAddr+4.
		k.mem.Write32(im.StubAddr+4, syscallWord(code))
	}

	main, err := k.createThread("root", mod.Entry, 0x20, 256*1024, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// Boot arguments: a0 is the length of the boot path string and
	// a1 points at the string itself, placed in the partition.
	pathAddr, err := k.writeBootArgs(main)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	k.startThreadPrepared(main, uint32(len(k.bootPath)), pathAddr, mod.GP)
	return nil
}

// writeBootArgs copies the boot path string into the partition and
// returns its address.
func (k *Kernel) writeBootArgs(main *Thread) (uint32, error) {
	_, addr, err := k.part.allocInternal(k, "bootargs", allocLow, uint32(len(k.bootPath)+1), 0)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(k.bootPath); i++ {
		k.mem.Write8(addr+uint32(i), k.bootPath[i])
	}
	k.mem.Write8(addr+uint32(len(k.bootPath)), 0)
	return addr, nil
}

// syscallWord encodes a SYSCALL instruction with the given code.
func syscallWord(code uint32) uint32 {
	return (code << 6) | 0x0C
}

// assignSyscall returns the syscall number for a (module, NID)
// pair, allocating a new one on first sight. Known pairs dispatch
// to their HLE handler; unknown pairs dispatch to the logger.
func (k *Kernel) assignSyscall(module string, nid uint32) uint32 {
	key := modNid{module, nid}
	if code, ok := k.assigned[key]; ok {
		return code
	}
	code := k.nextCode
	k.nextCode++
	k.assigned[key] = code
	if e, ok := registry[key]; ok {
		cp := e
		k.codes[code] = &cp
	} else {
		k.codes[code] = nil // unknown: handleSyscall logs it
	}
	return code
}

// handleSyscall is the allegrex SyscallHook. It returns false when
// no thread is running (the bare PSP-1/2 path keeps its exception
// behavior); the kernel installs it only for kernel mode anyway.
func (k *Kernel) handleSyscall(cpu *allegrex.CPU, code uint32) bool {
	cpu.ClearLL() // a SYSCALL breaks any LL reservation (llsc corpus case)
	th := k.current
	if th == nil {
		return false
	}
	e := k.codes[code]
	if e == nil {
		// Either an unassigned raw SYSCALL or an import whose
		// (module, NID) pair is not implemented. Recover the pair
		// from the assignment table when the code is one of ours.
		key, known := k.keyForCode(code)
		mn := UnknownCall{Module: "<raw syscall>", NID: code}
		if known {
			mn = UnknownCall{Module: key.module, NID: key.nid}
		}
		slot := modNid{mn.Module, mn.NID}
		if u, ok := k.unknown[slot]; ok {
			u.Count++
		} else {
			cp := mn
			cp.Count = 1
			k.unknown[slot] = &cp
		}
		cpu.SetReg(2, ErrUnknownSyscall)
		cpu.SetReg(3, 0)
		return true
	}
	action := e.fn(k, th)
	switch action {
	case actBlock:
		th.blocked = true
	case actResched:
		k.resched = true
	}
	return true
}

func (k *Kernel) keyForCode(code uint32) (modNid, bool) {
	for key, c := range k.assigned {
		if c == code {
			return key, true
		}
	}
	return modNid{}, false
}

// arg helpers: HLE functions take their arguments from $a0..$a3
// (regs 4..7) and $t0..$t3 (regs 8..11).

func (k *Kernel) arg(th *Thread, i int) uint32 { return k.cpu.Reg(4 + i) }

// stackArg reads argument i (i >= 4) from the caller's stack slot:
// o32 puts argument slots 4 and up at $sp+16, $sp+20, ...
func (k *Kernel) stackArg(th *Thread, i int) uint32 {
	return k.mem.Read32(k.cpu.Reg(29) + 16 + uint32(i-4)*4)
}
func (k *Kernel) ret(th *Thread, v uint32) { k.cpu.SetReg(2, v) }
func (k *Kernel) ret64(th *Thread, v uint64) {
	k.cpu.SetReg(2, uint32(v))
	k.cpu.SetReg(3, uint32(v>>32))
}

// readCString reads a NUL terminated string from guest memory,
// capped at max bytes.
func (k *Kernel) readCString(addr uint32, max int) string {
	if addr == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	var sb strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < max; i++ {
		b := k.mem.Read8(addr + uint32(i))
		if b == 0 {
			break
		}
		sb.WriteByte(b)
	}
	return sb.String()
}

// readBytes copies n bytes out of guest memory.
func (k *Kernel) readBytes(addr uint32, n int) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, n)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = k.mem.Read8(addr + uint32(i))
	}
	return out
}

// writeBytes copies b into guest memory.
func (k *Kernel) writeBytes(addr uint32, b []byte) {
	for i, v := range b {
		k.mem.Write8(addr+uint32(i), v)
	}
}

// write32 stores one little endian word through the bus, so KSEG
// aliases behave the same as for guest stores.
func (k *Kernel) write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	k.mem.Write32(addr, v)
}
