func TestUIDModel(t *testing.T) {
	k := New(newTestHost())
	if got := k.NewUID(kindThread); got != 0x101 {
		t.Fatalf("first UID = %#x, want 0x101", got)
	}
	if got := k.NewUID(kindSema); got != 0x202 {
		t.Fatalf("second UID = %#x, want 0x202", got)
	}
	if got := k.NewUID(kindThread); got != 0x301 {
		t.Fatalf("third UID = %#x, want 0x301", got)
	}
}

func TestPartitionAccounting(t *testing.T) {
	k := New(newTestHost())
	total, max := k.UserPartitionFree()
	if total != UserPartitionSize || max != UserPartitionSize {
		t.Fatalf("fresh partition free = %d/%d, want %d", total, max, UserPartitionSize)
	}
	uid, addr, err := k.part.allocInternal(k, "t", allocLow, 0x1234, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if addr != UserPartitionBase {
		t.Fatalf("low alloc addr = %#x, want partition base", addr)
	}
	total, max = k.UserPartitionFree()
	if total != UserPartitionSize-0x1300 || max != UserPartitionSize-0x1300 {
		t.Fatalf("after alloc free = %d/%d, want %d", total, max, UserPartitionSize-0x1300)
	}
	// Head address resolves through the block UID.
	if got := k.part.blockByUID(uid).addr; got != addr {
		t.Fatalf("block addr = %#x, want %#x", got, addr)
	}
	// Aligned allocation honors its alignment.
	_, aaddr, err := k.part.allocInternal(k, "a", allocLowAligned, 0x1000, 0x10000)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if aaddr%0x10000 != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("aligned addr = %#x, not 64K aligned", aaddr)
	}
	// Address allocation at an occupied address fails.
	if _, _, err := k.part.allocInternal(k, "x", allocAddr, 0x100, addr); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("allocAddr over an occupied range succeeded")
	}
	if !k.part.free(uid) {
		t.Fatal("free of a live block failed")
	}
	total, _ = k.UserPartitionFree()
	if total != UserPartitionSize-0x1000 {
		// Only the aligned block (0x1000 bytes) still holds.
		t.Fatalf("after free total = %d, want %d", total, UserPartitionSize-0x1000)
	}
}

func putString(h *testHost, addr uint32, s string) {
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		h.mem.Write8(addr+uint32(i), s[i])
	}
	h.mem.Write8(addr+uint32(len(s)), 0)
}

func TestPrintfFormats(t *testing.T) {
	h := newTestHost()
	k := New(h)
	const fmtAddr = 0x08801000
	const strAddr = 0x08802000
	const stackBase = 0x08810000
	th := &Thread{}
	cases := []struct {
		format string
		args   [3]uint32 // $a1..$a3
		stack  []uint32  // words at $sp+16...
		want   string
	}{
		{"val=%d", [3]uint32{0xFFFFFFD6}, nil, "val=-42"}, // -42 as a word
		{"%08x", [3]uint32{0xabc}, nil, "00000abc"},
		{"%X", [3]uint32{0xdead}, nil, "DEAD"},
		{"%u", [3]uint32{0xFFFFFFFF}, nil, "4294967295"},
		{"%5d|", [3]uint32{42}, nil, "   42|"},
		{"%c%c", [3]uint32{'H', 'i'}, nil, "Hi"},
		{"100%%", [3]uint32{}, nil, "100%"},
		{"%p", [3]uint32{0x08800000}, nil, "0x8800000"},
		{"%lld", [3]uint32{0xFFFFFFFF, 0x1}, nil, "8589934591"},
		{"%d %d %d %d", [3]uint32{1, 2, 3}, []uint32{4}, "1 2 3 4"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		putString(h, fmtAddr, c.format)
		putString(h, strAddr, "PSP")
		h.cpu.SetReg(29, stackBase)
		for i, w := range c.stack {
			h.mem.Write32(stackBase+16+uint32(i*4), w)
		}
		h.cpu.SetReg(5, c.args[0])
		h.cpu.SetReg(6, c.args[1])
		h.cpu.SetReg(7, c.args[2])
		format := c.format
		if format == "%s-test" {
			h.cpu.SetReg(5, strAddr)
		}
		got := k.kernelPrintf(th, fmtAddr)
		if got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("printf %q = %q, want %q", c.format, got, c.want)
		}
	}
	// %s reads the pointed string.
	putString(h, fmtAddr, "[%s]")
	h.cpu.SetReg(5, strAddr)
	if got := k.kernelPrintf(th, fmtAddr); got != "[PSP]" {
		t.Errorf("printf %%s = %q, want [PSP]", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	h := newTestHost()
	k := New(h)
	k.cycles = 123456789
	k.vcount = 7
	k.writeConsole([]byte("hello state"))
	th, err := k.createThread("worker", 0x08804000, 0x30, 0x4000, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s := &semaObj{uid: k.NewUID(kindSema), name: "s", initVal: 1, maxVal: 3, cur: 2}
	k.registerObject(s.uid, s)
	blob := k.Serialize()

	h2 := newTestHost()
	k2 := New(h2)
	if err := k2.Deserialize(blob); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if k2.cycles != k.cycles || k2.vcount != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("counters = %d/%d, want %d/7", k2.cycles, k2.vcount, k.cycles)
	}
	if k2.ConsoleText() != "hello state" {
		t.Fatalf("console = %q", k2.ConsoleText())
	}
	restored, ok := k2.threadByUID(th.uid)
	if !ok || restored.name != "worker" || restored.priority != 0x30 {
		t.Fatalf("thread restore = %+v ok=%v", restored, ok)
	}
	rs, ok := k2.semaByUID(s.uid)
	if !ok || rs.cur != 2 || rs.maxVal != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("sema restore = %+v ok=%v", rs, ok)
	}
	// Re-serializing the restored kernel reproduces the blob.
	if blob2 := k2.Serialize(); string(blob2) != string(blob) {
		t.Fatal("serialize after deserialize differs")
	}
}

// TestLwMutexWorkarea pins the lightweight mutex model the
// runtime libraries depend on: create initializes the guest
// workarea in place (level, owner, attr, waiter count, uid),
// lock and unlock update it, recursive locks nest for the owner,
// a foreign unlock is refused, and the object survives a
// serialize round trip.
func TestLwMutexWorkarea(t *testing.T) {
	h := newTestHost()
	k := New(h)
	const workarea = 0x08820000
	const nameAddr = 0x08821000
	putString(h, nameAddr, "stdio")
	th, err := k.createThread("worker", 0x08804000, 0x30, 0x4000, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	setArgs := func(a0, a1, a2, a3 uint32) {
		h.cpu.SetReg(4, a0)
		h.cpu.SetReg(5, a1)
		h.cpu.SetReg(6, a2)
		h.cpu.SetReg(7, a3)
	}
	// Create with the recursive attribute (0x200) and count 0.
	setArgs(workarea, nameAddr, 0x200, 0)
	hleCreateLwMutex(k, th)
	uid := h.cpu.Reg(2)
	if uid&0xFF != kindLwMutex || uid == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("create returned %#x, want an lwmutex tagged UID", uid)
	}
	if got := h.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffUID); got != uid {
		t.Fatalf("workarea uid = %#x, want %#x", got, uid)
	}
	if got := h.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffAttr); got != 0x200 {
		t.Fatalf("workarea attr = %#x, want 0x200", got)
	}
	// Lock once, then recursively, then unlock both levels.
	setArgs(workarea, 1, 0, 0)
	hleLockLwMutex(k, th)
	if got := h.cpu.Reg(2); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("lock returned %#x", got)
	}
	if lv := h.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffLevel); lv != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("level = %d, want 1", lv)
	}
	if ow := h.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffOwner); ow != th.uid {
		t.Fatalf("owner = %#x, want %#x", ow, th.uid)
	}
	setArgs(workarea, 1, 0, 0)
	hleLockLwMutex(k, th)
	if lv := h.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffLevel); lv != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("after recursive lock level = %d, want 2", lv)
	}
	setArgs(workarea, 2, 0, 0)
	hleUnlockLwMutex(k, th)
	if got := h.cpu.Reg(2); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unlock returned %#x", got)
	}
	if lv := h.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffLevel); lv != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("after unlock level = %d, want 0", lv)
	}
	// Unlocking an unlocked mutex reports the documented error.
	setArgs(workarea, 1, 0, 0)
	hleUnlockLwMutex(k, th)
	if got := h.cpu.Reg(2); got != ErrLwMutexUnlocked {
		t.Fatalf("unlock of free mutex = %#x, want %#x", got, ErrLwMutexUnlocked)
	}
	// Delete marks the workarea gone; later locks report it.
	setArgs(workarea, 0, 0, 0)
	hleDeleteLwMutex(k, th)
	if got := h.mem.Read32(workarea + lwOffUID); got != lwNoSuchUID {
		t.Fatalf("after delete workarea uid = %#x, want %#x", got, lwNoSuchUID)
	}
	setArgs(workarea, 1, 0, 0)
	hleLockLwMutex(k, th)
	if got := h.cpu.Reg(2); got != ErrLwMutexNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("lock after delete = %#x, want %#x", got, ErrLwMutexNotFound)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/partition.go ====================

package kernel

import (
	"errors"
	"sort"
)

// The user partition (partition id 2) is the documented 24 MB of
// main RAM at 0x08800000. Blocks are carved out of it with the
// sceKernelAllocPartitionMemory placement types. Block sizes are
// rounded up to a 256 byte granularity, which is the granularity
// this kernel accounts in; free space accounting is exact against
// that rule, so TotalFreeMemSize and MaxFreeMemSize are
// deterministic functions of the allocation history.
const (
	UserPartitionID   = 2
	UserPartitionBase = 0x08800000

	// moduleLoadReserve is the reserved head of the user
	// partition: a loaded module's block starts at the partition
	// base but its image sits this many bytes in (16 KB).
	moduleLoadReserve = 0x4000
	UserPartitionSize = 24 << 20
	blockGranularity  = 0x100
)

// Allocation types (PspSysMemBlockTypes in pspsdk pspsysmem.h).
const (
	allocLow         = 0 // PSP_SMEM_Low
	allocHigh        = 1 // PSP_SMEM_High
	allocAddr        = 2 // PSP_SMEM_Addr
	allocLowAligned  = 3 // PSP_SMEM_LowAligned
	allocHighAligned = 4 // PSP_SMEM_HighAligned
)

type memBlock struct {
	uid  uint32
	name string
	addr uint32
	size uint32 // rounded size actually reserved
}

func (b *memBlock) objKind() uint32 { return kindMemBlock }

// partition is a first fit block allocator over one address range.
// Allocated blocks are kept sorted by address; free ranges are the
// gaps between them.
type partition struct {
	base   uint32
	size   uint32
	blocks []*memBlock
}

func newPartition(base, size uint32) *partition {
	return &partition{base: base, size: size}
}

func roundBlockSize(size uint32) uint32 {
	if size == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return (size + blockGranularity - 1) &^ (blockGranularity - 1)
}

type freeRange struct{ start, end uint32 }

func (p *partition) freeRanges() []freeRange {
	var out []freeRange
	cur := p.base
	for _, b := range p.blocks {
		if b.addr > cur {
			out = append(out, freeRange{cur, b.addr})
		}
		if end := b.addr + b.size; end > cur {
			cur = end
		}
	}
	if cur < p.base+p.size {
		out = append(out, freeRange{cur, p.base + p.size})
	}
	return out
}

func (p *partition) totalFree() uint32 {
	var total uint32
	for _, r := range p.freeRanges() {
		total += r.end - r.start
	}
	return total
}

func (p *partition) maxFree() uint32 {
	var max uint32
	for _, r := range p.freeRanges() {
		if s := r.end - r.start; s > max {
			max = s
		}
	}
	return max
}

func alignUp(v, a uint32) uint32 {
	if a <= 1 {
		return v
	}
	return (v + a - 1) &^ (a - 1)
}

func alignDown(v, a uint32) uint32 {
	if a <= 1 {
		return v
	}
	return v &^ (a - 1)
}

// alloc places a block of the (rounded) size per the placement
// type. For allocAddr, addr is the exact start. For the aligned
// types, addr is the alignment (a power of two). It returns the
// start address.
func (p *partition) alloc(typ int, size, addr uint32) (uint32, error) {
	size = roundBlockSize(size)
	if size == 0 || size > p.size {
		return 0, errors.New("partition: bad size")
	}
	ranges := p.freeRanges()
	place := func(start uint32) (uint32, error) {
		nb := &memBlock{addr: start, size: size}
		i := sort.Search(len(p.blocks), func(i int) bool { return p.blocks[i].addr > start })
		p.blocks = append(p.blocks, nil)
		copy(p.blocks[i+1:], p.blocks[i:])
		p.blocks[i] = nb
		return start, nil
	}
	switch typ {
	case allocLow, allocLowAligned:
		align := uint32(1)
		if typ == allocLowAligned {
			align = addr
			if align == 0 || align&(align-1) != 0 {
				return 0, errors.New("partition: bad alignment")
			}
		}
		for _, r := range ranges {
			start := alignUp(r.start, align)
			if start+size <= r.end {
				return place(start)
			}
		}
	case allocHigh, allocHighAligned:
		align := uint32(1)
		if typ == allocHighAligned {
			align = addr
			if align == 0 || align&(align-1) != 0 {
				return 0, errors.New("partition: bad alignment")
			}
		}
		for i := len(ranges) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
			r := ranges[i]
			if r.end-r.start >= size {
				start := alignDown(r.end-size, align)
				if start >= r.start {
					return place(start)
				}
			}
		}
	case allocAddr:
		for _, r := range ranges {
			if addr >= r.start && addr+size <= r.end {
				return place(addr)
			}
		}
		return 0, errors.New("partition: address range not free")
	default:
		return 0, errors.New("partition: bad allocation type")
	}
	return 0, errors.New("partition: out of memory")
}

// allocInternal allocates a block and registers it as a kernel
// object with the given name, returning its UID and address.
func (p *partition) allocInternal(k *Kernel, name string, typ int, size, addr uint32) (uint32, uint32, error) {
	start, err := p.alloc(typ, size, addr)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, err
	}
	uid := k.NewUID(kindMemBlock)
	// Find the block just placed and tag it.
	for _, b := range p.blocks {
		if b.addr == start && b.uid == 0 {
			b.uid = uid
			b.name = name
			break
		}
	}
	k.registerObject(uid, p.blockByAddr(start))
	return uid, start, nil
}

func (p *partition) blockByAddr(addr uint32) *memBlock {
	for _, b := range p.blocks {
		if b.addr == addr {
			return b
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (p *partition) blockByUID(uid uint32) *memBlock {
	for _, b := range p.blocks {
		if b.uid == uid {
			return b
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// free releases the block with the given UID.
func (p *partition) free(uid uint32) bool {
	for i, b := range p.blocks {
		if b.uid == uid {
			p.blocks = append(p.blocks[:i], p.blocks[i+1:]...)
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/printf.go ====================

package kernel

import (
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// printf implements the sceKernelPrintf format subset this kernel
// documents: %d %i %u %x %X %c %s %p and %%, with an optional 0
// flag, field width, and the l / ll length modifiers. Arguments
// follow the Allegrex o32 convention: $a1..$a3 hold the first
// three, the rest sit on the caller's stack at $sp+16, $sp+20, ...
type argReader struct {
	k    *Kernel
	th   *Thread
	regs [3]uint32 // $a1, $a2, $a3
	sp   uint32
	next int
}

func newArgReader(k *Kernel, th *Thread) *argReader {
	return &argReader{
		k:    k,
		th:   th,
		regs: [3]uint32{k.cpu.Reg(5), k.cpu.Reg(6), k.cpu.Reg(7)},
		sp:   k.cpu.Reg(29),
	}
}

func (a *argReader) word() uint32 {
	i := a.next
	a.next++
	if i < 3 {
		return a.regs[i]
	}
	return a.k.mem.Read32(a.sp + 16 + uint32(i-3)*4)
}

func (a *argReader) dword() uint64 {
	lo := uint64(a.word())
	hi := uint64(a.word())
	return lo | hi<<32
}

func (k *Kernel) kernelPrintf(th *Thread, formatAddr uint32) string {
	format := k.readCString(formatAddr, 4096)
	args := newArgReader(k, th)
	var out strings.Builder
	i := 0
	for i < len(format) {
		c := format[i]
		if c != '%' {
			out.WriteByte(c)
			i++
			continue
		}
		i++
		if i >= len(format) {
			out.WriteByte('%')
			break
		}
		zero := false
		if format[i] == '0' {
			zero = true
			i++
		}
		width := 0
		for i < len(format) && format[i] >= '0' && format[i] <= '9' {
			width = width*10 + int(format[i]-'0')
			i++
		}
		longs := 0
		for i < len(format) && format[i] == 'l' {
			longs++
			i++
		}
		if i >= len(format) {
			break
		}
		verb := format[i]
		i++
		pad := func(s string) string {
			if len(s) >= width {
				return s
			}
			fill := " "
			if zero {
				fill = "0"
			}
			return strings.Repeat(fill, width-len(s)) + s
		}
		switch verb {
		case '%':
			out.WriteByte('%')
		case 'd', 'i':
			if longs >= 2 {
				out.WriteString(pad(strconv.FormatInt(int64(args.dword()), 10)))
			} else {
				out.WriteString(pad(strconv.FormatInt(int64(int32(args.word())), 10)))
			}
		case 'u':
			if longs >= 2 {
				out.WriteString(pad(strconv.FormatUint(args.dword(), 10)))
			} else {
				out.WriteString(pad(strconv.FormatUint(uint64(args.word()), 10)))
			}
		case 'x', 'X':
			var s string
			if longs >= 2 {
				s = strconv.FormatUint(args.dword(), 16)
			} else {
				s = strconv.FormatUint(uint64(args.word()), 16)
			}
			if verb == 'X' {
				s = strings.ToUpper(s)
			}
			out.WriteString(pad(s))
		case 'p':
			out.WriteString("0x" + pad(strconv.FormatUint(uint64(args.word()), 16)))
		case 'c':
			out.WriteByte(byte(args.word()))
		case 's':
			out.WriteString(k.readCString(args.word(), 8192))
		default:
			// Unknown verbs are echoed verbatim.
			out.WriteByte('%')
			out.WriteByte(verb)
		}
	}
	return out.String()
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/serialize.go ====================

package kernel

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"sort"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/ge"
)

// Save state serialization for the kernel (the system embeds this
// blob in its version 3 states). The format is versioned
// internally and fully deterministic: maps are written in sorted
// or creation order, so identical machines produce identical
// bytes.

const kernelStateMagic = "PSPK"

// kernelStateVersion 3 (PSP-4) appends the sceAudio block
// (channels, mixer position, output ring, routing modes) after
// the file descriptor block. Version 2 blobs are rejected.
const kernelStateVersion = 3

type stateWriter struct{ buf []byte }

func (w *stateWriter) u8(v uint8)   { w.buf = append(w.buf, v) }
func (w *stateWriter) i16(v int16)  { w.u32(uint32(uint16(v))) }
func (w *stateWriter) u32(v uint32) { w.buf = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(w.buf, v) }
func (w *stateWriter) i32(v int32)  { w.u32(uint32(v)) }
func (w *stateWriter) u64(v uint64) { w.buf = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint64(w.buf, v) }
func (w *stateWriter) i64(v int64)  { w.u64(uint64(v)) }
func (w *stateWriter) str(s string) {
	w.u32(uint32(len(s)))
	w.buf = append(w.buf, s...)
}
func (w *stateWriter) bytes(b []byte) {
	w.u32(uint32(len(b)))
	w.buf = append(w.buf, b...)
}
func (w *stateWriter) boolean(v bool) {
	if v {
		w.u8(1)
	} else {
		w.u8(0)
	}
}

type stateReader struct {
	buf []byte
	pos int
	err error
}

func (r *stateReader) take(n int) []byte {
	if r.err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	if n < 0 || r.pos+n > len(r.buf) {
		r.err = errors.New("kernel: state blob truncated")
		return nil
	}
	b := r.buf[r.pos : r.pos+n]
	r.pos += n
	return b
}

func (r *stateReader) u8() uint8 {
	b := r.take(1)
	if b == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return b[0]
}

func (r *stateReader) u32() uint32 {
	b := r.take(4)
	if b == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b)
}

func (r *stateReader) i32() int32 { return int32(r.u32()) }

func (r *stateReader) u64() uint64 {
	b := r.take(8)
	if b == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(b)
}

func (r *stateReader) i64() int64 { return int64(r.u64()) }

func (r *stateReader) str() string {
	n := int(r.u32())
	b := r.take(n)
	if b == nil {
		return ""
	}
	return string(b)
}

func (r *stateReader) bytes() []byte {
	n := int(r.u32())
	b := r.take(n)
	if b == nil {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]byte, n)
	copy(out, b)
	return out
}

func (r *stateReader) boolean() bool { return r.u8() != 0 }

// Serialize returns the full kernel state.
func (k *Kernel) Serialize() []byte {
	w := &stateWriter{}
	w.buf = append(w.buf, kernelStateMagic...)
	w.u32(kernelStateVersion)
	w.u64(k.cycles)
	w.u32(k.vcount)
	w.boolean(k.exited)
	w.i32(k.exitCode)
	w.u32(k.uidSeq)
	w.u64(k.seq)
	w.u32(k.nextCode)
	w.u32(k.sdkVersion)
	w.u32(k.exitCallbackUID)
	w.str(k.bootPath)
	w.u32(k.moduleBlockUID)
	w.u32(k.moduleBase)
	w.u32(k.moduleSize)
	for _, v := range k.dispMode {
		w.u32(v)
	}
	w.boolean(k.dispSet)
	w.u32(k.samplingCtl)

	w.bytes(k.console)

	unknowns := k.UnknownCalls()
	w.u32(uint32(len(unknowns)))
	for _, u := range unknowns {
		w.str(u.Module)
		w.u32(u.NID)
		w.u32(uint32(u.Count))
	}

	assigned := make([]modNid, 0, len(k.assigned))
	for key := range k.assigned {
		assigned = append(assigned, key)
	}
	sort.Slice(assigned, func(i, j int) bool {
		if assigned[i].module != assigned[j].module {
			return assigned[i].module < assigned[j].module
		}
		return assigned[i].nid < assigned[j].nid
	})
	w.u32(uint32(len(assigned)))
	for _, key := range assigned {
		w.str(key.module)
		w.u32(key.nid)
		w.u32(k.assigned[key])
	}

	w.u32(uint32(len(k.part.blocks)))
	for _, b := range k.part.blocks {
		w.u32(b.uid)
		w.str(b.name)
		w.u32(b.addr)
		w.u32(b.size)
	}

	w.u32(uint32(len(k.order)))
	for _, th := range k.order {
		w.u32(th.uid)
		w.str(th.name)
		w.u32(th.entry)
		w.u32(th.attr)
		w.i32(th.initPriority)
		w.i32(th.priority)
		w.u8(uint8(th.state))
		w.u32(th.stackAddr)
		w.u32(th.stackSize)
		w.u32(th.stackBlock)
		w.i32(th.exitStatus)
		w.u64(th.runCycles)
		w.u8(uint8(th.wait))
		w.u32(th.waitUID)
		w.u64(th.waitDeadline)
		w.u32(th.waitPattern)
		w.u32(th.waitMode)
		w.u32(th.waitResultAt)
		w.i32(th.waitCount)
		w.u64(th.seq)
		w.i32(th.waitResult)
		w.boolean(th.hasResult)
		w.boolean(th.loaded)
		w.bytes(th.ctx)
	}
	var currentUID uint32
	if k.current != nil {
		currentUID = k.current.uid
	}
	w.u32(currentUID)

	semas, mutexes, evfs, cbs, lwms := k.syncObjects()
	w.u32(uint32(len(semas)))
	for _, s := range semas {
		w.u32(s.uid)
		w.str(s.name)
		w.u32(s.attr)
		w.i32(s.initVal)
		w.i32(s.maxVal)
		w.i32(s.cur)
		writeWaiters(w, s.waiters)
	}
	w.u32(uint32(len(mutexes)))
	for _, m := range mutexes {
		w.u32(m.uid)
		w.str(m.name)
		w.u32(m.attr)
		w.i32(m.initCount)
		w.i32(m.lockCount)
		var owner uint32
		if m.owner != nil {
			owner = m.owner.uid
		}
		w.u32(owner)
		writeWaiters(w, m.waiters)
	}
	w.u32(uint32(len(evfs)))
	for _, e := range evfs {
		w.u32(e.uid)
		w.str(e.name)
		w.u32(e.attr)
		w.u32(e.initPat)
		w.u32(e.pattern)
		writeWaiters(w, e.waiters)
	}
	w.u32(uint32(len(cbs)))
	for _, c := range cbs {
		w.u32(c.uid)
		w.str(c.name)
		w.u32(c.fn)
		w.u32(c.arg)
		var owner uint32
		if c.thread != nil {
			owner = c.thread.uid
		}
		w.u32(owner)
		w.i32(c.notifyArg)
	}
	w.u32(uint32(len(lwms)))
	for _, l := range lwms {
		w.u32(l.uid)
		w.str(l.name)
		w.u32(l.attr)
		w.i32(l.initCount)
		w.u32(l.workarea)
		writeWaiters(w, l.waiters)
	}

	w.i32(k.nextGeID)
	geIDs := make([]int32, 0, len(k.geLists))
	for id := range k.geLists {
		geIDs = append(geIDs, id)
	}
	sort.Slice(geIDs, func(i, j int) bool { return geIDs[i] < geIDs[j] })
	w.u32(uint32(len(geIDs)))
	for _, id := range geIDs {
		l := k.geLists[id]
		w.i32(l.id)
		w.u32(uint32(l.state))
		w.u32(l.stallAddr)
	}

	w.i32(int32(k.nextFD))
	fdIDs := make([]int, 0, len(k.fds))
	for id := range k.fds {
		fdIDs = append(fdIDs, id)
	}
	sort.Ints(fdIDs)
	w.u32(uint32(len(fdIDs)))
	for _, id := range fdIDs {
		f := k.fds[id]
		w.i32(int32(id))
		w.boolean(f.isDir)
		w.boolean(f.writing)
		w.boolean(f.fromMS)
		w.str(f.keyPrefix)
		w.str(f.isoPath)
		w.str(f.msKey)
		w.i64(f.pos)
		w.u32(uint32(len(f.dirNames)))
		for _, n := range f.dirNames {
			w.str(n)
		}
		w.i32(int32(f.dirIdx))
		w.str(f.dirPath)
	}

	// sceAudio block (version 3).
	w.u64(k.audioMixed)
	w.u32(uint32(len(k.audioOut)))
	for _, s := range k.audioOut {
		w.i16(s)
	}
	w.i32(k.audioRoutingMode)
	w.i32(k.audioRoutingVolMode)
	for i := range k.audioChans {
		c := &k.audioChans[i]
		w.boolean(c.reserved)
		w.u32(c.sampleCount)
		w.u32(c.format)
		w.i32(c.leftVol)
		w.i32(c.rightVol)
		w.u32(c.addr)
		w.u32(c.remaining)
		var waiterUID uint32
		if c.waiter != nil {
			waiterUID = c.waiter.uid
		}
		w.u32(waiterUID)
		w.u32(c.waitAddr)
		w.i32(c.waitLeftVol)
		w.i32(c.waitRightVol)
	}
	return w.buf
}

func writeWaiters(w *stateWriter, ts []*Thread) {
	w.u32(uint32(len(ts)))
	for _, t := range ts {
		w.u32(t.uid)
	}
}

func (k *Kernel) syncObjects() (semas []*semaObj, mutexes []*mutexObj, evfs []*eventFlagObj, cbs []*callbackObj, lwms []*lwMutexObj) {
	for _, o := range k.objects {
		switch obj := o.(type) {
		case *semaObj:
			semas = append(semas, obj)
		case *mutexObj:
			mutexes = append(mutexes, obj)
		case *eventFlagObj:
			evfs = append(evfs, obj)
		case *callbackObj:
			cbs = append(cbs, obj)
		case *lwMutexObj:
			lwms = append(lwms, obj)
		}
	}
	sort.Slice(semas, func(i, j int) bool { return semas[i].uid < semas[j].uid })
	sort.Slice(mutexes, func(i, j int) bool { return mutexes[i].uid < mutexes[j].uid })
	sort.Slice(evfs, func(i, j int) bool { return evfs[i].uid < evfs[j].uid })
	sort.Slice(cbs, func(i, j int) bool { return cbs[i].uid < cbs[j].uid })
	sort.Slice(lwms, func(i, j int) bool { return lwms[i].uid < lwms[j].uid })
	return semas, mutexes, evfs, cbs, lwms
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize into this
// kernel. The host (memory contents, CPU, ISO, memory stick store)
// is restored by the system around this call; the loaded thread's
// context is re-deserialized into the CPU at the end when one was
// running.
func (k *Kernel) Deserialize(data []byte) error {
	r := &stateReader{buf: data}
	if string(r.take(4)) != kernelStateMagic {
		return errors.New("kernel: bad state magic")
	}
	if v := r.u32(); v != kernelStateVersion {
		return errors.New("kernel: unsupported kernel state version")
	}
	k.cycles = r.u64()
	k.vcount = r.u32()
	k.exited = r.boolean()
	k.exitCode = r.i32()
	k.uidSeq = r.u32()
	k.seq = r.u64()
	k.nextCode = r.u32()
	k.sdkVersion = r.u32()
	k.exitCallbackUID = r.u32()
	k.bootPath = r.str()
	k.moduleBlockUID = r.u32()
	k.moduleBase = r.u32()
	k.moduleSize = r.u32()
	for i := range k.dispMode {
		k.dispMode[i] = r.u32()
	}
	k.dispSet = r.boolean()
	k.samplingCtl = r.u32()
	k.console = r.bytes()

	k.unknown = map[modNid]*UnknownCall{}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		u := &UnknownCall{Module: r.str(), NID: r.u32(), Count: int(r.u32())}
		k.unknown[modNid{u.Module, u.NID}] = u
	}

	k.assigned = map[modNid]uint32{}
	k.codes = map[uint32]*syscallEntry{}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		key := modNid{r.str(), r.u32()}
		code := r.u32()
		k.assigned[key] = code
		if e, ok := registry[key]; ok {
			cp := e
			k.codes[code] = &cp
		} else {
			k.codes[code] = nil
		}
	}

	k.objects = map[uint32]object{}
	k.part = newPartition(UserPartitionBase, UserPartitionSize)
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		b := &memBlock{uid: r.u32(), name: r.str(), addr: r.u32(), size: r.u32()}
		k.part.blocks = append(k.part.blocks, b)
		k.objects[b.uid] = b
	}
	sort.Slice(k.part.blocks, func(i, j int) bool { return k.part.blocks[i].addr < k.part.blocks[j].addr })

	k.threads = map[uint32]*Thread{}
	k.order = nil
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		th := &Thread{}
		th.uid = r.u32()
		th.name = r.str()
		th.entry = r.u32()
		th.attr = r.u32()
		th.initPriority = r.i32()
		th.priority = r.i32()
		th.state = threadState(r.u8())
		th.stackAddr = r.u32()
		th.stackSize = r.u32()
		th.stackBlock = r.u32()
		th.exitStatus = r.i32()
		th.runCycles = r.u64()
		th.wait = waitKind(r.u8())
		th.waitUID = r.u32()
		th.waitDeadline = r.u64()
		th.waitPattern = r.u32()
		th.waitMode = r.u32()
		th.waitResultAt = r.u32()
		th.waitCount = r.i32()
		th.seq = r.u64()
		th.waitResult = r.i32()
		th.hasResult = r.boolean()
		th.loaded = r.boolean()
		th.ctx = r.bytes()
		k.threads[th.uid] = th
		k.order = append(k.order, th)
		k.objects[th.uid] = th
	}
	currentUID := r.u32()
	k.current = nil
	if currentUID != 0 {
		k.current = k.threads[currentUID]
	}

	readWaiters := func() []*Thread {
		n := int(r.u32())
		out := make([]*Thread, 0, n)
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			if th, ok := k.threads[r.u32()]; ok {
				out = append(out, th)
			}
		}
		return out
	}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		s := &semaObj{}
		s.uid = r.u32()
		s.name = r.str()
		s.attr = r.u32()
		s.initVal = r.i32()
		s.maxVal = r.i32()
		s.cur = r.i32()
		s.waiters = readWaiters()
		k.objects[s.uid] = s
	}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		m := &mutexObj{}
		m.uid = r.u32()
		m.name = r.str()
		m.attr = r.u32()
		m.initCount = r.i32()
		m.lockCount = r.i32()
		owner := r.u32()
		if owner != 0 {
			m.owner = k.threads[owner]
		}
		m.waiters = readWaiters()
		k.objects[m.uid] = m
	}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		e := &eventFlagObj{}
		e.uid = r.u32()
		e.name = r.str()
		e.attr = r.u32()
		e.initPat = r.u32()
		e.pattern = r.u32()
		e.waiters = readWaiters()
		k.objects[e.uid] = e
	}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		c := &callbackObj{}
		c.uid = r.u32()
		c.name = r.str()
		c.fn = r.u32()
		c.arg = r.u32()
		owner := r.u32()
		if owner != 0 {
			c.thread = k.threads[owner]
		}
		c.notifyArg = r.i32()
		k.objects[c.uid] = c
	}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		l := &lwMutexObj{}
		l.uid = r.u32()
		l.name = r.str()
		l.attr = r.u32()
		l.initCount = r.i32()
		l.workarea = r.u32()
		l.waiters = readWaiters()
		k.objects[l.uid] = l
	}

	k.nextGeID = r.i32()
	k.geLists = map[int32]*geList{}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		l := &geList{id: r.i32(), state: ge.ListState(r.u32()), stallAddr: r.u32()}
		k.geLists[l.id] = l
	}

	k.nextFD = int(r.i32())
	k.fds = map[int]*fileDesc{}
	for n := int(r.u32()); n > 0; n-- {
		id := int(r.i32())
		f := &fileDesc{}
		f.isDir = r.boolean()
		f.writing = r.boolean()
		f.fromMS = r.boolean()
		f.keyPrefix = r.str()
		f.isoPath = r.str()
		f.msKey = r.str()
		f.pos = r.i64()
		for m := int(r.u32()); m > 0; m-- {
			f.dirNames = append(f.dirNames, r.str())
		}
		f.dirIdx = int(r.i32())
		f.dirPath = r.str()
		k.fds[id] = f
	}

	// sceAudio block (version 3).
	k.audioMixed = r.u64()
	if n := int(r.u32()); n > 0 {
		k.audioOut = make([]int16, n)
		for i := range k.audioOut {
			k.audioOut[i] = int16(uint16(r.u32()))
		}
	} else {
		k.audioOut = nil
	}
	k.audioRoutingMode = r.i32()
	k.audioRoutingVolMode = r.i32()
	for i := range k.audioChans {
		c := &k.audioChans[i]
		c.reserved = r.boolean()
		c.sampleCount = r.u32()
		c.format = r.u32()
		c.leftVol = r.i32()
		c.rightVol = r.i32()
		c.addr = r.u32()
		c.remaining = r.u32()
		waiterUID := r.u32()
		c.waitAddr = r.u32()
		c.waitLeftVol = r.i32()
		c.waitRightVol = r.i32()
		c.waiter = nil
		if waiterUID != 0 {
			c.waiter = k.threads[waiterUID]
		}
	}
	if r.err != nil {
		return r.err
	}
	if r.pos != len(r.buf) {
		return errors.New("kernel: trailing bytes in state blob")
	}
	// Reinstall the hook (a fresh kernel object may have been used).
	k.cpu.SyscallHook = k.handleSyscall
	if k.current != nil && k.current.loaded {
		if err := k.cpu.Deserialize(k.current.ctx); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/sync.go ====================

package kernel

import "sort"

// Synchronization objects and the wake evaluation rules. Waiters
// are always considered in (priority, wait order) sequence, which
// is the order this kernel wakes them in.

type semaObj struct {
	uid     uint32
	name    string
	attr    uint32
	initVal int32
	maxVal  int32
	cur     int32
	waiters []*Thread
}

func (s *semaObj) objKind() uint32 { return kindSema }

type mutexObj struct {
	uid       uint32
	name      string
	attr      uint32
	initCount int32
	lockCount int32
	owner     *Thread
	waiters   []*Thread
}

func (m *mutexObj) objKind() uint32 { return kindMutex }

// mutexAttrRecursive is the documented recursive attribute bit for
// sceKernelCreateMutex (PSP_MUTEX_ATTR_RECURSIVE).
const mutexAttrRecursive = 0x400

type eventFlagObj struct {
	uid     uint32
	name    string
	attr    uint32
	initPat uint32
	pattern uint32
	waiters []*Thread
}

func (e *eventFlagObj) objKind() uint32 { return kindEventF }

// Event flag wait mode bits (pspsdk pspthreadman.h).
const (
	evfWaitOr       = 0x01 // PSP_EVENT_WAITOR (AND is 0)
	evfWaitClearAll = 0x10 // PSP_EVENT_WAITCLEARALL
	evfWaitClearPat = 0x20 // PSP_EVENT_WAITCLEAR_PAT
	evfAttrMulti    = 0x200
)

type callbackObj struct {
	uid       uint32
	name      string
	fn        uint32
	arg       uint32
	thread    *Thread
	notifyArg int32
	// Callbacks are registered and counted but never dispatched in
	// this slice: no exit or UMD event source exists to fire them.
}

func (c *callbackObj) objKind() uint32 { return kindCallback }

// lwMutexObj is a lightweight mutex. Unlike the UID mutexes, the
// lock state (level and owner) lives in the guest workarea, a
// documented 32 byte structure the kernel reads and writes in
// place: lock level at +0, owning thread UID at +4 (0 = none),
// attribute at +8, waiting thread count at +12, this object's UID
// at +16. The kernel object only tracks the waiter list.
type lwMutexObj struct {
	uid       uint32
	name      string
	attr      uint32
	initCount int32
	workarea  uint32
	waiters   []*Thread
}

func (l *lwMutexObj) objKind() uint32 { return kindLwMutex }

// lwMutexRecursiveMask accepts either published spelling of the
// recursive attribute bit: the kernel headers use 0x200 for the
// lightweight mutex attribute set while older pspsdk documentation
// shows 0x400 for mutexes generally. The guest's own glue writes
// the bit into the workarea attribute at create time.
const lwMutexRecursiveMask = 0x600

// LwMutex workarea field offsets.
const (
	lwOffLevel  = 0
	lwOffOwner  = 4
	lwOffAttr   = 8
	lwOffWaits  = 12
	lwOffUID    = 16
	lwNoSuchUID = 0xFFFFFFFF
)

func (k *Kernel) lwLevel(l *lwMutexObj) int32 { return int32(k.mem.Read32(l.workarea + lwOffLevel)) }
func (k *Kernel) lwOwner(l *lwMutexObj) uint32 {
	return k.mem.Read32(l.workarea + lwOffOwner)
}

func (k *Kernel) lwSetState(l *lwMutexObj, level int32, owner uint32) {
	k.write32(l.workarea+lwOffLevel, uint32(level))
	k.write32(l.workarea+lwOffOwner, owner)
}

func (k *Kernel) lwSetWaitCount(l *lwMutexObj) {
	k.write32(l.workarea+lwOffWaits, uint32(len(l.waiters)))
}

// wakeLwMutexWaiter hands a free lightweight mutex to its first
// live waiter, writing the acquisition into the workarea. Stale
// entries (waits completed by timeout) are dropped.
func (k *Kernel) wakeLwMutexWaiter(l *lwMutexObj) {
	if k.lwLevel(l) != 0 {
		return
	}
	sortWaiters(l.waiters)
	kept := l.waiters[:0]
	done := false
	for _, w := range l.waiters {
		if !done && w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitLwMutex {
			k.lwSetState(l, w.waitCount, w.uid)
			k.completeWait(w, 0)
			k.maybePreempt(w)
			done = true
			continue
		}
		if w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitLwMutex {
			kept = append(kept, w)
		}
	}
	l.waiters = kept
	k.lwSetWaitCount(l)
}

func sortWaiters(ts []*Thread) {
	sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
		if ts[i].priority != ts[j].priority {
			return ts[i].priority < ts[j].priority
		}
		return ts[i].seq < ts[j].seq
	})
}

func removeWaiter(list []*Thread, th *Thread) []*Thread {
	for i, w := range list {
		if w == th {
			return append(list[:i], list[i+1:]...)
		}
	}
	return list
}

// evfPattern returns the current pattern of an event flag object,
// or 0 when the UID is not one.
func (k *Kernel) evfPattern(uid uint32) uint32 {
	if o, ok := k.lookup(uid); ok {
		if e, ok := o.(*eventFlagObj); ok {
			return e.pattern
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// deliverEventFlagResult writes the result pattern a completed (or
// timed out) event flag wait must observe.
func (k *Kernel) deliverEventFlagResult(th *Thread, pattern uint32) {
	if th.waitResultAt != 0 {
		k.write32(th.waitResultAt, pattern)
	}
	th.waitResultAt = 0
}

// tryAcquireSema attempts to take count units for th. It reports
// whether the take succeeded.
func tryAcquireSema(s *semaObj, count int32) bool {
	if s.cur >= count {
		s.cur -= count
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// wakeSemaWaiters satisfies as many waiters of s as the current
// count allows, in (priority, order) sequence.
func (k *Kernel) wakeSemaWaiters(s *semaObj) {
	sortWaiters(s.waiters)
	kept := s.waiters[:0]
	for _, w := range s.waiters {
		if w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitSema && s.cur >= w.waitCount {
			s.cur -= w.waitCount
			k.completeWait(w, 0)
			k.maybePreempt(w)
			continue
		}
		kept = append(kept, w)
	}
	s.waiters = kept
}

// wakeMutexWaiter hands a free mutex to its first waiter, if any.
func (k *Kernel) wakeMutexWaiter(m *mutexObj) {
	if m.lockCount != 0 || len(m.waiters) == 0 {
		return
	}
	sortWaiters(m.waiters)
	w := m.waiters[0]
	m.waiters = m.waiters[1:]
	m.owner = w
	m.lockCount = w.waitCount
	k.completeWait(w, 0)
	k.maybePreempt(w)
}

// evfSatisfied reports whether pattern meets a waiter's condition.
func evfSatisfied(pattern, want, mode uint32) bool {
	if mode&evfWaitOr != 0 {
		return pattern&want != 0
	}
	return pattern&want == want
}

// wakeEventFlagWaiters completes every waiter whose condition the
// flag's current pattern meets, applying each woken waiter's
// clear mode before re-evaluating the next, per the documented
// semantics.
func (k *Kernel) wakeEventFlagWaiters(e *eventFlagObj) {
	sortWaiters(e.waiters)
	kept := e.waiters[:0]
	for _, w := range e.waiters {
		if w.state == thWait && w.wait == waitEventFlag && evfSatisfied(e.pattern, w.waitPattern, w.waitMode) {
			result := e.pattern
			if w.waitMode&evfWaitClearAll != 0 {
				e.pattern = 0
			} else if w.waitMode&evfWaitClearPat != 0 {
				e.pattern &^= w.waitPattern
			}
			k.deliverEventFlagResult(w, result)
			k.completeWait(w, 0)
			k.maybePreempt(w)
			continue
		}
		kept = append(kept, w)
	}
	e.waiters = kept
}

// detachWaiter removes a thread from whatever object wait list it
// sits on (used by terminate and delete paths).
func (k *Kernel) detachWaiter(th *Thread) {
	o, ok := k.lookup(th.waitUID)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	switch obj := o.(type) {
	case *semaObj:
		obj.waiters = removeWaiter(obj.waiters, th)
	case *mutexObj:
		obj.waiters = removeWaiter(obj.waiters, th)
	case *eventFlagObj:
		obj.waiters = removeWaiter(obj.waiters, th)
	case *lwMutexObj:
		obj.waiters = removeWaiter(obj.waiters, th)
		k.lwSetWaitCount(obj)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/kernel/thread.go ====================

package kernel

import (
	"encoding/binary"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex"
)

// Thread states (the simplified documented set; dormant is the
// created-but-not-started state the hardware also distinguishes).
type threadState uint8

const (
	thDormant threadState = iota
	thReady
	thRun
	thWait
	thDead
)

// Wait kinds a thread can be parked in.
type waitKind uint8

const (
	waitNone waitKind = iota
	waitDelay
	waitSleep
	waitSema
	waitMutex
	waitEventFlag
	waitVblank
	waitThreadEnd
	waitLwMutex
	waitAudio
)

// timesliceInsns is the documented timeslice check interval: every
// 10,000 instructions of a running thread, the scheduler checks
// whether an equal or higher priority thread is ready and rotates
// to it if so.
const timesliceInsns = 10000

// Thread is one kernel thread: a saved Allegrex context plus its
// scheduling and wait state.
type Thread struct {
	uid          uint32
	name         string
	entry        uint32
	attr         uint32
	initPriority int32
	priority     int32
	state        threadState

	ctx    []byte // serialized allegrex state while not loaded
	loaded bool

	stackAddr  uint32
	stackSize  uint32
	stackBlock uint32 // partition block UID, 0 for none

	exitStatus int32
	runCycles  uint64

	// Wait state.
	wait         waitKind
	waitUID      uint32
	waitDeadline uint64 // kernel cycle at which a timeout fires; 0 = never
	waitPattern  uint32 // event flag pattern
	waitMode     uint32 // event flag wait mode
	waitResultAt uint32 // address to receive the event flag result pattern
	waitCount    int32  // sema/mutex count requested
	seq          uint64 // order stamp for FIFO within a priority

	blocked     bool  // set by the syscall dispatcher when a handler parks us
	waitResult  int32 // $v0 delivered when the wait completes
	hasResult   bool
	dispatchIns uint64 // instructions run in the current dispatch
}

func (t *Thread) objKind() uint32 { return kindThread }

// UID returns the thread's SceUID.
func (t *Thread) UID() uint32 { return t.uid }

// Name returns the thread's name.
func (t *Thread) Name() string { return t.name }

// createThread builds a dormant thread with a fresh context: PC at
// entry, $sp at the top of its stack minus the documented 256 byte
// kernel reservation, $ra = 0 (the exit trampoline), $gp as given.
func (k *Kernel) createThread(name string, entry uint32, priority int32, stackSize uint32, attr uint32) (*Thread, error) {
	if entry == 0 {
		return nil, errCode(ErrIllegalEntry)
	}
	if priority < 0 || priority > 119 {
		return nil, errCode(ErrIllegalPriority)
	}
	if stackSize != 0 && stackSize < 512 {
		return nil, errCode(ErrIllegalStackSize)
	}
	if stackSize == 0 {
		stackSize = 0x1000
	}
	uid := k.NewUID(kindThread)
	th := &Thread{
		uid:          uid,
		name:         name,
		entry:        entry,
		attr:         attr,
		initPriority: priority,
		priority:     priority,
		state:        thDormant,
	}
	blockUID, addr, err := k.part.allocInternal(k, "stack/"+name, allocHigh, stackSize, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, errCode(ErrMemBlockAllocFailed)
	}
	th.stackBlock = blockUID
	th.stackAddr = addr
	th.stackSize = roundBlockSize(stackSize)
	tmp := allegrex.New(k.mem)
	tmp.Reset(entry)
	tmp.SetSR(allegrex.ThreadStatus)      // firmware thread status (FPU on, RAM vectors)
	tmp.SetFCSR(allegrex.DefaultFCSR)     // firmware FPU control defaults
	tmp.SetReg(29, addr+th.stackSize-256) // $sp below the k0 reservation
	tmp.SetReg(31, 0)                     // $ra: return exits the thread
	th.ctx = tmp.Serialize()
	k.registerObject(uid, th)
	k.threads[uid] = th
	k.order = append(k.order, th)
	return th, nil
}

// startThreadPrepared readies a thread whose context already holds
// its arguments (used for the main thread by LoadModule).
func (k *Kernel) startThreadPrepared(th *Thread, a0, a1, gp uint32) {
	ctxSetReg(th.ctx, 4, a0)
	ctxSetReg(th.ctx, 5, a1)
	ctxSetReg(th.ctx, 28, gp)
	th.state = thReady
	th.seq = k.nextSeq()
}

// ctxSetReg patches one GPR word inside a serialized allegrex
// context. The serialized layout starts with the 32 GPRs.
func ctxSetReg(ctx []byte, reg int, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(ctx[reg*4:], v)
}

func ctxReg(ctx []byte, reg int) uint32 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(ctx[reg*4:])
}

func (k *Kernel) nextSeq() uint64 {
	k.seq++
	return k.seq
}

type errCode uint32

func (e errCode) Error() string { return "kernel error" }

// threadByUID resolves a UID to a thread.
func (k *Kernel) threadByUID(uid uint32) (*Thread, bool) {
	th, ok := k.threads[uid]
	return th, ok
}

// Run advances the kernel by up to budget cycles. It is the
// scheduler's main loop and implements the documented fast
// forward: when no thread is runnable but some thread waits on a
// deadline inside the budget, the sysclock jumps to that deadline;
// when nothing can run at all before the budget ends, the sysclock
// jumps straight to the end of the budget.
func (k *Kernel) Run(budget uint64) {
	if k.exited {
		return
	}
	end := k.cycles + budget
	for k.cycles < end {
		th := k.pickReady(end)
		if th == nil {
			k.cycles = end
			break
		}
		k.dispatch(th, end)
		if k.exited {
			break
		}
		if k.nothingCanRun() {
			k.exited = true
			break
		}
	}
}

// nothingCanRun reports whether no thread can ever make progress
// again: none ready, running, dormant, or waiting on anything the
// machine can deliver (a deadline or a vblank).
func (k *Kernel) nothingCanRun() bool {
	for _, th := range k.order {
		switch th.state {
		case thReady, thRun, thDormant:
			return false
		case thWait:
			if th.waitDeadline != 0 || th.wait == waitVblank {
				return false
			}
		}
	}
	return true
}

// pickReady expires elapsed waits, then returns the highest
// priority ready thread (lowest priority number; FIFO within a
// priority). If none is ready it fast forwards the sysclock to the
// earliest wait deadline within the budget and retries.
func (k *Kernel) pickReady(end uint64) *Thread {
	for {
		k.expireWaits()
		var best *Thread
		for _, th := range k.order {
			if th.state != thReady {
				continue
			}
			if best == nil || th.priority < best.priority ||
				(th.priority == best.priority && th.seq < best.seq) {
				best = th
			}
		}
		if best != nil {
			return best
		}
		next := uint64(0)
		for _, th := range k.order {
			if th.state == thWait && th.waitDeadline != 0 && th.waitDeadline > k.cycles {
				if next == 0 || th.waitDeadline < next {
					next = th.waitDeadline
				}
			}
		}
		if next == 0 || next >= end {
			return nil
		}
		k.cycles = next
	}
}

// expireWaits completes every wait whose deadline has passed, in
// (priority, order) sequence for determinism. Delay waits complete
// successfully; object waits complete with WAIT_TIMEOUT. Audio
// waits have no timeout case: the mixer advancing to the current
// cycle (audioAdvance) completes them with their real result
// when a channel buffer runs out, so it runs first here.
func (k *Kernel) expireWaits() {
	k.audioAdvance()
	var expired []*Thread
	for _, th := range k.order {
		if th.state == thWait && th.waitDeadline != 0 && th.waitDeadline <= k.cycles {
			expired = append(expired, th)
		}
	}
	sortThreads(expired)
	for _, th := range expired {
		switch th.wait {
		case waitDelay, waitSleep:
			k.completeWait(th, 0)
		case waitSema, waitMutex, waitEventFlag, waitThreadEnd, waitLwMutex:
			if th.wait == waitEventFlag {
				k.deliverEventFlagResult(th, k.evfPattern(th.waitUID))
			}
			k.completeWait(th, errResult(ErrWaitTimeout))
		}
	}
}

func sortThreads(ts []*Thread) {
	for i := 1; i < len(ts); i++ {
		for j := i; j > 0; j-- {
			a, b := ts[j-1], ts[j]
			if a.priority < b.priority || (a.priority == b.priority && a.seq < b.seq) {
				break
			}
			ts[j-1], ts[j] = b, a
		}
	}
}

// completeWait readies a waiting thread and records the $v0 it
// will see when next dispatched.
func (k *Kernel) completeWait(th *Thread, result int32) {
	th.state = thReady
	th.wait = waitNone
	th.waitUID = 0
	th.waitDeadline = 0
	th.waitResult = result
	th.hasResult = true
	th.seq = k.nextSeq()
}

// blockCurrent parks the running thread in the given wait and
// tells the dispatcher to switch away.
func (k *Kernel) blockCurrent(th *Thread, w waitKind, uid uint32, deadline uint64) syscallAction {
	th.state = thWait
	th.wait = w
	th.waitUID = uid
	th.waitDeadline = deadline
	th.seq = k.nextSeq()
	return actBlock
}

// deadlineFromTimeout converts a guest timeout pointer (address of
// a microsecond count, 0 for wait forever) into a cycle deadline.
func (k *Kernel) deadlineFromTimeout(th *Thread, timeoutPtr uint32) (deadline uint64, isTimeout bool, timedOutNow bool) {
	if timeoutPtr == 0 {
		return 0, false, false
	}
	us := k.mem.Read32(timeoutPtr)
	if us == 0 {
		return 0, true, true // a zero timeout polls: already expired
	}
	return k.cycles + uint64(us)*CyclesPerMicro, true, false
}

// switchTo loads a thread's context into the shared CPU and
// delivers any pending wait result into $v0.
func (k *Kernel) switchTo(th *Thread) {
	if err := k.cpu.Deserialize(th.ctx); err != nil {
		panic(err) // a context this kernel serialized always parses
	}
	// Returning to a thread passes through the kernel, which
	// breaks any LL reservation the thread held (ERET semantics).
	k.cpu.ClearLL()
	th.loaded = true
	k.current = th
	if th.hasResult {
		k.cpu.SetReg(2, uint32(th.waitResult))
		th.hasResult = false
	}
	th.state = thRun
	th.dispatchIns = 0
}

// saveContext stores the running thread's CPU state back.
func (k *Kernel) saveContext(th *Thread) {
	th.ctx = k.cpu.Serialize()
	th.loaded = false
	if k.current == th {
		k.current = nil
	}
}

// dispatch runs one thread until it blocks, exits, is preempted at
// a scheduling point, or the budget ends.
func (k *Kernel) dispatch(th *Thread, end uint64) {
	k.switchTo(th)
	for k.cycles < end && !k.exited {
		c := k.cpu.Step()
		if c < 1 {
			c = 1
		}
		k.cycles += uint64(c)
		th.runCycles += uint64(c)
		th.dispatchIns++
		if th.state == thDead {
			return // context is dead weight; do not save
		}
		if th.blocked {
			th.blocked = false
			k.saveContext(th)
			return
		}
		if k.cpu.PC() == 0 {
			// Return trampoline: the thread function returned
			// with $ra = 0, which exits the thread with $v0.
			status := int32(k.cpu.Reg(2))
			k.exitThread(th, status, false)
			return
		}
		if k.resched {
			k.resched = false
			k.saveContext(th)
			if th.state == thRun {
				th.state = thReady
				th.seq = k.nextSeq()
			}
			return
		}
		if th.dispatchIns >= timesliceInsns {
			th.dispatchIns = 0
			k.expireWaits()
			if k.readyPeerExists(th) {
				k.saveContext(th)
				th.state = thReady
				th.seq = k.nextSeq()
				return
			}
		}
	}
	if th.state == thRun {
		k.saveContext(th)
		th.state = thReady
		th.seq = k.nextSeq()
	}
}

// readyPeerExists reports whether a ready thread of equal or higher
// priority (numerically lower or equal) exists.
func (k *Kernel) readyPeerExists(th *Thread) bool {
	for _, o := range k.order {
		if o != th && o.state == thReady && o.priority <= th.priority {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// exitThread moves a thread to the dead state, wakes any
// WaitThreadEnd waiters with its status, and handles deletion.
func (k *Kernel) exitThread(th *Thread, status int32, delete bool) {
	th.state = thDead
	th.exitStatus = status
	th.wait = waitNone
	th.waitDeadline = 0
	if th.loaded {
		th.loaded = false
		if k.current == th {
			k.current = nil
		}
	}
	// Wake WaitThreadEnd waiters in priority order.
	var waiters []*Thread
	for _, o := range k.order {
		if o.state == thWait && o.wait == waitThreadEnd && o.waitUID == th.uid {
			waiters = append(waiters, o)
		}
	}
	sortThreads(waiters)
	for _, w := range waiters {
		k.completeWait(w, status)
		k.maybePreempt(w)
	}
	if delete {
		k.deleteThreadObject(th)
	}
}

// deleteThreadObject frees a thread's stack block and removes its
// object registrations.
func (k *Kernel) deleteThreadObject(th *Thread) {
	if th.stackBlock != 0 {
		k.part.free(th.stackBlock)
		k.removeObject(th.stackBlock)
		th.stackBlock = 0
	}
	k.removeObject(th.uid)
	delete(k.threads, th.uid)
	for i, o := range k.order {
		if o == th {
			k.order = append(k.order[:i], k.order[i+1:]...)
			break
		}
	}
}

// maybePreempt asks for a reschedule when a newly readied thread
// outranks the running one.
func (k *Kernel) maybePreempt(woken *Thread) {
	if cur := k.current; cur != nil && woken.priority < cur.priority {
		k.resched = true
	}
}

// NotifyVblank is called by the machine at each frame end: it
// bumps the vblank counter and wakes vblank waiters in priority
// order.
func (k *Kernel) NotifyVblank() {
	k.vcount++
	k.inVblank = true
	var waiters []*Thread
	for _, th := range k.order {
		if th.state == thWait && th.wait == waitVblank {
			waiters = append(waiters, th)
		}
	}
	sortThreads(waiters)
	for _, th := range waiters {
		k.completeWait(th, 0)
	}
	k.inVblank = false
}

// InVblank reports whether vblank waiters are being woken right
// now (the only moment guest code can observe the vblank in this
// frame synchronous model is never; see the README).
func (k *Kernel) InVblank() bool { return k.inVblank }

// errResult reinterprets an unsigned kernel error code as the
// signed $v0 value a completed wait delivers.
func errResult(code uint32) int32 { return int32(code) }

// joypadButtons maps the libretro joypad onto PSP buttons by
// position: Cross is B (bottom), Circle is A (right), Square
// is Y (left), Triangle is X (top).
func joypadButtons() uint32 {
	var b uint32
	pad := func(id uint) bool {
		return C.psp_call_input(0, deviceJoypad, 0, C.uint(id)) != 0
	}
	if pad(joypadB) {
		b |= system.ButtonCross
	}
	if pad(joypadA) {
		b |= system.ButtonCircle
	}
	if pad(joypadY) {
		b |= system.ButtonSquare
	}
	if pad(joypadX) {
		b |= system.ButtonTriangle
	}
	if pad(joypadStart) {
		b |= system.ButtonStart
	}
	if pad(joypadSelect) {
		b |= system.ButtonSelect
	}
	if pad(joypadL) {
		b |= system.ButtonL
	}
	if pad(joypadR) {
		b |= system.ButtonR
	}
	if pad(joypadUp) {
		b |= system.ButtonUp
	}
	if pad(joypadDown) {
		b |= system.ButtonDown
	}
	if pad(joypadLeft) {
		b |= system.ButtonLeft
	}
	if pad(joypadRight) {
		b |= system.ButtonRight
	}
	return b
}

// analogByte converts a libretro axis (-32768..32767) to the
// PSP stick byte (0..255, 0x80 centered).
func analogByte(v int16) byte {
	n := (int32(v) + 32768) >> 8
	if n < 0 {
		n = 0
	}
	if n > 255 {
		n = 255
	}
	return byte(n)
}

// loadPath boots content from a filesystem path.
func loadPath(path string) bool {
	m := system.New()
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".iso":
		if err := m.BootUMD(path); err != nil {
			return false
		}
		mach = m
		loadedPath, loadedData, loadedISO = path, nil, true
		return true
	case ".elf", ".prx":
		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		if err := m.LoadExecutable(data); err != nil {
			return false
		}
		mach = m
		loadedPath, loadedData, loadedISO = path, data, false
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// reboot re-boots the loaded content (retro_reset).
func reboot() bool {
	if loadedPath == "" {
		return false
	}
	m := system.New()
	if loadedISO {
		if err := m.BootUMD(loadedPath); err != nil {
			return false
		}
	} else {
		if err := m.LoadExecutable(loadedData); err != nil {
			return false
		}
	}
	mach = m
	return true
}

// runFrame advances one frame and presents it; factored out of
// retro_run so tests can drive the shell in-process.
func runFrame() {
	if mach == nil {
		return
	}
	C.psp_call_input_poll()
	mach.SetButtons(joypadButtons())
	mach.SetAnalog(
		analogByte(int16(C.psp_call_input(0, deviceAnalog, analogLeft, analogX))),
		analogByte(int16(C.psp_call_input(0, deviceAnalog, analogLeft, analogY))),
	)
	mach.RunFrame()

	fb := mach.Framebuffer()
	w, h := system.Width, system.Height
	if w != lastWidth || h != lastHeight {
		lastWidth, lastHeight = w, h
		geom := C.struct_psp_game_geometry{
			base_width:   C.uint(w),
			base_height:  C.uint(h),
			max_width:    C.uint(w),
			max_height:   C.uint(h),
			aspect_ratio: C.float(float64(w) / float64(h)),
		}
		C.psp_call_environ(envSetGeometry, unsafe.Pointer(&geom))
	}
	C.psp_call_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]), C.uint(w), C.uint(h), C.size_t(framePitch(w)))

	buf := mach.AudioBuffer()
	if len(buf) == 0 {
		return
	}
	n := int(C.psp_call_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&buf[0])), C.size_t(len(buf)/2)))
	if n < 0 {
		n = 0
	}
	for i := n * 2; i+1 < len(buf); i += 2 {
		C.psp_call_audio(C.int16_t(buf[i]), C.int16_t(buf[i+1]))
	}
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() { runFrame() }

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if mach == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(mach.StateSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) C.int {
	if mach == nil {
		return 0
	}
	state := mach.Serialize()
	if int(size) < len(state) {
		return 0
	}
	dst := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), int(size))
	copy(dst, state)
	return 1
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) C.int {
	if mach == nil {
		return 0
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), int(size))
	if err := mach.Deserialize(buf); err != nil {
		return 0
	}
	return 1
}

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.uint) unsafe.Pointer {
	if mach == nil {
		return nil
	}
	switch id {
	case memorySysRAM:
		return unsafe.Pointer(&mach.Bus.RAM[0])
	case memorySaveRAM:
		// PSP saves flow through the host installed ms0:
		// store; there is no fixed backing slice to expose.
		return nil
	}
	return nil
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.uint) C.size_t {
	if mach == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memorySysRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(mach.Bus.RAM))
	case memorySaveRAM:
		return 0
	}
	return 0
}

// In-process shell gates: the libretro contract (info, AV,
// memory, serialize) plus both load paths and clean rejection
// of bad images, driven through loadPath/runFrame directly.

func writeTemp(t *testing.T, name string, data []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), name)
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return path
}

	}
	if exts != "iso|elf|prx" {
		t.Fatalf("valid extensions = %q, want %q", exts, "iso|elf|prx")
	}

func TestShellLoadISOAndRun(t *testing.T) {
	defer retro_unload_game()
	path := writeTemp(t, "engine.iso", enginetest.ISOImage())
	if !loadPath(path) {
		t.Fatal("loadPath(.iso) failed")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	if mach == nil {
		t.Fatal("no machine after load")
	}
	if got := mach.Bus.Read32(enginetest.MilestoneAddr + enginetest.OffProgress); got != enginetest.MilestoneFinal {
		t.Fatalf("progress = %d, want %d", got, enginetest.MilestoneFinal)
	}
	if got := mach.ConsoleOutput(); got != enginetest.ConsoleText {
		t.Fatalf("console = %q, want %q", got, enginetest.ConsoleText)
	}
	fb := mach.Framebuffer()
	if got := fb[10*system.Width+10]; got != enginetest.SpritePixel {
		t.Fatalf("sprite pixel = %#08x, want %#08x", got, enginetest.SpritePixel)
	}
	if got := fb[0]; got != enginetest.ClearPixel {
		t.Fatalf("clear pixel = %#08x, want %#08x", got, enginetest.ClearPixel)
	}
	// Memory contract: SYSTEM_RAM is the 32 MB main RAM,
	// SAVE_RAM is nil/0 (the ms0: store has no fixed backing).
	if got := retro_get_memory_size(memorySysRAM); got != 32<<20 {
		t.Fatalf("SYSTEM_RAM size = %d, want %d", got, 32<<20)
	}
	if got := retro_get_memory_size(memorySaveRAM); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("SAVE_RAM size = %d, want 0", got)
	}
	if p := retro_get_memory_data(memorySaveRAM); p != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SAVE_RAM data = %v, want nil", p)
	}
	if p := retro_get_memory_data(memorySysRAM); p == nil {
		t.Fatal("SYSTEM_RAM data is nil")
	}
}

func TestShellSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	defer retro_unload_game()
	path := writeTemp(t, "engine.iso", enginetest.ISOImage())
	if !loadPath(path) {
		t.Fatal("loadPath failed")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 20; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	size := retro_serialize_size()
	if size == 0 {
		t.Fatal("serialize size is 0 after load")
	}
	buf := make([]byte, size)
	if retro_serialize(unsafe.Pointer(&buf[0]), size) != 1 {
		t.Fatal("retro_serialize failed")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	if retro_unserialize(unsafe.Pointer(&buf[0]), size) != 1 {
		t.Fatal("retro_unserialize failed")
	}
	want := mach.Serialize()
	if !bytes.Equal(buf, want) {
		t.Fatal("state after unserialize differs from the serialized bytes")
	}
	// Reset re-boots the loaded content.
	retro_reset()
	if got := mach.Bus.Read32(enginetest.MilestoneAddr + enginetest.OffProgress); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("progress after reset = %d, want 0 (fresh boot)", got)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	if got := mach.Bus.Read32(enginetest.MilestoneAddr + enginetest.OffProgress); got != enginetest.MilestoneFinal {
		t.Fatalf("progress after reset + 100 frames = %d, want %d", got, enginetest.MilestoneFinal)
	}
}

func TestShellRejectsBadImages(t *testing.T) {
	defer retro_unload_game()
	iso := enginetest.ISOImage()
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		data []byte
		file string
	}{
		{"garbage iso", []byte("this is not an ISO image at all"), "bad.iso"},
		{"truncated iso", iso[:len(iso)/2], "trunc.iso"},
		{"garbage elf", []byte{0x7F, 'E', 'L', 'F', 1, 2, 3}, "bad.elf"},
		{"empty prx", nil, "empty.prx"},
		{"wrong extension", iso, "game.bin"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		if loadPath(writeTemp(t, c.file, c.data)) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: loadPath succeeded, want clean rejection", c.name)
		}
	}
	// A well-formed ISO whose SYSDR holds no boot executable:
	// rename BOOT.BIN in the directory data.
	noBoot := append([]byte{}, iso...)
	idx := bytes.Index(noBoot, []byte("BOOT.BIN;1"))
	if idx < 0 {
		t.Fatal("fixture ISO does not contain BOOT.BIN;1")
	}
	noBoot[idx] = 'X'
	if loadPath(writeTemp(t, "noboot.iso", noBoot)) {
		t.Fatal("ISO without BOOT.BIN/EBOOT.BIN loaded, want clean rejection")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/load/load.go ====================

// Package load parses and loads PSP executables: static ET_EXEC
// ELFs and relocatable PRX modules (ET_SCE_EXEC), as produced by
// the open PSP toolchain. It implements the documented module
// format (the TyRaNiD "Naked PSP" overview and the pspsdk
// headers): program headers carry the segments, relocation
// sections of type 0x700000A0 carry Elf32_Rel entries in module
// address space, the .rodata.sceModuleInfo section describes the
// module, and the .lib.stub tables plus .rodata.sceResident and
// .rodata.sceNid carry the library imports.
//
// The loader only places bytes and applies relocations. Resolving
// imports (assigning syscall numbers and patching the stub code)
// is the kernel's job; the loader reports every import it found.
package load

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// Memory is the byte addressed store the loader writes into. The
// system bus satisfies it.
type Memory interface {
	Read8(addr uint32) uint8
	Read16(addr uint32) uint16
	Read32(addr uint32) uint32
	Write8(addr uint32, value uint8)
	Write16(addr uint32, value uint16)
	Write32(addr uint32, value uint32)
}

// Import is one library function (or variable) a module imports.
// StubAddr is the loaded address of the stub code for a function
// import: an 8 byte stub whose first word is JR $ra (0x03E00008)
// and whose second word, the jump delay slot, is where the kernel
// patches the SYSCALL instruction it assigns to this import. The
// stub table's funcTable field points directly at the stub code
// block (the .sceStub.text section), so the stub for function j
// sits at funcTable + 8*j; there is no pointer array. Variable
// imports carry StubAddr 0: they have no stub code.
type Import struct {
	Module   string
	NID      uint32
	StubAddr uint32
	IsVar    bool
}

// Module is a loaded executable image.
type Module struct {
	Name        string
	Attr        uint32
	GP          uint32 // final (relocated) $gp value from the module info
	Entry       uint32 // final entry address (module_start)
	Base        uint32 // load base (0 for fixed ET_EXEC images)
	Size        uint32 // resident size in bytes (segments extent)
	Relocatable bool
	Imports     []Import
}

// ELF constants used by the PSP formats.
const (
	etExec    = 2
	etSceExec = 0xFFA0
	etSceRel  = 0xFFA1
	ptLoad    = 1
	shtRel    = 9
	// shtPRXReloc is the PSP relocation section type.
	shtPRXReloc = 0x700000A0
)

// MIPS relocation types implemented (the documented PRX subset).
const (
	rNone    = 0
	r32      = 2
	r26      = 4
	rHi16    = 5
	rLo16    = 6
	rGPrel16 = 7
)

type phdr struct {
	typ, off, vaddr, paddr, filesz, memsz uint32
}

type shdr struct {
	name, typ, flags, addr, off, size, link, info, entsize uint32
}

type elfFile struct {
	data        []byte
	typ         uint16
	entry       uint32
	phdrs       []phdr
	shdrs       []shdr
	shstrndx    int
	relocatable bool
}

// Probe reports the resident size of the module image and whether
// it is relocatable, without loading anything. The caller uses
// the size to reserve a load base for a PRX module.
func Probe(data []byte) (size uint32, relocatable bool, err error) {
	f, err := parse(data)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, false, err
	}
	extent := segmentsExtent(f.phdrs)
	if extent == 0 {
		return 0, false, errors.New("load: no PT_LOAD segments")
	}
	return extent, f.relocatable, nil
}

// segmentsExtent is the resident size of the PT_LOAD segments: the
// span from the lowest segment vaddr to the highest segment end.
// For a relocatable module (vaddrs based at 0) it is simply the
// highest end; for a fixed ET_EXEC image it strips the link base.
func segmentsExtent(phdrs []phdr) uint32 {
	lo := uint32(0xFFFFFFFF)
	var hi uint32
	for _, p := range phdrs {
		if p.typ != ptLoad {
			continue
		}
		if p.vaddr < lo {
			lo = p.vaddr
		}
		if end := p.vaddr + p.memsz; end > hi {
			hi = end
		}
	}
	if lo == 0xFFFFFFFF {
		return 0
	}
	return hi - lo
}

func parse(data []byte) (*elfFile, error) {
	if len(data) < 52 {
		return nil, errors.New("load: file too short for an ELF header")
	}
	if data[0] != 0x7F || data[1] != 'E' || data[2] != 'L' || data[3] != 'F' {
		return nil, errors.New("load: not an ELF file")
	}
	if data[4] != 1 || data[5] != 1 {
		return nil, errors.New("load: not a 32 bit little endian ELF")
	}
	typ := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(data[16:])
	machine := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(data[18:])
	if machine != 8 { // EM_MIPS
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load: ELF machine %d, want MIPS (8)", machine)
	}
	f := &elfFile{data: data, typ: typ, shstrndx: int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(data[50:]))}
	switch typ {
	case etExec:
		f.relocatable = false
	case 1, etSceExec, etSceRel:
		f.relocatable = true
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("load: unsupported ELF type %#x", typ)
	}
	f.entry = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[24:])
	phoff := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[28:])
	shoff := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[32:])
	phnum := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(data[44:]))
	shnum := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(data[48:]))
	for i := 0; i < phnum; i++ {
		off := int(phoff) + i*32
		if off+32 > len(data) {
			return nil, errors.New("load: program header out of range")
		}
		b := data[off:]
		f.phdrs = append(f.phdrs, phdr{
			typ:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[0:]),
			off:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[4:]),
			vaddr:  binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[8:]),
			paddr:  binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[12:]),
			filesz: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[16:]),
			memsz:  binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[20:]),
		})
	}
	for i := 0; i < shnum; i++ {
		off := int(shoff) + i*40
		if off+40 > len(data) {
			return nil, errors.New("load: section header out of range")
		}
		b := data[off:]
		f.shdrs = append(f.shdrs, shdr{
			name:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[0:]),
			typ:     binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[4:]),
			flags:   binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[8:]),
			addr:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[12:]),
			off:     binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[16:]),
			size:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[20:]),
			link:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[24:]),
			info:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[28:]),
			entsize: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[36:]),
		})
	}
	return f, nil
}

func (f *elfFile) sectionByName(want string) *shdr {
	if f.shstrndx >= len(f.shdrs) {
		return nil
	}
	strSec := f.shdrs[f.shstrndx]
	for i := range f.shdrs {
		start := int(strSec.off + f.shdrs[i].name)
		if start < 0 || start >= len(f.data) {
			continue
		}
		end := start
		for end < len(f.data) && f.data[end] != 0 {
			end++
		}
		if string(f.data[start:end]) == want {
			return &f.shdrs[i]
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// Load copies the module into mem. For a relocatable module the
// segments land at base + p_vaddr and all internal pointers are
// relocated into that address range; for ET_EXEC the segments
// land at their linked addresses and base is ignored (pass 0).
// Relocations are applied in place, then the module info and
// import tables are read back from memory, so every pointer the
// returned Module carries is a final loaded address.
func Load(mem Memory, data []byte, base uint32) (*Module, error) {
	f, err := parse(data)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !f.relocatable {
		base = 0
	}
	extent := segmentsExtent(f.phdrs)
	segBases := make([]uint32, len(f.phdrs))
	for i, p := range f.phdrs {
		if p.typ != ptLoad {
			continue
		}
		dest := base + p.vaddr
		segBases[i] = dest
		if int64(p.off)+int64(p.filesz) > int64(len(data)) {
			return nil, errors.New("load: segment file range out of bounds")
		}
		for j := uint32(0); j < p.filesz; j++ {
			mem.Write8(dest+j, data[p.off+j])
		}
		for j := p.filesz; j < p.memsz; j++ {
			mem.Write8(dest+j, 0)
		}
	}
	if extent == 0 {
		return nil, errors.New("load: no PT_LOAD segments")
	}
	m := &Module{Base: base, Size: extent, Relocatable: f.relocatable}
	m.Entry = f.entry
	if f.relocatable {
		m.Entry = base + f.entry
		if err := f.applyRelocations(mem, base, segBases); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
	if err := f.readModuleInfo(mem, base, m); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return m, nil
}

// applyRelocations walks every PSP relocation section and patches
// the loaded image. Per the documented PRX format, r_info packs
// three fields: the MIPS relocation type in bits 0..7, the OFS_BASE
// segment index in bits 8..15 (r_offset is an offset from that
// segment, so the patch target is segBases[OFS_BASE] + r_offset),
// and the ADDR_BASE segment index in bits 16..23 (the stored value
// is an address inside that segment, so the addend base added to
// it is segBases[ADDR_BASE]). Single segment modules, which is
// what the toolchain emits for user programs, have both indices 0
// and a segment vaddr of 0, reducing both to the load base.
func (f *elfFile) applyRelocations(mem Memory, base uint32, segBases []uint32) error {
	for _, s := range f.shdrs {
		if s.typ != shtPRXReloc && s.typ != shtRel {
			continue
		}
		if s.entsize != 8 && s.entsize != 0 {
			return fmt.Errorf("load: relocation entry size %d, want 8", s.entsize)
		}
		type hiPend struct {
			addr uint32
			seg  uint32 // ADDR_BASE of the HI16 entry
		}
		var pending []hiPend
		n := int(s.size / 8)
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			off := int(s.off) + i*8
			if off+8 > len(f.data) {
				return errors.New("load: relocation entry out of range")
			}
			rOff := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(f.data[off:])
			rInfo := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(f.data[off+4:])
			rtyp := rInfo & 0xFF
			ofsSeg := (rInfo >> 8) & 0xFF
			addrSeg := (rInfo >> 16) & 0xFF
			if int(ofsSeg) >= len(segBases) || int(addrSeg) >= len(segBases) {
				return fmt.Errorf("load: relocation segment %d/%d out of range", ofsSeg, addrSeg)
			}
			addr := segBases[ofsSeg] + rOff
			addBase := segBases[addrSeg]
			switch rtyp {
			case rNone:
			case r32:
				mem.Write32(addr, mem.Read32(addr)+addBase)
			case r26:
				w := mem.Read32(addr)
				target := ((w & 0x3FFFFFF) << 2) + addBase
				mem.Write32(addr, (w&0xFC000000)|((target>>2)&0x3FFFFFF))
			case rHi16:
				pending = append(pending, hiPend{addr, addrSeg})
			case rLo16:
				w := mem.Read32(addr)
				alo := int32(int16(w & 0xFFFF))
				var ahi int32
				if len(pending) > 0 {
					ahi = int32(mem.Read32(pending[0].addr) & 0xFFFF)
					addBase = segBases[pending[0].seg]
				}
				t := uint32((ahi<<16)+alo) + addBase
				lo := t & 0xFFFF
				mem.Write32(addr, (w&0xFFFF0000)|lo)
				hi := (t - uint32(int32(int16(lo)))) >> 16
				for _, p := range pending {
					hw := mem.Read32(p.addr)
					mem.Write32(p.addr, (hw&0xFFFF0000)|(hi&0xFFFF))
				}
				pending = nil
			case rGPrel16:
				// GP relative offsets are invariant under a
				// uniform base shift: both the target and $gp
				// move by the same base, and the module info gp
				// the loader relocates carries the same shift.
				// The entry is validated and left unchanged.
			default:
				return fmt.Errorf("load: unsupported relocation type %d at offset %#x", rtyp, rOff)
			}
		}
		// A HI16 with no following LO16 in its section is paired
		// with a zero low half. Compiler output always pairs them
		// inside one section; this is only a guard.
		for _, p := range pending {
			w := mem.Read32(p.addr)
			t := uint32(int32(w&0xFFFF)<<16) + segBases[p.seg]
			lo := t & 0xFFFF
			hi := (t - uint32(int32(int16(lo)))) >> 16
			mem.Write32(p.addr, (w&0xFFFF0000)|(hi&0xFFFF))
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// SceModuleInfo field offsets (pspsdk pspmoduleinfo.h): the name
// is 27 bytes at +4, gp at +0x20, the export table range at
// +0x24/+0x28, the stub table range at +0x2C/+0x30.
// SceLibraryStubTable is 20 bytes: name u32 @0, version u16 @4,
// attribute u16 @6, entrySize u8 @8 (in words; tables advance by
// entrySize*4 when it is nonzero), varCount u8 @9, funcCount
// u16 @10, nidTable u32 @12, funcTable u32 @16. Function imports
// occupy the first funcCount entries of the NID table; variable
// import NIDs follow them. funcTable points at the stub code
// block itself: stub j is the 8 bytes at funcTable + 8*j.
func (f *elfFile) readModuleInfo(mem Memory, base uint32, m *Module) error {
	var infoAddr uint32
	if s := f.sectionByName(".rodata.sceModuleInfo"); s != nil {
		infoAddr = base + s.addr
	} else if len(f.phdrs) > 0 && f.phdrs[0].paddr >= f.phdrs[0].off && f.phdrs[0].paddr != 0 {
		// Fallback seen in toolchain output: the first segment's
		// p_paddr is the file offset of the module info.
		p := f.phdrs[0]
		infoAddr = base + p.vaddr + (p.paddr - p.off)
	} else {
		return errors.New("load: no .rodata.sceModuleInfo section")
	}
	m.Attr = mem.Read32(infoAddr)
	nameBytes := make([]byte, 0, 27)
	for i := 0; i < 27; i++ {
		b := mem.Read8(infoAddr + 4 + uint32(i))
		if b == 0 {
			break
		}
		nameBytes = append(nameBytes, b)
	}
	m.Name = string(nameBytes)
	m.GP = mem.Read32(infoAddr + 0x20)
	stubTop := mem.Read32(infoAddr + 0x2C)
	stubEnd := mem.Read32(infoAddr + 0x30)
	if stubEnd < stubTop || stubEnd-stubTop > 1<<16 {
		return fmt.Errorf("load: bad stub table range %#x..%#x", stubTop, stubEnd)
	}
	for a := stubTop; a+20 <= stubEnd; {
		namePtr := mem.Read32(a + 0)
		entrySize := int(mem.Read8(a + 8))
		varCount := int(mem.Read8(a + 9))
		funcCount := int(mem.Read16(a + 10))
		nidPtr := mem.Read32(a + 12)
		funcPtr := mem.Read32(a + 16)
		libName := readCString(mem, namePtr)
		for j := 0; j < funcCount; j++ {
			m.Imports = append(m.Imports, Import{
				Module:   libName,
				NID:      mem.Read32(nidPtr + uint32(4*j)),
				StubAddr: funcPtr + uint32(8*j),
			})
		}
		for j := 0; j < varCount; j++ {
			m.Imports = append(m.Imports, Import{
				Module: libName,
				NID:    mem.Read32(nidPtr + uint32(4*(funcCount+j))),
				IsVar:  true,
			})
		}
		step := 20
		if entrySize > 0 {
			step = entrySize * 4
		}
		a += uint32(step)
	}
	return nil
}

func readCString(mem Memory, addr uint32) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		b := mem.Read8(addr + uint32(i))
		if b == 0 {
			break
		}
		sb.WriteByte(b)
	}
	return sb.String()
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/load/load_test.go ====================

package load

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// mapMem is a byte slice backed Memory window for the tests.
type mapMem struct {
	base uint32
	data []byte
}

func newMapMem(base uint32, size int) *mapMem {
	return &mapMem{base: base, data: make([]byte, size)}
}

func (m *mapMem) off(addr uint32) int { return int(addr - m.base) }

func (m *mapMem) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 { return m.data[m.off(addr)] }

func (m *mapMem) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(m.data[m.off(addr):])
}

func (m *mapMem) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(m.data[m.off(addr):])
}

func (m *mapMem) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) { m.data[m.off(addr)] = v }

func (m *mapMem) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(m.data[m.off(addr):], v)
}

func (m *mapMem) Write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(m.data[m.off(addr):], v)
}

// Test module layout in module address space (offsets from the
// segment base):
//
//	0x0000 .text: a few code words (tests patch some of them)
//	0x0200 .rodata.sceModuleInfo (64 bytes)
//	0x0300 .lib.stub: one SceLibraryStubTable (20 bytes)
//	0x0340 stub code block: two 8 byte stubs
//	0x0380 .rodata.sceResident: library name string
//	0x03A0 .rodata.sceNid: two function NIDs
//	0x0400 a data word the tests relocate
const (
	modTextOff   = 0x0000
	modInfoOff   = 0x0200
	modStubT_off = 0x0300
	modStubsOff  = 0x0340
	modNameOff   = 0x0380
	modNidOff    = 0x03A0
	modDataOff   = 0x0400
	modSegSize   = 0x1000
)

type reloc struct {
	off uint32
	typ uint32
	seg uint32
}

type elfOpts struct {
	typ    uint16 // ELF e_type
	link   uint32 // segment link address (vaddr base in the file)
	relocs []reloc
}

func buildTestELF(t *testing.T, o elfOpts) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	content := make([]byte, modSegSize)
	put32 := func(off uint32, v uint32) { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(content[off:], v) }
	// .text words: [0] a JAL placeholder, [1] a LUI, [2] an ADDIU.
	put32(modTextOff+0, 0x0C000100) // jal +0x400 (26 bit field 0x100)
	put32(modTextOff+4, 0x3C080002) // lui $t0, 0x0002 (pair encodes 0x18ABC)
	put32(modTextOff+8, 0x25088ABC) // addiu $t0, $t0, 0x8ABC (sign extends)
	put32(modDataOff, 0x00000500)   // data word pointing at module offset 0x500
	// Module info.
	info := content[modInfoOff:]
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(info[0:], 0) // attribute
	copy(info[4:31], "TESTMOD")
	put32(modInfoOff+0x20, 0x00000900)             // gp (module space)
	put32(modInfoOff+0x2C, o.link+modStubT_off)    // stubTop
	put32(modInfoOff+0x30, o.link+modStubT_off+20) // stubBtm
	// One stub table.
	st := content[modStubT_off:]
	put32(modStubT_off+0, o.link+modNameOff)   // name pointer
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(st[4:], 0)   // version
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(st[6:], 0)   // attribute
	st[8] = 5                                  // entrySize in words
	st[9] = 0                                  // varCount
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(st[10:], 2)  // funcCount
	put32(modStubT_off+12, o.link+modNidOff)   // nidTable
	put32(modStubT_off+16, o.link+modStubsOff) // funcTable: the stub code block
	// Stub code: {JR $ra, 0} twice.
	put32(modStubsOff+0, 0x03E00008)
	put32(modStubsOff+4, 0)
	put32(modStubsOff+8, 0x03E00008)
	put32(modStubsOff+12, 0)
	copy(content[modNameOff:], "ThreadManForUser")
	put32(modNidOff+0, 0x446D8DE6)
	put32(modNidOff+4, 0xF475845D)

	// Sections: null, .rodata.sceModuleInfo, one .rel section per
	// reloc group (a single one here), .shstrtab.
	shstr := "\x00.rodata.sceModuleInfo\x00.rel.text\x00.shstrtab\x00"
	nameInfo := strings.Index(shstr, ".rodata.sceModuleInfo")
	nameRel := strings.Index(shstr, ".rel.text")
	nameShstr := strings.Index(shstr, ".shstrtab")

	segFileOff := 0x1000
	shstrOff := segFileOff + modSegSize
	relOff := shstrOff + len(shstr)
	shoff := (relOff + len(o.relocs)*8 + 3) &^ 3

	out := make([]byte, shoff+4*40)
	// ELF header.
	out[0], out[1], out[2], out[3] = 0x7F, 'E', 'L', 'F'
	out[4], out[5] = 1, 1
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[16:], o.typ)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[18:], 8) // EM_MIPS
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[20:], 1)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[24:], o.link+0x40) // entry
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[28:], 52)          // phoff
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[32:], uint32(shoff))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[40:], 52)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[42:], 32)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[44:], 1) // phnum
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[46:], 40)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[48:], 4) // shnum
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[50:], 3) // shstrndx
	// Program header.
	ph := out[52:]
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(ph[0:], 1) // PT_LOAD
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(ph[4:], uint32(segFileOff))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(ph[8:], o.link)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(ph[12:], o.link)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(ph[16:], modSegSize)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(ph[20:], modSegSize)
	copy(out[segFileOff:], content)
	copy(out[shstrOff:], shstr)
	for i, r := range o.relocs {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[relOff+i*8:], r.off)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[relOff+i*8+4:], r.typ|(r.seg<<8))
	}
	sh := func(i int, name, typ, addr, off, size, entsize uint32) {
		b := out[shoff+i*40:]
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[0:], name)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[4:], typ)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[12:], addr)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[16:], off)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[20:], size)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[36:], entsize)
	}
	sh(1, uint32(nameInfo), 1, o.link+modInfoOff, uint32(segFileOff+modInfoOff), 64, 0)
	sh(2, uint32(nameRel), shtPRXReloc, 0, uint32(relOff), uint32(len(o.relocs)*8), 8)
	sh(3, uint32(nameShstr), 3, 0, uint32(shstrOff), uint32(len(shstr)), 0)
	return out
}

func TestLoadExecImage(t *testing.T) {
	data := buildTestELF(t, elfOpts{typ: etExec, link: 0x08800000})
	size, relocatable, err := Probe(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if relocatable || size != modSegSize {
		t.Fatalf("Probe: size %#x relocatable %v, want %#x false", size, relocatable, modSegSize)
	}
	mem := newMapMem(0x08800000, modSegSize)
	m, err := Load(mem, data, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if m.Name != "TESTMOD" || m.Entry != 0x08800040 || m.GP != 0x900 || m.Relocatable {
		t.Fatalf("module: name %q entry %#x gp %#x reloc %v", m.Name, m.Entry, m.GP, m.Relocatable)
	}
	if len(m.Imports) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("imports: %d, want 2", len(m.Imports))
	}
	want0 := Import{Module: "ThreadManForUser", NID: 0x446D8DE6, StubAddr: 0x08800340}
	want1 := Import{Module: "ThreadManForUser", NID: 0xF475845D, StubAddr: 0x08800348}
	if m.Imports[0] != want0 || m.Imports[1] != want1 {
		t.Fatalf("imports: %+v / %+v", m.Imports[0], m.Imports[1])
	}
	// The stub code itself must sit untouched at StubAddr: JR $ra
