		t.Skip("pspautotests corpus not present locally (testroms/pspautotests); skipping")
	}
	return dir
}

// runCorpusTest boots one PRX and returns the content of its
// host0 result file. The guest exits through the crt0 exit path;
// the loop also stops at a generous cycle cap for tests that
// never terminate, returning whatever output was produced.
func runCorpusTest(prxPath string) (string, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(prxPath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	m := New()
	files := map[string][]byte{}
	m.SetMemoryStickFiles(files)
	if err := m.LoadExecutable(data); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("LoadExecutable(%s): %w", filepath.Base(prxPath), err)
	}
	const slice = 4 << 20 // cycles per scheduler slice
	out := func() string { return string(files["host0:/__testoutput.txt"]) }
	for i := 0; i < 75; i++ {
		m.RunCycles(slice)
		if m.Exited() {
			return out(), nil
		}
	}
	return out(), fmt.Errorf("%s: guest did not exit within the cycle cap", filepath.Base(prxPath))
}

func normalizeCRLF(s string) string { return strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\r\n", "\n") }

func firstDiff(got, want string) string {
	g := strings.Split(got, "\n")
	w := strings.Split(want, "\n")
	for i := 0; i < len(g) || i < len(w); i++ {
		gs, ws := "<eof>", "<eof>"
		if i < len(g) {
			gs = g[i]
		}
		if i < len(w) {
			ws = w[i]
		}
		if gs != ws {
			return fmt.Sprintf("line %d: got %q, want %q", i+1, truncLine(gs), truncLine(ws))
		}
	}
	return "outputs differ only in length"
}

func truncLine(s string) string {
	if len(s) > 60 {
		return s[:60] + "..."
	}
	return s
}

// corpusTestNames lists the test names (PRX basenames) of a group.
func corpusTestNames(t *testing.T, root, group string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(filepath.Join(root, "cpu", group))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read corpus group %s: %v", group, err)
	}
	var names []string
	for _, e := range entries {
		if strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".prx") {
			names = append(names, strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".prx"))
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	return names
}

func corpusOne(root, group, name string) (string, bool) {
	dir := filepath.Join(root, "cpu", group)
	wantRaw, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, name+".expected"))
	if err != nil {
		return "missing .expected: " + err.Error(), false
	}
	got, runErr := runCorpusTest(filepath.Join(dir, name+".prx"))
	gotN, wantN := normalizeCRLF(got), normalizeCRLF(string(wantRaw))
	if runErr != nil {
		return runErr.Error() + "; " + firstDiff(gotN, wantN), false
	}
	if gotN != wantN {
		return firstDiff(gotN, wantN), false
	}
	return "", true
}

// TestPSPAutotestsCPUALU is the gating corpus test: the whole
// cpu_alu group must reproduce its .expected output exactly.
func TestPSPAutotestsCPUALU(t *testing.T) {
	root := corpusDir(t)
	for _, name := range corpusTestNames(t, root, "cpu_alu") {
		name := name
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if diff, ok := corpusOne(root, "cpu_alu", name); !ok {
				t.Fatalf("console mismatch: %s", diff)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestPSPAutotestsReport runs the remaining cpu groups report
// only: every outcome is logged, nothing here fails the suite.
func TestPSPAutotestsReport(t *testing.T) {
	root := corpusDir(t)
	for _, group := range []string{"fpu", "icache", "lsu", "vfpu"} {
		var passed, failed []string
		diffs := map[string]string{}
		for _, name := range corpusTestNames(t, root, group) {
			if diff, ok := corpusOne(root, group, name); ok {
				passed = append(passed, name)
			} else {
				failed = append(failed, name)
				diffs[name] = diff
			}
		}
		t.Logf("%s: %d passed, %d failed", group, len(passed), len(failed))
		if len(failed) > 0 {
			t.Logf("%s failing: %s", group, strings.Join(failed, ", "))
		}
		for _, name := range failed {
			t.Logf("%s/%s: %s", group, name, diffs[name])
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/system/system.go ====================

// Package system wires the Allegrex CPU (with its VFPU), the GE display
// list processor, the memory bus and the UMD reader into the machine the
// rest of the project builds on.
//
// Slice PSP-3 state: LoadExecutable boots an ELF or PRX through the HLE
// kernel in the kernel package (threads, sync objects, the published
// HLE library subset, a virtual file system over the UMD image and an
// in-memory Memory Stick). The PSP-1/2 direct path stays available
// when no executable is loaded: display lists submitted through
// SubmitDisplayList execute synchronously through the GE. Save states
// are version 2 without a kernel and version 3 with one; the two do
// not mix (see Deserialize).
package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/chips/allegrex"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/ge"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/kernel"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/load"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-psp/umd"
)

// Display geometry of the PSP LCD.
const (
	Width  = 480
	Height = 272
)

// FrameCycles is the frame budget at the Allegrex default clock:
// 222 MHz / 60 frames = 3,700,000 cycles per frame. The real refresh is
// about 59.94 Hz; 60 is the family convention for this skeleton.
const FrameCycles = 3700000

// stateVersion tags the serialized layout of a machine without a
// kernel. Version 2 (PSP-2) appends the GE state block and the
// GE-active flag, and the CPU block grew to include the VFPU state.
// Version 3 (PSP-3) is the kernel mode layout: the version 2 body
// followed by the serialized kernel blob. A version 2 state loads
// only into a machine that has not booted an executable, and a
// version 3 state only makes sense with its kernel; both rules are
// enforced in Deserialize.
const stateVersion = 2
const stateVersionKernel = 3

// PSP controller button bits (sceCtrl masks).
const (
	ButtonSelect   uint32 = 0x00000001
	ButtonStart    uint32 = 0x00000008
	ButtonUp       uint32 = 0x00000010
	ButtonRight    uint32 = 0x00000020
	ButtonDown     uint32 = 0x00000040
	ButtonLeft     uint32 = 0x00000080
	ButtonL        uint32 = 0x00000100
	ButtonR        uint32 = 0x00000200
	ButtonTriangle uint32 = 0x00001000
	ButtonCircle   uint32 = 0x00002000
	ButtonCross    uint32 = 0x00004000
	ButtonSquare   uint32 = 0x00008000
)

// defaultEntry is where New leaves the CPU parked: the start of main RAM.
// No code lives there until a loader (PSP-3) or a test puts some there.
const defaultEntry = 0x08000000

// Machine is the PSP system.
type Machine struct {
	CPU *allegrex.CPU
	Bus *bus.Bus
	GE  *ge.GE

	iso *umd.ISO
	sfo *umd.SFO

	framebuffer []uint32
	buttons     uint32
	analogX     byte
	analogY     byte
	cycles      uint64
	geActive    bool // a display list was submitted; Framebuffer presents the GE

	kern       *kernel.Kernel // non-nil in kernel mode (after LoadExecutable)
	kernelMode bool
	msFiles    map[string][]byte
}

// New returns a machine with zeroed memory and the CPU parked at the
// default entry point.
func New() *Machine {
	b := bus.New()
	m := &Machine{
		Bus:         b,
		GE:          ge.New(b),
		framebuffer: make([]uint32, Width*Height),
		analogX:     0x80,
		analogY:     0x80,
	}
	for i := range m.framebuffer {
		m.framebuffer[i] = 0xFF000000 // opaque black until the GE draws
	}
	m.CPU = allegrex.New(b)
	m.Boot(defaultEntry)
	return m
}

// Boot resets the CPU at the given entry point. The PSP-3 module loader
// will call this with the entry of the loaded executable.
func (m *Machine) Boot(entry uint32) {
	m.CPU.Reset(entry)
}

// LoadISO mounts a user-supplied disc image and reads its PARAM.SFO
// metadata when present. The image is not decrypted and nothing is
// executed from it in this slice.
func (m *Machine) LoadISO(path string) error {
	iso, err := umd.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if m.iso != nil {
		m.iso.Close()
	}
	m.iso = iso
	m.sfo = nil
	if sfo, err := iso.ParamSFO(); err == nil {
		m.sfo = sfo
	}
	return nil
}

// ISO returns the mounted disc image, or nil.
func (m *Machine) ISO() *umd.ISO {
	return m.iso
}

// --- Kernel mode (PSP-3) ---

// LoadExecutable boots an ELF (ET_EXEC / ET_SCE_EXEC) or PRX
// (ET_SCE_REL) image through the HLE kernel: the machine resets,
// the module loads into the user partition, and its main thread is
// created ready to run on the next RunFrame. Loading an executable
// replaces any previously running program.
func (m *Machine) LoadExecutable(data []byte) error {
	m.Bus = bus.New()
	m.GE = ge.New(m.Bus)
	m.CPU = allegrex.New(m.Bus)
	m.cycles = 0
	m.geActive = false
	for i := range m.framebuffer {
		m.framebuffer[i] = 0xFF000000
	}
	k := kernel.New(m)
	if err := k.LoadModule(data); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	m.kern = k
	m.kernelMode = true
	return nil
}

// KernelMode reports whether an executable has been booted.
func (m *Machine) KernelMode() bool { return m.kernelMode }

// Kernel returns the HLE kernel, or nil outside kernel mode.
func (m *Machine) Kernel() *kernel.Kernel { return m.kern }

// Exited reports whether the guest program has exited (through
// sceKernelExitGame or by every thread dying).
func (m *Machine) Exited() bool {
	return m.kernelMode && m.kern.Exited()
}

// ConsoleOutput returns everything the guest has written to the
// kernel console so far (empty outside kernel mode).
func (m *Machine) ConsoleOutput() string {
	if !m.kernelMode {
		return ""
	}
	return m.kern.ConsoleText()
}

// SetMemoryStickFiles installs the in-memory ms0: store the
// kernel's file system serves. Keys are full guest paths
// ("ms0:/SAVEDATA/x.bin"); writes through sceIo go to the same map.
func (m *Machine) SetMemoryStickFiles(files map[string][]byte) {
	m.msFiles = files
}

// MemoryStickFiles returns the ms0: store (kernel.Host).
func (m *Machine) MemoryStickFiles() map[string][]byte { return m.msFiles }

// The kernel.Host implementation.

var _ kernel.Host = (*Machine)(nil)

// Memory returns the bus as the loader's memory (kernel.Host).
func (m *Machine) Memory() load.Memory { return m.Bus }

// SharedCPU returns the shared Allegrex (kernel.Host).
func (m *Machine) SharedCPU() *allegrex.CPU { return m.CPU }

// PresentFrameBuffer routes a guest framebuffer selection to the
// GE display buffer and marks the GE as the presented source
// (kernel.Host; format codes are the GE codes 0=5650, 1=5551,
// 2=4444, 3=8888).
func (m *Machine) PresentFrameBuffer(addr uint32, width, format int) {
	m.GE.SetDisplayBuffer(addr, width, format)
	m.geActive = true
}

// BootUMD mounts an ISO image and boots the executable the
// documented UMD layout puts at PSP_GAME/SYSDR/BOOT.BIN (with
// the documented fallback to EBOOT.BIN beside it) through the
// HLE kernel. An image with neither file fails cleanly.
func (m *Machine) BootUMD(path string) error {
	if err := m.LoadISO(path); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	data, err := m.iso.ReadFile("PSP_GAME/SYSDR/BOOT.BIN")
	if err != nil {
		data, err = m.iso.ReadFile("PSP_GAME/SYSDR/EBOOT.BIN")
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("system: %s: no boot executable at PSP_GAME/SYSDR/BOOT.BIN or EBOOT.BIN", path)
		}
	}
	return m.LoadExecutable(data)
}

// AudioBuffer drains the mixed sceAudio output in kernel mode:
// stereo int16 at 44,100 Hz, everything mixed since the last
// drain (735 frames per frame budget once the stream is
// running). Outside kernel mode there is no audio path and the
// result is nil, the PSP-2 behavior.
func (m *Machine) AudioBuffer() []int16 {
	if !m.kernelMode {
		return nil
	}
	return m.kern.DrainAudio()
}

// GameTitle returns the TITLE field of the mounted disc's PARAM.SFO,
// falling back to the ISO volume id, then to the empty string.
func (m *Machine) GameTitle() string {
	if m.sfo != nil {
		if title, ok := m.sfo.String("TITLE"); ok {
			return title
		}
	}
	if m.iso != nil {
		return m.iso.VolumeID()
	}
	return ""
}

// LoadBytes copies data into memory through the bus. Loaders and tests use
// it to place code; it is not a disc operation.
func (m *Machine) LoadBytes(vaddr uint32, data []byte) {
	for i, v := range data {
		m.Bus.Write8(vaddr+uint32(i), v)
	}
}

// Framebuffer returns the 480x272 XRGB8888 frame. Before any display
// list is submitted it is the opaque black buffer from boot; afterwards
// it presents the GE display buffer (the current draw buffer, or the
// buffer chosen with SetDisplayBuffer) converted from VRAM.
func (m *Machine) Framebuffer() []uint32 {
	if !m.geActive {
		return m.framebuffer
	}
	rgba := m.GE.ConvertDisplay(Width, Height)
	for i := 0; i < Width*Height; i++ {
		r := uint32(rgba[i*4])
		g := uint32(rgba[i*4+1])
		b := uint32(rgba[i*4+2])
		a := uint32(rgba[i*4+3])
		m.framebuffer[i] = a<<24 | r<<16 | g<<8 | b
	}
	return m.framebuffer
}

// SubmitDisplayList executes the display list at the given bus address
// synchronously through the GE and returns the resulting list state.
// Execution stops at END (StateCompleted) or at a SIGNAL
// (StateStalled); ContinueDisplayList resumes a stalled list. The HLE
// sceGu path that games use arrives in PSP-3; this direct API is how
// slices and tests drive the GE until then.
func (m *Machine) SubmitDisplayList(addr uint32) ge.ListState {
	st := m.GE.Submit(addr)
	m.geActive = true
	return st
}

// ContinueDisplayList resumes a display list that stalled on a SIGNAL.
func (m *Machine) ContinueDisplayList() ge.ListState {
	st := m.GE.Continue()
	m.geActive = true
	return st
}

// DisplayListState returns the GE list state: ready, stalled on a
// signal, or completed.
func (m *Machine) DisplayListState() ge.ListState {
	return m.GE.State()
}

// SetDisplayBuffer selects which VRAM buffer Framebuffer presents, in
// the GE pixel format codes (0=5650, 1=5551, 2=4444, 3=8888). Until a
// list or a game sets one, the GE draw buffer is presented.
func (m *Machine) SetDisplayBuffer(addr uint32, width, format int) {
	m.GE.SetDisplayBuffer(addr, width, format)
}

// SetButtons stores the current controller button bitset.
func (m *Machine) SetButtons(mask uint32) {
	m.buttons = mask
}

// Buttons returns the stored button bitset.
func (m *Machine) Buttons() uint32 {
	return m.buttons
}

// SetAnalog stores the analog stick position (0..255 per axis, 0x80 is
// centered). The stick is a stub in this slice: the value is kept and
// serialized, and the HLE input layer in PSP-3 will serve it to games.
func (m *Machine) SetAnalog(x, y byte) {
	m.analogX = x
	m.analogY = y
}

// Analog returns the stored analog stick position.
func (m *Machine) Analog() (x, y byte) {
	return m.analogX, m.analogY
}

// RunCycles advances the machine until at least n CPU cycles have been
// consumed. In kernel mode the cycles go through the scheduler.
func (m *Machine) RunCycles(n int) {
	if m.kernelMode {
		m.kern.Run(uint64(n))
		return
	}
	spent := 0
	for spent < n {
		c := m.CPU.Step()
		if c < 1 {
			c = 1
		}
		spent += c
		m.cycles += uint64(c)
	}
}

// RunFrame advances one frame budget. In kernel mode the budget is
// consumed across threads by the scheduler, then the vblank is
// notified (waking sceDisplayWaitVblankStart waiters for the next
// frame). Once the guest has exited, RunFrame is a no-op.
func (m *Machine) RunFrame() {
	if m.kernelMode {
		if m.kern.Exited() {
			return
		}
		m.kern.Run(FrameCycles)
		m.kern.NotifyVblank()
		return
	}
	m.RunCycles(FrameCycles)
}

// TotalCycles returns the total cycles executed since New. It is part of
// the serialized state, so a restored machine continues the count.
func (m *Machine) TotalCycles() uint64 {
	if m.kernelMode {
		return m.kern.Cycles()
	}
	return m.cycles
}

// StateSize returns the exact serialized size in bytes for the current
// format and the machine's current GE state (the GE block is variable
// length because the stencil plane is optional). Kernel mode states
// (version 3) add the length prefixed kernel blob.
func (m *Machine) StateSize() int {
	cpuLen := len(m.CPU.Serialize())
	geLen := len(m.GE.Serialize())
	n := 1 + 4 + cpuLen + bus.RAMSize + bus.VRAMSize + bus.ScratchpadSize + 4 + 2 + 2 + 8 + 4 + 4 + geLen
	if m.kernelMode {
		n += 4 + len(m.kern.Serialize())
	}
	return n
}

// Serialize captures the full machine state: CPU (including the VFPU),
// RAM, VRAM, scratchpad, input, the cycle counter, and the GE. The
// layout is:
//
//	[0]      state version byte (2, or 3 in kernel mode)
//	[1:5]    uint32 LE CPU state length
//	[5:...]  CPU state, then RAM, VRAM, scratchpad,
//	         buttons uint32, analog X, analog Y, 2 pad bytes,
//	         total cycles uint64, GE-active uint32,
//	         uint32 LE GE state length, GE state
//	         (version 3 only: uint32 LE kernel length, kernel state)
func (m *Machine) Serialize() []byte {
	cpuState := m.CPU.Serialize()
	geState := m.GE.Serialize()
	out := make([]byte, 0, m.StateSize())
	version := byte(stateVersion)
	if m.kernelMode {
		version = stateVersionKernel
	}
	out = append(out, version)
	var tmp [8]byte
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp[:4], uint32(len(cpuState)))
	out = append(out, tmp[:4]...)
	out = append(out, cpuState...)
	out = append(out, m.Bus.RAM...)
	out = append(out, m.Bus.VRAM...)
	out = append(out, m.Bus.Scratchpad...)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp[:4], m.buttons)
	out = append(out, tmp[:4]...)
	out = append(out, m.analogX, m.analogY, 0, 0)
	// In kernel mode the authoritative cycle count is the kernel's
	// (m.cycles is not advanced there); TotalCycles reports it in
	// both modes, and Deserialize adopts it back the same way.
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(tmp[:8], m.TotalCycles())
	out = append(out, tmp[:8]...)
	geActive := uint32(0)
	if m.geActive {
		geActive = 1
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp[:4], geActive)
	out = append(out, tmp[:4]...)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp[:4], uint32(len(geState)))
	out = append(out, tmp[:4]...)
	out = append(out, geState...)
	if m.kernelMode {
		kernelState := m.kern.Serialize()
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(tmp[:4], uint32(len(kernelState)))
		out = append(out, tmp[:4]...)
		out = append(out, kernelState...)
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize. The bytes are
// parsed field by field and must be consumed exactly; anything else is
// an error and leaves the machine untouched. Version rules: a
// version 2 state carries no kernel and loads only into a machine
// that has not booted an executable; loading one into a kernel mode
// machine is an error (the kernel's threads and objects cannot be
// reconstructed from it). A version 3 state restores its kernel and
// puts the machine in kernel mode. Version 1 is rejected.
func (m *Machine) Deserialize(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) < 1+4 {
		return errors.New("system: state too short")
	}
	version := data[0]
	if version != stateVersion && version != stateVersionKernel {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state version %d, want %d or %d", version, stateVersion, stateVersionKernel)
	}
	if version == stateVersion && m.kernelMode {
		return errors.New("system: version 2 state has no kernel state; refusing to load into a kernel mode machine")
	}
	kernelMode := version == stateVersionKernel
	off := 1
	cpuLen := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[off:]))
	off += 4
	if cpuLen != len(m.CPU.Serialize()) {
		return errors.New("system: CPU state length mismatch")
	}
	tailLen := cpuLen + bus.RAMSize + bus.VRAMSize + bus.ScratchpadSize + 4 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 4
	if len(data) < off+tailLen {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d too short for layout", len(data))
	}
	cpuState := data[off : off+cpuLen]
	off += cpuLen
	ram := data[off : off+bus.RAMSize]
	off += bus.RAMSize
	vram := data[off : off+bus.VRAMSize]
	off += bus.VRAMSize
	scratch := data[off : off+bus.ScratchpadSize]
	off += bus.ScratchpadSize
	buttons := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[off:])
	off += 4
	analogX, analogY := data[off], data[off+1]
	off += 4 // analog pair plus 2 pad bytes
	cycles := binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(data[off:])
	off += 8
	geActive := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[off:]) != 0
	off += 4
	geLen := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[off:]))
	off += 4
	if len(data) < off+geLen {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d too short for GE block", len(data))
	}
	geState := data[off : off+geLen]
	off += geLen
	var kernelState []byte
	if kernelMode {
		if len(data) < off+4 {
			return errors.New("system: version 3 state missing kernel block")
		}
		kernelLen := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[off:]))
		off += 4
		if len(data) != off+kernelLen {
			return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d, want %d", len(data), off+kernelLen)
		}
		kernelState = data[off : off+kernelLen]
	} else if len(data) != off {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d, want %d", len(data), off)
	}

	if err := m.CPU.Deserialize(cpuState); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := m.GE.Deserialize(geState); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	copy(m.Bus.RAM, ram)
	copy(m.Bus.VRAM, vram)
	copy(m.Bus.Scratchpad, scratch)
	m.buttons = buttons
	m.analogX = analogX
	m.analogY = analogY
	m.cycles = cycles
	m.geActive = geActive
	if kernelMode {
		k := kernel.New(m)
		if err := k.Deserialize(kernelState); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		m.kern = k
		m.kernelMode = true
		m.cycles = k.Cycles()
	}
	return nil
}

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// checksumProgram sums the 64 data bytes at 0x08000100 (values 1..64) and
// stores the total (2080) as a word at VRAM address 0x04000000, then spins.
// Hand-assembled MIPS, little endian words.
var checksumProgram = []uint32{
	0x3C080800, // lui   t0, 0x0800
	0x35080100, // ori   t0, t0, 0x0100        ; t0 = data pointer
	0x25090040, // addiu t1, t0, 64            ; t1 = end pointer
	0x240A0000, // addiu t2, $zero, 0          ; t2 = sum
	0x910B0000, // loop: lbu t3, 0(t0)
	0x014B5021, // addu  t2, t2, t3
	0x25080001, // addiu t0, t0, 1
	0x1509FFFC, // bne   t0, t1, loop
	0x3C0C0400, // lui   t4, 0x0400
	0xAD8A0000, // sw    t2, 0(t4)             ; checksum to VRAM
	0x0A00000A, // j     self
	0x00000000, // nop (delay slot)
}

func loadChecksumMachine(t *testing.T) *Machine {
	t.Helper()
	m := New()
	buf := make([]byte, 4)
	for i, w := range checksumProgram {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf, w)
		m.LoadBytes(0x08000000+uint32(4*i), buf)
	}
	data := make([]byte, 64)
	for i := range data {
		data[i] = byte(i + 1)
	}
	m.LoadBytes(0x08000100, data)
	m.Boot(0x08000000)
	return m
}

func TestChecksumProgram(t *testing.T) {
	m := loadChecksumMachine(t)
	m.RunCycles(10000)
	if got := m.Bus.Read32(0x04000000); got != 2080 {
		t.Fatalf("VRAM checksum = %d, want 2080", got)
	}
}

func TestSerializeDeterministicContinuation(t *testing.T) {
	a := loadChecksumMachine(t)
	a.RunCycles(100)
	mid := a.Serialize()
	if len(mid) != a.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("serialized %d bytes, StateSize says %d", len(mid), a.StateSize())
	}
	a.RunCycles(2000)
	finalA := a.Serialize()

	b := loadChecksumMachine(t)
	if err := b.Deserialize(mid); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	b.RunCycles(2000)
	finalB := b.Serialize()

	if !bytes.Equal(finalA, finalB) {
		t.Fatal("continuation after restore diverged from the uninterrupted run")
	}
	if got := b.Bus.Read32(0x04000000); got != 2080 {
		t.Fatalf("restored machine checksum = %d, want 2080", got)
	}
	if b.TotalCycles() != a.TotalCycles() {
		t.Fatalf("cycle counts differ: %d vs %d", b.TotalCycles(), a.TotalCycles())
	}
}

func TestDeserializeRejectsBadStates(t *testing.T) {
	m := New()
	if err := m.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("short state accepted")
	}
	state := m.Serialize()
	state[0] = 0xEE
	if err := m.Deserialize(state); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("bad version accepted")
	}
}

	if len(fb) != Width*Height {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer has %d pixels, want %d", len(fb), Width*Height)
	}
	for i, px := range fb {
		if px != 0xFF000000 {
			t.Fatalf("pixel %d = %#x, want opaque black", i, px)
		}
	}
}

	m := New()
	m.SetButtons(ButtonCross | ButtonStart)
	m.SetAnalog(0x10, 0xE0)
	state := m.Serialize()

	n := New()

	if n.Buttons() != ButtonCross|ButtonStart {
		t.Errorf("buttons = %#x, want %#x", n.Buttons(), ButtonCross|ButtonStart)
	}
	if x, y := n.Analog(); x != 0x10 || y != 0xE0 {
		t.Errorf("analog = (%#x, %#x), want (0x10, 0xE0)", x, y)
	}
}

// --- synthetic ISO / SFO builders (test fixtures only) ---

func both16(dst []byte, v uint16) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(dst[0:], v)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(dst[2:], v)
}

func both32(dst []byte, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(dst[0:], v)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(dst[4:], v)
}

func dirRecord(name []byte, extent, size uint32, dir bool) []byte {
	n := 33 + len(name)
	if n%2 == 1 {
		n++
	}
	rec := make([]byte, n)
	rec[0] = byte(n)
	both32(rec[2:], extent)
	both32(rec[10:], size)
	rec[18] = 125 // year 2025
	rec[19] = 10
	rec[20] = 13
	if dir {
		rec[25] = 2
	}
	both16(rec[28:], 1)
	rec[32] = byte(len(name))
	copy(rec[33:], name)
	return rec
}

func buildTestSFO() []byte {
	// Keys sorted: CATEGORY ("UG"), TITLE ("Sys Test").
	hdr := make([]byte, 20)
	hdr[1], hdr[2], hdr[3] = 'P', 'S', 'F'
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(hdr[4:], 0x00000101)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(hdr[8:], 52)  // key table offset
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(hdr[12:], 68) // data table offset
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(hdr[16:], 2)  // entry count

	out := append([]byte{}, hdr...)
	entry := func(keyOff uint16, length, maxLen, dataOff uint32) {
		e := make([]byte, 16)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(e[0:], keyOff)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(e[2:], 0x0204) // UTF-8, null terminated
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(e[4:], length)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(e[8:], maxLen)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(e[12:], dataOff)
		out = append(out, e...)
	}
	entry(0, 3, 4, 0)  // CATEGORY -> data offset 0
	entry(9, 9, 16, 4) // TITLE -> data offset 4
	out = append(out, "CATEGORY\x00TITLE\x00"...)
	out = append(out, 0) // pad key table to 4-byte alignment (52+15+1 = 68)
	data := make([]byte, 20)
	copy(data[0:], "UG\x00")
	copy(data[4:], "Sys Test\x00")
	out = append(out, data...)
	return out
}

func buildTestISO(t *testing.T, sfo []byte) string {
	t.Helper()
	const sec = 2048
	img := make([]byte, 24*sec)

	pvd := img[16*sec:]
	pvd[0] = 1
	copy(pvd[1:], "CD001")
	pvd[6] = 1
	for i := 40; i < 72; i++ {
		pvd[i] = ' '
	}
	copy(pvd[40:], "PSP_SYS_TEST")
	both32(pvd[80:], 24)
	both16(pvd[120:], 1)
	both16(pvd[124:], 1)
	both16(pvd[128:], sec)
	both32(pvd[132:], 10)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(pvd[140:], 19)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(pvd[148:], 19)
	copy(pvd[156:], dirRecord([]byte{0}, 20, sec, true))

	root := img[20*sec:]
	off := 0
	for _, r := range [][]byte{
		dirRecord([]byte{0}, 20, sec, true),
		dirRecord([]byte{1}, 20, sec, true),
		dirRecord([]byte("PSP_GAME"), 21, sec, true),
	} {
		copy(root[off:], r)
		off += len(r)
	}

	game := img[21*sec:]
	off = 0
	for _, r := range [][]byte{
		dirRecord([]byte{0}, 21, sec, true),
		dirRecord([]byte{1}, 21, sec, true),
		dirRecord([]byte("PARAM.SFO;1"), 22, uint32(len(sfo)), false),
	} {
		copy(game[off:], r)
		off += len(r)
	}
	copy(img[22*sec:], sfo)

	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "test.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, img, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return path
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/umd/iso.go ====================

// Package umd reads PSP UMD disc images in ISO9660 format and parses the
// PARAM.SFO metadata file that every PSP game ships in /PSP_GAME.
package umd

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
)

// sectorSize is the fixed ISO9660 logical sector size used by UMD images.
const sectorSize = 2048

// pvdSector is the sector number of the Primary Volume Descriptor.
const pvdSector = 16

// Entry is a single file or directory inside an ISO image.
type Entry struct {
	Name      string // file or directory name, version suffix stripped, e.g. "PARAM.SFO"
	Size      uint32
	Directory bool
}

// dirRecord is the parsed form of one ISO9660 directory record.
type dirRecord struct {
	extent uint32
	size   uint32
	flags  byte
	name   string // raw name as stored, or "." / ".." for the special entries
}

func (r dirRecord) isDir() bool {
	return r.flags&0x02 != 0
}

// ISO is an opened ISO9660 image. The underlying file is kept open and all
// reads go through ReadAt, so the whole image is never loaded into memory.
type ISO struct {
	file     *os.File
	volumeID string
	root     dirRecord
}

// Open opens the image at path and validates its Primary Volume Descriptor.
func Open(path string) (*ISO, error) {
	f, err := os.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: open %q: %w", path, err)
	}
	iso := &ISO{file: f}
	if err := iso.readPVD(); err != nil {
		f.Close()
		return nil, err
	}
	return iso, nil
}

// Close closes the underlying image file.
func (iso *ISO) Close() error {
	if iso == nil || iso.file == nil {
		return nil
	}
	err := iso.file.Close()
	iso.file = nil
	return err
}

// VolumeID returns the trimmed volume identifier from the PVD.
func (iso *ISO) VolumeID() string {
	return iso.volumeID
}

// readPVD reads and validates sector 16 and extracts the volume identifier
// and the root directory record.
func (iso *ISO) readPVD() error {
	pvd := make([]byte, sectorSize)
	if _, err := iso.file.ReadAt(pvd, pvdSector*sectorSize); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("umd: read primary volume descriptor: %w", err)
	}
	if pvd[0] != 1 {
		return fmt.Errorf("umd: not an ISO9660 image: volume descriptor type %d, want 1", pvd[0])
	}
	if string(pvd[1:6]) != "CD001" {
		return fmt.Errorf("umd: not an ISO9660 image: bad descriptor magic %q", string(pvd[1:6]))
	}
	// The volume identifier is a 32 byte space padded field at offset 40.
	iso.volumeID = strings.Trim(string(pvd[40:72]), " \t\r\n\x00")

	// The root directory record is a 34 byte record at offset 156.
	root, _, err := parseDirRecord(pvd[156:])
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("umd: parse root directory record: %w", err)
	}
	iso.root = root
	return nil
}

// parseDirRecord parses one directory record from the start of b. It returns
// the record and the record length in bytes. The caller guarantees b holds at
// least the start of a record; a zero first byte is handled by callers as a
// sector padding marker, not passed here.
func parseDirRecord(b []byte) (dirRecord, int, error) {
	var rec dirRecord
	if len(b) < 34 {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("directory record truncated: %d bytes available", len(b))
	}
	recLen := int(b[0])
	if recLen < 33 {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("directory record length %d is too small", recLen)
	}
	if recLen > len(b) {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("directory record length %d exceeds %d available bytes", recLen, len(b))
	}
	// Extent and data length are 733 fields: a little endian value followed
	// by a big endian copy. The little endian half is authoritative here.
	rec.extent = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[2:6])
	rec.size = binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[10:14])
	rec.flags = b[25]
	nameLen := int(b[32])
	if 33+nameLen > recLen {
		return rec, 0, fmt.Errorf("directory record name length %d exceeds record length %d", nameLen, recLen)
	}
	nameBytes := b[33 : 33+nameLen]
	switch {
	case nameLen == 1 && nameBytes[0] == 0x00:
		rec.name = "."
	case nameLen == 1 && nameBytes[0] == 0x01:
		rec.name = ".."
	default:
		rec.name = string(nameBytes)
	}
	return rec, recLen, nil
}

// stripVersion removes a trailing version suffix such as ";1" from a file
// name. A suffix counts only when every byte after the semicolon is a digit.
func stripVersion(name string) string {
	i := strings.LastIndexByte(name, ';')
	if i < 0 || i == len(name)-1 {
		return name
	}
	for j := i + 1; j < len(name); j++ {
		if name[j] < '0' || name[j] > '9' {
			return name
		}
	}
	return name[:i]
}

// readDir returns every record stored in the directory described by rec,
// including the "." and ".." entries.
func (iso *ISO) readDir(rec dirRecord) ([]dirRecord, error) {
	if !rec.isDir() {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: extent %d is not a directory", rec.extent)
	}
	data := make([]byte, rec.size)
	if rec.size > 0 {
		if _, err := iso.file.ReadAt(data, int64(rec.extent)*sectorSize); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: read directory at extent %d: %w", rec.extent, err)
		}
	}
	var out []dirRecord
	offset := 0
	for offset < len(data) {
		// A record never spans a sector. A zero length byte means the rest
		// of the current sector is padding, so jump to the next boundary.
		if data[offset] == 0 {
			offset = (offset/sectorSize + 1) * sectorSize
			continue
		}
		sectorEnd := (offset/sectorSize + 1) * sectorSize
		if sectorEnd > len(data) {
			sectorEnd = len(data)
		}
		entry, recLen, err := parseDirRecord(data[offset:sectorEnd])
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: parse directory at extent %d offset %d: %w", rec.extent, offset, err)
		}
		out = append(out, entry)
		offset += recLen
	}
	return out, nil
}

// splitPath splits an absolute image path into its components. Empty
// components and "." components are dropped.
func splitPath(path string) []string {
	var parts []string
	for _, p := range strings.Split(path, "/") {
		if p == "" || p == "." {
			continue
		}
		parts = append(parts, p)
	}
	return parts
}

// lookup finds the child of dir whose name matches component, comparing
// case-insensitively with version suffixes stripped.
func (iso *ISO) lookup(dir dirRecord, component string) (dirRecord, error) {
	entries, err := iso.readDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return dirRecord{}, err
	}
	want := stripVersion(component)
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.name == "." || e.name == ".." {
			continue
		}
		if strings.EqualFold(stripVersion(e.name), want) {
			return e, nil
		}
	}
	return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("umd: %q not found", component)
}

// resolve walks path components from the root and returns the final record.
func (iso *ISO) resolve(path string) (dirRecord, error) {
	cur := iso.root
	for _, part := range splitPath(path) {
		if !cur.isDir() {
			return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("umd: %q: %q is not a directory", path, part)
		}
		next, err := iso.lookup(cur, part)
		if err != nil {
			return dirRecord{}, fmt.Errorf("umd: resolve %q: %w", path, err)
		}
		cur = next
	}
	return cur, nil
}

// List returns the entries of the directory at dirPath, for example "/" or
// "/PSP_GAME". The listing is not recursive and excludes "." and "..".
func (iso *ISO) List(dirPath string) ([]Entry, error) {
	rec, err := iso.resolve(dirPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !rec.isDir() {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: list %q: not a directory", dirPath)
	}
	records, err := iso.readDir(rec)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var out []Entry
	for _, r := range records {
		if r.name == "." || r.name == ".." {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, Entry{
			Name:      stripVersion(r.name),
			Size:      r.size,
			Directory: r.isDir(),
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

// ReadFile returns the full contents of the file at path, for example
// "/PSP_GAME/PARAM.SFO". Multi-extent files are not supported: the file is
// read from its single starting extent for its recorded data length, which
// covers the small single-extent metadata files this package targets.
func (iso *ISO) ReadFile(path string) ([]byte, error) {
	rec, err := iso.resolve(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if rec.isDir() {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: read %q: is a directory", path)
	}
	data := make([]byte, rec.size)
	if rec.size > 0 {
		if _, err := iso.file.ReadAt(data, int64(rec.extent)*sectorSize); err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: read file %q at extent %d: %w", path, rec.extent, err)
		}
	}
	return data, nil
}

// ParamSFO reads and parses /PSP_GAME/PARAM.SFO from the image.
func (iso *ISO) ParamSFO() (*SFO, error) {
	data, err := iso.ReadFile("/PSP_GAME/PARAM.SFO")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return ParseSFO(data)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/umd/sfo.go ====================

package umd

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// SFO format codes from the documented PSF (PARAM.SFO) format.
const (
	sfoFormatRawString = 0x0004 // raw UTF-8 string, not null terminated
	sfoFormatString    = 0x0204 // UTF-8 string, null terminated
	sfoFormatInt32     = 0x0404 // little endian int32
)

// SFOValue is one PARAM.SFO value: either a string or an int32.
type SFOValue struct {
	IsInt bool
	Str   string
	Int   int32
}

// SFO is a parsed PARAM.SFO file.
type SFO struct {
	Values map[string]SFOValue
}

// ParseSFO parses PARAM.SFO data in the documented PSF format. Malformed
// data returns an error; ParseSFO never panics on bad input.
func ParseSFO(data []byte) (*SFO, error) {
	const headerSize = 20
	const indexEntrySize = 16
	if len(data) < headerSize {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO data too short: %d bytes, need at least %d", len(data), headerSize)
	}
	if data[0] != 0x00 || data[1] != 'P' || data[2] != 'S' || data[3] != 'F' {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: bad SFO magic %q, want 0x00 PSF", string(data[0:4]))
	}
	version := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[4:8])
	if version&0xFFFFFF00 != 0x00000100 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: unsupported SFO version %#08x, want 0x000001xx", version)
	}
	keyTableOffset := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[8:12])
	dataTableOffset := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[12:16])
	entryCount := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[16:20])

	if uint64(keyTableOffset) > uint64(len(data)) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO key table offset %d exceeds data length %d", keyTableOffset, len(data))
	}
	if uint64(dataTableOffset) > uint64(len(data)) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO data table offset %d exceeds data length %d", dataTableOffset, len(data))
	}
	indexEnd := uint64(headerSize) + uint64(entryCount)*indexEntrySize
	if indexEnd > uint64(len(data)) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO index of %d entries exceeds data length %d", entryCount, len(data))
	}

	sfo := &SFO{Values: make(map[string]SFOValue, entryCount)}
	for i := uint32(0); i < entryCount; i++ {
		off := headerSize + int(i)*indexEntrySize
		entry := data[off : off+indexEntrySize]
		keyOffset := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(entry[0:2])
		paramFormat := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(entry[2:4])
		paramLength := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(entry[4:8])
		// entry[8:12] is paramMaxLength, the padded capacity of the value.
		// Reads are bounded by paramLength, so it is not needed here.
		dataOffset := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(entry[12:16])

		key, err := sfoKey(data, keyTableOffset, keyOffset)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO entry %d: %w", i, err)
		}

		valueStart := uint64(dataTableOffset) + uint64(dataOffset)
		valueEnd := valueStart + uint64(paramLength)
		switch paramFormat {
		case sfoFormatRawString:
			if valueEnd > uint64(len(data)) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO entry %d (%s): value of %d bytes at offset %d exceeds data length %d", i, key, paramLength, valueStart, len(data))
			}
			sfo.Values[key] = SFOValue{Str: string(data[valueStart:valueEnd])}
		case sfoFormatString:
			if valueEnd > uint64(len(data)) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO entry %d (%s): value of %d bytes at offset %d exceeds data length %d", i, key, paramLength, valueStart, len(data))
			}
			sfo.Values[key] = SFOValue{Str: strings.TrimRight(string(data[valueStart:valueEnd]), "\x00")}
		case sfoFormatInt32:
			if paramLength != 4 {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO entry %d (%s): int32 value length %d, want 4", i, key, paramLength)
			}
			if valueEnd > uint64(len(data)) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("umd: SFO entry %d (%s): value at offset %d exceeds data length %d", i, key, valueStart, len(data))
			}
			sfo.Values[key] = SFOValue{
				IsInt: true,
				Int:   int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(data[valueStart:valueEnd])),
			}
		default:
			// Unknown formats are skipped, not an error, so newer files
			// with extra value kinds still parse.
			continue
		}
	}
	return sfo, nil
}

// sfoKey reads the null terminated key string at
// keyTableOffset + keyOffset inside data.
func sfoKey(data []byte, keyTableOffset uint32, keyOffset uint16) (string, error) {
	start := uint64(keyTableOffset) + uint64(keyOffset)
	if start >= uint64(len(data)) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("key offset %d exceeds data length %d", start, len(data))
	}
	rest := data[start:]
	end := -1
	for j, c := range rest {
		if c == 0 {
			end = j
			break
		}
	}
	if end < 0 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("key at offset %d is not null terminated", start)
	}
	return string(rest[:end]), nil
}

// String returns the string value stored under key. The second result is
// false when the key is missing or holds an integer.
func (s *SFO) String(key string) (string, bool) {
	v, ok := s.Values[key]
	if !ok || v.IsInt {
		return "", false
	}
	return v.Str, true
}

// Int returns the int32 value stored under key. The second result is false
// when the key is missing or holds a string.
func (s *SFO) Int(key string) (int32, bool) {
	v, ok := s.Values[key]
	if !ok || !v.IsInt {
		return 0, false
	}
	return v.Int, true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-psp/umd/umd_test.go ====================

package umd

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// put723 writes a both-endian 16 bit value: little endian then big endian.
func put723(b []byte, off int, v uint16) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[off:], v)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(b[off+2:], v)
}

// put733 writes a both-endian 32 bit value: little endian then big endian.
func put733(b []byte, off int, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[off:], v)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[off+4:], v)
}

// makeDirRecord builds one ISO9660 directory record for name. A name of a
// single 0x00 byte is ".", a single 0x01 byte is "..".
func makeDirRecord(name []byte, extent, size uint32, isDir bool) []byte {
	recLen := 33 + len(name)
	if recLen%2 != 0 {
		recLen++ // records are padded to an even length
	}
	rec := make([]byte, recLen)
	rec[0] = byte(recLen)
	rec[1] = 0 // extended attribute record length
	put733(rec, 2, extent)
	put733(rec, 10, size)
	// Bytes 18..24 (recording date) are left zero; the reader ignores them.
	if isDir {
		rec[25] = 0x02
	}
	put723(rec, 28, 1) // volume sequence number
	rec[32] = byte(len(name))
	copy(rec[33:], name)
	return rec
}

// writeRecord copies a directory record into img at a sector offset and
// returns the offset just past it.
func writeRecord(img []byte, sector, offset int, rec []byte) int {
	copy(img[sector*sectorSize+offset:], rec)
	return offset + len(rec)
}

func align4(n int) int {
	return (n + 3) &^ 3
}

// sfoEntrySpec describes one value for the synthetic SFO builder.
type sfoEntrySpec struct {
	key    string
	format uint16
	str    string
	num    int32
}

// buildSFO builds a synthetic PARAM.SFO. Specs must be sorted by key, as the
// real format requires. String values use the null terminated format and
// are padded to 4 byte alignment inside their maximum lengths; integer
// values use the int32 format.
func buildSFO() []byte {
	specs := []sfoEntrySpec{
		{key: "APP_VER", format: sfoFormatString, str: "01.00"},
		{key: "CATEGORY", format: sfoFormatString, str: "UG"},
		{key: "DISC_ID", format: sfoFormatString, str: "TEST00001"},
		{key: "PSP_SYSTEM_VER", format: sfoFormatInt32, num: 0x00050010},
		{key: "TITLE", format: sfoFormatString, str: "Synthetic Test Game"},
	}

	const headerSize = 20
	keyTableOffset := headerSize + len(specs)*16

	// Lay out the key table: null terminated keys in key order.
	var keyTable []byte
	keyOffsets := make([]int, len(specs))
	for i, spec := range specs {
		keyOffsets[i] = len(keyTable)
		keyTable = append(keyTable, spec.key...)
		keyTable = append(keyTable, 0)
	}
	dataTableOffset := align4(keyTableOffset + len(keyTable))

	// Lay out the data table in key order with 4 byte alignment.
	var dataTable []byte
	dataOffsets := make([]int, len(specs))
	lengths := make([]int, len(specs))
	maxLengths := make([]int, len(specs))
	for i, spec := range specs {
		for len(dataTable)%4 != 0 {
			dataTable = append(dataTable, 0)
		}
		dataOffsets[i] = len(dataTable)
		switch spec.format {
		case sfoFormatString:
			raw := append([]byte(spec.str), 0)
			lengths[i] = len(raw)
			maxLengths[i] = align4(len(raw))
			dataTable = append(dataTable, raw...)
			for len(dataTable) < dataOffsets[i]+maxLengths[i] {
				dataTable = append(dataTable, 0)
			}
		case sfoFormatInt32:
			lengths[i] = 4
			maxLengths[i] = 4
			var buf [4]byte
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(buf[:], uint32(spec.num))
			dataTable = append(dataTable, buf[:]...)
		}
	}

	out := make([]byte, dataTableOffset+len(dataTable))
	// Header: magic, version 1.1, table offsets, entry count.
	out[1] = 'P'
	out[2] = 'S'
	out[3] = 'F'
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[4:], 0x00000101)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[8:], uint32(keyTableOffset))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[12:], uint32(dataTableOffset))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[16:], uint32(len(specs)))
	// Index entries.
	for i, spec := range specs {
		off := headerSize + i*16
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[off:], uint16(keyOffsets[i]))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[off+2:], spec.format)
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off+4:], uint32(lengths[i]))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off+8:], uint32(maxLengths[i]))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(out[off+12:], uint32(dataOffsets[i]))
	}
	copy(out[keyTableOffset:], keyTable)
	copy(out[dataTableOffset:], dataTable)
	return out
}

var testReadme = []byte("Hello from a synthetic PSP disc.\n")

// buildTestISO writes a synthetic 24 sector ISO image holding a README file
// and /PSP_GAME/PARAM.SFO, and returns its path plus the SFO bytes used.
func buildTestISO(t *testing.T) (string, []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	sfo := buildSFO()

	const (
		rootSector     = 20
		gameSector     = 21
		sfoSector      = 22
		readmeSector   = 23
		totalSectors   = 24
		volumeIDSector = 16
	)
	img := make([]byte, totalSectors*sectorSize)

	// Primary Volume Descriptor at sector 16.
	pvd := volumeIDSector * sectorSize
	img[pvd] = 1
	copy(img[pvd+1:], "CD001")
	img[pvd+6] = 1
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		img[pvd+40+i] = ' '
	}
	copy(img[pvd+40:], "PSP_TEST_DISC")
	rootRec := makeDirRecord([]byte{0x00}, rootSector, sectorSize, true)
	copy(img[pvd+156:], rootRec)

	// Root directory at sector 20.
	off := 0
	off = writeRecord(img, rootSector, off, makeDirRecord([]byte{0x00}, rootSector, sectorSize, true))
	off = writeRecord(img, rootSector, off, makeDirRecord([]byte{0x01}, rootSector, sectorSize, true))
	off = writeRecord(img, rootSector, off, makeDirRecord([]byte("README.TXT;1"), readmeSector, uint32(len(testReadme)), false))
	writeRecord(img, rootSector, off, makeDirRecord([]byte("PSP_GAME"), gameSector, sectorSize, true))

	// PSP_GAME directory at sector 21.
	off = 0
	off = writeRecord(img, gameSector, off, makeDirRecord([]byte{0x00}, gameSector, sectorSize, true))
	off = writeRecord(img, gameSector, off, makeDirRecord([]byte{0x01}, rootSector, sectorSize, true))
	writeRecord(img, gameSector, off, makeDirRecord([]byte("PARAM.SFO;1"), sfoSector, uint32(len(sfo)), false))

	// File data.
	copy(img[sfoSector*sectorSize:], sfo)
	copy(img[readmeSector*sectorSize:], testReadme)

	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "test.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, img, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write test ISO: %v", err)
	}
	return path, sfo
}

func findEntry(entries []Entry, name string) (Entry, bool) {
	for _, e := range entries {
		if e.Name == name {
			return e, true
		}
	}
	return Entry{}, false
}

func TestISOFromSyntheticImage(t *testing.T) {
	path, sfoBytes := buildTestISO(t)

	iso, err := Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Open: %v", err)
	}
	defer iso.Close()

	if got := iso.VolumeID(); got != "PSP_TEST_DISC" {
		t.Errorf("VolumeID = %q, want %q", got, "PSP_TEST_DISC")
	}

	root, err := iso.List("/")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("List(/): %v", err)
	}
	if len(root) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("List(/) returned %d entries, want 2: %+v", len(root), root)
	}
	game, ok := findEntry(root, "PSP_GAME")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("List(/) missing PSP_GAME: %+v", root)
	}
	if !game.Directory {
		t.Errorf("PSP_GAME Directory = false, want true")
	}
	readme, ok := findEntry(root, "README.TXT")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("List(/) missing README.TXT: %+v", root)
	}
	if readme.Directory {
		t.Errorf("README.TXT Directory = true, want false")
	}
	if readme.Size != uint32(len(testReadme)) {
		t.Errorf("README.TXT Size = %d, want %d", readme.Size, len(testReadme))
	}

	gameEntries, err := iso.List("/PSP_GAME")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("List(/PSP_GAME): %v", err)
	}
	if len(gameEntries) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("List(/PSP_GAME) returned %d entries, want 1: %+v", len(gameEntries), gameEntries)
	}
	param := gameEntries[0]
	if param.Name != "PARAM.SFO" {
		t.Errorf("PSP_GAME entry Name = %q, want %q", param.Name, "PARAM.SFO")
	}
	if param.Directory {
		t.Errorf("PARAM.SFO Directory = true, want false")
	}
	if param.Size != uint32(len(sfoBytes)) {
		t.Errorf("PARAM.SFO Size = %d, want %d", param.Size, len(sfoBytes))
	}

	gotSFO, err := iso.ReadFile("/PSP_GAME/PARAM.SFO")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadFile(/PSP_GAME/PARAM.SFO): %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(gotSFO, sfoBytes) {
		t.Errorf("ReadFile(/PSP_GAME/PARAM.SFO) returned %d bytes that differ from the %d synthetic bytes", len(gotSFO), len(sfoBytes))
	}

	// Path lookup is case-insensitive.
	gotReadme, err := iso.ReadFile("/readme.txt")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadFile(/readme.txt): %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(gotReadme, testReadme) {
		t.Errorf("ReadFile(/readme.txt) = %q, want %q", gotReadme, testReadme)
	}

	sfo, err := iso.ParamSFO()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParamSFO: %v", err)
	}
	checkSFO(t, sfo)

	if _, err := iso.ReadFile("/PSP_GAME/MISSING.BIN"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadFile on a missing path: got nil error, want an error")
	}
	if _, err := iso.ReadFile("/NOPE/PARAM.SFO"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadFile in a missing directory: got nil error, want an error")
	}
	if _, err := iso.ReadFile("/PSP_GAME"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ReadFile on a directory: got nil error, want an error")
	}
	if _, err := iso.List("/README.TXT"); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("List on a file: got nil error, want an error")
	}
}

func checkSFO(t *testing.T, sfo *SFO) {
	t.Helper()
	strChecks := map[string]string{
		"TITLE":    "Synthetic Test Game",
		"CATEGORY": "UG",
		"APP_VER":  "01.00",
		"DISC_ID":  "TEST00001",
	}
	for key, want := range strChecks {
		got, ok := sfo.String(key)
		if !ok {
			t.Errorf("String(%q): not found", key)
			continue
		}
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("String(%q) = %q, want %q", key, got, want)
		}
	}
	ver, ok := sfo.Int("PSP_SYSTEM_VER")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("Int(PSP_SYSTEM_VER): not found")
	}
	if ver != 0x00050010 {
		t.Errorf("Int(PSP_SYSTEM_VER) = %#08x, want 0x00050010", ver)
	}
	if _, ok := sfo.String("PSP_SYSTEM_VER"); ok {
		t.Errorf("String(PSP_SYSTEM_VER): got ok for an integer value, want false")
	}
	if _, ok := sfo.Int("TITLE"); ok {
		t.Errorf("Int(TITLE): got ok for a string value, want false")
	}
	if _, ok := sfo.String("NO_SUCH_KEY"); ok {
		t.Errorf("String(NO_SUCH_KEY): got ok for a missing key, want false")
	}
}

func TestParseSFOStandalone(t *testing.T) {
	sfo, err := ParseSFO(buildSFO())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ParseSFO: %v", err)
	}
	if len(sfo.Values) != 5 {
		t.Errorf("ParseSFO parsed %d values, want 5", len(sfo.Values))
	}
	checkSFO(t, sfo)
}

func TestOpenRejectsNonISO(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "not-an-iso.bin")
	junk := bytes.Repeat([]byte("this is not an iso "), 2048)
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, junk, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write junk file: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := Open(path); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("Open on a non-ISO file: got nil error, want an error")
	}

	empty := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "empty.bin")
	if err := os.WriteFile(empty, nil, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write empty file: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := Open(empty); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("Open on an empty file: got nil error, want an error")
	}
}

func TestParseSFORejectsBadMagic(t *testing.T) {
	data := buildSFO()
	data[1] = 'X'
	if _, err := ParseSFO(data); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("ParseSFO with bad magic: got nil error, want an error")
	}
}

func TestParseSFOTruncated(t *testing.T) {
	full := buildSFO()
	for _, n := range []int{0, 3, 10, 19, 20, 40, 99, len(full) / 2, len(full) - 1} {
		func() {
			defer func() {
				if r := recover(); r != nil {
					t.Errorf("ParseSFO truncated to %d bytes panicked: %v", n, r)
				}
			}()
			if _, err := ParseSFO(full[:n]); err == nil {
				t.Errorf("ParseSFO truncated to %d bytes: got nil error, want an error", n)
			}
		}()
	}
}
