==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/README.md ====================

# go-saturn

A from-scratch Sega Saturn emulator core in Go, written from
published hardware documentation (the SH-2 and SH7604 manuals,
the Saturn hardware and CD block references). Zero third-party
dependencies. No BIOS bytes are used or shipped anywhere in
this module; the boot path is HLE (system.BootDisc loads
the game's initial program per the documented header
fields and enters it, SAT-4).

## What exists in SAT-1

### chips/sh2: dual SH-2 CPU

The complete SH-2 instruction set as listed in the SH-2
hardware manual: the MOV family in every addressing mode,
MAC.W and MAC.L, MUL.L, DMULS.L and DMULU.L, the full
arithmetic, logic, shift and rotate sets, system control
(LDC, STC, LDS, STS for GBR, VBR, SR, PR, MACH, MACL),
branches with exact delay slots, TRAPA, RTE, SLEEP, and
the exception model (general illegal vector 4, slot
illegal vector 6, CPU address error vector 7, TRAPA base
vector 32 plus the trap number). The CPU is instantiated
twice, master and slave, with fully independent state and
a shared bus interface. NMI and maskable interrupt inputs
are exposed for the system, vectoring through VBR with the
documented stack frame. Each CPU serializes to exactly
104 bytes.

SH-2 versus SH-4 boundary, decided from the SH-2 manual:
DMULS.L and DMULU.L ARE SH-2 instructions and are
implemented; MUL.L and MAC.L are SH-2. SH-4-only forms are
illegal here: register banks (LDC Rn,Rn_BANK and friends),
the FPU register set (STS and LDS of FPUL and FPSCR), and
MOVUA. The SH-2 has no banked general registers and no
FPU, so those encodings raise the general illegal
instruction exception. The 0xF group is entirely illegal
on SH-2.

Gate: hand-derived unit vectors from the manual, 85 test
nodes and about 240 assertions, covering every instruction
group, delay slot legality including the slot illegal
exception, MAC.W and MAC.L accumulation, software division
through the DIV0S, DIV0U and DIV1 sequence matching Go
division for signed and unsigned cases, interrupt masking
and RTE return, NMI, misaligned access traps, and a
mid-program serialize round trip. No Tom Harte SH-2 corpus
exists to run; the gate is the manual vectors.

### bus: the Saturn memory map

Both SH-2 CPUs share one bus. The slave starts held; the
system API releases it. Bus arbitration between the two
CPUs is round robin and flat; no cycle-accurate contention
is modeled in this slice.

Map: BIOS window 512 KiB at 0x00000000 (reads return 0, no
Sega bytes), SMPC register page at 0x00100000 (stored
bytes), backup RAM 32 KiB at 0x00180000 with the documented
odd-byte addressing (data lives on odd byte offsets; even
offsets read 0xFF), Work RAM-L 1 MiB at 0x00200000, the
MINIT and SINIT inter-CPU windows at 0x01000000 and
0x01800000 (a 16-bit write raises the other CPU's FRT
input capture flag), A-bus CS0 and CS1 stub windows, the
CD block register block at CS2 0x05800000 (CR1 to CR4,
HIRQ and mask stored), sound CPU work RAM 512 KiB at
0x05A00000, SCSP registers, VDP1 VRAM 512 KiB, VDP1
framebuffer (two 256 KiB banks since SAT-2; the window
maps the current draw bank), VDP1 registers, VDP2 VRAM 512 KiB,
color RAM 4 KiB, VDP2 registers, SCU registers, and Work
RAM-H 1 MiB at 0x06000000 (mirrored, also reachable
cache-through at 0x26000000). Addresses are masked with
0x1FFFFFFF, so the cache and cache-through aliases land on
the same storage.

The SH7604 on-chip register window lives at 0xFFFFFE00
and up, selected per CPU by the bus: FRT, WDT, cache
control (CCR is stored; the cache is not simulated), INTC
interrupt controller fields, and the hardware divide unit
(DVSR, DVDNT, DVCR, VCRDIV, DVDNTH, DVDNTL at 0xFFFFFF00).
A 32-bit write to DVDNT runs a signed 32 by 32 division;
a write to DVDNTL runs a signed 64 by 32 division. Results
appear in DVDNT (quotient) and DVDNTH (remainder) with the
documented overflow flag behavior in DVCR: divide by zero
and quotient overflow set OVF and saturate. Division is
instant in this slice; the hardware latency is not
modeled.

Gate: 17 test functions, 120 assertions over the map, the
backup RAM byte rules, the inter-CPU capture flags, and
divide unit math for 32/32 and 64/32 including overflow,
divide by zero, and the INT_MIN edge cases.

### cd: disc images and Saturn metadata

User-supplied image loading only. The .cue and .bin
reader parses single-FILE cues (AUDIO, MODE1/2048,
MODE1/2352, MODE2/2352, MODE2/2336, MODE2/2324 tracks,
PREGAP and INDEX 00/01), exposes sector access by LBA and
MSF, and returns user data per track mode (2048 bytes for
Mode 1 and Mode 2 Form 1, 2324 for Mode 2 Form 2). The
.iso reader synthesizes raw sectors for Mode 1 images.
ISO9660: primary volume descriptor check, root directory
walk, and single-extent file reads. The Saturn IP header
parse validates the exact 16-byte SEGA SEGASATURN
signature and reads maker ID, product number, version,
release date, device info, area symbols, peripheral list,
title, the IP size at 0xE0, the master and slave stack
addresses at 0xE8 and 0xEC, and the first read address
and size at 0xF0 and 0xF4. SAT-4 corrected those
offsets: the SAT-1 parse read the stack fields at
0xF0 and 0xF8, which the published System ID layout
(Sega's disc format documentation, as tabulated in
the public Sega Retro reference) shows are the first
read fields; the stack fields live at 0xE8 and 0xEC
and the IP size at 0xE0 was not parsed at all before
SAT-4.

Gate: 11 test functions, 121 assertions over cue parsing,
sector math, pregap handling, ISO9660 on a synthetic
image built inside the tests, and header parsing. All test
data is synthetic.

### system: deterministic machine skeleton

LoadDisc (.cue or .iso by extension) and LoadDiscImage
validate the Saturn header before accepting a disc.
RunFrame spends a 477,273 cycle budget per CPU (28.6364
MHz at 60 frames per second, truncated) stepping the
master, and the slave too once released. Framebuffer()
returns a blank 320 by 224 XRGB8888 buffer in this slice.
SetButtons stores the standard digital pad bitmask
(peripheral ID 0x02 convention). Serialize and
Deserialize use a versioned 2,130,132 byte state covering
both CPUs, both work RAMs, and the backup RAM; disc
contents are not part of the state.

Gate: synthetic SH-2 programs on master and slave
communicating through Work RAM-H, a mid-run save state
round trip with byte-identical continuation, header
validation, and bad-state rejection.

## What exists in SAT-2

### vdp2: the background and composition engine

Built from the VDP2 user's manual (ST-58). The package
renders per scanline into the system framebuffer as
XRGB8888 and owns no memory of its own: VRAM (512 KiB),
CRAM (4 KiB), and the 512 byte register page are shared
slices handed in by the bus, so CPU writes take effect
immediately.

Coverage: TVMD display control with every resolution
mode decoded to its pixel dimensions (widths 320, 352,
640, 704; heights 224, 240, 256; interlace doubling to
448, 480, 512; the exclusive monitor modes at their
fixed 480 line height and 525 or 561 total lines).
TVSTAT readback (VBLANK, HBLANK, ODD field) and VCNT are
maintained by the system timing calls. All five scroll
layers (NBG0 to NBG3, RBG0, RBG1) in cell and bitmap
modes: character color modes 16, 256, 2048 palette plus
RGB 5.5.5 and RGB 8.8.8, 1x1 and 2x2 characters, 1 word
and 2 word pattern name data with every character
number supplement mode, plane sizes, and the full map
register set. Scrolling: integer and fractional screen
scroll, per line scroll tables for X, Y, and zoom at
every documented line density, vertical cell scroll,
zoom with the ZMCTL reductions (1/2, 1/4, and the
quarter step modes), and mosaic. Rotation: both
parameter sets read from VRAM with the full documented
parameter set (screen start, per line and per dot
increments, display point, center point, view point,
coefficients kx and ky from registers or the
coefficient table in VRAM or CRAM), RPMD parameter
switching modes, and all four screen over modes.
Priorities: per layer registers, sprite priorities
PRISA to PRISD for all 16 sprite types with the field
positions decoded per type, and special priority and
special color calculation from pattern supplementary
bits or per dot code matches (SFSEL and SFCODE). Color
calculation: per layer enable and 5 bit ratios in 1/32
steps, both ratio selection modes, addition mode,
extended color calculation blending the third image,
and the back screen ratio path. Color offset registers
A and B applied after color calculation. Windows: W0
and W1 rectangles, the line window table, inside and
outside areas, per layer logic, the sprite window, and
the rotation parameter window. Back screen in single
color and per line table forms, the line color screen
with per layer insertion enables, and shadow sprites
halving the scroll color under them. CRAM reads honor
all four RAMCTL modes, including mode 2 and 3 where
RGB888 longs are stored split across word pairs.

Gate: 15 test functions of hand-derived pixel probes:
NBG0 cell mode with scroll offset in both pattern name
formats, line scroll shifting one line by exactly the
table value, vertical cell scroll, RBG0 identity and
half coefficient sampling, frame buffer rotation
coordinates, register versus special priority at one
pixel, an exact half ratio color blend (127, 0, 127),
window outside area, the CRAM mode 2 round trip, back
screen versus line color across a boundary line, sprite
composition including the priority 0 transparency rule,
zoom and ZMHF, and the display size and total line
tables.

### vdp1: the sprite and polygon engine

Built from the VDP1 user's manual (ST-013). The package
owns the command processor and draws into one of two
256 KiB frame buffer banks; the system CPU window maps
only the current draw bank. Command tables are read
from VRAM at 32 bytes per command and walked until an
END command, honoring all eight jump modes (next,
assign, call, return, and the four skip forms) with a
call stack. Commands: system clipping, user clipping,
local coordinate set, normal sprite, scaled sprite with
all documented zoom point positions, distorted sprite,
polygon, polyline, and line. Drawing attributes per the
manual: texture color modes 0 to 5 (16, CLUT 16, 64,
128, and 256 color palette banks with the documented
bit stream fetches and end codes, plus direct RGB),
gouraud shading from the VRAM table interpolated per
pixel, mesh checkerboard skip by frame buffer
coordinate parity, half transparent blending, shadow
writes, color calculation modes, ECD and SPD bits, user
clipping with inside and outside modes, and pre
clipping. Frame change follows FBCR at each frame
boundary: 1-cycle mode swaps banks, erases the new draw
bank through EWDR, EWLR, and EWRR, and auto starts
drawing when PTMR selects it; manual erase and manual
change modes behave per the manual, including the FCT
bit clearing itself. PTMR mode 1 draws on a 0 to 1
trigger transition polled once per line. TVMR selects
the 16 bit and 8 bit frame buffer formats and the frame
buffer rotation read path, which asks VDP2 for rotated
coordinates. LOPR, COPR, and MODR readback are written
into the register page. The finished bank is exposed to
VDP2 as the sprite source: each pixel supplies its
color word plus, through the VDP2 sprite decode, its
priority and color calculation fields.

Gate: 18 test functions over synthetic command lists:
clipping and local coordinates with a scaled sprite,
distorted sprite corner sampling at a hand-computed
probe, polygon span fill, the gouraud midpoint value,
mesh parity, half transparent blending against previous
frame buffer content, user clipping inside and outside,
both frame change modes with erase fill values, jump
assign and call with return, sprite flips, CLUT lookup,
end codes with ECD on and off, and status readback.

### scu: interrupt status and mask

A thin view over the SCU register page (no shadow copy)
with real IMS and IST words. Wired sources: VBlank-IN,
VBlank-OUT, HBlank-IN, and the VDP1 sprite draw end,
each with its documented vector (0x40 up through 0x4D).
Delivery picks the lowest set unmasked status bit,
which is the documented SCU priority order, and the
system offers one delivery per scanline to the master
SH-2 at level 6, the documented default level for
these sources. Timer, DSP end, sound request, SMPC, pad,
and DMA end sources remain status storage only until
SAT-3 (which completes all of them; see the SAT-3 scu
section).

Gate: unit tests for raise and pending, mask blocking
delivery while status still records, priority order
delivery with software clearing, and the vector table;
system tests prove an SH-2 handler runs through the
bus on delivery and stays silent when masked.

### system: scanline timing and version 2 states

RunFrame now advances scanline by scanline: VDP1 frame
change at the top, then per line the VDP2 timing state,
the SCU raises (VBlank-OUT at line 0, HBlank-IN every
line, VBlank-IN at the first blanking line, which is
line 224 in the default mode), one interrupt delivery,
the CPU slice, the VDP1 draw trigger poll, and the
scanline render. The 477,273 cycle per CPU budget is
split by lines: every line gets CyclesPerFrame divided
by TotalLines, and the first remainder lines of the
frame get one extra cycle (at 263 lines: base 1814,
191 lines get 1815). States are version 2 and
3,708,004 bytes, adding VDP2 VRAM, CRAM, and registers,
VDP1 VRAM, both frame buffer banks, and registers, and
the SCU register page.

Gate: the SAT-1 gates plus a dual CPU determinism gate
where the master programs a VDP2 layer and a VDP1
command list through the bus, a mid-run save is
restored into a fresh machine, and the continuation
state bytes and framebuffer pixels are identical;
pixel probes check the NBG0 pattern colors, sprite
over background priority, and background beside the
sprite.

## What exists in SAT-3

### chips/m68ec000: the SCSP sound CPU

A full integer Motorola 68000 written from the 68000
user manual inside this module (the project rule is one
standalone module per core, so it is not imported from
go-genesis): the complete integer instruction set with
all addressing modes, address error exceptions with
the documented 14 byte group 0 frame, illegal and
privilege exceptions, line A and line F vectors,
autovector interrupts, and a flat cycle model (one base
cycle per instruction plus the manual's EA cycle table
where it is cheap). Divergences chosen and documented
in code: DIVU and DIVS overflow sets V and leaves the
destination unchanged; the BCD overflow flag follows
the symmetric documented model with pinned vectors;
RTE pops only SR and PC (the group 0 frame is
documented as not reliably restartable). Serialize is
exactly 88 bytes.

Conformance outcome, stated plainly: no Tom Harte
680x0 single-step corpus exists in this workspace or
upstream (the Tom Harte tree has no 680x0 set, and the
go-genesis 68000 was differential tested against a
library oracle with no corpus on disk), so the corpus
gate is DEFERRED. The gate here is hand-derived
vectors: 21 tests covering every instruction group,
the address error frame byte for byte, the MOVEM
memory image, DBcc loop counts, TAS, MOVEP,
multi-precision BCD carry chaining, an interrupt entry
at the correct vector, and a serialize round trip with
a deterministic summation program.

### scu: DMA, DSP, timers, and two-CPU delivery

DMA channels 0 to 2 with the documented register sets:
direct mode and the indirect table walk (three long
entries, bit 31 end flag), source and destination add
codes, the start factors (immediate on the enable edge,
VBlank-IN, VBlank-OUT, HBlank-IN, timer 0, timer 1,
sound request, sprite end), address save and update
semantics, and completion through the IST DMA end
bits. Prohibition enforced: a transfer touching the
SCU register page window is skipped and counted by
IllegalDMA (this core's IST map has no DMA illegal
bit; see the divergence note below). The SCU DSP:
program RAM 256 by 32 bit, data RAM 4 banks of 64 by
32 bit, the parallel operation fields (ALU, X
multiplier, Y, D1 move), the hardware loop, DMA
between DSP RAM and the bus, program control through
the register page, and the DSP end interrupt. Gate:
a hand-assembled program computes a dot product over
data RAM with the exact accumulator result 156, and
DSP DMA moves data both ways. Timers: timer 0 in the
dot position model (compare 0 fires at line start),
timer 1 counting lines, gated by the T1MD enable bit
as the manual specifies.

Delivery model: one pending source per scanline is
offered to BOTH SH-2s at the per source levels of the
SCU manual Table 2.1 (LevelOf), in the documented
priority order. IST bits stay set until software clears
them, so both CPUs see the same source; each takes it
only when its own SR mask allows, and the slave is
offered sources only while released. CD block
interrupts arrive as the A-Bus external input at IST
bit 16 (the manual has no CD bit in IST), with a fixed
vector 0x50 and level 8: on hardware the interrupting
device supplies the vector during the acknowledge
cycle, and this core models its one external input
with a fixed assignment. Known divergence, kept from
SAT-2: IST bit 12 is sprite draw end here (the manual
puts DMA illegal at 12 and sprite at 13; the vector
0x4D matches the manual's sprite vector either way).

### scsp: the sound chip and its DSP

Register map from the SCSP manual (ST-77, the ST-068
family): 32 slots of 12 words on a 32 byte stride,
common registers at 0x400, the sound stack at 0x600,
and the DSP register area at 0x700 and up. The chip
shares the 512 KiB sound RAM and the 4 KiB register
page as plain storage with the SH-2 side and polls the
page at sample ticks, so key execution (KYONEX with
KYONB), DMA triggers, and interrupt clears are observed
from either CPU's writes. The 68EC000 runs at
11.2896 MHz inside the 44,100 Hz sample clock, both
advanced from the machine clock by exact rational
accumulation; the phase accumulator is in the state.
Slot engine: 16 bit and 8 bit PCM, all four loop modes,
the EG rate system (AR, D1R, D2R, RR, DL, key rate
scaling) with levels in the manual's attenuation
domain, FM modulation from the previous sample's slot
outputs per MDL and MDXSL/MDYSL, the LFO (all four
waveforms, pitch and amplitude paths), and TL, send,
and pan gains computed from the manual's decibel
figures. Timers A, B, and C with their prescalers; the
interrupt registers in the manual's roles (SCIEB and
friends belong to the sound CPU side, MCIEB to the
main CPU side, pending bits clear through SCIRE and
MCIRE); main CPU requests raise the SCU sound request
source through a callback. CD audio enters on the
EXTS inputs and mixes through the EFREG path of slots
16 and 17, the routing the boot ROM uses; the manual
has no dedicated CD level and pan registers.

Measured gates: a 256 sample loop at unity pitch has
period exactly 256 samples (172.27 Hz, bit exact
across the LEA wrap); OCT plus 1 gives period exactly
128; EG attack at AR 20 reaches full in exactly 128
samples and release passes its checkpoints exactly; a
full-left DIPAN leaves the right channel at exactly
zero; a Timer A handler on the 68EC000 counts exactly
44,100 interrupts over 60 frames of machine cycles;
mid-playback serialize and restore reproduce the next
200 sample ticks bit identically. Serialized size is
1,958 bytes with an empty CD queue (sound RAM and the
register page are the system's, not the chip state's).

DSP coverage boundary, stated plainly: ST-77 does not
publish the FH-1 microprogram encoding, so the DSP
executes a documented subset encoding of this
project's design over the manual's data set (COEF,
MADRS, TEMP ring, MEMS, MIXS, EFREG, EXTS, an
accumulator ALU with load, add, sub, and, or, xor and
shifts, multiply by COEF, and memory access through
MADRS). Real game DSP microcode written for the FH-1
encoding will NOT run on it. Not in the subset: the Y
bus and table addressing, the second accumulator, and
conditionals. The subset is gated by two hand-written
microprograms checked against hand-computed outputs:
a gain of 0.5 through MEMS to EFREG, and a feedback
delay (a 0.5, b 0.25, depth 4) exact for the first 16
outputs. Stored only or stub: MEM4MB, DAC18B, VER, the
MIDI buffers (reads empty), and the INT0 to INT2 input
bits.

### cdblock: the CD block command layer

The register page uses the hardware placement: HIRQ
at page bytes [0x08:0x0A], its mask at [0x0C:0x0E],
CR1 to CR4 at [0x18:0x1A] through [0x24:0x26], and the
data port at [0x28:0x2A] (on hardware the data FIFO
sits at its own CS2 offset; the port's placement
inside the page is this core's model). A command
executes only while HIRQ CMOK is clear; completions
set the documented HIRQ bits and fire the OnIRQ
callback (wired to the SCU A-Bus input) for newly set
bits the mask allows. The command numbering is the
production firmware numbering, verified against
public firmware trace documentation; an earlier draft
numbering in the build notes was superseded by it.

Implemented commands: Get Status (0x00), Get HW Info
(0x01), Get TOC (0x02, through the data FIFO), Get
Session Info (0x03), Initialize (0x04), End Data
Transfer (0x06), Play Disc (0x10), Seek Disc (0x11),
Scan Disc (0x12, 16x, buffers nothing), Get Subcode Q
(0x20, the 10 Q bytes through the data FIFO; no CRC is
appended), Set and Get CD Device Connection (0x30 and
0x31), the filter family (0x40 to 0x47 set and get
range, subheader, mode, and connection, plus reset):
24 filters and 24 buffer partitions sharing one
200 block pool, with filter 0 passing everything to
partition 0 by default. Get Buffer Size (0x50), Get
Sector Number (0x51), Calculate Actual Data Size
(0x52), Get Actual Data Size (0x53), Get Sector Info
(0x54), Execute FAD Search (0x55), Get FAD Search
Result (0x56), Set Sector Length (0x60), Get Sector
Data (0x61), Delete Sector Data (0x62), Get Then
Delete Sector Data (0x63). Play streams at exactly
75 sectors per second by cycle accumulation (the
streaming phase is in the state): audio sectors go to
the SCSP sink and are never buffered, data sectors
route through the filter chain into partitions, and
buffered payloads are stored as descriptors and
re-read from the attached image by FAD after a state
restore. Not implemented: Put Sector Data (0x64)
rejects with the documented 0xFF status (the firmware
implements it with allocation semantics; deferred),
Copy (0x65) and Move (0x66) reject as unknown, and
Authenticate Device is out of scope. Gate: 13 tests
and more than 3,600 assertions over handshakes, TOC
bytes, the buffer command family, filter routing
including Mode 2 subheader file number matching,
CD-DA delivery byte for byte, subcode Q fields, and
the serialize round trip.

### smpc: the system manager

The full register file (IREG0 to IREG6, OREG0 to
OREG31, COMREG, SR, SF, PDR1 and PDR2) with the
documented command protocol in the package's poll
driven model: a command written to COMREG executes at
the next Poll, SF is set by the executing Poll and
clears at the following one. Commands: MSHON, SSHON,
SSHOFF, SNDON, SNDOFF, CDON, CDOFF, SYSRES, CKCHG352
and CKCHG320 (stored and reported; the frame budget
does not switch), INTBACK (the status report with the
RTC fields, then per port peripheral chunks in the
documented Saturn pad layout, across the continuation
protocol), SETTIME, SETSMEM, NMIREQ, RESENAB, and
RESDISA. The RTC advances from machine cycles with
the weekday computed from the date, not trusted from
the set packet. The package was audited line by line
against the SMPC manual (ST-169) during this slice;
four defects were found and fixed (INTBACK port modes
live in IREG0, not IREG1; SNDRES and CDRES are
asserted-high reset signals, so the power on status
now reads 35H and 40H like a hardware capture; one SR
comment). At power on the slave, the sound chip, and
the CD block are all held, matching that status.

### system: SAT-3 wiring and version 3 states

RunFrame steps the devices per scanline after the CPU
slice: the SCSP by the line's cycle budget, then SMPC,
CD block, and SCU polls. The SMPC hooks own the
machine resets: SSHON releases the slave, SSHOFF holds
and resets it, SNDON and SNDOFF release and hold the
SCSP, CDON and CDOFF power the CD block, and NMIREQ
raises the master NMI. AudioBuffer drains the SCSP
mix. States are version 3: the version 2 layout as a
strict prefix, then the sound RAM and SCSP page, the
SMPC and CD pages, the SCU and SMPC states, and the
length prefixed SCSP and CD block states: 4,241,176
bytes for an idle machine (the total varies with the
SCSP CD queue and the CD buffer contents, so StateSize
is now a method reporting the current size).

Slice gate, TestSAT3FullStackDeterminism: the master
boots the machine through the SMPC (SSHON from a CPU
program, SNDON and CDON through the page), the slave
runs its handshake, an SCU DMA copy lands byte exact,
the SCU DSP raises its end interrupt, the CD block
plays the synthetic audio track through the SCSP and
raises the SCU A-Bus input, status reads back PLAY, a
mid-play save restores to a byte identical
continuation of state, framebuffer, and audio
samples, and the CD still reads PLAY afterwards.

SAT-2 gate adjustments in this slice, both forced by
SAT-3 scope: TestVBlankInterruptMaskedByIMS now masks
the timer 0 source as well (bit 3, mask 0x100F) and
asserts IST bits 0x100F, because the timers are wired
into the frame now; the same gate caught that timer 1
must be gated by its T1MD enable bit (it fired every
line at power on before the fix). The state size
assertions use the StateSize method, and the bad state
test truncates a real snapshot, because version 3
states are variable size.

## SAT-4: HLE boot, libretro shell, enginetest (core complete)

### system: BootDisc, the documented HLE boot

BootDisc replaces the boot ROM with its documented
transfers, and no boot ROM bytes are read or embedded
(the BIOS window keeps reading zero). The attached
image's System ID is re-verified, the IP named by the
header IP size field is loaded from the start of the
data area to Work RAM-H at 0x06002000, the boot ROM's
own copies are made (the System ID at 0x06000C00 and
the 32 parameter bytes at 0x060002A0), and the machine
is left in the documented post boot state: the master
SH-2 enters the IP at 0x06002100 (the first byte after
the System ID) with the Stack-M stack pointer, the
slave SH-2 resets to the same entry with the Stack-S
pointer and stays held until the IP releases it with
SMPC SSHON, the SMPC reports its power on status, and
the sound chip and CD block wait for their SMPC ON
commands with the CD block holding the image at
standby. A zero stack field falls back to the
conventional 0x06001000 power on stack (some published
headers leave the fields zero). The host button mask
survives BootDisc's internal reset: buttons are host
input state, not machine state. The old power on
seeding in Reset is kept for the device gates;
BootDisc is the real path, and the enginetest below
boots only through it.

### libretro: the shell

libretro/main.go follows the family pattern: core
name "iTaK GoSaturn", extensions cue|iso, content by
path only, booted through BootDisc. The framebuffer
is presented at the machine's current TVMD size with
SET_GEOMETRY on a change; base geometry 320x224, max
640x480, aspect 4:3. Timing is declared 60.0 fps (the
machine runs 477,273 master cycles per frame at
28.6364 MHz, the NTSC rate; PAL is out of scope) and
44,100 Hz stereo from the SCSP, pixel format
XRGB8888. The pad maps the libretro standard ids to
the Saturn digital pad letter for letter where the
letters exist; Saturn C sits on R2 and Z on L2, and
Select is unmapped (the Saturn pad has none).
RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM is the backup RAM's logical
32 KiB store, exposed directly from the bus.
RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM is Work RAM Low followed by
Work RAM High as one 2 MiB mirror cache with the GBA
shell's hash sync discipline. Serialize goes through
the version 3 system states. retro_reset resets and
re-boots the loaded disc, because a bare reset parks
the CPUs with no program.

### enginetest: the full stack gate

The enginetest package builds a synthetic 24 sector
ISO (IP size 0x4000) whose IP is hand assembled SH-2
(a small two pass assembler is part of the fixture).
Booted only through BootDisc, the IP: releases the
slave with SSHON and completes the 42/43 handshake;
opens the CD block, walks the ISO root through the
data port (reads synchronized one word per scanline
on the SCU HBlank-IN status bit), reads PAYLOAD.BIN
into Work RAM-L and checksums it against the fixture;
programs the SAT-2 gate's VDP2 NBG0 plus VDP1 polygon
display; uploads a 512 byte 68EC000 driver and a sine
table through sound RAM, releases the sound CPU with
SNDON, and the driver keys a PCM slot playing the
table; reads the pad once through SMPC INTBACK; and
round trips 32 bytes through the backup RAM odd byte
path. Milestones land in order in a Work RAM-H block.

Gate results (TestEnginetestDiscFullStack): all 7
milestones set in order within 15 frames; framebuffer
probes exact ((0,0) green, (1,0) red, (105,55) white,
(99,55) black); the tone measures a period of exactly
256.0 samples, 172.27 Hz, the table rate at unity
pitch; the guest payload checksum equals the fixture
checksum and the size reads 1000; the INTBACK report
for the host set mask (Up, A, R, Start) is exactly
F1 02 E3 7F; the backup read back is byte exact; a
mid run save taken just after the sound starts (state
size 4,241,176 bytes) restores to a byte identical
continuation of state, framebuffer, and 44,100 audio
samples. The same disc through the built desktop
libgo_saturn.so in the shared go_backend enginetest
harness reports ALL TESTS PASSED. The shell has its
own in-process gates in libretro/main_test.go.

Two defects were found and fixed on the way, both
verified against the published documentation. The
SAT-1 header parse read the stack fields at the
first read offsets (above, in the cd section). And
the SH-2 core executed opcode 0x0009 as MOVT R0: the
manual gives MOVT the 0x0n29 encoding and 0x0009 is
NOP, changing no register. The SAT-1 behavior was a
directed choice of that slice; it corrupts R0 across
every NOP delay slot whenever the T flag is set,
which breaks real code, so SAT-4 corrects it to the
manual (the one SAT-1 hand test pinning the old
behavior now asserts the manual behavior; the corpus
gates pass unchanged).

### App wiring state

Prepared locally, not pushed (the parent ships):
go_backend/internal/core/types.go's Cores64BitOnly
Saturn entry is now "Go Saturn" with libgo_saturn.so
and extensions cue|iso, and the hardcoded Dart system
grid in flutter_ui/lib/main.dart names libgo_saturn.so
with exts .cue and .iso (.chd dropped: this core does
not read it). tools/autobuild-server.sh has no 64-bit
branch at all (it builds android-arm only and keeps no
explicit core list), so there is nothing to add there
yet: shipping any 64-bit core in the android-64bit
build waits on the parent creating that pipeline
branch (gomobile bind for android/arm64, a flutter
build for android-arm64, and arm64 core asset
staging).

## Slice roadmap

- SAT-2: done. VDP2 backgrounds plus the VDP1 sprite
  and polygon engine, composition, and SCU interrupt
  wiring.
- SAT-3: done. SCU DMA, DSP, and timers with two-CPU
  delivery, SCSP audio with its 68EC000, the CD block
  command layer, SMPC behavior, and version 3 states.
- SAT-4: done. HLE boot through BootDisc, the libretro
  shell, the full stack enginetest gate, and the
  android-64bit wiring preparation. The core is
  complete; the remaining gaps are the honesty notes
  below.

## Honesty notes

- No BIOS bytes anywhere; the boot is the documented
  HLE in system/boot.go.
- The SCSP DSP executes a project subset encoding:
  the FH-1 microprogram encoding is not published in
  ST-77, so real game FH-1 microcode will not run on
  it (SAT-3 note, unchanged).
- CD block Put Sector Data is rejected and Copy and
  Move Sector are unimplemented (SAT-3 note,
  unchanged).
- The m68ec000 corpus gate stays deferred: no Tom
  Harte 680x0 corpus exists in this workspace or the
  SingleStepTests tree, and the ProcessorTests
  repository's 680x0 tree did not fetch (two HTTPS
  tarball attempts against the public repo path
  returned Not Found). The chip is gated by 21 hand
  vector tests and the pinned address error frame.
- PAL timing is out of scope: the shell declares the
  NTSC 60.0 fps frame and the machine runs the NTSC
  cycle budget.
- The shell's SYSTEM_RAM is a mirror cache over the
  two disjoint Work RAM regions, and its retro_reset
  re-boots the disc (see the SAT-4 section for both
  choices and the pad map choice).
- The SH-2 caches are not simulated; CCR is stored only.
- Bus arbitration is round robin and flat.
- The divide unit answers instantly; its hardware
  latency is not modeled.
- The CD block register block is mirrored across its
  window in this slice; real hardware places it at a
  fixed offset inside CS2.
- SMPC, SCSP, CD block, and the full SCU behavior
  landed in SAT-3 (see the SAT-3 sections for their
  coverage boundaries, in particular the SCSP DSP
  subset boundary).
- The SH-2 instruction set is implemented strictly per
  the SH-2 manual, not the wider SH-4 set.

### SAT-2 approximations, each documented in code

- Hi-res and exclusive monitor modes are decoded to
  their pixel dimensions only; the doubled pixel clock
  timing of those modes is not modeled (vdp2 DisplaySize
  and TotalLines).
- VDP1 drawing is instantaneous at the frame change or
  trigger poll, not spread across the frame; EDSR draw
  end is reported at the poll, not at a cycle offset.
- The SCU delivers at most one interrupt source per
  scanline, to the master only, always at level 6
  (SAT-2 model; SAT-3 delivers to both CPUs at the
  per source manual levels).
- Pre-clipping: when a part exceeds the system clip
  with Pclp clear, the effective clip shrinks by one
  dot on the right and bottom only (vdp1 commands.go).
- Gouraud shading does not apply to palette bank sprite
  data or to CLUT entries with bit 15 set (vdp1
  commands.go).
- Color calculation mode 3, prohibited on hardware, is
  treated as replace (vdp1 commands.go).
- The HSS bit is a no-op, and the distorted sprite
  samples its corner texture coordinates clamped to the
  pattern edge (vdp1 commands.go).
- Line drawing steps by the longer axis with integer
  interpolation instead of hardware edge walking (vdp1
  commands.go). Span texture interpolation uses 16 bit
  fraction fixed point (vdp1 commands.go).
- MODR readback is a composed value from TVMR, FBCR,
  and PTMR rather than the hardware status mix (vdp1
  vdp1.go).
- In 8 bit frame buffer mode, color calculation runs on
  the 16 bit value and only the low byte is stored
  (vdp1 vdp1.go).
- Mosaic evaluates the whole layer fetch at the snapped
  sample coordinates, including that position's scroll
  state (vdp2 layers.go and rotation.go).
- Rotation bitmap sizes use the single BMSZ bit in
  CHCTLB, so sizes 0 and 1 only (vdp2 rotation.go).
- RPMD mode 2 probes the coefficient entry of set A at
  dot 0 of the line to pick the line's set (vdp2
  rotation.go). The over pattern reuses the single
  OVPN word as both words of the pattern entry (vdp2
  rotation.go). Screen over mode 3 is treated as
  transparent like mode 2 (vdp2 rotation.go).
- The coefficient KLCE line color path is not
  implemented (vdp2 rotation.go).
- Special priority and special CC mode 3, prohibited on
  hardware, are treated as mode 0 (vdp2 vdp2.go).
- Sprite color calculation permission (SPCCCS) is
  resolved by direct comparison of the sprite priority
  number with the CC number (vdp2 sprite.go). 8 bit
  sprite words are treated as palette dots even when
  SPCLMD selects RGB (vdp2 sprite.go).
- RBG0 and RBG1 share the single CHCTLB and PNCR
  character control block and one window control byte,
  as the register file provides only one (vdp2
  rotation.go and windows.go).
- With the ZMCTL reduction bits clear, the zoom
  increment comes from the ZM registers exactly as
  programmed; an increment of 0 freezes sampling, as
  the manual's register definition implies (vdp2
  layers.go).
- Extended background (EXBG) input is not implemented;
  NBG0 and NBG1 render independently. Gradation
  calculation is not implemented. MSB shadow is not
  implemented (vdp2 vdp2.go).
- The VDP1 register page returns stored values on read;
  hardware returns real values only for LOPR, COPR, and
  MODR and garbage elsewhere.


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/bus/bus.go ====================

// Package bus implements the shared Sega Saturn memory bus.
//
// Two SH-2 CPUs, a sound CPU, the SCU, both VDPs, the SMPC, the CD block
// and the cartridge port all sit behind one big endian address space.
// This slice provides plain storage for every region listed in the
// package contract, the MINIT and SINIT capture flags, and the SH-2
// on-chip divide unit. It does not model bus wait states, DMA, or any
// device command behaviour.
//
// Simplifications baked into this slice, stated plainly:
//
//   - The BIOS window reads as zero. No BIOS bytes exist in this core,
//     the window is an HLE stub.
//   - The A-bus CS0 and CS1 cartridge windows and the A-bus dummy area
//     read as the open value zero and ignore writes.
//   - The CD block register page mirrors one 64 byte block across the
//     whole CS2 window. Real hardware places the block at CS2 offset
//     0x90000 with its registers at the offsets defined below; mirroring
//     the block everywhere is the simplification for this slice.
//   - The SCU DSP program and data RAMs are not present yet. Only the
//     256 byte SCU register page is stored here; the DSP RAMs are a
//     later slice.
//   - Sound CPU work RAM is 512 KiB mirrored across its 1 MiB window.
//   - Division is computed immediately on the trigger write. The 39
//     cycle hardware latency is not modelled.
//   - On quotient overflow the remainder stored is the value computed
//     from the saturated quotient, truncated to 32 bits. The divide by
//     zero remainder follows the documented partial behaviour instead:
//     the dividend shifted right 29 places, arithmetic.
//   - Since SAT-2 the VDP1 frame buffer storage holds both 256 KiB
//     banks. The CPU window at 0x05C80000 maps the current draw bank
//     only, matching the hardware rule that the display bank is not
//     CPU accessible. SetVDP1DrawBank selects the mapped bank; the
//     system flips it when the VDP1 swaps banks at a frame change.
package bus

import "math"

// Exported divide unit register addresses. These are the documented
// SH7604 absolute addresses inside the on-chip window.
const (
	RegDVSR   uint32 = 0xFFFFFF00
	RegDVDNT  uint32 = 0xFFFFFF04
	RegDVCR   uint32 = 0xFFFFFF08
	RegVCRDIV uint32 = 0xFFFFFF0C
	RegDVDNTH uint32 = 0xFFFFFF10
	RegDVDNTL uint32 = 0xFFFFFF14
)

// Aliases used by some Saturn documentation for the same registers.
const (
	RegDIVSOR uint32 = RegDVSR
	RegDVDEN  uint32 = RegDVCR
	RegDIVSRC uint32 = RegDVDNTH
)

// CD block register offsets within the mirrored 64 byte block.
const (
	CDHIRQ     uint32 = 0x08
	CDHIRQMask uint32 = 0x0C
	CDCR1      uint32 = 0x18
	CDCR2      uint32 = 0x1C
	CDCR3      uint32 = 0x20
	CDCR4      uint32 = 0x24
)

// Short aliases for the CD block register offsets.
const (
	HIRQ     uint32 = CDHIRQ
	HIRQMask uint32 = CDHIRQMask
	CR1      uint32 = CDCR1
	CR2      uint32 = CDCR2
	CR3      uint32 = CDCR3
	CR4      uint32 = CDCR4
)

const (
	maskAddr     uint32 = 0x1FFFFFFF
	onChipBase   uint32 = 0x1FFFFE00
	onChipTop    uint32 = 0x1FFFFFFF
	onChipSize          = 0x200
	divFileStart uint32 = 0x100
	divFileEnd   uint32 = 0x120
)

// Divide register offsets inside the on-chip window.
const (
	divOffDVSR         uint32 = 0x100
	divOffDVDNT        uint32 = 0x104
	divOffDVCR         uint32 = 0x108
	divOffVCRDIV       uint32 = 0x10C
	divOffDVDNTH       uint32 = 0x110
	divOffDVDNTL       uint32 = 0x114
	divOffDVDNTHMirror uint32 = 0x118
	divOffDVDNTLMirror uint32 = 0x11C
)

// divUnit holds one CPU divide unit register file.
// The file is five storage words plus the control and vector words:
// divisor, dividend and quotient word, control, vector, dividend high
// and remainder word, and dividend low and quotient mirror word.
type divUnit struct {
	dvsr   uint32
	dvdnt  uint32
	dvcr   uint32
	vcrdiv uint32
	dvdnth uint32
	dvdntl uint32
}

// regValue returns the word stored for a divide register offset.
// The two mirror offsets read back the high and low words.
func (d *divUnit) regValue(off uint32) uint32 {
	switch off {
	case divOffDVSR:
		return d.dvsr
	case divOffDVDNT:
		return d.dvdnt
	case divOffDVCR:
		return d.dvcr
	case divOffVCRDIV:
		return d.vcrdiv
	case divOffDVDNTH, divOffDVDNTHMirror:
		return d.dvdnth
	case divOffDVDNTL, divOffDVDNTLMirror:
		return d.dvdntl
	}
	return 0
}

// assign stores a word without triggering a division.
// A write to the control word follows the hardware rule as a plain
// store: writing bit 0 as zero clears the overflow flag, writing it
// as one leaves the stored word with the flag set.
func (d *divUnit) assign(off uint32, v uint32) {
	switch off {
	case divOffDVSR:
		d.dvsr = v
	case divOffDVDNT:
		d.dvdnt = v
	case divOffDVCR:
		d.dvcr = v
	case divOffVCRDIV:
		d.vcrdiv = v
	case divOffDVDNTH, divOffDVDNTHMirror:
		d.dvdnth = v
	case divOffDVDNTL, divOffDVDNTLMirror:
		d.dvdntl = v
	}
}

// runDivide performs one signed division, truncating toward zero.
// dividend is the full signed dividend, the divisor is the stored
// DVSR word read as a signed value.
func (d *divUnit) runDivide(dividend int64) {
	divisor := int32(d.dvsr)
	if divisor == 0 {
		d.dvcr |= 1
		var q int32
		if dividend >= 0 {
			q = math.MaxInt32
		} else {
			q = math.MinInt32
		}
		rem := int32(dividend >> 29)
		d.dvdnt = uint32(q)
		d.dvdntl = uint32(q)
		d.dvdnth = uint32(rem)
		return
	}
	// One documented special case: the most negative 32 bit dividend
	// divided by negative one is not overflow on this unit. It yields
	// the most negative value as the quotient and zero as remainder.
	if dividend == int64(math.MinInt32) && divisor == -1 {
		d.dvdnt = 0x80000000
		d.dvdntl = d.dvdnt
		d.dvdnth = 0
		return
	}
	q64 := dividend / int64(divisor)
	if q64 > int64(math.MaxInt32) || q64 < int64(math.MinInt32) {
		d.dvcr |= 1
		var q int32
		if q64 > 0 {
			q = math.MaxInt32
		} else {
			q = math.MinInt32
		}
		// Stated choice for this slice: the remainder on quotient
		// overflow is computed from the saturated quotient and then
		// truncated to 32 bits.
		rem := int32(dividend - int64(q)*int64(divisor))
		d.dvdnt = uint32(q)
		d.dvdntl = uint32(q)
		d.dvdnth = uint32(rem)
		return
	}
	q := int32(q64)
	rem := int32(dividend - q64*int64(divisor))
	d.dvdnt = uint32(q)
	d.dvdntl = uint32(q)
	d.dvdnth = uint32(rem)
}

// write32 stores a full word in the divide file, triggering a
// division for the two documented trigger offsets.
func (d *divUnit) write32(off uint32, v uint32) {
	switch off {
	case divOffDVDNT:
		// The written value sign extends to a 64 bit dividend.
		d.runDivide(int64(int32(v)))
	case divOffDVDNTL:
		// The stored high word and the written low word form the
		// 64 bit dividend.
		bits := uint64(d.dvdnth)<<32 | uint64(v)
		d.runDivide(int64(bits))
	default:
		d.assign(off, v)
	}
}

// Bus is the shared Saturn memory bus. The zero value is not usable;
// build one with New.
type Bus struct {
	workLow  []byte
	workHigh []byte
	backup   []byte
	smpc     [128]byte
	cdRegs   [64]byte
	soundRAM []byte
	scspRegs []byte
	vdp1VRAM []byte
	vdp1FB   []byte
	vdp1Draw int
	vdp1Regs [128]byte
	vdp2VRAM []byte
	vdp2CRAM []byte
	vdp2Regs [512]byte
	scuRegs  [256]byte
	onChip   [2][onChipSize]byte
	div      [2]divUnit
	capture  [2]bool
	current  int
}

// New returns a bus with all storage zeroed.
func New() *Bus {
	return &Bus{
		workLow:  make([]byte, 1<<20),
		workHigh: make([]byte, 1<<20),
		backup:   make([]byte, 32<<10),
		soundRAM: make([]byte, 512<<10),
		scspRegs: make([]byte, 4<<10),
		vdp1VRAM: make([]byte, 512<<10),
		vdp1FB:   make([]byte, 512<<10),
		vdp2VRAM: make([]byte, 512<<10),
		vdp2CRAM: make([]byte, 4<<10),
	}
}

// SetCurrentCPU selects whose on-chip register window answers in the
// on-chip range: 0 for the master, 1 for the slave. Other values are
// ignored so a bad selector cannot corrupt the current choice.
func (b *Bus) SetCurrentCPU(id int) {
	if id == 0 || id == 1 {
		b.current = id
	}
}

// WorkRAMLow returns the 1 MiB Work RAM-L backing store, for save
// states. Writes through the slice are visible through the bus.
func (b *Bus) WorkRAMLow() []byte { return b.workLow }

// WorkRAMHigh returns the 1 MiB Work RAM-H backing store.
func (b *Bus) WorkRAMHigh() []byte { return b.workHigh }

// BackupRAM returns the 32 KiB logical backup data store. This is the
// packed data, not the odd byte window layout seen on the bus.
func (b *Bus) BackupRAM() []byte { return b.backup }

// VDP1VRAM returns the 512 KiB VDP1 VRAM backing store. The vdp1
// package wraps this slice; writes through the slice are visible
// through the bus and the other way around.
func (b *Bus) VDP1VRAM() []byte { return b.vdp1VRAM }

// VDP1Framebuffer returns the full VDP1 frame buffer storage: two
// 256 KiB banks, bank 0 first. The CPU window maps only the draw
// bank (see SetVDP1DrawBank); this accessor exists for the vdp1
// package and for save states.
func (b *Bus) VDP1Framebuffer() []byte { return b.vdp1FB }

// SetVDP1DrawBank selects which frame buffer bank the CPU window at
// 0x05C80000 maps: 0 or 1. Other values are ignored. The vdp1
// package owns the bank state; the system calls this after a frame
// change so CPU accesses follow the swap.
func (b *Bus) SetVDP1DrawBank(bank int) {
	if bank == 0 || bank == 1 {
		b.vdp1Draw = bank
	}
}

// VDP1DrawBank reports the bank the CPU frame buffer window maps.
func (b *Bus) VDP1DrawBank() int { return b.vdp1Draw }

// VDP1Registers returns the 128 byte VDP1 register page backing.
func (b *Bus) VDP1Registers() []byte { return b.vdp1Regs[:] }

// VDP2VRAM returns the 512 KiB VDP2 VRAM backing store.
func (b *Bus) VDP2VRAM() []byte { return b.vdp2VRAM }

// VDP2CRAM returns the 4 KiB VDP2 color RAM backing store. The raw
// bytes live here; the vdp2 package applies the CRAM mode address
// rules on its read path.
func (b *Bus) VDP2CRAM() []byte { return b.vdp2CRAM }

// VDP2Registers returns the 512 byte VDP2 register page backing.
func (b *Bus) VDP2Registers() []byte { return b.vdp2Regs[:] }

// SCURegisters returns the 256 byte SCU register page backing.
func (b *Bus) SCURegisters() []byte { return b.scuRegs[:] }

// SMPCRegisters returns the 128 byte SMPC register page backing.
// The smpc package wraps this slice; only odd bus offsets are
// stored, matching the window decode.
func (b *Bus) SMPCRegisters() []byte { return b.smpc[:] }

// CDRegisters returns the 64 byte CD block register page backing.
// The cdblock package wraps this slice; the page is mirrored
// across the CS2 window by the address decode.
func (b *Bus) CDRegisters() []byte { return b.cdRegs[:] }

// SoundRAM returns the 512 KiB SCSP sound RAM backing store. The
// scsp package and its 68EC000 share this slice with the SH-2
// window at 0x05A00000.
func (b *Bus) SoundRAM() []byte { return b.soundRAM }

// SCSPRegisters returns the 4 KiB SCSP register page backing.
// The scsp package wraps this slice; the SH-2 window at
// 0x05B00000 mirrors it.
func (b *Bus) SCSPRegisters() []byte { return b.scspRegs }

// CaptureEvent reports whether the given CPU has a pending FRT
// capture flag raised by a 16 bit write to the other CPU MINIT or
// SINIT window. Reading a pending flag clears it, so a true result
// is delivered exactly once.
func (b *Bus) CaptureEvent(cpu int) bool {
	if cpu != 0 && cpu != 1 {
		return false
	}
	if !b.capture[cpu] {
		return false
	}
	b.capture[cpu] = false
	return true
}

// Divide32 divides dividend by the stored divisor of the given CPU
// divide unit, through the same code path as a DVDNT trigger write.
// It returns the resulting quotient and remainder.
func (b *Bus) Divide32(cpu int, dividend int32) (quotient, remainder int32) {
	if cpu != 0 && cpu != 1 {
		return 0, 0
	}
	d := &b.div[cpu]
	d.write32(divOffDVDNT, uint32(dividend))
	return int32(d.dvdnt), int32(d.dvdnth)
}

// Divide64 divides a 64 bit dividend by the stored divisor of the
// given CPU divide unit, through the same code path as a DVDNTL
// trigger write. It returns the resulting quotient and remainder.
func (b *Bus) Divide64(cpu int, dividend int64) (quotient, remainder int32) {
	if cpu != 0 && cpu != 1 {
		return 0, 0
	}
	d := &b.div[cpu]
	d.dvdnth = uint32(uint64(dividend) >> 32)
	d.write32(divOffDVDNTL, uint32(uint64(dividend)&0xFFFFFFFF))
	return int32(d.dvdnt), int32(d.dvdnth)
}

// isOnChip reports whether a masked address falls in the on-chip
// register window. Checking the masked form first means the original
// 0xFFFFFE00 range and every cache alias of it land here before the
// external decode below can claim the address.
func isOnChip(masked uint32) bool {
	return masked >= onChipBase && masked <= onChipTop
}

// divByte reads one big endian lane byte of a divide register word.
func (b *Bus) divByte(off uint32) uint8 {
	base := off &^ uint32(3)
	lane := off & uint32(3)
	word := b.div[b.current].regValue(base)
	shift := (3 - lane) * 8
	return uint8(word >> shift)
}

// writeDivByte composes one byte into a divide register word without
// triggering a division. Partial writes update storage only; only a
// full 32 bit write to a trigger offset starts a division.
func (b *Bus) writeDivByte(off uint32, v uint8) {
	base := off &^ uint32(3)
	lane := off & uint32(3)
	d := &b.div[b.current]
	word := d.regValue(base)
	shift := (3 - lane) * 8
	word &^= uint32(0xFF) << shift
	word |= uint32(v) << shift
	d.assign(base, word)
}

// read8At reads one byte at an already masked address.
func (b *Bus) read8At(masked uint32) uint8 {
	if isOnChip(masked) {
		off := masked - onChipBase
		if off >= divFileStart && off < divFileEnd {
			return b.divByte(off)
		}
		return b.onChip[b.current][off]
	}
	switch {
	case masked < 0x00100000:
		// BIOS window: HLE stub, reads return zero.
		return 0
	case masked < 0x00180000:
		off := masked - 0x00100000
		if off&1 == 0 {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return b.smpc[off&0x7F]
	case masked < 0x00200000:
		off := masked - 0x00180000
		if off&1 == 0 {
			return 0xFF
		}
		return b.backup[(off>>1)&0x7FFF]
	case masked < 0x00300000:
		return b.workLow[masked-0x00200000]
	case masked < 0x01000000:
		return 0
	case masked < 0x02000000:
		// MINIT and SINIT windows read as all ones.
		return 0xFF
	case masked < 0x05000000:
		// A-bus CS0, CS1: open value zero.
		return 0
	case masked < 0x05800000:
		// A-bus dummy area.
		return 0
	case masked < 0x05900000:
		return b.cdRegs[(masked-0x05800000)&0x3F]
	case masked < 0x05A00000:
		return 0
	case masked < 0x05B00000:
		return b.soundRAM[(masked-0x05A00000)&0x7FFFF]
	case masked < 0x05C00000:
		return b.scspRegs[(masked-0x05B00000)&0xFFF]
	case masked < 0x05C80000:
		return b.vdp1VRAM[masked-0x05C00000]
	case masked < 0x05D00000:
		return b.vdp1FB[b.vdp1Draw*0x40000+int((masked-0x05C80000)&0x3FFFF)]
	case masked < 0x05D80000:
		return b.vdp1Regs[(masked-0x05D00000)&0x7F]
	case masked < 0x05E00000:
		return 0
	case masked < 0x05F00000:
		return b.vdp2VRAM[(masked-0x05E00000)&0x7FFFF]
	case masked < 0x05F80000:
		return b.vdp2CRAM[(masked-0x05F00000)&0xFFF]
	case masked < 0x05FC0000:
		return b.vdp2Regs[(masked-0x05F80000)&0x1FF]
	case masked < 0x05FE0000:
		return 0
	case masked < 0x05FF0000:
		return b.scuRegs[(masked-0x05FE0000)&0xFF]
	case masked < 0x06000000:
		return 0
	case masked < 0x08000000:
		return b.workHigh[(masked-0x06000000)&0xFFFFF]
	}
	return 0
}

// write8At writes one byte at an already masked address.
func (b *Bus) write8At(masked uint32, v uint8) {
	if isOnChip(masked) {
		off := masked - onChipBase
		if off >= divFileStart && off < divFileEnd {
			b.writeDivByte(off, v)
			return
		}
		b.onChip[b.current][off] = v
		return
	}
	switch {
	case masked < 0x00100000:
		// BIOS window: writes ignored.
	case masked < 0x00180000:
		off := masked - 0x00100000
		if off&1 == 1 {
			b.smpc[off&0x7F] = v
		}
	case masked < 0x00200000:
		off := masked - 0x00180000
		// A write at any offset lands in the logical cell. Writing
		// an even byte is the same as writing its odd neighbour.
		b.backup[(off>>1)&0x7FFF] = v
	case masked < 0x00300000:
		b.workLow[masked-0x00200000] = v
	case masked < 0x05000000:
		// MINIT, SINIT and cartridge windows: byte writes have no
		// effect. In particular a byte write never raises a capture
		// flag; only an exact 16 bit write does.
	case masked < 0x05800000:
		// A-bus dummy area: writes ignored.
	case masked < 0x05900000:
		b.cdRegs[(masked-0x05800000)&0x3F] = v
	case masked < 0x05A00000:
		// Unmapped gap: writes ignored.
	case masked < 0x05B00000:
		b.soundRAM[(masked-0x05A00000)&0x7FFFF] = v
	case masked < 0x05C00000:
		b.scspRegs[(masked-0x05B00000)&0xFFF] = v
	case masked < 0x05C80000:
		b.vdp1VRAM[masked-0x05C00000] = v
	case masked < 0x05D00000:
		b.vdp1FB[b.vdp1Draw*0x40000+int((masked-0x05C80000)&0x3FFFF)] = v
	case masked < 0x05D80000:
		b.vdp1Regs[(masked-0x05D00000)&0x7F] = v
	case masked < 0x05E00000:
		// Unmapped gap: writes ignored.
	case masked < 0x05F00000:
		b.vdp2VRAM[(masked-0x05E00000)&0x7FFFF] = v
	case masked < 0x05F80000:
		b.vdp2CRAM[(masked-0x05F00000)&0xFFF] = v
	case masked < 0x05FC0000:
		b.vdp2Regs[(masked-0x05F80000)&0x1FF] = v
	case masked < 0x05FE0000:
		// Unmapped gap: writes ignored.
	case masked < 0x05FF0000:
		b.scuRegs[(masked-0x05FE0000)&0xFF] = v
	case masked < 0x06000000:
		// Unmapped gap: writes ignored.
	case masked < 0x08000000:
		b.workHigh[(masked-0x06000000)&0xFFFFF] = v
	}
}

// Read8 reads one byte. The address is masked to the external decode
// space first, so cache and cache through aliases land on the same
// storage as their plain forms.
func (b *Bus) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	return b.read8At(addr & maskAddr)
}

// Read16 reads one big endian 16 bit word, composed of byte reads.
func (b *Bus) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	hi := uint16(b.Read8(addr))
	lo := uint16(b.Read8(addr + 1))
	return hi<<8 | lo
}

// Read32 reads one big endian 32 bit word, composed of byte reads.
func (b *Bus) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	b0 := uint32(b.Read8(addr))
	b1 := uint32(b.Read8(addr + 1))
	b2 := uint32(b.Read8(addr + 2))
	b3 := uint32(b.Read8(addr + 3))
	return b0<<24 | b1<<16 | b2<<8 | b3
}

// Write8 writes one byte.
func (b *Bus) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) {
	b.write8At(addr&maskAddr, v)
}

// Write16 writes one big endian 16 bit word. A write of exactly this
// size to the MINIT window raises the slave capture flag, and one to
// the SINIT window raises the master capture flag. Everywhere else
// the write is composed of two byte writes.
func (b *Bus) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	masked := addr & maskAddr
	if !isOnChip(masked) {
		if masked >= 0x01000000 && masked < 0x01800000 {
			b.capture[1] = true
			return
		}
		if masked >= 0x01800000 && masked < 0x02000000 {
			b.capture[0] = true
			return
		}
	}
	b.write8At(masked, uint8(v>>8))
	b.write8At((addr+1)&maskAddr, uint8(v))
}

// Write32 writes one big endian 32 bit word. A full word write to a
// divide unit trigger register starts a division; a full word write
// anywhere else is composed of byte writes. A 32 bit write to the
// MINIT or SINIT window does not raise a capture flag.
func (b *Bus) Write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	masked := addr & maskAddr
	if isOnChip(masked) {
		off := masked - onChipBase
		if off >= divFileStart && off < divFileEnd && off&3 == 0 {
			b.div[b.current].write32(off, v)
			return
		}
	}
	b.write8At(masked, uint8(v>>24))
	b.write8At((addr+1)&maskAddr, uint8(v>>16))
	b.write8At((addr+2)&maskAddr, uint8(v>>8))
	b.write8At((addr+3)&maskAddr, uint8(v))
}

	}

==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/cd/cd.go ====================

// Package cd reads Saturn disc images in ISO and cue sheet form.
//
// It exposes raw and user sector reads, a small ISO9660 reader for the
// root directory of the primary volume, and a parser for the Saturn IP
// header that lives in the first sector of a game disc.
package cd

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

// Track describes one track of a disc image in the virtual disc layout.
//
// Start is the logical block address of the track INDEX 01 position.
// Pregap sectors occupy the virtual sectors immediately before Start and
// read back as zeros. Length counts only the data sectors of the track,
// from Start up to the next track pregap or the end of the image.
type Track struct {
	Number     int
	Mode       int
	Form2      bool
	SectorSize int
	Pregap     int
	Start      int
	Length     int
	FileOffset int64
}

// trackState pairs the public Track description with the file sector
// index of the track INDEX 01 position inside the backing data.
type trackState struct {
	pub      Track
	rawIndex int
}

// Image is an opened disc image. The whole backing file is held in
// memory, which keeps the layout logic simple and is adequate for the
// synthetic and tooling uses this package targets.
type Image struct {
	data       []byte
	tracks     []trackState
	total      int
	synthRaw   bool
	detectMode bool
}

// OpenISO opens a plain 2048 byte per sector data image holding a
// single Mode 1 track.
func OpenISO(path string) (*Image, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: open iso %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	im, err := newSingleTrack(data, 2048, 1)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	im.synthRaw = true
	return im, nil
}

// OpenBytes builds an in memory single track image from data.
//
// A sector size of 2048 means a Mode 1 track. A sector size of 2352
// means raw sectors whose mode is detected per sector from the sector
// header, with Mode 2 subheader form detection on Mode 2 sectors.
// Sector sizes 2336 and 2324 are accepted as Mode 2 raw forms.
func OpenBytes(data []byte, sectorSize int) (*Image, error) {
	mode := 0
	switch sectorSize {
	case 2048:
		mode = 1
	case 2352, 2336, 2324:
		mode = 2
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: unsupported sector size %d", sectorSize)
	}
	cp := make([]byte, len(data))
	copy(cp, data)
	im, err := newSingleTrack(cp, sectorSize, mode)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if sectorSize == 2352 {
		im.detectMode = true
	}
	if sectorSize == 2324 {
		im.tracks[0].pub.Form2 = true
	}
	return im, nil
}

// newSingleTrack validates data against sectorSize and builds an Image
// with one track starting at virtual sector zero.
func newSingleTrack(data []byte, sectorSize int, mode int) (*Image, error) {
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: empty image")
	}
	if len(data)%sectorSize != 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: image size %d is not a multiple of sector size %d", len(data), sectorSize)
	}
	n := len(data) / sectorSize
	st := trackState{
		pub: Track{
			Number:     1,
			Mode:       mode,
			SectorSize: sectorSize,
			Start:      0,
			Length:     n,
			FileOffset: 0,
		},
		rawIndex: 0,
	}
	return &Image{data: data, tracks: []trackState{st}, total: n}, nil
}

// Tracks returns a copy of the track table.
func (im *Image) Tracks() []Track {
	out := make([]Track, len(im.tracks))
	for i, st := range im.tracks {
		out[i] = st.pub
	}
	return out
}

// NumSectors returns the total number of virtual sectors, including
// pregap sectors that read back as zeros.
func (im *Image) NumSectors() int {
	return im.total
}

// locate finds the track state owning virtual sector lba. It reports
// whether the sector is a pregap sector of that track.
func (im *Image) locate(lba int) (trackState, bool, error) {
	if lba < 0 || lba >= im.total {
		return trackState{}, false, fmt.Errorf("cd: sector %d out of range, image has %d sectors", lba, im.total)
	}
	for _, st := range im.tracks {
		segStart := st.pub.Start - st.pub.Pregap
		segEnd := st.pub.Start + st.pub.Length
		if lba >= segStart && lba < segEnd {
			return st, lba < st.pub.Start, nil
		}
	}
	return trackState{}, false, fmt.Errorf("cd: sector %d is not mapped to any track", lba)
}

// ReadSector returns the user data of one virtual sector: 2048 bytes
// for Mode 1 and Mode 2 Form 1 tracks, 2324 bytes for Mode 2 Form 2
// sectors. Pregap sectors return zero filled user data. Reading an
// audio sector returns an error.
func (im *Image) ReadSector(lba int) ([]byte, error) {
	st, pregap, err := im.locate(lba)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if st.pub.Mode == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: sector %d is an audio sector, not data", lba)
	}
	if pregap {
		return make([]byte, userSize(st.pub, nil)), nil
	}
	raw, err := im.storedSector(st, lba)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return im.extractUser(st, raw)
}

// ReadRawSector returns the full raw sector as stored, SectorSize
// bytes. Pregap sectors return zero filled raw sectors. For images
// opened with OpenISO a raw 2352 byte Mode 1 sector is synthesized
// around the stored 2048 data bytes, with a sync pattern, an MSF header
// for lba plus 150, and a zero filled EDC and ECC tail.
func (im *Image) ReadRawSector(lba int) ([]byte, error) {
	st, pregap, err := im.locate(lba)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if pregap {
		return make([]byte, st.pub.SectorSize), nil
	}
	if im.synthRaw {
		user, err := im.storedSector(st, lba)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return synthesizeRawMode1(lba, user), nil
	}
	return im.storedSector(st, lba)
}

// storedSector returns a copy of the raw stored bytes for a data
// sector of the given track at virtual sector lba.
func (im *Image) storedSector(st trackState, lba int) ([]byte, error) {
	size := int64(st.pub.SectorSize)
	off := st.pub.FileOffset + int64(lba-st.pub.Start)*size
	if off < 0 || off+size > int64(len(im.data)) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: sector %d maps outside the backing data", lba)
	}
	out := make([]byte, size)
	copy(out, im.data[off:off+size])
	return out, nil
}

// userSize gives the user data size for a track, consulting a raw
// sector when one is supplied because Mode 2 form varies per sector.
func userSize(t Track, raw []byte) int {
	if t.Mode == 2 {
		if t.SectorSize == 2324 {
			return 2324
		}
		if raw != nil && len(raw) >= 24 && form2Sector(raw, t.SectorSize) {
			return 2324
		}
		if t.Form2 {
			return 2324
		}
	}
	return 2048
}

// extractUser pulls the user data bytes out of one raw stored sector.
func (im *Image) extractUser(st trackState, raw []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	t := st.pub
	switch t.SectorSize {
	case 2048:
		return append([]byte(nil), raw...), nil
	case 2324:
		return append([]byte(nil), raw...), nil
	case 2336:
		if form2Sector(raw, 2336) {
			return append([]byte(nil), raw[8:2332]...), nil
		}
		return append([]byte(nil), raw[8:2056]...), nil
	case 2352:
		mode := t.Mode
		if im.detectMode {
			hdr := int(raw[15])
			if hdr == 1 || hdr == 2 {
				mode = hdr
			}
		}
		if mode == 1 {
			return append([]byte(nil), raw[16:2064]...), nil
		}
		if mode == 2 {
			if form2Sector(raw, 2352) {
				return append([]byte(nil), raw[24:2348]...), nil
			}
			return append([]byte(nil), raw[24:2072]...), nil
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: unsupported sector mode %d", mode)
	}
	return nil, fmt.Errorf("cd: unsupported sector size %d", t.SectorSize)
}

// form2Sector reports whether a Mode 2 raw sector is Form 2. The form
// bit is bit 5 of the subheader submode byte. In a 2352 byte sector the
// subheader starts at byte 16, so the submode byte is byte 18 with its
// duplicate at byte 22. In a 2336 byte sector the subheader starts at
// byte 0, so the submode byte is byte 2 with its duplicate at byte 6.
// As a tolerance for writers that place the value one byte later, the
// byte pair after the submode pair is also accepted when both copies
// carry the form bit.
func form2Sector(raw []byte, sectorSize int) bool {
	base := 16
	if sectorSize == 2336 {
		base = 0
	}
	if len(raw) < base+8 {
		return false
	}
	if raw[base+2]&0x20 != 0 || raw[base+6]&0x20 != 0 {
		return true
	}
	if raw[base+3]&0x20 != 0 && raw[base+7]&0x20 != 0 {
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// synthesizeRawMode1 wraps 2048 user bytes in a raw 2352 byte Mode 1
// sector for virtual sector lba.
func synthesizeRawMode1(lba int, user []byte) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 2352)
	out[0] = 0x00
	for i := 1; i <= 10; i++ {
		out[i] = 0xff
	}
	out[11] = 0x00
	m, s, f := LBAtoMSF(lba)
	out[12] = toBCD(m)
	out[13] = toBCD(s)
	out[14] = toBCD(f)
	out[15] = 1
	copy(out[16:2064], user)
	return out
}

// toBCD converts a value in the range 0 to 99 to binary coded decimal.
func toBCD(v int) byte {
	return byte((v/10)<<4 | (v % 10))
}

// fromBCD converts a binary coded decimal byte back to an integer.
func fromBCD(b byte) int {
	return int(b>>4)*10 + int(b&0x0f)
}

// MSFtoLBA converts a minutes, seconds, frames position to a logical
// block address. The 150 sector offset accounts for the disc lead in
// area, so the position 0 minutes, 2 seconds, 0 frames is LBA zero.
func MSFtoLBA(m, s, f int) int {
	return (m*60+s)*75 + f - 150
}

// LBAtoMSF converts a logical block address back to minutes, seconds
// and frames. It is the inverse of MSFtoLBA.
func LBAtoMSF(lba int) (m, s, f int) {
	total := lba + 150
	m = total / 4500
	rem := total % 4500
	s = rem / 75
	f = rem % 75
	return m, s, f
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/cd/cd_test.go ====================

package cd

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// assertions counts every named check in this file so the suite can
// prove its own coverage at the end.
var assertions int

func check(t *testing.T, cond bool, format string, args ...any) {
	t.Helper()
	assertions++
	if !cond {
		t.Fatalf(format, args...)
	}
}

func checkBytes(t *testing.T, got []byte, want []byte, what string) {
	t.Helper()
	assertions++
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("%s mismatch: got %d bytes starting %v, want %d bytes starting %v", what, len(got), first8(got), len(want), first8(want))
	}
}

func first8(b []byte) []byte {
	if len(b) > 8 {
		return b[:8]
	}
	return b
}

var helloContents = []byte("Hello, Saturn world, from a synthetic disc.\n")

func dataBinContents() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 5000)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = byte(i*7 + 3)
	}
	return out
}

// putText writes s into a fixed width field at off, padding the rest of
// the field with spaces.
func putText(sec []byte, off int, width int, s string) {
	for i := 0; i < width; i++ {
		sec[off+i] = ' '
	}
	copy(sec[off:off+width], s)
}

// putBothEndian32 writes a 32 bit value as little endian followed by
// big endian, the ISO9660 both endian form.
func putBothEndian32(rec []byte, off int, v uint32) {
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rec[off:off+4], v)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[off+4:off+8], v)
}

// dirRecord builds one ISO9660 directory record.
func dirRecord(extent int, size int, flags byte, name []byte) []byte {
	length := 33 + len(name)
	if length%2 == 1 {
		length++
	}
	rec := make([]byte, length)
	rec[0] = byte(length)
	putBothEndian32(rec, 2, uint32(extent))
	putBothEndian32(rec, 10, uint32(size))
	rec[18] = 0x7c
	rec[19] = 1
	rec[20] = 1
	rec[25] = flags
	rec[32] = byte(len(name))
	copy(rec[33:], name)
	return rec
}

// buildISO constructs a synthetic 2048 byte sector ISO9660 image with
// a Saturn IP header in sector zero, a primary volume descriptor at
// sector 16, a root directory at sector 20, HELLO.TXT at sector 21 and
// DATA.BIN spanning sectors 22 to 24.
func buildISO() []byte {
	const total = 25
	img := make([]byte, total*2048)

	// Sector 0: Saturn IP header.
	sec0 := img[0:2048]
	copy(sec0[0:16], "SEGA SEGASATURN ")
	putText(sec0, 0x10, 16, "SEGA ENTERPRISES")
	putText(sec0, 0x20, 10, "MK-12345")
	putText(sec0, 0x2a, 6, "V1.000")
	putText(sec0, 0x30, 8, "19960101")
	putText(sec0, 0x38, 8, "CD-1/1")
	putText(sec0, 0x40, 10, "JTUE")
	putText(sec0, 0x50, 16, "JOYPAD")
	putText(sec0, 0x60, 112, "SYNTHETIC TEST")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(sec0[0xe0:0xe4], 0x1000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(sec0[0xe8:0xec], 0x06001000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(sec0[0xec:0xf0], 0x06000800)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(sec0[0xf0:0xf4], 0x06010000)

	// Sector 16: primary volume descriptor.
	pvd := img[16*2048 : 17*2048]
	pvd[0] = 1
	copy(pvd[1:6], "CD001")
	pvd[6] = 1
	copy(pvd[156:190], dirRecord(20, 2048, 2, []byte{0}))

	// Sector 17: volume descriptor terminator.
	term := img[17*2048 : 18*2048]
	term[0] = 255
	copy(term[1:6], "CD001")
	term[6] = 1

	// Sector 20: root directory records.
	root := img[20*2048 : 21*2048]
	off := 0
	for _, rec := range [][]byte{
		dirRecord(20, 2048, 2, []byte{0}),
		dirRecord(20, 2048, 2, []byte{1}),
		dirRecord(21, len(helloContents), 0, []byte("HELLO.TXT;1")),
		dirRecord(22, len(dataBinContents()), 0, []byte("DATA.BIN;1")),
	} {
		copy(root[off:], rec)
		off += len(rec)
	}

	// Sectors 21 to 24: file contents.
	copy(img[21*2048:], helloContents)
	copy(img[22*2048:], dataBinContents())
	return img
}

// wrapMode1Raw wraps every 2048 byte sector of iso in a raw 2352 byte
// Mode 1 sector with sync, a BCD MSF header and a zero tail.
func wrapMode1Raw(iso []byte) []byte {
	n := len(iso) / 2048
	out := make([]byte, n*2352)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		sec := out[i*2352 : (i+1)*2352]
		sec[0] = 0x00
		for j := 1; j <= 10; j++ {
			sec[j] = 0xff
		}
		sec[11] = 0x00
		m, s, f := LBAtoMSF(i)
		sec[12] = toBCD(m)
		sec[13] = toBCD(s)
		sec[14] = toBCD(f)
		sec[15] = 1
		copy(sec[16:2064], iso[i*2048:(i+1)*2048])
	}
	return out
}

// writeFile is a small test helper that writes data and fails on error.
func writeFile(t *testing.T, path string, data []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write %s: %v", path, err)
	}
}

func TestMSFConversions(t *testing.T) {
	check(t, MSFtoLBA(0, 2, 0) == 0, "MSFtoLBA(0,2,0) = %d, want 0", MSFtoLBA(0, 2, 0))
	check(t, MSFtoLBA(1, 0, 0) == 4350, "MSFtoLBA(1,0,0) = %d, want 4350", MSFtoLBA(1, 0, 0))
	check(t, MSFtoLBA(0, 0, 0) == 0-150, "MSFtoLBA(0,0,0) = %d, want %d", MSFtoLBA(0, 0, 0), 0-150)
	m, s, f := LBAtoMSF(0)
	check(t, m == 0 && s == 2 && f == 0, "LBAtoMSF(0) = %d:%d:%d, want 0:2:0", m, s, f)
	m, s, f = LBAtoMSF(4350)
	check(t, m == 1 && s == 0 && f == 0, "LBAtoMSF(4350) = %d:%d:%d, want 1:0:0", m, s, f)
	m, s, f = LBAtoMSF(MSFtoLBA(12, 34, 56))
	check(t, m == 12 && s == 34 && f == 56, "round trip = %d:%d:%d, want 12:34:56", m, s, f)
}

func TestOpenBytesAndSaturnHeader(t *testing.T) {
	iso := buildISO()
	im, err := OpenBytes(iso, 2048)
	check(t, err == nil, "OpenBytes error: %v", err)
	check(t, im.NumSectors() == 25, "NumSectors = %d, want 25", im.NumSectors())
	tr := im.Tracks()
	check(t, len(tr) == 1, "tracks = %d, want 1", len(tr))
	check(t, tr[0].Mode == 1 && tr[0].SectorSize == 2048, "track mode %d size %d, want 1 and 2048", tr[0].Mode, tr[0].SectorSize)
	check(t, tr[0].Start == 0 && tr[0].Length == 25, "track start %d length %d, want 0 and 25", tr[0].Start, tr[0].Length)

	sec0, err := im.ReadSector(0)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(0) error: %v", err)
	checkBytes(t, sec0[0:16], []byte("SEGA SEGASATURN "), "sector 0 signature")
	pvd, err := im.ReadSector(16)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(16) error: %v", err)
	check(t, pvd[0] == 1 && string(pvd[1:6]) == "CD001", "PVD marker wrong: type %d id %q", pvd[0], string(pvd[1:6]))

	h, err := im.SaturnHeader()
	check(t, err == nil, "SaturnHeader error: %v", err)
	check(t, h.Signature == "SEGA SEGASATURN ", "Signature = %q", h.Signature)
	check(t, h.MakerID == "SEGA ENTERPRISES", "MakerID = %q", h.MakerID)
	check(t, h.ProductNumber == "MK-12345", "ProductNumber = %q", h.ProductNumber)
	check(t, h.Version == "V1.000", "Version = %q", h.Version)
	check(t, h.ReleaseDate == "19960101", "ReleaseDate = %q", h.ReleaseDate)
	check(t, h.DeviceInfo == "CD-1/1", "DeviceInfo = %q", h.DeviceInfo)
	check(t, h.AreaSymbols == "JTUE", "AreaSymbols = %q", h.AreaSymbols)
	check(t, h.Peripherals == "JOYPAD", "Peripherals = %q", h.Peripherals)
	check(t, h.Title == "SYNTHETIC TEST", "Title = %q", h.Title)
	check(t, h.MasterStack == 0x06001000, "MasterStack = %#x, want 0x06001000", h.MasterStack)
	check(t, h.SlaveStack == 0x06000800, "SlaveStack = %#x, want 0x06000800", h.SlaveStack)
	check(t, h.IPSize == 0x1000, "IPSize = %#x, want 0x1000", h.IPSize)
	check(t, h.FirstReadAddress == 0x06010000, "FirstReadAddress = %#x, want 0x06010000", h.FirstReadAddress)
}

func TestISOListRootAndReadFile(t *testing.T) {
	im, err := OpenBytes(buildISO(), 2048)
	check(t, err == nil, "OpenBytes error: %v", err)
	entries, err := im.ListRoot()
	check(t, err == nil, "ListRoot error: %v", err)
	check(t, len(entries) == 2, "root entries = %d, want 2", len(entries))
	check(t, entries[0].Name == "HELLO.TXT", "entry 0 name = %q", entries[0].Name)
	check(t, entries[1].Name == "DATA.BIN", "entry 1 name = %q", entries[1].Name)
	check(t, entries[0].LBA == 21 && entries[0].Size == len(helloContents), "HELLO.TXT lba %d size %d", entries[0].LBA, entries[0].Size)
	check(t, entries[1].LBA == 22 && entries[1].Size == 5000, "DATA.BIN lba %d size %d", entries[1].LBA, entries[1].Size)
	check(t, !entries[0].IsDir && !entries[1].IsDir, "file entries marked as directories")
	hello, err := im.ReadFile(entries[0])
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadFile HELLO.TXT error: %v", err)
	checkBytes(t, hello, helloContents, "HELLO.TXT contents")
	data, err := im.ReadFile(entries[1])
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadFile DATA.BIN error: %v", err)
	check(t, len(data) == 5000, "DATA.BIN read length = %d, want 5000", len(data))
	checkBytes(t, data, dataBinContents(), "DATA.BIN contents spanning 3 sectors")
	_, err = im.ReadFile(FileEntry{Name: "ROOT", LBA: 20, Size: 2048, IsDir: true})
	check(t, err != nil, "ReadFile on a directory should fail")
}

func TestCueRawMode1(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	iso := buildISO()

	writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "disc.bin"), bin)
	cue := "FILE \"disc.bin\" BINARY\n  TRACK 01 MODE1/2352\n    INDEX 01 00:00:00\n"
	writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "disc.cue"), []byte(cue))

	check(t, im.NumSectors() == 25, "NumSectors = %d, want 25", im.NumSectors())
	sec, err := im.ReadSector(16)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(16) error: %v", err)
	checkBytes(t, sec, iso[16*2048:17*2048], "raw cue PVD user sector")
	raw, err := im.ReadRawSector(3)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadRawSector(3) error: %v", err)
	checkBytes(t, raw, bin[3*2352:4*2352], "raw cue stored sector 3")
	entries, err := im.ListRoot()
	check(t, err == nil, "ListRoot error: %v", err)
	check(t, len(entries) == 2, "root entries = %d, want 2", len(entries))
	content, err := im.ReadFile(entries[1])
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadFile error: %v", err)
	checkBytes(t, content, dataBinContents(), "raw cue DATA.BIN contents")
	h, err := im.SaturnHeader()
	check(t, err == nil, "SaturnHeader error: %v", err)
	check(t, h.Title == "SYNTHETIC TEST", "Title = %q", h.Title)
}

func TestCueIndex00Pregap(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	const sectors = 65
	img := make([]byte, sectors*2048)
	for i := 0; i < sectors; i++ {
		sec := img[i*2048 : (i+1)*2048]
		for j := range sec {
			sec[j] = 0xee
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		sec := img[i*2048 : (i+1)*2048]
		for j := range sec {
			sec[j] = byte(i + 1)
		}
	}
	for i := 60; i < sectors; i++ {
		sec := img[i*2048 : (i+1)*2048]
		for j := range sec {
			sec[j] = byte(0xa0 + i - 60)
		}
	}
	writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "two.bin"), img)
	cue := strings.Join([]string{
		"FILE \"two.bin\" BINARY",
		"  TRACK 01 MODE1/2048",
		"    INDEX 01 00:00:00",
		"  TRACK 02 MODE1/2048",
		"    INDEX 00 00:00:10",
		"    INDEX 01 00:00:60",
		"",
	}, "\n")
	writeFile(t, filepath.Join(dir, "two.cue"), []byte(cue))
	im, err := OpenCue(filepath.Join(dir, "two.cue"))
	check(t, err == nil, "OpenCue error: %v", err)
	tr := im.Tracks()
	check(t, len(tr) == 2, "tracks = %d, want 2", len(tr))
	check(t, tr[0].Start == 0 && tr[0].Length == 10, "track 1 start %d length %d, want 0 and 10", tr[0].Start, tr[0].Length)
	check(t, tr[1].Pregap == 50, "track 2 pregap = %d, want 50", tr[1].Pregap)
	check(t, tr[1].Start == 60, "track 2 start = %d, want 60", tr[1].Start)
	check(t, tr[1].Length == 5, "track 2 length = %d, want 5", tr[1].Length)
	check(t, tr[1].FileOffset == 60*2048, "track 2 file offset = %d, want %d", tr[1].FileOffset, 60*2048)
	check(t, im.NumSectors() == 65, "NumSectors = %d, want 65", im.NumSectors())
	last, err := im.ReadSector(9)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(9) error: %v", err)
	check(t, last[0] == 10 && last[2047] == 10, "track 1 last sector fill = %d", last[0])
	pre, err := im.ReadSector(10)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(10) error: %v", err)
	check(t, len(pre) == 2048 && pre[0] == 0 && pre[2047] == 0, "pregap sector should be zeros, first byte %d", pre[0])
	preRaw, err := im.ReadRawSector(59)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadRawSector(59) error: %v", err)
	check(t, len(preRaw) == 2048 && preRaw[0] == 0 && preRaw[2047] == 0, "pregap raw sector should be zeros")
	t2, err := im.ReadSector(60)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(60) error: %v", err)
	check(t, t2[0] == 0xa0 && t2[2047] == 0xa0, "track 2 first sector fill = %#x, want 0xa0", t2[0])
}

func TestCuePregapCommand(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()

	for i := 0; i < 7; i++ {
		sec := img[i*2048 : (i+1)*2048]

		"    INDEX 01 00:00:00",
		"  TRACK 02 MODE1/2048",
		"    PREGAP 00:00:25",
		"    INDEX 01 00:00:04",

	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(29) error: %v", err)
