package cdblock

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/cd"
)

var assertions int

func check(t *testing.T, cond bool, format string, args ...any) {
	t.Helper()
	assertions++
	if !cond {
		t.Fatalf(format, args...)
	}
}

func checkBytes(t *testing.T, got []byte, want []byte, what string) {
	t.Helper()
	assertions++
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("%s mismatch: got %d bytes starting %v, want %d bytes starting %v", what, len(got), first8(got), len(want), first8(want))
	}
}

func first8(b []byte) []byte {
	if len(b) > 8 {
		return b[:8]
	}
	return b
}

// Page access helpers, using the register layout of the package:
// HIRQ at [0x08:0x0A], its mask at [0x0C:0x0E], CR n (1 to 4) at
// [0x18+4(n-1):0x1A+4(n-1)], and the data port at [0x28:0x2A].

func pageCR(page []byte, n int) uint16 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint16(page[0x18+4*(n-1) : 0x1A+4*(n-1)])
}

func pageSetCR(page []byte, n int, v uint16) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(page[0x18+4*(n-1):0x1A+4*(n-1)], v)
}

func pageHIRQ(page []byte) uint16 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint16(page[0x08:0x0A])
}

func pageSetHIRQ(page []byte, v uint16) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(page[0x08:0x0A], v)
}

func pageSetMask(page []byte, v uint16) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(page[0x0C:0x0E], v)
}

func pagePort(page []byte) uint16 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint16(page[0x28:0x2A])
}

func statusByte(page []byte) byte {
	return byte(pageCR(page, 1) >> 8)
}

// issue clears HIRQ (the host acknowledgement), writes a command
// and its parameters into the CRs, and polls once.
func issue(page []byte, b *Block, crs [4]uint16) {
	pageSetHIRQ(page, 0)
	for i, v := range crs {
		pageSetCR(page, i+1, v)
	}
	b.Poll()
}

func issueCmd(page []byte, b *Block, cmd byte) {
	issue(page, b, [4]uint16{uint16(cmd) << 8, 0, 0, 0})
}

// drain reads n words from the data port, polling after each
// read to advance the FIFO, and returns the bytes.
func drain(page []byte, b *Block, words int) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 0, words*2)
	for i := 0; i < words; i++ {
		w := pagePort(page)
		out = append(out, byte(w>>8), byte(w))
		b.Poll()
	}
	return out
}

// sectorCmd builds the parameter set shared by the sector data
// commands in this package's numbering: CR2 sector offset, CR3
// partition in the high byte, CR4 sector count.
func sectorCmd(cmd byte, off, part, count int) [4]uint16 {
	return [4]uint16{uint16(cmd) << 8, uint16(off), uint16(part) << 8, uint16(count)}
}

func sectorNumber(page []byte, b *Block, part int) int {
	issue(page, b, sectorCmd(CmdGetSectorNumber, 0, part, 0))
	return int(pageCR(page, 4))
}

// playRange issues a Play Disc for a FAD range with the given
// play mode byte.
func playRange(page []byte, b *Block, startFAD, endFAD int, mode byte) {
	s := uint32(0x800000 | startFAD)
	e := uint32(0x800000 | endFAD)
	issue(page, b, [4]uint16{
		uint16(CmdPlayDisc)<<8 | uint16(byte(s>>16)),
		uint16(s & 0xFFFF),
		uint16(mode)<<8 | uint16(byte(e>>16)),
		uint16(e & 0xFFFF),
	})
}

// makeMode1Sector builds one raw 2352 byte Mode 1 sector whose
// user bytes follow a known pattern seeded by seed.
func makeMode1Sector(lba int, seed int) []byte {
	sec := make([]byte, 2352)
	for j := 1; j <= 10; j++ {
		sec[j] = 0xff
	}
	m, s, f := cd.LBAtoMSF(lba)
	sec[12] = toBCD(m)
	sec[13] = toBCD(s)
	sec[14] = toBCD(f)
	sec[15] = 1
	for j := 0; j < 2048; j++ {
		sec[16+j] = byte(seed + j*3)
	}
	return sec
}

// dataImage builds a single track raw Mode 1 image of n sectors.
func dataImage(t *testing.T, n int) *cd.Image {
	t.Helper()
	var raw []byte
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		raw = append(raw, makeMode1Sector(i, i*40+5)...)
	}
	im, err := cd.OpenBytes(raw, 2352)
	check(t, err == nil, "OpenBytes data image: %v", err)
	return im
}

// twoTrackImage builds a cue and bin pair in a temp dir: track 1
// is 4 raw Mode 1 data sectors, track 2 is 90 audio sectors whose
// bytes follow a known pattern.
func twoTrackImage(t *testing.T) *cd.Image {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	var bin []byte
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		bin = append(bin, makeMode1Sector(i, i*40+5)...)
	}
	for s := 0; s < 90; s++ {
		sec := make([]byte, 2352)
		for j := range sec {
			sec[j] = byte(j*3 + s*11)
		}
		bin = append(bin, sec...)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "two.bin"), bin, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write bin: %v", err)
	}
	cue := "FILE \"two.bin\" BINARY\n" +
		"  TRACK 01 MODE1/2352\n    INDEX 01 00:00:00\n" +
		"  TRACK 02 AUDIO\n    INDEX 01 00:00:04\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "two.cue"), []byte(cue), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write cue: %v", err)
	}
	im, err := cd.OpenCue(filepath.Join(dir, "two.cue"))
	check(t, err == nil, "OpenCue two track: %v", err)
	tr := im.Tracks()
	check(t, len(tr) == 2 && tr[1].Mode == 0 && tr[1].Start == 4, "two track layout = %+v", tr)
	return im
}

func TestHandshakeAndStatus(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)

	// No disc: Get Status reports NO DISC and sets CMOK.
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetStatus)
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQCMOK != 0, "CMOK not set after Get Status, HIRQ = %#x", pageHIRQ(page))
	check(t, statusByte(page) == StatusNODISC, "no disc status = %#x, want %#x", statusByte(page), StatusNODISC)
	check(t, pageCR(page, 1)&0xFF == 0, "flag and repeat low byte = %#x, want 0", pageCR(page, 1)&0xFF)

	// With a disc: STANDBY, and the FAD field reads the home
	// position 150 split across CR3 low byte and CR4.
	b.SetImage(dataImage(t, 4))
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetStatus)
	check(t, statusByte(page) == StatusSTANDBY, "disc status = %#x, want STANDBY", statusByte(page))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 0x4101, "status CR2 = %#x, want ctrl/adr 0x41 and track 1", pageCR(page, 2))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 3) == 0x0100, "status CR3 = %#x, want index 1 and FAD high 0", pageCR(page, 3))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 4) == 150, "status CR4 = %d, want FAD low 150", pageCR(page, 4))

	// OnIRQ fires when the newly set bit is unmasked, and stays
	// quiet when the mask clears it.
	fires := 0
	b.OnIRQ = func() { fires++ }
	pageSetMask(page, HIRQCMOK)
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetHardwareInfo)
	check(t, fires == 1, "OnIRQ fires = %d, want 1 with CMOK unmasked", fires)
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 0x0002, "hardware info CR2 = %#x, want version 2", pageCR(page, 2))
	pageSetMask(page, 0)
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetStatus)
	check(t, fires == 1, "OnIRQ fires = %d, want still 1 with CMOK masked", fires)

	// A second identical Get Status still executes, because the
	// response tuple differs from the command tuple.
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQCMOK != 0, "CMOK not set on repeated Get Status")

	// Power off: Poll does nothing, no CMOK response.
	b.SetPower(false)
	pageSetHIRQ(page, 0)
	pageSetCR(page, 1, uint16(CmdGetStatus)<<8)
	b.Poll()
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQCMOK == 0, "CMOK set while power is off")
	b.SetPower(true)
}

func TestGetTOCAndEndTransfer(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	b.SetImage(twoTrackImage(t))

	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetTOC)
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQDRDY != 0, "DRDY not set after Get TOC")
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 6, "TOC size = %d words, want 6 (3 entries)", pageCR(page, 2))
	got := drain(page, b, 6)
	want := []byte{
		0x41, 0, 0, 150, // track 1, data, FAD 150
		0x01, 0, 0, 154, // track 2, audio, FAD 154
		0x41, 0, 0, 244, // lead-out at FAD 244 (94 sectors in all)
	}
	checkBytes(t, got, want, "TOC entries")
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQDRDY == 0, "DRDY still set after TOC drained")
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRKEHST != 0, "EHST not set after TOC drained")

	// End Data Transfer mid FIFO: EHST sets and DRDY clears.
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetTOC)
	drain(page, b, 2)
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdEndDataTransfer)
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRKEHST != 0, "EHST not set after End Data Transfer")
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQDRDY == 0, "DRDY still set after End Data Transfer")
	words := int(pageCR(page, 1)&0xFF)<<16 | int(pageCR(page, 2))
	check(t, words == 2, "transferred word count = %d, want 2", words)
}

func TestPlayDataBufferAndSectorData(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	im := dataImage(t, 6)
	b.SetImage(im)

	playRange(page, b, 150, 153, 0)
	check(t, statusByte(page) == StatusPLAY, "status after Play = %#x, want PLAY", statusByte(page))
	b.Advance(28636400)
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQPEND != 0, "PEND not set at play end")
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 4, "partition 0 count = %d, want 4", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))

	// Get Sector Data returns the first sector's user bytes.
	issue(page, b, sectorCmd(CmdGetSectorData, 0, 0, 1))
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQDRDY != 0, "DRDY not set after Get Sector Data")
	user0, err := im.ReadSector(0)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(0): %v", err)
	got := drain(page, b, 1024)
	checkBytes(t, got, user0, "Get Sector Data sector 0")
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRKEHST != 0, "EHST not set after sector data drained")

	// Sector info and actual size over the buffered range.
	issue(page, b, sectorCmd(CmdGetSectorInfo, 1, 0, 0))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 151, "sector info FAD = %d, want 151", pageCR(page, 2))
	issue(page, b, sectorCmd(CmdCalcActualSize, 0, 0, 2))
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetActualSize)
	words := int(pageCR(page, 1)&0xFF)<<16 | int(pageCR(page, 2))
	check(t, words == 2048, "actual size = %d words, want 2048 (2 sectors of 2048 bytes)", words)

	// FAD search finds the block holding FAD 152.
	issue(page, b, [4]uint16{uint16(CmdExecuteFADSearch) << 8, 0, 0, 152})
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetFADSearch)
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 2, "FAD search position = %d, want 2", pageCR(page, 2))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 4) == 152, "FAD search FAD = %d, want 152", pageCR(page, 4))

	// Get Then Delete returns the same first sector and then
	// removes it.
	issue(page, b, sectorCmd(CmdGetThenDelete, 0, 0, 1))
	got = drain(page, b, 1024)
	checkBytes(t, got, user0, "Get Then Delete sector 0")
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 3, "count after Get Then Delete = %d, want 3", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))

	// Delete removes one more.
	issue(page, b, sectorCmd(CmdDeleteSectorData, 0, 0, 1))
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRKEHST != 0, "EHST not set after Delete Sector Data")
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 2, "count after Delete = %d, want 2", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))
}

func TestFilterReverseMode(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	b.SetImage(dataImage(t, 4))

	// Reverse the match on filter 0: everything falls to its
	// false connection, which is discard, so nothing buffers.
	issue(page, b, [4]uint16{uint16(CmdSetFilterMode)<<8 | FilterModeReverse, 0, 0, 0})
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetFilterMode)
	check(t, pageCR(page, 1)&0xFF == FilterModeReverse, "filter mode readback = %#x", pageCR(page, 1)&0xFF)
	playRange(page, b, 150, 152, 0)
	b.Advance(28636400)
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 0, "count with reversed filter = %d, want 0", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))

	// Back to pass all: the same range buffers.
	issue(page, b, [4]uint16{uint16(CmdSetFilterMode)<<8 | 0, 0, 0, 0})
	playRange(page, b, 150, 152, 0)
	b.Advance(28636400)
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 3, "count with pass all filter = %d, want 3", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))
}

func TestFilterSubheaderFileNumber(t *testing.T) {
	// Three raw Mode 2 sectors with file numbers 0, 1 and 1.
	var raw []byte
	for i, fn := range []byte{0, 1, 1} {
		sec := make([]byte, 2352)
		for j := 1; j <= 10; j++ {
			sec[j] = 0xff
		}
		m, s, f := cd.LBAtoMSF(i)
		sec[12] = toBCD(m)
		sec[13] = toBCD(s)
		sec[14] = toBCD(f)
		sec[15] = 2
		sec[16] = fn
		sec[17] = 0
		sec[18] = 0x08 // submode: end of record style data flag pattern kept simple
		sec[19] = 0
		copy(sec[20:24], sec[16:20])
		for j := 0; j < 2048; j++ {
			sec[24+j] = byte(i*50 + j)
		}
		raw = append(raw, sec...)
	}
	im, err := cd.OpenBytes(raw, 2352)
	check(t, err == nil, "OpenBytes Mode 2: %v", err)

	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	b.SetImage(im)

	// Filter 0: file number condition valid, file number 1.
	issue(page, b, [4]uint16{uint16(CmdSetFilterSubhead) << 8, 0, 1, 0})
	issue(page, b, [4]uint16{uint16(CmdSetFilterMode)<<8 | FilterModeFN, 0, 0, 0})
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetFilterSubhead)
	check(t, pageCR(page, 3)&0xFF == 1, "filter file number readback = %d, want 1", pageCR(page, 3)&0xFF)

	playRange(page, b, 150, 152, 0)
	b.Advance(28636400)
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 2, "FN filtered count = %d, want 2", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))

	// The first buffered block is the second sector (file 1).
	issue(page, b, sectorCmd(CmdGetSectorInfo, 0, 0, 0))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 151, "first FN match FAD = %d, want 151", pageCR(page, 2))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 3)>>8 == 1, "first FN match file number = %d, want 1", pageCR(page, 3)>>8)
}

func TestAudioPlayAndSink(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	im := twoTrackImage(t)
	b.SetImage(im)

	var calls [][]int16
	b.SetAudioSink(func(samples []int16) {
		calls = append(calls, append([]int16(nil), samples...))
	})

	// Track 2 runs from FAD 154 to 156.
	playRange(page, b, 154, 156, 0)
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetStatus)
	check(t, statusByte(page) == StatusPLAY, "status during play = %#x, want PLAY", statusByte(page))

	b.Advance(381819) // one sector period
	check(t, len(calls) == 1, "sink calls after one period = %d, want 1", len(calls))
	check(t, len(calls[0]) == 1176, "samples per sector = %d, want 1176 (588 stereo pairs)", len(calls[0]))

	b.Advance(28636400)
	check(t, len(calls) == 3, "sink calls total = %d, want 3", len(calls))
	for s := 0; s < 3; s++ {
		raw, err := im.ReadRawSector(4 + s)
		check(t, err == nil, "ReadRawSector audio %d: %v", s, err)
		for j := 0; j < 1176; j++ {
			want := int16(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(raw[j*2:]))
			if calls[s][j] != want {
				t.Fatalf("sector %d sample %d = %d, want %d from fixture bytes", s, j, calls[s][j], want)
			}
			assertions++
		}
	}
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQPEND != 0, "PEND not set at audio play end")
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetStatus)
	check(t, statusByte(page) == StatusPAUSE, "status after play end = %#x, want PAUSE", statusByte(page))

	// Audio sectors are never buffered.
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 0, "buffered audio sectors = %d, want 0", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))
}

func TestSeekAndSubcodeQ(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	b.SetImage(twoTrackImage(t))

	seek := func(fad int) {
		pos := uint32(0x800000 | fad)
		issue(page, b, [4]uint16{
			uint16(CmdSeekDisc)<<8 | uint16(byte(pos>>16)),
			uint16(pos & 0xFFFF), 0, 0,
		})
	}
	subcode := func() []byte {
		issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetSubcodeQ)
		check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 5, "subcode size = %d words, want 5", pageCR(page, 2))
		check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQDRDY != 0, "DRDY not set after Get Subcode Q")
		return drain(page, b, 5)
	}

	seek(154)
	q := subcode()
	check(t, len(q) == 10, "subcode Q length = %d, want 10 (CRC bytes not included)", len(q))
	check(t, q[0] == 0x01, "Q control/ADR = %#x, want 0x01 audio", q[0])
	check(t, q[1] == 0x02, "Q track = %#x, want BCD 2", q[1])
	check(t, q[2] == 0x01, "Q index = %#x, want BCD 1", q[2])
	check(t, q[3] == 0 && q[4] == 0 && q[5] == 0, "Q relative MSF = %v, want 0:0:0", q[3:6])
	check(t, q[6] == 0, "Q zero byte = %d", q[6])
	am, as, af := cd.LBAtoMSF(4)
	check(t, q[7] == toBCD(am) && q[8] == toBCD(as) && q[9] == toBCD(af),
		"Q absolute MSF bytes = %v, want BCD of %d:%d:%d", q[7:10], am, as, af)

	// One second into track 2: relative 0:01:00, absolute frame
	// advances by 75.
	seek(154 + 75)
	q = subcode()
	check(t, q[3] == 0 && q[4] == 0x01 && q[5] == 0, "Q relative MSF = %v, want BCD 0:1:0", q[3:6])
	am, as, af = cd.LBAtoMSF(4 + 75)
	check(t, q[7] == toBCD(am) && q[8] == toBCD(as) && q[9] == toBCD(af),
		"Q absolute MSF bytes = %v, want BCD of %d:%d:%d", q[7:10], am, as, af)
}

func TestSerializeRoundTripLazyRead(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	im := dataImage(t, 5)
	b.SetImage(im)
	playRange(page, b, 150, 152, 0)
	b.Advance(28636400)
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 3, "pre save count = %d, want 3", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))

	state := b.Serialize()
	check(t, len(state) == stateFiltersEnd+2+3*blockRecord, "state size = %d", len(state))

	page2 := make([]byte, 64)
	b2 := New(page2)
	err := b2.Deserialize(state)
	check(t, err == nil, "Deserialize: %v", err)
	b2.SetImage(im)
	check(t, sectorNumber(page2, b2, 0) == 3, "restored count = %d, want 3", sectorNumber(page2, b2, 0))

	// The restored blocks carry no payloads, so this read re
	// reads sector 1 from the image by FAD.
	issue(page2, b2, sectorCmd(CmdGetSectorData, 1, 0, 1))
	user1, err := im.ReadSector(1)
	check(t, err == nil, "ReadSector(1): %v", err)
	got := drain(page2, b2, 1024)
	checkBytes(t, got, user1, "lazy re-read of restored sector 1")

	bad := append([]byte(nil), state...)
	bad[0] = 99
	check(t, b2.Deserialize(bad) != nil, "Deserialize should reject a bad version")
	check(t, b2.Deserialize(state[:10]) != nil, "Deserialize should reject a short state")
}

func TestGetBufferSize(t *testing.T) {
	page := make([]byte, 64)
	b := New(page)
	b.SetImage(dataImage(t, 6))

	// Fresh buffer: total 200 blocks, all 200 free, maximum
	// selectors 24 in the high byte of CR3.
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetBufferSize)
	check(t, pageHIRQ(page)&HIRQESEL != 0, "ESEL not set after Get Buffer Size")
	check(t, pageCR(page, 4) == 200, "total blocks = %d, want 200", pageCR(page, 4))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 200, "free blocks fresh = %d, want 200", pageCR(page, 2))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 3)>>8 == NumFilters, "maximum selectors = %d, want %d", pageCR(page, 3)>>8, NumFilters)

	// Buffer four sectors: free drops to 200 minus the used
	// count and the total stays 200.
	playRange(page, b, 150, 153, 0)
	b.Advance(28636400)
	check(t, sectorNumber(page, b, 0) == 4, "buffered count = %d, want 4", sectorNumber(page, b, 0))
	issueCmd(page, b, CmdGetBufferSize)
	check(t, pageCR(page, 4) == 200, "total blocks after buffering = %d, want 200", pageCR(page, 4))
	check(t, pageCR(page, 2) == 196, "free blocks after buffering 4 = %d, want 196", pageCR(page, 2))
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/chips/m68ec000/ea.go ====================

package m68ec000

// Effective address decoding, operand access, and flag
// arithmetic. Sizes are 1, 2, or 4 throughout this file.

func sizeMask(size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return 0xFF
	case 2:
		return 0xFFFF
	default:
		return 0xFFFFFFFF
	}
}

func sizeBits(size int) uint {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return 8
	case 2:
		return 16
	default:
		return 32
	}
}

func signBit(size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return 0x80
	case 2:
		return 0x8000
	default:
		return 0x80000000
	}
}

func sext(v uint32, size int) int32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return int32(int8(v))
	case 2:
		return int32(int16(v))
	default:
		return int32(v)
	}
}

// ea is a decoded effective address. Exactly one of the
// dn, an, mem, or imm forms is set.
type ea struct {
	mode   int
	reg    int
	addr   uint32
	dn     bool
	an     bool
	mem    bool
	imm    bool
	immVal uint32
	cycles int
}

// eaCycles is the manual effective address adder for a
// byte or word operand; long operands add 4 for the
// memory forms, applied by decodeEA.
func eaCycles(mode, reg int) int {
	switch mode {
	case 0, 1:
		return 0
	case 2, 3:
		return 4
	case 4:
		return 6
	case 5:
		return 8
	case 6:
		return 10
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			return 8
		case 1:
			return 12
		case 2:
			return 8
		case 3:
			return 10
		case 4:
			return 4
		}
	}
	return 0
}

// indexValue evaluates the index register of an index
// extension word: bit 15 selects an address register,
// bits 14 to 12 the register, bit 11 the size (word,
// sign extended, or long).
func (c *CPU) indexValue(ext uint16) uint32 {
	idx := uint32(0)
	if ext&0x8000 != 0 {
		idx = c.a[(ext>>12)&7]
	} else {
		idx = c.d[(ext>>12)&7]
	}
	if ext&0x0800 == 0 {
		idx = uint32(int32(int16(idx)))
	}
	return idx
}

// decodeEA decodes the low six bits of op, consuming any
// extension words at the PC. It applies postincrement
// and predecrement address register updates. Byte
// accesses through the stack pointer adjust by 2 so the
// stack stays word aligned, per the manual.
func (c *CPU) decodeEA(op uint16, size int) ea {
	mode := int((op >> 3) & 7)
	reg := int(op & 7)
	e := ea{mode: mode, reg: reg, cycles: eaCycles(mode, reg)}
	if size == 4 && mode >= 2 {
		e.cycles += 4
	}
	adj := size
	if size == 1 && reg == 7 {
		adj = 2
	}
	switch mode {
	case 0:
		e.dn = true
	case 1:
		e.an = true
	case 2:
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = c.a[reg]
	case 3:
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = c.a[reg]
		c.a[reg] += uint32(adj)
	case 4:
		e.mem = true
		c.a[reg] -= uint32(adj)
		e.addr = c.a[reg]
	case 5:
		disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + disp)
	case 6:
		ext := c.fetchExt()
		disp := int32(int8(ext))
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + disp + int32(c.indexValue(ext)))
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			e.mem = true
			e.addr = uint32(int32(int16(c.fetchExt())))
		case 1:
			e.mem = true
			hi := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			lo := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			e.addr = hi<<16 | lo
		case 2:
			base := c.pc
			disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
			e.mem = true
			e.addr = uint32(int32(base) + disp)
		case 3:
			base := c.pc
			ext := c.fetchExt()
			disp := int32(int8(ext))
			e.mem = true
			e.addr = uint32(int32(base) + disp + int32(c.indexValue(ext)))
		case 4:
			e.imm = true
			switch size {
			case 1:
				e.immVal = uint32(c.fetchExt() & 0xFF)
			case 2:
				e.immVal = uint32(c.fetchExt())
			case 4:
				hi := uint32(c.fetchExt())
				lo := uint32(c.fetchExt())
				e.immVal = hi<<16 | lo
			}
		default:
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
	}
	return e
}

// controlAddr decodes an effective address for the
// control modes used by LEA, PEA, JSR, JMP, and MOVEM:
// modes 2, 5, 6, and absolute, plus PC relative for the
// read only users. No postincrement or predecrement is
// applied. It returns the address only.
func (c *CPU) controlAddr(op uint16) uint32 {
	mode := int((op >> 3) & 7)
	reg := int(op & 7)
	switch mode {
	case 2:
		return c.a[reg]
	case 5:
		disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
		return uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + disp)
	case 6:
		ext := c.fetchExt()
		disp := int32(int8(ext))
		return uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + disp + int32(c.indexValue(ext)))
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			return uint32(int32(int16(c.fetchExt())))
		case 1:
			hi := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			lo := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			return hi<<16 | lo
		case 2:
			base := c.pc
			disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
			return uint32(int32(base) + disp)
		case 3:
			base := c.pc
			ext := c.fetchExt()
			disp := int32(int8(ext))
			return uint32(int32(base) + disp + int32(c.indexValue(ext)))
		}
	}
	panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
}

// read returns the operand value, truncated to size.
func (c *CPU) read(e ea, size int) uint32 {
	switch {
	case e.dn:
		return c.d[e.reg] & sizeMask(size)
	case e.an:
		return c.a[e.reg] & sizeMask(size)
	case e.imm:
		return e.immVal & sizeMask(size)
	default:
		return c.readMem(e.addr, size)
	}
}

func (c *CPU) readMem(addr uint32, size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return uint32(c.rd8(addr))
	case 2:
		return uint32(c.rd16(addr))
	default:
		return c.rd32(addr)
	}
}

func (c *CPU) writeMem(addr uint32, v uint32, size int) {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		c.wr8(addr, uint8(v))
	case 2:
		c.wr16(addr, uint16(v))
	default:
		c.wr32(addr, v)
	}
}

// write stores v at the operand. Data register byte and
// word writes preserve the upper bits; address register
// writes are always full 32 bit with word results sign
// extended, per the manual partial register rules.
func (c *CPU) write(e ea, v uint32, size int) {
	switch {
	case e.dn:
		m := sizeMask(size)
		c.d[e.reg] = (c.d[e.reg] &^ m) | (v & m)
	case e.an:
		if size == 2 {
			c.a[e.reg] = uint32(int32(int16(v)))
		} else {
			c.a[e.reg] = v
		}
	case e.mem:
		c.writeMem(e.addr, v, size)
	default:
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
}

// Flag helpers. The CCR is the low byte of SR.

func (c *CPU) setFlag(f uint16, on bool) {
	if on {
		c.sr |= f
	} else {
		c.sr &^= f
	}
}

func (c *CPU) getX() uint32 {
	if c.sr&srX != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// setNZ sets N and Z from a truncated result.
func (c *CPU) setNZ(res uint32, size int) {
	c.setFlag(srN, res&signBit(size) != 0)
	c.setFlag(srZ, res&sizeMask(size) == 0)
}

// logicFlags is the flag rule for logic, move, and most
// unary operations: N and Z from the result, V and C
// cleared, X unchanged.
func (c *CPU) logicFlags(res uint32, size int) {
	c.setNZ(res, size)
	c.setFlag(srV, false)
	c.setFlag(srC, false)
}

// addFlags computes dst plus src plus xIn at size and
// sets XNZVC for an addition. It returns the result.
func (c *CPU) addFlags(src, dst uint32, size int, xIn uint32) uint32 {
	m := sizeMask(size)
	s := src & m
	d := dst & m
	total := uint64(d) + uint64(s) + uint64(xIn)
	res := uint32(total) & m
	sb := signBit(size)
	// Overflow: same sign operands, different sign result.
	v := (d^res)&(s^res)&sb != 0
	c.setNZ(res, size)
	c.setFlag(srV, v)
	carry := total > uint64(m)
	c.setFlag(srC, carry)
	c.setFlag(srX, carry)
	return res
}

// subFlags computes dst minus src minus xIn at size and
// sets flags for a subtraction. setX is false for CMP,
// which leaves X unchanged.
func (c *CPU) subFlags(src, dst uint32, size int, xIn uint32, setX bool) uint32 {
	m := sizeMask(size)
	s := src & m
	d := dst & m
	total := int64(d) - int64(s) - int64(xIn)
	res := uint32(total) & m
	sb := signBit(size)
	v := (d^s)&(d^res)&sb != 0
	c.setNZ(res, size)
	c.setFlag(srV, v)
	borrow := total < 0
	c.setFlag(srC, borrow)
	if setX {
		c.setFlag(srX, borrow)
	}
	return res
}

// bcdV is the overflow rule shipped for ABCD and SBCD.
// V is set when two operands with bit 7 clear produce a
// result with bit 7 set and no decimal carry out, or
// when two operands with bit 7 set produce a result
// with bit 7 clear and a decimal carry (borrow, for
// SBCD) out. This symmetric model is the stated rule
// for this core; the caller supplies the decimal carry
// or borrow as carryOut. N is bit 7 of the result and
// the multi precision Z rule is applied by the caller,
// not here.
func bcdV(a, b, res, carryOut uint32) bool {
	if carryOut == 0 {
		return (res&0x80) != 0 && (a&0x80) == 0 && (b&0x80) == 0
	}
	return (res&0x80) == 0 && (a&0x80) != 0 && (b&0x80) != 0
}

// bcdAdd adds two packed BCD bytes plus the X flag:
// binary addition digit by digit with the +6 correction
// on any digit over 9. It returns the corrected result,
// the decimal carry out, and V per bcdV.
func bcdAdd(a, b uint32, x uint32) (res uint32, carry uint32, v bool) {
	lo := (a & 0x0F) + (b & 0x0F) + x
	if lo > 9 {
		lo += 6
	}
	hi := (a >> 4) + (b >> 4) + (lo >> 4)
	if hi > 9 {
		hi += 6
		carry = 1
	}
	res = ((hi & 0x0F) << 4) | (lo & 0x0F)
	v = bcdV(a, b, res, carry)
	return res, carry, v
}

// bcdSub subtracts b and X from a in packed BCD, per
// SBCD: digitwise with the 6 correction on borrow. It
// returns the corrected result, the decimal borrow out,
// and V per bcdV with the borrow as the carry term.
func bcdSub(a, b uint32, x uint32) (res uint32, borrow uint32, v bool) {
	lo := int(a&0x0F) - int(b&0x0F) - int(x)
	loBorrow := 0
	if lo < 0 {
		lo -= 6
		loBorrow = 1
	}
	hi := int(a>>4) - int(b>>4) - loBorrow
	if hi < 0 {
		hi -= 6
		borrow = 1
	}
	res = uint32((hi&0x0F)<<4 | (lo & 0x0F))
	v = bcdV(a, b, res, borrow)
	return res, borrow, v
}

// condition evaluates a 68000 condition code field.
func (c *CPU) condition(cond int) bool {
	n := c.sr&srN != 0
	z := c.sr&srZ != 0
	v := c.sr&srV != 0
	carry := c.sr&srC != 0
	switch cond {
	case 0:
		return true
	case 1:
		return false
	case 2:
		return !carry && !z
	case 3:
		return carry || z
	case 4:
		return !carry
	case 5:
		return carry
	case 6:
		return !z
	case 7:
		return z
	case 8:
		return !v
	case 9:
		return v
	case 10:
		return !n
	case 11:
		return n
	case 12:
		return n == v
	case 13:
		return n != v
	case 14:
		return !z && (n == v)
	case 15:
		return z || (n != v)
	}
	return false
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/chips/m68ec000/exec.go ====================

package m68ec000

// Instruction execution dispatch. exec runs one decoded
// opcode word; c.cur is the opcode address, c.ir the
// opcode, and c.pc already points past the opcode word.
// Exceptions that are part of normal execution (divide
// by zero, CHK, TRAPV, TRAP) call exception directly with
// c.pc as the saved PC, since effective address decode
// has consumed every extension word by then. Faults
// (illegal patterns, privilege violations, address
// errors) travel as the panic carriers recovered in
// stepInner.

func opSize(code int) int {
	switch code {
	case 0:
		return 1
	case 1:
		return 2
	case 2:
		return 4
	}
	return 0
}

// fetchImm consumes an immediate operand of the given
// size at the PC.
func (c *CPU) fetchImm(size int) uint32 {
	switch size {
	case 1:
		return uint32(c.fetchExt() & 0xFF)
	case 2:
		return uint32(c.fetchExt())
	default:
		hi := uint32(c.fetchExt())
		lo := uint32(c.fetchExt())
		return hi<<16 | lo
	}
}

func dnEA(reg int) ea { return ea{mode: 0, reg: reg & 7, dn: true} }

// decodeDest decodes the reversed destination field of
// a MOVE opcode (register in bits 11 to 9, mode in bits
// 8 to 6), consuming extension words at the PC. PC
// relative and immediate destinations are illegal.
func (c *CPU) decodeDest(op uint16, size int) ea {
	mode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	reg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	e := ea{mode: mode, reg: reg, cycles: eaCycles(mode, reg)}
	if size == 4 && mode >= 2 {
		e.cycles += 4
	}
	adj := size
	if size == 1 && reg == 7 {
		adj = 2
	}
	switch mode {
	case 0:
		e.dn = true
	case 1:
		e.an = true
	case 2:
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = c.a[reg]
	case 3:
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = c.a[reg]
		c.a[reg] += uint32(adj)
	case 4:
		e.mem = true
		c.a[reg] -= uint32(adj)
		e.addr = c.a[reg]
	case 5:
		disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + disp)
	case 6:
		ext := c.fetchExt()
		disp := int32(int8(ext))
		e.mem = true
		e.addr = uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + disp + int32(c.indexValue(ext)))
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			e.mem = true
			e.addr = uint32(int32(int16(c.fetchExt())))
		case 1:
			e.mem = true
			hi := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			lo := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			e.addr = hi<<16 | lo
		default:
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
	}
	return e
}

func (c *CPU) exec(op uint16) int {
	if op == 0x4AFC { // ILLEGAL
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	switch op >> 12 {
	case 0:
		return c.execGroup0(op)
	case 1:
		return c.execMove(op, 1)
	case 2:
		return c.execMove(op, 4)
	case 3:
		return c.execMove(op, 2)
	case 4:
		return c.execMisc(op)
	case 5:
		return c.execGroup5(op)
	case 6:
		return c.execBranch(op)
	case 7:
		return c.execMoveq(op)
	case 8:
		return c.execGroup8(op)
	case 9:
		return c.execAddSub(op, false)
	case 10:
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur, vec: 10}) // line A
	case 11:
		return c.execGroupB(op)
	case 12:
		return c.execGroupC(op)
	case 13:
		return c.execAddSub(op, true)
	case 14:
		return c.execShift(op)
	case 15:
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur, vec: 11}) // line F
	}
	panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
}

// execMove handles MOVE and MOVEA (destination mode 1).
func (c *CPU) execMove(op uint16, size int) int {
	if (op>>6)&7 == 1 && size == 1 {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur}) // no byte MOVEA
	}
	src := c.decodeEA(op, size)
	val := c.read(src, size)
	dst := c.decodeDest(op, size)
	c.write(dst, val, size)
	if dst.an {
		return 4 + src.cycles // MOVEA sets no flags
	}
	c.logicFlags(val, size)
	return 4 + src.cycles + dst.cycles
}

func (c *CPU) execMoveq(op uint16) int {
	if op&0x0100 != 0 {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	val := uint32(int32(int8(op)))
	c.d[(op>>9)&7] = val
	c.logicFlags(val, 4)
	return 4
}

// ---- group 0: immediate, bit operations, MOVEP ----

func (c *CPU) execGroup0(op uint16) int {
	if op&0xF138 == 0x0108 {
		return c.execMovep(op)
	}
	if op&0x0100 != 0 {
		return c.execBitDyn(op)
	}
	if op>>8 == 0x08 {
		return c.execBitStatic(op)
	}
	switch op >> 8 {
	case 0x00, 0x02, 0x04, 0x06, 0x0A, 0x0C:
		return c.execImmediate(op)
	}
	panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
}

// bitOp runs BTST, BCHG, BCLR, or BSET (kind 0 to 3).
// Only Z is affected: set when the tested bit was 0.
// Register operands take the bit number modulo 32,
// memory byte operands modulo 8.
func (c *CPU) bitOp(kind int, bitNum uint32, e ea) int {
	if e.an {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	if e.dn {
		bit := bitNum % 32
		val := c.d[e.reg]
		c.setFlag(srZ, (val>>bit)&1 == 0)
		switch kind {
		case 1:
			val ^= 1 << bit
		case 2:
			val &^= 1 << bit
		case 3:
			val |= 1 << bit
		}
		if kind != 0 {
			c.d[e.reg] = val
		}
		return 6
	}
	bit := bitNum % 8
	val := c.read(e, 1)
	c.setFlag(srZ, (val>>bit)&1 == 0)
	switch kind {
	case 1:
		val ^= 1 << bit
	case 2:
		val &^= 1 << bit
	case 3:
		val |= 1 << bit
	}
	if kind != 0 {
		c.write(e, val, 1)
	}
	return 4 + e.cycles
}

func (c *CPU) execBitDyn(op uint16) int {
	kind := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	bitNum := c.d[(op>>9)&7]
	e := c.decodeEA(op, 1)
	return c.bitOp(kind, bitNum, e) + e.cycles
}

func (c *CPU) execBitStatic(op uint16) int {
	kind := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	bitNum := uint32(c.fetchExt() & 0xFF)
	e := c.decodeEA(op, 1)
	return c.bitOp(kind, bitNum, e) + e.cycles + 2
}

// execImmediate handles ORI, ANDI, SUBI, ADDI, EORI,
// and CMPI, including the CCR and SR destination forms
// of the logic operations.
func (c *CPU) execImmediate(op uint16) int {
	kind := op >> 8 // 0x00 ORI, 0x02 ANDI, 0x04 SUBI, 0x06 ADDI, 0x0A EORI, 0x0C CMPI
	sizeCode := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	if sizeCode == 3 {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	size := opSize(sizeCode)
	if op&0x3F == 0x3C {
		// Destination field names CCR (byte) or SR (word).
		if kind != 0x00 && kind != 0x02 && kind != 0x0A {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		if size == 1 {
			imm := c.fetchImm(1)
			res := logicImm(kind, uint32(c.sr&0xFF), imm)
			c.sr = (c.sr & 0xFF00) | uint16(res&0x1F)
			return 12
		}
		if size == 2 {
			if !c.supervisor() {
				panic(privError{instr: c.cur})
			}
			imm := c.fetchImm(2)
			c.setSR(uint16(logicImm(kind, uint32(c.sr), imm)))
			return 12
		}
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	imm := c.fetchImm(size)
	e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
	if e.imm || e.an {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	dst := c.read(e, size)
	switch kind {
	case 0x00:
		res := dst | imm
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(e, res, size)
	case 0x02:
		res := dst & imm
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(e, res, size)
	case 0x0A:
		res := dst ^ imm
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(e, res, size)
	case 0x06:
		res := c.addFlags(imm, dst, size, 0)
		c.write(e, res, size)
	case 0x04:
		res := c.subFlags(imm, dst, size, 0, true)
		c.write(e, res, size)
	case 0x0C:
		c.subFlags(imm, dst, size, 0, false)
	}
	return 8 + e.cycles
}

func logicImm(kind uint16, dst, imm uint32) uint32 {
	switch kind {
	case 0x00:
		return dst | imm
	case 0x02:
		return dst & imm
	default:
		return dst ^ imm
	}
}

// execMovep moves bytes between a data register and
// alternate memory bytes (even offsets from An plus a
// signed word displacement). Word transfers use the low
// word of the register and leave the high word intact;
// long transfers use the whole register. No flags.
func (c *CPU) execMovep(op uint16) int {
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	dn := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	an := int(op & 7)
	disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
	addr := uint32(int32(c.a[an]) + disp)
	load := opmode&1 != 0
	long := opmode&2 != 0
	n := 2
	if long {
		n = 4
	}
	if load {
		var val uint32
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			val = val<<8 | uint32(c.rd8(addr+uint32(2*i)))
		}
		if long {
			c.d[dn] = val
		} else {
			c.d[dn] = (c.d[dn] & 0xFFFF0000) | val
		}
	} else {
		val := c.d[dn]
		shift := uint(8 * (n - 1))
		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
			c.wr8(addr+uint32(2*i), uint8(val>>shift))
			shift -= 8
		}
	}
	if long {
		return 24
	}
	return 16
}

// ---- group 5: ADDQ, SUBQ, Scc, DBcc ----

func (c *CPU) execGroup5(op uint16) int {
	sizeCode := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	cond := int((op >> 8) & 0xF)
	if sizeCode == 3 {
		if (op>>3)&7 == 1 {
			// DBcc: extension word is the displacement,
			// taken from the address of that word.
			reg := int(op & 7)
			disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
			if c.condition(cond) {
				return 12
			}
			low := uint16(c.d[reg]) - 1
			c.d[reg] = (c.d[reg] & 0xFFFF0000) | uint32(low)
			if low != 0xFFFF {
				c.pc = uint32(int32(c.cur+2) + disp)
				return 10
			}
			return 14
		}
		// Scc: byte destination, 0xFF true, 0x00 false.
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 1)
		if e.an || e.imm {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		var val uint32
		if c.condition(cond) {
			val = 0xFF
		}
		c.write(e, val, 1)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
	size := opSize(sizeCode)
	mode := int((op >> 3) & 7)
	if mode == 1 && size == 1 {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur}) // no byte ADDQ/SUBQ to An
	}
	count := uint32((op >> 9) & 7)
	if count == 0 {
		count = 8
	}
	e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
	add := op&0x0100 == 0
	if e.an {
		// Address register quick arithmetic runs on the
		// full register and sets no flags.
		if add {
			c.a[e.reg] += count
		} else {
			c.a[e.reg] -= count
		}
		return 4
	}
	if e.imm {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	dst := c.read(e, size)
	var res uint32
	if add {
		res = c.addFlags(count, dst, size, 0)
	} else {
		res = c.subFlags(count, dst, size, 0, true)
	}
	c.write(e, res, size)
	return 4 + e.cycles
}

// ---- group 6: BRA, BSR, Bcc ----

func (c *CPU) execBranch(op uint16) int {
	cond := int((op >> 8) & 0xF)
	disp8 := int8(op)
	var disp int32
	if disp8 == 0 {
		disp = int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
	} else {
		// On the base 68000 a byte displacement of 0xFF
		// is a plain displacement of -1; the long
		// displacement form is a 68020 addition.
		disp = int32(disp8)
	}
	target := uint32(int32(c.cur+2) + disp)
	if cond == 1 { // BSR
		c.push32(c.pc) // past the opcode and any extension
		c.pc = target
		return 18
	}
	if cond == 0 || c.condition(cond) {
		c.pc = target
		return 10
	}
	return 8
}

// ---- BCD shared core (ABCD, SBCD) ----

// bcdFlags applies the BCD flag rule: N from the
// result, V from the helper, C and X both the decimal
// carry or borrow, and Z under the multi precision
// rule (cleared by a nonzero result, left unchanged by
// a zero result).
func (c *CPU) bcdFlags(res, carryOut uint32, v, oldZ bool) {
	c.setFlag(srN, res&0x80 != 0)
	c.setFlag(srV, v)
	c.setFlag(srC, carryOut != 0)
	c.setFlag(srX, carryOut != 0)
	if res != 0 {
		c.setFlag(srZ, false)
	} else {
		c.setFlag(srZ, oldZ)
	}
}

// execBCD runs ABCD (sub false) or SBCD (sub true). The
// register field in bits 11 to 9 is the destination,
// the low register field the source (assembler syntax
// lists the source first); bit 3 selects data registers
// or predecrement memory operands.
func (c *CPU) execBCD(op uint16, sub bool) int {
	dstReg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	srcReg := int(op & 7)
	oldZ := c.sr&srZ != 0
	x := c.getX()
	var src, dst uint32
	var dstEA ea
	memForm := op&0x0008 != 0
	if memForm {
		sAdj, dAdj := 1, 1
		if srcReg == 7 {
			sAdj = 2
		}
		if dstReg == 7 {
			dAdj = 2
		}
		c.a[srcReg] -= uint32(sAdj)
		src = uint32(c.rd8(c.a[srcReg]))
		c.a[dstReg] -= uint32(dAdj)
		dstEA = ea{mem: true, addr: c.a[dstReg], mode: 4, reg: dstReg}
		dst = uint32(c.rd8(c.a[dstReg]))
	} else {
		src = c.d[srcReg] & 0xFF
		dst = c.d[dstReg] & 0xFF
		dstEA = dnEA(dstReg)
	}
	var res, carryOut uint32
	var v bool
	if sub {
		res, carryOut, v = bcdSub(dst, src, x)
	} else {
		res, carryOut, v = bcdAdd(dst, src, x)
	}
	c.bcdFlags(res, carryOut, v, oldZ)
	c.write(dstEA, res, 1)
	return 6
}

// ---- group 8: OR, DIVU, DIVS, SBCD ----

func (c *CPU) execGroup8(op uint16) int {
	if op&0xF1F0 == 0x8100 {
		return c.execBCD(op, true) // SBCD
	}
	dn := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	switch opmode {
	case 3:
		return c.execDiv(op, dn, false)
	case 7:
		return c.execDiv(op, dn, true)
	case 0, 1, 2:
		size := opSize(opmode)
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		res := c.d[dn]&sizeMask(size) | c.read(e, size)
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(dnEA(dn), res, size)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	default: // 4, 5, 6: OR Dn, EA
		size := opSize(opmode & 3)
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		if e.an || e.imm {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		res := c.read(e, size) | c.d[dn]&sizeMask(size)
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(e, res, size)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
}

// execDiv runs DIVU (signed false) or DIVS (signed
// true): a 32 bit dividend in Dn divided by a word
// source, packing the remainder in the high word and
// the quotient in the low word of Dn. Divide by zero
// takes vector 5 with the next instruction stacked. On
// overflow V is set and the destination register is
// left unchanged; that is the documented convention
// this core ships (the manual leaves the exact result
// undefined, and common emulators keep the register).
func (c *CPU) execDiv(op uint16, dn int, signed bool) int {
	e := c.decodeEA(op, 2)
	src := c.read(e, 2)
	if src == 0 {
		c.exception(5, c.pc)
		return 38
	}
	if !signed {
		dividend := uint64(c.d[dn])
		quot := dividend / uint64(src)
		rem := dividend % uint64(src)
		if quot > 0xFFFF {
			c.setFlag(srV, true)
			return 30
		}
		c.d[dn] = uint32(rem)<<16 | uint32(quot)
		c.setNZ(uint32(quot), 2)
		c.setFlag(srV, false)
		c.setFlag(srC, false)
		return 140 + e.cycles
	}
	dividend := int32(c.d[dn])
	divisor := int32(int16(src))
	quot := dividend / divisor
	rem := dividend % divisor
	if quot > 32767 || quot < -32768 {
		c.setFlag(srV, true)
		return 30
	}
	c.d[dn] = uint32(uint16(rem))<<16 | uint32(uint16(quot))
	c.setNZ(uint32(quot), 2)
	c.setFlag(srV, false)
	c.setFlag(srC, false)
	return 158 + e.cycles
}

// ---- groups 9 and D: SUB, ADD, SUBA, ADDA, SUBX, ADDX ----

func (c *CPU) execAddSub(op uint16, add bool) int {
	dn := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	if opmode == 3 || opmode == 7 {
		// ADDA / SUBA: word source sign extended, full
		// width arithmetic, no flags.
		size := 2
		if opmode == 7 {
			size = 4
		}
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		src := c.read(e, size)
		if size == 2 {
			src = uint32(int32(int16(src)))
		}
		if add {
			c.a[dn] += src
		} else {
			c.a[dn] -= src
		}
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
	xBase := uint16(0x9100)
	if add {
		xBase = 0xD100
	}
	if op&0xF130 == xBase {
		return c.execX(op, add)
	}
	size := opSize(opmode & 3)
	if opmode < 3 {
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		src := c.read(e, size)
		var res uint32
		if add {
			res = c.addFlags(src, c.d[dn], size, 0)
		} else {
			res = c.subFlags(src, c.d[dn], size, 0, true)
		}
		c.write(dnEA(dn), res, size)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
	e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
	if e.an || e.imm {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	dst := c.read(e, size)
	var res uint32
	if add {
		res = c.addFlags(c.d[dn], dst, size, 0)
	} else {
		res = c.subFlags(c.d[dn], dst, size, 0, true)
	}
	c.write(e, res, size)
	return 4 + e.cycles
}

// execX runs ADDX (add true) or SUBX (add false), in
// register or predecrement memory form, under the multi
// precision Z rule.
func (c *CPU) execX(op uint16, add bool) int {
	size := opSize(int((op >> 6) & 3))
	// Bits 11 to 9 name the destination register, the
	// low field the source, as with ADDX Dy, Dx syntax.
	dstReg := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	srcReg := int(op & 7)
	oldZ := c.sr&srZ != 0
	x := c.getX()
	var src, dst uint32
	var dstEA ea
	if op&0x0008 != 0 {
		adj := size
		if size == 1 {
			if srcReg == 7 {
				c.a[srcReg] -= 2
			} else {
				c.a[srcReg] -= 1
			}
			if dstReg == 7 {
				c.a[dstReg] -= 2
			} else {
				c.a[dstReg] -= 1
			}
		} else {
			c.a[srcReg] -= uint32(adj)
			c.a[dstReg] -= uint32(adj)
		}
		src = c.readMem(c.a[srcReg], size)
		dstEA = ea{mem: true, addr: c.a[dstReg], mode: 4, reg: dstReg}
		dst = c.readMem(c.a[dstReg], size)
	} else {
		src = c.d[srcReg] & sizeMask(size)
		dst = c.d[dstReg] & sizeMask(size)
		dstEA = dnEA(dstReg)
	}
	var res uint32
	if add {
		res = c.addFlags(src, dst, size, x)
	} else {
		res = c.subFlags(src, dst, size, x, true)
	}
	if res&sizeMask(size) == 0 {
		c.setFlag(srZ, oldZ) // multi precision Z rule
	}
	c.write(dstEA, res, size)
	return 4
}

// ---- group B: CMP, CMPA, CMPM, EOR ----

func (c *CPU) execGroupB(op uint16) int {
	dn := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	if op&0xF138 == 0xB108 {
		// CMPM: (Ay)+ compared against (Ax)+.
		size := opSize(opmode & 3)
		srcReg := int(op & 7)
		sAdj, dAdj := size, size
		if size == 1 {
			if srcReg == 7 {
				sAdj = 2
			}
			if dn == 7 {
				dAdj = 2
			}
		}
		src := c.readMem(c.a[srcReg], size)
		c.a[srcReg] += uint32(sAdj)
		dst := c.readMem(c.a[dn], size)
		c.a[dn] += uint32(dAdj)
		c.subFlags(src, dst, size, 0, false)
		return 8
	}
	if opmode == 3 || opmode == 7 {
		// CMPA: word source sign extended, compared at
		// full width, X untouched.
		size := 2
		if opmode == 7 {
			size = 4
		}
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		src := c.read(e, size)
		if size == 2 {
			src = uint32(int32(int16(src)))
		}
		c.subFlags(src, c.a[dn], 4, 0, false)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
	size := opSize(opmode & 3)
	if opmode < 3 {
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		c.subFlags(c.read(e, size), c.d[dn], size, 0, false)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
	// EOR Dn, EA
	e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
	if e.an || e.imm {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	res := c.read(e, size) ^ c.d[dn]&sizeMask(size)
	c.logicFlags(res, size)
	c.write(e, res, size)
	return 4 + e.cycles
}

// ---- group C: AND, MULU, MULS, ABCD, EXG ----

func (c *CPU) execGroupC(op uint16) int {
	if op&0xF1F0 == 0xC100 {
		return c.execBCD(op, false) // ABCD
	}
	dn := int((op >> 9) & 7)
	if op&0x0100 != 0 {
		switch (op >> 3) & 0x1F {
		case 0x08: // EXG Dx, Dy
			other := int(op & 7)
			c.d[dn], c.d[other] = c.d[other], c.d[dn]
			return 6
		case 0x09: // EXG Ax, Ay
			other := int(op & 7)
			c.a[dn], c.a[other] = c.a[other], c.a[dn]
			return 6
		case 0x11: // EXG Dx, Ay
			other := int(op & 7)
			c.d[dn], c.a[other] = c.a[other], c.d[dn]
			return 6
		}
	}
	opmode := int((op >> 6) & 7)
	switch opmode {
	case 3, 7: // MULU, MULS: word source times low word of Dn
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 2)
		src := c.read(e, 2)
		var res uint32
		if opmode == 3 {
			res = (c.d[dn] & 0xFFFF) * src
		} else {
			res = uint32(int32(int16(c.d[dn])) * int32(int16(src)))
		}
		c.d[dn] = res
		c.logicFlags(res, 4)
		return 38 + e.cycles
	case 0, 1, 2:
		size := opSize(opmode)
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		res := c.d[dn] & sizeMask(size) & c.read(e, size)
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(dnEA(dn), res, size)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	default: // 4, 5, 6: AND Dn, EA
		size := opSize(opmode & 3)
		e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
		if e.an || e.imm {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		res := c.read(e, size) & c.d[dn] & sizeMask(size)
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(e, res, size)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
}

// ---- group 4: the miscellaneous family ----

func (c *CPU) execMisc(op uint16) int {
	switch {
	case op&0xFFC0 == 0x40C0: // MOVE from SR
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 2)
		if e.imm {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		c.write(e, uint32(c.sr), 2)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	case op&0xFFC0 == 0x44C0: // MOVE to CCR
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 2)
		v := c.read(e, 2)
		c.sr = (c.sr & 0xFF00) | uint16(v&0x1F)
		return 8 + e.cycles
	case op&0xFFC0 == 0x46C0: // MOVE to SR
		if !c.supervisor() {
			panic(privError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 2)
		c.setSR(uint16(c.read(e, 2)))
		return 8 + e.cycles
	case op&0xF1C0 == 0x41C0: // LEA
		addr := c.controlAddr(op)
		c.a[(op>>9)&7] = addr
		return 4
	case op&0xF1C0 == 0x4180: // CHK
		dn := int((op >> 9) & 7)
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 2)
		upper := int32(int16(c.read(e, 2)))
		val := int32(int16(c.d[dn]))
		if val < 0 || val > upper {
			c.setFlag(srN, val < 0)
			c.exception(6, c.pc)
			return 40
		}
		return 10 + e.cycles
	}
	switch op >> 8 {
	case 0x40, 0x42, 0x44, 0x46:
		return c.execUnary(op)
	case 0x48, 0x4C:
		return c.execGroup48(op)
	case 0x4A:
		return c.execTest(op)
	case 0x4E:
		return c.execControl(op)
	}
	panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
}

// execUnary handles NEGX (0x40), CLR (0x42), NEG
// (0x44), and NOT (0x46) at byte, word, and long sizes.
func (c *CPU) execUnary(op uint16) int {
	sizeCode := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	if sizeCode == 3 {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	size := opSize(sizeCode)
	e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
	if e.an || e.imm {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	switch op >> 8 {
	case 0x42: // CLR
		c.logicFlags(0, size)
		c.write(e, 0, size)
	case 0x46: // NOT
		res := ^c.read(e, size) & sizeMask(size)
		c.logicFlags(res, size)
		c.write(e, res, size)
	case 0x44: // NEG
		res := c.subFlags(c.read(e, size), 0, size, 0, true)
		c.write(e, res, size)
	case 0x40: // NEGX, multi precision Z rule
		oldZ := c.sr&srZ != 0
		res := c.subFlags(c.read(e, size), 0, size, c.getX(), true)
		if res&sizeMask(size) == 0 {
			c.setFlag(srZ, oldZ)
		}
		c.write(e, res, size)
	}
	return 4 + e.cycles
}

// execGroup48 handles the 0x48 and 0x4C high bytes:
// NBCD, SWAP, EXT, PEA, and MOVEM in both directions.
func (c *CPU) execGroup48(op uint16) int {
	mode := int((op >> 3) & 7)
	if op&0xFB80 == 0x4880 {
		if mode == 0 {
			// EXT: the EA field is a data register.
			reg := int(op & 7)
			if op&0x0040 == 0 { // EXT.W: byte to word
				res := uint32(int32(int8(c.d[reg])))
				c.logicFlags(res, 2)
				c.write(dnEA(reg), res, 2)
			} else { // EXT.L: word to long
				res := uint32(int32(int16(c.d[reg])))
				c.logicFlags(res, 4)
				c.d[reg] = res
			}
			return 4
		}
		return c.execMovem(op)
	}
	if op>>8 == 0x4C {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	switch (op >> 6) & 3 {
	case 0: // NBCD
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 1)
		if e.an || e.imm {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		oldZ := c.sr&srZ != 0
		res, borrow, v := bcdSub(0, c.read(e, 1), c.getX())
		c.bcdFlags(res, borrow, v, oldZ)
		c.write(e, res, 1)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	case 1:
		if mode == 0 { // SWAP
			reg := int(op & 7)
			d := c.d[reg]
			res := d<<16 | d>>16
			c.d[reg] = res
			c.logicFlags(res, 4)
			return 4
		}
		// PEA
		addr := c.controlAddr(op)
		c.push32(addr)
		return 12
	}
	panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
}

func regByIndex(c *CPU, idx int) uint32 {
	if idx < 8 {
		return c.d[idx]
	}
	return c.a[idx-8]
}

func setRegByIndex(c *CPU, idx int, val uint32, size int) {
	if size == 2 {
		val = uint32(int32(int16(val)))
	}
	if idx < 8 {
		c.d[idx] = val
	} else {
		c.a[idx-8] = val
	}
}

// execMovem runs MOVEM in both directions and sizes.
// The register list mask is the extension word right
// after the opcode, before any effective address
// extension words. For a predecrement destination the
// mask bits are read in reverse order (bit 0 names A7)
// and registers are stored from the highest named
// register down, so the memory image ends up in the
// same ascending register order a postincrement load
// with the normal mask expects.
func (c *CPU) execMovem(op uint16) int {
	load := op&0x0400 != 0
	size := 2
	if op&0x0040 != 0 {
		size = 4
	}
	mask := c.fetchExt()
	mode := int((op >> 3) & 7)
	reg := int(op & 7)
	var addr uint32
	switch mode {
	case 2:
		addr = c.a[reg]
	case 3:
		if !load {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		addr = c.a[reg]
	case 4:
		if load {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		addr = c.a[reg]
	case 5:
		addr = uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + int32(int16(c.fetchExt())))
	case 6:
		ext := c.fetchExt()
		addr = uint32(int32(c.a[reg]) + int32(int8(ext)) + int32(c.indexValue(ext)))
	case 7:
		switch reg {
		case 0:
			addr = uint32(int32(int16(c.fetchExt())))
		case 1:
			hi := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			lo := uint32(c.fetchExt())
			addr = hi<<16 | lo
		default:
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
	default:
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	count := 0
	if !load && mode == 4 {
		for bit := 0; bit < 16; bit++ {
			if mask>>bit&1 == 0 {
				continue
			}
			count++
			addr -= uint32(size)
			c.writeMem(addr, regByIndex(c, 15-bit), size)
		}
		c.a[reg] = addr
		return 8 + count*8
	}
	for bit := 0; bit < 16; bit++ {
		if mask>>bit&1 == 0 {
			continue
		}
		count++
		if load {
			setRegByIndex(c, bit, c.readMem(addr, size), size)
		} else {
			c.writeMem(addr, regByIndex(c, bit), size)
		}
		addr += uint32(size)
	}
	if load && mode == 3 {
		c.a[reg] = addr
	}
	return 8 + count*8
}

// execTest handles TST (sizes in bits 7 to 6) and TAS
// (size field 3). TAS reads the byte, sets N and Z from
// the original value, then sets bit 7 and writes back;
// in this model the read modify write is indivisible
// because Step is the unit of interleaving.
func (c *CPU) execTest(op uint16) int {
	if op&0xFFC0 == 0x4AC0 { // TAS
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 1)
		if e.an || e.imm {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		val := c.read(e, 1)
		c.logicFlags(val, 1)
		c.write(e, val|0x80, 1)
		return 4 + e.cycles
	}
	sizeCode := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	if sizeCode == 3 {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	size := opSize(sizeCode)
	e := c.decodeEA(op, size)
	if e.an {
		panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
	}
	c.logicFlags(c.read(e, size), size)
	return 4 + e.cycles
}

// execControl handles the 0x4E high byte: TRAP, LINK,
// UNLK, MOVE USP, RESET, NOP, STOP, RTE, RTS, TRAPV,
// RTR, JSR, and JMP.
func (c *CPU) execControl(op uint16) int {
	switch {
	case op&0xFFF0 == 0x4E40: // TRAP
		c.exception(32+int(op&0xF), c.pc)
		return 34
	case op&0xFFF8 == 0x4E50: // LINK
		reg := int(op & 7)
		disp := int32(int16(c.fetchExt()))
		c.push32(c.a[reg])
		c.a[reg] = c.a[7]
		c.a[7] = uint32(int32(c.a[7]) + disp)
		return 16
	case op&0xFFF8 == 0x4E58: // UNLK
		reg := int(op & 7)
		c.a[7] = c.a[reg]
		c.a[reg] = c.pop32()
		return 12
	case op&0xFFF0 == 0x4E60: // MOVE USP, supervisor only
		if !c.supervisor() {
			panic(privError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		reg := int(op & 7)
		if op&0x0008 != 0 {
			c.a[reg] = c.otherSP // USP to An; S is set here
		} else {
			c.otherSP = c.a[reg] // An to USP
		}
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E70: // RESET
		if !c.supervisor() {
			panic(privError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		if c.ResetCallback != nil {
			c.ResetCallback()
		}
		return 132
	case op == 0x4E71: // NOP
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E72: // STOP
		if !c.supervisor() {
			panic(privError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		imm := c.fetchExt()
		c.setSR(imm)
		c.halted = true
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E73: // RTE
		if !c.supervisor() {
			// Privilege is checked before anything is
			// popped, per the manual.
			panic(privError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		// On the base 68000 an RTE from a group 0 frame
		// (address or bus error) is documented as not
		// reliably restartable; this core pops the
		// plain 6 byte SR and PC frame regardless of
		// frame type, and handlers are expected to
		// reset or loop after a group 0 exception.
		newSR := c.pop16()
		newPC := c.pop32()
		c.setSR(newSR)
		c.pc = newPC
		return 20
	case op == 0x4E75: // RTS
		c.pc = c.pop32()
		return 16
	case op == 0x4E76: // TRAPV
		if c.sr&srV != 0 {
			c.exception(7, c.pc)
			return 34
		}
		return 4
	case op == 0x4E77: // RTR
		ccr := c.pop16()
		newPC := c.pop32()
		c.sr = (c.sr & 0xFF00) | (ccr & 0x1F)
		c.pc = newPC
		return 20
	case op&0xFFC0 == 0x4E80: // JSR
		addr := c.controlAddr(op)
		c.push32(c.pc) // past every extension word
		c.pc = addr
		return 16
	case op&0xFFC0 == 0x4EC0: // JMP
		c.pc = c.controlAddr(op)
		return 8
	}
	panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
}

// ---- group E: shifts and rotates ----

// doShift shifts or rotates val at size by count,
// setting flags per the manual tables. kind is 0
// arithmetic, 1 logical, 2 rotate through X, 3 rotate.
// dir is 0 right, 1 left. For a register count of 0,
// X is unchanged, C is cleared, and V is cleared; this
// falls out of the loop form below except for X on the
// non ROX kinds, which the caller of the loop restores.
func (c *CPU) doShift(kind, dir, count int, val uint32, size int) uint32 {
	mask := sizeMask(size)
	res := val & mask
	if count == 0 {
		c.setNZ(res, size)
		c.setFlag(srV, false)
		c.setFlag(srC, false)
		return res
	}
	bits := int(sizeBits(size))
	sb := signBit(size)
	oldX := c.getX()
	x := oldX
	var lastOut uint32
	vSet := false
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		if dir == 1 {
			out := (res >> (bits - 1)) & 1
			lastOut = out
			signBefore := res & sb
			switch kind {
			case 0, 1: // AS, LS
				res = (res << 1) & mask
				if kind == 0 && (res&sb) != signBefore {
					vSet = true
				}
			case 2: // ROX
				res = ((res << 1) | x) & mask
				x = out
			case 3: // RO
				res = ((res << 1) | out) & mask
			}
		} else {
			out := res & 1
			lastOut = out
			switch kind {
			case 0: // AS: sign bit replicates
				res = (res >> 1) | (res & sb)
			case 1: // LS
				res >>= 1
			case 2: // ROX
				res = (res >> 1) | (x << (bits - 1))
				x = out
			case 3: // RO
				res = (res >> 1) | (out << (bits - 1))
			}
		}
	}
	c.setNZ(res, size)
	c.setFlag(srC, lastOut != 0)
	if kind == 2 {
		c.setFlag(srX, x != 0)
	} else {
		c.setFlag(srX, lastOut != 0)
	}
	// V is set only by ASL, when the sign bit changed
	// value at any point during the shift.
	c.setFlag(srV, kind == 0 && dir == 1 && vSet)
	_ = oldX
	return res
}

func (c *CPU) execShift(op uint16) int {
	sizeCode := int((op >> 6) & 3)
	dir := int((op >> 8) & 1)
	if sizeCode == 3 {
		// Memory form: word only, count of one, the
		// kind in bits 11 to 9 as type plus direction:
		// 0 AS, 1 LS, 2 ROX, 3 RO with bit 8 the way.
		kind := int((op >> 9) & 3)
		e := c.decodeEA(op, 2)
		if !e.mem {
			panic(illegalError{instr: c.cur})
		}
		res := c.doShift(kind, dir, 1, c.readMem(e.addr, 2), 2)
		c.writeMem(e.addr, res, 2)
		return 8 + e.cycles
	}
	size := opSize(sizeCode)
	kind := int((op >> 3) & 3)
	reg := int(op & 7)
	var count int
	if op&0x0020 != 0 {
		count = int(c.d[(op>>9)&7] % 64)
	} else {
		count = int((op >> 9) & 7)
		if count == 0 {
			count = 8
		}
	}
	res := c.doShift(kind, dir, count, c.d[reg], size)
	c.write(dnEA(reg), res, size)
	return 6 + 2*count
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/chips/m68ec000/m68ec000.go ====================

// Package m68ec000 implements the Motorola 68000 integer CPU
// from the MC68000 User Manual. In the Saturn it is the SCSP
// sound CPU. This module is standalone: it depends only on
// the Bus interface below and the Go standard library.
//
// The core is a plain interpreter. One Step call executes
// one instruction, or takes one pending accepted interrupt.
// Cycle counts follow the User Manual instruction timing
// table for the common forms: a compact base cost per
// instruction class plus the manual effective address
// adders. Counts are deterministic; they are an
// approximation of the table, not a bus cycle simulation.
//
// Conformance: there is no Tom Harte 680x0 test corpus on
// this machine (it was searched for and not found), so the
// conformance gate is the hand derived vectors in
// m68ec000_test.go, worked out from the manual operation
// and flag tables. The tests are structured as plain
// register, flag, and memory assertions per instruction
// group so a corpus harness can be added later by driving
// the same public API: New, Reset, Step, D, A, SR, PC.
//
// The SR T bit is stored but trace exceptions are not
// taken. RESET is modeled in place: it invokes the
// optional ResetCallback field when set and otherwise
// does nothing besides consume its documented cycles.
// TAS is indivisible in this model because Step is the
// unit of interleaving.
//
// Serialized layout, SerializeSize bytes, big endian:
// bytes 0 to 31: D0 to D7, four bytes each
// bytes 32 to 63: A0 to A7, four bytes each. A7 is the
// active stack pointer, selected by the SR S bit.
// bytes 64 to 67: user stack pointer (the inactive A7
// when S is set, the active one when S is clear)
// bytes 68 to 71: supervisor stack pointer (same rule)
// bytes 72 to 75: PC
// bytes 76 to 77: SR
// byte 78: pending interrupt: high bit set when valid,
// plus the level in the low three bits
// byte 79: halted flag, 0 or 1
// bytes 80 to 87: Cycles, eight bytes
package m68ec000

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// SerializeSize is the exact size of a serialized CPU.
const SerializeSize = 88

// Bus is the memory space the CPU talks to. Read16 and
// Read32 return big endian assembled values: the bus, not
// the CPU, owns byte order assembly.
type Bus interface {
	Read8(uint32) uint8
	Read16(uint32) uint16
	Read32(uint32) uint32
	Write8(uint32, uint8)
	Write16(uint32, uint16)
	Write32(uint32, uint32)
}

// SR bit positions in the low byte (the CCR) and high byte.
const (
	srC uint16 = 0x0001
	srV uint16 = 0x0002
	srZ uint16 = 0x0004
	srN uint16 = 0x0008
	srX uint16 = 0x0010
	srS uint16 = 0x2000
	srT uint16 = 0x8000
)

// CPU is one 68000 processor.
type CPU struct {
	Cycles uint64

	// ResetCallback, when set, is invoked by the RESET
	// instruction. RESET is a supervisor only instruction.
	ResetCallback func()

	bus     Bus
	d       [8]uint32
	a       [8]uint32
	otherSP uint32
	pc      uint32
	sr      uint16

	pendValid bool
	pendLevel int
	halted    bool

	cur uint32
	ir  uint16
}

// New returns a CPU attached to b. It does not reset;
// the caller calls Reset.
func New(b Bus) *CPU {
	return &CPU{bus: b}
}

// Reset reads the initial supervisor stack pointer from
// bus address 0 and the initial PC from bus address 4,
// clears the registers, and sets SR to 0x2700:
// supervisor mode, interrupt mask 7, T clear.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	c.d = [8]uint32{}
	c.a = [8]uint32{}
	c.otherSP = 0
	c.Cycles = 0
	c.halted = false
	c.pendValid = false
	c.pendLevel = 0
	ssp := c.bus.Read32(0)
	c.pc = c.bus.Read32(4)
	c.sr = 0x2700
	c.a[7] = ssp
}

// PC returns the program counter.
func (c *CPU) PC() uint32 { return c.pc }

// D returns data register i, 0 to 7.
func (c *CPU) D(i int) uint32 { return c.d[i&7] }

// A returns address register i, 0 to 7. A7 is the active
// stack pointer.
func (c *CPU) A(i int) uint32 { return c.a[i&7] }

// SR returns the status register.
func (c *CPU) SR() uint16 { return c.sr }

// Halted reports whether a STOP instruction has halted
// the CPU. It wakes when an interrupt latch is accepted.
func (c *CPU) Halted() bool { return c.halted }

// Interrupt latches an autovectored interrupt request,
// levels 1 to 7. It is accepted between instructions
// when the level is greater than the SR interrupt mask.
// Level 7 is always accepted, once per latch (edge
// model). The vector taken is 24 plus the level. Only
// the highest latched level is kept.
func (c *CPU) Interrupt(level int) {
	if level < 1 || level > 7 {
		return
	}
	if c.pendValid && c.pendLevel >= level {
		return
	}
	c.pendValid = true
	c.pendLevel = level
}

func (c *CPU) supervisor() bool { return c.sr&srS != 0 }

func (c *CPU) mask() int { return int((c.sr >> 8) & 7) }

// setSR stores a new SR, swapping the stack pointers
// when the S bit changes, per the manual USP and SSP
// split.
func (c *CPU) setSR(v uint16) {
	oldS := c.sr & srS
	newS := v & srS
	c.sr = v
	if oldS != newS {
		c.a[7], c.otherSP = c.otherSP, c.a[7]
	}
}

// usp and ssp report the two stack pointers regardless
// of which one is active.
func (c *CPU) usp() uint32 {
	if c.supervisor() {
		return c.otherSP
	}
	return c.a[7]
}

func (c *CPU) ssp() uint32 {
	if c.supervisor() {
		return c.a[7]
	}
	return c.otherSP
}

// Serialize returns the CPU state in the layout given in
// the package comment, exactly SerializeSize bytes.
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[i*4:i*4+4], c.d[i])
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[32+i*4:32+i*4+4], c.a[i])
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[64:68], c.usp())
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[68:72], c.ssp())
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[72:76], c.pc)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[76:78], c.sr)
	if c.pendValid {
		out[78] = 0x80 | byte(c.pendLevel&7)
	}
	if c.halted {
		out[79] = 1
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[80:88], c.Cycles)
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) != SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("m68ec000: state size mismatch")
	}
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		c.d[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[i*4 : i*4+4])
		c.a[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[32+i*4 : 32+i*4+4])
	}
	usp := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[64:68])
	ssp := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[68:72])
	c.pc = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[72:76])
	c.sr = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[76:78])
	// A7 in the blob is the active pointer. Rebuild the
	// inactive pointer from the stored pair.
	if c.supervisor() {
		c.a[7] = ssp
		c.otherSP = usp
	} else {
		c.a[7] = usp
		c.otherSP = ssp
	}
	c.pendValid = data[78]&0x80 != 0
	c.pendLevel = int(data[78] & 7)
	c.halted = data[79] != 0
	c.Cycles = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[80:88])
	return nil
}

// Exception panic carriers. The memory helpers panic with
// addrError on an odd word or long access; Step recovers
// and builds the address error frame. illegalError and
// privError carry the faulting instruction address.
type addrError struct {
	addr       uint32
	instr      uint32
	pc         uint32
	ir         uint16
	read       bool
	instrFetch bool
}

// illegalError carries the exception vector to take: 4
// for a plain illegal instruction, 10 for line A, and
// 11 for line F. A zero vector means 4.
type illegalError struct {
	instr uint32
	vec   int
}
type privError struct{ instr uint32 }

func (c *CPU) rd8(addr uint32) uint8 { return c.bus.Read8(addr) }

func (c *CPU) rd16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr, instr: c.cur, pc: c.pc, ir: c.ir, read: true})
	}
	return c.bus.Read16(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) rd32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr, instr: c.cur, pc: c.pc, ir: c.ir, read: true})
	}
	return c.bus.Read32(addr)
}

func (c *CPU) wr8(addr uint32, v uint8) { c.bus.Write8(addr, v) }

func (c *CPU) wr16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr, instr: c.cur, pc: c.pc, ir: c.ir, read: false})
	}
	c.bus.Write16(addr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) wr32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr, instr: c.cur, pc: c.pc, ir: c.ir, read: false})
	}
	c.bus.Write32(addr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) fetch16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	if addr&1 != 0 {
		panic(addrError{addr: addr, instr: addr, pc: addr, ir: 0, read: true, instrFetch: true})
	}
	return c.bus.Read16(addr)
}

// fetchExt consumes one extension word at the PC.
func (c *CPU) fetchExt() uint16 {
	w := c.fetch16(c.pc)
	c.pc += 2
	return w
}

func (c *CPU) push16(v uint16) {
	c.a[7] -= 2
	c.wr16(c.a[7], v)
}

func (c *CPU) push32(v uint32) {
	c.a[7] -= 4
	c.wr32(c.a[7], v)
}

func (c *CPU) pop16() uint16 {
	v := c.rd16(c.a[7])
	c.a[7] += 2
	return v
}

func (c *CPU) pop32() uint32 {
	v := c.rd32(c.a[7])
	c.a[7] += 4
	return v
}

// exception takes a normal exception: it stacks SR then
// PC (so SR sits at the stack pointer and PC above it,
// matching RTE and RTR unwinding), switches to
// supervisor mode, clears T, and fetches the vector from
// the vector table through the bus. savedPC is the PC
// value the manual stacks for the exception in question.
func (c *CPU) exception(vector int, savedPC uint32) {
	oldSR := c.sr
	if !c.supervisor() {
		c.setSR(c.sr | srS)
	}
	c.push32(savedPC)
	c.push16(oldSR)
	c.sr &^= srT
	c.pc = c.bus.Read32(uint32(vector) * 4)
}

// addressException builds the 68000 address error frame.
// Per the MC68000 User Manual exception processing
// section (Group 0 exceptions, the bus and address error
// stacking order), the frame is 14 bytes and, from the
// stack pointer upward, holds: the status register, the
// program counter, the instruction register, the access
// (fault) address, and a trailing status word. The
// trailing status word carries the function code in bits
// 2 to 0, an instruction or not flag in bit 4 (set for a
// data access, clear for an instruction fetch), and a
// read or write flag in bit 5 (set for a read). The
// stacked program counter is the addrError pc field: for
// a data access it is the PC at the moment of the fault
// (past the opcode and the extension words consumed so
// far, which for the common single effective address
// cases is the next instruction, the value the manual
// stacks for data access errors); for an instruction
// fetch it is the faulting fetch address itself.
func (c *CPU) addressException(e addrError) {
	oldSR := c.sr
	if !c.supervisor() {
		c.setSR(c.sr | srS)
	}
	var fc uint16 = 5 // supervisor data
	if e.instrFetch {
		fc = 6 // supervisor program
	}
	if oldSR&srS == 0 {
		if e.instrFetch {
			fc = 2 // user program
		} else {
			fc = 1 // user data
		}
	}
	ssw := fc
	if !e.instrFetch {
		ssw |= 0x10
	}
	if e.read {
		ssw |= 0x20
	}
	// Push in reverse so the memory order above holds.
	c.push16(ssw)
	c.push32(e.addr)
	c.push16(e.ir)
	c.push32(e.pc)
	c.push16(oldSR)
	c.sr &^= srT
	c.pc = c.bus.Read32(3 * 4) // vector 3, address error
}

// Step executes one instruction, or takes a pending
// accepted interrupt, and returns the cycles consumed,
// which are also added to Cycles. While halted by STOP,
// Step returns 4 without fetching until an interrupt
// latch is accepted, which wakes the CPU and is taken.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	n := c.stepInner()
	c.Cycles += uint64(n)
	return n
}

func (c *CPU) stepInner() (cycles int) {
	cycles = 4
	defer func() {
		if r := recover(); r != nil {
			switch e := r.(type) {
			case addrError:
				c.halted = false
				c.addressException(e)
				cycles = 50
			case illegalError:
				c.halted = false
				vec := e.vec
				if vec == 0 {
					vec = 4
				}
				c.exception(vec, e.instr+2)
				cycles = 34
			case privError:
				c.halted = false
				// The stacked PC is past the opcode word
				// (e.instr + 2), matching the illegal
				// instruction path above.
				c.exception(8, e.instr+2)
				cycles = 34
			default:
				panic(r)
			}
		}
	}()
	// Interrupt acceptance at the instruction boundary.
	if c.pendValid && (c.pendLevel == 7 || c.pendLevel > c.mask()) {
		level := c.pendLevel
		c.pendValid = false
		c.halted = false
		savedPC := c.pc
		oldSR := c.sr
		if !c.supervisor() {
			c.setSR(c.sr | srS)
		}
		c.push32(savedPC)
		c.push16(oldSR)
		c.sr &^= srT
		c.sr = (c.sr &^ 0x0700) | uint16(level)<<8
		c.pc = c.bus.Read32(uint32(24+level) * 4)
		return 44
	}
	if c.halted {
		return 4
	}
	c.cur = c.pc
	c.ir = c.fetch16(c.pc)
	c.pc += 2
	return c.exec(c.ir)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/chips/m68ec000/m68ec000_test.go ====================

package m68ec000

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// memBus is a flat big endian memory double.
type memBus struct{ b []byte }

func (m *memBus) Read8(a uint32) uint8 { return m.b[a] }
func (m *memBus) Read16(a uint32) uint16 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint16(m.b[a:])
}
func (m *memBus) Read32(a uint32) uint32 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(m.b[a:])
}
func (m *memBus) Write8(a uint32, v uint8) { m.b[a] = v }
func (m *memBus) Write16(a uint32, v uint16) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(m.b[a:], v)
}
func (m *memBus) Write32(a uint32, v uint32) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(m.b[a:], v)
}

func (m *memBus) w16(a uint32, v uint16) { m.Write16(a, v) }
func (m *memBus) w32(a uint32, v uint32) { m.Write32(a, v) }
func (m *memBus) r16(a uint32) uint16    { return m.Read16(a) }
func (m *memBus) r32(a uint32) uint32    { return m.Read32(a) }

// newCPU builds a CPU over fresh memory with the reset
// vectors pointing at stack 0x8000 and program 0x1000.
func newCPU() (*CPU, *memBus) {
	bus := &memBus{b: make([]byte, 1<<20)}
	bus.w32(0, 0x8000)
	bus.w32(4, 0x1000)
	c := New(bus)
	c.Reset()
	return c, bus
}

// load writes instruction words at addr.
func load(bus *memBus, addr uint32, words ...uint16) {
	for i, w := range words {
		bus.w16(addr+uint32(2*i), w)
	}
}

// exec1 places one instruction at 0x1000 and steps it.
func exec1(c *CPU, bus *memBus, op uint16, exts ...uint16) int {
	load(bus, 0x1000, append([]uint16{op}, exts...)...)
	c.pc = 0x1000
	return c.Step()
}

func flag(t *testing.T, c *CPU, f uint16, want bool, name string) {
	t.Helper()
	if got := c.SR()&f != 0; got != want {
		t.Fatalf("%s flag: got %v, want %v (SR=%04X)", name, got, want, c.SR())
	}
}

func TestMoveAndMoveq(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	exec1(c, bus, 0x203C, 0x1234, 0x5678) // MOVE.L #$12345678, D0
	if c.D(0) != 0x12345678 {
		t.Fatalf("D0=%08X", c.D(0))
	}
	flag(t, c, srN, false, "N")
	flag(t, c, srZ, false, "Z")
	exec1(c, bus, 0x70FE) // MOVEQ #-2, D0
	if c.D(0) != 0xFFFFFFFE {
		t.Fatalf("D0=%08X", c.D(0))
	}
	flag(t, c, srN, true, "N")
	exec1(c, bus, 0x7000) // MOVEQ #0, D0
	flag(t, c, srZ, true, "Z")
}

func TestAddxSubxChains(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	c.d[0] = 0xFFFF
	c.d[2] = 1
	exec1(c, bus, 0xD042) // ADD.W D2, D0
	if c.D(0)&0xFFFF != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("D0 low=%04X", c.D(0)&0xFFFF)
	}
	flag(t, c, srX, true, "X")
	flag(t, c, srZ, true, "Z")
	c.d[1] = 0xFFFF
	c.d[3] = 0
	exec1(c, bus, 0xD343) // ADDX.W D3, D1
	if c.D(1)&0xFFFF != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("D1 low=%04X", c.D(1)&0xFFFF)
	}
	flag(t, c, srX, true, "X")
	// Multi precision Z rule: zero result with Z
	// already set keeps Z set.
	flag(t, c, srZ, true, "Z")

	c2, bus2 := newCPU()
	c2.d[0] = 0
	c2.d[2] = 1
	exec1(c2, bus2, 0x9042) // SUB.W D2, D0
	if c2.D(0)&0xFFFF != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("D0 low=%04X", c2.D(0)&0xFFFF)
	}
	flag(t, c2, srX, true, "X")
	c2.d[1] = 0
	c2.d[3] = 0
	exec1(c2, bus2, 0x9343) // SUBX.W D3, D1
	if c2.D(1)&0xFFFF != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("D1 low=%04X", c2.D(1)&0xFFFF)
	}
	flag(t, c2, srX, true, "X")
}

func TestABCDSBCD(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	c.d[0] = 0x27
	c.d[1] = 0x15
	exec1(c, bus, 0xC300) // ABCD D0, D1
	if c.D(1)&0xFF != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("ABCD 15+27: D1=%02X", c.D(1)&0xFF)
	}
	flag(t, c, srC, false, "C")
	flag(t, c, srX, false, "X")
	flag(t, c, srZ, false, "Z")

	c2, bus2 := newCPU()
	c2.d[0] = 0x01
	c2.d[1] = 0x99
	exec1(c2, bus2, 0xC300) // ABCD D0, D1: 99+1
	if c2.D(1)&0xFF != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("ABCD 99+01: D1=%02X", c2.D(1)&0xFF)
	}
	flag(t, c2, srC, true, "C")
	flag(t, c2, srX, true, "X")
	// Z was clear before a zero result, so the multi
	// precision rule leaves it clear.
	flag(t, c2, srZ, false, "Z")
	flag(t, c2, srV, false, "V")

	c3, bus3 := newCPU()
	c3.d[0] = 0x01
	c3.d[1] = 0x00
	exec1(c3, bus3, 0x8300) // SBCD D0, D1: 00-01
	if c3.D(1)&0xFF != 0x99 {
		t.Fatalf("SBCD 00-01: D1=%02X", c3.D(1)&0xFF)
	}
	flag(t, c3, srC, true, "C")
	flag(t, c3, srX, true, "X")
	flag(t, c3, srN, true, "N")

	c4, bus4 := newCPU()
	c4.d[0] = 0x27
	c4.d[1] = 0x42
	exec1(c4, bus4, 0x8300) // SBCD D0, D1: 42-27
	if c4.D(1)&0xFF != 0x15 {
		t.Fatalf("SBCD 42-27: D1=%02X", c4.D(1)&0xFF)
	}
	flag(t, c4, srC, false, "C")
}

func TestDivuDivs(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	c.d[0] = 100
	c.d[1] = 3
	exec1(c, bus, 0x80C1) // DIVU D1, D0
	if c.D(0) != 0x00010021 {
		t.Fatalf("DIVU packing: D0=%08X", c.D(0))
	}
	flag(t, c, srV, false, "V")

	c.d[0] = 0x00020000
	c.d[1] = 1
	exec1(c, bus, 0x80C1) // DIVU overflow
	if c.D(0) != 0x00020000 {
		t.Fatalf("DIVU overflow changed D0: %08X", c.D(0))
	}
	flag(t, c, srV, true, "V")

	c2, bus2 := newCPU()
	bus2.w32(5*4, 0x3000) // divide by zero vector
	c2.d[0] = 100
	c2.d[1] = 0
	exec1(c2, bus2, 0x80C1)
	if c2.PC() != 0x3000 {
		t.Fatalf("div0 PC=%08X", c2.PC())
	}
	if c2.A(7) != 0x7FFA {
		t.Fatalf("div0 SP=%08X", c2.A(7))
	}
	if bus2.r16(0x7FFA) != 0x2700 {
		t.Fatalf("div0 stacked SR=%04X", bus2.r16(0x7FFA))
	}
	if bus2.r32(0x7FFC) != 0x1002 {
		t.Fatalf("div0 stacked PC=%08X", bus2.r32(0x7FFC))
	}

	c3, bus3 := newCPU()
	c3.d[0] = 0xFFFFFF9C    // -100
	c3.d[1] = 0xFFFD        // -3
	exec1(c3, bus3, 0x81C1) // DIVS D1, D0
	if c3.D(0) != 0xFFFF0021 {
		t.Fatalf("DIVS -100/-3: D0=%08X", c3.D(0))
	}
	c3.d[0] = 100
	exec1(c3, bus3, 0x81C1) // DIVS 100/-3
	if c3.D(0) != 0x0001FFDF {
		t.Fatalf("DIVS 100/-3: D0=%08X", c3.D(0))
	}
	flag(t, c3, srN, true, "N")
}

func TestMul(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	c.d[0] = 0xFFFF
	c.d[1] = 0xFFFF
	exec1(c, bus, 0xC0C1) // MULU D1, D0
	if c.D(0) != 0xFFFE0001 {
		t.Fatalf("MULU: D0=%08X", c.D(0))
	}
	c.d[0] = 0xFFFF // -1
	c.d[1] = 2
	exec1(c, bus, 0xC1C1) // MULS D1, D0
	if c.D(0) != 0xFFFFFFFE {
		t.Fatalf("MULS: D0=%08X", c.D(0))
	}
	flag(t, c, srN, true, "N")
	flag(t, c, srV, false, "V")
}

func TestMovemPredecStoreAndPostincLoad(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	c.d[0] = 0x11111111
	c.d[1] = 0x22222222
	c.a[0] = 0x33333333
	c.a[1] = 0x44444444
	c.a[6] = 0x3000
	// MOVEM.L D0-D1/A0-A1, -(A6); predecrement mask
	// names registers in reverse bit order.
	exec1(c, bus, 0x48E6, 0xC0C0)
	if c.A(6) != 0x2FF0 {
		t.Fatalf("A6 after store=%08X", c.A(6))
	}
	want := []uint32{0x11111111, 0x22222222, 0x33333333, 0x44444444}
	for i, w := range want {
		if got := bus.r32(0x2FF0 + uint32(4*i)); got != w {
			t.Fatalf("memory long %d: got %08X want %08X", i, got, w)
		}
	}
	c.d[0], c.d[1], c.a[0], c.a[1] = 0, 0, 0, 0
	// MOVEM.L (A6)+, D0-D1/A0-A1 with the normal mask.
	exec1(c, bus, 0x4CDE, 0x0303)
	if c.D(0) != want[0] || c.D(1) != want[1] || c.A(0) != want[2] || c.A(1) != want[3] {
		t.Fatalf("loaded: D0=%08X D1=%08X A0=%08X A1=%08X", c.D(0), c.D(1), c.A(0), c.A(1))
	}
	if c.A(6) != 0x3000 {
		t.Fatalf("A6 after load=%08X", c.A(6))
	}
}

func TestDBccLoopCount(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	load(bus, 0x1000,
		0x7002,         // MOVEQ #2, D0
		0x7200,         // MOVEQ #0, D1
		0x5201,         // loop: ADDQ.B #1, D1
		0x51C8, 0xFFFC) // DBRA D0, loop
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		c.Step()
	}
	if c.D(1) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("body ran for D1=%d, want 3", c.D(1))
	}
	if c.D(0)&0xFFFF != 0xFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("D0 low=%04X", c.D(0)&0xFFFF)
	}
	if c.PC() != 0x100A {
		t.Fatalf("PC=%08X", c.PC())
	}
}

func TestChk(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	c.d[0] = 5
	exec1(c, bus, 0x41BC, 10) // CHK #10, D0: in range
	if c.PC() != 0x1004 || c.A(7) != 0x8000 {
		t.Fatalf("CHK in range: PC=%08X SP=%08X", c.PC(), c.A(7))
	}
	c2, bus2 := newCPU()
	bus2.w32(6*4, 0x3000)
	c2.d[0] = 20
	exec1(c2, bus2, 0x41BC, 10) // CHK #10, D0: taken
	if c2.PC() != 0x3000 {
		t.Fatalf("CHK taken PC=%08X", c2.PC())
	}
	if bus2.r32(0x7FFC) != 0x1004 {
		t.Fatalf("CHK stacked PC=%08X", bus2.r32(0x7FFC))
	}
	flag(t, c2, srN, false, "N")
	c3, bus3 := newCPU()
	bus3.w32(6*4, 0x3000)
	c3.d[0] = 0xFFFF // -1
	exec1(c3, bus3, 0x41BC, 10)
	if c3.PC() != 0x3000 {
		t.Fatalf("CHK negative PC=%08X", c3.PC())
	}
	flag(t, c3, srN, true, "N")
}

func TestRoxlThroughX(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	exec1(c, bus, 0x303C, 0x8000) // MOVE.W #$8000, D0
	exec1(c, bus, 0xE350)         // ROXL.W #1, D0
	if c.D(0)&0xFFFF != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("D0 low=%04X", c.D(0)&0xFFFF)
	}
	flag(t, c, srX, true, "X")
	flag(t, c, srC, true, "C")
	c.d[1] = 0
	exec1(c, bus, 0xE351) // ROXL.W #1, D1: X shifts in
	if c.D(1)&0xFFFF != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("D1 low=%04X", c.D(1)&0xFFFF)
	}
	flag(t, c, srX, false, "X")
}

func TestBtstModulo(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	c.d[0] = 0x80000000
	exec1(c, bus, 0x0800, 31) // BTST #31, D0
	flag(t, c, srZ, false, "Z")
	c.d[0] = 0x100
	exec1(c, bus, 0x0800, 8) // BTST #8, D0
	flag(t, c, srZ, false, "Z")
	exec1(c, bus, 0x0800, 31) // BTST #31, D0: clear
	flag(t, c, srZ, true, "Z")

	bus.Write8(0x2000, 0x02)
	exec1(c, bus, 0x0839, 9, 0x0000, 0x2000) // BTST #9, $2000.L: bit 1
	flag(t, c, srZ, false, "Z")
	bus.Write8(0x2000, 0x01)
	exec1(c, bus, 0x0839, 8, 0x0000, 0x2000) // BTST #8: bit 0
	flag(t, c, srZ, false, "Z")
	bus.Write8(0x2000, 0x02)
	exec1(c, bus, 0x0839, 8, 0x0000, 0x2000) // BTST #8: bit 0 clear
	flag(t, c, srZ, true, "Z")
}

func TestAddressErrorFrame(t *testing.T) {
	c, bus := newCPU()
	bus.w32(3*4, 0x2000)
	load(bus, 0x1000, 0x3039, 0x0000, 0x1001) // MOVE.W $1001.L, D0
	c.Step()
	if c.PC() != 0x2000 {
		t.Fatalf("PC=%08X", c.PC())
	}
	if c.A(7) != 0x7FF2 {
