==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/enginetest/disc.go ====================

package enginetest

import "encoding/binary"

// Disc layout: the IP occupies sectors 0 to 7 (its
// header size is 0x4000), the primary volume descriptor
// is sector 16, the volume descriptor terminator sector
// 17, the root directory sector 18, and PAYLOAD.BIN
// sector 19. The image is 24 sectors of zeros beyond
// that.

// IPSize is the header IP size of the enginetest disc
// and the length of the IP image at its start.
const IPSize = 0x4000

// BuildDisc returns the complete synthetic ISO9660 disc
// image for the enginetest gate.
func BuildDisc() []byte {
	ip := buildIP(PayloadChecksum(), IPSize)
	const sectors = 24
	img := make([]byte, sectors*2048)
	copy(img, ip)

	pvd := img[16*2048 : 17*2048]
	pvd[0] = 1
	copy(pvd[1:6], "CD001")
	pvd[6] = 1
	copy(pvd[156:190], dirRecord(18, 2048, 2, []byte{0}))

	term := img[17*2048 : 18*2048]
	term[0] = 255
	copy(term[1:6], "CD001")
	term[6] = 1

	root := img[18*2048 : 19*2048]
	off := 0
	for _, rec := range [][]byte{
		dirRecord(18, 2048, 2, []byte{0}),
		dirRecord(18, 2048, 2, []byte{1}),
		dirRecord(19, PayloadSize, 0, []byte("PAYLOAD.BIN;1")),
	} {
		copy(root[off:], rec)
		off += len(rec)
	}

	copy(img[19*2048:], Payload())
	return img
}

// vdpTable returns the (address, value) poke table the
// IP runs to program the display, byte identical in
// effect to the SAT-2 gate's table in the system tests:
// VDP2 NBG0 with a two color character (green then red
// on the first row) and a white VDP1 polygon at
// (100,50) to (119,69) whose priority beats the
// background. The table is terminated by a zero address.
func vdpTable() []byte {
	e := []uint32{
		0x05F80000, 0x8000, // TVMD: DISP on, 320x224
		0x05F80020, 0x0001, // BGON: NBG0 on
		0x05F80028, 0x0000, // CHCTLA: NBG0 16 colors, cells, 1x1
		0x05F80030, 0x8020, // PNCN0: 1 word, SPLT = 1
		0x05F80078, 0x0001, // ZMXIN0
		0x05F8007C, 0x0001, // ZMYIN0
		0x05F800F8, 0x0002, // PRINA: NBG0 priority 2
		0x05F800F4, 0x0007, // PRISC: sprite priority 7
		0x05F00202, 0x03E0, // CRAM palette 16 code 1: green
		0x05F00204, 0x7C00, // CRAM palette 16 code 2: red
		0x05F0003E, 0x7FFF, // CRAM sprite color 31: white
		0x05E00000, 0x0001, // pattern name (0,0): character 1
		0x05E00020, 0x1211, // character row 0: codes 1,2,1,1
	}
	for i := 1; i < 16; i++ {
		e = append(e, 0x05E00020+uint32(2*i), 0x1111)
	}
	e = append(e,
		0x05C00000, 0x0004, // CMDCTRL: polygon
		0x05C00002, 0x0000, // CMDLINK
		0x05C00004, 0x0000, // CMDPMOD
		0x05C00006, 0x801F, // CMDCOLR: color 31
		0x05C00008, 0x0000, // CMDSRCA
		0x05C0000A, 0x0000, // CMDSIZE
		0x05C0000C, 100, // XA
		0x05C0000E, 50, // YA
		0x05C00010, 119, // XB
		0x05C00012, 50, // YB
		0x05C00014, 119, // XC
		0x05C00016, 69, // YC
		0x05C00018, 100, // XD
		0x05C0001A, 69, // YD
		0x05C0001C, 0x0000, // CMDGRDA
		0x05C00020, 0x8000, // END
		0x05D00000, 0x0000, // TVMR
		0x05D00002, 0x0000, // FBCR
		0x05D00004, 0x0000, // PTMR
		0x05D00006, 0x0000, // EWDR
		0x05D00008, 0x0000, // EWLR
		0x05D0000A, 0x4EDF, // EWRR
	)
	out := make([]byte, 0, len(e)*4+8)
	for _, v := range e {
		var b [4]byte
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], v)
		out = append(out, b[:]...)
	}
	return append(out, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
}

// sndDriverBlob returns the 512 byte sound RAM image the
// IP uploads before SNDON: the 68EC000 reset vectors
// (SSP 0x0007F000, PC 0x00000100), zero padding, and at
// 0x100 a hand assembled driver that programs SCSP slot
// 0 exactly as the SCSP package gates do (master volume
// 15, forward loop over the 256 sample table at sound
// RAM 0x2000, instant attack, unity pitch, direct send
// 7) and keys it on, then spins.
//
// Every driver instruction is MOVE.W #imm,(abs).L
// (0x33FC) except the final BRA.S self (0x60FE).
func sndDriverBlob() []byte {
	blob := make([]byte, 512)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(blob[0:4], 0x0007F000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(blob[4:8], 0x00000100)
	code := []uint32{
		// addr, value pairs for MOVE.W #value, addr
		0x100400, 0x800F, // RegMaster: MEM4MB, MVOL 15
		0x100000, 0x4100, // slot 0 ctrl: KYONB, forward loop
		0x100002, 0x2000, // SA low: table at 0x2000
		0x100004, 0x0000, // LSA
		0x100006, 0x00FF, // LEA 255
		0x100008, 0x001F, // EG1: AR 31 instant
		0x10000A, 0x7800, // EG2: KRS 15, scaling off
		0x10000C, 0x0000, // Vol: TL 0
		0x100010, 0x0000, // Pitch: unity
		0x100016, 0xE000, // OutSel: DISDL 7, centre
		0x100000, 0xC100, // slot 0 ctrl: KYONEX on
	}
	off := 0x100
	put := func(w uint16) {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(blob[off:off+2], w)
		off += 2
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(code); i += 2 {
		put(0x33FC)
		put(uint16(code[i+1]))
		put(uint16(code[i] >> 16))
		put(uint16(code[i]))
	}
	put(0x60FE) // BRA.S self
	return blob
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/enginetest/enginetest.go ====================

// Package enginetest builds the synthetic Saturn disc the
// SAT-4 full stack gate boots: a 2048 byte sector ISO9660
// image whose initial program is hand assembled SH-2 (built
// with the tiny assembler in asm.go) plus a hand assembled
// 68EC000 sound driver, all synthetic data generated here.
// Nothing in this package is a Sega artifact: the System ID
// is written from the published layout, the IP is original
// code written for this gate, and PAYLOAD.BIN is a byte
// pattern defined below.
//
// The IP runs only through system BootDisc. Its jobs, in
// order, each recorded as a numbered milestone in Work
// RAM-H at MilestoneAddress:
//
//	1: the master released the slave with SMPC SSHON and
//	   the slave answered the 42 to 43 handshake
//	2: the CD block read PAYLOAD.BIN from the ISO root
//	   through the command and data port path and its
//	   checksum matched the builder's checksum
//	3: VDP2 NBG0 and a VDP1 polygon are programmed (the
//	   frame probes match the SAT-2 gate's display)
//	4: the 68EC000 sound driver was uploaded to sound RAM
//	   and SNDON released it; the driver keys a PCM slot
//	   looping the sine table at unity pitch
//	5: the pad was read once through SMPC INTBACK
//	6: a backup RAM pattern round tripped through the
//	   odd byte bus path
//	7: the IP reached its idle loop
//
// On a failure the IP stores a stage code at
// MilestoneAddress+0x20 and parks: 1 slave handshake
// timeout is not implemented (the spin is unbounded by
// design; the host gate fails on its frame budget), 2 is
// checksum mismatch, 4 file not found in the root
// directory, 5 backup read back mismatch, 6 a CD command
// answered with the reject status byte.
package enginetest

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
)

// MilestoneAddress is the Work RAM-H address of the
// milestone block the IP writes.
const MilestoneAddress = 0x06004000

// Milestone block field offsets (bytes from
// MilestoneAddress).
const (
	MileMagic    = 0x00 // 0x53415434, "SAT4"
	MileCount    = 0x04 // number of milestones recorded
	MileOrder    = 0x08 // milestone IDs in hit order, one byte each
	MileChecksum = 0x10 // guest computed PAYLOAD.BIN checksum
	MileSize     = 0x14 // guest read PAYLOAD.BIN size
	MilePad      = 0x18 // four INTBACK bytes: port status, ID, data 1, data 2
	MileBackup   = 0x1C // 0xA5 when the backup round trip matched
	MileError    = 0x20 // failure stage code, 0 while healthy
	MileMaster   = 0x30 // master handshake cell: the master writes 42
	MileSlave    = 0x34 // slave handshake cell: the slave answers 43
	MileAlive    = 0x38 // slave alive counter, incremented in its idle loop
)

// MileMagicValue is the magic the IP stores at
// MilestoneAddress on entry.
const MileMagicValue = 0x53415434

// PadMask is the button mask the host sets before running
// the machine: Up, A, R and Start. In the SMPC INTBACK
// data format (active low) the expected report bytes are
// port status 0xF1, peripheral ID 0x02, data byte 1 0xE3
// (Right, Left, Down, C and B read 1; Up, Start and A
// read 0) and data byte 2 0x7F (R reads 0, the rest 1).
const PadMask = 0x1811 // Start | R | A | Up in system button bits

// ExpectedPad is the four byte INTBACK report for PadMask.
var ExpectedPad = [4]byte{0xF1, 0x02, 0xE3, 0x7F}

// PayloadSize is the size of PAYLOAD.BIN in bytes.
const PayloadSize = 1000

// Payload returns the PAYLOAD.BIN contents: a fixed byte
// pattern, byte i = (31*i + 7) mod 256.
func Payload() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, PayloadSize)
	for i := range out {
		out[i] = byte(31*i + 7)
	}
	return out
}

// PayloadChecksum is the additive byte checksum the IP
// computes over the payload (a 32 bit wrapping sum).
func PayloadChecksum() uint32 {
	var sum uint32
	for _, b := range Payload() {
		sum += uint32(b)
	}
	return sum
}

// SineTable returns the 256 sample 16 bit sine table the
// 68EC000 driver loops on SCSP slot 0, the same table the
// SCSP package gates use: at unity pitch the loop period
// is exactly 256 samples, 172.27 Hz at 44100 Hz.
func SineTable() []uint16 {
	out := make([]uint16, 256)
	for i := range out {
		v := int16(30000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/256))
		out[i] = uint16(v)
	}
	return out
}

// putText writes s into a fixed width field, padding with
// spaces, matching the System ID text field convention.
func putText(sec []byte, off int, width int, s string) {
	for i := 0; i < width; i++ {
		sec[off+i] = ' '
	}
	copy(sec[off:off+width], s)
}

// dirRecord builds one ISO9660 directory record with both
// endian extent and size fields.
func dirRecord(extent int, size int, flags byte, name []byte) []byte {
	length := 33 + len(name)
	if length%2 == 1 {
		length++
	}
	rec := make([]byte, length)
	rec[0] = byte(length)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rec[2:6], uint32(extent))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[6:10], uint32(extent))
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(rec[10:14], uint32(size))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[14:18], uint32(size))
	rec[25] = flags
	rec[32] = byte(len(name))
	copy(rec[33:], name)
	return rec
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/enginetest/enginetest_test.go ====================

package enginetest_test

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/cd"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/enginetest"
)

// The fixture disc parses through the cd layer with the
// documented header fields, and the payload in its root
// reads back as the fixture pattern.
func TestBuildDiscParses(t *testing.T) {
	iso := enginetest.BuildDisc()
	img, err := cd.OpenBytes(iso, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenBytes: %v", err)
	}
	hdr, err := img.SaturnHeader()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SaturnHeader: %v", err)
	}
	if hdr.IPSize != enginetest.IPSize {
		t.Fatalf("IPSize = %#x, want %#x", hdr.IPSize, enginetest.IPSize)
	}
	if hdr.MasterStack != 0x06001000 || hdr.SlaveStack != 0x06000800 {
		t.Fatalf("stacks = %#x/%#x, want 0x06001000/0x06000800", hdr.MasterStack, hdr.SlaveStack)
	}
	entries, err := img.ListRoot()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListRoot: %v", err)
	}
	if len(entries) != 1 || entries[0].Name != "PAYLOAD.BIN" || entries[0].Size != enginetest.PayloadSize {
		t.Fatalf("root entries = %v", entries)
	}
	data, err := img.ReadFile(entries[0])
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadFile: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(data, enginetest.Payload()) {
		t.Fatal("payload bytes differ from the fixture pattern")
	}
	// The image is deterministic: rebuilding gives the
	// same bytes.
	if again := enginetest.BuildDisc(); !bytes.Equal(again, iso) {
		t.Fatal("BuildDisc is not deterministic")
	}
	sum := enginetest.PayloadChecksum()
	manual := uint32(0)
	for _, b := range enginetest.Payload() {
		manual += uint32(b)
	}
	if sum != manual {
		t.Fatalf("PayloadChecksum = %#x, manual sum %#x", sum, manual)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/enginetest/ip.go ====================

package enginetest

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
)

// This file builds the initial program: hand assembled
// SH-2 (master and slave) plus the data it works on (the
// VDP poke table, the 68EC000 sound driver blob, the sine
// table, and the payload file name). The program is
// written against the documented device interfaces only:
// SMPC commands through COMREG with the SF handshake, CD
// block commands through CR1 to CR4 with the CMOK
// handshake and the one word per scanline data port
// (reads synchronized to the SCU HBlank-IN status bit),
// SCSP sound RAM uploads, SMPC INTBACK pad reports, and
// backup RAM through its odd byte window.
//
// Register plan for the master: R14 is the milestone
// block base, R13 the Work RAM-L sector buffer. The leaf
// subroutines (smpc_cmd, cd_cmd, copy_words) and the
// inlined fetch sequence use R0 to R12 as scratch and
// never touch R13 or R14.

// Device addresses used by the IP.
const (
	addrSMPCComReg = 0x0010001F
	addrSMPCSF     = 0x00100063
	addrSMPCOREGB  = 0x00100021 // OREG0; OREGs stride 2 from here
	addrBackupBase = 0x00180000
	addrSCUIMS     = 0x05FE00A0
	addrSCUIST     = 0x05FE00A4
	addrCDHIRQ     = 0x05800008
	addrCDCR1      = 0x05800018
	addrCDCR4      = 0x05800024
	addrCDDataPort = 0x05800028
	addrSoundRAM   = 0x05A00000
	addrSineRAM    = 0x05A02000
	addrSectorBuf  = 0x00200000
	addrStackM     = 0x060020E8 // Stack-M field of the loaded System ID
)

// ipDataAddrs carries the absolute RAM addresses of the
// data section, recomputed per assembly pass until the
// layout is stable.
type ipDataAddrs struct {
	table  uint32
	driver uint32
	sine   uint32
	name   uint32
}

// movC loads a small constant (0 to 255) into a register
// using the sign extended immediate plus an EXTU.B fixup
// where needed.
func movC(a *Asm, rn int, v int) {
	switch {
	case v >= -128 && v <= 127:
		a.MovImm(rn, v)
	case v >= 0 && v <= 255:
		a.MovImm(rn, v-256)
		a.ExtuB(rn, rn)
	default:
		panic("movC: constant out of range")
	}
}

// addC adds a positive constant to a register in
// immediate sized chunks.
func addC(a *Asm, rn int, v int) {
	for v > 127 {
		a.AddImm(rn, 127)
		v -= 127
	}
	if v > 0 {
		a.AddImm(rn, v)
	}
}

// mark emits the milestone recording sequence: the ID
// byte appends to the order log and the count increments.
func mark(a *Asm, id int) {
	a.LoadLDisp(0, 14, MileCount)
	a.MovReg(1, 14)
	a.AddImm(1, MileOrder)
	a.AddReg(1, 0)
	movC(a, 2, id)
	a.StoreB(1, 2)
	a.LoadLDisp(0, 14, MileCount)
	a.AddImm(0, 1)
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 0, MileCount)
}

var rejSeq int

// checkReject emits the response check after a cd_cmd:
// the status byte (the high byte of the CR1 response in
// R0) of 0xFF is the reject encoding and parks the IP at
// the stage 6 failure.
func checkReject(a *Asm) {
	rejSeq++
	skip := fmt.Sprintf("rejok%d", rejSeq)
	a.Shlr8(0)
	a.Shlr8(0)
	a.ExtuB(0, 0)
	a.MovImm(1, -1)
	a.ExtuB(1, 1)
	a.CmpEq(0, 1)
	a.Bf(skip)
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("fail6")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label(skip)
}

// loadBE32 emits a big endian 32 bit load assembled from
// byte loads: the word at byte offset off from the base
// register lands in rdst. R0, R1 and R2 are scratch.
func loadBE32(a *Asm, rbase int, off int, rdst int) {
	a.MovReg(1, rbase)
	addC(a, 1, off)
	a.LoadBInc(0, 1)
	a.ExtuB(rdst, 0)
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		a.LoadBInc(0, 1)
		a.ExtuB(0, 0)
		a.Shll8(rdst)
		a.OrReg(rdst, 0)
	}
}

var fetchSeq int

// fetch emits the CD read sequence: with the FAD in R4,
// the sector count in R5 and the destination in R6, it
// plays the range into buffer partition 0, waits until
// the partition holds the sectors, pulls them through
// the data port with Get Then Delete, and waits for the
// transfer end flag. R0 to R12 are scratch.
func fetch(a *Asm) {
	fetchSeq++
	id := fetchSeq
	a.MovReg(10, 4) // FAD
	a.MovReg(11, 5) // count
	a.MovReg(12, 6) // dest
	// Play: start24 = 0x800000|FAD, end24 = 0x800000|FAD+count-1.
	a.LoadLit(0, 0x800000)
	a.AddReg(0, 10)
	a.MovReg(1, 0)
	a.Shlr8(1)
	a.Shlr8(1)
	movC(a, 2, 0x10)
	a.Shll8(2)
	a.AddReg(1, 2)
	a.MovReg(4, 1) // CR1
	a.MovReg(5, 0)
	a.ExtuW(5, 5) // CR2 = start24 low
	a.MovReg(0, 10)
	a.AddReg(0, 11)
	a.AddImm(0, -1)
	a.LoadLit(1, 0x800000)
	a.AddReg(0, 1)
	a.MovReg(6, 0)
	a.Shlr8(6)
	a.Shlr8(6) // CR3 = end24 high, play mode 0
	a.MovReg(7, 0)
	a.ExtuW(7, 7) // CR4 = end24 low
	a.Bsr("cd_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	checkReject(a)
	// Wait until partition 0 holds count sectors.
	ws := fmt.Sprintf("fws%d", id)
	a.Label(ws)
	movC(a, 4, 0x51)
	a.Shll8(4)
	a.MovImm(5, 0)
	a.MovImm(6, 0)
	a.MovImm(7, 0)
	a.Bsr("cd_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	a.CmpHS(1, 11) // R1 = buffered count from the CR4 response
	a.Bf(ws)
	a.Nop()
	// Get Then Delete the range into the destination.
	movC(a, 4, 0x63)
	a.Shll8(4)
	a.MovImm(5, 0)
	a.MovImm(6, 0)
	a.MovReg(7, 11)
	a.Bsr("cd_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	checkReject(a)
	// Read count*1024 words from the data port, one word
	// per scanline, synchronized on the HBlank-IN bit.
	a.MovReg(9, 11)
	a.Shll8(9)
	a.Shll2(9) // words = count * 1024
	a.MovReg(10, 12)
	a.LoadLit(3, addrCDDataPort)
	a.LoadLit(8, addrSCUIST)
	rd := fmt.Sprintf("frd%d", id)
	wt := fmt.Sprintf("fwt%d", id)
	dn := fmt.Sprintf("fdn%d", id)
	a.Label(rd)
	a.LoadW(0, 3)
	a.StoreW(10, 0)
	a.AddImm(10, 2)
	a.Dt(9)
	a.Bt(dn)
	a.Nop()
	a.MovImm(0, 0)
	a.StoreL(8, 0) // clear IST, HBlank-IN included
	a.Label(wt)
	a.LoadL(0, 8)
	a.TstImm(4) // HBlank-IN is IST bit 2
	a.Bt(wt)
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra(rd)
	a.Nop()
	a.Label(dn)
	// Wait for the transfer end flag (HIRQ EHST, bit 7)
	// so the pending delete lands before the next
	// command.
	a.LoadLit(8, addrCDHIRQ)
	eh := fmt.Sprintf("feh%d", id)
	a.Label(eh)
	a.LoadW(0, 8)
	a.TstImm(0x80)
	a.Bt(eh)
	a.Nop()
}

// buildIP assembles the IP code and data and returns the
// full IP image: System ID, code at offset 0x100, then
// the data section. ipSize is the header IP size; the
// image is exactly that long.
func buildIP(checksum uint32, ipSize int) []byte {
	codeLen := 0
	var words []uint16
	var data []byte
	for pass := 0; pass < 4; pass++ {
		dataOff := 0x100 + codeLen
		if dataOff%4 != 0 {
			dataOff += 4 - dataOff%4
		}
		base := uint32(0x06002000 + dataOff)
		table := vdpTable()
		driver := sndDriverBlob()
		sine := SineTable()
		name := []byte("PAYLOAD.BIN;1\x00")
		addrs := ipDataAddrs{
			table:  base,
			driver: base + uint32(len(table)),
			sine:   base + uint32(len(table)+len(driver)),
			name:   base + uint32(len(table)+len(driver)+2*len(sine)),
		}
		data = data[:0]
		data = append(data, table...)
		data = append(data, driver...)
		for _, w := range sine {
			var b [2]byte
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(b[:], w)
			data = append(data, b[:]...)
		}
		data = append(data, name...)
		words = assembleIP(addrs, checksum)
		if got := len(words) * 2; got == codeLen {
			break
		} else {
			codeLen = got
		}
		if pass == 3 {
			panic("enginetest: IP layout did not converge")
		}
	}

	img := make([]byte, ipSize)
	putText(img, 0x10, 16, "SEGA ENTERPRISES")
	putText(img, 0x20, 10, "MK-SAT4")
	putText(img, 0x2A, 6, "V1.000")
	putText(img, 0x30, 8, "20261013")
	putText(img, 0x38, 8, "CD-1/1")
	putText(img, 0x40, 10, "JTUE")
	putText(img, 0x50, 16, "JOYPAD")
	putText(img, 0x60, 112, "SAT-4 ENGINETEST")
	copy(img[0:16], "SEGA SEGASATURN ")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xE0:0xE4], uint32(ipSize))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xE8:0xEC], 0x06001000) // Stack-M
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xEC:0xF0], 0x06000800) // Stack-S
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xF0:0xF4], 0x06010000) // first read address
	for i, w := range words {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(img[0x100+2*i:0x100+2*i+2], w)
	}
	dataOff := 0x100 + len(words)*2
	if dataOff%4 != 0 {
		dataOff += 4 - dataOff%4
	}
	copy(img[dataOff:], data)
	return img
}

// assembleIP emits the whole SH-2 program against the
// given data addresses.
func assembleIP(addrs ipDataAddrs, checksum uint32) []uint16 {
	rejSeq = 0
	fetchSeq = 0
	a := NewAsm(0x06002100)

	// Entry: the boot ROM enters both CPUs here with
	// their header stacks. SP equal to Stack-M means
	// this is the master; anything else is the slave.
	a.Label("entry")
	a.LoadLit(1, addrStackM)
	a.LoadL(1, 1)
	a.CmpEq(15, 1)
	a.Bt("master")
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("slave")
	a.Nop()
	a.Pool()

	// ---- master ----
	a.Label("master")
	a.LoadLit(14, MilestoneAddress)
	a.LoadLit(13, addrSectorBuf)
	a.LoadLit(0, MileMagicValue)
	a.StoreL(14, 0)
	a.MovImm(0, 0)
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 0, MileCount)
	// Mask every SCU source and clear the status word:
	// this program polls status bits and takes no
	// interrupts.
	a.LoadLit(1, addrSCUIMS)
	a.MovImm(0, -1)
	a.StoreL(1, 0)
	a.LoadLit(1, addrSCUIST)
	a.MovImm(0, 0)
	a.StoreL(1, 0)
	// Slave handshake: write 42, release the slave, wait
	// for its 43.
	a.MovImm(0, 42)
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 0, MileMaster)
	movC(a, 0, 0x02) // SSHON
	a.Bsr("smpc_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("wslave")
	a.LoadLDisp(0, 14, MileSlave)
	a.CmpEqImm(43)
	a.Bf("wslave")
	a.Nop()
	mark(a, 1)
	a.Pool()

	// CD on, then initialize the block.
	movC(a, 0, 0x08) // CDON
	a.Bsr("smpc_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	movC(a, 4, 0x04)
	a.Shll8(4)
	a.MovImm(5, 0)
	a.MovImm(6, 0)
	a.MovImm(7, 0)
	a.Bsr("cd_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	// Fetch the primary volume descriptor (LBA 16 is
	// FAD 166).
	movC(a, 4, 166)
	a.MovImm(5, 1)
	a.MovReg(6, 13)
	fetch(a)
	// Root directory extent from the root record at
	// PVD+156 (its big endian extent field is +6 into
	// the record).
	loadBE32(a, 13, 162, 7)
	movC(a, 0, 150)
	a.AddReg(7, 0)
	a.MovReg(4, 7)
	a.MovImm(5, 1)
	a.MovReg(6, 13)
	fetch(a)
	a.Pool()

	// Scan the root directory for PAYLOAD.BIN;1.
	a.MovReg(5, 13) // record pointer
	a.Label("scan")
	a.LoadB(0, 5)
	a.ExtuB(0, 0)
	a.TstReg(0, 0)
	a.Bf("scanlive")
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("fail4") // zero length record: end of the used directory
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("scanlive")
	a.MovReg(1, 5)
	a.AddImm(1, 32)
	a.LoadB(0, 1)
	a.ExtuB(0, 0)
	movC(a, 2, 13)
	a.CmpEq(0, 2)
	a.Bt("scanname")
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("nextrec")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("scanname")
	a.MovReg(1, 5)
	a.AddImm(1, 33)
	a.LoadLit(2, addrs.name)
	movC(a, 3, 13)
	a.Label("cmpbyte")
	a.LoadB(0, 1)
	a.LoadB(4, 2)
	a.CmpEq(0, 4)
	a.Bt("byteok")
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("nextrec")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("byteok")
	a.AddImm(1, 1)
	a.AddImm(2, 1)
	a.Dt(3)
	a.Bf("cmpbyte")
	a.Nop()
	// Found: extent big endian at record+6, size at
	// record+14.
	loadBE32(a, 5, 6, 7)
	loadBE32(a, 5, 14, 8)
	a.Bra("haverec")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("nextrec")
	a.LoadB(0, 5)
	a.ExtuB(0, 0)
	a.AddReg(5, 0)
	a.Bra("scan")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("haverec")
	a.Pool()

	// Fetch the payload, then checksum its bytes. The
	// size is stashed in the milestone block first: the
	// fetch sequence uses every scratch register,
	// R8 included.
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 8, MileSize)
	movC(a, 0, 150)
	a.AddReg(7, 0)
	a.MovReg(4, 7)
	a.MovReg(5, 8)
	a.LoadLit(0, 2047)
	a.AddReg(5, 0)
	a.Shlr8(5)
	a.Shlr2(5)
	a.Shlr(5) // sector count = (size + 2047) / 2048
	a.MovReg(6, 13)
	fetch(a)
	a.MovReg(1, 13)
	a.LoadLDisp(2, 14, MileSize)
	a.MovImm(0, 0)
	a.Label("sumloop")
	a.LoadBInc(3, 1)
	a.ExtuB(3, 3)
	a.AddReg(0, 3)
	a.Dt(2)
	a.Bf("sumloop")
	a.Nop()
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 0, MileChecksum)
	a.LoadLit(1, checksum)
	a.LoadLDisp(0, 14, MileChecksum)
	a.CmpEq(0, 1)
	a.Bt("sumok")
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("fail2")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("sumok")
	mark(a, 2)
	a.Pool()

	// VDP: run the poke table (address, value) pairs,
	// terminated by a zero address.
	a.LoadLit(1, addrs.table)
	a.Label("vploop")
	a.LoadLInc(2, 1)
	a.LoadLInc(3, 1)
	a.TstReg(2, 2)
	a.Bt("vpdone")
	a.Nop()
	a.StoreW(2, 3)
	a.Bra("vploop")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("vpdone")
	mark(a, 3)
	a.Pool()

	// Sound: upload the driver blob and the sine table,
	// then release the sound CPU.
	a.LoadLit(4, addrs.driver)
	a.LoadLit(5, addrSoundRAM)
	a.MovImm(6, 1)
	a.Shll8(6) // 256 words: the 512 byte blob
	a.Bsr("copy_words")
	a.Nop()
	a.LoadLit(4, addrs.sine)
	a.LoadLit(5, addrSineRAM)
	a.MovImm(6, 1)
	a.Shll8(6) // 256 words
	a.Bsr("copy_words")
	a.Nop()
	movC(a, 0, 0x06) // SNDON
	a.Bsr("smpc_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	mark(a, 4)
	a.Pool()

	// Pad: one INTBACK for port 1 peripheral data only
	// (IREG0 port 2 mode 3 skips the second port, IREG1
	// PEN set, IREG2 F0).
	a.LoadLit(1, 0x00100001)
	movC(a, 0, 0xC0)
	a.StoreB(1, 0)
	a.LoadLit(1, 0x00100003)
	movC(a, 0, 0x08)
	a.StoreB(1, 0)
	a.LoadLit(1, 0x00100005)
	movC(a, 0, 0xF0)
	a.StoreB(1, 0)
	movC(a, 0, 0x10) // INTBACK
	a.Bsr("smpc_cmd")
	a.Nop()
	a.LoadLit(1, addrSMPCOREGB)
	a.LoadLit(2, MilestoneAddress+MilePad)
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		a.LoadB(0, 1)
		a.StoreB(2, 0)
		if i < 3 {
			a.AddImm(1, 2)
			a.AddImm(2, 1)
		}
	}
	mark(a, 5)
	a.Pool()

	// Backup RAM: even offsets must read 0xFF; write a
	// 32 byte pattern through the odd byte path and read
	// it back byte for byte.
	a.LoadLit(1, addrBackupBase)
	a.LoadB(0, 1)
	a.CmpEqImm(-1)
	a.Bt("bkuok")
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("fail5")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("bkuok")
	a.LoadLit(1, addrBackupBase+1)
	movC(a, 2, 32)
	movC(a, 3, 0x41)
	a.Label("bkwr")
	a.StoreB(1, 3)
	a.AddImm(1, 2)
	a.AddImm(3, 1)
	a.Dt(2)
	a.Bf("bkwr")
	a.Nop()
	a.LoadLit(1, addrBackupBase+1)
	movC(a, 2, 32)
	movC(a, 3, 0x41)
	a.Label("bkrd")
	a.LoadB(0, 1)
	a.ExtuB(0, 0)
	a.CmpEq(0, 3)
	a.Bt("bkbyteok")
	a.Nop()
	a.Bra("fail5")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("bkbyteok")
	a.AddImm(1, 2)
	a.AddImm(3, 1)
	a.Dt(2)
	a.Bf("bkrd")
	a.Nop()
	a.LoadLit(1, MilestoneAddress+MileBackup)
	movC(a, 0, 0xA5)
	a.StoreB(1, 0)
	mark(a, 6)
	mark(a, 7)
	a.Label("park")
	a.Bra("park")
	a.Nop()
	a.Pool()

	// Failure parks: store the stage code and park.
	a.Label("fail2")
	movC(a, 0, 2)
	a.Bra("failstore")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("fail4")
	movC(a, 0, 4)
	a.Bra("failstore")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("fail5")
	movC(a, 0, 5)
	a.Bra("failstore")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("fail6")
	movC(a, 0, 6)
	a.Bra("failstore")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("failstore")
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 0, MileError)
	a.Label("park2")
	a.Bra("park2")
	a.Nop()
	a.Pool()

	// ---- leaf subroutines ----

	// smpc_cmd: R0 is the command byte. Writes COMREG,
	// then waits out the SF handshake (SF sets as the
	// command executes and clears on the next poll).
	a.Label("smpc_cmd")
	a.LoadLit(1, addrSMPCComReg)
	a.StoreB(1, 0)
	a.LoadLit(1, addrSMPCSF)
	a.Label("scset")
	a.LoadB(0, 1)
	a.TstImm(1)
	a.Bt("scset")
	a.Nop()
	a.Label("scclr")
	a.LoadB(0, 1)
	a.TstImm(1)
	a.Bf("scclr")
	a.Nop()
	a.Rts()
	a.Nop()
	a.Pool()

	// cd_cmd: R4 to R7 are CR1 to CR4; returns the
	// response CR1 in R0 and CR4 in R1. The CRs are
	// written while CMOK is still set (so no poll can
	// execute a half written command), then HIRQ is
	// cleared to admit the command.
	a.Label("cd_cmd")
	a.LoadLit(8, addrCDHIRQ)
	a.Label("ccready")
	a.LoadW(0, 8)
	a.TstImm(1)
	a.Bt("ccready")
	a.Nop()
	a.LoadLit(9, addrCDCR1)
	a.StoreW(9, 4)
	a.AddImm(9, 4)
	a.StoreW(9, 5)
	a.AddImm(9, 4)
	a.StoreW(9, 6)
	a.AddImm(9, 4)
	a.StoreW(9, 7)
	a.MovImm(0, 0)
	a.StoreW(8, 0)
	a.Label("ccresp")
	a.LoadW(0, 8)
	a.TstImm(1)
	a.Bt("ccresp")
	a.Nop()
	a.LoadLit(9, addrCDCR1)
	a.LoadW(0, 9)
	a.LoadLit(9, addrCDCR4)
	a.LoadW(1, 9)
	a.Rts()
	a.Nop()
	a.Pool()

	// copy_words: R4 source, R5 destination, R6 word
	// count; copies upward.
	a.Label("copy_words")
	a.Label("cwloop")
	a.LoadWInc(0, 4)
	a.StoreW(5, 0)
	a.AddImm(5, 2)
	a.Dt(6)
	a.Bf("cwloop")
	a.Nop()
	a.Rts()
	a.Nop()
	a.Pool()

	// ---- slave ----
	// Waits for the master's 42, answers 43, then counts
	// forever in the alive cell.
	a.Label("slave")
	a.LoadLit(14, MilestoneAddress)
	a.Label("swait")
	a.LoadLDisp(0, 14, MileMaster)
	a.CmpEqImm(42)
	a.Bf("swait")
	a.Nop()
	movC(a, 0, 43)
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 0, MileSlave)
	a.Label("alive")
	a.LoadLDisp(0, 14, MileAlive)
	a.AddImm(0, 1)
	a.StoreLDisp(14, 0, MileAlive)
	a.Bra("alive")
	a.Nop()
	a.Pool()

	words, err := a.Build()
	if err != nil {
		panic("enginetest: assembling the IP: " + err.Error())
	}
	return words
}

// Command libretro is the libretro shell for the
// from-scratch Go Sega Saturn core (SAT-4). It
// follows the family pattern set by the SNES,
// Genesis and PS1 shells: a c-shared package main
// exporting the retro_* C ABI, with the machine
// behind it in the system package.
//
// Choices specific to this core:
//
//   - Content loads by path (need_fullpath): .cue
//     and .iso images open through the cd image
//     layer and boot through system.BootDisc, the
//     documented HLE boot (System ID verified, IP
//     loaded to Work RAM-H, entry at 0x06002100).
//     No boot ROM is involved. A disc whose System
//     ID or IP does not check out is rejected.
//   - The guest framebuffer is presented at the
//     machine's current TVMD display size every
//     frame, with a SET_GEOMETRY notice when the
//     size changes (the PS1 shell's approach). Base
//     geometry 320x224, max 640x480, aspect 4:3.
//   - The frame rate is declared 60.0: the machine
//     runs 477,273 master cycles per frame at
//     28.6364 MHz, the NTSC rate. PAL timing is out
//     of scope for this core.
//   - Audio is 44,100 Hz stereo from the SCSP.
//   - The Saturn digital pad has no Select button,
//     so the libretro Select id is unmapped. Face
//     buttons map letter for letter (A, B, X, Y);
//     the Saturn C and Z buttons, which have no
//     libretro face counterparts, sit on R2 and L2.
//     L and R are the libretro L and R ids.
//   - RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM is the backup RAM's
//     LOGICAL view: the bus stores backup data in a
//     32 KiB packed slice that the odd byte window
//     maps onto the cells, and Bus.BackupRAM exposes
//     exactly that logical store, so the pointer is
//     handed out directly and guest writes are live
//     in it.
//   - RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM is Work RAM Low
//     followed by Work RAM High (2 MiB). The two
//     regions live in disjoint bus slices, so the
//     shell mirrors them in one cache slice with the
//     GBA shell's hash discipline: frontend edits to
//     the cache are pushed into the machine before
//     the frame runs, and machine state is pulled
//     back into the cache after it.
//   - retro_reset re-boots the loaded disc: a bare
//     machine Reset parks the CPUs at the BIOS
//     window with no program, so the shell resets
//     and runs BootDisc again when a disc is loaded.
package main

/*
#cgo CFLAGS: -std=c11

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

}

	if (!saturn_audio_batch_cb) return 0;
	return saturn_audio_batch_cb(data, frames);

}

struct saturn_log_callback { saturn_log_printf_t log; };

	struct saturn_log_callback *lc = (struct saturn_log_callback *)data;
	if (saturn_call_environ(27, data)) { // GET_LOG_INTERFACE
		saturn_log_fn = lc->log;
	}
}
static void saturn_log_msg(int level, const char *msg) {
	if (saturn_log_fn) saturn_log_fn(level, "%s", msg);
}

	const void *data;
	size_t size;
	const char *meta;

import "C"

import (
	"hash/fnv"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/system"
)

// libretro constants used by this shell.
const (
	envSetPixelFormat  = 10
	envGetLogInterface = 27 // handled inside the C helper
	envSetGeometry     = 37

	pixelFormatXRGB8888 = 1

	deviceJoypad = 1

	logInfo = 1
	logWarn = 2

	memSaveRAM   = 0 // RETRO_MEMORY_SAVE_RAM
	memSystemRAM = 1 // RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM
)

var (
	sys     *system.System
	hasDisc bool
	videoW  int
	videoH  int

	// sysRAMCache mirrors Work RAM Low then High for
	// RETRO_MEMORY_SYSTEM_RAM; sysRAMHash is the hash
	// of the cache as of the last sync.
	sysRAMCache []byte
	sysRAMHash  uint64
)

// joypadMap pairs libretro joypad ids with the
// Saturn pad bits they drive (see the package
// comment for the map's rationale). Id 2 (Select)
// is absent: the Saturn digital pad has no Select.
var joypadMap = []struct {
	id  uint
	bit uint16
}{
	{0, system.ButtonB},     // B
	{1, system.ButtonY},     // Y
	{3, system.ButtonStart}, // Start
	{4, system.ButtonUp},    // Up
	{5, system.ButtonDown},  // Down
	{6, system.ButtonLeft},  // Left
	{7, system.ButtonRight}, // Right
	{8, system.ButtonA},     // A
	{9, system.ButtonX},     // X
	{10, system.ButtonL},    // L
	{11, system.ButtonR},    // R
	{12, system.ButtonZ},    // L2: Saturn Z
	{13, system.ButtonC},    // R2: Saturn C
}

// saturnLog prints one line through the frontend
// log interface when one was offered.
func saturnLog(level int, msg string) {
	cmsg := C.CString(msg)
	C.saturn_log_msg(C.int(level), cmsg)
	C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cmsg))
}

func hashBytes(b []byte) uint64 {
	h := fnv.New64a()
	h.Write(b)
	return h.Sum64()
}

// pullSystemRAM refreshes the SYSTEM_RAM cache from
// the machine and records its hash.
func pullSystemRAM() {
	copy(sysRAMCache[:0x100000], sys.Bus.WorkRAMLow())
	copy(sysRAMCache[0x100000:], sys.Bus.WorkRAMHigh())
	sysRAMHash = hashBytes(sysRAMCache)
}

// syncSystemRAM pushes frontend edits into the
// machine when the cache changed since the last
// sync, then pulls the machine state back after
// the frame. Called around RunFrame.
func pushSystemRAM() {
	if hashBytes(sysRAMCache) != sysRAMHash {
		copy(sys.Bus.WorkRAMLow(), sysRAMCache[:0x100000])
		copy(sys.Bus.WorkRAMHigh(), sysRAMCache[0x100000:])
	}
}

// loadPath loads a disc image from a filesystem
// path and boots it through BootDisc. It is the
// Go-level core of retro_load_game, kept plainly
// typed so the shell test can drive it in-process.
func loadPath(path string) bool {
	m := system.New()
	if err := m.LoadDisc(path); err != nil {
		saturnLog(logWarn, "[GoSaturn] cannot open disc image: "+err.Error())
		return false
	}
	if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
		saturnLog(logWarn, "[GoSaturn] disc does not boot: "+err.Error())
		return false
	}
	pf := C.int(pixelFormatXRGB8888)
	C.saturn_call_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&pf))
	sys = m
	hasDisc = true
	videoW, videoH = m.DisplaySize()
	sysRAMCache = make([]byte, 2*1024*1024)
	pullSystemRAM()
	saturnLog(logInfo, "[GoSaturn] loaded "+path)
	return true
}

// runFrame advances the loaded machine one frame,
// presenting video and audio. It is the Go-level
// core of retro_run.
func runFrame() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	C.saturn_call_input_poll()
	var mask uint16
	for _, b := range joypadMap {
		if C.saturn_call_input_state(0, deviceJoypad, 0, C.uint(b.id)) != 0 {
			mask |= b.bit
		}
	}
	sys.SetButtons(mask)
	pushSystemRAM()
	sys.RunFrame()
	pullSystemRAM()

	w, h := sys.DisplaySize()
	if w != videoW || h != videoH {
		videoW, videoH = w, h
		geom := C.struct_saturn_game_geometry{
			base_width:   C.uint(w),
			base_height:  C.uint(h),
			max_width:    640,
			max_height:   480,
			aspect_ratio: 4.0 / 3.0,
		}
		C.saturn_call_environ(envSetGeometry, unsafe.Pointer(&geom))
	}
	if fb := sys.Framebuffer(); len(fb) >= w*h && w > 0 && h > 0 {
		C.saturn_call_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]), C.uint(w), C.uint(h), C.size_t(w*4))
	}
	samples := sys.AudioBuffer()
	if len(samples) == 0 {
		return
	}
	frames := len(samples) / 2
	done := int(C.saturn_call_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&samples[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
	for i := done * 2; i+1 < len(samples); i += 2 {
		C.saturn_call_audio(C.int16_t(samples[i]), C.int16_t(samples[i+1]))
	}
}

//export retro_api_version
func retro_api_version() C.uint { return 1 }

//export retro_init
func retro_init() {}

//export retro_deinit
func retro_deinit() { sys = nil }

//export retro_set_environment
func retro_set_environment(cb C.saturn_environ_cb_t) {
	C.saturn_set_environ_cb(cb)
	var lc C.struct_saturn_log_callback
	C.saturn_grab_log(unsafe.Pointer(&lc))
}

//export retro_set_audio_sample

//export retro_set_audio_sample_batch

	C.saturn_set_audio_batch_cb(cb)
}

//export retro_set_input_poll

//export retro_set_input_state

//export retro_get_system_info
func retro_get_system_info(info *C.struct_saturn_system_info) {
	info.library_name = C.saturn_core_name()
	info.library_version = C.saturn_core_version()
	info.valid_extensions = C.saturn_core_extensions()
	info.need_fullpath = true
	info.block_extract = false
}

//export retro_get_system_av_info
func retro_get_system_av_info(info *C.struct_saturn_system_av_info) {
	w, h := 320, 224
	if sys != nil {
		w, h = sys.DisplaySize()
	}
	info.geometry.base_width = C.uint(w)
	info.geometry.base_height = C.uint(h)
	info.geometry.max_width = 640
	info.geometry.max_height = 480
	info.geometry.aspect_ratio = 4.0 / 3.0
	// 477,273 master cycles per frame at 28.6364 MHz
	// is the NTSC frame; the timing is declared as
	// the round 60.0 the machine definition gives.
	info.timing.fps = 60.0
	info.timing.sample_rate = 44100
}

//export retro_get_region
func retro_get_region() C.uint { return 0 } // NTSC

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_saturn_game_info) bool {
	if info == nil || info.path == nil {
		return false
	}
	return loadPath(C.GoString(info.path))
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() {
	sys = nil
	hasDisc = false
}

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	sys.Reset()
	if hasDisc {
		// A bare reset parks the CPUs with no program;
		// re-boot the loaded disc (see the package
		// comment).
		if err := sys.BootDisc(); err != nil {
			saturnLog(logWarn, "[GoSaturn] re-boot after reset failed: "+err.Error())
		}
	}
	videoW, videoH = sys.DisplaySize()
	pullSystemRAM()
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() { runFrame() }

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.StateSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) bool {
	if sys == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	if int(size) < len(state) {
		return false
	}
	C.memcpy(data, unsafe.Pointer(&state[0]), C.size_t(len(state)))
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer, size C.size_t) bool {
	if sys == nil {
		return false
	}
	ok := sys.Deserialize(C.GoBytes(data, C.int(size))) == nil
	if ok {
		videoW, videoH = sys.DisplaySize()
		pullSystemRAM()
	}
	return ok
}

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.uint) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		// The backup RAM logical store (32 KiB),
		// handed out directly: guest writes land in
		// this very slice through the bus.
		return unsafe.Pointer(&sys.Bus.BackupRAM()[0])
	case memSystemRAM:
		return unsafe.Pointer(&sysRAMCache[0])
	}
	return nil
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.uint) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.Bus.BackupRAM()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sysRAMCache))
	}
	return 0
}

//export retro_cheat_reset
func retro_cheat_reset() {}

//export retro_cheat_set
func retro_cheat_set(index C.uint, enabled bool, code *C.char) {}

func main() {}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/libretro/main_test.go ====================

package main

// In-process shell gates. The payload is the
// enginetest package's synthetic Saturn disc, driven
// through the same Go-level load and run functions
// the retro_* exports wrap. The literal C ABI is
// gated end to end by the shared enginetest harness
// (go_backend), which loads the built .so through
// the production bridge; this test exists so go test
// alone catches shell regressions: load by path,
// BootDisc boot, guest milestones, save state round
// trip, memory regions, clean rejection of bad
// content.
//
// The guest's pad stage reads no buttons here (no
// frontend input callbacks are installed), so its
// INTBACK report is the all released pattern; the
// system gate covers the pressed buttons case.

import (
	"bytes"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/enginetest"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/system"
)

func mileCount() int {
	return int(sys.Bus.Read32(enginetest.MilestoneAddress + enginetest.MileCount))
}

func TestShellDisc(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	isoPath := filepath.Join(dir, "enginetest.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(isoPath, enginetest.BuildDisc(), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !loadPath(isoPath) {
		t.Fatal("loadPath(.iso) returned false")
	}
	defer func() { sys = nil; hasDisc = false }()

	// The guest runs from BootDisc and completes all
	// seven milestones through the shell's runFrame.
	frames := 0
	for frames < 300 && mileCount() < 7 {
		runFrame()
		frames++
	}
	if got := sys.Bus.Read32(enginetest.MilestoneAddress + enginetest.MileError); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("guest failure stage = %d", got)
	}
	if got := mileCount(); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("milestones = %d after %d shell frames, want 7", got, frames)
	}
	if got := sys.Bus.Read32(enginetest.MilestoneAddress + enginetest.MileChecksum); got != enginetest.PayloadChecksum() {
		t.Fatalf("guest checksum = %#x, want %#x", got, enginetest.PayloadChecksum())
	}
	// No buttons through the shell: the INTBACK data
	// bytes read all released.
	pad := sys.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()[0x4000+enginetest.MilePad : 0x4000+enginetest.MilePad+4]
	if !bytes.Equal(pad, []byte{0xF1, 0x02, 0xFF, 0xFF}) {
		t.Fatalf("INTBACK report = % x, want f1 02 ff ff (no buttons)", pad)
	}

	// Settle the VDP1 draw and swap pipeline, then
	// probe the frame the system gate proves.
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		runFrame()
	}
	if w, h := sys.DisplaySize(); w != 320 || h != 224 {
		t.Fatalf("display size = %dx%d, want 320x224", w, h)
	}
	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if got := fb[0]; got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (0,0) = %#x, want green 0xFF00FF00", got)
	}
	if got := fb[55*320+105]; got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (105,55) = %#x, want white 0xFFFFFFFF", got)
	}

	// Save state round trip through the machine the
	// shell wraps (retro_serialize forwards here).
	saved := sys.Serialize()
	if len(saved) != sys.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state length = %d, want StateSize %d", len(saved), sys.StateSize())
	}
	m2 := system.New()
	if err := m2.Deserialize(saved); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if again := m2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(saved, again) {
		t.Error("state bytes differ after a serialize/deserialize round trip")
	}

	// Memory regions: backup RAM logical store is
	// 32 KiB; the SYSTEM_RAM mirror is 2 MiB and
	// holds the booted IP in its Work RAM-H half.
	if got := len(sys.Bus.BackupRAM()); got != 32*1024 {
		t.Errorf("backup RAM length = %d, want %d", got, 32*1024)
	}
	if got := len(sysRAMCache); got != 2*1024*1024 {
		t.Fatalf("SYSTEM_RAM cache length = %d, want %d", got, 2*1024*1024)
	}
	if got := string(sysRAMCache[0x100000+0x2000 : 0x100000+0x2000+16]); got != "SEGA SEGASATURN " {
		t.Errorf("SYSTEM_RAM Work RAM-H holds %q at the IP base, want the System ID", got)
	}
	// The guest's backup pattern is visible through
	// the logical store the shell exposes.
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if got := sys.Bus.BackupRAM()[i]; got != byte(0x41+i) {
			t.Fatalf("backup byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, got, byte(0x41+i))
		}
	}
}

func TestShellRejectsBadContent(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	raw := filepath.Join(dir, "data.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(raw, make([]byte, 40*2048), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if loadPath(raw) {
		t.Error("loadPath accepted an .iso with no Saturn System ID")
	}
	missing := filepath.Join(dir, "missing.iso")
	if loadPath(missing) {
		t.Error("loadPath accepted a missing .iso file")
	}
	if sys != nil {
		t.Error("a rejected load left a machine behind")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scsp/dsp.go ====================

package scsp

import (
	"encoding/binary"
)

// The SCSP effect DSP (FH-1) subset implemented here.
//
// ST-77 documents the DSP register areas, its internal buffers
// and the ring buffer used for delays, but it does not publish
// the FH-1 microinstruction encoding. This package therefore
// executes a documented subset encoding of its own design, using
// the manual's data set: COEF (64 signed 13 bit coefficients in
// Q12), MADRS (32 sound RAM address entries), TEMP (128 words of
// 24 bit work RAM whose base pointer decreases by one every
// sample, per the manual), MEMS (32 inputs), MIXS (16 mix inputs
// from the slots), EFREG (16 outputs) and EXTS (2 CD inputs).
//
// Per sample, MEMS is loaded as: MEMS 0 to 15 are the MIXS slot
// sends for this sample, MEMS 16 and 17 are EXTS (CD left and
// right), and MEMS 18 to 31 start at 0 and are the destinations
// for memory reads. TEMP, EFREG and the accumulator persist
// across samples. All values are held in sample units (a full
// scale sample is 32767) inside 24 bit containers; memory reads
// and writes move one 16 bit big endian sound RAM word.
//
// One microprogram step is four 16 bit words in MPRO at page
// offset 800H plus 8 times the step index. Execution runs steps
// 0 to 127 and stops early at the first all zero step, which is
// the no-op padding.
//
//	word 0: bits 15 to 12 destination (0 none, 1 TEMP, 2 EFREG,
//	  3 MEMS, 4 sound RAM write through MADRS), bits 11 to 5
//	  destination index, bits 4 to 1 ALU operation, bit 0 MUL
//	  enable.
//	word 1: bits 15 to 14 source kind (0 MEMS, 1 TEMP, 2 MIXS,
//	  3 EFREG), bit 13 source extension (when set: 4 EXTS,
//	  5 last memory read result, 6 zero, 7 immediate from
//	  word 3), bits 12 to 6 source index, bits 5 to 0 COEF
//	  index.
//	word 2: bit 15 memory read enable, bits 12 to 8 MEMS index
//	  the read lands in, bits 7 to 2 MADRS index.
//	word 3: bits 7 to 0 immediate byte (sign extended), the
//	  remaining bits are unused in this subset.
//
// Per step: the source value X is selected. If MUL is enabled the
// operand P is (X times COEF) shifted right 12 (the Q12 product);
// otherwise P is X. The ALU then applies its operation between
// the accumulator and P: 0 none (accumulator unchanged), 1 load,
// 2 add, 3 subtract, 4 and, 5 or, 6 xor, 7 shift left 1, 8
// arithmetic shift right 1 (the shifts ignore the accumulator).
// The destination, if any, receives the accumulator after the
// ALU step, except destination 4 which writes the accumulator as
// one sound RAM word at the MADRS address plus the memory phase.
//
// Memory addressing: the word address is the ring base from RBP
// plus the MADRS entry plus the memory phase, wrapped to the
// ring length. The memory phase advances by one word per sample.
// The ring length is RBL (8K, 16K, 32K or 64K words) unless
// COEF 63 is nonzero, in which case COEF 63 is the ring length in
// words; that extension exists so small delay lines are usable
// and testable, and it is the one deliberate departure from the
// manual data set in this subset. A read in a step happens before
// that step's source selection result is used by later steps, so
// a program can read a delay tap into MEMS and multiply it in the
// following step.
//
// Not in the subset, stored only in the page: the Y bus and table
// addressing of the real FH-1, the second accumulator, and any
// conditional execution. Programs using fields outside the list
// above are not executed by this subset.

// DSP destination kinds (word 0 bits 15 to 12).
const (
	dspDestNone = iota
	dspDestTEMP
	dspDestEFREG
	dspDestMEMS
	dspDestMemWrite
)

// DSP ALU operations (word 0 bits 4 to 1).
const (
	dspALUNone = iota
	dspALULoad
	dspALUAdd
	dspALUSub
	dspALUAnd
	dspALUOr
	dspALUXor
	dspALUShl
	dspALUShr
)

// DSP source kinds.
const (
	dspSrcMEMS = iota
	dspSrcTEMP
	dspSrcMIXS
	dspSrcEFREG
	dspSrcEXTS
	dspSrcMemRead
	dspSrcZero
	dspSrcImm
)

type dspState struct {
	acc      int32
	temp     [128]int32
	tempBase int // ring base, decreases by one per sample
	mems     [32]int32
	mixs     [16]int32
	efreg    [16]int32
	exts     [2]int32
	memrd    int32
	memPhase uint32
	samples  uint64
}

// coef reads COEF entry i from the page as a signed 13 bit value.
func (s *SCSP) coef(i int) int32 {
	v := int32(s.reg16(RegCOEF+i*2)) & 0x1FFF
	if v&0x1000 != 0 {
		v -= 0x2000
	}
	return v
}

// madrs reads MADRS entry i from the page (a word address).
func (s *SCSP) madrs(i int) uint32 {
	return uint32(s.reg16(RegMADRS + i*2))
}

// ringWords returns the DSP ring buffer length in words.
func (s *SCSP) ringWords() uint32 {
	if c := s.reg16(RegCOEF + 63*2); c != 0 {
		return uint32(c)
	}
	rbl := (s.reg16(RegRing) >> 12) & 3
	return 8192 << uint(rbl)
}

// ringBaseWords returns the DSP ring buffer base in words, from
// RBP (byte address bits 19 to 13).
func (s *SCSP) ringBaseWords() uint32 {
	rbp := uint32(s.reg16(RegRing) & 0x7F)
	return rbp << 12
}

func (d *dspState) memAddr(s *SCSP, madrsIdx int) uint32 {
	wrap := s.ringWords()
	if wrap == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	a := s.madrs(madrsIdx) + d.memPhase
	return s.ringBaseWords() + a%wrap
}

// runDSP executes this sample's microprogram. mixs holds the 16
// slot sends computed by renderSlots.
func (s *SCSP) runDSP(mixs [16]int32) {
	d := &s.dsp
	d.mixs = mixs
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		d.mems[i] = mixs[i]
	}
	d.mems[16] = d.exts[0]
	d.mems[17] = d.exts[1]
	for i := 18; i < 32; i++ {
		d.mems[i] = 0
	}
	d.memrd = 0
	d.tempBase = (d.tempBase - 1) & 127

	for step := 0; step < 128; step++ {
		off := RegMPRO + step*8
		if off+7 >= len(s.regs) {
			break
		}
		w0 := s.reg16(off)
		w1 := s.reg16(off + 2)
		w2 := s.reg16(off + 4)
		w3 := s.reg16(off + 6)
		if w0|w1|w2|w3 == 0 {
			break
		}
		s.dspStep(w0, w1, w2, w3)
	}

	if wrap := s.ringWords(); wrap != 0 {
		d.memPhase = (d.memPhase + 1) % wrap
	}
	d.samples++
}

func (s *SCSP) dspStep(w0, w1, w2, w3 uint16) {
	d := &s.dsp

	// Memory read first, so later steps (and this step's MEMRD
	// source) can use the value.
	if w2&0x8000 != 0 {
		madrsIdx := int(w2>>2) & 0x3F
		if madrsIdx > 31 {
			madrsIdx = 31
		}
		addr := d.memAddr(s, madrsIdx)
		var v int32
		if int(addr)*2+1 < len(s.ram) {
			v = int32(int16(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(s.ram[addr*2 : addr*2+2])))
		}
		d.mems[int(w2>>8)&0x1F] = v
		d.memrd = v
	}

	srcKind := int(w1>>14) & 3
	if w1&0x2000 != 0 {
		srcKind += 4
	}
	srcIdx := int(w1>>6) & 0x7F
	var x int32
	switch srcKind {
	case dspSrcMEMS:
		x = d.mems[srcIdx&31]
	case dspSrcTEMP:
		x = d.temp[(d.tempBase+srcIdx)&127]
	case dspSrcMIXS:
		x = d.mixs[srcIdx&15]
	case dspSrcEFREG:
		x = d.efreg[srcIdx&15]
	case dspSrcEXTS:
		x = d.exts[srcIdx&1]
	case dspSrcMemRead:
		x = d.memrd
	case dspSrcZero:
		x = 0
	case dspSrcImm:
		x = int32(int8(w3))
	}

	p := x
	if w0&1 != 0 {
		coefIdx := int(w1) & 0x3F
		p = int32((int64(x) * int64(s.coef(coefIdx))) >> 12)
	}

	switch int(w0>>1) & 0xF {
	case dspALULoad:
		d.acc = p
	case dspALUAdd:
		d.acc += p
	case dspALUSub:
		d.acc -= p
	case dspALUAnd:
		d.acc &= p
	case dspALUOr:
		d.acc |= p
	case dspALUXor:
		d.acc ^= p
	case dspALUShl:
		d.acc = p << 1
	case dspALUShr:
		d.acc = p >> 1
	}
	d.acc = clamp24(d.acc)

	destIdx := int(w0>>5) & 0x7F
	switch int(w0>>12) & 0xF {
	case dspDestTEMP:
		d.temp[(d.tempBase+destIdx)&127] = d.acc
	case dspDestEFREG:
		d.efreg[destIdx&15] = d.acc
	case dspDestMEMS:
		d.mems[destIdx&31] = d.acc
	case dspDestMemWrite:
		madrsIdx := destIdx & 31
		addr := d.memAddr(s, madrsIdx)
		if int(addr)*2+1 < len(s.ram) {
			v := uint16(int16(clamp16(int64(d.acc))))
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(s.ram[addr*2:addr*2+2], v)
		}
	}
}

// clamp24 keeps a DSP value inside the signed 24 bit container.
func clamp24(v int32) int32 {
	if v > 0x7FFFFF {
		return 0x7FFFFF
	}
	if v < -0x800000 {
		return -0x800000
	}
	return v
}

// writePage mirrors the DSP internal buffers into the page areas
// the manual defines: TEMP as two words per entry (low byte in
// the first word, bits 23 to 8 in the second), MEMS the same,
// MIXS the same, EFREG one word per entry, and EXTS one word per
// entry.
func (d *dspState) writePage(s *SCSP) {
	put24 := func(off int, v int32) {
		if off+3 < len(s.regs) {
			s.setReg16(off, uint16(v&0xFF))
			s.setReg16(off+2, uint16((v>>8)&0xFFFF))
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 128; i++ {
		put24(RegTEMP+i*4, d.temp[(d.tempBase+i)&127])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		put24(RegMEMS+i*4, d.mems[i])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		put24(RegMIXS+i*4, d.mixs[i])
	}
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		if RegEFREG+i*2+1 < len(s.regs) {
			s.setReg16(RegEFREG+i*2, uint16(int16(clamp16(int64(d.efreg[i])))))
		}
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if RegEXTS+i*2+1 < len(s.regs) {
			s.setReg16(RegEXTS+i*2, uint16(int16(d.exts[i])))
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scsp/scsp.go ====================

// Package scsp models the Sega Saturn SCSP (Yamaha YMF292) sound
// processor: 32 PCM and FM slots, the FH-1 style effect DSP, three
// timers, the internal DMA, the MIDI stub, and the on chip MC68EC000
// sound CPU.
//
// Register map and semantics follow the SCSP User's Manual
// (Sega ST-77-R2-052594, the ST-068 family document). Where the
// manual and the slice brief disagreed, the manual won; the
// divergences are:
//
//   - Slot registers: the manual allocates 12 words per slot on a
//     32 byte stride (words 12 to 15 of each stride are unused),
//     not 8 words per slot.
//   - MADRS: the manual allocates 32 words at 100780H, not 64.
//     COEF is 64 words at 100700H. The DSP internal buffers live
//     at 100C00H and up: TEMP 128 entries, MEMS 32, MIXS 16,
//     EFREG 16 and EXTS 2.
//   - Interrupt enables: SCIEB, SCIPD and SCIRE belong to the sound
//     CPU (the 68EC000); MCIEB, MCIPD and MCIRE belong to the main
//     CPU (the SH-2 side). SCIPD bit 5 written by the main CPU is
//     the manual request to the sound CPU; MCIPD bit 5 written by
//     the sound CPU is the manual request to the main CPU, exported
//     here as OnSoundRequest. Pending bits are cleared by writing
//     1 bits to the matching reset register (SCIRE or MCIRE), not
//     by writing the pending register.
//   - There is no CD send level or pan field in the common register
//     area. CD-DA arrives on EXTS0 and EXTS1 and is mixed with the
//     EFSDL and EFPAN fields of slot registers 16 and 17, which is
//     the routing games and the BIOS use.
//   - DIPAN full left is 1FH (right channel at minus infinity) and
//     full right is 0FH, per the manual pan table.
//   - The m68ec000 package in this module exposes PC, D, A and SR
//     as methods, not fields.
//
// Shared storage model: the caller owns the 512 KB sound RAM slice
// and the 4 KB register page slice. New keeps both slices without
// copying them. Because both CPUs write the page directly, this
// chip observes writes by polling the page once per sample tick:
// KYONEX execution, the SCIRE and MCIRE clear registers, the bit 5
// manual request bits of SCIPD and MCIPD, and the DMA DEXE bit are
// all edge processed at that poll. The chip writes back the bits
// hardware would clear (KYONEX, DEXE, the reset registers) and
// mirrors the pending registers, the monitor call address, the
// sound stacks and the DSP internal buffer areas into the page.
//
// Clock model: the SCSP runs at 22.5792 MHz and the machine (SH-2)
// clock at 28.63636 MHz. One sample tick is 512 SCSP cycles, which
// is 44100 Hz. Step takes SH-2 cycles and converts them with an
// exact integer accumulator (cycles times 22579200, divided by
// 512 times 28636360), so there is no float drift. The accumulator
// is part of the serialized state; a restore that shifted the
// sample phase would be a determinism failure. Per sample tick the
// 68EC000 runs a 256 cycle budget of its own 11.2896 MHz clock
// (11289600 divided by 44100 is exactly 256) by calling its Step
// until the budget is spent; the final instruction may overshoot
// the budget, which is deterministic because the CPU state is
// serialized.
//
// Sound hold: SetSoundOn(false) models SMPC SNDOFF. While off, the
// 68EC000 is held in reset (its PC never advances), no sample ticks
// are generated, AudioBuffer stays empty, and Step accumulates
// nothing at all (the cycles are discarded, not banked). Turning
// sound on resets the 68EC000, which reads its initial stack
// pointer and PC from sound RAM addresses 0 and 4. Power on state
// on real hardware is sound held off until the SMPC releases it,
// but New starts in the released (on) state so package level tests
// can drive the chip directly; the system calls SetSoundOn(false)
// at boot.
//
// Approximations, stated plainly:
//
//   - Slot sample interpolation is linear between adjacent
//     samples.
//   - EG moves linearly in its 10 bit attenuation level. The rate
//     table below stands in for the manual rate descriptions; key
//     rate scaling follows the formula other implementations
//     document from hardware (effective rate is twice the rate
//     field plus twice KRS plus the signed octave plus FNS bit 9,
//     and KRS 15 turns scaling off, per the manual).
//   - Attenuation (EG level, TL bit weights, send levels and pan)
//     is computed from the manual decibel figures with the exact
//     20 log10 relation, not from a copied ROM table.
//   - MVOL gain is MVOL divided by 15, so 15 is unity and 0 is
//     silent, matching how the BIOS and drivers use it.
//   - FM modulation uses the previous sample outputs of the two
//     selected slots, averaged, scaled by the manual MDL maximum
//     address shift table. The manual two generation sound stack
//     timing is not modelled.
//   - The DSP executes the documented subset described in dsp.go,
//     not the full FH-1 encoding, which ST-77 does not publish.
package scsp

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"math"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/chips/m68ec000"
)

// Clock and geometry constants.
const (
	scspClockHz   = 22579200
	machineClock  = 28636360
	sampleRate    = 44100
	scspPerSample = 512 // SCSP cycles per sample tick
	cpuPerSample  = 256 // 68EC000 cycles per sample tick

	soundRAMSize = 512 * 1024
	regPageSize  = 4 * 1024

	addrRAMLimit = 0x080000 // CPU byte addresses 0x000000 to 0x07FFFF
	addrRegBase  = 0x100000 // CPU byte addresses 0x100000 to 0x100FFF
)

// Slot register word offsets within one slot stride of 0x20 bytes.
// The manual figure 4.2 lists 12 words; words 12 to 15 are unused.
const (
	slotStride = 0x20

	SlotCtrl   = 0x00 // KYONEX, KYONB, SBCTL, SSCTL, LPCTL, PCM8B, SA[19:16]
	SlotSA     = 0x02 // SA[15:0]
	SlotLSA    = 0x04
	SlotLEA    = 0x06
	SlotEG1    = 0x08 // D2R, D1R, EGHOLD, AR
	SlotEG2    = 0x0A // LPSLNK, KRS, DL, RR
	SlotVol    = 0x0C // STWINH, SDIR, TL
	SlotFM     = 0x0E // MDL, MDXSL, MDYSL
	SlotPitch  = 0x10 // OCT, FNS
	SlotLFO    = 0x12 // LFORE, LFOF, PLFOWS, PLFOS, ALFOWS, ALFOS
	SlotInSel  = 0x14 // ISEL, IMXL
	SlotOutSel = 0x16 // DISDL, DIPAN, EFSDL, EFPAN
)

// Common register offsets within the page, from the manual common
// control register figure and the worked interrupt example (which
// pins SCIEB at word address 10041EH, SCILV0 at 100424H, SCILV1 at
// 100426H, SCILV2 at 100428H and MCIEB at 10042AH). Words 40AH to
// 40EH and word 416H are unused in the manual figure; they stay
// plain storage here.
const (
	RegMaster  = 0x400 // MEM4MB, DAC18B, VER, MVOL
	RegRing    = 0x402 // RBL, RBP
	RegMIDIIn  = 0x404 // MOFULL, MOEMP, MIOVF, MIFULL, MIEMP, MIBUF
	RegMIDIOut = 0x406 // MOBUF
	RegMonitor = 0x408 // MSLC, CA
	RegDMALow  = 0x410 // DMEA[15:1]
	RegDMAHigh = 0x412 // DMEA[19:16], DRGA[11:1]
	RegDMACtrl = 0x414 // DGATE, DDIR, DEXE, DTLG[11:1]
	RegTimerA  = 0x418 // TACTL, TIMA
	RegTimerB  = 0x41A // TBCTL, TIMB
	RegTimerC  = 0x41C // TCCTL, TIMC
	RegSCIEB   = 0x41E
	RegSCIPD   = 0x420
	RegSCIRE   = 0x422
	RegSCILV0  = 0x424
	RegSCILV1  = 0x426
	RegSCILV2  = 0x428
	RegMCIEB   = 0x42A
	RegMCIPD   = 0x42C
	RegMCIRE   = 0x42E
)

// Sound stack and DSP register area offsets within the page, from
// the manual memory map figure.
const (
	RegStackA = 0x600 // SOUS generation A, 32 words
	RegStackB = 0x640 // SOUS generation B, 32 words
	RegCOEF   = 0x700 // 64 words
	RegMADRS  = 0x780 // 32 words
	RegMPRO   = 0x800 // 128 steps of 4 words
	RegTEMP   = 0xC00 // 128 entries of 2 words
	RegMEMS   = 0xE00 // 32 entries of 2 words
	RegMIXS   = 0xE80 // 16 entries of 2 words
	RegEFREG  = 0xEC0 // 16 words
	RegEXTS   = 0xEE0 // 2 words
)

// Interrupt source bits, from the manual interrupt factor table.
const (
	IntEXT0    = 0
	IntEXT1    = 1
	IntEXT2    = 2
	IntMIDIIn  = 3
	IntDMAEnd  = 4
	IntCPU     = 5
	IntTimerA  = 6
	IntTimerB  = 7
	IntTimerC  = 8
	IntMIDIOut = 9
	IntSample  = 10
)

// SCSP is one sound processor over shared RAM and register storage.
type SCSP struct {
	ram  []byte
	regs []byte

	cpu *m68ec000.CPU
	bus *cpuBus
	on  bool

	// OnSoundRequest, when set, is called once per rising main CPU
	// interrupt bit: a bit that is pending in MCIPD and enabled in
	// MCIEB and was not already signalled. The system wires it to
	// the SCU sound request source.
	OnSoundRequest func()

	acc int64 // SH-2 cycle to sample tick rational accumulator

	timers   [3]timerState
	sciPend  uint16
	mciPend  uint16
	mainSent uint16 // main bits already signalled via OnSoundRequest

	dma dmaState

	slots [32]slotState
	dsp   dspState

	cdQueue []int16
	audio   []int16
}

type timerState struct {
	preset  uint8
	counter uint8
	phase   int // prescaler phase, counts samples modulo 2^ctl
}

type dmaState struct {
	active      bool
	remaining   int
	ramWord     uint32
	regWord     uint32
	dirRegToRAM bool
	gate        bool
}

// cpuBus adapts the SCSP memory map to the 68EC000 Bus interface.
// CPU byte address 0x000000 to 0x07FFFF maps to sound RAM and
// 0x100000 to 0x100FFF maps to the register page. Every other
// address reads as 0 and ignores writes.
type cpuBus struct {
	s *SCSP
}

func (b *cpuBus) Read8(addr uint32) uint8 {
	v, _ := b.read(addr)
	return v
}

func (b *cpuBus) read(addr uint32) (byte, bool) {
	switch {
	case addr < addrRAMLimit:
		if int(addr) < len(b.s.ram) {
			return b.s.ram[addr], true
		}
	case addr >= addrRegBase && addr < addrRegBase+regPageSize:
		if int(addr-addrRegBase) < len(b.s.regs) {
			return b.s.regs[addr-addrRegBase], true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

func (b *cpuBus) write(addr uint32, v byte) {
	switch {
	case addr < addrRAMLimit:
		if int(addr) < len(b.s.ram) {
			b.s.ram[addr] = v
		}
	case addr >= addrRegBase && addr < addrRegBase+regPageSize:
		if int(addr-addrRegBase) < len(b.s.regs) {
			b.s.regs[addr-addrRegBase] = v
		}
	}
}

func (b *cpuBus) Read16(addr uint32) uint16 {
	hi, _ := b.read(addr)
	lo, _ := b.read(addr + 1)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

func (b *cpuBus) Read32(addr uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(b.Read16(addr))<<16 | uint32(b.Read16(addr+2))
}

func (b *cpuBus) Write8(addr uint32, v uint8) { b.write(addr, v) }

func (b *cpuBus) Write16(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	b.write(addr, byte(v>>8))
	b.write(addr+1, byte(v))
}

func (b *cpuBus) Write32(addr uint32, v uint32) {
	b.Write16(addr, uint16(v>>16))
	b.Write16(addr+2, uint16(v))
}

// New builds an SCSP over the caller owned sound RAM (512 KB) and
// register page (4 KB). Neither slice is copied. The chip starts
// in the sound on (released) state described in the package
// comment, with the 68EC000 reset once against the current RAM
// contents.
func New(ram []byte, regs []byte) *SCSP {
	s := &SCSP{ram: ram, regs: regs, on: true}
	s.bus = &cpuBus{s: s}
	s.cpu = m68ec000.New(s.bus)
	for i := range s.slots {
		s.slots[i].lfsr = 0xACE1 + uint32(i)*0x1B31
		s.slots[i].egLevel = egMaxQ
		s.slots[i].egPhase = egEnded
	}
	s.dsp.tempBase = 0
	s.cpu.Reset()
	return s
}

// CPU exposes the sound CPU for inspection by the system and by
// tests. The SCSP owns its stepping; callers must not Step it
// themselves while the SCSP is running.
func (s *SCSP) CPU() *m68ec000.CPU { return s.cpu }

// SoundOn reports whether sound is released.
func (s *SCSP) SoundOn() bool { return s.on }

// SetSoundOn releases or holds the sound block. Turning sound on
// after it was off resets the 68EC000 from the vectors in sound
// RAM. Turning it off holds the CPU in reset; while off, Step
// accumulates nothing and produces no audio.
func (s *SCSP) SetSoundOn(on bool) {
	if on == s.on {
		return
	}
	s.on = on
	if on {
		s.cpu.Reset()
	}
}

// Step advances the chip by the given number of SH-2 cycles. While
// sound is off the cycles are discarded entirely.
func (s *SCSP) Step(cycles int) {
	if cycles <= 0 || !s.on {
		return
	}
	s.acc += int64(cycles) * scspClockHz
	const denom = int64(scspPerSample) * machineClock
	for s.acc >= denom {
		s.acc -= denom
		s.sampleTick()
	}
}

// AudioBuffer drains the interleaved stereo output produced since
// the last call, at 44100 Hz.
func (s *SCSP) AudioBuffer() []int16 {
	out := s.audio
	s.audio = nil
	return out
}

// InputCDSamples queues interleaved stereo CD-DA samples. Each
// sample tick consumes one pair; an empty queue feeds silence.
func (s *SCSP) InputCDSamples(samples []int16) {
	s.cdQueue = append(s.cdQueue, samples...)
}

// reg16 reads one big endian word of the register page.
func (s *SCSP) reg16(off int) uint16 {
	if off+1 >= len(s.regs) {
		return 0
	}
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint16(s.regs[off : off+2])
}

// setReg16 writes one big endian word of the register page.
func (s *SCSP) setReg16(off int, v uint16) {
	if off+1 >= len(s.regs) {
		return
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(s.regs[off:off+2], v)
}

func (s *SCSP) slotReg(slot, wordOff int) uint16 {
	return s.reg16(slot*slotStride + wordOff)
}

// sampleTick runs one 44100 Hz tick: poll the page, advance the
// timers, render the slots, run the DSP, mix CD and effect output,
// service DMA and interrupts, then run the sound CPU.
func (s *SCSP) sampleTick() {
	s.pollPage()
	s.tickTimers()
	s.raiseSource(IntSample)

	var mixL, mixR int64
	mixs := s.renderSlots(&mixL, &mixR)

	// CD input for this tick.
	var cdL, cdR int16
	if len(s.cdQueue) >= 2 {
		cdL, cdR = s.cdQueue[0], s.cdQueue[1]
		s.cdQueue = s.cdQueue[2:]
	}
	s.dsp.exts[0] = int32(cdL)
	s.dsp.exts[1] = int32(cdR)

	s.runDSP(mixs)

	// Effect returns: EFREG[i] through EFSDL and EFPAN of slot i.
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		w := s.slotReg(i, SlotOutSel)
		g := sendGain(int(w>>5) & 7)
		if g == 0 || s.dsp.efreg[i] == 0 {
			continue
		}
		gl, gr := panGains(int(w & 0x1F))
		v := int64(s.dsp.efreg[i])
		mixL += int64(float64(v) * g * gl)
		mixR += int64(float64(v) * g * gr)
	}
	// CD returns: EXTS0 and EXTS1 through EFSDL and EFPAN of
	// slots 16 and 17.
	for ch, v := range []int32{int32(cdL), int32(cdR)} {
		w := s.slotReg(16+ch, SlotOutSel)
		g := sendGain(int(w>>5) & 7)
		if g == 0 || v == 0 {
			continue
		}
		gl, gr := panGains(int(w & 0x1F))
		mixL += int64(float64(v) * g * gl)
		mixR += int64(float64(v) * g * gr)
	}

	mvol := float64(s.reg16(RegMaster)&0x000F) / 15.0
	l := clamp16(int64(float64(mixL) * mvol))
	r := clamp16(int64(float64(mixR) * mvol))
	s.audio = append(s.audio, l, r)

	s.serviceDMA()
	s.deliverInterrupts()
	s.runCPU()
	s.writeMirrors()
}

// pollPage edge processes the page registers the chip owns.
func (s *SCSP) pollPage() {
	// KYONEX: any slot word 0 with bit 15 set executes key on and
	// off for every slot from its KYONB bit, then clears.
	kyonex := false
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if s.slotReg(i, SlotCtrl)&0x8000 != 0 {
			kyonex = true
		}
	}
	if kyonex {
		for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
			off := i*slotStride + SlotCtrl
			w := s.reg16(off)
			s.setReg16(off, w&^0x8000)
			if w&0x4000 != 0 {
				s.keyOn(i)
			} else {
				s.keyOff(i)
			}
		}
	}

	// Interrupt reset registers: a nonzero word clears the
	// matching pending bits and is then zeroed, as hardware does.
	if v := s.reg16(RegSCIRE); v != 0 {
		s.sciPend &^= v & 0x07FF
		s.setReg16(RegSCIRE, 0)
	}
	if v := s.reg16(RegMCIRE); v != 0 {
		s.mciPend &^= v & 0x07FF
		s.mainSent &^= v & 0x07FF
		s.setReg16(RegMCIRE, 0)
	}

	// Manual request bits: bit 5 of SCIPD written by the main CPU
	// requests the sound CPU; bit 5 of MCIPD written by the sound
	// CPU requests the main CPU. The page words are mirrors of the
	// internal pending state, so a set bit 5 that is not already
	// pending is a fresh request.
	if s.reg16(RegSCIPD)&(1<<IntCPU) != 0 && s.sciPend&(1<<IntCPU) == 0 {
		s.sciPend |= 1 << IntCPU
	}
	if s.reg16(RegMCIPD)&(1<<IntCPU) != 0 && s.mciPend&(1<<IntCPU) == 0 {
		s.mciPend |= 1 << IntCPU
	}

	// Timer presets: a changed TIMx byte restarts that timer from
	// the new preset.
	for i, off := range []int{RegTimerA, RegTimerB, RegTimerC} {
		p := uint8(s.reg16(off))
		if p != s.timers[i].preset {
			s.timers[i].preset = p
			s.timers[i].counter = p
			s.timers[i].phase = 0
		}
	}

	// DMA trigger: DEXE set starts a transfer at this tick. The
	// bit is cleared in the page, as hardware clears it at the end
	// of the transfer, which is instant in this model.
	ctrl := s.reg16(RegDMACtrl)
	if ctrl&0x2000 != 0 && !s.dma.active {
		low := s.reg16(RegDMALow)
		high := s.reg16(RegDMAHigh)
		s.dma.active = true
		s.dma.ramWord = (uint32(high>>12)&0xF)<<16 | uint32(low>>1)
		s.dma.regWord = uint32(high>>1) & 0x7FF
		s.dma.remaining = int(ctrl>>1) & 0x7FF
		s.dma.dirRegToRAM = ctrl&0x4000 != 0
		s.dma.gate = ctrl&0x8000 != 0
		s.setReg16(RegDMACtrl, ctrl&^0x2000)
	}
}

// tickTimers advances the three prescaled up counters. A counter
// that reaches FFH raises its interrupt source and reloads from
// its preset, so the interrupt period is 255 minus the preset
// prescaled ticks (a preset of FEH interrupts every tick).
func (s *SCSP) tickTimers() {
	for i, off := range []int{RegTimerA, RegTimerB, RegTimerC} {
		ctl := int(s.reg16(off)>>8) & 7
		t := &s.timers[i]
		t.phase++
		if t.phase < (1 << uint(ctl)) {
			continue
		}
		t.phase = 0
		t.counter++
		if t.counter == 0xFF {
			s.raiseSource(IntTimerA + i)
			t.counter = t.preset
		}
	}
}

// raiseSource sets a source bit in both pending registers; the two
// enable registers decide delivery per side.
func (s *SCSP) raiseSource(bit int) {
	s.sciPend |= 1 << uint(bit)
	s.mciPend |= 1 << uint(bit)
}

// interruptLevel returns the autovector level programmed for a
// source. SCILV0, SCILV1 and SCILV2 hold bits 0, 1 and 2 of the
// level code. Sources 0 to 6 use their own column; sources 7 to
// 10 share column 7, per the manual level register figure.
func (s *SCSP) interruptLevel(src int) int {
	col := src
	if col > 7 {
		col = 7
	}
	l0 := (s.reg16(RegSCILV0) >> uint(col)) & 1
	l1 := (s.reg16(RegSCILV1) >> uint(col)) & 1
	l2 := (s.reg16(RegSCILV2) >> uint(col)) & 1
	return int(l0 | l1<<1 | l2<<2)
}

// deliverInterrupts fires the main CPU callback for rising enabled
// main bits and latches the best enabled sound CPU interrupt.
func (s *SCSP) deliverInterrupts() {
	mciEnabled := s.mciPend & s.reg16(RegMCIEB) & 0x07FF
	rising := mciEnabled &^ s.mainSent
	if rising != 0 {
		s.mainSent |= rising
		if s.OnSoundRequest != nil {
			for b := 0; b <= 10; b++ {
				if rising&(1<<uint(b)) != 0 {
					s.OnSoundRequest()
				}
			}
		}
	}
	// Bits that are no longer pending and enabled stop being
	// signalled, so a later raise fires again.
	s.mainSent &= mciEnabled

	sciEnabled := s.sciPend & s.reg16(RegSCIEB) & 0x07FF
	best := 0
	for b := 0; b <= 10; b++ {
		if sciEnabled&(1<<uint(b)) != 0 {
			if lv := s.interruptLevel(b); lv > best {
				best = lv
			}
		}
	}
	if best > 0 {
		s.cpu.Interrupt(best)
	}
}

// serviceDMA runs a latched transfer instantly at tick
// granularity and raises the DMA end source.
func (s *SCSP) serviceDMA() {
	if !s.dma.active {
		return
	}
	s.dma.active = false
	for n := 0; n < s.dma.remaining; n++ {
		ramOff := int(s.dma.ramWord+uint32(n)) * 2
		regOff := int(s.dma.regWord+uint32(n)) * 2
		switch {
		case s.dma.gate:
			// DGATE zero clear: the destination is filled with 0
			// and the source is not read.
			if s.dma.dirRegToRAM {
				if ramOff+1 < len(s.ram) {
					s.ram[ramOff], s.ram[ramOff+1] = 0, 0
				}
			} else {
				if regOff+1 < len(s.regs) {
					s.regs[regOff], s.regs[regOff+1] = 0, 0
				}
			}
		case s.dma.dirRegToRAM:
			if ramOff+1 < len(s.ram) && regOff+1 < len(s.regs) {
				s.ram[ramOff] = s.regs[regOff]
				s.ram[ramOff+1] = s.regs[regOff+1]
			}
		default:
			if ramOff+1 < len(s.ram) && regOff+1 < len(s.regs) {
				s.regs[regOff] = s.ram[ramOff]
				s.regs[regOff+1] = s.ram[ramOff+1]
			}
		}
	}
	s.raiseSource(IntDMAEnd)
}

// runCPU spends this tick's 256 cycle 68EC000 budget.
func (s *SCSP) runCPU() {
	budget := cpuPerSample
	for budget > 0 {
		budget -= s.cpu.Step()
	}
}

// writeMirrors updates the page words the chip owns as outputs:
// the pending registers, the MIDI status (input empty, output
// empty), the monitor call address for the MSLC slot, and the DSP
// internal buffer areas.
func (s *SCSP) writeMirrors() {
	s.setReg16(RegSCIPD, s.sciPend)
	s.setReg16(RegMCIPD, s.mciPend)

	// MIDI stub: input FIFO empty (MIEMP), output FIFO empty
	// (MOEMP), no data in MIBUF.
	s.setReg16(RegMIDIIn, 0x4800)

	mon := s.reg16(RegMonitor)
	mslc := int(mon>>11) & 0x1F
	ca := 0
	if mslc < 32 {
		ca = int(s.slots[mslc].phase>>16) >> 12 & 0x7FF
	}
	s.setReg16(RegMonitor, mon&0xF800|uint16(ca))

	s.dsp.writePage(s)
}

func clamp16(v int64) int16 {
	if v > 32767 {
		return 32767
	}
	if v < -32768 {
		return -32768
	}
	return int16(v)
}

// decibel gain helpers. The manual tables are in decibels; the
// gain is 10 to the power of dB over 20, computed, not tabulated.
func dbGain(db float64) float64 {
	if db <= -96 {
		return 0
	}
	return math.Pow(10, db/20)
}

// sendGain maps a 3 bit send level (DISDL, EFSDL, IMXL) through
// the manual table: 0 is no send, 1 to 7 are minus 36 dB up to
// 0 dB in 6 dB steps.
func sendGain(v int) float64 {
	if v == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return dbGain(float64(v-7) * 6)
}

// panGains maps a 5 bit pan value through the manual pan table:
// 00H and 10H are centre, 01H to 0FH move right by attenuating
// the left channel 3 dB per step (0FH is full right), and 11H to
// 1FH move left the same way (1FH is full left).
func panGains(pan int) (float64, float64) {
	switch {
	case pan == 0x00 || pan == 0x10:
		return 1, 1
	case pan == 0x0F:
		return 0, 1
	case pan == 0x1F:
		return 1, 0
	case pan < 0x10:
		return dbGain(-3 * float64(pan)), 1
	default:
		return 1, dbGain(-3 * float64(pan-0x10))
	}
}
