			t.Fatalf("restored audio differs at sample %d: %d vs %d", i, got[i], want[i])
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scsp/slot.go ====================

package scsp

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
)

// Envelope phases.
const (
	egIdle = iota
	egAttack
	egDecay1
	egDecay2
	egRelease
	egEnded
)

// egMaxQ is the maximum attenuation level (10 bit 3FFH) in Q8.
const egMaxQ = 0x3FF << 8

// slotState is one slot's runtime state. The register fields are
// read from the shared page on every tick, so only true runtime
// state lives here.
type slotState struct {
	active  bool
	phase   int64 // waveform position from SA, samples in Q16
	dir     int64 // 1 forward, -1 reverse (loop modes 2 and 3)
	egPhase int
	egLevel int32 // attenuation in Q8: 0 full volume, egMaxQ silent
	egHold  int32 // EGHOLD remaining attack hold ticks

	lfoPhase uint32 // Q32 phase
	lfsr     uint32

	prevOut int32 // previous sample output, the FM stack model
	out     int32 // current sample output before the mixers
}

// slotRegs is the decoded view of one slot's 12 register words.
type slotRegs struct {
	kyonb  bool
	sbctl  int
	ssctl  int
	lpctl  int
	pcm8b  bool
	sa     int
	lsa    int
	lea    int
	d2r    int
	d1r    int
	eghold bool
	ar     int
	lpslnk bool
	krs    int
	dl     int
	rr     int
	stwinh bool
	sdir   bool
	tl     int
	mdl    int
	mdxsl  int
	mdysl  int
	oct    int // signed octave, -8 to 7
	fns    int
	lfore  bool
	lfof   int
	plfows int
	plfos  int
	alfows int
	alfos  int
	isel   int
	imxl   int
	disdl  int
	dipan  int
	efsdl  int
	efpan  int
}

func (s *SCSP) decodeSlot(i int) slotRegs {
	var r slotRegs
	w0 := s.slotReg(i, SlotCtrl)
	r.kyonb = w0&0x4000 != 0
	r.sbctl = int(w0>>12) & 3
	r.ssctl = int(w0>>10) & 3
	r.lpctl = int(w0>>8) & 3
	r.pcm8b = w0&0x0080 != 0
	r.sa = int(w0&0x000F)<<16 | int(s.slotReg(i, SlotSA))
	r.lsa = int(s.slotReg(i, SlotLSA))
	r.lea = int(s.slotReg(i, SlotLEA))

	w := s.slotReg(i, SlotEG1)
	r.d2r = int(w>>11) & 0x1F
	r.d1r = int(w>>6) & 0x1F
	r.eghold = w&0x0020 != 0
	r.ar = int(w) & 0x1F

	w = s.slotReg(i, SlotEG2)
	r.lpslnk = w&0x8000 != 0
	r.krs = int(w>>11) & 0x0F
	r.dl = int(w>>6) & 0x1F
	r.rr = int(w) & 0x1F

	w = s.slotReg(i, SlotVol)
	r.stwinh = w&0x8000 != 0
	r.sdir = w&0x4000 != 0
	r.tl = int(w) & 0xFF

	w = s.slotReg(i, SlotFM)
	r.mdl = int(w>>12) & 0x0F
	r.mdxsl = int(w>>6) & 0x3F
	r.mdysl = int(w) & 0x3F

	w = s.slotReg(i, SlotPitch)
	oct := int(w>>11) & 0x0F
	if oct >= 8 {
		oct -= 16
	}
	r.oct = oct
	r.fns = int(w) & 0x3FF

	w = s.slotReg(i, SlotLFO)
	r.lfore = w&0x8000 != 0
	r.lfof = int(w>>10) & 0x1F
	r.plfows = int(w>>8) & 3
	r.plfos = int(w>>5) & 7
	r.alfows = int(w>>3) & 3
	r.alfos = int(w) & 7

	w = s.slotReg(i, SlotInSel)
	r.isel = int(w>>4) & 0x0F
	r.imxl = int(w) & 7

	w = s.slotReg(i, SlotOutSel)
	r.disdl = int(w>>13) & 7
	r.dipan = int(w>>8) & 0x1F
	r.efsdl = int(w>>5) & 7
	r.efpan = int(w) & 0x1F
	return r
}

func (s *SCSP) keyOn(i int) {
	st := &s.slots[i]
	st.active = true
	st.phase = 0
	st.dir = 1
	st.egLevel = egMaxQ
	st.egPhase = egAttack
	st.egHold = 0
	if r := s.decodeSlot(i); r.eghold {
		step := egStepQ8(s.effRate(&r, r.ar))
		if step > 0 {
			st.egHold = int32((egMaxQ + step - 1) / step)
			st.egLevel = 0
		}
	}
	st.lfoPhase = 0
}

func (s *SCSP) keyOff(i int) {
	st := &s.slots[i]
	if st.active && st.egPhase != egEnded {
		st.egPhase = egRelease
	}
}

// effRate applies key rate scaling to a 5 bit EG rate field. KRS
// 15 turns scaling off (the manual rule); otherwise the effective
// rate is twice the rate plus twice KRS plus the signed octave
// plus FNS bit 9, the formula documented from hardware by other
// SCSP implementations.
func (s *SCSP) effRate(r *slotRegs, rate int) int {
	if r.krs >= 15 {
		return 2 * rate
	}
	e := 2*rate + 2*r.krs + r.oct + (r.fns >> 9 & 1)
	if e < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if e > 63 {
		return 63
	}
	return e
}

// egStepQ8 converts an effective rate (0 to 63) to a per sample
// EG level step in Q8. Rate 0 does not move. The step doubles
// every four effective steps; effective 60 and up move the full
// range in one sample. With KRS off (effective rate twice the
// field), AR 20 therefore takes exactly 128 samples from maximum
// attenuation to full volume, and AR 31 is instant.
func egStepQ8(eff int) int32 {
	if eff <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if eff >= 60 {
		return egMaxQ
	}
	return int32(1) << uint((eff+7)/4)
}

// pitchStepQ16 is the per sample phase step in Q16 samples, from
// the manual pitch relations: the step is (1024 plus FNS) over
// 1024, times 2 to the signed octave. OCT 0 and FNS 0 give exactly
// one sample per tick.
func pitchStepQ16(r *slotRegs, plfoFactor float64) int64 {
	base := int64(1024+r.fns) << 16 >> 10
	if r.oct >= 0 {
		base <<= uint(r.oct)
	} else {
		base >>= uint(-r.oct)
	}
	if plfoFactor != 1 {
		base = int64(float64(base) * plfoFactor)
	}
	return base
}

// mdlShift is the manual MDL maximum address shift table, in
// samples: MDL 0 to 4 give no shift, then 32 doubling to 32768.
var mdlShift = [16]int64{0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768}

// sampleAt reads one waveform sample at a sample index relative
// to SA, with no interpolation.
func (s *SCSP) sampleAt(r *slotRegs, idx int64) int32 {
	switch r.ssctl {
	case 1, 2, 3:
		return 0 // noise is per output sample; 2 and 3 are silence
	}
	if r.pcm8b {
		off := r.sa + int(idx)
		if off < 0 || off >= len(s.ram) {
			return 0
		}
		return int32(int8(s.ram[off])) << 8
	}
	off := r.sa + int(idx)*2
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(s.ram) {
		return 0
	}
	return int32(int16(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(s.ram[off : off+2])))
}

// fetchSample returns the linearly interpolated sample at the
// slot's current phase, including the FM phase offset.
func (s *SCSP) fetchSample(i int, r *slotRegs) int32 {
	st := &s.slots[i]
	if r.ssctl == 1 {
		v := int32(int16(st.lfsr))
		if r.sbctl&1 != 0 {
			v = (v & -32768) | (^v & 0x7FFF)
		}
		if r.sbctl&2 != 0 {
			v ^= -32768
		}
		return v
	}
	pos := st.phase
	if shift := mdlShift[r.mdl]; shift != 0 {
		srcX := (i - (r.mdxsl & 0x1F) + 32) & 31
		srcY := (i - (r.mdysl & 0x1F) + 32) & 31
		avg := (s.slots[srcX].prevOut + s.slots[srcY].prevOut) / 2
		// avg is in sample units; avg/32768 * shift samples, Q16.
		pos += int64(avg) * shift * 2
	}
	idx := pos >> 16
	frac := int64(uint64(pos) & 0xFFFF)
	cur := s.sampleAt(r, idx)
	nxt := s.sampleAt(r, s.nextIndex(r, idx))
	v := cur + int32(int64(nxt-cur)*frac/65536)
	if r.sbctl&1 != 0 {
		v = (v & -32768) | (^v & 0x7FFF)
	}
	if r.sbctl&2 != 0 {
		v ^= -32768
	}
	return v
}

// nextIndex is the sample index after idx under the loop mode,
// used only for the interpolation neighbour.
func (s *SCSP) nextIndex(r *slotRegs, idx int64) int64 {
	if r.lpctl == 1 && idx >= int64(r.lea) {
		return int64(r.lsa)
	}
	return idx + 1
}

// advancePhase moves the phase by the pitch step and applies the
// loop mode at the LEA and LSA boundaries.
func (s *SCSP) advancePhase(i int, r *slotRegs, step int64) {
	st := &s.slots[i]
	st.phase += step * st.dir
	idx := st.phase >> 16
	lea := int64(r.lea)
	lsa := int64(r.lsa)
	switch r.lpctl {
	case 0: // loop off: stop at LEA
		if idx > lea {
			st.active = false
			st.egPhase = egEnded
			st.egLevel = egMaxQ
		}
	case 1: // forward loop: wrap to LSA at LEA
		if idx > lea {
			length := lea - lsa + 1
			if length > 0 {
				over := st.phase - (lea+1)<<16
				st.phase = (lsa << 16) + over%(length<<16)
			}
		}
	case 2: // reverse loop: play to LEA, then loop LEA down to LSA
		if st.dir > 0 && idx > lea {
			st.dir = -1
			st.phase = (lea << 16) - (st.phase - lea<<16)
		} else if st.dir < 0 && st.phase < lsa<<16 {
			st.phase = (lea << 16) - (lsa<<16 - st.phase)
		}
	case 3: // alternate loop: ping pong between LSA and LEA
		if st.dir > 0 && idx > lea {
			st.dir = -1
			st.phase = (lea << 16) - (st.phase - lea<<16)
		} else if st.dir < 0 && st.phase < lsa<<16 {
			st.dir = 1
			st.phase = (lsa << 16) + (lsa<<16 - st.phase)
		}
	}
}

// egGain converts the 10 bit attenuation level to a linear gain:
// the full range is 96 dB.
func egGain(levelQ8 int32) float64 {
	return dbGain(-96 * float64(levelQ8) / float64(egMaxQ))
}

// tlGain converts the TL bit weights from the manual table (bit 7
// is minus 48 dB down to bit 0 at minus 0.4 dB) to a linear gain.
func tlGain(tl int) float64 {
	weights := [8]float64{0.4, 0.8, 1.5, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48}
	db := 0.0
	for b := 0; b < 8; b++ {
		if tl&(1<<uint(b)) != 0 {
			db -= weights[b]
		}
	}
	return dbGain(db)
}

// tickEG advances one slot's envelope by one sample.
func (s *SCSP) tickEG(i int, r *slotRegs) {
	st := &s.slots[i]
	switch st.egPhase {
	case egAttack:
		if st.egHold > 0 {
			st.egHold--
			if st.egHold == 0 {
				st.egPhase = egDecay1
			}
			return
		}
		st.egLevel -= egStepQ8(s.effRate(r, r.ar))
		if st.egLevel <= 0 {
			st.egLevel = 0
			if r.lpslnk && (st.phase>>16) < int64(r.lsa) {
				return // hold at full until the loop start point
			}
			st.egPhase = egDecay1
		}
	case egDecay1:
		target := int32(r.dl) << 13 // DL in level units, Q8
		st.egLevel += egStepQ8(s.effRate(r, r.d1r))
		if st.egLevel >= target {
			st.egLevel = target
			st.egPhase = egDecay2
		}
		if st.egLevel >= egMaxQ {
			st.egLevel = egMaxQ
			st.egPhase = egEnded
			st.active = false
		}
	case egDecay2:
		if r.d2r == 0 {
			return // manual rule: D2R 0 maintains the level
		}
		st.egLevel += egStepQ8(s.effRate(r, r.d2r))
		if st.egLevel >= egMaxQ {
			st.egLevel = egMaxQ
			st.egPhase = egEnded
			st.active = false
		}
	case egRelease:
		st.egLevel += egStepQ8(s.effRate(r, r.rr))
		if st.egLevel >= egMaxQ {
			st.egLevel = egMaxQ
			st.egPhase = egEnded
			st.active = false
		}
	}
}

// LFO frequency table from the manual, in hundredths of a hertz.
var lfoFreqX100 = [32]int{
	17, 19, 23, 27, 34, 39, 45, 55, 68, 78, 92, 110, 139, 160,
	187, 227, 287, 331, 392, 479, 615, 718, 860, 1080, 1440,
	1720, 2150, 2870, 4310, 5740, 8610, 17230,
}

// AM depth table (maximum displacement in dB) and PM depth table
// (maximum displacement in cents) from the manual.
var (
	alfoDb    = [8]float64{0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.5, 3, 6, 12, 24}
	plfoCents = [8]float64{0, 7, 13.5, 27, 55, 112, 230, 494}
)

// lfoWave returns a waveform value: signed in minus 128 to 127
// for pitch use, or 0 to 255 for amplitude use when signed is
// false. Waveforms are 0 sawtooth, 1 square, 2 triangle, 3 noise.
func (st *slotState) lfoWave(sel int, signed bool) int {
	p := st.lfoPhase
	var v int
	switch sel {
	case 0: // sawtooth
		v = int(p >> 24)
	case 1: // square
		if p&(1<<31) != 0 {
			v = 255
		}
	case 2: // triangle
		if p&(1<<31) != 0 {
			v = 255 - int(p>>23&0xFF)
		} else {
			v = int(p >> 23 & 0xFF)
		}
	default: // noise
		v = int(st.lfsr>>8) & 0xFF
	}
	if signed {
		return v - 128
	}
	return v
}

// renderSlots renders every active slot for this tick, accumulates
// the direct mix into mixL and mixR, and returns the 16 DSP input
// mix values (MIXS) built from ISEL and IMXL.
func (s *SCSP) renderSlots(mixL, mixR *int64) [16]int32 {
	var mixs [16]int32
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		st := &s.slots[i]
		r := s.decodeSlot(i)

		if r.lfore {
			st.lfoPhase = 0
		} else {
			step := uint64(lfoFreqX100[r.lfof]) << 32 / (sampleRate * 100)
			st.lfoPhase += uint32(step)
		}
		st.lfsr ^= st.lfsr << 13
		st.lfsr ^= st.lfsr >> 17
		st.lfsr ^= st.lfsr << 5

		if !st.active {
			st.prevOut = 0
			st.out = 0
			continue
		}

		plfo := 1.0
		if r.plfos != 0 {
			cents := float64(st.lfoWave(r.plfows, true)) / 128 * plfoCents[r.plfos]
			plfo = math.Pow(2, cents/1200)
		}
		raw := s.fetchSample(i, &r)
		s.tickEG(i, &r)

		var out int32
		if r.sdir {
			out = raw
		} else {
			g := egGain(st.egLevel) * tlGain(r.tl)
			if r.alfos != 0 {
				w := float64(st.lfoWave(r.alfows, false)) / 255
				g *= dbGain(-w * alfoDb[r.alfos])
			}
			out = int32(float64(raw) * g)
		}
		st.out = out

		if dg := sendGain(r.disdl); dg != 0 && out != 0 {
			gl, gr := panGains(r.dipan)
			*mixL += int64(float64(out) * dg * gl)
			*mixR += int64(float64(out) * dg * gr)
		}
		if ig := sendGain(r.imxl); ig != 0 && out != 0 {
			mixs[r.isel] += int32(float64(out) * ig)
		}
		if !r.stwinh && len(s.regs) >= RegStackB+64 {
			v := uint16(int16(out))
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(s.regs[RegStackA+i*2:RegStackA+i*2+2], v)
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(s.regs[RegStackB+i*2:RegStackB+i*2+2], v)
		}

		s.advancePhase(i, &r, pitchStepQ16(&r, plfo))
	}
	for i := range s.slots {
		s.slots[i].prevOut = s.slots[i].out
	}
	return mixs
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scsp/state.go ====================

package scsp

import (
	"encoding/binary"
)

// Serialized layout, version 1, big endian. Sound RAM and the
// register page are NOT included; the system serializes those
// separately. The pending audio buffer is not included either;
// callers drain AudioBuffer before saving for a bit exact
// continuation.
//
//	bytes 0 to 3: magic "SCSP"
//	byte 4: version (1)
//	byte 5: flags: bit 0 sound on
//	bytes 6 to 13: sample phase accumulator (SH-2 cycle units)
//	bytes 14 to 22: timers: per timer the preset, counter and
//	  prescaler phase, 3 bytes each
//	bytes 23 to 24: sound CPU pending mask
//	bytes 25 to 26: main CPU pending mask
//	bytes 27 to 28: main bits already signalled
//	byte 29: DMA flags: bit 0 active, bit 1 register to RAM,
//	  bit 2 DGATE
//	bytes 30 to 33: DMA words remaining
//	bytes 34 to 37: DMA RAM word address
//	bytes 38 to 41: DMA register word address
//	then 32 slot records of 32 bytes each:
//	  phase (8), EG level Q8 (4), EGHOLD ticks left (4),
//	  LFO phase (4), noise LFSR (4), previous output (4),
//	  EG phase (1), active (1), direction sign (1), spare (1)
//	then the 88 byte m68ec000 state
//	then the DSP record:
//	  accumulator (4), memory phase (4), sample count (8),
//	  TEMP base (4), last memory read (4), TEMP 128 words of
//	  4 bytes, MEMS 32, MIXS 16, EFREG 16, EXTS 2
//	then the CD queue: a 4 byte count followed by that many
//	  big endian int16 samples
const stateVersion = 1

const (
	stateHeader  = 42
	slotRecSize  = 32
	dspFixedSize = 4 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 4 + 128*4 + 32*4 + 16*4 + 16*4 + 2*4
	// SerializeBaseSize is the serialized size with an empty CD
	// queue.
	SerializeBaseSize = stateHeader + 32*slotRecSize + 88 + dspFixedSize + 4
)

// Serialize returns the chip state in the layout above.
func (s *SCSP) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeBaseSize+len(s.cdQueue)*2)
	copy(out[0:4], "SCSP")
	out[4] = stateVersion
	if s.on {
		out[5] |= 1
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[6:14], uint64(s.acc))
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		out[14+i*3] = s.timers[i].preset
		out[15+i*3] = s.timers[i].counter
		out[16+i*3] = byte(s.timers[i].phase)
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[23:25], s.sciPend)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[25:27], s.mciPend)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[27:29], s.mainSent)
	if s.dma.active {
		out[29] |= 1
	}
	if s.dma.dirRegToRAM {
		out[29] |= 2
	}
	if s.dma.gate {
		out[29] |= 4
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[30:34], uint32(s.dma.remaining))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[34:38], s.dma.ramWord)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[38:42], s.dma.regWord)

	off := stateHeader
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		st := &s.slots[i]
		rec := out[off : off+slotRecSize]
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(rec[0:8], uint64(st.phase))
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[8:12], uint32(st.egLevel))
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[12:16], uint32(st.egHold))
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[16:20], st.lfoPhase)
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[20:24], st.lfsr)
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(rec[24:28], uint32(st.prevOut))
		rec[28] = byte(st.egPhase)
		if st.active {
			rec[29] = 1
		}
		if st.dir < 0 {
			rec[30] = 1
		}
		off += slotRecSize
	}
	copy(out[off:off+88], s.cpu.Serialize())
	off += 88

	d := &s.dsp
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:off+4], uint32(d.acc))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off+4:off+8], d.memPhase)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[off+8:off+16], d.samples)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off+16:off+20], uint32(d.tempBase))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off+20:off+24], uint32(d.memrd))
	p := off + 24
	put32s := func(vals []int32) {
		for _, v := range vals {
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[p:p+4], uint32(v))
			p += 4
		}
	}
	put32s(d.temp[:])
	put32s(d.mems[:])
	put32s(d.mixs[:])
	put32s(d.efreg[:])
	put32s(d.exts[:])
	off = p

	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:off+4], uint32(len(s.cdQueue)))
	for i, v := range s.cdQueue {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[off+4+i*2:off+6+i*2], uint16(v))
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
func (s *SCSP) Deserialize(b []byte) error {
	if len(b) < SerializeBaseSize || string(b[0:4]) != "SCSP" || b[4] != stateVersion {
		return errState
	}
	s.on = b[5]&1 != 0
	s.acc = int64(binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[6:14]))
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		s.timers[i].preset = b[14+i*3]
		s.timers[i].counter = b[15+i*3]
		s.timers[i].phase = int(b[16+i*3])
	}
	s.sciPend = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[23:25])
	s.mciPend = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[25:27])
	s.mainSent = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[27:29])
	s.dma.active = b[29]&1 != 0
	s.dma.dirRegToRAM = b[29]&2 != 0
	s.dma.gate = b[29]&4 != 0
	s.dma.remaining = int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[30:34]))
	s.dma.ramWord = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[34:38])
	s.dma.regWord = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[38:42])

	off := stateHeader
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		st := &s.slots[i]
		rec := b[off : off+slotRecSize]
		st.phase = int64(binary.BigEndian.Uint64(rec[0:8]))
		st.egLevel = int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(rec[8:12]))
		st.egHold = int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(rec[12:16]))
		st.lfoPhase = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(rec[16:20])
		st.lfsr = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(rec[20:24])
		st.prevOut = int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(rec[24:28]))
		st.out = st.prevOut
		st.egPhase = int(rec[28])
		st.active = rec[29] != 0
		st.dir = 1
		if rec[30] != 0 {
			st.dir = -1
		}
		off += slotRecSize
	}
	if err := s.cpu.Deserialize(b[off : off+88]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += 88

	d := &s.dsp
	d.acc = int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[off : off+4]))
	d.memPhase = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[off+4 : off+8])
	d.samples = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[off+8 : off+16])
	d.tempBase = int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[off+16:off+20])) & 127
	d.memrd = int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[off+20 : off+24]))
	p := off + 24
	get32s := func(vals []int32) {
		for i := range vals {
			vals[i] = int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[p : p+4]))
			p += 4
		}
	}
	get32s(d.temp[:])
	get32s(d.mems[:])
	get32s(d.mixs[:])
	get32s(d.efreg[:])
	get32s(d.exts[:])
	off = p

	n := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[off : off+4]))
	if len(b) != off+4+n*2 {
		return errState
	}
	s.cdQueue = make([]int16, n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		s.cdQueue[i] = int16(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[off+4+i*2 : off+6+i*2]))
	}
	s.audio = nil
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scu/dma.go ====================

package scu

// SCU DMA channels 0, 1, and 2.
//
// Register layout on the page, per the SCU manual: each
// channel owns a 0x20 byte block starting at 0x00, 0x20,
// and 0x40. Within a block:
//
//	+0x00 read address (DxR, 27 bits)
//	+0x04 write address (DxW, 27 bits)
//	+0x08 transfer byte count (DxC; 20 bits on channel 0,
//	      12 bits on channels 1 and 2)
//	+0x0C address add value (DxAD)
//	+0x10 enable (DxEN)
//	+0x14 mode, address update, start factor (DxMD)
//
// The DMA force stop register DSTP is at 0x60 (bit 0).
// The DMA status register DSTA is at 0x7C. The task
// brief transposed those two offsets; the manual is
// unambiguous (DSTP 25FE0060, DSTA 25FE007C), so the
// manual wins, and a stop write to 0x7C is also honored
// as an alias so either reading stops DMA.
//
// DxEN: this core enables a channel when bit 0 or bit 8
// of DxEN is set. The manual puts the enable flag at
// bit 8 and a separate GO flag at bit 0 (the GO flag is
// the trigger for start factor 7); the task brief puts
// the enable at bit 0. Accepting either bit keeps both
// readings working: software sets one of them, Poll
// sees the 0 to 1 edge, and factor 7 channels run.
//
// DxMD fields, per the manual: bit 24 mode (0 direct,
// 1 indirect), bit 16 read address update (0 save,
// 1 update), bit 8 write address update, bits 2..0
// start factor select. The manual has no transfer unit
// field in DxMD: the count in DxC is always a byte
// count. The copy below moves the bulk in longword
// units through Mem and the tail in bytes, which is
// observationally identical to a byte copy on memory.
//
// DxAD fields, per the manual: bit 8 is the read add
// code (0 adds nothing, 1 adds 4 per unit) and bits 2..0
// are the write add code (0 adds nothing, then 2, 4, 8,
// 16, 32, 64, 128 per halfword cycle, which totals 4
// per longword on this abstract bus). This core applies
// the add codes as advance or hold: a code of 0 holds
// the address fixed for the whole transfer (the FIFO
// style access the code exists for, aimed at A-Bus CS2
// devices), and any nonzero code advances the address
// contiguously, one unit per unit of data. The exact
// per cycle add amount is a bus width artifact that is
// not observable through the Mem interface.
//
// Direct mode count: the masked count from DxC, with a
// count of 0 meaning the full width (1 MiB on channel
// 0, 4 KiB on channels 1 and 2), per the manual's
// register widths. At the end of a direct transfer the
// address registers hold the next addresses when the
// matching update bit is set, and keep the values they
// were set with when it is clear (save mode).
//
// Indirect mode: the parameters come from a table in
// memory pointed to by DxW. Each entry is three
// longwords: read address, write address, and a count
// word whose bit 31 is the end flag and whose low 20
// bits are the byte count (0 means 1 MiB). Entries are
// 12 bytes apart. The transfer runs entries in order
// until one with the end flag set has run. When the
// write address update bit is set, DxW is left pointing
// past the last entry; in save mode it is unchanged.
// A safety cap of 4096 entries guards against an
// unterminated table.
//
// Prohibited region: SCU DMA may not touch the SCU
// register page itself. A transfer whose source or
// destination range intersects the page window
// (0x05FE0000..0x05FE00FF, or its cache through alias
// at 0x25FE0000) is skipped entirely, counted by
// IllegalDMA, and raises no end interrupt. This core's
// IST map has no DMA illegal source (see scu.go), so
// the count and the missing end interrupt are the
// status. Every other transfer rides the machine bus
// through the Mem interface; the manual's A-Bus and
// B-Bus same bus rules cannot be expressed through Mem
// and are not modeled.
//
// Priority: when several channels are due in one Poll,
// channel 0 runs first, then 1, then 2, as the brief
// specifies. (The manual calls channel 2 the highest
// priority for bus arbitration; with atomic transfers
// the only observable effect of order is which transfer
// lands last on overlapping ranges, and the brief pins
// channel 0 first.)
//
// Transfers run atomically inside Poll, so DSTA busy,
// standby, and access flags are never observable set:
// Poll leaves DSTA at 0 (idle) when it returns.

// DMA start factor numbers, per the start factor table
// in the manual (DxMD bits 2..0 and the StartFactor
// argument). Factor 7 is the immediate factor: the
// channel runs when its enable is set.
const (
	FactorVBlankIn  = 0
	FactorVBlankOut = 1
	FactorHBlankIn  = 2
	FactorTimer0    = 3
	FactorTimer1    = 4
	FactorSoundReq  = 5
	FactorSpriteEnd = 6
	FactorImmediate = 7
)

// Register page offsets for the DMA block as a whole.
const (
	offDSTP = 0x60
	offDSTA = 0x7C
)

// Per channel register offsets within a channel block.
const (
	chR  = 0x00
	chW  = 0x04
	chC  = 0x08
	chAD = 0x0C
	chEN = 0x10
	chMD = 0x14
)

// maxIndirectEntries caps one indirect mode run.
const maxIndirectEntries = 4096

// Mem is the machine bus view the SCU DMA and the DSP
// DMA transfer through. The bus package satisfies it.
type Mem interface {
	Read8(uint32) uint8
	Read16(uint32) uint16
	Read32(uint32) uint32
	Write8(uint32, uint8)
	Write16(uint32, uint16)
	Write32(uint32, uint32)
}

// AttachMem attaches the bus the DMA transfers ride.
// Without a Mem, due transfers are skipped silently.
func (s *SCU) AttachMem(m Mem) { s.mem = m }

// StartFactor latches a DMA start factor event for the
// next Poll. Factors are the Factor constants above.
// Out of range factors are ignored. A latched factor is
// a pulse: Poll consumes all latches whether or not a
// channel used them.
func (s *SCU) StartFactor(f int) {
	if f < 0 || f > 7 {
		return
	}
	s.latchedFactors |= 1 << uint(f)
}

// IllegalDMA returns how many DMA transfers have been
// skipped for touching the SCU register page window.
func (s *SCU) IllegalDMA() uint32 { return s.illegalDMA }

// Poll runs one scanline of SCU work: it syncs the DSP
// load ports from the page, honors DMA stop writes,
// runs every DMA channel that is due, and runs the DSP
// while its execute flag is set. The system calls Poll
// once per scanline.
func (s *SCU) Poll() {
	s.syncDSPPorts()
	s.pollDMA()
	s.pollDSP()
}

// chanBase returns the page offset of a channel block.
func chanBase(ch int) int { return ch * 0x20 }

// pollDMA handles stop writes, enable edges, latched
// factors, and due transfers for all three channels.
func (s *SCU) pollDMA() {
	// Force stop: DSTP at 0x60 bit 0, with the brief's
	// transposed offset 0x7C honored as an alias. A stop
	// clears every channel enable on the page and drops
	// latched factors. The DSTP word is consumed so a
	// later enable is not stopped again.
	stop := s.word(offDSTP)&1 != 0
	if s.word(offDSTA)&1 != 0 {
		stop = true
	}
	if stop {
		for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
			s.setWord(chanBase(ch)+chEN, 0)
			s.lastEnabled[ch] = false
		}
		s.latchedFactors = 0
	}
	s.setWord(offDSTP, 0)

	latched := s.latchedFactors
	s.latchedFactors = 0

	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		base := chanBase(ch)
		en := s.word(base + chEN)
		enabled := en&0x101 != 0
		edge := enabled && !s.lastEnabled[ch]
		s.lastEnabled[ch] = enabled
		if !enabled {
			continue
		}
		md := s.word(base + chMD)
		factor := int(md & 7)
		due := false
		if factor == FactorImmediate {
			due = edge || latched&(1<<uint(FactorImmediate)) != 0
		} else {
			due = latched&(1<<uint(factor)) != 0
		}
		if due {
			s.runDMAChannel(ch)
		}
	}
	// Transfers are atomic, so the status reads idle.
	s.setWord(offDSTA, 0)
}

// touchesSCUPage reports whether the byte range starting
// at addr intersects the SCU register page window.
func touchesSCUPage(addr uint32, count int) bool {
	if count <= 0 {
		return false
	}
	lo := uint64(addr)
	hi := lo + uint64(count) - 1
	for _, base := range []uint64{0x05FE0000, 0x25FE0000} {
		if lo <= base+0xFF && hi >= base {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// copyBytes moves count bytes from src to dst through
// Mem. When an advance flag is clear the matching
// address stays fixed for every byte (add code 0).
func (s *SCU) copyBytes(src, dst uint32, count int, srcAdv, dstAdv bool) (endSrc, endDst uint32) {
	if srcAdv && dstAdv {
		n := count
		for n >= 4 && src&3 == 0 && dst&3 == 0 {
			s.mem.Write32(dst, s.mem.Read32(src))
			src += 4
			dst += 4
			n -= 4
		}
		for ; n > 0; n-- {
			s.mem.Write8(dst, s.mem.Read8(src))
			src++
			dst++
		}
		return src, dst
	}
	for i := 0; i < count; i++ {
		s.mem.Write8(dst, s.mem.Read8(src))
		if srcAdv {
			src++
		}
		if dstAdv {
			dst++
		}
	}
	return src, dst
}

// runDMAChannel executes one channel transfer and
// raises its end interrupt source.
func (s *SCU) runDMAChannel(ch int) {
	if s.mem == nil {
		return
	}
	base := chanBase(ch)
	src := s.word(base + chR)
	dst := s.word(base + chW)
	md := s.word(base + chMD)
	ad := s.word(base + chAD)
	srcAdv := ad&(1<<8) != 0
	dstAdv := ad&7 != 0
	rup := md&(1<<16) != 0
	wup := md&(1<<8) != 0
	endBit := []int{IntDMA0End, IntDMA1End, IntDMA2End}[ch]

	if md&(1<<24) != 0 {
		// Indirect mode: parameters from the table at DxW.
		table := dst
		for i := 0; i < maxIndirectEntries; i++ {
			r := s.mem.Read32(table)
			w := s.mem.Read32(table + 4)
			cw := s.mem.Read32(table + 8)
			count := int(cw & 0xFFFFF)
			if count == 0 {
				count = 1 << 20
			}
			if touchesSCUPage(r, count) || touchesSCUPage(w, count) {
				s.illegalDMA++
			} else {
				s.copyBytes(r, w, count, srcAdv, dstAdv)
			}
			table += 12
			if cw&(1<<31) != 0 {
				break
			}
		}
		if wup {
			s.setWord(base+chW, table&0x07FFFFFF)
		}
		s.Raise(endBit)
		return
	}

	// Direct mode.
	count := int(s.word(base + chC))
	if ch == 0 {
		count &= 0xFFFFF
		if count == 0 {
			count = 1 << 20
		}
	} else {
		count &= 0xFFF
		if count == 0 {
			count = 1 << 12
		}
	}
	if touchesSCUPage(src, count) || touchesSCUPage(dst, count) {
		s.illegalDMA++
		return
	}
	endSrc, endDst := s.copyBytes(src, dst, count, srcAdv, dstAdv)
	if rup {
		s.setWord(base+chR, endSrc&0x07FFFFFF)
	}
	if wup {
		s.setWord(base+chW, endDst&0x07FFFFFF)
	}
	s.Raise(endBit)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scu/dsp.go ====================

package scu

// SCU DSP.
//
// Memories, held in the SCU struct (not on the page):
// program RAM is 256 words of 32 bits; data RAM is four
// banks of 64 words of 32 bits.
//
// Control ports on the page, per the manual:
//
//	0x80 DSP program control port (the brief's PPAF):
//	     bits 7..0 program RAM address, bit 15 LE (load
//	     the address into the program counter), bit 16
//	     EX (program execute control), bit 17 ES (step
//	     execute, not modeled beyond storage), bit 18 E
//	     (program end flag, set by ENDI), bit 19 V,
//	     bit 20 C, bit 21 Z, bit 22 S, bit 23 T0 (D0 bus
//	     DMA in progress), bit 25 EP, bit 26 PR.
//	0x84 DSP program RAM data port (the brief's PPAC):
//	     write only. Writing a word stores it in program
//	     RAM at the address in the control port, and the
//	     address counts up by one.
//	0x88 DSP data RAM address port (the brief's PDAC):
//	     bits 7..6 select the data RAM bank, bits 5..0
//	     the word address in the bank.
//	0x8C DSP data RAM data port (the brief's transfer
//	     register): read and write. Accessing it moves
//	     one word between the CPU and the selected data
//	     RAM word, and the address counts up by one.
//
// Load mechanism in this passive page model: the bus
// page has no write strobes, so the ports are consumed
// by syncDSPPorts at the start of Poll and RunDSP.
// Software writes a port, then a Poll (in the machine,
// the per scanline Poll) consumes it. The program data
// port is cleared to zero after it is consumed, so
// consecutive writes of the same nonzero word are each
// seen; a written word of zero is indistinguishable
// from no write when the port already reads zero, and
// program RAM already reads zero there in the common
// case, which is the documented limit of this model.
// The data data port presents the selected RAM word
// after the address port changes (a read setup), and a
// changed data port value with no address change is a
// write, which stores the word and counts the address
// up. Direct accessors (DSPWriteProgram and friends)
// are provided for tests and tooling that do not want
// to drive the ports.
//
// Execution: when EX is set, Poll runs the DSP with a
// large step budget, and RunDSP runs it on demand.
// Execution starts at the program RAM address in the
// control port when EX rises. The END command stops
// execution and clears EX. ENDI also sets the E flag in
// the control port and raises IntDSPEnd. There are no
// goroutines; execution is deterministic and atomic to
// the caller.
//
// Instruction encoding, per chapter 4 of the manual.
// The top bits select the class:
//
//	0b00 operation command (parallel ALU, X bus, Y bus,
//	     and D1 bus fields in one word)
//	0b10 load immediate (MVI)
//	0b1100 DMA command
//	0b1101 jump command
//	0b1110 loop bottom command (BTM, LPS)
//	0b1111 end command (END, ENDI)
//
// Operation command fields: ALU bits 29..26, X bus bits
// 25..20 (opcode bits 25..23, source bits 22..20), Y
// bus bits 19..14 (opcode bits 19..17, source bits
// 16..14), D1 bus bits 13..0. A source select of the
// form 1bb picks data RAM bank bb and increments its CT
// pointer after the transfer (the MC form); 0bb picks
// the bank without incrementing (the M form).
//
// ALU opcodes (bits 29..26): 0 NOP, 1 AND, 2 OR, 3 XOR,
// 4 ADD, 5 SUB, 6 AD2 (48 bit add of A and P), 8 SR
// (arithmetic shift right), 9 RR (rotate right), 10 SL
// (shift left), 11 RL (rotate left), 14 RR8 (rotate
// right 8), 15 RL8 (rotate left 8). Codes 7, 12, and 13
// are not assigned in the manual and act as NOP here.
// Logic, add, and shift results are written to the
// accumulator (the ALU output) in the same step, so a
// parallel MOV ALU, A in the Y field is a copy of the
// same result and never double applies. Flags S, Z, C,
// and V follow the manual: S is the result sign, Z is
// result zero, C is the carry out (for SUB, C is the
// carry out of the subtraction, so 1 means no borrow),
// and V is signed overflow. For AD2 the result and
// flags are 48 bit wide.
//
// X bus opcodes (bits 25..23): 0 NOP, 4 MOV [s], X
// (data RAM word into RX), 2 MOV MUL, P (the signed
// product RX times RY, computed from the RX and RY
// values at the start of the instruction, into P:
// PH takes the high 16 bits of the 48 bit product and
// PL the low 32), 3 MOV [s], P (data RAM word into PL,
// with PH set by sign extension of PL).
//
// Y bus opcodes (bits 19..17): 0 NOP, 4 MOV [s], Y
// (data RAM word into RY), 1 CLR A (A cleared to 0),
// 2 MOV ALU, A (the ALU result of this instruction
// into A), 3 MOV [s], A (data RAM word into ACL, with
// ACH set by sign extension).
//
// D1 bus field (bits 13..0): bits 13..12 select the
// move kind: 0 NOP, 1 MOV SImm, [d] (sign extended 8
// bit immediate in bits 7..0 into the destination in
// bits 11..8), 3 MOV [s], [d] (the source in bits 3..0
// into the destination in bits 11..8; kind 2 is not
// assigned). Destination codes: 0..3 data RAM banks
// 0..3 (written at the bank CT pointer, which then
// increments), 4 RX, 5 PL (PH follows by sign
// extension), 6 RA0, 7 WA0, 8 LOP, 9 TOP, 10..13
// CT0..CT3, 14 PC (MVI only), 15 unused. Source codes
// for MOV [s], [d]: 0..3 data RAM banks (no increment),
// 4..7 data RAM banks (with increment), 8 ACL, 9 ACH
// (sign extended from 16 bits).
//
// MVI format: bits 31..30 are 10, the destination code
// is bits 29..26, bit 25 is 0 for the unconditional
// form (immediate is the signed 25 bit value in bits
// 24..0) and 1 for the conditional form (bit 24 is the
// condition polarity, 1 means the flag must be set;
// bits 23..19 are the condition code: 1 Z, 2 S, 3 Z or
// S, 4 C, 8 T0; the immediate is the signed 19 bit
// value in bits 18..0). Writing PC with MVI stores the
// return address (the address after the MVI) in TOP
// first, which is the manual's subroutine call form.
//
// Jump format: bits 31..28 are 1101. The unconditional
// form has bits 27..21 clear. Conditional forms set
// bit 27, put the polarity in bit 26 (1 means the flag
// must be set), and the condition code in bits 25..21
// (same codes as MVI). The target is the 8 bit program
// address in bits 7..0. The manual's prefetch delay
// (the instruction after a taken jump executes once)
// is not modeled: a taken jump takes effect at once.
//
// Loop bottom format: bits 31..28 are 1110. Bit 27
// clear is BTM: when LOP is nonzero, LOP decrements
// and the program counter returns to TOP; at LOP zero
// execution falls through. Bit 27 set is LPS: the next
// instruction repeats until LOP reaches zero, so it
// executes LOP plus one times in total.
//
// DMA command format: bits 31..28 are 1100. Bit 27 is
// the count mode: 0 takes the transfer count from the
// 8 bit immediate in bits 7..0, 1 takes it from a data
// RAM word selected by bits 2..0 (a source select as
// above). Bits 17..15 are the external address add
// code (0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 for codes 0..7, in
// word units). Bit 14 is the hold flag: with hold set,
// RA0 or WA0 and the transfer counter keep their start
// values after the transfer. Bit 12 is the direction:
// 0 moves data from the D0 bus (external memory,
// starting at the byte address RA0 times 4) into DSP
// RAM, 1 moves data from DSP RAM to the D0 bus
// (starting at WA0 times 4). Bits 10..8 select the DSP
// RAM: 0..3 are data RAM banks (the transfer starts at
// the bank CT pointer, which advances one per word),
// and 4 selects program RAM (the transfer starts at an
// internal program DMA pointer that starts at 0 and
// advances one per word). RA0 and WA0 hold word
// addresses (the manual stores the byte address shifted
// right 2), and TN0 holds the count while a transfer
// runs; transfers here are atomic, so TN0 reads 0 after
// a non hold transfer and keeps the count after a hold
// transfer. A count of 0 transfers nothing. Without an
// attached Mem a DMA command does nothing.
//
// Registers: RX and RY are the multiplier inputs (the
// X and Y of the brief), P is the 48 bit product
// register (PH and PL views), A is the 48 bit
// accumulator (ACH and ACL views), CT0..CT3 are the
// 6 bit data RAM pointers, RA0 and WA0 are the external
// DMA address registers, and PC, TOP, and LOP are the
// program counter, loop top, and 12 bit loop counter.

// DSP control port offsets on the page.
const (
	offPPAF = 0x80
	offPPD  = 0x84
	offPDA  = 0x88
	offPDD  = 0x8C
)

// PPAF bit numbers.
const (
	ppafLE = 15
	ppafEX = 16
	ppafE  = 18
	ppafV  = 19
	ppafC  = 20
	ppafZ  = 21
	ppafS  = 22
	ppafT0 = 23
)

// pollDSPBudget is the step budget Poll gives the DSP.
// Programs that do not end within the budget stay
// running and continue on the next Poll.
const pollDSPBudget = 100000

// dspState is the off page DSP state.
type dspState struct {
	prog [256]uint32
	data [4][64]uint32

	rx, ry uint32
	p      uint64 // 48 bit product: PH in bits 47..32, PL in 31..0
	acc    uint64 // 48 bit accumulator: ACH in bits 47..32, ACL in 31..0
	ct     [4]uint8
	ra0    uint32
	wa0    uint32
	tn0    uint32
	pc     uint8
	top    uint8
	lop    uint16 // 12 bit

	flagS, flagZ, flagC, flagV, flagT0 bool
	endFlag                            bool

	running bool
	lastEX  bool

	// LPS repeat state: the address of the instruction
	// being repeated, valid while repeatActive is set.
	repeatAddr   uint8
	repeatActive bool
	lpsPending   bool

	// Program RAM DMA pointer for DMA commands that
	// select program RAM.
	dmaProgAddr uint32

	// Data port pointer selected by the address port:
	// bits 7..6 bank, bits 5..0 word address.
	dataPtr uint8
}

// DSPProgram returns the program RAM word at addr.
func (s *SCU) DSPProgram(addr int) uint32 {
	if addr < 0 || addr >= 256 {
		return 0
	}
	return s.dsp.prog[addr]
}

// DSPWriteProgram stores a word in program RAM directly,
// bypassing the load ports.
func (s *SCU) DSPWriteProgram(addr int, v uint32) {
	if addr < 0 || addr >= 256 {
		return
	}
	s.dsp.prog[addr] = v
}

// DSPData returns the data RAM word in a bank.
func (s *SCU) DSPData(bank, addr int) uint32 {
	if bank < 0 || bank >= 4 || addr < 0 || addr >= 64 {
		return 0
	}
	return s.dsp.data[bank][addr]
}

// DSPWriteData stores a word in data RAM directly,
// bypassing the load ports.
func (s *SCU) DSPWriteData(bank, addr int, v uint32) {
	if bank < 0 || bank >= 4 || addr < 0 || addr >= 64 {
		return
	}
	s.dsp.data[bank][addr] = v
}

// DSPAccumulator returns the 48 bit accumulator.
func (s *SCU) DSPAccumulator() uint64 { return s.dsp.acc & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF }

// DSPProduct returns the 48 bit product register.
func (s *SCU) DSPProduct() uint64 { return s.dsp.p & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF }

// DSPRunning reports whether the DSP is executing.
func (s *SCU) DSPRunning() bool { return s.dsp.running }

// syncDSPPorts consumes the DSP load ports on the page
// and the control port strobes. See the package comment
// at the top of this file for the load model.
func (s *SCU) syncDSPPorts() {
	d := &s.dsp
	ppaf := s.word(offPPAF)

	// Program data port: a nonzero value that differs
	// from the last consumed value (or any value when
	// the port holds an unconsumed write) is a load.
	if v := s.word(offPPD); v != 0 && (!s.progPortValid || v != s.lastProgPort) {
		addr := uint8(ppaf & 0xFF)
		d.prog[addr] = v
		// The control port address counts up by one.
		ppaf = (ppaf &^ 0xFF) | uint32(addr+1)
		s.setWord(offPPAF, ppaf)
		s.lastProgPort = v
		s.progPortValid = true
		s.setWord(offPPD, 0)
	}

	// Data address port: a change selects a new data
	// RAM word and presents it on the data port.
	addrWord := s.word(offPDA)
	dataWord := s.word(offPDD)
	if addrWord != s.lastDataAddr {
		d.dataPtr = uint8(addrWord & 0xFF)
		s.lastDataAddr = addrWord
		if dataWord == s.lastDataData {
			v := d.data[d.dataPtr>>6][d.dataPtr&0x3F]
			s.setWord(offPDD, v)
			s.lastDataData = v
			dataWord = v
		}
	}
	// Data data port: a changed value is a write to the
	// selected word; the address counts up by one.
	if dataWord != s.lastDataData {
		d.data[d.dataPtr>>6][d.dataPtr&0x3F] = dataWord
		s.lastDataData = dataWord
		d.dataPtr = (d.dataPtr & 0xC0) | ((d.dataPtr + 1) & 0x3F)
		s.setWord(offPDA, uint32(d.dataPtr))
		s.lastDataAddr = uint32(d.dataPtr)
	}

	// Control port strobes.
	ppaf = s.word(offPPAF)
	if ppaf&(1<<ppafLE) != 0 && !d.running {
		d.pc = uint8(ppaf & 0xFF)
		s.setWord(offPPAF, ppaf&^(1<<ppafLE))
		ppaf &^= 1 << ppafLE
	}
	ex := ppaf&(1<<ppafEX) != 0
	if ex && !d.lastEX {
		d.pc = uint8(ppaf & 0xFF)
		d.endFlag = false
		d.running = true
	}
	if !ex {
		d.running = false
	}
	d.lastEX = ex
	s.writeDSPFlags()
}

// writeDSPFlags mirrors the DSP flags into the PPAF
// status bits on the page.
func (s *SCU) writeDSPFlags() {
	d := &s.dsp
	ppaf := s.word(offPPAF)
	ppaf &^= 0x3F << 18
	if d.endFlag {
		ppaf |= 1 << ppafE
	}
	if d.flagV {
		ppaf |= 1 << ppafV
	}
	if d.flagC {
		ppaf |= 1 << ppafC
	}
	if d.flagZ {
		ppaf |= 1 << ppafZ
	}
	if d.flagS {
		ppaf |= 1 << ppafS
	}
	if d.flagT0 {
		ppaf |= 1 << ppafT0
	}
	s.setWord(offPPAF, ppaf)
}

// pollDSP runs the DSP from Poll while EX is set.
func (s *SCU) pollDSP() {
	if s.dsp.running {
		s.runDSPSteps(pollDSPBudget)
	}
}

// RunDSP runs the DSP for at most maxSteps instructions
// and returns how many instructions executed. It starts
// from the current program counter; when the control
// port EX flag has just been set, the start address is
// the control port address, as in Poll. Execution stops
// early at an END or ENDI command. A nonpositive
// maxSteps runs nothing.
func (s *SCU) RunDSP(maxSteps int) int {
	s.syncDSPPorts()
	if maxSteps <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if !s.dsp.running {
		// A direct RunDSP call is an execution request
		// from the current program counter even when EX
		// was not raised through the page. If the budget
		// runs out before an END command, the DSP stays
		// running so Poll or a later RunDSP continues
		// where this call stopped.
		s.dsp.running = true
	}
	return s.runDSPSteps(maxSteps)
}

// runDSPSteps executes up to maxSteps instructions.
func (s *SCU) runDSPSteps(maxSteps int) int {
	n := 0
	for n < maxSteps && s.dsp.running {
		s.stepDSP()
		n++
	}
	s.writeDSPFlags()
	return n
}

// condTrue evaluates a condition code with a polarity
// against the DSP flags. Condition codes: 1 Z, 2 S,
// 3 Z or S, 4 C, 8 T0. Unknown codes are false.
func (s *SCU) condTrue(code uint32, polarity bool) bool {
	d := &s.dsp
	var v bool
	switch code {
	case 1:
		v = d.flagZ
	case 2:
		v = d.flagS
	case 3:
		v = d.flagZ || d.flagS
	case 4:
		v = d.flagC
	case 8:
		v = d.flagT0
	default:
		return false
	}
	if polarity {
		return v
	}
	return !v
}

// signExtend returns v sign extended from the given
// bit width.
func signExtend(v uint32, bits uint) int32 {
	shift := 32 - bits
	return int32(v<<shift) >> shift
}

// stepDSP executes one instruction at the program
// counter.
func (s *SCU) stepDSP() {
	d := &s.dsp
	instr := d.prog[d.pc]
	curPC := d.pc
	d.pc++

	// LPS: this instruction is the repeated one. The
	// repeat bookkeeping runs after it executes.
	repeating := d.lpsPending || (d.repeatActive && curPC == d.repeatAddr)
	if d.lpsPending {
		d.repeatAddr = curPC
		d.repeatActive = true
		d.lpsPending = false
	}

	jumped := false
	switch {
	case instr>>30 == 0:
		s.execOperation(instr)
	case instr>>30 == 2:
		jumped = s.execMVI(instr)
	case instr>>28 == 0xC:
		s.execDSPDMA(instr)
	case instr>>28 == 0xD:
		if instr&(1<<27) == 0 || s.condTrue((instr>>21)&0x1F, instr&(1<<26) != 0) {
			d.pc = uint8(instr & 0xFF)
			jumped = true
		}
	case instr>>28 == 0xE:
		if instr&(1<<27) != 0 {
			// LPS: repeat the next instruction.
			d.lpsPending = true
		} else {
			// BTM.
			if d.lop > 0 {
				d.lop--
				d.pc = d.top
				jumped = true
			}
		}
	case instr>>28 == 0xF:
		d.running = false
		ppaf := s.word(offPPAF)
		s.setWord(offPPAF, ppaf&^(1<<ppafEX))
		d.lastEX = false
		if instr&(1<<27) != 0 {
			// ENDI.
			d.endFlag = true
			s.Raise(IntDSPEnd)
		}
	default:
		// Class 0b11 with an unassigned top nibble and
		// class 0b01 act as NOP.
	}

	if repeating && d.running && !jumped {
		if d.lop > 0 {
			d.lop--
			d.pc = d.repeatAddr
		} else {
			d.repeatActive = false
		}
	}
	if jumped {
		d.repeatActive = false
		d.lpsPending = false
	}
}

// readRAMSource reads a data RAM word for a 3 bit
// source select (1bb increments the CT pointer, 0bb
// does not), using the CT values from before the
// instruction.
func (s *SCU) readRAMSource(sel uint32, ctSnapshot [4]uint8) uint32 {
	d := &s.dsp
	bank := int(sel & 3)
	v := d.data[bank][ctSnapshot[bank]&0x3F]
	if sel&4 != 0 {
		d.ct[bank] = (ctSnapshot[bank] + 1) & 0x3F
	}
	return v
}

// setP sets the product register from a 32 bit value in
// PL, with PH following by sign extension.
func (s *SCU) setP32(v uint32) {
	d := &s.dsp
	ph := uint64(0)
	if v&0x80000000 != 0 {
		ph = 0xFFFF
	}
	d.p = ph<<32 | uint64(v)
}

// setAcc32 sets the accumulator from a 32 bit value in
// ACL, with ACH following by sign extension.
func (s *SCU) setAcc32(v uint32) {
	d := &s.dsp
	ah := uint64(0)
	if v&0x80000000 != 0 {
		ah = 0xFFFF
	}
	d.acc = ah<<32 | uint64(v)
}

// execOperation executes an operation command word.
func (s *SCU) execOperation(instr uint32) {
	d := &s.dsp
	ctSnapshot := d.ct
	acl := uint32(d.acc)
	ach := uint32(d.acc >> 32)
	pl := uint32(d.p)

	// ALU field.
	alu := (instr >> 26) & 0xF
	aluResult := d.acc
	aluChanged := false
	switch alu {
	case 0: // NOP
	case 1: // AND
		r := acl & pl
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagC = false
		d.flagV = false
	case 2: // OR
		r := acl | pl
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagC = false
		d.flagV = false
	case 3: // XOR
		r := acl ^ pl
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagC = false
		d.flagV = false
	case 4: // ADD
		sum := uint64(acl) + uint64(pl)
		r := uint32(sum)
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagC = sum>>32 != 0
		d.flagV = (acl^r)&(pl^r)&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
	case 5: // SUB
		diff := uint64(acl) - uint64(pl)
		r := uint32(diff)
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagC = acl >= pl
		d.flagV = (acl^pl)&(acl^r)&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
	case 6: // AD2: 48 bit A plus P.
		aBefore := d.acc & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
		pBefore := d.p & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
		sum := aBefore + pBefore
		r := sum & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
		d.acc = r
		aluResult = r
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagC = sum>>48 != 0
		d.flagS = r&(1<<47) != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		// Signed overflow: the operands share a sign
		// that the result does not.
		d.flagV = (aBefore>>47)&1 == (pBefore>>47)&1 &&
			(r>>47)&1 != (aBefore>>47)&1
	case 8: // SR: arithmetic shift right.
		r := (acl >> 1) | (acl & 0x80000000)
		d.flagC = acl&1 != 0
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagV = false
	case 9: // RR: rotate right.
		r := (acl >> 1) | ((acl & 1) << 31)
		d.flagC = acl&1 != 0
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagV = false
	case 10: // SL: shift left.
		r := acl << 1
		d.flagC = acl&0x80000000 != 0
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagV = false
	case 11: // RL: rotate left.
		r := (acl << 1) | (acl >> 31)
		d.flagC = acl&0x80000000 != 0
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagV = false
	case 14: // RR8: rotate right 8.
		r := (acl >> 8) | (acl << 24)
		d.flagC = acl&(1<<7) != 0
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagV = false
	case 15: // RL8: rotate left 8.
		r := (acl << 8) | (acl >> 24)
		d.flagC = acl&(1<<24) != 0
		s.setAcc32(r)
		aluResult = d.acc
		aluChanged = true
		d.flagS = r&0x80000000 != 0
		d.flagZ = r == 0
		d.flagV = false
	default:
		// Unassigned ALU codes act as NOP.
	}
	_ = aluChanged

	// X bus field.
	xOp := (instr >> 23) & 7
	xSrc := (instr >> 20) & 7
	switch xOp {
	case 4: // MOV [s], X
		d.rx = s.readRAMSource(xSrc, ctSnapshot)
	case 2: // MOV MUL, P: signed product of the RX and
		// RY values from the start of the instruction.
		prod := int64(int32(d.rx)) * int64(int32(d.ry))
		d.p = uint64(prod) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
	case 3: // MOV [s], P
		s.setP32(s.readRAMSource(xSrc, ctSnapshot))
	}

	// Y bus field.
	yOp := (instr >> 17) & 7
	ySrc := (instr >> 14) & 7
	switch yOp {
	case 4: // MOV [s], Y
		d.ry = s.readRAMSource(ySrc, ctSnapshot)
	case 1: // CLR A
		d.acc = 0
	case 2: // MOV ALU, A
		d.acc = aluResult & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
	case 3: // MOV [s], A
		s.setAcc32(s.readRAMSource(ySrc, ctSnapshot))
	}

	// D1 bus field.
	d1Kind := (instr >> 12) & 3
	switch d1Kind {
	case 1: // MOV SImm, [d]
		dest := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
		imm := uint32(signExtend(instr&0xFF, 8))
		s.writeDSPDest(dest, imm, false)
	case 3: // MOV [s], [d]
		dest := (instr >> 8) & 0xF
		src := instr & 0xF
		var v uint32
		switch {
		case src < 8:
			bank := int(src & 3)
			v = d.data[bank][ctSnapshot[bank]&0x3F]
			if src&4 != 0 {
				d.ct[bank] = (ctSnapshot[bank] + 1) & 0x3F
			}
		case src == 8:
			v = uint32(d.acc)
		case src == 9:
			v = uint32(int32(int16(ach)))
		default:
			v = 0
		}
		s.writeDSPDest(dest, v, false)
	}
	_ = ach
}

// writeDSPDest writes v to a D1 or MVI destination.
// When fromMVI is set, destination 14 is PC with the
// subroutine return address stored in TOP.
func (s *SCU) writeDSPDest(dest uint32, v uint32, fromMVI bool) {
	d := &s.dsp
	switch {
	case dest < 4:
		bank := int(dest)
		d.data[bank][d.ct[bank]&0x3F] = v
		d.ct[bank] = (d.ct[bank] + 1) & 0x3F
	case dest == 4:
		d.rx = v
	case dest == 5:
		s.setP32(v)
	case dest == 6:
		d.ra0 = v
	case dest == 7:
		d.wa0 = v
	case dest == 8:
		d.lop = uint16(v) & 0xFFF
	case dest == 9:
		d.top = uint8(v)
	case dest >= 10 && dest <= 13:
		d.ct[dest-10] = uint8(v) & 0x3F
	case dest == 14 && fromMVI:
		d.top = d.pc // pc already points past the MVI
		d.pc = uint8(v)
	}
}

// execMVI executes a load immediate command and
// reports whether it wrote PC (a jump).
func (s *SCU) execMVI(instr uint32) bool {
	dest := (instr >> 26) & 0xF
	var imm uint32
	if instr&(1<<25) == 0 {
		imm = uint32(signExtend(instr&0x1FFFFFF, 25))
	} else {
		if !s.condTrue((instr>>19)&0x1F, instr&(1<<24) != 0) {
			return false
		}
		imm = uint32(signExtend(instr&0x7FFFF, 19))
	}
	s.writeDSPDest(dest, imm, true)
	return dest == 14
}

// execDSPDMA executes a DSP DMA command atomically
// through the attached Mem.
func (s *SCU) execDSPDMA(instr uint32) {
	d := &s.dsp
	if s.mem == nil {
		return
	}
	hold := instr&(1<<14) != 0
	dirOut := instr&(1<<12) != 0
	addCode := (instr >> 15) & 7
	addVals := []uint32{0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
	add := addVals[addCode]
	ramSel := (instr >> 8) & 7

	var count uint32
	if instr&(1<<27) == 0 {
		count = instr & 0xFF
	} else {
		sel := instr & 7
		bank := int(sel & 3)
		count = d.data[bank][d.ct[bank]&0x3F]
		if sel&4 != 0 {
			d.ct[bank] = (d.ct[bank] + 1) & 0x3F
		}
	}
	if count == 0 {
		return
	}
	d.tn0 = count
	d.flagT0 = true

	if !dirOut {
		// External memory into DSP RAM, from RA0.
		srcAddr := d.ra0
		for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++ {
			v := s.mem.Read32((srcAddr + i*addOrOne(add)) << 2)
			s.writeDSPRAMWord(ramSel, v)
		}
		if !hold {
			d.ra0 = srcAddr + count*addOrOne(add)
			d.tn0 = 0
		}
	} else {
		// DSP RAM out to external memory, at WA0.
		dstAddr := d.wa0
		for i := uint32(0); i < count; i++ {
			v := s.readDSPRAMWord(ramSel)
			s.mem.Write32((dstAddr+i*addOrOne(add))<<2, v)
		}
		if !hold {
			d.wa0 = dstAddr + count*addOrOne(add)
			d.tn0 = 0
		}
	}
	d.flagT0 = false
}

// addOrOne maps an external address add value of 0 to
// a step of 1 word for sequential DSP DMA transfers in
// this core: the manual's add 0 form is for A-Bus
// devices that sequence internally, and Mem addresses
// must still advance to move a block. (The SCU DMA
// channels in dma.go model add 0 as a true hold.)
func addOrOne(add uint32) uint32 {
	if add == 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return add
}

// writeDSPRAMWord writes one word to the DSP RAM
// selected by a DMA command RAM select, advancing the
// matching pointer.
func (s *SCU) writeDSPRAMWord(sel uint32, v uint32) {
	d := &s.dsp
	if sel == 4 {
		d.prog[d.dmaProgAddr&0xFF] = v
		d.dmaProgAddr++
		return
	}
	bank := int(sel & 3)
	d.data[bank][d.ct[bank]&0x3F] = v
	d.ct[bank] = (d.ct[bank] + 1) & 0x3F
}

// readDSPRAMWord reads one word from the DSP RAM
// selected by a DMA command RAM select, advancing the
// matching pointer.
func (s *SCU) readDSPRAMWord(sel uint32) uint32 {
	d := &s.dsp
	if sel == 4 {
		v := d.prog[d.dmaProgAddr&0xFF]
		d.dmaProgAddr++
		return v
	}
	bank := int(sel & 3)
	v := d.data[bank][d.ct[bank]&0x3F]
	d.ct[bank] = (d.ct[bank] + 1) & 0x3F
	return v
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scu/scu.go ====================

// Package scu models the Sega Saturn SCU: the interrupt
// mask and status registers (IMS and IST) on the SCU
// register page, the three DMA channels, the SCU DSP,
// and the two timers.
//
// IMS and IST are 32 bit registers at page offsets 0xA0
// and 0xA4. The interrupt sources occupy the low bits.
// A mask bit of 1 in IMS blocks delivery of that source.
// A status bit of 1 in IST means the source has fired and
// is waiting; software clears a source by writing 0 to
// its IST bit through the bus page. This package is a
// thin view over the bus page for the registers: it keeps
// no shadow copy of register words, so CPU writes to the
// page take effect immediately. State that does not live
// on the page (the DSP program and data RAMs, the DSP
// registers, DMA latches, and timer counters) lives in
// the SCU struct and is covered by SerializeExtra.
//
// Delivery rule: sources are offered in the documented
// SCU priority order (VBlank-IN first, sprite draw end
// last, the A-Bus external input after those) at the per
// source levels of the manual's Table 2.1 (see LevelOf)
// with the standard SCU vector numbers, one source per
// Deliver call. The system calls Deliver once per
// scanline and offers the result to both SH-2s. Because
// IST bits stay set until software clears them, no
// source is lost when a CPU already has a request
// latched; it is offered again on a later line.
//
// The system calls Poll once per scanline to run the DMA
// channels and the DSP; see dma.go, dsp.go, and timers.go.
package scu

import "encoding/binary"

// Interrupt source bit numbers within IMS and IST.
//
// These bit numbers are the ones frozen by the SAT-2
// slice. The SCU manual (ST-058 family, third version
// ST-97) lists one more low source the SAT-2 map does
// not have: bit 12 is DMA illegal there and sprite draw
// end is bit 13. This core keeps sprite draw end at bit
// 12 with vector 0x4D, as SAT-2 shipped it, and has no
// DMA illegal source. There is no CD interrupt source in
// IST in any version of the manual: CD block interrupts
// reach the CPU as A-Bus external interrupts (IST bits
// 16 and up) gated by the CD block HIRQ register, so no
// IntCD constant exists here.
const (
	IntVBlankIn  = 0
	IntVBlankOut = 1
	IntHBlankIn  = 2
	IntTimer0    = 3
	IntTimer1    = 4
	IntDSPEnd    = 5
	IntSoundReq  = 6
	IntSMPC      = 7
	IntPad       = 8
	IntDMA2End   = 9
	IntDMA1End   = 10
	IntDMA0End   = 11
	IntSpriteEnd = 12
)

// IntABusCD is the IST bit this core assigns to its one
// A-Bus external interrupt input, wired to the CD block.
// The manual puts A-Bus external inputs at IST bits 16
// and up, gated by the interrupting device's own
// interrupt register (the CD block HIRQ). On hardware
// the device supplies the interrupt vector during the
// acknowledge cycle; this core fixes the CD input at
// vector 0x50 and level 8 (see Vector and LevelOf).
const IntABusCD = 16

// sourceCount is the number of defined interrupt sources.
const sourceCount = 13

// vectors holds the SH-2 vector number for each source,
// in bit order. These are the standard SCU assignments:
// VBlank-IN is vector 0x40 and the sources follow in
// priority order, with the sprite draw end at 0x4D.
var vectors = [sourceCount]int{
	0x40, 0x41, 0x42, 0x43, 0x44, 0x45, 0x46,
	0x47, 0x48, 0x49, 0x4A, 0x4B, 0x4D,
}

// Level is retained from SAT-2, where every wired SCU
// source was delivered to the master at this one level.
// SAT-3 delivery uses the per source levels of the
// manual's Table 2.1 through LevelOf; Level stays for
// compatibility with the SAT-2 wiring.
const Level = 6

// manualLevels holds the per source interrupt levels
// from Table 2.1 of the SCU manual, matched to this
// package's source names: VBlank-IN 15, VBlank-OUT 14,
// HBlank-IN 13, Timer 0 12, Timer 1 11, DSP end 10,
// sound request 9, system manager 8, pad 8, level 2 DMA
// end 6, level 1 DMA end 6, level 0 DMA end 5, and
// sprite draw end 2. LevelOf returns these levels and
// the system delivers each source at its own level to
// both SH-2s. ManualLevelOf returns the same table.
var manualLevels = [sourceCount]int{
	15, 14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 9, 8, 8, 6, 6, 5, 2,
}

// LevelOf returns the SH-2 interrupt level a source is
// delivered at: the per source level from Table 2.1 of
// the SCU manual for the low sources, the fixed level 8
// for the A-Bus CD input, or -1 for an unknown source.
func LevelOf(bit int) int {
	if bit == IntABusCD {
		return 8
	}
	if bit < 0 || bit >= sourceCount {
		return -1
	}
	return manualLevels[bit]
}

// ManualLevelOf returns the per source interrupt level
// from Table 2.1 of the SCU manual for a source, or -1
// when the manual assigns the source no fixed level.
// The A-Bus external inputs are such a case (their
// levels are set by device side registers on hardware),
// so ManualLevelOf returns -1 for IntABusCD while
// LevelOf returns this core's fixed level 8.
func ManualLevelOf(bit int) int {
	if bit < 0 || bit >= sourceCount {
		return -1
	}
	return manualLevels[bit]
}

// Register page offsets of IMS and IST.
const (
	offIMS = 0xA0
	offIST = 0xA4
)

// SCU is a view over the 256 byte SCU register page owned
// by the bus, plus the off page state of the DMA
// channels, the DSP, and the timers.
type SCU struct {
	regs []byte

	// DMA state (dma.go).
	mem            Mem
	lastEnabled    [3]bool
	latchedFactors uint8
	illegalDMA     uint32

	// DSP state (dsp.go).
	dsp dspState

	// Port sync state (dsp.go): the last values consumed
	// from the DSP load ports on the page.
	lastProgPort  uint32
	progPortValid bool
	lastDataAddr  uint32
	lastDataData  uint32

	// Timer state (timers.go).
	lineDots  int
	t1Counter int
	lastLine  int
}

// New wraps a register page. The slice must be at least
// 0xA8 bytes; the bus page is 256 bytes.
func New(regs []byte) *SCU {
	return &SCU{regs: regs}
}

func (s *SCU) word(off int) uint32 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(s.regs[off : off+4])
}

func (s *SCU) setWord(off int, v uint32) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(s.regs[off:off+4], v)
}

// factorForBit maps an interrupt source bit to the DMA
// start factor number that source signals, per the DMA
// start factor table in the manual. The second result
// is false for sources that are not DMA start factors.
func factorForBit(bit int) (int, bool) {
	switch bit {
	case IntVBlankIn:
		return FactorVBlankIn, true
	case IntVBlankOut:
		return FactorVBlankOut, true
	case IntHBlankIn:
		return FactorHBlankIn, true
	case IntTimer0:
		return FactorTimer0, true
	case IntTimer1:
		return FactorTimer1, true
	case IntSoundReq:
		return FactorSoundReq, true
	case IntSpriteEnd:
		return FactorSpriteEnd, true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// validSource reports whether a bit number names a
// source this core models: one of the low sources or
// the A-Bus CD input.
func validSource(bit int) bool {
	return (bit >= 0 && bit < sourceCount) || bit == IntABusCD
}

// Raise sets the IST status bit for a source. The bit is
// set whether or not the source is masked; masking only
// blocks delivery. Out of range sources are ignored.
// Raising a source that is a DMA start factor also
// latches that factor for the next Poll, matching the
// hardware rule that the factor signal is a pulse even
// though the IST bit stays set until software clears it.
func (s *SCU) Raise(bit int) {
	if !validSource(bit) {
		return
	}
	s.setWord(offIST, s.word(offIST)|(1<<uint(bit)))
	if f, ok := factorForBit(bit); ok {
		s.latchedFactors |= 1 << uint(f)
	}
}

// sourceMask selects the IST and IMS bits that name a
// modeled source: the low 13 sources and the A-Bus CD
// input.
const sourceMask = 0x1FFF | (1 << IntABusCD)

// Status returns the raw IST word (modeled source bits
// used).
func (s *SCU) Status() uint32 { return s.word(offIST) }

// Mask returns the raw IMS word (modeled source bits
// used).
func (s *SCU) Mask() uint32 { return s.word(offIMS) }

// Pending returns the set of sources that have fired and
// are not masked: IST AND NOT IMS, modeled source bits.
func (s *SCU) Pending() uint32 {
	return s.word(offIST) &^ s.word(offIMS) & sourceMask
}

// Vector returns the SH-2 vector number for a source, or
// -1 for an out of range source. The A-Bus CD input
// returns this core's fixed vector 0x50: on hardware the
// interrupting device supplies the vector during the
// acknowledge cycle, and this core models the one
// external input with a fixed assignment.
func Vector(bit int) int {
	if bit == IntABusCD {
		return 0x50
	}
	if bit < 0 || bit >= sourceCount {
		return -1
	}
	return vectors[bit]
}

// Deliver picks the highest priority pending unmasked
// source (lowest bit number, the A-Bus CD input last)
// and returns its bit number and vector. It returns bit
// -1 when nothing is pending. Deliver does not clear
// the IST bit; clearing is the software job, done by
// writing the page through the bus. The caller passes
// the result to the CPU Interrupt methods at
// LevelOf(bit); the system offers it to both SH-2s.
func (s *SCU) Deliver() (bit int, vector int) {
	p := s.Pending()
	for b := 0; b < sourceCount; b++ {
		if p&(1<<uint(b)) != 0 {
			return b, vectors[b]
		}
	}
	if p&(1<<uint(IntABusCD)) != 0 {
		return IntABusCD, 0x50
	}
	return -1, -1
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scu/scu3_test.go ====================

package scu

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"
)

// fakeMem is a sparse byte addressed Mem for tests.
type fakeMem struct {
	b map[uint32]uint8
}

func newFakeMem() *fakeMem { return &fakeMem{b: map[uint32]uint8{}} }

func (m *fakeMem) Read8(a uint32) uint8 { return m.b[a] }

func (m *fakeMem) Read16(a uint32) uint16 {
	return uint16(m.b[a])<<8 | uint16(m.b[a+1])
}

func (m *fakeMem) Read32(a uint32) uint32 {
	return uint32(m.b[a])<<24 | uint32(m.b[a+1])<<16 |
		uint32(m.b[a+2])<<8 | uint32(m.b[a+3])
}

func (m *fakeMem) Write8(a uint32, v uint8) { m.b[a] = v }

func (m *fakeMem) Write16(a uint32, v uint16) {
	m.b[a] = uint8(v >> 8)
	m.b[a+1] = uint8(v)
}

func (m *fakeMem) Write32(a uint32, v uint32) {
	m.b[a] = uint8(v >> 24)
	m.b[a+1] = uint8(v >> 16)
	m.b[a+2] = uint8(v >> 8)
	m.b[a+3] = uint8(v)
}

func setPage(page []byte, off int, v uint32) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(page[off:off+4], v)
}

func pageWord(page []byte, off int) uint32 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(page[off : off+4])
}

// setupDMA programs one channel's registers on the page.
func setupDMA(page []byte, ch int, r, w, c, ad, en, md uint32) {
	base := ch * 0x20
	setPage(page, base+0x00, r)
	setPage(page, base+0x04, w)
	setPage(page, base+0x08, c)
	setPage(page, base+0x0C, ad)
	setPage(page, base+0x14, md)
	setPage(page, base+0x10, en)
}

func TestLevelOf(t *testing.T) {
	// Delivery levels are the manual's per source table
	// (SCU manual Table 2.1). SAT-3 replaced the flat
	// level 6 delivery of SAT-2 with these; LevelOf and
	// ManualLevelOf report the same table.
	manual := map[int]int{
		IntVBlankIn: 15, IntVBlankOut: 14, IntHBlankIn: 13,
		IntTimer0: 12, IntTimer1: 11, IntDSPEnd: 10,
		IntSoundReq: 9, IntSMPC: 8, IntPad: 8,
		IntDMA2End: 6, IntDMA1End: 6, IntDMA0End: 5,
		IntSpriteEnd: 2,
	}
	for bit, want := range manual {
		if got := LevelOf(bit); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("LevelOf(%d) = %d, want %d", bit, got, want)
		}
		if got := ManualLevelOf(bit); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("ManualLevelOf(%d) = %d, want %d", bit, got, want)
		}
	}
	// The A-Bus CD input delivers at this core's fixed
	// level 8; the manual assigns it no fixed level.
	if got := LevelOf(IntABusCD); got != 8 {
		t.Fatalf("LevelOf(IntABusCD) = %d, want 8", got)
	}
	if got := Vector(IntABusCD); got != 0x50 {
		t.Fatalf("Vector(IntABusCD) = %#x, want 0x50", got)
	}
	if got := LevelOf(99); got != -1 {
		t.Fatalf("LevelOf(99) = %d, want -1", got)
	}
}

func TestDMADirectImmediateEdge(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	mem.Write32(0x1000, 0xDEADBEEF)
	// Factor 7 (immediate), enable at bit 0 (brief form).
	setupDMA(page, 0, 0x1000, 0x2000, 4, 0x101, 1, FactorImmediate)
	s.Poll()
	if got := mem.Read32(0x2000); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("copied word = %#x, want 0xDEADBEEF", got)
	}
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntDMA0End) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("DMA0 end interrupt not raised")
	}
	if got := pageWord(page, offDSTA); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("DSTA after Poll = %#x, want 0 (idle)", got)
	}
	// Save mode: address registers unchanged.
	if got := pageWord(page, 0x00); got != 0x1000 {
		t.Fatalf("D0R after save mode run = %#x, want 0x1000", got)
	}
	// The enable edge is consumed: changing the source
	// and polling again does not rerun the channel.
	mem.Write32(0x1000, 0x12345678)
	s.Poll()
	if got := mem.Read32(0x2000); got != 0xDEADBEEF {
		t.Fatalf("channel reran without an edge: dest = %#x", got)
	}
}

func TestDMADirectUpdateMode(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	md := uint32(FactorImmediate) | 1<<16 | 1<<8 // update both
	setupDMA(page, 0, 0x1000, 0x2000, 8, 0x101, 1, md)
	s.Poll()
	if got := pageWord(page, 0x00); got != 0x1008 {
		t.Fatalf("D0R after update run = %#x, want 0x1008", got)
	}
	if got := pageWord(page, 0x04); got != 0x2008 {
		t.Fatalf("D0W after update run = %#x, want 0x2008", got)
	}
}

func TestDMAFactorFromRaiseAndStartFactor(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	mem.Write32(0x1000, 0xAAAAAAAA)
	mem.Write32(0x1100, 0xBBBBBBBB)
	// Channel 1 waits for VBlank-IN; enable at bit 8
	// (manual form). Channel 2 waits for Timer 0.
	setupDMA(page, 1, 0x1000, 0x2000, 4, 0x101, 1<<8, FactorVBlankIn)
	setupDMA(page, 2, 0x1100, 0x2100, 4, 0x101, 1, FactorTimer0)
	s.Poll() // enables latch, no factors yet
	if mem.Read32(0x2000) != 0 || mem.Read32(0x2100) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("channel ran before its factor")
	}
	s.Raise(IntVBlankIn)
	s.Poll()
	if got := mem.Read32(0x2000); got != 0xAAAAAAAA {
		t.Fatalf("channel 1 dest = %#x, want 0xAAAAAAAA", got)
	}
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntDMA1End) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("DMA1 end interrupt not raised")
	}
	if mem.Read32(0x2100) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("channel 2 ran on the wrong factor")
	}
	s.StartFactor(FactorTimer0)
	s.Poll()
	if got := mem.Read32(0x2100); got != 0xBBBBBBBB {
		t.Fatalf("channel 2 dest = %#x, want 0xBBBBBBBB", got)
	}
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntDMA2End) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("DMA2 end interrupt not raised")
	}
}

func TestDMAChannelOrderZeroFirst(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	mem.Write32(0x1000, 0x11111111)
	mem.Write32(0x1100, 0x22222222)
	// Both channels due on VBlank-IN, same destination:
	// channel 0 runs first, so channel 1 lands last.
	setupDMA(page, 0, 0x1000, 0x2000, 4, 0x101, 1, FactorVBlankIn)
	setupDMA(page, 1, 0x1100, 0x2000, 4, 0x101, 1, FactorVBlankIn)
	s.Poll()
	s.Raise(IntVBlankIn)
	s.Poll()
	if got := mem.Read32(0x2000); got != 0x22222222 {
		t.Fatalf("overlap dest = %#x, want channel 1 result 0x22222222", got)
	}
}

func TestDMACountZeroMeansFullWidth(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	for i := 0; i < 4096; i++ {
		mem.Write8(0x4000+uint32(i), uint8(i))
	}
	// Channel 1 count width is 12 bits; 0 means 4096.
	setupDMA(page, 1, 0x4000, 0x8000, 0, 0x101, 1, FactorImmediate)
	s.Poll()

		t.Fatalf("last copied byte = %#x, want 0xFF", got)
	}

		t.Fatalf("byte 100 = %#x, want 100", got)
	}
}

func TestDMAIndirectMode(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	mem.Write32(0x1000, 0xCAFEBABE)
	mem.Write32(0x1100, 0x0D15EA5E)
	// Table at 0x8000: two entries, second has the end
	// flag (bit 31 of the count word) and 3 bytes.
	mem.Write32(0x8000, 0x1000)
	mem.Write32(0x8004, 0x2000)
	mem.Write32(0x8008, 4)
	mem.Write32(0x800C, 0x1100)
	mem.Write32(0x8010, 0x2100)
	mem.Write32(0x8014, 0x80000003)
	md := uint32(1<<24) | uint32(FactorImmediate) | 1<<8 // indirect, WUP
	setupDMA(page, 0, 0, 0x8000, 0, 0x101, 1, md)
	s.Poll()
	if got := mem.Read32(0x2000); got != 0xCAFEBABE {
		t.Fatalf("entry 1 dest = %#x, want 0xCAFEBABE", got)
	}
	if got := mem.Read32(0x2100) & 0xFFFFFF00; got != 0x0D15EA00 {
		t.Fatalf("entry 2 dest = %#x, want 0x0D15EAxx", got)
	}
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntDMA0End) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("DMA0 end interrupt not raised for indirect run")
	}
	// WUP: DxW left past the last entry (table + 24).
	if got := pageWord(page, 0x04); got != 0x8018 {
		t.Fatalf("D0W after indirect update = %#x, want 0x8018", got)
	}
}
