func TestDMAForceStop(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	mem.Write32(0x1000, 0x77777777)
	setupDMA(page, 0, 0x1000, 0x2000, 4, 0x101, 1, FactorImmediate)
	setPage(page, offDSTP, 1)
	s.Poll()
	if got := pageWord(page, 0x10); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("D0EN after DSTP = %#x, want 0 (cleared)", got)
	}
	if mem.Read32(0x2000) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("transfer ran despite force stop")
	}
	// The brief's transposed stop offset 0x7C also stops.
	setupDMA(page, 0, 0x1000, 0x2000, 4, 0x101, 1, FactorImmediate)
	setPage(page, offDSTA, 1)
	s.Poll()
	if got := pageWord(page, 0x10); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("D0EN after stop write to 0x7C = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
	if mem.Read32(0x2000) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("transfer ran despite stop write to 0x7C")
	}
}

// opWord assembles a DSP operation command word.
func opWord(alu, xField, yField, d1Field uint32) uint32 {
	return alu<<26 | xField<<20 | yField<<14 | d1Field
}

// loadProgramThroughPorts writes a program into DSP
// program RAM using the control port and the program
// data port, one Poll per word, as software would.
func loadProgramThroughPorts(t *testing.T, s *SCU, page []byte, prog []uint32) {
	t.Helper()
	for i, w := range prog {
		setPage(page, offPPAF, uint32(i))
		setPage(page, offPPD, w)
		s.Poll()
		if got := s.DSPProgram(i); got != w {
			t.Fatalf("program[%d] = %#x, want %#x (port load)", i, got, w)
		}
	}
}

func TestDSPDotProduct(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	bank0 := []uint32{3, 5, 7, 11}
	bank1 := []uint32{2, 4, 6, 8}
	for i, v := range bank0 {
		s.DSPWriteData(0, i, v)
	}
	for i, v := range bank1 {
		s.DSPWriteData(1, i, v)
	}
	prog := []uint32{
		opWord(0, 0, 1<<3, 0),              // CLR A
		opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(10<<8)|0), // MOV 0, [CT0]
		opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(11<<8)|0), // MOV 0, [CT1]
		opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(9<<8)|5),  // MOV 5, [TOP]
		opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(8<<8)|3),  // MOV 3, [LOP]
		opWord(0, (4<<3)|4, (4<<3)|5, 0),   // loop: MOV MC0,X | MOV MC1,Y
		opWord(0, 2<<3, 0, 0),              // MOV MUL, P
		opWord(4, 0, 2<<3, 0),              // ADD | MOV ALU, A
		0xE0000000,                         // BTM
		0xF8000000,                         // ENDI
	}
	loadProgramThroughPorts(t, s, page, prog)

	setPage(page, offPPAF, 1<<ppafEX) // start at 0, execute
	s.Poll()
	if got := s.DSPAccumulator(); got != 156 {
		t.Fatalf("dot product accumulator = %d, want 156", got)
	}
	if s.dsp.ct[0] != 4 || s.dsp.ct[1] != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("CT after loop = %v, want CT0 and CT1 at 4", s.dsp.ct)
	}
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntDSPEnd) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("DSP end interrupt not raised after ENDI")
	}
	ppaf := pageWord(page, offPPAF)
	if ppaf&(1<<ppafEX) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("EX flag still set after ENDI")
	}
	if ppaf&(1<<ppafE) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("E flag not set in PPAF after ENDI")
	}
	if s.DSPRunning() {
		t.Fatal("DSP still running after ENDI")
	}
}

func TestDSPDataPortLoadAndRead(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	// Select data RAM bank 1, address 0, then write a
	// word through the data port.
	setPage(page, offPDA, 0x40)
	s.Poll()
	setPage(page, offPDD, 0xCAFEBABE)
	s.Poll()
	if got := s.DSPData(1, 0); got != 0xCAFEBABE {
		t.Fatalf("data RAM bank 1 word 0 = %#x, want 0xCAFEBABE", got)
	}
	// The address counts up after the access.
	if got := pageWord(page, offPDA); got != 0x41 {
		t.Fatalf("PDA after write = %#x, want 0x41", got)
	}
	// Read back: select the address again and Poll;
	// the data port then presents the stored word.
	setPage(page, offPDA, 0x40)
	s.Poll()
	if got := pageWord(page, offPDD); got != 0xCAFEBABE {
		t.Fatalf("PDD read back = %#x, want 0xCAFEBABE", got)
	}
}

func TestDSPDMATransfers(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	for i, v := range []uint32{111, 222, 333, 444} {
		mem.Write32(0x1000+uint32(i*4), v)
	}
	// Program: CT2 = 0, RA0 = 0x400 (byte 0x1000),
	// DMA D0, [M2], 4, ENDI.
	s.DSPWriteProgram(0, opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(12<<8)|0))
	s.DSPWriteProgram(1, (2<<30)|(6<<26)|0x400) // MVI 0x400, [RA0]
	s.DSPWriteProgram(2, 0xC0000000|(1<<15)|(2<<8)|4)
	s.DSPWriteProgram(3, 0xF8000000) // ENDI
	if n := s.RunDSP(100); n != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("RunDSP executed %d instructions, want 4", n)
	}
	for i, want := range []uint32{111, 222, 333, 444} {
		if got := s.DSPData(2, i); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("DSP DMA in: data RAM2[%d] = %d, want %d", i, got, want)
		}
	}
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntDSPEnd) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("DSP end interrupt not raised")
	}

	// Second program at 10: CT2 = 0, WA0 = 0x800
	// (byte 0x2000), DMA [M2], D0, 4, ENDI.
	s.DSPWriteProgram(10, opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(12<<8)|0))
	s.DSPWriteProgram(11, (2<<30)|(7<<26)|0x800) // MVI 0x800, [WA0]
	s.DSPWriteProgram(12, 0xC0000000|(1<<15)|(1<<12)|(2<<8)|4)
	s.DSPWriteProgram(13, 0xF8000000)
	setPage(page, offPPAF, 10|(1<<ppafLE)) // load PC = 10
	s.Poll()
	s.RunDSP(100)
	for i, want := range []uint32{111, 222, 333, 444} {
		if got := mem.Read32(0x2000 + uint32(i*4)); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("DSP DMA out: mem word %d = %d, want %d", i, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestDSPJump(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := newPage()
	s.DSPWriteProgram(0, 0xD0000002) // JMP 2
	s.DSPWriteProgram(1, opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(4<<8)|99))
	s.DSPWriteProgram(2, opWord(0, 0, 0, (1<<12)|(4<<8)|7))
	s.DSPWriteProgram(3, 0xF8000000) // ENDI
	s.RunDSP(100)
	if got := s.dsp.rx; got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("RX after jump = %d, want 7 (address 1 skipped)", got)
	}
}

func TestTimer0DotModel(t *testing.T) {
	// No dot timing set: only compare 0 fires.
	s, page := newPage()
	setPage(page, offT0C, 0)
	s.TickLine(0)
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntTimer0) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 0 did not fire for compare 0 without dot timing")
	}
	s2, page2 := newPage()
	setPage(page2, offT0C, 5)
	s2.TickLine(0)
	if s2.Status()&(1<<IntTimer0) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 0 fired for compare 5 without dot timing")
	}
	// With 100 dots per line, compare 250 lies in the
	// dot range of line 2 only.
	s3, page3 := newPage()
	s3.SetLineDots(100)
	setPage(page3, offT0C, 250)
	s3.TickLine(0)
	s3.TickLine(1)
	if s3.Status()&(1<<IntTimer0) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 0 fired before line 2")
	}
	s3.TickLine(2)
	if s3.Status()&(1<<IntTimer0) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 0 did not fire on line 2 for compare 250")
	}
	_ = page
}

func TestTimer1LineCounting(t *testing.T) {
	// Mode 0: counts every line, fires at T1S = 3, and
	// resets to fire again three lines later.
	s, page := newPage()
	setPage(page, offT0C, 900) // timer 0 out of the way
	setPage(page, offT1S, 3)
	setPage(page, offT1MD, 1) // enabled, mode bit clear
	s.TickLine(0)
	s.TickLine(1)
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntTimer1) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 1 fired before 3 lines")
	}
	s.TickLine(2)
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntTimer1) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 1 did not fire at 3 lines")
	}
	setPage(page, offIST, 0)
	s.TickLine(3)
	s.TickLine(4)
	s.TickLine(5)
	if s.Status()&(1<<IntTimer1) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 1 did not fire again after reset")
	}

	// Mode 1 (bit 8): counts only lines where timer 0
	// fires. Compare 250 with 100 dots per line fires
	// on line 2, so two ticks of line 2 reach T1S = 2.
	s2, page2 := newPage()
	s2.SetLineDots(100)
	setPage(page2, offT0C, 250)
	setPage(page2, offT1S, 2)
	setPage(page2, offT1MD, (1<<8)|1) // enabled, mode bit set
	s2.TickLine(0)
	s2.TickLine(1)
	s2.TickLine(2)
	if s2.Status()&(1<<IntTimer1) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 1 fired after only one timer 0 line")
	}
	s2.TickLine(2)
	if s2.Status()&(1<<IntTimer1) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("timer 1 did not fire after two timer 0 lines")
	}
}

func TestSerializeExtraRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	mem := newFakeMem()
	s.AttachMem(mem)
	s.DSPWriteData(0, 0, 42)
	s.DSPWriteProgram(0, 0xF8000000)
	s.SetLineDots(228)
	setupDMA(page, 0, 0x1000, 0x2000, 4, 0x101, 1, FactorImmediate)
	s.StartFactor(FactorTimer1)
	s.Poll()
	first := s.SerializeExtra()
	if len(first) != ExtraSize {
		t.Fatalf("SerializeExtra len = %d, want %d", len(first), ExtraSize)
	}
	s2, _ := newPage()
	if err := s2.DeserializeExtra(first); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	second := s2.SerializeExtra()
	if !bytes.Equal(first, second) {
		t.Fatal("extra state did not round trip")
	}
	if got := s2.DSPData(0, 0); got != 42 {
		t.Fatalf("restored data RAM = %d, want 42", got)
	}
	if got := s2.DSPProgram(0); got != 0xF8000000 {
		t.Fatalf("restored program RAM = %#x, want 0xF8000000", got)
	}
	if err := s2.DeserializeExtra(first[:100]); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("short extra state accepted")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scu/scu_test.go ====================

package scu

import "testing"

// fakeCPU records the last interrupt offered to it.
type fakeCPU struct {
	level  int
	vector int
	calls  int
}

func (f *fakeCPU) offer(s *SCU) bool {
	bit, vec := s.Deliver()
	if bit < 0 {
		return false
	}
	f.level = Level
	f.vector = vec
	f.calls++
	return true
}

func newPage() (*SCU, []byte) {
	page := make([]byte, 256)
	return New(page), page
}

func TestRaiseAndPending(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := newPage()
	if got := s.Pending(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pending = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
	s.Raise(IntVBlankIn)
	s.Raise(IntSpriteEnd)
	want := uint32(1<<IntVBlankIn | 1<<IntSpriteEnd)
	if got := s.Pending(); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("pending = %#x, want %#x", got, want)
	}
	if got := s.Status(); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("status = %#x, want %#x", got, want)
	}
}

func TestMaskBlocksDeliveryNotStatus(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	s.Raise(IntVBlankIn)
	// Mask VBlank-IN by writing IMS through the page: bit 0
	// of the word at 0xA0. Big endian: bits 0..7 live in
	// the last byte of the word.
	page[0xA3] = 0x01
	if got := s.Pending(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("pending = %#x, want 0 while masked", got)
	}
	if got := s.Status(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("status = %#x, want 1 (mask must not clear status)", got)
	}
	f := &fakeCPU{}
	if f.offer(s) {
		t.Fatal("masked source was delivered")
	}
}

func TestDeliverPriorityOrderAndClear(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newPage()
	s.Raise(IntSpriteEnd)
	s.Raise(IntHBlankIn)
	s.Raise(IntVBlankIn)
	f := &fakeCPU{}
	if !f.offer(s) || f.vector != 0x40 {
		t.Fatalf("first delivery vector = %#x, want 0x40 (VBlank-IN)", f.vector)
	}
	// Software clears VBlank-IN by writing 0 to IST bit 0
	// through the page.
	page[0xA7] &^= 0x01
	if !f.offer(s) || f.vector != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("second delivery vector = %#x, want 0x42 (HBlank-IN)", f.vector)
	}
	page[0xA7] &^= 0x04
	if !f.offer(s) || f.vector != 0x4D {
		t.Fatalf("third delivery vector = %#x, want 0x4D (sprite end)", f.vector)
	}
	page[0xA6] &^= 0x10
	if f.offer(s) {
		t.Fatal("delivery reported with nothing pending")
	}
}

func TestVectorTable(t *testing.T) {
	if got := Vector(IntVBlankIn); got != 0x40 {
		t.Fatalf("VBlank-IN vector = %#x, want 0x40", got)
	}
	if got := Vector(IntVBlankOut); got != 0x41 {
		t.Fatalf("VBlank-OUT vector = %#x, want 0x41", got)
	}
	if got := Vector(IntHBlankIn); got != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("HBlank-IN vector = %#x, want 0x42", got)
	}
	if got := Vector(99); got != -1 {
		t.Fatalf("out of range vector = %d, want -1", got)
	}
	s, _ := newPage()
	s.Raise(99)
	if got := s.Status(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("out of range raise changed status: %#x", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scu/state.go ====================

package scu

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
)

// Extra save state: everything the SCU keeps off the
// register page. The page itself is part of the main
// machine state. All integers are big endian.
//
// Layout:
//
//	0..1023      DSP program RAM (256 words)
//	1024..2047   DSP data RAM (4 banks of 64 words)
//	2048..2111   DSP register block:
//	               +0 RX, +4 RY, +8 P (64 bit),
//	               +16 A (64 bit), +24 RA0, +28 WA0,
//	               +32 TN0, +36 CT0..CT3 (one byte
//	               each), +40 PC, +41 TOP, +42 LOP
//	               (16 bit), +44 flags (bit 0 S, 1 Z,
//	               2 C, 3 V, 4 T0, 5 end), +45 running,
//	               +46 last EX, +47 repeat address,
//	               +48 repeat active, +49 LPS pending,
//	               +50 data port pointer, +52 program
//	               DMA pointer (32 bit)
//	2112..2127   DSP port sync block: +0 last program
//	               port word, +4 program port valid,
//	               +8 last data address port word,
//	               +12 last data data port word
//	2128..2143   DMA block: +0 latched start factors,
//	               +1 last enabled mask (bit per
//	               channel), +4 illegal DMA count
//	2144..2159   timer block: +0 line dots, +4 timer 1
//	               counter, +8 last ticked line
const ExtraSize = 2160

// Block offsets within the extra state.
const (
	extraProg    = 0
	extraData    = 1024
	extraDSPRegs = 2048
	extraPorts   = 2112
	extraDMA     = 2128
	extraTimers  = 2144
)

// SerializeExtra returns the off page SCU state as
// exactly ExtraSize bytes.
func (s *SCU) SerializeExtra() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, ExtraSize)
	d := &s.dsp
	for i, v := range d.prog {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[extraProg+i*4:], v)
	}
	for b := 0; b < 4; b++ {
		for i, v := range d.data[b] {
			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[extraData+(b*64+i)*4:], v)
		}
	}
	r := extraDSPRegs
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[r:], d.rx)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[r+4:], d.ry)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[r+8:], d.p)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[r+16:], d.acc)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[r+24:], d.ra0)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[r+28:], d.wa0)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[r+32:], d.tn0)
	for i, v := range d.ct {
		out[r+36+i] = v
	}
	out[r+40] = d.pc
	out[r+41] = d.top
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[r+42:], d.lop)
	var flags byte
	if d.flagS {
		flags |= 1 << 0
	}
	if d.flagZ {
		flags |= 1 << 1
	}
	if d.flagC {
		flags |= 1 << 2
	}
	if d.flagV {
		flags |= 1 << 3
	}
	if d.flagT0 {
		flags |= 1 << 4
	}
	if d.endFlag {
		flags |= 1 << 5
	}
	out[r+44] = flags
	if d.running {
		out[r+45] = 1
	}
	if d.lastEX {
		out[r+46] = 1
	}
	out[r+47] = d.repeatAddr
	if d.repeatActive {
		out[r+48] = 1
	}
	if d.lpsPending {
		out[r+49] = 1
	}
	out[r+50] = d.dataPtr
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[r+52:], d.dmaProgAddr)

	p := extraPorts
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[p:], s.lastProgPort)
	if s.progPortValid {
		out[p+4] = 1
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[p+8:], s.lastDataAddr)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[p+12:], s.lastDataData)

	m := extraDMA
	out[m] = s.latchedFactors
	var enMask byte
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		if s.lastEnabled[ch] {
			enMask |= 1 << uint(ch)
		}
	}
	out[m+1] = enMask
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[m+4:], s.illegalDMA)

	t := extraTimers
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[t:], uint32(int32(s.lineDots)))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[t+4:], uint32(int32(s.t1Counter)))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[t+8:], uint32(int32(s.lastLine)))
	return out
}

// DeserializeExtra restores state produced by
// SerializeExtra. The input must be exactly ExtraSize
// bytes.
func (s *SCU) DeserializeExtra(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) != ExtraSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("scu: extra state size %d, want %d", len(data), ExtraSize)
	}
	d := &s.dsp
	for i := range d.prog {
		d.prog[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[extraProg+i*4:])
	}
	for b := 0; b < 4; b++ {
		for i := range d.data[b] {
			d.data[b][i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[extraData+(b*64+i)*4:])
		}
	}
	r := extraDSPRegs
	d.rx = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[r:])
	d.ry = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[r+4:])
	d.p = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[r+8:])
	d.acc = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[r+16:])
	d.ra0 = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[r+24:])
	d.wa0 = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[r+28:])
	d.tn0 = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[r+32:])
	for i := range d.ct {
		d.ct[i] = data[r+36+i]
	}
	d.pc = data[r+40]
	d.top = data[r+41]
	d.lop = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[r+42:])
	flags := data[r+44]
	d.flagS = flags&(1<<0) != 0
	d.flagZ = flags&(1<<1) != 0
	d.flagC = flags&(1<<2) != 0
	d.flagV = flags&(1<<3) != 0
	d.flagT0 = flags&(1<<4) != 0
	d.endFlag = flags&(1<<5) != 0
	d.running = data[r+45] != 0
	d.lastEX = data[r+46] != 0
	d.repeatAddr = data[r+47]
	d.repeatActive = data[r+48] != 0
	d.lpsPending = data[r+49] != 0
	d.dataPtr = data[r+50]
	d.dmaProgAddr = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[r+52:])

	p := extraPorts
	s.lastProgPort = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[p:])
	s.progPortValid = data[p+4] != 0
	s.lastDataAddr = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[p+8:])
	s.lastDataData = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[p+12:])

	m := extraDMA
	s.latchedFactors = data[m]
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch++ {
		s.lastEnabled[ch] = data[m+1]&(1<<uint(ch)) != 0
	}
	s.illegalDMA = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[m+4:])

	t := extraTimers
	s.lineDots = int(int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[t:])))
	s.t1Counter = int(int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[t+4:])))
	s.lastLine = int(int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[t+8:])))
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/scu/timers.go ====================

package scu

// SCU timers 0 and 1.
//
// Registers on the page, per the manual: timer 0
// compare at 0x90 (T0C, 10 bits), timer 1 set data at
// 0x94 (T1S, 9 bits), and timer 1 mode at 0x98 (T1MD:
// bit 8 is the mode bit, bit 0 is the timer enable
// bit). The brief calls the compare register TC0; the
// manual name is T0C, at the same offset 0x90.
//
// The system drives the timers with TickLine, once per
// scanline, and tells the SCU the display dot timing
// with SetLineDots.
//
// Timer 0 model: the compare value is a dot position.
// Each line covers the dot range that starts at
// line times the dots per line and runs for the dots
// per line. Timer 0 fires once, on the line whose range
// contains the compare value; a compare of 0 therefore
// fires at the start of line 0. When SetLineDots has
// never been called with a positive value, the dot
// ranges are unknown and timer 0 fires only for a
// compare of 0 (on whatever line is ticked). This is a
// deliberate simplification of the hardware counter,
// which counts HBlank-IN pulses from VBlank-OUT and
// compares against T0C as a line count; the dot model
// is the one the brief specifies, and it agrees with
// the hardware model when the dots per line are treated
// as one unit.
//
// Timer 1 model: timer 1 counts lines. With the T1MD
// mode bit clear it counts every ticked line; with the
// mode bit set it counts only lines on which timer 0
// fired (the manual's "occurs only at lines designated
// by timer 0"). When the counter reaches the T1S value
// the SCU raises IntTimer1 and the counter resets to
// zero, so timer 1 fires repeatedly with a period of
// T1S qualifying lines. A T1S of 0 fires on every
// qualifying line. The manual's timer 1 is a countdown
// in dot clocks from a value reloaded each HBlank; the
// line counting model here is the brief's, with the
// same observable interrupt cadence at line level.
//
// The T1MD enable bit (bit 0) gates timer 1, as the
// manual specifies: with it clear, timer 1 never counts
// or fires. That is the power on state, so a machine
// that never programs T1MD sees no timer 1 interrupts;
// software sets the enable bit when it programs T1S.
// (The SAT-3 SCU first shipped without the gate; the
// system level masked interrupt gate caught it, because
// an always on timer 1 with T1S 0 fires every line.)
// Firing raises the interrupt source, which also
// latches the matching DMA start factor (see Raise).

// Timer register page offsets.
const (
	offT0C  = 0x90
	offT1S  = 0x94
	offT1MD = 0x98
)

// SetLineDots records how many display dots one
// scanline spans, for the timer 0 dot range model.
// A nonpositive value disables the dot ranges (timer 0
// then fires only for a compare of 0).
func (s *SCU) SetLineDots(dots int) {
	if dots < 0 {
		dots = 0
	}
	s.lineDots = dots
}

// TickLine advances the timers by one scanline. The
// line argument is the scanline index within the frame.
func (s *SCU) TickLine(line int) {
	s.lastLine = line

	compare := int(s.word(offT0C) & 0x3FF)
	fired0 := false
	if s.lineDots > 0 {
		lo := line * s.lineDots
		if compare >= lo && compare < lo+s.lineDots {
			fired0 = true
		}
	} else if compare == 0 {
		fired0 = true
	}
	if fired0 {
		s.Raise(IntTimer0)
	}

	if s.word(offT1MD)&1 == 0 {
		return // timer 1 disabled (T1MD enable bit clear)
	}
	modeAtTimer0 := s.word(offT1MD)&(1<<8) != 0
	if modeAtTimer0 && !fired0 {
		return
	}
	s.t1Counter++
	set := int(s.word(offT1S) & 0x1FF)
	if set == 0 || s.t1Counter >= set {
		s.Raise(IntTimer1)
		s.t1Counter = 0
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/smpc/smpc.go ====================

// Package smpc models the Sega Saturn SMPC (System Manager and
// Peripheral Control): the command processor behind the 128 byte
// register page owned by the bus, a battery backed real time clock,
// four bytes of battery backed SMPC memory (SMEM), and the INTBACK
// status and peripheral reports for two standard digital pads.
//
// Register page layout: the page indices are the documented offsets
// within the SMPC window (bus base 0x00100000), so IREG0 is page
// offset 0x01, COMREG is 0x1F, OREG0 is 0x21, OREG31 is 0x5F, SR is
// 0x61 and SF is 0x63. Only odd offsets carry data on the bus; the
// even bytes of the page are unused storage here.
//
// Command timing model: Poll is called once per scanline. A command
// is pending when COMREG differs from the last polled value, or
// when software has set SF in the page again for a repeat of the
// same command code. A pending command executes instantly inside
// that Poll, SF reads 1 in the page for the rest of that Poll, and
// SF is cleared at the next Poll. That one Poll of SF latency is
// the whole timing model; the microsecond execution times in the
// manual are not modelled.
//
// INTBACK model: the manual splits INTBACK into a status report
// and peripheral data, gated independently. IREG0 low bits select
// the status report (00H means no status, 01H means status), IREG1
// bit 3 (PEN) enables peripheral data, IREG0 bits 7 to 4 select the
// per port data modes, and IREG2 is written F0H. Continuation on
// real hardware is requested by toggling IREG0 bit 7 and a break
// by setting IREG0 bit 6; in this Poll driven model a continuation
// is a fresh INTBACK command issued while a report sequence is
// still pending, and IREG0 bit 6 on such a call aborts the
// sequence. Reports are emitted one chunk per INTBACK call: the
// status chunk first when selected, then one chunk per port. SR
// carries the manual continuation bits (PDE in the status phase,
// NPE and PDL in the peripheral phase) and OREG31 carries the
// command echo 10H at the end of a sequence and F0H while chunks
// remain; the manual leaves OREG31 during peripheral data
// explicitly overwritable, and F0H is the remaining marker chosen
// for this core.
//
// Simplifications, stated plainly:
//
//   - PDR1 and PDR2 (page offsets 0x75 and 0x77) stay plain storage
//     bytes. Driving them needs the SH-2 direct port mode and the
//     INTBACK port mode setup, which are out of scope here; pads
//     are read through INTBACK reports and SetPad.
//   - SYSRES only records a reset request (see ResetRequested).
//     The system owns the actual machine reset.
//   - The reset button is never pressed in this core, so the SR
//     RESB bit and the status report reset data always read 0.
//   - The cartridge code always reads 0 (no cartridge). The area
//     code is fixed at 04H, North America, from the manual table.
//   - SETTIME takes the weekday from the date itself. The manual
//     leaves an inconsistent weekday undefined; deriving it keeps
//     the clock self consistent as Advance rolls the days.
//   - The power on clock is 1994-01-01 00:00:00, a Saturday. That
//     is one second past the manual cold reset value of Friday
//     1993-12-31 23:59:59, stated here so the default is pinned.
package smpc

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
)

// Register page offsets. The page is the slice returned by
// bus.SMPCRegisters; indices match the documented SMPC window
// offsets.
const (
	OffIREG0  = 0x01
	OffIREG1  = 0x03
	OffIREG2  = 0x05
	OffIREG3  = 0x07
	OffIREG4  = 0x09
	OffIREG5  = 0x0B
	OffIREG6  = 0x0D
	OffCOMREG = 0x1F
	OffOREG0  = 0x21
	OffOREG31 = 0x5F
	OffSR     = 0x61
	OffSF     = 0x63
	OffPDR1   = 0x75
	OffPDR2   = 0x77
)

// oregOff returns the page offset of OREG n.
func oregOff(n int) int { return OffOREG0 + 2*n }

// Command codes, from the SMPC command list in the manual.
const (
	CmdMSHON    = 0x00
	CmdSSHON    = 0x02
	CmdSSHOFF   = 0x03
	CmdSNDON    = 0x06
	CmdSNDOFF   = 0x07
	CmdCDON     = 0x08
	CmdCDOFF    = 0x09
	CmdSYSRES   = 0x0D
	CmdCKCHG352 = 0x0E
	CmdCKCHG320 = 0x0F
	CmdINTBACK  = 0x10
	CmdSETTIME  = 0x16
	CmdSETSMEM  = 0x17
	CmdNMIREQ   = 0x18
	CmdRESENAB  = 0x19
	CmdRESDISA  = 0x1A
)

// AreaNorthAmerica is the INTBACK area code this machine reports:
// 04H in the manual area code table (United States, Canada and
// the Latin America NTSC region).
const AreaNorthAmerica = 0x04

// Pad button bits, in the system PadState order used by SetPad.
// The values match the system package button constants.
const (
	BtnUp    = 1 << 0
	BtnDown  = 1 << 1
	BtnLeft  = 1 << 2
	BtnRight = 1 << 3
	BtnA     = 1 << 4
	BtnB     = 1 << 5
	BtnC     = 1 << 6
	BtnX     = 1 << 7
	BtnY     = 1 << 8
	BtnZ     = 1 << 9
	BtnL     = 1 << 10
	BtnR     = 1 << 11
	BtnStart = 1 << 12
)

// ClockCyclesPerSecond is the machine cycle rate the RTC advance
// counts against: 28.6364 MHz.
const ClockCyclesPerSecond = 28636400

// Hooks carries the machine level effects of the reset system
// commands out of this package. Any hook left nil is skipped, so a
// partially wired system still runs every other command.
type Hooks struct {
	OnSSHON  func() // release the slave SH-2 from reset
	OnSSHOFF func() // hold and reset the slave SH-2
	OnNMIReq func() // raise NMI to the master SH-2
	OnSNDON  func() // release the SCSP 68EC000 from reset
	OnSNDOFF func() // hold the SCSP 68EC000 in reset
	OnCDOn   func() // CD block power on
	OnCDOff  func() // CD block power off
}

// Report sequence stages for a pending INTBACK sequence.
const (
	stageIdle      = 0 // no sequence pending
	stagePort0     = 1 // port 0 chunk is next
	stagePort1     = 2 // port 1 chunk is next
	stagePort1Only = 3 // port 1 chunk is next, port 0 was skipped
)

// SMPC is the command processor view over the bus SMPC page.
type SMPC struct {
	page  []byte
	hooks Hooks

	lastPolled byte // COMREG value seen at the previous Poll
	sfBusy     bool // SF was set by the executing Poll, clear next Poll

	clock352      bool
	resetEnabled  bool
	resetReq      bool
	timeSet       bool // STE: SETTIME ran since power on
	sndOn         bool
	cdOn          bool
	unknown       int
	portModes     byte // SR low bits: P2MD and P1MD of the last INTBACK
	stage         int  // pending INTBACK report stage
	statusPhaseSR bool // SR shows the status phase layout

	days   int64 // RTC day count, days since 1970-01-01
	secDay int   // RTC seconds into the day, 0 to 86399
	cycRem int   // sub second cycle remainder for Advance
	smem   [4]byte
	pads   [2]uint16
}

// New wraps the 128 byte bus SMPC page. The clock starts at the
// power on value 1994-01-01 00:00:00, the clock mode at 320, and
// the reset button NMI path enabled, matching the boot ROM
// defaults the manual describes.
func New(page []byte, hooks Hooks) *SMPC {
	s := &SMPC{page: page, hooks: hooks, resetEnabled: true}
	s.days = daysFromCivil(1994, 1, 1)
	s.lastPolled = page[OffCOMREG]
	s.syncSR()
	return s
}

// Poll runs the per scanline command check described in the
// package comment.
func (s *SMPC) Poll() {
	if s.sfBusy {
		s.page[OffSF] = 0
		s.sfBusy = false
		s.lastPolled = s.page[OffCOMREG]
		s.syncSR()
		return
	}
	cur := s.page[OffCOMREG]
	repeat := s.page[OffSF]&1 != 0
	if cur == s.lastPolled && !repeat {
		s.syncSR()
		return
	}
	s.lastPolled = cur
	s.execute(cur)
	s.page[OffSF] = 1
	s.sfBusy = true
	s.syncSR()
}

// execute runs one command code instantly.
func (s *SMPC) execute(cmd byte) {
	// Every command echoes its code into OREG31 when processing
	// begins. INTBACK may overwrite OREG31 with its remaining
	// marker while a report sequence is pending.
	s.page[OffOREG31] = cmd
	switch cmd {
	case CmdMSHON:
		// Master SH-2 on: no state change in this core. The
		// master is the CPU issuing the command.
	case CmdSSHON:
		if s.hooks.OnSSHON != nil {
			s.hooks.OnSSHON()
		}
	case CmdSSHOFF:
		if s.hooks.OnSSHOFF != nil {
			s.hooks.OnSSHOFF()
		}
	case CmdSNDON:
		s.sndOn = true
		if s.hooks.OnSNDON != nil {
			s.hooks.OnSNDON()
		}
	case CmdSNDOFF:
		s.sndOn = false
		if s.hooks.OnSNDOFF != nil {
			s.hooks.OnSNDOFF()
		}
	case CmdCDON:
		s.cdOn = true
		if s.hooks.OnCDOn != nil {
			s.hooks.OnCDOn()
		}
	case CmdCDOFF:
		s.cdOn = false
		if s.hooks.OnCDOff != nil {
			s.hooks.OnCDOff()
		}
	case CmdSYSRES:
		s.resetReq = true
	case CmdCKCHG352:
		s.clock352 = true
	case CmdCKCHG320:
		s.clock352 = false
	case CmdINTBACK:
		s.intback()
	case CmdSETTIME:
		s.setTime()
	case CmdSETSMEM:
		s.smem[0] = s.page[OffIREG0]
		s.smem[1] = s.page[OffIREG0+2]
		s.smem[2] = s.page[OffIREG0+4]
		s.smem[3] = s.page[OffIREG0+6]
	case CmdNMIREQ:
		if s.hooks.OnNMIReq != nil {
			s.hooks.OnNMIReq()
		}
	case CmdRESENAB:
		s.resetEnabled = true
	case CmdRESDISA:
		s.resetEnabled = false
	default:
		s.unknown++
	}
}

// ResetRequested reports whether SYSRES has asked for a whole
// system reset. The flag latches; the system owns the reset and
// any clearing policy.
func (s *SMPC) ResetRequested() bool { return s.resetReq }

// ClockMode returns the current clock mode: 352 or 320.
func (s *SMPC) ClockMode() int {
	if s.clock352 {
		return 352
	}
	return 320
}

// UnknownCommands returns how many unrecognised command codes
// have been executed, for diagnostics.
func (s *SMPC) UnknownCommands() int { return s.unknown }

// syncSR rewrites the SR page byte from the current phase state.
// In the peripheral phase SR follows the manual peripheral
// control layout: bit 7 set, PDL, NPE, RESB (always 0 here) and
// the two port mode fields. In the status phase SR follows the
// manual status layout: bit 6 set, PDE for remaining peripheral
// data, and RESB. Outside an INTBACK sequence the peripheral
// layout reads with NPE clear.
func (s *SMPC) syncSR() {
	if s.statusPhaseSR {
		v := byte(0x40)
		if s.stage != stageIdle {
			v |= 0x20 // PDE: peripheral data remaining
		}
		s.page[OffSR] = v
		return
	}
	v := byte(0x80) | s.portModes
	if s.stage != stageIdle {
		v |= 0x20 // NPE: peripheral data remaining
	}
	if s.stage == stagePort1 || s.stage == stagePort1Only {
		v |= 0x40 // PDL: the peripheral data present is the first port group
	}
	s.page[OffSR] = v
}

// intback runs one INTBACK call: the next chunk of the pending
// report sequence, or the start of a new sequence.
func (s *SMPC) intback() {
	ireg0 := s.page[OffIREG0]
	ireg1 := s.page[OffIREG1]
	if s.stage != stageIdle {
		if ireg0&0x40 != 0 {
			// Break request: drop the rest of the sequence.
			s.stage = stageIdle
			s.statusPhaseSR = false
			s.page[OffOREG31] = CmdINTBACK
			return
		}
		s.emitPortChunk()
		return
	}
	// New sequence. Record the port modes for SR: IREG0 holds
	// P2MD in bits 7 to 6 and P1MD in bits 5 to 4; SR holds
	// P2MD in bits 3 to 2 and P1MD in bits 1 to 0.
	s.portModes = (ireg0 >> 4) & 0x0F
	wantStatus := ireg0&0x0F != 0
	pen := ireg1&0x08 != 0
	// Build the port queue, skipping ports in 0 byte mode.
	var ports []int
	if pen {
		if (ireg0>>4)&0x03 != 0x03 {
			ports = append(ports, 0)
		}
		if (ireg0>>6)&0x03 != 0x03 {
			ports = append(ports, 1)
		}
	}
	switch {
	case wantStatus:
		s.writeStatusReport()
		s.statusPhaseSR = true
		s.stage = stageForPorts(ports)
		if s.stage == stageIdle {
			s.page[OffOREG31] = CmdINTBACK
		} else {
			s.page[OffOREG31] = 0xF0
		}
	case len(ports) > 0:
		s.statusPhaseSR = false
		s.stage = stageForPorts(ports[1:])
		s.emitPortData(ports[0])
		if s.stage == stageIdle {
			s.page[OffOREG31] = CmdINTBACK
		} else {
			s.page[OffOREG31] = 0xF0
		}
	default:
		s.statusPhaseSR = false
		s.page[OffOREG31] = CmdINTBACK
	}
}

// stageForPorts maps the ports still to emit onto a stage value.
func stageForPorts(ports []int) int {
	if len(ports) == 0 {
		return stageIdle
	}
	if ports[0] == 0 {
		return stagePort0
	}
	return stagePort1Only
}

// emitPortChunk emits the chunk for the port named by the stage
// and advances the sequence.
func (s *SMPC) emitPortChunk() {
	s.statusPhaseSR = false
	switch s.stage {
	case stagePort0:
		s.emitPortData(0)
		s.stage = stagePort1
		s.page[OffOREG31] = 0xF0
	case stagePort1, stagePort1Only:
		s.emitPortData(1)
		s.stage = stageIdle
		s.page[OffOREG31] = CmdINTBACK
	}
}

// writeStatusReport writes the 16 byte status report into OREG0
// to OREG15. The layout follows the manual INTBACK result table:
// OREG0 status flags, OREG1 to OREG7 the RTC, OREG8 the
// cartridge code, OREG9 the area code, OREG10 and OREG11 the
// system status words, and OREG12 to OREG15 the SMEM bytes.
func (s *SMPC) writeStatusReport() {
	y, mo, d, wd, hh, mm, ss := s.rtcFields()
	var st byte
	if s.timeSet {
		st |= 0x80 // STE
	}
	if !s.resetEnabled {
		st |= 0x40 // RESD
	}
	s.page[oregOff(0)] = st
	s.page[oregOff(1)] = toBCD(y / 100)
	s.page[oregOff(2)] = toBCD(y % 100)
	// Weekday in the high nibble, month in the low nibble. Both
	// are plain hex values in the manual, not BCD: Sunday is 0
	// and December is 0x0C.
	s.page[oregOff(3)] = byte(wd<<4 | mo)
	s.page[oregOff(4)] = toBCD(d)
	s.page[oregOff(5)] = toBCD(hh)
	s.page[oregOff(6)] = toBCD(mm)
	s.page[oregOff(7)] = toBCD(ss)
	s.page[oregOff(8)] = 0 // cartridge code: no cartridge
	s.page[oregOff(9)] = AreaNorthAmerica
	// System status 1: fixed bits 5, 4 and 2 read 1, DOTSEL in
	// bit 6 follows the clock mode, and SNDRES in bit 0 reads 1
	// while the sound CPU is held in reset (sound off). The
	// MSHNMI and SYSRES signal bits read 0 in this core.
	var ss1 byte = 0x34
	if s.clock352 {
		ss1 |= 0x40
	}
	if !s.sndOn {
		ss1 |= 0x01
	}
	s.page[oregOff(10)] = ss1
	// System status 2: CDRES in bit 6 reads 1 while the CD block
	// is held in reset (CD off).
	var ss2 byte
	if !s.cdOn {
		ss2 |= 0x40
	}
	s.page[oregOff(11)] = ss2
	for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
		s.page[oregOff(12+i)] = s.smem[i]
	}
}

// emitPortData writes one port report chunk at OREG0: the port
// status byte, the Saturn peripheral ID byte, and the pad data
// bytes. The port status for a directly connected pad is F1H:
// multitap ID F in the high nibble and one connector in the low
// nibble. The peripheral ID for the standard digital device is
// 02H: peripheral type 0 in the high nibble and a data size of 2
// in the low nibble. The pad data follows the manual Saturn
// digital device format and is active low: a pressed button
// reads 0. Data byte 1 is Right, Left, Down, Up, Start, A, C, B
// in bits 7 to 0. Data byte 2 is R, X, Y, Z, L in bits 7 to 3
// with the three extended bits reading 1 (unpressed).
func (s *SMPC) emitPortData(port int) {
	m := s.pads[port]
	s.page[oregOff(0)] = 0xF1
	s.page[oregOff(1)] = 0x02
	var d1 byte = 0xFF
	if m&BtnRight != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 7
	}
	if m&BtnLeft != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 6
	}
	if m&BtnDown != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 5
	}
	if m&BtnUp != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 4
	}
	if m&BtnStart != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 3
	}
	if m&BtnA != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 2
	}
	if m&BtnC != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 1
	}
	if m&BtnB != 0 {
		d1 &^= 1 << 0
	}
	s.page[oregOff(2)] = d1
	var d2 byte = 0xFF
	if m&BtnR != 0 {
		d2 &^= 1 << 7
	}
	if m&BtnX != 0 {
		d2 &^= 1 << 6
	}
	if m&BtnY != 0 {
		d2 &^= 1 << 5
	}
	if m&BtnZ != 0 {
		d2 &^= 1 << 4
	}
	if m&BtnL != 0 {
		d2 &^= 1 << 3
	}
	s.page[oregOff(3)] = d2
}

// SetPad stores the button mask for a port: 0 or 1. Other port
// numbers are ignored. Button bits use the PadState order in the
// Btn constants.
func (s *SMPC) SetPad(port int, buttons uint16) {
	if port == 0 || port == 1 {
		s.pads[port] = buttons
	}
}

// setTime applies a SETTIME command. IREG0 and IREG1 are the year
// as two BCD bytes (century digits, then year digits). IREG2
// packs the weekday in its high nibble and the month in its low
// nibble, both plain hex. IREG3 to IREG6 are day, hour, minute
// and second in BCD. The supplied weekday is not trusted: the
// clock derives the weekday from the date. An out of range field
// makes the command a no-op, where the manual leaves the result
// undefined.
func (s *SMPC) setTime() {
	y := fromBCD(s.page[OffIREG0])*100 + fromBCD(s.page[OffIREG0+2])
	packed := s.page[OffIREG0+4]
	mo := int(packed & 0x0F)
	d := fromBCD(s.page[OffIREG0+6])
	hh := fromBCD(s.page[OffIREG0+8])
	mm := fromBCD(s.page[OffIREG0+10])
	ss := fromBCD(s.page[OffIREG0+12])
	if mo < 1 || mo > 12 || d < 1 || d > 31 || hh > 23 || mm > 59 || ss > 59 {
		return
	}
	s.days = daysFromCivil(y, mo, d)
	s.secDay = hh*3600 + mm*60 + ss
	s.cycRem = 0
	s.timeSet = true
}

// Advance moves the RTC forward by whole machine cycles. Cycles
// accumulate into a sub second remainder so repeated small calls
// still track real time. Negative counts are ignored.
func (s *SMPC) Advance(cycles int) {
	if cycles <= 0 {
		return
	}
	s.cycRem += cycles
	secs := s.cycRem / ClockCyclesPerSecond
	s.cycRem %= ClockCyclesPerSecond
	if secs == 0 {
		return
	}
	s.secDay += secs
	for s.secDay >= 86400 {
		s.secDay -= 86400
		s.days++
	}
}

// rtcFields derives the calendar fields from the day count and
// the seconds into the day. Weekday uses the manual numbering:
// Sunday 0 through Saturday 6. 1970-01-01 was a Thursday, which
// anchors the weekday arithmetic.
func (s *SMPC) rtcFields() (y, mo, d, wd, hh, mm, ss int) {
	y, mo, d = civilFromDays(s.days)
	wd = int(((s.days+4)%7 + 7) % 7)
	hh = s.secDay / 3600
	mm = s.secDay % 3600 / 60
	ss = s.secDay % 60
	return y, mo, d, wd, hh, mm, ss
}

// toBCD converts a value in the range 0 to 99 to BCD.
func toBCD(v int) byte {
	return byte((v/10)<<4 | (v % 10))
}

// fromBCD converts a BCD byte back to an integer.
func fromBCD(b byte) int {
	return int(b>>4)*10 + int(b&0x0F)
}

// daysFromCivil returns the day count since 1970-01-01 for a
// Gregorian date, using the standard civil calendar arithmetic.
func daysFromCivil(y, m, d int) int64 {
	if m <= 2 {
		y--
	}
	era := floorDiv(y, 400)
	yoe := y - era*400
	mp := m - 3
	if m <= 2 {
		mp = m + 9
	}
	doy := (153*mp+2)/5 + d - 1
	doe := yoe*365 + yoe/4 - yoe/100 + doy
	return int64(era)*146097 + int64(doe) - 719468
}

// civilFromDays is the inverse of daysFromCivil.
func civilFromDays(z int64) (y, m, d int) {
	z += 719468
	era := floorDiv64(z, 146097)
	doe := int(z - era*146097)
	yoe := (doe - doe/1460 + doe/36524 - doe/146096) / 365
	yy := yoe + int(era)*400
	doy := doe - (365*yoe + yoe/4 - yoe/100)
	mp := (5*doy + 2) / 153
	d = doy - (153*mp+2)/5 + 1
	if mp < 10 {
		m = mp + 3
	} else {
		m = mp - 9
	}
	y = yy
	if m <= 2 {
		y = yy + 1
	}
	return y, m, d
}

func floorDiv(a, b int) int {
	q := a / b
	if a%b != 0 && (a < 0) != (b < 0) {
		q--
	}
	return q
}

func floorDiv64(a, b int64) int64 {
	q := a / b
	if a%b != 0 && (a < 0) != (b < 0) {
		q--
	}
	return q
}

// Serialized layout, SerializeSize bytes, big endian:
//
//	byte 0: version (1)
//	byte 1: flags: bit 0 reset enabled, bit 1 time set (STE),
//	  bit 2 clock 352 mode, bit 3 reset requested,
//	  bit 4 sound on, bit 5 CD on, bit 6 status phase SR,
//	  bit 7 SF busy
//	bytes 2 to 5: RTC day count since 1970-01-01
//	bytes 6 to 9: RTC seconds into the day
//	bytes 10 to 13: sub second cycle remainder
//	bytes 14 to 17: unknown command count
//	bytes 18 to 19: port 0 pad mask
//	bytes 20 to 21: port 1 pad mask
//	bytes 22 to 25: SMEM bytes
//	byte 26: last executed command code
//	byte 27: report sequence stage
//	byte 28: last polled COMREG value
//	byte 29: SR port mode bits
//	bytes 30 to 31: zero
const stateVersion = 1

// SerializeSize is the exact size of a serialized SMPC.
const SerializeSize = 32

// Serialize writes the SMPC internal state in the layout above.
// The register page itself belongs to the bus and is saved by the
// system state, not duplicated here.
func (s *SMPC) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	out[0] = stateVersion
	if s.resetEnabled {
		out[1] |= 1 << 0
	}
	if s.timeSet {
		out[1] |= 1 << 1
	}
	if s.clock352 {
		out[1] |= 1 << 2
	}
	if s.resetReq {
		out[1] |= 1 << 3
	}
	if s.sndOn {
		out[1] |= 1 << 4
	}
	if s.cdOn {
		out[1] |= 1 << 5
	}
	if s.statusPhaseSR {
		out[1] |= 1 << 6
	}
	if s.sfBusy {
		out[1] |= 1 << 7
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[2:6], uint32(int32(s.days)))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[6:10], uint32(s.secDay))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[10:14], uint32(s.cycRem))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[14:18], uint32(s.unknown))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[18:20], s.pads[0])
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[20:22], s.pads[1])
	copy(out[22:26], s.smem[:])
	out[26] = s.page[OffOREG31]
	if s.stage != stageIdle {
		out[26] = s.lastPolled
	}
	out[27] = byte(s.stage)
	out[28] = s.lastPolled
	out[29] = s.portModes
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize. After a
// restore the poll tracker resyncs to the page COMREG value, so
// a state saved mid sequence does not re-execute its command.
func (s *SMPC) Deserialize(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) != SerializeSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("smpc: state size %d, want %d", len(data), SerializeSize)
	}
	if data[0] != stateVersion {
		return fmt.Errorf("smpc: state version %d, want %d", data[0], stateVersion)
	}
	s.resetEnabled = data[1]&(1<<0) != 0
	s.timeSet = data[1]&(1<<1) != 0
	s.clock352 = data[1]&(1<<2) != 0
	s.resetReq = data[1]&(1<<3) != 0
	s.sndOn = data[1]&(1<<4) != 0
	s.cdOn = data[1]&(1<<5) != 0
	s.statusPhaseSR = data[1]&(1<<6) != 0
	s.sfBusy = data[1]&(1<<7) != 0
	s.days = int64(int32(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[2:6])))
	s.secDay = int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[6:10]))
	s.cycRem = int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[10:14]))
	s.unknown = int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[14:18]))
	s.pads[0] = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[18:20])
	s.pads[1] = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[20:22])
	copy(s.smem[:], data[22:26])
	s.stage = int(data[27])
	s.portModes = data[29]
	s.lastPolled = s.page[OffCOMREG]
	s.syncSR()
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/smpc/smpc_test.go ====================

package smpc

import "testing"

// newTestSMPC builds an SMPC over a fresh zeroed 128 byte page.
func newTestSMPC(hooks Hooks) (*SMPC, []byte) {
	page := make([]byte, 128)
	return New(page, hooks), page
}

// issueCmd writes cmd to COMREG and runs the two Polls of the
// command timing model: the executing Poll leaves SF reading 1,
// the next Poll clears it to 0.
func issueCmd(t *testing.T, s *SMPC, page []byte, cmd byte) {
	t.Helper()
	page[OffCOMREG] = cmd
	s.Poll()
	if got := page[OffSF]; got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("cmd %02X: SF after executing Poll = %d, want 1", cmd, got)
	}
	s.Poll()
	if got := page[OffSF]; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("cmd %02X: SF after next Poll = %d, want 0", cmd, got)
	}
}

// repeatCmd reissues the command code already sitting in COMREG
// by setting SF again, the repeat path of the Poll model, and
// runs the same two Polls.
func repeatCmd(t *testing.T, s *SMPC, page []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	page[OffSF] = 1
	s.Poll()
	if got := page[OffSF]; got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("repeat: SF after executing Poll = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	s.Poll()
	if got := page[OffSF]; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("repeat: SF after next Poll = %d, want 0", got)
	}
}

// setIREGs loads the seven input registers.
func setIREGs(page []byte, v [7]byte) {
	for i, b := range v {
		page[OffIREG0+2*i] = b
	}
}

// intbackStatus runs a status only INTBACK (IREG0 01H, PEN off,
// IREG2 F0H) and leaves the status report in the OREG block.
func intbackStatus(t *testing.T, s *SMPC, page []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	setIREGs(page, [7]byte{0x01, 0x00, 0xF0, 0, 0, 0, 0})
	issueCmd(t, s, page, CmdINTBACK)
}

func oreg(page []byte, n int) byte { return page[oregOff(n)] }

// setLeapTime loads SETTIME for 2024-02-29 and issues it. The
// date is a Thursday, weekday 4 in the manual numbering with
// Sunday as 0, so IREG2 packs weekday 4 and month 2 as 42H.
func setLeapTime(t *testing.T, s *SMPC, page []byte, hh, mm, ss byte) {
	t.Helper()
	setIREGs(page, [7]byte{0x20, 0x24, 0x42, 0x29, hh, mm, ss})
	issueCmd(t, s, page, CmdSETTIME)
}

type hookCounts struct {
	sshon, sshoff, nmi, sndon, sndoff, cdon, cdoff int
}

func (c *hookCounts) hooks() Hooks {
	return Hooks{
		OnSSHON:  func() { c.sshon++ },
		OnSSHOFF: func() { c.sshoff++ },
		OnNMIReq: func() { c.nmi++ },
		OnSNDON:  func() { c.sndon++ },
		OnSNDOFF: func() { c.sndoff++ },
		OnCDOn:   func() { c.cdon++ },
		OnCDOff:  func() { c.cdoff++ },
	}
}

func (c *hookCounts) total() int {
	return c.sshon + c.sshoff + c.nmi + c.sndon + c.sndoff + c.cdon + c.cdoff
}

// TestHookCommandsFireOnce covers task item (a): each hook
// command fires its hook exactly once per COMREG write, SF reads
// 1 after the executing Poll and 0 after the next.
func TestHookCommandsFireOnce(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		cmd  byte
		pick func(*hookCounts) int
	}{
		{"SSHON", CmdSSHON, func(c *hookCounts) int { return c.sshon }},
		{"SSHOFF", CmdSSHOFF, func(c *hookCounts) int { return c.sshoff }},
		{"SNDON", CmdSNDON, func(c *hookCounts) int { return c.sndon }},
		{"SNDOFF", CmdSNDOFF, func(c *hookCounts) int { return c.sndoff }},
		{"CDON", CmdCDON, func(c *hookCounts) int { return c.cdon }},
		{"CDOFF", CmdCDOFF, func(c *hookCounts) int { return c.cdoff }},
		{"NMIREQ", CmdNMIREQ, func(c *hookCounts) int { return c.nmi }},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			counts := &hookCounts{}
			s, page := newTestSMPC(counts.hooks())
			page[OffCOMREG] = tc.cmd
			s.Poll()
			if got := page[OffSF]; got != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("SF after executing Poll = %d, want 1", got)
			}
			if got := tc.pick(counts); got != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("hook fired %d times, want 1", got)
			}
			if got := counts.total(); got != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("total hook firings = %d, want 1 (no other hook may fire)", got)
			}
			s.Poll()
			if got := page[OffSF]; got != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("SF after next Poll = %d, want 0", got)
			}
			s.Poll()
			if got := tc.pick(counts); got != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("hook refired on idle Polls: %d firings, want 1", got)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestSetTimeThenIntbackStatus covers task item (b): SETTIME
// then an INTBACK status report returns the exact date bytes at
// the manual offsets. 2024-02-29 23:59:30, a Thursday.
func TestSetTimeThenIntbackStatus(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newTestSMPC(Hooks{})
	setLeapTime(t, s, page, 0x23, 0x59, 0x30)
	intbackStatus(t, s, page)
	want := map[int]byte{
		0:  0x80,                               // STE set, RESD clear (reset enabled)
		1:  0x20,                               // year century digits, BCD
		2:  0x24,                               // year low digits, BCD
		3:  0x42,                               // weekday 4 (Thursday) high nibble, month 2 low nibble, plain hex
		4:  0x29,                               // day, BCD
		5:  0x23,                               // hour, BCD
		6:  0x59,                               // minute, BCD
		7:  0x30,                               // second, BCD
		8:  0x00,                               // cartridge code: none
		9:  0x04,                               // area code: North America
		10: 0x35,                               // system status 1: fixed bits plus SNDRES (sound held in reset)
		11: 0x40,                               // system status 2: CDRES (CD block held in reset)
		12: 0x00, 13: 0x00, 14: 0x00, 15: 0x00, // SMEM, never set
	}
	for n, w := range want {
		if got := oreg(page, n); got != w {
			t.Errorf("OREG%d = %02X, want %02X", n, got, w)
		}
	}
	if got := page[OffOREG31]; got != CmdINTBACK {
		t.Errorf("OREG31 = %02X, want %02X (INTBACK echo at end of sequence)", got, CmdINTBACK)
	}
	if got := page[OffSR]; got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("SR = %02X, want 40 (status phase, nothing pending)", got)
	}
}

// TestAdvanceRollsMinuteAndDay covers task item (c): advancing
// 61 seconds of machine cycles from 23:59:30 rolls the minute,
// the hour, the day, the weekday and the month, verified through
// a second INTBACK status report.
func TestAdvanceRollsMinuteAndDay(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newTestSMPC(Hooks{})
	setLeapTime(t, s, page, 0x23, 0x59, 0x30)
	intbackStatus(t, s, page)
	s.Advance(ClockCyclesPerSecond * 61)
	// COMREG still holds INTBACK; reissue through the SF repeat
	// path for a fresh status report.
	repeatCmd(t, s, page)
	want := map[int]byte{
		1: 0x20, 2: 0x24, // still 2024
		3: 0x53, // weekday 5 (Friday), month 3
		4: 0x01, // day 1
		5: 0x00, // hour 0
		6: 0x00, // minute 0: the 61st second crossed 00:00
		7: 0x31, // second 31
	}
	for n, w := range want {
		if got := oreg(page, n); got != w {
			t.Errorf("after Advance: OREG%d = %02X, want %02X", n, got, w)
		}
	}
}

// TestPadReports covers task item (d): two pads report in the
// manual peripheral chunk layout across the continuation call,
// and OREG31 reaches the manual end value 10H. Pad data is
// active low: a pressed button reads 0.
func TestPadReports(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newTestSMPC(Hooks{})
	s.SetPad(0, BtnStart|BtnA|BtnR)
	s.SetPad(1, BtnB|BtnL)
	// Peripheral only INTBACK: IREG0 00H (no status, both port
	// modes 0 in bits 7 to 4), IREG1 PEN set, IREG2 F0H.
	setIREGs(page, [7]byte{0x00, 0x08, 0xF0, 0, 0, 0, 0})
	issueCmd(t, s, page, CmdINTBACK)
	// First chunk is port 0.
	if got := oreg(page, 0); got != 0xF1 {
		t.Errorf("port 0 status byte = %02X, want F1 (multitap ID F, 1 connector)", got)
	}
	if got := oreg(page, 1); got != 0x02 {
		t.Errorf("port 0 peripheral ID = %02X, want 02 (type 0, data size 2)", got)
	}
	// Data byte 1: Start (bit 3) and A (bit 2) pressed read 0.
	if got := oreg(page, 2); got != 0xF3 {
		t.Errorf("port 0 data byte 1 = %02X, want F3", got)
	}
	// Data byte 2: R (bit 7) pressed reads 0.
	if got := oreg(page, 3); got != 0x7F {
		t.Errorf("port 0 data byte 2 = %02X, want 7F", got)
	}
	if got := page[OffOREG31]; got != 0xF0 {
		t.Errorf("OREG31 mid sequence = %02X, want F0 (chunks remain)", got)
	}
	if got := page[OffSR]; got != 0xE0 {
		t.Errorf("SR mid sequence = %02X, want E0 (peripheral phase, NPE and PDL set)", got)
	}
	// Continuation: IREG0 80H is the manual continue request.
	page[OffIREG0] = 0x80
	repeatCmd(t, s, page)
	// Second chunk is port 1.
	if got := oreg(page, 0); got != 0xF1 {
		t.Errorf("port 1 status byte = %02X, want F1", got)
	}
	if got := oreg(page, 1); got != 0x02 {
		t.Errorf("port 1 peripheral ID = %02X, want 02", got)
	}
	// Data byte 1: B (bit 0) pressed reads 0.
	if got := oreg(page, 2); got != 0xFE {
		t.Errorf("port 1 data byte 1 = %02X, want FE", got)
	}
	// Data byte 2: L (bit 3) pressed reads 0.
	if got := oreg(page, 3); got != 0xF7 {
		t.Errorf("port 1 data byte 2 = %02X, want F7", got)
	}
	if got := page[OffOREG31]; got != CmdINTBACK {
		t.Errorf("OREG31 at end = %02X, want %02X (manual end value: command echo)", got, CmdINTBACK)
	}
	if got := page[OffSR]; got != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("SR at end = %02X, want 80 (peripheral phase, nothing pending)", got)
	}

	// A port in 0 byte mode (mode 3 in IREG0 bits 7 to 4) is
	// skipped: with port 1 in 0 byte mode the sequence ends with
	// the port 0 chunk and OREG31 reaches 10H at once.
	s2, page2 := newTestSMPC(Hooks{})
	s2.SetPad(0, BtnStart|BtnA|BtnR)
	s2.SetPad(1, BtnB|BtnL)
	setIREGs(page2, [7]byte{0xC0, 0x08, 0xF0, 0, 0, 0, 0})
	issueCmd(t, s2, page2, CmdINTBACK)
	if got := oreg(page2, 2); got != 0xF3 {
		t.Errorf("0 byte mode skip: first chunk data byte 1 = %02X, want F3 (port 0)", got)
	}
	if got := page2[OffOREG31]; got != CmdINTBACK {
		t.Errorf("0 byte mode skip: OREG31 = %02X, want %02X (sequence already ended)", got, CmdINTBACK)
	}
}

// TestSerializeRoundTrip covers task item (e): SETSMEM bytes, the
// RTC and the clock mode survive a Serialize/Deserialize round
// trip, verified through an INTBACK status report afterwards.
func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newTestSMPC(Hooks{})
	smem := [4]byte{0xA5, 0x3C, 0x7E, 0x19}
	setIREGs(page, [7]byte{smem[0], smem[1], smem[2], smem[3], 0, 0, 0})
	issueCmd(t, s, page, CmdSETSMEM)
	setLeapTime(t, s, page, 0x12, 0x34, 0x56)
	issueCmd(t, s, page, CmdCKCHG352)

	blob := s.Serialize()
	if len(blob) != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize size = %d, want %d", len(blob), SerializeSize)
	}
	s2, page2 := newTestSMPC(Hooks{})
	if err := s2.Deserialize(blob); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if got := s2.ClockMode(); got != 352 {
		t.Errorf("restored ClockMode = %d, want 352", got)
	}
	intbackStatus(t, s2, page2)
	wantRTC := map[int]byte{
		1: 0x20, 2: 0x24, 3: 0x42, 4: 0x29, 5: 0x12, 6: 0x34, 7: 0x56,
	}
	for n, w := range wantRTC {
		if got := oreg(page2, n); got != w {
			t.Errorf("restored OREG%d = %02X, want %02X", n, got, w)
		}
	}
	for i, w := range smem {
		if got := oreg(page2, 12+i); got != w {
			t.Errorf("restored SMEM byte %d at OREG%d = %02X, want %02X", i, 12+i, got, w)
		}
	}
	if got := oreg(page2, 0); got != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("restored OREG0 = %02X, want 80 (STE survived)", got)
	}
	if got := oreg(page2, 10); got != 0x75 {
		t.Errorf("restored OREG10 = %02X, want 75 (DOTSEL survived, SNDRES set)", got)
	}
}

// TestClockChange352 covers task item (f): CKCHG352 sets
// ClockMode 352, and the mode shows where the code models it:
// the DOTSEL bit of the INTBACK system status byte OREG10. SR
// itself carries no clock bit in this model; it keeps its
// documented phase layouts.
func TestClockChange352(t *testing.T) {
	s, page := newTestSMPC(Hooks{})
	if got := s.ClockMode(); got != 320 {
		t.Fatalf("power on ClockMode = %d, want 320", got)
	}
	issueCmd(t, s, page, CmdCKCHG352)
	if got := s.ClockMode(); got != 352 {
		t.Fatalf("ClockMode after CKCHG352 = %d, want 352", got)
	}
	if got := page[OffSR]; got != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("SR after CKCHG352 = %02X, want 80 (peripheral layout, modes 0, no clock bit)", got)
	}
	intbackStatus(t, s, page)
	if got := oreg(page, 10); got != 0x75 {
		t.Errorf("OREG10 = %02X, want 75 (fixed bits, DOTSEL for 352, SNDRES)", got)
	}
	if got := page[OffSR]; got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("SR after status INTBACK = %02X, want 40 (status phase layout)", got)
	}
	issueCmd(t, s, page, CmdCKCHG320)
	if got := s.ClockMode(); got != 320 {
		t.Errorf("ClockMode after CKCHG320 = %d, want 320", got)
	}
}

func TestUnknownCommand(t *testing.T) {
