==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/system/boot.go ====================

package system

import "fmt"

// HLE boot constants, from the published Saturn boot process.
//
// The boot ROM loads the initial program (IP) from the start
// of the disc data area into Work RAM-H at IPLoadAddress. The
// first 256 bytes of the loaded area are the System ID itself,
// and the boot ROM enters the IP at IPEntryAddress, the first
// byte after the System ID (the security code area of a
// licensed IP). On the way it copies the System ID to
// SysIDCopyAddress and the 32 parameter bytes at IP offset
// 0xE0 (the IP size, stack and first read fields) to
// BootParamsAddress, both in Work RAM-H, where system software
// reads them back. The master SH-2 stack comes from the
// System ID Stack-M field and the slave stack from Stack-S;
// the slave stays held in reset until the IP releases it with
// the SMPC SSHON command, as real software does.
const (
	IPLoadAddress     = 0x06002000
	IPEntryAddress    = 0x06002100
	SysIDCopyAddress  = 0x06000C00
	BootParamsAddress = 0x060002A0

	// ipLoadRoom is the space available for the IP in Work
	// RAM-H from the load address to the end of the 1 MiB
	// window.
	ipLoadRoom = 0x100000 - 0x2000
)

// BootDisc performs the documented HLE boot of the attached
// disc: the System ID signature is verified (again, from the
// image), the IP named by the header IP size field is loaded
// from the start of the data area to Work RAM-H at
// 0x06002000, the boot ROM's System ID and parameter copies
// are made, and the machine is left in the documented post
// boot state: the master SH-2 executing the IP at 0x06002100
// with the Stack-M stack pointer, the slave SH-2 reset at the
// same entry with the Stack-S stack pointer and held (the IP
// releases it with SMPC SSHON), the SMPC at its power on
// status values, the sound chip and the CD block held off
// until their SMPC ON commands, and the CD block holding the
// attached image at its standby state.
//
// No boot ROM bytes are read or embedded: the BIOS window
// keeps reading zero, and this function replaces the boot
// ROM with the documented transfers above. BootDisc is the
// real boot path used by the libretro shell. The power on
// seeding in Reset is kept for the device gates that seed
// their own programs.
//
// A stack field of zero in the header falls back to the
// conventional 0x06001000 power on stack for that CPU: some
// published headers leave the fields zero and rely on the
// boot area default. An IP size below 256 (the System ID
// alone) or above the Work RAM-H room is an error, as is a
// size the image does not contain.
func (s *System) BootDisc() error {
	if s.disc == nil {
		return ErrNoDisc
	}
	hdr, err := s.disc.SaturnHeader()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	size := int(hdr.IPSize)
	if size < 0x100 {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: IP size %#x is smaller than the 256 byte System ID", hdr.IPSize)
	}
	if size > ipLoadRoom {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: IP size %#x does not fit in Work RAM-H from %#x", hdr.IPSize, uint32(IPLoadAddress))
	}
	// Read the whole IP before touching the machine, so a
	// short or unreadable image fails the boot cleanly.
	ip := make([]byte, 0, size)
	for lba := 0; len(ip) < size; lba++ {
		sec, err := s.disc.ReadLogicalSector(lba)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("system: reading IP sector %d: %w", lba, err)
		}
		if len(sec) == 0 {
			return fmt.Errorf("system: empty sector while reading IP sector %d", lba)
		}
		ip = append(ip, sec...)
	}
	ip = ip[:size]

	// The button mask is host input state, not machine
	// state: it survives the power on reset so a frontend
	// that sets buttons before booting sees them
	// reflected in the booted program's pad reads.
	buttons := s.buttons
	s.Reset()
	s.buttons = buttons
	s.header = hdr
	ram := s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()
	copy(ram[IPLoadAddress-0x06000000:], ip)
	copy(ram[SysIDCopyAddress-0x06000000:], ip[:0x100])
	copy(ram[BootParamsAddress-0x06000000:], ip[0xE0:0x100])

	masterStack := hdr.MasterStack
	if masterStack == 0 {
		masterStack = 0x06001000
	}
	slaveStack := hdr.SlaveStack
	if slaveStack == 0 {
		slaveStack = 0x06001000
	}
	s.Master.Reset(IPEntryAddress, masterStack)
	s.Slave.Reset(IPEntryAddress, slaveStack)
	s.slaveReleased = false
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/system/boot_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/cd"
)

// bootTestImage builds a minimal bootable disc image: a
// System ID with the documented binary fields set, and a
// tiny IP at offset 0x100 that writes its entry marker to
// Work RAM-H and spins.
func bootTestImage(t *testing.T) *cd.Image {
	t.Helper()
	img := make([]byte, 4*2048)
	copy(img[0:16], "SEGA SEGASATURN ")
	copy(img[0x60:0x60+12], "BOOT TEST IP")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xE0:0xE4], 0x1000)     // IP size
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xE8:0xEC], 0x06001800) // Stack-M
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xEC:0xF0], 0x06001400) // Stack-S
	// IP code at file offset 0x100 (RAM 0x06002100):
	// load two literals, store the marker at 0x06003000,
	// then spin.
	words := []uint16{
		0xD105,         // 0x00 MOV.L @(20,PC),R1 ; R1 = 0x06003000
		0xD206,         // 0x02 MOV.L @(24,PC),R2 ; R2 = 0xB007600D
		0x2122,         // 0x04 MOV.L R2,@R1
		0xAFFE,         // 0x06 BRA self
		0x0009,         // 0x08 delay NOP
		0x0009, 0x0009, // 0x0A padding
		0x0009, 0x0009, // 0x0E padding
		0x0009, 0x0009, // 0x12 padding
		0x0009,         // 0x16 padding
		0x0600, 0x3000, // 0x18 literal 0x06003000
		0xB007, 0x600D, // 0x1C literal 0xB007600D
	}
	for i, w := range words {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(img[0x100+2*i:0x100+2*i+2], w)
	}
	im, err := cd.OpenBytes(img, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenBytes: %v", err)
	}
	return im
}

func TestBootDiscPostBootState(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	if err := s.LoadDiscImage(bootTestImage(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDiscImage: %v", err)
	}
	if err := s.BootDisc(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("BootDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if got := s.Master.PC; got != IPEntryAddress {
		t.Fatalf("master PC = %#x, want %#x", got, uint32(IPEntryAddress))
	}
	if got := s.Master.Reg[15]; got != 0x06001800 {
		t.Fatalf("master SP = %#x, want Stack-M 0x06001800", got)
	}
	if got := s.Slave.PC; got != IPEntryAddress {
		t.Fatalf("slave PC = %#x, want %#x", got, uint32(IPEntryAddress))
	}
	if got := s.Slave.Reg[15]; got != 0x06001400 {
		t.Fatalf("slave SP = %#x, want Stack-S 0x06001400", got)
	}
	if s.SlaveReleased() {
		t.Fatal("slave released at boot, want held until SSHON")
	}
	// The IP bytes landed at the load address, including
	// the System ID at its base.
	if got := string(s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()[0x2000:0x2010]); got != "SEGA SEGASATURN " {
		t.Fatalf("Work RAM-H at load base = %q, want the System ID", got)
	}
	// The boot ROM copies: System ID at 0x06000C00 and the
	// parameter block at 0x060002A0.
	ram := s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()
	if got := string(ram[0xC00:0xC10]); got != "SEGA SEGASATURN " {
		t.Fatalf("System ID copy = %q", got)
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(ram[0x2A0:0x2A4]); got != 0x1000 {
		t.Fatalf("boot params IP size = %#x, want 0x1000", got)
	}
	if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(ram[0x2A8:0x2AC]); got != 0x06001800 {
		t.Fatalf("boot params Stack-M = %#x, want 0x06001800", got)
	}
	// Sound and CD start held off, matching the SMPC power
	// on status the gates pin.
	if s.Sound.SoundOn() {
		t.Fatal("sound on at boot, want held until SNDON")
	}
	// Run: the IP writes its marker and spins; the slave
	// never runs a step while held.
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
	}
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x06003000); got != 0xB007600D {
		t.Fatalf("IP marker = %#x, want 0xB007600D", got)
	}
	if got := s.Slave.Cycles; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("slave cycles = %d while held, want 0", got)
	}
	// The BIOS window still reads zero: no BIOS bytes are
	// involved in the boot.
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x00000000); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("BIOS window = %#x, want 0", got)
	}
}

func TestBootDiscErrors(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	if err := s.BootDisc(); !errors.Is(err, ErrNoDisc) {
		t.Fatalf("BootDisc with no disc = %v, want ErrNoDisc", err)
	}
	// IP size smaller than the System ID.
	img := make([]byte, 2*2048)
	copy(img[0:16], "SEGA SEGASATURN ")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xE0:0xE4], 0x80)
	im, err := cd.OpenBytes(img, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.LoadDiscImage(im); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.BootDisc(); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("BootDisc accepted an IP size below the System ID size")
	}
	// IP size larger than the image holds.
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(img[0xE0:0xE4], 0x4000)
	im2, err := cd.OpenBytes(img, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.LoadDiscImage(im2); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.BootDisc(); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("BootDisc accepted an IP size beyond the image")
	}
	// A failed boot leaves the master at the power on park.
	if got := s.Master.PC; got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("master PC after failed boot = %#x, want the power on park 0", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/system/enginetest_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/cd"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/enginetest"
)

// The SAT-4 full stack gate. A synthetic disc whose IP is
// hand assembled SH-2 boots ONLY through BootDisc and
// drives every device through its documented guest
// interface: SMPC SSHON slave release, CD block file
// reads through the data port, VDP2 and VDP1 programming,
// a 68EC000 sound driver uploaded through sound RAM and
// released with SNDON, an SMPC INTBACK pad read, and a
// backup RAM round trip through the odd byte path. A mid
// run save taken just after the sound starts restores to
// a byte identical continuation.

// mileWord reads one word of the milestone block.
func mileWord(s *System, off int) uint32 {
	return s.Bus.Read32(enginetest.MilestoneAddress + uint32(off))
}

func mileCount(s *System) int {
	return int(mileWord(s, enginetest.MileCount))
}

func TestEnginetestDiscFullStack(t *testing.T) {
	iso := enginetest.BuildDisc()

	// The cd layer agrees with the fixture: the payload
	// is in the root and reads back byte exact.
	img, err := cd.OpenBytes(iso, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenBytes: %v", err)
	}
	entries, err := img.ListRoot()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ListRoot: %v", err)
	}
	var payloadEntry *cd.FileEntry
	for i := range entries {
		if entries[i].Name == "PAYLOAD.BIN" {
			payloadEntry = &entries[i]
		}
	}
	if payloadEntry == nil {
		t.Fatalf("PAYLOAD.BIN not in the root listing: %v", entries)
	}
	payload, err := img.ReadFile(*payloadEntry)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReadFile: %v", err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(payload, enginetest.Payload()) {
		t.Fatal("payload through the cd layer differs from the fixture pattern")
	}

	dir := t.TempDir()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "enginetest.iso")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, iso, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Keep a copy for the desktop .so harness run.
	buildsDir := filepath.Join("..", "builds")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(buildsDir, 0o755); err == nil {
		_ = os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(buildsDir, "enginetest.iso"), iso, 0o644)
	}

	s := New()
	s.SetButtons(enginetest.PadMask)
	if err := s.LoadDisc(path); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	if err := s.BootDisc(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("BootDisc: %v", err)
	}
	// Documented post boot state.
	if got := s.Master.PC; got != IPEntryAddress {
		t.Fatalf("master PC = %#x, want %#x", got, uint32(IPEntryAddress))
	}
	if got := s.Master.Reg[15]; got != 0x06001000 {
		t.Fatalf("master SP = %#x, want the header Stack-M 0x06001000", got)
	}
	if got := s.Slave.Reg[15]; got != 0x06000800 {
		t.Fatalf("slave SP = %#x, want the header Stack-S 0x06000800", got)
	}
	if s.SlaveReleased() {
		t.Fatal("slave released at boot; the IP must release it with SSHON")
	}

	// Run until every milestone lands, saving mid run
	// just after the sound starts (milestone 4).
	var snap []byte
	snapFrame := 0
	frames := 0
	for frames < 300 {
		s.RunFrame()
		frames++
		if snap == nil && mileCount(s) >= 4 {
			s.AudioBuffer() // drain: pending output is not part of a state
			snap = s.Serialize()
			snapFrame = frames
			if len(snap) != s.StateSize() {
				t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want StateSize %d", len(snap), s.StateSize())
			}
		}
		if mileCount(s) >= 7 {
			break
		}
	}
	if got := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileError); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("IP failure stage = %d after %d frames", got, frames)
	}
	if got := mileCount(s); got != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("milestones = %d after %d frames, want 7 (order log % x)",
			got, frames, s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()[0x4008:0x4008+7])
	}
	if got := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileMagic); got != enginetest.MileMagicValue {
		t.Fatalf("milestone magic = %#x, want %#x", got, uint32(enginetest.MileMagicValue))
	}
	order := s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()[0x4000+enginetest.MileOrder : 0x4000+enginetest.MileOrder+7]
	for i, b := range order {
		if b != byte(i+1) {
			t.Fatalf("milestone order = % x, want 1..7 in order", order)
		}
	}
	if got := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileMaster); got != 42 {
		t.Fatalf("master handshake cell = %d, want 42", got)
	}
	if got := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileSlave); got != 43 {
		t.Fatalf("slave handshake cell = %d, want 43", got)
	}
	alive1 := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileAlive)
	s.RunFrame()
	if alive2 := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileAlive); alive2 <= alive1 {
		t.Fatalf("slave alive counter did not advance: %d then %d", alive1, alive2)
	}

	// CD payload: the guest checksum and size, and the
	// bytes themselves in Work RAM-L.
	if got := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileChecksum); got != enginetest.PayloadChecksum() {
		t.Fatalf("guest payload checksum = %#x, want %#x", got, enginetest.PayloadChecksum())
	}
	if got := mileWord(s, enginetest.MileSize); got != enginetest.PayloadSize {
		t.Fatalf("guest payload size = %d, want %d", got, enginetest.PayloadSize)
	}
	if got := s.Bus.WorkRAMLow()[:enginetest.PayloadSize]; !bytes.Equal(got, enginetest.Payload()) {
		t.Fatal("payload bytes in Work RAM-L differ from the fixture")
	}

	// Pad report bytes for the mask set before the run.
	pad := s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()[0x4000+enginetest.MilePad : 0x4000+enginetest.MilePad+4]
	if !bytes.Equal(pad, enginetest.ExpectedPad[:]) {
		t.Fatalf("INTBACK report = % x, want % x", pad, enginetest.ExpectedPad)
	}

	// Backup RAM: the result byte in the block, and the
	// logical store itself holds the pattern.
	if got := s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh()[0x4000+enginetest.MileBackup]; got != 0xA5 {
		t.Fatalf("backup result byte = %#x, want 0xA5", got)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		if got := s.Bus.BackupRAM()[i]; got != byte(0x41+i) {
			t.Fatalf("backup logical byte %d = %#x, want %#x", i, got, byte(0x41+i))
		}
	}

	// Framebuffer probes, the SAT-2 gate's display. The
	// VDP1 draw and framebuffer swap pipeline takes a
	// few frames to present after the guest programs it,
	// so settle first (the assertions stay exact).
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
	}
	if w, h := s.DisplaySize(); w != 320 || h != 224 {
		t.Fatalf("display size = %dx%d, want 320x224", w, h)
	}
	fb := s.Framebuffer()
	px := func(x, y int) uint32 { return fb[y*320+x] }
	if got := px(0, 0); got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (0,0) = %#x, want green 0xFF00FF00", got)
	}
	if got := px(1, 0); got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (1,0) = %#x, want red 0xFFFF0000", got)
	}
	if got := px(105, 55); got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (105,55) = %#x, want white 0xFFFFFFFF", got)
	}
	if got := px(99, 55); got != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (99,55) = %#x, want black 0xFF000000", got)
	}

	// Audio: the sine table at unity pitch must measure
	// at 44100/256 Hz within two percent.
	var samples []int16
	for i := 0; i < 15; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
		samples = append(samples, s.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	var crossings []int
	for n := 1; n*2 < len(samples); n++ {
		if samples[(n-1)*2] < 0 && samples[n*2] >= 0 {
			crossings = append(crossings, n)
		}
	}
	if len(crossings) < 4 {
		t.Fatalf("only %d positive crossings in %d stereo samples; the tone is not playing",
			len(crossings), len(samples)/2)
	}
	period := float64(crossings[len(crossings)-1]-crossings[0]) / float64(len(crossings)-1)
	freq := 44100.0 / period
	want := 44100.0 / 256.0
	if math.Abs(freq-want)/want > 0.02 {
		t.Fatalf("tone frequency = %.2f Hz, want %.2f within 2 percent", freq, want)
	}
	t.Logf("enginetest: 7 milestones in %d frames, tone %.2f Hz (period %.1f samples), state at sound start %d bytes",
		frames, freq, period, len(snap))

	// Mid run save: byte identical continuation of
	// state, framebuffer and audio. The restored machine
	// first replays the frames the original ran between
	// the snapshot and the measured window (the rest of
	// the milestone run, the alive check frame, the five
	// settle frames and the fifteen tone frames), then
	// both run the same 30 measured frames.
	if snap == nil {
		t.Fatal("the mid run save was never taken")
	}
	preFrames := (frames - snapFrame) + 1 + 5 + 15
	var audioA []int16
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
		audioA = append(audioA, s.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	wantState := s.Serialize()
	wantFB := append([]uint32(nil), s.Framebuffer()...)

	s2 := New()
	img2, err := cd.OpenBytes(iso, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s2.LoadDiscImage(img2); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s2.Deserialize(snap); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < preFrames; i++ {
		s2.RunFrame()
		s2.AudioBuffer()
	}
	var audioB []int16
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		s2.RunFrame()
		audioB = append(audioB, s2.AudioBuffer()...)
	}
	equalI16 := func(a, b []int16) bool {
		if len(a) != len(b) {
			return false
		}
		for i := range a {
			if a[i] != b[i] {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	}
	if !equalI16(audioA, audioB) {
		t.Fatal("audio continuation differs after restore")
	}
	if got := s2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Fatal("state continuation differs after restore")
	}
	gotFB := s2.Framebuffer()
	if len(gotFB) != len(wantFB) {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer size = %d, want %d", len(gotFB), len(wantFB))
	}
	for i := range wantFB {
		if gotFB[i] != wantFB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d = %#x, want %#x", i, gotFB[i], wantFB[i])
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/system/sat3_gate_test.go ====================

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/scsp"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/scu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/smpc"
)

// sat3MasterProgram writes the SMPC SSHON command byte
// (0x02) to COMREG at 0x0010001F and then spins. One
// command only: the polled SMPC samples COMREG once per
// scanline, and real software waits for the SF handshake
// between commands, so this gate issues SNDON and CDON
// through the page between frames instead.
var sat3MasterProgram = []uint16{
	0xD104,         // MOV.L @(4,PC),R1 -> R1 = 0x0010001F
	0xE002,         // MOV #2,R0 (SSHON)
	0x2100,         // MOV.B R0,@R1
	0xAFFE,         // BRA self
	0x0009,         // delay slot: NOP
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0010, 0x001F, // literal: 0x0010001F
}

// setupSAT3Sound loads a 68EC000 spin program and a
// looped 256 sample sine slot into the shared sound RAM
// and SCSP register page, following the SCSP package's
// own key on recipe. The slot keys on at the first
// sample tick after the SMPC SNDON releases the chip.
func setupSAT3Sound(s *System) {
	ram := s.Bus.SoundRAM()
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ram[0:4], 0x0007F000)     // SSP
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ram[4:8], 0x00000100)     // PC
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(ram[0x100:0x102], 0x60FE) // BRA.W self
	const sa = 0x2000
	for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {
		v := int16(30000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i)/256))
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(ram[sa+i*2:sa+i*2+2], uint16(v))
	}
	regs := s.Bus.SCSPRegisters()
	put := func(off int, v uint16) {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(regs[off:off+2], v)
	}
	put(scsp.RegMaster, 0x800F) // MEM4MB, MVOL 15
	put(scsp.SlotCtrl, 0x4100)  // KYONB, forward loop
	put(scsp.SlotSA, sa)
	put(scsp.SlotLSA, 0)
	put(scsp.SlotLEA, 255)
	put(scsp.SlotEG1, 31)     // instant attack
	put(scsp.SlotEG2, 0x7800) // KRS 15: scaling off
	put(scsp.SlotVol, 0)      // TL 0
	put(scsp.SlotPitch, 0)    // unity pitch
	put(scsp.SlotOutSel, 0xE000)
	put(scsp.SlotCtrl, 0xC100) // KYONEX + KYONB
}

// setupSAT3DMA programs SCU DMA channel 0 for a 16 byte
// Work RAM-H to Work RAM-L copy on the VBlank-IN start
// factor (the enable edge fires it at the first Poll).
func setupSAT3DMA(s *System) {
	for i, v := range []uint32{0x11223344, 0x55667788, 0x99AABBCC, 0xDDEEFF00} {
		s.Bus.Write32(0x06000400+uint32(4*i), v)
	}
	page := s.Bus.SCURegisters()
	put32 := func(off int, v uint32) {
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(page[off:off+4], v)
	}
	put32(0x00, 0x06000400) // D0R source
	put32(0x04, 0x00200000) // D0W destination
	put32(0x08, 16)         // D0C count
	put32(0x0C, 0x101)      // D0AD: read +4, write advance
	put32(0x14, 0)          // D0MD: direct, factor VBlank-IN
	put32(0x10, 1)          // D0EN: enable
}

// writeGateDisc builds a synthetic cue/bin image in a
// temp dir: track 1 is ten MODE1/2352 data sectors
// (sector 0 carries the Saturn IP signature), track 2
// is sixty audio sectors of a sine in little endian
// stereo, exactly the CD-DA layout the CD block streams.
func writeGateDisc(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir := t.TempDir()
	var img []byte
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		sec := make([]byte, 2352)
		for j := 1; j <= 10; j++ {
			sec[j] = 0xFF
		}
		sec[12] = 0x00
		sec[13] = 0x02
		sec[14] = byte(i)
		sec[15] = 0x01
		user := sec[16 : 16+2048]
		for j := range user {
			user[j] = byte(j)
		}
		if i == 0 {
			copy(user[0:16], "SEGA SEGASATURN ")
		}
		img = append(img, sec...)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 60; i++ {
		sec := make([]byte, 2352)
		for n := 0; n < 588; n++ {
			v := int16(12000 * math.Sin(2*math.Pi*float64(i*588+n)/100))
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[n*4:n*4+2], uint16(v))
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(sec[n*4+2:n*4+4], uint16(v))
		}
		img = append(img, sec...)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "gate.bin"), img, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cue := "FILE \"gate.bin\" BINARY\n" +
		"  TRACK 01 MODE1/2352\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 00:00:00\n" +
		"  TRACK 02 AUDIO\n" +
		"    INDEX 01 00:00:10\n"
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "gate.cue"), []byte(cue), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return filepath.Join(dir, "gate.cue")
}

// CD block page helpers. The register placement is the
// hardware one the cdblock package implements: HIRQ at
// page bytes [0x08:0x0A], its mask at [0x0C:0x0E], CR1
// at [0x18:0x1A] through CR4 at [0x24:0x26].
func cdPageWrite(s *System, off int, v uint16) {
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(s.Bus.CDRegisters()[off:off+2], v)
}

func cdPageRead(s *System, off int) uint16 {
	return binary.BigEndian.Uint16(s.Bus.CDRegisters()[off : off+2])
}

// cdStatusCode issues Get Status through the page and
// returns the status code (the low nibble of the status
// byte in the CR1 high byte).
func cdStatusCode(t *testing.T, s *System) int {
	t.Helper()
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x08, 0) // HIRQ clear: CMOK 0 admits a command
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x18, 0x0000)
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x1C, 0)
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x20, 0)
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x24, 0)
	s.RunFrame()
	return int(cdPageRead(s, 0x18)>>8) & 0x0F
}

func frameHash(fb []uint32) uint64 {
	h := uint64(1469598103934665603)
	for _, p := range fb {
		h ^= uint64(p)
		h *= 1099511628211
	}
	return h
}

func equalInt16(a, b []int16) bool {
	if len(a) != len(b) {
		return false
	}
	for i := range a {
		if a[i] != b[i] {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// TestSAT3FullStackDeterminism is the slice gate: the
// master boots the machine through the SMPC (SSHON from
// a CPU program, then SNDON and CDON through the page),
// the slave runs, the SCSP plays a looped slot under its
// 68EC000, the SCU DMA and DSP fire, the CD block plays
// the audio track through the SCSP CD input, and a mid
// run save restores to a byte identical continuation
// including the audio samples.
func TestSAT3FullStackDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	if got := len(s.Serialize()); got != 4241176 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh v3 state size = %d, want 4241176", got)
	}
	if err := s.LoadDisc(writeGateDisc(t)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDisc: %v", err)
	}
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000000, sat3MasterProgram)
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000200, slaveProgram)
	s.Bus.Write32(0x06000100, 41)
	s.Master.PC = 0x06000000
	s.Slave.PC = 0x06000200
	setupSAT3Sound(s)
	setupSAT3DMA(s)
	s.SCU.DSPWriteProgram(0, 0xF8000000) // ENDI
	s.SCU.RunDSP(4)
	s.SetButtons(ButtonA | ButtonStart)

	// Frame 0: the master program's SSHON lands.
	s.RunFrame()
	if !s.SlaveReleased() {
		t.Fatal("SMPC SSHON from the master program did not release the slave")
	}
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x06000104); got != 42 {
		t.Fatalf("slave result cell = %d, want 42 (slave ran after SSHON)", got)
	}
	if s.SCU.Status()&(1<<scu.IntDMA0End) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("SCU DMA channel 0 end not raised")
	}
	if s.SCU.Status()&(1<<scu.IntDSPEnd) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("SCU DSP end not raised")
	}
	for i, want := range []uint32{0x11223344, 0x55667788, 0x99AABBCC, 0xDDEEFF00} {
		if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x00200000 + uint32(4*i)); got != want {
			t.Fatalf("DMA destination word %d = %#x, want %#x", i, got, want)
		}
	}

	// SNDON and CDON through the SMPC page, one command
	// per frame like the SF handshake requires.
	s.Bus.SMPCRegisters()[smpc.OffCOMREG] = smpc.CmdSNDON
	s.RunFrame()
	if !s.Sound.SoundOn() {
		t.Fatal("SMPC SNDON did not release the SCSP")
	}
	if pc := s.Sound.CPU().PC(); pc != 0x100 {
		t.Fatalf("68EC000 PC = %#x, want 0x100 (reset from sound RAM vectors, spinning)", pc)
	}
	s.Bus.SMPCRegisters()[smpc.OffCOMREG] = smpc.CmdCDON
	s.RunFrame()

	// Play the audio track by FAD through the CD block,
	// with the HIRQ mask open so completions raise the
	// SCU A-Bus input.
	trs := s.Disc().Tracks()
	if len(trs) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("disc tracks = %d, want 2", len(trs))
	}
	start24 := uint32(0x800000 | (trs[1].Start + 150))
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x0C, 0xFFFF) // HIRQ mask: all sources
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x08, 0)      // HIRQ clear
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x18, 0x1000|uint16((start24>>16)&0xFF))
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x1C, uint16(start24&0xFFFF))
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x20, 0) // mode 0 (play once), end high 0
	cdPageWrite(s, 0x24, 0) // end 0: to disc end
	s.RunFrame()
	s.RunFrame()
	if s.SCU.Status()&(1<<scu.IntABusCD) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("CD block interrupt did not reach the SCU A-Bus input")
	}
	if code := cdStatusCode(t, s); code != 0x03 {
		t.Fatalf("CD status = %#x, want 0x03 (PLAY)", code)
	}

	// Pre run, drain (the pending output buffer is not
	// part of the state, by the documented contract),
	// then save mid play.
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
	}
	_ = s.AudioBuffer()
	snap := s.Serialize()
	if len(snap) != s.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("snapshot size = %d, StateSize = %d", len(snap), s.StateSize())
	}
	for i := 0; i < 15; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
	}
	audioA := s.AudioBuffer()
	snapA := s.Serialize()
	fbA := frameHash(s.Framebuffer())
	if len(audioA) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no audio in the continuation window")
	}
	nonzero := false
	for _, v := range audioA {
		if v != 0 {
			nonzero = true
			break
		}
	}
	if !nonzero {
		t.Fatal("continuation audio is silent (slot and CD both missing)")
	}

	if err := s.Deserialize(snap); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 15; i++ {
		s.RunFrame()
	}
	audioB := s.AudioBuffer()
	if !equalInt16(audioA, audioB) {
		t.Fatal("audio continuation differs after restore")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(s.Serialize(), snapA) {
		t.Fatal("state continuation differs after restore")
	}
	if frameHash(s.Framebuffer()) != fbA {
		t.Fatal("framebuffer continuation differs after restore")
	}
	// The CD is still mid track on the restored timeline.
	if code := cdStatusCode(t, s); code != 0x03 {
		t.Fatalf("CD status after restore = %#x, want 0x03 (PLAY)", code)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/system/system.go ====================

// Package system is the whole Sega Saturn machine: two
// SH-2 CPUs (master and slave) on the shared bus, the
// VDP1 sprite and polygon engine, the VDP2 background
// engine composing the picture, the SCU interrupt
// controller wiring, the CD image foundations, the
// standard pad state, and deterministic save states.
//
// SAT-3 state of the machine: RunFrame advances the
// display scanline by scanline. At the start of each
// frame the VDP1 performs its frame change processing
// (bank swap, erase, auto draw per FBCR and PTMR). Each
// line the SCU gains its HBlank-IN status, VBlank-IN at
// the first blanking line, and VBlank-OUT at line 0, and
// one pending unmasked SCU interrupt is offered to both
// CPUs at the per source level of the SCU manual. The
// VDP2 renders each visible line into the framebuffer
// after that line's CPU slice, so mid frame register
// writes take effect on later lines just like hardware
// raster effects. Per line the machine also steps the
// SCSP sound chip by the line's cycle budget and polls
// the SMPC (executing any command written to COMREG),
// the CD block, and the SCU (DMA channels and DSP).
//
// The SMPC owns the machine level resets: SSHON and
// SSHOFF release and hold the slave, SNDON and SNDOFF
// release and hold the SCSP 68EC000, CDON and CDOFF
// power the CD block, and NMIREQ raises the master NMI.
// At power on the sound chip and the CD block are held
// off, matching the SMPC reset status the boot ROM
// reports, until their ON commands run. The CD block
// interrupt reaches the SCU as its A-Bus external input
// (scu.IntABusCD). SCSP main CPU requests raise the SCU
// sound request source. CD audio streams from the CD
// block into the SCSP CD input; AudioBuffer drains the
// mixed 44100 Hz stereo output.
//
// Slice boundaries, stated plainly: there is no BIOS in
// this core and none is loaded here. Reset parks the
// master CPU at address 0 with the conventional stack
// pointer, which the device gates use to seed their own
// programs. Real game boot is BootDisc (boot.go): an HLE
// implementation of the documented boot process that
// loads the disc's initial program to Work RAM-H and
// enters it, with the slave held until the IP releases
// it through the SMPC SSHON command.
package system

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/bus"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/cd"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/cdblock"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/chips/sh2"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/scsp"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/scu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/smpc"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/vdp1"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/vdp2"
)

// Width and Height are the framebuffer dimensions of
// the power on display mode (TVMD cleared: 320 by 224).
// The live dimensions follow TVMD and are reported by
// DisplaySize; the framebuffer resizes when they change.
const (
	Width  = 320
	Height = 224
)

// CyclesPerFrame is the per CPU cycle budget of one
// frame at 28.6364 MHz and 60 frames per second,
// truncated to a whole cycle (477273 of 477273.33). The
// budget is split across the total scanlines of the
// current display mode: every line gets
// CyclesPerFrame/TotalLines cycles, and the first
// CyclesPerFrame%TotalLines lines get one extra cycle,
// so a frame always totals exactly CyclesPerFrame.
const CyclesPerFrame = 477273

// Standard Saturn digital pad buttons, in the bit order
// used by SetButtons. The peripheral ID convention for
// the standard digital pad is 0x02 (see PadID).
const (
	ButtonUp    = 1 << 0
	ButtonDown  = 1 << 1
	ButtonLeft  = 1 << 2
	ButtonRight = 1 << 3
	ButtonA     = 1 << 4
	ButtonB     = 1 << 5
	ButtonC     = 1 << 6
	ButtonX     = 1 << 7
	ButtonY     = 1 << 8
	ButtonZ     = 1 << 9
	ButtonL     = 1 << 10
	ButtonR     = 1 << 11
	ButtonStart = 1 << 12
)

// PadID is the Saturn peripheral ID byte for the standard
// digital pad. SMPC peripheral polling lands in SAT-3;
// the ID is recorded here as part of the pad state.
const PadID = 0x02

// Save state layout (all integers big endian):
//
//	byte 0: version (3)
//	byte 1: flags, bit 0 set when the slave is released,
//	  bit 1 set when the next frame is the odd field
//	bytes 2..3: button mask
//	bytes 4..11: frame counter
//	bytes 12..15: current scanline
//	bytes 16..17: VDP1 misc state (draw bank, trigger
//	  latch, draw end flag)
//	bytes 18..19: zero
//	then the master CPU state (sh2.SerializeSize bytes)
//	then the slave CPU state (sh2.SerializeSize bytes)
//	then Work RAM-L (1 MiB), Work RAM-H (1 MiB), and the
//	logical backup RAM (32 KiB)
//	then VDP2 VRAM (512 KiB), VDP2 CRAM (4 KiB), and the
//	VDP2 register page (512 bytes)
//	then VDP1 VRAM (512 KiB), the VDP1 frame buffer
//	(both banks, 512 KiB), and the VDP1 register page
//	(128 bytes)
//	then the SCU register page (256 bytes)
//
// Version 3 appends, after that layout: the sound RAM
// (512 KiB) and the SCSP register page (4 KiB), the
// SMPC page (128 bytes) and the CD block page (64
// bytes), the SCU extra state (scu.ExtraSize bytes), the
// SMPC state (smpc.SerializeSize bytes), and the two
// variable sections, each a 4 byte big endian length
// followed by its bytes: the SCSP state, then the CD
// block state (buffered sector descriptors only; sector
// payloads re-read from the attached disc by FAD).
const stateVersion = 3

// stateHeader is the size of the fixed state header.
const stateHeader = 20

// stateFixedSize is the size of the fixed part of a
// version 3 state: everything except the two variable
// sections (the SCSP and CD block states), whose sizes
// depend on their queue and buffer contents.
const stateFixedSize = stateHeader + 2*sh2.SerializeSize +
	0x100000 + 0x100000 + 0x8000 +
	0x80000 + 0x1000 + 0x200 +
	0x80000 + 0x80000 + 0x80 +
	0x100 +
	0x80000 + 0x1000 + 0x80 + 0x40 +
	scu.ExtraSize + smpc.SerializeSize + 8

// System is one powered on Saturn.
type System struct {
	Master *sh2.CPU
	Slave  *sh2.CPU
	Bus    *bus.Bus
	VDP1   *vdp1.VDP1
	VDP2   *vdp2.VDP2
	SCU    *scu.SCU
	SMPC   *smpc.SMPC
	CD     *cdblock.Block
	Sound  *scsp.SCSP

	disc   *cd.Image
	header *cd.IPHeader

	slaveReleased bool
	buttons       uint16
	frame         uint64
	line          int
	oddField      bool
	fbW, fbH      int
	framebuffer   []uint32
}

// New builds a System and resets it.
func New() *System {
	s := &System{Bus: bus.New()}
	s.Master = sh2.New(s.Bus)
	s.Slave = sh2.New(s.Bus)
	s.VDP1 = vdp1.New(s.Bus.VDP1VRAM(), s.Bus.VDP1Framebuffer(), s.Bus.VDP1Registers())
	s.VDP2 = vdp2.New(s.Bus.VDP2VRAM(), s.Bus.VDP2CRAM(), s.Bus.VDP2Registers(), s.VDP1)
	s.SCU = scu.New(s.Bus.SCURegisters())
	s.SCU.AttachMem(s.Bus)
	// Timer 0 compares against the NTSC line width in
	// dot clocks (1708 per line at 320 wide); the SCU
	// timers only need a fixed positive line width.
	s.SCU.SetLineDots(1708)
	s.VDP1.SetRotateFunc(s.VDP2.FBRotationCoord)
	s.Reset()
	return s
}

// Reset returns the machine to its power on state. The
// master is parked at the BIOS window base with the
// conventional initial stack; the slave is held again.
// Device memories keep their contents, matching SAT-1:
// a fresh System is all zero because the bus starts
// zeroed.
func (s *System) Reset() {
	s.slaveReleased = false
	s.buttons = 0
	s.frame = 0
	s.line = 0
	s.oddField = false
	s.Bus.SetCurrentCPU(0)
	s.Master.Reset(0x00000000, 0x06001000)
	s.Slave.Reset(0x00000000, 0x06001000)
	s.wireDevices()
	s.updateDisplaySize()
	for i := range s.framebuffer {
		s.framebuffer[i] = 0
	}
}

// wireDevices (re)builds the SAT-3 devices over the bus
// pages and memories and connects their callbacks. It
// runs at power on (through Reset): the SCSP and the CD
// block start held off, matching the SMPC power on
// reset status, until the SMPC SNDON and CDON commands
// release them. The SMPC command hooks land here: SSHON
// releases the slave (ReleaseSlave semantics; the slave
// keeps its current PC), SSHOFF holds and resets it,
// NMIREQ raises the master NMI, and the sound and CD
// hooks drive the devices built above.
func (s *System) wireDevices() {
	s.Sound = scsp.New(s.Bus.SoundRAM(), s.Bus.SCSPRegisters())
	s.Sound.OnSoundRequest = func() { s.SCU.Raise(scu.IntSoundReq) }
	s.Sound.SetSoundOn(false)
	s.CD = cdblock.New(s.Bus.CDRegisters())
	s.CD.OnIRQ = func() { s.SCU.Raise(scu.IntABusCD) }
	s.CD.SetAudioSink(func(samples []int16) {
		s.Sound.InputCDSamples(samples)
	})
	s.CD.SetPower(false)
	if s.disc != nil {
		s.CD.SetImage(s.disc)
	}
	s.SMPC = smpc.New(s.Bus.SMPCRegisters(), smpc.Hooks{
		OnSSHON: func() { s.slaveReleased = true },
		OnSSHOFF: func() {
			s.slaveReleased = false
			s.Slave.Reset(0x00000000, 0x06001000)
		},
		OnNMIReq: func() { s.Master.RaiseNMI() },
		OnSNDON:  func() { s.Sound.SetSoundOn(true) },
		OnSNDOFF: func() { s.Sound.SetSoundOn(false) },
		OnCDOn:   func() { s.CD.SetPower(true) },
		OnCDOff:  func() { s.CD.SetPower(false) },
	})
}

// updateDisplaySize follows TVMD: when the VDP2 reports
// new dimensions, the framebuffer is rebuilt and the
// VDP1 learns its drawing bounds.
func (s *System) updateDisplaySize() {
	w, h := s.VDP2.DisplaySize()
	if w == s.fbW && h == s.fbH && s.framebuffer != nil {
		return
	}
	s.fbW, s.fbH = w, h
	s.framebuffer = make([]uint32, w*h)
	s.VDP1.SetDisplaySize(w, h)
}

// DisplaySize reports the current framebuffer dimensions
// as set by TVMD.
func (s *System) DisplaySize() (w, h int) { return s.fbW, s.fbH }

// LoadDisc opens a user supplied disc image by file
// extension (.cue or .iso) and parses its Saturn IP
// header. The image bytes stay with the caller supplied
// file; nothing is copied into the repository or the
// save state.
func (s *System) LoadDisc(path string) error {
	var img *cd.Image
	var err error
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".cue":
		img, err = cd.OpenCue(path)
	case ".iso":
		img, err = cd.OpenISO(path)
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("system: unsupported disc image extension %q", filepath.Ext(path))
	}
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return s.LoadDiscImage(img)
}

// LoadDiscImage attaches an already opened image and
// validates the Saturn IP header signature.
func (s *System) LoadDiscImage(img *cd.Image) error {
	hdr, err := img.SaturnHeader()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.disc = img
	s.header = hdr
	s.CD.SetImage(img)
	return nil
}

// Disc returns the attached image, or nil.
func (s *System) Disc() *cd.Image { return s.disc }

// Header returns the parsed Saturn IP header of the
// attached disc, or nil when no disc is attached.
func (s *System) Header() *cd.IPHeader { return s.header }

// ReleaseSlave releases the slave CPU from its held
// state so RunFrame starts stepping it.
func (s *System) ReleaseSlave() { s.slaveReleased = true }

// SlaveReleased reports whether the slave CPU runs.
func (s *System) SlaveReleased() bool { return s.slaveReleased }

// SetButtons stores the standard pad button mask.
func (s *System) SetButtons(mask uint16) { s.buttons = mask }

// Buttons returns the stored pad button mask.
func (s *System) Buttons() uint16 { return s.buttons }

// Frame returns the number of completed frames.
func (s *System) Frame() uint64 { return s.frame }

// Line returns the scanline currently being executed,
// or 0 between frames.
func (s *System) Line() int { return s.line }

// RunFrame advances the machine by one frame. Frame
// change processing runs first (it belongs to the
// vertical blank of the previous frame), then each
// scanline: timing flags and SCU status for the line,
// the SCU timers, one interrupt delivery attempt, the
// CPU cycle slice for the line, the SAT-3 device step
// (SCSP, SMPC, CD block, SCU DMA and DSP), the VDP1
// trigger watch, and the VDP2 render of the line when
// it is a visible line.
func (s *System) RunFrame() {
	s.VDP1.FrameBoundary()
	s.Bus.SetVDP1DrawBank(s.VDP1.DrawBank())
	s.updateDisplaySize()
	s.SMPC.SetPad(0, s.buttons)
	s.SMPC.SetPad(1, 0)

	total := s.VDP2.TotalLines()
	dispH := s.fbH
	base := CyclesPerFrame / total
	rem := CyclesPerFrame % total
	for line := 0; line < total; line++ {
		s.line = line
		s.VDP2.SetTiming(line, s.oddField)
		if line == dispH {
			s.SCU.Raise(scu.IntVBlankIn)
		}
		if line == 0 {
			s.SCU.Raise(scu.IntVBlankOut)
		}
		s.SCU.Raise(scu.IntHBlankIn)
		s.SCU.TickLine(line)
		s.deliverInterrupts()
		s.VDP2.SetHBlank(true)
		budget := base
		if line < rem {
			budget++
		}
		s.runCPUs(budget)
		s.stepDevices(budget)
		s.VDP2.SetHBlank(false)
		s.VDP1.PollTrigger()
		if s.VDP1.TakeDrawEnd() {
			s.SCU.Raise(scu.IntSpriteEnd)
		}
		if line < dispH {
			s.VDP2.RenderLine(s.framebuffer, line)
		}
	}
	s.frame++
	s.oddField = !s.oddField
	s.line = 0
}

// runCPUs steps both CPUs for one scanline slice. The
// master always runs; the slave runs the same budget
// when released. The bus current CPU selector is set
// before every step so the per CPU on-chip register
// windows answer for the CPU that is executing.
func (s *System) runCPUs(budget int) {
	s.runOne(0, s.Master, budget)
	if s.slaveReleased {
		s.runOne(1, s.Slave, budget)
	}
}

func (s *System) runOne(id int, cpu *sh2.CPU, budget int) {
	start := cpu.Cycles
	for cpu.Cycles-start < uint64(budget) {
		s.Bus.SetCurrentCPU(id)
		cpu.Step()
	}
}

// deliverInterrupts offers the highest priority pending
// unmasked SCU source to both CPUs at the per source
// level of the SCU manual (scu.LevelOf). IST bits stay
// set until software clears them, so the slave is
// offered the same source the master sees; each CPU
// takes it only when its own SR mask allows. The slave
// is offered sources only while released.
func (s *System) deliverInterrupts() {
	bit, vec := s.SCU.Deliver()
	if vec < 0 {
		return
	}
	level := scu.LevelOf(bit)
	s.Master.Interrupt(level, vec)
	if s.slaveReleased {
		s.Slave.Interrupt(level, vec)
	}
}

// stepDevices advances the SAT-3 devices by one
// scanline slice, after the CPUs have run: the SCSP by
// the line's cycle budget, then the polled devices. The
// SMPC executes at most one command per line (a command
// written by a CPU during this line runs at its end);
// the CD block polls its command registers and streams
// at sector rate; the SCU Poll runs any DMA channel
// whose start factor latched and services the DSP.
func (s *System) stepDevices(cycles int) {
	s.Sound.Step(cycles)
	s.SMPC.Poll()
	s.SMPC.Advance(cycles)
	s.CD.Poll()
	s.CD.Advance(cycles)
	s.SCU.Poll()
}

// Framebuffer returns the shared frame buffer in
// XRGB8888 at the current TVMD dimensions. Pixels are
// written by the VDP2 during RunFrame; before the first
// frame the buffer is all zero.
func (s *System) Framebuffer() []uint32 { return s.framebuffer }

// AudioBuffer drains the SCSP mixed output: interleaved
// stereo int16 samples at 44100 Hz produced since the
// previous call. Callers that save state for a bit
// exact continuation drain first: the pending output
// buffer is not part of the save state (the SCSP
// documents the same contract).
func (s *System) AudioBuffer() []int16 { return s.Sound.AudioBuffer() }

// StateSize returns the exact serialized size of the
// current machine state. Unlike SAT-2 the size is not
// constant: the SCSP section grows with its CD queue
// and the CD block section with its buffered sectors.
func (s *System) StateSize() int {
	return stateFixedSize + len(s.Sound.Serialize()) + len(s.CD.Serialize())
}

// Serialize writes the full deterministic machine state
// described at the top of this file.
func (s *System) Serialize() []byte {
	scspState := s.Sound.Serialize()
	cdState := s.CD.Serialize()
	out := make([]byte, stateFixedSize+len(scspState)+len(cdState))
	out[0] = stateVersion
	if s.slaveReleased {
		out[1] |= 1
	}
	if s.oddField {
		out[1] |= 2
	}
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[2:4], s.buttons)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(out[4:12], s.frame)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[12:16], uint32(s.line))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[16:18], s.VDP1.Misc())
	off := stateHeader
	copy(out[off:off+sh2.SerializeSize], s.Master.Serialize())
	off += sh2.SerializeSize
	copy(out[off:off+sh2.SerializeSize], s.Slave.Serialize())
	off += sh2.SerializeSize
	copy(out[off:off+0x100000], s.Bus.WorkRAMLow())
	off += 0x100000
	copy(out[off:off+0x100000], s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh())
	off += 0x100000
	copy(out[off:off+0x8000], s.Bus.BackupRAM())
	off += 0x8000
	copy(out[off:off+0x80000], s.Bus.VDP2VRAM())
	off += 0x80000
	copy(out[off:off+0x1000], s.Bus.VDP2CRAM())
	off += 0x1000
	copy(out[off:off+0x200], s.Bus.VDP2Registers())
	off += 0x200
	copy(out[off:off+0x80000], s.Bus.VDP1VRAM())
	off += 0x80000
	copy(out[off:off+0x80000], s.Bus.VDP1Framebuffer())
	off += 0x80000
	copy(out[off:off+0x80], s.Bus.VDP1Registers())
	off += 0x80
	copy(out[off:off+0x100], s.Bus.SCURegisters())
	off += 0x100
	copy(out[off:off+0x80000], s.Bus.SoundRAM())
	off += 0x80000
	copy(out[off:off+0x1000], s.Bus.SCSPRegisters())
	off += 0x1000
	copy(out[off:off+0x80], s.Bus.SMPCRegisters())
	off += 0x80
	copy(out[off:off+0x40], s.Bus.CDRegisters())
	off += 0x40
	copy(out[off:off+scu.ExtraSize], s.SCU.SerializeExtra())
	off += scu.ExtraSize
	copy(out[off:off+smpc.SerializeSize], s.SMPC.Serialize())
	off += smpc.SerializeSize
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:off+4], uint32(len(scspState)))
	off += 4
	copy(out[off:off+len(scspState)], scspState)
	off += len(scspState)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[off:off+4], uint32(len(cdState)))
	off += 4
	copy(out[off:off+len(cdState)], cdState)
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state produced by Serialize.
// The total length is validated against the two
// length prefixed variable sections, so a truncated or
// overlong state errors instead of restoring garbage.
func (s *System) Deserialize(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) < stateFixedSize {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state size %d, want at least %d", len(data), stateFixedSize)
	}
	if data[0] != stateVersion {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: state version %d, want %d", data[0], stateVersion)
	}
	s.slaveReleased = data[1]&1 != 0
	s.oddField = data[1]&2 != 0
	s.buttons = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[2:4])
	s.frame = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[4:12])
	s.line = int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[12:16]))
	off := stateHeader
	if err := s.Master.Deserialize(data[off : off+sh2.SerializeSize]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += sh2.SerializeSize
	if err := s.Slave.Deserialize(data[off : off+sh2.SerializeSize]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += sh2.SerializeSize
	copy(s.Bus.WorkRAMLow(), data[off:off+0x100000])
	off += 0x100000
	copy(s.Bus.WorkRAMHigh(), data[off:off+0x100000])
	off += 0x100000
	copy(s.Bus.BackupRAM(), data[off:off+0x8000])
	off += 0x8000
	copy(s.Bus.VDP2VRAM(), data[off:off+0x80000])
	off += 0x80000
	copy(s.Bus.VDP2CRAM(), data[off:off+0x1000])
	off += 0x1000
	copy(s.Bus.VDP2Registers(), data[off:off+0x200])
	off += 0x200
	copy(s.Bus.VDP1VRAM(), data[off:off+0x80000])
	off += 0x80000
	copy(s.Bus.VDP1Framebuffer(), data[off:off+0x80000])
	off += 0x80000
	copy(s.Bus.VDP1Registers(), data[off:off+0x80])
	off += 0x80
	copy(s.Bus.SCURegisters(), data[off:off+0x100])
	off += 0x100
	copy(s.Bus.SoundRAM(), data[off:off+0x80000])
	off += 0x80000
	copy(s.Bus.SCSPRegisters(), data[off:off+0x1000])
	off += 0x1000
	copy(s.Bus.SMPCRegisters(), data[off:off+0x80])
	off += 0x80
	copy(s.Bus.CDRegisters(), data[off:off+0x40])
	off += 0x40
	if err := s.SCU.DeserializeExtra(data[off : off+scu.ExtraSize]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += scu.ExtraSize
	// The SMPC page is restored above: the SMPC poll
	// tracker resyncs to its COMREG value, so a state
	// saved mid sequence does not re-execute a command.
	if err := s.SMPC.Deserialize(data[off : off+smpc.SerializeSize]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += smpc.SerializeSize
	n := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[off : off+4]))
	off += 4
	if n < 0 || off+n > len(data) {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: SCSP state length %d overruns the state", n)
	}
	if err := s.Sound.Deserialize(data[off : off+n]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	off += n
	m := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[off : off+4]))
	off += 4
	if m < 0 || off+m != len(data) {
		return fmt.Errorf("system: CD block state length %d does not close the state", m)
	}
	if err := s.CD.Deserialize(data[off : off+m]); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.VDP1.SetMisc(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[16:18]))
	s.Bus.SetVDP1DrawBank(s.VDP1.DrawBank())
	s.updateDisplaySize()
	return nil
}

// ErrNoDisc is returned by helpers that need a disc when
// none is attached. It is exported for SAT-4 boot code.
var ErrNoDisc = errors.New("system: no disc attached")

package system

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-saturn/cd"
)

// masterProgram writes the value 42 into the cell at
// 0x06000100 and then spins in a BRA loop. The literal
// pool word at index 6 is the cell address.
var masterProgram = []uint16{
	0xD102,         // MOV.L @(2,PC),R1  -> R1 = 0x06000100
	0xE02A,         // MOV #42,R0
	0x2102,         // MOV.L R0,@R1
	0xAFFE,         // BRA self
	0x0009,         // delay slot: NOP (MOVT R0 encoding, T is 0)
	0x0000,         // padding, never executed
	0x0600, 0x0100, // literal: 0x06000100
}

// slaveProgram reads the cell at 0x06000100, adds 1, and
// writes the result into the cell at 0x06000104, then
// spins. Its BRA delay slot is a NOP; the literals sit
// after the NOP and a pad word.
var slaveProgram = []uint16{
	0xD103,         // MOV.L @(3,PC),R1  -> R1 = 0x06000100
	0x6012,         // MOV.L @R1,R0
	0x7001,         // ADD #1,R0
	0xD103,         // MOV.L @(3,PC),R1  -> R1 = 0x06000104
	0x2102,         // MOV.L R0,@R1
	0xAFFE,         // BRA self
	0x0009,         // delay slot: NOP
	0x0009,         // padding, never executed
	0x0600, 0x0100, // literal: 0x06000100
	0x0600, 0x0104, // literal: 0x06000104
}

func loadProgram(s *System, addr uint32, prog []uint16) {
	for i, w := range prog {
		s.Bus.Write16(addr+uint32(2*i), w)
	}
}

func TestDualCPUCommunication(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000000, masterProgram)
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000200, slaveProgram)
	s.Master.PC = 0x06000000
	s.Slave.PC = 0x06000200

	s.RunFrame()
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x06000100); got != 42 {
		t.Fatalf("master cell = %#x, want 42", got)
	}
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x06000104); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("slave wrote before release: cell = %#x", got)
	}

	s.ReleaseSlave()
	s.RunFrame()
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x06000104); got != 43 {
		t.Fatalf("slave cell = %#x, want 43", got)
	}
}

func TestSaveStateDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000000, masterProgram)
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000200, slaveProgram)
	s.Master.PC = 0x06000000
	s.Slave.PC = 0x06000200
	s.ReleaseSlave()
	s.SetButtons(ButtonStart | ButtonA)
	s.RunFrame()

	snap := s.Serialize()
	if len(snap) != s.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(snap), s.StateSize())
	}
	s.RunFrame()
	want := s.Serialize()

	s2 := New()
	if err := s2.Deserialize(snap); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if !s2.SlaveReleased() {
		t.Fatal("slave release flag lost in restore")
	}
	if s2.Buttons() != ButtonStart|ButtonA {
		t.Fatalf("buttons = %#x after restore", s2.Buttons())
	}
	s2.RunFrame()
	got := s2.Serialize()
	if !bytes.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatal("continuation after restore differs from uninterrupted run")
	}
	if v := s2.Bus.Read32(0x06000104); v != 43 {
		t.Fatalf("slave cell after restore = %#x, want 43", v)
	}
}

func TestLoadDiscImageHeader(t *testing.T) {
	sector := make([]byte, 2048)
	copy(sector[0:16], "SEGA SEGASATURN ")
	copy(sector[0x60:0x60+14], "SYNTHETIC TEST")
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(sector[0xE8:0xEC], 0x06001000)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(sector[0xEC:0xF0], 0x06000800)
	img, err := cd.OpenBytes(sector, 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenBytes: %v", err)
	}
	s := New()
	if err := s.LoadDiscImage(img); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadDiscImage: %v", err)
	}
	hdr := s.Header()
	if hdr == nil {
		t.Fatal("no header stored")
	}
	if hdr.MasterStack != 0x06001000 || hdr.SlaveStack != 0x06000800 {
		t.Fatalf("stacks = %#x / %#x", hdr.MasterStack, hdr.SlaveStack)
	}

	blank, err := cd.OpenBytes(make([]byte, 2048), 2048)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("OpenBytes blank: %v", err)
	}
	if err := s.LoadDiscImage(blank); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("blank image accepted as a Saturn disc")
	}
}
