// irqMasterProgram points VBR at 0x06001000, loads SR with
// 0 (interrupt mask open, block bit clear), then spins.
// Its literals sit after the code; the disp fields match
// the offsets in the listing.
var irqMasterProgram = []uint16{
	0xD102,         // MOV.L @(2,PC),R1 -> R1 = 0x06001000
	0x412E,         // LDC R1,VBR
	0xD102,         // MOV.L @(2,PC),R1 -> R1 = 0x00000000
	0x410E,         // LDC R1,SR
	0xAFFE,         // BRA self
	0x0009,         // delay slot NOP
	0x0600, 0x1000, // literal: 0x06001000 (VBR)
	0x0000, 0x0000, // literal: 0x00000000 (SR)
}

// irqHandler writes 42 into the cell at 0x06003000 and
// returns from the interrupt.
var irqHandler = []uint16{
	0xD102,         // MOV.L @(2,PC),R1 -> R1 = 0x06003000
	0xE02A,         // MOV #42,R0
	0x2102,         // MOV.L R0,@R1
	0x002B,         // RTE
	0x0009,         // delay slot NOP
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0600, 0x3000, // literal: 0x06003000
}

func setupIRQ(s *System) {
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000000, irqMasterProgram)
	loadProgram(s, 0x06002000, irqHandler)
	// Vector entries for VBlank-IN (0x40), VBlank-OUT
	// (0x41), HBlank-IN (0x42), and the sprite draw end
	// (0x4D) all point at the one handler; whichever is
	// delivered first proves the path. In practice
	// VBlank-OUT wins the first frame because its IST bit
	// is raised at line 0 and never cleared by the
	// handler.
	s.Bus.Write32(0x06001100, 0x06002000)
	s.Bus.Write32(0x06001104, 0x06002000)
	s.Bus.Write32(0x06001108, 0x06002000)
	s.Bus.Write32(0x06001134, 0x06002000)
	s.Master.PC = 0x06000000
}

func TestVBlankInterruptDelivered(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	setupIRQ(s)
	s.RunFrame()
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x06003000); got != 42 {
		t.Fatalf("handler cell = %#x, want 42 (interrupt never reached the CPU)", got)
	}
	// The VBlank-IN status bit must be set in IST at
	// 0x05FE00A4 even though the handler never clears it.
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x05FE00A4); got&1 == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("IST = %#x, want VBlank-IN bit set", got)
	}
}

func TestVBlankInterruptMaskedByIMS(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	setupIRQ(s)
	// Mask every wired source: VBlank-IN, VBlank-OUT,
	// HBlank-IN, the sprite draw end (bit 12, raised by
	// the frame boundary auto draw), and, since SAT-3
	// wired the SCU timers into the frame, timer 0 (bit
	// 3: its power on compare of 0 fires at line 0).
	// Timer 1 stays silent here because its T1MD enable
	// bit is clear at power on.
	s.Bus.Write32(0x05FE00A0, 0x0000100F)
	s.RunFrame()
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x06003000); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("handler ran while masked: cell = %#x", got)
	}
	// Status still records the events; only delivery is
	// blocked.
	if got := s.Bus.Read32(0x05FE00A4); got&0x100F != 0x100F {
		t.Fatalf("IST = %#x, want bits 0, 1, 2, 3, and 12 set", got)
	}
}

// pokeProgram is a table driven device programmer. It
// walks (address, value, pad) entries of 8 bytes at the
// table address in its literal pool, storing each 16 bit
// value at its address through the bus, and stops at an
// entry whose address is zero. The slave has nothing to
// do in this gate beyond spinning once released.
var pokeProgram = []uint16{
	0xD107,         // MOV.L @(7,PC),R1 -> R1 = table address
	0x6216,         // loop: MOV.L @R1+,R2 (address)
	0x6315,         // MOV.W @R1+,R3 (value)
	0x6415,         // MOV.W @R1+,R4 (pad, keeps the 8 byte stride)
	0xE000,         // MOV #0,R0
	0x3200,         // CMP/EQ R0,R2
	0x8903,         // BT done (+3)
	0x2231,         // MOV.W R3,@R2
	0xAFF7,         // BRA loop (-9)
	0x0009,         // delay slot NOP
	0x0009,         // padding (unreachable)
	0xAFFE,         // done: BRA done
	0x0009,         // delay slot NOP
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0009,         // padding
	0x0600, 0x0100, // literal: 0x06000100 (table)
}

// poke builds one table of (address, value) pairs for
// pokeProgram, terminated by a zero address entry.
func poke(entries ...uint32) []byte {
	out := make([]byte, 0, len(entries)*4+8)
	for i := 0; i < len(entries); i += 2 {
		var b [8]byte
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[0:4], entries[i])
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(b[4:6], uint16(entries[i+1]))
		out = append(out, b[:]...)
	}
	return append(out, make([]byte, 8)...)
}

// vdpPokeTable programs the SAT-2 display through the
// bus: VDP2 shows NBG0 with one 16 color character (code
// 1 = green, code 2 = red, palette supplement 1), and
// VDP1 draws one white polygon at (100,50)-(119,69)
// whose sprite priority (7) beats NBG0 (2).
func vdpPokeTable() []byte {
	e := []uint32{
		// VDP2 registers.
		0x05F80000, 0x8000, // TVMD: DISP on, 320x224
		0x05F80020, 0x0001, // BGON: NBG0 on
		0x05F80028, 0x0000, // CHCTLA: NBG0 16 colors, cells, 1x1
		0x05F80030, 0x8020, // PNCN0: 1 word, SPLT = 1
		0x05F80078, 0x0001, // ZMXIN0: zoom increment 1
		0x05F8007C, 0x0001, // ZMYIN0: zoom increment 1
		0x05F800F8, 0x0002, // PRINA: NBG0 priority 2
		0x05F800F4, 0x0007, // PRISC: sprite S4 priority 7
		// CRAM: palette 16 code 1 green, code 2 red,
		// sprite color index 31 white.
		0x05F00202, 0x03E0,
		0x05F00204, 0x7C00,
		0x05F0003E, 0x7FFF,
		// VDP2 VRAM: pattern name (0,0) = character 1,
		// then the character pattern: first byte codes
		// 1,2 and the rest code 1.
		0x05E00000, 0x0001,
		0x05E00020, 0x1211,
	}
	for i := 1; i < 16; i++ {
		e = append(e, 0x05E00020+uint32(2*i), 0x1111)
	}
	e = append(e,
		// VDP1 command list: one polygon, then END.
		0x05C00000, 0x0004, // CMDCTRL: polygon
		0x05C00002, 0x0000, // CMDLINK
		0x05C00004, 0x0000, // CMDPMOD
		0x05C00006, 0x801F, // CMDCOLR: PR bit set, color 31
		0x05C00008, 0x0000, // CMDSRCA
		0x05C0000A, 0x0000, // CMDSIZE
		0x05C0000C, 100, // XA
		0x05C0000E, 50, // YA
		0x05C00010, 119, // XB
		0x05C00012, 50, // YB
		0x05C00014, 119, // XC
		0x05C00016, 69, // YC
		0x05C00018, 100, // XD
		0x05C0001A, 69, // YD
		0x05C0001C, 0x0000, // CMDGRDA
		0x05C00020, 0x8000, // END command CMDCTRL
		// VDP1 registers: 1 cycle frame change, auto
		// draw, erase with 0 over the full screen.
		0x05D00000, 0x0000, // TVMR
		0x05D00002, 0x0000, // FBCR
		0x05D00004, 0x0000, // PTMR
		0x05D00006, 0x0000, // EWDR
		0x05D00008, 0x0000, // EWLR: (0,0)
		0x05D0000A, 0x4EDF, // EWRR: x2 = 39, y2 = 223
	)
	return poke(e...)
}

func TestVDPDualCPUDisplayDeterminism(t *testing.T) {
	s := New()
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000000, pokeProgram)
	// The slave spin sits clear of the poke table, which
	// occupies 0x06000100 to 0x06000280.
	loadProgram(s, 0x06000400, []uint16{0xAFFE, 0x0009})
	table := vdpPokeTable()
	for i, b := range table {
		s.Bus.Write8(0x06000100+uint32(i), b)
	}
	s.Master.PC = 0x06000000
	s.Slave.PC = 0x06000400
	s.ReleaseSlave()

	s.RunFrame()
	s.RunFrame()
	snap := s.Serialize()
	if len(snap) != s.StateSize() {
		t.Fatalf("state size = %d, want %d", len(snap), s.StateSize())
	}
	s.RunFrame()
	s.RunFrame()
	wantState := s.Serialize()
	wantFB := append([]uint32(nil), s.Framebuffer()...)

	s2 := New()
	if err := s2.Deserialize(snap); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	s2.RunFrame()
	s2.RunFrame()
	if got := s2.Serialize(); !bytes.Equal(got, wantState) {
		t.Fatal("continuation state differs after restore")
	}
	gotFB := s2.Framebuffer()
	if len(gotFB) != len(wantFB) {
		t.Fatalf("framebuffer size = %d, want %d", len(gotFB), len(wantFB))
	}
	for i := range wantFB {
		if gotFB[i] != wantFB[i] {
			t.Fatalf("framebuffer pixel %d = %#x, want %#x", i, gotFB[i], wantFB[i])
		}
	}

	// Hand derived probes on the restored machine.
	px := func(x, y int) uint32 { return gotFB[y*Width+x] }
	if got := px(0, 0); got != 0xFF00FF00 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (0,0) = %#x, want green 0xFF00FF00 (NBG0 code 1)", got)
	}
	if got := px(1, 0); got != 0xFFFF0000 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (1,0) = %#x, want red 0xFFFF0000 (NBG0 code 2)", got)
	}
	if got := px(105, 55); got != 0xFFFFFFFF {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (105,55) = %#x, want white 0xFFFFFFFF (VDP1 polygon over NBG0)", got)
	}
	if got := px(99, 55); got != 0xFF000000 {
		t.Fatalf("pixel (99,55) = %#x, want black 0xFF000000 (NBG0 palette 16 code 0)", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp1/commands.go ====================

package vdp1

// Command list processing and rasterization.
//
// Commands are 32 byte tables in VRAM. The walker starts at byte
// address 0 and follows the jump mode of each command. All texture
// and table byte addresses wrap at the VRAM end with the 0x7FFFF
// mask, byte by byte.

type pt struct {
	x, y int
}

// cmd holds one decoded command table.
type cmd struct {
	ctrl uint16
	link uint16
	pmod uint16
	colr uint16
	srca uint16
	size uint16
	raw  [4]pt // vertex words decoded as signed coordinates
	rawW int   // raw unsigned XB word, scaled sprite width
	rawH int   // raw unsigned YB word, scaled sprite height
	grda uint16
}

// decodeCoord decodes an 11 bit two complement vertex coordinate.
func decodeCoord(word uint16) int {
	val := int(word & 0x7FF)
	if val >= 0x400 {
		val -= 0x800
	}
	return val
}

func (v *VDP1) vramByte(addr int) byte {
	if len(v.vram) == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	a := addr & vramMask
	if a >= len(v.vram) {
		a %= len(v.vram)
	}
	return v.vram[a]
}

func (v *VDP1) vramWord(addr int) uint16 {
	hi := v.vramByte(addr)
	lo := v.vramByte(addr + 1)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

func (v *VDP1) loadCmd(addr int) cmd {
	// The vertex slots hold raw words; XA and friends live at
	// consecutive word offsets from 0x0C to 0x1A.
	words := func(off int) uint16 { return v.vramWord(addr + off) }
	c := cmd{
		ctrl: words(0x00),
		link: words(0x02),
		pmod: words(0x04),
		colr: words(0x06),
		srca: words(0x08),
		size: words(0x0A),
		grda: words(0x1C),
	}
	for i := 0; i < 4; i += 1 {
		c.raw[i] = pt{
			x: decodeCoord(words(0x0C + i*4)),
			y: decodeCoord(words(0x0E + i*4)),
		}
	}
	c.rawW = int(words(0x10))
	c.rawH = int(words(0x12))
	return c
}

// Draw runs the command list now, starting at VRAM byte address 0.
// Draw state resets first: system clip is the full display, the user
// clip is invalid and the local coordinate is (0, 0).
//
// At completion CEF is set, BEF takes the previous CEF value, the
// draw end flag is raised, and LOPR and COPR hold the address of
// the last command processed.
func (v *VDP1) Draw() {
	prevCEF := v.reg(regEDSR) & 1
	// Clear CEF while drawing; BEF is left as it was until the
	// completion write below.
	v.setReg(regEDSR, v.reg(regEDSR)&0x0002)

	v.sysClip = rect{x1: 0, y1: 0, x2: v.width - 1, y2: v.height - 1}
	v.userClip = rect{}
	v.userValid = false
	v.localX = 0
	v.localY = 0

	addr := 0
	last := 0
	var stack []int
	stop := false
	for count := 0; count < maxCommands && !stop; count += 1 {
		last = addr
		v.setReg(regCOPR, uint16(addr))
		c := v.loadCmd(addr)
		if c.ctrl&0x8000 != 0 {
			// End command: process nothing, stop here. LOPR
			// was updated to this address above via last.
			break
		}
		jp := (c.ctrl >> 12) & 0x7
		skip := jp >= 4
		if !skip {
			v.execCmd(c)
		}
		linkAddr := int(c.link) * 8 & vramMask
		switch jp {
		case 0, 4: // next, skip next
			addr = (addr + 0x20) & vramMask
		case 1, 5: // assign, skip assign
			addr = linkAddr
		case 2, 6: // call, skip call
			stack = append(stack, (addr+0x20)&vramMask)
			addr = linkAddr
		case 3, 7: // return, skip return
			if len(stack) == 0 {
				stop = true
			} else {
				addr = stack[len(stack)-1]
				stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
			}
		}
	}

	v.setReg(regLOPR, uint16(last))
	v.setReg(regCOPR, uint16(last))
	v.setReg(regEDSR, uint16(1|(prevCEF<<1)))
	v.setReg(regMODR, v.composeMODR())
	v.drawEnd = true
}

// execCmd executes one command. Jump handling lives in Draw.
func (v *VDP1) execCmd(c cmd) {
	sel := c.ctrl & 0xF
	switch sel {
	case 8: // user clipping set, absolute screen coordinates
		v.userClip = normRect(c.raw[0].x, c.raw[0].y, c.raw[2].x, c.raw[2].y)
		v.userValid = true
		return
	case 9: // system clipping set, absolute screen coordinates
		v.sysClip = normRect(c.raw[0].x, c.raw[0].y, c.raw[2].x, c.raw[2].y)
		return
	case 10: // local coordinate set
		v.localX = c.raw[0].x
		v.localY = c.raw[0].y
		return
	}

	// Drawing commands: vertices are relative to the local
	// coordinate.
	var pts [4]pt
	for i := 0; i < 4; i += 1 {
		pts[i] = pt{x: c.raw[i].x + v.localX, y: c.raw[i].y + v.localY}
	}
	// CMDSIZE width field holds (dots/8 minus 1) in bits 13-8.
	srcW := ((int(c.size>>8) & 0x3F) + 1) * 8
	srcH := int(c.size&0xFF) + 1

	switch sel {
	case 0: // normal sprite, texture sampled 1:1
		bbox := rect{x1: pts[0].x, y1: pts[0].y, x2: pts[0].x + srcW - 1, y2: pts[0].y + srcH - 1}
		ctx := v.makeCtx(c, bbox)
		v.drawSpriteRect(ctx, c, srcW, srcH, pts[0].x, pts[0].y, srcW, srcH)
	case 1: // scaled sprite
		v.execScaled(c, pts, srcW, srcH)
	case 2: // distorted sprite
		bbox := quadBBox(pts)
		ctx := v.makeCtx(c, bbox)
		v.rasterQuad(ctx, c, pts, true, srcW, srcH)
	case 4: // polygon
		bbox := quadBBox(pts)
		ctx := v.makeCtx(c, bbox)
		v.rasterQuad(ctx, c, pts, false, srcW, srcH)
	case 5: // polyline: edges A-B, B-C, C-D, D-A
		bbox := quadBBox(pts)
		ctx := v.makeCtx(c, bbox)
		v.drawLine(ctx, c, pts[0], pts[1], 0, 1)
		v.drawLine(ctx, c, pts[1], pts[2], 1, 2)
		v.drawLine(ctx, c, pts[2], pts[3], 2, 3)
		v.drawLine(ctx, c, pts[3], pts[0], 3, 0)
	case 6: // line: edge A-B only
		bbox := quadBBox([4]pt{pts[0], pts[1], pts[0], pts[1]})
		ctx := v.makeCtx(c, bbox)
		v.drawLine(ctx, c, pts[0], pts[1], 0, 1)
	default:
		// Other command values are ignored.
	}
}

// execScaled handles the scaled sprite command, both the zoom point
// equals 0 form (destination rectangle A to C) and the zoom point
// form (A is the zoom point, XB and YB are the size).
func (v *VDP1) execScaled(c cmd, pts [4]pt, srcW, srcH int) {
	zp := (c.ctrl >> 8) & 0xF
	if zp == 0 {
		destW := pts[2].x - pts[0].x + 1
		destH := pts[2].y - pts[0].y + 1
		if destW <= 0 || destH <= 0 {
			return
		}
		bbox := rect{x1: pts[0].x, y1: pts[0].y, x2: pts[2].x, y2: pts[2].y}
		ctx := v.makeCtx(c, bbox)
		v.drawSpriteRect(ctx, c, srcW, srcH, pts[0].x, pts[0].y, destW, destH)
		return
	}
	// XB and YB are unsigned word values here, not coordinates.
	// loadCmd kept them raw in rawW and rawH for exactly this.
	w, h := c.scaledSize()
	if w <= 0 || h <= 0 {
		return
	}
	anchorX := anchorOffset(int(zp&0x3), w)
	anchorY := anchorOffset(int((zp>>2)&0x3), h)
	ox := pts[0].x - anchorX
	oy := pts[0].y - anchorY
	bbox := rect{x1: ox, y1: oy, x2: ox + w - 1, y2: oy + h - 1}
	ctx := v.makeCtx(c, bbox)
	v.drawSpriteRect(ctx, c, srcW, srcH, ox, oy, w, h)
}

// anchorOffset maps an anchor selector to a pixel offset: 0 is the
// origin, 1 is half the size, 2 is the full size. Selector 3 is
// treated as the full size, a documented simplification.
func anchorOffset(sel, size int) int {
	switch sel {
	case 1:
		return size / 2
	case 2, 3:
		return size
	default:
		return 0
	}
}

func quadBBox(pts [4]pt) rect {
	r := rect{x1: pts[0].x, y1: pts[0].y, x2: pts[0].x, y2: pts[0].y}
	for i := 1; i < 4; i += 1 {
		if pts[i].x < r.x1 {
			r.x1 = pts[i].x
		}
		if pts[i].y < r.y1 {
			r.y1 = pts[i].y
		}
		if pts[i].x > r.x2 {
			r.x2 = pts[i].x
		}
		if pts[i].y > r.y2 {
			r.y2 = pts[i].y
		}
	}
	return r
}

// partCtx carries the per part drawing state derived from CMDPMOD
// and the current clip state.
type partCtx struct {
	calc      int
	colorMode int
	mesh      bool
	mon       bool
	ecd       bool
	spd       bool
	clip      bool
	cmod      int
	flipH     bool
	flipV     bool
	effSys    rect
	gour      [4][3]int
}

// makeCtx builds the part context. Pre clipping: when the Pclp bit
// is 0 (pre clipping enabled) and the part bounding box extends
// beyond the system clip rectangle, the effective system clip
// shrinks by 1 on the right and bottom for this part. That is a
// documented simplification of the hardware 1 pixel preclip rule.
func (v *VDP1) makeCtx(c cmd, bbox rect) partCtx {
	ctx := partCtx{
		calc:      int(c.pmod & 0x7),
		colorMode: int((c.pmod >> 3) & 0x7),
		mesh:      c.pmod&0x0100 != 0,
		mon:       c.pmod&0x8000 != 0,
		ecd:       c.pmod&0x0080 != 0,
		spd:       c.pmod&0x0040 != 0,
		clip:      c.pmod&0x0400 != 0,
		cmod:      int((c.pmod >> 9) & 1),
		flipH:     c.ctrl&0x0010 != 0,
		flipV:     c.ctrl&0x0020 != 0,
		effSys:    v.sysClip,
	}
	// CMDPMOD bit12 (HSS) is a documented no op here.
	if c.pmod&0x0800 == 0 {
		sc := v.sysClip
		if bbox.x1 < sc.x1 || bbox.y1 < sc.y1 || bbox.x2 > sc.x2 || bbox.y2 > sc.y2 {
			ctx.effSys.x2 -= 1
			ctx.effSys.y2 -= 1
		}
	}
	ctx.gour = v.gouraudTable(c.grda)
	return ctx
}

// clipPass applies the per dot clip tests in pipeline order:
// frame buffer bounds, system clip, then user clipping when the
// command enables it and a user rectangle is valid.
func (v *VDP1) clipPass(ctx partCtx, x, y int) bool {
	if x < 0 || x >= v.width || y < 0 || y >= v.height {
		return false
	}
	if !ctx.effSys.contains(x, y) {
		return false
	}
	if ctx.clip && v.userValid {
		inside := v.userClip.contains(x, y)
		if ctx.cmod == 0 && !inside {
			return false
		}
		if ctx.cmod == 1 && inside {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// gouraudTable reads the four RGB555 gouraud entries for corners
// A, B, C and D. The table byte address is (CMDGRDA and 0xFFF8)
// times 8.
func (v *VDP1) gouraudTable(grda uint16) [4][3]int {
	var out [4][3]int
	base := int(grda&0xFFF8) * 8
	for i := 0; i < 4; i += 1 {
		w := v.vramWord(base + i*2)
		out[i] = [3]int{
			int((w >> 10) & 0x1F),
			int((w >> 5) & 0x1F),
			int(w & 0x1F),
		}
	}
	return out
}

// scaledSize returns the raw XB and YB words of a scaled sprite
// command, which hold the destination size in the zoom point form.
// They are stored in the vertex slots as unsigned values alongside
// the decoded coordinates.
func (c cmd) scaledSize() (int, int) {
	return c.rawW, c.rawH
}

// fetch holds the result of one texture dot fetch.
type fetch struct {
	data        uint16
	end         bool
	transparent bool
	rgb         bool // gouraud applies to this data
}

// fetchTex samples one dot of the character pattern. u and vv are
// texture coordinates before flip handling; out of range values are
// clamped to the pattern edge, which matters for the distorted
// sprite right and bottom edges whose corner coordinate is srcW
// and srcH by definition.
func (v *VDP1) fetchTex(ctx partCtx, c cmd, srcW, srcH, uRaw, vvRaw int) fetch {
	if srcW <= 0 || srcH <= 0 {
		return fetch{transparent: true}
	}
	u := clampInt(uRaw, 0, srcW-1)
	vv := clampInt(vvRaw, 0, srcH-1)
	if ctx.flipH {
		u = srcW - 1 - u
	}
	if ctx.flipV {
		vv = srcH - 1 - vv
	}
	base := int(c.srca) * 8 & vramMask
	switch ctx.colorMode {
	case 0, 1:
		off := vv*(srcW/2) + u/2
		b := v.vramByte(base + off)
		var code uint16
		if u%2 == 0 {
			code = uint16(b >> 4)
		} else {
			code = uint16(b & 0xF)
		}
		if code == 0xF && !ctx.ecd {
			return fetch{end: true}
		}
		if code == 0 && !ctx.spd {
			return fetch{transparent: true}
		}
		if ctx.colorMode == 0 {
			return fetch{data: (c.colr & 0xFFF0) | code}
		}
		clutAddr := int(c.colr&0xFFF8) * 8
		data := v.vramWord(clutAddr + int(code)*2)
		// Gouraud applies to CLUT entries whose bit15 is 0 and
		// does not apply when bit15 is set; the entry is palette
		// bank data in that case. Documented rule from the spec.
		return fetch{data: data, rgb: data&0x8000 == 0}
	case 2, 3:
		bits := 6
		if ctx.colorMode == 3 {
			bits = 7
		}
		code := v.readBits(base, (vv*srcW+u)*bits, bits)
		allOnes := uint16((1 << bits) - 1)
		if code == allOnes && !ctx.ecd {
			return fetch{end: true}
		}
		if code == 0 && !ctx.spd {
			return fetch{transparent: true}
		}
		if ctx.colorMode == 2 {
			return fetch{data: (c.colr & 0xFFC0) | code}
		}
		return fetch{data: (c.colr & 0xFF80) | code}
	case 4:
		code := uint16(v.vramByte(base + vv*srcW + u))
		if code == 0xFF && !ctx.ecd {
			return fetch{end: true}
		}
		if code == 0 && !ctx.spd {
			return fetch{transparent: true}
		}
		return fetch{data: (c.colr & 0xFF00) | code}
	default: // color mode 5, RGB 32768 colors
		data := v.vramWord(base + (vv*srcW+u)*2)
		// Mode 5 has no end code; that is a documented rule.
		if data&0x7FFF == 0 && !ctx.spd {
			return fetch{transparent: true}
		}
		return fetch{data: data, rgb: true}
	}
}

// readBits reads n bits from a big endian bit stream starting at a
// bit offset from a pattern base byte address. Byte addresses wrap
// at the VRAM end.
func (v *VDP1) readBits(base, bitOff, n int) uint16 {
	var code uint16
	for i := 0; i < n; i += 1 {
		pos := bitOff + i
		b := v.vramByte(base + pos/8)
		bit := (b >> (7 - pos%8)) & 1
		code = code<<1 | uint16(bit)
	}
	return code
}

func clampInt(x, lo, hi int) int {
	if x < lo {
		return lo
	}
	if x > hi {
		return hi
	}
	return x
}

func floorDiv(a, b int64) int64 {
	if b < 0 {
		a = -a
		b = -b
	}
	if a >= 0 {
		return a / b
	}
	return -((-a + b - 1) / b)
}

// finishDot runs the tail of the per dot pipeline: color
// calculation, then the mesh test, then the frame buffer write.
// The caller has already done clipping and texture fetch.
func (v *VDP1) finishDot(ctx partCtx, x, y int, data uint16, g [3]int, gouraudOK bool) {
	data = v.applyCalc(ctx, x, y, data, g, gouraudOK)
	if ctx.mesh && ((x^y)&1) == 0 {
		return
	}
	v.writeDrawPixel(x, y, data)
}

// applyCalc applies the CMDPMOD color calculation mode to one dot.
// Modes: 0 replace, 1 shadow, 2 half transparent, 3 replace
// (prohibited value, documented as replace), 4 gouraud only,
// 5 gouraud plus half transparent, 6 gouraud plus shadow,
// 7 replace.
func (v *VDP1) applyCalc(ctx partCtx, x, y int, data uint16, g [3]int, gouraudOK bool) uint16 {
	switch ctx.calc {
	case 1:
		return (data & 0x8000) | 0x7FFE
	case 2:
		return blendHalf(data, v.readDrawPixel(x, y))
	case 4:
		if gouraudOK {
			return addGouraud(data, g)
		}
		return data
	case 5:
		d := data
		if gouraudOK {
			d = addGouraud(d, g)
		}
		return blendHalf(d, v.readDrawPixel(x, y))
	case 6:
		d := data
		if gouraudOK {
			d = addGouraud(d, g)
		}
		return (d & 0x8000) | 0x7FFE
	default:
		return data
	}
}

// blendHalf averages the 5 bit channels of the new and old pixels.
// Bit15 comes from the new pixel.
func blendHalf(newData, oldData uint16) uint16 {
	r := ((newData >> 10) & 0x1F) + ((oldData >> 10) & 0x1F)
	g := ((newData >> 5) & 0x1F) + ((oldData >> 5) & 0x1F)
	b := (newData & 0x1F) + (oldData & 0x1F)
	return (newData & 0x8000) | uint16(r>>1)<<10 | uint16(g>>1)<<5 | uint16(b>>1)
}

// addGouraud adds a gouraud RGB555 value to the base data channels
// with clamping to 31. Bit15 of the data is preserved.
func addGouraud(data uint16, g [3]int) uint16 {
	r := clampInt(int((data>>10)&0x1F)+g[0], 0, 31)
	gg := clampInt(int((data>>5)&0x1F)+g[1], 0, 31)
	b := clampInt(int(data&0x1F)+g[2], 0, 31)
	return (data & 0x8000) | uint16(r)<<10 | uint16(gg)<<5 | uint16(b)
}

// bilinearGouraud interpolates the four corner gouraud values at
// destination fraction (dx, dy) inside a destW by destH rectangle.
// Fixed point with 16 bit fractions, floored at the end, so the
// center pixel of an odd sized rectangle gets the exact per
// channel average of the four corners when it divides evenly.
func bilinearGouraud(ctx partCtx, dx, dy, destW, destH int) [3]int {
	fxQ := 0
	if destW > 1 {
		fxQ = dx * 65536 / (destW - 1)
	}
	fyQ := 0
	if destH > 1 {
		fyQ = dy * 65536 / (destH - 1)
	}
	var out [3]int
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch += 1 {
		a := ctx.gour[0][ch]
		b := ctx.gour[1][ch]
		cc := ctx.gour[2][ch]
		d := ctx.gour[3][ch]
		topQ := a<<16 + fxQ*(b-a)
		botQ := d<<16 + fxQ*(cc-d)
		valQ := topQ + fyQ*(botQ-topQ)/65536
		out[ch] = int(floorDiv(int64(valQ), 65536))
	}
	return out
}

// drawSpriteRect rasterizes an axis aligned sprite (normal and
// scaled forms) into the destination rectangle.
func (v *VDP1) drawSpriteRect(ctx partCtx, c cmd, srcW, srcH, destX, destY, destW, destH int) {
	if srcW <= 0 || srcH <= 0 || destW <= 0 || destH <= 0 {
		return
	}
	for dy := 0; dy < destH; dy += 1 {
		y := destY + dy
		for dx := 0; dx < destW; dx += 1 {
			x := destX + dx
			if !v.clipPass(ctx, x, y) {
				continue
			}
			u := dx * srcW / destW
			vv := dy * srcH / destH
			f := v.fetchTex(ctx, c, srcW, srcH, u, vv)
			if f.end {
				// End code stops the rest of this row.
				break
			}
			if f.transparent {
				continue
			}
			data := f.data
			if ctx.mon {
				data |= 0x8000
			}
			g := bilinearGouraud(ctx, dx, dy, destW, destH)
			v.finishDot(ctx, x, y, data, g, f.rgb)
		}
	}
}

// spanHit is one scanline and edge intersection in fixed point.
// All values are scaled by 65536.
type spanHit struct {
	xF int64
	uF int64
	vF int64
	gF [3]int64
}

// rasterQuad draws a distorted sprite (textured) or a polygon
// (flat) using edge interpolation. For each scanline of the quad
// bounding box the intersections with the four edges are found;
// the leftmost and rightmost hits bound the span and texture
// coordinates and gouraud values interpolate across the span with
// fixed point math, floored at the end.
func (v *VDP1) rasterQuad(ctx partCtx, c cmd, pts [4]pt, textured bool, srcW, srcH int) {
	tex := [4]pt{{0, 0}, {srcW, 0}, {srcW, srcH}, {0, srcH}}
	bbox := quadBBox(pts)
	edges := [4][2]int{{0, 1}, {1, 2}, {2, 3}, {3, 0}}
	for y := bbox.y1; y <= bbox.y2; y += 1 {
		var hits []spanHit
		for e := 0; e < 4; e += 1 {
			i := edges[e][0]
			j := edges[e][1]
			p := pts[i]
			q := pts[j]
			if p.y == q.y {
				if y == p.y {
					hits = append(hits, vertHit(p, tex[i], ctx.gour[i]))
					hits = append(hits, vertHit(q, tex[j], ctx.gour[j]))
				}
				continue
			}
			lo, hi := p.y, q.y
			if hi < lo {
				lo, hi = hi, lo
			}
			if y < lo || y > hi {
				continue
			}
			tQ := int64(y-p.y) * 65536 / int64(q.y-p.y)
			h := spanHit{
				xF: int64(p.x)<<16 + tQ*int64(q.x-p.x),
				uF: int64(tex[i].x)<<16 + tQ*int64(tex[j].x-tex[i].x),
				vF: int64(tex[i].y)<<16 + tQ*int64(tex[j].y-tex[i].y),
			}
			for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch += 1 {
				h.gF[ch] = int64(ctx.gour[i][ch])<<16 + tQ*int64(ctx.gour[j][ch]-ctx.gour[i][ch])
			}
			hits = append(hits, h)
		}
		if len(hits) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		left := hits[0]
		right := hits[0]
		for _, h := range hits {
			if h.xF < left.xF {
				left = h
			}
			if h.xF > right.xF {
				right = h
			}
		}
		xStart := int(floorDiv(left.xF, 65536))
		xEnd := int(floorDiv(right.xF, 65536))
		denom := right.xF - left.xF
		for x := xStart; x <= xEnd; x += 1 {
			if !v.clipPass(ctx, x, y) {
				continue
			}
			var u, vv int
			var g [3]int
			if denom == 0 {
				u = int(floorDiv(left.uF, 65536))
				vv = int(floorDiv(left.vF, 65536))
				for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch += 1 {
					g[ch] = int(floorDiv(left.gF[ch], 65536))
				}
			} else {
				num := (int64(x) << 16) - left.xF
				u = int(floorDiv(left.uF+num*(right.uF-left.uF)/denom, 65536))
				vv = int(floorDiv(left.vF+num*(right.vF-left.vF)/denom, 65536))
				for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch += 1 {
					g[ch] = int(floorDiv(left.gF[ch]+num*(right.gF[ch]-left.gF[ch])/denom, 65536))
				}
			}
			if textured {
				f := v.fetchTex(ctx, c, srcW, srcH, u, vv)
				if f.end {
					break
				}
				if f.transparent {
					continue
				}
				data := f.data
				if ctx.mon {
					data |= 0x8000
				}
				v.finishDot(ctx, x, y, data, g, f.rgb)
			} else {
				data := c.colr
				if ctx.mon {
					data |= 0x8000
				}
				// Non textured parts always take gouraud
				// as RGB data.
				v.finishDot(ctx, x, y, data, g, true)
			}
		}
	}
}

func vertHit(p pt, t pt, g [3]int) spanHit {
	h := spanHit{
		xF: int64(p.x) << 16,
		uF: int64(t.x) << 16,
		vF: int64(t.y) << 16,
	}
	for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch += 1 {
		h.gF[ch] = int64(g[ch]) << 16
	}
	return h
}

// drawLine draws one straight edge with the non textured color.
// Gouraud for a line is linear between the two endpoint corners
// given by gi and gj (A and B for the line command). Without
// gouraud color calculation the whole line uses CMDCOLR.
// Simplification: the line is stepped by max(abs(dx), abs(dy))
// with integer interpolation rather than hardware edge walking.
func (v *VDP1) drawLine(ctx partCtx, c cmd, p1, p2 pt, gi, gj int) {
	dx := p2.x - p1.x
	dy := p2.y - p1.y
	steps := absInt(dx)
	if absInt(dy) > steps {
		steps = absInt(dy)
	}
	for i := 0; i <= steps; i += 1 {
		x := p1.x
		y := p1.y
		if steps > 0 {
			x = p1.x + i*dx/steps
			y = p1.y + i*dy/steps
		}
		if !v.clipPass(ctx, x, y) {
			continue
		}
		data := c.colr
		if ctx.mon {
			data |= 0x8000
		}
		var g [3]int
		for ch := 0; ch < 3; ch += 1 {
			a := ctx.gour[gi][ch]
			b := ctx.gour[gj][ch]
			if steps == 0 {
				g[ch] = a
			} else {
				q := a<<16 + (i*65536/steps)*(b-a)
				g[ch] = int(floorDiv(int64(q), 65536))
			}
		}
		v.finishDot(ctx, x, y, data, g, true)
	}
}

func absInt(x int) int {
	if x < 0 {
		return -x
	}
	return x
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp1/vdp1.go ====================

// Package vdp1 implements the Sega Saturn VDP1 sprite and polygon
// processor. It owns no memory of its own: the caller supplies the
// VRAM slice, the frame buffer slice and the register page, all of
// which the system wires to the bus.
//
// Frame buffer layout: 512 KiB total, two banks of 256 KiB. Bank 0
// starts at offset 0 and bank 1 at offset 262144. The draw bank is
// the bank being rendered into; the display bank is the other one.
//
// Simplifications relative to real hardware are documented at the
// site where each one lives.
package vdp1

// Register page offsets, in bytes. All registers are 16 bit big
// endian words inside the 128 byte page.
const (
	regTVMR = 0x00
	regFBCR = 0x02
	regPTMR = 0x04
	regEWDR = 0x06
	regEWLR = 0x08
	regEWRR = 0x0A
	regEDSR = 0x10
	regLOPR = 0x12
	regCOPR = 0x14
	regMODR = 0x16
)

const (
	vramSize    = 512 * 1024
	vramMask    = vramSize - 1
	fbBankSize  = 256 * 1024
	maxCommands = 200000
)

// rect is an inclusive rectangle in frame buffer coordinates.
type rect struct {
	x1, y1, x2, y2 int
}

func normRect(x1, y1, x2, y2 int) rect {
	if x2 < x1 {
		x1, x2 = x2, x1
	}
	if y2 < y1 {
		y1, y2 = y2, y1
	}
	return rect{x1: x1, y1: y1, x2: x2, y2: y2}
}

func (r rect) contains(x, y int) bool {
	return x >= r.x1 && x <= r.x2 && y >= r.y1 && y <= r.y2
}

// VDP1 is the sprite processor state. Memory slices are shared with
// the caller; register values are read fresh from the page on every
// use and status values are written back into the page.
type VDP1 struct {
	vram []byte
	fb   []byte
	regs []byte

	width  int
	height int

	drawBank int
	drawEnd  bool
	prevPTM  uint16

	rotate func(x, y, line int) (int, int, bool)

	// Draw state, reset at the start of every Draw call.
	sysClip   rect
	userClip  rect
	userValid bool
	localX    int
	localY    int
}

// New creates a VDP1 bound to the supplied memory. The vram slice is
// expected to be 512 KiB, the frame buffer 512 KiB and the register
// page 128 bytes.
func New(vram, fb, regs []byte) *VDP1 {
	return &VDP1{vram: vram, fb: fb, regs: regs}
}

// SetDisplaySize records the frame buffer line stride in pixels and
// the clip bounds, taken from the VDP2 TVMD register by the system.
func (v *VDP1) SetDisplaySize(w, h int) {
	v.width = w
	v.height = h
}

func (v *VDP1) reg(off int) uint16 {
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(v.regs) {
		return 0
	}
	return uint16(v.regs[off])<<8 | uint16(v.regs[off+1])
}

func (v *VDP1) setReg(off int, val uint16) {
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(v.regs) {
		return
	}
	v.regs[off] = byte(val >> 8)
	v.regs[off+1] = byte(val)
}

// composeMODR builds the MODR readback value. This is a documented
// approximation of the hardware mode register readback.
func (v *VDP1) composeMODR() uint16 {
	return (v.reg(regTVMR) & 0xF) |
		(v.reg(regFBCR)&0x1F)<<4 |
		(v.reg(regPTMR)&0x3)<<9
}

// EightBit reports the TVMR depth bit: true means 8 bit per pixel
// frame buffer mode, false means 16 bit per pixel.
func (v *VDP1) EightBit() bool {
	return v.reg(regTVMR)&0x1 != 0
}

// DrawBank returns the index of the bank currently drawn into.
func (v *VDP1) DrawBank() int {
	return v.drawBank
}

// SetDrawBank sets the draw bank index. The display bank is always
// the other bank.
func (v *VDP1) SetDrawBank(b int) {
	v.drawBank = b & 1
}

// TakeDrawEnd reports the draw end flag once per completed Draw,
// clearing it as it is consumed.
func (v *VDP1) TakeDrawEnd() bool {
	if !v.drawEnd {
		return false
	}
	v.drawEnd = false
	return true
}

// Misc packs the extra state that save states need and the register
// page does not hold: bit0 is the draw bank, bit1 is the draw end
// flag pending, bits3-2 are the previous PTM value seen by
// PollTrigger.
func (v *VDP1) Misc() uint16 {
	m := uint16(v.drawBank & 1)
	if v.drawEnd {
		m |= 0x2
	}
	m |= (v.prevPTM & 0x3) << 2
	return m
}

// SetMisc restores the state packed by Misc.
func (v *VDP1) SetMisc(m uint16) {
	v.drawBank = int(m & 1)
	v.drawEnd = m&0x2 != 0
	v.prevPTM = (m >> 2) & 0x3
}

// SetRotateFunc installs the rotation coordinate transform used by
// SpriteWordAt while TVMR rotation is enabled. The system supplies
// it from the VDP2 rotation parameter tables.
func (v *VDP1) SetRotateFunc(f func(x, y, line int) (int, int, bool)) {
	v.rotate = f
}

// SpriteWordAt samples the display bank for the VDP2 sprite layer.
// In bounds positions always report present, even when the sampled
// word is zero; the VDP2 side applies the sprite priority 0
// transparency rule. Out of bounds positions report not present.
func (v *VDP1) SpriteWordAt(x, y, line int) (uint16, bool) {
	sx, sy := x, y
	// TVMR bit1 is the rotation enable.
	if v.reg(regTVMR)&0x2 != 0 && v.rotate != nil {
		rx, ry, ok := v.rotate(x, y, line)
		if !ok {
			return 0, false
		}
		sx, sy = rx, ry
	}
	if sx < 0 || sx >= v.width || sy < 0 || sy >= v.height {
		return 0, false
	}
	base := (v.drawBank ^ 1) * fbBankSize
	if v.EightBit() {
		off := base + sy*v.width + sx
		if off < 0 || off >= len(v.fb) {
			return 0, false
		}
		return uint16(v.fb[off]), true
	}
	off := base + (sy*v.width+sx)*2
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(v.fb) {
		return 0, false
	}
	return uint16(v.fb[off])<<8 | uint16(v.fb[off+1]), true
}

// FrameBoundary runs frame change processing: it decodes the frame
// change mode from (VBE, FCM, FCT), then swaps banks, erases and
// auto draws as the mode requires. Combinations not listed in the
// mode table do nothing.
func (v *VDP1) FrameBoundary() {
	tvmr := v.reg(regTVMR)
	fbcr := v.reg(regFBCR)
	ptmr := v.reg(regPTMR)
	vbe := (tvmr >> 3) & 1
	fcm := (fbcr >> 1) & 1
	fct := fbcr & 1
	ptm := ptmr & 0x3
	autoDraw := ptm == 0 || ptm == 2

	switch {
	case vbe == 0 && fcm == 0 && fct == 0:
		// 1 cycle mode.
		v.drawBank ^= 1
		v.eraseBank(v.drawBank)
		if autoDraw {
			v.Draw()
		}
	case vbe == 0 && fcm == 1 && fct == 0:
		// Manual erase: the display bank is erased, no swap.
		v.eraseBank(v.drawBank ^ 1)
	case vbe == 0 && fcm == 1 && fct == 1:
		// Manual change: swap only, then the CPU owned FCT bit
		// is cleared in the page.
		v.drawBank ^= 1
		v.setReg(regFBCR, v.reg(regFBCR)&^0x0001)
	case vbe == 1 && fcm == 1 && fct == 1:
		// Erase and change. VBE stays as written; FCT is cleared.
		v.drawBank ^= 1
		v.eraseBank(v.drawBank)
		if autoDraw {
			v.Draw()
		}
		v.setReg(regFBCR, v.reg(regFBCR)&^0x0001)
	default:
		// All other combinations do nothing.
	}
}

// eraseBank fills the erase rectangle of one frame buffer bank with
// the EWDR fill word. The rectangle comes from EWLR and EWRR: the X
// fields are in 8 dot units, the Y fields are in lines. The
// rectangle is clipped to the display size.
func (v *VDP1) eraseBank(bank int) {
	ewdr := v.reg(regEWDR)
	ewlr := v.reg(regEWLR)
	ewrr := v.reg(regEWRR)
	x1 := int((ewlr>>9)&0x7F) * 8
	y1 := int(ewlr & 0x1FF)
	x2 := int((ewrr>>9)&0x7F)*8 + 7
	y2 := int(ewrr & 0x1FF)
	if x1 < 0 {
		x1 = 0
	}
	if y1 < 0 {
		y1 = 0
	}
	if x2 >= v.width {
		x2 = v.width - 1
	}
	if y2 >= v.height {
		y2 = v.height - 1
	}
	if x1 > x2 || y1 > y2 || v.width <= 0 || v.height <= 0 {
		return
	}
	base := bank * fbBankSize
	if v.EightBit() {
		fill := byte(ewdr)
		for y := y1; y <= y2; y += 1 {
			off := base + y*v.width + x1
			for x := x1; x <= x2; x += 1 {
				if off >= 0 && off < len(v.fb) {
					v.fb[off] = fill
				}
				off += 1
			}
		}
		return
	}
	hi := byte(ewdr >> 8)
	lo := byte(ewdr)
	for y := y1; y <= y2; y += 1 {
		off := base + (y*v.width+x1)*2
		for x := x1; x <= x2; x += 1 {
			if off >= 0 && off+1 < len(v.fb) {
				v.fb[off] = hi
				v.fb[off+1] = lo
			}
			off += 2
		}
	}
}

// PollTrigger is called once per scanline. It watches the PTMR
// word: when the PTM bits become 1 and were not 1 at the previous
// poll, a manual draw starts.
func (v *VDP1) PollTrigger() {
	cur := v.reg(regPTMR) & 0x3
	prev := v.prevPTM
	v.prevPTM = cur
	if cur == 1 && prev != 1 {
		v.Draw()
	}
}

// readDrawPixel returns the current draw bank pixel at (x, y) as a
// 16 bit value. In 8 bit mode the stored byte is zero extended;
// color calculation in 8 bit mode operates on 16 bit values first,
// so this is the documented source for the old value there.
func (v *VDP1) readDrawPixel(x, y int) uint16 {
	base := v.drawBank * fbBankSize
	if v.EightBit() {
		off := base + y*v.width + x
		if off < 0 || off >= len(v.fb) {
			return 0
		}
		return uint16(v.fb[off])
	}
	off := base + (y*v.width+x)*2
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(v.fb) {
		return 0
	}
	return uint16(v.fb[off])<<8 | uint16(v.fb[off+1])
}

// writeDrawPixel writes one computed pixel to the draw bank. In 8
// bit mode only the low byte of the 16 bit value is stored.
func (v *VDP1) writeDrawPixel(x, y int, data uint16) {
	base := v.drawBank * fbBankSize
	if v.EightBit() {
		off := base + y*v.width + x
		if off >= 0 && off < len(v.fb) {
			v.fb[off] = byte(data)
		}
		return
	}
	off := base + (y*v.width+x)*2
	if off >= 0 && off+1 < len(v.fb) {
		v.fb[off] = byte(data >> 8)
		v.fb[off+1] = byte(data)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp1/vdp1_test.go ====================

package vdp1

import "testing"

// Synthetic fixtures only: fresh memory per test, commands written
// by hand into VRAM, pixels read back from the frame buffer slices.

type fixture struct {
	v    *VDP1
	vram []byte
	fb   []byte
	regs []byte
}

func newFixture() *fixture {
	f := &fixture{
		vram: make([]byte, 512*1024),
		fb:   make([]byte, 512*1024),
		regs: make([]byte, 128),
	}
	f.v = New(f.vram, f.fb, f.regs)
	f.v.SetDisplaySize(64, 64)
	return f
}

func putWord(b []byte, addr int, val uint16) {
	b[addr] = byte(val >> 8)
	b[addr+1] = byte(val)
}

func getWord(b []byte, addr int) uint16 {
	return uint16(b[addr])<<8 | uint16(b[addr+1])
}

func (f *fixture) setReg(off int, val uint16) { putWord(f.regs, off, val) }
func (f *fixture) getReg(off int) uint16      { return getWord(f.regs, off) }

// cmdSpec is one command table. The v array holds the eight vertex
// words in XA, YA, XB, YB, XC, YC, XD, YD order as raw words.
type cmdSpec struct {
	ctrl uint16
	link uint16
	pmod uint16
	colr uint16
	srca uint16
	size uint16
	grda uint16
	v    [8]uint16
}

func (f *fixture) writeCmd(addr int, s cmdSpec) {
	putWord(f.vram, addr+0x00, s.ctrl)
	putWord(f.vram, addr+0x02, s.link)
	putWord(f.vram, addr+0x04, s.pmod)
	putWord(f.vram, addr+0x06, s.colr)
	putWord(f.vram, addr+0x08, s.srca)
	putWord(f.vram, addr+0x0A, s.size)
	for i := 0; i < 8; i += 1 {
		putWord(f.vram, addr+0x0C+i*2, s.v[i])
	}
	putWord(f.vram, addr+0x1C, s.grda)
}

func (f *fixture) drawPixel(x, y int) uint16 {
	off := f.v.DrawBank()*262144 + (y*64+x)*2
	return getWord(f.fb, off)
}

func checkPix(t *testing.T, f *fixture, x, y int, want uint16) {
	t.Helper()
	if got := f.drawPixel(x, y); got != want {
		t.Errorf("pixel (%d, %d) = %#06x, want %#06x", x, y, got, want)
	}
}

// patternMode0 fills a 16x8 mode 0 pattern at 0x1000 with code 1,
// first dot code 2.
func (f *fixture) patternMode0() {
	for i := 0; i < 64; i += 1 {
		f.vram[0x1000+i] = 0x11
	}
	f.vram[0x1000] = 0x21
}

// Gate 1: command list with system clipping, local coordinate and
// a scaled sprite, plus END termination.
func TestCommandListGate(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.patternMode0()
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{ctrl: 9, v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 0, 0, 63, 63, 0, 0}})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 10, v: [8]uint16{10, 5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}})
	f.writeCmd(0x40, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 1, colr: 0x1230, srca: 0x200, size: 0x0107,
		v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 0, 0, 15, 7, 0, 0},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x60, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	// A polygon after END must never execute.
	f.writeCmd(0x80, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, colr: 0x7C00,
		v: [8]uint16{50, 50, 60, 50, 60, 60, 50, 60},
	})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 10, 5, 0x1232)
	checkPix(t, f, 11, 5, 0x1231)
	checkPix(t, f, 25, 12, 0x1231)
	checkPix(t, f, 9, 5, 0)
	checkPix(t, f, 26, 5, 0)
	checkPix(t, f, 55, 55, 0)
}

// Gate 2a: distorted sprite as a plain rectangle.
func TestDistortedSpriteRectangle(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	for row := 0; row < 32; row += 1 {
		for u := 0; u < 32; u += 1 {
			f.vram[0x1000+row*32+u] = byte(u/8 + 1)
		}
	}
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 2, pmod: 4 << 3, colr: 0x4000, srca: 0x200, size: 0x031F,
		v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 31, 0, 31, 31, 0, 31},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	// Center (16, 16): u is 16, code is 16/8 + 1 = 3.
	checkPix(t, f, 16, 16, 0x4003)
}

// Gate 2b: distorted sprite as a true trapezoid.
//
// Hand computation for pixel (16, 16) with quad A(8,0), B(23,0),
// C(31,31), D(0,31) and a 32x32 texture:
//
//	left edge A to D at y=16: x = 8 - 8*16/31 = 3.87, u = 0,
//	  vv = 32*16/31 = 16.52
//	right edge B to C at y=16: x = 23 + 8*16/31 = 27.13, u = 32,
//	  vv = 16.52
//	span fraction at x=16: (16 - 3.87) / (27.13 - 3.87) = 0.5215
//	u = 0.5215 * 32 = 16.69, floored to 16
//	code = 16/8 + 1 = 3, so the pixel is 0x4003.
func TestDistortedSpriteTrapezoid(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	for row := 0; row < 32; row += 1 {
		for u := 0; u < 32; u += 1 {
			f.vram[0x1000+row*32+u] = byte(u/8 + 1)
		}
	}
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 2, pmod: 4 << 3, colr: 0x4000, srca: 0x200, size: 0x031F,
		v: [8]uint16{8, 0, 23, 0, 31, 31, 0, 31},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 16, 16, 0x4003)
}

// Gate 3: polygon fill.
func TestPolygonFill(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, colr: 0x7C00,
		v: [8]uint16{10, 10, 29, 10, 29, 19, 10, 19},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 10, 10, 0x7C00)
	checkPix(t, f, 29, 19, 0x7C00)
	checkPix(t, f, 20, 15, 0x7C00)
	checkPix(t, f, 30, 15, 0)
	checkPix(t, f, 9, 15, 0)
}

// Gate 4: gouraud midpoint. The polygon is 21 by 21 so (20, 20) is
// the exact center. Corner channels are A(20,0,0), B(0,20,0),
// C(0,0,20), D(20,20,20); each channel sums to 40 over the four
// corners, so the center average is exactly (10, 10, 10), which
// packs to 10<<10 | 10<<5 | 10 = 0x294A. Base color is 0 and the
// color calculation mode is 4 (gouraud only), so the pixel is
// the interpolated gouraud value alone.
func TestGouraudMidpoint(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	putWord(f.vram, 0x2000, 0x5000) // A: RGB(20, 0, 0)
	putWord(f.vram, 0x2002, 0x0280) // B: RGB(0, 20, 0)
	putWord(f.vram, 0x2004, 0x0014) // C: RGB(0, 0, 20)
	putWord(f.vram, 0x2006, 0x5294) // D: RGB(20, 20, 20)
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, pmod: 4, colr: 0, grda: 0x0400,
		v: [8]uint16{10, 10, 30, 10, 30, 30, 10, 30},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 20, 20, 0x294A)
}

// Gate 5: mesh pattern.
func TestMesh(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, pmod: 0x0100, colr: 0x7C00,
		v: [8]uint16{10, 10, 29, 10, 29, 19, 10, 19},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	// (10 xor 10) and 1 is 0, so the dot is skipped.
	checkPix(t, f, 10, 10, 0)
	// (11 xor 10) and 1 is 1, so the dot is drawn.
	checkPix(t, f, 11, 10, 0x7C00)
}

// Gate 6: half transparent blending. Existing pixel RGB(0, 0, 31),
// new pixel RGB(31, 0, 0): channels become ((31+0)>>1, 0,
// (0+31)>>1) = (15, 0, 15), packed as 15<<10 | 15 = 0x3C0F.
func TestHalfTransparent(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	verts := [8]uint16{10, 10, 20, 10, 20, 20, 10, 20}
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{ctrl: 4, colr: 0x001F, v: verts})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 4, pmod: 2, colr: 0x7C00, v: verts})
	f.writeCmd(0x40, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 15, 15, 0x3C0F)
}

// Gate 7: user clipping, inside mode and outside mode.
func TestUserClipping(t *testing.T) {
	build := func(cmod uint16) *fixture {
		f := newFixture()
		f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{ctrl: 8, v: [8]uint16{20, 20, 0, 0, 29, 29, 0, 0}})
		f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{
			ctrl: 4, pmod: 0x0400 | (cmod << 9), colr: 0x7C00,
			v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 63, 0, 63, 63, 0, 63},
		})
		f.writeCmd(0x40, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
		f.v.Draw()
		return f
	}
	inside := build(0)
	checkPix(t, inside, 25, 25, 0x7C00)
	checkPix(t, inside, 15, 15, 0)
	outside := build(1)
	checkPix(t, outside, 25, 25, 0)
	checkPix(t, outside, 15, 15, 0x7C00)
}

// Gate 8a: 1 cycle frame change swaps banks, erases the new draw
// bank and auto draws; the display bank shows the drawn pixels.
func TestFrameChangeOneCycle(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.setReg(0x00, 0)      // TVMR: no VBE, 16 bit
	f.setReg(0x02, 0)      // FBCR: 1 cycle mode
	f.setReg(0x04, 0)      // PTMR: auto draw
	f.setReg(0x06, 0x4242) // EWDR
	f.setReg(0x08, 0)      // EWLR: X1 0, Y1 0
	f.setReg(0x0A, (7<<9)|63)
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, colr: 0x7C00,
		v: [8]uint16{5, 5, 10, 5, 10, 10, 5, 10},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	if f.v.DrawBank() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("draw bank before frame boundary = %d, want 0", f.v.DrawBank())
	}
	f.v.FrameBoundary()
	if f.v.DrawBank() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("draw bank after frame boundary = %d, want 1", f.v.DrawBank())
	}
	// The new draw bank was erased with the fill word where the
	// auto draw did not paint.
	checkPix(t, f, 30, 30, 0x4242)
	// Auto draw repainted the polygon into the new draw bank.
	checkPix(t, f, 5, 5, 0x7C00)
	// The display bank is the old bank and shows the drawn pixels.
	w, ok := f.v.SpriteWordAt(5, 5, 0)
	if !ok || w != 0x7C00 {
		t.Errorf("SpriteWordAt(5, 5) = %#06x, %v; want 0x7c00, true", w, ok)
	}
}

// Gate 8b: manual change swaps without erasing and clears FCT.
func TestFrameChangeManualChange(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.setReg(0x00, 0)
	f.setReg(0x02, 0x0003) // FBCR: FCM 1, FCT 1
	f.setReg(0x06, 0x4242)
	f.setReg(0x08, 0)
	f.setReg(0x0A, (7<<9)|63)
	f.v.FrameBoundary()
	if f.v.DrawBank() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("draw bank = %d, want 1", f.v.DrawBank())
	}
	if got := f.getReg(0x02); got != 0x0002 {
		t.Errorf("FBCR after manual change = %#06x, want 0x0002 (FCT cleared)", got)
	}
	// No erase happened: the new draw bank is still zeroed.
	checkPix(t, f, 30, 30, 0)
}

// Gate 9a: jump assign skips a command.
func TestJumpAssignSkips(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x100A, link: 0x40 / 8})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, colr: 0x7C00,
		v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 10, 0, 10, 10, 0, 10},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x40, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, colr: 0x03E0,
		v: [8]uint16{20, 20, 30, 20, 30, 30, 20, 30},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x60, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 5, 5, 0)
	checkPix(t, f, 25, 25, 0x03E0)
}

// Gate 9b: call and return run a subroutine command.
func TestJumpCallReturn(t *testing.T) {

	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.writeCmd(0x40, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 0x3004, colr: 0x001F,
		v: [8]uint16{20, 20, 30, 20, 30, 30, 20, 30},

// Gate 10: normal sprite with horizontal flip. Pattern codes are
// 5 at u=0 and 9 at u=7, so the flipped leftmost dot carries 9.
func TestNormalSpriteFlipH(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.vram[0x1000] = 0x51
	f.vram[0x1001] = 0x11
	f.vram[0x1002] = 0x11
	f.vram[0x1003] = 0x19
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 0x0010, colr: 0x1000, srca: 0x200, size: 0,
		v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 0, 0, 0x1009)
	checkPix(t, f, 7, 0, 0x1005)
