// Gate 11: CLUT color mode. Pattern code 3 selects CLUT entry 3,
// which holds green 0x03E0.
func TestCLUTMode(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	for i := 0; i < 4; i += 1 {
		f.vram[0x1000+i] = 0x33
	}
	putWord(f.vram, 0x2000+3*2, 0x03E0)
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 0, pmod: 1 << 3, colr: 0x0400, srca: 0x200, size: 0,
		v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 0, 0, 0x03E0)
}

// Gate 12: end code stops the rest of the row when ECD is 0 and is
// drawn as data when ECD is 1. Row codes are 1, 0xF, 1, 1, then 1s.
func TestEndCode(t *testing.T) {
	build := func(ecd uint16) *fixture {
		f := newFixture()
		f.vram[0x1000] = 0x1F
		f.vram[0x1001] = 0x11
		f.vram[0x1002] = 0x11
		f.vram[0x1003] = 0x11
		f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
			ctrl: 0, pmod: ecd << 7, colr: 0x1000, srca: 0x200, size: 0,
			v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0},
		})
		f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
		f.v.Draw()
		return f
	}
	off := build(0)
	checkPix(t, off, 0, 0, 0x1001)
	checkPix(t, off, 1, 0, 0)
	checkPix(t, off, 2, 0, 0)
	checkPix(t, off, 3, 0, 0)
	on := build(1)
	checkPix(t, on, 1, 0, 0x100F)
	checkPix(t, on, 2, 0, 0x1001)
}

// Gate 13: LOPR, COPR, EDSR and the draw end flag after a draw of
// two commands plus END at 0x40.
func TestStatusRegisters(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{ctrl: 10, v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 4, colr: 0x7C00,
		v: [8]uint16{0, 0, 10, 0, 10, 10, 0, 10},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x40, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	if got := f.getReg(0x12); got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("LOPR = %#06x, want 0x0040", got)
	}
	if got := f.getReg(0x14); got != 0x40 {
		t.Errorf("COPR = %#06x, want 0x0040", got)
	}
	if got := f.getReg(0x10); got&1 == 0 {
		t.Errorf("EDSR = %#06x, want CEF bit set", got)
	}
	if !f.v.TakeDrawEnd() {
		t.Error("TakeDrawEnd = false, want true once")
	}
	if f.v.TakeDrawEnd() {
		t.Error("TakeDrawEnd = true twice, want false the second time")
	}
}

// Extra gate: scaled sprite zoom point form. ZP is 5, so the
// horizontal anchor is half the width and the vertical anchor is
// half the height. The zoom point is (20, 20) and the size words
// XB and YB are 16 each, so the destination is (12, 12) to
// (27, 27).
func TestScaledZoomPoint(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	for i := 0; i < 32; i += 1 {
		f.vram[0x1000+i] = 0x11
	}
	f.writeCmd(0x00, cmdSpec{
		ctrl: 1 | (5 << 8), colr: 0x1000, srca: 0x200, size: 0x0007,
		v: [8]uint16{20, 20, 16, 16, 0, 0, 0, 0},
	})
	f.writeCmd(0x20, cmdSpec{ctrl: 0x8000})
	f.v.Draw()
	checkPix(t, f, 12, 12, 0x1001)
	checkPix(t, f, 27, 27, 0x1001)
	checkPix(t, f, 11, 12, 0)
	checkPix(t, f, 28, 28, 0)
}

// Extra gate: Misc packs and restores bank, draw end and previous
// PTM state.
func TestMiscRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture()
	f.v.SetMisc(0x000D) // bank 1, previous PTM 3
	if f.v.DrawBank() != 1 {
		t.Errorf("DrawBank = %d, want 1", f.v.DrawBank())
	}
	if got := f.v.Misc(); got != 0x000D {
		t.Errorf("Misc = %#06x, want 0x000d", got)
	}
	f.v.SetMisc(0)
	if got := f.v.Misc(); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Misc after clear = %#06x, want 0", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp2/layers.go ====================

package vdp2

// Color modes shared by every background layer.
const (
	col16 = iota
	col256
	col2048
	colRGB555
	colRGB888
)

// pix is one fetched layer dot before priority processing.
type pix struct {
	col      rgb
	dotColor int
	spPri    bool
	spCC     bool
}

// charCfg carries everything needed to fetch dots for one layer
// or one rotation parameter set.
type charCfg struct {
	colorMode int
	charSize  int // 0 is 1 by 1 cells, 1 is 2 by 2 cells
	bmen      bool
	bmsz      int
	pnb       bool // true is 1 word pattern names
	cnsm      bool
	spr       bool
	scc       bool
	splt      int
	scn       int
	planeSize int
	mapOffset int
	maps      [16]int
	craof     int
	tpon      bool
	// Bitmap pattern supplement fields.
	bmpPal int
	bmpr   bool
	bmcc   bool
}

func planeGrid(planeSize int) (int, int) {
	switch planeSize & 0x3 {
	case 1:
		return 2, 1
	case 2:
		return 1, 2
	case 3:
		return 2, 2
	default:
		return 1, 1
	}
}

func codeBits(colorMode int) int {
	switch colorMode {
	case col16:
		return 4
	case col256:
		return 8
	case col2048:
		return 11
	}
	return 0
}

// nbgCfg extracts the character configuration for NBG0 to NBG3,
// where idx runs 0 to 3 in that order.
func (v *VDP2) nbgCfg(idx int) charCfg {
	cfg := charCfg{}
	chctla := v.reg16(0x028)
	chctlb := v.reg16(0x02A)
	bgon := v.reg16(regBGON)
	switch idx {
	case 0:
		cfg.colorMode = int((chctla >> 4) & 0x7)
		cfg.bmsz = int((chctla >> 2) & 0x3)
		cfg.bmen = chctla&0x2 != 0
		cfg.charSize = int(chctla & 0x1)
		cfg.tpon = bgon&0x0100 != 0
		p := v.bmpnaFields(false)
		cfg.bmpPal, cfg.bmpr, cfg.bmcc = p.pal, p.pr, p.cc
	case 1:
		cfg.colorMode = int((chctla >> 12) & 0x3)
		cfg.bmsz = int((chctla >> 10) & 0x3)
		cfg.bmen = chctla&0x0200 != 0
		cfg.charSize = int((chctla >> 8) & 0x1)
		cfg.tpon = bgon&0x0200 != 0
		p := v.bmpnaFields(true)
		cfg.bmpPal, cfg.bmpr, cfg.bmcc = p.pal, p.pr, p.cc
	case 2:
		cfg.colorMode = col16
		if chctlb&0x2 != 0 {
			cfg.colorMode = col256
		}
		cfg.charSize = int(chctlb & 0x1)
		cfg.tpon = bgon&0x0400 != 0
	case 3:
		cfg.colorMode = col16
		if chctlb&0x20 != 0 {
			cfg.colorMode = col256
		}
		cfg.charSize = int((chctlb >> 4) & 0x1)
		cfg.tpon = bgon&0x0800 != 0
	}
	if cfg.colorMode > colRGB888 {
		cfg.colorMode = colRGB888
	}
	pnc := v.reg16(0x030 + idx*2)
	cfg.pnb = pnc&0x8000 != 0
	cfg.cnsm = pnc&0x4000 != 0
	cfg.spr = pnc&0x0200 != 0
	cfg.scc = pnc&0x0100 != 0
	cfg.splt = int((pnc >> 5) & 0x7)
	cfg.scn = int(pnc & 0x1F)
	plsz := v.reg16(0x03A)
	cfg.planeSize = int((plsz >> uint(idx*2)) & 0x3)
	mpofn := v.reg16(0x03C)
	cfg.mapOffset = int((mpofn >> uint(idx*4)) & 0x7)
	// Map register pairs: MPAB holds planes A and B, MPCD holds
	// planes C and D, each as 6 bit fields.
	ab := v.reg16(0x040 + idx*4)
	cd := v.reg16(0x042 + idx*4)
	cfg.maps[0] = int(ab & 0x3F)
	cfg.maps[1] = int((ab >> 8) & 0x3F)
	cfg.maps[2] = int(cd & 0x3F)
	cfg.maps[3] = int((cd >> 8) & 0x3F)
	cfg.craof = int((v.reg16(0x0E4) >> uint(idx*4)) & 0x7)
	return cfg
}

type bmpFields struct {
	pal int
	pr  bool
	cc  bool
}

// bmpnaFields reads BMPNA for NBG0 (low byte) or NBG1 (high byte).
func (v *VDP2) bmpnaFields(high bool) bmpFields {
	r := v.reg16(0x02C)
	if high {
		return bmpFields{pal: int((r >> 8) & 0x7), pr: r&0x2000 != 0, cc: r&0x1000 != 0}
	}
	return bmpFields{pal: int(r & 0x7), pr: r&0x20 != 0, cc: r&0x10 != 0}
}

// patternInfo is the decoded pattern name.
type patternInfo struct {
	charBase int
	palette  int
	spPri    bool
	spCC     bool
	flipH    bool
	flipV    bool
}

func (v *VDP2) decodePattern(cfg charCfg, w0, w1 uint16) patternInfo {
	if !cfg.pnb {
		// 2 word form: first word holds flips, special bits, and
		// the full 7 bit palette; second word holds the character.
		return patternInfo{
			charBase: int(w1 & 0x7FFF),
			palette:  int((w0 >> 5) & 0x7F),
			spPri:    w0&0x2000 != 0,
			spCC:     w0&0x1000 != 0,
			flipH:    w0&0x4000 != 0,
			flipV:    w0&0x8000 != 0,
		}
	}
	p := patternInfo{spPri: cfg.spr, spCC: cfg.scc}
	w := w0
	palData := func(cnsm1 bool) int {
		if cfg.colorMode == col16 {
			if cnsm1 {
				return int((w >> 12) & 0xF)
			}
			return int((w >> 10) & 0xF)
		}
		if cnsm1 {
			return int((w >> 12) & 0x7)
		}
		return int((w >> 10) & 0x7)
	}
	if cfg.charSize == 0 {
		if cfg.cnsm {
			p.charBase = ((cfg.scn & 0x1C) << 10) | int(w&0xFFF)
			p.palette = (cfg.splt << 4) | palData(true)
		} else {
			p.charBase = (cfg.scn << 10) | int(w&0x3FF)
			p.palette = (cfg.splt << 4) | palData(false)
			p.flipV = w&0x8000 != 0
			p.flipH = w&0x4000 != 0
		}
	} else {
		if cfg.cnsm {
			p.charBase = ((cfg.scn & 0x10) << 10) | (int((w>>2)&0xFFF) << 2)
			p.palette = (cfg.splt << 4) | palData(true)
		} else {
			p.charBase = ((cfg.scn & 0x1C) << 10) | (int((w>>2)&0x3FF) << 2)
			p.palette = (cfg.splt << 4) | palData(false)
			p.flipV = w&0x8000 != 0
			p.flipH = w&0x4000 != 0
		}
	}
	return p
}

// charDot reads one dot of one character. It returns the palette
// code for palette modes, or the direct color for RGB modes, plus
// the raw value used for transparency and special function tests.
func (v *VDP2) charDot(charNo, dotX, dotY int, cfg charCfg) (int, rgb, int) {
	base := charNo * 0x20
	switch cfg.colorMode {
	case col16:
		addr := base + dotY*4 + dotX/2
		b := v.vramByte(addr)
		code := int(b & 0xF)
		if dotX%2 == 0 {
			code = int(b >> 4)
		}
		return code, rgb{}, code
	case col256:
		code := int(v.vramByte(base + dotY*8 + dotX))
		return code, rgb{}, code
	case col2048:
		w := v.vramWord(base + (dotY*8+dotX)*2)
		return int(w & 0x7FF), rgb{}, int(w & 0x7FF)
	case colRGB555:
		w := v.vramWord(base + (dotY*8+dotX)*2)
		return 0, expand555(w & 0x7FFF), int(w & 0x7FFF)
	default: // colRGB888
		l := v.vramLong(base + (dotY*8+dotX)*4)
		c := rgb{int((l >> 16) & 0xFF), int((l >> 8) & 0xFF), int(l & 0xFF)}
		return 0, c, int(l & 0xFFFFFF)
	}
}

// assemble turns raw dot data into a pixel, or reports the dot as
// transparent. Palette modes look the color up in CRAM; RGB modes
// carry their color directly.
func (v *VDP2) assemble(cfg charCfg, code int, direct rgb, raw int, palette int, p patternInfo) (pix, bool) {
	if cfg.colorMode == colRGB555 || cfg.colorMode == colRGB888 {
		if raw == 0 && !cfg.tpon {
			return pix{}, false
		}
		return pix{col: direct, dotColor: raw, spPri: p.spPri, spCC: p.spCC}, true
	}
	dotColor := (palette << uint(codeBits(cfg.colorMode))) | code
	if dotColor == 0 && !cfg.tpon {
		return pix{}, false
	}
	return pix{
		col:      v.cramColorForDot(dotColor, cfg.craof),
		dotColor: dotColor,
		spPri:    p.spPri,
		spCC:     p.spCC,
	}, true
}

// cellPixel fetches the dot at source coords (sx, sy) in cell mode.
func (v *VDP2) cellPixel(cfg charCfg, sx, sy int) (pix, bool) {
	cellX := floorDiv(sx, 8)
	cellY := floorDiv(sy, 8)
	dotX := sx - cellX*8
	dotY := sy - cellY*8
	gridW, gridH := planeGrid(cfg.planeSize)
	planeX := floorMod(floorDiv(cellX, 64), gridW)
	planeY := floorMod(floorDiv(cellY, 64), gridH)
	plane := planeY*gridW + planeX
	mapVal := cfg.maps[plane]
	pageBase := ((mapVal + (cfg.mapOffset << 6)) * 0x2000) & 0x7FFFF
	inX := floorMod(cellX, 64)
	inY := floorMod(cellY, 64)
	var entryIdx int
	if cfg.charSize == 0 {
		entryIdx = inY*64 + inX
	} else {
		entryIdx = (inY/2)*32 + (inX / 2)
	}
	entrySize := 4
	if cfg.pnb {
		entrySize = 2
	}
	addr := pageBase + entryIdx*entrySize
	w0 := v.vramWord(addr)
	w1 := uint16(0)
	if !cfg.pnb {
		w1 = v.vramWord(addr + 2)
	}
	p := v.decodePattern(cfg, w0, w1)
	charNo := p.charBase
	dx, dy := dotX, dotY
	if cfg.charSize == 1 {
		subX := cellX & 1
		subY := cellY & 1
		if p.flipH {
			subX = 1 - subX
			dx = 7 - dx
		}
		if p.flipV {
			subY = 1 - subY
			dy = 7 - dy
		}
		charNo = p.charBase + subY*2 + subX
	} else {
		if p.flipH {
			dx = 7 - dx
		}
		if p.flipV {
			dy = 7 - dy
		}
	}
	code, direct, raw := v.charDot(charNo, dx, dy, cfg)
	return v.assemble(cfg, code, direct, raw, p.palette, p)
}

var bitmapSizes = [4][2]int{{512, 256}, {512, 512}, {1024, 256}, {1024, 512}}

// bitmapPixel fetches the dot at source coords in bitmap mode.
// Simplification: bytes per dot are 1 for 16 and 256 color modes
// (the 16 color code is the low nibble of the byte), 2 for 2048
// and RGB555 modes, and 4 for RGB888 mode, matching the address
// formula in the specification.
func (v *VDP2) bitmapPixel(cfg charCfg, sx, sy int) (pix, bool) {
	size := bitmapSizes[cfg.bmsz&0x3]
	x := floorMod(sx, size[0])
	y := floorMod(sy, size[1])
	base := ((cfg.maps[0] + (cfg.mapOffset << 6)) * 0x2000) & 0x7FFFF
	p := patternInfo{spPri: cfg.bmpr, spCC: cfg.bmcc}
	addr := base + y*size[0] + x // dot index, scaled below per mode
	switch cfg.colorMode {
	case col16:
		code := int(v.vramByte(addr) & 0xF)
		return v.assemble(cfg, code, rgb{}, code, cfg.bmpPal<<4, p)
	case col256:
		code := int(v.vramByte(addr))
		return v.assemble(cfg, code, rgb{}, code, cfg.bmpPal<<4, p)
	case col2048:
		w := v.vramWord(base + (y*size[0]+x)*2)
		return v.assemble(cfg, int(w&0x7FF), rgb{}, int(w&0x7FF), cfg.bmpPal<<4, p)
	case colRGB555:
		w := v.vramWord(base + (y*size[0]+x)*2)
		return v.assemble(cfg, 0, expand555(w&0x7FFF), int(w&0x7FFF), 0, p)
	default:
		l := v.vramLong(base + (y*size[0]+x)*4)
		c := rgb{int((l >> 16) & 0xFF), int((l >> 8) & 0xFF), int(l & 0xFF)}
		return v.assemble(cfg, 0, c, int(l&0xFFFFFF), 0, p)
	}
}

// scrollSource computes the source dot coords for NBG0 and NBG1,
// applying base scroll, line scroll, zoom, and vertical cell
// scroll. All intermediate math is in 1 over 256 fixed point.
// NBG2 and NBG3 use the integer path in fetchNBG instead.
func (v *VDP2) scrollSource(idx, ex, ey int) (int, int) {
	base := 0x070 + idx*0x10
	scrollReg := func(off int) int {
		intPart := signExtendWord(v.reg16(off)&0x7FF, 11)
		return intPart*256 + int(v.reg16(off+2)>>8)
	}
	scrollX := scrollReg(base)
	scrollY := scrollReg(base + 4)
	incX := int(v.reg16(base+8)&0x7)*256 + int(v.reg16(base+10)>>8)
	incY := int(v.reg16(base+12)&0x7)*256 + int(v.reg16(base+14)>>8)

	scrctl := v.reg16(0x09A)
	field := uint16(0)
	if idx == 0 {
		field = scrctl & 0x3F
	} else {
		field = (scrctl >> 8) & 0x3F
	}
	lss := int((field >> 4) & 0x3)
	lscx := field&0x2 != 0
	lscy := field&0x4 != 0
	lzmx := field&0x8 != 0
	vcsc := field&0x1 != 0

	if lscx || lscy || lzmx {
		u := v.reg16(0x0A0 + idx*4)
		table := (int(u&0x7) << 16) | int(v.reg16(0x0A2+idx*4)&0xFFFE)
		entry := ey >> uint(lss)
		// Walk the enabled fields in X, Y, zoom order. Each field
		// is two words, so one entry spans field count times 4
		// bytes.
		pos := 0
		entryBase := table + entry*countLineFields(field)*4
		readPair := func() (uint16, uint16) {
			a := v.vramWord(entryBase + pos*2)
			b := v.vramWord(entryBase + pos*2 + 2)
			pos += 2
			return a, b
		}
		if lscx {
			iw, fw := readPair()
			scrollX = signExtendWord(iw&0x7FF, 11)*256 + int(fw>>8)
		}
		if lscy {
			iw, fw := readPair()
			scrollY = signExtendWord(iw&0x7FF, 11)*256 + int(fw>>8)
		}
		if lzmx {
			iw, fw := readPair()
			z := int(iw&0x7)*256 + int(fw>>8)
			incX = z
			incY = z
		}
	}

	zmctl := v.reg16(0x098)
	var zmField uint16
	if idx == 0 {
		zmField = zmctl & 0x3
	} else {
		zmField = (zmctl >> 8) & 0x3
	}
	if zmField&0x2 != 0 {
		incX = 4 * 256
		incY = 4 * 256
	} else if zmField&0x1 != 0 {
		incX = 2 * 256
		incY = 2 * 256
	}

	srcX := scrollX + ex*incX
	srcY := scrollY + ey*incY

	if vcsc {
		u := v.reg16(0x09C)
		table := (int(u&0x7) << 16) | int(v.reg16(0x09E)&0xFFFE)
		col := ex >> 3
		iw := v.vramWord(table + col*4)
		fw := v.vramWord(table + col*4 + 2)
		// The vertical cell scroll integer word is treated as a
		// plain signed 16 bit integer part.
		srcY += int(int16(iw))*256 + int(fw>>8)
	}

	return floorDiv(srcX, 256), floorDiv(srcY, 256)
}

func countLineFields(field uint16) int {
	n := 0
	if field&0x2 != 0 {
		n++
	}
	if field&0x4 != 0 {
		n++
	}
	if field&0x8 != 0 {
		n++
	}
	return n
}

// fetchNBG fetches one dot of NBG layer idx at screen evaluation
// coords (ex, ey). Mosaic is applied by the caller by passing the
// snapped evaluation coords, so the scroll state used here is the
// state of the sample line, as documented in the specification.
func (v *VDP2) fetchNBG(idx, ex, ey int) (pix, bool) {
	cfg := v.nbgCfg(idx)
	var sx, sy int
	if idx < 2 {
		sx, sy = v.scrollSource(idx, ex, ey)
	} else {
		off := 0x090
		if idx == 3 {
			off = 0x094
		}
		scx := signExtendWord(v.reg16(off)&0x7FF, 11)
		scy := signExtendWord(v.reg16(off+2)&0x7FF, 11)
		sx = scx + ex
		sy = scy + ey
	}
	if cfg.bmen {
		return v.bitmapPixel(cfg, sx, sy)
	}
	return v.cellPixel(cfg, sx, sy)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp2/rotation.go ====================

package vdp2

// Rotation parameter handling. All math is stateless per line:
// the effective parameter set for a line is rebuilt from the
// parameter table in VRAM on every fetch.

// rotParams holds one decoded parameter set in mixed fixed point
// units. Values ending in 1024 are in 1 over 1024 units, values
// ending in 65536 are in 1 over 65536 units, and px, py, cx, and
// cy are plain integers.
type rotParams struct {
	xst1024, yst1024   int32
	dxst1024, dyst1024 int32
	dx1024, dy1024     int32
	a1024, b1024       int32
	c1024, d1024       int32
	px, py             int64
	cx, cy             int64
	mx1024, my1024     int32
	kx65536, ky65536   int32
	kast1024           int32
	dkast1024          int32
	dkax1024           int32
}

// rotLead returns the lead byte addresses of sets A and B.
func (v *VDP2) rotLead() (int, int) {
	up := v.reg16(0x0BC)
	lo := v.reg16(0x0BE)
	combined := (int(up&0x7) << 15) | int((lo>>1)&0x7FFF)
	leadA := ((combined &^ 0x40) << 1) & 0x7FFFF
	return leadA, leadA + 0x80
}

// decodePx decodes the 13 bit signed integer stored in a word
// whose sign sits in bit 15 and whose value sits in bits 12 to 0.
func decodePx(w uint16) int64 {
	n := int64(w & 0x1FFF)
	if n >= 0x1000 {
		n -= 0x2000
	}
	return n
}

// parseRotEntry decodes the 0x60 byte parameter block at addr.
func (v *VDP2) parseRotEntry(addr int) rotParams {
	var p rotParams
	pair := func(off, intBits int) int32 {
		return fixed1024(v.vramWord(addr+off), v.vramWord(addr+off+2), intBits)
	}
	p.xst1024 = pair(0x00, 12)
	p.yst1024 = pair(0x04, 12)
	p.dxst1024 = pair(0x0C, 3)
	p.dyst1024 = pair(0x10, 3)
	p.dx1024 = pair(0x14, 3)
	p.dy1024 = pair(0x18, 3)
	p.a1024 = pair(0x1C, 4)
	p.b1024 = pair(0x20, 4)
	p.c1024 = pair(0x24, 4)
	p.d1024 = pair(0x28, 4)
	p.px = decodePx(v.vramWord(addr + 0x34))
	p.py = decodePx(v.vramWord(addr + 0x36))
	p.cx = decodePx(v.vramWord(addr + 0x3C))
	p.cy = decodePx(v.vramWord(addr + 0x3E))
	p.mx1024 = pair(0x44, 12)
	p.my1024 = pair(0x48, 12)
	kpair := func(off int) int32 {
		iw := v.vramWord(addr + off)
		fw := v.vramWord(addr + off + 2)
		return int32(signExtendWord(iw&0xFF, 8))<<16 + int32(fw)
	}
	p.kx65536 = kpair(0x4C)
	p.ky65536 = kpair(0x50)
	// KAst is an unsigned 16 bit integer plus a 10 bit fraction.
	p.kast1024 = int32(v.vramWord(addr+0x54))<<10 + int32(v.vramWord(addr+0x56)>>6)
	p.dkast1024 = fixed1024(v.vramWord(addr+0x58), v.vramWord(addr+0x5A), 9)
	p.dkax1024 = fixed1024(v.vramWord(addr+0x5C), v.vramWord(addr+0x5E), 9)
	return p
}

// effectiveRotParams builds the parameters for one set on one
// line. When any read enable for the set is on, fields come from
// the per line entry, except Xst, Yst, and KAst, which come from
// the per line entry only when their own read enable is on and
// otherwise advance from the base entry by their per line delta.
// When no read enable is on, the base entry is used with the same
// delta advance, which is the stateless form of the hardware
// start address counters.
func (v *VDP2) effectiveRotParams(set, line int) rotParams {
	leadA, _ := v.rotLead()
	baseAddr := leadA + set*0x80
	base := v.parseRotEntry(baseAddr)
	rprctl := v.reg16(0x0B2)
	var en uint16
	if set == 0 {
		en = rprctl & 0x7
	} else {
		en = (rprctl >> 8) & 0x7
	}
	if en == 0 {
		p := base
		p.xst1024 = base.xst1024 + base.dxst1024*int32(line)
		p.yst1024 = base.yst1024 + base.dyst1024*int32(line)
		p.kast1024 = base.kast1024 + base.dkast1024*int32(line)
		return p
	}
	p := v.parseRotEntry(leadA + line*0x100 + set*0x80)
	if en&0x1 == 0 {
		p.xst1024 = base.xst1024 + base.dxst1024*int32(line)
	}
	if en&0x2 == 0 {
		p.yst1024 = base.yst1024 + base.dyst1024*int32(line)
	}
	if en&0x4 == 0 {
		p.kast1024 = base.kast1024 + base.dkast1024*int32(line)
	}
	return p
}

// rotCfg builds the character configuration for one rotation set.
// Character control and pattern name control are shared by both
// sets (there is a single RBG block in CHCTLB and PNCR), while
// plane size, over mode, map offset, maps, and the over pattern
// follow the set. The over fields are returned alongside.
func (v *VDP2) rotCfg(set int) (charCfg, int, uint16) {
	cfg := charCfg{}
	chctlb := v.reg16(0x02A)
	cfg.colorMode = int((chctlb >> 12) & 0x7)
	if cfg.colorMode > colRGB888 {
		cfg.colorMode = colRGB888
	}
	cfg.bmsz = int((chctlb >> 10) & 0x1)
	cfg.bmen = chctlb&0x0200 != 0
	cfg.charSize = int((chctlb >> 8) & 0x1)
	bgon := v.reg16(regBGON)
	cfg.tpon = bgon&0x1000 != 0
	p := v.bmpnbFields()
	cfg.bmpPal, cfg.bmpr, cfg.bmcc = p.pal, p.pr, p.cc
	pnc := v.reg16(0x038)
	cfg.pnb = pnc&0x8000 != 0
	cfg.cnsm = pnc&0x4000 != 0
	cfg.spr = pnc&0x0200 != 0
	cfg.scc = pnc&0x0100 != 0
	cfg.splt = int((pnc >> 5) & 0x7)
	cfg.scn = int(pnc & 0x1F)
	plsz := v.reg16(0x03A)
	if set == 0 {
		cfg.planeSize = int((plsz >> 8) & 0x3)
	} else {
		cfg.planeSize = int((plsz >> 12) & 0x3)
	}
	ovr := 0
	if set == 0 {
		ovr = int((plsz >> 10) & 0x3)
	} else {
		ovr = int((plsz >> 14) & 0x3)
	}
	mpofr := v.reg16(0x03E)
	if set == 0 {
		cfg.mapOffset = int(mpofr & 0x7)
	} else {
		cfg.mapOffset = int((mpofr >> 8) & 0x7)
	}
	base := 0x050 + set*0x10
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		r := v.reg16(base + i*2)
		cfg.maps[i*2] = int(r & 0x3F)
		cfg.maps[i*2+1] = int((r >> 8) & 0x3F)
	}
	cfg.craof = int(v.reg16(0x0E6) & 0x7)
	ovpn := v.reg16(0x0B8 + set*2)
	return cfg, ovr, ovpn
}

func (v *VDP2) bmpnbFields() bmpFields {
	r := v.reg16(0x02E)
	return bmpFields{pal: int(r & 0x7), pr: r&0x20 != 0, cc: r&0x10 != 0}
}

// coeffFor reads the coefficient table entry for one dot and
// returns the coefficient in 1 over 65536 units plus the raw word
// (whose top bit drives RPMD mode 2). It reports false when the
// coefficient table is disabled for this set.
func (v *VDP2) coeffFor(set int, p rotParams, x int) (int32, uint32, bool) {
	ktctl := v.reg16(0x0B4)
	var field uint16
	if set == 0 {
		field = ktctl & 0x1F
	} else {
		field = (ktctl >> 8) & 0x1F
	}
	if field&0x1 == 0 {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	kastNow := int64(p.kast1024) + int64(p.dkax1024)*int64(x)
	ki := floorDiv64(kastNow, 1024)
	ktaof := v.reg16(0x0B6)
	var ofs int
	if set == 0 {
		ofs = int(ktaof & 0x7)
	} else {
		ofs = int((ktaof >> 8) & 0x7)
	}
	byteAddr := (((ofs << 16) | int(ki&0xFFFF)) << 2) & 0x7FFFF
	var word uint32
	if field&0x2 != 0 {
		// KDBS: the coefficient table lives in CRAM instead.
		a := byteAddr & 0xFFF
		word = uint32(v.cramByte(a))<<24 | uint32(v.cramByte(a+1))<<16 | uint32(v.cramByte(a+2))<<8 | uint32(v.cramByte(a+3))
	} else {
		word = v.vramLong(byteAddr)
	}
	se := int32(uint32(word>>8)<<(32-24)) >> (32 - 24)
	return se, word, true
}

// applyCoeff replaces kx and ky from the coefficient by KMD mode.
// KLCE is ignored: line color insertion through the coefficient
// table is not modeled.
func (v *VDP2) applyCoeff(set int, p *rotParams, coeff int32) {
	ktctl := v.reg16(0x0B4)
	var kmd int
	if set == 0 {
		kmd = int((ktctl >> 2) & 0x3)
	} else {
		kmd = int((ktctl >> 10) & 0x3)
	}
	switch kmd {
	case 0:
		p.kx65536 = coeff
		p.ky65536 = coeff
	case 1:
		p.kx65536 = coeff
	case 2:
		p.ky65536 = coeff
	case 3:
		// Both scale factors come from the table parameters.
	}
}

// rotationSetFor picks the parameter set a rotation layer uses at
// one dot, following RPMD.
func (v *VDP2) rotationSetFor(layer, x, y, evalLine int) int {
	rpmd := int(v.reg16(regRPMD) & 0x3)
	isRBG0 := layer == layerRBG0
	switch rpmd {
	case 0:
		if isRBG0 {
			return 0
		}
		return 1
	case 1:
		if isRBG0 {
			return 1
		}
		return 0
	case 2:
		// Per line switching by the coefficient MSB read for the
		// line. The probe reads set A at dot 0 of the line, or
		// set B when only set B has its table enabled.
		msb := uint32(0)
		pa := v.effectiveRotParams(0, evalLine)
		if _, w, ok := v.coeffFor(0, pa, 0); ok {
			msb = w
		} else {
			pb := v.effectiveRotParams(1, evalLine)
			if _, w, ok := v.coeffFor(1, pb, 0); ok {
				msb = w
			}
		}
		setA := msb>>31 == 0
		if isRBG0 {
			if setA {
				return 0
			}
			return 1
		}
		if setA {
			return 1
		}
		return 0
	default: // mode 3
		inside := v.insideRPWindow(x, y)
		if isRBG0 {
			if inside {
				return 1
			}
			return 0
		}
		if inside {
			return 0
		}
		return 1
	}
}

// rotTransform runs the rotation matrix for one dot and returns
// source dot coords. Units throughout are 1 over 65536.
func rotTransform(p rotParams, x int) (int, int) {
	xst := int64(p.xst1024) << 6
	yst := int64(p.yst1024) << 6
	xv := xst + (int64(p.dx1024)<<6)*int64(x)
	yv := yst + (int64(p.dy1024)<<6)*int64(x)
	px := p.px << 16
	py := p.py << 16
	cx := p.cx << 16
	cy := p.cy << 16
	mx := int64(p.mx1024) << 6
	my := int64(p.my1024) << 6
	a := int64(p.a1024) << 6
	b := int64(p.b1024) << 6
	c := int64(p.c1024) << 6
	d := int64(p.d1024) << 6
	innerX := (a*(xv-px))>>16 + (b*(yv-py))>>16
	innerY := (c*(xv-px))>>16 + (d*(yv-py))>>16
	outX := cx + (int64(p.kx65536)*innerX)>>16 + mx
	outY := cy + (int64(p.ky65536)*innerY)>>16 + my
	return int(floorDiv64(outX, 65536)), int(floorDiv64(outY, 65536))
}

// fetchRotation fetches one rotation layer dot. evalX and evalY
// are screen coords; evalY is also the line used for parameter
// selection, which is how mosaic on rotation layers ends up using
// the sample line parameters.
func (v *VDP2) fetchRotation(set, evalX, evalY int) (pix, bool) {
	cfg, ovr, ovpn := v.rotCfg(set)
	p := v.effectiveRotParams(set, evalY)
	if coeff, _, ok := v.coeffFor(set, p, evalX); ok {
		v.applyCoeff(set, &p, coeff)
	}
	sx, sy := rotTransform(p, evalX)

	gridW, gridH := planeGrid(cfg.planeSize)
	fieldW := gridW * 512
	fieldH := gridH * 512
	outside := sx < 0 || sy < 0 || sx >= fieldW || sy >= fieldH
	if outside {
		switch ovr {
		case 0:
			sx = floorMod(sx, fieldW)
			sy = floorMod(sy, fieldH)
		case 1:
			return v.overPatternPixel(cfg, ovpn, sx, sy)
		default:
			// Modes 2 and 3 are both transparent outside here.
			// Mode 3 on hardware applies a display limit rather
			// than field limits; the field limit is used.
			return pix{}, false
		}
	}
	if cfg.bmen {
		return v.bitmapPixel(cfg, sx, sy)
	}
	return v.cellPixel(cfg, sx, sy)
}

// overPatternPixel samples the single over pattern entry for a
// dot outside the rotation field. Simplification: the OVPN
// register word is used as both words of the 2 word pattern
// entry, since the register page holds only one word per set for
// this value; its low bits then form the character number.
func (v *VDP2) overPatternPixel(cfg charCfg, ovpn uint16, sx, sy int) (pix, bool) {
	forced := cfg
	forced.pnb = false
	p := v.decodePattern(forced, ovpn, ovpn)
	dx := floorMod(sx, 8)
	dy := floorMod(sy, 8)
	if p.flipH {
		dx = 7 - dx
	}
	if p.flipV {
		dy = 7 - dy
	}
	code, direct, raw := v.charDot(p.charBase, dx, dy, forced)
	return v.assemble(forced, code, direct, raw, p.palette, p)
}

// FBRotationCoord returns the VDP1 frame buffer rotation read
// coords for a display dot, from the rotation parameter A
// viewpoint only. No rotation matrix is applied, per the frame
// buffer rotation read rule.
func (v *VDP2) FBRotationCoord(x, y, line int) (int, int, bool) {
	p := v.effectiveRotParams(0, line)
	xv := (int64(p.xst1024) << 6) + (int64(p.dx1024)<<6)*int64(x)
	yv := (int64(p.yst1024) << 6) + (int64(p.dy1024)<<6)*int64(x)
	return int(floorDiv64(xv, 65536)), int(floorDiv64(yv, 65536)), true
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp2/sprite.go ====================

package vdp2

// Sprite type fields from SPCTL SPTYPE. PR and CC positions are
// the least significant bit of a field that grows upward, so the
// priority field always occupies the top bits of the word and the
// color field always starts at bit 0. shadowPos is negative when
// the type has no shadow bit.
type spriteType struct {
	prPos, prCount int
	ccPos, ccCount int
	colorBits      int
	shadowPos      int
}

var spriteTypes = [16]spriteType{
	{15, 1, 12, 3, 11, -1}, // type 0
	{15, 1, 12, 3, 11, 11}, // type 1
	{14, 2, 12, 2, 11, 11}, // type 2
	{14, 2, 11, 3, 10, -1}, // type 3
	{13, 3, 12, 1, 11, 11}, // type 4
	{15, 1, 13, 2, 11, 11}, // type 5
	{14, 2, 13, 1, 11, 11}, // type 6
	{13, 3, 10, 3, 9, 9},   // type 7
	{15, 1, 0, 0, 11, -1},  // type 8
	{14, 2, 0, 0, 11, -1},  // type 9
	{15, 1, 13, 2, 11, -1}, // type A
	{13, 3, 0, 0, 11, -1},  // type B
	{15, 1, 12, 3, 11, -1}, // type C
	{14, 2, 12, 2, 11, -1}, // type D
	{13, 3, 12, 1, 11, -1}, // type E
	{15, 1, 13, 2, 11, -1}, // type F
}

// spriteInfo is the decoded sprite dot at one screen position.
// present reports a color candidate; shadow reports a shadow dot,
// which is never a color candidate; signal is the sprite window
// signal used by other layers at this dot.
type spriteInfo struct {
	present   bool
	shadow    bool
	signal    bool
	col       rgb
	prio      int
	ccRatio   int
	ccEnabled bool
}

func spriteRegValue(regs [4]uint16, idx int) int {
	r := regs[idx/2]
	if idx%2 == 0 {
		return int(r & 0x7)
	}
	return int((r >> 8) & 0x7)
}

func spriteRatioValue(regs [4]uint16, idx int) int {
	r := regs[idx/2]
	if idx%2 == 0 {
		return int(r & 0x1F)
	}
	return int((r >> 8) & 0x1F)
}

func (v *VDP2) decodeSprite(x, y int) spriteInfo {
	var out spriteInfo
	if v.spr == nil {
		return out
	}
	word, ok := v.spr.SpriteWordAt(x, y, y)
	if !ok {
		return out
	}
	spctl := v.reg16(0x0E0)
	sptype := int(spctl & 0xF)
	spclmd := spctl&0x20 != 0
	spccn := int((spctl >> 8) & 0x7)

	// The sprite window signal is independent of whether the dot
	// becomes a color candidate.
	if spctl&0x10 != 0 && !spclmd && sptype >= 2 && sptype <= 7 && word&0x8000 != 0 {
		out.signal = true
	}

	prioRegs := [4]uint16{v.reg16(0x0F0), v.reg16(0x0F2), v.reg16(0x0F4), v.reg16(0x0F6)}
	ratioRegs := [4]uint16{v.reg16(0x100), v.reg16(0x102), v.reg16(0x104), v.reg16(0x106)}
	sprOffset := int((v.reg16(0x0E6) >> 4) & 0x7)
	ccctl := v.reg16(regCCCTL)

	finish := func(prioIdx, ccIdx int, col rgb) spriteInfo {
		out.present = true
		out.col = col
		out.prio = spriteRegValue(prioRegs, prioIdx)
		out.ccRatio = spriteRatioValue(ratioRegs, ccIdx)
		ccen := ccctl&0x40 != 0
		if ccen {
			// SPCCCS gates sprite color calculation by comparing
			// the sprite priority number with the CC index. This
			// is the documented simplification of the condition.
			switch (spctl >> 12) & 0x3 {
			case 1:
				ccen = out.prio <= ccIdx
			case 2:
				ccen = out.prio == ccIdx
			case 3:
				ccen = out.prio >= ccIdx
			}
		}
		out.ccEnabled = ccen
		return out
	}

	if v.spr.EightBit() {
		code := int(word & 0xFF)
		if code == 0 {
			return out
		}
		// In 8 bit mode an RGB sprite word cannot exist, so the
		// dot is treated as a palette dot even when SPCLMD is 1.
		return finish(0, spccn, v.cramColorForDot(code, sprOffset))
	}

	t := spriteTypes[sptype]
	field := func(pos, count int) int {
		if count == 0 {
			return 0
		}
		return int((word >> uint(pos)) & uint16((1<<uint(count))-1))
	}
	prBits := field(t.prPos, t.prCount)
	prioIdx := prBits << uint(3-t.prCount)
	ccIdx := spccn
	if t.ccCount > 0 {
		ccIdx = field(t.ccPos, t.ccCount) << uint(3-t.ccCount)
	}
	colorField := int(word & uint16((1<<uint(t.colorBits))-1))
	colorMask := (1 << uint(t.colorBits)) - 1
	if t.shadowPos >= 0 && word&(1<<uint(t.shadowPos)) != 0 && colorField == colorMask^1 {
		out.shadow = true
		return out
	}
	if spclmd {
		if word&0x7FFF == 0 {
			return out
		}
		return finish(prioIdx, ccIdx, expand555(word&0x7FFF))
	}
	if colorField == 0 {
		return out
	}
	return finish(prioIdx, ccIdx, v.cramColorForDot(colorField, sprOffset))
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp2/vdp2.go ====================

// Package vdp2 implements the Sega Saturn VDP2 background and
// composition hardware as a pure function of VRAM, CRAM, the
// register page, and a sprite word source supplied by VDP1.
//
// Rendering holds no state between lines. Every line is recomputed
// from the three slices and the sprite source, and all rotation
// math is rebuilt from the parameter table for the requested line.
package vdp2

import "sort"

// SpriteSource supplies raw VDP1 frame buffer words to VDP2.
type SpriteSource interface {
	// SpriteWordAt returns the raw VDP1 display frame buffer word
	// at display coords (x, y) on scanline line, plus whether a dot
	// position exists there at all (false outside the frame buffer).
	SpriteWordAt(x, y, line int) (uint16, bool)
	// EightBit reports the VDP1 8 bit per pixel frame buffer mode.
	EightBit() bool
}

// VDP2 is the background processor. Its fields are the exact slices
// handed to New, so callers observe register writes made here and
// this type observes memory writes made by callers.
type VDP2 struct {
	vram []byte
	cram []byte
	regs []byte
	spr  SpriteSource
}

// New builds a VDP2 over the given slices. Expected lengths are
// 512K of VRAM, 4K of CRAM, and 512 bytes of registers.
func New(vram, cram, regs []byte, spr SpriteSource) *VDP2 {
	return &VDP2{vram: vram, cram: cram, regs: regs, spr: spr}
}

// Register offsets in the 512 byte register page.
const (
	regTVMD   = 0x000
	regTVSTAT = 0x004
	regRAMCTL = 0x00E
	regBGON   = 0x020
	regMZCTL  = 0x022
	regSFSEL  = 0x024
	regSFCODE = 0x026
	regRPMD   = 0x0B0
	regCCCTL  = 0x0EC
	regSFPRMD = 0x0EA
	regSFCCMD = 0x0EE
	regLNCLEN = 0x0E8
	regSDCTL  = 0x0E2
	regCLOFEN = 0x110
	regCLOFSL = 0x112
	regCCRLB  = 0x10E
)

// Layer identifiers in fixed tie break order for equal priority.
// Back screen and line color sit outside the sorted layer order.
const (
	layerSprite = iota
	layerRBG0
	layerRBG1
	layerNBG0
	layerNBG1
	layerNBG2
	layerNBG3
	layerBack
	layerLine
)

type rgb struct {
	r, g, b int
}

func (c rgb) pack() uint32 {
	return 0xFF000000 | uint32(c.r&0xFF)<<16 | uint32(c.g&0xFF)<<8 | uint32(c.b&0xFF)
}

func expand555(w uint16) rgb {
	exp := func(v uint16) int {
		return int(v)<<3 | int(v)>>2
	}
	return rgb{exp((w >> 10) & 0x1F), exp((w >> 5) & 0x1F), exp(w & 0x1F)}
}

func (v *VDP2) reg16(off int) uint16 {
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(v.regs) {
		return 0
	}
	return uint16(v.regs[off])<<8 | uint16(v.regs[off+1])
}

func (v *VDP2) setReg16(off int, val uint16) {
	if off < 0 || off+1 >= len(v.regs) {
		return
	}
	v.regs[off] = byte(val >> 8)
	v.regs[off+1] = byte(val)
}

func sliceByte(s []byte, addr int) byte {
	if addr < 0 || addr >= len(s) {
		return 0
	}
	return s[addr]
}

// vramByte reads VRAM with the address wrapped into the 512K space.
func (v *VDP2) vramByte(addr int) byte {
	return sliceByte(v.vram, addr&0x7FFFF)
}

func (v *VDP2) vramWord(addr int) uint16 {
	return uint16(v.vramByte(addr))<<8 | uint16(v.vramByte(addr+1))
}

func (v *VDP2) vramLong(addr int) uint32 {
	return uint32(v.vramWord(addr))<<16 | uint32(v.vramWord(addr+2))
}

func (v *VDP2) cramByte(addr int) byte {
	return sliceByte(v.cram, addr&0xFFF)
}

// DisplaySize decodes TVMD into the visible resolution.
func (v *VDP2) DisplaySize() (int, int) {
	tvmd := v.reg16(regTVMD)
	hreso := int(tvmd & 0x7)
	widths := [8]int{320, 352, 640, 704, 320, 352, 640, 704}
	w := widths[hreso]
	if hreso >= 4 {
		// Exclusive modes are already 480 line modes, so no
		// interlace doubling is applied on top of them.
		return w, 480
	}
	heights := [4]int{224, 240, 256, 256}
	h := heights[(tvmd>>4)&0x3]
	if (tvmd>>6)&0x3 == 3 {
		h = h * 2
	}
	return w, h
}

// TotalLines reports total lines per frame including blanking.
func (v *VDP2) TotalLines() int {
	tvmd := v.reg16(regTVMD)
	hreso := int(tvmd & 0x7)
	if hreso >= 4 {
		w := [8]int{320, 352, 640, 704, 320, 352, 640, 704}[hreso]
		if w == 352 || w == 704 {
			return 561
		}
		return 525
	}
	return 263
}

// SetTiming writes VCNT and the TVSTAT VBLANK and ODD bits for the
// line that is about to be stepped. The system calls it at each
// line start before stepping the CPUs.
func (v *VDP2) SetTiming(line int, oddField bool) {
	v.setReg16(0x00A, uint16(line&0x3FF))
	_, h := v.DisplaySize()
	st := v.reg16(regTVSTAT)
	st &^= (1 << 3) | (1 << 1)
	if line >= h || v.reg16(regTVMD)&0x8000 == 0 {
		st |= 1 << 3
	}
	if oddField {
		st |= 1 << 1
	}
	v.setReg16(regTVSTAT, st)
}

// SetHBlank writes the TVSTAT HBLANK bit.
func (v *VDP2) SetHBlank(in bool) {
	st := v.reg16(regTVSTAT)
	st &^= 1 << 2
	if in {
		st |= 1 << 2
	}
	v.setReg16(regTVSTAT, st)
}

// cramMode returns RAMCTL CRMD.
func (v *VDP2) cramMode() int {
	return int((v.reg16(regRAMCTL) >> 12) & 0x3)
}

// cramReadIndex resolves a CRAM index to a color by CRAM mode.
// Modes 0 and 1 read RGB555 words. Modes 2 and 3 read RGB888 longs
// whose bytes are split across the two halves of CRAM: bytes 0 and
// 1 sit at the low half offset and bytes 2 and 3 at the plus 0x800
// offset, so red is byte 1, green byte 2, and blue byte 3.
func (v *VDP2) cramReadIndex(idx int) rgb {
	switch v.cramMode() {
	case 0:
		return expand555(uint16(v.cramByte((idx&0x3FF)*2))<<8 | uint16(v.cramByte((idx&0x3FF)*2+1)))
	case 1:
		return expand555(uint16(v.cramByte((idx&0x7FF)*2))<<8 | uint16(v.cramByte((idx&0x7FF)*2+1)))
	default:
		li := idx & 0x3FF
		r := int(v.cramByte(li*2 + 1))
		g := int(v.cramByte(0x800 + li*2))
		b := int(v.cramByte(0x800 + li*2 + 1))
		return rgb{r, g, b}
	}
}

// cramColorForDot forms a CRAM index from a palette dot color with
// the layer color offset added into bits 10 to 8, then reads it.
func (v *VDP2) cramColorForDot(dotColor, offset int) rgb {
	idx := (dotColor & 0xFF) | ((((dotColor >> 8) + offset) & 0x7) << 8)
	return v.cramReadIndex(idx)
}

// tableEntryColor reads one back screen or line color table entry.
// Long entries are plain sequential bytes in VRAM, unlike the
// split CRAM long layout. The insert flag is bit 15 of a word
// entry or bit 31 of a long entry.
func (v *VDP2) tableEntryColor(addr int) (rgb, bool) {
	if v.cramMode() >= 2 {
		b0 := v.vramByte(addr)
		r := int(v.vramByte(addr + 1))
		g := int(v.vramByte(addr + 2))
		b := int(v.vramByte(addr + 3))
		return rgb{r, g, b}, b0&0x80 != 0
	}
	w := v.vramWord(addr)
	return expand555(w & 0x7FFF), w&0x8000 != 0
}

func (v *VDP2) tableEntrySize() int {
	if v.cramMode() >= 2 {
		return 4
	}
	return 2
}

// backColorForLine reads the back screen color for a line.
func (v *VDP2) backColorForLine(line int) rgb {
	up := v.reg16(0x0AC)
	addr := (int(up&0x7) << 16) | int(v.reg16(0x0AE))
	if up&0x8000 != 0 {
		addr += line * v.tableEntrySize()
	}
	c, _ := v.tableEntryColor(addr)
	return c
}

// lineColorForLine reads the line color entry and its insert flag.
func (v *VDP2) lineColorForLine(line int) (rgb, bool) {
	up := v.reg16(0x0A8)
	addr := (int(up&0x7) << 16) | int(v.reg16(0x0AA))
	if up&0x8000 != 0 {
		addr += line * v.tableEntrySize()
	}
	return v.tableEntryColor(addr)
}

type candidate struct {
	col       rgb
	prio      int
	ccRatio   int
	ccEnabled bool
	layer     int
}

func blend(a, b rgb, ratio int) rgb {
	mix := func(x, y int) int {
		return (x*ratio + y*(32-ratio)) / 32
	}
	return rgb{mix(a.r, b.r), mix(a.g, b.g), mix(a.b, b.b)}
}

func clamp255(x int) int {
	if x < 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if x > 255 {
		return 255
	}
	return x
}

// clofBit maps a layer to its bit in CLOFEN and CLOFSL, whose
// layout runs sprite, back, R0, N3, N2, N1, N0.
func clofBit(layer int) int {
	switch layer {
	case layerSprite:
		return 6
	case layerBack:
		return 5
	case layerRBG0, layerRBG1:
		return 4
	case layerNBG3:
		return 3
	case layerNBG2:
		return 2
	case layerNBG1:
		return 1
	case layerNBG0:
		return 0
	}
	return -1
}

func sdctlBit(layer int) int {
	switch layer {
	case layerBack:
		return 5
	case layerRBG0, layerRBG1:
		return 4
	case layerNBG3:
		return 3
	case layerNBG2:
		return 2
	case layerNBG1:
		return 1
	case layerNBG0:
		return 0
	}
	return -1
}

func lnclBit(layer int) int {
	switch layer {
	case layerSprite:
		return 5
	case layerRBG0, layerRBG1:
		return 4
	case layerNBG3:
		return 3
	case layerNBG2:
		return 2
	case layerNBG1:
		return 1
	case layerNBG0:
		return 0
	}
	return -1
}

// anyDisplayedLNCL reports whether any BGON enabled layer has its
// line color enable bit set. Used when no layer produced a dot.
func (v *VDP2) anyDisplayedLNCL() bool {
	bgon := v.reg16(regBGON)
	lncl := v.reg16(regLNCLEN)
	// BGON low bits run N0, N1, N2, N3, R0, R1 while LNCLEN bits
	// run N0, N1, N2, N3, R0, sprite, so map each enabled layer.
	pairs := [][2]int{{0, 0}, {1, 1}, {2, 2}, {3, 3}, {4, 4}, {5, 4}}
	for _, p := range pairs {
		if bgon&(1<<uint(p[0])) != 0 && lncl&(1<<uint(p[1])) != 0 {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (v *VDP2) colorOffset(layer int, col rgb) rgb {
	bit := clofBit(layer)
	if bit < 0 {
		return col
	}
	if v.reg16(regCLOFEN)&(1<<uint(bit)) == 0 {
		return col
	}
	base := 0x114
	if v.reg16(regCLOFSL)&(1<<uint(bit)) != 0 {
		base = 0x11A
	}
	off := func(off int) int {
		n := int(v.reg16(off) & 0x1FF)
		if n >= 256 {
			n -= 512
		}
		return n
	}
	return rgb{
		clamp255(col.r + off(base)),
		clamp255(col.g + off(base+2)),
		clamp255(col.b + off(base+4)),
	}
}

// RenderLine renders one visible line into fb, which is w by h
// XRGB8888 pixels. Only lines 0 to h minus 1 are expected.
func (v *VDP2) RenderLine(fb []uint32, y int) {
	w, h := v.DisplaySize()
	if y < 0 || y >= h || w <= 0 {
		return
	}
	base := y * w
	if base+w > len(fb) {
		return
	}
	tvmd := v.reg16(regTVMD)
	back := v.backColorForLine(y)
	if tvmd&0x8000 == 0 {
		fill := uint32(0xFF000000)
		if tvmd&0x0100 != 0 {
			fill = back.pack()
		}
		for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
			fb[base+x] = fill
		}
		return
	}
	lineCol, lineInsert := v.lineColorForLine(y)
	mzctl := v.reg16(regMZCTL)
	mzW := int((mzctl>>8)&0xF) + 1
	mzH := int((mzctl>>12)&0xF) + 1

	for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
		spr := v.decodeSprite(x, y)
		cands := make([]candidate, 0, 8)

		if spr.present && spr.prio != 0 {
			if v.windowPass(v.spriteWindowByte(), x, y, spr.signal) {
				cands = append(cands, candidate{spr.col, spr.prio, spr.ccRatio, spr.ccEnabled, layerSprite})
			}
		}

		// Rotation layers.
		bgon := v.reg16(regBGON)
		if bgon&0x30 != 0 {
			for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
				layer := layerRBG0 + i
				if bgon&(1<<uint(4+i)) == 0 {
					continue
				}
				ex, ey := x, y
				if mzctl&0x10 != 0 {
					ex = x - x%mzW
					ey = y - y%mzH
				}
				set := v.rotationSetFor(layer, x, y, ey)
				if pix, ok := v.fetchRotation(set, ex, ey); ok {
					v.addScrollCandidate(&cands, pix, layer, 4, x, y, spr.signal)
				}
			}
		}
		// Normal backgrounds.
		for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
			layer := layerNBG0 + i
			if bgon&(1<<uint(i)) == 0 {
				continue
			}
			ex, ey := x, y
			mzBit := uint(i)
			if i == 0 {
				mzBit = 0
			}
			// MZCTL enable bits run N0 bit 0, N1 bit 1, N2 bit 2,
			// N3 bit 3, so the loop index is the bit directly.
			if mzctl&(1<<mzBit) != 0 {
				ex = x - x%mzW
				ey = y - y%mzH
			}
			if pix, ok := v.fetchNBG(i, ex, ey); ok {
				v.addScrollCandidate(&cands, pix, layer, i, x, y, spr.signal)
			}
		}

		sort.SliceStable(cands, func(a, b int) bool {
			if cands[a].prio != cands[b].prio {
				return cands[a].prio > cands[b].prio
			}
			return cands[a].layer < cands[b].layer
		})

		backCand := candidate{back, 0, int((v.reg16(regCCRLB) >> 8) & 0x1F), v.reg16(regCCCTL)&0x8000 != 0, layerBack}
		lineCand := candidate{lineCol, 0, int(v.reg16(regCCRLB) & 0x1F), v.reg16(regCCCTL)&0x20 != 0, layerLine}

		list := make([]candidate, 0, 10)
		inserted := false
		if lineInsert && len(cands) > 0 {
			topBit := lnclBit(cands[0].layer)
			if topBit >= 0 && v.reg16(regLNCLEN)&(1<<uint(topBit)) != 0 {
				list = append(list, cands[0], lineCand)
				list = append(list, cands[1:]...)
				inserted = true
			}
		}
		if !inserted {
			if lineInsert && len(cands) == 0 && v.anyDisplayedLNCL() {
				list = append(list, lineCand, backCand)
				inserted = true
			} else {
				list = append(list, cands...)
				list = append(list, backCand)
			}
		}

		out := v.compose(list, inserted, x, y, spr)
		fb[base+x] = out.pack()
	}
}

// compose applies color calculation, color offset, and shadow to
// the ordered candidate list for one dot. The list always ends
// with the back screen candidate unless line color was placed on
// top of it.
func (v *VDP2) compose(list []candidate, inserted bool, x, y int, spr spriteInfo) rgb {
	top := list[0]
	out := top.col
	ccctl := v.reg16(regCCCTL)
	if len(list) >= 2 && top.ccEnabled && v.windowPass(v.reg16(0x0D6)>>8, x, y, spr.signal) {
		second := list[1].col
		if ccctl&0x0400 != 0 && ccctl&0x0100 == 0 {
			// Extended color calculation, ratio mode only. The
			// effective second image is a half blend down the
			// candidate chain before the main blend. The
			// hardware restriction of extended calculation to
			// normal TV modes is not applied here.
			if inserted {
				third := second
				haveThird := false
				if len(list) >= 4 {
					third = blend(list[2].col, list[3].col, 16)
					haveThird = true
				} else if len(list) >= 3 {
					third = list[2].col
					haveThird = true
				}
				if haveThird {
					second = blend(list[1].col, third, 16)
				}
			} else if len(list) >= 3 {
				second = blend(list[1].col, list[2].col, 16)
			}
		}
		if ccctl&0x0100 != 0 {
			// Addition mode.
			out = rgb{
				clamp255(top.col.r + second.r),
				clamp255(top.col.g + second.g),
				clamp255(top.col.b + second.b),
			}
		} else {
			ratio := top.ccRatio
			if ccctl&0x0200 != 0 {
				ratio = list[1].ccRatio
			}
			out = blend(top.col, second, ratio)
		}
	}
	out = v.colorOffset(top.layer, out)
	if spr.shadow {
		bit := sdctlBit(top.layer)
		if bit >= 0 && v.reg16(regSDCTL)&(1<<uint(bit)) != 0 {
			// Shadow halves the final color. TPSDSL is ignored:
			// transparent shadow handling is not modeled.
			out = rgb{out.r >> 1, out.g >> 1, out.b >> 1}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// addScrollCandidate converts a fetched scroll layer pixel into a
// candidate, applying special priority and special color
// calculation modes and the per layer window test.
func (v *VDP2) addScrollCandidate(cands *[]candidate, pix pix, layer, scrollIdx, x, y int, sprSignal bool) {
	regPrio := v.scrollPriority(scrollIdx)
	ratio := v.scrollCCRatio(scrollIdx)

	sfCodeMatch := false
	{
		sel := v.reg16(regSFSEL)
		code := uint16(v.reg16(regSFCODE) & 0xFF)
		if sel&(1<<uint(scrollIdx)) != 0 {
			code = v.reg16(regSFCODE) >> 8
		}
		sfCodeMatch = (pix.dotColor >> 3) == int(code)
	}

	prio := regPrio
	switch (v.reg16(regSFPRMD) >> uint(scrollIdx*2)) & 0x3 {
	case 1:
		sp := 0
		if pix.spPri {
			sp = 1
		}
		prio = (regPrio & 6) | sp
	case 2:
		sp := 0
		if sfCodeMatch {
			sp = 1
		}
		prio = (regPrio & 6) | sp
	case 3:
		// Mode 3 is forbidden on hardware; it is treated as
		// mode 0 here.
		prio = regPrio
	}
	if prio == 0 {
		return
	}

	ccEnabled := false
	switch (v.reg16(regSFCCMD) >> uint(scrollIdx*2)) & 0x3 {
	case 0:
		ccEnabled = v.reg16(regCCCTL)&(1<<uint(ccctlScrollBit(scrollIdx))) != 0
	case 1:
		ccEnabled = pix.spCC
	case 2:
		ccEnabled = sfCodeMatch
	case 3:
		// Undocumented for color calculation; treated as mode 0.
		ccEnabled = v.reg16(regCCCTL)&(1<<uint(ccctlScrollBit(scrollIdx))) != 0
	}

	if !v.windowPass(v.layerWindowByte(layer), x, y, sprSignal) {
		return
	}
	*cands = append(*cands, candidate{pix.col, prio, ratio, ccEnabled, layer})
}

func ccctlScrollBit(scrollIdx int) int {
	// CCCTL low byte bits run N0, N1, N2, N3, R0 at bits 0 to 4,
	// which matches the scroll index order used here.
	return scrollIdx
}

func (v *VDP2) scrollPriority(scrollIdx int) int {
	switch scrollIdx {
	case 0:
		return int(v.reg16(0x0F8) & 0x7)
	case 1:
		return int((v.reg16(0x0F8) >> 8) & 0x7)
	case 2:
		return int(v.reg16(0x0FA) & 0x7)
	case 3:
		return int((v.reg16(0x0FA) >> 8) & 0x7)
	default:
		return int(v.reg16(0x0FC) & 0x7)
	}
}

func (v *VDP2) scrollCCRatio(scrollIdx int) int {
	switch scrollIdx {
	case 0:
		return int(v.reg16(0x108) & 0x1F)
	case 1:
		return int((v.reg16(0x108) >> 8) & 0x1F)
	case 2:
		return int(v.reg16(0x10A) & 0x1F)
	case 3:
		return int((v.reg16(0x10A) >> 8) & 0x1F)
	default:
		return int(v.reg16(0x10C) & 0x1F)
	}
}

func floorDiv(a, b int) int {
	q := a / b
	if a%b != 0 && (a < 0) != (b < 0) {
		q -= 1
	}
	return q
}

func floorMod(a, b int) int {
	return a - floorDiv(a, b)*b
}

func floorDiv64(a, b int64) int64 {
	q := a / b
	if a%b != 0 && (a < 0) != (b < 0) {
		q -= 1
	}
	return q
}

func signExtendWord(w uint16, bits int) int {
	if bits <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if bits >= 32 {
		return int(int32(w))
	}
	return int(int32(uint32(w)<<(32-uint(bits))) >> (32 - uint(bits)))
}

// fixed1024 decodes a fixed point pair with 10 fraction bits. The
// integer word contributes intBits of signed integer, masked from
// its low bits, and the fraction word contributes its top 10 bits.
func fixed1024(intWord, fracWord uint16, intBits int) int32 {
	return int32(signExtendWord(intWord, intBits))<<10 + int32(fracWord>>6)
}

package vdp2

import "testing"

// fakeSprite is a synthetic sprite source. It returns the same
// word at every dot position.
type fakeSprite struct {
	word    uint16
	present bool
	eight   bool
}

func (f *fakeSprite) SpriteWordAt(x, y, line int) (uint16, bool) {
	return f.word, f.present
}

func (f *fakeSprite) EightBit() bool { return f.eight }

type fixture struct {
	v          *VDP2
	vram, cram []byte
	regs       []byte
	fb         []uint32
	w, h       int
}

func newFixture(spr SpriteSource) *fixture {
	f := &fixture{
		vram: make([]byte, 512*1024),
		cram: make([]byte, 4096),
		regs: make([]byte, 512),
	}
	f.v = New(f.vram, f.cram, f.regs, spr)
	f.setReg(0x000, 0x8000) // TVMD: DISP on, 320 by 224
	// Back screen: single blue entry at VRAM 0x4600.
	f.setReg(0x0AE, 0x4600)
	f.vramWord(0x4600, 0x001F)
	f.w, f.h = f.v.DisplaySize()
	f.fb = make([]uint32, f.w*f.h)
	return f
}

func (f *fixture) setReg(off int, val uint16) {
	f.regs[off] = byte(val >> 8)
	f.regs[off+1] = byte(val)
}

func (f *fixture) vramWord(addr int, val uint16) {
	f.vram[addr] = byte(val >> 8)
	f.vram[addr+1] = byte(val)
}

func (f *fixture) cram555(idx int, val uint16) {
	off := (idx & 0x3FF) * 2
	f.cram[off] = byte(val >> 8)
	f.cram[off+1] = byte(val)
}

func (f *fixture) fillChar(charNo int, b byte) {
	base := charNo * 0x20
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		f.vram[base+i] = b
	}
}

func (f *fixture) render() {
	for y := 0; y < f.h; y++ {
		f.v.RenderLine(f.fb, y)
	}
}

func (f *fixture) pixel(x, y int) uint32 {
	return f.fb[y*f.w+x]
}

func pack(r, g, b int) uint32 {
	return 0xFF000000 | uint32(r)<<16 | uint32(g)<<8 | uint32(b)
}

var (
	red   = pack(255, 0, 0)
	green = pack(0, 255, 0)
	blue  = pack(0, 0, 255)
	white = pack(255, 255, 255)
)

// setupBasicNBG0 builds the probe used by several tests: NBG0 in
// 16 color 1 word cell mode, plane A map value 1, cell 0 holding
// character 1 with palette 1. Character 1 is all code 1 except
// its first dot, which is code 2. CRAM 17 is red, CRAM 18 green.
func setupBasicNBG0(f *fixture) {
	f.setReg(0x020, 0x0001) // BGON: NBG0 on
	f.setReg(0x030, 0x8000) // PNCN0: 1 word patterns
	f.setReg(0x0F8, 0x0002) // PRINA: NBG0 priority 2
	f.setReg(0x040, 0x0001) // MPABN0: plane A map value 1
	f.setReg(0x078, 0x0001) // ZMXIN0: zoom increment 1
	f.setReg(0x07C, 0x0001) // ZMYIN0: zoom increment 1
	f.vramWord(0x2000, (1<<10)|1)
	f.fillChar(1, 0x11)
	f.vram[0x20] = 0x21 // first dot code 2, second dot code 1
	f.cram555(17, 0x7C00)
	f.cram555(18, 0x03E0)
}

func TestNBG0CellMode(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(nil)
	setupBasicNBG0(f)
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(0, 0); got != green {
		t.Fatalf("pixel(0,0) = %08x, want green %08x", got, green)
	}
	if got := f.pixel(1, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("pixel(1,0) = %08x, want red %08x", got, red)
	}
	if got := f.pixel(7, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("pixel(7,0) = %08x, want red %08x", got, red)
	}
	// Scroll right by 3: screen dot 0 shows pattern dot 3, and
	// screen dot 5 lands on the empty cell 1, showing the back
	// screen.
	f.setReg(0x070, 3) // SCXIN0
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(0, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("scrolled pixel(0,0) = %08x, want red %08x", got, red)
	}
	if got := f.pixel(5, 0); got != blue {
		t.Fatalf("scrolled pixel(5,0) = %08x, want back blue %08x", got, blue)
	}
}

func TestPatternNameVariants(t *testing.T) {
	// 2 word pattern: palette 2 from the word, special priority
	// bit set in the word, character 1 in the second word.
	f := newFixture(nil)

	f.setReg(0x078, 0x0001)
	f.setReg(0x07C, 0x0001)

	f.vramWord(0x2002, 1)
	f.fillChar(1, 0x11)
	f.cram555(33, 0x7C00) // palette 2, code 1
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(0, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("2 word pixel(0,0) = %08x, want red %08x", got, red)
	}

	// 1 word pattern with CNSM set: 12 bit character number and
	// palette in bits 15 to 12.
	g := newFixture(nil)
	g.setReg(0x020, 0x0001)
	g.setReg(0x030, 0xC000) // PNCN0: 1 word, CNSM on
	g.setReg(0x0F8, 0x0002)
	g.setReg(0x040, 0x0001)
	g.setReg(0x078, 0x0001)
	g.setReg(0x07C, 0x0001)
	g.vramWord(0x2000, (1<<12)|1)
	g.fillChar(1, 0x11)
	g.cram555(17, 0x7C00) // palette 1, code 1
	g.render()
	if got := g.pixel(0, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("CNSM pixel(0,0) = %08x, want red %08x", got, red)
	}
}

	}

// setupRotation builds RBG0 with the identity transform over the
// same probe pattern as the NBG0 test.
func setupRotation(f *fixture) {
	f.setReg(0x020, 0x0010) // BGON: RBG0 on
	f.setReg(0x038, 0x8000) // PNCR: 1 word patterns
	f.setReg(0x0FC, 0x0001) // PRIR: RBG0 priority 1
	f.setReg(0x050, 0x0001) // MPABRA: plane A map value 1

	f.vramWord(tab+0x10, 1) // dYst integer: advance Y by 1 per line
	f.vramWord(tab+0x14, 1) // dX integer: advance X by 1 per dot
	f.vramWord(tab+0x1C, 1) // matrix A: 1
	f.vramWord(tab+0x28, 1) // matrix D: 1
	f.vramWord(tab+0x4C, 1) // kx integer: 1
	f.vramWord(tab+0x50, 1) // ky integer: 1
}

func TestPriorityAndSpecialPriority(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(nil)
	// NBG0: solid red, cells 0 and 1.
	f.setReg(0x020, 0x0003) // BGON: NBG0 and NBG1 on
	f.setReg(0x030, 0x8000)
	f.setReg(0x040, 0x0001)
	f.setReg(0x078, 0x0001)
	f.setReg(0x07C, 0x0001)
	f.vramWord(0x2000, 1)
	f.vramWord(0x2002, 1)
	f.fillChar(1, 0x11)
	f.cram555(1, 0x7C00)
	// NBG1: solid green via 2 word patterns, palette 3, char 2.
	// Cell 0 carries the special priority bit, cell 1 does not.
	f.setReg(0x032, 0x0000)
	f.setReg(0x044, 0x0002) // MPABN1: plane A map value 2
	f.setReg(0x088, 0x0001)
	f.setReg(0x08C, 0x0001)
	f.vramWord(0x4000, 0x2000|(3<<5))
	f.vramWord(0x4002, 2)
	f.vramWord(0x4004, 3<<5)
	f.vramWord(0x4006, 2)
	f.fillChar(2, 0x11)
	f.cram555(49, 0x03E0)
	// Phase A: plain register priorities 2 against 5, green wins.
	f.setReg(0x0F8, 0x0502)
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(0, 0); got != green {
		t.Fatalf("phase A pixel(0,0) = %08x, want green %08x", got, green)
	}
	// Phase B: SFPRMD mode 1 for NBG1, both registers at 4. The
	// special bit raises the cell 0 dot to priority 5 (green
	// wins) while the cell 1 dot ties at 4 and loses to NBG0 by
	// the fixed tie break order (red wins).
	f.setReg(0x0EA, 0x0004) // SFPRMD: NBG1 mode 1
	f.setReg(0x0F8, 0x0404)
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(0, 0); got != green {
		t.Fatalf("phase B pixel(0,0) = %08x, want green %08x (special priority 5)", got, green)
	}
	if got := f.pixel(8, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("phase B pixel(8,0) = %08x, want red %08x (tie at 4, NBG0 first)", got, red)
	}
}

func TestColorCalculationBlend(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(nil)
	f.setReg(0x020, 0x0003)
	// NBG0 top: solid red, palette 0 code 1.
	f.setReg(0x030, 0x8000)
	f.setReg(0x040, 0x0001)

	f.vramWord(0x2000, 1)
	f.fillChar(1, 0x11)

	f.setReg(0x044, 0x0003)
	f.setReg(0x088, 0x0001)
	f.setReg(0x08C, 0x0001)
	f.vramWord(0x6000, (2<<10)|3)
	f.fillChar(3, 0x11)
	f.cram555(33, 0x001F)
	// Priorities 5 over 3, NBG0 ratio 16, NBG0 CC enabled.
	f.setReg(0x0F8, 0x0305)
	f.setReg(0x108, 0x0010) // CCRNA: NBG0 ratio 16
	f.setReg(0x0EC, 0x0001) // CCCTL: N0CCEN on
	f.render()
	want := pack(127, 0, 127)
	if got := f.pixel(0, 0); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("blend pixel(0,0) = %08x, want %08x", got, want)
	}
}

func TestSpriteComposition(t *testing.T) {
	spr := &fakeSprite{word: 0x8003, present: true}
	f := newFixture(spr)
	setupBasicNBG0(f)
	// Make the NBG0 cell solid red for a clean witness: palette 0
	// code 1 via a second entry is overkill; reuse palette 1
	// code 1 red at CRAM 17 and accept the green first dot by
	// probing dot 1 instead of dot 0.
	f.setReg(0x0E0, 0x0000) // SPCTL: type 0
	f.cram555(3, 0x7FFF)    // sprite color code 3: white
	// Sprite word: PR bit 15 set means index 4, S4 in PRISC.
	f.setReg(0x0F4, 0x0006) // PRISC: S4 priority 6
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(1, 0); got != white {
		t.Fatalf("sprite pixel(1,0) = %08x, want white %08x (sprite priority 6)", got, white)
	}
	f.setReg(0x0F4, 0x0001) // S4 priority 1, under NBG0 priority 2
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(1, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("sprite pixel(1,0) = %08x, want red %08x (NBG0 wins)", got, red)
	}
	f.setReg(0x0F4, 0x0000) // S4 priority 0: sprite invisible
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(1, 0); got != red {
		t.Fatalf("sprite pixel(1,0) = %08x, want red %08x (sprite priority 0)", got, red)
	}
}

func TestZoom(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(nil)
	setupRowCells(f)
	// Register zoom 2: screen dot 4 samples source dot 8, which
	// is the blue cell 1.
	f.setReg(0x078, 0x0002) // ZMXIN0 = 2
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(4, 0); got != blue {
		t.Fatalf("zoom 2 pixel(4,0) = %08x, want blue %08x (source dot 8)", got, blue)
	}
	// Register zoom 3: screen dot 6 samples source dot 18, the
	// green cell 2.
	f.setReg(0x078, 0x0003)
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(6, 0); got != green {
		t.Fatalf("zoom 3 pixel(6,0) = %08x, want green %08x (source dot 18)", got, green)
	}
	// ZMHF forces increment 2 regardless of the register: screen
	// dot 6 samples source dot 12, the blue cell 1.
	f.setReg(0x098, 0x0001) // ZMCTL NBG0: ZMHF on
	f.render()
	if got := f.pixel(6, 0); got != blue {
		t.Fatalf("ZMHF pixel(6,0) = %08x, want blue %08x (source dot 12)", got, blue)
	}
}

func TestDisplaySizeAndTotalLines(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		tvmd      uint16
		w, h, tot int
	}{
		{0x0000, 320, 224, 263},
		{(1 << 4) | 1, 352, 240, 263},
		{2, 640, 224, 263},
		{7, 704, 480, 561},
		{4, 320, 480, 525},
		{5, 352, 480, 561},
		{3 << 6, 320, 448, 263},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		f := newFixture(nil)
		f.setReg(0x000, c.tvmd)
		w, h := f.v.DisplaySize()
		if w != c.w || h != c.h {
			t.Fatalf("TVMD %04x size = %dx%d, want %dx%d", c.tvmd, w, h, c.w, c.h)
		}
		if tot := f.v.TotalLines(); tot != c.tot {
			t.Fatalf("TVMD %04x total lines = %d, want %d", c.tvmd, tot, c.tot)
		}
	}
}

func TestSetTimingAndHBlank(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFixture(nil)
	f.v.SetTiming(300, true)
	if got := f.v.reg16(0x00A); got != 300 {
		t.Fatalf("VCNT = %d, want 300", got)
	}
	st := f.v.reg16(0x004)
	if st&(1<<3) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("TVSTAT %04x missing VBLANK at line 300 of 224", st)
	}
	if st&(1<<1) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("TVSTAT %04x missing ODD", st)
	}
	f.v.SetTiming(10, false)
	st = f.v.reg16(0x004)
	if st&(1<<3) != 0 || st&(1<<1) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("TVSTAT %04x should have VBLANK and ODD clear at line 10", st)
	}
	f.v.SetHBlank(true)
	if f.v.reg16(0x004)&(1<<2) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("TVSTAT missing HBLANK after SetHBlank(true)")
	}
	f.v.SetHBlank(false)
	if f.v.reg16(0x004)&(1<<2) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("TVSTAT HBLANK stuck after SetHBlank(false)")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-saturn/vdp2/windows.go ====================

package vdp2

// Window rectangles come from the WPS and WPE register pairs, or
// from a line window table for the X range when that window has
// its line window enable bit set. Ranges are inclusive.

// windowInside reports whether screen dot (x, y) is inside the
// window numbered w, which is 0 or 1.
func (v *VDP2) windowInside(w, x, y int) bool {
	sxReg := 0x0C0 + w*8
	exReg := 0x0C4 + w*8
	sx := int(v.reg16(sxReg) & 0x3FF)
	ex := int(v.reg16(exReg) & 0x3FF)
	upOff := 0x0D8 + w*4
	up := v.reg16(upOff)
	if up&0x8000 != 0 {
		table := (int(up&0x7) << 16) | int(v.reg16(upOff+2)&0xFFFE)
		addr := table + y*4
		sx = int(v.vramWord(addr) & 0x3FF)
		ex = int(v.vramWord(addr+2) & 0x3FF)
	}
	sy := int(v.reg16(0x0C2+w*8) & 0x1FF)
	ey := int(v.reg16(0x0C6+w*8) & 0x1FF)
	return x >= sx && x <= ex && y >= sy && y <= ey
}

// windowPass evaluates one per layer window control byte at a dot.
// The byte layout is LOG at bit 7, SWE at bit 5, SWA at bit 4,
// W1E at bit 3, W1A at bit 2, W0E at bit 1, and W0A at bit 0. When
// SWE is set, the sprite window signal replaces the rectangle
// test for the window slot selected by SWA.
func (v *VDP2) windowPass(b uint16, x, y int, sprSignal bool) bool {
	bb := byte(b)
	results := make([]bool, 0, 2)
	for w := 0; w < 2; w++ {
		enBit := uint(1 + w*2)
		areaBit := uint(0 + w*2)
		if bb&(1<<enBit) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		win := v.windowInside(w, x, y)
		if bb&0x20 != 0 && int((bb>>4)&0x1) == w {
			win = sprSignal
		}
		if bb&(1<<areaBit) != 0 {
			win = !win
		}
		results = append(results, win)
	}
	if len(results) == 0 {
		return true
	}
	if len(results) == 1 {
		return results[0]
	}
	if bb&0x80 != 0 {
		return results[0] || results[1]
	}
	return results[0] && results[1]
}

// layerWindowByte returns the window control byte for a layer.
// RBG0 and RBG1 share the RBG0 byte of WCTLC.
func (v *VDP2) layerWindowByte(layer int) uint16 {
	switch layer {
	case layerNBG0:
		return v.reg16(0x0D0) & 0xFF
	case layerNBG1:
		return v.reg16(0x0D0) >> 8
	case layerNBG2:
		return v.reg16(0x0D2) & 0xFF
	case layerNBG3:
		return v.reg16(0x0D2) >> 8
	case layerRBG0, layerRBG1:
		return v.reg16(0x0D4) & 0xFF
	case layerSprite:
		return v.reg16(0x0D4) >> 8
	}
	return 0
}

func (v *VDP2) spriteWindowByte() uint16 {
	return v.reg16(0x0D4) >> 8
}

// insideRPWindow evaluates the rotation parameter window from the
// low byte of WCTLD. Its bits are RPLOG at bit 7, RPW1E at bit 3,
// RPW1A at bit 2, RPW0E at bit 1, and RPW0A at bit 0. There is no
// sprite window input for this window.
func (v *VDP2) insideRPWindow(x, y int) bool {
	bb := byte(v.reg16(0x0D6) & 0xFF)
	results := make([]bool, 0, 2)
	for w := 0; w < 2; w++ {
		enBit := uint(1 + w*2)
		areaBit := uint(0 + w*2)
		if bb&(1<<enBit) == 0 {
			continue
		}
		win := v.windowInside(w, x, y)
		if bb&(1<<areaBit) != 0 {
			win = !win
		}
		results = append(results, win)
	}
	if len(results) == 0 {
		return true
	}
	if len(results) == 1 {
		return results[0]
	}
	if bb&0x80 != 0 {
		return results[0] || results[1]
	}
	return results[0] && results[1]
}

==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/README.md ====================

# go-snes

A from-scratch Super Nintendo Entertainment System core in Go for
iTaK Gaming, built the same way as the go-genesis, go-gameboy, and
go-nes cores in this repository: every chip is our own code, written
from published hardware documentation, proven against public
conformance corpora kept as local evidence only, and wrapped in a
libretro-compatible shell for the app. No third-party Go
dependencies.

## Status

**SNES-4 (the final slice): shipped. This core is
COMPLETE.**

- `libretro`: the cgo c-shared shell over the `system`
  package (library name "iTaK GoSNES", extensions
  sfc|smc, 256x224 XRGB8888, 60.0988 fps, 32040 Hz
  stereo, serialize passthrough to the machine state,
  SAVE_RAM and SYSTEM_RAM memory interfaces, joypad
  bits mapped 1:1). The desktop shell was driven through
  the iTaK engine bridge against Super Mario World as
  the ship gate: non-black pixel counts of 57,288 /
  53,601 / 53,534 / 53,259 at frames 120 / 400 / 600 /
  1200 (logo, title, and the full attract demo stay
  visible), audio non-silent from the title onward
  (34,084 non-silent samples in frames 301-400 alone),
  a 267,085-byte save state taken at a demo frame whose
  restore is byte-identical and whose 120-frame
  continuation matches the uninterrupted run in frame
  hash and in every audio sample.
- The road here caught one real bug worth recording:
  the SNES-4a black screen. SMW booted, showed its
  title, then faded to permanent black with the music
  still playing. Root cause was a PPU register decode
  bug, not NMI, joypad, DMA, or APU (all cleared by
  traces): `ppu/render.go` read the CGWSEL ($2130)
  fields from the wrong bit positions, so SMW's $12
  was misread as clip-main-inside-window and its
  full-width HDMA window color-mathed every pixel to
  black. The fix follows the documented $2130 layout
  (clip bits 7-6, sub transparent bits 5-4, addend
  bit 1, direct color bit 0; force-blacked pixels still
  get color math; halving divides before clamp and is
  suppressed on blacked and fallback pixels).
  Permanent gates live in `system/smw_gate_test.go`
  (they skip when the ROM is absent): the attract demo
  stays above 50,000 non-black pixels at frames 120 /
  320 / 450 / 600 / 1200 with two-run determinism, B
  exits the demo to file select, A and Start reach the
  overworld, and a save at the overworld restores with
  a byte-identical 30-frame continuation in frame hash
  and audio. Post-fix demo counts run 57,288 / 56,065 /
  53,601 / 53,534 / 53,259 against the reference core's
  53,300-53,700 band.
- Shipped as iTaK Gaming build 52 (version 1.0.52,
  published 2026-10-13): the app's SNES slot now loads
  `libgo_snes.so` (armeabi-v7a, Android 24, NDK r26b,
  the same target as the other Go cores) and Snes9x is
  retired from the SNES slot and no longer bundled.
  This is the fourth system running 100 percent on our
  own from-scratch cores, after Genesis (build 42),
  Game Boy and Game Boy Color (build 50), and NES
  (build 51). Host desktop frame cost for SMW measured
  13.055 ms per frame in the SNES-4 stage runs, inside
  the 16.68 ms NTSC budget; on-device play is David's
  TV check, as with builds 50 and 51.
- Known minor items (observed against the reference
  core during SNES-4a, none blocking): the title iris
  entrance phase timing differs slightly; some scenes
  show small sampled color deltas versus the reference;
  and Start pressed during the attract demo does not
  exit the demo on this core. That last one is
  consistent with SMW's own ROM code, whose demo-exit
  button mask excludes Start (Start works normally in
  the title, file select, and overworld flow); the
  reference core answers Start during the demo anyway,
  which remains unexplained.

**SNES-3: the audio unit: SPC700, SMP, and
S-DSP.**

- `chips/spc700`: the complete SPC700 audio CPU: all 256
  opcodes with published cycle counts, the direct-page
  base from the P flag, the page-1 stack, MOVW word
  operations, the bit operations (SET1/CLR1, TSET1/TCLR1,
  BBS/BBC, MOV1, AND1/OR1/EOR1/NOT1), CBNE/DBNZ loops,
  MUL and the documented DIV behavior (overflow flag,
  half-carry rule, divide by zero), DAA/DAS, TCALL, PCALL,
  BRK, STOP/SLEEP, and full serialization. Bus access
  order is modeled (dummy fetches, interleaved
  read-modify-write, the always-performed bit-op read)
  because the conformance corpus traces it. Conformance:
  the Tom Harte SPC700 single-step corpus (256 files,
  1,000 tests each, 256,000 tests) passes 100%: every
  register including PSW, every listed final RAM cell,
  the exact cycle count, and the data-carrying bus access
  sequence per test. The corpus is local evidence only,
  under `testroms/tomharte-spc700/`.
- `apu`: the SMP and the S-DSP. 64 KB of APU RAM, the
  documented 64-byte IPL ROM running the real boot
  handshake (0xAA/0xBB on the ports) and the block
  transfer protocol, the $00F0-$00FF IO window (CONTROL
  with timer enables, port clear strobes, and the IPL
  ROM enable; the DSP address/data latch with the bit-7
  write lockout; both communication port directions;
  RAM-backed aux ports; the three timers with 8000 Hz
  and 64000 Hz stage rates and read-clear 4-bit output
  counters), and the DSP stepped once per output sample
  at 32040 Hz: BRR sample decoding (all four filters,
  the range 13-15 sign collapse, end and loop handling
  with ENDX), Gaussian interpolation from the published
  512-entry table, ADSR and GAIN envelopes from the
  published 32-entry rate table, pitch modulation from
  the previous voice's output, the 15-bit noise LFSR,
  and the echo ring with its 8-tap FIR filter. Measured
  proofs, all derived from the documentation rather than
  another emulator: a looping BRR sine at pitch 0x385
  measures 439.00 Hz by zero crossings against 440.06
  expected at the original 32000 Hz rate (440.55 at the
  current 32040 Hz rate); timers count exactly 62 (T0, target 128) and
  640 (T2, target 100) increments in one simulated
  second; an echo impulse returns at exactly 512
  samples for EDL 1; and a hand-assembled tone program
  uploaded through the real IPL protocol posts its
  magic on the ports and plays.
- `system`: the APU is wired into the machine.
  $2140-$2143 read and write the real ports, the APU
  advances by exact ratio accumulation against the
  master clock (see the SNES-3 notes), and
  `AudioBuffer()` drains interleaved stereo samples at
  32040 Hz (about 533 per frame). Save states are
  version 2 and carry the full APU (RAM, SPC state,
  SMP timers and latches, DSP registers and per-voice
  state, echo position, and the clock ratio remainder):
  273,229 bytes for a cartridge with 8 KB of SRAM. The
  machine gate drives the IPL upload from a synthetic
  65816 program through the actual ports and continues
  31,920 audio values bit-identically across a
  mid-frame save and restore.

**SNES-2: PPU, DMA/HDMA, and the real machine.**

- `ppu`: the full PPU register file ($2100-$213F) and renderer.
  VRAM (64K words) with the VMAIN increment and rotate
  translations, the per-half prefetch read buffer (the first read
  after an address change returns the stale half; a $2139 read
  refills only the low half, a $213A read only the high half),
  CGRAM (256 colors, pair latch, writes landing in the active
  display area dropped), OAM (544 bytes, buffered pair writes),
  the shared-latch scroll registers, the Mode 7 registers with
  the $2134-$2136 multiply results, the $2137 counter latch, and
  $213E/$213F status. Rendering covers background modes 0-7
  with 8/16-pixel tiles, 2/4/8 bpp planar decode, per-layer
  tilemap sizes, offset-per-tile (modes 2, 4, 6; horizontal and
  vertical for mode 2, mode 4's per-column H-or-V entries, mode
  6 horizontal and vertical), Mode 7 affine with the documented
  26-bit product wrap and all four screen-over behaviors plus
  EXTBG, sprites in all eight size pairs with the 32-per-line
  and 34-tile limits and range/time over flags, OAM priority
  rotation, mosaic, both window channels with per-layer masks
  and the color window, color math (add/subtract, halved
  addend, sub screen or fixed color, clip-to-black and
  prevent-math window modes), direct color for 8bpp layers,
  brightness and forced blank, and interlace/overscan/
  pseudo-hires flags. Output is always 256x224 XRGB8888.
- `system`: the real frame-clocked machine. Master-clock line
  timing (1364 clocks per line, 262 lines, pre-render line 0,
  vblank from line 225, the short line 0 on alternating frames,
  interlace 262/263 line alternation), the CPU-side registers
  ($4200-$421F: NMI flag, TIMEUP, HVBJOY, the H/V IRQ timer,
  the multiply/divide unit with its 8/16-cycle result latency,
  $420D MEMSEL gating the map's FastROM speed class), the WRAM
  port, 8 channels of general DMA (all 8 transfer modes, the
  documented B-register patterns, live address/count readback),
  HDMA (per-line table walking, direct and indirect modes,
  repeat lines, the $00 terminator, mid-frame enable starting
  at the next display line), joypads (auto-read at vblank with
  the busy window, manual serial ports, both pads), and the APU
  mailboxes as plain latches in this slice (SNES-3 makes them
  the real ports).
  Save states cover the whole machine (CPU, WRAM, SRAM, PPU
  memory and registers, DMA/HDMA channel state, position and
  frame counters): 207,237 bytes for a cartridge with 8 KB of
  SRAM.
- Proofs for SNES-2: hand-derived synthetic render probes per
  mode (exact pixel values, not emulator comparisons), DMA and
  HDMA unit suites (mode 1 into VRAM, mode 3's paired-register
  pattern into CGRAM, decrement and fixed addressing, HDMA
  direct/indirect/repeat/terminator), and a whole-machine
  determinism gate: a synthetic ROM that DMA-uploads tiles, a
  tilemap, and a palette, then runs an HDMA brightness-band
  effect under an NMI frame counter; state and framebuffer are
  bit-identical across a save/restore boundary taken
  mid-frame. The Peter Lemon (Krom) test ROMs run headlessly
  as report-only evidence (they expose no CPU-readable
  verdicts): all five fetched ROMs (8bpp tilemap, Mode 3
  mosaic, Mode 7 rotate/zoom, HDMA window, HDMA color
  gradient) render non-blank frames. The Krom gradient ROM is
  what pinned the DMA mode 3 B-pattern to (0,0,1,1).

**SNES-1: CPU, cartridge, and test rig.**

- `chips/w65c816`: a complete W65C816S: all 256 opcodes, emulation
  and native modes, the M/X width flags with their register and
  stack consequences, 24-bit banked addressing, the full interrupt
  model (RESET, NMI, IRQ, ABORT at the documented level, BRK/COP
  with signature byte), WAI/STP, MVN/MVP block moves with the
  hardware's interrupt-suspension shape, and save-state
  serialization in the family style. Cycle accounting runs through
  a bus interface that reports a memory speed (fast, slow, XSlow)
  per access, because SNES instruction timing depends on ROM
  speed; internal cycles are counted separately so the DMA and
  HDMA engines of later slices can interleave against them.
- Conformance: the Tom Harte SingleStepTests 65816 corpus (the
  public v1 JSON set: 512 files, 256 opcodes in emulation and
  native modes, 10,000 randomized tests each, 5,120,000 tests)
  passes 100% on this machine. The runner checks every register,
  the final contents of every touched RAM cell, the exact cycle
  count, and the full sequence of valid bus accesses (address,
  direction, and data) per test. The corpus is local evidence
  only: it lives under `testroms/` and is never committed.
- `cart`: SNES cartridge header parsing with the standard scoring
  heuristic (checksum and complement pairing, map-mode agreement,
  reset vector sanity, title plausibility) across the LoROM
  (0x7FC0), HiROM (0xFFC0), and ExHiROM (0x40FFC0) candidate
  locations; title decoding in the documented JIS X 0201 encoding;
  ROM and RAM size exponents; the LoROM, HiROM, ExLoROM, and
  ExHiROM layouts; and the console memory map (Work RAM and its
  low mirror, ROM windows per layout, the LoROM and HiROM SRAM
  windows, per-region access speeds). Games whose headers name a
  coprocessor this core does not implement (SA-1, SuperFX, the
  DSP family, S-DD1, SPC7110, Cx4, and the rest) are refused at
  load with an error naming the chip; they are never silently
  misrun. The IO region (0x2000-0x5FFF in the system banks) is a
  documented placeholder in this slice: reads return an open-bus
  byte, writes are dropped, and the PPU, APU, and DMA slices
  replace it without changing the map's shape.
- `system` (SNES-1 form): CPU plus cartridge map, `RunCycles`,
  and a hand-assembled LoROM smoke program (mode switch, wide
  registers, long stores, a block move, and a long jump across
  banks) proving the parts integrate. SNES-2 replaced this rig
  with the real machine above, keeping its shape (exported
  CPU/Cart/Map, `New`, `LoadGame`, `Title`).
- `libretro`: a documented placeholder; the shell lands in
  SNES-4.
