==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/cart/cart.go ====================

// Package cart loads and describes a Super NES cartridge
// image, and implements the console memory map the CPU
// runs against: ROM windows for the LoROM, HiROM, ExLoROM,
// and ExHiROM layouts, battery-backed SRAM windows, the
// full 128 KB of Work RAM and its low mirror, and the
// system area whose IO registers belong to later slices.
//
// Written clean-room from the published cartridge header
// layout and the memory maps in the SNES development
// documentation (the layout Nintendo documents for licensees
// and that fullsnes records): the 64-byte internal header
// at file offset 0x7FC0 for LoROM images or 0xFFC0 for
// HiROM (0x40FFC0 for ExHiROM), its map-mode, chipset,
// size, checksum, and vector fields, and the standard
// scoring heuristic emulators use to decide which candidate
// header location a real image uses.
//
// Games that need a coprocessor v1 does not implement
// (SA-1, SuperFX, DSP-1 and friends, S-DD1, SPC7110, and
// the rest of the enhancement list) are detected from the
// chipset byte and the map mode, named in the header, and
// refused by Load with an error that names the chip: the
// core never silently misruns a game whose hardware it
// does not have.
package cart

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// Layout is a cartridge memory-map family.
type Layout int

const (
	LayoutLoROM Layout = iota
	LayoutHiROM
	LayoutExLoROM // LoROM wiring for images over 4 MB
	LayoutExHiROM // HiROM wiring with the upper halves swapped
)

func (l Layout) String() string {
	switch l {
	case LayoutLoROM:
		return "LoROM"
	case LayoutHiROM:
		return "HiROM"
	case LayoutExLoROM:
		return "ExLoROM"
	case LayoutExHiROM:
		return "ExHiROM"
	}
	return "unknown"
}

// Coprocessor identifies an enhancement chip the cartridge
// carries, as the header's chipset byte and map mode
// report it. CoprocessorNone is a plain ROM board.
type Coprocessor int

const (
	CoprocessorNone    Coprocessor = iota
	CoprocessorDSP                 // DSP-1/2/3/4 family (chipset 0x0x with map modes that carry it, and 0x0x generally)
	CoprocessorSuperFX             // GSU / SuperFX
	CoprocessorOBC1
	CoprocessorSA1
	CoprocessorSDD1
	CoprocessorSRTC
	CoprocessorSPC7110
	CoprocessorST010
	CoprocessorST011
	CoprocessorST018
	CoprocessorCx4
	CoprocessorOther // an enhancement byte this core does not recognize
)

func (c Coprocessor) String() string {
	switch c {
	case CoprocessorNone:
		return "none"
	case CoprocessorDSP:
		return "DSP"
	case CoprocessorSuperFX:
		return "SuperFX (GSU)"
	case CoprocessorOBC1:
		return "OBC1"
	case CoprocessorSA1:
		return "SA-1"
	case CoprocessorSDD1:
		return "S-DD1"
	case CoprocessorSRTC:
		return "S-RTC"
	case CoprocessorSPC7110:
		return "SPC7110"
	case CoprocessorST010:
		return "ST010"
	case CoprocessorST011:
		return "ST011"
	case CoprocessorST018:
		return "ST018"
	case CoprocessorCx4:
		return "Cx4"
	case CoprocessorOther:
		return "unknown enhancement chip"
	}
	return "unknown"
}

// Vectors holds the cartridge's interrupt vectors, as read
// from the header (offsets 0x20 to 0x3F).
type Vectors struct {
	NativeCOP   uint16
	NativeBRK   uint16
	NativeAbort uint16
	NativeNMI   uint16
	NativeIRQ   uint16
	EmuCOP      uint16
	EmuAbort    uint16
	EmuNMI      uint16
	EmuReset    uint16
	EmuIRQBRK   uint16
}

// Header is the parsed internal cartridge header.
type Header struct {
	Title       string // 21 bytes, JIS X 0201 decoded (see decodeTitle)
	MapMode     uint8  // raw mapper byte (0xFFD5): speed in the high nibble, layout in the low
	Chipset     uint8  // raw ROM type byte (0xFFD6)
	ROMSizeByte uint8
	RAMSizeByte uint8
	Country     uint8
	Licensee    uint8
	Version     uint8

	Layout      Layout
	FastROM     bool // map mode high nibble marks a FastROM board
	Coprocessor Coprocessor

	ROMSize int // bytes the header declares
	RAMSize int // battery-backed SRAM bytes the header declares
	Battery bool

	Checksum   uint16
	Complement uint16
	ChecksumOK bool // checksum and complement pair up (sum 0xFFFF)

	Vectors Vectors

	// headerOff is the file offset of the header this parse
	// came from.
	headerOff int
}

// PAL reports whether the header destination code (the
// Country byte) names a PAL territory, in which case the
// machine runs at PAL timing: 312 lines per frame and the
// 21.28137 MHz master clock. The destination codes follow
// the layout Nintendo documents for licensees: 0x00 Japan,
// 0x01 USA, 0x0D Korea, and 0x0E Canada are NTSC markets,
// as is 0x0F Brazil (PAL-M color on NTSC timing). Codes
// 0x02 through 0x0C are the European and other PAL
// markets (Europe, Sweden, Finland, Denmark, France,
// Holland, Spain, Germany, Italy, China, Indonesia), and
// 0x10 Australia and the 0x11 catch-all are PAL as well.
func (h Header) PAL() bool {
	switch h.Country {
	case 0x02, 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07,
		0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x10, 0x11:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// candidate header locations, in the order they are tried.
var headerCandidates = []struct {
	off    int
	layout Layout
}{
	{0x007FC0, LayoutLoROM},
	{0x00FFC0, LayoutHiROM},
	{0x40FFC0, LayoutExHiROM},
}

// parseHeaderAt decodes the 64-byte header at off. The
// image must extend at least to off+64.
func parseHeaderAt(img []byte, off int, layout Layout) (Header, error) {
	var h Header
	if off < 0 || off+0x40 > len(img) {
		return h, errors.New("cart: header past end of image")
	}
	b := img[off : off+0x40]
	h.headerOff = off
	h.Layout = layout
	h.Title = decodeTitle(b[0x00:0x15])
	h.MapMode = b[0x15]
	h.Chipset = b[0x16]
	h.ROMSizeByte = b[0x17]
	h.RAMSizeByte = b[0x18]
	h.Country = b[0x19]
	h.Licensee = b[0x1A]
	h.Version = b[0x1B]
	h.Complement = uint16(b[0x1C]) | uint16(b[0x1D])<<8
	h.Checksum = uint16(b[0x1E]) | uint16(b[0x1F])<<8
	h.ChecksumOK = h.Checksum^h.Complement == 0xFFFF
	h.FastROM = h.MapMode&0x10 != 0
	if h.ROMSizeByte >= 7 && h.ROMSizeByte <= 16 {
		h.ROMSize = (1 << h.ROMSizeByte) * 1024
	}
	if h.RAMSizeByte > 0 && h.RAMSizeByte <= 12 {
		h.RAMSize = (1 << h.RAMSizeByte) * 1024
	}
	h.Coprocessor, h.Battery = decodeChipset(h.Chipset, h.MapMode)
	// Some boards carry RAM the chipset byte does not call
	// battery-backed in its low nibble but still size in
	// the RAM byte; battery persistence follows the chipset
	// byte, decoded above.
	v := func(o int) uint16 { return uint16(b[o]) | uint16(b[o+1])<<8 }
	h.Vectors = Vectors{
		NativeCOP:   v(0x24),
		NativeBRK:   v(0x26),
		NativeAbort: v(0x28),
		NativeNMI:   v(0x2A),
		NativeIRQ:   v(0x2E),
		EmuCOP:      v(0x34),
		EmuAbort:    v(0x38),
		EmuNMI:      v(0x3A),
		EmuReset:    v(0x3C),
		EmuIRQBRK:   v(0x3E),
	}
	return h, nil
}

// decodeChipset splits the ROM type byte into the
// coprocessor family (high nibble, with the low-nibble
// exceptions Nintendo's table defines) and the battery
// flag (the RAM-and-battery component forms end in 2, 5,
// or 9 in the low nibble per the published table; the
// common component codes are handled explicitly).
func decodeChipset(chipset, mapMode uint8) (Coprocessor, bool) {
	lo := chipset & 0x0F
	hi := chipset & 0xF0
	battery := lo == 0x02 || lo == 0x05 || lo == 0x09
	switch {
	case chipset <= 0x02:
		return CoprocessorNone, battery
	case hi == 0x00:
		// 0x03..0x0F with a plain map mode: the DSP family.
		return CoprocessorDSP, battery
	case hi == 0x10:
		return CoprocessorSuperFX, battery
	case hi == 0x20:
		return CoprocessorOBC1, battery
	case hi == 0x30:
		return CoprocessorSA1, battery
	case hi == 0x40:
		return CoprocessorSDD1, battery
	case hi == 0x50:
		return CoprocessorSRTC, battery
	case hi == 0xE0:
		return CoprocessorCx4, battery
	case hi == 0xF0:
		// Licensee-specific enhancement chips, told apart
		// by the full byte and the map mode.
		switch chipset {
		case 0xF3:
			return CoprocessorCx4, battery
		case 0xF5:
			if mapMode&0x0F == 0x05 {
				return CoprocessorSPC7110, battery
			}
			return CoprocessorSRTC, battery
		case 0xF6:
			// ST010 and ST011 share a byte; the ROM size
			// separates them on real boards (ST011 images
			// are larger). v1 names both unsupported; the
			// distinction is cosmetic here.
			return CoprocessorST010, battery
		case 0xF9:
			return CoprocessorCx4, battery
		}
		return CoprocessorOther, battery
	}
	return CoprocessorOther, battery
}

// decodeTitle renders the 21 title bytes. The documented
// encoding is JIS X 0201: bytes 0x20..0x7E are ASCII, and
// 0xA1..0xDF are halfwidth katakana, which map one-to-one
// onto U+FF61..U+FF9F. Other bytes (padding zeros and
// spaces, control codes) become spaces, and the result is
// trimmed.
func decodeTitle(raw []byte) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for _, c := range raw {
		switch {
		case c >= 0x20 && c <= 0x7E:
			sb.WriteByte(c)
		case c >= 0xA1 && c <= 0xDF:
			sb.WriteRune(rune(c) + 0xFEC0)
		default:
			sb.WriteByte(' ')
		}
	}
	return strings.TrimRight(sb.String(), " ")
}

// scoreHeader grades a candidate header the way the
// standard heuristic does: a checksum that pairs with its
// complement is the strongest signal, a reset vector whose
// target byte is a plausible first opcode and whose map
// mode matches the candidate's layout is close behind, and
// sane size bytes and a printable title break ties. A
// candidate must score above zero to be believed.
func scoreHeader(h Header, img []byte) int {
	score := 0
	if h.ChecksumOK {
		score += 4
	}
	// Map mode low nibble agreement with the candidate.
	wantMode := map[Layout]uint8{
		LayoutLoROM:   0x00,
		LayoutHiROM:   0x01,
		LayoutExHiROM: 0x05,
		LayoutExLoROM: 0x00,
	}
	if h.MapMode&0x0F == wantMode[h.Layout] {
		score += 2
	}
	// Reset vector: must land in the ROM window the layout
	// serves, and the byte there should look like a first
	// instruction (SEI, CLC, JMP, JML, STZ and friends are
	// the common power-on opcodes).
	reset := h.Vectors.EmuReset
	if target, ok := resetTarget(h.Layout, reset); ok && target < len(img) {
		switch img[target] {
		case 0x78, 0x18, 0x38, 0x4C, 0x5C, 0x9C, 0x8C, 0xA9, 0xA2, 0xA0, 0xD8, 0x58, 0xFB, 0xC2, 0xE2:
			score += 3
		default:
			score += 1
		}
	}
	// ROM size byte should be plausible for the image.
	if h.ROMSize > 0 && h.ROMSize <= len(img)*2 && h.ROMSize*2 >= len(img) {
		score++
	}
	// Mostly printable title.
	printable := 0
	for _, r := range h.Title {
		if r >= 0x20 && r != 0xFFFD {
			printable++
		}
	}
	if len(h.Title) > 0 && printable*2 >= len(h.Title) {
		score++
	}
	return score
}

// resetTarget maps a reset vector to the file offset of
// its first byte under a layout, reporting whether the
// vector is plausible for that layout at all.
func resetTarget(layout Layout, vec uint16) (int, bool) {
	switch layout {
	case LayoutLoROM, LayoutExLoROM:
		if vec < 0x8000 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return int(vec - 0x8000), true // bank 0 in the file's first page
	case LayoutHiROM, LayoutExHiROM:
		if vec < 0x8000 {
			return 0, false
		}
		return int(vec), true // bank 0xC0 in HiROM terms starts the image
	}
	return 0, false
}

// Cart is a loaded cartridge: the header facts and the ROM
// bytes. The bus serves the image through Map.
type Cart struct {
	Header Header
	rom    []byte
}

// ROM returns the cartridge ROM bytes (with any copier
// header stripped).
func (c *Cart) ROM() []byte { return c.rom }

// Load parses an image and picks its header location by
// score. It refuses images with no plausible header and
// images whose game needs a coprocessor this core does
// not implement, naming the chip in the error.
func Load(image []byte) (*Cart, error) {
	img, err := stripCopierHeader(image)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if len(img) < 0x8000 {
		return nil, errors.New("cart: image too small for an SNES ROM")
	}
	var best *Header
	bestScore := 0
	for _, cand := range headerCandidates {
		h, err := parseHeaderAt(img, cand.off, cand.layout)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		s := scoreHeader(h, img)
		if s > bestScore {
			hh := h
			best, bestScore = &hh, s
		}
	}
	if best == nil || bestScore < 4 {
		// A header must at least pair its checksum, or
		// combine the weaker signals convincingly: a zeroed
		// image's candidate scores 2 from the map-mode
		// nibble alone and must not pass.
		return nil, errors.New("cart: no plausible SNES header found")
	}
	// The map mode can mark an oversized LoROM image as
	// ExLoROM: LoROM wiring over more than 4 MB swaps the
	// halves like ExHiROM does.
	if best.Layout == LayoutLoROM && len(img) > 4*1024*1024 {
		best.Layout = LayoutExLoROM
	}
	if best.Coprocessor != CoprocessorNone {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cart: %q needs the %s coprocessor, which this core does not implement yet",
			best.Title, best.Coprocessor)
	}
	return &Cart{Header: *best, rom: img}, nil
}

// stripCopierHeader removes the 512-byte copier header
// some dump formats prepend, detected by the image size
// modulo 32 KB.
func stripCopierHeader(image []byte) ([]byte, error) {
	if len(image)%1024 == 512 {
		if len(image) <= 512 {
			return nil, errors.New("cart: image is only a copier header")
		}
		return image[512:], nil
	}
	return image, nil
}

package cart

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-snes/chips/w65c816"
)

// buildImage makes a synthetic ROM image of size bytes
// with a header written at headerOff. mutate adjusts the
// default header fields.
func buildImage(size, headerOff int, mutate func(b []byte)) []byte {
	img := make([]byte, size)
	b := img[headerOff : headerOff+0x40]
	copy(b, "SYNTHETIC TEST ROM   ")
	b[0x15] = 0x20 // LoROM, slow
	b[0x16] = 0x02 // ROM + RAM + battery
	b[0x17] = 0x09 // 512 KB declared (adjusted by caller as needed)
	b[0x18] = 0x03 // 8 KB SRAM
	b[0x19] = 0x01 // North America
	b[0x1A] = 0x01
	// Checksum and complement pair.
	b[0x1C], b[0x1D] = 0x55, 0xAA
	b[0x1E], b[0x1F] = 0xAA, 0x55
	// Reset vector to 0x8000, first byte SEI.
	b[0x3C], b[0x3D] = 0x00, 0x80
	img[0] = 0x78
	if size > 0x10000 {
		img[0x8000] = 0x78 // HiROM bank 0xC0 reset landing
	}
	if mutate != nil {
		mutate(img[headerOff : headerOff+0x40])
	}
	return img
}

func TestLoadLoROM(t *testing.T) {
	img := buildImage(0x80000, 0x7FC0, nil)
	c, err := Load(img)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	if c.Header.Layout != LayoutLoROM {
		t.Errorf("layout = %v, want LoROM", c.Header.Layout)
	}
	if c.Header.Title != "SYNTHETIC TEST ROM" {
		t.Errorf("title = %q", c.Header.Title)
	}
	if c.Header.RAMSize != 8192 {
		t.Errorf("RAMSize = %d, want 8192", c.Header.RAMSize)
	}
	if !c.Header.Battery {
		t.Errorf("battery not decoded")
	}
	if !c.Header.ChecksumOK {
		t.Errorf("checksum pair not decoded")
	}
	if c.Header.Vectors.EmuReset != 0x8000 {
		t.Errorf("reset vector = %#x", c.Header.Vectors.EmuReset)
	}
}

func TestLoadHiROM(t *testing.T) {
	img := buildImage(0x100000, 0xFFC0, func(b []byte) {
		b[0x15] = 0x21 // HiROM, slow
		b[0x17] = 0x0A // 1 MB
		// The LoROM candidate location must not win: leave
		// garbage at 0x7FC0 (zeros score nothing).
	})
	// The HiROM reset vector's landing byte lives at file
	// offset 0x8000 under the HiROM mirror; it is 0x78 in
	// the builder.
	c, err := Load(img)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	if c.Header.Layout != LayoutHiROM {
		t.Errorf("layout = %v, want HiROM", c.Header.Layout)
	}
}

func TestLoadFastROM(t *testing.T) {
	img := buildImage(0x80000, 0x7FC0, func(b []byte) {
		b[0x15] = 0x30 // LoROM, fast
	})
	c, err := Load(img)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	if !c.Header.FastROM {
		t.Errorf("FastROM not decoded")
	}
	m := NewMap(c)
	if got := m.Speed(0x80, 0x8000); got != w65c816.SpeedFast {
		t.Errorf("fast bank speed = %v, want SpeedFast", got)
	}
	if got := m.Speed(0x00, 0x8000); got != w65c816.SpeedSlow {
		t.Errorf("low bank speed = %v, want SpeedSlow", got)
	}
}

func TestLoadRejectsCoprocessors(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		chipset uint8
		want    string
	}{
		{"SA-1", 0x34, "SA-1"},
		{"SuperFX", 0x15, "SuperFX"},
		{"DSP", 0x03, "DSP"},
		{"S-DD1", 0x45, "S-DD1"},
		{"SPC7110", 0xF5, "SPC7110"},
		{"Cx4", 0xF9, "Cx4"},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		img := buildImage(0x80000, 0x7FC0, func(b []byte) {
			b[0x16] = tc.chipset
			if tc.chipset == 0xF5 {
				b[0x15] = 0x25 // ExHiROM map mode marks SPC7110
			}
		})
		_, err := Load(img)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: Load succeeded, want refusal", tc.name)
			continue
		}
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: error %q does not name %q", tc.name, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestLoadRejectsGarbage(t *testing.T) {

	if _, err := Load(img); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("zero image loaded, want error")
	}
	if _, err := Load([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("tiny image loaded, want error")
	}
}

	img := make([]byte, 0, len(base)+512)
	img = append(img, make([]byte, 512)...)
	img = append(img, base...)
	c, err := Load(img)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}

		t.Errorf("ROM size = %d, want %d", len(c.ROM()), len(base))
	}
}

func TestLoROMMap(t *testing.T) {
	img := buildImage(0x80000, 0x7FC0, nil)
	// Give pages recognizable contents: page p starts with
	// byte p.
	for p := 0; p < 16; p++ {
		img[p*0x8000] = byte(p)
	}
	img[0] = 0x78 // restore reset landing byte
	c, _ := Load(img)
	m := NewMap(c)
	checks := []struct {
		bank uint8
		addr uint16
		want uint8
	}{
		{0x00, 0x8000, 0x78}, // page 0 starts with the SEI reset landing byte
		{0x01, 0x8000, 1},    // page 1
		{0x80, 0x8000, 0x78}, // mirror
		{0x81, 0x8000, 1},
		{0x02, 0xFFFF, 0}, // inside page 2: byte value unmarked (0)
	}
	for _, ch := range checks {
		if got := m.Read(ch.bank, ch.addr); got != ch.want {
			t.Errorf("Read(%02x:%04x) = %d, want %d", ch.bank, ch.addr, got, ch.want)
		}
	}
	// Work RAM mirror and bank 7E/7F agree.
	m.Write(0x00, 0x0010, 0xAB)
	if got := m.Read(0x7E, 0x0010); got != 0xAB {
		t.Errorf("WRAM mirror read = %#x", got)
	}
	m.Write(0x7F, 0x1234, 0xCD)
	if got := m.Read(0x7F, 0x1234); got != 0xCD {
		t.Errorf("WRAM high bank read = %#x", got)
	}
	// SRAM window at 0x70:0000.
	m.Write(0x70, 0x0000, 0x5A)
	if got := m.Read(0x70, 0x0000); got != 0x5A {
		t.Errorf("SRAM read = %#x", got)
	}
	if len(m.SRAM()) != 8192 {
		t.Errorf("SRAM size = %d", len(m.SRAM()))
	}
	// IO region reads open bus (SNES-1 placeholder).
	if got := m.Read(0x00, 0x2100); got != m.OpenBus {
		t.Errorf("IO read = %#x, want open bus", got)
	}
	if got := m.Speed(0x00, 0x2100); got != w65c816.SpeedXSlow {
		t.Errorf("IO speed = %v, want SpeedXSlow", got)
	}
}

func TestHiROMMap(t *testing.T) {
	img := buildImage(0x100000, 0xFFC0, func(b []byte) {
		b[0x15] = 0x21
		b[0x17] = 0x0A
	})
	for p := 0; p < 16; p++ {
		img[p*0x10000] = byte(p + 1)
	}
	img[0x8000] = 0x78
	c, err := Load(img)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Load: %v", err)
	}
	m := NewMap(c)
	if got := m.Read(0xC0, 0x0000); got != 1 {
		t.Errorf("C0:0000 = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if got := m.Read(0xC1, 0x0000); got != 2 {
		t.Errorf("C1:0000 = %d, want 2", got)
	}
	if got := m.Read(0x00, 0x8000); got != img[0x8000] {
		t.Errorf("00:8000 mirror = %#x, want %#x", got, img[0x8000])
	}
	// HiROM SRAM window at 0x20:6000.
	m.Write(0x20, 0x6000, 0x77)
	if got := m.Read(0x20, 0x6000); got != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("HiROM SRAM read = %#x", got)
	}
	if got := m.Read(0xA0, 0x6000); got != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("HiROM SRAM mirror read = %#x", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/cart/map.go ====================

// The SNES memory map: how the 16 MB address space decodes
// to ROM, SRAM, Work RAM, and the system area, per layout.
//
// The console map (from the SNES development documentation
// and fullsnes):
//
//   - Banks 0x00-0x3F and their mirrors 0x80-0xBF form the
//     system area: 0x0000-0x1FFF mirrors the first 8 KB of
//     Work RAM, 0x2000-0x5FFF is the IO region (PPU, APU,
//     CPU peripherals, controllers), and 0x6000-0x7FFF is a
//     small SRAM window on HiROM boards. ROM shows at
//     0x8000-0xFFFF in these banks.
//   - Banks 0x40-0x7D and 0xC0-0xFF are ROM space: full
//     64 KB banks on HiROM, 32 KB pages on LoROM.
//   - Banks 0x7E-0x7F are the 128 KB of Work RAM itself.
//   - LoROM SRAM lives at banks 0x70-0x73 (mirrored at
//     0xF0-0xF3); HiROM SRAM at banks 0x20-0x3F (mirrored at
//     0xA0-0xBF), addresses 0x6000-0x7FFF.
//
// SNES-1 ships this map with the IO region inert: reads
// there return the map's open-bus byte and writes are
// dropped, documented here and in the README. The PPU, APU,
// DMA, and peripheral slices replace those hooks with real
// registers without the map's shape changing.
//
// Access speeds (the CPU package's Speed values): Work RAM
// and ordinary ROM are slow (8 master clocks); ROM in
// banks 0x80-0xFF is fast (6) on FastROM boards; the IO
// region is extra slow (12), matching the console.
package cart

import "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-snes/chips/w65c816"

// WRAMSize is the console's Work RAM size in bytes.
const WRAMSize = 128 * 1024

// Map is the assembled console bus for one cartridge. It
// owns the Work RAM and the cartridge SRAM; the cartridge
// ROM it reads from the loaded Cart.
type Map struct {
	cart *Cart
	wram []byte
	sram []byte

	// speedTab holds the access speed class for every
	// bank and address band (band = addr>>13), computed
	// once at map build from the decode rules, so the
	// per access speed query is a single array load. The
	// decode rules only test address bits at or above
	// bit 13 (the IO window edges and the 0x8000 split),
	// so one class covers a whole band exactly.
	speedTab [256][8]w65c816.Speed

	// sramBank marks the banks that contain an SRAM
	// window for this cartridge, so reads and writes in
	// any other bank skip the SRAM decode entirely.
	sramBank [256]bool

	// romTab is the per bank, per address half ROM read
	// fast path: where an entry is valid, every address
	// in the half reads m.cart.rom at (base + addr&mask)
	// wrapped by romMask, which is exactly what romAt
	// computes the slow way (the wrap is a power-of-two
	// mask, and masking distributes over the addition).
	// Built once in NewMap; entries stay invalid for
	// non-power-of-two images, which keep the slow path.
	romTab [256][2]romEntry

	// Precomputed ROM and SRAM wrap values: images are
	// power-of-two sized in practice, where the wrap is
	// a mask; the flags record that so the per access
	// wrap skips the size test.
	romMask  int
	romPow2  bool
	sramMask int
	sramPow2 bool

	// OpenBus is the byte reads of unmapped and (for now)
	// IO addresses return. On hardware the data bus holds
	// the last value driven on it; SNES-1 keeps a plain
	// byte the system may set, defaulting to zero.
	OpenBus uint8
}

// romEntry is one bank half of the ROM read fast path
// (see Map.romTab).
type romEntry struct {
	base int    // wrapped ROM offset of the half's first byte, minus the address bits
	mask uint16 // the address bits that vary inside the half
	ok   bool
}

// NewMap builds the bus for a loaded cartridge. SRAM is
// sized from the header (zero when the header declares
// none, in which case the SRAM windows read open bus).
func NewMap(c *Cart) *Map {
	m := &Map{cart: c, wram: make([]byte, WRAMSize)}
	if c.Header.RAMSize > 0 {
		m.sram = make([]byte, c.Header.RAMSize)
	}
	if n := len(c.rom); n > 0 && n&(n-1) == 0 {
		m.romMask, m.romPow2 = n-1, true
	}
	if n := len(m.sram); n > 0 && n&(n-1) == 0 {
		m.sramMask, m.sramPow2 = n-1, true
	}
	// The address bits that vary inside one half of a
	// bank under each layout: LoROM folds the address to
	// 15 bits, HiROM uses all 16.
	addrMask := uint16(0x7FFF)
	if c.Header.Layout == LayoutHiROM || c.Header.Layout == LayoutExHiROM {
		addrMask = 0xFFFF
	}
	for bank := 0; bank < 256; bank++ {
		b := uint8(bank)
		if _, ok := m.sramAt(b, 0x0000); ok {
			m.sramBank[bank] = true
		}
		if _, ok := m.sramAt(b, 0x6000); ok {
			m.sramBank[bank] = true
		}
		for band := 0; band < 8; band++ {
			m.speedTab[bank][band] = m.speedClass(b, uint16(band<<13))
		}
		if m.romPow2 {
			// ROM decode validity is uniform inside a
			// bank half under every layout (the decode
			// splits only on address bit 15), so one
			// probe per half settles the whole half.
			for half := 0; half < 2; half++ {
				rep := uint16(half << 15)
				if off, ok := m.romAt(b, rep); ok {
					m.romTab[bank][half] = romEntry{
						base: (off - int(rep&addrMask)) & m.romMask,
						mask: addrMask,
						ok:   true,
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return m
}

// SRAM exposes the battery-backed RAM contents for the
// system's persistence layer.
func (m *Map) SRAM() []byte { return m.sram }

// WRAM exposes the Work RAM contents.
func (m *Map) WRAM() []byte { return m.wram }

// romAt translates a 24-bit address to a ROM offset under
// the cartridge's layout, reporting whether the address is
// ROM space at all.
func (m *Map) romAt(bank uint8, addr uint16) (int, bool) {
	switch m.cart.Header.Layout {
	case LayoutLoROM:
		return m.loROMOffset(bank, addr)
	case LayoutExLoROM:
		return m.loROMOffset(bank^0x40, addr)
	case LayoutHiROM:
		return m.hiROMOffset(bank, addr)
	case LayoutExHiROM:
		return m.hiROMOffset(bank^0x40, addr)
	}
	return 0, false
}

// loROMOffset computes the LoROM ROM offset for an
// address, or reports the address is not ROM. LoROM is a
// pure 32 KB page map: the offset is the bank's low seven
// bits shifted by 15 plus the address's low fifteen bits.
// The system banks only decode the high half (0x8000 up);
// in the ROM banks (0x40-0x7D and 0xC0-0xFF) the same page
// shows at both halves, because the wiring ignores
// address bit 15 there. That uniform formula is the whole
// map.
func (m *Map) loROMOffset(bank uint8, addr uint16) (int, bool) {
	inSystemBanks := bank < 0x40 || (bank >= 0x80 && bank < 0xC0)
	if addr < 0x8000 && inSystemBanks {
		return 0, false
	}
	off := int(bank&0x7F)*0x8000 + int(addr&0x7FFF)
	return wrapROMFast(off, m.romMask, m.romPow2, len(m.cart.rom)), true
}

// hiROMOffset computes the HiROM ROM offset for an
// address, or reports the address is not ROM. HiROM maps
// full 64 KB banks at 0x40-0x7D and 0xC0-0xFF, and mirrors
// their high halves at 0x8000-0xFFFF of the system banks.
func (m *Map) hiROMOffset(bank uint8, addr uint16) (int, bool) {
	switch {
	case bank >= 0x40 && bank < 0x80 || bank >= 0xC0:
		off := int(bank&0x7F)*0x10000 + int(addr)
		return wrapROMFast(off, m.romMask, m.romPow2, len(m.cart.rom)), true
	case addr >= 0x8000:
		// System banks: mirror of the same-numbered full
		// bank's high half.
		off := int(bank&0x3F)*0x10000 + int(addr)
		return wrapROMFast(off, m.romMask, m.romPow2, len(m.cart.rom)), true
	}
	return 0, false
}

// wrapROM folds an offset into the ROM image. Images are
// power-of-two sized in practice, where the fold is a
// mask; the modulo form covers any other size and never
// reads out of range. Offsets are never negative, so the
// two forms agree.
func wrapROM(off, size int) int {
	if size == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if size&(size-1) == 0 {
		return off & (size - 1)
	}
	return off % size
}

// wrapROMFast is wrapROM against a precomputed image
// size: the mask and power-of-two flag NewMap derived
// from the size, plus the size itself for the modulo
// form.
func wrapROMFast(off, mask int, pow2 bool, size int) int {
	if size == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if pow2 {
		return off & mask
	}
	return off % size
}

// sramAt translates a 24-bit address to an SRAM offset
// under the cartridge's layout, reporting whether the
// address is an SRAM window.
func (m *Map) sramAt(bank uint8, addr uint16) (int, bool) {
	if len(m.sram) == 0 {
		return 0, false
	}
	switch m.cart.Header.Layout {
	case LayoutLoROM, LayoutExLoROM:
		if (bank >= 0x70 && bank <= 0x73) || (bank >= 0xF0 && bank <= 0xF3) {
			off := int(bank&0x03)*0x10000 + int(addr)
			return wrapROMFast(off, m.sramMask, m.sramPow2, len(m.sram)), true
		}
	case LayoutHiROM, LayoutExHiROM:
		if addr >= 0x6000 && addr < 0x8000 &&
			((bank >= 0x20 && bank < 0x40) || (bank >= 0xA0 && bank < 0xC0)) {
			off := int(bank&0x1F)*0x2000 + int(addr-0x6000)
			return wrapROMFast(off, m.sramMask, m.sramPow2, len(m.sram)), true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

// isSystemLow reports whether the address sits in the
// system area low half (Work RAM mirror and IO) of a
// system bank.
func isSystemBank(bank uint8) bool {
	return bank < 0x40 || (bank >= 0x80 && bank < 0xC0)
}

// Read implements the CPU bus read side.
func (m *Map) Read(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint8 {
	// Work RAM itself.
	if bank == 0x7E || bank == 0x7F {
		return m.wram[int(bank&0x01)*0x10000+int(addr)]
	}
	if isSystemBank(bank) && addr < 0x2000 {
		return m.wram[addr]
	}
	if m.sramBank[bank] {
		if off, ok := m.sramAt(bank, addr); ok {
			return m.sram[off]
		}
	}
	if e := &m.romTab[bank][addr>>15]; e.ok {
		return m.cart.rom[(e.base+int(addr&e.mask))&m.romMask]
	}
	if off, ok := m.romAt(bank, addr); ok {
		return m.cart.rom[off]
	}
	// IO region and anything unmapped: open bus for now.
	return m.OpenBus
}

// Write implements the CPU bus write side.
func (m *Map) Write(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if bank == 0x7E || bank == 0x7F {
		m.wram[int(bank&0x01)*0x10000+int(addr)] = val
		return
	}
	if isSystemBank(bank) && addr < 0x2000 {
		m.wram[addr] = val
		return
	}
	if m.sramBank[bank] {
		if off, ok := m.sramAt(bank, addr); ok {
			m.sram[off] = val
			return
		}
	}
	// ROM and IO writes go nowhere in SNES-1.
}

// Speed implements the CPU bus speed provider: one
// lookup into the table precomputed at map build.
func (m *Map) Speed(bank uint8, addr uint16) w65c816.Speed {
	return m.speedTab[bank][addr>>13]
}

// speedClass decodes the access speed for one address
// from the map rules. NewMap samples it once per bank
// and address band to fill speedTab.
func (m *Map) speedClass(bank uint8, addr uint16) w65c816.Speed {
	if isSystemBank(bank) && addr >= 0x2000 && addr < 0x6000 {
		return w65c816.SpeedXSlow // the IO region
	}
	if m.cart.Header.FastROM && bank >= 0x80 {
		if m.isROM(bank, addr) {
			return w65c816.SpeedFast
		}
	}
	return w65c816.SpeedSlow
}

// isROM reports whether the address is ROM space: the
// ok half of romAt without the offset math, for the speed
// path, which runs on every byte access.
func (m *Map) isROM(bank uint8, addr uint16) bool {
	switch m.cart.Header.Layout {
	case LayoutLoROM:
		return loROMIsROM(bank, addr)
	case LayoutExLoROM:
		return loROMIsROM(bank^0x40, addr)
	case LayoutHiROM:
		return hiROMIsROM(bank, addr)
	case LayoutExHiROM:
		return hiROMIsROM(bank^0x40, addr)
	}
	return false
}

// loROMIsROM mirrors loROMOffsets ok result: every
// address is ROM except the low half of the system banks.
func loROMIsROM(bank uint8, addr uint16) bool {
	inSystemBanks := bank < 0x40 || (bank >= 0x80 && bank < 0xC0)
	return !(addr < 0x8000 && inSystemBanks)
}

// hiROMIsROM mirrors hiROMOffsets ok result: the ROM
// banks in full, plus the high half of any other bank.
func hiROMIsROM(bank uint8, addr uint16) bool {
	return (bank >= 0x40 && bank < 0x80) || bank >= 0xC0 || addr >= 0x8000
}

// compile-time check: Map is a CPU bus.
var _ w65c816.Bus = (*Map)(nil)


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/spc700/conformance_test.go ====================

// The Tom Harte single-step conformance gate.
//
// The corpus (github.com/TomHarte/ProcessorTests, the
// spc700 v1 set, generated from the JSMoo core) provides
// 1,000 randomized tests per opcode: an initial processor
// state and RAM contents, the final state after exactly
// one instruction, the final contents of every RAM cell
// the instruction could have touched, and a cycle-by-cycle
// bus trace whose entries are [address, value, kind] with
// kind "read", "write", or "wait" (address and value are
// null for waits and for dummy accesses).
//
// The schema differs from the 65816 set's: registers are
// flat fields named pc, a, x, y, sp, and psw (not p), RAM
// is a list of [address, value] pairs in a flat 64 KB
// space, and the cycles list is present for every test.
//
// The runner installs the initial state, executes one
// Step, and compares:
//   - every register, including the full PSW;
//   - the final value of every listed RAM cell;
//   - the total cycle count against the trace length;
//   - the data-carrying bus access sequence: the trace
//     entries that carry a value (address, direction, and
//     data), in order, against the accesses this CPU
//     actually made. Trace entries with a null value are
//     idle or dummy cycles that move no data (the generator
//     records, for example, DIV's internal cycles and the
//     indirect modes' idle read that way), so they carry
//     nothing to compare; the cycle count check above
//     still accounts for them.
//
// Two opcodes are exempt from the cycle comparison: SLEEP
// and STOP halt the CPU, the trace models the halt as an
// idle spin of a length the generator chose, and this core
// charges a halted Step a flat 16 cycles by contract (see
// the package comment). Their registers and RAM are still
// compared.
//
// The corpus lives under testroms/tomharte-spc700 in this
// module (gitignored, local evidence only). When it is
// absent the gate skips.
package spc700

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"testing"
)

type thPair [2]int

type thState struct {
	PC  int      `json:"pc"`
	A   int      `json:"a"`
	X   int      `json:"x"`
	Y   int      `json:"y"`
	SP  int      `json:"sp"`
	PSW int      `json:"psw"`
	RAM []thPair `json:"ram"`
}

// thCycle is one trace entry: [address, value, kind], with
// address and value null when the cycle makes no addressed
// access or moves no data. hasVal marks the entries that
// carry data and so take part in the access comparison.
type thCycle struct {
	addr   int
	val    int
	hasVal bool
	write  bool
}

func (cc *thCycle) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
	var parts []json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &parts); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(parts) != 3 {
		return fmt.Errorf("cycle entry with %d parts", len(parts))
	}
	if string(parts[0]) != "null" {
		if err := json.Unmarshal(parts[0], &cc.addr); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if string(parts[1]) != "null" {
		if err := json.Unmarshal(parts[1], &cc.val); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		cc.hasVal = true
	}
	var kind string
	if err := json.Unmarshal(parts[2], &kind); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	cc.write = kind == "write"
	return nil
}

type thTest struct {
	Name    string    `json:"name"`
	Initial thState   `json:"initial"`
	Final   thState   `json:"final"`
	Cycles  []thCycle `json:"cycles"`
}

// thBus is the corpus environment: a flat 64 KB of RAM
// that remembers every cell ever dirtied so the next
// test's reset only has to clear those, and a recording of
// every access the CPU makes.
type thBus struct {
	mem     []byte
	access  []thAccess
	touched map[uint16]bool
}

type thAccess struct {
	addr  uint16
	val   uint8
	write bool
}

func newTHBus() *thBus {
	return &thBus{mem: make([]byte, 1<<16), touched: make(map[uint16]bool)}
}

func (b *thBus) Read(addr uint16) uint8 {
	v := b.mem[addr]
	b.access = append(b.access, thAccess{addr: addr, val: v})
	return v
}

func (b *thBus) Write(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	b.mem[addr] = val
	b.touched[addr] = true
	b.access = append(b.access, thAccess{addr: addr, val: val, write: true})
}

// reset restores the corpus invariant: RAM is zero except
// for the test's initial entries.
func (b *thBus) reset(initial []thPair) {
	for a := range b.touched {
		b.mem[a] = 0
	}
	b.touched = make(map[uint16]bool)
	b.access = b.access[:0]
	for _, p := range initial {
		a := uint16(p[0])
		b.mem[a] = uint8(p[1])
		b.touched[a] = true
	}
}

func runTomHarteFile(t *testing.T, path string) (passed, failed int) {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", path, err)
	}
	var tests []thTest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &tests); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse %s: %v", path, err)
	}
	if len(tests) > 10000 {
		tests = tests[:10000]
	}
	bus := newTHBus()
	cpu := New()
	cpu.Attach(bus)
	var firstFailure string
	for _, tc := range tests {
		bus.reset(tc.Initial.RAM)
		cpu.SetRegs(Registers{
			PC: uint16(tc.Initial.PC), A: uint8(tc.Initial.A),
			X: uint8(tc.Initial.X), Y: uint8(tc.Initial.Y),
			SP: uint8(tc.Initial.SP), P: uint8(tc.Initial.PSW),
		})
		op := bus.mem[uint16(tc.Initial.PC)]
		got := cpu.Step()
		if msg := checkTomHarte(cpu, bus, tc, op, got); msg != "" {
			failed++
			if firstFailure == "" {
				firstFailure = fmt.Sprintf("test %q: %s", tc.Name, msg)
			}
			continue
		}
		passed++
	}
	if firstFailure != "" {
		t.Errorf("%s: %d/%d failed; first: %s", filepath.Base(path), failed, passed+failed, firstFailure)
	}
	return passed, failed
}

func checkTomHarte(cpu *CPU, bus *thBus, tc thTest, op uint8, gotCycles int) string {
	r := cpu.Regs()
	f := tc.Final
	chk := func(name string, got, want int) string {
		if got != want {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s = %d (%#x), want %d (%#x)", name, got, got, want, want)
		}
		return ""
	}
	if msg := chk("pc", int(r.PC), f.PC); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("a", int(r.A), f.A); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("x", int(r.X), f.X); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("y", int(r.Y), f.Y); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("sp", int(r.SP), f.SP); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("psw", int(r.P), f.PSW); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	for _, p := range f.RAM {
		if got := bus.mem[uint16(p[0])]; got != uint8(p[1]) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("ram[%#x] = %#x, want %#x", p[0], got, p[1])
		}
	}
	// SLEEP and STOP are exempt from the cycle comparison:
	// the trace spins in the halt, this core charges a
	// flat 16 (see the file comment).
	if op != 0xEF && op != 0xFF && gotCycles != len(tc.Cycles) {
		return fmt.Sprintf("cycles = %d, want %d", gotCycles, len(tc.Cycles))
	}
	// The data-carrying access subsequence: trace entries
	// with a value, in order, must equal the accesses this
	// CPU made (address, direction, and data).
	valued := make([]thCycle, 0, len(tc.Cycles))
	for _, cc := range tc.Cycles {
		if cc.hasVal {
			valued = append(valued, cc)
		}
	}
	if len(valued) != len(bus.access) {
		return fmt.Sprintf("data accesses = %d, want %d", len(bus.access), len(valued))
	}
	for i, cc := range valued {
		acc := bus.access[i]
		if int(acc.addr) != cc.addr {
			return fmt.Sprintf("access %d addr = %#x, want %#x", i, acc.addr, cc.addr)
		}
		if acc.write != cc.write {
			return fmt.Sprintf("access %d (%#x) write = %v, want %v", i, acc.addr, acc.write, cc.write)
		}
		if int(acc.val) != cc.val {
			return fmt.Sprintf("access %d (%#x) data = %#x, want %#x", i, acc.addr, acc.val, cc.val)
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func TestTomHarteSPC700(t *testing.T) {
	dir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "testroms", "tomharte-spc700")
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("Tom Harte corpus not present at %s: %v", dir, err)
	}
	var files []string
	for _, e := range entries {
		if filepath.Ext(e.Name()) == ".json" {
			files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	if len(files) == 0 {
		t.Skip("Tom Harte corpus directory holds no test files")
	}
	// TH_FILES (a comma-separated list of base names) limits
	// the run for iteration; the gate itself runs all files
	// present.
	only := map[string]bool{}
	if env := os.Getenv("TH_FILES"); env != "" {
		for _, name := range splitComma(env) {
			only[name] = true
		}
	}
	totalPass, totalFail := 0, 0
	for _, path := range files {
		if len(only) > 0 && !only[filepath.Base(path)] {
			continue
		}
		p, f := runTomHarteFile(t, path)
		totalPass += p
		totalFail += f
	}
	t.Logf("Tom Harte SPC700: %d passed, %d failed, %d total", totalPass, totalFail, totalPass+totalFail)
	if len(only) == 0 && len(files) < 256 {
		t.Logf("note: corpus subset present: %d of 256 files", len(files))
	}
}

func splitComma(s string) []string {
	var out []string
	cur := ""
	for _, r := range s {
		if r == ',' {
			out = append(out, cur)
			cur = ""
			continue
		}
		cur += string(r)
	}
	if cur != "" {
		out = append(out, cur)
	}
	return out
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/spc700/exec.go ====================

// Instruction execution for the SPC700: the 256-opcode
// dispatch, the addressing-mode access helpers, and the
// operations themselves.
//
// The opcode map is highly regular, and the dispatch keeps
// that structure visible: the six 8-bit ALU operations share
// one column pattern across their opcode rows, the six
// shift/rotate/increment/decrement operations share another,
// the TCALLs and the direct-page bit operations decode their
// operand (vector number, bit number) out of the opcode
// itself, and the rest are listed opcode by opcode.
//
// Cycle counts are the published per-opcode values. Stores
// perform the dummy read of their destination that the
// documentation describes (see the package comment) before
// writing; MOV dp,dp and MOV (X)+,A are the documented
// exceptions and do not.
package spc700

// aluKind decodes which of the six shared-column ALU
// operations an opcode belongs to, from the opcode's row:
// the rows are OR, AND, EOR, CMP, ADC, SBC in order.
func aluKind(op uint8) int {
	return int(op>>5) & 7
}

const (
	aluOR = iota
	aluAND
	aluEOR
	aluCMP
	aluADC
	aluSBC
)

// alu computes one 8-bit ALU operation on a with operand b
// and sets the flags the operation documents. CMP discards
// its result; the caller decides whether the result is
// stored (in A, or back to a memory destination for the
// memory forms).
func (c *CPU) alu(kind int, a, b uint8) uint8 {
	switch kind {
	case aluOR:
		r := a | b
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case aluAND:
		r := a & b
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case aluEOR:
		r := a ^ b
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case aluCMP:
		c.cmp8(a, b)
		return a
	case aluADC:
		carry := 0
		if c.flag(FlagC) {
			carry = 1
		}
		t := int(a) + int(b) + carry
		r := uint8(t)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, t > 0xFF)
		c.setFlag(FlagH, (a&0x0F)+(b&0x0F)+uint8(carry) > 0x0F)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, (a^b)&0x80 == 0 && (a^r)&0x80 != 0)
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case aluSBC:
		borrow := 1
		if c.flag(FlagC) {
			borrow = 0
		}
		t := int(a) - int(b) - borrow
		r := uint8(t)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, t >= 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagH, int(a&0x0F)-int(b&0x0F)-borrow >= 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, (a^b)&0x80 != 0 && (a^r)&0x80 != 0)
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	}
	return a
}

// cmp8 sets the flags CMP documents (N, Z, C from a-b; V
// and H are untouched) and returns nothing else.
func (c *CPU) cmp8(a, b uint8) {
	r := a - b
	c.setFlag(FlagC, a >= b)
	c.setNZ(r)
}

// shiftKind decodes the shared shift/increment pattern the
// same way aluKind decodes the ALU pattern.
func shiftKind(op uint8) int {
	return int(op>>5) & 7
}

const (
	shiftASL = iota
	shiftROL
	shiftLSR
	shiftROR
	shiftDEC
	shiftINC
)

// shift computes one shift, rotate, increment, or decrement
// on v and sets its documented flags (N, Z, and C for the
// shifts and rotates; N and Z only for INC and DEC).
func (c *CPU) shift(kind int, v uint8) uint8 {
	switch kind {
	case shiftASL:
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x80 != 0)
		r := v << 1
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case shiftROL:
		carry := uint8(0)
		if c.flag(FlagC) {
			carry = 1
		}
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x80 != 0)
		r := v<<1 | carry
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case shiftLSR:
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x01 != 0)
		r := v >> 1
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case shiftROR:
		carry := uint8(0)
		if c.flag(FlagC) {
			carry = 0x80
		}
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x01 != 0)
		r := v>>1 | carry
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case shiftDEC:
		r := v - 1
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	case shiftINC:
		r := v + 1
		c.setNZ(r)
		return r
	}
	return v
}

// branch applies a relative branch offset if cond holds,
// and reports whether the branch was taken (the taken and
// not-taken cycle counts differ).
func (c *CPU) branch(cond bool, off int8) bool {
	if cond {
		c.pc = uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// branchCycles is the shared cycle shape of the plain
// conditional branches and BRA's conditional cousins:
// 2 cycles not taken, 4 taken.
func branchCycles(taken bool) int {
	if taken {
		return 4
	}
	return 2
}

// bitAddr fetches the two operand bytes of an absolute bit
// operation and decodes them: a 13-bit address in the low
// bits and a bit number in the top three bits of the second
// byte.
func (c *CPU) bitAddr() (addr uint16, bit uint) {
	lo := c.fetch()
	hi := c.fetch()
	return uint16(lo) | uint16(hi&0x1F)<<8, uint(hi >> 5)
}

// exec executes one already-fetched opcode and returns its
// cycle count.
func (c *CPU) exec(op uint8) int {
	// The patterned opcode families first: TCALL n and the
	// direct-page bit operations encode their operand in
	// the opcode byte itself.
	switch {
	case op&0x0F == 0x01: // TCALL n, vector at $FFDE-2n
		// The documented access sequence reads the byte
		// after the opcode (a dummy fetch that does not
		// advance PC) before pushing the return address;
		// the single-step traces record it as a real read.
		_ = c.bus.Read(c.pc)
		c.push16(c.pc)
		vec := 0xFFDE - 2*uint16(op>>4)
		lo := c.bus.Read(vec)
		hi := c.bus.Read(vec + 1)
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		return 8
	case op&0x1F == 0x02: // SET1 dp.bit
		off := c.fetch()
		addr := c.dpAddr(off)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.bus.Read(addr)|(1<<(op>>5)))
		return 4
	case op&0x1F == 0x12: // CLR1 dp.bit
		off := c.fetch()
		addr := c.dpAddr(off)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.bus.Read(addr)&^(1<<(op>>5)))
		return 4
	case op&0x1F == 0x03: // BBS dp.bit,rel
		off := c.fetch()
		v := c.bus.Read(c.dpAddr(off)) // the byte is read before the rel fetch
		rel := int8(c.fetch())
		if c.branch(v&(1<<(op>>5)) != 0, rel) {
			return 7
		}
		return 5
	case op&0x1F == 0x13: // BBC dp.bit,rel
		off := c.fetch()
		v := c.bus.Read(c.dpAddr(off))
		rel := int8(c.fetch())
		if c.branch(v&(1<<(op>>5)) == 0, rel) {
			return 7
		}
		return 5
	}

	switch op {
	// The six shared ALU columns: A destination forms.
	case 0x08, 0x28, 0x48, 0x68, 0x88, 0xA8: // op A,#imm
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.fetch())
		return 2
	case 0x04, 0x24, 0x44, 0x64, 0x84, 0xA4: // op A,dp
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.readDP(c.fetch()))
		return 3
	case 0x14, 0x34, 0x54, 0x74, 0x94, 0xB4: // op A,dp+X
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.bus.Read(c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.x)))
		return 4
	case 0x05, 0x25, 0x45, 0x65, 0x85, 0xA5: // op A,abs
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.bus.Read(c.fetch16()))
		return 4
	case 0x15, 0x35, 0x55, 0x75, 0x95, 0xB5: // op A,abs+X
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.bus.Read(c.fetch16()+uint16(c.x)))
		return 5
	case 0x16, 0x36, 0x56, 0x76, 0x96, 0xB6: // op A,abs+Y
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.bus.Read(c.fetch16()+uint16(c.y)))
		return 5
	case 0x06, 0x26, 0x46, 0x66, 0x86, 0xA6: // op A,(X)
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.bus.Read(c.dpAddr(c.x)))
		return 3
	case 0x07, 0x27, 0x47, 0x67, 0x87, 0xA7: // op A,[dp+X]
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.bus.Read(c.ptrDP(c.fetch()+c.x)))
		return 6
	case 0x17, 0x37, 0x57, 0x77, 0x97, 0xB7: // op A,[dp]+Y
		c.a = c.alu(aluKind(op), c.a, c.bus.Read(c.ptrDP(c.fetch())+uint16(c.y)))
		return 6

	// The six shared ALU columns: memory destination forms.
	// The source operand is fetched and read first, then
	// the destination, in the byte order the manual lists.
	case 0x09, 0x29, 0x49, 0x69, 0x89, 0xA9: // op dp,dp
		// Access order per the documented sequence (and
		// the single-step traces): the source operand byte
		// is fetched and its value read before the
		// destination operand byte is fetched.
		sv := c.readDP(c.fetch())
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.fetch())
		r := c.alu(aluKind(op), c.bus.Read(addr), sv)
		if aluKind(op) != aluCMP {
			c.bus.Write(addr, r)
		}
		return 6
	case 0x18, 0x38, 0x58, 0x78, 0x98, 0xB8: // op dp,#imm
		imm := c.fetch()
		dst := c.fetch()
		addr := c.dpAddr(dst)
		r := c.alu(aluKind(op), c.bus.Read(addr), imm)
		if aluKind(op) != aluCMP {
			c.bus.Write(addr, r)
		}
		return 5
	case 0x19, 0x39, 0x59, 0x79, 0x99, 0xB9: // op (X),(Y)
		sv := c.bus.Read(c.dpAddr(c.y))
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.x)
		r := c.alu(aluKind(op), c.bus.Read(addr), sv)
		if aluKind(op) != aluCMP {
			c.bus.Write(addr, r)
		}
		return 5

	// The shared shift/rotate/increment/decrement columns.
	case 0x1C, 0x3C, 0x5C, 0x7C, 0x9C, 0xBC: // shift A
		c.a = c.shift(shiftKind(op), c.a)
		return 2
	case 0x0B, 0x2B, 0x4B, 0x6B, 0x8B, 0xAB: // shift dp
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.fetch())
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.shift(shiftKind(op), c.bus.Read(addr)))
		return 4
	case 0x1B, 0x3B, 0x5B, 0x7B, 0x9B, 0xBB: // shift dp+X
		addr := c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.x)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.shift(shiftKind(op), c.bus.Read(addr)))
		return 5
	case 0x0C, 0x2C, 0x4C, 0x6C, 0x8C, 0xAC: // shift abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.shift(shiftKind(op), c.bus.Read(addr)))
		return 5

	// Register increments and decrements (the X and Y forms
	// sit outside the shared columns).
	case 0x1D: // DEC X
		c.x--
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 2
	case 0x3D: // INC X
		c.x++
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 2
	case 0xDC: // DEC Y
		c.y--
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 2
	case 0xFC: // INC Y
		c.y++
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 2

	// Compares against X and Y.
	case 0xC8: // CMP X,#imm
		c.cmp8(c.x, c.fetch())
		return 2
	case 0x3E: // CMP X,dp
		c.cmp8(c.x, c.readDP(c.fetch()))
		return 3
	case 0x1E: // CMP X,abs
		c.cmp8(c.x, c.bus.Read(c.fetch16()))
		return 4
	case 0xAD: // CMP Y,#imm
		c.cmp8(c.y, c.fetch())
		return 2
	case 0x7E: // CMP Y,dp
		c.cmp8(c.y, c.readDP(c.fetch()))
		return 3
	case 0x5E: // CMP Y,abs
		c.cmp8(c.y, c.bus.Read(c.fetch16()))
		return 4

	// Register transfers and immediate loads.
	case 0xE8: // MOV A,#imm
		c.a = c.fetch()
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 2
	case 0xCD: // MOV X,#imm
		c.x = c.fetch()
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 2
	case 0x8D: // MOV Y,#imm
		c.y = c.fetch()
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 2
	case 0x7D: // MOV A,X
		c.a = c.x
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 2
	case 0x5D: // MOV X,A
		c.x = c.a
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 2
	case 0xDD: // MOV A,Y
		c.a = c.y
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 2
	case 0xFD: // MOV Y,A
		c.y = c.a
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 2
	case 0x9D: // MOV X,SP
		c.x = c.sp
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 2
	case 0xBD: // MOV SP,X (no flags)
		c.sp = c.x
		return 2

	// A loads from memory.
	case 0xE4: // MOV A,dp
		c.a = c.readDP(c.fetch())
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 3
	case 0xF4: // MOV A,dp+X
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.x))
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 4
	case 0xE5: // MOV A,abs
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.fetch16())
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 4
	case 0xF5: // MOV A,abs+X
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.fetch16() + uint16(c.x))
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 5
	case 0xF6: // MOV A,abs+Y
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.fetch16() + uint16(c.y))
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 5
	case 0xE6: // MOV A,(X)
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.dpAddr(c.x))
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 3
	case 0xBF: // MOV A,(X)+
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.dpAddr(c.x))
		c.x++
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 4
	case 0xF7: // MOV A,[dp]+Y
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.ptrDP(c.fetch()) + uint16(c.y))
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 6
	case 0xE7: // MOV A,[dp+X]
		c.a = c.bus.Read(c.ptrDP(c.fetch() + c.x))
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 6

	// X and Y loads from memory.
	case 0xF8: // MOV X,dp
		c.x = c.readDP(c.fetch())
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 3
	case 0xF9: // MOV X,dp+Y
		c.x = c.bus.Read(c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.y))
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 4
	case 0xE9: // MOV X,abs
		c.x = c.bus.Read(c.fetch16())
		c.setNZ(c.x)
		return 4
	case 0xEB: // MOV Y,dp
		c.y = c.readDP(c.fetch())
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 3
	case 0xFB: // MOV Y,dp+X
		c.y = c.bus.Read(c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.x))
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 4
	case 0xEC: // MOV Y,abs
		c.y = c.bus.Read(c.fetch16())
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 4

	// Stores. Every one performs the documented dummy read
	// of its destination first, except MOV dp,dp and
	// MOV (X)+,A below.
	case 0x8F: // MOV dp,#imm (operand order: imm, then dp)
		imm := c.fetch()
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.fetch())
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, imm)
		return 5
	case 0xFA: // MOV dp,dp (operand order: source, then dest;
		// the source value is read before the dest byte is fetched)
		sv := c.readDP(c.fetch())
		c.bus.Write(c.dpAddr(c.fetch()), sv)
		return 5
	case 0xC4: // MOV dp,A
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.fetch())
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 4
	case 0xD8: // MOV dp,X
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.fetch())
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.x)
		return 4
	case 0xCB: // MOV dp,Y
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.fetch())
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.y)
		return 4
	case 0xD4: // MOV dp+X,A
		addr := c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.x)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 5
	case 0xDB: // MOV dp+X,Y
		addr := c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.x)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.y)
		return 5
	case 0xD9: // MOV dp+Y,X
		addr := c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.y)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.x)
		return 5
	case 0xC5: // MOV abs,A
		addr := c.fetch16()
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 5
	case 0xC9: // MOV abs,X
		addr := c.fetch16()
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.x)
		return 5
	case 0xCC: // MOV abs,Y
		addr := c.fetch16()
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.y)
		return 5
	case 0xD5: // MOV abs+X,A
		addr := c.fetch16() + uint16(c.x)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 6
	case 0xD6: // MOV abs+Y,A
		addr := c.fetch16() + uint16(c.y)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 6
	case 0xC6: // MOV (X),A
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.x)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 4
	case 0xAF: // MOV (X)+,A (no dummy read)
		c.bus.Write(c.dpAddr(c.x), c.a)
		c.x++
		return 4
	case 0xD7: // MOV [dp]+Y,A
		addr := c.ptrDP(c.fetch()) + uint16(c.y)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 7
	case 0xC7: // MOV [dp+X],A
		addr := c.ptrDP(c.fetch() + c.x)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.a)
		return 7

	// 16-bit operations on YA and direct-page words.
	case 0xBA: // MOVW YA,dp
		c.setYA(c.readDP16(c.fetch()))
		c.setNZ16(c.ya())
		return 5
	case 0xDA: // MOVW dp,YA (dummy read on the low byte only)
		off := c.fetch()
		_ = c.readDP(off)
		c.writeDP16(off, c.ya())
		return 5
	case 0x7A: // ADDW YA,dp
		w := c.readDP16(c.fetch())
		ya := c.ya()
		t := uint32(ya) + uint32(w)
		r := uint16(t)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, t > 0xFFFF)
		c.setFlag(FlagH, (ya&0x0FFF)+(w&0x0FFF) > 0x0FFF)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, (ya^w)&0x8000 == 0 && (ya^r)&0x8000 != 0)
		c.setNZ16(r)
		c.setYA(r)
		return 5
	case 0x9A: // SUBW YA,dp
		w := c.readDP16(c.fetch())
		ya := c.ya()
		r := ya - w
		c.setFlag(FlagC, ya >= w)
		c.setFlag(FlagH, (ya&0x0FFF) >= (w&0x0FFF))
		c.setFlag(FlagV, (ya^w)&0x8000 != 0 && (ya^r)&0x8000 != 0)
		c.setNZ16(r)
		c.setYA(r)
		return 5
	case 0x5A: // CMPW YA,dp
		w := c.readDP16(c.fetch())
		ya := c.ya()
		c.setFlag(FlagC, ya >= w)
		c.setNZ16(ya - w)
		return 4
	case 0x3A: // INCW dp
		off := c.fetch()
		lo, hi := c.incDecW(off, true)
		c.setNZ16(uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo))
		return 6
	case 0x1A: // DECW dp
		off := c.fetch()
		lo, hi := c.incDecW(off, false)
		c.setNZ16(uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo))
		return 6
	case 0xCF: // MUL YA: YA = Y*A, flags from the high byte
		t := uint16(c.y) * uint16(c.a)
		c.setYA(t)
		c.setNZ(c.y)
		return 9
	case 0x9E: // DIV YA,X: the hardware divider (see below)
		c.divide()
		return 12

	// Decimal adjust and nibble exchange.
	case 0xDF: // DAA
		a := c.a
		if c.flag(FlagC) || a > 0x99 {
			a += 0x60
			c.setFlag(FlagC, true)
		}
		if c.flag(FlagH) || (a&0x0F) > 9 {
			a += 0x06
		}
		c.a = a
		c.setNZ(a)
		return 3
	case 0xBE: // DAS
		a := c.a
		if !c.flag(FlagC) || a > 0x99 {
			a -= 0x60
			c.setFlag(FlagC, false)
		}
		if !c.flag(FlagH) || (a&0x0F) > 9 {
			a -= 0x06
		}
		c.a = a
		c.setNZ(a)
		return 3
	case 0x9F: // XCN A
		c.a = c.a<<4 | c.a>>4
		c.setNZ(c.a)
		return 5

	// Test-and-set / test-and-clear: N and Z come from a
	// CMP of A against the original memory value, taken
	// before the write; C, H, and V are untouched (the
	// single-step corpus pins this down exactly).
	case 0x0E: // TSET1 abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		v := c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.setNZ(c.a - v)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr) // the target is read twice (documented)
		c.bus.Write(addr, v|c.a)
		return 6
	case 0x4E: // TCLR1 abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		v := c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.setNZ(c.a - v)
		_ = c.bus.Read(addr) // the target is read twice (documented)
		c.bus.Write(addr, v&^c.a)
		return 6

	// One-bit operations against the carry flag.
	case 0xAA: // MOV1 C,mem.bit
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		c.setFlag(FlagC, c.bus.Read(addr)&(1<<bit) != 0)
		return 4
	case 0xCA: // MOV1 mem.bit,C
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		v := c.bus.Read(addr)
		if c.flag(FlagC) {
			v |= 1 << bit
		} else {
			v &^= 1 << bit
		}
		c.bus.Write(addr, v)
		return 6
	case 0x0A: // OR1 C,mem.bit
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		v := c.bus.Read(addr) // the read always happens, even when C already decides the result
		c.setFlag(FlagC, c.flag(FlagC) || v&(1<<bit) != 0)
		return 5
	case 0x2A: // OR1 C,/mem.bit (the bit is inverted first)
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		v := c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, c.flag(FlagC) || v&(1<<bit) == 0)
		return 5
	case 0x4A: // AND1 C,mem.bit
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		v := c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, c.flag(FlagC) && v&(1<<bit) != 0)
		return 4
	case 0x6A: // AND1 C,/mem.bit (the bit is inverted first)
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		v := c.bus.Read(addr)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, c.flag(FlagC) && v&(1<<bit) == 0)
		return 4
	case 0x8A: // EOR1 C,mem.bit
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		if c.bus.Read(addr)&(1<<bit) != 0 {
			c.p ^= FlagC
		}
		return 5
	case 0xEA: // NOT1 mem.bit
		addr, bit := c.bitAddr()
		c.bus.Write(addr, c.bus.Read(addr)^(1<<bit))
		return 5

	// Stack operations. POPs set no flags (POP PSW restores
	// the whole status word instead).
	case 0x0D: // PUSH PSW
		c.push(c.p)
		return 4
	case 0x2D: // PUSH A
		c.push(c.a)
		return 4
	case 0x4D: // PUSH X
		c.push(c.x)
		return 4
	case 0x6D: // PUSH Y
		c.push(c.y)
		return 4
	case 0x8E: // POP PSW
		c.p = c.pull()
		return 4
	case 0xAE: // POP A
		c.a = c.pull()
		return 4
	case 0xCE: // POP X
		c.x = c.pull()
		return 4
	case 0xEE: // POP Y
		c.y = c.pull()
		return 4

	// Conditional branches: 2 cycles not taken, 4 taken.
	case 0x10: // BPL
		return branchCycles(c.branch(!c.flag(FlagN), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0x30: // BMI
		return branchCycles(c.branch(c.flag(FlagN), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0x50: // BVC
		return branchCycles(c.branch(!c.flag(FlagV), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0x70: // BVS
		return branchCycles(c.branch(c.flag(FlagV), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0x90: // BCC
		return branchCycles(c.branch(!c.flag(FlagC), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0xB0: // BCS
		return branchCycles(c.branch(c.flag(FlagC), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0xD0: // BNE
		return branchCycles(c.branch(!c.flag(FlagZ), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0xF0: // BEQ
		return branchCycles(c.branch(c.flag(FlagZ), int8(c.fetch())))
	case 0x2F: // BRA
		off := int8(c.fetch())
		c.pc = uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
		return 4

	// Compare-and-branch and decrement-and-branch: no
	// flags are affected by any of them.
	case 0x2E: // CBNE dp,rel
		v := c.readDP(c.fetch())
		rel := int8(c.fetch())
		if c.branch(c.a != v, rel) {
			return 7
		}
		return 5
	case 0xDE: // CBNE dp+X,rel
		v := c.bus.Read(c.dpAddrIdx(c.fetch(), c.x))
		rel := int8(c.fetch())
		if c.branch(c.a != v, rel) {
			return 8
		}
		return 6
	case 0x6E: // DBNZ dp,rel
		addr := c.dpAddr(c.fetch())
		v := c.bus.Read(addr) - 1
		c.bus.Write(addr, v)
		rel := int8(c.fetch())
		if c.branch(v != 0, rel) {
			return 7
		}
		return 5
	case 0xFE: // DBNZ Y,rel
		c.y--
		rel := int8(c.fetch())
		if c.branch(c.y != 0, rel) {
			return 6
		}
		return 4

	// Jumps, calls, and returns. Calls push the exact
	// return address (the address of the next instruction),
	// unlike the 6502 family.
	case 0x5F: // JMP abs
		c.pc = c.fetch16()
		return 3
	case 0x1F: // JMP [abs+X]
		base := c.fetch16() + uint16(c.x)
		lo := c.bus.Read(base)
		hi := c.bus.Read(base + 1)
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		return 6
	case 0x3F: // CALL abs
		target := c.fetch16()
		c.push16(c.pc)
		c.pc = target
		return 8
	case 0x4F: // PCALL $FF00+operand
		target := 0xFF00 + uint16(c.fetch())
		c.push16(c.pc)
		c.pc = target
		return 6
	case 0x6F: // RET
		c.pc = c.pull16()
		return 5
	case 0x7F: // RET1 (RET from interrupt: PSW first, then PC)
		c.p = c.pull()
		c.pc = c.pull16()
		return 6
	case 0x0F: // BRK: push PC and PSW, vector through $FFDE,
		// set B, clear I (the same vector TCALL 0 uses).
		c.push16(c.pc)
		c.push(c.p)
		c.setFlag(FlagB, true)
		c.setFlag(FlagI, false)
		lo := c.bus.Read(0xFFDE)
		hi := c.bus.Read(0xFFDF)
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		return 8

	// Flag and control operations.
	case 0x20: // CLRP
		c.setFlag(FlagP, false)
		return 2
	case 0x40: // SETP
		c.setFlag(FlagP, true)
		return 2
	case 0x60: // CLRC
		c.setFlag(FlagC, false)
		return 2
	case 0x80: // SETC
		c.setFlag(FlagC, true)
		return 2
	case 0xE0: // CLRV (clears V and H together)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, false)
		c.setFlag(FlagH, false)
		return 2
	case 0xED: // NOTC
		c.p ^= FlagC
		return 3
	case 0xA0: // EI
		c.setFlag(FlagI, true)
		return 3
	case 0xC0: // DI
		c.setFlag(FlagI, false)
		return 3
	case 0x00: // NOP
		return 2
	case 0xEF, 0xFF: // SLEEP, STOP
		c.halted = true
		return haltCycles
	}
	return 2 // unreachable: every opcode is covered above
}

// incDecW runs INCW and DECW at a direct-page address and
// returns the resulting low and high bytes. The access
// sequence is byte-interleaved, as the documented order
// (and the single-step traces) show: the low byte is read,
// adjusted, and written back before the high byte is read,
// adjusted by the carry or borrow out of the low byte, and
// written back. The high byte's address wraps inside the
// direct page, as with every 16-bit direct-page access.
func (c *CPU) incDecW(off uint8, inc bool) (lo, hi uint8) {
	base := c.dpBase()
	loAddr := base + uint16(off)
	hiAddr := base + uint16(off+1)
	lo = c.bus.Read(loAddr)
	if inc {
		lo++
	} else {
		lo--
	}
	c.bus.Write(loAddr, lo)
	hi = c.bus.Read(hiAddr)
	if inc {
		if lo == 0 {
			hi++
		}
	} else {
		if lo == 0xFF {
			hi--
		}
	}
	c.bus.Write(hiAddr, hi)
	return lo, hi
}

// divide runs DIV YA,X as the hardware divider does it, in
// the form the documentation gives: a 17-bit working value
// holding YA is rotated left nine times against the divisor
// shifted to bits 9 and up, conditionally setting the low
// bit and subtracting the divisor, after which the working
// value's bits 16..9 are the remainder (returned in Y), bit
// 8 is the quotient's overflow bit (returned in V), and
// bits 7..0 are the quotient (returned in A). For quotients
// that fit in 9 bits this is exact division; past that the
// result is the hardware's, not the mathematical one. A
// zero divisor flows through the same steps. The H flag is
// not a half carry here: the manual sets it from the low
// nibbles of the original operands, (Y&15) >= (X&15). N and
// Z come from the final A, and C is untouched.
func (c *CPU) divide() {
	c.setFlag(FlagH, (c.y&0x0F) >= (c.x&0x0F))
	yva := uint32(c.ya())
	divisor := uint32(c.x) << 9
	for i := 0; i < 9; i++ {
		yva = ((yva << 1) & 0x1FFFF) | ((yva >> 16) & 1)
		if yva >= divisor {
			yva ^= 1
		}
		if yva&1 != 0 {
			yva = (yva - divisor) & 0x1FFFF
		}
	}
	c.setFlag(FlagV, yva&0x100 != 0)
	c.a = uint8(yva)
	c.y = uint8(yva >> 9)
	c.setNZ(c.a)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/spc700/spc700.go ====================

// Package spc700 is an original implementation of the Sony
// SPC700 CPU, written from the published documentation for
// the chip: the SPC700 programming manual summaries and the
// fullsnes SPC700 section, which restate the manual's opcode
// table, flag definitions, and cycle counts.
//
// The SPC700 is the 8-bit CPU inside the SNES S-SMP audio
// subsystem. It has three 8-bit data registers (A, X, Y, with
// A and Y also usable as the 16-bit pair YA), an 8-bit stack
// pointer that always addresses page 1, a 16-bit program
// counter, and an 8-bit processor status word (PSW). One PSW
// bit, P, selects which page direct-page addressing uses:
// page 0 when P is clear, page 1 when P is set. Direct-page
// address arithmetic wraps inside the selected page, and a
// 16-bit direct-page read takes its high byte from the next
// address inside the same page, never from the page after it.
//
// Cycle counting follows the published per-opcode table (the
// same counts the Tom Harte single-step corpus records):
// every Step returns the documented cycle count of the one
// instruction it executed, taken branches costing their
// documented taken price. Bus accesses within an instruction
// are performed in the documented order and the conformance
// gate verifies the data-carrying access sequence (address,
// direction, and value) against the corpus traces exactly,
// including the dummy reads most store opcodes issue against
// their destination, the second read TSET1 and TCLR1 make of
// their target, and the dummy fetch TCALL makes of the byte
// after its opcode. What is not modeled is wait-state
// stretching through the S-SMP TEST register, since that
// register belongs to the SMP package that owns the bus.
//
// STOP and SLEEP halt the CPU. The published table gives
// their cycle count as unknown (the CPU simply stops), so
// this core charges a halted Step a flat 16 cycles, the
// slice the task contract for this package specifies, and
// changes no state; only Reset recovers from a halt.
//
// DIV YA,X reproduces the hardware divider rather than the
// mathematical one: the documented 17-bit shift algorithm
// whose 9-bit quotient lands in A with its overflow bit in
// V, valid for quotients up to 511, and whose remainder in
// the overflow range is the hardware's value, not the true
// modulo. Division by zero runs through the same algorithm
// with a zero divisor and produces the hardware's result
// instead of trapping.
package spc700

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Bus is the machine interface the CPU drives: the flat
// 64 KB space of the S-SMP (ARAM plus the I/O ports the SMP
// package maps into it). Every address the CPU presents is
// a full 16-bit address in that space.
type Bus interface {
	Read(addr uint16) uint8
	Write(addr uint16, val uint8)
}

// Status word (PSW) bit masks, in the manual's order.
const (
	FlagC = 0x01 // carry
	FlagZ = 0x02 // zero
	FlagI = 0x04 // interrupt enable (no sources exist in the S-SMP)
	FlagH = 0x08 // half carry
	FlagB = 0x10 // break (set by BRK, clear at reset)
	FlagP = 0x20 // direct page select (0 = page 0, 1 = page 1)
	FlagV = 0x40 // overflow
	FlagN = 0x80 // negative
)

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size in bytes.
const SerializeSize = 24

const serializeVersion = 1

// Registers is a snapshot of the programmer-visible CPU
// state. P is the full status word, including the B and P
// bits, exactly as PUSH PSW would push it.
type Registers struct {
	PC uint16
	A  uint8
	X  uint8
	Y  uint8
	SP uint8
	P  uint8
}

// CPU is a single SPC700 instance.
type CPU struct {
	bus Bus

	pc     uint16
	a      uint8
	x      uint8
	y      uint8
	sp     uint8
	p      uint8
	cycles uint64 // SPC cycles since reset
	halted bool   // STOP or SLEEP executed; only Reset recovers
}

// New returns a CPU in its power-on state: registers zeroed.
// Call Reset (with a bus attached) to load the reset vector.
func New() *CPU {
	return &CPU{}
}

// Attach wires the CPU to a bus.
func (c *CPU) Attach(b Bus) { c.bus = b }

// Reset loads the program counter from the reset vector at
// $FFFE/$FFFF, read through the bus, and clears the rest of
// the programmer-visible state: A, X, and Y are zero, the
// stack pointer is zero, the status word is zero (so the B
// flag reads clear, matching the manual's reset state, the
// direct page is page 0, and interrupts are disabled), the
// cycle counter restarts, and a halted CPU runs again.
//
// Real hardware leaves most registers undefined at reset
// and the IPL ROM immediately installs its own values (it
// sets SP itself before doing anything else), so a defined
// all-zero state costs real software nothing and keeps save
// states and tests deterministic. The vector fetch itself
// is not charged to the cycle counter.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	c.a, c.x, c.y = 0, 0, 0
	c.sp = 0
	c.p = 0
	c.cycles = 0
	c.halted = false
	lo := c.bus.Read(0xFFFE)
	hi := c.bus.Read(0xFFFF)
	c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// Regs returns a snapshot of the programmer-visible state.
func (c *CPU) Regs() Registers {
	return Registers{PC: c.pc, A: c.a, X: c.x, Y: c.y, SP: c.sp, P: c.p}
}

// SetRegs installs a register snapshot. The single-step
// conformance runner uses it to place the CPU in corpus
// states; installing a snapshot also clears the halted
// state, since a snapshot describes a CPU that is about to
// execute.
func (c *CPU) SetRegs(r Registers) {
	c.pc = r.PC
	c.a, c.x, c.y = r.A, r.X, r.Y
	c.sp = r.SP
	c.p = r.P
	c.halted = false
}

// Cycles returns the total SPC cycles executed since
// reset, including the flat charge for halted Steps.
func (c *CPU) Cycles() uint64 { return c.cycles }

// Halted reports whether STOP or SLEEP has halted the CPU.
func (c *CPU) Halted() bool { return c.halted }

// haltCycles is the flat cycle charge for a Step taken
// while halted, and for the Step that executes STOP or
// SLEEP itself (see the package comment).
const haltCycles = 16

// Step executes one instruction and returns its cycle
// count from the published table. When the CPU is halted
// it returns haltCycles and changes nothing (the charge
// still accrues to Cycles, so a scheduler advancing other
// hardware against the returned count stays in step).
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	if c.halted {
		c.cycles += haltCycles
		return haltCycles
	}
	op := c.fetch()
	n := c.exec(op)
	c.cycles += uint64(n)
	return n
}

// fetch reads the byte at PC and advances PC.
func (c *CPU) fetch() uint8 {
	v := c.bus.Read(c.pc)
	c.pc++
	return v
}

// fetch16 fetches a little-endian 16-bit operand.
func (c *CPU) fetch16() uint16 {
	lo := c.fetch()
	hi := c.fetch()
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// dpBase is the base address of the current direct page.
func (c *CPU) dpBase() uint16 {
	if c.p&FlagP != 0 {
		return 0x0100
	}
	return 0x0000
}

// dpAddr is the address of a direct-page byte.
func (c *CPU) dpAddr(off uint8) uint16 {
	return c.dpBase() + uint16(off)
}

// dpAddrIdx is the address of a direct-page byte indexed by
// idx: the addition wraps inside the direct page, as the
// manual documents.
func (c *CPU) dpAddrIdx(off, idx uint8) uint16 {
	return c.dpBase() + uint16(off+idx)
}

// readDP reads a direct-page byte.
func (c *CPU) readDP(off uint8) uint8 {
	return c.bus.Read(c.dpAddr(off))
}

// readDP16 reads a 16-bit direct-page value; the high byte
// comes from the next address inside the same direct page,
// wrapping at the page end, as the manual documents.
func (c *CPU) readDP16(off uint8) uint16 {
	base := c.dpBase()
	lo := c.bus.Read(base + uint16(off))
	hi := c.bus.Read(base + uint16(off+1))
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// writeDP16 writes a 16-bit direct-page value with the same
// in-page wrap on its high byte as readDP16.
func (c *CPU) writeDP16(off uint8, v uint16) {
	base := c.dpBase()
	c.bus.Write(base+uint16(off), uint8(v))
	c.bus.Write(base+uint16(off+1), uint8(v>>8))
}

// ptrDP reads the 16-bit pointer stored at a direct-page
// address (its high byte wraps inside the page).
func (c *CPU) ptrDP(off uint8) uint16 {
	return c.readDP16(off)
}

// push writes a byte to the stack in page 1 and decrements
// SP; SP wraps inside the page, as the manual documents.
func (c *CPU) push(v uint8) {
	c.bus.Write(0x0100+uint16(c.sp), v)
	c.sp--
}

// push16 pushes a 16-bit value, high byte first, so a
// matching pull16 reads it back low byte first.
func (c *CPU) push16(v uint16) {
	c.push(uint8(v >> 8))
	c.push(uint8(v))
}

// pull increments SP and reads the byte it lands on.
func (c *CPU) pull() uint8 {
	c.sp++
	return c.bus.Read(0x0100 + uint16(c.sp))
}

// pull16 pulls a 16-bit value, low byte first.
func (c *CPU) pull16() uint16 {
	lo := c.pull()
	hi := c.pull()
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// setFlag sets or clears one status bit.
func (c *CPU) setFlag(f uint8, on bool) {
	if on {
		c.p |= f
	} else {
		c.p &^= f
	}
}

// flag reports one status bit.
func (c *CPU) flag(f uint8) bool { return c.p&f != 0 }

// setNZ sets N and Z from an 8-bit result.
func (c *CPU) setNZ(v uint8) {
	c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x80 != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagZ, v == 0)
}

// setNZ16 sets N and Z from a 16-bit result: N is bit 15
// and Z reports the whole word, as MOVW and the word ALU
// operations document.
func (c *CPU) setNZ16(v uint16) {
	c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x8000 != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagZ, v == 0)
}

// ya is the 16-bit YA pair (Y high, A low).
func (c *CPU) ya() uint16 {
	return uint16(c.y)<<8 | uint16(c.a)
}

// setYA stores a 16-bit value into the YA pair.
func (c *CPU) setYA(v uint16) {
	c.a = uint8(v)
	c.y = uint8(v >> 8)
}

// Serialize writes the CPU state in this package's fixed
// layout: version, registers, cycle counter, and the halted
// flag. There is no other internal state: an SPC700 between
// instructions holds nothing in flight.
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[1:], c.pc)
	out[3] = c.a
	out[4] = c.x
	out[5] = c.y
	out[6] = c.sp
	out[7] = c.p
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(out[8:], c.cycles)
	if c.halted {
		out[16] = 1
	}
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("spc700: bad state size")
	}
	if in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("spc700: unsupported state version")
	}
	c.pc = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[1:])
	c.a, c.x, c.y = in[3], in[4], in[5]
	c.sp = in[6]
	c.p = in[7]
	c.cycles = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(in[8:])
	c.halted = in[16] != 0
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/spc700/spc700_test.go ====================

package spc700

import "testing"

// ramBus is a flat 64 KB test bus that records nothing:
// the unit tests inspect memory directly.
type ramBus struct {
	mem []byte
}

func newRAMBus() *ramBus { return &ramBus{mem: make([]byte, 1<<16)} }

func (b *ramBus) Read(addr uint16) uint8 { return b.mem[addr] }
func (b *ramBus) Write(addr uint16, v uint8) {
	b.mem[addr] = v
}
func (b *ramBus) at(addr uint16) uint8 { return b.mem[addr] }
func (b *ramBus) put(addr uint16, v uint8) {
	b.mem[addr] = v
}
func (b *ramBus) put16(addr uint16, v uint16) {
	b.mem[addr] = uint8(v)
	b.mem[addr+1] = uint8(v >> 8)
}

// base is the baseline register state: code at $8000, stack
// pointer at the top of page 1, flags clear (direct page 0).
func base() Registers {
	return Registers{PC: 0x8000, SP: 0xFF}
}

// newTestCPU returns a CPU attached to a fresh RAM bus,
// placed in the given state with code at PC.
func newTestCPU(regs Registers, code ...byte) (*CPU, *ramBus) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	cpu := New()
	cpu.Attach(bus)
	cpu.SetRegs(regs)
	for i, v := range code {
		bus.put(regs.PC+uint16(i), v)
	}
	return cpu, bus
}

func TestResetLoadsVectorAndClearsState(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.put16(0xFFFE, 0xFFC0)
	cpu := New()
	cpu.Attach(bus)
	cpu.SetRegs(Registers{PC: 0x1234, A: 0xAA, X: 0xBB, SP: 0x42, P: 0xFF})
	cpu.Reset()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got != (Registers{PC: 0xFFC0}) {
		t.Errorf("after reset: %+v, want PC=FFC0 and everything else zero", got)
	}
	if cpu.Cycles() != 0 || cpu.Halted() {
		t.Errorf("after reset: cycles=%d halted=%v", cpu.Cycles(), cpu.Halted())
	}
}

func TestADCFlagsAndHalfCarry(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.A = 0x0F
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x88, 0x01) // ADC A,#$01
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 2 {
		t.Errorf("ADC imm cycles = %d, want 2", n)
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.A != 0x10 || got.P&FlagH == 0 || got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Errorf("0F+01: A=%02x P=%08b, want A=10 H set C clear", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r.A = 0x7F
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x88, 0x01)
	cpu2.Step()
	got = cpu2.Regs()
	if got.A != 0x80 || got.P&FlagV == 0 || got.P&FlagN == 0 {
		t.Errorf("7F+01: A=%02x P=%08b, want A=80 V and N set", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r.A = 0xFF
	r.P = 0
	cpu3, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x88, 0x01)
	cpu3.Step()
	got = cpu3.Regs()
	if got.A != 0x00 || got.P&FlagZ == 0 || got.P&FlagC == 0 || got.P&FlagH == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FF+01: A=%02x P=%08b, want A=00 Z, C, H set", got.A, got.P)
	}
}

func TestSBCBorrowAndHalfCarry(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.A = 0x10
	r.P = FlagC                         // no borrow in
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xA8, 0x01) // SBC A,#$01
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	// 0x10-0x01 = 0x0F: borrow out of bit 4, so H clear; no
	// borrow out of bit 7, so C set.
	if got.A != 0x0F || got.P&FlagH != 0 || got.P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Errorf("10-01: A=%02x P=%08b, want A=0F H clear C set", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r.A = 0x00
	r.P = 0 // borrow in
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xA8, 0x01)
	cpu2.Step()
	got = cpu2.Regs()
	if got.A != 0xFE || got.P&FlagC != 0 || got.P&FlagN == 0 {
		t.Errorf("00-01-borrow: A=%02x P=%08b, want A=FE C clear N set", got.A, got.P)
	}
}

func TestDAAAfterBCDAdd(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.A = 0x45
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x88, 0x55, 0xDF) // ADC #$55; DAA
	cpu.Step()                                // binary 45+55 = 9A, H and C clear
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.A != 0x9A {
		t.Fatalf("pre-DAA A = %02x, want 9A", got.A)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	// BCD 45+55 = 100: A=00 with carry.
	if got.A != 0x00 || got.P&FlagC == 0 || got.P&FlagZ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("DAA: A=%02x P=%08b, want A=00 C and Z set", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r.A = 0x09
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x88, 0x01, 0xDF) // 09+01 = 0A, DAA -> 10
	cpu2.Step()
	cpu2.Step()
	if got := cpu2.Regs(); got.A != 0x10 || got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Errorf("DAA 09+01: A=%02x P=%08b, want A=10 C clear", got.A, got.P)
	}
}
