func TestMULFlagsFromHighByte(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.Y, r.A = 0x10, 0x10
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xCF) // MUL YA
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 9 {
		t.Errorf("MUL cycles = %d, want 9", n)
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	// Product 0x0100: A=00 but Z must be clear, because the
	// flags come from Y (the high byte), not from A.
	if got.A != 0x00 || got.Y != 0x01 || got.P&FlagZ != 0 {
		t.Errorf("10*10: A=%02x Y=%02x P=%08b, want A=00 Y=01 Z clear", got.A, got.Y, got.P)
	}
	r.Y, r.A = 0xFF, 0xFF
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xCF)
	cpu2.Step()
	got = cpu2.Regs()
	if got.Y != 0xFE || got.A != 0x01 || got.P&FlagN == 0 {
		t.Errorf("FF*FF: YA=%02x%02x P=%08b, want FE01 N set", got.Y, got.A, got.P)
	}
}

func TestDIVNormalOverflowAndZero(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.Y, r.A, r.X = 0x00, 100, 10
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x9E) // DIV YA,X
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 12 {
		t.Errorf("DIV cycles = %d, want 12", n)
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.A != 10 || got.Y != 0 || got.P&FlagV != 0 {
		t.Errorf("100/10: A=%d Y=%d P=%08b, want A=10 Y=0 V clear", got.A, got.Y, got.P)
	}
	// Overflow: 0x80E1 / 0x53. The hardware divider leaves
	// A=8D, Y=2A with V set (the true remainder would be
	// 4A; the overflow range is the documented quirk).
	r.Y, r.A, r.X = 0x80, 0xE1, 0x53
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x9E)
	cpu2.Step()
	got = cpu2.Regs()
	if got.A != 0x8D || got.Y != 0x2A || got.P&FlagV == 0 || got.P&FlagN == 0 {
		t.Errorf("80E1/53: A=%02x Y=%02x P=%08b, want A=8D Y=2A V and N set", got.A, got.Y, got.P)
	}
	// Divide by zero runs the same algorithm with a zero
	// divisor: YA=0 becomes A=FF, Y=00, V set, H set (the
	// nibble compare 0 >= 0).
	r.Y, r.A, r.X = 0x00, 0x00, 0x00
	cpu3, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x9E)
	cpu3.Step()
	got = cpu3.Regs()
	if got.A != 0xFF || got.Y != 0x00 || got.P&FlagV == 0 || got.P&FlagH == 0 {
		t.Errorf("0/0: A=%02x Y=%02x P=%08b, want A=FF Y=00 V and H set", got.A, got.Y, got.P)
	}
	// H is the nibble compare of the original operands.
	r.Y, r.A, r.X = 0x25, 0x00, 0x13
	cpu4, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x9E)
	cpu4.Step()
	if got := cpu4.Regs(); got.P&FlagH == 0 {
		t.Errorf("DIV H: P=%08b, want H set ((Y&F)=5 >= (X&F)=3)", got.P)
	}
}

func TestMOVWDirectPageWrap(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.P = FlagP                           // direct page = page 1
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0xBA, 0xFF) // MOVW YA,$FF
	bus.put(0x01FF, 0x34)                 // low byte at the page end
	bus.put(0x0100, 0x12)                 // high byte wraps inside the page
	bus.put(0x0200, 0x99)                 // decoy: the next page must not be read
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 5 {
		t.Errorf("MOVW load cycles = %d, want 5", n)
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.A != 0x34 || got.Y != 0x12 {
		t.Errorf("MOVW wrap: YA=%02x%02x, want 1234", got.Y, got.A)
	}
	// The store wraps the same way.
	r.A, r.Y = 0xEF, 0xBE
	cpu2, bus2 := newTestCPU(r, 0xDA, 0xFF) // MOVW $FF,YA
	cpu2.Step()
	if bus2.at(0x01FF) != 0xEF || bus2.at(0x0100) != 0xBE || bus2.at(0x0200) != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("MOVW store wrap: [01FF]=%02x [0100]=%02x [0200]=%02x, want EF BE 00",
			bus2.at(0x01FF), bus2.at(0x0100), bus2.at(0x0200))
	}
}

func TestStackPushPopOrderAndPageWrap(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.SP = 0x00
	r.A, r.X = 0xAA, 0xBB
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r,
		0x2D, // PUSH A: writes $0100, SP wraps to FF
		0x4D, // PUSH X: writes $01FF, SP = FE
		0xCE, // POP X
		0xAE, // POP A
	)
	cpu.Step()
	if bus.at(0x0100) != 0xAA || cpu.Regs().SP != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("PUSH A at SP=00: [0100]=%02x SP=%02x, want AA FF", bus.at(0x0100), cpu.Regs().SP)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	if bus.at(0x01FF) != 0xBB || cpu.Regs().SP != 0xFE {
		t.Fatalf("PUSH X: [01FF]=%02x SP=%02x, want BB FE", bus.at(0x01FF), cpu.Regs().SP)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.X != 0xBB || got.A != 0xAA || got.SP != 0x00 {
		t.Errorf("after pops: X=%02x A=%02x SP=%02x, want BB AA 00", got.X, got.A, got.SP)
	}
	// POPs set no flags.
	if got.P != 0 {
		t.Errorf("POP set flags: P=%08b, want 0", got.P)
	}
}

func TestCallPushesExactReturnAndRet(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x3F, 0x00, 0x90) // CALL $9000
	bus.put(0x9000, 0x6F)                       // RET
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 8 {
		t.Errorf("CALL cycles = %d, want 8", n)
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.PC != 0x9000 || got.SP != 0xFD {
		t.Fatalf("after CALL: PC=%04x SP=%02x, want 9000 FD", got.PC, got.SP)
	}
	// Return address is the exact next instruction, high
	// byte at $01FF, low at $01FE.
	if ret := uint16(bus.at(0x01FF))<<8 | uint16(bus.at(0x01FE)); ret != 0x8003 {
		t.Errorf("pushed return = %04x, want 8003", ret)
	}
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 5 {
		t.Errorf("RET cycles = %d, want 5", n)
	}
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.PC != 0x8003 || got.SP != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("after RET: PC=%04x SP=%02x, want 8003 FF", got.PC, got.SP)
	}
}

func TestBRKPushesPSWAndRET1Restores(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.P = FlagI | FlagC
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x0F) // BRK
	bus.put16(0xFFDE, 0x9100)
	bus.put(0x9100, 0x7F) // RET1
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 8 {
		t.Errorf("BRK cycles = %d, want 8", n)
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.PC != 0x9100 || got.SP != 0xFC {
		t.Fatalf("after BRK: PC=%04x SP=%02x, want 9100 FC", got.PC, got.SP)
	}
	// Stack: PCH at $01FF, PCL at $01FE, PSW at $01FD, and
	// the pushed PSW is the pre-BRK one (B still clear in
	// the copy); the live PSW has B set and I clear.
	if bus.at(0x01FD) != FlagI|FlagC {
		t.Errorf("pushed PSW = %08b, want %08b", bus.at(0x01FD), FlagI|FlagC)
	}
	if got.P&FlagB == 0 || got.P&FlagI != 0 || got.P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Errorf("after BRK: P=%08b, want B set, I clear, C kept", got.P)
	}
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 6 {
		t.Errorf("RET1 cycles = %d, want 6", n)
	}
	got = cpu.Regs()
	if got.PC != 0x8001 || got.P != FlagI|FlagC || got.SP != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("after RET1: PC=%04x P=%08b SP=%02x, want 8001 IC FF", got.PC, got.P, got.SP)
	}
}

func TestBBSAndBBC(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()

	}

	bus3.put(0x0010, 0x00)
	cpu3.Step()

		t.Errorf("BBC taken: PC=%04x, want 8001", got.PC)
	}
}

func TestCBNETakenAndNot(t *testing.T) {

	r.A = 0x42

		t.Errorf("CBNE not taken cycles = %d, want 5", n)
	}

func TestDBNZLoops(t *testing.T) {
	// MOV $10,#3; loop: DBNZ $10, loop; STOP
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(base(),
		0x8F, 0x03, 0x10, // MOV $10,#$03
		0x6E, 0x10, 0xFD, // DBNZ $10,-3
		0xFF, // STOP
	)
	total := 0
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		total += cpu.Step()
	}
	if bus.at(0x0010) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("after 2 DBNZ: dp[10]=%d, want 1", bus.at(0x0010))
	}
	total += cpu.Step() // third DBNZ falls through
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.PC != 0x8006 {
		t.Fatalf("after loop: PC=%04x, want 8006", got.PC)
	}
	if total != 5+7+7+5 {
		t.Errorf("loop cycles = %d, want %d", total, 5+7+7+5)
	}
	if bus.at(0x0010) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("dp[10] = %d, want 0", bus.at(0x0010))
	}
	// DBNZ Y form: Y counts down in the register.
	r := base()
	r.Y = 2
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xFE, 0xFE, 0xFF) // DBNZ Y,-2; STOP
	cpu2.Step()
	if got := cpu2.Regs(); got.PC != 0x8000 || got.Y != 1 {
		t.Errorf("DBNZ Y taken: PC=%04x Y=%d, want 8000 1", got.PC, got.Y)
	}
	if n := cpu2.Step(); n != 4 {
		t.Errorf("DBNZ Y not taken cycles = %d, want 4", n)
	}
}

func TestTSET1AndTCLR1Semantics(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.A = 0x0F
	r.P = FlagC | FlagH                         // both must survive: only N and Z change
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x0E, 0x34, 0x12) // TSET1 $1234
	bus.put(0x1234, 0xF0)
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 6 {
		t.Errorf("TSET1 cycles = %d, want 6", n)
	}
	if got := bus.at(0x1234); got != 0xFF {
		t.Errorf("TSET1 result = %02x, want FF (F0 OR 0F)", got)
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	// Flags from CMP A,mem on the original value: 0F-F0 =
	// 1F, so N and Z clear; C and H are the caller's.
	if got.P != FlagC|FlagH {
		t.Errorf("TSET1 flags: P=%08b, want C and H only", got.P)
	}
	cpu2, bus2 := newTestCPU(r, 0x4E, 0x34, 0x12) // TCLR1 $1234
	bus2.put(0x1234, 0xFF)
	cpu2.Step()
	if got := bus2.at(0x1234); got != 0xF0 {
		t.Errorf("TCLR1 result = %02x, want F0 (FF AND NOT 0F)", got)
	}
}

func TestBitOpsOnCarry(t *testing.T) {
	// Address $0234 bit 5 encodes as operand bytes 34 A2:
	// low byte 34, then (bit<<5)|(addr>>8) = A0|02.
	r := base()
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r,
		0xAA, 0x34, 0xA2, // MOV1 C,$0234.5
		0x8A, 0x34, 0xA2, // EOR1 C,$0234.5
		0xCA, 0x34, 0xC2, // MOV1 $0234.6,C
		0xEA, 0x34, 0x82, // NOT1 $0234.4
		0x6A, 0x34, 0x22, // AND1 C,/$0234.1
		0x0A, 0x34, 0x22, // OR1 C,$0234.1
	)
	bus.put(0x0234, 0x20) // bit 5 set, bits 6,4,1 clear
	cpu.Step()            // MOV1: C = 1
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("MOV1 C,bit: C clear, want set")
	}
	cpu.Step() // EOR1 with a set bit: C = 0
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("EOR1: C set, want clear")
	}
	cpu.Step() // MOV1 bit,C with C=0: bit 6 stays clear
	if got := bus.at(0x0234); got != 0x20 {
		t.Fatalf("MOV1 bit,C: mem=%02x, want 20", got)
	}
	cpu.Step() // NOT1 bit 4: mem becomes 30
	if got := bus.at(0x0234); got != 0x30 {
		t.Fatalf("NOT1: mem=%02x, want 30", got)
	}
	cpu.Step() // AND1 C,/bit1: bit 1 is 0, inverted to 1; C was 0, stays 0
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("AND1 /bit: C set, want clear (C was 0)")
	}
	cpu.Step() // OR1 C,bit1: bit is 0, C stays 0... then set up a set-bit case below
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("OR1 bit: C set, want clear (bit is 0)")
	}
	// SET1/CLR1 on the direct page.
	cpu2, bus2 := newTestCPU(base(), 0xE2, 0x10, 0x12, 0x10) // SET1 $10.7; CLR1 $10.0
	bus2.put(0x0010, 0x01)
	cpu2.Step()
	if got := bus2.at(0x0010); got != 0x81 {
		t.Errorf("SET1: mem=%02x, want 81", got)
	}
	cpu2.Step()
	if got := bus2.at(0x0010); got != 0x80 {
		t.Errorf("CLR1: mem=%02x, want 80", got)
	}
}

func TestWordALUFlags(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x7A, 0x30) // ADDW YA,$30
	bus.put16(0x0030, 0x0001)
	r.A, r.Y = 0xFF, 0x0F // YA = 0FFF
	cpu.SetRegs(r)
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	// 0FFF+0001 = 1000: H set (carry out of bit 11), C clear.
	if got.A != 0x00 || got.Y != 0x10 || got.P&FlagH == 0 || got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ADDW: YA=%02x%02x P=%08b, want 1000 H set C clear", got.Y, got.A, got.P)
	}
	cpu2, bus2 := newTestCPU(base(), 0x9A, 0x30) // SUBW YA,$30
	bus2.put16(0x0030, 0x0001)
	r2 := base()
	r2.A, r2.Y = 0x00, 0x10 // YA = 1000
	cpu2.SetRegs(r2)
	cpu2.Step()
	got = cpu2.Regs()
	// 1000-0001 = 0FFF: C set (no borrow), H clear (the
	// low 12 bits borrowed: 000 < 001).
	if got.Y != 0x0F || got.A != 0xFF || got.P&FlagC == 0 || got.P&FlagH != 0 {
		t.Errorf("SUBW: YA=%02x%02x P=%08b, want 0FFF C set H clear", got.Y, got.A, got.P)
	}
	cpu3, bus3 := newTestCPU(base(), 0x5A, 0x30) // CMPW YA,$30
	bus3.put16(0x0030, 0x1234)
	r3 := base()
	r3.A, r3.Y = 0x34, 0x12
	cpu3.SetRegs(r3)
	cpu3.Step()
	if got := cpu3.Regs(); got.P&FlagZ == 0 || got.P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Errorf("CMPW equal: P=%08b, want Z and C set", got.P)
	}
	// INCW wraps to zero and reports it.
	cpu4, bus4 := newTestCPU(base(), 0x3A, 0x30) // INCW $30
	bus4.put16(0x0030, 0xFFFF)
	cpu4.Step()
	if bus4.at(0x30) != 0 || bus4.at(0x31) != 0 || cpu4.Regs().P&FlagZ == 0 {
		t.Errorf("INCW wrap: word=%02x%02x P=%08b, want 0000 Z set",
			bus4.at(0x31), bus4.at(0x30), cpu4.Regs().P)
	}
}

func TestAddressingModesIndirect(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.Y = 0x05
	r.X = 0x20
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r,
		0xF7, 0x40, // MOV A,[$40]+Y
		0xE7, 0x10, // MOV A,[$10+X]
		0xBF, // MOV A,(X)+
		0xAF, // MOV (X)+,A
	)
	bus.put16(0x0040, 0x9000)
	bus.put(0x9005, 0x77)
	bus.put16(0x0030, 0x9100) // pointer at dp 10+X = 30
	bus.put(0x9100, 0x66)
	bus.put(0x0020, 0x55) // (X) with X=20
	cpu.Step()
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.A != 0x77 {
		t.Fatalf("MOV A,[dp]+Y: A=%02x, want 77", got.A)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.A != 0x66 {
		t.Fatalf("MOV A,[dp+X]: A=%02x, want 66", got.A)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.A != 0x55 || got.X != 0x21 {
		t.Fatalf("MOV A,(X)+: A=%02x X=%02x, want 55 21", got.A, got.X)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	got = cpu.Regs()
	if bus.at(0x0021) != 0x55 || got.X != 0x22 {
		t.Errorf("MOV (X)+,A: [0021]=%02x X=%02x, want 55 22", bus.at(0x0021), got.X)
	}
}

func TestDirectPageSelectFlag(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(base(),
		0x40,       // SETP
		0xE4, 0x10, // MOV A,$10 (page 1 while P is set)
		0x20,       // CLRP
		0xE4, 0x10, // MOV A,$10 (page 0)
	)
	bus.put(0x0110, 0x11)
	bus.put(0x0010, 0x22)
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.A != 0x11 {
		t.Fatalf("SETP MOV A,dp: A=%02x, want 11 (page 1)", got.A)
	}
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.A != 0x22 {
		t.Errorf("CLRP MOV A,dp: A=%02x, want 22 (page 0)", got.A)
	}
}

func TestShiftsRotatesAndXCN(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.A = 0x81
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x1C) // ASL A
	cpu.Step()
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.A != 0x02 || got.P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Errorf("ASL: A=%02x P=%08b, want 02 C set", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r.A = 0x02
	r.P = FlagC
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x3C) // ROL A (carry in at bit 0)
	cpu2.Step()
	if got := cpu2.Regs(); got.A != 0x05 || got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ROL: A=%02x P=%08b, want 05 C clear", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r.A = 0x03
	r.P = FlagC
	cpu3, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x7C) // ROR A (carry in at bit 7)
	cpu3.Step()
	if got := cpu3.Regs(); got.A != 0x81 || got.P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Errorf("ROR: A=%02x P=%08b, want 81 C set", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r.A = 0xAB
	r.P = 0
	cpu4, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x9F) // XCN A
	if n := cpu4.Step(); n != 5 {
		t.Errorf("XCN cycles = %d, want 5", n)
	}
	if got := cpu4.Regs(); got.A != 0xBA {
		t.Errorf("XCN: A=%02x, want BA", got.A)
	}
}

func TestMOVDpDpAndDpImmOperandOrder(t *testing.T) {
	// MOV dp,dp takes source first, then destination.
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(base(), 0xFA, 0x30, 0x40)
	bus.put(0x0030, 0x99)
	cpu.Step()
	if bus.at(0x0040) != 0x99 || bus.at(0x0030) != 0x99 {
		t.Errorf("MOV dp,dp: dst=%02x src=%02x, want 99 99", bus.at(0x0040), bus.at(0x0030))
	}
	// MOV dp,#imm takes the immediate first, then the dp.
	cpu2, bus2 := newTestCPU(base(), 0x8F, 0x77, 0x40)
	cpu2.Step()
	if bus2.at(0x0040) != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("MOV dp,#imm: [0040]=%02x, want 77", bus2.at(0x0040))
	}
}

func TestJMPIndirectX(t *testing.T) {
	r := base()
	r.X = 0x10
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x1F, 0x00, 0x20) // JMP [$2000+X]
	bus.put16(0x2010, 0x3456)
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 6 {
		t.Errorf("JMP [abs+X] cycles = %d, want 6", n)
	}
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.PC != 0x3456 {
		t.Errorf("JMP [abs+X]: PC=%04x, want 3456", got.PC)
	}
}

func TestHaltStopAndSleep(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(base(), 0xFF) // STOP
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 16 {
		t.Errorf("STOP step cycles = %d, want 16", n)
	}
	if !cpu.Halted() {
		t.Fatalf("STOP did not halt")
	}
	before := cpu.Regs()
	if n := cpu.Step(); n != 16 {
		t.Errorf("halted step cycles = %d, want 16", n)
	}
	if cpu.Regs() != before {
		t.Errorf("halted step changed state: %+v vs %+v", cpu.Regs(), before)
	}
	if cpu.Cycles() != 32 {
		t.Errorf("cycles = %d, want 32", cpu.Cycles())
	}
	cpu.Reset()
	if cpu.Halted() {
		t.Errorf("reset did not clear the halt")
	}
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(base(), 0xEF) // SLEEP
	cpu2.Step()
	if !cpu2.Halted() {
		t.Errorf("SLEEP did not halt")
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundtripMidProgram(t *testing.T) {
	// Program: MOV $10,#5; loop: DBNZ $10,loop; MOV A,#$42; STOP
	prog := []byte{0x8F, 0x05, 0x10, 0x6E, 0x10, 0xFD, 0xE8, 0x42, 0xFF}
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(base(), prog...)
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	state := cpu.Serialize()
	if len(state) != SerializeSize {
		t.Fatalf("Serialize len = %d, want %d", len(state), SerializeSize)
	}
	// Restore into a fresh CPU on a bus with identical
	// contents, then run both to the halt and compare
	// everything.
	bus2 := newRAMBus()
	copy(bus2.mem, bus.mem)
	cpu2 := New()
	cpu2.Attach(bus2)
	if err := cpu2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if cpu2.Regs() != cpu.Regs() || cpu2.Cycles() != cpu.Cycles() {
		t.Fatalf("restored state differs: %+v/%d vs %+v/%d",
			cpu2.Regs(), cpu2.Cycles(), cpu.Regs(), cpu.Cycles())
	}
	for !cpu.Halted() {
		cpu.Step()
		cpu2.Step()
	}
	if cpu2.Regs() != cpu.Regs() || cpu2.Cycles() != cpu.Cycles() {
		t.Errorf("post-restore runs diverged: %+v/%d vs %+v/%d",
			cpu2.Regs(), cpu2.Cycles(), cpu.Regs(), cpu.Cycles())
	}
	for i := range bus.mem {
		if bus.mem[i] != bus2.mem[i] {
			t.Fatalf("bus diverged at %04x: %02x vs %02x", i, bus.mem[i], bus2.mem[i])
		}
	}
	if got := cpu.Regs(); got.A != 0x42 {
		t.Errorf("final A = %02x, want 42", got.A)
	}
	// Halted state roundtrips too.
	cpu3 := New()
	cpu3.Attach(newRAMBus())
	if err := cpu3.Deserialize(cpu.Serialize()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize halted: %v", err)
	}
	if !cpu3.Halted() {
		t.Errorf("halted flag lost in round trip")
	}
	if err := cpu3.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("short state accepted")
	}
	bad := cpu.Serialize()
	bad[0] = 0xFF
	if err := cpu3.Deserialize(bad); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("bad version accepted")
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/w65c816/conformance_test.go ====================

// The Tom Harte single-step conformance gate.
//
// The corpus (github.com/TomHarte/ProcessorTests, the
// 65816 v1 set) provides 10,000 randomized tests per
// opcode per mode: an initial processor state and RAM
// contents, the final state after exactly one instruction,
// the final contents of every RAM cell the instruction
// could have touched, and a cycle-by-cycle bus trace.
//
// The runner installs the initial state, executes one
// Step, and compares:
//   - every register, including PBR, DBR, D, and the
//     emulation flag;
//   - the final value of every listed RAM cell;
//   - the total bus cycle count against the trace length;
//   - the subsequence of valid bus accesses (cycles whose
//     trace entry asserts VDA, VPA, or VPB) against the
//     accesses this CPU actually made: address, direction,
//     and data (the value written, or the value a read
//     returned).
//
// The corpus lives under testroms/tomharte in this module
// (gitignored, local evidence only). When it is absent the
// gate skips. Fetch it with:
//
//	git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/TomHarte/ProcessorTests
//	# then copy or link ProcessorTests/65816/v1/*.json into
//	# testroms/tomharte/
package w65c816

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"testing"
)

type thPair [2]int

type thState struct {
	PC  int      `json:"pc"`
	S   int      `json:"s"`
	P   int      `json:"p"`
	A   int      `json:"a"`
	X   int      `json:"x"`
	Y   int      `json:"y"`
	DBR int      `json:"dbr"`
	D   int      `json:"d"`
	PBR int      `json:"pbr"`
	E   int      `json:"e"`
	RAM []thPair `json:"ram"`
}

type thCycle struct {
	addr  uint32
	val   int // -1 when the trace records null
	write bool
	valid bool
}

func (cc *thCycle) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
	var parts []json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &parts); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(parts) != 3 {
		return fmt.Errorf("cycle entry with %d parts", len(parts))
	}
	var addr int
	if err := json.Unmarshal(parts[0], &addr); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	cc.addr = uint32(addr)
	cc.val = -1
	if string(parts[1]) != "null" {
		var v int
		if err := json.Unmarshal(parts[1], &v); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		cc.val = v
	}
	var pins string
	if err := json.Unmarshal(parts[2], &pins); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(pins) >= 4 {
		cc.write = pins[3] == 'w'
		cc.valid = pins[0] == 'd' || pins[1] == 'p' || pins[2] == 'v'
	}
	return nil
}

type thTest struct {
	Name    string    `json:"name"`
	Initial thState   `json:"initial"`
	Final   thState   `json:"final"`
	Cycles  []thCycle `json:"cycles"`
}

// thBus is the corpus environment: a flat 16 MB of RAM,
// uniform slow accesses, and a recording of every access
// the CPU makes.
type thBus struct {
	mem     []byte
	access  []thAccess
	touched map[uint32]bool
}

type thAccess struct {
	addr  uint32
	val   uint8
	write bool
}

func newTHBus() *thBus {
	return &thBus{mem: make([]byte, 1<<24), touched: make(map[uint32]bool)}
}

func (b *thBus) Read(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint8 {
	a := uint32(bank)<<16 | uint32(addr)
	v := b.mem[a]
	b.access = append(b.access, thAccess{addr: a, val: v})
	return v
}

func (b *thBus) Write(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	a := uint32(bank)<<16 | uint32(addr)
	b.mem[a] = val
	b.touched[a] = true
	b.access = append(b.access, thAccess{addr: a, val: val, write: true})
}

func (b *thBus) Speed(bank uint8, addr uint16) Speed { return SpeedSlow }

// WriteDummy performs an RMW restore write: the memory
// changes, but the corpus does not count the cycle as a
// valid access, so nothing is recorded.
func (b *thBus) WriteDummy(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	a := uint32(bank)<<16 | uint32(addr)
	b.mem[a] = val
	b.touched[a] = true
}

// reset restores the corpus invariant: RAM is zero except
// for the test's initial entries.
func (b *thBus) reset(initial []thPair) {
	for a := range b.touched {
		b.mem[a] = 0
	}
	b.touched = make(map[uint32]bool)
	b.access = b.access[:0]
	for _, p := range initial {
		a := uint32(p[0])
		b.mem[a] = uint8(p[1])
		b.touched[a] = true
	}
}

func runTomHarteFile(t *testing.T, path string) (passed, failed int) {
	t.Helper()
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("read %s: %v", path, err)
	}
	var tests []thTest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &tests); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse %s: %v", path, err)
	}
	bus := newTHBus()
	cpu := New()
	cpu.Attach(bus)
	var firstFailure string
	for _, tc := range tests {
		bus.reset(tc.Initial.RAM)
		cpu.SetRegs(Registers{
			A: uint16(tc.Initial.A), X: uint16(tc.Initial.X), Y: uint16(tc.Initial.Y),
			S: uint16(tc.Initial.S), D: uint16(tc.Initial.D), PC: uint16(tc.Initial.PC),
			DBR: uint8(tc.Initial.DBR), PBR: uint8(tc.Initial.PBR),
			P: uint8(tc.Initial.P), E: tc.Initial.E != 0,
		})
		before := cpu.Cycles()
		// Block moves are the corpus's special case: its
		// generator records at most 100 cycles of a move
		// and stops mid-iteration, so the final state is
		// a truncation, not a completion. The CPU's cycle
		// budget cuts the execution at exactly the
		// recorded cycle so the states line up.
		op := bus.mem[uint32(tc.Initial.PBR)<<16|uint32(tc.Initial.PC)]
		if op == 0x44 || op == 0x54 {
			cpu.SetCycleBudget(before + uint64(len(tc.Cycles)))
			func() {
				defer func() { _ = recover() }()
				cpu.Step()
			}()
			cpu.SetCycleBudget(0)
		} else {
			cpu.Step()
		}
		got := int(cpu.Cycles() - before)
		if msg := checkTomHarte(cpu, bus, tc, got); msg != "" {
			failed++
			if firstFailure == "" {
				firstFailure = fmt.Sprintf("test %q: %s", tc.Name, msg)
			}
			continue
		}
		passed++
	}
	if firstFailure != "" {
		t.Errorf("%s: %d/%d failed; first: %s", filepath.Base(path), failed, passed+failed, firstFailure)
	}
	return passed, failed
}

func checkTomHarte(cpu *CPU, bus *thBus, tc thTest, gotCycles int) string {
	r := cpu.Regs()
	f := tc.Final
	chk := func(name string, got, want int) string {
		if got != want {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s = %d (%#x), want %d (%#x)", name, got, got, want, want)
		}
		return ""
	}
	if msg := chk("pc", int(r.PC), f.PC); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("pbr", int(r.PBR), f.PBR); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("s", int(r.S), f.S); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("p", int(r.P), f.P); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("a", int(r.A), f.A); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("x", int(r.X), f.X); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("y", int(r.Y), f.Y); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("dbr", int(r.DBR), f.DBR); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	if msg := chk("d", int(r.D), f.D); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	gotE := 0
	if r.E {
		gotE = 1
	}
	if msg := chk("e", gotE, f.E); msg != "" {
		return msg
	}
	for _, p := range f.RAM {
		if got := bus.mem[uint32(p[0])]; got != uint8(p[1]) {
			return fmt.Sprintf("ram[%#x] = %#x, want %#x", p[0], got, p[1])
		}
	}
	if gotCycles != len(tc.Cycles) {
		return fmt.Sprintf("cycles = %d, want %d", gotCycles, len(tc.Cycles))
	}
	// The valid-access subsequence: addresses, direction,
	// and data must match the trace exactly.
	valid := make([]thCycle, 0, len(tc.Cycles))
	for _, cc := range tc.Cycles {
		if cc.valid {
			valid = append(valid, cc)
		}
	}
	if len(valid) != len(bus.access) {
		return fmt.Sprintf("valid accesses = %d, want %d", len(bus.access), len(valid))
	}
	for i, cc := range valid {
		acc := bus.access[i]
		if acc.addr != cc.addr {
			return fmt.Sprintf("access %d addr = %#x, want %#x", i, acc.addr, cc.addr)
		}
		if acc.write != cc.write {
			return fmt.Sprintf("access %d (%#x) write = %v, want %v", i, acc.addr, acc.write, cc.write)
		}
		if cc.val >= 0 && int(acc.val) != cc.val {
			return fmt.Sprintf("access %d (%#x) data = %#x, want %#x", i, acc.addr, acc.val, cc.val)
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func TestTomHarte65816(t *testing.T) {
	dir := filepath.Join("..", "..", "testroms", "tomharte")
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("Tom Harte corpus not present at %s: %v", dir, err)
	}
	var files []string
	for _, e := range entries {
		if filepath.Ext(e.Name()) == ".json" {
			files = append(files, filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(files)
	if len(files) == 0 {
		t.Skip("Tom Harte corpus directory holds no test files")
	}
	// TH_FILES (a comma-separated list of base names) limits
	// the run for iteration; the gate itself runs all files
	// present.
	only := map[string]bool{}
	if env := os.Getenv("TH_FILES"); env != "" {
		for _, name := range splitComma(env) {
			only[name] = true
		}
	}
	totalPass, totalFail := 0, 0
	for _, path := range files {
		if len(only) > 0 && !only[filepath.Base(path)] {
			continue
		}
		p, f := runTomHarteFile(t, path)
		totalPass += p
		totalFail += f
	}
	t.Logf("Tom Harte 65816: %d passed, %d failed, %d total", totalPass, totalFail, totalPass+totalFail)
	if len(only) == 0 && len(files) < 512 {
		t.Logf("note: corpus subset present: %d of 512 files", len(files))
	}
}

func splitComma(s string) []string {
	var out []string
	cur := ""
	for _, r := range s {
		if r == ',' {
			out = append(out, cur)
			cur = ""
			continue
		}
		cur += string(r)
	}
	if cur != "" {
		out = append(out, cur)
	}
	return out
}

package w65c816

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

// TestDebugOne runs a single named corpus test named by
// the TH_ONE env var ("<file>:<test name>") and prints the
// full divergence: states, cycles, and both access lists.
// It is a debugging aid, not a gate.
func TestDebugOne(t *testing.T) {
	spec := os.Getenv("TH_ONE")
	if spec == "" {
		t.Skip("TH_ONE not set")
	}
	var file, name string
	for i := 0; i < len(spec); i++ {
		if spec[i] == ':' {
			file, name = spec[:i], spec[i+1:]
			break
		}
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "testroms", "tomharte", file))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var tests []thTest
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &tests); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		if tc.Name != name {
			continue
		}
		bus := newTHBus()
		cpu := New()
		cpu.Attach(bus)
		bus.reset(tc.Initial.RAM)
		cpu.SetRegs(Registers{
			A: uint16(tc.Initial.A), X: uint16(tc.Initial.X), Y: uint16(tc.Initial.Y),
			S: uint16(tc.Initial.S), D: uint16(tc.Initial.D), PC: uint16(tc.Initial.PC),
			DBR: uint8(tc.Initial.DBR), PBR: uint8(tc.Initial.PBR),
			P: uint8(tc.Initial.P), E: tc.Initial.E != 0,
		})
		before := cpu.Cycles()
		cpu.Step()
		got := int(cpu.Cycles() - before)
		t.Logf("initial: %+v", tc.Initial)
		t.Logf("want final: %+v", tc.Final)
		t.Logf("got regs: %+v cycles %d want %d", cpu.Regs(), got, len(tc.Cycles))
		t.Logf("msg: %s", checkTomHarte(cpu, bus, tc, got))
		for i, cc := range tc.Cycles {
			mine := ""
			if i < len(bus.access) {
				a := bus.access[i]
				dir := "r"
				if a.write {
					dir = "w"
				}
				mine = fmt.Sprintf("mine[%d] %s %#x %#x", i, dir, a.addr, a.val)
			}
			t.Logf("cyc %d: want addr %#x val %d write %v valid %v | %s", i, cc.addr, cc.val, cc.write, cc.valid, mine)
		}
		return
	}
	t.Fatalf("test %q not found in %s", name, file)
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/w65c816/exec.go ====================

// Instruction execution for the W65C816S: the 256-opcode
// dispatch, the addressing-mode access sequences, and the
// operations themselves.
//
// Access sequences follow the datasheet's cycle tables.
// Operand fetches read from the program bank; data accesses
// read from the data bank (or bank 0 for direct page, stack
// relative, and pointer fetches); indexed modes perform the
// documented dummy read at the partially computed address
// (high byte not yet fixed) whenever a page is crossed, and
// always for stores and read-modify-writes. Sixteen-bit
// values move low byte first for loads and stores, and high
// byte first on the write-back of a read-modify-write, as
// the datasheet's tables show.
package w65c816

// setFlag sets or clears one status bit.
func (c *CPU) setFlag(f uint8, on bool) {
	if on {
		c.p |= f
	} else {
		c.p &^= f
	}
}

// setNZ8 sets N and Z from an 8-bit result.
func (c *CPU) setNZ8(v uint8) {
	c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x80 != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagZ, v == 0)
}

// setNZ16 sets N and Z from a 16-bit result.
func (c *CPU) setNZ16(v uint16) {
	c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x8000 != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagZ, v == 0)
}

// setNZM sets N and Z from a result at the M width.
func (c *CPU) setNZM(v uint16) {
	if c.m8() {
		c.setNZ8(uint8(v))
	} else {
		c.setNZ16(v)
	}
}

// setNZX sets N and Z from a result at the X width.
func (c *CPU) setNZX(v uint16) {
	if c.x8() {
		c.setNZ8(uint8(v))
	} else {
		c.setNZ16(v)
	}
}

// setA stores an M-width result in the accumulator: in
// 8-bit mode only the low byte changes and the B
// accumulator is preserved.
func (c *CPU) setA(v uint16) {
	if c.m8() {
		c.a = (c.a & 0xFF00) | (v & 0x00FF)
	} else {
		c.a = v
	}
}

// setX stores an X-width result in X; the high byte clears
// in 8-bit index mode.
func (c *CPU) setX(v uint16) {
	if c.x8() {
		c.x = v & 0x00FF
	} else {
		c.x = v
	}
}

// setY stores an X-width result in Y.
func (c *CPU) setY(v uint16) {
	if c.x8() {
		c.y = v & 0x00FF
	} else {
		c.y = v
	}
}

// hiBank picks the bank of a 16-bit access's second
// byte: bank 0 accesses (direct page, stack relative)
// wrap inside bank 0, while data bank accesses carry
// into the next bank at 0xFFFF (the corpus shows both:
// STZ dp wraps its high byte to bank 0, LDA abs,X reads
// its high byte from DBR+1).
func hiBank(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint8 {
	if bank == 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return bank + uint8((uint32(addr)+1)>>16)
}

// readW reads an M-width value at a bank:offset address.
func (c *CPU) readW(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint16 {
	lo := c.read(bank, addr)
	if c.m8() {
		return uint16(lo)
	}
	hi := c.read(hiBank(bank, addr), addr+1)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// readWL reads an M-width value at a 24-bit address; the
// second byte increments the full address (into the next
// bank at a boundary).
func (c *CPU) readWL(addr uint32) uint16 {
	lo := c.read24(addr)
	if c.m8() {
		return uint16(lo)
	}
	hi := c.read24(addr + 1)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// writeW stores an M-width value, low byte first; the
// high byte's bank follows hiBank.
func (c *CPU) writeW(bank uint8, addr uint16, v uint16) {
	c.write(bank, addr, uint8(v))
	if !c.m8() {
		c.write(hiBank(bank, addr), addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
	}
}

// writeWL stores an M-width value at a 24-bit address.
func (c *CPU) writeWL(addr uint32, v uint16) {
	c.write24(addr, uint8(v))
	if !c.m8() {
		c.write24(addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
	}
}

// readXW reads an X-width value at a bank:offset address;
// the high byte's bank follows hiBank.
func (c *CPU) readXW(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint16 {
	lo := c.read(bank, addr)
	if c.x8() {
		return uint16(lo)
	}
	hi := c.read(hiBank(bank, addr), addr+1)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// writeXW stores an X-width value, low byte first; the
// high byte's bank follows hiBank.
func (c *CPU) writeXW(bank uint8, addr uint16, v uint16) {
	c.write(bank, addr, uint8(v))
	if !c.x8() {
		c.write(hiBank(bank, addr), addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
	}
}

// --- direct page address computation -------------------------------------

// dpAddrEx computes a direct-page address: the direct
// page register plus an 8-bit offset, an index, and a small
// displacement (for pointer byte fetches). In emulation
// mode with the direct page low byte zero, the additions
// wrap within the page the register points at, the classic
// 6502 behavior; otherwise the full 16-bit sum is used.
func (c *CPU) dpAddrEx(off uint8, idx uint16, n uint16) uint16 {
	if c.e && c.d&0x00FF == 0 {
		return (c.d & 0xFF00) | uint16(uint8(off)+uint8(idx)+uint8(n))
	}
	return c.d + uint16(off) + idx + n
}

// dpOff fetches a direct-page offset byte and charges the
// extra cycle the hardware spends when the direct page low
// byte is nonzero.
func (c *CPU) dpOff() uint8 {
	off := c.fetch()
	if c.d&0x00FF != 0 {
		c.io()
	}
	return off
}

// dpPtr16 fetches a 16-bit pointer from direct page. The
// base address (offset plus index) follows the direct
// page rules, including the emulation page wrap on the
// addition itself; the high byte is then fetched from
// the next address up with a plain increment, page
// boundary or not (the corpus's (dp,X) trace at the
// boundary reads it from the following page).
func (c *CPU) dpPtr16(off uint8, idx uint16) uint16 {
	base := c.dpAddrEx(off, idx, 0)
	lo := c.read(0, base)
	hi := c.read(0, base+1)
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// dpPtr16Wrapped fetches a 16-bit pointer the way PEI
// does: both bytes addressed through the direct page
// rules, so in emulation mode with DL = 0 the high byte
// wraps inside the page (PEI's corpus trace reads it
// from the page base at offset 0xFF, where the (dp)
// modes read the following page).
func (c *CPU) dpPtr16Wrapped(off uint8) uint16 {
	lo := c.read(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0))
	hi := c.read(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 1))
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// --- operations ----------------------------------------------------------

func (c *CPU) opORA(v uint16) {
	r := c.a | v
	c.setA(r)
	c.setNZM(c.a)
}

func (c *CPU) opAND(v uint16) {
	r := c.a & v
	c.setA(r)
	c.setNZM(c.a)
}

func (c *CPU) opEOR(v uint16) {
	r := c.a ^ v
	c.setA(r)
	c.setNZM(c.a)
}

func (c *CPU) opLDA(v uint16) {
	c.setA(v)
	c.setNZM(v)
}

func (c *CPU) opLDX(v uint16) {
	c.setX(v)
	c.setNZX(v)
}

func (c *CPU) opLDY(v uint16) {
	c.setY(v)
	c.setNZX(v)
}

func (c *CPU) carryIn() uint16 {
	if c.p&FlagC != 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

func (c *CPU) opADC(v uint16) {
	if c.p&FlagD != 0 {
		c.adcDecimal(v)
		return
	}
	cy := c.carryIn()
	if c.m8() {
		a := c.a & 0x00FF
		m := v & 0x00FF
		r := a + m + cy
		c.setFlag(FlagV, (^(a^m)&(a^r)&0x0080) != 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, r > 0x00FF)
		c.setA(r)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(r))
		return
	}
	r := uint32(c.a) + uint32(v) + uint32(cy)
	c.setFlag(FlagV, (^(c.a^v)&(c.a^uint16(r))&0x8000) != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagC, r > 0xFFFF)
	c.a = uint16(r)
	c.setNZ16(c.a)
}

func (c *CPU) opSBC(v uint16) {
	if c.p&FlagD != 0 {
		c.sbcDecimal(v)
		return
	}
	cy := c.carryIn()
	if c.m8() {
		a := c.a & 0x00FF
		m := v & 0x00FF
		r := a - m - (1 - cy)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, ((a^m)&(a^r)&0x0080) != 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, r <= 0x00FF)
		c.setA(r & 0x00FF)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(r))
		return
	}
	r := uint32(c.a) - uint32(v) - uint32(1-cy)
	c.setFlag(FlagV, ((c.a^v)&(c.a^uint16(r))&0x8000) != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagC, r <= 0xFFFF)
	c.a = uint16(r)
	c.setNZ16(c.a)
}

// bcdAddByte adds two bytes as BCD with a carry in,
// returning the adjusted byte, the carry out, and the
// intermediate sum taken after the low nibble's adjust
// but before the high nibble's: the value the overflow
// flag is computed from, on this core as on the 65C02
// family. The low adjust is the hardware's: a nibble sum
// of ten or more gets six added, and the carry between
// nibbles is a plain boolean (the corpus's invalid-digit
// cases pin this down: 0x5F + 0x2C in decimal is 0x81
// with no carry, because the low nibble's 0x1B adjusts to
// a digit of 1 with a carry of exactly 1 into the high
// nibble's 5 + 2 + 1 = 8).
func bcdAddByte(a, m, cy int) (uint8, int, int) {
	lo := (a & 0x0F) + (m & 0x0F) + cy
	if lo >= 10 {
		lo += 6
	}
	c1 := 0
	if lo > 0x0F {
		c1 = 1
	}
	mid := (a & 0xF0) + (m & 0xF0) + (lo & 0x0F) + c1<<4
	r, cout := mid, 0
	if r >= 0xA0 {
		r += 0x60
	}
	if r > 0xFF {
		cout = 1
	}
	return uint8(r), cout, mid
}

// adcDecimal performs BCD addition at the M width. The
// sign and zero flags come from the adjusted result; the
// overflow flag comes from the intermediate sum (see
// bcdAddByte), which is the documented 65C02-family
// decimal behavior the corpus exhibits. Note the corpus
// charges no extra cycle for decimal arithmetic on this
// core.
func (c *CPU) adcDecimal(v uint16) {
	cy := int(c.carryIn())
	if c.m8() {
		a := int(c.a & 0x00FF)
		m := int(v & 0x00FF)
		r, cout, mid := bcdAddByte(a, m, cy)
		c.setFlag(FlagV, (^(a^m)&(a^mid)&0x80) != 0)
		c.setFlag(FlagC, cout != 0)
		c.setA(uint16(r))
		c.setNZ8(r)
		return
	}
	a := int(c.a)
	m := int(v)
	loByte, cy2, _ := bcdAddByte(a&0x00FF, m&0x00FF, cy)
	hiA, hiM := (a>>8)&0x00FF, (m>>8)&0x00FF
	hiByte, cout, mid := bcdAddByte(hiA, hiM, cy2)
	c.setFlag(FlagV, (^(hiA^hiM)&(hiA^mid)&0x80) != 0)
	c.setFlag(FlagC, cout != 0)
	c.a = uint16(hiByte)<<8 | uint16(loByte)
	c.setNZ16(c.a)
}

// sbcDecimal performs BCD subtraction at the M width.
func (c *CPU) sbcDecimal(v uint16) {
	borrow := 1 - int(c.carryIn())
	if c.m8() {
		a := int(c.a & 0x00FF)
		m := int(v & 0x00FF)
		bin := a - m - borrow
		c.setFlag(FlagV, ((a^m)&(a^bin)&0x80) != 0)
		lo := (a & 0x0F) - (m & 0x0F) - borrow
		b2 := 0
		if lo < 0 {
			lo -= 6
			b2 = 1
		}
		hi := (a >> 4) - (m >> 4) - b2
		cOut := true
		if hi < 0 {
			hi -= 6
			cOut = false
		}
		r := uint8((hi&0x0F)<<4 | (lo & 0x0F))
		c.setFlag(FlagC, cOut)
		c.setA(uint16(r))
		c.setNZ8(r)
		return
	}
	a := int(c.a)
	m := int(v)
	bin := a - m - borrow
	c.setFlag(FlagV, ((a^m)&(a^bin)&0x8000) != 0)
	bcdByte := func(av, mv, b int) (uint8, int) {
		lo := (av & 0x0F) - (mv & 0x0F) - b
		b2 := 0
		if lo < 0 {
			lo -= 6
			b2 = 1
		}
		hi := (av >> 4) - (mv >> 4) - b2
		out := 0
		if hi < 0 {
			hi -= 6
			out = 1
		}
		return uint8((hi&0x0F)<<4 | (lo & 0x0F)), out
	}
	loByte, b1 := bcdByte(a&0x00FF, m&0x00FF, borrow)
	hiByte, bOut := bcdByte((a>>8)&0x00FF, (m>>8)&0x00FF, b1)
	c.setFlag(FlagC, bOut == 0)
	c.a = uint16(hiByte)<<8 | uint16(loByte)
	c.setNZ16(c.a)
}

func (c *CPU) opCMP(v uint16) {
	if c.m8() {
		a := c.a & 0x00FF
		m := v & 0x00FF
		c.setFlag(FlagC, a >= m)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(a - m))
		return
	}
	c.setFlag(FlagC, c.a >= v)
	c.setNZ16(c.a - v)
}

func (c *CPU) opCPX(v uint16) { c.compareIdx(c.x, v) }
func (c *CPU) opCPY(v uint16) { c.compareIdx(c.y, v) }

func (c *CPU) compareIdx(reg, v uint16) {
	if c.x8() {
		r := reg & 0x00FF
		m := v & 0x00FF
		c.setFlag(FlagC, r >= m)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(r - m))
		return
	}
	c.setFlag(FlagC, reg >= v)
	c.setNZ16(reg - v)
}

// opBIT tests the accumulator against memory. The immediate
// form sets only Z; memory forms also copy the value's top
// two bits into N and V (at the M width).
func (c *CPU) opBIT(v uint16, imm bool) {
	if !imm {
		if c.m8() {
			c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x0080 != 0)
			c.setFlag(FlagV, v&0x0040 != 0)
		} else {
			c.setFlag(FlagN, v&0x8000 != 0)
			c.setFlag(FlagV, v&0x4000 != 0)
		}
	}
	if c.m8() {
		c.setFlag(FlagZ, (c.a&v)&0x00FF == 0)
	} else {
		c.setFlag(FlagZ, c.a&v == 0)
	}
}

// Shifts and rotates operate on M-width values; each returns
// the new value and sets C, N, Z on the way.

func (c *CPU) opASL(v uint16) uint16 {
	if c.m8() {
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x0080 != 0)
		r := uint16(uint8(v) << 1)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(r))
		return r
	}
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x8000 != 0)
	r := v << 1
	c.setNZ16(r)
	return r
}

func (c *CPU) opLSR(v uint16) uint16 {
	if c.m8() {
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x0001 != 0)
		r := uint16(uint8(v) >> 1)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(r))
		return r
	}
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x0001 != 0)
	r := v >> 1
	c.setNZ16(r)
	return r
}

func (c *CPU) opROL(v uint16) uint16 {
	in := c.carryIn()
	if c.m8() {
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x0080 != 0)
		r := uint16(uint8(v)<<1) | in
		c.setNZ8(uint8(r))
		return r
	}
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x8000 != 0)
	r := (v << 1) | in
	c.setNZ16(r)
	return r
}

func (c *CPU) opROR(v uint16) uint16 {
	in := c.carryIn()
	if c.m8() {
		c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x0001 != 0)
		r := uint16(uint8(v)>>1) | (in << 7)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(r))
		return r
	}
	c.setFlag(FlagC, v&0x0001 != 0)
	r := (v >> 1) | (in << 15)
	c.setNZ16(r)
	return r
}

func (c *CPU) opINC(v uint16) uint16 {
	r := (v + 1) & c.mMask()
	c.setNZM(r)
	return r
}

func (c *CPU) opDEC(v uint16) uint16 {
	r := (v - 1) & c.mMask()
	c.setNZM(r)
	return r
}

// mMask is the value mask at the M width.
func (c *CPU) mMask() uint16 {
	if c.m8() {
		return 0x00FF
	}
	return 0xFFFF
}

// --- addressing-mode runners ---------------------------------------------
//
// Each runner fetches its operands, performs the mode's
// access sequence, and hands the value (for reads) or the
// target address (for stores and read-modify-writes) to the
// operation.

type readFn func(v uint16)

// immM runs an immediate-mode M-width operation.
func (c *CPU) immM(fn readFn) {
	if c.m8() {
		fn(uint16(c.fetch()))
		return
	}
	fn(c.fetch16())
}

// immX runs an immediate-mode X-width operation.
func (c *CPU) immX(fn readFn) {
	if c.x8() {
		fn(uint16(c.fetch()))
		return
	}
	fn(c.fetch16())
}

// rdDP runs a direct-page read.
func (c *CPU) rdDP(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	fn(c.readW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0)))
}

// rdDPX runs a direct-page,X read.
func (c *CPU) rdDPX(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	fn(c.readW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, c.x, 0)))
}

// rdDPY runs a direct-page,Y read (LDX only).
func (c *CPU) rdDPY(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	fn(c.readXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, c.y, 0)))
}

// rdDPIndX runs a (direct page,X) read.
func (c *CPU) rdDPIndX(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	ptr := c.dpPtr16(off, c.x)
	fn(c.readW(c.dbr, ptr))
}

// rdDPInd runs a (direct page) read.
func (c *CPU) rdDPInd(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := c.dpPtr16(off, 0)
	fn(c.readW(c.dbr, ptr))
}

// rdDPIndY runs a (direct page),Y read.
func (c *CPU) rdDPIndY(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := c.dpPtr16(off, 0)
	c.rdIndexedY(c.dbr, ptr, fn, c.readW)
}

// rdDPLong runs a [direct page] long read.
func (c *CPU) rdDPLong(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := c.dpPtr24Linear(off)
	fn(c.readWL(ptr))
}

// rdDPLongY runs a [direct page],Y long read.
func (c *CPU) rdDPLongY(fn readFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := c.dpPtr24(off) + uint32(c.y)
	fn(c.readWL(ptr & 0xFFFFFF))
}

// dpPtr24 fetches a 24-bit pointer from direct page for
// the [dp],Y modes: all three bytes follow the direct
// page wrap rules (in emulation with DL = 0 the bank
// byte's fetch wraps inside the page too: offset 0xFE
// reads it from the page base).
func (c *CPU) dpPtr24(off uint8) uint32 {
	lo := c.read(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0))
	hi := c.read(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 1))
	bk := c.read(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 2))
	return uint32(bk)<<16 | uint32(hi)<<8 | uint32(lo)
}

// dpPtr24Linear fetches a 24-bit pointer for the plain
// [dp] modes: the base follows the direct page rules and
// the remaining bytes are plain increments from it (the
// corpus's lone DL = 0, offset 0xFE case for [dp] reads
// the bank byte from base+2 across the page line). The
// [dp],Y form wraps all three fetches instead; see
// dpPtr24. The split is what the corpus's sparse
// boundary cases show; see the README notes.
func (c *CPU) dpPtr24Linear(off uint8) uint32 {
	base := c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0)
	lo := c.read(0, base)
	hi := c.read(0, base+1)
	bk := c.read(0, base+2)
	return uint32(bk)<<16 | uint32(hi)<<8 | uint32(lo)
}

// rdAbs runs an absolute read.
func (c *CPU) rdAbs(fn readFn) {
	addr := c.fetch16()
	fn(c.readW(c.dbr, addr))
}

// rdAbsLong runs an absolute long read.
func (c *CPU) rdAbsLong(fn readFn) {
	addr := uint32(c.fetch16())
	bank := c.fetch()
	fn(c.readWL(uint32(bank)<<16 | addr))
}

// rdAbsX runs an absolute,X read.
func (c *CPU) rdAbsX(fn readFn) {
	base := c.fetch16()
	c.rdIndexed(c.dbr, base, c.x, fn, c.readW)
}

// rdAbsY runs an absolute,Y read.
func (c *CPU) rdAbsY(fn readFn) {
	base := c.fetch16()
	c.rdIndexed(c.dbr, base, c.y, fn, c.readW)
}

// rdAbsLongX runs an absolute long,X read. Long indexed
// modes never pay a page-cross cycle; the index carries
// into the bank.
func (c *CPU) rdAbsLongX(fn readFn) {
	addr := uint32(c.fetch16())
	bank := c.fetch()
	fn(c.readWL((uint32(bank)<<16 | addr) + uint32(c.x)))
}

// rdSR runs a stack-relative read.
func (c *CPU) rdSR(fn readFn) {
	off := c.fetch()
	c.io()
	fn(c.readW(0, c.s+uint16(off)))
}

// rdSRIndY runs a (stack relative),Y read: the pointer
// comes off the stack, the data from the data bank. The
// Y addition always costs a dead cycle, spent driving the
// pointer's high-byte address again (per the corpus
// trace), whether or not the addition crosses a page.
func (c *CPU) rdSRIndY(fn readFn) {
	off := c.fetch()
	c.io()
	loAddr := c.s + uint16(off)
	lo := c.read(0, loAddr)
	hi := c.read(0, loAddr+1)
	ptr := uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
	c.dummy(0, loAddr+1)
	sum := uint32(ptr) + uint32(c.y)
	fn(c.readW(c.dbr+uint8(sum>>16), uint16(sum)))
}

// rdIndexed performs an indexed read within a bank. When
// the index addition changes the page, the hardware
// spends a dead cycle driving the partially fixed address
// (the corpus records it with no valid-access pins, so it
// is a dummy cycle here). When the addition overflows 16
// bits entirely, the data bank increments: the corpus's
// BIT abs,X trace reads its data from DBR+1 in that case.
func (c *CPU) rdIndexed(bank uint8, base, idx uint16, fn readFn, rd func(uint8, uint16) uint16) {
	sum := uint32(base) + uint32(idx)
	eff := uint16(sum)
	if (base^eff)&0xFF00 != 0 || !c.x8() {
		// The fixup cycle is owed when the addition
		// changes the page, and always when the index
		// registers are 16-bit (the corpus's (dp),Y trace
		// spends it on an in-page addition with a 16-bit
		// index whose value happens to be small).
		c.dummy(bank, (base&0xFF00)|(eff&0x00FF))
	}
	fn(rd(bank+uint8(sum>>16), eff))
}

// rdIndexedY is rdIndexed for a pointer already fetched:
// the same carry rule against the pointer.
func (c *CPU) rdIndexedY(bank uint8, ptr uint16, fn readFn, rd func(uint8, uint16) uint16) {
	c.rdIndexed(bank, ptr, c.y, fn, rd)
}

// --- store runners ---------------------------------------------------------

type addrFn func(bank uint8, addr uint16)

// stIndexed is shared by the indexed store modes: the
// dead fixup cycle always happens (a dummy cycle; see
// rdIndexed), and a 16-bit overflow carries into the
// bank like the read side.
func (c *CPU) stIndexed(bank uint8, base, idx uint16, wr func(uint8, uint16)) {
	sum := uint32(base) + uint32(idx)
	c.dummy(bank, (base&0xFF00)|(uint16(sum)&0x00FF))
	wr(bank+uint8(sum>>16), uint16(sum))
}

func (c *CPU) stDP(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.writeW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0), v)
}

func (c *CPU) stDPX(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	c.writeW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, c.x, 0), v)
}

func (c *CPU) stDPIndX(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	ptr := c.dpPtr16(off, c.x)
	c.writeW(c.dbr, ptr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) stDPInd(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := c.dpPtr16(off, 0)
	c.writeW(c.dbr, ptr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) stDPIndY(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := c.dpPtr16(off, 0)
	c.stIndexed(c.dbr, ptr, c.y, func(b uint8, a uint16) { c.writeW(b, a, v) })
}

func (c *CPU) stDPLong(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := c.dpPtr24Linear(off)
	c.writeWL(ptr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) stDPLongY(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	ptr := (c.dpPtr24(off) + uint32(c.y)) & 0xFFFFFF
	c.writeWL(ptr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) stAbs(v uint16) {
	addr := c.fetch16()
	c.writeW(c.dbr, addr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) stAbsLong(v uint16) {
	addr := uint32(c.fetch16())
	bank := c.fetch()
	c.writeWL(uint32(bank)<<16|addr, v)
}

func (c *CPU) stAbsX(v uint16) {
	base := c.fetch16()
	c.stIndexed(c.dbr, base, c.x, func(b uint8, a uint16) { c.writeW(b, a, v) })
}

func (c *CPU) stAbsY(v uint16) {
	base := c.fetch16()
	c.stIndexed(c.dbr, base, c.y, func(b uint8, a uint16) { c.writeW(b, a, v) })
}

func (c *CPU) stAbsLongX(v uint16) {
	addr := uint32(c.fetch16())
	bank := c.fetch()
	c.writeWL((uint32(bank)<<16|addr)+uint32(c.x), v)
}

func (c *CPU) stSR(v uint16) {
	off := c.fetch()
	c.io()
	c.writeW(0, c.s+uint16(off), v)
}

func (c *CPU) stSRIndY(v uint16) {
	off := c.fetch()
	c.io()
	loAddr := c.s + uint16(off)
	lo := c.read(0, loAddr)
	hi := c.read(0, loAddr+1)
	ptr := uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
	c.dummy(0, loAddr+1)
	sum := uint32(ptr) + uint32(c.y)
	c.writeW(c.dbr+uint8(sum>>16), uint16(sum), v)
}

// Index stores at X width (STX uses dp,Y; STY uses dp,X).

func (c *CPU) stXDP(v uint16) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.writeXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0), v)
}

func (c *CPU) stXDPX(v uint16) { // STY dp,X
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	c.writeXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, c.x, 0), v)
}

func (c *CPU) stXDPY(v uint16) { // STX dp,Y
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	c.writeXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, c.y, 0), v)
}

func (c *CPU) stXAbs(v uint16) {
	addr := c.fetch16()
	c.writeXW(c.dbr, addr, v)
}

// --- read-modify-write runners ---------------------------------------------

type rmwFn func(v uint16) uint16

// rmwFinish writes a modified value back, matching the
// corpus traces. In 8-bit mode the hardware first drives
// the original value back out (the dummy write: a real
// bus write the corpus does not count as a valid access)
// and then writes the modified value, with no internal
// cycle. In 16-bit mode the modify costs one internal
// cycle, then the new value is written high byte first.
func (c *CPU) rmwFinish(bank uint8, addr uint16, orig, v uint16) {
	if c.m8() {
		c.writeDummy(bank, addr, uint8(orig))
		c.write(bank, addr, uint8(v))
		return
	}
	c.io()
	c.write(bank, addr+1, uint8(v>>8))
	c.write(bank, addr, uint8(v))
}

func (c *CPU) rmwDP(fn rmwFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	addr := c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0)
	v := c.readW(0, addr)
	c.rmwFinish(0, addr, v, fn(v))
}

func (c *CPU) rmwDPX(fn rmwFn) {
	off := c.dpOff()
	c.io()
	addr := c.dpAddrEx(off, c.x, 0)
	v := c.readW(0, addr)
	c.rmwFinish(0, addr, v, fn(v))
}

func (c *CPU) rmwAbs(fn rmwFn) {
	addr := c.fetch16()
	v := c.readW(c.dbr, addr)
	c.rmwFinish(c.dbr, addr, v, fn(v))
}

func (c *CPU) rmwAbsX(fn rmwFn) {
	base := c.fetch16()
	sum := uint32(base) + uint32(c.x)
	c.dummy(c.dbr, (base&0xFF00)|(uint16(sum)&0x00FF))
	bank := c.dbr + uint8(sum>>16)
	addr := uint16(sum)
	v := c.readW(bank, addr)
	c.rmwFinish(bank, addr, v, fn(v))
}

// --- branches and jumps ----------------------------------------------------

// branch performs a short relative branch: the taken
// case costs one internal cycle. The page-cross penalty
// the 6502 pays applies on this core only in emulation
// mode; the corpus's native-mode traces cross pages in
// three cycles total.
func (c *CPU) branch(cond bool) {
	off := int8(c.fetch())
	if !cond {
		return
	}
	c.io()
	target := uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
	if c.e && (c.pc^target)&0xFF00 != 0 {
		c.io()
	}
	c.pc = target
}

// branchLong performs a 16-bit relative branch (BRA and
// BRL: always taken, 4 cycles either way).
func (c *CPU) branchLong() {
	off := int16(c.fetch16())
	c.io()
	c.pc = uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off))
}

// --- block moves -----------------------------------------------------------

// execBlockMove executes an MVN (0x54) or MVP (0x44) from
// its opcode fetch (already done by Step) to completion.
// The corpus's traces pin the shape: the move runs as a
// series of identical seven-cycle iterations, each one
// re-fetching the opcode and both bank operands
// (destination first, then source, as they lie in memory),
// reading the source byte, writing the destination byte,
// and spending two dead cycles at the write address. DBR
// takes the destination bank as the move runs. Between
// iterations the interrupt poll is honored: if an
// interrupt was recognized the move suspends with PC back
// on its own opcode byte and A, X, and Y holding the
// progress, so the interrupt is taken at the boundary and
// the re-executed move continues on return, which is the
// hardware's documented block-move interrupt behavior.
func (c *CPU) execBlockMove(op uint8) {
	c.mvOp = op
	opAddr := c.pc - 1
	c.mvOpcodePC = opAddr
	first := true
	for {
		if !first {
			c.fetch() // the iteration's opcode re-fetch
		}
		first = false
		c.mvDstBank = c.fetch()
		c.mvSrcBank = c.fetch()
		c.dbr = c.mvDstBank
		v := c.read(c.mvSrcBank, c.x)
		c.write(c.mvDstBank, c.y, v)
		wa := c.y // the dead cycles sit on the write address
		// The register updates land before the iteration's
		// two dead cycles: the corpus's states cut at a
		// completing move's final cycle already show them.
		if op == 0x54 { // MVN counts up
			c.x++
			c.y++
		} else { // MVP counts down
			c.x--
			c.y--
		}
		if c.x8() {
			// In 8-bit index mode the pointers wrap inside
			// their low bytes, like every other index
			// register update.
			c.x &= 0x00FF
			c.y &= 0x00FF
		}
		c.a--
		done := c.a == 0xFFFF
		c.dummy(c.mvDstBank, wa)
		c.dummy(c.mvDstBank, wa)
		if done {
			return
		}
		c.pc = opAddr
		// Poll between bytes: the samples from the move's
		// cycles decide whether an interrupt suspends it.
		c.latchPoll()
		if c.takeNMI || c.takeIRQ || c.takeAbort {
			return
		}
	}
}

// --- dispatch ---------------------------------------------------------------

// alu selects an M-width ALU operation by its group index:
// the order matches the opcode map's aaa field for the
// cc=01 family (0 ORA, 1 AND, 2 EOR, 3 ADC, 4 STA, 5 LDA,
// 6 CMP, 7 SBC).
func (c *CPU) alu(aaa uint8, v uint16) {
	switch aaa {
	case 0:
		c.opORA(v)
	case 1:
		c.opAND(v)
	case 2:
		c.opEOR(v)
	case 3:
		c.opADC(v)
	case 5:
		c.opLDA(v)
	case 6:
		c.opCMP(v)
	case 7:
		c.opSBC(v)
	}
}

// aluMode runs the ALU operation aaa in addressing mode
// bbb of the cc=01 family: 0 (dp,X), 1 dp, 2 immediate,
// 3 absolute, 4 (dp),Y, 5 dp,X, 6 absolute,Y, 7 absolute,X.
// STA (aaa 4) has a store runner per mode instead, and its
// immediate slot is BIT #.
func (c *CPU) aluMode(aaa, bbb uint8) {
	if aaa == 4 { // STA
		switch bbb {
		case 0:
			c.stDPIndX(c.a)
		case 1:
			c.stDP(c.a)
		case 3:
			c.stAbs(c.a)
		case 4:
			c.stDPIndY(c.a)
		case 5:
			c.stDPX(c.a)
		case 6:
			c.stAbsY(c.a)
		case 7:
			c.stAbsX(c.a)
		}
		return
	}
	fn := func(v uint16) { c.alu(aaa, v) }
	switch bbb {
	case 0:
		c.rdDPIndX(fn)
	case 1:
		c.rdDP(fn)
	case 2:
		c.immM(fn)
	case 3:
		c.rdAbs(fn)
	case 4:
		c.rdDPIndY(fn)
	case 5:
		c.rdDPX(fn)
	case 6:
		c.rdAbsY(fn)
	case 7:
		c.rdAbsX(fn)
	}
}

// aluExt runs the additional modes the 65816 adds around
// the cc=01 family: stack relative, direct page indirect
// variants, and the longs. slot names the mode by its
// offset in the opcode row (0x03 sr, 0x07 [dp], 0x12 (dp),
// 0x0F absl, 0x13 (sr,s),Y, 0x17 [dp],Y, 0x1F absl,X).
func (c *CPU) aluExt(aaa uint8, slot uint8) {
	if aaa == 4 { // STA
		switch slot {
		case 0x03:
			c.stSR(c.a)
		case 0x07:
			c.stDPLong(c.a)
		case 0x12:
			c.stDPInd(c.a)
		case 0x0F:
			c.stAbsLong(c.a)
		case 0x13:
			c.stSRIndY(c.a)
		case 0x17:
			c.stDPLongY(c.a)
		case 0x1F:
			c.stAbsLongX(c.a)
		}
		return
	}
	fn := func(v uint16) { c.alu(aaa, v) }
	switch slot {
	case 0x03:
		c.rdSR(fn)
	case 0x07:
		c.rdDPLong(fn)
	case 0x12:
		c.rdDPInd(fn)
	case 0x0F:
		c.rdAbsLong(fn)
	case 0x13:
		c.rdSRIndY(fn)
	case 0x17:
		c.rdDPLongY(fn)
	case 0x1F:
		c.rdAbsLongX(fn)
	}
}

// exec executes the instruction whose opcode was just
// fetched. The dispatch is an explicit switch over all 256
// opcodes: the 65816 map extends the 6502's regular groups
// with enough single opcodes that a table reads clearer
// than a decoder.
func (c *CPU) exec(op uint8) {
	// The cc=01 ALU family occupies opcodes whose low two
	// bits are 01, laid out as (aaa<<5)|(bbb<<2)|1.
	if op&0x03 == 0x01 {
		aaa := op >> 5
		bbb := (op >> 2) & 0x07
		if aaa == 4 && bbb == 2 {
			// 0x89: BIT # takes STA's immediate slot.
			c.immM(func(v uint16) { c.opBIT(v, true) })
			return
		}
		c.aluMode(aaa, bbb)
		return
	}
	// The 65816's extra cc=01 modes sit at offsets 0x02,
	// 0x03, 0x07, 0x0F, 0x12, 0x13, 0x17, 0x1F in each row
	// for some slots; those opcodes are dispatched in the
	// switch below by their exact values.
	switch op {
	// Row 0x00
	case 0x00: // BRK
		c.softwareInterrupt(false)
	case 0x02: // COP
		c.softwareInterrupt(true)
	case 0x03, 0x07, 0x0F, 0x13, 0x17, 0x1F, 0x12:
		c.aluExt(0, op&0x1F) // ORA extended modes (0x12 grouped here)
	case 0x04: // TSB dp
		c.rmwDP(func(v uint16) uint16 {
			c.setFlag(FlagZ, c.a&v&c.mMask() == 0)
			return v | c.a&c.mMask()
		})
	case 0x06: // ASL dp
		c.rmwDP(c.opASL)
	case 0x08: // PHP
		c.io()
		c.push(c.statusByte(true))
	case 0x0A: // ASL A
		c.io()
		c.setA(c.opASL(c.a))
	case 0x0B: // PHD
		c.io()
		c.push16(c.d)
	case 0x0C: // TSB abs
		c.rmwAbs(func(v uint16) uint16 {
			c.setFlag(FlagZ, c.a&v&c.mMask() == 0)
			return v | c.a&c.mMask()
		})
	case 0x0E: // ASL abs
		c.rmwAbs(c.opASL)

	// Row 0x10
	case 0x10: // BPL
		c.branch(c.p&FlagN == 0)
	case 0x14: // TRB dp
		c.rmwDP(func(v uint16) uint16 {
			c.setFlag(FlagZ, c.a&v&c.mMask() == 0)
			return v &^ (c.a & c.mMask())
		})
	case 0x16: // ASL dp,X
		c.rmwDPX(c.opASL)
	case 0x18: // CLC
		c.io()
		c.p &^= FlagC
	case 0x1A: // INC A
		c.io()
		c.setA(c.opINC(c.a))
	case 0x1B: // TCS
		c.io()
		if c.e {
			c.s = 0x0100 | (c.a & 0x00FF)
		} else {
			c.s = c.a
		}
	case 0x1C: // TRB abs
		c.rmwAbs(func(v uint16) uint16 {
			c.setFlag(FlagZ, c.a&v&c.mMask() == 0)
			return v &^ (c.a & c.mMask())
		})
	case 0x1E: // ASL abs,X
		c.rmwAbsX(c.opASL)
	case 0x23, 0x27, 0x2F, 0x33, 0x37, 0x3F, 0x32:
		c.aluExt(1, op&0x1F) // AND extended modes

	// Row 0x20
	case 0x20: // JSR abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.io()
		ret := c.pc - 1 // return address: the high operand byte
		c.pushInt(uint8(ret >> 8))
		c.pushInt(uint8(ret))
		c.pc = addr
	case 0x22: // JSR long (JSL)
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.push(c.pbr)
		c.io()
		bank := c.fetch()
		c.push16(c.pc - 1) // return address: the bank operand byte
		c.pbr = bank
		c.pc = addr
	case 0x24: // BIT dp
		c.rdDP(func(v uint16) { c.opBIT(v, false) })
	case 0x26: // ROL dp
		c.rmwDP(c.opROL)
	case 0x28: // PLP
		c.io()
		c.setP(c.pullB())
		c.io()
	case 0x2A: // ROL A
		c.io()
		c.setA(c.opROL(c.a))
	case 0x2B: // PLD
		c.io()
		c.d = c.pull16()
		c.setNZ16(c.d)
		c.io()
	case 0x2C: // BIT abs
		c.rdAbs(func(v uint16) { c.opBIT(v, false) })
	case 0x2E: // ROL abs
		c.rmwAbs(c.opROL)

	// Row 0x30
	case 0x30: // BMI
		c.branch(c.p&FlagN != 0)
	case 0x34: // BIT dp,X
		off := c.dpOff()
		c.io()
		c.opBIT(c.readW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, c.x, 0)), false)
	case 0x36: // ROL dp,X
		c.rmwDPX(c.opROL)
	case 0x38: // SEC
		c.io()
		c.p |= FlagC
	case 0x3A: // DEC A
		c.io()
		c.setA(c.opDEC(c.a))
	case 0x3B: // TSC
		c.io()
		c.a = c.s
		c.setNZ16(c.a)
	case 0x3C: // BIT abs,X
		base := c.fetch16()
		c.rdIndexed(c.dbr, base, c.x, func(v uint16) { c.opBIT(v, false) }, c.readW)
	case 0x3E: // ROL abs,X
		c.rmwAbsX(c.opROL)
	case 0x43, 0x47, 0x4F, 0x53, 0x57, 0x5F, 0x52:
		c.aluExt(2, op&0x1F) // EOR extended modes

	// Row 0x40
	case 0x40: // RTI
		c.io()
		c.io()
		c.setP(c.pullB())
		if c.e {
			lo := c.pullB()
			hi := c.pullB()
			c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		} else {
			c.pc = c.pull16()
			c.pbr = c.pull()
		}
	case 0x42: // WDM: a two-byte NOP; the reserved second
		// byte is skipped in a dead cycle, not fetched (the
		// corpus records only the opcode fetch as valid).
		c.dummy(c.pbr, c.pc)
		c.pc++
	case 0x44: // MVP
		c.execBlockMove(op)
	case 0x50: // BVC
		c.branch(c.p&FlagV == 0)
	case 0x58: // CLI
		c.io()
		c.p &^= FlagI
	case 0x46: // LSR dp
		c.rmwDP(c.opLSR)
	case 0x48: // PHA
		c.io()
		if c.m8() {
			c.push(uint8(c.a))
		} else {
			c.push16(c.a)
		}
	case 0x4A: // LSR A
		c.io()
		c.setA(c.opLSR(c.a))
	case 0x4B: // PHK
		c.io()
		c.push(c.pbr)
	case 0x4C: // JMP abs
		c.pc = c.fetch16()
	case 0x4E: // LSR abs
		c.rmwAbs(c.opLSR)
	case 0x54: // MVN
		c.execBlockMove(op)
	case 0x56: // LSR dp,X
		c.rmwDPX(c.opLSR)
	case 0x5A: // PHY
		c.io()
		if c.x8() {
			c.push(uint8(c.y))
		} else {
			c.push16(c.y)
		}
	case 0x5B: // TCD
		c.io()
		c.d = c.a
		c.setNZ16(c.d)
	case 0x5C: // JMP absl
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.pbr = c.fetch()
		c.pc = addr
	case 0x5E: // LSR abs,X
		c.rmwAbsX(c.opLSR)
	case 0x63, 0x67, 0x6F, 0x73, 0x77, 0x7F, 0x72:
		c.aluExt(3, op&0x1F) // ADC extended modes

	// Row 0x60
	case 0x60: // RTS
		c.io()
		if c.e {
			lo := c.pullB()
			hi := c.pullB()
			c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		} else {
			c.pc = c.pull16()
		}
		c.io()
		c.pc++
		c.io()
	case 0x62: // PER
		off := int16(c.fetch16())
		c.io()
		c.push16(uint16(int32(c.pc) + int32(off)))
	case 0x64: // STZ dp
		c.stDP(0)
	case 0x66: // ROR dp
		c.rmwDP(c.opROR)
	case 0x68: // PLA
		c.io()
		if c.m8() {
			c.setA(uint16(c.pullB()))
		} else {
			c.setA(c.pull16())
		}
		c.setNZM(c.a)
		c.io()
	case 0x6A: // ROR A
		c.io()
		c.setA(c.opROR(c.a))
	case 0x6B: // RTL
		c.io()
		c.pc = c.pull16()
		c.pbr = c.pull()
		c.pc++
		c.io()
	case 0x6C: // JMP (abs)
		addr := c.fetch16()
		lo := c.read(0, addr)
		hi := c.read(0, addr+1)
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
	case 0x6E: // ROR abs
		c.rmwAbs(c.opROR)
	case 0x70: // BVS
		c.branch(c.p&FlagV != 0)
	case 0x74: // STZ dp,X
		c.stDPX(0)
	case 0x76: // ROR dp,X
		c.rmwDPX(c.opROR)
	case 0x78: // SEI
		c.io()
		c.p |= FlagI
	case 0x7A: // PLY
		c.io()
		if c.x8() {
			c.setY(uint16(c.pullB()))
		} else {
			c.setY(c.pull16())
		}
		c.setNZX(c.y)
		c.io()
	case 0x7B: // TDC: like TSC, it flags the moved value.
		c.io()
		c.a = c.d
		c.setNZ16(c.a)
	case 0x7C: // JMP (abs,X): the pointer table lives in
		// the program bank (unlike JMP [abs], whose pointer
		// is in bank 0; the corpus traces separate the two).
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.io()
		sum := addr + c.x
		lo := c.read(c.pbr, sum)
		hi := c.read(c.pbr, sum+1)
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
	case 0x7E: // ROR abs,X
		c.rmwAbsX(c.opROR)
	case 0x83, 0x87, 0x8F, 0x93, 0x97, 0x9F, 0x92:
		c.aluExt(4, op&0x1F) // STA extended modes

	// Row 0x80
	case 0x80: // BRA
		c.branch(true)
	case 0x82: // BRL
		c.branchLong()
	case 0x84: // STY dp
		c.stXDP(c.y)
	case 0x86: // STX dp
		c.stXDP(c.x)
	case 0x88: // DEY
		c.io()
		c.setY(c.y - 1)
		c.setNZX(c.y)
	case 0x8A: // TXA
		c.io()
		if c.m8() {
			c.setA(c.x & 0x00FF)
		} else {
			c.setA(c.x)
		}
		c.setNZM(c.a)
	case 0x8B: // PHB
		c.io()
		c.push(c.dbr)
	case 0x8C: // STY abs
		c.stXAbs(c.y)
	case 0x8E: // STX abs
		c.stXAbs(c.x)
	case 0x90: // BCC
		c.branch(c.p&FlagC == 0)
	case 0x94: // STY dp,X
		c.stXDPX(c.y)
	case 0x96: // STX dp,Y
		c.stXDPY(c.x)
	case 0x98: // TYA
		c.io()
		if c.m8() {
			c.setA(c.y & 0x00FF)
		} else {
			c.setA(c.y)
		}
		c.setNZM(c.a)
	case 0x9A: // TXS
		c.io()
		if c.e {
			c.s = 0x0100 | (c.x & 0x00FF)
		} else {
			c.s = c.x
		}
	case 0x9B: // TXY
		c.io()
		c.setY(c.x)
		c.setNZX(c.y)
	case 0x9C: // STZ abs
		c.stAbs(0)
	case 0x9E: // STZ abs,X
		c.stAbsX(0)
	case 0xA3, 0xA7, 0xAF, 0xB3, 0xB7, 0xBF, 0xB2:
		c.aluExt(5, op&0x1F) // LDA extended modes

	// Row 0xA0
	case 0xA0: // LDY #
		c.immX(c.opLDY)
	case 0xA2: // LDX #
		c.immX(c.opLDX)
	case 0xA4: // LDY dp
		off := c.dpOff()
		c.opLDY(c.readXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0)))
	case 0xA5:
		// (LDA dp is in the cc=01 family.)
	case 0xA6: // LDX dp
		off := c.dpOff()
		c.opLDX(c.readXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0)))
	case 0xA8: // TAY
		c.io()
		c.setY(c.a)
		c.setNZX(c.y)
	case 0xAA: // TAX
		c.io()
		c.setX(c.a)
		c.setNZX(c.x)
	case 0xAB: // PLB
		c.io()
		c.dbr = c.pullB()
		c.setNZ8(c.dbr)
		c.io()
	case 0xAC: // LDY abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.opLDY(c.readXW(c.dbr, addr))
	case 0xAE: // LDX abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.opLDX(c.readXW(c.dbr, addr))
	case 0xB0: // BCS
		c.branch(c.p&FlagC != 0)
	case 0xB4: // LDY dp,X
		off := c.dpOff()
		c.io()
		c.opLDY(c.readXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, c.x, 0)))
	case 0xB6: // LDX dp,Y
		c.rdDPY(c.opLDX)
	case 0xB8: // CLV
		c.io()
		c.p &^= FlagV
	case 0xBA: // TSX
		c.io()
		if c.x8() {
			c.x = c.s & 0x00FF
		} else {
			c.x = c.s
		}
		c.setNZX(c.x)
	case 0xBB: // TYX
		c.io()
		c.setX(c.y)
		c.setNZX(c.x)
	case 0xBC: // LDY abs,X
		base := c.fetch16()
		c.rdIndexed(c.dbr, base, c.x, c.opLDY, c.readXW)
	case 0xBE: // LDX abs,Y
		base := c.fetch16()
		c.rdIndexed(c.dbr, base, c.y, c.opLDX, c.readXW)
	case 0xC3, 0xC7, 0xCF, 0xD3, 0xD7, 0xDF, 0xD2:
		c.aluExt(6, op&0x1F) // CMP extended modes

	// Row 0xC0
	case 0xC0: // CPY #
		c.immX(c.opCPY)
	case 0xC2: // REP #
		v := c.fetch()
		c.io()
		c.p &^= v
		// If REP widened the indexes, nothing is forced;
		// the stored high bytes simply count again.
	case 0xC4: // CPY dp
		off := c.dpOff()
		c.opCPY(c.readXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0)))
	case 0xC6: // DEC dp
		c.rmwDP(c.opDEC)
	case 0xC8: // INY
		c.io()
		c.setY(c.y + 1)
		c.setNZX(c.y)
	case 0xCA: // DEX
		c.io()
		c.setX(c.x - 1)
		c.setNZX(c.x)
	case 0xCB: // WAI
		// The single-step corpus models WAI as the fetch
		// plus three internal cycles (the last standing in
		// for the wait itself); the wait proper continues
		// one internal cycle per Step until a wake input.
		c.io()
		c.io()
		c.io()
		c.waiting = true
	case 0xCC: // CPY abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.opCPY(c.readXW(c.dbr, addr))
	case 0xCE: // DEC abs
		c.rmwAbs(c.opDEC)
	case 0xD0: // BNE
		c.branch(c.p&FlagZ == 0)
	case 0xD4: // PEI (dp)
		off := c.dpOff()
		ptr := c.dpPtr16Wrapped(off)
		c.push16(ptr)
	case 0xD6: // DEC dp,X
		c.rmwDPX(c.opDEC)
	case 0xD8: // CLD
		c.io()
		c.p &^= FlagD
	case 0xDA: // PHX
		c.io()
		if c.x8() {
			c.push(uint8(c.x))
		} else {
			c.push16(c.x)
		}
	case 0xDB: // STP: like WAI in the corpus's accounting,
		// the fetch plus three internal cycles.
		c.io()
		c.io()
		c.io()
		c.stopped = true
	case 0xDC: // JMP [abs]
		addr := c.fetch16()
		lo := c.read(0, addr)
		hi := c.read(0, addr+1)
		bk := c.read(0, addr+2)
		c.pbr = bk
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
	case 0xDE: // DEC abs,X
		c.rmwAbsX(c.opDEC)
	case 0xE3, 0xE7, 0xEF, 0xF3, 0xF7, 0xFF, 0xF2:
		c.aluExt(7, op&0x1F) // SBC extended modes

	// Row 0xE0
	case 0xE0: // CPX #
		c.immX(c.opCPX)
	case 0xE2: // SEP #
		v := c.fetch()
		c.io()
		c.p |= v
		if c.x8() {
			c.x &= 0x00FF
			c.y &= 0x00FF
		}
	case 0xE4: // CPX dp
		off := c.dpOff()
		c.opCPX(c.readXW(0, c.dpAddrEx(off, 0, 0)))
	case 0xE6: // INC dp
		c.rmwDP(c.opINC)
	case 0xE8: // INX
		c.io()
		c.setX(c.x + 1)
		c.setNZX(c.x)
	case 0xEA: // NOP
		c.io()
	case 0xEB: // XBA
		c.io()
		c.io()
		c.a = (c.a << 8) | (c.a >> 8)
		c.setNZ8(uint8(c.a))
	case 0xEC: // CPX abs
		addr := c.fetch16()
		c.opCPX(c.readXW(c.dbr, addr))
	case 0xEE: // INC abs
		c.rmwAbs(c.opINC)
	case 0xF0: // BEQ
		c.branch(c.p&FlagZ != 0)
	case 0xF4: // PEA
		v := c.fetch16()
		c.push16(v)
	case 0xF6: // INC dp,X
		c.rmwDPX(c.opINC)
	case 0xF8: // SED
		c.io()
		c.p |= FlagD
	case 0xFA: // PLX
		c.io()
		if c.x8() {
			c.setX(uint16(c.pullB()))
		} else {
			c.setX(c.pull16())
		}
		c.setNZX(c.x)
		c.io()
	case 0xFB: // XCE
		c.io()
		carry := c.p&FlagC != 0
		if c.e {
			c.p |= FlagC
		} else {
			c.p &^= FlagC
		}
		c.e = carry
		if c.e {
			c.s = 0x0100 | (c.s & 0x00FF)
			c.x &= 0x00FF
			c.y &= 0x00FF
		}
	case 0xFC: // JSR (abs,X): low operand byte, the return
		// address push (the high operand byte's address),
		// high operand byte, an internal cycle, then the
		// target pointer from the program bank; 8 cycles in
		// all per the corpus trace.
		lo := c.fetch()
		if c.e {
			// Emulation JSR pushes use the page-1 form on
			// every access, like JSR absolute's.
			c.pushInt(uint8(c.pc >> 8))
			c.pushInt(uint8(c.pc))
		} else {
			c.push16(c.pc) // PC points at the high operand byte
		}
		hi := c.fetch()
		c.io()
		ptr := uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		sum := ptr + c.x
		tlo := c.read(c.pbr, sum)
		thi := c.read(c.pbr, sum+1)
		c.pc = uint16(thi)<<8 | uint16(tlo)
	case 0xFE: // INC abs,X
		c.rmwAbsX(c.opINC)

	default:
		// The remaining opcodes belong to the cc=01 family
		// (handled above) or the extended-mode groups
		// dispatched in this switch. Anything reaching here
		// is a one-byte NOP in this table (0xA5 is LDA dp,
		// reached via the family decoder; it is listed in
		// the switch only to keep the map complete).
		c.io()
	}
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/w65c816/w65c816.go ====================

// Package w65c816 is an original implementation of the
// Western Design Center W65C816S CPU, written from the
// published datasheet and the programming documentation
// collected for the chip (Eyes and Lichty's "Programming the
// 65816" and the SNES development documentation that restates
// the datasheet's cycle tables).
//
// The 65816 is a 16-bit extension of the 6502: a 16-bit
// accumulator whose high byte is separately addressable, 16-bit
// index registers, a 24-bit address space split into a program
// bank and a data bank, a relocatable direct page, a 16-bit
// stack in native mode, and two processor widths (the M and X
// status flags) that most instructions obey. It powers on in
// emulation mode, where it behaves like a 6502 with its stack
// confined to page 1 and its widths forced to 8 bits, until
// software swaps the carry and emulation flags with XCE.
//
// Cycle counting mirrors the go-nes 6502 in this repository:
// every bus access the CPU makes takes exactly one cycle, in
// the documented order (including the dummy reads indexed
// modes perform), and internal cycles are charged where the
// datasheet's tables show them, so a machine hanging devices
// off the bus observes accesses in the hardware's order and
// count. Because SNES memory timing depends on what is being
// accessed, the bus also reports an access speed per address;
// the CPU accumulates both bus cycles (Cycles) and master
// clock cycles (MasterCycles) so DMA and HDMA engines in the
// system package can interleave against real time later.
//
// Interrupts poll the way the hardware polls them: the lines
// are sampled before every cycle the CPU spends, and the
// sample taken before an instruction's last cycle is the
// decision the next Step acts on. NMI is an edge latch with
// priority over the level-triggered IRQ, and a latched NMI
// hijacks a BRK or IRQ sequence at its vector fetch, as on
// the 6502. ABORT is exposed at the documented level this
// core promises: the line is sampled like IRQ, and when it
// is recognized the CPU takes the abort vector at the
// next instruction boundary, pushing the address of the
// instruction that was about to execute, rather than
// modeling the chip's cycle-by-cycle partial register
// state mid-instruction. The SNES never asserts
// ABORT (the pin is tied inactive on the console), so the
// approximation costs nothing there.
//
// Block moves (MVN and MVP) are interruptible the way the
// hardware makes them: each byte moves in a seven-cycle
// iteration that re-fetches the instruction, the CPU polls
// between bytes, and when an interrupt is recognized the
// move suspends with its progress in A, X, and Y exactly as
// the hardware leaves them and PC on the move's own opcode,
// the interrupt is taken, and the re-executed move
// continues after the handler returns. No move state lives
// outside the programmer-visible registers.
package w65c816

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Speed is the access speed a bus reports for an address. On
// the SNES the same bus cycle lasts 6, 8, or 12 master clocks
// depending on the region accessed; the bare CPU does not
// care, but the console's DMA timing does, so the CPU tracks
// the weighted total alongside the plain cycle count.
type Speed uint8

const (
	// SpeedFast accesses complete in 6 master clocks (FastROM
	// in the high banks, and the CPU's internal cycles).
	SpeedFast Speed = iota
	// SpeedSlow accesses complete in 8 master clocks (Work
	// RAM, most ROM, most cartridge space).
	SpeedSlow
	// SpeedXSlow accesses complete in 12 master clocks (the
	// console's IO and controller region).
	SpeedXSlow
)

// MasterCycles returns how many master clocks an access at
// this speed occupies on the SNES.
func (s Speed) MasterCycles() uint64 {
	switch s {
	case SpeedFast:
		return 6
	case SpeedSlow:
		return 8
	case SpeedXSlow:
		return 12
	}
	return 8
}

// internalMasterCycles is the master-clock cost of a cycle
// the CPU spends internally.
const internalMasterCycles = 6

// Bus is the machine interface the CPU drives. Addresses are
// presented as a bank and a 16-bit offset, exactly as the
// chip's pins separate them. Every Read or Write is one bus
// cycle.
type Bus interface {
	Read(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint8
	Write(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8)
	// Speed reports the access speed of an address. The CPU
	// asks once per access, before performing it.
	Speed(bank uint8, addr uint16) Speed
}

// speedBus is the optional bus extension for fused access:
// the speed query and the transfer in one call. The speed
// a fused call reports is the one the separate Speed call
// would have returned before the access, so cycle
// accounting is identical; the fusion only removes one
// interface call from the hottest path in the machine.
// Attach detects the extension once, so buses that do not
// implement it pay nothing.
type speedBus interface {
	ReadSpeed(bank uint8, addr uint16) (uint8, Speed)
	WriteSpeed(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8) Speed
}

// Status register bit masks. Unlike the 6502, every bit of
// the 65816 status register is real storage: bit 5 is the M
// flag (accumulator and memory width) and bit 4 is the X flag
// (index width). In emulation mode the M and X flags are
// forced to 1 in effect whatever the stored bits say, and an
// interrupt or PHP push presents bit 4 as the 6502's B flag
// instead; see statusByte.
const (
	FlagC = 0x01 // carry
	FlagZ = 0x02 // zero
	FlagI = 0x04 // interrupt disable
	FlagD = 0x08 // decimal mode
	FlagX = 0x10 // index register width (1 = 8 bit)
	FlagM = 0x20 // accumulator/memory width (1 = 8 bit)
	FlagV = 0x40 // overflow
	FlagN = 0x80 // negative
)

// Vector addresses (all in bank 0).
const (
	vecNativeCOP   = 0xFFE4
	vecNativeBRK   = 0xFFE6
	vecNativeAbort = 0xFFE8
	vecNativeNMI   = 0xFFEA
	vecNativeIRQ   = 0xFFEE

	vecEmuCOP   = 0xFFF4
	vecEmuAbort = 0xFFF8
	vecEmuNMI   = 0xFFFA
	vecReset    = 0xFFFC
	vecEmuIRQ   = 0xFFFE // shared by IRQ and BRK in emulation mode
)

// SerializeSize is the fixed save-state size in bytes.
const SerializeSize = 96

const serializeVersion = 1

// Registers is a snapshot of the programmer-visible CPU
// state. A is the full 16-bit accumulator (the datasheet's
// C), with A>>8 the B accumulator. P is the stored status
// byte; in emulation mode its M and X bits are stored but
// inert (the effective widths are 8 bit).
type Registers struct {
	A, X, Y, S, D uint16
	PC            uint16
	DBR, PBR      uint8
	P             uint8
	E             bool
}

// CPU is a single W65C816S instance.
type CPU struct {
	bus Bus

	// fastBus is bus viewed through the optional speedBus
	// extension, captured at Attach; nil when the bus does
	// not implement it.
	fastBus speedBus

	a, x, y, s, d uint16
	pc            uint16
	dbr, pbr      uint8
	p             uint8
	e             bool

	cycles uint64 // bus cycles since power-on
	master uint64 // master clocks since power-on

	nmiLine    bool
	nmiPending bool
	irqLine    bool
	abortLine  bool

	waiting bool // WAI executed, awaiting an interrupt input
	stopped bool // STP executed; only Reset recovers

	// Interrupt poll state: samples refresh before every
	// cycle, and the takes are the decision latched at the
	// end of each Step.
	smpNMI, smpIRQ, smpAbort bool
	takeNMI, takeIRQ         bool
	takeAbort                bool
	abortPC                  uint16 // PC of the instruction ABORT preempts
	abortPBR                 uint8

	// The most recent block move's shape, kept for state
	// inspection: a suspended move needs nothing else,
	// since its progress lives in A, X, Y, and PC.
	mvOp       uint8
	mvSrcBank  uint8
	mvDstBank  uint8
	mvOpcodePC uint16

	// budget, when positive, is a hard cycle stop used by
	// test harnesses: charge panics with budgetExhausted
	// once the cycle counter reaches it, which lets a
	// harness cut an execution at an exact cycle (the
	// single-step corpus truncates block-move traces at
	// 100 cycles, mid-iteration). Production code never
	// sets it.
	budget uint64
}

// New returns a CPU in its power-on state: emulation mode,
// registers zeroed. Call Reset (with a bus attached) to run
// the reset sequence.
func New() *CPU {
	return &CPU{e: true}
}

// Attach wires the CPU to a bus.
func (c *CPU) Attach(bus Bus) {
	c.bus = bus
	c.fastBus, _ = bus.(speedBus)
}

// Reset runs the hardware reset sequence: emulation mode is
// forced, the M, X, I, and D flags take their reset values,
// the direct page and both banks clear, the stack pointer is
// loaded with 0x01FF, and the program counter loads from the
// reset vector. Seven cycles pass: five internal and the two
// vector fetches.
func (c *CPU) Reset() {
	c.e = true
	c.p = FlagM | FlagX | FlagI // M, X set; D, C, Z, V, N clear
	c.d = 0
	c.dbr = 0
	c.pbr = 0
	c.s = 0x01FF
	c.nmiPending = false
	c.waiting = false
	c.stopped = false
	c.smpNMI, c.smpIRQ, c.smpAbort = false, false, false
	c.takeNMI, c.takeIRQ, c.takeAbort = false, false, false
	for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {
		c.io()
	}
	lo := c.read(0, vecReset)
	hi := c.read(0, vecReset+1)
	c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// Regs returns a snapshot of the programmer-visible state.
// In emulation mode the exported stack pointer always
// shows 0x0100|(low byte), and the status register always
// shows the M and X bits set, as the hardware presents
// them and the corpus records them, whatever the internal
// storage currently holds.
func (c *CPU) Regs() Registers {
	s, p := c.s, c.p
	if c.e {
		s = 0x0100 | (c.s & 0x00FF)
		p = c.p | FlagM | FlagX
	}
	return Registers{
		A: c.a, X: c.x, Y: c.y, S: s, D: c.d, PC: c.pc,
		DBR: c.dbr, PBR: c.pbr, P: p, E: c.e,
	}
}

// SetRegs installs a register snapshot. The single-step
// conformance runner uses it to place the CPU in corpus
// states; in emulation mode the stack pointer is folded
// to 0x0100|(low byte), the form the corpus's counter
// starts from (see stackAddr), since corpus initial
// states carry random junk in the stored high byte.
func (c *CPU) SetRegs(r Registers) {
	c.a, c.x, c.y, c.s, c.d = r.A, r.X, r.Y, r.S, r.D
	c.pc = r.PC
	c.dbr, c.pbr = r.DBR, r.PBR
	c.p = r.P
	c.e = r.E
	if c.e {
		c.s = 0x0100 | (c.s & 0x00FF)
	}
	c.waiting = false
	c.stopped = false
	c.takeNMI, c.takeIRQ, c.takeAbort = false, false, false
	c.smpNMI, c.smpIRQ, c.smpAbort = false, false, false
	c.nmiPending = false
}

// PC returns the current program counter (within PBR).
func (c *CPU) PC() uint32 { return uint32(c.pbr)<<16 | uint32(c.pc) }

// Cycles returns the bus cycles executed since power-on,
// including reset, internal, and stall cycles.
func (c *CPU) Cycles() uint64 { return c.cycles }

// MasterCycles returns the master clocks those cycles
// occupy at the access speeds the bus reported.
func (c *CPU) MasterCycles() uint64 { return c.master }

// SetNMILine drives the NMI pin. The input is edge
// triggered: a low-to-high transition latches a pending NMI.
func (c *CPU) SetNMILine(high bool) {
	if high && !c.nmiLine {
		c.nmiPending = true
	}
	c.nmiLine = high
}

// SetIRQLine drives the IRQ pin, level triggered and masked
// by the I flag at the poll point.
func (c *CPU) SetIRQLine(asserted bool) { c.irqLine = asserted }

// SetAbortLine drives the ABORT pin, level triggered and
// not masked by any flag.
