func (c *CPU) SetAbortLine(asserted bool) { c.abortLine = asserted }

// NMIPending reports whether an NMI edge is latched.
func (c *CPU) NMIPending() bool { return c.nmiPending }

// Waiting reports whether the CPU sits in WAI.
func (c *CPU) Waiting() bool { return c.waiting }

// Stopped reports whether STP has halted the CPU.
func (c *CPU) Stopped() bool { return c.stopped }

// m8 reports the effective accumulator/memory width:
// forced 8 bit in emulation mode.
func (c *CPU) m8() bool { return c.e || c.p&FlagM != 0 }

// x8 reports the effective index width.
func (c *CPU) x8() bool { return c.e || c.p&FlagX != 0 }

// sampleInterrupts records the interrupt lines as they stand
// before a cycle is spent.
func (c *CPU) sampleInterrupts() {
	if !c.nmiPending && !c.irqLine && !c.abortLine {
		// The quiet fast path: no line is active and
		// no NMI is latched, so the sample is all
		// clear. This still runs at every access, so
		// a pulse spanning any access is seen by the
		// full path below.
		c.smpNMI = false
		c.smpIRQ = false
		c.smpAbort = false
		return
	}
	c.smpNMI = c.nmiPending
	c.smpIRQ = c.irqLine && c.p&FlagI == 0
	c.smpAbort = c.abortLine
}

// budgetExhausted is the panic charge raises when a test
// harness cycle budget runs out; see the budget field.
type budgetExhausted struct{}

// SetCycleBudget arms the hard cycle stop described on the
// budget field, as an absolute cycle count (the value of
// Cycles at which to stop); zero disarms it. Harness use
// only.
func (c *CPU) SetCycleBudget(cycles uint64) { c.budget = cycles }

// latchPoll moves the latest samples into the decisions the
// next Step acts on.
func (c *CPU) latchPoll() {
	c.takeNMI = c.smpNMI
	c.takeIRQ = c.smpIRQ
	if c.smpAbort && !c.takeAbort {
		// The abort is recognized at the boundary: the
		// return address pushed is the instruction that has
		// not executed yet (see the package comment).
		c.takeAbort = true
		c.abortPC = c.pc
		c.abortPBR = c.pbr
	}
}

// charge accounts for one bus cycle at a master-clock cost.
func (c *CPU) charge(master uint64) {
	c.cycles++
	c.master += master
	if c.budget > 0 && c.cycles >= c.budget {
		panic(budgetExhausted{})
	}
}

// read performs one bus read and charges one cycle at the
// speed the bus reports for the address.
func (c *CPU) read(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint8 {
	c.sampleInterrupts()
	if c.fastBus != nil {
		v, sp := c.fastBus.ReadSpeed(bank, addr)
		c.charge(sp.MasterCycles())
		return v
	}
	sp := c.bus.Speed(bank, addr)
	v := c.bus.Read(bank, addr)
	c.charge(sp.MasterCycles())
	return v
}

// write performs one bus write and charges one cycle.
func (c *CPU) write(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	c.sampleInterrupts()
	if c.fastBus != nil {
		sp := c.fastBus.WriteSpeed(bank, addr, val)
		c.charge(sp.MasterCycles())
		return
	}
	sp := c.bus.Speed(bank, addr)
	c.bus.Write(bank, addr, val)
	c.charge(sp.MasterCycles())
}

// read24 reads at a full 24-bit address.
func (c *CPU) read24(addr uint32) uint8 {
	return c.read(uint8(addr>>16), uint16(addr))
}

// write24 writes at a full 24-bit address.
func (c *CPU) write24(addr uint32, val uint8) {
	c.write(uint8(addr>>16), uint16(addr), val)
}

// io charges one internal cycle: no bus access, 6 master
// clocks, interrupts still sampled (the hardware polls
// during internal cycles too).
func (c *CPU) io() {
	c.sampleInterrupts()
	c.charge(internalMasterCycles)
}

// dummy charges one bus cycle at the given address
// without transferring data: the dead cycles the hardware
// spends driving a partially fixed address while an index
// addition completes (indexed reads on a page cross,
// indexed stores, read-modify-write fixups). The
// single-step corpus records these cycles with no
// valid-access pins set, so this core makes no bus access
// for them either; the cycle still costs the target
// address's access speed.
func (c *CPU) dummy(bank uint8, addr uint16) {
	c.sampleInterrupts()
	c.charge(c.bus.Speed(bank, addr).MasterCycles())
}

// dummyWriter is the optional bus extension for the
// write half of a read-modify-write pair: hardware drives
// the original value onto the bus in a cycle the
// single-step corpus records as not valid, before the
// modified value's real write. A bus that implements it
// performs the write without counting it as a data
// transfer; other buses get a plain write.
type dummyWriter interface {
	WriteDummy(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8)
}

// writeDummy writes through the dummy channel (see
// dummyWriter), charging one cycle at the address's
// speed.
func (c *CPU) writeDummy(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	if dw, ok := c.bus.(dummyWriter); ok {
		c.sampleInterrupts()
		dw.WriteDummy(bank, addr, val)
		c.charge(c.bus.Speed(bank, addr).MasterCycles())
		return
	}
	c.write(bank, addr, val)
}

// fetch reads the byte at PBR:PC and advances PC within its
// bank. The advance happens before the read's cycle is
// charged, so a harness cycle budget cutting the execution
// inside this fetch leaves PC past the byte, the position
// the corpus's truncated states show.
func (c *CPU) fetch() uint8 {
	addr := c.pc
	c.pc++
	return c.read(c.pbr, addr)
}

// fetch16 fetches a little-endian 16-bit operand.
func (c *CPU) fetch16() uint16 {
	lo := c.fetch()
	hi := c.fetch()
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// stackAddr is the bank-0 address the stack currently
// occupies.
//
// In emulation mode the single-step corpus's stack model
// is unusual, and this core follows it exactly: the
// pointer is a plain counter that is folded to
// 0x0100|(low byte) whenever a register snapshot is
// installed or emulation is entered, and then increments
// and decrements without masking. A push sequence that
// underflows 0x0100 continues into page 0 (a PHD from a
// low byte of 0x00 writes at 0x0100 then 0x00FF); a pull
// sequence crossing 0x01FF reads on into 0x0200 (a PLD
// from a low byte of 0xFE reads at 0x01FF then 0x0200).
// The exported S always reads 0x0100|(low byte). The
// datasheet describes the emulation stack as confined to
// page 1; the corpus is the gate for this core. In
// practice the difference needs a stack crossing the
// page 1 boundary in emulation mode, which real software
// never does. Interrupt entry pushes are the exception:
// they address the stack through the page-1 form on every
// access (see pushInt).
func (c *CPU) stackAddr() uint16 {
	return c.s
}

// decS moves the stack pointer down after a push.
func (c *CPU) decS() { c.s-- }

// incS moves the stack pointer up before a pull.
func (c *CPU) incS() { c.s++ }

// push writes a byte to the stack and decrements S.
func (c *CPU) push(v uint8) {
	c.write(0, c.stackAddr(), v)
	c.decS()
}

// push16 pushes a 16-bit value, high byte first.
func (c *CPU) push16(v uint16) {
	c.push(uint8(v >> 8))
	c.push(uint8(v))
}

// pushInt pushes a byte as part of an interrupt entry
// sequence. In emulation mode the corpus's interrupt
// microprogram addresses the stack with the pointer's
// high byte pinned to page 1 on every access (a push
// sequence crossing 0x0100 wraps to 0x01FF), where
// ordinary instruction pushes follow the nine-bit counter
// of stackAddr. Native mode is identical to push.
func (c *CPU) pushInt(v uint8) {
	if c.e {
		c.write(0, 0x0100|(c.s&0x00FF), v)
		c.s = 0x0100 | ((c.s - 1) & 0x00FF)
		return
	}
	c.push(v)
}

// pull increments S and reads the byte it lands on.
func (c *CPU) pull() uint8 {
	c.incS()
	return c.read(0, c.stackAddr())
}

// pullB pulls one byte the way the corpus's single-byte
// pull instructions (PLA, PLP, PLX, PLY) and the RTS/RTI
// sequences do in emulation mode: the increment wraps
// inside page 1 (0x01FF up to 0x0100). The 16-bit pulls
// (PLD, RTL) use plain pull and pull16 instead; the
// corpus traces pin the split down exactly.
func (c *CPU) pullB() uint8 {
	if c.e {
		c.s = 0x0100 | ((c.s + 1) & 0x00FF)
		return c.read(0, c.s)
	}
	return c.pull()
}

// pull16 pulls a 16-bit value, low byte first.
func (c *CPU) pull16() uint16 {
	lo := c.pull()
	hi := c.pull()
	return uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// statusByte renders P for a stack push. In native mode the
// stored byte goes out as it is. In emulation mode the push
// follows the 6502 convention: bit 5 reads 1 and bit 4 is
// the B flag, set for PHP and BRK, clear for IRQ and NMI.
func (c *CPU) statusByte(brk bool) uint8 {
	if !c.e {
		return c.p
	}
	p := c.p | FlagM // bit 5 (the M position) reads 1
	if brk {
		p |= FlagX // bit 4 position carries B in emulation pushes
	} else {
		p &^= FlagX
	}
	return p
}

// setP installs a pulled status byte. If the X flag is now
// set (8-bit index), the index registers' high bytes clear,
// as the hardware clears them whenever 8-bit index width is
// in force.
func (c *CPU) setP(v uint8) {
	c.p = v
	if c.x8() {
		c.x &= 0x00FF
		c.y &= 0x00FF
	}
}

// Step executes one instruction, one interrupt sequence,
// one block-move resumption, or one idle cycle (WAI/STP),
// and returns the bus cycles it consumed.
func (c *CPU) Step() int {
	start := c.cycles
	if c.stopped {
		c.io()
		c.latchPoll()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	if c.waiting {
		c.io()
		// WAI ends when an interrupt input is active, even
		// one the I flag masks; a masked IRQ just wakes the
		// CPU, an unmasked one (or an NMI) is then taken
		// through the ordinary poll decisions.
		if c.nmiPending || c.irqLine {
			c.waiting = false
		}
		c.latchPoll()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	if c.takeAbort {
		c.takeAbort = false
		c.hardwareInterrupt(c.interruptVector(true, false), true, false)
		c.latchPoll()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	if c.takeNMI {
		c.takeNMI = false
		c.nmiPending = false
		c.hardwareInterrupt(c.interruptVector(false, true), false, false)
		c.latchPoll()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	if c.takeIRQ {
		c.takeIRQ = false
		c.hardwareInterrupt(c.interruptVector(false, false), false, true)
		c.latchPoll()
		return int(c.cycles - start)
	}
	op := c.fetch()
	c.exec(op)
	c.latchPoll()
	return int(c.cycles - start)
}

// hardwareInterrupt runs the NMI, IRQ, or ABORT sequence
// to the given vector. Native mode pushes PBR, PC, and P
// and reads the native vectors (8 cycles); emulation mode
// pushes PC and a B-clear P and reads the emulation vectors
// (7 cycles). When irq is true an NMI latched after the
// sequence began hijacks the entry to the NMI vector, as
// the hardware does for IRQ (and BRK) entries.
func (c *CPU) hardwareInterrupt(vec uint16, abort, irq bool) {
	c.io()
	c.io()
	if c.e {
		ret := c.pc
		if abort {
			ret = c.abortPC
		}
		c.pushInt(uint8(ret >> 8))
		c.pushInt(uint8(ret))
		c.pushInt(c.statusByte(false))
	} else {
		ret, retBank := c.pc, c.pbr
		if abort {
			ret, retBank = c.abortPC, c.abortPBR
		}
		c.pushInt(retBank)
		c.pushInt(uint8(ret >> 8))
		c.pushInt(uint8(ret))
		c.pushInt(c.p)
	}
	c.p |= FlagI
	c.p &^= FlagD
	if irq && c.nmiPending {
		c.nmiPending = false
		vec = c.interruptVector(false, true)
	}
	lo := c.read(0, vec)
	hi := c.read(0, vec+1)
	c.pbr = 0
	c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// interruptVector picks a vector address. nmi selects the
// NMI vector over the IRQ one; abort selects ABORT over
// both.
func (c *CPU) interruptVector(abort, nmi bool) uint16 {
	if c.e {
		switch {
		case abort:
			return vecEmuAbort
		case nmi:
			return vecEmuNMI
		default:
			return vecEmuIRQ
		}
	}
	switch {
	case abort:
		return vecNativeAbort
	case nmi:
		return vecNativeNMI
	default:
		return vecNativeIRQ
	}
}

// softwareInterrupt runs BRK and COP: the program counter
// skips the signature byte that follows the opcode, then
// the sequence is the hardware one with a B-set status in
// emulation mode and the BRK or COP vector.
func (c *CPU) softwareInterrupt(cop bool) {
	c.fetch() // the signature byte is read and skipped
	if c.e {
		vec := uint16(vecEmuIRQ)
		if cop {
			vec = vecEmuCOP
		}
		c.pushInt(uint8(c.pc >> 8))
		c.pushInt(uint8(c.pc))
		c.pushInt(c.statusByte(true))
		c.p |= FlagI
		c.p &^= FlagD
		if c.nmiPending {
			c.nmiPending = false
			vec = vecEmuNMI
		}
		lo := c.read(0, vec)
		hi := c.read(0, vec+1)
		c.pbr = 0
		c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
		return
	}
	vec := uint16(vecNativeBRK)
	if cop {
		vec = vecNativeCOP
	}
	c.pushInt(c.pbr)
	c.pushInt(uint8(c.pc >> 8))
	c.pushInt(uint8(c.pc))
	c.pushInt(c.p)
	c.p |= FlagI
	c.p &^= FlagD
	if c.nmiPending {
		c.nmiPending = false
		vec = vecNativeNMI
	}
	lo := c.read(0, vec)
	hi := c.read(0, vec+1)
	c.pbr = 0
	c.pc = uint16(hi)<<8 | uint16(lo)
}

// Serialize writes the CPU state in this package's fixed
// layout.
func (c *CPU) Serialize() []byte {
	out := make([]byte, SerializeSize)
	out[0] = serializeVersion
	put := func(off int, v uint16) { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[off:], v) }
	put(1, c.a)
	put(3, c.x)
	put(5, c.y)
	put(7, c.s)
	put(9, c.d)
	put(11, c.pc)
	out[13] = c.dbr
	out[14] = c.pbr
	out[15] = c.p
	if c.e {
		out[16] = 1
	}
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(out[17:], c.cycles)
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(out[25:], c.master)
	var lines uint8
	if c.nmiLine {
		lines |= 1
	}
	if c.nmiPending {
		lines |= 2
	}
	if c.irqLine {
		lines |= 4
	}
	if c.abortLine {
		lines |= 8
	}
	if c.waiting {
		lines |= 16
	}
	if c.stopped {
		lines |= 32
	}
	out[33] = lines
	var poll uint8
	if c.smpNMI {
		poll |= 1
	}
	if c.smpIRQ {
		poll |= 2
	}
	if c.smpAbort {
		poll |= 4
	}
	if c.takeNMI {
		poll |= 8
	}
	if c.takeIRQ {
		poll |= 16
	}
	if c.takeAbort {
		poll |= 32
	}
	out[34] = poll
	put(35, c.abortPC)
	out[37] = c.abortPBR
	out[38] = c.mvOp
	out[39] = c.mvSrcBank
	out[40] = c.mvDstBank
	// out[41] is reserved (a removed in-flight flag); the
	// layout does not change within a state version.
	put(42, c.mvOpcodePC)
	return out
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (c *CPU) Deserialize(in []byte) error {
	if len(in) != SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("w65c816: bad state size")
	}
	if in[0] != serializeVersion {
		return errors.New("w65c816: unsupported state version")
	}
	get := func(off int) uint16 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(in[off:]) }
	c.a, c.x, c.y, c.s, c.d = get(1), get(3), get(5), get(7), get(9)
	c.pc = get(11)
	c.dbr, c.pbr = in[13], in[14]
	c.p = in[15]
	c.e = in[16] != 0
	c.cycles = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(in[17:])
	c.master = binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(in[25:])
	lines := in[33]
	c.nmiLine = lines&1 != 0
	c.nmiPending = lines&2 != 0
	c.irqLine = lines&4 != 0
	c.abortLine = lines&8 != 0
	c.waiting = lines&16 != 0
	c.stopped = lines&32 != 0
	poll := in[34]
	c.smpNMI = poll&1 != 0
	c.smpIRQ = poll&2 != 0
	c.smpAbort = poll&4 != 0
	c.takeNMI = poll&8 != 0
	c.takeIRQ = poll&16 != 0
	c.takeAbort = poll&32 != 0
	c.abortPC = get(35)
	c.abortPBR = in[37]
	c.mvOp, c.mvSrcBank, c.mvDstBank = in[38], in[39], in[40]
	c.mvOpcodePC = get(42)
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/chips/w65c816/w65c816_test.go ====================

package w65c816

import "testing"

// ramBus is a flat 16 MB test bus, uniform slow, that
// records nothing: the unit tests inspect memory directly.
type ramBus struct {
	mem []byte
}

func newRAMBus() *ramBus { return &ramBus{mem: make([]byte, 1<<24)} }

func (b *ramBus) Read(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint8 {
	return b.mem[uint32(bank)<<16|uint32(addr)]
}

func (b *ramBus) Write(bank uint8, addr uint16, val uint8) {
	b.mem[uint32(bank)<<16|uint32(addr)] = val
}

func (b *ramBus) Speed(uint8, uint16) Speed { return SpeedSlow }

func (b *ramBus) at(bank uint8, addr uint16) uint8 { return b.Read(bank, addr) }
func (b *ramBus) put(bank uint8, addr uint16, v uint8) {
	b.mem[uint32(bank)<<16|uint32(addr)] = v
}

// newTestCPU returns a CPU attached to a fresh RAM bus,
// placed in the given state with code at PBR:PC.
func newTestCPU(regs Registers, code ...byte) (*CPU, *ramBus) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	cpu := New()
	cpu.Attach(bus)
	cpu.SetRegs(regs)
	for i, v := range code {
		bus.put(regs.PBR, regs.PC+uint16(i), v)
	}
	return cpu, bus
}

// native returns baseline native-mode registers: 16-bit
// accumulator and indexes, D=0, DBR=0, stack at 0x01FF,
// code at 00:8000.
func native() Registers {
	return Registers{S: 0x01FF, PC: 0x8000, P: 0x00, E: false}
}

// emu returns baseline emulation-mode registers.
func emu() Registers {
	return Registers{S: 0x01FF, PC: 0x8000, P: FlagM | FlagX, E: true}
}

func TestXCEClampsIndexHighBytes(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	r.X, r.Y = 0x1234, 0xABCD
	r.P = FlagC                   // carry set: XCE swaps it into E
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xFB) // XCE
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if !got.E {
		t.Fatalf("E = false after XCE with carry set")
	}
	if got.X != 0x0034 || got.Y != 0x00CD {
		t.Errorf("X,Y = %#x,%#x, want 0x34, 0xCD (high bytes clamped)", got.X, got.Y)
	}
	if got.P&FlagC != 0 {
		t.Errorf("C still set after XCE swapped in the old E (0)")
	}
	if got.S != 0x01FF {
		t.Errorf("S = %#x, want 0x01FF (already page 1)", got.S)
	}
}

func TestXCERoundTripRestoresWidths(t *testing.T) {
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(emu(), 0xFB, 0xFB) // XCE, XCE
	// Start: E=1, C=0. First XCE: E<-0, C<-1. Second: E<-1, C<-0.
	cpu.Step()
	if cpu.Regs().E {
		t.Fatalf("first XCE should leave emulation")
	}
	cpu.Step()
	if !cpu.Regs().E {
		t.Fatalf("second XCE should re-enter emulation")
	}
}

func TestSEPWidthTransitionPreservesB(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	r.A = 0xBEEF
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xE2, 0x20, 0xA9, 0x42, 0xEA) // SEP #$20; LDA #$42; NOP
	cpu.Step()                                            // SEP: M set
	cpu.Step()                                            // LDA #$42 (8-bit)
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.A != 0xBE42 {
		t.Errorf("A = %#x, want 0xBE42 (B accumulator preserved)", got.A)
	}
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(native(), 0xC2, 0x20) // REP #$20 from M=0: no-op on width
	cpu2.Step()
	if cpu2.Regs().P&FlagM != 0 {
		t.Errorf("REP set M")
	}
}

func TestDirectPageWrapEmulationVsNative(t *testing.T) {
	// LDA $FF with D=0x1200: emulation wraps the pointer
	// arithmetic in the page; native reads D+0xFF linear.
	code := []byte{0xA5, 0xFF} // LDA dp $FF
	r := emu()
	r.D = 0x1200
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, code...)
	bus.put(0, 0x12FF, 0x11) // linear target
	bus.put(0, 0x1200+0xFF, 0x11)
	bus.put(0, 0x12FF, 0x11)
	// Emu wrap: address = (D & 0xFF00) | (0x00 + 0xFF) = 0x12FF
	// (DL=0, so it coincides here); the distinguishing case
	// is the pointer high byte of (dp) at offset 0xFF, see
	// the indirect test below.
	cpu.Step()
	if cpu.Regs().A != 0x11 {
		t.Errorf("emu LDA dp: A = %#x", cpu.Regs().A)
	}
	// Native with D=0x12FF, LDA $02: reads 0x1301.
	r2 := native()
	r2.D = 0x12FF
	cpu2, bus2 := newTestCPU(r2, 0xA5, 0x02)
	bus2.put(0, 0x1301, 0x77)
	bus2.put(0, 0x1201, 0x66) // page-wrapped decoy
	cpu2.Step()
	if cpu2.Regs().A != 0x77 {
		t.Errorf("native LDA dp: A = %#x, want 0x77 (no wrap)", cpu2.Regs().A)
	}
}

func TestDPIndirectPointerSecondByteIncrements(t *testing.T) {
	// LDA ($FF) with D=0x1200 in emulation: the base
	// addition wraps in the page (the pointer low byte is
	// at 0x12FF), but the pointer's high byte is fetched
	// from the next address up, 0x1300, with a plain
	// increment. The single-step corpus's (dp,X) boundary
	// traces show the second byte always at base+1.
	r := emu()
	r.D = 0x1200
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0xB2, 0xFF) // LDA (dp) $FF
	bus.put(0, 0x12FF, 0x34)              // pointer low
	bus.put(0, 0x1300, 0x12)              // pointer high at base+1
	bus.put(0, 0x1200, 0x99)              // page-wrap decoy
	bus.put(0, 0x1234, 0x5C)              // the data
	cpu.Step()
	if cpu.Regs().A != 0x5C {
		t.Errorf("A = %#x, want 0x5C", cpu.Regs().A)
	}
}

func TestPHBPLBAndDBRWraps(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	r.DBR = 0x42
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r,
		0x8B,       // PHB
		0xA9, 0x99, // LDA #$99 (M=0: two bytes follow)
		0x00, // operand high byte of LDA (0x9900 & ...)
		0xAB, // PLB (pulls back 0x42 after we trash DBR)
	)
	_ = bus
	// Simpler direct sequence: PHB; LDA #imm16 (0x0099); PLB
	// would pull the wrong byte if the immediate is consumed
	// wrong. Instead verify with a hand-driven stack:
	cpu.Step() // PHB pushes 0x42
	if got := bus.at(0, 0x01FF); got != 0x42 {
		t.Fatalf("stack top = %#x, want 0x42", got)
	}
	cpu.SetRegs(Registers{S: 0x01FE, PC: 0x8004, DBR: 0x00, P: 0, E: false})
	// PC 0x8004 is the PLB in the stream above only if stream
	// laid out so; this state drives PLB directly:
	bus.put(0, 0x8004, 0xAB)
	cpu.Step()
	if cpu.Regs().DBR != 0x42 {
		t.Errorf("DBR = %#x, want 0x42", cpu.Regs().DBR)
	}
}

func TestJMPLongAndJSRReturn(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r,
		0x22, 0x00, 0x90, 0x05, // JSL $05:9000
	)
	bus.put(0x05, 0x9000, 0x6B) // RTL
	cpu.Step()                  // JSL
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.PBR != 0x05 || got.PC != 0x9000 {
		t.Fatalf("after JSL: PBR:PC = %02x:%04x", got.PBR, got.PC)
	}
	cpu.Step() // RTL
	got = cpu.Regs()
	if got.PBR != 0x00 || got.PC != 0x8004 {
		t.Errorf("after RTL: PBR:PC = %02x:%04x, want 00:8004", got.PBR, got.PC)
	}
	if got.S != 0x01FF {
		t.Errorf("S = %#x, want restored 0x01FF", got.S)
	}
}

func TestJMPIndirectNoPageWrap(t *testing.T) {
	// The 65816 (unlike the NMOS 6502) does not wrap the
	// JMP (abs) pointer fetch at a page boundary: the high
	// byte comes from 0x0300 here. The single-step corpus
	// trace for 0x6C shows the 0x59FF to 0x5A00 fetch pair.
	r := native()
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x6C, 0xFF, 0x02) // JMP ($02FF)
	bus.put(0, 0x02FF, 0x00)
	bus.put(0, 0x0200, 0x90) // the 6502's wrap target: must NOT be used
	bus.put(0, 0x0300, 0x77)
	cpu.Step()
	if cpu.Regs().PC != 0x7700 {
		t.Errorf("PC = %#x, want 0x7700 (no page wrap)", cpu.Regs().PC)
	}
}

func TestBRKSkipsSignatureAndPushesBank(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	r.PBR = 0x03
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x00, 0xEA) // BRK, signature byte
	bus.put(0, 0xFFE6, 0x00)
	bus.put(0, 0xFFE7, 0x95) // native BRK vector = 0x9500
	bus.put(0, 0x9500, 0xEA)
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.PC != 0x9500 || got.PBR != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("after BRK: %02x:%04x, want 00:9500", got.PBR, got.PC)
	}
	// Stack: PBR at 0x01FF, PCH 0x01FE, PCL 0x01FD, P 0x01FC.
	if v := bus.at(0, 0x01FF); v != 0x03 {
		t.Errorf("pushed PBR = %#x", v)
	}
	ret := uint16(bus.at(0, 0x01FE))<<8 | uint16(bus.at(0, 0x01FD))
	if ret != 0x8002 {
		t.Errorf("pushed return = %#x, want 0x8002 (signature skipped)", ret)
	}
	if got.P&FlagI == 0 {
		t.Errorf("I not set after BRK")
	}
}

func TestCOPUsesCOPVector(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x02, 0x07) // COP 7
	bus.put(0, 0xFFE4, 0x00)
	bus.put(0, 0xFFE5, 0x91)
	cpu.Step()
	if cpu.Regs().PC != 0x9100 {
		t.Errorf("PC = %#x, want 0x9100 (COP vector)", cpu.Regs().PC)
	}
}

func TestBlockMoveCopiesAndSetsDBR(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	// MVN dst=0x7E src=0x00: copy 4 bytes (A=3) from
	// 00:9000.. to 7E:8000...
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x54, 0x7E, 0x00)
	cpu.SetRegs(Registers{A: 3, X: 0x9000, Y: 0x8000, S: 0x01FF, PC: 0x8000, E: false})
	for i, v := range []byte{0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF} {
		bus.put(0x00, 0x9000+uint16(i), v)
	}
	cycles := cpu.Step()
	for i, want := range []byte{0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF} {
		if got := bus.at(0x7E, 0x8000+uint16(i)); got != want {
			t.Errorf("dest[%d] = %#x, want %#x", i, got, want)
		}
	}
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.A != 0xFFFF {
		t.Errorf("A = %#x, want 0xFFFF (counter wrapped)", got.A)
	}
	if got.X != 0x9004 || got.Y != 0x8004 {
		t.Errorf("X,Y = %#x,%#x, want 0x9004,0x8004", got.X, got.Y)
	}
	if got.DBR != 0x7E {
		t.Errorf("DBR = %#x, want 0x7E (destination bank)", got.DBR)
	}
	// Cycle structure: seven cycles per byte copied, each
	// iteration carrying its own opcode and operand
	// fetches (the single-step corpus's shape).
	if cycles != 7*4 {
		t.Errorf("MVN cycles = %d, want %d", cycles, 7*4)
	}
}

func TestBlockMoveBackwards(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x44, 0x7E, 0x00) // MVP dst=0x7E src=0x00
	cpu.SetRegs(Registers{A: 1, X: 0x9001, Y: 0x8001, S: 0x01FF, PC: 0x8000, E: false})
	bus.put(0, 0x9001, 0x11)
	bus.put(0, 0x9000, 0x22)
	cpu.Step()
	if got := bus.at(0x7E, 0x8001); got != 0x11 {
		t.Errorf("dest[1] = %#x, want 0x11", got)
	}
	if got := bus.at(0x7E, 0x8000); got != 0x22 {
		t.Errorf("dest[0] = %#x, want 0x22", got)
	}
	if cpu.Regs().X != 0x8FFF {
		t.Errorf("X = %#x, want 0x8FFF (counted down past start)", cpu.Regs().X)
	}
}

func TestSerializeRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	r.A, r.X, r.D, r.DBR = 0x1234, 0x5678, 0x9ABC, 0x42
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xEA)
	cpu.Step()
	state := cpu.Serialize()
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(emu())
	if err := cpu2.Deserialize(state); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Deserialize: %v", err)
	}
	if cpu2.Regs() != cpu.Regs() {
		t.Errorf("regs differ after round trip: %+v vs %+v", cpu2.Regs(), cpu.Regs())
	}
	if cpu2.Cycles() != cpu.Cycles() || cpu2.MasterCycles() != cpu.MasterCycles() {
		t.Errorf("cycle counters differ after round trip")
	}
	if err := cpu2.Deserialize([]byte{1, 2, 3}); err == nil {
		t.Errorf("short state accepted")
	}
}

func TestResetEntersEmulationAtVector(t *testing.T) {
	bus := newRAMBus()
	bus.put(0, 0xFFFC, 0x00)
	bus.put(0, 0xFFFD, 0x80)
	cpu := New()
	cpu.Attach(bus)
	cpu.Reset()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if !got.E || got.PC != 0x8000 || got.S != 0x01FF {
		t.Errorf("after reset: %+v", got)
	}
	if cpu.Cycles() != 7 {
		t.Errorf("reset cycles = %d, want 7", cpu.Cycles())
	}
}

func TestEmulationStackConfinedToPage1(t *testing.T) {
	r := emu()
	r.S = 0x3456                    // stored high byte is junk; addressing must confine
	cpu, bus := newTestCPU(r, 0x48) // PHA
	cpu.Step()
	if got := bus.at(0, 0x0156); got != uint8(cpu.Regs().A) {
		t.Errorf("PHA wrote %#x at 0x0156", got)
	}
	if cpu.Regs().S != 0x0155 {
		t.Errorf("S = %#x, want 0x0155", cpu.Regs().S)
	}
}

func TestWAISleepsUntilInterrupt(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	r.P = FlagI                         // IRQ masked: wake but do not take
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0xCB, 0xEA) // WAI; NOP
	cpu.Step()
	if !cpu.Waiting() {
		t.Fatalf("WAI did not stop the CPU")
	}
	cpu.Step()
	cpu.Step()
	if !cpu.Waiting() {
		t.Fatalf("WAI woke without an interrupt input")
	}
	cpu.SetIRQLine(true)
	cpu.Step() // the wake cycle
	if cpu.Waiting() {
		t.Fatalf("WAI did not wake on IRQ line")
	}
	cpu.Step() // masked by I: executes the NOP, no interrupt taken
	if cpu.Regs().PC != 0x8002 {
		t.Errorf("PC = %#x, want 0x8002 (resumed past NOP)", cpu.Regs().PC)
	}
}

func TestDecimalADC(t *testing.T) {
	r := native()
	r.P = FlagD | FlagM // decimal, 8-bit accumulator
	r.A = 0x0045
	cpu, _ := newTestCPU(r, 0x69, 0x55) // ADC #$55: 45 + 55 = 00 carry 1 in BCD
	cpu.Step()
	got := cpu.Regs()
	if got.A&0xFF != 0x00 || got.P&FlagC == 0 {
		t.Errorf("BCD 45+55: A = %#x, P = %08b, want 0x00 with carry", got.A, got.P)
	}
	r2 := native()
	r2.P = FlagD | FlagM
	r2.A = 0x0009
	cpu2, _ := newTestCPU(r2, 0x69, 0x01) // ADC #$01: 09 + 01 = 10
	cpu2.Step()
	if cpu2.Regs().A&0xFF != 0x10 {
		t.Errorf("BCD 09+01: A = %#x, want 0x10", cpu2.Regs().A)
	}
}

// Command libretro builds the Go SNES core as a libretro shared
// library (go build -buildmode=c-shared). It is a thin C ABI shell
// over the system package: the frontend (the iTaK engine) registers
// its callbacks, hands us a ROM, and calls retro_run once per
// frame.
package main

/*

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>

typedef bool (*retro_environment_t)(unsigned cmd, void *data);
typedef void (*retro_video_refresh_t)(const void *data, unsigned width, unsigned height, size_t pitch);
typedef void (*retro_audio_sample_t)(int16_t left, int16_t right);

static void snes_video(const void *data, unsigned w, unsigned h, size_t pitch) { if (video_cb) video_cb(data, w, h, pitch); }

import "C"

	"os"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-snes/ppu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-snes/system"

// libretro constants used here (from the public libretro API).
const (
	envSetPixelFormat  = 10
	pixelFormatXRGB888 = 1
	deviceJoypad       = 1
	joypadB            = 0
	joypadY            = 1
	joypadSelect       = 2
	joypadStart        = 3
	joypadUp           = 4
	joypadDown         = 5
	joypadLeft         = 6
	joypadRight        = 7
	joypadA            = 8
	joypadX            = 9
	joypadL            = 10
	joypadR            = 11
	regionNTSC         = 0
	snesFPS            = 60.0988 // NTSC SNES frame rate
	snesAspect         = 1.33333 // 4/3, the app convention for SNES
	snesSampleRate     = 32040   // DSP output rate, stereo
	memSaveRAM         = 0
	memSystemRAM       = 1
)

var sys *system.System

func main() {}

//export retro_api_version
func retro_api_version() C.uint { return 1 }

//export retro_init

//export retro_deinit

//export retro_set_environment

//export retro_set_video_refresh
func retro_set_video_refresh(cb C.retro_video_refresh_t) { C.snes_set_video(cb) }

//export retro_set_audio_sample_batch

//export retro_get_system_info

	info.library_name = C.snes_get_name()
	info.library_version = C.snes_get_version()
	info.valid_extensions = C.snes_get_exts()
	info.need_fullpath = false
	info.block_extract = false
}

	info.geometry.base_width = ppu.Width
	info.geometry.base_height = ppu.Height
	info.geometry.max_width = ppu.Width
	info.geometry.max_height = ppu.Height
	info.geometry.aspect_ratio = snesAspect
	info.timing.fps = snesFPS
	info.timing.sample_rate = snesSampleRate

//export retro_get_region

//export retro_load_game
func retro_load_game(info *C.struct_snes_game_info) C.bool {
	var data []byte
	if info.data != nil && info.size > 0 {
		data = C.GoBytes(info.data, C.int(info.size))
	} else if info.path != nil {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(C.GoString(info.path))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		data = b
	} else {
		return false
	}
	s, err := system.New(data)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	sys = s
	// Ask the frontend for XRGB8888 frames (what the PPU produces).
	fmt888 := C.uint32_t(pixelFormatXRGB888)
	C.snes_environ(envSetPixelFormat, unsafe.Pointer(&fmt888))
	return true
}

//export retro_unload_game
func retro_unload_game() { sys = nil }

//export retro_reset
func retro_reset() {
	if sys != nil {
		sys.Reset()
	}
}

func pressed(port int, id uint) bool {
	return C.snes_input_state(C.unsigned(port), deviceJoypad, 0, C.unsigned(id)) != 0
}

// pollPad translates libretro joypad state into the SNES button
// mask. The libretro joypad ids use the standard order B, Y,
// Select, Start, Up, Down, Left, Right, A, X, L, R, which matches
// the system Button bit order 1:1, so this is a direct mapping.
func pollPad(port int) uint16 {
	var m uint16
	if pressed(port, joypadB) {
		m |= system.ButtonB
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadY) {
		m |= system.ButtonY
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadSelect) {
		m |= system.ButtonSelect
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadStart) {
		m |= system.ButtonStart
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadUp) {
		m |= system.ButtonUp
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadDown) {
		m |= system.ButtonDown
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadLeft) {
		m |= system.ButtonLeft
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadRight) {
		m |= system.ButtonRight
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadA) {
		m |= system.ButtonA
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadX) {
		m |= system.ButtonX
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadL) {
		m |= system.ButtonL
	}
	if pressed(port, joypadR) {
		m |= system.ButtonR
	}
	return m
}

//export retro_run
func retro_run() {
	if sys == nil {
		return
	}
	C.snes_input_poll()
	sys.SetButtons(0, pollPad(0))
	sys.SetButtons(1, pollPad(1))
	sys.RunFrame()

	fb := sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) > 0 {
		C.snes_video(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0]),
			C.unsigned(ppu.Width), C.unsigned(ppu.Height),
			C.size_t(ppu.Width*4))
	}
	ab := sys.AudioBuffer()
	if len(ab) >= 2 {
		frames := len(ab) / 2
		done := int(C.snes_audio_batch((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&ab[0])), C.size_t(frames)))
		for i := done; i < frames; i++ {
			C.snes_audio_sample(C.int16_t(ab[2*i]), C.int16_t(ab[2*i+1]))
		}
	}
}

//export retro_serialize_size
func retro_serialize_size() C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return C.size_t(sys.StateSize())
}

//export retro_serialize
func retro_serialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	state := sys.Serialize()
	if len(state) == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), len(state))
	copy(buf, state)
	return true
}

//export retro_unserialize
func retro_unserialize(data unsafe.Pointer) C.bool {
	if sys == nil || data == nil {
		return false
	}
	size := sys.StateSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return false
	}
	buf := unsafe.Slice((*byte)(data), size)
	cp := make([]byte, size)
	copy(cp, buf)
	return sys.Deserialize(cp) == nil
}

// The memory interface exposes cartridge RAM as SAVE_RAM and the
// console work RAM as SYSTEM_RAM, the standard libretro memory
// map ids.

//export retro_get_memory_data
func retro_get_memory_data(id C.unsigned) unsafe.Pointer {
	if sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var ram []uint8
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		ram = sys.SaveRAM()
	case memSystemRAM:
		ram = sys.SystemRAM()
	}
	if len(ram) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Pointer(&ram[0])
}

//export retro_get_memory_size
func retro_get_memory_size(id C.unsigned) C.size_t {
	if sys == nil {
		return 0
	}
	switch id {
	case memSaveRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SaveRAM()))
	case memSystemRAM:
		return C.size_t(len(sys.SystemRAM()))
	}
	return 0
}

func retro_cheat_reset() {}

==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/ppu/ppu.go ====================

// Package ppu is the SNES picture processing unit: the
// register file ($2100-$213F), VRAM, CGRAM, and OAM, and the
// renderer. Rendering is evaluated per scanline: at the end
// of each display line the machine asks for that line, and
// the PPU composes it from the register and memory state as
// it stands at that moment. Register changes made mid-line
// by the CPU therefore take effect from the following line,
// not partway through the current one; that is the one
// documented timing simplification of this slice (SNES-2).
// Sprite and background fetches, windows, and color math
// otherwise follow the published register documentation
// (the SNES development manual material as collected in
// fullsnes and the SNESdev wiki).
package ppu

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
)

// Display geometry of the framebuffer this core produces.
const (
	Width  = 256
	Height = 224
)

// VRAM translation and increment helpers.

// translate applies the VMAIN address translation (the
// rotate modes used by games uploading interleaved tile
// data) to a VRAM word address.
func (p *PPU) translate(addr uint16) uint16 {
	switch p.vmIncTrans {
	case 1: // 8-bit rotation
		return addr&0xFF00 | (addr&0x00FF)>>3 | (addr&0x07)<<5
	case 2: // 9-bit rotation
		return addr&0xFE00 | (addr&0x01FF)>>3 | (addr&0x07)<<6
	case 3: // 10-bit rotation
		return addr&0xFC00 | (addr&0x03FF)>>3 | (addr&0x07)<<7
	}
	return addr
}

var vmIncAmount = [4]uint16{1, 32, 128, 128}

// bgLayer holds one background layer's register state.
type bgLayer struct {
	tilemapBase uint16 // word address of the tilemap
	tilemapW    int    // in tiles: 32 or 64
	tilemapH    int
	chrBase     uint16 // word address of the tile data
	hofs, vofs  uint16 // raw latch-formula values; masked at use
	tile16      bool   // 16x16 tiles (mode 5/6 force 16 wide)
}

// PPU is the whole picture unit.
type PPU struct {
	vram  [0x8000]uint16
	cgram [256]uint16
	oam   [544]byte
	frame []uint32

	// $2100 INIDISP.
	forcedBlank bool
	brightness  uint8

	// $2101 OBSEL.
	objBase uint16 // word address
	objGap  uint16 // word offset of the second tile page
	objSize int    // size select 0..7

	// OAM access.
	oamAddr    int  // byte address, wraps at 1024
	oamPrioRot bool // $2103 bit 7: priority rotation
	oamBuf     byte // buffered even byte for $2104 writes

	// $2105 BGMODE, $2106 mosaic.
	bgMode     uint8
	bg3PrioBit bool
	mosaicSize int // 1..16
	mosaicBG   uint8

	bg [4]bgLayer

	// Scroll write latches (the documented shared-latch
	// formula: one latch for the previous byte across all
	// scroll registers, plus per-axis low-bit latches).
	bgofsLatch uint8
	hofsLatch  uint8
	vofsLatch  uint8

	// $2115 VMAIN.
	vmIncHigh  bool   // increment after $2119 (else after $2118)
	vmIncAmt   uint16 // 1, 32, or 128
	vmIncTrans uint8

	// VRAM port.
	vmAddr     uint16 // word address, 15 bits
	vmPrefetch uint16

	// $211A M7SEL and the matrix.
	m7FlipX, m7FlipY   bool
	m7Over             uint8 // screen-over mode 0..3
	m7a, m7b, m7c, m7d int16
	m7x, m7y           uint16 // 13-bit values, sign-extended at use
	m7Latch            uint8
	mpy                int32 // last Mode 7 multiply result

	// CGRAM port.
	cgAddr     uint8 // color index
	cgBuf      byte  // buffered low byte for $2122 writes
	cgHighNext bool  // next $2122 write is the high byte
	cgReadHigh bool  // next $213B read is the high byte

	// Windows.
	w12sel, w34sel, wobjsel uint8
	wh                      [4]uint8 // left/right of window 1, left/right of window 2
	wbglog, wobjlog         uint8
	tm, ts, tmw, tsw        uint8

	// Color math.
	cgwsel uint8
	cgadsb uint8
	fixedR uint8 // 5-bit fixed color channels from $2132
	fixedG uint8
	fixedB uint8

	// $2133 SETINI.
	setINI uint8

	// Counters and status.
	hLatch, vLatch uint16
	ophctHigh      bool // next $213C read returns the high bit
	opvctHigh      bool
	latchFlag      bool // counters latched ($2137 or pin) since last $213F read
	rangeOver      bool
	timeOver       bool
	field          bool // interlace field for $213F

	// Set by the machine at every sync: whether a CPU write
	// right now would land in the active display area (used
	// to gate CGRAM writes the way the hardware drops them
	// mid-display).
	displayActive bool

	// Scanline composition scratch, owned by the renderer
	// and rewritten on every RenderLine: it is derived
	// state, never saved, and exists so a frame of
	// composition allocates nothing.
	lbBG      [4]lineBuf
	lbObj     lineBuf
	lbMain    lineBuf
	lbSub     lineBuf
	winIn     [6][512]bool
	winMask   [512]uint8 // per pixel window verdicts for layers 0..4, one bit each
	blackAt   [512]bool
	subRegAt  [512]bool
	objOnLine [33]objSpr
	objDraw   [33]objSpr
	rowMemo   [128]tileRowEntry
	lineStamp uint32
	// The last tile row tileRow returned, keyed and
	// stamped exactly like a memo entry: consecutive
	// spans of a line repeat the same tile row often
	// enough that the shortcut pays for its compare.
	lastRowKey   uint32
	lastRowStamp uint32
	lastRowPix   [8]uint8
	expTab       [32768]uint32
	expBright    uint8
	expValid     bool
}

// New returns a PPU in its power-on state.
func New() *PPU {
	p := &PPU{frame: make([]uint32, Width*Height)}
	p.mosaicSize = 1
	p.vmIncAmt = 1
	return p
}

// Framebuffer returns the current picture: 256 by 224
// pixels in XRGB8888.
func (p *PPU) Framebuffer() []uint32 { return p.frame }

// SetDisplayActive tells the PPU whether the machine is
// currently inside the active display area (a visible line,
// before HBlank, not forced blank). The hardware drops
// CGRAM writes that land there; the machine tracks the dot
// position, the PPU just records the verdict.
func (p *PPU) SetDisplayActive(active bool) { p.displayActive = active }

// ForcedBlank reports whether INIDISP bit 7 forces the
// picture blank.
func (p *PPU) ForcedBlank() bool { return p.forcedBlank }

// Overscan reports whether SETINI bit 3 selects the
// 239-line picture.
func (p *PPU) Overscan() bool { return p.setINI&0x08 != 0 }

// Interlace reports whether SETINI bit 0 selects interlace.
func (p *PPU) Interlace() bool { return p.setINI&0x01 != 0 }

// Field returns the current interlace field.
func (p *PPU) Field() bool { return p.field }

// SetField records the interlace field parity the machine
// is running (it owns the frame timing).
func (p *PPU) SetField(f bool) { p.field = f }

// ClearSpriteFlags resets the range-over and time-over
// flags; the machine calls this at the frame boundary the
// documentation gives them.
func (p *PPU) ClearSpriteFlags() { p.rangeOver, p.timeOver = false, false }

// LatchCounters captures the H and V counters (the $2137
// read); the machine owns the position and passes it in.
func (p *PPU) LatchCounters(h, v uint16) {
	p.hLatch, p.vLatch = h, v
	p.latchFlag = true
}

// vramWord reads one VRAM word for the renderer and tests.
func (p *PPU) vramWord(addr uint16) uint16 { return p.vram[addr&0x7FFF] }

// WriteReg handles a CPU write to $2100-$213F.
func (p *PPU) WriteReg(addr uint16, val uint8) {
	switch {
	case addr == 0x2100: // INIDISP
		p.forcedBlank = val&0x80 != 0
		p.brightness = val & 0x0F
	case addr == 0x2101: // OBSEL
		p.objBase = uint16(val&0x03) << 13
		p.objGap = (uint16((val>>3)&0x03) + 1) << 12
		p.objSize = int(val >> 5)
	case addr == 0x2102: // OAMADDL
		p.oamAddr = (p.oamAddr & 0x200) | int(val)<<1
	case addr == 0x2103: // OAMADDH
		p.oamAddr = (p.oamAddr & 0x1FE) | int(val&0x01)<<9
		p.oamPrioRot = val&0x80 != 0
	case addr == 0x2104: // OAMDATA
		p.writeOAM(val)
	case addr == 0x2105: // BGMODE
		p.bgMode = val & 0x07
		p.bg3PrioBit = val&0x08 != 0
		p.bg[0].tile16 = val&0x10 != 0
		p.bg[1].tile16 = val&0x20 != 0
		p.bg[2].tile16 = val&0x40 != 0
		p.bg[3].tile16 = val&0x80 != 0
	case addr == 0x2106: // MOSAIC: size in the high nibble,
		// per-layer enables (BG1 is bit 0) in the low
		p.mosaicSize = int(val>>4) + 1
		p.mosaicBG = val & 0x0F
	case addr >= 0x2107 && addr <= 0x210A: // BGnSC
		b := &p.bg[addr-0x2107]
		b.tilemapBase = uint16(val&0xFC) << 8
		switch val & 0x03 {
		case 0:
			b.tilemapW, b.tilemapH = 32, 32
		case 1:
			b.tilemapW, b.tilemapH = 64, 32
		case 2:
			b.tilemapW, b.tilemapH = 32, 64
		case 3:
			b.tilemapW, b.tilemapH = 64, 64
		}
	case addr == 0x210B: // BG12NBA
		p.bg[0].chrBase = uint16(val&0x0F) << 12
		p.bg[1].chrBase = uint16(val>>4) << 12
	case addr == 0x210C: // BG34NBA
		p.bg[2].chrBase = uint16(val&0x0F) << 12
		p.bg[3].chrBase = uint16(val>>4) << 12
	case addr >= 0x210D && addr <= 0x2114: // scroll registers
		p.writeScroll(int(addr-0x210D), val)
	case addr == 0x2115: // VMAIN
		p.vmIncHigh = val&0x80 != 0
		p.vmIncAmt = vmIncAmount[val&0x03]
		p.vmIncTrans = (val >> 2) & 0x03
	case addr == 0x2116: // VMADDL
		p.vmAddr = (p.vmAddr & 0x7F00) | uint16(val)
	case addr == 0x2117: // VMADDH
		p.vmAddr = (p.vmAddr & 0x00FF) | uint16(val&0x7F)<<8
	case addr == 0x2118: // VMDATAL
		ta := p.translate(p.vmAddr)
		p.vram[ta] = (p.vram[ta] & 0xFF00) | uint16(val)
		if !p.vmIncHigh {
			p.vmAddr = (p.vmAddr + p.vmIncAmt) & 0x7FFF
		}
	case addr == 0x2119: // VMDATAH
		ta := p.translate(p.vmAddr)
		p.vram[ta] = (p.vram[ta] & 0x00FF) | uint16(val)<<8
		if p.vmIncHigh {
			p.vmAddr = (p.vmAddr + p.vmIncAmt) & 0x7FFF
		}
	case addr == 0x211A: // M7SEL
		p.m7Over = val & 0x03
		p.m7FlipX = val&0x40 != 0
		p.m7FlipY = val&0x80 != 0
	case addr >= 0x211B && addr <= 0x2120: // Mode 7 registers
		p.writeMode7(int(addr-0x211B), val)
	case addr == 0x2121: // CGADD
		p.cgAddr = val
		p.cgHighNext = false
	case addr == 0x2122: // CGDATA
		p.writeCGRAM(val)
	case addr == 0x2123: // W12SEL
		p.w12sel = val
	case addr == 0x2124: // W34SEL
		p.w34sel = val
	case addr == 0x2125: // WOBJSEL
		p.wobjsel = val
	case addr >= 0x2126 && addr <= 0x2129: // WH0..WH3
		p.wh[addr-0x2126] = val
	case addr == 0x212A: // WBGLOG
		p.wbglog = val
	case addr == 0x212B: // WOBJLOG
		p.wobjlog = val
	case addr == 0x212C: // TM
		p.tm = val & 0x1F
	case addr == 0x212D: // TS
		p.ts = val & 0x1F
	case addr == 0x212E: // TMW
		p.tmw = val & 0x1F
	case addr == 0x212F: // TSW
		p.tsw = val & 0x1F
	case addr == 0x2130: // CGWSEL
		p.cgwsel = val
	case addr == 0x2131: // CGADSUB
		p.cgadsb = val
	case addr == 0x2132: // COLDATA
		if val&0x20 != 0 {
			p.fixedR = val & 0x1F
		}
		if val&0x40 != 0 {
			p.fixedG = val & 0x1F
		}
		if val&0x80 != 0 {
			p.fixedB = val & 0x1F
		}
	case addr == 0x2133: // SETINI
		p.setINI = val
	}
	// All other $21xx writes (read-only registers, the
	// multiply outputs, and the rest) are dropped.
}

// oamIndex folds a byte address into the 544-byte OAM.
func oamIndex(addr int) int {
	addr %= 1024
	if addr >= 544 {
		addr -= 544
	}
	return addr
}

// writeOAM implements the $2104 buffered pair write: the
// even byte is held in the internal buffer and only lands
// (together with the odd byte that follows it) when the
// odd byte is written; the address then advances.
func (p *PPU) writeOAM(val uint8) {
	if p.oamAddr&1 == 0 {
		p.oamBuf = val
	} else {
		p.oam[oamIndex(p.oamAddr-1)] = p.oamBuf
		p.oam[oamIndex(p.oamAddr)] = val
	}
	// The byte pointer advances on every write; only the
	// word address (for priority rotation) stands still
	// between the two halves of a pair.
	p.oamAddr = (p.oamAddr + 1) & 0x3FF
}

// writeScroll implements the shared-latch write formula
// for $210D-$2114: the value written becomes the high byte,
// the low bits come from the previous scroll write (one
// latch shared by all eight registers, one low-3-bit latch
// per axis). Registers: 0 BG1H, 1 BG1V (also Mode 7
// scrolls), 2 BG2H, 3 BG2V, 4 BG3H, 5 BG3V, 6 BG4H, 7 BG4V.
func (p *PPU) writeScroll(idx int, val uint8) {
	bg := &p.bg[idx/2]
	if idx%2 == 0 { // horizontal
		bg.hofs = (uint16(val) << 8) | uint16(p.bgofsLatch&0xF8) | uint16(p.hofsLatch&0x07)
		p.hofsLatch = val
	} else { // vertical
		bg.vofs = (uint16(val) << 8) | uint16(p.bgofsLatch&0xF8) | uint16(p.vofsLatch&0x07)
		p.vofsLatch = val
	}
	p.bgofsLatch = val
}

// writeMode7 implements the $211B-$2120 register writes,
// all sharing the one-byte latch: 0 M7A, 1 M7B, 2 M7C,
// 3 M7D, 4 M7X, 5 M7Y. Writing M7B also updates the
// multiply result ($2134-$2136): M7A times the high byte
// of M7B, signed, 24 bits.
func (p *PPU) writeMode7(idx int, val uint8) {
	full := uint16(val)<<8 | uint16(p.m7Latch)
	p.m7Latch = val
	switch idx {
	case 0:
		p.m7a = int16(full)
	case 1:
		p.m7b = int16(full)
		p.mpy = int32(p.m7a) * int32(int8(p.m7b>>8))
	case 2:
		p.m7c = int16(full)
	case 3:
		p.m7d = int16(full)
	case 4:
		p.m7x = full & 0x1FFF
	case 5:
		p.m7y = full & 0x1FFF
	}
}

// writeCGRAM implements the $2122 write: pairs of bytes
// form one 15-bit color, and a write that lands in the
// active display area is dropped, as on hardware.
func (p *PPU) writeCGRAM(val uint8) {
	if !p.cgHighNext {
		p.cgBuf = val
		p.cgHighNext = true
		return
	}
	p.cgHighNext = false
	if p.displayActive {
		// The address still advances; the write is lost.
		p.cgAddr++
		return
	}
	p.cgram[p.cgAddr] = uint16(val&0x7F)<<8 | uint16(p.cgBuf)
	p.cgAddr++
}

// ReadReg handles a CPU read of $2134-$213F, given the
// machine's open-bus byte for the fields hardware leaves
// undriven.
func (p *PPU) ReadReg(addr uint16, openBus uint8) uint8 {
	switch addr {
	case 0x2134: // MPYL
		return uint8(p.mpy)
	case 0x2135: // MPYM
		return uint8(p.mpy >> 8)
	case 0x2136: // MPYH
		return uint8(p.mpy >> 16)
	case 0x2137: // SLHV (the machine latches via LatchCounters)
		return openBus
	case 0x2138: // OAMDATAREAD
		v := p.oam[oamIndex(p.oamAddr)]
		if p.oamAddr&1 == 1 {
			p.oamAddr = (p.oamAddr + 1) & 0x3FF
		} else {
			p.oamAddr++
		}
		return v
	case 0x2139: // VMDATALREAD
		v := uint8(p.vmPrefetch)
		w := p.vram[p.translate(p.vmAddr)]
		p.vmPrefetch = (p.vmPrefetch & 0xFF00) | (w & 0x00FF)
		if !p.vmIncHigh {
			p.vmAddr = (p.vmAddr + p.vmIncAmt) & 0x7FFF
		}
		return v
	case 0x213A: // VMDATAHREAD
		v := uint8(p.vmPrefetch >> 8)
		w := p.vram[p.translate(p.vmAddr)]
		p.vmPrefetch = (p.vmPrefetch & 0x00FF) | (w & 0xFF00)
		if p.vmIncHigh {
			p.vmAddr = (p.vmAddr + p.vmIncAmt) & 0x7FFF
		}
		return v
	case 0x213B: // CGDATAREAD
		var v uint8
		if p.cgReadHigh {
			v = uint8(p.cgram[p.cgAddr] >> 8)
			p.cgAddr++
			p.cgReadHigh = false
		} else {
			v = uint8(p.cgram[p.cgAddr])
			p.cgReadHigh = true
		}
		return v
	case 0x213C: // OPHCT
		if p.ophctHigh {
			p.ophctHigh = false
			return uint8(p.hLatch>>8) & 0x01
		}
		p.ophctHigh = true
		return uint8(p.hLatch)
	case 0x213D: // OPVCT
		if p.opvctHigh {
			p.opvctHigh = false
			return uint8(p.vLatch>>8) & 0x01
		}
		p.opvctHigh = true
		return uint8(p.vLatch)
	case 0x213E: // STAT77
		v := uint8(1) // PPU1 version
		if p.timeOver {
			v |= 0x40
		}
		if p.rangeOver {
			v |= 0x80
		}
		return v
	case 0x213F: // STAT78
		v := uint8(3) // PPU2 version (NTSC part)
		if p.field {
			v |= 0x40
		}
		if p.latchFlag {
			v |= 0x80
		}
		p.latchFlag = false
		p.ophctHigh = false
		p.opvctHigh = false
		return v
	}
	return openBus
}

// The register block serialized below is fixed-size; the
// memory arrays are serialized by the same block layout in
// the same order the fields appear here.

// serializeSize is the PPU's save-state size: VRAM
// (64 KB), CGRAM (512), OAM (544), then registers.
const serializeRegsSize = 256
const SerializeSize = 0x8000*2 + 256*2 + 544 + serializeRegsSize

// Serialize writes the PPU state into buf, which must be
// at least SerializeSize.
func (p *PPU) Serialize(buf []byte) {
	off := 0
	for _, w := range p.vram {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[off:], w)
		off += 2
	}
	for _, w := range p.cgram {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(buf[off:], w)
		off += 2
	}
	copy(buf[off:], p.oam[:])
	off += len(p.oam)
	r := buf[off : off+serializeRegsSize]
	for i := range r {
		r[i] = 0
	}
	put16 := func(o int, v uint16) { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(r[o:], v) }
	put32 := func(o int, v int32) { binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(r[o:], uint32(v)) }
	if p.forcedBlank {
		r[0] |= 1
	}
	r[1] = p.brightness
	put16(2, p.objBase)
	put16(4, p.objGap)
	r[6] = uint8(p.objSize)
	put16(7, uint16(p.oamAddr))
	if p.oamPrioRot {
		r[9] |= 1
	}
	r[10] = p.oamBuf
	r[11] = p.bgMode
	if p.bg3PrioBit {
		r[12] |= 1
	}
	r[13] = uint8(p.mosaicSize)
	r[14] = p.mosaicBG
	for i := range p.bg {
		b := 16 + i*10
		put16(b, p.bg[i].tilemapBase)
		r[b+2] = uint8(p.bg[i].tilemapW)
		r[b+3] = uint8(p.bg[i].tilemapH)
		put16(b+4, p.bg[i].chrBase)
		put16(b+6, p.bg[i].hofs)
		put16(b+8, p.bg[i].vofs)
		if p.bg[i].tile16 {
			r[15] |= 1 << i
		}
	}
	r[56] = p.bgofsLatch
	r[57] = p.hofsLatch
	r[58] = p.vofsLatch
	if p.vmIncHigh {
		r[59] |= 1
	}
	put16(60, p.vmIncAmt)
	r[62] = p.vmIncTrans
	put16(63, p.vmAddr)
	put16(65, p.vmPrefetch)
	if p.m7FlipX {
		r[67] |= 1
	}
	if p.m7FlipY {
		r[67] |= 2
	}
	r[68] = p.m7Over
	put16(69, uint16(p.m7a))
	put16(71, uint16(p.m7b))
	put16(73, uint16(p.m7c))
	put16(75, uint16(p.m7d))
	put16(77, p.m7x)
	put16(79, p.m7y)
	r[81] = p.m7Latch
	put32(82, p.mpy)
	r[86] = p.cgAddr
	r[87] = p.cgBuf
	if p.cgHighNext {
		r[88] |= 1
	}
	if p.cgReadHigh {
		r[88] |= 2
	}
	r[89], r[90], r[91] = p.w12sel, p.w34sel, p.wobjsel
	copy(r[92:], p.wh[:])
	r[96], r[97] = p.wbglog, p.wobjlog
	r[98], r[99], r[100], r[101] = p.tm, p.ts, p.tmw, p.tsw
	r[102], r[103] = p.cgwsel, p.cgadsb
	r[104], r[105], r[106] = p.fixedR, p.fixedG, p.fixedB
	r[107] = p.setINI
	put16(108, p.hLatch)
	put16(110, p.vLatch)
	if p.ophctHigh {
		r[112] |= 1
	}
	if p.opvctHigh {
		r[112] |= 2
	}
	if p.latchFlag {
		r[112] |= 4
	}
	if p.rangeOver {
		r[112] |= 8
	}
	if p.timeOver {
		r[112] |= 16
	}
	if p.field {
		r[112] |= 32
	}
	if p.displayActive {
		r[112] |= 64
	}
}

// Deserialize restores a state written by Serialize.
func (p *PPU) Deserialize(buf []byte) error {
	if len(buf) < SerializeSize {
		return errors.New("ppu: state too small")
	}
	off := 0
	for i := range p.vram {
		p.vram[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[off:])
		off += 2
	}
	for i := range p.cgram {
		p.cgram[i] = binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(buf[off:])
		off += 2
	}
	copy(p.oam[:], buf[off:])
	off += len(p.oam)
	r := buf[off : off+serializeRegsSize]
	get16 := func(o int) uint16 { return binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(r[o:]) }
	p.forcedBlank = r[0]&1 != 0
	p.brightness = r[1]
	p.objBase = get16(2)
	p.objGap = get16(4)
	p.objSize = int(r[6])
	p.oamAddr = int(get16(7))
	p.oamPrioRot = r[9]&1 != 0
	p.oamBuf = r[10]
	p.bgMode = r[11]
	p.bg3PrioBit = r[12]&1 != 0
	p.mosaicSize = int(r[13])
	p.mosaicBG = r[14]
	for i := range p.bg {
		b := 16 + i*10
		p.bg[i].tilemapBase = get16(b)
		p.bg[i].tilemapW = int(r[b+2])
		p.bg[i].tilemapH = int(r[b+3])
		p.bg[i].chrBase = get16(b + 4)
		p.bg[i].hofs = get16(b + 6)
		p.bg[i].vofs = get16(b + 8)
		p.bg[i].tile16 = r[15]&(1<<i) != 0
	}
	p.bgofsLatch = r[56]
	p.hofsLatch = r[57]
	p.vofsLatch = r[58]
	p.vmIncHigh = r[59]&1 != 0
	p.vmIncAmt = get16(60)
	p.vmIncTrans = r[62]
	p.vmAddr = get16(63)
	p.vmPrefetch = get16(65)
	p.m7FlipX = r[67]&1 != 0
	p.m7FlipY = r[67]&2 != 0
	p.m7Over = r[68]
	p.m7a = int16(get16(69))
	p.m7b = int16(get16(71))
	p.m7c = int16(get16(73))
	p.m7d = int16(get16(75))
	p.m7x = get16(77)
	p.m7y = get16(79)
	p.m7Latch = r[81]
	p.mpy = int32(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(r[82:]))
	p.cgAddr = r[86]
	p.cgBuf = r[87]
	p.cgHighNext = r[88]&1 != 0
	p.cgReadHigh = r[88]&2 != 0
	p.w12sel, p.w34sel, p.wobjsel = r[89], r[90], r[91]
	copy(p.wh[:], r[92:96])
	p.wbglog, p.wobjlog = r[96], r[97]
	p.tm, p.ts, p.tmw, p.tsw = r[98], r[99], r[100], r[101]
	p.cgwsel, p.cgadsb = r[102], r[103]
	p.fixedR, p.fixedG, p.fixedB = r[104], r[105], r[106]
	p.setINI = r[107]
	p.hLatch = get16(108)
	p.vLatch = get16(110)
	p.ophctHigh = r[112]&1 != 0
	p.opvctHigh = r[112]&2 != 0
	p.latchFlag = r[112]&4 != 0
	p.rangeOver = r[112]&8 != 0
	p.timeOver = r[112]&16 != 0
	p.field = r[112]&32 != 0
	p.displayActive = r[112]&64 != 0
	return nil
}


==================== FILE: cores/go-snes/ppu/ppu_test.go ====================

package ppu

import "testing"

func wr(p *PPU, addr uint16, v uint8) { p.WriteReg(addr, v) }

// setVMADD points the VRAM address at a word address.
func setVMADD(p *PPU, w uint16) {
	wr(p, 0x2116, uint8(w))
	wr(p, 0x2117, uint8(w>>8))
}

func TestVRAMWriteAndIncrement(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	wr(p, 0x2115, 0x80) // increment after high byte, step 1
	setVMADD(p, 0x0100)
	wr(p, 0x2118, 0x34)
	if p.vram[0x100] != 0x0034 {
		t.Fatalf("after low write vram = %#06x, want 0x0034", p.vram[0x100])
	}
	wr(p, 0x2119, 0x12)
	if p.vram[0x100] != 0x1234 {
		t.Fatalf("after high write vram = %#06x, want 0x1234", p.vram[0x100])
	}
	// The address incremented after the high byte only.
	setVMADD(p, 0x0101)
	wr(p, 0x2118, 0x78)
	wr(p, 0x2119, 0x56)
	if p.vram[0x101] != 0x5678 {
		t.Fatalf("vram[0x101] = %#06x, want 0x5678", p.vram[0x101])
	}
}

func TestVRAMIncrementAfterLow(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	wr(p, 0x2115, 0x00) // increment after low byte, step 1
	setVMADD(p, 0x0200)
	wr(p, 0x2118, 0xAA) // low of 0x0200, address advances
	wr(p, 0x2118, 0xBB) // low of 0x0201
	if p.vram[0x200] != 0x00AA || p.vram[0x201] != 0x00BB {
		t.Fatalf("vram = %#06x %#06x, want 0x00aa 0x00bb", p.vram[0x200], p.vram[0x201])
	}
}

func TestVRAMPrefetchDiscard(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	p.vram[0x100] = 0x1234
	p.vram[0x101] = 0x5678
	wr(p, 0x2115, 0x80)
	setVMADD(p, 0x0100)
	// First low read returns the stale (power-on) buffer
	// and refills it from the addressed word.
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x2139, 0); v != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("first $2139 = %#x, want stale 0x00", v)
	}
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x2139, 0); v != 0x34 {
		t.Fatalf("second $2139 = %#x, want 0x34", v)
	}
	// The low reads never touched the high buffer: the
	// first high read is stale too. Each high read
	// refills its own half from the addressed word and
	// (increment-after-high mode) advances the address:
	// the reads return 0x12 (word 0x100), then 0x56
	// (word 0x101).
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x213A, 0); v != 0x00 {
		t.Fatalf("first $213A = %#x, want stale 0x00", v)
	}
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x213A, 0); v != 0x12 {
		t.Fatalf("second $213A = %#x, want 0x12", v)
	}
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x213A, 0); v != 0x56 {
		t.Fatalf("third $213A = %#x, want 0x56", v)
	}
}

func TestVRAMTranslationMode1(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	wr(p, 0x2115, 0x80|0x04) // inc after high, translation 1
	setVMADD(p, 0x0108)
	wr(p, 0x2118, 0xAB)
	// Mode 1 rotates the low address byte per the
	// documented bit order (a2 a1 a0 a7 a6 a5 a4 a3):
	// 0x08 (bit a3) lands at bit 0, giving 0x01.
	if p.vram[0x101] != 0x00AB {
		t.Fatalf("vram[0x101] = %#06x, want 0x00ab", p.vram[0x101])
	}
	if p.vram[0x108] != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("vram[0x108] written despite translation")
	}
}

func TestCGRAMPairLatch(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	wr(p, 0x2121, 0x10) // CGADD is the color index
	wr(p, 0x2122, 0xFF) // low byte buffered
	if p.cgram[0x10] != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("color committed on low byte alone")
	}
	wr(p, 0x2122, 0x7F) // high byte commits the pair
	if p.cgram[0x10] != 0x7FFF {
		t.Fatalf("cgram[0x10] = %#06x, want 0x7fff", p.cgram[0x10])
	}
	// Read back: low then high, address advances after
	// the high read.
	wr(p, 0x2121, 0x10)
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x213B, 0); v != 0xFF {
		t.Fatalf("CGDATAREAD low = %#x, want 0xff", v)
	}
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x213B, 0); v != 0x7F {
		t.Fatalf("CGDATAREAD high = %#x, want 0x7f", v)
	}
}

func TestCGRAMWriteDroppedDuringDisplay(t *testing.T) {
	p := New()
	p.SetDisplayActive(true)
	wr(p, 0x2121, 0x00)
	wr(p, 0x2122, 0x34)
	wr(p, 0x2122, 0x12) // dropped: active display
	if p.cgram[0] != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("cgram[0] = %#06x, want 0 (write dropped)", p.cgram[0])
	}
	p.SetDisplayActive(false)
	wr(p, 0x2121, 0x00)
	wr(p, 0x2122, 0x34)
	wr(p, 0x2122, 0x12)
	if p.cgram[0] != 0x1234 {
		t.Fatalf("cgram[0] = %#06x, want 0x1234", p.cgram[0])
	}
}

func TestOAMBufferedWritesAndReads(t *testing.T) {

	}

	wr(p, 0x2103, 0x00)
	if v := p.ReadReg(0x2138, 0); v != 0x11 {
		t.Fatalf("OAMDATAREAD = %#x, want 0x11", v)
