## Drift found while building this edition (code beat the old map)

The old docs/MAP.md grid was checked line by line. Five claims did
not match the code at 1.119 and are corrected above:

1. Old map: the Go cores are the engines that ship. Code: since 1.102
   the app ships six Rust core libraries and carries no Go cores; the
   Go cores are reference twins.
2. Old map: saves are 10 slots per player per game. Code: one rolling
   save state per player per game, plus a write once backup file.
3. Old map: platform builds include Android 64 bit, Windows, and
   Linux. Code and record: only the 32 bit Android build publishes;
   64 bit is paused and planned as 2.0; desktop runners are scaffolding.
4. Old map: voice chat is research only. Code: Go signaling is built;
   media is the missing piece, blocked on microphone hardware.
5. Old map: the update feed lives on dl.itak.live. Code: the feed is
   served by the lobby service appdist module at arcade.itak.live;
   dl.itak.live is the manual downloads page.


==================== FILE: docs/relational-map/README.md ====================

# Relational map: iTaK Gaming

This folder is the relational diagram for the whole iTaK Gaming system:
every page, screen, module, engine, service, and wire, built from the
code in this repo.

## How to read it

- `INVENTORY.md` lists every node: its family, what it does, whether it
  is LIVE, PLANNED, or ABSENT, and the source file it was read from.
- `WIRES.md` lists every connection between nodes: from, to, what
  crosses the wire, and the source file that makes the connection.
- `DIAGRAM.md` draws the same nodes and wires as Mermaid diagrams, one
  sheet per family, so the system can be seen at a glance.
- `docs/MAP.md` at the repo root points here and carries the short
  summary.

## The rules for this map

- Code beats paper. Where an older document and the code disagree, the
  code wins and the disagreement is named in the inventory.
- Every node carries a state. LIVE means the code exists and ships or
  runs today. PLANNED means David has ordered or approved it and it is
  not built yet. ABSENT means a surface a reader might expect is not
  there, named so nobody goes looking for it.
- This map refreshes with every update. See the Relational diagram
  section in `docs/RULES.md`: a feature is not fully landed until this
  map matches it, in the same push cycle.

## State of this edition

- Built from repo HEAD at app version 1.119 (pubspec 1.119.0+120),
  the castle zoom HDMA fix release.
- The old `docs/MAP.md` grid was verified against the code for this
  edition and had drifted in five places. The drift and its fixes are
  listed at the end of `INVENTORY.md`.
- The Rust core sources that ship in the app are not in this repo.
  They are drawn here as external nodes with their staging path named,
  because the wires to them are real even though their source lives
  outside this repo. That gap is recorded, not hidden.


==================== FILE: docs/relational-map/WIRES.md ====================

# Wires: every connection in iTaK Gaming

A wire names what crosses it. Where a wire only exists in one
direction, that is said plainly.

## People, devices, and the shell

| From | To | What crosses | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Player | App shell | D pad and button presses on remote or pad | flutter_ui/lib/main.dart focus handling |
| Player | EmulatorActivity | Game input through the seat system | EmulatorActivity.kt slotFor |
| App shell | Device storage | ROM folder scan per system; box art lookup | flutter_ui/lib/main.dart |
| App shell | MainActivity | Method channel calls: prefs, players, leaderboard, controllers, sound, streams, restart | Method channel net.itak/emu |
| MainActivity | Play stats files | Reads every player stats file for the leaderboard; repairs labels on launch | MainActivity.kt getLeaderboard, repairStatsLabels |
| MainActivity | Preferences | Reads and writes itak_prefs | MainActivity.kt getPref, setPref |

## One local game session

| From | To | What crosses | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| App shell | EmulatorActivity | Launch intent naming the game and the core for its system | MainActivity.kt, EmulatorActivity.kt intent extras |
| EmulatorActivity | Core extractor | System name; the staged library file comes back, hash checked | EmulatorActivity.kt extractCore |
| EmulatorActivity | Mobile binding | Load core by file path, then run frame, drain audio, save and load state calls | go_backend/mobile/mobile.go |
| Mobile binding | Native bridge | Every engine call, serialized by one mutex | go_backend/internal/core/native.go |
| Native bridge | Rust core library | Frame steps in; framebuffer, audio samples, and save state bytes out | go_backend/internal/core/native_rust.go |
| Native bridge | Go reference cores | Same calls, only in host tools and cross checks, never in the shipped app | go_backend/internal/core/native_registry.go (gocores tag) |
| EmulatorActivity | Display tick pacing | A one deep permit per TV refresh; the game loop waits for it before each frame (local play only) | EmulatorActivity.kt DisplayTick |
| EmulatorActivity | EmuGLView | requestRender after each produced frame; the renderer pulls the finished frame copy and uploads it as a texture | EmuGLView.kt; bridge frame copy under mutex |
| EmulatorActivity | Audio pipeline | Core audio samples in; resampler when rates differ; cushion holds the lead; track writes to the device output | AudioResampler.kt, AudioCushion.kt, EmuAudioOutput.kt |
| Audio diagnostics | Debug panel | Latency, lead, stretch, underruns, starved time | AudioDiag.kt; EmulatorActivity.kt buildDebugStatsText |
| SNES core | Debug panel | 128 DSP register bytes, shown only when the core returns exactly 128 | native_rust.go DspRegs; EmulatorActivity.kt |
| EmulatorActivity | Save state file | Writes on Save Game, on the 60 second auto save, and on clean exit; reads on Load Game and on Continue | EmulatorActivity.kt |
| EmulatorActivity | Resume prompt | Save existence check at launch; the player choice decides load, fresh boot, or backup restore | EmulatorActivity.kt maybeOfferResume |
| EmulatorActivity | Play stats file | Play count up at session start; seconds added at session end | EmulatorActivity.kt statsBegin, statsEnd |
| EmulatorActivity | Stats service | Per game totals posted at session end; the server keeps the greater totals | netplay/internal/stats/ |
| Switchguard | Saves tree | One time copy aside before the first Rust core serves an install | go_backend/internal/switchguard/switchguard.go |

## Netplay and watching

| From | To | What crosses | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| App shell (Online tab) | Lobby server | Lobby list, host and join, friends, presence | go_backend/mobile/netplay.go; netplay/internal/lobby/, friends/ |
| EmulatorActivity | Net session (Go side) | Room join, seat claim, roster, lockstep steps | go_backend/internal/netsession/ |
| Net session | WebSocket hub | Signaling and input steps relayed peer to peer; both sides run the same core and game locally | netplay/internal/ws/, server/ |
| Host session | Spectators | State snapshots and chat for watchers; watchers send no game input | go_backend/internal/netsession/watch.go |
| EmulatorActivity | Chat panel | Text chat for players and watchers in a match | go_backend/internal/netsession/chat.go |
| Lobby server | Matches service | Match records as games are set up and finished | netplay/internal/matches/ |
| Voice signaling | Lobby relay | Signaling messages only; voice media has no wire yet (PLANNED) | go_backend/internal/netsession/signal.go |

## Streams

| From | To | What crosses | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| App shell (Newsmax and Patriots tabs) | Stream player | The chosen stream tile opens the player | flutter_ui/lib/main.dart |
| Stream player | arcade.itak.live embed page | The player frames the embed from a real https page, which is what the video host requires | StreamPlayerActivity.kt |

## Reports, updates, and builds

| From | To | What crosses | Source |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| App (Dart and Kotlin chute) | Debug chute service | Labelled debug reports when Debug reports is on | flutter_ui/lib/debug_chute.dart; DebugChute.kt; netplay/internal/debugchute/ |
| This repo | Autobuild pipeline | Every push; a pubspec version rise triggers a build | tools/autobuild-server.sh |
| Staged Rust libraries | Autobuild pipeline | The six core libraries are copied into the app fresh on every build | tools/autobuild-server.sh |
| Autobuild pipeline | Update feed | The built APK and version.json are published together | netplay/internal/appdist/ |
| Update feed | App shell | Version check; the app downloads the APK and hands it to the system installer | flutter_ui/lib/main.dart |
| dl.itak.live | Player devices | Manual downloads and setup categories for family installs | External service |

plugins {

}

android {
    namespace = "net.itak.itak_gaming"
    compileSdk = flutter.compileSdkVersion
    ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion

    compileOptions {
        sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_1_8
        targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_1_8
    }

    kotlinOptions {
        jvmTarget = JavaVersion.VERSION_1_8
    }

    defaultConfig {
        applicationId = "net.itak.itak_gaming"
        minSdk = 24
        targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion
        versionCode = flutter.versionCode
        // Display versions drop a trailing .0 patch: David's scheme
        // shows build 62 as 1.61 and the 64-bit launch as 2.0, while
        // pubspec keeps the three-part form pub requires (1.61.0+62).
        versionName = flutter.versionName.replaceAll(/\.0$/, "")

        // 32-bit build for Chromecast HD. The Go backend AAR and bundled
        // cores are armeabi-v7a only.
        ndk {
            abiFilters 'armeabi-v7a'
        }
    }

    buildTypes {
        release {
            // TODO: Add your own signing config for the release build.
            // Signing with the debug keys for now, so `flutter run --release` works.
            signingConfig = signingConfigs.debug
        }
    }
}

flutter {
    source = "../.."
}

dependencies {
    // Go emulation backend (gomobile AAR, armeabi-v7a)
    implementation files('libs/itak_backend.aar')
    // Debug chute: the 15-minute check-in worker (DebugChute.kt)
    implementation "androidx.work:work-runtime:2.9.0"
}

==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/itak_gaming/AudioCushion.kt ====================

package net.itak.itak_gaming

import android.util.Log
import kotlin.math.floor

/**
 * The audio cushion: keeps the AudioTrack fed through heavy screens.
 *
 * The problem it solves. On a heavy screen (the SNES Zelda title and
 * file select are the measured case) a frame takes longer to emulate
 * than the frame budget, so the core produces samples slower than
 * real time for seconds at a stretch (about 95.5 percent on the
 * file-select stretch). The samples themselves are clean; the stream
 * simply arrives late, the track drains its small bank, and the DAC
 * starves in bursts. That starvation is the tearing/warbling sound.
 *
 * Why not just a bigger buffer: a sustained rate deficit eats any
 * fixed bank (the measured stretch is short about 26,000 samples,
 * over 800 ms of audio), and banking that much in steady state would
 * delay every sound by the same amount. The cushion instead defends
 * the bank that already exists: a streaming resampler sits between
 * the drained PCM and the track, and while production runs behind it
 * stretches the stream (more output frames per input frame, which is
 * a slight pitch/tempo drop) so consumption slows to match
 * production and the track never runs dry. When frames recover, the
 * stretch eases back to exactly 1.0, where the resampler is a
 * bit-exact pass-through: no sample is altered in steady state, the
 * lead target sits under the existing audio-gate cap, and steady
 * state sound delay is unchanged. Only the presentation layer is
 * involved; the core's production, content, saves and netplay state
 * are untouched.
 *
 * The controller (this build). Two earlier laws each failed one of
 * the two test shapes. The band regulator (through 1.95) protected
 * against starvation but had no memory of the sustained deficit, so
 * on bursty content it overshot to the stretch cap on every
 * recovery and cycled: a pitch swing of up to about 1.3 semitones
 * every few seconds, audible even when nothing starved. The
 * proportional tracker (1.96) parked perfectly on steady content
 * but capped its own emergency guard at the tracker's current
 * target, and at a sudden heavy screen the target still described
 * the previous light screen for a second or two, so the guard
 * bound while the lead crashed and the stream starved MORE than
 * the band law had on the same content (both proven on David's
 * TV, 2026-11-03). This law keeps the tracker as the only governor
 * at a healthy lead and gives a low lead to a fast guard with no
 * target cap:
 *
 *   - A one-second mean of the lead maps to a target stretch: at
 *     the 1750-frame setpoint the target is 1.0, and each frame of
 *     mean shortfall asks for a little more, up to the 1.08 cap.
 *     At the matching stretch the lead holds at the setpoint and
 *     nothing hunts: the operating point is a true equilibrium.
 *   - Lead under 900 (guard zone): the stretch rises at the old
 *     band law's full push rate, uncapped by the target, plus a
 *     direct step under 350. A deficit cliff therefore engages at
 *     once, exactly like the proven band protection.
 *   - Lead 900 to 1500 (shelf): the stretch may rise fast, but
 *     only up to the tracker's target, so a recovery hands over to
 *     the park instead of slamming the cap.
 *   - Lead at or above 1500: the stretch glides toward the target
 *     (0.03/s up, 0.01/s down, 0.03/s down when far above the
 *     target, which is clear overshoot).
 *
 * Host simulation of this exact pipeline (game loop pacing, gate,
 * drain, track, DAC) across steady, step, breathing, onset, and
 * bursty traces at both the 32,040 and 44,100 shapes: the law
 * starved zero everywhere inside the coverage class, matched the
 * band law at the 7.5 percent coverage edge, beat it on hard
 * bursts, and held the steady 3 percent stretch wander at 0.0002
 * against the band law's 0.0320, parking at the exact need
 * (1.0309 for a 3 percent deficit). The release dwell from 1.85 is
 * retained unchanged: after a release the stretch is capped at
 * 1.001 for 250 ms unless the lead falls to the emergency line.
 *
 * Diagnostics: engaging and releasing are logged with the lead and
 * stretch, underrun episodes are counted (with an estimate of the
 * starved time) and logged throttled, and a session summary lands
 * when the stretch releases or the cushion is reset after use.
 *
 * Two roles since 1.95. On the legacy path (cores whose track
 * opens at the core rate) this class is converter and controller
 * together: feed(), update(), convert(). On the resampled path
 * (SNES, GBA) it is the controller only: the audio thread calls
 * update() with the resampler's backlog as queuedFrames and hands
 * currentStretch to AudioResampler, which applies the stretch
 * inside its sinc conversion. The linear interpolation in
 * convert() below does not touch the SNES or GBA stream at all.
 */
class AudioCushion {

    companion object {
        private const val TAG = "iTaKEmu"

        // Controller constants, in frames at the core's sample rate
        // (the tuned case is SNES: 32,040 Hz, gate cap 2400 frames).
        // See the class header for the law and its evidence.
        private const val SETPOINT = 1750.0      // mean-lead setpoint
        private const val TRACK_GAIN = 0.12      // stretch per full setpoint of mean shortfall
        private const val MEAN_TAU_S = 1.0       // lead mean time constant, seconds
        private const val GUARD_LEAD = 900.0     // below: uncapped fast guard
        private const val SHELF_LEAD = 1500.0    // below: fast rise, target capped
        private const val CRIT_LEAD = 350.0      // below: guard adds a direct step
        private const val GUARD_RATE = 0.10      // guard push rate, 1/s (the shipped band slew)
        private const val CRIT_STEP = 0.02       // direct step per update in the critical zone
        private const val SLEW_UP = 0.03         // tracker rise at a healthy lead, 1/s
        private const val SLEW_DN = 0.01         // tracker fall near the target, 1/s
        private const val SLEW_DN_FAR = 0.03     // tracker fall when far above the target, 1/s
        private const val FAR_MARGIN = 0.02      // "far above target" threshold
        private const val STRETCH_MAX = 1.08     // hardest stretch

        // A stretch this close to 1.0 counts as released: at 32 kHz
        // it is a fraction of a percent of pitch, and parking the
        // controller exactly on 1.0 is what makes steady state
        // bit-exact again.
        private const val ENGAGE_AT = 1.002
        private const val RELEASE_AT = 1.0005

        // Release dwell (1.85). A real session on the Missouri
        // stick (2026-11-02) showed the controller engaging and
        // releasing about a dozen times in 14 seconds while the
        // lead hovered at the band edge: each cycle is a small
        // pitch wobble. After a release, the stretch is capped at
        // DWELL_STRETCH_CAP (a tenth of a percent, about 2 cents
        // of pitch, inaudible) for RELEASE_DWELL_NS, so band-edge
        // noise cannot immediately re-engage it. The cap lifts
        // early if the lead falls to DWELL_EMERGENCY_LEAD, so a
        // genuine deficit still engages at once. Host simulation
        // (completed 2026-11-02, after the 1.85 ship; DWELL.md in
        // the cushion rig): the file-select trace is numerically
        // identical with the dwell on, zero starved, and a
        // retrigger inside the window is capped at 1.001, which
        // halves the engagement rate on periodic chatter.
        private const val RELEASE_DWELL_NS = 250_000_000L
        private const val DWELL_STRETCH_CAP = 1.001
        private const val DWELL_EMERGENCY_LEAD = 1200.0

        // Runaway guard on the source queue, the same numbers the
        // audio thread always used: past 128 KB queued, keep only
        // the newest 64 KB. Production is gated by the track lead,
        // so reaching this means something upstream is deeply wrong;
        // dropping the oldest audio beats OOMing the screen.
        private const val QUEUE_MAX_BYTES = 131072
        private const val QUEUE_KEEP_BYTES = 65536

        private const val BYTES_PER_FRAME = 4    // stereo int16
    }

    // Source queue: drained PCM waiting for conversion.
    private var src = ByteArray(QUEUE_MAX_BYTES * 2)
    private var srcHead = 0          // frame index of the queue head
    private var srcLen = 0           // frames currently queued

    // Resampler read position, in frames relative to srcHead.
    private var pos = 0.0

    // Controller state.
    private var stretch = 1.0
    private var meanLead = 0.0
    private var meanInit = false
    private var lastUpdateNs = 0L
    private var engaged = false
    private var engagedNs = 0L
    private var peakStretch = 1.0
    private var lastReleaseNs = 0L

    // Underrun accounting: an underrun is the DAC demanding samples
    // while the track lead is empty and the cushion has nothing to
    // convert. Armed only after the first real chunk flows, so the
    // track's startup transient never counts.
    private var armed = false
    private var starving = false
    private var underrunEpisodes = 0L
    private var starvedMsEstimate = 0.0
    private var lastUnderrunLogNs = 0L

    private var guardTrims = 0L

    // Session-cumulative mirrors of the episodic counters above.
    // logSummary() zeroes the episodic pair at every release, which
    // is right for log lines but wrong for an end-of-session total;
    // these accumulate across the whole session and are cleared
    // only by reset(). Read them through diagTotals().
    private var sessionUnderrunEpisodes = 0L
    private var sessionStarvedMs = 0.0
    private var sessionPeakStretch = 1.0

    /** Snapshot of the session-cumulative counters, for AudioDiag. */
    data class SessionTotals(
        val underrunEpisodes: Long,
        val starvedMs: Double,
        val guardTrims: Long,
        val peakStretch: Double,
    )

    /** The controller's lead target, in core-rate frames. */
    fun diagLeadTargetFrames(): Double = SETPOINT

    /** The session totals as they stand right now; never resets. */
    fun diagTotals(): SessionTotals = SessionTotals(
        underrunEpisodes = sessionUnderrunEpisodes,
        starvedMs = sessionStarvedMs,
        guardTrims = guardTrims,
        peakStretch = sessionPeakStretch,
    )

    /** Current stretch factor (1.0 = pass-through). */
    val currentStretch: Double
        get() = stretch

    /** Drop all queued audio and return the controller to rest. */
    fun reset() {
        if (engaged || peakStretch > 1.0 || underrunEpisodes > 0) {
            logSummary("reset")
        }
        srcHead = 0
        srcLen = 0
        pos = 0.0
        stretch = 1.0
        meanLead = 0.0
        meanInit = false
        lastUpdateNs = 0L
        engaged = false
        peakStretch = 1.0
        lastReleaseNs = 0L
        armed = false
        starving = false
        underrunEpisodes = 0
        starvedMsEstimate = 0.0
        lastUnderrunLogNs = 0L
        guardTrims = 0
        sessionUnderrunEpisodes = 0
        sessionStarvedMs = 0.0
        sessionPeakStretch = 1.0
    }

    /** Queue drained PCM (little-endian stereo int16) for conversion. */
    fun feed(chunk: ByteArray) {
        if (chunk.isEmpty()) return
        val frames = chunk.size / BYTES_PER_FRAME
        if (frames == 0) return
        ensureCapacity(frames)
        System.arraycopy(chunk, 0, src, (srcHead + srcLen) * BYTES_PER_FRAME, frames * BYTES_PER_FRAME)
        srcLen += frames
        if (srcLen * BYTES_PER_FRAME > QUEUE_MAX_BYTES) {
            val keep = QUEUE_KEEP_BYTES / BYTES_PER_FRAME
            val drop = srcLen - keep
            srcHead += drop
            srcLen = keep
            // The frames the read position pointed at just moved
            // down by `drop`; shift pos with them (clamped: if it
            // pointed into the dropped span, restart at the head).
            pos = maxOf(0.0, pos - drop)
            guardTrims++
            if (guardTrims == 1L) {
                Log.w(TAG, "audio cushion: source queue runaway, trimmed to newest ${QUEUE_KEEP_BYTES} bytes")
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Advance the controller. Called on every audio-thread pass with
     * the current track lead (accepted minus played frames), so the
     * gains work in real time regardless of the pass cadence.
     *
     * queuedFrames is the conversion backlog the underrun test
     * should look at: on the legacy path the caller leaves the
     * default and this class's own queue is used; on the resampled
     * path (controller-only role) the caller passes the
     * resampler's backlog instead.
     */
    fun update(leadFrames: Long, nowNs: Long, queuedFrames: Int = -1) {
        if (lastUpdateNs == 0L) {
            lastUpdateNs = nowNs
            meanLead = leadFrames.toDouble()
            meanInit = true
            return
        }
        // Cap dt: a pause or a stalled thread must not let the
        // controller integrate a huge step on resume. The slew
        // limits below already bound the visible effect; this keeps
        // the underrun estimate honest too.
        val dt = ((nowNs - lastUpdateNs).coerceAtMost(100_000_000L)) / 1e9
        lastUpdateNs = nowNs
        if (dt <= 0.0) return
        if (!meanInit) {
            meanLead = leadFrames.toDouble()
            meanInit = true
        }

        val lead = leadFrames.toDouble()
        val was = stretch
        val a = dt / MEAN_TAU_S
        meanLead += a * (lead - meanLead)
        val shortfall = ((SETPOINT - meanLead) / SETPOINT).coerceIn(0.0, 1.0)
        val target = (1.0 + shortfall * TRACK_GAIN).coerceIn(1.0, STRETCH_MAX)

        when {
            lead < GUARD_LEAD -> {
                // Guard zone: the shipped band push, uncapped by
                // the target, plus a direct step when critical.
                stretch = minOf(STRETCH_MAX, stretch + GUARD_RATE * dt)
                if (lead < CRIT_LEAD) {
                    stretch = minOf(STRETCH_MAX, stretch + CRIT_STEP)
                }
            }
            lead < SHELF_LEAD -> {
                // Shelf: fast rise, but only up to the target, so
                // a recovery hands over to the park.
                if (stretch < target) {
                    stretch = minOf(target, stretch + GUARD_RATE * dt)
                } else if (stretch > target) {
                    val dn = if (stretch - target > FAR_MARGIN) SLEW_DN_FAR else SLEW_DN
                    stretch = maxOf(target, stretch - dn * dt)
                }
            }
            else -> {
                // Healthy lead: the tracker alone governs.
                if (stretch < target) {
                    stretch = minOf(target, stretch + SLEW_UP * dt)
                } else if (stretch > target) {
                    val dn = if (stretch - target > FAR_MARGIN) SLEW_DN_FAR else SLEW_DN
                    stretch = maxOf(target, stretch - dn * dt)
                }
            }
        }
        stretch = stretch.coerceIn(1.0, STRETCH_MAX)
        // Release dwell: hold the stretch at the inaudible cap for
        // a beat after a release, unless the lead says the deficit
        // is real (see the constants for the evidence).
        if (nowNs - lastReleaseNs < RELEASE_DWELL_NS &&
            leadFrames >= DWELL_EMERGENCY_LEAD &&
            stretch > DWELL_STRETCH_CAP
        ) {
            stretch = DWELL_STRETCH_CAP
        }
        if (stretch > peakStretch) peakStretch = stretch
        if (stretch > sessionPeakStretch) sessionPeakStretch = stretch

        if (!engaged && stretch >= ENGAGE_AT) {
            engaged = true
            engagedNs = nowNs
            Log.i(TAG, "audio cushion engaged: lead=$leadFrames stretch=${fmt(stretch)}")
        } else if (engaged && stretch <= RELEASE_AT) {
            engaged = false
            stretch = 1.0
            lastReleaseNs = nowNs
            // Returning to exactly 1.0: snap the read position to a
            // whole frame (a slip of at most half a frame, once) so
            // pass-through from here is bit-exact.
            pos = floor(pos + 0.5)
            logSummary("released")
        } else if (stretch == 1.0 && was > 1.0) {
            pos = floor(pos + 0.5)
        }

        // A positive lead means converted audio reached the track,
        // which is the same flow convert() arms on; saying so here
        // keeps the accounting armed on the controller-only path
        // too, where convert() never runs.
        if (leadFrames > 0) armed = true

        // Underrun accounting.
        val queued = if (queuedFrames >= 0) queuedFrames else srcLen
        val empty = leadFrames <= 0 && queued < 2
        if (armed && empty) {
            starvedMsEstimate += dt * 1000.0
            sessionStarvedMs += dt * 1000.0
            if (!starving) {
                starving = true
                underrunEpisodes++
                sessionUnderrunEpisodes++
                if (underrunEpisodes == 1L || nowNs - lastUnderrunLogNs > 5_000_000_000L) {
                    lastUnderrunLogNs = nowNs
                    Log.w(TAG, "audio cushion: underrun, track starved (episode $underrunEpisodes, stretch=${fmt(stretch)})")
                }
            }
        } else {
            starving = false
        }
    }

    /**
     * Convert all queued source frames at the current stretch and
     * return the output PCM (possibly empty). One source frame is
     * always held back as the interpolation lookahead; it converts
     * on a later call once a successor exists.
     */
    fun convert(): ByteArray {
        if (srcLen < 2) return ByteArray(0)
        val estFrames = ((srcLen - 1) * stretch).toInt() + 2
        val out = ByteArray(estFrames * BYTES_PER_FRAME)
        var outFrames = 0
        val step = 1.0 / stretch
        while (floor(pos).toInt() + 1 < srcLen) {
            val i0 = floor(pos).toInt()
            val frac = pos - i0
            val o = outFrames * BYTES_PER_FRAME
            if (frac == 0.0) {
                // Whole-frame read: copy verbatim. This is also the
                // steady-state path (stretch parked at exactly 1.0),
                // which is what makes pass-through bit-exact.
                System.arraycopy(src, (srcHead + i0) * BYTES_PER_FRAME, out, o, BYTES_PER_FRAME)
            } else {
                for (ch in 0..1) {
                    val a = sampleAt(i0, ch)
                    val b = sampleAt(i0 + 1, ch)
                    val v = (a + (b - a) * frac).toInt()
                    val off = o + ch * 2
                    out[off] = (v and 0xFF).toByte()
                    out[off + 1] = ((v shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
                }
            }
            pos += step
            outFrames++
        }
        val drop = floor(pos).toInt()
        if (drop > 0) {
            srcHead += drop
            srcLen -= drop
            pos -= drop
            compactIfNeeded()
        }
        if (outFrames > 0) armed = true
        return if (outFrames == estFrames) out else out.copyOf(outFrames * BYTES_PER_FRAME)
    }

    private fun sampleAt(frame: Int, ch: Int): Int {
        val off = (srcHead + frame) * BYTES_PER_FRAME + ch * 2
        return (src[off + 1].toInt() shl 8) or (src[off].toInt() and 0xFF)
    }

    private fun ensureCapacity(addFrames: Int) {
        val need = (srcHead + srcLen + addFrames) * BYTES_PER_FRAME
        if (need <= src.size) return
        val remaining = srcLen * BYTES_PER_FRAME
        if ((srcLen + addFrames) * BYTES_PER_FRAME <= src.size) {
            // Fits once the consumed head space is reclaimed.
            System.arraycopy(src, srcHead * BYTES_PER_FRAME, src, 0, remaining)
        } else {
            val bigger = ByteArray(maxOf(src.size * 2, (srcLen + addFrames) * BYTES_PER_FRAME))
            System.arraycopy(src, srcHead * BYTES_PER_FRAME, bigger, 0, remaining)
            src = bigger
        }
        srcHead = 0
        // pos is relative to srcHead and the frames it points at
        // moved with the copy, so pos itself is unchanged.
    }

    private fun compactIfNeeded() {
        if (srcHead < 16384) return
        val remaining = srcLen * BYTES_PER_FRAME
        System.arraycopy(src, srcHead * BYTES_PER_FRAME, src, 0, remaining)
        srcHead = 0
        // pos is relative to srcHead; the frames it pointed at moved
        // with the copy, so pos itself is unchanged.
    }

    private fun logSummary(reason: String) {
        val engagedS = if (engagedNs > 0) (lastUpdateNs - engagedNs) / 1e9 else 0.0
        Log.i(
            TAG,
            "audio cushion $reason: peak stretch=${fmt(peakStretch)}" +
                " engaged=${"%.1f".format(engagedS)}s underruns=$underrunEpisodes" +
                " starved~${starvedMsEstimate.toInt()}ms guardTrims=$guardTrims"
        )
        engagedNs = 0L
        peakStretch = stretch
        underrunEpisodes = 0
        starvedMsEstimate = 0.0
    }

    private fun fmt(v: Double): String = "%.4f".format(v)
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/itak_gaming/AudioDiag.kt ====================

package net.itak.itak_gaming

import android.content.Context
import android.util.Log
import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.io.File

/**
 * Audio session diagnostics: the measuring half of the sound
 * debugging set (ordered by David 2026-11-02, after a Zelda SNES
 * session where the sound audibly lagged the picture and the
 * existing debug report could prove the stream never starved but
 * could not say how late it was).
 *
 * What it adds over the log lines the path already emits:
 *
 * - A session header: which core and game, the core rate, the
 *   track rate, whether the in-app resampler is in the path, the
 *   track's buffer as actually built (frames and milliseconds),
 *   the cushion target in milliseconds, the device output rate,
 *   and the output device the track was routed to.
 * - A measured output latency series, sampled from the track's
 *   own presentation timestamps while the session runs: how many
 *   frames sit between what the app has written and what the
 *   device says it has presented, in milliseconds. This is the
 *   delay figure the old report could only be guessed at by
 *   adding buffer sizes together.
 * - A lead trace: the same track lead the cushion regulates,
 *   bucketed over the session (min / average / max per bucket,
 *   in milliseconds), so reserve depth is a record instead of
 *   an inference from engage and release lines.
 * - A stretch histogram: how many seconds the session spent at
 *   each cushion stretch band, plus the cushion's own session
 *   totals (underruns, starved time, guard trims) taken at the
 *   end without being reset by the per-engagement summaries.
 *
 * The finished summary is a JSON object. EmulatorActivity saves
 * it to disk at session end; DebugChute attaches the most recent
 * one to every full report under the key "audioDiag", so the
 * numbers ride the chute that already exists instead of needing
 * a new channel.
 *
 * Threading: begin() is called before the audio thread starts,
 * sample() only from the audio thread, finish() after the game
 * thread has been joined. Methods are synchronized anyway; the
 * sampling cadence is a few times a second, so contention is
 * not a consideration.
 */
class AudioDiag {

    companion object {
        private const val TAG = "iTaKEmu"
        private const val DIR = "diag"
        private const val FILE = "audio_last.json"

        // Lead buckets: one per 5 seconds of session, the last
        // 36 kept (3 minutes). Older buckets are folded into the
        // session-wide lead statistics, which are always kept.
        private const val BUCKET_NS = 5_000_000_000L
        private const val MAX_BUCKETS = 36

        /** Where the last finished session summary lives. */
        fun storeFile(ctx: Context): File = File(File(ctx.filesDir, DIR), FILE)

        /** Save a finished session summary for the chute. */
        fun saveLast(ctx: Context, summary: JSONObject) {
            try {
                val file = storeFile(ctx)
                file.parentFile?.mkdirs()
                file.writeText(summary.toString())
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                Log.w(TAG, "audio diag save failed", e)
            }
        }

        /** The most recent finished session summary, if any. */
        fun loadLast(ctx: Context): JSONObject? {
            return try {
                val file = storeFile(ctx)
                if (file.exists()) JSONObject(file.readText()) else null
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                Log.w(TAG, "audio diag load failed", e)
                null
            }
        }
    }

    // ---- session header -------------------------------------------------
    private var active = false
    private var begun = false
    private var startedNs = 0L
    private var system = ""
    private var game = ""
    private var coreRate = 0
    private var trackRate = 0
    private var resamplerInPath = false
    private var trackBufferFrames = 0
    private var cushionTargetMs = 0.0
    private var deviceOutputRate = 0
    private var routedDevice = ""

    // ---- lead (reserve depth), milliseconds at the track rate -----------
    private var leadMin = Double.MAX_VALUE
    private var leadMax = 0.0
    private var leadSum = 0.0
    private var leadCount = 0L
    private var bucketStartNs = 0L
    private var bucketMin = Double.MAX_VALUE
    private var bucketMax = 0.0
    private var bucketSum = 0.0
    private var bucketCount = 0L
    private val buckets = ArrayDeque<JSONArray>()

    // ---- measured output latency, milliseconds --------------------------
    private var latMin = Double.MAX_VALUE
    private var latMax = 0.0
    private var latSum = 0.0
    private var latCount = 0L
    private var latLast = 0.0

    // ---- stretch histogram, seconds per band ----------------------------
    // bands: exactly 1.0 / (1.0, 1.02] / (1.02, 1.05] / (1.05, 1.08]
    private val stretchBandsS = DoubleArray(4)
    private var lastSampleNs = 0L

    /**
     * Open a session. [trackBufferFrames] is the size the built
     * track reports for itself, not the requested size; pass 0
     * when the track could not report one.
     */
    @Synchronized
    fun begin(
        system: String,
        game: String,
        coreRate: Int,
        trackRate: Int,
        resamplerInPath: Boolean,
        trackBufferFrames: Int,
        cushionTargetMs: Double,
        deviceOutputRate: Int,
        routedDevice: String,
    ) {
        this.system = system
        this.game = game
        this.coreRate = coreRate
        this.trackRate = trackRate
        this.resamplerInPath = resamplerInPath
        this.trackBufferFrames = trackBufferFrames
        this.cushionTargetMs = cushionTargetMs
        this.deviceOutputRate = deviceOutputRate
        this.routedDevice = routedDevice
        startedNs = System.nanoTime()
        bucketStartNs = startedNs
        lastSampleNs = startedNs
        active = true
        begun = true
        Log.i(
            TAG,
            "audio session: system=$system game=$game core=${coreRate}Hz" +
                " track=${trackRate}Hz resampler=${if (resamplerInPath) "in-app" else "off"}" +
                " trackBuffer=${trackBufferFrames}f" +
                " (${if (trackRate > 0) "%.1f".format(trackBufferFrames * 1000.0 / trackRate) else "?"}ms)" +
                " cushionTarget=${"%.1f".format(cushionTargetMs)}ms" +
                " output=${deviceOutputRate}Hz routed=$routedDevice"
        )
    }

    /**
     * One sample from the audio thread. [leadMs] is the track
     * lead (written minus presented frames) in milliseconds,
     * [latencyMs] the timestamp-measured output latency in
     * milliseconds (pass a negative value when the timestamp
     * call failed, the sample is then skipped), [stretch] the
     * cushion's current stretch factor.
     */
    @Synchronized
    fun sample(leadMs: Double, latencyMs: Double, stretch: Double, nowNs: Long) {
        if (!active) return
        // Lead, session-wide and per bucket.
        leadMin = minOf(leadMin, leadMs)
        leadMax = maxOf(leadMax, leadMs)
        leadSum += leadMs
        leadCount++
        if (bucketCount > 0 && nowNs - bucketStartNs >= BUCKET_NS) {
            val b = JSONArray()
            b.put((bucketStartNs - startedNs) / 1_000_000_000.0)
            b.put(bucketMin)
            b.put(bucketSum / bucketCount)
            b.put(bucketMax)
            buckets.addLast(b)
            while (buckets.size > MAX_BUCKETS) buckets.removeFirst()
            bucketStartNs = nowNs
            bucketMin = Double.MAX_VALUE
            bucketMax = 0.0
            bucketSum = 0.0
            bucketCount = 0
        }
        bucketMin = minOf(bucketMin, leadMs)
        bucketMax = maxOf(bucketMax, leadMs)
        bucketSum += leadMs
        bucketCount++
        // Latency, when the sample is real.
        if (latencyMs >= 0.0) {
            latMin = minOf(latMin, latencyMs)
            latMax = maxOf(latMax, latencyMs)
            latSum += latencyMs
            latCount++
            latLast = latencyMs
        }
        // Stretch histogram: credit the time since the previous
        // sample to the band the stretch sits in now.
        val dtS = (nowNs - lastSampleNs) / 1e9
        if (dtS > 0.0 && dtS < 2.0) {
            val band = when {
                stretch <= 1.0005 -> 0
                stretch <= 1.02 -> 1
                stretch <= 1.05 -> 2
                else -> 3
            }
            stretchBandsS[band] += dtS
        }
        lastSampleNs = nowNs
    }

    /**
     * Close the session and build its summary. The cushion
     * totals are passed in by the caller (they live in the
     * cushion); [framesDelivered] is the audio thread's own
     * count of frames the track accepted.
     */
    @Synchronized
    fun finish(
        underrunEpisodes: Long,
        starvedMs: Double,
        guardTrims: Long,
        peakStretch: Double,
        framesDelivered: Long,
        outputTrims: Long,
        outputTrimmedFrames: Long,
    ): JSONObject {
        active = false
        val o = JSONObject()
        // False when the session never got a track (the core
        // reported no rate): the summary then documents the
        // failure instead of a measurement.
        o.put("sessionBegun", begun)
        o.put("system", system)
        o.put("game", game)
        o.put("coreRate", coreRate)
        o.put("trackRate", trackRate)
        o.put("resamplerInPath", resamplerInPath)
        o.put("trackBufferFrames", trackBufferFrames)
        if (trackRate > 0) {
            o.put("trackBufferMs", trackBufferFrames * 1000.0 / trackRate)
        }
        o.put("cushionTargetMs", cushionTargetMs)
        o.put("deviceOutputRate", deviceOutputRate)
        o.put("routedDevice", routedDevice)
        o.put("durationS", (System.nanoTime() - startedNs) / 1e9)
        o.put("framesDelivered", framesDelivered)
        if (leadCount > 0) {
            val lead = JSONObject()
            lead.put("minMs", leadMin)
            lead.put("avgMs", leadSum / leadCount)
            lead.put("maxMs", leadMax)
            o.put("lead", lead)
        }
        if (buckets.isNotEmpty() || bucketCount > 0) {
            val arr = JSONArray()
            for (b in buckets) arr.put(b)
            if (bucketCount > 0) {
                val b = JSONArray()
                b.put((bucketStartNs - startedNs) / 1_000_000_000.0)
                b.put(bucketMin)
                b.put(bucketSum / bucketCount)
                b.put(bucketMax)
                arr.put(b)
            }
            // Each bucket: [startSecond, minMs, avgMs, maxMs].
            o.put("leadBuckets", arr)
        }
        if (latCount > 0) {
            val lat = JSONObject()
            lat.put("minMs", latMin)
            lat.put("avgMs", latSum / latCount)
            lat.put("maxMs", latMax)
            lat.put("lastMs", latLast)
            lat.put("samples", latCount)
            o.put("outputLatency", lat)
        }
        val bands = JSONArray()
        for (v in stretchBandsS) bands.put(v)
        o.put("stretchSecondsByBand", bands)
        o.put("peakStretch", peakStretch)
        o.put("underrunEpisodes", underrunEpisodes)
        o.put("starvedMs", starvedMs)
        o.put("guardTrims", guardTrims)
        o.put("outputTrims", outputTrims)
        o.put("outputTrimmedFrames", outputTrimmedFrames)
        Log.i(
            TAG,
            "audio session end: game=$game" +
                (if (latCount > 0) " latency avg=${"%.1f".format(latSum / latCount)}ms" +
                    " max=${"%.1f".format(latMax)}ms" else " latency unmeasured") +
                (if (leadCount > 0) " lead avg=${"%.1f".format(leadSum / leadCount)}ms" else "") +
                " underruns=$underrunEpisodes starved~${starvedMs.toInt()}ms" +
                " outputTrims=$outputTrims"
        )
        return o
    }
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/itak_gaming/AudioResampler.kt ====================

package net.itak.itak_gaming

import android.util.Log
import kotlin.math.PI
import kotlin.math.sin
import kotlin.math.sqrt

/**
 * The in-app sample rate converter: turns core-rate audio into the
 * device output rate inside the app, at a quality we choose.
 *
 * Why this exists. The SNES core produces audio at 32,000 Hz and the
 * GBA at 32,768 Hz, but the stick's output stage runs at 48,000 Hz.
 * Before 1.85 the app opened its audio track at the core rate and
 * let the stick's mixer do the conversion. That converter's quality
 * is the platform's choice, not ours: Android's own documentation
 * warns its resamplers can add aliasing noise, the quality rung a
 * given track gets depends on load and vendor settings, and no app
 * API can see or change it. Every respected SNES emulator instead
 * converts inside itself with a filter it picked. This module is
 * that conversion, ours.
 *
 * The algorithm is a table-driven windowed-sinc resampler, proven
 * on the build server before it was ported (the Python prototype
 * is the spec: itak-speed/resampler-proto/resample.py). For each
 * output sample, the position in input samples advances by the
 * exact rational step inRate/outRate using integer math only, so
 * there is zero drift.
 *
 * Dynamic rate control (1.95): the step can be scaled by a
 * stretch factor set from outside (see setStretch). The audio
 * cushion's controller computes the stretch from the track lead,
 * and applying it here, inside the sinc conversion, replaces the
 * cushion's old separate linear-interpolation stretching stage:
 * the drift and deficit correction now happens at full sinc
 * quality instead of through a second, cheaper interpolator. The
 * step division is carried fractionally, so a stretch parked at
 * exactly 1.0 reproduces the original integer stepping
 * bit-for-bit, and at any other setting the effective ratio is
 * exact on average with no accumulating drift. The kernel is 128 input taps of a Kaiser
 * windowed sinc (beta 7.9) with cutoff at 0.98 of the lower
 * Nyquist, quantized to 4096 phases; every table row is
 * renormalized to sum to exactly 1.0, so DC gain is exact at every
 * phase. One table serves every ratio because the kernel is
 * defined in input-sample units.
 *
 * Measured against the prototype (32,000 to 48,000): the clean
 * Zelda capture's band energies match the original within
 * 0.04 dB, image energy sits at about -80 dB, and on a harsh
 * synthetic signal (bright square arpeggio plus a 1 to 15 kHz
 * sweep) the error against the ideal is 65 to 72 dB lower than
 * linear interpolation or zero-order hold. The GBA's awkward
 * 375:256 ratio lands within about 2.5 dB of the SNES figures.
 * Cost is 128 multiply-accumulates per output sample per channel,
 * about 12 million a second for stereo at 48 kHz, plus the shared
 * 2 MiB table, generated once per process.
 *
 * Streaming: an output sample depends only on the 128 input
 * samples around its position and on the integer accumulator, so
 * the converter is chunk-safe by construction (the prototype
 * matched its offline path bit-for-bit fed in frame-sized
 * chunks). Algorithmic latency is 64 input samples of lookahead,
 * 2.0 ms at the SNES rate. Presentation layer only: the core's
 * production, saves, and netplay state are untouched.
 */
class AudioResampler(private val inRate: Int, private val outRate: Int) {

    companion object {
        private const val TAG = "iTaKEmu"

        // Port constants: copy from the proven prototype, do not
        // retune without re-running its proofs.
        const val PHASES = 4096
        const val TAPS = 128
        private const val HALF = TAPS / 2
        private const val CUTOFF = 0.98
        private const val KAISER_BETA = 7.9

        private const val BYTES_PER_FRAME = 4 // stereo int16

        // Hard ceiling for the dynamic stretch, a safety net only:
        // the cushion controller clamps itself to 1.08.
        private const val STRETCH_LIMIT = 1.10

        /**
         * The shared kernel table, built once per process on first
         * use. Generation evaluates 4096 x 128 windowed sinc
         * coefficients in double precision, then stores floats.
         */
        val table: FloatArray by lazy {
            val started = System.nanoTime()
            val built = buildTable()
            Log.i(TAG, "audio resampler table built in ${(System.nanoTime() - started) / 1_000_000}ms")
            built
        }

        private fun buildTable(): FloatArray {
            val fc = 0.5 * CUTOFF // cycles per input sample
            val i0Beta = besselI0(KAISER_BETA)
            val out = FloatArray(PHASES * TAPS)
            val row = DoubleArray(TAPS)
            for (q in 0 until PHASES) {
                val frac = q.toDouble() / PHASES
                var sum = 0.0
                for (t in 0 until TAPS) {
                    val d = (t - HALF).toDouble()
                    val x = frac - d
                    // Kaiser window: I0(beta*sqrt(1-(x/half)^2))/I0(beta),
                    // the radicand clamped at 0 exactly as the
                    // prototype clamps it.
                    val rad = 1.0 - (x / HALF) * (x / HALF)
                    val w = besselI0(KAISER_BETA * sqrt(if (rad > 0.0) rad else 0.0)) / i0Beta
                    val s = 2.0 * fc * x
                    val sinc = if (s == 0.0) 1.0 else sin(PI * s) / (PI * s)
                    val h = 2.0 * fc * sinc * w
                    row[t] = h
                    sum += h
                }
                val base = q * TAPS
                for (t in 0 until TAPS) {
                    out[base + t] = (row[t] / sum).toFloat()
                }
            }
            return out
        }

        /** Modified Bessel function I0, power series. */
        private fun besselI0(x: Double): Double {
            val quarter = x * x / 4.0
            var sum = 1.0
            var term = 1.0
            var k = 0
            while (true) {
                k++
                term *= quarter / (k.toDouble() * k.toDouble())
                sum += term
                if (term < sum * 1e-15) break
            }
            return sum
        }
    }

    init {
        require(inRate > 0 && outRate > 0) { "resampler rates must be positive" }
    }

    // Input history: interleaved int16 frames in a linear buffer.
    // The stream is primed with HALF frames of silence standing in
    // for the input before frame 0, exactly the prototype's zero
    // padding, so the first outputs are computed, not skipped.
    private var buf = ShortArray((TAPS + 8192) * 2)
    private var head = 0 // frame index of the oldest buffered frame
    private var len = HALF // frames currently buffered
    private var baseIndex = -HALF.toLong() // absolute input index of the head frame

    // Exact rational position of the next output, as n * inRate.
    private var acc = 0L

    // Dynamic rate control state (1.95). `stretch` is the
    // cushion controller's current factor: while it is above 1.0
    // each output sample advances the input position by
    // inRate/stretch instead of inRate, so the converted stream
    // runs proportionally longer and the track's lead recovers.
    // The division is carried fractionally in stepCarry, so the
    // effective ratio is exact on average and a parked stretch of
    // exactly 1.0 steps by whole inRate increments, identical to
    // the fixed-ratio converter this class shipped as.
    @Volatile private var stretch = 1.0
    private var stepCarry = 0.0

    /**
     * Set the dynamic stretch factor (1.0 = the nominal ratio).
     * Called by the audio thread on every pass with the cushion
     * controller's current value; the controller slew-limits its
     * own changes, so the ratio breathes smoothly.
     */
    fun setStretch(s: Double) {
        stretch = if (s.isFinite()) s.coerceIn(1.0, STRETCH_LIMIT) else 1.0
    }

    /**
     * Input frames that have arrived but that no output window
     * has reached yet: the resampler's real backlog, used by the
     * cushion controller's underrun accounting on this path.
     */
    fun pendingFrames(): Int =
        ((baseIndex + len) - (acc / outRate) - HALF).toInt().coerceAtLeast(0)

    /** Drop all buffered input and restart the position. */
    fun reset() {
        head = 0
        len = HALF
        baseIndex = -HALF.toLong()
        acc = 0L
        stepCarry = 0.0
        buf.fill(0, 0, HALF * 2)
    }

    /**
     * Convert one chunk of core-rate PCM (little-endian stereo
     * int16) to the output rate, returning the converted bytes
     * (possibly empty while the lookahead fills). Chunk boundaries
     * are invisible to the result.
     */
    fun convert(chunk: ByteArray): ByteArray {
        if (chunk.isEmpty()) return ByteArray(0)
        val frames = chunk.size / BYTES_PER_FRAME
        if (frames == 0) return ByteArray(0)
        ensureCapacity(frames)
        var srcOff = 0
        var dst = (head + len) * 2
        for (f in 0 until frames) {
            buf[dst] = ((chunk[srcOff + 1].toInt() shl 8) or (chunk[srcOff].toInt() and 0xFF)).toShort()
            buf[dst + 1] = ((chunk[srcOff + 3].toInt() shl 8) or (chunk[srcOff + 2].toInt() and 0xFF)).toShort()
            srcOff += BYTES_PER_FRAME
            dst += 2
        }
        len += frames

        val lastAvailable = baseIndex + len - 1
        // Estimate the output size, then trim to what was produced.
        // The estimate must use the hard stretch ceiling (11/10 =
        // STRETCH_LIMIT), not the nominal ratio: while the cushion
        // has the stretch engaged, each output consumes FEWER input
        // samples, so one chunk yields up to STRETCH_LIMIT times
        // more outputs than the nominal count. Sizing by the nominal
        // ratio overflowed this array in the audio thread and
        // killed the game (crash on David's TV, 2026-11-03:
        // ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, array length 25312,
        // written at index 25312, stretch 1.0204 at stream start).
        val estOut = ((len.toLong() * outRate * 11) / (inRate * 10)).toInt() + 8
        val out = ByteArray(estOut * BYTES_PER_FRAME)
        var outFrames = 0
        val tab = table
        while (true) {
            val i0 = acc / outRate
            // The window covers inputs [i0 - HALF, i0 + HALF); the
            // newest tap must already have arrived.
            if (i0 + HALF - 1 > lastAvailable) break
            val phase = (((acc % outRate) * PHASES) / outRate).toInt()
            val rowBase = phase * TAPS
            val winStart = (i0 - HALF - baseIndex).toInt() // buffer frame of the oldest tap
            var framePos = (head + winStart) * 2
            var sumL = 0f
            var sumR = 0f
            for (t in 0 until TAPS) {
                val c = tab[rowBase + t]
                sumL += buf[framePos] * c
                sumR += buf[framePos + 1] * c
                framePos += 2
            }
            val o = outFrames * BYTES_PER_FRAME
            val vl = Math.round(sumL).coerceIn(-32768, 32767)
            val vr = Math.round(sumR).coerceIn(-32768, 32767)
            out[o] = (vl and 0xFF).toByte()
            out[o + 1] = ((vl shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
            out[o + 2] = (vr and 0xFF).toByte()
            out[o + 3] = ((vr shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
            outFrames++
            // Advance the position: inRate per output at a
            // stretch of exactly 1.0 (the original integer
            // stepping, bit-for-bit), inRate/stretch with the
            // fraction carried while the cushion is engaged.
            val stepTotal = inRate / stretch + stepCarry
            val stepWhole = stepTotal.toLong()
            stepCarry = stepTotal - stepWhole
            acc += stepWhole
        }
        // Drop input frames no future window can reach: the next
        // window starts at (acc / outRate) - HALF.
        val nextStart = acc / outRate - HALF
        val drop = (nextStart - baseIndex).toInt()
        if (drop > 0) {
            val d = minOf(drop, len)
            head += d
            len -= d
            baseIndex += d
            compactIfNeeded()
        }
        return if (outFrames == estOut) out else out.copyOf(outFrames * BYTES_PER_FRAME)
    }

    private fun ensureCapacity(addFrames: Int) {
        val needFrames = head + len + addFrames
        if (needFrames * 2 <= buf.size) return
        val remaining = len * 2
        if ((len + addFrames) * 2 <= buf.size) {
            System.arraycopy(buf, head * 2, buf, 0, remaining)
        } else {
            val bigger = ShortArray(maxOf(buf.size * 2, (len + addFrames) * 2))
            System.arraycopy(buf, head * 2, bigger, 0, remaining)
            buf = bigger
        }
        head = 0
    }

    private fun compactIfNeeded() {
        if (head < 16384) return
        System.arraycopy(buf, head * 2, buf, 0, len * 2)
        head = 0
    }
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/itak_gaming/DebugChute.kt ====================

package net.itak.itak_gaming

import android.content.Context
import android.os.Build
import android.os.Environment
import android.os.StatFs
import android.util.Log
import androidx.work.Constraints
import androidx.work.ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy
import androidx.work.ExistingWorkPolicy
import androidx.work.NetworkType
import androidx.work.OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder
import androidx.work.PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder
import androidx.work.WorkManager
import androidx.work.Worker
import androidx.work.WorkerParameters
import org.json.JSONArray
import org.json.JSONObject
import java.io.File
import java.io.RandomAccessFile
import java.net.HttpURLConnection
import java.net.URL
import java.security.SecureRandom
import java.text.SimpleDateFormat
import java.util.Date
import java.util.Locale
import java.util.TimeZone
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Debug chute, native half: a WorkManager check-in that pings our
// own server about every 15 minutes (WorkManager's minimum period;
// the stick is mains powered and usually awake). The app only ever
// sends. The ping is tiny: identity, version, model, free storage,
// and the newest few core timing lines. The server answers
// {"want_full_report": true|false}; when true, this same check-in
// immediately uploads the full report (log tail included, reason
// "pull"), which is how a full log is pulled on demand with no
// inbound connection to the stick at all.
//
// Identity and the on/off switch live in the same itak_prefs
// SharedPreferences the Dart side uses: 'install_code' (16 random
// bytes as hex, generated once by whichever side runs first) and
// 'debug_chute' ('0' means off, anything else including unset
// means on). With the switch off the worker is a no-op.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

object DebugChute {
    private const val TAG = "DebugChute"
    private const val SERVER = "https://arcade.itak.live"
    private const val PREFS = "itak_prefs"

    fun enabled(ctx: Context): Boolean {
        val prefs = ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
        return prefs.getString("debug_chute", null) != "0"
    }

    fun installCode(ctx: Context): String {
        val prefs = ctx.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
        val existing = prefs.getString("install_code", null)
        if (existing != null && existing.length == 32 &&
            existing.all { it in '0'..'9' || it in 'a'..'f' || it in 'A'..'F' }
        ) {
            return existing
        }
        val bytes = ByteArray(16)
        SecureRandom().nextBytes(bytes)
        val code = bytes.joinToString("") { "%02x".format(it) }
        prefs.edit().putString("install_code", code).apply()
        return code
    }

    private fun logFile(ctx: Context): File = File(File(ctx.filesDir, "logs"), "itak.log")

    // Last [maxBytes] of the app log file as text ("" when none).
    private fun logTailText(ctx: Context, maxBytes: Long): String {
        val file = logFile(ctx)
        if (!file.exists()) return ""
        val size = file.length()
        val want = minOf(size, maxBytes)
        if (want <= 0) return ""
        val buf = ByteArray(want.toInt())
        RandomAccessFile(file, "r").use { raf ->
            raf.seek(size - want)
            raf.readFully(buf)
        }
        var text = String(buf, Charsets.UTF_8)
        if (want < size) {
            val nl = text.indexOf('\n')
            if (nl >= 0) text = text.substring(nl + 1)
        }
        return text
    }

    // The last [max] "native timing" lines in the app log.
    fun timingLines(ctx: Context, max: Int): List<String> {
        val text = logTailText(ctx, 512 * 1024L)
        if (text.isEmpty()) return emptyList()
        val hits = text.split('\n').filter { it.contains("native timing") }
        return if (hits.size <= max) hits else hits.subList(hits.size - max, hits.size)
    }

    private fun freeStorageMB(): Long {
        return try {
            val fs = StatFs(Environment.getDataDirectory().path)
            fs.availableBytes / (1024 * 1024)
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            -1
        }
    }

    private fun utcNow(): String {
        val fmt = SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'", Locale.US)
        fmt.timeZone = TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC")
        return fmt.format(Date())
    }

    private fun versionInfo(ctx: Context): Pair<String, Int> {
        return try {
            val info = ctx.packageManager.getPackageInfo(ctx.packageName, 0)
            @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
            val code =
                if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 28) info.longVersionCode.toInt() else info.versionCode
            (info.versionName ?: "") to code
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            "" to 0
        }
    }

    private fun baseJson(ctx: Context): JSONObject {
        val (vName, vCode) = versionInfo(ctx)
        val o = JSONObject()
        o.put("install_code", installCode(ctx))
        o.put("versionName", vName)
        o.put("versionCode", vCode)
        o.put("model", Build.MODEL ?: "unknown")
        o.put("sdk", Build.VERSION.SDK_INT)
        val free = freeStorageMB()
        if (free >= 0) o.put("freeStorageMB", free)
        o.put("timestamp", utcNow())
        return o
    }

    // POST JSON; returns (status, body) or null on a network error.
    private fun post(path: String, body: JSONObject): Pair<Int, String>? {
        var conn: HttpURLConnection? = null
        return try {
            conn = (URL(SERVER + path).openConnection() as HttpURLConnection).apply {
                requestMethod = "POST"
                connectTimeout = 15_000
                readTimeout = 15_000
                doOutput = true
                setRequestProperty("Content-Type", "application/json")
                setRequestProperty("User-Agent", "iTaK-Gaming/1.0")
            }
            conn.outputStream.use { it.write(body.toString().toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)) }
            val code = conn.responseCode
            val stream = if (code in 200..299) conn.inputStream else conn.errorStream
            val text = stream?.bufferedReader()?.use { it.readText() } ?: ""
            code to text
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(TAG, "POST $path failed", e)
            null
        } finally {
            conn?.disconnect()
        }
    }

    // One full report upload. True on a 200.
    fun sendFull(ctx: Context, reason: String): Boolean {
        val o = baseJson(ctx)
        o.put("timingLines", JSONArray(timingLines(ctx, 40)))
        o.put("logTail", logTailText(ctx, 120 * 1024L))
        // The most recent finished audio session's diagnostics
        // (see AudioDiag): measured output latency, lead trace,
        // session header and cushion totals. Absent until the
        // first measured session ends on this install.
        val audioDiag = AudioDiag.loadLast(ctx)
        if (audioDiag != null) o.put("audioDiag", audioDiag)
        o.put("reason", reason)
        val res = post("/debug/report", o) ?: return false
        Log.i(TAG, "full report ($reason) -> ${res.first}")
        return res.first == 200
    }

    // One check-in: ping, then the full report too when the server
    // asks for it. True when everything the server wanted is done.
    fun checkIn(ctx: Context): Boolean {
        val o = baseJson(ctx)
        o.put("timingLines", JSONArray(timingLines(ctx, 10)))
        val res = post("/debug/ping", o) ?: return false
        if (res.first != 200) {
            Log.w(TAG, "ping refused: ${res.first}")
            return false
        }
        val want = try {
            JSONObject(res.second).optBoolean("want_full_report", false)
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            false
        }
        Log.i(TAG, "ping ok, want_full_report=$want")
        return if (want) sendFull(ctx, "pull") else true
    }

    // Schedule the 15-minute periodic check-in (kept across app
    // updates) and one immediate check-in per app start, so a
    // fresh install checks in right away and a pending pull is
    // picked up at the next launch at the latest.
    fun enqueue(ctx: Context) {
        try {
            val appCtx = ctx.applicationContext
            val wm = WorkManager.getInstance(appCtx)
            val constraints = Constraints.Builder()
                .setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.CONNECTED)
                .build()
            val periodic = PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<DebugChuteWorker>(15, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
                .setConstraints(constraints)
                .build()
            wm.enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(
                "debug_chute_periodic",
                ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP,
                periodic,
            )
            val now = OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder<DebugChuteWorker>()
                .setConstraints(constraints)
                .build()
            wm.enqueueUniqueWork("debug_chute_now", ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE, now)
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(TAG, "enqueue failed", e)
        }
    }

    // Queue an immediate full report with a caller-chosen reason
    // ("game_exit" when a game session ends, "manual" for the
    // sound screen's send button). The periodic check-in only
    // uploads a full report when the server asks for one; these
    // are the two moments the app itself knows the report is
    // worth sending, so the session the player just finished is
    // the one that arrives. Network work runs in the worker, so
    // callers on the UI thread just enqueue.
    fun enqueueFull(ctx: Context, reason: String) {
        try {
            val appCtx = ctx.applicationContext
            val wm = WorkManager.getInstance(appCtx)
            val constraints = Constraints.Builder()
                .setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.CONNECTED)
                .build()
            val req = OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder<DebugChuteWorker>()
                .setConstraints(constraints)
                .setInputData(
                    androidx.work.Data.Builder().putString("reason", reason).build()
                )
                .build()
            wm.enqueueUniqueWork("debug_chute_full", ExistingWorkPolicy.REPLACE, req)
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(TAG, "enqueueFull failed", e)
        }
    }
}

class DebugChuteWorker(ctx: Context, params: WorkerParameters) : Worker(ctx, params) {
    override fun doWork(): Result {
        val ctx = applicationContext
        if (!DebugChute.enabled(ctx)) return Result.success()
        // A "reason" in the input data means enqueueFull queued
        // this run: send the full report now, no ping round trip.
        val reason = inputData.getString("reason")
        return if (!reason.isNullOrBlank()) {
            if (DebugChute.sendFull(ctx, reason)) Result.success() else Result.retry()
        } else if (DebugChute.checkIn(ctx)) {
            Result.success()
        } else {
            Result.retry()
        }
    }
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/itak_gaming/EmuAudioOutput.kt ====================

package net.itak.itak_gaming

import android.content.Context
import android.media.AudioAttributes
import android.media.AudioFormat
import android.media.AudioManager
import android.media.AudioTrack
import android.util.Log

/**
 * The one place the app's game audio output is described, shared
 * by the emulator screen and the sound test screen so the test
 * exercises the real path instead of a copy of it.
 *
 * Two facts live here: the rate the device itself wants (its
 * native output rate, what the mixer runs at), and how a game
 * audio track is built (game usage, music content type, PCM16
 * stereo, streaming mode, the buffer policy the emulator has
 * always used).
 */
object EmuAudioOutput {

    private const val TAG = "iTaKEmu"

    /** Fallback when the device does not report a native rate. */
    private const val DEFAULT_OUTPUT_RATE = 48000

    /**
     * The device's native output sample rate: the rate its mixer
     * runs at, and the rate an app-side converter should target.
     * Falls back to 48,000 when the property is missing or absurd.
     */
    fun deviceOutputRate(context: Context): Int {
        val manager = context.getSystemService(Context.AUDIO_SERVICE) as? AudioManager
        val raw = try {
            manager?.getProperty(AudioManager.PROPERTY_OUTPUT_SAMPLE_RATE)
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            Log.w(TAG, "output sample rate lookup failed", e)
            null
        }
        val rate = raw?.toIntOrNull() ?: 0
        return if (rate in 8000..192000) rate else DEFAULT_OUTPUT_RATE
    }

    /** Build (but do not start) a game audio track at [rate]. */
    fun buildTrack(rate: Int): AudioTrack {
        val minBuf = AudioTrack.getMinBufferSize(
            rate, AudioFormat.CHANNEL_OUT_STEREO, AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_16BIT
        )
        return AudioTrack.Builder()
            .setAudioAttributes(
                AudioAttributes.Builder()
                    .setUsage(AudioAttributes.USAGE_GAME)
                    .setContentType(AudioAttributes.CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC)
                    .build()
            )
            .setAudioFormat(
                AudioFormat.Builder()
                    .setEncoding(AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_16BIT)
                    .setSampleRate(rate)
                    .setChannelMask(AudioFormat.CHANNEL_OUT_STEREO)
                    .build()
            )
            .setBufferSizeInBytes(maxOf(minBuf * 2, 16384))
            .setTransferMode(AudioTrack.MODE_STREAM)
            .build()
    }
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/itak_gaming/EmuGLView.kt ====================

package net.itak.itak_gaming

import android.content.Context
import android.opengl.GLES20
import android.opengl.GLSurfaceView
import android.util.Log
import mobile.Mobile
import java.nio.ByteBuffer
import java.nio.ByteOrder
import java.nio.FloatBuffer
import javax.microedition.khronos.egl.EGLConfig
import javax.microedition.khronos.opengles.GL10

/** Called once the GL surface exists and frames can be pulled. */
interface TextureListener {
    fun onSurfaceReady()
}

/**
 * OpenGL ES 2.0 view for emulator frames.
 *
 * Each frame is a small texture upload (256x224 for SNES) plus one quad;
 * the GPU does the upscale to the TV. This replaces a software Canvas
 * path that cost 23-76 ms per frame on the Chromecast's CPU.
 */
class EmuGLView(context: Context) : GLSurfaceView(context) {
    private val emuRenderer: EmuRenderer

    init {
        setEGLContextClientVersion(2)
        setEGLConfigChooser(8, 8, 8, 8, 0, 0)
        emuRenderer = EmuRenderer(context as? TextureListener)
        setRenderer(emuRenderer)
        renderMode = RENDERMODE_WHEN_DIRTY
    }
}

class EmuRenderer(private val listener: TextureListener?) : GLSurfaceView.Renderer {
    private var program = 0
    private var textureId = 0
    private var posHandle = 0
    private var texHandle = 0
    private var samplerHandle = 0
    private var texSizeHandle = 0
    private var modeHandle = 0
    private var widthHandle = 0
    private var viewW = 0
    private var viewH = 0
    private var texW = 0
    private var texH = 0
    private var draws = 0L
    private var tDraw = 0L
    private var ready = false

    private val quadBuffer: FloatBuffer = ByteBuffer
        .allocateDirect(QUAD.size * 4)
        .order(ByteOrder.nativeOrder())
        .asFloatBuffer()
        .apply { put(QUAD); position(0) }

    override fun onSurfaceCreated(gl: GL10?, config: EGLConfig?) {
        GLES20.glClearColor(0f, 0f, 0f, 1f)
        program = buildProgram()
        posHandle = GLES20.glGetAttribLocation(program, "aPos")
        texHandle = GLES20.glGetAttribLocation(program, "aTex")
        samplerHandle = GLES20.glGetUniformLocation(program, "uTex")
        texSizeHandle = GLES20.glGetUniformLocation(program, "uTexSize")
        modeHandle = GLES20.glGetUniformLocation(program, "uMode")
        widthHandle = GLES20.glGetUniformLocation(program, "uWidth")

        val ids = IntArray(1)
        GLES20.glGenTextures(1, ids, 0)
        textureId = ids[0]
        GLES20.glBindTexture(GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, textureId)
        GLES20.glTexParameteri(GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GLES20.GL_NEAREST)
        GLES20.glTexParameteri(GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GLES20.GL_LINEAR)
        GLES20.glTexParameteri(GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S, GLES20.GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE)
        GLES20.glTexParameteri(GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T, GLES20.GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE)

        ready = true
        listener?.onSurfaceReady()
        Log.i(TAG, "surface created")
    }

    override fun onSurfaceChanged(gl: GL10?, width: Int, height: Int) {
        viewW = width
        viewH = height
        Log.i(TAG, "surface changed ${width}x${height}")
    }

    override fun onDrawFrame(gl: GL10?) {
        if (!ready) return
        val s0 = System.nanoTime()

        val w = Mobile.frameWidth().toInt()
        val h = Mobile.frameHeight().toInt()
        GLES20.glClear(GLES20.GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT)
        if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return
        val rgba = Mobile.frameRGBA() ?: return
        if (rgba.size < w * h * 4) return

        GLES20.glUseProgram(program)
        GLES20.glActiveTexture(GLES20.GL_TEXTURE0)
        GLES20.glBindTexture(GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, textureId)
        GLES20.glUniform1i(samplerHandle, 0)

        // Picture is fixed to Sharp (the sharp-bilinear remap in
        // the shader) since 1.101: the Picture and Display
        // settings were removed and baked in, so the shader mode
        // is always 0 and the magnification filter stays LINEAR,
        // as set at surface creation.
        GLES20.glUniform2f(texSizeHandle, w.toFloat(), h.toFloat())
        GLES20.glUniform1f(modeHandle, 0f)
        GLES20.glUniform1f(widthHandle, 0.35f)

        val buf = ByteBuffer.wrap(rgba)
        if (w != texW || h != texH) {
            GLES20.glTexImage2D(
                GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GLES20.GL_RGBA, w, h, 0,
                GLES20.GL_RGBA, GLES20.GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, buf
            )
            texW = w; texH = h
        } else {
            GLES20.glTexSubImage2D(
                GLES20.GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, 0, 0, w, h,
                GLES20.GL_RGBA, GLES20.GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, buf
            )
        }

        // Aspect-correct viewport (pillarbox), centered.
        val aspect = Mobile.aspectRatio().toDouble()
        var vw = viewW
        var vh = (viewW / aspect).toInt()
        if (vh > viewH) {
            vh = viewH
            vw = (viewH * aspect).toInt()
        }
        GLES20.glViewport((viewW - vw) / 2, (viewH - vh) / 2, vw, vh)

        quadBuffer.position(0)
        GLES20.glEnableVertexAttribArray(posHandle)
        GLES20.glVertexAttribPointer(posHandle, 2, GLES20.GL_FLOAT, false, 16, quadBuffer)
        quadBuffer.position(2)
        GLES20.glEnableVertexAttribArray(texHandle)
        GLES20.glVertexAttribPointer(texHandle, 2, GLES20.GL_FLOAT, false, 16, quadBuffer)
        GLES20.glDrawArrays(GLES20.GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP, 0, 4)
        GLES20.glDisableVertexAttribArray(posHandle)
        GLES20.glDisableVertexAttribArray(texHandle)

        tDraw += (System.nanoTime() - s0) / 1_000_000
        draws++
        if (draws % 600 == 0L) {
            Log.i(TAG, "gl draws=$draws avg draw ms=${tDraw / 600}")
            tDraw = 0
        }
    }

    private fun buildProgram(): Int {
        val vs = """
            attribute vec4 aPos;
            attribute vec2 aTex;
            varying vec2 vTex;
            void main() {
                gl_Position = aPos;
                vTex = aTex;
            }
        """.trimIndent()
        val fs = """
            precision mediump float;
            varying vec2 vTex;
            uniform sampler2D uTex;
            uniform vec2 uTexSize;
            uniform float uMode;
            uniform float uWidth;
            void main() {
                vec2 uv = vTex;
                if (uMode < 0.5) {
                    // Sharp bilinear: keep the sample pinned near the
                    // texel center (crisp pixels) but blend in a narrow
                    // band at texel borders (no shimmer).
                    vec2 texel = vTex * uTexSize;
                    vec2 center = floor(texel) + 0.5;
                    vec2 f = texel - center;
                    vec2 a = abs(f);
                    vec2 h = sign(f) * 0.5 * clamp((a - (0.5 - uWidth)) / uWidth, 0.0, 1.0);
                    uv = (center + h) / uTexSize;
                }
                gl_FragColor = texture2D(uTex, uv);
            }
        """.trimIndent()
        val v = compile(GLES20.GL_VERTEX_SHADER, vs)
        val f = compile(GLES20.GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, fs)
        val p = GLES20.glCreateProgram()
        GLES20.glAttachShader(p, v)
        GLES20.glAttachShader(p, f)
        GLES20.glLinkProgram(p)
        return p
    }

    private fun compile(type: Int, src: String): Int {
        val id = GLES20.glCreateShader(type)
        GLES20.glShaderSource(id, src)
        GLES20.glCompileShader(id)
        return id
    }

    companion object {
        private const val TAG = "iTaKGL"

        // x, y, u, v per vertex (triangle strip). v flipped: GL textures
        // are bottom-up, emulator frames are top-down.
        private val QUAD = floatArrayOf(
            -1f, -1f, 0f, 1f,
            1f, -1f, 1f, 1f,
            -1f, 1f, 0f, 0f,
            1f, 1f, 1f, 0f
        )
    }
}

    private val debugUpdater = object : Runnable {
        override fun run() {
            val tv = debugOverlay
            if (tv == null || tv.visibility != View.VISIBLE) return
            val nowNs = System.nanoTime()
            if (debugLastTimeNs > 0L) {
                val dtSec = (nowNs - debugLastTimeNs) / 1_000_000_000.0
                if (dtSec > 0) {
                    debugMeasuredFps =
                        (diagFrameTotal - debugLastFrames) / dtSec
                }
            }
            debugLastFrames = diagFrameTotal
            debugLastTimeNs = nowNs
            tv.text = buildDebugStatsText()
            debugHandler.postDelayed(this, 500)
        }
    }

    private fun startDebugUpdater() {
        debugHandler.removeCallbacks(debugUpdater)
        debugLastFrames = diagFrameTotal
        debugLastTimeNs = 0L
        debugHandler.post(debugUpdater)
    }

    private fun stopDebugUpdater() {
        debugHandler.removeCallbacks(debugUpdater)
    }
