class MainActivity : FlutterActivity() {

    companion object {
        private val logLock = Object()
        private var logStarted = false

        // Launch intro verdict, kept in native process memory.
        // The Flutter isolate is recreated when the app returns
        // from EmulatorActivity, which wipes the Dart-side
        // static, so "the intro already played this launch"
        // lives here: it survives the trip to a game and back,
        // and a fresh process starts false, so a cold start
        // plays the intro again. Proven on hardware 2026-10-23:
        // one process (PID 14849), two "intro: start" lines.
        @Volatile
        var introPlayed = false
    }

    private var channel: MethodChannel? = null
    private var lastControllerPromptMs = 0L

    // Self-update download progress, streamed to Dart over the
    // update_progress event channel while downloadAndInstall runs
    // on its worker thread.
    @Volatile
    private var updateProgressSink: EventChannel.EventSink? = null
    private val mainHandler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())

    // The official Newsmax app, launched by the home screen's
    // Newsmax tab. One package serves phones and TV boxes. The
    // manifest names it in <queries> so this app is allowed to see
    // whether it is installed.
    private fun launchNewsmaxApp(): String {
        val pkg = "com.fli.android.newsmaxapp"
        var intent = packageManager.getLaunchIntentForPackage(pkg)
        if (intent == null) {
            // TV boxes enter through the leanback launcher entry.
            intent = packageManager.getLeanbackLaunchIntentForPackage(pkg)
        }
        if (intent == null) return "missing"
        intent.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
        return try {
            startActivity(intent)
            "launched"
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            android.util.Log.w("iTaKApp", "Newsmax launch failed", e)
            "missing"
        }
    }

    // Newsmax's page in the Play Store, offered when the app is
    // not installed. Falls back to the web page if the store app
    // itself is somehow absent.
    private fun openNewsmaxStorePage() {
        val pkg = "com.fli.android.newsmaxapp"
        val market = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, Uri.parse("market://details?id=$pkg"))
        market.setPackage("com.android.vending")
        market.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
        try {

        } catch (e: Exception) {

                    Intent(

                    ).addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)

            }
        }
    }

    private fun reportUpdateProgress(downloaded: Long, total: Long) {
        if (updateProgressSink == null) return
        mainHandler.post {
            updateProgressSink?.success(
                mapOf("downloaded" to downloaded, "total" to total)
            )
        }
    }

    // Controller assignment capture: while armed, the next gamepad
    // button press identifies that controller to Dart.
    @Volatile
    private var captureArmed = false

    // A device is a gamepad only when it carries the FULL gamepad
    // or joystick source value. Source values share bits (SOURCE_
    // KEYBOARD 0x101 shares 0x100 with SOURCE_GAMEPAD 0x401), so an
    // "any bit set" test brands the TV remote (sources 0x81000311 on
    // David's Philips) as a gamepad: it could be captured as a
    // player's controller, listed as one, and announced as one.
    // Same fix as EmulatorActivity's seat routing (2026-11-03).
    private fun isGamepad(dev: InputDevice?): Boolean {
        if (dev == null) return false
        return (dev.sources and InputDevice.SOURCE_GAMEPAD) ==
            InputDevice.SOURCE_GAMEPAD ||
            (dev.sources and InputDevice.SOURCE_JOYSTICK) ==
                InputDevice.SOURCE_JOYSTICK
    }

    override fun dispatchKeyEvent(event: KeyEvent): Boolean {
        if (captureArmed && event.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN) {
            val dev = event.device
            val gamepad = isGamepad(dev)
            if (gamepad && event.keyCode != KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK) {
                captureArmed = false
                channel?.invokeMethod(
                    "controllerCaptured",
                    mapOf(
                        "id" to event.deviceId,
                        "name" to (dev?.name ?: "Controller"),
                        // The descriptor is the pad's permanent identity;
                        // the numeric id changes on every re-pair.
                        "desc" to (dev?.descriptor ?: ""),
                    ),
                )
                return true
            }
        }
        return super.dispatchKeyEvent(event)
    }

    // When a gamepad shows up, ask the UI who picked it up. The TV
    // remote is not a gamepad source, so it never triggers this.
    private val deviceListener = object : InputManager.InputDeviceListener {
        override fun onInputDeviceAdded(deviceId: Int) {
            val dev = InputDevice.getDevice(deviceId) ?: return
            if (!isGamepad(dev)) return
            val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
            if (now - lastControllerPromptMs < 4000) return
            lastControllerPromptMs = now
            channel?.invokeMethod("controllerConnected", mapOf("name" to dev.name))
        }

        override fun onInputDeviceRemoved(deviceId: Int) {}
        override fun onInputDeviceChanged(deviceId: Int) {}
    }

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        val im = getSystemService(Context.INPUT_SERVICE) as InputManager
        im.registerInputDeviceListener(deviceListener, Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()))
        startLogCapture()
        // Debug chute: schedule the periodic check-in worker and
        // one immediate check-in for this launch (DebugChute.kt).
        DebugChute.enqueue(this)
        repairStatsLabels()
    }

    // ----- Play stats rename merge and label repair (1.111) -----
    // A rename used to move the stats file only when the
    // destination did not exist, silently. Any earlier session
    // under the new name creates that file (the session writer
    // persists at launch), the move was skipped forever, and
    // the player's history stayed behind under the old name:
    // that is how Terry's play history detached on the Missouri
    // stick in Nov 2026. A rename now MERGES instead: plays and
    // seconds sum per game, last takes the later time, and the
    // file's name field is set to the new name.
    private fun relabelStatsFile(f: File, playerName: String) {
        if (!f.exists()) return
        try {
            val obj = JSONObject(f.readText())
            if (obj.optString("name", "") != playerName) {
                obj.put("name", playerName)
                f.writeText(obj.toString())
                android.util.Log.i("iTaKApp", "stats: relabeled " + f.name + " to " + playerName)
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            android.util.Log.w("iTaKApp", "stats: relabel failed for " + f.name, e)
        }
    }

    private fun mergeStatsOnRename(oldStats: File, newStats: File, newName: String) {
        if (!oldStats.exists()) {
            relabelStatsFile(newStats, newName)
            return
        }
        if (!newStats.exists()) {
            newStats.parentFile?.mkdirs()
            if (oldStats.renameTo(newStats)) {
                android.util.Log.i("iTaKApp", "rename stats: moved " + oldStats.name + " -> " + newStats.name)
                relabelStatsFile(newStats, newName)
                return
            }
            // renameTo failed: fall through to read-merge-write.
        }
        try {
            val oldObj = try { JSONObject(oldStats.readText()) } catch (e: Exception) { JSONObject() }
            val newObj = try { JSONObject(newStats.readText()) } catch (e: Exception) { JSONObject() }
            val oldGames = oldObj.optJSONObject("games") ?: JSONObject()
            val newGames = newObj.optJSONObject("games") ?: JSONObject()
            val keys = oldGames.keys()
            while (keys.hasNext()) {
                val rom = keys.next()
                val o = oldGames.optJSONObject(rom) ?: continue
                val nw = newGames.optJSONObject(rom)
                if (nw == null) {
                    newGames.put(rom, o)
                } else {
                    nw.put("plays", nw.optInt("plays", 0) + o.optInt("plays", 0))
                    nw.put("seconds", nw.optInt("seconds", 0) + o.optInt("seconds", 0))
                    nw.put("last", maxOf(nw.optLong("last", 0), o.optLong("last", 0)))
                }
            }
            newObj.put("games", newGames)
            newObj.put("name", newName)
            newStats.parentFile?.mkdirs()
            newStats.writeText(newObj.toString())
            oldStats.delete()
            android.util.Log.i("iTaKApp", "rename stats: merged " + oldStats.name + " into " + newStats.name)
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            android.util.Log.w("iTaKApp", "rename stats: merge failed", e)
        }
    }

    // One consistency pass per launch: a stats file whose name
    // field names someone who is not a current player, while
    // the file name itself matches exactly one current player,
    // is that player's file wearing a stale label (the window
    // between a rename and the next session under the new
    // name). Relabel it so the Leaderboard and Manage players
    // show the history right away. Counters are never touched.
    private fun repairStatsLabels() {
        try {
            val prefs = getSharedPreferences("itak_prefs", MODE_PRIVATE)
            val players = (prefs.getString("players", "") ?: "")
                .split("\n").map { it.trim() }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
            if (players.isEmpty()) return
            val sanitize = { s: String -> s.replace(Regex("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]"), "_") }
            val byBase = players.groupBy { sanitize(it) }
            val playerNames = players.toSet()
            val dir = File(filesDir, "stats")
            val files = dir.listFiles() ?: return
            for (f in files) {
                if (!f.name.endsWith(".json")) continue
                val owners = byBase[f.name.removeSuffix(".json")] ?: continue
                if (owners.size != 1) continue
                val owner = owners[0]
                try {
                    val obj = JSONObject(f.readText())
                    val inner = obj.optString("name", "")
                    if (inner != owner && inner !in playerNames) {
                        obj.put("name", owner)
                        f.writeText(obj.toString())
                        android.util.Log.i("iTaKApp", "stats repair: relabeled " + inner + " -> " + owner + " in " + f.name)
                    }
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    android.util.Log.w("iTaKApp", "stats repair: skipped " + f.name, e)
                }
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            android.util.Log.w("iTaKApp", "stats repair failed", e)
        }
    }

    // ----- Debug log capture (Settings -> Logs) -----
    // Streams this app's own logcat (every Log.* line from the UI,
    // the emulator activity, the Go engine, and crashes) into a
    // rotating file the Logs screen can read, export, and clear.

    private fun logFile(): File {
        val dir = File(filesDir, "logs")
        if (!dir.exists()) dir.mkdirs()
        return File(dir, "itak.log")
    }

    private fun startLogCapture() {
        synchronized(logLock) {
            if (logStarted) return
            logStarted = true
        }
        thread(name = "log-capture") {
            try {
                val file = logFile()
                val pidFile = File(file.parentFile, "capture.pid")
                // Kill a logcat left behind by a previous run so
                // lines are never written twice.
                try {
                    val oldPid = pidFile.readText().trim().toInt()
                    if (oldPid > 0) android.os.Process.killProcess(oldPid)
                } catch (e: Exception) { /* none recorded */ }
                val ver = try {
                    packageManager.getPackageInfo(packageName, 0).versionName
                } catch (e: Exception) { "?" }
                var writer = BufferedWriter(FileWriter(file, true))
                writer.write("==== iTaK Gaming v$ver start ${java.util.Date()} ====\n")
                writer.flush()
                val cmd = "echo \$\$ > ${pidFile.absolutePath}; " +
                    "exec logcat -v threadtime --pid=${android.os.Process.myPid()}"
                val proc = Runtime.getRuntime().exec(arrayOf("sh", "-c", cmd))
                val reader = proc.inputStream.bufferedReader()
                var sinceFlush = 0
                var sinceCheck = 0
                while (true) {
                    val line = reader.readLine() ?: break
                    writer.write(line)
                    writer.write("\n")
                    sinceFlush++
                    sinceCheck++
                    if (sinceFlush >= 25) {
                        writer.flush()
                        sinceFlush = 0
                    }
                    if (sinceCheck >= 400) {
                        sinceCheck = 0
                        if (file.length() > 2_000_000L) {
                            writer.flush()
                            writer.close()
                            val old = File(file.parentFile, "itak.old.log")
                            if (old.exists()) old.delete()
                            file.renameTo(old)
                            writer = BufferedWriter(FileWriter(file, true))
                            writer.write("==== log rotated ${java.util.Date()} ====\n")
                            writer.flush()
                        }
                    }
                }
                writer.flush()
                writer.close()
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                android.util.Log.w("iTaKLog", "capture failed", e)
            }
        }
    }

    private fun readLogTail(): Map<String, Any> {
        val file = logFile()
        if (!file.exists()) return mapOf("text" to "", "size" to 0L)
        val size = file.length()
        val want = minOf(size, 200_000L)
        val buf = ByteArray(want.toInt())
        java.io.RandomAccessFile(file, "r").use { raf ->
            raf.seek(size - want)
            raf.readFully(buf)
        }
        var text = String(buf, Charsets.UTF_8)
        if (want < size) {
            val nl = text.indexOf('\n')
            if (nl >= 0) text = text.substring(nl + 1)
        }
        return mapOf("text" to text, "size" to size)
    }

    override fun configureFlutterEngine(flutterEngine: FlutterEngine) {
        super.configureFlutterEngine(flutterEngine)
        val ch = MethodChannel(flutterEngine.dartExecutor.binaryMessenger, "net.itak/emu")
        channel = ch
        EventChannel(
            flutterEngine.dartExecutor.binaryMessenger,
            "net.itak/emu/update_progress"
        ).setStreamHandler(object : EventChannel.StreamHandler {
            override fun onListen(arguments: Any?, events: EventChannel.EventSink?) {
                updateProgressSink = events
            }

            override fun onCancel(arguments: Any?) {
                updateProgressSink = null
            }
        })
        ch.setMethodCallHandler { call, result ->
                when (call.method) {
                    // SharedPreferences bridge (itak_prefs), shared with
                    // EmulatorActivity: player list and current player.
                    "getPref" -> {
                        val key = call.argument<String>("key")
                        val prefs = getSharedPreferences("itak_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                        result.success(if (key != null) prefs.getString(key, null) else null)
                    }
                    "setPref" -> {
                        val key = call.argument<String>("key")
                        val value = call.argument<String>("value")
                        if (key != null && value != null) {
                            getSharedPreferences("itak_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                                .edit().putString(key, value).apply()
                            result.success(true)
                        } else {
                            result.error("BAD_ARGS", "key and value required", null)
                        }
                    }
                    // Int flavor: EmulatorActivity reads filter/display
                    // modes with getInt; a String stored under those keys
                    // would crash that read.
                    "getPrefInt" -> {
                        val key = call.argument<String>("key")
                        val prefs = getSharedPreferences("itak_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                        result.success(
                            if (key != null && prefs.contains(key)) prefs.getInt(key, 0) else null
                        )
                    }
                    "setPrefInt" -> {
                        val key = call.argument<String>("key")
                        val value = call.argument<Int>("value")
                        if (key != null && value != null) {
                            getSharedPreferences("itak_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
                                .edit().putInt(key, value).apply()
                            result.success(true)
                        } else {
                            result.error("BAD_ARGS", "key and value required", null)
                        }
                    }
                    // Launch intro: read or record the once-per
                    // launch verdict held in the companion object.
                    "getIntroPlayed" -> {
                        result.success(introPlayed)
                    }
                    "markIntroPlayed" -> {
                        introPlayed = true
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    // Controller assignment: list connected gamepads,
                    // or arm the one-shot "press any button" capture.
                    "listControllers" -> {
                        val list = mutableListOf<Map<String, Any>>()
                        for (id in InputDevice.getDeviceIds()) {
                            val dev = InputDevice.getDevice(id) ?: continue
                            if (isGamepad(dev)) {
                                list.add(mapOf("id" to id, "name" to dev.name, "desc" to dev.descriptor))
                            }
                        }
                        result.success(list)
                    }
                    "captureController" -> {
                        captureArmed = true
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    "cancelCapture" -> {
                        captureArmed = false
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    // One app for every box: Dart asks whether this
                    // device is 64-bit capable; 64-bit-only systems
                    // show locked on 32-bit hardware.
                    "deviceInfo" -> {
                        result.success(
                            mapOf("is64" to android.os.Build.SUPPORTED_64_BIT_ABIS.isNotEmpty())
                        )
                    }
                    // Friend alert chime: Dart calls this when a
                    // friend alert banner shows. Fire and forget;
                    // the chime plays on its own thread and any
                    // failure is silent.
                    "playNotifySound" -> {
                        playNotifyChime()
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    // Settings -> Sound test: the native speaker and
                    // microphone level-bar screen.
                    "soundTest" -> {
                        startActivity(
                            android.content.Intent(
                                this,
                                SoundTestActivity::class.java
                            )
                        )
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    // Settings -> Sound test popup: run the same
                    // sound delay measurement the native sound
                    // test screen runs and hand the result text
                    // back to Dart, so the popup can show it
                    // without opening the full screen. Takes
                    // about three seconds on a worker thread.
                    "measureSoundDelay" -> {
                        thread {
                            val text = measureSoundDelayBlocking()
                            mainHandler.post { result.success(text) }
                        }
                    }
                    // App root BACK popup (1.109): restart the
                    // app. CLEAR_TASK finishes the current task
                    // and a fresh MainActivity becomes the root:
                    // new Flutter engine, new Dart state, back at
                    // the home screen. The process itself is NOT
                    // killed: every kill-after-launch shape was
                    // proven broken on David's TV, because the
                    // relaunch lands in this same still-living
                    // process and the delayed kill then removes
                    // the newborn activity too ("app died, no
                    // saved state"); an alarm-scheduled relaunch
                    // never fired at all, inexact alarms being
                    // batched.
                    "restartApp" -> {
                        val launch = android.content.Intent(
                            this, MainActivity::class.java
                        )
                        launch.addFlags(
                            android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK or
                                android.content.Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TASK
                        )
                        try {
                            startActivity(launch)
                            result.success(true)
                        } catch (e: Exception) {
                            result.success(false)
                        }
                    }
                    // PATRIOTS screen: play one channel's YouTube
                    // livestream in the native stream player. The
                    // video id is the live broadcast Dart pulled
                    // from the channel's live page; when it is
                    // absent the player uses the channel's
                    // permanent live embed instead.
                    "playStream" -> {
                        val intent = android.content.Intent(
                            this,
                            StreamPlayerActivity::class.java
                        )
                        intent.putExtra(
                            "videoId", call.argument<String>("videoId")
                        )
                        intent.putExtra(
                            "channelId", call.argument<String>("channelId")
                        )
                        intent.putExtra(
                            "name", call.argument<String>("name")
                        )
                        startActivity(intent)
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    // A player rename moves their saves folder and
                    // stats file so nothing is lost.
                    "renamePlayerFiles" -> {
                        val oldName = call.argument<String>("old")
                        val newName = call.argument<String>("new")
                        if (oldName != null && newName != null) {
                            try {
                                val oldSaves = File(filesDir, "saves/$oldName")
                                val newSaves = File(filesDir, "saves/$newName")
                                if (oldSaves.exists() && !newSaves.exists()) {
                                    oldSaves.renameTo(newSaves)
                                }
                                val sanitize = { s: String ->
                                    s.replace(Regex("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]"), "_")
                                }
                                val oldStats = File(filesDir, "stats/${sanitize(oldName)}.json")
                                val newStats = File(filesDir, "stats/${sanitize(newName)}.json")
                                mergeStatsOnRename(oldStats, newStats, newName)
                            } catch (e: Exception) {
                                android.util.Log.w("iTaKApp", "renamePlayerFiles failed", e)
                            }
                            result.success(true)
                        } else {
                            result.error("BAD_ARGS", "old and new required", null)
                        }
                    }
                    // Newsmax tab on the home screen: open the
                    // official Newsmax app, or report it missing so
                    // Dart can offer the download prompt.
                    "launchNewsmax" -> {
                        result.success(launchNewsmaxApp())
                    }
                    "openNewsmaxStore" -> {
                        openNewsmaxStorePage()
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    // Leaderboard: hand Dart the raw per-player stat
                    // files (files/stats/*.json) as one JSON array.
                    "getLeaderboard" -> {
                        val dir = File(filesDir, "stats")
                        val parts = mutableListOf<String>()
                        dir.listFiles { f -> f.name.endsWith(".json") }
                            ?.sortedBy { it.name }
                            ?.forEach { f ->
                                try {
                                    parts.add(f.readText())
                                } catch (e: Exception) { /* skip bad file */ }
                            }
                        result.success("[" + parts.joinToString(",") + "]")
                    }
                    // Self-update: installed version facts for the
                    // update check in Dart.
                    "appInfo" -> {
                        @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
                        val info = packageManager.getPackageInfo(packageName, 0)
                        val code = if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 28) {
                            info.longVersionCode.toInt()
                        } else {
                            @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
                            info.versionCode
                        }
                        result.success(
                            mapOf(
                                "versionCode" to code,
                                "versionName" to (info.versionName ?: "")
                            )
                        )
                    }
                    // Debug logs (Settings -> Logs). Dart app
                    // events are written into logcat so the
                    // capture thread files them with everything
                    // else.
                    "log" -> {
                        val msg = call.argument<String>("message") ?: ""
                        android.util.Log.i("iTaKApp", msg)
                        result.success(true)
                    }
                    "readLog" -> {
                        thread { result.success(readLogTail()) }
                    }
                    "logInfo" -> {
                        val f = logFile()
                        result.success(
                            mapOf("size" to if (f.exists()) f.length() else 0L)
                        )
                    }
                    "clearLog" -> {
                        thread {
                            try {
                                java.io.FileOutputStream(logFile(), false)
                                    .close()
                                result.success(true)
                            } catch (e: Exception) {
                                result.error("IO", e.message, null)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    "exportLog" -> {
                        thread {
                            try {
                                val stamp = java.text.SimpleDateFormat(
                                    "yyyyMMdd-HHmmss", java.util.Locale.US
                                ).format(java.util.Date())
                                val dir = File(
                                    android.os.Environment
                                        .getExternalStorageDirectory(), "iTaK"
                                )
                                if (!dir.exists()) dir.mkdirs()
                                val out = File(dir, "itak-log-$stamp.txt")
                                logFile().copyTo(out, overwrite = true)
                                result.success(out.absolutePath)
                            } catch (e: Exception) {
                                result.error("IO", e.message, null)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    // Self-update: download the APK on a worker
                    // thread, verify its SHA-256, then hand it to
                    // the system installer. Byte progress streams to
                    // Dart over the update_progress event channel.
                    // Returns "" on success, "needs-permission" when
                    // the TV still has to allow installs from this
                    // app (the settings page is opened for the user),
                    // or an error message. Android always shows its
                    // own Install prompt; no sideloaded app can skip
                    // that.
                    "installUpdate" -> {
                        val dlUrl = call.argument<String>("url")
                        val wantSha = call.argument<String>("sha256")
                        val wantSize = call.argument<Number>("size")?.toLong() ?: 0L
                        if (dlUrl == null || wantSha == null) {
                            result.error("BAD_ARGS", "url and sha256 required", null)
                        } else {
                            thread(name = "app-update") {
                                val outcome = try {
                                    downloadAndInstall(dlUrl, wantSha, wantSize)
                                } catch (e: Exception) {
                                    "Download failed: ${e.message ?: "network error"}"
                                }
                                runOnUiThread { result.success(outcome) }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    "launch" -> {
                        val core = call.argument<String>("core") ?: "libitak_snes.so"
                        val rom = call.argument<String>("rom")
                        if (rom == null) {
                            result.error("NO_ROM", "rom path required", null)
                        } else {
                            val intent = Intent(this, EmulatorActivity::class.java)
                            intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_CORE, core)
                            intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_ROM, rom)
                            // Optional netplay session (Online screen).
                            call.argument<String>("npRole")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_ROLE, it)
                            }
                            call.argument<String>("npLobby")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_LOBBY, it)
                            }
                            call.argument<String>("npToken")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_TOKEN, it)
                            }
                            call.argument<String>("npServer")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_SERVER, it)
                            }
                            // The lobby password, so a seat
                            // rotation inside the game screen can
                            // re-enter the room (watch or join)
                            // without asking for it again.
                            call.argument<String>("npPassword")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_PASSWORD, it)
                            }
                            // The tournament name for a hosted
                            // room (Online screen, optional): the
                            // game screen's host client reports
                            // the room's results under it.
                            call.argument<String>("npTournament")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_TOURNAMENT, it)
                            }
                            // Optional watch mode (spectator from the
                            // Online screen): mode/server/lobby/token
                            // ride the same extras the netplay launch
                            // uses, plus the watcher's player name.
                            call.argument<String>("mode")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_MODE, it)
                            }
                            call.argument<String>("serverBase")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_SERVER, it)
                            }
                            call.argument<String>("lobbyId")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_LOBBY, it)
                            }
                            call.argument<String>("token")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_TOKEN, it)
                            }
                            call.argument<String>("playerName")?.let {
                                intent.putExtra(EmulatorActivity.EXTRA_NP_PLAYER, it)
                            }
                            startActivity(intent)
                            result.success(true)
                        }
                    }
                    else -> result.notImplemented()
                }
            }
    }

    // Downloads an update APK, verifies it, and opens the system
    // installer. Runs on a worker thread; returns "" on success,
    // "needs-permission", or a plain error message for the user.
    // The bytes land in update.apk.part first and are renamed to
    // update.apk only after the size and SHA-256 both check out,
    // so a partial file can never reach the installer.
    // The sound delay measurement from the sound test screen
    // (SoundTestActivity.measureDelay), callable from Dart so the
    // Settings sound popup can show the result without opening
    // the full screen: open a track exactly the way a game does
    // (EmuAudioOutput), feed it a soft tone for a few seconds, and
    // read the track's own presentation timestamps to learn how
    // many milliseconds of sound sit between the app and the
    // speaker. Blocking; call from a worker thread. Returns the
    // same result text the native screen shows.
    private fun measureSoundDelayBlocking(): String {
        var track: AudioTrack? = null
        try {
            val rate = EmuAudioOutput.deviceOutputRate(this)
            track = EmuAudioOutput.buildTrack(rate)
            val t = track
            val bufFrames = try { t.bufferSizeInFrames } catch (e: Exception) { 0 }
            t.play()
            // A soft 220 Hz tone, written in quarter-second
            // chunks for about three seconds.
            val chunkFrames = rate / 4
            val pcm = ByteArray(chunkFrames * 4)
            var frame = 0
            val samples = mutableListOf<Double>()
            val ts = AudioTimestamp()
            var written = 0L
            val started = System.nanoTime()
            while ((System.nanoTime() - started) / 1_000_000 < 3000) {
                for (i in 0 until chunkFrames) {
                    val s = (sin(2.0 * PI * 220.0 * (frame + i) / rate) * 0.2 * 32767).toInt()
                    val o = i * 4
                    pcm[o] = (s and 0xFF).toByte()
                    pcm[o + 1] = ((s shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
                    pcm[o + 2] = (s and 0xFF).toByte()
                    pcm[o + 3] = ((s shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
                }
                frame += chunkFrames
                val n = t.write(pcm, 0, pcm.size, AudioTrack.WRITE_BLOCKING)
                if (n > 0) written += n / 4
                try {
                    if (t.getTimestamp(ts)) {
                        val inFlight = written - ts.framePosition
                        if (inFlight >= 0) samples.add(inFlight * 1000.0 / rate)
                    }
                } catch (e: Exception) { /* keep measuring */ }
            }
            val routed = try {
                val dev = t.routedDevice
                if (dev != null) dev.productName.toString() else "unknown"
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                "unknown"
            }
            return if (samples.size >= 3) {
                val sorted = samples.sorted()
                val median = sorted[sorted.size / 2]
                val bufMs = if (rate > 0) bufFrames * 1000.0 / rate else 0.0
                "Sound delay on this box: about ${"%.0f".format(median)} ms.\n" +
                    "Track runs at $rate Hz, its buffer is " +
                    "${"%.0f".format(bufMs)} ms, output to $routed."
            } else {
                "The track would not report its timing on this " +
                    "box, so the delay could not be measured here."
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            return "The delay measurement failed on this box."
        } finally {
            try { track?.stop() } catch (e: Exception) { /* already stopped */ }
            try { track?.release() } catch (e: Exception) { /* already released */ }
        }
    }

    private fun downloadAndInstall(
        dlUrl: String,
        wantSha: String,
        wantSize: Long
    ): String {
        val out = File(cacheDir, "update.apk")
        val part = File(cacheDir, "update.apk.part")
        part.delete()
        val digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")
        val conn = URL(dlUrl).openConnection() as HttpURLConnection
        conn.connectTimeout = 15000
        conn.readTimeout = 60000
        conn.instanceFollowRedirects = true
        conn.connect()
        if (conn.responseCode != 200) {
            return "Download failed: server answered ${conn.responseCode}"
        }
        // Progress total: the HTTP length when the server sends one,
        // else the size version.json promised (0 = unknown).
        val httpTotal = conn.contentLengthLong
        val total = if (httpTotal > 0) httpTotal else wantSize
        var downloaded = 0L
        reportUpdateProgress(0L, total)
        try {
            conn.inputStream.use { input ->
                FileOutputStream(part).use { fos ->
                    val buf = ByteArray(64 * 1024)
                    var lastReport = 0L
                    while (true) {
                        val n = input.read(buf)
                        if (n < 0) break
                        fos.write(buf, 0, n)
                        digest.update(buf, 0, n)
                        downloaded += n
                        if (downloaded - lastReport >= 256 * 1024) {
                            lastReport = downloaded
                            reportUpdateProgress(downloaded, total)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        } catch (e: Exception) {
            part.delete()
            throw e
        }
        reportUpdateProgress(downloaded, total)
        if (httpTotal > 0 && downloaded != httpTotal) {
            part.delete()
            return "Download failed: the connection dropped. Try again."
        }
        val gotSha = digest.digest().joinToString("") { "%02x".format(it) }
        if (!gotSha.equals(wantSha, ignoreCase = true)) {
            part.delete()
            return "Download failed: the file did not verify. Try again."
        }
        if (!part.renameTo(out)) {
            try {
                part.copyTo(out, overwrite = true)
                part.delete()
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                part.delete()
                return "Download failed: could not save the update file."
            }
        }
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 26 && !packageManager.canRequestPackageInstalls()) {
            // One-time TV setting: allow iTaK Gaming to install
            // updates, then the user taps Update again.
            val settings = Intent(
                Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_UNKNOWN_APP_SOURCES,
                Uri.parse("package:$packageName")
            )
            settings.addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK)
            startActivity(settings)
            return "needs-permission"
        }
        val uri = FileProvider.getUriForFile(this, "$packageName.fileprovider", out)
        val install = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW)
        install.setDataAndType(uri, "application/vnd.android.package-archive")
        install.addFlags(
            Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION or Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK
        )
        startActivity(install)
        return ""
    }

    // Soft two-tone chime for friend alerts, generated as sine
    // samples (no audio asset ships with the app): a low tone
    // then a higher one, about 0.35 s total at modest volume,
    // each tone fading in and out so it dings instead of clicks.
    // Plays through the notification stream. Everything is
    // wrapped so a failure can never crash or block the caller.
    private fun playNotifyChime() {
        thread(name = "notify-chime") {
            try {
                val sampleRate = 44100
                val tones = doubleArrayOf(880.0, 1318.5)
                val segSeconds = 0.175
                val framesPerSeg = (sampleRate * segSeconds).toInt()
                val frames = framesPerSeg * tones.size
                val samples = ShortArray(frames)
                val peak = Short.MAX_VALUE * 0.22
                for (seg in tones.indices) {
                    val freq = tones[seg]
                    for (j in 0 until framesPerSeg) {
                        val t = j / sampleRate.toDouble()
                        val attack = Math.min(1.0, t / 0.012)
                        val decay = Math.exp(-2.4 * t / segSeconds)
                        val s = Math.sin(2.0 * Math.PI * freq * t) *
                            attack * decay * peak
                        samples[seg * framesPerSeg + j] = s.toInt().toShort()
                    }
                }
                val track = AudioTrack.Builder()
                    .setAudioAttributes(
                        AudioAttributes.Builder()
                            .setUsage(AudioAttributes.USAGE_NOTIFICATION)
                            .setContentType(
                                AudioAttributes.CONTENT_TYPE_SONIFICATION
                            )
                            .build()
                    )
                    .setAudioFormat(
                        AudioFormat.Builder()
                            .setEncoding(AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_16BIT)
                            .setSampleRate(sampleRate)
                            .setChannelMask(AudioFormat.CHANNEL_OUT_MONO)
                            .build()
                    )
                    .setBufferSizeInBytes(samples.size * 2)
                    .setTransferMode(AudioTrack.MODE_STATIC)
                    .build()
                try {
                    track.write(samples, 0, samples.size)
                    track.play()
                    // MODE_STATIC plays out in real time; wait a
                    // little past the end before releasing.
                    Thread.sleep(500)
                } finally {
                    try {
                        track.release()
                    } catch (e: Exception) { /* already gone */ }
                }
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                // Silent by design: an alert sound must never
                // take the app down with it.
            }
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Sound test screen. Proves audio paths with moving level bars
 * instead of ears: play a generated jingle and watch the speaker
 * bar follow it, play the game sound path test (bright tones made
 * at the SNES rate and converted inside the app, the exact path
 * games take since 1.85), then run the mic test and watch the mic
 * bar follow your voice. If a bar moves, that path works on this
 * box.
 *
 * The mic half doubles as the voice chat hardware checker: any
 * microphone the box can hear (a USB mic, or a Bluetooth mic if
 * the box exposes one as an input) moves the bar.
 */
class SoundTestActivity : Activity() {

    companion object {
        private const val TAG = "iTaKSoundTest"
        private const val REQ_MIC = 4107
    }

    private val uiHandler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())
    private var uiBuilt = false

    private lateinit var speakerBar: LevelBar
    private lateinit var micBar: LevelBar
    private lateinit var speakerStatus: TextView
    private lateinit var micStatus: TextView
    private lateinit var peakLabel: TextView
    private lateinit var playButton: Button
    private lateinit var micButton: Button
    private lateinit var gameButton: Button
    private lateinit var gameBar: LevelBar
    private lateinit var gameStatus: TextView
    private lateinit var delayButton: Button
    private lateinit var delayStatus: TextView
    private lateinit var debugButton: Button
    private lateinit var debugStatus: TextView

    // Delay measurement state: its own short-lived track and
    // thread, independent of the speaker tests above.
    @Volatile private var measuring = false

    // Speaker state. The play thread owns its AudioTrack; other
    // threads only set flags and read the envelope.
    @Volatile private var playing = false
    @Volatile private var playAbort = false
    @Volatile private var speakerEnv = 0f
    @Volatile private var playTrack: AudioTrack? = null

    // Game path test state: shares the playing/playAbort/playTrack
    // bookkeeping with the jingle (only one speaker test runs at a
    // time), with its own bar envelope.
    @Volatile private var gamePlaying = false
    @Volatile private var gameEnv = 0f

    // Mic state. The record thread releases its AudioRecord when
    // it exits; stopMic only flags and stops.
    @Volatile private var micRunning = false
    @Volatile private var micEnv = 0f
    @Volatile private var micPeakPct = 0
    @Volatile private var recorder: AudioRecord? = null
    private var wantMicAfterPermission = false

    // Drives both bars toward their live envelopes 25 times a
    // second: fast rise so hits register, slower fall so the bar
    // settles at zero instead of snapping off.
    private val meterTicker = object : Runnable {
        override fun run() {
            if (uiBuilt) {
                speakerBar.tick(if (playing && !gamePlaying) speakerEnv else 0f)
                gameBar.tick(if (gamePlaying) gameEnv else 0f)
                micBar.tick(if (micRunning) micEnv else 0f)
                if (micRunning) peakLabel.text = "Peak ${micPeakPct}%"
            }
            uiHandler.postDelayed(this, 40)
        }
    }

    // A chunky horizontal level bar. tick() eases the shown level
    // toward the target; the fill is green, then yellow, then red
    // as it approaches full scale.
    private class LevelBar(context: android.content.Context) : View(context) {
        private var shown = 0f
        private val bounds = RectF()
        private val clip = Path()
        private val trackPaint = Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG).apply {
            color = Color.rgb(16, 16, 28)
        }
        private val fillPaint = Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG)

        private fun radius(): Float = 10f * resources.displayMetrics.density

        fun tick(target: Float) {
            val t = target.coerceIn(0f, 1f)
            shown = if (t >= shown) {
                shown + (t - shown) * 0.55f
            } else {
                shown * 0.86f
            }
            if (shown < 0.004f && t == 0f) shown = 0f
            invalidate()
        }

        override fun onSizeChanged(w: Int, h: Int, oldw: Int, oldh: Int) {
            super.onSizeChanged(w, h, oldw, oldh)
            bounds.set(0f, 0f, w.toFloat(), h.toFloat())
            clip.reset()
            clip.addRoundRect(bounds, radius(), radius(), Path.Direction.CW)
        }

        override fun onDraw(canvas: Canvas) {
            super.onDraw(canvas)
            canvas.drawRoundRect(bounds, radius(), radius(), trackPaint)
            if (shown > 0.004f) {
                fillPaint.color = when {
                    shown < 0.75f -> Color.rgb(0, 230, 118)
                    shown < 0.92f -> Color.rgb(255, 214, 0)
                    else -> Color.rgb(255, 82, 82)
                }
                canvas.save()
                canvas.clipPath(clip)
                canvas.drawRect(0f, 0f, bounds.width() * shown, bounds.height(), fillPaint)
                canvas.restore()
            }
        }
    }

    private fun dp(v: Int): Int = (v * resources.displayMetrics.density + 0.5f).toInt()

    private fun makeText(text: String, size: Float, bold: Boolean = false, dim: Boolean = false): TextView {
        val tv = TextView(this)
        tv.text = text
        tv.textSize = size
        tv.setTextColor(if (dim) Color.argb(185, 255, 255, 255) else Color.WHITE)
        if (bold) tv.setTypeface(null, Typeface.BOLD)
        return tv
    }

    private fun spacer(h: Int): View {
        val v = View(this)
        v.layoutParams = LinearLayout.LayoutParams(1, dp(h))
        return v
    }

    }

        micCard.addView(micStatus)
        root.addView(
            micCard,
            LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                LinearLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT,
                LinearLayout.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT
            )
        )
        root.addView(spacer(24))

        // Debug card: measure the sound delay on this box, and
        // send the full debug report up on the spot instead of
        // waiting for the server to ask for one.
        val debugCard = makeCard()
        debugCard.addView(makeText("DEBUG", 20f, bold = true))
        debugCard.addView(spacer(14))
        delayButton = makeButton("Measure sound delay")
        delayButton.setOnClickListener { measureDelay() }
        debugCard.addView(
            delayButton,
            LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                LinearLayout.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT, dp(56)
            )
        )
        debugCard.addView(spacer(12))
        delayStatus = makeText(
            "Plays a soft tone through the game sound path and " +
                "measures how far the sound trails behind, in " +
                "milliseconds.",
            17f, dim = true
        )
        debugCard.addView(delayStatus)
        debugCard.addView(spacer(16))
        debugButton = makeButton("Send debug report now")
        debugButton.setOnClickListener { sendDebugNow() }
        debugCard.addView(
            debugButton,
            LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                LinearLayout.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT, dp(56)
            )
        )
        debugCard.addView(spacer(12))
        debugStatus = makeText(
            "Sends the full report, the latest game session's " +
                "sound measurements included, to the debug server.",
            17f, dim = true
        )
        debugCard.addView(debugStatus)
        root.addView(
            debugCard,
            LinearLayout.LayoutParams(
                LinearLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT,
                LinearLayout.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT
            )
        )
        root.addView(spacer(24))
        root.addView(makeText("Press BACK to leave this screen.", 15f, dim = true))

        // Simple vertical D-pad flow: play, game path, mic, debug.
        playButton.nextFocusDownId = gameButton.id
        gameButton.nextFocusUpId = playButton.id
        gameButton.nextFocusDownId = micButton.id
        micButton.nextFocusUpId = gameButton.id
        micButton.nextFocusDownId = delayButton.id
        delayButton.nextFocusUpId = micButton.id
        delayButton.nextFocusDownId = debugButton.id
        debugButton.nextFocusUpId = delayButton.id

        setContentView(scroll)
        uiBuilt = true
        playButton.post { playButton.requestFocus() }
        uiHandler.post(meterTicker)
    }

    override fun onPause() {
        super.onPause()
        abortPlayback()
        stopMic()
    }

    override fun onDestroy() {
        uiHandler.removeCallbacks(meterTicker)
        abortPlayback()
        stopMic()
        super.onDestroy()
    }

    // Send the full debug report immediately (reason "manual"),
    // through the same chute the periodic check-in uses. The
    // upload itself runs in the chute's worker; this just queues
    // it and says so on screen.
    private fun sendDebugNow() {
        DebugChute.enqueueFull(this, "manual")
        debugStatus.text =
            "Debug report queued. It sends as soon as the network " +
                "allows, with the latest game session's sound " +
                "measurements inside."
    }

    // Measure the sound delay on this box: open a track exactly
    // the way a game does (EmuAudioOutput), feed it a soft tone
    // for a few seconds, and read the track's own presentation
    // timestamps to learn how many milliseconds of sound sit
    // between the app and the speaker. The same measurement the
    // emulator now records for every game session (see
    // AudioDiag), runnable here on demand.
    private fun measureDelay() {
        if (measuring) return
        measuring = true
        delayButton.isEnabled = false
        delayStatus.text = "Measuring..."
        thread {
            var track: AudioTrack? = null
            try {
                val rate = EmuAudioOutput.deviceOutputRate(this)
                track = EmuAudioOutput.buildTrack(rate)
                val t = track
                val bufFrames = try { t.bufferSizeInFrames } catch (e: Exception) { 0 }
                t.play()
                // A soft 220 Hz tone, written in quarter-second
                // chunks for about three seconds.
                val chunkFrames = rate / 4
                val pcm = ByteArray(chunkFrames * 4)
                var frame = 0
                val samples = mutableListOf<Double>()
                val ts = AudioTimestamp()
                var written = 0L
                val started = System.nanoTime()
                while ((System.nanoTime() - started) / 1_000_000 < 3000) {
                    for (i in 0 until chunkFrames) {
                        val s = (sin(2.0 * PI * 220.0 * (frame + i) / rate) * 0.2 * 32767).toInt()
                        val o = i * 4
                        pcm[o] = (s and 0xFF).toByte()
                        pcm[o + 1] = ((s shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
                        pcm[o + 2] = (s and 0xFF).toByte()
                        pcm[o + 3] = ((s shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
                    }
                    frame += chunkFrames
                    val n = t.write(pcm, 0, pcm.size, AudioTrack.WRITE_BLOCKING)
                    if (n > 0) written += n / 4
                    try {
                        if (t.getTimestamp(ts)) {
                            val inFlight = written - ts.framePosition
                            if (inFlight >= 0) samples.add(inFlight * 1000.0 / rate)
                        }
                    } catch (e: Exception) { /* keep measuring */ }
                }
                val routed = try {
                    val dev = t.routedDevice
                    if (dev != null) dev.productName.toString() else "unknown"
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    "unknown"
                }
                val text = if (samples.size >= 3) {
                    val sorted = samples.sorted()
                    val median = sorted[sorted.size / 2]
                    val bufMs = if (rate > 0) bufFrames * 1000.0 / rate else 0.0
                    "Sound delay on this box: about ${"%.0f".format(median)} ms.\n" +
                        "Track runs at $rate Hz, its buffer is " +
                        "${"%.0f".format(bufMs)} ms, output to $routed."
                } else {
                    "The track would not report its timing on this " +
                        "box, so the delay could not be measured here."
                }
                uiHandler.post {
                    delayStatus.text = text
                    delayButton.isEnabled = true
                    measuring = false
                }
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                uiHandler.post {
                    delayStatus.text = "The delay measurement failed on this box."
                    delayButton.isEnabled = true
                    measuring = false
                }
            } finally {
                try { track?.stop() } catch (e: Exception) { /* already stopped */ }
                try { track?.release() } catch (e: Exception) { /* already released */ }
            }
        }
    }

    // Speaker: a rising three note jingle, generated as PCM, no
    // audio assets. 440, 554.37 and 659.25 Hz, 0.60 seconds each
    // with 0.08 second gaps, stereo so both sides are exercised.

    private val noteFreqs = doubleArrayOf(440.0, 554.37, 659.25)
    private val noteFrames = 26460
    private val gapFrames = 3528

    private fun melodyFrames(): Int =
        noteFreqs.size * noteFrames + (noteFreqs.size - 1) * gapFrames

    // One mono sample of the jingle at an absolute frame index.
    // Sine plus a little second and third harmonic reads as a soft
    // triangle tone; each note has a short attack and release so
    // it does not click, and the peak sits at a comfortable 0.62
    // of full scale.
    private fun melodySample(frame: Int): Double {
        var idx = frame
        for (n in noteFreqs.indices) {
            if (idx < noteFrames) {
                val t = idx / 44100.0
                val phase = 2.0 * PI * noteFreqs[n] * t
                var s = sin(phase) + 0.25 * sin(2.0 * phase) + 0.08 * sin(3.0 * phase)
                s /= 1.33
                var env = 1.0
                val attack = 882.0
                val release = 6615.0
                if (idx < attack) env = idx / attack
                val left = noteFrames - idx
                if (left < release) {
                    val r = left / release
                    if (r < env) env = r
                }
                return 0.62 * env * s
            }
            idx -= noteFrames
            if (n < noteFreqs.size - 1) {
                if (idx < gapFrames) return 0.0
                idx -= gapFrames
            }
        }
        return 0.0
    }

    private fun playJingle() {
        if (playing) return
        playing = true
        playAbort = false
        speakerEnv = 0f
        speakerStatus.text = "Playing the test sound now."
        thread(name = "soundtest-play", isDaemon = true) {
            var outcome = "Done. If the bar moved, this box is putting out sound."
            var track: AudioTrack? = null
            try {
                // The shared builder, same as the emulator's.
                track = EmuAudioOutput.buildTrack(44100)
                if (track.state != AudioTrack.STATE_INITIALIZED) {
                    throw IllegalStateException("audio output did not start")
                }
                playTrack = track
                track.play()
                val totalFrames = melodyFrames()
                val chunkFrames = 1024
                val chunk = ShortArray(chunkFrames * 2)
                var frame = 0
                while (frame < totalFrames && !playAbort) {
                    val n = minOf(chunkFrames, totalFrames - frame)
                    var peak = 0
                    for (i in 0 until n) {
                        val v = (melodySample(frame + i) * 32767.0).toInt()
                            .coerceIn(-32767, 32767)
                        chunk[i * 2] = v.toShort()
                        chunk[i * 2 + 1] = v.toShort()
                        val a = abs(v)
                        if (a > peak) peak = a
                    }
                    val shorts = n * 2
                    var off = 0
                    while (off < shorts && !playAbort) {
                        val w = track.write(chunk, off, shorts - off)
                        if (w < 0) throw IllegalStateException("audio write failed")
                        off += w
                    }
                    // The bar follows the signal that was just
                    // handed to the output, chunk by chunk.
                    if (!playAbort) speakerEnv = peak / 32767f
                    frame += n
                }
                // Writes return once data is buffered, not played;
                // wait for the head to reach the end so the tail
                // of the jingle is heard and metered too.
                val deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + 2500
                while (!playAbort && System.currentTimeMillis() < deadline) {
                    val head = try {
                        track.playbackHeadPosition.toLong() and 0xFFFFFFFFL
                    } catch (e: Exception) {
                        totalFrames.toLong()
                    }
                    if (head >= totalFrames.toLong()) break
                    speakerEnv *= 0.9f
                    Thread.sleep(40)
                }
                if (playAbort) outcome = "Stopped."
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                Log.w(TAG, "speaker test failed", e)
                outcome = "Speaker error: " + (e.message ?: "unknown problem")
            } finally {
                try {
                    track?.stop()
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                }
                track?.release()
                if (playTrack === track) playTrack = null
                playing = false
                speakerEnv = 0f
                val msg = outcome
                uiHandler.post {
                    if (uiBuilt) {
                        speakerStatus.text = msg
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private fun abortPlayback() {
        playAbort = true
        try {
            playTrack?.stop()
        } catch (e: Exception) {
        }
    }

    // Game sound path test: the jingle's three notes as bright
    // band-limited square tones, generated at 32,040 Hz (the SNES
    // rate the emulator runs at since 1.95) and converted to this
    // box's output rate by the same AudioResampler the emulator
    // uses, then played on a track built by the same shared
    // builder. Rich harmonics are the point: a conversion that
    // adds scratch or buzz is obvious on square tones and
    // invisible on the soft jingle above.

    private val gameNoteFrames = 19200 // 0.60 s at 32,040 Hz
    private val gameGapFrames = 2560 // 0.08 s at 32,040 Hz

    private fun gameToneFrames(): Int =
        noteFreqs.size * gameNoteFrames + (noteFreqs.size - 1) * gameGapFrames

    // One mono sample of the game path signal at an absolute frame
    // index. Odd harmonics to the 15th, Gibbs-safe peak, and the
    // same attack and release discipline as the jingle.
    private fun gameSample(frame: Int): Double {
        var idx = frame
        for (n in noteFreqs.indices) {
            if (idx < gameNoteFrames) {
                val t = idx / 32040.0
                var s = 0.0
                var k = 1
                while (k <= 15) {
                    s += sin(2.0 * PI * noteFreqs[n] * k * t) / k
                    k += 2
                }
                s /= 2.03
                var env = 1.0
                val attack = 640.0
                val release = 4800.0
                if (idx < attack) env = idx / attack
                val left = gameNoteFrames - idx
                if (left < release) {
                    val r = left / release
                    if (r < env) env = r
                }
                return 0.5 * env * s
            }
            idx -= gameNoteFrames
            if (n < noteFreqs.size - 1) {
                if (idx < gameGapFrames) return 0.0
                idx -= gameGapFrames
            }
        }
        return 0.0
    }

    private fun playGamePath() {
        if (playing) return
        playing = true
        gamePlaying = true
        playAbort = false
        gameEnv = 0f
        gameStatus.text = "Playing the game sound path now."
        thread(name = "soundtest-gamepath", isDaemon = true) {
            var outcome = "Done. Clean tones mean the game sound path is healthy on this box."
            var track: AudioTrack? = null
            try {
                val nativeRate = EmuAudioOutput.deviceOutputRate(this)
                track = EmuAudioOutput.buildTrack(nativeRate)
                if (track.state != AudioTrack.STATE_INITIALIZED) {
                    throw IllegalStateException("audio output did not start")
                }
                playTrack = track
                track.play()
                val resampler = AudioResampler(32040, nativeRate)
                val totalFrames = gameToneFrames()
                val chunkFrames = 533 // about one video frame of audio
                var frame = 0
                var writtenTotal = 0L
                while (frame < totalFrames && !playAbort) {
                    val n = minOf(chunkFrames, totalFrames - frame)
                    val pcm = ByteArray(n * 4)
                    for (i in 0 until n) {
                        val v = (gameSample(frame + i) * 32767.0).toInt()
                            .coerceIn(-32767, 32767)
                        val o = i * 4
                        pcm[o] = (v and 0xFF).toByte()
                        pcm[o + 1] = ((v shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
                        pcm[o + 2] = (v and 0xFF).toByte()
                        pcm[o + 3] = ((v shr 8) and 0xFF).toByte()
                    }
                    val out = resampler.convert(pcm)
                    var off = 0
                    var peak = 0
                    while (off < out.size && !playAbort) {
                        val w = track.write(out, off, out.size - off)
                        if (w < 0) throw IllegalStateException("audio write failed")
                        off += w
                    }
                    writtenTotal += out.size / 4
                    // The bar follows the converted signal, the
                    // one the box actually plays.
                    var j = 0
                    while (j + 1 < out.size) {
                        val v = (out[j + 1].toInt() shl 8) or (out[j].toInt() and 0xFF)
                        val a = abs(v)
                        if (a > peak) peak = a
                        j += 4
                    }
                    if (!playAbort && out.isNotEmpty()) gameEnv = peak / 32767f
                    frame += n
                }
                // Writes return once data is buffered, not played;
                // wait for the head to reach the end so the tail is
                // heard and metered too.
                val deadline = System.currentTimeMillis() + 2500
                while (!playAbort && System.currentTimeMillis() < deadline) {
                    val head = try {
                        track.playbackHeadPosition.toLong() and 0xFFFFFFFFL
                    } catch (e: Exception) {
                        writtenTotal
                    }
                    if (head >= writtenTotal) break
                    gameEnv *= 0.9f
                    Thread.sleep(40)
                }
                if (playAbort) outcome = "Stopped."
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                Log.w(TAG, "game path test failed", e)
                outcome = "Game path error: " + (e.message ?: "unknown problem")
            } finally {
                try {
                    track?.stop()
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                }
                track?.release()
                if (playTrack === track) playTrack = null
                playing = false
                gamePlaying = false
                gameEnv = 0f
                val msg = outcome
                uiHandler.post {
                    if (uiBuilt) {
                        gameStatus.text = msg
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Mic: first working input config wins. Sources in order
    // VOICE_RECOGNITION, then MIC; for each source the rates are
    // 44100, then 16000; mono PCM 16 bit throughout. The input
    // device is the system default input, so a USB mic plugged
    // into the box is picked up automatically.

    private fun onMicButton() {
        if (micRunning) {
            stopMic()
            return
        }
        if (checkSelfPermission(Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO) ==
            PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        ) {
            startMic()
        } else {
            wantMicAfterPermission = true
            requestPermissions(arrayOf(Manifest.permission.RECORD_AUDIO), REQ_MIC)
        }
    }

    override fun onRequestPermissionsResult(
        requestCode: Int,
        permissions: Array<out String>,
        grantResults: IntArray
    ) {
        super.onRequestPermissionsResult(requestCode, permissions, grantResults)
        if (requestCode != REQ_MIC) return
        val granted = grantResults.isNotEmpty() &&
            grantResults[0] == PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED
        if (granted && wantMicAfterPermission) {
            startMic()
        } else if (!granted) {
            micStatus.text =
                "No microphone found or permission denied. This box cannot hear you."
        }
        wantMicAfterPermission = false
    }

    private fun startMic() {
        if (micRunning) return
        if (recorder != null) {
            micStatus.text = "The last mic test is still stopping. Try again in a second."
            return
        }
        val sources = intArrayOf(
            MediaRecorder.AudioSource.VOICE_RECOGNITION,
            MediaRecorder.AudioSource.MIC
        )
        val rates = intArrayOf(44100, 16000)
        var found: AudioRecord? = null
        var foundBuf = 0
        outer@ for (src in sources) {
            for (rate in rates) {
                val minBuf = AudioRecord.getMinBufferSize(
                    rate, AudioFormat.CHANNEL_IN_MONO, AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_16BIT
                )
                if (minBuf <= 0) continue
                val bufSize = maxOf(minBuf, 4096)
                try {
                    val rec = AudioRecord.Builder()
                        .setAudioSource(src)
                        .setAudioFormat(
                            AudioFormat.Builder()
                                .setEncoding(AudioFormat.ENCODING_PCM_16BIT)
                                .setSampleRate(rate)
                                .setChannelMask(AudioFormat.CHANNEL_IN_MONO)
                                .build()
                        )
                        .setBufferSizeInBytes(bufSize)
                        .build()
                    if (rec.state != AudioRecord.STATE_INITIALIZED) {
                        rec.release()
                        continue
                    }
                    rec.startRecording()
                    if (rec.recordingState != AudioRecord.RECORDSTATE_RECORDING) {
                        try {
                            rec.stop()
                        } catch (e: Exception) {
                        }
                        rec.release()
                        continue
                    }
                    found = rec
                    foundBuf = bufSize
                    break@outer
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    Log.w(TAG, "mic attempt failed, source $src rate $rate", e)
                }
            }
        }
        val rec = found
        if (rec == null) {
            micStatus.text = "No microphone found on this box. Plug in a USB mic and try again."
            return
        }
        recorder = rec
        micRunning = true
        micEnv = 0f
        micPeakPct = 0
        peakLabel.text = "Peak 0%"
        micButton.text = "Stop"
        micStatus.text = "Listening. Talk now and watch the bar."
        val bufSize = foundBuf
        thread(name = "soundtest-mic", isDaemon = true) {
            val buf = ShortArray(bufSize / 2)
            var sessionPeak = 0
            while (micRunning) {
                val n = try {
                    rec.read(buf, 0, buf.size)
                } catch (e: Exception) {
                    -1
                }
                if (n > 0) {
                    var peak = 0
                    for (i in 0 until n) {
                        val a = abs(buf[i].toInt())
                        if (a > peak) peak = a
                    }
                    // Peak of this buffer over full scale drives
                    // the bar; the loudest buffer since the test
                    // started drives the percent label.
                    micEnv = peak / 32768f
                    val pct = peak * 100 / 32768
                    if (pct > sessionPeak) {
                        sessionPeak = pct
                        micPeakPct = pct
                    }
                } else if (n < 0) {
                    break
                }
            }
            try {
                rec.release()
            } catch (e: Exception) {
            }
            if (recorder === rec) recorder = null
        }
    }

    private fun stopMic() {
        val wasRunning = micRunning
        micRunning = false
        val rec = recorder
        if (rec != null) {
            try {
                rec.stop()
            } catch (e: Exception) {
            }
        }
        micEnv = 0f
        if (uiBuilt && wasRunning) {
            micButton.text = "Start mic test"
            micStatus.text = "Mic test is off."
        }
    }
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/itak_gaming/StreamPlayerActivity.kt ====================

package net.itak.itak_gaming

import android.app.Activity
import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.KeyEvent
import android.view.WindowManager
import android.webkit.WebChromeClient
import android.webkit.WebView
import android.webkit.WebViewClient

// Full-screen player for the PATRIOTS livestreams (David,
// 2026-11-02). Terry's stick has no YouTube app (removed on
// David's order), so streams play here, in YouTube's own
// embedded player inside a WebView. When the PATRIOTS screen
// pulled the channel's current live video id, that broadcast is
// embedded directly; otherwise the channel's permanent live
// embed is used, which always resolves to whatever is live now.
class StreamPlayerActivity : Activity() {

    private var webView: WebView? = null

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        window.addFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON)
        val videoId = intent.getStringExtra("videoId")
        val channelId = intent.getStringExtra("channelId")
        // YouTube's embed player only plays when the page framing
        // it is served over HTTPS from a real domain, so the
        // iframe request carries a genuine Referer. Proven on the
        // Missouri stick (2026-11-02): an in-app iframe wrapper
        // (loadDataWithBaseURL) got error 152 on every channel,
        // and loading the bare embed URL with a spoofed desktop
        // user agent got error 153. The player therefore loads
        // our own tiny host page on the update service, which
        // frames the channel's embed; the WebView itself stays
        // completely stock.
        val page = if (!videoId.isNullOrEmpty()) {
            "https://arcade.itak.live/app/embed.html?v=$videoId"
        } else {
            "https://arcade.itak.live/app/embed.html?c=$channelId"
        }
        val wv = WebView(this)
        webView = wv
        val settings = wv.settings
        settings.javaScriptEnabled = true
        settings.domStorageEnabled = true
        settings.mediaPlaybackRequiresUserGesture = false
        settings.loadWithOverviewMode = true
        settings.useWideViewPort = true
        wv.webViewClient = WebViewClient()
        wv.webChromeClient = WebChromeClient()
        wv.loadUrl(page)
        setContentView(wv)
    }

    override fun onPause() {
        webView?.onPause()
        super.onPause()
    }

    override fun onResume() {
        super.onResume()
        webView?.onResume()
    }

    override fun onDestroy() {
        webView?.let {
            it.stopLoading()
            it.destroy()
        }
        webView = null
        super.onDestroy()
    }

    // BACK leaves the player. Every other key keeps its default
    // behavior so the volume and media keys reach the system.
    override fun dispatchKeyEvent(event: KeyEvent): Boolean {
        if (event.keyCode == KeyEvent.KEYCODE_BACK &&
            event.action == KeyEvent.ACTION_DOWN
        ) {
            finish()
            return true
        }
        return super.dispatchKeyEvent(event)
    }
}
