==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-anydpi-v26/ic_launcher.xml ====================

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- Adaptive launcher icon (API 26+).

     The app used to ship only legacy density PNGs. The install
     prompt draws that bitmap straight from the submitted APK and
     looked right, but the "App installed" screen on Android TV
     loads the installed app's icon through the adaptive icon
     path; with no adaptive form declared it substituted the
     system default Android head. This file (plus roundIcon in
     the manifest) gives every icon surface a real form to load.

     Foreground: the existing logo artwork, inset 16 percent.
     The artwork has no padding of its own; measured on the
     192px master, the logo occupies the center 74 percent of
     the width and 51 percent of the height. At a 16 percent
     inset the whole logo sits inside the 72dp keyline circle
     that every launcher mask guarantees to keep visible, and
     the flat #171E26 surround of the artwork meets the matching
     background color with no seam. -->
<adaptive-icon xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
    <background android:drawable="@color/ic_launcher_background" />
    <foreground>
        <inset
            android:drawable="@mipmap/ic_launcher_foreground"
            android:inset="16%" />
    </foreground>
</adaptive-icon>

==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/gradlew ====================

#!/usr/bin/env bash

##############################################################################
##
##  Gradle start up script for UN*X
##
##############################################################################

# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS=""

APP_NAME="Gradle"
APP_BASE_NAME=`basename "$0"`

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD="maximum"

warn ( ) {
    echo "$*"
}

die ( ) {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
}

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
case "`uname`" in
  CYGWIN* )
    cygwin=true
    ;;
  Darwin* )
    darwin=true
    ;;
  MINGW* )
    msys=true
    ;;
esac

# Attempt to set APP_HOME
# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
PRG="$0"
# Need this for relative symlinks.
while [ -h "$PRG" ] ; do
    ls=`ls -ld "$PRG"`
    link=`expr "$ls" : '.*-> \(.*\)$'`
    if expr "$link" : '/.*' > /dev/null; then
        PRG="$link"
    else
        PRG=`dirname "$PRG"`"/$link"
    fi
done
SAVED="`pwd`"
cd "`dirname \"$PRG\"`/" >/dev/null
APP_HOME="`pwd -P`"
cd "$SAVED" >/dev/null

CLASSPATH=$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar

# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD="$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java"
    else
        JAVACMD="$JAVA_HOME/bin/java"
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD="java"
    which java >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if [ "$cygwin" = "false" -a "$darwin" = "false" ] ; then
    MAX_FD_LIMIT=`ulimit -H -n`
    if [ $? -eq 0 ] ; then
        if [ "$MAX_FD" = "maximum" -o "$MAX_FD" = "max" ] ; then
            MAX_FD="$MAX_FD_LIMIT"
        fi
        ulimit -n $MAX_FD
        if [ $? -ne 0 ] ; then
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit: $MAX_FD"
        fi
    else
        warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit: $MAX_FD_LIMIT"
    fi
fi

# For Darwin, add options to specify how the application appears in the dock
if $darwin; then
    GRADLE_OPTS="$GRADLE_OPTS \"-Xdock:name=$APP_NAME\" \"-Xdock:icon=$APP_HOME/media/gradle.icns\""
fi

# For Cygwin, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if $cygwin ; then
    APP_HOME=`cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME"`
    CLASSPATH=`cygpath --path --mixed "$CLASSPATH"`
    JAVACMD=`cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD"`

    # We build the pattern for arguments to be converted via cygpath
    ROOTDIRSRAW=`find -L / -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d 2>/dev/null`
    SEP=""
    for dir in $ROOTDIRSRAW ; do
        ROOTDIRS="$ROOTDIRS$SEP$dir"
        SEP="|"
    done
    OURCYGPATTERN="(^($ROOTDIRS))"
    # Add a user-defined pattern to the cygpath arguments
    if [ "$GRADLE_CYGPATTERN" != "" ] ; then
        OURCYGPATTERN="$OURCYGPATTERN|($GRADLE_CYGPATTERN)"
    fi
    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    i=0
    for arg in "$@" ; do
        CHECK=`echo "$arg"|egrep -c "$OURCYGPATTERN" -`
        CHECK2=`echo "$arg"|egrep -c "^-"`                                 ### Determine if an option

        if [ $CHECK -ne 0 ] && [ $CHECK2 -eq 0 ] ; then                    ### Added a condition
            eval `echo args$i`=`cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg"`
        else
            eval `echo args$i`="\"$arg\""
        fi
        i=$((i+1))
    done
    case $i in
        (0) set -- ;;
        (1) set -- "$args0" ;;
        (2) set -- "$args0" "$args1" ;;
        (3) set -- "$args0" "$args1" "$args2" ;;
        (4) set -- "$args0" "$args1" "$args2" "$args3" ;;
        (5) set -- "$args0" "$args1" "$args2" "$args3" "$args4" ;;
        (6) set -- "$args0" "$args1" "$args2" "$args3" "$args4" "$args5" ;;
        (7) set -- "$args0" "$args1" "$args2" "$args3" "$args4" "$args5" "$args6" ;;
        (8) set -- "$args0" "$args1" "$args2" "$args3" "$args4" "$args5" "$args6" "$args7" ;;
        (9) set -- "$args0" "$args1" "$args2" "$args3" "$args4" "$args5" "$args6" "$args7" "$args8" ;;
    esac
fi

# Split up the JVM_OPTS And GRADLE_OPTS values into an array, following the shell quoting and substitution rules
function splitJvmOpts() {
    JVM_OPTS=("$@")
}
eval splitJvmOpts $DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS
JVM_OPTS[${#JVM_OPTS[*]}]="-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME"

exec "$JAVACMD" "${JVM_OPTS[@]}" -classpath "$CLASSPATH" org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain "$@"


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/android/gradlew.bat ====================

@if "%DEBUG%" == "" @echo off
@rem ##########################################################################
@rem
@rem  Gradle startup script for Windows
@rem
@rem ##########################################################################

@rem Set local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" setlocal

@rem Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
set DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS=

set DIRNAME=%~dp0
if "%DIRNAME%" == "" set DIRNAME=.
set APP_BASE_NAME=%~n0
set APP_HOME=%DIRNAME%

@rem Find java.exe
if defined JAVA_HOME goto findJavaFromJavaHome

set JAVA_EXE=java.exe
%JAVA_EXE% -version >NUL 2>&1
if "%ERRORLEVEL%" == "0" goto init

echo.
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.
echo.
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
echo location of your Java installation.

goto fail

:findJavaFromJavaHome
set JAVA_HOME=%JAVA_HOME:"=%
set JAVA_EXE=%JAVA_HOME%/bin/java.exe

if exist "%JAVA_EXE%" goto init

echo.
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: %JAVA_HOME%
echo.
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
echo location of your Java installation.

goto fail

:init
@rem Get command-line arguments, handling Windowz variants

if not "%OS%" == "Windows_NT" goto win9xME_args
if "%@eval[2+2]" == "4" goto 4NT_args

:win9xME_args
@rem Slurp the command line arguments.
set CMD_LINE_ARGS=
set _SKIP=2

:win9xME_args_slurp
if "x%~1" == "x" goto execute

set CMD_LINE_ARGS=%*
goto execute

:4NT_args
@rem Get arguments from the 4NT Shell from JP Software
set CMD_LINE_ARGS=%$

:execute
@rem Setup the command line

set CLASSPATH=%APP_HOME%\gradle\wrapper\gradle-wrapper.jar

@rem Execute Gradle
"%JAVA_EXE%" %DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS% %JAVA_OPTS% %GRADLE_OPTS% "-Dorg.gradle.appname=%APP_BASE_NAME%" -classpath "%CLASSPATH%" org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain %CMD_LINE_ARGS%

:end
@rem End local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if "%ERRORLEVEL%"=="0" goto mainEnd

:fail
rem Set variable GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE if you need the _script_ return code instead of
rem the _cmd.exe /c_ return code!
if  not "" == "%GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE%" exit 1
exit /b 1

:mainEnd
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" endlocal

:omega

You can customize the launch screen with your own desired assets by replacing the image files in this directory.

You can also do it by opening your Flutter project's Xcode project with `open ios/Runner.xcworkspace`, selecting `Runner/Assets.xcassets` in the Project Navigator and dropping in the desired images.

==================== FILE: flutter_ui/lib/debug_chute.dart ====================

import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:math';

import 'package:flutter/services.dart';

import 'main.dart' show AppUpdate, Prefs, appLog, kServerBase;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Debug chute: one-way health reports from this install to our own
// server (POST https://arcade.itak.live/debug/report), so a stick
// can be diagnosed without Android wireless debugging, which turns
// itself off whenever it likes. The app only ever sends; nothing
// here listens or accepts commands back.
//
// Identity is an install code: 16 random bytes as hex, generated
// once and kept in the 'install_code' pref for the life of the
// install. The server keys everything by a hash of it and a human
// labels sticks there, so the app never carries names or accounts.
//
// Two senders share this payload: this Dart side (launch send,
// throttled to one success per 6 h, and the manual Settings row)
// and the native WorkManager check-in (DebugChute.kt), which adds
// a tiny 15-minute ping and uploads this same full report when the
// server answers want_full_report.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class DebugChute {
  static const _channel = MethodChannel('net.itak/emu');

  static const String _codePref = 'install_code';
  static const String _togglePref = 'debug_chute';
  static const String _lastPref = 'debug_chute_last';

  /// One full report at most per this window on the launch path.
  static const int launchThrottleSeconds = 6 * 3600;

  /// The install code, generated on first ask and then stable.
  /// The native check-in worker uses the same pref and format, so
  /// whichever side runs first establishes the same identity.
  static Future<String> installCode() async {
    final existing = await Prefs.get(_codePref);
    if (existing != null && _isHex(existing, 32)) return existing;
    final rnd = Random.secure();
    final bytes = List<int>.generate(16, (_) => rnd.nextInt(256));
    final code =
        bytes.map((b) => b.toRadixString(16).padLeft(2, '0')).join();
    await Prefs.set(_codePref, code);
    return code;
  }

  static bool _isHex(String s, int len) {
    if (s.length != len) return false;
    for (final c in s.codeUnits) {
      final ok = (c >= 0x30 && c <= 0x39) || // 0-9
          (c >= 0x61 && c <= 0x66) || // a-f
          (c >= 0x41 && c <= 0x46); // A-F
      if (!ok) return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

  /// Settings -> Debug reports toggle; default on.
  static Future<bool> enabled() async {
    return (await Prefs.get(_togglePref)) != '0';
  }

  /// The app's log text (the native side streams logcat to a
  /// file; readLog hands back its tail, up to about 200 KB).
  static Future<String> _logText() async {
    try {
      final data =
          await _channel.invokeMethod<Map<dynamic, dynamic>>('readLog');
      return (data?['text'] ?? '').toString();
    } catch (_) {
      return '';
    }
  }

  /// The last [max] log lines that carry a core frame timing.
  static List<String> timingLines(String logText, int max) {
    final hits = logText
        .split('\n')
        .where((l) => l.contains('native timing'))
        .toList();
    if (hits.length <= max) return hits;
    return hits.sublist(hits.length - max);
  }

  /// The log tail, capped at the last 120 KB of UTF-8 so the
  /// report stays small no matter how chatty the session was.
  static String logTail(String logText) {
    const cap = 120 * 1024;
    final bytes = utf8.encode(logText);
    if (bytes.length <= cap) return logText;
    var tail = utf8.decode(bytes.sublist(bytes.length - cap),
        allowMalformed: true);
    final nl = tail.indexOf('\n');
    if (nl >= 0) tail = tail.substring(nl + 1); // drop the partial line
    return tail;
  }

  /// The full report payload. [reason] is launch, manual, or pull
  /// (the native side sends pull itself; Dart sends launch and
  /// manual). Model and SDK have no cheap Dart source here, so
  /// they ride as unknown/0; the native check-in reports the real
  /// values in its pings.
  static Future<Map<String, dynamic>> buildReport(String reason) async {
    final info = await AppUpdate.installed();
    final log = await _logText();
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'install_code': await installCode(),
      'versionName': info?['versionName']?.toString() ?? '',
      'versionCode': (info?['versionCode'] as num?)?.toInt() ?? 0,
      'model': 'unknown',
      'sdk': 0,
      'timingLines': timingLines(log, 40),
      'logTail': logTail(log),
      'reason': reason,
      'timestamp': DateTime.now().toUtc().toIso8601String(),
    };
  }

  /// POST one full report. True on a 200 from the server; stamps
  /// the last-success pref either way it goes only on success, so
  /// a dead network never throttles the next launch's retry.
  static Future<bool> sendReport(String reason) async {
    final payload = await buildReport(reason);
    final client = HttpClient();
    client.connectionTimeout = const Duration(seconds: 15);
    try {
      final req =
          await client.postUrl(Uri.parse('$kServerBase/debug/report'));
      req.headers.contentType = ContentType.json;
      req.headers.set(HttpHeaders.userAgentHeader, 'iTaK-Gaming/1.0');
      req.write(jsonEncode(payload));
      final resp = await req.close().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 15));
      await resp.drain<void>();
      if (resp.statusCode == 200) {
        await Prefs.set(_lastPref,
            (DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch ~/ 1000).toString());
        appLog('debug chute: report sent ($reason)');
        return true;
      }
      appLog(
          'debug chute: report refused (${resp.statusCode}, $reason)');
      return false;
    } catch (e) {
      appLog('debug chute: report failed ($reason): $e');
      return false;
    } finally {
      client.close(force: true);
    }
  }

  /// Launch path: fire and forget after the home screen paints.
  /// Silent apart from appLog lines; the toggle gates it and the
  /// 6 h throttle keeps a TV that relaunches all day quiet.
  static Future<void> maybeSendOnLaunch() async {
    try {
      if (!await enabled()) return;
      final last = int.tryParse(await Prefs.get(_lastPref) ?? '') ?? 0;
      final now = DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch ~/ 1000;
      if (now - last < launchThrottleSeconds) return;
      await sendReport('launch');
    } catch (_) {
      // Never let the chute disturb a launch.
    }
  }
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/lib/intro_video.dart ====================

import 'dart:async';

import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart';
import 'package:video_player/video_player.dart';

import 'main.dart' show Prefs, SystemSelectScreen, appLog;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Launch intro (owner, 2026-10-23): the iTaK Gaming intro plays once
// on a cold start, before the home screen. Any remote key (DPAD,
// CENTER, BACK) or a tap skips it, it hands off to home when it
// ends, and any failure at all (missing asset, player error, a
// stalled start) falls through to home instead: the intro can
// never trap or crash the app. Settings -> Intro video (pref
// 'intro_video', default on) turns it off entirely; with it off
// the app opens straight to home as it always did. The gate
// gives its verdict at most once per app process: returning
// home after a game rebuilds this widget, and the intro must
// not replay for that (seen on hardware 2026-10-23). The
// verdict itself lives in Kotlin process memory (channel
// methods 'getIntroPlayed' / 'markIntroPlayed' on
// net.itak/emu): this isolate is recreated when MainActivity
// returns from EmulatorActivity, which wiped the Dart static
// and replayed the intro on 1.73 (one process, two
// "intro: start" lines). The static below stays as a
// same-isolate fast path; native is the source of truth. A
// cold start is a new process, the native flag starts
// false, and the intro plays again. On the way out the
// picture fades to black (about 750 ms at the clip's
// natural end, 250 ms on any early exit) instead of
// cutting; a hard timer backs the fade so the handoff to
// home can never stall.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const String kIntroAsset = 'assets/intro/itak_intro.mp4';
const String kIntroPref = 'intro_video';

enum _IntroEnd { done, skipped, error, off }

class IntroGate extends StatefulWidget {
  const IntroGate({super.key});

  @override
  State<IntroGate> createState() => _IntroGateState();
}

class _IntroGateState extends State<IntroGate>
    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
  /// Set the first time the gate reaches any verdict (played,
  /// skipped, errored, off) in this process. Static on purpose:
  /// State objects are recreated when the home route rebuilds
  /// on the way back from a game, but the process, and this
  /// flag, live on, so the intro plays at most once per launch.
  /// It only covers gates rebuilt inside this same isolate;
  /// across an isolate recreation the native flag decides.
  static bool _verdictGiven = false;

  static const MethodChannel _channel = MethodChannel('net.itak/emu');

  final FocusNode _focusNode = FocusNode();
  VideoPlayerController? _controller;
  Timer? _watchdog;
  AnimationController? _fadeController;
  Timer? _fadeTimer;
  bool _fading = false;
  bool _showHome = false;
  bool _finished = false;
  bool _started = false;

  @override
  void initState() {
    super.initState();
    if (_verdictGiven) {
      // The gate already ran once in this process (the player
      // is returning home from a game): go straight home.
      _finished = true;
      _showHome = true;
      return;
    }
    // Absolute backstop: whatever happens below, the app reaches
    // home. Twenty seconds is far beyond the 10 s clip plus any
    // sane start-up stall.
    _watchdog = Timer(const Duration(seconds: 20), () {
      _beginFade(_IntroEnd.done, const Duration(milliseconds: 250));
    });
    _run();
    WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
      if (mounted) _focusNode.requestFocus();
    });
  }

  Future<void> _run() async {
    try {
      // Native first: it holds the verdict for the whole
      // process, this isolate included. If it says the intro
      // already played, go straight home without a fresh
      // "intro: start" in the log.
      var nativePlayed = false;
      try {
        nativePlayed =
            await _channel.invokeMethod<bool>('getIntroPlayed') ?? false;
      } catch (_) {
        // A channel failure must never trap the app: fall
        // back to the Dart static, which _finish maintains.
        nativePlayed = false;
      }
      if (_finished || _fading) return;
      if (nativePlayed) {
        _verdictGiven = true;
        _finished = true;
        _watchdog?.cancel();
        if (mounted) {
          setState(() => _showHome = true);
        } else {
          _showHome = true;
        }
        return;
      }
      final pref = await Prefs.get(kIntroPref);
      if (_finished || _fading) return;
      if (pref == '0') {
        _beginFade(_IntroEnd.off, const Duration(milliseconds: 250));
        return;
      }
      final controller = VideoPlayerController.asset(kIntroAsset);
      _controller = controller;
      await controller.initialize().timeout(const Duration(seconds: 6));
      if (_finished || _fading) return;
      controller.addListener(_onPlayerUpdate);
      await controller.play();
      if (_finished || _fading) return;
      _started = true;
      appLog('intro: start');
      if (mounted) setState(() {});
    } catch (e) {
      _beginFade(_IntroEnd.error, const Duration(milliseconds: 250), '$e');
    }
  }

  void _onPlayerUpdate() {
    final controller = _controller;
    if (controller == null || _finished || _fading) return;
    final value = controller.value;
    if (value.hasError) {
      _beginFade(_IntroEnd.error, const Duration(milliseconds: 250),
          value.errorDescription ?? 'player error');
    } else if (value.isCompleted) {
      // No usable duration to time the long fade against (or
      // the end arrived between ticks): short fade from here.
      _beginFade(_IntroEnd.done, const Duration(milliseconds: 250));
    } else if (value.duration > Duration.zero) {
      // Natural end approaching: start the fade to black so
      // the clip melts out instead of cutting off.
      final remaining = value.duration - value.position;
      if (remaining <= const Duration(milliseconds: 800)) {
        _beginFade(_IntroEnd.done, const Duration(milliseconds: 750));
      }
    }
  }

  /// Starts the fade to black and runs the existing finish
  /// path when it lands. The first exit request wins; later
  /// ones are ignored, exactly like _finish's guard. A hard
  /// timer backs the animation up, so even a stalled fade
  /// finishes within the fade length plus 300 ms and the
  /// gate can never hang.
  void _beginFade(_IntroEnd end, Duration fadeDuration, [String? detail]) {
    if (_finished || _fading) return;
    if (!mounted || _showHome) {
      _finish(end, detail);
      return;
    }
    _fading = true;
    _fadeTimer = Timer(fadeDuration + const Duration(milliseconds: 300), () {
      _finish(end, detail);
    });
    final controller = AnimationController(
      vsync: this,
      duration: fadeDuration,
    );
    _fadeController = controller;
    controller.addStatusListener((status) {
      if (status == AnimationStatus.completed) {
        _finish(end, detail);
      }
    });
    setState(() {});
    controller.forward();
  }

  void _finish(_IntroEnd end, [String? detail]) {
    if (_finished) return;
    _finished = true;
    _verdictGiven = true;
    _fadeTimer?.cancel();
    _fadeController?.stop();
    // Record the verdict natively as well: the next gate may
    // run in a recreated isolate where the static above is
    // gone. Fire and forget; a failure only costs a replay.
    unawaited(_channel
        .invokeMethod<bool>('markIntroPlayed')
        .then((_) {}, onError: (_) {}));
    _watchdog?.cancel();
    final controller = _controller;
    _controller = null;
    if (controller != null) {
      controller.removeListener(_onPlayerUpdate);
      // Dispose once the player widget is out of the tree.
      WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
        controller.dispose();
      });
    }
    switch (end) {
      case _IntroEnd.done:
        appLog('intro: done');
        break;
      case _IntroEnd.skipped:
        appLog('intro: skipped');
        break;
      case _IntroEnd.error:
        appLog('intro: error ${detail ?? 'unknown'}');
        break;
      case _IntroEnd.off:
        break;
    }
    if (mounted) {
      setState(() => _showHome = true);
    } else {
      _showHome = true;
    }
  }

  void _onKey(KeyEvent event) {
    if (event is KeyDownEvent) {
      _beginFade(_IntroEnd.skipped, const Duration(milliseconds: 250));
    }
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    _watchdog?.cancel();
    _fadeTimer?.cancel();
    _fadeController?.dispose();
    _controller?.removeListener(_onPlayerUpdate);
    _controller?.dispose();
    _focusNode.dispose();
    super.dispose();
  }

  Widget _playerWidget() {
    final controller = _controller;
    if (!_started || controller == null || !controller.value.isInitialized) {
      return const SizedBox.expand();
    }
    return Center(
      child: AspectRatio(
        aspectRatio: controller.value.aspectRatio,
        child: VideoPlayer(controller),
      ),
    );
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    if (_showHome) return const SystemSelectScreen();
    return PopScope(
      canPop: false,
      child: Scaffold(
        backgroundColor: Colors.black,
        body: KeyboardListener(
          focusNode: _focusNode,
          onKeyEvent: _onKey,
          child: GestureDetector(
            behavior: HitTestBehavior.opaque,
            onTap: () => _beginFade(
              _IntroEnd.skipped,
              const Duration(milliseconds: 250),
            ),
            child: Stack(
              children: [
                Container(
                  color: Colors.black,
                  child: _playerWidget(),
                ),
                if (_fadeController != null)
                  AnimatedBuilder(
                    animation: _fadeController!,
                    builder: (context, _) {
                      return Opacity(
                        opacity: _fadeController!.value,
                        child: const SizedBox.expand(
                          child: ColoredBox(color: Colors.black),
                        ),
                      );
                    },
                  ),
              ],
            ),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// The app's own navigator, so the root BACK handler can raise
/// its popup through the navigator the MaterialApp created.
final GlobalKey<NavigatorState> _appNavigatorKey =
    GlobalKey<NavigatorState>();

/// The channel MainActivity answers on (restart requests ride it).
const MethodChannel _appChannel = MethodChannel('net.itak/emu');

/// BACK at the app root asks first (David, 2026-11-04): leave to
/// the TV home screen, restart the app, or stay. Focus starts on
/// Stay, so a stray OK press can never close the app.
void _showExitAppPopup() {
  final nav = _appNavigatorKey.currentState;
  if (nav == null) return;
  showDialog<void>(
    context: nav.context,
    builder: (dialogContext) {
      return Dialog(
        backgroundColor: const Color(0xFF232338),
        shape: RoundedRectangleBorder(
          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(24),
        ),
        child: Padding(
          padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(28, 24, 28, 16),
          child: Column(
            mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
            crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
            children: [
              const Text(
                'Leave the app?',
                style: TextStyle(
                  fontSize: 26,
                  fontWeight: FontWeight.bold,
                  color: Colors.white,
                ),
              ),
              const SizedBox(height: 12),
              const Text(
                'Close iTaK Gaming and go back to the TV home '
                'screen, or restart the app.',
                style: TextStyle(fontSize: 17, color: Colors.white70),
              ),
              const SizedBox(height: 20),
              Row(
                mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.end,
                children: [
                  TextButton(
                    autofocus: true,
                    onPressed: () => Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop(),
                    child:
                        const Text('Stay', style: TextStyle(fontSize: 17)),
                  ),
                  TextButton(
                    onPressed: () {
                      Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop();
                      SystemNavigator.pop();
                    },
                    child: const Text('Exit to TV home',
                        style: TextStyle(fontSize: 17)),
                  ),
                  TextButton(
                    onPressed: () async {
                      Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop();
                      try {
                        await _appChannel.invokeMethod('restartApp');
                      } catch (_) {
                        // A failed restart request just leaves
                        // the app as it is; never crash the popup.
                      }
                    },
                    child: const Text('Restart the app',
                        style: TextStyle(fontSize: 17)),
                  ),
                ],
              ),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      );
    },
  );
}

class ITaKGamingApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const ITaKGamingApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      title: 'iTaK Gaming',
      navigatorKey: _appNavigatorKey,
      debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false,
      theme: ThemeData.dark().copyWith(
        scaffoldBackgroundColor: const Color(0xFF0A0A14),
        primaryColor: const Color(0xFF00E676),
      ),
      // The exit popup's PopScope lives inside the home route
      // (wrapping the IntroGate) on purpose: a PopScope outside
      // the MaterialApp never sees the root route's pop, and
      // BACK then finishes the activity with no popup at all
      // (proven on David's TV). Inside the home route it sees
      // only root pops; dialogs and pushed routes take BACK
      // themselves first.
      home: PopScope(
        canPop: false,
        onPopInvokedWithResult: (bool didPop, Object? result) {
          if (didPop) return;
          _showExitAppPopup();
        },
        child: const IntroGate(),
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// Key/value store backed by Android SharedPreferences (itak_prefs),
/// shared with the emulator screen. String and int flavors: the Kotlin
/// side reads filter/display modes as ints, so those go through the
/// int methods or the read crashes.
const MethodChannel _logChannel = MethodChannel('net.itak/emu');

/// Writes one line into the app debug log (Settings -> Logs).
/// Native writes it to logcat, and the capture thread files it
/// with every emulator and system line.
Future<void> appLog(String msg) async {
  try {
    await _logChannel.invokeMethod('log', {'message': msg});
  } catch (_) {}
}

class Prefs {
  static const _channel = MethodChannel('net.itak/emu');

  static Future<String?> get(String key) async {
    try {
      return await _channel.invokeMethod<String>('getPref', {'key': key});
    } catch (_) {
      return null;
    }
  }

  static Future<void> set(String key, String value) async {
    try {
      await _channel.invokeMethod('setPref', {'key': key, 'value': value});
    } catch (_) {}
  }

  static Future<int?> getInt(String key) async {
    try {
      return await _channel.invokeMethod<int>('getPrefInt', {'key': key});
    } catch (_) {
      return null;
    }
  }

  static Future<void> setInt(String key, int value) async {
    try {
      await _channel
          .invokeMethod('setPrefInt', {'key': key, 'value': value});
    } catch (_) {}
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Player identity. The first name stays the account key everywhere
// (saves, stats files, server). Each player also carries a middle
// initial, a last initial, and a home state or region, collected when
// the player is added or edited, so the boards can show a fuller
// identity ("David M. P.", Kentucky) and stay organized when more
// people join. Stored as one JSON map in the 'player_info' pref.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const List<String> kUsStates = [
  'AL', 'AK', 'AZ', 'AR', 'CA', 'CO', 'CT', 'DE', 'DC', 'FL', 'GA', 'HI',
  'ID', 'IL', 'IN', 'IA', 'KS', 'KY', 'LA', 'ME', 'MD', 'MA', 'MI', 'MN',
  'MS', 'MO', 'MT', 'NE', 'NV', 'NH', 'NJ', 'NM', 'NY', 'NC', 'ND', 'OH',
  'OK', 'OR', 'PA', 'RI', 'SC', 'SD', 'TN', 'TX', 'UT', 'VT', 'VA', 'WA',
  'WV', 'WI', 'WY',
];

class PlayerIdentity {
  final String middle; // one letter, may be empty
  final String last; // one letter, may be empty
  final String region; // state code or free text, may be empty
  final String city; // free text, may be empty
  const PlayerIdentity(this.middle, this.last, this.region, this.city);

  // A first name is a complete identity now (David, 2026-11-02:
  // keep it simple and small). City, state, and the initials are
  // optional extras; when present they help the leaderboards
  // tell players with the same first name apart.
  bool get complete => true;

  String displayName(String name) {
    final parts = <String>[name];
    if (middle.isNotEmpty) parts.add('$middle.');
    if (last.isNotEmpty) parts.add('$last.');
    var out = parts.join(' ');
    final place = [city, region].where((s) => s.isNotEmpty).join(', ');
    if (place.isNotEmpty) out = '$out, $place';
    return out;
  }
}

class PlayerInfoStore {
  static Map<String, PlayerIdentity> _cache = {};
  static bool _loaded = false;

  static Future<Map<String, PlayerIdentity>> load() async {
    if (_loaded) return _cache;
    _loaded = true;
    final raw = await Prefs.get('player_info');
    if (raw != null && raw.isNotEmpty) {
      try {
        final map = jsonDecode(raw) as Map<String, dynamic>;
        _cache = map.map((k, v) {
          final m = v as Map<String, dynamic>;
          return MapEntry(
            k,
            PlayerIdentity(
              (m['m'] ?? '').toString(),
              (m['l'] ?? '').toString(),
              (m['st'] ?? '').toString(),
              (m['c'] ?? '').toString(),
            ),
          );
        });
      } catch (_) {}
    }
    return _cache;
  }

  static Future<void> _persist() async {
    final map = _cache.map(
      (k, v) => MapEntry(k,
          {'m': v.middle, 'l': v.last, 'st': v.region, 'c': v.city}),
    );
    await Prefs.set('player_info', jsonEncode(map));
  }

  static Future<void> save(String name, PlayerIdentity id) async {
    await load();
    _cache[name] = id;
    await _persist();
  }

  static Future<void> rename(String oldName, String newName) async {
    await load();
    final id = _cache.remove(oldName);
    if (id != null) _cache[newName] = id;
    await _persist();
  }

  static Future<void> remove(String name) async {
    await load();
    _cache.remove(name);
    await _persist();
  }

  static PlayerIdentity? of(String name) => _cache[name];

  static String displayOf(String name) =>
      _cache[name]?.displayName(name) ?? name;

  // The native stats uploader reads these three prefs when it
  // reports a finished session to the global board, so the board
  // can show the same identity as the local screens. Refreshed
  // whenever the current player or their identity changes.
  static Future<void> publishForUpload(String name) async {
    await load();
    final id = _cache[name];
    await Prefs.set('identity_name', name);
    await Prefs.set('identity_display', id?.displayName(name) ?? name);
    await Prefs.set('identity_region', id?.region ?? '');
  }
}

    required this.thumbRepo,

}
