# === Flutter tool backend ===
# _phony_ is a non-existent file to force this command to run every time,
# since currently there's no way to get a full input/output list from the
# flutter tool.
set(PHONY_OUTPUT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/_phony_")
set_source_files_properties("${PHONY_OUTPUT}" PROPERTIES SYMBOLIC TRUE)
add_custom_command(
  OUTPUT ${FLUTTER_LIBRARY} ${FLUTTER_LIBRARY_HEADERS}
    ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_CORE} ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_PLUGIN}
    ${CPP_WRAPPER_SOURCES_APP}
    ${PHONY_OUTPUT}
  COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E env
    ${FLUTTER_TOOL_ENVIRONMENT}

==================== FILE: flutter_ui/windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp ====================

#include "flutter_window.h"

#include <optional>

#include "flutter/generated_plugin_registrant.h"

FlutterWindow::FlutterWindow(const flutter::DartProject& project)
    : project_(project) {}

FlutterWindow::~FlutterWindow() {}

bool FlutterWindow::OnCreate() {
  if (!Win32Window::OnCreate()) {
    return false;
  }

  RECT frame = GetClientArea();

  // The size here must match the window dimensions to avoid unnecessary surface
  // creation / destruction in the startup path.
  flutter_controller_ = std::make_unique<flutter::FlutterViewController>(
      frame.right - frame.left, frame.bottom - frame.top, project_);
  // Ensure that basic setup of the controller was successful.
  if (!flutter_controller_->engine() || !flutter_controller_->view()) {
    return false;
  }
  RegisterPlugins(flutter_controller_->engine());
  SetChildContent(flutter_controller_->view()->GetNativeWindow());

  flutter_controller_->engine()->SetNextFrameCallback([&]() {
    this->Show();
  });

  // Flutter can complete the first frame before the "show window" callback is
  // registered. The following call ensures a frame is pending to ensure the
  // window is shown. It is a no-op if the first frame hasn't completed yet.
  flutter_controller_->ForceRedraw();

  return true;
}

void FlutterWindow::OnDestroy() {
  if (flutter_controller_) {
    flutter_controller_ = nullptr;
  }

  Win32Window::OnDestroy();
}

LRESULT
FlutterWindow::MessageHandler(HWND hwnd, UINT const message,
                              WPARAM const wparam,
                              LPARAM const lparam) noexcept {
  // Give Flutter, including plugins, an opportunity to handle window messages.
  if (flutter_controller_) {
    std::optional<LRESULT> result =
        flutter_controller_->HandleTopLevelWindowProc(hwnd, message, wparam,
                                                      lparam);
    if (result) {
      return *result;
    }
  }

  switch (message) {
    case WM_FONTCHANGE:
      flutter_controller_->engine()->ReloadSystemFonts();
      break;
  }

  return Win32Window::MessageHandler(hwnd, message, wparam, lparam);
}

==================== FILE: flutter_ui/windows/runner/main.cpp ====================

#include <flutter/dart_project.h>
#include <flutter/flutter_view_controller.h>
#include <windows.h>

#include "flutter_window.h"
#include "utils.h"

int APIENTRY wWinMain(_In_ HINSTANCE instance, _In_opt_ HINSTANCE prev,
                      _In_ wchar_t *command_line, _In_ int show_command) {
  // Attach to console when present (e.g., 'flutter run') or create a
  // new console when running with a debugger.
  if (!::AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) && ::IsDebuggerPresent()) {
    CreateAndAttachConsole();
  }

  // Initialize COM, so that it is available for use in the library and/or
  // plugins.
  ::CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED);

  flutter::DartProject project(L"data");

  std::vector<std::string> command_line_arguments =
      GetCommandLineArguments();

  project.set_dart_entrypoint_arguments(std::move(command_line_arguments));

  FlutterWindow window(project);
  Win32Window::Point origin(10, 10);
  Win32Window::Size size(1280, 720);
  if (!window.Create(L"itak_gaming", origin, size)) {
    return EXIT_FAILURE;
  }
  window.SetQuitOnClose(true);

  ::MSG msg;
  while (::GetMessage(&msg, nullptr, 0, 0)) {
    ::TranslateMessage(&msg);
    ::DispatchMessage(&msg);
  }

  ::CoUninitialize();
  return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}

==================== FILE: flutter_ui/windows/runner/utils.cpp ====================

#include "utils.h"

#include <flutter_windows.h>
#include <io.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <windows.h>

#include <iostream>

void CreateAndAttachConsole() {
  if (::AllocConsole()) {
    FILE *unused;
    if (freopen_s(&unused, "CONOUT$", "w", stdout)) {
      _dup2(_fileno(stdout), 1);
    }
    if (freopen_s(&unused, "CONOUT$", "w", stderr)) {
      _dup2(_fileno(stdout), 2);
    }
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio();
    FlutterDesktopResyncOutputStreams();
  }
}

std::vector<std::string> GetCommandLineArguments() {
  // Convert the UTF-16 command line arguments to UTF-8 for the Engine to use.
  int argc;
  wchar_t** argv = ::CommandLineToArgvW(::GetCommandLineW(), &argc);
  if (argv == nullptr) {
    return std::vector<std::string>();
  }

  std::vector<std::string> command_line_arguments;

  // Skip the first argument as it's the binary name.
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
    command_line_arguments.push_back(Utf8FromUtf16(argv[i]));
  }

  ::LocalFree(argv);

  return command_line_arguments;
}

std::string Utf8FromUtf16(const wchar_t* utf16_string) {
  if (utf16_string == nullptr) {
    return std::string();
  }
  unsigned int target_length = ::WideCharToMultiByte(
      CP_UTF8, WC_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf16_string,
      -1, nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr)
    -1; // remove the trailing null character
  int input_length = (int)wcslen(utf16_string);
  std::string utf8_string;
  if (target_length == 0 || target_length > utf8_string.max_size()) {
    return utf8_string;
  }
  utf8_string.resize(target_length);
  int converted_length = ::WideCharToMultiByte(
      CP_UTF8, WC_ERR_INVALID_CHARS, utf16_string,
      input_length, utf8_string.data(), target_length, nullptr, nullptr);
  if (converted_length == 0) {
    return std::string();
  }
  return utf8_string;
}

==================== FILE: flutter_ui/windows/runner/win32_window.cpp ====================

#include "win32_window.h"

#include <dwmapi.h>
#include <flutter_windows.h>

#include "resource.h"

namespace {

/// Window attribute that enables dark mode window decorations.
///
/// Redefined in case the developer's machine has a Windows SDK older than
/// version 10.0.22000.0.
/// See: https://docs.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/dwmapi/ne-dwmapi-dwmwindowattribute
#ifndef DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE
#define DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE 20
#endif

constexpr const wchar_t kWindowClassName[] = L"FLUTTER_RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW";

/// Registry key for app theme preference.
///
/// A value of 0 indicates apps should use dark mode. A non-zero or missing
/// value indicates apps should use light mode.
constexpr const wchar_t kGetPreferredBrightnessRegKey[] =
  L"Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Themes\\Personalize";
constexpr const wchar_t kGetPreferredBrightnessRegValue[] = L"AppsUseLightTheme";

// The number of Win32Window objects that currently exist.
static int g_active_window_count = 0;

using EnableNonClientDpiScaling = BOOL __stdcall(HWND hwnd);

// Scale helper to convert logical scaler values to physical using passed in
// scale factor
int Scale(int source, double scale_factor) {
  return static_cast<int>(source * scale_factor);
}

// Dynamically loads the |EnableNonClientDpiScaling| from the User32 module.
// This API is only needed for PerMonitor V1 awareness mode.
void EnableFullDpiSupportIfAvailable(HWND hwnd) {
  HMODULE user32_module = LoadLibraryA("User32.dll");
  if (!user32_module) {
    return;
  }
  auto enable_non_client_dpi_scaling =
      reinterpret_cast<EnableNonClientDpiScaling*>(
          GetProcAddress(user32_module, "EnableNonClientDpiScaling"));
  if (enable_non_client_dpi_scaling != nullptr) {
    enable_non_client_dpi_scaling(hwnd);
  }
  FreeLibrary(user32_module);
}

}  // namespace

// Manages the Win32Window's window class registration.
class WindowClassRegistrar {
 public:
  ~WindowClassRegistrar() = default;

  // Returns the singleton registrar instance.
  static WindowClassRegistrar* GetInstance() {
    if (!instance_) {
      instance_ = new WindowClassRegistrar();
    }
    return instance_;
  }

  // Returns the name of the window class, registering the class if it hasn't
  // previously been registered.
  const wchar_t* GetWindowClass();

  // Unregisters the window class. Should only be called if there are no
  // instances of the window.
  void UnregisterWindowClass();

 private:
  WindowClassRegistrar() = default;

  static WindowClassRegistrar* instance_;

  bool class_registered_ = false;
};

WindowClassRegistrar* WindowClassRegistrar::instance_ = nullptr;

const wchar_t* WindowClassRegistrar::GetWindowClass() {
  if (!class_registered_) {
    WNDCLASS window_class{};
    window_class.hCursor = LoadCursor(nullptr, IDC_ARROW);
    window_class.lpszClassName = kWindowClassName;
    window_class.style = CS_HREDRAW | CS_VREDRAW;
    window_class.cbClsExtra = 0;
    window_class.cbWndExtra = 0;
    window_class.hInstance = GetModuleHandle(nullptr);
    window_class.hIcon =
        LoadIcon(window_class.hInstance, MAKEINTRESOURCE(IDI_APP_ICON));
    window_class.hbrBackground = 0;
    window_class.lpszMenuName = nullptr;
    window_class.lpfnWndProc = Win32Window::WndProc;
    RegisterClass(&window_class);
    class_registered_ = true;
  }
  return kWindowClassName;
}

void WindowClassRegistrar::UnregisterWindowClass() {
  UnregisterClass(kWindowClassName, nullptr);
  class_registered_ = false;
}

Win32Window::Win32Window() {
  ++g_active_window_count;
}

Win32Window::~Win32Window() {
  --g_active_window_count;
  Destroy();
}

bool Win32Window::Create(const std::wstring& title,
                         const Point& origin,
                         const Size& size) {
  Destroy();

  const wchar_t* window_class =
      WindowClassRegistrar::GetInstance()->GetWindowClass();

  const POINT target_point = {static_cast<LONG>(origin.x),
                              static_cast<LONG>(origin.y)};
  HMONITOR monitor = MonitorFromPoint(target_point, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST);
  UINT dpi = FlutterDesktopGetDpiForMonitor(monitor);
  double scale_factor = dpi / 96.0;

  HWND window = CreateWindow(
      window_class, title.c_str(), WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW,
      Scale(origin.x, scale_factor), Scale(origin.y, scale_factor),
      Scale(size.width, scale_factor), Scale(size.height, scale_factor),
      nullptr, nullptr, GetModuleHandle(nullptr), this);

  if (!window) {
    return false;
  }

  UpdateTheme(window);

  return OnCreate();
}

bool Win32Window::Show() {
  return ShowWindow(window_handle_, SW_SHOWNORMAL);
}

// static
LRESULT CALLBACK Win32Window::WndProc(HWND const window,
                                      UINT const message,
                                      WPARAM const wparam,
                                      LPARAM const lparam) noexcept {
  if (message == WM_NCCREATE) {
    auto window_struct = reinterpret_cast<CREATESTRUCT*>(lparam);
    SetWindowLongPtr(window, GWLP_USERDATA,
                     reinterpret_cast<LONG_PTR>(window_struct->lpCreateParams));

    auto that = static_cast<Win32Window*>(window_struct->lpCreateParams);
    EnableFullDpiSupportIfAvailable(window);
    that->window_handle_ = window;
  } else if (Win32Window* that = GetThisFromHandle(window)) {
    return that->MessageHandler(window, message, wparam, lparam);
  }

  return DefWindowProc(window, message, wparam, lparam);
}

LRESULT
Win32Window::MessageHandler(HWND hwnd,
                            UINT const message,
                            WPARAM const wparam,
                            LPARAM const lparam) noexcept {
  switch (message) {
    case WM_DESTROY:
      window_handle_ = nullptr;
      Destroy();
      if (quit_on_close_) {
        PostQuitMessage(0);
      }
      return 0;

    case WM_DPICHANGED: {
      auto newRectSize = reinterpret_cast<RECT*>(lparam);
      LONG newWidth = newRectSize->right - newRectSize->left;
      LONG newHeight = newRectSize->bottom - newRectSize->top;

      SetWindowPos(hwnd, nullptr, newRectSize->left, newRectSize->top, newWidth,
                   newHeight, SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE);

      return 0;
    }
    case WM_SIZE: {
      RECT rect = GetClientArea();
      if (child_content_ != nullptr) {
        // Size and position the child window.
        MoveWindow(child_content_, rect.left, rect.top, rect.right - rect.left,
                   rect.bottom - rect.top, TRUE);
      }
      return 0;
    }

    case WM_ACTIVATE:
      if (child_content_ != nullptr) {
        SetFocus(child_content_);
      }
      return 0;

    case WM_DWMCOLORIZATIONCOLORCHANGED:
      UpdateTheme(hwnd);
      return 0;
  }

  return DefWindowProc(window_handle_, message, wparam, lparam);
}

void Win32Window::Destroy() {
  OnDestroy();

  if (window_handle_) {
    DestroyWindow(window_handle_);
    window_handle_ = nullptr;
  }
  if (g_active_window_count == 0) {
    WindowClassRegistrar::GetInstance()->UnregisterWindowClass();
  }
}

Win32Window* Win32Window::GetThisFromHandle(HWND const window) noexcept {
  return reinterpret_cast<Win32Window*>(
      GetWindowLongPtr(window, GWLP_USERDATA));
}

void Win32Window::SetChildContent(HWND content) {
  child_content_ = content;
  SetParent(content, window_handle_);
  RECT frame = GetClientArea();

  MoveWindow(content, frame.left, frame.top, frame.right - frame.left,
             frame.bottom - frame.top, true);

  SetFocus(child_content_);
}

RECT Win32Window::GetClientArea() {
  RECT frame;
  GetClientRect(window_handle_, &frame);
  return frame;
}

HWND Win32Window::GetHandle() {
  return window_handle_;
}

void Win32Window::SetQuitOnClose(bool quit_on_close) {
  quit_on_close_ = quit_on_close;
}

bool Win32Window::OnCreate() {
  // No-op; provided for subclasses.
  return true;
}

void Win32Window::OnDestroy() {
  // No-op; provided for subclasses.
}

void Win32Window::UpdateTheme(HWND const window) {
  DWORD light_mode;
  DWORD light_mode_size = sizeof(light_mode);
  LSTATUS result = RegGetValue(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, kGetPreferredBrightnessRegKey,
                               kGetPreferredBrightnessRegValue,
                               RRF_RT_REG_DWORD, nullptr, &light_mode,
                               &light_mode_size);

  if (result == ERROR_SUCCESS) {
    BOOL enable_dark_mode = light_mode == 0;
    DwmSetWindowAttribute(window, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE,
                          &enable_dark_mode, sizeof(enable_dark_mode));
  }
}


==================== FILE: flutter_ui/windows/runner/win32_window.h ====================

#ifndef RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW_H_
#define RUNNER_WIN32_WINDOW_H_

#include <windows.h>

#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

// A class abstraction for a high DPI-aware Win32 Window. Intended to be
// inherited from by classes that wish to specialize with custom
// rendering and input handling
class Win32Window {
 public:
  struct Point {
    unsigned int x;
    unsigned int y;
    Point(unsigned int x, unsigned int y) : x(x), y(y) {}
  };

  struct Size {
    unsigned int width;
    unsigned int height;
    Size(unsigned int width, unsigned int height)
        : width(width), height(height) {}
  };

  Win32Window();
  virtual ~Win32Window();

  // Creates a win32 window with |title| that is positioned and sized using

  bool Create(const std::wstring& title, const Point& origin, const Size& size);

==================== FILE: go_backend/BACKUP_HOLD.md ====================

# Backup-and-Hold: design note

The save-state audit (~/itak-rust-bridge/SAVE_STATES.md) found
the switch's data-loss trap: the app has no battery files, each
saves/<player>/<game>.sav holds the core's full state blob, a
failed load is graceful, but auto-save (on by default) overwrites
that same file every 60 seconds and again on exit. After a core
swap the old blob fails to load and the only copy of the player's
progress is silently overwritten within about a minute. This
feature is the adopted countermeasure. It lives in the staged
switch backend (~/itak-switch-backend) plus one staged Kotlin
file (~/itak-switch-app). Nothing here touches ~/itak-repo.

## Trigger

The trigger fires inside core.LoadRust (internal/core/
native_rust.go), at the one moment a Rust core is known to be
about to serve: the adapter library opened, its ABI magic and
major version checked, a handle created, and its system id
accepted. Construction failures never fire it. The pure-Go path
(LoadNative) never calls it, and neither does the desktop .so
bridge. LoadRust's signature has no error return, so a protection
failure is deferred to LoadGame, the same surface construction
failures already use: the app sees the load fail, logs why, and
no Rust game ever runs unprotected.

Once per root, not once per launch: a completed protection
writes a versioned marker (see below). Later launches and later
switch builds find the marker, log that protection already
exists, and do not back up again, do not hold again.

Contexts with no app files root configured (desktop harnesses,
core tests) skip protection inside switchguard with a one-line
log: they have no saves tree to protect. The app always
configures its root before loading a core (staged Kotlin edit
1), so a shipped switched build cannot reach the Rust path
unconfigured.

## Backup

Location rule, derived from the app's storage layout
(EmulatorActivity.kt: filesDir/saves/<player>/<game>.sav, plus
the legacy filesDir/saves/<game>.sav):

- Live tree: <filesDir>/saves, never written by this feature.
- Backup: <filesDir>/saves-backup-before-rust, a verbatim copy
  of the whole saves tree (every regular file, relative paths
  preserved, byte-identical). No code path writes to it after
  creation; there is no restore, prune, or rotation code.
- If that name is already taken (an earlier backup, or anything
  else) it is never overwritten: the copy goes to
  saves-backup-before-rust-2, then -3, and so on.
- Marker: <filesDir>/switchguard/marker.json, written only
  after the copy completes, atomically (tmp file plus rename).
  Format carries a version field (1) plus created time, backup
  dir name, file count, and total bytes.
- A partial copy is removed on failure, so a half backup can
  never be mistaken for a complete one on the next attempt.
- A fresh install with no saves tree still protects: an empty
  backup plus a marker recording zero files.

## Hold

Protection starts the hold in the same call. While the hold is
active, mobile.AutoSaveState returns nil, and the activity's
two automatic saves (the 60 second timer and the exit save)
both route through AutoSaveState in the staged Kotlin, so the
auto-save path writes nothing into the live saves tree. Manual
saves are never blocked: they use Mobile.saveState as before.

The hold ends at the first of:

- the player saves manually once (Kotlin doSave calls
  Mobile.noteManualSave after its write lands), or
- the session ends cleanly (mobile.Close calls
  switchguard.EndHold).

The hold is process state only. It is never written to the
player's stored auto-save preference (the itak_prefs "autosave"
key is read by the activity exactly as before and written by
nobody in this feature), and gate tests prove the stored
preference survives a full cycle byte-identical. The exit
dialog asks Mobile.backupHoldActive so it does not promise an
auto-save while the hold is on.

Why a one-session hold is enough: the backup is the durable
protection. The hold covers the audited danger window, the
first session, where a player whose old save failed to load
would otherwise lose it before ever deciding to save by hand.
From the second session on, the pre-switch saves still exist
in the backup even if the live slot has moved on.

## Failure behavior

- Backup copy fails (unreadable saves tree, unwritable root,
  marker write fails): EnsureProtected returns an error naming
  the failure, LoadRust converts it into a deferred LoadGame
  error, and the log carries "backup-hold: refusing Rust core
  <name>: backup-hold: backup failed, Rust core refused: ...".
  No marker, no hold, no partial backup left behind.
- Marker exists but does not parse, or carries a foreign
  version: treated as a failure, never as "already protected".
  Guessing here could skip a needed backup.
- Pure-Go builds: no trigger, no backup, no hold, never blocked.

## Diagnostics

Every step goes through the standard log package with the
"backup-hold:" prefix (the backend's diagnostic channel; the
bridges log the same way, and it reaches logcat and the app's
log screen): root configured, trigger, backup source and
destination, files and bytes copied, backup complete, hold
start, every skipped auto-save, hold end with its reason,
already-protected notices, and refusals with their cause.

## Files assembly must take

Backend (from ~/itak-switch-backend):

- internal/switchguard/switchguard.go (new package)
- internal/switchguard/switchguard_test.go (new)
- internal/core/native_rust.go (trigger wiring in LoadRust,
  one import)
- internal/core/backup_hold_test.go (new)
- mobile/backup_hold.go (new: SetFilesDir, BackupHoldActive,
  NoteManualSave, AutoSaveState)
- mobile/backup_hold_test.go (new: the live drill)
- mobile/mobile.go (Close ends the hold; one import)
- BACKUP_HOLD.md (this note)

App (from ~/itak-switch-app, a copy of flutter_ui; the only
changed file is android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/itak/
itak_gaming/EmulatorActivity.kt, five edits):

1. onCreate: Mobile.setFilesDir(filesDir.absolutePath)
   immediately before Mobile.loadCore, beside setSystemDir.
2. The 60 second auto-save calls Mobile.autoSaveState()
   instead of Mobile.saveState().
3. autoSaveNow (the exit save) calls Mobile.autoSaveState().
4. doSave calls Mobile.noteManualSave() after its write.
5. confirmExit checks Mobile.backupHoldActive() for its
   message text.

No Dart change, no pubspec change, no new permissions. The
gomobile names surface in Kotlin exactly as written above
(setFilesDir, autoSaveState, noteManualSave, backupHoldActive),
matching the existing setSystemDir / saveState pattern.

## Gate record (2026-10-22, this host)

- go test ./... : all packages pass, same as the pristine
  baseline run taken before the changes.
- Targeted gates: switchguard 6 tests (byte-identical backup;
  second run leaves the backup untouched and starts no hold;
  backup failure refuses with no marker and no partial backup;
  stored preference unchanged across a full cycle and the hold
  ends on manual save; existing backup without a marker gets a
  sibling; empty tree still protects). Core 3 tests (pure-Go
  path creates nothing and is never blocked; failed Rust
  construction creates nothing; real adapter plus unmakeable
  backup refuses at LoadGame naming the failure).
- Live drill (mobile TestBackupHoldDrill, pilot configuration):
  a real Go-produced tobutobugirl state at frame 300 seeded as
  saves/Player 1/tobutobugirl.sav; the Rust Game Boy adapter
  served through production LoadCore and NativeBridge; backup
  byte-identical (2 files, 150,791 bytes); AutoSaveState nil
  during the hold with the live tree untouched while manual
  SaveState returned bytes; the Go state loaded into the Rust
  core and its frame-900 continuation state was byte-identical
  to the Go core's own frame-900 state; hold ended on the
  manual save; preference bytes unchanged.
- Race: go test -race on internal/switchguard, internal/core,
  mobile, internal/save: clean.
- go vet ./... clean; gofmt clean on all touched files.
- The env-gated production bridge test (TestRustBridgeAdapter,
  ITAK_RUST_TEST_SO pointed at the current adapter build)
  passes with the trigger wired in.

## What assembly still owes

- Ship the staged Kotlin file with the switched build. A
  switched build without edit 1 never configures the root and
  the backend then skips protection as a non-app context; the
  pairing is the safety property.
- Device proof, when a stick is reachable: seed an old-format
  save, install the switched build, confirm the backup folder
  on disk and the hold lines in the app log, and confirm the
  second launch creates nothing new.
- A restore path for the backup is deliberately not built: the
  backup is a safety copy a human can inspect or copy back by
  hand. Building restore UI is a separate decision.


==================== FILE: go_backend/cmd/coretest/main.go ====================

package main

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"fmt"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/core"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/save"
)

func frameHash(b *core.Bridge) string {
	_, _, rgba, err := b.FrameToRGBA()
	if err != nil { return "" }
	s := sha256.Sum256(rgba)
	return fmt.Sprintf("%x", s[:8])
}

func main() {
	b, err := core.LoadCore("/home/hatch/workspace/itak-gaming/testdata/snes9x_libretro.so")
	if err != nil { fmt.Printf("FAILED load core: %v\n", err); return; }
	defer b.Close()
	if err := b.LoadGame("/home/hatch/workspace/itak-gaming/testdata/Super Mario World (USA).sfc"); err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("FAILED load game: %v\n", err); return
	}

	// --- AUDIO TEST ---
	for i := 0; i < 120; i++ { b.RunFrame() }
	samples := b.DrainAudio(48000)
	nonSilent := 0
	for _, s := range samples { if s != 0 { nonSilent++ } }
	fmt.Printf("AUDIO: total frames produced=%d, drained samples=%d, non-silent=%d\n",
		b.AudioSamplesTotal(), len(samples), nonSilent)

	// --- SAVE STATE TEST ---
	// Get to title, press start for file select, snapshot state
	for i := 0; i < 480; i++ { b.RunFrame() }
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonStart, true)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ { b.RunFrame() }
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonStart, false)
	for i := 0; i < 120; i++ { b.RunFrame() }
	hashAtSave := frameHash(b)

	state, err := b.SaveState()
	if err != nil { fmt.Printf("FAILED save state: %v\n", err); return }
	fmt.Printf("SAVE STATE: captured %d bytes at file-select (hash %s)\n", len(state), hashAtSave)

	// Save it under two different players via the save manager
	mgr := save.NewManager("/tmp/itak_saves")
	mgr.Save("dad", "Super Mario World (USA)", 0, state)
	mgr.Save("kid", "Super Mario World (USA)", 0, state)
	fmt.Println("SAVE MANAGER: wrote state for players 'dad' and 'kid'")

	// Play on: move cursor down (changes screen), then load the state back
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonDown, true)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ { b.RunFrame() }
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonDown, false)
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ { b.RunFrame() }
	hashMoved := frameHash(b)
	fmt.Printf("After moving cursor: hash %s (differs: %v)\n", hashMoved, hashMoved != hashAtSave)

	// Load dad's state back
	loaded, err := mgr.Load("dad", "Super Mario World (USA)", 0)
	if err != nil { fmt.Printf("FAILED load from manager: %v\n", err); return }
	if err := b.LoadState(loaded); err != nil { fmt.Printf("FAILED load state: %v\n", err); return }
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ { b.RunFrame() }
	hashRestored := frameHash(b)
	fmt.Printf("After restoring save: hash %s\n", hashRestored)
	// Note: 2 frames of fade may differ slightly; check save/load round trip byte equality
	state2, _ := b.SaveState()
	same := len(state2) == len(state)
	if same {
		for i := range state { if state[i] != state2[i] { same = false; break } }
	}
	fmt.Printf("SAVE ROUND TRIP: state identical after reload: %v\n", same)
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/cmd/enginetest/main.go ====================

// Command enginetest runs the iTaK engine (libretro bridge +
// per-player save manager) against a core and a ROM and reports
// PASS/FAIL lines for: core load, game load, AV info, video
// frames, audio output, save-state capture, per-player save
// round trip, and state restore byte equality.
//
// It is the cross-platform sibling of cmd/coretest (which has
// Linux paths baked in): pass -core and -rom for the platform's
// core library (.so on Linux, .dll on Windows). Every line is
// printed and also written to the result file (-out, default
// itak-test-result.txt next to the executable) so a run on a
// machine without a console still leaves a report behind.
package main

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/core"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/save"
)

var failures int
var logFile *os.File

func say(format string, args ...any) {
	line := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
	fmt.Println(line)
	if logFile != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(logFile, line)
	}
}

func fail(format string, args ...any) {
	failures++
	say("FAILED "+format, args...)
}

func frameHash(b *core.Bridge) string {
	_, _, rgba, err := b.FrameToRGBA()
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	s := sha256.Sum256(rgba)
	return fmt.Sprintf("%x", s[:8])
}

func main() {
	corePath := flag.String("core", "", "path to the libretro core library (.so or .dll)")
	romPath := flag.String("rom", "", "path to the ROM file")
	outPath := flag.String("out", "", "result file (default: itak-test-result.txt next to the exe)")
	flag.Parse()

	out := *outPath
	if out == "" {
		if exe, err := os.Executable(); err == nil {
			out = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(exe), "itak-test-result.txt")
		} else {
			out = "itak-test-result.txt"
		}
	}
	if f, err := os.Create(out); err == nil {
		logFile = f
	}

	say("=== iTaK Gaming engine test (%s/%s) ===", runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
	say("core: %s", *corePath)
	say("rom:  %s", *romPath)
	if *corePath == "" || *romPath == "" {
		fail("both -core and -rom are required")
		finish()
	}

	b, err := core.LoadCore(*corePath)
	if err != nil {
		fail("load core: %v", err)
		finish()
	}
	defer b.Close()
	say("core loaded")

	if err := b.LoadGame(*romPath); err != nil {
		fail("load game: %v", err)
		finish()
	}
	say("game loaded")
	say("AV: aspect=%.4f fps=%.2f audio=%.0f Hz pixelFormat=%d",
		b.AspectRatio(), b.FPS(), b.SampleRate(), b.PixelFormat())

	// Video + audio: run 2 seconds worth of frames.
	for i := 0; i < 120; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	w, h, _, ferr := b.FrameToRGBA()
	if ferr != nil {
		fail("frame decode: %v", ferr)
	} else {
		say("video: %dx%d, frames=%d, non-blank=%v",
			w, h, b.VideoFrameCount(), b.VideoEverNonzero())
		if !b.VideoEverNonzero() {
			fail("video frames are all blank")
		}
	}
	samples := b.DrainAudio(48000)
	nonSilent := 0
	for _, s := range samples {
		if s != 0 {
			nonSilent++
		}
	}
	say("audio: produced=%d drained=%d non-silent=%d",
		b.AudioSamplesTotal(), len(samples), nonSilent)
	if nonSilent == 0 {
		fail("audio is silent")
	}

	// Save states: title screen, press Start, snapshot.
	for i := 0; i < 480; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonStart, true)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonStart, false)
	for i := 0; i < 120; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	hashAtSave := frameHash(b)
	state, err := b.SaveState()
	if err != nil {
		fail("save state: %v", err)
		finish()
	}
	say("save state: %d bytes at frame hash %s", len(state), hashAtSave)

	// Per-player saves through the save manager.
	tmp, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "itak_saves")
	if err != nil {
		fail("temp dir: %v", err)
		finish()
	}
	defer os.RemoveAll(tmp)
	gameName := filepath.Base(*romPath)
	mgr := save.NewManager(tmp)
	if err := mgr.Save("dad", gameName, 0, state); err != nil {
		fail("manager save dad: %v", err)
	}
	if err := mgr.Save("kid", gameName, 0, state); err != nil {
		fail("manager save kid: %v", err)
	}
	say("save manager: wrote one state each for players dad and kid")

	// Play on (screen changes), then restore dad's state.
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonDown, true)
	for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	b.SetButton(0, core.ButtonDown, false)
	for i := 0; i < 30; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	say("after moving on: hash %s (differs from save point: %v)",
		frameHash(b), frameHash(b) != hashAtSave)

	loaded, err := mgr.Load("dad", gameName, 0)
	if err != nil {
		fail("manager load dad: %v", err)
		finish()
	}
	if err := b.LoadState(loaded); err != nil {
		fail("load state: %v", err)
		finish()
	}
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		b.RunFrame()
	}
	// The restore is exact when the screen is back at the save
	// point. (A re-serialized state after running frames is not
	// byte-compared: cores advance internal counters as they run.)
	hashRestored := frameHash(b)
	say("after restoring save: hash %s (save point %s)", hashRestored, hashAtSave)
	if hashRestored != hashAtSave {
		fail("restored frame does not match the save point")
	}
	finish()
}

func finish() {
	if failures == 0 {
		say("RESULT: ALL TESTS PASSED")
	} else {
		say("RESULT: %d FAILURE(S)", failures)
	}
	if logFile != nil {
		logFile.Close()
	}
	if failures > 0 {
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}

package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"runtime"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/server"
)

func main() {
	var (
		addr    = flag.String("addr", "127.0.0.1:8081", "API server address")
		saveDir = flag.String("savedir", "./data", "Save data directory")
		romDir  = flag.String("romdir", "./roms", "ROM directory")
	)
	flag.Parse()

	is64Bit := runtime.GOARCH == "amd64" || runtime.GOARCH == "arm64"
	fmt.Printf("iTaK Gaming Backend (64-bit: %v)\n", is64Bit)

	srv := server.New(*saveDir, *romDir, is64Bit)
	log.Printf("Starting API server on %s", *addr)
	if err := srv.Start(*addr); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/cmd/netplayguest/main.go ====================

// netplayguest is a headless netplay test client: it joins a lobby
// as the guest, runs the lockstep session against the real core and
// ROM, presses Start at a scripted frame, and reports the final
// state hash. It exists to prove box-to-box sync without needing a
// second TV: the TV hosts, this guest plays.
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/core"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/netsession"
)

type adapter struct{ b *core.Bridge }

func (a adapter) RunFrame() { a.b.RunFrame() }

func (a adapter) SetButtons(player int, mask uint16) {
	for i := 0; i < 16; i++ {
		a.b.SetButton(player, i, mask&(1<<uint(i)) != 0)
	}
}

func (a adapter) SaveState() []byte {
	data, err := a.b.SaveState()
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	return data
}

func (a adapter) LoadState(d []byte) error { return a.b.LoadState(d) }

func httpJSON(method, url string, body any, out any) error {
	var rdr io.Reader
	if body != nil {
		buf, _ := json.Marshal(body)
		rdr = bytes.NewReader(buf)
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequest(method, url, rdr)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if body != nil {
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	}
	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	data, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", resp.Status, data)
	}
	if out != nil && len(data) > 0 {
		return json.Unmarshal(data, out)
	}
	return nil
}

func main() {
	server := flag.String("server", "http://127.0.0.1:8790", "lobby server base URL")
	corePath := flag.String("core", "", "libretro core .so path")
	romPath := flag.String("rom", "", "ROM path")
	lobbyID := flag.String("lobby", "", "lobby id (default: first open lobby)")
	asHost := flag.Bool("host", false, "create the lobby and play as host (player 1)")
	givenToken := flag.String("token", "", "skip lobby create/join; use this token with -lobby")
	frames := flag.Int("frames", 3600, "frames to simulate")
	startAt := flag.Int("start-at", 400, "frame to start pressing Start")
	pressFor := flag.Int("press-for", 12, "frames to hold Start")
	name := flag.String("name", "", "player name for the waiting room (default TestHost/TestGuest)")
	readyDelay := flag.Int("ready-delay", -1, "seconds before pressing Ready in the room; -1 readies instantly")
	pauseAt := flag.Int("pause-at", -1, "frame at which to signal a pause (as a player opening their menu would)")
	pauseSecs := flag.Int("pause-secs", 20, "how long the -pause-at pause lasts")
	flag.Parse()
	if *name == "" {
		if *asHost {
			*name = "TestHost"
		} else {
			*name = "TestGuest"
		}
	}
	if *corePath == "" || *romPath == "" {
		fmt.Println("need -core and -rom")
		os.Exit(2)
	}

	token := *givenToken
	if token != "" {
		// Token supplied: straight to the session.
	} else if *asHost {
		var created struct {
			ID        string `json:"id"`
			HostToken string `json:"hostToken"`
		}
		gameName := filepath.Base(*romPath)
		if err := httpJSON("POST", *server+"/lobbies",
			map[string]any{"name": "TestHost lobby", "game": gameName,
				"hostPlayer": *name, "password": ""}, &created); err != nil {
			fmt.Println("create:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		*lobbyID = created.ID
		token = created.HostToken
		fmt.Println("hosting lobby", created.ID)
	}
	// Find and join the lobby.
	var list struct {
		Lobbies []struct {
			ID   string `json:"id"`
			Game string `json:"game"`
		} `json:"lobbies"`
	}
	if err := httpJSON("GET", *server+"/lobbies", nil, &list); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("list lobbies:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	id := *lobbyID
	if !*asHost {
		// guest path continues below
	} else {
		goto joined
	}
	if id == "" {
		if len(list.Lobbies) == 0 {
			fmt.Println("no open lobbies")
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		id = list.Lobbies[0].ID
	}
	{
		var join struct {
			GuestToken string `json:"guestToken"`
		}
		if err := httpJSON("POST", *server+"/lobbies/"+id+"/join",
			map[string]any{"player": *name, "password": ""}, &join); err != nil {
			fmt.Println("join:", err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		token = join.GuestToken
		fmt.Println("joined lobby", id)
	}
joined:

	bridge, err := core.LoadCore(*corePath)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("load core:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	if err := bridge.LoadGame(*romPath); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("load game:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	romBytes, err := os.ReadFile(*romPath)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("read rom:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(romBytes)

	wsBase := "ws" + (*server)[4:]
	conn, err := netsession.DialWS(wsBase+"/ws?lobby="+id+"&token="+token, 10*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("dial:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	sess := netsession.NewSession(conn, adapter{bridge}, netsession.Config{
		Game:       filepath.Base(*romPath),
		ROMHash:    hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]),
		IsHost:     *asHost,
		PlayerName: *name,
		ReadyNow:   *readyDelay < 0,
	})
	if *readyDelay >= 0 {
		go func() {
			time.Sleep(time.Duration(*readyDelay) * time.Second)
			sess.SetReady()
			fmt.Println("pressed Ready in the room")
		}()
	}
	t0 := time.Now()
	if err := sess.Start(); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("session start:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("session started, stepping", *frames, "frames")
	const btnStart = uint16(1) << 3
	for f := 0; f < *frames; f++ {
		if f == *pauseAt {
			fmt.Printf("pausing for %ds at frame %d (menu open)\n",
				*pauseSecs, f)
			sess.SetPaused(true)
			time.Sleep(time.Duration(*pauseSecs) * time.Second)
			sess.SetPaused(false)
			fmt.Println("resumed from pause")
		}
		var mask uint16
		if f >= *startAt && f < *startAt+*pressFor {
			mask = btnStart
		}
		if *asHost {
			// Drive the menus: confirm file, pick 1 player, skip story.
			for _, at := range []int{1100, 1300, 1550, 1750} {
				if f >= at && f < at+*pressFor {
					mask = btnStart
				}
			}
		}
		if err := sess.Step(mask); err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("step %d: %v\n", f, err)
			os.Exit(1)
		}
		if (f+1)%600 == 0 {
			fmt.Printf("frame %d (%.1fs wall)\n", f+1, time.Since(t0).Seconds())
		}
	}
	state, err := bridge.SaveState()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("save state:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	finalSum := sha256.Sum256(state)
	fmt.Printf("DONE frames=%d desyncs=%d state_sha256=%s\n",
		sess.Frame(), sess.Desyncs(), hex.EncodeToString(finalSum[:]))
	sess.End("test complete")
}

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package core

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/switchguard"
)

// Backup-and-hold trigger tests. The guard's own copy logic is
// gated in internal/switchguard; these tests gate the wiring:
// the trigger fires only on the Rust path, only when a Rust
// core actually constructs, and a failed backup turns into a
// refused serve at LoadGame.

func seedCoreSaves(t *testing.T, root string) {
	t.Helper()
	p := filepath.Join(root, "saves", "Player 1", "game.sav")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte("progress"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func backupExists(root string) bool {
	_, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, switchguard.BackupDirName))
	return err == nil
}

// Gate (d): the pure-Go path creates no backup, starts no hold,
// and is never blocked, even with a root configured and saves
// present.
func TestPureGoPathCreatesNoBackup(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	seedCoreSaves(t, root)
	switchguard.Configure(root)
	defer switchguard.Reset()

	nb, ok := LoadNative("/cores/libgo_gameboy.so")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("LoadNative does not know libgo_gameboy.so")
	}
	defer nb.Close()
	rom := writeGame(t, "spin.gb", gbROM())
	if err := nb.LoadGame(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("pure-Go LoadGame blocked: %v", err)
	}
	nb.RunFrame()
	if backupExists(root) {
		t.Fatalf("pure-Go path created a backup")
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "switchguard")); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatalf("pure-Go path wrote guard state")
	}
	if switchguard.HoldActive() {
		t.Fatalf("pure-Go path started a hold")
	}
}

// A Rust library that fails to construct never serves a game,
// so the trigger must not fire for it either.
func TestRustConstructionFailureCreatesNoBackup(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	seedCoreSaves(t, root)
	switchguard.Configure(root)
	defer switchguard.Reset()

	nb, ok := LoadRust("/cores/libitak_gameboy.so")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("LoadRust does not know libitak_gameboy.so")
	}
	defer nb.Close()
	rom := writeGame(t, "spin.gb", gbROM())
	if err := nb.LoadGame(rom); err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame with a missing adapter library succeeded")
	}
	if backupExists(root) {
		t.Fatalf("failed Rust construction created a backup")
	}
	if switchguard.HoldActive() {
		t.Fatalf("failed Rust construction started a hold")
	}
}

// Gate (e), wiring level: a real adapter library constructs,
// the backup cannot be made, and the serve is refused loudly
// at LoadGame with the backup failure named.
func TestRustBackupFailureRefusesServe(t *testing.T) {
	so := os.Getenv("ITAK_BACKUP_TEST_SO")
	if so == "" {
		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
		so = filepath.Join(home, "itak-adapter-gameboy", "target", "release", "libitak_gameboy.so")
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(so)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("adapter library not available at %s", so)
	}
	dir := t.TempDir()
	soPath := filepath.Join(dir, "libitak_gameboy.so")
	if err := os.WriteFile(soPath, data, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	root := t.TempDir()
	// A saves path that is a regular file, not a tree: the
	// backup copy cannot be made, on any uid.
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "saves"), []byte("not a tree"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	switchguard.Configure(root)
	defer switchguard.Reset()

	nb, ok := LoadRust(soPath)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("LoadRust does not know the adapter name")
	}
	defer nb.Close()
	rom := writeGame(t, "spin.gb", gbROM())
	err = nb.LoadGame(rom)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("Rust serve proceeded with no backup in place")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "backup-hold") {
		t.Fatalf("refusal does not name the backup failure: %v", err)
	}
	t.Logf("refused as designed: %v", err)
	if switchguard.HoldActive() {
		t.Fatalf("hold started despite the refused serve")
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "switchguard", "marker.json")); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatalf("marker written despite the refused serve")
	}
}

package core

/*
#cgo CFLAGS: -I.
#cgo !windows LDFLAGS: -ldl
#ifndef _WIN32
#include <dlfcn.h>
#endif
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#endif

// Dynamic library loader, per platform: dlopen on unix/Android,
// LoadLibrary on Windows. The rest of the bridge only calls these.
#ifdef _WIN32
static void* ll_open(const char* path) { return (void*)LoadLibraryA(path); }
static void* ll_sym(void* h, const char* name) { return (void*)GetProcAddress((HMODULE)h, name); }
static void ll_close(void* h) { if (h) FreeLibrary((HMODULE)h); }
#else
static void* ll_open(const char* path) { return dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW); }
static void* ll_sym(void* h, const char* name) { return dlsym(h, name); }
static void ll_close(void* h) { if (h) dlclose(h); }
#endif
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdarg.h>

// Core log sink: cores explain themselves here (load failures,
// missing firmware, bad options) instead of failing silently.
static void core_log_printf(int level, const char* fmt, ...) {
    (void)level;
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    fprintf(stderr, "[core] ");
    vfprintf(stderr, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
}

// Libretro API function pointers
typedef void (*retro_init_fn)(void);
typedef void (*retro_deinit_fn)(void);
typedef bool (*retro_load_game_fn)(void* game_info);
typedef void (*retro_run_fn)(void);
typedef void (*retro_set_environment_fn)(void* cb);
typedef void (*retro_set_video_refresh_fn)(void* cb);
typedef void (*retro_set_audio_sample_batch_fn)(void* cb);
typedef void (*retro_set_input_poll_fn)(void* cb);
typedef void (*retro_set_input_state_fn)(void* cb);
typedef size_t (*retro_serialize_size_fn)(void);
typedef bool (*retro_serialize_fn)(void* data, size_t size);
typedef bool (*retro_unserialize_fn)(void* data, size_t size);
typedef void (*retro_get_system_av_info_fn)(void* info);
typedef void (*retro_cheat_reset_fn)(void);
typedef void (*retro_cheat_set_fn)(unsigned index, bool enabled, const char* code);

typedef struct {
    void* handle;
    retro_init_fn init;
    retro_deinit_fn deinit;
    retro_load_game_fn load_game;
    retro_run_fn run;
    retro_serialize_size_fn serialize_size;
    retro_serialize_fn serialize;
    retro_unserialize_fn unserialize;
    retro_get_system_av_info_fn get_av_info;
    retro_cheat_reset_fn cheat_reset;
    retro_cheat_set_fn cheat_set;
    float aspect_ratio;
    double fps;
    double sample_rate;
} CoreHandle;

// Video frame buffer (shared with Go)
static unsigned char* video_buffer = NULL;
static unsigned video_width = 0;
static unsigned video_height = 0;
static unsigned video_pitch = 0;
static unsigned long video_frame_count = 0;
static unsigned long video_null_count = 0;
static long video_first_nonzero = -1;
static int video_ever_nonzero = 0;

// Called by the core for each video frame
static void video_refresh_cb(const void* data, unsigned width, unsigned height, size_t pitch) {
    video_frame_count++;
    if (!data) { video_null_count++; return; }
    // Scan for first non-zero byte in this frame
    const unsigned char* p = (const unsigned char*)data;
    size_t total = height * pitch;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < total; i++) {
        if (p[i] != 0) { video_first_nonzero = (long)i; break; }
    }
    if (video_first_nonzero >= 0) video_ever_nonzero = 1;
    // Allocate buffer if needed
    size_t size = height * pitch;
    if (!video_buffer || width != video_width || height != video_height) {
        free(video_buffer);
        video_buffer = malloc(size);
        video_width = width;
        video_height = height;
        video_pitch = pitch;
    }
    memcpy(video_buffer, data, size);
}

// Audio capture ring buffer. The core pushes interleaved int16 stereo samples;
// Go drains them for playback.
#define AUDIO_RING_SIZE (48000 * 2 * 4)
static int16_t audio_ring[AUDIO_RING_SIZE];
static volatile size_t audio_write_pos = 0;
static volatile size_t audio_read_pos = 0;
static unsigned long audio_samples_total = 0;

// Audio callback - captures samples into the ring buffer
static size_t audio_batch_cb(const short* data, size_t frames) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < frames * 2; i++) {
        audio_ring[audio_write_pos] = data[i];
        audio_write_pos = (audio_write_pos + 1) % AUDIO_RING_SIZE;
        if (audio_write_pos == audio_read_pos) {
            // Drop the oldest stereo frame (2 samples) so the read
            // position stays frame-aligned; dropping a single sample
            // would swap left/right channels for everything after.
            audio_read_pos = (audio_read_pos + 2) % AUDIO_RING_SIZE;
        }
    }
    audio_samples_total += frames;
    return frames;
}

// Drain up to max_frames stereo frames into out. Returns frames written.
int core_drain_audio(int16_t* out, int max_frames) {
    int n = 0;
    while (n < max_frames && audio_read_pos != audio_write_pos) {
        out[n*2] = audio_ring[audio_read_pos];
        audio_read_pos = (audio_read_pos + 1) % AUDIO_RING_SIZE;
        out[n*2+1] = audio_ring[audio_read_pos];
        audio_read_pos = (audio_read_pos + 1) % AUDIO_RING_SIZE;
        n++;
    }
    return n;
}

unsigned long core_get_audio_samples() { return audio_samples_total; }

// Input state shared between Go and the core callbacks.
// 2 players, 16 joypad buttons each. Set from Go via core_set_button.
static int input_buttons[2][16];
static unsigned long input_state_calls = 0;

// Input callbacks
static void input_poll_cb(void) {
    // State is pushed from Go; nothing to poll here.
}

static int16_t input_state_cb(unsigned port, unsigned device, unsigned index, unsigned id) {
    input_state_calls++;
    // device 1 = RETRO_DEVICE_JOYPAD
    if (device != 1) return 0;
    if (port > 1 || id > 15) return 0;
    return input_buttons[port][id] ? 1 : 0;
}

void core_set_button(int port, int id, int pressed) {
    if (port < 0 || port > 1 || id < 0 || id > 15) return;
    input_buttons[port][id] = pressed;
}

void core_clear_buttons() {
    memset(input_buttons, 0, sizeof(input_buttons));
}

unsigned long core_get_input_state_calls() { return input_state_calls; }

// Environment callback
static int g_pixel_format = -1;
static bool env_cb(unsigned cmd, void* data) {
    // cmd 10 = RETRO_ENVIRONMENT_SET_PIXEL_FORMAT
    // data is enum retro_pixel_format: 0=0RGB1555, 1=XRGB8888, 2=RGB565
    if (cmd == 10) {
        if (data) g_pixel_format = *(int*)data;
        return true;
    }
    // cmd 3 = GET_CAN_DUPE: can the frontend show a duplicated
    // frame (video callback with NULL data)? Yes: the bridge keeps
    // the last frame and the renderer redraws it. Gambatte refuses
    // to load at all without this.
    if (cmd == 3) {
        if (data) *(bool*)data = true;
        return true;
    }
    // cmd 27 = GET_LOG_INTERFACE: hand the core a log function so
    // its complaints land on stderr instead of vanishing.
    if (cmd == 27) {
        if (data) {
            void** log_fn = (void**)data;
            *log_fn = (void*)core_log_printf;
        }
        return true;
    }
    // cmd 9 = GET_SYSTEM_DIRECTORY, 30 = GET_CORE_ASSETS_DIRECTORY,
    // 31 = GET_SAVE_DIRECTORY. CD cores (PS1, Sega CD) ask where the
    // system folder is (BIOS files live there) and refuse to load
    // without an answer. The app points ITAK_SYSTEM_DIR at its own
    // folder; the fallback keeps headless tools working.
    if (cmd == 9 || cmd == 30 || cmd == 31) {
        if (data) {
            const char* dir = getenv("ITAK_SYSTEM_DIR");
            if (!dir || !*dir) dir = "/tmp";
            *(const char**)data = dir;
        }
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
int core_get_pixel_format() { return g_pixel_format; }

CoreHandle* core_load(const char* path) {
    CoreHandle* h = calloc(1, sizeof(CoreHandle));
    h->handle = ll_open(path);
    if (!h->handle) {
        free(h);
        return NULL;
    }
    h->init = (retro_init_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_init");
    h->deinit = (retro_deinit_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_deinit");
    h->load_game = (retro_load_game_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_load_game");
    h->run = (retro_run_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_run");
    h->serialize_size = (retro_serialize_size_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_serialize_size");
    h->serialize = (retro_serialize_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_serialize");
    h->unserialize = (retro_unserialize_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_unserialize");
    h->get_av_info = (retro_get_system_av_info_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_get_system_av_info");
    // Cheats are optional: a core without these exports simply has none.
    h->cheat_reset = (retro_cheat_reset_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_cheat_reset");
    h->cheat_set = (retro_cheat_set_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_cheat_set");
    h->aspect_ratio = 0;
    h->fps = 60.0;
    h->sample_rate = 32000.0;

    if (!h->init || !h->load_game || !h->run) {
        ll_close(h->handle);
        free(h);
        return NULL;
    }

    retro_set_environment_fn set_env = (retro_set_environment_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_set_environment");
    retro_set_video_refresh_fn set_video = (retro_set_video_refresh_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_set_video_refresh");
    retro_set_audio_sample_batch_fn set_audio = (retro_set_audio_sample_batch_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_set_audio_sample_batch");
    retro_set_input_poll_fn set_poll = (retro_set_input_poll_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_set_input_poll");
    retro_set_input_state_fn set_state = (retro_set_input_state_fn)ll_sym(h->handle, "retro_set_input_state");

    if (set_env) set_env(env_cb);
    if (set_video) set_video(video_refresh_cb);
    if (set_audio) set_audio(audio_batch_cb);
    if (set_poll) set_poll(input_poll_cb);
    if (set_state) set_state(input_state_cb);

    h->init();
    return h;
}

bool core_load_game(CoreHandle* h, const char* path, const void* data, size_t size) {
    // retro_game_info struct. The path matters: some cores
    // (Gambatte, PCSX ReARMed) load from the path and ignore the
    // memory buffer entirely, so a NULL path fails their load.
    struct {
        const char* path;
        const void* data;
        size_t size;
        const char* meta;
    } info = {path, data, size, NULL};
    bool ok = h->load_game(&info);
    if (ok && h->get_av_info) {
        // retro_system_av_info: geometry then timing
        struct {
            unsigned base_width;
            unsigned base_height;
            unsigned max_width;
            unsigned max_height;
            float aspect_ratio;
        } geometry;
        struct {
            double fps;
            double sample_rate;
        } timing;
        struct {
            typeof(geometry) geometry;
            typeof(timing) timing;
        } av;
        memset(&av, 0, sizeof(av));
        h->get_av_info(&av);
        h->aspect_ratio = av.geometry.aspect_ratio;
        h->fps = av.timing.fps;
        h->sample_rate = av.timing.sample_rate;
    }
    return ok;
}

float core_get_aspect(CoreHandle* h) { return h->aspect_ratio; }
double core_get_fps(CoreHandle* h) { return h->fps; }
double core_get_sample_rate(CoreHandle* h) { return h->sample_rate; }

void core_run(CoreHandle* h) {
    h->run();
}

void core_unload(CoreHandle* h) {
    if (h->deinit) h->deinit();
    if (h->handle) ll_close(h->handle);
    free(h);
    if (video_buffer) {
        free(video_buffer);
        video_buffer = NULL;
    }
}

    size_t size = video_height * video_pitch;
    if ((int)size > max_size) return -1;
    memcpy(out, video_buffer, size);
