import "C"
import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"unsafe"
)

// Bridge wraps a loaded libretro core
type Bridge struct {
	handle *C.CoreHandle
}

// LoadCore loads a libretro core from path
func LoadCore(path string) (*Bridge, error) {
	cpath := C.CString(path)
	defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cpath))

	h := C.core_load(cpath)
	if h == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to load core: %s", path)
	}
	return &Bridge{handle: h}, nil
}

// LoadGame loads a ROM file into the core
func (b *Bridge) LoadGame(romPath string) error {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("empty ROM file")
	}
	cdata := C.CBytes(data)
	defer C.free(cdata)
	cpath := C.CString(romPath)
	defer C.free(unsafe.Pointer(cpath))

	ok := C.core_load_game(b.handle, cpath, cdata, C.size_t(len(data)))
	if !bool(ok) {
		return fmt.Errorf("core failed to load game")
	}
	return nil
}

// RunFrame runs one emulation frame
func (b *Bridge) RunFrame() {
	C.core_run(b.handle)
}

// VideoFrameCount returns how many times the video callback fired
func (b *Bridge) VideoFrameCount() uint64 {
	return uint64(C.core_get_frame_count())
}

// VideoNullCount returns frames where data was NULL (dupe frames)
func (b *Bridge) VideoNullCount() uint64 {
	return uint64(C.core_get_null_count())
}

// VideoFirstNonzero returns offset of first non-zero byte in latest frame, -1 if all black
func (b *Bridge) VideoFirstNonzero() int64 {
	return int64(C.core_get_first_nonzero())
}

// VideoEverNonzero returns 1 if any frame ever had visible content
func (b *Bridge) VideoEverNonzero() bool {
	return C.core_get_ever_nonzero() == 1
}

// PixelFormat returns the libretro pixel format the core requested
// 0=0RGB1555, 1=XRGB8888, 2=RGB565
func (b *Bridge) PixelFormat() int {
	return int(C.core_get_pixel_format())
}

// AspectRatio returns the display aspect ratio reported by the core
// (e.g. 4/3 for SNES). Falls back to 4:3 when the core reports 0.
// The renderer must scale the raw frame to this ratio (pillarboxed),
// NOT show raw square pixels, or games look squished.
func (b *Bridge) AspectRatio() float64 {
	ar := float64(C.core_get_aspect(b.handle))
	if ar <= 0 {
		return 4.0 / 3.0
	}
	return ar
}

// FPS returns the core's target frame rate
func (b *Bridge) FPS() float64 {
	return float64(C.core_get_fps(b.handle))
}

// SampleRate returns the core's audio sample rate
func (b *Bridge) SampleRate() float64 {
	return float64(C.core_get_sample_rate(b.handle))
}

// FrameToRGBA converts the latest frame to RGBA bytes at native resolution.
// The caller scales it to AspectRatio() for display.
func (b *Bridge) FrameToRGBA() (width, height int, rgba []byte, err error) {
	w, h, pitch, data := b.GetFrame()
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return 0, 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("no frame available")
	}
	rgba = make([]byte, w*h*4)
	switch b.PixelFormat() {
	case 2: // RGB565
		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				off := y*pitch + x*2
				v := uint16(data[off]) | uint16(data[off+1])<<8
				r := (v >> 11) & 0x1F
				g := (v >> 5) & 0x3F
				bl := v & 0x1F
				dst := (y*w + x) * 4
				rgba[dst+0] = byte(r<<3 | r>>2)
				rgba[dst+1] = byte(g<<2 | g>>4)
				rgba[dst+2] = byte(bl<<3 | bl>>2)
				rgba[dst+3] = 0xFF
			}
		}
	case 1: // XRGB8888 (memory: B,G,R,X)
		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				off := y*pitch + x*4
				dst := (y*w + x) * 4
				rgba[dst+0] = data[off+2]
				rgba[dst+1] = data[off+1]
				rgba[dst+2] = data[off+0]
				rgba[dst+3] = 0xFF
			}
		}
	default:
		return 0, 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported pixel format %d", b.PixelFormat())
	}
	return w, h, rgba, nil
}

// GetFrame returns the latest video frame as bytes
func (b *Bridge) GetFrame() (width, height, pitch int, data []byte) {
	w := int(C.core_get_width())
	h := int(C.core_get_height())
	p := int(C.core_get_pitch())
	if w == 0 || h == 0 {
		return 0, 0, 0, nil
	}
	size := h * p
	buf := make([]byte, size)
	n := C.core_get_frame((*C.uchar)(unsafe.Pointer(&buf[0])), C.int(size))
	if n <= 0 {
		return 0, 0, 0, nil
	}
	return w, h, p, buf[:n]
}

// SaveState captures the current emulation state
func (b *Bridge) SaveState() ([]byte, error) {
	size := C.core_save_size(b.handle)
	if size == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("core does not support save states")
	}
	buf := make([]byte, size)
	ok := C.core_save(b.handle, unsafe.Pointer(&buf[0]), size)
	if !bool(ok) {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("save failed")
	}
	return buf, nil
}

// LoadState restores an emulation state
func (b *Bridge) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("empty save data")
	}
	ok := C.core_load_save(b.handle, unsafe.Pointer(&data[0]), C.size_t(len(data)))
	if !bool(ok) {
		return fmt.Errorf("load state failed")
	}
	return nil
}

// CheatsSupported reports whether the loaded core accepts cheat codes
// (Game Genie / Action Replay). The core decodes the codes itself.
func (b *Bridge) CheatsSupported() bool {
	return bool(C.core_cheats_supported(b.handle))
}

// DspRegs returns nil: the libretro .so bridge has no sound
// chip register surface. The debug export exists only on the
// Rust switch adapter (see NativeBridge.DspRegs).
func (b *Bridge) DspRegs() []byte { return nil }

// ApplyCheats replaces the core's cheat list with the given codes and
// returns how many entries were set. Multi-part codes joined with '+'
// are registered as separate entries, the way cheat managers hand
// them to cores.
func (b *Bridge) ApplyCheats(codes []string) int {
	C.core_cheat_reset(b.handle)
	idx := 0
	for _, code := range codes {
		for _, part := range strings.Split(code, "+") {
			part = strings.TrimSpace(part)
			if part == "" {
				continue
			}
			ccode := C.CString(part)
			C.core_cheat_set(b.handle, C.unsigned(idx), ccode)
			C.free(unsafe.Pointer(ccode))
			idx++
		}
	}
	return idx
}

// ClearCheats removes every cheat from the core.
func (b *Bridge) ClearCheats() {
	C.core_cheat_reset(b.handle)
}

// Joypad button IDs (libretro RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD_*)
const (
	ButtonB      = 0
	ButtonY      = 1
	ButtonSelect = 2
	ButtonStart  = 3
	ButtonUp     = 4
	ButtonDown   = 5
	ButtonLeft   = 6
	ButtonRight  = 7
	ButtonA      = 8
	ButtonX      = 9
	ButtonL      = 10
	ButtonR      = 11
	ButtonL2     = 12
	ButtonR2     = 13
	ButtonL3     = 14
	ButtonR3     = 15
)

// SetButton sets a joypad button state for a player (0 or 1)
func (b *Bridge) SetButton(player int, button int, pressed bool) {
	p := 0
	if pressed {
		p = 1
	}
	C.core_set_button(C.int(player), C.int(button), C.int(p))
}

// ClearButtons releases all buttons
func (b *Bridge) ClearButtons() {
	C.core_clear_buttons()
}

// InputStateCalls returns how many times the core queried input (diagnostics)
func (b *Bridge) InputStateCalls() uint64 {
	return uint64(C.core_get_input_state_calls())
}

// DrainAudio returns up to maxFrames stereo frames of int16 samples
func (b *Bridge) DrainAudio(maxFrames int) []int16 {
	out := make([]int16, maxFrames*2)
	n := C.core_drain_audio((*C.int16_t)(unsafe.Pointer(&out[0])), C.int(maxFrames))
	if n <= 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return out[:n*2]
}

// AudioSamplesTotal returns total audio frames the core produced (diagnostics)
func (b *Bridge) AudioSamplesTotal() uint64 {
	return uint64(C.core_get_audio_samples())
}

// Close unloads the core
func (b *Bridge) Close() {
	if b.handle != nil {
		C.core_unload(b.handle)
		b.handle = nil
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native.go ====================

package core

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"time"
)

// This file is the native core path: the bundled Go cores linked
// straight into the backend as Go packages, behind the same calls
// the cgo .so bridge (bridge.go) serves.
//
// Why it exists: a Go c-shared core (.so) carries its own Go
// runtime. Loaded into the app process, which already runs the
// gomobile backend runtime, the second runtime dies during its
// own startup (fatal error: stoplockedm: not runnable, captured
// on the Death Star 2026-10-15 for every 32-bit core). Multiple
// Go runtimes in one process are not a supported configuration.
// Linking the engines into the backend keeps exactly one
// runtime in the process. The .so bridge remains for desktop
// harness use (cmd/enginetest, cmd/coretest).
//
// Threading contract (learned on device, build 57): the app
// calls the backend from several threads at once (game loop,
// audio, UI). The engines are single-threaded state machines,
// so every engine touch is serialized under the bridge mutex,
// and the audio path never touches the engine at all: RunFrame
// moves each frame's samples into the bridge's pending buffer,
// and DrainAudio only slices that buffer. Build 57 let the
// audio thread drain the engine directly, racing the game
// loop inside the APU and panicking both goroutines
// (nil pointer dereference, captured 2026-10-15 10:50/10:51).

// NativeCore is the uniform contract each bundled core adapter
// implements. Adapters wrap a core engine's system package the
// same way that core's libretro shell does; the shell stays the
// reference for every mapping (input bit order, timing
// constants, memory exposure). All methods are called with the
// bridge mutex held, except where an adapter only reads values
// it fixed at load.
type NativeCore interface {
	// LoadGame starts the machine on a game. Cartridge cores
	// use data; disc cores use path (data then holds the small
	// descriptor file, e.g. the .cue sheet).
	LoadGame(data []byte, path string) error
	RunFrame()
	// FrameSize is the native frame geometry in pixels.
	FrameSize() (w, h int)
	// Frame returns the latest frame in PixelFormat, tightly
	// packed (pitch = width * bytes per pixel). The slice is
	// owned by the engine and rewritten by the next RunFrame;
	// callers that keep it must copy.
	Frame() []byte
	// PixelFormat is the libretro pixel format: 0 = 0RGB1555,
	// 1 = XRGB8888, 2 = RGB565.
	PixelFormat() int
	AspectRatio() float64
	FPS() float64
	SampleRate() float64
	// SetInput hands the core one player's buttons as a
	// libretro-order mask (bit b = RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD b).
	// The adapter translates to the engine's own bit order.
	SetInput(player int, libretroMask uint16)
	// AudioDrain returns every pending stereo int16 sample
	// (interleaved L, R) and clears the engine's buffer. It is
	// called from RunFrame only, never from the audio thread.
	AudioDrain() []int16
	SaveState() ([]byte, error)
	LoadState(data []byte) error
	CheatSupported() bool
	CheatReset()
	CheatSet(index int, code string)
	Close()
}

// The bundled Go core registry (the nativeCores map and
// LoadNative) lives in native_registry.go, compiled only
// under the gocores build tag, with a stub in
// native_registry_off.go for normal builds: the shipped
// app carries no Go cores (1.102), so LoadNative reports
// no bundled core there and every game resolves to the
// Rust adapter or the libretro bridge.

// NativeBridge serves the same method set as Bridge (bridge.go)
// over a NativeCore, so the mobile package drives either
// without knowing which is underneath.
type NativeBridge struct {
	mu   sync.Mutex // serializes every engine touch
	core NativeCore
	name string

	buttons [2]atomic.Uint32 // libretro-order masks

	pendMu  sync.Mutex // guards pending only; never the engine
	pending []int16    // samples RunFrame produced, awaiting DrainAudio

	frames      uint64
	everNonzero bool
	// The diagnostic counters are typed atomics: the free
	// atomic functions panic on unaligned 64-bit values, and
	// on 32-bit ARM a struct field after a slice header lands
	// on a 4-byte boundary. atomic.Uint64 aligns itself.
	// (Build 58 died on exactly this, on device, 2026-10-15.)
	audioTotal atomic.Uint64
	inputCalls atomic.Uint64

	// Frame timing diagnostics: average RunFrame duration is
	// logged every 600 frames so the app log shows what each
	// core costs on the real device.
	ftAcc   time.Duration
	ftCount int
}

// LoadGame loads a ROM file into the core.
func (b *NativeBridge) LoadGame(romPath string) error {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(romPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("empty ROM file")
	}
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("no core loaded")
	}
	return b.core.LoadGame(data, romPath)
}

// RunFrame runs one emulation frame, then moves the frame's
// audio into the pending buffer for the audio thread.
func (b *NativeBridge) RunFrame() {
	start := time.Now()
	b.mu.Lock()
	if b.core == nil {
		b.mu.Unlock()
		return
	}
	b.core.SetInput(0, uint16(b.buttons[0].Load()))
	b.core.SetInput(1, uint16(b.buttons[1].Load()))
	b.core.RunFrame()
	if samples := b.core.AudioDrain(); len(samples) > 0 {
		b.pendMu.Lock()
		b.pending = append(b.pending, samples...)
		b.pendMu.Unlock()
	}
	b.frames++
	if !b.everNonzero && firstNonzero(b.core.Frame()) >= 0 {
		b.everNonzero = true
	}
	b.mu.Unlock()

	b.ftAcc += time.Since(start)
	b.ftCount++
	if b.ftCount >= 600 {
		log.Printf("native timing: %s avg frame %v over %d frames",
			b.name, b.ftAcc/time.Duration(b.ftCount), b.ftCount)
		b.ftAcc, b.ftCount = 0, 0
	}
}

// GetFrame returns the latest video frame as bytes. The data
// is a copy taken under the engine lock, so it never mixes two
// frames and never races the renderer.
func (b *NativeBridge) GetFrame() (width, height, pitch int, data []byte) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return 0, 0, 0, nil
	}
	w, h := b.core.FrameSize()
	raw := b.core.Frame()
	if w == 0 || h == 0 || len(raw) == 0 {
		return 0, 0, 0, nil
	}
	pitch = len(raw) / h
	out := make([]byte, len(raw))
	copy(out, raw)
	return w, h, pitch, out
}

// PixelFormat returns the libretro pixel format the core
// produces (0=0RGB1555, 1=XRGB8888, 2=RGB565).
func (b *NativeBridge) PixelFormat() int {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return 1
	}
	return b.core.PixelFormat()
}

// AspectRatio returns the display aspect ratio reported by the
// core, falling back to 4:3.
func (b *NativeBridge) AspectRatio() float64 {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return 4.0 / 3.0
	}
	if ar := b.core.AspectRatio(); ar > 0 {
		return ar
	}
	return 4.0 / 3.0
}

// FPS returns the core's target frame rate.
func (b *NativeBridge) FPS() float64 {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return 60
	}
	return b.core.FPS()
}

// SampleRate returns the core's audio sample rate.
func (b *NativeBridge) SampleRate() float64 {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return 44100
	}
	return b.core.SampleRate()
}

// FrameToRGBA converts the latest frame to RGBA bytes at
// native resolution; the caller scales to AspectRatio().
func (b *NativeBridge) FrameToRGBA() (width, height int, rgba []byte, err error) {
	w, h, pitch, data := b.GetFrame()
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return 0, 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("no frame available")
	}
	format := b.PixelFormat()
	rgba, err = convertToRGBA(w, h, pitch, data, format)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, nil, err
	}
	return w, h, rgba, nil
}

// convertToRGBA expands a raw frame in a libretro pixel format
// to RGBA8888. Shared by the native bridge; the cgo bridge
// carries the same conversion for .so cores.
func convertToRGBA(w, h, pitch int, data []byte, format int) ([]byte, error) {
	rgba := make([]byte, w*h*4)
	switch format {
	case 2: // RGB565
		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				off := y*pitch + x*2
				v := uint16(data[off]) | uint16(data[off+1])<<8
				r := (v >> 11) & 0x1F
				g := (v >> 5) & 0x3F
				bl := v & 0x1F
				dst := (y*w + x) * 4
				rgba[dst+0] = byte(r<<3 | r>>2)
				rgba[dst+1] = byte(g<<2 | g>>4)
				rgba[dst+2] = byte(bl<<3 | bl>>2)
				rgba[dst+3] = 0xFF
			}
		}
	case 1: // XRGB8888 (memory: B, G, R, X)
		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
				off := y*pitch + x*4
				dst := (y*w + x) * 4
				rgba[dst+0] = data[off+2]
				rgba[dst+1] = data[off+1]
				rgba[dst+2] = data[off+0]
				rgba[dst+3] = 0xFF
			}
		}
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported pixel format %d", format)
	}
	return rgba, nil
}

// SaveState captures the current emulation state.
func (b *NativeBridge) SaveState() ([]byte, error) {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no core loaded")
	}
	return b.core.SaveState()
}

// DspRegs returns the sound chip's register file when the
// loaded core offers the optional debug export: the Rust
// switch adapter does, through itak_dsp_regs. Every other
// core answers nil. This is a diagnostic surface, and
// callers treat nil as "not offered".
func (b *NativeBridge) DspRegs() []byte {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return nil
	}
	if dc, ok := b.core.(interface{ DspRegs() []byte }); ok {
		return dc.DspRegs()
	}
	return nil
}

// LoadState restores an emulation state.
func (b *NativeBridge) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if len(data) == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("empty save data")
	}
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("no core loaded")
	}
	return b.core.LoadState(data)
}

// CheatsSupported reports whether the core accepts cheat codes.
func (b *NativeBridge) CheatsSupported() bool {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.core != nil && b.core.CheatSupported()
}

// ApplyCheats replaces the core's cheat list and returns how
// many entries were set; multi-part codes joined with '+' are
// registered as separate entries, as in the .so bridge.
func (b *NativeBridge) ApplyCheats(codes []string) int {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core == nil {
		return 0
	}
	b.core.CheatReset()
	if !b.core.CheatSupported() {
		return 0
	}
	idx := 0
	for _, code := range codes {
		for _, part := range strings.Split(code, "+") {
			part = strings.TrimSpace(part)
			if part == "" {
				continue
			}
			b.core.CheatSet(idx, part)
			idx++
		}
	}
	return idx
}

// ClearCheats removes every cheat from the core.
func (b *NativeBridge) ClearCheats() {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core != nil {
		b.core.CheatReset()
	}
}

// SetButton sets a joypad button state for a player (0 or 1).
// It only updates the bridge mask; the engine receives it at
// the next RunFrame, so input never touches the engine off the
// game thread's schedule.
func (b *NativeBridge) SetButton(player int, button int, pressed bool) {
	if player < 0 || player > 1 || button < 0 || button > 15 {
		return
	}
	b.inputCalls.Add(1)
	for {
		old := b.buttons[player].Load()
		next := old
		if pressed {
			next = old | (1 << uint(button))
		} else {
			next = old &^ (1 << uint(button))
		}
		if b.buttons[player].CompareAndSwap(old, next) {
			return
		}
	}
}

// ClearButtons releases all buttons.
func (b *NativeBridge) ClearButtons() {
	b.buttons[0].Store(0)
	b.buttons[1].Store(0)
}

// DrainAudio returns up to maxFrames stereo frames of int16
// samples from the pending buffer. It never touches the
// engine, so the audio thread can call it at any rate.
func (b *NativeBridge) DrainAudio(maxFrames int) []int16 {
	b.pendMu.Lock()
	defer b.pendMu.Unlock()
	n := len(b.pending) / 2
	if n > maxFrames {
		n = maxFrames
	}
	if n <= 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]int16, n*2)
	copy(out, b.pending[:n*2])
	b.pending = append(b.pending[:0], b.pending[n*2:]...)
	b.audioTotal.Add(uint64(n))
	return out
}

// VideoFrameCount returns how many frames have run.
func (b *NativeBridge) VideoFrameCount() uint64 {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.frames
}

// VideoNullCount returns 0: native cores always produce a
// frame, there are no dupe frames.
func (b *NativeBridge) VideoNullCount() uint64 { return 0 }

// VideoFirstNonzero returns the offset of the first non-zero
// byte in the latest frame, or -1 when it is all black.
func (b *NativeBridge) VideoFirstNonzero() int64 {
	_, _, _, data := b.GetFrame()
	return int64(firstNonzero(data))
}

// VideoEverNonzero reports whether any frame had visible
// content.
func (b *NativeBridge) VideoEverNonzero() bool {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	return b.everNonzero
}

// InputStateCalls returns how many button updates arrived
// (diagnostics).
func (b *NativeBridge) InputStateCalls() uint64 {
	return b.inputCalls.Load()
}

// AudioSamplesTotal returns total audio frames handed out
// (diagnostics).
func (b *NativeBridge) AudioSamplesTotal() uint64 {
	return b.audioTotal.Load()
}

// Close unloads the core.
func (b *NativeBridge) Close() {
	b.mu.Lock()
	defer b.mu.Unlock()
	if b.core != nil {
		b.core.Close()
		b.core = nil
	}
}

func firstNonzero(data []byte) int {
	for i, v := range data {
		if v != 0 {
			return i
		}
	}
	return -1
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native_gameboy.go ====================

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package core

import (
	"fmt"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gameboy/ppu"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gameboy/sound"
	gbsystem "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gameboy/system"
)

// Native adapter for the Go Game Boy core. Every constant and
// mapping mirrors cores/go-gameboy/libretro/main.go, which
// stays the reference shell for this engine. The one binary
// serves .gb and .gbc images; the system package picks DMG or
// CGB mode from the cartridge header.

type gameboyCore struct {
	sys   *gbsystem.System
	input [2]uint16
}

func (c *gameboyCore) LoadGame(data []byte, _ string) error {
	s, err := gbsystem.New(data)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	c.sys = s
	return nil
}

func (c *gameboyCore) RunFrame() {
	if c.sys == nil || !c.sys.Loaded() {
		return
	}
	c.sys.SetButtons(0, c.input[0])
	c.sys.SetButtons(1, c.input[1])
	c.sys.RunFrame()
}

func (c *gameboyCore) FrameSize() (int, int) { return ppu.Width, ppu.Height }

func (c *gameboyCore) Frame() []byte {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	fb := c.sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Slice((*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0])), len(fb)*4)
}

// PixelFormat: the PPU produces XRGB8888.
func (c *gameboyCore) PixelFormat() int { return 1 }

// AspectRatio mirrors the shell's declared 1.1111
// (160/144 = 10/9, pixel aspect 1:1).
func (c *gameboyCore) AspectRatio() float64 { return 1.1111 }

// FPS mirrors the shell's frame rate: 4194304 dots per second
// over 70224 dots per frame.
func (c *gameboyCore) FPS() float64 { return 59.7275 }

// SampleRate mirrors the shell, which declares the sound
// package's host output rate.
func (c *gameboyCore) SampleRate() float64 { return sound.SampleRate }

// Libretro joypad ids as bits of the mask SetInput receives
// (bit b = RETRO_DEVICE_ID_JOYPAD b), matching the joypad*
// constants in the shell.
const (
	lrJoypadB      = 1 << 0
	lrJoypadY      = 1 << 1
	lrJoypadSelect = 1 << 2
	lrJoypadStart  = 1 << 3
	lrJoypadUp     = 1 << 4
	lrJoypadDown   = 1 << 5
	lrJoypadLeft   = 1 << 6
	lrJoypadRight  = 1 << 7
	lrJoypadA      = 1 << 8
	lrJoypadX      = 1 << 9
)

// SetInput translates a libretro-order mask into the engine's
// button bits, replicating the shell's pollPad: the Game Boy
// has four buttons, and the shell maps libretro A and X to the
// console A, B and Y to the console B (the usual handheld map).
func (c *gameboyCore) SetInput(player int, libretroMask uint16) {
	if player < 0 || player > 1 {
		return
	}
	var m uint16
	if libretroMask&lrJoypadRight != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonRight
	}
	if libretroMask&lrJoypadLeft != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonLeft
	}
	if libretroMask&lrJoypadUp != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonUp
	}
	if libretroMask&lrJoypadDown != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonDown
	}
	if libretroMask&(lrJoypadA|lrJoypadX) != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonA
	}
	if libretroMask&(lrJoypadB|lrJoypadY) != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonB
	}
	if libretroMask&lrJoypadSelect != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonSelect
	}
	if libretroMask&lrJoypadStart != 0 {
		m |= gbsystem.ButtonStart
	}
	c.input[player] = m
}

// AudioDrain mirrors the shell, which hands the frontend
// everything sys.AudioBuffer returns; that call drains the
// samples produced since the previous one.
func (c *gameboyCore) AudioDrain() []int16 {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return c.sys.AudioBuffer()
}

// SaveState mirrors the shell's retro_serialize: the engine
// writes into a caller buffer sized by SerializeSize.
func (c *gameboyCore) SaveState() ([]byte, error) {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	size := c.sys.SerializeSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("core does not support save states")
	}
	buf := make([]byte, size)
	if err := c.sys.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return buf, nil
}

func (c *gameboyCore) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	return c.sys.Deserialize(data)
}

// Cheats: the shell's cheat hooks are no-ops (it exposes no
// cheat support yet), so the native adapter honestly reports
// none.
func (c *gameboyCore) CheatSupported() bool { return false }
func (c *gameboyCore) CheatReset()          {}
func (c *gameboyCore) CheatSet(int, string) {}
func (c *gameboyCore) Close()               { c.sys = nil }


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native_gba.go ====================

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package core

import (
	"fmt"
	"unsafe"

	gbasystem "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-gba/system"
)

// Native adapter for the Go GBA core. Every constant and
// mapping mirrors cores/go-gba/libretro/main.go, which stays
// the reference shell for this engine.

// gbaDefaultAudioRate is the shell's defaultAudioRate: the
// SOUNDBIAS power-on sample rate, reported until a game is
// loaded (and the fallback when a rate reads as 0).
const gbaDefaultAudioRate = 32768

type gbaCore struct {
	sys   *gbasystem.Machine
	input uint32 // translated GBA button mask, single pad

	// declaredRate is the audio sample rate captured from
	// the machine at load time, exactly as the shell does:
	// the frontend consumes at this rate for the whole
	// session, even if the game later rewrites SOUNDBIAS.
	declaredRate int

	// Resampler state for the SOUNDBIAS rate conversion,
	// carried across frames as in the shell: leftover input
	// samples and the fractional read position within them.
	resBuf   []int16
	resPhase float64
}

func (c *gbaCore) LoadGame(data []byte, _ string) error {
	// The engine installs its own BIOS stub at power-on
	// (system power() runs bios.Install), so no external
	// BIOS file is needed or read here; the shell likewise
	// loads from the ROM bytes alone.
	if c.sys == nil {
		c.sys = gbasystem.New()
	}
	if err := c.sys.LoadCart(data); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	c.declaredRate = c.sys.AudioSampleRate()
	c.resBuf = c.resBuf[:0]
	c.resPhase = 0
	return nil
}

func (c *gbaCore) RunFrame() {
	if c.sys == nil || c.sys.Cart() == nil {
		return
	}
	// The shell polls input, sets the pad, then runs the
	// frame. Its save RAM cache sync has no native
	// counterpart: nothing outside the machine writes the
	// save contents here (the shell's cache exists only
	// for the libretro memory interface), and the save
	// device plus bus SRAM ride inside save states.
	c.sys.SetButtons(c.input)
	c.sys.RunFrame()
}

func (c *gbaCore) FrameSize() (int, int) {
	return gbasystem.Width, gbasystem.Height
}

func (c *gbaCore) Frame() []byte {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	fb := c.sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Slice((*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0])), len(fb)*4)
}

// PixelFormat: the GPU produces XRGB8888; the shell asks the
// frontend for that format at load.
func (c *gbaCore) PixelFormat() int { return 1 }

// AspectRatio mirrors the shell's gbaAspect (240x160, square
// pixels).
func (c *gbaCore) AspectRatio() float64 { return 1.5 }

// FPS mirrors the shell's gbaFPS: the master clock over the
// cycles in one frame.
func (c *gbaCore) FPS() float64 { return 16777216.0 / 280896.0 }

// SampleRate mirrors the shell's AV info: the rate declared
// at load time, with the power-on rate as fallback.
func (c *gbaCore) SampleRate() float64 {
	rate := c.declaredRate
	if rate == 0 {
		rate = gbaDefaultAudioRate
	}
	return float64(rate)
}

// SetInput translates a libretro-order mask into the GBA
// button mask, replicating the shell's pollPad: the GBA bits
// are GBATEK KEYINPUT order via the system Button constants.
// Libretro ids the shell never polls (Y, X, L2, R2, L3, R3)
// have no GBA counterpart and are dropped. The GBA has one
// pad; the shell polls port 0 only, so other ports are
// ignored.
func (c *gbaCore) SetInput(player int, libretroMask uint16) {
	if player != 0 {
		return
	}
	var m uint32
	if libretroMask&(1<<8) != 0 { // joypadA
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonA
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<0) != 0 { // joypadB
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonB
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<2) != 0 { // joypadSelect
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonSelect
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<3) != 0 { // joypadStart
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonStart
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<7) != 0 { // joypadRight
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonRight
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<6) != 0 { // joypadLeft
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonLeft
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<4) != 0 { // joypadUp
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonUp
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<5) != 0 { // joypadDown
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonDown
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<11) != 0 { // joypadR
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonR
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<10) != 0 { // joypadL
		m |= gbasystem.ButtonL
	}
	c.input = m
}

// AudioDrain mirrors the shell's drainAudio: it returns the
// machine's pending samples at the declared rate. When the
// machine's live rate differs (a game rewrote SOUNDBIAS
// after load), the input is converted with the shell's
// linear interpolator over a carried buffer, so the
// conversion is continuous across calls.
func (c *gbaCore) AudioDrain() []int16 {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	in := c.sys.AudioBuffer()
	live := c.sys.AudioSampleRate()
	if live == c.declaredRate || live == 0 || c.declaredRate == 0 {
		c.resBuf = c.resBuf[:0]
		c.resPhase = 0
		return in
	}
	c.resBuf = append(c.resBuf, in...)
	total := len(c.resBuf) / 2
	step := float64(live) / float64(c.declaredRate)
	var out []int16
	for c.resPhase+1 < float64(total) {
		i := int(c.resPhase)
		frac := c.resPhase - float64(i)
		l := gbaLerp(c.resBuf[2*i], c.resBuf[2*i+2], frac)
		r := gbaLerp(c.resBuf[2*i+1], c.resBuf[2*i+3], frac)
		out = append(out, l, r)
		c.resPhase += step
	}
	consumed := int(c.resPhase)
	if consumed > 0 {
		c.resBuf = append(c.resBuf[:0], c.resBuf[2*consumed:]...)
		c.resPhase -= float64(consumed)
	}
	return out
}

// gbaLerp is the shell's lerp for the rate conversion.
func gbaLerp(a, b int16, frac float64) int16 {
	return int16(float64(a) + (float64(b)-float64(a))*frac)
}

func (c *gbaCore) SaveState() ([]byte, error) {
	if c.sys == nil || c.sys.Cart() == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	st := c.sys.Serialize()
	if len(st) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("core does not support save states")
	}
	return st, nil
}

func (c *gbaCore) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if c.sys == nil || c.sys.Cart() == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	// Deserialize itself demands exactly StateSize bytes
	// and the current state version, as in the shell path.
	return c.sys.Deserialize(data)
}

// Cheats: the shell's cheat hooks are empty no-ops, so the
// native adapter honestly reports none.
func (c *gbaCore) CheatSupported() bool { return false }
func (c *gbaCore) CheatReset()          {}
func (c *gbaCore) CheatSet(int, string) {}

// Close mirrors the shell's unload: a fresh empty machine
// state, with the declared rate back at the power-on rate.
func (c *gbaCore) Close() {
	c.sys = nil
	c.declaredRate = gbaDefaultAudioRate
	c.resBuf = nil
	c.resPhase = 0
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native_genesis.go ====================

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package core

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/bus"
	gensystem "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/system"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-genesis/vdp"
)

// Native adapter for the Go Genesis core, cartridge and Sega CD
// in one adapter, matching the one .so the shell builds. Every
// constant and mapping mirrors cores/go-genesis/libretro/main.go
// and libretro/disc.go, which stay the reference shell for this
// engine.

type genesisCore struct {
	sys     *gensystem.System
	input   [2]uint16 // translated to bus.Pad* layout by SetInput
	packed  []uint16  // frame repacked to the display width
	tempISO string    // routeDiscData temp file, as in the shell

	// ranFrames mirrors the shell's flag of the same name: the
	// VDP powers on in H32 mode, but most games switch to H40
	// during boot, so before the first frame the honest
	// reported geometry is the 320 wide default.
	ranFrames bool
}

// discSignature is the boot signature at the start of every
// Sega CD disc's data area (libretro/disc.go).
const discSignature = "SEGADISCSYSTEM"

// sniffDisc reports whether data looks like a Sega CD disc
// image, copied from libretro/disc.go: a 2048 byte sector image
// carries the signature at offset 0; a raw 2352 byte sector
// image carries the twelve byte sync pattern first (0x00, ten
// 0xFF bytes, 0x00) then a four byte header, so the signature
// lands at offset 16. A cartridge, which carries "SEGA" at
// offset 0x100 instead, returns false.
func sniffDisc(data []byte) bool {
	if len(data) >= len(discSignature) && string(data[:len(discSignature)]) == discSignature {
		return true
	}
	if len(data) < 16+len(discSignature) {
		return false
	}
	if data[0] != 0x00 || data[11] != 0x00 {
		return false
	}
	for i := 1; i <= 10; i++ {
		if data[i] != 0xFF {
			return false
		}
	}
	return string(data[16:16+len(discSignature)]) == discSignature
}

// Load routes, the same three the shell's routeFor picks
// between (libretro/disc.go).
const (
	genesisRouteCartridge = iota
	genesisRouteDiscPath
	genesisRouteDiscData
)

// routeFor picks the loader for one load, copied from
// libretro/disc.go: a .cue or .iso path always wins (the cue
// sheet is not the disc data, and an ISO is a disc by
// definition); otherwise the data decides, a disc signature
// means a disc, loaded from its path when it has one and from
// the bytes themselves when it does not; anything else is a
// cartridge.
func genesisRouteFor(path string, data []byte) int {
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".cue", ".iso":
		return genesisRouteDiscPath
	}
	if sniffDisc(data) {
		if path != "" {
			return genesisRouteDiscPath
		}
		return genesisRouteDiscData
	}
	return genesisRouteCartridge
}

func (c *genesisCore) LoadGame(data []byte, path string) error {
	if c.sys == nil {
		c.sys = gensystem.New()
	}
	switch genesisRouteFor(path, data) {
	case genesisRouteDiscPath:
		// Disc loads work on files: LoadDisc opens the .cue,
		// .iso or .bin at path (scd.OpenDisc) and, for a CD
		// only boot, powers the machine on around the
		// project's own main stub program (system.LoadDisc via
		// scd.MainStubROM). No Sega BIOS file is read at load
		// time or later; the BIOS service layer is HLE inside
		// the scd package.
		return c.sys.LoadDisc(path)
	case genesisRouteDiscData:
		// LoadDisc works on files, so park the bytes in a temp
		// ISO first, exactly as the shell does. Close deletes
		// it, mirroring retro_unload_game.
		f, err := os.CreateTemp("", "itak-disc-*.iso")
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		tmpPath := f.Name()
		if _, err := f.Write(data); err != nil {
			f.Close()
			os.Remove(tmpPath)
			return err
		}
		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
			os.Remove(tmpPath)
			return err
		}
		if err := c.sys.LoadDisc(tmpPath); err != nil {
			os.Remove(tmpPath)
			return err
		}
		c.tempISO = tmpPath
		return nil
	default:
		return c.sys.LoadGame(data)
	}
}

func (c *genesisCore) RunFrame() {
	if c.sys == nil || !c.sys.Loaded() {
		return
	}
	c.ranFrames = true
	c.sys.SetButtons(0, c.input[0])
	c.sys.SetButtons(1, c.input[1])
	c.sys.RunFrame()
}

// FrameSize mirrors retro_get_system_av_info: 320 by 224 until
// a game is loaded and a frame has run, then the VDP's live
// display size (256 or 320 wide, 224 or 240 tall; CD games run
// through the same VDP, so disc mode changes nothing here).
func (c *genesisCore) FrameSize() (int, int) {
	if c.sys != nil && c.sys.Loaded() && c.ranFrames {
		return c.sys.Width(), c.sys.Height()
	}
	return 320, 224
}

// Frame repacks the VDP frame. The engine framebuffer is
// always vdp.MaxWidth pixels wide (system.Framebuffer, "the
// system crops each line to DisplayWidth when presenting");
// the shell presents it with a MaxWidth pitch, while the
// NativeCore contract wants a tightly packed frame, so each
// line is cropped to the display width here.
func (c *genesisCore) Frame() []byte {
	if c.sys == nil || !c.sys.Loaded() {
		return nil
	}
	fb := c.sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	w, h := c.FrameSize()
	if len(c.packed) != w*h {
		c.packed = make([]uint16, w*h)
	}
	for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
		row := fb[y*vdp.MaxWidth:]
		copy(c.packed[y*w:(y+1)*w], row[:w])
	}
	return unsafe.Slice((*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&c.packed[0])), len(c.packed)*2)
}

// PixelFormat: the VDP produces RGB565 (the shell asks the
// frontend for RGB565 in retro_load_game).
func (c *genesisCore) PixelFormat() int { return 2 }

// AspectRatio mirrors the shell's pixel aspect corrected
// constants ("matches Genesis Plus GX"): 1.3061 for H40, and
// 1.2152 once a loaded game has run a frame in H32 (width
// 256). The default applies before that, as in
// retro_get_system_av_info.
func (c *genesisCore) AspectRatio() float64 {
	if c.sys != nil && c.sys.Loaded() && c.ranFrames && c.sys.Width() == 256 {
		return 1.2152
	}
	return 1.3061
}

// FPS mirrors the shell's genesisFPS constant.
func (c *genesisCore) FPS() float64 { return 59.9227 }

// SampleRate mirrors the shell's sampleRate constant.
func (c *genesisCore) SampleRate() float64 { return 44100 }

// SetInput translates the libretro-order mask into the bus
// pad layout, replicating the shell's pollPad: the 3-button
// Genesis pad mapping (same as Genesis Plus GX defaults),
// libretro Y = Genesis A, B = B, A = C, Select = Mode, Start =
// Start. The shell's libretro ids are B 0, Y 1, Select 2,
// Start 3, Up 4, Down 5, Left 6, Right 7, A 8; the bus bits
// are the bus.Pad* constants.
func (c *genesisCore) SetInput(player int, libretroMask uint16) {
	if player < 0 || player > 1 {
		return
	}
	var m uint16
	if libretroMask&(1<<4) != 0 { // Up
		m |= bus.PadUp
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<5) != 0 { // Down
		m |= bus.PadDown
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<6) != 0 { // Left
		m |= bus.PadLeft
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<7) != 0 { // Right
		m |= bus.PadRight
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<1) != 0 { // Y
		m |= bus.PadA
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<0) != 0 { // B
		m |= bus.PadB
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<8) != 0 { // A
		m |= bus.PadC
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<3) != 0 { // Start
		m |= bus.PadStart
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<2) != 0 { // Select
		m |= bus.PadMode
	}
	c.input[player] = m
}

// AudioDrain: system.AudioBuffer drains every sample the
// machine has produced and not yet handed out (cartridge
// sound plus, in CD mode, CD-DA and PCM mixed by the same
// system), which is exactly the drain all contract.
func (c *genesisCore) AudioDrain() []int16 {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return c.sys.AudioBuffer()
}

// SaveState serves both modes through the one System
// serializer: SerializeSize grows when a Sega CD unit is
// attached (the CD section is appended), and Serialize fills
// a buffer of that size, exactly the shell's retro_serialize
// path.
func (c *genesisCore) SaveState() ([]byte, error) {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	size := c.sys.SerializeSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("core does not support save states")
	}
	buf := make([]byte, size)
	if err := c.sys.Serialize(buf); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return buf, nil
}

// LoadState mirrors retro_unserialize: the state is taken at
// the current machine's SerializeSize (extra bytes are cut,
// as the shell slices the frontend buffer), and Deserialize
// itself handles the rest, including its legacy CD state
// expansion and its refusal of a CD state in cartridge mode
// or the reverse.
func (c *genesisCore) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	size := c.sys.SerializeSize()
	if size == 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	if len(data) > size {
		data = data[:size]
	}
	return c.sys.Deserialize(data)
}

// Cheats: the shell's retro_cheat_reset and retro_cheat_set
// are empty hooks ("this core does not expose cheat hooks
// yet"), so the native adapter honestly reports none.
func (c *genesisCore) CheatSupported() bool { return false }
func (c *genesisCore) CheatReset()          {}
func (c *genesisCore) CheatSet(int, string) {}

// Close mirrors retro_unload_game: delete the temp ISO if a
// disc was loaded from bytes, and reset to a fresh, unloaded
// system.
func (c *genesisCore) Close() {
	if c.tempISO != "" {
		os.Remove(c.tempISO)
		c.tempISO = ""
	}
	c.sys = gensystem.New()
	c.ranFrames = false
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native_nes.go ====================

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package core

import (
	"fmt"
	"unsafe"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nes/ppu"
	nessystem "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-nes/system"
)

// Native adapter for the Go NES core. Every constant and
// mapping mirrors cores/go-nes/libretro/main.go, which stays
// the reference shell for this engine.

type nesCore struct {
	sys   *nessystem.System
	input [2]uint8
}

func (c *nesCore) LoadGame(data []byte, _ string) error {
	s, err := nessystem.New(data)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	c.sys = s
	return nil
}

func (c *nesCore) RunFrame() {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return
	}
	c.sys.SetButtons(0, c.input[0])
	c.sys.SetButtons(1, c.input[1])
	c.sys.RunFrame()
}

func (c *nesCore) FrameSize() (int, int) { return ppu.Width, ppu.Height }

func (c *nesCore) Frame() []byte {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	fb := c.sys.Framebuffer()
	if len(fb) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return unsafe.Slice((*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0])), len(fb)*4)
}

// PixelFormat: the PPU produces XRGB8888 (the format the
// shell requests from the frontend in retro_load_game).
func (c *nesCore) PixelFormat() int { return 1 }

// AspectRatio mirrors the shell's declared 1.33333.
func (c *nesCore) AspectRatio() float64 { return 1.33333 }

// FPS mirrors the shell's NTSC frame rate.
func (c *nesCore) FPS() float64 { return 60.0988 }

// SampleRate mirrors the shell's timing report: the APU
// renders at sound.SampleRate, 44100 Hz.
func (c *nesCore) SampleRate() float64 { return 44100 }

// SetInput translates a libretro-order mask into the NES
// button mask, replicating the shell's pollPad: libretro A
// (bit 8) or X (bit 9) is the console A, libretro B (bit 0)
// or Y (bit 1) is the console B, and Select, Start and the
// d-pad map straight across. The result uses the shift
// register order SetButtons expects: A, B, Select, Start,
// Up, Down, Left, Right in bits 0 to 7. Libretro L, R and
// the remaining buttons have no NES counterpart and are
// dropped, exactly as the shell drops them.
func (c *nesCore) SetInput(player int, libretroMask uint16) {
	if player < 0 || player > 1 {
		return
	}
	var m uint8
	if libretroMask&(1<<8) != 0 || libretroMask&(1<<9) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 0 // console A
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<0) != 0 || libretroMask&(1<<1) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 1 // console B
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<2) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 2 // Select
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<3) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 3 // Start
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<4) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 4 // Up
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<5) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 5 // Down
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<6) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 6 // Left
	}
	if libretroMask&(1<<7) != 0 {
		m |= 1 << 7 // Right
	}
	c.input[player] = m
}

// AudioDrain: the engine's AudioBuffer hands over every
// pending sample and clears its buffer (sound.APU.AudioBuffer
// in the go-nes module), which is the drain the contract
// asks for.
func (c *nesCore) AudioDrain() []int16 {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return c.sys.AudioBuffer()
}

func (c *nesCore) SaveState() ([]byte, error) {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	st := c.sys.Serialize()
	if len(st) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("core does not support save states")
	}
	return st, nil
}

func (c *nesCore) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	return c.sys.Deserialize(data)
}

// Cheats: the shell's retro_cheat_reset and retro_cheat_set
// are empty no-ops (its comment: the core does not expose
// cheat hooks yet), so the native adapter honestly reports
// none.
func (c *nesCore) CheatSupported() bool { return false }
func (c *nesCore) CheatReset()          {}
func (c *nesCore) CheatSet(int, string) {}
func (c *nesCore) Close()               { c.sys = nil }


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native_ps1.go ====================

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package core

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"unsafe"

	ps1system "github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/cores/go-ps1/system"
)

// Native adapter for the Go PlayStation core. Every
// constant and mapping mirrors
// cores/go-ps1/libretro/main.go, which stays the
// reference shell for this engine.

type ps1Core struct {
	sys   *ps1system.Machine
	input uint32 // translated pad mask, port 1 only
}

// ps1JoypadMap translates libretro joypad ids to the
// engine's pad bits, in libretro id order. It is the
// shell's joypadMap table (libretro/main.go) laid out
// by id: the standard libretro pad layout mapped
// onto the PlayStation pad.
var ps1JoypadMap = [16]uint32{
	ps1system.ButtonCross,  // 0: B
	ps1system.ButtonSquare, // 1: Y
	ps1system.ButtonSelect, // 2: Select
	ps1system.ButtonStart,  // 3: Start
	ps1system.ButtonUp,     // 4: Up
	ps1system.ButtonDown,   // 5: Down
	ps1system.ButtonLeft,   // 6: Left
	ps1system.ButtonRight,  // 7: Right
	ps1system.ButtonCircle, // 8: A
	ps1system.ButtonTri,    // 9: X
	ps1system.ButtonL1,     // 10: L
	ps1system.ButtonR1,     // 11: R
	ps1system.ButtonL2,     // 12: L2
	ps1system.ButtonR2,     // 13: R2
	ps1system.ButtonL3,     // 14: L3
	ps1system.ButtonR3,     // 15: R3
}

// LoadGame dispatches exactly like the shell's
// loadPath: the content kind is decided by the path
// extension. Discs (.cue, .bin, .iso, .img) open by
// path through the cd image layer and boot through
// SYSTEM.CNF; a .exe boots directly from its bytes;
// anything else is accepted only when the data
// carries the PS-X EXE magic. The new machine is
// installed only after a successful load, as in the
// shell.
func (c *ps1Core) LoadGame(data []byte, path string) error {
	m := ps1system.New()
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".exe":
		if len(data) == 0 {
			b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
			if err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("cannot read %s: %w", path, err)
			}
			data = b
		}
		if err := m.LoadEXE(data); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("bad PS-X EXE: %w", err)
		}
	case ".cue", ".bin", ".iso", ".img":
		if err := m.OpenDisc(path); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("cannot open disc image: %w", err)
		}
		if err := m.BootDisc(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("disc does not boot: %w", err)
		}
	default:
		// A data-only load with no usable path: a
		// PS-X EXE is recognizable by its magic.
		if len(data) < 8 || string(data[:8]) != "PS-X EXE" {
			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported content: %s", path)
		}
		if err := m.LoadEXE(data); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("bad PS-X EXE: %w", err)
		}
	}
	// The shell always presents an analog pad (see
	// the shell's package comment), forced at load.
	m.SetAnalogMode(true)
	// The native contract carries no analog axes.
	// The shell converts an untouched frontend axis
	// (raw 0) through its axis() helper to 128,
	// centered, every frame; pin the sticks there.
	m.SetAnalog(128, 128, 128, 128)
	c.sys = m
	return nil
}

func (c *ps1Core) RunFrame() {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return
	}
	c.sys.SetButtons(c.input)
	c.sys.RunFrame()
}

// FrameSize reports the GPU's current display size.
// PlayStation games change resolution mid-game: the
// shell answers with a SET_GEOMETRY notice, the
// native bridge simply reads the live size on every
// call. The 320x240 fallback before a load mirrors
// the shell's retro_get_system_av_info default
// (declared base geometry 320x240, max 640x480).
func (c *ps1Core) FrameSize() (int, int) {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return 320, 240
	}
	return c.sys.DisplayWidth(), c.sys.DisplayHeight()
}

func (c *ps1Core) Frame() []byte {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	w, h := c.sys.DisplayWidth(), c.sys.DisplayHeight()
	fb := c.sys.Framebuffer()
	if w <= 0 || h <= 0 || len(fb) < w*h {
		return nil
	}
	// The engine framebuffer is exactly the current
	// display size, tightly packed (the shell
	// presents it with pitch w*4).
	fb = fb[:w*h]
	return unsafe.Slice((*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&fb[0])), len(fb)*4)
}

// PixelFormat: the shell requests XRGB8888 through
// SET_PIXEL_FORMAT and the engine framebuffer is
// XRGB8888.
func (c *ps1Core) PixelFormat() int { return 1 }

// AspectRatio mirrors the shell's declared 4:3.
func (c *ps1Core) AspectRatio() float64 { return 4.0 / 3.0 }

// FPS mirrors the shell's declared 59.94.
func (c *ps1Core) FPS() float64 { return 59.94 }

// SampleRate mirrors the shell's av info, which
// reports the engine's AudioSampleRate (44100).
func (c *ps1Core) SampleRate() float64 { return ps1system.AudioSampleRate }

// SetInput translates the libretro-order mask into
// the engine's pad bits through ps1JoypadMap. The
// machine has one pad port and the shell only ever
// polls libretro port 0, so player 1 input has no
// shell counterpart and is dropped.
func (c *ps1Core) SetInput(player int, libretroMask uint16) {
	if player != 0 {
		return
	}
	var mask uint32
	for id := 0; id < 16; id++ {
		if libretroMask&(1<<uint(id)) != 0 {
			mask |= ps1JoypadMap[id]
		}
	}
	c.input = mask
}

// AudioDrain: the engine's AudioBuffer drains every
// pending sample, the same call the shell presents
// per frame.
func (c *ps1Core) AudioDrain() []int16 {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return c.sys.AudioBuffer()
}

func (c *ps1Core) SaveState() ([]byte, error) {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	st := c.sys.Serialize()
	if len(st) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("core does not support save states")
	}
	return st, nil
}

func (c *ps1Core) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if c.sys == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("no game loaded")
	}
	return c.sys.Deserialize(data)
}

// Cheats: the shell's retro_cheat_reset and
// retro_cheat_set are empty stubs, so the native
// adapter honestly reports none.
func (c *ps1Core) CheatSupported() bool { return false }
func (c *ps1Core) CheatReset()          {}
func (c *ps1Core) CheatSet(int, string) {}
func (c *ps1Core) Close()               { c.sys = nil }


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native_race_test.go ====================

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package core

import (
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// TestNativeConcurrentAccess drives a bridge the way the app
// does: a game loop thread running frames and reading them
// back, an audio thread draining samples, and a UI thread
// poking buttons and save states, all at once. Build 57 let
// the audio thread reach into the engine while the game loop
// was inside it and both goroutines panicked on device; this
// test (especially under -race) is the regression gate.
func TestNativeConcurrentAccess(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		core, name string
		rom        []byte
	}{
		{"libgo_nes.so", "spin.nes", nesROM()},
		{"libgo_snes.so", "loop.sfc", loopROM()},
		{"libgo_gameboy.so", "spin.gb", gbROM()},
		{"libgo_gba.so", "spin.gba", gbaROM()},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.core, func(t *testing.T) {
			nb, ok := LoadNative("/x/" + tc.core)
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("no adapter for %s", tc.core)
			}
			if err := nb.LoadGame(writeGame(t, tc.name, tc.rom)); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("LoadGame: %v", err)
			}
			defer nb.Close()

			stop := make(chan struct{})
			var wg sync.WaitGroup

			// Game loop: frames plus frame readback.
			wg.Add(1)
			go func() {
				defer wg.Done()
				for {
					select {
					case <-stop:
						return
					default:
					}
					nb.RunFrame()
					if _, _, _, err := nb.FrameToRGBA(); err != nil {
						t.Error(err)
						return
					}
				}
			}()

			// Audio thread: drain at full rate.
			wg.Add(1)
			go func() {
				defer wg.Done()
				for {
					select {
					case <-stop:
						return
					default:
					}
					_ = nb.DrainAudio(4096)
				}
			}()

			// UI thread: input and periodic save states.
			wg.Add(1)
			go func() {
				defer wg.Done()
				tick := time.NewTicker(7 * time.Millisecond)
				defer tick.Stop()
				for {
					select {
					case <-stop:
						return
					case <-tick.C:
					}
					nb.SetButton(0, 3, true)
					nb.SetButton(0, 3, false)
					if st, err := nb.SaveState(); err == nil {
						_ = nb.LoadState(st)
					}
				}
			}()

			time.Sleep(1500 * time.Millisecond)
			close(stop)
			wg.Wait()

			if nb.VideoFrameCount() == 0 {
				t.Fatal("no frames ran under concurrency")
			}
		})
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/core/native_registry.go ====================

//go:build gocores

package core

import "path/filepath"

// The bundled Go core registry, compiled only under the
// gocores build tag (server-side reference and cross-check
// runs). The shipped app builds without the tag and gets
// the stub in native_registry_off.go instead.

// nativeCores maps a core file name (what the app passes to
// LoadCore) to its adapter constructor.
var nativeCores = map[string]func() NativeCore{
	"libgo_gameboy.so": func() NativeCore { return &gameboyCore{} },
	"libgo_nes.so":     func() NativeCore { return &nesCore{} },
	"libgo_snes.so":    func() NativeCore { return &snesCore{} },
	"libgo_genesis.so": func() NativeCore { return &genesisCore{} },
	"libgo_gba.so":     func() NativeCore { return &gbaCore{} },
	"libgo_ps1.so":     func() NativeCore { return &ps1Core{} },
}

// LoadNative returns a bridge over the bundled native core for
// the given core path, or false when the path names no bundled
// core (the caller then falls back to the .so bridge).
func LoadNative(corePath string) (*NativeBridge, bool) {
	base := filepath.Base(corePath)
	ctor, ok := nativeCores[base]
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	return &NativeBridge{core: ctor(), name: base}, true
}
