==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/matchend.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"errors"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// Match end (PROTOCOL.md section 4.9, SPECTATOR_DESIGN.md
// slice S4). A game ending used to end the session; rotation
// (seat swaps, Got Next, tournaments) needs the opposite: the
// match ends, the session does not. Either player sends
// match_end, both sides fall back to the waiting room on the
// same sockets with their readys reset and their frame state
// cleared, and the next match starts through StartNextMatch
// whenever the room is ready again. The lobby persists
// because nothing here ever closes the transport.
//
// The envelope is game traffic, so the reader honors it only
// from the peer (the same fromPeer gate as section 4.8): a
// spectator sharing the socket cannot end a match it is only
// watching.

// SendMatchEnd ends the current match and returns both
// players to the room. The sender's own transition happens
// here too (the host's client treats its own send as
// authoritative for rotation), so the sender's bridge sees
// the event through PollMatchEnd exactly like the receiver.
// Only a live match can end: calling this from the room is
// an error, as is calling it on a watch session, which must
// never send session traffic at all.
func (s *Session) SendMatchEnd(reason string) error {
	if s.watch {
		return errors.New("a spectator cannot end a match")
	}
	if err := s.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	playing := s.phase == phasePlaying
	s.mu.Unlock()
	if !playing {
		return errors.New("no match is running")
	}
	reason = strings.TrimSpace(reason)
	if err := s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "match_end", Reason: reason}); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.returnToRoomLocked(reason)
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.signal()
	return nil
}

// PollMatchEnd reports the most recent match end, ours or the
// peer's, exactly once: the reason (possibly empty) and true,
// then ("", false) until another match ends. The bridge
// flattens this to a plain string for the UI.
func (s *Session) PollMatchEnd() (string, bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if !s.matchEndSet {
		return "", false
	}
	reason := s.matchEndReason
	s.matchEndSet = false
	return reason, true
}

// noteMatchEndLocked folds a match_end from the peer into the
// session. Called by the reader with s.mu held.
func (s *Session) noteMatchEndLocked(reason string) {
	if s.ended {
		return
	}
	s.returnToRoomLocked(reason)
}

// returnToRoomLocked records the match-end event and, when a
// match was actually running, resets everything a match owns:
// the frame counter, both input maps, the hash books (frame
// numbers restart at 0, so a stale entry would corrupt the
// next match's checks), the setup handshake, both readys, the
// countdown, any half-assembled snapshot, resync bookkeeping,
// and pause state. Room membership is NOT reset: the peer is
// still here, their name is still known, chat and signaling
// history survive, and the socket was never touched. Called
// with s.mu held; idempotent, because both players may send
// match_end at the same moment and each side then processes
// the other's copy after its own transition.
func (s *Session) returnToRoomLocked(reason string) {
	s.matchEndReason = reason
	s.matchEndSet = true
	if s.phase != phasePlaying {
		return
	}
	s.phase = phaseRoom
	s.frame = 0
	s.localIn = make(map[int]uint16)
	s.remoteIn = make(map[int]uint16)
	s.localHash = make(map[int]string)
	s.remoteHash = make(map[int]string)
	s.checked = make(map[int]bool)
	s.offer = nil
	s.accept = nil
	s.reject = ""
	s.peerReady = false
	s.localReady = false
	s.countdownEnds = time.Time{}
	s.snapBuf = nil
	s.snapWant, s.snapChunks, s.snapGot, s.snapFrame = 0, 0, 0, 0
	s.snapReady = false
	s.snapFrom = ""
	s.snapApplied = -1
	s.resyncPending = false
	s.resyncReqFrame = 0
	s.lastResyncFrame = -1
	s.localPaused = false
	s.peerPaused = false
	s.lastPeerMsg = time.Now()
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/matchend_test.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"bytes"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// startMatchPair is startChatPair with the cores handed back:
// the match end tests compare core states across two matches.
func startMatchPair(t *testing.T) (*Session, *Session, *fakeCore, *fakeCore) {
	t.Helper()
	ta, tb := transportPair()
	hostCore := newFakeCore()
	guestCore := newFakeCore()
	base := Config{
		Game: "Super Mario World (USA).sfc", ROMHash: "deadbeef",
		CoreName: "snes9x", ReadyNow: true, Countdown: 100 * time.Millisecond,
	}
	hostCfg := base
	hostCfg.IsHost = true
	hostCfg.PlayerName = "Host"
	guestCfg := base
	guestCfg.PlayerName = "Guest"
	host := NewSession(ta, hostCore, hostCfg)
	guest := NewSession(tb, guestCore, guestCfg)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"peer_joined","role":"guest"}`)

	errCh := make(chan error, 2)
	go func() { errCh <- host.Start() }()
	go func() { errCh <- guest.Start() }()
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if err := <-errCh; err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
		}
	}
	return host, guest, hostCore, guestCore
}

// The money test for section 4.9: a match ends, both players
// land back in the room on the SAME sessions and sockets, and
// a second full handshake plus a full second match (hash
// checks included) completes in sync on them.
func TestMatchEndReturnsToRoomAndSecondMatchRuns(t *testing.T) {
	host, guest, hostCore, guestCore := startMatchPair(t)

	// Match 1: a short game, in sync.
	stepBurst(t, host, guest, 0, 150)
	if host.Frame() != 150 || guest.Frame() != 150 {
		t.Fatalf("match 1 frames: host %d guest %d", host.Frame(), guest.Frame())
	}
	// No next match while one is live.
	if err := host.StartNextMatch(); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("StartNextMatch ran during a live match")
	}

	// The host ends the match.
	if err := host.SendMatchEnd("good game"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendMatchEnd: %v", err)
	}
	// The sender sees its own event exactly once.
	if reason, ok := host.PollMatchEnd(); !ok || reason != "good game" {
		t.Fatalf("host PollMatchEnd = %q, %v; want good game, true", reason, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := host.PollMatchEnd(); ok {
		t.Fatal("host match end event reported twice")
	}
	// So does the guest.
	pollUntil(t, "guest match end event", func() bool {
		reason, ok := guest.PollMatchEnd()
		return ok && reason == "good game"
	})
	// A second end while already back in the room is an error.
	if err := host.SendMatchEnd("again"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("SendMatchEnd in the room was allowed")
	}

	// Both sides are in the room: readys reset, frame state
	// cleared, session alive, socket untouched.
	if host.RoomPhase() != "room" || guest.RoomPhase() != "room" {
		t.Fatalf("phases after match end: host %q guest %q",
			host.RoomPhase(), guest.RoomPhase())
	}
	if host.LocalReady() || host.PeerReady() || guest.LocalReady() || guest.PeerReady() {
		t.Error("readys were not reset by the match end")
	}
	if host.Frame() != 0 || guest.Frame() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("frames after match end: host %d guest %d, want 0",
			host.Frame(), guest.Frame())
	}
	if err := host.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("host session ended by match end: %v", err)
	}
	if err := guest.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("guest session ended by match end: %v", err)
	}
	// The socket still carries traffic both ways.
	if err := host.SendChat("good game, run it back"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("chat after match end: %v", err)
	}
	msgs := waitChat(t, guest, 0, 1)
	if msgs[0].From != "Host" || msgs[0].Text != "good game, run it back" {
		t.Errorf("chat after match end = %+v", msgs[0])
	}

	// Match 2: a full second handshake on the same sessions,
	// then a full game, long enough to cross a hash check,
	// ending in sync.
	errCh := make(chan error, 2)
	go func() { errCh <- host.StartNextMatch() }()
	go func() { errCh <- guest.StartNextMatch() }()
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if err := <-errCh; err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("second start: %v", err)
		}
	}
	stepBurst(t, host, guest, 0, 320)
	if host.Desyncs() != 0 || guest.Desyncs() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("match 2 desyncs: host %d guest %d", host.Desyncs(), guest.Desyncs())
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(hostCore.stateBytes(), guestCore.stateBytes()) {
		t.Fatal("core states differ after match 2")
	}
	if host.Frame() != 320 || guest.Frame() != 320 {
		t.Fatalf("match 2 frames: host %d guest %d", host.Frame(), guest.Frame())
	}
}

// A spectator sharing the socket cannot end the match: the
// envelope is gated on the peer, exactly like the other game
// traffic of section 4.8.
func TestMatchEndFromForeignSenderIgnored(t *testing.T) {
	r := startWatchRoom(t)
	stepBurst(t, r.host, r.guest, 0, 30)

	r.hostEnd.inject(`{"type":"match_end","reason":"rigged","from":"Watcher"}`)
	r.guestEnd.inject(`{"type":"match_end","reason":"rigged","from":"Watcher"}`)
	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)

	if r.host.RoomPhase() != "playing" || r.guest.RoomPhase() != "playing" {
		t.Fatalf("a spectator ended the match: host %q guest %q",
			r.host.RoomPhase(), r.guest.RoomPhase())
	}
	if _, ok := r.host.PollMatchEnd(); ok {
		t.Error("host recorded a spectator's match end")
	}
	if _, ok := r.guest.PollMatchEnd(); ok {
		t.Error("guest recorded a spectator's match end")
	}
}

// The watch side of match end: the watcher does not end, it
// falls back to the room with the players, hears the event,
// and asks for a fresh snapshot so the next match has its
// landing.
func TestWatchMatchEndReturnsToRoom(t *testing.T) {
	r := startWatchRoom(t)
	stepBurst(t, r.host, r.guest, 0, 30)

	if err := r.host.SendMatchEnd("tournament break"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendMatchEnd: %v", err)
	}
	if r.host.RoomPhase() != "room" {
		t.Fatalf("host phase after its own match end = %q, want room", r.host.RoomPhase())
	}
	pollUntil(t, "guest back in the room", func() bool {
		return r.guest.RoomPhase() == "room"
	})
	if reason, ok := r.guest.PollMatchEnd(); !ok || reason != "tournament break" {
		t.Errorf("guest PollMatchEnd = %q, %v", reason, ok)
	}

	pollUntil(t, "watcher back in the room", func() bool {
		phase, hostName, guestName, _ := r.watcher.WatchInfo()
		return phase == "room" && hostName == "Host" && guestName == "Guest"
	})
	if reason, ok := r.watcher.PollMatchEnd(); !ok || reason != "tournament break" {
		t.Errorf("watcher PollMatchEnd = %q, %v; want tournament break, true", reason, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := r.watcher.PollMatchEnd(); ok {
		t.Error("watcher match end event reported twice")
	}

	// The watcher asks for a fresh snapshot for the next
	// match (its second watch_sync: StartWatch sent the
	// first).
	syncs := func() int {
		n := 0
		for _, e := range r.watcherEnd.sentEnvelopes() {
			if e.Type == "watch_sync" {
				n++
			}
		}
		return n
	}
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for syncs() < 2 && time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		r.watcher.WatchStep()
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	if syncs() < 2 {
		t.Fatal("watcher never asked for a fresh snapshot after the match end")
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/room.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"errors"
	"time"
)

// The waiting room (PROTOCOL.md section 4.0): before the session
// setup handshake, the two players see each other in a room, both
// press Ready, and a shared countdown runs so both sides (and the
// relay) are settled before frame 0. The host owns the countdown.

const (
	phaseRoom = iota
	phasePlaying
)

const defaultCountdown = 5 * time.Second

// A peer that connects but never says hello is an older build;
// after this grace the room is skipped so mixed versions can
// still play.
const legacyPeerGrace = 20 * time.Second

func (s *Session) roomPhase() error {
	if s.cfg.ReadyNow {
		// Headless peers (tests, the netplayguest rig): introduce
		// and ready up immediately, then let the normal setup
		// waits take over.
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.localReady = true
		s.mu.Unlock()
		_ = s.sendEnv(s.helloEnv())
		_ = s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "ready"})
		return nil
	}
	countdown := s.cfg.Countdown
	if countdown <= 0 {
		countdown = defaultCountdown
	}
	_ = s.sendEnv(s.helloEnv())
	deadline := time.Now().Add(600 * time.Second)
	var helloAt, readyAt time.Time
	for {
		if err := s.checkEnded(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			return errors.New("timed out waiting for the other player")
		}
		s.mu.Lock()
		offer := s.offer
		present := s.peerPresent
		presentAt := s.peerPresentAt
		name := s.peerName
		bothReady := s.localReady && s.peerReady
		ends := s.countdownEnds
		s.mu.Unlock()

		// Legacy peers skip the room entirely.
		if offer != nil && !s.cfg.IsHost {
			return nil // an old host already sent its offer
		}
		if present && name == "" &&
			time.Since(presentAt) > legacyPeerGrace {
			return nil // an old peer never says hello
		}

		if bothReady {
			if s.cfg.IsHost && ends.IsZero() {
				ends = time.Now().Add(countdown)
				s.mu.Lock()
				s.countdownEnds = ends
				s.mu.Unlock()
				_ = s.sendEnv(envelope{
					Type: "countdown", EndsAt: ends.UnixMilli(),
				})
			}
			if !ends.IsZero() && !time.Now().Before(ends) {
				return nil
			}
		}

		// Re-introduce and re-state readiness (at most once a
		// second) until the peer has them: messages sent before
		// the peer's socket finished joining are lost.
		if present && name == "" && time.Since(helloAt) > time.Second {
			helloAt = time.Now()
			_ = s.sendEnv(s.helloEnv())
		}
		s.mu.Lock()
		lr := s.localReady
		s.mu.Unlock()
		if lr && time.Since(readyAt) > time.Second {
			readyAt = time.Now()
			_ = s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "ready"})
		}

		select {
		case <-s.notifyCh:
		case <-time.After(200 * time.Millisecond):
		}
	}
}

// SetReady marks the local player ready in the room. One-way by
// design: ready means ready.
func (s *Session) SetReady() {
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.localReady = true
	s.mu.Unlock()
	_ = s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "ready"})
	s.signal()
}

// RoomPhase reports where the session is for the UI:
// "waiting" (nobody else here yet), "room" (peer present, not
// both ready), "countdown", or "playing".
func (s *Session) RoomPhase() string {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if s.phase == phasePlaying {
		return "playing"
	}
	if !s.countdownEnds.IsZero() {
		return "countdown"
	}
	if s.peerName != "" {
		return "room"
	}
	return "waiting"
}

// PeerName is the other player's display name, once known.
func (s *Session) PeerName() string {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.peerName
}

// PeerReady reports whether the other player has pressed Ready.
func (s *Session) PeerReady() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.peerReady
}

// LocalReady reports whether this player has pressed Ready.
func (s *Session) LocalReady() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.localReady
}

// CountdownSeconds is the whole seconds left on the shared
// countdown (0 when none is running).
func (s *Session) CountdownSeconds() int {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if s.countdownEnds.IsZero() {
		return 0
	}
	d := time.Until(s.countdownEnds)
	if d <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	return int((d + time.Second - 1) / time.Second)
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/roster.go ====================

package netsession

// Room roster (PROTOCOL.md sections 3 and 4.8). The server
// mints a roster notice on every membership change: the full
// member list, seats and watchers alike. Every client in the
// room keeps the latest copy so the UI can show who holds the
// seats and who is watching, which is also what the host
// referee's seat controls (section 4.9) are built on. The
// roster is display state only: it never touches lockstep.

// noteRosterLocked stores the server's latest member list.
// Called by the reader with s.mu held (both the player
// dispatch in step.go and the watch dispatch in watch.go).
func (s *Session) noteRosterLocked(members []RosterMember) {
	cp := make([]RosterMember, len(members))
	copy(cp, members)
	s.roster = cp
}

// Roster returns the room's member list, host first, in the
// order the server sent it. The result is a copy; callers may
// keep it.
//
// Until the first roster notice arrives (an older server, or
// the moment before it lands), the list is synthesized from
// what the session already knows: a player session knows
// itself and its peer from the hello exchange, and a watch
// session knows the two seat holders and itself. A plain
// two-player room therefore reports the right list either
// way; only the watchers are missing from a synthesized one.
func (s *Session) Roster() []RosterMember {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if len(s.roster) > 0 {
		out := make([]RosterMember, len(s.roster))
		copy(out, s.roster)
		return out
	}
	out := []RosterMember{}
	if s.watch {
		if s.watchHost != "" {
			out = append(out, RosterMember{Name: s.watchHost, Role: "host"})
		}
		if s.watchGuest != "" {
			out = append(out, RosterMember{Name: s.watchGuest, Role: "guest"})
		}
		if s.cfg.PlayerName != "" {
			out = append(out, RosterMember{Name: s.cfg.PlayerName, Role: "spectator"})
		}
		return out
	}
	hostName, guestName := s.peerName, s.cfg.PlayerName
	if s.cfg.IsHost {
		hostName, guestName = s.cfg.PlayerName, s.peerName
	}
	if hostName != "" {
		out = append(out, RosterMember{Name: hostName, Role: "host"})
	}
	if guestName != "" {
		out = append(out, RosterMember{Name: guestName, Role: "guest"})
	}
	return out
}

package netsession

import (
	"reflect"
	"testing"
)

// Before any roster notice lands, a plain two-player room
// synthesizes its list from the hello exchange: both sides
// report the same two members, host first.
func TestRosterSynthesizedFromHello(t *testing.T) {
	host, guest, _, _ := startChatPair(t)
	want := []RosterMember{
		{Name: "Host", Role: "host"},
		{Name: "Guest", Role: "guest"},
	}
	if got := host.Roster(); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("host roster = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
	if got := guest.Roster(); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("guest roster = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
}

// A roster notice from the server is stored whole and wins
// over the synthesis, watchers included. The returned list is
// a copy: mutating it must not corrupt the session's.
func TestRosterNoticeStoredForPlayer(t *testing.T) {
	_, guest, _, tb := startChatPair(t)
	tb.inject(`{"type":"roster","members":[` +
		`{"name":"Host","role":"host"},` +
		`{"name":"Guest","role":"guest"},` +
		`{"name":"Fan","role":"spectator"}]}`)
	want := []RosterMember{
		{Name: "Host", Role: "host"},
		{Name: "Guest", Role: "guest"},
		{Name: "Fan", Role: "spectator"},
	}
	pollUntil(t, "guest stores the roster notice", func() bool {
		return reflect.DeepEqual(guest.Roster(), want)
	})
	got := guest.Roster()
	got[0].Name = "Mutated"
	if guest.Roster()[0].Name != "Host" {
		t.Error("Roster handed out the session's own slice")
	}
}

// A later notice replaces the earlier one whole: a member
// who left is gone, not merged.
func TestRosterNoticeReplaces(t *testing.T) {
	_, guest, _, tb := startChatPair(t)
	tb.inject(`{"type":"roster","members":[` +
		`{"name":"Host","role":"host"},` +
		`{"name":"Guest","role":"guest"},` +
		`{"name":"Fan","role":"spectator"}]}`)
	pollUntil(t, "first roster stored", func() bool {
		return len(guest.Roster()) == 3
	})
	tb.inject(`{"type":"roster","members":[` +
		`{"name":"Host","role":"host"},` +
		`{"name":"Guest","role":"guest"}]}`)
	want := []RosterMember{
		{Name: "Host", Role: "host"},
		{Name: "Guest", Role: "guest"},
	}
	pollUntil(t, "second roster replaces the first", func() bool {
		return reflect.DeepEqual(guest.Roster(), want)
	})
}

// The watcher synthesizes its room from the players' hellos
// (plus itself, as a spectator) before any roster notice, and
// stores the notice whole when one lands.
func TestRosterWatchSynthesisAndNotice(t *testing.T) {
	r := startWatchRoom(t)
	wantSynth := []RosterMember{
		{Name: "Host", Role: "host"},
		{Name: "Guest", Role: "guest"},
		{Name: "Watcher", Role: "spectator"},
	}
	pollUntil(t, "watcher synthesizes from hellos", func() bool {
		return reflect.DeepEqual(r.watcher.Roster(), wantSynth)
	})

	r.watcherEnd.inject(`{"type":"roster","members":[` +
		`{"name":"Host","role":"host"},` +
		`{"name":"Guest","role":"guest"},` +
		`{"name":"Watcher","role":"spectator"},` +
		`{"name":"SecondFan","role":"spectator"}]}`)
	want := append(wantSynth, RosterMember{Name: "SecondFan", Role: "spectator"})
	pollUntil(t, "watcher stores the roster notice", func() bool {
		return reflect.DeepEqual(r.watcher.Roster(), want)
	})
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/seats.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"errors"
	"strings"
)

// Seat assignment (PROTOCOL.md section 4.9, SPECTATOR_DESIGN.md
// slice S4). The host client is the room's referee: it alone
// decides who fills the two player seats next, and it says so
// out loud with a seat_assign envelope so the guest and every
// spectator hear the same call at the same time. The envelope
// is a broadcast of a decision, not a request; the named player
// takes the seat through the normal room flow (joining as that
// seat, or being promoted from the watcher row), and naming
// someone else for seat 2 is how the current guest rotates
// out. No server state is involved.
//
// Honor rules: the send API refuses anyone but the host, and
// receivers never trust claims inside the envelope. A player
// session records an assignment only when it arrives from the
// peer (for the guest, the peer IS the host; see the fromPeer
// gate in step.go), and a watch session only when it carries
// the known host's stamp. An assignment from a spectator, or
// one naming nobody, or one for a seat that does not exist,
// is dropped on the floor.

// seatAssignQueueCap bounds the pending assignment queue the
// same way the watch sync queue is bounded: a referee making
// calls faster than the UI polls cannot grow it forever.
const seatAssignQueueCap = 16

// SeatAssign is one recorded seat call: who the host named,
// and for which seat (1 or 2).
type SeatAssign struct {
	Player string
	Seat   int
}

// SendSeatAssign broadcasts the host's seat call. Only the
// host client may send it (a guest or a spectator gets an
// error and nothing goes out), the player must be named, and
// the seat must be 1 or 2.
func (s *Session) SendSeatAssign(player string, seat int) error {
	if s.watch {
		return errors.New("a spectator cannot assign seats")
	}
	if !s.cfg.IsHost {
		return errors.New("only the host assigns seats")
	}
	player = strings.TrimSpace(player)
	if player == "" {
		return errors.New("seat assignment names nobody")
	}
	if seat != 1 && seat != 2 {
		return errors.New("seat must be 1 or 2")
	}
	return s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "seat_assign", Player: player, Seat: seat})
}

// noteSeatAssignLocked records an assignment the reader has
// already attributed to a legitimate referee (the peer for a
// player session, the known host for a watch session).
// Malformed calls are ignored rather than trusted. Called
// with s.mu held.
func (s *Session) noteSeatAssignLocked(player string, seat int) {
	player = strings.TrimSpace(player)
	if player == "" || (seat != 1 && seat != 2) {
		return
	}
	s.seatAssigns = append(s.seatAssigns, SeatAssign{Player: player, Seat: seat})
	if len(s.seatAssigns) > seatAssignQueueCap {
		s.seatAssigns = s.seatAssigns[len(s.seatAssigns)-seatAssignQueueCap:]
	}
}

// PollSeatAssign drains the oldest recorded seat call, the
// same drain-one shape as PollWatchSync: the player (or
// spectator) it names, the seat, and false when no call is
// waiting.
func (s *Session) PollSeatAssign() (player string, seat int, ok bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if len(s.seatAssigns) == 0 {
		return "", 0, false
	}
	a := s.seatAssigns[0]
	s.seatAssigns = s.seatAssigns[1:]
	return a.Player, a.Seat, true
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/seats_test.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// Send side: only the host may assign, the call must name
// someone, the seat must exist, and a valid call reaches the
// guest's queue exactly once.
func TestSeatAssignSendValidationAndDelivery(t *testing.T) {
	host, guest, _, _ := startChatPair(t)

	if err := guest.SendSeatAssign("Fan", 2); err == nil {
		t.Error("a guest was allowed to assign seats")
	}
	for _, bad := range []struct {
		player string
		seat   int
	}{
		{"", 1}, {"   ", 2}, {"Fan", 0}, {"Fan", 3}, {"Fan", -1},
	} {
		if err := host.SendSeatAssign(bad.player, bad.seat); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("SendSeatAssign(%q, %d) was allowed", bad.player, bad.seat)
		}
	}
	// None of the refused calls may have leaked an envelope.
	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
	if _, _, ok := guest.PollSeatAssign(); ok {
		t.Fatal("a refused seat assignment reached the guest")
	}

	if err := host.SendSeatAssign("Fan", 2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendSeatAssign: %v", err)
	}
	pollUntil(t, "guest records the seat call", func() bool {
		player, seat, ok := guest.PollSeatAssign()
		return ok && player == "Fan" && seat == 2
	})
	if _, _, ok := guest.PollSeatAssign(); ok {
		t.Error("the same seat call was handed out twice")
	}
}

// Receive side: malformed calls are dropped even from the
// host, and a well-formed call from a non-host (a spectator
// sharing the socket) is ignored by the guest. Authority is
// the sender's identity, never a field in the envelope.
func TestSeatAssignInboundGateAndValidation(t *testing.T) {
	_, guest, _, tb := startChatPair(t)

	tb.inject(`{"type":"seat_assign","player":"Fan","seat":1,"from":"Watcher"}`)
	tb.inject(`{"type":"seat_assign","player":"","seat":2,"from":"Host"}`)
	tb.inject(`{"type":"seat_assign","player":"Fan","seat":0,"from":"Host"}`)
	tb.inject(`{"type":"seat_assign","player":"Fan","seat":3,"from":"Host"}`)
	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
	if player, seat, ok := guest.PollSeatAssign(); ok {
		t.Fatalf("guest recorded %q for seat %d from a foreign or malformed call",
			player, seat)
	}

	tb.inject(`{"type":"seat_assign","player":"Fan","seat":1,"from":"Host"}`)
	pollUntil(t, "guest records the host's call", func() bool {
		player, seat, ok := guest.PollSeatAssign()
		return ok && player == "Fan" && seat == 1
	})
}

// The watcher hears the referee too, on the host's stamp
// alone: a call stamped by the guest is not the referee's
// and is not recorded.
func TestWatchSeatAssignFromHostOnly(t *testing.T) {
	r := startWatchRoom(t)

	r.watcherEnd.inject(`{"type":"seat_assign","player":"Watcher","seat":1,"from":"Guest"}`)
	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
	if _, _, ok := r.watcher.PollSeatAssign(); ok {
		t.Fatal("watcher recorded a seat call stamped by the guest")
	}

	if err := r.host.SendSeatAssign("Watcher", 2); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendSeatAssign: %v", err)
	}
	pollUntil(t, "watcher records the host's call", func() bool {
		player, seat, ok := r.watcher.PollSeatAssign()
		return ok && player == "Watcher" && seat == 2
	})
	// The guest hears the same call from its peer.
	pollUntil(t, "guest records the host's call", func() bool {
		player, seat, ok := r.guest.PollSeatAssign()
		return ok && player == "Watcher" && seat == 2
	})
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/session.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Core is the slice of the emulator bridge the session drives. The
// mobile package adapts the real bridge to it; tests use a fake.
type Core interface {
	RunFrame()
	// SetButtons applies a full 16-bit button mask (libretro order)
	// to one player slot.
	SetButtons(player int, mask uint16)
	SaveState() []byte
	LoadState(data []byte) error
}

// Transport is the signaling socket (WSConn satisfies it).
type Transport interface {
	WriteText(text string) error
	ReadMessage() ([]byte, error)
	Close() error
}

type Config struct {
	Game     string // ROM file name both sides must agree on
	ROMHash  string // sha256 hex of the local ROM file
	CoreName string
	IsHost   bool
	// InputDelay is what the guest proposes in session_accept.
	// Zero means the default (4).
	InputDelay int
	// PlayerName is this player's display name, exchanged in the
	// waiting room.
	PlayerName string
	// ReadyNow skips the waiting room's ready ritual: the peer
	// introduces itself and readies immediately. For headless
	// drivers (tests, the netplayguest rig) that have no UI.
	ReadyNow bool
	// Countdown is the shared countdown once both players are
	// ready. Zero means the default (5s).
	Countdown time.Duration
	// SilenceLimit is how long the peer may go quiet mid-session
	// before the session is declared lost. Time the peer spends
	// paused (see SetPaused) does not count. Zero means the
	// default (15s).
	SilenceLimit time.Duration
}

// RosterMember is one entry of the server's roster notice
// (PROTOCOL.md section 3): a room member's name and role
// ("host", "guest", or "spectator"). Exported because the
// mobile bridge hands the list to the UI (roster.go).
type RosterMember struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
	Role string `json:"role"`
}

type envelope struct {
	Type string          `json:"type"`
	Raw  json.RawMessage `json:"-"`
	// sender tagging (PROTOCOL.md section 4.8): with spectators
	// in the room a socket carries frames from several people,
	// so senders stamp who they are. From is set by sendEnv on
	// every envelope; Seat (host 1, guest 2) rides input
	// envelopes so a watcher can attribute the two streams.
	From string `json:"from,omitempty"`
	Seat int    `json:"seat,omitempty"`
	// To addresses a snapshot transfer to one room member
	// (section 4.4); empty means unaddressed, the pre-spectator
	// behavior.
	To string `json:"to,omitempty"`
	// common fields
	Role     string   `json:"role,omitempty"`
	Game     string   `json:"game,omitempty"`
	ROMHash  string   `json:"romHash,omitempty"`
	Core     string   `json:"core,omitempty"`
	Protocol int      `json:"protocol,omitempty"`
	Cheats   []string `json:"cheats,omitempty"`
	Reason   string   `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	// roster notice (server minted)
	Members []RosterMember `json:"members,omitempty"`
	// input
	Frame   int    `json:"frame,omitempty"`
	Buttons uint16 `json:"buttons,omitempty"`
	// hash check
	Hash string `json:"hash,omitempty"`
	// session accept
	InputDelay   int `json:"inputDelay,omitempty"`
	HashInterval int `json:"hashInterval,omitempty"`
	// waiting room
	Player string `json:"player,omitempty"`
	EndsAt int64  `json:"endsAt,omitempty"`
	// Got Next line (gotnext.go): Action is "join" or "leave"
	// on a got_next envelope; Queue is the host referee's
	// authoritative line order on a got_next_queue envelope.
	Action string   `json:"action,omitempty"`
	Queue  []string `json:"queue,omitempty"`
	// Tournament name (tournament.go): on a "tournament"
	// envelope, the host's name for the event this room's
	// results are reported under (PROTOCOL.md section 8).
	Name string `json:"name,omitempty"`
	// pause
	Paused bool `json:"paused,omitempty"`
	// chat
	Text string `json:"text,omitempty"`
	// voice signaling (PROTOCOL.md 3.1)
	SDP           string `json:"sdp,omitempty"`
	Candidate     string `json:"candidate,omitempty"`
	SDPMid        string `json:"sdpMid,omitempty"`
	SDPMLineIndex int    `json:"sdpMLineIndex,omitempty"`
	// snapshot
	Bytes  int    `json:"bytes,omitempty"`
	Chunks int    `json:"chunks,omitempty"`
	Seq    int    `json:"seq,omitempty"`
	Data   string `json:"data,omitempty"`
	SHA256 string `json:"sha256,omitempty"`
}

const (
	defaultInputDelay   = 4
	defaultHashInterval = 300
	snapshotChunkBytes  = 64 * 1024
	peerSilenceLimit    = 15 * time.Second
)

type Session struct {
	t    Transport
	core Core
	cfg  Config

	delay        int
	hashInterval int

	mu       sync.Mutex
	notifyCh chan struct{}

	frame    int // next frame to simulate
	localIn  map[int]uint16
	remoteIn map[int]uint16

	localHash  map[int]string
	remoteHash map[int]string
	checked    map[int]bool

	offer      *envelope
	accept     *envelope
	reject     string
	peerJoined bool
	peerGone   bool
	ended      bool
	endErr     error

	// snapshot assembly (guest side) / application
	snapBuf     []byte
	snapWant    int
	snapChunks  int
	snapGot     int
	snapFrame   int
	snapReady   bool
	snapFrom    string // sender of the snapshot being assembled
	snapApplied int    // last frame the peer confirmed applying, -1 none

	// snapMu serializes whole snapshot transfers on the wire:
	// a transfer is a run of envelopes that must not interleave
	// with another transfer (a desync resync to the guest and a
	// watch answer to a spectator can be in flight together).
	snapMu sync.Mutex

	// watchSyncReqs holds the names of spectators who asked
	// this player session for a snapshot (watch.go), oldest
	// first. Guarded by mu.
	watchSyncReqs []string

	// Spectator state (watch.go): only used when watch is true.
	// Guarded by mu like the rest.
	watch             bool
	watchHost         string // seat 1 player's name, once known
	watchGuest        string // seat 2 player's name, once known
	watchIn1          map[int]uint16
	watchIn2          map[int]uint16
	watchFrame        int // next frame the watcher will deliver
	watchNeutralUntil int // frames below this are agreed neutral
	watchDelay        int // input delay, learned from session_accept
	watchLive         bool
	watchSnapFrame    int // frame of the last applied snapshot, -1 none
	watchSnapPending  bool
	watchMaxPair      int // highest frame holding both seats' inputs
	watchGoneHost     bool
	watchGoneGuest    bool
	watchNeedSync     bool // a fresh snapshot is owed (match ended)
	lastWatchSync     time.Time
	lastWatchStep     time.Time // last frame delivered or snapshot applied

	// host side: a resync was requested
	resyncPending   bool
	resyncReqFrame  int
	lastResyncFrame int // snapshot frame of the last completed resync

	lastPeerMsg time.Time
	desyncs     int
	stalls      int

	// waiting room state (room.go)
	phase         int
	peerPresent   bool
	peerPresentAt time.Time
	peerName      string
	peerReady     bool
	localReady    bool
	countdownEnds time.Time

	// chat log (chat.go): every message sent or received this
	// session, oldest first, capped. Guarded by mu like the rest.
	chatLog []ChatMessage
	chatSeq int // seq of the most recent log entry, 0 when empty

	// voice signaling queue (signal.go): inbound offer,
	// answer, and ice entries from the peer, oldest first,
	// capped. Guarded by mu like the rest.
	signalQueue []SignalMessage
	signalSeq   int // seq of the most recent entry, 0 when empty

	// match end and seat assignment (matchend.go, seats.go):
	// the most recent match_end's reason and whether the UI
	// has yet to collect it, plus the queue of seat calls the
	// host referee has made. Guarded by mu like the rest.
	matchEndReason string
	matchEndSet    bool
	seatAssigns    []SeatAssign

	// roster is the latest member list the server sent
	// (roster.go), guarded by mu like the rest. Empty until
	// the first roster notice lands.
	roster []RosterMember

	// Got Next line (gotnext.go): the tracked queue order
	// (the host's own list, or the host's last broadcast as
	// mirrored by everyone else) and, on the host, whether
	// it changed since the last broadcast went out. Guarded
	// by mu like the rest. Deliberately NOT reset by a match
	// end: the line is what the next match is for.
	gotNextQueue []string
	gotNextDirty bool

	// tournamentName is the room's tournament name as the
	// host named it (tournament.go), guarded by mu like the
	// rest. Room state, not match state: like the Got Next
	// line, a match end deliberately leaves it standing.
	tournamentName string

	// started reports whether Start has launched the reader;
	// StartNextMatch refuses to run without it.
	started bool

	// pause state: while either side is paused, lockstep stalls
	// by design and the silence limit does not apply.
	localPaused bool
	peerPaused  bool
	// lastResume is when this side last unpaused. The silence
	// clock restarts there: the quiet during our own pause was
	// our doing, and the peer needs a moment to answer anyway.
	lastResume time.Time
}

func NewSession(t Transport, core Core, cfg Config) *Session {
	return &Session{
		t:               t,
		core:            core,
		cfg:             cfg,
		delay:           defaultInputDelay,
		hashInterval:    defaultHashInterval,
		notifyCh:        make(chan struct{}, 1),
		localIn:         make(map[int]uint16),
		remoteIn:        make(map[int]uint16),
		localHash:       make(map[int]string),
		remoteHash:      make(map[int]string),
		checked:         make(map[int]bool),
		snapApplied:     -1,
		lastResyncFrame: -1,
		lastPeerMsg:     time.Now(),
	}
}

func (s *Session) silenceLimit() time.Duration {
	if s.cfg.SilenceLimit > 0 {
		return s.cfg.SilenceLimit
	}
	return peerSilenceLimit
}

// SetPaused tells the peer this side has paused (its menu is
// open) or resumed. While either side is paused the other side
// waits without tripping the silence limit: a paused game is
// stalled, not lost. The transport itself still reports a peer
// that truly vanishes (socket close ends the session as before).
func (s *Session) SetPaused(p bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.localPaused = p
	if !p {
		s.lastResume = time.Now()
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	_ = s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "pause", Paused: p})
}

// PeerPaused reports whether the other player has told us they
// are paused.
func (s *Session) PeerPaused() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.peerPaused
}

// LocalPaused reports whether this side is marked paused.
func (s *Session) LocalPaused() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.localPaused
}

func (s *Session) signal() {
	select {
	case s.notifyCh <- struct{}{}:
	default:
	}
}

func (s *Session) send(v any) error {
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return s.t.WriteText(string(b))
}

// sendEnv is the single send path for session envelopes, so
// it is where sender tagging happens (PROTOCOL.md section
// 4.8): every envelope carries "from" with our player name,
// and input envelopes additionally carry our seat number. No
// call site can forget, and a receiver can always tell a
// player's frames apart from a spectator's on the same socket.
// (Voice signaling in signal.go deliberately keeps its own
// exact wire shape and does not go through here.)
func (s *Session) sendEnv(e envelope) error {
	if s.cfg.PlayerName != "" {
		e.From = s.cfg.PlayerName
	}
	if e.Type == "input" {
		e.Seat = s.seatNumber()
	}
	return s.send(e)
}

// seatNumber is our seat at the table: host 1, guest 2.
// Spectators hold no seat (0) and never send inputs.
func (s *Session) seatNumber() int {
	if s.watch {
		return 0
	}
	if s.cfg.IsHost {
		return 1
	}
	return 2
}

// playerRole is how a player marks its hello: the seat it
// holds, "host" or "guest". A spectator's hello says
// "spectator" instead (watch.go), which is how player
// sessions know never to mistake it for the peer.
func (s *Session) playerRole() string {
	if s.cfg.IsHost {
		return "host"
	}
	return "guest"
}

func (s *Session) helloEnv() envelope {
	return envelope{
		Type: "hello", Player: s.cfg.PlayerName, Role: s.playerRole(),
	}
}

// Start runs the waiting room (PROTOCOL.md section 4.0) and then
// the session setup handshake (section 4.1), returning once both
// sides are ready to step frames from 0.
func (s *Session) Start() error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.started = true
	s.mu.Unlock()
	go s.reader()
	return s.beginMatch()
}

// StartNextMatch runs the room and the setup handshake again on
// a session a match_end already returned to the room
// (PROTOCOL.md section 4.9): the socket, the reader, and the
// room membership all survive a match, so the next one needs
// no new connection, just the same ritual as the first. It
// refuses to run while a match is live or the session is over.
func (s *Session) StartNextMatch() error {
	if s.watch {
		return errors.New("a spectator has no match to start")
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	ready := s.started && s.phase == phaseRoom && !s.ended
	s.mu.Unlock()
	if !ready {
		return errors.New("the session is not waiting in the room")
	}
	return s.beginMatch()
}

// beginMatch is the shared body of Start and StartNextMatch:
// the waiting room ritual, then the setup handshake.
func (s *Session) beginMatch() error {
	if err := s.roomPhase(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.phase = phasePlaying
	s.mu.Unlock()
	if s.cfg.IsHost {
		return s.startHost()
	}
	return s.startGuest()
}

func (s *Session) startHost() error {
	// Wait for the guest to show up on the socket.
	if err := s.waitFor(func() bool { return s.peerJoined || s.ended }, 600*time.Second); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := s.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := s.sendEnv(envelope{
		Type: "session_offer", Game: s.cfg.Game, ROMHash: s.cfg.ROMHash,
		Core: s.cfg.CoreName, Protocol: 1, Cheats: []string{},
	}); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := s.waitFor(func() bool {
		return s.accept != nil || s.reject != "" || s.ended
	}, 60*time.Second); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if s.reject != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("guest rejected the session: %s", s.reject)
	}
	if err := s.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.delay = s.accept.InputDelay
	if s.delay <= 0 {
		s.delay = defaultInputDelay
	}
	s.hashInterval = s.accept.HashInterval
	if s.hashInterval <= 0 {
		s.hashInterval = defaultHashInterval
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
	// Starting snapshot: the power-on state, captured before any
	// frame runs, so both sides begin byte-identical.
	state := s.core.SaveState()
	if len(state) == 0 {
		return errors.New("core returned an empty starting state")
	}
	if err := s.sendSnapshot(0, state); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := s.waitFor(func() bool {
		return s.snapApplied >= 0 || s.ended
	}, 60*time.Second); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.prefillNeutral(0)
	return nil
}

// prefillNeutral seeds both input maps with neutral (no buttons)
// inputs for frames [from, from+delay). Both sides do this wherever
// a snapshot (re)starts play: those frames were never sampled by
// either player, and lockstep needs an agreed value for them.
func (s *Session) prefillNeutral(from int) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	for f := from; f < from+s.delay; f++ {
		s.localIn[f] = 0
		s.remoteIn[f] = 0
	}
}

func (s *Session) startGuest() error {
	if err := s.waitFor(func() bool {
		return s.offer != nil || s.ended
	}, 120*time.Second); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := s.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	offer := s.offer
	s.mu.Unlock()
	if offer.ROMHash != s.cfg.ROMHash || offer.Game != s.cfg.Game {
		_ = s.sendEnv(envelope{
			Type:   "session_reject",
			Reason: "different game or ROM version",
		})
		return fmt.Errorf("session rejected: ROM mismatch (host has %q)", offer.Game)
	}
	delay := s.cfg.InputDelay
	if delay <= 0 {
		delay = defaultInputDelay
	}
	if err := s.sendEnv(envelope{
		Type: "session_accept", InputDelay: delay,
		HashInterval: defaultHashInterval,
	}); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.delay = delay
	s.hashInterval = defaultHashInterval
	s.mu.Unlock()
	// Wait for the starting snapshot and apply it.
	if err := s.waitFor(func() bool { return s.snapReady || s.ended }, 60*time.Second); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := s.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	state, frame, from := s.takeSnapshot()
	if err := s.core.LoadState(state); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("loading starting snapshot: %w", err)
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.frame = frame
	s.mu.Unlock()
	s.prefillNeutral(frame)
	return s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "snapshot_applied", Frame: frame, To: from})
}

package netsession

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// --- fake transport pair (stands in for the relaying hub) ---

type fakeTransport struct {
	inbox  chan []byte
	peer   *fakeTransport
	closed chan struct{}
	once   sync.Once
}

func transportPair() (*fakeTransport, *fakeTransport) {
	a := &fakeTransport{inbox: make(chan []byte, 4096), closed: make(chan struct{})}
	b := &fakeTransport{inbox: make(chan []byte, 4096), closed: make(chan struct{})}
	a.peer = b
	b.peer = a
	return a, b
}

func (t *fakeTransport) WriteText(text string) error {
	select {
	case <-t.closed:
		return errors.New("closed")
	default:
	}
	select {
	case t.peer.inbox <- []byte(text):
		return nil
	case <-t.peer.closed:
		return errors.New("peer closed")
	}
}

func (t *fakeTransport) ReadMessage() ([]byte, error) {
	select {
	case msg := <-t.inbox:
		return msg, nil
	case <-t.closed:
		return nil, errors.New("closed")
	}
}

func (t *fakeTransport) Close() error {
	t.once.Do(func() { close(t.closed) })
	return nil
}

func (t *fakeTransport) inject(text string) {
	t.inbox <- []byte(text)
}

// --- deterministic fake core ---

type fakeCore struct {
	mu        sync.Mutex
	state     [64]byte
	masks     [2]uint16
	frames    int
	corruptAt int // frame at which to flip a state byte once, -1 never
}

func newFakeCore() *fakeCore {
	c := &fakeCore{corruptAt: -1}
	for i := range c.state {
		c.state[i] = byte(i * 7)
	}
	return c
}

func (c *fakeCore) SetButtons(player int, mask uint16) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	c.masks[player] = mask
}

func (c *fakeCore) RunFrame() {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	m0, m1 := c.masks[0], c.masks[1]
	for i := range c.state {
		c.state[i] = c.state[i]*33 ^ byte(m0) ^ byte(m0>>8) ^ byte(m1<<1) ^ byte(m1>>3) ^ byte(i)
	}
	c.frames++
	if c.corruptAt >= 0 && c.frames == c.corruptAt {
		c.state[0] ^= 0xFF
		c.corruptAt = -1
	}
}

func (c *fakeCore) SaveState() []byte {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]byte, 0, 72)
	out = append(out, c.state[:]...)
	var fb [8]byte
	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(fb[:], uint64(c.frames))
	return append(out, fb[:]...)
}

func (c *fakeCore) LoadState(data []byte) error {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	if len(data) != 72 {
		return errors.New("bad state size")
	}
	copy(c.state[:], data[:64])
	c.frames = int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint64(data[64:]))
	return nil
}

func (c *fakeCore) stateBytes() []byte {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]byte, 64)
	copy(out, c.state[:])
	return out
}

// --- session driver ---

func runPair(t *testing.T, frames int, corruptGuestAt int) (*Session, *Session, *fakeCore, *fakeCore) {
	t.Helper()
	ta, tb := transportPair()
	hostCore := newFakeCore()
	guestCore := newFakeCore()
	guestCore.corruptAt = corruptGuestAt
	cfg := Config{Game: "Super Mario World (USA).sfc", ROMHash: "deadbeef", CoreName: "snes9x", ReadyNow: true}
	hostCfg := cfg
	hostCfg.IsHost = true
	host := NewSession(ta, hostCore, hostCfg)
	guest := NewSession(tb, guestCore, cfg)
	// The hub tells the host a guest connected.
	ta.inject(`{"type":"peer_joined","role":"guest"}`)

	errCh := make(chan error, 2)
	go func() { errCh <- host.Start() }()
	go func() { errCh <- guest.Start() }()
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if err := <-errCh; err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
		}
	}

	hostMask := func(f int) uint16 { return uint16((f * 3) % 512) }
	guestMask := func(f int) uint16 { return uint16((f * 5) % 1024) }
	stepErr := make(chan error, 2)
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	wg.Add(2)
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		for f := 0; f < frames; f++ {
			if err := host.Step(hostMask(f)); err != nil {
				stepErr <- err
				return
			}
		}
	}()
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		for f := 0; f < frames; f++ {
			if err := guest.Step(guestMask(f)); err != nil {
				stepErr <- err
				return
			}
		}
	}()
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() { wg.Wait(); close(done) }()
	select {
	case <-done:
	case err := <-stepErr:
		t.Fatalf("step: %v", err)
	case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("timed out: lockstep deadlocked")
	}
	return host, guest, hostCore, guestCore
}

func TestLockstepStaysInSync(t *testing.T) {
	host, guest, hc, gc := runPair(t, 700, -1)
	if host.Desyncs() != 0 || guest.Desyncs() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected desyncs: host %d guest %d", host.Desyncs(), guest.Desyncs())
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(hc.stateBytes(), gc.stateBytes()) {
		t.Fatal("final states differ after 700 in-sync frames")
	}
	if host.Frame() != 700 || guest.Frame() != 700 {
		t.Fatalf("frame counters: host %d guest %d", host.Frame(), guest.Frame())
	}
}

// The waiting room: names are exchanged, the session must not
// start until BOTH players ready up, then the shared countdown
// runs and lockstep proceeds in sync.
func TestRoomReadyThenLockstep(t *testing.T) {
	ta, tb := transportPair()
	hostCore := newFakeCore()
	guestCore := newFakeCore()
	base := Config{
		Game: "Super Mario World (USA).sfc", ROMHash: "deadbeef",
		CoreName: "snes9x", Countdown: 300 * time.Millisecond,
	}
	hostCfg := base
	hostCfg.IsHost = true
	hostCfg.PlayerName = "Host"
	guestCfg := base
	guestCfg.PlayerName = "Guest"
	host := NewSession(ta, hostCore, hostCfg)
	guest := NewSession(tb, guestCore, guestCfg)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"peer_joined","role":"guest"}`)

	errCh := make(chan error, 2)
	go func() { errCh <- host.Start() }()
	go func() { errCh <- guest.Start() }()

	waitUntil := func(what string, pred func() bool) {
		t.Helper()
		deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
		for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
			if pred() {
				return
			}
			time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
		}
		t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
	}
	waitUntil("name exchange", func() bool {
		return host.PeerName() == "Guest" && guest.PeerName() == "Host"
	})
	if host.RoomPhase() != "room" || guest.RoomPhase() != "room" {
		t.Fatalf("phases: host %q guest %q", host.RoomPhase(), guest.RoomPhase())
	}

	guest.SetReady()
	waitUntil("host sees guest ready", host.PeerReady)
	// The host has not readied: nobody may have started.
	select {
	case err := <-errCh:
		t.Fatalf("session started before both players were ready: %v", err)
	case <-time.After(300 * time.Millisecond):
	}

	host.SetReady()
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		select {
		case err := <-errCh:
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("start after ready: %v", err)
			}
		case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
			t.Fatal("countdown never released the session")
		}
	}

	// Lockstep from frame 0, in sync.
	stepErr := make(chan error, 2)
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	wg.Add(2)
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		for f := 0; f < 150; f++ {
			if err := host.Step(uint16(f % 256)); err != nil {
				stepErr <- err
				return
			}
		}
	}()
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		for f := 0; f < 150; f++ {
			if err := guest.Step(uint16((f * 2) % 256)); err != nil {
				stepErr <- err
				return
			}
		}
	}()
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() { wg.Wait(); close(done) }()
	select {
	case <-done:
	case err := <-stepErr:
		t.Fatalf("step: %v", err)
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("lockstep deadlocked after the room")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(hostCore.stateBytes(), guestCore.stateBytes()) {
		t.Fatal("final states differ after the room test")
	}
}

func TestDesyncHealsViaSnapshot(t *testing.T) {
	host, guest, hc, gc := runPair(t, 900, 350)
	if host.Desyncs()+guest.Desyncs() == 0 {
		t.Fatal("corruption at frame 350 was never detected")
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(hc.stateBytes(), gc.stateBytes()) {
		t.Fatal("states did not reconverge after resync")
	}
	if host.Frame() != guest.Frame() {
		t.Fatalf("frame counters diverged: host %d guest %d", host.Frame(), guest.Frame())
	}
}

// A paused player must not kill the session: while the guest is
// paused far longer than the silence limit, the host waits it
// out without erroring; once the guest resumes, lockstep runs
// on in sync (a hash check at frame 300 compares clean).
func TestPauseSurvivesSilence(t *testing.T) {
	ta, tb := transportPair()
	hostCore := newFakeCore()
	guestCore := newFakeCore()
	cfg := Config{
		Game: "Super Mario World (USA).sfc", ROMHash: "deadbeef",
		CoreName: "snes9x", ReadyNow: true,
		Countdown:    100 * time.Millisecond,
		SilenceLimit: 300 * time.Millisecond,
	}
	hostCfg := cfg
	hostCfg.IsHost = true
	host := NewSession(ta, hostCore, hostCfg)
	guest := NewSession(tb, guestCore, cfg)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"peer_joined","role":"guest"}`)

	errCh := make(chan error, 2)
	go func() { errCh <- host.Start() }()
	go func() { errCh <- guest.Start() }()
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if err := <-errCh; err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
		}
	}

	const total = 400
	const pauseAt = 100
	errs := make(chan error, 2)
	go func() {
		for f := 0; f < total; f++ {
			if err := host.Step(uint16(f % 256)); err != nil {
				errs <- err
				return
			}
		}
		errs <- nil
	}()
	go func() {
		for f := 0; f < total; f++ {
			if f == pauseAt {
				guest.SetPaused(true)
				time.Sleep(1200 * time.Millisecond) // 4x the limit
				guest.SetPaused(false)
			}
			if err := guest.Step(uint16((f * 2) % 256)); err != nil {
				errs <- err
				return
			}
		}
		errs <- nil
	}()

	// The host must learn about the pause...
	deadline := time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second)
	for !host.PeerPaused() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatal("host never saw the guest pause")
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	// ...and mid-pause, with the silence limit long past, neither
	// side may have ended.
	time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
	select {
	case err := <-errs:
		t.Fatalf("a side ended during the pause: %v", err)
	default:
	}

	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
			if err := <-errs; err != nil {
				t.Errorf("step after resume: %v", err)
			}
		}
		close(done)
	}()
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(15 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("lockstep did not finish after the pause")
	}
	if host.Desyncs() != 0 || guest.Desyncs() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("desyncs after pause: host %d guest %d",
			host.Desyncs(), guest.Desyncs())
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(hostCore.stateBytes(), guestCore.stateBytes()) {
		hb, gb := hostCore.stateBytes(), guestCore.stateBytes()
		for i := range hb {
			if hb[i] != gb[i] {
				t.Logf("first diff at byte %d: host %d guest %d", i, hb[i], gb[i])
				break
			}
		}
		t.Logf("frames: host %d guest %d, core frames host %d guest %d, desyncs %d/%d",
			host.Frame(), guest.Frame(), hostCore.frames, guestCore.frames,
			host.Desyncs(), guest.Desyncs())
		t.Fatal("final states differ after pause/resume")
	}
	if host.Frame() != total || guest.Frame() != total {
		t.Fatalf("frame counters: host %d guest %d",
			host.Frame(), guest.Frame())
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/signal.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"fmt"
)

// Voice chat signaling (PROTOCOL.md section 3.1). The media
// itself is peer to peer WebRTC audio handled by the client;
// Go only relays the three signaling envelopes (offer, answer,
// ice) between the two players over the same signaling socket
// as everything else, in the waiting room and during play.
// Like chat, signaling is deliberately kept out of the
// lockstep machinery: it never touches frames, inputs,
// hashes, or the session phase.

const (
	// signalQueueCap is how many inbound signaling entries
	// the session keeps. A voice setup is one offer, one
	// answer and a burst of ICE candidates, so this is
	// generous headroom, not a working limit.
	signalQueueCap = 100
	// signalSDPMaxBytes caps an offer or answer payload.
	// Real SDP bodies are a few KB; the 256 KB socket limit
	// in PROTOCOL.md section 3 is the hard ceiling.
	signalSDPMaxBytes = 32 * 1024
	// signalICEMaxBytes caps one ICE candidate payload.
	signalICEMaxBytes = 4 * 1024
)

// SignalMessage is one inbound signaling entry from the peer.
type SignalMessage struct {
	Seq           int    // 1-based, grows by one per entry, never reused
	Kind          string // "offer", "answer", or "ice"
	SDP           string // offer/answer payload, empty for ice
	Candidate     string // ice payload, empty for offer/answer
	SDPMid        string // ice only
	SDPMLineIndex int    // ice only
}

// signalWire is the exact on the wire shape of an outbound
// signaling envelope. It is separate from envelope so an ICE
// envelope always carries sdpMLineIndex, even when it is 0:
// the shared envelope marks that field omitempty.
type signalWire struct {
	Type          string `json:"type"`
	SDP           string `json:"sdp,omitempty"`
	Candidate     string `json:"candidate,omitempty"`
	SDPMid        string `json:"sdpMid,omitempty"`
	SDPMLineIndex *int   `json:"sdpMLineIndex,omitempty"`
}

// SendSignal sends one WebRTC signaling envelope to the other
// player: kind "offer" or "answer" with an SDP payload, or
// kind "ice" with a candidate payload. Empty payloads, unknown
// kinds, and payloads over the caps are rejected and nothing
// is sent. Sent signals are not echoed into the local queue:
// the sender's client produced them and already has them.
func (s *Session) SendSignal(kind, payload string) error {
	switch kind {
	case "offer", "answer":
		if payload == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("signal %s has an empty SDP", kind)
		}
		if len(payload) > signalSDPMaxBytes {
			return fmt.Errorf("signal %s SDP is too large (%d bytes max)",
				kind, signalSDPMaxBytes)
		}
		return s.send(signalWire{Type: kind, SDP: payload})
	case "ice":
		if payload == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("signal ice has an empty candidate")
		}
		if len(payload) > signalICEMaxBytes {
			return fmt.Errorf("signal ice candidate is too large (%d bytes max)",
				signalICEMaxBytes)
		}
		zero := 0
		return s.send(signalWire{
			Type: "ice", Candidate: payload, SDPMid: "0",
			SDPMLineIndex: &zero,
		})
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("unknown signal kind %q", kind)
	}
}

// notePeerSignal records a signaling envelope from the peer.
// Called by the reader with s.mu held. Envelopes with an empty
// payload or a payload over the caps are dropped whole: a
// truncated SDP is worse than none, because the receiver
// would try to apply half a description.
func (s *Session) notePeerSignal(e envelope) {
	switch e.Type {
	case "offer", "answer":
		if e.SDP == "" || len(e.SDP) > signalSDPMaxBytes {
			return
		}
	case "ice":
		if e.Candidate == "" || len(e.Candidate) > signalICEMaxBytes {
			return
		}
	default:
		return
	}
	s.signalSeq++
	s.signalQueue = append(s.signalQueue, SignalMessage{
		Seq: s.signalSeq, Kind: e.Type, SDP: e.SDP,
		Candidate: e.Candidate, SDPMid: e.SDPMid,
		SDPMLineIndex: e.SDPMLineIndex,
	})
	if len(s.signalQueue) > signalQueueCap {
		kept := make([]SignalMessage, signalQueueCap)
		copy(kept, s.signalQueue[len(s.signalQueue)-signalQueueCap:])
		s.signalQueue = kept
	}
}

// SignalsSince returns the queued entries newer than afterSeq
// (pass 0 for everything kept) plus the seq of the newest
// entry overall, mirroring ChatSince so the UI polls both
// with the same cursor pattern.
func (s *Session) SignalsSince(afterSeq int) (msgs []SignalMessage, latest int) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	for _, m := range s.signalQueue {
		if m.Seq > afterSeq {
			msgs = append(msgs, m)
		}
	}
	return msgs, s.signalSeq
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/signal_test.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func waitSignal(t *testing.T, s *Session, afterSeq, want int) []SignalMessage {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		msgs, _ := s.SignalsSince(afterSeq)
		if len(msgs) >= want {
			return msgs
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	msgs, latest := s.SignalsSince(afterSeq)
	t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %d signals after seq %d; got %d (latest %d)",
		want, afterSeq, len(msgs), latest)
	return nil
}

// (a) SendSignal emits the exact PROTOCOL.md 3.1 wire shapes:
// an offer or answer envelope is exactly {type, sdp} and an
// ice envelope is exactly {type, candidate, sdpMid,
// sdpMLineIndex} with sdpMLineIndex present even at 0. Own
// sends never enter the inbound queue.
func TestSendSignalEmitsWireShapes(t *testing.T) {
	ta, tb := transportPair()
	sess := NewSession(ta, newFakeCore(), Config{PlayerName: "Sender"})

	readOne := func() map[string]any {
		t.Helper()
		select {
		case raw := <-tb.inbox:
			var m map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("sent bytes are not JSON: %v", err)
			}
			return m
		case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
			t.Fatal("SendSignal wrote nothing to the transport")
			return nil
		}
	}

	const sdpOffer = "v=0 o=guest 1 IN IP4 0.0.0.0"
	if err := sess.SendSignal("offer", sdpOffer); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendSignal offer: %v", err)
	}
	m := readOne()
	if len(m) != 2 || m["type"] != "offer" || m["sdp"] != sdpOffer {
		t.Errorf("offer envelope = %v, want exactly {type: offer, sdp: %q}", m, sdpOffer)
	}

	const sdpAnswer = "v=0 o=host 2 IN IP4 0.0.0.0"
	if err := sess.SendSignal("answer", sdpAnswer); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendSignal answer: %v", err)
	}
	m = readOne()
	if len(m) != 2 || m["type"] != "answer" || m["sdp"] != sdpAnswer {
		t.Errorf("answer envelope = %v, want exactly {type: answer, sdp: %q}", m, sdpAnswer)
	}

	const cand = "candidate:1 1 udp 2113937151 192.0.2.1 54400 typ host"
	if err := sess.SendSignal("ice", cand); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendSignal ice: %v", err)
	}
	m = readOne()
	if len(m) != 4 || m["type"] != "ice" || m["candidate"] != cand ||
		m["sdpMid"] != "0" {
		t.Errorf("ice envelope = %v, want {type: ice, candidate, sdpMid: 0, sdpMLineIndex: 0}", m)
	}
	if v, ok := m["sdpMLineIndex"]; !ok || v != float64(0) {
		t.Errorf("ice sdpMLineIndex = %v (present %v), want 0 present", v, ok)
	}

	if msgs, latest := sess.SignalsSince(0); latest != 0 || len(msgs) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("own sends entered the inbound queue: latest %d, %d entries",
			latest, len(msgs))
	}
}

// (b) Signaling envelopes from the peer land in the queue in
// order with their fields intact, and the cursor drains them.
func TestSignalFromPeerLandsInOrder(t *testing.T) {
	host, _, ta, _ := startChatPair(t)

	ta.inject(`{"type":"offer","sdp":"v=0 o=guest 1 IN IP4 0.0.0.0"}`)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"ice","candidate":"candidate:a","sdpMid":"0","sdpMLineIndex":0}`)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"ice","candidate":"candidate:b","sdpMid":"1","sdpMLineIndex":1}`)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"answer","sdp":"v=0 o=guest 2 IN IP4 0.0.0.0"}`)

	msgs := waitSignal(t, host, 0, 4)
	wantKinds := []string{"offer", "ice", "ice", "answer"}
	for i, m := range msgs {
		if m.Seq != i+1 {
			t.Errorf("entry %d Seq = %d, want %d", i, m.Seq, i+1)
		}
		if m.Kind != wantKinds[i] {
			t.Errorf("entry %d Kind = %q, want %q", i, m.Kind, wantKinds[i])
		}
	}
	if msgs[0].SDP != "v=0 o=guest 1 IN IP4 0.0.0.0" || msgs[0].Candidate != "" {
		t.Errorf("offer entry = %+v", msgs[0])
	}
	if msgs[1].Candidate != "candidate:a" || msgs[1].SDPMid != "0" ||
		msgs[1].SDPMLineIndex != 0 || msgs[1].SDP != "" {
		t.Errorf("first ice entry = %+v", msgs[1])
	}
	if msgs[2].Candidate != "candidate:b" || msgs[2].SDPMid != "1" ||
		msgs[2].SDPMLineIndex != 1 {
		t.Errorf("second ice entry = %+v", msgs[2])
	}
	if msgs[3].SDP != "v=0 o=guest 2 IN IP4 0.0.0.0" {
		t.Errorf("answer entry = %+v", msgs[3])
	}
	// Cursors: nothing new after the latest seq, tail works.
	if rest, _ := host.SignalsSince(4); len(rest) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("SignalsSince(latest) returned %d entries, want 0", len(rest))
	}
	if tail, _ := host.SignalsSince(2); len(tail) != 2 || tail[0].Seq != 3 {
		t.Errorf("SignalsSince(2) = %+v, want seqs 3 and 4", tail)
	}
}

// (c) Outbound payloads over the caps are rejected and never
// reach the wire; exactly at the cap is fine.
func TestSendSignalRejectsOversized(t *testing.T) {
	ta, tb := transportPair()
	sess := NewSession(ta, newFakeCore(), Config{PlayerName: "Picky"})

	bigSDP := strings.Repeat("a", signalSDPMaxBytes+1)
	bigICE := strings.Repeat("c", signalICEMaxBytes+1)
	for _, tc := range []struct{ kind, payload string }{
		{"offer", bigSDP},
		{"answer", bigSDP},
		{"ice", bigICE},
	} {
		if err := sess.SendSignal(tc.kind, tc.payload); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("SendSignal(%s, %d bytes) accepted, want error",
				tc.kind, len(tc.payload))
		}
	}
	select {
	case raw := <-tb.inbox:
		t.Errorf("rejected signal reached the wire: %.40s", raw)
	default:
	}
	if err := sess.SendSignal("offer", strings.Repeat("a", signalSDPMaxBytes)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("SendSignal offer at the cap: %v", err)
	}
	if err := sess.SendSignal("ice", strings.Repeat("c", signalICEMaxBytes)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("SendSignal ice at the cap: %v", err)
	}
}

// (f) Signaling traffic in both directions leaves every piece
// of lockstep state exactly as it was.
func TestSignalTrafficLeavesLockstepAlone(t *testing.T) {
	host, guest, ta, _ := startChatPair(t)
	before := snapLockstep(host)

	ta.inject(`{"type":"offer","sdp":"v=0 o=guest 1 IN IP4 0.0.0.0"}`)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"ice","candidate":"candidate:a","sdpMid":"0","sdpMLineIndex":0}`)
	if err := guest.SendSignal("ice", "candidate:b"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("guest SendSignal: %v", err)
	}
	if err := host.SendSignal("answer", "v=0 o=host 2 IN IP4 0.0.0.0"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("host SendSignal: %v", err)
	}

	// The host queue proves the reader ran: two injected plus
	// the guest's send. The guest queue gets the host's answer.
	waitSignal(t, host, 0, 3)
	waitSignal(t, guest, 0, 1)

	if after := snapLockstep(host); after != before {
		t.Errorf("lockstep state changed by signaling:\nbefore %+v\nafter  %+v",
			before, after)
	}
}

// (g) The queue is capped at signalQueueCap; the oldest drop
// off and seqs keep climbing.
func TestSignalQueueCapDropsOldest(t *testing.T) {
	ta, _ := transportPair()
	sess := NewSession(ta, newFakeCore(), Config{PlayerName: "Cap"})
	const total = signalQueueCap + 5
	sess.mu.Lock()
	for i := 0; i < total; i++ {
		sess.notePeerSignal(envelope{
			Type: "ice", Candidate: "candidate:n", SDPMid: "0",
		})
	}
	sess.mu.Unlock()

	msgs, latest := sess.SignalsSince(0)
	if latest != total {
		t.Errorf("latest = %d, want %d", latest, total)
	}
	if len(msgs) != signalQueueCap {
		t.Fatalf("queue holds %d entries, want cap %d", len(msgs), signalQueueCap)
	}
	if msgs[0].Seq != total-signalQueueCap+1 {
		t.Errorf("oldest kept seq = %d, want %d", msgs[0].Seq, total-signalQueueCap+1)
	}
	if msgs[len(msgs)-1].Seq != total {
		t.Errorf("newest seq = %d, want %d", msgs[len(msgs)-1].Seq, total)
	}
}

// (h) Signaling works while the session is still in the
// waiting room, and what arrived there is still queued once
// play begins. Voice starts in the room, so the pipe has to.
func TestSignalArrivesDuringWaitingRoom(t *testing.T) {
	ta, tb := transportPair()
	base := Config{
		Game: "Super Mario World (USA).sfc", ROMHash: "deadbeef",
		CoreName: "snes9x", Countdown: 100 * time.Millisecond,
	}
	hostCfg := base
	hostCfg.IsHost = true
	hostCfg.PlayerName = "Host"
	guestCfg := base
	guestCfg.PlayerName = "Guest"
	host := NewSession(ta, newFakeCore(), hostCfg)
	guest := NewSession(tb, newFakeCore(), guestCfg)
	ta.inject(`{"type":"peer_joined","role":"guest"}`)

	errCh := make(chan error, 2)
	go func() { errCh <- host.Start() }()
	go func() { errCh <- guest.Start() }()

	// Wait until both sides can see each other in the room.
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		if host.RoomPhase() == "room" && guest.RoomPhase() == "room" {
			break
		}
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	if host.RoomPhase() != "room" {
		t.Fatalf("host phase = %q, want room", host.RoomPhase())
	}

	// The guest offers before anyone readies up.
	if err := guest.SendSignal("offer", "v=0 o=guest 1 IN IP4 0.0.0.0"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("guest SendSignal in room: %v", err)
	}
	msgs := waitSignal(t, host, 0, 1)
	if msgs[0].Kind != "offer" {
		t.Errorf("room signal kind = %q, want offer", msgs[0].Kind)
	}

	// Finish the ritual; the queued offer survives into play.
	host.SetReady()
	guest.SetReady()
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if err := <-errCh; err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("start: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if msgs, _ := host.SignalsSince(0); len(msgs) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("after start the queue holds %d entries, want the room offer", len(msgs))
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/internal/netsession/step.go ====================

package netsession

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"time"
)

// reader pumps peer messages into session state until the socket
// dies or the session ends.
func (s *Session) reader() {
	for {
		raw, err := s.t.ReadMessage()
		if err != nil {
			s.mu.Lock()
			if !s.ended {
				s.ended = true
				if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
					s.endErr = errors.New("peer disconnected")
				} else {
					s.endErr = err
				}
			}
			s.mu.Unlock()
			s.signal()
			return
		}
		var e envelope
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &e); err != nil {
			continue
		}
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.lastPeerMsg = time.Now()
		if s.watch {
			// A spectator session reads the whole room; its
			// dispatch lives in watch.go.
			s.watchNoteLocked(e)
			s.mu.Unlock()
			s.signal()
			continue
		}
		// Sender filtering (PROTOCOL.md section 4.8): with
		// spectators in the room, this socket also carries
		// frames from people who are not the peer. Game
		// critical envelopes count only when they come from
		// the peer. Senders stamp "from" (see sendEnv); an
		// empty from is an older client and is always
		// accepted, and before the peer's name is known
		// nothing is filtered, so a pre-spectator session is
		// handled exactly as it always was.
		fromPeer := s.peerName == "" || e.From == "" || e.From == s.peerName
		switch e.Type {
		case "roster":
			// The server's member list (roster.go): who holds
			// the seats, who is watching. Server notices are
			// accepted from the relay as they come; the list
			// is display state for the UI and never touches
			// lockstep.
			s.noteRosterLocked(e.Members)
		case "peer_joined":
			s.peerJoined = true
			if !s.peerPresent {
				s.peerPresent = true
				s.peerPresentAt = time.Now()
			}
		case "hello":
			// A spectator's hello (role "spectator") never
			// names our peer, and once the peer is known a
			// hello from anyone else cannot rename them.
			if e.Role == "spectator" {
				break
			}
			if s.peerName == "" || e.From == "" || e.From == s.peerName {
				s.peerName = e.Player
				if !s.peerPresent {
					s.peerPresent = true
					s.peerPresentAt = time.Now()
				}
			}
		case "ready":
			if fromPeer {
				s.peerReady = true
				if !s.peerPresent {
					s.peerPresent = true
					s.peerPresentAt = time.Now()
				}
			}
		case "countdown":
			if fromPeer && e.EndsAt > 0 {
				s.countdownEnds = time.UnixMilli(e.EndsAt)
			}
		case "pause":
			if fromPeer {
				s.peerPaused = e.Paused
			}
		case "chat":
			// Recorded for the UI only. Chat must never touch
			// lockstep state (see chat.go). Anyone in the room
			// may speak; the sender stamp says who did.
			from := e.From
			if from == "" {
				from = s.peerName
			}
			s.notePeerChat(from, e.Text)
		case "offer", "answer", "ice":
			// Voice signaling, queued for the UI layer only.
			// Like chat, it must never touch lockstep state
			// (see signal.go).
			s.notePeerSignal(e)
		case "watch_sync":
			// A spectator asking for a snapshot (watch.go).
			// Not game traffic: anyone may ask, the bridge
			// decides whether to answer.
			name := e.From
			if name == "" {
				name = e.Player
			}
			if name != "" {
				s.noteWatchSyncLocked(name)
			}
		case "peer_left":
			// Whoever left the room leaves the Got Next
			// line too (gotnext.go); the name is captured
			// before the room branch clears it.
			s.noteMemberLeftLocked(s.peerName)
			if s.phase == phaseRoom {
				// Still in the waiting room: the seat simply
				// empties and both readys reset, so whoever
				// joins next starts the ritual fresh.
				s.peerPresent = false
				s.peerName = ""
				s.peerReady = false
				s.localReady = false
				s.countdownEnds = time.Time{}
			} else {
				s.peerGone = true
				s.ended = true
				s.endErr = errors.New("the other player left")
			}
		case "lobby_closed":
			s.peerGone = true
			s.ended = true
			s.endErr = errors.New("the host closed the lobby")
		case "session_offer":
			if fromPeer {
				cp := e
				s.offer = &cp
			}
		case "session_accept":
			if fromPeer {
				cp := e
				s.accept = &cp
			}
		case "session_reject":
			if fromPeer {
				s.reject = e.Reason
			}
		case "input":
			if fromPeer {
				s.remoteIn[e.Frame] = e.Buttons
			}
		case "state_hash":
			if fromPeer {
				s.remoteHash[e.Frame] = e.Hash
			}
		case "resync_request":
			// Ignore requests for desyncs already healed: their
			// snapshot frame is at or below the last completed one.
			if fromPeer && s.cfg.IsHost && e.Frame >= s.lastResyncFrame {
				s.resyncPending = true
				s.resyncReqFrame = e.Frame
			}
		case "snapshot_begin", "snapshot_chunk", "snapshot_end":
			s.noteSnapshotLocked(e)
		case "snapshot_applied":
			if fromPeer && e.Frame > s.snapApplied {
				s.snapApplied = e.Frame
			}
		case "match_end":
			// Back to the room (section 4.9): the match is
			// over but the session and the socket live on.
			// Only the peer can end our match; a spectator's
			// match_end on the shared socket is noise.
			if fromPeer {
				s.noteMatchEndLocked(e.Reason)
			}
		case "seat_assign":
			// The host referee names the next seat holders
			// (section 4.9). Recorded only from the peer,
			// which for the guest is the host itself; an
			// assignment claimed by anyone else in the room
			// (a spectator, say) is ignored.
			if fromPeer {
				s.noteSeatAssignLocked(e.Player, e.Seat)
			}
		case "spectator_left":
			// A server notice, not a peer envelope: a
			// watcher who left the room leaves the Got
			// Next line too (gotnext.go).
			s.noteMemberLeftLocked(e.Player)
		case "got_next":
			// A room member joins or leaves the winner
			// stays line (section 4.10). Only the host
			// folds these into the authoritative list;
			// the helper enforces that.
			s.noteGotNextLocked(e)
		case "got_next_queue":
			// The host referee's line order (section
			// 4.10). Believed only from the known host;
			// the helper enforces that too.
			s.noteGotNextQueueLocked(e)
		case "tournament":
			// The room's tournament name (section 8).
			// Believed only on the known host's stamp;
			// the helper enforces that.
			s.noteTournamentLocked(e)
		case "session_end":
			if fromPeer {
				s.ended = true
				s.endErr = fmt.Errorf("the other player ended the session: %s", e.Reason)
			}
		}
		s.mu.Unlock()
		s.signal()
	}
}

func (s *Session) waitFor(pred func() bool, timeout time.Duration) error {
	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
	for {
		s.mu.Lock()
		ok := pred()
		ended := s.ended
		endErr := s.endErr
		s.mu.Unlock()
		if ok {
			return nil
		}
		if ended {
			if endErr != nil {
				return endErr
			}
			return errors.New("session ended")
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			return errors.New("timed out waiting for the other player")
		}
		select {
		case <-s.notifyCh:
		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
		}
	}
}

func (s *Session) checkEnded() error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if s.ended {
		if s.endErr != nil {
			return s.endErr
		}
		return errors.New("session ended")
	}
	return nil
}

// takeSnapshot drains the assembled snapshot, returning its
// bytes, its frame, and who sent it (so the reply can be
// addressed back, section 4.4).
func (s *Session) takeSnapshot() ([]byte, int, string) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	buf := s.snapBuf
	frame := s.snapFrame
	from := s.snapFrom
	s.snapBuf = nil
	s.snapReady = false
	s.snapFrom = ""
	return buf, frame, from
}

// noteSnapshotLocked folds one snapshot envelope into the
// assembly state. Called by the reader with s.mu held. A
// transfer addressed to another room member (a nonempty "to"
// that is not us) is ignored envelope by envelope: several
// transfers can share one room (a desync resync to the guest,
// a watch answer to a spectator), and each receiver assembles
// only its own. An empty "to" is the pre-spectator behavior
// and is always assembled.
func (s *Session) noteSnapshotLocked(e envelope) {
	if e.To != "" && e.To != s.cfg.PlayerName {
		return
	}
	switch e.Type {
	case "snapshot_begin":
		s.snapBuf = nil
		s.snapWant = e.Bytes
		s.snapChunks = e.Chunks
		s.snapGot = 0
		s.snapFrame = e.Frame
		s.snapReady = false
		s.snapFrom = e.From
	case "snapshot_chunk":
		if e.Seq == s.snapGot {
			data, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(e.Data)
			if err == nil {
				s.snapBuf = append(s.snapBuf, data...)
				s.snapGot++
			}
		}
	case "snapshot_end":
		if s.snapGot == s.snapChunks && len(s.snapBuf) == s.snapWant {
			sum := sha256.Sum256(s.snapBuf)
			if hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]) == e.SHA256 {
				s.snapReady = true
			}
		}
	}
}

// sendSnapshot chunks a save state per PROTOCOL.md section
// 4.4, addressed to the peer. Guest side of the resync and
// starting-snapshot paths; SendSnapshotTo (watch.go) is the
// same delivery aimed at a spectator.
func (s *Session) sendSnapshot(frame int, state []byte) error {
	s.mu.Lock()
	to := s.peerName
	s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.deliverSnapshot(frame, state, to)
}

// deliverSnapshot sends one snapshot transfer addressed to
// the named room member (empty name: unaddressed, the
// pre-spectator behavior). The transfer is serialized on
// snapMu so two transfers never interleave their chunks.
func (s *Session) deliverSnapshot(frame int, state []byte, to string) error {
	s.snapMu.Lock()
	defer s.snapMu.Unlock()
	chunks := (len(state) + snapshotChunkBytes - 1) / snapshotChunkBytes
	if err := s.sendEnv(envelope{
		Type: "snapshot_begin", Frame: frame, Bytes: len(state),
		Chunks: chunks, To: to,
	}); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for i := 0; i < chunks; i++ {
		lo := i * snapshotChunkBytes
		hi := lo + snapshotChunkBytes
		if hi > len(state) {
			hi = len(state)
		}
		if err := s.sendEnv(envelope{
			Type: "snapshot_chunk", Seq: i, To: to,
			Data: base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(state[lo:hi]),
		}); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(state)
	return s.sendEnv(envelope{
		Type: "snapshot_end", SHA256: hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]), To: to,
	})
}

func (s *Session) mySlot() int {
	if s.cfg.IsHost {
		return 0
	}
	return 1
}

func (s *Session) peerSlot() int { return 1 - s.mySlot() }

// Step simulates exactly one frame using the sampled local buttons,
// blocking while the peer's input for the frame is in flight. It is
// called from the emulator thread; a false step with an error means
// the session is over.
func (s *Session) Step(local uint16) error {
	if err := s.checkEnded(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// Host duty: answer a resync request before simulating further.
	if s.cfg.IsHost {
		s.mu.Lock()
		pending := s.resyncPending
		s.mu.Unlock()
		if pending {
			if err := s.hostResync(); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	f := s.frame
	applyFrame := f + s.delay
	s.mu.Lock()
	s.localIn[applyFrame] = local
	s.mu.Unlock()
	if err := s.sendEnv(envelope{Type: "input", Frame: applyFrame, Buttons: local}); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// Wait for the peer's input labeled f.
	waitStart := time.Now()
	waitLogged := false
	for {
		s.mu.Lock()
		_, have := s.remoteIn[f]
		ended := s.ended
		endErr := s.endErr
		// A match_end resets the session back to the room
		// (section 4.9); a step still waiting for this frame's
		// input must notice, or it would sit here until the
		// silence limit for a frame that will never be played.
		backInRoom := s.phase == phaseRoom
		endReason := s.matchEndReason
		// Silence is measured from the last peer message, or
		// from our own resume if that is later (see lastResume).
		silentSince := s.lastPeerMsg
		if s.lastResume.After(silentSince) {
			silentSince = s.lastResume
		}
		silent := time.Since(silentSince)
		paused := s.localPaused || s.peerPaused
		s.mu.Unlock()
		if backInRoom {
			if endReason != "" {
				return fmt.Errorf("the match ended: %s", endReason)
			}
			return errors.New("the match ended")
		}
		if have {
