	fired, err := g.EnsureProtected()
	if err != nil || !fired {
		t.Fatalf("EnsureProtected fired=%v err=%v", fired, err)
	}
	if got := treeHashes(t, filepath.Join(root, BackupDirName)); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("backup of an empty tree holds %d files", len(got))
	}
	if !g.HoldActive() {
		t.Fatalf("hold not active")
	}
	g.EndHold("session end")
	if g.HoldActive() {
		t.Fatalf("hold did not end at session end")
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/mobile/backup_hold.go ====================

// Backup-and-hold surface for the app. The Kotlin activity
// calls SetFilesDir before LoadCore (the SetSystemDir pattern),
// asks BackupHoldActive for its exit messaging, routes its
// automatic saves through AutoSaveState, and reports manual
// saves through NoteManualSave. All state and all enforcement
// live in internal/switchguard; this file is only the
// gomobile-shaped doorway, plus the one behavior that belongs
// to this layer: an automatic save during the hold produces no
// bytes, so the Kotlin write that follows it cannot happen.
package mobile

import (
	"log"
	"os"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/switchguard"
)

// SetFilesDir points backup-and-hold at the app's files
// directory, the directory that contains saves/. Call before
// LoadCore. It mirrors SetSystemDir: the path is also kept in
// the environment so any layer that asks switchguard later in
// the process sees the same root.
func SetFilesDir(path string) {
	_ = os.Setenv("ITAK_FILES_DIR", path)
	switchguard.Configure(path)
	if path != "" {
		log.Printf("backup-hold: app files root set to %s", path)
	}
}

// BackupHoldActive reports whether auto-save is held for the
// first switched session. The activity uses it only for what
// it tells the player; enforcement does not depend on it,
// because AutoSaveState already returns nothing while held.
func BackupHoldActive() bool {
	return switchguard.HoldActive()
}

// NoteManualSave reports that the player saved by hand. That
// is one of the hold's two safe ends (the other is a clean
// session end, reported by Close): the live slot now holds a
// state the current core wrote on purpose.
func NoteManualSave() {
	switchguard.NoteManualSave()
}

// AutoSaveState returns the serialized state for an automatic
// save (the 60 second timer and the exit save in the
// activity), or nil while the backup-and-hold hold is active.
// The activity treats nil as "nothing to write", exactly like
// a failed SaveState today, so during the hold the auto-save
// path writes nothing into the live saves tree. Manual saves
// keep using SaveState and are never blocked.
func AutoSaveState() []byte {
	if switchguard.HoldActive() {
		log.Printf("backup-hold: auto-save skipped: hold active for the first switched session")
		return nil
	}
	return SaveState()
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/mobile/backup_hold_test.go ====================

//go:build gocores

// This file is one of the bundled Go core adapters. The
// shipped app does not carry the Go cores (David's order,
// 1.102): the Rust cores are the only cores in the app, so
// these adapters are compiled only under the gocores build
// tag, which server-side reference and cross-check runs
// use. The Go core sources themselves live in cores/ and
// are untouched.

package mobile

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/core"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/switchguard"
)

// The backup-and-hold live drill (gate 3) plus the hold's
// write gate (gate b) and preference rule (gate f), driven
// through the production mobile surface and the production
// NativeBridge, in the pilot configuration: the Rust Game Boy
// adapter behind LoadCore, a real homebrew ROM, and a real
// Go-produced save state seeded into an app-shaped saves tree.
//
// Env, house style:
//   ITAK_RUST_TEST_SO   adapter .so (default: the Game Boy
//                       adapter's release build on this host)
//   ITAK_RUST_TEST_ROM  ROM (default: tobutobugirl.gb from the
//                       homebrew folder on this host)

func drillHashes(t *testing.T, dir string) map[string]string {
	t.Helper()
	out := map[string]string{}
	err := filepath.Walk(dir, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if info.IsDir() {
			return nil
		}
		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		rel, err := filepath.Rel(dir, path)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
		out[filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return out
}

func TestBackupHoldDrill(t *testing.T) {
	home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
	so := os.Getenv("ITAK_RUST_TEST_SO")
	if so == "" {
		so = filepath.Join(home, "itak-adapter-gameboy", "target", "release", "libitak_gameboy.so")
	}
	rom := os.Getenv("ITAK_RUST_TEST_ROM")
	if rom == "" {
		rom = filepath.Join(home, "itak-dev", "homebrew", "tobutobugirl.gb")
	}
	soData, err := os.ReadFile(so)
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("adapter library not available at %s", so)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(rom); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("drill ROM not available at %s", rom)
	}
	soDir := t.TempDir()
	soPath := filepath.Join(soDir, "libitak_gameboy.so")
	if err := os.WriteFile(soPath, soData, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	// A real Go-produced state at frame 300, and the Go core's
	// own continuation state at frame 900 to compare against.
	goBridge, ok := core.LoadNative("libgo_gameboy.so")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatalf("LoadNative does not know libgo_gameboy.so")
	}
	if err := goBridge.LoadGame(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Go LoadGame: %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 300; i++ {
		goBridge.RunFrame()
	}
	goState, err := goBridge.SaveState()
	if err != nil || len(goState) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Go SaveState: %v (%d bytes)", err, len(goState))
	}
	for i := 0; i < 600; i++ {
		goBridge.RunFrame()
	}
	goState900, err := goBridge.SaveState()
	if err != nil || len(goState900) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Go SaveState at 900: %v", err)
	}
	goBridge.Close()

	// Seed an app-shaped files root: the Go state in a player
	// slot, a second player's file, and the stored auto-save
	// preference standing by as a prefs file.
	root := t.TempDir()
	savePath := filepath.Join(root, "saves", "Player 1", "tobutobugirl.sav")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(savePath), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(savePath, goState, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	otherPath := filepath.Join(root, "saves", "David", "other.sav")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(otherPath), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(otherPath, []byte("other progress"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	prefs := []byte("autosave=1\n")
	prefsPath := filepath.Join(root, "itak_prefs.xml")
	if err := os.WriteFile(prefsPath, prefs, 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	seeded := drillHashes(t, filepath.Join(root, "saves"))

	// The switched run: files root first (the SetFilesDir
	// call the staged activity makes), then the Rust core.
	SetFilesDir(root)
	defer switchguard.Reset()
	defer Close()
	if err := LoadCore(soPath); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadCore (Rust): %v", err)
	}
	if err := LoadGame(rom); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadGame (Rust): %v; the backup must have failed", err)
	}

	// The backup exists and is byte-identical to the seeded
	// tree (gate a at the drill level).
	if !BackupHoldActive() {
		t.Fatalf("hold not active after the first Rust serve")
	}
	backupDir := filepath.Join(root, switchguard.BackupDirName)
	backup := drillHashes(t, backupDir)
	if len(backup) != len(seeded) {
		t.Fatalf("backup holds %d files, seeded %d", len(backup), len(seeded))
	}
	for rel, h := range seeded {
		inner := strings.TrimPrefix(rel, "")
		if backup[inner] != h {
			t.Fatalf("backup file %s differs from the seeded save", inner)
		}
	}

	// Gate (b): during the hold the auto-save path produces
	// nothing, so the Kotlin write that follows it cannot
	// happen; the live tree is untouched. A manual SaveState
	// in the same moment returns real bytes, proving the nil
	// came from the hold and not a dead core.
	if data := AutoSaveState(); data != nil {
		t.Fatalf("AutoSaveState returned %d bytes during the hold", len(data))
	}
	if manual := SaveState(); len(manual) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("manual SaveState returned nothing during the hold")
	}
	if after := drillHashes(t, filepath.Join(root, "saves")); len(after) != len(seeded) {
		t.Fatalf("live saves changed during the hold")
	} else {
		for rel, h := range seeded {
			if after[rel] != h {
				t.Fatalf("live save %s changed during the hold", rel)
			}
		}
	}

	// The seeded Go state still loads through the Rust core,
	// and the continuation lands byte-identical to the Go
	// core's own continuation state at frame 900: the player's
	// progress survives the switch.
	if err := LoadState(goState); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("LoadState (Go state into Rust core): %v", err)
	}
	for i := 0; i < 600; i++ {
		RunFrame()
	}
	rustState900 := SaveState()
	if !bytes.Equal(rustState900, goState900) {
		t.Fatalf("Rust continuation state at 900 differs from Go's (%d vs %d bytes)",
			len(rustState900), len(goState900))
	}

	// The manual save ends the hold; auto-save produces bytes
	// again; the stored preference was never touched (gate f).
	NoteManualSave()
	if BackupHoldActive() {
		t.Fatalf("hold did not end on the manual save")
	}
	if data := AutoSaveState(); len(data) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("AutoSaveState returned nothing after the hold ended")
	}
	gotPrefs, err := os.ReadFile(prefsPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(gotPrefs, prefs) {
		t.Fatalf("stored auto-save preference changed: %q", gotPrefs)
	}

	// Session end: the backup is still exactly the seeded
	// tree. Nothing wrote to it at any point.
	Close()
	finalBackup := drillHashes(t, backupDir)
	for rel, h := range seeded {
		if finalBackup[rel] != h {
			t.Fatalf("backup file %s changed by the end of the drill", rel)
		}
	}
}


==================== FILE: go_backend/mobile/mobile.go ====================

// Package mobile is the gomobile-bound API surface for iTaK Gaming.
// The Android (Flutter) app calls these functions to run emulation.
// Only gomobile-supported types are used.
package mobile

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"os"
	"strings"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/core"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/switchguard"
)

// emuFace is the core handle the app drives. Two
// implementations satisfy it: the native bridge (bundled Go
// cores linked into this binary, the app path) and the cgo .so
// bridge (desktop harness path).
type emuFace interface {
	LoadGame(path string) error
	RunFrame()
	GetFrame() (width, height, pitch int, data []byte)
	FrameToRGBA() (width, height int, rgba []byte, err error)
	AspectRatio() float64
	FPS() float64
	SampleRate() float64
	SetButton(player, button int, pressed bool)
	ClearButtons()
	DrainAudio(maxFrames int) []int16
	SaveState() ([]byte, error)
	LoadState(data []byte) error
	CheatsSupported() bool
	DspRegs() []byte
	ApplyCheats(codes []string) int
	ClearCheats()
	Close()
}

var emu emuFace

// SetSystemDir points the bridge's system directory at a folder
// the user controls. CD cores (PlayStation, Sega CD) look there
// for the BIOS files the user supplies; the cores refuse to load
// games until the folder is at least answerable. Call before
// LoadCore.
func SetSystemDir(path string) {
	_ = os.Setenv("ITAK_SYSTEM_DIR", path)
}

// Joypad button IDs mirror core package constants.
const (
	ButtonB      = core.ButtonB
	ButtonY      = core.ButtonY
	ButtonSelect = core.ButtonSelect
	ButtonStart  = core.ButtonStart
	ButtonUp     = core.ButtonUp
	ButtonDown   = core.ButtonDown
	ButtonLeft   = core.ButtonLeft
	ButtonRight  = core.ButtonRight
	ButtonA      = core.ButtonA
	ButtonX      = core.ButtonX
	ButtonL      = core.ButtonL
	ButtonR      = core.ButtonR
)

// LoadCore selects the core for the given core path. A Rust
// adapter library (libitak_<system>.so) resolves to the Rust
// switch adapter, which drives it through the bridge ABI
// behind the same NativeBridge; anything else falls back to
// loading the libretro .so at the path. Bundled Go cores
// (libgo_<system>.so names) resolve to their native adapter
// only in gocores-tagged reference builds: the shipped app
// carries no Go cores (1.102), so in the app the LoadNative
// step below is a stub that never matches.
func LoadCore(path string) error {
	if nb, ok := core.LoadNative(path); ok {
		emu = nb
		noteLoadedCore(path)
		return nil
	}
	if rb, ok := core.LoadRust(path); ok {
		emu = rb
		noteLoadedCore(path)
		return nil
	}
	b, err := core.LoadCore(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	emu = b
	noteLoadedCore(path)
	return nil
}

// LoadGame loads a ROM file into the loaded core.
func LoadGame(path string) error {
	if emu == nil {
		return errNoCore
	}
	if err := emu.LoadGame(path); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	noteLoadedGame(path)
	return nil
}

var errNoCore = &simpleError{"no core loaded"}

type simpleError struct{ msg string }

func (e *simpleError) Error() string { return e.msg }

// RunFrame advances emulation by one frame.
func RunFrame() {
	if emu != nil {
		emu.RunFrame()
	}
}

// FrameWidth returns the native frame width in pixels.
func FrameWidth() int {
	if emu == nil {
		return 0
	}
	w, _, _, _ := emu.GetFrame()
	return w
}

// FrameHeight returns the native frame height in pixels.
func FrameHeight() int {
	if emu == nil {
		return 0
	}
	_, h, _, _ := emu.GetFrame()
	return h
}

// FrameRGBA returns the latest frame converted to RGBA bytes
// (width*height*4). Draw it scaled to AspectRatio().
func FrameRGBA() []byte {
	if emu == nil {
		return nil
	}
	_, _, rgba, err := emu.FrameToRGBA()
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	return rgba
}

// AspectRatio returns the display aspect ratio reported by the core.
func AspectRatio() float32 {
	if emu == nil {
		return 4.0 / 3.0
	}
	return float32(emu.AspectRatio())
}

// FPS returns the core target frame rate.
func FPS() float32 {
	if emu == nil {
		return 60
	}
	return float32(emu.FPS())
}

// SampleRate returns the core audio sample rate in Hz, or 0 when
// no core is loaded. It used to return a made-up 32040 with no
// core, which the app trusted and built a track from; a missing
// rate is an error the caller must surface, not a number to play
// at the wrong speed.
func SampleRate() int {
	if emu == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return int(emu.SampleRate())
}

// SetButton sets a joypad button for a player (0 or 1).
func SetButton(player, button int, pressed bool) {
	if emu != nil {
		emu.SetButton(player, button, pressed)
	}
}

// ClearButtons releases all buttons.
func ClearButtons() {
	if emu != nil {
		emu.ClearButtons()
	}
}

// DrainAudio returns pending stereo int16 audio as little-endian bytes.
func DrainAudio() []byte {
	if emu == nil {
		return nil
	}
	samples := emu.DrainAudio(4096)
	if len(samples) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]byte, len(samples)*2)
	for i, s := range samples {
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(out[i*2:], uint16(s))
	}
	return out
}

// SaveState returns the serialized emulation state.
func SaveState() []byte {
	if emu == nil {
		return nil
	}
	data, err := emu.SaveState()
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	return data
}

// LoadState restores a serialized emulation state.
func LoadState(data []byte) error {
	if emu == nil {
		return errNoCore
	}
	return emu.LoadState(data)
}

// CheatsSupported reports whether the loaded core takes cheat codes.
func CheatsSupported() bool {
	if emu == nil {
		return false
	}
	return emu.CheatsSupported()
}

// DspRegs returns the sound chip's 128-byte register file
// when the loaded core offers the debug export, else nil.
func DspRegs() []byte {
	if emu == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return emu.DspRegs()
}

// ApplyCheats replaces the core's cheat list. Codes arrive newline
// separated; multi-part codes keep their '+' joins and are expanded
// by the bridge. Returns how many entries were set on the core.
func ApplyCheats(joined string) int {
	if emu == nil {
		return 0
	}
	var codes []string
	for _, line := range strings.Split(joined, "\n") {
		if line = strings.TrimSpace(line); line != "" {
			codes = append(codes, line)
		}
	}
	return emu.ApplyCheats(codes)
}

// ClearCheats removes all cheats from the core.
func ClearCheats() {
	if emu != nil {
		emu.ClearCheats()
	}
}

// Close shuts down the core. Closing is the clean session
// end: if a backup-and-hold hold is still active, it ends
// here (the backup itself stays on disk, untouched).
func Close() {
	if emu != nil {
		emu.Close()
		emu = nil
	}
	switchguard.EndHold("session closed cleanly")
}

package mobile

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/go_backend/internal/netsession"
)

// Netplay wiring: the lockstep session from internal/netsession,
// driven over the shared emulator bridge. Kotlin starts a session
// after loading the game, then calls NetplayStep once per frame
// instead of RunFrame while it is active.

// romHashHex is the SHA-256 of the loaded ROM, computed at LoadGame
// time; both peers must present identical hashes to start.
var romHashHex string
var coreLabel string

func noteLoadedGame(path string) {
	romHashHex = ""
	if data, err := os.ReadFile(path); err == nil {
		sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
		romHashHex = hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
	}
}

func noteLoadedCore(path string) {
	base := filepath.Base(path)
	base = strings.TrimSuffix(base, ".so")
	base = strings.TrimPrefix(base, "lib")
	base = strings.TrimSuffix(base, "_libretro")
	coreLabel = base
}

// bridgeCore adapts the singleton bridge to netsession.Core.
type bridgeCore struct{}

func (bridgeCore) RunFrame() { emu.RunFrame() }

func (bridgeCore) SetButtons(player int, mask uint16) {
	for b := 0; b < 16; b++ {
		emu.SetButton(player, b, mask&(1<<uint(b)) != 0)
	}
}

func (bridgeCore) SaveState() []byte {
	data, err := emu.SaveState()
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	return data
}

func (bridgeCore) LoadState(data []byte) error { return emu.LoadState(data) }

var npSession *netsession.Session

// npPending is the session while Start() is still blocked in the
// waiting room / handshake, so the UI can poll room state.
var npPending *netsession.Session
var npErr string

// npPlayerName is the local player's display name from the most
// recent NetplayStart, used to label our own chat messages.
var npPlayerName string

func npActive() *netsession.Session {
	if npSession != nil {
		return npSession
	}
	if npPending != nil {
		return npPending
	}
	// Watching is a session too: chat (and signaling, later)
	// resolve to the watch session when no player session runs.
	return npWatch
}

// NetplayStart connects to the lobby signaling socket and runs the
// waiting room plus session handshake (PROTOCOL.md 4.0-4.1). It
// blocks until both players are ready to step frames, so call it
// from a background thread. Returns "" on success or an error.
func NetplayStart(serverBase, lobbyID, token, game string, isHost bool, playerName string) string {
	if emu == nil {
		return "no core loaded"
	}
	if npWatch != nil {
		return "a watch session is already running"
	}
	if npSession != nil || npPending != nil {
		return "a session is already running"
	}
	wsBase := strings.Replace(serverBase, "http://", "ws://", 1)
	wsBase = strings.Replace(wsBase, "https://", "wss://", 1)
	wsURL := wsBase + "/ws?lobby=" + url.QueryEscape(lobbyID) +
		"&token=" + url.QueryEscape(token)
	conn, err := netsession.DialWS(wsURL, 10*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return "cannot connect to the lobby server: " + err.Error()
	}
	npPlayerName = playerName
	sess := netsession.NewSession(conn, bridgeCore{}, netsession.Config{
		Game: game, ROMHash: romHashHex, CoreName: coreLabel,
		IsHost: isHost, PlayerName: playerName,
	})
	npPending = sess
	if err := sess.Start(); err != nil {
		_ = conn.Close()
		npPending = nil
		npErr = err.Error()
		return npErr
	}
	npPending = nil
	npErr = ""
	npSession = sess
	return ""
}

// NetplayPhase reports the waiting-room state for the UI:
// "idle", "waiting", "room", "countdown", or "playing".
func NetplayPhase() string {
	if npSession != nil {
		return "playing"
	}
	if npPending != nil {
		return npPending.RoomPhase()
	}
	return "idle"
}

	return ""
}

	}
	return false
}

	}
	return 0
}

	}
}

		npSession.SetPaused(paused)
	}

// NetplayStep simulates one frame with the local player's current
// button mask, blocking while the peer's input is in flight.
// Returns "" or the error that ended the session.
func NetplayStep(buttons int) string {
	if npSession == nil {
		return "no netplay session"
	}
	if err := npSession.Step(uint16(buttons)); err != nil {
		npErr = err.Error()
		return npErr
	}
	return ""
}

// NetplaySendChat sends a chat message to the other player
// (waiting room or in game). Returns "" on success or the error
// text. Chat is best effort and never affects the game itself.
func NetplaySendChat(text string) string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"
	}
	if err := s.SendChat(text); err != nil {
		return err.Error()
	}
	return ""
}

// chatMsgJSON and chatPollJSON are the wire shape NetplayChatJSON
// hands the UI: the messages newer than the caller's cursor plus
// the newest seq, which the UI passes back next time.
type chatMsgJSON struct {
	Seq  int    `json:"seq"`
	From string `json:"from"`
	Text string `json:"text"`
	Mine bool   `json:"mine"`
}

type chatPollJSON struct {
	Seq  int           `json:"seq"`
	Msgs []chatMsgJSON `json:"msgs"`
}

// NetplayChatJSON returns the chat messages with seq greater
// than afterSeq as JSON:
// {"seq":N,"msgs":[{"seq":..,"from":"..","text":"..","mine":bool}]}.
// With no session it returns the cursor unchanged and no messages.
func NetplayChatJSON(afterSeq int) string {
	out := chatPollJSON{Seq: afterSeq, Msgs: []chatMsgJSON{}}
	if s := npActive(); s != nil {
		msgs, latest := s.ChatSince(afterSeq)
		out.Seq = latest
		for _, m := range msgs {
			from := m.From
			if m.Mine && npPlayerName != "" {
				from = npPlayerName
			}
			out.Msgs = append(out.Msgs, chatMsgJSON{
				Seq: m.Seq, From: from, Text: m.Text, Mine: m.Mine,
			})
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return `{"seq":0,"msgs":[]}`
	}
	return string(b)
}

// NetplaySendSignal sends one voice chat signaling envelope to
// the other player (PROTOCOL.md 3.1): kind "offer" or "answer"
// with an SDP payload, or kind "ice" with a candidate payload.
// Returns "" on success or the error text. It works in the
// waiting room too, so voice can connect before the game
// starts. Signaling is best effort and never affects the game.
func NetplaySendSignal(kind, payload string) string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"
	}
	if err := s.SendSignal(kind, payload); err != nil {
		return err.Error()
	}
	return ""
}

// signalMsgJSON and signalPollJSON are the wire shape
// NetplaySignalJSON hands the UI: the signaling entries newer
// than the caller's cursor plus the newest seq, mirroring the
// chat poll shape. Empty payload fields are omitted.
type signalMsgJSON struct {
	Seq           int    `json:"seq"`
	Kind          string `json:"kind"`
	SDP           string `json:"sdp,omitempty"`
	Candidate     string `json:"candidate,omitempty"`
	SDPMid        string `json:"sdpMid,omitempty"`
	SDPMLineIndex int    `json:"sdpMLineIndex,omitempty"`
}

type signalPollJSON struct {
	Seq  int             `json:"seq"`
	Msgs []signalMsgJSON `json:"msgs"`
}

// NetplaySignalJSON returns the voice signaling entries with
// seq greater than afterSeq as JSON:
// {"seq":N,"msgs":[{"seq":..,"kind":"offer","sdp":".."}]}.
// With no session it returns the cursor unchanged and no
// messages.
func NetplaySignalJSON(afterSeq int) string {
	out := signalPollJSON{Seq: afterSeq, Msgs: []signalMsgJSON{}}
	if s := npActive(); s != nil {
		msgs, latest := s.SignalsSince(afterSeq)
		out.Seq = latest
		for _, m := range msgs {
			out.Msgs = append(out.Msgs, signalMsgJSON{
				Seq: m.Seq, Kind: m.Kind, SDP: m.SDP,
				Candidate: m.Candidate, SDPMid: m.SDPMid,
				SDPMLineIndex: m.SDPMLineIndex,
			})
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return `{"seq":0,"msgs":[]}`
	}
	return string(b)
}

// NetplayActive reports whether a session is live.
func NetplayActive() bool { return npSession != nil }

func NetplayFrame() int {
	if npSession == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return npSession.Frame()
}

// NetplayError returns the last session error, if any.
func NetplayError() string { return npErr }

// NetplayStop ends the session politely.
func NetplayStop() {
	if npPending != nil {
		npPending.End("quit")
		npPending = nil
	}
	if npSession != nil {
		npSession.End("quit")
		npSession = nil
	}
}

// Spectating (PROTOCOL.md 4.8)
// A watch session is a separate lifecycle from a player session:
// the spectator loads the same game locally, joins the room with
// a spectator token, and reconstructs the match from both
// players' input streams. One mode at a time: NetplayStart
// refuses while a watch runs and vice versa.

var npWatch *netsession.Session
var npWatchErr string

// NetplayStartWatch connects to the lobby signaling socket as a
// spectator and introduces us in the room. Unlike NetplayStart
// it does not block on the match: it returns "" as soon as we
// are in the room, and the UI polls NetplayWatchInfo and steps
// with NetplayWatchStep.
func NetplayStartWatch(serverBase, lobbyID, token, game string, playerName string) string {
	if emu == nil {
		return "no core loaded"
	}
	if npWatch != nil {
		return "a watch session is already running"
	}
	if npSession != nil || npPending != nil {
		return "a session is already running"
	}
	wsBase := strings.Replace(serverBase, "http://", "ws://", 1)
	wsBase = strings.Replace(wsBase, "https://", "wss://", 1)
	wsURL := wsBase + "/ws?lobby=" + url.QueryEscape(lobbyID) +
		"&token=" + url.QueryEscape(token)
	conn, err := netsession.DialWS(wsURL, 10*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return "cannot connect to the lobby server: " + err.Error()
	}
	npPlayerName = playerName
	sess := netsession.NewWatchSession(conn, bridgeCore{}, netsession.Config{
		Game: game, PlayerName: playerName,
	})
	if err := sess.StartWatch(); err != nil {
		_ = conn.Close()
		npWatchErr = err.Error()
		return npWatchErr
	}
	npWatch = sess
	npWatchErr = ""
	return ""
}

// watchStepJSON is the wire shape NetplayWatchStep hands the
// UI: whether a frame ran, the two players' button masks for
// it, and the frame number those masks belong to. When ok is
// false, frame is the frame the watcher is waiting on.
type watchStepJSON struct {
	OK    bool `json:"ok"`
	P1    int  `json:"p1"`
	P2    int  `json:"p2"`
	Frame int  `json:"frame"`
}

// NetplayWatchStep simulates one frame of the watched match.
// Call it from the emulator thread in place of NetplayStep
// while watching; when it reports ok:false the caller renders
// nothing new and calls again next tick.
func NetplayWatchStep() string {
	out := watchStepJSON{}
	if npWatch != nil {
		p1, p2, frame, ok := npWatch.WatchStep()
		out = watchStepJSON{
			OK: ok, P1: int(p1), P2: int(p2), Frame: frame,
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return `{"ok":false,"p1":0,"p2":0,"frame":0}`
	}
	return string(b)
}

// watchInfoJSON is the wire shape NetplayWatchInfo hands the
// UI: the watch phase plus the two seat holders' names and,
// once ended, why.
type watchInfoJSON struct {
	Phase string `json:"phase"`
	Host  string `json:"host"`
	Guest string `json:"guest"`
	Error string `json:"error"`
}

// NetplayWatchInfo reports the watch state for the UI:
// {"phase":"waiting|room|playing|ended","host":"...",
// "guest":"...","error":"..."}. With no watch running the
// phase is "idle" and error carries the last start failure.
func NetplayWatchInfo() string {
	out := watchInfoJSON{Phase: "idle", Error: npWatchErr}
	if npWatch != nil {
		phase, host, guest, errText := npWatch.WatchInfo()
		out = watchInfoJSON{
			Phase: phase, Host: host, Guest: guest, Error: errText,
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return `{"phase":"idle","host":"","guest":"","error":""}`
	}
	return string(b)
}

// NetplayStopWatch ends the watch. A spectator sends no
// session traffic on the way out, not even a goodbye
// envelope: its socket simply closes.
func NetplayStopWatch() {
	if npWatch != nil {
		npWatch.Close()
		npWatch = nil
	}
}

// NetplayPollWatchSync returns the name of a spectator who is
// waiting for a snapshot from this player session, or "".

func NetplayPollWatchSync() string {

		return s.PollWatchSync()
	}
	return ""

// NetplayAnswerWatchSync sends this session's current state

func NetplayAnswerWatchSync(name string) string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"

		return err.Error()

// Match end and seat assignment (PROTOCOL.md 4.9)
// A match can end without the session ending: both players
// fall back to the waiting room on the same connection and
// the host referee names who holds the seats next. The UI
// learns a match ended by polling NetplayPollMatchEnd; it
// drives the next match itself from there.

// NetplaySendMatchEnd ends the current match on this player
// session and returns both players to the room. Returns ""
// on success or the error text.
func NetplaySendMatchEnd(reason string) string {
	if npSession == nil {
		return "no netplay session"
	}
	if err := npSession.SendMatchEnd(reason); err != nil {
		return err.Error()
	}
	return ""
}

// NetplayPollMatchEnd returns the reason of a match end, ours
// or the peer's, exactly once, then "". A match that ended
// with no stated reason reports "match ended". A watch
// session reports the room's match end the same way, so the
// spectator UI transitions with everyone else.
func NetplayPollMatchEnd() string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return ""
	}
	reason, ok := s.PollMatchEnd()
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	if reason == "" {
		return "match ended"
	}
	return reason
}

// NetplaySendSeatAssign broadcasts the host's call for who
// fills a seat next (seat 1 or 2). Returns "" on success or
// the error text; only the host client may send it.
func NetplaySendSeatAssign(player string, seat int) string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"
	}
	if err := s.SendSeatAssign(player, seat); err != nil {
		return err.Error()
	}
	return ""
}

// seatAssignJSON is the wire shape NetplayPollSeatAssign
// hands the UI for one recorded seat call.
type seatAssignJSON struct {
	Player string `json:"player"`
	Seat   int    `json:"seat"`
}

// NetplayPollSeatAssign returns the oldest seat call this
// client has recorded as JSON {"player":"...","seat":N}, or
// "" when none is waiting. Each call is handed out once.
func NetplayPollSeatAssign() string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return ""
	}
	player, seat, ok := s.PollSeatAssign()
	if !ok {
		return ""
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(seatAssignJSON{Player: player, Seat: seat})
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	return string(b)
}

// NetplayStartNextMatch runs the waiting room and the session
// handshake again on the session a match end returned to the
// room (PROTOCOL.md 4.9), so the next match starts on the same
// connection with whoever holds the seats now. It blocks like
// NetplayStart until both players are ready to step frames,
// so call it from a background thread. While it runs, the
// session sits in the pending slot and NetplayPhase reports
// the room again. Returns "" on success or an error.
func NetplayStartNextMatch() string {
	if npSession == nil {
		return "no netplay session"
	}
	sess := npSession
	npSession = nil
	npPending = sess
	if err := sess.StartNextMatch(); err != nil {
		npPending = nil
		npErr = err.Error()
		return npErr
	}
	npPending = nil
	npErr = ""
	npSession = sess
	return ""
}

// NetplayLeaveSeat drops the player session WITHOUT the
// polite session_end envelope NetplayStop sends: the socket
// simply closes, so the room sees a peer_left and the host's
// waiting room treats the seat as emptied. Seat rotation uses
// this when the host names someone else for seat 2: the
// outgoing guest falls back to watching, and a session_end
// would end the host's session along with the guest's, room
// and all. A plain quit still goes through NetplayStop.
func NetplayLeaveSeat() {
	if npPending != nil {
		npPending.Close()
		npPending = nil
	}
	if npSession != nil {
		npSession.Close()
		npSession = nil
	}
}

// rosterJSON is the wire shape NetplayRosterJSON hands the
// UI: the room's members as the server's roster notice named
// them, or the session's synthesis (session participants
// only) before the first notice lands.
type rosterJSON struct {
	Members []netsession.RosterMember `json:"members"`
}

// NetplayRosterJSON returns the room roster as JSON:
// {"members":[{"name":"...","role":"host|guest|spectator"}]}.
// With no session of any kind it returns an empty list.
func NetplayRosterJSON() string {
	out := rosterJSON{Members: []netsession.RosterMember{}}
	if s := npActive(); s != nil {
		out.Members = s.Roster()
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return `{"members":[]}`
	}
	return string(b)
}

// Got Next (PROTOCOL.md 4.10)
// The winner-stays line: anyone in the room joins with
// NetplaySendGotNext, the host referee's session tracks the
// authoritative order, and every client reads the same list
// back through NetplayGotNextJSON. The host UI keeps the
// room in sync by broadcasting whenever NetplayGotNextDirty
// says the line moved.

// NetplaySendGotNext joins the Got Next line (join true) or
// leaves it (join false). Works for players and watchers.
// Returns "" on success or the error text.
func NetplaySendGotNext(join bool) string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"
	}
	if err := s.SendGotNext(join); err != nil {
		return err.Error()
	}
	return ""
}

// gotNextJSON is the wire shape NetplayGotNextJSON hands
// the UI: the line in order, whether the local player is in
// it, and their 1 based position (0 when not in line).
type gotNextJSON struct {
	Queue    []string `json:"queue"`
	Mine     bool     `json:"mine"`
	Position int      `json:"position"`
}

// NetplayGotNextJSON returns the Got Next line as JSON:
// {"queue":["..."],"mine":bool,"position":N}. With no
// session it returns the empty shape.
func NetplayGotNextJSON() string {
	out := gotNextJSON{Queue: []string{}}
	if s := npActive(); s != nil {
		queue := s.GotNextQueue()
		out.Queue = queue
		for i, name := range queue {
			if name == npPlayerName && npPlayerName != "" {
				out.Mine = true
				out.Position = i + 1
			}
		}
	}
	b, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return `{"queue":[],"mine":false,"position":0}`
	}
	return string(b)
}

// NetplayGotNextDirty reports whether the host's line
// changed since the last broadcast. Only meaningful on the
// host client; everywhere else it is false.
func NetplayGotNextDirty() bool {
	if s := npActive(); s != nil {
		return s.GotNextDirty()
	}
	return false
}

// NetplayBroadcastGotNextQueue sends the host's line order
// to the room. Returns "" on success or the error text;
// only the host client may broadcast.
func NetplayBroadcastGotNextQueue() string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"
	}
	if err := s.BroadcastGotNextQueue(); err != nil {
		return err.Error()
	}
	return ""
}

// NetplayNoteSeatTaken tells the session that name now
// holds a seat, so they come off the Got Next line. The
// host UI calls it right after a seat assignment goes out.
// Returns "" on success or the error text.
func NetplayNoteSeatTaken(name string) string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"
	}
	s.NoteSeatTaken(name)
	return ""
}

// Tournament naming (PROTOCOL.md section 8)
// A hosted room can run under a tournament name the host
// picked on the Online screen. The host client broadcasts
// it with NetplaySendTournamentName so the guest's room and
// every watcher learn it; everyone reads it back through
// NetplayTournamentName. The host client also reports the
// room's results to the server under this name; the name's
// trip around the room is display state only.

// NetplaySendTournamentName broadcasts the room's
// tournament name. Returns "" on success or the error
// text; only the host client may send it, and watch and
// room-less callers hear so.
func NetplaySendTournamentName(name string) string {
	s := npActive()
	if s == nil {
		return "not in a session"
	}
	if err := s.SendTournamentName(name); err != nil {
		return err.Error()
	}
	return ""
}

// NetplayTournamentName returns the room's tournament name
// as this client knows it, or "" for a casual room (or one
// whose host never named it). Safe to poll from any screen.
func NetplayTournamentName() string {
	if s := npActive(); s != nil {
		return s.TournamentName()
	}
	return ""
}

package mobile
