==================== FILE: netplay/internal/friends/friends.go ====================

// Package friends is the friends list service for iTaK Gaming.
//
// A friend edge is one-directional: player A follows player B.
// Following is how a player keeps track of people they play with,
// so the app can show those people first and say whether any of
// them are in a lobby or online with the app open right now.
// There is no consent handshake in
// this version: player names are already public on the global
// leaderboard, so following a name reveals nothing that the board
// does not already show. A follow is not mutual unless both
// players follow each other.
//
// Like the leaderboard, the list is keyed by the raw player name
// alone, exactly as reported. Names are case-sensitive and are
// stored as given (after trimming), so "David" and "david" are
// different players here just as they are on the board.
package friends

// Limits.
const (
	// MaxFriendsPerPlayer caps how many players one player may
	// follow. The cap keeps a single list (and its JSON file)
	// small enough to load and render whole.
	MaxFriendsPerPlayer = 200

	// MaxNameChars bounds a player or friend name, counted in
	// runes after trimming. It matches the leaderboard's player
	// name limit (stats.MaxPlayerChars): names come from the same
	// place, so they follow the same rule.
	MaxNameChars = 40
)

// Status values for a friend's presence, in precedence order:
// in_lobby beats online beats offline.
const (
	// StatusInLobby means the friend is the host or a guest of a
	// lobby that exists in the lobby registry right now.
	StatusInLobby = "in_lobby"
	// StatusOnline means the friend's app pinged the presence
	// endpoint within PresenceWindow (see presence.go) but the
	// friend is not in a lobby.
	StatusOnline = "online"
	// StatusOffline means the friend is not in any live lobby
	// and their app has not pinged recently: either it is closed
	// or it has never pinged since the server started.
	StatusOffline = "offline"
)

// Entry is one friend in a list response: the followed name, the
// identity the leaderboard knows for that name (empty when the
// name has never reported one), and live presence.
type Entry struct {
	Name    string `json:"name"`
	Display string `json:"display"`
	Region  string `json:"region"`
	Status  string `json:"status"`
	Game    string `json:"game,omitempty"` // set only when Status is in_lobby
}

// ListResponse is the wire shape of every friends endpoint: the
// player whose list it is, and their friends in name order.
type ListResponse struct {
	Player  string  `json:"player"`
	Friends []Entry `json:"friends"`
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/friends/http.go ====================

package friends

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strings"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/lobby"
)

// maxBodyBytes caps a friends request body. A request is two short
// names; 4 KB is far more than enough.
const maxBodyBytes = 4 << 10

// IdentitySource resolves the display identity (display name and
// region) the server knows for a player name. The stats store is
// the implementation: it answers from the most recent stat report
// that carried an identity for the name. Both strings are empty
// when the name is unknown.
type IdentitySource interface {
	Identity(player string) (display, region string)
}

// PresenceSource reports which live lobby a player is in, if any.
// The lobby registry is the implementation.
type PresenceSource interface {
	PlayerLobby(player string) (lobby.PublicLobby, bool)
}

// Handler is the HTTP front door for friends lists. It registers
// on the same mux (and therefore the same port) as the lobby and
// leaderboard services.
type Handler struct {
	store    *Store
	identity IdentitySource // may be nil: identities come back empty
	presence PresenceSource // may be nil: no one reads in_lobby
	tracker  *Presence      // app-open presence; always set by NewHandler
	log      *log.Logger
}

// NewHandler builds a Handler over a friends store, an identity
// source (for display names and regions), and a presence source
// (for who is in a lobby right now). The app-open presence
// tracker is part of the handler: it holds no state worth
// configuring, so it is created here rather than wired in main.
func NewHandler(store *Store, identity IdentitySource, presence PresenceSource, logger *log.Logger) *Handler {
	if logger == nil {
		logger = log.Default()
	}
	return &Handler{store: store, identity: identity, presence: presence, tracker: NewPresence(), log: logger}
}

// Register adds the friends routes to a mux. Method patterns make
// the mux itself answer 405 for wrong verbs on these paths.
func (h *Handler) Register(mux *http.ServeMux) {
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /friends", h.handleList)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /friends", h.handleAdd)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /friends/remove", h.handleRemove)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /friends/presence", h.handlePresence)
}

// Handlers.

// changeRequest is the wire form of an add or remove: who is
// editing their list, and which name it concerns.
type changeRequest struct {
	Player string `json:"player"`
	Friend string `json:"friend"`
}

func (h *Handler) handleList(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	player := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("player"))
	if player == "" {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "player query parameter is required")
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, h.buildList(player))
}

func (h *Handler) handleAdd(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req changeRequest
	if err := decodeBody(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	if _, err := h.store.Add(req.Player, req.Friend); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, h.buildList(clean(req.Player)))
}

func (h *Handler) handleRemove(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req changeRequest
	if err := decodeBody(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	if _, err := h.store.Remove(req.Player, req.Friend); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, h.buildList(clean(req.Player)))
}

// presenceRequest is the wire form of a presence ping: just the
// player whose app is open.
type presenceRequest struct {
	Player string `json:"player"`
}

// handlePresence records an app-open ping. It answers 204 with
// no body: the client fires these on a timer and has nothing to
// render from them, so the handler stays as cheap as a map write.
func (h *Handler) handlePresence(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req presenceRequest
	if err := decodeBody(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	if err := h.tracker.Ping(req.Player); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
}

// buildList assembles the response for one player: each followed
// name in order, enriched with the identity the leaderboard knows
// and with live presence. Presence precedence: a live lobby wins
// over app-open, which wins over offline.
func (h *Handler) buildList(player string) ListResponse {
	names := h.store.List(player)
	out := ListResponse{Player: player, Friends: make([]Entry, 0, len(names))}
	for _, name := range names {
		e := Entry{Name: name, Status: StatusOffline}
		if h.identity != nil {
			e.Display, e.Region = h.identity.Identity(name)
		}
		if h.presence != nil {
			if pub, ok := h.presence.PlayerLobby(name); ok {
				e.Status = StatusInLobby
				e.Game = pub.Game
			}
		}
		if e.Status == StatusOffline && h.tracker != nil && h.tracker.Online(name) {
			e.Status = StatusOnline
		}
		out.Friends = append(out.Friends, e)
	}
	return out
}

// JSON helpers (kept local: the other packages' copies are unexported).

func decodeBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) error {
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
	dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
	dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
	return dec.Decode(dst)
}

func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
}

func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, msg string) {
	writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": msg})
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/friends/http_test.go ====================

package friends

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/lobby"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/stats"
)

// world wires a friends handler to a real lobby registry and a
// real stats store, the same collaborators main wires together.
type world struct {
	ts      *httptest.Server
	handler *Handler
	friends *Store
	lobbies *lobby.MemoryStore
	stats   *stats.Store
}

func newWorld(t *testing.T) *world {
	t.Helper()
	w := &world{
		friends: Open("", discardLog()),
		lobbies: lobby.NewMemoryStore(),
		stats:   stats.Open("", discardLog()),
	}
	h := NewHandler(w.friends, w.stats, w.lobbies, discardLog())
	w.handler = h
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	h.Register(mux)
	w.ts = httptest.NewServer(mux)
	t.Cleanup(w.ts.Close)
	return w
}

func (w *world) getList(t *testing.T, player string) (int, ListResponse, []map[string]any) {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Get(w.ts.URL + "/friends?player=" + player)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var raw struct {
		Player  string           `json:"player"`
		Friends []map[string]any `json:"friends"`
	}
	var out ListResponse
	dec := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body)
	if err := dec.Decode(&raw); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decode raw: %v", err)
	}
	out.Player = raw.Player
	out.Friends = make([]Entry, 0, len(raw.Friends))
	for _, m := range raw.Friends {
		b, _ := json.Marshal(m)
		var e Entry
		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &e); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("decode entry: %v", err)
		}
		out.Friends = append(out.Friends, e)
	}
	return resp.StatusCode, out, raw.Friends
}

func (w *world) post(t *testing.T, path, body string) (int, ListResponse) {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Post(w.ts.URL+path, "application/json", bytes.NewBufferString(body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var out ListResponse
	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK {
		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("decode %s response: %v", path, err)
		}
	}
	return resp.StatusCode, out
}

func entryByName(list ListResponse, name string) (Entry, bool) {
	for _, e := range list.Friends {
		if e.Name == name {
			return e, true
		}
	}
	return Entry{}, false
}

// TestPresenceAndIdentity is the headline behavior: a friend who
// is in a live lobby reads in_lobby with the game name, identity
// comes from the stats store, and everyone else reads offline.
func TestPresenceAndIdentity(t *testing.T) {
	w := newWorld(t)
	const game = "Mortal Kombat (USA).md"

	// Mary hosts a lobby for the game; Terry joins as guest.
	l, _, err := w.lobbies.Create(lobby.CreateInput{
		Name: "Fight night", Game: game, HostPlayer: "Mary",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("create lobby: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := w.lobbies.Join(l.ID, "Terry", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("join lobby: %v", err)
	}

	// Mary has reported stats with an identity; Terry reported
	// without one; Ghost has never reported anything.
	w.stats.Report(stats.Report{
		DeviceID: "tv", Player: "Mary", Game: game,
		Plays: 5, Seconds: 3600, LastPlayed: 1000,
		Display: "Mary P.", Region: "MO",
	})
	w.stats.Report(stats.Report{
		DeviceID: "tv", Player: "Terry", Game: game,
		Plays: 2, Seconds: 600, LastPlayed: 900,
	})

	for _, name := range []string{"Mary", "Terry", "Ghost"} {
		if _, err := w.friends.Add("David", name); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("follow %s: %v", name, err)
		}
	}

	status, list, raw := w.getList(t, "David")
	if status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("GET status = %d, want 200", status)
	}
	if list.Player != "David" || len(list.Friends) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("list = %+v, want David with 3 friends", list)
	}

	mary, ok := entryByName(list, "Mary")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("Mary missing from list")
	}
	if mary.Status != StatusInLobby {
		t.Errorf("Mary status = %q, want in_lobby (she hosts a live lobby)", mary.Status)
	}
	if mary.Game != game {
		t.Errorf("Mary game = %q, want %q", mary.Game, game)
	}
	if mary.Display != "Mary P." || mary.Region != "MO" {
		t.Errorf("Mary identity = %q / %q, want Mary P. / MO from the stats store", mary.Display, mary.Region)
	}

	terry, ok := entryByName(list, "Terry")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("Terry missing from list")
	}
	if terry.Status != StatusInLobby || terry.Game != game {
		t.Errorf("Terry = status %q game %q, want in_lobby with %q (he is the guest)", terry.Status, terry.Game, game)
	}
	if terry.Display != "" || terry.Region != "" {
		t.Errorf("Terry identity = %q / %q, want empty (he never reported one)", terry.Display, terry.Region)
	}

	ghost, ok := entryByName(list, "Ghost")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("Ghost missing from list")
	}
	if ghost.Status != StatusOffline {
		t.Errorf("Ghost status = %q, want offline (not in any lobby)", ghost.Status)
	}
	if ghost.Display != "" || ghost.Region != "" || ghost.Game != "" {
		t.Errorf("Ghost = %+v, want empty identity and no game", ghost)
	}

	// The game key is omitted from the wire for offline friends.
	for _, m := range raw {
		if m["name"] == "Ghost" {
			if _, present := m["game"]; present {
				t.Errorf("offline entry carries a game field: %v", m)
			}
		}
		if m["name"] == "Mary" {
			if _, present := m["game"]; !present {
				t.Errorf("in-lobby entry is missing its game field: %v", m)
			}
		}
	}

	// Presence is live, not cached: once the lobby is gone, Mary
	// reads offline.
	w.lobbies.Delete(l.ID)
	_, list, _ = w.getList(t, "David")
	mary, _ = entryByName(list, "Mary")
	if mary.Status != StatusOffline || mary.Game != "" {
		t.Errorf("after lobby delete, Mary = status %q game %q, want offline", mary.Status, mary.Game)
	}
}

func TestAddAndRemoveOverHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	w := newWorld(t)

	status, list := w.post(t, "/friends", `{"player":"David","friend":"Mary"}`)
	if status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("POST /friends status = %d, want 200", status)
	}
	if len(list.Friends) != 1 || list.Friends[0].Name != "Mary" {
		t.Fatalf("list after add = %+v, want one friend Mary", list)
	}
	if list.Friends[0].Status != StatusOffline {
		t.Errorf("Mary status = %q, want offline (no lobby)", list.Friends[0].Status)
	}

	// Adding again returns the same list, no duplicate.
	status, list = w.post(t, "/friends", `{"player":"David","friend":"Mary"}`)
	if status != http.StatusOK || len(list.Friends) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("re-add: status %d list %+v, want 200 with one friend", status, list)
	}

	status, list = w.post(t, "/friends/remove", `{"player":"David","friend":"Mary"}`)
	if status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("POST /friends/remove status = %d, want 200", status)
	}
	if len(list.Friends) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("list after remove = %+v, want no friends", list)
	}
	if list.Friends == nil {
		t.Error("friends must marshal as [] after the last remove, not null")
	}
}

==================== FILE: netplay/internal/friends/presence.go ====================

package friends

import (
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// PresenceWindow is how long a player still counts as online
// after their app last pinged. Clients ping every 30 s or so
// while the app is open, so 90 s absorbs two missed pings before
// a friend flips to offline.
const PresenceWindow = 90 * time.Second

// sweepThreshold bounds the tracker's memory: once this many
// names are tracked, a ping also sweeps out the expired ones.
// Below the threshold, expiry is pruned lazily on read instead,
// so the hot paths stay proportional to one name.
const sweepThreshold = 1024

// Presence tracks which players have the app open right now.
// It is deliberately memory only: presence is a statement about
// this moment, so it is never written to disk and a server
// restart simply starts everyone at offline until their apps
// ping again. All methods are safe for concurrent use.
type Presence struct {
	mu   sync.Mutex
	seen map[string]time.Time // player name to last ping time
	now  func() time.Time     // the clock; tests replace it
}

// NewPresence returns an empty tracker reading the real clock.
func NewPresence() *Presence {
	return &Presence{seen: make(map[string]time.Time), now: time.Now}
}

// Ping records that player's app is open now. The name gets the
// package's usual hygiene (trimmed, control characters stripped)
// and must satisfy the usual rules; Ping returns the validation
// error otherwise and records nothing.
func (p *Presence) Ping(player string) error {
	player = clean(player)
	if err := validateName(player); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	now := p.now()
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	if len(p.seen) >= sweepThreshold {
		p.sweepLocked(now)
	}
	p.seen[player] = now
	return nil
}

// Online reports whether player's app pinged within
// PresenceWindow. An expired entry is deleted on the way out,
// so stale names do not pile up behind the friends people
// actually look at.
func (p *Presence) Online(player string) bool {
	player = clean(player)
	now := p.now()
	p.mu.Lock()
	defer p.mu.Unlock()
	last, ok := p.seen[player]
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	if now.Sub(last) > PresenceWindow {
		delete(p.seen, player)
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// sweepLocked deletes every expired entry. Caller holds p.mu.
func (p *Presence) sweepLocked(now time.Time) {
	for name, last := range p.seen {
		if now.Sub(last) > PresenceWindow {
			delete(p.seen, name)
		}
	}
}

package friends

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"

	"net/http"

// fakeClock is a manually advanced clock for presence tests.
type fakeClock struct{ t time.Time }

func (c *fakeClock) now() time.Time          { return c.t }
func (c *fakeClock) advance(d time.Duration) { c.t = c.t.Add(d) }

func newTestPresence() (*Presence, *fakeClock) {
	clock := &fakeClock{t: time.Unix(1_700_000_000, 0)}
	p := NewPresence()
	p.now = clock.now
	return p, clock
}

func TestPresencePingAndWindow(t *testing.T) {
	p, clock := newTestPresence()

	if p.Online("Mary") {
		t.Fatal("Mary reads online before any ping")
	}
	if err := p.Ping("Mary"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ping: %v", err)
	}
	if !p.Online("Mary") {
		t.Fatal("Mary must read online right after a ping")
	}

	clock.advance(PresenceWindow - time.Second)
	if !p.Online("Mary") {
		t.Error("Mary must still read online just inside the window")
	}

	clock.advance(2 * time.Second) // now past the window
	if p.Online("Mary") {
		t.Error("Mary must read offline once the window passes")
	}

	// The expired read pruned the entry instead of leaving it.
	p.mu.Lock()
	_, kept := p.seen["Mary"]
	p.mu.Unlock()
	if kept {
		t.Error("expired entry should be pruned on read")
	}
}

func TestPresenceRefreshExtendsWindow(t *testing.T) {
	p, clock := newTestPresence()
	if err := p.Ping("Mary"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	clock.advance(80 * time.Second)
	if err := p.Ping("Mary"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	clock.advance(80 * time.Second) // 160 s since first, 80 since refresh
	if !p.Online("Mary") {
		t.Error("a fresh ping must restart the window")
	}
}

func TestPresencePingValidation(t *testing.T) {
	p, _ := newTestPresence()

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		in   string
		err  error
	}{
		{"empty", "", ErrEmptyName},
		{"blank", "   ", ErrEmptyName},
		{"too long", strings.Repeat("a", MaxNameChars+1), ErrNameLong},
		{"too long in runes", strings.Repeat("é", MaxNameChars+1), ErrNameLong},
	} {
		if err := p.Ping(tc.in); err != tc.err {
			t.Errorf("%s: Ping error = %v, want %v", tc.name, err, tc.err)
		}
		if p.Online(tc.in) {
			t.Errorf("%s: a rejected ping must not record presence", tc.name)
		}
	}

	// Exactly at the cap is fine.
	if err := p.Ping(strings.Repeat("a", MaxNameChars)); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("name at the cap: Ping error = %v, want nil", err)
	}

	// Hygiene matches the store: padding and control characters
	// are cleaned away, so the ping lands on the bare name.
	if err := p.Ping("  Mary\x00 "); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("padded ping: %v", err)
	}
	if !p.Online("Mary") {
		t.Error("cleaned ping should record presence for Mary")
	}
	if !p.Online("  Mary ") {
		t.Error("Online should clean its argument the same way")
	}
}

func TestPresenceConcurrentUse(t *testing.T) {
	p := NewPresence() // real clock: nothing expires during the test
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for i := 0; i < 32; i++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go func(i int) {
			defer wg.Done()
			name := fmt.Sprintf("Player%d", i%8)
			for j := 0; j < 50; j++ {
				if err := p.Ping(name); err != nil {
					t.Error(err)
					return
				}
				p.Online(name)
			}
		}(i)
	}
	wg.Wait()
	for i := 0; i < 8; i++ {
		if !p.Online(fmt.Sprintf("Player%d", i)) {
			t.Errorf("Player%d should read online after concurrent pings", i)
		}
	}
}

// pingPresence posts to the presence endpoint and returns the
// HTTP status.
func (w *world) pingPresence(t *testing.T, body string) int {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Post(w.ts.URL+"/friends/presence", "application/json", bytes.NewBufferString(body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	return resp.StatusCode
}

// TestPresenceEndpointShowsOnline is the headline HTTP behavior:
// after a ping, the friend reads online in the list (not in a
// lobby, not offline), until the window runs out.
func TestPresenceEndpointShowsOnline(t *testing.T) {
	w := newWorld(t)
	for _, name := range []string{"Mary", "Ghost"} {
		if _, err := w.friends.Add("David", name); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("follow %s: %v", name, err)
		}
	}

	status := w.pingPresence(t, `{"player":"Mary"}`)
	if status != http.StatusNoContent {
		t.Fatalf("POST /friends/presence status = %d, want 204", status)
	}

	_, list, _ := w.getList(t, "David")
	mary, _ := entryByName(list, "Mary")
	if mary.Status != StatusOnline {
		t.Errorf("Mary status = %q, want online after her ping", mary.Status)
	}
	if mary.Game != "" {
		t.Errorf("Mary game = %q, want empty when merely online", mary.Game)
	}
	ghost, _ := entryByName(list, "Ghost")
	if ghost.Status != StatusOffline {
		t.Errorf("Ghost status = %q, want offline (never pinged)", ghost.Status)
	}

	// Age Mary's ping past the window: she falls back to offline
	// on the next read.
	base := time.Now()
	w.handler.tracker.now = func() time.Time { return base.Add(PresenceWindow + time.Minute) }
	_, list, _ = w.getList(t, "David")
	mary, _ = entryByName(list, "Mary")
	if mary.Status != StatusOffline {
		t.Errorf("Mary status after window = %q, want offline", mary.Status)
	}
}

	}

==================== FILE: netplay/internal/friends/store.go ====================

package friends

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// Store errors. The HTTP layer maps all of them to 400: every one
// is a problem with the request, not with the server.
var (
	ErrEmptyName = errors.New("player and friend names are required")
	ErrSelf      = errors.New("a player cannot follow themselves")
	ErrNameLong  = errors.New("name must be at most 40 characters")
	ErrTooMany   = errors.New("friend list is full (max 200)")
)

// Store keeps every follow edge in memory behind a mutex and
// persists them to a JSON file so a restart does not wipe anyone's
// list. It mirrors the stats store's shape on purpose: same open,
// save and save-loop lifecycle, same degrade-to-empty behavior on
// a corrupt file. All methods are safe for concurrent use.
type Store struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	edges map[string]map[string]struct{} // player name to its set of friend names
	path  string                         // "" means ephemeral: never touch disk
	log   *log.Logger
	dirty bool
}

// Open creates a store backed by the JSON file at path, loading
// any edges a previous run saved. A missing file is a fresh set of
// lists, not an error; a corrupt file is logged and also degrades
// to empty. Path "" keeps everything in memory.
func Open(path string, logger *log.Logger) *Store {
	if logger == nil {
		logger = log.Default()
	}
	s := &Store{
		edges: make(map[string]map[string]struct{}),
		path:  path,
		log:   logger,
	}
	s.load()
	return s
}

func (s *Store) load() {
	if s.path == "" {
		return
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(s.path)
	if err != nil {
		if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
			s.log.Printf("friends: cannot read %s (%v); starting empty", s.path, err)
		}
		return
	}
	var file diskFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &file); err != nil {
		s.log.Printf("friends: %s is corrupt (%v); starting empty", s.path, err)
		return
	}
	for player, names := range file.Follows {
		set := make(map[string]struct{}, len(names))
		for _, n := range names {
			set[n] = struct{}{}
		}
		if len(set) > 0 {
			s.edges[player] = set
		}
	}
	count := 0
	for _, set := range s.edges {
		count += len(set)
	}
	s.log.Printf("friends: loaded %d follows for %d players from %s", count, len(s.edges), s.path)
}

// diskFile is the on-disk shape of the friends file: each player's
// followed names as one sorted list.
type diskFile struct {
	Version int                 `json:"version"`
	Follows map[string][]string `json:"follows"`
}

// Save writes the current edges to the backing file atomically
// (temp file + rename, so a crash mid-save cannot truncate the
// last good file). It is a no-op for ephemeral stores.
func (s *Store) Save() error {
	if s.path == "" {
		return nil
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	file := diskFile{Version: 1, Follows: make(map[string][]string, len(s.edges))}
	for player, set := range s.edges {
		names := make([]string, 0, len(set))
		for n := range set {
			names = append(names, n)
		}
		sort.Strings(names)
		file.Follows[player] = names
	}
	s.dirty = false
	s.mu.Unlock()

	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(file, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.dirty = true
		s.mu.Unlock()
		return err
	}
	if dir := filepath.Dir(s.path); dir != "." && dir != "" {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	tmp := s.path + ".tmp"
	if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.Rename(tmp, s.path)
}

// SaveLoop persists the edges every interval, but only when a
// change marked them dirty, and once more when ctx ends (server
// shutdown). It runs until ctx is cancelled.
func (s *Store) SaveLoop(ctx context.Context, interval time.Duration) {
	ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
	defer ticker.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			if s.isDirty() {
				if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
					s.log.Printf("friends: final save failed: %v", err)
				}
			}
			return
		case <-ticker.C:
			if s.isDirty() {
				if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
					s.log.Printf("friends: save failed: %v", err)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func (s *Store) isDirty() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.dirty
}

// clean normalizes a name the same way the leaderboard normalizes
// the names it stores: control characters stripped, edges trimmed.
// Case is preserved; names are case-sensitive.
func clean(name string) string {
	stripped := strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
		if unicode.IsControl(r) {
			return -1
		}
		return r
	}, name)
	return strings.TrimSpace(stripped)
}

// validateName applies the rules every stored name must satisfy.
func validateName(name string) error {
	switch {
	case name == "":
		return ErrEmptyName
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(name) > MaxNameChars:
		return ErrNameLong
	}
	return nil
}

// Add records that player follows friend. It is idempotent:
// following someone already on the list succeeds and changes
// nothing. Both names are trimmed first; empty names, following
// yourself, and growing a list past MaxFriendsPerPlayer are
// rejected. It returns true when the list changed.
func (s *Store) Add(player, friend string) (bool, error) {
	player, friend = clean(player), clean(friend)
	if err := validateName(player); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if err := validateName(friend); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if player == friend {
		return false, ErrSelf
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	set := s.edges[player]
	if set == nil {
		set = make(map[string]struct{})
		s.edges[player] = set
	}
	if _, ok := set[friend]; ok {
		return false, nil
	}
	if len(set) >= MaxFriendsPerPlayer {
		return false, ErrTooMany
	}
	set[friend] = struct{}{}
	s.dirty = true
	return true, nil
}

// Remove drops friend from player's list. Removing someone who is
// not on the list (or a list that does not exist) succeeds and
// changes nothing. It returns true when the list changed.
func (s *Store) Remove(player, friend string) (bool, error) {
	player, friend = clean(player), clean(friend)
	if err := validateName(player); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if err := validateName(friend); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	set := s.edges[player]
	if set == nil {
		return false, nil
	}
	if _, ok := set[friend]; !ok {
		return false, nil
	}
	delete(set, friend)
	if len(set) == 0 {
		delete(s.edges, player)
	}
	s.dirty = true
	return true, nil
}

// List returns the names player follows, sorted. A player with no
// list gets an empty slice, never nil.
func (s *Store) List(player string) []string {
	player = clean(player)
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	set := s.edges[player]
	out := make([]string, 0, len(set))
	for n := range set {
		out = append(out, n)
	}
	sort.Strings(out)
	return out
}

// Count returns how many follow edges are stored, across all
// players.
func (s *Store) Count() int {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	n := 0
	for _, set := range s.edges {
		n += len(set)
	}
	return n
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/friends/store_test.go ====================

package friends

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func discardLog() *log.Logger { return log.New(io.Discard, "", 0) }

func newTestStore(t *testing.T) *Store {
	t.Helper()
	return Open("", discardLog())
}

func TestAddAndListSorted(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	for _, name := range []string{"Terry", "alice", "Mary"} {
		changed, err := s.Add("David", name)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Add(%q): %v", name, err)
		}
		if !changed {
			t.Errorf("Add(%q) should report a change", name)
		}
	}
	got := s.List("David")
	want := []string{"Mary", "Terry", "alice"} // plain byte order, case-sensitive
	if fmt.Sprint(got) != fmt.Sprint(want) {
		t.Errorf("List = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	if s.Count() != 3 {
		t.Errorf("Count = %d, want 3", s.Count())
	}
}

func TestAddIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "Mary"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	changed, err := s.Add("David", "Mary")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("re-Add: %v", err)
	}
	if changed {
		t.Error("re-Add should report no change")
	}
	if got := s.List("David"); len(got) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("List = %v, want exactly one Mary", got)
	}
}

func TestAddTrimsAndRejectsEmpty(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	if _, err := s.Add("  David  ", "  Mary "); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Add with padded names: %v", err)
	}
	if got := s.List("David"); len(got) != 1 || got[0] != "Mary" {
		t.Errorf("List = %v, want [Mary] (names stored trimmed)", got)
	}
	for _, tc := range [][2]string{
		{"", "Mary"},
		{"David", ""},
		{"   ", "Mary"},
		{"David", "  "},
		{"", ""},
	} {
		if _, err := s.Add(tc[0], tc[1]); !errors.Is(err, ErrEmptyName) {
			t.Errorf("Add(%q, %q) err = %v, want ErrEmptyName", tc[0], tc[1], err)
		}
		if _, err := s.Remove(tc[0], tc[1]); !errors.Is(err, ErrEmptyName) {
			t.Errorf("Remove(%q, %q) err = %v, want ErrEmptyName", tc[0], tc[1], err)
		}
	}
}

func TestAddRejectsSelf(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "David"); !errors.Is(err, ErrSelf) {
		t.Errorf("self follow err = %v, want ErrSelf", err)
	}
	// Trimming happens before the self check.
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "  David "); !errors.Is(err, ErrSelf) {
		t.Errorf("padded self follow err = %v, want ErrSelf", err)
	}
	// Case differs: a different player, allowed.
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "david"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("case-different follow should be allowed, got %v", err)
	}
}

func TestAddNameTooLong(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	long := make([]rune, MaxNameChars+1)
	for i := range long {
		long[i] = 'x'
	}
	if _, err := s.Add("David", string(long)); !errors.Is(err, ErrNameLong) {
		t.Errorf("long friend err = %v, want ErrNameLong", err)
	}
}

func TestAddCap(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	for i := 0; i < MaxFriendsPerPlayer; i++ {
		if _, err := s.Add("David", fmt.Sprintf("friend%03d", i)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("Add #%d: %v", i, err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "one too many"); !errors.Is(err, ErrTooMany) {
		t.Errorf("add past cap err = %v, want ErrTooMany", err)
	}
	// Re-adding an existing friend at the cap still succeeds:
	// idempotence wins over the cap because nothing grows.
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "friend000"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("re-Add at cap: %v", err)
	}
	// The cap is per player, not global.
	if _, err := s.Add("Mary", "David"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("another player adding: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestRemove(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "Mary"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "Terry"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	changed, err := s.Remove("David", "Mary")
	if err != nil || !changed {
		t.Errorf("Remove existing = (%v, %v), want (true, nil)", changed, err)
	}
	if got := s.List("David"); len(got) != 1 || got[0] != "Terry" {
		t.Errorf("List after remove = %v, want [Terry]", got)
	}

	// Removing again, and removing from a player with no list, are
	// quiet no-ops.
	if changed, err := s.Remove("David", "Mary"); err != nil || changed {
		t.Errorf("re-Remove = (%v, %v), want (false, nil)", changed, err)
	}
	if changed, err := s.Remove("Nobody", "Mary"); err != nil || changed {
		t.Errorf("Remove with no list = (%v, %v), want (false, nil)", changed, err)
	}
}

func TestPersistenceRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "friends.json")

	s := Open(path, discardLog())
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "Mary"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "Terry"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Add("Mary", "David"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Save: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("friends file missing after Save: %v", err)
	}

	reopened := Open(path, discardLog())
	if got := reopened.List("David"); fmt.Sprint(got) != "[Mary Terry]" {
		t.Errorf("reopened David list = %v, want [Mary Terry]", got)
	}
	if got := reopened.List("Mary"); fmt.Sprint(got) != "[David]" {
		t.Errorf("reopened Mary list = %v, want [David]", got)
	}
	if reopened.Count() != 3 {
		t.Errorf("reopened Count = %d, want 3", reopened.Count())
	}

	// A removal survives the same trip.
	if _, err := reopened.Remove("David", "Terry"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := reopened.Save(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	again := Open(path, discardLog())
	if got := again.List("David"); fmt.Sprint(got) != "[Mary]" {
		t.Errorf("after remove, David list = %v, want [Mary]", got)
	}
}

func TestCorruptFileDegradesToEmpty(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "friends.json")
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte("{not json"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s := Open(path, discardLog())
	if s.Count() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Count = %d, want 0 for a corrupt file", s.Count())
	}
	// And the store still works afterwards.
	if _, err := s.Add("David", "Mary"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("Add after corrupt load: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestEphemeralStoreNeverTouchesDisk(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)

		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("ephemeral Save should be a no-op, got %v", err)
	}
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/lobby/lobby.go ====================

// Package lobby is the in-memory lobby store for iTaK Gaming netplay.
//
// A lobby is a room created by a host for one game session. Other players
// join with an optional password and receive a bearer token. Tokens and
// password hashes never leave this package: the public view of a lobby
// (PublicLobby) is the only shape the HTTP layer serializes for listing.
package lobby

import "time"

// Role is a member's role inside a lobby.
type Role string

const (
	RoleHost      Role = "host"
	RoleGuest     Role = "guest"
	RoleSpectator Role = "spectator"
)

// member is one joined member. Members exist independently of WebSocket
// connections: a player joins over HTTP first, then connects to the
// signaling socket with the token they were issued.
type member struct {
	id     string // internal random id
	player string // display name chosen by the player
	role   Role
	seq    int // join order within the lobby, for stable rosters
}

// Member is the public view of one lobby member: a display name and a
// role, nothing else. The signaling layer uses it to build the room
// roster notice; it carries no ids and no tokens.
type Member struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`
	Role Role   `json:"role"`
}

// Lobby is a single netplay room. All fields are guarded by the owning
// Store's mutex; nothing outside this package touches them directly.
type Lobby struct {
	ID         string
	Name       string
	Game       string // ROM path or title, opaque to the server
	HostPlayer string
	MaxPlayers int
	CreatedAt  time.Time

	salt     []byte // nil when the lobby has no password
	passHash []byte // nil when the lobby has no password

	members  map[string]*member // member id -> player member (host, guests)
	watchers map[string]*member // member id -> spectator member
	tokens   map[string]string  // sha256(token) hex -> member id
	nextSeq  int                // next member join-order value

	peers        int       // live WebSocket connections, reported by the hub
	everHadPeers bool      // at least one peer connected at some point
	emptySince   time.Time // last time the peer count dropped to zero
}

// PublicLobby is the wire-safe view of a Lobby: no hashes, no tokens.
type PublicLobby struct {
	ID         string    `json:"id"`
	Name       string    `json:"name"`
	Game       string    `json:"game"`
	HostPlayer string    `json:"hostPlayer"`
	Players    int       `json:"players"`
	MaxPlayers int       `json:"maxPlayers"`
	Spectators int       `json:"spectators"`
	Locked     bool      `json:"locked"`
	CreatedAt  time.Time `json:"createdAt"`
}

// Public returns the wire-safe view of the lobby.
func (l *Lobby) Public() PublicLobby {
	return PublicLobby{
		ID:         l.ID,
		Name:       l.Name,
		Game:       l.Game,
		HostPlayer: l.HostPlayer,
		Players:    len(l.members),
		MaxPlayers: l.MaxPlayers,
		Spectators: len(l.watchers),
		Locked:     l.passHash != nil,
		CreatedAt:  l.CreatedAt,
	}
}

// HasPassword reports whether the lobby is password protected.
func (l *Lobby) HasPassword() bool { return l.passHash != nil }


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/lobby/password.go ====================

package lobby

import (
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"crypto/subtle"
	"encoding/hex"
)

// Passwords are never stored. A lobby keeps a random 16-byte salt and
// sha256(salt || password); verification is constant-time. Bearer tokens
// get the same treatment: only their SHA-256 digest is stored, so a
// memory dump of the store does not hand out live tokens.

const (
	saltBytes  = 16
	tokenBytes = 32 // 256-bit tokens, hex encoded on the wire
	idBytes    = 5  // lobby id entropy before encoding
)

// idAlphabet avoids look-alike characters (0/O, 1/I/L) so codes can be
// read off a TV screen and typed on another one.
const idAlphabet = "ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789"

func randomBytes(n int) ([]byte, error) {
	b := make([]byte, n)
	if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return b, nil
}

// newLobbyID returns a short human-friendly lobby code.
func newLobbyID() (string, error) {
	raw, err := randomBytes(idBytes)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	out := make([]byte, len(raw))
	for i, b := range raw {
		out[i] = idAlphabet[int(b)%len(idAlphabet)]
	}
	return string(out), nil
}

// newToken returns a fresh bearer token (hex) for a lobby member.
func newToken() (string, error) {
	raw, err := randomBytes(tokenBytes)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(raw), nil
}

// tokenDigest is the stored form of a bearer token.
func tokenDigest(token string) string {
	sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte(token))
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
}

func hashPassword(password string, salt []byte) []byte {
	h := sha256.New()
	h.Write(salt)
	h.Write([]byte(password))
	return h.Sum(nil)
}

func checkPassword(password string, salt, want []byte) bool {
	got := hashPassword(password, salt)
	return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(got, want) == 1
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/lobby/store.go ====================

package lobby

import (
	"errors"
	"sort"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Store errors. The HTTP layer maps these to status codes.
var (
	ErrNotFound       = errors.New("lobby not found")
	ErrBadPassword    = errors.New("wrong password")
	ErrFull           = errors.New("lobby is full")
	ErrNameTaken      = errors.New("player name already in lobby")
	ErrTooMany        = errors.New("too many lobbies")
	ErrSpectatorsFull = errors.New("spectator seats are full")
)

// Limits and lifetimes.
const (
	DefaultMaxLobbies = 500
	DefaultMaxPlayers = 2

	// MaxSpectators caps how many watchers one lobby holds. Spectators
	// are tracked apart from the player seats, so this never interacts
	// with MaxPlayers.
	MaxSpectators = 10

	// StaleAfterPeers: a lobby whose peers all left is reaped once it
	// has sat empty this long (the game is over; lingering is a leak).
	StaleAfterPeers = 60 * time.Second
	// EmptyLifetime: a lobby nobody ever connected to expires this
	// long after creation (host created it and walked away).
	EmptyLifetime = 10 * time.Minute
)

// CreateInput is everything needed to open a lobby. Password may be
// empty, which creates an open lobby.
type CreateInput struct {
	Name       string
	Game       string
	HostPlayer string
	Password   string
	MaxPlayers int // 0 means DefaultMaxPlayers
}

// Store is the lobby store contract. The in-memory implementation below
// is the only one for now; the interface keeps the HTTP and signaling
// layers testable and leaves room for a persistent store later.
type Store interface {
	// Create opens a lobby and returns it plus the host's bearer token.
	Create(in CreateInput) (*Lobby, string, error)
	// List returns public views of all lobbies, oldest first.
	List() []PublicLobby
	// Public returns the public view of one lobby.
	Public(id string) (PublicLobby, bool)
	// PlayerLobby returns the public view of the live lobby the
	// named player belongs to as host or guest, if any. It backs
	// presence lookups ("is this player in a game right now").
	PlayerLobby(player string) (PublicLobby, bool)
	// Join adds a player and returns their bearer token.
	Join(id, player, password string) (string, error)
	// Watch adds a spectator and returns their bearer token.
	// Spectators get their own token class (it authenticates as
	// RoleSpectator) and never occupy a player seat.
	Watch(id, player, password string) (string, error)
	// Members returns the lobby's full roster, players and
	// spectators, in join order.
	Members(id string) ([]Member, bool)
	// Authenticate resolves a bearer token to a role in a lobby.
	Authenticate(id, token string) (Role, bool)
	// LookupMember resolves a bearer token to the member it belongs
	// to (name and role). The signaling layer uses it to greet a
	// connecting socket by name.
	LookupMember(id, token string) (Member, bool)
	// RemoveMemberByToken revokes the membership a token belongs to.
	// Used when a guest's socket drops for good.
	RemoveMemberByToken(id, token string) bool
	// SetPeers records the live WebSocket connection count for a lobby,
	// reported by the signaling hub. Drives the reaper.
	SetPeers(id string, n int)
	// Delete removes a lobby immediately (e.g. the host hung up).
	Delete(id string)
	// Sweep reaps expired lobbies as of now and returns how many died.
	Sweep(now time.Time) int
	// Count is the number of live lobbies.
	Count() int
}

// MemoryStore is a goroutine-safe in-memory Store.
type MemoryStore struct {
	mu         sync.RWMutex
	lobbies    map[string]*Lobby
	maxLobbies int
	now        func() time.Time // injectable clock for tests
}

// NewMemoryStore returns an empty store with default limits.
func NewMemoryStore() *MemoryStore {
	return &MemoryStore{
		lobbies:    make(map[string]*Lobby),
		maxLobbies: DefaultMaxLobbies,
		now:        time.Now,
	}
}

func (s *MemoryStore) Create(in CreateInput) (*Lobby, string, error) {
	maxPlayers := in.MaxPlayers
	if maxPlayers <= 0 {
		maxPlayers = DefaultMaxPlayers
	}

	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()

	if len(s.lobbies) >= s.maxLobbies {
		return nil, "", ErrTooMany
	}

	// Allocate a unique short code; collisions are retried.
	var id string
	for range 10 {
		candidate, err := newLobbyID()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, "", err
		}
		if _, exists := s.lobbies[candidate]; !exists {
			id = candidate
			break
		}
	}
	if id == "" {
		return nil, "", ErrTooMany
	}

	now := s.now()
	l := &Lobby{
		ID:         id,
		Name:       in.Name,
		Game:       in.Game,
		HostPlayer: in.HostPlayer,
		MaxPlayers: maxPlayers,
		CreatedAt:  now,
		members:    make(map[string]*member),
		watchers:   make(map[string]*member),
		tokens:     make(map[string]string),
		emptySince: now,
	}

	if in.Password != "" {
		salt, err := randomBytes(saltBytes)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, "", err
		}
		l.salt = salt
		l.passHash = hashPassword(in.Password, salt)
	}

	token, err := s.addMemberLocked(l, in.HostPlayer, RoleHost)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	s.lobbies[id] = l
	return l, token, nil
}

// addMemberLocked registers a member and returns their bearer token.
// Spectators land in the watchers set, players in the members set; the
// two never mix, so player counts and the MaxPlayers cap only ever
// see player members. Callers hold s.mu.
func (s *MemoryStore) addMemberLocked(l *Lobby, player string, role Role) (string, error) {
	raw, err := randomBytes(8)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	token, err := newToken()
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	m := &member{id: hexID(raw), player: player, role: role, seq: l.nextSeq}
	l.nextSeq++
	if role == RoleSpectator {
		l.watchers[m.id] = m
	} else {
		l.members[m.id] = m
	}
	l.tokens[tokenDigest(token)] = m.id
	return token, nil
}

// memberByIDLocked finds a member by id in either set.
// Callers hold s.mu (read or write).
func memberByIDLocked(l *Lobby, id string) (*member, bool) {
	if m, ok := l.members[id]; ok {
		return m, true
	}
	m, ok := l.watchers[id]
	return m, ok
}

func hexID(b []byte) string {
	const hexdigits = "0123456789abcdef"
	out := make([]byte, len(b)*2)
	for i, v := range b {
		out[i*2] = hexdigits[v>>4]
		out[i*2+1] = hexdigits[v&0x0f]
	}
	return string(out)
}

func (s *MemoryStore) List() []PublicLobby {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	out := make([]PublicLobby, 0, len(s.lobbies))
	for _, l := range s.lobbies {
		out = append(out, l.Public())
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].CreatedAt.Before(out[j].CreatedAt) })
	return out
}

func (s *MemoryStore) Public(id string) (PublicLobby, bool) {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	l, ok := s.lobbies[id]
	if !ok {
		return PublicLobby{}, false
	}
	return l.Public(), true
}

// PlayerLobby finds the live lobby the named player belongs to.
// The host is a member too, so one pass over the members covers
// both roles; the host name check is belt and braces for a lobby
// observed mid-create. Lobbies are few (hundreds at most), so a
// scan beats keeping a second index in sync.
func (s *MemoryStore) PlayerLobby(player string) (PublicLobby, bool) {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	for _, l := range s.lobbies {
		if l.HostPlayer == player {
			return l.Public(), true
		}
		for _, m := range l.members {
			if m.player == player {
				return l.Public(), true
			}
		}
	}
	return PublicLobby{}, false
}

func (s *MemoryStore) Join(id, player, password string) (string, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()

	l, ok := s.lobbies[id]
	if !ok {
		return "", ErrNotFound
	}
	if l.passHash != nil && !checkPassword(password, l.salt, l.passHash) {
		return "", ErrBadPassword
	}
	if len(l.members) >= l.MaxPlayers {
		return "", ErrFull
	}
	for _, m := range l.members {
		if m.player == player {
			return "", ErrNameTaken
		}
	}
	return s.addMemberLocked(l, player, RoleGuest)
}

// Watch adds a spectator to a lobby and returns their bearer token.
// The password is checked exactly like a guest join. Names must be
// unique across the whole room (players and spectators alike) so the
// roster never shows two people with one name. Spectators have their
// own cap (MaxSpectators) and never touch the player seats: a full
// player lobby can still take watchers, and a full watcher bench
// never blocks a guest join.
func (s *MemoryStore) Watch(id, player, password string) (string, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()

	l, ok := s.lobbies[id]
	if !ok {
		return "", ErrNotFound
	}
	if l.passHash != nil && !checkPassword(password, l.salt, l.passHash) {
		return "", ErrBadPassword
	}
	if len(l.watchers) >= MaxSpectators {
		return "", ErrSpectatorsFull
	}
	for _, m := range l.members {
		if m.player == player {
			return "", ErrNameTaken
		}
	}
	for _, m := range l.watchers {
		if m.player == player {
			return "", ErrNameTaken
		}
	}
	return s.addMemberLocked(l, player, RoleSpectator)
}

// Members returns the lobby's full roster in join order: the host
// first, then whoever joined or started watching after.
func (s *MemoryStore) Members(id string) ([]Member, bool) {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	l, ok := s.lobbies[id]
	if !ok {
		return nil, false
	}
	all := make([]*member, 0, len(l.members)+len(l.watchers))
	for _, m := range l.members {
		all = append(all, m)
	}
	for _, m := range l.watchers {
		all = append(all, m)
	}
	sort.Slice(all, func(i, j int) bool { return all[i].seq < all[j].seq })
	out := make([]Member, 0, len(all))
	for _, m := range all {
		out = append(out, Member{Name: m.player, Role: m.role})
	}
	return out, true
}

func (s *MemoryStore) Authenticate(id, token string) (Role, bool) {
	m, ok := s.LookupMember(id, token)
	if !ok {
		return "", false
	}
	return m.Role, true
}

func (s *MemoryStore) LookupMember(id, token string) (Member, bool) {
	if token == "" {
		return Member{}, false
	}
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	l, ok := s.lobbies[id]
	if !ok {
		return Member{}, false
	}
	memberID, ok := l.tokens[tokenDigest(token)]
	if !ok {
		return Member{}, false
	}
	m, ok := memberByIDLocked(l, memberID)
	if !ok {
		return Member{}, false
	}
	return Member{Name: m.player, Role: m.role}, true
}

func (s *MemoryStore) RemoveMemberByToken(id, token string) bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	l, ok := s.lobbies[id]
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	digest := tokenDigest(token)
	memberID, ok := l.tokens[digest]
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	m, ok := memberByIDLocked(l, memberID)
	if !ok {
		return false
	}
	delete(l.tokens, digest)
	if m.role == RoleSpectator {
		delete(l.watchers, memberID)
	} else {
		delete(l.members, memberID)
	}
	return true
}

func (s *MemoryStore) SetPeers(id string, n int) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	l, ok := s.lobbies[id]
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	prev := l.peers
	l.peers = n
	if n > 0 {
		l.everHadPeers = true
	} else if prev > 0 {
		l.emptySince = s.now()
	}
}

func (s *MemoryStore) Delete(id string) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	delete(s.lobbies, id)
}

func (s *MemoryStore) Count() int {
	s.mu.RLock()
	defer s.mu.RUnlock()
	return len(s.lobbies)
}

// Sweep deletes:
//   - lobbies that had peers, then sat empty for StaleAfterPeers
//   - lobbies nobody ever connected to once EmptyLifetime has passed
//
// Lobbies with live peers are never swept.
func (s *MemoryStore) Sweep(now time.Time) int {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	reaped := 0
	for id, l := range s.lobbies {
		if l.peers > 0 {
			continue
		}
		switch {
		case l.everHadPeers && now.Sub(l.emptySince) > StaleAfterPeers:
			delete(s.lobbies, id)
			reaped++
		case !l.everHadPeers && now.Sub(l.CreatedAt) > EmptyLifetime:
			delete(s.lobbies, id)
			reaped++
		}
	}
	return reaped
}

package lobby

import (
	"encoding/json"

// testStore returns a store pinned to a controllable clock.
func testStore(start time.Time) (*MemoryStore, *time.Time) {
	cur := new(time.Time)
	*cur = start
	s := NewMemoryStore()
	s.now = func() time.Time { return *cur }
	return s, cur
}

var t0 = time.Date(2026, 10, 11, 22, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

func TestCreateAndList(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := testStore(t0)

	l, hostToken, err := s.Create(CreateInput{
		Name:       "Mario Kart night",
		Game:       "Super Mario Kart (USA).sfc",
		HostPlayer: "David",
		Password:   "secret",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("create: %v", err)
	}
	if l.ID == "" || hostToken == "" {
		t.Fatal("create returned empty id or token")
	}
	if got := s.Count(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("count = %d, want 1", got)
	}

	list := s.List()
	if len(list) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("list len = %d, want 1", len(list))
	}
	pub := list[0]
	if pub.ID != l.ID || pub.Name != "Mario Kart night" || pub.HostPlayer != "David" {
		t.Errorf("public view wrong: %+v", pub)
	}
	if !pub.Locked {
		t.Error("password lobby should report locked")
	}
	if pub.Players != 1 || pub.MaxPlayers != DefaultMaxPlayers {
		t.Errorf("players/max = %d/%d, want 1/%d", pub.Players, pub.MaxPlayers, DefaultMaxPlayers)
	}

	// The public JSON must never carry secret material.
	raw, err := json.Marshal(pub)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, leak := range []string{"hash", "salt", "token", "secret"} {
		if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(string(raw)), leak) {
			t.Errorf("public JSON leaks %q: %s", leak, raw)
		}
	}

	// The host token authenticates as host; garbage does not.
	if role, ok := s.Authenticate(l.ID, hostToken); !ok || role != RoleHost {
		t.Errorf("host auth = %v/%v, want host/true", role, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := s.Authenticate(l.ID, "deadbeef"); ok {
		t.Error("bogus token authenticated")
	}
	if _, ok := s.Authenticate("ZZZZZ", hostToken); ok {
		t.Error("token authenticated against the wrong lobby")
	}
}

func TestPlayerLobby(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := testStore(t0)

		Name:       "Fight night",
		Game:       "Mortal Kombat (USA).md",

	for _, name := range []string{"Mary", "Terry"} {

			t.Errorf("PlayerLobby(%q) not found, want the live lobby", name)
			continue
		}

		t.Error("PlayerLobby(Ghost) found a lobby, want none")
	}
	if _, ok := s.PlayerLobby(""); ok {
		t.Error("PlayerLobby(empty) found a lobby, want none")
	}

	// Once the lobby is deleted, its members no longer resolve.
	s.Delete(l.ID)
	if _, ok := s.PlayerLobby("Mary"); ok {
		t.Error("PlayerLobby(Mary) after delete found a lobby, want none")
	}
}

func TestWatchPasswordAndTokenClass(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := testStore(t0)
	l, hostToken, err := s.Create(CreateInput{Name: "L", Game: "G", HostPlayer: "David", Password: "hunter2"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	if _, err := s.Watch(l.ID, "Fan", "wrong"); !errors.Is(err, ErrBadPassword) {
		t.Errorf("watch wrong password err = %v, want ErrBadPassword", err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Watch(l.ID, "Fan", ""); !errors.Is(err, ErrBadPassword) {
		t.Errorf("watch empty password err = %v, want ErrBadPassword", err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Watch("ZZZZZ", "Fan", "hunter2"); !errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) {
		t.Errorf("watch missing lobby err = %v, want ErrNotFound", err)
	}

	specToken, err := s.Watch(l.ID, "Fan", "hunter2")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("watch with correct password: %v", err)
	}
	if specToken == "" || specToken == hostToken {
		t.Error("spectator token must be its own token")
	}
	// The spectator token authenticates as its own class, apart from
	// the guest token a Join would have issued.
	if role, ok := s.Authenticate(l.ID, specToken); !ok || role != RoleSpectator {
		t.Errorf("spectator auth = %v/%v, want spectator/true", role, ok)
	}
	if m, ok := s.LookupMember(l.ID, specToken); !ok || m.Name != "Fan" || m.Role != RoleSpectator {
		t.Errorf("spectator lookup = %+v/%v, want Fan/spectator/true", m, ok)
	}

	// Watching never fills a player seat: players still counts the
	// host alone, and the listing gains the spectator count.
	if pub, _ := s.Public(l.ID); pub.Players != 1 || pub.Spectators != 1 {
		t.Errorf("players/spectators = %d/%d, want 1/1", pub.Players, pub.Spectators)
	}

	// A spectator is not "in a lobby" for presence: only seats count.
	if _, ok := s.PlayerLobby("Fan"); ok {
		t.Error("PlayerLobby(Fan) found a lobby for a spectator, want none")
	}

	// The guest seat is still open after watching started.
	guestToken, err := s.Join(l.ID, "Brother", "hunter2")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("guest join after watch: %v", err)
	}
	if guestToken == specToken {
		t.Error("guest token equals spectator token")
	}
	if role, ok := s.Authenticate(l.ID, guestToken); !ok || role != RoleGuest {
		t.Errorf("guest auth = %v/%v, want guest/true", role, ok)
	}
	if pub, _ := s.Public(l.ID); pub.Players != 2 || pub.Spectators != 1 {
		t.Errorf("players/spectators = %d/%d, want 2/1", pub.Players, pub.Spectators)
	}
}

==================== FILE: netplay/internal/matches/http.go ====================

package matches

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"log"
	"net/http"
)

// maxBodyBytes caps a matches request body. A report is a handful
// of short strings; 16 KB is far more than enough (the same cap
// the stats report uses).
const maxBodyBytes = 16 << 10

// IdentitySource resolves the display identity (display name and
// region) the server knows for a player name. The stats store is
// the implementation: it answers from the most recent stat report
// that carried an identity for the name. Both strings are empty
// when the name is unknown.
type IdentitySource interface {
	Identity(player string) (display, region string)
}

// Handler is the HTTP front door for tournament results. It
// registers on the same mux (and therefore the same port) as the
// lobby, leaderboard, and friends services.
type Handler struct {
	store    *Store
	identity IdentitySource // may be nil: identities come from reports only
	log      *log.Logger
}

// NewHandler builds a Handler over a matches store and an
// identity source (used to fill board identities for players
// whose match reports never carried one).
func NewHandler(store *Store, identity IdentitySource, logger *log.Logger) *Handler {
	if logger == nil {
		logger = log.Default()
	}
	return &Handler{store: store, identity: identity, log: logger}
}

// Register adds the matches routes to a mux. Method patterns
// make the mux itself answer 405 for wrong verbs on these paths.
func (h *Handler) Register(mux *http.ServeMux) {
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /matches/report", h.handleReport)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /matches/champion", h.handleChampion)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /matches/leaderboard", h.handleLeaderboard)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /matches/recent", h.handleRecent)
}

// Handlers.

// reportRequest is the wire form of a match report.
type reportRequest struct {
	Tournament    string `json:"tournament"`
	Game          string `json:"game"`
	Winner        string `json:"winner"`
	Loser         string `json:"loser"`
	Host          string `json:"host"`
	WinnerDisplay string `json:"winnerDisplay"`
	WinnerRegion  string `json:"winnerRegion"`
	LoserDisplay  string `json:"loserDisplay"`
	LoserRegion   string `json:"loserRegion"`
}

// handleReport records one finished match. Success is 204 with
// no body, like the stats report: the host's client fires it at
// match end and reads nothing back; it refreshes the board on
// its own schedule.
func (h *Handler) handleReport(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req reportRequest
	if err := decodeBody(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	_, err := h.store.ReportMatch(MatchReport{
		Tournament:    req.Tournament,
		Game:          req.Game,
		Winner:        req.Winner,
		Loser:         req.Loser,
		Host:          req.Host,
		WinnerDisplay: req.WinnerDisplay,
		WinnerRegion:  req.WinnerRegion,
		LoserDisplay:  req.LoserDisplay,
		LoserRegion:   req.LoserRegion,
	})
	if err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
}

// championRequest is the wire form of a champion report. The
// identity extras are optional, as on a match report.
type championRequest struct {
	Tournament      string `json:"tournament"`
	Champion        string `json:"champion"`
	Host            string `json:"host"`
	ChampionDisplay string `json:"championDisplay"`
	ChampionRegion  string `json:"championRegion"`
}

func (h *Handler) handleChampion(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req championRequest
	if err := decodeBody(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	err := h.store.ReportChampion(req.Tournament, req.Champion, req.Host,
		req.ChampionDisplay, req.ChampionRegion)
	if err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
}

// handleLeaderboard serves the tournament board. A row's
// identity comes from the player's match reports; when no report
// ever carried one, the identity source (the playtime
// leaderboard) fills it, so a known player is never anonymous
// here just because their host's client sent no identity.
func (h *Handler) handleLeaderboard(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	players := h.store.Leaderboard(LeaderboardSize)
	for i := range players {
		if players[i].Display == "" && h.identity != nil {
			players[i].Display, players[i].Region = h.identity.Identity(players[i].Name)
		}
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, LeaderboardResponse{Players: players})
}

func (h *Handler) handleRecent(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, RecentResponse{Recent: h.store.Recent(RecentSize)})
}

// JSON helpers (kept local: the other packages' copies are unexported).

func decodeBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) error {
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
	dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
	dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
	return dec.Decode(dst)
}

func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
}

func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, msg string) {
	writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": msg})
}

// world wires a matches handler to a real stats store as its
// identity source, the same collaborator main wires in.
type world struct {
	ts      *httptest.Server
	handler *Handler
	matches *Store
	stats   *stats.Store
}

func newWorld(t *testing.T) *world {
	t.Helper()
	w := &world{
		matches: Open("", discardLog()),
		stats:   stats.Open("", discardLog()),
	}
	h := NewHandler(w.matches, w.stats, discardLog())
	w.handler = h
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	h.Register(mux)
	w.ts = httptest.NewServer(mux)
	t.Cleanup(w.ts.Close)
	return w
}

func (w *world) post(t *testing.T, path, body string) int {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Post(w.ts.URL+path, "application/json", bytes.NewBufferString(body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, resp.Body)
	return resp.StatusCode
}

func (w *world) get(t *testing.T, path string) (int, []byte) {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Get(w.ts.URL + path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return resp.StatusCode, body
}

	t.Helper()

	if code != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("GET /matches/leaderboard = %d, want 200 (%s)", code, body)
	}

	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &out); err != nil {

		t.Fatalf("decode recent: %v", err)

func boardRow(board LeaderboardResponse, name string) (PlayerRecord, bool) {
	for _, rec := range board.Players {
		if rec.Name == name {
			return rec, true
		}
	}
	return PlayerRecord{}, false
}

func TestReportAndBoardOverHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	w := newWorld(t)
	code := w.post(t, "/matches/report",
		`{"tournament":"Friday Night Fights","game":"Mortal Kombat (USA).md",`+
			`"winner":"David","loser":"Brother","host":"David"}`)
	if code != http.StatusNoContent {
		t.Fatalf("POST /matches/report = %d, want 204", code)
	}

	board := w.leaderboard(t)
	if len(board.Players) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("board = %+v, want 2 players", board.Players)
	}
	// Equal titles and matches: the win puts David first.
	if board.Players[0].Name != "David" || board.Players[1].Name != "Brother" {
		t.Errorf("board order = %q, %q; want David, Brother",
			board.Players[0].Name, board.Players[1].Name)
	}
	david, _ := boardRow(board, "David")
	if david.Wins != 1 || david.Matches != 1 || david.Losses != 0 ||
		david.LastTournament != "Friday Night Fights" || david.LastGame != "Mortal Kombat (USA).md" {
		t.Errorf("David row = %+v, want 1 win in Friday Night Fights", david)
	}

	recent := w.recent(t)
	if len(recent.Recent) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("recent = %+v, want 1 match", recent.Recent)
	}
	got := recent.Recent[0]
	if got.Tournament != "Friday Night Fights" || got.Game != "Mortal Kombat (USA).md" ||
		got.Winner != "David" || got.Loser != "Brother" || got.At == 0 {
		t.Errorf("recent[0] = %+v, want the reported match with a timestamp", got)
	}

	// A champion report moves Brother to the top of the board:
	// titles outrank wins.
	code = w.post(t, "/matches/champion",
		`{"tournament":"Friday Night Fights","champion":"Brother","host":"David"}`)
	if code != http.StatusNoContent {
		t.Fatalf("POST /matches/champion = %d, want 204", code)
	}
	board = w.leaderboard(t)
	if board.Players[0].Name != "Brother" || board.Players[0].TournamentsWon != 1 {
		t.Errorf("board head = %+v, want Brother with 1 title", board.Players[0])
	}
	// The champion report is not a match: the feed still holds 1.
	if recent := w.recent(t); len(recent.Recent) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("recent after champion = %d rows, want 1", len(recent.Recent))
	}
}

func TestIdentityFromReportAndStatsFallback(t *testing.T) {
	w := newWorld(t)
	// Mary has an identity on the playtime board but her match
	// report carries none: the board falls back to it.
	w.stats.Report(stats.Report{
		DeviceID: "box-1", Player: "Mary", Game: "Tetris (USA).gb",
		Plays: 3, Seconds: 900, LastPlayed: 1000,
		Display: "Mary P.", Region: "MO",
	})
	code := w.post(t, "/matches/report",
		`{"tournament":"Cup","game":"Mortal Kombat (USA).md","winner":"David","loser":"Mary","host":"David",`+
			`"winnerDisplay":"David P.","winnerRegion":"KY"}`)
	if code != http.StatusNoContent {
		t.Fatalf("report = %d, want 204", code)
	}
	board := w.leaderboard(t)
	david, _ := boardRow(board, "David")
	if david.Display != "David P." || david.Region != "KY" {
		t.Errorf("David identity = %q/%q, want from the match report", david.Display, david.Region)
	}
	mary, _ := boardRow(board, "Mary")
	if mary.Display != "Mary P." || mary.Region != "MO" {
		t.Errorf("Mary identity = %q/%q, want the stats fallback", mary.Display, mary.Region)
	}

	// A record's own identity beats the fallback: a later report
	// carrying one for Mary replaces what the board shows.
	w.stats.Report(stats.Report{
		DeviceID: "box-1", Player: "David", Game: "Tetris (USA).gb",
		Plays: 1, Seconds: 60, LastPlayed: 1000,
		Display: "David From Stats", Region: "ZZ",
	})
	code = w.post(t, "/matches/report",
		`{"tournament":"Cup","game":"Mortal Kombat (USA).md","winner":"Mary","loser":"David","host":"David"}`)
	if code != http.StatusNoContent {
		t.Fatalf("report = %d, want 204", code)
	}
	board = w.leaderboard(t)
	david, _ = boardRow(board, "David")
	if david.Display != "David P." || david.Region != "KY" {
		t.Errorf("David identity = %q/%q, want the match report's to win over the fallback",
			david.Display, david.Region)
	}
}

func TestHTTPValidation(t *testing.T) {
	w := newWorld(t)
	bad := []struct {
		name, path, body string
	}{
		{"malformed JSON", "/matches/report", `{"winner":`},
		{"unknown field", "/matches/report",
			`{"tournament":"Cup","game":"G","winner":"David","loser":"Brother","host":"David","ranked":true}`},
		{"empty tournament", "/matches/report",
			`{"tournament":"","game":"G","winner":"David","loser":"Brother","host":"David"}`},
		{"empty winner", "/matches/report",
			`{"tournament":"Cup","game":"G","winner":"","loser":"Brother","host":"David"}`},
		{"empty loser", "/matches/report",
			`{"tournament":"Cup","game":"G","winner":"David","loser":"","host":"David"}`},
		{"empty host", "/matches/report",
			`{"tournament":"Cup","game":"G","winner":"David","loser":"Brother","host":""}`},
		{"self match", "/matches/report",
			`{"tournament":"Cup","game":"G","winner":"David","loser":"David","host":"David"}`},
		{"empty champion", "/matches/champion",
			`{"tournament":"Cup","champion":"","host":"David"}`},
		{"empty champion tournament", "/matches/champion",
			`{"tournament":"","champion":"David","host":"David"}`},
		{"empty champion host", "/matches/champion",
			`{"tournament":"Cup","champion":"David","host":""}`},
	}
	for _, tc := range bad {
		if code := w.post(t, tc.path, tc.body); code != http.StatusBadRequest {
			t.Errorf("%s: POST %s = %d, want 400", tc.name, tc.path, code)
		}
	}
	if w.matches.PlayerCount() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("PlayerCount = %d, want 0: rejected reports record nothing", w.matches.PlayerCount())
	}

	// Wrong verbs are the mux's job: 405.
	resp, err := http.Get(w.ts.URL + "/matches/report")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusMethodNotAllowed {
		t.Errorf("GET /matches/report = %d, want 405", resp.StatusCode)
	}
}
