==================== FILE: netplay/internal/matches/matches.go ====================

// Package matches is the tournament results service for iTaK
// Gaming: a win/loss board for host-run tournaments, kept
// completely separate from the playtime leaderboard (package
// stats). Nothing here counts seconds or plays; a row exists
// because a match was reported, not because time passed.
//
// The reporting model is the honor system, stated plainly in the
// design doc: when a tournament match ends, the HOST's client
// reports the result (POST /matches/report), and when a
// tournament finishes, the host reports its champion
// (POST /matches/champion). The server trusts the report; there
// is no referee on the server in this version.
//
// Player identity is the raw player name, exactly as on the
// other boards: case-sensitive, trimmed, control characters
// stripped. A record may carry a display name and region (the
// identity extras the stats reports introduced); the newest
// report that carries one wins, and reads fall back to the
// leaderboard's identity for names that have none here.
package matches

// Limits.
const (
	// MaxNameChars bounds a player name (winner, loser, champion,
	// host), counted in runes after cleaning. It matches the
	// leaderboard's player name limit (stats.MaxPlayerChars):
	// names come from the same place, so they follow the same
	// rule.
	MaxNameChars = 40
	// MaxTournamentChars bounds a tournament name.
	MaxTournamentChars = 80
	// MaxGameChars bounds a game title. It matches the
	// leaderboard's game limit (stats.MaxGameChars).
	MaxGameChars = 120
	// MaxDisplayChars and MaxRegionChars bound the optional
	// identity strings a report may carry, as in stats.
	MaxDisplayChars = 60
	MaxRegionChars  = 40

	// LeaderboardSize is how many rows the tournament board
	// returns at most.
	LeaderboardSize = 100
	// RecentSize is how many matches the recent feed returns.
	RecentSize = 20
	// MaxRecentStored caps how many reported matches the store
	// keeps (and persists) for the recent feed.
	MaxRecentStored = 50
)

// MatchReport is one finished tournament match, as reported by
// the host's client. Display and region fields are optional
// identity extras for the two players, in the same spirit as the
// stats report: when present and non-empty they become the
// identity attached to that player's record until a newer report
// replaces them.
type MatchReport struct {
	Tournament    string
	Game          string
	Winner        string
	Loser         string
	Host          string
	WinnerDisplay string
	WinnerRegion  string
	LoserDisplay  string
	LoserRegion   string
}

// MatchEntry is one reported match in the recent feed: who beat
// whom, in which tournament and game, and when the server
// recorded it (unix milliseconds).
type MatchEntry struct {
	Tournament string `json:"tournament"`
	Game       string `json:"game"`
	Winner     string `json:"winner"`
	Loser      string `json:"loser"`
	At         int64  `json:"at"`
}

// PlayerRecord is one player's tournament standing: the row the
// leaderboard serves and the unit the store persists.
type PlayerRecord struct {
	Name           string `json:"name"`
	Display        string `json:"display"`
	Region         string `json:"region"`
	Wins           int    `json:"wins"`
	Losses         int    `json:"losses"`
	Matches        int    `json:"matches"`
	TournamentsWon int    `json:"tournamentsWon"`
	// LastTournament and LastGame name the event of the player's
	// most recent reported match (or, for LastTournament, of a
	// championship reported after it).
	LastTournament string `json:"lastTournament"`
	LastGame       string `json:"lastGame"`
	// LastTitle is the tournament this player most recently won
	// outright, empty until a champion report names them.
	LastTitle string `json:"lastTitle,omitempty"`
	// LastPlayed is when the player's latest tournament activity
	// was recorded (unix milliseconds).
	LastPlayed int64 `json:"lastPlayed"`
}

// LeaderboardResponse is the wire shape of GET
// /matches/leaderboard.
type LeaderboardResponse struct {
	Players []PlayerRecord `json:"players"`
}

// RecentResponse is the wire shape of GET /matches/recent.
type RecentResponse struct {
	Recent []MatchEntry `json:"recent"`
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/matches/store.go ====================

package matches

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// Store errors. The HTTP layer maps all of them to 400: every one
// is a problem with the report, not with the server.
var (
	ErrEmptyTournament = errors.New("tournament is required")
	ErrEmptyWinner     = errors.New("winner is required")
	ErrEmptyLoser      = errors.New("loser is required")
	ErrEmptyChampion   = errors.New("champion is required")
	ErrEmptyHost       = errors.New("host is required")
	ErrSelfMatch       = errors.New("winner and loser must be different players")
	ErrNameLong        = errors.New("name must be at most 40 characters")
	ErrTournamentLong  = errors.New("tournament must be at most 80 characters")
	ErrGameLong        = errors.New("game must be at most 120 characters")
	ErrDisplayLong     = errors.New("display must be at most 60 characters")
	ErrRegionLong      = errors.New("region must be at most 40 characters")
)

// Store keeps every player's tournament record and the recent
// match feed in memory behind a mutex, and persists them to a
// JSON file so a restart does not wipe the board. It mirrors the
// stats and friends stores' shape on purpose: same open, save and
// save-loop lifecycle, same degrade-to-empty behavior on a
// corrupt file. All methods are safe for concurrent use.
type Store struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	players map[string]*PlayerRecord
	recent  []MatchEntry // newest first, capped at MaxRecentStored
	path    string       // "" means ephemeral: never touch disk
	log     *log.Logger
	dirty   bool
	now     func() time.Time // tests substitute a fake clock
}

// Open creates a store backed by the JSON file at path, loading
// any records a previous run saved. A missing file is a fresh
// board, not an error; a corrupt file is logged and also degrades
// to a fresh board (the tournament board is a nice-to-have, never
// a reason for the server to refuse to start). Path "" keeps
// everything in memory.
func Open(path string, logger *log.Logger) *Store {
	if logger == nil {
		logger = log.Default()
	}
	s := &Store{
		players: make(map[string]*PlayerRecord),
		path:    path,
		log:     logger,
		now:     time.Now,
	}
	s.load()
	return s
}

func (s *Store) load() {
	if s.path == "" {
		return
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(s.path)
	if err != nil {
		if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
			s.log.Printf("matches: cannot read %s (%v); starting empty", s.path, err)
		}
		return
	}
	var file diskFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &file); err != nil {
		s.log.Printf("matches: %s is corrupt (%v); starting empty", s.path, err)
		return
	}
	for _, p := range file.Players {
		rec := p
		s.players[rec.Name] = &rec
	}
	s.recent = file.Recent
	if len(s.recent) > MaxRecentStored {
		s.recent = s.recent[:MaxRecentStored]
	}
	s.log.Printf("matches: loaded %d players and %d recent matches from %s",
		len(s.players), len(s.recent), s.path)
}

// diskFile is the on-disk shape of the matches file: the player
// records in name order, and the recent feed newest first.
type diskFile struct {
	Version int            `json:"version"`
	Players []PlayerRecord `json:"players"`
	Recent  []MatchEntry   `json:"recent"`
}

// Save writes the current records to the backing file atomically
// (temp file + rename, so a crash mid-save cannot truncate the
// last good board). It is a no-op for ephemeral stores.
func (s *Store) Save() error {
	if s.path == "" {
		return nil
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	file := diskFile{Version: 1, Recent: append([]MatchEntry{}, s.recent...)}
	names := make([]string, 0, len(s.players))
	for name := range s.players {
		names = append(names, name)
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	for _, name := range names {
		file.Players = append(file.Players, *s.players[name])
	}
	s.dirty = false
	s.mu.Unlock()

	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(file, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.dirty = true
		s.mu.Unlock()
		return err
	}
	if dir := filepath.Dir(s.path); dir != "." && dir != "" {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	tmp := s.path + ".tmp"
	if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.Rename(tmp, s.path)
}

// SaveLoop persists the board every interval, but only when a
// report changed it, and once more when ctx ends (server
// shutdown). It runs until ctx is cancelled.
func (s *Store) SaveLoop(ctx context.Context, interval time.Duration) {
	ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
	defer ticker.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			if s.isDirty() {
				if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
					s.log.Printf("matches: final save failed: %v", err)
				}
			}
			return
		case <-ticker.C:
			if s.isDirty() {
				if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
					s.log.Printf("matches: save failed: %v", err)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func (s *Store) isDirty() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.dirty
}

// clean normalizes a name the same way the other boards normalize
// the names they store: control characters stripped, edges
// trimmed. Case is preserved; names are case-sensitive.
func clean(name string) string {
	stripped := strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
		if unicode.IsControl(r) {
			return -1
		}
		return r
	}, name)
	return strings.TrimSpace(stripped)
}

// validateName applies the rules every stored player name must
// satisfy. emptyErr says which field was empty, so the client
// hears about the actual problem.
func validateName(name string, emptyErr error) error {
	switch {
	case name == "":
		return emptyErr
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(name) > MaxNameChars:
		return ErrNameLong
	}
	return nil
}

// validateDisplay checks an optional identity pair: either may be
// empty, but a present one must fit its cap.
func validateIdentity(display, region string) error {
	switch {
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(display) > MaxDisplayChars:
		return ErrDisplayLong
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(region) > MaxRegionChars:
		return ErrRegionLong
	}
	return nil
}

// recordFor returns the record for a cleaned name, creating and
// storing a fresh one when the name is new. Caller holds s.mu.
func (s *Store) recordFor(name string) *PlayerRecord {
	rec := s.players[name]
	if rec == nil {
		rec = &PlayerRecord{Name: name}
		s.players[name] = rec
	}
	return rec
}

// attachIdentity updates a record's identity from a report's
// extras. A report that carries no display leaves the stored
// identity alone; one that carries a display replaces both
// fields (latest identity wins, the stats rule). Caller holds
// s.mu.
func attachIdentity(rec *PlayerRecord, display, region string) {
	if display == "" {
		return
	}
	rec.Display = display
	rec.Region = region
}

// ReportMatch records one finished match: the winner gains a win
// and a match, the loser a loss and a match, both are stamped
// with the tournament and game as their most recent event, and
// the match joins the head of the recent feed. Every string is
// cleaned before validation. It returns the recorded entry,
// stamped with the server's clock.
func (s *Store) ReportMatch(r MatchReport) (MatchEntry, error) {
	r.Tournament = clean(r.Tournament)
	r.Game = clean(r.Game)
	r.Winner = clean(r.Winner)
	r.Loser = clean(r.Loser)
	r.Host = clean(r.Host)
	r.WinnerDisplay = clean(r.WinnerDisplay)
	r.WinnerRegion = clean(r.WinnerRegion)
	r.LoserDisplay = clean(r.LoserDisplay)
	r.LoserRegion = clean(r.LoserRegion)
	switch {
	case r.Tournament == "":
		return MatchEntry{}, ErrEmptyTournament
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(r.Tournament) > MaxTournamentChars:
		return MatchEntry{}, ErrTournamentLong
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(r.Game) > MaxGameChars:
		return MatchEntry{}, ErrGameLong
	}
	if err := validateName(r.Winner, ErrEmptyWinner); err != nil {
		return MatchEntry{}, err
	}
	if err := validateName(r.Loser, ErrEmptyLoser); err != nil {
		return MatchEntry{}, err
	}
	if err := validateName(r.Host, ErrEmptyHost); err != nil {
		return MatchEntry{}, err
	}
	if r.Winner == r.Loser {
		return MatchEntry{}, ErrSelfMatch
	}
	if err := validateIdentity(r.WinnerDisplay, r.WinnerRegion); err != nil {
		return MatchEntry{}, err
	}
	if err := validateIdentity(r.LoserDisplay, r.LoserRegion); err != nil {
		return MatchEntry{}, err
	}

	at := s.now().UnixMilli()
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	winner := s.recordFor(r.Winner)
	winner.Wins++
	winner.Matches++
	winner.LastTournament = r.Tournament
	winner.LastGame = r.Game
	winner.LastPlayed = at
	attachIdentity(winner, r.WinnerDisplay, r.WinnerRegion)

	loser := s.recordFor(r.Loser)
	loser.Losses++
	loser.Matches++
	loser.LastTournament = r.Tournament
	loser.LastGame = r.Game
	loser.LastPlayed = at
	attachIdentity(loser, r.LoserDisplay, r.LoserRegion)

	entry := MatchEntry{
		Tournament: r.Tournament,
		Game:       r.Game,
		Winner:     r.Winner,
		Loser:      r.Loser,
		At:         at,
	}
	s.recent = append([]MatchEntry{entry}, s.recent...)
	if len(s.recent) > MaxRecentStored {
		s.recent = s.recent[:MaxRecentStored]
	}
	s.dirty = true
	return entry, nil
}

// ReportChampion records that a player won a tournament outright:
// their titles count rises by one and the tournament becomes
// their latest title and most recent event. The record is
// created when the champion has never played a reported match.
// display and region are the champion's optional identity extras.
func (s *Store) ReportChampion(tournament, champion, host, display, region string) error {
	tournament = clean(tournament)
	champion = clean(champion)
	host = clean(host)
	display = clean(display)
	region = clean(region)
	switch {
	case tournament == "":
		return ErrEmptyTournament
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(tournament) > MaxTournamentChars:
		return ErrTournamentLong
	}
	if err := validateName(champion, ErrEmptyChampion); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := validateName(host, ErrEmptyHost); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := validateIdentity(display, region); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	rec := s.recordFor(champion)
	rec.TournamentsWon++
	rec.LastTournament = tournament
	rec.LastTitle = tournament
	rec.LastPlayed = s.now().UnixMilli()
	attachIdentity(rec, display, region)
	s.dirty = true
	return nil
}

// Leaderboard returns the tournament board: every recorded
// player, ranked by tournaments won, then match wins, then
// matches played, then name, capped at limit rows.
func (s *Store) Leaderboard(limit int) []PlayerRecord {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]PlayerRecord, 0, len(s.players))
	for _, rec := range s.players {
		out = append(out, *rec)
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].TournamentsWon != out[j].TournamentsWon {
			return out[i].TournamentsWon > out[j].TournamentsWon
		}
		if out[i].Wins != out[j].Wins {
			return out[i].Wins > out[j].Wins
		}
		if out[i].Matches != out[j].Matches {
			return out[i].Matches > out[j].Matches
		}
		return out[i].Name < out[j].Name
	})
	if limit < 0 {
		limit = 0
	}
	if len(out) > limit {
		out = out[:limit]
	}
	return out
}

// Recent returns the newest reported matches, newest first,
// capped at limit entries. It hands back a copy: callers may not
// mutate the store's feed.
func (s *Store) Recent(limit int) []MatchEntry {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if limit < 0 {
		limit = 0
	}
	if len(s.recent) < limit {
		limit = len(s.recent)
	}
	out := make([]MatchEntry, limit)
	copy(out, s.recent[:limit])
	return out
}

// PlayerCount returns how many players have records.
func (s *Store) PlayerCount() int {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return len(s.players)
}

package matches

func discardLog() *log.Logger { return log.New(io.Discard, "", 0) }

func newTestStore(t *testing.T) *Store {
	t.Helper()
	return Open("", discardLog())
}

// fakeClock replaces the store's clock with one the test steps by
// hand, so timestamps and ordering are deterministic.
type fakeClock struct{ t time.Time }

func (c *fakeClock) now() time.Time {
	c.t = c.t.Add(time.Second)
	return c.t
}

func newClockedStore(t *testing.T) (*Store, *fakeClock) {
	t.Helper()
	s := newTestStore(t)
	c := &fakeClock{t: time.Unix(1_700_000_000, 0)}
	s.now = c.now
	return s, c
}

func mustReport(t *testing.T, s *Store, r MatchReport) MatchEntry {
	t.Helper()
	entry, err := s.ReportMatch(r)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReportMatch(%+v): %v", r, err)
	}
	return entry
}

func recordByName(t *testing.T, s *Store, name string) PlayerRecord {
	t.Helper()
	for _, rec := range s.Leaderboard(LeaderboardSize) {
		if rec.Name == name {
			return rec
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no record for %q", name)
	return PlayerRecord{}
}

func TestReportMatchAccounting(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := newClockedStore(t)
	entry := mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Friday Night Fights",
		Game:       "Mortal Kombat (USA).md",
		Winner:     "David",
		Loser:      "Brother",
		Host:       "David",
	})
	if entry.Winner != "David" || entry.Loser != "Brother" ||
		entry.Tournament != "Friday Night Fights" || entry.Game != "Mortal Kombat (USA).md" {
		t.Errorf("entry = %+v, want the reported match", entry)
	}
	if entry.At == 0 {
		t.Error("entry.At = 0, want a server timestamp")
	}

	winner := recordByName(t, s, "David")
	if winner.Wins != 1 || winner.Losses != 0 || winner.Matches != 1 || winner.TournamentsWon != 0 {
		t.Errorf("winner record = %+v, want 1 win, 0 losses, 1 match, 0 titles", winner)
	}
	if winner.LastTournament != "Friday Night Fights" || winner.LastGame != "Mortal Kombat (USA).md" {
		t.Errorf("winner stamps = %q/%q, want the match's tournament and game",
			winner.LastTournament, winner.LastGame)
	}
	if winner.LastPlayed != entry.At {
		t.Errorf("winner LastPlayed = %d, want the match time %d", winner.LastPlayed, entry.At)
	}

	loser := recordByName(t, s, "Brother")
	if loser.Wins != 0 || loser.Losses != 1 || loser.Matches != 1 {
		t.Errorf("loser record = %+v, want 0 wins, 1 loss, 1 match", loser)
	}

	// A rematch the other way accumulates on the same records.
	mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Friday Night Fights",
		Game:       "Mortal Kombat (USA).md",
		Winner:     "Brother",
		Loser:      "David",
		Host:       "David",
	})
	winner = recordByName(t, s, "David")
	if winner.Wins != 1 || winner.Losses != 1 || winner.Matches != 2 {
		t.Errorf("after rematch, David = %+v, want 1 win, 1 loss, 2 matches", winner)
	}
	if s.PlayerCount() != 2 {
		t.Errorf("PlayerCount = %d, want 2", s.PlayerCount())
	}
}

func TestReportMatchValidation(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	base := MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Friday Night Fights",
		Game:       "Mortal Kombat (USA).md",
		Winner:     "David",
		Loser:      "Brother",
		Host:       "David",
	}
	longName := strings.Repeat("x", MaxNameChars+1)
	cases := []struct {
		name   string
		mutate func(*MatchReport)
		want   error
	}{
		{"empty tournament", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Tournament = "" }, ErrEmptyTournament},
		{"blank tournament", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Tournament = "   " }, ErrEmptyTournament},
		{"empty winner", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Winner = "" }, ErrEmptyWinner},
		{"blank winner", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Winner = "  " }, ErrEmptyWinner},
		{"empty loser", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Loser = "" }, ErrEmptyLoser},
		{"empty host", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Host = "" }, ErrEmptyHost},
		{"self match", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Loser = "David" }, ErrSelfMatch},
		{"self match after clean", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Loser = "  David " }, ErrSelfMatch},
		{"winner too long", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Winner = longName }, ErrNameLong},
		{"host too long", func(r *MatchReport) { r.Host = longName }, ErrNameLong},
		{"tournament too long", func(r *MatchReport) {
			r.Tournament = strings.Repeat("x", MaxTournamentChars+1)
		}, ErrTournamentLong},
		{"game too long", func(r *MatchReport) {
			r.Game = strings.Repeat("x", MaxGameChars+1)
		}, ErrGameLong},
		{"winner display too long", func(r *MatchReport) {
			r.WinnerDisplay = strings.Repeat("x", MaxDisplayChars+1)
		}, ErrDisplayLong},
		{"loser region too long", func(r *MatchReport) {
			r.LoserDisplay = "Brother P."
			r.LoserRegion = strings.Repeat("x", MaxRegionChars+1)
		}, ErrRegionLong},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		r := base
		tc.mutate(&r)
		if _, err := s.ReportMatch(r); !errors.Is(err, tc.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: err = %v, want %v", tc.name, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if s.PlayerCount() != 0 {
		t.Errorf("PlayerCount = %d, want 0: rejected reports must record nothing", s.PlayerCount())
	}
	if got := s.Recent(RecentSize); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Recent = %v, want empty after rejected reports", got)
	}
}

func TestReportChampion(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := newClockedStore(t)
	// A champion with no reported matches gets a fresh record.
	if err := s.ReportChampion("Friday Night Fights", "David", "David", "", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReportChampion: %v", err)
	}
	rec := recordByName(t, s, "David")
	if rec.TournamentsWon != 1 || rec.Wins != 0 || rec.Matches != 0 {
		t.Errorf("champion record = %+v, want 1 title, 0 wins, 0 matches", rec)
	}
	if rec.LastTitle != "Friday Night Fights" || rec.LastTournament != "Friday Night Fights" {
		t.Errorf("title stamps = %q/%q, want the tournament", rec.LastTitle, rec.LastTournament)
	}
	if rec.LastPlayed == 0 {
		t.Error("LastPlayed = 0, want the championship time")
	}

	// A second title accumulates and replaces the latest title.
	if err := s.ReportChampion("Saturday Showdown", "David", "David", "", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rec = recordByName(t, s, "David")
	if rec.TournamentsWon != 2 || rec.LastTitle != "Saturday Showdown" {
		t.Errorf("after second title: %+v, want 2 titles, latest Saturday Showdown", rec)
	}
	// Champions do not touch the recent match feed.
	if got := s.Recent(RecentSize); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Recent = %v, want empty: champions are not matches", got)
	}
}

func TestLeaderboardOrdering(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	play := func(winner, loser string) {
		mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
			Tournament: "Cup", Game: "Game (USA).md",
			Winner: winner, Loser: loser, Host: "Host",
		})
	}
	// Titles first: Champ has 2.
	for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
		if err := s.ReportChampion("Cup", "Champ", "Host", "", ""); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	// Carol and Bob tie on 1 title and 3 wins; Carol has more
	// matches (5 to 3). Alice has 1 title but only 1 win.
	if err := s.ReportChampion("Cup", "Carol", "Host", "", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.ReportChampion("Cup", "Bob", "Host", "", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.ReportChampion("Cup", "Alice", "Host", "", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	play("Carol", "Opp1")
	play("Carol", "Opp2")
	play("Carol", "Opp3")
	play("Opp4", "Carol")
	play("Opp5", "Carol")
	play("Bob", "Opp1")
	play("Bob", "Opp2")
	play("Bob", "Opp3")
	play("Alice", "Opp1")
	// Dave and Erin are identical but for the name: 1 win,
	// 2 matches each, no titles. Their conquerors only ever win
	// once in one match, so Dave and Erin head the 1-win group
	// on the matches tie-break.
	play("Dave", "Fall1")
	play("Fall2", "Dave")
	play("Erin", "Fall3")
	play("Fall4", "Erin")

	board := s.Leaderboard(LeaderboardSize)
	var names []string
	for _, rec := range board {
		names = append(names, rec.Name)
	}
	wantHead := []string{"Champ", "Carol", "Bob", "Alice", "Dave", "Erin"}
	if len(names) < len(wantHead) || fmt.Sprint(names[:len(wantHead)]) != fmt.Sprint(wantHead) {
		t.Errorf("board head = %v, want %v", names, wantHead)
	}
}

		}
	}

func TestIdentityAttachment(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Cup", Game: "Game (USA).md",
		Winner: "David", Loser: "Brother", Host: "David",
		WinnerDisplay: "David P.", WinnerRegion: "KY",
		LoserDisplay: "Brother P.", LoserRegion: "MO",
	})
	rec := recordByName(t, s, "David")
	if rec.Display != "David P." || rec.Region != "KY" {
		t.Errorf("winner identity = %q/%q, want David P./KY", rec.Display, rec.Region)
	}
	rec = recordByName(t, s, "Brother")
	if rec.Display != "Brother P." || rec.Region != "MO" {
		t.Errorf("loser identity = %q/%q, want Brother P./MO", rec.Display, rec.Region)
	}

	// A report with no identity leaves the stored one alone.
	mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Cup", Game: "Game (USA).md",
		Winner: "David", Loser: "Brother", Host: "David",
	})
	rec = recordByName(t, s, "David")
	if rec.Display != "David P." || rec.Region != "KY" {
		t.Errorf("after identity-free report, identity = %q/%q, want unchanged", rec.Display, rec.Region)
	}

	// A newer identity replaces the old one (latest wins), and a
	// champion report can carry one too.
	mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Cup", Game: "Game (USA).md",
		Winner: "David", Loser: "Brother", Host: "David",
		WinnerDisplay: "David R. P.", WinnerRegion: "KY",
	})
	if err := s.ReportChampion("Cup", "Brother", "David", "Brother P.", "KS"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	rec = recordByName(t, s, "David")
	if rec.Display != "David R. P." {
		t.Errorf("identity = %q, want the newest report's", rec.Display)
	}
	rec = recordByName(t, s, "Brother")
	if rec.Region != "KS" {
		t.Errorf("champion identity region = %q, want KS from the champion report", rec.Region)
	}
}

func TestRecentOrderingAndStoredCap(t *testing.T) {
	s, _ := newClockedStore(t)
	for i := 0; i < MaxRecentStored+5; i++ {
		mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
			Tournament: "Cup", Game: "Game (USA).md",
			Winner: fmt.Sprintf("W%02d", i), Loser: "Loser", Host: "Host",
		})
	}
	recent := s.Recent(RecentSize)
	if len(recent) != RecentSize {
		t.Fatalf("Recent(%d) returned %d rows", RecentSize, len(recent))
	}
	if recent[0].Winner != fmt.Sprintf("W%02d", MaxRecentStored+4) {
		t.Errorf("newest = %q, want the last reported match", recent[0].Winner)
	}
	for i := 1; i < len(recent); i++ {
		if recent[i-1].At <= recent[i].At {
			t.Fatalf("recent feed not newest first at %d: %d then %d", i, recent[i-1].At, recent[i].At)
		}
	}
	if got := s.Recent(MaxRecentStored + 10); len(got) != MaxRecentStored {
		t.Errorf("stored feed = %d rows, want the %d cap", len(got), MaxRecentStored)
	}
}

func TestPersistenceRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "matches.json")
	s, _ := newClockedStore(t)
	s.path = path
	mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Friday Night Fights", Game: "Mortal Kombat (USA).md",
		Winner: "David", Loser: "Brother", Host: "David",
		WinnerDisplay: "David P.", WinnerRegion: "KY",
	})
	mustReport(t, s, MatchReport{
		Tournament: "Friday Night Fights", Game: "Mortal Kombat (USA).md",
		Winner: "Brother", Loser: "David", Host: "David",
	})
	if err := s.ReportChampion("Friday Night Fights", "David", "David", "", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Save: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("matches file missing after Save: %v", err)
	}

	reopened := Open(path, discardLog())
	want := s.Leaderboard(LeaderboardSize)
	got := reopened.Leaderboard(LeaderboardSize)
	if fmt.Sprint(got) != fmt.Sprint(want) {
		t.Errorf("reopened board = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
	wantRecent := s.Recent(RecentSize)
	gotRecent := reopened.Recent(RecentSize)
	if fmt.Sprint(gotRecent) != fmt.Sprint(wantRecent) {
		t.Errorf("reopened recent = %+v, want %+v", gotRecent, wantRecent)
	}
}

==================== FILE: netplay/internal/server/hub.go ====================

package server

import (
	"sync"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/lobby"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/ws"
)

// peer is one connected signaling socket in a lobby room.
type peer struct {
	conn    *ws.Conn
	lobbyID string
	role    lobby.Role
	player  string // display name, for server notices that name a member
	token   string // kept only to revoke membership on disconnect
}

// hub tracks live sockets per lobby and relays messages between them.
// Messages are opaque: the hub never parses client payloads, it only
// forwards the exact bytes (and opcode) to everyone else in the room.
type hub struct {
	mu    sync.Mutex
	rooms map[string]map[*peer]struct{}
}

func newHub() *hub {
	return &hub{rooms: make(map[string]map[*peer]struct{})}
}

// add registers p in its room and returns the room's peer count.
func (h *hub) add(p *peer) int {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	room, ok := h.rooms[p.lobbyID]
	if !ok {
		room = make(map[*peer]struct{})
		h.rooms[p.lobbyID] = room
	}
	room[p] = struct{}{}
	return len(room)
}

// remove unregisters p and returns the room's remaining peer count.
func (h *hub) remove(p *peer) int {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	room, ok := h.rooms[p.lobbyID]
	if !ok {
		return 0
	}
	delete(room, p)
	if len(room) == 0 {
		delete(h.rooms, p.lobbyID)
		return 0
	}
	return len(room)
}

// others returns a snapshot of the other peers in p's room.
func (h *hub) others(p *peer) []*peer {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]*peer, 0, 2)
	for q := range h.rooms[p.lobbyID] {
		if q != p {
			out = append(out, q)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// all returns a snapshot of every peer in p's room, p included. If p
// has already been removed from the room, the snapshot is the room
// that remains, which is what teardown notices want.
func (h *hub) all(p *peer) []*peer {
	h.mu.Lock()
	defer h.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]*peer, 0, 2)
	for q := range h.rooms[p.lobbyID] {
		out = append(out, q)
	}
	return out
}

// relay forwards a client message verbatim to everyone else in the room.
func (h *hub) relay(from *peer, op int, data []byte) {
	for _, q := range h.others(from) {
		// A dead socket is cleaned up by its own read loop; a failed
		// relay write is not the sender's problem.
		_ = q.conn.WriteMessage(op, data)
	}
}

// notify sends a server-generated JSON control message to a peer.
func (h *hub) notify(p *peer, msg []byte) {
	_ = p.conn.WriteMessage(ws.OpText, msg)
}

// broadcastOthers sends a server-generated message to the rest of the room.
func (h *hub) broadcastOthers(from *peer, msg []byte) {
	for _, q := range h.others(from) {
		h.notify(q, msg)
	}
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/server/ratelimit.go ====================

package server

import (
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// rateLimiter is a small sliding-window limiter keyed by an arbitrary
// string (usually client IP, or IP+lobby for join attempts). It exists
// to slow password guessing and lobby spam, not to be a precise quota
// system.
type rateLimiter struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	events map[string][]time.Time
	limit  int
	window time.Duration
	now    func() time.Time
}

func newRateLimiter(limit int, window time.Duration) *rateLimiter {
	return &rateLimiter{
		events: make(map[string][]time.Time),
		limit:  limit,
		window: window,
		now:    time.Now,
	}
}

// allow records an attempt for key and reports whether it is within
// the limit. Every call counts, success or failure.
func (rl *rateLimiter) allow(key string) bool {
	rl.mu.Lock()
	defer rl.mu.Unlock()
	now := rl.now()
	cutoff := now.Add(-rl.window)
	kept := rl.events[key][:0]
	for _, t := range rl.events[key] {
		if t.After(cutoff) {
			kept = append(kept, t)
		}
	}
	if len(kept) >= rl.limit {
		rl.events[key] = kept
		return false
	}
	rl.events[key] = append(kept, now)
	return true
}

// clientIP extracts the host part of the request's remote address.
func clientIP(r *http.Request) string {
	host, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(r.RemoteAddr)
	if err != nil {
		return r.RemoteAddr
	}
	return host
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/server/server.go ====================

// Package server is the HTTP + WebSocket front door for netplay
// lobbies: lobby CRUD over HTTP, and a signaling relay over WebSocket
// that passes client messages between the peers of a lobby verbatim.
package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/lobby"
	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/ws"
)

// Rate limits (per client IP unless noted).
const (
	createLimit     = 10          // lobby creates per minute
	createWindow    = time.Minute //
	joinLimit       = 20          // join attempts per minute per IP+lobby
	joinWindow      = time.Minute //
	maxWSPerIP      = 10          // concurrent signaling sockets per IP
	maxBodyBytes    = 64 << 10    // HTTP request body cap
	pingInterval    = 25 * time.Second
	connIdleTimeout = 90 * time.Second
	hardMaxPlayers  = 8
)

// Server wires the lobby store, the signaling hub, and the HTTP mux.
type Server struct {
	store   lobby.Store
	hub     *hub
	log     *log.Logger
	create  *rateLimiter
	join    *rateLimiter
	wsCount *ipCounter
}

// New builds a Server on top of a lobby store.
func New(store lobby.Store, logger *log.Logger) *Server {
	if logger == nil {
		logger = log.Default()
	}
	return &Server{
		store:   store,
		hub:     newHub(),
		log:     logger,
		create:  newRateLimiter(createLimit, createWindow),
		join:    newRateLimiter(joinLimit, joinWindow),
		wsCount: newIPCounter(),
	}
}

// Handler returns the HTTP routing tree.
func (s *Server) Handler() http.Handler {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", s.handleHealth)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /lobbies", s.handleCreateLobby)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /lobbies", s.handleListLobbies)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /lobbies/{id}/join", s.handleJoinLobby)
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /lobbies/{id}/watch", s.handleWatchLobby)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /ws", s.handleWS)
	return mux
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// HTTP handlers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func (s *Server) handleHealth(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
		"status":  "ok",
		"lobbies": s.store.Count(),
	})
}

type createLobbyRequest struct {
	Name       string `json:"name"`
	Game       string `json:"game"`
	HostPlayer string `json:"hostPlayer"`
	Password   string `json:"password"`
	MaxPlayers int    `json:"maxPlayers"`
}

func (s *Server) handleCreateLobby(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if !s.create.allow(clientIP(r)) {
		writeError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too many lobbies created; slow down")
		return
	}
	var req createLobbyRequest
	if err := decodeJSON(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	switch {
	case len(req.Name) == 0 || len(req.Name) > 64:
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "name must be 1-64 characters")
		return
	case len(req.Game) == 0 || len(req.Game) > 256:
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "game must be 1-256 characters")
		return
	case len(req.HostPlayer) == 0 || len(req.HostPlayer) > 32:
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "hostPlayer must be 1-32 characters")
		return
	case len(req.Password) > 128:
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "password too long")
		return
	case req.MaxPlayers != 0 && (req.MaxPlayers < 2 || req.MaxPlayers > hardMaxPlayers):
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "maxPlayers must be between 2 and 8")
		return
	}

	l, hostToken, err := s.store.Create(lobby.CreateInput{
		Name:       req.Name,
		Game:       req.Game,
		HostPlayer: req.HostPlayer,
		Password:   req.Password,
		MaxPlayers: req.MaxPlayers,
	})
	if errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrTooMany) {
		writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "server is full of lobbies; try again later")
		return
	}
	if err != nil {
		s.log.Printf("create lobby: %v", err)
		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "could not create lobby")
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{
		"id":        l.ID,
		"hostToken": hostToken,
		"wsUrl":     wsURL(l.ID, hostToken),
		"lobby":     l.Public(),
	})
}

func (s *Server) handleListLobbies(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
		"lobbies": s.store.List(),
	})
}

type joinLobbyRequest struct {
	Player   string `json:"player"`
	Password string `json:"password"`
}

func (s *Server) handleJoinLobby(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id := r.PathValue("id")
	// Every attempt counts against the limit, right or wrong: this is
	// the password-guessing brake.
	if !s.join.allow(clientIP(r) + ":" + id) {
		writeError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too many join attempts; slow down")
		return
	}
	var req joinLobbyRequest
	if err := decodeJSON(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	if len(req.Player) == 0 || len(req.Player) > 32 {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "player must be 1-32 characters")
		return
	}

	token, err := s.store.Join(id, req.Player, req.Password)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrNotFound):
		writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "lobby not found")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrBadPassword):
		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong password")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrFull):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "lobby is full")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrNameTaken):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that name is already in the lobby")
		return
	case err != nil:
		s.log.Printf("join lobby: %v", err)
		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "could not join lobby")
		return
	}
	public, _ := s.store.Public(id)
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
		"guestToken": token,
		"wsUrl":      wsURL(id, token),
		"lobby":      public,
	})
}

// handleWatchLobby admits a spectator. Same request shape and the
// same password brake as a guest join; the difference is the seat:
// a spectator gets a spectator token, never a player seat.
func (s *Server) handleWatchLobby(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id := r.PathValue("id")
	if !s.join.allow(clientIP(r) + ":" + id) {
		writeError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too many join attempts; slow down")
		return
	}
	var req joinLobbyRequest
	if err := decodeJSON(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	if len(req.Player) == 0 || len(req.Player) > 32 {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "player must be 1-32 characters")
		return
	}

	token, err := s.store.Watch(id, req.Player, req.Password)
	switch {
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrNotFound):
		writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "lobby not found")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrBadPassword):
		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "wrong password")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrSpectatorsFull):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "spectator seats are full")
		return
	case errors.Is(err, lobby.ErrNameTaken):
		writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "that name is already in the lobby")
		return
	case err != nil:
		s.log.Printf("watch lobby: %v", err)
		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "could not watch lobby")
		return
	}
	public, _ := s.store.Public(id)
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
		"spectatorToken": token,
		"wsUrl":          wsURL(id, token),
		"lobby":          public,
	})
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WebSocket signaling relay
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// handleWS upgrades the connection after authenticating the token. From
// then on, every message the client sends is relayed verbatim to the
// other peers in the lobby: SDP offers/answers, ICE candidates, and (as
// a fallback path) lockstep "input"/"relay" frames all look the same to
// this server. The direct-vs-relay choice belongs to the clients.
func (s *Server) handleWS(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	lobbyID := r.URL.Query().Get("lobby")
	token := r.URL.Query().Get("token")
	self, ok := s.store.LookupMember(lobbyID, token)
	if !ok {
		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "invalid lobby or token")
		return
	}
	role := self.Role
	ip := clientIP(r)
	if !s.wsCount.acquire(ip, maxWSPerIP) {
		writeError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too many connections from this address")
		return
	}
	defer s.wsCount.release(ip)

	conn, err := ws.Upgrade(w, r)
	if err != nil {
		s.log.Printf("ws upgrade from %s: %v", ip, err)
		return
	}
	p := &peer{conn: conn, lobbyID: lobbyID, role: role, player: self.Name, token: token}

	count := s.hub.add(p)
	s.store.SetPeers(lobbyID, count)
	s.log.Printf("ws: %s joined lobby %s (%d peers)", role, lobbyID, count)
	// Spectators get their own arrival notice. peer_joined stays
	// player-only: player clients read it as "my opponent is here",
	// and a watcher is not an opponent. Everyone then gets the full
	// roster, the new arrival included.
	if role == lobby.RoleSpectator {
		s.hub.broadcastOthers(p, playerMsg("spectator_joined", p.player))
	} else {
		s.hub.broadcastOthers(p, controlMsg("peer_joined", role))
	}
	s.sendRoster(p)

	defer s.teardown(p)
	s.servePeer(p)
}

// servePeer runs the read/ping loop for one connected peer.
func (s *Server) servePeer(p *peer) {
	conn := p.conn
	extendDeadline := func() {
		_ = conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(connIdleTimeout))
	}
	conn.OnPong = extendDeadline
	extendDeadline()

	done := make(chan struct{})
	defer close(done)
	go func() {
		ticker := time.NewTicker(pingInterval)
		defer ticker.Stop()
		for {
			select {
			case <-done:
				return
			case <-ticker.C:
				if err := conn.WriteMessage(ws.OpPing, nil); err != nil {
					conn.Close()
					return
				}
			}
		}
	}()

	for {
		op, data, err := conn.ReadMessage()
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		extendDeadline()
		s.hub.relay(p, op, data)
	}
}

// teardown handles a peer's socket going away.
//
// Host leaving ends the session for everyone, spectators included:
// the room is told the lobby closed, every socket is closed, and
// the lobby is deleted. A guest leaving frees their slot: the host
// is notified, the guest's membership token is revoked, and the
// lobby stays open for a replacement guest (the reaper collects it
// later if the host abandons it too). A spectator leaving is the
// quiet case: their token is revoked and the room hears about it,
// but no seat frees and the session carries on untouched. Guests
// and spectators both end with a fresh roster for the room.
func (s *Server) teardown(p *peer) {
	remaining := s.hub.remove(p)
	p.conn.Close()

	if p.role == lobby.RoleHost {
		s.hub.broadcastOthers(p, controlMsg("lobby_closed", p.role))
		for _, q := range s.hub.others(p) {
			q.conn.Close()
			s.hub.remove(q)
		}
		s.store.Delete(p.lobbyID)
		s.log.Printf("ws: host left, lobby %s closed", p.lobbyID)
		return
	}

	s.store.RemoveMemberByToken(p.lobbyID, p.token)
	s.store.SetPeers(p.lobbyID, remaining)
	if p.role == lobby.RoleSpectator {
		s.hub.broadcastOthers(p, playerMsg("spectator_left", p.player))
		s.sendRoster(p)
		s.log.Printf("ws: spectator left lobby %s (%d peers)", p.lobbyID, remaining)
		return
	}
	s.hub.broadcastOthers(p, controlMsg("peer_left", p.role))
	s.sendRoster(p)
	s.log.Printf("ws: guest left lobby %s (%d peers)", p.lobbyID, remaining)
}

// sendRoster delivers the room's current roster to every socket in
// p's room. It runs on every membership change so all clients,
// players and watchers alike, render the same room. The roster comes
// from lobby membership (names and roles), not from socket state:
// someone who joined over HTTP is on it before their socket lands.
func (s *Server) sendRoster(p *peer) {
	members, ok := s.store.Members(p.lobbyID)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	msg := rosterMsg(members)
	for _, q := range s.hub.all(p) {
		s.hub.notify(q, msg)
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// controlMsg builds a server-generated control envelope. Client
// messages pass through untouched; only these lifecycle notices are
// minted by the server.
func controlMsg(kind string, role lobby.Role) []byte {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"type": kind, "role": string(role)})
	return b
}

// playerMsg builds a server-generated envelope naming one member,
// used by the spectator arrival and departure notices.
func playerMsg(kind string, player string) []byte {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"type": kind, "player": player})
	return b
}

// rosterMsg builds the roster notice: the room's full member list,
// names and roles, in join order.
func rosterMsg(members []lobby.Member) []byte {
	b, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"type": "roster", "members": members})
	return b
}

func wsURL(lobbyID, token string) string {
	return "/ws?lobby=" + lobbyID + "&token=" + token
}

func decodeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) error {
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBodyBytes)
	dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
	dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
	return dec.Decode(dst)
}

func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
}

func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, msg string) {
	writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": msg})
}

// ipCounter tracks concurrent connections per IP.
type ipCounter struct {
	mu sync.Mutex
	m  map[string]int
}

func newIPCounter() *ipCounter { return &ipCounter{m: make(map[string]int)} }

func (c *ipCounter) acquire(ip string, max int) bool {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	if c.m[ip] >= max {
		return false
	}
	c.m[ip]++
	return true
}

func (c *ipCounter) release(ip string) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	if c.m[ip] <= 1 {
		delete(c.m, ip)
	} else {
		c.m[ip]--
	}
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/server/server_test.go ====================

package server

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/davidpatton/itak-gaming/netplay/internal/lobby"
)

func newTestServer(t *testing.T) *httptest.Server {
	t.Helper()
	s := New(lobby.NewMemoryStore(), log.New(io.Discard, "", 0))
	ts := httptest.NewServer(s.Handler())
	t.Cleanup(ts.Close)
	return ts
}

func post(t *testing.T, url, body string) (int, map[string]any) {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Post(url, "application/json", bytes.NewBufferString(body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var out map[string]any
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decode response: %v", err)
	}
	return resp.StatusCode, out
}

func TestLobbyFlowOverHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	ts := newTestServer(t)

	// Health.
	resp, err := http.Get(ts.URL + "/healthz")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("healthz = %d, want 200", resp.StatusCode)
	}

	// Create.
	status, created := post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies",
		`{"name":"Kart night","game":"Super Mario Kart (USA).sfc","hostPlayer":"David","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusCreated {
		t.Fatalf("create = %d, want 201: %v", status, created)
	}
	id, _ := created["id"].(string)
	hostToken, _ := created["hostToken"].(string)
	if id == "" || hostToken == "" {
		t.Fatalf("create response missing id/token: %v", created)
	}

	// List: the lobby shows up, locked, without secrets.
	resp, err = http.Get(ts.URL + "/lobbies")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var list struct {
		Lobbies []lobby.PublicLobby `json:"lobbies"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&list); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(list.Lobbies) != 1 || list.Lobbies[0].ID != id || !list.Lobbies[0].Locked {
		t.Fatalf("list wrong: %+v", list.Lobbies)
	}

	// Wrong password -> 401. Right password -> token.
	status, _ = post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/"+id+"/join", `{"player":"Bro","password":"nope"}`)
	if status != http.StatusUnauthorized {
		t.Fatalf("wrong password = %d, want 401", status)
	}
	status, joined := post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/"+id+"/join", `{"player":"Bro","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("join = %d, want 200: %v", status, joined)
	}
	if tok, _ := joined["guestToken"].(string); tok == "" || tok == hostToken {
		t.Fatalf("guest token bad: %v", joined)
	}
	if wsURL, _ := joined["wsUrl"].(string); !strings.Contains(wsURL, "/ws?lobby="+id) {
		t.Fatalf("wsUrl bad: %v", joined)
	}

	// Lobby is full at 2 players.
	status, _ = post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/"+id+"/join", `{"player":"Third","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusConflict {
		t.Fatalf("third join = %d, want 409", status)
	}

	// Joining a ghost lobby -> 404.
	status, _ = post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/ZZZZZ/join", `{"player":"X"}`)
	if status != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("ghost join = %d, want 404", status)
	}

	// WS endpoint rejects a bad token before upgrading.
	resp, err = http.Get(ts.URL + "/ws?lobby=" + id + "&token=bogus")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	resp.Body.Close()
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusUnauthorized {
		t.Fatalf("ws bad token = %d, want 401", resp.StatusCode)
	}
}

func TestCreateValidation(t *testing.T) {
	ts := newTestServer(t)
	for _, body := range []string{
		`{"name":"","game":"G","hostPlayer":"D"}`,
		`{"name":"N","game":"","hostPlayer":"D"}`,
		`{"name":"N","game":"G","hostPlayer":""}`,
		`{"name":"N","game":"G","hostPlayer":"D","maxPlayers":99}`,
		`{"name":"N","game":"G","hostPlayer":"D","bogusField":1}`,
	} {
		status, _ := post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies", body)
		if status != http.StatusBadRequest {
			t.Errorf("body %s -> %d, want 400", body, status)
		}
	}
}

func TestWatchFlowOverHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	ts := newTestServer(t)

	status, created := post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies",
		`{"name":"Fight night","game":"Mortal Kombat (USA).md","hostPlayer":"David","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusCreated {
		t.Fatalf("create = %d, want 201: %v", status, created)
	}
	id, _ := created["id"].(string)

	// Wrong password -> 401, ghost lobby -> 404, host name -> 409.
	status, _ = post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/"+id+"/watch", `{"player":"Fan","password":"nope"}`)
	if status != http.StatusUnauthorized {
		t.Fatalf("watch wrong password = %d, want 401", status)
	}
	status, _ = post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/ZZZZZ/watch", `{"player":"Fan","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusNotFound {
		t.Fatalf("watch ghost lobby = %d, want 404", status)
	}
	status, _ = post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/"+id+"/watch", `{"player":"David","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusConflict {
		t.Fatalf("watch with host name = %d, want 409", status)
	}

	// Right password -> a spectator token of its own.
	status, watched := post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/"+id+"/watch", `{"player":"Fan","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("watch = %d, want 200: %v", status, watched)
	}
	specToken, _ := watched["spectatorToken"].(string)
	if specToken == "" {
		t.Fatalf("watch response missing spectatorToken: %v", watched)
	}
	if wsURL, _ := watched["wsUrl"].(string); !strings.Contains(wsURL, "/ws?lobby="+id) {
		t.Fatalf("wsUrl bad: %v", watched)
	}
	pub, _ := watched["lobby"].(map[string]any)
	if pub["players"] != float64(1) || pub["spectators"] != float64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("lobby after watch = players %v spectators %v, want 1/1", pub["players"], pub["spectators"])
	}

	// The listing shows the spectator count too.
	resp, err := http.Get(ts.URL + "/lobbies")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var list struct {
		Lobbies []lobby.PublicLobby `json:"lobbies"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&list); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(list.Lobbies) != 1 || list.Lobbies[0].Players != 1 || list.Lobbies[0].Spectators != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("list wrong: %+v", list.Lobbies)
	}

	// The player seats are untouched: a guest still joins, and the
	// join response counts players only.
	status, joined := post(t, ts.URL+"/lobbies/"+id+"/join", `{"player":"Brother","password":"pw"}`)
	if status != http.StatusOK {
		t.Fatalf("join after watch = %d, want 200: %v", status, joined)
	}
	if tok, _ := joined["guestToken"].(string); tok == "" || tok == specToken {
		t.Fatalf("guest token bad: %v", joined)
	}
	pub, _ = joined["lobby"].(map[string]any)
	if pub["players"] != float64(2) || pub["spectators"] != float64(1) {
		t.Fatalf("lobby after join = players %v spectators %v, want 2/1", pub["players"], pub["spectators"])
	}
}

// WebSocket level

// wsTestClient is a minimal masked-frame WebSocket client: just
// enough of RFC 6455 to talk to the signaling endpoint in tests.
type wsTestClient struct {
	nc net.Conn
	br *bufio.Reader

	wmu sync.Mutex

	mu     sync.Mutex
	msgs   []string // text payloads, in arrival order
	closed bool
}

func dialWS(t *testing.T, ts *httptest.Server, lobbyID, token string) *wsTestClient {
	t.Helper()
	u, err := url.Parse(ts.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	nc, err := net.Dial("tcp", u.Host)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c := &wsTestClient{nc: nc, br: bufio.NewReader(nc)}
	req := "GET /ws?lobby=" + lobbyID + "&token=" + token + " HTTP/1.1\r\n" +
		"Host: " + u.Host + "\r\n" +
		"Upgrade: websocket\r\n" +
		"Connection: Upgrade\r\n" +
		"Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==\r\n" +
		"Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n"
	if _, err := nc.Write([]byte(req)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	status, err := c.br.ReadString('\n')
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(status, "101") {
		t.Fatalf("handshake status line = %q, want 101", status)
	}
	for {
		line, err := c.br.ReadString('\n')
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if line == "\r\n" {
			break
		}
	}
	go c.readLoop()
	t.Cleanup(func() { nc.Close() })
	return c
}

func (c *wsTestClient) readLoop() {
	for {
		op, payload, err := c.readFrame()
		if err != nil {
			c.markClosed()
			return
		}
		switch op {
		case ws.OpPing:
			_ = c.writeFrame(ws.OpPong, payload)
		case ws.OpClose:
			c.markClosed()
			return
		case ws.OpText, ws.OpBinary:
			c.mu.Lock()
			c.msgs = append(c.msgs, string(payload))
			c.mu.Unlock()
		}
	}
}

func (c *wsTestClient) readFrame() (int, []byte, error) {
	var hdr [2]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, hdr[:]); err != nil {
		return 0, nil, err
	}
	op := int(hdr[0] & 0x0f)
	masked := hdr[1]&0x80 != 0
	length := uint64(hdr[1] & 0x7f)
	switch length {
	case 126:
		var b [2]byte
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, b[:]); err != nil {
			return 0, nil, err
		}
		length = uint64(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[:]))
	case 127:
		var b [8]byte
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, b[:]); err != nil {
			return 0, nil, err
		}
		length = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[:])
	}
	var mask [4]byte
	if masked {
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, mask[:]); err != nil {
			return 0, nil, err
		}
	}
	payload := make([]byte, length)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, payload); err != nil {
		return 0, nil, err
	}
	if masked {
		for i := range payload {
			payload[i] ^= mask[i%4]
		}
	}
	return op, payload, nil
}

func (c *wsTestClient) writeFrame(op int, payload []byte) error {
	c.wmu.Lock()
	defer c.wmu.Unlock()
	var hdr []byte
	switch n := len(payload); {
	case n < 126:
		hdr = []byte{0x80 | byte(op), 0x80 | byte(n)}
	case n <= 0xffff:
		hdr = make([]byte, 4)
		hdr[0] = 0x80 | byte(op)
		hdr[1] = 0x80 | 126
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(hdr[2:], uint16(n))
	default:
		hdr = make([]byte, 10)
		hdr[0] = 0x80 | byte(op)
		hdr[1] = 0x80 | 127
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(hdr[2:], uint64(n))
	}
	mask := [4]byte{0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44}
	hdr = append(hdr, mask[:]...)
	if _, err := c.nc.Write(hdr); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	masked := make([]byte, len(payload))
	for i := range payload {
		masked[i] = payload[i] ^ mask[i%4]
	}
	_, err := c.nc.Write(masked)
	return err
}

// send transmits one text message.
func (c *wsTestClient) send(t *testing.T, msg string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := c.writeFrame(ws.OpText, []byte(msg)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("send: %v", err)
	}
}

// close drops the socket abruptly, the way a real disconnect looks.
func (c *wsTestClient) close() { c.nc.Close() }

func (c *wsTestClient) markClosed() {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.closed = true
	c.mu.Unlock()
}

func (c *wsTestClient) isClosed() bool {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return c.closed
}

func (c *wsTestClient) snapshot() []string {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), c.msgs...)
}

// waitFor scans the received messages until pred matches one.
func waitFor(t *testing.T, c *wsTestClient, what string, pred func(map[string]any) bool) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		for _, raw := range c.snapshot() {
			var m map[string]any
			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &m); err != nil {
				continue
			}
			if pred(m) {
				return m
			}
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s; received: %v", what, c.snapshot())
	return nil
}

// waitRaw waits for one exact payload, byte for byte.
func waitRaw(t *testing.T, c *wsTestClient, want string) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		for _, raw := range c.snapshot() {
			if raw == want {
				return
			}
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for payload %q; received: %v", want, c.snapshot())
}

func waitClosed(t *testing.T, c *wsTestClient, who string) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second)
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		if c.isClosed() {
			return
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
	t.Fatalf("%s socket never closed; received: %v", who, c.snapshot())
}

// assertNone fails if any received message matches pred.
func assertNone(t *testing.T, c *wsTestClient, what string, pred func(map[string]any) bool) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, raw := range c.snapshot() {
		var m map[string]any
		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &m); err != nil {
			continue
		}
		if pred(m) {
			t.Errorf("%s unexpectedly received %s: %s", what, what, raw)
		}
	}
}

func typeIs(kind string) func(map[string]any) bool {
	return func(m map[string]any) bool { return m["type"] == kind }
}

// rosterIs matches a roster notice listing exactly these members, in
// order, as (name, role) pairs.
func rosterIs(want ...lobby.Member) func(map[string]any) bool {
	return func(m map[string]any) bool {
		if m["type"] != "roster" {
			return false
		}
		list, ok := m["members"].([]any)
		if !ok || len(list) != len(want) {
			return false
		}
		for i, w := range want {
			mm, ok := list[i].(map[string]any)
			if !ok || mm["name"] != w.Name || mm["role"] != string(w.Role) {
				return false
			}
		}
		return true
	}
}

func newStoreServer(t *testing.T) (*lobby.MemoryStore, *httptest.Server) {
	t.Helper()
	store := lobby.NewMemoryStore()
	s := New(store, log.New(io.Discard, "", 0))
	ts := httptest.NewServer(s.Handler())
	t.Cleanup(ts.Close)
	return store, ts
}

// room is a full house over the store: host, guest, spectator, with
// their tokens.
type room struct {
	id         string
	hostToken  string
	guestToken string
	specToken  string
}

func newRoom(t *testing.T, store *lobby.MemoryStore) room {
	t.Helper()
	l, hostToken, err := store.Create(lobby.CreateInput{Name: "Fight night", Game: "G", HostPlayer: "David"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	guestToken, err := store.Join(l.ID, "Brother", "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	specToken, err := store.Watch(l.ID, "Fan", "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return room{id: l.ID, hostToken: hostToken, guestToken: guestToken, specToken: specToken}
}

var (
	mDavid  = lobby.Member{Name: "David", Role: lobby.RoleHost}
	mBro    = lobby.Member{Name: "Brother", Role: lobby.RoleGuest}
	mFan    = lobby.Member{Name: "Fan", Role: lobby.RoleSpectator}
	roomAll = []lobby.Member{mDavid, mBro, mFan}
)

func TestSpectatorNoticesOverWS(t *testing.T) {
	store, ts := newStoreServer(t)
	r := newRoom(t, store)

	// Host connects: only a roster comes back, listing the seats
	// already taken over HTTP.
	host := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.hostToken)
	waitFor(t, host, "host roster", rosterIs(roomAll...))

	// Guest connects: host hears peer_joined for the guest and then
	// a fresh roster. The guest hears the roster only.
	guest := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.guestToken)
	waitFor(t, host, "peer_joined for guest", func(m map[string]any) bool {
		return m["type"] == "peer_joined" && m["role"] == "guest"
	})
	waitFor(t, guest, "guest roster", rosterIs(roomAll...))
	assertNone(t, guest, "peer_joined", typeIs("peer_joined"))

	// Spectator connects: the room hears spectator_joined naming the
	// watcher, plus a fresh roster. The spectator hears the roster
	// only, and nobody anywhere hears a peer_joined for a spectator.
	spec := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.specToken)
	for _, c := range []*wsTestClient{host, guest} {
		waitFor(t, c, "spectator_joined", func(m map[string]any) bool {
			return m["type"] == "spectator_joined" && m["player"] == "Fan"
		})
		waitFor(t, c, "roster after spectator joined", rosterIs(roomAll...))
	}
	waitFor(t, spec, "spectator roster", rosterIs(roomAll...))
	for _, c := range []*wsTestClient{host, guest, spec} {
		assertNone(t, c, "peer_joined for spectator", func(m map[string]any) bool {
			return m["type"] == "peer_joined" && m["role"] == "spectator"
		})
		assertNone(t, spec, "spectator_joined about itself", typeIs("spectator_joined"))
	}
}

func TestSpectatorTrafficRelays(t *testing.T) {
	store, ts := newStoreServer(t)
	r := newRoom(t, store)

	host := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.hostToken)
	guest := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.guestToken)
	spec := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.specToken)
	waitFor(t, spec, "spectator roster", rosterIs(roomAll...))

	// A spectator's chat reaches both players, byte for byte.
	chat := `{"type":"chat","from":"Fan","text":"gl hf"}`
	spec.send(t, chat)
	waitRaw(t, host, chat)
	waitRaw(t, guest, chat)

	// And a player's frames reach the spectator too: watching runs
	// on the same relayed stream the players exchange.
	input := `{"type":"input","frame":12,"buttons":9}`
	host.send(t, input)
	waitRaw(t, guest, input)
	waitRaw(t, spec, input)
}

func TestSpectatorDisconnectLeavesSessionAlone(t *testing.T) {
	store, ts := newStoreServer(t)
	r := newRoom(t, store)

	host := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.hostToken)
	guest := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.guestToken)
	spec := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.specToken)
	waitFor(t, spec, "spectator roster", rosterIs(roomAll...))

	spec.close()

	// The room hears spectator_left and a roster without the fan.
	for _, c := range []*wsTestClient{host, guest} {
		waitFor(t, c, "spectator_left", func(m map[string]any) bool {
			return m["type"] == "spectator_left" && m["player"] == "Fan"
		})
		waitFor(t, c, "roster after spectator left", rosterIs(mDavid, mBro))
		assertNone(t, c, "peer_left", typeIs("peer_left"))
		assertNone(t, c, "lobby_closed", typeIs("lobby_closed"))
	}

	// The lobby survives, the guest seat is untouched, and only the
	// spectator token died.
	if got := store.Count(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("lobby count = %d, want 1", got)
	}
	if role, ok := store.Authenticate(r.id, r.guestToken); !ok || role != lobby.RoleGuest {
		t.Errorf("guest auth after spectator left = %v/%v, want guest/true", role, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := store.Authenticate(r.id, r.specToken); ok {
		t.Error("spectator token still authenticates after disconnect")
	}
	if pub, _ := store.Public(r.id); pub.Players != 2 || pub.Spectators != 0 {
		t.Errorf("players/spectators = %d/%d, want 2/0", pub.Players, pub.Spectators)
	}

	// The two players are still talking.
	still := `{"type":"input","frame":99,"buttons":1}`
	guest.send(t, still)
	waitRaw(t, host, still)
}

func TestHostDisconnectClosesRoomForEveryone(t *testing.T) {
	store, ts := newStoreServer(t)
	r := newRoom(t, store)

	host := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.hostToken)
	guest := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.guestToken)
	spec := dialWS(t, ts, r.id, r.specToken)
	waitFor(t, spec, "spectator roster", rosterIs(roomAll...))

	host.close()

	// Guest and spectator alike get lobby_closed, then the server
	// closes their sockets, and the lobby is gone.
	for _, c := range []*wsTestClient{guest, spec} {
		waitFor(t, c, "lobby_closed", typeIs("lobby_closed"))
	}
	waitClosed(t, guest, "guest")
	waitClosed(t, spec, "spectator")
	if got := store.Count(); got != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("lobby count = %d, want 0", got)
	}
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/stats/http.go ====================

package stats

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// maxReportBody caps a single stats report. A report is six small
// fields; 16 KB is far more than enough.
const maxReportBody = 16 << 10

// Handler is the HTTP front door for the global leaderboard. It
// registers on the same mux (and therefore the same port) as the
// lobby service.
type Handler struct {
	store   *Store
	log     *log.Logger
	limiter *deviceLimiter
}

// NewHandler builds a Handler over a stats store.
func NewHandler(store *Store, logger *log.Logger) *Handler {
	if logger == nil {
		logger = log.Default()
	}
	return &Handler{
		store:   store,
		log:     logger,
		limiter: newDeviceLimiter(reportLimit, reportWindow),
	}
}

// Register adds the leaderboard routes to a mux. Method patterns
// make the mux itself answer 405 for wrong verbs on these paths.
func (h *Handler) Register(mux *http.ServeMux) {
	mux.HandleFunc("POST /stats/report", h.handleReport)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /leaderboard/players", h.handleTopPlayers)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /leaderboard/games", h.handleTopGames)
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /leaderboard/recent", h.handleRecent)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Handlers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// reportRequest is the wire form of a stats report. It decodes into
// Report only after validation and sanitization.
type reportRequest struct {
	DeviceID   string `json:"deviceId"`
	Player     string `json:"player"`
	Game       string `json:"game"`
	Plays      int    `json:"plays"`
	Seconds    int    `json:"seconds"`
	LastPlayed int64  `json:"lastPlayed"`
	Display    string `json:"display"`
	Region     string `json:"region"`
}

func (h *Handler) handleReport(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req reportRequest
	if err := decodeReport(w, r, &req); err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body")
		return
	}
	rep, err := validateReport(req)
	if err != nil {
		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if !h.limiter.allow(rep.DeviceID) {
		writeError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too many stats reports; slow down")
		return
	}
	// A stale report (lower than what is stored) is still a success:
	// the client's totals were received and the board already holds
	// newer ones.
	h.store.Report(rep)
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
}

func (h *Handler) handleTopPlayers(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, h.store.TopPlayers(BoardSize))
}

func (h *Handler) handleTopGames(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, h.store.TopGames(BoardSize))
}

func (h *Handler) handleRecent(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, h.store.Recent(BoardSize))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Validation and sanitization
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// validateReport cleans a decoded request into a storable Report:
// control characters are stripped, edges are trimmed, lengths are
// enforced, and counters are range-checked and clamped.
func validateReport(req reportRequest) (Report, error) {
	device := sanitize(req.DeviceID)
	player := sanitize(req.Player)
	game := sanitize(req.Game)
	display := sanitize(req.Display)
	region := sanitize(req.Region)
	switch {
	case device == "":
		return Report{}, errors.New("deviceId is required")
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(device) > MaxDeviceChars:
		return Report{}, errors.New("deviceId is too long")
	case player == "":
		return Report{}, errors.New("player is required")
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(player) > MaxPlayerChars:
		return Report{}, errors.New("player must be at most 40 characters")
	case game == "":
		return Report{}, errors.New("game is required")
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(game) > MaxGameChars:
		return Report{}, errors.New("game must be at most 120 characters")
	case req.Plays < 0:
		return Report{}, errors.New("plays must be >= 0")
	case req.Seconds < 0:
		return Report{}, errors.New("seconds must be >= 0")
	case req.LastPlayed < 0:
		return Report{}, errors.New("lastPlayed must be >= 0")
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(display) > MaxDisplayChars:
		return Report{}, errors.New("display must be at most 60 characters")
	case utf8.RuneCountInString(region) > MaxRegionChars:
		return Report{}, errors.New("region must be at most 40 characters")
	}
	return Report{
		DeviceID:   device,
		Player:     player,
		Game:       game,
		Plays:      minInt(req.Plays, MaxValue),
		Seconds:    minInt(req.Seconds, MaxValue),
		LastPlayed: req.LastPlayed,
		Display:    display,
		Region:     region,
	}, nil
}

// sanitize strips control characters (newlines, NULs, escape codes)
// from a display string so a hostile name cannot smuggle terminal
// tricks or broken rows into other clients' leaderboard screens.
func sanitize(s string) string {
	clean := strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
		if unicode.IsControl(r) {
			return -1
		}
		return r
	}, s)
	return strings.TrimSpace(clean)
}

func minInt(a, b int) int {
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// JSON helpers (kept local: the lobby server's copies are unexported)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

func decodeReport(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) error {
	r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxReportBody)
	dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
	dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
	return dec.Decode(dst)
}

func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(status)
	_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
}

func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, msg string) {
	writeJSON(w, status, map[string]string{"error": msg})
}

package stats

func newTestHandler(t *testing.T) (*httptest.Server, *Store) {

	store := Open("", discardLog())
	h := NewHandler(store, discardLog())
	mux := http.NewServeMux()

	return ts, store

func postRaw(t *testing.T, url, body string) *http.Response {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Post(url, "application/json", bytes.NewBufferString(body))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { resp.Body.Close() })
	return resp
}

func getJSON[T any](t *testing.T, url string) (int, string, T) {
	t.Helper()
	resp, err := http.Get(url)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	var out T
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("decode %s: %v", url, err)
	}
	return resp.StatusCode, resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), out
}

func TestReportAndLeaderboardRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	ts, _ := newTestHandler(t)

	// Two devices report; David appears on both.

	}
	if len(players) != 2 || players[0].Player != "David" ||
		players[0].Seconds != 700 || players[0].Plays != 4 || players[0].Games != 1 {
		t.Errorf("players board = %+v, want David 700s/4 plays/1 game first", players)
	}

	if len(games) != 2 || games[0].Game != "SMW" || games[0].Seconds != 700 || games[0].Players != 1 {

	}

	_, _, recent := getJSON[[]RecentEntry](t, ts.URL+"/leaderboard/recent")
	if len(recent) != 3 || recent[0].LastPlayed != 2000 || recent[0].Player != "David" {
		t.Errorf("recent = %+v, want David's 2000 entry first", recent)
	}

	// board back.
	resp := postRaw(t, ts.URL+"/stats/report",
		`{"deviceId":"tv","player":"David","game":"SMW","plays":1,"seconds":50,"lastPlayed":500}`)

		t.Fatalf("stale report status = %d, want 204", resp.StatusCode)
	}

	if players[0].Seconds != 700 {
		t.Errorf("after stale report David seconds = %d, want 700", players[0].Seconds)
	}
}

func TestReportValidation(t *testing.T) {
	ts, _ := newTestHandler(t)
	cases := map[string]string{
		"malformed JSON":   `{`,
		"unknown field":    `{"deviceId":"d","player":"P","game":"G","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0,"nope":1}`,
		"missing deviceId": `{"player":"P","game":"G","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"missing player":   `{"deviceId":"d","game":"G","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"missing game":     `{"deviceId":"d","player":"P","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"blank player":     `{"deviceId":"d","player":"   ","game":"G","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"player too long":  `{"deviceId":"d","player":"` + strings.Repeat("x", 41) + `","game":"G","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"game too long":    `{"deviceId":"d","player":"P","game":"` + strings.Repeat("g", 121) + `","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"negative plays":   `{"deviceId":"d","player":"P","game":"G","plays":-1,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"negative seconds": `{"deviceId":"d","player":"P","game":"G","plays":0,"seconds":-5,"lastPlayed":0}`,
		"float plays":      `{"deviceId":"d","player":"P","game":"G","plays":1.5,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`,
	}
	for name, body := range cases {
		resp := postRaw(t, ts.URL+"/stats/report", body)
		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusBadRequest {
			t.Errorf("%s: status = %d, want 400", name, resp.StatusCode)
		}
	}

	// Oversized body: 16 KB cap.
	big := `{"deviceId":"d","player":"` + strings.Repeat("y", 20000) + `","game":"G","plays":0,"seconds":0,"lastPlayed":0}`
	resp := postRaw(t, ts.URL+"/stats/report", big)
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusBadRequest {
		t.Errorf("oversized body: status = %d, want 400", resp.StatusCode)
	}
}
