==================== FILE: netplay/internal/stats/ratelimit.go ====================

package stats

import (
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Rate limit for stat reports, per device ID. A box legitimately
// bursts when it syncs a whole library of per-player/per-game totals,
// so the allowance is generous; it exists to stop a runaway or
// hostile client from hammering the endpoint, not to meter honest
// syncs.
const (
	reportLimit  = 300
	reportWindow = time.Minute
)

// deviceLimiter is a sliding-window limiter keyed by device ID. It
// mirrors the lobby server's per-IP limiter, with the addition that
// idle keys are dropped so the map cannot grow without bound as
// devices come and go.
type deviceLimiter struct {
	mu     sync.Mutex
	events map[string][]time.Time
	limit  int
	window time.Duration
	now    func() time.Time
}

func newDeviceLimiter(limit int, window time.Duration) *deviceLimiter {
	return &deviceLimiter{
		events: make(map[string][]time.Time),
		limit:  limit,
		window: window,
		now:    time.Now,
	}
}

// allow records an attempt for key and reports whether it is within
// the limit. Every call counts, accepted or not.
func (l *deviceLimiter) allow(key string) bool {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	now := l.now()
	cutoff := now.Add(-l.window)
	kept := l.events[key][:0]
	for _, t := range l.events[key] {
		if t.After(cutoff) {
			kept = append(kept, t)
		}
	}
	if len(kept) == 0 {
		delete(l.events, key)
	} else {
		l.events[key] = kept
	}
	if len(kept) >= l.limit {
		return false
	}
	l.events[key] = append(kept, now)
	return true
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/stats/stats.go ====================

// Package stats is the global leaderboard service for iTaK Gaming.
//
// Every copy of the app keeps per-player play stats locally (plays,
// seconds, last played, per game). Clients periodically report those
// cumulative totals here, keyed by an opaque device ID, and anyone
// can read the aggregated rankings: top players by time played, top
// games, and the most recent activity across every device that has
// ever reported in.
//
// Player identity for display is the player NAME: the same name
// reported from two devices (David on the TV box and on a handheld)
// is one person on the board, so their totals are summed together.
package stats

// Limits.
const (
	// MaxTriples caps how many (device, player, game) entries the
	// store keeps. Inserts beyond the cap evict the least recently
	// played entry.
	MaxTriples = 20_000

	// MaxPlayerChars and MaxGameChars bound the display strings a
	// report may carry (counted in runes, after sanitization).
	MaxPlayerChars = 40
	MaxGameChars   = 120
	// MaxDeviceChars bounds the opaque device ID.
	MaxDeviceChars = 128
	// MaxDisplayChars and MaxRegionChars bound the optional
	// identity strings a report may carry.
	MaxDisplayChars = 60
	MaxRegionChars  = 40

	// MaxValue clamps cumulative counters to a sane range (about
	// 31 years of seconds); anything larger is treated as corrupt
	// or abusive and pinned to the cap.
	MaxValue = 1_000_000_000

	// BoardSize is how many rows each leaderboard endpoint returns.
	BoardSize = 50
)

// Report is one client's cumulative totals for one player in one
// game, as kept for that (device, player, game) triple. Clients send
// totals for the whole history of that triple, never deltas.
//
// Display and Region are optional identity extras (a display name
// with initials, a home state or region) the client attaches so the
// boards can tell players apart. Older clients omit them; the raw
// Player name remains the identity and aggregation key either way.
type Report struct {
	DeviceID   string `json:"deviceId"`
	Player     string `json:"player"`
	Game       string `json:"game"`
	Plays      int    `json:"plays"`
	Seconds    int    `json:"seconds"`
	LastPlayed int64  `json:"lastPlayed"` // unix milliseconds
	Display    string `json:"display,omitempty"`
	Region     string `json:"region,omitempty"`
}

// PlayerStat is one row of the players leaderboard: a player name
// aggregated across every device that reported it. Display and
// Region carry the identity from that player's most recent report
// that included them.
type PlayerStat struct {
	Player  string `json:"player"`
	Seconds int    `json:"seconds"`
	Plays   int    `json:"plays"`
	Games   int    `json:"games"` // distinct games played
	Display string `json:"display,omitempty"`
	Region  string `json:"region,omitempty"`
}

// GameStat is one row of the games leaderboard: a game aggregated
// across every player and device.
type GameStat struct {
	Game    string `json:"game"`
	Seconds int    `json:"seconds"`
	Plays   int    `json:"plays"`
	Players int    `json:"players"` // distinct player names
}

// RecentEntry is one row of the recent-activity feed: the latest
// totals a device reported for one player in one game.
type RecentEntry struct {
	Player     string `json:"player"`
	Game       string `json:"game"`
	LastPlayed int64  `json:"lastPlayed"` // unix milliseconds
	Seconds    int    `json:"seconds"`
	Display    string `json:"display,omitempty"`
	Region     string `json:"region,omitempty"`
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/stats/store.go ====================

package stats

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// key identifies one stored triple: one player, in one game, on one
// device. Aggregation happens at read time, keyed by player name or
// game title alone.
type key struct {
	device string
	player string
	game   string
}

// Store keeps every reported triple in memory behind a mutex and
// persists them to a JSON file so a restart does not wipe the global
// board. All methods are safe for concurrent use.
type Store struct {
	mu         sync.Mutex
	entries    map[key]Report
	path       string // "" means ephemeral: never touch disk
	log        *log.Logger
	dirty      bool
	maxTriples int
}

// Open creates a store backed by the JSON file at path, loading any
// entries a previous run saved. A missing file is a fresh board, not
// an error; a corrupt file is logged and also degrades to a fresh
// board (the leaderboard is a nice-to-have, never a reason for the
// server to refuse to start). Path "" keeps everything in memory.
func Open(path string, logger *log.Logger) *Store {
	if logger == nil {
		logger = log.Default()
	}
	s := &Store{
		entries:    make(map[key]Report),
		path:       path,
		log:        logger,
		maxTriples: MaxTriples,
	}
	s.load()
	return s
}

func (s *Store) load() {
	if s.path == "" {
		return
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile(s.path)
	if err != nil {
		if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
			s.log.Printf("stats: cannot read %s (%v); starting empty", s.path, err)
		}
		return
	}
	var file diskFile
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &file); err != nil {
		s.log.Printf("stats: %s is corrupt (%v); starting empty", s.path, err)
		return
	}
	for _, r := range file.Entries {
		s.entries[key{r.DeviceID, r.Player, r.Game}] = r
	}
	s.enforceCap()
	s.log.Printf("stats: loaded %d entries from %s", len(s.entries), s.path)
}

// diskFile is the on-disk shape of the stats file.
type diskFile struct {
	Version int      `json:"version"`
	Entries []Report `json:"entries"`
}

// Save writes the current entries to the backing file atomically
// (temp file + rename, so a crash mid-save cannot truncate the last
// good board). It is a no-op for ephemeral stores.
func (s *Store) Save() error {
	if s.path == "" {
		return nil
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	file := diskFile{Version: 1, Entries: make([]Report, 0, len(s.entries))}
	for _, r := range s.entries {
		file.Entries = append(file.Entries, r)
	}
	s.dirty = false
	s.mu.Unlock()

	// Stable file layout, diff-friendly and easy to eyeball.
	sort.Slice(file.Entries, func(i, j int) bool {
		a, b := file.Entries[i], file.Entries[j]
		if a.DeviceID != b.DeviceID {
			return a.DeviceID < b.DeviceID
		}
		if a.Player != b.Player {
			return a.Player < b.Player
		}
		return a.Game < b.Game
	})
	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(file, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.dirty = true
		s.mu.Unlock()
		return err
	}
	if dir := filepath.Dir(s.path); dir != "." && dir != "" {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	tmp := s.path + ".tmp"
	if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.Rename(tmp, s.path)
}

// SaveLoop persists the board every interval, but only when a report
// changed it, and once more when ctx ends (server shutdown). It runs
// until ctx is cancelled.
func (s *Store) SaveLoop(ctx context.Context, interval time.Duration) {
	ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
	defer ticker.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			if s.isDirty() {
				if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
					s.log.Printf("stats: final save failed: %v", err)
				}
			}
			return
		case <-ticker.C:
			if s.isDirty() {
				if err := s.Save(); err != nil {
					s.log.Printf("stats: save failed: %v", err)
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

func (s *Store) isDirty() bool {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.dirty
}

// Count returns how many triples are stored.
func (s *Store) Count() int {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return len(s.entries)
}

// Report records one client's cumulative totals for a triple. The
// report REPLACES the stored entry only when it is at least as new:
// both plays and seconds must be >= the stored values (clients send
// cumulative totals, so anything lower is a stale echo from an older
// sync and is ignored). It returns true when the stored entry
// changed.
func (s *Store) Report(r Report) bool {
	k := key{r.DeviceID, r.Player, r.Game}
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if cur, ok := s.entries[k]; ok {
		if r.Plays < cur.Plays || r.Seconds < cur.Seconds {
			return false
		}
		if r == cur {
			return false
		}
		s.entries[k] = r
		s.dirty = true
		return true
	}
	if len(s.entries) >= s.maxTriples {
		s.evictOldest()
	}
	s.entries[k] = r
	s.dirty = true
	return true
}

// evictOldest drops the entry whose last play is longest ago. Caller
// holds s.mu and the store is at capacity.
func (s *Store) evictOldest() {
	var oldest key
	var oldestReport Report
	first := true
	for k, r := range s.entries {
		if first || lessRecent(r, k, oldestReport, oldest) {
			oldest, oldestReport, first = k, r, false
		}
	}
	delete(s.entries, oldest)
}

// lessRecent orders entries for eviction: smaller LastPlayed first,
// key fields as a deterministic tie-break.
func lessRecent(a Report, ak key, b Report, bk key) bool {
	if a.LastPlayed != b.LastPlayed {
		return a.LastPlayed < b.LastPlayed
	}
	if ak.device != bk.device {
		return ak.device < bk.device
	}
	if ak.player != bk.player {
		return ak.player < bk.player
	}
	return ak.game < bk.game
}

func (s *Store) enforceCap() {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	for len(s.entries) > s.maxTriples {
		s.evictOldest()
	}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Leaderboard reads
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// TopPlayers aggregates every triple by player name across all
// devices, ranked by total seconds (then plays, then name).
func (s *Store) TopPlayers(limit int) []PlayerStat {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	type agg struct {
		seconds, plays int
		games          map[string]struct{}
		// Identity from the most recent report that carried one.
		display, region string
		idSeen          int64
	}
	byPlayer := make(map[string]*agg)
	for _, r := range s.entries {
		a := byPlayer[r.Player]
		if a == nil {
			a = &agg{games: make(map[string]struct{})}
			byPlayer[r.Player] = a
		}
		a.seconds += r.Seconds
		a.plays += r.Plays
		a.games[r.Game] = struct{}{}
		if r.Display != "" && r.LastPlayed >= a.idSeen {
			a.display = r.Display
			a.region = r.Region
			a.idSeen = r.LastPlayed
		}
	}
	out := make([]PlayerStat, 0, len(byPlayer))
	for name, a := range byPlayer {
		out = append(out, PlayerStat{
			Player:  name,
			Seconds: a.seconds,
			Plays:   a.plays,
			Games:   len(a.games),
			Display: a.display,
			Region:  a.region,
		})
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].Seconds != out[j].Seconds {
			return out[i].Seconds > out[j].Seconds
		}
		if out[i].Plays != out[j].Plays {
			return out[i].Plays > out[j].Plays
		}
		return out[i].Player < out[j].Player
	})
	return truncate(out, limit)
}

// Identity returns the display name and region the store knows
// for one player: the values from the most recent report (by
// LastPlayed) that carried a display name, the same rule the
// players board uses. Both come back empty when the player never
// reported an identity, or never reported at all.
func (s *Store) Identity(player string) (display, region string) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	var seen int64
	for _, r := range s.entries {
		if r.Player != player || r.Display == "" {
			continue
		}
		if display == "" || r.LastPlayed >= seen {
			display, region, seen = r.Display, r.Region, r.LastPlayed
		}
	}
	return display, region
}

// TopGames aggregates every triple by game title across all players
// and devices, ranked by total seconds (then plays, then title).
func (s *Store) TopGames(limit int) []GameStat {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	type agg struct {
		seconds, plays int
		players        map[string]struct{}
	}
	byGame := make(map[string]*agg)
	for _, r := range s.entries {
		a := byGame[r.Game]
		if a == nil {
			a = &agg{players: make(map[string]struct{})}
			byGame[r.Game] = a
		}
		a.seconds += r.Seconds
		a.plays += r.Plays
		a.players[r.Player] = struct{}{}
	}
	out := make([]GameStat, 0, len(byGame))
	for title, a := range byGame {
		out = append(out, GameStat{
			Game:    title,
			Seconds: a.seconds,
			Plays:   a.plays,
			Players: len(a.players),
		})
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].Seconds != out[j].Seconds {
			return out[i].Seconds > out[j].Seconds
		}
		if out[i].Plays != out[j].Plays {
			return out[i].Plays > out[j].Plays
		}
		return out[i].Game < out[j].Game
	})
	return truncate(out, limit)
}

// Recent lists the most recently played triples, newest first
// (player, then game, as deterministic tie-breaks).
func (s *Store) Recent(limit int) []RecentEntry {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	out := make([]RecentEntry, 0, len(s.entries))
	for _, r := range s.entries {
		out = append(out, RecentEntry{
			Player:     r.Player,
			Game:       r.Game,
			LastPlayed: r.LastPlayed,
			Seconds:    r.Seconds,
			Display:    r.Display,
			Region:     r.Region,
		})
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
		if out[i].LastPlayed != out[j].LastPlayed {
			return out[i].LastPlayed > out[j].LastPlayed
		}
		if out[i].Player != out[j].Player {
			return out[i].Player < out[j].Player
		}
		return out[i].Game < out[j].Game
	})
	return truncate(out, limit)
}

func truncate[T any](rows []T, limit int) []T {
	if limit < 0 {
		limit = 0
	}
	if len(rows) > limit {
		return rows[:limit]
	}
	return rows
}

package stats

func newTestStore(t *testing.T) *Store {
	t.Helper()
	return Open("", log.New(io.Discard, "", 0))
}

func discardLog() *log.Logger { return log.New(io.Discard, "", 0) }

func TestReportReplaceIfGreater(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)
	base := Report{DeviceID: "box1", Player: "David", Game: "SMW", Plays: 3, Seconds: 600, LastPlayed: 1000}
	if !s.Report(base) {
		t.Fatal("first report should be stored")
	}
	if s.Count() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("count = %d, want 1", s.Count())
	}

	// Identical re-report: no change.
	if s.Report(base) {
		t.Error("identical report should report no change")
	}

	// Lower plays: stale, ignored.
	stale := base
	stale.Plays--
	stale.LastPlayed = 2000
	if s.Report(stale) {
		t.Error("report with lower plays should be ignored")
	}

	// Lower seconds: stale, ignored (both counters must be >=).
	stale = base
	stale.Seconds--
	stale.Plays++
	if s.Report(stale) {
		t.Error("report with lower seconds should be ignored even with higher plays")
	}

	// Higher totals replace, including a newer LastPlayed.
	newer := base
	newer.Plays = 4
	newer.Seconds = 900
	newer.LastPlayed = 3000
	if !s.Report(newer) {
		t.Fatal("higher report should replace")
	}
	recent := s.Recent(10)
	if len(recent) != 1 || recent[0].Seconds != 900 || recent[0].LastPlayed != 3000 {
		t.Errorf("stored entry = %+v, want seconds 900 lastPlayed 3000", recent)
	}

	// Equal counters with a newer LastPlayed still refresh recency.
	refresh := newer
	refresh.LastPlayed = 4000
	if !s.Report(refresh) {
		t.Error("equal totals with newer lastPlayed should replace")
	}
	if got := s.Recent(1)[0].LastPlayed; got != 4000 {
		t.Errorf("lastPlayed = %d, want 4000", got)
	}
}

func TestIdentity(t *testing.T) {
	s := newTestStore(t)

	// Unknown player: empty identity, no error.
	if d, r := s.Identity("Ghost"); d != "" || r != "" {
		t.Errorf("Identity(Ghost) = %q/%q, want empty", d, r)
	}

	// A report without an identity teaches the store nothing.
	s.Report(Report{DeviceID: "tv", Player: "Mary", Game: "Kart", Plays: 1, Seconds: 60, LastPlayed: 1000})
	if d, r := s.Identity("Mary"); d != "" || r != "" {
		t.Errorf("Identity(Mary) before any identity report = %q/%q, want empty", d, r)
	}

	// The most recent report carrying an identity wins, across
	// devices and games.
	s.Report(Report{DeviceID: "tv", Player: "Mary", Game: "Kart", Plays: 2, Seconds: 120, LastPlayed: 2000, Display: "Mary P.", Region: "MO"})
	s.Report(Report{DeviceID: "handheld", Player: "Mary", Game: "SMW", Plays: 1, Seconds: 30, LastPlayed: 1500, Display: "Old Name", Region: "KS"})
	if d, r := s.Identity("Mary"); d != "Mary P." || r != "MO" {
		t.Errorf("Identity(Mary) = %q/%q, want Mary P./MO (newest identity report)", d, r)
	}

	// A newer report for another game, carrying no identity, does
	// not erase it: identity is read from whichever stored entries
	// carry one, newest LastPlayed first (the players board's rule).
	s.Report(Report{DeviceID: "tv", Player: "Mary", Game: "Tetris", Plays: 1, Seconds: 10, LastPlayed: 3000})
	if d, r := s.Identity("Mary"); d != "Mary P." || r != "MO" {
		t.Errorf("Identity(Mary) after identity-free report = %q/%q, want Mary P./MO kept", d, r)
	}
}


==================== FILE: netplay/internal/ws/ws.go ====================

// Package ws is a minimal server-side WebSocket (RFC 6455)
// implementation built only on the standard library. It covers what the
// netplay signaling relay needs: upgrade handshake, text/binary frames
// with fragmentation, ping/pong, close, and a hard message size cap.
// It is not a general-purpose WebSocket library.
package ws

import (
	"bufio"
	"crypto/sha1"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/binary"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Frame opcodes.
const (
	OpContinuation = 0
	OpText         = 1
	OpBinary       = 2
	OpClose        = 8
	OpPing         = 9
	OpPong         = 10
)

// Close codes used by the relay.
const (
	CloseNormal    = 1000
	CloseGoingAway = 1001
	CloseTooBig    = 1009
	CloseInternal  = 1011
)

var (
	// ErrClosed is returned by ReadMessage after a close frame.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("ws: connection closed")
	// ErrTooBig is returned when a message exceeds the size cap.
	ErrTooBig = errors.New("ws: message too big")
)

const magicGUID = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11"

// DefaultMaxMessage caps a single (reassembled) message.
const DefaultMaxMessage = 256 << 10 // 256 KB

// Conn is one upgraded WebSocket connection. ReadMessage must be called
// from a single goroutine; WriteMessage is safe for concurrent use.
type Conn struct {
	nc         net.Conn
	br         *bufio.Reader
	wmu        sync.Mutex
	closeOnce  sync.Once
	maxMessage int

	// OnPong, if set, runs when a pong arrives. The server uses it to
	// extend the read deadline as proof of life.
	OnPong func()
}

// Upgrade hijacks w's connection and performs the server handshake.
// On failure it writes an HTTP error and returns a non-nil error.
func Upgrade(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (*Conn, error) {
	if !headerHasToken(r.Header, "Connection", "upgrade") ||
		!headerHasToken(r.Header, "Upgrade", "websocket") {
		http.Error(w, "not a websocket upgrade", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return nil, errors.New("ws: missing upgrade headers")
	}
	key := r.Header.Get("Sec-WebSocket-Key")
	if key == "" {
		http.Error(w, "missing Sec-WebSocket-Key", http.StatusBadRequest)
		return nil, errors.New("ws: missing key")
	}
	hj, ok := w.(http.Hijacker)
	if !ok {
		http.Error(w, "hijacking unsupported", http.StatusInternalServerError)
		return nil, errors.New("ws: hijacking unsupported")
	}
	nc, brw, err := hj.Hijack()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("ws: hijack: %w", err)
	}

	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(key + magicGUID))
	accept := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(sum[:])
	_, err = fmt.Fprintf(brw,
		"HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Accept: %s\r\n\r\n",
		accept)
	if err == nil {
		err = brw.Flush()
	}
	if err != nil {
		nc.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("ws: handshake write: %w", err)
	}
	return &Conn{nc: nc, br: brw.Reader, maxMessage: DefaultMaxMessage}, nil
}

func headerHasToken(h http.Header, name, token string) bool {
	for _, v := range h.Values(name) {
		for _, part := range strings.Split(v, ",") {
			if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(part), token) {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

// SetReadDeadline passes through to the underlying connection.
func (c *Conn) SetReadDeadline(t time.Time) error { return c.nc.SetReadDeadline(t) }

// RemoteAddr is the peer's network address.
func (c *Conn) RemoteAddr() net.Addr { return c.nc.RemoteAddr() }

// ReadMessage returns the next complete text or binary message.
// Ping frames are answered with pong automatically, pongs trigger
// OnPong, and a close frame ends the read with ErrClosed.
func (c *Conn) ReadMessage() (int, []byte, error) {
	var msgOp int
	var buf []byte
	for {
		fin, op, payload, err := c.readFrame()
		if err != nil {
			return 0, nil, err
		}
		switch op {
		case OpPing:
			_ = c.WriteMessage(OpPong, payload)
			continue
		case OpPong:
			if c.OnPong != nil {
				c.OnPong()
			}
			continue
		case OpClose:
			c.Close()
			return 0, nil, ErrClosed
		case OpText, OpBinary:
			if msgOp != 0 {
				c.Close()
				return 0, nil, errors.New("ws: new message before final frame")
			}
			msgOp = op
		case OpContinuation:
			if msgOp == 0 {
				c.Close()
				return 0, nil, errors.New("ws: unexpected continuation frame")
			}
		default:
			c.Close()
			return 0, nil, fmt.Errorf("ws: unknown opcode %d", op)
		}
		buf = append(buf, payload...)
		if len(buf) > c.maxMessage {
			_ = c.WriteClose(CloseTooBig, "message too big")
			c.Close()
			return 0, nil, ErrTooBig
		}
		if fin {
			return msgOp, buf, nil
		}
	}
}

func (c *Conn) readFrame() (bool, int, []byte, error) {
	var hdr [2]byte
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, hdr[:]); err != nil {
		return false, 0, nil, err
	}
	fin := hdr[0]&0x80 != 0
	op := int(hdr[0] & 0x0f)
	masked := hdr[1]&0x80 != 0
	length := uint64(hdr[1] & 0x7f)

	switch length {
	case 126:
		var b [2]byte
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, b[:]); err != nil {
			return false, 0, nil, err
		}
		length = uint64(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[:]))
	case 127:
		var b [8]byte
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, b[:]); err != nil {
			return false, 0, nil, err
		}
		length = binary.BigEndian.Uint64(b[:])
	}
	// A single frame larger than the message cap can never reassemble
	// into a legal message; fail fast instead of allocating for it.
	if length > uint64(c.maxMessage) {
		return false, 0, nil, ErrTooBig
	}

	var mask [4]byte
	if masked {
		if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, mask[:]); err != nil {
			return false, 0, nil, err
		}
	}
	payload := make([]byte, length)
	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, payload); err != nil {
		return false, 0, nil, err
	}
	if masked {
		for i := range payload {
			payload[i] ^= mask[i%4]
		}
	}
	return fin, op, payload, nil
}

// WriteMessage sends one unfragmented frame.
func (c *Conn) WriteMessage(op int, data []byte) error {
	c.wmu.Lock()
	defer c.wmu.Unlock()

	var hdr []byte
	switch n := len(data); {
	case n < 126:
		hdr = []byte{0x80 | byte(op), byte(n)}
	case n <= 0xffff:
		hdr = make([]byte, 4)
		hdr[0] = 0x80 | byte(op)
		hdr[1] = 126
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(hdr[2:], uint16(n))
	default:
		hdr = make([]byte, 10)
		hdr[0] = 0x80 | byte(op)
		hdr[1] = 127
		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(hdr[2:], uint64(n))
	}
	if _, err := c.nc.Write(hdr); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err := c.nc.Write(data)
	return err
}

// WriteClose sends a close frame with the given code (best effort).
func (c *Conn) WriteClose(code int, reason string) error {
	payload := make([]byte, 2+len(reason))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(payload, uint16(code))
	copy(payload[2:], reason)
	return c.WriteMessage(OpClose, payload)
}

// Close shuts the underlying connection. Safe to call more than once.
func (c *Conn) Close() error {
	var err error
	c.closeOnce.Do(func() { err = c.nc.Close() })
	return err
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Download console photos from Wikimedia Commons and cut the studio
background out (border flood fill), saving transparent PNGs.

Usage: python3 art_transparent.py [outdir]
Prints one line per system: id<TAB>status<TAB>source filename used.
"""
import io
import json
import sys
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from collections import deque

from PIL import Image

UA = {"User-Agent": "iTaK-Gaming-Art/1.0 (family arcade project)"}

# Candidate Commons file names per system, best first.
CANDIDATES = {
    "nes": ["NES-Console-Set.png", "NES-Console-Set.jpg"],
    "snes": ["SNES-Mod1-Console-Set.png"],
    "genesis": ["Sega-Genesis-NA-Mk2-Console-Set.png"],
    "gameboy": ["Game-Boy-Original.png", "Game-Boy-Original.jpg"],
    "gba": ["Nintendo-Game-Boy-Advance-Purple-FL.png",
            "Nintendo-Game-Boy-Advance-Purple-FL.jpg"],
    "ps1": ["PSX-Console-wController.png", "PSX-Console-wController.jpg"],
    "n64": ["N64-Console-Set.png", "Nintendo-64-Console-Set.png"],
    "dc": ["Dreamcast-Console-Set.png", "Sega-Dreamcast-Console-Set.png"],
    "psp": ["PSP-1000-Console-Set.png", "Sony-PSP-1000-Body.png",
            "PSP-Console-Set.png"],
    "ds": ["Nintendo-DS-Lite-Console-Set.png", "Nintendo-DS-Lite-Black.png",
           "Nintendo-DS-Fat-Blue.png"],
    "saturn": ["Sega-Saturn-Console-Set-Mk1.png",
               "Sega-Saturn-Console-Set.png", "Sega-Saturn-Console.png"],
    "gc": ["GameCube-Console-Set.png", "Nintendo-GameCube-Console-Set.png",
           "GameCube-Set.png"],
}

SEARCH_TERMS = {
    "psp": "PSP console set",
    "ds": "Nintendo DS Lite console",
    "saturn": "Sega Saturn console set",
    "gc": "GameCube console set",
    "n64": "Nintendo 64 console set",
    "dc": "Dreamcast console set",
}


def fetch(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        return r.read(), r.headers.get_content_type()


def fetch_file(filename, width=900):
    q = urllib.parse.quote(filename)
    url = f"https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/{q}?width={width}"
    data, ctype = fetch(url)
    if "image" not in ctype:
        raise ValueError(f"not an image: {ctype}")
    return data


def search_file(term):
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({
        "action": "query", "format": "json", "list": "search",
        "srsearch": f"filetype:bitmap {term}", "srnamespace": "6",
        "srlimit": "10",
    })
    data, _ = fetch(f"https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/api.php?{q}")
    hits = json.loads(data)["query"]["search"]
    for h in hits:
        title = h["title"].replace("File:", "")
        if title.lower().endswith(".png") and "console" in title.lower():
            return title
    for h in hits:
        title = h["title"].replace("File:", "")
        if "console" in title.lower():
            return title
    return None


def cut_background(img):
    """Flood fill from the borders; background pixels go transparent."""
    img = img.convert("RGBA")
    w, h = img.size
    px = img.load()
    corners = [px[2, 2], px[w - 3, 2], px[2, h - 3], px[w - 3, h - 3]]
    bg = tuple(sum(c[i] for c in corners) // 4 for i in range(3))

    def dist(a, b):
        return max(abs(a[0] - b[0]), abs(a[1] - b[1]), abs(a[2] - b[2]))

    def flood(tol):
        seen = bytearray(w * h)
        queue = deque()
        for x in range(w):
            queue.append((x, 0))
            queue.append((x, h - 1))
        for y in range(h):
            queue.append((0, y))
            queue.append((w - 1, y))
        mask = bytearray(w * h)
        while queue:
            x, y = queue.popleft()
            i = y * w + x
            if seen[i]:
                continue
            seen[i] = 1
            if dist(px[x, y], bg) <= tol:
                mask[i] = 1
                if x + 1 < w:
                    queue.append((x + 1, y))
                if x > 0:
                    queue.append((x - 1, y))
                if y + 1 < h:
                    queue.append((x, y + 1))
                if y > 0:
                    queue.append((x, y - 1))
        return mask

    # Pass 1: strictly background-colored pixels connected to the edge.
    # (No neighbor-drift rule: it creeps across smooth console shading
    # and eats dark consoles like the Genesis and Saturn.)
    mask = flood(46)
    removed = 0
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            if mask[y * w + x]:
                p = px[x, y]
                px[x, y] = (p[0], p[1], p[2], 0)
                removed += 1
    frac = removed / (w * h)
    # Trim to the real content. Cropping to the alpha bbox is not
    # enough: studio backdrops are gradients, so regions the flood
    # never reached stay opaque and keep the box huge, which makes
    # the console render tiny under contain-fit. Instead, bound the
    # pixels that actually differ from the background color (whether
    # or not the flood reached them) and crop there, with a margin.
    content = None
    for y in range(h):
        for x in range(w):
            r, g, b, a = px[x, y]
            if a > 8 and dist((r, g, b), bg) > 46:
                if content is None:
                    content = [x, y, x, y]
                else:
                    content[0] = min(content[0], x)
                    content[1] = min(content[1], y)
                    content[2] = max(content[2], x)
                    content[3] = max(content[3], y)
    if content is not None:
        margin = 14
        box = (
            max(0, content[0] - margin),
            max(0, content[1] - margin),
            min(w, content[2] + margin + 1),
            min(h, content[3] + margin + 1),
        )
        img = img.crop(box)
    return img, frac


def main():
    outdir = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "sysart_png"
    import os
    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
    for sid, names in CANDIDATES.items():
        used = None
        data = None
        for name in names:
            try:
                data = fetch_file(name)
                used = name
                break
            except Exception:
                continue
        if used is None and sid in SEARCH_TERMS:
            found = search_file(SEARCH_TERMS[sid])
            if found:
                try:
                    data = fetch_file(found)
                    used = found
                except Exception:
                    pass
        if used is None:
            print(f"{sid}\tFAILED\t-")
            continue
        try:
            img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(data))
            out, frac = cut_background(img)
            if frac > 0.93:
                print(f"{sid}\tSUSPICIOUS({frac:.0%} removed)\t{used}")
            out.save(f"{outdir}/{sid}.png")
            print(f"{sid}\tok removed={frac:.0%} size={out.size}\t{used}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{sid}\tERROR {e}\t{used}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()


==================== FILE: tools/autobuild-server.sh ====================

#!/bin/bash
# iTaK Gaming auto-build (runs on the ubuntu-server via cron).
#
# Watches the GitHub repo's main branch. When a push raises the
# pubspec version above the published one, this script rebuilds
# the APK with the server toolchain and publishes it to the app
# update feed (~/itak-netplay/app), where the app's self-updater
# picks it up. Publishing is the only outward effect; a failed
# build leaves the published version untouched.
#
# Invoked through ~/itak-autobuild.sh, a stable wrapper that
# refreshes the clone and runs a copy of this file so a push can
# never replace the script mid-run.
set -u
export PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin

CLONE=$HOME/itak-repo
WORK=$HOME/itak-gaming
APPDIR=$HOME/itak-netplay/app
STATE=$HOME/itak-autobuild.state
LOG=$HOME/itak-autobuild.log
exec >>"$LOG" 2>&1

echo "=== $(date -Is)"

state_get() { grep "^$1=" "$STATE" 2>/dev/null | cut -d= -f2-; }
state_set() {
    local tmp="$STATE.tmp"
    grep -v "^$1=" "$STATE" 2>/dev/null > "$tmp" || true
    echo "$1=$2" >> "$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$STATE"
}

SHA=$(git -C "$CLONE" rev-parse HEAD)
LAST=$(state_get LAST_SHA)
if [ "$SHA" = "$LAST" ]; then
    echo "no change: $SHA"
    exit 0
fi

# A failed build for this commit retries at most every 30 min.
FAIL_SHA=$(state_get FAIL_SHA)
FAIL_EPOCH=$(state_get FAIL_EPOCH)
NOW=$(date +%s)
if [ "$SHA" = "$FAIL_SHA" ] && [ -n "$FAIL_EPOCH" ] && [ $((NOW - FAIL_EPOCH)) -lt 1800 ]; then
    echo "build for $SHA failed recently; backing off"
    exit 0
fi
fail() {
    state_set FAIL_SHA "$SHA"
    state_set FAIL_EPOCH "$(date +%s)"
    echo "FAILED: $1"
    exit 0
}

# Version gate: only a pubspec version bump ships an update.
VERLINE=$(grep '^version:' "$CLONE/flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml")
VNAME=$(echo "$VERLINE" | sed 's/^version: //; s/+.*$//; s/\.0$//')
VCODE=$(echo "$VERLINE" | sed 's/^.*+//')
PUBCODE=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$APPDIR/version.json'))['versionCode'])" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
echo "repo version $VNAME+$VCODE, published code $PUBCODE"
if ! [ "$VCODE" -gt "$PUBCODE" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    state_set LAST_SHA "$SHA"
    echo "not a version bump; marked seen"
    exit 0
fi

# Sync sources into the build copy. Binary-only paths that git
# does not carry (emulator cores, the Go AAR) are preserved.
rsync -a --delete \
    --exclude '.git' \
    --exclude 'flutter_ui/build' \
    --exclude 'flutter_ui/.dart_tool' \
    --exclude 'flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/assets/cores' \
    --exclude 'flutter_ui/android/app/libs/itak_backend.aar' \
    --exclude 'testdata' \
    "$CLONE/" "$WORK/" || fail "rsync"

# Rebind the Go backend when it or the bundled cores changed.
# The cores are linked into the backend as native packages, so a
# core-only fix must rebind too; hashing go_backend alone would
# silently ship the stale AAR.
export JAVA_HOME=$HOME/toolchain/jdk17
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$HOME/toolchain/go/bin:$HOME/go/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
export ANDROID_NDK_HOME=$HOME/toolchain/android-sdk/ndk/26.1.10909125
export ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/toolchain/android-sdk
AAR_TREE=$(git -C "$CLONE" rev-parse HEAD:go_backend HEAD:cores | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1)
if [ "$AAR_TREE" != "$(state_get AAR_TREE)" ] || [ ! -f "$WORK/flutter_ui/android/app/libs/itak_backend.aar" ]; then
    echo "go_backend changed; rebinding AAR"
    (cd "$WORK/go_backend" && gomobile bind -target=android/arm -androidapi 24 \
        -o "$WORK/flutter_ui/android/app/libs/itak_backend.aar" ./mobile) \
        || fail "gomobile bind"
    cp "$WORK/flutter_ui/android/app/libs/itak_backend.aar" "$WORK/builds/itak_backend.aar" 2>/dev/null || true
    state_set AAR_TREE "$AAR_TREE"
fi

# Rust switch: stage the six prebuilt Rust adapter libraries.
# Each library ships two ways: as a jniLibs entry (packaged
# into lib/armeabi-v7a) and as the assets/cores payload under
# its libitak name. The app picks its core by shipped file
# name: libitak_<system>.so resolves to the Rust adapter
# through the backend switch, libgo_<system>.so to the
# bundled Go core. The rsync above excludes assets/cores, so
# the payload swap is explicit here: the libgo payload files
# leave the build tree and the libitak files take their
# place, byte-identical to the staged prebuilt libraries.
RUSTLIBS=$HOME/itak-rust-libs/armeabi-v7a
JNILIBDIR="$WORK/flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/jniLibs/armeabi-v7a"
CORESDIR="$WORK/flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/assets/cores"
mkdir -p "$JNILIBDIR" "$CORESDIR" || fail "rust staging mkdir"
for so in libitak_gameboy.so libitak_nes.so libitak_snes.so libitak_genesis.so libitak_gba.so libitak_ps1.so; do
    cp "$RUSTLIBS/$so" "$JNILIBDIR/$so" || fail "rust jniLibs staging: $so"
    cp "$RUSTLIBS/$so" "$CORESDIR/$so" || fail "rust cores staging: $so"
done
rm -f "$CORESDIR"/libgo_*.so
echo "staged Rust libraries:"; ls -la "$JNILIBDIR" "$CORESDIR"

# Build the APK.
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$HOME/toolchain/flutter/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
(cd "$WORK/flutter_ui" && env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/toolchain/xdg \
    flutter build apk --release --target-platform android-arm) \
    || fail "flutter build"

# Publish: versioned APK + fresh manifest, then prune old ones.
APK="$WORK/flutter_ui/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk"
[ -f "$APK" ] || fail "APK missing after build"
OUT="$APPDIR/iTaKGaming-$VNAME.apk"
cp "$APK" "$OUT" || fail "publish copy"
python3 - "$OUT" "$VNAME" "$VCODE" "$CLONE/release-notes.txt" "$APPDIR/version.json" <<'PYEOF' || fail "manifest write"
import hashlib, json, sys, os, datetime
apk, vname, vcode, notes_path, out_path = sys.argv[1:6]
data = open(apk, "rb").read()
notes = "A new build of iTaK Gaming."
if os.path.exists(notes_path):
    txt = open(notes_path).read().strip()
    if txt:
        notes = txt
manifest = {
    "versionCode": int(vcode),
    "versionName": vname,
    "apk": os.path.basename(apk),
    "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
    "size": len(data),
    "notes": notes,
    "publishedAt": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
}
tmp = out_path + ".tmp"
open(tmp, "w").write(json.dumps(manifest))
os.replace(tmp, out_path)
print("manifest:", json.dumps(manifest))
PYEOF
ls -t "$APPDIR"/iTaKGaming-*.apk 2>/dev/null | tail -n +4 | xargs -r rm -f

state_set LAST_SHA "$SHA"
state_set FAIL_SHA ""
echo "published $VNAME ($SHA)"
